title: fix(engine): report the stream duration as the keyframe interval for single-GOP videos
body:
Closes #3460

`analyzeKeyframeIntervals` returned `isProblematic: false` for any video with fewer than two keyframes. A video with exactly one keyframe is one GOP spanning the whole file, so every seek past 0 decodes from the start. The compiler warned about a 5s GOP and stayed silent about a 10s one.

This change splits the early return. Zero keyframes (still images) keep the old result. One keyframe now reports the video stream's duration as both the average and max interval, and flags the file when that duration exceeds the existing 2s threshold. It reads `videoStreamDurationSeconds` from the cached `extractMediaMetadata` probe, per the maintainer note on the issue: a 1s picture in a 10s audio container has a 1s GOP, so the container duration is the wrong number.

Scope: interval math only. The warning text in `compileForRender` is unchanged.

Repro (from the issue), before and after, on macOS with ffmpeg 8:

```
single-gop.mp4       before {"avgIntervalSeconds":0,"maxIntervalSeconds":0,"keyframeCount":1,"isProblematic":false}
single-gop.mp4       after  {"avgIntervalSeconds":10,"maxIntervalSeconds":10,"keyframeCount":1,"isProblematic":true}
five-second-gop.mp4  both   {"avgIntervalSeconds":5,"maxIntervalSeconds":5,"keyframeCount":2,"isProblematic":true}
```

Tests: three new cases in `ffprobe.test.ts` (single keyframe over 2s flags, short video stream inside a long audio container does not flag, zero keyframes stays silent). `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, engine `tsc --noEmit`, and the producer `mediaProbeConcurrency` test pass.

title: fix(producer): bound nested media by a host's data-duration when it has no data-end
body:
## What

The render-media planner now closes a composition host (`data-composition-file` element) at the same window the runtime uses to hide its descendants. `resolveHostEnd` in `packages/producer/src/services/renderMediaCollector.ts` delegates to the runtime's own `resolveAuthoredTimingWindow` from `@hyperframes/core`: a positive `data-duration` closes the host at `start + duration`; `data-end` applies only when `data-duration` is absent or non-positive, and only when it lies past the host start.

## Why

The compiler only stamps `data-end` on media tags, so a host authored with just `data-duration` was unbounded for the media planner. Audio and video nested in a shortened scene kept playing over the next scene (#3964).

The first cut of this fix read `data-end` first and `data-duration` second, which is the reverse of the runtime's precedence (`resolveDurationForElement` in `packages/core/src/runtime/startResolver.ts`). It also treated `data-duration="0"` as a real duration, which collapsed the host window to its start and dropped every nested clip. Sharing the runtime's resolver instead of re-implementing the rule removes both divergences and the local `parseNumeric` copy (`parseFloat` vs the runtime's `Number` parsing).

## How

- `resolveHostEnd` returns `resolveAuthoredTimingWindow({ start, duration, end })?.end ?? null`.
- `resolveHostWindow` doc block rewritten to describe the shared rule.
- Tests in `renderMediaCollector.test.ts`:
  - host with `data-duration` and no `data-end` bounds nested media (including an id-ref `data-start`);
  - conflicting `data-start=2 data-duration=2 data-end=6` bounds nested media at 4 (duration wins);
  - `data-duration="0"` and `"-1"` are treated as absent: unbounded when there is no `data-end`, otherwise fall back to `data-end`; nested clips are not dropped;
  - `data-end` at or before the host start is ignored rather than collapsing the window.
- `htmlCompiler.test.ts`: the template-wrapped sub-composition test now expects the 4s clip to close with its 2s host (`end: 4`, was `6`).

## Verification

- `bun test packages/producer/src/services/renderMediaCollector.test.ts` — 7 pass.
- `bun test packages/producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.test.ts` — 135 pass.
- `bun run --cwd packages/producer typecheck` — clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the touched files.
- Mutation checks: reverting to end-first precedence fails the conflicting-attribute test; removing the non-positive guard fails both `it.each` cases; reading `data-end` raw fails the end-before-start test.

Closes #3964

Supersedes #3965 — carries valeriangalliat's fix verbatim with signed commits so it can merge under the repo's signed-commit ruleset; adds duration-first precedence to match the runtime and a non-positive-duration guard, with tests.

— Miga

title: fix(engine): preserve composition root background in alpha exports
body:
## Summary

`initTransparentBackground()` prepares a page for alpha capture (`webm`, `mov` ProRes 4444, `png-sequence`, and the HDR layered DOM pass). Because Chrome's default-background override does not beat author CSS, it also injects a stylesheet. That stylesheet forced `html`, `body` **and every `[data-composition-id]` element** to transparent, unconditionally.

Clearing composition roots is right for the HDR layered DOM pass, where the HDR video is the backdrop and the DOM layer may only contribute foreground pixels. For a plain alpha export it is wrong: a background the author painted on the composition root (or a nested sub-composition root) is real content, and it was silently dropped. A root `<div data-composition-id>` with `background: rgb(0,0,255)` rendered blue in mp4 but decoded as `rgba(0,0,0,0)` in webm.

## Fix

- `initTransparentBackground(page, { clearCompositionRoot })`: by default it clears only `html`/`body`; `clearCompositionRoot: true` also clears every `[data-composition-id]` element (top-level and nested).
- The only callers that pass `true` are the two HDR layered stages (`captureHdrStage`, `captureHdrHybridLoop`), which already call the helper explicitly right after `initializeSession()`. That explicit call is the single owner of the decision; the engine's internal calls (for `png` capture sessions) use the default. No new `CaptureOptions` field.
- The injected `<style>` is rewritten on a repeat call instead of insert-once. This is load-bearing: when an HDR layered session captures `png` (alpha output with layered shader transitions), the engine's internal call runs first with the default, and the stage's explicit `clearCompositionRoot: true` call must win.

Behaviour change to note: an alpha export whose composition root paints a full-frame background now comes out opaque, as authored. None of the alpha regression fixtures (`webm-transparency`, `distributed/{webm-vp9,mov-prores,png-sequence}`) paint a root background, so their baselines are unaffected.

## Known exception

A webm, mov or png-sequence export that uses shader transitions still renders through the HDR layered stage, which clears the composition root on purpose (the layer must carry only foreground pixels). Such an export still comes out transparent where the root painted. mp4, gif and hls shader transitions composite in the page and keep the root background.

## Test plan

- 3 unit tests in `packages/engine/src/services/screenshotService.test.ts`: default clears only `html`/`body`; `clearCompositionRoot: true` adds `[data-composition-id]`; a later call replaces the earlier rule. 35/35 pass. Mutation checks: with the old helper the first test fails (`expected 'html,body,[data-composition-id]{backg…' to contain 'html,body{'`); with insert-once restored the third test fails.
- New fixture `transparency-regression-root-bg` plus a `root-bg` check in `transparency-test.ts` (renders webm, asserts the root's blue survives as opaque and the red card still renders). Ran on Linux: passes at this head; with the old helper it fails with `root-bg: pixel (10,10) expected fully opaque (alpha=255), got rgba(0,0,0,0)`.
- HDR layered behaviour is unchanged (root backgrounds still cleared there); the `hdr-regression` fixture in the regression shards covers it.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in `packages/engine` and `packages/producer`; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on touched files.

title: fix(cli): strip the scaffolded <audio> placeholder for a silent video
body:
## Summary

`hyperframes init --video <file>` scaffolds the bundled `from-file` template, which contains both a `<video src="__VIDEO_SRC__">` placeholder and an `<audio id="a-roll-audio" src="__VIDEO_SRC__">` placeholder. `probeVideo()` (shells to ffprobe) already detects whether the supplied video has an audio track — but that result was only ever used for a console log, never passed to the function that patches the placeholders. For a video with no audio stream, the scaffolded `<audio>` element ends up pointing at a silent source, which fails the very next render at compile time (the compiler rejects a scaffolded element whose authored type doesn't match what its source actually contains). The failure isn't obvious from the `init` output — it only surfaces on the next command.

## Fix

- Thread the probed `hasAudio` result through `scaffoldProject()` into `patchVideoSrc()`.
- When a video has no audio track, strip its `<audio>` placeholder the same way the existing "no media supplied at all" branch already strips both placeholders — factored the shared regex pair into one `stripPlaceholderMediaElement(content, tag)` helper instead of adding a third copy.
- Fixed a latent edge case surfaced during review: the ffprobe-unavailable fallback defaulted `hasAudio` to `false`. "Couldn't probe" isn't the same fact as "confirmed no audio track" — with the flag now wired up, that default would have silently stripped the audio placeholder even for a real video with audio, on any machine without ffprobe on `PATH`. Flipped the fallback to `true` (matches the previous, safe behavior in that specific case) so only a positive no-audio detection ever removes the element.

## Test plan

- New negative case: a silent (video-only, no audio stream) source generated with ffmpeg — asserts the `<video>` element is still wired up correctly but the `<audio id="a-roll-audio">` placeholder is gone.
- New positive control: a real video with an audio track — asserts the `<audio>` placeholder is kept, so the negative case can't be passing for an unrelated reason (e.g. a hardcoded strip).
- Both verified with a real revert-and-restore: reverting the fix makes the negative case fail with the audio element present; reverting to an unconditional strip makes the positive control fail with the audio element missing.
- `packages/cli`: `init.test.ts` 29/29 passing. `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` clean on both touched files.

title: fix(skills): stage a preset's own fonts/ folder in every build-frame.mjs
body:
## What

Every workflow's `build-frame.mjs` (faceless-explainer, pr-to-video, product-launch-video) now stages a frame preset's own `fonts/` folder into `assets/fonts/` and appends one `@font-face` block to `frame.md`, covering both font sources (captured brand files + preset files). The filename → face helpers move into a shared `scripts/lib/font-faces.mjs`, byte-identical across the three skills and consumed by both `build-frame.mjs` and `captions.mjs`.

Refs #3583 (the media-use font-resolver half of that issue stays open).

Supersedes #3950 — carries srikarsunchu's change with signed commits so it can merge under the repo's signed-commit ruleset, plus: repo-oxfmt formatting, captions.mjs now imports the shared font-faces library instead of a hand copy, overlapping-family test, isFile guard.

## Why

`code-editorial` ships licensed WOFF2 files and its `FRAME.md` promises they are staged. Only the pr-to-video copy did so, with the six filenames hard-coded and a hard exit for any other preset shipping a `fonts/` folder; the other two copies never read the folder. A frame worker following `font_family_without_font_face` then found no file behind the preset's families and fell back to a system stack.

## How

- `lib/font-faces.mjs` (new, ×3 identical): `FONT_FORMAT`, `normFontName`, `fontExtOf`, `fontWeightInfo`, `fontStyleOf`, `fontFamiliesNamed`, `rankFontFamilies` (longest family key first — the one ranking the brand block, `stagePresetFonts` and `captions.mjs` all use), `familyOfFaceFile`, `stageFontFile`, `stagePresetFonts`.
- `stagePresetFonts` is directory-driven: each plain file (`statSync(...).isFile()` in a try/catch, so a subdirectory or dangling symlink named like a font cannot reach `copyFileSync` and throw `EISDIR`/`ENOENT`) is assigned to the longest family the remixed `frame.md` still names whose key its stem starts with (`familyOfFaceFile`; a brand renamed to "Garamond" does not claim `EBGaramond-400.woff2`); files matching no named family are reported as skipped ("matching no family frame.md names"); faces the brand already staged are not staged twice (`stagedFaces` is shared across both sources and keyed on family + numeric weight + style, so `Inter-Regular.ttf` from the capture and `Inter-400.woff2` from the preset are one face — first source wins); staged bytes are refreshed from the source only for the preset's `fonts/` folder (`stageFontFile({ refresh: true })`; a skills update may ship re-subsetted files), skipping only a self-copy, while a capture file never overwrites a file already at its staged path, so a hand-placed face in `assets/fonts/` keeps winning over the download; `OFL-*`/`LICENSE*` texts travel with any staged face.
- `build-frame.mjs`: the brand block calls `stageFontFile`; the preset block calls `stagePresetFonts`; one `## Font loading (auto-generated)` section lists both sources. The brand scan's "single family owns every file" shortcut now applies only to `capture/assets/fonts` (hash-named downloads); files already in `assets/fonts/` follow the staged-name contract and are matched by family-key prefix, because a previous run may have put the preset's faces there and a rerun after brand tokens arrive must not relabel EB Garamond's bytes as the brand font. pr-to-video drops its hard-coded six-file list and the `die()` on a missing file — a preset folder is now read as-is, so a missing file simply is not staged (this is the intended change: the hard exit fired for any other preset shipping a `fonts/` folder).
- `captions.mjs` (×3 identical): `brandFontFaces` imports weight/style/format/key helpers from `./lib/font-faces.mjs`; the private `weightOf`/`styleOf`/`fmtOf`/`norm` copies are deleted. Behaviour unchanged (the old `fmtOf` "opentype" fallback was unreachable behind the extension gate).
- `code-editorial/FRAME.md` notes that families the brand remix replaced are skipped.
- Formatted with the repo-pinned oxfmt (`bunx oxfmt --check` passes on all changed `.mjs`); `skills-manifest.json` regenerated.

## Tests

- `build-frame-fonts.test.mjs` (new, ×3; tmp dirs removed in `test.after`): staging by family/weight/style from a fake preset; remix-replaced family skipped; brand-staged face not re-staged from the preset; preset without `fonts/` stages nothing; shipped `code-editorial` stages six faces + three OFL texts; `fontFamiliesNamed`, `fontWeightInfo`, `stageFontFile` units; **overlapping families** "Inter" + "Inter Tight" → `InterTight-700.woff2` lands on "Inter Tight", `Inter-400.woff2` on "Inter" (fails with the length sort reversed); **directory entry / dangling symlink** named like a font is neither staged nor a crash (fails with the `isFile` guard removed, `EISDIR`; fails with the try/catch removed, `ENOENT`); **word-vs-numeric dedup** across sources (`OtherMono-Bold.woff2` captured + `OtherMono-700.woff2` preset → one file, one rule; fails with the dedup keyed on the weight token); **stale bytes refreshed** by `stageFontFile` with `refresh: true` and left alone without it (fails with the flag ignored either way); **capture keeps a staged file** end-to-end (`brand-grotesk-400.woff2` captured vs a pre-existing `BrandGrotesk-400.woff2`; fails with the capture source refreshing); **preset refresh** end-to-end on a rerun after the staged bytes went stale (fails with `stagePresetFonts` not passing the flag); **hash-named capture file** `19cfc7226ec3afaa-s.woff2` staged as the single brand family and **two brand families** told apart by substring on CDN-style names (both fail with the capture rule replaced by the staged-name prefix rule); **rerun after brand tokens** does not relabel staged preset faces (brand "Sans" vs staged `AcmeSans-*`; fails with the shortcut applied to `assets/fonts` or with substring matching); **substring family** ("Tight" owns neither `Inter-400` nor `InterTight-700`); font-faces.mjs byte-identity across the three skills.
- `captions.test.mjs` (×3): style-token check now targets `lib/font-faces.mjs`, restores the negative "must not assert `font-style:normal`" check, and asserts `captions.mjs` imports its helpers from the library (replacing the import with a stub fails the round-trip tests).
- `env -u NODE_ENV node --test "skills/**/*.test.mjs"`: 684/687 pass; the single failure (`media-use/scripts/resolve.test.mjs`) is a missing `@hyperframes/parsers/dist` build in a fresh clone and fails identically on `main`.
- `bunx tsx scripts/lint-skills.ts` clean; `bunx oxlint` 0 warnings on the 15 changed `.mjs`; `bun packages/cli/scripts/gen-skills-manifest.ts --check` in sync.

— Miga

title: fix(lint): error on digit-leading ids only when a selector targets them
body:
## Summary

An element `id` that starts with a digit (e.g. `id="1-hook"`) makes the bare selector `#1-hook` invalid: `querySelector()` and GSAP string targets throw a `SyntaxError` at runtime, which aborts the rest of that inline `<script>` while the render still reports success. `id_requires_css_escape` already flagged every digit-leading id, but only as a `"warning"`, so `hyperframes check` passed.

An id that no selector names is harmless, though: `getElementById`, `url(#id)` and `href="#id"` all work with it. Erroring on every digit-leading id would fail `check` on valid compositions.

## Fix

`id_requires_css_escape` now reports `"error"` only when the composition itself uses an unescaped `#<id>` selector for that id, and stays a `"warning"` otherwise. A selector counts when it appears in:

- a CSS rule selector in a `<style>` block (parsed with the `postcss` and `postcss-selector-parser` already used by the CSS selector-safety rule in `core.ts`; declarations such as `url(#id)` and colours are not selectors), or
- the first string argument of `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll`, `closest`, `matches`, or a GSAP `to`/`from`/`fromTo`/`set` call in an inline script (comments stripped with the existing `stripJsComments`).

Ids are matched as whole selector tokens, so `#1-frame-2` does not count for `id="1-frame"`. Escaped selectors (`#\31 -frame`, `` `#${CSS.escape(id)}` ``) are valid and do not count.

`hyperframes check` fails on any `"error"` finding, so a composition that actually selects a digit-leading id now fails the pre-render gate. `hyperframes render` blocks on errors only under `--strict`, as before.

## Test plan

- `core.test.ts`: a table test for the rule covering a CSS selector, a GSAP string target and a `querySelector` string (error), and an unused id, `url(#id)`, a longer id, `getElementById`, an escaped CSS selector, an escaped script selector and `CSS.escape` (warning). File result: 94 passed.
- Mutation checks, each run against the test: always-warning fails 3 cases; dropping the CSS scan fails the CSS case; dropping the script scan fails the GSAP and `querySelector` cases; prefix instead of exact id match fails the longer-id case; ignoring escapes fails the escaped CSS case; counting any id-like string in a lookup call fails the `getElementById` case.
- `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/lint`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on both files: clean.

## Size

About 80 changed lines across two files: one rule's severity decision, one helper that collects selector-targeted ids, and the table test. Nothing else needed to change.

title: fix(engine): recover audio duration by decoding the final frame
body:
## Summary
- An authored `data-duration` on an `<audio>` element could be silently shortened when a source file's container-summary duration (`mvhd`/`tkhd`/`mdhd`) undercounts the real audio length while the underlying audio frames are intact.
- Replaces the old AAC-LC-only packet-count refinement inside `extractAudioMetadata` (a profile allowlist assuming a fixed 1024-samples-per-frame constant) with a single, codec-agnostic mechanism: decode the final audio frame via ffprobe and read its own timestamp plus real sample count. This has no per-codec assumption, so every caller of `extractAudioMetadata` benefits uniformly, not just one call site.
- The corrected duration is used when it exceeds the container's own summary by more than a small margin (absorbing a few milliseconds of edit-list/priming-delay drift that's normal even on an honest file). For every container except raw ADTS the correction only goes up: a shorter decode there can be an MP4 edit list trimming the tail, which must not be undone.
- Start time: the decoded frame timestamp is absolute, while the container duration is measured from the stream start. The decoded end now subtracts the audio stream's `start_time` (falling back to the format's, else 0), and the tail read starts at `start + duration - 1 s`, the same shape as the final-video-frame probe in the same file. Without this, MPEG-TS audio (1.4 s default start) and `-output_ts_offset` MP4s came out longer by their start time: a 10 s TS read as 11.431 s (41.408 s with a 30 s offset), a 10 s offset M4A as 12.007 s. Now 10.031 s and 10.023 s.
- Raw ADTS (`format_name` `aac`): the format has no duration field, so ffprobe estimates one from the opening bitrate, which overclaims after a quiet opening (the case the old packet-count refinement covered). ADTS frame timestamps are counted in samples from the first frame, both after a tail seek and in a full scan, so for raw ADTS the decoded end now wins in both directions beyond the margin. Measured with ffprobe 8.1.1: 1 s silence + 9 s tone (24 kHz mono, 64k) claims 13.970 s, now 10.069 s; 1.5 s silence + 8.5 s noise (44.1 kHz, 128k) claims 244.477 s, now 10.031 s; 8 s silence + 2 s noise (VBR) claims 110.800 s, now 10.031 s. All three match main.
- The decode probe reads CSV output and retains only its tail under a small size cap — a lying container's true duration can be arbitrarily larger than its declared one, so an unbounded scan of a long file could otherwise exceed ffprobe's stdout limit and silently fall back to the wrong duration; CSV (unlike JSON) stays parseable when truncated from the front.
- Fixes a stale regression-suite golden fixture (`style-7-prod`) whose expected `data-duration` value came from the OLD, now-deleted AAC-LC packet-count mechanism's own bug: it counted one demuxed packet that never actually decodes into a real audio frame, overcounting duration by that phantom frame's worth of samples. Verified against the real source file via raw PCM sample count, and confirmed via a standalone compile-and-validate sweep that no other audio-bearing fixture in the repo needed the same correction.
- Regenerates the `speed-ramp` golden video. The mixed AAC now probes as its true 4.000 s instead of the old packet count's 4.032 s, so the pad/trim step stream-copies the mix instead of re-encoding it once more. Same waveform as the old golden (sample-level correlation 0.9996), 3.1 dB less true-peak attenuation, all 120 video frames byte-identical. The fixture's envelope-correlation gate reads a constant-level sweep, so one encode generation less moved it from 1.000 to 0.457.
- Performance: the decode probe now seeks to ~1 second before the container's already-known claimed end via `-read_intervals`, decoding only that tail instead of the entire file — every `extractAudioMetadata` caller pays this cost (once per audio element during HTML compilation, plus audio mixing/padding/encoding steps), and a full decode of a long file could itself take several seconds. Falls back to a full unseeked decode if the tail read finds no frames, which protects files whose seek index is unreliable (e.g. an index-less or non-seekably-sourced container) from silently missing a real correction.
- `packages/producer/src/services/render/audioPadTrim.ts` has a comment-only update describing the new mechanism; no behavior change there.

## Test plan
- Unit tests for the decode-based correction covering: normal correction, staying within the margin (no correction), no decodable frames, zero sample rate (probe skipped), decode-probe failure/malformed output (swallowed, container duration kept), an aborted signal during the decode probe (rethrown), and the tail-seek-then-full-decode fallback (a seeked read that finds nothing falls back to a full scan before giving up).
- A real-fixture regression test using two small, committed binary fixtures (an honest FLAC-in-MP4 file and a byte-identical copy with its `mvhd`/`tkhd`/`mdhd` duration atoms halved while every real frame stays intact). The real-file tests use the `ffprobe` on PATH and are skipped where none exists; the `Test (runtime)` CI job installs a pinned static FFmpeg before running the engine suite, so they run in CI.
- Two more real fixtures, about 10 KB each, made with ffmpeg: 2 s of AAC in MPEG-TS starting at 1.4 s (expects 2.112 s, not 3.512 s), and 2 s of silence + 1 s of noise as raw ADTS that ffprobe claims is about 9.1 s long (expects 3.072 s). Mock-level cases cover the stream and format start-time fallback and the tail read interval, a shorter decode trusted for ADTS but not for MP4, and a decode listing longer than the stdout cap (pins the tail-retaining read). The five new start-time and ADTS cases fail on the previous head and pass with the fix.
- Verified this test's discriminating power directly against the prior code, not just the current one: substituted the actual pre-existing file content and confirmed the test genuinely fails against it (reports the halved duration), then confirmed it passes against the current fix.
- Manually reproduced and confirmed the fix on a real ~33-minute file with a patched (halved) container duration — the boundary case where an earlier JSON-based decode probe exceeded ffprobe's stdout cap and silently failed to correct; the CSV-based version correctly recovers the true duration.
- The `style-7-prod` golden fix was verified three ways: raw PCM ground-truth arithmetic against the real source file, a full local compilation + visual + audio comparison against the real (LFS-hosted) golden video, and a standalone compile-and-validate sweep across every audio-bearing fixture suite in the repo confirming no other golden needed the same correction.
- `speed-ramp`: with main's `ffprobe.ts` mounted into the same test image the old golden passes (1.000); with this branch it reads 0.457. Regenerated through `docker:test:update`, then 3 consecutive non-update runs at 1.000. Pitch at each of the 99 visual checkpoints follows the rate lane's source time as closely as the old golden (median error 0.19% vs 0.18%).
- Full producer + engine test suites run clean (only pre-existing, environment-specific failures remain: LFS-pointer-fixture tests and one ffmpeg negative-timestamp MPEG-TS quirk, both unrelated to this change).

title: fix(cli): reject a swallowed --json when catalog's string flags have no value
body:
## Summary

`catalog --query --json` (a missing `--query` value) silently parsed as `query: "--json"`, `json: false` instead of erroring. citty's parser (`node:util.parseArgs`, `strict: false`) consumes the next argv token as a `type: "string"` option's value, even when that token is another declared flag. A consumer piping stdout got a human-readable table instead of JSON, with exit code 0.

Control case keeps working: `catalog --query "kinetic type" --json` still emits parseable JSON on stdout.

## Fix

`guardSwallowedFlagValues(cmd, path, rawArgs)` in `packages/cli/src/utils/reject-unknown-flags.ts` scans the raw argv for a string/enum flag followed by `--` or by a spelling of one of the command's own flags, and fails with `Missing value for --<flag>: ... use --<flag>= or move --<flag> to the end`. It scans raw argv because the parsed args cannot tell `--query --json` from the legitimate `--query=--json`.

The guard is shared: `wrapCommand` in `packages/cli/src/utils/command-failure-tracking.ts` runs it for every leaf command right after the existing unknown-flag check, so every command's string flags get the protection, not just catalog's. Two commands keep their documented behaviour through per-path exceptions:

- `check --frame-check` is documented to work bare or followed by another flag. The guard rewrites a bare `--frame-check` to `--frame-check=` and re-parses the args, replacing check's own raw-args preprocessing.
- `upgrade --project` already recovers a swallowed value itself, so the guard skips it.

The exceptions are keyed by full command path, so `skills check` does not inherit check's rewrite. The error is printed once and marked as presented, so `--json` callers get an empty stdout instead of a usage dump. `init --example`'s hand-rolled check is removed in favour of the shared one.

Behaviour notes:
- citty drops every `--no-<flag>` before parsing, so the guard looks past them: `--output --no-docker --json` is rejected naming `--json`, a trailing `--output --no-docker` is fine, and check rewrites `--frame-check --no-browser-gpu <dir>` to `--frame-check=` as before.
- The error tells a value-taking flag to pass a value (`--output <value>` or `--output=<value>`); check's `--frame-check` keeps its "use `--frame-check=`" hint.
- Under `--json`, a swallowed-value error now goes to stderr with empty stdout and exit 1, the same as an unknown flag. Scripts that parsed a JSON error object from stdout for this case (e.g. `check --json --layout --strict`) get nothing on stdout now.

## Test plan

- `reject-unknown-flags.test.ts`: the swallow is rejected; the equals form, an unrecognised dash value, a trailing bare flag and boolean args are accepted; `--` gets its own wording; check's rewrite, upgrade's skip and the path scoping each have a case; end-to-end through citty's real `runCommand` and the real `wrapCommand` (the reported `catalog --query --json` repro, a positional ahead of the flags, nested `skills check`); stdout stays empty on the built CLI.
- `check.test.ts`: a dash-prefixed `--frame-check` value fails once, not twice, and `--json` after a `--layout` value is no longer swallowed.
- `reject-unknown-flags`, `command-failure-tracking`, `check` and `init` test files pass 3 runs in a row; breaking the upgrade skip or the re-parse fails the matching tests.

title: Avoid duplicate Codex skill discovery when the universal skills store is already populated
body:
## Summary

The global installation mirror can expose the same skill twice to a Codex host that discovers both `.agents/skills` and `.codex/skills`. This report concerns the upstream mirror implementation and a synthetic reproduction; it contains no private installation inventory.

## Verified source and reproduction

Current upstream `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.ts` declares `UNIVERSAL_STORE_READERS = new Set(["pi"])`; the generated agent table maps Codex to `codexHome/skills`. `mirrorGlobalSkills` skips universal readers but not Codex. After installing real copies into the Claude and universal stores, the CLI calls its mirror step, creating Codex symlinks into the Claude store. This matches the observed filesystem. No private machine data is needed to reproduce it.

In a disposable HOME, create Claude and universal copies of one published skill plus a Codex home; invoke `mirrorGlobalSkills`. Observe a redundant Codex link. The existing Pi exemption provides a reusable implementation pattern.

## Files to change

- `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.ts`: skip redundant Codex mirrors after verifying supported Codex discovery, including custom CODEX_HOME.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.test.ts`: add isolated-HOME regression cases and preservation controls. Run `bun test packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.test.ts` from the repository root.

## Acceptance criteria and verification

- [ ] Install/update does not create a second copy for Codex versions that discover the universal store.
- [ ] Repeated updates preserve Claude/universal bytes and produce no duplicate discovery.
- [ ] Preserve `.codex/skills/.system`, unrelated skills, divergent same-name entries and non-Codex mirrors.
- [ ] Any migration only unlinks positively identified installer-owned mirrors; it never deletes arbitrary real directories.
- [ ] Focused skillsMirror tests fail before the fix and pass afterward, including custom-home and existing alias-safety cases.

This is distinct from the previously fixed unrelated-skill deletion issue: the remaining defect is duplicate discovery. Confirm exact host/version support before broadening the universal-reader exemption.

Related prior work: [heygen-com/hyperframes#3294](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues/3294) fixed the Pi case. This is a separate Codex follow-on building on that closed fix, not a request to duplicate or reopen Pi's implementation.

<!-- hyperframes-triage-followup:2026-09-23 -->
## Triage follow-up — September 23, 2026

Ownership overlap: this issue has an assignment request from Erebuzzz, while #4105 by lorenzozanee already implements the Codex exclusion. The issue is currently unassigned. Coordinate with the existing PR before accepting a second implementation; this triage pass makes no assignment.

Scope inspected at PR head `dabb513f0f5a76aa5b0505ff31efba7141c10df9`: it adds Codex to the universal-reader set and tests default/custom home preservation. It leaves existing Codex entries untouched, so legacy duplicate cleanup is not implemented.

The exclusion is unconditional, although the description says “when the universal store is available.” Current `skills.ts` installs Claude and universal copies and invokes the mirror after installation. Verify those caller guarantees, supported Codex discovery, and any partial-install cases during review before treating the wording difference as a bug. No private installation data is needed. Current-head tests and host compatibility were not verified in this pass; keep this in triage.

title: fix(cli): hide console windows on Windows for background/detached spawns
body:
## Summary
Adds `windowsHide: true` to the spawns on the preview and background-server path that origin/main still leaves without it:

- `preview.ts` `runDevMode`: the `bun run dev` studio dev server.
- `preview.ts` `runLocalStudioMode`: the local Vite studio server.
- `studio-server` `loudness.ts` `measureAudio`: the ffmpeg loudness measurement behind Studio's "Normalize loudness", which runs inside the background preview server.
- `init.ts` `transcodeToMp4`: the ffmpeg transcode, matching the other ffmpeg spawns on main.

A background preview runs without a console (`DETACHED_PROCESS`). Any console child it spawns without `windowsHide` gets a new, visible console window on Windows for as long as that child runs.

With the flag, the studio dev server sits in its own hidden console. Closing the terminal now signals only the CLI wrapper, with SIGHUP. `waitForStudioChildClose` handled only SIGINT and SIGTERM, so the wrapper would die and leave the dev server running, still holding the port. It now handles SIGHUP the same way, killing the process tree, as render cancellation already does.

The remaining CLI spawns without the flag are foreground-only and share the user's console, so they cannot open a window (for example `portUtils.ts` netstat, `optionalPackages.ts` npm, `skills.ts` npx). This follows the existing pattern: main sets the flag at each call site (#3839, #4604). There is no shared spawn wrapper these sites could route through. `runCancellableProcess` buffers output and waits for exit, so it cannot run a long-lived streaming dev server.

## Dropped from the original change
- Telemetry `flushSync`, `psnr.ts`, `psnrFilterAvailability.ts` and `audioPadTrim.ts` already have the flag on main (#3839, #4604).
- `openBrowser.ts`: Node maps `windowsHide` to libuv `UV_PROCESS_WINDOWS_HIDE`. That flag also sets `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` with `wShowWindow = SW_HIDE` (libuv `src/win/process.c`), so a browser started this way can open hidden. A browser is a GUI app and never gets a console, so the flag only adds that risk.
- `previewLifecycle.ts`: the background preview child redirects its stdio to a log fd. libuv therefore skips `CREATE_NO_WINDOW`, and `DETACHED_PROCESS` already leaves the child without a console, so the flag would do nothing.

## Test plan
- `preview.test.ts`: `runDevMode` and `runLocalStudioMode` pass `windowsHide: true` to `spawn`, and `waitForStudioChildClose` registers and removes a SIGHUP handler.
- `init.transcodeToMp4.windowsHide.test.ts` and `loudness.windowsHide.test.ts`: the ffmpeg spawns pass `windowsHide: true`.
- Each test fails when its fix is removed.

title: fix(engine): classify a single-keyframe video as problematic, not healthy
body:
## Summary
- `analyzeKeyframeIntervals` (used only by an advisory compile-time warning for sparse-keyframe videos) returned `isProblematic: false` whenever a video had fewer than 2 detected keyframes — but exactly one keyframe is the worst case for seek performance, not the healthy one: every seek past frame 0 must decode the entire file. A library scan found dozens of single-GOP files (a few seconds to ~10s each) silently skipping this check.
- The new single-keyframe branch treats the remaining span of the video stream's own duration as one uninterrupted GOP and flags it against the same >2s threshold already used for the multi-keyframe case (now a single named constant instead of a literal repeated in two branches).
- Callers must now pass the video stream's own duration/start (`VideoMetadata.videoStreamDurationSeconds`/`videoStreamStartSeconds`), not a container-level duration — a container whose audio track outlasts a short video track would otherwise overstate the GOP span. ffprobe's frame timestamps are absolute presentation timestamps rather than relative to stream start, so a re-muxed/trimmed clip with a nonzero start time is normalized the same way the sibling function `extractFinalVideoFrameTimestamp` already does for the same quirk — including matching its cache-key convention (keyed by file + start + duration, not file alone), so a future caller passing a different duration for the same file can't silently collide with a stale cached result.
- The one production call site (`compileForRender`'s advisory video-check loop) now probes metadata first, then feeds its resolved duration/start into the keyframe check, rather than probing both independently in parallel.
- **Breaking change:** `analyzeKeyframeIntervals` is a public export of the published `@hyperframes/engine` package. Its signature changes from a single `filePath` argument to `(filePath, metadata)`, with `metadata` required (not optional) — any external caller of this function needs to pass a `{videoStreamDurationSeconds, videoStreamStartSeconds}` object alongside the path. The parameter is intentionally required rather than optional-with-a-fallback: an optional param would recreate the dormant "healthy by default" path this fix exists to close.
- The duplicated stream-window normalization (start fallback, finite guard, cache-key format) that `extractFinalVideoFrameTimestamp` and `analyzeKeyframeIntervals` each computed independently is now a single shared helper, `resolveStreamWindow`, so the two can't drift out of sync with each other going forward.

## Test plan
- New regression tests: a single keyframe is flagged problematic; a single keyframe with a nonzero stream start is still correctly flagged (regression for the absolute-vs-relative timestamp bug); a single keyframe exactly at the 2s threshold stays healthy (strict `>`, not `>=`); a short single-keyframe video stays healthy; an unknown (NaN) duration doesn't propagate NaN into the result; a zero-keyframe video is unaffected.
- `packages/engine/src/utils/ffprobe.test.ts` and `packages/producer/src/services/mediaProbeConcurrency.test.ts` both pass (121 total, 117 passing) — the 4 failures are pre-existing, confirmed via `git stash` to reproduce identically on the unmodified base commit (an unrelated Git-LFS fixture that isn't fetched in this environment), not touched by this change.
- `typecheck` clean for both `packages/engine` and `packages/producer`.

title: fix(skills): bake a short edge fade into faceless-explainer voice clips
body:
## Summary
- Per-frame voice clips in the `faceless-explainer` skill's assembly script are placed back-to-back with zero gap by the cumulative-start layout (adjacent clips touch exactly, by construction — no true overlap is possible). Pre-fix they were mounted with no fade at all, producing a hard cut at both edges of every line and audible word-jumps/abrupt cuts at scene seams.
- `applyVoiceEdgeFade()` bakes an ~11ms fade-in and fade-out into each voice file before it's mounted, reusing the exact same ffprobe-then-ffmpeg shape and codec discipline (explicit PCM `.wav` output, not a smuggled container) that `ensureBgmCovers()` already uses for BGM's own loop-fade — no new/parallel fade mechanism introduced. The shared duration probe is now a single `probeDuration()` helper used by both.
- The fade-out is built as `afade=t=in,areverse,afade=t=in,areverse` rather than a computed `afade=t=out:st=<seek>`, so it always lands at the file's real end regardless of what the probe reported — it needs no absolute seek position derived from duration. The probe is still consulted for one thing only: sizing the short-clip half-duration clamp (a clip shorter than two fade windows gets a proportionally smaller fade on each edge, so it still fades smoothly instead of the two edges overlapping and over-attenuating the whole clip). That clamp does still trust the probed duration; documented in code as a real, currently-unreachable gap (voice clips here are always real WAV, not a compressed container with its own duration metadata that could lie).
- Degrades to the untouched clip (with an anomaly note in the assembly summary) when ffmpeg/ffprobe are unavailable, matching `ensureBgmCovers()`'s own degrade path — assembly never hard-fails on audio tooling.
- **Cost:** one ffprobe + one ffmpeg subprocess per voice clip in the assembly step (unchanged from the first version of this PR — the probe is still needed for the short-clip clamp, so it wasn't eliminated), each a fast audio-only pass over a few seconds of speech. For a typical video with a handful of narrated frames this adds on the order of a second or two of one-time assembly overhead — negligible next to the render pipeline's own screenshot/encode time, and it never runs per-render (only once at assembly).

## Test plan
- Test 1: generates a real constant-amplitude tone as a voice clip, assembles a project, and measures actual RMS level (via `ffmpeg astats`) at the start, middle, and end of the mounted clip — confirms both the start and the end read markedly quieter than the steady middle (a real fade-in and fade-out, not just one side).
- Test 2: a clip shorter than two fade windows asserts the actual level shape (start/end well below the clip's own midpoint) rather than only checking output duration — the duration-only version of this test passed even against the unfaded original, so it wasn't a real regression test.
- Both tests confirmed genuinely RED against the pre-fix code (reverted the source to `origin/main`, kept the new tests, got real assertion failures, e.g. `start -20.7 dB vs mid -21.5 dB`) and GREEN after the fix, verified locally via `node --test`.
- **CI note:** the `Test: skills` job (`ci.yml`) currently has no ffmpeg on its runner, so these two tests (and the pre-existing bgm loop-fade test) currently `{ skip: !HAS_FFMPEG }` in CI even though they run and pass locally. Adding `- uses: ./.github/actions/install-ffmpeg-linux` to that job (the step `producer-source-tests` already uses) is a separate change; until it lands, the RED-then-GREEN verification below is local-only.
- Full existing `assemble-index.test.mjs` suite (6 tests) passes with no regressions.
- `oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean on all touched files.

title: fix(media-use): reconcile disk-only narration WAVs into the audio ledger
body:
## Summary
- A narration WAV can land in `assets/voice/<id>.wav` without ever going through this engine's own TTS synthesis loop: hand-placed, copied over from another project, or left behind by a run that wrote the file but didn't finish registering it. `audio_meta.json`'s `voices[]` only ever grows inside that synthesis loop, so a file like this was invisible to every consumer that trusts `voices[]` (each workflow's `assemble-index.mjs` `<audio>` emission, `captions.mjs`) — the render succeeds and simply plays without that narration line, with zero warning.
- `skills/media-use/audio/scripts/audio.mjs` is the one shared engine backing this (its own header: "ONE implementation... workflows do NOT vendor a copy"), used by `product-launch-video`, `faceless-explainer`, and `pr-to-video`. Added a reconciliation step there — the single correct fix location — that scans `assets/voice/` on every invocation (independent of `--only`, so a bgm/sfx-only re-run still catches drift) and backfills any file whose id isn't already known but is still requested by the current script with non-empty text. A stale file from a since-edited or since-cleared line is left alone, not resurrected.
- Placed before the existing `hasVoice`/`totalDuration` computation so a reconciled voice correctly participates in the BGM sizing/retrieval decision downstream, not just the final ledger output.
- Extracted the "does this line have real text" check (previously only inline in the synthesis loop) into a shared `lineText()` helper so the two call sites can't drift on that decision.

## Test plan
- New test file with 5 cases, spawning the real engine script end-to-end (no mocks): a disk-only WAV gets backfilled with a real ffprobe-read duration; an already-registered voice isn't duplicated; a WAV with no matching current script line is left alone; a WAV for a line whose text was since cleared is left alone; a project with no `assets/voice/` directory is an unaffected no-op.
- Confirmed genuine RED on the unmodified code (2 of the 5 cases fail with 0 backfilled voices instead of 1), then GREEN after restoring the fix.
- All 5 tests pass locally where ffmpeg/ffprobe are on PATH. In the `Test: skills` CI job specifically (no ffmpeg on that runner), these 5 tests currently `{skip: !HAS_FFMPEG}`, the same as the pre-existing BGM loop-fade test in this same skill — a pre-existing gap in that job's own design, not something introduced by this change.
- All 3 consuming workflows' own test suites (194 tests) and the full `media-use` test tree (351 tests) pass with no regressions.

title: player: window.__hf from @hyperframes/shader-transitions makes an src embed reject its own composition
body:
### Summary `` treats the mere existence of `window.__hf` in the composition frame as "the core runtime is present". But `@hyperframes/shader-transitions` — the sibling package, at the same version — creates that global itself at the end of `HyperShader.init()`: ```js // @hyperframes/shader-transitions 0.8.41, dist/index.global.js let gr = window; return gr.__hf = gr.__hf || {}, gr.__hf.shaderTransitionsReady = Qo, ... ``` So any composition that uses shader transitions **and** registers its own timeline (`window.__timelines`) — i.e. an authored GSAP composition, not one bundled by the CLI — can never be played through the player when loaded with `src`. The probe: 1. sees `hasRuntime = !!(win.__hf || win.__player)` → `true`, so it **never injects the runtime** (`we()` returns false); and 2. `hasRuntimeBridge()` → `true`, so `_resolveDirectTimelineAdapterFromWindow()` returns `null` and the direct-timeline adapter is refused. Nothing is ever resolved, and 8 s later the element emits `error: "Composition timeline not found after 8s"`. The frame stays black. `window.__hf` is a namespace, not a bridge — shader-transitions only ever *augments* it (it polls for `window.__hf.seek` and warns "the engine bridge did not initialize" when the core runtime is absent). title: feat(engine): sub-frame multi-sample motion blur for rotation, scale and opacity
body:
## Summary

The motion blur catalog component (#4008) integrates an element's **translation** over the shutter window: it reads the element's position at the start and end of the window and stacks N equal-weight copies along that path. That matches a 180 degree shutter reference within a pixel for elements that move across the frame.

It cannot blur change that is not a position change inside the same frame:

- rotation during the shutter window (a spinning logo has crisp edges),
- scale changes (a zoom pop has no radial smear),
- opacity ramps and colour changes,
- anything driven by a filter, clip-path, or child animation rather than a transform on the blurred element.

After Effects handles all of these with one mechanism: the layer is re-rendered at several sub-frame times inside the shutter window and the results are averaged.

## Proposal

Add an engine-level accumulation mode to frame capture: for each output frame, seek the timeline to K sub-frame positions spread over the shutter window (default 180 degrees, phase -90 degrees, K configurable), capture each, and average the captures into the output frame.

- Opt-in per composition (root attribute, for example `data-motion-blur-samples="8"` and `data-shutter-angle="180"`), default off so render cost is unchanged for existing projects.
- Reuse the existing seek plumbing: the timeline is already sought per frame; this is K seeks per frame followed by a blend.
- Blend in linear light or at least document that the blend is in sRGB, so results match the component's behaviour.
- Preview/Studio can show the effect at a lower K or disable it, the way HDR preview already degrades.

## Acceptance

- A spinning element renders with radial smear proportional to angular velocity; a scaling element renders with a radial zoom smear; an opacity ramp renders as the integrated opacity over the window.
- A translation-only composition rendered with the engine mode matches the catalog component output within the tolerance measured in #4008.
- Render time scales linearly with K and is unchanged when the mode is off.

## Context

The catalog component stays as the cheap default for moving elements. The engine mode is what makes AE-style blur complete for rotation, scale, and fades, which are the cases people currently call "impossible on the web".

title: [Windows] Visible console window per render shot: 0.8.44 resolves @puppeteer/browsers 3.2.1, where detached defeats windowsHide (fixed upstream in 3.2.2)
body:
## Summary

On Windows, every `hyperframes render` opens a visible console window per browser launch (78 shots = 78 windows), stealing focus and making the machine unusable for anything else during a render.

This is **not** one of the `windowsHide` gaps already tracked in #3476 / #3500 / #3851 / #3960 / #3996 — those all cover hyperframes' own spawns. This one comes from `@puppeteer/browsers`, and it is already fixed upstream. `0.8.44` just resolves to the one broken version.

## Root cause

`hyperframes@0.8.44` declares `"puppeteer-core": "^25.8.0"`. In practice that resolved here to `puppeteer-core@25.9.0` → `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.1`.

`@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.1` `lib/launch.js` spawns the browser with **both** flags:

```js
opts.detached ??= true;          // line 157
...
childProcess.spawn(this.#executablePath, this.#args, {
  detached: opts.detached,       // line 173
  windowsHide: true,             // line 174
  ...
});
```

On Windows libuv ORs `DETACHED_PROCESS | CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP` (from `detached`) together with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (from `windowsHide`) into the `CreateProcessW` creation flags. Those are mutually exclusive: `DETACHED_PROCESS` wins, the child inherits no console, and `chrome-headless-shell.exe` — a console-subsystem binary (`IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_CUI`) — gets a freshly allocated, **visible** console. `windowsHide: true` is dead code in that combination.

Upstream: puppeteer/puppeteer#15410, introduced by #15339, reverted by #15415, **released in `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.2`**.

## Evidence

Controlled A/B on the same binary, same machine, only `detached` differs. External `EnumWindows` + `IsWindowVisible` monitor sampling at 25 ms:

```
MODE=detached  ({detached:true,  windowsHide:true})  browser procs=4  NEW visible windows=1  <- class=ConsoleWindowClass proc=chrome-headless-shell
MODE=hidden    ({detached:false, windowsHide:true})  browser procs=4  NEW visible windows=0
```

Live capture during an actual `hyperframes render`, before any workaround:

```
class=CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  proc=WindowsTerminal
class=PseudoConsoleWindow            proc=chrome-headless-shell
class=CASCADIA_HOSTING_WINDOW_CLASS  proc=WindowsTerminal
class=PseudoConsoleWindow            proc=chrome-headless-shell
```

(There is a second, independent aggravating factor worth knowing about: when Windows' *Default terminal application* is **Windows Terminal** — the Windows 11 default — the console handoff ignores `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` entirely, so console children pop a real Windows Terminal window even where `windowsHide` is correctly set. Switching to Console Host removes that layer; the `@puppeteer/browsers` bug above survives the switch and still produces `ConsoleWindowClass` windows.)

## Environment

- Windows 11 Pro 26200, Node 24
- `hyperframes@0.8.44`, `puppeteer-core@25.9.0`, `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.1`
- Reproduced via `hyperframes render --quality high` and `hyperframes snapshot`

## Suggested fix

Require `puppeteer-core >= 25.10.0` (the first release that pulls `@puppeteer/browsers@3.2.2`). `^25.8.0` silently permits the one broken version. #3933 already bumps `@puppeteer/browsers` to 3.2.2 — this is the reason it matters on Windows.

## Workaround for anyone hitting this now

Patch the resolved copy in the npx cache, `@puppeteer/browsers/lib/launch.js`:

```js
- opts.detached ??= true;
+ opts.detached ??= process.platform !== 'win32';
```

Verified: renders run with zero new visible windows afterwards.

title: feat(engine): adaptive per-frame sample count for motion blur (floor 16, ceiling 64)
body:
## Summary

`data-motion-blur-samples` / `CaptureOptions.motionBlur.samplesPerFrame` (`packages/engine/src/services/motionBlur.ts:23,53,55,70-77`) is a fixed per-render sample count, default 16, ceiling 64 (`MAX_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME`). Measuring the shipped feature (v0.8.45) against the accuracy bar set in #4010 (72.4 dB mean PSNR vs. the 960fps shutter integral) shows the default does not universally clear it: it depends on the content's edge hardness and displacement.

## Measurements

Harness: an independent 128-sample reference per frame, built by hand (raw sub-frame `window.__hf.seek(t, {subframe, suppressEvents})` calls + screenshots, averaged with a standalone accumulator — not the production accumulation code). Validated before trusting it: the production K=16 output and a hand-rolled K=16 reference built the same way are byte-identical, confirming the harness measures the real pipeline rather than a stand-in.

Composition: a single 20px-wide opaque bar on a 1536x200 transparent canvas, 30fps, default shutter (180°, phase -90°).

1. **PSNR, moderate translation** (66.7 px/frame — the same displacement basis used for the original 72.4 dB number in #4008): default K=16 → **30.1 dB mean PSNR**, well under the bar. K=64 → **80.0 dB**, clears it comfortably.
2. **High-velocity** (1020 px/frame, matching the registry `motion-blur` example's fastest row): K=16 → **15 true zero-coverage gaps** across the swept region (the smear visibly breaks into separate copies). K=64 → **0 gaps** (fully continuous, resolved into a smear).
3. **At-rest**: blur on vs. off is byte-identical — stays pixel-sharp.

Cases 2 and 3 match the acceptance criteria from #4010 as written. Case 1 does not.

**Caveat**: this is one hard-edge synthetic frame, not the original multi-frame text composition that produced 72.4 dB. A sharp, narrow, fully-opaque edge is a harder case for discretization at low K than typical content (antialiased text, softer boundaries) — this is not "the feature is broken," it's evidence that a fixed default sample count is content-dependent and can miss the bar on legitimately common content (thin high-contrast elements: text strokes, iconography, UI chrome).

## Proposal

Adaptive per-frame sample count, derived from the motion magnitude measured across the shutter window (e.g. displacement of the animated properties between the window's sub-frame endpoints), rather than a fixed `samplesPerFrame`. Floor at the current default (16), ceiling at the current max (64, `MAX_SAMPLES_PER_FRAME`), so:

- Static and slow-moving content pays what it already pays today, at the floor — case 3 above must stay free. Cost never drops below today's fixed 16; it only rises on the frames that need it.
- Fast or hard-edged content scales up toward 64 automatically, closing the gap in case 1 without every render paying the 64-sample cost.

Open question for whoever picks this up: what "motion across the shutter window" should be measured from — screen-space displacement of the blurred element's bounding box between the window's endpoint samples is the cheapest signal and is already implicitly available since the endpoints are captured either way; whether that alone is a good enough proxy for rotation/scale-driven blur (as opposed to pure translation) needs checking against a case like case 1 but with rotation instead of translation.

title: chore(engine): trim an 8-line comment in armStaticDedup
body:
## What

Trims one comment block in `armStaticDedup` (`packages/engine/src/services/frameCapture.ts`) from 8 lines to 3.

## Why

Held #4031 under `no-essay-comments`' 4-line limit; Miguel bypassed the hold to land #4031 (merged at `2ab7b8686`) and asked for this trim as a small follow-up. The full reasoning the original comment carried:

`armStaticDedup`'s adaptive motion-blur classification gate reads `session.options.motionBlur` (the raw caller options, set at session creation) rather than `session.motionBlur` (the resolved plan). Every `armStaticDedup` call site runs *before* `finalizeSessionInit` resolves `session.motionBlur`, so a gate reading the resolved field would always be false — an earlier version of this code had exactly that bug, caught by an independent review on #4031 before it merged.

Comment only; no logic change.

title: Composition scope shim doesn't scope array selector targets: tweens leak across compositions (element stays visibility:hidden for a whole beat)
Studio: VideoFrameThumbnail enters an infinite error → cleanup loop — one CPU core pinned + unbounded React update allocation (OOM in long-running embeds)
fix(studio): stop VideoFrameThumbnail error→cleanup infinite loop
body:
Fixes #4036

## Problem

`VideoFrameThumbnail`'s error handler called `cleanup()`, which sets `video.src = ""` and calls `video.load()`. Clearing `src` itself fires another `error` event on the element, re-entering the handler — an event-loop-speed infinite loop. Every pass allocates a React update object via `setFailed(true)`.

The `seeked` path triggers the same loop: its `cleanup()` call provokes the synthetic `error` right after a successful frame extraction, so **every thumbnail ends up spinning, whether the video loads or not**.

## Evidence (real project, embedded studio)

- Instrumented `HTMLMediaElement.src` setter: **~475,000 assignments/second** from the `error → cleanup → error` cycle.
- Allocation sampling: **~8.6 MB/s** of React update objects (`{lane, revertLane, gesture, action, hasEagerState, eagerState, next}`) inside `dispatchSetState`, attributed to this component's `setFailed(true)`.
- A heap snapshot after ~40 minutes: **24.6M update objects / 983 MB (93% of heap)**, renderer pinned at ~100% CPU; in our Electron embed the JS heap grew to 2.8 GB at ~7 MB/s until the page died.

## Fix

- Name the error handler and detach it inside `cleanup()` before clearing `src`.
- Ignore the synthetic empty-src error (`!video.getAttribute("src")`) as a belt-and-braces guard.

## Test

New `VideoFrameThumbnail.test.tsx` covers: fallback label on error, staying inert after repeated post-cleanup synthetic errors, keeping the extracted frame when the post-seek cleanup error fires, and re-arming a fresh video element when `src` changes.

title: fix(engine,producer): retry transient Windows spawn file locks on ffmpeg/ffprobe
body:
### Summary

Fixes #4058

On Windows, `spawn` of the managed `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` binaries can fail transiently with `EBUSY`/`ETXTBSY` — typically antivirus real-time scanning a just-executed exe, or a lingering handle from a concurrent sibling invocation (one render shares a single managed ffmpeg binary across many stages). Today a single transient failure fails the whole render with a bare `spawn EBUSY` and no retry.

This adds a shared engine helper, `withTransientSpawnRetry`, and adopts it at the three spawn sites:

- `runFfmpeg` (engine): retries when the `ManagedChildProcess` outcome is a `spawn_error` carrying a transient errno.
- `audioExtractor.runFFmpeg` (producer): retries a rejected transient spawn error.
- `audioPadTrim.runFfprobeJson` (producer): retries a result-shaped `spawn_error` outcome.

### Behavior

- Transient errnos: `EBUSY`, `ETXTBSY`, `EAGAIN`, `EMFILE`, `ENFILE` — retried with exponential backoff (250 ms base, up to 3 attempts total); each retry is logged with the binary path and errno.
- When retries are exhausted, the error names the binary, the errno, and the usual cause ("transient file lock — often antivirus real-time scanning").
- Permanent failures (`ENOENT`, `EACCES`, …) pass through on the first attempt, unchanged.
- The helper wraps the caller's existing spawn-and-wait flow rather than the raw `spawn()` call, so a healthy spawn keeps its exact synchronous timing — no changes to existing fake-timer test choreography.

### Test plan

- [x] New unit tests (`packages/engine/src/utils/ffSpawnRetry.test.ts`, 13 cases): errno classification, backoff math, message enrichment, result-shaped vs rejected failure retry, exhaustion enrichment, permanent-failure pass-through.
- [x] Existing `runFfmpeg` (incl. the `windowsHide` regression) and `chunkEncoder` timeout suites pass unchanged.
- [x] `audioPadTrim` suite passes (37/37).
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for `@hyperframes/engine` and `@hyperframes/producer`.

title: [Windows] Disk-capture headroom gate rejects ordinary renders: uncompressed-RGBA estimate (~16 GB for ~1 min of 1080p) and no streaming fallback
body:
### Describe the bug

On Windows (and any host with modest free disk), ordinary renders were rejected by the disk-capture headroom gate with a message like:

```
Disk capture may need ~16331.7 MB of temporary frame storage, but only 18092.4 MB is free at
C:\Users\...\AppData\Local\Temp\hf-render-xxxx\captured-frames. Re-run with --low-memory-mode ...
```

A few seconds of video "requiring 16 GB" looks alarming — and in our field case the machine had 18 GB free yet a ~1-minute 1080p30 export was refused **only because the estimate crossed the 90% gate by 48 MB**. Two compounding problems:

**1. The estimate is an uncompressed RGBA ceiling, while disk frames are written compressed.**
`estimateDiskCaptureBytes` bills `totalFrames × width × height × 4` (raw RGBA), but the capture stage writes `jpg` (or `png` for alpha). Measured 1080p JPEG captures land at ~150–400 KB/frame — roughly **1/20–1/30 of the estimate**. A 44 s 1080p30 composition estimated at ~11 GB against 11.4 GB free failed, with an actual JPEG footprint of a few hundred MB.

**2. When the gate rejects, the render fails outright even when streaming was possible.**
Auto-parallel renders always take the disk path (ordered streaming would stall later workers), and `shouldUseStreamingEncode` requires `workerCount === 1` — so the only reason a render landed on the disk path was parallelism. The gate then runs as a hard error at capture time instead of a replan trigger. Long renders past the streaming duration cap (240 s) had no escape at all: 5 minutes of 1080p30 estimated at ~60 GB under the RGBA ceiling, rejecting effectively every machine.

### Expected behavior

- The estimate should reflect the actual (compressed) capture format with a safety margin, not a raw RGBA ceiling.
- When disk headroom is insufficient but single-worker streaming is eligible for the render, the orchestrator should degrade the plan to single-worker streaming instead of failing.

### Environment

- Windows 11 x64, HyperFrames producer ~v0.8.40 (observed in an Electron integration; applies to CLI renders too)
- C: drive with ~18 GB free; capture temp dir on the system drive (`hf-render-*`)

### Proposed fix

Two-part (PR to follow):

1. `estimateDiskCaptureBytes` bills by capture format: JPEG 0.5 B/px (keeps a ~5× safety margin, shrinks the estimate 8×) and PNG 2 B/px (lossless, half the RGBA ceiling). Gate message updated to the compressed-frame estimate basis.
2. `executeRenderJob` checks the gate right after the initial capture plan is built; when headroom is insufficient and `shouldUseStreamingEncode(cfg, format, 1, duration)` is true, the plan degrades to single-worker streaming via a `shouldDegradeDiskCaptureToStreaming` predicate — before capture and telemetry observe it, so the degraded plan is indistinguishable from one the streaming gate chose up front.

title: fix(producer): respect real disk headroom — compressed-format estimate + single-worker streaming fallback
body:
### Summary

Fixes #4060

Two-part fix for the disk-capture headroom gate rejecting ordinary renders on machines with modest free disk:

**1. Calibrate the estimate to the actual capture format** (`captureStage.ts`)
`estimateDiskCaptureBytes` billed `totalFrames × width × height × 4` — a raw RGBA ceiling — while the capture stage writes compressed `jpg` (or `png` for alpha) frames. It now bills by format:

- JPEG: 0.5 B/px (measured 1080p captures are ~0.05–0.1 B/px, so a ~5× safety margin; the estimate shrinks 8×)
- PNG: 2 B/px (lossless — photographic content can approach raw size, so half the RGBA ceiling)

The gate message now states the compressed-frame estimate basis. A 44 s 1080p30 composition that previously estimated ~11 GB now estimates ~1.4 GB (actual JPEG footprint: a few hundred MB).

**2. Degrade to single-worker streaming when headroom is insufficient** (`renderOrchestrator.ts`)
Auto-parallel renders always take the disk path (`shouldUseStreamingEncode` requires `workerCount === 1`), so the only reason a render landed on the disk path was parallelism — and the gate then hard-failed the render even though single-worker streaming could finish it. `executeRenderJob` now checks `inspectDiskCaptureHeadroom` right after the initial capture plan is built; when headroom is insufficient and `shouldUseStreamingEncode(cfg, format, 1, duration)` is eligible, a `shouldDegradeDiskCaptureToStreaming` predicate triggers a rebuild of the plan as single-worker streaming — before capture and telemetry observe it, so the degraded plan is indistinguishable from one the streaming gate chose up front. Permanent ineligibility (png-sequence/gif output, duration past the streaming cap, `enableStreamingEncode=false`) keeps the existing gate error, now with the calibrated estimate.

### Test plan

- [x] `captureStage.test.ts`: format-dependent estimate (JPEG vs PNG), calibrated gate rejection, updated message assertion.
- [x] `renderOrchestrator.test.ts`: new `shouldDegradeDiskCaptureToStreaming` decision table (5 cases — multi-worker disk + no headroom + streaming-eligible degrades; sufficient headroom / streaming plans / ineligible streaming / single-worker plans do not).
- [x] Full `renderOrchestrator.test.ts` + `captureStage.test.ts` suites pass (the only failures are 6 pre-existing environment-dependent cases that fail identically on clean `main`).
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for `@hyperframes/producer`.

title: feat(cli): --motion-blur flag and hyperframes.json render.motionBlur
body:
## What

Plumbs the engine's sub-frame motion blur (`packages/engine/src/services/motionBlur.ts`, #4010) into `hyperframes render` through both entry points the After Effects exporter needs: the `--motion-blur` CLI flag and the `hyperframes.json` `render.motionBlur` object. `RenderConfig.motionBlur` existed but nothing set it.

## Why

The exporter (hyperframes-ae-mcp, Plan 5) writes a comp's own AE shutter into `hyperframes.json`; without CLI plumbing that config is inert and the engine route renders sharp. This is the prerequisite PR for that path.

## How

- `--motion-blur[=angle[:phase[:samples]]]` — the empty value (`--motion-blur=`) asks for the engine defaults (180 / −90 / adaptive); `180:-90:16` sets them. `--no-motion-blur` overrides a project config off for one run.
- `hyperframes.json` gains `render.motionBlur`, validated and whitelist-rebuilt in `normalizeConfig` so the exporter's write survives a round trip.
- The option travels plan → `RenderOptions` → `RenderRequestOptions` (validated at that boundary) → `RenderConfig.motionBlur`.
- PNG frame formation follows inside the producer (`resolveCaptureImageFormat`); screenshot capture is forced onto the engine config in `renderLocal`, since sub-frame accumulation seeks the live timeline.
- Docker forwards the flag in a named form (`--motion-blur=angle=180,samples=16`) so a partially-specified option survives the in-container re-parse.
- The flag's help and the docs say to pass it with `=`: as an optional-value flag the space form reads the next argument, so bare `--motion-blur` is only safe as the final argument.

## Test plan

- `packages/cli` suite: 3346 passed, 3 skipped.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/render/motionBlur.e2e.test.ts`: 6/6 against a real render (~45 s) — the shutter window's ends land one frame either side of the frame time over 16 sub-intervals, the smear is a 16-column partial-alpha staircase with none unblurred, and the blurred frame scores 55.5 dB against the independently derived AE shutter model vs 36.6 dB for the unblurred frame.

title: fix(registry): declare @font-face for system-only fonts used without one
body:
## What changed

`vfx-text-cursor` used "Impact" and `caption-emoji-pop` used the platform emoji font stack ("Apple Color Emoji", "Segoe UI Emoji", "Noto Color Emoji") with no `@font-face` declaration for any of them. The lint rule `font_family_without_font_face` flags this because these fonts aren't Google Fonts and aren't in the auto-resolved alias list, so the renderer has no declared way to know they're OS-bundled and auto-suppliable — the risk surfaces specifically in distributed/Lambda rendering, where system-font capture is disabled and an undeclared font silently falls back to a generic typeface.

Declared each via `@font-face { font-family: "..."; src: local("..."); }`, matching the existing pattern already shipped in `registry/blocks/chatgpt-exchange/chatgpt-exchange.html` (which does the same for "Apple Color Emoji"). The `local()` form is the lint rule's own documented fix for exactly this case — it tells the renderer the font is OS-bundled rather than pointing at a downloadable file.

## Review

Independent adversarial review (separate subagent, not the authoring context). No blocking findings.

Audited / Trusting / Not exercised:
- Audited: diff matches the claim exactly (2 files, 18 insertions, 0 deletions); font-family names in the new `@font-face` blocks match byte-for-byte against where each is actually used.
- Audited: lint proven both directions with real runs — reverted to the pre-fix file content, reran lint, got the exact predicted failures; restored the fix, reran, 0 errors.
- Audited: standalone renders of both items — no broken/tofu glyphs, emoji render in full color.
- Audited: commit message format, no AI attribution.
- Trusting: none.

`node scripts/lint-registry-items.mjs caption-emoji-pop vfx-text-cursor` passes cleanly (0 errors) on the rebased branch.

A local macOS render can't show a visible before/after difference here — this rule targets distributed/Lambda rendering correctness (where system-font capture is disabled), and local rendering already substitutes system fonts correctly regardless of the declaration. Confirmed via standalone renders that nothing broke; this is a compliance fix, not a locally-visible one, consistent with how the earlier raf-desync and async-timeline-registration fixes in this same lane also had no visible standalone difference.

title: fix(skills): stop mirroring skills into Codex and remove old mirror links
body:
## What

The global skills mirror no longer creates a Codex-specific copy: Codex reads the universal `~/.agents/skills` store, so a second copy made every skill show up twice.

## Why

Codex discovers the user-level universal skills store, so creating another Codex mirror causes duplicate skill discovery.

## How

Add Codex to the universal-store reader capability set and skip it before directory creation or target replacement. Symlinks an earlier mirror left in the Codex skills dir (they resolve to the same Claude-store skill) are removed, but only when the universal store holds that skill and the Codex dir passes the same alias check every other destructive path runs; real directories and Windows copies carry no ownership proof, so they stay. Add isolated default and custom `CODEX_HOME` regression coverage.

## Size

Small on purpose: one gate in the skills mirror plus a cleanup of the links it used to create, with tests. Extending the skip to the other agents that read the universal store is a separate follow-up.

title: feat(studio): dragging a clip over another overwrites it, alt inserts, one undo
body:
## What

In the Studio timeline, dragging a clip over other clips on the same track now follows the rule editors expect from Premiere and CapCut: an ordinary drop overwrites (cuts away exactly the range the dragged clip covers), and holding Alt or Cmd at release inserts instead (splits the clip under the drop point and pushes everything after it later). The whole drop, however many clips it touches, undoes in one step.

Two things that surfaced while capturing this are fixed in the same PR because they share the drop's commit path:

- A drop never shows the timeline an older state. Before, a clip the drop had just removed could reappear for a moment, and the dragged clip could flash back at its old position.
- Editing a clip while playback is running keeps the playhead running. Before, the preview jumped back and stopped while the button still said Pause.

## Why

Dropping a clip onto another clip on the same track used to leave what is underneath alone: the dragged clip either moved to a new track or silently overlapped the clip under it. That is not how a track-level drop works in an editor.

## How

- `timelinePlacement.ts`: a pure function, `placeClip`, that takes the clips already on a track plus the drop's start, duration and mode and returns which clips are removed, trimmed (head or tail), split, or shifted (insert only). No side effects.
- `timelinePlacementCommit.ts`: turns that result into ordered writes (split, remove, resize, move) under one shared undo key. It refuses the whole drop, writing nothing, if it would touch a locked or expanded clip, split too close to a clip's edge, leave a sliver thinner than the split epsilon, or touch a split tail the reload has not reported yet.
- Wiring: the drag lifecycle reads Alt/Cmd at pointer-up and passes the mode through; a plain move with no overlap is untouched.
- No older state: the timeline store is repopulated from the preview iframe's clip manifest, and the iframe still holds the pre-drop document until the drop's reload. The drop now (1) holds incoming manifests at the single shared boundary, `syncTimelineElements`, while it runs, (2) writes its whole end state to the store in one update before any file write starts, and (3) reloads the preview once at the end, only when a clip was removed or split. A delete or split folded into a drop skips its own reload and its own store write.
- Playing while editing: `finalizeSoftReload` re-seeked the preview to the store's current time, which while playing is the last seek and not the playhead. It now re-seeks to the player's live time and keeps playing when the player is running.
- `timelineCollision.ts`: the zone-drop resolver destructured `relocateOnOverlap` off the wrong object, so a wrong-zone drag with it unset still spawned a track. Fixed.

The frame-checking script used below is a separate PR (#4167).

### Scope

The branch is over the ~1k changed-line guideline (about 1.8k including tests and the test harness). The checker script was split out into its own PR; the rest is one path (rule, commit, the drop's store/reload behaviour, and the playing fix). Most of the excess is the placement, commit and monotonic-state test suites.

### Preview blank at the reload: fixed by the never-blank swap PR, not here

The preview goes blank for about five frames at the drop's single reload (and at undo's reload, the timeline is empty for about a third of a second). Both are the preview reload swap, not the drop's state; the never-blank swap for the preview closes them, so they are not fixed here. The checker flags them on the preview region.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `timelinePlacement.test.ts`, `timelinePlacementCommit.test.ts`, `timelinePlacementMonotonic.test.ts` (mounts the real player hook, posts a stale manifest mid-drop, asserts no state after the first contains a removed clip and the first store write is the whole end state), `useTimelineDeleteOps.test.tsx` (a folded delete leaves the store to the drop), `gsapSoftReload.test.ts` (keeps the live playhead and playback while playing), plus drag-lifecycle and collision updates. Each new test was checked by breaking the implementation on purpose.
- [x] Full Studio suite, tsc, oxlint and oxfmt pass (453 files, 5060 tests).
- [x] Manual testing performed: nine drop cases driven in a real Studio (Chrome, headless), recorded below. After mouse-up every drop case shows exactly one timeline state (sampled per animation frame), and in the playing case the player time increases on every sample with playback running and the button on Pause.
- [ ] Documentation updated (n/a: no user docs for this interaction)

### Frame check (scripts/check-capture-reversion.mjs, timeline strip crop)

Each capture was run through the checker over the timeline strip (`--crop=1280:200:0:600`), all frames of each clip:

- Nine after clips, all frames: clean on 01-04, 06, 07 and 09 (frames 0 to 227, 228, 228, 229, 227, 230, 215). 05 and 08 flag frame 50, which is the drag ghost and its guide lines appearing mid-drag, before release (a moving gesture, not a state reverting).
- The same nine clips from release onward (the part after mouse-up, from 2.6s): clean on all, 01 to 08 (150 to 270 frames each; 09 has no separate post clip and is clean in full).
- Older main clips for comparison: before 01 flags frame 43 and before 07 flags frame 171 (the clip coming back), before 05 is clean.

Two independent adversarial reviews by a second reviewer, before this was posted.

**Blocking, fixed.** The delete folded into a drop rebuilt the timeline from the clips it saw when the gesture began, after the drop had already written its end state, so the dragged clip flashed back at its old position for a moment.
