A drop whose first write failed now toasts instead of staying silent; a trim thinner than the split epsilon is refused.

title: feat(studio): edit a clip's speed ramp with a rate lane and presets
body:
Speed ramps, end to end: an editor can ramp a clip's speed in Studio, an agent can write the same ramp in the format, and snapshots and the docs agree with the preview and the render. (This folds the former #4170 and #4171 into one PR, one feature, one review.)

## What a user can do now
**Editor, in Studio**
- A log-scale Speed slider (0.1x-10x) replaces the plain constant-rate slider.
- An "A" toggle turns the speed into a curve over the clip's timeline, drawn as a lane like volume automation, editable point by point.
- A Speed preset picker applies one of six ready-made curves (montage, hero, bullet, jump cut, flash in, flash out).

**Agent or anyone reading a project, from the CLI**
- `hyperframes snapshot` now shows the right frame for a clip with a speed ramp, and for a clip at a constant rate above 5x. It used to clamp at 5x and ignore the ramp, so those snapshots disagreed with the preview and the render.

**Anyone learning the format, in the docs**
- One reference page, `speed-ramps`, teaches the `rate` lane in `data-automation` (fields, presets, what Studio shows, pitch, limits, and which speed limits belong to the viewer instead of the clip).
- The `data-playback-rate` range in the HTML schema now says 0.1 to 10, and the skills no longer tell agents that speed ramps are unsupported.

## Shape
- Studio reuses the volume-lane binding and geometry helpers through one shared lane binding, rather than a second implementation, and adds a `@hyperframes/core/speed-ramp` subpath mirroring the existing subpath shape.
- Fixes a bug in the shared attribute-commit path found by review: the optimistic live write and the on-disk write could disagree for any attribute whose "off" value is the literal string `"false"`. The live write now matches the file write for exactly the attributes the patcher treats as booleans, with a regression test.
- Snapshot reads the rate through the runtime's own reader and maps time with the shared `sourceTimeAt` / `timeAtSourceTime`, so there is no second copy of the clamp.
- The viewer's transport speed is a separate limit from a clip's rate (0.1 to 10, owned by `packages/core/src/playbackRateBounds.ts`); they are not unified.

title: feat(scripts): flag a capture region that briefly returns to an older picture
body:
## What

`scripts/check-capture-reversion.mjs`: checks a screen recording for a region that briefly returns to an older picture (a clip that reappears for one frame, a panel that flashes its previous state). It compares cropped, downscaled frames and reports a frame that differs between two matching frames within a window. Continuous motion is not flagged.

## Why

A recording attached to a PR can look fine at a glance and still contain a one-frame reversion. Eyeballing does not catch it reliably; a mechanical frame comparison does, and every author can run the same check on their own captures.

## How

- Frames are cropped (`--crop=W:H:X:Y`), scaled to 96px wide, grayscale. A reversion is an A, B, A pattern: frame k nearly equals an earlier frame i while a frame between them clearly differs from both.
- Exit codes: 0 clean, 1 flagged, 2 could not check (bad option, missing binary or file, undecodable video, time limit). A failure to check can never read as clean.
- Each video has one wall-clock budget (`--timeout`, default 120s) shared by ffprobe, ffmpeg and the comparison. A timed-out tool is killed with its whole process group, also when the checker itself gets SIGINT or SIGTERM.
- Options are validated up front; the frame height is passed to ffmpeg explicitly so the size the check assumes always matches what ffmpeg produces (a two-pixel-tall crop used to make the assumed frame size zero and the loop never end).
- A short "Checking a capture" section in CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: 22 in `scripts/check-capture-reversion.test.mjs` (`node --test`), registered in `test:scripts`. They cover the thresholds, window boundary, ordering, option validation, the real CLI exit codes (0, 1, 2) including a symlinked path, the time limit against a fake hung ffmpeg and ffprobe, and no orphaned child after a timeout or SIGTERM.
- [x] Manual testing performed: run over eight fresh Studio drop recordings (clean on the timeline strip) and three older recordings (two flag the known reversion), each with `--crop` on the timeline strip.
- [x] Documentation updated

An independent adversarial review ran over four rounds; its findings (exit-code conflation, NaN options reading clean, a hang on a thin crop, a symlink entry-guard silent pass, deadline granularity, orphaned children) are fixed and covered by tests, and I mutation-checked the guards.

title: fix(cli): the npx shim test runs a stub npx, not the runners
body:
## What changes

The `npxCommand` unit test that ran the host's real `npx --version` through `cmd.exe` timed out on the Windows CI runner (`spawnSync cmd.exe ETIMEDOUT`), so an unrelated PR could go red on a machine-load problem. A unit test should not depend on the runner's `npx` or the network.

The test now writes a stub `npx` (`npx.cmd` on Windows) into a temp folder, puts that folder first on `PATH`, and runs the command `buildNpxCommand` builds. It expects the stub's output. So `cmd.exe /d /s /c npx.cmd` resolution is still exercised end to end, with no host `npx`, no network and a 15 second bound. The test itself is not retried.

The per-platform command-shape tests are unchanged.

## Verification

- `npxCommand.test.ts`: 7 pass on Linux at the first head. The last commit only adds `maxRetries: 3, retryDelay: 100` to the temp-dir cleanup (a Windows file lock could otherwise hide the assertion); it was not re-run on the remote runner, so CI on this head is its verification.
- Deliberate mutation: with the stub folder left off `PATH`, the new test fails (`expected '10.9.4' to be '9.9.9'`, the real npx's answer), so it does test the stub path.
- Not exercised here: Windows and macOS. The `cli-npx-shim` CI job runs this file on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, which is the check for the `cmd.exe` and `npx.cmd` path.

title: fix(media-use): remove clicks and ~25ms gaps at every transcript-cut splice
body:
## The problem

`skills/media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.mjs` extracts each kept range to its own final-codec file, then concat-copies them. Two audible artifacts result at every cut, and they are separate bugs:

1. **No boundary fades.** Concat splices raw segment edges together, so the waveform steps discontinuously and each cut clicks.
2. **Encoder priming silence.** Each segment is encoded to AAC independently, so the encoder pads every one with priming samples; stream-copy concat bakes that in as a silent gap. It also accumulates — the *n*th splice lands roughly 25*n* ms late, so splice positions no longer match the sum of the preceding segment durations.

The second survives the first. Adding fades alone still leaves the gap, which is what made it easy to miss.

## Reproduce

```bash
node skills/media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.mjs \
  --input take.mp4 --transcript take.json --keep "5-10,20-25,40-45" --out out.mp4
```

Widest run of digital silence within ±0.25 s of each nominal splice:

| | splice @5s | splice @10s |
|---|---|---|
| main | 24.4 ms | 24.1 ms |
| this PR | 0.1 ms | 0.1 ms |

## The fix

Intermediates carry PCM (`.mkv` for video, `.wav` for audio-only) rather than the final codec, so audio is encoded exactly once — at concat. Per-segment 30 ms `afade` in/out ramps handle the click, scaled down on segments shorter than 4× the ramp and skipped on degenerate ones.

## Not changed

- **`--copy`** — stream copy cannot filter, so it still produces final-codec segments and a copy concat. The flag already trades accuracy for speed; this leaves that trade alone.
- **Audio-only output** — identical duration before and after (10.000000 s on the same two-range cut). `.wav` intermediates avoid the aac-in-wav timing break the existing `encodeArgsFor` comment warns about.

## Verification

- `scripts/lib/*.test.mjs`: 34/35. The one failure, `lut-preset-provider.test.mjs`, reproduces on unmodified `main` and is unrelated (it reads a `packages/core/src/colorGrading.ts` that does not exist in this repo).
- Measurements above taken on public-domain footage (Prelinger Archives, *The Quiet Revolution*, 1956).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cli): stopping the preview server no longer leaves a Chrome running
body:
## What changes

Stopping the preview server could leave a Chrome running. If a render was in progress when the stop signal arrived, its Chrome was killed by that same signal. The render then read that as a transient browser failure and its bounded retry launched a fresh Chrome that nothing tracked, so it outlived the server process.

- `createStudioServer` now returns a `shutdown()`. It marks the server as shutting down first, cancels every in-flight render, kills tracked processes, waits for the renders to finish, closes the thumbnail browser (waiting for one that is mid-launch), and drains the browser pool.
- An aborted render is classified as cancelled before the transient-browser check, so the retry does not fire (`packages/engine/src/services/captureFailure.ts:158`, rethrown at `renderOrchestrator.ts:1266`).
- Once shutdown has begun, a new render request is answered with a failed state ("Studio server is shutting down"), and a new thumbnail request does not launch a browser. The check lives in one place, in front of the thumbnail launch.
- `preview` calls `shutdown()` in its signal handler instead of the previous inline cleanup. `closeThumbnailBrowser` is no longer exported (nothing else used it).

## Verification

- `studioServer.test.ts`: 17 pass on a remote Linux runner; typecheck and lint clean; comment check clean.
- New tests: shutdown cancels an in-flight render and waits for it before draining; a render started after shutdown began is refused; a thumbnail request after shutdown launches no browser; a thumbnail launch that finishes after shutdown began is released.
- Deliberate mutations, each turning one test red: no wait for the render, no shutdown check in front of the thumbnail launch, closing without waiting for an in-flight launch, no shutdown check in `startRender`.
- Not exercised: a real Chrome, and the 3 second forced-exit timer in `preview`. `src/server/portUtils.test.ts` fails one PID-provenance test on the remote runner; that file is not touched here and I did not compare it against main.
- Follow-up on this head: `shutdown()` still waited on every render before closing browsers, so a render slower than the 3s exit watchdog left Chrome running when it fired; a second Ctrl+C/SIGTERM also bypassed cleanup by dropping the one-shot signal handlers. Both fixed, plus a lease-reuse gap during the shutdown race window. Two new tests (a render whose `done` never settles still gets the browser closed and the pool drained within a bound; a thumbnail request landing in that race window is refused instead of reusing a live lease) bring `studioServer.test.ts` to 19/19; the full `packages/cli` suite (3442 tests), typecheck, and lint stay green on a remote Linux runner.

## Review

An independent review found no blocking issues. Its three should-fix items are closed: the render test settled synchronously (now asynchronous, so it fails without the wait), the thumbnail test passed without Chrome (now asserts the launch is never attempted), and a thumbnail launch could start after shutdown had begun (fixed at the launch, with a test for the window).

title: test(engine): hold the download attempt deadline so slow runners cannot trip it
body:
## What changes

Main went red on Windows in `urlDownloader.test.ts` ("locally refetches a caller checksum mismatch...") with `Download timeout after 1s` where `hash_mismatch` was expected.

Cause: every download attempt starts a real 1 second deadline timer, and the tests all pass 1_000. That test runs two attempts (fetch, hash, refetch, hash); on a slow Windows runner one attempt can outlast the timer. The earlier fix (#4155) faked only `Date`, so this timer was still real.

- The test file now holds that 1 second deadline timer instead of starting it. Other timers (cache-lock poll, test delays, the 20 ms stalled-body test) stay real. No timeout value is raised.
- "does not let one caller cancellation abort another caller" only passed because the real deadline fired after about 1 s (1078 ms on main). It now fires the held deadline by hand once the stalled first fetch has started.
- New test: a fetch that takes 1.2 s against a 1 s deadline still succeeds, and the stub rejects on abort, so an armed deadline would fail it.

No product code changes.

## Verification

- `urlDownloader.test.ts`: 81 pass, three runs in a row on a remote Linux runner, exit 0 each. Lint and format clean.
- Deliberate mutation: turning the hold off makes the new test fail.
- Not exercised: the hosted Windows job (the flake is Windows-only, so the next Windows run is the real check).

## Review

An independent read-only review found no blocking or should-fix items. One note: the hold matches a delay of exactly 1_000 ms, so a future test using 1_000 for something else would be held too.

title: feat(studio): audio level meters at the timeline's right edge
body:
## What

Studio gets audio level meters at the right edge of the timeline: one stereo meter with peak hold and a dB scale (0, -3, -6, -12, -24) for each audio group, plus Master, moving with the real playback level in the preview. A speaker button in the timeline toolbar hides and shows the strip and the choice is remembered. A project with no audio gets no strip and no button.

Read-only in this PR. Faders (each strip's volume through the existing group volume write path) follow in the next PR.

## How

- Core: `window.__hf.audioMeter = { start, stop, read }` (`levelTap.ts`, `webAudioTransport.ts`). `start()` adds a stereo analyser branch after each group bus and after master; `read()` returns the linear peak per channel; `stop()` disconnects everything. Taps are side branches, so the audible path is unchanged, and nothing exists until `start()`.
- Studio: `AudioMeterStrip` runs one rAF loop that re-reads the hook off the live preview window each frame, so a reloaded preview is followed and its taps started. Bars are written straight to the DOM; no React state per frame.
- Groups that appear or disappear mid-session appear in or leave `read()`.
- Ungrouped clips play straight into master (no per-track bus), so they show in Master only.

## Before

![Timeline with audio groups and no meter strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78234293-fc00-4d60-b635-54fe8eb55659)

## After

![Meter strip at the timeline right edge reading Music, VO and Master while playing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a0bcd2d-10c8-4a50-9eaf-dbb8fc8fb390)

Captured in Studio on this head, from a fixture built of generated tones in two audio groups plus Master. After is playing; the bars are filled, not an idle rail.

## Checks

- Rebased onto current `origin/main`. The previous `regression` red was the aggregate job of a cancelled shard (`One or more regression shards failed`); shard-6 was cancelled during Docker image build and never ran the fixtures.
- Core `webAudioTransport` tests 77 passed, exit 0 (includes taps created only on start, side-branch wiring, idempotent start, group added or removed mid-session, metering started before audio context init).
- Studio strip, meter math, preference and TimelinePane suites 25 passed, exit 0; `tsc --noEmit` clean for studio.
- Independent adversarial review: recorded for this head.

title: fix(studio): undo waits for in-flight hand edits before consuming history
body:
## What
Undo and redo now wait for any hand edit (split, move, resize, razor, group move, hide, audio attrs, delete, drop) that is still writing before they touch history. Every handler `useTimelineEditing` returns is wrapped so its write is registered in Studio's existing shared pending-edit registry, the same one undo/redo already waits on.

## Why
On a slow write, pressing Undo right after Delete lost the clip: the delete's write reached disk before its undo entry was recorded, so Undo found nothing to restore and the deletion stuck. Reproduced on a fixture with the write's network call throttled to make the window visible; a plain fast localhost click is too quick to show it reliably, which is why this needed a deliberate throttle rather than a stopwatch. Fix reuses `trackStudioPendingEdit`/`flushStudioPendingEdits` (already wired into undo through the DOM-edit save queue) instead of adding a new wait path.

## How
- `hooks/useTrackPendingTimelineEdit.ts`: wraps a handler so its promise is tracked, returning the same wrapper for the same handler across renders so a caller's memoized deps stay stable.
- `hooks/useTimelineEditing.ts`: every returned handler is wrapped at its one shared exit point; only the live-DOM half of the audio/fx attribute setters is left untouched, since only the persist half writes.
- Tests: `useTrackPendingTimelineEdit.test.tsx` (the wrapper genuinely feeds the shared registry, stable identity); `useTimelineDeleteOps.test.tsx`'s new "undo race" block (the flush waits while the delete's write is still landing, and resolves immediately once it's already done).

## Before
Delete a clip on a fixture project, with its write artificially slowed. Undo right after: the clip stays gone, no "Undid" toast, the timeline is short by one clip:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce26c82e-2464-4541-83a8-fb199dafe348

## After

## What a user gets

Studio gets its own icon set: one grid, one stroke, one corner language, drawn for the dark Studio surface and legible at 12 px. This PR adds the module and the specimen sheet only; no call site changes yet, so nothing a user sees moves in this PR. The sweep by area follows in small PRs, and the last one removes the third-party icon library.

## What is in it

- `packages/studio/src/icons/glyphs.ts`: 102 glyphs as path data on a 16-unit grid with a 1-unit safe margin. A few glyphs carry a `small` drawing used below 14 px (sidebar pair, order quartet, file types) instead of scaling the 16 px shape down. Four names (`bring-forward`, `send-backward`, `bring-to-front`, `send-to-back`) map verbatim to Studio's existing default icons rather than a new drawing; everything else in the set is custom.

- `packages/studio/src/icons/index.tsx`: one named export per glyph with an `Icon` suffix (`CheckIcon`, `EyeOffIcon`, `WindowIcon`) so a call site imports by name and nothing shadows `Image`, `File` or `Window`.
- `packages/studio/scripts/icon-specimen.tsx`: renders the specimen sheet from the module itself, so the sheet cannot drift from the code.
- `Icon.test.tsx`: every glyph renders with the 16 viewBox in currentColor, no hard-coded colour, stays inside the safe margin (every path point, relative commands resolved, plus primitive boxes), has a named export; `title` announces, `filled` respects the silhouette rule, small variants switch at 14 px, stroke follows the size class.

title: refactor(studio): move playback adapter resolution into its own module
body:
## What
The playback-adapter resolution logic that lived inline inside `useTimelinePlayer`'s `getAdapter` moves into its own module, `playbackAdapterResolution.ts`. The two near-duplicate branches that checked `window.__timeline` and `window.__timelines` are collapsed into one `pickTimelineAdapter`/`timelineCandidates` loop. The shared test-mount harness (`TimelinePlayerHarness`, `renderTimelinePlayerHarness`, `attachIframeAdapter`) moves out of `useTimelinePlayer.seek.test.ts` into `timelinePlayerTestHarness.ts` so other test files can reuse it. Behaviour is unchanged.

## Why
`getAdapter` carried the full player/timeline/static-seek-fallback decision inline, flagged for its own complexity. Extracting it gives that decision one owner and a name, and lets the shadow-swap work (a separate PR) mount the same timeline player harness without copying it.

## How
- `player/hooks/playbackAdapterResolution.ts`: `resolvePlaybackAdapter`, `pickTimelineAdapter`, `timelineCandidates` — the exact branch order and fallback precedence from the old inline code (player adapter match, then timeline match, then static-seek wrap of the best available adapter).
- `player/hooks/useTimelinePlayer.ts`: `getAdapter` now calls `resolvePlaybackAdapter(iframe, win, { cache, warned })`; unused imports (`getAdapterDuration`, `wrapTimeline`, `getDefaultStaticSeekPlaybackClock`, `resolveStaticSeekFallback`, `readTimelineDurationFromDocument`) dropped, `releaseStaticSeekCache`/`StaticSeekCacheEntry` stay (still used at unmount).
- `player/hooks/timelinePlayerTestHarness.ts`: the mount harness, moved as-is.
- `player/hooks/useTimelinePlayer.seek.test.ts`: imports the harness instead of defining it; same 11 tests, unchanged assertions.

Independently reviewed (branch-by-branch trace against the pre-image, mutation-style check on the static-seek fallback path): PASS, nothing blocking.

Pure internal extraction — `playbackAdapterResolution.ts`, `timelinePlayerTestHarness.ts` and the two files that route through them are `.ts`/test files only, no `.tsx`/`.css`/`.html` touched, and the decision logic is call-for-call identical to the code it replaces. title: fix(docs): catalog player cap, fetch-mirror bounds, scroll cue, drift check
body:
Follow-up to #4056: three defects Miguel found on the deployed preview, plus the CodeQL bound he asked to ride along since he dismissed the alert on his word to merge that PR.

## Tune panel: scroll cue

The Tune panel's variable list can run longer than the visible area with no sign more is below. Added a small pulsing chevron that shows only while unseen variables remain below the fold, gone once scrolled to the end. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion` (no animation, cue still present).

## Blank Carousel tiles

Miguel: every Orbit/Path Carousel tile on the live catalog showed a plain dark card, no preview, only revealed on hover.

Root cause: `MAX_DOM_PLAYERS` capped concurrent live-preview players at 6, shared across the whole page. A 3-column grid shows 9+ tiles per screen, so most tiles were permanently starved onto their dark fallback; hover was the only way to steal a mounted slot from another tile, which is why it looked hover-gated. Raised the cap to 24 (headroom over a typical viewport's tile count), one line plus a test tying it to the real column count so it can't silently shrink back.

## Fetch-mirror write bounds (CodeQL alert 997, `js/http-to-file-access`)

`catalog-fetch-mirror.ts`'s record mode wrote a fetched response body to disk keyed by its own hash; the scanner flagged the write of untrusted bytes. Bounded it instead of dismissing: a content-type allowlist (text/font/image/video/json/js), an 8 MiB size cap, and a path-containment check reusing the existing `isContainedIn` helper. Refused writes are reported as misses, not silently dropped. Five new tests, each mutation-checked.

## orbit-card poster + codeLines drift

Swapped orbit-card's poster to the already-uploaded `orbit-card-v2.png`. While regenerating, found `meta.codeLines` on two unrelated pages (motion-blur, shutter-slam) had drifted from their real registry source line counts — `check:catalog-drift` never covered that field. Extended it to catch a stale `codeLines` (reusing the generator's own `discoverItems`/`primarySource`, not a reimplementation), regenerated the two pages, added a test that fails without the check.

## Verification

- 61 tests pass (`catalog-detail`, `catalog-fetch-mirror`, `catalog-drift`, `generate-catalog-pages`), typecheck and lint clean — all run on the devbox.
- `check:catalog-drift` clean against the fix (payload diffs 0, codeLines drift 0).
- Independent review: no blocking findings. Simplify pass: found and fixed a real issue (the scroll-cue's resize listener was being re-bound on every keystroke).

title: fix(studio): swap the preview via a shadow iframe instead of blanking on reload
body:
## Summary
Dragging or trimming a clip in the timeline reloaded the preview by hiding the live iframe first, so every edit produced a visible blank/flash before the new frame arrived. This loads the new document in a hidden shadow iframe instead and only swaps it in once the player itself reports the new frame is actually painted (assets ready and its own loading overlay has finished fading out), so the live iframe never blanks.

Builds on the shared iframe-owner store and the playback-adapter extraction from the two prior PRs in this stack; this is the PR that changes visible behavior.

## Before
Base flashes to black on several gesture types (cross-row move, delete, rapid double-edit, slow-path drag): 4 of 10 tested scenarios, 0.4-2.0s of near-black frames each. Worst case shown (delete):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0458318b-fd30-4e38-a1c9-8187c474bade

The more severe case is a file-watcher-triggered reload (an external tool or editor touching the project file): the base build goes black and does not recover within a 95-second test window.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cef82bb7-d7d9-449b-9134-f4a45c393a54

## After
Same gesture, same fixture: zero near-black frames across all 10 tested scenarios.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47ddca45-a6a2-4c03-bf3d-e708c10be715

Same file-watcher reload burst: never goes black, across two independent runs.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b0df51d-911a-4781-ad88-cad02457c738

## What changed
- Player: a new `painted` event/getter, reusing the existing fade-cleanup timer, fired once per document load after assets are ready and the loading overlay has finished fading (or immediately if no overlay was ever shown).
- Studio: the preview reload no longer hides the live iframe. It loads the new document in a hidden shadow iframe and promotes it to live in one atomic state update, gated on the player's `painted` signal in addition to the existing readiness checks.
- Each reload is generation-tagged so a second reload starting before the first promotes cancels the first's pending promotion outright (ref guards plus an actual DOM unmount of the stale shadow).
- A reload that never becomes ready within the existing wait budget (15s) discards cleanly: toast shown, error logged, the last-good frame stays on screen. No silent failure, no blank, no duplicate.
- New regression test drives the real preview + player hook through two back-to-back reload/promote cycles with no settle wait and asserts exactly one iframe in the DOM immediately after each promotion.

## Rerunnable check
`cd packages/studio && bunx vitest run src/components/nle/NLEPreview.test.ts src/player/hooks/useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts src/player/components/Player.test.ts`
`cd packages/player && bunx vitest run src/hyperframes-player.test.ts`

## Capture method
Real dev server, real Playwright pointer input, one neutral fixture (built from the repo's own example registry plus synthetic generated media, no project-specific content). 10 gesture scenarios recorded on both the base build and this branch; frame darkness measured on the preview-stage region only, within the actual gesture-to-settle window per run. Full per-scenario table and methodology in the PR discussion on request.

## Review (independent, adversarial)
| Finding | Result |
|---|---|
| Race: a second reload could resolve after a newer one is already live | Traced: generation counters checked at every promotion entry point, plus the stale shadow is unmounted from the DOM outright. No stomp path found. |
| The player's readiness signal could get stuck and never fire | Traced: the fade-complete callback fires synchronously when no loading overlay was ever shown, covering instant loads. No stuck path found. |
| The 15s give-up could fail silently or leak the hidden iframe | Traced: give-up unconditionally logs an error and shows a toast, and unmounts the shadow iframe. Not silent, not leaked. |
| Regression test could be vacuous | Reverting the atomic promotion to a naive append was traced through the assertion and would fail it. Test targets the real invariant. |

One known, accepted tradeoff: a burst of many reloads in a short window (an external tool touching the project file repeatedly) can hit the give-up on the last one and discard that particular reload, correctly falling back to the last-good frame rather than blanking. Whether that burst case should also coalesce rapid reloads is a separate, smaller follow-up under investigation; it does not affect the fix here.

## Notes for review
- 21 files changed, ~1550 insertions, stacked on the playback-adapter-extraction PR.
- Searched for an existing swap/double-buffer pattern first: none existed; the live iframe was previously hidden and reloaded in place.

title: fix(cli): bound capture runs and degrade WebGL navigation
body:

title: fix(server): contain static file requests within their served roots
body:
## What

The embedded Studio server and the engine's render file server both took the raw request path, joined it onto their root directory, and opened whatever landed there. Nothing checked that the result stayed inside the root, so a request carrying percent-encoded separators or dot segments could name a file anywhere on the disk and receive its bytes. This change resolves the request path first and answers 404 for anything that collapses outside the root being served. Two handlers changed and two route-level test suites were added; no public API or serving behavior for legitimate assets is affected.

## Why

Hono decodes percent escapes while it routes, and that decode is where the gap opens. On Windows an encoded backslash (`%5c`) arrives at the handler as a real path separator, so `/assets/..%5c..%5csecrets.txt` walks out of the Studio bundle directory, and the same shape works against the engine file server's `projectDir` and `compiledDir`. Browsers normalize dot segments before sending and never emit `%5c`, so ordinary Studio usage and capture sessions never produce these requests. The reachable senders are everything else that can touch the bound port: any local process, another user's process on a shared machine reaching the render server, and LAN peers whenever the preview server is bound to `0.0.0.0`, which is a documented supported mode. Each of them can read files with the CLI user's permissions.

A realpath-based containment like the repo's `resolveWithinProject` would be the wrong tool here. Bundle and project assets are allowed to sit behind symlinked directories, and #3725 and #3728 deliberately preserved that behavior while hardening these same servers. What separates an attack from that supported workflow is lexical: dot segments collapsing upward through `..`. So the guard rejects escape-by-collapse and keeps serving symlinked assets exactly as before, which keeps the fix consistent with the tradeoff the preview asset route already documents.

## How

Both handlers resolve the request path against their root and refuse the request when the resolved path lands outside it:

- `packages/cli/src/server/studioServer.ts` — `serveStudioStaticFile`, which backs the `/assets/*`, `/icons/*` and `/favicon.svg` SPA routes, now checks the resolved path before opening it.
- `packages/engine/src/services/fileServer.ts` — the `GET /*` handler checks both roots it serves, `compiledDir` when present and `projectDir`.

The check is `isWithinProjectRoot` from `@hyperframes/parsers/asset-resolution`, the same helper the preview asset route uses. It compares lexically, so an in-root symlinked or junctioned asset directory still resolves and still serves, while `../` collapse is rejected. Failures return the same 404 the handlers already used for missing files, so error responses do not leak whether a path escaped or simply did not exist.

The tests pin the behavior from the attacker's side. `fileServer.pathSafety.test.ts` starts a real listening server and fetches over HTTP, since that is the only faithful way to reproduce raw request shapes; it covers `/..%2f`, `/%2e%2e%2f`, a nested `%2f` hop, `%5c`, and repeated `%5c` variants, asserting that an outside file's contents never come back. On the previous handlers those requests return 200 with the file's bytes. `studioServer.pathSafety.test.ts` does the equivalent through the Studio app router with a marker file one level above the bundle root. Both suites also keep the positive cases green: in-root assets serve normally, the SPA shell still renders, cache headers are unchanged, and the symlinked-asset cases from the descriptor-pinning regressions still pass.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated — two new pathSafety suites; `packages/cli/src/server` passes in full (142 tests) and `packages/engine/src/services` matches the main baseline, including the pre-existing `browserManager` failures unrelated to this change
- [x] Manual testing performed — the engine containment suite runs against a real listening HTTP server on an ephemeral port; typecheck, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the workspace build all pass
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) — no user-facing behavior changes beyond the fix itself

title: feat(studio): a per-page tab id, and the hash-validation verdict
body:
## Why

Two Studio investigations this week ended at "can't tell" rather than "not worth fixing", and both gaps are one small change each.

**No tab id.** `distinct_id` identifies a browser, not a page. A burst of events alternating between two project hashes is indistinguishable from a user moving between projects — and `session_start` fires once per page **load** (`main.tsx:10`), so counting it can't separate them either. Three separate questions stalled on this: whether the `absent_or_empty` bursts are two tabs, whether a 404 belongs to the tab that loaded that hash, and how much of a version's traffic is one person reloading.

**No record of what the hash check decided.** v0.8.52 added a tri-state validation (`ok` / `missing` / `unknown`) and the `unknown` branch deliberately keeps the user's hash when the *check itself* fails. From outside, that is indistinguishable from a check that never ran — different causes, different fixes, one silent bucket. This is what made it impossible to tell whether that fix was working.

## What changes

**`tab_id`** — one id per page load, from a new shared module, attached by **both** transports:

| transport | where |
|---|---|
| `studio:*` | `utils/studioTelemetry.ts` → `getSessionProperties()` |
| `studio_*` | `telemetry/system.ts` → `getBrowserSystemMeta()` |

One module rather than two call sites because these two families have already drifted once on how `agent_runtime` is encoded, and a disagreement here would silently split every tab breakdown.

**Deliberately not persisted.** Storage would survive a reload and quietly turn this into a tab-session id — changing what every existing query means without anyone editing a query. Blocked or cleared storage would also make the property intermittently absent, which reads as "old client" rather than "storage unavailable". A test asserts the module never touches storage at all, so adding either a read or a write fails.

**`project_hash_validated`** — emitted wherever the hash is validated:

```json
{ "stage": "mount", "outcome": "unknown", "status": 500, "url_hash": "my-video" }
```

`status` is present only when the server answered; a rejected request leaves it off rather than inventing one.

## Before

A `session_start` on 0.8.55. Nothing names the page load, and there is no record of any hash check.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a6f3201-b945-40c8-af93-6611deca6cb1)

## After

Same session. `tab_id` names the page load; `project_hash_validated` records what the check decided — including the `unknown` case that keeps the hash.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bd89e63-fa68-4cf0-a764-391ea0200d65)

Both payloads are **generated from the code on each branch**, not restated by hand: the script imports the real `telemetry/system.ts` for the meta block and reads `useServerConnection.ts` to decide whether the verdict event exists. Studio disables telemetry under Vite dev, so a live network capture isn't possible locally, and a UI screenshot would be identical on both sides — this change has no visible surface — which would trip the #4177 same-image gate.

## Verification

- **8 mutants, 8 caught:** regenerate the id per read; persist it to storage; drop `tab_id` from either transport; empty it in the no-DOM fallback; stop emitting the verdict; collapse `unknown` into `missing`; drop `status`.
- The transport wiring has its own test in each family, because the module test passes whether or not anything attaches the value.
- The no-DOM test stubs `window`/`navigator` — without that it re-tests the browser path and never reaches the fallback branch.
- Full studio suite: **5,314 passed / 496 files**. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt clean. Fallow exits 0 (its one finding, `@google/genai` in `packages/cli`, is pre-existing on main).

## Scope

Instrumentation only. No behaviour change, nothing branches on either value. This is §A of `plans/sdk/2026-09-20-stale-project-id-remaining-doors-plan.md`; §B (validate on `hashchange`) and §C (recover at a read 404) follow, and §B's acceptance query needs `tab_id` to exist first.

title: fix(studio): validate the hash on hashchange, and stop pushing dead ids
body:
**#4224 has merged**, so this is rebased onto `main` and is no longer stacked. It uses the `reportHashVerdict` helper that landed in #4224.

## The bug

v0.8.52 taught the **mount** path to validate its hash. The **hashchange** path still adopted whatever the URL offered:

```ts
const next = parseProjectIdFromHash(window.location.hash);
if (next && next !== projectId) setProjectId(next);   // no check
```

So changing projects walked straight around the mount fix. Every later `/api/projects/<id>/...` request 404s for the life of the tab — including the composition read that opens the SDK session, so every edit falls back to the server path and the resolver shadow never runs.

The plan called this "door 2". It is real in code and was unmeasurable in production before #4224 — there was no way to tell a hashchange from a second tab. #4224's `tab_id` makes that distinguishable, so the acceptance query below can now attribute a 404 to this door rather than to a second tab.

## What changes

Same tri-state as mount: `ok` adopts, `unknown` adopts, `missing` falls back to the first project and rewrites the hash.

Three details that aren't obvious from the diff:

**The race guard compares the live hash, not a counter.** This effect is keyed on `[projectId]`, so it re-registers on every project change — a `generation` counter inside that closure resets, and an in-flight verdict from the previous registration compares against its own dead copy and passes. It would adopt a project the user already navigated away from. `window.location.hash` cannot go stale, so that is what the handler re-reads after the await.

**The fallback re-fetches the project list.** `tryConnect` has `data.projects` in scope; this path does not. Caching the mount value would be stale in exactly the long-lived-tab case this exists for. There is a test with two consecutive dead hashes and the list changing between them, because a memo is invisible with only one — my first version of that test passed against the caching mutant.

**Both rewrites use `replaceState`.** `location.hash =` pushes, leaving the dead id one Back away — and Back would then re-validate, fall back, and push again, forever. The mount fallback had the same bug from the other end; fixed here too.

Also emits the hashchange verdict, so the `unknown` branch — which deliberately keeps the hash and looks like success from outside — is countable.

## Before

Navigating to a project that no longer exists. The dead id is adopted, and the URL keeps it.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1be0413-695e-497e-b2df-7bb51c79626d)

## After

Same navigation. The dead id is caught, the first project is opened, and the hash is rewritten — via `replaceState`, so Back does not return to it.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/106b2781-dd93-4d16-a5f1-a7105abcd096)

Printed by mounting the real `useServerConnection` under happy-dom on each branch — observed, not restated. Studio's UI is pixel-identical either way, so a screenshot would trip the #4177 same-image gate.

## Verification

- **7 mutants, 7 caught:** adopt without validating; collapse `unknown` into `missing`; trust the verdict instead of the live hash; memoize the fallback list; push on either rewrite.
- One test had to be rebuilt. My first "does not push" assertion spied on `history.pushState` — which does not catch `location.hash =`, because that pushes by browser navigation, not through the API. The mutant survived, which is how I found it. The test now changes the hash with `replaceState` + a manual `hashchange` dispatch, so the test itself neither pushes nor fires, and any `history.length` growth after that is the hook's.
- Full studio suite: **5,323 passed / 496 files**. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt clean. Fallow exits 0.

## Scope

Closes the hashchange door only. A project deleted *after* a valid mount still poisons the tab — that is the `out-fb1` timeline in the plan, and nothing here catches it. §C (recover at a read 404) does, and is blocked on a product decision: silent redirect vs. a visible "project no longer available" state.

## Note on the stack

If #4224 is **squash-merged**, this branch's base disappears and GitHub retargets this PR to `main`, re-including #4224's diff. Merge that one with a merge commit, or rebase this onto `main` before merging it.

title: feat(studio): say which project this Studio is serving when a read 404s
body:
## Summary

A tab whose project the running Studio cannot resolve failed every composition read with a 404 and said nothing at all. `useSdkSession` recorded the failure to telemetry and returned; the editor looked normal, and every edit silently took the server path instead of the SDK — so nothing the user did landed, and nothing told them why. The `out-fb1` timeline in our own telemetry sat in exactly that state from 13:18 to 14:58, through a reload that passed mount validation.

This adds a banner that names both sides: **"This Studio is serving `out-video1`. This tab was opened for `out-fb1`."**

That wording is the whole truth in the host that produces these 404s. The CLI-embedded Studio serves exactly one project, and `hyperframes preview` reuses port 3002 when the folder matches — so starting it on a *different* folder takes the port out from under an open tab. The project the old tab was pointed at is untouched on disk. "This project is no longer available" would therefore be false twice over: nothing was lost, and the same timeline shows the project come back twice in one afternoon.

When more than one project is served (the Vite host) a rename cannot be told from a deletion, so the banner says *"may have been renamed, moved, or deleted"* and claims no cause.

## Before

Same scenario on the base build: the composition read 404s, and the editor simply looks normal. No banner, no error, no indication that every subsequent edit will be discarded.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/40aece84f837b743ea5be821ab524e90936dbf77/before.png)

## After

Same scenario, same fixture, same moment: the banner names the project this Studio is actually serving.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/40aece84f837b743ea5be821ab524e90936dbf77/after.png)

## What changed

- `useSdkSession` exposes `unreachableProject`, set **only** when the composition read fails with a 404. A 500 or a dropped request says nothing about which project the server serves, and `absent_or_empty` / `missing_content` say nothing about the project at all, so neither claims it.
- `ProjectUnreachableBanner` reads `/api/projects` and picks one of the two wordings. It renders nothing until that list resolves — which wording applies is a claim about what this server serves, and guessing it would flash the wrong one.
- In the single-project case the button reloads, which re-runs the mount-time hash check and lands on the project this server actually serves. That is the same fallback a fresh load already performs, so the button promises nothing beyond what a reload already does.
- `useFileTree` now checks `r.ok` before parsing. An unresolvable project answers 404 with a JSON *body*, so the failure took the success branch and recorded an empty tree **and an empty provenance snapshot for a project that was never read** — which then travelled out in bug reports. This half closes nothing on its own; it stops the recording of a project that does not exist.
- No navigation change and no new API field, so this needs no product decision and behaves identically whether mid-session recovery later auto-falls-back or not.

## What this does not fix

The 404s continue, and telemetry keeps counting them. This ends the *silent* part of the failure, not the failure: a tab in this state still cannot edit — it now knows why, and can get back to the project the server is serving. The stale-id class itself is tracked in `plans/sdk/2026-09-20-stale-project-id-remaining-doors-plan.md`, where §A (#4224) and §B (#4225) are still open.

## Rerunnable check

```
cd packages/studio && bunx vitest run src/components/ProjectUnreachableBanner.test.tsx src/hooks/useFileTree.test.tsx src/hooks/useSdkSession.lifecycle.test.tsx
```

Seven mutations were run against the new guards; six are behavioural and all six were caught: dropping the `r.ok` check; claiming `unreachableProject` for any `http_error` rather than only a 404; never clearing it once the project resolves; treating any non-empty project list as the sole served project; failing to exclude this tab's own project; and rendering before the project list resolves.

The seventh — deleting `reportReadFailure`'s `if (read.reason !== "http_error") return null;` guard — is an *equivalent* mutant, not a gap: every other reason carries no `status`, so `read.status === 404` is false and the function returns `null` either way. The guard is there to narrow the union so `read.status` compiles, and to state the intent.

## Capture method

Both images are the **same scenario, same fixture, same viewport (1440x900), captured at the same moment** — the only difference is the build.

Method: the Studio dev server (`packages/studio`, Vite adapter) with two throwaway fixture projects, `capture-alpha` (two compositions) and `capture-beta` (one). The page is opened on `#project/capture-alpha` and allowed to load fully; then `capture-alpha` is deleted from disk while the page stays open; then the second composition is clicked in the sidebar, which re-runs the composition read against the now-unresolvable project → 404. Nothing else is driven.

The Vite host is used because it needs no Studio build to stand up, and the banner is host-agnostic — the read, the status code and the state it sets are identical on the CLI host. The CLI host reaches the same state by port reuse: `hyperframes preview` reuses port 3002 for the same folder, so starting it on a different folder leaves an open tab pointing at a project that server does not serve. Both screenshots also show the pre-existing `Failed to load second.html (404)` toast, which is the only feedback that existed before this change.

title: chore: release v0.8.57
body:
## Summary

Release **v0.8.57**. Merging this PR publishes: the workflow checks out the merge SHA, creates the `v0.8.57` tag there, publishes to npm, and cuts the GitHub release.

The release summary, as written into `releases/v0.8.57.md` and `docs/changelog.mdx`:

> Studio now says which project it is actually serving when a link points at one it cannot open, instead of failing quietly. Links to a project that was renamed or deleted are caught as you navigate, and the address bar is corrected.

**Features** — the unreachable-project banner (#4228); per-page `tab_id` and the hash-validation verdict event (#4224); preview overlay guides (#4220); speed-ramp editing with a rate lane (#4153).

title: feat(studio): render geometry-sized video filmstrips
body:
## Summary

Video clips request a geometry-sized filmstrip after measurement and keep a one-frame poster tier available during fast scroll. Geometry requests use stable quantized cache identities and one 4K geometry ceiling.

## Before

Origin/main, timeline region at Fit with video clips and the Voiceover audio row at rest:

![Before, Fit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a32f287-dc9b-4798-a3f0-215bfdf8a8fe)

Origin/main, mid-scroll timeline region with video clips and the Voiceover audio row:

![Before, mid-scroll](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2789056-8243-4cc2-95ff-b02e58e7edf8)

Origin/main, the same timeline at 4x zoom and the same scroll position as After:

![Before, 4x zoom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/664d5c0c-32ef-476b-bfa2-bce991c2fc04)

Origin/main, 400% zoom, Glass Intro filling the lane from the start. The long clip paints a real poster strip.

![Before, 4x, Glass Intro in view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8de1f10e-51c4-470c-9989-cb1911a25ae2)

## After

After the change, timeline region at Fit with video clips and the Voiceover audio row:

![After, Fit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed78b2a0-f746-4dd7-80e0-1b3a2289d455)

After the change, timeline region at 4x zoom with video clips and the Voiceover audio row:

![After, 4x zoom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8219a4bb-1b94-47ed-b2ee-8eceacd475e1)

Same zoom and scroll. Glass Intro paints tiles across the full clip.

![After, 4x, Glass Intro in view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6280938-bbce-4192-8886-ff9fd59f15b8)

The Footage Frame 1 and Footage Frame 2 `no preview` labels are not an intended 4x behavior. The non-rich one-frame poster lease remains active at every zoom and is the fallback while rich work is unavailable; those rows are failing both poster and rich decoding in this capture and therefore remain an open preview defect, not an expected filmstrip state.

## Decode cost

Devbox decode-cost proxy on the 1080x1920 fixture, evenly spaced timestamps across the first 6 seconds, 3 runs: 6 frames averaged 1.67 s; 20 frames averaged 5.47 s, 3.26x. The 500px example needs 5 visible frames but quantizes the rich request to 8, trading a bounded decode step for stable cache identities. Every video clip now enqueues TWO jobs where main enqueued one, against `concurrentVideoDecodes: 2`; the 1-frame poster is what paints during scroll, and the filmstrip follows once scrolling settles.

## Scheduler safety

120 mounted clips do not decode 20 frames each at once. The scheduler limits video work to the concurrency bucket at `packages/studio/src/player/lib/thumbnailScheduler.ts:345-348`, pauses only rich work while scrolling at `packages/studio/src/player/lib/thumbnailScheduler.ts:207-210` and `:258-261`, and retains results only within byte and entry budgets at `packages/studio/src/player/lib/thumbnailScheduler.ts:327-334` and `:384-392`, configured by `packages/studio/src/player/lib/timelineViewportBudgets.ts:70-82`. The one-frame poster request is non-rich, so it remains eligible during scrolling. Quantised request counts and the cache byte budget keep a 120-clip timeline from holding 120 x 20 decoded frames.

## Validation

- Focused Studio suites: 26 tests passed for poster deferral, two-tier requests, and thumbnail geometry.
- Studio typecheck passed after generated core artifacts were built; Oxlint and oxfmt passed on the changed files.
- The capture script waited for readiness, asserted a non-zero clip count, and asserted the audio control before taking screenshots.
- The 4K ceiling is `Math.ceil(3840 / (66 * (16 / 9)))`, named once with its geometry reasoning beside the owner budget.

title: fix(docs): restore the sidebar gutter on catalog pages
body:
## Summary

Catalog pages had no left gutter: the title, install block and stage sat flush against the sidebar's border on desktop, and flush against the screen edge on a phone. Every other page on the docs site has one.

Catalog pages set `mode: "frame"` so the stage and the Tune panel get the full content width (`scripts/generate-catalog-pages.ts`). Frame mode renders no `main#content-container`, and that element is exactly what carries the theme's `px-5 lg:pr-10 lg:pl-[5.5rem]`. Losing the container lost the gutter with it.

This re-applies the same padding to frame-mode pages only. The values are the theme's own class list, not new ones.

## Measured on the live site

Playwright against `https://hyperframes.heygen.com/catalog/blocks/canopy-part-title`, with the rule injected for the "after" column:

| Viewport | Before | After | Matches |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1440 | title at x=308, sidebar edge at x=308 (0px) | title at x=396 (88px) | `lg:pl-[5.5rem]` |
| 390 | title at x=0, flush to the screen edge | title at x=20 (20px) | `px-5` |

Cross-checked in a browser at a 1523 viewport: `/introduction` puts its title at x=422, and the catalog page with this rule also puts it at x=422.

## Scope

`mode: "frame"` appears in 412 files under `docs/`, all of them under `docs/catalog/`, and nothing else on the site carries `is-frame`. The `/catalog` gallery landing is one of them and had the same defect; it gains the same gutter and its three-column grid is unchanged at 3 x 304px.

Between 1024px and roughly 1200px the stage is about 88px narrower than before. That is the same squeeze every other page on the site takes at that width, and the alternative is leaving the catalog misaligned with the rest of the docs.

No screenshots: the live composition player on a catalog page never goes idle, so a headless screenshot times out there. The layout numbers above were taken on two machines instead.

title: fix(studio): report a rejected read as a network reason, not an open failure
body:
## The problem

`stage: "open"` means `openComposition` threw — an unparseable composition, or OOM. Every event in that bucket on 0.8.56 and 0.8.57 says something else:

| error message | 0.8.56 users | 0.8.57 users |
|---|---|---|
| `Failed to fetch` | 28 | 11 |
| `Load failed` | 2 | 1 |
| `NetworkError when attempting to fetch resource.` | 3 | 1 |

All three are fetch rejections — the request never produced a response. So this is the largest SDK-session failure class in Studio (2.9% of session users on 0.8.56, 2.3% on 0.8.57) and it has been filed as a parser problem.

The cause is one missing `catch`. `readProjectFileOptional` awaits `fetch` with no try/catch, so a rejected request escapes the function and is caught by the effect's outer `.catch` — the handler written for `openComposition`. The read path has a five-member reason union precisely so this class of failure is diagnosable, and the one case that never produces a response was the case outside it.

`absent_or_empty`, `http_error`, `unsafe_path` and `missing_content` all got their own reason; a rejection had none, and took the label of a different failure. The class was therefore unaddressable: you cannot fix a network failure while it is reported as a composition that failed to parse.

## The change

`readProjectFileOptional` catches its own fetch rejection and returns `reason: "network"`, so it lands in `stage: read` with everything else. `stage: open` now means only what its comment says it means.

Telemetry only. Nothing branches on the stage, and no user-facing behaviour changes.

This is the same split that has shipped four times now — `ineligible_operation` (v0.8.49), `stage: read` (v0.8.51), `block_detail` (#4214), and this. Three of the four exposed a real bug underneath, and the earlier `stage: read` split is what made this one findable.

## Before

A rejected fetch on the composition read, on 0.8.57 and earlier. The payload claims the composition failed to open.

![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/60044a80e128fdb84dec5f4879d58b4045308e79/before.png)

## After

The same rejected fetch. It is a read failure with a network reason, and `stage: open` is left to mean what it says.

![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/60044a80e128fdb84dec5f4879d58b4045308e79/after.png)

## What this does not fix

Nothing user-facing. 11 users on 0.8.57 still hit a request that never completes, and this change only makes that countable and addressable.

That class has a starting point already, and it is not the server: the team vault carries a page for this exact signature — a bare `Failed to fetch` with **no** entry in the browser's Network panel means the request never left the browser, and points at CSP `connect-src`, Private Network Access, or an extension rewriting `fetch`. That page records nine diagnoses spent server-side before the console was read. The AbortError work also found extension fetch wrappers interfering with Studio's requests, which is consistent.

So the next move is a browser-side triage of `reason: "network"`, not a server fix — and that triage is only possible once this label exists.

## Also in this PR: a test left stale by #4238

`scripts/catalog-detail.test.ts` was asserting the exact strings #4238 deleted:

```
.hf-ve-tabs-row { margin: 20px 0 0 16px; }
.hf-ve-body { padding: 2rem 0 0 16px; }
```

That PR removed both insets on purpose — its comment says "the page gutter is the page's job, and a second 16px here put everything below the stage on a different left edge from the title, install block and stage above it" — and restored the inset on `#content-area` in `docs/custom.css` instead. The test was not updated, so **main has been red on it since**, unnoticed because the `Test` workflow does not run for a docs-only change. This PR is the first to touch `packages/studio` since, which is why it surfaced here.

The invariant did not change — this content is still inset from the page edge. Only the mechanism did, so the test now asserts both halves of it: the two rules carry no inset of their own, **and** the gutter that replaces them is still present at both its values. Asserting only the first would keep passing if the gutter were deleted outright, which is the regression the test exists to catch. Both mutations were run and both fail the test.

## Rerunnable check

```
cd packages/studio && bunx vitest run src/hooks/useSdkSession.lifecycle.test.tsx
```

Two mutations were run against the new guard and both were caught: removing the try/catch so the rejection escapes to `stage: open` again, and labelling a rejection `http_error` with a synthetic status instead of `network`.

## Capture method

Both images are the payload Studio emits when the composition read's fetch rejects, produced by running `useSdkSession` against a rejecting `fetch` on `main` and on this branch. Nothing visible changes in the product, so a UI screenshot would be identical on both sides and would trip the same-image gate from #4177 — the payload is the artifact. Same approach as #4214.

title: Harden capture file writes against pre-existing symlinks
body:
The centralized capture-file writer uses restrictive permissions but does not require exclusive creation. A local pre-planted symlink could therefore redirect a capture write.

Harden the writer with exclusive-create semantics or an equivalent containment guard, while preserving any intentional overwrite behavior, and add a regression test for a pre-existing symlink.

This is a local-access hardening follow-up; captured website content is not the threat actor.

### [`v1.5.0`](https://redirect.github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/blob/HEAD/packages/prompts/CHANGELOG.md#150)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/compare/@clack/prompts@1.4.0...@clack/prompts@1.5.0)

##### Minor Changes

- [#​543](https://redirect.github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/pull/543) [`83428ac`](https://redirect.github.com/bombshell-dev/clack/commit/83428ac6d8bc5eda87615cc7b1f14e0c8b16e1b6) Thanks [@​florian-lefebvre](https://redirect.github.com/florian-lefebvre)! - Adds support for Standard Schema validation

  Prompts accept an optional `validate()` function to validate user input. While a function provides more flexibility and customization over your validation, it can be a bit verbose. To help solve this, there are libraries that provide schema-based validation to make shorthand and type-strict validation substantially easier.

  Libraries following the [Standard Schema specification](https://redirect.github.com/standard-schema/standard-schema) are now natively supported. For example, using [Arktype](https://arktype.io/):

  ```diff
  import { text } from '@clack/prompts';
  import { type } from 'arktype';

  const name = await text({
  	message: 'Enter your email',
  +	validate: type('string.email').describe('Invalid email'),
  });
  ```

title: fix(player): detect the runtime by __player and honour runtime-src for src embeds
body:
Closes #4002
Closes #4003

## Problem

Two related defects in how `<hyperframes-player src="...">` discovers and injects the core runtime:

1. **`window.__hf` was treated as the runtime bridge.** `@hyperframes/shader-transitions` also creates that global (`window.__hf = window.__hf || {}`) to publish `shaderTransitionsReady`. Any authored composition that uses shader transitions and registers its own `__timelines` therefore looked like it already had the runtime: the probe never injected it, `hasRuntimeBridge()` refused the direct-timeline adapter, and the element emitted `error: "Composition timeline not found after 8s"` with a black frame (#4002).
2. **`runtime-src` only applied to srcdoc.** The probe's late injection closed over the module-level CDN constant, so an `src` embed always fetched the runtime from jsDelivr even when the element carried a valid `runtime-src`. Offline, air-gapped, or behind a `script-src 'self'` CSP that silently fails and the embed times out (#4003).

## Fix

- `hasRuntimeBridge(win)` now checks for `window.__player` only. The core runtime installs `__player` synchronously in the same task as `__hf` (`initSandboxRuntimeModular` has no awaits between the two), so there is no tick on which a real runtime has `__hf` but not `__player`. Both the probe tick's `hasRuntime` and the adapter path use the same helper.
- The `runtime-src` resolver in `shader-options.ts` is exported as `resolveRuntimeUrlFromElement` and the player hands it to the probe via a new `resolveRuntimeUrl` callback. It is read at injection time, so a `runtime-src` set after construction is still honoured. The existing origin/loopback validation is unchanged and now covers both paths.
- The injected `<script>` gets an `onerror` handler: a blocked or 404 runtime now stops the probe and reports `HyperFrames runtime failed to load from <url>` instead of waiting out the 8 s timeout with a message about the timeline.

## Tests

New unit tests in `composition-probe.test.ts` cover: the shader-transitions `__hf` namespace next to `__timelines` resolving via the direct-timeline adapter; `__player` still winning over `__timelines`; injection into a nested composition despite a pre-existing `__hf`; injection using `resolveRuntimeUrl`; and the script error path stopping the probe without a second timeout error. `hyperframes-player.test.ts` gains an element-level test that an `src` embed with `runtime-src` injects the configured URL.

`bun run --filter @hyperframes/player test` (excluding the pre-existing slideshow presenter-mode failures, which fail identically on `main` in this environment), `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, the lefthook pre-commit gate, and the player build with `verify-runtime-pin.mjs` all pass.

Repro from the issues (both `host.html` variants in the linked gist) is expected to report `ready` for the shader-transitions composition and to request `/local-runtime.js` instead of jsDelivr for the `src` embed.

title: docs(changelog): weekly digest 2026-09-14 to 2026-09-21
body:
## What

The weekly digest for September 14 to 21, added to `docs/weekly-updates.mdx`. One file, additive.

## Why

The Monday changelog cron. This week was large: 242 non-merge commits, 176 of them carrying a PR link.

## How

Generated with `bun run changelog:weekly --from 2026-09-14 --to 2026-09-21 --write`, then rewritten. The generator picked 10 items and split them Highlights / Also-notable, which buried the week's actual story, so the entry is grouped by theme instead: Studio becoming composable for host apps, speed ramps landing end to end, timeline editing, the design system and dock layout, motion blur, long renders, playback and output, CLI.

Two things worth flagging for reviewers:

- **Segmented capture is described as opt-in, because it is.** `renderOrchestrator.ts` says so directly: the duration constant that would make it default is "not the shipped default: that flip is its own release step, gated on the 40-minute soak." The entry says `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE` and does not claim a default.
- **Speed ramps are described as ungated**, checked at HEAD rather than assumed from the commit subjects.

No SHA in this entry was hand-typed. The digest was written with `{{c:<sha>}}` / `{{p:<n>}}` tokens and expanded by a script that refuses to write unless every SHA resolves to 40 characters, prefix-matches, is an ancestor of `origin/main`, and falls inside the digest window, and unless every cited PR number appears in the subject of the commit it is cited beside. 53 commits, 53 PRs, 53 pairings verified.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)

Docs-only, so every code job path-filters to skipping. `Validate docs` and `Format` are the gates that matter. Link targets verified by the expansion script above; PR titles spot-checked against the API.

title: feat(studio): typed audio values, clip fades, audible video drops
body:
## What

Three audio changes in Studio, plus the fix they surfaced.

- **Typed values.** The readout beside Volume, Speed and Media start is click-to-type. Enter or blur commits, Escape cancels, a refused value stays open and turns red. Volume takes dB as shown ("-6", "+0.5 dB", "-inf") or "x0.8" / "80%". Speed takes "1.5x", "1.5" or "150%". Times take "2.5", "2.5s", "500ms" or "1:02.5". Mixing is exact work; a 200px slider is not.
- **Speed presets are video-only.** The row no longer renders for an `<audio>` clip. The presets are picture-driven ramps; on a bare audio clip they only warp pitch.
- **Clip fades.** `data-fade-in` / `data-fade-out` in seconds, on `<audio>` and on `<video data-has-audio="true">`. Studio shows them as Fade in / Fade out rows in the Design tab and as dots at the top corners of the clip in the timeline: drag inward to set, the faded region shades as a wedge, release lands one undoable edit.
- **Dropped videos keep their sound.** The drop path wrote every video as `muted` with no `data-has-audio`, so preview silenced it and the mixer skipped its track. The media metadata endpoint now reports `hasAudio` from the ffprobe call it already makes, and a video with an audio stream lands as `data-has-audio="true"` with no `muted`.

## How

- Core: `audioFade.ts` owns the attributes, parsing and the gain curve (`fadeGain`), exported at `@hyperframes/core/audio-fade`. Linear on both sides, which is ffmpeg's `afade` default (`tri`), so preview and render agree without a curve table. Fades that together outrun the clip scale down to meet inside it. A fade multiplies whatever the level resolved to: `data-volume`, a volume lane, probed keyframes. Decibel conversion lives in `audioDbToGain` / `audioGainToDb`.
- Runtime: `syncRuntimeMedia` multiplies `fadeGain` into the author volume at clip-local time, the same time base the volume lane uses. A 0, negative, or NaN fade never reaches a media element's `volume`.
- Engine: `AudioElement` / `AudioTrack` carry `fadeIn` / `fadeOut`; one shared filter chain appends `afade` after the volume filter in both the master and the group-member graphs. A fade-out ends at the clip's end, so it also silences an FX tail and follows a later trim.
- Studio: `FlatSliderReadout` is the click-to-type readout, opt-in per `FlatSlider` via `onCommitText`. `audioInspectorInput.ts` holds the three parsers and returns null on garbage so the field stays open and turns red. `TimelineClipFades` renders the dots and wedges and writes through the existing live-then-quiet attribute path the FX rack uses. `TimelineElement` gains `hasAudio`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`.
- Docs: `html-schema.mdx`, the CLI `data-attributes.md` and `core.md` document the two attributes.

Fades ship as `data-fade-in` / `data-fade-out` attributes composing over the resolved level.

## Before

![Before: selected audio clip on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6566b76-f08d-4466-8304-9818390d8981)

Music clip selected on current main: the readouts are labels, the Speed preset row shows on an audio clip, there are no Fade rows, and the clip has no fade handles.

## After

![After: selected audio clip with fade controls](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc0c6d56-046a-4dba-819c-88a06b8468b2)

Same clip on this branch: readouts are click-to-type, Speed preset is gone for audio, Fade in / Fade out rows appear, and the clip carries fade dots with the faded region shaded.

## Checks

- Core, engine, studio and studio-server typecheck clean; oxlint and oxfmt clean; pre-commit fallow gate green.
- New tests: fade math (including 0 / negative / NaN / longer-than-clip), engine parser and `afade` builder (filter order and trim-anchored fade-out), runtime fade over `data-volume` plus illegal fade values, typed readout (refused input stays open and `aria-invalid`), input parsers, inspector audio rows, timeline fade handles, drop builder muted vs audible, server `hasAudio`.
- Render path: the built engine mixed a steady 220 Hz fixture through real ffmpeg with fade-in 1 s and fade-out 3 s. Measured level ramps from silence over the first second, holds flat, and returns to silence over the last three.
- Studio: dragged the fade-in dot from 1 s to 4.02 s and the file updated; typed "-6 dB" into Volume and "0.75" into Fade out and both landed; dropped an mp4 with a stereo AAC track and it inserted with `data-has-audio="true"` and no `muted`, took fade dots, and the mixer parsed it as a track.

title: chore: release v0.8.59
body:
# HyperFrames v0.8.59

Released on 2026-09-21.

Studio makes audio edits easier with typed values, fades, sound-aware video drops, and timeline meters. The CLI can search media and let agents edit timelines while previews reach their first frame with less setup.

## Features

- **Studio:** Type audio values, fade clip edges, and keep sound when dropping a video with audio ([839ae426d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/839ae426ddbcb3ad13ba21c586d87cde3aefa6f5), [#4250](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4250)).
- **CLI:** Search media assets through media-use ([3091dcb78](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/3091dcb787163db2e9d6082d926fe7a332d4ae4d), [#4230](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4230)).
- **CLI:** Let agents edit timelines through timeline workflows ([4e9059ad5](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/4e9059ad598add05f9b74346526e7ee3daddb1c4), [#4241](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4241)).
- **Studio:** See audio level meters at the timeline's right edge ([97420736d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/97420736d56e6feef7396c8d100a33b2e913844a), [#4193](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4193)).
- **Studio:** Compose a timeline from the parts a host app needs ([064192155](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/0641921558eadcee0a026fa6db39e3e9e5b76f62), [#4229](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4229)).

## Fixes

- **CLI:** Keep partial site captures after a deadline and navigate pages without WebGL ([952e9228b](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/952e9228b5cdf4387ecb4b6f220ef8e5d9143a73), [#4215](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4215)).

## Performance

- **Player:** Prepare previews from only the assets needed for their first frame ([16fab47a8](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/16fab47a8eb245feab1cc786b9c9c14e41487283), [#4239](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4239)).

## Full changelog

https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/compare/v0.8.58...v0.8.59

## No visible change

This release PR updates package versions and release notes. The user-visible changes are listed above.

title: ci: ratchet test reachability across workflow filters
body:
Adds an unconditional, dependency-free CI check that maps tracked test files through workflow jobs, package scripts, runner selection and guarded paths. New orphan tests and uncovered guard paths fail. Existing debt is ratcheted at 45 test files, 83 violations; baseline counts can only shrink.

Declare cross-directory ownership with a first-line `// guards: <glob>` or `scripts/test-reachability.json`. Custom shell runners have exact-command mappings and source fingerprints. A changed producer requires reviewing and refreshing its mapping and reason. There is no blanket test exclusion allowlist.

Verified on head `694797ec17e4ae2f5c8bcdad406e8903ae9c1473` by [CI](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/actions/runs/35673653368/job/106575668654), using Node 22 on Ubuntu. The planted guard-filter hole fails before its route is restored. Both shell-condition probes now report unreachable, while ordinary sequential runners remain credited:

```text
ok 1 - planted guard-filter hole fails and adding its directory passes
ok 18 - single-line shell conditions cannot credit their guarded runner
ok 19 - folded shell conditions cannot credit their guarded runner
ok 22 - ordinary sequential runners remain reachable
ok 25 - a missing pinned package gives the runner mapping diagnostic
# tests 25
# pass 25
# fail 0
Test reachability verified: 45 baselined test files.
```

The baseline remains 45 files and 83 findings. The review fix also rejects fallback branches, directory changes, false commands and negation. Missing pinned sources produce the mapping-review diagnostic; `scripts/test-reachability.md` documents that only `ci.yml` is modelled. Full CI and approving review remain pending on this head.
