title: feat(studio): panel tabs take the decided Current design
body:
Studio's panels become cards on a dark shell, and each panel's tabs take the "Current" design: the open tab is a fill in the card's colour that slides to the tab you pick, only the open tab shows its icon and close glyph, and a strip that is too narrow scrolls with a soft edge instead of hiding tabs behind a menu. This replaces the pill, underline and close treatment that was on this PR before.

## Before

![Before 2x: main, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00ec6f33-082a-4209-917d-dea3c73c5b3d)

![Before 2x: main, paper theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09b01028-fa94-4946-bc47-a9abe7111a2f)

## After

![After 2x: dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/041dfebf-c2cd-48bb-9ad4-5200d9f2ef9a)

![After 2x: paper theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d901bda4-ed7a-462f-8b83-0a7e3d4a7eff)

Switching tabs (the fill slides in about 140 ms and the new icon fades in over 80 ms; the panel body switches at once):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d359ada-c9e1-4425-9c95-61d5d4f5271b

### Every label whole, and the tabs use the whole strip (2x)

An earlier head clipped the left strip's fourth tab next to empty strip space. That space was a 72 px slot (plus 4 px) held on every strip for the strip actions, even on strips whose panel is not focused and so draws no actions. Dockview sizes that slot by its content; this PR had pinned it. Now the slot takes room only where the actions are drawn, so an unfocused strip gives its tabs the whole width. Tab padding is 6 px with no gap between tabs, so the tabs also fit next to the actions. Labels, icons and close glyphs sit on the tab's centre in every strip.

Left strip at 1440 x 900, tabs width against the room before the action slot:

| | macOS | Linux (these captures) |
|---|---|---|
| Earlier head | 322 in 280, clipped | 312 in 280, clipped |
| Now, panel unfocused | 278 in 358 | 268 in 358 |
| Now, panel focused (actions shown) | 278 in 282 | 268 in 282 |

![Left strip 2x at 1440, earlier head: Catalog clipped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42d8eae9-67f5-49b6-b581-19c5185a4bdc)

![Left strip 2x at 1440, now: every label whole](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc5d9137-1cfe-42eb-a6cd-f8bd90c19b4d)

![Left strip 2x at 1440, panel focused: actions shown, labels still whole](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66ce47c2-5bd9-47ca-870e-9c3acf6001fc)

At 1280 x 800 the left column is narrower, and the pinned slot clipped Catalog next to the empty space. Room for the tabs there went from 241 px to 317 px:

![Left strip 2x at 1280, earlier head: Catalog clipped next to the empty action slot](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0603454-7c2f-4a4c-98b4-9028bc9c0d31)

![Left strip 2x at 1280, now: the tabs use the whole strip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3dfb3ce-ccb8-4221-8339-e481ff31df7f)

Captured at the PR head (5fd6c7bd) from a fixture project (the `warm-grain` registry example) in headless Chrome on Linux, 2x, each state loaded fresh so Studio builds its default layout for that window. Before is `main`; the strip Befores use the earlier heads' `dock.css` (8079c635 at 1440, 8ed7ab69 at 1280) on the same build. The macOS column was measured live in Chrome on macOS. The paper theme only re-themes the timeline today, so the panels look the same in both themes.

## What changed

- **Cards on the shell.** Each dock group is a card with the only 1 px border (radius 10) and a 6 px gutter to its neighbours. The preview and timeline no longer draw a second rounded border inside it; the preview stage is an inset well. Dockview's tab dividers and separators are gone.
- **Tabs.** Tabs use the whole strip unless the panel shows its actions. Every label is whole at the default 1440 x 900 layout (6 px side padding, no gap between tabs), and labels and icons are centred in the tab. The open tab is a fill with rounded top corners, flush with the card body. Only the open tab shows its type icon and close glyph (the glyph appears on hover or keyboard focus, and its space is kept so the label never moves). Other tabs are labels.
- **One sliding fill per strip.** One element slides (transform and width, 140 ms ease-out) under the open tab. Reduced motion turns the slide and the icon fade off. Hover is instant.
- **Strip actions** (panel menu, maximise or restore, close group) sit on the active group only, at half opacity while the pointer is in the panel and full on hover or focus. They take room only on the strip that draws them, so the other strips give their tabs the whole width. The panel menu lists that side's panels as checkboxes, plus Reset layout.
- **Narrow strips** scroll sideways with a 12 px fade on the clipped edge. Dockview's overflow dropdown is off.
- Tokens: `--panel-shell-bg`, `--panel-card-bg`, `--panel-card-border`, `--panel-strip-bg`, `--panel-tab-bg-hover`, with contrast pairs registered.

## Timeline viewport gate

The first head of this rebuild (b20ff32a4) cost the timeline gate one frame on CI: interaction p95 33 ms on every run (first attempt 100 ms on three runs), against main's 20 ms. Main-thread traces were identical; the extra cost was compositing, from a fade mask on every tab strip. Masking only a strip that is actually clipped brought it back:

| Head | Interaction p95 per run (ms) | Frame p95 (ms) | Runs passing |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 20, 20, 19, 20, 18 | 34 | 5/5 |
| b20ff32a4 (rerun) | 33, 33, 33, 33, 33 | 33 | 5/5 |
| 41302773 | 18, 20, 19, 20, 17 | 33 | 5/5 |
| eefaa839 | 18, 20, 18, 18, 20 | 17 | 5/5 |
| af4f2b9b (tab spacing), first attempt | 18, 79, 18, 116, 19 | 100 | 3/5 |
| af4f2b9b, rerun | 18, 16, 20, 18, 18 | 33 | 5/5 |
| 8ed7ab69 | 17, 16, 19, 24, 20 | 33 | 5/5 |
| 6a5edd89 | 33, 33, 33, 33, 33 | 17 | 5/5 |

From about 14:30Z `main` itself reads 33 ms on every run (three consecutive `main` CI runs), and CI tests this PR merged with the current `main`, so the 6a5edd89 row matches `main`'s level at that time.

The af4f2b9b first attempt had three runs at main's level and two single-run spikes; the same commit's rerun passed 5/5, and the change is tab spacing only.

## Tests

Each rule that could regress without anyone noticing has a test, and each test was proved by breaking the code once:

| Rule | Test | Break | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Icon and close glyph on the open tab only | `DockTabs.test.tsx` (dock.css applied, computed display) | delete the hide rule | 2 red |
| Actions on the active group only | `DockTabs.test.tsx` | drop the active-group check | 1 red |
| One fill per strip, following the open tab | `DockTabs.test.tsx` | fill stays at 0 / a second fill | 1 red each |
| One border per surface | `dockTabs.contract.test.ts` | add a strip border | 1 red |
| Only the slide and icon fade animate | `dockTabs.contract.test.ts` | add a hover transition | 1 red |
| Reduced motion turns them off | `dockTabs.contract.test.ts` | remove the reduced-motion rule | 1 red |
| Label and icon centred in the tab | `dockTabs.contract.test.ts` | drop the full-height rule | 1 red |
| Every tab label whole at 1440 x 900 on each strip while its panel is focused (the least room it gets), with 10 px for macOS's wider system font (CI renders a Linux fallback) | `scripts/studio-runtime-smoke.mjs` (CI "Studio: load smoke", real Chrome) | the "Ca" head's spacing; a spacing that fits on Linux but clips on macOS | red on both ("312px of tabs in 280px", "276px of tabs in 280px"); green on main and this head |
| Unfocused strips hold no room for actions they do not draw | `scripts/studio-runtime-smoke.mjs` | pin the action slot at 72 px again | red: "3 inactive dock strips hold width for actions they do not draw" |
| The shown tab stays whole when its strip narrows (its panel gains focus and the actions appear), comes back narrower than it was before it was hidden, or when a neighbouring tab closes and it moves | `DockTabs.test.tsx` | ignore each of those changes in turn | 1 red each; checked live at 1280 x 800: clicking into the left panel's body used to leave Catalog 37 px hidden, now it is whole |
| A strip the user scrolled by hand stays put when something else in the dock changes, when it widens, and through another panel's maximise and restore | `DockTabs.test.tsx` | reveal on every pass; on any width change; after a hidden spell | red each; checked live: a hand scroll of 20 px is still 20 px after a maximise and restore |

Run alone, each exits 0: `DockTabs.test.tsx` 5, `dockTabs.contract.test.ts` 5, `Dock.test.tsx` 14, `dockAccessibility.test.ts` 10, `PreviewPane.test.tsx` 1, `Menu.test.tsx` 10, `scripts/contrastRatchet.test.ts` passing.

## Independent review

An adversarial review (separate agent, mandate to refute) at 41302773, eefaa839, 8079c635, af4f2b9b and 8ed7ab69: **no blockers; one major, fixed.**

- MAJOR (af4f2b9b), fixed in 8ed7ab69: CI renders Studio's system font stack with a narrower Linux fallback, so the clip check could pass while a Mac clips. The check now keeps 10 px of room for the macOS font, and a spacing that fits on Linux but clips on macOS turns it red. The 8ed7ab69 review asked whether 10 px holds for every strip, not just the left one it was measured on. Measured macOS minus Linux tab width at 1440 x 900: left 10 px, right 6 px, Preview and Timeline 2 px each, so the left strip is the widest gap and 10 px covers all four.
- MINOR, left as is: the room check has no unit test of its own; it runs only in a real browser, and the smoke is its test (red on both broken spacings above).

- MINOR: a panel cannot be closed from the focused tab itself by keyboard. The keyboard path is focused tab, Tab to "Panel menu", Enter, uncheck the panel (checked live: closes that one panel; checking it again reopens it). The tab's close glyph is not focusable, the same as dockview's stock tab on main, because a tab cannot hold a focusable button.
- MINOR: the open tab is 16 px wider than on the design page (the close glyph's space is kept; see For Miguel).
- Resolved: a contrast pair cited stale line numbers.

## UX checklist

**Job:** someone editing a video moves between panels (Compositions, Assets, Code, Catalog; Design, Layers, Renders, Variables) many times an hour and needs to see which one is open and reach the next without hunting.
**One action:** click the tab of the panel you want.

| # | Question | Y/N | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First-time user knows what to do | Y | Tabs keep their labels; the open tab is joined to the body it controls (After captures) |
| 2 | Interactive things look interactive | N | Strip actions are hidden until the pointer is in the panel (Miguel's decision; see Traded off) |
| 3 | User's words, no internal ids | Y | Titles unchanged; controls named "Close Design", "Panel menu", "Maximize panel", "Close group" |
| 4 | Works like other tools | Y | Editor-style tabs with maximise and a panel menu |
| 5 | Guidance at the control | N | The three icon buttons have accessible names but no visible tooltip |
| 6 | Primary action reachable without reading | Y | The tabs are the strip |
| 7 | Exactly one primary action | Y | Tabs; actions are secondary and quiet |
| 8 | Counts match data | Y | Titles come from each panel through `Dock.Panel` (`Dock.tsx` setTitle) |
| 9 | Excluded items announce themselves | Y | Every label is whole at the default width (the load smoke checks it); a narrowed strip scrolls with an edge fade, and the panel menu lists every panel |
| 10 | Long names recoverable | Y | Tabs never truncate; the strip scrolls |
| 11 | Keyboard path | Y | Arrow keys move and activate tabs (existing); strip actions are buttons and show on focus |
| 12 | Nothing hover-only that must be acted on | N | Same as 2 |
| 13 | Refusals say what next | n/a | No refusals here |
| 14 | Refusal next to the thing | n/a | |
| 15 | Error prevented | n/a | |
| 16 | Can leave any state without losing work | Y | Closed panels reopen from Window or the panel menu; Reset layout restores the default |
| 17 | Destructive looks different | N | "Close group" uses the same x as a tab's close; it loses no work, and the Window menu reopens the panels |
| 18 | Empty state names what is empty | n/a | |
| 19 | Feedback within 400 ms | Y | The tab state and icon change in the same frame as the click; the fill arrives in 140 ms |
| 20 | Progress on waits | n/a | |
| 21 | Hand-built state survives reload | Y | Layout, open tab and maximised group persist per project (existing dock persistence) |

**Choice:** four tabs per side, one click each. **The end:** the panel body appears at once and the fill settles under the tab you picked.
**Not exercised:** a screen reader pass; touch input.
**Traded off:** hover-only strip actions (rows 2 and 12) and scroll-plus-fade instead of an overflow menu when a strip is narrowed are Miguel's decided design.

## For Miguel

- **Paper (light) theme:** Studio's paper block only re-themes the timeline today, so the panels are dark in both the Before and After paper shots. Panel paper values are Desktop's to set (design principles, section 7); this PR adds the token names Desktop can override.
- **Action slot:** the design review asked for the action slot to be reserved on every strip, so tabs never move when focus changes panel. That reservation is what clipped "Ca" next to empty space, so it now holds room only on the focused panel. The cost: when a strip that is already too narrow gains focus, its actions take 76 px. The strip then scrolls so the shown tab stays whole, and a neighbouring tab can go under the edge fade. At the default 1440 x 900 nothing clips either way.
- **Tab spacing:** side padding is 6 px (10 on the design page) and tabs have no gap. The design's 10 px would need 322 px on macOS; the left strip has 282 px beside its actions at 1440. A wider default left column would allow the design padding again. A narrower window scrolls the strip with the edge fade; per the decision there is no overflow chevron.
- **Close glyph space:** the open tab keeps its close glyph's space at rest, so it is 16 px wider than on the design page, where the label shifts on hover.
- **Not in this PR:** inspector section headers and the focused-card border step (later build steps).

title: fix(engine): read extensible PCM and float WAV headers
body:
FFmpeg can write PCM and IEEE-float audio inside a WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (`0xFFFE`) header. The FX reader rejected these files and the volume-envelope reader declined to apply gain. Both now resolve the complete sub-format GUID through one shared helper to the existing PCM/float codecs. Truncated extensions and unknown GUIDs remain rejected; sample-width limits are unchanged.

Reader change: 30 added lines, 18 removed across three source files. No encoder pinning, baseline changes, or added skips.

Validation:
- Captured complete four-channel PCM and float WAV files from FFmpeg 8.1.1. Always-running regression tests decode their samples through the FX reader and apply gain through the envelope reader, preserving the header.
- Added rejection tests for unknown GUIDs, chunk-boundary truncation, physical truncation, and invalid extension lengths.
- The existing installed-FFmpeg test now asserts decoded IEEE-float audio rather than requiring the outer header tag to be 3.
- Formatting and whitespace checks pass. Local lint/test execution is deferred to CI. CI results pending.

This fixes the WAV failures exposed by #4260 and should land before it. #4260 will rebase after this merges.

title: fix(studio): cutover gate classification, SSE cross-project bleed, benign races
body:
## What

Fixes from the 2026-09-21 SDK cutover dashboard read (plan: `~/src/docs/hyperframes/plans/sdk/2026-09-21-cutover-dashboard-fixes-plan.md`, not in this repo per team convention).

- **Gate classification** — `sdk_cutover_failed` now carries `family` and `error_kind` (network/conflict/http/sdk). The one production gate event was a raw `TypeError: Failed to fetch` from an unwrapped fetch (`readProjectFile` / `writeProjectFile`'s preflight), which an `instanceof`-only classifier would still file as `"sdk"` and trip the rollback gate. Added a message-based fallback for the browser's fetch-rejection strings.
- **Network read timing** — `sdk_session_unavailable`'s `network` reason now carries `elapsed_ms` and `hidden` (`document.visibilityState` at rejection), separating a near-instant policy block (CSP/PNA/extension) from a dropped connection (tab or server going away mid-flight).
- **Benign race relabeled** — the ownership-race branch in `useSdkSession`'s open effect now emits `sdk_session_superseded` instead of `sdk_session_unavailable{stage:ownership}` — it's a benign race (identity moved on mid-open), not a broken precondition, and was being counted as one on the dashboard.
- **The real bug** — root-caused and fixed the read-404 "storm": `/api/events` (CLI host) and the vite-dev hot-reload channel are one connection per SERVER, not per project. A stale tab left open after `hyperframes preview` restarts on a different folder (same port) received every save the CURRENT project made, reloading its preview (which then 404s) and re-reading its own composition on each one. Both transports now carry `projectId`; the client-side coordinator drops a delivery whose `projectId` doesn't match the tab's (absent field still passes, for one release of skew).
- **403/404 `why`** — studio-server's file routes now report `why`: `project_dir_missing` (new — the CLI host's static `resolveProject` kept answering for a project whose folder was renamed/deleted under a running server, which used to fail closed as an indistinguishable path-traversal 403), `nul`, or `outside_project`.
- **`path_in_tree` instrumentation** — `absent_or_empty` reads now carry `path_in_tree` (against the caller's loaded file tree). Instrumentation only, per the graveyard finding that refuted the "clear `activeCompPath`" fix this was the proposed next step for.

## Before

The payload `sdkCutoverPersist` sends when the exact production gate event fires: a bare `TypeError("Failed to fetch")` from an unwrapped `readProjectFile` fetch. No `family`, no `error_kind` — indistinguishable from a real SDK defect, so it trips the dashboard's rollback gate.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16ea90c0-d936-42d4-ba9b-e22092406db9)

## After

Same scenario, this branch. `family` + `error_kind` (message-fallback classifier, since this exact error reaches `failedCutover` as a plain `TypeError`, not a wrapped `StudioSaveNetworkError`) let the gate exclude a fetch rejection the SDK never had a chance to own.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/52ac6a08-f610-4608-88d5-d4721a28a872)

Generated by running `sdkCutoverPersist` with an identical failing `readProjectFile` on `main` and on this branch (mocked `trackStudioEvent`, captured the call). Studio disables telemetry under Vite dev, so a live network capture isn't available locally, and a UI screenshot would be identical on both sides — this PR changes no rendering — which would trip the "After capture is a Before capture" gate.

## Test plan

- `sdkCutover.test.ts` — 3 new tests pin `error_kind` classification (bare `TypeError`, `StudioSaveNetworkError`, plain `Error`).
- `useSdkSession.lifecycle.test.tsx` — new tests for `elapsed_ms`/`hidden` timing (fake clock), `why` passthrough, `path_in_tree`, and the `sdk_cutover_failed` → `sdk_cutover_success`/`family` wiring.
- `useExternalFileChangeCoordinator.test.tsx` — new `describe` block: ignores a delivery with a mismatched `projectId`, still reloads on a match or an absent field.
- `studioServer.test.ts` — pins `projectId` in the SSE payload.
- `files.pathSafety.test.ts` — pins the three `why` values, including a missing project directory reporting 404 instead of the old indistinguishable 403.
- `oxlint`/`oxfmt` clean, `tsc --noEmit` clean on `studio`/`studio-server`/`cli`, zero regressions (the 8 pre-existing failing test files are identical on a clean checkout — confirmed via `git stash`).

title: feat(registry): colorama-wipe
body:
## What

`colorama-wipe` — a `hyperframes:component`. A headline reveals through a feathered, leaning wipe front that is blurred and colour-mapped as it passes, then settles to clean type and wipes off again. It is the After Effects "shiny wipe" (masked text + Compound Blur + Colorama over a moving gradient, crisp duplicate on top) as a deterministic canvas effect on any text element.

```js
attachColoramaWipe("#headline", tl, { at: 0.3, in: 0.75, hold: 2.0, out: 0.55 });
window.__timelines["my-comp"] = tl;
```

One call per element adds a single linear clock tween to the host timeline. The component measures the element, hides it (visibility, layout untouched) and paints on two canvases over its box for `[at, at + in + hold + out]`. Options: colour cycle, feather, tilt, blur, trail, noise, crisp overlay, render scale. All sizes derive from the element's font size, so it works at any type size and aspect ratio.

Deterministic: hash noise keyed by frame, no `Math.random`, no clocks; a seek anywhere outside the window paints an empty stage.

## Preview

Reference build (three headlines, 10 s, 1920×1080, finish-pass grade on top): https://hyperframes.dev/p/fabab042-1661-4a63-9143-3a6bf2034a76 — published from the demo project. Preview MP4 attached in a comment below; catalog PNG/MP4 to be uploaded by a maintainer.

## Checks

- `hyperframes check` on the reference build: 0 lint errors, runtime / layout / motion clean
- `npx oxfmt --check registry/components/colorama-wipe/*.html` passes
- `registry/registry.json`, `docs/docs.json`, `docs/public/catalog-index.json` regenerated with the two generator scripts (not hand-edited). The regeneration also picks up drift already on main (example items, docs nav groups); happy to split that into its own commit if preferred.

## Notes for reviewers

- The source text is hidden with `visibility: hidden` rather than `color: transparent` on purpose: the layout audit flags transparent text as unpainted.
- The effect canvas' alpha follows raw glyph coverage, not the noised intensity, so no-ink pixels stay transparent over any background.
- Two canvases (half-res effect + full-res crisp copy); cost is a per-pixel loop over the padded element box per frame — fine for headlines, heavy for paragraph-sized targets.

title: feat(registry): extended-keyframe
body:
## What

`extended-keyframe` — a `hyperframes:component`. The "never fully lands" arrival: an element covers most of its move in the first fifth of the duration and creeps the rest to the final frame (After Effects' extended-last-keyframe technique), exits along the vector it arrived on, and carries shutter motion blur. Direction and property agnostic: from left / right / above / below, scale up or down.

```js
var a = attachExtendedArrival("#word-1", tl, { at: 0.3, from: { x: -1400 } });
attachExtendedArrival("#word-2", tl, { at: a.end, from: { scale: 0.35 } });   // next arrival when the exit has cleared
window.__timelines["my-comp"] = tl;
```

One call per element adds the arrival (one continuous velocity profile, no piecewise join, so no brake at the hand-over), the exit igniting at 60% of the arrival while the element is still creeping, and the blur: slides get the bundled feOffset filter smear (240° shutter, 32 samples), scale beats get a per-frame blur radius from |Δscale| across the shutter. Returns `end`, the earliest the next arrival may start.

The ease is also exposed alone: `EK.ease(opts)` for any GSAP tween, `EK.next(duration)` for sequencing, `EK.gate(fn, frames)` as a numeric check (single velocity peak, no rises after it, tail above zero to the last frame).

Deterministic: no `Math.random`, no clocks.

## Preview

Reference build, the word "keyframe" arriving six ways (12.5 s, 1920×1080): https://hyperframes.dev/p/5b474b49-be92-4dd8-86e8-000238cca596 — published from the demo project. Preview MP4 attached in a comment below; catalog PNG/MP4 to be uploaded by a maintainer.

## Checks

- `hyperframes check` on the reference build: 0 lint errors, runtime / layout / motion clean
- `npx oxfmt --check registry/components/extended-keyframe/*.html` passes
- `EK.gate(EK.ease(), 75)`: peak 7.9× mean at f3, max step drop 17%, 0 rises after peak, tail above zero
- `registry/registry.json`, `docs/docs.json`, `docs/public/catalog-index.json` regenerated with the two generator scripts (not hand-edited). Same drift note as #4273: the regeneration also picks up changes already on main; happy to split.

## Notes for reviewers

- The house feOffset filter blur is bundled (as `window.attachMotionBlurFilter`, coexisting with the registry `motion-blur` component's `window.attachMotionBlur`) because the DOM-clone variant leaves a sharp stale instance on stage when the element lives inside a timed clip; the filter variant does not.
- Elements inside timed clips are fine; each arrival in the reference build is its own clip.
- Sequencing rule, stated in the header: the next arrival starts when the previous exit has cleared, never before; the exit ignites while the element is still creeping.

title: feat(registry): text-match-cut
body:
## What

A new component, `text-match-cut`: one line of text becomes another in the middle of a move. Both texts ride a single keyframe pair and hard-swap at the speed peak, so the cut lands at peak velocity with no crossfade.

Reversed from an After Effects tutorial (Editing Snapped, *The Match Cut Technique Every After Effects User Needs*), measured per frame at 60 fps rather than taken from the narration:

- curve `cubic-bezier(.85, 0, .15, 1)` over 2 s (fit rmse 0.0015), split at exactly frame 60 of 120
- gradient sweep on its own 87 % curve, 2316 px of travel at 1920, centre 948 px at the cut
- motion smear stands in for AE motion blur, proportional to px per frame

## Variables

| id | type | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_a` | string | Basic Interface Behavior | outgoing line |
| `text_b` | string | Thoughtful Experience Design | incoming line, continues the same move |
| `mode` | enum | scale-down | scale-down (the tutorial), scale-up, tracking-in, slide-left, slide-right, slide-up, slide-down |
| `sweep` | enum | on | cyan-to-blue bar through the glyphs |
| `background` | enum | navy | the tutorial's navy glow, or transparent |

Envelope: IN 2.0 s (the move), elastic HOLD, OUT 0.3 s. Sync point `hard-cut` at 1.0 s.

## Checks

- Author-reported `hyperframes check` on the demo: 0 errors (see maintainer validation below for the current CLI limitation).
- `node scripts/lint-registry-items.mjs`: passes for this item (the two existing failures, `vfx-text-cursor` and `caption-emoji-pop`, are untouched)

```js
var a = attachExtendedArrival("#word-1", tl, { at: 0.3, from: { x: -1400 } });
attachExtendedArrival("#word-2", tl, { at: a.end, from: { scale: 0.35 } });   // next arrival when the exit has cleared
window.__timelines["my-comp"] = tl;
```

One call per element adds the arrival (one continuous velocity profile, no piecewise join, so no brake at the hand-over), the exit igniting at 60% of the arrival while the element is still creeping, and the blur: slides get the bundled feOffset filter smear (240° shutter, 32 samples), scale beats get a per-frame blur radius from |Δscale| across the shutter. Returns `end`, the earliest the next arrival may start.

The ease is also exposed alone: `EK.ease(opts)` for any GSAP tween, `EK.next(duration)` for sequencing, `EK.gate(fn, frames)` as a numeric check (single velocity peak, no rises after it, tail above zero to the last frame).

Deterministic: no `Math.random`, no clocks.

## Preview

Reference build, the word "keyframe" arriving six ways (12.5 s, 1920×1080): https://hyperframes.dev/p/5b474b49-be92-4dd8-86e8-000238cca596 — published from the demo project. Preview MP4 attached in a comment below; catalog PNG/MP4 to be uploaded by a maintainer.

## Checks

- `hyperframes check` on the reference build: 0 lint errors, runtime / layout / motion clean
- `npx oxfmt --check registry/components/extended-keyframe/*.html` passes
- `EK.gate(EK.ease(), 75)`: peak 7.9× mean at f3, max step drop 17%, 0 rises after peak, tail above zero
- `registry/registry.json`, `docs/docs.json`, `docs/public/catalog-index.json` regenerated with the two generator scripts (not hand-edited). Same drift note as #4273: the regeneration also picks up changes already on main; happy to split.

## Notes for reviewers

- The house feOffset filter blur is bundled (as `window.attachMotionBlurFilter`, coexisting with the registry `motion-blur` component's `window.attachMotionBlur`) because the DOM-clone variant leaves a sharp stale instance on stage when the element lives inside a timed clip; the filter variant does not.
- Elements inside timed clips are fine; each arrival in the reference build is its own clip.
- Sequencing rule, stated in the header: the next arrival starts when the previous exit has cleared, never before; the exit ignites while the element is still creeping.

title: fix(studio-server): write served files atomically
body:
Studio served project files were rewritten in place. A concurrent reader could observe an empty or partial HTML document while a writer truncated and rewrote the file.

This PR writes each replacement to a unique sibling temporary file, preserves the existing mode, and publishes it with rename. On Windows, Node's rename reaches libuv's `uv_fs_rename`, which calls `MoveFileExW` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING`: https://github.com/libuv/libuv/blob/v1.x/src/win/fs.c#L2177-L2184

## No visible change

This preserves the served file behavior while removing torn reads during concurrent writes.

title: ci: shard the Test job by package group

## What users get

The required `Test` check keeps its existing name while the package suite runs in three independently visible jobs: `Test (studio)`, `Test (runtime)`, and `Test (support)`. The `Test` aggregator waits for all three package shards and the producer source tests, then fails if any required result is not successful.

The split follows measured wall time. Studio runs alone. Runtime groups CLI, core, and engine. Support groups lint, parsers, studio-server, SDK, player, AWS Lambda, GCP Cloud Run, SDK Playground, and shader transitions, and runs `test:scripts` once.

The Test job first crossed eight minutes after merge [#4249](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4249), commit `eeabbe839`. The previous passing run after #4203 was 6.15 minutes; #4249 measured 8.02 minutes.

title: fix(catalog): registry set-delta check accepts intentional additions
body:
## Why

`check-registry-set-delta.mjs` compared `registry.json`'s item set against a base ref and only
recognized removals, by checking that the removed name's `registry-item.json` file was actually
deleted. Any legitimate addition had no matching allowance, so a pure-addition PR (a new catalog
item, no removals) always failed with "unexpected in registry.json: <name>" even though the item's
own `registry-item.json` was added in the same diff. Caught while re-landing a fork PR that adds a
single new catalog component.

## Fix

Mirror the deletion rule for additions: an added name only counts as expected when its own
`registry/(blocks|components|examples)/<name>/registry-item.json` was added in the same diff, same
condition the removal side already required for deletions. A bare `registry.json` edit with no
matching file change still fails on either side.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test scripts/check-registry-set-delta.test.mjs`: 6 pass, 0 fail (4 delta
  cases, 2 path-parsing cases; one case proves a fake registry.json addition with no folder still
  fails).
- Mutation check: commented out the added-names line, reran, 1 test failed as expected, restored,
  6 pass again.
- Ran the fixed script against a real branch that adds exactly one catalog item:
  `Registry item-set delta matches 0 removal(s) and 1 addition(s) against origin/main`, exit 0.

title: feat(registry): text-match-cut
body:
Supersedes #4276.

## What

A new component, `text-match-cut`: one line of text becomes another in the middle of a move. Both texts ride a single keyframe pair and hard-swap at the speed peak, so the cut lands at peak velocity with no crossfade.

Reversed from an After Effects tutorial (Editing Snapped, *The Match Cut Technique Every After Effects User Needs*), measured per frame at 60 fps rather than taken from the narration:

- curve `cubic-bezier(.85, 0, .15, 1)` over 2 s (fit rmse 0.0015), split at exactly frame 60 of 120
- gradient sweep on its own 87 % curve, 2316 px of travel at 1920, centre 948 px at the cut
- motion smear stands in for AE motion blur, proportional to px per frame

## Variables

| id | type | default | notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `text_a` | string | Basic Interface Behavior | outgoing line |
| `text_b` | string | Thoughtful Experience Design | incoming line, continues the same move |
| `mode` | enum | scale-down | scale-down (the tutorial), scale-up, tracking-in, slide-left, slide-right, slide-up, slide-down |
| `sweep` | enum | on | cyan-to-blue bar through the glyphs |
| `background` | enum | navy | the tutorial's navy glow, or transparent |

Envelope: IN 2.0 s (the move), elastic HOLD, OUT 0.3 s. Sync point `hard-cut` at 1.0 s.

title: Studio 0.8.61: preview reload times out at 15 s ("The preview did not reload") though the server answers in ms — stale canvas, toast repeats
body:
## What happens

Studio repeatedly shows the toast:

> The preview did not reload (it took too long to load). The previous preview is still showing.

It stacks (two or more at once) during a normal edit loop: the generator rewrites `index.html`, Studio picks up the change, and instead of the new preview the old one stays on the canvas. The harmful part is the stale canvas: after a few of these there is no way to tell whether what is on screen is the current `index.html`, so every visual judgement has to be re-checked by rendering a PNG outside Studio.

Recovering seems to need a reload of the Studio tab (or a preview restart).

## Where it comes from

In `dist/studio/index.js` (0.8.61) the preview does a shadow reload: the new document loads in a hidden iframe and is promoted once it reports "visually ready", with

```js
readyTimerRef.current = setTimeout(
  () => failShadow(gen, "it took too long to load"),
  SHADOW_READY_TIMEOUT_MS   // = 15e3
);
```

So the toast means the readiness signal did not arrive within 15 s.

## Why 15 s looks like the wrong diagnosis here

Measured on the affected project while Studio was running (same machine, same files):

| what | measured |
| --- | --- |
| Studio serves the compiled preview HTML (`/api/projects/<id>/preview/index.html`, 50 KB) | **~1 ms** |
| Studio serves the heaviest asset (8.9 MB PNG) through the same route | **~13 ms** |
| the same `index.html` loaded from disk in headless Chrome (chrome-headless-shell, `networkidle0` + fonts + 2 frames) | **~0.6 s** (3 runs: 1.02 s cold, 0.53 s, 0.58 s) |

The document is 50 KB and renders in well under a second, and the server answers in milliseconds, yet the shadow iframe never reports ready inside 15 s. That points at the readiness handshake (or the iframe never painting / never being asked to), not at a genuinely slow page.

## Project characteristics (in case they matter)

- 1080×1350 composition, 6 sibling clips, root carries **`data-no-timeline`** (nothing animates, so no GSAP timeline is registered on `window.__timelines`). If the "visually ready" handshake waits on a timeline adapter, a `data-no-timeline` composition may never satisfy it — **unverified**, I could not tell from the minified bundle.
- Each clip contains a sizeable static DOM (an iMessage phone UI), two clips apply a CSS `filter: blur()` to a scaled layer.
- Assets: three PNGs totalling ~14 MB (8.9 MB, 3.1 MB, 1.6 MB), referenced as CSS backgrounds and shared across clips.
- Environment: hyperframes 0.8.61 via `npx hyperframes@latest`, Studio preview on `127.0.0.1:3002`, WSL2 (Ubuntu) with the browser on the Windows side. A related WSL2 relay stall was the root cause of #3646, so that may contribute here too; the measurements above were taken from inside WSL.

## Expected

Either the new preview is promoted, or Studio makes the failure actionable and recoverable.

## Suggestions

1. Say **what** did not arrive (first paint, adapter ready, asset load) and log it to the console, so the cause is diagnosable from the toast.
2. Offer a **retry** on the toast, so recovery does not need a tab reload.
3. If the shadow iframe has painted but the adapter never reported, **promote it anyway** after the timeout rather than keeping a stale document, or fall back to a hard reload of the visible iframe.
4. Handle `data-no-timeline` compositions explicitly in the readiness path if it currently depends on a timeline being registered.
5. Consider making `SHADOW_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` configurable, or scaling it with document weight, for heavy previews on slower hosts.

## Related

- #3646 — Studio preview hangs and stops reflecting `index.html` after a burst of external rewrites (closed; root cause there was the WSL2 localhost relay)
- #3564 — Studio serves stale project assets after an in-place image edit (closed)
- #2982 — external change to `index.html` discards unsaved editor state (closed)

A screenshot of the stacked toasts is available and can be attached.

title: feat(media-use): resolve brand logos from theSVG
body:
## What

The `logo` cascade in media-use now resolves brand marks from [theSVG](https://thesvg.org), replacing the svgl and simple-icons tiers. theSVG ships 7,400+ official brand SVGs with color, mono, light/dark and wordmark variants.

New cascade: **theSVG → GitHub org avatar → domain favicon**.

Because every logo is now an SVG fetched from the internet and written into the user's project, this PR also hardens the shared SVG sanitizer (`packages/core/src/figma/sanitizeSvg.ts`, also used by the Figma import).

## Why

svgl and simple-icons each covered part of the brand long tail, and both needed hand-kept alias maps (`nextjs` → `next.js`, `aws` → `amazonwebservices`, `cocacola` → `coca-cola`...). theSVG covers both sets in one library, in full color, so one tier replaces two and the alias maps go away.

## How

- **One pinned manifest.** `thesvgSearch` fetches `src/data/icons.json` from a fixed `glincker/thesvg` commit on jsDelivr. Icon URLs resolve against the same pin, so a resolve is reproducible. Bumping theSVG means changing `THESVG_REV`.
- **Fetched once per process**, memoized; a failed load isn't cached, the next call retries. Streamed with a 20MB cap and a 10s timeout.
- **Local matching.** `thesvgMatch` compares the normalized entity against slug, then title, then aliases. "Next.js", "nextjs" and "next js" hit the same entry. Lookalikes like Slackware never match "slack". Ties rank the `brands` collection over auth badges.
- **License gate.** Only entries under the ten SPDX ids theSVG's own submission form verifies are returned; a rejected entry falls through to the next match, then to the avatar/favicon tiers.
- **Same safety path.** The manifest goes through `fetchMedia`, so the public-host redirect policy still applies. Every `.svg` written by `freeze` passes the sanitizer first.
- **Sanitizer is a DOM allowlist.** `sanitizeSvg` parses with linkedom and keeps only known SVG elements and attributes; `href` only as a `#fragment` (or `data:image/` off `<a>`). Every kept attribute value and every `<style>` block must pass a CSS check: on escape-decoded text, no `@import`, every function on a compute-only list (color, transform, filter, math), every `url()` a same-document fragment. The scans are single-pass, linear in input size.
- **One source, generated copy.** media-use runs with zero installs, so it can't import `@hyperframes/core`. `scripts/generate-media-use-svg-sanitize.mjs` bundles the core sanitizer into `media-use/lib/svg-sanitize.mjs`; a drift test fails if the committed bundle differs from a fresh build, and a parity test runs both copies over a hostile corpus.
- Provenance records `slug`, `variant`, the available `variants`, `collection`, `license` and the pinned revision.

## Test plan

- `node --test 'packages/cli/src/media-use/**/*.test.mjs'`: 307/307
- `sanitizeSvg.test.ts`: 56/56, including CSS-escape, `image-set()` and input-size cases
- `check-svg-sanitize-parity.test.mjs`: 42/42; generated-bundle drift test: 1/1
- `bun run lint`, `oxfmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit` (core, cli), fallow audit: clean
- Every new test proven non-vacuous by reverting the code it covers and watching it go red
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (media-use `SKILL.md`, `resolve.md`, `meta.md`, `setup-providers.md`, motion-graphics news module)

## What I measured

**Real browser, attack payloads.** Headless Chrome 152, a local server counting requests, each payload loaded inline in HTML and as a standalone SVG. Through the sanitizer before this round: 8 of 8 external requests fired (`fill="\75 rl(...)"`, escaped `style=`, `@\69mport`, `image-set("...")`). Through this head: 0 of 8. Four more shapes judged inert on paper (`var()` holding a bare URL string, `url (` with a space, a comment-split `@import`, `attr(... url)`) fire nothing in Chrome either.

**Real logos.** Old vs new sanitizer over all 13,384 SVGs in the pinned theSVG commit: 13,383 byte-identical. One (`xrp/default.svg`) loses `id="XRP-(XRP)"`, which nothing references; it renders the same. The CSS function list comes from the same corpus: `url`, `matrix`, `translate`, `scale`, `rotate`, `skewX/Y`, `rgb(a)`, `color(display-p3 ...)`, bare parens, `@media` only, zero escapes, zero comments.

**Hostile input size.** An unclosed `url(` followed by 4,000 spaces took 20s in the previous regex scan, and a parenless 80,000-character word took 7.7s; `freeze` runs the sanitizer synchronously on bodies up to 256MB. The single-pass scans handle a million characters in under 15ms; both payloads now take about 3ms.

**Live resolve** through the real cascade (network, pinned manifest): slack, next.js (falls to the CC0 `nextdotjs` entry; the exact `nextjs` entry is `brand-use`, gated out), aws, coca-cola, github, openai, google, stripe, vercel and notion all resolve from theSVG; heygen falls through to its GitHub avatar; a non-brand word misses cleanly.

**License field.** In the pinned manifest (7,417 icons), 109 entries carry a license theSVG itself marks as not cleared (`Proprietary`, `Unknown`, `Custom`, `TODO`, and 37 Microsoft product icons tagged "no express redistribution license supplied"). The gate keeps them out.

## Review findings (independent adversarial passes)

| Round | Finding | Severity | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fetched SVGs written to disk unsanitized | BLOCKER | `freeze` sanitizes every `.svg` |
| 2 | Unquoted `href`, unchecked `style=`, renamed xlink prefix survived | BLOCKER | tokenizer, then replaced by the DOM allowlist |
| 3 | Presentation-attribute `url()`, SMIL `<animate>/<set>` href rewrite, `data:` navigation on `<a>`, tokenizer truncation | BLOCKER | DOM allowlist closes the class |
| 4 | CSS escapes (`\75 rl(`, `@\69mport`) and `image-set("...")` load external URLs | BLOCKER | escape-decoded CSS check with a function allowlist; Chrome 8 → 0 |
| 4 | Parity oracle shared the sanitizer's blind spot | MINOR | oracle fails on any surviving attacker host |
| 5 | Backtracking regexes: function-name scan quadratic, `url()` scan cubic | BLOCKER | single-pass scans; size test |
| 5 | `var()` can carry a bare URL-shaped string | MINOR | not a live bypass: a string loads only via `image-set()`/`src()`/`@import`, all rejected; confirmed in Chrome. Left as is |
| 6 | The single-pass `url(` scan accepts a quoted fragment holding `)`, e.g. `url('#a)b')`, which the old regex rejected | MINOR | safe: a quoted value starting with `#` is a same-document fragment; 0 requests in Chrome. Left as is |
| simplify | `fetchJson` duplicated `freezeUrl`'s capped body read | cleanup | shared `readCappedBody` in `media-fetch.mjs`, with its own tests |

## What I did NOT exercise

- Rendering a frozen logo inside the Studio UI itself; the browser checks above load the sanitized SVG in Chrome directly.
- The ~1,270 manifest entries in the gray zone between theSVG's ten accepted SPDX ids and its explicitly-unresolved set (`brand-use`, `Trademark`, per-brand fair-use strings, pre-4.0 CC). They carry the same trademark posture the removed svgl/simple-icons tiers had. Whether to also exclude them is a product and legal call, not an engineering default.
- Full XML-namespace resolution: any attribute whose name ends in `:href` is treated as an href, which is broader than strict XLink, not narrower.
- Exhaustive fuzzing of CSS escape and whitespace forms beyond the cases listed in the tests.
- A server that sends headers fast and then trickles the body forever. `freezeUrl` bounds the wait for response headers (10s) and the body size (256MB), not the total download time (`main` bounded neither). A slow but progressing body now freezes; see `freeze.test.mjs`.

title: fix(studio): don't fail a shadow reload while the tab is hidden
body:
## What

Studio no longer fails a shadow reload while its tab is hidden. The 15s ready budget now only runs while the document is visible: hiding the tab pauses it, and showing the tab again restarts the full budget for the pending shadow.

Fixes #4290.

## Why

The shadow reload promotes on readiness signals that depend on frames being rendered: the player's paint-and-idle, then two `requestAnimationFrame`s in `Player.tsx`. But it failed on a wall-clock `setTimeout(failShadow, 15_000)`. A hidden tab renders no frames, so any external edit made while Studio was in the background hit the timeout. The result:

- every edit showed "The preview did not reload (it took too long to load)", and the toasts stacked;
- the shadow was discarded, so the preview stayed stale even after the user returned to the tab, until the next edit or a tab reload.

This is the common agent loop: the agent rewrites `index.html` from a terminal while the Studio window sits behind it. Chrome treats a fully covered window as hidden.

It is not specific to `data-no-timeline`. A composition with a GSAP timeline fails identically, and a `data-no-timeline` composition promotes in about 1s while visible, because the adapter falls back to static seek over `data-duration`.

## How

`useShadowPreviewReload.ts`:
- `armReadyTimer(gen)` starts the budget only when `document.visibilityState !== "hidden"`.
- `budgetGenRef` records which shadow is still owed a budget; `stopPendingShadow` clears it on promote, fail or supersede.
- A `visibilitychange` listener clears the timer on hide and restarts the full budget on show, but only if the owed shadow is still the current one.

A genuinely stuck document still fails, after 15s of visible time. Nothing changes for a visible tab.

## Before

`hyperframes@0.8.61`. `index.html` was rewritten twice while the Studio tab was hidden, then the tab was brought back. Both reloads failed with stacked toasts, and the canvas still shows the original `MARKER` text instead of the latest edit.

![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f54284a50bde1591fba113a85589c204d2064821/before.png)

## After

This branch, same steps. There are no toasts, and on return the preview promotes straight to the latest edit (`HID2`).

![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f54284a50bde1591fba113a85589c204d2064821/after.png)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: a hidden tab never fails, and the shadow promotes once visible and ready; the budget pauses while hidden, restarts in full on show, and still fails a silent shadow at exactly 15s. Both fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- [x] Full studio suite: 510 files, 5467 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- [x] Manual, against a real `hyperframes preview` in headless Chromium, with two external rewrites of `index.html` per run:

| build | tab | result |
|---|---|---|
| 0.8.61 | visible | promoted in about 1s |
| 0.8.61 | hidden | toast at +15s for each edit, 2 stacked, still stale after returning to the tab |
| this branch | visible | promoted in about 1s |
| this branch | hidden | no toasts; on return it promotes directly to the latest edit |

- [ ] Documentation updated: not applicable

— Rames Jusso

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Cloud renders fail instantly when the composition contains a <video> element
body:
## Summary

Every render we submit to `POST /v3/hyperframes/renders` whose composition contains a `<video>` element fails within roughly 2–5 seconds:

```
status: failed
failure_reason: "HyperFrames render failed; see workflow logs for details."
```

Nothing further is exposed through the API — no line number, no asset name, no log excerpt — so we can't tell whether the problem is our bundle, the video source, or something at the account level.

## It is specifically the video element

Two renders submitted minutes apart from the same account, using the same bundle format (a stored/uncompressed zip posted as `project: {type: "base64", media_type: "application/zip", data: ...}`), the same `composition: "index.html"`, `format: "mp4"`, `fps: 30`, `quality: "standard"`, `resolution: "1080p"`:

| Render | Composition | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `6ff6eb3f-e162-4b06-9a11-c89649abaf8f` | includes a `<video>` element | `failed` in ~5s |
| `4acf2338-c035-49a7-9299-9d9b3c25507a` | identical bundle with the `<video>` element removed | `completed`, MP4 returned |

The only difference between the two is the presence of the video element.

## What we've ruled out

- **Our bundle layout** — the project generated by the official CLI (`hyperframes init`, then render) fails identically, so it isn't our hand-authored HTML.
- **The video source** — a remote `https://` URL, a local file packaged into the zip, and an `asset_id` from `POST /v3/assets` all fail the same way.
- **Account/API health** — the same key renders text-and-graphics compositions to MP4 fine, and `POST /v3/videos` (avatar video generation) works normally.
- **Composition metadata** — the root element carries `data-composition-id`, `data-start`, `data-duration`, `data-width`, `data-height`, `data-no-timeline`; the video element carries its own `data-start` / `data-duration`.

## What we're trying to do

Lay a brand overlay (primary logo, lower-third headline bar, sponsor logo) on top of a finished avatar video: the avatar MP4 as the background layer, HTML/CSS elements above it, rendered out as one MP4 by cloud rendering — the avatar-compositing pipeline described in your docs (`POST /v3/videos` → `GET /v3/audio/sounds` → `POST /v3/hyperframes/renders`).

## Asks

1. Confirm whether cloud rendering of compositions containing video is enabled on our account; if not, what's required to turn it on (plan tier, feature flag, etc.).
2. If it is enabled, please surface a usable reason in the render response. "See workflow logs" isn't actionable for API users, since we have no access to those logs.
3. #2810 and #3526 look like related cloud-side capture and error-reporting gaps — happy to help test a fix.

Happy to share the exact zip bundles and additional render IDs if that helps.

title: fix(cli): replace pre-planted links when writing capture files
body:
## What

Capture writes no longer follow a symlink or hard link that already sits at the target path. `writeCaptureFileSync` now stages each file in a private directory next to the target and renames it into place. The two capture writes that bypassed it, contact sheets and `BLOCKED.md`, go through it too.

Fixes #4243

## Why

`writeFileSync` follows whatever is at the path. A link planted in the capture directory before a run redirected the write to its target, and `mode: 0o600` did not help because modes only apply when a file is created. With `-o <dir>` the command reuses an existing directory, so it can be prepared ahead of time.

I reproduced it with a real `hyperframes capture` against a local page on current `main` (v0.8.62). A symlink at `extracted/page.html` pointing outside the capture directory ended up holding the captured HTML.

## How

- **Stage and rename, same pattern as the font cache in #3669.** `mkdtempSync(join(dirname(path), ".capture-"))` creates a private directory on the same filesystem. The file is written inside it, `renameSync` moves it over the target, and `finally` removes that directory. `rename` replaces the directory entry itself, so a planted symlink or hard link is swapped out instead of written through. Intentional overwrites keep working: the deadline partial bundle still rewrites `extracted/page.html` and `tokens.json` from the in-progress attempt. The staging directory is new for each call, so nothing in it can be pre-planted and cleanup only removes what this call created.
- **Why not `wx` or `O_NOFOLLOW` alone?** `wx` on the target breaks those intentional overwrites. `O_NOFOLLOW` still truncates through a planted hard link and isn't available on Windows.
- **Caller flags are kept.** If a caller passes its own flag, it goes through unchanged. `partialCapture` passes `wx` for `meta.json`, and `O_EXCL` already refuses a planted symlink there.
- **Writes that bypassed the writer.** `createContactSheet` used sharp's `toFile`, which opens the path itself. It now encodes to a buffer and writes through `writeCaptureFileSync`. The `BLOCKED.md` failure note in `commands/capture.ts` used plain `writeFileSync` and now uses the writer. After this, nothing under `capture/` or in the capture command writes around it. `meta.json` goes through `writeNewFileSync`, which is already exclusive.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `captureFile.test.ts` (new):
    - A planted symlink and a planted hard link are replaced, and the file outside the directory is untouched. Both fail on `main`.
    - Overwriting an existing file still works.
    - A caller's `wx` still throws `EEXIST`, on a regular file and on a symlink.
    - The result is `0o600`.
    - Cleanup leaves a neighbouring file alone and leaves nothing behind when the final rename fails.
  - `contactSheet.test.ts`: a symlink at the sheet path is replaced. Fails on `main`.
  - `commands/capture.test.ts`: `BLOCKED.md` is written without following a planted symlink. Fails on `main`.
  - Symlink and mode cases are skipped on Windows, where creating symlinks needs elevated rights.
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Ran a real capture with the patched CLI against a local page, with three symlinks (`extracted/page.html`, `AGENTS.md`, `screenshots/contact-sheet.jpg`) and one hard link (`extracted/tokens.json`) planted to the same file outside the directory.
  - That file stayed untouched and its link count went back to 1. Every planted path ended up as a regular file with the captured content. No staging directories or temp files were left behind.
  - The same run on `main` overwrote the file.
- `packages/cli` suite: 3536 tests, 0 failures, after building parsers, lint, studio-server and core the way the runtime test job does. Pre-commit gates pass: lint, format, fallow audit, typecheck and commitlint.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce it by hand</summary>

Serve any page locally, for example `python3 -m http.server 8000` in a folder with an `index.html`, then:

```sh
echo "do not touch" > victim.txt
mkdir -p out/extracted
ln -s "$PWD/victim.txt" out/extracted/page.html
hyperframes capture http://127.0.0.1:8000/ -o out --skip-vision
cat victim.txt
```

On `main`, `victim.txt` now holds the captured HTML. On this branch it still says `do not touch`, and `out/extracted/page.html` is a regular file with the capture.

</details>

Not covered here:
- **A planted symlink on a parent directory.** For example, `extracted/` pointing elsewhere still redirects writes into that directory. Closing that needs a realpath containment check on every write. I left it out to keep this focused, but I'm happy to add it here or in a follow-up.
- **The `wx` pass-through on Windows.** #3720 found that `wx` behaves differently there with a dangling symlink, and I couldn't test Windows.
- **`meta.json` mode.** It is created safely but with the default mode, not `0o600`.

title: fix(registry): restore week-in-merges entry dropped in #4277
body:
## What

Restores the `week-in-merges` entry in `registry/registry.json`.

## Why

- #4264 added the `week-in-merges` block together with its `registry.json` entry.
- #4277 (colorama-wipe) regenerated `registry.json` from a branch that predated #4264, which dropped the entry again. Its diff shows the removal: `-      "name": "week-in-merges",`.
- Every commit since has kept the gap, and `main` still has it.

The rest of the block is still in place:
- `registry/blocks/week-in-merges/`
- `docs/catalog/blocks/week-in-merges.mdx`
- the nav link in `docs/docs.json`
- the entries in `docs/public/catalog-index.json` and the catalog search index

So the catalog advertises a block that can't be installed:

```
$ hyperframes add week-in-merges
Item "week-in-merges" not found in registry. Available: ai-chat-reveal, ...
```

## Verification

- I called the CLI's `resolveItemWithDependencies("week-in-merges")` against each registry, with `fetch` stubbed to serve local files:
  - `main`: `Item "week-in-merges" not found in registry`
  - this branch: resolves `week-in-merges (hyperframes:block, 1 files)`
- `bun x vitest run src/registry/` in `packages/cli` passes: 17 files, 234 tests passed, 1 skipped.
- `oxfmt --check registry/registry.json` passes.
- Only `registry.json` was out of sync. I checked `docs.json`, `catalog-index.json` and `catalog-artifact/`.

## Note on the `check:catalog-drift` CI step

I expect `scripts/check-registry-set-delta.mjs` to fail on this PR:

```
Registry item-set delta mismatch against origin/main:
  unexpected in registry.json: week-in-merges
```

The check only accepts a new name when the same diff also adds that item's `registry-item.json`. Restoring an item whose files already exist on `main` doesn't do that. The check also compares only against the PR base, which is why #4277's removal got through.

If it's useful, I can follow up with a change to the check itself. It would accept, and also require, every name whose `registry-item.json` exists at HEAD. That would catch this kind of drift directly.

I also left out the other change `scripts/generate-registry-items.ts` produces. It moves the 8 `hyperframes:example` entries from the end of the list to the top, which is ordering only, so this diff is limited to the one missing entry.

title: fix(lint): flag seek-unsafe CSS transitions as css_transition_used
body:
Implements the proposed solution in #3493 verbatim.

CSS transitions run on the browser clock: a GSAP class swap looks correct in preview and --workers 1, but parallel chunk workers restore the class on a fresh page and restart the fade. The CSS adapter only discovers animation-name; finite @keyframes are seekable, transition is not.

New error-level core rule (same family as non_deterministic_code):
- Flags transition / transition-* and -webkit- in <style> blocks (postcss walkDecls) and inline style attributes.
- Allows transition: none / transition-property: none (including !important).
- Ignores custom properties (--*).
- Reuses the frame-worker css_transition_used label, so check fails.

Verification:
- 6 new behavior tests in packages/lint/src/rules/core.test.ts (style block, transition-*/-webkit-, inline style, none-allowlist, custom-property ignore, @keyframes not flagged).
- Full @hyperframes/lint suite: 18 files / 683 tests pass; lint typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow audit clean.
- End-to-end on the issue fixture (ArcadeHQ/hyperframes-repros@patch/jump-seek-css-settle): hyperframes lint reports css_transition_used error on #swatch, and hyperframes check exits 1 with ok:false (previously clean per the issue).

Fixes #3493.

title: ci: compare test reachability against the merge ref's base parent
body:
## What failed

The "Test reachability" job's base-report step ran `git worktree add --detach "$RUNNER_TEMP/reachability-base" "$BASE_SHA"` with `BASE_SHA` set from `github.event.pull_request.base.sha`. On a PR branch that predates `scripts/check-test-reachability.mjs`, that sha can be stale enough to predate the script's own addition, so the checkout fails with:

```
Error: Cannot find module '/home/runner/work/_temp/reachability-base/scripts/check-test-reachability.mjs'
```

Reproduced on today's failing run: the step used `BASE_SHA: 08d48ab7539e3a21facbe005c0610f2dbc8bf5a5`, a commit 286 commits behind main and before the script existed, even though `github.event.pull_request.base.sha` is meant to track the base branch.

## Why

For `pull_request` events, `actions/checkout` (with `fetch-depth: 0`, already set on this job) checks out the PR's merge ref, whose first parent is the live base branch tip at the time GitHub built that ref. That is always at least as fresh as `pull_request.base.sha`, which reflects whatever the base pointer was at the PR's last sync and can go stale if the PR sits idle while the base branch moves.

Confirmed on the failing run itself: its checked-out `HEAD^1` was the then-current main tip, which already had the script, while the event's `base.sha` field pointed at the 286-commits-stale sha that caused the crash.

## What changed

Derive `BASE_SHA` from `git rev-parse HEAD^1` instead of the event payload, in both:
- the "Test reachability" job (`ci.yml`)
- the "Render changed block/component previews" step (`catalog-previews.yml`), which read the same stale `base.sha` for its own changed-items diff. Its checkout already used `fetch-depth: 0`, so no history-fetch change was needed there.

No change to the reachability script or its baseline logic, and the head check is untouched.

title: capture writes: a symlinked parent directory still escapes the output root
body:
`writeCaptureFileSync` (added in #4298) closes the direct pre-planted-file case: writes go through a fresh `mkdtemp` staging directory and an atomic `rename`, so a planted symlink or hard link at the exact output path can no longer redirect the write.

A parent-directory case is still open. If a directory in the output path itself (e.g. `extracted/` or `assets/`) is a planted symlink, both `mkdtempSync(dirname(path))` and the final `renameSync` land inside whatever that symlink points to, not inside the intended output root. Most path segments are fixed strings the tool controls (`page.html`, `tokens.json`), but asset filenames are derived from the captured page — so a hostile page combined with a planted `assets -> ~/somewhere` symlink could still choose where inside that target directory the file lands.

Fix shape: a realpath containment check against the output root, run once per directory at creation, rejecting (or refusing to write into) a directory whose real path resolves outside the intended root.

Follow-up to #4298; not a regression in that PR, called out as a known remaining gap in review.

title: fix(studio): timeline clips keep their pictures while you scroll
body:
## What changes for a person

When you scroll a zoomed-in timeline, clips that were already on screen keep their pictures. Before, all clip
pictures (video filmstrips, composition and text frames, images) vanished for as long as your fingers were moving
and came back about 100 ms after you stopped, so a trackpad sweep showed a row of grey boxes.

A clip that scrolls into view during the gesture gets its picture when the scroll stops, as it does on `main` today.

## How

- `resolveRenderClipContent` handed the timeline no clip-content renderer while the scroll viewport reported
  `isScrolling` under row virtualization, which is the product default. Every clip's content unmounted at the start
  of a gesture and remounted when it settled. The helper is deleted and `renderClipContent` always reaches the
  lanes.
- Mounting every new clip's content during a scroll is what `main` was avoiding: in the viewport gate below, each
  jump across a 50,000-clip timeline then mounted and laid out a screenful of new thumbnails, a 90 to 130 ms long
  task per run where `main` has none. So `ClipContentOnceShown` mounts a clip's content only while the timeline is
  at rest and keeps it through later scrolls. A picture on screen never blanks, and a scroll never mounts new ones.
- A live dump of the thumbnail scheduler during repeated scroll sweeps showed every picture staying ready and
  cached, so the scheduler was never the cause.

## Before

![Before: mid-scroll at 400% zoom, every clip in view is a grey box with only its timecode](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e96bfd14-591b-4698-b874-d9e2b97e4b99)

## After

![After: the same moment, every clip keeps its picture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2770166-2920-43f6-8788-9759e14fd7b9)

Same fixture project (video, text layer, sub-composition, image and audio clips), Studio dev server, 400% zoom,
captured headless while the page keeps scrolling. Every clip in these frames was on screen before the scroll
started, so the second commit does not change what they show; the captures were taken on the first commit.

## What I measured

- CI's timeline viewport gate (50,000 clips, row virtualization on) on this head: 5 of 5 runs passing,
  interaction p95 33.2 ms, longest task 0 ms in every run. `main` at the same hour (after #4324): p95 33.1 ms,
  longest task 0 ms in every run.
- The first commit alone on the same gate: p95 89.3 ms, 4 of 5 runs passing, a long task of 87 to 105 ms in every
  run. A CPU profile of the measured runs put the extra time in mounting new thumbnails and the layout that
  follows; with the second commit the same local profile run shows p95 33 ms and no long tasks, matching `main`.
- New tests fail on the old code: a clip's picture survives a scroll and its settle (`main` drops it:
  `expected null to be <span data-rich-content>`), and a clip that appears mid-scroll gets its picture only
  after the settle (the first commit alone mounts it at once).
- `Timeline.virtualization.test.tsx` 10/10, `timelineProviderStateBuilders.test.ts` 6/6, `TimelineLanes.test.tsx`
  15/15; pre-commit lint, format, fallow, filesize and typecheck green.
- On the first commit, scripted sweeps at 400% zoom sampling every 40 ms mid-gesture: before, 15 of 68 positions
  had every clip in view without a picture; after, 0 of 68. Not re-measured with the second commit.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Hosts other than Studio's own dev server.
- A drag that auto-scrolls the timeline: the drag preview goes through the same renderer, so a preview that
  first mounts mid-scroll shows its picture when the scroll stops, as on `main`.

title: feat(runtime): data-vfx-chain — a seek-deterministic per-pixel effect element
body:
## What

A runtime-owned, seek-deterministic per-pixel effect element, `data-vfx-chain`, mirroring the
shipped audio FX rack (`data-fx-chain`): a versioned JSON chain, a def registry with typed params,
WebGL2 kernels painted on every seek from `(t, params)` only. Each def declares
`capture: "none" | "self" | "backdrop"` — whether it needs nothing beyond its own params, its own
captured layer, or the layers below it.

Shipped kernels: `fractal-noise` (generator, `none`; fBm approximation of AE's Basic type — exact
port deferred), `wave-warp` (Sine, `self`), `displacement-map` (self-referential map, `self`).

Driving use case: the `hyperframes-ae-mcp` After Effects exporter currently bakes Wave Warp,
Displacement Map and Fractal Noise to video because HyperFrames has no per-pixel element. This
branch is the runtime side of that; the exporter side is on that repo's `main` (`b1e3c85`).

## Status

Every unit test and browser test is green (`packages/core`: `bun run test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` —
1249/1249; `vfx.test.ts` + `init.test.ts` — 155/155; producer `vfxDeterminism.test.ts` — 10/10;
`typecheck:runtime` and `lint:runtime-preview-guards` both clean). Kernel-vs-CPU-reference and chain-order-vs-plain-DOM were both measured at PSNR ∞ on the
dev machine's own GPU backend at the time this was written; the tests enforce the weaker,
cross-backend-safe bars that number is expected to drift against (fractal-noise ≥32 dB vs the CPU
reference, filter-ordering ≥40 dB) rather than pin ∞, since a different GPU/driver combination in
CI would otherwise flake on a same-backend claim.

**The first real After Effects corpus row to exercise this end to end (retro-wave,
`hyperframes-ae-mcp`) still FAILs its fidelity gate, and this PR alone won't flip that** — the
remaining gaps are exporter-side (a mount/3D-projection interaction and an unmapped AE blend popup),
tracked as Tasks 19/20 there, not in this repo. What moved since the runtime landed:

- **Fixed here:** `hyperframes snapshot`/`render` armed the page-composite protocol
  (`__hf_page_composite_pending`) via the same `renderSeek` path the engine uses, but nothing ever
  resolved it under `snapshot` — no engine, no shader-transitions call reaches
  `__hf_page_composite_resolve` there. Any page-side compositor was blank at the corpus gate. Now
  the runtime arms the preview-side capture too and paints on whichever completes first (a seek
  token lets the engine's post-video-injection resolve still win when it runs). Same hole covered
  incidentally for `beginframe`/`drawelement` capture modes in the engine path.
- **Fixed here:** a host arriving via a mount (sub-composition load) was never registered with the
  vfx runtime; output canvas was sized from the host's transformed AABB instead of its layout box;
  an adopted (not created) `.hf-vfx-out` skipped its layout styles.
- **Fixed on the exporter** (`hyperframes-ae-mcp` Task 18, not in this diff): `inlineSubCompositions`
  deletes a mount host's children, including any `<svg><defs>` an effect wrote there — killing
  Tritone/Choker filters and Ramp gradients on layers that also mount. Measured gain on retro-wave
  once fixed: 2.603 s +2.74 dB, 6.54 s +3.84 dB, 10.444 s +7.92 dB. Still not enough to pass: mountain
  ridges now match AE colour to 1/1/2, but the row still bakes (`Main/Text` gate error 78.78 → 40.61
  — better, still over threshold) pending the camera-parented-null projection work and the sky-haze
  compositing decision, both exporter-side.

I'm leaving this open for review now rather than waiting for that row to go fully green — the
runtime contract, tests and the two protocol fixes above are the reviewable unit, and the remaining
work is tracked separately (see Follow-on).

## Fixed along the way (each with a browser-test reproduction)

See Status above for the two protocol-level fixes; each has a corresponding case in
`vfxDeterminism.test.ts` or `vfx.test.ts`/`init.test.ts`.

## Interface

Full spec, with amendments from the implementation: see the exporter repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-vfx-chain-interface.md` and
`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-22-vfx-chain-runtime.md` (the cross-repo plan). Guide:
`docs/guides/vfx-chain.mdx` in this branch.

## Cost

Capture-dependent kernels (`self`/`backdrop`) put the whole composition on screenshot capture
pinned to one worker (the existing `htmlInCanvas` render-mode hint); `none` kernels put it on
screenshot capture with workers unpinned (`webgl-context` gate). Neither regresses a composition
that would otherwise be baked in After Effects; both are slower than a drawElement render of the
same composition without the node. Measured cost: 21.7 ms/frame at 1080p on an Apple M4 Pro
hardware GPU. SwiftShader/fleet cost is unmeasured (Docker daemon unavailable in this environment).
Telemetry (`vfx_node_count`, `vfx_capture`, `vfx_types` on `render_complete`) is in this branch;
no dashboard tile yet.

## Follow-on (not in this branch)

- Exporter Task 19: camera-parented null / POI rig projection (retro-wave's remaining geometry gap).
- Exporter Task 20: bake-verify block-error threshold review; Fractal Noise blend-mode popup mapping.
- Phase 2b: `backdrop` capture (group the layers below a host into the source canvas) and the
  `luma-matte`/`noise` kernels it enables — designed, not built.
- Phase 5: run the page-side compositor *inside* drawElement capture instead of gating one off for
  the other — would also lift the ~16% of local renders currently refused by the
  `mix-blend-mode`/`filter`/`backdrop-filter` gates.
- SwiftShader kernel cost (needs a running Docker daemon).
