title: feat(catalog): Cursors catalog section, the film opening cursor, and eight new pointer animations
body:
Mintlify preview: https://hyperframes-feat-catalog-cursors-section.mintlify.site/catalog/index

## What

A new Cursors section in the public HyperFrames catalog: the six existing
pointer items (moved there by their tags, not rebuilt) plus the film's
opening cursor and eight new professional cursor animations.

- **Existing, retagged**: oversized-cursor, simulated-cursor,
  multiplayer-cursors, cursor-glyph-trail, press-ripple, touch-indicator.
  `vfx-text-cursor` (a shader text caret) stays out — its first tag is
  `html-in-canvas`, a caret is not a pointer.
- **dart-cursor** — the arrowhead from the opening of the film, extracted:
  its markup, styles and motion only, nothing else from the film (no text,
  brand, logos, or project names). Dives in from depth, flies nose-first
  with motion blur along its path, squashes on two clicks, whips out.
- **Eight new**: drag-and-drop (a task-board card carried in lockstep),
  marquee select (a drawn selection rectangle, tiles join as the box
  reaches them), text select (arrow to I-beam, a selection that grows
  character by character, a floating format toolbar), context menu
  (right-click, a menu that blooms from the tip and flips at the frame
  edge), magnetic pointer (a dot that morphs into a toolbar button's own
  hover plate), zoom follow (Screen-Studio-style auto-zoom on a spring),
  annotate (a pen that hand-draws a circle, underline or arrow exactly
  under its own nib), agent (a narrated status tag, thinking shimmer,
  sparkle clicks). Each is a distinct mechanic, not a tint of another.

## Where the section comes from

`scripts/generate-catalog-pages.ts`'s `groupForItem()` shelves an item on
"Cursors" when its first tag is `cursor` — the same tags[0]-precedence
pattern `3d-motion` and `carousel` already use. `SECTIONS`/`GROUP_ORDER`
place the new shelf next to Motion & effects.

## A real bug found and fixed at the root

Regenerating the catalog on a clean `origin/main`, with nothing else
changed, still rewrote `docs.json`: `generate-catalog-pages.ts`'s own nav
builder double-nests any section wrapping exactly one identically-named
child shelf (`3D motion`, `Carousels`, `Blocks`, and this PR's own
`Cursors`) — `{group:"3D motion", pages:[{group:"3D motion",
pages:[...]}]}`. `sync-docs-catalog.mjs`, run afterward, silently repaired
it, which is why the documented single-command CONTRIBUTING.md recipe never
surfaced it.

Fixed at the root with `sectionEntry()`, a pure function extracted from the
section-building loop: flatten to the child's own pages when a section
wraps exactly one identically-named shelf, keep nesting otherwise (a
differently-named single child, like "Data & charts" wrapping "Data", still
nests on purpose). Shown red without the fix (31 passed, 1 failed), green
with it (32 passed). Verified programmatically after a full regeneration:
no node in the Catalog tab nests a child whose own group equals its
parent's.

## Commits

1. Regenerate `registry.json` and the pages that had drifted from main
   before this PR touched anything (week-in-merges missing, stale source on
   four pages).
2. The Cursors section, the six retagged items, dart-cursor.
3. The eight new cursors.
4. Simplify two of the nine (a duplicated SVG pass collapsed to `<defs>` +
   `<use>`, a hand-inlined clamp replaced by the file's own helper) and
   regenerate the eight pages that had gone live before their own payload
   existed (empty variables + a dead video fallback instead of the live
   Tune panel).
5. `oxfmt` over the nine new compositions (never run before; cosmetic
   line-wrap only, pixel-verified unchanged).
6. The `sectionEntry()` fix above, with its regression test.
7. Regenerate the nine pages/payloads to match the reformatted source.
8. Trim a comment under the repo's 4-line cap.

## Verification

- `node scripts/lint-registry-items.mjs` on all 15 items: 0 errors.
- Every new component's `<html data-composition-variables>` matches its
  `registry-item.json` exactly.
- Every new component's visual state is a pure function of timeline time
  (no `Math.random`, no `Date`, no state mutated across frames) — seeking
  either direction reproduces the same frame.
- All 9 rendered end-to-end through the branch CLI on ai-miga; all 9
  snapshotted and reviewed by eye across their durations, no clipping, no
  overlap, no frozen frames.
- Independent review, two passes (base branch, then this fix's delta): no
  BLOCKERs, no MAJORs.

## Before / After

### Before

Production catalog sidebar, no Cursors section.

![Before: production catalog sidebar, no Cursors section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54ae4fd2-6485-4635-8c64-5a6f7f98aa8f)

### After

This branch's own Mintlify preview deployment. The Cursors shelf (15
items) in the sidebar, and the Dart Cursor's page rendering live in the
real HyperFrames player, not a mock.

![After: Cursors shelf in the sidebar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c31de104-fb5b-48e0-82c6-c3b7a267e891)

![After: Dart Cursor live in the player](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5ec1ee5d-5e5b-4869-b9ea-ec1170275f43)

All 8 new cursors plus dart-cursor, one representative frame each,
rendered end-to-end through the branch CLI:

![The nine cursors, one frame each](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/937e270b-a0f8-42cd-874b-abaac88d98fa)

title: fix(studio): clip pictures at full strength and a seam where touching clips meet
body:
## What changes for a person

- Sub-composition and text clips on the timeline now show their frame at full strength, like video and image clips
  already do. Before, their frame was drawn at 70% opacity through a `lighten` blend; on the light theme
  (`data-theme="paper"`) the picture nearly vanished into the clip.
- Two clips that meet end to start now have a 1px line in the row colour at the exact point where they meet. No clip
  moves or shrinks, so clip edges, keyframe diamonds and the time ruler still agree.

## How

- `CompositionThumbnail` reads two new theme tokens instead of hard-coded values:
  `--timeline-composition-thumbnail-opacity` (default `1`) and `--timeline-composition-thumbnail-blend`
  (default `normal`), declared with the other `--timeline-*` tokens in `styles/theme.css`. A host that wants the old
  dimmed look sets `0.7` / `lighten`.
- `TimelineClipJoins` finds the times where one clip on a row ends as the next begins (within the lane's existing
  1 ms tolerance, `TRACK_GAP_EPSILON_S`) and draws a 1px line there in `theme.rowBackground`, so a host's theme
  override carries through. It sits above an idle or hovered clip and below the keyframe diamonds and a selected
  clip.
- The row overlay that already draws transition badges now draws the joins too, and works out its own transition
  seams, which keeps `TimelineLanes.tsx` under the 600-line limit.
- While a clip is being moved, rows draw no join lines: the moved clip is drawn by the drag overlay rather than at
  its position, so a line would mark a boundary that is not there. They come back on drop. Resizing keeps them,
  following the resize preview.
- A selected clip draws above the line, so a join next to a selected clip shows the selection outline instead.
  Putting the line above a selected clip would also put it above the keyframe diamonds of unselected clips.

## Before

![Before, light theme: the Title and Card clips are faint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/627b4fb6-472d-40cc-b3df-ac2706ce1987)
![Before, dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d17a5472-ca4b-4c5f-9c1a-e6c810c3c8ba)
![Before, where two clips meet (4x, dark above, light below)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc2bb032-82c3-46b8-a40e-d0610e74ef7e)

## After

![After, light theme: the Title and Card clips read at full strength](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bec8a689-b202-4f5b-b52d-f7c89179af7c)
![After, dark theme](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/96c55c89-13a0-41a9-81e2-3d2169ecb8a5)
![After, where two clips meet: a 1px row-coloured line on the boundary (4x, dark above, light below)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2aec954e-5678-45db-9cd2-94db7ca161c1)

Same fixture project (video, text layer, sub-composition, image and audio clips), Studio dev server, default dark
theme and `data-theme="paper"`, captured headless at 2x pixel density.

## What I measured

- Computed styles on every pictured clip, Before: Title and Card `opacity 0.7`, `mix-blend-mode lighten`; After:
  `opacity 1`, `normal`. Video filmstrips and the image clip read `1` / `normal` in both.
- The fixture has two touching pairs. Before: 0 join lines; After: 2. The first join sits at the same x in both
  captures, and a pixel diff of the close-up changes only the 2 device pixels on the boundary, which now read as
  the row colour in each theme.
- New tests fail on the old code: `CompositionThumbnail.test.ts` (1 of 6 red), and the new `TimelineLanes.test.tsx`
  case (0 join lines drawn). `TimelineClipJoins.test.ts` covers ordering, float noise, a one-frame gap and overlaps.
- `TimelineLanes.test.tsx` 14/14 (including no join lines during a move drag, which fails on the first version),
  `TimelineClipJoins.test.ts` 2/2, `timelineGaps.test.ts`, `timelineTransitionSeams.test.ts`,
  `theme.test.ts`, `tokenGate.test.ts`, `hexRatchet.test.ts` green; pre-commit lint, format, fallow, filesize and
  typecheck green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Hosts other than Studio's own dev server. A host that never loads `theme.css` falls back to each property's
  initial value (`1`, `normal`), which is the new default look.
- The join line during a resize, and on rows with keyframe lanes expanded; covered by reading the code and tests,
  not captured.
- Only the default fit zoom was captured.

title: feat(catalog): add a 3D section with product turntable, glass hero, exploded stack, 3D logo
body:
**Preview:** https://hyperframes-feat-catalog-3d-objects.mintlify.site/catalog (the 3D section; item pages at https://hyperframes-feat-catalog-3d-objects.mintlify.site/catalog/blocks/product-turntable, /glass-hero, /exploded-stack, /extruded-logo)

## What this adds

The catalog gets one **3D** section with two shelves:

- **3D motion**: the seven existing pieces, unchanged (same pages, same URLs).
- **3D objects** (new): four Three.js blocks built for the things agents most often ask the catalog for and cannot find: a product on a turntable, glass, an exploded layer diagram, and a 3D logo.

The camera-move shelf under Motion & effects was called "Camera & 3D" but holds only camera moves, so it is now **Camera** and 3D lives in one place. No page URL changes; only the shelf label on those 11 pages.

## The four items, and why each looks the way it does

| Item | What it is | Design call |
|---|---|---|
| Product Turntable | One full revolution on a studio plinth, seamless loop. `model_url` takes a GLB/glTF (auto-scaled and centred on the plinth); empty uses a built-in procedural drink can with an editable label. | Static camera and a linear spin so the clip loops cleanly; baked contact shadow instead of shadow maps to keep render cost down. |
| Glass Hero | A solid glass object (torus knot, ring or lens) rises in front of a giant headline and keeps turning, so the type bends and splits into colour through it. | The headline is drawn inside the 3D scene, because transmission only refracts what the renderer drew; a faint dot grid gives the glass something to bend everywhere. |
| Exploded Stack | Isometric layer plates explode apart with a numbered label per layer, hold, then collapse, so it loops. | True isometric (orthographic) camera and one motif per layer so plates read as different systems; labels sit on the open right-hand corner. |
| Extruded Logo | Beveled letters flip up one by one, the word swings so light runs across the bevels, then settles readable. Chrome, gold or matte. | A softbox studio environment (bright strips on black) so chrome shows crisp highlight bands instead of flat grey. |

All four follow the Three.js adapter contract: every frame is `render(t)` from one paused GSAP clock registered on `window.__timelines`, and `window.__hf.buildReady` holds render-ready until the scene module has built. Three.js 0.184 and fonts load from jsdelivr, like other catalog items. Variables are declared in `data-composition-variables`, so the docs pages show live controls.

## Render cost (5 s clip, 1920x1080, default quality)

Measured on the shared 32-core render box during its reserved timing slot (load average ~13 when the run started, so not fully idle), 150 frames each, default settings.

| Item | Render time |
|---|---|
| Exploded Stack | 17 s |
| Extruded Logo | 29 s |
| Product Turntable | 57 s |
| Glass Hero | 119 s (transmission renders the scene twice per frame; a half-resolution transmission pass saved only 7% and softened the refraction, so it stays full quality) |

## What I measured

- **Seek-safety:** each item rendered as a PNG sequence with 1 worker (frames in order) and with 4 workers (out of order), compared byte for byte: 0 differing frames for all four (60, 50, 60, 50 frames). The check caught a real defect on the way: exploded-stack labels moved by fractional pixels and rasterised differently by frame order (18 of 60 frames differed); they now move in whole pixels.
- **Model slot:** Khronos' WaterBottle glTF sample renders fitted on the plinth; a dead `model_url` fails the render (exit 1) naming the block, instead of silently showing the built-in can.
- **Failure is loud and bounded:** with a broken font URL the render fails at the engine's readiness timeout (45 s, retried once; ~93 s observed) with `buildReady never resolved for: extruded-logo` and the 404. A stalled model URL is bounded the same way.
- **Grouping test:** `node --import tsx --test scripts/generate-catalog-pages.test.ts` exit 0, 29 passed. Removing the `3d-object` rule fails exactly the new test (28 pass, 1 fail).
- **Generated files:** produced by `generate-registry-items` -> `generate-catalog-payloads --only <item>` -> `generate-catalog-pages` -> `sync-docs-catalog` (last). `main` itself drifts from these generators (8 unrelated files, plus the texture-mask duplicate section); that drift is kept out of this PR, which carries only the delta this change produces.
- **Install:** all four resolve and install from this branch's registry (`resolveItem` + `installItem` against the branch's raw registry URL) into `compositions/<name>.html`.
- `hyperframes lint` on each item: 0 errors, 0 warnings.
- On-device search index regenerated with `scripts/catalog/build-local-vectors.ts`: additive only (4 new names, 4 new vectors, the revision line in `registry.json`).

## What I did NOT exercise

- Catalog preview posters/videos on the CDN are not uploaded (that is a maintainer step); tiles show the live player instead.
- Mounting a block inside another composition with `data-composition-src` renders a blank 3D layer today: the render bundler merges a sub-composition's `<script type="module">` into one classic script (`packages/core/src/compiler/inlineSubCompositions.ts`), while the preview runtime keeps it a module. That is a core bug outside this PR, reported separately. Each block renders correctly as its own composition.

## Before

The live catalog today: a flat "3D motion" section pinned first.

![Before: live catalog landing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91aca20f-d33d-46de-93ed-4deaf58510de)

## After

The landing, with **3D** first (the four new objects sit under "Show All 11" until they have CDN posters):

![After: landing with the 3D section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/563f9b4d-c6d7-4194-abfa-dfce45f9f0d1)

The sidebar nests **3D > 3D motion / 3D objects**; every item page plays live with its variables:

![After: Glass Hero page](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b9bffbc8-a514-42e0-a16f-026c62747db5)

![After: the other three pages playing live](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61ca844d-2f8a-4340-a4ff-06aba669fd67)

Six frames across each clip:

![Product Turntable frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efbfd183-43db-4590-b040-527f2127b8dc)
![Glass Hero frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec5c4db9-5f1f-4a65-b3c1-eb50d396fc7b)
![Exploded Stack frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06d404c6-3c7b-4365-9738-73b5248e7919)
![Extruded Logo frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36ef4eff-7e32-46ea-abcb-bdf7cc33fea5)

Product Turntable with a real GLB in `model_url` (Khronos WaterBottle sample):

title: fix(catalog): editor search vocabulary + positional query
body:
## Summary

Two fixes for `hyperframes catalog` search:

- **Editor vocabulary.** `crossfade`, `cross dissolve`, `countdown timer`
  and `split screen comparison` are phrasings agents commonly search with,
  but they used to miss existing catalog items (`fade-through`,
  `transitions-dissolve`, `count-up`, `before-after-wipe`) because the
  items' tags never used those words. Adds the missing vocabulary as tags
  on the four items, extends the word-tier retrieval eval with a regression
  test against the real registry, and rebuilds the on-device vector artifact
  to match.
- **Positional query.** `hyperframes catalog "smoke"` silently printed the
  whole catalog: the command declared no positional argument, so citty
  dropped the word. Declares one (`words`, same pattern as `add`'s item name
  and `docs`' topic) that means the same thing as `--query`, with `--query`
  winning if both are given.

One candidate pairing considered for the vocabulary fix — "ken burns / slow
pan zoom on a photo" against `push-in` and `cinematic-zoom` — turned out not
to fit either item and was dropped. `push-in` has no image/photo slot at all
(text-only), `cinematic-zoom` is a hardcoded shader-transition demo with no
photo slot either, and neither scores above 0 for the query "ken burns"
against the real catalog. This reads as a genuine missing catalog item (a
pan/zoom-on-a-photo primitive with a media slot), not a vocabulary gap —
out of scope here.

## Test plan

- [x] `vitest run packages/cli/src/registry/localSearch.test.ts` — 32/32 passed,
      including the new real-registry regression cases; proven non-vacuous by
      mutation (broke one target name, watched it go red, reverted).
- [x] `vitest run packages/cli/src/commands/catalog.test.ts` — 42/42 passed,
      including new positional-arg cases.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` in packages/cli — clean.
- [x] `oxlint` / `oxfmt --check` on every changed file — clean.

title: chore: release v0.8.63
body:
# HyperFrames v0.8.63

Released on 2026-09-23.

HyperFrames adds IBM Bob as a supported coding agent, and Studio stops a thumbnail error loop that could hang the timeline. Static file requests now stay inside their served folders, closing a path traversal gap.

## Features

- **Studio:** Export AudioWaveform, ImageThumbnail, useRenderClipContent ([b9fe13ad8](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b9fe13ad8cfcbf1c8c0a95cf19cce7cf2918944d), [#4301](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4301)).
- **CLI:** Add IBM Bob runtime support ([105984cac](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/105984cac4d8a52d99075cc06ed25ab2f12451e2), [#3930](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/3930)).

## Fixes

- **Engine:** Classify a single-keyframe video as problematic, not healthy ([29378b6c7](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/29378b6c7f08bf62635e7e80286021c2af57de9a), [#3998](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/3998)).
- **CLI:** Replace pre-planted links when writing capture files ([42eb6e9ad](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/42eb6e9ad2ca75fe1d5ac79794935f3ee523b979), [#4298](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4298)).
- **Producer:** Bound nested media by a host's data-duration when it has no data-end ([1d6a0d514](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/1d6a0d5141d0c71b0af94ac993590966d53f4aff), [#3975](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/3975)).
- **Studio:** Stop VideoFrameThumbnail error→cleanup infinite loop ([e5eeeef97](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/e5eeeef972f264b3989e004ec0de6862db31709a), [#4037](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4037)).
- **CLI:** Stopping the preview server no longer leaves a Chrome running ([1b8f8a43d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/1b8f8a43d43bc2456075215b066b23e11d821435), [#4183](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4183)).
- **Server:** Contain static file requests within their served roots ([cc19b8c81](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/cc19b8c8121d938aa589c50363f3c099e8dec8e7), [#4217](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4217)).
- **Media Use:** Remove clicks and ~25ms gaps at every transcript-cut splice ([dd9747817](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/dd97478175584cca0e071ed2e3ba686fd57c48db), [#4179](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4179)).

## Docs & Examples

- Alphabetize supported coding agents ([ec3bc93b9](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/ec3bc93b90e482141da324568124ce7cf094eafe), [#4297](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4297)).

## Catalog

- **Catalog:** Regenerating the texture-mask page no longer duplicates its section ([bc1c60ae5](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/bc1c60ae5b6e599a3caa482052547a5775a52261), [#4302](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4302)).

## Internal

- **Studio:** Remove unreachable expanded-child timeline code ([b73df3549](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b73df3549eb52744fe54dac2728a2f9d0fb6a9c7), [#4219](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4219)).
- Compare test reachability against the merge ref's base parent ([8027c758d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/8027c758d1d5fb5a43439ecdd7e0e12ead80de41), [#4303](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4303)).

## Full changelog

https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/compare/v0.8.62...v0.8.63

title: feat(registry): starfield
body:
## Summary
- Adds `starfield`, a seek-safe twinkling night-sky overlay block to the HyperFrames catalog (gaps row C2): sparse or dense stars in a warm/cool/white tone, radial-masked so the frame center stays clear by default for a subject or caption underneath.
- (Note, not in this PR: the regenerator that adds `starfield` also incidentally restores a stale-index item, `week-in-merges`, whose files already exist on main but were missing from `registry.json` — confirmed reproducible on a clean `origin/main` with zero of my changes. `check-registry-set-delta` correctly rejects bundling that fix here, so I reverted it out; flagging it separately for whoever owns that item.)

## Design decisions (UX calls made without asking, per gaps lane convention)
- **Type: `hyperframes:block`**, not `hyperframes:component`. It mounts on its own timeline track above footage (like `organic-light-leak-overlay`, `camcorder-hud`), not pasted inline into a host composition. Matches the existing `media-treatment-overlay` family.
- **Determinism**: one non-repeating GSAP tween drives `state.phase` 0→1 over the mounted host clip's duration; every star's opacity is `sin(2*PI * integer * phase + const)`, so phase=0 and phase=1 always match exactly, and each star runs its own independent whole cycle count so the field's *pattern* repeats only at that loop boundary, not every ~1.5s.
- **Star scatter**: a golden-ratio low-discrepancy (Weyl) sequence for x/y placement (even 2D coverage, no clumping, no PRNG state), and the registry's existing sin-fold index hash (`stop-motion-cadence.html`'s `rnd(n)`) for the other per-star scalars — no `Math.random()` anywhere.
- **Center clearance**: a CSS `mask-image: radial-gradient(...)` on the star field, not per-particle JS — same idiom as 7+ other registry items (`code-highlight.html`, `conic-progress-ring.html`, etc.).
- **No visual reference photo/video shipped in the demo**: `demo.html`'s backdrop is a CSS gradient (not a licensed stock photo) to avoid introducing an unlicensed binary asset; the overlay composites correctly over any real footage in actual use.

## Open question for gaps/home (batch-level, not decided here)
An independent altitude review flagged that the `profile`/`family`/`jobs` taxonomy fields (used by `grain-field`, `aurora-drift`, `drift-hold` — all `hyperframes:component`) are currently components-only; no block carries them. So `starfield` and its coming siblings (snow, rain, smoke/fog, dust motes, embers) won't be discoverable as an "ambient" family the way the component-side ambient primitives are, unless that's extended to blocks or these ship as components instead. Flagging for a batch decision before building the rest — starfield itself is defensible either way (it matches the existing block precedent exactly), so I didn't block on it.

## Evidence
Agents' catalog-miss reports repeatedly ask for a night-sky/starfield overlay. Repro on 0.8.62: `catalog --query "starfield"` returns unrelated items (a rating-star icon fill, a grain texture), never an actual starfield.

**Honest limitation**: I could not verify live search ranking for the word "starfield" against this branch pre-merge — `hyperframes catalog --query` reads the *published* main-branch registry manifest by default, not a local checkout, so a not-yet-merged item can't rank in that command regardless of its tags. I did confirm the mechanical piece: `scripts/catalog/check-artifact-coverage.ts` passes, meaning the local search-vector artifact correctly embeds and covers this item with its current name/title/description/tags. Whether it actually surfaces near the top of a live "starfield" query — including against the word tier's known 3x name/title weighting over description/tags (per catsearch's C1 work) — can only be checked post-merge; I'm not claiming it here.

## What I verified
- `hyperframes lint` / `hyperframes check`: 0 errors, 0 warnings (via a scratch harness outside the repo, since registry items ship without their own `index.html`)
- Determinism: two independent renders at the same timestamps are byte-identical (sha256), both on the 6s demo and on a 12s-mount scratch harness
- **Caught by an independent adversarial review, fixed before this PR opened**: (1) the block read its own duration via its own DOM id, which the runtime strips once mounted as a sub-composition — every mount silently pinned to 6s and stars froze past that; fixed by reading duration from the host clip. Re-verified independently: a 12s-mounted instance now renders 4 distinct frames at 0/7/8.3/11s where it was previously byte-identical past 6s. (2) all stars shared one cycle-count divisor, so the field's pattern visibly repeated every ~1.5s instead of only at the true loop boundary; fixed by giving each star an independent whole cycle count. Full report: `~/.claude/state/pr-reports/hyperframes-starfield-047273a712-review.md` (local, not attached — team-local path).
- `scripts/catalog/check-artifact-coverage.ts`: passes, search index covers the new item
- `node scripts/lint-registry-items.mjs`: passes for `starfield` (2 pre-existing unrelated failures elsewhere in the registry, not touched by this PR: `blocks/vfx-text-cursor`, `components/caption-emoji-pop`, both missing `@font-face` declarations)
- `node scripts/check-docs-catalog.mjs`: all 4 checks pass
- Visual: rendered snapshots at 5 evenly-spaced timestamps, reviewed by eye (attached)

## What I did NOT exercise
- No production render through the full `hyperframes render` pipeline (used `snapshot`/`check`, which cover the same runtime path used for CI's `verify-catalog-payloads`)
- No real footage composited underneath in the demo (CSS gradient backdrop, see design decisions)
- No live catalog search ranking against this branch (see "Honest limitation" above)

Simplify pass (4 parallel reviewers: reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) and an independent adversarial correctness review both ran on this diff, findings applied, before opening.

![Rendered frame at t=0s, sparse warm tone, default variables](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfb2c1f5-d801-4a6f-9908-4f599a8eacd6)

![Rendered frame at t=3s — different stars lit, confirming twinkle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec5c21c9-b3de-4dbc-a427-0d95617f45cf)

![5-frame contact sheet across the 6s loop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92800bc7-519d-4e18-b721-9d9be4639b0b)

title: fix(skills): push transitions reveal the incoming scene on every seek path
body:
## What changes

The four incoming-scene tweens in `skills/hyperframes-animation/transitions/css-push.md` (push slide, vertical push, elastic push, squeeze) set `opacity: 1` only in their from-vars. The catalog's hard rule starts every scene after the first at `opacity: 0`, so a project copied from these snippets fails lint with the error `gsap_cold_seek_hidden_fromto_missing_reveal` (and a `--strict` render refuses it). Each destination now carries `opacity: 1` too. The motion is unchanged: the tween holds opacity at 1 → 1.

The same templates live in `TRANSITION-REGISTRY.md` and its three vendored copies (`skills/{faceless-explainer,pr-to-video,product-launch-video}/scripts/lib/transitions.json`), whose header asks to keep them in step with `css-push.md`; they get the same one-token change.

## What I measured

A two-scene project built from the catalog's scene template plus the push slide, linted with a CLI built from main:

| Snippet | `hyperframes lint` |
|---|---|
| before | 1 error: `gsap_cold_seek_hidden_fromto_missing_reveal` on `#scene2` |
| after | 0 errors, 0 warnings |

Both versions render the push correctly in a normal render.

The workflow injectors were not failing today: a project built with `product-launch-video`'s `assemble-index.mjs` + `transitions.mjs inject` (push-slide) lints clean with the old and the new template alike, because those hosts never start hidden. For them the change is consistency with the source they vendor. The injectors' own tests still pass (`product-launch-video/scripts/transitions.test.mjs` 4 passed, `faceless-explainer/scripts/transitions.test.mjs` 1 passed), but they cover cut and crossfade only; no test pins the push templates.

## What I did NOT exercise

The lint rule's cold-worker failure (the incoming scene staying invisible in the encoded video) did not reproduce in my renders; this PR is proven against the lint error only.

## Review

Independent review, two rounds: no blocking findings. Round one found the vendored copies (fixed here); round two confirmed every changed line holds opacity 1 → 1 and that no other copy of the old template remains in the repo.

title: perf(studio): re-render only the edited scene's thumbnails after an edit
body:
## What this fixes

Editing one scene file made Studio re-render the thumbnail of every scene.

- **Server.** The thumbnail cache key included the whole-project signature, so any file change invalidated every scene's cached thumbnail.
- **Client.** It kept one global thumbnail revision, so every mounted thumbnail refetched at once.
- **Contention.** About 24 renders then queued in the thumbnail browser, ahead of the shadow preview reload the person was actually waiting for.

On a 12-scene project that thumbnail storm is most of the edit-to-screen time.

## What changed

- **Server key per composition** (`studio-server/src/helpers/compositionInputs.ts`, `routes/thumbnail.ts`).
  - A composition's thumbnail is keyed on what it renders from: the project minus the other compositions the root mounts. The root counts as an input, because sub-composition previews are built on its `<head>`.
  - Editing `compositions/scene-3.html` no longer moves scene-0's key.
  - The in-flight guard checks both the adapter's cached signature and a fresh one, because the adapter's can lag the file watcher.
- **Which compositions an edit affects** (`compositionsAffectedBy`). The `file-change` event now carries `affectedCompositions`.
  - `null` means "all": the root, assets, and files the root doesn't mount.
  - An older server that sends no field also reads as "all".
- **Per-composition revisions** (`player/store/thumbnailSlice.ts`). `thumbnailRevisions` is keyed by composition path, with `*` meaning "every composition". Paths are normalized, so a scene mounted as `./scene.html` matches the server's `scene.html`.
- **The preview reload goes first** (`player/lib/thumbnailScheduler.ts`, `player/hooks/useShadowPreviewReload.ts`).
  - While the shadow preview reloads, composition thumbnail jobs are held.
  - Composition thumbnails already rendering are aborted and requeued, then run once the preview has swapped in.
  - Every exit releases the hold: promote, fail, reset and unmount.

## Measured

Same run, interleaved, on one Linux dev box: main at the merge base (06340f656) vs this branch. A 12-scene, 60 s fixture project (sub-compositions, images, video, audio, a local font). One on-disk edit to one scene. Headless Chrome, thumbnails on. 5 rounds each.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Edit to new pixels on screen, median | **5.14 s** (4.75-6.75) | **1.62 s** (1.55-1.64) |
| Thumbnail requests triggered by the edit | 19-21 (every scene) | 3 (the edited scene only; one preempted and retried) |

- **What's left.** Most of the remaining 1.6 s is the preview document rebuild and the full iframe reload, both unchanged here.
- **Causal check, from an earlier profiling run.** With every `/thumbnail/` request blocked on main, edit to screen fell from 5.4 s to 1.9 s. This PR gets to 1.6 s with thumbnails on.

## Before

Main, one scene edit (shape colour and title in scene-0). The captures run over an ssh tunnel, so absolute times are longer than local.

- +20 s: every scene thumbnail on the timeline is blank while all 12 re-render.
- +40 s: back.

![main before the edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25f38f89-c3a5-4c9f-8320-c1588c4b01d7)
![main, 20 s after the edit: all scene thumbnails re-rendering](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ffb24922-6968-438d-9c4f-f3904a26bbb1)
![main, 40 s after the edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3edfec7e-b9d3-4555-a48c-7db24c6f5223)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec55f43c-0f62-48c4-a76c-dbe25512d72f

## After

The same edit on this branch. The server rendered only scene-0 again, and the other scenes came back from cache. The timeline still re-mounts during the preview reload (unchanged here), so the other thumbnails redraw as it mounts.

![this PR, 20 s after the edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b68904b-e7f9-44d8-9ea5-b3a475e779bd)
![this PR, 40 s after the edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cb6353d-757d-4b3b-98eb-d550bfc1f466)
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36123ee2-4149-4c5b-8707-03092f43083d

## Tests

Each changed test file was run alone, and every one exits 0.

- **studio-server.** `compositionInputs` (3), `routes/thumbnail` (20).
- **studio.**
  - `thumbnailScheduler` (17), `playerStore` (67), `useRenderClipContent` (12), `useExternalFileChangeCoordinator` (18).
  - The three sidebar tests (1, 7, 2).
- **Checks.** `tsc` is 0 in studio, studio-server and cli; oxfmt and oxlint are clean on every changed file.
- **Proven non-vacuous.**
  - Removing the `./` normalization fails "finds the revision of a composition mounted with a ./ path".
  - Removing the fresh-signature check fails "does not cache pixels changed in flight behind a stale adapter signature".

## Not exercised

- Nested compositions more than one level deep, edited in a live Studio. They are covered by `compositionsAffectedBy`'s closure and its unit test only.
- Windows paths, in a live run.
- **Cache growth.** The signature caches keep one small, fixed-size entry per composition ever thumbnailed and are never evicted. That is fine for normal sessions; add an LRU if a server ever holds thousands.
- **Known follow-up, not in this PR.** On Studio startup every composition thumbnail is fetched twice (a first fetch is orphaned when the timeline session starts). It gets its own PR.

title: feat(registry): a Lottie character walk-in, and looping Lottie that keeps playing
body:
## What this does

Agents often ask for character animation: a mascot that walks in, a walk cycle, a character that points or reacts. HyperFrames already plays Lottie files, which is where a jointed, animator-made character lives, but nothing told an agent that, and two bugs made character Lottie break in renders:

1. **A looping Lottie vanished after its first cycle.** A 1 s walk cycle with `loop: true` in a 3 s scene rendered blank from 1 s on. The adapter handed lottie-web a time past the file's end, and lottie-web draws nothing there.
2. **A one-shot Lottie vanished when it finished.** Same cause: a `loop: false` animation shorter than its scene went blank after its last frame instead of holding it, as lottie-web does when it plays by itself.

Both fixes live in the Lottie adapter's `seek`, which every render and Studio preview goes through. A `loop: true` animation is wrapped by frame number (`time × frameRate` modulo the file's frame count), with a value a float hair under a whole cycle treated as the next cycle's frame 0, so a loop never holds or skips at its seam. A lottie-web one-shot past its end is seeked to its last frame by frame number. In-range one-shots take the same millisecond path as before.

On top of that:

- **`lottie-character-walk` block.** A jointed flat character walks in on planted feet, stops, and points at a card that comes in on the point. The body acting is one Lottie file; the card is the usual paused GSAP timeline. Monochrome per the placeholder rule, one accent.
- **Docs where an agent looks.** A Characters section in the Lottie adapter skill (acting in the Lottie, stage in GSAP, no per-animation start offset, license the file), a routing row in the animation skill for walk cycle, mascot and puppet, loop semantics corrected in the techniques and Remotion port notes, and a short Characters paragraph in the prompting guide.

## The character file

`registry/blocks/lottie-character-walk/assets/mascot.json` was made for this repo and ships under its Apache-2.0 license. It was generated from a small rig description: each limb is a shape layer parented at its joint, the legs are solved with two-bone IK so planted feet do not slide, and keyframes are reduced to those linear interpolation cannot reproduce within a quarter pixel or degree. No third-party character or asset is used. It is listed in `.prettierignore` next to the other generated block assets, because pretty-printing multiplies its size.

## Missing `loop`

A Lottie registered without `loop` now cycles, because lottie-web's own default for a missing `loop` is `true` and that is what an author who read the lottie docs expects.

## Before / After

A 1 s walk cycle with `loop: true` in a 3 s scene, rendered frames at the same six times.

![Before: blank from 1 s on](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4858d1df-69d3-4cd4-b9de-3cd29c6f989a)

![After: the cycle keeps walking](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68e9a27e-00d2-4360-9ff3-623dab40d649)

The new block:

![lottie-character-walk](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/820f4da2-7c05-4ab7-a7a7-ee8676ef7d2d)

## What I measured

- `packages/core` `lottie.test.ts`: exit 0, 30 passed. Each change was removed in turn and its tests went red: no loop wrap (2 fail), the old seconds-based wrap (the seam test fails), no end-of-file hold (2 fail), no dotLottie wrap (1 fails), no seam snap (the 23.976 fps and 25 fps seam cases fail). `tsc --noEmit` exit 0, oxlint 0 / 0, oxfmt clean.
- Seam sweep against the real adapter: 1,176 frame-count × frame-rate pairs over 60 cycles each (70,560 seeks), plus 224 pairs where the composition rate differs from the file's rate checked with exact rational arithmetic: no seam misses and no wrong snaps. The snap tolerance (1e-6 frame) is about 68,000× the worst float error at a million frames and about 24,000× below the smallest real subframe step.
- Real renders with this branch's CLI, 1 s file in a 3 s scene: with `loop: true` the frames at 1.3 s and 2.3 s are byte-identical to 0.3 s, and 1.6 s / 2.6 s to 0.6 s. With `loop: false` every frame from 0.98 s on is identical and shows the character. On main both go blank after 1 s.
- The block renders 7.5 s at 1080p in 32-45 s. A headless probe that seeks lottie-web straight to a frame and one that steps through every frame produce identical SVG transforms.
- `lint-registry-items`, `check-docs-catalog`, `check-artifact-coverage`, `gen-skills-manifest --check`, `lint-skills`, `check:catalog-drift`, and `verify:catalog-payloads --changed origin/main` (headless Chrome load of the block's payload) all pass.

## What I did NOT exercise

- dotLottie players in a real browser: the dotLottie loop path is covered by the unit test only.
- A 1-worker and a 6-worker render of the block differ in 9 of 225 frames by at most 36 levels, on the edge of the foot shadow only. The pose is identical (checked at the SVG level); this is rasterization, and a pure-SVG control shows the same class of difference (1 of 150 frames), so it is not introduced here.
- Studio preview of a looping Lottie was not walked by hand; it calls the same `seek`.
- dotLottie v2 keeps its existing `Math.min(frame, totalFrames - 1)` clamp, so in the last frame of each loop cycle a dotLottie player may show whole frames instead of subframes. Unchanged from main and unconfirmed; left alone because dotLottie's valid frame range was not verified.

## Review

Independent adversarial review over four rounds; each round's findings were fixed and re-reviewed at the new head.

- Round 1: the one-shot hold round-tripped through milliseconds and could land a hair short of the last frame. Fixed by seeking by frame number.
- Round 2: after that refactor, a loop could hit the hold at its own seam for some frame-count and rate pairs. Fixed by wrapping loops by frame.
- Round 3: the frame wrap still landed a float hair under a whole cycle for about half of ordinary pairs, repeating the previous cycle's last frame. Fixed with the seam snap and two tests at 23.976 fps and 25 fps.
- Round 4 (this head): no blockers, no majors. Minors: the dotLottie clamp noted above; exact-boundary and dotLottie v1 loop coverage are thin but the paths are shared.

title: feat(registry): torn-paper-rip transition
body:
## What

Adds `torn-paper-rip` to the catalog: a jagged, fibrous paper tear that travels across the frame, taking the outgoing scene with it and leaving the next one standing, with an exposed paper cross-section riding just behind the cut edge.

## Why

Agents searching the catalog for a physical paper-tear transition repeatedly come up empty — the closest existing items (`ink-bleed-reveal`, `svg-mask-reveal`, `directional-wipe`) are an ink dissolve, a generic mask, or a straight-line wipe, none of which read as torn paper.

## Look

The tear edge is a per-frame `clip-path: polygon()` built from a fixed-seed jitter table (16 segments, a few amplified into isolated fiber "spikes" so the edge reads as individual torn fibers rather than smooth noise), plus a second offset "rim" layer showing the paper cross-section color. `filter: drop-shadow(...)` on the clipped layer traces the jagged silhouette automatically for the physical-lift look. Direction, paper tone, and roughness are all authored variables.

## Structure

Copies the catalog item layout from `registry/components/ink-bleed-reveal/` — slot-mount pattern at `registry/components/ink-bleed-reveal/ink-bleed-reveal.html:233-247` (inert `<template data-slot>` in the host document, cloned via `hostDoc.querySelector` + `importNode`), `registry-item.json` shape, and docs page structure from `docs/catalog/components/grade-split-reveal.mdx`.

## Determinism

Every frame is a pure function of progress: the tear geometry table is computed once from a fixed LCG seed during synchronous timeline construction; the clip-path polygon is repainted per-frame as a closed-form function of that table and progress, never mutated incrementally. No `Math.random`, wall clock, or `requestAnimationFrame`.

## Note

title: perf(studio): find timeline transition seams once per track, not once per row
body:
## What changes for a person

- Scrolling and editing a large timeline does less work on every redraw. Before, each redraw re-sorted every clip
  in the project once per visible row to find transitions.
- A transition between two clips now always shows its badge. Before, the badge disappeared whenever a clip on
  another track started between the transition's two clips, which is common: a voiceover or title that starts a
  moment into the first clip was enough.

## How

- Each row's `TimelineTransitionOverlays` derived transition seams itself:
  `deriveTimelineTransitionSeams(transitionElements).filter(seam => seam.incoming.track === track)`, a sort of every
  clip in the project per row, per render.
- `TimelineLanes` now derives them once, in a `useMemo` over the clip set, through
  `deriveTimelineTransitionSeamsByTrack`, and hands each row's overlay its own `seams`.
- `deriveTimelineTransitionSeams` pairs neighbours in start order. Given every track's clips at once, a clip on
  another track between the two halves of a transition broke the pair. The by-track version groups clips by track
  first and pairs within each track, which fixes the missing badge.

## Before

![Before: Clip Warp and Clip Demo overlap with a transition, a Title on the next track starts between them, and no transition badge is drawn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c3496871-4737-4cb7-9112-70cdf49ced73)

## After

![After: the same project, the transition badge sits on the overlap](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86e25a33-36a9-4874-91df-09b7ccc34554)

Same fixture project, Studio dev server, default zoom, pictures loaded before each capture. The two video clips
share a transition label and overlap by 0.8 s; the Title on the next track starts at 0.5 s.

## What I measured

- Transition badges drawn: 0 before, 1 after on that project. On a control copy where nothing starts between the
  two clips, both builds draw 1, so the fixture's transition is recognised by both and the only difference is the
  interleaving clip.
- CI's timeline viewport gate on this head (50,000 clips, row virtualization on): 5 of 5 runs passing,
  interaction p95 33.1 ms, and a longest task of 0 ms in every run. Recent `main` runs of the same gate had longest
  tasks of 79 to 238 ms.
- A CPU profile of the gate's measured scroll runs: on `main` the transition-seam sort is the largest self-time
  entry, about 44 s across the runs; with this change it does not appear in the top 30.
- New tests fail on the old code: a `TimelineLanes` render of three rows derives seams once (`main` derives them
  three times), and the by-track derivation finds a transition with another track's clip starting inside it.
- `TimelineLanes.test.tsx`, `timelineTransitionSeams.test.ts` and `TimelineClipJoins.test.ts` 22/22; pre-commit lint, format, fallow, filesize
  and typecheck green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- `TimelineLanes.tsx` is now exactly at the 600-line limit for Studio files; the next addition there needs a split.

- Transitions during a clip drag or resize; seams follow the same preview elements as before.
- Hosts other than Studio's own dev server.

title: fix(studio): split the empty-read reason and stop blaming the composition
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #4269, driven by what the telemetry it shipped actually measured on 0.8.61/0.8.62. Two of the remaining classes could not name their own cause.

**`absent_or_empty` is one label over two different failures.** The route answers `content: ""` both from the `optional=1` shim (nothing resolved at that path) and for a real 0-byte file — the code comment said as much and called them indistinguishable. They need different fixes, so the class could not move.

That matters more than the label suggests: the class is large and, until now, undiagnosable — on 0.8.62 it covered 85 tabs across a rate that sat near 5% of Studio users. Every measured case with a loaded tree carries `path_in_tree: true`: a file the tree lists and this read cannot get.

**A 200 carrying HTML was blamed on the composition.** `res.json()` at the end of the read was unguarded, so an SPA fallback or a proxy answering in the route's place rejected out of the function and the effect's outer catch filed it as `stage: "open"` — which asserts the *composition* failed to parse. Seen in production on 0.8.62: `Unexpected token '<' ... is not valid JSON`, where the body was an HTML document. That is the third label to make the same wrong claim, after the fetch-rejection split in #4240 and #4269.

## What changed

- Route marks its shim `missing: true`, and the read path `missing: false` — the field's *presence* is what tells the client this server draws the distinction at all. Without it on both, a new server's empty file looks exactly like either case from an old one and the split buys nothing.
- Client splits into `absent` and `empty_file`. A server without the field still reports `absent_or_empty`, so the existing series stays honest instead of silently folding into one of the new ones.
- Non-JSON 200 → `reason: "invalid_json"` with the response's `content_type`, as a read failure.
- `path_in_tree` rides all three empty-read reasons now, not just the combined one.

Scope note: `useProjectFileWriter.readOptionalProjectFile` has the same unguarded `res.json()`. Different call site, different error handling, no telemetry mislabel — left alone deliberately.

## Before

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af45221c-e6eb-4c56-a487-f4edc468549d)

## After

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44854684-b596-49f1-8926-c1d0d1a26001)

Payloads generated by driving `readProjectFileOptional` through each response shape with `trackStudioEvent` mocked. Studio disables telemetry under Vite dev, so a live capture isn't available locally, and this PR changes no rendering — a UI screenshot would be identical on both sides.

## Test plan

- 4 new client tests: `absent` (`missing: true`), `empty_file` (`missing: false`), combined-label fallback (no field, older server), and a non-JSON 200 asserting `invalid_json` **and** that nothing lands in `stage: "open"`.
- 1 new server test pinning `missing` on both answers — the shim and a real 0-byte file.
- 1172 tests green across studio hooks + studio-server routes. oxlint, oxfmt, `tsc --noEmit` clean on both packages.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


---

**Correction (post-merge).** The original version of this description claimed "75 tabs hit this class and not one of them ever landed an SDK edit afterwards — it is terminal for the tab." That inference was wrong. SDK-success is rare per tab overall (31 of 8928 tabs on 0.8.62, 0.35%), so the expected overlap with an 85-tab subset under independence is 0.3 — observing zero is unremarkable, not evidence of anything. Whether the condition is terminal for a tab is currently **unmeasurable**: there is no successful-session event to use as the recovery proxy. The split was still worth shipping, and the shipped data settled the actual question — see below.

**What the split found (0.8.64):** `absent` 36 events / 13 users, `empty_file` **zero**. The entire class is the route shim — nothing resolves at that path — not a real 0-byte placeholder file. A local probe of the read route across 14 path shapes (subdirs, spaces, %, +, #, &, unicode, emoji, parens, quotes, deep nesting) resolved all of them, so percent-encoding is ruled out as the cause. Remaining hypothesis: the file tree is stale relative to disk — the path was listed before something (commonly an agent) removed or replaced it.

title: chore: release v0.8.64
body:
# HyperFrames v0.8.64

Released on 2026-09-23.

HyperFrames adds `data-vfx-chain`, a per-pixel effect element that paints GPU shader chains such as fractal noise, wave warp and displacement map. Every frame is computed from the seek time alone, so renders and previews match exactly. Chains that read their own content rely on Chrome's HTML-in-Canvas capture, and the runtime reports when that is unavailable instead of painting a blank.

## Features

- **Runtime:** Add `data-vfx-chain`, a seek-deterministic per-pixel effect element ([b32b9a7da](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b32b9a7dabf71e97049d1fa91a818817191414fc), [#4306](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4306)).

https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/compare/v0.8.63...v0.8.64

Version bump only across package.json/plugin manifests and the changelog artifacts; no packages/studio or packages/player source changed.

title: fix(player): drop the empty transition label from the Loading assets card
body:
## What changes for the user

The player's "Loading assets" card no longer shows a stray "transition" label under its progress bar.

## Why it happened

The Loading assets card reuses the shader-transition loading panel. `showAssetsLoading()` resets that panel first, and `reset()` hid the transition-frame row but only emptied the transition row, so its "transition" label stayed on the card with no value next to it. The same bare label could show during a shader load that had not reported a count yet.

## The fix

`createShaderLoader()` now returns the transition row too, and `ShaderLoaderState` sets both progress rows through one helper: a row is visible only while it has a value. `reset()` and `update()` both go through it, so the rule holds for the assets card and for shader loads.

## Tests

- New `packages/player/src/shader-loader-state.test.ts` (3 tests): no progress rows on the Loading assets card; the rows a shader load left behind are hidden when assets start loading; the transition row appears only once it has a count. All 3 fail on the previous code and pass now.
- Player suite: 14 files, 397 tests passed. Typecheck, lint and format clean.

## Review notes

An independent review found no blockers or majors. Two minor notes, left as they are:
- The rows start visible when the panel is first built; every path that shows the panel resets or updates it first, so this is not reachable today.
- The card keeps the rows' space (they are hidden with `visibility`, as the frame row already was), so there is a small blank area under the bar instead of the label.

title: feat(runtime): data-vfx-chain backdrop capture and two-source kernels (luma-matte, noise)
body:
Follow-up to #4306. Adds the second capture source and the first two-source kernels to the `data-vfx-chain` runtime.

## What
- **Backdrop capture.** A kernel that needs what is *behind* its host (an adjustment-layer effect) reads a `<canvas layoutsubtree class="hf-vfx-src" data-vfx-for="<host id>">` placed as the host's preceding sibling. Resolution order: `data-vfx-for` sibling → the host's own child wrapper → loud error. `self` and `backdrop` share one runtime path; which element fills the texture is the exporter's placement, and `VfxEntry.capture` reports what was resolved.
- **Ref second sources** (`u_src2`): a kernel param may name an element id whose subtree carries its own `canvas.hf-vfx-src > .hf-vfx-in`.
- **`luma-matte`** (matte ref + mode 1–4) and **`noise`** (amount, `useColorNoise`, `clipping`; exact-hash port, `precision highp int`).
- Hidden backdrop host passes the captured bitmap through instead of skipping (skipping would delete every layer below the adjustment). A hidden ref/matte captures empty instead of waiting out the 2 s paint ceiling per frame.

## Why the deviations from the plan
Measured HTML-in-Canvas rules (children of a `layoutsubtree` canvas are not painted by the page; only immediate children are capturable; `inset:0` captures 0×0): a runtime-injected second staging canvas would hide the `htmlInCanvas` render-mode hint, so the exporter's wrapper is the staging canvas; a non-immediate `.hf-vfx-in` child is refused at registration; a 0×0 `.hf-vfx-in` is reported once.

## Verify
- `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck:runtime` clean
- `bun run --cwd packages/core test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` 59 files / 1266 tests
- vfx suites directly: 7 files / 103 tests
- Zero-host path unchanged: no new timers, observers, canvases or GL contexts when no `data-vfx-chain` host exists.

## Browser verification (`1a48b48ca`)
9 new puppeteer checks in `packages/producer/src/services/vfxDeterminism.test.ts` (20/20), Chrome 152 headless with `--enable-features=CanvasDrawElement`, capability probe guards against a silent pass: backdrop identity reproduces two stacked blocks exactly (PSNR ≥ 40 dB vs a plain-DOM control); a host outside its clip window passes the captured backdrop through; `luma-matte` modes 1–4 track the matte's alpha/luma within ±4/255 at 4 sample points each; `noise` at amount 0 equals its input, same seek time is byte-identical, different time differs.

## External displacement maps and visible ref sources (`657980307`)
- `displacement-map` gains `map` as an optional `ref` param (`HfVfxRefParam.optional`, a v1.1 amendment). Empty `map` is the self-referential form every corpus instance uses; a `map` naming its own host resolves to self. Frag: `u_src2` + `u_hasSrc2`, CPU reference unchanged.
- A ref whose layer also paints in AE is marked `data-vfx-ref-visible` on its wrapper: the runtime uploads the texture AND keeps the bitmap, drawn at the ref's own box. The three capture shapes are one `{upload, keepBitmap}` mode now.
- Tests: jsdom vfx 38 → 44, browser `vfxDeterminism` 20 → 24 (an external map translates a block by exactly `maxH` as one run; a self map splits it in two — verified with a negative control). `test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` 59 files / 1272.
- Exporter contract: a visible wrapper's `<canvas>` must carry CSS `width`/`height` equal to the layer box (the runtime rewrites `canvas.width/height` in device pixels; at DPR 2 an attribute-only canvas doubles its layout footprint).

## Known limits
`vfx_capture` telemetry under-reports `backdrop` until the producer's markup scan also looks for `data-vfx-for`. A matte whose box differs from the host's is scaled into the host box (every corpus matte is a full-frame sibling).

title: feat(registry): add snow ambient overlay catalog item
body:
## Summary
- Adds `snow`, a seek-safe falling-snow overlay block to the HyperFrames catalog (gaps row C2, second of six ambient-overlay items): sparse or dense flakes fall calm or gust-speed, radial-masked so the frame center stays clear by default for a subject or caption underneath. Same validated design pattern as `starfield` (#4313).

## Design decisions (UX calls made without asking, per gaps lane convention)
- **Type: `hyperframes:block`**, matching `starfield` and the `media-treatment-overlay` family — mounts on its own timeline track above footage.
- **Determinism**: one non-repeating GSAP tween drives `state.phase` 0→1 over the mounted host clip's duration. Fall position is `frac(integer_cycles * phase + const)`, sway is `sin(2*PI * integer_cycles * phase + const)` — both always exactly periodic over the mount, so phase=0 and phase=1 match exactly.
- **Fall-speed depth layering**: one per-flake `depth` draw sets size and opacity continuously and buckets the flake into one of three deliberately distinct fall-speed layers (an additive integer offset onto a shared base cycle count, not a multiplier). A naive continuous multiplier rounds to the same integer cycle count at short mount durations and collapses the whole field to one speed — caught by an altitude review, see below.
- **Scatter/placement**: golden-ratio Weyl sequence for lane position and vertical phase offset (reusing starfield's `RT2` constant), the registry's sin-fold `rnd(n)` hash for decorrelated scalars — no `Math.random()`.
- **Off-screen entry/exit**: flakes travel from just above the top edge to just below the bottom before wrapping (`WRAP_MARGIN`, sized to the largest flake's own radius plus safety margin, not an arbitrary value) so the loop seam never pops one into view mid-frame; marked with `data-layout-allow-overflow` per the layout-audit contract.
- **No visual reference photo/video shipped in the demo**: `demo.html`'s backdrop is a CSS gradient, not a licensed stock asset.

## Evidence
Same PostHog `cli_catalog_search_miss` gap as starfield: agents search for winter/snow overlays and get no match.

**Honest limitation**: same as starfield — I cannot verify live search ranking against this branch pre-merge (`hyperframes catalog --query` reads the published main-branch manifest). `check-artifact-coverage.ts` confirms the local search-vector artifact correctly embeds and covers this item.

## What I verified
- `hyperframes lint` / `check` on a scratch harness: 0 errors, 0 warnings (Layout 0/9, Motion 0, Contrast 0/0).
- Determinism: two-run `snapshot --at ... --no-end` sha256 comparison, byte-identical.
- **New this item**: `render --format png-sequence -w 1` vs `-w 4` (parallel render workers), all 60 frames `cmp`'d byte-for-byte — 0 diffs. Targets a frame-order-dependent rasterization bug class from a fractional-pixel `transform` under `will-change` (documented by a teammate on an unrelated block); closed here by rounding per-frame pixel values. Re-ran the same proof retroactively against already-shipped `starfield` (PR #4313): also 0/60 diffs.
- **Caught by an independent altitude review, fixed before this PR opened**: the fall-speed depth model collapsed to a single bucket at mount durations <=4s (measured: all 50 flakes at one speed), silently breaking the claimed near/far parallax — the four sibling `media-treatment-overlay` blocks all ship `duration: 4`. Fixed by replacing the continuous multiplier with three additive integer-offset depth layers, which stay numerically distinct on any mount length. Also fixed: vertical placement used a weaker hash instead of the Weyl sequence (measured largest gap 7.9% of travel vs. 2.9% after the fix); an undocumented 37x-oversized wrap margin (named and shrunk to ~6x the actual requirement); the `speed` variable silently not affecting sway rate.
- **Independent adversarial correctness review** (separate agent, hand-traced the loop invariant, the new 3-layer bucketing for off-by-ones, and whether removing the multiplier broke the size/opacity/speed correlation): no bugs found. Full report: `~/.claude/state/pr-reports/hyperframes-snow-acb1d33cc3-review.md` (local, team path, not attached).
- `scripts/catalog/check-artifact-coverage.ts`, `check:catalog-drift`, `check-docs-catalog.mjs`: all pass; only pre-existing unrelated drift observed and excluded (an unindexed `week-in-merges` on main, 3 stale component doc pages, 2 pre-existing lint errors on unrelated items, 4 pre-existing `caption-*` payload 404s from a missing test fixture — none touch `snow`).
- `verify:catalog-payloads` (headless Chrome, full 387-item catalog): `snow` passes.
- Visual: rendered snapshots at 6 evenly-spaced timestamps, reviewed by eye (attached).

## What I did NOT exercise
- No production render through the full `hyperframes render` MP4 pipeline (used `snapshot`/`check`/`png-sequence`, which cover the same runtime path CI's `verify-catalog-payloads` uses).
- No real footage composited underneath in the demo (CSS gradient backdrop, see design decisions).
- No live catalog search ranking against this branch (see "Honest limitation" above).

Simplify pass (4 parallel reviewers: reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) and an independent adversarial correctness review both ran on this diff, findings applied, before opening.

title: perf(studio): stop the manual-edit loop from running while the preview is paused
body:
## What this fixes

Studio's manual-edit reapply loop ran 60 times a second while the preview sat paused. It started when the preview opened and ran until the first play/pause, so a project that is just open and idle burned CPU the whole time.

The cause, in `packages/studio/src/components/editor/manualEdits.ts`:
- `isStudioManualEditPlaybackActive` asks every `window.__timelines` entry whether it is playing.
- A scene timeline nested under the paused master reports `paused() === false`, `isActive() === false` and `time < duration`.
- So `isTimelinePlaying` fell through to its "time left" fallback and answered "playing".
- The rAF loop in `startStudioManualEditPlaybackReapply` never met its stop condition.

Checked live on a 12-scene project: `__timelines.scene0.parent === __timelines.main`, the master is paused, and the scene children are not.

## What changed

A timeline with a paused ancestor is not playing.
- `hasPausedAncestor` walks `.parent` (bounded to 32 levels). It stops only on an ancestor whose `paused()` returns true, and ignores unknown shapes.
- Everything else is unchanged:
  - the player transport check
  - a master Studio drives directly through `wrapTimeline`
  - the "just played, not yet initted" fallback for top-level timelines

An earlier version trusted `__player.isPlaying()` alone. Review showed that is wrong when Studio's playback adapter drives a raw timeline and the player reads idle. A regression test now covers that case.

## Measured

Same run, interleaved, on one Linux dev box: main at the merge base (06340f656) vs this branch. A 12-scene, 60 s fixture project, opened in Studio and left idle. 3 rounds each; each measures 10 s of idle, 15 s after open. Headless Chrome.

| Idle, preview paused | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| rAF callbacks per second in the preview frame | 60.3 | **0** |
| Main-thread script time (ms per second) | 13.3 | **6.3** |
| Browser CPU (all Chrome processes) | 9.3% | **6.7%** |

Loop liveness in the same build: 0 frames at idle, live while playing, 0 again after pause (main: 60 at idle).

## Before

Main, idle and then playing. Nothing visible changes in this PR; the captures show the same UI, and that playback still works.

![main, idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e8614c92-df41-4ef1-8ea7-f977df84c5cf)
![main, playing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49bf8d48-3ffd-4886-bfa7-52bae86d3da6)

## After

This branch, the same two states.

![this PR, idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56263822-7e51-4057-9edf-7d7169bd1b34)
![this PR, playing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b2dedf2-a11e-4d24-86a5-85391caa108a)

## Tests

- `manualEdits.test.ts` 27/27, run alone, exit 0. `tsc` is 0 in studio, studio-server and cli; oxfmt and oxlint are clean.

title: ci: generate catalog artifacts through a standing publish PR
body:
Catalog item PRs currently rewrite shared indexes, search vectors, and documentation, so independent items conflict on generated files. This change lets additions and edits contain only item sources. CI generates and validates the complete catalog from those sources.

Generated files remain committed on main because the CLI and documentation consume them directly from the repository. A main-push workflow maintains one `bot/catalog-publish` branch and one publication PR, using GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub-signed API commits. It preserves branch protection and requires normal review and approval of token-triggered CI runs.

Deletions and renames remove the old `registry/registry.json` entry in the same PR as the complete item directory. The guard requires exactly those removals, preserves every other entry and index metadata, and rejects additions. New names wait for publication. This keeps the live CLI index from pointing at deleted source files.

The shared generation command separates example scaffolding from indexing and owns the explicit output paths. Publication stages signed batches before updating the standing branch, refuses a stale main snapshot, and clears obsolete output when sources are reverted.

Validation:

- Full lint, formatting, workspace and script typechecks; focused generator, payload selection, drift, and publication tests. Deletion-policy tests cover delete, rename, add-plus-delete, dangling entries, added entries, live directories, metadata changes, partial directory deletion, and nested asset metadata. Deliberate mutations make the regressions fail. Publication reads each artifact through one non-symlink file descriptor, with a symlink-rejection regression.
- Independent regeneration matched all 1,094 generated files byte-for-byte. A second generation changed none. Applying the publisher's nine planned changes to the committed tree reconstructed that same snapshot; a second plan was identical.
- Source-only sibling proof PRs: #4338 and #4339. Each adds only three files inside its own item directory. Both merge directions produce the same tree, and an actual local merge had no conflicts. The combined catalog generated successfully and both payloads loaded in headless Chrome without request or page errors. These fixtures must not merge.
- Independent review found no remaining blockers. The complexity audit reports no new findings after splitting generation and publication responsibilities.

Live signed publication with the workflow token can only run after this workflow lands. Additions become discoverable when the standing publication PR is reviewed and merged; deletions are unpublished immediately with their sources.
