title: fix(lint): validate composition variables on every declaring element
body:
## What

Broken `data-composition-variables` JSON was only caught on `<html>`. If you put the same broken attribute on a composition root div or a template root, lint said nothing, even though the runtime reads it from there too and silently drops the defaults.

## Why

A typo in the variables declaration on a root element meant defaults just disappeared, with no hint from lint. The binding check already looks at every declaring element, so this rule was the odd one out.

## How

The rule now runs its existing checks (JSON, array shape, entry shape, and the unloadable media default check that lives in the same body) on every element that carries the attribute, not just `<html>`. Most of the diff is moving that body into a small helper so it can run per element.

Each finding points at its own element, so the line number is right. When the declaration isn't on `<html>`, the message names the element, so two broken declarations show up as two findings instead of being merged. Messages for `<html>` are exactly the same as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - New cases in `composition.test.ts`: broken JSON on a full-document root and on a template root (checking element and line), bad entry shapes on a template root, `<html>` and root checked independently, and a valid template declaration that stays clean. 4 of them fail on `main`.
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Ran the repro script from the issue: `html`, `root` and `template` now all report `invalid_composition_variables_declaration`.

title: fix(studio): ship component styles as their own stylesheet for embedders
body:
## What changes

A page that embeds Studio's components can now style them. Studio's component rules (timeline clips and their labels, loaders, range inputs, toasts, preset shelf, CodeMirror overrides and the rest) lived only in Studio's app stylesheet. An embedder that imports `@hyperframes/studio/theme.css` got none of them: timeline clips drew as bare boxes, most disappeared against the row, and clip labels rendered black on a dark background.

Those rules now live in `packages/studio/src/styles/components.css`, exported as `@hyperframes/studio/components.css`. `studio.css` keeps the app shell (Tailwind, palette reset, theme, `@source`, the button cursor, color scheme, `body`, `#root`) and imports `components.css`, so each rule has one home and Studio itself is unchanged.

An embedder on Tailwind v4 imports:

```css
@import "tailwindcss";
@import "@hyperframes/studio/theme.css";
@import "@hyperframes/studio/components.css";
```

The class names and `@keyframes` names in `components.css` are global, as they are in Studio: `timeline-*` and `hf-*` prefixed, so a clash with the host page is unlikely but not impossible.

## How

- The rules moved byte for byte. Nothing in them changed.
- The export is added to `exports`, `publishConfig.exports` and `package-subpaths.json`, shaped like the existing `./theme.css` (served from `src`).
- `hex-baseline.json`: the 48 colour literals are now counted under the new file. The total is unchanged.
- `scripts/contrast-pairs.json`: the 33 source pointers into `studio.css` now point at the same lines in `components.css`. Each one was checked by line content, not by arithmetic.
- Two existing tests that read `studio.css` as text for rules that moved (`VolumeControl.styles.test.ts`, `timelineMotionStyles.test.ts`) now read `components.css`.
- New `componentStyles.test.ts`:
  - `studio.css` may define no class rules at any depth, including inside `@layer` and `@media`, so a component rule can't drift back where an embedder never sees it.
  - Tailwind, `theme.css` and `components.css` alone must yield the timeline clip label rule.
  - Each was checked by breaking the code: a toast rule added to `studio.css` at top level and inside `@layer base`, the label rule added back, and the label rule removed from `components.css` each fail the matching test.

## Evidence

- Every Studio test file that references a stylesheet (17 files) passes one by one, as do the three typechecks and the package-subpath check.
- Studio's compiled `dist/styles.css`, built before and after: the same 2 280 rules (identical as a multiset; only the order changed, because the imported rules now come before `body` and `#root`, which target different elements).
- Studio screenshots on a 24-scene project, before and after, with scene thumbnails hidden (they finish loading at different times on every run): one before/after pair is byte-identical. The other runs differ by at most 30 pixels, the same as two runs of one build.
- Embedder: a page with only Tailwind, `theme.css` and Studio's real timeline markup. The clip label's computed colour is `rgb(0, 0, 0)` before and `rgb(255, 255, 255)` after.

## Before

Timeline markup embedded with `theme.css` only (today's embedder):

![Embedder timeline before: clips missing or bare, no label](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7109672-b892-49f5-87ee-c06931521662)


## After

The same markup with `theme.css` and `components.css`:

![Embedder timeline after: clips styled, label visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/03a7eb52-bb57-4e96-b7b6-be852194fe63)


## Studio is unchanged

The same 24-scene project in Studio, scene thumbnails hidden. main's screenshot and this branch's screenshot are byte-identical (md5 `412b74d27e7c2f8716ae46fa1b9e2245` for both), so it appears once:

![Studio, identical on main and this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e7bb54e9-9203-4013-acef-d55cdcb20d95)

## Review

An independent adversarial review over three passes:
- **Pass 1** found one blocker: two existing tests read `studio.css` as text for rules that moved. It also flagged a guard test that missed classes applied outside `className` literals, and a stale comment. All three are fixed here.
- **Pass 2** found that the guard missed class rules nested inside `@layer` or `@media`. That is fixed too.
- **At this head:** no blockers, no majors, no minors.

The review also confirmed:
- the byte-for-byte move (rebuilding the old file from the two new ones gives an empty diff);
- equal compiled output apart from order;
- that the order change cannot change any cascade winner;
- that nothing page-global moved into `components.css`;
- the published export;
- the colour-literal and contrast-pointer updates.

Media lint attribute detection no longer treats words inside quoted HTML attribute values as real attributes.

title: fix(core): a section whose root sets pointer-events:none stays pickable
body:
## What

A click inside a sub-composition whose root sets `pointer-events: none` now picks the element under the pointer instead of the whole section.

## Why

The picker hit-tests with `document.elementsFromPoint`, which skips `pointer-events: none` elements, and `isEffectivelyHidden` also treats `pointer-events: none` as hidden. Authors often put `pointer-events: none` on a composition root because the section is not meant to be interactive during playback. On mount, the section's root rule is rescoped onto its `[data-hf-inner-root]`, and the property inherits into every element of the section. The picker then sees nothing inside it and returns the host element, so a click on a card inside the section selects the section.

## Related work

None; found while picking inside a launch film's glass intro section.

## How

While the picker hit-tests (`getPickInfosFromPoint`, which also serves `pickAtPoint` and `pickManyAtPoint`, and the pick-mode hover):

- Section inner roots (`[data-hf-inner-root]`, where a mounted section's own root rules land) and the page's outermost composition root (`[data-composition-id]:not([data-composition-id] *)`, a composition opened on its own) take `pointer-events: auto !important` from a constructed stylesheet adopted into `document.adoptedStyleSheets`, removed again in a `finally`. Content that only inherits `none` from its section root becomes pickable.
- A host keeps its own `none`: that is the parent composition making an overlay click-through (`overlay-montage-prod`'s full-screen `intro_outro` host), and `isEffectivelyHidden`'s ancestor walk still hides everything under it.
- Roots that were `none` before the override are never pick targets themselves, so a click on a section's empty background falls through to the host, as on `main`.
- An inner root's selector is `[data-composition-id="<host>"] > [data-hf-inner-root]`; the mount strips its id, so its bare tag matched the composition's first div.
- A page with no `none` root skips the override entirely.

An adopted sheet is not a DOM node: no MutationObserver hears it (the runtime's timing observer would wake a paused transport), and `documentElement.outerHTML` never contains it (Studio's style save for elements without an id writes that into the source). The rule sits in a cascade layer, so its `!important` outranks every normal author rule and every unlayered author `!important`. Where `adoptedStyleSheets` is missing (older engines, jsdom), it falls back to a `<style>` element around the hit test, like `packages/player/src/styles.ts`.

Per-hover cost, Chromium 152, median of 300 hovers:

| Page | Bare `elementsFromPoint` | With this change |
|---|---|---|
| 2k elements, no `none` inner root | 0.1 ms | 0.1 ms |
| 10k elements, no `none` inner root | 0.5 ms | 0.5 ms |
| 2k elements, every section `none` | 0.1 ms | 2.9 ms |
| 10k elements, every section `none` | 0.5 ms | 14.6 ms |

The cost when a section does need the override is two document restyles per hover (adopt, then un-adopt).

Not covered, same as `main`: a section mounted without an inner root that sets `none` on itself (indistinguishable from a click-through host); an author `!important` inside the author's own cascade layer, or inline. Studio's own canvas hit test (`studioPreviewHelpers.ts` `hasAuthorPointerEventsNone`) likely has the same inherited-`none` gap and follows separately with the same host rule.

## Test plan

`picker.test.ts`, 21/21:
- "picks inside a mounted section whose root sets pointer-events:none": fails on `main` (`expected '[data-composition-id="intro"]' to be '#code'`).
- "picks inside a composition opened on its own whose root sets pointer-events:none": fails on `main` and on the previous head of this PR (`expected [] to deeply equal ['#code', '#card']`).
- "keeps a click-through overlay host passing through to what is under it": the `overlay-montage-prod` shape; `main` and this change return `["#aroll", "#root"]`; the previous head of this PR failed it.
- "a section background click picks the host, and an inner root never gets a bare tag selector": fails on `main` (bare `div`) and on the previous head.
- "adopts the override only for the hit test, leaving the DOM and a saved outerHTML untouched", and nothing adopted when no inner root is `none`.

Mutations that turn them red: not skipping pass-through roots, not using the inner-root selector, always adopting, and each earlier head of this branch. oxlint and oxfmt are clean. Not run: core's full suite, and a real-browser pick through the runtime (the cascade and cost figures above come from standalone Chromium pages).

title: perf(studio): open a large film ready to play in about 4 s instead of 32 s
body:
## Summary

Opening a large film in Studio is ready to play in about 4.0 s instead of 32.8 s on a cold open, and
the server starts listening in 3.1 s instead of 13.2 s. Frames, lint findings, thumbnails and
playback are unchanged. Most of the time on main went to work that competed with the first frame: lint on the open
path and on the boot, building the preview document late and more than once, thumbnail renders of the whole film,
and editor work that the first frame doesn't need. This PR moves that work out of the way, one commit per cause.

It also fixes three ways a play could be lost, each undone by the preview's load step (which pauses and rewinds):
Space pressed before the preview could play, the same after switching composition, and a Play pressed the moment the
button enabled on a cold open. The last one is main's too: Play could enable before the preview document's load event,
from the runtime's timeline message or from the blank page's load step. On the film, clicking Play the instant it
enables, 3 of 8 cold opens lost the play before `8b4e1a6d5` and 0 of 20 after.

  32.83 s, 33.03 s); every other row is from the first run. Waiting for the load step costs about 0.1 s against
  `3b78344d6`, inside the round spread.
- Single slow rounds (for example `689fda498` round 2, `ff17f436c` round 1) line up with load spikes; the median
  drops them.
- First picture is missing from one round of `01966ab78`, `cf9a6563d`, `eb8f6860b` and `06754b972` (the capture
  ended before a moving frame); their median is the lower of the other two, so it can sit under Play enabled.

### Lint off the boot

Four commits take lint off the path to the first frame. Lint still runs and reports the same findings (see
the follow-up comment for time to findings); it just no longer blocks the server or competes with the preview.

| Commit | What moves | Effect in the table |
|---|---|---|
| `5b91a4ca2` | No lint to build a preview bundle; the lint route runs in a child process | ready 22.28 to 6.16 s, Play enabled 31.66 to 7.67 s |
| `db7205662` | `hyperframes preview` listens before the startup lint finishes | listening 11.8 to 3.2 s; ready rises 4.02 to 5.36 s because the startup lint now runs during the open, which `3c03fd23b` and `cf9a6563d` win back |
| `cf9a6563d` | Studio's background lint waits for the boot; lint runs at the lowest CPU priority | ready 3.78 to 3.73 s |
| `3b78344d6` | Refactor of the background and manual lint paths, no behaviour change | ready 3.25 to 3.38 s, inside the round spread |

## No regressions, main vs this PR

Same method and box, main (86fa10ced) against this PR's head, on the film above, a 60 s fixture with eight large PNGs
and an mp4 (plus a copy with a 20 s audio track), and a 24-scene fixture whose scenes are separate composition files.

| Check | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| CLI render of the fixture, 60 frames at 1 fps, PNG | 60 frames | 60 frames, all 60 byte-identical to main (52 distinct, none blank) |
| Studio preview at 0 s, the middle and the end, all three projects | frame hashes | identical hashes on all 9 frames |
| Play 2 s, pause 1 s | plays, holds | plays, holds |
| Seek: click the ruler at the 30 s tick | lands on 30.000 | lands on 30.000 |
| Scrub: drag the ruler from the 10 s to the 35 s tick | rises steadily, ends at 35.000 | the same 12 samples, ends at 35.000 |
| Audio clip against the player clock while playing | 15 ms max drift | 14 ms max drift |
| Open a sub-composition from its card and play | plays | plays |
| Composition thumbnails, 24-scene fixture | 25 of 25 once each card is on screen (cards load lazily) | 25 of 25; each off-screen card within 0.8 s of scrolling to it (main 1.4 s) |
| Composition thumbnail, the film | none within 105 s | shown |

Lint time to findings and warm (second) open, main vs this PR, follow in a comment.

### Idle with the film open

A separate benchmark measures the 20 s after the first frame settles (5 s in): CPU of the browser, CPU of the preview server with all its child processes, and the memory of each. Its first run showed this PR heavier at idle than main: server tree 1.7 % to 8.7 %, browser 9.1 % to 13.4 %, memory 744 to 767 MB. Since then:

- **Server CPU, fixed.** The thumbnail page used to stay loaded for 10 s after each thumbnail, still running the composition. It now closes 1 s after its last frame (`5882e61b1`). The preview also counts as booted at its first frame, so the thumbnail burst starts and ends earlier (`eb94b3beb`). Scene renders drop from 20 to 12 on a 12-scene film, because a composition's card and clip share one frame (`a3e3d487f`).
- **Decoded-image memory, fixed in main by #4460.** This PR's preview arrives early enough that the browser painted every scene before the runtime hid the ones out of time, and kept all eight 1600x900 background images decoded. With #4460, which this branch now includes, only the first scene's images are decoded. The browser's decoded-image cache is then below main's (84-85 MB against 92 MB, compositor image cache 115 against 122 MB).

Last clean three-round run (before #4460), main against this PR:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| First frame | 4.80 s | 1.75 s |
| Browser CPU | 8.8 % | 9.5 % |
| Server tree CPU | 1.9 % | 1.3 % |
| Browser memory | 729 MB | 768 MB |
| Server tree memory | 327 MB | 333 MB |

Later runs overlapped other jobs on the shared box and are not reported.

**Known, measured follow-up (not in this PR):** the page's own general-purpose memory in the Studio renderer is still 15-22 MB above main at the 30 s mark with thumbnails hidden, and a few MB more with them shown. Excluded so far, each by an on/off test:
- the preview prefetch;
- the frame-0 poster;
- the server prebuild;
- the preview document itself (252 KB).

Per build, it swings by about 15 MB between samples, which looks like work in flight rather than a steady leak. Browser CPU at idle is also a little above main. Both are tracked as a follow-up with the numbers above.

## What changed

Server and CLI:

- `5b91a4ca2` A preview bundle no longer lints to print a StaticGuard warning, and Studio's lint route runs in the
  CLI's child-process worker instead of on the server event loop.
- `db7205662` `hyperframes preview` starts Studio before its startup lint finishes; the lint prints its summary
  when done, and `--json` skips it.
- `cf9a6563d` Studio's background lint waits until the preview has booted, and lint processes run at the lowest
  CPU priority.
- `33fdc1fe1` Identical GSAP source is parsed once.
- `54f960f11` The preview document is built once per content version and served from memory by ETag.
- `087398efc` The CLI builds the opening film's preview right after it listens; concurrent requests share the build.
- `4b615375b` Thumbnails come from one loaded page per preview document, seeked per frame, after the preview boots.
- `2808dcece` A thumbnail page unused for 10 s closes, so an idle Studio runs no composition.
- `97e787755` Orphaned browsers are found with one process-table read (about 20 ms instead of about 500).
- `e3b3eda49` Compositions get their ids stamped once before the watcher starts, so opening a film of scene files no
  longer reloads the preview once per scene.
- `65d6775ea`, `eb8f6860b` `hyperframes play` serves with validators, so a reload costs a 304; text assets get a
  content-hash tag.

Studio:

- `38b2fa13c` The preview document is requested at page load, not when the player mounts.
- `01966ab78` The cached frame 0 covers the preview while it boots.
- `3c03fd23b`, `e8f3cc9a0`, `689fda498` The GSAP parse, the editing session and the editor overlays wait for the
  preview to boot.
- `d6e375d15` The boot counts as done once the preview can show and play (or fails to load).
- `ff17f436c` Deferred work waits per project, so leaving a project before it boots can't run its work in the next.
- `06754b972` `play()` waits for the timeline to be ready, the gate the Play button already uses, so Space can't
  start a play that the preview's load step undoes.
- `4a37b0737` Switching composition marks the timeline not ready until the new preview loads.
- `3b78344d6` Refactor: the background lint and the manual lint are separate functions, and thumbnail page lookup and
  idle close are their own steps. No behaviour change.
- `8b4e1a6d5` Play enables only after the preview document's load step: `requestTimelineReady` holds a request until
  the load step has marked that document, whichever path asks (the runtime's timeline message, or the blank page's
  load step settling on the preview's first message).
- `1faf65e2e` The poster's state moves into `usePreviewPoster` beside `PreviewPoster` (keeps `NLEPreview.tsx` under
  the 600-line limit after main grew it). No behaviour change.

Server and CLI, after review:

- `0c970f4b5` A thumbnail page whose load fails is closed (a WebGPU composition without an adapter, or the navigation
  timeout on a big film, leaked one page per request).
- `def28344b` `hyperframes play` matches text assets by exact type (`text/*`, `application/json`, `image/svg+xml`) and
  still answers a `Range` request on them with 206.
- `385869828` A thumbnail takes its page version from the server's cached project signature instead of walking and
  hashing the project per thumbnail; an aborted thumbnail request stops before its screenshot.
- `e185ffeea` The render-setup worker, spawned by path, is declared as a fallow entry.

Idle work, after the benchmark:

- `5882e61b1` A kept thumbnail page closes one second after its last frame (it was 10 s).
- `eb94b3beb` The preview counts as booted at its first frame, not once all its media has buffered, so the work that waits for the boot starts seconds earlier.
- `a3e3d487f` A composition's timeline clip asks for the same thumbnail frame as its card (3.00 s, or the midpoint of a composition under 3 s), so one render serves both.

## Tests

- Every behaviour commit adds or changes tests; `useTimelinePlayer.play.test.ts` covers the three lost-play cases and
  `playerStore.test.ts` the load-step wait (each fails without its fix). The thumbnail leak, the cached signature, the
  aborted thumbnail and the text `Range` each have a test that fails without the fix.
- Full suites at `8b4e1a6d5` (the head adds only a no-behaviour refactor and a main merge; CI covers it):
  `parsers`, `core` (3 092 tests), `studio-server` (594), `studio` (5 528), `cli` (3 587 of 3 591, 3 skipped), plus
  `tsc --noEmit` for `studio` and `cli`. The one failing `cli` test, the `portUtils` PID
  check, needs `lsof`, which the test box lacks; it fails the same way on main there and passes on a machine with it.
- `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues`: exit 0.

## Before

main `86fa10ced`, cold open of the film, headless Chrome beside the server, Play clicked the moment it enables. The
button enables 32.9 s in; the film plays from there. The video's own timeline starts at navigation.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fe62e42-228c-45ac-b45b-6ee7dee9cb3f

## After

This PR `1faf65e2e`, same film, same way. The button enables 4.0 s in and the film plays from there.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64a2c55a-2807-4bdc-92b0-2c3a28e31ccf

Main and this PR paint the same frames (film, audio fixture and 24-scene fixture, middle frame, sha256 prefix in
each label):

![Main and this PR, same frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a371947-0b6f-4840-bae7-46cc88ad887b)

Earlier recordings of `3b78344d6`, made through an ssh tunnel, showed playback jumping back to 00:00 a few seconds after
Play on main and on this PR alike; that was the lost-play race `8b4e1a6d5` fixes (the slow link delayed the preview's
load event past the click).

## Review notes

The carried commits were reviewed independently before this rebase; 19 of them are patch-identical to what was
reviewed, and three changed only to fit current main. One independent adversarial pass covered the three new
commits and those three adaptations:

- MAJOR, fixed: the first version of the play gate read a readiness flag that was reset only on a project change,
  so switching composition reopened the lost-play window. `4a37b0737` resets it on the switch, with a test.
- MAJOR, answered: the review expected removing the `fallow-ignore-file unused-file` line from
  `renderSetupWorker.ts` to bring back an unused-file error, because the file is only reached by a path string.
  fallow reports that suppression as stale at this head, and both CI's command (`fallow audit --base origin/main
  --fail-on-issues`) and `--gate all` pass without it.
- The readiness ordering on a composition switch, the refresh path, and the three rebased adaptations checked out
  clean.

Changes requested at `e185ffee`, all taken:

- BLOCKER, fixed in `0c970f4b5`: a thumbnail page whose load throws was never closed. Regression test: three failing
  loads, then `closeAll`, three pages closed (0 before the fix).
- Text assets and `Range`: kept, `def28344b` (with CodeQL's anchoring finding on the same line).
- Uncached signature per thumbnail: `385869828`.
- Aborted thumbnail runs to the screenshot: `385869828`.

One independent pass over `3b78344d6..1faf65e2e`:

- MAJOR, answered: `syncTimelineElements` is shared by the live and the shadow (edit reload) pipelines and asks for
  readiness with the live iframe's document. During an edit reload that starts before the first ready, readiness
  settles on the old document's inputs. This is main's wiring and cannot lose a play: the shadow document's load step
  runs before its commit, promotion commits and swaps the iframe synchronously, and a readiness settle needs at least
  one animation frame. Checking the right document's media is its own small fix, in a follow-up PR.
- MINOR, intended: thumbnails now share the watcher-invalidated signature cache (a 30 to 300 ms staleness bound, the
  same one the preview accepts); the thumbnail route's own fresh check still refuses to cache a frame whose inputs
  changed during generation.
- Clean: the load-step wait (single pending slot, generation guard, every path that loads a preview marks it), the
  leak fix, `play.ts` against main, both main merges, the poster move.

title: docs: state the 45 s cost of a missing data-no-timeline
body:
## What

`data-no-timeline` is in the [HTML schema reference](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/main/docs/reference/html-schema.mdx) and is enforced by the `missing_data_no_timeline` lint rule, but no page states **what omitting it costs**: a composition that never registers a GSAP timeline waits out `player-ready-timeout` — 45 s by default — on every render.

## Why it's worth a docs change rather than nothing

The cost is **fixed**, and the troubleshooting page only documents costs that **scale**.

`docs/guides/troubleshooting.mdx` → "The render is slow" currently lists draft quality, media size, and filter complexity. An author whose renders are all mysteriously ~45 s longer than they should be reads that section, tunes every item in it, and sees no improvement — because none of those levers touch a constant.

The lint rule already says this well, in its message and its `fixHint`. But it only reaches an author who runs `hyperframes lint`; someone debugging render time goes to the troubleshooting guide first.

## Changes

- **`docs/guides/troubleshooting.mdx`** — new entry keyed on the *symptom* ("Every render takes about 45 seconds longer than expected") placed just above "The render is slow", and a one-line pointer from that section for the constant-penalty case.
- **`docs/reference/html-schema.mdx`** — the `data-no-timeline` row gains the consequence and the lint code. It previously said only what the attribute does, not what skipping it costs.

Docs only — no behaviour change.

## Verification

- 45 s traced to source, not quoted from a changelog: `packages/engine/src/config.ts` → `playerReadyTimeout: 45_000`, exposed as `--player-ready-timeout` in `packages/cli/src/commands/render.ts` with "Default: 45000 (45 s)".
- Measured the difference on a minimal composition with three animated elements and no registered timeline: **46.7 s → 1.7 s** wall with the attribute added, output md5 **identical**.
- All three internal links resolve (`/guides/gsap-animation`, `/reference/html-schema`, and the existing section anchors).
- `scripts/check-docs-snippet-motion.mjs` is scoped to `docs/snippets/` autoplay guards and is unaffected.

title: feat(lint): warn on negative z-index, which renders as a missing element
body:
Follow-up to #4366, which is labelled `triage/needs-design`. That issue asked for a **diagnostic** rather than a behaviour change, on the grounds that whether negative stacking is in scope for the renderer is your call. This is that diagnostic.

## The problem

An element at a negative `z-index` does not appear in `snapshot` or `render` output. Siblings differing only in the sign of `z-index` render exactly. `lint`, `validate` and `render` all exit 0 and say nothing, so the element is simply missing and the first suspicion falls on the author's own CSS.

Re-verified on **0.8.71** before opening this (the issue was filed against 0.8.68) — three absolutely-positioned sibling bands, identical but for `z-index`:

| band | `z-index` | expected | sampled pixel |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#underA` | `-1` | `#f5e6c8` | `(10,10,10)` — **absent**, reads the page background |
| `#underB` | `0` | `#20a0f0` | `(32,160,240)` — exact |
| `#over` | `1` | `#d02020` | `(208,32,32)` — exact |

One variable, three values, two controls passing. Nothing in the 0.8.69–0.8.71 release notes touches paint order.

## The rule

`negative_z_index`, **severity `warning`**. Deliberately not an error: the rule should not presume the outcome of the design question in #4366. If negative stacking is later supported, the rule comes out; if it is declared out of scope, this is the thing that tells authors so.

Covers `<style>` blocks and inline `style` attributes, and names the owning selector so the finding points at something searchable.

`fixHint` steers to DOM order — an earlier sibling paints behind a later one — rather than to lowering an element, since raising the others is the change that survives whatever #4366 decides.

## False positives I went looking for

The lookbehind is the load-bearing part. A plain `\b` boundary treats the hyphen in a custom property as a word break:

```css
#a { --z-index: -1; --panel-z-index: -3; }   /* declares variables, stacks nothing */
```

A `\b` pattern flags **both**. The rule's `(?<![\w-])` flags neither — I ran that exact mutation as a control, and it goes red as it should, so the lookbehind is pinned by a test rather than by a comment. Also excluded: `-0` (not a negative stacking level), CSS comments (via the existing `stripCssComments`), and `z-index: var(--x)`, which cannot be resolved statically and so stays silent rather than guessing.

7 tests added, covering both true-positive forms and all five of those negative cases.

## What I could not run

**I did not run the vitest suite locally** — this box has no `bun` and no installed `node_modules`, and installing a monorepo's dependencies was not something I was willing to do on it right now. I validated the rule's discriminating logic by executing the exact pattern against the same fixtures in plain node (12/12, plus the mutation control above), which covers the part most likely to be wrong. **The suite itself needs CI to confirm** — please don't read my green as a passing test run.

title: fix(render): preserve zero duration and clarify render errors
body:
## What

Preserve `0` when a composition has no known duration. An empty draft remains serializable, but rendering still requires a positive duration.

- `generateHyperframesHtml` computes the root duration from the supplied total, timed elements, and zoom keyframes. It preserves `0` for an empty draft and rejects non-finite results.
- The render readiness probe continues to fail on zero duration. Its diagnostic now explains when a registered GSAP timeline has no positive length and points authors to a positive root `data-duration`.

## Why

Zero duration means the renderer has no valid video length. Giving it an arbitrary positive duration could truncate an animation and make an invalid composition appear to export successfully. The producer must supply the intended positive duration or register a seekable timeline with positive length.

## Scope

This PR makes invalid duration values explicit and the render failure actionable. It does not establish which producer emits the live failing HTML or assign a duration to that composition. If that producer is outside this repo, it still needs to declare the intended positive root duration or register a timed seekable timeline.

## Validation

- Core generator tests: 49 passed.
- Parser round-trip and stable-ID tests: 14 passed, 1 existing todo.
- Engine frame-capture and error-classification tests: 101 passed.
- Core and engine typechecks passed; oxlint and oxfmt passed on changed files.
- Pre-commit checks passed.

title: fix(core): frame captures wait for a seeking video to land its frame
body:
## What changes for a user

A frame grabbed right after the first seek on a freshly loaded preview now shows the frame you asked for. Before, a capture that waited for the runtime's seek-completion barrier (`window.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`, which the CLI's frame capture and `motion-shot` already await) got whatever the `<video>` was showing before the seek, often its first frame or nothing, while every other layer had already moved to the new time.

## Why

`syncRuntimeMedia` seeks a paused video by writing `el.currentTime` and returns. The browser finishes that seek asynchronously. The seek-completion barrier only knew about `hf-seek` listeners and VFX captures, so it resolved while the video was still `seeking`. A second seek to the same time looked right only because the first one had finished landing by then.

The fix joins each video that is still `seeking` after the media sync's write to the same barrier, until `seeked`, `error`, `emptied` or `abort`. No timers and no retries. Render export is unchanged: videos that have an injected render-frame sibling skip the `currentTime` write, and the new call sits inside that branch.

## Before

![main: video pixels at the seek barrier (0s frame) vs settled 12s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1584aa3a-7e2d-4a83-a646-109e657ef723)

## After

![fix: video pixels at the seek barrier match the settled 12s frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04a33ce5-a6d0-4c68-9eb9-5866aab4a892)

Left: the video's pixels at the moment the barrier resolves after the first `seek(12)` on a fresh page. Right: the same video once it has settled at 12 s. Fixture: a generated 20 s `testsrc` clip (the timestamp is burned into the picture), one `<video data-start="0">`, served by the Studio preview route from this branch.

## What I measured

- Fixture above, 6 fresh page loads each, headless Chrome on a loaded Linux box: **main 6/6 wrong** at the barrier (video still `seeking`, `readyState` 1, no frame decoded), **fix 0/6 wrong** (`seeking` false, `readyState` 4, pixels identical to the settled frame).
- A real multi-scene launch film (13 videos, 17 sub-composition timelines), first `seek(12)` after `__renderReady`, 8 fresh loads per build: on main the in-window video was still `seeking` when the barrier resolved in 8/8 runs. On the fix, 0/8, and 8/8 first-seek screenshots matched the settled frame. The system load was higher during the fix run.
- On main, a fixed 500 ms settle after the first seek (no barrier) still produced a visibly wrong frame in 1/4 and 2/8 runs of that film. Waiting for the video's `seeked` fixed 8/8.
- `packages/core`: `src/runtime/media.test.ts` exit 0, 119 passed. The whole `src/runtime` folder exit 0, 59 files, 1292 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- The new tests fail on main (`holds the seek-completion barrier…`: barrier resolved while the video was seeking). Two mutations, each run: dropping the call turns that test red, and dropping `error` from the end events turns only `releases the barrier when the seek ends in error` red.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A capture caller that seeks but never awaits the barrier and sleeps a fixed time instead is unchanged by this PR. It has to await `window.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion()` to benefit.
- A video whose network stalls mid-seek keeps the barrier open until the element errors or is emptied. I did not measure a stalled network. The same holds for a video that composition code removes from the page mid-seek. The runtime itself never detaches media, and the barrier already had this shape for `hf-seek` `waitUntil()` promises.
- Playback paths: a hard sync while playing also registers when the video is seeking. Nothing awaits the barrier during playback, and the entry drops out when the seek ends.
- Windows and macOS browsers. Linux headless Chrome only.

title: feat(studio): let an embedder draw the preview edge to edge with fillBox
body:
## What

`NLEPreview` gets an optional `fillBox` prop. When it is on, the picture is drawn edge to edge in the preview's box instead of 8px in from each side on a dark band. Without the prop nothing changes.

## Why

An app that embeds `NLEPreview` and sizes its box to the film's shape saw the film smaller than the box, framed by a black band. In a 640x360 box with a 16:9 film, the picture was 611.5x344. There was no way to turn the band off: the inset lived in two places (the inner container's `inset-2` and a 16px subtraction in `resolvePreviewStageSize`), and neither was reachable from props.

## How

- One constant owns the per-side inset (`PREVIEW_STAGE_INSET_PX = 8`). `fillBox` sets it to 0.
- The same value drives the inner container's `inset` and the stage-size math, so the layout and the sizing cannot drift apart.
- `resolvePreviewStageSize` takes the inset as a parameter that defaults to the constant, so existing callers keep their numbers.
- The viewport's `p-2` is removed: every child of the viewport is absolutely positioned, so the padding never affected layout.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `NLEPreview.test.ts`: in a 640x360 box, the default stays 611.5556x344 with an 8px inset, and `fillBox` gives a 640x360 stage with no inset. It passes on this branch (11 passed, exit 0). It fails when `fillBox` is ignored (exit 1, only this test red).
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.
- [x] A page that mounts `NLEPreview` in a 640x360 box (pink outline) with a 16:9 registry example, same URL both times. Measured in the browser: main draws 611.5x344 inside the box; this branch with `fillBox` draws 640x360. With the prop off, this branch's screenshot is pixel-identical to main.

### Before

main: the picture sits 8px in from the box on a black band.

![main: 611x344 picture on a black band in a 640x360 box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0af502c-f15e-4e87-b697-b76127eca363)

### After

this branch with `fillBox`: the picture fills the box.

![fillBox: 640x360 picture fills the 640x360 box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8c555fd3-a49d-4a8d-85b0-54b6a445b110)

## Review

Independent adversarial review of this head: blocking none, should fix none. Notes: the new test covers a same-shape landscape box without the ruler gutter; the gutter and letterbox paths reuse the same arithmetic (checked by hand, `2 * (inset + gutter)` equals the old single subtraction when the inset is 8). Every consumer of the stage geometry (pan and zoom clamp, ruler, deselect outside the frame, drop coordinates) reads live rects, so none assumes the inset.

title: fix(engine): resolve the version by walking to our own package root
body:
Fixes the `hyperframes_version` mp4 tag always reading `0.0.0-dev` (#4365).

## What was wrong

`readEngineVersion()` resolved `../../package.json` relative to `import.meta.url`. **No single relative literal can be correct, because the code runs in two layouts:**

```
repo       packages/engine/src/utils/  + ../../  →  packages/engine/package.json   ✓
published  <pkg>/dist/cli.js           + ../../  →  node_modules/package.json      ✗
```

The published CLI **bundles** the engine, so the file that runs sits at `<pkg>/dist/`, one level shallower than the source. `node_modules/package.json` does not exist → `MODULE_NOT_FOUND` → the bare `catch` → the sentinel.

Verified on the published **0.8.71** artifact: both `dist/cli.js` and `dist/fontLocalizeCli.js` still carry the relative require, and the overshoot path is absent on disk.

## The fix: walk up, and match on the package name

**The name check is the fix, not a refinement.** A bare *"first `package.json` found while walking up"* resolves to whatever happens to sit above us in a hoisted install and returns a **confident wrong version** — the same class of defect as the sentinel, and harder to notice because the answer looks plausible. Only a `package.json` whose own `name` is `hyperframes` or `@hyperframes/*` may answer. That reasoning is in the code, not just here.

A test pins it: with the name check removed, **exactly one** case fails — a foreign `some-consumer-app@9.9.9` sitting above `node_modules/hyperframes/dist` gets returned as the engine version.

## The sentinel was the deeper defect

`0.0.0-dev` parses as a version, compares against one, and sorts below every real release — so a **total resolution failure was indistinguishable from a dev build**. That is why it shipped unnoticed across twenty published versions.

The fallback is now `"unresolved"`, deliberately not semver-shaped, and **every failure path warns with its reason**. A failed lookup still never breaks a render — it just can no longer be read as a measurement.

## The comment was asserting a false premise

The old comment said the engine *"ships as raw TS and exports `./package.json`"*. The published package has **no `exports` field at all** and bundles the engine, so that premise does not hold where the code runs. Replaced with the two layouts and why they conflict — a comment asserting something untrue of the runtime is how the next person repeats this.

## Verification

`resolveOwnVersionFrom(startDir)` is exported so the walk is testable against real fixture layouts — a guard that can't be exercised is a guard nobody has checked.

**9 tests**, covering: package root; nested `dist/` (the published layout); repo `src/utils` depth; **the hoisted-install trap**; our root preferred over a foreign one further up; our root with no version returning the sentinel rather than a foreign version; stepping over a malformed `package.json`; no match at all; and that the sentinel is not semver-shaped.

I ran the real function against those fixtures directly — **8/8 green**, warnings firing visibly — and the mutation above red on exactly the trap case. **I could not run the vitest suite** (no `bun`/`node_modules` on this machine), so please let CI confirm the suite itself rather than reading my green as a test run.

title: fix(engine): name the data-no-timeline opt-out in the timeline-timeout warning
body:
## The gap

A sub-composition timeline timeout emits **two** messages, and only one of them is useful:

| | names the opt-out | names the pending ids | who reads it |
|---|---|---|---|
| stderr, inside `pollSubCompositionTimelines` | yes | yes | a human watching the run |
| structured `CaptureWarning` | **no** | **no** | `render`'s summary, `result.warnings`, the SDK, CI |

The structured one said only:

```
[sub_timeline_readiness_timeout] Sub-composition timelines did not become ready within 45000ms
```

`render.ts` re-prints that in the `completed_with_warnings` block and returns it in the
result's `warnings` array, so a programmatic caller gets the symptom with no remedy — and a
human reading scrollback gets it *after* the rich line has scrolled away.

It also reads as a fault to diagnose. The commonest cause is the opposite: a composition
driven by CSS animations or rAF never registers `window.__timelines[id]`, so it is polled
for the whole `playerReadyTimeout` (45 s, `packages/engine/src/config.ts`) and then proceeds
with a warning. That composition is correct. It is paying 45 s a render because nothing told
the author the wait was theirs to switch off.

## The change

- The timeout message says the wait **can be intentional**, names `data-no-timeline` as the
  opt-out, and keeps the async-setup case as the other branch.
- The pending composition ids were already computed for the stderr line and thrown away. An
  optional `onPending` callback carries them to the session, so the structured warning and
  its `details.pendingCompositionIds` name them too — matching the `sub_timeline_script_failure`
  branch, which already names its failed sources.
- **The stderr text is unchanged**; `missing` is still `ids.join(", ")`.
- The script-failure branch is untouched and deliberately does *not* gain the
  `data-no-timeline` advice: there the timeline can never arrive, so that would be the wrong
  remedy.

Before / after, for a composition with no timeline:

```
- Sub-composition timelines did not become ready within 45000ms
+ Sub-composition timelines did not become ready within 45000ms (still unregistered: scene-2).
+ This can be intentional: a composition driven by CSS animations or rAF never registers
+ window.__timelines[id], and marking its host with data-no-timeline skips the wait entirely.
+ Otherwise, a composition that sets up asynchronously must register window.__timelines[id]
+ once setup completes.
```

## Tests

`packages/engine/src/services/frameCapture-subTimelineWarning.test.ts` — 6 cases:
no warning on `ready`/absent outcome, the remedy named, the ids named, no empty
parenthetical when the list is empty, and the script-failure branch left alone.

**I could not run `vitest` in this environment** (no installed `node_modules` for the
workspace), so I will not claim the suite is green. What I did instead, and what I can
stand behind: I extracted `recordCaptureWarnings` and `recordSubTimelineWarning` verbatim
from the patched file and executed them under `node --experimental-strip-types` against the
same assertions plus a dedup case — **16/16 pass**. Two mutants confirm the assertions
discriminate rather than passing by construction:

- the **pre-patch message** → 4 red (remedy, "intentional", `window.__timelines[id]`, ids);
- the **plausible-but-incomplete fix** — names `data-no-timeline` but omits that the wait can
  be intentional → **exactly 1 red**, the assertion for that clause.

Please still run the real suite in CI; the extraction shares the production lines but not
the production module graph.

title: fix(studio): a timeline at 00:00 stays at 00:00 when the window resizes or the zoom is set
body:
## What

A timeline that sits at 00:00 stays at 00:00 when the window is resized or the zoom level is set. Before, 00:00 slid under the track header and the playhead was drawn over the header.

## Why

When the zoom scale changes, the timeline keeps the time at the middle of the view in place. That step ran on every scale change: a window resize (the fit scale follows the window width) and a zoom set from code by an app that embeds Studio (the Desktop app restores a zoom once per project). From a view at the start, keeping the middle time in place always moves the view to the right, by (half the view width minus the header) times (new scale / old scale - 1). At 200%, resizing from 1200x733 to 1440x900 moved the view by 117px.

## How

One condition in the existing centre-anchor layout effect in `useTimelinePlayhead.ts`: when the view is at the start (`scrollLeft < 1`), it stays there. A scrolled view still keeps its middle time. The pinch zoom keeps anchoring at the cursor: it opts out of this step before the new check.

This also applies to Studio's own toolbar and slider, on purpose. On main, zooming in from 00:00 (200% to 400% at 1200 wide) moves the view 332px right. That hides the clip starts and their names under the track header and draws the playhead over the gutter. The fix keeps 00:00 and every clip label visible. A scrolled view still keeps its centre time, so zooming mid-film is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] New `useTimelinePlayhead.test.tsx`: from scroll 0 a scale change keeps scroll at 0 (fails on main: 51.52), and from scroll 400 the middle time stays put (1168, passes on both). Exit 0, 2 passed. With the new check removed, only the start test fails (exit 1).
- [x] `Timeline.test.ts` (81 passed) and `timelineZoom.test.ts` (29 passed), each exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- [x] Live Studio with a registry example, timeline at 00:00. Window resized from 1200x733 to 1440x900 at 200%: main scrollLeft 117, this branch 0. Toolbar zoom-in from 200% to 400%: main scrollLeft 332, this branch 0.

### Before

main, window resize at 200%: 00:00 is hidden under the track header and the clips start under it.

![main: resize at 200%, 00:00 hidden under the track header](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3c68d6c-1f0c-4259-851f-3392454430f5)

main, toolbar zoom-in from 00:00: the ruler starts past 00:05 and the clip names are gone.

![main: toolbar zoom-in from 00:00, clip names gone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79d058bf-9653-4746-a7d9-322df0537ff9)

### After

this branch, same resize: the ruler still starts at 00:00.

![fix: resize at 200%, ruler starts at 00:00](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1a732952-d65c-4374-8587-9170bdbcbb59)

this branch, same zoom-in: 00:00 and every clip label stay visible.

![fix: toolbar zoom-in from 00:00, every clip label visible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2074e735-98a8-4ce2-85a2-5cc53e7897f8)

## Review

Independent adversarial review of this head: blocking none, should fix none. Checked: the pinch zoom still anchors at the cursor (its skip flag is consumed before the new check), fit mode, the zoom-mode switch and playback follow are untouched, the hook has one consumer, and no existing test depends on the old scroll from 00:00.

title: feat(lint): flag a canvas-level CSS zoom that rescales a fixed frame
body:
## What it catches

The capture frame is sized from the root's `data-width`/`data-height` — **layout** pixels.
CSS `zoom` on the canvas itself (the root, or `html`/`body` above it) rescales the painted
content inside that frame without changing the frame. The author gets neither of the two
things they might have meant.

Measured at **0.8.71**, on an 800×400 composition holding two 100×100 boxes at `left:100`
and `left:600`, rendered to a PNG sequence with the boxes located by colour:

| | canvas | box at left:100 | box at left:600 |
|---|---|---|---|
| no zoom | 800×400 | (100,50) 100×100 | (600,50) 100×100 |
| root `zoom: 0.5` | 800×400 | (50,25) 50×50 | (300,25) 50×50 |
| root `zoom: 2` | 800×400 | (200,100) 200×200 | **zero pixels** |

The last cell is the one worth an error. That box is inside the declared composition, it
scales to x=1200 in a frame that is still 800 wide, and **nothing** — lint, `check`, the
render log — reports that it is gone.

## What it deliberately does not catch

`zoom` on a **descendant**. Measured in the same run: a child at `left:100` with `zoom: 2`
paints at (200,100) at 200×200 — exactly what CSS `zoom` specifies. It is honoured, not
ignored, so a rule that fired on every `zoom` would be flagging correct authoring. The rule
only fires when the declaration's leftmost compound targets the root, one of its classes,
its id, or `html` / `body` / `:root` / `*`, or when it is inline on one of those elements.

Identity values (`1`, `1.0`, `100%`, `normal`, `unset`, `initial`, `revert`, and any of
those with `!important`) are silent.

The `(?<![\w-])` lookbehind is load-bearing, same trap as #4403: `--zoom: 2` and
`--panel-zoom: 0.5` are author variables, and a plain `\b` flags both.

## Tests

11 cases in `packages/lint/src/rules/composition.test.ts`: the enlarging and shrinking
messages (they say different things), `html`/`body` selectors, inline style, descendant
silence, every identity value, custom properties, `!important` both ways, and a zoom inside
a CSS comment.

**I could not run `vitest` here** (no installed `node_modules` for the workspace), so I am
not claiming the suite is green. What I did instead: extracted the rule and its helpers
verbatim — plus `readAttr`, `stripCssComments`, `truncateSnippet`, `findHtmlTag`,
`leftmostCompoundId`, `leftmostCompoundClasses` straight from `utils.ts` — and ran them under
`node --experimental-strip-types` against hand-built `OpenTag`/`ExtractedBlock` inputs:
**27/27 pass**. Three mutants confirm the assertions discriminate:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| `\b` instead of the lookbehind | 1 red — the custom-property case |
| **drop the canvas-root restriction** (the plausible "just flag every zoom" fix) | 3 red — descendant, foreign id, at-rule stop |
| identity list without `100%` | 1 red — that case |

The extraction shares the production lines but not the real HTML parser, so the inputs are
hand-built; please let CI run the real suite.

title: feat(lint): warn when a composition is wider than the inspection viewport cap
body:
## The asymmetry

`packages/cli/src/utils/compositionViewport.ts` caps a parsed `data-width` / `data-height`
at `MAX_VIEWPORT_DIMENSION = 4096` with a plain `Math.min` and no warning.
`captureCompositionFrame` resolves its viewport through that helper, and **`check`,
`validate`, `snapshot`, `compare` and `layout`** all capture through it. `layout` and
`motionShot` carry their own independent `Math.min(..., 4096)`.

**`render` does not go through it.** Measured at **0.8.71** on a 5000×400 composition with
100×100 boxes at `left:100` and `left:4500`:

| command | frame | box at left:100 | box at left:4500 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render` | **5000×400** | present | **present** |
| `snapshot` | **4096×400** | present | **absent** |

So the video is correct and the tools you would reach for to check it silently cannot see
the last 904 px.

Both directions of that are awkward. `check` comes back clean on a region it never
rendered — a false pass. And someone debugging a missing element through `snapshot` chases
a difference that exists only in the instrument.

## The rule

`data-width` or `data-height` above 4096 on the composition root → **warning**, naming the
axis (or both) and saying plainly that render is unaffected.

Warning rather than error on purpose: the deliverable is fine and a canvas wider than 4096
can be entirely deliberate. What the author needs is the knowledge that a clean inspection
result does not cover all of it.

The constant is a literal with a comment pointing at `compositionViewport.ts` rather than an
import — `@hyperframes/lint` should not depend on the CLI, and the number is a property of
the capture path being warned about. If the cap moves, this comment is the breadcrumb.

## Tests

7 cases in `packages/lint/src/rules/composition.test.ts`: width over, height over, both
named, silent exactly at 4096, fires at 4097, silent on 4K, silent when absent or
unparseable.

**I could not run `vitest` here** (no installed `node_modules` for the workspace). Instead I
extracted the rule plus `readAttr` and `truncateSnippet` verbatim and ran them under
`node --experimental-strip-types`: **13/13 pass**, including both boundary neighbours
(4095 silent / 4096 silent / 4097 fires) rather than only a far probe. Three mutants:

| mutant | result |
|---|---|
| `>=` instead of `>` | 1 red — *exactly* the at-the-cap case |
| cap constant 8192 | 6 red |
| never return empty | 5 red — every silence case |

Please let CI run the real suite; the extraction shares the production lines but not the
HTML parser.

title: fix(producer): report render progress from the first frame, at most four times a second
body:
## What changes for a person watching a render

Export progress now moves from the first frame. Before, a render sat at 25% "Starting frame capture" with no report at all while the browsers started and the first 30 frames were captured: about 3 s on a quiet machine and over 30 s on a busy one. Then it jumped in 30-frame steps. The sequential capture paths had the opposite problem and reported every single frame, so a piped CLI printed one line per frame.

Now every capture stage reports the first frame, the last frame, and at most one update every 250 ms in between. The warm-up steps before frame 1 each report their own label:

- `Checking browser GPU` (the GPU probe launches a throwaway Chrome in auto mode)
- `Measuring capture speed` (capture calibration, when worker count is auto)
- `Starting browsers (k/n ready)` (parallel workers, from the engine's existing worker phase events)

## How

- `reportFrameProgress` in `packages/producer/src/services/render/shared.ts` is the one owner of capture-loop cadence. The job's fields still update on every frame; only the callback is throttled (per job, WeakMap). It replaces the `% 30`, `% 10` and every-frame checks in the disk, streaming, segmented and both HDR loops.
- `reportWorkerStartup` counts workers that reached their first capture. Worker ids past a smaller retry's worker count are ignored. Start-up and frame reports keep separate timers, so the first captured frame is always reported.
- Frame labels (`Streaming frame N/M`, `Capturing frame N/M`, `Layered composite frame N/M`) are unchanged, so parsers that read them keep working.

## Before / after

Same 300-frame project, `--quality draft --workers auto`, piped (non-TTY) CLI, one Linux machine at the same load, run back to back; both took the six-worker streaming route. Seconds since spawn. Before is the published 0.8.71, which is this branch's base.

Before (0.8.71):
```
17.6   25% Starting frame capture
27.7   31% Streaming frame 30/300 (6 workers)     <- 10.1 s with no report
29.0   36% Streaming frame 60/300 (6 workers)
30.5   42% Streaming frame 90/300 (6 workers)
...    13 reports after 25% in total
42.3   80% Streaming frame 300/300 (6 workers)
```

After (this branch):
```
 4.6   25% Starting frame capture
 4.6   25% Checking browser GPU
 5.8   25% Measuring capture speed
 7.0   25% Starting browsers (0/6 ready)
 8.6   25% Starting browsers (1/6 ready)
 8.9   25% Starting browsers (6/6 ready)
 8.9   25% Streaming frame 1/300 (6 workers)
 9.3   27% Streaming frame 12/300 (6 workers)
 9.7   29% Streaming frame 24/300 (6 workers)
10.0   31% Streaming frame 33/300 (6 workers)
...    76 reports after 25% in total
41.1   80% Streaming frame 300/300 (6 workers)
```

Longest gap between reports after 25%: 10.1 s before, 5.1 s after. The remaining 5.1 s is a stretch around frame 160 of this project where no worker finished any frame, so there was nothing to report (the same stretch is hidden inside a 30-frame step before).

Under much heavier load on the same machine the difference grows: 32.6 s of silence after 25% before, 6.5 s after (same frame-160 stretch).

## Tests

- `captureStreamingStage.test.ts`: a slow fake parallel capture (400 ms per frame) must report browser start-up, then frame 1 and frame 2, then every frame; a fast one (300 frames at 1 ms) must report fewer than 5 frame lines and end on 300/300. Both fail on main (main reports frames 30 and 60 only, and 10 lines for the fast run).
- `shared.test.ts`: ready count across a retry with fewer workers.

## Consequences worth knowing

- Render-failure telemetry takes its stage code from the current label. A failure during warm-up used to be filed under `starting_frame_capture`; it is now filed under the step that failed: `checking_browser_gpu`, `measuring_capture_speed` or `starting_browsers` (the CLI's `normalizeStageCode` keeps one code for the counted label).
- Not in this change: the disk-frame encode path reports nothing between `Encoding video` (75%) and `Assembling` (90%). That is one ffmpeg call with no progress parsing; separate follow-up.

## Independent review

Two passes by a reviewer that did not write the code (first head, then the fix-up). Mutations run against every new assertion (interval to 0, no first-call report, no last-frame force, no worker-id filter, start-up call removed, shared timer, telemetry prefix removed): each one fails a test. Lint and format clean on changed files; each changed test file passes alone.

- Should fix (fixed): a counted `Starting browsers (k/n ready)` label would have split the CLI's failure stage code per count. `normalizeStageCode` now maps it to `starting_browsers`.
- Should fix (fixed, found in the live trace): frame 1 was swallowed when it landed within 250 ms of the last start-up report. Start-up and frame reports now keep separate timers.
- Note (left as is): after a transient capture retry with the same worker count, the first start-up line can count a worker from the failed attempt as ready until that worker's fresh launch event arrives (milliseconds). Display only; it corrects itself.
- Note (pre-existing): Studio's render-error event sends the raw stage text with no bucketed code, so it already varies with frame counts on main.

title: fix: serve projects and assets whose names contain @ % # & or ?
body:
## What changes for a user

A project whose name contains `@`, `%`, `#`, `&` or `?` now loads its files, preview assets, sub-compositions, thumbnails and waveforms when the client percent-encodes the name in the URL. Before, those requests answered 404 (403 for the files route), so a project named from a sentence with an `@` mention showed no preview or timeline pictures. `hyperframes play` and `hyperframes present` had the same problem with asset and scene files named with those characters.

## Why

Seven routes turned a request path into a file path by cutting a prefix out of Hono's `c.req.path`. Hono decodes that path with `decodeURI`, which leaves `%40 %25 %23 %26 %3F` encoded. So the cut missed (studio-server, where the prefix holds the decoded project id), or the file name kept its escapes (CLI, which never decoded).

One helper, `requestSubPath(url, route)` in `@hyperframes/studio-server`, now takes the part after the route by segment from the raw URL and decodes it once. The seven sites:

| Package | Site | Route |
|---|---|---|
| studio-server | `routes/files.ts` `resolveProjectPath` (six callers: files, file-mutations, gsap-animations, gsap-mutations, gsap-mutations-batch, gsap-mutation-rollback) | `projects/:id/<route>` |
| studio-server | `routes/preview.ts` | `projects/:id/preview/comp` |
| studio-server | `routes/preview.ts` | `projects/:id/preview` |
| studio-server | `routes/thumbnail.ts` | `projects/:id/thumbnail` |
| studio-server | `routes/waveform.ts` | `projects/:id/waveform` |
| cli | `commands/play.ts` `registerCompositionRoute` | `composition` |
| cli | `commands/present.ts` (route extracted into `registerPresentCompositionRoute`, same behaviour) | `composition` |

Two more defects in the same routes, fixed here:
- `thumbnail/*` built its internal preview URL from the raw id and path, so `#` turned the rest into a fragment, `?` into a query string, and a lone `%` was malformed. It now encodes both.
- `thumbnail/*` and `waveform/*` joined the decoded path with no containment check, so an encoded `../` reached outside the project. That was the same on main. They now use the guards their siblings already use: `resolveWithinProject` like `preview/comp/*` for compositions, `isWithinProjectRoot` like `preview/*` for read-only assets.
- An empty `thumbnail/` path resolved to the project folder and crashed reading it (500). It now answers 404.

## Name matrix

studio-server: `src/routes/projectIdEncoding.test.ts` runs every name as a project id against all five routes, plus two traversal cases. cli: `src/commands/compositionRoute.encoding.test.ts` runs the same names as asset file names against `play` and `present` (`?` is skipped on Windows, where file names cannot hold it).

| Name | files | preview asset | preview comp | thumbnail | waveform |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `A @HyperFrames launch` | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed |
| `50% off` | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed |
| `#2 take` | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed |
| `Tom & Jerry` | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed |
| `why?` | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed | main fails, fixed |
| double space, accents, emoji | pass on both | pass on both | pass on both | pass on both | pass on both |

`play` and `present`: with the old line, both fail the same five reserved names (10 of 16); on this branch, 16 passed.

## What I measured

- Against main's four route files, the new tests fail 27: the five reserved characters on all five routes, plus both traversal tests. On this branch: exit 0, 47 passed (the extra test is the empty thumbnail path, which fails with a 500 without its check).
- Mutations, each run: removing only the waveform guard fails only the waveform traversal test. Removing only the thumbnail URL encoding fails only the thumbnail cases for `#`, `%` and `?`. Skipping one segment too few in the helper turns the matrix red.
- CLI on this branch: `compositionRoute.encoding.test.ts` 16 passed and `play.test.ts` 14 passed, each exit 0. Putting only `present` back on the old line fails only `present`'s five reserved names.
- Route suites on this branch: `files.test.ts` 80 passed, `files.pathSafety.test.ts` 25 passed, `preview.test.ts` 52 passed, `thumbnail.test.ts` 20 passed, each exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 in studio-server and cli. `oxfmt --check` exit 0 on every changed file.
- Live, the CLI's Studio server serving a project named `A @HyperFrames launch`, requested as `A%20%40HyperFrames%20launch` (first commit):

| Request | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `files/index.html` | 403 | 200 |
| `preview/clip.mp4` | 404 | 200 |
| `preview/index.html` | 404 | 200 |
| `preview/comp/index.html` | 404 | 200 |

No visual change: server routing only.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real thumbnail capture in a browser. The test checks the URL handed to the generator parses back to the exact project and file, and that the route serves the result.
- Hosts other than the CLI server and `app.request` in tests. The helper finds the first `projects` segment, so a host that mounts the API under a prefix still works unless the prefix itself contains a `projects` segment.
- `render.ts` `renders/file/` and the engine's file server take a path the same way, but the names there are generated (job ids), so this bug does not reach a user. Not changed.

title: feat(studio): an embedder can change what the shortcuts panel lists
body:
## What

An app that embeds `PlayerControls` can choose what its shortcuts panel lists. `DEFAULT_SHORTCUT_SECTIONS` is exported, and `PlayerControls` takes an optional `shortcutSections`. An embedder can pass the defaults with entries dropped or relabelled. Without the prop nothing changes.

## Why

The panel read a private list, so an embedder showed Studio's full editor list even for keys it doesn't use. The HyperFrames Desktop app mounts `PlayerControls` but not Studio's app hotkeys, and uses S for its own Select tool. Its panel still said "S: Split clip at playhead", while S in Desktop means Select.

## How

- The list moved as it was from `ShortcutsPanel.tsx` into `studioShortcuts.ts`, as `DEFAULT_SHORTCUT_SECTIONS` (checked entry for entry against main).
- `ShortcutsPanel` takes `sections` (default: that list); `PlayerControls` passes `shortcutSections` through.
- The app hotkey dispatcher's bare F (fullscreen), S (split) and R (record) now come from `STUDIO_PLAIN_KEYS` in the same module, and the list's F, S and R rows are built from those constants. Changing one of those keys updates the panel with it.
- Rows and sections are keyed by position, so an embedder's list can repeat a key (two rows for S) or a section title.
- `DEFAULT_SHORTCUT_SECTIONS` is typed as `readonly ShortcutSection[]` with `string` keys and labels. The old private list was `as const`, but nothing read its literal types.
- Not in this PR: an override for the app hotkeys themselves. Only Studio's own app mounts them today.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `ShortcutsPanel.test.tsx`, through `PlayerControls`: the default panel lists "Split clip at playhead"; with the defaults minus that row it doesn't, and other rows stay.
