title: fix(cli): stop check --at false alarms and name a stale CLI version
body:
## What changes for the person running `hyperframes check`

1. `check --at 51,52.5` on a still end card no longer fails with `sweep_static` ("Timeline did not advance under seek"). The frozen-sweep guard no longer judges the times the user picked with `--at`, because they can all fall inside a legitimately still stretch. Samples the sweep adds on its own (`--at-transitions`, `--caption-zone`, `--frame-check`) are still judged, and runs without `--at` behave exactly as before.
2. Running an older CLI than the one the project pins now prints, on every run (except `--json`, CI and dev mode):
   ```
   This is hyperframes 0.7.71, but this project pins hyperframes@0.8.66.
   Run it through the project's npm scripts, or npx hyperframes@0.8.66.
   ```
   With several pins it names the highest. The existing throttled "bump your pin" notice is unchanged for the case where the running CLI is at or above the pin.

## Why

- **`--at` false positive.** With `--at`, `buildLayoutSampleTimes` returns only the user's times, and `detectSweepStatic` compared their geometry as if they were the sweep's own spread across the timeline. Two samples 1.5s apart on a static end card had identical geometry, so the run failed with an error that says every other verdict is unreliable. The same project passed with no `--at` and with `--samples 30`.
- **Pinned version.** A real failure: an agent ran a bare `npx hyperframes add` in a project whose scripts pin `hyperframes@0.8.66`. npx resolved an older global install, 0.7.71, which ignores a registry item's `file.url` and 404s fetching it from raw GitHub. Nothing told the person which version was running or that the project expected a newer one. The CLI already reads the project's pins (`readPinnedHyperframesVersions`) for the stale-pin notice; this adds the comparison against its own version. It covers every command that prints notices (`add`, `check`, `lint`, `render`, ...), including when the command fails.
- **Limit:** the notice ships in the new CLI, so a copy that is already older than this release cannot print it. It helps from this release forward.

## What `check` can and cannot see (canvas)

`check`'s layout inspection reads DOM boxes: text elements, panels and media are measured against the frame. Content drawn *into* a `<canvas>` (for example `ctx.fillText` in a grid) is pixels, not boxes, so text on a canvas that runs past the frame edge is clipped silently and `check` passes. The only canvas read today is a downsampled pixel hash for the frozen-sweep signature. A follow-up PR adds a warning for canvas content touching the frame edge, reusing that read, with a `data-layout-allow-overflow` opt-out.

## What I measured

- A real 53.7s project with a still end card: `check --at 51,52.5` on `main` (58c873d81) exited 1 with `sweep_static` as its only error; with this branch it exits 0 with no errors.
- A built CLI (0.8.71) in a project whose scripts pin `hyperframes@0.9.99`: `add <missing item>`, `lint` and `check` each print the notice to stderr, also when the command exits 1. `check --json` prints no notice and its stdout parses as JSON. (Built from the first commit; the last commit only changes which pin is named when there are several.)
- `check.test.ts`: 63 passed, exit 0. `updateCheck.stalepin.test.ts` + `projectPin.test.ts`: 9 passed, exit 0. `updateCheck.test.ts`: 16 passed, exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- Each new test goes red under its own mutation, and nothing else does: dropping the user-picked filter fails only the `--at` still-end-card test; marking every sample as user-picked fails only the `--at` + `--at-transitions` test; reverting the pin comparison fails only the new stale-pin test.
- fallow audit, typecheck, lint and format hooks pass on the commit.

## What I did NOT exercise

- `--at` combined with `--caption-zone` or `--frame-check` on a real project (unit-tested for `--at-transitions` only; all three feed the grid the same way).
- The notice under `--json`: it stays silent there, as all update notices do; agents reading JSON get the running version in `_meta.version`.
- A multi-pin project: the notice names the highest newer pin (sorted by semver), but no test has more than one newer pin.
- An `--at` time that coincides exactly with a transition, caption or frame sample is also left out of the frozen-sweep comparison. This drops one comparison point, erring toward no false alarm.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, two rounds:
- **First round:** one blocker. The first version switched the frozen-sweep guard off for the whole run whenever `--at` was passed, which hid a frozen timeline in the samples `--at-transitions`/`--caption-zone`/`--frame-check` add. Fixed: only the user-picked times are left out, and a test pins the combination. Two minor findings, both fixed: the pin suggestion used a lexicographic sort (now semver), and a stale comment.
- **Second round:** no blockers, no majors. The two minor notes are listed under "What I did NOT exercise" above.
- The second round's own test runs were blocked by shared-machine load. It read the code and ran lint and format itself; test and mutation results come from the author's runs at this head.

title: fix(studio): an edit still reaches the preview when its reload is slow
body:
## What

A full-reload edit loads in a hidden shadow iframe and is promoted once it paints. If the shadow was not ready within one 15 s budget, it was discarded for good: the stage kept the previous document, the edit never appeared, and nothing retried. On a busy machine this silently dropped deletes, trims and file writes made by agents.

The shadow now keeps loading for up to three budgets (`SHADOW_READY_BUDGETS`) before it is dropped. A slow load still lands; a load that never becomes ready still fails with the same message and callback. Pausing the budget while the tab is hidden is unchanged. A reload that replaces a slow one starts with a fresh set of budgets, and the timer checks the shadow generation before extending, like the other shadow callbacks.

## Tests

`useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts` run alone: 20 passed, exit 0.

- New: a shadow that paints after its first budget is promoted. On the previous code it is dropped at 15 s (the only failure, 18 others pass).
- New: a reload that replaces a slow one gets its own full set of budgets. Deleting the budget reset fails it (1 failed, 19 passed).
- Existing failure thresholds now wait for all budgets (`SHADOW_READY_TIMEOUT_MS * SHADOW_READY_BUDGETS`).

oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. oxfmt: clean. Studio typecheck: clean.

## Review

Independent adversarial review with mutation testing: no blocking findings. Its two should-fix items (the untested budget reset, the missing generation check on the re-arm) are both addressed above.

| Mutation | Caught by |
|---|---|
| Budget reset removed | new replacing-reload test |
| `<` changed to `<=` in the budget check | 4 tests |
| `SHADOW_READY_BUDGETS = 1` | new slow-shadow test |
| Extension branch removed (old behaviour) | 3 tests |

## Before

Studio dev server with a project whose one script answers at once, then takes 20 s after the file is edited, standing in for a slow machine. 24 s after the edit the stage still shows the old text and the reload error.

![Before: the preview still shows "Before the edit" with the "did not reload" error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4d7760f-8a22-436d-a986-704791d97fb4)

## After

Same setup with this change: the edit is on stage from 19 s after the write, with no error.

![After: the preview shows "After the edit"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9490b3fe-339c-4772-8b52-d87747c10796)

title: fix(engine): download tests stop racing real deadlines, and failures name their cause
body:
## What changes

1. **The Windows flake that hit the v0.8.72 release PR is gone.** `urlDownloader.test.ts > never overwrites an artifact returned by a concurrent checksum scope` failed on `windows-latest` with `Download failed while writing the local artifact`. Nothing was wrong with writing files. Every test passes a 1 s download deadline, and that deadline is a real timer. On a slow runner (every test in the file ran 10 to 100 times slower on the failing run; this one took 1363 ms) the first attempt timed out and was retried. The retry made a third fetch call, the test's two-response mock returned `undefined`, and the resulting `TypeError` was reported as a filesystem failure.
   The first commit is #4190 unchanged: the test file holds the 1 s attempt deadline instead of arming it, and a new test proves a 1.2 s fetch against a 1 s deadline still succeeds.
   The third commit removes the same race from three stalled-body tests, which passed a real 20 ms deadline and needed the retry to finish inside it. On a loaded Linux box the old file failed 3 of 3 runs there (`Download timeout after 0.02s`). They now use the held deadline and fire it by hand once the first fetch has started.
2. **A download failure now says what actually failed.** `classifyDownloadFailure` threw away the original error, so any unexpected error, a programming error included, read "writing the local artifact" with nothing else. The message now ends with the underlying error's name and code, for example `Download failed while writing the local artifact (Error ENOSPC)` or `Download failed due to a transient network error (TypeError)`. The flake above would have read `(TypeError)`, pointing at the mock instead of the disk.

## Why only the name and code

Fetch errors can carry the signed request URL in their message, and this file redacts by never copying original messages anywhere. The new suffix keeps that rule: the name must be a bare word and the code a bare `UPPER_CASE` identifier, or it is dropped. The raw error is not attached as `cause`, because loggers print cause chains, and server-side logs would then carry customer URLs. Message prefixes are unchanged, so anything grouping failures by prefix keeps working.

## Proof

- Without the first commit, delaying that test's first response to 1100 ms reproduces the release failure exactly on Linux: same message, same line (`urlDownloader.ts:1132`), 1401 ms. With it, the same change passes.
- `urlDownloader.test.ts` alone: 85 pass, exit 0, five runs in a row on the same loaded box (load average about 55).
- Removing the pipeline's abort signal still turns the two stalled-body guard tests red, so the rewritten tests still test their guard.
- Mutations, each turning a test red: suffix removed (2 tests), code pattern removed (the hostile-name test), deadline hold disabled (the slow-attempt test).
- Engine typecheck, lint and format clean.
- Not exercised: a hosted Windows run of this head. The CI Windows job on this PR is that check.

## Independent review

Two passes by a reviewer that did not write the code (first on the cause change, then on the test fix it prompted).

- Should fix (fixed): three stalled-body tests raced a real 20 ms deadline the same way the 1 s tests did. Reproduced on a loaded box; now fired by hand (third commit).
- Should fix (left as is): "keeps the deadline active through a stalled response body" is guarded by the attempt's own abort, not by the pipeline's abort signal, so removing the signal leaves it green. That is real coverage of a different line, and the test's name is accurate.
- Note: the name and code are read only from `Error` instances; a non-`Error` (such as a `DOMException`) gets no tag. That path is not reachable today, because aborts are classified before `classifyDownloadFailure` runs.
- Verified: the rewritten tests fire the deadline only after the body pipeline is wired, and the retry's deadline is never held at that moment. Lint and format clean; the file passes alone.

Supersedes #4190 (its commit is included unchanged).

title: ci: editing a PR's text no longer cancels its running checks
body:
## What

Editing a PR's description or title no longer cancels its running checks. Before this, every body edit cancelled the in-flight CI, and the required `Test` check stayed red on the cancelled run.

## Why

CI, regression and Windows render run on `pull_request` `edited`, so a base change (a stack restack setting the base back to `main`) re-runs them. A text edit fires the same event. With `cancel-in-progress: true`, the new run cancelled the running one. `Test` runs with `always()` and fails closed when its producer or shard jobs didn't succeed, which is correct, so it failed on the cancelled run. That failure stays on the PR next to the new run's result. It happened on #4401, #4416 and #4418 today.

## How

In `ci.yml`, `regression.yml` and `windows-render.yml`:

```yaml
cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event.action != 'edited' || github.event.changes.base != null }}
```

A push, an open or reopen, or a base change still cancels the running run. A description or title edit waits behind it, then runs. `Semantic PR title` still checks the newest title.

Why a text edit still runs the jobs instead of skipping them: required checks go by the newest check of each name on the head commit, and a skipped job counts as passing. An edit run that skipped `Test` would turn a real failure green. The queued run costs the same as today, minus the cancelled work.

`pr-captures.yml` keeps cancelling, because it reads the description itself and the newest one should win.

## Test plan

- [x] New `scripts/pr-edit-concurrency.test.mjs` (added to `test:scripts`). It checks that the set of workflows reacting to `edited` is known, and that each workflow running code checks uses the expression above. On main: exit 1, 3 of 4 fail. On this branch: exit 0, 4 passed.
- [x] `actionlint` on the three workflows: the same three shellcheck warnings as main, nothing new.
- [x] `node scripts/check-test-reachability.mjs`: exit 0, "zero orphan tests".
- [x] Live check on this PR. With CI run 36011098009 in progress, I edited this description: that run kept going, and the edit's CI run (36011312044) waited behind it. A second edit replaced the waiting run, which was cancelled with zero jobs, so it left no checks. No cancelled or failed `Test` appeared on the PR.
- [x] `bunx fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues`: exit 0 on this head. The first head read the workflows folder through a module URL and failed fallow with an unresolved import; the second commit uses `import.meta.dirname`, as `scripts/check-skill-mirror.mjs` does.

## Review

Independent adversarial review of this head: blocking none, should fix none. It confirmed from GitHub's docs that `cancel-in-progress` accepts an expression, and that the missing `action` and `changes` fields on push and synchronize read as null, so pushes still cancel. It also confirmed that a newer queued run replaces a pending one. From #4411's history it confirmed that the newest same-name check wins, which is why the edit run doesn't skip. Notes: `pr-captures.yml` can still flash red for a moment during an edit, and its newer run replaces the result; and replacing a queued run has not been seen on real PR history yet.

Second head (the fallow fix): independent review, blocking none, should fix none. It confirmed `import.meta.dirname` resolves to `scripts/` on CI's Node 22, and that the test's assertions are unchanged.

title: fix(studio): trimming a scene no longer shrinks it to the length of a video inside
body:
## What

A timeline clip's source length is read from its element: the element itself when it is a video, audio or image, otherwise the first one found inside it. The trim preview then caps a clip's end at that length. For a composition clip, the media inside belongs to the composition's own timeline, not to the clip. So a scene that holds a short video could never be longer than that video, and trimming its end by a few pixels collapsed it to the video's length and saved that.

`resolveMediaElement` no longer looks inside a composition host (`data-composition-id`, `data-composition-src` or `data-composition-file`). A composition clip gets no source length and is trimmed freely. A plain wrapper around one video still takes its length from that video. Composition thumbnails are unaffected: they key on `compositionSrc`, which is set separately. An inline composition (no source file) used to get its thumbnail from that same lookup when its only media was an image; the inline branch that already exposed an inner video for thumbnails now exposes an inner image too.

## Tests

In `timelineDOM.test.ts`, a scene composition holding a 1.77 s video next to a wrapper clip holding a 4 s video:

- Parsed from the DOM, the scene has no source length and no video tag. The wrapper keeps 4 s.
- An end trim of the 18 s scene gives 16.5 s through `computeResizePreview`, not the video's length.
- Built from the runtime manifest, the scene has no source length or src.
- An inline composition holding only an image still gets that image as its thumbnail. Reverting the inline branch to video only fails this test alone.

With the fix, `timelineDOM.test.ts` and `timelineClipDragPreview.test.ts` pass, 39 of 39. On the previous helper, exactly the three new tests fail (the other tests pass). oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. oxfmt: clean. Studio typecheck: clean.

## Before

Studio dev server, one 18 s scene composition whose template holds a 1.8 s video. Drag the scene's right edge 60 px left (about 2.7 s), then reload. The scene is saved as 1.8 s long.

![Before: after the trim the scene is a 1.8 s sliver on the timeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64bdca0d-fdf8-4ed9-8c10-3718adde5696)

## After

Same steps with this change: the scene is saved as 15.33 s long and keeps its thumbnails.

![After: the scene is 15.33 s long with its thumbnails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1df331a8-bb34-4481-854e-23a3b3c6c651)

title: fix(core): a preview that is never seeked shows only the clips of its current time
body:
## What changes for a user

A preview that nobody has seeked yet now shows only the clips that belong at its current time. Before, a page loaded on its own published `__renderReady` with every caption and every composition host visible at once, and stayed that way until something called `seek`. Anything that captures the page as it loads (a poster, a thumbnail, an app's frame grab, a plain browser tab) saw every caption stacked on top of each other.

## Why

The timed-element visibility pass (`syncTimedElementVisibility`) only runs from the media sync, which seek, pause and play call, and which the transport loop calls only while playing or while timed media is running. At init it runs once for `video[data-start]` and `img[data-start]` only, for color grading. A paused page that is never seeked therefore never hides its out-of-window captions and composition hosts.

Readiness now runs that pass for every non-media timed element right before it sets `__renderReady`, so readiness means the current frame is placed. Media stays with its existing init pass and with seeks. Running the full pass here instead of excluding media made two existing tests fail: it allocated color grading a second time, and it consumed the hidden-audio flag that Web Audio scheduling reschedules on.

One existing assertion changes. `allocates color grading only for the active timed media` pinned a composition host that starts at 2 s to `visibility: ""` and `display: ""` right after init at 0 s. That was the bug itself: the host is now `hidden` / `none`, the same values a seek to 0 writes. The color-grading allocation count it guards is unchanged (one context).

## Before

![main: never-seeked page at 0 s shows every caption and the 5 s card](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/feb32868-f6b4-4f2f-b8b2-7fccfdbd877d)

## After

![fix: never-seeked page at 0 s shows only the 0 s caption](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d33ffc18-a717-4904-9b59-1babb0220ce7)

Fixture: three captions timed at 0 s, 5 s and 10 s plus a card at 5 s, served by the Studio preview route, screenshot 2 s after `__renderReady` with no seek. Before: all four clips are visible at 0 s. After: only the 0 s caption.

## What I measured

- `src/runtime/init.test.ts` adds two tests: a page that is never seeked publishes readiness with an out-of-window clip hidden, and a seek made before readiness followed by clips mounted before readiness ends up painted at the sought time. Both fail on main (the clips were never touched by the pass) and pass here.
- Removing the readiness pass fails exactly those two tests plus the updated color-grading assertion.
- `packages/core` `src/runtime`: exit 0, 59 files, 1299 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. `oxfmt --check` exit 0.
- A real 50 s launch film with 14 captions and 16 sub-compositions, a plain tab with no seek, visible captions at 1, 4 and 8 s: main 14, 14, 14; this branch 0, 0, 0. The never-seeked frame on this branch is pixel-identical to main's frame after an explicit `seek(0)`.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A page that is playing when readiness publishes a second time (for example after a late `hf-timelines-built`). The pass writes the same visibility the playing loop writes each frame, but I did not measure it during playback.
- Render export frames. The engine seeks every frame after readiness, and that seek runs the full visibility pass, but I did not diff a render before and after this change.
- A separate cause of stale frames in one app's capture path (a hidden window that does not repaint after a seek) belongs to that app and is not touched here.

title: fix(registry): glass-shard-title renders when mounted, and 4 skipped blocks install again
body:
## What changes for a user

- `glass-shard-title` shows its glass headline when it is mounted into a film, in Studio's preview and in snapshots. Before, it was blank: its HDR environment 404'd and the scene never started.
- Opened on its own with `?play`, the block loads its script and fonts instead of 404ing them.
- `hyperframes catalog` no longer skips `liquid-glass-notification`, `liquid-glass-widgets`, `lt-neon-border` and `vfx-iphone-device` as "Invalid registry manifest", so they can be listed and added again.

## Why

Three things stacked up for the glass block:

1. `glass-main.js` loaded `"assets/ferndale_studio_01_1k.hdr"` and `"assets/matcap-1.png"` as strings. A mounted block runs in the film's document, and the compiler rebases only `src`/`href` attributes of a mounted composition (`rewriteAssetPaths`, `packages/parsers/src/rewriteSubCompPaths.ts`), never strings inside a script. So the path resolved against the film root.
2. The block's head carried `document.write('<base href="../">')` for `?play`. The manifest installs every asset next to the block file, so under `?play` that base sent the script and fonts to `compositions/assets/…`. In Studio the text alone did harm too: the preview route adds its own `<base href="/api/projects/<id>/preview/">` only when the page has no `"<base"` in it (`packages/studio-server/src/routes/preview.ts:385`). The string inside the script matched, Studio skipped its base, and every relative asset that the bundler does not inline as data (the 1.6 MB hdr, the 3 MB matcap) resolved under `/api/projects/<id>/` and 404'd. That is the 404 qa2 saw.
3. The four manifests used file types outside the published schema (`registry:asset`, `asset`, and `hyperframes:block` as a file type), and `lt-neon-border`'s file had no `target`. The CLI validates every manifest against that schema and drops the ones that fail. Nothing in CI ran the repo's own manifests through that validator.

## How

- `glass-shard-title.html` declares the two files as `<link rel="preload" id="gst-hdr|gst-matcap">` inside the composition root. `glass-main.mjs` and the bundled `glass-main.js` read `document.getElementById(...).href`. Mounted, the compiler rebases the href. Standalone, the browser resolves it next to the page. The preload also starts the 3 MB matcap download earlier.
- The `?play` `<base>` line is removed.
- `glass-main.js` is edited at exactly the two call sites, matching the `.mjs`. A rebuild with esbuild and three r185 does not reproduce the committed bundle byte for byte, so a rebuild would have replaced 550 KB of unrelated code.
- `scripts/catalog-script-inlining.ts`: the docs payload no longer rewrites the hdr path inside the script. The payload build inlines the `<link>` href as a data URL and points the matcap at its CDN copy through the generic asset path. The glass step now inlines the script, and throws if the hdr path is still in the payload (tested for both quote styles).
- The four manifests use `hyperframes:asset` / `hyperframes:composition`, and `lt-neon-border` gets `target: compositions/lt-neon-border.html`, the path its docs page already tells users to mount.
- `packages/cli/src/registry/validation.test.ts` runs every `registry-item.json` in the repo through the CLI's own `validRegistryItem`. On `main` it fails and names exactly the four items above.

## Before

Studio (`hyperframes preview`, published 0.8.72), block installed from `main`, playhead at 00:03:

![main: Studio preview of the mounted block is blank at 00:03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61745923-46ed-4d5a-98a6-86afe500d607)

## After

The same, block installed from this branch:

![branch: Studio preview shows the glass shards and the headline at 00:03](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1a3f75d-9f40-46f5-b0e9-da7429f5e29a)

## Verification

- Studio, main vs branch (headless Chrome, software WebGL, published CLI 0.8.72 serving the project): main requests `/api/projects/<id>/assets/ferndale_studio_01_1k.hdr` → 404 plus a page error. The branch requests the hdr and matcap from `/api/projects/<id>/preview/compositions/glass-shard-title/assets/…` → 200, with no page errors.
- `?play` (static server, the installed block file): main 404s `compositions/assets/glass-main.js` and two Geist fonts. The branch has no 404s.
- `hyperframes snapshot` of the mounted block at 3 s and 6 s: main blank, branch shows the shards. The block's own catalog preview is black at 9 s and 11 s too, so those frames are not a regression.
- `hyperframes catalog` against `main` skips the four items. Against this branch it skips none.
- `validation.test.ts` 4 passed. With `main`'s four manifests restored, 1 failed listing exactly those four. `catalog-script-inlining.test.ts` 6 passed. Turning the guard off, or going back to a quote-sensitive check, fails the new test. `catalog-drift.ts` exit 0; derived catalog files are left to the publish PR, as it says.

Independent review, three rounds, final head: no blocking or should-fix findings. Round 1 asked whether Studio's live preview mounts blocks through the client runtime loader (which only rebases `../` paths). The Studio measurement above shows the server-side bundler path serves it, and round 2 confirmed that from the code. Round 2's two should-fix items (the hdr guard had no test, and its check depended on quote style) are fixed and pinned by the new test.

## What I did NOT exercise

- `hyperframes render` on its own. This block also needs the render-compiler fix on `fix/render-local-script-order` (its PR follows), which keeps a mounted composition's local script after the inline script that sets it up. With both, a render draws the shards:

![render with this branch and the render-compiler fix: the headline assembled at 3 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ee58289-7ec0-481e-aa4c-c1f5d2b0d29d)

- `hyperframes check` loses its page ("Target closed") on this block once WebGL starts, on the unmodified block opened standalone too, so its sweep verdicts are not usable either way.
- Other blocks that build `assets/...` paths inside scripts (for example `canopy-part-title`, `wireframe-portal-title`, `frost-sequence-camera-orbit`) are not changed here.

title: fix(studio): a ruler label that slides under the track header is hidden, not sliced
body:
## What

Once a timeline scroll settles, the ruler time label that the track header would slice is covered, so the ruler never rests on a fragment like "0:05" or "0".

Trade-off, chosen for scroll performance: while a scroll is in progress, a fragment can still show, as it does today. Within about 100ms of the scroll stopping, it is covered.

## Why

The ruler's track-header corner is sticky and opaque, and the tick labels scroll natively underneath it. Nothing hid a label that was only partly covered, so the visible part stayed next to the header.

## How

- `TimelineRuler` renders one small mask, `HeaderSlicedLabelMask`. It subscribes to the timeline viewport's scroll through `useSyncExternalStore`, with no effect. It binary-searches the one major tick whose label starts under the header, and paints the ruler background over that label's text band, which stops at the next tick.
- The mask is removed when a scroll starts and placed when it settles. `TIMELINE_SCROLL_SETTLE_MS` (100ms) is now exported from `useTimelineScrollViewport.ts`, which already used that value for its own settle, so both read one constant.
- The label list and tick marks render exactly as on main.

Why not live while scrolling: on the timeline viewport gate's large, unvirtualized arm, any change to the ruler's DOM each time a label crosses the edge cost 2 to 3 times the frame and interaction budget. I measured a scroll CSS variable, per-label scroll-driven animations, a re-rendered label list, and a mask moved plainly, in a contained layer, and by transform on its own layer. The subscription alone costs nothing; the per-crossing DOM change is what costs.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TimelineRuler.test.tsx`: scroll a real element to 204, then 205, around the 10s label's edge (204.5). There is no mask while scrolling; after the settle, the mask sits over 00:00, then over 00:10. Making the mask never render fails it (exit 1). A second test swaps the scroll element mid-scroll: the mask must not stay off. It failed before the reset in the unsubscribe (exit 1). The file: exit 0, 2 passed.
- [x] `Timeline.virtualization.test.tsx` (10 passed) and `useTimelineGeometry.test.tsx` (2 passed), each exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- [x] Real Studio in headless Chromium, 1200x733, a registry example at 200% zoom, scrolled 166px. The "00:05" label straddles the header edge; after the scroll settles, the mask covers its whole box.
- [x] Timeline viewport gate, unvirtualized arm, run interleaved with main on a shared machine. Live variants: frame p95 50-133ms and interaction 90-192ms, against main's 33ms and 65-86ms (budget 75). The subscription alone: 33ms and 65-79ms, the same as main. On this head, CI's gate passes: the unvirtualized arm has frame p95 17-33ms and interaction 38-59ms (budget 75), and the default arm has frame 17ms and interaction 33ms.

### Before

main: the "00:05" label is sliced to "0:05" at the header edge.

![main: 00:05 sliced to 0:05 at the track header edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cefeb786-cde3-4272-bd9f-fd9575a9bd24)

### After

this branch, at rest after the scroll: the partial label is covered, and "00:10" onward are unchanged.

![fix: at rest, the sliced label is covered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb2807e8-dadd-4a3f-8564-14c3c2b3e9d3)

## Review

Independent adversarial review of the first head: blocking none. It checked the geometry (contentOrigin cancels between the corner and the label), the virtualized ruler (its overscan covers the needed tick), and the `useSyncExternalStore` wiring (numeric snapshot, no tearing, and the ref is attached before subscribe). One should-fix: unsubscribing mid-scroll left the "scrolling" flag set, so the mask could stay off. It is fixed in the second commit, with a regression test. Notes: the mask reads the live `scrollLeft`, while the virtualized tick window follows its own rAF-throttled state; and the last tick's mask is 80px wide.

title: fix(producer): a mounted composition's local script runs after the inline script before it
body:
## What changes for a user

A film that mounts a block whose local script depends on the block's own setup script now renders. Before, `hyperframes render` ran the block's `<script src>` before the inline script written above it, so the block threw and rendered a flat frame. `glass-shard-title` hit this: `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'st')`, because `window.__GST` was not set yet. Studio's preview was not affected; it already ran them in order.

## Why

When the render compiler inlines a mounted composition (`inlineSubCompositions` in `packages/producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`), it put every external script of that composition first and appended all its inline scripts afterwards as one block. That ordering exists so CDN libraries (GSAP plugins and similar) register before composition code runs. It also moved project-local scripts, which can depend on the inline script before them. The preview bundler (`packages/core/src/compiler/htmlBundler.ts`) already keeps local scripts in authored order and moves only integrity-pinned and non-relative scripts first, so preview and render disagreed.

#4133 fixed the same shape for scripts in the root document. This is the mounted-composition path.

## How

- Integrity-pinned and non-relative (CDN) scripts still go first, as before.
- Then the composition's scripts are emitted in authored order: consecutive inline scripts batched into one `<script>` (the per-instance variables script leading, as before), and each local `<script src>` at its own place between them.
- Same rule as the preview bundler: `integrity || isNonRelativeUrl(src)` is what moves first.

## Before

`hyperframes render` (published 0.8.72) of a film mounting `glass-shard-title`, frame at 3 s:

![main: the render is a flat frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58b88e3-5d9a-437f-bfc5-f0be19048210)

## After

The same film rendered with this branch (and the block's asset fix, #4423), frame at 3 s:

![branch: the glass headline is assembled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca8565b4-50fd-42e4-b95f-3d070658ce4e)

## Verification

- `htmlCompiler.scriptOrder.test.ts`: a new test mounts a composition with inline → local src → inline and checks the order. It fails on `main` (the src script lands ahead of the inline one) and passes here. A second new test checks that a mounted composition's CDN script still lands before its inline scripts (fetch stubbed). Each direction of mutation (move every script first / move none first) turns exactly one of the two red.
- `htmlCompiler.test.ts` (bun) 136 pass, `htmlCompiler.parity.test.ts` 9 pass. Typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- A real render of the glass film from this branch's CLI: no page errors, and the shards fly in (1 s), assemble (2 s) and settle into the headline (3 s). The published CLI renders the same film flat.

Independent review of this head: no blocking or should-fix findings. It confirmed that the inline script content is byte-identical to what was emitted before, that nothing else in the producer relied on everything being hoisted, and that the later coalescing and CDN-inlining steps do not cross the new boundaries. Two notes, both unchanged by this PR and shared with preview: a composition mounted twice runs a shared local `<script src>` once (tags dedupe by `src`), and a newly created tag carries only `integrity`/`crossorigin`, not `type="module"`.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio and preview: unchanged code path, not re-walked.
- Distributed or Lambda render modes: they call the same compiler, but I did not run them.

title: fix(studio-server): preview keeps its base URL when a script mentions a <base> tag
body:
## What changes for a user

Studio's preview keeps loading a composition's files when one of its scripts merely mentions a `<base>` tag. Before, any page whose text contained `<base` (for example a script doing `document.write('<base href="../">')` for a standalone mode) lost Studio's own base URL. Every relative asset the bundler does not inline as data (large images, `.hdr`, models) then resolved one level too high and 404'd.

## Why

The preview route adds `<base href="/api/projects/<id>/preview/">` only when the page does not have one already, and it decided that with `bundled.includes("<base")` (`packages/studio-server/src/routes/preview.ts`). Text inside a script matched. The sub-composition preview (`helpers/subComposition.ts`) made the same check over the project's `index.html` head. This is what made `glass-shard-title`'s environment map 404 in Studio (#4423 removes that block's line; this fixes the check for any composition).

## How

`hasBaseElement(html)` in `helpers/subComposition.ts` asks the HTML parser (linkedom, already used in that file) for a real `<base>` element, so text inside scripts, comments and `<template>` does not count. Both call sites use it. An authored `<base>` still wins, as before. It costs about 6 ms on a 750 KB preview page, and the route is cached by ETag.

## Verification

- `preview.test.ts`: a page whose head script mentions `<base href="../">` now gets the preview base, and a page with an authored `<base href="/cdn/">` keeps its own. With the old `includes("<base")` the first assertion fails; with a helper that never finds a base, the second fails. 53 pass.
- `subComposition.test.ts`: the same script-mention case through the sub-composition preview (fails with the old check at that site), plus `hasBaseElement` edge cases: `</script >`, a comment, `<template>` content, `<basefont>`, and an uppercase `<BASE>`. 14 pass.
- studio-server helper tests 334 pass, typecheck and oxlint clean.
- In Studio itself (published 0.8.72, headless Chrome), the glass block's page is where I first saw it: the served page had no base element, and the hdr request went to `/api/projects/<id>/compositions/...` → 404. The same file is served at `/api/projects/<id>/preview/compositions/...` → 200.

Independent review, three rounds, final head: no blocking or should-fix findings. Round 1 asked for a test at the second call site (added). The first version used a regex; CodeQL flagged it (slow on repeated `<!--`, missed `</script >`), so it now uses the parser, and CodeQL passes. No other naive `"<base"` check remains in the repo.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A Studio build from this branch walked in a browser. The route tests drive the real Hono routes; the Studio walk above is on the published build with the block-side fix.
- A `<base>` inside `<noscript>` still counts, because the parser treats `<noscript>` content as markup. Nothing in the repo does that.

title: feat(cli): warn when canvas content touches the frame edge
body:
## What changes for the person running `hyperframes check`

`check` now warns when a `<canvas>` shows sharp content along the frame edge:

```
⚠ canvas_content_at_edge #tc-canvas: Canvas content touches the frame edge (left, right).
  Fix: Keep drawn text inside the visible part of the canvas, or mark intentional full-bleed art with data-layout-allow-overflow.
```

Before, text drawn *into* a canvas and cut off by the frame passed `check` silently. Layout inspection measures DOM boxes, and canvas pixels have none, so `canvas_overflow` never saw them. A real launch film shipped its closing headline "THANKS FOR WATCHING" as "…KS FOR WAT…" this way.

## How it decides

For each visible canvas that reaches a frame edge, it reads a 4px band just inside that edge. It draws the band into a scratch canvas, the same way the frozen-sweep fingerprint already reads media pixels, so the film's own canvas never gets a new context. Along the edge it counts sharp steps in brightness or alpha. Two or more steps mean content is cut by the edge.

- Drawn text and hard shapes crossing the edge fire.
- Smooth full-bleed gradients stay silent.
- Busy full-bleed art (particle fields, photos drawn into a canvas) can fire. `data-layout-allow-overflow` on the canvas silences it, the same opt-out every other edge finding uses.
- A hit at a single sample demotes to info, like the other edge findings, so a transient crossing does not warn.
- It is a warning: it gates only under `--strict`.

## What I measured

Real runs of `check` with this branch:

| Project | Result |
|---|---|
| The launch film's closing scene (`--at 51.5,52.089`) | warning on the headline canvas, held across both samples; at 52.089s alone it names both left and right |
| Full-bleed linear gradient canvas | silent |
| Particle field (4000 dots) | warning on all four edges |
| The same particle field with `data-layout-allow-overflow` | silent |
| Canvas at `transform: scale(1.25)`, bars crossing the visible left edge | warning, left |
| The same scaled canvas, bars only in the part the scale pushes off-screen | silent |

- `layout-audit.browser.test.ts`: 134 passed, exit 0. `utils/layoutAudit.test.ts`: 39 passed, exit 0. `commands/check.test.ts`: 61 passed, exit 0. The commit hooks pass: typecheck, fallow, lint, format and skills manifest.
- Each new test is pinned by a mutation that turns it red:

| Mutation | Tests that fail |
|---|---|
| Step count raised out of reach | both "fires" tests |
| Step threshold dropped to 1 | the gradient test |
| Band narrowed to 1px | the glyph-gap test (bitmap and monospace glyph cells end in a gap, so the outermost column alone reads empty; that is how the real headline was first missed) |
| Opt-out removed | the opt-out test |
| Edge coverage forced on | the canvas-inside-the-frame test |
| Right edge reads the left band | the test that names only the edge holding the content |

## What I did NOT exercise

- WebGL canvases. A WebGL canvas without `preserveDrawingBuffer` reads blank through `drawImage`, so it never fires: a known blind spot.
- Rotated or skewed canvases. The band is mapped through the canvas's bounding box: exact for scale and translate (measured above), wrong under rotation or skew.
- A shape flush in a frame corner (a badge drawn into the corner) crosses each edge only once, which is below the two-step bar, so it is not flagged. The bar is two so that a canvas split into a dark half and a bright half does not warn.
- Across samples, the merged finding keeps the first sample's message. If the right edge only gets cut at a later sample, the merged line can name only "left".
- Canvases inside iframes. They are outside the audit's document, as for every other layout finding.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, two rounds.

First round: no blockers, three majors.
1. The tests could not catch a band read from the wrong edge. Fixed: the test stub now serves ink only for the band drawn from a named source origin, and a new test pins "(right)".
2. "Any CSS scale breaks the mapping." Disproved with the two scaled-canvas runs above. The comment now names rotation and skew as the ceiling.
3. The corner-shape limit. Documented above.

Second round: no blockers, no majors. It reran both scaled-canvas fixtures with matching output, and checked the mapping by hand for non-uniform scale and an off-centre transform origin.

title: fix(player): a play() made while the composition loads still plays
body:
## What changes for a user

`player.play()` called while a composition is still loading now plays. Before, on a same-origin composition (any `srcdoc` player) whose assets were still loading, a `play()` made after the first `ready` and before the iframe's own `load` event was dropped: the player stayed paused at 0 with no error and no `play` event.

Also new: `assets-loading-ui="none"` turns off the player's "Loading assets" card for hosts that draw their own loading state. Every asset signal still fires.

## Why the play was lost

`play()` before assets settle queues the intent in `_pendingPlay`. The iframe's `load` event runs `_onIframeLoad`, which resets the asset wait through `_invalidateAssetsWait()`, and that reset also cleared `_pendingPlay`. When the second `ready` arrived, nothing was queued.

The cause is that play intent lived inside the asset-wait reset. It no longer does: `_invalidateAssetsWait` only resets the asset wait. The shared teardown the five navigation sites repeated moves into `_abandonComposition`, and the queued play is cleared only where the caller's intent really ends.

| Site | Clears the queued play? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pause()` | yes (unchanged) | the caller stopped playback |
| `seek()` | yes (unchanged) | a seek lands paused by contract |
| `disconnectedCallback` | yes | the element is gone |
| live `src` change | yes | a different composition; like a `<video>` given a new `src`, it does not inherit a pending play |
| live `srcdoc` change | yes | same as `src` |
| iframe `load` (`_onIframeLoad`) | **no** (this was the bug) | the same document finishing its load, not a navigation |
| sandbox-policy reload | **no** (changed) | reloads the same composition because an attribute changed; the caller did not navigate |
| shader-options reload (`shader-loading`, `shader-capture-scale`, `runtime-src`) | **no** (changed) | same as the sandbox reload |
| `play()` itself | sets / clears (unchanged) | queues while not ready, clears once it starts |

## Before

![Before: play() made during load is dropped, player paused at 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09bb94ff-322e-4cb8-9cab-b3968ee3de52)

## After

![After: the same play() plays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5afbab0-8b3b-4f74-9ebf-c4a33b134bb7)

Real browser, the built player bundle with a local runtime (`runtime-src`), a `srcdoc` composition whose image the server holds back for 3 s, and `play()` called on the first `ready`. Screenshot 6.5 s later. Before: `paused: true`, time 0.00, events `ready, play() called, ready, assetsready, painted` and no `play`. After: playing at 6.2 s, and the `play` event fired.

## `assets-loading-ui`

| Attribute | Values | Default | Property |
|---|---|---|---|
| `assets-loading-ui` | `player`, `none` | `player` | `assetsLoadingUi` |

Why this shape: the player already has `shader-loading` with values `composition | player | none`, where `none` suppresses that loader, so this uses the same vocabulary and the same enum-plus-property pattern. The name `assets-loading` was not available: it is already the host attribute that reflects the loading state and that hosts style on. With `none`, the card is never shown, a live switch to `none` hides a card that is already up (only the card, see below), and `assets-loading`, `assetsready` and `painted` behave exactly as before. Documented in the player README's attribute table (plus a short section) and on the docs player page.

## The loading card and a shader load share one panel

The "Loading assets" card and the shader-transition progress overlay draw into the same panel, and on main each could take down the other: assets settling hid a shader load still in progress (it came back on the next progress message, so it flickered), and any shader message that draws nothing (`loading: false`, `ready`, or `shader-loading` other than `player`) hid or wiped a card that was still waiting on assets. The panel now remembers which of the two drew it, and each only hides its own. A consequence: when assets settle under a live shader load, `painted` fires once the shader load is gone, since until then the frame is still covered.

| Default (`player`) | `assets-loading-ui="none"` |
|---|---|
| ![Loading assets card up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aeac45b6-e909-41d2-a899-09af28edd58f) | ![No card, the composition's own frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/060fe729-8b54-441b-b877-ecd2813e89d2) |

Same page with a 3 s video in the composition, 1.5 s after load, `play()` already queued. Left: default, the card is up. Right: `assets-loading-ui="none"`, the composition's own frame. Both start playing once the video lands.

## What I measured

- `packages/player/src/hyperframes-player.test.ts` adds six tests: the repro (play queued before a same-origin iframe load plays once the wait settles), a new `srcdoc` drops a queued play, a shader-options reload keeps it, `none` never raises the card while `assets-loading`, `assetsready` and `painted` still happen, a live switch to `none` hides a card that is up, the same switch leaves a shader-transition load that took over the panel on screen, and assets settling leaves a live shader load up with `painted` waiting for it. `shader-loader-state.test.ts` adds two: the card switch hides only the card, and shader messages that draw nothing leave the card up. Against main's player and loader sources 7 of these 9 fail. Two pass on both: the `srcdoc` one pins unchanged behaviour, and on main the card switch cannot hide a shader load because the attribute does not exist.
- Mutations, each run: putting the clear back into `_invalidateAssetsWait` fails exactly the two intent tests. Removing the `srcdoc` clear fails only its test. Ignoring the attribute in the card timer fails only the `none` test. Dropping the live hide fails only its test. Hiding the panel whoever drew it fails exactly the two switch tests. Putting the plain hide back on assets settle fails only the settle test. Dropping the shader-message guard fails only its loader test.
- `packages/player`: exit 0, 14 files, 406 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0. `oxfmt --check` exit 0 on every changed file.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The opaque-origin path (`allow-same-origin` absent): `_onIframeLoad` returns early there when ready, as before, and its existing test is unchanged.
- Hosts that call `play()` and then change `shader-loading` mid-load: covered by a unit test, not in a browser.
- Switching `assets-loading-ui` back to `player` while a wait is already showing nothing does not redraw the card; the next wait does.

title: snapshot --at renders on a 30 fps grid instead of the exact time
body:
## Summary

`hyperframes snapshot --at <t>` does not seek to the exact time `<t>` — it renders the state for `floor(t * 30) / 30`, a 30 fps grid, regardless of the project's own declared `data-fps`. On a project with `data-fps` below 30 (the common NTSC-derived 29.97 case), this silently renders the wrong instant by up to 1/30 s (≈33 ms).

## Numeric proof (research on `hyperframes-ae-mcp`, corpus row `long-shadow-titles`, `data-fps="29.97"`)

Four independent back-solves against an AE-rendered reference frame all landed on the same ~0.019 s offset:

- Root time requested: **19.019018 s** (AE frame 126 at 29.97 fps, i.e. AE's own frame boundary for that instant).
- `hyperframes snapshot --at 19.019018` actually rendered the state for **19.000 s** (sample 125.43 of a 29.97 fps composition), not 19.019.
- The back-solved sample values from the four independent measurements: **125.42–125.46**, all clustering just below sample 125.5 (19.000 s), while AE's own reference measured **125.99–126.03** (19.019 s) — a constant **~0.019 s (0.57 of a 29.97 fps frame)** offset, in every case.

## Step 1 reproduction (AE-free, CLI 0.8.72, this issue's own isolated measurement)

Built a synthetic project (`data-fps="29.97"`, one `.clip` element with a linear GSAP tween `ease:"none"` moving at exactly 1000 px/s, so the rendered x position back-solves the exact instant the runtime rendered) and swept `--at` across several 1/30 s boundaries. Measured the element's left edge in each PNG:

| `--at` requested (s) | rendered as (s) | back-solved from pixels |
|---|---|---|
| 1.0190 | 1.0000 | left = 1000 → t = 1.000 |
| 1.0333 | 1.0000 | left = 1000 → t = 1.000 |
| 1.0500 | 1.0333 | left = 1033 → t = 1.033 |
| 1.0667 | 1.0667 | left = 1067 → t = 1.067 |
| 2.3457 | 2.3333 | left = 2333 → t = 2.333 |
| 19.000000 | 19.0000 | left = 1900 → t = 19.000 |
| 19.019018 | 19.0000 | left = 1900 → t = 19.000 |
| 19.038000 | 19.0333 | left = 1903 → t = 19.033 |
| 19.050000 | 19.0333 | left = 1903 → t = 19.033 (byte-identical to 19.038) |
| 19.066700 | 19.0667 | left = 1907 → t = 19.067 |

This exactly reproduces the plan's back-solve (19.019018 → 19.000, not 19.019) and confirms the rule is **floor to the nearest 1/30 s**, not round-to-nearest and not the project's own 29.97 fps grid: 19.05 s (571.5/30, past the half-frame boundary) still floors down to 571/30 = 19.0333, which a round-to-nearest rule would not do.

## Ask

Either:
1. Make `--at` seek to the exact requested time (no quantization), or
2. Document the quantization explicitly and add a `--fps` (or similar) flag so a caller can request the project's own frame grid instead of a hardcoded 30.

Right now `snapshot --help` on 0.8.72 documents `--at`, `--frames`, `--no-end` with no mention of any seek grid, so a caller has no way to know `--at` is quantized at all.

## Environment

- `hyperframes --version`: 0.8.72
- Reproduced with `--no-browser-gpu --no-end --describe false`

title: feat(studio-server): every write to a project is kept in a history that can be undone or restored
body:
## What this gives you

Every change to a project's files is kept automatically, whoever made it: an edit in Studio, an agent working on
the project, a tool call, or an editor outside the app. Any change can be undone later, and the project can be put
back to how it was at any point. Nobody has to take a snapshot or ask for one.

This PR is the engine and its API. Hosts wire it in next (the CLI preview and Studio's Cmd+Z), in follow-up PRs.

## How it works

- **Capture.** When a project opens, the engine stores a copy of every project file by its sha256, outside the
  project (clones on file systems that support them, so this is close to free on APFS). After that, every write is
  taken in by a sweep: a stat per file, and a hash only when the stat moved.
- **Who made it.** A writer opens a window (`beginWindow(who, label)`) around its writes; everything written until
  `close()` is one entry of theirs. Writes with no window open are grouped into one "Changed outside the app" entry
  after 2 s of quiet (30 s at most). Overlapping windows give a write to the newest one.
- **Entries** are `{ id, who, label, startedAt, endedAt, files: [{ path, before, after }] }`, where before and after
  are hashes and `null` means the file did not exist, so creates and deletes undo like any edit. The log is
  append-only JSONL beside the stored bytes.
- **Undo, redo, restore** are plain file writes, and each one is a new entry, so nothing is ever lost: redo is
  undoing the undo. `step("back" | "forward")` is Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z in time order, whoever made the change.
- **Conflicts.** If a file changed after the entry being undone, undo writes nothing and returns the files and the
  newer entries. The caller then picks `just-this` (put back this entry's files only) or `back-to-before` (return the
  whole project to the point before this entry, as one new entry).
- **Peek and pin.** `peek(point)` returns the files at a point without writing anything; `pin` keeps an entry.
- **Retention.** Past a byte budget (default 2 GB per project), the oldest entries are folded into the baseline and
  bytes nothing needs any more are deleted. Folding stops at the first pinned entry.
- **Stable id.** A project's history is keyed by an id kept in `.hyperframes/history-id`, so renaming or moving the
  folder keeps its history, and a copy of the folder starts a history of its own.

Which files count as the project is the same set the preview signature already uses (`listProjectFiles`, beside
`createProjectSignature`), so Studio's manual-edit and motion manifests in `.hyperframes/` are covered, and caches,
renders and `node_modules` are not.

## API

`openProjectHistory({ projectDir, historyRoot })` returns `beginWindow`, `noteChange` (for a file watcher), `list`,
`step`, `undo`, `restore`, `peek`, `readBlob`, `pin`, `onEntry`, `flush` and `close`. `createStudioApi` gains
`/projects/:id/history` routes (list, step, undo, restore, peek, pin, and edit windows) when the host's adapter
provides the new optional `history(project)`; without it they answer 404.

## Decisions worth a look

- **A stat is trusted only once the file is at least 2 s old** (git's "racily clean" rule). Linux timestamps tick
  coarsely, so a same-size rewrite inside one tick keeps its size, mtime and ctime. The tests caught exactly that.
  Files changed in the last 2 s are re-hashed on each sweep.
- **A missing project folder is a move, not an empty project.** A sweep of a folder that is gone records nothing,
  rather than "every file deleted".
- **A watcher report triggers a full sweep,** not a sweep of the reported path. Watchers report a deleted folder by
  its own name, not by the files inside it.
- The existing per-file backups in `.hyperframes/backup` are left alone here. A follow-up moves their one consumer
  (the timeline undo receipts) onto this engine and removes them.

## Tests

`src/history/projectHistory.test.ts` and `src/routes/history.test.ts` (11 tests): automatic capture of an
unannounced write, undo and redo of text and binary files, a window's create, delete and manifest edit, the
conflict and both of its choices, restore and peek, a move plus a reopen plus a copy, retention with a pin, a history
folder removed while open, and a damaged log line. The full studio-server suite passes.

Two robustness cases are covered because a review found them. If the history folder is removed while a project is
open, the next write recreates it and rewrites the whole log from memory, so a restart still has every entry. A
damaged line in the middle of the log is reported through `onError` rather than dropped silently; a torn last line
from a crash is still dropped quietly.

title: fix(cli): the block snippet from add carries the block's own composition id
body:
## What changes for a user

The include snippet that `hyperframes add <block>` prints now works as pasted. It carries the `data-composition-id` the block's own file declares, so the block passes lint and renders as authored. Before, the snippet had no id: `hyperframes lint` flagged the host, and a block like `code-snippet-dark-modern` rendered with its wallpaper black.

## Why

A host needs `data-composition-id` equal to the id on the mounted file's root (inside its `<template>` when it has one). Assembly only flattens the file into the host on that exact match (`packages/core/src/compiler/compositionAssembly.ts`). The snippet omitted the id. Using the registry name would also be wrong: 35 blocks declare a different root id, for example `code-snippet-dark-modern` declares `vscode-dark-modern`.

## How

- `compositionRootId(html)` in `packages/cli/src/commands/add.ts` reads the id the way core does: the first `<template>`'s content if there is one, else the document, then the first `[data-composition-id]`. `runAdd` reads the file it just installed and passes that id to `buildSnippet`.
- If the installed block declares no root id, `add` now warns instead of silently printing a snippet that fails lint. No registry block hits this today (172 of 172 declare one).
- `add <tag> --json` dropped every item's warnings. It now reports them, each prefixed with the item name.

## Verification

- `add.test.ts`, 28 pass:
  - a lint-backed test: the snippet host passes `lintHyperframeHtml`;
  - root id from a templated file, a plain file, and a file with none;
  - a `runAdd` integration test expecting the installed file's id on the snippet;
  - the missing-id warning;
  - `tagAddJson`.
  Removing the warning fails exactly its assertion; dropping `warnings` from the tag JSON fails exactly its test.
- CLI from source against the real registry: `code-snippet-dark-modern` → `vscode-dark-modern`, `vfx-magnetic` → `magnetic-cursor`, `glass-shard-title` → `glass-shard-title`. A script over every registry block found a root id in each.
- `tsc -p packages/cli` clean.

### Before

`code-snippet-dark-modern` mounted with main's snippet (no id): the wallpaper renders black.

![main snippet, no id](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92a6ff25-5ab1-4954-8e90-61e64efc1d46)

### After

The same block mounted with this branch's snippet: rendered as authored.

![branch snippet, root id](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d9cc1422-8b59-4146-809a-6be8a6dd8c11)

Independent review, three rounds; the final head has no blocking findings. Round 1 found the registry-name approach wrong for 35 blocks (fixed as above). Later rounds asked for the missing-id warning (added) and flagged the tag `--json` gap (fixed).

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio's block installer and the catalog page generator put the registry name in `data-composition-id` too. That is separate code; I measured no visible symptom there, and it is not changed here.
- A live `hyperframes add <tag> --json` run; the JSON is covered by the unit test.

title: feat(cli): render --require-version turns a version pin into a gate
body:
Adds `render --require-version X.Y.Z`: refuse to render unless the running
renderer is exactly that version.

## Why a pin is not enough

`npx hyperframes@X.Y.Z` stops the renderer drifting between runs, but nothing
checks the claim afterwards. A project states the version it believes it used
and no artifact can contradict it.

The provenance tag does not close the gap either. `hyperframes_version` stamped
a constant `0.0.0-dev` for twenty published versions (#4365) — measured across
710 tagged mp4s, 710 carry that value, so the tag identifies nothing. #4409
fixes the stamp, which makes drift VISIBLE once a fixed build ships. This makes
it ENFORCEABLE at the point it matters, before the encode.

## Three properties

1. **Fails closed on an unresolved version.** If the engine cannot say what it
   is, the gate cannot verify anything, and passing would hand back exactly the
   unfalsifiable claim the flag exists to remove — while looking green. It
   compares against the engine's exported `UNRESOLVED_VERSION` rather than a
   re-typed literal.
2. **Exact, never a range.** npm already gives the caller ranges. This answers
   "did the version I named run", and a caret would let the gate pass on a
   version the caller never named.
3. **Runs before the plan**, so a mismatch costs a startup rather than a full
   encode.

## Verification

`checkRequiredVersion` is a pure function so the guard can be exercised; a
guard that cannot be reached is one nobody has checked. 9 tests, extracted and
executed: exact match, whitespace, mismatch naming both versions, fail-closed
on unresolved, three exactness cases, empty value, and that the sentinel cannot
be satisfied by asking for it by name.

Two mutations, both red attributably:

- drop the fail-closed branch  -> exactly the 2 unresolved tests fail
- lenient `startsWith` match   -> exactly the 2 exactness tests fail

The second is the one worth having: a prefix match is the tempting lenient
implementation, and it silently passes `--require-version 0.8.7` against a
running 0.8.72.

I could not run the vitest suite here (no bun/node_modules on this machine), so
please let CI confirm the suite itself rather than reading my green as a test
run.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: feat(core): a composition's script can load its own files with __hyperframes.assetUrl
body:
## What changes for a user

A composition's script can now load files that sit next to it, like a texture, a font or a JSON file, and they keep loading after the composition is mounted inside another one. Call `window.__hyperframes.assetUrl("assets/earth.jpg")` with the path written relative to the composition's own file, and use the URL it returns.

## Why

Mounting a composition rewrites a `src` or `href` attribute that points at a file next to it, so it keeps loading from `compositions/<name>/...`. A path a script builds is a plain string, so it is never rewritten. `new THREE.TextureLoader().load("assets/x.png")` works when the block is opened on its own and 404s once it is mounted. Six registry blocks that install into their own folder load assets this way today (canopy-part-title, cuboid-carousel, frost-sequence-camera-orbit, lottie-character-walk, orbit-card, wireframe-portal-title). They move to this helper in a follow-up PR. Blocks whose assets install to the project's own `assets/` already work with plain project-root paths and do not need it.

## How

- `runtime/assetUrl.ts`: the page-level `assetUrl(path)` resolves against `document.baseURI`. That is correct at the top level and for a composition opened on its own.
- The scoped wrapper for sub-composition scripts (`compiler/compositionScoping.ts`) already shadows `__hyperframes.getVariables` per composition. It now shadows `assetUrl` the same way, bound to the composition's own file: it resolves the path against the host's `data-composition-src`, which in turn resolves against the page. One owner, so every path that mounts a composition gets the same behaviour:
  - compile time (`inlineSubCompositions`, used by preview and render) passes the host's `src`;
  - the runtime loader (`compositionLoader`) passes the URL it fetched the file from;
  - a `<template>` composition resolves from the file it is written in: the page for the top-level page, the mounted file for one inside a mounted file.
- A separate `<script src="...">` file has no composition of its own. The docs tell authors to resolve URLs in the inline script and hand them over.
- Types: `window.d.ts` and the runtime entry. Docs: a new section in `concepts/compositions.mdx`. The registry contributing guide gains a rule for block authors.

## Verification

- A unit test for the scoped `assetUrl` (relative `src`, absolute `src`, no `src`). Bundler tests: the compiled page binds a mounted composition's script to its `src`, and a `<template>` composition authored inside a mounted file to that file. A loader test: the runtime-mounted script binds the fetched URL. Each fails when its wiring is removed. 189 pass across the three suites.
- End to end, with a composition mounted at `compositions/blk/blk.html` whose script sets `img.src = __hyperframes.assetUrl("assets/dot.png")` (a red square):
  - on main, snapshot and render both fail with `__hyperframes.assetUrl is not a function`, leaving an empty image box;
  - on this branch, snapshot and render both show the red square.

### Before

`hyperframes render` on main: the script throws, and the image stays an empty box.

![main render](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/757092b6-dcf9-4dd7-9bf7-9928478884b2)

### After

The same project rendered from this branch: the red square loads from the block's own `assets/`.

![branch render](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/783e7732-a01f-4d0a-8372-9d237b915939)

Independent review, four rounds, final head: no blocking or should-fix findings. Round 1 suspected that a `<template>` composition inside a mounted file would lose its file binding. It did not reproduce: the inliner binds it to the mounted file, at any depth. That case is now a test. A later round asked the docs to say that `assetUrl` misses a project-root path (added).

## What I did NOT exercise

- The Studio preview walked in a browser. The compile path it uses is the one covered by the bundler test and the snapshot above.
- `<script type="module">` in a mounted file. The runtime loader injects module scripts unwrapped, and the compile-time inliner does not handle them yet: it wraps an import map or a module script like a classic script, which breaks. So a module script's `__hyperframes.assetUrl` is still the page-level one. The follow-up that fixes module and import-map handling binds it there too.
- Migrating those six blocks. That is the follow-up PR, with mounted captures of each.

title: fix(studio): a playhead scrolled off to the left no longer draws over the track names
body:
## What

When the timeline is scrolled so the playhead's time is off to the left, the playhead no longer draws across the track names. Once the scroll settles, it is hidden under the track headers, the same way the clips are.

Trade-off, chosen for scroll performance and matching the ruler label fix in #4424: while a scroll is in progress the playhead can still show over the track names. Within about 100ms of the scroll stopping, it is hidden.

## Why

The playhead layer sits at z-index 100 inside the scrolling content, above the sticky track headers. Nothing clipped it at the headers' edge, so a playhead scrolled past them stayed drawn on top of the names.

## How

- The playhead now renders inside `TimelinePlayheadLayer`, which clips its left edge at the track headers' edge (`clip-path: inset(...)`) once a scroll settles. Half the playhead's glow may pass the edge, so at scroll 0 the playhead at 00:00 looks exactly as on main.
- The settle-time scroll subscription that the ruler's label mask already used (#4424) moves into `useSettledScrollLeft`, now shared by the mask and the playhead layer. Readers re-render twice per scroll gesture, never per frame, and no effect is added.
- `PLAYHEAD_GLOW_W` names the existing 13px glow width so the clip and the indicator read one value.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `Timeline.virtualization.test.tsx`: scroll the timeline to 166px; while scrolling the layer is unclipped; after the settle, its clip sits at the track headers' edge less half the glow. With the clip removed, only this test fails and every other test in the file passes (exit 1). `Timeline.virtualization.test.tsx` and `TimelineRuler.test.tsx` together: exit 0, 13 passed.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio exit 0; `oxlint` 0 warnings and 0 errors on the components directory; `oxfmt --check` clean on the changed files.
- [x] Real Studio in headless Chromium, 1440x900, the registry `product-promo` example at 400% zoom, scrolled 166px. main: the playhead line crosses both track names. This branch: nothing over the track names. At scroll 0, the playhead at 00:00 draws in full.

### Before

main, 400% zoom, scrolled 166px: the playhead at 00:00 is drawn across the track names.

![main: playhead drawn over the track names](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9ad07a4-d2e2-4e14-90ef-dd88c684bb4c)

### After

this branch, same zoom and scroll, at rest: the playhead is hidden under the track headers.

![fix: playhead hidden under the track headers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60cf78db-c5c9-473d-bcf4-15a15a4fdce1)

## Review

Independent adversarial review of this head: no blockers, no majors. It checked the clip coordinate by hand and with two mutations (each turned the new test red), the wrapped playhead's positioning, beat-drag hiding and stacking, and that the ruler mask behaves exactly as before. Minor notes, left as is: the ruler mask and the playhead layer each keep their own scroll listener; in label mode the clip edge sits at the content origin, 32px right of the row header, which is the empty gutter the ruler corner already covers; the new test runs with labels off.

title: feat(cli): preview keeps project history, and Studio can claim its own edits
body:
## What

`hyperframes preview` now keeps a project history; Studio can claim the writes it just made as its own edit; and the history routes tell Studio what Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z would revert next. Stacked on #4431 (the history engine); nothing in Studio calls these yet. Studio's undo moves onto them in the next PR.

- **Preview keeps a history.** The CLI preview server gives the shared API `history(project)`: the engine opened on first use under `~/.cache/hyperframes/history` (overridable with the new `historyRoot` option). The file watcher feeds every change it sees to `noteChange`. A server that never serves a history route never writes one. If opening fails, the history stays off for that run with a warning, and the routes answer 404.
- **Shutdown commits open windows without holding exit.** `shutdown()` closes the history inside the same bounded wait as in-flight renders, so a history that is still opening cannot push shutdown past preview's 3 s exit watchdog.
- **`GET /projects/:id/history` also returns `back` and `forward`.** For each direction, the entry a step would revert (`id`, `label`, `endedAt`, `paths`), from the engine's `stepTarget`. Undo and Redo buttons can name the step without node code in the browser, and Studio knows which files a step will change before it takes it.
- **`claim()`: a writer that records after writing.** Studio saves an edit first (often through a server mutation deep in its save path) and records it afterwards. `ProjectHistory.claim(who, label, paths, { coalesceKey?, idleMs? })` sweeps now and moves the not yet committed outside changes to `paths` into one entry of the claimer's, under the edit's label; other outside writes stay outside. Claims with one `coalesceKey` merge into one entry (a drag) until a claim with another key, `idleMs` (default `quietMs`) without one, or any operation, so Cmd+Z right after a drag undoes all of it. Route: `POST /projects/:id/history/claim { label, paths, coalesceKey?, idleMs? }` returning `{ claimed: { id } | null }`; null when nothing was claimed, including a drag that ends where it started. The known ceiling, named in the code: another writer's write to a claimed file between Studio's write and its claim (milliseconds) folds into Studio's entry, and a write filed to another writer's open window stays that window's.
- **`POST /projects/:id/history/window` takes an optional `idleMs`.** A drag's burst of writes can share one window that ends by itself. It's capped at 10 minutes, below where a timer overflows.

## Why

The engine records every write to a project, but only a host that opens it gets history. The CLI preview is one such host. Studio's buttons need to know the next step, which the engine computes server-side. And Studio records after it writes, so it needs a way to say which writes were its own without restructuring its save paths.

## Tests

- `projectHistory.test.ts`: a claim files only the claimed paths as the claimer's entry (and undoes); coalesced claims make one entry that Cmd+Z right after undoes (fails if a settle does not commit the held claim); another key or the idle time ends a coalescing claim; a coalescing claim whose writes net to nothing returns null and records nothing; an outside write between the write and the claim folds into the claim (the ceiling, asserted).
- `routes/history.test.ts`: `/claim` makes the person's entry under the edit's label and names it as the next Cmd+Z; `back`/`forward` (with the files they change) before an edit, after it, and after a step back; a window given `idleMs` ends by itself and `close` still returns its entry. Both fail on the base branch.
- `studioServer.test.ts`: the preview server serves the history, and a change the watcher reports becomes an entry. It fails on the base, and also with only the watcher line removed. Shutdown returns in under 2.9 s while the history never finishes opening; it times out on the unbounded version.
- All 22 tests in `studioServer.test.ts`, 18 in `projectHistory.test.ts` and 6 in `routes/history.test.ts` pass; the typecheck, lint, format and fallow hooks pass.

## Notes

- Shutdown bounds the history close with the renders' 2 s wait. The close starts first and runs alongside the renders, so it is only cut short if the close itself takes longer than that; past 3 s preview's watchdog exits the process regardless.
- Cmd+Z follows the order entries were committed in, as it already does for windows. A coalescing claim commits when its drag goes idle or at the next operation, so a drag that overlaps another writer's changes can sort before or after them.

title: fix(studio): a preview reload keeps a playing film playing where it was
body:
## What

An edit that reloads the preview (an outside file change, a drop that rewrites the composition) used to stop playback. The reload saved the time, paused the live frame and marked the player paused, and the reloaded document started paused. Anyone watching the film while an agent or a tool wrote to it saw it stop.

Now a film that is playing forward keeps playing in the live frame while the new document loads behind it. At promotion the live frame's current time is read and the old frame is paused. The new document moves to that time, and plays on if the live frame was playing. Because the time comes from the live frame at promotion, not from when the reload started, a film that reached its end, was paused or was seeked during the load also stays where it was. A paused film, a reverse shuttle and a reload that is dropped behave as before. Studio still pauses when the tab is hidden.

- `useTimelinePlayer.ts`: `saveSeekPosition` leaves forward playback running and reports it; `refreshPlayer` pauses the old frame only when it is not kept playing. `handOverPlayback` moves the playhead with `seek(time, { keepPlaying: true })` (no paused-seek audio scrub, no play-state change, as trims do) and calls `play()` if the film was playing, unless the edit cut the film short of the live time: then it stops at the new end, as playback does.
- `useShadowPreviewReload.ts`: `promoteWhenReady` reads the live time and play state and pauses the old frame before the commit, then hands both over after the swap.

## Tests

In `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`:

- "keeps a playing film playing through a reload, from where the live frame had reached": play, reload, advance the live frame to 5.5 s, promote. The player is still playing, the old frame is paused, and the new document is playing at 5.5 s. On main it fails: the player reports paused right after the reload.
- "keeps where a film was paused while the reload loaded": play, reload, move to 7 s and pause, promote. The new document is paused at 7 s. On main it fails: the new document is at 4.2 s, where the reload started.

- "stops a playing film at the new end when the edit cut it short of the live time": playing at 12 s, the new document is 10 s long. It is paused at 10 s. Without the end check it rewinds to the start and plays.

With the change the file passes, 23 of 23. `useTimelinePlayer.test.ts` (28) and `useTimelineSyncCallbacks.test.ts` (17) pass. oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. oxfmt: clean. Studio typecheck: clean.

## Before

Studio dev server, a 20 s composition with a moving square. Press Play, then an outside edit rewrites `index.html` about 2 s later. The film stops at 00:02 and the button returns to Play.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c27bfda5-2cee-4c07-8d49-0d56818fa870

## After

Same steps with this change: the film keeps playing through the reload (00:06, 00:08, 00:11, 00:14 in the last seconds) and the square keeps moving.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83cec851-a560-466e-b44d-cbaab33434d3
