title: ci: skip Windows runs for player and Studio UI-only changes
body:
## What

Windows render and test jobs no longer run for a PR whose changes are all under `packages/player/src/**`, `packages/studio/src/**` or a package `README.md`. That code runs in a browser, and no code or test reads a package README, and the Windows jobs took about 20 minutes on every such PR. Everything else still runs Windows: engine, producer, CLI, studio-server, lint, scripts, the lockfile, `package.json` files, each package's Node-side root files, such as Studio's `vite.*.ts` and player's `vitest.config.ts` (which guards a Windows path bug), and the CLI's runtime docs.

The filter uses `predicate-quantifier: every`: a changed file counts only if it is in the watched set and outside the browser-only trees and package READMEs.

## Evidence

Out of 400 failed Windows runs on PRs since 2026-08-13, 30 were on PRs touching only `packages/studio` or `packages/player`. None were player-only. Among them, Windows failed where Linux tests passed in two real cases, and both are still covered:
- #4272, `packages/studio/vite.browser.ts` (Chrome lookup): runs under the new filter
- #3808, `packages/studio/vite.adapter.projects` (symlinked projects): runs under the new filter

The known cost: #3623 failed on Windows in `packages/studio/src/styles/hexRatchet.test.ts`, a repo tooling test that reads files and printed Windows path separators. Tooling of that kind under `packages/studio/src` is no longer tested on Windows for UI-only PRs. It still runs on any PR that also touches a watched path. The other failures were CLI test timeouts unrelated to those diffs.

Checked with the action's own matcher (picomatch 2.3.2 and 4.0.4, `dot: true`) on real PR file lists:
- #4429 (player): skips
- #4249 and #3623 (studio `src/`): skip
- #4272 and #3808 (studio root vite files): run
- #4267 (engine): runs
- `bun.lock`, `packages/studio/package.json`, `packages/player/vitest.config.ts` and this workflow: run

## Required checks

`Render on windows-latest` and `Tests on windows-latest` are required. The workflow still triggers on every PR (no `on.paths`), and both jobs skip through `if:` on the `changes` output, which reports as success. The aggregate job's handling of failed and cancelled lanes is unchanged.

Open question, not caused by this change: the workflow re-runs on `edited` (base changes after a restack). A re-run can compute a different diff for the same head. With a narrower filter, a later run could skip and report success after an earlier run on the same commit failed. This PR leaves that behaviour as it is.

## Review

An independent review ran on this head:
- **No blockers, no majors.**
- An earlier draft excluded all of `packages/player/**`. The review caught that `packages/player/vitest.config.ts` guards a Windows path bug, so the exclusion is now `packages/player/src/**` only.
- **Minor:** the `edited` re-run question above. It existed before this change.
- **Minor:** `!packages/*/README.md` covers a package's own README only, not nested ones. That is intended.

title: fix(cli): catalog --json carries each item's preview video and poster
body:
## What

`hyperframes catalog --json` now includes each item's `preview` (`video` and `poster` URLs) when the item has one.

## Why

The catalog already loads every item's manifest, `preview` included, but the `--json` rows dropped it. So a tool or app listing the catalog could not show what an item looks like before `add` downloads it. On the registry today, 167 of 396 items have a preview, all as absolute https URLs.

## Related work

None.

## How

- The row mapping moves into one exported `catalogRow(item)`, used by both `--json` shapes (the plain array and the `--query` envelope).
- It adds `preview` only when the item has one. Every existing field is unchanged, so the change is additive for current consumers.
- `docs/packages/cli.mdx` now lists the fields a `--json` row carries.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `catalogRow` carries `preview`. Deleting the one line that adds it fails the test (1 failed, 41 passed). With it restored, 41/41 pass.
- [x] Typecheck of `packages/cli` shows no errors in the changed files.
- [x] Documentation updated

Independent review before posting found nothing blocking. It flagged one should-fix, a second test that could not fail, and that test was removed. It also left one note: the preview type's comment says "Path or URL", but every preview in the registry is an absolute URL today.

title: ci: grade the comments each PR touches
body:
## What

A new `Comments` check grades the comments a PR adds or edits, and CONTRIBUTING.md gains a "Comments" section stating the rules.

- **Citations must resolve**: a backticked path, `path:line`, backticked camelCase symbol, or "pinned by / covered by / see <file>" must point at something tracked in the repo.
- **No history narration**: "used to", "previously", "was removed", "before this change", "PR #123".
- **No commented-out code**: detected by parsing the comment with the TypeScript parser, not a word list.
- **No comment block over 40 lines**, unless its first line says `comment-length: <reason>`.

## Scope: only what the PR touched

A citation fails only on a line the PR added. The three block rules fail only on a block containing such a line. Everything else in a touched file is printed as a warning. Measured on main (3,567 code files), grading every block of every touched file would red any PR that opens one of 410 files, mostly on "used to" (347 hits) and "load-bearing" (49). With touched-block scope, main passes as it is.

## How it runs

- `.github/workflows/comments.yml`, on every `pull_request` (no branch filter, so stacked PRs run too). It runs with `contents: read` and no secrets, so fork PRs run it as well.
- It checks out the PR head and grades it against the merge-base with the PR's base, so a branch that falls behind is not charged for comments main changed.
- Skipped for `release/*` head branches: their commits already passed on their own PRs.
- The checker grades a built-in probe file with two dead citations before anything else. If either resolver stops reporting, the run exits 2 instead of printing OK.
- The test file also runs in `test:scripts`, so the test-reachability check sees it.

## Proof

- `node --test scripts/check-comment-citations.test.mjs`: 71 pass, 0 fail, exit 0. The checker on this branch: `comments: OK (3 file(s) examined of 5 in scope)`.
- Scratch commits on top of this branch, each touching `packages/core/src/adapters/gsap.ts`:
  - a stale citation `src/gone-for-good.ts:12`: exit 1
  - `// const cached = readCache(key);`: exit 1, "parses as code"
  - a 41-line block: exit 1, "41-line comment block"
- A pure rename is not graded as new: the diff runs without a pathspec, so git pairs the rename. Deleting a comment line inside a block (for example a `comment-length:` marker) grades the block it leaves.
- Mutations, one per rule, each turning only its own tests red:
  - making every block count as touched: 4 scope tests
  - re-adding a pathspec to the scope diff: the rename test
  - ignoring deleted comment lines: the marker-deletion test
  - letting `#` count as a comment outside Python: the private-field test (a deleted `#field = 0;` line is not a comment)
- oxfmt --check exit 0, `fallow audit --base origin/main` exit 0, actionlint exit 0.

## Review

Independent reviews ran over three rounds; every blocker and major they found is fixed, with a regression test for each:
- **Blocker, fixed:** a plain rename graded the whole file as added (the scope diff had a pathspec that broke rename pairing).
- **Major, fixed:** deleting a `comment-length:` marker left the wall it exempted ungraded.
- **Major, fixed:** deleting a TypeScript private field (`#count = 0;`) next to an old wall graded that wall.
- **Minors, not changed:**
  - A path containing a literal double quote is written in quotes in git's diff header, so its added lines are not tracked. This predates these changes and no such path exists.
  - The scope diff now reads the whole PR diff; it is still bounded by the same buffer.
  - A deleted JavaScript shebang no longer counts as a comment line, which errs toward grading less.

title: ci: a package file's comment share may not rise
body:
Stacked on #4444: review that first; this PR's diff is the last commit.

## What

A step in the `Comments` check: a changed source file under `packages/*/src` (tests and `.d.ts` excluded) may not raise its share of comment lines compared with its own copy at the merge-base.

- **Share**: fails when the share rose and the file carries more comment lines than at the base. Deleting code alone lifts the share of comments nobody touched, so that passes.
- **Walls**: fails when a file gains a comment block over 12 lines. Existing ones are left alone. `comment-length: <reason>` exempts a block.
- **New files**: may not open above their package's share, measured over the files that existed at the base, so new files never set their own bar. A brand-new package is held to all packages. New files may not carry a block over 12 lines either.
- **Renames** are compared with the file under its old name (`git diff -M`), so a rename is not graded as a new file.

There is no stored baseline: git already holds each file at the fork point. Counting "which lines are comment" reuses the citation checker's `commentBlocks`, so both gates agree.

## Proof

- `node --test scripts/comment-ratchet.test.mjs`: 20 pass, 0 fail. Both test files together: 91 pass, 0 fail. Dropping the base-only exclusion turns the new-package test red.
- The ratchet on this branch exits 0: `0 changed source file(s) at or under their share at the merge-base 201c829c4`.
- A scratch commit adding two clean prose lines to `packages/core/src/adapters/gsap.ts` (share 4.4% to 8.3%): the citation checker exits 0, the ratchet exits 1 with `RAISED comment share`.
- oxfmt --check exit 0, `fallow audit --base origin/main` exit 0.

## Review

Independent reviews over three rounds; every blocker and major is fixed, with a regression test for each:
- **Major, fixed:** the share a new file is held to included the new files themselves, so a new package set its own bar.
- **Minor, not changed:** a PR that adds a whole new package measures every package once to build its bar. That is bounded to one pass per new package.
- **Minor, for maintainers:** this step is not a required check, so it only blocks merging if the check is made required.

title: fix(core): a mounted composition's import map and module scripts run as such
body:
## What changes for a user

A composition that uses an import map or a `<script type="module">` now works when it is mounted inside another composition, in preview and in render. Before, mounting one broke the page with `Unexpected token ':'`. The error took down every mounted composition's script in the same film, not just that block. Five registry blocks hit this: canopy-part-title, cuboid-carousel, orbit-card, wireframe-portal-title and three-orbiting-cards.

## Why

The compile-time inliner (`inlineSubCompositions`, used by the preview bundler and the render compiler) wrapped every inline script of a mounted file in the classic scoped wrapper and concatenated them into one script. An import map's JSON and a module's `import` statements are syntax errors in that position, so the whole chunk failed to parse. The runtime loader kept module scripts as modules, but it gave them no scoped `__hyperframes`, and it wrapped import maps as JavaScript too.

## How

- **Import maps** stay import maps. A page has one, and it must come before every module script, so each mounted file's map merges into the page's own; one is created at the top of `<head>` if the page has none. Addresses are rebased the way a mounted file's `src`/`href` attributes are, so `./assets/three.module.min.js` keeps pointing beside the block, and a prefix mapping such as `"three/addons/": "./assets/addons/"` keeps its trailing slash. When two blocks map the same specifier to different URLs, the first mapping wins and the compiler warns. For example, canopy-part-title and wireframe-portal-title pin different three.js versions.
- **Module scripts** are emitted as modules, after the classic scripts. A `<script type="module" src>` keeps its `type` and is never folded into the classic chunk. A module cannot sit inside the classic wrapper, so each one gets a one-line prelude, `const __hyperframes = <the composition's own copy>`. Its `getVariables()` and `assetUrl()` then resolve for that composition, as in a classic script.
- One owner per piece:
  - the scoped `__hyperframes` expression lives in `compositionScoping.ts` and is shared by the classic wrapper and the module prelude;
  - the merge and emit rules live in the new `compiler/importMaps.ts`, called by both the bundler and the render compiler;
  - the runtime loader uses the same prelude, and resolves import-map addresses with its existing script-URL resolver.

## Verification

- A test for each case, each failing on the base branch or when its piece of the fix is removed:
  - preview bundle (`htmlBundler.test.ts`) and render compile (`htmlCompiler.moduleScripts.test.ts`): one import map with the rebased address, one inline module script with the prelude, a module loaded by `src` kept as a module tag, and nothing JSON or `import` left in the classic chunk;
  - runtime loader: the import map is injected as an import map with absolute addresses, and the module script gets the prelude;
  - the prelude binds `assetUrl` to the file and `getVariables` to the composition;
  - merge rules: the page map is kept, the first mapping wins with a warning, the page's other keys are kept, and nothing is emitted when no mounted file has a map.
- Ten mutations, one per piece, each turn a test red. Core compiler and runtime suites: 364 pass. Producer compile tests: 11 pass.
- End to end: a mounted block whose module script imports a local module through its import map, then sets `img.src = __hyperframes.assetUrl("assets/" + NAME)` (a red square). Rendered three times on each side:
  - base: no square, and the page error `Unexpected token ':'`;
  - this branch: the square, every run, in both snapshot and render.

### Before

![base render: empty image box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e39f23a1-3a64-42de-b393-b9f10cbfde77)

### After

![branch render: red square](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca1d983c-5207-49fd-b8d7-870f3d7a52aa)

Independent review, three rounds; the final head has no blocking findings. Round 3 covered a bug I found by mounting the real cuboid-carousel block: rebasing dropped a prefix address's trailing slash, and the browser rejected the mapping. Round 1 found that a mounted `<script type="module" src>` still lost its `type` (fixed as above). It also questioned leaving an import-map address with no `./` or `/` as written; that address is invalid in the author's own file too, and a block now behaves the same mounted and standalone, so the reviewer withdrew it.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Module scripts and import maps inside an inline `<template>` composition on the top-level page. That is a separate bundler path, not changed here, and no registry block uses one.
- Other non-JavaScript script types, such as `application/json` data blocks, in a mounted file. None in the registry.
- The real blocks rendered as a whole. With this fix, canopy-part-title mounted no longer throws `Unexpected token ':'`. It now reaches its own script, which reads its variable defaults from its `<html>` element; a mounted block has none, so the script throws on `null`. That is a bug in the block, previously hidden by the syntax error. The blocks also load textures and fonts from script strings that 404 once mounted. The follow-up PR fixes both in the blocks, with a mounted capture of each.
- `htmlCompiler.mediaType.test.ts` has one failing test ("shares a four-wide media-probe limiter"). It fails the same way on the base branch.

This PR is stacked on #4434 (it uses `assetUrl` in the prelude); its base moves to main once #4434 merges.

title: fix(studio): a deleted clip leaves the timeline as soon as the file drops it
body:
## What

Deleting a sub-composition clip on the timeline now removes it from the timeline right away. Before, the deleted clip stayed drawn indefinitely, even though the file no longer had it.

## Why

Two things kept it on screen:

1. The live preview still held the removed host until the preview reload landed. Composition enrichment (`enrichMissingCompositions`) scans that live document, found the host, and re-added the clip; `mergeTimelineElementsPreservingDowngrades` then kept it on every shorter scan because it carries `compositionSrc`.
2. The delete only updated the timeline after the ripple move finished saving, so a manifest arriving in between kept the clip as well.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `removeIframeTimelineElements`, beside `patchIframeDomTiming` and using the same `findTimelineElementInIframe` lookup the trim path uses, takes the deleted clips out of the live preview right after the delete's write. Nothing is removed if the write fails.
- The delete sets the survivors, with the ripple's shifts, in the store right after its write: it is the gesture owner that `useTimelineGroupEditing` expects to make the optimistic update. A ripple that fails to save sets the survivors unshifted, so the gap comes back. The ripple notice now keys on "the ripple ran and did not fail".
- The merge rule is unchanged: it exists for hosts a manifest legitimately misses, and the store no longer carries the deleted host into it.

## Test plan

- [x] Two regression tests in `useTimelineDeleteOps.test.tsx`: the deleted clip is gone from the live preview, and the timeline drops it while the ripple is still saving. Each fails when its half of the fix is reverted.
- [x] `packages/studio` `src/hooks` and `src/player`: 234 files, 2514 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt clean; `fallow audit --base origin/main` reports no issues in the changed files.
- [x] Manual: Studio dev server on the `product-promo` registry example, delete `scene-2-4` from its right-click menu, sample the timeline for 20 s.

## Before

2 s and 20 s after the delete, the clip is still drawn on its own row:

![Before, 2 s after the delete: scene-2-4 is still on the timeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92cc0f85-9f4a-4055-a9a5-47194a368283)

![Before, 20 s after the delete: scene-2-4 is still on the timeline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79aa56a4-c7f9-4615-99c1-d8d0045582d7)

## After

Gone by 2 s with the ripple applied, and still gone at 20 s:

![After, 2 s after the delete: scene-2-4 is gone and the next clip has moved up](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ae35ad1-05d8-4557-a19f-d47cccaedaf9)

![After, 20 s after the delete: the timeline still matches the file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c043cf1b-d300-4394-9ed5-b47cc6ecf718)

## Review notes

Independent adversarial review: nothing blocking, nothing to fix. Two notes, both pre-existing and unchanged here: a marquee delete whose per-clip `remove-element` call fails partway leaves the earlier clips removed on disk without a history entry (follow-up); and `.remove()` leaves the old iframe mounted for one render pass before the reload, as with every structural edit that reloads.

title: fix(studio-server): one process at a time keeps a project's history open
body:
Based on main (#4437 has merged).

## What changes

Opening a project's history now takes an owner lock (`owner.pid` in that project's history folder). A second process that opens the same history waits up to 5 s for the first to close, then fails with `HistoryBusyError` naming the owner's pid. A lock left behind by a process that died is taken over, under a second short lock (`owner.pid.evict`) with a re-read of the owner, so two openers never both take it. Closing releases the lock only while it still names the closing process. A lock file that holds no pid counts as dead; one that cannot be read fails the open.

The default history root (`~/.cache/hyperframes/history`) moves from the preview server into `@hyperframes/studio-server` as `DEFAULT_HISTORY_ROOT`, so every app that opens a history opens the same one.

## Why

Each open keeps its own in-memory copy of the log and appends to one JSONL file. With two processes on the same project (a preview and a CLI command, or two apps), each one files the same outside edit as its own entry, and a trim rewrites the file from one process's copy, dropping the other's entries. No line is ever torn; the log just has two owners. The lock sits in `openProjectHistory`, the one function every opener goes through.

The preview server opens its history on first use and keeps a failed open off for the run. A busy history (another process holding it for more than 5 s, for example a first open hashing a large project) is now tried again on the next request instead.

## Known limit

An opener that crashes in the middle of a takeover leaves its evict lock to the next opener that finds it dead; with three openers racing that crash, two could again both win. The comment in `ownerLock.ts` names it.

## Tests

- A second opener is refused while the first holds the history; one that waits gets it once the first closes.
- A lock whose pid is dead is taken over.
- The preview tries a busy history again on the next request (404, then 200).

With the lock short-circuited (`return () => {}`), the first test fails; without the retry, the preview test fails.

## Independent review

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Blocker | The preview kept a busy history off for its whole run | Fixed: a busy open is tried again next request, with a test |
| Note | A pid reused by an unrelated live process holds the lock until that process exits | Kept; the error names the pid |

title: feat(cli): hyperframes history lists, undoes and restores a project's recorded changes
body:
Builds on the owner lock (#4448, merged). A trial: if people don't use it, it goes (see "How to remove it").

## What you can do now

Agents (and people) can read and undo a project's history from the terminal, the same way they already read its timeline:

```bash
npx hyperframes history                                  # newest first: id, who, label, when, files
npx hyperframes history --since mine --who my-agent        # what changed since my last entry, and who changed it
npx hyperframes history show 9f623f43 --diff             # one entry's files, with a text diff
npx hyperframes history undo --who my-agent                # undo my last turn, every part of it
npx hyperframes history undo 9f623f43 --just-this        # or --back-to-before, when a newer edit conflicts
npx hyperframes history restore start|<id>|<time>        # time: 2026-09-24 or 2026-09-24T10:00, local
npx hyperframes history peek <id|time|start> [path]      # read-only
npx hyperframes history pin <id> [--off]
npx hyperframes history begin --who my-agent --label "Bigger title"   # my writes until `end` are one entry
npx hyperframes history end
```

Agents always pass `--who`; without it the caller is the person. Text output is one short line per entry; `--json` gives `{id, who: {kind, name}, label, startedAt, endedAt, files: [path], undone, pinned}`. `show`, `end`, `undo` and `restore` use the same shape; `show --json` adds each file's change (`added`, `modified`, `deleted`) and, with `--diff`, the diff. Refusals exit 2: one line on stderr, or `{ok: false, error}` on stdout with `--json`. `history` refuses a folder with no `index.html`, like `timeline`. Ids accept any unique prefix.

A conflicting undo exits 2 and prints the newer entries and both choices:

```
index.html changed since "Bigger title". Newer entries:
  e9316337  0s ago  Outside  Changed outside the app  (index.html)
Choose one:
  hyperframes history undo 9f623f43 --just-this       put back only its files, over the newer edits to them
  hyperframes history undo 9f623f43 --back-to-before  go back to before it, undoing the newer entries too
```

## In the agent loop

`skills/hyperframes-cli/SKILL.md` gains one marked block, and `skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md` one sentence pointing at it. Two moments only, never every step:

1. Start of a turn: `history begin`, then `history --since mine` to see what the person changed since the agent's last turn, so the agent builds on those edits instead of overwriting them.
2. After a failed check, or "that's worse": `history undo --who <agent>` instead of hand-editing back.

`history end` closes the turn, so the agent's writes read as its own, not as "Changed outside the app".

## One owner for the log

- If a preview server for the project is running and keeps its history, the command goes through its `/projects/:id/history` routes.
- Otherwise it opens the history directly, under the owner lock from the base PR, so a second process waits instead of forking the log.
- Through a preview, a turn is a server window. Without one, a turn is a small marker file (`.hyperframes/history-turn.json`, which history ignores) plus a new engine option, `closedWindow`: the next open files what changed since `begin` to the agent's entry, not to Outside.
- The opener (preview or direct) lives in `packages/cli/src/utils/historyOwner.ts`, so other commands can open a project's history the same way.

## A turn ends after 10 minutes without a write, on every path

One rule, owned by the engine (`takesWrite` in `projectHistory.ts`): a window takes a write only within its idle limit of its previous write. Past that it has ended, even before its timer commits it. `MAX_WINDOW_IDLE_MS` (10 minutes) is exported once and used by the routes' clamp and by the CLI.

- A live window (preview) already had the timer; the check makes a write swept just after the limit go to Outside too.
- A marker turn (no preview) has no timer, so the engine replays it: each write's time is the file's change time (the later of mtime and ctime, so a copy that keeps an old mtime still counts as now), writes are taken oldest first, and a removal counts as now. The marker carries the turn's last write time, and each direct open moves it forward to the entry it just filed.
- A window's entry now ends at its last write, not when a timer or a later open noticed it had ended, so `--since <time>`, `restore <time>` and "when" line up with the edit itself. It never ends before the entry logged ahead of it, so ends stay in log order for every reader.
- A write past a window's idle limit first ends that window, so the log keeps the order the writes happened in.
- A Studio edit claimed during an agent's window goes to the person. That is main's claim rule (#4456): a claim takes its paths from another writer's open window, cut at the version it overwrote. This PR adds nothing to claims.

Engine and route changes needed by the command: the window, undo and restore routes take an agent `who` from the body (`{kind: "agent", name}`; anything else is still the person); `GET /projects/:id/history/blob/:hash` returns a kept file's bytes for `show --diff` and `peek <point> <path>` (the hash must be 64 hex characters).

## Known limits

- While a turn is open, any write outside Studio within 10 minutes of the agent's previous write counts as the agent's: a file write carries no identity. The skill says so.
- Without a preview, a history command run in the middle of a turn files the turn so far as one entry and continues it as a second. `undo --who` still undoes the whole turn: the turn keeps the entries it filed (`.hyperframes/history-turns.json` holds each agent's last turn), and `end --json` lists them as `parts`.
- Without a preview, an agent's deletion counts as the moment it is noticed. If the next history command comes more than 10 minutes later, the deletion is filed to Outside, and `end` prints "Nothing changed in this turn."
- A turn begun without a preview and ended after one starts shows up as Outside, because the preview took in the writes first.
- A turn begun through a preview that then stops cleanly is filed at the stop; the agent's writes after the stop, before `history end`, show up as Outside.
- A second agent's `history begin` on the same project ends the first agent's open turn (one turn per project at a time).
- `--diff` needs `git` on PATH (it uses `git diff --no-index`); without it the command says so.

## How to read its usage

It uses the CLI's existing telemetry, no new pipeline. Each run already sends `cli_command` with `command: "history"`. Each subcommand also sends `cli_history` with `action` (`list`, `show`, `undo`, `restore`, `peek`, `pin`, `begin`, `end`) and `via` (`preview` or `direct`). Count `cli_history` by `action` to see which moments agents actually use.

## How to remove it

Delete `packages/cli/src/commands/history.ts` and its test, its line in `cli.ts` and `help.ts`, the two `<!-- history (trial) -->` blocks in `skills/hyperframes-cli/SKILL.md` and `skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md`, and `history, ` from that first skill's description line; then regenerate `skills-manifest.json`. Nothing else imports the command. The opener (`utils/historyOwner.ts`), the engine's idle rule and the owner lock are shared and stay.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/commands/history.test.ts` runs each case twice, once through a real preview HTTP server and once direct:

- an agent's labelled turn, then a person's edit: `--since <time>` shows both with the right `who`, `--since mine` shows only the person's, and `undo --who` of the agent's turn leaves the person's edit
- a conflicting undo exits 2 with the newer entry and both choices, then `--just-this` takes one
- `show` marks and `--diff`; `peek` reads without writing; `restore start`; `pin` and `--off`
- through a preview the log keeps one baseline and each entry once
- a real second CLI process waits while another process holds the history, and the log gets the edit exactly once
- a turn left open past the idle limit (both paths): the person's later edit is theirs, and `undo --who <agent>` leaves it
- a turn whose writes come closer together than the limit stays the agent's past it, across a mid-turn command
- `undo --who` refuses when the agent's last turn recorded nothing, and leaves its earlier turn alone
- `undo --who` reverts every part of a turn a mid-turn command split
- `undo --who` of a split turn that meets a conflict changes nothing, and offers `--just-this` / `--back-to-before` for the whole turn
- a marker with no last write time has ended
- refusals: undo of an already undone entry, `restore <digit>`, `--json` refusals on stdout, `--limit 0`, a folder with no `index.html`, and exit 2 with the holder's pid when the history stays busy

Engine and route tests cover `closedWindow` and its idle limit (file times set with `utimes`, no sleeps), the logged entry's exact fields, the agent `who` on window, undo and restore, and the blob route (a traversal aimed at a file that exists).

Each new behaviour was mutated once and its tests failed: the idle rule, counting from each write, the marker moving forward, the time parser, the undo target, `index.html`, `--json` refusals, `--limit`, the blob hash check, lock, `closedWindow` (and its kept-id guard), agent `who`, blob route, `--since mine`, the undo target, undo leaving another agent's turn open, a turn outliving its preview, pin, and the conflict exit code.

## Independent review

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Major | `undo --who Y` ended another agent's open turn | Fixed: undo ends only the caller's own turn, with a test |
| Major | A turn begun through a preview that then stopped was filed as Outside | Fixed: the next direct open files it to the agent's entry; an id already kept is not reused. Tested |
| Major | `undo <id>` without `--who` ran as the open turn's agent and ended its turn | Fixed: without `--who` the caller is the person, never the turn's agent. Tested |
| Major | A second agent's `begin` ends the first agent's open turn | Kept as a stated limit: a write carries no identity, so two open turns on one project cannot be told apart anyway (the engine gives a write to the newest) |
| Note | If the history folder is deleted mid-turn, the turn's entry is lost (its writes become part of the new baseline) | Kept: no file content is lost, and it needs the history cache removed during a turn |
| Note | The turn marker is written in place, not atomically | Kept: it is one small JSON file read by the same user's next command |

### Change request at 301b7378

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Blocker | Without a preview, an open turn never expired, so a person's edits were filed to it and `undo --who <agent>` reverted them | Fixed at the engine: one idle rule for both paths (above). Regression test fails at 301b7378 |
| Should-fix | A Studio edit during an agent's window was filed to the agent | Now main's claim rule (#4456); this PR's own takeback was dropped when rebasing onto it |
| Should-fix | `restore 1` read as the year 2001; a bare date read as UTC | Fixed: only `YYYY-MM-DD[Thh:mm]` is a time, read as local; anything else must be an entry id. Tested |
| Should-fix | `history` snapshot any folder it ran in | Fixed: it needs `index.html`, like `timeline`. Tested |
| Should-fix | `--json` refusals went to stderr | Fixed: `{ok: false, error}` on stdout, like `add` and `check`. Tested |
| Should-fix | No test failed without the blob hash check | Fixed: the test aims at a file that exists and fails without the check |
| Nit | `via` reached the log | Fixed at the engine: an entry is written from its own fields only (this also kept a window's idle timer out of the log) |
| Nit | `--limit 0` or a non-number showed everything | Fixed: refused. Tested |
| Nit | Two preview lookup failures printed a stack | Fixed: an ambiguous preview is a refusal; an unreachable one falls back to the direct path under the lock |
| Nit | Only `list --json` used the public entry shape | Fixed: all subcommands do |
| Nit | No test for an already undone target, or for the busy exit | Added both |

A second independent review of the fix found that a marker written before it (no last write time) would still match; such a marker now reads as an ended turn, with a test.

### Change request at 4acd0bdb

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Blocker | `undo --who` fell through to the agent's earlier turn when the open turn recorded nothing | Fixed: a turn keeps the entries it filed and `undo --who` reverts exactly those, or refuses. Test fails at 4acd0bdb |
| Should-fix | A turn split in several entries was undone only partly | Fixed: every part, newest first; a conflict partway puts back the parts already undone and offers the choices for the whole turn. Tests |
| Should-fix | Settle the claim rule with #4456 | Settled: #4456 landed first, this PR keeps its rule and only adds the idle limit |

### Rebase onto #4456

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Should-fix | A window past its idle limit could be logged after a later Studio edit to its file | A write past a window's limit ends the window first. Tested |
| Should-fix | `undo --who` missed the part of a turn that a Studio claim cut off | A turn's parts include every entry with its agent, label and start. Tested |
| Should-fix | An entry could end before the one logged ahead of it, so a time could pick a point that includes a later edit | Ends never go backwards in the log. Tested |
| Should-fix | A file stamped in the future could end every open turn, or push ends ahead of the clock | A write's time is capped at the scan's time. Tested |
| Should-fix | A turn cut off whole by a Studio edit, then a preview restart, lost its parts for `undo --who` | The engine window's start time travels to the CLI's turn marker, so the parts are found from the turn itself. Tested |
| Should-fix | Two tests rewritten for the time cap no longer proved "counting from each write" and "oldest first" | Re-spaced; breaking either rule fails them |
| Should-fix | Four mutations survived (oldest-first sort, mtime vs ctime, a removal as now, `endedAt` from the last write) | One engine test now fails for each |
| Nit | `2026-02-31` rolled over to March | Refused. Test |
| Correction | #4448 is still open | Body says so |

An independent review of this round found that a conflict partway through a multi-part undo left the earlier parts undone silently; that is the rollback above.

title: fix: install contributor hooks in linked worktrees
body:

Dependency installation now runs `lefthook install` in linked worktrees, where `.git` is a file, and skips directories without Git metadata.
