title: fix(registry): six blocks load their own files and variables when mounted
body:
## What changes for a user

Six registry blocks now render when they are added to a film, not only when opened on their own. Before, a mounted canopy-part-title, lottie-character-walk, orbit-card, wireframe-portal-title or cuboid-carousel came out dark or empty. Each one's script asked for its own textures, fonts, animation data or modules at paths that only work beside the block file. canopy-part-title also read its settings from the page's `<html>` element, which belongs to the host film once it is mounted.

## Why

A mounted block lives at `compositions/<name>/`. Its `src`/`href` attributes are rebased when it is mounted, but paths its scripts build are plain strings (#4434), so they 404. Module scripts and import maps only started working mounted in #4446, which this PR is stacked on.

## How

| Block | Before (mounted) | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| canopy-part-title | textures 404; settings read from `<html>` threw on `null` | textures through `__hyperframes.assetUrl`; settings from `getVariables()`, which already carries the declared defaults; with no runtime, its fallbacks now equal those defaults |
| lottie-character-walk | animation JSON 404 | `path: assetUrl("assets/mascot.json")` |
| orbit-card | its scene module 404'd, and it read the host page's variables | an import-map entry for its own module, rebased on mount (#4446); the scene module exports `createOrbitScene(V)`, and the inline module passes its own composition's variables |
| wireframe-portal-title | font fetch 404 | `fetch(assetUrl(...))` |
| cuboid-carousel | its motion module 404'd | an import-map entry for its own module |
| frost-sequence-camera-orbit | asset base unset | sets `window.__frostAssetBase` (the hook its bundle already reads) before `frost.js` loads; its font and default logo resolve beside the file, a logo the user sets is left as their project's path |

- In module scripts, blocks now use bare `__hyperframes`, which #4446 binds to the composition. `window.__hyperframes` inside a module is still the page's.
- Each block uses a one-line helper that falls back to the plain path when the runtime has no `assetUrl`, so its files load as before on an older CLI.
- An imported module (not the inline one) gets the page's `__hyperframes`, not the composition's, so a block reads its variables in the inline module and hands them on, as orbit-card now does.
- The catalog serves cuboid-carousel and orbit-card from blob URLs through its own import map (`scripts/catalog-script-inlining.ts`). That map now carries the new specifiers (`cuboid-carousel/motion`, `orbit-card/scene`), and orbit-card's own map is removed there so it cannot shadow it. A test checks that every specifier an entry module imports is mapped.
- Blocks whose assets install to the project's own `assets/` folder (heygen-avatar-promo-card, ios26-liquid-glass, slack-notification-ad) already work with plain project-root paths and are not changed. glass-shard-title is covered by #4423.

## Verification

Each block was mounted in a test film and snapshotted at mid-duration with #4446's CLI (before) and this branch (after):

- canopy-part-title, lottie-character-walk, orbit-card and wireframe-portal-title mounted are **pixel-identical** to the same block opened on its own at the same instant (mean difference 0.00). Before, all four were dark or empty.
- cuboid-carousel mounted now renders its cards and text. Its frames do not match standalone at the same times, though: the animation is driven at the wrong point once mounted. That is a separate timeline issue, called out below.
- orbit-card mounted with its own `data-variable-values` (a new title and a red accent) now shows them. Before, the frame was identical to the defaults. Standalone orbit-card and canopy-part-title frames are identical before and after this change.
- `hyperframes lint` on each mounted film: 0 errors, and the same warnings as before. Catalog drift check passes; registry validation passes; the catalog inlining tests pass, and the new one fails if either map key is reverted.

### Before

![before: mounted blocks render dark or empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfc19da4-7678-436b-a4f2-2948464c0ddf)

### After

![after: mounted blocks render](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/010f91c7-7d37-46f1-a002-79d204654981)

orbit-card mounted with its own variables, before (left, the defaults) and after (right):

![orbit-card override: before shows defaults, after shows the override](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e8a73c4-8cf6-4965-9af9-e424e9235d73)

Independent review, two rounds, plus a bot review; the final head has no blocking findings.
- Round 1 caught that moving frost's declarations off `<html>` emptied its declarations in the SDK (0 instead of 216), so that move is backed out here.
- The bot review found three gaps, all fixed here: orbit-card's variables came from the host page, frost's font path was missed, and canopy's fallbacks without a runtime differed from its defaults.
- Round 2 generated the catalog previews for orbit-card and cuboid-carousel and loaded them in headless Chrome. On the base, orbit-card's scene module 404'd and cuboid-carousel failed to resolve `cuboid-carousel/motion`. On this head, both load cleanly.

## What I did NOT exercise

- **frost-sequence-camera-orbit mounted.** It still reads its settings from `<html>`, so mounted it still throws `rigSchema is not iterable`. A follow-up moves its declarations to its root. It is stacked on #4454, which makes the SDK, metadata and lint read root declarations; moving them earlier would have emptied frost's Variables panel in Studio. Frost also needs WebGPU, which my render machine lacks, so its pixels are unverified either way.
- **cuboid-carousel timing when mounted**, as above. #4455, stacked on this PR, fixes it.
- Mounting the same block twice in one film. Five of the six share page-level ids, timelines or globals, so only one instance per film works today (see the review thread).

title: ci: check TODO owners, public URLs and source links in comments
body:
Stacked on #4445 (its branch is this PR's base).

## What

The `Comments` rules now follow the [Stack Overflow guidance on code comments](https://stackoverflow.blog/2021/12/23/best-practices-for-writing-code-comments/). CONTRIBUTING states its nine rules, and the check enforces the ones a machine can check reliably.

- **Fails:** a TODO, FIXME or XXX that opens a comment line without an owner, area or issue in its parentheses (`TODO(name):`, `TODO(player-perf):`, `TODO(#1234):`) or a `github.com` issue URL on that line. A bare `#123456` doesn't count, because it may be a colour.
- **Fails:** a URL in a comment that doesn't parse, uses a private IP address or an internal host (`.internal`, `.corp`, …), or carries a signature or token in its query. `localhost` notes about dev servers are fine.
- **Warns:** "copied / adapted / ported / borrowed from" with no link to the source.
- **Warns:** a one- or two-line comment whose words mostly repeat the next line of code (`// Count label` above `const countLabel`).
- Rules 2 to 5 and 8 need judgment, so they are in CONTRIBUTING and a new line in the PR template's checklist. Rule 8 is stated as "what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug", never history or a PR number.

Like the other rules, these only grade what the PR added. Main passes as it is.

## Calibration on main (3,571 code files)

Each rule was measured on main before being allowed to fail a PR, and its matches were checked by hand:

| Rule | First version | Hits | Real | Final version | Hits on main | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TODO owner | any `TODO` word | 10 | 1 | marker opening a line, then `:` or `(`; owner, area or issue in the parentheses, or an issues link | 2, both real unowned TODOs; every parenthesised TODO on main passes | fails |
| Public URL | any non-public host | 10 | 0 (all `localhost` dev-server notes) | loopback allowed | 0 | fails |
| Source link | copied / adapted / ported / borrowed / taken from | 18 | ~2 | "taken from" dropped | 10 | warns: still ~2 real of 10 |
| Restates the code | word overlap ≥ 80% | 62 | 14 of 30 sampled (47%) | section dividers (Unicode and ASCII) and JSDoc excluded | 30 | warns: two hand counts gave ~74% and ~40%, both under the 90% bar |

"via" and "based on" were measured as source-link phrases too. They appear constantly in ordinary prose ("passes via props", "based on the width"), so they are not used.

## Proof

- `node --test` on both test files: 121 pass, 0 fail. The checker on this branch: `comments: OK (4 file(s) examined of 4 in scope)`.
- Scratch commits on top of this branch, each touching `packages/core/src/adapters/gsap.ts`:
  - `// TODO: memoise the timeline lookup`: exit 1
  - `http://10.0.4.2/grafana`: exit 1, "points at a private host"
  - an S3 URL with `X-Amz-Signature`: exit 1
  - `// Proof restate` above `export const proofRestate`: exit 0, prints the restate warning
  - `// Adapted from the upstream easing implementation.`: exit 0, prints the source warning
  - a comment that explains why: exit 0, nothing printed
- Mutations, each turning only its own tests red: dropping the owner check, the private-host check, the restate rule or the source rule's warning level; reading the issue link from the whole block, accepting a bare `#1234` on the TODO's line, or accepting any text in the TODO's parentheses; dropping the ASCII divider exclusion; counting `#` as a comment in TypeScript.
- oxfmt --check exit 0, `fallow audit --base origin/main` exit 0.

## Review

Independent reviews over five rounds; every blocker and major is fixed with a regression test and a mutation that turns only that test red:
- **CodeQL, fixed:** the issue-link match was an unanchored substring, so `https://evil.example/github.com/o/r/issues/1` counted. The URL is now parsed and must be a `github.com` issue path; putting the old match back fails the new test.
- **Major, fixed:** a bare `#123456` (a colour) counted as a TODO's issue. Now the owner or issue goes in the parentheses, or the line links the issue.
- **Major, fixed:** any text in the parentheses counted as an owner (`TODO(#)`, `TODO(-)`). Now it must be a name, an area or `#1234`.
- **Major, fixed:** the private-host check matched hostname prefixes, so a public `10.cdn.example.com` failed. Now only whole private IP addresses and internal suffixes fail.
- **Major, fixed:** ASCII section dividers (`// ---- … ----`) were not excluded from the restating check.
- **Minors kept:**
  - `TODO(fix this later)` counts as owned. Telling an area from a lazy phrase would need a list of areas this checker does not have.
  - An issue link that wraps onto the TODO's next line does not count.
  - A URL written with a bracketed IPv6 address is cut at the `]`. Rare, and it errs toward not flagging.

title: fix(sdk): read a composition's variables from its root when its html has none
body:
## What changes for a user

Opening a composition that declares its variables on its composition root, not on `<html>`, now shows those variables in the SDK and in Studio's editing path, and edits them in place. Before, `openComposition()` reported no variables for such a file. Ten registry blocks ship this shape, among them cosmic-orb, bar-chart-race, gallery-tunnel and week-in-merges.

`hyperframes render --strict-variables` and `hyperframes lint` now read those declarations too. Before, strict mode could not check a root-declared file's variables, and the lint rule never looked at a root's declarations.

## Why

The runtime (`getVariables()`) and the compiler read `data-composition-variables` from `<html>` and from the composition root. Three other readers looked at `<html>` only:
- the SDK's `declarationElement()`, which reported 0 declarations for a root-declared file and would have written a new declaration to `<html>`;
- the parsers' `extractCompositionMetadata()`, which feeds `--strict-variables`;
- the lint rule `invalid_composition_variables_declaration`.

This also unblocks a follow-up. Blocks that declare on `<html>` and read it at runtime (frost-sequence-camera-orbit and others) break when mounted, because a mounted block brings no `<html>` along. They can move their declarations to the root once every tool reads them there.

## How

- **SDK.** It reads declarations the way the runtime does: from `<html>` and from the composition root, merged, the root winning a shared id (`declarationCarriers()`).
  - An edit to an existing variable (update, remove, a new default, patch replay) lands on the element that declares it.
  - A new variable goes to the root if the root carries declarations, else to `<html>`.
  - The duplicate check covers both elements.
  - When the last variable is removed from a root, the root keeps `data-composition-variables="[]"` instead of losing the attribute, so undo and later declares land back on the root rather than on `<html>`. `<html>` still drops the attribute as before.
- **Parsers.** `extractCompositionMetadata()` reads `<html>` and the composition root (inside its `<template>` when templated), the root winning a shared id, as in the runtime.
- **Lint.** The declaration rule checks every tag that declares, not only `<html>`.
- **Registry.** Once the rule looked at roots, it flagged two items whose declarations were an object map instead of the required array: lower-third-bild and caption-texture (and caption-texture's demo file). The runtime ignored those maps, so their variables never reached the Variables panel. Both now use the array form with the same ids, labels and defaults.

## Verification

- SDK tests in `session.variabledecls.test.ts` on the cosmic-orb shape (a full page, `<html>` empty, the root declaring):
  - the declarations are read, and declare and remove edit them on the root;
  - removing the last variable, then undo, puts it back on the root while `<html>` stays empty;
  - with both `<html>` and the root declaring, the SDK shows all of them, edits each where it is declared, refuses a duplicate of an `<html>` id, and takes the root's version of a shared id.

  Each test fails when its fix is reverted. SDK suite: 554 pass; typecheck clean.
- Parsers and lint tests cover a root declaration, templated or not, and a shared id declared in both places; each fails when its fix is reverted. Parsers: 1059 pass. Lint: 725 pass.
- Real blocks through `openComposition()`: cosmic-orb 9, bar-chart-race 10, gallery-tunnel 10, week-in-merges 9 declarations, each 0 before. `<html>`-declared blocks are unchanged (frost-sequence-camera-orbit 216, canopy-part-title 11). The metadata `--strict-variables` reads now reports cosmic-orb 9 and bar-chart-race 10.
- Lint across all 388 registry items: 0 findings for this rule after the two conversions. The two converted items render identically standalone before and after (mean difference 0.0). No registry file declares on both `<html>` and its root, so the change of precedence alters nothing that ships.

Independent review, three rounds plus a bot review; the final head has no blocking findings.
- A remove-then-undo on a root-declared file restored the variable on `<html>`. Fixed: the root keeps `[]`.
- A file declaring on both `<html>` and its root showed only one set in the SDK. Fixed: the SDK reads both.
- The metadata and lint readers ignored root declarations, and three registry files used an invalid object map. Both fixed.

One behaviour is kept deliberately: in a file declaring on both, removing an `<html>` variable and then undoing it restores the variable on the root. The values are identical before and after, because the runtime merges both elements. A location-exact undo would need the patch format to record the element.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio's Variables panel in a browser. The panel reads through this SDK path; the numbers above come from the SDK itself.
- A real file declaring on both `<html>` and its root: no registry file has this shape; the tests use a synthetic one.
- A wrapped template or fragment composition now also keeps `[]` on its root after its last variable is removed, where it used to drop the attribute. The runtime reads `[]` as no variables.

title: fix(registry): cuboid-carousel plays from the start when mounted
body:
## What changes for a user

cuboid-carousel now plays its whole animation when it is added to a film. Before, a mounted cuboid-carousel skipped straight to the last quarter of its move: at 2 seconds it showed a close-up that belongs near the end, instead of the card spread.

## Why

The block drives its 3D scene from one animated number, `S.t`, with a GSAP tween. A plain `tl.to(S, { t: DUR })` records its starting value when it first renders past 0. The block's GPU warm-up draws three frames ahead (`renderAt(DUR * 0.75)` and so on), and `renderAt` writes `S.t`. The warm-up then meant to restore the current time with `renderAt(S.t)`, but `S.t` had just been overwritten. Mounted, the warm-up finished before the renderer's first seek, so the tween started from 5.0 instead of 0. A probe during a render read the timeline at 1.000 s while `S.t` was 5.250. Standalone, the order happened to be the other way round.

## How

- `tl.fromTo(S, { t: 0 }, { t: DUR, ... })`: the tween's start is fixed, whatever the warm-up leaves behind.
- The warm-up ends with `renderAt(tl.time())`, restoring from the timeline, as canopy-part-title's warm-up already does. No other registry block has this pattern (grepped).

## Verification

- Mounted vs the block opened on its own, snapshots at 0.5, 2, 3.33, 5 and 6.5 s: pixel-identical at every time (mean difference 0.0). Before the fix, all five differed.
- Standalone frames at the same times are identical before and after the fix, so standalone playback is unchanged.
- `hyperframes lint`: 0 errors, the same warnings as before.

### Before

Mounted (top) against standalone (bottom), same times:

![before: mounted frames do not match standalone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/234a3a74-0211-4c10-b7c3-5d651ad40446)

### After

![after: mounted frames match standalone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d808ed4e-b61a-4183-a17a-a17ec3163d57)

Independent review: no findings. The reviewer reproduced it on fresh copies of the fixtures at 2 s. Before the fix, 667,041 pixels differed between mounted and standalone; after the fix, none. Standalone frames were identical before and after.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Scrubbing in Studio.
- Two cuboid-carousels in one film.

Stacked on #4452, which makes cuboid-carousel load its motion module when mounted at all.

title: feat(studio): undo and redo step through the project history, whoever made the change
body:
## What

Studio's undo and redo now run on the project's history (#4431, #4437) instead of a store in the browser. Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z step through every change to the project by time, whoever made it: your own edits, an agent's, or a file changed in another editor. The browser's IndexedDB history is deleted.

- **An edit claims what it just wrote.** Every Studio edit already calls `recordEdit` after it saves. That call now claims the files it wrote as your entry, under the edit's label (`POST /history/claim`). Edits sharing a coalesce key (a drag) become one entry, so Cmd+Z right after a drag undoes the whole drag.
- **Cmd+Z / Cmd+Shift+Z step the history** (`POST /history/step`). The preview still updates in place: before stepping, Studio reads the files the step will change, and afterwards passes the before/after contents to the existing in-place preview sync. The toast names the step the way the history does ("Undid: Moved Title", "Undid: Changed outside the app").
- **An agent's write stays the agent's.** A claim sends, per file, the version Studio overwrote. The history cuts each change there, so an agent's edit a few seconds before yours stays a separate entry, and Cmd+Z undoes only yours. A claim also takes your writes out of an agent's open window, instead of leaving them inside the agent's entry.
- **An undo is not mistaken for an outside edit.** Step, undo and restore take Studio's write token (`X-Hyperframes-Write-Token`). The history records a write receipt before each file it writes, and before each file it deletes, under the new `DELETED_VERSION`. So the watcher's echo reads as Studio's own write, and the preview is not reloaded on top of the in-place update. The CLI preview and Studio's dev server both look up deletions this way.
- **Studio run from source keeps a history too.** The dev server's adapter opens each project's history once, in the same folder as `hyperframes preview` (`DEFAULT_HISTORY_ROOT`, now exported). It opens it through the module instance whose receipts its watcher reads, and it closes the histories when the dev server stops.
- **Your edit cuts an agent's turn only where it has to, and Cmd+Z walks back in order.** A window holds one change per file. When your edit cuts a file out of an agent's open turn, the agent's change to that file so far is committed at that moment as an entry of its own. The turn keeps its other files and goes on under its own id. Cmd+Z then walks back in the order the file changed: the agent's later write, your edit, then the agent's earlier write. Before, the agent's next write to the same file merged back into one change spanning your edit, and undoing the turn wiped your edit.
- **A drag ends where someone else wrote.** A drag's next step continues its entry only where the drag's own last change left off, and only while every file the drag holds is still as the drag left it. If another writer (an agent, even one whose turn already closed, or an outside editor) wrote the file in between, the drag's entry ends there and a new one starts after it, so no entry spans another writer's change.
- **Cmd+Z steps past an entry whose files moved on under an earlier-ending edit.** One case still commits out of order: a drag claim that is still held while the agent's turn closes. There, Cmd+Z undoes the newest earlier entry that touched those files, if it still applies. The buttons name the same step.
- **A step that fails says why.** A refused step names the files that changed since its edit. A step the server could not take shows its error. A claim the server refused is logged; its write still reaches the history, as a change made outside the app.
- **Blob reads are checked.** The blob store refuses any hash that is not 64 hex characters at the point it joins the path.

## Why

The browser's history only knew Studio's own edits. It refused to undo once anything else had touched a file ("File changed outside Studio"), and it was one of three histories for the same project. With the project's history, there is one list, it survives a reload, and Cmd+Z works the same whoever made the last change.

## Before / After

An agent (simulated by a write to `index.html` outside Studio) changes the title to "Hello, agent", then the person presses Cmd+Z.

### Before

Nothing happens. The title stays "Hello, agent", and the Undo button is disabled because Studio's own history is empty.

![Before: after the outside edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9bcbfbb3-20df-4688-96bc-12fed20ad9d0)
![Before: after Cmd+Z, the title is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/237f10e0-d760-4bdc-82fb-3111f74f5fb1)

### After

The title is back to "Hello, film", and the toast says "Undid: Changed outside the app". Redo is now available.

![After: after the outside edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1003f03c-b588-4d9b-b7b7-5abc2cb63498)
![After: after Cmd+Z, the title is restored and the toast names the step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6c1b653-93aa-434f-a4d7-9cdd0b543a01)

## Tests

- `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts` drives the hook against the real history routes and engine:
  - an edit is undone and redone, with the preview's before and after contents;
  - a drag's claims undo as one step before the drag goes idle;
  - an agent's earlier edit stays the agent's;
  - an undo's writes carry the token Studio marked;
  - with no history on the server, an edit still saves and nothing throws.
- `projectHistory.test.ts`:
  - a claim cut at the overwritten version, and each half undoes alone;
  - Studio's write taken out of an agent's open window, with the agent's own write left there;
  - a claim under another key that takes nothing still ends the held one;
  - no blob is read outside the store.
- `projectHistory.test.ts` also: an agent turn cut by Studio's edit walks back C, B, A (also when nothing follows the cut, across two files); a cut takes only the cut file out of the turn, so undoing the turn reverts its other files; a held drag across an agent's write, an outside write, or an agent turn that already closed ends at that write, and Cmd+Z walks back every step; a drag that adds a file midway stays one entry; a held claim that deleted a file ends where someone else recreated it; a held drag ends when someone else changed a file it already holds, or when one file of its next step continues and another does not; a held drag claim that commits after the turn is stepped past; a logged entry carries only its own fields.
- `routes/history.test.ts` also: the GET names the step the engine takes when it steps past an entry.
- `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts` also: a failed step says why; a refused step names its files; a reply that cannot be read, or a server that cannot be reached, is a failure, not a throw; a refused claim is logged and stays undoable. The drag test now passes the content each edit really overwrote, so it fails if the held drag's files are not read before the step.
- `useEditHistoryActions.test.tsx`: the conflict and failure toasts.
- `routes/history.test.ts`:
  - an undo's writes and deletions are labelled with Studio's token;
  - the 10-minute idle cap holds;
  - `overwrote` is passed to the claim.
- `studioServer.test.ts` (CLI): the deletion an undo makes reaches `/api/events` carrying Studio's token.
- `vite.adapter.projects.test.ts`:
  - the dev server serves a project's history and opens it once;
  - it closes the history when it stops, through the opener it was given.
- Reworked tests:
  - `useCanvasZOrderTimelineMirror`, `useRazorSplit`, `useRazorSplit.history` and `timelineClipDragCommit` now assert what Studio records: label, kind, coalesce key and before/after. They no longer re-implement the deleted reducer. Merging and undo are the engine's, and are tested there.
  - `hostMount` runs its undo through the real history routes.
  - One test was dropped: "trips the guard when edited externally after a split". That guard now lives in the engine and is covered there.
- Every new test fails with its line of the fix removed.

## Notes

- Desktop embeds Studio and needs the history on its own Studio API, plus the `DELETED_VERSION` lookup in its watcher, when it moves to this release. Until then its undo list is empty; no fallback is kept.
- #4448 exports the same `DEFAULT_HISTORY_ROOT` line; whichever of the two merges second drops its copy.
- The first history request snapshots the project. Whether that stays on by default is being decided separately.
- Undo order is the order entries end, except that Cmd+Z steps past an entry whose files moved on under an earlier-ending edit (above). A claim first commits the outside writes made before it, so they sort before your edit. The cost: another writer's burst during a drag can land as several outside entries instead of one.
- The buttons name the next step from the history as of its last scan; a step scans first. A write not yet scanned can make the step differ from the button, and the toast then names what was actually undone.
- A turn cut by a person's edit keeps every file but the cut one in its own entry; the cut file's earlier part is an entry of its own (a fresh id). `history undo` of the turn undoes the turn's entry; the earlier part sits under the person's edit, and `history undo <that part> --back-to-before` goes back past both. If nothing but the cut file was written, closing the turn returns that part.
- `recordEdit` still takes `kind`, which the history does not use; about 40 callers pass it. Removing it is a separate small PR.
- A claim only cuts a change at a version whose bytes the history holds. No current caller creates a file through `recordEdit`, so an empty "before" never reaches the cut.

title: ci(studio): gate opening a film in Studio on work counts that only go down
body:
## Summary

Studio's perf gates measure milliseconds, and nothing measures how much work opening a film costs. This adds
a work-count gate for one journey: open a 12-scene film in Studio, wait until it can play, idle 20 s, and
wait until thumbnail work is done. Each count has a checked-in ceiling that may only go down. A count repeats
exactly on the same code, so when one rises the gate names the work that grew:

```
[perf-ratchet] studio-open: FAIL
[perf-ratchet]   FAIL thumbnailRenders rose 20 -> 33 (+13, +65%)
[perf-ratchet]   FAIL total.requests.thumbnail rose 20 -> 33 (+13, +65%)
```

That is from a CI run of this branch plus a throwaway patch that gives each composition card a second
thumbnail. The same patch on main passes CI: nothing there counts this work.

## Before

Main with the planted second card thumbnail: the timeline viewport job passes. No gate counts the extra
renders.

![CI log: main passes the planted extra thumbnails](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7cab68dd-c109-4e04-a219-9dc3c8a71004)

## After

The same patch on this branch: the open-journey count fails and names the counter.

![CI log: the open-journey count fails with thumbnailRenders rose](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63b6b8ff-3871-42d4-9536-7d2669b87582)

## What is counted

| Counter (gated) | Ceiling | What it is |
|---|---:|---|
| `thumbnailRenders` | 20 | thumbnail files the server wrote: 12 timeline clips and 8 composition cards (card images load lazily, so the 1600x900 viewport decides which) |
| `total.requests.thumbnail` | 20 | thumbnail requests the page made |
| `total.frameNavigations` | 7 | page and frame loads |
| `total.requests.document` | 2 | document requests |

All four are app-level: what Studio asks for and what the server renders. None comes from Chrome's
internals. Each journey in `perf-ceilings.json` also records the Chrome major version it was measured on.
Other counters (DOM mutations, timer and animation-frame callbacks, React commits, style recalcs, fetches by
kind, idle-window counts) go into the uploaded evidence but aren't gated, because they follow elapsed time.

## How

- `studio-open-counts.mjs` is the journey. Before it opens anything it checks that every scene
  `index.html` mounts exists, and refuses to measure otherwise, naming the missing file. It reads thumbnail
  work only once it has gone quiet (nothing in flight, nothing new for 10 s), because Studio asks for
  thumbnails a few at a time and a count read at a fixed moment follows machine speed.
- `perf-counters.mjs` counts from the browser with no timing: requests by kind, frame navigations, targets,
  React commits through the devtools hook, and page activity.
- `perf-ratchet.mjs check` passes only when every gated counter sits exactly at its ceiling:
  - a rise fails and says by how much;
  - a fall fails until the PR banks it (`perf-ratchet.mjs lower`), as `contrastRatchet` does;
  - a counter that wasn't measured fails;
  - in CI it also reads the base branch's `perf-ceilings.json`, and fails any ceiling raised or removed
    against it.

  `lower` refuses evidence from a different Chrome major than the journey records. `correlate` tells
  whether a counter repeats exactly and tracks wall-clock, and a rise prints how to use it.
- CI: a step in "Studio: timeline viewport gate" runs the journey and the check. The evidence is uploaded
  with the existing artifact.
- The fixture's scene files are committed with `git add -f`, because the repository ignores `compositions/`.

## Checks run

- Two runs of the journey on a Linux box: 20 renders, 7 frame navigations, 2 documents, 20 thumbnail
  requests, identical both times. With one scene deleted, the journey exits 2 naming `scene-4.html`.
- CI at 0a1c2fa3d, on Chrome 153: exactly 20 / 7 / 2 / 20, the ceilings. A Linux box on Chrome 152 read the same.
- `perf-ratchet.test.mjs`: 15 passed. Each rule has a test: rise, fall, missing or NaN, empty, raised or removed
  against base, a dropped journey, an unreadable base, browser parsing, `lower` refusing another Chrome,
  lower-only, correlate. Removing each base rule turns its test red.
- oxlint and oxfmt over the changed files: clean.
- Fallow: no findings in the ratchet script. The previous head's four complexity findings reproduce on that version and are gone here.

## Not in this PR

- **A scroll-work count for the timeline gate.** An earlier head gated React commits per scroll step. Review
  showed it was a ~2-frame timing gate: on a 4x slower CPU the count doubled. The root cause: with 50,000
  clips, about 141 thumbnails are visible per viewport and the server renders them two at a time, so the page
  never rests, and any per-step count includes however much of that backlog drained. Answering thumbnails
  instantly in an untimed pass made it steady (151.5 commits a step) but a planted 3x regression moved it by
  only about 3.5. An exact scroll count needs a test-only switch to turn timeline thumbnails off, which is a
  product-code change for its own PR. `timeline-virtualization.mjs` is unchanged from main.
- **Limits.** React commit counts would miss extra renders batched into an existing commit; no commit counter
  is gated here.
- **Maintainer decisions, not made here.** A CODEOWNERS entry for `perf-ceilings.json`, and making "Studio:
  timeline viewport gate" a required check (it isn't one in the main ruleset today).
- **A scheduled lowering job.** `perf-ratchet.mjs lower` does the rewrite by hand.

## Pre-review

Review on the earlier heads found these; each is answered on the thread too.

| Finding | Severity | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| The fixture's scene files were gitignored, so CI measured a film with no scenes (ceilings of 13) | blocking | fixed: scenes committed; the journey refuses a missing scene; ceilings re-measured at 20 |
| Per-step scroll counts moved with CPU speed: a ~2-frame timing gate | blocking | scroll count removed; root cause and what an exact one needs are under "Not in this PR" |
| Style recalcs differ by Chrome version on identical code | blocking | nothing browser-internal is gated; each journey records its Chrome; `lower` refuses another |
| A count below its ceiling passed, and raising a ceiling was a quiet JSON edit | should fix | a fall fails until banked; CI fails a ceiling raised or removed, and a journey dropped, against the base branch |
| `lower` accepted evidence from any machine | should fix | refuses a different Chrome major |
| Commit counts miss batched re-renders | should fix | stated under "Limits"; no commit counter is gated |
| The gate is not a required check | should fix | a maintainer decision, listed above |
| A base file in an unexpected shape skipped the comparison instead of failing | should fix | fixed: an unreadable base fails |
| Gateability is established once and never re-checked | note | a rise prints how to re-check with `correlate` |
| A scene file that exists but fails to load passes the guard | note | kept: the counts catch it (a broken film read 13, not 20) |

Audited: the committed fixture (`git ls-files`), CI evidence on Chrome 153 at the ceilings, the planted regression
failing here and passing on main, and one mutation per ratchet rule (each caught).

title: test(studio): wait for the off-canvas indicator instead of a fixed number of frames
body:
## What

`offCanvasIndicatorRefresh.test.tsx` waited a fixed time: one `Promise.resolve()`, 105 ms and two animation frames. It then assumed three things had already happened:

1. the MutationObserver delivered the style change;
2. the overlay loop woke;
3. the 100 ms rebuild throttle let the refresh through.

On a loaded runner any of these can land later. That is how the off→on case failed on Windows studio-core for #4445, a PR that touches no Studio code.

The test now waits for what it asserts. `untilIndicator` flushes frames inside `act` until the indicator reaches the expected state, with a 4 s ceiling. All three fixed waits in the file use it: the initial appearance, off→on, and off→off.

## Proof

A new case runs off→on with MutationObserver delivery delayed 300 ms, past the old fixed wait, which makes the race deterministic.

- Putting the old fixed wait back fails only that case: "expected <div role=button>… to be null".
- With the new wait, all 3 tests pass in 6 of 6 consecutive runs on Linux. `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/studio` exits 0.

## Before

The old fixed wait, with MutationObserver delivery 300 ms late: the lagging off→on case fails and the indicator is still there.

![Before: old fixed wait fails when the observer is late](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04c60b97-6d68-4f26-8ebf-e54cff66be3c)

## After

The same lag, with this PR's wait: all 3 tests pass.

![After: waiting for the indicator passes](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c986ce1-3278-43fd-a6e3-bed7310447a7)

## Why only the test changes

The component recovers from a late mutation on its own. The overlay loop re-checks every 250 ms while idle, so a late `markDirty()` is picked up within about 250 + 100 ms and never stays stale. A real browser also delivers MutationObserver records for a style write at microtask speed. The lag exists only in a busy test runner.

## Review

An independent review ran on this head.
- **No blockers, no majors.** It reproduced the race by putting the old wait back, and confirmed the observer patch stays inside the test's own iframe window.
- **Minor:** a real regression now fails after the 4 s ceiling rather than at once.

title: fix(media-use): tests never write into the person's media library
body:
## What

The media-use tests wrote fixture rows into the real `~/.media`, the media library apps list as the person's own files. Running `resolve.test.mjs` from main appended three `misses.jsonl` lines to the real library of the machine running it, and earlier runs left `bgm_001` "soft minimal ambient" rows in its manifest.

The cause: every test pointed `HOME` at a temp dir and hoped each module read `HOME` late enough. Some modules resolved `homedir()` on their own, so a test that forgot, or ran in the wrong order, wrote to the real one.

## How

- **One owner.** `lib/media-home.mjs` is now the only place that decides where the media library lives. The cache, misses, preferences, recipes and the legacy telemetry id all resolve through `globalMediaDir()`. The copy in `skills/media-use/scripts/lib/` is byte-identical and enforced by the copy-parity test.
- **One knob for tests.** `HYPERFRAMES_MEDIA_HOME` points the library at a temp dir. Every media-use test sets it, per test where a shared dir would leak cache between cases.
- **A guard in this repo only.** The skills test step in CI and `bun run test:skills` set `HYPERFRAMES_MEDIA_HOME_REQUIRED`. There, a test that reaches the library without the override throws instead of writing. Nothing else sets the marker, so end users, and other projects whose own `node --test` runs spawn this CLI, keep the normal `~/.media`.
- Miss logging stays best-effort. An unresolvable home still never breaks `resolve`.

## Proof

Run on Linux over every skills and media-use test file, with the marker set.
- **Suite:** 698 of 700 pass, 0 fail, one commit before the miss-logging fix.
- **After that fix:** `misses.test.mjs` and `media-home.test.mjs` re-ran, 7 of 7 pass.
- **Real library:** an md5 snapshot of the real `~/.media` taken before and after each run is identical.

Mutations, each run against `media-home.test.mjs` and `misses.test.mjs`:
- **Guard keyed on Node's own test flag** (`NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`) instead of the marker: the external-consumer test fails.
- **Guard removed:** the "fails instead of writing" test fails.
- **Home resolved outside `recordMiss`'s try:** the best-effort test fails.

## Follow-up

Studio's server resolves the same library in `globalAssets.ts` with its own `homedir()` call. It lives in another package, so it is left for its own change.

title: fix(core): paint no timed clip until the runtime decides its visibility
body:
## What a user sees

Opening a composition no longer flashes a later scene before the first one. Until the runtime has decided which clips are on screen at the current time, it now paints none of them. The first frame a viewer sees is the right one.

## Why it happened

A paused page shows a timed clip only after the runtime's visibility pass sets its visibility. Before that pass (at readiness, or at the first seek), every clip sat in the page at once, stacked. In a page without a loader, the top clip, often a later scene, flashed before the first. In the Studio the player covers the preview with its loader, but the browser still painted the stacked clips underneath and decoded every scene's images. On a 12-scene project that is all eight 1600x900 background images, about 44 MB of decoded image cache held by an idle Studio, where only one should be.

## The change

- The runtime adds one rule when its script is evaluated, before the body is parsed: timed clips (not video, audio or img; the runtime's media pass already handles those) are hidden.
- The first visibility pass that decides those clips removes the rule. After that, as before, each clip shows or hides only through the inline visibility the pass writes, so behaviour after the first pass is unchanged.
- The rule and its flag live on the page, not in the runtime module. A second copy of the runtime (a sub-composition with its own runtime tag, or a page that includes it twice) shares them instead of adding a rule nothing removes.
- HyperShader's capture clone forces its scene visible with `!important`, so a transition captured before the first pass still shows the scene's clips.
- Color grading registers only media it can see. When the pass lifts the rule it refreshes grading, so an image or video inside a clip (with no timing of its own) is graded from the first frame.

## Limits

- When the runtime script is injected at the end of the body (the preview fallback when bundling fails, or a runtime injected into an already loaded document), the browser can paint the body before the rule exists. Those pages behave as before until the rule lands.
- A page that never reaches readiness and is never seeked now shows only its background instead of every clip stacked. Both are wrong. The one consumer found that screenshots such a page is `grade-compare`'s readiness-timeout path, which already warns that its output may be inaccurate.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/runtime/entry.test.ts`:
  - A composition evaluated while the document is still loading keeps its timed clips hidden before DOMContentLoaded and before readiness, including a clip whose script wrote an inline `visibility: visible`.
  - A timed image stays visible throughout.
  - After readiness, only the clip at the current time is visible.
  - A second evaluation of the runtime leaves a paused, never-seeked composition visible, with no rule left behind.
  - An untimed graded video inside a clip is registered for grading after readiness, with no seek.
- `packages/shader-transitions/src/capture.clone.test.ts`: the capture clone shows its scene and timed clips while the hide rule is up.
- Each of these changes, made on its own, turns a test red:
  - main's runtime;
  - dropping `!important`;
  - dropping the reveal;
  - revealing on the media-only pass;
  - hiding inside init instead of at evaluation;
  - hiding media too;
  - module-scoped state;
  - dropping the already-initialised guard;
  - dropping the grading refresh;
  - the clone without `important`.

## Captures

Before/After: the raw preview document of a 12-scene project loading at 1600x900, every frame the browser painted, from navigation until the first scene is up.

### Before

On main, a later scene (the colour bars) paints for about 100-150 ms before the first scene.

![Before: on main a later scene's colour bars paint before the first scene](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46ff1cc7-6c71-419a-9798-e4292bfd358f)

### After

With this change, only the background paints until the first scene is decided.

![After: only the background paints until the first scene](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f54dd0c7-3218-4c10-8a1e-b718ee2df9b8)

## Independent review

Three rounds of adversarial review, each checked with real-browser probes:

| Round | Found | Resolution |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | BLOCKER: a second runtime copy left its rule in place, so the film stayed invisible | Rule and flag moved onto the page; every copy shares them |
| 1 | MAJOR: HyperShader prewarm could capture scenes with their clips missing | Clone visibility forced with `!important` |
| 1 | MINOR: four load-bearing choices had no test | Tests added; each mutation now fails |
| 2 | MAJOR: grading skipped untimed media inside a clip | Pass refreshes grading when it lifts the rule |
| 2 | MINOR: second-copy test asserted only after a seek | Asserts on the paused page |
| 3 | No BLOCKERs, no MAJORs, no MINORs | |

Pre-existing issues found along the way, reported separately and not changed here:
- graded images in scenes after the first are never graded;
- HyperShader's html-in-canvas capture returns blank frames in engine-launched Chrome.

| Audited | Trusting | Not exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Real-Chromium probes: one and two runtime copies, sub-composition runtime, paused and seeked, grading pixels, capture clone | jsdom cascade for `!important` vs inline, cross-checked in Chromium | A full `hyperframes render` of a graded pure-image composition |
| Pixel consumers that seek or wait for readiness first: engine render, producer, Studio thumbnails, snapshot, compare, check | | `grade-compare` readiness-timeout path, by reading only |

title: docs(cli): explain how catalog search works and which model it downloads
body:
## Summary

`hyperframes catalog --query` can download a search model, but nothing in the docs said which model, why, what
lands on the machine, or what stays private. This adds a page that does, written from the code:

- **New page, Developers > Command line > How catalog search works** (`docs/developers/catalog-search.mdx`):
  the two ways search runs (word match by default, on-device meaning search after a yes), when the download
  prompt appears and what a yes does, the pinned model (`bge-small-en-v1.5`, quantized ONNX, fixed revision)
  and why it was chosen, every file downloaded with its source and location, what gets embedded for each item
  (title, description and tags, not the name), privacy (`catalog --query` sends nothing; only
  `feedback --search-miss` sends a query, and only when run), and how the index is built and checked (batches
  of 16 reproduce the shipped rows exactly).
- **CLI reference**: the `catalog` section now mentions `--query` and `--on-device` and links the page.
- **hyperframes-cli skill**: the offline-tier guidance links the page for when a person asks what the download
  is, and word match is described as covering tags too. `skills-manifest.json` regenerated.
- **`registry/catalog-artifact/README.md`**, corrected where it had gone stale: the JSON now records
  `modelRevision` and `revision` (the README said nothing was recorded), `media-vectors.*` also ship from that
  folder, the fixed row count is gone, and the rebuild runs through `bun run generate:catalog` and the catalog
  publication PR, not a lefthook pre-commit command (lefthook has none).
- **Stale code comments, no code changes**:
  - `localSearch.ts` said words of three characters or fewer are dropped; the tokenizer keeps three-letter
    words (`word.length > 2`), and the compound splitter relies on that floor. The header now states only the
    rules the code enforces.
  - `localModel.ts` named the comparison model "the hosted model"; its figures (62.3 MTEB, 1536 dimensions)
    are `text-embedding-3-small`'s. `localSemantic.ts` and `build-local-vectors.ts` called the hosted vectors
    1536-dimension; `build-catalog-artifact.ts` builds them with `text-embedding-3-large` at 3072.

## Checks run

- `mint validate`: build validation passed.
- `mint broken-links --check-redirects`: no broken links.
- Viewed the page on a local `mint dev`: it appears under Command line, and its tables and lists render.
- `gen-skills-manifest --check`, skill mirror, `lint-skills`, docs snippet checks: pass.
- oxfmt over the changed files: clean. `check-comment-citations`: OK.

## Pre-review

An independent review checked every factual sentence on the page, and every changed sentence elsewhere,
against the code, with the line that makes each true. Then a second pass reviewed the fixes.

| Finding | Severity | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| The page compared the model with a "1,536-dimension hosted model", but the hosted builder uses `text-embedding-3-large` at 3072 | blocking | fixed: the page names `text-embedding-3-small`, which the 62.3 and 1,536 figures belong to, and the three stale comments are corrected |
| A cosine figure for single-text embedding (0.9969) was backed only by the README's prose | note | fixed: removed from the page; the README keeps its own record |
| After the first fix, one sibling comment still said the hosted vectors are 1536-dimension | should fix | fixed |
| The `text-embedding-3-small` comparison is the recorded reason for the choice, not something the repo measures | note | kept: it is why the model was chosen, and no sentence on the page is false because of it |

Audited against the code: the prompt and consent flow and its order, prompts in terminals versus CI and `--json`,
model hashes, sizes and the revision pin, runtime before model, cache paths, vector refresh by revision,
word-match scoring, the "query is never sent" claim (no telemetry in `catalog.ts`; only `feedback --search-miss`
sends it), the rebuild paths, and the CI coverage check.

title: fix(registry): three blocks keep their settings when mounted
body:
## What changes for a user

Three registry blocks now keep their settings when they are added to a film:
- code-slice-hero rendered blank when mounted; it now matches the block opened on its own;
- frost-sequence-camera-orbit threw `rigSchema is not iterable` when mounted; it no longer does;
- oscilloscope-trace fell back to built-in defaults when mounted; it now reads its own settings, not the host film's.

## Why

These blocks declared their variables on `<html>` and read them back at runtime with `document.documentElement`. A mounted block brings no `<html>` along: `document.documentElement` is the host film's page, so the read came back empty or, worse, returned the host's declarations.

## How

Each block now declares on its own root (`#frost-root`, `#csh-root`, `#os-root`) and reads from it with `document.getElementById(...)`, which resolves inside the mounted block. Four registry blocks already declare this way (cosmic-orb, bar-chart-race, gallery-tunnel, week-in-merges). The runtime and the compiler read a root declaration, and #4454, which this PR is stacked on, makes the SDK (and so Studio's Variables panel) read it too.

The two components that declare on `<html>` (device-frame-stage, oversized-cursor) are not changed: their `<html>` is itself the composition root, and they install as snippets, not mounted files.

## Verification

- Variables the SDK sees, before and after, through `openComposition()`: frost 216 → 216, code-slice-hero 18 → 18, oscilloscope-trace 7 → 7.
- Each block opened on its own renders identically before and after (mean difference 0.0).
- Mounted vs standalone at mid-duration:
  - code-slice-hero: before 16.27 (blank frame), after 0.0;
  - oscilloscope-trace: 0.0 both before and after, because its defaults happen to match; it now reads its own settings.
- frost mounted: a render no longer throws `rigSchema is not iterable` and gets as far as the WebGPU check.
- `hyperframes lint` counts match the base; catalog drift check passes.
- Metadata (`--strict-variables`) sees the same variables as the SDK: 216, 18 and 7.

### Before

code-slice-hero mounted (left), blank.

### After

code-slice-hero mounted (middle) and opened on its own (right).

![code-slice-hero: mounted before, mounted after, standalone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/369418fb-497b-4e97-9211-11fd2a486bab)

Independent review, two rounds.
- Round 1 found that the metadata `--strict-variables` reads and the lint rule looked at `<html>` only, so this move would have hidden the three blocks' variables from them. #4454 now reads root declarations in both.
- Round 2 reproduced these results independently:
  - metadata and SDK counts of 216, 18 and 7, with no lint findings; reverting #4454's metadata fix drops all three to 0;
  - code-slice-hero and oscilloscope-trace mounted are byte-identical to standalone;
  - frost reaches its WebGPU check with no `rigSchema` error;
  - two oscilloscope-trace instances with different settings, mounted in one film, each render their own.

## What I did NOT exercise

- frost rendered with a GPU: it needs WebGPU, and my render machine has none.
