title: feat(cli): timeline undo reverts the history entry its receipt names
body:
## What

`hyperframes timeline` edits now go into the project's history, and `timeline undo` undoes them through it. The per-write backup folder (`.hyperframes/backup`) is gone.

- **Each timeline edit is one history entry.** `move`, `trim`, `split`, `delete`, `set`, `duplicate`, `ids` and `apply` write inside a window of their own, labelled after the command (for example "timeline move #clip"). The entry goes under the open turn's writer, if an agent has one open, and under You otherwise. Through a running preview the edit uses the preview's window routes; without one it uses the engine directly.
- **Receipts name their entry.** Every receipt carries `entryId`. `backupPath` is removed.
- **`timeline undo <receipt>` undoes that entry**, the same way `hyperframes history undo <id>` does. That includes its conflict choices when a file changed since. A receipt from before this change has no `entryId` and is refused (exit 2), with the fix: find the change with `hyperframes history`, then run `hyperframes history undo <id>`.
- **The backup journal is deleted.** Studio's file routes and `applyFileMutations` no longer copy each file into `.hyperframes/backup` before writing. The history already keeps every version. The project file list still hides a leftover `.hyperframes/backup` folder in existing projects.
- **When another process holds the history** and no preview reaches it, the edit is still written, with `entryId: null` and a warning. The history's owner records it as a change made outside.

## Why

There were two undo records for the same project: the backup journal and the project history. `timeline undo` only knew the first, and only as a copy of one file, even when an `apply` changed several. With the history there is one list of every writer's changes, and a timeline edit shows up in it like any other, with its own undo and conflict choices.

## Tests

- `timeline.e2e.test.ts` (runs the real CLI, with its history kept in a temp HOME):
  - an edit is one history entry named on its receipt, and `timeline undo` with that receipt reverts it;
  - a receipt from before the history is refused and points at `history undo`;
  - the existing plan-and-undo test now goes through the history.

  Both new tests fail on the base branch.
- `routes/files.test.ts`: writes, deletes and DOM mutations leave no backup folder. The three tests for a failing backup are removed, since there is no backup left to fail.
- `applyFileMutations.test.ts`: updated to the signature without the project folder.
- `history.test.ts`: a write recorded through `recordInHistory` is one entry under its label with its id handed back, both directly and through a running preview.

## Notes

- Stacked on #4449, which owns the history command and its owner helper. This PR adds `record` to that owner, plus `recordInHistory` and `undoEntry`.
- The JSON that `timeline undo` prints is now `history undo`'s result, not a list of receipts.
- `timeline undo` records the undo under You, or under `--who <name>` as `history undo --who` does (which first ends that agent's open turn).

title: ci: comment checks grade branches cut before their scripts existed
body:
## What

A PR whose branch was cut before a Comments script existed crashes the Comments job before any comment is graded. Branches older than #4444 fail on `scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs`, and branches older than #4445 fail on `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs` with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. The job ran every script from the PR's own head, and an older branch has no copy.

Now one list in the job names every repo script it runs, and a first step picks where they run from:
- **The branch has all of them:** its own copies run, as before, so a PR that fixes a check is graded by its fix.
- **The branch lacks any of them:** the job checks out the base commit next to the PR head and runs all of them from there. They import each other, so they always come from one tree.

Grading is unchanged: the PR's own head against its merge-base, not the merge preview.

## Proof

- **Real CI on a branch cut before #4445,** with a dead citation planted and this workflow in force (a throwaway draft PR, since closed):
  - Picking: the job picked the base's scripts.
  - Tests: the checker's 91 tests passed.
  - Grading: the citation checker reported the planted citation, and the ratchet graded the branch, instead of `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.
- **Before this fix, a branch cut before #4444, on Linux:** the old wiring crashed on the missing script. The base's checker graded the branch and reported the citation.
- **New `scripts/comments-workflow.test.mjs`:**
  - What it runs: the pick step in a temp workspace, first with every script present, then with each one missing.
  - What it asserts: the base checkout and every script step follow the pick, and every script the job runs is in the list.
  - Result: 4 of 4 pass. It fails against main's workflow, when the pick always uses the PR's copies, and when the ratchet is left off the list.

title: fix(core): a seek during playback lands a playing video on the new time
body:
## What was wrong

A seek while the film plays (the transport `seek` handler) sets the transport to paused and syncs media in the same pass. During that pass the `<video>` element is still playing, so `syncRuntimeMedia` counted it as a playing video. It skipped the forced correction (which it withholds from playing videos so their decoder does not stutter), then paused the element wherever it was. When a clip lags the playhead (for example, a clip that has just started playing), the preview kept that stale frame until the next seek.

In the preview: a clip entering at 3.85 s, playing at 4.03 s with the clip still at 0.03 s, seek to 4.4 s. The clip paused at 0.03 s instead of 0.55 s. Pause does not have the problem, because it hard-syncs media before the sync pass. Seek and render seek do not.

## Fix

The playing-video exemption now applies only while the transport keeps playing. When the transport is paused, the same pass pauses the element, so there is no decoder stutter to avoid, and a forced seek lands the video on the new time. Behaviour with the transport playing is unchanged.

## Tests

- `media.test.ts`: "a seek that pauses mid-playback lands a lagging playing video on the new time". It fails with the old line and passes with the fix.
- Runtime suite: 59 files, 1301 tests pass. oxlint, oxfmt and `tsc` are clean.

## Before

A seek to 4.4 s while the clip plays: the clip stays on its first frame (cover only).

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/24185ad8-88a8-434e-ada2-2ea31ef2410b)

## After

The same seek: the clip lands at 0.55 s.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61e8e228-3889-45c2-8b06-de312359359e)

title: ci(windows): run each Windows test group on its own runner
body:
## What

The Windows tests are the last required check to finish on most PRs: they were last on 28 of the last 40 merged PRs.

They ran on two runners, and each runner did its work in series:
- **First runner:** a Studio shard, then the core, player and shader-transitions tests.
- **Second runner:** the other Studio shard, then the engine and CLI tests, the runtime contract, and the Windows-only file checks.

Each group now gets its own runner: studio-1, studio-2, core, and engine-cli. They are the same tests, with the same worker caps, on four runners instead of two. The required check, `Tests on windows-latest`, keeps its name and still fails when any lane does.

The Studio halves and the engine and CLI suites still never share a runner. #3579 found that sharing one runner is what caused load timeouts.

## Before and after, from real CI runs

The Windows workflow was dispatched on this change and on an unchanged copy of main at the same moment, three times, so runner queueing hit both alike.

| Pair | This change | Main | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 529 s | 758 s | -229 s |
| 2 | 586 s | 676 s | -90 s |
| 3 | 558 s | 718 s | -160 s |
| **Median** | **558 s** | **718 s** | **-22%** |

- **Same tests:** every run of this change passed 15,994 vitest tests on Windows. Two of the main runs passed the same number and one passed 15,993.
- **Cost:** about 7 more Windows runner-minutes per run, from the two extra runners' setup. That is accepted for the shorter wait.

title: ci: run the required checks on merge queue groups
body:
## What

This lets main use a GitHub merge queue. Today every merge sends every approved PR back for a full rerun and a branch update. With a queue, the required checks run once on the queued merge instead.

A queue only merges when every required check reports on the queued merge. So each workflow that produces one now also runs on `merge_group`: `ci.yml`, `regression.yml`, `windows-render.yml`, `pr-captures.yml`, and `codeql.yml` for the code scanning rule.

How the checks behave in the queue:
- **Semantic PR title:** skipped in the queue, as it already was off pull requests. A skipped required check counts as passing, and the title was checked on the PR.
- **Studio and player captures:** now skipped in the queue. It reads the PR body, and a queued merge has none. The captures were checked on the PR.
- **Path-filtered jobs:** they still report. `dorny/paths-filter`, at the version pinned here, diffs the group's base against its head. A job its filter skips reports as skipped.
- **Aggregators:** `Test`, `regression` and `Tests on windows-latest` already fail closed on any failed or cancelled lane.
- **Concurrency:** each queue entry has its own ref, so runs of different entries never cancel each other.

## Verification

- The existing workflow tests pass (81 of 81), including the edit-concurrency and captures tests.
- An independent review walked every required check's jobs, `needs` and `if` conditions under `merge_group`.

## Before turning the queue on

- **CodeQL:** confirm that the first queued run posts a code scanning result. An old report says the CodeQL action once failed to post one on `merge_group`.
- **Render on windows-latest:** a separate PR fixes a bug that predates this one. The check is skipped, which counts as passing, when the lint preflight fails.

title: fix(ci): required checks fail instead of skipping when a job they need fails
body:
## What

A job skipped because a job it needs failed reports "skipped", and a skipped required check counts as passing. So several required checks passed without running:
- **Render on windows-latest,** when the lint and format preflight failed.
- **Typecheck, Build and Test: runtime contract,** when change detection failed.
- **Test and Tests on windows-latest,** when change detection failed before it set its outputs.

#4347 fixed this for the `regression` summary only.

Now these jobs run unless the run is cancelled. Their first step fails when a job they need did not succeed. A docs-only change still skips them as before, and a green run is unchanged.

## Proof, on real CI

Two scratch branches, one on main and one on this fix, each broke the preflight with a badly formatted file and change detection with an `exit 1`. Then the CI and Windows workflows were dispatched on both.

| Required check | main | this fix |
|---|---|---|
| Render on windows-latest (preflight failed) | skipped, so it passed | failure |
| Typecheck (change detection failed) | skipped, so it passed | failure |
| Build (change detection failed) | skipped, so it passed | failure |
| Test: runtime contract (change detection failed) | skipped, so it passed | failure |
| Test, Tests on windows-latest | failure | failure |

The runs on main were 36090489786 and 36090488082. The runs on this fix were 36090492993 and 36090491439. The simulated breakage fails after the filter has already set its outputs, which is why `Test` fails on main too. When the filter itself fails, its outputs are empty and `Test` skips on main; this fix covers that case as well.

This matters more once main uses a merge queue (#4469): a queue merges on its own as soon as the required checks pass.

title: fix(core): a Lottie animation in a mounted composition plays from its start
body:
## What changes for a user

A Lottie animation inside a composition mounted later in a film now plays from that composition's start, the way it does when the composition is opened on its own. Before, it ran ahead by however late the composition started. For example, lottie-character-walk mounted at 3 s showed, at its own first second, the pose from its fourth.

## Why

The runtime's Lottie adapter seeked every registered player to the page's time. The CSS adapter already subtracts each element's composition start; the Lottie one did not.

## How

- `createLottieAdapter` takes the same `resolveStartSeconds` the CSS adapter takes, and the runtime passes its existing start resolver.
- For each player, the adapter finds the composition containing its element (lottie-web's `wrapper`, dotlottie's `canvas`) and seeks to page time minus that composition's start.
- A player outside any composition, or in one that starts at 0, is seeked exactly as before.

## Verification

- New adapter tests use the runtime's real start resolver. A lottie-web player and a dotlottie player in a composition mounted at 3 s seek to local time: 1 s at page time 4, and 0 before the composition starts. A player in a composition starting at 0 keeps page time. Reverting the adapter change fails them. Lottie adapter tests: 32 pass. Core typecheck clean; comment ratchet passes.
- End to end with the CLI's snapshot: lottie-character-walk mounted at `data-start="3"`, snapshotted at 4, 5 and 7 s, against the block opened on its own at 1, 2 and 4 s:
  - before: 104,548, 101,393 and 80,063 pixels differ;
  - after: 0 at every time.

Before (left) and after (middle), mounted at 3 s and captured at 5 s, against the block on its own at 2 s (right):

![lottie-character-walk mounted: before, after, standalone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b274443-182c-41c2-b96f-8de170cf8be5)

Independent review: no blocking findings.
- It checked the property names against the real libraries: lottie-web 5.12.2's `AnimationItem.wrapper` and dotlottie-web's `canvas` getter.
- `init.ts` is the one place the adapter is created, and every render path goes through it.
- The runtime suite passes: 1,305 tests.
- It reproduced the end-to-end numbers.

Two notes are kept as they are:
- The one-line `init.ts` wiring is covered only by the end-to-end check, as the CSS adapter's wiring beside it is.
- A dotlottie player with no `canvas`, or an `OffscreenCanvas` one, keeps page time, as before this change.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A full `render` to video; the snapshots use the same runtime seek.
- dotlottie-web end to end; its path is covered by the unit test only. No registry block uses dotlottie.

title: ci(regression): rebalance shards on current fixture timings
body:
## What

The producer regression check is the last required check to finish on PRs that touch the producer, engine or core: it was last on 11 of the last 40 merged PRs.

Its fixtures are bin-packed into shards using the per-fixture timings in `packages/producer/tests/shard-schedule.json`. Those timings came from an old CI run. They added up to 6,738 seconds, while the fixtures now run in about 2,900, and their proportions had drifted. So some shards ran their fixtures for 174 seconds and others for 494.

Each timing is now the median of two recent green main runs, 36060644404 and 36034224538. A fixture's time runs from its `test_start` event in the shard log to the next fixture's start. `typegpu-adapter` and `webm-transparency` keep their existing values: the CI test image skips them by tag, so they never run in a shard. The fixture set is unchanged, and the planner now packs the eight in-process shards at about 5.6 minutes each.

## Before and after, from real CI runs

The regression workflow was dispatched with every shard, on this change and on an unchanged copy of main at the same moment, three times.

| Pair | This change | Main | Slowest shard (this change / main) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 789 s | 809 s | 633 s / 727 s |
| 2 | 717 s | 809 s | 619 s / 727 s |
| 3 | 701 s | 793 s | 608 s / 701 s |
| **Median** | **717 s** | **809 s (-11%)** | |

- **Required checks:** every run was green.
- **Tests:** `regression-shard-plan.test.ts` passes, 18 of 18.
- **Cost:** the runner-minutes are about the same.

title: fix(studio): every project opens its preview at Fit, and a zoom says so
body:
## What changes

Every project opens its preview at Fit. Before, the preview zoom was one value saved for every project, so a single pinch (on purpose or by accident) made each project open zoomed to about 245%, which reads as a preview that is cut off.

- A zoom now lasts only while that project is open. Switching to another project resets to Fit, and nothing about zoom is saved (an old saved value is ignored and dropped on the next preference write).
- While the preview is not at Fit, a chip at the top of the canvas says so: `Zoomed 248% · Fit` (or `Panned · Fit` after a pan at 100%). `Fit` puts the whole frame back.
- A small navigator in the bottom-right corner shows which part of the frame is visible, and follows a pan or pinch as it happens. Both vanish at Fit. They replace the old `248% — Reset` corner button.

## Before

A pinch on one project, then another project opened: it opens at 248% with its diagram cut off, and only the corner button as a hint.

![Before: a second project opens at 248%, its diagram cut off](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3090445b-1ed1-461c-b1c9-f6501c4946cd)

## After

The same saved 248% is still in storage, and the project opens at Fit. A pinch shows the chip and the navigator, and `Fit` clears both.

![After: the same saved 248%, the project opens at Fit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bd67df0-4c01-463f-bb7d-15109ebbba33)

![After: a pinch shows the Zoomed 248% · Fit chip and the navigator](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c25a1f0-dc2f-457a-9399-baa2219cd7b7)

![After: Fit returns to the whole frame, chip and navigator gone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e417ac8d-7d7f-45c4-8568-6a954f980efa)

## UX checklist

**Job:** someone editing a film who zoomed the preview (on purpose or with an accidental pinch) needs to know the view is zoomed and get back to the whole frame.
**One action:** Fit.

| # | Question | Y/N | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Clear what the state is and what to do | Y | chip text `Zoomed 248%` next to `Fit` |
| 2 | Interactive things look interactive | Y | `Fit` is an accent-coloured button with hover; navigator is `pointer-events-none`, `aria-hidden` |
| 3 | User's words, no internal ids | Y | "Zoomed", "Panned", "Fit" |
| 4 | Works like other tools | Y | corner navigator as in Figma and Photoshop; zoom readout plus fit action as in most editors |
| 5 | Guidance at the control | Y | the chip sits on the canvas it describes |
| 6 | Primary action reachable without reading | Y | top centre of the canvas, where the eye goes after a pinch |
| 7 | Exactly one primary action | Y | `Fit` is the only button in the chip |
| 8 | Numbers match the data | Y | the chip rounds the settled zoom state; the test asserts `Zoomed 2xx%` after a pinch |
| 9 | Hidden state announces itself | Y | that is this PR: a zoom no longer hides behind a saved value |
| 10 | Truncation | n/a | no names shown |
| 11 | Keyboard path | Y | `Fit` is a native button with `aria-label="Fit the whole frame in view"` |
| 12 | Visible without hover or scroll | Y | the chip and navigator show whenever the view is not at Fit |
| 13-15 | Refusals and errors | n/a | none on this surface |
| 16 | Get out of any state without losing work | Y | Fit, or opening another project; zoom never changes the film |
| 17 | Destructive action distinct | n/a | none |
| 18 | Empty states | n/a | none |
| 19 | Feedback within 400 ms | Y | the navigator follows each wheel event; the chip appears when the zoom settles (200 ms) |
| 20 | Progress for long waits | n/a | none |
| 21 | Hand-built state survives a reload | N, deliberate | zoom is a view setting, not work; the decided shape is Fit on every open |

**Not exercised:** a real trackpad pinch (captures drive the same wheel events with `ctrlKey`, which is what a trackpad pinch sends).
**Traded off:** #21, by decision: a zoom no longer survives a reload or a project switch.

## Tests

- `NLEPreview.test.ts`: opens at Fit even with a saved 245%; a pinch shows `Zoomed …% · Fit` and the navigator, and `Fit` clears both; a zoom is not saved and does not follow into another project; a pan at 100% reads `Panned`. With `NLEPreview.tsx` and `studioUiPreferences.ts` from main, all of these fail. The old two-finger pan test also failed on main once the preferences mock was removed, because main saved each pan and the next test opened with it.
- `previewZoom.test.ts`: the visible part of the frame at Fit, at 200%, and after a pan.
- `studioUiPreferences.test.ts`: a stored preview zoom is no longer read.
- A click on `Fit` stops at the chip, so it no longer clears the timeline selection (test fails without it).
- `src/components/nle` and `src/utils`: 792 tests pass; studio `tsc` is clean.

Captures: taken on the first commit (the review fixes after it change no pixels, except that focus returns to the preview after Fit), from a dev Studio on a Linux box with two registry examples (decision-tree and kinetic-type) as projects, driven by agent-browser, at 1440×900.

title: refactor(studio): drop recordEdit's kind, which the project history never read
body:
## What

Studio's `recordEdit` no longer takes a `kind` (manual, motion, timeline or source). Since #4456, an edit is recorded by claiming the files it wrote on the project's history, and the history never read `kind`. The field, the `EditHistoryKind` type and its file are deleted, along with every caller's copy of the value.

`heldFor`'s one-line doc in the history engine now names both of its conditions, as the #4456 reviewers asked.

## Why

A parameter every caller fills in and nothing reads is a false promise: a reader assumes the kind changes how the edit is undone, and it does not.

## Before

An outside edit, then Ctrl+Z, at #4456's head.

![Before: after Ctrl+Z, the title is restored and the toast names the step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bce7ae1e-8e2a-40a0-85a3-5ac17a358444)

## After

The same walk at this head. Undo behaves the same.

![After: after Ctrl+Z, the title is restored and the toast names the step](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b79c4aa3-c4f4-4e52-b64f-5c3cf4f68b2f)

## Tests

- The Studio typecheck and lint are clean; the full Studio suite (5513) and the history tests pass.
- Tests that asserted an edit's `kind` now assert its label, coalesce key and files only.

## Notes

- Stacked on #4456; it merges after it.
- Hosts that forward `recordEdit` (Desktop does) are unaffected; a host that built its own `recordEdit` input with `kind` gets a type error on the extra property.

title: fix(producer): give each parallel segmented-capture worker its own browser
body:
## What was broken

Segmented capture with two or more workers failed before the first frame on Linux:

```
HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true HF_SEGMENTED_MIN_SECONDS=1 HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=100 \
  hyperframes render -o o.mp4 -w 2 --quality draft
→ Invalid JPEG input at frame 0: empty frame
```

`-w 1` passed, and so did a render with a single segment.

## Why

Two bugs in `captureSegmentedStage.ts`, both only visible with more than one worker:

1. **Workers shared one Chrome.** Each fresh worker session came from the pooled browser, so N workers meant N pages in one Chrome process. BeginFrame capture does not survive that: a worker's first `beginFrame` came back with no screenshot. The parallel disk path already avoids this through `shouldDisableBrowserPoolForParallelWorker` (`parallelCoordinator.ts`). The segmented stage never called it. This is the cause of the reported failure.
2. **Every worker could take the probe session.** `defaultSessionFactory` was built once per worker, and each copy started holding `input.probeSession`. When a probe session exists, every worker reused that same page. This did not trigger in the repro above, which has no probe session, but it is the same class of fault.

## Fix

- Fresh segmented worker sessions ask `shouldDisableBrowserPoolForParallelWorker` and open their own browser when it says to. That function stays the single owner of the rule; the engine now exports it.
- The default session factory is built once per run, so only the first worker takes the probe session. The probe branch inside `openSegmentedSession` could never run and is gone.
- Workers are now created inside the `try`. With one Chrome per worker, a later worker that fails to launch would otherwise leak the browsers already opened, since the `finally` never ran.

- The default session factory now closes a fresh session when its initialization throws, then rethrows. The streaming stage already does this; the segmented factory leaked that Chrome on a page-load or init timeout.

Not in this PR: when there are more workers than pending segments, the extra workers still open a browser each. Clamping the worker count changes the single-worker fallback rule, so that belongs in its own change.

## Verification

- Exact repro built from `main`: exits 1 with `empty frame`, one browser launched.
- The same repro built from this branch: exits 0 at `-w 2` and at `-w 3`, one browser per worker, 300 frames in the output.
- New unit test `gives each parallel worker its own browser and the probe session to one worker`: passes with the fix. It fails when either change is reverted on its own (the pool change: config assertion; the shared factory: 1 distinct session instead of 2).
- New unit test `closes the workers already opened when a later worker fails to launch`: fails when the creation loop is moved back outside the `try`, passes with the fix.
- New unit test `closes a fresh session whose initialization fails`: fails without the close, passes with it.
- `captureSegmentedStage`, `captureStreamingStage`, `probeStage` and `encodeStage` tests pass together (96 tests; these four files fully mock the engine module). Engine and producer typecheck, oxlint, and the comment ratchet are all clean.

title: fix(core): preview time follows a voiceover that plays through Web Audio
body:
## What was wrong

In preview, a same-origin `<audio data-start>` plays through the Web Audio media-element route (`scheduleMediaElementPlayback`). On that route the element still keeps its own source time; Web Audio is only downstream of it.

The transport clock, though, followed `AudioContext` time whenever `webAudio.isActive()` was true, and `isActive()` counted routed sources too. So when the voiceover stalled to buffer or started late, the timeline kept running without it. `syncRuntimeMedia` then seeked the element forward to catch up, which skipped speech, started a new buffer stall, and repeated.

Measured in a real preview of a 50 s film whose only audio is a voiceover (every media element sampled every 100 ms for 12 s of playback from 0):

|  | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Largest timeline vs voiceover gap | 2.97 s | 0.00 s |
| Forward seeks during playback | 5 (+3.49, +0.84, +1.09, +1.73 s, and one small one) | 0 |
| Speech skipped | 7.42 s | 0 s |

After the fix, while the voiceover buffers, the picture waits and resumes with the voice.

## The fix

`isActive()` had one caller: the clock choice in `init.ts`. It is now `ownsClock()`, true only while a decoded `AudioBufferSourceNode` plays, since only then is `AudioContext` time the source time. A routed element falls through to the existing element-clock branch, so the timeline reads the element's `currentTime`.

## Tests

- `init.test.ts`: a routed voiceover (asserted: one `createMediaElementSource`) that is playing but stuck buffering. After 2 s of `AudioContext` time the timeline holds under 0.1 s and nothing seeks the element forward. With the old body, the timeline reaches 2.0 s.
- `webAudioTransport.test.ts`: a routed element does not make the transport own the clock. With the old body this is `true`.
- The Web Audio test setup (mock `AudioContext`, `mountAudio`, `startPlayback`) is now shared by both describes.

## Known limits, unchanged by this PR

- The element-clock branch follows the first in-window `audio[data-start]` in document order. If a music bed comes before the voiceover, a voiceover stall is still corrected by seeking it.
- A decoded buffer (a CORS-enabled cross-origin track, or the decode fallback) together with a routed track keeps `AudioContext` as the clock, as before.
- Volume and FX automation lanes are scheduled on `AudioContext` time, so during a stall of a routed track they keep running. Before, the forward seek kept them aligned, at the cost of skipped audio.
- Other media (a second routed track, a playing video) keeps playing while the clock waits for a stalled first track, and is corrected afterwards.


## Before

The same 50 s preview on a slow machine, with a readout drawn into the preview: the timeline's time, the voiceover's time, their gap, and each time the runtime seeks the voiceover during playback. Before, the voiceover stalls, the picture runs ahead, and the voice is seeked forward (+0.69 s here).

![Before and after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/269464c0-9530-4c73-bda9-6f4b6c52f392)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4565b04-0863-4b32-8645-750a85f03e97

## After

The picture waits while the voiceover buffers: the gap stays at 0.00 s and the voice is never seeked forward.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13be8155-2728-48d6-a9fc-61ba84559bc4

title: fix(cli): render --quiet stops printing producer info and trace lines
body:
## What changes for the person rendering

`hyperframes render --quiet` in a terminal no longer prints the producer's `[INFO]` lines, the `[Render:trace]` JSON among them. A plain `render` still prints them, since tools parse those trace lines for progress. The page's fps line reads as JSON instead of `[object Object]`.

Before, under `script` (a TTY), `render --quiet` printed every producer `[INFO]` line, among them each `[Render:trace] {...}` event and a worker's local browser executable path, plus `[HyperFrames] render runtime fps [object Object]`.

## Where each fix lives

- **`--quiet` level** (`cli/src/commands/render.ts`): the CLI created the producer logger at `info` whether or not `--quiet` was set. It is now `warn` under `--quiet`; `--debug` still wins. Telemetry is unaffected: the CLI's telemetry logger tracks every trace regardless of the console level. `render --batch ... --json` already renders as quiet (`execute.ts`), so its stderr loses the trace lines too; a plain render and a plain batch keep them.
- **fps line** (`core/src/runtime/init.ts`): the engine forwards page console output as text (`msg.text()`), which flattens an object argument. The runtime now logs one string with the fields as JSON.
- **Trace level stays `info`**: an earlier version moved `[Render:trace]` to `debug`, which would silently break consumers that parse the lines from a plain render. A test now pins that contract.

## Not in this PR

A few engine lines print with a bare `console.log` and so ignore `--quiet`: `[BrowserManager] Browser launched`, `[initSession:*]` timings, and page logs forwarded as `[HyperFrames] ...`. Silencing them means routing the engine's own output through a level-aware logger, a separate change.

## Tests

- `render.test.ts`: `--quiet` creates the producer logger at `warn`, a plain render at `info`, `--debug` at `debug`.
- `observability.test.ts`: through the real console logger, a stage's `[Render:trace]` lines print at `info` (a plain render) and not at `warn` (`--quiet`).
- `init.test.ts`: the fps log is one string whose JSON carries the fields.

Each fails on the change it guards: the old `--quiet` level (1), traces moved to `debug` (1), the old fps call (2). A real `render --quiet` of a fresh `init` project under `script` printed no `[INFO]` or `[Render:trace]` line and wrote the mp4.

## Review

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Change request | Moving traces to `debug` breaks consumers that parse them from a plain render | Traces stay at `info`; only `--quiet` changes; test added |
| Should-fix (independent review) | Failed-stage traces at `warn` still printed under `--quiet` | Moot: under `--quiet` the logger is `warn` and traces are `info` |
| Nit | An unrelated schedule file rode along | Fixed by rebasing onto main |
| Nit (second review) | The console spy was not restored on a failed assertion; an engine fixture still showed the old flattened fps log | Fixed |

title: fix(studio): render a missing preview poster in either order and bank the open counts
body:
## Summary

Every Studio PR now fails "Studio: timeline viewport gate", and the merge queue drops them for the same reason. #4401 and the open-journey count gate were each green alone. With both on main, opening the fixture film does less rendering and makes two more requests, and the checked-in ceilings still hold the old numbers.

Banking the new numbers alone would have banked a race. #4401 shows a cached frame-0 poster while the preview boots. When the cache misses, it asks the server to render that poster for the next open. But it only asks if the cache miss arrives before the live preview is ready to show. If the live preview wins, the poster image is unmounted, the miss is never seen, the next open has no poster either, and the gate would read one request fewer. CI has read the same counts every time so far, because a cold boot takes seconds, but that depends on timing.

This PR:

1. **Fixes the race in Studio.** The render for the next open fires once the poster is known missing *and* the live frame is ready, in either order. The poster stays mounted, hidden, until its cache-only request settles, so a late 404 is still seen.
2. **Banks the open counts at main's numbers**, which no longer depend on arrival order:

| Counter | Was | Now | Why |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `thumbnailRenders` | 20 | 14 | #4401: clip thumbnails reuse the composition card's frame (13 renders at t=3.00), plus one poster render at t=0 |
| `total.requests.thumbnail` | 20 | 22 | #4401: the cache-only poster request (a miss on a fresh open), then the poster render for the next open |

3. **Adds a way to raise a ceiling on purpose**, with a reason in `perf-ceilings.json`, so the next deliberate change doesn't need a special PR. Before this, a ceiling could never go up, which is how two green PRs left main red.

## Before

An unrelated core PR fails the Studio gate:

![Before: an unrelated core PR fails the Studio viewport gate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33ffa7fd-beb2-4fee-9dec-d9a6f4ed4840)

## After

The same gate on this branch passes, and the raise prints its reason:

![After: the same gate passes on this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2df1a3e5-c882-4ad2-a37a-e75b7b5f7498)

## How a raise works now

A ceiling can still only go down, unless the PR says why it goes up. Each journey in `perf-ceilings.json` can have a `raised` map with a reason for each counter:

```json
"raised": {
  "total.requests.thumbnail": "#4401 shows a cached frame-0 poster while the preview boots: a cache-only ask that misses on a fresh open, then a render of that poster for the next open (+2 requests)"
}
```

- In CI, a ceiling above the base branch's passes only if its reason is new: not blank, and not the base branch's text for that counter (whitespace changes don't count). The next PR that raises the same counter has to write its own reason, and a copied reason fails.
- The job log prints each accepted raise with its reason, so reviewers see it in the check, not only in the JSON diff. Only counters that actually rose get the note.
- A raise without a reason fails, and the message now points at `raised`. Removed ceilings and dropped journeys still fail, reason or not.

## Checks run

- `NLEPreview.test.ts`: 15 passed. New: a missing poster is rendered when the live frame is ready first, when the poster is missing first (once, even when "ready" repeats), and on a return from a sub-composition. On main the first and third fail, and so does the updated cover test; the return test also fails on this PR's earlier head. Studio typecheck: clean.

- `perf-ratchet.test.mjs`: 23 passed, 8 of them new, including two that run the `check` CLI against a base file. Each rule turns a test red when removed: ignoring the base's reason (in the helper or in the CLI), dropping accepted raises, accepting a blank or respaced reason, and noting counters that did not rise.
- The check CLI, run against main's `perf-ceilings.json` as the base with the counts CI measured:
  - this branch passes, and prints the reason;
  - the same file without the reason fails;
  - a later raise that reuses the reason fails;
  - an unchanged file after merge passes;
  - main's script fails, as CI does.
- oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files: clean. `fallow audit --base origin/main`: no issues in changed files.

## For maintainers

- With this, raising a ceiling takes a sentence in `perf-ceilings.json`, so it holds only if a reviewer reads that file. A CODEOWNERS entry for it would make every raise need an owner's review. That's your call; this PR doesn't add one.
- On main and in the merge queue there is no base file (that step runs on pull requests only), so those runs compare counts only.

## Pre-review

Two independent reviews, one of the ratchet and one of the poster fix, found nothing blocking. Their findings, all fixed here:

| Finding | Severity | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| A whitespace-only edit to an existing reason counted as a new reason | should fix | fixed: reasons compare after collapsing whitespace; tested |
| The CLI's comparison against the base file had no test (two mutants passed) | should fix | fixed: two `check` CLI tests |
| The "raised on purpose" note printed for counters that did not rise | nit | fixed: only raised counters are accepted |
| The CI comment still said a ceiling may not rise | nit | fixed |
| The reason described the #4401 mechanism loosely | nit | reworded |
| Non-string and blank reasons were not fully tested | nit | tested |
| Poster: returning from a sub-composition brought the race back, because the hook's flags were keyed by a name that repeats | should fix | fixed: each stay on a composition is its own visit; tested |
| Poster: nothing tested that a repeated "ready" renders only once (the Player does repeat it) | should fix | tested |
| Poster: a late load of the hidden poster could resize the stage | nit | a hidden poster no longer reports its size |
| Poster: naming and a style spread where the native `hidden` attribute works | nit | renamed; uses `hidden` |

title: fix(studio-server): previewing a project never rewrites its files
body:
## What was wrong

The preview routes wrote `data-hf-id` into project files the first time they served each composition: `persistHfIdsIfNeeded` on the main build, and `stampFileHfIds` on the sub-composition route. Timeline thumbnails request every sub-composition, so opening and playing a film rewrote its files one after another. A host's file watcher sees each write as an outside edit and reloads the preview mid-playback. In one play of a 50 s film with 16 sections, 8 composition files were rewritten, and the preview reloaded 8 to 10 times. The rewrite also reformats the author's HTML (the doctype's case, multi-line attributes collapsed onto one line).

## The fix

- **Serving never writes.** Serve paths mint ids in memory from the raw file (`ensureHfIds`), before any rewrite, so each served id is the one the source file mints. `persistHfIdsIfNeeded` is deleted.
- **Ids reach disk in two ways only:** once when a project opens (`stampProjectHfIds`, which the CLI already calls at start), and with a real save. A matched save already returns `ensureHfIds(html)`. `parseSourceDocument` now mints before its lookup, so a save finds an element by its served id even when the file has no ids yet.
- **GSAP saves mint too.** A tween added on an element with no `id` targets `[data-hf-id="…"]`, the served id. The GSAP mutation routes (single and batch) parse the file through `extractGsapScriptBlock`, which now mints first, so the tween and the element's id land in the same write. Without it the tween is saved but the id is not, and a render (which never mints) drops the animation. No other save route stores a served id as a reference without minting.
- **Compositions added after open.** When an agent adds a composition, the bundler inlines it and rewrites its attributes (sibling asset paths, inline styles). Minting after the bundle would give ids the source doesn't have, and a save would miss them. So `bundleToSingleHtml` gets a `stampHfIds` option. It mints on each HTML source as the bundler reads it: the entry and every inlined sub-composition. `adapter.bundle(dir, options)` gains the argument. The preview build is the one place that sets it, and hosts only spread it over their own options (the CLI and the Studio Vite adapter here). Renders never set it.

A host that implements `StudioApiAdapter.bundle` should forward `options` to `bundleToSingleHtml`. Without that, a composition added after open is served with ids minted after the bundle. `docs/packages/studio-server.mdx` now says so.

## Tests

- **Serving leaves files alone.** Serving the preview and a sub-composition twice leaves both files' bytes and mtime unchanged (fails on main).
- **Saves find served ids** in a sub-composition with no ids on disk, and in a composition the bundler inlined and re-pointed (the second fails without the bundler option).
- **GSAP saves:** a tween added on a served id saves that id onto the element, through the single route, the batch route, and a file with no GSAP script yet (all three fail without the mint).
- **Core:** the option gives an inlined, re-pointed element the id its source mints (fails without the option), and a render bundle carries no ids.
- **CLI:** a scene added after open is served with its source's ids, and neither its file nor `index.html` is written (fails without the host forwarding the option).
- **Existing tests updated.** The four id-consistency tests now compare against `ensureHfIds(raw)` instead of the disk. The template clone-source guard moves to the save. The fragment removal test now expects ids after a save.

## Before

The CLI's Studio server on main, with a project where an agent adds a scene after open; then the preview and every scene are served twice.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e957757b-af03-4e6a-948c-c2d2aa17e629)

## After

The same project and the same requests on this branch.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82390424-4a2f-4bbf-b94c-f60090a954d0)

title: fix(studio): a timeline row binds to its own composition's element when an id repeats
body:
## What

A timeline row whose element id also appears inside a mounted sub-composition could bind to the sub-composition's copy, because that copy came first in document order. Every edit on the row then targeted the other file: a drag wrote `data-start` into the sub-composition, the preview reload put the row back where it was, and nothing said why. The sub-composition's own element moved as a side effect.

## Why

`findTimelineDomNodeForClip` resolved a clip with `doc.getElementById(clip.id)` and only checked the tag. The two composition-host lookups in `timelineSyncHydration.ts` did the same.

## Fix

Lookups now prefer an element in the clip's own composition, the chain of `data-composition-id` ancestors the runtime records as `compositionAncestors` (`resolveNearestCompositionContext` in core's `runtime/timeline.ts`). `findInClipScope` tries every selector in scope first; only when all miss does a selector with a single match in the document stand, since a host healed after the manifest was built can leave the chain stale for a pass. The row binding searches id, `data-hf-id`, `data-composition-id` and class; the two sub-composition host lookups search by id, as on main. A unique id in scope still costs one `getElementById`. A clip without `compositionAncestors` (an older runtime) keeps the old behaviour.

The Layers panel re-finds a replaced layer after a soft reload through `findElementForSelection` with the layer's own source file, instead of the first id match in the document.

## Tests

- `timelineDomBinding.test.ts`: a root clip whose id repeats in a mounted sub-composition binds to the root element (its `hfId`, no `sourceFile`). Fails on main.
- `timelineSyncHydration.test.ts`: a composition host whose id repeats inside an earlier sub-composition resolves to its own host, for both host state and row collection. Fails on main.
- `timelineDomBinding.test.ts`: a unique id stays bound while its host's composition id is healed after the manifest; an id-less host keyed by its composition id binds over a lone id inside its own sub-composition.
- `domEditingLayers.test.ts`: a replaced layer is found again in its own file when a sub-composition repeats its id. Fails with the old re-find.
- Studio suite on this branch: 5590 tests, 0 failed. `tsc` clean, oxlint clean, `fallow audit`: no issues in changed files.

## Before

A fixture with a root card and a sub-composition holding a card with the same id. Dragging the root card's row on main writes the new start into `compositions/strip.html`; the row snaps back and the sub-composition's card disappears from the preview.

![Before: mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c4f3d93e-9755-4b06-95a5-c20f5eba1b45)
![Before: released, the row is back at 0:05 and the preview is empty](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a5d555a4-8c91-473c-9959-960a74fff337)

## After

The same drag on this branch writes `index.html`; the sub-composition is untouched and its card still shows.

![After: mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/522c449a-e028-483d-a6e2-e2c9515576cc)
![After: released at the new time, the strip card still in the preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d576d13b-e934-465f-a756-0beb48b65a57)

## Known limits

- During the one hydration pass after a host's composition id is healed, a later selector that finds an in-scope element with the same name (for example a `class` equal to a nested host's composition id) wins over the lone stale match, where main took the first match. Marking healed hosts so the scope check can ignore them would remove this.
- The two sub-composition host lookups search by id only, as on main.
- The last-resort timing and position match is not scoped (unchanged).
- Other bare-id lookups that do not write (automation store sync, iframe helpers, GSAP live preview) are left for a follow-up.

title: fix(studio): undo works right after pasting or duplicating clips
body:
## Summary

Undo right after pasting or duplicating timeline clips doesn't take the clips back out. The first Undo reverts "Changed outside the app" instead, and the pasted clips stay. Before #4456 the same bug showed as "File changed outside Studio. Undo history was not applied."

The cause is the clips' `data-hf-id`s. Paste strips them from the copies so each copy gets its own, and writes the file. When the preview reloads, the server finds elements without an id, mints them, and writes the file again. That second write isn't part of the paste, so the history sees an outside change sitting on top of it.

Paste and duplicate now mint the copies' ids themselves, inside the edit, avoiding every id already in the file. The file Studio writes is complete, the server has nothing to add, and Undo takes the paste back.

Pasting a copied element (not a timeline clip) had the opposite problem: it kept the original's hf-ids, so the copy and the original shared them, and an edit to the copy could land on the original, which comes first in the file. It now goes through the same step.

## Before

main: paste two clips, then Undo. The toast says it undid an outside change, and the two pasted clips are still on the timeline.

![Before: Undo reverts an outside change and the pasted clips stay](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/808d63f8-58e5-42f9-9a07-f2190fc6147b)

## After

This branch: the same steps. "Undid: Paste clips", and the file is byte for byte what it was before the paste.

![After: Undo takes the pasted clips back out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8597df81-04e3-4674-abf6-9037349abb19)

The grey tiles right after Undo are thumbnails re-rendering after the preview reloads; 10 s later every clip has repainted (main behaves the same):

![After, 10 s later: every clip thumbnail has repainted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab0401bd-fee5-4a3f-8b53-0081c2485b38)

## How

- `remintHfIds` in `useClipboard.ts` replaces `stripHfIds`. It removes the copied ids from the clip's root and its descendants, then gives each one a fresh id with the parsers package's own `mintHfId`, walking the same elements the server's stamp does (`walkCompositionDescendants`, skipping `EXCLUDED_TAGS`).
- The ids already in the file seed the set of taken ids, so a copy never reuses its original's id, which would be the same content hash.
- Element paste (`pasteElementHtml`) uses the same step, before its `id` dedupe.
- The fallback for a clip with no element root still strips, as before.

## Checks run

- A browser walk of the running Studio dev server with a fixture project (a blank template with five clips on one track). It selects two clips, copies, pastes past the end, and presses Undo, capturing the file Studio writes and the file on disk:
  - main: written with 6 hf-ids, 8 on disk; Undo reverts "Changed outside the app" and the paste stays.
  - this branch: written and on disk are the same file (8 hf-ids); Undo says "Undid: Paste clips" and the file matches the pre-paste file exactly.
- `useClipboard.test.ts`: 23 passed. Three tests paste into a file the server already stamped (two clips, a nested clip, and an element with a child), then run the server's own `ensureHfIds` over the result: it must add nothing, and no id may repeat. On main's `useClipboard.ts`, 7 tests fail. Seeding the taken set with nothing, or skipping the step for element paste, each fails a test.
- Studio typecheck: clean.

## Not in this PR

- Creating an audio group writes an `<hf-audio-group>` without an hf-id, so the server stamps it later and a later Undo hits the same "Changed outside the app" step. It's a different write path, so it comes as its own fix.
- After Undo, the inspector can still list the clips it just removed as selected (visible in the After capture). The timeline's element list is replaced without pruning the selection; also its own fix.

## Pre-review

An independent review found nothing blocking.

| Finding | Severity | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Element paste kept the original's hf-ids, so the copy and original shared them | should fix | fixed here: same reminting step; tested |
| Creating an audio group writes an element with no hf-id | should fix | separate path; listed above |
| The taken-id collector missed unquoted, spaced or uppercase `data-hf-id` | nit | fixed |
| Nested clips were not tested against originals already in the file | nit | tested |
| Two loops where one does | nit | merged |
| Import from the package root where the `hf-ids` subpath is what the SDK and server use | nit | switched |

title: perf(player): let paused players check in once a second with low-power-idle
body:
## What a person sees now

A page can show many paused `<hyperframes-player>` elements (a catalog grid, a gallery) without each one keeping the browser busy. Add `low-power-idle` to a player and, while it is paused, its composition checks in with the page once a second instead of every 80 ms. Nothing changes for players without the attribute, including Studio.

## Why

A paused player is not idle today. The runtime's parked transport wakes every `bridgeMaxPostIntervalMs` (80 ms) to confirm its position to the host and to re-read what no observer can report (the timeline registry and the adapters' animation durations, which calls `document.getAnimations()`). That contract exists for editors that need a paused timeline to stay live (#3910). A page showing 15 paused previews pays it 15 times: about 190 messages a second to the host, each one a wake of the composition's document and of the page.

## What changed

- Runtime: a new control action, `set-idle-heartbeat` with `{ slow: boolean }`. While `slow` is set and the timeline is fully bound (the same test the runtime uses to stop re-resolving: a usable root timeline and its sub-compositions bound), the parked heartbeat arms at 1000 ms instead of `bridgeMaxPostIntervalMs`. Until then it stays at 80 ms, so a composition that registers a timeline late (many catalog blocks do, after fonts load) is still picked up at once. Changing the setting wakes the transport, so turning it off takes effect immediately. The playing path, the audio-mirror cadence and the default heartbeat are untouched; `transportPark.test.ts` "posts the paused bridge heartbeat on its documented interval while parked" is unchanged.
- Player: the `low-power-idle` boolean attribute sends that control when it changes and replays it with the rest of the bridge state when the runtime announces ready, so it survives the iframe finishing after the page.
- Docs: the attribute in the player README and `docs/packages/player.mdx`.

Trade: with `low-power-idle` and a bound timeline, what the paused runtime only finds by polling (another timeline written into `window.__timelines`, an animation that lengthens with no DOM change) reaches the host up to a second later. Seeks, play and every other control still act immediately.

## What I measured

Headless Chromium on a Linux box, one paused catalog composition (`count-up`), seeked to 1.5 s and paused through the player's API. The message count is this branch's built player and runtime; the two trace rows are the released runtime with only its parked timer rewritten to 1000 ms, which is the change this PR makes:

| | without `low-power-idle` | with `low-power-idle` |
|---|---|---|
| Messages from the paused player to the page, 10 s | 124 | 10 |
| Page renderer main-thread work, 10 s (devtools trace) | 51 ms | 7 ms |
| Timer fires in the renderer, 10 s | 125 | 11 |

A static iframe of the same size costs nothing measurable over the same window, so the remaining work is the once-a-second heartbeat itself.

A catalog page with 15 paused players (this branch's runtime swapped into each preview), quiet 15 s: about 2,700 messages to the page on the released runtime, 375 with `low-power-idle`. One tile there stays on the 80 ms beat because its document never counts as fully bound (see below).

## Tests

- `transportPark.test.ts`: a parked runtime asked for the slow heartbeat posts exactly 3 states in 3 s, and returns to one per 80 ms when asked to stop (fails when the timer ignores the flag); under a slow request, a timeline registered late is still seen within 80 ms (fails when the slow interval ignores whether a timeline is bound).
- `hyperframes-player.test.ts`: the ready replay carries `slow: false` by default and `slow: true` with the attribute (fails with the replay line removed); setting and removing the attribute on a ready player sends the control at once (fails when the attribute is not forwarded).
- `transportPark.test.ts`: under a slow request, a document with an unbound sub-composition keeps the 80 ms beat (fails when the gate ignores sub-composition binding); turning the setting off mid-interval resumes the 80 ms beat at once (fails without the wake).
- Core runtime park and bridge tests 58/58, player tests 176/176, core and player typecheck clean, comment ratchet clean.

## Known limit

A document the runtime never counts as fully bound keeps the 80 ms beat, so `low-power-idle` does nothing for it: a root registered alongside another `data-composition-id` node that never registers a timeline, a wrapper whose root has no timeline of its own, or a root whose id does not match the key it registers under. That is the safe direction (only the saving is lost).

## What I did NOT exercise

- The captures and browser numbers were taken on this branch before the review fixes (late-timeline guard, immediate wake on toggle). Those fixes do not change the cadence of a paused player whose timeline is bound, which is what the numbers measure.
- A real GPU or a phone. All numbers are from headless Chromium on a GPU-less box.
- Studio. It never sets the attribute, so it keeps the 80 ms contract; I did not open it.
- Many players at once with the released build of this branch; the catalog page that motivated this will re-measure once a release carries it.

## Before

![One paused player sends the page 124 messages in 10 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71e6cf19-a956-4053-84d5-5e0385735535)

## After

![With low-power-idle the same paused player sends 10 messages in 10 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd1ea451-d728-42c1-a883-494e62058d2a)

title: fix(studio-server): inject page tags at the document's own head and body, not inside a script
body:
## What was broken

`hyperframes snapshot` of a project that loads a local `vendor/p5.min.js` (p5 2.3.3) painted p5's source code as page text, while `render` of the same project was correct.

## Why

The bundler inlines local scripts into one inline `<script>`. p5.min.js contains the literal strings `"</head>"` and `"</body>"` inside JS strings (its HTML table writer). When a project has media some browser cannot decode (webm here), snapshot's static server injects the media codec map with `html.replace("</head>", tag + "</head>")`. The first `</head>` in the page was inside p5's script, so the injected `<script>…</script>` landed in the middle of p5, its `</script>` ended p5 early, and everything after painted as text. `render` never goes through that server, which is why it was fine.

The bundled page itself was intact. Only the text-based injection was wrong, and the same first-match pattern was used in several other places that handle bundled pages.

## The fix

One owner for "where are this document's own head and body tags": a scanner in `core/src/compiler/htmlDocument.ts` that skips comments, attribute values and `<script>`, `<style>`, `<title>`, `<textarea>` text, reads a stray quote or a self-closing SVG `<title/>` the way a browser does, and is exported as `insertBeforeCloseTag(html, "head" | "body", markup)` (returns `null` when there is none, so each caller keeps its fallback). Routed through it:

- the media codec map (`studio-server/src/helpers/mediaProxyPreview.ts`), the reported bug
- `injectScriptsIntoHtml` head and body scripts (core; used by the preview route and the file servers)
- the runtime tag in `bundleToSingleHtml` (core)
- `injectTagsAtHeadStart` and the `<body` fallbacks when a page omits `</head>` (core)
- the two position scripts the render compiler adds at `</body>` right after inlining CDN scripts (`producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`), the same bug on the render path for a CDN-loaded p5 with Studio position edits
- the preview route's project signature, GSAP CDN tags and runtime-at-body-end (`studio-server/src/routes/preview.ts`)
- the GSAP bootstrap that `routes/files.ts` writes into a project file

Each keeps its old placement (before the real `</head>` or `</body>`), so script order is unchanged.

The scanner matches tags case-insensitively on A to Z only. `"İ".toLowerCase()` is two characters, so indexes taken from a fully lowercased copy land one character late per `İ`; that also fixes the same slip in the existing `stripEmbeddedRuntimeScripts`, `getScriptSource` and the `</script` / `<!--` escaping of inline scripts.

Same as before this change (a plain substring search also got these wrong): a `</head>` inside a bogus comment (`<!x ...>`, `<?x ...>`), inside `<xmp>`, or inside a script's `<!--<script>` escape.

Not changed: `cli/src/fontLocalize.ts` still finds `</head>` by pattern. It is a standalone entry with no imports, the scanner's module pulls in `linkedom`, and its input is compiled HTML from stdin.

## Tests

- `htmlDocument.test.ts`: a page whose head and body scripts print `</head>` and `</body>`, plus a style and a comment carrying them, gets its injected scripts at the real `</HEAD >` and `</body>`, and the decoy scripts stay whole. A fragment has no close tag.
- `htmlDocument.test.ts` also: with `</head>` omitted, head scripts land before the real `<body>`; head-start tags skip a script that prints `<head>`; `<title>` text and an empty comment `<!-->` are skipped; `<script>` inside an attribute value is skipped; a stray quote, an SVG `<title/>` and a `"</scripts>"` string do not hide the real tag; indexes stay right after `İ` for injection, runtime stripping and script escaping.
- `mediaProxyPreview.test.ts`: the codec map lands after an inline script that prints `</head>`, and that script stays whole.
- `htmlCompiler.test.ts` (producer): the position-edit script lands before the real `</body>`, not inside a script that prints one.

Each rule was broken on purpose once and its test failed: the codec map, `injectScriptsIntoHtml` head and `<body` fallback, head-start, the producer body script, the `title` skip, full-Unicode lowercasing, attribute skipping, stray quotes, self-closing raw text and the close-tag boundary. A snapshot of the reporting project at 12s with this branch's CLI shows the composition; with main and with 0.8.74 it shows p5 source.

## Independent review

Rounds by an independent reviewer, each finding fixed before the next:

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Should-fix | The render compiler inserts two position scripts at the first `</body>` right after inlining CDN scripts | Fixed, tested |
| Should-fix | Pages that omit `</head>` fell back to the first `<body` text | Fixed, tested |
| Blocker | `İ` lowercases to two characters, so indexes from a lowercased copy were off (new scanner, and existing runtime stripping and script escaping) | Fixed with A-to-Z-only lowercasing, tested |
| Should-fix | `<script>` inside an attribute value hid the real `</head>` | Fixed, tested |
| Should-fix | A stray quote in a tag, or SVG `<title/>`, hid the real tag | Fixed, tested |
| Nit | `<title>` text, `<!-->`, `"</scripts>"` inside a script | Fixed, tested |
| Should-fix | The existing quote-aware tag-end helper treated any quote as opening a value, so `<meta name=it's>` paired with a later "don't" and skipped real tags | Fixed at the helper, which now follows the HTML tokenizer: a quote opens a value only right after an attribute name's `=` (not in a tag name, an unquoted value, or after a quoted value); tested |
| Nit | An unclosed `<script>` in the head exposed a later `</head>` | Only a start tag ending in `/>` counts as self-closing; tested |
| Should-fix | `/` after a tag or attribute name did not start a fresh attribute, and `</` plus a non-letter was not read as a bogus comment | Fixed; a fuzz of the helper against a tokenizer model (millions of random tags) then found no mismatch |
| Nit | A comment ending in `--!>` hid the tags after it | Fixed, tested |
| Should-fix | Quadratic time on thousands of `<script/>` with no `</script>` (80k tags: 7.3 s) | A missing close tag is remembered per element name (80k tags: 10 ms); tested with a time bound |
| Should-fix | `<!--!>` could end a comment on its own opening dashes | The end search starts after `<!--`; `<!-->` and `<!--->` handled first; tested |
| Should-fix | A tag whose quoted value never closes fell back to its first `>`, which could sit inside the value, and repeated that scan per tag (20k tags: 9 s) | An unfinished tag ends the search, as in the tokenizer (4 ms); tested with a time bound |
| Kept | `cli/src/fontLocalize.ts` keeps its pattern | Standalone entry, see above |
| CI | Fallow's complexity gate flagged the scanner and the tag-end helper | Split into small functions (none above cyclomatic 8); an old-vs-new fuzz found no behaviour change |

title: fix(studio): preview lookups use the right element when an id repeats across files
body:
## What

Follow-up to #4481. When an element's `id` or `data-hf-id` also appears in a mounted sub-composition, several preview lookups still took the first match in the document, which can be the sub-composition's copy:

- the property panel read GSAP values and corner radius from the other copy, and matched its tween list (class and descendant tweens such as `.dot` with a stagger) against the other copy's classes;
- the 3D-transform live preview animated the other copy, including in a second mount of the same sub-composition;
- gesture recording called `gsap.set("#id")`, which moves every copy with that id;
- scrubbing the playhead auditioned a sub-composition's audio instead of the music row's;
- automation read-back and the composition-source patch read the other copy;
- a composition row with no `compositionSrc` rebound to the first host with its composition id, so a second mount of the same sub-composition took the first mount's id and hf-id.


## Fix

- `previewElementFinder(doc)` (player/lib) indexes `[data-hf-id], [id]` once per pass and returns a per-row lookup: hf-id matches, then id matches, preferring one in the row's own file (`getTimelineElementSourceFile`), else the first. Automation read-back, the composition-source patch (which runs on the runtime's state tick) and scrub audio use it, so a pass over every row costs one scan instead of a lookup per row.
- `findPreviewNode(doc, selection)` (components/editor) returns the selected node while it is still mounted, then `findElementForSelection` in the selection's own file, then anywhere. The live preview, both panel reads and the panel's tween list use it.
- Gesture recording sets GSAP values on the element itself.
- `createTimelineElementFromManifestClip` keeps the host it was given when that host already carries the clip's composition id.

## Tests

Each fails on main:
- `automationStoreSync.test.ts`: an earlier same-id copy in a sub-composition, and the same hf-id in two files.
- `timelineIframeHelpers.test.ts`: the composition-source patch labels a row from its own host; scrub plays the music row's own track.
- `gsapLivePreview.test.ts`: live preview on the selected element over an earlier copy, in the selection's own file for a repeated hf-id, and on the mounted node in a second mount; the panel reads GSAP values off that same node.
- `timelineDOM.test.ts`: a sub-composition mounted twice keeps each host.
- `useGestureRecording.test.tsx`: the release clears props on the element.
- `useGsapTweenCache.element.test.tsx`: a class tween is attributed by the selected element, not an earlier same-id copy.

Studio suite: 5596 passed, 0 failed. `tsc`, oxlint and `fallow audit` clean.

## Before

A fixture with a root card (upright, one opacity tween) and a sub-composition holding a card with the same id, rotated -30deg by CSS. With the root card selected at 0:02, the panel on main reads the sub-composition's copy: Angle and RotZ show -30deg and the 3D gizmo is tilted for an upright card.

![Before: root card selected, the panel shows -30deg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1da73b15-3a83-4c54-aa5f-dca0550efec1)

## After

The same selection on this branch reads the root card: 0deg, gizmo upright.

![After: root card selected, the panel shows 0deg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4407b873-3a46-4adc-abca-000442266221)

## Known limits

- An element in a flattened sub-composition whose root lost its file attribute reports no source file, the same as a root element, so when the two share an id the first match still wins.
- After a soft reload replaces the selected node, the live preview and panel reads find it again by file without the active composition path, so while drilled into a nested sub-composition they fall back to the first match until the selection is refreshed.
- Gesture recording still starts a live preview only for an element with an id, as on main; targeting the element itself would let id-less elements preview too, left for a separate change.
- Other first-match lookups outside these paths are unchanged: the element picker; the colour-grading canvas, which the runtime names by element id, so two graded elements with the same id in different files share a canvas id (the fix belongs where the runtime names it); and the fx carve's audio and group-member lookups.

title: fix(core): a frame capture waits for a video that is still loading its first data
body:
## What was wrong

A frame capture seeks, awaits `window.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion()`, then captures. The barrier only held a video that was `seeking`. A video that has not received its first data yet (`readyState` 0, still loading) does not start a seek when `currentTime` is set: the browser stores the time as the default start position and `seeking` stays false. So the barrier resolved at once and the capture painted the page without the video.

It shows whenever media arrives late. In a host app that captures project posters in a hidden window, about half the posters taken while the machine was busy came out with every video layer missing. Holding that window's video responses for 4 s reproduces it every time: at capture both visible videos were at `readyState` 0 with `currentTime` already set and `seeking` false.

## The fix

`holdSeekBarrierUntilVideoLands` also holds a video that is still loading its first data (`readyState < HAVE_CURRENT_DATA` and `networkState === NETWORK_LOADING`). It releases on `seeked` or `loadeddata`, or on `suspend`, `error`, `emptied` or `abort` so a video that stops fetching never keeps the barrier open. `loadeddata` and `suspend` are ignored while a seek is still in flight. Render mode is unchanged: renders paint injected frames, so a loading `<video>` there holds nothing.

## Tests

- **A video still loading holds the barrier** until it has data. A `loadeddata` during a pending seek does not release it; `seeked` does. This fails without the fix.
- **A loading video that stops fetching** (`suspend`) releases it.
- **Render mode** does not hold for a loading video.
- The existing seek-completion tests pass unchanged; the core runtime suite passes (1315).

Verified in the host app as well: with the same 4 s hold, the patched runtime captured both videos (`readyState` 4) and the poster came out right.
