title: fix(core): a frame capture keeps waiting for a video between its range requests
body:
## What was wrong

#4487 made a frame capture wait for a video that is still fetching its first data. It also released that wait on `suspend`, as a sign the browser had stopped fetching. Chromium fires `suspend` whenever the network goes idle between two range requests, including at `readyState` 0 before metadata. So a video that needs several requests lost its hold after the first one.

Measured in Chromium with a video whose `moov` atom sits at the end of the file, each response held 2 s and capped at 512 KB:

- requests: `bytes=0-` (0.26 to 2.26 s), then `bytes=1540096-` for the index (2.27 to 4.27 s), then the data for the target time (4.32 to 6.33 s)
- `suspend` at 4.031 s with `readyState` 0 and `seeking` false, then `loadedmetadata` and `seeking` at 4.032 s, then `seeked` and `loadeddata` at 6.122 s

The hold released at 4.031 s, two seconds before the frame. On a paused page nothing registers a new hold, so the capture painted the page without the video. With no delay at all, `suspend` still fired at `readyState` 0 before `loadedmetadata`.

## The fix

`suspend` is no longer a release event. A video still loading is released by `loadeddata` or `seeked` once it has its frame, by `error`, `emptied` or `abort`, or by the 5 s cap. The cap is now the only end for a source that stops before its first frame. That wait only applies to paused seeks: renders never hold, and the runtime already forces `preload="auto"` on active clips, so an idle `preload` does not park a video.

## Tests

`media.test.ts`: "keeps holding a loading video through a suspend between range requests" replays the measured order (`suspend` at `readyState` 0, then the seek, then `seeked`). It replaces the old test that asserted `suspend` releases the hold, and it fails on 0.8.77's release logic. The core runtime suite passes (1321).

title: fix(studio-server): stamping ids at open never reverts a write that lands meanwhile
body:
## What this fixes

Opening a project stamps `data-hf-id`s into its compositions. Since 0.8.77 that stamp could undo someone else's work: it read a file, spent time minting ids, then replaced the file with no second look. Any save or agent write that landed in between was reverted. One measurement with concurrent writers lost 197 of 1017 writes. 0.8.75 compared the file before replacing it; that check went away when stamping moved to `stampFileHfIds`.

A second problem in the same open path: one unreadable or vanished subfolder (permissions, a folder deleted mid-walk) made `walkDir` throw, which aborted the whole stamp, and also failed the project file tree and lint routes.

## Change

- `stampFileHfIds` re-reads the file (no-follow) right before the replace and writes only if it still holds the bytes it stamped. Otherwise the file is left as the other writer made it, and the next open or save stamps it. A file deleted meanwhile stays deleted.
- `walkDir` skips a subfolder whose listing fails with EACCES, EPERM, ENOENT or ENOTDIR. Any other error, or an unreadable project folder itself, still throws.

Known limit: POSIX has no compare-and-rename, so a window of microseconds remains between the re-read and the rename. A writer that writes a file in pieces and pauses longer than the minting step can also be caught mid-write. Both are far narrower than before, where the window was the whole minting step.

## Tests

- `hfIdPersist.test.ts`: a write landing while ids are minted (in place, and by rename) is kept; a file deleted while ids are minted stays deleted.
- `safePath.test.ts`: subfolders failing with each of the four codes are skipped; EMFILE in a subfolder still throws; an unreadable project folder still throws.

On the current main code the 7 new tests fail; with this change both files pass (8 and 7), `studioServer.stampOnOpen.test.ts` passes, and `tsc` is clean. Mutations checked: letting a failed re-read count as unchanged, swallowing the root error, and dropping the error-code filter each turn exactly one test red.

## Review

Independent adversarial review over three rounds (the first head, the fixes, the final head). Nothing blocking. Acted on:
- Should fix: a file deleted while ids are minted could be recreated by the stamp. Now it stays deleted, with a test.
- Note: `walkDir` skipped a subfolder on any error. It now skips only the four codes above and rethrows the rest.
- Notes: the doc comment claimed a single file descriptor (no longer true); the mode is read after minting again, so a permission change made meanwhile is kept; a stale test name.

Left as is: moving the re-check inside the atomic write (tiny gain, adds a parameter); a symlink swapped in at the exact moment of the re-check (no-follow open, no test).

Follow-up, separate PR: `hyperframes ids` (CLI) writes minted ids without a version check, so it has the same revert on a concurrent save.

| Audited | Trusting | Not exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Every caller of `walkDir`, `stampFileHfIds`, `stampProjectHfIds`; concurrent writes in place, by rename, identical bytes, delete, symlink swap; the stamp record after a skipped write | Windows error-code mapping for unreadable folders | Windows (studio-server tests run on Linux in CI) |

title: ci: stop running CodeQL on merge queue groups, where its upload races the merge
body:
## What

CodeQL stops running on merge queue groups. It keeps running on every pull request, every push to main, the weekly schedule and manual dispatch. A new script test pins which workflows run on queue groups.

## Why

Since #4469 added the `merge_group` trigger, CodeQL fails on about half the queue groups: 7 of the last 12. The analysis finishes, then the upload is refused:

```
##[error]ref 'refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/main/pr-4449-e266…' not found in this repository
```

The queue does not wait for CodeQL. It merges the group and deletes the group's temporary branch, and the upload then points at a branch that no longer exists. In the run above, #4449 merged at 14:38:06Z and the upload started at 14:38:18Z. This is a known, open issue in the CodeQL action (github/codeql-action#1572).

#4469 added the trigger "for the code scanning rule". That rule never looks at queue groups. From GitHub's [code scanning merge protection](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/code-scanning/merge-protection) page:

> Merge protection with rulesets will **not apply** to:
>
> * Merge queue groups

The history agrees: the rule blocks while "a required tool's analysis is still in progress", yet #4449's group merged while its CodeQL analysis was still running.

So the queue run couldn't block a merge. All it did was fail at random. The group's commit becomes the main commit, so each failure also leaves a red CodeQL check on main. For example, #4486's commit on main shows the queue run's failed `Analyze (javascript-typescript)`, while the push-to-main scan of that same commit passed.

## Related work

Refs #4469

## How

- `.github/workflows/codeql.yml`: drop `merge_group`, with a two-line comment saying why.
- `scripts/merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs`: asserts the workflows triggered on `merge_group` are exactly `ci.yml`, `pr-captures.yml`, `regression.yml` and `windows-render.yml`, the ones that report required checks. It reads the trigger however it is written (map, list or single string) in `.yml` and `.yaml` files. Same parse-every-workflow shape as `scripts/pr-edit-concurrency.test.mjs`.

**The one doc line that points the other way.** GitHub's [workflow configuration options](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/code-scanning/workflow-configuration-options) page says:

> If your repository is configured with a merge queue, you need to include the `merge_group` event as an additional trigger for code scanning. This will ensure that pull requests are also scanned when they are added to a merge queue.

That line only matters if a queued merge has to wait for CodeQL, meaning CodeQL is a required status check. It isn't one here. The [merge queue docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/configuring-pull-request-merges/managing-a-merge-queue) give the same reason for triggering on `merge_group`: "A merge queue will wait for required checks to be reported before it can proceed with merging."

**Coverage.** Nothing that reaches main goes unscanned. The code scanning rule still gates every PR on its own CodeQL result, and the push to main scans the exact commit the queue merged.

**The alternative, and why not.** Making CodeQL a required check would make the queue wait for it. It averages 11 minutes on a queue group, where every current required check takes 5 to 6, so every group would take about twice as long. The wait would also buy almost nothing. The analysis job passes even when it finds alerts, and the alert threshold doesn't apply to groups, so the only thing the queue would learn is that the analysis finished. No ruleset change is needed for this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Each file run alone:

- `scripts/merge-queue-workflows.test.mjs`: exit 0, 1 passed. Each of these turns it red (exit 1): `merge_group` put back in `codeql.yml`, and a probe workflow declaring it as `on: [push, merge_group]`, as `on: merge_group`, or in a `.yaml` file.
- `scripts/pr-edit-concurrency.test.mjs`: exit 0, 4 passed.
- `scripts/catalog-publication.test.mjs`: exit 0, 16 passed. It covers the dispatch of `codeql.yml`, which this PR leaves alone.
- `oxfmt --check`, `check-test-reachability`, `check-comment-citations` and `comment-ratchet` all exit 0.

After merge: the next two queue groups run no CodeQL workflow, so no CodeQL failure, and the push-to-main CodeQL run for each merged commit succeeds.

## Independent review

A separate reviewer tried to refute the change, over two rounds.

**Findings at this head:** no blocking issues and no should-fix findings. The first round's two minor findings are fixed here:
- The test missed `merge_group` written as a list or string, or in a `.yaml` file.
- The `codeql.yml` comment described an intermittent race as a certainty.

| Audited | Trusting | Not exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Ruleset: no CodeQL job in required checks; the queue waits only on required checks | GitHub's docs for how merge protection treats queue groups | A real queue group after merge (checked after it lands) |
| 16 recent CodeQL queue runs: all 8 failures merged before the scan ended | | The full `test:scripts` suite; CI runs it on this PR |
| No script or workflow depends on the `merge_group` trigger (catalog publish uses dispatch only) | | |
| The new test goes red for every trigger form and file extension, and does not over-trigger | | |

title: feat(studio-server): history can copy the files before or after any change into a folder
body:
## What this adds

`ProjectHistory.checkout(entryId, side, emptyDir)` writes the project as history entry `entryId` found it (`"before"`) or left it (`"after"`) into an empty folder outside the project, leaving the project and its history untouched. A host can serve an older version beside the live one, for example to play a change's before and after side by side.

- The entry's own files come from its recorded change; the rest are the files as the entries before it left them.
- The folder must be empty (a missing one counts as empty and is created by the first file written) and outside the project. Both are refused otherwise; the project check compares real on-disk paths, so a symlink alias or a path typed in another letter case on a case-insensitive disk is still recognised as the project. A checkout after the project folder is gone is refused too.
- The destination is resolved once, and that one path is checked for emptiness and containment, written and cleaned up, so a spelling like `""` (the working folder) or `out/link/../co` can't pass the check on one folder and fill another.
- A copy that fails partway empties the folder again, so it can be retried.
- It runs in the history's queue, so a prune cannot remove a blob mid-copy.

## Undo one part of an agent turn, keeping later edits

`history.undo(id, { who, mode: "keep-later-edits" })` reverts an entry's files except those changed since, which it leaves as they are. A host undoing an agent turn calls it for each of the turn's parts, last first; a `null` entry means that part had nothing left to revert. A person's edit made between two parts survives, including on a file both parts wrote. The modes are exported as `UNDO_MODES`.

## History now logs changes in the order they were written

A review found the log could list changes out of write order, which made any replay (checkout, restore, peek, reopening a project) show files that never sat on disk together. Examples: an outside change pending when an agent turn started was logged after the turn, so a file replaced by a folder showed both in the turn's before-tree; a drag claimed during a turn was logged after it, so reopening recorded a phantom "Changed outside the app" entry.

Fix, at the one place all of these come from: before a window opens and before any history operation, `settle()` commits the held claim, the outside group, and every open window's pending writes as a part (the window stays open). A held drag ends as soon as any other write is pending, and the outside group commits the held claim before itself.

Visible changes:
- An agent turn that overlaps a person's edit or another turn is logged as two or more parts, in write order.
- An outside burst that spans an agent turn is two entries, and a drag ends at a turn's start or at any other pending write.

## A file replaced by a folder, or the reverse

A removed path is dated by what took its place: the folder now at file `a`'s path, or the file now at folder `a/`'s path. A file that could only appear once the old path was gone (`a/b.html` over file `a`, or the reverse) is dated no earlier than that removal. So an agent turn that swaps a file for a folder and then idles keeps both halves in its entry, and a folder a person moves in after the turn ended is logged as "Changed outside the app" even when its files are older than the turn. A folder's change time moves whenever anything inside it changes, so a touch inside the folder after the turn ends and before the next scan (a Finder `.DS_Store`, an editor swap file) also files the agent's swap as outside. It stays undoable under that label. On a disk that treats `A` and `a` as one name (checked once per project from its own history-id file), a file `A` replaced by a folder `a/` is dated the same way, so the entry stays one checkable tree.

Undo, redo and restore apply deletions before writes, and remove a folder that stands where a file goes once it holds only empty folders. Before writing anything they check that nothing left behind is in the way: a file added inside that folder since (tracked or not, `.DS_Store` included), a file or link at a folder above the written path, or a link at the written path. If something is in the way they refuse with "`<path>` is in the way; move or delete it, then try again" (409) and touch no file. Links are never followed or replaced, so an undo can't write outside the project. Folders an undone agent turn created are left behind empty, as on main.

## Cmd+Z is per author

Studio's Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z now step over the person's own changes and changes made outside the app, and leave an agent's writes alone, including during a running turn. Undoing an agent turn stays an explicit action on the turn. "Changed outside the app" entries count as the person's: they have no known author, and a Studio edit whose record the server refused is logged as one, so it stays undoable. The label Studio shows is the entry the step reverts, a drag, outside edit or open window of the person's still pending included. Cmd+Shift+Z redoes only the person's own undos, and a new change of theirs (or an outside one) ends it.

When an agent later changed a file of the person's newest edit, Cmd+Z still refuses with "changed since"; a follow-up names the agent there and offers to undo its turn first.

One edge: an agent whose window idles out (a window opened with no idle time ends after 30 s without a write, as an external agent client's can) has its later writes logged as "Changed outside the app", and Cmd+Z can revert those with that label. Studio's own agent runs hold their window for the whole run.

## Before
On main, while a drag is still held and during an agent's open turn, Studio's Undo button is greyed out and unlabelled ("Undo (Ctrl+Z)"), although Cmd+Z still reverts the person's edit.

![Before: held drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ce63b1e-c0ef-4940-8710-15efca42c198)

![Before: agent turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/36f7732c-8f18-4c71-ba30-e94091adac5c)

## After
The button names what the step will revert: the held drag, and during the agent's turn (it just turned the background red) the person's own drag. Cmd+Z reverts exactly that and keeps the agent's write. When the agent changed the same file since, Cmd+Z refuses with "changed since", as on main.

![After: held drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e90fc113-0b74-4cb9-94ed-c5dd3041d868)

![After: agent turn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49c45d51-b8ed-4e98-aff1-a69c0070cc8b)

## Tests changed

- "Cmd+Z undoes an agent's later write first when a held drag claim commits after the agent's turn" pinned the old log order and cross-author Cmd+Z; it is replaced by tests that pin the new order.
- "a cut takes only the cut file's earlier part out of the turn" is replaced by "a person's edit during an agent turn splits the turn around it".
- The route test for the step label now expects the person's own newest change, not an agent's later write.
- The Studio hook test for a held drag now expects the drag's label instead of none.
- Engine tests that walked back through agent entries with Cmd+Z now undo those entries explicitly.

## Tests

`projectHistory.test.ts` adds checkout (an empty path and a `link/..` spelling of a nonempty folder refused, before and after, a drag held at a turn's start, file-to-folder, refusals inside the project however reached, a sibling folder sharing the project's name prefix, a missing project, cleanup after a failed copy), write order (a person's edit splitting a turn, overlapping turns, a restore inside a turn, drags against turns, other files and outside writes, reopening without phantom entries), per-author Cmd+Z (during a turn, a held drag, a pending outside edit, an outside edit over a held drag, the person's open window), per-author Cmd+Shift+Z (never an agent's own undo, across an agent's write to another file, an agent turn the person redid) and keep-later-edits last first. File and folder swaps: an idled turn that turned a file into a folder, or the reverse, keeps both halves and checks out; undo and redo of a file-to-folder turn; a folder moved in after the turn idled out is the outside's; undo refuses, touching nothing, when a file added since, a link at the written path, or a link where a folder was stands in the way; undo of file `A` turned into folder `a/`. The two letter-case tests run only on case-insensitive disks (macOS, Windows) and skip on Linux; the link tests skip on Windows.

Results: `projectHistory.test.ts` 78 passed (2 skipped on Linux), `routes/history.test.ts` 12, Studio `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts` 10 and `hostMount.test.tsx` 2, CLI `commands/history.test.ts` 31; `tsc` clean in studio-server, studio and cli. Single mutations, each failing its intended test: keep-later-edits keeping nothing; Cmd+Z stepping over anyone's change; the label ignoring a held drag; outside changes not counted as the person's (fails the engine test and the Studio refused-claim test); the label ignoring a pending outside edit; redo of anyone's undo; any change blocking redo; redo not transferring ownership; the held drag named before a newer outside edit; open windows not named. Each fails exactly one new test. For swaps: applying writes before deletions, keeping the folder in the way, dating a removal at scan time, dating a file before the removal it blocks, dropping the in-the-way check, the link check, the tracked-only deletion set, or the walk into subfolders; each fails its swap test, and the swap tests fail on the previous heads.

title: fix(cli): timeline ids never writes over a save that lands while it stamps
body:
## What this fixes

`hyperframes timeline ids` read every file, minted ids, then wrote the results without a version check. A save or agent write that landed while it was minting was replaced by the stamped old content. Every other timeline edit already passes the version it read; `ids` now does too.

On a conflict the command stops, rolls back any file it already wrote, and refuses the same way the other timeline edits do: exit code 2 and `{ ok: false, reason, fix }` on stderr (JSON with `--json`). Running it again stamps the new content.

The check for that conflict moves into one shared `isFileChanged` helper, used by both the mutation commands and `ids`.

A refused batch could still lose a save: when a later file conflicted, the rollback wrote every earlier file's old content back, including one another writer had just saved. `applyFileMutations` now checks every file's version before its first write (a batch that is already stale writes nothing), and a rollback restores only files that still hold this batch's write. A file whose own write failed is still restored.

## Tests

- `a2Commands.ids.test.ts`: a save that lands while ids are minted survives, the exit code is 2 and the refusal is JSON. It fails on the current main code (the save is overwritten).
- `applyFileMutations.test.ts`: a later file's conflict after the first file was written and then saved by someone else keeps that save; an already-stale later file means nothing is written. Both fail on main. `timeline.e2e.test.ts` (19 tests, including the existing `ids` one) and `tsc` pass.

## Review

Independent adversarial review over two heads, nothing blocking. Acted on: the missing JSON refusal. Next PR: `timeline apply` and `timeline undo` refuse a conflict the same way, and the same version check moves into `applyFileMutations` itself so Studio's element-patch route is covered too.

| Audited | Trusting | Not exercised |
|---|---|---|
| Rollback of earlier files on a later conflict; refusal shape against the other timeline edits; `isFileChanged` keeps their behaviour | `applyFileMutations` journal and receipts | A conflict on a second file after the first was written |

title: fix(core): a clip that starts later keeps the place and size its CSS gives it
body:
## What changes

A clip that starts after 0 now appears where its CSS puts it, the same as a clip that shows at load.

Before this, moving a title's start from 0 s to 0.88 s in a flex-centred film drew it in the top-left corner of the preview. An empty full-frame clip starting later (a colour card, say) did not show at all.

## Why it happened

`applyClipLayout` makes every timed root clip `position: absolute`. It then read the clip's computed box:

- top/left `auto` → pin the clip to `top: 0; left: 0`
- width/height `0px` → fill it to `100%`

When the layout pass runs after the visibility pass, a clip that has not started yet is already `display: none`. The browser reports `auto` for every box value of a `display: none` element. A clip that is showing always reports pixels. So the pin only ever fired on hidden clips, and the fill never did. The result depended on whether the clip had started when the layout pass ran.

The fix is in that one function:

- Measure hidden clips with their inline `display: none` lifted, then put each back with its priority. All hidden clips are lifted at once, so a pass (it runs every 20 frames during playback) forces one layout, not one per hidden clip.
- Never pin top/left. An absolute clip keeps the static position its CSS gives it: centred in a flex root, top-left in a block root.

Clips that were showing at layout time take the same path as before.

## Before / After

Headless Chrome, runtime built from `main` and from this branch. Frame at 2 s.

Flex-centred root, title starting at 0.88 s:

Before:
![Before: title pinned top-left](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/daa563ff-f2ec-40ee-bd59-6cdc9c7fc58c)

After:
![After: title centred](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/38884bdf-93bd-423f-951a-a64ef1cc6a11)

Block root, empty full-frame card starting at 1 s:

Before:
![Before: card is 0x0 and missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15b3589c-de11-40b4-9800-a8bd35f25a2b)

After:
![After: card fills the frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b852326b-3bde-4f6e-9ea3-f97c72c23789)

## Renders

Renders were already right, and they are unchanged. The same film (title moved to 0.88 s) rendered with `main` and with this branch puts the title in the same box, (793,513) to (1128,582), at 1 s and at 3 s. The only difference is inside the title's glyphs: 0.1% of their total brightness (anti-aliasing), with the same bounding box. Two renders of the branch are byte-identical.

Render at 3 s, `main` then this branch:

![Render at 3 s on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77394ab0-3221-4e90-b41a-fa651bb6b748)
![Render at 3 s on this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c1067fe8-7303-48d2-8474-03d571409158)

## What I measured

- `packages/core/src/runtime/init.test.ts`: 140 passed, exit 0. `src/runtime`: 60 files, 1324 passed, exit 0 (Linux, vitest 4, `--maxWorkers=4`).
- On `main`'s `init.ts`, the three late-clip `applyClipLayout` tests fail: `expected '0px' to be ''` (twice) and `expected '' to be '100%'`.
- Mutations: without the lift, the size test and the `!important` test fail. Without the restore, all three hidden-clip tests fail. Restoring without the priority fails the `!important` test.
- Real Chrome, same fixtures: late title at 0,0 on `main` and at 784,499 on this branch (the title starting at 0 is at 784,499 on both). Late card 0x0 on `main` and 1920x1080 on this branch.
- Studio dev server with this branch: the title stays centred on open and after an outside save moves it to 0.88 s.
- The render and Studio checks ran on the first commit. The second commit only batches the same lift, and the Chrome numbers above were re-run at the head.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The Studio dev server on `main` already keeps this title centred, on open and after the save. Whether a surface shows the bug depends on whether a clip gets hidden before its first layout pass. So Studio is not shown as a before/after.
- No producer regression fixture: its baseline video needs the Docker test image. The unit tests pin the behaviour.
- A visible change for existing films: a clip that starts after 0, has no top/left of its own, and sat in the corner only because of the pin will now sit where its CSS puts it. In a flex-centred root that is the centre, the same as a clip starting at 0 already is.

title: fix(core): report one composition size in stage-size and timeline messages
body:
## What this fixes

A composition whose root sizes itself with units, `data-width="1080px" data-height="1920px"`, was shown as a cropped landscape picture in `<hyperframes-player>`.

The runtime reports the root's size to its host twice, and the two reports disagreed:

- the `stage-size` message read `1080px` as 1080;
- the `timeline` message used the strict timing-number parser, which rejects `1080px`, and fell back to 1920×1080.

The player applies both, the `timeline` one last, so the portrait film was framed at 1920×1080. The two messages could also describe different compositions: `stage-size` took the root marked `data-root="true"`, the `timeline` message took the first composition in the page.

Now, in `packages/core/src/runtime/compositionDimension.ts`:

- `parseCompositionDimension` is the one reader for the size the runtime reports. It reads whole px with `parseInt`, as the producer's render viewport and Studio's document read already do, so `1080px` and `1080.5` are both reported as 1080 in both messages.
- `parseLayoutDimension` is the one reader for laying out the stage and timed clips. It keeps fractions, as the layout did before, so a `0.5px` clip stays `0.5px`.
- `findRootCompositionElement` is the one root finder: the `data-root="true"` composition, else the first composition. Both size messages, the `timeline` payload's duration and ids, the clip tree and the `composition_loaded` analytics event now use it.

Two more readers were wrong the same way and now use the layout reader: the root-stage layout diagnostic used `Number()` and never fired for a px-suffixed root, and a flattened nested root was given `width: 1080pxpx`, which the browser ignores.

Behaviour this changes, all on purpose:

- A fractional root size (`1080.5`) is reported as 1080 in the `timeline` message, as `stage-size` already did. The stage is still laid out at 1080.5px, as before.
- `0` or a negative size falls back to the default on that side in the `timeline` message, as a missing attribute already did. Before, the message carried 0 and the player ignored the pair.
- Values the layout already read loosely (`1,920` as 1, `100%` as 100, `1e3` as 1 in `stage-size`) are now reported the same way by the `timeline` message, where the strict reader fell back to 1920×1080.
- A page with a composition before the one marked `data-root="true"`: the `timeline` message and the clip tree now describe the marked root, the one the runtime plays.

## Before

Main (0.8.77): a 1080×1920 composition written with `px` sizes, in a portrait player box.

![Before: portrait composition cropped to a landscape band](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aee4e1be-b116-40eb-bcae-58c02fabe897)

## After

This branch, same page, same player build: the composition fills the portrait box.

![After: portrait composition fills the player](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b68e2001-0d81-483a-b0fb-e4f6138cb736)

## What I measured

- New tests fail on main and pass here: the timeline payload reads `1080px` as 1080; `stage-size` and `timeline` report one size for `1080px × 1920px` and for `1080.5 × 1920`; the stage is laid out at the authored size; a `0.5px` clip keeps `0.5px`; with a composition placed before the marked root, both messages, the timeline duration, the clip tree and the analytics event describe the marked root; the layout diagnostic fires for a px-suffixed root; a flattened nested root gets `1080px`, not `1080pxpx`.
- One mutation per fix, each killed by its own test.
- `packages/core` `src/runtime` test files run one at a time, exit 0. Typecheck, lint, format and the comment ratchet green.
- Captures: headless Chrome, the player bundle from main, the runtime bundle built from main (Before) and from this branch (After).

## What I did NOT exercise

- A producer render of a px-suffixed or fractional size; the render viewport reads the root with `parseInt`, which already accepted `1080px`.
- Readers outside the runtime are unchanged here and move onto these readers in a follow-up PR: the compiler (`htmlBundler.ts`), Studio's editor copies, and the root choice of the producer's render viewport, the CLI and the player's probe. Two differences stay until then:
  - with a composition placed before the marked root, the preview shows the marked root's size while a render's viewport still uses the first composition's;
  - a nested composition's size is read by the runtime's loader and by the bundler with different rules for inputs like `1080px` or `100%`.

## Independent review

Four review passes by a reviewer that did not write the change. No open blockers. Findings and what happened to them:

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| A sub-pixel clip (`data-width="0.5"`) expanded to the full stage | Fixed: layout keeps fractions; test |
| The two size messages could read different roots | Fixed: one root finder for both, the timeline payload, the clip tree and analytics; tests |
| Fractional sizes made Studio's two size readers disagree | Fixed: reported sizes are whole px |
| No test that the timeline takes its duration from the marked root | Fixed: test |
| Preview and render can pick different roots when a composition precedes the marked root | Documented above; the render's root choice moves in the follow-up |
| The layout diagnostic now warns for `1080px` and is silent for `0x10` | Kept on purpose: it now reads sizes the way the layout does |
| Runtime loader and bundler size nested roots differently | Documented above; follow-up |
| The clip tree's cache key ignores `data-root` | Kept: nothing reads the map it feeds today |

title: fix(core): a clip gets its own inline display back when the runtime shows it
body:
## What changes

A timed clip that the runtime hides before its start gets its own inline `display` back when it appears.

Before this:
- A clip with `style="display:flex"` that starts after 0 appeared as `display: block`, so its flex layout was gone.
- A clip the author hid with `style="display:none !important"` was shown once its time came.
- A `data-hidden` clip lost the `!important` on its display when the attribute was removed. If the clip had already been hidden for its start time, it lost the value itself.

## Why it happened

The visibility pass hides an in-flow leaf clip that is not showing with `display: none`, and hides `data-hidden` elements the same way.

- The timed path wrote a plain `none` over whatever inline display the author had, and removed the property when the clip showed. The author's value was gone.
- The `data-hidden` path saved the value without its priority. When the clip was already hidden by the timed path, the value it saved was the runtime's own `none`.

## The fix

One place now owns the runtime's display hiding. `hideByDisplay` saves the author's inline display, value and priority, the first time the runtime hides an element. `restoreDisplay` puts exactly that back. Both the timed path and the `data-hidden` path go through them. They replace the separate set and map the two paths kept.

One exception: a plain inline `none`, with no priority, is not kept. It can't be told apart from a runtime hide left behind, for example by Studio's layer reveal putting back the runtime's own `none`. So a clip like that still shows at its start, as it does on `main`. This applies to the timed hide only: a `data-hidden` hide keeps an author's plain `none`, so un-hiding leaves the clip hidden, as on `main`.

## Before / After

Real Chrome, 3 s into a film. A clip that starts at 2 s carries the author's inline `display: flex` and holds three boxes.

Before (`main`): the flex is lost, the clip renders as `block`, and the boxes stack:
![Before: boxes stacked, display block](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1b27ca9-ba23-46e9-991b-f969df4deaf8)

After (this branch): the author's `display: flex` comes back and the boxes sit in a row:
![After: boxes in a row, display flex](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47f29a52-9894-4929-bd68-7a367ac879b9)

## What I measured

- `src/runtime` (includes `init.test.ts`): 60 files, 1326 passed, exit 0 (Linux, vitest 4).
- Three of the five new tests fail on `main` (the other two pin `main`'s plain-`none` behaviour): `expected '' to be 'flex'`, `expected '' to be 'none'`, `expected '' to be 'grid'`.
- Mutations: restoring without the priority fails the `!important` test and the `data-hidden` test. Keeping a plain `none` on the timed hide fails the plain-`none` test; dropping it on the `data-hidden` hide fails the toggle test.
- Real Chrome, a clip starting at 2 s, inside a plain wrapper, seeked to 3 s:

| Author's inline display | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `display: flex` | inline `""`, computed `block` | inline `flex`, computed `flex` |
| `display: none !important` | inline `""`, computed `block`, shown | inline `none !important`, computed `none`, height 0 |
| `display: none` | inline `""`, computed `block` | inline `""`, computed `block` (unchanged) |

## What I did NOT exercise

- No producer render comparison. Films with no inline display on their timed clips take the same path as before: nothing to save, and the property is removed on show, as it was.
- If a script changes a clip's inline display while the runtime has it hidden, showing the clip now puts back the value from before the hide rather than removing the property.

title: perf(studio): swap an edited scene into the live preview instead of reloading
body:
## Summary

An edit to one scene now reaches Studio's preview in about a third of the time (0.92 s to 0.29 s for a text edit, about 0.9 s to 0.25 s for a colour or timing edit, faster than Remotion Studio on all three). Studio asks the running preview to swap in just the edited scene instead of reloading the whole film. Whenever the preview can't do that exactly, Studio falls back to the full reload it does today. Selection, manual edits and the Layers panel follow the swapped scene.

This merges only after #4503 (the preview marks which scenes can swap) and #4542 (the swap stops everything a scene started, or refuses); without them a swap can leave a scene wrong. It requires #4542's cancel parameter: `__hfSwapScenes(html, signal)`. A runtime without it ignores the signal, so a swap Studio gave up on could still land after the fallback reload began. This PR is therefore stacked on #4542: its base is `fix/runtime-swap-safety` and its head merges that branch, so #4542's runtime is in this PR's merge result and the diff shows only this PR's files. Once #4542 merges, this PR goes back to `main`.

## What changed

- `refreshPlayer` first tries the preview's scene swap:
  1. fetch the rebuilt preview document;
  2. hand it to `__hfSwapScenes` (runtime PR) with the request's abort signal;
  3. if the preview refuses, log `scene-swap-refused` with the reason and run the shadow reload.
- A preview without the swap (any runtime before the runtime PR) reloads exactly as before.
- When the 5 s budget runs out, Studio aborts the signal before it starts the fallback reload, and the runtime refuses a cancelled swap after its caption wait, before it changes anything. A caption answer that arrives later replaces nothing. A newer edit also aborts the previous attempt's signal, so an older swap still waiting cannot land after the newer edit falls back to a reload.
- A newer edit supersedes an older one still downloading; the older one is dropped.
- A swap fires no `load`, so the Studio parts that re-resolve preview DOM on `load` now use `onPreviewContentReplaced`, which listens for either a load or a swap:
  - selection sync, which also re-applies manual edits and hotkeys and bumps the document version;
  - the Layers panel;
  - the edit callout.
- Consumers left on `load` only, deliberately:
  - color grading: the runtime re-applies it on DOM changes;
  - grading thumbnails;
  - console error capture: re-attaching on the same window would drop the capture;
  - player init.

## Before

Main: one scene's title is edited on disk while the preview is paused; the whole film reloads before the new title shows. Clock in ms since the save; recorded on a busy 8-core machine, so both clips are slower than the medians in the table below.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6811a6cf-e034-4958-89a4-bb2b28e32df3

## After

The same edit with the scene swap: only that scene is replaced in the running preview, and the title changes in place.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95234898-4627-458d-b0b0-21215c11b35d

## Measured

Studio vs Remotion Studio on the same 60 s, 12-scene fixture: current main, main plus the three scene-swap PRs, and Remotion 4.0.527. 5 interleaved rounds on a 32-core Linux box, headless Chrome 152, medians. The box was shared with other test runs (1-minute load 3 to 37 at session start), so the open and idle rows move within that noise; the edit rows do not.

| | main | with the scene swap | Remotion Studio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edit to new pixels: text | 924 ms | **288 ms** | 835 ms |
| Edit to new pixels: color | 904 ms | **247 ms** | 728 ms |
| Edit to new pixels: timing | 895 ms | **227 ms** | 612 ms |
| Cold open, first frame | 3.08 s | 2.14 s | 9.92 s |
| Warm open, first frame | 1.98 s | 2.01 s | 2.59 s |
| Scrub, warm, event to pixel p50 / p95 | 15 / 123 ms | 16 / 54 ms | 120 / 318 ms |
| Sessions / errors | 5 / 0 | 5 / 0 | 5 / 0 |

No edit was missed in any session. The only work the swap adds before the first frame is the server's scene manifest (3-14 ms on this fixture's preview document, timed on its own).

## Tests

- Scene swap in `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`:
  - the swap replaces the live preview with no shadow reload;
  - a refusal falls back;
  - no swap available reloads at once;
  - an older document never lands after a newer edit;
  - a playing film that a swap cuts short of the playhead shows stopped at its new end, with no restart and no reload (the runtime's stop is tested in #4542).
- `useDomEditPreviewSync.test.ts`: re-syncs after a swap, not after a refused one.
- `LayersPanel.test.ts`: re-collects after a swap.
- `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`: an older swap still waiting on captions replaces nothing once a newer edit has been refused and is reloading; without the cancel it landed.
- The shortened playing film is covered in two parts: #4542's runtime test runs the real clock, transport and swap; this PR's Studio test uses a stand-in for the runtime's stop and shows Studio does not restart playback.
- `sceneSwap.test.ts`: a swap that times out while the runtime waits for caption overrides replaces nothing when the captions arrive later; without the signal, the late answer replaced the scene.
- Mutations: each of removing the swap event, removing its listener, or reverting either consumer to `load` fails a test.

## Known limits

- Color grading thumbnails in the grading panel are not re-rendered after a swap (they refresh when the preview reloads).
- An edit that swaps leaves a reverse shuttle running; an edit that reloads stops it, as today.
- A swap gets 5 s in total (download, then the preview's swap); past that, Studio falls back to the full reload.
- An edit that brings in a video, audio or image the preview has not loaded yet is refused by the runtime (#4502) and takes the full reload, which keeps the old frame until the new media can play.

title: fix(telemetry): honor CLI opt-out in Studio and render CI
body:
A CLI launched with telemetry disabled currently withholds its anonymous identity, but Studio has a separate browser telemetry policy and can still send events. Pass a page-scoped disabled flag before Studio initializes and honor it in the shared browser policy, covering both telemetry transports and canary eligibility. Enabled CLI sessions and standalone Studio keep their existing behavior; no browser preference is persisted.

Also pass the explicit `HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1` opt-out into the first-party regression and fast-video Docker jobs. A workflow-level environment does not cross `docker run`. The public render image keeps its existing defaults.

Validation: 109 focused CLI opt-out/identity, Studio policy, and Studio client tests pass against built core outputs. The transport test attempts the same render event in both modes: disabled sends nothing, enabled sends once. Full pre-commit checks pass, including oxlint, oxfmt, core/Studio/scripts typechecks, fallow, file-size/artifact checks and commitlint. Core was built to generate the runtime artifacts required by these checks; no generated artifact is committed.

This requires a normal package release and downstream CLI pin updates to protect deployments still serving older Studio bundles. No publication or deployment is included. Ready for review; keep unmerged pending explicit merge authorization.

## Before

Browser regression harness using the base Studio policy and the real client transport. A CLI opt-out does not set a browser flag; attempting one `render_complete` event produces one intercepted PostHog batch. The harness intercepts fetch locally; no test analytics are transmitted. This is behavioral evidence, not a screenshot of a visible Studio layout change.

![Before: one intercepted telemetry batch despite CLI opt-out](https://www.heygenverse.com/s/176960a7-1afe-463a-a547-eb63d1baa161/raw)

## After

Same browser harness and event attempt, with this PR's policy and injected CLI disabled flag. Zero PostHog batches. Captures use Chrome, the actual bundled Studio client/policy, and a fresh browser profile for each state.

![After: zero intercepted telemetry batches](https://www.heygenverse.com/s/24efed7e-7339-4ac3-a28f-2fef2e67737a/raw)

title: docs: clip visibility advice matches lint's gsap_animates_clip_element
body:
## What changes

The skills and docs now say what lint enforces about clip visibility: GSAP must not write `display`, `visibility` or `autoAlpha` on a clip element, a zero-duration `tl.set()` included. Fade a clip with `opacity`, or animate a child element inside it.

## Why

Lint's `gsap_animates_clip_element` is the one rule for "the framework owns a clip's visibility". Three docs contradicted it:

- `skills/hyperframes-animation/adapters/gsap.md` said these are forbidden, then recommended `autoAlpha` or a zero-duration timeline set at a boundary. Lint rejects both.
- `skills/music-to-video/references/montage.md` crossfaded clips with `opacity`/`autoAlpha`. `autoAlpha` on a `.clip` is a lint error.
- `docs/prompting/anatomy.mdx` forbade animating a clip's own `opacity`, which lint allows and the core rules recommend for fading a clip. It also left out `visibility` and `autoAlpha`.

Checked against lint on a fixture: `tl.set("#row", { display: "none" }, 4)` and `tl.set("#row", { autoAlpha: 0 }, 5)` on a `.clip` are both reported as `gsap_animates_clip_element` errors.

### Scene clips in the Claude Design guides

`docs/guides/claude-design-hyperframes.md` and `docs/guides/claude-design-send-to-hyperframes.md` taught toggling every non-anchor scene clip with `tl.set("#sN", { autoAlpha: 0/1 })` over an inline `visibility:hidden`. Their skeletons fail lint with 4, 4 and 3 `gsap_animates_clip_element` errors, while the guide promises zero.

The toggles were there for one real reason: when a shader fires, HyperShader resets every `.scene` to `opacity: 0`. So the guides now teach:

- Non-anchor scenes carry no inline visibility; the runtime shows and hides every scene in its `data-start` / `data-duration` window.
- Each non-anchor scene after scene 1 gets `tl.set("#sN", { opacity: 1 }, <start>)`, which undoes the reset. `opacity` on a clip is allowed.
- The first anchor keeps its explicit `opacity: 1` show; HyperShader owns the rest of the anchors' opacity.
- The add/remove-a-shader steps, troubleshooting rows and checklists follow the same rule.

`skills/talking-head-recut/SKILL.md` set `visibility` on its `card-host clip` elements at exactly their `data-start` and end. Those three sets are removed; the runtime already does it, and the opacity fades stay.

title: perf(runtime): swap edited scenes into the running preview from a rebuilt document
perf(studio): tag each scene's parts in the preview so one scene can be swapped
body:
## Summary

Studio's preview now marks each scene's own parts, so an edit to one scene can be swapped into the live preview instead of reloading the whole film. This PR only prepares the served document. The runtime swap and Studio's use of it are separate PRs, and each merges on its own.

## What changed

- `bundleToSingleHtml` gains `sceneParts` (preview only; renders are unchanged). With it:
  - each top-level scene's host, its `<style>` and its inline `<script>` carry `data-hf-scene="<id>"`;
  - nested sub-compositions belong to their top-level scene;
  - tagged parts are kept out of style and script coalescing.
- A scene's style keeps every `@import` first, deduped. The joining helper is shared with the existing coalesce step.
- A scene's local script files go into its own script part too, in source order with its inline scripts, so the preview runs them in the same order a render does.
- The preview route adds `<meta name="hf-scene-parts">` holding a hash of everything outside the scenes (`shared`) and one hash per scene. The project-signature meta is ignored, because it changes on every edit.
  - Each scene part leaves a positional marker in the `shared` hash, so moving or reordering a scene counts as a change outside the scenes.
- A scene whose own script can leave work running after it is replaced gets `data-hf-scene-no-swap="<reason>"`, and edits to it keep today's full reload.
  - Covered: listeners, timers, animation frames, GPU and canvas contexts, observers, workers, sockets, async setup (`async`/`await`/`.then`/`fetch`), direct `element.animate`, the GSAP ticker, infinite tweens, standalone GSAP tweens (`gsap.to`/`from`/`fromTo` outside a timeline, which a swap cannot kill), page-level DOM (`document.head`/`body`/`documentElement`), registrations that throw when run again (custom elements, CSS properties), runtime hooks, and script files that are not library URLs.
  - The check reads the authored script before it is wrapped, and is conservative: when unsure, it refuses.
  - Library scripts from a URL do not refuse. A swap never re-runs them.
  - Module scripts and import maps refuse too: the bundler emits them outside the scene's parts, so a swap could not re-run them.
- A scene whose nodes a script outside it names (by selector, id or class, in any quoted string of the root's own scripts: inline, local files and inline templates) is marked too, whatever the script does with them (a listener, a root-timeline tween, a timer): a swap would leave that script holding the old nodes. In the repo's 80 example, template and fixture projects this marks 4 scenes in 3 projects (a root timeline fading a scene out, a picture-in-picture host, a hook scene); 86 of 99 scenes still swap (one more is refused for building a timeline in one chained expression). The catalog count below is unchanged.

## Design

The bundler is the one owner of how a scene becomes preview DOM. An earlier approach mounted scene files directly in the preview. It bypassed the bundler, and its review found that nested scenes never loaded and the server's preview transforms skipped scenes (fonts, GIFs, the video codec map, motion paths). This design keeps today's inlined preview and only tags it; the swap takes the rebuilt document from the same route.

## How many catalog blocks can swap

| canvas, WebGL or three.js | 33 |
| a script file that is not a library URL | 7 |
| timers, page-level DOM or other lasting work | 4 |
| runtime hooks | 2 |
