## Before

Nothing visible changes with this PR alone: it only tags the served preview document; the runtime swap (#4502) and Studio's use of it (#4499) act on the tags.

## After

See #4499's Before/After captures.

## Measured

Studio vs Remotion Studio on the same 60 s, 12-scene fixture: current main, main plus the three scene-swap PRs, and Remotion 4.0.527. 5 interleaved rounds on a 32-core Linux box, headless Chrome 152, medians. The box was shared with other test runs (1-minute load 3 to 37 at session start), so the open and idle rows move within that noise; the edit rows do not.

| | main | with the scene swap | Remotion Studio |
|---|---|---|---|
| Edit to new pixels: text | 924 ms | **288 ms** | 835 ms |
| Edit to new pixels: color | 904 ms | **247 ms** | 728 ms |
| Edit to new pixels: timing | 895 ms | **227 ms** | 612 ms |
| Cold open, first frame | 3.08 s | 2.14 s | 9.92 s |
| Warm open, first frame | 1.98 s | 2.01 s | 2.59 s |
| Scrub, warm, event to pixel p50 / p95 | 15 / 123 ms | 16 / 54 ms | 120 / 318 ms |
| Sessions / errors | 5 / 0 | 5 / 0 | 5 / 0 |

No edit was missed in any session. The only work the swap adds before the first frame is the server's scene manifest (3-14 ms on this fixture's preview document, timed on its own).

## Tests

- Tagging (nested owner, renders untagged), `@import` placement, the no-swap mark (listener, local file, CDN library, standalone GSAP tween, a root script reaching a scene node by listener, local file, root-timeline tween, timer or inline template, a root selector by tag name in any case, `"*"`, or through a tag above the scenes, a scene script chaining a new timeline, and none when a root script never names scene nodes or only posts a message to `"*"`), the manifest (only the edited scene changes, root edits change `shared`, reorder changes `shared`), and the preview route serving a manifest whose `shared` ignores the signature.
- Manifest placement: a head attribute holding a quoted `>` (double or single quotes), a `<head` inside a comment or an `<html>` attribute, and a script before the doctype. The manifest goes in through the shared head scanner (`injectTagsAtHeadStart`), and 2 MB adversarial inputs to it stay under 1.5 s.
- One mutation per new test; each fails without its fix.

## Known limits

- A local script file used by more than one composition is emitted once, in the first scene that uses it. If a composition that runs earlier in the preview needs it, the preview can run it too late; renders are unaffected. No composition, example or catalog block in the repo does this today.

## Follow-up

The root scan is static: it sees a scene's ids, classes, tag names (in any case) and selectors written as quoted strings, including `"*"` and selectors through tags above the scenes (a selector naming a tag the document lacks is skipped without a query; a `"*"` after a comma, like `postMessage`'s target origin, is not a selector), not selectors a script builds at run time, and not scripts loaded from an absolute path. A string that happens to match a scene's node refuses that scene, which only costs a full reload. It indexes each scene's ids, classes and tags once per build, so a long root script (1,500 words and 500 short phrases over a 5,000-node film) stays at 0.6 s.

A scene script that builds and chains a timeline in one expression (`gsap.timeline().to(...)`) is refused, since nothing registers it. The same check also refuses the registered form (`window.__timelines.x = gsap.timeline().to(...)`), one scene in the repo. Other unregistered shapes (a timeline kept in a variable and never registered, `gsap["timeline"]`, an alias of `gsap`) cannot be found by reading the script. #4542 records every animation a scene script starts and stops them all on a swap, and Studio does not turn swaps on (#4499) until #4542 has merged.

The refusal list is a denylist, so a script shape it misses (for example `defineProperty` on `top` or `parent`) would throw when a swap runs it again. A follow-up makes the runtime swap reject when a re-run scene script throws, so any gap costs a full reload instead of a broken scene.

A refused scene keeps today's full reload, so nothing regresses; it only misses the faster path. The follow-up that would bring most of the 87 refused blocks back is a per-scene unmount hook: the runtime announces that a scene is about to be replaced, and blocks that start listeners, loops, contexts or async setup stop them there. Blocks that honour it could then drop the refusal.

title: fix(player): end and loop films whose length falls between two frames
body:
## What this fixes

A film whose length is not a whole number of frames never ended in `<hyperframes-player>` when played through the runtime's messages (a cross-origin or `sandbox-origin` embed). With `loop` it froze on its last frame, no `ended` fired, and a page's own loop (`play()` from an `ended` listener) never ran.

The runtime posts its position as a whole frame, `Math.round(currentTime * fps)`. A 1.97 s film at 30 fps is 59.1 frames long, so its last post is frame 59, 1.967 s, and the player counted a film as finished only when `frame / fps >= duration`.

The frame alone cannot tell the end from a pause just before it: a pause at 1.95 s also posts frame 59. Comparing times is not enough either: the length the player holds comes from the `timeline` message and can sit a float step past where the runtime's clock stops (`0.48 + 4.49` is `4.970000000000001`). So the runtime's `state` message now says so itself: `ended` is true once its clock has reached the film's end, and `currentTime` carries its exact time. `ended: true` ends the film. `ended: false` from a stopped runtime is a pause, even at exactly the length. A runtime still playing past the length ends the film as before, so a composition with no length of its own keeps looping. It snaps its time to the length at the end so a later `play()` starts over, and otherwise keeps the exact time: a pause at 1.95 s reports 1.95 s, stays a pause, and a later `play()` resumes there.

A runtime that sends neither field is read as before, from the frame.

The same-origin path reads the timeline's own time rather than a rounded frame, so it did not have this bug and is unchanged.

## Before

Main's player and runtime, `loop` on a 1.97 s composition in a `sandbox-origin` player: after 7 s it has not restarted once; it sits paused on the last frame at 1.967 s.

![Before: the film is paused on its last frame and never loops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6f0f989-337e-4ac1-beac-18fd879b79f8)

The previous head of this PR, same film, with the composition pausing itself at 1.95 s: the pause is taken for the end and the film loops.

![Before: a pause at 1.95 s restarts the film](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01c77d69-e572-4ff9-90fd-bd54bd8125be)

## After

This branch's player and runtime, same pages: the film restarts every 2 s, and a pause at 1.95 s stays paused, with no `ended` and no restart.

![After: the film loops three times in seven seconds](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ba9906aa-fc53-47ea-b24b-5332f1913b55)

![After: a pause at 1.95 s stays paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5aaa35a6-2566-4d71-bbf6-125f040a02f3)

## What I measured

- New tests fail on main and pass here: a film ends when the runtime reports its end even though the player's length is a float step past the runtime's time, and it loops there. Two more fail at 40df8e12: a pause from inside the composition on the last frame neither ends nor loops the film, and a host pause there resumes in place instead of rewinding. Runtime tests pin that a pause at 4.95 s posts frame 149, `currentTime` 4.95 and `ended: false`, and that playing a 4.97 s film with a clip to its end finishes on a post with `ended: true`.
- A pause the runtime marks `ended: false` at exactly the length neither ends nor loops the film (fails at ce995e79). A runtime playing past the length while reporting `ended: false` still ends or loops the film, and a film paused at its end is left alone while the runtime keeps reporting the end.
- Mutations each fail their tests: the decoder turning an absent `ended` into `false` (breaks older runtimes' frame rule), the time check overriding `ended: false`, the runtime never reporting the end, the runtime posting `frame / fps` as its time, the player ignoring `ended`, and the player ignoring `currentTime`.
- `packages/player` `hyperframes-player.test.ts` (183) and `runtime-message-handler.test.ts` (21), `packages/core` `init.test.ts` (146) and `transportPark.test.ts` (25), each run alone, exit 0.
- In headless Chrome, a 1.16 s film with a clip running to its end (the float-step case) loops 6 times in 7 s. Typecheck, lint, format and the comment ratchet green.
- Captures: headless Chrome with the player and runtime bundles built from main, from this PR's previous head and from this branch, same host pages and compositions.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio's own transport, which does not use this code; Studio reads `frame` from the same message and ignores the new field.
- A film shorter than one second: the runtime still reports at least 1 s for it; the player now ends it on the runtime's `ended`, with its time shown as 1 s. Reporting the real length is a separate runtime fix.
- `ended` can fire twice if the runtime reaches its end again before the player's restart arrives from another origin; that race exists on main for every film and is not changed here.

## Independent review

Six review passes by reviewers that did not write the change. No open blockers or majors at this head. Findings and what happened to them:

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| A pause near the end became `ended` or a rewind (maintainer's review) | Fixed: the runtime reports `ended` and its exact time; tests for a composition pause and a host pause on the last frame |
| The player's length can sit a float step past the runtime's end, so the film never ended | Fixed: the film ends on the runtime's `ended`; test with a length a float step long; runtime test plays to the end |
| At an exact length boundary the time check overrode the runtime's `ended: false` (maintainer's second review) | Fixed: an explicit `ended` wins; absent still falls back to the frame rule; test at the boundary with loop off and on |
| Trusting `ended: false` stopped a composition with no length from looping (its runtime clock never ends) | Fixed: `ended: false` is trusted only from a stopped runtime; tests for playing past the length and for a paused film at its end |
| `ended` read from a second clock read can mark the end about a frame early | Kept: harmless; main already ended up to half a frame early |
| No test that a state sent while paused at the end neither ends nor loops | Noted; the was-playing check covers it |
| A scrub to 100% then Play plays the last few ms and ends | Kept: same as main |

title: feat(player): expose picture size, durationchange and a click-to-play opt-out
body:
## What this changes

A page that embeds `<hyperframes-player>` can now:

- read the composition's size: `player.compositionWidth` / `player.compositionHeight`, also carried in `ready`'s detail, with a `resize` event when it changes;
- hear about a duration that changes after `ready`: a `durationchange` event with `{ duration }`. On the runtime path it fires when a later `timeline` message carries a new duration; on the same-origin `__timelines` path, when the composition registers a new timeline object (seen on the next play, pause or seek);
- own clicks on the picture: with `disable-click-to-play` (or `player.disableClickToPlay = true`) a click no longer plays or pauses, so a host overlay (for example, a click that leaves a note on a frame) can use it.

Names follow `<video>`: `resize`, `durationchange`, and `disable*` like `disablepictureinpicture`.

Nothing changes for an existing embed: no new attribute means today's click behaviour, and `ready`'s detail only gains two fields. `durationchange` fires only for changes after `ready`; `ready` still carries the first duration.

Orderings moved so listeners see a fully applied message: the runtime's `timeline` message now applies the size and the scenes before `durationchange` and `ready` fire (so a `ready` listener reading `player.scenes` sees them; before this it saw the previous list), and the same-origin probe applies the document size before dispatching `ready`. The rescale that follows `ready` now lives in the one place that dispatches it, so the zero-size warning fires on both paths.

Setting `width` and then `height` fires `resize` once per attribute, since the attributes change one at a time.

TypeScript note: the DOM's built-in event map types `resize` on an element as `UIEvent`, so a typed listener reads the detail with `(event as unknown as CustomEvent)`, or reads `player.compositionWidth` instead.

## Before

Main (0.8.77), a 1080×1920 composition that grows from 4 s to 6 s after it loads, `disable-click-to-play` set, one click on the picture: `ready` carries only the duration, the size is not readable, the duration change is silent, and the click still plays.

![Before: no size in ready, no durationchange, the click plays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc689dc6-4db4-4034-be90-e611e9f17757)

## After

This branch, same page and viewport: `resize` and `ready` carry 1080×1920, `durationchange` reports 6, and the click leaves the film paused.

![After: resize and ready carry 1080x1920, durationchange reports 6, the click leaves it paused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bcf717b-ec03-41db-aea0-f50f3be9ea09)

## What I measured

- New tests fail on main (all but one, which pins today's default click behaviour) and pass on this branch: 15 of them fail with main's player sources. `hyperframes-player.test.ts`: 194 tests, exit 0; the slideshow and message-handler files pass.
- One mutation per behaviour, each killed only by its own test: `durationchange` never fires, `durationchange` also fires at `ready`, `resize` on an unchanged size, the click opt-out ignored, the probe path applying the size after `ready`, the runtime path applying the size after `ready`, scenes applied after `ready`, no rescale once the probe path is ready, autoplay decided before `ready`'s listeners ran, a queued play started before an `assetsready` listener's pause, the event queue left open after an action throws.
- `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the package; pre-commit hooks green.
- Captures: headless Chrome against both builds of `hyperframes-player.global.js`, same host page and composition.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A cross-origin (opaque sandbox) embed in a real browser; covered by unit tests of the message path only.
- Other embedders in a browser. In this repo, Studio and the slideshow read nothing from `ready`'s detail and do not set the new attribute; Desktop was not checked. The new events do not bubble, so Studio's window-level `resize` listener cannot see them.

## Events now fire after the update that raised them

Every event the player raises while applying a runtime message, a probe result or video metadata now fires once that update is fully applied, in the order raised; an event a listener raises goes behind the rest. Two bugs on main go away with it: an `ended` listener that calls `play()` was overwritten by the paused state committed after it (a page's own loop froze), and a `ready` listener that seeks cancelled autoplay. If a listener or queued action throws, the rest of the update's events still fire and the first error is rethrown.

## Independent review

Five review passes by a reviewer that did not write the change. No open blockers or majors. Findings and what happened to them:

| Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Listeners saw a half-applied message (size, scenes) | Fixed: apply-then-emit queue; tests |
| Direct events (`play`, `assetsready`) overtook a queued `ready` | Fixed: every event goes through the queue |
| A `ready` listener's seek cancelled autoplay | Fixed: autoplay decided after the listeners; test |
| A throw while flushing left the queue stuck | Fixed: every action runs, the first error is rethrown; tests |
| No test for an `assetsready` listener that pauses | Fixed: test |
| The `ended`/`play()` test did not drive a ready player or check the rewind | Fixed |
| A listener that re-raises its own event forever loops instead of overflowing the stack | Kept: needs a buggy host listener |
| Only the first of several errors is rethrown | Kept: in a browser the page's own listener errors are reported by the browser, not by this loop |

title: fix(studio): a copied clip pastes as saved, not with the preview's hidden styles
body: ## What changes A clip copied in Studio pastes as it is saved in the file. Before this, a clip copied while the playhead was before its start was pasted with the preview's hidden styles, and the pasted clip never showed. ## Why it happened Copy took each clip's markup from the live preview page. The runtime keeps a clip that has not started hidden with inline styles, so a copy taken then carried `visibility: hidden; position: absolute; display: none`. Paste wrote that into the source. Nothing ever removes those styles from a pasted clip, so it stayed invisible inside its own window. ## The fix Copy reads the element from its saved file and takes that markup. The lookup is one shared helper (`findAuthoredElement` in `utils/authoredSource.ts`), also used by the GSAP soft reload, which had its own private copy of it. - The saved file is stamped with hf-ids the same way the preview stamps the files it serves, so a live element's `data-hf-id` finds its source even when the file on disk has none. The lookup is an attribute selector over cached search roots, as fast as main's. - The shared lookup keeps main's rule: an element's `id` is used only when it has no hf-id. Copy alone also tries the `id` when the hf-id misses (a clip edited on disk since the preview loaded). The soft reload therefore never takes another file's same-id element. - Composition `

title: fix(cli): use onnxruntime-node installed beside the CLI when it is the pinned version
body:
## What changes

An optional package (`onnxruntime-node`, `@google/genai`) installed next to the CLI at the pinned version is now used from there. The CLI no longer installs its own copy into `~/.cache/hyperframes/optional` on first use. Any other version beside the CLI is ignored and the cache path runs as before.

## Why

The CLI installs these packages on first use with `npm`, into its cache. A setup that already ships the pinned version alongside the CLI had no way to use it: the loader only looked in the cache. The only lever was moving `HOME`, and the first-use install runs `npm` from the `PATH`.

## The fix

`loadOptionalPackage`, the loader every caller goes through (on-device search, background removal, `--describe` and vision captioning), first asks Node which copy `require` would load from the CLI's own location (`require.resolve`). Both paths are compared as real paths, so symlinked installs count with or without `--preserve-symlinks`. If that copy's `package.json` version equals the pin in `OPTIONAL_PACKAGES`, it loads that copy. Otherwise (another version, no manifest, an unreadable manifest) nothing changes.

`doctor` reports the same thing: a pinned copy beside the CLI shows as installed.

## What I measured

- New tests in `optionalPackages.test.ts`, 9 of them: a pinned copy beside the CLI is loaded without installing; the real lookup loads a copy at the pin and reports its version, including one symlinked into a store the way bun and pnpm install, also in a Node subprocess run with `--preserve-symlinks`; an empty folder `require` skips is looked past; a same-named file `require` would load first, a copy with no manifest, an unreadable manifest and another version are each ignored. All 9 fail on `main`. Removing the version comparison, or the `realpath` of either side, makes one of them fail.
- End to end, the CLI bundle built from `main` and from this branch, run from `packages/cli/dist/cli.js` with an empty `HOME` (the repo's dev dependencies put both packages beside it at the pinned versions):
  - `main`: `catalog --query "kinetic title" --on-device --yes` logs `installing onnxruntime-node for on-device search, once` and fills `~/.cache/hyperframes/optional`.
  - This branch: the same command installs nothing, leaves the cache empty, and answers with `"tier": "on-device"`. `doctor --json` reports `onnxruntime-node` `1.21.1 installed`.
- CLI suite at this head: 260 files, 3670 passed. Typecheck clean; fallow, comment ratchet and format pass.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A copy beside the CLI whose native binding fails to load: it is used because its version matches, so the load error surfaces instead of falling back to the cache install. That is deliberate: the pinned copy is the one the setup chose, and falling back would hide that it is broken.
- The published package from npm: `onnxruntime-node` and `@google/genai` stay out of its dependencies, so a plain `npm install hyperframes` behaves as before.

title: fix(studio): a picked element's edit writes only that element to source
body:
## What changes A style edit through `useElementPicker` on an element with no `id` now saves only that edit. Before this, it saved the whole live preview page over the source file, including the runtime's hide styles on every clip not showing at that moment. ## Why it happened With no `id` to patch by, `setStyle` took `documentElement.outerHTML` of the preview iframe and wrote it to the file. That is the page as the runtime left it: clips outside their window carry `visibility: hidden; display: none`, and anything added to the live page is saved with them. Once saved, those styles are authored, so the edited clip never shows again. Attribute and text edits on such an element were dropped instead. ## The fix The edit goes through the same target patch the timeline editors use (`applyPatchByTarget` in `utils/sourcePatcher.ts`), aimed at the `data-hf-id` the preview gives the element. hf-ids are content hashes, unique within one file only, so an element identical to one in another file shares its hf-id. The patch therefore goes into the element's own file (from its composition host, or the previewed composition, via `getSourceFileForElement`), else the one file that holds the hf-id. If no file matches, or several do and none is its own, nothing is written. - Elements with an `id` keep the old id path, unchanged. - Style, attribute and text edits all take this path, so attribute and text edits on an element with no `id` now persist. - Each write builds on this hook's own latest write to that file while the host still shows a source from that chain of writes, so two edits before the host rerenders both reach the file. Pending writes settle on every render, the way the property panel's optimistic commit does (`propertyPanelCommitField.tsx`): the host showing the newest write, an undo, or an outside edit drops them; the host showing an earlier write keeps the later ones. This applies to the `id` path too. - The two identical "picked element" builders in the message handler are now one function, `toPickedElement`. `useElementPicker` has no caller inside Studio; it is a public export of `@hyperframes/studio`. ## Before A film whose title clip runs from 2 s to 5 s. With the playhead at 0 (title hidden by the runtime), pick the title and set its color. `main` saves the title as `

` That saved file, opened in Chrome at 3 s, inside the title's window: the title is `display: none` and never shows. ![Before: the saved file hides the title](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61e7c0b8-fedc-4206-9328-b8d851abeb0e) ## After Same steps on this branch. The title is saved as `

` and shows at 3 s in the new color: ![After: the saved title shows in its new color](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fc297fcd-4c73-4e1b-90e3-ef5306726cb8) ## What I measured - New `packages/studio/src/hooks/useElementPicker.test.ts`, 9 tests. The harness host keeps the files in React state and applies each write. The first 5: a style edit writes only that edit (no hide styles, and not a script the test adds to the live page); a text edit persists; an element identical to one in a sub-composition is written to its own file, in both file orders; an element no saved file holds writes nothing. All 5 fail on `main`. - Four tests cover writes that land before the host rerenders: two edits in one React batch keep both (fails on the previous head `d218482f`); an edit after the host changed the file builds on the host's file; an edit after a host undo does not bring the undone edit back; with a host that has applied only the first of two writes, a third edit keeps all three. - The captures above come from the real hook run on `main` and on this branch, with the file each one saved opened in Chrome and read at 3 s: `main` `display: none`, branch `display: block`. - Full Studio suite at this head: 521 files, 5594 passed. Typecheck clean; the fallow audit, comment ratchet and format check pass. ## What I did NOT exercise - Studio itself: the hook has no caller there, so the captures run it in a test harness, not in the app. - An element the preview gave an hf-id that the saved file does not carry: nothing is written, where `main` wrote the page. Studio started from the CLI pins hf-ids into every composition on disk, so this needs a host that does not. - When no file or more than one file matches (and none is the element's own), the edit stays in the preview and nothing tells the user it was not saved. - Two behaviours of the shared `sourcePatcher` that the timeline editors share, unchanged here: a text edit is written as markup (`x` becomes bold in the file), and a `data-hf-id` value quoted inside an inline script can be matched instead of the element. - An embedder whose preview iframe `src` holds a raw `%`: `compositionPathOfPreviewUrl` throws while decoding it, so an edit to an element with no `id` is not saved. Studio encodes its own preview URLs. - A host that refuses a write without ever showing it: later edits to that file keep carrying the refused change. A host that shows a write and then rolls it back is handled. - Pending writes are matched to the host by file text, so a host that skips ahead to a version equal to an earlier write can keep a stale pending write until the next change. No host in the repo lags or skips. - Tests do not pin two paths: an element with an `id` never reading the iframe `src`, and the fallback to the single matching file when the element's own file does not hold it. Both were checked by the reviewer with a script.

title: fix(shader-transitions): the render leaves scene visibility to the runtime
body:
## What changes

A rendered video no longer shows a HyperShader scene outside its own time window. The preview was already right; the render now matches it. The case that showed it: the last shader scene stayed on screen after its end, drawn over the plain scene that follows it.

## Why it happened

On render frames outside a transition, the page-side compositor un-hid the "settled" scene: the destination of the latest finished shader transition, or the first shader scene before any transition. It was a workaround for the runtime hiding a film's final scene a beat before the end. The runtime has kept the last frame since #4158, so the workaround only had one effect left: it overrode the runtime's hide on a shader scene before it starts and after it ends.

## The fix

The workaround is removed. The runtime alone decides when a scene is visible, in preview and render. (This branch first narrowed the workaround to the scene's own window; review showed that copy of the runtime's timing rules misses `data-end`, reference starts and composition hosts, so it is deleted instead.)

`installPageSideCompositor` and two functions inside it get a `fallow-ignore-next-line complexity`: their complexity is unchanged from `main`, and fallow re-flags them because their lines moved.

## Before

A six-scene film: scenes 4 and 5 are joined by a shader transition, scene 5 runs 6.4 s to 8.0 s, and a plain scene 6 runs 8.0 s to 9.6 s. At 8.8 s the browser preview shows scene 6 only:

![Preview at 8.8 s: scene 6 only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/009d2dea-4a48-46cb-9bd4-5bda8bbd3547)

The render with HyperShader built from `main`, frame at 8.8 s: scene 5 is drawn over scene 6.

![Before: render at 8.8 s shows scene 5 over scene 6](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63e0cf55-015a-4b3d-87ad-9153e3956bcc)

## After

The same film rendered with HyperShader built from this branch, frame at 8.8 s: scene 6 only, as in the preview.

![After: render at 8.8 s shows scene 6 only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/912cde11-5193-4c49-8536-b90047c799a1)

## What I measured

- New tests drive the real `installPageSideCompositor` through its wrapped seek, with a fake document and WebGL context: a shader scene the runtime hid stays hidden before its window (2.4 s) and after it (8.8 s). Both fail on `main`.
- Renders, HyperShader built from `main` and from this branch: at 8.8 s the frames differ over about 48,000 pixels (scene 5); at 2.4 s and 7.2 s they match (largest pixel difference 7 of 255, encoder noise).
- The case the workaround was added for: the same film without scene 6, so scene 5 ends with the film, rendered from this branch. The last of its 240 frames shows scene 5.
- `shader-transitions` tests: 4 files, 16 passed. Typecheck clean; fallow, comment ratchet and format pass.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A film that loads this HyperShader with a runtime older than v0.8.51 (before #4158): its final scene can drop in the last beat again, as it did before the workaround. HyperShader loads unpinned from the CDN, so a CLI older than v0.7.59 rendering a 25 fps film that ends on a shader scene can lose its last frame (found by reading the code, not rendered).
- A film that runs past its last shader scene with nothing after it: `main` held that scene over the tail; the render now shows the background, as the preview does.
- The new tests do not assert that the seek was wrapped; if the install stopped polling for the seek, they would pass without exercising it.
- Browser preview has its own copy of this rule (`paintSettledSceneState` in `hyper-shader.ts`); it is not changed here.

title: fix(studio-server): studio element edits keep a save that lands while they apply
body:
## What this fixes

Studio's element edits (style, text and attribute patches, batch patches, and inserting a composition) read a file, changed it in memory and wrote it back with no check that the file was still what they read. A save that landed in between, from an agent, the CLI or another tab, was overwritten and lost.

Now:
- `applyFileMutations` checks every file against what the caller read even when no version is passed, re-checks after it takes its backup, and refuses with `FileChangedError` when the file moved on. A batch that fails partway restores only files that still hold its own write.
- The element-patch routes refold on the fresh content and retry, up to three tries, then answer 409 `{ error: "file changed", conflict: true }`. The other writer's save is kept either way, and when a retry succeeds the person's edit lands on top of it.
- `patch-element` checks after its backup and retries on that race too.
- `insert-composition` re-checks after its backup and answers 409 instead of writing over a save.
- Content writes pin their target when the path is checked: `pinWithinProject` resolves every link inside the project once, at validation, and the write goes to that file. An edit to a linked file inside the project updates that file and keeps the link (before, every element edit, batch, split cut, PUT and GSAP write replaced the link with a copy), and a file or folder link retargeted after the check, even to an outside file with the same bytes, can't redirect the write. The atomic writer itself never follows a link, as on main. Deletes and renames still act on a link itself, and create-only writes (POST, upload, duplicate) use `wx`; duplicate now does too and answers 409 if its name was taken. Two aliases of one file in one batch request now answer 400 "duplicate".
- Write receipts are keyed by real path (for a path not there yet or any more, the nearest existing folder's real path joined with the rest). A write through a link, and an undo that deletes or restores a file in a project reached through a linked folder, now match the watcher's report instead of reading as an outside change.

When all three tries race, Studio shows "Couldn't save edit: file changed" and reverts the edit in the preview, as it already does for any refused save.

A ceiling: a write from another process that lands in the few milliseconds between the final check and the rename can still be lost. Closing that needs a cross-process lock.

## Tests

`files.patchRace.test.ts` (16 cases): each patch route keeps a save that lands mid-edit and applies the edit on top; answers 409 after three raced tries and keeps the other write; refolds when a save lands during its backup; a two-file batch refolds when its first file changes after it was read; remove-element and insert-composition answer 409 instead of writing over a save; each patch route edits a linked file through its link, keeps the link, and leaves a receipt the watcher's report of the target finds; each patch route writes the file it checked when a file link or a folder link on its path is retargeted outside during its backup, and so does a split cut. `atomicFile.test.ts` checks the writer replaces a link, never its target; `hfIdPersist.noFollow.test.ts` swaps a link to an outside file in just before the stamp's write and checks the outside file is untouched; `fileVersion.test.ts` records deletion, creation and restore-into-a-missing-folder receipts in a linked folder before the file changes and finds them after. `applyFileMutations.test.ts` covers the default check and the guarded rollback. Link tests skip on Windows, where creating a symlink needs a privilege.

Results: studio-server `src/helpers` 347 pass, `src/routes` 343, `src/history` 45; `tsc`, oxfmt and oxlint clean. Single mutations, each failing its intended tests: removing patch-element's retry on a backup-time race (4 tests), removing `applyFileMutations`' post-backup check (3), removing insert-composition's post-backup re-read (1), keying receipts by the given path (3), a non-recursive folder fallback (5), leaving the element-edit context unpinned (2) or the batch resolver unpinned (4). The retargeted-link tests fail on the head that followed links at write time. No test covers duplicate's `wx`: its check-to-write window is synchronous, and a dangling link planted beforehand is already refused. At least eight of the race tests fail on main.

title: fix(core): a video's voice keeps pace with the playhead instead of trailing it
body:
## What was broken

A `<video>` with sound (a talking head, a screen recording with narration) played its voice behind the playhead for the whole clip, and further behind after each loop.

Media sync exempts a playing video from seek-based drift correction on purpose: seeking resets the decoder, which freezes the frame for about 150 ms and turns into a seek, freeze, drift, seek stutter. But nothing else corrected a playing video. A video that started a few frames late stayed that late until a hard sync (drift over 0.5 s) or the next Play.

## The fix

The fix is in `media.ts` `syncRuntimeMedia`, the one place playing media is kept on the playhead:

- **Rate steering instead of seeks:** a playing video that drifts past the media-sync tolerance (40 ms, the same threshold `<audio>` uses, now one shared constant) runs 3% fast or slow. It keeps steering until it is within 10 ms, then returns to its authored rate. Pitch is preserved by the browser's default, and the decoder is never reset.
- **One write per change:** the rate is written only when steering starts or stops, because every `playbackRate` write costs the pipeline a frame. An earlier version steered proportionally on every tick and showed a one-frame sawtooth.
- **Per-element state:** the steering direction is kept per element, so a speed-ramp clip keeps steering while its base rate moves.
  - The state is cleared on pause, hard sync and eviction.
  - A hard-sync tick plays the authored rate.
  - A rate that reads back at lower precision is not rewritten.

## Measured in Studio (real browser)

The fixture is one talking-head `<video>` with sound, taken from the public launch-video projects. Log the video's lag behind its target (`playhead - start - currentTime`) during 14 s of play from 0:

| | lag |
|---|---|
| main | 92 ms, constant for the whole clip (rate stays 1) |
| this branch | 135 ms at start, closing at 3% to 22 ms by 4 s, then a steady 9-10 ms at rate 1 |

## Tests

`media.test.ts`, `playing video drift`:

- lag past tolerance → 3% fast, no seek
- ahead → 3% slow
- steering holds until nearly back, then returns to the authored rate
- no steering inside the tolerance
- scales with the transport rate
- holds through a speed ramp
- a hard-sync tick plays the authored rate
- pause returns to the authored rate
- eviction clears the steering
- a lower-precision readback is written once

The first four steering tests fail on main. Each later test fails when the line it guards is removed. On this head: `media` 139/139, `mediaProxy` 34/34, `init` 152/152.

## Review

- **First review:** approved with minors, fixed in the second commit: speed ramps stopped steering early, possible Safari readback precision, and a stale offset on hard-sync ticks.
- **Delta review:** approved, with test-coverage nits that are fixed in the third commit.
- **Final delta review:** approved at this head with no findings.

Not verified in a browser: Safari and Firefox rate-change behaviour. The logic only assumes `playbackRate` is writable and pitch-preserving by default.

## Before

Main, same fixture (one talking-head `<video>` with sound), Play from 0 for 12 s with the audio recorded from the output. The picture runs a constant 47 ms ahead of the heard voice for the whole clip, measured in 45 half-second windows against the rendered film.

_Capture removed: it showed a private project; a fixture capture will replace it._

## After

The same steps on this branch. The gap starts at 76 ms, closes by 2.5 s, and holds at 1-2 ms after that (median 1 ms across the same 45 windows).

_Capture removed: it showed a private project; a fixture capture will replace it._

title: perf(studio): let a paused preview check in once a second instead of every 80 ms
body:
## Summary

A paused Studio preview now checks in with Studio once a second instead of about 12 times a second. Studio's preview is a `<hyperframes-player>`, and Studio now sets the player's `low-power-idle` attribute (added in #4483). A paused, untouched Studio stops waking the preview and itself on every 80 ms beat. The browser's idle CPU drops by about a fifth on the bench below, and edits reach the screen as fast as before.

## The trade

This is the trade #4483 describes, now taken by Studio:

- While the preview is paused and its timeline is fully bound, anything the runtime can only find by polling reaches Studio up to 1 s later instead of 80 ms later. That covers a timeline written into `window.__timelines` with no DOM change, or an animation that lengthens by itself.
- Until the timeline is fully bound, the runtime keeps the 80 ms beat, so a composition that registers its timeline late is still picked up at once.
- Edits, seeks, play and DOM changes act at once, as before. Playback is unchanged.

## A fix the slower beat needed

A preview load could wait for the runtime's next post before Studio took it over. This applies to every reload after an edit, since the shadow reload uses the same load path. With one post a second, that wait could reach a full second.

- `onIframeLoad` now retries on each animation frame after a readiness post whose attempt failed, until it settles or the existing 5 s safety net fires.
- The retry stops when the player unmounts or resets. Both now go through `cancelPendingLoad`, which also drops the wait's message listener; before, unmount left that listener behind.

## Measured

Studio at main vs this branch, the same 60 s, 12-scene fixture, headless Chrome 152 on a shared 32-core Linux box. Medians.

Idle, 5 interleaved rounds, the 20 s after the first frame plus 5 s (box load 4 to 25 during the run):

| | main | this branch | Remotion Studio 4.0.527, same rounds |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser CPU, all processes | 13.1% | **10.7%** | 7.3% |
| Server CPU | 1.7% | 1.2% | 0.5% |
| Browser memory (PSS) | 735 MB | 728 MB | 577 MB |

The idle run measured the attribute alone; the load fix above changes nothing while idle.

Edit to new pixels, with the heartbeat logged around each edit (this branch before the unmount and reset fixes, which do not touch edits). Only the rounds where the box load was under 15 count here; the other rounds ran at load 20 to 42, where every build's edits took two to four times longer:

| | main (2 rounds) | this branch (2 rounds) |
|---|---|---|
| State messages to Studio in the second before the edit | 12-13 | 1-2 |
| Text edit | 872, 1072 ms | 871, 855 ms |
| Colour edit | 820, 959 ms | 831, 808 ms |
| Timing edit | 734, 1009 ms | 811, 814 ms |

## Tests

- `Player.test.ts`: the preview's player element carries `low-power-idle` (fails without the attribute).
- `useTimelinePlayer.play.test.ts`:
  - a load whose runtime learns its duration after its only readiness post still settles, one frame later;
  - the retry stops when the player unmounts, and when it resets.

  Each fails on the code before its fix.
- The runtime side (the 1 s beat, the late-timeline guard, turning it off) is covered by #4483's `transportPark.test.ts`.

## Before

Main, paused and untouched 25 s after opening. The badge at the top is injected by the capture script, not by Studio: it counts the preview's state messages to Studio in the last second.

![Before: 12 state messages a second](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca34eb57-dd0c-4b0d-a840-fa2d1255b711)

## After

This branch, same project, same moment: one message a second, same picture.

![After: 1 state message a second](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9e7d6d9-74c8-4eab-a144-1306b4102508)

title: fix(studio-server): a drag gesture stays one undo step however long it pauses
body:
## What this fixes

Studio's drag gestures ask the project history to keep one drag as one undo step until another edit starts (`coalesceMs: Infinity`). JSON turns `Infinity` into `null`, the claim route dropped it, and the history fell back to its 2-second idle default, so a drag that paused for 2 seconds became several undo steps.

Now a claim with a coalescing key and no usable `idleMs` holds until another key, and the history starts no timer for a non-finite idle time. Finite idle times behave as before. Studio needs no change: the `null` it already sends now means "until another key".

A held gesture stays out of the history list until the next edit or history operation commits it (the Undo button names it meanwhile), and if the server stops while one is held, its writes are filed as "Changed outside the app" on reopen. Before, both lasted at most 2 seconds.

## Tests

`routes/history.test.ts`: a gesture claimed with `idleMs: null` that pauses longer than the idle default stays one entry. Results: routes 13, `projectHistory.test.ts` 78 (2 skipped on Linux), Studio `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts` 10, CLI `src/utils` 859 and `commands/history.test.ts` 31, `tsc` clean in studio-server, studio and cli. Single mutations, each failing the new test: the route keeping the engine's default, and the engine starting a timer for `Infinity`.

title: fix(core): a project path typed in another letter case stays inside the project
body:
## What this fixes

`isSafePath` (and `resolveWithinProject`) compared paths resolved with `realpathSync`, which keeps the letter case the caller typed. On a case-insensitive disk (the macOS default, and Windows) a path inside the project typed in another case, or a project path typed in another case, compared as outside and was refused.

Now both sides resolve with `realpathSync.native`, which returns the case on disk, so containment is decided on the real path. Symlink resolution and the handling of not-yet-existing trailing segments are unchanged. On volumes where the native call refuses with `EISDIR` (some Windows RAM disks), it falls back to `realpathSync`, as before this change.

## Tests

- `safePath.test.ts`: an in-project path typed in another letter case is admitted, and a path outside stays refused. It runs only on case-insensitive disks (macOS, Windows) and skips on Linux. Checked on macOS against the file on main: main refuses both in-project paths, this change admits them, the outside path stays refused.
- `safePath.eisdir.test.ts`: with the native call throwing `EISDIR`, paths still resolve, and the outside path is still refused.

Results: `safePath.test.ts` 14 (1 skipped on Linux), `safePath.eisdir.test.ts` 1. Removing the `EISDIR` fallback fails the new test.

title: fix(core): scrubbing stays audible after the first Play
body:
## What was broken

In Studio, dragging the playhead while paused plays a short audition of the music track. After the first Play and Pause of a session, that audition went silent for the rest of the session.

The preview routes each `<audio>` element into Web Audio with `createMediaElementSource`. After that call the element has no native output of its own: it is audible only while its source node is connected to the graph. `stopAll()` (Pause, seek, end of film) disconnected the node, and only the next Play reconnected it. Studio's scrub audition plays the element directly under a paused clock, so it played into nothing.

## The fix

`webAudioTransport.ts` is the one owner of that routing:

- **Outside a play:** `stopAll()` connects each captured element straight to the context's destination. It behaves exactly like an element that was never captured: its own `volume` and `muted` apply, and master volume and mute do not.
- **Inside a play:** `scheduleMediaElementPlayback()` disconnects that route before building the element's chain, so an element always has one path out.
- **Review follow-ups:**
  - A track hidden while playing is zeroed in the same task as the reschedule, so it cannot sound for a frame on the direct route.
  - `stopAll()` advances the play generation, so a schedule still waiting on `resume()` when Pause lands is dropped instead of adding a second path.
  - The capture fallback in `init.ts` skips a pass that a newer pass or a stop already replaced, so it can no longer mute a track the newer pass captured.

## Measured in Studio (real browser, audio recorded from the output)

The film is `pr-to-video-launch` from the public launch-video projects. It has a music-classified track, so Studio auditions it on scrub. Drag the playhead, Play for 3 s, Pause, then drag again:

| | scrub before any Play | scrub after Play and Pause |
|---|---|---|
| main | -23.2 dB RMS | -180 dB (digital silence) |
| fix | -23.8 dB RMS | -22.3 dB RMS |

Films without a music-classified track never audition on scrub; that is unchanged.

The fix-side numbers and the After clip come from a build that also carried two separate playback-clock fixes, which are going up as their own PRs. Scrub routing is only touched by this change.

## Tests

- `capturedMediaIdleRoute.test.ts` fails on main and passes here:
  - A captured element is audible to a paused scrub after the first Play and Pause.
  - During the next Play it reaches the speakers only through its chain.
  - A track hidden while playing is silent at once.
  - A processed track whose capture a newer pass replaced is not muted, and still reaches the output.
- `webAudioTransport.test.ts` has a new case: a schedule waiting on `resume()` returns null when `stopAll()` comes first. One existing assertion there used "the source is never disconnected" as a stand-in for "the cached node is reused". It is removed, because the other two assertions in that test already pin reuse.
- Each new test was checked against the code before its fix and fails there. Removing the direct route, or skipping the disconnect on Play, fails the first test.
- Run on this head: `capturedMediaIdleRoute` 3/3, `webAudioTransport` 80/80, `init` 152/152, `webAudioRoute` 29/29, `deckAudio` 1/1.

## Review

An independent adversarial review found no blockers and no majors. Its two minors are fixed in the second commit. The delta review of that commit raised one minor (the stale capture fallback), fixed in the third commit. A test-hygiene minor from the next delta review is fixed in the fourth. The final delta review approved this head with no findings.

## Before

Main: drag, Play 3 s, Pause, drag again. The second drag is silent.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ecd305e-fa64-4b5d-962e-7d77f99ed50e

## After

The same film, steps and viewport on the fix. The second drag is audible.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14ecd911-7b6e-4196-8e87-94c80661c00e

title: Studio: resizing after a drag inserts tl.set before the timeline declaration (TDZ ReferenceError)
body:
### Describe the bug After an element has been dragged in Studio (which writes a global `gsap.set("#el", { x, y })` **above** the timeline declaration, per #2099), resizing it writes `tl.set("#el", { width, height }, 0)` **also above** the declaration. `const tl` is then referenced in its temporal dead zone, the composition script throws, and every animation in the composition stops working. Cause: `findInsertionPoint` in `packages/parsers/src/gsapWriterAcorn.ts` anchors new `tl.*` statements after the last located GSAP call. When the only located call is a global hold, that position is before `const tl = gsap.timeline(...)`. `addLabelToScript` and `addAnimationWithKeyframesToScript` share the same insertion point. ### Minimal reproduction ```html
``` Or directly against the writer: ```ts const s1 = addAnimationToScript(script, { targetSelector: "#box", method: "set", position: 0, properties: { x: 53, y: 157 }, global: true }).script; const s2 = addAnimationToScript(s1, { targetSelector: "#box", method: "set", position: 0, properties: { width: 512, height: 670 } }).script; // s2: gsap.set(...); tl.set(...); const tl = gsap.timeline(...) ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npx hyperframes preview` on the composition above. 2. Drag `#box` on the canvas (a global `gsap.set` is written above the timeline). 3. Resize `#box` with a corner handle. ### Expected behavior `tl.set("#box", { width, height }, 0)` is inserted after `const tl = gsap.timeline(...)`. ### Actual behavior ```js gsap.set("#box", { x: 53, y: 157 }); tl.set("#box", { width: 512, height: 670 }, 0); const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true }); ``` → `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'tl' before initialization`; the composition script aborts. Workaround: put any `tl.*` call (e.g. `tl.set({}, {}, 0);`) right after the declaration so there is a located call to anchor on. ### Environment hyperframes CLI 0.8.77 (also reproduced on `main` @ 0985b45), macOS, Chrome. ### Additional context Fix PR to follow. The legacy recast writer in `gsapParser.ts` (`insertAfterAnchor`) has the same shape, but its write path is retired, so the PR leaves it alone.

title: Preview: tl.set holds never render when the root timeline has zero duration
body:
### Describe the bug A root timeline whose own duration is 0 — e.g. one that only holds `tl.set(...)` at position 0, which is exactly what Studio writes for a static resize — never renders its sets in the preview. After resizing an element in Studio the file is correct, but the element snaps back to its authored size in the preview (keeping the drag offset), so it looks like the resize was lost. Cause: in `packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`, an unusable (zero) root duration takes the `createDurationFloorTimeline` fallback: the root timeline is added to a new paused wrapper padded to the composition duration. The author's root was created `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })` and stays paused, and a paused child is never rendered when its parent is seeked. The nested-composition path already unpauses held children (`ensureChildCandidatesActive`); the floor wrapper does not. ### Minimal reproduction ```html
``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. `npx hyperframes preview` on the composition above (or produce it by resizing an element in Studio in a composition without tweens). 2. Look at `#box` at any playhead position. ### Expected behavior `#box` renders at 200×150. ### Actual behavior `#box` stays at 400×300. In the preview iframe, `__timelines.main.paused()` is `true`, its children are never initialised, and `__player.seek(t)` has no effect on it. After `__timelines.main.paused(false)`, `__player.seek(0.5)` renders 200×150. A single tween in the timeline (non-zero duration) avoids the fallback and the bug. `hyperframes snapshot --at 0.5` of the same file renders 200×150 correctly, so only the preview runtime is affected. ### Environment hyperframes CLI 0.8.77 (also on `main` @ 0985b45), GSAP 3.12.5 and 3.15.0, macOS, Chrome (headed and headless). ### Additional context Fix PR to follow: unpause the root timeline once the floor wrapper actually holds it, mirroring `ensureChildCandidatesActive`.

title: fix(parsers): never insert timeline calls before the timeline declaration
body:
## What

`findInsertionPoint` in the acorn GSAP writer no longer returns a position before the timeline declaration.

## Why

Since #2099, a canvas drag writes a global `gsap.set(...)` **above** `const tl = gsap.timeline(...)`. A later static resize anchors its new `tl.set(...)` after the last located call. That call is the global set, so the new statement is emitted before `const tl` exists. The composition then throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'tl' before initialization` and stops rendering.

## Related work

Fixes #4518

## How

If the last located call ends before the timeline declaration, insert after the declaration instead. Other cases behave as before. The legacy `gsapParser.ts` `insertAfterAnchor` has the same pattern but is no longer on the Studio write path, so it is left untouched.

## Test plan

- [x] Added two tests in `gsapWriter.acorn.test.ts` (global set only → `tl.set` / `addLabel` insert). Each executes the rewritten script against stubs to prove it runs without a TDZ error.
- [x] The new tests fail without the fix and pass with it.
- [x] `vitest`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit` pass.
- [x] Reproduced the ReferenceError in Studio (drag, then resize) on 0.8.77; the fix itself is verified at the writer level by the tests above.

title: fix(runtime): unpause a zero-duration root timeline held by the duration-floor wrapper
body:
## What

When the runtime wraps a zero-duration root timeline in the duration-floor timeline, it now unpauses the author's root timeline once the wrapper actually holds it.

## Why

A root timeline made only of `tl.set(..., 0)` calls has zero duration. This is exactly what Studio writes for a static resize. `createDurationFloorTimeline` wraps that root in a paused, padded timeline. The author's `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })` stays paused inside it, and a paused child never renders when its parent is seeked. As a result, the preview keeps showing the authored size, while `hyperframes snapshot` renders the correct one.

## Related work

Fixes #4519

## How

After `fallbackTimeline.add(existingRootTimeline, 0)`, the new code reads the children back with `getChildren(true, true, true)`. It calls `existingRootTimeline.paused(false)` only when the root is present. This is the same rule the nested-composition path already applies (`ensureChildCandidatesActive`). The wrapper remains the paused transport, so the paused-transport invariant holds.

## Test plan

- [x] Added two tests in `init.test.ts`: the root is unpaused when the wrapper holds it, and it stays paused when the wrapper does not.
- [x] The regression test fails without the fix and passes with it.
- [x] `init.test.ts` + `pausedTransportInvariant.test.ts` (159 tests), `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` pass.
- [x] Verified in a live preview that `__timelines.main.paused(false)` makes the resized size appear.

title: fix(shader-transitions): a paused preview keeps the runtime's scene visibility
body:
## What this changes

A paused preview no longer shows a HyperShader scene outside its time window once the transition prewarm finishes. Before, a scene with a background could cover the film until the next seek.

## Why it happened

The prewarm scrubs the timeline with events on to capture transition frames. That fired HyperShader's transition-start callback, which made both scenes of the transition visible. The prewarm's teardown then restored a visibility snapshot, and the settled state outside a transition set visibility too. On a paused page nothing re-syncs visibility afterwards, so the runtime's hide (from `data-start` / `data-duration`) was lost.

## The fix

HyperShader now leaves the CSS `visibility` of scenes it is not showing to the runtime.

- The transition-start callback does nothing while the prewarm runs. The prewarm counts as running until after its restore seek.
- The prewarm's style snapshot no longer saves or restores visibility.
- Outside a transition, HyperShader resets opacity and pointer-events only.
- During a transition, scenes outside the pair get opacity 0 and no pointer events, not `visibility: hidden`. A scene with no timing attributes is therefore not left hidden after a seek that skips events. The two scenes of the pair are still shown, as before.
- The native html-in-canvas capture now honours `forceVisible` like the html2canvas path. The prewarm no longer makes scenes visible before capturing them, so without this a scene the runtime hid would capture blank.
- If a timeline callback throws during the prewarm's restore seek, HyperShader warns and finishes the prewarm (repaint, resume, ready event), the way a failed capture already does. On main the throw skipped the rest.

The transition-end callback is unchanged from main. It only sets opacity and pointer-events, and the prewarm restores both.

## Tests

- `hyper-shader.preview.test.ts`, on a paused fake timeline:
  - Both scenes, hidden after the prewarm took its snapshot, stay hidden once `shaderTransitionsReady` resolves. The test also checks that the prewarm ran. It fails on main, and it fails with any one of the start guard, the flag move, the snapshot change or the settled-state change reverted on its own.
  - A scene outside the pair is not left hidden after a seek that skips events. Fails with the old pair painter.
  - A callback that throws during the restore seek is warned about, and seeking keeps working. Fails with the previous rethrow.
- `capture.clone.test.ts`: a hidden scene and its timed clip are drawn visible by the html-in-canvas path when `forceVisible` is set. Fails with main's `capture.ts`.
- The shader-transitions package passes 47/47 tests, and its typecheck passes.

## Before / After

A film loaded paused at 1.0 s, after the prewarm, with no seek. Scene 1 (0 to 1.6 s) has a light background and a line of static text. Scene 4 (due at 4.8 s) has a solid blue background, so the runtime hides it at 1.0 s. Captured in headless Chrome at this head (4dc67e28) and on main.

Before (main): scene 4's blue background covers scene 1's light background. Scene 1's text still shows because it stacks above scene 4 in this film.

After (this PR): scene 1 as authored, light background and text.

Scene 1's animated headline is missing in both frames: the film's own tweens are not drawn after the prewarm until the next seek. That also happens on main and gets its own fix.

## Not in this PR

- A scene outside the pair can still be clicked through a child with an explicit `pointer-events: auto`, and an author's own opacity tween on a scene element can win over the opacity 0 mid-transition. Outside transitions the same opacity-only policy applies.
- A clip the runtime hides with `display: none`, and with no timed children, still captures blank on both capture paths. This predates this change.
- A runtime seek through `totalTime` during the prewarm is not held back by the prewarm. This predates this change.

![Before (main): scene 4 blue background covers scene 1 at 1.0 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8883d80a-af13-43b3-8972-f0d744725f00)

![After: scene 1 as authored at 1.0 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86fa16c4-1d9e-4627-a856-c7c6eef05ddf)

title: fix(shader-transitions): a runtime seek during the prewarm is where the preview lands
body:
## What this changes

A paused preview that is seeked while the shader-transition prewarm runs (for example, Studio restoring the playhead on load) now shows the film at that time once the prewarm finishes. Before, the prewarm put the timeline back where it was before the seek: the film's own tweens showed that older time (the headline missing at 1.0 s) while the player reported the new time, until the next seek.

## Why it happened

The runtime seeks the timeline through `totalTime` (`packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`). HyperShader wraps `play`, `pause`, `time` and `seek` so it can put the playhead back after the prewarm scrubs through transitions, but it did not wrap `totalTime`. A runtime seek during the prewarm was never recorded, so the prewarm restored the playhead from before the seek.

Measured in headless Chrome, paused film, `__player.seek(1.0)` while the prewarm runs, read after `hyperShader:ready`:

| | timeline time | player time | headline |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0 | 1.0 | hidden |
| this PR | 1.0 | 1.0 | visible |

## The fix

- `totalTime` is wrapped. A call from outside HyperShader is applied as before and recorded as the playhead the prewarm restores. Reading `totalTime` during the prewarm returns that recorded playhead, as reading `time` already does.
- GSAP's `play`, `pause`, `time` and `seek` go through `totalTime` internally, as do `timeScale`, `paused` and `reversed`, which re-render in place. HyperShader's own calls to these, and any call to the last three, pass through without being recorded. So a speed change during the prewarm does not record a capture frame as the playhead.
- Each capture re-seeks to its sample frame, with events suppressed, right after its paint wait. An outside seek that lands during that wait therefore cannot put another frame into the snapshot cache. Examples are the runtime's volume probe restoring the playhead, a transport tick, or Studio restoring the playhead. On main such a seek could land in a capture too.

## Tests

`hyper-shader.preview.test.ts`. The fake timeline now routes `time()`, `timeScale()` and `paused(value)` through `totalTime()`, as GSAP does. Each test below fails without the piece named.

- A `totalTime` seek during the prewarm is where the playhead ends up (the wrapper).
- A seek on a capture frame is applied at once, reads back the recorded playhead before it, and is restored to (applying, the getter, recording).
- A speed change, or `paused(false)`, on a capture frame does not move the playhead (the in-place re-render list).
- A seek after the prewarm passes straight through.
- An outside seek during every paint wait does not reach the capture (the re-seek).
- A callback that throws inside a capture seek does not stop later outside seeks from being recorded (the `finally` in the own-seek counter).
- The existing test that a throwing callback does not stop later seeks also fails if HyperShader's own seeks go through the wrapper unmarked.
- The shader-transitions package passes 54/54 tests, and its typecheck passes.

Also measured in headless Chrome with the real runtime: a film with `tl.set("#x", { opacity: 0.25 }, 0)`, reloaded paused at 0 with a warm snapshot cache, draws the set (opacity 0.25), as on main.

## Before / After

The same film, loaded paused and seeked to 1.0 s while the prewarm runs, captured in headless Chrome after `hyperShader:ready` at this head. Scene 1 has a static line of text, so both frames show it rendering.

Before (main): the static line shows, but the headline and tagline, which tween in by 0.7 s, are missing.

After (this PR): headline, tagline and the static line.

## Not in this PR

- On a repeating or yoyo timeline, the recorded playhead is a `totalTime` value, but the prewarm restores it through `time()`, which folds it into the first cycle. The `seek` wrapper already had this mismatch before this change.
- If HyperShader's timeline is nested in a parent timeline, the parent drives it through `render()` and none of the wrappers run. That is unchanged.

![Before (main): headline and tagline missing at 1.0 s after the prewarm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed176b68-a4f3-439f-9d92-7891c410ed02)

![After: headline and tagline drawn at 1.0 s after the prewarm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e0a953cd-e69e-4bd2-ab1f-a43d2b57d0ea)

title: fix(studio-server): undo of a studio edit keeps a save that landed just before it
body:
Stacked on #4493 (it changes the claim step #4493 adds). Review after #4493; the base retargets to `main` once it lands.

## What this fixes

Studio's element edit reads a file, changes it and writes it back, then tells the project history which version it overwrote so the history can split off anyone else's save. The version Studio reports is the one its client last knew. When a save B lands between the server's read and its write (from an agent, the CLI or an editor), Studio's write replaces B, the client still reports the older A, and the history files A → edit as Studio's. Undo then writes A, and B is gone from the file and from the history.

Now the server's writes record the bytes each write replaced on its write receipt, and the claim step walks those receipts back from the claimed bytes. It stops at the version the client reported, at the change's own starting point, or at bytes the server did not write. The stop point is the cut: B is kept as "Changed outside the app" and Studio's entry is B → edit, so undo returns to B.

- Several server writes before one claim (a group timing move over animated clips writes once per clip) walk back through all of them and stay one entry, one undo.
- A whole-file save that follows a patch (fonts added to the page) records what it replaced too.
- If Studio's writes loop back to earlier bytes, the walk says nothing about what came first, so the client's reported version stands.
- Once a claim has walked through a write's replaced bytes they are dropped, so a later claim can't walk back through a write that an editor has since restored. Only the writes the walk visited are touched, so a Studio write landing while the claim runs keeps its bytes for the next claim.
- Replaced bytes are read as raw bytes in the file routes, and a receipt holding them expires with the receipt: every record drops every path's expired receipts.
- A cut the history stored for the kept save is protected from budget cleanup while it is still pending.
- Every cut is stored before any change is split, so a disk error part-way leaves the pending changes whole.

`identifyFileWrite` still returns `{ path, version, writeToken }`; the replaced bytes stay internal to the receipt store.

## No visible change

Server only. Nothing in Studio's UI changes; undo simply lands on the right bytes.

## Tests

`routes/history.test.ts`, through the real file and history routes, undo after: a save landing between Studio's read and its write (back to B); an edit written as two patches (back to A, one step); a save before a patch and its whole-file follow-up (back to B); patches that come back to earlier bytes (back to A). `projectHistory.test.ts`: a budget cleanup running before the kept save is logged keeps its bytes; a claim after an editor restored earlier bytes cuts at the restored save, not at bytes an earlier claim used; a Studio write landing during a claim keeps what it replaced for the next claim.

Results: studio-server `src/history` 79 passed (2 skipped on Linux), `src/routes` 324, `src/helpers` 332; `tsc`, oxfmt and oxlint clean. Single mutations, each failing its intended tests: the route recording no replaced bytes, the whole-file save recording none, a single lookup instead of the walk, cutting at the claimed bytes on a loop, leaving pending cuts out of the cleanup's keep set, not dropping used bytes, and dropping every write's bytes instead of the walked ones. The first test fails on #4493's head.

title: fix(repo): keep one fallow audit base cache per checkout instead of one per main commit
body:
## What this fixes

Every commit that touches `packages/**` runs `fallow audit --base origin/main` from lefthook. fallow 2.75 builds a snapshot of the base commit as a git worktree in the temp dir, named `fallow-audit-base-cache-<hash of the checkout path>-<first 16 chars of the base sha>`, and keeps it for reuse. It reuses it only while `origin/main` stays on the same commit, and it never removes the one for an old base. So each checkout gains a new snapshot (about 250 to 800 MB) every time main moves, forever. On one shared dev machine with many checkouts, 849 of them filled 28 GB.

The lockfile pins fallow 2.75, which has no option for this: the path is fixed to the temp dir and its orphan sweep skips reusable snapshots on purpose. fallow 2.77 added age-based cleanup (`audit.cacheMaxAgeDays`, default 30 days, shortest 1 day). Even at 1 day it keeps every base audited that day, so a checkout still holds many snapshots; this keeps one.

This change runs a small script right after the audit in the same hook command. It removes this checkout's snapshots for any base other than the current `origin/main`, deregisters them from git's worktree list, and leaves the current one so the next audit reuses it. Snapshots of other checkouts are left alone. The commit still gets the audit's own exit status.

## What I measured

On a Linux dev machine, fallow 2.75, isolated temp dir, audits against two successive base commits:

| | Snapshots left | Disk |
|---|---|---|
| Without the prune | 2 | 484 MB |
| With the prune | 1 | 243 MB |

- The exact hook command run twice leaves 1 snapshot and exits 0; the second run reuses it (3 s against 5 s).
- `scripts/prune-fallow-audit-caches.test.mjs` passes (2/2): a unit test of which names are stale, and an end-to-end run with the repo's own fallow in a temp repo: two audits against two bases leave two snapshots, the prune leaves the new base's, removes the old one from git's worktree list and leaves another checkout's alone. It runs the real fallow, so a change to fallow's naming fails it.
- The test clears git's hook variables and turns off commit signing and hooks for its temp repo, so it also passes when run from inside a git hook or on a machine that signs commits.
- Mutations each fail the test: removing the current base's snapshot too, deleting the folder without deregistering the worktree, and a prune that removes nothing.
- The script's hash of the checkout path reproduces fallow's snapshot name exactly (xxh3-64 of the canonical checkout path), also for a non-ASCII path, a checkout reached through a symlink, and a symlinked or unset temp dir.

## What I did NOT exercise

- macOS: the hash and temp-dir rules are the same in fallow's source, but I measured on Linux only.
- Snapshots of a checkout that has since been deleted: this only runs in a live checkout. fallow 2.77+'s own age-based cleanup covers those; upgrading is a separate change.
- A prune racing a hand-run audit against a different base in the same checkout: the script does not take fallow's lock.

title: perf(studio): a clip's filmstrip decodes 9 frames instead of 272 and reaches the clip's end
body:
## What changes for a user

- Opening a project with a video clip decodes far fewer video frames to draw the clip's timeline strip: 272 down to 9 on our benchmark film, per Studio open.
- A video clip's strip now reaches the end of the clip. Before, a clip with fewer tiles than requested frames showed only the start of the clip, and one with more tiles repeated the strip.
- A trimmed video whose file reports no length (a fragmented MP4) now shows a strip across its trim, instead of one frame repeated on every tile.

## How

1. **Keyframes** (`thumbnailVideoDecoder.ts`). A frame that sits on a keyframe decodes alone; a frame between keyframes decodes the whole run before it. Each strip slot now decodes at the keyframe at or before its time, but only when that keyframe is within half a slot (a quarter of the clip for the poster) and inside the trim. Otherwise it keeps its own time, so every tile still shows its own stretch of the clip.
2. **One lookup per decode.** The canvas sink pulls decode times from a generator that looks up each keyframe just before its frame is decoded. A WebM keyframe lookup loads its whole cluster. Doing every lookup first pushed the early clusters out of the source cache, so the decode pass downloaded them again. A cancel during a lookup ends the generator without throwing, so the decoder still closes (a throw there skips the decoder close). The cancel is raised after the loop.
3. **Missing length.** When the file reports no duration, the source is taken to end at trim start plus trim length. It used to end at the trim length, so a trim starting later collapsed to zero length.
4. **Tiles** (`VideoThumbnail.tsx`). The strip requests a power of two of frames spread over the whole clip, and tile `i` used to show frame `i`. Each tile now shows the frame nearest its own place along the clip.

## Numbers

Studio open on the benchmark film (a 60 s film with one 30 s, 1080p H.264 video clip), headless Chrome, 1600x900, all `VideoDecoder.decode` calls counted for 30 s after navigation. Run on a 32-core Linux box, 3 rounds per build:

| build | decodes per open (each round) | of which keyframes |
|---|---|---|
| main | 272, 272, 272 | 9 |
| this branch | 9, 9, 9 | 9 |

Idle browser CPU in the 7 to 27 s window after open, median of 3 rounds (box load 13 to 26): 12.6% on main, 11.3% on this branch. After 40 s there is no difference (6.3% vs 6.8%). This was measured at the first commit, which decodes the same 9 frames on this film.

Bytes and decodes through mediabunny's real demuxer and decode pump in Node, with a counting decoder and an HTTP server that counts Range requests and bytes (2 rounds on the WebM, identical):

| file | slots | main | keyframes, all lookups first | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 s WebM with Cues, 25 Mbps (187 MB) | 32 | 973 decodes, 183,003 KiB | 778 decodes, 365,897 KiB | 778 decodes, 183,003 KiB |
| same | 16 | 75 decodes, 87,835 KiB | 16 decodes, 173,275 KiB | 16 decodes, 87,131 KiB |
| 20 s MP4, keyframe every 2 s | 8 | 244 decodes | 160 | 160 |
| 60 s MP4, keyframe every 2 s | 16 | 75 decodes | 16 | 16 |
| fragmented MP4 with no reported length, trimmed 5 to 10 s | 8 | 1 distinct image | 1 distinct image | 8 distinct images |

## The trade

- A tile can show a frame up to half a slot before its own time, and the poster up to a quarter of the clip before its midpoint.
- The saving only exists where slots are further apart than about one keyframe interval. A dense strip (zoomed in, a short clip, or a screen recording with keyframes 10 s apart or a single keyframe) keeps exact times and decodes the same frames as main.

## Known limits

- **WebM without Cues** still loses tiles. The cause is in mediabunny (1.45.3, still present in 1.60.0): a second key lookup into a cluster it already visited returns nothing. This branch returns 5 of 8 tiles where main returns 1 of 8. The fix belongs upstream.
- **Frames decoded but not shown.** 5 tiles decode 8 frames and show the 5 nearest their places (3 unused keyframe decodes on the benchmark film, and uneven spacing: 0, 8, 16, 20, 28 s on a 30 s clip), because the request stays a power of two so a resize keeps a stable cache identity (#4234).

## Tests

- `thumbnailVideoDecoder.test.ts`: new tests for lookups running just before each decode, the cancel ending the decode times without throwing, and the no-length trim. They failed on the previous head (`expected [ 'key 0', 'key 5', 'key 10', …] to deeply equal [ 'key 0', 'frame 0', 'key 5', …]`, `expected [ [ 5, 5, 5 ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 5, 7.5, 10 ] ]`).
- `VideoThumbnail.test.tsx`: a new test that 5 tiles over 8 frames show frames 0, 2, 4, 5 and 7. It failed on the previous head (`blob:0, blob:1, blob:2, blob:3, blob:4`).
- Mutants checked: throwing inside the generator on cancel, and dropping the cancel check after the loop. Both are caught.
- The whole studio suite passes (520 files, 5597 tests). Each commit passes the two changed test files on its own.

## Before

Top: the benchmark film's video clip. Bottom: the same film with a 30 s clip whose frames show their own second.

![Before: the strip stops at the 17 s frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c85c3c63-8c3b-4a6e-9651-0394b9bd2321)

## After

The same two clips on this branch.

![After: the strip reaches the 28 s frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/77be2b47-9cc3-495e-9355-7342c1b650dc)

title: feat(registry): add ai-answer-rank
body:
## What

Adds `ai-answer-rank`, a 1080×1080, 9 s block that asks "Is your brand in the AI answer?"

1. A prompt types into a chat card.
2. The assistant lists three picks.
3. The list re-ranks: the brand slides into its slot and the picks below step down.
4. The brand row lands with the one accent highlight and a drawn check.

**Preview (MP4, 1080×1080, 9 s):** https://github.com/tugrawork-creator/saas-motion-kit/releases/download/v1.2/hyperframes-ai-answer-rank-preview.mp4

## Why

Answer-engine and AI-visibility marketing needs a ranking story. `ai-chat-reveal` streams a free-text reply; this block makes "you are now in the answer" the payoff.

## Related work

None found. I searched the issues and PRs for ranking, AI answer and chat reveal.

## How

- **Motion without re-layout:**
  - Rank numbers belong to the slots, not the rows, so rows move only by transform and no text changes mid-shot.
  - The pick pushed out of the top three fades through a masked edge instead of a hard clip.
  - The prompt bubble is pre-sized, so the card never reflows while the prompt types.
- **Variables:** `prompt`, `lead`, `rowA`, `rowB`, `rowC`, `brand`, `brandRank` (1–3), `accent`, `ink` and `ground`. They are declared on `<html>` and read the way `ai-chat-reveal` reads them, including its `portrays` tags.
- **Placeholder material:** the UI is monochrome, and the accent appears only on the brand row. There are no assets, and it uses `Inter` with system fallbacks.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated (not applicable to a registry item)
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - `hyperframes lint`: 0 errors, 2 warnings (the same kinds as `ai-chat-reveal`, which gets 3). Mounted the way `scripts/lint-registry-items.mjs` mounts it, it reports 0 errors.
