title: SDR renders darken footage shadows: extracted PNG frames carry the source's BT.709 transfer tag and Chrome colour-manages them
body:
**Summary** When HyperFrames extracts footage frames to PNG, the pixel data is right: every pixel equals ffmpeg's BT.709 decode. The problem is the colour tag on those files. ffmpeg's PNG encoder copies the source's colour description into cICP `01/01/00/01` (BT.709 primaries and transfer), plus cHRM and gAMA. The render page runs with `--force-color-profile=srgb`, so Chrome colour-manages each frame from the BT.709 transfer to sRGB. It decodes that transfer as a pure 2.4 power (BT.1886) and re-encodes the result as sRGB. The SDR encoder then writes the canvas code values into a BT.709-tagged stream with no inverse conversion (`chunkEncoder.ts` tags the Chrome output bt709 as-is, which is the code-value convention). The transfer is converted on the way in but not on the way out. Footage in every affected SDR render comes out darker than its source, most visibly in the shadows: 0x10 becomes 0x04. **Who is affected** - Every render with `--video-frame-format png`. - Every alpha-capable source (VP8/VP9 WebM, ProRes 4444, and so on). `resolveFrameFormat` always extracts these as PNG, so they are affected at the default setting. - The default `auto` → JPEG path is not affected by this transfer problem, because ffmpeg's JPEG output carries no transfer tag. It has a separate matrix problem, listed at the end. **Versions** - hyperframes 0.8.64 through 0.8.79 (current main, `0ae223773`). The extraction code is identical in 0.8.78 `dist/cli.js`: `extractVideoFramesRange` is at line 93146 and the PNG arguments at line 93212. - Chrome 152 (headless shell 152.0.7977.42 / 152.0.7977.83), macOS arm64. - ffmpeg 9.0.2 (Homebrew). ffmpeg 8.1.1 writes the same chunks. **Measurements** The test clip is patch colour 0xC83C28 plus greys, BT.709 limited range with every tag set to bt709. The reference is the source's own decode. | Stage | 0xC83C28 | 0x101010 | 0x404040 | |---|---|---|---| | Source decode (ffmpeg, BT.709) | c53b26 | 0f0f0f | 3e3e3e | | HyperFrames' extracted PNG (pixel data) | c53b26 | 0f0f0f | 3e3e3e | | Frame captured by Chrome (`--format png-sequence`) | **c2301a** | **040404** | **333333** | | Delivered `mp4` | **be3017** | **000202** | **2e3030** | For the A/B test, the same extracted PNG pixels were shown as `` in one composition and rendered with `--format png-sequence`. Only the PNG colour chunks differ between rows. | PNG colour chunks | Chrome shows (C83C28 / 101010 / 404040) | |---|---| | as extracted: cICP 01/01/00/01 + cHRM + gAMA | c2301a / 040404 / 333333 | | cICP only | c2301a / 040404 / 333333 | | cHRM + gAMA 1/2.2 only | c63821 / 060606 / 3c3c3c | | all colour chunks removed | c53b26 / 0f0f0f / 3e3e3e (exact) | | re-extracted with `setparams=color_trc=unknown:color_primaries=unknown` (no chunks) | c53b26 / 0f0f0f / 3e3e3e (exact) | | re-extracted with `setparams=color_trc=iec61966-2-1` (sRGB chunk) | c53b26 / 0f0f0f / 3e3e3e (exact) | **Model.** For each channel, Chrome maps `v → round(255 · sRGB_encode((v/255)^2.4))`. This predicts every measured value (5 greys and 4 colours) to within 1 code. For example: 0x0f → 0x04, 0x3e → 0x33, 0x7e → 0x77, 0xbe → 0xba. **Minimal repro** ```sh # 1. A 1 s BT.709 clip with three patches. ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "color=c=0xC83C28:s=1080x1920:r=30,format=rgb24,drawbox=x=0:y=0:w=360:h=200:c=0x101010:t=fill,drawbox=x=0:y=200:w=360:h=200:c=0x404040:t=fill" \ -t 1 -vf "scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv,format=yuv420p,setparams=color_primaries=bt709:color_trc=bt709:colorspace=bt709:range=tv" \ -c:v libx264 -crf 12 patch.mp4 # 2. index.html beside it: cat > index.html <<'HTML'
HTML # 3. Render lossless frames and compare one with the source. npx hyperframes@0.8.79 render . --output out --format png-sequence --sdr --workers 1 --video-frame-format png --frames-cache-dir off ffmpeg -v error -i patch.mp4 -vf "select=eq(n\,15),format=rgb24" -frames:v 1 -f rawvideo src.rgb # pixel (700,1000) = c53b26 ffmpeg -v error -i out/frame_000016.png -vf format=rgb24 -f rawvideo out.rgb # pixel (700,1000) = c2301a ``` - Expected: `c53b26` at (700,1000), `0f0f0f` at (180,100) and `3e3e3e` at (180,300), the same values as the source. - Actual: `c2301a`, `040404` and `333333`. This composition has no timeline, so the render waits for player readiness and takes about 50 s. The result is the same with a timeline. **Where it happens (main)** - `packages/engine/src/services/videoFrameExtractor.ts`, `extractVideoFramesRange`: builds `-ss … -i … -vf fps=… -q:v 0 -compression_level 1 frame_%05d.png`. The decoded frames' colour description flows into the PNG encoder, which writes cICP, cHRM and gAMA. - `packages/engine/src/services/videoFrameInjector.ts`: hands the PNG bytes to the page verbatim (`image/png`). - `packages/engine/src/services/browserManager.ts`: `--force-color-profile=srgb`. - `packages/engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts` and `streamingEncoder.ts`: the SDR encode tags the Chrome output `bt709/bt709/bt709` with no transfer conversion. **Related issues found in the same audit (probably separate)** 1. **JPEG extraction** (the default `auto` for opaque SDR sources) loses the BT.709 matrix. ffmpeg converts BT.709 `yuv420p` to `yuvj420p` without a matrix change, and the file is decoded as BT.601: 0xC83C28 comes out as b52d23. 2. **mp4 capture and encode.** Each frame is captured as a BT.601 JPEG and encoded with `scale=in_range=pc:out_range=tv` into BT.709. swscale goes BT.601 YUV → BT.709 YUV through a low-precision intermediate RGB step ("YUV color matrix differs for YUV->YUV, using intermediate RGB"). Page colours shift by up to 4 codes, and greys pick up a tint (#101010 → 0b0d0d). 3. **Forced-SDR HDR sources on macOS.** The VideoToolbox path (`-hwaccel videotoolbox` + `format=nv12`) writes PNG frames tagged cICP `09/10/00/01` (BT.2020 PQ), which Chrome then interprets as PQ. The Linux zscale tone-map path sets `t=bt709` and very likely hits this issue's darkening too. I could not check that locally, because this ffmpeg build has no zscale.

title: fix(engine): declare SDR extracted frames as sRGB so Chrome does not darken footage
body:
## What

For SDR sources, `extractVideoFramesRange` now appends `setparams=color_trc=iec61966-2-1` to the extraction filter chain. SDR PNG frames therefore declare the sRGB transfer (an `sRGB` chunk for BT.709 sources) instead of the source's BT.709 transfer (cICP `01/01/00/01`). The extraction cache schema moves to `hfcache-v5-`, so frames cached with the old tag are not served again.

## Why

The render page runs Chrome with `--force-color-profile=srgb`, and the SDR encoder writes the canvas code values straight into a BT.709-tagged stream. A frame must therefore reach the canvas unconverted.

A PNG tagged with the BT.709 transfer is colour-managed by Chrome: it is decoded as BT.1886 (2.4 power) and re-encoded as sRGB. Nothing converts it back, so every SDR render that extracts PNG frames darkens footage shadows. Two cases hit this: `--video-frame-format png`, and every alpha-capable source (always PNG). A BT.709 0x10 grey renders as 0x04, 0x40 as 0x33, and 0xC83C28 as 0xC2301A. Measurements and a repro are in #4549.

## Related work

Fixes #4549

## How

- **Why an sRGB tag and not an untagged frame.** Both make Chrome show the source exactly for BT.709 sources: both were measured and give identical results. I chose the tag because it states the convention outright (canvas code values are the frame's code values) instead of relying on how Chrome treats untagged images. It also changes only the transfer. The source's primaries stay in the file (cHRM, or cICP `pp/0d` for non-BT.709 primaries), so Chrome still maps a BT.601/SMPTE-C or BT.2020-SDR source's gamut to the sRGB/BT.709 space the encoder tags. Writing untagged frames would silently drop that conversion.
- **Only SDR sources.** The filter is gated on `!isHdr && !options.sdrToHdrTransfer`. The HDR paths are untouched: native HDR sources, SDR→HDR remap in HDR renders, and forced-SDR tone-mapping.
- **Placement.** `setparams` changes frame metadata only. It sits after `fps=` and leaves `colorspace` alone, so the YUV→RGB conversion still uses the source matrix. Pixel data is byte-identical to before (asserted by the new test).
- **JPEG frames.** ffmpeg writes no transfer tag into JPEG, so the same filter leaves JPEG output byte-identical. It applies to both formats, so the rule reads as one statement: every SDR frame handed to the canvas declares sRGB.
- **Untagged sources.** When the source has no colour description at all, the frame gains cICP `02/0d/00/01` + gAMA. Chrome still renders it exactly (checked end to end below).
- **Cache.** The frames' bytes change under an unchanged key tuple, so `SCHEMA_PREFIX` bumps from v4 to v5, per the versioning note in `extractionCache.ts`.
- **No new comment in `videoFrameExtractor.ts`.** Any comment there raises the file's comment share, which fails `comment-ratchet`. The constant name `SDR_CANVAS_PASSTHROUGH_FILTER` carries the intent, and the test comment carries the reason.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. The new test is `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts`, "declares png frames of a BT.709 source as sRGB so Chrome shows their code values". It synthesizes a fully BT.709-tagged clip, extracts PNG frames, and asserts three things: the frame's transfer is `iec61966-2-1`, its primaries stay `bt709`, and its pixels equal the source decode. Before the fix it fails with `expected 'bt709' to be 'iec61966-2-1'`; after the fix it passes. The existing `SCHEMA_PREFIX` test was updated to v5.
- [x] Manual testing performed. I built the CLI from this branch and ran the issue's repro (ffmpeg 9.0.2, Chrome headless shell 152):

  | Source | Output | 0xC83C28 patch | 0x101010 | 0x404040 |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | BT.709 | source decode | c53b26 | 0f0f0f | 3e3e3e |
  | BT.709 | png-sequence, 0.8.79 | c2301a | 040404 | 333333 |
  | BT.709 | png-sequence, this branch (frames 1, 16, 30) | **c53b26** | **0f0f0f** | **3e3e3e** |
  | BT.709 | mp4, 0.8.79 | be3017 | 000202 | 2e3030 |
  | BT.709 | mp4, this branch | c13821 | 0a0c0c | 3a3c3c |
  | untagged | source decode / png-sequence, this branch | ba2e28 / ba2e28 | 0f0f0f / 0f0f0f | 3e3e3e / 3e3e3e |
  | BT.601 (smpte170m) | source decode / png-sequence, this branch | c63c26 / c14225 | 0f0f0f / 0f0f0f | 3e3e3e / 3e3e3e |

  - The png-sequence output now equals the source exactly.
  - The remaining mp4 difference is the capture path's JPEG and BT.601→BT.709 conversion (issue, related item 2). It is not this defect.
  - The BT.601 row keeps Chrome's SMPTE-C→sRGB gamut mapping on saturated colours, as intended. Its greys are exact.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable). Not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments". `check-comment-citations` and `comment-ratchet` both pass.

title: fix(producer): a misspelled font-family resolves to the family the document declares
body:
## What

1. **producer:** a `font-family` that no path resolves, but whose spelling uniquely matches a family the document itself declares, now resolves to that declared family. `"Saira ExtraCondensed"` in CSS plus `@import …family=Saira+Extra+Condensed` becomes Saira Extra Condensed. Before this change it was an unresolved font, and fail-closed compiles threw.
2. **cli:** a failed font-localization run (`fontLocalize.ts`) now names the unresolved families after the existing prefix. The names come from a new structured `FontFetchError.unresolvedFamilies` field and are sanitized. The error message, URLs and HTML are still never printed.

## Why

Receipt `6e9a4401`: the user's brief said "Saira ExtraCondensed". The compose agent copied that spelling into `font-family`, while the document's own `@import` correctly used `family=Saira+Extra+Condensed`.

- Google Fonts returns **HTTP 400** for `family=Saira+ExtraCondensed` and 200 for `Saira+Extra+Condensed`.
- `fetchGoogleFont` treats a 4xx as "not served" and returns `[]`. The family then lands in `unresolved`, and `injectDeterministicFontFaces` throws `FontFetchError: Unresolved fonts in fail-closed mode: Saira ExtraCondensed`.
- The CLI (`failClosedFontFetch: true`) exits 1 and prints only `font localization failed (FontFetchError)`. The caller can't tell which font caused it.

Local repro against the real composition, before this change:

```
failClosed=true THREW FontFetchError FONT_FETCH_FAILED [Compiler] Unresolved fonts in fail-closed mode: Saira ExtraCondensed. ...
```

After (same document, fail-closed):

```
[INFO] [Compiler] Fetched 9 font face(s) for "Saira Extra Condensed" from Google Fonts
[WARN] [Compiler] font-family "Saira ExtraCondensed" is not a known family; resolved it to "Saira Extra Condensed", which this document declares. Correct the authored font-family to "Saira Extra Condensed".
[INFO] [Compiler] Injected deterministic @font-face rules for 3 requested font families
injected faces per family: { Inter: 5, "Saira ExtraCondensed": 9, "JetBrains Mono": 4 }
```

This error class hit **46 runs in the last 7 days**. Not all of them come from this trigger, and the CLI change is what will let us attribute the rest.

## Related work

Refs #4450 (`fix/font-localization-fallback`). This PR is independent of #4450 and complements it:

- #4450 switches preview bundling to fail-open, so an unresolved font substitutes a fallback instead of failing the activity.
- This PR makes this class of family resolve to the correct font, in both modes, and makes whatever is still unresolved visible.

The two PRs touch disjoint files. This one doesn't modify `fontLocalizeCli.ts` or `failClosedFontFetch`, so they merge cleanly in either order.

## How

**Alias resolution (`deterministicFonts.ts`)**
- The per-family body of `buildFontFaceCss` is split into `resolveFamilyFaceRules(normalized, lookupFamily, emitFamily)` and one helper per existing path: bundled, Google and system capture. For ordinary families `lookupFamily === emitFamily`, so behavior is unchanged.
- The alias pass runs **only after every existing path has failed**, right before a family would be pushed to `unresolved`. A document that resolves today gets exactly the faces it got before, so determinism is unaffected. The declared-family scan is lazy and only runs if something is unresolved.
- Declared families are collected from two places:
  - Google Fonts stylesheet URLs in `@import` (inside `<style>`) and in `<link href>`. Both `css2` (repeated `family=Name:axes`) and legacy `css` (`family=A:400|B`) forms are handled. Only the `fonts.googleapis.com` host with the `/css` or `/css2` path counts.
  - Top-level `@font-face` rules. Faces and imports nested in at-rules are ignored because re-emitting them unconditionally can change rendering. Stylesheet sources must be unconditional: media is empty or `all`, type is empty or `text/css`, and titled/disabled/alternate sources are excluded. Links must have `rel="stylesheet"`; imports with media, supports, or layer suffixes are excluded except bare `all`.
- Matching key: the name lower-cased, with whitespace, `-`, `_` and `+` removed. `+` is included because `fetchGoogleFont` already treats it as a URL-encoded space.
  - A **unique** match resolves.
  - Zero matches leave behavior unchanged.
  - Two declared families that collapse to the same key count as ambiguous and stay unresolved.
  - If the authored name is itself declared verbatim, it is never substituted.
- The resolved canonical family goes back through the normal paths, so it composes with `FONT_ALIASES`. For example, `"OpenSans"` with an `Open+Sans` import gets the bundled Open Sans faces plus the canonical Google supplement.
- When the match is a `@font-face` declared in the document, that rule is cloned instead of fetching, so the document's own face wins, as it would have if the name were spelled correctly.
- It logs through `defaultLogger.warn` with both names when it fires.

**Design choice: faces are emitted under the authored name; the authored CSS is not rewritten.**
- This is the convention the file already follows:
  - `FONT_ALIASES` emits Inter faces under `"Helvetica"`.
  - The `+`-spelling path fetches `DM Mono` but emits under `"DM+Mono"`.
- Rewriting would also have to reach every surface a family can be named on: `<style>`, inline `style`, `data-font-family`, `var()` custom properties, and script-assigned `el.style.fontFamily` / GSAP. The last of these can't be rewritten statically.
- Emitting under the authored name covers all of them, and the output never names a family that has no `@font-face`. The tests assert that the injected faces carry the authored name and the declared family's bytes.

**CLI output (`fontLocalize.ts`)**
- `FontFetchError` gains `readonly unresolvedFamilies: readonly string[]`. The existing constructor gets an optional 6th parameter with default `[]`, so existing callers are unaffected. It is populated by the fail-closed unresolved throw.
- `runFontLocalize` reads **only** that structured field (duck-typed, so the file still has no producer import). It never reads `error.message`.
- Sanitization:
  - Non-strings are dropped.
  - A name containing any of `: / ? # & = % @ \` is dropped whole. It is URL- or query-shaped, and stripping its punctuation would still print the token it carries.
  - Any other character outside `[A-Za-z0-9 _-]` becomes a space.
  - Each name is capped at 64 characters, and at most 8 names are listed. The rest are counted as `(+N more)`.
- New stderr format. The prefix is byte-identical, and the bare line is unchanged when there's no family list:
  ```
  font localization failed (FontFetchError): unresolved font families: "Foo Bar", "Baz"
  font localization failed (FontFetchError): unresolved font families: "A", …, "H" (+3 more)
  font localization failed (FontFetchError)
  ```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `packages/producer/src/services/deterministicFonts-declaredAlias.test.ts` (new, fake `fetchImpl` and a temp `HYPERFRAMES_FONT_CACHE_DIR`, following `deterministicFonts-aliasSupplement.test.ts`):
    - The exact typo, `"Saira ExtraCondensed"` with a css2 `@import` of `Saira+Extra+Condensed`, resolves in fail-closed mode. The faces are named `"Saira ExtraCondensed"`, carry Saira Extra Condensed's bytes, and the authored rule is untouched.
    - Legacy `css` `<link>` with `family=A:400,800|B`, and authored `saira-extra_condensed`.
    - The document's own `@font-face "Brand Sans"` is re-emitted under `"BrandSans"`, with no fetch for the canonical name.
    - It composes with `FONT_ALIASES`: `"OpenSans"` → bundled Open Sans faces.
    - Declared `Saira` and `Saira Extra Condensed`: authored `"Saira ExtraCondensed"` → Saira Extra Condensed, and `"Saira"` → Saira.
    - An already-resolving document makes exactly one request and gets the same faces.
    - The typo also resolves in fail-open mode.
    - Still fails closed, with `unresolvedFamilies` set and only the authored name requested, for:
      - a truly unknown family
      - an ambiguous collision (`Saira Extra Condensed` + `Saira ExtraCondensed` declared)
      - a verbatim-declared family
      - a non-Google stylesheet URL
    - Mutation-checked: disabling the alias lookup fails the 6 positive tests, and disabling the ambiguity guard fails the collision test.
  - `packages/cli/src/fontLocalize.test.ts`:
    - Families are listed after the unchanged prefix.
    - **A URL / `X-Amz-Signature` in `error.message` never reaches stderr.**
    - URL-shaped names are dropped whole, and other characters are stripped.
    - Per-name length cap and count cap.
    - The bare line is kept when there's no family list.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the real composition from the receipt compiles fail-closed, and an unknown family prints `unresolved font families: "Totally Unknown Face"`.
- [x] `bun test src/services/deterministicFonts` (105 pass), producer unit lane (bun + vitest; the only local failures, `htmlCompiler.parity.test.ts` "No such built-in module: node:" and a `fontCompression` 5s timeout, reproduce on unchanged code), cli `fontLocalize.test.ts`, `tsc --noEmit` for producer and cli after a full `bun run build`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `fallow audit --base origin/main` (pass), and the comment citation and ratchet checks.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): n/a
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Note: bot-authored PR — needs a human reviewer per org rules.

— tai2

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


## Review follow-up validation

Conditional declarations no longer become global alias faces. Added 19 regression/control cases for style media, nested rules, conditional imports, conditional/alternate/disabled/non-stylesheet links, non-CSS types, titled stylesheets, and unconditional `all` controls. Fifteen new cases failed on the original head and all pass with the guards. Tested both fail-closed rejection and fail-open absence of injected faces.

Bun 1.4.2: 136 focused deterministic-font and CLI tests pass; changed-file oxlint and oxfmt pass. Full producer typecheck is unverified locally because this isolated checkout reuses workspace dependencies with missing generated runtime files and missing/mismatched workspace exports; hosted CI must validate the complete workspace.


## Quality-gate follow-up

The conditional-source audit split declaration scanning into focused style and link helpers. The new collector's CRAP finding is gone; `fetchGoogleFont` is unchanged from before this PR and has a function-local Fallow suppression because the insertion shifted its line fingerprint. The reported font-data duplication and `parseFontFamilyValue` complexity were classified by Fallow as inherited. Local Fallow reports zero newly introduced complexity/duplication findings; its only failure is an `@hyperframes/lint` dependency warning from the temporary checkout's reused workspace dependencies, which was absent in hosted CI. Focused Bun 1.4.2 tests still pass 136/136, and changed-file oxlint/oxfmt pass. Hosted CI on the updated head remains the release gate.

title: fix(cli): snapshot shows a short video's last frame instead of going black
body:
## What this fixes

`hyperframes snapshot` showed a black (or stale) video when the snapshot landed inside a video's slot but at or past the end of its source, for example a 5-second clip placed in a 10-second slot, captured at 7 seconds. The preview holds the clip's last frame there. Snapshot asked FFmpeg for a frame at 7 seconds of a 5-second file, FFmpeg returned nothing (it exits cleanly with no frame at or past a file's end), and the snapshot warned that the video "will appear black/stale".

Now a time at or past the end of the source samples the source's last frame, the same way snapshot already handled a clip held at the end of the composition. Snapshot first asks for a frame just inside the end (one frame at 30 fps), which is enough for most clips; when FFmpeg still returns nothing near the end, as it does for 24 and 25 fps clips or a file whose audio runs longer than its video, it reads the file's final second and keeps the last frame. The same fallback also covers a time inside the last frame but past its timestamp, which went black before. Times inside the source are unchanged, and a looped clip is unaffected because it wraps before this point.

## Tests

- `snapshot.test.ts`: a 5-second source in a 10-second slot, captured at 5 (exactly the source's end), at 7, and at 3 with a 5-second media offset, each samples the source's last frame. These fail on `main`, which returns 5, 7 and 8.
- `snapshot.test.ts`, with FFmpeg: on a 1-second 24 fps clip, a held tail just inside the end gives exactly the clip's last frame, where the plain extract gives nothing.
- FFmpeg with snapshot's own arguments, on a 1-second 30 fps clip: a frame at 0.5 and 0.9666 seconds, none at 1 or 2.

Results: `snapshot.test.ts` 46; `tsc`, oxfmt, oxlint and Fallow clean. Dropping the new condition fails the 7 and 3 cases; stopping only strictly past the end fails the exact-end case; removing the last-frame fallback fails the 24 fps case.

Known limits:

- At 60 fps the first request succeeds one frame early, so the snapshot shows the second-to-last frame where the preview shows the last.
- A file whose audio runs more than a second past its video still shows black past the video's end: the fallback reads the file's last second, which then holds no video. It was black before too.
- A 24 or 25 fps held tail now runs FFmpeg twice for that frame.

title: fix(studio): avoid preview reloads for temporary and excluded files
body:
Writing agent notes or check reports inside an open project currently tears down and reloads the entire preview. On an image-heavy composition this repeatedly recompiles the page, decodes images, interrupts audio, and looks like slow playback even when settled playback holds 60 fps. Atomic saves also deliver a temporary filename before the actual source save.

This filters temporary save artifacts before SSE hashing/delivery and adds opt-in `preview.watchIgnore` literal project-relative file/directory paths in `hyperframes.json`. For example, `{"preview":{"watchIgnore":["docs","references/check-results.json"]}}` keeps report writes from resetting playback or regenerating thumbnails. Source and assets remain watched by default; ignored files remain served/rendered and still invalidate conservative cache signatures. Config changes are read live and the config itself cannot be ignored. The same policy applies in Vite, resolving configuration from the real watched project root (including symlinked projects).

### Reproduction and measurements

With a photo-heavy local composition open in Studio, write `docs/report.json` every two seconds during playback. Compare the iframe URL/player identity, RAF intervals, and composition time over 12 seconds. Then configure `preview.watchIgnore: ["docs"]` and repeat.

| 12-second report-writing workload | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Preview replacements | 3 | 0 |
| RAF frames | 504 | 716 |
| Frame gaps >50 ms | 15 | 0 |
| Worst RAF gap | 650.1 ms | 44.2 ms |

Measured with the web component playback API in the same local Chromium setup on a stable snapshot with 199 image elements. A separate test through Studio's Play control and authoritative iframe runtime clock confirmed zero reloads and 12.00 seconds of clock advancement over 12 seconds with exclusions enabled. The runtime clock also keeps up during reloads; the improvement is in visual continuity and reduced frame stalls, not timeline clock speed. The full 175.894-second composition also completed after the fix: 10,494 RAF callbacks (about 59.7 fps), three isolated gaps over 50 ms, worst 191.7 ms. These are local workload measurements, not universal performance guarantees. Private project media and traces are not included.

### Validation

- CLI watcher/SSE/config/schema tests: 78 passed, one Linux-only test skipped on macOS; real filesystem atomic-save coverage included.
- Server filter/signature/composition-input tests: 17 passed, including a 100,000-separator malformed-setting regression.
- Vite project ownership/exclusion tests: 2 passed.
- CLI, Studio, and studio-server typechecks passed.
- Relevant packages built; lint, formatting, tracked-artifact checks and changed-file fallow audit passed. The audit excludes an inherited duplication finding in unchanged portions of a touched test.
- Full baseline monorepo build reaches the unrelated sdk-playground and fails there with Node `ERR_UNKNOWN_FILE_EXTENSION` for `packages/sdk/src/adapters/fs.ts`. The Vite test runner reports a shutdown timeout after passing assertions.

No player clock, composition animation, image quality, or rendering behavior changes. Removing an exclusion restores automatic reload for that path.

### Before

Public GSAP performance fixture, report files written during playback, no exclusions:

[Before recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f25defd547b928f9d231fa723bc7f960c15b2b87/docs/images/preview-reload-evidence/before.webm)

### After

The same public fixture and report writes with `preview.watchIgnore: ["docs"]`. These clips illustrate the workflow without private media; the numerical photo-heavy measurements above use the separate local snapshot.

[After recording](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f25defd547b928f9d231fa723bc7f960c15b2b87/docs/images/preview-reload-evidence/after.webm)


### Dynamic-project review follow-up

Commit c5fe2ae3616ccfb0fd9e3b3dd84ac1e3df7fd27d addresses the lost-reload path for projects opened after Vite startup. The adapter registers each resolved canonical project ID and real directory before signature-cache watching, including symlink roots and session aliases. Regression coverage now includes projects created after adapter initialization; 27 focused adapter/signature/ownership tests pass. An actual Vite browser/WebSocket check imported a symlinked project after startup, received its source-change event with the correct project ID, and verified excluded report writes stayed silent. Normal lint, formatting, typecheck and audit commit checks pass.

title: fix(core): a CSS animation in a later clip shows the right frame after a seek
body:
## What this fixes

A CSS animation in a clip that starts later shows the wrong frame after a seek, in Studio's preview and in rendered video. The runtime hides a clip with `display: none` until it starts. When the clip is shown, the browser gives its element a new `CSSAnimation`. The CSS adapter kept seeking the handle it saved when it first scanned the page, so the animation the viewer sees stayed at its first frame, and rendered frames of that clip lagged one step behind.

Now the CSS adapter seeks, plays and pauses the element's live CSS animations, read when it needs them. It also keeps the handles it has seen that the browser has not cancelled, so seeking back into a finished animation with no fill (which leaves the page's live list) still shows its frame; a handle the browser cancelled when its clip was hidden is never written to again. It acts only on `CSSAnimation`s: CSS transitions and script-created animations stay with their own clocks. When an element has no live animation yet (its clip is still hidden), the adapter keeps posing it with an inline paused `animation-delay`, and pausing no longer strips that pose, so the first frame after a jump into the clip is right.

The adapter times an animation from its clip: an element without its own `data-start` (a box inside a clip) counts from its nearest ancestor that has one, resolved through the runtime's start resolver so nested compositions keep their offsets. Showing a clip restarts its children's CSS animations in the browser, and scene timelines are already nested at their host's start, so this is the timing a viewer expects. When an element has no live animation yet, the inline delay the adapter writes is, per animation, the author's delay minus the time into the clip, so an authored delay is kept.

The CSS and WAAPI adapters share one `document.getAnimations()` scan per seek and per render seek, including the pause that follows it, as main scans once per seek today. Starting playback scans once more.

## Before

Main, a clip at 6 s with `animation: slide 4s linear both`, seeked to 7 s: the box sits on the 0 px guide.

![Before: the late clip shows its first frame at 7 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d9a2725-4a6a-45c9-8229-e4df02123855)

## After

This branch, same page and seek: the box sits on the 25 px guide.

![After: the late clip shows the right frame at 7 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/62ad4508-875e-4537-8d1f-ac4cb3d0574c)

## What I measured

- Real headless Chrome, the runtime built from main and from this branch:

  | Case | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Seek to 7 s into a clip at 6 s (expect 25 px) | 0 | 25 |
  | Render frames at 6.5 / 7 / 7.5 / 9 s (expect 12.5 / 25 / 37.5 / 75 px) | 0 / 12.5 / 25 / 62.5 | 12.5 / 25 / 37.5 / 75 |
  | A render that starts at 7 s, first frame (expect 25 px) | 0 | 25 |
  | Play from 6 s for 1 s (expect about 25 px) | 0.1 | 25.3 |
  | A clip with a 1 s CSS delay, seek 8 / 9 / 6.5 (expect 25 / 50 / 0) | 0 / 0 / 0 | 25 / 50 / 0 |
  | A 2 s colour transition from 3 s, frames at 3.07 / 3.5 / 4 s | unchanged | same as main |
  | A WAAPI animation created after the first scan, at 3 s | 75 px | 75 px |
  | A hidden clip at 6 s holding a box with `animation: slide 4s linear 1s both`, first visible frame at 6.5 / 8 s, seek and render seek | 0 / 0 | 0 / 25 |
  | The same box in a clip at 1 s inside a scene at 6 s, at 7.5 / 9 s | 0 / 0 | 0 / 25 |
  | A 1 s no-fill animation, seek 0.5 / 5 / 0.5 / 0.25 / 3 / 0.75 s | 50, none, 50, 23.3, none, 73.3 | same |
  | The same in a clip at 6 s, seek 6.5 / 8 / 6.5 / 7.5 / 6.25 s | 0, none, 0, none, 0 | 50, none, 50, none, 23.3 |

  Every other fixture reads the same on both builds.
- Per-seek cost, median milliseconds per call, three rounds of 300, same minified build of each; `document.getAnimations()` calls per seek in the last column (main / this branch):

  | Film | seek, main | seek, this branch | renderSeek, main | renderSeek, this branch | scans |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 20 CSS-animated clips | 0.240 | 0.250 | 0.235 | 0.255 | 1 / 1 |
  | 200 CSS-animated clips, 125 hidden | 2.780 | 2.475 | 2.800 | 2.815 | 1 / 1 |
  | 200 GSAP-tweened elements, 20 CSS clips | 1.910 | 2.005 | 2.150 | 2.175 | 1 / 1 |
  | 200 GSAP-tweened elements, no CSS | 1.565 | 1.555 | 1.465 | 1.545 | 0 / 0 |

  The machine was shared with other work, so the p95 figures were too noisy to report; the medians and the scan counts are the stable parts.
- New `css.test.ts` tests: a replaced animation handle is the one seeked; play and pause act on the live handles; pseudo-element animations, CSS transitions and WAAPI animations are left alone; the fallback delay is cleared once a live animation exists and kept through a pause while there is none; a second scan does not read the fallback delay back as the authored one; a finished no-fill animation that left the page's list is still seeked; a cancelled animation is never written to and is forgotten; known animations survive a rediscover for elements still on the page and are forgotten on revert; one seek, and a seek plus its pause, scan the page once, and two seeks scan twice. `init.swapScenes.test.ts` now serves its CSS animation only through `document.getAnimations()`, so it fails if the adapter stops seeking live handles.
- Mutations each fail a test: dropping the `CSSAnimation` filter, dropping the guard for browsers without `CSSAnimation`, stripping the fallback pose on pause, dropping the no-entries early return, dropping the idle check, keeping idle handles until the write, keeping handles across a revert, sharing one page list across calls, and either adapter ignoring the shared list.
- Each run alone: `adapters/css.test.ts` (41), `adapters/waapi.test.ts` (22), `adapters/lottie.test.ts` (36), `init.test.ts` (181), `init.swapScenes.test.ts` (45), `transportPark.test.ts` (28), `timeline.test.ts` (70). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- In a film with no `data-duration`, the film's length comes from the animations. A child animation that outlasts its clip now counts from the clip's start, so it can lengthen such a film past the clip's end, as the same animation placed on the clip element already does on main.
- The producer's rendered-video baselines; the render path was checked frame by frame through `renderSeek` in headless Chrome.
- No automated real-browser test: the two browser behaviours this relies on (a re-shown element gets a new `CSSAnimation`; a paused, past-end, no-fill animation leaves `document.getAnimations()`) are pinned only by the unit tests' stand-ins and the headless Chrome runs above, on Chrome 113 and 152.
- A cached animation list across frames. It would have to watch inline style changes, and GSAP writes inline styles on every animated element each frame, so in GSAP films it cost more than the scans it saved.
- CSS animations inside shadow roots or on pseudo-elements stay with the WAAPI adapter, whose starting point can vary by about a frame between runs; unchanged here.

title: Shadow-root and pseudo-element CSS animations land about a frame off, differently each load
body:
## What happens A CSS animation inside a shadow root, or on a `::before`/`::after` pseudo-element, lands at a slightly different frame each time the page loads. Seeking to the same time gives a position that varies by about one frame between runs (0.4 to 1.25 px on a 4 s, 100 px slide), in Studio's preview and in renders. The CSS adapter only drives an element's own animations, so these are left to the WAAPI adapter. The WAAPI adapter records a baseline for each animation the first time it sees it, including the animation's own `currentTime` at that moment (`ensureBaseline` in `packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/waapi.ts`). For a CSS animation that has been running since the page loaded, that value is however much wall-clock time passed before discover, so every later seek is offset by it. ## Repro Headless Chrome, the runtime built from main, `window.__player.seek(2)`, then read the computed transform. Load the page several times. ```html
el
``` Read after `seek(2)`: - `getComputedStyle(document.getElementById("el"), "::before").transform` - `getComputedStyle(document.getElementById("host").shadowRoot.getElementById("in")).transform` **Expected:** `translateX(50px)` on every load. **Observed:** about 50.4 to 51.25 px, different from run to run. ## Notes - Animations on an element in the light DOM are driven by the CSS adapter from the clip's `data-start` and are exact. - Found while testing #4554. It is not caused by it; main behaves the same.

title: fix(cli): stop background update and skills checks from holding a finished command open
body:
## What changes for users

A finished command no longer sits waiting on the network. On a machine whose DNS never answers (offline sandboxes, locked-down CI, a network namespace with no resolver), `hyperframes init --example blank --non-interactive` used to stay alive for 10 to 120 seconds after it was done. Now it exits in about 2 to 3 seconds.

`HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, `CI` and `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` now skip the background fetches, not just the notices they would have printed. An app or harness that drives the CLI unattended can set `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` and `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` to start no background fetch at all.

Agents and scripts without a terminal still refresh the update cache, so `--json` output keeps `_meta.updateAvailable` current as the docs promise.

## Root cause

Every command starts background requests: the npm update check, the skills check (`git ls-remote`, then the manifest), and the telemetry flush that `finalizeCli` awaits. `fetch` resolves the host with the system resolver (`getaddrinfo` on the libuv threadpool). That lookup:

- cannot be aborted: the `AbortController` timeout ends the request, but not the lookup;
- keeps the event loop alive;
- holds even `process.exit()` until the resolver gives up.

`git ls-remote` is a child process with a 4 s timeout that keeps the parent alive the same way.

A minimal repro on Node 22 with a DNS server that never replies:

| Pending lookup | `process.exit()` called | Process gone |
|---|---|---|
| `dns.lookup` / `fetch` | 0.2 s | ~10 s |
| `dns.promises.Resolver().resolve4` (c-ares) | 0.2 s | 0.25 s |

The opt-outs did not help because they were read only when printing the notice, after the requests had already started.

## Fix

**`utils/hostAnswers.ts`** is a short c-ares probe: 1 s per nameserver, one try, A or AAAA. It never holds exit and never rejects. Each background request asks it first and skips the request when DNS is silent:

| Background request | Where the probe sits | When DNS is silent |
|---|---|---|
| Update check | `checkForUpdate()`, unforced only (the background call) | Falls back to the cached result. `upgrade` (forced) still waits for the registry. |
| Skills check | `checkSkillsForUpdate()`, before `git ls-remote` starts | Returns the cached meta. `skills check`/`update` are unchanged. |
| Telemetry flush | `flush()` | Leaves events queued for the existing detached `flushSync()` child. `events` now hands its leftovers to that child too. |

**Gates.** Each sits next to its probe, in the function that owns the background check. `cli.ts` is unchanged.
- **Update check:** the unforced `checkForUpdate()` returns the cached result under CI, dev or `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`.
  - It still runs without a terminal, so agents keep `_meta` fresh.
  - The background install reads the same rule (`updateCheckDisabled()`, or `HYPERFRAMES_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1`), so a cached result never starts an install in those runs.
  - `updateNoticesSuppressed()` is now that same rule, or stderr not being a terminal.
- **Skills check:** `checkSkillsForUpdate()` also skips in every run that shows no notices, and under `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1`. Its only consumer is the notice those runs never print.

**Telemetry flushes run one at a time.** `render` sends `render_complete` early, then `finalizeCli` flushes again.
- Two overlapping flushes could each send the same queued event. The probe widened that window, and the CLI smoke caught it (`got: 2`).
- Now a flush started while one is in flight sends after it, so the awaited final flush also covers the early one before exit.
- A flush queued behind a failed send leaves the batch to `flushSync()`, so a dead network costs one attempt, as before. A slow first send that does succeed is followed by the final one in series; on a healthy network that is one extra round trip.

The skills probe asks about `github.com` (where `git ls-remote` goes). The manifest then comes from `raw.githubusercontent.com`, which in practice shares its resolver's fate.

## Evidence

`init --example blank --non-interactive`, with a DNS server that accepts queries and never replies, in a network namespace on Linux:

| Run | Before (0.8.78) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` | 22 s | 2.0 s |
| `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1`, no terminal, empty cache (update check runs) | 10-14 s | 2.3 s |
| `CI=1 HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` | 10-14 s | 2.1 s |
| Terminal `lint`, empty update and skills caches (both checks run) | n/a | 2.2-3.4 s |
| Normal network, `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` | 0.84 s | 0.84 s |

After the fix, node's `exit` event and the process end are within 0.25 s of each other in every run. Before, they were about 5 s apart.

On a normal network:
- A terminal run with empty caches refreshes both, recording `lastUpdateCheck` and `lastSkillsCheck`.
- A run without a terminal records `latestVersion`.
- With both opt-outs, nothing is recorded.

Not changed here: a default `init` with no opt-outs still spends most of its time in its own foreground skills install, which is the command's work rather than a background check.

## Tests

Each new test fails with its guard removed:

- `updateCheck.test.ts`:
  - a run without a terminal still asks the registry;
  - an unforced check makes no request under `CI=1`, `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`, or when DNS does not answer, while a forced one (`upgrade`) still does.
- `skillsUpdateCheck.test.ts`: no skills check under `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1`, in a run that shows no notices, or when DNS does not answer.
- `telemetry/client.test.ts`: events stay queued when DNS does not answer, and go out on the next flush.
- `commands/events.test.ts`: the beacon hands anything left queued to the detached sender.
- `telemetry/client.test.ts` also checks that:
  - two overlapping flushes send an event once;
  - a flush queued behind a failed send does not retry it;
  - a flush queued behind one that threw still sends.
- The CLI telemetry smoke (`scripts/ci/cli-telemetry-e2e.mjs`) failed with `got: 2` before the serialisation and passes after it.

The existing in-flight flush test now waits for the request to start, because the probe comes first.

The update and skills tests no longer depend on the developer's shell: they pass with `CI`, `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK` or `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS` set.

title: fix(studio-server): probe each proxied clip once instead of on every request
body:
## What

A `?hf-proxy=` request for a video ran ffprobe every time, even for a clip that had not changed. The probe sits before the 304 shortcut, so every request for a proxied HEVC clip started a new ffprobe process, range requests and revalidations included.

`probeAssetCodec` is now the cached probe. It remembers the result per path until the file's target, mtime or size changes. The target is the path with symlinks resolved, as in the proxy transcoder's cache key, so repointing an asset symlink at another file is a miss even when mtime and size match. `hyperframes play` and the static project server keep their call and now use the shared process cache; the Studio server preview route passes the server's own probe cache, the one its codec-map scan already uses. The uncached probe is private.

A failed ffprobe (missing binary, timeout, bad output) is not cached, so the next probe retries. A preview document already built keeps the codec map it was built with until the project signature changes; that is unchanged from main. A file that probes fine but is not video, or has no codec name, is cached as `null` like any other answer. The tradeoff: a file ffprobe cannot read is probed again on each scan and request, where main's scan cached that failure.

## Why here

The scan had a cached wrapper; the exported function was the raw probe. The routes called the export, so each of them bypassed the cache. Making the export the cached one fixes all three routes in one place, and a future route cannot pick the uncached one by mistake.

## Impact on callers

`probeAssetCodec(filePath, runner?)` keeps its signature and gains an optional `cache` argument. It still resolves to `null` on any probe failure and never throws. A caller now gets a cached result for a path whose target, mtime and size are unchanged; a cache hit does not call `runner`. Like the transcoder's cache, it does not notice a file rewritten in place with the same mtime and size. The cache holds at most 512 entries, as before. Concurrent first requests for one clip each start a probe; after the first result they share it.

## Tests

`preview.test.ts`, "runs ffprobe once for repeated proxy requests of the same unchanged clip": two `?hf-proxy=h264` requests for the same HEVC clip. With this change ffprobe runs once. With main's `mediaCodecMap.ts` the same test fails: expected 1 call, got 2.

`mediaCodecMap.test.ts`, "probes again after ffprobe failed instead of caching the failure": the first probe fails (ffprobe path missing), the second has a working runner and must return the codec. With the failure cached, the second call returns `null`.

`preview.test.ts`, "probes again when a clip's symlink is repointed at a file with the same mtime and size": a clip symlink moves from an HEVC file to an H.264 file with the same mtime and size. The second proxy request must answer 422 (browser-safe codec). Without the target in the cache key it serves the old HEVC proxy (200).

title: fix(studio): reload the dev preview after edits to a symlinked project
body:
## What

In Studio's dev server, an edit made outside Studio to a symlinked project never reloaded the preview.

`hyperframes preview` links a project into `data/projects/<id>` with a symlink. The dev server's watcher follows the link and reports changed files by their real path. The `hf:file-change` event took its project id from the first path segment under `data/projects`, which for a real path outside that folder is `..`. Studio drops a file change whose project id is not the open project, as it must for a stale tab on a shared connection, so every external edit to that project was dropped as "other project".

`projectIdForWatchedFile` in `vite.adapter.ts` now names the project. A file inside `data/projects` keeps the first-segment rule, which costs nothing. A file outside it is matched against the real path of each project entry. A file no project owns is not announced; the client dropped those anyway. The dev server serves every project under `data/projects`, so unlike the CLI host, which always sends its one project's id, it has to name the owning project per file.

## Scope

- The CLI host is not affected: it serves one project and always sends that project's id.
- Known limit: when two entries resolve to the same real folder, the first entry wins. That takes two links to one folder, or one project linked inside another.
- Not covered, same as main: opening a symlinked project through a URL whose letter case differs from the link's name.

## Test

`vite.adapter.projects.test.ts`, "names a symlinked project from the real path the watcher reports". It checks a symlinked project (file at the root and nested), a plain project whose id starts with `..`, and a file outside every project. With main's first-segment rule in the helper, it fails: expected `'..'` to be `'promo'`.

## Before

Studio dev server with a synthetic test film linked into `data/projects` the way `hyperframes preview` links it. An editor outside Studio changes the title from "Test pattern film" to "Edited outside Studio". On main, Studio logs the change as `suppressed: other project`, no new preview loads, and the old title stays.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/253525a0-024a-4d1f-b27a-135f5c4c157e

## After

The same edit: the change is accepted, the new preview loads (the overlay lists its events), and the title reads "Edited outside Studio".

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d21e2773-9292-4160-a3ff-de3b6e6b47dc

Both clips were recorded on Linux at 7a8e5b0f. The two later commits only resolve project folders with `realpathSync` instead of `realpathSync.native` (the call the watcher uses; on Linux the two give the same path) and shorten a comment.

title: Animations a script creates before the runtime loads land up to a frame off, differently each load
body:
## What happens An animation a composition's script creates with `el.animate()` before the runtime loads lands up to a frame off after a seek, differently on each page load. A 4 s linear 100 px slide seeked to 2 s reads 50 to 51.25 px instead of 50. The WAAPI adapter records a baseline for each animation the first time it sees it, including the animation's own `currentTime` at that moment (`ensureBaseline` in `packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/waapi.ts`). An animation created before the runtime has already been running on the wall clock for however long loading took, so every later seek is offset by that amount. Animations created after the runtime loads go through the adapter's `Element.prototype.animate` hook and are anchored where they are created. ## Repro Headless Chrome, the runtime built from main, `window.__player.seek(2)`, then read the computed transform. Load the page several times. ```html
el
``` **Expected:** `translateX(50px)` on every load. **Observed:** 50 to 51.25 px, varying by load. ## Notes - Same family as #4555 (CSS animations in shadow roots and on pseudo-elements), which anchors CSS animations at their clip's start. Script-created animations need their own decision about where they start, so they are kept separate.

title: perf(studio): serve bounded JPEG timeline thumbnails
body:
## What

Serve bounded JPEG images to Studio timeline strips instead of displaying full-resolution originals. A 2560×1920 source becomes a 180×135 timeline thumbnail; the composition and exported video continue to use the original.

## Why

ImageThumbnail currently displays original photos in tiny tiles and accounts for each cached image as 240×135 regardless of its actual dimensions. This change requests small JPEG responses and accounts for their real decoded dimensions.

Three local runs per variant on the same frozen photo-heavy project, Chrome 147 at 1280×720:

| Median | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Largest frame gap during 10 seconds of Studio playback | 208 ms | 58 ms |
| Frame gaps over 50 ms | 3 | 1 |
| RAF callbacks / 10 seconds | 579 | 593 |
| Loading benchmark readiness threshold | 2342 ms | 2418 ms |
| Summed Chrome process RSS | 2205 MiB | 2239 MiB |

The 52 loaded timeline sources' decoded-pixel estimate falls from 956 MiB to 4.4 MiB. **This is not a measured RAM reduction:** RSS did not improve. Loading is 76 ms slower in these samples, and no startup speedup is claimed. Results support improved frame pacing in this workload, not a whole-film FPS guarantee. The readiness threshold is at least 147 mounted timeline image elements decoded, not time-to-first-frame. Composition photo downloads are unchanged.

## How

- Same-origin preview JPEGs use a fixed 240×135 image-thumbnail endpoint; no arbitrary remote URLs or requested output sizes.
- Existing project/path containment, JPEG magic/format checks, 64 MiB input and 40 MP decode limits, two concurrent jobs, bounded queue, and 8 MiB/128-entry in-memory cache.
- Cache identities include source file metadata; private HTTP responses revalidate. EXIF orientation is respected.
- Other formats and external sources retain their behavior. Older servers or failed conversions fall back to originals with honest size accounting.
- Uses the same Sharp version already present in the CLI workspace.

A client-side resizing prototype was rejected because it added approximately 1.3 seconds to loading. Details and limitations are recorded in `docs/plans/2026-09-26-image-thumbnails.md`.

## Related work

Refs #4553 (unwanted preview reloads). This PR is independent, based on main after #4546; it does not include the watcher changes.

## Test plan

- [x] 32 client/component/scheduler tests and 13 server/coordinator tests
- [x] Source invalidation, concurrent requests, cancellation/fallback, unknown projects, traversal, symlink escape, corrupt/mislabelled/oversized images, pixel limits, EXIF orientation, and no upscaling
- [x] Studio and studio-server TypeScript checks
- [x] Studio and studio-server builds
- [x] Changed-file lint, format, and Fallow audit (duplication warnings only)
- [x] Actual Studio playback clock and frame pacing; all mounted image URLs decode
- [x] Synthetic public media captures below; private project media was not uploaded

## Before

Actual ImageThumbnail component, synthetic 2560×1920 JPEG at timeline tile size.

![Original JPEG timeline strip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/fix/studio-image-thumbnails/docs/images/image-thumbnail-evidence/before.png)

## After

Same component and display size, using the bounded 180×135 JPEG response.

![Bounded JPEG timeline strip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/fix/studio-image-thumbnails/docs/images/image-thumbnail-evidence/after.png)

title: docs: credit the background-removal model as Apache-2.0, matching upstream U-2-Net
body:
## What changes

The background-removal model `u2net_human_seg` is now credited as Apache-2.0 everywhere. Two places said MIT and three said Apache-2.0.

## Why Apache-2.0

- The weights come from U-2-Net, which is Apache-2.0.
- The CLI downloads them from a rembg release. rembg is MIT, but its README credits U-2-Net for this model and says the model weights carry their own licenses. The MIT credit came from the packaging tool, not the model.

## Diff
