- `skills/media-use/audio/references/remove-background.md`: MIT becomes Apache-2.0.
- `skills-manifest.json`: the media-use skill hash, regenerated by the pre-commit hook.

After this, no mention of the model says MIT.

title: fix(core): preserve in-flight video preloads during runtime binding
body:
## What

Preserve an in-flight video download when the runtime binds media metadata listeners. Keep eager `preload="auto"`, but do not call `load()` again on a VIDEO whose `networkState` is already `NETWORK_LOADING`.

## Why

The binding pass currently calls `load()` whenever `readyState` is below `HAVE_FUTURE_DATA`, even if the browser is already fetching that video's selected resource. That resets resource selection and buffering. In the reported four-video project, all four videos reached binding at `NETWORK_LOADING` / `HAVE_NOTHING` and were explicitly reloaded.

## How

Extract the initial preload decision into a small tested helper. Audio behavior is unchanged, including its streaming-source recovery path. Incomplete videos that are idle, empty or have no selected source still call `load()`. Ready media remains untouched. No lazy-loading policy, clock changes, prototype overrides or source rewrites are included.

## Before / after verification

A browser run with the actual compiled runtime, plus instrumentation that only observed load calls:

| Observation | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Explicit video load calls while already fetching | 4 | 0 |
| Audio load calls | 1 | 1 |
| Videos fully ready after loading | 4 / 4 | 4 / 4 |

Cold seeks at 150.3, 87 and 40.3 seconds still settled; the changed run took 16.5–22.6 ms. Additional runs hit `NETWORK_NO_SOURCE` during binding and correctly retained retry calls. Request/resource-byte totals varied with browser scheduling and aborted range requests, so this PR does **not** claim a fixed bandwidth or FPS improvement. The measured effect is eliminating redundant resets when video loading is already active.

## Related work

Refs #4553 and #4560. Independent PR based on current main 76723c614; neither prior performance patch is included.

## Test plan

- [x] 232 tests: preload helper, runtime initialization, scene swaps
- [x] Network-state/readiness matrix, auto-preload promotion, unchanged audio path, idle/no-source recovery
- [x] Core and runtime TypeScript checks
- [x] Runtime IIFE build and actual browser verification
- [x] Lint, formatting, Fallow audit, commit hooks
- [x] Complete diff review; no change to authoring assets or export timing

title: fix(producer): use screenshot capture for distributed video chunks
body:
> Draft: this is a correctness baseline, not the proposed final fix. It sends every video-bearing chunk through screenshot capture and has a measurable latency cost. I am investigating a targeted first-worker-frame validation and conditional fallback before requesting review.

## Problem

Distributed rendering of plans with extracted video frames can sporadically emit a fully black frame at a worker/chunk boundary. The video frame is already injected, decoded, and visible in the DOM, yet Chrome's `HeadlessExperimental.beginFrame` screenshot sometimes omits it. The existing fallback only reacts to protocol failures and therefore cannot detect a successful capture containing the wrong pixels.

## Change

Start distributed chunks that contain extracted video frames in page screenshot mode. Keep the existing capture decision for plans without extracted video. This also passes the chosen mode into engine configuration so Chrome is launched consistently with the capture path.

## Verification

- Reproduced the bad frame in 2 of 4 runs of the same 120-frame chunk with three capture workers using the 0.7.94 Lambda renderer. The affected source image was decoded and visible; `beginFrame` returned an image with damage but black pixels.
- Applied the equivalent source change to 0.7.94 and reran that chunk five times: 120/120 frames each time, no black frame.
- Rendered the full 840-frame, 28-second composition with four chunks and audio. All 840 frames passed a black-frame scan; the assembled MP4 retained its audio track.
- On current main: `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, producer typecheck, and 11 focused producer tests pass.

## Cost

Screenshot capture increases rendering time for video-bearing chunks. In the full validation render, chunk wall times were approximately 35–93 seconds versus 23–79 seconds with BeginFrame. This chooses correct output over the faster path until the Chromium capture race can be fixed or detected reliably.

title: fix(engine): SDR renders keep footage and page colours as in the source
body:
## What

SDR renders now keep footage and page colours. There are three fixes, one for each place the colour went wrong:

1. **PNG frame tag** (commit by @sontiac, cherry-picked unchanged from #4550; tightened in a follow-up commit). SDR frames extracted for the page now say they are plain sRGB, so Chrome shows their code values instead of colour-managing them. This fixes darkened shadows in every `--video-frame-format png` render, and for every alpha-capable source (VP8/VP9 WebM, ProRes 4444), which always extracts as PNG.
2. **JPEG frame matrix** (default format for opaque SDR sources). The JPEG frames kept the source's BT.709 matrix, but every JPEG reader, Chrome included, decodes BT.601. They are now converted to BT.601 full range through RGB, and stay 4:2:0.
3. **mp4 encode matrix**. Chrome's captures are BT.601 JPEGs. The SDR encoders only converted the range, so the mp4 carried BT.601 colour maths under its BT.709 tag. Frames now go to RGB with the capture's matrix, then to the BT.709 the file is tagged with. One shared filter covers both encoders on every SDR path (software, VAAPI, the other GPU encoders, and the raw RGB frames of the layered path).

Footage without colour tags is read with the matrix Chrome plays it with, so renders match Studio's preview: BT.709 from 720 coded lines up and BT.601 below for H.264 and VP8, BT.601 at every size for VP9 (with or without alpha) and AV1.

Refs #4549. The forced-SDR tone-map part of the issue follows in a stacked PR, which closes it.

## Credit

@sontiac found and diagnosed this. That includes the colour-tag model behind the darkening, the measurements and minimal repro in #4549, the JPEG and mp4 matrix problems listed there as related items 1 and 2, and the extraction fix itself. Their commit is kept as is, with their authorship; only a tool co-author trailer was dropped from its message. The follow-up commits that build on it credit them as co-author. This PR supersedes #4550 so all three fixes land together.

## Decisions

- **One PR for all three fixes.** The JPEG error and the old mp4 encode error cancelled each other for footage on the default path: on main a BT.709 clip's mp4 came out right by accident. Fixing the encode alone turned the same clip from c73a27 into ba2c29 (measured). The JPEG fix therefore has to ship with the encode fix, not after it.
- **PNG frames declare BT.709 primaries as well as the sRGB transfer.** ffmpeg writes an `sRGB` chunk only for BT.709 primaries, and only writes `cICP` from 6.0 on. On ffmpeg 5.1 (Debian bookworm, the base of `Dockerfile.test` and the Cloud Run image), a BT.601-tagged source therefore got cHRM plus gAMA 1/2.2, which Chrome decodes as a pure 2.2 power (0x10 shadows rendered as 0x07). With BT.709 primaries every ffmpeg writes the `sRGB` chunk, and Chrome shows the frame's code values for every SDR source. The cost: SDR sources with non-BT.709 primaries (SMPTE-C, BT.2020 SDR) no longer get Chrome's gamut mapping. Exact code values were chosen over that mapping; the target is the source's own decode.
- **Through RGB, not YUV to YUV.** swscale's direct YUV-to-YUV scale ignores a matrix change on ffmpeg 7 and older, and on 8 and newer converts through a low-precision step that tints greys (0x101010 became 0x0b0d0d). The RGB route is exact for greys on every version tested.
- **VFR sources keep main's frame timing.** ffmpeg 5.1 and 6.0, which the Docker and Cloud Run images install, use each frame's duration for CFR resampling only when no filter is set. The new colour filters would therefore have cut the still that ends a VFR window short (17 frames instead of 19 on the test fixture, 32 instead of 60 on a longer window). A filtered SDR VFR extraction now runs as two processes: the first is main's exact decode and resample, writing raw frames to a pipe; the second restores the source's colour tags and applies the colour filters with passthrough timing. Frame counts and repeat patterns equal main's unfiltered command on 5.1.9 and 7.0.2, and on 7.0.2 the frames are byte-identical to a single-process run. Cost: 2 to 20% more wall time for those extractions. HDR sources and pixel formats the raw pipe does not carry unchanged keep main's single-process command; HDR's existing truncation on ffmpeg below 6.1 is tracked for a follow-up, because the pipe would drop HDR10 light levels.
- **Untagged footage follows Chrome.** Chrome 152 decodes untagged H.264 at 1280x720, 406x720 or 1920x1080 as BT.709, and at 1280x718, 720x406 or 960x540 as BT.601: the rule is coded height. VP8 follows the same rule; untagged VP9, VP9 with alpha and AV1 play as BT.601 at 480 and at 1080 lines. Extraction now declares that matrix for untagged SDR sources. Before this, main read every untagged clip as BT.709 (wrong for SD and for VP9/AV1), and this branch's first version read every one as BT.601 (wrong for HD H.264). The 718-line and 720-line H.264 cases and the 720-line VP9 and AV1 cases are tests.
- **Nearest-neighbour chroma in both conversions.** With swscale's default filter, the RGB round trip smeared colour about 2 px across edges on ffmpeg 4.4 to 7.x. Next to a blue edge, red 254 left 8 inside the blue; main left 0. `flags=neighbor` maps the half-resolution chroma back one to one: edges stay as sharp as main on every version tested, and flat colours do not change.

## Measurements

The issue's patch clip: patch colour 0xC83C28 plus greys, BT.709 limited range, every tag bt709. Values are at (700,1000) / (180,100) / (180,300), frame 16. Every render used `--sdr --workers 1 --frames-cache-dir off` with chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30. The reference is ffmpeg's own decode of the source on the same host. Numbers are identical on ffmpeg 5.1.9 (Debian bookworm, production base) and 7.0.2 unless a row says otherwise.

Source decode: BT.709 clip c73a27 / 101010 / 404040; BT.601 clip c83b27 / 101010 / 404040.

| Source, frame format, output | main (5.1) | main (7.0) | this branch (5.1 and 7.0) |
|---|---|---|---|
| BT.709, png, png-sequence | ce422c / 0e0e0e / 494949 | c42f1b / **040404** / 363636 | **c73a27 / 101010 / 404040** |
| BT.709, png, mp4 | d84c26 / 0d0d0d / 494949 | d03a16 / 030303 / 353535 | **c63827 / 101010 / 404040** |
| BT.709, default (jpg), png-sequence | bc2e2a / 101010 / 404040 | bc2e2a / 101010 / 404040 | **c93c28 / 101010 / 404040** |
| BT.709, default (jpg), mp4 | c73a27 / 101010 / 404040 (errors cancel) | c73a27 / 101010 / 404040 (errors cancel) | **c83a27 / 101010 / 404040** |
| BT.601, png, png-sequence | c9492b / 0e0e0e / 494949 | c0381a / 040404 / 353636 | **c83b27 / 101010 / 404040** |
| BT.601, default (jpg), mp4 | d44824 / 101010 / 404040 | d44824 / 101010 / 404040 | **c83a27 / 101010 / 404040** |
| alpha VP9 WebM, default (always png), png-sequence | ce422c / 0e0e0e / 494949 | c42f1b / 040404 / 363636 | **c73a27 / 101010 / 404040** |
| CSS-only page (#C83C28 / #101010 / #404040), mp4 | d44824 / 101010 / 404040 | d44824 / 101010 / 404040 | **c83a27 / 101010 / 404040** |

Crop of the patch area on ffmpeg 7.0.2. Columns: source, main, this branch. Rows: png-sequence with png frames; mp4 with png frames; mp4 at the default frame format, where main is right only because two errors cancel; CSS-only page mp4 (reference column: the page colours).

![Patch-area crops: source, main, this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/343128b7-5c73-41f9-8b29-c769b960c6e0)

**Greys are exact. Saturated colours land within 2 codes, and that is the format's floor.** 8-bit limited-range BT.709 has 219 luma steps, and one Cr step moves red by about 1.8 codes. Encoding a lossless RGB #C83C28 with zscale's float path gives the same c73a27 as this branch's filter, so the last code or two cannot be recovered in an 8-bit mp4. JPEG capture (quality 80) accounts for about one more code in the CSS row.

The mp4 encode chain alone, on one Chrome JPEG capture (reference: the JPEG's own decode, c83b27 / 101010 / 404040 / 1f4fdf / f0f0f0):

| ffmpeg | encoder | main chain | this branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| 5.1.9, 6.1.1, 7.0.2 | libx264 | d44824 / 101010 / 404040 / 1753e4 / efefef | c83a27 / 101010 / 404040 / 1f4fdf / efefef |
| 8.1.1 | libx264, h264_videotoolbox | c53b23 / **0b0d0d** / 3b3d3d / 1b50db / eceeee | c63c27 / 0f0f0f / 3e3e3e / 1b50de / eeeeee |

On 8.1 a lossless reference encoded straight from RGB decodes as 0f0f0f / 3e3e3e / eeeeee too, so those greys are that decoder's convention, not the chain's.

## Regression goldens

Eight fixtures changed, all for colour. Each new golden was rendered in the `Dockerfile.test` image (ffmpeg 5.1.9) and checked before commit against what it should show: the colours its page declares, or its source video's own decode read the way Chrome plays it. Values are the most common colours of a frame, decoded as the golden is tagged.

| Fixture | Reference | Old golden | New golden |
|---|---|---|---|
| subcomp-bare-fragment | page #00d4aa / #101820 | 00bcab / 0f181f | **00d3aa** / 0f181f |
| distributed/static-volume-future-set | page #087443 / #07111f | 006643 / 071020 | **087241** / 060f1f |
| timed-descendant-visibility | page #daebff / #f8fbff | d6e8fe / f7fbff | **d9e9ff** / f8f9fe |
| page-side-shader-compositor-render-compat | shader gradients, no flat colour | | |
| render-symlinked-assets | page #22c55e / #0b1220 | 16af5c / 09111f | **21c35c / 0a1220** |
| hf2550-video-subcomposition-ghost | untagged H.264, 2160 lines, as BT.709: ff1700 / 00d700 / ffee00 | ff1700 / 00d700 / ffee00 | fd1700 / 00d700 / fdee00 (page colours on top change) \* |
| nested-sequential-video-local-start | untagged H.264, 90 lines, as BT.601: fd0000 | ff1700 | **fd0000** |
| speed-ramp | untagged H.264, 180 lines, as BT.601: fe00fd / fdfd00 / 00fe00 | ff25ff / ffee00 | **fe00fd / fdfd00** |

\* The new hf2550 golden also shows the "Deploy" and "It's LIVE" pills during their fade frames, which the old one lacked. That is not from this PR: main's own render already differs from main's golden at that checkpoint (30.9 dB against a median of 49). The pills are also missing at 17.17 s, where they should be fully visible; that looks like a separate visibility bug and is reported separately.

Only the mp4 goldens change. Their `compiled.html` snapshots stay as they are: the harness would also rewrite them with unrelated compiler drift from main, which does not belong in this PR.

Six other fixtures fail in that image on this host on main too, at the same frames: heygen-promo-preview-assets, pip-video-late-host, fast-capture-gsap, style-17-prod, webgl-video-texture-render-compat and maplibre-adapter (zero-duration composition). Their goldens are unchanged. portrait-edge-bleed, video-hfid-no-id, render-video-overlay-stretch, vfr-screen-recording and plan-v2-partial-color pass against their existing goldens.

## Not changed

- HDR renders: extraction changes are gated on `!isHdr && !sdrToHdrTransfer`, and the encoders keep their HDR filters. `hdr-regression` and `hdr-hlg-regression` pass on main and on this branch, with identical per-checkpoint PSNR. A forced-SDR render of the HDR fixture clip is byte-identical to main.
- The forced-SDR tone-map paths (Linux zscale, macOS VideoToolbox) still tag their frames BT.709, so they are still affected. They are the remaining part of #4549, in the stacked follow-up PR.
- HDR VFR extraction keeps main's single-process command, including its frame loss on ffmpeg below 6.1 (see Decisions); that has its own follow-up.

## Known limits

- CPU: the encode filter costs about 6 ms per 1080p frame, and the JPEG extraction filter about 8 ms per extracted 1080p frame. The non-VAAPI GPU encoders had no software filter before and now pay the encode cost in full.
- JPEG frames are always 4:2:0. main kept full chroma for 4:4:4 sources; those now lose half the chroma resolution in extracted frames (the final mp4 is 4:2:0 either way).
- Extraction-cache entries under `hfcache-v5-` exist only from builds of this branch; the prefix is new in this PR, so shipped builds never wrote one. The version notes in `extractionCache.ts` stop at v4, because the comment ratchet refuses new comment lines in that file. The reason for v5: SDR frames now carry the sRGB tag and the BT.601 JPEG matrix, so v4 entries hold the old colours.
- CI installs ffmpeg 6.1.1, where CFR resampling already keeps frame durations with a filter set. The VFR tests below therefore pass there even without the two-process path; only a 5.1 or 6.0 run (the `Dockerfile.test` image) catches that regression.
- The two-process path covers the pixel formats checked to cross the raw pipe unchanged on ffmpeg 5.1.9, 7.0.2 and 8.1.1 (planar YUV at 8 to 12 bits with or without alpha, nv12/nv21, packed 4:2:2, gray, planar and packed RGB). An SDR VFR source in another format (a raw semi-planar 10-bit stream, bgr0, pal8, 12-bit ProRes 4444 with alpha) keeps a single process with the colour filters, so on ffmpeg 5.1 and 6.0 it loses a trailing still's frames.
- The untagged-matrix rule for codecs this Chrome does not play (HEVC on Linux, ProRes, MPEG-4 part 2) follows the 720-line rule by assumption; it was not measured.
- The colour tags restored in the second process use ffprobe's names. An ffprobe 7.1 or newer paired with an older ffmpeg can print a matrix name (`ipt-c2`, `ycgco-re`) that the older ffmpeg rejects; such a VFR extraction fails instead of rendering.
- The new chain was checked with libx264 on ffmpeg 5.1, 6.1, 7.0 and 8.1, and with h264_videotoolbox on 8.1. NVENC, QSV, AMF and VAAPI were not tested on hardware; the filter runs in software before them.
- SDR sources with BT.2020 or SMPTE-C primaries now render with their code values unmapped (see Decisions).

## Test plan

- [x] `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts`: every SDR PNG frame (BT.709 and BT.601 sources) carries an `sRGB` chunk and no `cICP`. A BT.709 source's JPEG frame decodes within 3 codes of the source, both on flat colour and one pixel inside a red to blue edge. Untagged H.264 sources extract as BT.601 at 718 lines and BT.709 at 720 lines (png and jpg), and untagged VP9 and AV1 at 720 lines as BT.601. A VFR window ending on a still extracts as many frames as main's unfiltered resample, with the source's colours, for full-range BT.709 (png, jpg), BT.470BG gamma 2.8 and RGB sources. A VFR HDR10 PQ window (MaxCLL 4000) tone-maps byte-identically to the single-process command. An SDR-to-HDR extraction carries no `sRGB` chunk.
- [x] `chunkEncoder.test.ts` and `streamingEncoder.test.ts`: the real encoder arguments turn a Chrome-style JPEG of 0xC83C28, 0xFE0000, 0x101010 and 0x2050E0 (each next to a blue edge), and a raw rgb48le frame of 0xC83C28 on the layered path, into an mp4 that decodes within 2 codes, on flat colour and at the edge. `runFfmpeg.test.ts`: the two-process runner passes every frame through, fails with the producer's error, stops an endless producer when the consumer fails, and releases a waiting consumer when the producer cannot start.
- [x] Each new test fails with its fix removed. Earlier round: no extraction filter fails both sRGB tests; the transfer-only filter from #4550 fails the BT.601 case; no JPEG filter fails the JPEG test (13 codes); JPEG filter without `neighbor` fails at the edge (10 codes); the old encode chain fails the pixel test (12 codes); encode filter without `neighbor` fails at the edge (15 codes). This round, on ffmpeg 5.1.9: no two-process path fails every VFR still case and the existing VFR superset test (17 frames instead of 19); no colour-tag restore fails the full-range cases (20 codes); HDR allowed into the pipe fails the HDR10 test; no release on a producer start failure times out that test; no untagged guess, or BT.601 at every size, fails the 720-line H.264 cases (13 codes); no VP9/AV1 rule fails those two cases (13 codes); gate without `!sdrToHdrTransfer` fails the SDR-to-HDR test; raw layered frames without the matrix fail their pixel test (10 codes on 7.0.2).
- [x] The five changed engine test files pass in the `Dockerfile.test` base with ffmpeg 5.1.9: 479 passed. The spawn-failure test passed 25 of 25 repeated runs. On ffmpeg 7.0.2 the same files pass apart from "extracts one real final SDR frame for 'unindexed negative-base MPEG-TS'", which fails on that host on origin/main too.
- [x] Engine `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt, `comment-ratchet` and the ffprobe argv contract are clean.
- [x] End to end: the render matrix above on ffmpeg 5.1.9 (bookworm container) and 7.0.2, plus `hdr-regression` and `hdr-hlg-regression`, plus the regression fixtures listed under Regression goldens.

title: fix(engine): export draws a video in exactly the frames it is shown in
body:
## What this fixes

When two videos meet a hair off a frame boundary, a render could draw the wrong one on the frame where they meet. Example at 30 fps: clip A ends and clip B starts at 1.00001 s. Export visibility treats a time within a thousandth of a frame of a boundary as that boundary, so on the 1 s frame it shows B and hides A. The engine's frame lookup used the raw times, so on that same frame it injected A's frame and not B's. The page and the frames disagreed on which clip was on screen.

Now there is one rule, `exportClipWindow(start, end, fps)` in core's parity contract, and both sides use it: export visibility in the runtime timeline, and the engine's frame lookup table for every membership check (which videos are active, the frame for a video at a time, and the order clips are swept in). The render fps passed to the table is the same value the page snaps to (`resolveRenderFpsConfig`), both in-process and in distributed chunks.

Which source frame is drawn does not change: the local time still counts from the clip's raw start, as the runtime's media time does. Without an fps, the table behaves as before, so the public engine API stays compatible.

## Tests

- `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts`: A = [0, 1.00001] and B = [1.00001, 2] at 30 fps; at 1 s only B is active, with its first frame, on both a fresh table and one stepping in from the previous frame, and A has no frame. This fails on `main`, which returns A.
- `planV2.test.ts`: a video starting a hair after the 1/30 s frame is given to the chunk that renders that frame, so distributed planning ships the frames a chunk will draw. Dropping the fps argument from the planner fails it.

Results: `tsc` in core, engine and producer; oxfmt, oxlint and Fallow clean; engine frame extractor, injector and boundary tests 179, core runtime and inline-script tests 1512, producer distributed tests 216. Putting the raw window back in the engine fails the new engine test; putting it back in core fails the existing nested-outro frame test.

Known limit: the fps argument is optional so the engine API stays compatible, and only the distributed planner has a test that fails when it is dropped. The in-process render and the chunk renderer pass it the same way but have no such test.

title: test: cli and studio-server tests remove the temp folders they create
body:
## What changes

The cli and studio-server test suites stop leaving folders in the system temp directory. Before this, one passing run of `packages/cli` left about 70 folders behind (`hf-preview-state-*`, `hf-plate-*`, `hf-installer-*`, `hf-cloud-render-test-*`, `hf-timeline-*`, `motion-*`, `hf-keyframes-*`, `hf-lintrun-*`, `hf-scroll-*`) and `packages/studio-server` about 14 (`hf-subcomp-preview-*`). On a machine that runs the suites all day, they pile up.

## How

- Each temp folder is removed where it is made, with `onTestFinished(() => rmSync(dir, { recursive: true, force: true }))`, the pattern `packages/cli/src/commands/history.test.ts` already uses. It runs whether the test passes or fails.
- A module-level folder (`lintRun.e2e.test.ts`) is removed in `afterAll`.
- `describeProject.test.ts` had one shared `dir` and one `afterEach`, so a test that built two projects only removed the second. Each folder now registers its own cleanup, and a project sits inside its own parent folder, so the fixtures some tests write next to the project (`../hf-outside.html`, `../hf-parent-media.mp3`) go with it instead of landing at a fixed name in the shared temp directory.
- `installer.test.ts` drops the try/finally removals that became redundant.

No assertion or test name changes.

## What I measured

- Each suite run with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty folder, then listing what is left:
  - `packages/cli` on main: about 70 test folders left. With this change: only `node-compile-cache` and `tsx-1000`, which are tool caches, not test folders.
  - `packages/studio-server` with this change: 800 pass, and nothing is left.
- The changed files run alone: they pass and leave nothing behind. With one assertion in `describeProject.test.ts` forced to fail, still nothing is left.
- Removing the cleanup line from `subComposition.test.ts` brings back 14 `hf-subcomp-preview-*` folders.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean on the changed files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The other packages (core, engine, producer and the rest), which also create temp folders in their tests.
- Windows and macOS: every run was on Linux.
- A test process killed mid-run (SIGKILL) still leaves its folders; `onTestFinished` does not run then.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, three rounds.
- Round 1: no blockers, no majors; three minors: `describeProject.test.ts` still removed only the last folder a test made; two fixtures there were written at a fixed name in the shared temp directory; `installer.test.ts` removed some folders twice. All fixed.
- Round 2: no findings except a helper (`runOneLiner`) that still removed its own folder twice. Fixed.
- Round 3: no findings.
- The reviewer also confirmed that vitest 4 throws when `onTestFinished` is called outside a test, so a misplaced cleanup fails loudly, and that no test's assertions or names changed.

title: fix(release): name Release once in a changelog entry's tags
body:
## What changes

A changelog entry whose commits include a `release`-scoped change no longer lists "Release" twice in its tags. `renderTags` always puts "Release" first, and then took up to three scope tags, which could include "Release" again.

## How

- `renderTags` filters "Release" out of the scope tags, in any case, before taking three, so the entry keeps up to three other scope tags. A `RELEASE` scope passes the scope formatter unchanged, so the comparison ignores case.
- Four published entries in `docs/changelog.mdx` that already listed "Release" twice (v0.6.113, v0.7.92 and two others) now list it once; their other tags are unchanged.
- `renderTags` is exported so the new test can call it.

## What I measured

- `node --import tsx --test scripts/draft-changelog.test.ts scripts/changelog-weekly.test.ts`: 22 pass.
- With the filter reverted, the first new test fails; with a case-sensitive filter, the uppercase-scope test fails.
- No entry in `docs/changelog.mdx` lists "Release" twice after the change.
- The branch is merged with current main; no conflicts.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real changelog run against the release history.
- The docs site build (`mint validate`) did not finish on my machine; the edited file compiles with the docs CLI's MDX compiler before and after, so the docs CI job has the final say.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, two rounds.
- Round 1: no blockers, no majors; two minors: the filter only matched the exact string "Release", so an uppercase scope would still duplicate it; and published entries already carried the duplicate. Both fixed.
- Round 2: no findings. It confirmed each doc edit removes exactly one duplicate token, and no tag list in the file repeats a tag in any case.

title: feat(cli): catalog --installed lists a project's catalog items and which the video uses
body:
## What this adds

`hyperframes catalog --installed` shows which catalog items a project has and whether its video uses each one:

```
Name                        Type        Status                      File
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ai-chat-reveal              block       not used                    compositions/ai-chat-reveal.html
animated-bar-chart          component   pasted inline, can't tell   compositions/components/animated-bar-chart.html
aurora-drift                component   pasted inline, can't tell   compositions/components/aurora-drift.html (found by file name)

3 items, 0 in use by index.html.
```

- **Where items come from**: what `hyperframes add` recorded in `hyperframes.json` (it records every item it installs, components included), plus any registry item whose file sits at its install path (`<dir>/<name>.html` or `<dir>/<name>/<name>.html`, under the project's configured block and component folders and the default ones, since Studio installs to the defaults). Those rows are marked "found by file name", which covers items added before recording existed, installed from Studio, or copied in by hand. Every block and component in the registry today installs at one of those two paths.
- **Status**: a block is "in use" when `index.html` reaches it through `data-composition-src`, the same walk the render event uses, and "not used" otherwise. A component is pasted into the author's own markup, so its use leaves nothing to detect: it reads "pasted inline, can't tell" instead of a guess. A recorded item whose file is gone reads "file removed".
- **`--json`** prints `{ items, scannedFiles, configUnreadable }` (`configUnreadable`: `hyperframes.json` could not be read); each item has `name`, `type`, `file`, `status` (`in-use` | `not-used` | `file-missing` | `pasted-inline`) and `foundBy` (`recorded` | `file`). `--type` filters both forms. Combining with `--query`, `--tag` or `--human-friendly` exits 1 and says why.
- **Empty project**: "No catalog items in this project yet." with how to browse and install. When the registry list cannot be fetched, only recorded items are listed and the output says so; when `hyperframes.json` cannot be read, the output says recorded items are missing. Outside a project (no `index.html`) it fails like other project commands.

## Telemetry

One new event, `cli_catalog_installed_view`, sent when the view runs:

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `registry_item_count`, `registry_blocks_used_count`, `registry_items`, `registry_blocks_used`, `registry_items_truncated`, `registry_manifest_unreadable` | the catalog properties `render_complete` sends, from the same helper; here the items include those found by file |
| `registry_items_found_by_file_count` | items found only by file name |
| `registry_items_file_missing_count` | recorded items whose file is gone |
| `registry_blocks_unused_count` | blocks installed but not reached from `index.html` |
| `scanned_files` | whether the registry list was available |
| `json` | whether `--json` was used |

Names are only registry item names that pass the existing name check, capped at 40 as on `render_complete`. No paths, project names or content. Opt-outs apply as for every event.

## Docs

The CLI reference (`catalog` section) and the `hyperframes-registry` skill document the flag and its statuses; the skill tells agents to check `--installed` before adding an item the project already has.

## Tests

- `catalogUsage.test.ts`: recorded blocks in use, not used and removed; recorded components; unrecorded items found by install path, flat and in their own folder, under the project's own configured paths; the view in the render event's shape.
- `catalogUsage.test.ts` also: an item in the default folder when the project sets its own, and the project's own folder winning when both hold it.
- `catalog.test.ts`: the table, the empty state, the registry-unavailable and unreadable-settings notes, one item in the singular; run for real, outside a project it exits 1 before fetching the registry, `--query` is refused before fetching, and `--json` carries `configUnreadable`.
- `events.test.ts`: the event's properties.

Results: CLI catalog, catalogUsage, events and add tests 188; `tsc`, oxfmt, oxlint, Fallow and the skills manifest check clean. Each of these fails a named test: components no longer reading "pasted inline", the file scan turned off, recorded components dropped, the default folder left out, the singular dropped, the project check removed, the refusal moved after the fetch, the JSON field dropped, the folder order swapped.

End to end with the built CLI in a fresh project: `add ai-chat-reveal`, `add animated-bar-chart` and a hand-copied component gave the table above; after mounting the block in `index.html`, `--json` showed it `in-use`; `--type component` listed only the two components; `--query` exited 1 with the message. In an empty folder it exits 1 with "No composition found"; with `paths.blocks` set to `scenes` a block at `compositions/` is still listed; with a broken `hyperframes.json` the note shows and `--json` has `"configUnreadable": true`.

title: fix(producer): embed the Google font the page linked instead of a wider cut
body:
## Cause

Rendered text could use a different Google font file than the preview. The producer reconstructed each family request using only italic and weight, discarding authored axes such as optical size. Because embedded font faces are written after the page stylesheet, that replacement wins in the render; a large Fraunces word can become roughly 70px wider and spill out of its card.

Using the authored URL for bundled-font supplements also removed real italic faces when the page requested only a normal face. That produced synthetic italic EB Garamond in style-18-prod and failed 22 visual checkpoints.

## Rationale

For fonts outside the deterministic bundled set, embed the page's Google Fonts resources instead of reconstructing a weight-only request. Parse HTML attributes so escaped query parameters are decoded, retain all active resources for each family in document order, and deduplicate repeated URLs at their last occurrence. Exclude disabled, alternate and conditionally applied sources from unconditional embedding; unconditional screen/all links and imports are supported. Preserve authored text subsets, variable weight ranges and oblique angle ranges, and keep each returned face under its own family name.

Bundled families keep their existing complete supplement of weights and italics, with bundled Latin faces retaining precedence. System aliases such as Arial still resolve to the bundled canonical family. A failed authored download does not fall back to a different local or weight-only font file. Embedded styles remain after page stylesheets to preserve render determinism.

## Validation

- 134 font and authored-resource tests pass, including regressions that fail before the fixes.
- style-18-prod passes a full local render, visual comparison and audio comparison after restoring italic supplements; the committed baseline is unchanged.
- Producer typecheck, lint, formatting and fallow checks pass.
- All CI checks pass at `509d2185d`, including every regression shard; style-18-prod has 0 of 100 failing checkpoints (minimum PSNR 42.7).

title: fix(studio): reload the preview only when a file it loaded changes
fix(studio-server): a thumbnail survives files vanishing mid-request
body:
## What changes

A Studio thumbnail request no longer fails when a file it reads disappears mid-request: the composition, the manual-edits or motion manifest, a cached thumbnail, or the cache folder itself. Before, the route checked that a file existed and then read it, and a file removed in between turned the request into an error.

## How

- Each file is opened once and stat'ed and read through the same descriptor (`readFileOnce`), which reports a missing file or a non-file instead of throwing.
- The two copied blocks that read and hashed the manual-edits and motion manifests become one helper (`manifestKey`). A missing manifest adds nothing to the cache key; any other read error still fails the request.
- A cached thumbnail removed mid-request falls through to generating a new one.
- Pruning the cache treats a missing cache folder as nothing to prune; other errors still throw.
- The cache folder is created with `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` without a separate existence check.
- A path that runs through a file (ENOTDIR) counts as "not a file": a stray `.hyperframes` file adds nothing to the key, as before, and a composition path through a file gets a 404 instead of an error.
- The cache key is byte-identical to main's for the same inputs, including files dated before 1970. One deliberate difference: a manifest is hashed from its raw bytes, so a manifest with invalid UTF-8 gets a new key once.

## What I measured

- `packages/studio-server`, full suite, with `TMPDIR` pointed at an empty folder: 51 files, 822 tests pass, and nothing is left behind except the Node compile cache.
- With `thumbnail.ts` reverted to main, the 4 race tests fail; with the ENOTDIR line removed, the stray-file test fails.
- `thumbnail.file-race.test.ts` and `thumbnail.test.ts` alone: 26 pass.
- The branch is merged with current main; no conflicts.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real Studio session hitting the race: the tests simulate each removal.
- Windows and macOS: every run was on Linux.
- No test pins the pre-1970 key; undoing that part would cost one extra regeneration, not a stale thumbnail.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, two rounds. It compared cache filenames from main and this branch side by side for plain projects, both manifests, BOMs, invalid UTF-8 and pre-1970 dates.
- Round 1: no blockers, no majors; three minors: a stray `.hyperframes` file turned into an error (fixed, with a test), pre-1970 dates changed the key (fixed), invalid-UTF-8 manifests hash differently (kept on purpose).
- Round 2: no blockers, no majors; one optional minor (no test for the pre-1970 case).

title: docs(cli): render help says when page-side compositing is actually used
body:
## What changes

`hyperframes render --help` described `--page-side-compositing` wrongly. It said "HDR/alpha/video content auto-disables" and that `--no-page-side-compositing` forces the layered path. The help and the CLI docs table now say what the render code does.

## What the code does (origin/main)

- The decision (`packages/producer/src/services/renderOrchestrator.ts`, `usePageSideCompositingForTransitions`) is: `(enablePageSideCompositing || isGif) && hasShaderTransitions && !hasHdrContent && outputSupportsPageSideShaderCompositing(format)`.
- `outputSupportsPageSideShaderCompositing` (`packages/producer/src/services/render/renderFormat.ts`) accepts `mp4`, `gif` and `hls` only. webm and mov then take the layered path (`hdrCompositor.ts`). png-sequence takes neither; the help makes no claim about it, and that behaviour is being looked at separately.
- There is no video-content condition anywhere in that decision, so "video content auto-disables" was not true. Alpha only matters through the output format.
- The engine config turns page-side compositing off when fast capture (drawElement) is on, and the compile stage turns it back on when fast capture does not engage; for shader compositions that is the usual case unless `--experimental-fast-capture` is passed, and even then three composition checks can keep page-side on. Hence "usually".
- Because of `|| isGif`, gif output uses the page-side canvas even with `--no-page-side-compositing`.

## What I measured

- `render --help` prints the new text (checked by running the CLI from source).
- `docs/packages/cli.mdx` repeated the old claim in the render flags table; that row now matches.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsc --noEmit` on `packages/cli` are clean; the render command tests pass (130).

## What I did NOT exercise

- I ran no render myself; the review's renders confirmed the path for mp4, gif, webm and mov. hls and Docker renders were checked by reading the code only, and the fast-capture path could not run on Linux.
- Whether gif should honour `--no-page-side-compositing` is a behaviour question left out of this PR.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, three rounds, including real renders of mp4, gif, webm and mov with the flag on and off.
- Round 1: "other renders take the layered path" was false for png-sequence; "when fast capture engages" read wrong; the docs row still carried the old claim. All fixed.
- Round 2: the docs row's "gif always uses it" read as the layered path; plus "usually" for fast capture. Both fixed.
- Round 3: no findings.

title: fix(cli): Studio's catalog install records the item and honours paths, as add does
body:
## What this fixes

Installing a catalog item from Studio (what `hyperframes preview` serves) did not install it the way `hyperframes add` does. It had its own copy of the install steps, which:

- ignored the project's `paths` in `hyperframes.json`, so with `paths.blocks: "scenes"` a block landed in `compositions/` anyway;
- never recorded the item in `hyperframes.json`, so render telemetry (and `catalog --installed`, #4568) could not tell it came from the catalog;
- always used the public registry, even when the project sets its own `registry`.

The catalog panel now reads the same registry the install uses, so a project pointed at its own registry lists what it can install. Studio now mounts the item's own file by the path `add` recorded (`scenes/my-block.html`, forward slashes on every OS), listed first even when the block has dependencies. Other written files come back project-relative with forward slashes, including for a project opened through a symlink.

Now Studio calls the same install function as `add`. `runAdd` becomes a thin wrapper over `addToProject`, which also hands back the installed item (Studio needs its size and duration to place it), so `add --json` output is unchanged. Studio keeps its own step after the install that fits a block to the project's canvas size, and now has the installer re-record the rewritten files in `hyperframes.lock.json` (through the installer's own record writer, only for files that install just wrote). Before, the record kept the hash from before the rewrite, so dropping the same block a second time read it as a local edit: the file was kept, Studio said no composition file was written, and a later `add` said "kept, you have edited this".

What Studio users will notice, all because Studio now follows `add`'s rules:

- A project without `hyperframes.json` gets the default one, as `add` writes it.
- A later `hyperframes add` of a block Studio installed replaces it with the registry's copy, because Studio's resize is no longer mistaken for the user's edit. A file the user did edit is still kept.
- Studio installs send the same `registry_item_added` event as `add`. The event gains `source`: `studio` for Studio installs, `cli` for `add`.

Studio's own development server (the Vite adapter) still has its separate install path; it gets its own change.

## Tests

- `studioServer.registryInstall.test.ts`, on a project opened through a symlink whose `hyperframes.json` sets `paths.blocks` to `scenes` and its own registry (the stub answers only that registry; item names no other test uses, since the registry cache is shared in a run):
  - a Studio install returns `scenes/<block>.html`, writes nothing under `compositions/`, records the item with that target, and sends `registry_item_added` with `source: "studio"`;
  - the catalog panel lists the items of the project's registry;
  - a block sized unlike the project installs a second time, and after a real edit the next install keeps the file and returns nothing for Studio to rewrite;
  - an edit to one block survives installing another block;
  - when the block folder is a symlink inside the project, the returned file is the recorded path;
  - a block with a dependency returns its own file first.

Results: `tsc`, oxfmt, oxlint and Fallow clean; CLI `add`, `catalog`, Studio server and the new tests pass. Each of these fails a named test: `main`'s install, the previous path mapping (symlinked folder, dependency order), returning a kept file, the catalog reading the default registry, the install without `source: "studio"`, the install without re-recording, and re-recording every lock entry instead of only the files just written.

Known limits, both as on `main`:
- A component's second drop inserts nothing: Studio makes its background transparent after the install record is written, so the next install reads that as the project's edit and keeps the file. The fix is to do that rewrite on the server before the record; it needs its own change in Studio.
- If a block the project edited has dependencies, dropping it again rewrites the dependencies and Studio mounts the first one. No public catalog item has dependencies.

title: fix(studio): the dev server leaves catalog installs to hyperframes preview
body:
## What this changes

Studio's own development server (the Vite dev server used to work on Studio itself) had a second copy of the catalog install: it copied an item's files from the local `registry/` checkout, without dependencies, compatibility checks, the project's `paths`, or a record in `hyperframes.json`. `hyperframes preview` installs through the same code as `hyperframes add`, and that is now the only installer.

The dev server's copy is removed. Its catalog panel still lists the local items, and an install now answers with a 501 whose message Studio shows as a toast: "Installing catalog items needs hyperframes preview".

Routing the dev server through `add`'s installer was considered: `add` reads registries over `https://` only, so it cannot install from the local checkout without a new reader for the registry list, item files and cache.

## Before

On `main`, Add on a catalog tile in the dev server installs it: an "X Post" row appears on the timeline and `compositions/x-post.html` is written.

![Before: the dev server installs the item](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/84943afa-c90e-4fc4-ac4f-d17f6f92a44f)

## After

The same click answers 501, and the "Adding …" toast gives way to the error toast (one toast); the timeline and the project folder are unchanged.

![After: the dev server points to hyperframes preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbea332f-4dda-4317-9353-1ae5859de847)

## Tests

- `useBlockHandlers.test.tsx`: when an install fails, the install's "Adding …" toast is dismissed after the installer's error toast, so only the error stays.

- `vite.adapter.projects.test.ts`: an install request through the dev server's real API answers 501 with that message. On `main` the same request installs the item (200).

Results: `tsc` for studio and studio-server, oxfmt and oxlint clean; studio dev-server tests 27 and studio-server route tests 359 pass.

title: feat(studio): the Enter key opens a section clip, and hosts can reuse the composition stack
body:
## What this adds

Three small pieces an app that embeds Studio needs to open a section from its own timeline without copying Studio code:

- **Enter opens a section clip.** With a clip that plays a sub-composition focused on the timeline, Enter drills in exactly like double-click. Both go through one helper in the timeline keyboard actor that decides "only a clip with a section file opens". Enter on a plain clip does nothing new; Enter on an expandable row still expands or collapses it; Enter typed into a control inside the timeline goes to that control. Enter during a drag or trim does nothing, so the gesture is kept, and Enter with Shift, Cmd, Ctrl or Alt is left to the browser. The clip tooltip now reads "Double-click or press Enter to open".
- **`useCompositionStack` is exported** from `@hyperframes/studio`, next to `CompositionBreadcrumb` and `CompositionLevel`, so a host can hold the drill-down stack (push on drill, back to a level, film playhead restored) instead of rebuilding it. Mounting it while the film is already showing leaves the timeline as it is; before, it emptied the timeline and reported a return to the film.
- **The breadcrumb uses Studio's theme tokens** instead of fixed `neutral-*` colours, so a host that re-points the tokens themes it. In Studio's dark theme it looks the same; the tokens used and their values are below.

## Before

Main, a film with an Intro clip that plays `compositions/intro.html`. The clip is selected and Enter is pressed: nothing happens, the preview still shows the whole 6 s film and there is no breadcrumb.

![Before: Enter on a selected section clip does nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/86cc34a3-7ce5-4e95-8c8d-afe0eb04eb1d)

## After

This branch, same film and key: Enter opens Intro, the preview shows the 3 s section, the timeline shows its own clips, and the breadcrumb reads "Master › intro".

![After: Enter opens the section with the breadcrumb](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bcc579d2-07eb-4200-b9e5-639100309277)

The breadcrumb in Studio's dark theme, before and after the token change:

![Breadcrumb before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7285739-54e4-4f31-9a0c-d02fdf92b9b2)
![Breadcrumb after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6dd1e633-7e3e-46f0-bbca-da5097f85768)

## What I measured

- Tokens (dark values): `border-neutral-800/50` → `border-border-strong/50` (same, #262626); `text-neutral-200` → `text-text-body` (same); `text-neutral-500` → `text-text-3` (#737373 → #71717a; 4.6:1 on a light host theme, where `text-text-muted` would be 2.5:1); `bg-neutral-900/50` → `bg-surface/50` (#171717 → #18181b); `text-neutral-400` → `text-text-2` and `text-neutral-600` → `text-text-4` (blue +9); `hover:bg-neutral-800` → `hover:bg-hover`; `hover:text-white` → `hover:text-text-0` (#fafafa, so it stays readable on a light host theme). The two breadcrumb crops look the same.
- Tests: Enter on a focused composition clip calls the drill-down with that element; Enter on a plain clip does not; Enter on an expandable row still toggles; Enter during a drag or trim, or with a modifier, opens nothing; double-click and Enter each open a section clip once, and the double-click that ends a drag or trim opens nothing; the package entry exports `useCompositionStack`, a host can hold the stack with it, and mounting it on a loaded film keeps the timeline; the breadcrumb carries no `neutral-` or `text-white` class; the tooltip names Enter. Each new test fails on main or on the first version of this branch; the drag guard and the wiring tests fail when the guard or the drill-down prop is removed.
- Each run alone: `useTimelineKeyboardActor.test.tsx` (12), `compositionStackExports.test.tsx` (3), `TimelineLanes` (19), `Timeline` (81), `TimelineClip` (9), `TimelineParts` (1), `TimelinePartsParity` (1), `timelineKeyboardNavigation` (12), `timelineEditing` (52), `useCompositionStack` (8). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit green.
- Captures: headless Chrome, Studio's dev server on main and on this branch, a fixture film with one section clip, keyboard focus on the clip and a real Enter key press.

## What I did NOT exercise

- After Enter opens a section, keyboard focus goes to the page, not the new level's timeline; one Tab brings it back. The timeline is replaced by its empty state while the section loads, so the focus has to be handed over by something that stays mounted.
- A host outside Studio using the exported stack.
- A host should pass `activeCompositionPath`, as Studio does. A host that leaves it out and remounts the hook while a section is open gets a stack of just Master while the timeline keeps the section's clips.

title: fix(core): a picked element's selector finds only that element
body:
## What this fixes

The element picker gives each picked element a CSS selector, used to find that element again in the live preview. It built the selector from the element alone, falling back to `tag:nth-of-type(n)` among its siblings. That is unique among siblings only, not in the page, so when two scenes shared an id, a track index or simply the same shape, the selector found the first scene's element instead of the one picked.

Now the picker returns the element's own selector only when it matches that element alone in the whole page. Otherwise it prefixes the parent's selector and takes a step that is unique among the parent's children, walking up until the path is unique. Tag names keep their letter case (SVG's `foreignObject`, `linearGradient`) and are escaped, so a script-built tag such as `x:y` no longer breaks the lookup.

The picker's consumers use the selector against the live page. The one that saves edits, Studio's `useElementPicker` (exported for apps that embed Studio), now also finds the element's source so that it names that element alone. Before, it patched by id first, so with a shared id an edit to the second scene's element was saved into the first file holding that id, changing the other scene's element while the preview showed the right one. Now, for an element with a `data-hf-id`:

- The file is the one it was served from if that file holds the hf-id, else the only file that holds it, else the only file that holds its id.
- In that file, it patches by the hf-id when exactly one tag carries it, else by the id when exactly one tag carries that. Markup copied by hand can leave two tags with one pinned hf-id; the id then tells them apart.
- When neither picks out one element, it saves nothing rather than change a different element. The live preview keeps the edit; the file does not get it.

An element without a `data-hf-id` still saves by its id, as before.

The source patcher also matched an attribute name at any word boundary, so `id="intro"` matched the end of `data-composition-id="intro"`, and `src=`, `class=` and `style=` matched the ends of `data-src=`, `data-class=` and `data-style=`. An edit by id could then land on the scene's wrapper instead of the element. Every attribute lookup in the patcher now requires the name to start the attribute, as the core timing compiler and lint already do.

Open question for the owner: when nothing picks out one element, the edit stays in the preview but is not saved, and the user is not told. The hook has no way to report it today.

## Before

Studio's own screens do not use `useElementPicker`, so there is no Studio screen to show. The captures are the reproduction run (two scenes sharing `id="dupe"`, the second one picked and restyled), against `main`'s hook: the edit is saved into `index.html`.

![Before: the edit is saved into index.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31ec6dda-1ba4-4664-8ef2-d43fa57c9f46)

## After

The same run against this branch's hook: the edit is saved into `compositions/second.html`.

![After: the edit is saved into compositions/second.html](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d5659a51-906e-4b0e-866c-a7de16b5401e)

## Tests

`picker.test.ts`:
- an element whose id or track index another scene shares gets a selector that finds only it;
- a shape in the second of two scenes that share it is picked in that scene;
- an element under an SVG `foreignObject` gets a selector that finds it;
- a script-built element whose tag needs escaping gets a selector that finds it.

`useElementPicker.test.ts`:
- with two files sharing `id="dupe"`, an edit to the element picked in the second scene is saved only into that scene's file;
- two tags in one file with the same pinned `data-hf-id` and different ids: the edit lands on the picked one;
- the hf-id and the id both repeated in one file: nothing is saved;
- the scene is unknown and the hf-id and id are in two files: nothing is saved (before, the first file got the edit);
- an element whose id equals its scene's `data-composition-id` is saved on the element, not the wrapper;
- an element with an id but no `data-hf-id` still saves by its id.

`sourcePatcher.test.ts`: a patch by id skips a tag whose `data-composition-id` has the same value; attributes are counted and read by their own name only; `src`, `class` and `style` are patched by their own names, not the `data-` ones.

Results: core and studio `tsc`, whole-tree `oxfmt --check` and `bun run lint`, fallow clean; the full studio suite (5660 tests) and core picker tests pass. `main`'s picker fails the first three picker tests; the unescaped tag fails the fourth; each save test fails on the previous hook, and each patcher test fails on the previous patcher.

title: fix(layout): flag text a clipping card cuts off
body:
## Summary

A short card with `overflow: hidden` could cut off heading text while the layout check passed. The check discarded text overflow whenever the ancestor clipped, and checking the card's direct child missed text overflowing a wrapper with `height: 100%`.

Report text overflow against the clipping card when a visible line extends beyond it. Use font ink bounds to exclude parked lines whose empty leading touches the window, and used line-height bounds to avoid treating the font's full ascent/descent as clipped display text. Convert font metrics into viewport coordinates so scaled cards retain the same decision. Non-clipping cards continue to report visible text outside their bounds, and intentional masks can opt out with `data-layout-allow-overflow`.

## Validation

- 191 tests pass, including 10 real Chromium cases: tight line heights, flush parked lines, empty-leading contact, actual cuts, scaled cuts, RTL and vertical text.
- Full `layout --json` runs pass with 0 errors for count-up, number-wheel, top-down-letters, slot-machine-roll, lt-mask-reveal and style-15-prod.
- A 160px clipping card with a label, two heading lines and a full-height inner wrapper reports `text_box_overflow` in Chrome.
- CLI typecheck, formatting, lint and fallow checks pass.

Run the Chromium tests by setting `PUPPETEER_EXECUTABLE_PATH` to an installed Chrome executable when invoking Vitest on `src/commands/layout-audit.chromium.test.ts`.

title: perf: the preview loads and decodes only the images of scenes on screen or due next
body: ## What Studio's preview keeps every scene of a composition in the page and hides the ones not on screen. Chrome still fetches and decodes the images inside those hidden scenes, at full size, so an idle preview holds every scene's pictures in memory. This PR makes Studio's preview fetch and decode only the images of the scene on screen and of scenes due within the next 2 s. A paused jump into a scene whose images are not decoded yet keeps the previous picture on screen until they are, then shows the new frame with its images. On the bench film (twelve 5 s scenes, each with a 1600x900 PNG plate, eight distinct files), an idle Studio drops from 606 to 554 MB of browser memory, and the images downloaded at open drop from 24.5 to 3.7 MB. **Scope: Studio's preview only.** Everything below switches on only in a document served by Studio's preview route. Render documents, the embedded `` and slideshow decks get none of it, and render output is byte-identical to main (Measured). ## Why - The runtime hides a timed clip with `visibility: hidden`. Chrome 152 decodes images under `visibility: hidden` (and `opacity: 0`) ahead of time at full size, so all eight plate files sat decoded in the renderer's image cache (83 MB, with the filmstrip's frames). An image with `display: none`, or a `loading="lazy"` image that is not laid out, is neither decoded nor fetched. - The preview document listed every scene's `` eagerly, so all eight PNGs downloaded at open. - Studio's play-readiness scan (`compositionReadiness.ts`, scope `"all"`) called `img.decode()` on every image in the composition, including later scenes', and waited for them. ## How - **Preview only** (`timedClipHide.ts`, `studioPreviewMark.ts`). The runtime installs the rules below only when the document carries ``, which Studio's preview route alone serves, at the start of `` (`routes/preview.ts`), before the runtime script runs. It is its own mark: the GSAP CDN fallback script keeps its `data-hf-gsap-fallback` attribute and no longer switches anything. Both sides read the name from one constant in core, and a studio-server test checks the served preview carries it. Nothing is authored or configured; a render or player document never has it. - **Captures get the unmarked document** (`routes/thumbnail.ts`, `routes/preview.ts`). Thumbnails, the filmstrip, composition cards, `PreviewPoster`, selection snapshots and "capture frame" all go through the thumbnail route, which builds the one URL both capture adapters load (CLI `studioServer.ts`, Vite `vite.browser.ts`). That URL now carries `?hf-capture=1`, and the preview route then serves the document without lazy images and without the mark, so a capture loads every image at parse and runs the runtime exactly as on main. The capture variant has its own ETag and in-memory build cache entry, and is never written to the CLI's on-disk preview store, so a thumbnail cannot evict the document a restarted server opens from. No other headless load of the preview route exists (every other `page.goto` in the repo opens its own file server). - **Skip rule.** In the preview, an image inside a timed clip the runtime has hidden gets `display: none`. The rule keys on the inline `visibility: hidden` the runtime writes, so anything that shows a clip (Studio's layer reveal sets `visibility: visible`) un-skips it with no extra wiring. It targets the images, not the clip: a first version put `content-visibility: hidden` on the clip, which also hid any child the author made `visibility: visible` inside a hidden clip. Main paints such a child, and so does this PR. - **Look-ahead.** On each visibility pass, a hidden clip that starts within the next 2 s, or is visible 2 s from now, gets `data-hf-upcoming`, which exempts it from the skip rule, so its images load and decode before the cut. A clip shorter than 2 s counts too. - **Before the first pass**, the preview's hide-until-first-pass rule (#4460) also takes lazy images out of layout, so hidden later scenes do not fetch theirs before the skip rule applies. - **Preview route** (`lazyPreviewImages.ts`, `routes/preview.ts`). Images inside a clip that starts after 0 are served with `loading="lazy" data-hf-preview-lazy`, inserted into the source text so nothing else in the document is re-encoded. An authored `loading` attribute in any letter case is kept, a start that is not a plain number keeps the image eager, and images on the first frame stay eager. The scanner that finds the `` content, as the DOM does; if its count still differs from the DOM's, the document is served unchanged. - **Paused jumps hold the previous picture** (`init.ts`, preview only). A paused seek first asks which images the target frame would reveal that the browser cannot paint yet: skipped with their clip, or still loading. If there are none, the seek applies at once, as before. Otherwise the runtime un-skips their clips, makes the images the route made lazy eager (an authored `loading` is never rewritten) and waits for `img.decode()` before applying the seek. A newer seek or a `renderSeek` drops a held seek; `play()` applies it first; `renderSeek` never holds; `getTime()` reports the held target. A held `seek()` returns a promise that settles once its images decode or the 1 s cap passes (by then it has applied, unless a newer seek or `play()` replaced it); one that applies at once returns nothing, as before. The hold joins the existing seek-completion barrier (`__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`). After 1 s the seek applies anyway and reports `runtime.init.seekHoldCap` through `swallow`. - **Studio follows the held seek.** A full-reload edit swaps in its shadow preview only after the restore seek has painted (`useShadowPreviewReload.ts`), and manual edits (size, rotation) are reapplied a second time only after a held player seek lands, through the promise that seek returned (`manualEdits.ts`). - **Copy/paste and Ask agent** (`authoredSource.ts`, `useClipboard.ts`, `useAskAgentModal.ts`). Both fall back to the live element's markup when its source markup is not found (Ask agent also while the source is still loading). That fallback now goes through one helper that drops `data-hf-upcoming`, and drops `loading` only from images the preview route made lazy, which it marks with the served-only `data-hf-preview-lazy`. An authored `loading`, in any value, reaches the agent and the pasted source unchanged; the route never marks or touches an image that already has one. The names come from the same core constants the runtime uses. - **Readiness** (`compositionReadiness.ts`). Scope `"all"` again covers every image, except a `loading="lazy"` image off the first frame: it loads only once shown, so no scope can wait on it (on main such an authored image stalled the scan until its 8 s timeout). In the preview, later scenes' images are served lazy, so Studio's play-readiness no longer waits on or decodes them. The player and the runtime already used the first-frame scope. ## Decisions A paused jump into a scene whose images are not decoded shows the full picture later than main: on a quiet 32-core Linux box (load under 15), 195 / 209 / 197 ms from the seek call against main's 174 / 149 / 135 ms, with no frame painted without the image on either (these were measured with the first version of the skip rule; the re-measure below, on a loaded box, again shows no imageless frame). The team chose to ship with this: a complete picture at about 200 ms beats 2-3 frames without the image at about 150 ms, and it keeps the idle-memory and open-time savings above. The hold is capped at 1 s. Captures are served the unmarked, eager document rather than waiting for visible images after the seek. That keeps capture behaviour identical to main with no new wait in the capture path, at the cost of one more cached preview build per project while captures run. The preview mark's names (`STUDIO_PREVIEW_MARK_META`, `STUDIO_PREVIEW_UPCOMING_ATTR`) have their own core subpath, `@hyperframes/core/studio-preview-mark`, so the preview route and Studio can read them without the compiler barrel that CLI tests mock wholesale. They are served-only marks for integrators, not something film authors write. Finding the images to mark uses core's existing comment- and quote-aware scanner (`compiler/htmlDocument.ts`), linear on any input; the lazy attributes are spliced in one pass. ## Measured Same film, Chrome 152 headless at 1600x900, an 8-core Linux box shared with other work (1-minute load at the start of each run in brackets, 18-45 during these runs, so timings are noisier than on an idle box). Main and this branch ran from two checkouts, interleaved round by round. Memory and bytes open Studio itself; memory is PSS per process type 60 s after open. Medians of 3 rounds. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | Browser memory, total (MB) | 606 (32.0 / 43.0 / 36.2) | 554 (20.0 / 38.7 / 46.7) | | Renderer (MB) | 324.8 | 291.5 | | Network service (MB) | 81.2 | 65.7 | | Renderer image cache (MB) | 83.4 | 45.0 | | Scene plates decoded | 8 / 8 / 8 | 1 / 1 / 1 | | PNG bytes downloaded at open (MB) | 24.5 (21.1 / 27.8 / 45.6) | 3.7 (24.2 / 44.3 / 51.5) | | All bytes downloaded at open (MB) | 44.0 | 26.8 | On a quiet 32-core box the same comparison measured 690 vs 617 MB total. The remaining image cache is the first scene's plate plus the filmstrip's frames. **Paused jump** from 0 to 32.5 s in the raw preview, screencast of the second after the seek call, each frame scored in the scene-image region against the picture before the jump and the settled picture 1 s later: | | main (32.1 / 27.7 / 38.5) | this PR (21.5 / 40.7 / 46.9) | |---|---|---| | Frames painted without the full image | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 | | Seek call to the full picture on screen | 835 / 314 / 464 ms | 766 / 867 / 389 ms | At this load both builds take several hundred ms and the spread swamps the difference; the Decisions numbers come from the quiet box. On this branch the frames before the full picture show the previous scene unchanged. Headless screencast frames arrive about every 58 ms, so the timings are that coarse. **Playback 0 -> 60 s, every cut**, raw preview, one round each: no frame showed a scene before its image loaded on either build; longest frame gap in the 200 ms after a cut, median / max, 133 / 383 ms on main (load 50.0) and 100 / 283 ms on this branch (load 57.1). **Render parity.** `hyperframes render --workers 2` from main and from this branch produce byte-identical MP4s for the bench film, `overlay-montage-prod` and `heygen-promo-preview-assets`, and for three compositions that broke on an earlier version of this branch: an authored lazy image in a clip behind a chunk boundary (also at `--workers 1`), a script that measures a lazy image at setup and feeds the width into a tween, and a `visibility: visible` child inside a hidden clip. Under heavy load `heygen-promo-preview-assets` and the bench film render differently from run to run on main itself; the bench film pair above matched at a load around 25 (0 of 1800 frames differ). **Studio captures.** Real Chrome, the built CLI Studio server, a 1600x900 PNG in a 5-10 s scene served from a second server with delayed responses, captured at 6 s through the thumbnail route (fresh page per capture), two runs per delay: | Image delay | before this fix | after | |---|---|---| | 0 / 150 ms | image | image | | 300 / 400 ms | black: scene shown, image not loaded | image | **Render parity after these changes.** With main merged in, `overlay-montage-prod` rendered with `--workers 2` from this branch and from main's head (b165b64ed, same checkout with main's tree restored and rebuilt) gives the same MP4 md5 (`af2e1d0a...`). Load at start about 15. ## Known limits - **A paused jump into a scene whose images are not decoded** shows the previous picture a little longer than main (Decisions). - **In the preview only, a script that measures a later scene's image** while its clip is hidden and not yet due reads a zero size, because the image is out of layout until then. Rendering is not affected. - Seeks while playing never hold, so a jump during playback into a skipped scene can still paint frames without the image. - Backward cuts into a skipped scene also hold for one image load while the playhead moves on (by design): reverse shuttle issues a paused seek per frame and the look-ahead only looks forward. - Images inside `
