title: fix(studio): read and write a clip's in-point the way playback does
body:
## What users saw

On a video or audio clip that keeps its in-point in `data-playback-start`, typing a new "Media start" in the Design panel changed the number in the panel and nothing else. The preview kept playing from the old point, and the saved file kept the old value. The edit had gone into `data-media-start`, which playback ignores whenever `data-playback-start` is there.

The same disagreement showed up in three quieter places:

- Splitting a clip with an unusual in-point gave the right half the wrong start. For example, a clip with `data-playback-start="-1" data-media-start="2"`, split at 2 s, gave the right half an in-point of 1 instead of 4.
- "Even Out Levels" measured the audio from the wrong point on such a clip, so its corrections landed early.
- Dragging a clip's head fully right, when the clip's start or end was off the 10 ms grid, could shrink it to 0.09 s, under the 0.1 s minimum. This happened for single clips and for group drags.

## Why

Playback has one rule for reading an in-point: `data-playback-start` first, then `data-media-start`, and a negative or unreadable value falls through to the next one (or to 0). The Studio timeline already uses that rule. The property panels, audio levelling, the server-side split and one fallback in the resize save each read it their own way: `media-start` first, `parseFloat` (so `"1.5s"` read as 1.5 and `-1` stayed -1), or no fall-through. The panels also always wrote `media-start`.

## The fix

One owner decides how an in-point is read: playback's own reader. Everything else now goes through it.

- **Reading.** A small helper next to the timeline's reader returns the in-point as playback reads it, plus the attribute that holds it. The timeline store, both media panels, audio levelling and the resize fallback all use it. The server split calls playback's reader directly, and playback's rate reader for the speed.
- **Writing.** A panel edit now goes to the attribute the clip already uses. The panels reuse the timeline's own rule for this, so a clip with neither attribute still gets `data-media-start`, as timeline edits do. The resize fallback writes to the attribute it found in the file, not the one in a possibly stale store entry. The split keeps each half's attribute name and rewrites a value only when it differs from what playback reads.
- **Speed.** The timeline's speed clamp is now playback's own (`clampPlaybackRate`), and the resize fallback uses it instead of its own copy. The speeds Studio reads are already inside those bounds, so nothing changes for them.
- **The 0.09 s clip.** The furthest right a head drag can reach is rounded down onto the 10 ms grid, so the clip keeps its minimum length. Both drags share that limit. A group drag also rounds the shared move; when that rounding would pass the tightest member's limit, the move stops exactly at the limit, and every member still moves by the same amount. In a sweep of 402,201 clips (starts 0 to 2 s on a 1 ms grid, lengths 0.1 to 0.3 s, head dragged fully right), no group drag ends under 0.1 s or before zero. Before this change, 3,640 group drags in a similar sweep ended under 0.1 s. In 262 of the 402,201 cases the group drag still stops 10 ms before the single-clip drag does, never past it.

## Tests

Each test below fails with the fix removed. To prove it, I put that file back to main, ran the test, then restored the file.

| Fix | Test | Output with the fix removed |
|---|---|---|
| Split | `sourceMutationSplitAndGroup.test.ts`: "splits … where playback reads it", 5 cases, each half read back with playback's reader | 4 of 5 fail, e.g. `data-media-start="1.5s"`: `expected [ +0, 3.5 ] to deeply equal [ +0, 2 ]`; `data-playback-start="abc" data-media-start="2"`: `expected [ +0, 2 ] to deeply equal [ 2, 4 ]` |
| Panel | `propertyPanelFlatMediaSection.test.tsx`: "shows and edits the in-point playback reads", 4 cases | `{ playback-start: 1, media-start: 5 }`: `expected '5.00s' to be '1.00s'` |
| Levelling | `propertyPanelAudioFxGroup.test.tsx`: "levels the part of the file the clip plays", now on a clip with `playback-start="2" media-start="0"` | `expected 0 to be greater than 4` |
| Resize fallback | `timelineEditingHelpers.test.ts`: "source in-point read as playback reads it", 4 cases | all 4 fail, e.g. `data-playback-start="2"`: `expected 2 to be 1.5`; `data-media-start="1.5s"`: `expected 2 to be 0.5` |
| 0.09 s clip | `timelineEditing.test.ts`: "keeps the minimum duration when a head trim runs off the grid" (start 1 / length 0.625, and start 1.005 / length 2; single clip and group) and a 360-clip sweep of off-grid starts and lengths | `expected 0.09 to be greater than or equal to 0.1`; sweep: `expected [ '1.065+0.1', '1.065+0.117', …(8) ] to deeply equal []` |
| Group drag limit | `timelineEditing.test.ts`: "stops a group head trim where the single-clip trim stops" (start 1.003 / length 2) and "never moves a group head trim left of zero near the minimum length" (start 0.004 / length 0.1) | with the grid floor put back on the limit: `expected 0.11 to be 0.1`; `expected -0.01 to be greater than or equal to 0` |
| Group moves together | `timelineEditing.test.ts`: "moves on-grid group members together when the tightest member sits 5 ms off the grid" | with the exact limit returned: `expected [ 2.9, 1.9, 2.13 ] to deeply equal [ 2.9, 1.89, 2.13 ]` |
| Old Design panel | `propertyPanelFlatMediaSection.test.tsx`: "the Design panel's Media start slider writes where playback reads" | with the write forced to `media-start`: `expected 1 to be 3` |

The reviews also asked for a test of how the timeline itself reads a bad `playback-start` that falls through to `media-start`, junk that reads as 0, and `"1.5s"`, which playback reads as 0 and Studio now does too. These are in `timelineDOM.test.ts`. They pass on main too, because the timeline reader was already fixed. They are there to keep it that way.

The other studio tests in the touched areas pass: timeline editing, group editing, drag preview, DOM parsing, both panels and levelling. So do the split tests. Studio and studio-server typecheck clean.

## Before

A clip with `data-playback-start="1"`. I type 6 into "Media start". The panel says 6.00 s, but the preview still shows the 1 s frame. The saved file keeps `data-playback-start="1"` and gains a `data-media-start="6.00"` that playback ignores.

![Before: panel says 6.00 s, preview still shows the 1 s frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/143e2139-c36f-40e3-872c-b43cf95907de)
![Before: saved source still has data-playback-start="1"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d6e037d4-9296-4880-8f2d-7ec11a10967e)

## After

Same clip, same edit. The preview jumps to the 6 s frame, and the saved file has `data-playback-start="6.00"`.

![After: preview shows the 6 s frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97b15882-cb0f-4f6e-8c5b-ebaa8d6c1f31)
![After: saved source has data-playback-start="6.00"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a0f9c212-7284-4ff7-9647-41234dab33f1)

## Not verified

- Levelling was only checked by the unit test, not by ear in Studio.
- The split, the resize fallback and group head drags were only checked by unit tests and the sweep, not driven in Studio.
- Captures were taken in headless Chrome on Linux only.
- I did not run the full studio or studio-server test suites; CI does.

title: test(producer): run the late-host pip and dogs-captions fixtures in CI
body:
## What

- Marks the picture-in-picture video in the `pip-video-late-host` fixture as root-global with `data-hf-media-start-basis="global"`.
- Schedules `pip-video-late-host` and `dogs-captions` in `packages/producer/tests/shard-schedule.json`, moving them from `excluded` to `timings`. They had never run in CI.
  - `pip-video-late-host` runs on every PR.
  - `dogs-captions` runs in a new nightly regression run, because on its own it takes longer than the rest of the check.

## Why

On main, `pip-video-late-host` renders the empty host instead of the video. The render log shows `videoCount 0`, and frames 74 to 143 are dark where the baseline shows the video. Nothing caught it because the fixture was on the "never run in CI" list.

A first-parent bisect from the baseline's last update (100d355e) to a bad main commit points to three changes:

- **#3342** (first bad commit) moved media collection onto the inlined document. The fixture's video is authored at `data-start="3"` in root time, inside a host at 3s. The new collector reads every nested media start as local (3 + 3 = 6). The old path only worked by accident: a second pass read the raw `3` and the two lists were merged. From #3342 on, the clip sat at 6 to 9s, past the 6s film. Frame extraction captured 0 of 72 frames, and the coverage guard aborted the render.
- **#3732** made "nested media time is local by default" the contract. A root-time start now has to opt in with `data-hf-media-start-basis="global"`, and the runtime's guess that a start inside the host's window meant root time was removed.
- **#3975** bounded nested media by the host's `data-duration`. The clip's start (6s) is now at or past the host's end (6s), so it is dropped entirely. The count went to `videoCount 0` and the guard no longer fires, so the render is silently wrong.

This fixture was written before #3732 and encodes the old guess. Under the current contract, a root-time start needs the marker. This PR keeps #3732's contract and adds the marker, which is the fixture's original intent: a legacy root-global picture-in-picture. A companion PR makes the silent drop visible in the render log and in lint.

`dogs-captions` has no timing problem and passes as it is. It was only unscheduled.

## How

- `pip.html`: one attribute on `#pip-video`, plus a shorter comment saying why.
- `shard-schedule.json`: both fixtures removed from `excluded` and added to `timings`.
  - `pip-video-late-host`: about 35s, estimated from a local Dockerfile.test run scaled by a calibration fixture (`style-9-prod`: 71s in CI, about 100s locally).
  - `dogs-captions`: 524s, the median of its render step in this PR's first two CI runs (629s and 419s).
  - A new `nightly` map, shaped like `distributed` (fixture name to reason), lists `dogs-captions`. A nightly fixture must also be in `timings`, the same check `distributed` has.
- `plan-regression-shards.mjs`: `planShards({ nightly })` leaves `nightly` fixtures out unless asked; the CLI flag is `--nightly`.
- `regression.yml`: a daily `schedule` run at 06:17 UTC plans with `--nightly`, so it runs every fixture including `dogs-captions`.
  - On that run the change filter is skipped and the regression is forced on, since there is no diff to filter.
  - Its concurrency group gets a `-nightly` suffix, so it and a push-to-main run on the same ref do not cancel each other.
  - GitHub emails a failed scheduled run only to whoever last edited the cron line, and a red nightly run blocks nothing.
- shardCount stays at 9. Without `dogs-captions`, the planner spreads the per-PR fixtures across nine shards.

Real per-shard times from CI. Runner speed swings by 3 to 4 minutes between runs, so the cost of `dogs-captions` is measured inside each run, against that run's slowest other shard:

| Run | dogs-captions shard (rendering) | slowest other shard | dogs-captions cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| 41e97d6d, run 1 | 14m13s (10m29s) | 12m33s | +1m40s |
| 41e97d6d, run 2 | 10m47s (6m59s) | 10m27s | +20s |
| cc53c936, nightly (per-PR run) | not run | 9m42s | none |

For scale, recent 8-shard runs of the same check without `dogs-captions` had slowest shards of 11m12s, 14m37s and 15m31s.

`dogs-captions` was the slowest shard in both runs, and one fixture cannot be split across shards, so it sets the check's wall time whenever it runs. It runs nightly instead. Making the fixture fast enough to return to every PR is a separate change.

## Known limits

- The nightly set cannot be started by hand: a manual run plans without `--nightly`, so checking a `dogs-captions` change in CI means waiting for the next nightly run.

## Test plan

- [x] Dockerfile.test image built from this branch; each fixture run the way the CI shard runs it:
  - `pip-video-late-host`: PASSED, `videoCount 1`, 0 failed frames (threshold 5).
  - `dogs-captions`: PASSED, `videoCount 1`, 0 failed frames (threshold 0), audio correlation 0.962, stream duration parity passed.
- [x] Before the change, on a bad main commit: `pip-video-late-host` FAILED, `videoCount 0`, frame 100 PSNR 7.1 against the baseline.
- [x] `bun test src/regression-shard-plan.test.ts`: 21 pass, 0 fail.
  - New: the per-PR plan leaves `dogs-captions` out and the nightly plan includes it. Fails when the planner ignores `nightly`.
  - New: a `nightly` entry that is not in `timings` is rejected. Fails when that check is removed.
  - New: every `nightly` entry has a written reason.
  - The two "every runnable fixture is scheduled" tests now check the nightly plan, so a fixture in `nightly` still counts as covered.
- [x] `plan-regression-shards.mjs --pretty`: nine in-process shards of about 5 min each, plus the distributed shard, and no `dogs-captions`. With `--nightly`, `dogs-captions` gets its own shard (about 10.5 min).
- [x] `actionlint` passes on `regression.yml`. `tsc --noEmit` passes for `packages/producer`.
- [x] No change under `packages/studio` or `packages/player`, so no before/after captures are needed.

title: fix(studio): the live clip list carries mute, volume and sound, and refreshes on change
body:
## What changes for a user

Studio's live clip list (what the timeline and any host app reading the player store see) now says whether each clip is muted, at what volume, and whether it has sound to mix, and it refreshes when only one of those changes. A clip is heard when it has sound (`hasAudio`, or it is an audio clip), is not `muted`, not `hidden`, its audio group is not hidden, and its volume (and its group's volume) is not 0; every one of those inputs is now in the list. `hasAudio` alone does not mean heard. Before, a clip that was muted, unmuted, turned to volume 0, sped up or hidden, with no timing change, kept its old values until the next timing edit or a reopen, and the list built from the runtime's clip manifest never carried `data-volume` at all.

## How

- **One place reads what a clip plays** (`packages/studio/src/player/lib/timelineElementHelpers.ts`, `applyAudioMetadataFromElement`). Both ways of building a clip (the runtime's manifest and the DOM fallback parser) already went through it. It now sets `muted` (the authored `muted` attribute on the clip or its media), `volume` (`data-volume`) and `hasAudio`. `hasAudio` follows the compiler's rule (`packages/core/src/compiler/timingCompiler.ts:277-278`): `data-has-audio` when present, otherwise a video has sound unless it is muted, and only the clip element itself counts (a timed wrapper does not take the sound of a video inside it). The DOM fallback's own `data-volume` read is gone.
- **The refresh check sees them** (`packages/studio/src/player/hooks/timelinePlayerSync.ts`): `timelineElementsChanged` now compares one list of fields, adding muted, hasAudio, volume, playback rate, hidden, the clip's audio group volume and hidden, and its fades. It compared only id, timing, track and source length, so a list that differed only in these fields was dropped.
- `TimelineElement` gains `muted`.

## Before

![main: opened](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab1ed1fe-d852-4832-be8a-0e36e95b5b5f)
![main: after muting plain at volume 0, unchanged after 45 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6d2775c-cf0b-4fd7-b8be-57de532f3c97)
![main: after restoring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa2a4f59-2a07-4de0-bc19-d19c1e2f4c6b)

main. A two-clip project in Studio: `plain` (no `muted`, no `data-has-audio`) and `quiet` (`muted`). The panel in the corner is drawn by the capture script from Studio's live clip list. Then the project file is saved with `muted data-volume="0"` added to `plain`: after 45 s the list still says `plain` is unmuted, has sound, and has no volume, and it never carries `muted` for `quiet`.

## After

![fix: opened](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48fa0093-d821-42d4-8b5a-e7482fa5bafc)
![fix: after muting plain at volume 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49615180-174e-4c4c-a987-39f328fc3c94)
![fix: after restoring](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/583e4038-19b8-4117-bd83-8f0daaa6a5d5)

This branch, same project and steps: the list reads `quiet` as muted, picks up `plain`'s save (muted, no sound, volume 0) within the wait, and goes back when the file is restored.

## What I measured

- The walk above, run on main and on this branch in headless Chromium against Studio's dev server, reading `window.__playerStore` after each file save.
- Tests: the 14 new tests (9 in `timelinePlayerSync.test.ts`, one per field of the refresh check; 5 in `timelineDOM.test.ts` for volume, muted, the compiler's has-audio rule, a timed wrapper around a video with and without `data-has-audio`, and the clip-edge fades on the manifest path) fail on main or with their rule removed. `timelineDOM.test.ts` and `useTimelinePlayer.test.ts` and `timelinePlayerSync.test.ts`: 74 passed with `TimelineClipFades.test.tsx`. The whole `packages/studio` suite: 5777 passed; one test (`vite.adapter.projects.test.ts`, catalog install answer) failed under a loaded full run and passes on its own (18/18).
- `bun run build`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, the comment ratchet and the comment-citation check: all exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The preview serves compiled HTML, so `data-has-audio` is already on every video there; the compiler rule in Studio matters where a clip reaches the list without it (a page that was not compiled). On main `plain` already read `hasAudio` true in the walk for that reason.
- A clip with neither `muted` nor `data-has-audio` now takes audio affordances (fades) in the timeline wherever the attribute is missing, as the render already mixes its sound.
- A live DOM edit that does not save the file (and so does not reload the preview) was not walked; the runtime re-posts its clip list on timing and `src` changes, and Studio re-syncs on each preview reload.
- A host app's own consumer of the list (for example a words panel) was not run; only Studio's store was read.

title: feat(core): export findProjects to list the HyperFrames projects on a machine
body:
## What

`@hyperframes/core/projects` finds every HyperFrames project under a folder, streaming each one as soon as it is found. It is a Node-only subpath:

```ts
import { findProjects } from "@hyperframes/core/projects";

const search = new AbortController();
const count = await findProjects({
  onProject: (project) => list.add(project),
  signal: search.signal,
});
```

Each project arrives as `{ path, name, source, mtime }`, for example:

```
{"path":"/Users/me/Videos/launch-film","name":"launch-film","source":"walk","mtime":"2026-09-28T01:28:31.339Z"}
```

- `root` defaults to the home folder.
- `onProject` is called with each project as it is found; the promise resolves with the count once the search is done.
- Aborting `signal` stops the search: no `onProject` call after it fires, no new walk reads (reads already started finish), a running Spotlight query is killed, and the promise rejects with the signal's reason (an `AbortError` by default). A signal that is already aborted rejects before anything is read.
- A root that is missing, not a folder or unreadable rejects with the file system error (for example `ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR`, `EACCES`, or `EPERM` for a macOS privacy-protected folder) before anything is searched, so no caller mistakes it for "no projects". Folders below the root that cannot be read are skipped.
- Paths are real paths: under a symlinked root they start with the link's target.
- If `onProject` throws, the search stops with no further `onProject` call and the promise rejects with that error; a running Spotlight query then finishes in the background and its hits are ignored.
- No async iterator: the callback already streams, and an iterator would add a buffering queue.

There is no CLI command; the functions are the whole surface. Studio only lists the projects in its own data folder and never searches the disk, so it has no caller to switch.

**One project rule.** A folder is a HyperFrames project when it holds `index.html` plus one of `hyperframes.json` or `meta.json` (written by `hyperframes init`) or `project.json`. That rule now lives once, in `@hyperframes/core` as `isHyperframesProject(fileNames)` and `PROJECT_MARKER_FILES` (also exported from `@hyperframes/core/projects`). The search uses it, and other tools can import it instead of keeping their own copy.

**How it searches.**
- A walk of the root with up to 64 folder reads at a time. It skips hidden folders, `node_modules` and `~/Library`, does not follow symlinks (so a symlink loop cannot trap it), skips unreadable folders, and does not look inside a project once it finds one.
- It also skips git worktree copies: a folder whose `.git` is a file pointing into another repo's `.git/worktrees/`. A git submodule also has a `.git` file, but not one under `worktrees/`, so submodules are still searched. On a developer machine this pruning is most of the speed: most folders under `~` can be worktree copies.
- On macOS, Spotlight is asked in parallel for the three marker names. A hit counts only where the walk would also have counted it, so both sources agree, and each project is reported once (by its real path) under whichever source found it first. The root is resolved to its real path first, since Spotlight reports real paths.
- Nothing new is added to projects; detection reads what they already contain. No new dependency.

## Measured

On a Mac with a busy home folder (checkouts, worktrees, downloads), idle, the same search over the home folder, run through a bundled build of an earlier command form of this branch (so the totals include process startup), three runs in a row:

| Run | First project | Total | Found |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0.13 s | 2.14 s | 661 |
| 2 | 0.10 s | 1.10 s | 661 |
| 3 | 0.10 s | 1.04 s | 661 |

The walk usually wins the race to the first project; Spotlight reported about 230 of the 661 first. Of the projects found, one was a false positive: a web app with an `index.html` and a `project.json` of its own. All the others have a `data-composition-id` in their `index.html`. The Spotlight path has no test of its own that proves it reports anything first (the walk races it in any test); these runs are its evidence.

Re-measured through the `@hyperframes/core/projects` entry while the same Mac was under heavy load (load average 35 to 49), interleaved with a minimal reference walk: first project 0.01 to 0.6 s, total 2 to 23 s, against 3 to 19 s for the reference, all swinging with the load.

On a Linux build server (walk only, no Spotlight) it finds 670 projects; the walk there takes 44 s warm under load, because that home folder holds dozens of full repository clones and their build output.

Known misses, by design: projects reached only through a symlink, inside hidden folders, inside git worktree copies (including every checkout of a bare-repo-plus-worktrees layout), or nested inside another project. A hung network mount under the root can stall the walk and keep the promise from settling, aborted or not.

## Tests

- `isHyperframesProject`: each marker counts next to `index.html`; `index.html` alone, or a marker alone, does not.
- `findProjects`: finds a project and nothing else; skips `node_modules` and hidden folders; skips a git worktree copy but searches a submodule; does not look inside a project; searches a root that is itself a worktree copy; finishes past a symlink loop and an unreadable folder; reports a Spotlight hit once, and only where the walk would also count it. Each rule's test fails with that rule removed.
- `findProjects`: skips `Library` in the home folder but not a folder named `Library` elsewhere.
- `findProjects`: rejects a root that is missing, not a folder, or unreadable instead of finding nothing.
- `findProjects`: searches the home folder when no root is given; stops reporting and rejects once its signal is aborted mid-search; rejects before reading anything when the signal is already aborted; stops the search when `onProject` throws. That the walk also stops reading folders after a stop is not observable without mocking the file system, so no test pins it.
- The tests build their folders under the real temp path, so they pass under a symlinked temp folder (as on macOS, where `/var` links to `/private/var`), and they run on the Windows lane.

title: feat(studio): let a host app mount the timeline toolbar, undo buttons, meters and clipboard
body:
## What a host can now do

An app that embeds Studio's timeline outside Studio's own shell can now mount the timeline's toolbar, the undo and redo buttons, the audio meter strip and the clip clipboard from `@hyperframes/studio`, and feed them its own history and preview. Before this change none of them were exported, and the toolbar, the buttons and the meters threw as soon as they rendered without Studio's shell around them.

Studio itself is unchanged. Every new prop is optional, and with no props each piece reads the shell exactly as before. Studio's own call sites are untouched.

## Exports and props

New exports from the package entry:

```ts
import {
  TimelineToolbar,
  type TimelineToolbarProps,
  TimelineHistoryButtons,
  type TimelineHistoryButtonsProps,
  AudioMeterStrip,
  type AudioMeterStripProps,
  useClipboard,
  type UseClipboardOptions,
} from "@hyperframes/studio";
```

- `TimelineToolbar`
  - `history?: TimelineHistoryButtonsProps` is passed to its undo and redo buttons.
  - `showAddBeat?: boolean` (default `true`). A host passes `false` to leave out "Add beat": beat edits are undone only through Studio's own app-level history, which a host's undo cannot reach.
- `TimelineHistoryButtons`: `canUndo`, `canRedo`, `undoLabel`, `redoLabel`, `onUndo` and `onRedo`, all optional. Each prop wins over the matching shell value.
  - It now reads the shell with `useStudioShellContextOptional()`, so it no longer throws without one.
  - With no props and no shell, both buttons render disabled.
  - A button is enabled only when it has a handler to call.
- `AudioMeterStrip`: `previewIframeRef?`, which wins over the shell's preview iframe. With neither, the strip renders and shows silence. Pass a stable ref (`useRef`): a new object on each render restarts the meter loop.
- `useClipboard` and `UseClipboardOptions`: exported as they are. A host with no DOM edit session passes `{ current: null }` as `domEditSelectionRef`, and copy, cut and duplicate then act on the timeline selection.

## For embedders

- Mounting `TimelineToolbar` adds a window-wide keydown listener: `N` toggles timeline snapping. A host that already binds `N` should drop its own binding, or one press toggles twice.
- Undo and Redo send Studio's `studio:toolbar_action` telemetry event. It follows Studio's telemetry policy: nothing is sent when the user opted out, Do Not Track is on, `VITE_HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY` is set or the build is a dev build.

## Tests

- `timelineChromeExports.test.tsx` imports all four by package name and mounts them with no `StudioShellProvider`, the way a host does. It checks that the toolbar calls the host's undo and leaves out Add beat, that the bare history buttons are disabled, that the meter strip renders, and that the clipboard runs with a null DOM selection ref.
- `TimelineHistoryButtons.dom.test.tsx` checks that host props win over the shell, labels included, and that a button with no handler stays disabled even when `canUndo` or `canRedo` is `true`. The existing tests still cover the shell path Studio uses.
- `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx` checks that Add beat shows by default, as Studio relies on. The exports test covers `showAddBeat={false}`.
- `AudioMeterStrip.test.tsx` checks that a host's preview iframe wins over the shell's, and that the strip mounts with neither. The existing tests still cover the shell path.
- `useClipboard.source.test.ts` checks that with no DOM edit session the hook refuses copy, cut and duplicate when nothing is selected, and deletes nothing.
- Four existing tests (toolbar, pointer target size, history buttons, meter strip) mocked `useStudioShellContext`. They now mock `useStudioShellContextOptional` instead.

Each new test fails without its change. I broke the code, ran the file and restored it each time:

| Break | Result |
|---|---|
| Main's `TimelineHistoryButtons` (throwing shell read) | exports test: `Error: useStudioShellContext must be used within StudioShellProvider` (toolbar and buttons) |
| Main's shell read in `AudioMeterStrip` | exports test: `Error: useStudioShellContext must be used within StudioShellProvider` (meter strip) |
| The four exports removed from `index.ts` | exports test, 4 failed: `Element type is invalid: expected a string ... but got: undefined` |
| Shell values put ahead of host props in the history buttons | `takes a host's history props over the shell's`: `expected false to be true` |
| Shell label put ahead of the host's redo label | `takes a host's history props over the shell's`: `expected 'Redo shell move (Ctrl+Shift+Z)' to contain 'Redo host trim'` |
| A button enabled without a handler (`Boolean(onClick) &&` removed) | `keeps a button disabled when it has no handler ...`: `expected false to be true` |
| Shell fallback removed from the history buttons | `calls handleUndo once ...`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` |
| Toolbar stops passing `history` through | exports test, `mounts the toolbar with the host's history ...`: `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times` |
| `showAddBeat` ignored | exports test, `mounts the toolbar with the host's history ...`: `expected <button ...> to be null` |
| `showAddBeat` default flipped to `false` | `shows Add beat by default ...`: `expected null not to be null` |
| Shell iframe put ahead of the host's in the meter strip | `reads a host's preview iframe over the shell's` fails |
| Shell fallback removed from the meter strip | the two existing preview-window tests fail |
| Clipboard treats a null DOM selection ref as a selection | `refuses copy, cut and duplicate when nothing is selected` fails |

The last row checks existing behaviour: `useClipboard` needed no code change to work with a null ref, so that test only locks in what it already does.

Run: the six test files above, plus EditorShell, StudioHeader, the timeline edit callbacks and the existing export tests (15 files, all green). `bun run format:check`, `bun run lint`, `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio, the comment ratchet and `fallow audit --base origin/main` all pass.

## Before

A host page that mounts the toolbar, the undo and redo buttons and the meter strip with no Studio shell around them. On main each one throws.

![Host page on main: each component throws](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/467ffc9e-544d-412c-a7fa-520647902975)

## After

The same page on this branch. The toolbar calls the host's undo and has no Add beat, the bare undo and redo buttons are disabled, and the meter strip renders on the host's preview iframe.

![Host page on this branch: all three render](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1615f45-3aca-469c-9104-1e3db918307e)

## Studio, unchanged

Studio at 1440x900 with a generated fixture project, on main and on this branch. The two are identical by design: the timeline toolbar, the undo and redo buttons and the meter strip are pixel-identical. The only differing pixels are clip and composition thumbnails, which load lazily and had not all arrived when the shot was taken.

![Studio on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9afe1efa-8a59-41c5-8752-3614a5aba25d)

![Studio on this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dbfc2d87-fe95-4747-8e15-fa9d4d0cc9b7)

## Not verified

- No real embedding host has mounted these yet. The host page above is a throwaway harness, and the host case is otherwise covered only by unit tests.
- Undo, redo and paste were not clicked in a running Studio. Studio's path is covered by the existing tests and the unchanged captures.
- The full Studio suite was not run locally; CI runs it.

The timeline edit provider's memo, which leaves `onResizeElements` out of its dependencies, ships as its own PR.

title: fix(studio): a host that swaps its multi-clip trim handler gets the new one
body:
## What changes for a user

An app that wraps the timeline in the exported `TimelineEditProvider` with its own callbacks, and later swaps only its multi-clip trim handler (`onResizeElements`), now has the new handler called. Before, the timeline kept calling the first one it saw, so a multi-clip trim could run against old state. The same happened when an app passed `onResizeElements` as a prop and later cleared it: the timeline fell back to the stale copy in context.

A handler passed as a prop to `Timeline` already won over the context copy, so that path was fine. Inside Studio nothing changes today: Studio's multi-clip move and trim handlers always change together, so the cached bag already refreshed.

## Why it happened

`TimelineEditProvider` caches the callback bag so consumers do not re-render when unrelated parent state changes. The cache's dependency list was written out by hand, and `onResizeElements` was never added to it when that callback was introduced.

## The fix

The dependency list now comes from a `Record<keyof TimelineEditCallbacks, true>`. TypeScript refuses that record when a key of the callback type is missing, so a callback added later cannot be left out of the cache again. Removing `onResizeElements` from it gives `TS2741: Property 'onResizeElements' is missing`.

## Tests

`TimelineEditContext.test.tsx` (new):
- "hands consumers the latest multi-clip resize callback" fails on main's provider: `expected [Function Mock] to be [Function Mock] // Object.is equality`.
- "keeps the same bag when the parent passes the same callbacks in a new object" passes on both, so the cache still does its job.

Studio typecheck, lint, format check, and the timeline provider and editor pane tests (151) pass.

## Before

![Before: on main the regression test fails, the provider keeps the old handler](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d43830d7-769d-49a1-bf6a-4145abf3d42f)

## After

![After: the provider hands out the handler passed last](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5f3a6cc-90ea-4f92-9cf9-c24ddb5e8327)

The change has no visual effect, so both captures show the regression test's run: failing on main, passing with the fix.

title: fix(studio-server): undo keeps an outside change even when Studio's history claim arrives late
feat(cli): tag telemetry and feedback with the app that launched the CLI
body:
## What

An app that launches the CLI can set `HYPERFRAMES_CLIENT=<app>/<version>/<channel>`. The CLI now carries that tag:

- as `client` on every CLI telemetry event, `cli_render_feedback` and `cli_catalog_search_miss` included;
- as `client=...` in the feedback env string that rides with a `hyperframes feedback` report.

Run from a shell, nothing changes: the variable is unset and no `client` property is sent.

## How

`getSystemMeta()` reads the variable once, into a new `client` field. Two places use it:

- `trackEvent`, the one place that adds the common properties to every event;
- `getDoctorSummary`, the only producer of the feedback env string.

Opt-out still wins, because `trackEvent` returns at `shouldTrack()` before it reads anything. No consent behaviour changes.

The value is kept only when it is a short slash-separated slug, which gives a 131-character maximum. The feedback env string is space-delimited `k=v`, so a stray space or newline would corrupt it, and a long value would push the report's join keys past its 500-character cap.

## Docs

The telemetry and feedback docs said environment variable values are never collected. That was already inaccurate: `agent_hint` and `term_program` send short, filtered values of `AGENT`, `AI_AGENT` and `TERM_PROGRAM`. The three disclosures now name those three and the new tag.

## Tests

Each new test fails with the three source files reverted to main (7 failures) and passes with this change:

- `system.test.ts`: the tag is read from the env; unset gives `null`; a value with a space, a newline or an over-long segment is dropped.
