title: fix(lint): warn when a clip ends past the root composition duration
body:
## What this adds

Since #4530 a film stops at its root composition's declared `data-duration`. A clip that ends past it is cut from previews, posters, catalog tiles and renders, with no message. An agent that adds a clip at the end of a film without extending the root length gets a silently shorter video.

`hyperframes lint` (and `check`, which runs the same linter) now warns about it:

```
⚠ clip_ends_past_root_duration [outro]: <div id="outro"> runs from 8s to 12.5s, past the root composition's data-duration of 10s, so it is cut off in previews, posters and renders.
  Fix: Extend the root data-duration to 12.5, or make <div id="outro"> end at or before 10s.
```

- It checks the root's own clips. A sub-composition counts by its host clip, the same way Studio measures a film's content.
- A clip's end is its start plus its written length (`data-duration`, or the older `data-end`), read with the parsers' existing timing readers. A clip may run up to 50 ms past the root, the same allowance the existing timing-mismatch detector uses; both now read one constant, `TIMING_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`, in the parsers package.
- It is a warning: it does not block renders, like the other timing rules.
- The hyperframes-core skill now tells agents to extend the root `data-duration` in the same edit when they add a clip past it.

## What I measured

- A real `hyperframes lint` run from this branch on a film with a 10 s root and a clip from 8 s to 12.5 s prints the warning above; with the clip ending at 10 s it reports no warnings.
- Tests: a direct clip past the root is named with its end and the root length; a sub-composition is judged by its host, not its inner clips; a clip ending exactly at the root, or 40 ms past it, is not reported, and one 60 ms past it is; a clip timed with `data-end` is read like one with `data-duration`, and one whose start refers to another clip is skipped; media with no written length is not reported; a root with no `data-duration` is left to the existing missing-duration rules. The tests that expect a warning fail on main. Shrinking the allowance to 5 ms or ignoring `data-end` each fails a test.
- The existing check over every registry item and skill example now includes this rule, and none of them trips it. That check lints block files as sub-compositions, which this rule skips. Linted on their own, two registry blocks run about 20 and 37 ms past their own length and stay quiet under the allowance.
- Each run alone: `structure.test.ts` (19), `structure.catalog.test.ts` (1), `sourceLocations.test.ts` (22), parsers `timingMismatches.test.ts` (21), `composition.test.ts` (177), `hyperframeLinter.test.ts` (8), `project.test.ts` (38), cli `check.test.ts` (63), cli `lintProject.test.ts` (77). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Clips whose start refers to another clip (`intro+2`) are skipped.
- Clips inside a sub-composition are not checked against their own composition's length; the runtime cuts a film only at the top root's length, and an inner clip's real bound is its host's window, which needs a read across files.
- Images: the parsers give an image a default 3 s length, but the runtime does not apply that default yet, so an image with no written length is not reported.
- A clip hidden with `data-hidden` still warns: Studio's hide is a toggle the runtime can undo mid-playback, and the clip then plays at its written time, where the root still cuts it.
- The 50 ms allowance lets a film lose up to about one frame at 30 fps (three at 60 fps) without a warning.
- `check` itself (it launches a browser); it calls the same `lintProject`.

title: fix(studio-server): remove the history of a project that no longer exists
feat(studio): a host app can reuse Studio's snapping and marquee selection in its own preview
body:
## What changes for a user

Nothing inside Studio. A host app that draws its own preview overlay can now reuse Studio's snapping and marquee selection instead of copying them, and a marquee pick in that host is the same pick a click would make.

## How

- **Snapping** is exported from `@hyperframes/studio`'s root as it is: the snap engine (`resolveSnapAdjustment`, `extractSnapTargets`, `buildCompositionSnapTarget`, `buildGridSnapEdges`, `resolveGuideLineRect`, `resolveEquidistanceGuides`, `snapEngagedForTravel`, `SNAP_THRESHOLD_PX` and their types, `Rect` as `SnapRect`), `collectSnapContext` (takes the host's iframe and overlay) and `SnapGuideOverlay` with its props type. The guides draw once the preview has booted, which Studio's player marks inside `NLEPreview`.
- **The marquee** (`packages/studio/src/components/editor/marqueeCommit.ts`, `useMarqueeGestures`) takes an optional `resolveHits(elements)` that turns the elements a drag touched into the host's own picks; without it the hook resolves Studio edit selections exactly as before, and a host that declares its own pick type must pass one (a type error otherwise). `gestures` and `selectionRef` are optional. It returns `begin(event)` to start a marquee at a press the host has judged empty canvas, and `cancel()` to drop an active one (a host can call it on Escape). The 4 px threshold, measuring candidates once per drag, and the visibility and covers-composition filters stay inside. `DomEditOverlay` now calls `begin(event)` where it used to write the hook's internal state by hand. Exported: `useMarqueeGestures`, `MarqueeGesturesDeps`, `MarqueeGestures`, `MarqueeOverlay` with its props type, and `Rect` as `MarqueeRect`.
- **One pick per element** (`packages/core/src/runtime/picker.ts`): the runtime picker API gains `describe(element)`, returning what a click on that element returns (the existing `extractElementInfo`), so a host can map marquee hits to the same selector and label a click gives. Non-elements return null. It is optional on `HyperframePickerApi`, since a preview on an older runtime does not have it.

## Before

![main: mid-drag, the marquee over Box A and Box B](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdea468f-9d01-48de-959f-1a7403e66b61)
![main: after release, Box A and Box B selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb0c1c23-7ecf-4632-86a0-2734b7a5d7fe)

main. A three-box fixture in Studio: a drag from empty canvas across the red and blue boxes, shot mid-drag and after release. The label in the corner of each shot names the build it came from.

## After

![branch: mid-drag, the marquee over Box A and Box B](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74d3fe49-f903-42cd-884c-542a59e25e41)
![branch: after release, Box A and Box B selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00eae251-5191-462f-9c53-02745b8a4851)

This branch, same fixture and drag: the same marquee, the same two candidates, the same selection (Box A and Box B).

## What I measured

- The walk above, headless Chromium against Studio's dev server on main and on this branch.
- Tests: `packages/studio/src/editorGesturesExports.test.tsx` (new, 9 tests) drives the marquee and snapping by package name with a host's own iframe and overlay: resolveHits, once-per-drag measuring, the click under the threshold, `cancel()` and a pointercancel mid-drag, the default Studio path, the pick-type guard (a `@ts-expect-error` the typecheck enforces), pointer events passed to Studio's gestures or to none, and a snapped drag drawing its guide. `packages/core/src/runtime/picker.test.ts` adds `describe` returning exactly the click's info. Removing `describe`, making the default resolver return nothing, or making `cancel()` do nothing each fails the matching test. Resetting before the commit (an earlier cut of this change) fails the once-per-drag test. Removing the overloads that require `resolveHits` for a host pick type fails the typecheck on the unused `@ts-expect-error`.
- The whole `packages/studio` suite: 5806 passed, run before the pointercancel and pick-type tests were added; those pass in their file. `picker.test.ts`: 45 passed.
- `bun run build`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `typecheck:scripts`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, the comment ratchet and the comment-citation check: all exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A host app actually wiring these exports; only the package-name test drives them outside Studio.
- `describe` inside a live preview; it is covered by the runtime picker's tests only, and the walk ran Studio from source without rebuilding the runtime.
- Snapping in the walk: Studio's snapping code is unchanged, only exported.

title: fix(studio): even out levels lifts the right part of a sped-up or slowed clip
body:
## What changes for a user

Even Out Levels now lifts the right part of a clip that plays faster or slower than 1x. Before, on a clip at 2x it measured only the first half of the audio the clip plays and put each correction at half the clip time it belonged to; at 0.5x it measured audio the clip never plays. Clips with a speed ramp are handled the same way.

## Why it happened

An effect lane runs on the clip's own seconds: preview and export apply the clip's speed to the audio before the effects, and effect timing follows only the global preview speed. The leveller measured `duration x sampleRate` samples from the in-point and wrote its points on the audio's clock, so at any speed other than 1x both the window and the point times were off.

## The fix

`useFxLevelling.ts` reads the clip's speed the way playback does: its `rate` lane when there is one, otherwise `data-playback-rate`. It then:
- measures the audio the clip actually plays: from the in-point for `sourceTimeAt(rate, duration)` seconds;
- moves each lane point from the audio's clock onto the clip's with `timeAtSourceTime(rate, t)`, rounded to 3 decimals like the leveller's own output.

Both the real run and the hover preview go through the same measuring function.

One thing that follows from the clip clock: the lift's fade-in and fade-out are measured on the audio, so at 2x they take half as long in clip time. Placement is right at any speed.

## Tests

`propertyPanelAudioFxGroup.test.tsx`, "levels on the clip's clock at …", on a tone with a quiet passage:

| Case | With the old hook |
|---|---|
| 2x | fails: the lift is on the wrong clip seconds |
| 0.5x | fails: the quiet stretch gets no lift and the loud one does |
| a 2x rate lane (no `data-playback-rate`) | fails, and also fails if the fix ignores the lane |

Each part of the fix is load-bearing: leaving the lane on the audio's clock fails all three cases; measuring a 1x window fails 2x and the rate lane. The older in-point test now shares the same helper and still catches an ignored in-point.

Studio typecheck, lint, format check and the audio FX panel tests (74) pass.

## Before

A clip at 2x playing a 16 s tone that is quiet from 4 to 10 s, so the waveform is quiet from clip 2 to 5 s. The green Gain lane under the clip is the lift Even Out Levels wrote. Before, it starts rising at clip 3.97 s and stays at +12 dB over the loud tail:

![Before: at 2x the lift starts late and stays up over the loud tail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0fed3f2a-8e0d-4ce6-b530-de49ab427e03)

## After

After, it rises from clip 1.98 s, holds +12 dB to 4.97 s and falls back by 6.55 s, over the quiet stretch:

![After: the lift sits over the quiet stretch the clip plays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7191c905-1f3b-48a9-8fc2-8a433840cf64)

title: fix(cli): an update never replaces the CLI's files while a hyperframes command is running
body:
## What

A silent auto-update no longer replaces the CLI's files while a `hyperframes` command is running. It waits until every running command has exited, then installs. The update still lands before a later run; only the moment it installs changes.

## Why

When a newer version exists, each command launches a detached installer as soon as it starts, and that installer replaces the global package in place. A long-running command such as `preview` or `render` keeps loading files from the package after it starts. Today that means lazily imported `puppeteer-core`, `sharp` and `esbuild`, plus worker entries. If the install lands mid-session, the next action that needs one of those files fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Splitting the CLI bundle into per-command chunks, the next change, would widen this to any code a command has not loaded yet.

## How

- Each CLI process writes an empty file named after its pid under `~/.hyperframes/running/` at startup, and removes it on exit (`utils/runningCli.ts`, called from `cli.ts`).
- Each running process rewrites its file every 30 s, which also restores a file that was removed. The detached installer checks every 2 s and installs only when no listed pid is still alive and heartbeating.
- A file counts as stale only when the installer itself has watched it go 10 minutes without a rewrite, timed on its own monotonic clock. A long jump in wall-clock time between two polls means the machine slept, so the installer then starts watching every file afresh. A live `preview` that looks old after waking is therefore never dropped, and a blocking call shorter than 10 minutes is covered too. A killed process's file, even one whose pid was later reused, goes stale and is removed.
- An install lock keeps a single waiting installer. It is taken under the existing settings lock and the waiter keeps it fresh. A later launch that sees it beating exits, logging that. The waiter checks it still owns the lock before installing, and removes only a lock it owns.
- A waiting installer gives up after an hour and logs that to `auto-update.log`. The next run schedules it again through the existing pending-install rules.
- The installer script moved into an exported `installerScript()`, so the tests run the real script instead of a copy.

## Tests

`utils/autoUpdate.installer.test.ts` runs the real installer as a child process. The install command only writes a marker file.

- While a registered process is alive, the marker is never written; once that process exits, the install runs and `completedUpdate` is recorded.
- A live command whose file looks ten minutes old, as after a laptop sleep, is still waited on.
- A pid file left by a process that is already dead does not block the install. Neither does a file whose pid now belongs to another process, once it stops changing. Both files are removed.
- A second installer launched while the first is waiting exits without installing. An install lock whose pid belongs to another process is taken over once it stops changing.

`utils/runningCli.test.ts` checks that the pid file exists while the process runs, is removed on exit, and is rewritten by the heartbeat.

Each part is pinned by a test that fails without it. Installing right away fails five of the six installer tests. Judging a file's age by the wall clock fails the sleep test. Never treating a file as stale fails both pid-reuse tests. Removing the heartbeat fails the heartbeat test. The related test files (44 tests) passed three runs in a row.

## Not covered

- A command started during the install itself, a window of seconds, can still see files change under it, exactly as before this change.
- A command that blocks its event loop for more than 10 minutes (for example a long synchronous build in `lambda deploy`) stops heartbeating and can be dropped.
- The sleep test simulates an old file; it does not sleep a real machine.
- A command suspended for more than 10 minutes (Ctrl-Z) stops heartbeating, so an update can land under it.

Local checks: `oxfmt --check .`, `bun run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` in packages/cli pass. The full CLI suite passed on this branch before the review fixes, which touched only the two files above and their tests.

title: fix(studio): a resize after a drag saves its size below the timeline it uses
body:
## What

After dragging an element on the canvas and then resizing it, Studio saved the resize's size (a `tl.set`) above the line that declares the timeline:

```js
window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
gsap.set("#card", { x: -216, y: -40 });
tl.set("#card", { width: 751, height: 871 }, 0);
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
window.__timelines["main"] = tl;
```

`tl.set` runs before `const tl` is initialised, so the saved film threw `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'tl' before initialization` on every load and render. A project with no script yet ended up with the same order.

The drag writes a global `gsap.set`, which is placed above the timeline declaration. Both GSAP script writers inserted new timeline calls "after the last existing call", and after a drag that call is the global `gsap.set`. They now insert after whichever comes later: the last existing call or the timeline declaration. The timeline variable name is read from the script, so `const master = gsap.timeline()` works the same way.

```js
window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};
gsap.set("#card", { x: -216, y: -40 });
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
tl.set("#card", { width: 751, height: 871 }, 0);
window.__timelines["main"] = tl;
```

## Where

Each writer has one function that picks where a new timeline call goes, and every insert goes through it: `findInsertionPoint` in the acorn writer (the default) and `insertAfterAnchor` in the recast writer. Global `gsap.set` placement and the other paths already anchored on the declaration and are unchanged.

## Verification

- `gsapWriter.timelineOrder.test.ts`: drag then resize, and drag then a keyframed tween, on both writers and with `tl` and `master` as the timeline name. Six cases fail on main and pass here. Resize alone and drag alone keep their exact output.
- `files.test.ts`: the script-less case through the real `/gsap-mutations` route fails on main and passes here.
- Each rule turns a test red when broken.
- The parsers suite and the studio-server route tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and the audit gate pass.
- In Studio, dragging a card and then resizing it on a fixture project, the saved file on main throws on reload. On this branch it reloads with no errors and the card at its new size.

Not in this change: when a timeline call sits inside a wrapper function (for example an IIFE that declares its own timeline), the default writer still inserts after the wrapper, as on main.

## Before

The saved film reloaded after drag, then resize: the `tl` error, no timeline registered, the card still at its original size.

![Before: saved film throws "Cannot access 'tl' before initialization" and the card keeps its original size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7c60635b-fa1c-4ef6-80eb-4ab8b02f37fc)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0cc4d38e-4468-49dc-aef4-5a9b2c2e80ee

## After

Same steps: no errors, the timeline is registered, and the card is at its resized size.

![After: saved film loads with no errors and the card at its resized size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a85c9071-e943-4289-aa37-b8b56854793d)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a3997867-3bda-4f14-b1c8-516d740bdde6

title: feat(studio-server): list the projects the history cache knows, with their folders
body:
## What this adds

A read-only list of the projects the history cache knows about: `listProjectHistories(historyRoot)` returns each history's id, its project folder, and when it was last used. It reads the same records the cleanup in #4634 reads, takes no locks and changes nothing.

It lists a history only while its project is still in the folder it was recorded for (the folder still holds that history's id), so a caller never gets a path that is gone or now holds something else. It is for a `clean` command that sweeps leftover files in every project the cache knows, not only the one it runs in.

Builds on #4634, now on main.

## Tests

`history/pruneHistories.test.ts`: lists only histories whose project is still in its folder (leaving out a deleted project and a folder that now holds another project), and skips folders that are not histories; lists nothing for a history cache that does not exist.

Results: studio-server and CLI `tsc`, whole-tree `oxfmt --check` and `bun run lint`, and fallow are clean; the history tests pass. Without the folder check, the listing test fails. The new tests call the function this adds, so they cannot pass without it.

title: feat(studio): export DOM editing for a host outside EditorShell
body: ## What this adds A host app that embeds Studio's preview outside `EditorShell` can now offer the same direct editing (select, drag, resize, rotate, edit text) without copying Studio code. Studio's own behaviour does not change, apart from one small fix below. - **Exports** from `@hyperframes/studio`: `useDomEditSession` and `UseDomEditSessionParams`, `usePreviewPersistence` and `UsePreviewPersistenceParams`, `DomEditProvider`, `useDomEditSelectionContext`, `PreviewReadOnlyProvider`, `ConnectedDomEditOverlay` and its props, and the types `DomEditSelection` and `DomEditCapabilities`. - **`ConnectedDomEditOverlay`**: the editing overlay block that `PreviewOverlays` rendered inline, moved into its own component that reads its handlers from the edit context. `PreviewOverlays` now renders it, so Studio and a host share one wiring. Two recording props the overlay never read are not part of its props. When a z-order change also moves sibling elements, which have no selection object, each sibling's save target comes from the node itself and the selection's file (siblings share its document). A sibling with no id or selector cannot be written to source, so its new z applies live only and reverts on reload. - **`canvasInput?: "overlay" | "host"`** on `DomEditOverlay` (default `"overlay"`). With `"host"` the overlay takes no presses of its own: no hover box, no marquee, no context menu, no re-select on a click, and no off-canvas indicators. The selection handles (move, resize, rotate) keep working, so a host with its own pointer layer keeps every other press. - **Text editing in host mode**: Enter starts editing whenever the selected element is text, and a double-press on the selection box still works. - **`onSelectionBoxClick`** (optional): a host receives clicks on a single selection's box (not a group's), for example to climb to the parent on a slower second click. The event is the pointerup or click that ended the press. Unset, nothing changes. - **`onTextEditingChange(editing)`** on `DomEditOverlay`: tells a host when the text caret goes live and when it ends (including when the overlay unmounts mid-edit), so a host pointer layer can stand aside while text is being edited, as Studio's own layer does. - **Fix: the first box click after a handle resize was lost.** A resize or rotate release sets a flag that swallows the release's trailing click, but that click lands on the handle, so the flag stayed set and ate the next click on the box of an element that can be resized but not moved. In Studio that click's re-select was dropped (on main too); a host would not hear it. Each new press now clears the flag first. ## Before A small host page outside `EditorShell` (a test harness, not part of this PR) that imports DOM editing from the package entry, on main's Studio source. It stops at the import: the export does not exist. ![Before: select](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4dabd817-f6eb-4132-b116-9b199860498f) ![Before: drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54aad113-8f80-41cd-ade5-d3c369d853a0) ![Before: text edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8fc1cdcb-b3b1-4119-8928-e6f244cdca0d) ## After The same page on this branch, with `canvasInput="host"`, the host's own pointer layer under the overlay, and a host status line fed by `onSelectionBoxClick` and `onTextEditingChange`. The host picks the title; the selection box drags it 120 px and reports the click; Enter with nothing focused opens the text. Both edits land in the saved file (`gsap.set("#title", { x: 120, y: 0 })`, then `Hosted`). ![After: select](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f4c4df3d-0883-4621-9fea-531ef621c39e) ![After: drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a1fd890a-9dce-4ace-8b6c-889b04c2d763) ![After: text edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2a66eeb-5167-4586-a3cd-e811bc130c96) ## Studio unchanged Studio itself, on main and on this branch: drag, rotate with the handle, and a text edit. Each pair is pixel-identical, and the saved file is byte-identical after both runs. ![Studio on main: drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7632d5be-a4da-4a19-ad19-1969f019f6c1) ![Studio on this branch: drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ed3ec024-2a78-4784-abd6-cfd695ee84df) ![Studio on main: rotate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/189310ad-6e12-4a85-bae9-cf0feedc474e) ![Studio on this branch: rotate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9756593b-4dc6-4b15-9512-6a747b23bf0a) ![Studio on main: text edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a8863a48-0c6e-4ca7-9749-f86829e7f971) ![Studio on this branch: text edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d1bfb8a-32e6-43d8-ad99-c50bb1f9005c) ## What I measured - Tests: `ConnectedDomEditOverlay` passes the same props `PreviewOverlays` passed before, never passes the recording props, and shows no hover box while playback runs. In host mode: - the root takes no pointer events; - there is no hover box, marquee, context menu or off-canvas indicator; - a click on the box does not re-select, and the handles still work; - Enter opens the text when nothing else has focus, but not from a focused field; - `onSelectionBoxClick` fires once per box click on either route, never for a press off the box or on a group's box, and still fires on the first box click after a handle resize. Also: `onTextEditingChange` reports true then false, and the new exports resolve from the package and mount inside a host's providers. The host-mode, text-editing and export tests fail on main. The handle test guards behaviour that already exists. Each of these edits fails its own test: - forcing the hover box on; - turning the window Enter off; - removing the box-click call; - widening the box check to any selection box; - removing the flag reset. - Each run alone: `previewReadOnly.overlay.test.tsx` (28), `ConnectedDomEditOverlay.test.tsx` (5), `domEditExports.test.tsx` (2), nle `previewReadOnly` (6), `PreviewOverlays.topologyLens` (2), `DomEditOverlay` (22), `DomEditOverlayHover` (2), `CanvasContextMenu` (7), `offCanvasIndicatorRefresh` (3), `groupDropKeepsSelection` (2), both anchored-resize tests, `InlineTextToolbar`. Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet, comment citations and the fallow audit are green. - Host captures: headless Chrome against Studio's dev server serving the harness page, the same scripted steps on this branch's head and at the point it leaves main; each step carries a caption so the three Before shots stay distinct. - Studio captures: headless Chrome, Studio's dev server on main and on an earlier head of this branch, running the same scripted drag, rotate and text edit. Later commits change host mode and the flag reset. In these steps the flag reset changes nothing: the text edit's first press sets the flag again either way. ## What I did NOT exercise - A host that mounts its own preview iframe must also mark the preview booted and begin a timeline session in the player store, as Studio's player does; without the first the selection box never draws, and without the second a drag moves the element but never saves, with no error. Neither step is documented or wrapped in a helper yet. It must also keep the values it passes to `useDomEditSession` stable across renders. - `DomEditOverlay` still declares the two unused recording props; removing them there is a separate cleanup. - If the overlay unmounts while a text caret is live, the typed words stay on screen but are neither saved nor reverted, and `onTextEditingChange(false)` still fires. This is the same on main; host mode makes it easier to reach. A follow-up makes unmount save, as blur does.

title: chore: release v0.8.82
body:
Cuts v0.8.82. Merging publishes: the workflow tags the merge commit, publishes npm and cuts the GitHub release.

Renders now match the preview more closely in video frames, fonts and shader transitions. Studio plays back and seeks faster, and the CLI can transcribe with Parakeet after an opt-in install.

## What ships

- Engine: renders show the video frame the preview shows at each output frame (#4596)
- Shader Transitions: transitions in renders keep scene layout, styles and animations (#4615)
- Producer: renders use the font named in a var() fallback, and embed the Google font the page linked (#4619, #4569)
- Studio: playback no longer relayouts the timecode and playhead every frame (#4593)
- Studio: a film with no manual edits skips the edit reapply on each seek (#4592)
- CLI: transcribe with Parakeet on macOS, Linux and Windows after an opt-in install (#4583)
- Studio: quick saves no longer refuse each other as outside changes (#4612)
- CLI: commands exit right away even when the network or DNS is broken (#4604)
- Studio: a resize after a drag saves its keyframe where the timeline can use it (#4638)

The full list is in `releases/v0.8.82.md` and `docs/changelog.mdx`.

## No visible change

Version bump and changelog only; every change listed above was reviewed and captured in its own PR.

title: perf(core): a host can import path, asset and runtime-script helpers without the parsers
body:
## What changes for a user

A host app that needs only core's path and asset helpers, or the runtime script, can import them without loading the parsers. In node, importing `@hyperframes/core` costs about 470 ms. Each new entry costs 10 to 14 ms. Existing imports are unchanged.

## How

Three entries in `packages/core/package-subpaths.json`, the source of the package's exports. `package.json` exports and `publishConfig.exports` were generated from it with `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs --write`.

| Import | Contains | Loads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@hyperframes/core/safe-path` | `resolveWithinProject`, `isSafePath`, `realpath` | `node:path`, `node:fs` |
| `@hyperframes/core/asset-paths` | `rewriteAssetPath`, `rewriteAssetPaths`, `rewriteInlineStyleAssetUrls`, `rewriteCssAssetUrls` | `@hyperframes/parsers/asset-paths` (`node:path` only) |
| `@hyperframes/core/runtime-script` | `getHyperframeRuntimeScript` | one generated string constant |

The root entry still exports all of these.

## What I measured

Import cost in node after `bun run build`, median of 7 fresh processes each:

| Import | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@hyperframes/core` (what a host had to load for these helpers) | 470 ms | 470 ms, unchanged |
| `@hyperframes/core/safe-path` | not available | 13 ms |
| `@hyperframes/core/asset-paths` | not available | 10 ms |
| `@hyperframes/core/runtime-script` | not available | 14 ms |
| `@hyperframes/core/compiler`, for reference | 364 ms | 364 ms |

- `packages/core/src/lightEntries.test.ts` bundles each light entry's source (read from the descriptor) and fails if recast, ast-types, `@babel/parser`, acorn, esprima, linkedom or postcss is in its graph. Pointing `./safe-path` at the compiler entry fails it.
- `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs` (the lint check), `bun run build`, core's `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass. `dist/safePath.js`, `dist/compiler/rewriteSubCompPaths.js` and `dist/generated/runtime-inline.js` are emitted and covered by `files`.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A host app switching its imports; that follows once this is published.
- `runtime-script` is not in the guard test, because its source only exists after a build. It is one string constant.
- The guard lists known heavy packages. A future import of another large package would not trip it.

title: perf(core): a bundled film inlines each shared font once instead of once per composition
body:
## What

A bundled film now carries one copy of each identical `@font-face` rule instead of one per composition that uses the font. Once fonts are inlined as data URLs, each repeat is the whole font file again, so this halves a typical single-file bundle.

## Why

Every composition that uses a font declares it in its own style. When the bundle inlines assets, each declaration's `src` becomes the full font file, so a film with three scenes sharing four faces carries twelve copies of the font bytes.

On `packages/producer/tests/heygen-promo-preview-assets` (3 scenes sharing 4 faces):

| Bundle | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Default (inlined assets) | 2,148,723 bytes, 12 `@font-face` | 1,069,271 bytes (-50.2%), 4 `@font-face` |
| Bundle time, median of 7 | 30.5 ms | 29.1 ms |

The same four faces load, and in headless Chrome every text node uses the same font as on main at 8 points across the film.

## How

- `dedupeFontFaceRules` (`compositionScoping.ts`) drops earlier copies of an identical top-level `@font-face` and keeps the last one, because the last matching rule is the one the browser uses. A rule in between never gains precedence.
- The key is every declaration, with `!important`, and whitespace collapsed only outside quotes, so `"Brand  Sans"` and `"Brand Sans"` stay apart.
- Only styles that always apply take part: no `media`, no non-CSS `type`, not inside `<noscript>` or `<svg>`. An excluded style can only keep an extra copy, never lose one.
- A style whose CSS does not parse is left exactly as authored and is never the kept copy, so a malformed style bundles as it does on main.
- Rules nested in `@media` or `@supports` are left alone.
- It runs before asset inlining. Sub-composition urls are already rewritten against the project root by then, so identical url text means the same file; running first is a speed choice (postcss parses paths, not inlined font bytes).
- Scene-part bundles (the Studio preview) are skipped: each scene keeps its own copy, so an edit to one scene still swaps that scene alone. The preview does not inline fonts, so it would only have saved about 1.7 KB.

Callers: the CLI commands that build one file (`validate`, `layout`, `compare`, `grade-compare`, `motion-shot`, HDR promotion, and the localized-fonts capture path). Renders do not call `bundleToSingleHtml`.

## Test plan

- [x] `compositionScoping.test.ts` and `htmlBundler.test.ts` pass (65 and 107).
- [x] Each fix has a test that fails without it: unparseable style left as authored, `!important` kept apart, quoted names differing in inner spaces kept apart, the four conditional-style cases, and each scene keeping its own copy in a scene-part bundle.
- [x] Keep-first instead of keep-last fails the unit tests.
- [x] Byte counts and fonts compared on main and this branch as above.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` passes for `packages/core`.
- [x] No change under `packages/studio` or `packages/player`, so no before/after captures are needed.

title: perf(studio-server): a host can import id stamping, file walking and history without the server
body:
Uses the `@hyperframes/core/safe-path` entry from #4642 (merged).

## What changes for a user

A host app that stamps element ids, walks a project's files, or keeps its undo history can import just that part of studio-server instead of the whole server. In node, importing `@hyperframes/studio-server` costs about 700 ms. The new entries cost 7 to 28 ms, except id stamping (195 ms, most of it linkedom, which stamping needs to parse HTML). Existing imports are unchanged.

## How

- `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/safePath.ts` takes `resolveWithinProject` and `realpath` from `@hyperframes/core/safe-path` rather than core's root, which loads the parsers. Every light entry below reaches core only through this file.
- `src/history/index.ts` now holds the history export list that `src/index.ts` spelled out. The root re-exports it, so both entries share one list.
- Three entries in `package-subpaths.json` (exports generated with `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs --write`), each also a tsup entry. Code splitting keeps one copy of shared state between the root and a light entry.

| Import | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/safe-path` | `walkDir`, `isSafePath`, `resolveWithinProject`, `realpath`, `realFilePath`, `pinWithinProject`, `isInHiddenOrVendorDir` |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/hf-ids` | `stampProjectHfIds`, `stampFileHfIds`, `isCompositionSource` |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/history` | `openProjectHistory`, `historyCache`, `listProjectHistories`, `pruneGoneProjectHistories`, the history error classes and types |

`./screenshot-clip` already existed and is now covered by the guard test too. `docs/packages/studio-server.mdx` lists the three new entries.

## What I measured

Import cost in node after `bun run build`, median of 7 fresh processes each:

| Import | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server` (what a host had to load for these helpers) | 696 ms | 696 ms, unchanged |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/safe-path` | not available | 16 ms |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/hf-ids` | not available | 195 ms (linkedom alone: about 170 ms) |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/history` | not available | 28 ms |
| `@hyperframes/studio-server/screenshot-clip` | 7 ms | 7 ms |

- `packages/studio-server/src/lightEntries.test.ts` makes core's root, the compiler, lint, hono, postcss and sharp throw on load, then imports each light entry's source (read from the descriptor). With `safePath.ts` back on core's root, the safe-path, hf-ids and history cases fail.
- The whole `packages/studio-server` suite: 897 passed, 2 skipped. `bun run build`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`: all exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A host app switching its imports; that follows once this is published.
- Loading linkedom lazily inside id stamping. Stamping is synchronous at its call sites, so deferring linkedom would change that API.

title: fix(studio): dragging an audio clip's edge trims it instead of moving it
body:
## What a user can do now

Drag the left or right edge of an audio clip in the timeline to trim it. Before this change, pressing the right edge of an audio clip and dragging moved the whole clip instead, so the clip's start changed and its length stayed the same.

## Why it happened

A clip's picture layer (the audio waveform, a video filmstrip, an image still, a composition thumbnail) is drawn inside the clip, on top of the trim handles. The waveform sits at a higher stacking level on purpose, so it stays visible above the fade wedges, and it covers the whole clip. A press at the clip's edge therefore landed on the waveform instead of the trim handle, bubbled up to the clip, and started a move.

## The fix

The picture layer takes no input. It is a picture only: every clip's content is wrapped in one layer in `timelineClipChildren.tsx`, and that layer now has `pointer-events: none`. Presses fall through to whatever sits under it, the trim handle at the edges and the clip body elsewhere. Nothing is drawn differently: the waveform still paints above the fade wedges. The fade handles are separate children of the clip, outside this layer, so they keep working. The `renderClipContent` prop now documents that its content takes no pointer input; interactive content belongs in `renderClipOverlay`, which is rendered outside this layer.

## Tests

`timelineClipChildren.test.ts`: "lets a press on a picture stacked above the trim handles fall through to them". The test environment cannot hit-test, so it pins the property that decides the hit: a picture rendered with `z-index: 10` sits inside a layer that takes no input.

Fails on main:

```
AssertionError: expected '' to be 'none' // Object.is equality
```

Also run: `TimelineClip.test.tsx`, `AudioWaveform.test.tsx`, and every `Timeline*` / `timelineClip*` test in `player/components` (56 files, 985 tests), plus format, lint and the studio typecheck.

## Before

Studio on main with a small fixture: an audio clip starting at 1 s, 4 s long. Pressing its right edge and dragging 1 s to the right moves the whole clip: it now starts at 2 s and is still 4 s long. The press lands on the waveform, not the trim handle.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f534c5d8-9f0d-47e5-ac43-661fbddd1fc7)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6226825-98bf-4159-b1f0-d80a79a8024a

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this branch: the edge press reaches the trim handle (resize cursor), the clip still starts at 1 s and is now 5 s long.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04cdeec7-9ae6-4cf3-9a51-3bd517844c1a)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ee80239-22d7-45b1-b829-6e8408193a54

title: fix(studio): a clip drag released outside the window is cancelled
body:
## What a user can do now

Abandon a clip drag by letting go outside the window. A clip move, a trim or a fade-handle drag released outside the window is cancelled and the clip goes back to how it was, the same as pressing Escape. Before this change, the drag committed to wherever its preview was last drawn, so a clip dragged off the top of the window landed on another track.

## Why it happened

The timeline captures the pointer when a drag starts, so the release reaches it even when it happens outside the window. The release handler committed any release from the gesture's pointer without looking at where it happened. Only Escape, a cancelled pointer and a lost pointer capture cancelled a drag.

## The fix

Clip moves, single and group trims, and the blocked-edit gesture on a locked clip all end in one release handler in `timelineClipDragGestureLifecycle.ts`. A release outside the window's bounds now goes through the same path as a cancelled pointer, which discards the preview and commits nothing. A release inside the window, up to its last pixel, still commits as before.

Fade handles run their own gesture in `TimelineClipFades.tsx`. Its release now uses the same outside-window check, moved into one shared module (`timelinePointerRelease.ts`): a fade drag released outside the window puts the fade back as it was and saves nothing, and a release inside still saves.

## Tests

`timelineClipDragGestureLifecycle.test.ts`:

- "cancels a drag released above the window and leaves the clip where it was" (released at y -40)
- "cancels a drag released past the window's right edge and leaves the clip where it was"
- "cancels a drag released on the window's right edge and leaves the clip where it was" (x equal to the window width)
- "cancels a drag released on the window's bottom edge and leaves the clip where it was" (y equal to the window height)
- "cancels a trim released outside the window"
- "still commits a drag released on the window's last pixel"

`TimelineClipFades.test.tsx`:

- "restores the fade and saves nothing when released above the window" (y -40)
- "restores the fade and saves nothing when released on the window's right edge" (x equal to the window width)

Two existing fade tests released at negative x as a stand-in for "far left"; they now release inside the window, since a release outside cancels.

The cancel cases, clip and fade, fail on main:

```
AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times
```

Also run: the `useTimelineClipDrag*`, `timelineClipDrag*`, `TimelineClip` and `TimelineClipFades` tests, plus format, lint and the studio typecheck.

## Before

Studio on main with a small fixture: the Bar clip (start 1 s, second row) is dragged 2 s right and up, then released above the top of the window. The move commits: Bar lands on a new top row at 0 s and pushes Title down.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f0d5990-0d29-4f48-8f9f-f588c23b4adf)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1ccc8d53-10b6-4946-98f9-ec48a9834311

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this branch: after the release above the window, Bar is back at 1 s on its own row and nothing was saved.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90fe494a-fd46-4bef-a4ec-11360b84b01c)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d79f9db1-ce62-43d5-9893-e69005af3497

## Not covered

Keyframe retimes, automation-lane point drags and beat drags have their own pointer handling and still save when released outside the window. They are a follow-up.

title: feat(studio): let a host app keep paint order in step with timeline rows
body:
## What a host can do now

A host app that mounts the standalone `Timeline` (without Studio's editor shell) can now keep the preview's paint order in step with the timeline rows. When a lane move puts a clip on a lower row than a clip it overlaps in time, the timeline asks the host to restack z-index, the same way it already does inside Studio. Before this, that sync could only turn on inside Studio's own DOM edit context, which the package does not export, so in a host the rows said one order and the film painted another.

## API

Two optional props on `Timeline`, and the commit's type from the package entry:

- `previewIframeRef?: RefObject<HTMLIFrameElement | null>`: the host's preview iframe (same origin), used to read each clip's current z-index and to resolve its live element.
- `onZIndexReorder?: TimelineZIndexReorderCommit`: called after a lane move with the z-index each clip needs. The host applies and saves it. Each entry carries the live `element`, the new `zIndex`, and `id` / `selector` / `selectorIndex` / `sourceFile` so the host can find the element in the source. The second argument is the lane move's coalesce key, so the z write can share the move's undo step.

```tsx
import { Timeline, type TimelineZIndexReorderCommit } from "@hyperframes/studio";

const onZIndexReorder: TimelineZIndexReorderCommit = async (entries, coalesceKey) => {
  for (const e of entries) e.element.style.zIndex = String(e.zIndex);
  await saveInlineZIndex(entries, coalesceKey); // the host's own write
};

<Timeline
  previewIframeRef={previewIframeRef}
  onZIndexReorder={onZIndexReorder}
  onMoveElement={onMoveElement}
  onMoveElements={onMoveElements}
/>;
```

The sync turns on only when both a ref and a commit are present; each prop overrides Studio's own separately. Studio does not pass these props, so its behaviour is the same as before.

What a host should know:
- The host saves the z-index change to its own file; Studio's save routine is tied to its editing session and is not exported.
- The z write runs only after the host's move save succeeds. A commit that throws is dropped without a log, and one that never settles blocks later lane moves.
- Clips in the root file arrive with `sourceFile` set to `index.html`, whatever the host's root file is called.
- The timeline's stored z-index goes stale unless the host re-reads elements; lane moves read z from the live preview, so later syncs stay correct when the host writes the style on the element, as above.
- The preview must be same-origin; a cross-origin preview is left alone.

Not in this change: `TimelinePane` and `EditorShell`, also public, do not pass these props through yet, so a host that builds its layout from them still gets rows and paint order out of step. That is a follow-up.

## Why this shape

The sync already runs through one hook (`useTimelineStackingSync`), which read its two inputs from Studio's DOM edit context. The smallest public surface is those two inputs as props, next to the edit callbacks `Timeline` already takes as host overrides. Exporting the whole DOM edit context would expose many fields a host cannot supply. `TimelineZIndexReorderCommit` was already the type of the matching option on `useTimelineEditing`; it is now exported by name.

## Tests

- `timelineStackingSyncExport.test.tsx` (new): mounts `Timeline` imported from `@hyperframes/studio`, with no Studio providers, a preview iframe holding three elements with no z-index, and a host commit. It drags a clip from the top row to the bottom row through real pointer events and checks that the host commit ran once with elements from the preview iframe, and that the clip left on the upper row now paints above the moved one. On main's source the move still lands (track assertion passes), then it fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`.
- `useTimelineStackingSync.test.tsx`: new case where both Studio's context and host props are present; the host's iframe and commit are used and Studio's commit is not called. It fails on main's source, and also fails if the precedence is flipped (context first): `expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ [ ObjectContaining{…} ], undefined ]`.
- Existing Studio path unchanged and green: the existing `useTimelineStackingSync` case, `timelineClipDragCommit.test.ts` (58 tests), `timelineChromeExports.test.tsx`.
- `bun run format:check`, `bun run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio, comment ratchet and fallow audit all pass.

## Before

A throwaway host page that mounts only the standalone `Timeline` and a preview iframe, with no Studio shell. Two overlapping blocks with no z-index: blue Title and red Tag. At the start, Tag is on the top row and paints on top, so rows and paint agree. Dragging Tag down to the bottom row on main: the rows now read Title above Tag, but the preview still paints Tag on top, and the host is never asked to restack.

![Before: at the start, rows and paint agree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60a09fd0-05f8-4d43-b56f-38acefeb211e)

![Before: after the move, Tag still paints on top](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f52c8d8-fd97-4f7d-a8bc-09d76b7d4cca)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40a0feeb-7961-418a-8faf-bd612f4e454e

## After

Same page and gesture on this branch: after the move the timeline calls the host's `onZIndexReorder` (Title gets z-index 1), and the preview paints Title on top, matching the rows.

![After: Title paints on top, matching the rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/041ed297-bb94-4f44-8555-630da5929de5)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/178344e4-e6e0-49b1-8798-ace7f69a1a94

title: fix(media-use): record agent-made voice, music and sound effects in the media manifest
body:
## What

media-use's audio engine writes voice-over to `assets/voice`, music to `assets/bgm` and sound effects to `assets/sfx`, but never recorded them in the project's media manifest (`.media/manifest.jsonl`). The manifest is where a host learns what a media file is and how it was made: its `source` says whether the agent generated or fetched it or the person brought it, and Studio's asset panel reads its description and duration. Worse, a later `media-use resolve` that scanned `assets/` recorded those files as `existing`, the label for the person's own files.

Now every file the engine writes is recorded where it lies, marked with how it was made:

- Each voice line as `generated`, music as `search` (retrieved) or `generated` (made locally), each sound effect as `search` (retrieved) or `bundled` (copied from the bundled library), with its duration and the text, mood or cue name as its description. Music that is still being generated is recorded by `wait-bgm.mjs` once the track is ready.
- A sound effect file that was already in `assets/sfx` under a library name but is not the library's copy is the person's own; the engine now leaves it unlabelled instead of calling it `bundled`.
- `media-use resolve --from <file> --source generated|search|bundled` does the same for any agent: a file already inside the project is recorded where it is, without a copy into `.media`. Without `--source`, `--from` works as before. `--source` is refused without `--from` and for a LUT or grade.
- `resolve`'s scan of `assets/` no longer adds an `existing` record for a file that already has one; it reuses that record.

**One owner.** The rule lives in the manifest library, `manifest.mjs`: `recordInPlace` and `latestRecordFor`. The skill ships its own copy of that library, and `scripts/check-media-use-copy-parity.test.mjs` keeps it byte-identical to the CLI's. So the engine records in-process through the same code the CLI uses, with no extra process per file and no dependence on which CLI version is installed.

**The latest record for a path wins.** The manifest only appends. Recording a file again adds nothing when its source, description and duration are unchanged, so re-running the engine on the same take does not grow the manifest. A regenerated take (new line text, new length, or a different source) appends a newer record. `resolve`'s scan of `assets/`, prompt and entity lookups, and Studio all read only a path's newest record, so the old text no longer finds audio that now says something else. `--candidates`, `index.md` and usage stats still list every record. Recording holds the manifest's lock and takes its id from the same count a download uses (recorded ids plus files reserved but not yet recorded), so a background `wait-bgm` and an agent's `resolve` cannot hand out the same id. On a project where an earlier `resolve` already labelled an engine file `existing`, the engine's next run appends the correct label and it takes over.

Usage events count these as `recorded`, not as fetches.

## Known limits

- The HeyGen sound-effect download and the retrieved music track overwrite a file of the same name that the person put in `assets/sfx` or `assets/bgm`. That is older than this change and is not fixed here.
- Music that wait-bgm records has no description beyond its file name and no duration, because the engine does not keep the music prompt in `audio_meta.json` and the generator reports no duration.
- Records are keyed by path. A file the person drops over an engine-made name keeps the engine's label, and an engine file moved by hand loses its record (the reference docs say so).

## Tests

- skills, "a voice run leaves a manifest entry marked generated": one `voice` record for `assets/voice/01.wav` with source `generated`, the line text as description, its duration and the TTS provider. Fails on `main`.
- skills, the Gemini engine pipeline test (the real engine with fixture providers) now also checks that the voice line it wrote is in `.media/manifest.jsonl` as `generated`. It fails if the engine stops recording.
- skills: music and sound effects are marked by where they came from; a person's own sound effect is not labelled; locally made music is recorded once ready, not while pending; a rerun of the same take keeps one record, while a rerun with new text records the new take and the old text no longer finds the file; a file that cannot be recorded becomes an anomaly, not a failure.
- skills, sound effects: a person's own file under a bundled name is labelled `project`, while the library's own copy stays `local`. Fails on `main`.
- skills, `wait-bgm.mjs` run on a ready track records it as `generated` with its provider.
- skills, "a record never takes the id of a download still in flight": with `bgm_001` reserved in `.media/audio/bgm`, recording a track gets `bgm_002`. Fails if recording counts only the manifest.
- media-use: `--from --source` records a project file where it is, adds a record only when what it says changes, and a replaced record no longer answers a prompt lookup; copies a file from outside the project with that label; refuses an unknown source, a LUT, and `--source` without `--from`. A broken ffprobe setting (`HYPERFRAMES_FFPROBE_PATH`) now fails with its one-line error instead of a stack trace (checked by hand).
- media-use, "resolve does not relabel a recorded file in assets/ as the person's own": an old `existing` record followed by the engine's `search` record resolves to `search`, and nothing is appended. Fails on `main`.
- The existing `--from` tests (freeze a copy under `.media`) still pass, so `--from` without `--source` is unchanged.

Each rule's test fails with that rule removed, in both copies of the manifest library.

title: fix(studio): the timeline takes m4v video and flac audio
body:
## What a user can do now

Drag an `.m4v` video or a `.flac` audio file onto the Studio timeline and it lands as a clip, the same as an `.mp4` or `.mp3`. Both files also show up in the Assets panel (Video and Audio groups), with a thumbnail and duration for the video, and open in the media preview from the Code tab.

## Why

Studio's list of media extensions did not include `m4v` or `flac`. The timeline asked that list what kind of file it was given, got no answer, and refused the drop with "Only image, video, and audio assets can be dropped onto the timeline." The Assets panel filtered with a second, hand-copied list, so the files were not listed there either. Chrome plays both formats, the preview server already serves them with the right content type, and a render of a composition holding both produces the video frames and the audio.

## The fix

`packages/studio/src/utils/mediaTypes.ts` now keeps one list of extensions per kind (image, video, audio), adds `m4v` to video and `flac` to audio, and builds the image, video, audio and "any media" patterns from those lists. The "any media" pattern can no longer drift from the three it is made of. The patterns keep the same shape as before: matched at the end of the path, case-insensitive.

Two copies of those lists outside the timeline agree with it now too:
- The feedback panel's media count uses the shared `isMediaFile` instead of its own list.
- The upload check on the studio server probes `.flac` with ffprobe like any other audio file (a broken `.flac` was accepted unchecked), and its metadata helper labels `.flac` as audio instead of unknown.

## Tests

New `packages/studio/src/utils/mediaTypes.test.ts`:

- `clip.m4v`, `assets/Take 2.M4V`, `song.flac` and `voice.FLAC` are taken by the timeline as video or audio and count as media; `.mp4`, `.mp3` and `.png` still do.
- `.pdf`, `.woff2`, `.cube`, `clip.m4v.txt` and a bare `flac` are still refused.
- A file counts as media exactly when it is an image, video or audio file.

On main, 4 of the 9 cases fail:

```
FAIL  media types > the timeline takes clip.m4v as video
FAIL  media types > the timeline takes assets/Take 2.M4V as video
AssertionError: expected null to be 'video' // Object.is equality
FAIL  media types > the timeline takes song.flac as audio
FAIL  media types > the timeline takes voice.FLAC as audio
AssertionError: expected null to be 'audio' // Object.is equality
```

With the fix, all 9 pass, along with the existing `timelineAssetDrop.test.ts` (40 tests in all).

On the server, two new cases (`mediaValidation.test.ts`: a `.flac` upload is probed; `mediaMetadata.test.ts`: a `.flac` file is audio) fail on main's lists and pass with the fix. Studio and studio-server typecheck, lint and format check pass.

## Before

title: perf(studio): a host's first screen can import Studio's UI and Player without the editor
body:
## What changes for a user

Nothing inside Studio. A host app whose first screen needs only Studio's buttons, menus, popovers, fields and the `Player` can import those without pulling in the editor. Bundled the way a host app builds it, those imports drop from 3823 KB to 354 KB, with no CodeMirror, parsers, shader transitions, linkedom, gsap, mediabunny or html2canvas. Existing imports are unchanged.

## How

- `packages/studio/src/ui.ts` holds the UI-primitives export block that `src/index.ts` spelled out. The root re-exports it, so both entries share one list.
- `HyperframesLogo` moved from `components/StudioHeader.tsx` into `components/ui/HyperframesLogo.tsx`, unchanged. In the header it pulled the Studio contexts, telemetry and the dock into `./ui`; the header now imports it.
- `src/playerEntry.ts` exports only `Player`. The existing `player/index.ts` also carries the timeline, which pulls in mediabunny, gsap and the parsers (1440 KB for `Player` through it).
- Two entries in `package-subpaths.json` (exports generated with `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs --write`), each also a tsup entry. Code splitting was already on, so a light entry loads only the chunks it reaches.

| Import | Contains |
| --- | --- |
| `@hyperframes/studio/ui` | `Button`, `IconButton`, `Tabs`, `Tooltip`, `cn`, the `Menu` family, `Popover`, `Input` / `fieldText`, `NumberField`, `Select`, `Slider`, `Toggle`, `HyperframesLoader`, `HyperframesLogo` and their types |
| `@hyperframes/studio/player` | `Player` |

`docs/packages/studio.mdx` lists both.

## Before

![main: mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da361735-ba18-44bc-be69-5e427ae029fa)
![main: after release, Box A and Box B selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1b07a349-0da8-4de7-a62d-601aca434926)

main. Studio opened on a three-box fixture, with a drag from empty canvas across two boxes, shot mid-drag and after release. The label in the corner of each shot names the build it came from.

![branch: after release, Box A and Box B selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a46c3bf-1a14-4f4b-a846-befd4fed3f5e)

This branch, same fixture and drag: Studio behaves the same.

## What I measured

A host-style bundle (esbuild, browser, minified, React external) of the built `dist`:

| Imports | Before (root) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cn, Button, Menu, MenuItem, ContextMenu, Popover, fieldText, Player` | 3823 KB, every heavy package | 354 KB from `./ui` + `./player`, none |
| the same without `Player` | 3823 KB | 236 KB from `./ui` |

- `packages/studio/src/lightEntries.test.ts` makes core's and the parsers' roots, the SDK, shader transitions, CodeMirror, the dock, mediabunny, gsap, linkedom and html2canvas throw on load, then imports each light entry's source (read from the descriptor). Pointing `./ui` at the root entry fails it with "a light entry loaded gsap"; exporting the Studio header from `./ui` fails it with "a light entry loaded dockview-react".

The one failure in that run was this new test timing out at the 5 s default while transforming the icon set; with a 30 s timeout it passes in 16 s. After the logo move, the guard and the three header test files pass (14 tests).
- `bun run build`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `node scripts/package-subpaths.mjs`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`: all exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A host app switching its imports; that follows once this is published.
- Module evaluation time in a browser; the measure above is bundle size.
- Adding `"sideEffects"` to the package. With separate entries a host no longer needs it, and marking modules side-effect free across Studio is a wider change.

title: fix(studio): unmounting mid-edit saves the typed words, as blur does
body:
## What this fixes

If Studio's editing overlay goes away while an in-place text edit is open, the typed words stay on screen but are never saved or reverted, and they are gone after the next reload. Studio can hit this today: hovering a block card in the Catalog while typing shows the block preview, which replaces the overlay. A host that embeds the overlay (#4640) hits it whenever it removes the overlay mid-edit while the preview stays mounted.

Now:

- **Unmounting mid-edit saves, the same as clicking away does.** The in-place editor's unmount runs its normal commit. It reads the commit through a ref, so a new commit function on a re-render never closes an open edit.
- **In-place text is not saved once the preview is read-only.** The save path for in-place text now refuses while the preview is read-only, as moves, resizes and rotations already do, and puts the old text back, as read-only's cancel does while the overlay is mounted. It reads the current value through a ref, because an unmounting editor saves through the handler from its last render.

This builds on #4640, which added `onTextEditingChange`.

## Before

Type a new word in the title, hover a Catalog block without clicking, move away, reload.

![Before: the title is back to its old words after the reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a71662f2-7f6a-41f8-89a7-e84acc30de46)

## After

Same steps. The typed word is still there after the reload, and it is in the saved file.

![After: the typed word survives the reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ef1abe3-70fc-44a2-8f9c-7b27a27dd8dd)

## What I measured

- Captures: headless Chrome against Studio's dev server, with the same scripted steps on this branch and on its base. On the base, the saved `index.html` stays byte-identical to the fixture. On this branch, it contains the typed word.
- Tests:
  - the in-place editor saves the typed text once when it unmounts mid-edit;
  - it keeps an open edit open when its commit function changes;
  - the overlay saves the typed words and reports `onTextEditingChange(false)` when it unmounts mid-edit;
  - an in-place text save reaches the writer while the preview is editable, and a handler taken before the preview turned read-only no longer writes after it did and puts the old text back.
- Each of these fails a test: unmount doing teardown only, an unmount effect keyed on the commit function, removing the read-only check or reading it from the closure, and removing the restore.
- Each run alone: `useInlineTextEdit.test.tsx` (31), `previewReadOnly.overlay.test.tsx` (28), `useDomEditTextCommits.test.tsx` (12), `InlineTextToolbar.test.tsx` (19). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet, comment citations and the fallow audit are green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- If the preview itself is removed in the same update as the overlay (a host closing its editor), the save is refused, as a blur is today. The save path will not write to a document that is gone.
- Only the in-place text save checks read-only; the design panel's text and style saves are unchanged.
- The block preview in the captures shows as a dark panel; its video does not play in headless Chrome. It still replaces the overlay, which is what the bug needs.

title: fix(studio-server): a cached-only thumbnail miss answers 204, so the page logs no error
body:
## What this fixes

Opening a project for the first time made the browser console log an error: Studio's preview poster asks for the cached first frame (`/thumbnail/index.html?...&cached=1`), and on a cache miss the server answered `404`. Chrome reports every 404 as "Failed to load resource", so any script that treats console errors as fatal failed on a fresh project.

A cache-only miss is expected, not an error, so the route now answers `204 No Content` instead, with the same `Cache-Control: no-cache` a hit carries, so nothing keeps the empty answer once the frame exists. It still never starts a render on a `cached=1` request.

## Visible change

None in Studio. The poster image still fails to load on a miss, so it falls back exactly as before (the live preview shows, and the poster is rendered for the next open); the console simply stays clean.

Checked with two images side by side: in Chrome the one answered `204` fires its error handler and logs nothing, while the one answered `404` fires it and logs "Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404"; in Firefox both fire the error handler. Safari was not tried.

## Tests

`routes/thumbnail.test.ts`: a cache-only request on a miss now gets `204` with an empty body and `no-cache`, and starts no render; a hit still returns the image.

Results: studio-server `tsc`, whole-tree `oxfmt --check` and `bun run lint`, fallow clean; the thumbnail route tests and Studio's preview component tests pass. With the old `404` restored, the updated test fails.

title: test(core): findProjects stop tests fit Windows' time budget and pin a stopped walk ending
body:
## What

The two `findProjects` stop tests build 65 projects instead of 200, and each gets a 20 s timeout. Test-only; `findProjects` is unchanged.

## Why

"stops the search when onProject throws" timed out at the default 5 s on windows-latest. Both stop tests wrote 400 files inside the test body, so the file writes counted against the test's time budget, and on Windows they used up most of it before the search began.

## Why 65

The walk visits up to 64 folders at once, so 65 is the smallest tree that still has a folder queued when the first project stops the search. Two things are pinned:

- The check in `report()` that returns when the search has stopped. Removing it gives 64 `onProject` calls instead of 1, and 64 found projects instead of 1.
- The walk finishing once stopped with folders still queued (`pending.length === 0 || stopped()`). Removing `|| stopped()` makes both tests hang until their timeout.

Fewer projects would leave the second point unpinned: with every folder already scheduled, the queue is empty at the stop and the walk ends anyway. The 20 s timeout leaves room for Windows to write the 130 files.

The pump's own `!stopped()` check was not pinned before this change and still is not.

## Checks

- `projects.test.ts`: 14/14, three runs in a row. Each of the two removals above fails both stop tests.
- `oxfmt --check .`, `bun run lint`, and `tsc --noEmit` in packages/core pass.

title: fix(studio-server): the server loads where sharp's native binary is missing
body:
## What changes for a user

`@hyperframes/studio-server` now loads on a platform where sharp's native binary is missing, for example a host app's test run on a runner that reports a different platform. Before, the whole package failed to import because one route imported sharp at the top level. Now sharp loads when the first JPEG thumbnail is made. Where it cannot load, the server logs one warning with sharp's own error, and JPEG thumbnail requests answer 422 ("image unavailable"), like any other thumbnail it cannot make.

## How

`packages/studio-server/src/routes/imageThumbnail.ts` was the only non-test module importing sharp. It now loads sharp once, on the first thumbnail, through `loadSharp()` instead of at the top of the file. A failed load warns once, and `generateThumbnail` checks for sharp before it reads the image. The route's existing error handling already answers 422 for a thumbnail it cannot make. The built `dist/index.js` keeps it as a dynamic `import("sharp")`.

## What I measured

- `packages/studio-server/src/routes/imageThumbnail.withoutSharp.test.ts` (new) makes `sharp` throw on load, then checks that the package index imports and that two requests for a real JPEG (made with the real sharp) answer 422 with exactly one warning. With sharp back at the top level, both tests fail. With the mock removed, a working sharp answers 200 and the test fails. Without the memo, it warns per request and the test fails.
- The built `dist/index.js` loads in node with a resolve hook that makes `sharp` unresolvable.
- The whole `packages/studio-server` suite: 884 passed, 2 skipped, run on the first commit; after the second, the thumbnail tests (10) re-ran and pass. `bun run build`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check`: all exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real platform without sharp's binary; the absence was simulated in vitest and with a node resolve hook.

title: perf(cli): load each command's code only when that command runs
body:
## What

`hyperframes lint`, `compositions`, `info` and every `--help` start about twice as fast. With telemetry off, `lint` drops from 0.70 s to 0.36 s and the root `--help` from 0.50 s to 0.04 s.

## Why it was slow

src/cli.ts already `import()`s each command lazily, but tsup built one 10.4 MB `dist/cli.js` with `splitting: false`. That has two costs:

- Every command parsed the whole bundle.
- In a single ESM bundle, the static imports of externals (`sharp`, `hono`, `@hono/node-server`, `postcss`, `adm-zip`, ...) are hoisted to the top, so every command loaded them, native `sharp` included.

## The change

`splitting: true` in packages/cli/tsup.config.ts. Each command becomes its own chunk, loaded only when that command runs:

- `dist/cli.js` is now 16 KB.
- `lint` no longer loads `sharp`, `ws`, `adm-zip` or `brotli`.

`bin/hyperframes.mjs` and the worker entries are unchanged. There is also a small timing script, `bun run bench:startup` (`packages/cli/scripts/bench-startup.mjs`). It times spawn to exit, N runs per command after one warm-up, and reports the nearest-rank median and p90.

## Timings

Same machine, same project (`hyperframes init --example warm-grain`), `bun run bench:startup <project> --runs 10` (one discarded warm-up run per command). The runs alternate between the base (main with the auto-update fix from #4637) and this branch, three rounds each. Each cell is the median of the three round medians, in seconds.

Linux x64, 8 cores, a shared machine at load 13 to 15:

| command | base, telemetry off | this PR, telemetry off | base, telemetry on | this PR, telemetry on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--help` | 0.51 | 0.05 | 0.66 | 0.05 |
| `lint --help` | 0.57 | 0.27 | 0.63 | 0.23 |
| `lint` | 1.00 | 0.46 | 0.79 | 0.42 |
| `compositions` | 0.67 | 0.36 | 0.63 | 0.35 |
| `info` | 0.57 | 0.43 | 0.63 | 0.29 |

A quieter single pass on the same machine measured this branch at 0.40 s for `lint`, 0.27 s for `compositions` and 0.26 s for `info`.

macOS (Apple M4 Pro, Node 22), the same change on an earlier base, measured under heavy load (20 to 35) and so noisier:

| command | main, telemetry off | this PR, telemetry off | main, telemetry on | this PR, telemetry on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--help` | 0.99 | 0.06 | 0.74 | 0.07 |
| `lint --help` | 0.66 | 0.35 | 0.69 | 0.35 |
| `lint` | 0.84 | 0.47 | 0.81 | 0.91 |
| `compositions` | 0.93 | 0.38 | 1.72 | 0.49 |
| `info` | 0.57 | 0.24 | 0.93 | 0.28 |

The one Mac cell where this PR is slower (`lint`, telemetry on) comes from one round at load 30 that measured 1.67 s.

## No behaviour change

Checked with both builds side by side on the same project:

- The root `--help`, each of the 44 subcommands' `--help`, and `--version`: byte-identical.
- The output of `lint`, `compositions` and `info`: byte-identical.
- A real `render` through the split build (it exercises the `import.meta.url` sibling lookups, such as the shader worker) produced a 10 s, 300-frame 1080p MP4.
- The CLI suite passes: 274 files, 3894 tests. So do `tsc --noEmit` and `scripts/ci/cli-telemetry-e2e.mjs` against the built CLI.
- `hyperframes upgrade` replaces the package and then uses only code it already loaded, so it keeps working. Since #4637 the auto-update waits for running commands, so a long `preview` never loses its chunk files mid-session.
- The unused `registry/localSemantic` entry is gone. Nothing imports it (catalog bundles the source), and with splitting, its two copies under `dist/skills/` would have imported chunks from the wrong folder.

## Known gap

Telemetry now loads as its own chunk instead of instantly. A crash in the first few milliseconds, before that chunk loads, can still lose its error event. Normal completion waits for telemetry, as before. The telemetry chunk is large because two telemetry modules import one helper each from the engine and core package roots; slimming that is a separate change.

title: fix(studio): the shortcut list shows only keyframe keys that work
body:
## What

Studio's shortcut list showed keyframe keys that do nothing:

- **H** "Toggle hold / bezier" and **U** "Expand / collapse properties" were listed in the app and in the docs. `useKeyframeKeyboard` had branches for them, but its only caller never passes those handlers, so neither key did anything, with or without a keyframe selected.
- The docs also listed **J / Shift+J** "jump to the previous or next keyframe" and **arrow keys** "nudge selected keyframes". J shuttles playback, and the arrows nudge the selected canvas element; neither ever touched a keyframe.

This removes them from the in-app list and from the docs (the shortcuts page and the animation guide):

- **H**: there is no hold/bezier toggle action to reuse; the Inspector sets a "hold" ease preset per keyframe.
- **U**: the expand action works on a track row or group, not on a keyframe selection.
- **J** and **arrows**: binding them to keyframes would clash with playback's shuttle and frame step.

**K** stays, relabelled "Add / remove keyframe at playhead" to match the toolbar tooltip (it removes when the playhead is on a keyframe). The list and the key handler now read K from the same constant, like the fullscreen, split and record keys. The unreachable branches are deleted from `useKeyframeKeyboard`; nothing called them, so no behaviour changes. `useKeyframeKeyboard` is not part of the package's exports.

## Verification

- `useKeyframeKeyboard.test.tsx`: "every key the Keyframes section lists does something with a keyframe selected" fails on main (H and U) and passes here. Two more tests pin what K already does: it adds only while enabled and leaves J and the arrows to playback, and it stays playback's stop key with nothing keyframeable selected.
