title: fix(core): a CSS animation a class adds mid-clip plays from where it starts
body:
## What this fixes

Since #4554, a CSS animation that a class adds partway through a clip shows its end state after a seek when its element already animates. #4554 made the CSS adapter read an element's live CSS animations on each pass and seek all of them from the clip's start, which fixed a late clip whose animation the browser replaces when the clip is shown. It also caught animations the page adds later: a second animation, or one that replaces the first, was seeked as if it had run since the clip began. A 1 s slide added at 2 s read 100 px at 2.5 s instead of 50.

Now:

- **The CSS adapter drives only the animations the page authored.** At discover it records the `animation-name`s each element carries in computed style, which a `display: none` clip keeps. On each pass it drives a live animation only if its element carried that name then. The late-clip case from #4554 still works: the browser's replacement has the same name. One owner in `adapters/cssAnimation.ts` records and answers this.
- **Animations added later go to the WAAPI adapter**, as they did before #4554, and start where they are first seen. That adapter now keeps scanning the page on each seek while the page authors any CSS animation. Before, it stopped scanning after a discover that found nothing live, for example when every CSS animation sat in a clip hidden at the start; without the scan, a class-added animation would not be driven at all.
- **A film with no `data-duration` counts animations in clips hidden at load again.** Since #4554 such a film reported only what was live at load (1 s where 7 s is right), because a hidden clip has no animation object yet. The CSS adapter now also reads each animation's end from computed style at discover (delay plus duration times iteration count; `infinite` has no end) and takes the later of that and the live animations.
- Names are read the way computed style writes them. They split on unescaped commas and CSS whitespace (space, tab, newline, form feed) and keep escapes whole: an escaped comma or space, or a hex escape with its trailing space, as Chrome writes a name that starts with a digit (`\35 nm`, or `\35 ` for `5`). A no-break space or other non-ASCII space, which computed style leaves raw, stays inside its name. A quoted keyword such as `"none"` matches. The timing lists pair with those names by position, so each name keeps its own delay and duration.

## What I measured

- Real headless Chrome 153, translateX px at 2.5 s for a 1 s slide a class adds at 2 s (ideal 50). Main and this branch were measured on fresh builds of each, two loads per case; the before-#4554 column is from an earlier run:

  | Case | before #4554 | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Element already animating, second animation added | 50 | 100 | 50 |
  | Same, the added animation replaces the first | 50 | 100 | 50 |
  | Nothing live at load, second animation added | 50 | 100 | 50, still 50 while paused |
  | Same, replaced | 50 | 100 | 50 |
  | Play, then pause at 2.25 s (ideal 25), three film shapes | 23.2 to 25.1 | 100 | 23.8 to 24.9, unchanged 500 ms later |
  | Paused jump from load to 2.5 s | 0, then 10 at 2.6 s | 100 | 0, then 10 at 2.6 s |
  | Authored `"n,m"` animation in a later clip, seek to 3 s | 0 | 50 | 50 |
  | Render worker starting at 2.2 s, read at 2.5 s | 30 | 100 | 30 |
  | Authored names Chrome escapes, quotes or keeps raw (escaped space, leading digit, digits only, no-break space, no-break space plus a second name, quoted comma, quoted comma with a space, quoted `"none"`, trailing space, two names with a trailing space) | not measured | 50 each | 50 each (the two no-break-space cases read 0 at this branch's previous head) |

  Film length with no `data-duration` and a CSS animation in a clip at 3 s:

  | Case | before #4554 | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | At load | 7 | 1 | 7 |
  | After a seek to 5 s, with a 1 s GSAP timeline | 9 | 1 | 9 (7 with #4555's fix on top) |
  | Unequal lists (`n\,m, slide`, durations `1s, 1s, 9s`, delays `0s, 1s`), animation end | not measured | 9 | 2 |

  #4554's own cases read as on main: a late clip whose animation the browser replaces, an authored delay while the clip is hidden, nested clip timing, and seeking back over an animation without fill.
- Tests: the CSS adapter seeks the authored animation and leaves a class-added or replacing one alone, records every name and only on its own element, and forgets names at the next discover; names with a trailing space, a leading digit, digits only, a no-break space (for the name match and for the timing lists) and a quoted keyword match; a hidden clip's end counts every iteration; a live animation the fallback pose shortened does not shorten the length; the lists pair by name, not by every comma. The WAAPI adapter keeps scanning after an empty discover while the page authors CSS animations; the runtime drives a class-added animation, with nothing live at load, from where the playhead meets it and from a render worker's first frame. Each of these breaks fails a test: keeping names across a discover (three ways), dropping the positive-length guard, counting one iteration, dropping the computed end, using it only with nothing live, no quoted-keyword match, the old splitter, no hex escape, JavaScript's wider whitespace, and splitting the timing lists on every comma.
- Each run alone: `adapters/css.test.ts` (55), `adapters/waapi.test.ts` (23), `adapters/lottie.test.ts` (36), `init.test.ts` (183), `init.swapScenes.test.ts` (45), `transportPark.test.ts` (28), `timeline.test.ts` (70). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A seek or a render worker that starts partway into an animation that began mid-clip starts it where it is first seen, as before #4554: a worker starting at 2.2 s reads 30 px at 2.5 s instead of 50 (26.7 when frames run back to back with no pause).
- With nothing live at load, the WAAPI adapter now also pins CSS transitions and other late animations on each seek, as it did before #4554 whenever it tracked anything; with 200 GSAP-driven opacity transitions that is about 400 more `currentTime` writes per frame, with no measurable time change. Still one `document.getAnimations()` call per frame.
- The length read from computed style counts an animation whose name has no `@keyframes`, or one on an element hidden some other way, so a film with no `data-duration` can come out longer (a stray `animation: missing 30s` makes it 30 s).
- With a GSAP timeline and no `data-duration`, the reported length can grow after a seek (7 to 9 s above), as before #4554; the stacked fix for #4555 anchors those animations at their clip's start and keeps it at 7.
- Computed-style names are a snapshot taken at discover: a class that removes an animation later still counts it until the next discover.
- An element whose class removes an animation and later adds the same name back gets a new animation that counts as authored and is seeked from the clip's start.
- A scene swap after a class has added an animation counts that animation as authored from then on.
- Browsers other than Chrome.

title: fix(core): shadow-root and pseudo-element CSS animations land on the same frame every load
body:
Fixes #4555. Stacked on #4658; review after it (the diff here is against its head).

## What this fixes

A CSS animation inside a shadow root, or on a `::before`/`::after` pseudo-element, landed on a different frame after the same seek on each page load, in Studio's preview and in renders. The CSS adapter drives only an element's own animations, so these belong to the WAAPI adapter, which anchored every animation at its own live `currentTime` when it first saw it. For a CSS animation running since the page loaded, that is however long loading took.

Shadow-root animations had a second cause: `document.getAnimations()` does not list them (checked on Chrome 113 and 152), so nothing drove them and they ran on the wall clock.

Now:

- **CSS animations the page authored are anchored at their clip's start**, as the CSS adapter already does for light-DOM elements: seek `t` gives `max(0, t − clipStart)`. Authored means that the element, or its `::before`/`::after`, carried the animation's name in computed style at discover, which a `display: none` clip keeps. One the page adds later (a class the timeline adds mid-clip, an element a script appends) starts where it is first seen, with no wall-clock offset. The clip is found in the shared `adapters/cssAnimation.ts` from the stacked PR, which now also finds the clip: walk out of shadow trees to the outermost host, take the nearest element with `data-start`, and resolve it through the runtime's start resolver so nested compositions keep their offsets.
- **Open shadow roots are scanned** alongside `document.getAnimations()` in the one page scan each seek already does. They are collected at each discover.
- **Shadow-root CSS animations count toward the WAAPI adapter's scan**, which the stacked PR keeps running while the page authors any CSS animation.

Script-created animations (`el.animate()`) and CSS transitions keep today's anchoring.

## What I measured

- Real headless Chrome, the runtime built from main and from this branch, five page loads each (translateX px; measured at an earlier head of this branch, whose shadow and pseudo-element paths this head keeps):

  | Case | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | Shadow-root animation, seek 0.5 / 2 / 3.5 s | 19–27 / 25–34 / 31–40, varying by load | 12.5 / 50 / 87.5 every load |
  | Shadow host in a clip at 3 s, seek 4 s | 5.83–6.25 | 25 every load |
  | `::before` animation, seek 0.5 / 2 / 3.5 s | up to 13.75 / 51.25 / 88.75 | 12.5 / 50 / 87.5 every load |
  | `::before` whose owner is in a clip at 3 s, seek 4 s | 0 to 6.25 | 25 every load |
  | Light-DOM animation in a clip at 0 | 12.5 / 50 / 87.5 | same |

  Against the stacked PR's head, 58 of 60 behaviour cases read the same; the other two differ by playback timing (49.3 to 50.1, ideal 50.2). The paused-tracking table matches within about 1 px, and a clip hidden through a seek then shown reads 0 at 6.5 s and 25 at 8 s on both.
- With no `data-duration`, a CSS animation in a clip at 3 s and a 1 s GSAP timeline, the film length stays 7 s after a seek to 5 s (9 s on the stacked PR alone). A quoted `"none"` name reads 50, where this branch's previous head read 0. On this head a shadow-root animation reads 50 px at 2 s, and a seek or a render seek makes one `document.getAnimations()` call (shadow roots are read in the same pass).
- Real headless Chrome, sequential render seeks: a class added at 2 s, a `::before` and an element appended at 2 s, each a 1 s slide, read 50 px at 2.5 s, as on the stacked PR's head.
- Tests: `waapi.test.ts` covers an animation added mid-clip (class, `::before`, appended element) starting where it is first seen, a CSS animation whose live `currentTime` is non-zero when first seen being seeked to clip time, a pseudo-element anchored at its owner's clip, nested shadow roots anchored at the outer host's clip, a script-created animation keeping today's anchor, scanning continuing after the adapter's CSS animations are cancelled, and duration inferred from the clip start. `init.test.ts` has a clip whose host, `::before` and a leaf two shadow roots deep all land at the same clip time through `seek` and `renderSeek`, with each root scanned once per pass. With main's runtime source and this branch's tests, 8 of the waapi tests and 11 of the init tests fail (some are the stacked PR's).
- Each run alone: `adapters/waapi.test.ts` (33), `adapters/css.test.ts` (56), `adapters/cssAnimation.test.ts` (3), `adapters/lottie.test.ts` (36), `init.test.ts` (190), `init.swapScenes.test.ts` (45), `transportPark.test.ts` (28), `timeline.test.ts` (70). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A jump straight into the middle of an animation that started mid-clip starts it at the jump (it was wrong there before too).
- In a film with no `data-duration`, shadow-root and pseudo-element animations in a later clip now count from their clip's start, so such a film can come out longer, matching light-DOM animations.
- Each seek reads every open shadow root's animations: about 0.2 to 0.4 ms per seek with 50 roots, more with hundreds (measured on a loaded machine; films without shadow roots are unaffected).
- Closed shadow roots cannot be reached; a shadow root attached after the last discover is picked up at the next one.
- Animations a script creates before the runtime loads still land up to a frame off by load (#4559).
- A Lottie inside a timed clip within a composition still counts from the composition's start, not the clip's; the CSS timing here counts from the clip.
- The producer's rendered-video baselines.

title: fix(catalog): drop preview links to files that were never uploaded
body:
## What

Catalog preview links in `registry-item.json` pointed at files that were never uploaded, and the docs pages guessed a poster URL for every item without one:

- 61 preview URLs on 60 items answered 403 from the CDN. Each is a missing object: the response is identical to a made-up key on the same path, while uploaded previews answer 200.
- The docs pages guessed a poster URL for every item without a preview; 232 of those guesses answered 403.
- `generate-catalog-previews.ts` caught every per-item render error and exited 0, so a failed render looked like a green run.

Catalog previews play live in the player, so this removes the dead links and stops guessing. It adds no new preview links and uploads nothing.

## Changes

- **The generator fails when an item fails.** It still renders every item, then exits 1 naming the ones that failed (a runner without a WebGPU adapter is still not a failure). `catalog-previews.yml` already counts a non-zero exit as a failed item.
- **A pruner for dead links.** `scripts/prune-catalog-previews.ts` replaces `backfill-block-previews.ts`. For each existing preview URL it removes only a definitive 403/404; a 200, a 5xx or a timeout keeps the link. It never adds a `preview` field, never adds a poster or video, and never changes a URL. It rewrites only the `preview` entry and refuses a rewrite that would change anything else or leave two `preview` keys.
- **One run of the pruner.** 61 dead URLs removed on 60 manifests; nothing else in those files changed, and every other manifest is untouched. `simulated-cursor` is left out, as it is being removed in a separate change.
- **The docs pages use the `preview` field only.** No guessed poster or video URLs; an item without a linked video falls back to the page's live player or notice, as before.
- **A CI check.** In the Catalog payloads job, every preview URL in a manifest the PR changes must answer 200. It checks eight items at a time with a short timeout, so a CDN outage fails the job in minutes (a re-run clears a brief outage).

## Verification

- Tests for the generator, the pruner (including the refused rewrite shapes and the transient-error rule), the check and the docs pages pass. Each rule turns a test red when broken, including a pruner that would add a link or remove one on a 5xx.
- Every removed URL answers 403, and every link left answers 200. The only other line change is a kept video URL losing its trailing comma where the poster after it was removed.
- The check passes this branch ("Preview links verified for 60 changed item(s)") and fails a link that does not answer 200.
- Generated catalog files are not committed; they regenerate on publish. Lint, format, typecheck, the audit gate, the source-PR check and the deletion guard pass.

title: fix(studio): carve and duck follow each clip's trim and speed
body:
## What you can do now

Trim a voice or music bed, set its in-point, or speed it up or down, and the carve and duck land where that clip actually plays. Before, the carve read every voice and the bed from the start of its file at 1x, so a trimmed or sped-up clip got its dip in the wrong place: the bed ducked after the voice had already ended, and stayed loud while it spoke.

## Why

Export plays each clip from its in-point, for its duration, at its speed (pitch kept). The carve analysis ignored all three for both the voices and the bed, so what Studio measured was not what the render plays.

## The fix

- One reader for "how a clip plays its file" (in-point, speed or speed ramp, duration), shared by the carve and by level-out, so the two cannot drift apart.
- Each voice and the bed are put on their own clip clock before the analysis: at 1x an exact slice of the file; at any other speed a pitch-kept stretch, so the bands match what export plays.
- Speech after the bed has stopped playing no longer shapes the carve.
- Known limit: the stretch reads about 1.3 dB quiet off 1x (up to about 3 dB on pure tones), so a sped-up voice asks for a slightly deeper duck than export needs.

## Tests

Each fails on main:

- `cuts where a trimmed voice speaks, not where its file does`: `expected { speaking: false, after: -2 } to deeply equal { speaking: true, after: +0 }`
- `cuts over half the source length for a voice at 2x`: `expected { speaking: false, …(1) } to deeply equal { speaking: true, after: +0 }`
- `ducks against the part of the bed that plays`: `expected 0 to be less than 0`
- `ignores speech after the bed has stopped playing`: `expected 4000 to be 1000`
- `ignores speech after a bed with no duration runs out, when it ducks`: `expected 4000 to be 1000` with the cut to the decoded bed removed
- `ignores speech after a 3 s bed file with no duration, without ducking` and `... with a duration longer than its file, without ducking`: `expected 4000 to be 1000`
- `clipAudioOnItsClock` unit tests (exact slice at 1x, length at 2x, pitch kept) and `readClipClock`: the module does not exist on main.

## Not covered

The carve re-analyses only when its voice list or strength changes, so trimming or re-speeding a clip after the carve exists leaves the old carve in place, as moving a voice already does today.

## Before

The fixture: a 12 s steady music bed, and a 10 s voice file that is silent for its first half, with 1 s tone bursts at 5, 7 and 9 s. The voice clip starts at 2 s on the timeline with a 5 s in-point and a 5 s duration, so its bursts play at 2, 4 and 6 s.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a433e0db-eeda-4124-8715-147dc97da7f4)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/314af13b-7826-437b-8bdf-f25978684e99

The carve read the voice file from its start, so it ducked the bed at 7-12 s, after the voice had finished. Bed level under the bursts: -18.0 dB.

## After

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/472bf6ae-e2ec-47e9-83f1-e10171d7c56a)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89d21383-442c-43b3-af6a-1adbefb3bd79

The bed dips at 2-7 s, under the bursts. Bed level under the bursts: -23.7 dB.

title: fix(studio): shortcut labels line up within each section whatever the key width
body:
## What this fixes

In Studio's shortcuts panel, each label started wherever its keycap happened to end. Keys wider than the keycap's minimum (Space, ⇧Click, ⌘ Scroll, Drag center) pushed their label right, so the labels in a section zigzagged.

Each section's shortcuts now sit in a two-column grid: the key column is as wide as that section's widest keycap, and every label in the section starts at the same place. Keycaps keep their own width.

## Before

![Before: Editing section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dc8386f-f392-4aae-91c2-46c83775dcb5)
![Before: gesture and canvas sections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/242a9a32-99db-444f-a46c-91d86ea6055f)

## After

![After: Editing section](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1db53dac-9230-4abc-865b-06e64b1d432b)
![After: gesture and canvas sections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01235d2c-3082-4eb5-8600-141b3aaf69e4)

## What I measured

- Label x positions, read in headless Chrome against Studio's dev server with the panel opened from its player-controls button, on main and on this branch:
  - Before: labels in one section differed by up to 24 px. The gesture modifiers section, for example, had five different starts, from 845 to 869.
  - After: every label within a section starts at the same x.
- Keycap widths are unchanged: 36 px for one- or two-character keys, up to 80 px for "Drag center".
- Labels on two lines: 1 of 43 before, 2 of 43 after. "Record rotationX / rotationY" now wraps, because its section's column follows the 62 px "⌘ Scroll" key and the panel keeps its minimum width.
- `ShortcutsPanel.test.tsx` (10) passes; typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet and the fallow audit are green.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Labels line up within a section, not across the whole panel. One column for the whole panel would take the width of the widest key anywhere (80 px), which narrowed every label and wrapped more of them.
- The "Work area" in/out rows above the list keep their own layout.

title: fix(studio): a clip dropped on a row stays on that row at the nearest free time
body: ## What a user can do now Drag a clip, or drop an asset, onto a row that already holds clips of its kind, and it stays on that row's track: at the time you let go if that time is free, otherwise at the nearest free time on that track. The timeline no longer opens a new track above the row, pushes the row's clips down, or moves the clip to time 0. Before this change, dragging a 5 s clip that starts at 2 s onto a row holding a clip at 0 to 6 s opened a new track above that row and pushed the row's clip down. Dropping it on the top row moved it to 0 s. ## Decisions 1. A clip dropped onto an existing row lands on that row at the nearest free time to where it was released. It never inserts a new track and never overlaps a clip on that row. For an asset drop, "that row" is the row's track in the file, and the clips checked are the ones of the dropped file's kind on that track. 2. The snap to 0 for a clip that lands on an empty main track no longer applies to drops. A clip lands where it was released, or at the nearest free time under decision 1. Why: a drop onto a row means "put it here". Opening a track, bumping the clip to another row, or moving it to 0 each put it somewhere the user did not point at, and the timeline then looked different from what they aimed for. ## The rule, precisely - **Nearest free time**: among all start times at which the clip fits on the row without overlapping another clip, the one closest to the release time. The dragged clip itself does not count. A tie goes to the later time. Clips that touch end to start do not overlap. - **No gap long enough**: the space after the row's last clip always fits, so the clip goes right after the last clip. - The edges of the clips around a gap are rounded inward to centiseconds, the precision the timeline writes, so a written start can never overlap its neighbour. A group's lower limit (below) is used as it is, not rounded. - **A clip's own spot always counts**: released on or near where it already is, a clip keeps its start when that is the nearest free time, even between neighbours whose edges are not on centiseconds (3.333, 6.666). Keeping it rewrites nothing, so nothing is rounded. - **Empty space still opens a track**: a drop in the space above the first row, or below the last row, is not a drop onto a row. It keeps opening a new track, as before. The thin band at the edge between two rows now counts as the row it is on. - **Kind zones**: - Clip moves: a visual clip still lands in the visual rows and an audio clip in the audio rows. An audio clip dragged onto a timeline with no audio row still opens the first audio row. - Asset drops never clamp to a zone, and an audio file shows in the audio rows whichever track it is written to. So only clips of the dropped file's kind (audio or not) count as obstacles for it. - An asset dropped on a row of its own kind is written to that row's track in the file, the same translation clip moves use. Rows and file tracks differ when an audio clip is written on a visual track number, or when track numbers skip. Only clips on that file track block it. - An asset dropped on a row of the other kind (for example audio onto a visual row) is written with the row's number, as on main. Clips of its kind already on that track in the file still block it, so it never overlaps them. - **Group moves**: - The clips a group drag moves are the selected clips that can move. A locked clip swept into the selection stays put, so it still blocks the grabbed clip. One helper decides this set for the obstacle check, the group limit and the commit. - The grabbed clip does not treat the other moving clips as obstacles, because they move with it. - The group's limit is the start at which the first moving clip reaches its own floor: 0, or the start of its host composition for a clip inside a nested composition. A lone clip's limit is its own floor. Neither the grabbed clip's position nor the nearest free time goes further left than that, so every moving clip moves by the same amount. - **Multi-file drops**: - Each next file aims right after the previous one, and the files this drop has already placed count as obstacles. - When the first file opened a new track, the later files are checked only against this drop's own files, since nothing else is on that track. - Which track a file goes to is decided from the timeline's own clips, never from files this drop already placed. So every file of one drop follows the same track rule a single file would. ## The fix The placement decision had two owners, and both now follow one rule: - Clip moves: `resolveZoneDropPlacement` (`timelineCollision.ts`) now returns the landing row and start together. On a row it calls the new `resolveNearestFreeStart`, passing a lowest allowed start for group drags. `resolveGroupMovers` and `groupMoveFloor` (`timelineMultiDragPreview.ts`) are the one owner of the moving set and the group limit. They are used by the drag preview, the live ghosts of the other moving clips and the commit, and replace `clampGroupMoveDelta`. `resolveZoneDropPlacement` no longer relocates the clip to another free row or opens a track next to it, so the `preferInsertAbove` bias and the origin snap-back case are gone. The drag preview and the commit read the same start, so the ghost is where the clip lands. - Row-edge inserts: `resolveInsertRow` now opens a track only outside all rows. It is shared by clip moves and asset drops, so the asset-drop insert band goes away with it. The band helpers it used (`INSERT_BOUNDARY_BAND`, `getTimelineInsertBoundaryBand`, `getTimelineRowPositionFromY`) had no other users and are deleted. - Asset and file drops: `resolveDropTrack` (`timelineDropTrackInsert.ts`) returns the start as well as the track. A drop onto a row is translated to the row's file track (`authoredTrackForLane`, as clip moves do) and goes through the same `resolveNearestFreeStart`, against clips of the same kind on that track. The multi-file loop in `useTimelineAssetDropOps.ts` feeds it the files already placed, and marks every clip it passes in as belonging to the target file, since track numbers only compare within one file. - Main-track snap: `resolveMainTrackDropStart` and `resolveDragLandingStart` are deleted. The commit uses the preview's start as is. Not changed: - Block and composition drops. Their installers take only a track, never open one, and still land at the release time. - The ghost for an asset drop still shows the release time. The asset's length is only known after the drop, so the written start can end up later than where the ghost was. ## Merged with main Main now keeps a clip inside a nested composition from starting before its host composition, and gives it that floor in drags, trims and the commit. This branch had replaced the group clamp main changed for that, so the merge carries the rule into `groupMoveFloor`: each moving clip's floor is its host's start (`clampToHostStart`), not 0. Main also passes where the timeline draws 0 s (`contentOrigin`) to the scroll viewport; this branch builds the viewport props in `buildTimelineShellMeta`, which now takes and passes it. ## Out of scope In a group move, the other selected clips can still overlap clips on their own rows, as on main. Only the grabbed clip is placed by this rule. ## Tests New tests. Each one fails on main: - `timelineClipDragPreview.test.ts`, "a drop onto an occupied row stays on that row", drag preview plus commit: - Tag (starts at 2 s, 5 s long) dropped on the Subtitle row (0 to 6 s) lands on Subtitle's track at 6 s, with no insert. On main: `expected { … } to match object { insertRow: null, … }`, because main returns `insertRow: 1`. - Tag dropped on the top Title row stays on track 0 at 10 s, right after Title. On main it is an insert that snaps the start to 0. - The top and bottom edges of a row stay on that row. On main: `expected +0 to be null`. - "a move onto an occupied row lands at its nearest free time, ghost and commit alike". On main: `expected +0 to be null`. - `timelineCollision.test.ts`: `resolveNearestFreeStart` covers a free span, the nearer side, a tie going to the later time, a gap too short, the excluded clip, and centisecond bounds. It also covers the reported case (Tag onto the Subtitle row) through `resolveZoneDropPlacement`. On main, that case returns `{ track: 1, insertRow: 1 }`. - `timelineDragDrop.test.tsx`: - An asset released at the top edge of a row goes to that row with no insert row. On main: `expected { start: 10, track: 1, …(2) } to deeply equal { start: 10, track: 1 }`. - `resolveDropInsertRow` stays on the row at a boundary. On main: `expected 1 to be null`. - `useTimelineAssetDropOps.test.tsx`: - An asset dropped on an occupied row is written at the row's nearest free time. On main: `expected '

title: fix(core): bundling and rendering keep print-only, titled and non-CSS styles conditional
body:
## What

Bundling and rendering no longer turn a conditional stylesheet into an always-on one. A `<style media="print">`, a titled (alternate) style, a disabled or non-CSS stylesheet, and the same inside a composition, now keep their condition in the bundled film and in the render, and the two paths produce the same styles.

## Why

`coalesceHeadStylesAndBodyScripts` merged every head `<style>` into the first one, keeping only that one's `media` and `type`. So `<style media="print">p{color:blue}</style>` came out as an unconditional `p{color:blue}` and applied on screen. The render path (`packages/producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`) had its own copy of the same merge, and composition styles were copied as text only, so they lost their attributes on both paths.

## How

- **One decision, both paths.** `cssStyleMergeKey` and `headStyleRuns` (`packages/core/src/compiler/scriptRuns.ts`) decide which head styles may merge: only adjacent styles that the browser applies under the same condition (same `media`, trimmed and lowercased, with `all` treated as none; same `title`, an empty title counting as none; a CSS `type`). Adjacent runs only, so rule order never changes. The bundler and the render path both call it.
- **Linked sheets.** Each local `<link rel="stylesheet">` is inlined as its own `<style>` in its own place, carrying the link's `media` and `title`. A `disabled` link and a non-CSS `type` are left as links.
- **Composition styles.** The shared inliner now returns style records (text, `media`, `title`) instead of strings. `styleElementsFor` turns them into `<style>` elements on both paths, so a conditional composition style is its own element. A malformed `media` value then matches nothing instead of swallowing later CSS, and an `@import` in it stays at the top of its own sheet. Composition `<link>` elements keep `media`, `title`, `type` and `disabled` too. A non-CSS composition style is kept out of CSS.
- **One key for hoisted links.** `linkDedupeKey` (`scriptRuns.ts`) is href plus rel plus the link's condition from `cssStyleMergeKey`, plus `disabled`. `ensureExternalLinkTag` (`inlineSubCompositions.ts`) is the one place that adds a hoisted link; the bundler, the render and the runtime mount all compare by that key. Two compositions linking the same file under different conditions now each keep their own link; the same file under the same condition still collapses to one. Fetch attributes (`crossorigin`, `integrity`, `referrerpolicy`) are not part of the key, so a root link and a composition's link to the same file ship once, as on main.
- **Font dedupe.** `isAlwaysAppliedStyle` now asks `cssStyleMergeKey` for the unconditional key, so an alternate titled style is no longer a place to keep the only copy of an `@font-face`.
- **Link types.** A link's `type` is read by its MIME essence, so `text/css; charset=utf-8` counts as CSS on a `<link>` (Chrome applies it) and still does not on a `<style>` (Chrome does not).

**API note:** `InlineSubCompositionsResult.styles`, exported from `@hyperframes/core/compiler`, changes from `string[]` to `{ css, media?, title? }[]`. A caller that joined the styles as text needs to read `.css`.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests, each failing on main: print head style stays print-only; non-CSS style not merged into CSS; same-condition styles still merge (including `type="TEXT/CSS"` and `media=" ALL "`); rule order kept across a conditional style; each linked sheet at its link's place with its media; non-CSS and disabled links not inlined; titled styles merge only with the same title; composition print style kept as its own element (file and inline template); non-CSS composition style kept out of CSS.
- [x] Parity tests (`htmlCompiler.parity.test.ts`): render equals preview for mixed conditional head styles, and for conditional composition styles and links (invalid media keeps later compositions styled, a screen-media `@import` survives, titles kept).
- [x] Checked in headless Chrome on the bundle, the render and the Studio preview: the malformed-media and screen-`@import` cases, and titled and linked composition styles.
- [x] Films with only plain styles are unchanged: 150 repo fixture folders through `bundleToSingleHtml` (plain and Studio options) are byte-identical to the merge base apart from the inlined preview runtime (whose loader changed), and 139 of the 141 that render through `compileForRender` are byte-identical (the other two differ only in embedded font bytes, which also differ between two runs of the same head). None of them has a conditional style or link.
- [x] Review follow-ups, each failing without its fix: the shared-file link cases (print then plain, titled then plain, plain then print, print then screen, print twice, plain twice, alternate then plain, a root print link plus a composition plain link), the font kept in the untitled style when an alternate style repeats it, `type` and `disabled` carried on hoisted links, a charset link inlined and a charset style not, and a template with no matching root and a non-CSS style. A parity test checks the shared-file case in the bundle, the render and the runtime mount.
- [x] Core compiler and runtime loader tests 473 pass; producer compiler tests pass (vitest and bun); `tsc --noEmit` passes for core and producer.
- [x] No change under `packages/studio` or `packages/player`, so no before/after captures are needed.

## Known limits

- A stylesheet `<link>` between two head styles does not yet end a merge run, so the render can reorder a linked sheet against the styles around it (as on main). The fix changes the Studio preview's style placement too and lands with the follow-up that keeps a lifted `@import` under its style's media.
- An `@import` inside a conditional `<style>` is not yet kept under that condition by the render's import promotion, by the render's run merge when the import has its own media, or by the Studio bundle's import lifting. The follow-up that keeps a lifted `@import` under its style's media owns all three.
- Links hoisted from compositions carry `media`, `title`, `type`, `disabled` and `crossorigin`, but not yet `integrity`, `referrerpolicy`, `as` or `fetchpriority` in the bundle and the render (the runtime mount keeps them), as on main.
- Because fetch attributes are not compared, a root `<link crossorigin>` whose server sends no CORS headers still stands in for a composition's plain link to the same file, and that composition renders unstyled, as on main.
- The producer's font helpers keep their own "is this stylesheet applied" checks, which do not yet read a link's `type` by its MIME essence.
- A Studio scene edit that adds or removes a conditional style reloads the preview instead of swapping the scene in place (the runtime's existing fallback).

title: fix(media-use): never replace a voice, music or sound file the person put in the project
body:
Stacked on #4648 (its base branch); review that first.

## What

media-use's audio engine wrote to fixed names in the project and replaced whatever was there: a voice line to `assets/voice/<line id>.wav`, retrieved music to `assets/bgm/track.mp3`, locally made music to `assets/bgm/track.wav`, and a HeyGen sound effect to `assets/sfx/<name>.mp3`. A person's own `assets/sfx/whoosh.mp3` or `assets/voice/intro.wav` was silently overwritten.

Now the engine never replaces a file the person put there:

- If the target name is free, or the project's media manifest records the file there as made by the agent (`generated`, `search` or `bundled`), the engine writes there as before, so a rerun still replaces its own takes.
- Otherwise it writes to the first free name, `whoosh-2.mp3`, `whoosh-3.mp3`, and so on, records that file, and reports the switch as an anomaly: `assets/sfx/whoosh.mp3: kept, because the file there is yours ...; writing assets/sfx/whoosh-2.mp3 instead (audio_meta.json has the path used)`. A second run reuses the same `-2` file, because it is now recorded as the agent's.
- Voice paths are all picked before lines synthesize in parallel, so two lines never land on one free name (ids `hook` and `hook-2` with a person's `hook.wav` get `hook-2.wav` and `hook-2-2.wav`).
- One effect named by two cues shares one file; two different effects never do, even when one's own name is another's `-2` (`glitch` and `glitch 2` beside a person's `glitch.mp3` get `glitch-2.mp3` and `glitch-2-2.mp3`).
- A copy from the bundled sound library with no manifest record is reused when it is byte-for-byte the library file (an engine older than #4648 made it). A file recorded as the person's own is never reused, even with the library's bytes.

The rule that decides what counts as agent-made (`AGENT_SOURCES`) now lives in the manifest library next to the records, and `resolve --source` uses the same list. The tts, bgm and sfx references say where a file lands when the fixed name is taken.

Also fixed: generating music again over the engine's own `track.wav` left the old file in place until the new one was written, and `wait-bgm` treats any file there as finished, so it reported the old track as ready at once. The old track is now removed right before the generator starts.

## Upgrade note

Files written by an engine older than #4648 carry no manifest record, so they count as the person's own: the first run after upgrading writes `-2` names beside them, leaves the old files in place and says so in the anomalies. The run's `audio_meta.json` names the files it used.

## Known limits

- Ownership is read from the manifest only. A person who drops their own file over an engine-recorded name gets it replaced on the next run, since records carry no size or hash.
- Regenerating music while an earlier generator is still running is not handled here; wait-bgm can still report that run's output.
- With the library file missing, a HeyGen download at the library name stands in and is re-recorded as `bundled`.

## Tests

- skills, sound effects: a person's own `assets/sfx/whoosh.mp3` survives unchanged, the cue lands on `assets/sfx/whoosh-2.mp3` with the library's bytes, and a second run reuses that file. Fails on the base.
- skills, the Gemini engine pipeline test (the real engine with fixture providers): with a person's own `assets/voice/intro.wav` present, the voice line is written to `assets/voice/intro-2.wav`, recorded as `generated`, and the person's file survives. Fails on the base.
- skills, `agentWritePath`: a free name is used; a person's file, and a file recorded as `existing`, move the write to `-2` with one anomaly each; a recorded agent file and a reusable file are replaced silently; a person's `-2` moves it to `-3`; an agent-made `-2` is reused.
- skills, `voicePaths`: two lines never share a file when one's name is taken by the person.
- skills, HeyGen sound effects (fake fetch): two effects never share a file when one's name is taken by the person, on the first run and on a rerun where the `-2` is already recorded as the engine's; a repeated effect reuses its file. The bundled branch uses the same rule without a test of its own (it needs a library file literally named `<other>-2`).
- skills, bundled sound effects: the engine's earlier copy stands in for a library file this install lacks; a person's file with the library's bytes, recorded as their own, gets `-2`.
- skills, music: generating again removes the engine's old `track.wav` before the generator runs (a fake `python3` stands in for the model; skipped on Windows).

Each rule's test fails with that rule removed (8 mutations, all caught).

title: fix(studio): hide handles Studio would refuse to commit
fix(studio): the timeline reads clip speed with the same limits as playback
body:
## What you can do now

Trim a clip that plays faster than 5x (Studio's speed field goes up to 10x), and the frame under the playhead stays put. Before this change, a 1 s head trim on an 8x clip moved its in-point by 5 s instead of 8 s, so the picture jumped back 3 s of source the moment you let go.

## Why

Playback and export clamp a clip's speed to 0.1x to 10x (`MIN_PLAYBACK_RATE` / `MAX_PLAYBACK_RATE` in `@hyperframes/parsers`). The timeline store read `data-playback-rate` (and a media element's `defaultPlaybackRate`) through its own helper that clamped to 0.1x to 5x. The timeline then did its trim and split math at 5x for any clip authored faster than that. This covers head trims, the drag preview, the source-length limit on an edge drag, razor splits, and the waveform and filmstrip windows.

## The fix

Delete the local helper in `timelineElementHelpers.ts` and use parsers' `clampPlaybackRate`, the same function playback uses. The timeline and playback now share one speed range.

## Tests

`packages/studio/src/player/lib/timelineDOM.test.ts`:
- The canonical-rate cases now assert against `MAX_PLAYBACK_RATE` / `MIN_PLAYBACK_RATE` and cover 8, 10, 50 and 0.01. On main: `expected 5 to be 8`, `expected 5 to be 10`.
- New case: head-trimming an 8x clip by 1 s moves its in-point from 1 s to 9 s. On main: `expected [ 3, 6 ] to deeply equal [ 3, 9 ]`.

Studio typecheck, oxlint, format check and the comment checks pass.

## Before

A 60 s test-pattern video (the big number is the source second) at `data-playback-rate="8"`, starting at 2 s with its in-point at 4 s. The playhead sits at 00:03. Top: before the trim. Bottom: after dragging the head edge right by 1 s. Captions read the saved file. The in-point moves 4 to 9 (5x the trim), and the frame at 00:03 jumps from source 12 s to 9 s.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14afeceb-4449-40d4-a17f-4ce2e72516ae)

## After

Same steps. The in-point moves 4 to 12 (8x the trim), and the frame at 00:03 stays at source 12 s, the same frame it showed before the trim.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff1475a-10ab-47a0-8de5-63c113f3c714)

title: fix(fonts): resolve declared family names with missing spaces
body:
## Problem and result

A page can declare `Saira Extra Condensed` through Google Fonts but use `"Saira ExtraCondensed"` in CSS. Before this change, the requested family remained unresolved and strict font localization failed the render. Now, after the normal resolution paths fail, the producer can use a **unique family declared by the page** whose name differs only by spaces or separators (`-`, `_`, `+`). It emits the font faces under the name the CSS requested, so the CSS does not need rewriting.

The match uses only active, unconditional stylesheet sources and top-level declarations. Conditional or nested rules, disabled/alternate/titled/non-CSS stylesheets, and conditional imports cannot supply a global alias. Ambiguous matches stay unresolved. The existing required-first order and optional `var()` fallback fetch policy are preserved.

The CLI also names unresolved families in its failure line. It reads a structured family list rather than echoing the underlying error message, drops URL-shaped names, and bounds **only the stderr diagnostic** to eight names of 64 characters each. Those limits do not restrict which fonts the producer processes.

## Validation

- 194 focused producer and CLI tests passed with Bun 1.4.2. One existing macOS system-font locator test was filtered because its local locator times out.
- Changed-file `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- All hosted checks on this PR passed at head `67d7f6104`.

Replaces #4551 so this PR is authored by `terencecho`. The previous review and conflict-resolution discussion remain there; the branch was rebased onto `main` with a regression test for the overlapping optional-font behavior.

title: feat(player): play video files with type="video/..."
body:
## What this changes

`<hyperframes-player>` can now play a video file. Set `type` to a video type and `src` plays in a `<video playsinline>` instead of loading as a composition:

```html
<hyperframes-player type="video/mp4" src="./render.mp4" poster="./poster.jpg" controls></hyperframes-player>
```

Today an mp4 given to the player is loaded into the composition iframe as a page. It never posts a timeline: `duration` stays 0, the size stays at the fallback, and it later fails with "Composition timeline not found".

In video mode, the page uses the same API and events as for a composition:

- `play()`, `pause()`, `seek()`, `currentTime`, `duration`, `playbackRate`, `muted`, `volume`, `loop`, `autoplay`, `poster` and `controls`.
- `ready` with `{ duration, compositionWidth, compositionHeight }` (the video's own size), `timeupdate`, `play`, `pause` and `ended`.
- `resize` when the video's size differs from the current one (before `ready` on a load, as for a composition), and `durationchange` when the duration changes after `ready`.
- `error` as soon as the video fails, with `{ message, code }`, where `code` is the `MediaError` code, so a page can refresh an expired signed URL at once. A load failure is reported only as `error`, not also as `playbackerror`.
- A `play()` the browser blocks fires `playbackerror` with `{ source: "video" }` and leaves the player paused. A play interrupted by `pause()` or a new `src` is not reported.
- A pause or play the page did not ask for (media keys, the browser's own controls) is followed by the player. A `pause` event that arrives after the page already called `play()` again is ignored, so `seek(t); play()` and `pause(); play()` keep playing.
- `pause()` reads the frame on screen, not the last clock sample, and fires one `timeupdate` with it before `pause`, as a `<video>` does.
- The playback rate survives a new `src`. A new `src` starts paused at 0:00 with no duration until its metadata loads.

`type` is read without regard to case or padding. `srcdoc` wins over a video `src`, as it does for an iframe: setting `srcdoc` removes the video, and removing it loads the video again. Changing `type` while `srcdoc` is set leaves the composition on screen. `scenes`, `setRuntimeData()`, `setColorGrading()`, `iframeElement` and `stopMedia()` stay composition-only.

How it works:
- The `<video>` is driven through the player's existing direct-timeline adapter and clock, the path a same-origin `__timelines` composition uses, so `timeupdate`, loop and `ended` share one code path.
- Every place that loaded `src` into the iframe (first connect, a `src` change, sandbox and shader-option reloads) now goes through one `_loadSrc`, which picks the video or the iframe from `type`.
- Each video load also runs the document cleanup from #4546 and then links the video to the clock again. Shader and sandbox reloads skip video mode.
- Runtime messages from the hidden iframe are ignored while a video plays, so a late message from the previous composition cannot take the clock away.
- Removing the player from the page removes the video; putting it back loads it again.

Nothing changes for a player without a `video/...` type. The fixes that touch shared code (the paused reset on a new source, the exact paused time, the reload when `srcdoc` goes away) run only when a video is involved. Tests pin a composition player's behaviour to main's for each one.

This builds on #4505 (merged), which added the picture size, `durationchange` and `disable-click-to-play` that this uses.

## Before

Main, `type="video/mp4"` with a generated 3 s, 320×180 test clip: the iframe shows the MP4 as a page, `duration` stays 0, the size stays at the 1920×1080 fallback, and no events fire.

![Before: after load](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bec312b-6ffc-4b2b-a487-4ff96a41c10f)
![Before: after seek to 1.5 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdc35de2-8005-4b46-b607-d26c032839a5)

## After

This branch, same page: `resize` then `ready` with `{ duration: 3, compositionWidth: 320, compositionHeight: 180 }`, the clip fills the player, and a seek to 1.5 s lands at 1.500.

![After: after load](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/31ee10ef-4bfd-4bbd-974f-72b292d83a5e)
![After: after seek to 1.5 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e92c72f-7e54-465c-88df-1ab9356c4d25)

## What I measured

- Real headless Chrome with the built player and a generated 4 s clip:
  - `seek(1.5); play()` while playing keeps playing (3 of 3 runs), where the previous version ended paused (3 of 3);
  - `pause(); play()` in one task keeps playing (3 of 3), where the previous version ended paused (3 of 3);
  - `loop` wraps past the end twice.
- Tests:
  - of the 22 tests from the feature commits, 20 fail against main's player. The two that pass there assert composition behaviour: a composition player never creates a `<video>`, and removing `type` goes back to the iframe.
  - `_loadSrc` always choosing the iframe, no `playbackerror`, no `resize` and no `durationchange` each fail a named test.
  - the two fix commits add 18 tests, and each fails when its own fix is reverted: the stale `pause`, `srcdoc` in both directions, a late runtime message, a load failure after `play()`, a blocked play after a page pause, a rejection after the video is removed, the paused frame, switching to a composition paused, a play the page did not ask for, the new source's duration, the type's case, `srcdoc` switches starting paused, `type` changing under `srcdoc`, the `timeupdate` on pause, and three pins of main's composition behaviour, which pass against main's own player.
- Every `packages/player` test file passes run alone, including 248 tests in `hyperframes-player.test.ts`. Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet, comment citations and the fallow audit are green.
- Captures: headless Chrome, the player bundle from main (Before) and from this branch one commit before its head (After), with the same host page and clip. The last commit does not touch loading or seeking.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Safari and mobile browsers: `playsinline` and the autoplay rules differ there, and only headless Chrome ran.
- A signed URL expiring mid-playback. The `error` event is unit-tested with a synthetic `MediaError`, not a real 403.
- A `play()` the browser blocks still fires `play` before `pause` and `playbackerror`, and takes the poster down. A native `<video>` fires no `play` for a rejected play and keeps its poster.
- In video mode `pause()` fires its `timeupdate` even when the player is already paused.
- A player that switches from a video to `srcdoc` and then drops both `type` and `srcdoc` without a new `src` shows an empty frame; main shows the file as a page there, which is no better.
- Range playback (`range-start` / `range-end`) comes in the next PR.

title: fix(docs): restore examples with the HyperFrames Player
body:
## What

Restore visible examples and show them in the same HyperFrames Player used by the catalog, as requested by Miguel. Example cards now expose the real player's play/pause, seek, sound and speed controls. Source links stay in the titles rather than wrapping interactive controls; the original responsive grid is retained.

The original failure was a Mintlify class boundary: `HoverVideo`'s interpolated classes became `mint-overflow-hiddenmint-aspect-video`, losing the aspect ratio and collapsing a loaded video to zero height. Forward sizing classes directly and keep wrapper positioning/clipping explicit. The remaining hover previews on Thirty Days retain their behavior.

The new self-contained snippet wraps each MP4 in a simple video composition. It derives dimensions/duration from metadata and loads the same player CDN runtime as the catalog. The embed also constrains the published player poster to the card bounds, avoiding a cropped intrinsic-size thumbnail during initialization. Frames are lazy-loaded, do not autoplay, and retain usable native video controls if the player script is unavailable. A fallback already playing carries its time, sound and play state into the player.

Fixes #4674.

## Validation

- Exact public `/examples` reproduced: first five videos had readyState 4 but 0px height; separating the corrupted class tokens immediately restored their area.
- Real local Mintlify build: HyperFrames Player reports ready, correct duration, advances on click and seeks to 10 seconds. Mobile cards measure 348 × 195.75px. All 23 cards and 11 source links remain.
- Simulated unavailable player CDN: native controls remain visible, 196px tall, with no custom player.
- Thirty Days still renders 30 nonzero-height hover videos.
- Existing snippet tests: the height regression failed before the fix; 14/14 tests now pass. Motion audit, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt and diff checks pass.
- Final expanded-player `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` both pass.
- React #418 is not independently attributed to this layout bug; no blanket hydration-error fix is claimed.

Built with the ce-debug / ce-commit-push-pr workflow. Hosted preview verified at https://hyperframes-magi-fix-examples-video.mintlify.site/examples: 23 players, click-to-play advances time, seek works, mobile 348 × 195.75px, no captured page errors. Poster follow-up: reproduced 1280×720 posters inside 226×127 cards, then verified fitted bounds of 470×264 in the local build. Removing the fitting CSS fails the regression. Final poster-head Mintlify validation and broken-link checks pass. title: fix(studio-server): answer 413/415 instead of reading huge or binary files as text
body:
## What

`GET /projects/:id/files/*` no longer reads huge or binary files into a JSON string.

- Over 32 MB: answers `413 { why: "too_large" }` from the file's size, without reading it.
- Binary (a NUL byte in the first 8000 bytes, the same test `hyperframes history` uses): answers `415 { why: "binary", version }`. The ETag and `version` stay, so conditional writes to binary files (#3653) keep working. Only the garbled `content` string is gone.
- Text files under the cap: unchanged.

## Why

Studio's undo history reads every file in a history step through this route, media included. A 309 MB video in a step was read whole, decoded as UTF-8 and JSON-escaped on every undo, and a host app's heap went from 32 MB to 645 MB until V8 aborted. Studio already treats a failed read there as "no file contents" and falls back to a full preview reload, so no client change is needed.

## Callers checked

- Only Studio calls this route.
- Studio reads text through it (compositions and the JSON files Studio writes) and writes text only.
- Media reaches the browser through `/preview/*`, thumbnails and the render routes, which stream bytes.
- The visible changes: clicking a non-media binary (a font, a zip) in the file tree shows a load error instead of opening garbled text in the editor. A text file over 32 MB (nothing in the repo produces one; bundled assets inline at 2 MiB at most) shows a load error instead of opening.

## Tests

- A 300 MB sparse file answers 413 with a reply under 1 KB, and the process's peak RSS grows by under 100 MB. With a read added above the size check, it grows by 300 MB and the test fails.
- A small mp4-like file answers 415 with its version and ETag.
- The #3653 binary tests now expect 415 plus the same version.
- All five fail on main.

## Known gaps, not in this PR

- A 413 reply carries no `version`. A conditional overwrite of a file over 32 MB has to take the version from the PUT's 428/409 reply, and those replies still read the whole file into a string. Undo does not use that path, because history restores from stored blobs. It is the same class of bug on the write side, and a small follow-up fixes it.
- In the file tree, a non-media binary such as a font shows a load error. A "binary file" placeholder would read better; that is a Studio change and needs captures.

title: fix(studio): back to the master after a nested drill restores the master playhead
body:
## What

Going back to the master composition after drilling into sub-compositions did not reliably put the playhead back where it was on the master:

- **Nested drills lost the master time.** Every drill saved the current time as the master's, so after master > intro > logo, going back landed on the intro's local time.
- **Only the breadcrumb restored it.** Escape, a double-click on an empty part of the timeline and the Comps panel went back without restoring the time, and the Comps panel never saved it on the way in.
- **A master playhead at 0 was never restored,** and drilling in while playing saved the time playback started from, not the live playhead.
- **The timeline needle showed 00:00** after any level change, even when the time readout and the preview were right. The timeline redraws its canvas when the level changes, and the needle was drawn at time 0 without being moved to the current time.

Now every change of composition level passes through the one function that updates the stack. Leaving the master saves the live playhead there, and returning to the master restores it, for every way back. A restore only happens in the project the time was saved in. The needle is placed again whenever the timeline redraws.

## Verification

title: fix(core): the playhead no longer jumps back when an audio clip starts
body:
## What was broken

In Studio preview, the playhead stepped backwards for a moment when an audio clip started while another one was playing. Every visual and every other track jumped back with it, by 30 to 414 ms in the public launch films.

When no Web Audio buffer is playing, the transport clock follows an `<audio>` element. Each frame it re-picked the first in-window `<audio>` in page order. When a sound effect started during a voice line, it took the clock over. A clip always starts late: it is seeked, asked to play, and produces sound a few frames later. So the playhead jumped back by that delay.

## The fix

- **`init.ts`, the element the clock follows keeps it while it plays.** The audio-clock scan checks that element first, so a clip starting later cannot take the clock over mid-line. An element media sync already calls unplayable (a media error, or no usable source), and an `<audio>` with no source at all, are skipped, so they can neither lead nor freeze the playhead, and the next clip can lead. (Chrome reports an `<audio>` with no source as playing with no data once `play()` is called, which main's clock treated as buffering and held the playhead for good.)
- **`clock.ts`, audio can pull the playhead forward or hold it, never push it back.**
  - While the followed element is seeking, buffering, or up to a hard-sync distance (0.5 s) behind, the playhead holds at the last time it reported.
  - A larger jump back is not where the sound is, so the clock falls back to its monotonic time. A native loop's wrap (a jump back of more than half the loop) does the same, so a short loop never freezes the playhead, while a looping bed that merely starts late still holds it.
  - The element's time is mapped through the clip's own rate, not the element's current `playbackRate`. A speed change writes the bare transport rate to every element before media sync restores the clip's rate, so reading `playbackRate` made the playhead jump on a speed change under a clip with its own `data-playback-rate`.
- **`media.ts`:** the hard-sync distance is one exported constant shared by media sync and the clock, and `isUnplayable` is exported for the scan.

Tradeoffs, stated plainly:

- **Short hold instead of a step back.** When the followed clip is late, the picture holds for a few frames instead of stepping back.
- **A stuck element freezes the film, as on main.** An element that is ready and not paused but whose time has stopped still freezes the film.
- **One test changed its expectation.** "composition time is correct when el.playbackRate differs from clock rate" expected an element at 1x under a 2x clock to read as film time 2 s. It now reads 1 s, where that audio actually is in the film; media sync owns correcting the element's rate.

## Measured in Studio (real browser, audio recorded from the output)

A scripted real-user walk (play, pause, stop, space, seek, scrub, arrow keys, loop, mute, volume, clip edits while playing, fast toggles, reload, and 65 s of continuous play) over 11 public launch films, in headless Chrome, with the output recorded and compared with the engine's own render. The page's playhead log counts every step back while playing.

| film | playhead steps back, main | this branch | worst step back on main |
|---|---|---|---|
| liquid-brand-refraction | 8 | 0 | -414 ms |
| timeline-launch | 5 | 0 | -86 ms |
| claude-paper-launch | 3 | 0 | -111 ms |
| frame-md-launch-storyboard | 2 | 0 | -157 ms |
| cloud-render-launch | 2 | 0 | -117 ms |
| the other 6 films | 0 | 0 | - |
| **total** | **20** | **0** | |

Scenario pass/fail counts are not a clean signal here: two runs of the same main disagree on 25 to 28 of 255 scenarios (Chrome start-up timing, intermittent silence after a reload that is a separate issue), and this branch's differences from main sit inside that. The walk ran at an earlier head of this branch (f21af600); the changes since are the review fixes below, each covered by a unit test.

The before/after clips below repeat the same plays across clip starts in `timeline-launch`. Main steps back once (-36 ms at 4.54 s); this branch does not step back. On both, the picture runs about 40 ms ahead of the sound, which is the output latency and is not changed here.

## Tests

- **`clock.test.ts`:** a late clip holds, then follows; it holds while seeking, even to a time ahead; a buffering element that is behind holds; a jump back past a hard sync is not followed; a short native loop that wraps does not freeze; a looping bed that starts late holds; a dropout continues from the last audio time; a seek moves back past the hold; the element's place in its file is read whatever `playbackRate` it has; the playhead keeps its place when the speed changes under a clip with its own rate.
- **`audioClockSource.test.ts` (new, the real runtime):** a sound effect earlier in the page starts late while a voice plays, and the playhead never decreases and keeps advancing; a clip that failed to load, and a clip with no source (in the state Chrome reports for it), do not stop the next clip from leading.
- **Checked against main:** main's `clock.ts`, `init.ts` and `media.ts` fail 12 of the 51 tests.
- **Mutations, each caught:** audio may push the playhead back; no hold while seeking; following a jump past a hard sync; a short loop holds; a late loop bed does not hold; reading `el.playbackRate`; a failed clip blocks the next one; a clip with no source leads; page order takes the clock.
- **Run on this head:** core 3597 passed, typecheck clean.

## Review

Two earlier versions of this fix were reviewed and replaced: one could make media sync chase a lagging element into a seek loop, and one used a stall timer that could loop the same way. This version has neither. An independent adversarial review of this head is recorded; it found the speed-change, short-loop and failed-clip cases above, which are fixed here.

## Before

Main: the playhead steps back at a clip start in `timeline-launch`.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b646d185-03a2-4683-b3dd-82c8c5470983

## After

The same film, steps and viewport on this branch (recorded at bda99388; the only change since splits one method in two). No step back.

title: fix(studio): timeline Fit fills the width with the film, and a host can hide keyframe controls
body:
## What

Fit now fits the film. A 17 s film filled 28% of the timeline's width at Fit, in any host, because Fit always mapped at least 60 s of ruler. It now ends at 83% of the width, leaving the same trailing room Fit already gave longer films.

- **Fit fits the film's real duration.** One private `getTimelineFitSpan` owns the seconds the timeline maps: the duration plus the existing 20% headroom, or 60 s only while the duration is unknown or 0. Fit zoom and the drawn timeline width both read it, so Fit never scrolls sideways.
- **Zoomed in, every film keeps 20% of room past its end.** Before, a film under 50 s kept room out to 1:00 at any zoom and a longer film kept none. Clips can still be dragged past the end as before; the timeline grows while dragging.
- **An edit that changes the film's length no longer rescales every clip.** Manual zoom is a percentage of Fit, and the first edit locks the zoom that way. With Fit following the length, that percentage alone would shrink or grow every clip whenever an edit (delete, paste, undo, a drag) changes the length. This already happened for films over 50 s. In manual zoom, when the length changes while clips stay loaded, the timeline now re-expresses the on-screen scale as the new percentage before paint. Resizing the timeline, the first load, and opening another composition (which empties the clips first) still scale with Fit, as before.
- **Fit is an icon** (`ArrowsOutLineHorizontal`, the size and weight of the zoom buttons beside it) with `aria-label="Fit timeline to width"` and `aria-pressed`. The tooltip is unchanged.
- **`TimelineToolbar` takes `showKeyframes` (default `true`).** A host that does not offer keyframes passes `false`: Add keyframe and auto-record are hidden, auto-record is turned off (it defaults to on, and dragging an animated element would otherwise keep recording keyframes with no visible control), and K is left to playback. Studio passes nothing and is unchanged.

The 60 s floor was the drop surface after a short film. That surface is now the 20% headroom at Fit plus the drag-to-extend margin.

## Before

`main`, a 17 s fixture film at Fit: the film fills the left 28%, and the ruler runs to 1:00.

![Before: the 17 s film fills 28% of the timeline at Fit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/358c0049-6efa-42cc-b0b9-7f55a09ea279)

## After

The same film at Fit ends at 83% of the width, and the ruler ends just past 0:20. The timeline does not scroll (scroll width equals client width, measured in the browser).

![After: the 17 s film fills the timeline at Fit with 20% headroom](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/df7a26b5-746b-4bb3-8273-2f958ab12225)

The Fit button, hovered, before and after:

![Before: the Fit button shows the word Fit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/413d8608-931d-4bff-b5b0-e7da15e71220)

![After: the Fit button shows an arrows icon with the same tooltip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e203c86-f46a-4f7d-9e18-a0b7739169e2)

## Tests

- `Timeline.test.ts`: a 17 s film at Fit ends at 1/1.2 of the usable width (fails on `main`), and its drawn width equals the viewport, so Fit never scrolls. Zoomed in, the drawn width keeps the headroom. The 60 s floor still applies with no duration. Existing expectations tied to the old floor are updated, and a drawn-width input that could no longer win is removed.
- `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`: by default Add keyframe and auto-record show and the K shortcut claims K; with `showKeyframes={false}` both are gone, auto-record is off and K is left to playback. The Fit button is an icon with no text, is named, and its `aria-pressed` follows the zoom mode.
- `useTimelineGeometry.test.tsx`: in manual zoom a 17 s film keeps its scale when the first edit lengthens it to 25 s, when a later edit shortens it to 12 s, and near the maximum zoom. A resize, the first load, a project reset and opening another composition still scale with Fit, and Fit mode leaves the manual zoom alone.
- Each piece was pinned by breaking it: restoring the 60 s floor in the fit span, keeping it in the drawn width, leaving the controls shown, leaving auto-record on, leaving K on, dropping `aria-pressed`, not keeping the scale across a length change, keeping it across a resize or a composition switch, clamping it against the old Fit, writing the manual zoom in Fit mode, and leaving Fit as text each fail at least one test.
- The three test files passed three runs in a row (103 tests), and the timeline and toolbar area passed (1927 tests) one commit earlier; the last commit only adds the project-reset test. Studio typecheck, lint, format, the comment checks and the audit gate pass.

## Not covered

- Manual zoom-out still stops at 10% of Fit, so a very short film cannot zoom out as far as before (a 2 s film shows at most 24 s). Zoom-in beyond Fit does nothing for films under about 0.7 s, where Fit already exceeds the frame-level cap.
- The kept scale is rounded to a whole percent of Fit, so at very low zoom repeated length changes can drift it by a few percent.
- The kept scale assumes a composition's clips arrive after its length. If a child composition's clips reached the timeline before its length, the parent's scale would carry over once. No such ordering was seen.
- With `showKeyframes={false}`, keyframes can still be added outside the toolbar (for example from the property panel). Showing the controls again leaves auto-record off, visibly, until it is switched back on.

title: fix(studio): clips inside nested compositions sit at their master time
body:
## What

On the master timeline, a clip inside a nested sub-composition was drawn at its start time inside its parent instead of the time it plays. With an intro at 2 s on the master and a logo at 3 s inside the intro, the logo was drawn at 3 to 8 s but plays at 5 to 10 s. Each level below the first dropped its parent's offset.

Studio built those rows from the clip's own start, which is relative to its parent. It now asks the same start-time rule the runtime uses to play the composition, which adds every parent's start at every depth. Both places that build master rows use it: the pass that adds nested composition clips, and the fallback that reads the timeline from the document. It also reads a scene's authored length the way the runtime does, so a scene that starts after another one (`data-start="intro + 2"`) lands where it plays.

`@hyperframes/core`'s start-time resolver now accepts any timeline registry whose entries have a duration, which is all it reads, so Studio's own timeline type fits, and it now also returns an element's host start (`resolveHostStartForElement`); the rule for whole-film media starts is shared as `isRootGlobalMediaStart`. Existing callers are unaffected.

Writes go the other way. Every row now carries the master start of the composition its `data-start` counts from, and one conversion subtracts it before any start is written: a move (the live preview, the file and the SDK call), a head trim (including the GSAP scale window), a group move or resize, and a razor split. So a nested row dragged to 6 s on the master timeline is written as its local start and plays at 6 s; before this change it would have been written as 6 inside the intro and played at 8. A video or audio clip whose start already counts from the whole film keeps it as written.

## Verification

- Tests build master > intro (2 s) > logo (3 s) > badge (1 s) and expect logo at 5 s and badge at 6 s, for both paths. They fail on main (logo at 3 s, badge at 1 s) and pass here. Adding only the nearest parent's offset fails the depth-3 case. Two more tests place a scene, and a clip inside it, after a referenced scene's authored length; they fail without that setting.
- Drag and trim tests at depth 2 and 3 check the round trip: the row is redrawn at the drop point, the written `data-start` is local, it plays there, and the parent's length does not grow. Top-level rows, tail trims, group moves, the SDK path, the razor split and a whole-film-time video are covered too. They fail without the conversion.
- The Studio test suite passes. The core start-resolver, readiness and timeline tests pass. Typecheck passes for Studio and core; lint, the audit gate and the comment check pass.
- In the app, with the playhead at 00:05, the logo clip now starts under it. Dragging the logo row from 5 s to 6 s and reloading leaves it at 6 s, and the preview shows it from 6 s; before, it was redrawn at 8 s and played from 8 s.
