title: perf(core): the preview loads only the media near the playhead
body:
## What
The Studio preview loads only the clips on screen or due in the next 2 s, instead of every video at once. On a 60-clip film, every clip's filmstrip shows within 60 to 90 s instead of 2 to 58 of them by 150 s, a far jump shows its first frame in 0.2 s instead of 16 s or never, and Studio's timeline appears as fast as on main.

## Why
With 60 video clips the preview opened every video at once and held over 100 media requests to the one origin that also serves the timeline thumbnails. Thumbnails queued behind them, so most clips showed a blank tile or "no preview", and a jump far down the film waited behind every other clip's download.

## How
All of it runs only in Studio's preview (behind the preview mark); render and export documents never carry it.

- **Near-playhead window.** Media farther than 2 s from the playhead stays at `preload="none"` and is armed as it comes due (`packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`, `preloadMedia.ts`).
- **The next clip on a track.** While playing, a clip that starts arms the next clip on its track (read by the timeline's own `parseAuthoredTrack`, same composition host), so a track never waits for its next clip. Paused or scrubbing, nothing extra is armed.
- **Leaving the window closes the fetch.** Chromium keeps downloading through `preload="none"` plus `load()`, so a clip that leaves the window drops and restores its `src`; it loads again when it comes due.
- **Timeline readiness.** Studio's readiness scan waited for every clip to become playable, so with clips left unloaded it hit its 8 s timeout. It now checks a clip the preview left unloaded only for its first frame, as it already does for lazy images (`packages/core/src/compositionReadiness.ts`).
- **Loop playback.** Studio's loop tick tells the runtime where the loop starts (`window.__hf.setLoopStart`), and while looping the runtime keeps the clips due within 4 s of the loop start loaded, so a wrap back to the in point does not start cold.
- **No flicker at the edge.** A clip is armed 2 s ahead and released only beyond 4 s, so scrubbing across the edge does not drop and refetch it. An arm made for the next clip on a track lasts only while the clip that made it is playing, so a jump while playing drops it.
- **Clips without an authored length** stay out of the window and load as in a render, since reloading one would lose its duration.
- **Player.** When a clip stops preloading, the player's parent-frame copy of it (which fetches the whole file) is dropped, and it is adopted again when the clip comes due (`packages/player/src/parent-media.ts`).

## Test plan
- [x] Unit tests, each failing without its change: the next clip is armed when the current one starts playing and nothing else is; nothing is armed while paused; a far clip on another track is not armed; an armed next clip survives a window pass; readiness waits on a later clip only once the runtime set it to buffer; the player drops a clip's copy and adopts it again when due; loop-start clips stay loaded while the loop plays; a jump while playing drops the next-clip arm; scrubbing across the edge does not refetch; back-to-back clips; same host and same authored track; a render document keeps loading every clip.
- [x] Render unchanged: a 3-video repo fixture rendered to 60 frames twice per side gives the same frame-set md5 on main and this branch.
- [x] 60-clip fixture built from repo media (6 tracks), headless Chrome, filmstrip / "no preview" / blank tiles and open media requests:

| | 30 s | 60 s | 90 s | 150 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main, run 1 | 1/0/59, 116 open | 2/0/58 | 2/1/57 | 2/3/55 |
| main, run 2 | 1/0/59, 95 open | 2/0/58 | 7/1/52 | 58/1/1 |
| branch, run 1 | 15/0/45, 0 open | 40/0/20 | 60/0/0 | 60/0/0 |
| branch, run 2 | 24/0/36, 0 open | 60/0/0 | 60/0/0 | 60/0/0 |

- [x] One-track playback, 13 clip boundaries: 13 of 13 clips start within 1 s of coming due, median 25 to 28 ms, worst 44 ms; a far jump from 0 to 150 s shows its first frame in about 0.2 s. On main the same jump took 16.5 s or never showed a frame (main's runs were on a busier machine).
- [x] Throttled to 3 MB/s, one track, rate-capped 6 Mb/s clips: 13 of 13 on time, median first frame about 30 ms, no `waiting` events, far jump 0.18 to 0.25 s. Main: 13 of 13 with 3 `waiting` events, 77 media requests open before play, and the far jump never became ready in 20 s.
- [x] Loop playback (in point 9.5 s, 6 s span, looped by Studio, 3 wraps): wrap to first moving frame 94 to 114 ms on a normal link (main 64 to 133 ms) and 62 to 142 ms at 3 MB/s over 3 runs (main 63 to 88 ms). Before the loop change the branch took up to 1.7 s at 3 MB/s.
- [x] Timeline: on the benchmark film, Studio's timeline fills 1.50 s after a cold open (median of 5; main 1.62 s). Before the readiness change the branch took 9.1 to 10.1 s.

## Known limits
- **A clip with a very heavy first second on a slow link.** The branch arms each clip about 2 to 3 s before it is due, and the playing clip and the next one share the link. A file that puts most of its bytes at the start (the repo's looped test clips carry 9.5 MB in their first second, then about 0.3 MB a second) cannot arrive in that time at 3 MB/s: 0 of 13 clips on time, where main managed 12 of 13 only because it had spent a minute buffering the start of every clip with 120 requests open. A rate-capped encode of the same frames at the same bitrate plays 13 of 13 (the row above).
- On a 3 MB/s link filmstrips still fill slowly (8 of 60 by 150 s, 2 on main), because thumbnail downloads are limited by bandwidth, not by connections.
- A clip more than 4 s ahead is released when playback pauses, so resuming far from it downloads it again.
- Clips with no authored length load in full, as on main (Studio writes a length on drop and on trim, so this is uncommon).
- Clips that use `<source>` children instead of `src` are not released, as on main.
- The preview's disk fallback loads the runtime at the end of the page, and nested clips at time 0 inside a later composition are not deferred; both load as on main.
- Idle memory and CPU are level with main; this change does not lower them.

## Before
Main, 60 s after opening the 60-clip film on a normal link: 2 filmstrips, 58 blank tiles.

![Before: main, 60 s, normal link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5d9799a0-2f30-4948-90cf-7842052ac4bb)

Main at 150 s on a 3 MB/s link: 120 media requests open.

![Before: main, 150 s, 3 MB/s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/70744aa4-84a0-445a-9840-6cc58b738575)

## After
This branch, 60 s, normal link: all 60 filmstrips.

![After: branch, 60 s, normal link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a157365-d64d-40c0-ad69-55bf0e4b8d1f)

This branch at 150 s on 3 MB/s: no media requests left open.

![After: branch, 150 s, 3 MB/s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/39ca307b-c538-4fa4-90b0-5915739ad0a3)

title: feat(player): play and loop a range of a film with range-start and range-end
body:
## What

`<hyperframes-player>` can play part of a film and loop it frame-exactly:

```html
<hyperframes-player src="./film/index.html" range-start="2" range-end="3" loop></hyperframes-player>
```

## Why

Today the player loops only the whole film. A page that loops a moment itself, by seeking back on `timeupdate`, runs past the end by up to about three frames, because `timeupdate` comes every 100 ms. A host that loops a moment of a film needs the end to be exact.

## Related work

Builds on #4673 (video mode, merged), so a range also works on a video, and on #4505.

## How

- **`range-start` / `range-end`**: seconds of film time, mirrored as the `rangeStart` / `rangeEnd` properties (`null` leaves that side open). A player with neither attribute behaves as before.
- **Where it plays:**
  - the player parks on `range-start` at `ready`, and again whenever the range changes while paused;
  - `play()` from outside the range starts at `range-start`;
  - the range is [start, end): the last frame shown is the one before `range-end`, so a scene that starts at `range-end` never shows;
  - at the end, with `loop` it wraps to `range-start` and keeps playing; without `loop` it pauses on that last frame and `ended` fires. `currentTime` then reads a time inside that frame (for a range ending at 3 s: 2.967 on a composition, 2.983 on a video), never `range-end` itself, so a host should listen for `ended` rather than compare times;
  - if the range changes and the playhead is now outside it, playback jumps to the new start, and a paused player parks there; inside the range, the playhead stays where it is, so dragging `range-end` doesn't move it;
  - `currentTime` and `duration` stay film time, and a `seek()` outside the range still parks there.
- **`rangeclamped`**: fires when the film is shorter than the range, including after a `durationchange`. It gives the range the player actually applies, `{ rangeStart, rangeEnd, duration }`. An invalid range (end not after start, or not a number) plays as if unset, and `rangeclamped` gives `null` for both ends. It fires once per range and film length, never before `ready`.
- **Frame-exact end:** a composition's runtime gets the range through a new `set-play-range` control, beside `set-root-duration`, and advertises a `play-range` capability. Its clock stops on its own frame at the last frame inside the range, the same way it stops at a film's length, and it makes the jump itself when a range change leaves the playhead outside. The player then wraps or stays paused. Against a runtime without the capability, the player stops or wraps from its own time check. Video mode (#4673) and same-origin `__timelines` compositions check the range on every tick of the player's clock and stop one tick early when the next tick would pass the end, so the frame after the range end does not show, unless the next browser frame runs longer than the last two (then it can show for one tick, as on main). The next tick is predicted from the smaller of the last two moves of the time, so one slow frame or a jump does not cut the range short; a tick where the time stands still (it moves once per video frame in some browsers) keeps the last prediction, and 1 ms of slack absorbs a `currentTime` rounded down onto a frame boundary. In a background tab, where animation frames stop, a video with a range checks it on its own `timeupdate`, so it stops only as precisely as that event fires (up to 250 ms apart). A video without a range is left as it is today.

## Before

Main, with `range-start="2" range-end="3"` on a 6 s test film that cuts to a second scene at 3 s, with a frame counter: there is no range support, so it plays on into the second scene.

![Before: playing past the range into the second scene](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e7932a0-56de-4a52-b5b2-f3ac4b694058)

## After

This branch, the same film with `range-start="2" range-end="3" loop`: it parks on 2.000, plays to its last frame inside the range (frame 89), and wraps to 2.000. No frame of the second scene shows. The status line's `last:` gives the frame painted on each side of the latest wrap: f89, then f60 at 2.000.

![After: looping inside the range](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ea27b50-04ba-4089-891a-0d1e7ad88588)

An earlier version of this capture read `f89 -> f89 (2.000)`. That came from the harness, not the player: it read the composition's frame label before the composition's own animation-frame callback updated it in the same browser frame. Keyed per browser frame, the label painted at 2.000 is f60 on all 4 wraps of every run (main's page loop reads the same way: f91 in the mid-frame text, f60 painted).

## Test plan

- Headless Chrome, range [2, 3) on a 30 fps film with a scene cut at 3 s; 5 s runs, 4 wraps each:

  | Case | Past the range end | Frame at each wrap or stop | Second-scene frames shown |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Main, looping from the page on `timeupdate` | 116 ms (3.5 frames) | 89 to 92 | 14 |
  | Composition with `loop` | none (latest time 2.999) | 89 every wrap | 0 |
  | Composition without `loop` | stops at 2.967 | 89, and `currentTime` matches | 0 |
  | Video with `loop` | usually none; one wrap of 4 in one of seven runs reached 3.006 when a browser frame ran long | 89, and once 90 for one tick | (no scene cut in the clip) |
  | Video without `loop` | stops at 2.983 | 89 | (no scene cut in the clip) |

- Tests:
  - player `range-playback`: parking; starting from outside; stopping on the last frame with `ended`; wrapping with `loop`; `rangeclamped` on a short film, after a `durationchange` and on an invalid range; range changes while playing and paused (a moved end below a playing playhead keeps playing from the start, with and without the runtime capability); attributes and properties both ways; a video and a same-origin `__timelines` composition; a video stopping one tick early at a range end, but not after one slow frame and not at the film's own end; the same when the time moves once per frame and is rounded down; a video's range end checked on its `timeupdate` in a hidden tab, and a video without a range left alone there;
  - core: the clock stops at the range's last frame; the transport stops on that frame, with a clip that starts at the range end never shown; playing again from the end restarts at the range start only while a range is set; clearing the range restores the full length.
  All fail before this change.
- Each of these fails a named test: the runtime ignoring the range; the player wrapping to 0 on either path; no `rangeclamped`; no fallback for older runtimes; the runtime not owning the jump; the capability ignored; a stale state ending the film; parking on the end frame instead of the last frame inside; showing the overshoot frame; the old always-re-park; an extra `play` event; the range sent twice; no early stop; predicting from the last tick alone; a still tick resetting the prediction; no rounding slack; rounding slack at the film's own end; an early stop at the film's own end; no `timeupdate` check in a hidden tab; a `timeupdate` check in a visible tab; a hidden-tab check without a range.
- Every changed or covering test file passes run alone. That includes player `range-playback` (20), `hyperframes-player` (248) and `parent-media` (22), and core `clock` (49), `bridge` (35), `protocol` (9), `transportPark` (35), `init` (181) and `init.swapScenes` (139). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment ratchet, comment citations and the fallow audit are green for both packages.

Not exercised:

- Safari and mobile browsers; only headless Chrome ran.
- A composition whose runtime is older than this change is covered only by unit tests of the player's fallback, not in a browser.
- A background tab is covered only by a unit test of the video's `timeupdate` check. From reading the code, a composition's own audio in a background tab can still play past the range end, because the runtime's transport runs on animation frames; a film's own end behaves the same way on main.

title: fix(studio): drilling in opens the composition's full project path
body:
## What

Drilling into a sub-composition stored under a folder, such as `sections/compositions/scene.html`, opens that file instead of `compositions/scene.html`.

## Why

Drilling into a sub-composition whose file lives under a folder whose name ends in `compositions`, for example `sections/compositions/scene.html`, opened `compositions/scene.html` instead. Studio took the drill path from the first `compositions/...html` it found anywhere in the source, so a longer path was cut down to that tail, and a different file with the same tail opened. It shows when the clip's element id differs from its composition id (for example `id="scene-host"` with `data-composition-id="scene"`); with matching ids the file is found by id and the path is never cut.

## Related work

None.

## How

The drill path now comes from Studio's existing source-path helper, which removes a preview URL's origin and prefix and otherwise keeps the full project-relative path. A leading `./` or `/` is dropped for the drill path only, so `./compositions/scene.html` still opens `compositions/scene.html`; the helper keeps a leading `./`, because the canvas lookup compares its result with the raw attribute. The helper now reads a preview prefix only from a URL, so a project folder named `preview` is no longer cut away.

## Test plan

- Tests drill into `sections/compositions/x.html` given as a plain path, a full preview URL and a `/preview/comp/` URL, and expect that full path and its preview URL. All three fail on main (they open `compositions/x.html`) and pass here. A fourth pins that `./compositions/x.html` still opens `compositions/x.html`.
- A canvas lookup test pins that a composition host written as `./compositions/scene.html` is still found from its timeline clip.
- A helper test pins that a plain project path with a folder named `preview` (`sections/preview/x.html`) keeps its folder, while preview URLs still lose their prefix. It fails on main, where the helper searched plain paths for the prefix too.
- The Studio component, hooks and player library tests pass (3167). Typecheck, lint, format, the audit gate and the comment check pass.

title: fix(studio-server): history never hangs on a pipe or follows a link swapped in for a file
body:
## What

The history blob store copies a project file in only while it is a regular file: it opens the path without following links and without blocking, checks the opened file, and clones or copies from that same handle. A named pipe or link swapped in for a file between the history's listing and its copy is skipped instead of blocking the history queue or being followed out of the project.

## Why

The history lists project files with `lstat` and skips anything that is not a regular file, but its copy then ran `copyFile` on the path with no type check. A FIFO swapped in between the two blocked the copy, and every history write queued behind it.

## Related work

None.

## How

`put` opens with `O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` and `fstat`s the handle. On Linux it clones through the open descriptor, so the path is never reopened; elsewhere, and when cloning fails, it streams from the handle. The sweep treats a path that is no longer a regular file like a removed one.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: a pipe is rejected at once, a link is never followed, a regular file still stores its hash, and a first baseline skips a file swapped for a pipe while it was read. They hang or fail on `main`.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(engine): HDR tone maps use the file's own peak brightness on every ffmpeg version
body:
## What

HDR-to-SDR tone maps pass the file's own peak brightness to ffmpeg's `tonemap` filter on every ffmpeg version. The peak comes from the first frame's content light level (MaxCLL), else its mastering display maximum. Before this change, ffmpeg 8 always assumed a peak of 10 (1000 nits), while ffmpeg 7 read it from the file.

## Why

The same HDR clip tone-mapped with a different brightness depending on the installed ffmpeg.

## Related work

Refs #4549.

## How

The first-frame probe parses the peak, the shared tone-map builder adds `:peak=`, and the engine and Studio proxy cache keys change so old frames are not reused.

## Test plan

title: fix(studio): arrow keys on a focused timeline control no longer nudge the canvas
body:
## What

With a timeline control focused, an arrow key only moves timeline focus; it no longer also nudges the selected element on the canvas or steps the playhead.

## Why

With a keyframe diamond focused on the timeline and an element selected, one ArrowRight did two things: the timeline moved focus to the next diamond, and the canvas nudge moved the selected element and saved the file. The canvas nudge listens on the whole window and never asked whether the timeline had focus. Delete already had that check.

A smaller case had the same cause: with a timeline row focused (a row is not a button) and nothing selected, an arrow moved timeline focus and also stepped the playhead one frame.

## Related work

None.

## How

The timeline now owns arrow keys while it has focus. The existing check Delete uses (`timelineOwnsKey`: focus is inside the timeline pane) moves to its own module unchanged, and the canvas nudge and the playback frame step use it too. Outside the timeline nothing changes: with the canvas focused, arrows nudge a selected element or step a frame when nothing is selected, and text inputs are untouched.

With focus on one of the timeline's toolbar buttons, arrows now do nothing, as Delete already did there.

## Test plan

Draft: review found two issues at this head, and their fix is not pushed yet. (1) After a click on the ruler or an empty lane, arrows no longer step frames, because the check covers the whole timeline pane rather than only its keyboard controls. (2) Two existing playback shortcut tests fail where no global `Element` exists. The planned change narrows ownership to the timeline's focusable controls and drops the `instanceof Element` check.

- `timelineArrowOwnership.test.tsx` mounts the real nudge, playback and timeline key handlers together. Diamond focused with an element selected: focus moves, no nudge, no pending file write, no seek. Row focused with nothing selected: focus moves, no frame step. Both fail on main and pass here. Two more pin what stays: from the canvas, arrows still nudge a selected element and still step a frame with nothing selected.
- Each rule turns a test red when broken.
- The nudge, playback, app hotkey and timeline keyboard tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format and the audit gate pass.

title: fix(producer): renders leave no captured frames behind when interrupted
body:
## What this fixes

A render that is interrupted leaves its captured frames on disk. With multi-worker capture on the disk path (the
default for screenshot capture, e.g. on macOS), each render writes its frames to `renders/work-<job>-*/` beside the
output. On Ctrl+C that whole folder stayed behind, plus an empty `.<name>.hf-transaction-*` staging folder, and the
CLI exited 130 without printing "Render cancelled". Repeated interrupted renders add up to gigabytes.

## Root cause

Puppeteer's default SIGINT handler kills Chrome and calls `process.exit(130)` synchronously. The CLI's render
cancellation scope aborts the render on SIGINT, but the process was gone before the orchestrator's `remove workDir`
disposer could run. On SIGTERM and SIGHUP Puppeteer only closes Chrome, so those already cleaned up.

## Change

- **engine:** `setHostHandlesSigint(owned)`. Every engine browser launch keeps Puppeteer's Ctrl+C handler unless the
  host says it owns SIGINT. Hosts that don't opt in (benchmark, library consumers) behave exactly as before.
- **cli:** the render cancellation scope claims SIGINT while it is open and releases it on dispose, so Ctrl+C aborts
  the render and the render cleans up after itself.
- **producer:** each work dir and output staging dir records its owner (`owner.json`: pid, hostname, boot (Linux boot id, else
  boot time to the minute) and, on Linux, pid namespace). A render killed outright (SIGKILL, crash) cannot clean up, so the next render into the same folder
  removes render temp dirs whose owner has exited. It never touches a dir with a live owner, no owner file, an owner in
  another pid scope (another host or boot, or a container, even one with host networking and the host's hostname), a staging dir still holding the previous output (`backup`), or anything not named like a render temp dir.
- **engine and producer, cancel during setup:** two leaks that Puppeteer's exit on Ctrl+C used to hide, and that kept
  `render --batch` alive after Ctrl+C (a single render exits anyway):
  - the BeginFrame warm-up loop now stops when capture setup fails (`cancelWarmupOnError` sets a `cancelled` flag the
    loop honours in locked and unlocked mode); before, any setup error except the readiness timeout left it ticking;
  - the probe stage's release guard now starts before it launches its browser, so a cancel during the probe closes
    the probe browser and file server; before, it only covered the final media preflight;
  - a parallel capture worker whose browser launch loses the race to cancel (or its phase deadline) now waits (up to
    10 s) for that launch and closes the browser before the worker settles; before, it was abandoned and kept running.
    Waiting matters: Puppeteer's process-exit hook kills browsers from a list it edits while iterating, so with two or
    more browsers alive at exit every other one survives.

  `frameCapture.ts` and `probeStage.ts` are mostly re-indentation: review them with whitespace hidden. The probe stage's
  BeginFrame liveness comment, moved by that re-indent, is condensed to three lines with the same facts.

## Evidence

Same 15 s fixture, `--workers 3`, disk capture path (`HF_CAPTURE_PARALLEL_STREAM=false`), Linux:

| Case | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| success | nothing left | nothing left |
| Ctrl+C mid-capture | 30 MB `work-*` + `.hf-transaction-*` left, exit 130 | nothing left, "Render cancelled", exit 1 |
| SIGTERM mid-capture | | nothing left, exit 1 |
| SIGKILL mid-capture | work dir left | work dir left, removed by the next render into the folder |
| second render in its own pid namespace, same folder, same hostname | | first render's dirs kept, both exit 0 |
| `render --batch` (2 rows), Ctrl+C to the process group once frames land, 5 runs | | exit 1 in 2 s every run, no temp dirs left |
| `render --batch`, Ctrl+C the moment capture setup starts, 5 runs | | exit 1 in 2-3 s every run (5 of 5 hung before this fix), no temp dirs left |
| `render --batch`, Ctrl+C while capture browsers launch | | exit 1 in 1 s, 8 of 8 runs (all hung before this fix), no temp dirs or Chrome left |
| single render, Ctrl+C while capture browsers launch, 10 runs | | exit 1 in 1 s, no orphaned Chrome (3 of 5 left one before this fix) |

## Tests

- `renderCancel.integration.test.ts` (integration lane, real Chrome + ffmpeg): Ctrl+C mid-capture leaves no temp dirs;
  a SIGKILLed render's dirs are reclaimed by the next render into the folder.
- `renderDirOwner.test.ts`: which dirs are reclaimed and which are kept.
- `renderCancellation.test.ts`: the CLI scope claims and releases SIGINT.
- `frameCapture-warmupTicks.test.ts`: the warm-up loop stops once cancelled, in both modes, even while every tick fails;
  a failed setup sets the flag and a successful one does not.
- `probeStage.test.ts`: a cancel right after the probe's file server or browser starts releases both.
- `parallelCoordinator-peerAbort.test.ts`: a capture browser whose launch finishes after the cancel is closed.

One deliberate mutation per new test, each turns exactly its test red:

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| host does not claim SIGINT (Puppeteer default, as on main) | Ctrl+C test fails: 2 temp dirs left |
| no sweep before creating the work dir | SIGKILL test fails |
| staging dir created without an owner | SIGKILL test fails |
| Windows `hf-render-` name dropped from the matcher | unit test fails |
| EPERM treated as a dead owner | unit test fails |
| CLI scope does not claim SIGINT | CLI test fails |
| owner's pid namespace not compared | unit test fails |
| warm-up loop ignores `cancelled` | warm-up test fails (timeout) |
| failed setup does not set `cancelled` | warm-up helper test fails |
| probe stage as on main | both new probe cases fail |
| owner's boot id not compared | unit test fails |
| worker settles without waiting for the late launch's close | peer-abort test fails |

## Not covered here

- A render inside Studio that is cut off when Studio shuts down: Studio aborts but does not await its renders. Its dirs
  are reclaimed by the next render into that folder.
- Windows and `render --docker` were not run.
- `initializeSession` calling `cancelWarmupOnError` is exercised end to end (batch Ctrl+C runs above), not by a unit
  test: the helper is unit tested, the call site is not.

title: fix(core): a sound effect starts on its time instead of a frame late
body:
## What

A short sound effect in Studio preview now starts on its time instead of up to a frame late. A sound effect authored faster than 1x starts early only as far as strict sync allows, so it can still land a little late.

## Why

Preview starts a sound only when the playhead is already inside its window, so every clip starts on the tick after its time: on average half a frame late, and a full frame or more after a long frame. On short sound effects (clicks, whooshes) that lag is audible against the picture.

## Related work

Refs #4679 (the playhead no longer jumps back when a clip takes over the clock; this PR builds on that).

## How

On each playing tick the runtime knows how far the playhead moved since the last tick. An audio clip that is due within that distance starts now, from its first sample, instead of on the next tick.
- The lead is capped at the strict sync tolerance (40 ms of film time), scaled down at slow speeds so it is never more than 40 ms of real time.
- A clip authored faster than 1x starts early only as far as keeps it inside strict sync when its window opens.
- Seeks, speed changes and play/pause start nothing early; a seek back before a clip that started early stops it.
- Video never starts early.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

**Measured in Studio on three public launch films** (pr-to-video, website-to-hyperframes, timeline; 26 s of playback from 0), main at a3b6eec against this branch at 3ee461aa (later commits change only tests). Each sound effect's start was recorded from inside the page and compared with its time on the timeline (positive = late):

| Film | Clips started, main / fix | Median, main → fix | Latest, main → fix | Earliest, main → fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pr-to-video | 16 / 19 | 17 → 1 ms | 39 → 15 ms | 1 → -22 ms |
| website-to-hyperframes | 21 / 21 | 12 → -4 ms | 90 → 11 ms | 0 → -18 ms |
| timeline | 5 / 5 | 11 → -4 ms | 20 → 1 ms | 3 → -17 ms |

An earlier run on this branch at 847b76c9, twice per film against the main of that time, gave the same picture: median 9 to 17 ms late on main against 10 ms early to 2 ms early with the fix, and no start earlier than 23 ms. No clip started more than 23 ms before its time in any run, inside the roughly 45 ms by which sound can lead picture before a viewer notices (ITU-R BT.1359).

**For embedders:** on the media-element route, when an early-started clip is the one the clock follows, the picture can move forward by up to 40 ms of film time when its window opens. It is never held back. The decoded-buffer (Web Audio) route is unchanged and not helped by this PR.

## Before

Main (a3b6eec): a test film built for this PR, a white flash and a click together at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 s, played from 0 in Studio with sound.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/51327600-5673-48da-8e07-97a8f903df39

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d43bfc9-97d0-4dc7-971d-11cc227b708b

A click moving 10 to 20 ms earlier is below what a screen recording can show: the recorder's own sound-to-picture offset moved by about 50 ms between two recordings of the same build. The captures show that every click still plays with its flash; the lateness numbers above come from the in-page probe.

title: feat(studio): a host can save style edits on a selection through the Studio style commit
body:
## What

A host app can save a style edit on a selection without mounting Studio's editor session:

- **`useDomStyleCommit({ projectId, iframeRef, writeProjectFile, recordEdit, activeCompPath?, showToast? })`** returns `commitStyle(selection, { property: value, ... })` and `waitForPendingSaves()`. `commitStyle` applies the styles live in the host's preview and saves them as one source patch and one undo step labelled "Edit layer style". It resolves to Studio's `DomEditCommitOutcome`: `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`. The hook starts no preview sync.
- **`resolveDomEditSelection(element, { activeCompositionPath, isMasterView, projectId })`** is exported: Studio's own builder that turns a preview element into a `DomEditSelection` (it finds the source file itself).
- The types `DomEditCommitOutcome` and `DomEditCommitDeclineReason` are exported.

## Why

The only DOM editing export, `useDomEditSession`, needs Studio's right panel, file tree and source editor, and starts its own preview sync. A host with its own preview and picker had no small way to save a style edit.

## Related work

Builds on the DOM editing exports for hosts outside `EditorShell`.

## How

No second writer. Studio's DOM-edit writer moves unchanged out of `useDomEditCommits` into `useDomEditPersist`, which Studio and the new hook both call. Studio's single-property style commit moves into `commitDomStyles`, which takes a map of properties. Studio calls it with one property, so its behaviour is unchanged. The hook calls it with several. The host passes the same `writeProjectFile` and `recordEdit` function objects it gives the timeline, so there is one writer and one undo list (Studio's file lock is keyed by the writer). The hook owns a DOM save queue, and `waitForPendingSaves` lets the host's undo wait for a save still in flight; a host's undo drain should also call `flushStudioPendingEdits`, as for the timeline.

Each property keeps its own latest-save version, so a failed save reverts only the properties no later call has changed. A failed save does not pause later host saves: each call is the user's own retry, and each failure is reported through `showToast`.

## Before

A throwaway host page (not part of this PR) with its own preview of a fixture project and no Studio editor, importing from the package entry, on `main`: the export does not exist, so the host cannot save a style edit.

![Before: the host page reports that the package exports no useDomStyleCommit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f98388a-0678-4dea-a41f-8f3581aaffda)

## After

The same page on this branch. The host picks the title with `resolveDomEditSelection` and calls `commitStyle(title, { color: "#facc15", "font-size": "140px" })`, using Studio's exported file writer and history. The title changes live in the host's preview. The outcome is `{ ok: true }`, the undo list shows one "Edit layer style" entry, and the saved source has both styles in one inline `style`.

![After: the title is gold and 140px, with the saved source and one undo entry shown](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e19b1195-739c-4344-bd2a-7669385d87a2)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: through the package entry, two properties apply live and save as one patch with one history entry. Geometry properties and read-only selections are refused with their reason and write nothing, and a missing project is refused. A failed save never reverts a later edit's property, and a save after a conflict succeeds.
- [x] Studio's existing DOM edit, text commit, session and quick-save tests pass unchanged (69). The hooks and editor area passed (2511 tests) before the review fixes, which touched only the new files. The new test file passed three runs in a row (5 tests). Typecheck, lint, format, the comment checks and the audit gate pass.
- [x] Each guard was pinned by breaking it: saving only the first property, not refusing geometry, not refusing a read-only selection, not refusing without a project, keying versions by the property set, and letting a conflict pause later saves each fail a test.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Not covered

- A font that exists only as a project font file is saved without its `@font-face` on this path (Studio's editor adds it from the file tree). Google fonts and system fonts are unaffected.
- After a save, the host's preview reseeks to Studio's player-store time, so a host that runs its own player should keep that store's time in step.
- An empty style map is refused with the reason `no-selection`.

title: docs(skills): studio agents answer questions before editing and plan new films like the launch films
body:
## What

The `hyperframes-studio` skill now tells an agent working with a person in Studio two things it did not before:

- **Section 0, "Talk before you build".** Read the message first and decide what it asks for. A change, however politely asked ("can you make the title bigger?"), gets made. A felt note on the built film ("the intro feels jolty") gets diagnosed and fixed. A question that names no change gets an answer; "don't change anything" gets nothing touched; an idea for the film gets a proposal added to the plan; a new film goes to section 5. A message with both a question and a change gets both. It also says how to reply (answer first, only questions that change the film, each with a recommended answer; directions per `pitch-round.md` for a new film, two or three options for an idea about this one) and to keep the plan in STORYBOARD.md the way `storyboard-recipe.md` § 4 records a round, so a new session can pick it up.
- **Section 5, "A new film: plan, storyboard, build".** The step order the public [hyperframes-launches](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes-launches) films followed (brief, directions, storyboard, build, notes), each step pointing at the guide that owns it, with build owned by whichever workflow the brief routes to. A new film asked for inside an existing project skips `hyperframes init` and never overwrites the project's BRIEF.md or STORYBOARD.md: it adds a new dated section to each and says so, and the reply may suggest a new project for a whole new film. It adds only the launch-film rules no guide states yet (real footage for the launched product, one world across beats, a cursor or scrolled content leaves through the edge while element and text swaps follow the workflow's `cut-catalog.md`, close on the command, state the runtime every version), and defers to the workflow's chosen arc where they differ.

Three small edits keep one owner per rule:

- `hyperframes/SKILL.md` § 1 gets two rows above "Specific edit to an existing project": a question, a hold, an idea or a felt note on an existing project goes to `/hyperframes-studio` § 0, and a new film asked for inside an existing project goes to § 5. Today the table has no row for those, so they fall into "Make the edit" or re-run the existing brief.
- `intent-interview.md` names that one exception to "fresh creation only".
- `hyperframes-creative/references/storyboard-recipe.md` narrows "Never draw a vendor's UI in DOM" to "never approximate the launched product's UI: use a capture or recording of it, rebuild only what the capture cannot move, or rebuild from its own design source (`/figma`); a third-party tool shown as context is rebuilt faithfully from a capture", which is what the launch films did and matches `/figma`.

The skills manifest is regenerated.

## Why

An agent in Studio today treats every message as an edit request: a question like "why does the title jump?" or "let's talk about the intro first" comes back as a changed film. There was also no written order for making a new film from nothing, so agents skipped straight to building.

## Related work

None.

## How

Docs only. Sections 1 to 4 and "Checking your work" are unchanged. Neither new section restates a rule a guide already owns: counts of directions and questions stay in `pitch-round.md` and `intent-interview.md`; build order, sound order and seams stay in the routed workflow; render-on-approval and note recording stay in `review-loop.md` and `storyboard-recipe.md`.

The storyboard-recipe narrowing is a choice for reviewers: it follows the launch films; the alternative is to keep the recipe line and drop section 5's rule about rebuilding third-party tools.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- Skills manifest regenerated from a clean `skills/` tree; regenerating again gives no diff.
- `oxfmt` over the changed files: no diff.
- Comment citation check and comment ratchet against the merge base: pass.
- Every guide the new sections point to exists at the cited path.

title: fix(studio): an escape that cancels a timeline band stops there
body:
## What

An Escape that cancels an in-progress selection band on the timeline stops there. It no longer also reaches the app hosting Studio, which could run its own Escape action (for example leaving the current section) on the same key press.

## Why

The timeline's Escape listener cancelled the band but left the key unclaimed: it neither prevented the default nor stopped propagation, so any host listener saw the same Escape.

## Related work

None.

## How

While a band or range selection is in flight, Escape is handled in the capture phase on the window: it cancels the band, prevents the default and stops propagation, so listeners on the document, on elements or in the window's bubble phase never see it. A host listening on the window in the capture phase still receives it and can check `defaultPrevented`. As a result, one Escape during a band no longer also leaves a sub-composition in Studio itself. With no band in flight, Escape behaves as before (it cancels a clip drag or clears the selection, unclaimed), so a popover that stops Escape to keep the selection still works.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `Timeline.bandEscape.test.tsx` renders the real timeline, drags a selection band on an empty lane and presses Escape with a document-level listener standing in for the host. With a band in flight, the host listener never sees the key, the default is prevented, the band is gone and the earlier selection is back. With no band, the host still receives Escape. The first case fails on main and fails with `stopPropagation` removed.
- The Studio player component tests pass (1380). Lint, format, typecheck, the audit gate, the comment check and the file-size check pass.

A small Escape listener was added to the page in both runs, standing in for a host app; it shows a red "Host received Escape" banner when the key reaches it. It is not part of Studio.

## Before

A band dragged on an empty timeline lane, then Escape: the band is cancelled and the host also receives the key.

![Before: the band is cancelled and the host banner shows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c41f64f-1b62-4496-bbb4-155abdaabec3)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfded28a-5713-4952-9a0b-0a4879d11956

## After

Same steps: the band is cancelled and the host never sees the key.

![After: the band is cancelled and no host banner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b8e72c6c-2951-4458-b1d0-3ad9b22ff305)

title: feat(cli): add hyperframes clean to find and remove what HyperFrames left on disk
body:
Follows #4694 (renders leave no captured frames behind), which records the owner each render temp dir uses here.

## What this adds

`hyperframes clean` reports what HyperFrames left on this machine, with sizes, and removes it.

```
hyperframes clean --dry-run    # list, remove nothing
hyperframes clean              # remove
hyperframes clean --snapshots  # also remove snapshots/ folders
hyperframes clean --json       # for agents
```

What it removes:
- **Render leftovers:** work and staging dirs of renders that are no longer running, in the current folder, in every project the history cache knows (and their `renders/`), and in the temp dir. A dir counts as abandoned only when its recorded owner (#4694) has exited in this pid scope, or, for dirs made before owners were recorded, when nothing in it has been written for 6 hours. Only render temp dir names are considered.
- **Debug renders:** job-id-named work dirs under the render debug dir, by the same rule. Nothing else in that dir is touched, even when `PRODUCER_RENDERS_DIR` points it somewhere shared.
- **Project history** of projects that no longer exist, using the studio server's own rule (`pruneGoneProjectHistories`).
- **Video proxies** nobody has used for an hour and **extracted video frames**, both regenerable. Each cache's existing sweep gains a `dryRun` option, so the listing and the removal run the same code.

Snapshots are listed as "also reclaimable" and removed only with `--snapshots`. Proxies and snapshots are only swept inside a HyperFrames project (a folder whose `index.html` holds a composition root). Outputs, sources, the browser download and any dir whose owner is still running are never touched. A leftover that cannot be removed, or an unreadable history folder, is reported under `errors`, the rest of the clean still runs, and the command exits 1.

## Engine fix this needed

A render renewed its lease on an extracted-frame cache entry only while that clip was on screen. A clip that first appears more than an hour into a long capture looked abandoned to any sweep in that window (the cache's own size-cap sweep before this PR, and `clean` now). The injector now renews every entry the render holds on every frame, throttled per directory as before (`FrameLookupTable.frameDirs()`).

## Evidence

On a shared Linux dev machine:

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `clean --dry-run` | 1.9 s, 11 rows, 5.8 GB, 0 errors |
| `clean --dry-run --json` | home folder redacted in every path |

### Sandboxed run of every delete path

The built CLI ran with HOME, TMPDIR, XDG dirs, `PRODUCER_RENDERS_DIR` and the frame cache redirected into a scratch root, while a watcher listed every pre-existing file outside it that disappeared. Result: 29 of 29 checks pass, nothing outside the scratch root removed.

| Path | Removed | Kept |
|---|---|---|
| Render leftovers | dead-owner work dir, dead staging dir, ownerless dir idle 7 h, dead-owner dir in the project root, temp-dir leftover | live render's dir, fresh ownerless dir, staging dir holding `backup`, `work-in-progress` user folder, the output and `index.html` |
| Debug renders | job-id dir idle 7 h | `.build-id`, `my-notes` |
| Project history | history of a project whose folder is gone | histories of existing projects, one of them reached through a symlinked path |
| Video proxies | idle proxy, stale temp file | recent proxy, a user's `holiday.mp4` in the cache folder |
| Extracted frames | entry unused for 2 h, aged partial | fresh entry, live partial |
| `--snapshots` | project snapshots | snapshots of a folder that is not a HyperFrames project (a plain website) |
| Ctrl+C in the middle of removing a 60,000-file leftover | exits 130, nothing on the keep list touched; the next run finishes the removal | |
| Symlinks to folders outside the scratch root, each holding a user file, an `.mp4` and a frame | | all six targets intact: render-named link, link inside a removed dir, `snapshots` link (only the link goes), `.transcode-cache` link, temp-dir link, frame-cache link |

The `.transcode-cache` case failed on the first run: the proxy sweep removed any idle `.mp4` or `.webm` in that folder, so an old video in a folder linked as the cache went. The sweep now removes only names the transcoder writes (`<sha256>.<ext>` and `.tmp-<uuid>-<proxy name>`), which also protects the Studio's own sweep.

## Tests

| Test | Fails without |
|---|---|
| `clean.test.ts` removes what dead renders left and keeps what a running render uses (live owner, fresh ownerless dir, user folder, output, non-job debug dir) | job-id matching for debug dirs |
| `clean.test.ts` reports a leftover it cannot remove and still removes the rest | per-dir error handling |
| `clean.test.ts` leaves snapshots alone in a folder that is not a HyperFrames project (a plain website) | the composition-root project check |
| `clean.test.ts` still cleans when the history folder cannot be read | the history error handling |
| `clean.test.ts` lists a leftover once when the project folder is a link to the temp dir | comparing real paths |
| `clean.test.ts` exits 1 when something could not be read or removed (through the command) | reporting the exit code through the CLI's command result |
| `clean.test.ts` lists snapshots as reclaimable and removes them only when asked | |
| `videoFrameInjector.test.ts` renews the entry of a clip that is not on screen yet | renewing every held entry |
| `proxyCache.test.ts` reports the same removals in a dry run and removes nothing | the budget pass seeing only what the idle pass kept |
| `proxyCache.test.ts` never removes a file the transcoder did not name, even from an idle cache over budget | matching transcoder names |
| `extractionCache.test.ts` counts the same evictions in a dry run and removes nothing | |

Each "fails without" was checked by reverting that piece and watching the test go red.

## Not covered here

- Sizes can under-report slightly: aged partial frame-cache dirs, stale proxy temp files and history dirs already mid-prune are removed but not counted.
- A render that hits the frame cache and then spends more than an hour extracting other, uncached videos renews nothing until its first captured frame, so a sweep in that window can remove the hit entry. This predates the PR (the cache's own sweep has the same window); closing it means renewing during extraction.
- Leftovers next to an output written outside any known project (`-o` elsewhere) are found only when `clean` runs in that folder.

title: fix(studio): an escape cancels a preview marquee band and stops there
body:
## What

An Escape pressed while a marquee band is being dragged on the preview canvas cancels the band: it disappears, releasing the pointer selects nothing, and that Escape stops there instead of also reaching the host page. An Escape with no band in flight reaches the host as before.

## Why

`useMarqueeGestures` had a `cancel()` that nothing called on Escape. The band stayed up, the release still selected everything under it, and the Escape went on to the host, which could act on it too.

## Related work

The same rule for the timeline's band: #4700.

## How

While mounted, the hook listens for Escape on `window` in the capture phase. Only while a band is in flight, it prevents the default, stops propagation and calls `cancel()`. Studio's overlay and any host using the exported hook get it from the one place.

## Before

`main`, Studio with a fixture film. A band is dragged on empty preview canvas, then Escape is pressed with the mouse still down: the band stays, and the page's own window listener receives the Escape (count 1).

![Before: after Escape the dashed band is still on the preview](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e0cccef-f901-48aa-b848-013b9b9359bd)

## After

The same steps on this branch. The band was up while dragging, and Escape removes it. The page's own listener receives nothing (count 0).

![After: the band while dragging](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e98b1fff-d712-4610-bc55-e18e48b1bf65)

![After: after Escape the band is gone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/839475d6-91ad-465d-92e0-65c2d775cd1a)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added (`marqueeCommit.test.tsx`): an Escape mid-drag removes the band while the pointer is still down, and the host's window listener never sees the key. An Escape with no band still reaches the host.
- [x] The test fails with `main`'s `marqueeCommit.ts` and with the `cancel()` call removed, and passed three runs in a row on the branch. The editor area passes (1499 tests). Studio typecheck, lint, format, the comment checks and the audit gate pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the captures above, driven in Chrome against Studio's dev server.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Not covered

- Other `window` capture-phase Escape listeners that registered before this one still run. For example, Studio's app hotkeys drop the razor tool on Escape. The timeline band in #4700 has the same limit.

title: feat(studio): a host can hide the timeline's audio effects controls
body:
## What

`Timeline` takes a new `showAudioEffects` prop. It defaults to `true`, so Studio looks and behaves exactly as before. A host that sets it to `false` gets track and group headers with no audio-effects controls:

- the Effects button on a single-clip audio track;
- the "group these clips" Effects button on an audio track of several clips;
- the Effects button on a group header;
- the group name's "Open effects" label. The name still selects the group, which keeps the group's automation lanes editable; it is labelled "Select" instead;
- the "Show … in the effect rack" shortcut on automation lane names, for clips and groups. The lanes stay and still show their values.

## Why

An app embedding the Studio timeline that does not offer audio effects has no way to hide these controls today.

## Related work

Mirrors how `showKeyframes` lets a host hide the keyframe controls on `TimelineToolbar`.

## How

One optional prop, threaded the way `theme` already reaches the headers: `TimelineProps` → the provider's lane props → `TimelineLanes` → `TimelineTrackHeader`, and `TimelineGroupRow` → `TimelineGroupHeader`. Each header defaults it to `true`.

Not covered by this prop: the effects rack inside the property panel, which is not part of `Timeline`, and a carve lane's tooltip that mentions the FX rack (a carve only exists on a film that already uses effects). Automation lanes stay, because they carry volume and fades as well as effect parameters.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `Timeline.audioEffects.test.tsx` mounts the real `Timeline` with the prop omitted and with `false`, on a single-clip audio track, a track of several clips and a group. Three of its four tests fail on main's code; the default-case test passes on both. The lane-shortcut tests in `TimelineTrackHeader.test.tsx` and `TimelineGroupRow.test.tsx` fail on main's code too.
- Each link in the chain was broken on purpose, one at a time (provider, lanes to track header, lanes to group row, group row to header, each of the four controls, both lane shortcuts, the group lane label, the default): all 12 breaks fail a test.
- Touched test files pass together and one by one; `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, the comment checks and the dead-code audit pass.
- In Studio on a test film built for this PR, main and this branch with the prop omitted produce byte-identical screenshots.

## Before

Studio on main (a0c72ad6): FX on the voice track, the track of two clicks and the group.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/efc72b80-c7f1-419e-983f-2b903ef5437f)

## After

The same film on this branch with `showAudioEffects={false}` passed to `Timeline` (a local change for the capture only; Studio itself does not set it). No FX controls; the group name remains.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22e4abbe-ed73-4366-ac52-be70b5e30ad1)

title: fix(studio): moving one word moves only that word, not every word sharing its animation
body:
## What

Dragging or arrow-nudging one word in the preview moves only that word, and the move survives a reload and a render. Before, when the words shared one staggered animation, the move was written into that shared animation and every word moved after the next reload. One drag is one undo step, and a second drag on the same word updates its saved position.

## Why

The drag commit resolved the word's position animation from its class selector, so a staggered tween on `.w` counted as the word's own. The drag then split that tween and rewrote it with keyframes aimed at `.w`: every word moved, and the tween was stretched, lost its ease and had its stagger copied into each keyframe. The split and the move were also two history entries, so the first undo left the file in an intermediate split state.

Dragging the end node of that shared tween's motion path did nothing at all.

## Related work

None.

## How

- Each tween is sorted against the live DOM as the element's own, shared with siblings, or not reaching it. A tween that does not reach the element no longer influences the drag.
- When the only thing positioning the element is a tween shared with its siblings, the drag or nudge is saved on that one element as `position: relative` with `left` and `top`, found by its `data-hf-id`. GSAP never touches these, so the word keeps its staggered entrance, shifted by the drag, in the preview and in the render. The shared tween's source is untouched.
- An element that already has its own `left`/`top` gets the move added to them. Before saving, the new values are applied and checked: if the box did not shift by exactly the drag (for example a box anchored by `right` or `bottom`), the change is rolled back and the existing toast explains why.
- Other edits still refuse `left` and `top`; only this case writes them.
- A top- or left-corner resize on such an element saves its anchor move the same way, after the size and under the same undo step; if the size save fails, the move is not kept.
- A word picked from the Layers panel (which lifts it to `position: relative` while shown) is saved against its authored position, so `position: relative` is written with the offset when the source had none.
- The motion-path end node of a shared tween is read-only, so pressing it drags the element itself.
- Every write of one drag carries one gesture key, so a drag through the tween path is one history entry however long the round trip takes.

## Test plan

- Unit tests: a shared-tween word's drag saves `left`/`top` and leaves the tween byte-identical; a second drag accumulates; a right-anchored box is refused and rolled back; a corner resize saves its move; a tween that targets only the word is still edited; a tween elsewhere in the page has no effect; one gesture key covers the split and the move; the shared motion path is read-only; an ordinary element's `left`/`top` edit is still refused. Removing each rule fails its test.
- In the app, with 8 words sharing one stagger tween, "How" moved:

  | Fixture | Saved on "How" | After reload, and after seeking back | Entrance slide | Other 7 words |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `from` stagger, drag | `left: 30px; top: 20px` | +30, +20 | kept | unmoved |
  | `fromTo` stagger, drag | `left: 30px; top: 20px` | +30, +20 | kept | unmoved |
  | `from` stagger, arrow nudge | `left: 40px; top: 20px` | +40, +20 | kept | unmoved |
  | main, `from` drag | the shared tween rewritten | all 8 words +30, +20 | changed | all moved |

  The drags land at +30 because Studio snaps to a guide on release, on main as well.
- A render of each fixture matches the table, with no pixels changed outside "How".
- One undo after a drag restores the file byte for byte, one redo re-applies it, and after two drags one undo reverts only the second.
- The Studio hooks and editor tests pass. Typecheck, lint, format, the audit gate, the comment check and the file-size check pass.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

## Before

"How" dragged, then the project reloaded: every word has moved.

![Before: after the reload the whole phrase has moved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d247eadf-3099-4127-92cc-598fd4db814f)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b54cf69-dc41-4aa9-b4ae-3053642ccc83

## After

Same steps: only "How" has moved.

![After: only the dragged word has moved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53e7366d-e9f3-4582-bcf4-c27d67b1ece0)

title: chore: release v0.8.87
body:
# HyperFrames v0.8.87

Released on 2026-09-28.

An app that embeds Studio can now save style edits on a selection without Studio's editor. Escape cancels a marquee band, and sound effects start on time.

## Features

- **Studio:** An embedding app can save style edits on a selection through Studio's own style save ([0af671c6d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/0af671c6df8f8f740f2e982247ae3eab67dd0514), [#4698](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4698)).

## Fixes

- **Studio:** Escape cancels a marquee band on the preview and goes no further ([a51992743](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/a519927436a75b48d8564c75206a8d9624fc0251), [#4703](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4703)).
- **Studio:** Escape cancels a marquee band on the timeline and goes no further ([f7207247d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/f7207247de18c616dd03b063c29a00f3e5000068), [#4700](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4700)).
- **Producer:** Renders leave no captured frames behind when interrupted ([f7ef18dca](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/f7ef18dca80c791a2991a90280638b32c109d227), [#4694](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4694)).
- **Core:** A sound effect starts on its time instead of a frame late ([e0b940aa3](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/e0b940aa302efb011009395af54d4023ae08baf1), [#4696](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4696)).
- **Studio:** Drilling in opens the composition's full project path ([a0c72ad64](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/a0c72ad64a3a68b115495f544e4aa675a41dd74e), [#4689](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4689)).

## Performance

- **Studio:** Swap an edited scene into the live preview instead of reloading ([303c8e922](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/303c8e922f89f657557ad304557101e36fbd7750), [#4499](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4499)).

title: perf(studio): clicking an element in the preview selects it without restyling the whole film
body:
## What

Clicking or hovering an element in Studio's preview no longer restyles the whole film. On a 1,426-element text film, click-to-selected drops from 219 ms to 120 ms (median) and the inspector fills in at 68 ms instead of 163 ms. Nothing changes in what gets selected, except two edge cases noted below where the new result is the one Chrome itself gives.

## Why

Selecting by hand in the preview felt slow, sometimes too slow to edit with. Every canvas hit test (a click runs up to four, a hover runs one per pointer move) added a `* { pointer-events: auto !important }` style element to the preview document, called `elementsFromPoint`, and removed it. That had two costs that grow with the number of elements:

- each insert and each removal invalidated style on every element, so the next `elementsFromPoint` and the next `getComputedStyle` each recalculated style for the whole document (a trace showed 18 full-document recalcs of 1,414 elements per click);
- the head mutation reached the off-canvas indicators' MutationObserver, which threw its layer-walk cache away and rebuilt it from scratch on the next frame.

The override was added before the author pointer-events filter existed. Since that filter landed, every element the override let into the hit list (those with computed `pointer-events: none`) is removed again, so the override did the expensive part and the filter undid it.

## How

`getPreviewTargetFromPointer` and `getAllPreviewTargetsFromPointer` call the browser's own `elementsFromPoint` and keep the existing author pointer-events filter. The override helpers are deleted.

Behaviour: on the heavy film, a grid of 5,280 points over six playhead times gave the same pick and the same click-through list from the old and new code, with no duplicates. A side-by-side run of both versions in headless Chrome found two edge cases that now follow the browser: a `pointer-events: none` child painted under its parent (`z-index: -1`) no longer hides the parent from selection, and SVG shapes with keyword `pointer-events` values (`fill`, `bounding-box`) hit-test the way Chrome defines them instead of as `auto`.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `studioPreviewHelpers.test.ts`: both hit tests run with no style added to the preview document and no DOM mutation. Fails on the old code (style count `[1, 1, 1]`, and separately the mutation list), passes on this branch. The file: 12 passed.
- [x] Latency, measured on the built CLI Studio (`hyperframes preview`) with headless Chrome: pointerdown to the frame after the selection box and the inspector both show the new element, 24 clicks per run plus 8 drag starts, text-heavy repo film (`packages/producer/tests/spanish-empire-cdn-inline`, 1,426 elements) and a light one (`sub-comp-t0`, 33 elements).
- [x] CPU profile of the same 24 clicks, before and after (see numbers below).

### Measurements

Built CLI Studio, headless Chrome on a shared 8-core Linux box. A click is timed from pointerdown to the frame after both the selection box and the inspector show the new element; a drag start from the first pointermove to the first frame the box moved. Only runs whose 1-minute load stayed under 16 at start and end are pooled.

| Film | Build | Clicks (runs) | Click to selected, median / p95 | Inspector filled, median / p95 | Drag start, median / p95 (n) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Text-heavy, 1,426 elements | v0.8.86 | 58 (3) | 219 / 403 ms | 163 / 331 ms | 74 / 417 ms (14) |
| Text-heavy, 1,426 elements | this branch | 34 (2) | 120 / 412 ms | 68 / 260 ms | 52 / 837 ms (8) |
| Light, 33 elements | v0.8.86 | 72 (3) | 80 / 184 ms | 38 / 147 ms | 28 / 34 ms (24) |
| Light, 33 elements | this branch | 48 (2) | 94 / 234 ms | 43 / 199 ms | 26 / 53 ms (16) |

The cost grows with the number of elements: the light film is the same before and after within run-to-run spread (single-run medians range from 72 to 154 ms on both sides). The p95 column is dominated by the first clicks of each run and by other work on the box; runs that went over load 16 were dropped, and in those the text film's run medians were 237 to 516 ms before and 87 to 182 ms after.

Trace of 10 clicks on the text film (per click):

| | v0.8.86 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Full-document style recalculations | 19 (1,414 elements each) | 0 (largest touches 317 elements) |
| Style recalculation time | 58 ms | 4 ms |
| Main-thread script time | 222 ms | 72 ms |

CPU profile of the same 24 clicks and 8 drag starts (total ms over the run, source-mapped; the box was busier during the before run, so compare ratios):

| Function | v0.8.86 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `getPreviewTargetFromPointer` (studioPreviewHelpers.ts) | 2,463 | 89 |
| `elementsFromPoint` (native, self) | 1,472 | 67 |
| `hasAuthorPointerEventsNone` (studioPreviewHelpers.ts, self) | 1,384 | 3 |
| `recomputeOffCanvasIndicators` (offCanvasIndicatorGeometry.ts) | 2,764 | 209 |
| All non-idle script | 11,615 | 3,471 |

What is left on a click is mostly the network round trip for the source probe and React rendering the inspector; that is a separate change.

## Before

v0.8.86: 10 clicks on the text film, the latency of each shown on the page (median 262 ms in this recording).

![Before: v0.8.86, last of 10 clicks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d96404c-775a-4362-97e8-7dcce66f9f81)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bda6bc9b-3a7c-455f-855f-3234e98bb0f3

## After

This branch: the same clicks (median 120 ms in this recording).

![After: this branch, last of 10 clicks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76515675-f168-436a-ae43-3448ae42a1f6)

title: feat(studio): a host can save canvas moves, resizes and rotations with the handles
body:
## What

A host can save canvas moves, resizes and rotations made with `DomEditOverlay` without mounting Studio's editor session:

- **`useDomGeometryCommit({ projectId, iframeRef, writeProjectFile, recordEdit, activeCompPath?, showToast?, reloadPreview? })`** returns `commitPathOffset`, `commitGroupPathOffset`, `commitBoxSize`, `commitRotation` and `waitForPendingSaves`. The four commits take the overlay's own arguments, so they plug straight into `onPathOffsetCommit`, `onGroupPathOffsetCommit`, `onBoxSizeCommit` and `onRotationCommit`.
- Each commit resolves to `{ ok: true }` once the edit is saved and rejects when it is not, so the overlay undoes the live gesture exactly as it does in Studio. `waitForPendingSaves` waits for every write still in flight.
- The host shows the project in Studio's `Player`, having run `usePlayerStore.getState().beginTimelineSession(projectId)` before it mounts, as Studio's own editor does. Until that preview has loaded, a commit refuses at once with an error toast instead of waiting, and a resize is undone. The host drains `waitForPendingSaves` before switching projects.

## Why

`DomEditOverlay` is exported (#4708), but its commits only existed inside `useDomEditSession`, which needs Studio's right panel, file tree and source editor and runs its own preview sync. A host with its own preview and picker could draw the handles but not save what they changed.

## Related work

Follows #4708 (exports `DomEditOverlay`) and `useDomStyleCommit` from #4698.

## How

No second writer and no copied logic. The hook composes the hooks `useDomEditSession` uses for canvas geometry: `useGsapScriptCommits` writes and records history, and `useGsapAwareEditing` routes the move, resize and rotate. A drag takes the same GSAP-aware path as in Studio: a static element gets a `gsap.set`, an animated one a keyframe, and a group drag is one undo step. The host passes the same `writeProjectFile` and `recordEdit` it gives the timeline, so both share one file lock and one undo list. The host owns selection, so each gesture reads its element's animations from the server.

Two changes outside the hook:

- The overlay's four geometry commit props now accept a promise of any value (as `onStyleCommit` already did), so commits that resolve to an outcome type-check. Every consumer only awaits the promise.
- A resize whose animation lookup fails now undoes its draft, reports the failure and rejects. Before, the lookup ran ahead of the transaction that owns the undo, so the element stayed resized with nothing saved. Studio hit this only when resizing an element that was not the selected one; for a host it is every resize.

## Before

A host page with its own preview and `DomEditOverlay` mounted: the drag draws live, but the package has no commit to save it, so on release the title snaps back and nothing is saved.

![Before: the move is refused and the title snaps back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e408a01c-1b5a-40ac-bc50-aca59dc25b50)

## After

The same page passes `useDomGeometryCommit`'s commits to the overlay: the move resolves `{ ok: true }`, adds one "Move layer" undo step, and writes `gsap.set("#title", { x: 620, y: 300 })` to the source.

![After: the move is saved as one undo step and a gsap.set](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f7bc86ab-25d4-4852-92a5-b96079748924)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added (`useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`, through the package entry):
  - the four commits type-check as the overlay's props
  - a move on a static element saves one GSAP `set` and one history entry, and resolves `{ ok: true }`
  - the commits keep their identity across renders
  - a refused save rejects with an error toast and records nothing
  - a resize whose animations cannot be read calls its restore, toasts, and saves nothing
  - when the player shows another project, or the preview has not loaded, a commit refuses at once, toasts and restores a resize
  - `waitForPendingSaves` waits for a move still being saved
  - without a project, a commit rejects and writes nothing
- [x] Each test fails when the behaviour it guards is removed (ten break proofs).
- [x] Manual testing performed: the host page below, driven with Playwright against Studio's dev server and a fixture built for it.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): the timeline follows a paused playhead and zoom keeps it in place
body:
## What

The Studio timeline now keeps the playhead in view while the film is paused:

- **A paused seek follows.** Moving the preview slider, stepping with the keys or any other seek that puts the playhead off screen scrolls the timeline so the playhead is visible again. A seek that lands on screen does not scroll.
- **Toolbar and slider zoom keep the playhead in place.** The playhead stays where it was on screen while the scale changes; if it was off screen, the zoom brings it into view. Before, zoom kept the middle of the view fixed, and did nothing at all when the view was at 00:00.

Unchanged: no scroll while the playhead or a beat is being dragged, none in Fit, and a person's own timeline scroll while paused is never undone. The view follows only a seek someone asked for. A window resize still keeps the view's middle time, or 00:00 when the view is at the start (#4411).

## Why

Paused, the timeline only followed during playback, so a seek from the preview or the keyboard could leave the playhead off screen with no way to see where it went. Zooming in to look closely at the playhead moved it away instead.

## Related work

Keeps #4411's rule for window resizes. A zoom set with the playhead at 00:00, such as a zoom restored when a project opens, still stays at 00:00.

## How

`useTimelinePlayhead.ts`:

- The live-time subscriber, which already scrolled during playback, now also runs while paused, after a seek. Paused, it scrolls only when the playhead is outside the view, reusing the playback follow position.
- A person's zoom is told apart from every other scale change by a counter: `useTimelineZoom`'s `setManualZoomPercent` (the toolbar buttons and slider) bumps `userZoomCount` in the store, while the zoom pin on a first edit and the re-pin after a length change write the percent directly. The anchor effect treats a scale change as a person's zoom only when the counter moved in the same commit. A person's zoom anchors on the playhead when it is on screen, then brings it into view if needed; a window resize, a pin or a re-pin keep the old centre anchor and the start-of-view rule.
- A seek is told apart from other publishes of the playhead time by a second counter: `useTimelinePlayer`'s `seek()`, which every seek a person makes goes through (keys, preview slider, ruler, Layers panel), publishes with `liveTime.notifySeek`, which counts it. Seeks Studio makes on its own pass `follow: false`, which publishes without counting: the hand-over to a reloaded preview, the return after an FX preset audition, and a clip trim's edge preview and its return to the playhead on release (while trimming, the trim's own edge auto-scroll owns the view). A preview reload republishes the playhead time, rounded down to a frame by the runtime, and a keyboard pause or a reverse shuttle stop leaves the published and stored times apart; comparing times would read those as moves and undo a person's scroll, so paused follow looks at the counter instead.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `useTimelinePlayhead.test.tsx` covers: a paused seek off screen scrolls it into view; a paused seek on screen (even past the playback follow line) does not; a republished paused time does not undo a manual scroll; no scroll while dragging the playhead or a beat, or in Fit; a toolbar zoom keeps the playhead's screen position, brings an off-screen playhead into view, and still anchors when it lands on the stored percent; a zoom with the playhead at 0 stays at 00:00; a resize keeps 00:00 (also after an edit pinned the zoom) and keeps the centre when scrolled; a length re-pin does not jump to an off-screen playhead; a resize after a toolbar zoom that hit the zoom limit keeps the centre; a seek to the time the playhead already has scrolls back to it; a preview reload that republishes a seek rounded to a frame, follows a keyboard pause, or stops a reverse shuttle does not undo a manual scroll. `useTimelinePlayer.seek.test.ts`: a seek is published as a counted seek, and a reload's hand-over and an audition's return are not. `useTimelineClipDrag.resize.test.tsx`: a trim's preview and release seeks pass `follow: false`. `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`: a Zoom in click counts as a person's zoom. Five of the new tests fail on main's code.
- Nineteen targeted breaks (seek check, playhead drag check, beat drag check, Fit check, paused reveal rule, playhead anchor, the 00:00 skip for zooms, resize treated as zoom, the counter bump, the resize 00:00 rule, a seek published as a plain time, comparing times instead of counting seeks, the seek count bump, the reload hand-over counted as a seek, the audition return counted as a seek, the trim preview and the trim release counted as seeks, `follow: false` ignored, the counter in the anchor effect's dependencies) each fail a test.
- Touched test files pass together and one by one (273 tests, with the player hook suites); `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, the comment checks and the dead-code audit pass.

## Before

Studio on main (2195db5e), paused, on the pr-to-video film from the public hyperframes-launches repo: zoom in three times, step the playhead past the right edge with Shift+Right, then zoom in once more. The timeline stays at 00:00 while the playhead leaves the view, and the last zoom keeps 00:00 with the playhead far off screen.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9ec5457-8418-41f8-9388-d3110d77b046

## After

The same steps on this branch (260bd4d1): the timeline scrolls to keep the stepped playhead in view, and the last zoom keeps the playhead where it was on screen.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05d1f019-2cef-401e-9e19-1db74326a837

title: feat(studio): one timeline tool picker with select leftward and rightward
body:
The timeline's Selection and Razor buttons become one tool button, like CapCut: it shows the active tool's icon and a chevron, and opens a menu with each tool's icon, name and key, the active one highlighted.

- **Select (V)** and **Split (B)**: the existing tools.
- **Select leftward ([)**: selects every clip, on every track, that starts before the playhead.
- **Select rightward (])**: selects every clip, on every track, that starts at or after the playhead.

The two selections are store actions next to `setActiveTool`, and `[` / `]` are wired beside V and B. No new host prop.

## Before

![After: one tool button with a chevron](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54aa18a7-6646-417b-a214-e145f97bfeb4)
