Captured from the repo's product-promo example in headless Chrome.

## Tests

`useAppHotkeys.test.ts`: `[` selects clips starting before the playhead on every track, `]` selects clips at or after it, neither selects anything when no clip is on that side, while playing they use the live playhead, and they clear a clicked keyframe like any other selection change (they select the way the marquee does).
`TimelineHistoryButtons.dom.test.tsx`: the toolbar reads Undo, Redo, then the picker, and the picker shows Split while the razor is active.



## Not in this PR

- The menu rows show the active tool by highlight only; radio semantics for screen readers can reuse `MenuRadioItem`.
- The picker has no hover tooltip; the "Shift+click splits all tracks" hint stays in the shortcuts sheet.

title: feat(studio): a host can hide the timeline's keyframe lanes and diamonds
body:
## What

`Timeline` takes a new `showKeyframes` prop. It defaults to `true`, so Studio is unchanged. A host that sets it to `false` gets a timeline with no keyframe lanes and no keyframe diamonds. Track names stay in the header.

## Why

An app embedding the Studio timeline that does not offer keyframe editing has no way to hide keyframes from the timeline today. `TimelineToolbar` already takes `showKeyframes` for its own keyframe controls (#4680); this is the same switch for the timeline itself.

## Related work

Refs #4680 (the toolbar's `showKeyframes`) and #4704 (`showAudioEffects`, threaded the same way).

## How

The provider reads the store's keyframe data (animations and the keyframe cache) through one small hook, `useTimelineKeyframeData(showKeyframes)`, which hands the timeline empty data when keyframes are hidden. Every keyframe lane, diamond and lane count derives from that data, so none of the drawing code changes. The label column still reads the unfiltered animations, so a keyframed film keeps its track names when keyframes are hidden.

The toolbar keeps its own `showKeyframes` prop (#4680): `Timeline` and `TimelineToolbar` are separate components a host renders separately, so a host passes the flag to both. The After capture does exactly that.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `Timeline.showKeyframes.test.tsx` mounts the real `Timeline`: a collapsed clip's diamonds and a keyframed clip's lanes are drawn by default and absent with `showKeyframes={false}`, and the track name stays in the header either way. The two off-state tests fail on main's code.
- Breaking the gate for diamonds, for lanes, for the track names, or flipping the default each fails a test.
- Touched test files pass together and one by one; `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, the comment checks and the dead-code audit pass.
- Studio on the pr-to-video film from the public hyperframes-launches repo: 12 diamonds on main, 12 on this branch with the prop omitted, 0 with `showKeyframes={false}`.

## Before

Studio on main (e07ea1fc): keyframe lanes and diamonds under the keyframed clips.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e44f977f-b183-477e-805e-fe400b72a983)

## After

The same film on this branch with `showKeyframes={false}` passed to both `Timeline` and `TimelineToolbar` (a local change for the capture only; Studio itself does not set it). Track names stay; no keyframe lanes, diamonds or toolbar keyframe buttons.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d682d640-9b64-420e-913e-03462ac5fb96)

title: chore: release v0.8.87
body:
# HyperFrames v0.8.87

Released on 2026-09-29.

An app that embeds Studio can now mount its canvas handles, save style edits and hide the audio effects controls. The player can loop a range of a film, `hyperframes clean` frees disk space, and sound effects start on time.

## Features

- **CLI:** `hyperframes clean` finds and removes what HyperFrames left on disk ([663b02297](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/663b02297d58b56d7153bb156451ebb2b830941b), [#4701](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4701)).
- **Studio:** An embedding app can mount Studio's move, resize and rotate handles over its own preview ([cc792d4a8](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/cc792d4a8a9e79cca0678f1be68b54a51ae59d81), [#4708](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4708)).
- **Player:** Play and loop a range of a film with range-start and range-end ([840f65702](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/840f657028b9cf7f20a1a2efb9d436e52aa42d71), [#4688](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4688)).
- **Studio:** An embedding app can hide the timeline's audio effects controls ([dc61ce105](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/dc61ce105bc5ead8d4c0262298bc2aff5031c233), [#4704](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4704)).
- **Studio:** An embedding app can save style edits on a selection through Studio's own style save ([0af671c6d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/0af671c6df8f8f740f2e982247ae3eab67dd0514), [#4698](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4698)).

## Fixes

- **Media Use:** Record agent-made voice, music and sound effects in the media manifest ([e25bc3a80](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/e25bc3a80625af41ca576d80224f1dc1a621eb42), [#4648](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4648)).
- **Studio Server:** The server loads where sharp's native binary is missing ([498643bea](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/498643bea46b15ab717769c44bf0ef333381b4b0), [#4654](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4654)).
- **Studio Server:** Undo keeps an outside change even when Studio's history claim arrives late ([381fb0fd9](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/381fb0fd9a24b0c49713452bb61314eccce0aaae), [#4631](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4631)).

title: fix(studio): undo and redo update the preview in place instead of reloading it
body:
## What

Undo and redo in Studio now update the preview in place by swapping only the edited scene, instead of reloading the whole preview. Redo no longer gets stuck on the undone state.

## Why

After a move, pressing undo should put the element back at once, the way it works in After Effects or Premiere. On main it did not, for two reasons:

1. **Undo reloaded the whole preview.** A normal edit (move, text, colour) is applied to the live preview in place and written to disk. The live preview keeps, per scene, a hash of the build it loaded. Undo writes the file back to exactly that build, so when Studio asked the preview to swap in the rebuilt scene, the hashes matched, the swap refused with "no scene changed", and Studio fell back to a full reload.
2. **A preview asked for right after an undo or redo could be the previous build.** The server caches the project signature until its file watcher reports the write, and the watcher waits for the file to settle first. Studio asks for the rebuilt preview as soon as the undo answers, so that request could get the old signature, and the fresh build was cached under it. The next redo was then served the undone state: the swap refused, the full reload loaded the same stale document, and the redo did not appear until a later edit.

## How

- `applyUndoRestoreToPreview` blanks the live scene hash of every scene holding a restored file whenever it falls back to a reload (`markScenesStale` in `player/sceneSwap.ts`). The swap then counts that scene as changed and swaps it in place. A restored page that sits outside every scene (the root `index.html`, or a sub-composition path that does not match a host exactly, such as `./scenes/a.html`) blanks the shared hash instead, so that undo still gets the full reload rather than a partial swap. A scene the swap cannot take still falls back to the full reload, as before.
- The Studio API drops the host's cached project signature once any request that may write (anything but GET or HEAD) under `/projects/:id/` has finished. Both hosts implement the new optional `invalidateProjectSignature` adapter hook: the Vite dev server and the CLI preview server. The watcher still covers outside writes.
- The preview route keeps a build only if the project signature, computed again from disk once the build is done, still matches the one the build was keyed under. A preview or thumbnail request that was already building when the undo landed can no longer leave the undone build under the edited state's signature (the CLI keeps that cache on disk, so it outlived restarts).
- Left as is: the signature is also dropped after requests that write nothing (selection updates, history claims). The next request then walks the project's file stats once; it does not rebuild.

## Test plan

- `packages/studio` `gsapUndoRestore.test.ts`, new case: an undo restoring a scene file blanks that scene's live hash before `reloadPreview` runs and leaves the other scene alone. Fails without the fix (`scene0` stays `"h0"`).
- `packages/studio` same file, second half: a restore that also includes a page outside every scene blanks the shared hash. Fails without it.
- `packages/studio-server` `history.test.ts`, new case: with a host-style cached signature, the signature after an undo reflects the restored file. Fails without the fix (the edited build's signature is still served).
- `packages/studio-server` `preview.test.ts`, new case: a write that lands while a preview builds, then a redo back to the first content, gets the redo's content, not the build from the middle. Fails without the check.
- `packages/studio-server` full suite green (928 passed); `tsc --noEmit` clean for studio, studio-server and cli.
- Real browser: headless Chrome on a Linux box, the Studio dev server, a 12-scene fixture with every scene a sub-composition and GSAP from a CDN, so a normal edit is applied in place. Edits go through Studio's own paths: a mouse drag of an element, and the `studio_set_text` / `studio_set_style` tools. Undo and redo are the real Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z. Each time runs from the key press (or the pointer release, or the tool call) to the first animation frame whose visible preview shows the target state; the file on disk is checked after each undo (equal to the bytes before the edit) and each redo (equal to the bytes after it). 10 reps per kind per run.

Main (a0c72ad64) and this branch, back to back, load average 4 to 16:

| kind | step | main median | main worst | main path | branch median | branch worst | branch path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| move | edit | -179 ms | -143 ms | in place | -156 ms | -118 ms | in place |
| move | undo | 184 ms | 1402 ms | full reload 4, swap 6 | 146 ms | 465 ms | swap 10 |
| move | redo | 334 ms | never, 8 of 10 | full reload 4, swap 6 | 188 ms | 1804 ms | swap 10 |
| text | edit | 164 ms | 231 ms | in place | 144 ms | 317 ms | in place |
| text | undo | 386 ms | 1377 ms | full reload 3, swap 7 | 257 ms | 384 ms | swap 10 |
| text | redo | 555 ms | never, 6 of 10 | full reload 6, swap 4 | 254 ms | 567 ms | swap 10 |
| colour | edit | 106 ms | 188 ms | in place | 106 ms | 187 ms | in place |
| colour | undo | 452 ms | 1778 ms | full reload 5, swap 5 | 349 ms | 456 ms | swap 10 |
| colour | redo | 267 ms | never, 7 of 10 | full reload 3, swap 7 | 242 ms | 1268 ms | swap 10 |

- "never" means the preview still did not show the redone state 15 s later; main medians count only the reps that landed. The move edit is negative because the element follows the pointer during the drag, before release.
- On main, "swap" rows are reps where the file did not return to the loaded build. Several of those swaps put in the stale build, which is why redo shows "never" while its path says swap.
- Two more branch runs on busier boxes: load 8 to 33, 30 of 30 undos and redos by swap, none missed, files correct every time, undo medians 210 ms (move), 588 ms (text), 300 ms (colour), worst 2.6 s; and at the final head, load 25 to 36, again 30 of 30 by swap, none missed, files correct, undo medians 566 / 716 / 878 ms, worst 3.4 s.
- Undo still waits on the history round trip that a normal edit skips: two file reads and the history step, then the rebuilt preview download, then the swap. On a quiet box that is 5 to 25 ms for the step and 45 to 200 ms for the download.

## Before

Main: drag the badge, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Shift+Z. The yellow box is a timer since the last key. Undo does not reach the preview within 2.3 s; redo then shows the undone state for about a second.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82857852-476c-4b0a-907d-d251df6192bd

## After

This branch, same steps, recorded on a busy box (load about 30, so slower than the table's medians): undo lands after about 1.3 s and redo in under 0.5 s, both swapped in place with no reload.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5436afaa-fba5-4790-a9e3-db1b75fa368d

title: fix(media-use): honour HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON in the audio engine (#4614)
body:
resolvePythonCommand() only probed python3/python on PATH, so on PEP 668 systems set up with a venv via HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON (the documented setup), doctor reported MusicGen installed while BGM was silently skipped.

Check HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON first, as the CLI's findPython() does, and fall through to the PATH probe when the override doesn't run.

## What

The audio engine's Python resolver (`skills/media-use/audio/scripts/lib/python.mjs`) now honours `HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON` before probing PATH, and only accepts an interpreter whose `--version` reports Python 3.

## Why

With the documented venv setup, `doctor` passed while background music silently disabled itself, because the audio engine never looked at the override the CLI uses.

## Related work

Fixes #4614

## How

One override check ahead of the existing PATH probe, matching the CLI's `findPython()`; the probe now requires `Python 3` in the version output, matching `validatePythonOverride()`, so a Python 2 `python` is rejected. The skills manifest hash is regenerated.

## Size

Small on purpose: a single resolver gains one override branch and a stricter probe, plus its tests and the regenerated manifest hash. Nothing else needed to change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`python.test.mjs`: override wins, broken override falls through, Python 2 rejected)
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: feat(studio): the timeline publishes where it draws 0 s, so a host can map a click to a time
body:
## What

The timeline's scroll viewport carries `data-timeline-content-origin`: how far from the scroll content's left edge the timeline draws 0 s, in px. It is 80 while the label column is off and 264 while it is on, and it updates live when the column opens or closes.

## Why

An app that embeds the timeline and maps a pointer on the ruler to a time (its own click handling, hover previews, overlays) needs the same origin the timeline draws with. Nothing exposed it, so a host had to copy the 80 px it measured once. That breaks as soon as the label column opens: keyframed clips and audio groups widen the origin to 264 px, and it opens after mount, once keyframe data loads. A host still using 80 then reads a click on the 00:03 tick as about 4.9 s.

The timeline's own ruler press was already right in every case (keyframes shown or hidden, loaded before or after mount). The new test pins that too.

## How

`buildTimelineMeta` adds the attribute to the viewport props from the same `contentOrigin` the ruler, lanes and playhead use, so there is still one owner.

## Before

A host maps a click on the 00:03 tick with the label column open. Nothing is published, so it assumes 80 and reads 4.89 s.

![Before: the host reads the 00:03 tick as 4.89 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b45d3c2e-5ed9-4d2c-b757-b0b03a0ca1d1)

## After

The host reads `data-timeline-content-origin` (264) and reads the same click as 3.00 s.

![After: the host reads the 00:03 tick as 3.00 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49597d8e-18f5-46c3-ab3d-ca50473c5e1c)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added (`Timeline.rulerSeek.test.tsx`, a whole mounted timeline): with keyframes shown or hidden, and loaded before or after mount, the attribute equals the origin the ruler draws 0 s at (264), and a press on a tick seeks to that tick's time. With no clip needing the label column it is 80. Removing the attribute fails all five cases.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the host overlay above on Studio's dev server with a fixture built for it.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): with keyframes hidden, a keyframed clip no longer opens the track-name column
body:
## What

With `showKeyframes={false}`, a keyframed clip no longer opens the timeline's 232 px track-name column. The column exists for the keyframe lanes' names, and those lanes are hidden. An audio group still opens it, since its row name needs the column.

## Why

The column moves where the timeline draws 0 s from 80 px to 264 px, shifting every clip 184 px right. A host that hides keyframes got that shift as soon as keyframe data loaded, with nothing on screen needing the space.

## Related work

Follows the `showKeyframes` prop (#4715), which kept the column when keyframes are hidden. #4724 publishes the origin so a host can follow whichever width is drawn.

## How

The label-column check reads the same keyframe data the timeline draws (empty when keyframes are hidden) instead of the store's full animation map.

## Before

A host timeline with `showKeyframes={false}` and a keyframed Title clip: the 232 px track-name column opens and 0 s sits at 264 px.

title: fix(studio): a corner drag on a small element resizes it instead of starting a crop
body:
## What

On a small element, dragging a corner dot now resizes it. Before, the crop handles sat on top of the corner dots, so the same drag cropped the element instead.

## Why

Each crop edge handle has a 32 px hit strip centred on its edge, and the crop layer paints above the selection's corner dots. The corner dots own a 16 px square on each corner. Once an edge is shorter than about 48 px on screen, its strip reaches into those corner squares and takes the press. A title about 29 x 14 px at preview scale lost almost every corner to crop. The centre "Reposition crop" handle on a small cropped element covered the corners the same way.

## Related work

Refs #4518 (a separate manual-edit bug that is already fixed on main).

## How

- The corner hit size (`RESIZE_HANDLE_HIT_PX`) now lives in `domEditOverlayGeometry.ts`, so the corner dots and the crop handles read the same number.
- Each crop edge strip is now an explicit rectangle, just outside its edge and shortened so it stops before the corner squares. An edge too short to leave any room shows no crop handle, so on a 29 x 14 px box only top and bottom crop remain. Zoom in to crop the short sides.
- The reposition handle shrinks until its box clears the corner squares, and is hidden when it cannot.
- Raising the corner dots above the crop layer was rejected: on a rotated element the chrome is its own stacking context, and the crop's centre handle would sit under the selection box.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `DomEditCropHandles.test.tsx` renders the crop handles on 29x14, 40x40, 29x14 cropped and 200x100 cropped boxes and checks that no handle's hit box overlaps a corner square. It also checks that all five handles still show on a normal cropped box.
- [x] Against main's source the new tests fail 4 of 10 ("Crop top covers a corner", "Reposition crop covers a corner"). With the fix, 10 of 10 pass. The overlay test files `DomEditCropHandles`, `DomEditSelectionChrome` and `DomEditOverlay` pass 39 of 39, and `tsc --noEmit` for studio exits 0.
- [x] Manual testing in headless Chrome on the built CLI Studio. The fixture has a 64 x 30 element, which is about 45 x 21 px on screen at Fit and about 90 x 42 px at 200%, plus a 60 x 28 element in a nested composition. At each corner-dot centre, the element under the pointer is:
  - on main: "Crop left" or "Crop right" at all four corners, at both zooms and in the nested composition;
  - with the fix: that corner's resize dot, in every case.

  Dragging the NE dot by (+20, -20) at 200%:
  - on main: the element stays 64 x 30, and the file gets a `clip-path`;
  - with the fix: the element becomes 135 x 63, and no `clip-path` is written.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main at 200%, dragging the small element's top-right corner dot does not resize it (the crop strip took the press):

![Before: corner drag on a small element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac0cddc7-0d64-4e4c-9da8-df70c2492fab)

## After

With the fix, the same drag resizes it from the corner:

![After: corner drag on a small element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7def269c-3e7d-46e0-8227-2e9713647147)

title: feat(studio): a host can say why Undo or Redo is off in its tooltip
body:
## What

A host can now tell the user why Undo or Redo is off. `TimelineHistoryButtons` (and `TimelineToolbar`'s `history` prop) take an optional `undoDisabledReason` and `redoDisabledReason`. While the button is off, its tooltip shows that reason instead of "Undo <step> (Cmd+Z)". While the button is on, the tooltip is unchanged.

## Why

A host that blocks history for a while (for example while an agent is still editing the file) greys the buttons, but the tooltip still offers "Undo Trim clip (Cmd+Z)". That reads as a broken button. The host knows the reason; Studio had no way to show it.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `HistoryButton` picks its tooltip in one place: the host's reason when the button is off and a reason was given, otherwise `historyTooltipLabel` as before.
- The Tooltip test's hover helper moved to `mountHost.testHelpers.ts` as `hoverTooltipWrapper`, so the history test reuses it instead of copying it. Hover reaches the wrapper span, never a disabled button.

title: feat(studio): a host can turn off body drags and keep the resize, rotate and crop handles
body:
## What

A host that takes the canvas input (`canvasInput="host"`) can now turn off moving an element by dragging its body, and keep every handle. `DomEditOverlay` and `ConnectedDomEditOverlay` take `allowBodyDrag` (default `true`). With `canvasInput="host"` and `allowBodyDrag={false}`:

- A press on a selection's body, or on a group selection's box, is left untouched for the host: Studio starts no drag, does not prevent the default or stop the event, takes no pointer capture and sets no cursor. The host decides what that press does, for example drawing its own move control.
- The corner handles still resize, the rotate handle still rotates, and the crop handles still crop.
- A second press that opens text editing still works, and arrow-key nudges still move the selection. That is the host's decision, and this PR leaves it as is.

## Why

A host that moves elements through its own control needs Studio to stop moving them on a body drag and to hand it the press, but keep the handles. Until now the only switch was `allowCanvasMovement`, which turns off the handles along with the drag.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `DomEditSelectionChrome` and `DomEditGroupChrome` read `allowBodyDrag`. When it is off, the box's pointerdown returns right after the text-edit press check, and the box's cursor is left unset.
- The switch only applies with `canvasInput="host"`. In Studio's own overlay mode there is no host to take the press: the overlay's own press handling would count it twice (a single click opening text editing) and a still click on a group would deselect it. So in overlay mode the flag is ignored, and the prop's doc says so.
- Studio itself never turns it off, so nothing changes in Studio. The trailing click after such a press is the host's to handle; a host that captures the pointer for its own control swallows it there.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `DomEditSelectionChrome.test.tsx`:
  - With body drag off, a body press reaches a parent listener with `defaultPrevented` false and no pointer capture. No drag or blocked-move notice starts, and no cursor is set.
  - A group body press behaves the same way.
  - The corner handle still starts a resize, and the rotate handle a rotation.
  - With the default, the body still drags with the move cursor.
  - `ConnectedDomEditOverlay` passes the prop through.
  - On the real `DomEditOverlay` (`DomEditOverlay.test.ts`), with the switch off an overlay-mode canvas still starts a body drag and a host-mode canvas does not. The overlay case fails on the previous head.
- [x] Against main's source, the two new press tests fail. With the change: `DomEditSelectionChrome`, `ConnectedDomEditOverlay`, `DomEditOverlay` and `groupDropKeepsSelection` pass 40 of 40, and studio `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- [x] Manual testing in headless Chrome on the built CLI Studio, 300 x 200 box. Studio never turns the switch off itself, so the After build carries a one-line capture-only change that makes the overlay refuse body drags the way a host does; it is not part of this PR.
  - Main, body drag of (+60, +40) screen px: the box moves to (253, 276) and the file gets a `gsap.set`.
  - Body drag refused, same drag: the box stays at (80, 160), and nothing is written to the file.
  - Body drag refused, corner handle drag: the box still resizes, to 502 x 334.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): an element placed by a stylesheet translate stays put after a move or resize
body:
## What

An element placed with a `translate` in a stylesheet no longer jumps when you move or resize it. Before, the preview showed it shifted a second time by that translate as soon as the drag ended, for example 200 px up for `translate: 0 -200px`. The saved file was already right: reloading the preview put it back where it was dropped.

## Why

While you drag, Studio sets an inline `translate: none` on the element and moves it through GSAP. GSAP folds any CSS translate it finds into its own transform. When the drag ends, Studio removed that inline `translate: none` to start the next gesture clean. For a translate written inline, the drag had already replaced it, so nothing came back. For a translate from a stylesheet, removing the mask let the stylesheet value apply again on top of GSAP's transform, which already contains it.

## Related work

Stacked on #4740 (this PR's base is that branch), so it cannot land first. After a move, this PR keeps GSAP's `translate: none` mask on the element, which is what a fresh load of the saved file shows. On main, undo's soft reload keeps that mask, so without #4740 an undo right after a move would leave the element offset by its stylesheet translate. #4740 makes the soft reload restore the file's own `translate`. The two together were walked on the stylesheet-translate fixture: move, undo, redo, undo and reload each match a fresh load.

This PR also covers elements still on the old `--hf-studio-offset` channel: its clean-up runs first, then the mask is settled.

## How

`endManualOffsetDragMembers` now removes the drag's `translate: none` only when nothing sits under it. If the computed translate without the mask is a real value from a stylesheet, the mask stays. That is also what GSAP leaves on the element when the saved file loads. Elements with no stylesheet translate keep the old clean-up, so the earlier fix for elements flying off after a reload still applies.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`:
  - After a committed GSAP drag on an element with `#title { translate: 0 -200px }` in a stylesheet, the element keeps `translate: none`.
  - With no stylesheet translate, the mask is removed as before.
  - The same holds for an element still on the old `--hf-studio-offset` channel.
  - When GSAP does not own the position, the element keeps its offset-channel translate, unmasked.
- [x] Against main's `manualOffsetDrag.ts` the first test fails (`expected '' to be 'none'`). With the fix, 25 of 25 pass across `manualOffsetDrag`, `groupDropKeepsSelection` and `anchoredResizeCommitFeedsOffset`, and studio `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- [x] Manual testing in headless Chrome, on the built CLI Studio with a fixture whose title has `translate: 0 -200px` in its stylesheet and an opacity tween, at the 3 s playhead:
  - Corner resize: the title's top was 299 before the drag. On main it landed at 21.5 on screen and 221.5 after a reload. With the fix it lands at 221.5 on screen and 221.5 after a reload.
  - Body move of (+40, +30) screen px: on main the title landed at 186 on screen and 386 after a reload. With the fix it lands at 386 on screen and 386 after a reload.
  - Together with #4740, on the stylesheet, inline and no-tween translate fixtures: move, undo, redo, undo and reload each match a fresh load (386, 299, 386, 299, 299). Two moves, and a move then resize, also match a reload.
- Out of scope, and already on main: in a composition that does not load GSAP, the first drag of a stylesheet-translated element still jumps by that translate. That is a separate follow-up.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Corner resize on main: the title jumps up to the top of the frame as soon as the drag ends.

![Before: resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/773095b1-5880-4b32-b504-1e4069a833a7)

Moving it on main: the title lands 200 px above where it was dropped.

![Before: move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d239e93f-a464-4cf3-97ce-8de43e268cc2)

## After

Corner resize with the fix: the title stays where it was resized.

![After: resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b71d90e-f234-4559-8a48-efee0783aa60)

Moving it with the fix: the title stays where it was dropped.

![After: move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/122b8842-828c-423b-a1b8-09d380c79491)

title: Distributed render plays a `data-playback-rate` clip's picture at 1× (audio keeps the rate)
body:
### Describe the bug

A `<video data-playback-rate="1.5">` renders correctly with `hyperframes render`, but through the distributed primitives (`planV2` → `renderChunkV2` → `assembleV2`, which the Lambda and Cloud Run adapters use) its picture plays at 1×. The mixed audio still follows 1.5×, so picture and sound drift apart. A faster clip shows only part of its footage; a slower one plays at 1× and then holds its last frame.

`parsePlanVideosJson` in `packages/producer/src/services/distributed/shared.ts` rebuilds each video from a fixed field list that has no `playbackRate`, so `meta/videos.json` drops it and each chunk's frame lookup falls back to rate 1. Audio is mixed on the planner from the full element list, so it keeps the rate. The parser was added in #2839; `playbackRate` joined `VideoElement` later and the list was not updated.

### Minimal reproduction

https://github.com/ArcadeHQ/hyperframes-repros/tree/patch/distributed-playback-rate

### Steps to reproduce

```bash
git clone -b patch/distributed-playback-rate https://github.com/ArcadeHQ/hyperframes-repros
cd hyperframes-repros
npm install
npx hyperframes@0.8.92 check                                   # clean
npx hyperframes@0.8.92 render -o out/render.mp4 --quality draft
node distributed-render.mjs out/distributed.mp4
./sample.sh out/render.mp4
./sample.sh out/distributed.mp4
```

The clip shows one colour per source second (0 red, 1 orange, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 cyan, 5 blue, …) and plays at 1.5×.

### Expected behavior

Both renders show source 2.25 s (yellow) at t = 1.5 s and source 5.25 s (blue) at t = 3.5 s.

### Actual behavior

| Renderer | t = 1.5 s | t = 3.5 s |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `hyperframes render` | `#fdfe01` yellow | `#0100ff` blue |
| distributed | `#ff8000` orange (source 1.5 s) | `#00ff01` green (source 3.5 s) |

### Environment

```shell
hyperframes doctor

  ✓ Version          0.8.92 (latest)
  ✓ Node.js          v24.21.0 (darwin arm64)
  ✓ CPU              10 cores · Apple M1 Pro @ 2400MHz
  ✓ Memory           16.0 GB total · 3.7 GB available
  ✓ Disk             267.3 GB free
  ✓ Archive extractor unzip
  ✓ Settings lock    Not locked
  ✓ Environment      non-TTY
  ✓ whisper-cpp      /opt/homebrew/bin/whisper-cli
  ✗ TTS (Kokoro)     Not installed (optional — local voice fallback)
  ✗ BGM (MusicGen)   Not installed (optional — local music fallback)
  ✓ onnxruntime-node Not installed (installs on first use)
  ✓ @google/genai    Not installed (installs on first use)
  ✓ FFmpeg           ffmpeg 9.0.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg
  ✓ FFprobe          ffprobe 9.0.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe
  ✓ Chrome           cache: chrome-headless-shell-mac-arm64 154.0.8037.57
  ✗ Docker           Not found
  ✗ Docker running   Not running
```

Still present on `main` at 5a77dbcea.

### Additional context

Keeping `playbackRate` in the parser (a finite number or a rate lane) makes the distributed render match: yellow and blue. I have a PR ready with that change and a test.

title: fix(producer): keep clip playback rate in distributed video metadata
body:
## What

The distributed video metadata keeps each clip's `playbackRate`, so chunk workers show a sped-up or slowed-down clip's picture at its authored rate.

## Why

`parsePlanVideosJson` rebuilt each video from a fixed field list without `playbackRate`. Chunk workers then indexed extracted frames at rate 1, while the planner mixed audio at the authored rate. A 1.5× clip showed its picture at 1× in `planV2` / `renderChunkV2` / `assembleV2` output. `hyperframes render` was correct.

## Related work

Fixes #4735

## How

`readRateSpec` accepts a finite number or a rate lane (an object with a `points` array), the two shapes of `RateSpec`. An absent rate stays absent, so plans written before this change still read as rate 1.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `videoMetadata.test.ts` round-trips 1.5×, 0.5× and a rate lane through JSON and checks the chunk-side frame index; malformed rates are rejected. The new tests fail without the fix.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the repro in #4735 renders yellow / blue through the distributed path with this change, orange / green without it.

title: fix(studio): resizing a faded or moving element writes a plain size, not keyframes
body:
## What

**Behaviour change:** resizing an element on the canvas now writes a plain size, unless the element's size is already animated. Before, resizing any element that had a tween of any kind (a fade, a slide) wrote the new size as keyframes into a new tween spanning that tween's time. Now:

- **Its size is not animated** (for example, a title with only an opacity fade): the resize writes one plain size, a `set` at 0 s, so the element has the new size for the whole film.
- **Its size is already animated:** unchanged, the resize still keyframes the size at the playhead.

This matches how moving and rotating already work. They only keyframe position or rotation when that same property is already animated, and otherwise write a plain value.

## Why

A resize on a title that only fades wrote keyframes such as `0%: old size, 30%: new size, 100%: old size`, or three stops of the new size, depending on the path. On screen the title grew from 0 s to the playhead and shrank back, or looked right in the editor but not after a reload. Nobody resizing a fading title expects the size to become an animation. Move and rotate already avoided this; resize was the odd one out.

## Related work

None.

## How

In `tryGsapResizeIntercept`, the route that keyframes the size into an existing tween now only considers tweens that already write `width` or `height` (`animationWritesAnyProperty` with the resize properties, the same check the resize preflight uses). Every other element falls through to the plain size `set`, which was already the path for elements without tweens.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test in `gsapResizeIntercept.test.ts`: a title whose only tween is a 10 s opacity fade, resized to 424 x 237, produces no keyframe mutation and one `add` of `set` at 0 with `{ width: 424, height: 237 }`.
- [x] On main's `gsapResizeIntercept.ts` that test fails. Main sends `add-with-keyframes` with `0%` and `100%` stops for the size. With the fix, the resize test files pass 63 of 63: `gsapResizeIntercept`, `gsapResizeMixedTween`, `gsapResizeSweep`, `gsapResizeGeometrySweep`, `gsapResizeDropPoint`, `useGsapAwareEditing` and `newTweenTarget`. Studio `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- [x] Manual testing in headless Chrome on the built CLI Studio. The fixture's box is 700 x 380 and its only tween is an opacity tween. It was resized from its corner to 908 x 493, the preview was reloaded, and the box was read at 0.5 s, 2 s and 3.5 s:
  - Main writes `keyframes: { "0%": 700x380, "12.5%": 908x493, "100%": 700x380 }`. After the reload the box measures 908, then 832, then 708 px wide: it shrinks back.
  - With the fix, the file gets `tl.set("#large", { width: 908, height: 493 }, 0)`. The box stays 908 x 493 at all three times, before and after the reload.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main, after resizing a box that only fades and reloading, it has shrunk back toward its old size at 3.5 s:

![Before: reloaded at 3.5 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78211c2f-2416-4653-9735-596aef061f3b)

## After

With the fix, the reloaded box keeps the size it was given:

![After: reloaded at 3.5 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1dac473d-d182-48fd-bf03-0cf4045ee007)

title: fix(studio): selecting words while editing text keeps the edit open
body:
## What

While editing text in place on the Studio canvas, dragging across words or clicking inside the text now keeps the edit open: the drag selects the characters, a click moves the caret, and Shift+Arrow extends the selection. A click outside the text still commits and ends the edit.

## Why

Today any press inside text that is being edited ends the edit. The text loses focus, nothing is selected, and a following Shift+Arrow nudges the element instead of extending a selection. It happens in the root composition and in nested ones.

The canvas overlay already steps aside while text is edited (it switches itself to `pointer-events: none` so presses reach the caret in the preview). But since the preview overlays were wrapped in a shared provider, that provider's full-size wrapper box sits above the preview and takes pointer events itself. Presses land on that box instead of the text, focus moves out of the preview, and the edit commits on blur.

Repro on main: open a project, double-press a text element so the caret shows, then drag across the first word. The edit closes and nothing is selected.

## Related work

Refs the Studio manual-editing reliability work. No overlapping PRs.

## How

- `PreviewOverlayProvider`'s wrapper is a positioning box only, so it is now `pointer-events-none`. It is still measured for the composition rect as before.
- Pointer events are inherited, so every direct child that needs presses now asks for them explicitly: the snap toolbar and the caption-mode chips (mode indicator, sync error, "Edit captions"). The canvas overlay and the caption overlay already set their own pointer events; the guides, grid, topology lens, motion path and gesture trail are already `pointer-events-none`.
- Host apps that compose the provider over their own iframe get the same benefit: the wrapper no longer blocks their preview.

### Known effects

- **Zooming while editing text:** with a text edit open, Ctrl+wheel or pinch over the preview no longer zooms Studio's preview. The wheel now reaches the preview frame, and Studio's zoom listens only on its own document. Zoom works as before whenever no text is being edited. This will be fixed separately by also listening inside the preview frame.
- **Hosts that mount `PreviewOverlayProvider` with their own children:** a child that takes clicks must now set `pointer-events-auto` itself, as Studio's own overlay children do.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `PreviewOverlayProvider.test.tsx` asserts the wrapper lets presses through and the snap toolbar opts back in. Fails on main's source, passes with the fix; removing the toolbar's opt-in also turns it red.
- [x] Manual testing performed: headless Chrome walk on main and on this branch (double-press, drag-select, click inside, Shift+Arrow x2, type, click outside), root text and nested text:
  - main: the drag ends the edit (not editable, focus on body, empty selection); typing goes nowhere.
  - branch: drag selects "Edit t" / "Ne", click inside keeps editing, Shift+Arrow selects two characters, typed " ok" lands, click outside commits and the file is saved with the new text.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main, while editing the headline in place, a drag across "Edit t" ends the edit and selects nothing:

![Before: drag-select while editing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dea828e8-dfdf-45f4-925e-fd25d6d7ffbf)

## After

With the fix, the same drag selects "Edit t" and the edit stays open, with the text toolbar showing:

![After: drag-select while editing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01cc0d21-dda2-4c40-b237-cbbdfb0a832c)

title: feat(studio): let a host hide timeline history, place the shortcuts button and set track padding
body:
## What

Three additive host props for apps that embed Studio. Every default keeps today's behaviour.

- `TimelineToolbar` gets `showHistory?: boolean` (default `true`). `false` renders no Undo and no Redo button; keyboard undo is untouched.
- `ShortcutsButton` is exported from the package index: the shortcuts button and panel that `PlayerControls` renders today, wired to the player store, so a host can place it in its own toolbar with `<ShortcutsButton sections={...} />`. `PlayerControls` now renders this same component, so there is one owner. `onSeek` is optional and defaults to the store's `requestSeek`.
- `Timeline` gets `trackPadding?: { top?: number; bottom?: number }` (px), the empty space above the first track and below the last. Defaults stay `TRACKS_TOP_PAD` (50) and `TRACKS_BOTTOM_PAD` (1.5 track heights). `TRACK_H` and the `TimelineTrackPadding` type are exported so a host can pass one track height without copying a constant.

## Why

A host app that embeds Studio wants a compact timeline: no Undo/Redo buttons in the timeline toolbar (keyboard undo stays), the shortcuts button in its own toolbar row, no band above the first track, and exactly one empty track-height below the last one (where a drag creates a new track). Today none of that is possible without CSS reaching into Studio internals, and CSS cannot move the pads, because drops and hit-tests compute rows from the pad constants.

## Related work

Follows the same host-prop pattern as `showKeyframes` (#4680) and the host-mountable toolbar (#4629).

## How

- The padding lives in one place: `TimelineRowGeometry` now carries `padding`, set by `createTimelineRowGeometry(keys, heights, padding?)`. `getRowTop`, `getRowFromY` and `canvasHeight` read it, so every reader that already goes through the geometry follows it: lanes, marquee, keyboard paging, focus scroll, viewport anchoring.
- The helpers that take a `rowHeights` array (`getTimelineRowTop`, `getTimelineRowFromY`, `resolveTimelineAssetDrop`, `getTimelineCanvasHeight`) already resolve an array back to the geometry that produced it through `getTimelineRowGeometry`'s cache. The drag preview and the asset drop pass `rowGeometryRef.current.rowHeights`, so they pick up the host's pads without a signature change. `getTimelineRowTop` now returns `geometry.getRowTop(row)` directly instead of re-adding the constant.
- The Timeline prop goes into `useTimelineTrackLayout` as two numbers (so an inline object from the host does not rebuild the geometry every render); the display geometry used while dragging inherits the base geometry's padding.
- The two remaining constant readers now read the geometry: `TimelineCanvas`'s flow spacers and drop, ghost, gap and insert-line tops, and the row virtualizer's `scrollMargin`. After this change `TRACKS_TOP_PAD` and `TRACKS_BOTTOM_PAD` have one reader each: the default in `createTimelineRowGeometry`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New tests, each seen failing with its prop's effect removed:

- `timelineLayout.test.ts` "host track padding": with `{ top: 0, bottom: TRACK_H }`, a pointer 10px into row 1 maps to row 1 for the drag path (`getRowFromY`, `getTimelineRowFromY`) and the drop path (`resolveTimelineAssetDrop`), a drop in the bottom pad opens a new track, and the canvas is ruler + rows + one track. Any reader left on the constant maps that pointer to row 0.
- `Timeline.trackPadding.test.tsx`: mounting `<Timeline trackPadding>` moves the first row's top and resizes the canvas; the default mount keeps Studio's numbers.
- `useTimelineVirtualRows.test.tsx`: the virtualizer's mounted range follows the geometry's own top pad.
- `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`: two history buttons by default, none with `showHistory={false}`.
- `timelineLayout.test.ts` also: a negative pad clamps to 0 and a non-finite pad falls back to the default, so a bad host value cannot put row 0 under the ruler or make the canvas height `NaN`.
- `Timeline.trackPadding.test.tsx` also mounts three tracks with `{ top: 0, bottom: TRACK_H }` and drives a real asset drag-over and drop (gap strip, drop preview, insert line, and the drop's track) and a real clip drag (drop placeholder, then a new-track insert line in the bottom pad).
- `ShortcutsPanel.test.tsx`: `<ShortcutsButton>` renders standalone, lists the host's sections, shows the store's in-point, and jump-to-frame seeks through the store.

## Before

Studio on `main` with a small synthetic fixture (three clips), 1440x900, headless Chrome: Undo and Redo sit at the left of the timeline toolbar, a band sits between the ruler and the first track, and 1.5 track heights of empty lane sit below the last one.

![Before: Studio defaults, Undo and Redo in the timeline toolbar, a band above the first track, 1.5 tracks below the last](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b30c32f8-dc7b-4d46-ae32-a4f45ff2a494)

## After

The same fixture on this branch, with Studio's own shell patched locally (not committed) to act as a host: `showHistory={false}` on `TimelineToolbar`, `<ShortcutsButton />` at the end of the toolbar row, and `trackPadding={{ top: 0, bottom: TRACK_H }}` on `Timeline`. No Undo or Redo, the first track starts right under the ruler, and exactly one track height of drop room sits below the last track. Studio's own app keeps the defaults. The clip thumbnails differ between the two shots only because of how far thumbnail loading had got.

![After: a host passes showHistory={false}, renders ShortcutsButton in its toolbar row, and trackPadding top 0, bottom one track](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f3b49d02-3148-4c26-86c2-3ba00c5700d6)

Not exercised: the non-virtualized rollback path (`VITE_STUDIO_TIMELINE_ROW_VIRTUALIZATION_ENABLED=0`), where `TimelineCanvas`'s flow spacers read the pads, has no mounted test.
The drag and drop helpers still find the host pads through the cache keyed on the geometry's own `rowHeights` array; the mounted drag and drop tests pin today's callers, but a host calling the exported `resolveTimelineAssetDrop` or `getTimelineCanvasHeight` with its own array gets Studio's default pads.

title: fix(studio): undo puts a resized, rotated or moved element back on screen
body:
## What

Undo and redo in Studio now leave the preview looking the way the reverted file looks when opened fresh:

- Undoing a resize puts the element back at its old size, and it stays there after a seek.
- Undoing a move, rotate or resize on an element that has an inline `transform: rotate(...)` keeps that rotation. Redo keeps it too.
- Undoing a move on an element whose stylesheet sets `translate` no longer leaves it 200 px off after undo, redo, undo.

## Why

When the composition has a GSAP script, Studio writes a resize or move into that script (`gsap.set` / `tl.set`). Undo then re-runs the old script in place instead of remounting the preview. Before this change, three kinds of state that only existed in the live preview survived that re-run:

1. **Size marks.** During the drag, the resize puts `data-hf-studio-box-size` and `--hf-studio-width/height` on the live element. The file never gets them, so the soft undo, which only syncs elements whose attributes changed in the file, never removed them. The seek reapply then put the new size back on every seek.
2. **Authored inline transform.** Before re-running the script, the soft reload wiped GSAP's inline `transform` on every element GSAP had touched. That also deleted an authored `transform: rotate(20deg)`, and the reverted script never sets it again.
3. **GSAP's `translate: none` mask.** When GSAP folds a stylesheet `translate` into its own transform, it writes an inline `translate: none`. The soft reload restored the live inline style with that mask still in it, so the stylesheet translate stayed hidden.

## Related work

Refs #4734. That PR keeps the `translate: none` mask after a committed drag on purpose. Its reviewer found that a single move followed by undo then left the title off by 200 px. This PR fixes that undo case: the mask goes back to what the file says, and GSAP puts it back itself if the script still moves the element.

## How

- `applyUndoRestoreToPreview` is the one function every soft undo and redo goes through. When the restore re-runs a changed GSAP script, it now:
  - syncs every live element whose Studio edit marks differ from the restored file back to the restored markup;
  - passes the restored file to `applySoftReload` as `authoredHtml`, so it knows what the file authors.
- In `applySoftReload`, after GSAP's props are cleared, each element's `transform` goes back to the authored value instead of being deleted. When the source file is known, `translate`, `rotate` and `scale` go back to their authored values too. With no authored source, `transform` is still cleared as before.
- Before re-running, the old timeline is cleared as well as killed. `kill()` only detaches a GSAP timeline, and the runtime still seeks it until the rebind swaps it, so its tweens repainted a stale transform. On an element with a Studio offset and a GSAP `x` tween, every undo pushed it further right.
- An SVG element's inline style now counts as an authored source too, for both the transform and the opacity restore.
- The list of edit marks is exported from `manualEditsSeekReapply.ts`, which already owns it, so the undo and the seek reapply read the same list.
- Known limits, the same on main: an SVG `transform` attribute is still dropped on a soft reload. On the first motionPath save of a session, which waits for the plugin to load, the root timeline is empty until the load finishes.
- Out of scope: when the script is unchanged, the undo still syncs only elements whose attributes changed in the file. In that case the marks still match what the script sets.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: three cases in `gsapUndoRestore.test.ts` (size marks, authored rotation, translate mask). All three fail on main and pass with the fix. Removing any one part of the fix turns its own test red.
- [x] Three tests in `gsapSoftReload.test.ts`: the save path restores the file's translate, rotate and scale; an SVG child keeps its inline transform; the finalize seek cannot paint the killed timeline. Each fails with its part of the fix removed.
- [x] `gsapSoftReload.test.ts` still passes, and the studio typecheck is clean.
- [x] Manual testing in headless Chrome, Before on main and After on this branch, on a repo-style fixture. Each walk does the gesture, then undo, a seek, and redo:
  - Resize a plain box. Before: undo leaves it at 502x334, still after a seek. After: back to 300x200.
  - Move, rotate or resize a box with inline `rotate(20deg)`. Before: undo shows it unrotated. After: undo gives back the original rotated box exactly, and redo matches the post-edit state.
  - Stylesheet `translate: 0 -200px` title, move then undo, redo, undo. Before: top 499. After: top 299, the same as a fresh load of the file.
  - A box with a Studio offset and a GSAP `x` tween, another element moved, then undo, redo, undo, redo. Before: left 601, 626, 639, 647 against a fresh load's 557.5. After: 557.5 at every step.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main, right after "Undid: Resize layer", the resized box stays at its new size on screen, though the file is back to 300 x 200:

![Before: undo of a resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe34546d-7795-455d-9586-190534cdacd1)

On main, undoing a resize of the element with an authored `rotate(20deg)` shows it unrotated and still enlarged:

![Before: undo on a rotated element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05df5c96-4b22-4d70-8762-72bb48370ec3)

## After

With the fix, the same undo puts the box back to 300 x 200:

![After: undo of a resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fb749439-7d35-4c80-8f05-1d61b8e57c14)

And the rotated element comes back at its size and its 20 degree rotation:

![After: undo on a rotated element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d824122-f4ec-47ae-becc-84b67ceb82d6)

title: feat(studio): draw the empty lane below the last track as a drop target and tighten the top gap
body:
## What

Studio's timeline gets a ghost lane and a tighter top gap. These are the new defaults, so Studio and every host that embeds it get them.

- The empty space below the last track is exactly one track tall (`TRACKS_BOTTOM_PAD = TRACK_H`, was 1.5 tracks). It draws as a dashed outline with a quiet "Drop media here" hint, and lights up while a clip or a file is dragged over it. A drop there creates a new bottom track, exactly as before.
- The gap between the ruler and the first track goes from 50px to 8px (`TRACKS_TOP_PAD = 8`), just enough that the first clip does not sit under the ruler.

## Why

The space above the first track had no function, and the space below the last track was a drop zone nobody could see. One visible lane says where a new track goes, and the tighter top shows more tracks in the same height.

## Related work

Builds on #4739 (host `trackPadding`, merged). The lane reads the row geometry, so it follows a host's pads:

- Its top is the row geometry's top for the row past the last committed track, so it sits wherever the host's top pad puts the rows.
- It is drawn only when the geometry's bottom pad holds a whole track. A host passing `trackPadding.bottom: 0` (or anything under one track) gets no lane. A lane is one track tall; a thinner band would not fit its hint and would look like a broken track, and with `bottom: 0` there is no room below the last row to draw it at all.

## How

- Two constants in `timelineLayout.ts`. Every row top, pointer-to-row mapping and canvas height already derives from them through the row geometry, so drag, drop, marquee and virtualized rows follow.
- `TimelineCanvas` draws the lane in the bottom pad, inset like a clip. It is `pointer-events-none`, so drops still land on the viewport's existing handlers, and `aria-hidden` like its sibling spacers (it is a pointer-only target).
- Its row is the one after the last committed track in the displayed order. Dragging the bottom track's clip down adds a preview row for the new track; that preview row is the lane, so the lit lane stays under the pointer instead of jumping one row below it. A drag that opens a new top track adds no preview row, so the lane stays unlit and in place.
- It lights up when the drop would open a new bottom track: an asset drag-over whose preview targets a track not yet in the order, or a clip drag whose insert row is past the last track.
- The "Drop media here" hint shows only when the host passes `onFileDrop` or `onAssetDrop`, the same way the empty timeline gates its drop copy. Without one, the dashed lane stays (it is still where a dragged clip opens a new track) but makes no promise about media.
- Styling reuses the empty-timeline drop zone's classes: `border-dashed rounded-lg border-neutral-700/50 text-neutral-500` at rest, and `border-studio-accent/60 bg-studio-accent/6 text-studio-accent` while dragged over. No new colours.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `Timeline.ghostLane.test.tsx` mounts three tracks:
  - the lane renders one row past the last, with its hint, `aria-hidden`;
  - no hint without a drop handler, and no lane with `trackPadding.bottom: 0`;
  - a real asset drag-over lights it (and does not over a track row), and a drop on it opens track 3;
  - a real clip drag into it lights it, for the first track's clip and for the last track's clip. The last-track case also pins the lane's top to the pointer's row. With the lane counted from the rows on screen it fails: `expected '227px' to be '179px'`.
- `timelineLayout.test.ts` "default track pads" pins row 0 at ruler + 8 and one track below the last. A drop anywhere in the bottom lane, from its top edge to the canvas's last pixel, opens a new track for both an asset drop and a clip drag's insert row.
- Tests that pinned the old numbers now use the new ones or derive from the constants.
- 23 timeline test files pass, one file per command, plus Studio typecheck, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files.

Notes, no code change here:
- #4739's mounted padding test (`Timeline.trackPadding.test.tsx`) uses host pads close to the new 8px default, so a reader that ignored the host pad would now land in the same row as a correct one. It still passes; picking host pads far from the default would make it discriminate again.
- The "drop above the first track to open a new top track" zone shrinks with the top gap, from 50px of lane plus the ruler to 8px plus the ruler. Dropping over the ruler still opens a top track.

## Before

Studio on `main`, synthetic three-clip fixture, 1440x900, headless Chrome. A 50px band sits above the first track and 1.5 track heights of unmarked lane sit below the last one.

![Before: 50px band above the first track, an invisible 1.5-track drop zone below the last](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dffbdd89-d0e1-4e6e-9c5a-74be324609d3)

With a file dragged below the last track, only the clip-sized drop slot shows.

![Before, file dragged below the last track: only the clip-sized drop slot shows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/066d2775-66bc-4860-a18e-902c7d5c4ce6)

## After

This branch rebased on `main`, Studio's own app with no host changes, a synthetic three-clip fixture, 1440x900, headless Chrome. The first track sits 8px under the ruler, and one track of ghost lane with a "Drop media here" hint sits below the last.

![After: 8px under the ruler, and a one-track ghost lane with a Drop media here hint](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e2c9ee4-f7cf-4874-a0a6-f801d4433469)

With a file dragged over the lane, it lights up in the accent colour (the drop slot still shows where the clip lands). The white dot marks the pointer; headless screenshots carry no cursor.

![After, file dragged over the ghost lane: the lane lights up in the accent colour](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c45ec4d0-3cda-48a3-bc5b-11c5efe66bde)

Dragging the bottom track's clip down into the lane: the lit lane stays under the pointer (white dot) and the dragged clip, labelled as the new track. The track the clip left shows empty until the drop.

![After, bottom clip dragged into the lane: the lit lane sits under the pointer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/43187440-5bae-47c0-a7b3-36e93ca05938)

title: fix(studio): a timeline scrubs when its host omits sessionEpoch
body:
## What

`<Timeline>` now follows the player store's `timelineSessionEpoch` when a host does not pass the `sessionEpoch` prop. An explicitly passed prop still wins.

## Why

The prop defaulted to `0`. Pointer gestures (ruler scrub, playhead drag, range selection) refuse a press whose epoch differs from the store's session (`canStartPointerGesture` in `useTimelineRangeSelection.ts`). Once `beginTimelineSession` advanced the store to epoch 1+, a host that renders `<Timeline>` directly and omits the prop had every press silently dropped: clicking the ruler did nothing. Studio's own `TimelinePane` passes the store's epoch, so Studio itself was unaffected.

Repro before this change: call `usePlayerStore.getState().beginTimelineSession("any-project")`, render `<Timeline onSeek={fn} />` with no `sessionEpoch`, press the ruler: `fn` is never called.

## Related work

None.

## How

One change in `useTimelineProviderState`, the single place the prop enters: `sessionEpoch = sessionEpochProp ?? timelineSessionEpoch` instead of a `0` default. Every downstream consumer (range selection, clip drag, drop, focus, virtualization) reads that one value, so no consumer changes.

## Test plan

- New case in `Timeline.rulerSeek.test.tsx`: begin a session, mount a Timeline without `sessionEpoch`, press the ruler, expect a seek. Fails with the old `0` default (`expected undefined to be close to 2`), passes with the fix.
- Existing Timeline, range selection, drag-drop and clip content tests pass; studio typecheck passes.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

## Before

A throwaway host page (not committed) begins a session, then renders `<Timeline onSeek={...} />` without `sessionEpoch`; a press on the ruler under 00:04 is ignored: 0 seeks, playhead stays at 0.

![Before: a host Timeline without sessionEpoch ignores a ruler press after a session began](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/54b576eb-d781-4e31-9ad2-5af1b5070e3c)

## After

Same page and press: the Timeline seeks and the playhead moves to 4 s.

![After: the same press seeks to 4 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/254bdf25-0a05-40ef-87be-455715b400b9)

title: fix(studio): resizing a cropped element keeps the same part of it in view
body:
## What

Resizing a cropped element now scales its crop with it, so the same part of the element stays in view, just larger or smaller. Before, the crop kept its pixel insets, so growing a cropped element showed more of it than was cropped (a 300 px wide element cropped to 81% showed 88% after being resized to 473 px).

This holds for every size write:

- **Resize commit** (`handleGsapAwareBoxSizeCommit`, with its CSS fallback): a corner drag, the design panel's W/H fields on an element with no animation, the agent resize tool, and a host's geometry commit.
- **Animated property commit** (`commitAnimatedProperties`): the W/H fields on an element that has any GSAP animation, and any other width/height edit made through the animated property path.

Both routes use the same pair, `prepareCropResize` then `saveCropResize`, from one module.

## Why

A crop is `clip-path: inset(...)` in pixels, measured against the element's box. Nothing on the resize path touched it, so every resize silently changed what the crop showed. Design tools treat a crop as part of the element: resizing it scales the crop too.

## Related work

Rebased onto #4745 and #4730. The crop release keeps #4745's rule that a drag ending where it started saves nothing (it compares against the press-time insets). This PR adds two things to it: the press-time insets are read from the element when you press, and the radius rides on the gesture.

## How

- **One owner for the crop: the element's own `clip-path`.** While an element is selected, the crop UI shows it uncropped so it can dim what is cut away. That used to be done by writing `clip-path: none` onto the element and keeping the real crop in component refs. Undo, redo and panel edits rewrite the element's style in place, so that held copy went stale.
  - The lift is now a `clip-path: none !important` rule keyed on the element's `data-hf-id` (or `id`), added while it is selected. The element's inline `clip-path` stays the one record of the crop, and everything reads it.
  - Deselect just removes the rule; there is nothing to restore.
  - The selection box and hover ring still show the full box while the element is lifted, as before.
- **The resize commit rescales that crop.** It scales per axis (left/right by the width ratio, top/bottom by the height ratio) and keeps the radius. It writes the result onto the element and saves it in the same undo step as the size:
  - CSS route: the `clip-path` patch rides in the same patch commit as the size.
  - GSAP route: the patch is saved after the script writes land, under the resize transaction's undo key, the same way the anchor move already is. Only then is the new size live for every caller, including the W/H fields, which apply no live draft.
  - Animated property route: the property writes are keyed to one undo step, and the crop patch is saved into that step once they land.
- **The ratio's starting box** is the element's box before Studio's resize draft first changed it, recorded by the draft writer (used by the corner drag and the agent tool). With no draft (the W/H fields), it is the box when the commit starts. The end box is measured, not requested, so a resize saved as a GSAP `scale` leaves the crop alone; it already scales with the transform.
- **During a drag**, the dimmed crop area follows the box only while a resize draft is live. So an element whose width is animated keeps its crop pixels when the playhead moves.
- **A crop drag reads the element when you press**, not the last render, so a drag right after a resize starts from the scaled crop.
- **The crop is left alone** when a GSAP tween drives `clip-path` (a percent crop already scales with the box), or when the crop was edited while the resize was still saving; that edit was drawn in the new box already. An inline `!important` crop keeps its priority.
- **Per axis, an animated size keeps its crop.** When GSAP tweens or keyframes the width, the left and right insets stay as authored, because one inline crop cannot match every time of an animated size. The same goes for height with top and bottom. The other axis still scales. An instant hold (`set`) does not count as animated. The drag preview and the save ask the same question, through the existing live-tween check (`hasNonHoldTweenForElement`), which now also takes an element and understands the `keyframes: { width: [...] }` form. The answer is taken before the write lands, because a W edit can add a width keyframe of its own.
- **The live-tween check reads every timeline.** It used to read only the first one registered. A soft reload re-adds the rebuilt composition's timeline last, so after any edit that soft-reloaded the main composition, a tween on main was missed. That affected the crop, and also the existing resize, drag and rotation preflights that share the check.

### Known limits

- If the crop's save fails after the size saved, the file keeps the new size with the old crop, while the preview puts back the old size and crop. This is the same order the anchor move already has.
- A sub-composition mounted twice: selecting one copy also shows the other copy uncropped while selected. The rule is keyed on the element's id, which the copies share. It is only visual, and nothing wrong is saved.
- A crop on an element whose size is animated is left as authored on that axis (a tweened or keyframed width keeps its left and right insets, a height its top and bottom), for the corner drag and the W/H fields alike.
- Follow-up: undo on four write routes has no test of its own yet (keyframe at the playhead, the set-props merge, the whole-tween offset and add-with-keyframes). Their code shares the keyed write that is tested, and add-with-keyframes was walked: one undo restores the file.
- An element whose inline `clip-path` is `!important` is not shown uncropped while selected, because an inline important declaration beats the lift rule. Its crop still scales.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. Each of these fails without its fix:
  - Undo while selected, then a crop drag: the drag starts from the undone crop.
  - W/H-style resize (size lands only when saved): the crop scales, under the resize's undo key.
  - A caller that applied a draft first (agent tool): the crop scales from the pre-draft box.
  - Deselect before the save lands: the preview shows the scaled crop.
  - A W field on an animated element: the crop scales, in the same undo step as the size.
  - A crop drag right after a resize, with no render in between: it starts from the scaled crop.
  - Per axis, while dragging and once saved: a height tween still lets a W edit scale the left/right insets; a width tween (percent or `{ width: [...] }` keyframes) keeps them; an instant `set` still scales.
  - The decision is made before the write lands, so a W edit that adds its own width tween still scales the crop.
  - The live-tween check finds a tween in a later timeline, as after a soft reload (the check itself, and the crop test with its tween in the second timeline).
  - The W field's real route (the hook's static set, alone and batched with another property): the size write and the crop patch share one undo key.
  - Also each of these: the lift rule (it hides the crop over the inline clip, and deselect removes it), a stylesheet crop read while lifted, the hover hug ignoring a lifted crop, the crop UI drawing the element's current crop, a failed save putting the crop back, the stage ending the draft, the kept `!important`, a crop edited during the save, and a tweened crop.
  - Also covered: the CSS route commit, a `scale` resize leaving the crop alone, and the lift never rewriting the element's clip.
- [x] Manual testing performed: headless Chrome walks on the fixture (below).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Walks: headless Chrome, edit fixture, `#medium` 300x200. "Share" is the visible width fraction.

| walk | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| Crop right edge, then corner resize to 473x316 (mid-drag / after release / deselected) | 0.8779 / 0.8779 / 0.8779, `inset(0 57.75px 0 0)` | 0.8075 / 0.8075 / 0.8075, `inset(0 91.05px 0 0)` |
| One undo after that | file back to the cropped 300x200 box | same; preview back to 300x200 at 57.75px |
| Undo, redo, undo while still selected, then deselect, 10px crop drag, reload | not walked | crop UI 0.8075 at every step, element stays uncropped while selected; deselect shows 57.75px; drag saves `inset(0 86.63px 0 0)`; same after reload |
| W field 300 -> 600, no animation | not walked on main | `inset(0 115.5px 0 0)`, share 0.8075, in the file and the preview |
| W field 300 -> 600 on an element with an opacity tween | crop stays 57.75px, share 0.9038 (at the previous head) | `inset(0 115.5px 0 0)`, share 0.8075; one undo puts back both the width and 57.75px |
| H field 200 -> 400 on the same element, bottom crop | crop stays 57.75px, vertical share 0.8556 (at the previous head) | `inset(0 0 115.5px 0)`, vertical share 0.7113 |
| Inline `clip-path: … !important`, corner resize | not walked | saved as `inset(0px 94.6px 0px 0px) !important` |
| px `clip-path` tween, corner resize | not walked | authored crop left as it was |
| Resize, Escape in the same tick as release (`#cropped` 400x300) | not walked | preview and file both `inset(28.33px 42.45px 56.67px 70.75px)` at 566x425, share 0.8 |
| W field 450 -> 900 at t=2 on an element with a keyframed width 300 -> 600 and a 60 px crop | crop doubled to 120 px for every time, so after reload t=0 shows 0.6 instead of 0.8 (at the previous head) | crop left at 60 px; after reload t=0 0.8 and t=4 0.9 as before, t=2 now 900 px wide at 0.9333 |
| W field 300 -> 600 at t=2 on an element whose height is tweened, 60 px right crop | crop stays 60 px, share 0.9 at every time after reload (at the previous head) | `inset(0 120px 0 0)`, share 0.8 at t=0, 2 and 4 after reload |
| W field -> 600 at t=2 on an element with `keyframes: { width: [300, 600] }`, 60 px crop | crop rescaled to 80 px for every time, after reload t=0 shows 0.7333 (at the previous head) | crop stays 60 px; after reload t=0 0.8 |
| Corner drag at t=2 on the keyframed-width element | dimmed crop 0.8667 while dragging, 0.9276 after release (at the previous head) | 0.9276 while dragging and after release |
| W on a keyframed-opacity element (soft-reloads main, moving its timeline last), then W 450 -> 900 at t=2 on the keyframed-width element with a 60 px crop | crop doubled to 120 px, after reload t=0 shows 0.6 (at the previous head) | crop stays 60 px; after reload t=0 0.8, t=4 0.9 |
| Resize saved as `scale` (element with a scale tween) | not walked | box stays 300 px, crop left alone, share 0.8161 before and after |

## Before

On main, the right edge of the red box is cropped, then a corner resize makes it larger. Mid-drag, the dimmed cropped strip stays thin while the box grows:

![Before: mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c5637400-c519-4625-9a62-041964576790)

After deselecting, the crop kept its old pixel width, so more of the box shows than before the resize:

![Before: deselected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6d08165-43cc-4faa-8152-16e78d89b81e)

## After

With the fix, the dimmed strip grows with the box during the drag:

![After: mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01517876-8887-4180-b233-a4f11aa4abb6)

After deselecting, the crop scaled with the box, so the same part of it stays in view:

![After: deselected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ef4a255-35a8-4f09-ab23-609d46b90a3a)

title: fix(studio): a crop drag that ends where it started saves nothing
body:
## What

A crop drag that ends where it started no longer saves anything. Before, pressing a crop edge or the reposition handle, moving and coming back to the same spot rewrote the element's `clip-path` in the file (often as `inset(0px)`) and added an undo step that changed nothing.

A crop also now saves exactly where you let go. Before, a release that came before the screen had drawn the last pointer move saved the crop from the move before it.

## Why

- The crop handles committed whenever the pointer had moved at all during the gesture. A drag that returns to its start moves the pointer but leaves the crop where it was.
- The release read the insets from the last rendered state, not from the gesture, so it could lag one move behind the pointer.

## How

`DomEditCropHandles` keeps the latest insets on the gesture itself, updated on every pointer move. On release it builds the `clip-path` it would write and skips the commit when that equals the one the gesture started from. Comparing the written value, not the raw numbers, also covers the reposition handle: its fractional insets can come back a float ulp off (`0.03 + 0.42 - 0.03`) while writing the same value. The `didMove` flag this replaces is gone.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `DomEditCropHandles.test.tsx`:
