title: fix(core): a video's sound plays at its boosted volume in the preview
body:
## What

A `<video data-start>` clip whose `data-volume` is above 1 now plays its own sound at that level in the preview, up to the same ceiling `<audio>` has. Videos at or below 1 play exactly as before.

## Why

`HTMLMediaElement.volume` stops at 1, so a video authored at `data-volume="1.5"` previewed at 1 while the export applied 1.5. `<audio>` clips already carry gain above 1 through the preview's Web Audio graph; videos never entered it.

## Related work

Refs the above-unity gain work in `audioGain.ts`, whose contract is that preview and render both carry gain above 1.

## How

### What changed

- One predicate in `packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`, `joinsWebAudio`, decides which media the Web Audio transport schedules: every `<audio>`, and a `<video>` only when its `data-volume` is above 1.
- The sites that ask "which elements does Web Audio schedule" now read it: the play-time scheduling pass, the hidden-volume reset before a reschedule, and the discovery-time route diagnostic.
- The `data-hidden` reschedule trigger also counts any element the transport routes right now. Without that, a video captured above 1, lowered to 1 or below and then hidden in the same playback kept sounding at gain 1.
- A routed video uses the existing media-element source path (the element keeps playing its picture; the transport sets `el.volume = 1` and puts the gain on a node). It has no decode fallback: if capture is withheld or fails, the video stays on its native output at volume 1, as today.
- Cross-origin videos without a CORS opt-in are withheld by `classifyWebAudioMediaRoute` like audio is, and stay native.

Sites deliberately left audio-only: the audio-master clock tier (a routed video is a media-element source, which never drives the clock), and the audio-only cue-ahead and seek rules in `media.ts` (element timing is unchanged for a routed video). `isWebAudioOwned` only matches decoded buffer sources, so a routed video is never muted.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `init.test.ts` "a video's sound above unity" (a video at 1.5 gets a media-element source with gain 1.5 and `el.volume` 1; a video at 1 is not captured; a cross-origin video at 1.5 stays native and is never decoded; a video captured at 1.5, lowered to 1 and then hidden mid-playback is released and silent).
- [x] The first test fails with the source change reverted: `expected undefined to be <video …>` (the video was never scheduled). The hidden-after-lowering test fails without the reschedule-trigger change: `expected true to be false` (the video is still routed).
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (core and runtime configs), `init.test.ts` (191 tests) and the neighbouring runtime Web Audio and media test files (517 tests total) pass.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

### What I measured

Built the preview runtime twice (this branch, and this branch with `init.ts` from `main`) and played a one-clip composition in headless Chrome over http, served from a generated test file (440 Hz sine, same file for every case). After 3 s of playback I read the Web Audio master peak with `window.__hf.audioMeter` and the element's own state.

| Clip | Before: master peak | After: master peak | `el.volume` / `muted` (both) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<audio data-volume="1">` (calibration) | 0.022284 | 0.022284 | 1 / false |
| `<video data-volume="1">` | 0 (native output) | 0 (native output) | 1 / false |
| `<video data-volume="1.5">` | 0 (native output, capped at 1) | 0.033426 | 1 / false |

After, the boosted video meters at exactly 1.500x the calibration clip (+3.52 dB). Before, it played natively at `el.volume` 1, which is gain 1.0. The video kept playing (`paused: false`) and was never muted in any case.

### What I did NOT exercise

- A video whose `data-volume` moves from at-or-below 1 to above 1 during playback is picked up at the next Play, not mid-playback. The reverse (above 1 to below) keeps working mid-playback through the existing per-tick gain update.
- A video whose level rises above 1 only through an automation lane or GSAP volume keyframes, with a static `data-volume` at or below 1, stays native.
- A boosted video with a speed ramp (a rate lane in `data-automation`) still plays capped at 1: the scheduling pass skips any clip whose rate is not a single number before capture, the same rule `<audio>` follows.
- A boosted video carrying `data-audio-group` goes to the master bus, not its group's. So muting the group during playback does not mute it, and unmuting the group mid-play leaves it capped at 1 until the next play. A group already muted when play starts keeps it silent. Only hand-written markup can produce this; Studio groups only `<audio>`.
- Studio, the player package and render were not touched or run.

title: fix(studio): shift+drag moves a selection along one axis instead of deselecting it
body:
## What

Holding Shift while dragging a selected element in the Studio preview now moves it along one axis, the one the pointer has travelled further on, as in Figma. Before, a shift+drag moved nothing and cleared the selection. This works for a single element and for a multi-selection. Shift+click still adds an element to the selection.

## Why

A shift+drag is how people keep a move straight. Studio read the Shift press as a multi-select toggle on pointer down, so the drag never started and the toggle deselected the element.

## Related work

None.

## How

- The selection box (single and group) starts the drag on a shift press as it does on a plain press. Boxes that cannot move still hand a shift press to the multi-select toggle.
- While Shift is held, each pointer move keeps only the larger of the horizontal and vertical travel from the press point. Pressing or releasing Shift mid-drag takes effect on the next move.
- Snapping skips the locked axis, so a locked drag snaps only along the axis it moves on and draws no guide for the other one.
- A press counts as a click only if the pointer never travelled past the existing 4 px drag threshold during the press. A drag that goes out and comes back near its start is still a drag and saves where it was dropped.
- A shift click hands the press to the canvas's shift+click path. A single selection already did this. A group now does too; before, a plain press on the group box did nothing, and it still does nothing.
- A click on a selected box now puts the preview back exactly where it was. Before, the drag preview moved through GSAP but the click rollback restored only the CSS offset. A press with 1 to 4 px of hand jitter left the element a few pixels off without saving, and the next drag saved that offset. This also fixes the same leak for plain presses on main, single and group. The rollback now resets GSAP x/y to the values read at the start of the gesture, and the single-element click and cancel paths use the same rollback as the group and resize paths.
- Removing a member of a multi-selection with shift+click is undone about 65 ms later by the timeline's selection sync, on main as well. That is a separate bug and this PR does not change it.
- Arrow nudges, the host mode with body drag turned off, and rotation's Shift snap are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `shiftDragAxisLock.test.tsx`. 14 of its 17 tests fail on main, and all 17 pass on this branch. The three that pass on main check that nothing else changed.
- [x] Manual testing performed in a real browser on a test fixture:
  - Single element: a shift+drag of 50 px right and 8 px down saved `translate(144px, 0px)`. The element stayed on its row and stayed selected. On main the same drag saved nothing and cleared the selection.
  - Group: a shift+drag of 8 px right and 60 px down saved `translate(0px, 180px)` on both members. On main nothing moved.
  - Shift+click on an unselected element still adds it.
  - A 2 px jitter shift-click or plain press, single or group: the preview returns to its start and nothing is saved. A 50 px drag right after it saves `x: 144`, the same as a drag with no jitter before it.
  - A drag 20 px out and back to 3 px saves `x: 9` (3 screen px) and the preview shows the same. A shift+drag 80 px out and back to 1 px saves `x: 3` and does not toggle the selection.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Shift+drag on the selected red box: it does not move and the selection is gone.

![Before, single](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0db04d8-7709-4f47-b3d8-10361ea13048)

Shift+drag on a two-element selection: nothing moves.

![Before, group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63cd031a-02a0-4d48-b714-a4e7bbed7565)

## After

Shift+drag on the selected red box: it moves right along its row and stays selected.

![After, single](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/64267ad1-014f-4cfc-a228-18471107bf7e)

Shift+drag on a two-element selection: both move straight down.

![After, group](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/914fe173-8b70-448a-91a4-43c45ad874eb)

title: feat(studio): let a host make the timeline read-only while seek, scroll and zoom stay live
body:
## What

`Timeline` takes two new props, `readOnly?: boolean` and `onReadOnlyPress?: () => void`.

With `readOnly` on, the timeline stays fully viewable: ruler scrub, playhead drag, click to seek, scrolling (wheel, trackpad, scrollbar), zoom (pinch, ctrl+wheel), hover and selection all work as before. Every edit is refused before it starts, with no drag preview, no menu and no store write, and each refused press calls `onReadOnlyPress` once. Without the prop nothing changes.

## Why

A host app can lock the timeline while something else owns the project, such as a build or an outside session. Today the only way to do that is to lay a cover over the whole timeline, and that cover also blocks seeking, scrolling and zooming. The timeline needs its own read-only mode that refuses edits and keeps viewing.

## Related work

Refs: none. This is a self-contained Studio addition.

## How

Decision: `readOnly` is read in one place, `TimelineProvider`, and reaches the rest through one small context (`timelineReadOnly.ts`). In read-only:

- The timeline subtree sees an empty edit-callback bag, so every control that edits through it (fade handles, FX writes, automation lanes) goes inert, the same way it does for a host that wires no editing. Host edit props still reach the timeline state, and each path that would use one is refused where its gesture starts. The empty timeline stops offering media drops.
- Every clip is locked (no trim handles). A clip press takes the existing blocked-edit path: a plain click still selects the clip, and a press that travels reports once through `onReadOnlyPress`. The host's `onBlockedEditAttempt` does not fire.
- Some edits start without a callback or must report, so they are refused where they start:
  - right-click on a clip, an empty lane (gap menu) or a keyframe: no menu opens
  - a file, asset, block or composition dragged over the timeline: `dropEffect` is `"none"`, no preview, no drop, one report per drag
  - one-click edits (track eye, property keyframe toggle, razor split and split-all): the click is reported instead of acted on
  - beat dot press or alt-click: no drag, no delete
  - FX button: no popover
  - keyframe diamonds: no retime drag; a click still selects

The provider keeps the same tree shape in both modes, so a host can switch read-only on and off without losing scroll, zoom or selection.

Switching read-only on mid-edit: a host can lock the timeline while the person is in the middle of something. On the switch from editable to read-only, one effect drops every edit already in flight without committing it: an active clip drag or resize, a beat drag and a keyframe retime are cancelled, and an open clip, gap or keyframe menu closes.

Reporting: a keyframe-diamond press that travels reports once (a click still selects), and an automation-lane press that travels, or a double-click there, reports once. The refusal is one stable function that always calls the host's latest `onReadOnlyPress`, so an inline callback does not re-render the timeline's children.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `Timeline.readOnly.test.tsx` mounts the whole `Timeline`. In read-only it checks that a ruler press still seeks, a clip drag starts nothing and reports once, a plain click still selects with no trim handle, a clip right-click opens no menu, an empty-lane right-click opens no gap menu, a file drag gets no preview and no commit, and the eye reports instead of toggling. Component tests cover the beat strip, the FX button and the keyframe diamonds. A control test checks that without `readOnly` the same gestures behave as today.
- [x] Each new test was proven non-vacuous: one mutation per test turned it red.
- [x] Existing covering test files re-run one by one, typecheck, oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files.
- [x] Manual: a small harness page mounts `Timeline` as a host would (captures below).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

### What I measured

Each file run alone on a Linux box, exit 0:

| File | Passed |
|---|---|
| `Timeline.readOnly.test.tsx` (new) | 24/24 |
| `TimelineAutomationLane.test.tsx` | 104/104 |
| `useTimelineKeyframeHandlers.test.ts` | 4/4 |
| `useAutomationLanes.test.tsx`, `TimelinePropertyLanes.test.tsx`, `Timeline.showKeyframes.test.tsx` | 6/6, 22/22, 5/5 |
| `Timeline.test.ts` | 83/83 |
| `TimelineLanes.test.tsx` | 15/15 |
| `timelineDragDrop.test.tsx` | 17/17 |
| `BeatStrip.test.tsx` | 11/11 |
| `TimelineClipDiamonds.test.tsx` | 34/34 |
| `TimelineFxButton.test.tsx` | 12/12 |
| `Timeline.rulerSeek.test.tsx` | 5/5 |
| `Timeline.trackPadding.test.tsx` | 4/4 |
| `useTimelineClipDrag.resize.test.tsx` | 26/26 |
| `TimelineClip.test.tsx`, `TimelineTrackPlainHeader.test.tsx`, `TimelineTrackHeader.test.tsx`, `TimelineGroupRow.test.tsx`, `Timeline.virtualization.test.tsx`, `TimelineParts.test.tsx`, `TimelinePartsParity.test.tsx`, `useTrackGapMenu.test.tsx` | all pass |

Each drop on the switch to read-only, removed on its own, turns its own test red (clip drag and resize, beat drag, keyframe retime, each menu), and all five go red if the switch never acts. Every refusal gate, removed on its own, turns its own test red, including the empty edit context (the fade-handle test) and the razor split, keyframe menu and property keyframe toggle. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; oxfmt and oxlint clean on the changed files.

### What I did NOT exercise

- A real host app wiring the prop (it arrives when a host adopts it).
- Keyboard shortcuts that a host handles itself, such as delete, copy and paste in Studio's own editor. Those live in the host and are the host's to gate.
- The range-selection prompt popover (shift-drag). It stays available because it only builds a prompt and writes nothing.
- Selecting an ease segment still opens the host's ease editor. The editor itself is the host's to lock.
- Right-clicking a clip in read-only no longer selects it, because the right-click is refused before selection runs.
- A fade-handle drag or an open FX popover at the moment read-only switches on commits nothing, since the edit callbacks are gone, but a fade preview already drawn stays until the next render of that clip.

## Before

(main, with a host passing `readOnly`: the prop is unknown, so a clip drag shows the drag preview and a right-click opens the clip menu)

Clip drag, mid-gesture (B-roll follows the pointer as a drag preview):

![before-1-clip-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49866602-f1da-4700-b9a1-0e2013ea0b32)

![before-2-right-click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/63119080-ac2b-429e-bab7-6879c1156e47)

## After

(this branch, same host and gestures: the drag is refused with the clip left in place, `onReadOnlyPress` counts each refused press, no menu opens, and a ruler scrub still moves the playhead)

Same drag, mid-gesture (B-roll stays at 3.5 s; `onReadOnlyPress` called once):

![after-1-clip-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fbfecfcd-126d-44df-bba1-1173963cfc90)

Same right-click (no menu; calls: 2):

![after-2-right-click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19ccf238-f468-472c-a182-088ca3433d4f)

Ruler scrub while read-only (playhead moves 2.00 s to 5.96 s; no report):

![after-3-ruler-scrub](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/644655b5-73d5-4fce-91f2-f291b4d0cad7)

title: fix(studio): a drag in a composition without GSAP keeps the element's CSS translate
body:
## What

In a composition that does not load GSAP, dragging an element that a stylesheet places with `translate` (or a `transform` translation) no longer jumps when you let go. A 30px drag now moves it 30px, while dragging, after the drop and after a reload.

## Why

Before this change, the element followed the pointer during the drag and then jumped by its stylesheet offset on release. For example, with `#title { translate: 0 -200px }`, a 30px drag down landed it about 200 composition pixels lower. The wrong position was saved to the file, so a reload showed it too.

The first move of an element in such a composition is saved as `gsap.set("#title", { x, y })`, and the server adds GSAP to the file for that write. That part is intended: a static element's position lives in one GSAP set. When GSAP loads, it folds the element's CSS `translate` and its transform's translation into x/y, so the saved x/y has to include them. The drag took its starting x/y from `gsap.getProperty`. With no GSAP on the page yet, it used 0, so the saved value dropped the stylesheet offset.

To reproduce on main: take a composition with no GSAP script and `#title { translate: 0 -200px }`, then drag `#title` 30px down. It jumps on drop, and the file gets `y: 87` where it should get `y: -113`.

## Related work

Refs #4734. That PR changes the drag teardown in the same file; this change is only in the drag setup, and the two do not overlap.

## How

`createManualOffsetDragMember` reads its starting x/y from `gsap.getProperty` when GSAP is on the page. When it is not, it now computes the value GSAP's CSS parser will report for the element once the commit loads it:

- the computed CSS `translate` (px, or % of the element's box), plus
- the translation of `rotate`, `scale` and the computed `transform` combined in that order, as GSAP builds them, minus
- a -50% centering, which GSAP keeps in `xPercent`/`yPercent` rather than x/y.

When the browser cannot parse that combination (for example `rotate: x 30deg`), GSAP keeps only the plain transform, and so does this.

Nothing changes when GSAP is loaded.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: a stylesheet `translate`, a stylesheet `transform`, and a `-50%` centering. The first two fail on main (`expected { x: 40, y: 30 } to deeply equal { x: 40, y: -170 }`). The third fails if the centering rule is removed.
- [x] Also tested: a CSS `rotate` or `scale` turns or scales the transform's translation, a combination the browser cannot parse falls back to the plain transform without throwing, and with GSAP on the page the base still comes from GSAP. Checked against real GSAP 3.12.5 in Chrome on 27 element styles: all match.
- [x] Manual testing performed: walked in Studio on fixture compositions. Each walk did two moves, then undo, redo and reload. Walks covered a no-GSAP `translate` element, a no-GSAP `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` element, and a GSAP composition with a stylesheet `translate` to check for regressions.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Walk results. Screen px in a 1600x900 Studio, from where the element started; the pointer moved +40,+30 and then -60,+20.

| Composition | Build | Saved first move | After drop | After two moves | Undo / redo | After reload |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| No GSAP, `translate: 0 -200px` | main | `y: 87` | 40, **99** | -20, 50 | 40, 99 / -20, **119** | -20, **119** |
| No GSAP, `translate: 0 -200px` | this PR | `y: -113` | 40, 30 | -20, -19 | 40, 30 / -20, 50 | -20, 50 |
| No GSAP, `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` | main | `x: 116` | **66**, 30 | **6**, 50 | 66, 30 / 6, 50 | **6**, 50 |
| No GSAP, `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` | this PR | `x: 42` | 40, 30 | -20, 50 | 40, 30 / -20, 50 | -20, 50 |
| GSAP, `translate: 0 -200px` | main and this PR (same) | `y: -113` | 40, -39 | -20, -19 | 40, 30 / -20, 50 | -20, 50 |

The saved values in the GSAP composition are the same on main and on this PR. The live -39 there, and the -19 after the second no-GSAP move on this PR, is the stylesheet translate showing again under GSAP's transform after a drop. That is #4734's bug. #4734 is now on main, and on main plus this PR every cell in both compositions is exact: 40, 30 / -20, 50.

## Before

No GSAP, `translate: 0 -200px`. Held at the end of the drag, the title is where the pointer put it:

![Before: title held under the pointer at the end of the drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1554f7e-ab79-4901-a492-33dbe3e0d04c)

After the drop it jumps down, and that is what gets saved:

![Before: title jumped down after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/adc476ce-b7ca-4f3a-bbc4-6b7b8e79c4b8)

No GSAP, `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)`. After the drop it jumps right:

![Before: centered title jumped right after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0817d0fa-e977-436b-ac07-353752397687)

## After

No GSAP, `translate: 0 -200px`. After the drop the title stays where the pointer left it:

![After: title stays under the pointer after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3e629be-4a87-4e0f-9410-2246decf1dd6)

No GSAP, `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)`. It stays put too:

![After: centered title stays put after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3373f384-8f58-4cf2-b207-f1450712bddf)

title: fix(studio): font faces a host saves keep their own weight and style
body:
## What changed

Studio writes an `@font-face` for each font file a text is set in, but it never says which weight or style that file draws. When a film holds several files of one family (a Bold for the title, a Regular for the subtitle, an Italic for a caption), every face claims the same default weight and style. The browser then draws every text of that family from the last file saved, in the editor and in the render.

This lets a host that knows each file's weight and style say so; Studio then writes it into the face.

- `ImportedFontAsset` takes an optional `weight` ("700" for a static file, "100 900" for a variable one) and `style` ("normal" or "italic").
- `importedFontFaceCss` writes them as `font-weight` and `font-style`, so each file draws only the texts that ask for its weight and style. A weight a browser would drop (0, 5000, `bold`, anything but one or two numbers from 1 to 1000) is left out.
- An asset with neither is written byte for byte as before, so faces already in a film still match and are not written twice.
- `injectPreviewImportedFont` keys its preview `<style>` by file path instead of by family. A second file of a family now reaches the preview, and the preview shows the same file as the render. Before, it kept showing the family's first file.
- Where the values come from: the assets a host passes to `useDomEditSession` as `importedFontAssetsRef`. `resolveImportedFontAsset` returns the first asset of the family in that list, so a host puts the file a save should write first in the list before that save. It returns them ahead of the file tree, and `commitDomStyles` and the text-field commit save them through `ensureImportedFontFace`. Studio's own font import passes no weight or style yet, so its behaviour is unchanged; reading them from the file name there is a separate change.
- Two fixes to the same save path, both already on `main`:
  - `ensureImportedFontFace` passed the new CSS to `String.replace` as a string. A file name holding `$'` or `$&` pasted part of the page into the saved HTML. It now passes a function.
  - `cssString` now escapes `<`, so a family decoded from a file name such as `</style><b>x` cannot close the fonts `<style>` block.

## What I measured

- `fontAssets.test.ts`, 5 tests:
  - A face with no weight or style is written as before.
  - The descriptors are written, including a variable weight range; values a browser would drop are left out; a family cannot close the style block.
  - Two weights of one family both stay in the saved HTML (a repeat is not written twice) and both reach the preview.
  - A `$'` or `$&` in a file name is saved as written.
- `domStyleCommit.fonts.test.ts`, 1 test: two `commitDomStyles` saves, whose resolver hands over Poppins SemiBold (600) and then Regular (400), leave two faces in the saved HTML with `font-weight: 600` and `font-weight: 400`.
- Mutations, each caught:
  - Dropping the descriptors fails 4 tests.
  - Keying the preview by family again fails 1.
  - Removing the `<` escape fails 1.
  - Loosening the weight check fails 1.
  - A string replacer fails 1.
- `useDomEditCommits`, `useDomEditTextCommits` and `useDomEditSession` tests: 64 pass. Studio `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet are clean.
- A host run against this change with the diff applied to its installed Studio: after a Poppins pick for a 600-weight title and one for a 400 subtitle, with the Google font hosts blocked, the saved page held two faces (600 and 400). Chrome loaded both from the project's files, and each text drew its own weight. At 0.8.96 the same run saved two faces with no descriptors.
- The pages behind the captures below use the real `importedFontFaceCss` from `main` and from this branch in a hand-built page, not the Studio UI: Poppins Bold, Regular and Italic from fonts.gstatic.com, with made-up text. At `main`, Chrome loads only the last face; with this change it loads all three.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio's own font import: it still passes no weight or style, so it still writes descriptor-less faces.
- A film that already has descriptor-less faces for a family keeps them. They claim weight 400 and style normal, so they can still win for texts that match those values after a newer face with descriptors is saved.
- Firefox and Safari.

## Before

At `main`, three Poppins files for three texts: every text draws from the last file, so the title and the subtitle come out italic.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b5fc457-d672-4216-9b35-a7f0c619d577)

## After

Each face says its weight and style: the title draws Bold, the subtitle Regular, the caption Italic.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afadb979-cde7-4fc2-b8cc-f357bd844ed1)

title: fix(studio): shift+click on a group member removes it for good
body:
## What

In the Studio preview, shift+click on a member of a group selection now removes it, and it stays removed. Before, the member came back a moment later, so a group could never be trimmed by clicking. The same happened when a marquee caught just one member of a live group.

## Why

The timeline keeps the selection set, and it syncs that set back onto the canvas. When shift+click shrank a group to one element, the canvas announced only a new anchor and left the timeline's set at two members. About 70 ms later the sync saw two wanted and one on the canvas, and re-selected both (`apply nextGroup:1`, then `timeline-sync wanted:2 had:1`, then `marquee hits:2` in the `hf-select` debug log). A move right after that dragged the removed element too.

The mirror guessed intent from the group size: a one-element group whose anchor is already in the set was treated as a late async primary and kept the old set. A shift toggle or a marquee that ends at one element looks the same by size.

## Related work

Refs #3146, which introduced the set-preserving rule this narrows.

## How

The caller now says when its group is the whole new selection. `applyDomSelection` passes that for a shift toggle, and `applyMarqueeSelection` always does, so `announceTimelineSelection` publishes the new set in the same step as the canvas change. There is no race left to lose, and no timer. A plain single selection of an element already inside the live set still keeps the set, as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `useDomSelection.test.ts` now reads back the set it last published, the way the timeline store does. Two new cases (shift+click removes a member, one-element marquee over a group) fail on main with the set still holding both ids, and pass here. A third case pins the old rule: re-announcing one member keeps the set; it fails if the mirror always replaces the set.
- [x] Manual testing performed on a fixture project with the timeline open: group two elements, shift+click one member (the timeline and inspector show one element at 150 ms and at 1 s, no sync re-select in the log), shift+click a non-member (added), shift+click it again (removed), move what is left (only that element's position is written), undo (file reverts). A one-element marquee over a group of two leaves one.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Group of two, then shift+click on Tiny. A second later both are selected again.

![Before: group of two](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4cdef051-cf91-49dc-a98d-5dce54e29b9f)
![Before: one second after shift+click on a member, both are selected again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0b166be-87f4-48da-bace-2684cb995bc6)

## After

Same gesture. Tiny is removed and stays removed; shift+click on Headline adds it.

![After: one second after shift+click on a member, only Medium is selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a989cba-a68e-4e48-8080-a30d6fccedba)
![After: shift+click on a non-member adds it](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8db56456-cb70-4c35-b576-5fba1e081a90)

title: feat(studio): select rightward takes crossing clips, and a host can keep only Select and Split
body:
## What

Two changes to the timeline's select-around-the-playhead tools.

**1. Select rightward now includes clips crossing the playhead. This changes OSS Studio's default behaviour.** Select rightward (and `]`) takes every clip still running at the playhead or later: a clip is picked when it ends after the playhead. Before, it picked only clips that start at or after the playhead, so a clip already playing under the playhead was skipped, and in the middle of a film it often selected nothing. Select leftward (and `[`) is unchanged: it already took every clip that started before the playhead, crossing clips included. A clip starting exactly at the playhead still goes to rightward and not leftward. The `]` hint in the shortcuts panel now reads "Select clips running at or after the playhead".

**2. A host can hide the two rows.** `TimelineToolbar` gets `showSelectAroundPlayhead?: boolean` (default `true`). With `false`, the timeline tool menu lists only Select and Split; Select leftward and Select rightward are not shown. The `[` and `]` shortcuts keep working either way. Studio's own app passes nothing, so it is unchanged.

## Why

"Select rightward" reads as "everything from here on". Skipping the clip under the playhead made it look broken mid-film, and it did not mirror leftward, which already included that clip.

A host app that embeds Studio wants a shorter tool menu with just the two tools, while keeping the keyboard shortcuts for people who know them. Today it cannot hide those rows without CSS reaching into Studio internals.

## Related work

Same host-prop pattern as `showHistory` (#4739) and `showKeyframes` (#4680). The menu rows came in with #4714.

## How

- `selectAroundPlayhead` in `playerStore.ts` now passes the whole clip to its predicate. Leftward keeps `start < playhead`; rightward is `start + duration > playhead`. The menu rows and the `[`/`]` keys both call these store actions, so both pick up the change.
- `TimelineToolbar` threads the prop to `TimelineToolPicker`, which appends the two rows only when it is `true`.
- The name follows the store helper both rows call, `selectAroundPlayhead` in `playerStore.ts`.
- The shortcuts are bound in `appHotkeysDispatch.ts` and call the store directly, not the menu, so hiding the rows leaves the keys alone.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

`useAppHotkeys.test.ts`, "select leftward / rightward": the fixture now has a clip crossing the playhead, one entirely before it, one starting exactly at it, and one entirely after.

- `[` selects the crossing clip and the clip entirely before it. It does not select the clip starting exactly at the playhead or the one after it. This already passed before the change, because leftward already included crossing clips.
- `]` selects the crossing clip, the clip starting exactly at the playhead and the clip entirely after it. It does not select the clip entirely before. Run against `main`'s store, this test fails: `expected [ 'at', 'late' ] to deeply equal [ 'at', 'early', 'late' ]`.

`TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`, "TimelineToolbar tool menu":

- The menu opened with no prop lists the four rows. With `showSelectAroundPlayhead: false` it lists Select and Split. Run against `main`'s picker, this test fails: `expected [ 'Select', 'Split', …(2) ] to deeply equal [ 'Select', 'Split' ]`.
- With the rows shown and with them hidden, `[` and `]` at the playhead select the same clips. With the `[`/`]` branch taken out of `appHotkeysDispatch.ts`, both cases fail: `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'c0' ]`.

Also run, one file per command: `playerStore.test.ts`, `ShortcutsPanel.test.tsx`, `TimelineHistoryButtons.dom.test.tsx`, `timelineChromeExports.test.tsx`, `pointerTargetSize.test.tsx`, `useAppHotkeys.test.ts`, `ui/Menu.test.tsx`. Plus Studio `tsc --noEmit`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` on the changed files.

In a browser, using Studio's dev app with a three-clip test composition (Title 0-4 s, Card 2-6 s, Outro 5-9 s):

- Playhead at 3 s. On `main`, Select rightward selected only Outro. On this branch, it selected Title, Card and Outro (Title and Card cross the playhead). `[` selected Title and Card on both.
- Playhead at 1.5 s, with the prop set to `false`: the menu showed only Select and Split, `]` selected Card and Outro, and `[` selected Title.

## Before

Studio on `main`, three-clip test composition, 1440x900, headless Chrome.

Select rightward with the playhead at 3 s selects only Outro. Title and Card are still playing under the playhead and are skipped.

![Before: Select rightward at 3 s selects only Outro](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fefa7dc0-e027-4c95-ae7b-d9e0b34d65b9)

The tool menu lists Select, Split, Select leftward and Select rightward.

![Before: the tool menu with four rows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb172660-8e80-40cf-9b07-83aa03519556)

## After

This branch, same composition. Select rightward with the playhead at 3 s selects Title, Card and Outro.

![After: Select rightward at 3 s selects Title, Card and Outro](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5e7590a1-98bd-4cf9-9229-18ae6f4a2457)

This branch, with the toolbar given `showSelectAroundPlayhead={false}` the way a host would pass it (for the capture only; Studio's own app passes nothing and still shows four rows). The menu lists Select and Split.

![After: the tool menu with Select and Split only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a30bfee3-d117-4d33-9b89-df592d824dde)

title: fix(studio): a copied clip keeps its look and motion, and a duplicated section keeps its name
body:
## What 

A clip copied with Cmd+C and Cmd+V, or duplicated with Cmd+D, now looks and moves like its original. Duplicating a section no longer renames both it and its copy.

## Why

- Paste and duplicate give the copy a new id when the original's id is taken (`goodbye` becomes `goodbye-2`). The film's CSS rules and GSAP tweens name the original by that id, so the copy lost both. It drew in the default black 24 px text and never faded in. On a dark film it was invisible.
- A duplicated section keeps its `data-composition-id`, which is how two instances of one sub-composition are written. At load, the runtime gives each instance a unique id (`benefit-fresh__hf1`, `benefit-fresh__hf2`) and keeps the authored one in `data-hf-original-composition-id`. The timeline label was built from the unique id, so both clips read "Benefit Fresh Hf1" and "Benefit Fresh Hf2".

To reproduce either bug on main: in a film with `<h2 id="goodbye">` styled by `#goodbye { color: ... }` and tweened by `tl.from("#goodbye", ...)`, select the clip and press Cmd+D. For the name, do the same on a clip that hosts a sub-composition through `data-composition-src`.

## How

- `packages/studio/src/utils/clipboardLook.ts` (new): for each id the paste renamed, it copies every top-level CSS rule keyed to the original id for the copy's id, using the browser's own CSS parser. Only the entries of a selector list that name the id are copied, and never one under `:not()`, so the copy restyles nothing else. It also copies the original's tweens through the GSAP writer. It reads scripts and styles in one pass, so a `<style>` written inside a script's text stays script.
- `pasteTimelineClips` calls it when the clips come from the same file of the same project. Duplicate always does; paste does when the copy's project and file are the target's. The clipboard now records the project.
- `packages/parsers/src/gsapWriterAcorn.ts` `copyAnimationsInScript`: a copy of a tween is exact or absent.
  - Only a tween at a number, written straight in the block that declares the timeline, is copied. The copy keeps the original's own argument text and moves its position by the paste's offset, so stagger, delay and ease behave the same.
  - A tween at a label or relative position, one with no position, one in a loop, one on a variable, and one inside a callback or a guard (`window.go && tl.from(...)`) are not copied. Their start depends on what comes before them, so a copy could not be placed exactly.
  - Copies go at the end of that block, before its `return`. The timeline is in scope there, and nothing that follows in its scope is pushed back. That holds when the timeline is declared at the top, inside an `if` or `try`, or inside a function.
  - A `gsap.set` on the original is copied right after itself.
  - This follows what split already does for its second half (`duplicateCssRulesForId`, `splitAnimationsInScript`), but runs in the browser, where paste and duplicate edit the file. The server's postcss version also covers `@media` and escaped ids. Sharing one owner would put postcss in the browser bundle; that is left for a follow-up.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/timeline.ts`: a clip's label, and a scene's, is built from the authored composition id when the runtime renamed the instance.

Not covered, and the copy keeps today's behaviour in these cases:
- a rule inside `@media` or `@supports`;
- a tween not at a number, in a loop, on a variable, inside a callback or guard, or outside the timeline's own block: the copy has no such tween;
- a clip pasted into a different file, whose ids can mean other elements there;
- a DOM element pasted outside the timeline.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## What I measured

On a Linux box:
- `clipboardLook.test.ts` runs the pasted film's own script with real GSAP. It checks three things: the copy's rules equal the original's, the copy's tween starts where the copy lands (4 s), and the title's positionless tween still starts at 1.5 s. It fails with the carry call removed. It also fails when the copies are inserted right after the original tween, which pushes the title's tween back.
- `gsapWriter.acorn.test.ts` has seven new tests:
  - the copy's text, and that it ends the timeline's block;
  - no copy of a tween at a label or with no position;
  - no copy of a tween inside a listener, a guard or a `tl.call` callback;
  - a copy inside the `if` block that declares the timeline;
  - a copy before a function's `return`;
  - a set's copy right after it;
  - a script with no tween on the id is left as it was.
- `clipboardLook.test.ts` runs the pasted film with real GSAP in four tests. The key one mixes a stagger, a delay, a positionless tween, a label, a tween on a variable and one in a loop, inside an `if` block. After the paste every one of the film's own tweens starts exactly where it did. The copy of the tween at a number starts 3 s after its original, as the clip does. Its check that the film's own tweens keep their starts fails when the copies are placed right after the copied tween. The others cover selector lists, `:not()`, a `<style>` string inside a script, and another file.
- `timeline.test.ts` has one new test: two instances of a scene are both named "Benefit Fresh". It fails without the fix, reading "Benefit Fresh Hf1" and "Hf2".
- Test runs: `timeline.test.ts` 71 of 71, `gsapWriter.acorn.test.ts` 38 of 38, Studio clipboard and payload tests 35 of 35.
- Typecheck, lint, format and the fallow audit are clean.
- End to end in Studio (`vite` dev server, headless Chromium) on a fixture film, with this head:
  - Cmd+D: the copy is orange at 96 px, with its own keyframes;
  - Cmd+C then Cmd+V: the same;
  - Cmd+D on a section: both timeline clips read "Benefit Fresh".
- The same steps on main: the copy is black at 24 px with no keyframes, and the section clips read "Benefit Fresh Hf2" and "Benefit Fresh Hf1".

## What I did NOT exercise

- No run on macOS or Windows.
- The Design panel's list of selected elements still names the two section instances "Benefit Fresh Hf2" and "Hf1" (visible in the last After image): its label reads the runtime id too. That fix is #4768.
- A paste across files.

## Before

Cmd+D on Goodbye: the copy's strip on the timeline is blank. It lost the original's orange text and its keyframes.

![Before: Cmd+D, the copy's timeline strip is blank](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c5a0406-0e29-48d0-a65f-55ab035a9109)

Cmd+C then Cmd+V: at 5 s the pasted copy is on screen but invisible, only its selection outline shows.

![Before: Cmd+V, the pasted copy at 5 s is invisible](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd61f18b-1a5c-49d8-8752-5f2235d11504)

Cmd+D on the section: the section and its copy read "Benefit Fresh Hf2" and "Benefit Fresh Hf1".

![Before: the section and its copy read Hf2 and Hf1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97b4866a-1341-4afe-b283-428b5fc0cc12)

## After

Cmd+D on Goodbye: at 5 s the copy shows in the original's orange, with its own keyframes.

![After: Cmd+D, the copy at 5 s is orange like the original](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c22840f9-6298-4364-a216-59a734e7a41e)

Cmd+C then Cmd+V: at 6 s the pasted copy is orange too.

![After: Cmd+V, the pasted copy is orange](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1345ec1b-cae4-4a15-a30c-54770bb0a462)

Cmd+D on the section: both timeline clips read "Benefit Fresh".

![After: both section clips read Benefit Fresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8d4dc809-8fe9-4545-bbe1-a4b54de26d7b)

title: fix(studio): undoing an agent's build takes its sections off the timeline too
body:
## What

Undoing an agent's build of sections now takes those sections off the timeline too. Before this change, the file went back but the timeline kept showing every section the build added, until the project was reopened.

## Why

When a shorter clip list arrives, `mergeTimelineElementsPreservingDowngrades` keeps each old element that has a `compositionSrc`. The rule exists for sub-composition children that a bare DOM re-scan drops and `enrichMissingCompositions` re-adds. A section the agent built is also a sub-composition host with a `compositionSrc`. So after an undo, the runtime reported the reverted film's clips (3), and the merge added the removed sections back (6).

To reproduce on main: while Studio is open, write sections hosted by `data-composition-src` into the file from outside Studio (as an agent does), then write the file back (its undo). The file and the picture go back, but the timeline keeps the sections.

## How

- `mergeTimelineElementsPreservingDowngrades` takes an `inPreview` check. An old element is kept only while its node is still in the preview.
- `syncTimelineElements`, the one place every discovery path writes through, passes `findTimelineElementInIframe`. That is the composition-aware lookup the other timeline edits use.
- A sub-composition child that a re-scan drops is still in the preview, so it is still kept.
- The check looks each row up as a composition host (`kind: "composition"`), as `parseTimelineFromDOM` names the same node. Without it the lookup searched `index.html` for a host that belongs to its own composition and never found it. The row itself keeps its kind, so trims and other edits on it are unchanged.
- On a background (shadow) reload, `iframeRef` points at the new document before its clip list is committed. Before, the commit read the old document, which still held the undone sections.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## What I measured

On a Linux box:
- Three new tests, each failing without its own fix:
  - `timelineDOM.test.ts`: a section whose host left the preview is dropped;
  - `timelineIframeHelpers.test.ts`: the lookup finds an enriched host in its preview when asked for it as a composition;
  - `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`: after a shadow reload, a section the new document no longer has leaves the timeline, though the old document still holds it. It fails with main's merge rule, and with the old commit order.
- The nearby test files (timelineDOM, useTimelinePlayer, its shadowReload tests, useTimelineSyncCallbacks, timelineIframeHelpers, previewMessageRouter): 141 of 141 pass.
- Typecheck, lint, format and the fallow audit are clean.
- End to end in Studio (`vite` dev server, headless Chromium) on a fixture film: a write from outside Studio adds two section hosts, the timeline shows them, then a second write puts the file back. On main the timeline kept both sections while the preview held none, in 2 of 2 runs. With this head it showed only Title, in 2 of 2 runs.

## What I did NOT exercise

- No run on macOS or Windows.
- An undo driven by a real agent run; the outside write stands in for it.
- Undo of a build of inline (not `data-composition-src`) compositions.

## Before

On main, after the file is put back, the preview shows only Title but the timeline still shows Benefit Fresh and Benefit Local.

![Before: the timeline still shows the two removed sections](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/238d803b-5247-4395-acd5-2557ea7c8ce3)

## After

With this change, the same steps leave only Title on the timeline, like the file.

![After: the timeline matches the file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/da10f1b6-1bda-4730-b0a0-4254b9548047)

title: feat(studio): a popover can point at its trigger with an optional arrow
body:
## What changed

`Popover` takes an optional `arrow` prop. When set, the popup draws a small arrow pointing at its trigger, using Base UI's `Popover.Arrow`, filled with the popup's surface and outlined with its border color, rotated to whichever side the popup landed on after collision flips. The default gap from the trigger grows by the arrow's height so the tip keeps the usual 6 px. Off by default: every existing popover renders exactly as before.

## Why

A popover opened from a small trigger in a dense surface (a chip on a timeline clip) reads as floating; the arrow ties it to the thing it edits.

## What I measured

- `Menu.test.tsx`, new case "points at its trigger only when asked": the popup opens without an arrow by default; with `arrow`, the arrow renders and carries the popup's `data-side`. With `main`'s `Popover.tsx` put back, it fails (`arrow not rendered`).
- `Menu.test.tsx` and `styles/tokenGate.test.ts`: 17 of 17 pass. Each new `data-[side=*]:` class was also compiled directly with Studio's Tailwind setup, since the token gate checks a class with its variant removed.
- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on both files: clean.
- A left or right arrow is 14 px along the popup's edge once rotated, so `arrowPadding` is 10 to keep it off the rounded corner when the popup is shifted against the viewport.

## Before

A throwaway page rendering `Popover` open on each side, from `main`: no arrow.

![Before: popovers on four sides, no arrow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/602ebf8d-6e01-4567-8db3-4bde71de10c3)

## After

The same page with `arrow`: each popup points at its trigger, and the gap to the tip stays 6 px.

![After: popovers on four sides, each with an arrow](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/178a9030-a641-4bab-8ee0-0771f08ed1c9)

## What I did NOT exercise

- No Studio surface opts in yet, so the captures come from a throwaway page, not from Studio itself.

title: fix(studio): a click after an empty-canvas press selects on the first try
body:
## What

In the Studio preview, a click on an element right after a press on empty canvas now selects it on the first try. Before, that click selected nothing and only a second click worked. The same happened after a confident shift+click add.

## Why

A press on empty canvas (which starts a marquee) and a confident shift+click both handle the press on `pointerdown`, call `preventDefault()`, and set `suppressNextOverlayMouseDownRef` so that the same press's `mousedown` is not handled a second time. But a browser sends no compatibility `mousedown` after a default-prevented `pointerdown`. Nothing clears the flag, so the check in `handleOverlayMouseDown` swallows the next real press instead (`mousedown-suppressed` in the `hf-select-debug` log).

Repro on main: turn on `localStorage["hf-select-debug"]="1"`, click empty canvas, then click an element once. Nothing is selected, and the log shows `mousedown-suppressed`.

## Related work

Refs #4747 (shift+drag axis lock and tap rollback) and #4754 (shift+click group removal). This PR does not change their behaviour.

## How

`suppressNextOverlayMouseDownRef` and `suppressNextBoxMouseDownRef` were dead code: they were set to swallow a `mousedown` that Chrome never sends.
- Every place that set them either ran inside a default-prevented `pointerdown` (Chrome 152 sends no compatibility `mousedown` after that, for mouse, pen or touch), or ran in the overlay's `mousedown` after the box's own `mousedown` had already fired.
- So they could never guard their own press. They only ever swallowed a later one.

This PR removes them:
- both flags;
- the `mousedown-suppressed` branch in `handleOverlayMouseDown`;
- `suppressBoxMouseDown`;
- the `onBoxMouseDown` prop on both selection chromes.

The browser's own compatibility-mousedown suppression is now the single owner of "do not handle this press twice". The shift branch of the overlay `mousedown` also set `suppressNextBoxClickRef`. That setter was dead as well and is removed: it only runs for a press that starts outside the selection box, and a click fires on the common parent of the down and up targets, so it never reaches the box. `suppressNextBoxClickRef` stays for the confident shift press: there a `click` does fire on the box after the prevented `pointerdown`, and without the flag an undraggable group or an immovable box would toggle twice. The flag is still cleared at the start of every press. Host mode (`canvasInput: "host"`) never set the removed flags, so its behaviour is unchanged.

Net lines: +122 / -40. All the added lines are the new test file; production code is +0 / -33.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `clickAfterPreventedPress.test.tsx` fires a press the way Chrome does (no `mousedown` after a prevented `pointerdown`). It covers an empty-canvas press and a shift+click add, each followed by a plain click. Both cases fail on main (`expected "vi.fn()" to be called 1 times, but got 0 times`) and pass with the fix. A third case shift+clicks a selected box that cannot move and expects exactly one toggle. It fails when the confident shift press stops setting the click flag (`expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times`). The full editor and hooks run passes: `Test Files 250 passed | 1 skipped (251)`, `Tests 2643 passed | 16 todo (2659)`, and `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- [x] Manual testing performed: walked a fixture project in headless Chrome. Before is main; after is this head rebased on main.
  - Empty canvas, then one click on an element: nothing selected before, selected after.
  - Marquee, then a click on another element: nothing selected before, selected after.
  - Empty canvas, then a double-click on text: before, the editor opened with nothing selected; after, the element is selected and editing.
  - Empty canvas, then a press-drag on an element: before, the press was swallowed; after, it selects, and the next drag moves it. A press-drag on an unselected element selects without moving it, on main too.
  - Shift+click add, then shift+click remove on the group, then a plain click: the removal leaves the other member selected, and the plain click selects.
  - A click on the already-selected box, also right after an empty-canvas press: it stays selected.
  - `mousedown-suppressed` count across the walk: 4 before, 0 after (the log line no longer exists).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Empty canvas, then one click on the red box: the box is hovered but nothing is selected.

![Before: click after empty canvas selects nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c8ea88f-38d1-4670-8d8a-8dcb1a67ede5)

Empty canvas, then a double-click on the headline: the editor opens, but nothing is selected.

![Before: double-click after empty canvas, nothing selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16ef280c-cdaf-4367-8387-602079783ba4)

## After

The same click selects the red box on the first try.

![After: click after empty canvas selects the box](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/11529de3-0825-4eb0-8287-46e998617c64)

The same double-click selects the headline and edits it.

![After: double-click selects and edits the headline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/83be6349-fcbb-4577-a3b6-a59a60e63c08)

title: test(studio): an edit accuracy benchmark for manual editing
body:
## What

A benchmark that measures how accurately manual editing in Studio follows the person doing it. One command drives real pointer and keyboard gestures in the built CLI Studio. Each case gets its own generated project and is scored in composition pixels.

This first part ships the grid, the project generator, the runner and six of the seven metrics. Render drift (the check against a producer frame) is the stacked follow-up, #4764. The CI gate comes after it, in #4765.

```
bun run --cwd packages/studio test:edit-accuracy -- --grid full --jobs 4 --lock /tmp/suite.lock
```

Flags:
- `--grid full|pr`, `--shard i/n`, `--jobs N`, `--filter <regex on case id>`;
- `--out <dir>`, `--port <first>`, `--cli <cli.js>`;
- `--lock <path>`: take a shared flock per chunk of 8 cases, so a full grid never holds a shared machine's lock for its whole run.

## Why

Nothing measured whether a move, resize, rotate, crop or nudge lands where the pointer put it, survives undo and a reload, and stays smooth. Manual edit fixes had no score to hold them to; this benchmark is that score. Later edit PRs should raise it and never lower it.

## Related work

Refs #4764 (render drift, stacked on this) and #4765 (the CI gate and ratchet over `baseline.json`).

## How

**Grid (660 cases)**
- Every case is one flat-coloured element in a fresh tmp copy of a generated project, so no checked-in fixture is ever edited.
- GSAP: none, an x/y tween spanning the playhead, or a `gsap.set` hold.
- Placement:
  - stylesheet `translate` in px;
  - `translate` in %;
  - `left/top: 50%` with a `-50%` translate;
  - GSAP `xPercent/yPercent: -50` (only with GSAP).
- Rotation 0 or 30deg; root or nested composition.
- Preview zoom 50%, 100% or 200%, set through Studio's own Ctrl+wheel zoom.
- Gestures:
  - move;
  - corner resize, dragged along the diagonal;
  - rotate;
  - crop of the right edge;
  - arrow nudge ×5.
- Studio has corner handles only (the edge strips crop), so there is no edge-resize gesture.
- Undo and redo run in every case, before any reload:
  - each waits up to 15 s for its own file write;
  - redo is sent only once undo has landed;
  - the reload waits until the files have held still.
- The nested host has no transform of its own. That class, a host transform missed or counted twice, is not exercised yet.

**Measurement**
- Positions come from the element's rendered quad (CDP `DOM.getContentQuads`), mapped to composition px through the root composition's own quad.
- Pointer steps run one per animation frame, in lockstep with the measurement.
- Studio is the built CLI, driven by real input events. WebMCP `studio_seek` is used only to seek.
- One Chrome for everything: the engine's pinned headless shell.
- Snapping is turned off through Studio's own toggle, because a snap moves the box off the pointer on purpose.
- **Settle.** Studio updates the preview asynchronously after a save: it reloads the edited document in a shadow iframe and swaps it in. So every snapshot (before the gesture, the commit, undo, redo, and after a reload) waits until two things have held still for 1 s: the set of preview frames and the element's box.
  - If the preview never holds still within 15 s, that is a Studio defect. The metrics fed by that snapshot fail with an `unsettled` flag. The case's other metrics still count, and it is not a harness error.
- Each case runs its own Studio server with its own HOME, so undo history stays inside the case's tmp dir. The tmp dir is removed after the case and on a signal.
- The runner refuses a port Studio did not announce. The CLI quietly moves to the next free port, which would drive another run's Studio.
- The table and `baseline.json` are stamped with:
  - the commit of the tree the CLI was built from;
  - a hash of the built CLI bundle;
  - the bench commit;
  - the load average at the start and end of the run.

**Metrics (all in composition px)**
1. **Tracking:** the max per-frame distance between the grabbed point and the pointer, relative to where both stood at press.
2. **Press jump:** the element's box one frame after press, against its box before press. Tracking is relative to the press, so a jump on grab is invisible to it; this metric catches it.
3. **Drop jump:** the last drag frame against the settled commit.
4. **Reload drift:** the settled commit against a fresh Studio load.
5. (Render drift, in #4764.)
6. **Undo fidelity:** undo is byte-identical to the file before the gesture and redo to the committed file, and each settled box lands within 0.5 px.
   - If the undo or redo write never lands, undo fails with `undoTimeout: "undo"` or `"redo"`. A redo that was never sent counts as untested, not as a pass.
7. **Smoothness:** compared against a blank-page control.
   - Before each case, the same drag schedule and the same per-frame reads run on a blank page, in the same Chrome with the same flags.
   - A frame counts as dropped when its interval, read from the rAF callback's own `performance.now()`, is over 25 ms. Chrome stamps a late frame with the vsync it missed, which would hide a stall.
   - Main-thread work per frame is thread CPU time from a trace of the drag.
   - Missing trace data makes the work unknown, which fails smoothness alone.

A case passes when:
- tracking, press jump, drop and reload are all ≤ 0.5 px;
- undo and redo are byte-identical, with the box ≤ 0.5 px;
- it drops no more frames than its control;
- its main-thread work is ≤ 8 ms per frame at p95.

Raw rAF p95 is still reported for the case and its control.

The table's headline counts the cases that pass every metric except smoothness. Smoothness gets its own line against the control, with the load stamp, because it moves with machine load.

**The tracking limit stays 0.5 px.**
- Main rounds live drag positions to whole composition px, so a 4.5 px move step makes the error an exact 0.5 px tie on alternate frames. The mapping then adds a fixed 0.00-0.06 px per case.
- On the 24-case repeat below, every tracking value repeated to 0.0001 px across the three runs. The ties read 0.4991 to 0.5541, and each one gave the same verdict 3 of 3 times. So noise does not decide the verdict.
- The tie exists only because of main's whole-px rounding, which #4766 removes. After that fix these values should fall to the mapping's own few hundredths, far from the limit. So the limit is not tuned around main's 0.50.

## Test plan

- [x] **The settle holds.** I re-measured each snapshot every 100 ms for 5 s afterwards, on the four cases where the preview had been seen moving after a snapshot. I used the same Studio build on a 32-core machine at low load.

| Case | Old settle ("committed" moved later) | New settle (commit, undo, redo moved later, at 3 s and over 5 s) |
|---|---|---|
| move-none-center-r0-nested-z100 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| move-none-pct-r30-nested-z50 | 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| move-none-px-r0-root-z100 | 50.02 px, 0.34 s later | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| resize-none-pct-r30-root-z100 | 216.63 px, 0.33 s later | 0 / 0 / 0 |

- [x] **Verdicts repeat.** 24 cases covering every gesture, both nestings, all zooms, 0 and 30deg and every GSAP mode, run 3 times on unchanged Studio:
  - the accuracy verdicts (tracking, press, drop, reload, undo) are identical in 24/24;
  - every value repeats to 0.01 px;
  - the large errors are now attributed consistently. For example, the 50-222 px no-GSAP move and resize errors are drop in every run and never reload, and reload equals the commit.
  - Smoothness verdicts repeat in 10/24. The control dropped 0 frames in 70 of 72 runs, while the cases dropped 0 to 9 with work p95 of 3.6 to 9.3 ms. So what varies is Studio's drag, not the machine.
- [x] **Undo waits hold under load.** I ran the 7 most race-prone cases 6 times each, at load average 25 to 44 on 32 cores. This includes crop-hold-pct-r0-nested-z50, which had failed undo and reload in 1 of 6 runs with the old fixed 4 s wait. Every accuracy verdict was identical in all 6 runs (7/7), with no undo timeouts. Smoothness verdicts agreed in 5/7.

| Case | Accuracy failures (6 of 6 runs) |
|---|---|
| crop-hold-pct-r0-nested-z50 | none |
| crop-tween-center-r30-root-z50 | undo (199.03 px) |
| move-none-center-r0-nested-z100 | tracking, drop (108.19 px) |
| move-none-pct-r30-nested-z50 | tracking, drop (108.22 px) |
| move-none-px-r0-root-z100 | tracking, drop (50.02 px) |
| resize-none-pct-r30-root-z100 | tracking, drop (216.63 px); render 110.04 px with #4764 |
| rotate-none-px-r0-root-z100 | none |

- [x] **Every metric catches an injected error** (clean values from the same cases):

| Injection | Metric | Clean | Injected |
|---|---|---|---|
| element shifted 3 px on pointerdown | press jump | 0.00 | 3.00, 3.02 |
| move commit +3 px (Studio build) | drop | 0.00 | 3.02 |
| every other pointer move dropped | tracking | 0.74 | 6.13 |
| preview shifted 3 px after reload | reload | 0.00 | 3.02 |
| undo writes one extra byte (server build) | undo bytes | identical | differ |
| 40 ms main-thread stall per pointer move | smoothness | control 0 dropped | 19-20 dropped vs control 0; work p95 43-45 ms |
| undo's history request aborted, so its write never lands | undo | lands, redo tested | `undoTimeout: "undo"`; undo fails; redo not sent; drop and reload unaffected; no harness error |
| preview jiggles 1 px every 200 ms after the gesture | settle | settled | commit, undo and redo flagged unsettled; drop, reload and undo fail; no harness error |

- [x] oxlint, oxfmt and `fallow audit --base origin/main` pass. The comment ratchet counts only `packages/*/src`, so I checked these comments by hand: none is over 120 chars and none runs 4+ lines.
- [ ] Unit tests added/updated. None: the benchmark itself is the test, and the injections above prove it.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

**Baseline on main 14e87005d** (committed `baseline.json`). One full run with the settle fix, press jump and the smoothness control. The CLI was built from that main commit, all 660 cases ran with 4 jobs on a 32-core machine, and there were 0 harness errors and 0 unsettled snapshots. That machine now owns the baseline, and every later comparison runs there.
- 70/660 pass every check.
- 314/660 pass everything except smoothness.
- Undo and redo were byte-identical in every case.

| Metric | Pass | Worst | Worst case |
|---|---|---|---|
| tracking | 466 | 1.0 | resize-none-pct-r0-nested-z50 |
| press jump | 660 | 0 | - |
| drop | 503 | 222.6 | resize-none-pct-r0-root-z50 |
| reload | 636 | 120.4 | resize-hold-pct-r0-root-z100 |
| undo | 591 | 199.0 | crop-tween-center-r30-root-z50 |
| smoothness | 131 | 16 frames over the control | resize-tween-center-r0-root-z100 |

Smoothness on this run is not a clean reference. Other jobs shared the machine, and the load average rose from 11 to 47 on 32 cores. The blank-page control itself dropped a median of 6 frames per case (the cases dropped a median of 10). Judge smoothness from a run on a quiet machine.

What the failures are:
- Every tracking failure is at most 1 px: Studio rounds the live drag position and size to whole composition px.
- The large drop errors are no-GSAP moves and resizes, and resizes of %-translated elements: the commit lands the element somewhere other than where it was dropped.
- The undo worst is the stylesheet `translate` applied again on top of GSAP's folded x/y after an undo.

## Before

There was no benchmark. This is one of its generated case projects in Studio before any gesture, which is where every case starts.

![A generated case project in Studio before any gesture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2596e86d-54f0-4107-b8f2-8d79ded706d4)

## After

The baseline table from the earlier full run on main made before the settle fix (the current numbers are in the table above), then two of the worst cases as the bench captured them: a resize that jumped 222.6 px on release, and a crop whose undo left the element displaced.

![Edit accuracy baseline table on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07b88cf1-95c8-4735-bfb9-9388f0581198)

![Resize that jumped 222.6 px on release](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c3a7c42-551f-4644-81aa-6b6dd345bb2c)

![Crop undo that left the element displaced](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a7f953d-2885-488f-97d7-e07549ced40b)

title: fix(parsers): moving a clip on the timeline moves its inner animations too
body:
## What

Moving or stretching a clip on the Studio timeline now carries every animation aimed at things inside that clip, not only the ones aimed at the clip itself. Animations on elements outside the clip are never rewritten.

## Why

The timeline's move and retime write-back (`shift-positions` / `scale-positions`) matched tweens by an exact string compare against the clip's `#id`. A scene that animates its own children (`"#scene h1"`, `"#child"`, a class used only inside the scene, a list of targets) kept those animations at their old times, so after a drag the scene appeared with its title already landed and its boxes already moved.

## Related work

Standalone fix; not part of the placement-model work.

## How

- One rule, in `@hyperframes/parsers` (`clipTweenMatcher`): a tween moves with the clip when its selector is the clip's own selector, or when its full target set is the clip or sits inside it, with no nearer timed (`data-start`) clip of its own. The acorn writer, the recast writer and the SDK's `setTiming` all use it, so there is one owner. `clipQueryRoot` (same file) owns where the clips are looked up: the `<template>` that holds the GSAP script, else the document, because linkedom keeps a template's children under the template where document queries do not reach them. The studio-server route and the SDK both use it. The SDK passes the exact selectors it matched before (`#id`, `[data-hf-id]` in both quote styles) as the clip's own selectors, so nothing it moved before is lost.
- **Tweens with no written time stay unwritten.** A chained tween (`tl.from(b, …)` with no position) follows the tween before it. `hasExplicitTime` (same file) decides this for all four writer loops and for the SDK: a move leaves such a tween alone, and a stretch scales its duration but never pins a position on it.
- **A tween whose targets are only partly known is never carried.** Both parsers now mark an array target with a part they cannot resolve (`["#scene h1", window.logo]`) with `hasPartialSelector`, and the matcher refuses it. The tween stays visible in the timeline and the property panel. This check runs before the own-selector match, so `["#scene", window.logo]` does not move the logo either.
- **A tween whose targets are partly inside and partly outside the clip does not move**, so moving one clip never rewrites anything outside it (chained tweens after it can still start later; see Known limits). Splitting such a tween in two would rewrite user code, so it is left out.
- **A tween aimed inside a nested timed clip belongs to that nested clip**: moving the parent leaves it alone, since the nested clip's own `data-start` is not moved either. A group move of a parent and its nested clip therefore shifts each tween once.
- Selectors that are not valid CSS (proxy and dwell labels) never match the DOM, so they only move on an exact match, as before.
- **Each clip timing edit syncs its animations once.** When Studio's SDK timing write commits (a composition opened on its own), the SDK has already moved the tweens, so Studio no longer also posts the server `shift-positions` / `scale-positions` for that edit. The committed result now carries the bytes before and after, and `sdkTimingGsapSync` reports a sync only when the timeline script in those bytes actually changed (it walks the parsed bytes with the same composition walker the SDK uses, so a script inside a `<template>` counts); otherwise the server pass runs. The single-clip move and resize and the group move and resize all read it. `findTimelineScript` (in the acorn parser) is now the one rule for which script holds a file's timeline, used by the SDK and the server, so a `gsap.config` script placed first no longer makes the SDK sync a different script than the server. With no SDK session (the master view) or a declined SDK write, the server pass stays the one sync. Before this, a +2s move in such a composition landed the clip's tweens at +4s, and the following stretch scaled from the wrong start.

## Known limits

- **An animation outside the clip that is chained right after the moved content (no written time) moves with the clip.** GSAP starts a chained tween where the timeline ends at that point, so when the clip's content moves later or gets longer, the chained outside tween follows it. Example: a CTA chained after a scene plays at 5.5s; stretch the scene from 4s to 7s and it plays at 7s. Holding it in place needs the live timeline's real start times and is a follow-up.
- Targets are resolved against the whole page, so a scoped query (`scene.querySelectorAll(".x")`) reads as the global `.x` and stays put when `.x` also exists outside.
- Only elements present in the file are seen; elements a script creates later are not.
- A group move of sibling clips does not move a tween whose targets span two of the moved clips (each clip sees mixed targets).
- A clip with no `data-start` attribute does not carry its descendants on its first move (the move writes the attribute).
- Relative positions and labels (`"<"`, `"+=1"`, `"intro"`) are skipped, for descendants as for the clip's own tweens.

## Test plan

- [x] `gsapWriter.parity.test.ts`, both writers, shift and scale on one composition: descendant selector, child id, list target and inside-only class move; an outside element, a class spanning inside and outside, a tween inside a nested timed clip, a chained tween (keeps no position; its duration scales) and an array with an unresolvable part stay.
- [x] Route test in `files.test.ts`: `shift-positions` then `scale-positions` on a template-wrapped composition move `#card h1` and `#line`, and leave `#side` and `#dot`, which sits in a nested timed clip.
- [x] SDK `mutate.gsap.test.ts`: `setTiming` on a scene carries `#scene h1`, and leaves a chained tween, a partly known array and an outside element alone, and leaves an outside tween chained after the scene's content unwritten (the known limit). A second test moves a clip in a `<template>`-wrapped composition and carries its `[data-hf-id]` tween and `#card h1`.
- [x] Parity rows added for an outside tween chained after carried ones (stays chained, and a row per writer pins that it then starts at 5.5 instead of 3.5, the known limit), `["#scene", window.logo]` (stays), and a clip without `data-start` whose tween targets it through a class (moves).
- [x] A `<template>` file with a `gsap.config` script before the timeline script: an SDK move then stretch lands each tween once (Studio test), and SDK `setTiming` syncs the timeline script there (SDK test). Before, the SDK moved no tween and the stretch then scaled from the new start.
- [x] Studio `useTimelineEditing.test.tsx`: a move, a resize and a group move in a sub-composition, each through the SDK and through the server (no SDK session), read the final file bytes from an in-memory project whose GSAP route runs the real server writer. Before the Studio fix the three SDK cases fail with doubled times (`#scene` at 5 instead of 3, `#scene h1` at 5.5, durations 4 instead of 2); the server cases pass before and after. The three older tests that expected a server post after an SDK commit are replaced by these.
- [x] Each rule was broken on purpose and a test caught it: counting implicit positions as written fails the 4 parity cases and 2 SDK tests; carrying partly known targets fails the 4 parity cases and the SDK test; letting any ancestor clip own a tween (instead of the nearest) fails the 4 parity cases and the route test; with the earlier follower pins still in, the 6 parity cases and the SDK test that pin the known limit fail; querying the SDK's document instead of the script's template fails the template SDK test; checking partial targets after the own-selector match fails the 4 parity cases; dropping the "target is the clip" branch fails the 2 new parity cases. Reading only document-level scripts in the sync check (no descent into the `<template>`) fails the template config-script Studio test.
- [x] Manual walk in the built Studio (scene 1s to 5s, a chained line after the title, a nested timed clip, a class used inside and outside, an outside box): dragging the scene to 3s moved its own tween and the title to 3 and left the chained line unwritten; stretching it to 7s scaled those durations by 1.75, and the chained line kept no position (it plays at 4.75, right after the title); the nested clip's tween, the shared class and the outside box kept their times. Moving the nested clip alone moved only its tween. Nothing outside the scene got a written position.
- [x] Walk in the built Studio with the composition opened on its own: dragging the scene +2s wrote each tween once (own tween and title at 3, never 5) with no server GSAP post; the stretch and the nested move then scaled and moved from those values. The master view still syncs through the server with the same numbers.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Main, just after dragging the scene 2s later, at 3.5s: the scene has just appeared, but its title has already landed and the gold box has already moved.

![Main after the drag, at 3.5s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc6662b0-542a-45f7-b962-24c522a6dc96)

Main after the stretch, at 4s: same, the inner animations still sit at their original times.

![Main after the stretch, at 4s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2bb7b14-d5fc-486a-b887-bd3b8a3fa392)

## After

This branch, same drag, at 3.5s: the title is sliding in and the gold box waits for its cue. After stretching the scene to 6s and reloading, at 4s and 5.5s, the inner animations play at their scaled times.

![Branch after the drag, at 3.5s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b137a740-0e04-4fc3-9ae3-1272c73eb7d6)

![Branch after the stretch, reloaded, at 4s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09d6851d-9ccc-43e9-91bf-2306ed1b192d)

![Branch after the stretch, reloaded, at 5.5s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01be48f0-4fee-441f-9f03-a2e345603a80)
- [x] Walks of the reviewer's fixtures in the built Studio (the sub-composition opened on its own, plain and with a `gsap.config` script first; the single-file master view, plain and config first), each start re-checked in real GSAP from the saved file: after the +2s move, the scene's timed tweens sit at 3 and the outside `#cta` still plays at 5.5 and the chained outside `#side` goes from 3 to 5. After the +3s stretch, the chained outside `#side` and `#cta` move to 6.5 and 7, as the known limit says. Each edit wrote the animations once, and nothing outside the scene got a written position.
