title: test(studio): measure render drift against a producer frame in the edit accuracy bench
body:
## What

Adds render drift to the edit accuracy benchmark, its fifth metric. After each case's edit and a fresh Studio load, the producer renders the saved file at the same playhead, and the benchmark compares where the element lands in that frame with where the reloaded preview shows it. `baseline.json` gains the render column. It comes from the same full run on main 14e87005d as #4760's baseline: render passes 618/660.

Stacked on the edit accuracy benchmark PR (#4760); review that one first.

## Why

A preview can show one thing while the export shows another. The other metrics only look at Studio, so they cannot catch a case where the preview and the rendered video disagree about the same file.

## Related work

Refs #4760 (the benchmark this extends). The CI gate follows in its own PR.

## How

- The producer frame comes from the engine's own capture session (`createCaptureSession` + `captureFrameToBuffer`), the path `scripts/preview-capture.ts` uses. It runs in the same pinned headless shell Studio is driven in, with JPEG output. PNG is the engine's transparent mode.
- The element's box is found by its flat fixture colour over the whole frame:
  - coverage per pixel comes from luminance, which JPEG keeps at full resolution;
  - area moments give the centre and both sides, corrected by 1/12 px² for pixel coverage;
  - so a rotated or cropped rectangle is measured the same way as an axis-aligned one.
- The reloaded preview is measured once it has held still for 1 s, as every snapshot in #4760 is. If the reload never settles, render fails with it, flagged `unsettled`.
- If the producer cannot render the case, only render fails: `render` is null and `renderError` holds the message. The case's other metrics still count, and the table counts these cases.
- Rotated elements compare axis-aligned boxes. The producer page's DOM rect is recorded as a diagnostic only, because it ignores `clip-path`.
- A composition with no GSAP never registers a timeline, so the capture session would wait its full 45 s `playerReadyTimeout`. The bench passes 10 s instead. The frame is identical: the measured box matches to every printed digit.

## Test plan

title: test(studio): gate edit accuracy in CI against the base branch baseline
body:
## What

A CI gate for the edit accuracy benchmark. On every pull request that touches the manual-edit path, the full grid runs in 8 shards against the built CLI, and one gate job compares the result with the base branch's `baseline.json`. It posts a single sticky comment, and it fails the check when accuracy falls.

Stacked on the render drift PR (#4764), which is stacked on the benchmark (#4760).

## Why

The benchmark only protects the score if a PR cannot quietly lower it. This makes "every later edit PR must not lower the score" a required check rather than a convention.

## Related work

Refs #4760 and #4764.

## How

**Jobs (`ci.yml`)**
- A new change filter, `edit_accuracy`, covers only the edit path: the Studio editor, NLE, hooks, utils, player and webmcp sources; studio-server, core and the CLI server sources; the bench itself; `bun.lock`; and `ci.yml`.
- The existing Build job already builds the full CLI; it now uploads `packages/cli/dist` for the shards (kept for one day).
- `Studio: edit accuracy (i/8)`:
  - `prepare-ffmpeg-bin` before the install;
  - the shared CLI;
  - `hyperframes browser ensure`, so Studio and the producer run in the engine's pinned headless shell;
  - `--grid full --shard i/8 --jobs 2`.
  - Any case whose verdict differs from the base branch, in either direction, is re-run twice in the same job (`ratchet.mjs flipped`).
- `Studio: edit accuracy gate`:
  - merges every run from every shard;
  - posts the sticky comment through the same action the fallow audit uses, with its own header;
  - uploads the report plus a `baseline.json` built from the first run of each shard, ready to commit when cases newly pass.

**The rule (`ratchet.mjs`).** One slow or noisy run must not fail a PR, and a case that flips must never pass unnoticed.
- The same 2-of-3 rule applies both ways:
  - a case that passes on the base branch fails the gate only if it fails 2 of its 3 runs;
  - a case that fails on the base branch counts as newly passing, and must be banked, only if it passes 2 of its 3 runs.
- Any case whose runs disagree is listed as **unstable**, with the values each run saw. It is never passed silently.
- An unsettled snapshot or a render error fails the case like any failed metric.
- A base `baseline.json` that does not parse fails the job. CI writes an empty baseline only when the base branch has none.
- The gate also fails when:
  - the passing count falls below the base branch's;
  - a newly passing case is not banked in `baseline.json`;
  - `baseline.json` marks as passing a case that fails here.
- "Passing" means tracking, press jump, drop, reload and render ≤ 0.5 px, byte-identical undo and redo, and no snapshot left unsettled. Smoothness is reported, not gated.

**Rounding.** `baseline.json` stores values rounded up to 0.01 (a change on #4760 and #4764), so a stored value is within 0.5 px exactly when the measured one is. Rounding to nearest had read seven 0.502 px results as passes.

**One source of truth.** `report.mjs` now exports `entry()`, the per-case shape `baseline.json` holds, and the gate reads the same projection. Regenerating the baseline through `entry()` from the main run's results reproduces the committed `baseline.json` byte for byte. The gate run against that baseline with the same results reports 314 passing on both sides and passes.

## Test plan

- [x] `ratchet.test.mjs` (9 tests, Vitest):
  - 2-of-3 regression, unstable listing, unbanked, overclaimed, count drop, smoothness ignored;
  - a lucky single pass of a base-failing case is re-run, listed as unstable and not required to be banked, while a 2-of-3 pass is required to be banked. Limiting `flipped` to regressions again fails the test;
  - press jump over the limit and an unsettled snapshot fail, and a nudge's null press jump passes. Dropping either check from `accurate()` fails the test;
  - non-vacuous: changing the 2-of-3 rule to "any failure" fails the 1-of-3 test.
- [x] Gate against the full-run results on main (before the settle fix) with its own baseline: 304 passing on both sides (matching the table's "all but smoothness"), so the gate passes.
- [x] Dry run of the shard and gate steps on real cases, with a base that marks two cases as passing:
  - the one that really fails (a 0.74 px tracking error) was re-run twice and confirmed;
  - the gate failed with the comment below;
  - the re-runs stayed out of the banked baseline.
- [x] `actionlint` on `ci.yml`, oxlint, oxfmt, `fallow audit --base origin/main` and the comment ratchet pass.
- [ ] The first real CI run on this PR. Its shard timing on GitHub runners is not measured yet. An 8-core dev machine ran 660 cases in 44 min with 4 jobs, before the settle fix added a few seconds per case.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

## Before

Without a gate, the benchmark only produced a table that nobody had to act on:

![The benchmark table with no gate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0a0ac084-c3db-4e99-90dc-8b83c0d6bf87)

## After

The gate's comment from the dry run: a case that passes on the base branch, failed 3 of 3 runs here, and fails the check.

![Edit accuracy gate comment from the dry run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8da85d6b-c296-4fef-bc87-663edbbccef7)

title: fix(studio): keep sub-pixel position and angle while dragging and on drop
body:
## What

Moving or rotating an element in Studio no longer snaps it to whole pixels (or a tenth of a degree). During the drag the box follows the pointer exactly, and the file saves the same fractional value the preview showed, to three decimals. A resized box's width and height stay on whole pixels, and the resize anchor now lands within 0.3 px of the pointer instead of up to 0.9 px.

## Why

Every writer rounded to whole composition pixels: the live drag, the saved offset, the saved size, the GSAP `x`/`y` and width/height commits, and the rotation angle. So the grabbed point drifted up to 1 px from the pointer while dragging (up to 0.9 px on a corner resize), and at 50% zoom the element visibly stepped instead of gliding.

## How

Position and angle: every `Math.round` in the drag and commit paths is replaced by the existing `roundTo3` helper, so draft and commit write the same value:

- `draggedGsapPosition`: GSAP `x`/`y` from a drag.
- `manualEditsDom`: Studio's offset and size variables, flex basis and rotation.
- `elementPositionOffset`: left/top for elements without GSAP.
- `gsapDragCommit` and `gsapResizeIntercept`: static and keyframed size, and the scale-finalize position.
- `gsapRuntimeBridge`: the committed rotation angle.

`roundAngle` and `roundRotationAngle` are deleted.

Box sizes: these stay on whole pixels through one helper, `roundToLayoutPx`, in the draft and the commit alike. GSAP turns a `-50%` translate into `xPercent`/`yPercent` by comparing it with the element's integer `offsetWidth`/`offsetHeight`. With a fractional height (226.576px, `offsetHeight` 227), `round(227 / 2)` is not `round(113.288)`. GSAP then missed the centring, and the keyframe commit saved `"0%": { x: 0.07, y: -113.281 }`: a centred element sat 113 px off at t=0. A test pins whole-px sizes.

## Edit accuracy score

The full grid (660 cases) of the edit accuracy bench, on the built CLI Studio with this PR merged onto main 14e87005d, against the baseline committed on main:

| Metric | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| tracking | 466/660 | 660/660 |
| drop | 503/660 | 505/660 |
| reload | 636/660 | 631/660 * |
| undo | 591/660 | 585/660 * |
| all but smoothness | 314/660 | 430/660 |

\* The full run was taken on a loaded machine. Each of the 6 cases below main's count was run twice more and passed both times (2 of 3), so they are load flakes, not regressions: four crops in a nested composition at 200% zoom, one nudge on an xPercent tween in a nested composition, and one resize of a px element at 50% zoom.

- For elements without GSAP (180 cases), tracking goes from 122 to 180, and move passes every check but smoothness in 6 of 36 cases, up from 0.
- Render is 618/660; main's baseline has no render column.
- Smoothness isn't compared here, because the machine was loaded; it's tracked separately.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for sub-pixel values. With this PR's tests on main's source, 6 of them fail, one per position or angle rounding site:
  - `manualOffsetDrag`: the drag draft and commit land at the exact fractional position;
  - `manualEdits`: an offset of 14.25px, and rotations of 24.247° and -12.26°;
  - `DomEditOverlay`: a rotation angle of 1.432;
  - `gsapRuntimeBridge`: a committed rotation of 75.25;
  - `useGsapAwareEditing`: the anchored resize settles at (70.2, 54.6).
  - `manualEdits` and `gsapDragCommit`: resized box sizes stay whole (240px and 136px; 300 × 200). These fail on a build that writes fractional sizes.
- [x] Studio `components/editor` and `hooks` suites: 2643 passed, 0 failed. Studio `tsc --noEmit` exits 0.
- [ ] Full edit accuracy grid, with no case that passes on main failing here
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main, a slow drag at 50% zoom moves the box (yellow dots) in whole composition pixels, so it holds still for three frames and then jumps past the pointer (blue line).

![Before: the box steps in whole composition pixels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47b87900-c10b-4aa0-91e7-58617e5944be)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8875c133-2538-4cda-b51c-397ce51ab448

## After

With this change, the same drag keeps the box on the pointer every frame.

![After: the box follows the pointer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0ca69d1-d091-4380-9a60-e3042b8fdfca)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17d40974-f0a2-4c5e-a14b-4974ae06625c

title: fix(cli): recapture snapshot composites after video injection
body:
## What

Recapture page-side VFX composites after decoded video frames have been injected into a snapshot.

## Why

A snapshot seeks and waits for the VFX preview capture before injecting decoded FFmpeg frames. The injected overlay updates the DOM, but the VFX output canvas still holds its earlier capture of the native video. Under load that capture can contain frame zero.

## Related work

Fixes #4762. The engine already runs a post-injection page-composite protocol; this brings snapshot capture into line with it.

## How

After injecting frames and syncing visibility, run the existing prepare → paint → resolve protocol. A one-pixel screenshot makes the updated subtree's paint records available before VFX captures them. Pages without a page compositor skip the extra screenshot. This adds no sleep or native-video decode heuristic.

## Size

Small on purpose: one extra prepare, paint and resolve pass after video injection in the snapshot path, plus two tests. The engine already does the same step, so nothing else needs to change.

## Test plan

- `bun run lint` passed.
- `bun run format:check` passed.
- Existing snapshot and captureCompositionFrame suites: 72 tests passed.
- `bun run --filter @hyperframes/cli typecheck` passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed: core/studio/scripts typecheck, lint/format, tracked artifacts, and fallow audit (no newly introduced findings).
- The initial whole-workspace typecheck failed on missing dependencies in the reused checkout (`acorn`, `sharp`, `@puppeteer/browsers`, `dockview-react`, `@base-ui/react`). Dependencies were then refreshed; the CLI typecheck above is the subsequent scoped check.
- The issue's exact synthetic-bar reproduction was attempted, but local Chrome failed to launch (Code: null, empty stderr), so this does not claim a local under-load pixel reproduction.

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): name a repeated section by its authored id in the Design panel
body:
## What

When a film holds two instances of one section, Studio now names each by the section's name ("Benefit Fresh"), not by its runtime instance id ("Benefit Fresh Hf1"). That covers the Design panel, the Layers panel, the on-canvas selection label, "Copy element info" and the WebMCP tools' output, plus the timeline when it reads the page directly.

## Why

At load, the runtime gives each instance of a repeated sub-composition a unique `data-composition-id` (`benefit-fresh__hf1`, `benefit-fresh__hf2`) and keeps the authored one in `data-hf-original-composition-id`. `buildElementLabel` read the unique id, and so did the label of `parseTimelineFromDOM`, the timeline's fallback when the runtime sends no clip list, for a host with no `id` of its own. The same file already prefers the authored id when it resolves a composition's source; the label did not.

To reproduce on main: author two hosts with the same `data-composition-id` and `data-composition-src`, open the film in Studio, and select one.

#4756 fixes the same leak in the runtime's clip list, which the timeline normally reads; this PR covers the rest of Studio.

## How

- `packages/studio/src/components/editor/domEditingDom.ts` `buildElementLabel`: reads `data-hf-original-composition-id` first, then `data-composition-id`. It names elements for the selection (`domEditingLayers.ts`) and the layer walk (`domEditLayerWalkCache.ts`).
- `packages/studio/src/player/lib/timelineDOM.ts` `parseTimelineFromDOM`: the label reads the authored id after `el.id`. The row's id still uses the runtime id, so two instances stay two rows.
- Two copies of a section now read the same in the Layers panel, where "Hf1" and "Hf2" used to tell them apart. Nothing uses the label to tell elements apart: each instance keeps its own selector (`[data-composition-id="...__hf1"]`), and layer rows are keyed by that.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## What I measured

On a Linux box:
- `domEditing.test.ts` has one new test: an instance renamed by the runtime is labelled "Benefit Fresh". It fails without the fix, reading "Benefit Fresh Hf2".
- `timelineDOM.test.ts` has one new test: two id-less instances both read "card" and stay two rows. It fails without the fix, reading "card__hf1" and "card__hf2".
- The label's callers' tests (domEditing, LayersPanel, domEditLayerWalkCache, domEditingLayers, motionPathSelection): 103 of 103 pass.
- `timelineDOM`, `useTimelinePlayer`, `timelineIframeHelpers` and `domEditing` tests: 141 of 141 pass.
- Typecheck, lint, format, the comment checks and the fallow audit are clean.
- In Studio (`vite` dev server, headless Chromium) on a fixture film with two instances of one section: selecting the first shows "Benefit Fresh Hf1" in the Design panel on main, and "Benefit Fresh" with this change.

## What I did NOT exercise

- No run on macOS or Windows.
- The timeline labels in the images still read Hf1 and Hf2: that is fixed separately in #4756.

## Before

Selecting the first instance: the Design panel reads "Benefit Fresh Hf1".

![Before: the Design panel reads Benefit Fresh Hf1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60e340c5-eb2b-451d-98e4-98a6aa9425f7)

## After

The same selection reads "Benefit Fresh".

![After: the Design panel reads Benefit Fresh](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bac31bfa-5b5b-40c9-a9d4-6444540fa492)

title: perf(studio): stop sorting the font list while the font picker is closed
body:
## What

The font field in the design panel builds its list of font options only while its dropdown is open.

## Why

`FontFamilyField` rebuilt and sorted the full option list (about 1.7k families: document, imported, Google, local, system) on mount and whenever the font lists or the current font changed, even while the dropdown was closed and nothing read the list. The sort comparator scans the common-font list twice per comparison, so each rebuild costs several milliseconds.

Those renders land inside gestures. The field fetches the Google font list on mount, and on a selection followed by a drag or an arrow-key nudge, that response arrives 20-50 ms into the gesture. That puts one 7-10 ms main-thread task in a single frame. A nudge has about 6 frames, so that one frame is the p95 the edit accuracy bench scores (7.8 and 8.6 ms of main-thread work on the `nudge-*-pct-r0-root-z100` cases).

## Related work

Refs #4760 (edit accuracy bench; this PR stacks on it).

## How

`options` returns an empty list while the dropdown is closed and depends on `open`. Every reader of `options` and `filteredOptions` sits inside the open dropdown (the list and the search input's key handling), so a closed field behaves exactly as before. Opening the dropdown builds the list once, as it did.

Deleted: building and sorting the font list while the font field is closed.
Net lines: +44 (source +1, test +43).

## Smoothness

Edit accuracy bench, `pr` grid (110 cases, root, 100% zoom), `--jobs 1`, the fixed bench with its blank-page control, all four runs back to back on one shared 32-core machine. "main" is this PR's base, run twice. Pass = no more dropped frames (over 25 ms) than the control, and main-thread CPU work at or under 8 ms per frame at p95.

| gesture | main (load 29) | main again (load 20) | #4769 (load 35) | #4770 (load 27) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| crop: pass / work p95 median | 2 / 5.94 ms | 12 / 5.44 ms | 2 / 5.78 ms | 6 / 5.70 ms |
| move | 5 / 7.41 ms | 8 / 7.16 ms | 1 / 7.47 ms | 1 / 7.56 ms |
| nudge | 7 / 9.41 ms | 16 / 6.42 ms | 6 / 7.69 ms | 6 / 8.07 ms |
| resize | 1 / 8.04 ms | 4 / 8.18 ms | 1 / 8.79 ms | 4 / 8.17 ms |
| rotate | 12 / 4.93 ms | 17 / 4.38 ms | 11 / 5.09 ms | 12 / 4.89 ms |

The two runs of the same main build differ more than either PR: paired per case, the second main run has nudge work p95 lower by a median of 2.52 ms, and its pass counts rise with the machine's load falling. So this bench, on a shared machine at this load, cannot resolve either PR's frame effect in either direction. Tracking is identical on every case in all four runs, so neither PR moves a geometry metric the bench measures during the drag (its drop, reload and undo verdicts are not quoted here).

The deterministic evidence for this PR is the unit test (the sort count) and the gesture-window CPU profile below.

## Before

CPU profile of the gesture window on main: the font field renders inside the gesture and sorts the font list.

![Before: FontFamilyField up to 8.0 ms and sortFontOptions up to 3.8 ms inside a gesture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2929443e-56fb-4dac-9f0c-d87765a227a1)

## After

With this PR: the font field costs at most 0.2 ms in the same window and never sorts.

![After: FontFamilyField at most 0.2 ms, sortFontOptions never runs](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94c8ba24-5b2c-418c-bdd7-387da8cfde5b)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test: `propertyPanelFont.test.tsx` counts `sortFontOptions` calls. None while the dropdown is closed, through a font-list response and a value change. Exactly one on open, and the fetched family is listed. It fails with main's `propertyPanelFont.tsx`. Every test in the file stubs the font APIs and uses families that are on no Google list, so none reaches the network, and the head and body are cleared after each. 38/38 pass with `PropertyPanel.test.ts(x)`.

title: fix(studio): save moves in GSAP-free files without a 2 s wait for a warm parse
body:
## What

A move, resize or nudge in a composition with no GSAP tweens saves right away instead of about 2 s later.

## Why

Before saving a move, Studio asks the GSAP parse endpoint which tweens own the element. `useGsapAnimationFetchFallback` treated a parse with zero animations as a "cold parse" (the endpoint reachable but not warm yet) and retried it 5 times, 120 ms apart. The commit path awaits that lookup more than once (the ownership preflight, then the drag intercept's own fallback fetch), so in a GSAP-free file every drop and nudge commit waited about 2 s before the file was written, and a single edit sent about 27 parse requests.

A cold parse cannot happen. The endpoint reads and parses the file on every request (`GET /projects/:id/gsap-animations/*`, synchronous `readFileSync` + parse, no cache), and it did the same when the retry was added. Studio's project-file saves replace the file atomically (temp file + rename). Any writer that does not is a separate bug, and a fixed wait on zero animations would not be a correct guard for it anyway. So zero animations is a definitive answer. Three readers acted on it: the commit fallback retried it, the element tween cache (`useGsapTweenCache`) re-fetched it 800 ms later as a "cold-load race", and `useCommitPreflightCapabilities` already treated it as final. All three now follow that one rule.

## Related work

Refs #4760 (edit accuracy bench; this PR stacks on it).

## How

The `cold` outcome and its retry budget are deleted. `selectElementAnimationsOrRetry` returns `resolved` for any parse, including an empty one, and `fetch-error` only when the fetch failed. A failed fetch still gets its one short retry.

Deleted: the `cold` outcome, its 5 x 120 ms retry budget and the loop branch that waited it out; the tween cache's 800 ms re-fetch after an empty parse; and a branch in `useCommitPreflightCapabilities` that could no longer run.
Net lines: +7 (source -56, test +63).

## Drop to saved file

Gesture end to the saved file changing on disk (5 ms polling), no-GSAP fixture from the edit accuracy bench, 3 runs each, measured at this PR's first commit. These are attribution runs outside the suite lock on a shared Linux runner at load about 50. The capture below repeats it at the same commit: 2001 ms on main, 50 ms with this PR.

| case | before (ms) | after (ms) | parse requests per case, before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| move-none-px-r0-root-z100 | 1994 / 2071 / 2002 | 47 / 81 / 42 | 27 / 28 / 27 → 12 / 12 / 13 |
| nudge-none-px-r0-root-z100 (includes the 400 ms nudge debounce) | 2324 / 2309 / 2327 | 419 / 512 / 346 | 28 / 27 / 26 → 12 / 12 / 10 |

## Smoothness

Edit accuracy bench, `pr` grid (110 cases, root, 100% zoom), `--jobs 1`, the fixed bench with its blank-page control, all four runs back to back on one shared 32-core machine. "main" is this PR's base, run twice. Pass = no more dropped frames (over 25 ms) than the control, and main-thread CPU work at or under 8 ms per frame at p95.

| gesture | main (load 29) | main again (load 20) | #4769 (load 35) | #4770 (load 27) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| crop: pass / work p95 median | 2 / 5.94 ms | 12 / 5.44 ms | 2 / 5.78 ms | 6 / 5.70 ms |
| move | 5 / 7.41 ms | 8 / 7.16 ms | 1 / 7.47 ms | 1 / 7.56 ms |
| nudge | 7 / 9.41 ms | 16 / 6.42 ms | 6 / 7.69 ms | 6 / 8.07 ms |
| resize | 1 / 8.04 ms | 4 / 8.18 ms | 1 / 8.79 ms | 4 / 8.17 ms |
| rotate | 12 / 4.93 ms | 17 / 4.38 ms | 11 / 5.09 ms | 12 / 4.89 ms |

The two runs of the same main build differ more than either PR: paired per case, the second main run has nudge work p95 lower by a median of 2.52 ms, and its pass counts rise with the machine's load falling. So this bench, on a shared machine at this load, cannot resolve either PR's frame effect in either direction. Tracking is identical on every case in all four runs, so neither PR moves a geometry metric the bench measures during the drag (its drop, reload and undo verdicts are not quoted here).

This PR's user-visible effect is the save latency above, which the bench does not score.

## Before

No-GSAP move on main. The overlay starts at the drop and turns green when the file changes on disk: saved 2001 ms after the drop.

![Before: saved to disk 2001 ms after drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/89d609f2-3205-428e-8ab5-88178d41cfcb)

[before-move-save-timer.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b90dac8-57df-4a0d-baf7-15ca742c5de5)

The same move with this PR: saved 50 ms after the drop.

![After: saved to disk 50 ms after drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/802c42f5-232d-4345-8a79-ae62384fe9c5)

[after-move-save-timer.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a2d32e7-5508-41dd-a397-3ac83e8e3a69)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: 74/74 pass across `useGsapAnimationFetchFallback`, `useGsapTweenCache` (both files), `gsapRuntimeBridge`, `useGsapAwareEditing` and `commitPreflightHandles`. With the three source files reverted to main, the three new tests fail: an empty parse resolves to `[]`, a GSAP-free file is answered with one parse request and no retries, and the tween cache reads a GSAP-free file once. The fourth new test (a failed fetch is retried once, then reports no animation) also passes on main; it stays because this PR rewrote that retry loop, and it pins the failed-fetch branch the rewrite kept.

title: fix(studio): undo re-reads elements GSAP parsed so crop undo lands exactly
body:
## What

**Merge together with #4778.** On its own this PR sends style-only undos through the soft reload, which on this branch still restarts other animated values (a width tween) from their live mid-tween state, so they drift on each undo or redo. #4778 fixes that; merging this without it makes the drift reachable from a crop undo.

One behaviour change against main: in a file with two or more GSAP scripts, an undo that syncs an element GSAP parsed reloads the preview, where main stays in place (see Known limits).

After one undo of a crop (or any style-only edit) on an element GSAP animates, the element now lands exactly where it was before the gesture. Before this change it came back up to 199 px away, often rotated twice.

## Why

A style-only undo copied the file's attributes onto the live element. That removed the inline `translate: none` / `rotate: none` masks GSAP writes when it folds a stylesheet translate or rotate into its own x/y and rotation, while GSAP's cache still held the folded values. So the stylesheet transform applied again on top of GSAP's. A fresh load of the same file never shows that, because GSAP parses the element from scratch.

Repro: an element placed with a stylesheet `translate: -50% -50%` and a `tl.to(x, y)` tween. Crop its right edge, then undo. The box jumps by the translate, and by the rotation when it has one.

## Related work

Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark in #4760 (not part of this PR). Builds on #4740, which restores authored transforms when undo re-runs a changed script. Merge together with #4778: re-running the script on a style-only undo also re-reads every other animated element, and until #4778 those restart from their live mid-tween values. Complements #4776: with #4776 alone the resize-under-a-GSAP-hold cells reload correctly but still fail undo; with this change on top, all 8 root resize-hold cells undo exactly (box 0) and still reload correctly.

## How

- When an undo syncs attributes onto an element GSAP has parsed and the file has a GSAP script, it re-runs the composition's script, as it already does for a script change, so GSAP re-reads that element as a fresh load would.
- With no GSAP script in either file (for example after undoing a first edit, which leaves GSAP loaded in the page) there is nothing to re-parse, so the undo stays in place with the rebind only, as on main.
- The soft reload reset every element on the page with a GSAP-written inline transform. It now resets every element GSAP parsed in the composition it re-runs, and nothing in a nested composition, whose script is not re-run. The old page-wide scan missed an element whose style the undo had just synced away (a `gsap.set` hold), and cleared nested elements the reload never restores.
- Deleted: the page-wide inline-transform scan. Net lines: +6 source, +51 test.

Known limits:
- A file with two or more GSAP scripts: an undo that syncs an element GSAP parsed now reloads the preview (it stayed in place on main). Only one script can be re-run in place, and leaving the element as GSAP last parsed it is the bug this PR fixes, so a fresh load is the only exact result.
- A file whose animation lives in an external script file keeps main's behaviour: the undo stays in place and the element is not re-parsed.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: an undo on a GSAP-parsed element re-runs the script and resets the element; the reset finds a hold target whose style was synced away; it leaves nested-composition elements alone; with no GSAP script in either file the undo stays in place. Each fails with the source reverted.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the edit accuracy benchmark, below.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Smoothness is not gated and is not compared here.

## Before

title: fix(studio): undoing a first edit keeps the preview mounted
body:
## What

Undoing (or redoing) the first canvas edit in a composition without GSAP no longer remounts the preview. Before this change the preview blanked, the timeline flashed its empty "Drop media here or describe your video to start" state, and for a moment the element showed at the wrong place until the reloaded page fetched GSAP again.

## Why

A first move, resize, rotate or nudge in a file without GSAP makes the server add a GSAP library tag and a script holding the `gsap.set` and a paused timeline. Undo removes those scripts and redo adds them back. The soft undo counted any script element added or removed as a structural change, so it fell back to a full remount. That remount is also what empties the timeline store until the new page reports its clips.

Repro: in a composition without GSAP, drag an element, then undo. The timeline blanks and the preview reloads; redo reloads again, and the element shows at its pre-drag place until GSAP loads.

## Related work

Stacks on the undo re-parse fix (#4771). Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark in #4760 (not part of this PR).

## How

- The structural check ignores GSAP scripts, the GSAP library tag and whitespace directly under head/body, so a restore that only adds or removes the bootstrap stays soft.
- Undo that removes the script tears the composition's timeline down, resets what GSAP parsed to the file's markup, drops the script and re-seeks. Nothing is executed. That is what a fresh load of the restored file shows.
- Redo runs the restored script in place even when the live page has no script element yet.
- A later style-only undo on the same element (a crop) stays in place too. The in-place undo leaves GSAP loaded and the element parsed, and with no GSAP script in either file there is nothing to re-parse (#4771 takes the rebind-only path for that case).
- Net lines: +20 source, +83 test.

Known limits:
- The in-place undo puts back the file's transform and opacity only; anything else the first edit's GSAP wrote (a width or colour from an added tween) stays until #4778, which restores each element's whole inline style from the file.
- The structural check now ignores the GSAP library tag and blank text for every restore, not only a first edit's. No Studio action changes only the library tag.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: the bootstrap-only difference is soft; undo tears down in place with no reload; redo runs the script in place; move, undo, crop, undo stays in place through the second undo. Each fails with the source reverted.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the edit accuracy benchmark (table below).

title: fix(studio): undo restores the Studio marks the file has, even after the page drifted
body:
## What

Undo now always lands on the Studio marks (offset, size, rotation) the restored file has, even when the live element drifted from the file during the gesture. Before, marks the live element lost stayed lost, and marks the file lacks stayed on screen when the script did not change.

## Why

Every seek re-imposes the Studio marks found on the live element. Undo only copied the attributes that differ between the previous file and the restored file. A separate pass then fixed marks, but only on live elements that still carried one, and only when the undo re-ran the script. So a move that dropped an element's offset marks while the file kept them left the element without its offset after undo. A resize whose marks never reached the file kept imposing its size after an undo that did not touch the script.

Repro: an element with a Studio offset (`data-hf-studio-path-offset`, 60 px by 40 px) and a GSAP tween. Move it, then undo. The file comes back byte-identical, but the live element has lost its offset marks and the box lands 54 px from where it started.

## How

- The elements an undo syncs are now the file-to-file changes plus every element whose live Studio marks differ from the restored file. This covers both the script branch and the in-place branch.
- Those elements are synced against the previous file like any other target. A layer in the middle of a drag therefore keeps the marks it is drawing (the existing mid-gesture merge).
- Deleted: the separate mark-sync pass, which only looked at live elements that still had a mark.

## Size

80 changed lines (+68 -12): one helper and one call in `gsapUndoRestore.ts`, the old pass removed, and three unit tests. The fix is small because the restore already syncs a target list; it only needed the drifted elements added to it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: offset marks a move dropped come back; marks the file lacks are dropped even without a script change. Both fail with the source reverted ("expected null to be 'true'", "expected true to be false").
- [x] Unit test: a layer mid-drag that the undo does not change keeps its marks and translate. This test and the existing mid-drag script test both fail if the drifted elements are synced without the previous file.
- [x] Manual: headless Studio on the edit-accuracy fixture (tween, offset marks added). Undo is 54.07 px off on main and 0.00 px off with this change. On a fixture whose element GSAP does not animate, undo is 0.00 px off on both.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

The element at the playhead, before the gesture:

![Before the gesture: the element with its Studio offset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fde6777e-198d-453c-95c4-7d89494357f8)

On main, after moving the element and undoing, it sits up and to the left of where it started (54 px off):

![Before: after undo the element lost its offset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f6622aa-045f-45a3-ad9e-27de45ecfec2)

## After

The same gesture with this change: after undo the element is back where it started (0 px off).

title: fix(studio): start every drag from one position reader and draft what it commits
body:
## What

Every position gesture (move, nudge, and the centre pin of a corner resize) now starts from one reader of the element's GSAP x/y, and the live draft shows the value the commit writes. Fixed along the way: two separate causes of large jumps after a drop.

- **xPercent/yPercent centring deleted on drop (the 144 px jump).** Before a move, the drag's self-heal (`consolidate-position-writes` in `packages/studio/src/hooks/gsapRuntimeBridge.ts`, the `isPosWrite` duplicate check) treated a `gsap.set("#el", { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50 })` as a second position write next to the element's x/y tween, and deleted it from the file. A few lines later, the stale-id refresh picked the first "position" animation by property group, which was that same set, so the keyframe went into the wrong call. Both now count only pure position writes of `x`/`y`, through one predicate (`isPositionXYWrite` in `@hyperframes/parsers/gsap-constants`) that the server's duplicate cleanup uses as well, in both writers. A drag writes those; a centring set does not compete with it.
- **The first move in a sub-composition without GSAP never saved (the 108 px jump).** On the first write into a file with no GSAP, the server inserts the GSAP script and a paused timeline before `</body>`. A templated sub-composition mounts only its `<template>` content: `packages/core/src/compiler/compositionAssembly.ts:190-192` collects scripts from `template.content` when a template exists. So the inserted script never ran, and the saved move was ignored on every load. The bootstrap now goes where the loader runs the edited element's own composition: the innermost template that holds it, else the root body (`insertGsapBootstrap` in `packages/studio-server/src/routes/files.ts`, parsed rather than matched as text). A root that holds an inline `<template>` composition keeps its bootstrap in its own body, and nested templates are searched as well.
- **A drag without GSAP started from 0.** With no `window.gsap` in the preview, the drag base was `|| 0`. The commit then wrote `gsap.set(x = delta)`, dropping the element's CSS `translate` (50-72 px jumps on reload). The reader computes what GSAP's CSSPlugin will parse once the commit loads GSAP: the CSS `translate`, then `rotate`, `scale` and `transform`, less a -50% centring kept as x/yPercent. This folds in the no-GSAP fix from #4750.
- **The draft without GSAP showed a different position than the commit.** It composed the element's old Studio offset variable into the authored `translate`, so a percent translate grew during a resize while the committed x did not (up to 222 px after a resize drop). The draft now writes the committed x/y as an inline `translate`, less what the transform already adds, keeping the -50% centring. The reader parses that draft back, so a second move or a nudge before the preview reloads starts where the first ended. A `transform` that alone centres the box keeps its -50% under the draft, so a resize scales it the way the committed xPercent does.

## Why

Manual editing has to land where the pointer left the element. The edit accuracy benchmark showed every no-GSAP move, nudge and resize, and every xPercent+tween move, nudge and resize, jumping on drop or on reload.

## Related work

Stacked on #4766 (sub-pixel placement). Folds in #4750, which can close once this lands. Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark from #4760.

## How

- One reader, `readGsapPosition(element)` in `hooks/draggedGsapPosition.ts`: GSAP's own x/y when the page has GSAP, else the CSS fold above.
- Deleted, now replaced by that reader:
  - the drag start's `gsap.getProperty(x) || 0`;
  - `readGsapPositionFromIframe`, a second read that re-found the element by selector and fell back to `{0,0}` at three commit sites;
  - the resize start's second position snapshot, which was never read;
  - `readElementGsapNumber`, whose only caller was that snapshot.
- One draft writer, `applyOffsetDragDraft`, used by the drag, the release and the nudge. It replaces three "GSAP, else the old CSS offset channel" branches in `manualOffsetDrag.ts`. The member's creation swaps the authored translate for the drafted one, so a resize's first frame does not see the percentage grow.
- Net lines: source +57 (233 added, 176 deleted across 13 files); tests +262.
- One existing assertion changed meaning. The #4734 test "is not masked when GSAP does not own the position" checked for the old offset variable. It now checks for the drafted px translate. The intent (not masked to `none`) is unchanged.

## Score

The edit accuracy benchmark was run on a dev machine: 68 cells covering move, nudge, resize and rotate, with and without GSAP, px/pct/centre/xPercent placements, 0°/30°, root and nested, at 100% zoom. Base is #4766. Both runs wait 3 s before each snapshot (the benchmark's settle fix is pending in #4760).

| Metric | #4766 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| tracking | 68/68 | 68/68 |
| drop | 15/68 | 56/68 |
| reload | 66/68 | 66/68 |
| undo | 66/68 | 66/68 |
| all but smoothness | 13/68 | 54/68 |

No cell got worse on tracking, drop, reload or undo. Still failing:
- corner resize at the root without GSAP, and under a GSAP hold: the saved size set is not shown in the live preview after the drop (next PR);
- rotate without GSAP on a CSS-rotated element: the rotation base ignores the authored `rotate`.

The full-grid score follows once the benchmark's baseline is re-banked.

## Before

xPercent/yPercent-centred element with an x/y tween, moved 90, 60 px. After the drop it jumps down-right by half its size, because the centring set was deleted from the file.

![Before: the element jumps after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe0ef2ed-f954-40fa-a2b5-a162ba0cee92)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c0390b4b-acc3-43eb-ac8d-a5e3d32f55c6

## After

Same move: the element stays where it was dropped, and the file keeps the centring set.

![After: the element stays where it was dropped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7be02e8c-f28b-4d9c-904e-28ea2cd198b3)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2cf9e815-2931-4ea7-a93b-aa76cfe09491

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - #4750's no-GSAP reader tests (stylesheet translate, transform, rotate, scale, unparseable fold, GSAP present, -50% centring);
  - a percent translate that does not grow during a resize;
  - the drag intercept keeping an xPercent set and keyframing the x/y tween;
  - the server writing the bootstrap inside a sub-composition's template, in a root that holds an inline template composition, and in a sub-composition with a nested template;
  - a second move before the preview reloads (percent, px and transform placements), and a transform-centred box during a resize;
  - both writers keeping an xPercent/yPercent set when merging duplicate position writes.

  Each fails with the source changes reverted.
- [x] studio (567 files, 6214 tests), studio-server (946) and parsers (1074) pass. tsc, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the benchmark cells above, and a before/after capture of the worst case.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): save a resized size as a global set so the preview shows it
body:
## What

A corner resize of a layer with no size animation saves its new size as a global `gsap.set("#el", { width, height })`, the same way a move saves `x`/`y` and a rotate saves `rotation`. The live preview and a fresh load then show the size that was saved.

## Why

The static size used to go onto the composition's paused timeline as a zero-length `tl.set(..., 0)`. In the root composition, the preview after the drop and after a fresh load showed the element back at its old size, while the moved position stuck. The benchmark saw this on every root resize without GSAP (60-120 px drop) and on every root resize under a GSAP position hold (60-120 px on reload).

## Related work

Stacked on #4774, which is stacked on #4766. Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark from #4760.

## How

- `commitStaticGsapSize` adds `global: true` to its `add` mutation (one line), which puts the static size in the same channel as the static position and rotation.
- An existing global size set is updated in place. A size saved the old way, as a timeline `tl.set` or a duration-0 hold, is replaced by one global set carrying the same properties, and the old one is deleted in the same undo entry. That is the path the keyframed position hold already took; both now share `replaceWithGlobalSet`.
- Net lines: source +12 (25 added, 13 deleted); tests +28.

## Score

The edit accuracy benchmark was run on a dev machine: every corner resize cell without GSAP or under a GSAP hold, with px, pct, centre and xPercent placements, 0°/30°, root and nested, at 100% zoom. That is 28 cells. Base is #4774. Both runs wait 3 s before each snapshot.

| drop | 22/28 | 28/28 |

| undo | 20/28 | 21/28 |

Undo restores the file bytes exactly, but the preview keeps the resized box until a reload (the same values as before this PR). That is in the undo restore, which is separate work.

A layer with a percent `translate` and no GSAP, resized from a corner. After the drop the box snaps back to its old size.
