title: fix: readers never see an empty or half-written project file
body:
## What

Every writer that saves a composition or project file now publishes it whole: the file a reader opens is either the old one or the complete new one, never empty or half-written.

## Why

Some writers replaced or created files in place. A reader running at the same moment (Studio's preview reads, the GSAP animations route, the file watcher's reloads) could see an empty or partial file. Studio's server already had an atomic writer, but these paths bypassed it:

- the SDK file adapter's `write`
- the CLI Studio server's viewport rewrite after a registry install
- Studio's create file, duplicate file, create-only save (`If-None-Match: *`) and upload routes, which opened the new file exclusively and then filled it, leaving it empty for an instant

## How

- `replaceFileAtomically` moves from `@hyperframes/studio-server` to `@hyperframes/core` (new subpath `@hyperframes/core/atomic-file`), the lowest package the SDK, the CLI and the Studio server all depend on. Studio server imports switch to it; nothing is copied.
- New `createFileAtomically` in the same module for "must not exist yet": write a sibling temp file, then hard-link it into place, which fails with `EEXIST` like the old exclusive open and never follows a link at the destination. On a volume without hard links (link fails with `EPERM`, `ENOTSUP`, `EOPNOTSUPP`, `EXDEV`, or `EISDIR`, which is how Node reports a FAT or exFAT drive refusing a link on Windows) it falls back to the old exclusive write, which is today's behaviour there; any other link error propagates. If only the temp file's cleanup fails after the link, the create still succeeds and logs a warning.
- New `resolveWritePath` in the same module: the file a write lands on, with folder links resolved as the system does and a link at the end followed, including one whose target does not exist yet. An existing target is resolved by the system itself; a missing one is walked link by link, with each link's text read against the real folder it sits in. The SDK adapter uses it, and the CLI's cloud download drops its own copy of that loop for it.
- The temp name is short (`<name>.<8 hex>.tmp`, created exclusively), so names up to about 13 bytes under the filesystem limit still work. If another writer already holds that name, a fresh one is drawn (up to three tries) and theirs is left alone.
- A rename refused with `EPERM`, `EBUSY` or `EACCES` (Windows, while another process briefly holds the target) is retried up to five times over about 100 ms.
- `mode` is now optional in `replaceFileAtomically`; without it the file gets the default creation mode, as `writeFile` would.
- The SDK adapter keeps the existing file's mode.

Behaviour otherwise unchanged: the create routes still answer 409 on an existing file, encoding and folder creation are as before.

## Known limits

- Replacing by rename gives the file a new identity: other hard links to it keep the old content, and owner, group, extended attributes and ACLs are not carried over. The Studio server's saves already worked this way; the SDK adapter and the CLI's block install now do too.
- File names of 243 to 255 bytes cannot be created or saved: the temp name next to them adds 13 bytes and passes the usual 255-byte limit.
- On NFS, a retransmitted `link()` can report `EEXIST` although our own link succeeded, so a create could answer 409 while holding the user's own content.

## Test plan

- `packages/core`: `createFileAtomically` publishes only complete content, refuses an existing file or dangling link without touching it, falls back for each no-hard-link code (including `EISDIR`) and propagates any other, draws a fresh temp name when one is taken without touching the other writer's file, succeeds when only cleanup fails, and leaves no temp file; both writers handle a name close to the 255-byte limit; `replaceFileAtomically` keeps the default mode when none is given, retries a busy rename and gives up after five tries; `resolveWritePath` follows a relative link inside a linked folder to the real target, reads a link like `x/../t.html` through a linked folder `x` the way the system does (existing and missing target), resolves a dangling link, and stops a loop.
- `packages/sdk`: a write replaces the file whole (a hard link held by a reader keeps the old content), keeps its mode, still writes through a symlink or a chain of them, creates the missing target of a dangling link, follows a relative link inside a linked project folder to the real file, creates new folders.
- `packages/studio-server`: create, create-only save, duplicate and upload never open the destination for writing directly, and leave no temp file.
- `packages/cli`: installing a block sized unlike the project fits it without rewriting the file in place.
- `packages/cli`: a cloud download through a relative link inside a linked folder lands on the real target.
- Each new regression test fails with its fix reverted.

## Not in this PR

Left for a follow-up:

- CLI commands that still rewrite a composition or project file in place: `packages/cli/src/commands/media-treatment.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/upgrade.ts` (wrapper rewrite), `packages/cli/src/whisper/normalize.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/figma/component.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/projectConfig.ts` (`hyperframes.json` updates), and `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` (rewrites inside a freshly scaffolded project).
- Studio server metadata written in place: `packages/studio-server/src/history/historyId.ts` (the project's history id file; a half-written one makes a concurrent start fail) and `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/hfIdPersist.ts` (a cache record that is re-parsed when unreadable).
- Private atomic writers in the CLI that should move onto the shared helper: `packages/cli/src/utils/writeNewFile.ts` (create without replacing), `packages/cli/src/registry/publication.ts` (staged replace on registry install) and `packages/cli/src/cloud/download.ts` (staged replace of a cloud download; its link following already uses the shared resolver here).

title: fix(studio): undo and soft reloads restore each element's inline style from the file
body:
## What

After an undo, and after any soft reload of the preview, each element's inline style is what a fresh load of the written file gives it. Before, the soft reload put back the live inline style and patched only transform and opacity, so any other animated value (a width, a color) was read back as the new tween start and drifted on every soft reload.

## Why

A soft reload clears GSAP's cache on each element (`clearProps: "all"`, which also empties the style attribute), then re-runs the script. Whatever inline style it puts back is what the re-run tweens start from. It put back the live style, a runtime state, and patched transform, translate, rotate, scale and opacity from the file. Everything else the runtime wrote stayed.

Repro: a composition with a second element that has a width tween (240 to 480 px over 4 s; 300 px at the 1 s playhead). Crop the first element, undo, redo. The second element's width at the same playhead goes 300, then 345, then 379. A fresh load shows 300.

## Related work

Stacks on #4773, #4772 and #4771, and should merge with them: #4771 makes a style-only undo soft-reload, which makes this drift reachable from a crop undo. #4783 takes the nested-composition case below. Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark in #4760 (not part of this PR).

## How

A soft reload re-runs one composition's script. It now resets only what that re-run rebuilds, and gives each of those elements what a fresh load gives it:
- **What the reset covers:** the tweens of the re-run composition's own timeline, plus what GSAP parsed in that composition. A nested composition's timeline, which the runtime nests inside the root one, belongs to its own script, so a root reload no longer resets what it animates. Before, a root move cleared the inline style of those nested elements.
- **An element written in the top-level file:** exactly the file's style attribute.
- **A node the script creates:** nothing. The re-run recreates its state.
- **What may be a clone of a plain `<template>`:** no counterpart in the file, and the same tag and classes as an element of a plain template's content. The soft reload refuses and the preview reloads, because the script re-clones on every run. An unrelated plain template no longer forces the reload.
- **Anything in an inlined nested composition, and every element of a nested composition's own reload:** the inline style is kept, minus GSAP's transform, as before. The preview marks an inlined composition with `data-composition-file` (the bundler removes `data-composition-src`), and the bundler rewrites parts of those inline styles, so the nested file alone cannot say what a fresh load shows. #4783 handles these.

Every soft-reload caller now passes the written file. Both callers already get it back from the server, and without it they reload the preview.

Deleted: the authored transform restore and the authored opacity restore for elements in the file, the lazy authored-style lookup, and the page-deep timeline walk. Net lines: +14 source, +7 test.

Known limit: a script copy made with `cloneNode` keeps its source's ids, so the reset gives it the source's file style, and it sits on the source until the re-run moves it. Script-made copies already pile up on every re-run before this change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated, one per element class, each compared with what a fresh load of the file puts inline. The nested cases use the markup the preview bundler writes. The new ones fail with the source reverted.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the edit accuracy benchmark (table below).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Score table: pending.

## Before

The fixture above at the 1 s playhead (the blue bar is the second element): crop the yellow box, then undo. The blue bar comes back 345 px wide instead of 300.

![The composition before the gesture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/92ac432b-f0ba-4f06-a4a5-f85f3f26b31d)

![Before: after undo the blue bar is wider than before the gesture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8a217fa3-6f80-42aa-bdb5-d306fc730b02)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5061eadc-bca3-43dc-9fe1-66225b5f36f3

## After

The same gesture: after undo, and after redo, the blue bar is 300 px, as a fresh load shows.

![After: after undo the blue bar is back to its width](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58a103e-2057-4f2a-9eda-97196cef5979)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/44fc4866-74a2-429c-991d-6a7c93b37287

title: fix(lint): recognise .avif and .m4a in the media src kind rule
body: ## What `media_src_kind_mismatch` classified `.mp3` and `.jpeg` but not `.m4a` or `.avif`, so the two mistakes the rule exists to catch went unreported for those formats. Two lines: `.avif` joins `IMAGE_SRC_EXT`, `.m4a` joins `AUDIO_SRC_EXT`. Regression cases cover both directions, the correctly-matched cases, and case/query/hash handling. ## Why The producer fail-closes when a tag and its file kind disagree, so a missed diagnostic here surfaces later as a broken render instead of a lint error. The rest of the toolchain already treats both formats as known — `packages/core/src/compiler/htmlBundler.ts` and both `fileServer.ts` implementations serve `.avif` as `image/avif`, `packages/studio/src/utils/mediaTypes.ts` lists it as an image, and `packages/lint/src/project.ts` already carries `.m4a` in its own audio set. The rule was the only place that did not. ## Related work Refs #4382. The issue's reproduction is unchanged and now returns the expected result: ```text voice.mp3 [ "media_src_kind_mismatch" ] voice.m4a [ "media_src_kind_mismatch" ] photo.jpg [ "media_src_kind_mismatch" ] photo.avif [ "media_src_kind_mismatch" ] ``` ## How `.ogg` deliberately stays out, and the existing test that paired it with `.m4a` is narrowed to `.ogg` alone. The distinction is that `.ogg` does not name a kind — the container carries Theora video as well as Vorbis/Opus — whereas `.m4a` is audio-only, and video in the same MP4 container is `.m4v`, which `VIDEO_SRC_EXT` already listed. So `.m4a` can be classified without the rule ever guessing, and the conservative behaviour the test was protecting is preserved for the extension that actually needs it. I renamed that test rather than deleting it, and added an unknown-extension (`.xyz`) case so the conservative path is pinned independently of OGG. New cases: ``→`.m4a`, `

title: fix(studio): rotate from the angle a CSS-rotated element shows, without GSAP too
body:
## What

A rotate gesture starts from the angle the element actually shows, and in a composition without GSAP the live draft shows the absolute angle the commit writes. Before this, a layer rotated by an authored CSS `rotate: 30deg` and turned another 25° was saved at 25°, and snapped back by 30° after the drop.

## Why

The rotate base was GSAP's `rotation` plus Studio's old rotation variable, with `|| 0` when the page had no GSAP. The authored CSS `rotate` was ignored. The commit saved the absolute angle (0 + 25) as `gsap.set({ rotation })`, which replaces the CSS rotation once GSAP loads, while the draft had shown 30 + 25 by composing onto the authored value. The benchmark saw a 74.7 px drop on every CSS-rotated rotate cell without GSAP.

## Related work

Stacked on #4776 (then #4774, #4766). Same reader as #4774: that PR reads position, this one adds rotation. Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark from #4760.

## How

- `readRotationBase(element)`: GSAP's rotation (plus the old variable) when the page has GSAP. Without GSAP it is the rotation GSAP's CSSPlugin will parse from the CSS `rotate`, `scale` and `transform`: the same folded matrix the #4774 position reader uses, now also giving `atan2(b, a)`. There is no `|| 0` fallback.
- One rotation draft writer, `applyRotationDraft`, used for the drag and the release: GSAP's `rotation`, or without GSAP a CSS `rotate` of the target angle less what `scale` and `transform` already turn. A `transform: rotate()` or a mirrored element then drafts exactly what the commit will show.
- One restore, `restoreRotationDraft`, used for no-change, failed-commit and cancel: the CSS snapshot plus GSAP's rotation without the old variable.
- Deleted: `readGsapRotation`, the old composed rotation draft (`applyStudioRotationDraft`), and three "GSAP, else the old CSS channel" branches in the overlay gesture handler.
- Net lines: source 0 (64 added, 64 deleted); tests +30.

## Score

The edit accuracy benchmark was run on a dev machine: every rotate cell at 100% zoom, with no GSAP, a GSAP tween or a GSAP hold, px/pct/centre/xPercent placements, 0°/30°, root and nested. That is 44 cells. Base is #4776. Both runs wait 3 s before each snapshot.

| Metric | #4776 | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| tracking | 44/44 | 44/44 |
| drop | 38/44 | 44/44 |
| reload | 44/44 | 44/44 |
| undo | 44/44 | 44/44 |
| all but smoothness | 38/44 | 44/44 |

No cell got worse.

## Before

A layer with an authored `rotate: 30deg` and no GSAP, rotated 25° more. After the drop it snaps back by 30°.

![Before: the rotation snaps back after the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af3c75f0-db0d-411a-a651-82e964caed57)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5a16afbd-46e5-4740-88c5-b112a14828eb

## After

Same rotation: the layer stays at the angle it was dropped at.

![After: the rotation is kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a9f2b626-98c2-459d-8130-2670ec3cb6ea)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd2719a6-9e28-4d11-8f0f-fe4450a0cd80

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: the rotate base without GSAP reads the authored CSS rotation and drafts the absolute angle, and the draft leaves the part of the angle a `transform` rotate or a mirror (`scale: -1 1`, `scaleX(-1)`) already draws. Each fails without the change. The old variable's snapshot/restore test now uses the committed path.
- [x] studio `src/components/editor` and `src/hooks`: all pass. tsc, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the 44 benchmark cells above, and a before/after capture.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): one GSAP-writes check that sees every keyframe form
body:
## What

Studio had two copies of the check "does GSAP write this channel on this element?". The copy used by the seek reapply, the drag reapply and the crop "GSAP owns clip-path" rule (`gsapAnimatesProperty`) read only top-level tween vars, so it missed object-of-arrays keyframes (`keyframes: { x: [0, 200] }`). A layer moved that way that still carried an old Studio offset got that offset put back after every seek, on top of GSAP's position: it showed up 300 px away from where its animation put it. A crop on a layer whose clip-path GSAP tweens that way was treated as Studio's to rewrite.

## How

- `gsapWritesChannels` in `gsapRuntimeKeyframes.ts` already answers the question for every keyframe form (top-level, percent, array, object-of-arrays) through `keyframeVarsCarryChannel`. It is now exported.
- The three callers use it: seek reapply and drag reapply with `["x", "y"]`, the crop rule with `["clipPath"]`.
- `gsapAnimatesProperty` is deleted. Its file keeps only `gsapRendersTransform`, which is a different question.
- No new authoring format and no behaviour change for top-level vars.

## Before

A layer with an old Studio offset of 300 px and a GSAP tween `keyframes: { x: [0, 200] }` (the dashed box is where the tween starts it), after seeking back to 0 s on main. Studio puts the offset back, so the layer sits 300 px right of its animated start.

![Before: the layer sits 300 px right of its animated start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8bbe48cd-1ab3-4e86-b855-b15e3edfe566)

## After

The same fixture and seek at this head. GSAP owns x, so Studio leaves the position alone and the layer sits on the dashed box.

![After: the layer sits at its animated start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95d3b69b-49f3-4ca3-a3b3-6af3b7aa1f11)

## Tests

- `reapplyPositionEditsAfterSeek.test.ts`: an element with an old offset and `keyframes: { x: [0, 200] }` keeps its offset off, while its untweened neighbour gets its offset back.
- `cropResize.test.ts`: a crop on an element whose clip-path GSAP tweens by object-of-arrays keyframes is left alone.
- Removing the object-of-arrays branch from `keyframeVarsCarryChannel` fails both new tests (and one existing crop test). The Studio unit suite passes.

title: ci: install a pinned static ffmpeg on linux instead of apt
body:
## What

`install-ffmpeg-linux` now downloads a pinned static ffmpeg 7.1.3 (with ffprobe) from BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds and puts it on PATH, instead of running `apt-get install ffmpeg`. Every Linux job that uses the action gets the change with no edits of its own: ci.yml's test shards, producer lanes and skills job, plus catalog-previews, player-perf and preview-regression.

## Why

The apt mirror is the slow, variable part of our test shards. Across 53 apt ffmpeg installs in the last 12 CI runs: median 30 s, p90 252 s, max 683 s. In merge-group run 36733841479, `Test (runtime)` spent 597 s in this step and hit its 10-minute timeout before any test ran. In run 36731827300, `Test (studio)` spent 284 s here and then timed out in its tests. Each timeout pushed a PR out of the merge queue. Raising the timeouts would hide the slow mirror and make every red run cost more, so this removes the live apt download instead.

## Related work

Same source and release tag as `install-ffmpeg-windows` (autobuild-2026-04-30-13-44), which already moved off a flaky package feed.

## How

- The tarball is pinned by URL and sha256 (from the release's `checksums.sha256`). Bump all three together.
- No Actions cache. On GitHub runners a cache hit took 9 s against 10 s for a fresh download, and a cache restore is bounded only by its 10-minute default, the kind of stall this PR removes.
- Each download attempt aborts after 20 s, or after 10 s below 5 MB/s. There is 1 retry, and `--retry-max-time 25` stops a `Retry-After` header from making curl wait longer (reproduced with curl 8.7.1 against a server sending `Retry-After: 30`: 30 s without the flag, 0 s with it).
- `ci.yml`'s `code` change filter now includes `.github/actions/**`, and `skills` includes `.github/actions/install-ffmpeg-linux/**` (Test: skills is gated only on `skills` and is the one skills job that uses a local action).
- The checksum is verified before extracting. Only `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are extracted, into `$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg-bin`, which is added to PATH. `prepare-ffmpeg-bin` then finds it with `which ffmpeg`, as before.
- Version: CI moves from Ubuntu's 6.1.1 to 7.1.3. Production images use Debian bookworm's 5.1, so CI and production already differed. Golden baselines are produced in `Dockerfile.test`, not with this binary.
- The build has every filter and library the code uses: zscale, tonemap, drawtext, subtitles/ass, ssim, psnr, colorspace, lut3d, signalstats, loudnorm, libx264, libx265, libvpx-vp9, prores_ks, libopus, fontconfig, freetype, harfbuzz.

## Test plan

- [x] Ran the step's script on a Linux x86_64 host. Download, verify and extract: 8.1 s. `ffmpeg -version` and `ffprobe -version` report n7.1.3.
- [x] Wrong sha256: the step exits 1 and extracts nothing. Right sha256: exit 0.
- [x] This PR's CI at the final head (run 36744305708): every Linux job that uses the action ran on the new binary and passed: Test (studio) 9 s, Test (runtime) 8 s, Test (support) 8 s, Producer integration tests 8 s, Test: skills 8 s, CLI smoke 9 s (download, verify, extract). Before, the same step took median 30 s, p90 252 s, max 683 s.
- [x] The first run skipped every test shard, because the `code` change filter did not count `.github/actions/**`. A CI change that CI cannot test is the bug, so `code` now includes `.github/actions/**` and `skills` includes the ffmpeg action, and a change to a shared action runs the jobs that use it.
- [x] Cache hit measured by rerunning Test (runtime) on the earlier cached head: 9 s, against 10 s for a miss, so the cache was dropped. Worst case now: 2 download attempts of at most 20 s each plus a honoured `Retry-After` of up to 25 s capped by `--retry-max-time 25` (about 46 s of curl), plus about 8 s to verify and unpack, so under a minute. The first version allowed about 123 s.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments". The action's long description is shortened to what it does.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A merge-group run. The shards are the same jobs, so the same step runs there.
- player-perf, preview-regression and catalog-previews, which use the action behind their own path filters. Risk is low: the same binary passed every ci.yml job.
- Known limits: a download slower than about 5 MB/s now fails the job in about 41 s, where apt would have eventually finished; a `Retry-After` longer than 25 s now fails the job at once instead of waiting; with no cache, every job downloads from GitHub, so a GitHub outage turns these jobs red (the Windows action already works this way); the pinned BtbN asset (the same release the Windows action pins) will eventually be pruned upstream, and then this step fails loudly until the pin is bumped.
- Windows and macOS jobs; they are unchanged.

title: fix(studio): soft reloads restore inline styles from a fresh load of the preview
body:
## What

**Merge together with #4771, #4772, #4773 and #4778.** On its own, #4778 leaves a nested composition's element with a stylesheet translate 15 px off after a nested edit, and a root script's tween of a nested element's width still creeps. This PR fixes both.

After any soft reload of the preview (undo and redo, commits, SDK edits, timing edits), every element the re-run rebuilds gets exactly the inline style a fresh load of the preview gives it. That now includes the elements of nested compositions. Before, those kept their live inline style minus GSAP's transform, so a nested width or colour tween drifted on each reload.

## Why

A fresh load does not show the raw files. The preview bundler writes a nested composition's flattened root with its size, and re-points asset `url(...)` values in nested inline styles at that file's folder. So the only exact source for "what a fresh load shows" is the page the preview route serves.

Repro: a root script that tweens the width of an element inside a nested composition. Move a root element, then undo, redo, undo. The nested element's width goes 332, 362, 384, 401 px against a fresh load's 293.

## Related work

Stacks on #4778, #4773, #4772 and #4771 (the undo fidelity stack). Measured with the edit accuracy benchmark in #4760 (not part of this PR).

## How

- **One source:** the soft reload reads the page the iframe itself loaded, with the same route a full reload uses and `cache: "no-store"`. It matches each reset element by `data-hf-id` or id, and gives it that page's style attribute.
- **No half-state frame:** the fetch and the parse run first, before anything touches the live DOM. Then one synchronous task does the undo's attribute sync, the timeline teardown, the style restore, the script re-run and the seek, so no frame paints between them.
- **Callers wait for it:** reloads apply in call order. The reload's promise settles after that task, and every caller that reads the preview afterwards awaits it: the undo's automation sync, commits, SDK edits and timing edits.
- **Refusals, where the preview reloads instead:** the page cannot be read; a target may be a plain template's clone; a script copy shares its source's ids, so which element is which is unknown.
- **Cost:** each soft reload waits for one fetch of the rebuilt page, about 40 to 68 ms on a small fixture.
- **Deleted:**
  - the per-file nested reads
  - the live-style fallback for nested elements
  - the last authored-opacity stamp use in the soft reload and its color-grading special case
  - the written-file plumbing in the four callers
  - the transient "verify-failed" result, which nothing produces any more
- **Net lines:** -44 source, +121 test.

Known limits, each a remaining preview reload or flash for the flash track:
- A motion path in a page without the MotionPath plugin still runs its script after the plugin loads.
- The refusals above reload the preview.
- The preview route can serve the pre-write page after a same-size rewrite inside one file-time tick. A separate server fix handles that.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. Each fails with the source reverted.
  - Every element class against the fetched page, including the bundler's nested markup (flattened root sizes, re-pointed urls).
  - The fetch fails.
  - A script copy shares its source's ids.
  - Reloads apply in order, and the settle promise waits for all of them.
  - The attribute sync runs in the reset's task.
  - An automation undo in a file with a GSAP script puts the undone envelope back in the lane.
- [x] Manual testing performed: an undo walk comparing every element with a fresh load after each step, root and nested, with a per-frame probe (below).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

## After

title: feat(studio): hosts can add their own items to the clip right-click menu
body:
## What

A host embedding the Studio `Timeline` can now add its own items to a clip's right-click menu. They are listed first, above Split, with an optional icon, shortcut hint and disabled state.

## Why

The clip menu's items were fixed: Split, Copy, Paste, Duplicate, Delete. A host that wants a clip action of its own, such as opening an assistant's prompt for that clip, had no supported way to add one. The only options were patching Studio's DOM or drawing a second menu.

## Related work

None.

## How

- New `Timeline` prop `clipMenuItems?: (element) => readonly TimelineClipMenuItem[]`, threaded through the provider and overlay state like `onCopyClip`, and forwarded by `TimelinePane` and `EditorShell` like `canPasteClip`. The overlay calls it with the clip the menu resolved, once per clip and function (memoized), not on every playback tick. A host whose items depend on changing state (a disabled flag) passes a new function when that state changes; an inline arrow does.
- `TimelineClipMenuItem` = `{ id, label, icon?, shortcut?, disabled?, onSelect }`, exported from the package root.
- `ClipContextMenu` renders the items first, with one divider under them, and counts them in its overflow height. A click closes the menu and calls `onSelect`.
- `useMenuKeyboardNav` (shared by the clip and keyframe menus) gave focus back to the element focused before the menu on every unmount. It now does so only when focus is still in the menu or on the page body, so an item that moves focus (a host's prompt field, sync or `autoFocus`) keeps it. A menu closed without moving focus (Escape, outside press, Copy) still returns it to the clip.
- `itemClass` moved to module scope so the new `HostItems` component reuses it; the menu's existing items render exactly as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added, each proven by a mutation that turns only it red:
  - `ClipContextMenu.test.tsx`, 7 tests: host items first with icon and shortcut; a disabled item stays inert; no host items leaves the menu unchanged; with two host items near the window's bottom the menu sits at 446 px (fails if host rows or their divider are dropped from the height); a real open and close (React state, not a mock `onClose`) where the host item focuses an existing field, or mounts an `autoFocus` field, and focus stays there (both fail when the hook restores unconditionally); Escape gives focus back to the clip (fails when the hook never restores). These focus tests render under `StrictMode`, as Studio's dev build does, where the effect cleanup also runs while the menu is still mounted; dropping the "focus still in the menu" check then fails the Escape test.
  - `TimelineOverlays.test.ts`, 1 new test: through the real overlay, `clipMenuItems` is called once, across a re-render, with the current model element, and its item is listed first (fails if the overlay drops the items or stops memoizing).
  - `KeyframeDiamondContextMenu.test.tsx` (the hook's other user): 3 passed, unchanged.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the real menu mounted in Studio's dev server by a throwaway harness page (not in this diff), once on main and once on this branch.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

- fallow audit: exit 0. It warns about one 8-line clone: the menu's keep-on-screen arithmetic, already copied across four Studio menus on main, now sits next to `AutomationSelectionMenu`'s copy. Not merged into a helper here, to keep this PR to the slot.

## Before

The clip menu on main, mounted by a harness that passes one host item (Ask): the item is ignored.

![Before: the clip menu on main ignores the host item](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ff1048b-ffc8-4e1a-a983-23a1b8a279f0)

## After

The same harness on this branch: Ask comes first, with its icon and shortcut hint, above Studio's own items.

![After: Ask is listed first, above Copy, Paste, Duplicate and Delete](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c95840d2-c6ed-4950-ab42-0494a23175fd)

title: feat(registry): cinemagraph
body: ## What A `cinemagraph` block: a still photograph with **one living region**. The frame is frozen; a single feathered mask window keeps moving — in the shipped placeholder, steam rising over a cup. The classic cinemagraph gesture: the camera stops, the world keeps breathing. ## How it works - **Deterministic and seek-safe**: the steam is drawn on a canvas purely from the seek time (state proxy + `onUpdate`, no rAF, seeded `mulberry32` PRNG — no `Math.random()`/`Date.now()`). - **Seamless loop by construction**: every wisp completes an integer number of rise cycles over the 10 s duration and sways at integer frequencies, so the frame at `t = duration` equals the frame at `t = 0`. Measured loop-seam RMS diff between first and last rendered frames: **0.215** (greyscale, 0–255 scale). - **Placeholder material**: the scene is monochrome, built from alpha steps of a single ink over the ground per the registry's placeholder conventions; no hue, no accent. - **Real-media path** (documented in the file header): base layer = looping `

title: fix: stop two merge-queue flakes in the history prune and timeline tests
body:
## What

Two merge-queue flakes, each fixed at its root.

**1. History prune tests (studio-server).** The history prune tests compute "14 days later" as `Date.now() + KEEP_GONE_PROJECT_HISTORY_MS`, and at four places expect a history last used just before that to be pruned. They now use `pastKeepWindow()`, which adds 1 ms.

**2. Timeline scroll-end timer (studio).** `@tanstack/react-virtual` goes from 3.14.6 to 3.14.13, which brings `@tanstack/virtual-core` from 3.17.4 to 3.17.11. virtual-core 3.17.8 made the scroll-end debounce cancel on cleanup. Before that, a scroll within 150 ms of unmount left a timer that later called `notify`, and so a React update. `useTimelineVirtualRows` dispatches a scroll whenever the virtualizer becomes ready.

## Why

**1.** `Date.now()` rounds down to the millisecond. A history's last use is a file's mtime, which keeps sub-millisecond precision. When the test writes `project.json` and reads `Date.now()` in the same millisecond, the mtime can be a fraction of a millisecond after "now". `now - lastUsed` then comes out just under 14 days, the history is kept, and the test gets `[]`. That is what failed in merge-group runs 36725492503 and 36750393590 (`pruneHistories.test.ts:231`, expected `[ id ]`, received `[]`).

Real users are not affected by 1. A last use a fraction of a millisecond in the future keeps a gone project's history for that fraction longer, which is the safe direction.

**2.** In run 36752435633 (job 110014311398, on #4761, which does not touch this code), all 6217 studio tests passed, but vitest failed the shard on an unhandled `ReferenceError: window is not defined`. The stack runs from virtual-core's debounce timeout (`utils.js:65`), through `observeOffset`'s scroll-end callback and `Virtualizer.notify`, to react-virtual's `onChange` and react-dom's `requestUpdateLane`. That timer fired after `timelineStackingSyncExport.test.tsx` had finished and its window was torn down. For users, the leftover timer only schedules an update on an unmounted tree.

## How

- One helper, `pastKeepWindow()`, at the top of the test, used by all four places that expected a prune at exactly 14 days (lines 108, 181, 209, 230 on main).
- `packages/studio/package.json` and `bun.lock`: the react-virtual bump. Only the two TanStack lock entries and the specifier change.
- `useTimelineVirtualRows.test.tsx`: a new test builds a `Virtualizer` on a scroll element, mounts it, dispatches a scroll, unmounts, waits 200 ms (past virtual-core's 150 ms scroll-end delay) and expects no `onChange` after unmount.
- No studio or studio-server source changes. The upgrade also brings virtual-core's other 3.17.5 to 3.17.11 fixes, including how the scroll position is corrected when the focused row resizes; this PR's full studio suite is the check that nothing we rely on moved.

## Test plan

On a hosted ubuntu-24.04 runner (kernel 6.17.0-1022-azure), in a temporary probe workflow on this PR, run 36754147351:

- [x] Root cause: in 18,805 of 20,000 writes, the file's `mtimeMs` came after the `Date.now()` read right after the write (19,042 of 20,000 when the file was stat'ed first). The largest gap was 0.983 ms, under the 1 ms margin. On a 5.15 kernel and a 6.12 kernel, the same probe found 0 of 20,000, which is why this passed on some machines.
- [x] Fails without the fix: main's `pruneHistories.test.ts`, run 200 times as 4 parallel workers x 50 `npx vitest run <file>`, failed 3 times. All 3 were `prunes a history recorded without its disk only when its folder is there without the project`, the test that failed in the merge queue.
- [x] Passes with the fix: the fixed file, same loop, 200 of 200 passed.

The loop, from `packages/studio-server`:

```
seq 4 | xargs -P4 -I{} bash -c 'f=0; for i in $(seq 50); do npx vitest run src/history/pruneHistories.test.ts > /tmp/out-{}-$i 2>&1 || f=$((f+1)); done; echo "worker {} failed $f/50"'
```

The probe workflow was removed from the branch (commit "ci: remove the temporary history prune probe").

For 2, on a Linux x86_64 host with the branch installed, from `packages/studio`:

- [x] Passes with the fix: react-virtual 3.14.13 (virtual-core 3.17.11), `useTimelineVirtualRows.test.tsx` run 200 times as 4 parallel workers x 50: 200 of 200 passed.
- [x] Fails without the fix: react-virtual 3.14.6 (virtual-core 3.17.4, main's pin), the same loop with `seq 10` per worker (4 x 10): 40 of 40 failed. Each time the new test got one `onChange` after unmount, and the other 5 tests passed.

```
seq 4 | xargs -P4 -I{} bash -c 'f=0; for i in $(seq 50); do npx vitest run src/player/components/useTimelineVirtualRows.test.tsx > /tmp/out-{}-$i 2>&1 || f=$((f+1)); done; echo "worker {} failed $f/50"'
```

## What I did NOT exercise

- The full studio-server suite 200 times; the loop runs this file alone, 4 at a time.
- Reproducing flake 2 through `timelineStackingSyncExport.test.tsx` itself. It depends on when vitest tears down the window, so the regression test checks the virtualizer contract directly, through the library's `_didMount`/`_willUpdate`, the lifecycle calls every TanStack adapter makes.

## Before

title: fix(cli): refuse capture folders that resolve outside the output root
body:
This is the follow-up I offered in #4298, where @jrusso1020 said he'd take it. I had it ready for a while and I'm sending it in case it's still useful. It's rebased on current main and all checks pass.

## What

Capture now creates its output folders through one helper, `ensureCaptureDirSync`, which walks from the output root one level at a time and refuses any folder whose real path isn't the one it has under the root. A planted `assets -> ~/somewhere` (or `extracted`, `screenshots`, `assets/svgs`, `assets/fonts`, the lottie and video preview folders) now stops the write instead of carrying page-named files into wherever the link points.

## Why

#4298 made `writeCaptureFileSync` refuse a planted link at the last path entry, but a symlinked *parent* folder still let the staging dir and the rename land outside the capture. I offered to cover that case in a follow-up there, and this is it.

## Related work

Fixes #4304
Refs #4298, #4243

## How

- `ensureCaptureDirSync(root, dir)` in `captureFile.ts` resolves each level with `realpathSync` (the JS one, not `.native`, so an existing `Assets/` on a case-insensitive disk isn't falsely refused) and compares it with the path it should have under the root. Dangling and looping links are refused the same way.
- The output root itself is the user's choice and is trusted as given, symlink included (`/tmp` on macOS is one). Only folders under it are checked.
- Every `mkdirSync` in the capture pipeline goes through it: the three top-level folders in `captureAttempt`, the partial bundle, screenshots, fonts, `assets/svgs`, `assets/lottie` and its previews, the video manifest, and `capture --video` (where the trusted root is the project folder).
- Under `--skip-assets` nothing else creates `assets/svgs`, so the SVG contact sheet now vets it before writing into it.
- Where the folder is required (`extracted/`, `screenshots/`, `assets/`, lottie), a refusal fails the capture with the usual `BLOCKED.md`. The contact sheets and the video manifest are best-effort phases, so a refused folder there skips the phase, and nothing is written outside. Refusals throw a `CaptureDirRefusedError`, which those two phases turn into a warning so the planted link doesn't go unnoticed.
- The check runs when a folder is created, not on every write, so a link swapped in by another process mid-capture is out of scope.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: the helper (nested create and re-run, planted link, link pointing elsewhere inside the root, dangling/looping link, symlinked root, a file where a folder belongs, a path outside the root), and a planted link at every folder the pipeline creates: the three top-level folders in `captureWebsiteAttempt` (with `ensureBrowser` mocked), `captureScrollScreenshots`, both folders in `downloadAssets`, the fonts folder, the partial bundle, `assets/lottie` and its previews, both video-manifest folders, the SVG contact sheet under `--skip-assets` (which also checks the warning), and `capture --video` in both layouts. Swapping any single `ensureCaptureDirSync` call for a plain `mkdirSync` makes at least one of them fail. With `main`'s sources, 25 of the 117 tests in the touched test files fail, and they all pass here.
- [x] `packages/cli` full suite: 3950 passed, 13 skipped. `tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint`, `oxfmt --check`, the comments check, the comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Manual testing: a real `hyperframes capture` against a local page with a planted link at `out/assets`, `out/extracted` and `out/assets/svgs`. On `main` all three exit 0 and write the SVGs, contact sheet and `extracted/*` into the link's target. On this branch each exits 1 with `BLOCKED.md` and the target only holds its marker file. Without a planted link, and with the output root itself a symlink, the capture is the same as on `main`. With `--skip-assets` and a planted `assets/svgs`, or a planted `assets/videos`, the capture finishes with a `SVG contact sheet skipped` / `Video manifest skipped` warning and nothing outside. `capture --video` with a planted `assets` (or `capture` in a W2H project) exits 1 and downloads nothing; without one it downloads as before.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): undo that reloads the preview keeps the timeline clips on screen
body:
## What

Undo or redo of an edit inside a nested composition (and any other undo that reloads the preview) no longer blanks the timeline. Before, the timeline dropped to its empty "Drop media here" state and the player controls greyed out until the reloaded preview reported its clips.

## Why

When an undo could not be applied in place, the undo path emptied the timeline store and marked it not ready before reloading the preview, and waited for the reload to fill it again. No other reload does that: a commit that reloads the preview keeps the clips on screen until the reloaded preview reports its own. The preview often reloads a nested composition in place now (a scene swap), so the store sat empty for the whole swap.

Repro: a root composition with a GSAP sub-composition. Move an element of the sub-composition, then undo. The timeline blanks, then comes back.

## Related work

Found while verifying the undo stack (#4771 to #4783); main has it too.

## How

- The undo path keeps the timeline's clips and readiness when it reloads the preview, like every other reload. It still clears the selection, since the undone edit may have removed the selected element.
- Deleted: the store clear and the readiness reset in the undo path.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test: an undo that reloads the preview leaves the store's clips and readiness as they were. It fails with the source reverted.
- [x] Manual testing performed: an undo walk on a generated fixture (root plus a GSAP sub-composition) sampled the timeline every frame after each key press. Moving a nested element, then undo, redo, undo: main drops to 0 clips on every step; this branch keeps all 6. The preview matched main on every element, with no half-state frame.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)

title: fix(studio): the preview serves a same-size edit written right after the last one
body:
## What

The preview now always serves what the files say right after they change, whoever wrote them: a Studio save, an external editor or the CLI's file watcher. That includes a same-size rewrite of a file made moments after the previous one. Before, it could serve the page from before the write, so a reload showed the old state. So did a soft reload, which reads the preview page.

## Why

The preview route keys its built page on a project signature. To avoid re-reading every file, the signature is cached against a fingerprint of each file's size, modification time and change time. File contents are only hashed when that fingerprint changes. File timestamps move in coarse ticks (10 ms on many Linux machines, up to 2 s on FAT). A rewrite that keeps the file's size inside the same tick keeps the fingerprint, so the old signature, and the old page, is served.

Measured on a Linux dev machine: write, sign, same-size rewrite, sign. The second signature was the old one 193 times out of 200.

Forgetting the shortcut from the API's write hook is not enough: the Studio dev server signs with its own copy of the signature module, and an external editor's writes never pass the hook.

## Related work

Found while making undo and soft reloads restore from a fresh load of the preview (#4783), which reads this page after every write.

## How

- The shortcut itself follows git's racy-clean rule. A signature is kept for reuse only when every file it read last changed more than one coarse tick (2 s) before signing began. Otherwise the next signing hashes the contents again.
- The rule lives in the one place every writer and every copy of the module goes through, so no writer has to invalidate anything, and the API's write hook is unchanged.
- Cost: signing in the 2 s after a change re-reads the project's text files, as the first signing after any change already did.

Known limit: a file server whose clock runs more than 2 s behind this machine can still hit the shortcut.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: two same-size writes through the API, with the file times pinned as they are inside one tick. The preview then serves the second content, both when the API signs with its own module and when the host signs with a second copy of it, as the Studio dev server does. Both fail on main. The second also fails when the write hook forgets the cache instead.
- [x] Studio server suite passes.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Studio on main, on a small fixture. Two same-size saves inside one file-time tick (the box reads ONE, then TWO), with the preview signing between them as a reload does. The file says TWO, but after a Studio reload the preview still shows ONE. 3 of 48 tries served the old page.

![Before: the file says TWO, the preview still shows ONE](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6fa75b3-c9dc-479d-b50b-d07904376a68)

## After

The same steps on this branch: 0 of 40 tries served the old page, and the reload shows TWO.

![After: the preview shows TWO](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6aa5fab7-def8-426f-a2fb-03b21d43e085)

title: feat(studio): hosts can apply the canvas menu's z-order through useDomEditZOrder
body:
## What changed

A host that mounts `DomEditProvider` (outside `EditorShell`) can now run the canvas context menu's z-order from its own UI: `useDomEditZOrder()` returns `enabled(selection, action)`, `apply(selection, action)` and `commit(selection, patches, action, crossed)`.

- The z-order commit (resolve entries, write, one undo entry, timeline lane mirror) moved out of the inline `onApplyZIndex` closure in `ConnectedDomEditOverlay.tsx` into the hook. The overlay now passes `zOrder.commit`, so the menu and a host share one path.
- `resolveZOrderStep(el, action)` returns the patches and the crossed sibling from the same pre-change render order. `CanvasContextMenu` uses it.
- Exported from the package: `useDomEditZOrder`, `DomEditZOrder`, `ZOrderAction`.

Read-only and a stale selection:
- The hook agrees with the overlay: `enabled` is false in a read-only preview (`usePreviewReadOnly`), and `commit` (so `apply` too) does nothing there. The session's own commits are unchanged: the timeline's lane-to-z sync goes through `handleDomZIndexReorderCommit` and stays editable in a read-only preview.
- A selection held across a preview reload points at an element of the old document, which stays connected to it but has no window (`ownerDocument.defaultView === null`). `enabled` and `apply` return false for it.
- `apply` and `commit` return false when no patch could be sent to be saved. True means sent: a save that later fails or is refused toasts and rolls back as in the menu, but `apply` cannot report it.
- A same-class sibling's entry now carries its selector index (`getSelectorIndex`, as the lane mirror already does for the crossed sibling), so a z change on the second `.card` is not saved onto the first.
- The hook returns a memoized object, safe in a dependency list.

## What I measured

At 03549eac, on Linux:
- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio is clean; oxfmt, oxlint, the comment ratchet and the citation check pass.
- The 18 test files that import the changed modules (the timeline editing and stacking tests among them): 250/250.
- The session's z reorder persists one batch with one undo entry with a read-only preview and without one. Restoring a read-only refusal in the session commit fails that test.
- Treating a selection from a windowless (reloaded) document as live fails its test.
- At 027461b6 (same hook logic, before the live-document check), each of these failed exactly its own test: `commit` ignoring read-only, `apply` taking a removed element, `enabled` ignoring one, and a sibling entry without its selector index.
- Earlier, at the first head: the export test fails when the export is removed from `index.ts`, when `apply` skips the commit, or when `enabled` is always true. In the browser (Studio dev server, a three-card fixture), right-click the back card, Bring to front: the menu is the same on the merge base and this branch, the card comes to the front, and the file saves `z-index: 4` on it.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Hosts calling `apply` themselves: the export test drives it through a mocked session commit; the end-to-end path a host would use is the same `commit` the canvas menu now calls, shown below.
- A host that sets the session's `readOnlyPreview` but mounts no `PreviewReadOnlyProvider` gets an enabled hook: the hook reads only the provider, as the overlay does. `StudioApp` sets both from one prop.
- A real preview reload in a browser: the stale-selection test moves the node into a document with no window, which is what a reload leaves behind.
- A host's `apply` does not flash the crossed sibling the way the menu does.

![Before: card A in front after Bring to front](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f95bfcb7-26ec-4cba-92b3-6e32d3c3003d)

![After: the canvas menu on card A](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aac2a866-6912-4696-bfee-851d57e6f742)

title: perf(studio): stop font list work from landing in drag frames
body:
## What

Selecting an element used to fetch both font lists, and the ~1.8k Google font names were then deduped (`uniqueFontFamilies`) and scanned again with `toLowerCase` inside the font field. The response usually lands a few frames after the selection, so a drag that starts right away paid 1.4-2.9 ms of that JS inside one of its first frames.

Now:
- Both lists are fetched once per session, when the first font field mounts, and live in a small module store (`useSyncExternalStore`).
- The Google names are deduped, and their lowercase key set is built, only once input has been idle for the overlay loop's awake window. The work runs in `requestIdleCallback` slices of at most 3 ms, and input arriving between slices holds the next one back. The helper for this is `runWhenInputIdle` in `overlayFrameLoop.ts`, which reuses the loop's own last-input clock.
- The trigger's stylesheet check is one `Set` lookup, so a selection does no list work.
- A failed fetch clears the request, so the next mount or picker open retries.
- The Local/Google tagging no longer walks the Google set. That walk was redundant, because `uniqueFontOptions` already keeps the Google entry first.

## Tests

- `propertyPanelFont.test.tsx`, "does no list work in a drag's frames when the lists land mid-drag": the lists land 200 ms into a 600 ms stream of pointermoves. It expects no `uniqueFontFamilies` call until input goes idle, and exactly one after.
- "retries a failed list fetch when the picker opens".
- `overlayFrameLoop.test.ts`, "runs idle work in capped slices, only while no input arrives".

With the three source files reverted to main, all three fail. With `runWhenInputIdle` turned into an immediate call, the mid-drag test fails.

## Measurements

These come from traces with 0.1 ms JS samples, taken on the bench fixture on a shared 32-core Linux box under load. Each case is the first drag right after selecting.
- Font-list JS inside the drag went from 1.4-2.9 ms (in one of frames 1-4) to 0.1-0.5 ms. What remains is the callback that receives the two responses and schedules the idle work.
- The idle slice itself takes 2.8-3.6 ms of wall time, including the React update it triggers, and ran 1.4-2.4 s after the drag ended.

The bench's per-frame work on the first-drag rows (px, r0/r30, root, z100) does not resolve a ~2 ms change in one frame of ~40. Medians of work p95 / max, in ms:

| gesture | main | this PR, run 1 | this PR, run 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| move | 6.36 / 7.33 | 6.55 / 7.22 | 6.28 / 7.66 |
| resize | 6.66 / 7.81 | 6.39 / 7.49 | 7.44 / 8.23 |
| rotate | 4.79 / 5.81 | 3.70 / 4.75 | 4.08 / 4.41 |
| crop | 5.53 / 6.01 | 5.31 / 5.33 | 5.70 / 6.18 |
| nudge | 5.30 / 5.30 | 6.99 / 6.99 | 6.04 / 6.04 |

On this box, two runs of the same build differ by up to ~1 ms per gesture, so these rows show no regression and no resolvable gain. The trace numbers above are the measurement.

## Before

![Before: 1.4-2.9 ms of font-list JS inside one of the drag's first frames](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19e4937a-a8f4-49e8-8743-3f3b4a04f15b)

## After

![After: 0.1-0.5 ms in the drag; the list is processed in an idle slice after input stops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bf8d237e-ccc8-46f5-8557-f16a77e0ca28)

title: perf(studio): track the motion path only while a path or create ring is drawn
body:
## What

The motion-path overlay used to poll the selected element on every overlay frame for as long as it was selected: two `getBoundingClientRect` reads, a `querySelector`, a visibility walk, a computed-style read, and a state update whenever the element's home point moved. It did this whether or not anything was drawn. On an element with no x/y motion, and with set-destination not armed, the overlay renders nothing, so that work was wasted. During a resize the home point moves every frame, so `MotionPathOverlay` also re-rendered on every pointermove (about 22 times per resize drag).

Now the per-frame tracking subscribes only while there is a path to draw or the create ring is armed. When either becomes true it resubscribes, and the next frame reads the element as before.

## Test

`useMotionPathData.test.tsx` runs ten overlay frames on a selection with no path and expects zero `getBoundingClientRect` calls. It then arms set-destination and expects the reads to resume. On main's source the first expectation fails, because the hook reads layout every frame.

## Smoothness

Measured with the edit accuracy bench (`test:edit-accuracy`) on its non-GSAP move and resize rows: `^(move|resize)-none-(px|pct|center)-r(0|30)-root-z100$`, 12 cases a side, one job, built CLI Studio, the same Linux machine and the same headless Chrome for both sides. "Before" is this branch with `useMotionPathData.ts` replaced by main's copy and Studio rebuilt, so nothing else differs. The bench records the main thread's CPU time inside each frame of the 20-step drag (thread time, so a descheduled thread does not count as work) and the frame intervals.

| Round (order) | Side | Frames | Mean main-thread ms per frame | p95 ms per frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 (after, then before) | Before | 614 | 5.21 | 8.29 |
| 1 | After | 497 | 5.06 | 7.15 |
| 2 (before, then after) | Before | 599 | 5.31 | 8.40 |
| 2 | After | 593 | 5.22 | 8.67 |

Mean main-thread work per drag frame drops by about 0.1 to 0.15 ms in both rounds, about the size of the run-to-run noise on the same side. The p95 fell by 1.1 ms in round 1 but rose by 0.3 ms in round 2, so on this machine both are inside the noise. The machine was shared and busy (1-minute load 22 to 37). Frame intervals and dropped frames followed that load, not the change: the bench's blank-page control, driven the same way in the same Chrome, dropped 0 frames during round 1's after run and 0 to 13 per case during its before run. So this PR removes the per-frame layout reads the test pins, and the CPU it saves during a drag is small.

## Before

Main's `useMotionPathData.ts`, round 1 and round 2.

![Before, round 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e1c83f49-9a0e-4099-9f50-1ea313f4a9e4)
![Before, round 2](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6e0e04a-9e7b-453a-a4bb-0de11e7bade3)

## After

This PR, round 1 and round 2.

![After, round 1](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a690497-be1f-46b1-9f54-8aa2e2543cb9)

title: test(studio): fail edit accuracy cases whose preview flashes or paints an edit late
body:
## What

The edit accuracy bench gains two metrics that feed the case pass:

- **flash**: from each committing input (pointer-up, key, undo, redo) and from a reload, to the settle, every painted frame must match the state before the input or the settled state after it, in the preview pane (with its chrome), the timeline pane and the inspector pane. A frame that matches neither is a flash.
- **paint** (edit-to-paint): the first frame painted after a committing input must already show the after-state, and arrive no later than a dropped frame (25 ms). Reported in frames and ms.

## How

- `Page.startScreencast` (JPEG q95, every frame, each frame acked at once) runs only in the untraced windows after the drag; the drag keeps its trace.
- A 16x16 marker in the top document, outside every pane, repaints each rAF with a frame counter in its colour (5 bits per channel in steps of 8, which survives JPEG), so every frame is sent and numbered. The marker also logs the counter at each committing input, in the top document and every same-origin frame (including the player's shadow root).
- Coverage is counters seen over counters in the window. A window is `uncovered` (never a pass) under 90%, or under the same run's blank-page control minus 5 points. The table lists each case's 1-frame miss chance (1 - coverage).
- Chrome runs with `--disable-gpu-compositing`: under swiftshader GL the screencast saw 40-70% of Studio's frames during heavy windows (Chrome drew 87 frames, the screencast delivered 35); with software compositing it sees about 95%.
- Tolerance per pane: the pixel count a 0.5 px shift of the element's perimeter touches.
- Nudge: the first four steps stay traced for smoothness; the fifth runs in the capture window as the committing key (the blank-page control traces four as well).
- Gate: a metric the base branch's baseline never measured is judged only for banking, so adding a metric cannot regress the gate.

## Controls

Main at ca3a3f6e0, this bench, one case (`rotate-none-px-r0-root-z100`) unless named, one job per run.

| Control | Runs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 2-frame preview blink after pointer-up | 20 | caught 20/20 (release coverage mean 0.92) |
| 1-frame preview blink after pointer-up | 20 | caught 20/20 (release coverage mean 0.91) |
| Same blinks without software compositing | 20 + 20 | caught 16/20 and 15/20 (coverage mean 0.41 and 0.40) |
| Forced preview iframe reload 100 ms after pointer-up | 10 | caught 10/10: 6-23 preview frames per run |
| No-move tap | 10 | 0 flash frames in every window, paint 1 frame |
| Clean repeat (no control) | 10 | 0/10 with a frame in the blink slot; 0-4 release frames of a real defect (below) |
| Real defect, `move-none-px-r0-nested-z100`, with marker | 5 | caught 5/5: undo 4-7 frames, redo 4-11 |
| Same, without marker | 5 | caught 5/5: undo 6-10 frames, redo 7-10 |

"Caught" for a blink means a preview-pane bad frame within 4 frames of the pointer-up (the blink is injected by a page call after the release). No gesture on main is free of flashes today: every case screened shows the timeline emptying for several frames on undo and redo, and rotate shows 1-2 frames of mixed selection chrome after release. So a whole-case "0 flashes over 10 runs" control is not available yet; the no-move tap stands in for it. With and without the marker the counts are separate runs of a defect whose length varies, and without the marker repeated frames cannot be deduped, so they do not agree within one frame.

(filled in with the run)

title: `snapshot`: option to capture frames with an alpha channel (transparent background)
body:
## Summary
`hyperframes snapshot` always writes opaque PNGs: whatever the composition leaves transparent comes out composited over black. A tool that compares a composition against a reference with an alpha channel (for example, checking that an overlay template composites correctly over any background) therefore has to render every frame twice. The workaround is to force the page background to black, then to white, and recover coverage from the pair. A `--transparent` (or `--alpha`) flag on `snapshot`, producing RGBA PNGs from the same seek and capture path, would halve that work and give exact alpha instead of a two-render estimate.

## Why `render` is not a substitute
`render --format png-sequence` can produce RGBA, but it is a different pipeline from `snapshot`. Callers that use `snapshot` for its exact, paused-timeline seek (`--at`) cannot swap in `render` frames without re-validating every pixel, because the two engines are not guaranteed to produce identical frames.

## Minimal reproduction (synthetic)
1. A one-element composition: a 50%-opacity red `<div>` covering half the frame. The root `#root` and `body` have no background.
2. Run `hyperframes snapshot . --at 0.5 --no-end -o out`.
3. **Observed:** `out/frame-00-at-0.5s.png` is opaque RGB. The uncovered half is black (0,0,0) and the covered half is (128,0,0). There is no way to tell "transparent" from "black" in the output.
4. **Asked for:** with `--transparent`, the same frame as RGBA: the uncovered half has alpha 0, and the covered half is (255,0,0) at alpha 128 (or premultiplied, documented either way).

## Ask
- A `snapshot` flag that captures with a transparent page background (in Chromium, `omitBackground` on the screenshot) and writes RGBA PNGs. It should leave seeking and every other capture setting unchanged.
- Document whether the output is straight or premultiplied alpha.

title: fix(studio): undo and redo show on the next frame instead of after the server answers
body:
## What

Undo and redo of a style or position edit in a composition without a GSAP script now show their result on the first frame after the key, in the root composition and inside nested compositions. Before, the preview held the old state for 3 to 16 frames while Studio asked the server for the restored file. A nested one also reloaded the edited scene, and the timeline dropped to its empty state while it did.

## Why

Two things made undo slow:

- Studio stepped the server's history first and only then touched the preview: drain pending saves, read the file, `POST /history/step`, read the file again, apply the restore. Every round trip was paid with the old state on screen. For a restore Studio itself wrote, it already holds both sides.
- The in-place apply only took a restore of the active composition's own file. A restore of a sub-composition file always reloaded the preview (a scene swap after a page fetch), and the full-reload path also cleared the timeline store.

## How

- The history hook remembers, per history entry id, the before and after it wrote (from the claim reply, and from each step's `undoes`). It offers a step's restore only while nothing has overtaken its last view of the history (a claim or a step in flight clears it).
- On the key, the undo action shows that restore in place, in the key's own task, after taking a copy of the attributes of every element it changes. Then it steps the server as before.
- The guess is trusted only when the server stepped the entry the tab predicted (the reply's `undoes`). Then the server's restore is applied as a diff from what the preview already shows, so a correct guess changes nothing. Otherwise (an agent, the CLI, another tab or a debounced save wrote in between, and the server undid that) the copied attributes are put back and the server's restore is applied against the file read from disk, as before this change. A refused step puts the copy back.
- An outside file change Studio accepts also drops the prediction and refreshes the history view, so the common case does not paint a wrong frame at all.
- The preview shows a restore early only when it can do it in place and synchronously: no GSAP script on either side, and no save queued or running (the save queue and the pending-edit tracker gained a synchronous idle check). Otherwise nothing is shown early, and nothing is marked stale. Each file is parsed once per side.
- The in-place apply takes a sub-composition file too. Its markup, unwrapped from the composition template, is matched by `data-hf-id` onto every host the preview inlines it into (`[data-composition-file]`). It still reloads when the restore changes the sub-composition's own root (the preview rewrites that element), touches a sub-composition that has a GSAP script (only the active composition's script can be re-run in place), or touches a file the preview does not show.
- A step taken before the history view caught up with the edit read no file first, so it had no "previous" and reloaded. It now starts from what the tab last wrote to that entry's files: the server only steps over an entry whose files are still as it left them.

The in-place apply is the same function the undo stack PRs rework (#4783); this changes only how it picks its targets, at the top.

## Measurement

Per-frame probe in the built Studio: a rAF sample of the target's box and computed style in the live preview, plus the timeline's clip count, from the key to 2.5 s after. The fixtures are the edit accuracy bench's gsap=none crop cases at 100% zoom, on the same machine, comparing main at the base commit against this branch. "First after-frame" is the first frame after the key that shows the settled state.

| case | step | main: first after-frame (ms) | branch: first after-frame (ms) | timeline min clips (main/branch) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| crop px r0 root | undo | 3 (48) | 1 (10) | 1/1 |
| crop px r0 root | redo | 3 (48) | 1 (14) | 1/1 |
| crop px r0 nested | undo | 12 (278) | 1 (11) | 0/1 |
| crop px r0 nested | redo | 11 (171) | 1 (15) | 0/1 |
| crop px r30 root | undo | 8 (193) | 1 (12) | 1/1 |
| crop px r30 root | redo | 5 (82) | 1 (5) | 1/1 |
| crop px r30 nested | undo | 10 (173) | 1 (12) | 0/1 |
| crop px r30 nested | redo | 13 (323) | 1 (54) | 0/1 |
| crop pct r0 root | undo | 5 (113) | 1 (11) | 1/1 |
| crop pct r0 root | redo | 3 (52) | 1 (15) | 1/1 |
| crop pct r0 nested | undo | 13 (235) | 1 (13) | 0/1 |
| crop pct r0 nested | redo | 11 (238) | 1 (10) | 0/1 |
| crop pct r30 root | undo | 4 (75) | 1 (9) | 1/1 |
| crop pct r30 root | redo | 4 (74) | 1 (15) | 1/1 |
| crop pct r30 nested | undo | 16 (417) | 1 (10) | 0/1 |
| crop pct r30 nested | redo | 13 (304) | 1 (10) | 0/1 |
| crop center r0 root | undo | 4 (73) | 1 (12) | 1/1 |
| crop center r0 root | redo | 4 (58) | 1 (11) | 1/1 |
| crop center r0 nested | undo | 11 (233) | 1 (11) | 0/1 |
| crop center r0 nested | redo | 11 (210) | 1 (5) | 0/1 |
| crop center r30 root | undo | 9 (228) | 1 (11) | 1/1 |
| crop center r30 root | redo | 4 (63) | 1 (13) | 1/1 |
| crop center r30 nested | undo | 11 (185) | 1 (12) | 0/1 |
| crop center r30 nested | redo | 11 (186) | 1 (5) | 0/1 |

On the branch, no frame left the settled state after reaching it, and no preview document was swapped, in any row. With the move and nudge PR (#4799) applied on top, move and nudge undo and redo are also on frame 1, root and nested.

Edit accuracy gate in CI at this head (full grid): 494 of 660 cases pass, the same as the base baseline, with none regressed. The gsap=none crop rows (36 cases, every zoom) pass undo, drop and reload in 36 of 36, as on the base. The per-frame probe above was run at the first commit; the later commits change which restores are shown early (none with a GSAP script, none after an outside write), not how a shown one paints.

## Test plan

- [x] `useEditHistoryActions.paint.test.tsx`: the real history engine, preview persistence and undo action over a live preview document. Undo and redo change the element in the key's own task, before the server answers. An undo pressed while a save is running shows nothing early. Each fails when the early show is removed or the pending-save check is dropped.
- [x] `useEditHistoryActions.paint.test.tsx`: after a Studio edit, an outside write and a reload, Cmd+Z ends with the preview equal to the file the server restored. Fails without the predicted-entry check.
- [x] `useEditHistoryActions.test.tsx`: a shown step is corrected from the server's restore as a diff from what is shown; when the server stepped another entry, the shown attributes are put back and the server's restore applies as read from disk; a refused step is put back. The second fails without the predicted-entry check.
- [x] `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts`: a step is predicted from what the tab wrote, and not while a claim or step is in flight or right after an outside change; the step's reply names the predicted entry. Fails when the outside change does not drop the prediction. An undo taken before the view caught up still reports its before and after; it fails without the fallback.
- [x] `gsapUndoRestore.test.ts`: a sub-composition file's restore lands in place on every host that inlines it; a restore of its own root, or of a sub-composition with a GSAP script, reloads. They fail without the host scope, the root guard and the script guard.
- [x] Studio typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt.

## Before

The first repaints after Ctrl+Z, then Ctrl+Shift+Z, on a cropped element: the old crop is still on screen.

![Before undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b32cf4fd-619a-423f-be95-21e46fb92ce4)
![Before redo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3ad312ff-2e8a-40c7-a1a6-fe0c1253248f)

## After

The first repaint after each key already shows the restored crop.

![After undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e63b07c6-b012-4edf-92f7-2d6d7f116881)
![After redo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0145753f-d6c0-40c0-9781-bbd44a9b7a90)

title: fix(studio): move and nudge an element without GSAP by its own CSS translate
body:
## What changes

When GSAP does not position an element, dragging it or nudging it with the arrow keys now moves it by its own CSS `translate`. The drag preview, the drop and the saved file all use the same literal: inline `translate: 130px 90px` in plain px. Nothing else is written: no `gsap.set`, no timeline, and no GSAP script from the CDN is added to a GSAP-free file. The save goes through the existing inline-style patch, with no preview reload and no read of the file's animations.

Before this change, every move went through the GSAP writer:
- It added a GSAP script and a `gsap.set` to a CSS-only composition. The first save took 2-3 s and failed offline.
- GSAP folded the stylesheet `translate` into `x`/`y`, then the set overwrote them, so the element landed short of the drop by its own translate (50 px on the fixture below).
- A sub-composition file got the script after `</template>`, where it never runs, so a nested move or nudge was lost.

## How

- **One decision, `gsapWritesPosition(el)`** (`gsapRuntimeKeyframes.ts`): GSAP positions the element if a live timeline tween or hold writes x/y/xPercent/yPercent/left/top/motionPath on it, or if GSAP already renders its transform. It is synchronous and does no fetch. The press, the drop and the save all ask it. A GSAP-positioned element keeps today's route unchanged.
- **One reader, `readTranslatePx`** (`plainTranslate.ts`): the element's translate in px as Chrome resolves it. `%`, `calc()`, `min()`/`max()`/`clamp()`, `var()` and `em` are resolved by Chrome itself, not by parsing.
- **One writer on the element** (`elementOffsetStager.ts`): a GSAP-free move is saved on the element itself, as a shared-tween word already was, and puts the live value back if the save fails. It serves single moves and group members.
- **The drag member keeps its start translate in JS.** A drop computes the absolute translate right away, so a second gesture that starts before the first save lands starts where the first dropped and cannot double-count.
- The press no longer calls `gsap.getProperty` on these elements, because that makes GSAP bake the CSS translate into its transform.
- The Properties panel's X/Y show and edit that same translate for these elements.
- Plain px only, because GSAP's CSSPlugin splits `translate` on spaces and loses a `calc()`.
- Accepted cost: a layer centred with `translate: -50% -50%` is stored in px at its current size once moved.

## Before

Main, edit accuracy fixture `move-none-px-r0-root-z100` (`translate: 40px 30px`, no GSAP), after dropping a +90/+60 move. The box lands 50 px short of the drop, and the file gains a CDN GSAP script plus `gsap.set("#target", { x: 90, y: 60 })`.

![Before: the box lands 50 px short of the drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9b743eb1-04cf-44fa-b93f-0a21e4f3dd35)

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this branch. The box stays where it was dropped, and the only change to the file is `style="translate: 129.998px 90px"` on the element. The Lint badge counts the fixture's own two findings (no `__timelines` registration), which the GSAP bootstrap used to hide.

![After: the box stays where it was dropped](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f16eea8-084a-4d9e-9f01-78b9a1cba9bd)

## Edit accuracy slice `^(move|nudge)-none-` (72 cases)

Before: main 299670e21, devbox.

| Gesture | Cases | tracking | press | drop | reload | undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| move | 36 | 2 | 36 | 7 | 35 | 35 |
| nudge | 36 | 36 | 36 | 6 | 36 | 36 |

After: this branch merged with main, CI edit accuracy gate (8 shards, each case 2 of 3 runs).

| Gesture | Cases | tracking | press | drop | reload | render | undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| move | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| nudge | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 | 36 |

All 72 pass every metric except smoothness; 59 of 72 pass smoothness too, which its own track scores. Across the whole 660-case grid the gate counts 494 passing (main: 434), 60 newly passing and none regressed. `baseline.json` banks them byte for byte from that run's artifact.

The press reads a `%` or `calc()` translate arithmetically against the border box and writes nothing to the element. An earlier head resolved it through a temporary inline `transform`, and that showed for the first frame after the press: CI saw a press jump equal to the element's own translate on every percent case.

## Tests
- A GSAP-free move saves one inline `translate` patch and makes no GSAP request. A failed save puts the live translate back (`useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`).
- The drag and drop draw plain px and never call GSAP. A second move started before the first save lands starts where the first dropped. A nudge adds to the translate. A GSAP-rendered element and a timeline hold keep the GSAP writer (`manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`).
- `readTranslatePx` resolves px, %, `calc(P% ± Lpx)` and padding plus border without writing to the element, and hands min()/max()/clamp() to Chrome with the style put back (`plainTranslate.test.ts`). A drag press on a page that loads GSAP but does not position the element (nothing animated, or only its parent) never asks GSAP and keeps the CSS route. A centred element starts from its -50% translate in px (`domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`).
- A single GSAP-free move saves on the element with no animation read. A group saves GSAP-free and shared-tween members on themselves under the group's undo key (`useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`).

## Not in this PR
Resize and rotate routing for GSAP-free elements, the nudge's layout read, and deleting the left/top and legacy offset channels come in follow-ups.
