title: test(studio): catch teleports and multi-step edit bugs in the edit accuracy bench
body:
## What

The edit accuracy bench gains a per-frame **teleport** metric, 113 new gsap=none cases that drag elements around and chain edits without waiting (where teleports show up), and a `gsap=idle` axis value: GSAP is loaded and a paused timeline tweens another element, while the target stays plain CSS.

### Teleport metric (every drag: move, resize, rotate, crop)
- A page script reads, as each frame paints from just before press until the commit settles, the pointer and the dragged element's quad (its centre plus the composed 2D transform, so rotation and zoom are exact). It agrees with CDP `DOM.getContentQuads` to within 0.06 px at z50/z200 and r30.
- The read runs in a ResizeObserver callback, which comes after every document's rAF callbacks and layout, just before paint. An earlier version read in a task posted from rAF; tasks queued ahead of it could run first, so it sometimes saw a state no frame painted. On nested tween saves it reported a one-frame 178.9 px jump about 0.3 s after release (4 of 14 runs). Paint-time reads of the same frames found 0 in 14, and a CDP screencast never showed it.
- The page script is wrapped in one function scope, so a composition's own top-level names cannot clash with it.
- The dragged point per gesture: move, the grabbed point; resize, the grabbed corner; rotate, the handle point (its angle at the handle radius, and any shift of the box); crop, the outline's edge while selected and the clipped edge after, and the element itself must hold still.
- A frame fails when that point moved more than the pointer did since the previous frame (+0.5 px), or sits where the pointer never put it. Once released, only the release point counts.
- A case reports the largest violation, its frame index and kind. A failing case keeps the per-frame trace (the point, where the pointer put it, and t) in results.json.
- Tracking (max/p95) is unchanged; teleport is the per-frame check.
- Lag is not a jump: a box may move by all the pointer travel it still owes, so a box that holds a frame and then catches up in one step passes. A one-frame 37 px jump still fails.
- Back-to-back drags share one recording, so a drag's frames run up to the next press, and a jump in the gap fails the earlier drag.
- The CI gate fails a case whose teleport check fails, an unmeasured drag included. This is its own commit, so it can be dropped to keep teleport report-only.
- The gate also fails a text case whose edit did not open, save or show its word (all 4 text rows pass today).
- One named quarantine list, `QUARANTINED` in ratchet.mjs, holds the cases a known Studio race flips run to run, each with the PR that fixes it: drag, undo, drag (6 placements, #4853), two nudge sequences whose redo write sits at the 2 s limit (#4857, which removes them once its redo-write p95 shows the gain) and one repeat drag (part C, the #4807 stack). They are still measured, and the gate comment lists each one's pass/fail on every run, but they never fail the gate, as regressed or as unbanked. The PR that fixes the race deletes its own ids from the list and banks them in the same PR.
- A drag's teleport scoring ends at its pointer-up. The pointer counts as down only while its button is held (a move after release is not a drag), and a release is counted even when no frame painted between it and the next press. Before this, the click that selects the next element became the release point, so drag A, B, A failed by the A-to-B distance.
- The gate's bank file now takes, for each case, a run that agrees with the gate's 2-of-3 verdict. It used to take each shard's first run, so an unstable case could be banked against its own verdict, and the gate then failed on the very run it was banked from.

### New cases (ids keep the `gesture-gsap-placement-rN-nesting-zN` scheme with a letters-only token, so `^[a-z]+-none-` selects them)
- Paths (45): zigzag, circle, flick, pause (1 s hold mid-drag), edge (past the visible canvas and back). Each runs × px/pct/center × root/nested at r0 z100, plus px root at r30, z50 and z200.
- Sequences (60), with no settle between steps. Each runs × px/pct/center × root/nested at r0 z100:
  - the same element dragged 3 times;
  - drag, undo, drag;
  - drag, nudge ×3, drag;
  - drag A, drag B, drag A;
  - resize, then move;
  - seek, then move;
  - a drag pressed right after pointer-up while the save is in flight;
  - resize then an immediate undo, and nudge then an immediate undo (the undo must win);
  - rotate, then nudge ×3.
  - Metrics per step: teleport, tracking and press jump. After the last step: drop and reload against the box the last step left, render, and an undo walk. The walk steps back one save at a time, each byte-identical to that step's file, then redoes forward.
- Text (4): double press to edit, type, then Enter, in root and nested. The select variant double-clicks a word mid-edit and needs a non-empty selection with the edit still open. Pass: the word is saved, shown after a reload, and undo restores the bytes.
- Rotate on `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` centring (4): r0/r30 × root/nested.
- `gsap=idle` (180): every gesture × px/pct/center × r0/r30 × root/nested × z50/100/200, ids like `move-idle-px-r0-root-z100`. Most real projects load GSAP for something; a plain-CSS edit has to behave the same there.
- The non-GSAP slice (`^[a-z]+-(none|idle)-`) grows from 180 to 473.

### Bench fixes on the way
- Undo and redo saves are timed from the key to the write, and one rule judges them: main's `UNDO_WRITE_MAX_MS` (2 s) fails undo, for single gestures and for each write of a sequence's undo walk (its slowest write). A write that never lands within 60 s is `undo lost` / `redo lost` and fails undo too. A late save no longer stops the redo, so it stops showing up as a reload failure.
- runCase and the sequence runner share one harness (open, snap off, zoom, select, error capture, teardown).
- The preview lookup could pick Studio's hidden shadow iframe, which is the same size as the live one, whenever it ran during a pending reload. It now skips frames that are not visible.
- The reload check also compares against the box the gesture left, so a write the file loses fails reload, not only drop.
- A sequence records every save from file events. The old watcher kept a state only after two equal reads 20 ms apart, so two saves landing about 40 ms apart lost the middle one, and the undo walk then compared against the wrong file.

## CI time
- Measured per case on the bench box: the existing 660 cases come to about 17.3 min per CI shard (8 shards x 2 jobs). With all 953 rows, about 26.8 min, before any reruns.
- Fewer pointer steps on paths save about 1 s per path case (28.5 s to 27.5 s), with identical teleport values. Case time is mostly fixed: Studio start, settle, undo and redo, reload and render.

## Validation
- The in-page quads agree with CDP `DOM.getContentQuads` within 0.06 px (z50/z200, r30). CDP-dispatched fractional pointer coordinates arrive exactly in `PointerEvent.clientX/Y`.
- Positive control, run 1 of 5: a page script offsets the element 37 px for exactly one frame mid-drag. It was caught at that frame on move, resize, rotate, crop (through the element-centre tracker), a path and a sequence.
- Not done yet: control runs 2-5, the 5-run clean control, and the 3-run repeatability of the new rows. They are parked while the shared bench machine is down and release PRs hold the lock.

## Scores on main (Studio at #4764, before #4766)

| Rows | Cases | All pass | All but smooth | Teleport pass | Worst teleport |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| new path/sequence/text/rotate rows (gsap none) | 113 | 1 | 5 | see per family | 616 px (flick, nested, after release) |
| move, gsap idle | 36 | 0 | 2 | 36 | 0.50 px |
| nudge, gsap idle | 36 | 5 | 36 | n/a | n/a |

Per family, new rows:

- Paths fail teleport in 9 of 9 cases per family, except flick (3 of 9 pass). The box tracks the pointer while held, then jumps 50 to 616 px after release.
- Back-to-back drags (repeat, undo, in-flight) jump up to 463 px; in repeat the jump lands while the next drag is held.
- Undo raced against the save: nudge then undo fails undo 6 of 6; resize then undo fails 5 of 6.
- Text: root passes; nested saves the word, but a reload does not show it.

The teleport pass over the existing 180 rows and the rest of the idle rows are still to run.

## Before
The old bench measured a drag only while the pointer was held, once per pointer step. This zigzag drag on main scores 0.57 px there, so nothing looks wrong:

title: fix(studio): a rotate without GSAP saves where you let go, nested too
body:
## What

Rotating an element that GSAP does not turn now saves where you let go, nested compositions included:

1. **One decision, at press.** `gsapWritesRotation(el)` sits beside the move's `gsapWritesPosition(el)`: GSAP owns the rotate when it renders the element's transform or a tween or hold writes a rotation channel (`rotation`, `rotate` and their X/Y/Z forms). Everything else is a plain rotate, decided once when the gesture starts, before anything reads GSAP (a `gsap.getProperty` call would bake the CSS into GSAP's transform and flip the decision mid-gesture).
2. **The turn starts from the angle the element shows.** A plain rotate's base folds the CSS `rotate`, `scale` and `transform` the way GSAP would parse them, so an element authored with `rotate: 30deg` no longer saves at the dragged amount alone (25 deg instead of 55). Ported from the approved rotation-preview change, which stays parked; only its CSS-rotation reader comes along.
3. **The save is plain CSS.** `savePlainRotation` writes the element's own inline `rotate`, the same value the draft draws: the angle less what its `scale` and `transform` already turn. No script, no Studio rotation marks, no preview reload, no animation fetch. It is reached the way the move's on-element writer is, through `handleDomRotationCommit` passed into `useGsapAwareEditing`, in the Studio session and in the host wiring. A read-only preview writes nothing. An element still carrying the legacy Studio rotation marks has them removed in the same write, so the seek re-apply cannot put the old angle back.
4. **A transform-centred element turns in place.** The CSS `rotate` property applies before `transform`, so a turn written there also turns a `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` and the box swings around its old centre (62 px on the bench's centred box). When the element's transform translates it, the turn goes into that transform right after its leading translate (`translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(25deg) scaleX(-1)`), so it applies in screen space about the centre: a mirrored or stretched element still turns with the cursor and does not shear. A mirroring `scale` property flips the turn's sign. A second rotate replaces its own `rotate()`. The authored transform comes from the inline style, else the last matching stylesheet rule (specificity, `!important` and `@media` are not weighed, so a later but less specific rule can win; noted in the code, left for a follow-up). Before this PR, on a page that loads GSAP such an element rotated through GSAP and stayed put, so the plain writer must not regress it.
5. **Inline elements and the panel.** An inline element becomes `inline-block` in the same write, as the old writer did, since an inline box does not transform. The overlay hands the rotate target it read at press to the commit, so the save draws and patches exactly what the draft did; re-reading at save time saw the `inline-block` the draft had already set and dropped it from the write, so the word lost its turn on reload. The GSAP-aware commit routes on that same press-time decision. The property panel shows a plain element's angle from its CSS (it read 0 deg after a plain rotate).
6. **No per-frame style read.** The `scale`/`transform` share is read once at press; the draft only sets `rotate`.

Deleted: the legacy CSS-variable rotation writer and its patch builder (`buildRotationPatches`).

Stacked on #4799 (its three commits are included and drop out when it merges).

## Why nested rotates were lost

A rotate on a non-GSAP element went through the GSAP route and wrote a `gsap.set` into the file. In a sub-composition that script lands after the `</template>` and never runs, so the element snapped back on release (all 18 nested rotate rows, 62 px). The CSS write lands on the element inside the template.

## Score (edit accuracy bench, `--grid full --filter '^rotate-none-'`, 36 cases, same machine)

| | all but smoothness | tracking | press | drop | reload | render | undo |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main (before) | 9/36 | 36 | 36 | 9 (worst 74.8 px) | 36 | 36 | 36 |
| this branch (after) | 35/36 | 36 | 36 | 36 (worst 0.00 px) | 35 | 36 | 35 |

The one miss is a nested case whose undo did not land within the bench's 15 s window (intermittent: 0 to 2 nested cases per run, only in the slowest cases); it is the nested undo path, not this writer. Transform-centred rotate rows (the bench's `transform` placement from #4801, 4 cases, same machine): before this change's centring step 0/4, worst swing while dragging 62.4 px; after 4/4, 0.0 px.

Smoothness is out of scope here (another track owns per-frame work); the after run shared the machine at about twice the load of the before run.

## Tests

- `plainRotation.test.ts`: saves only `rotate`, less what the transform turns, with no Studio marks; a legacy-marked element keeps the new angle through a seek re-apply; a failed save puts the live rotate back; a read-only preview writes nothing.
- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: a plain element goes to the CSS writer with no GSAP write; an element a GSAP tween turns stays on the GSAP route.
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`: a rotate press on a page that loads GSAP never asks GSAP about an element it does not turn, and the draft draws a CSS `rotate`.
- `manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`: the base starts from the authored CSS rotation; the draft leaves the transform's and scale's share alone; with GSAP loaded and the element not animated, nothing calls `gsap.getProperty` or `gsap.set`, and the draft does no computed-style read.
- `rotateInlineSave.test.ts`: the real press, draft, hold and save order on a span made inline by a stylesheet saves `display: inline-block` with the turn; it fails if the save re-reads the target or the overlay drops it.
- `rotationDraft.test.ts` and `plainRotation.test.ts`: a transform-centred element turns inside its transform after the translate; mirrored (`scaleX(-1)`), stretched (`scale(2, 1)`) and `scale: -1 1` centred elements turn with the cursor, unsheared, translate kept and a second turn replaces the first; the save patches the transform, and a failed save puts it back; an inline element is saved inline-block and restored on a failed save; the panel readout shows the CSS turn, and the legacy reading once GSAP turns the element.
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`: a press on an element a GSAP tween turns (`rotation`, `rotate`, `rotateZ`) reads its base from GSAP.
- Each was run against a broken copy and fails: writer ignoring the transform, legacy marks kept, routing line removed, routing always plain, plain ignored in the draft, share re-read per frame, base back to 0 without GSAP, read-only ignored, press asking GSAP, centring never taken, trailing turn appended, transform not restored.

## Before

Nested, released after a 25 deg turn: the element is back at 0 deg.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cd9871f-7fda-4232-85fe-c6fb01d63bc1)

An inline word, turned 25 deg, after a reload: the save wrote `rotate` without `inline-block`, so the word is flat again.

![before inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2d15aebe-9b61-40d0-8a36-a784836b199f)

## After

The same case keeps its 25 deg turn.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/22febf72-690b-40eb-89ad-949844f269a6)

Transform-centred, before: the box swings off its centre.

![before centred](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49fed704-0465-4a79-b7cc-b96b7324fa85)

After: it turns in place.

![after centred](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2ddfc27-93ad-409e-9ab6-6e3cd77657cf)

The inline word after a reload keeps its turn: the save wrote `display: inline-block; rotate: 24.997deg`.

![after inline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b612f934-178c-49ba-83d2-f9d419527ace)

title: fix(studio): a text edit saves to the element that was edited, or says why it could not
body:
## What

A text edit made in place on the Studio canvas is now saved to the element that was edited, whatever is selected when the edit closes. When a text edit cannot be saved, Studio says so in an error toast, logs why, and puts the old text back, so the screen never shows text that is not in the file.

## Why

Today the in-place text commit saves against the *current selection*, and silently drops the edit when the edited element is not that selection. The typed text stays on screen, nothing is written, no toast appears, and the text is gone after a reload.

Repro on main (built Studio via `hyperframes preview`): double-press a headline and type. While the edit is open, something else changes the selection (an agent calls `studio_select` on another element, or a host app clears its pick). Press Enter: nothing is written in 8 s, no toast, and a reload shows the old text. A host that opens the edit on a child of what it has selected (a composition host or a container) hits the same path, and so does a host whose Escape clears the pick before the edit closes.

## How

- `handleDomRichTextCommit` resolves the selection from the edited element itself (`buildDomSelectionFromTarget(element, { exactTarget: true, skipSourceProbe: true })`), so the patch targets that element's own source file (a nested element saves to its sub-composition file).
- The three silent returns are gone. Each refusal (the preview reloaded under the edit, the element is not in the source, the element cannot be edited in place) shows an error toast, logs with `console.error`, and puts the previous markup back.
- The read-only refusal is unchanged (quiet, old text back).
- After a save, Studio refreshes the selection only when the edited element is still what is selected. If the selection moved on (or a host cleared it) while the edit was open, it is left as it is, so a following Delete or move never picks up the edited text by surprise.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `useDomEditTextCommits.test.tsx` (the selection is another element, or none: the edit saves to the edited element and the selection is left unchanged; the edited element still selected: the selection is refreshed; an unresolvable element: toast, console error, old text back) and `useDomEditCommits.test.tsx` (a commit onto a removed preview node is refused and now says so). The new tests fail on main's source; breaking the selection condition either way turns one of them red.
- [x] Studio unit tests for `src/hooks` and `src/components/editor`: 1662 passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] Manual: headless Chrome on a built CLI preview, root and nested text: double-press, type, Enter writes in about 100 to 170 ms (unchanged); the agent-select repro above writes on the branch and not on main.
- [x] Edit accuracy bench, text cases (from the open bench PR that adds them), same machine, same main, 2 jobs:

  | Build | textedit root | textedit nested | textselect root | textselect nested | text metric |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | main | pass | pass | pass | pass | 4/4 |
  | this branch | pass | pass | pass | pass | 4/4 |

  All four fail only `smooth` on both builds (a loaded Linux box; the blank-page control drops frames there too). The bench's text route keeps the selection on the edited element, so it passes on main; the repro above is the route it does not cover.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

On main: the headline was double-pressed and " typed" entered; an agent then selected the card, and Enter was pressed. The typed text stays on screen, nothing is written and no toast appears:

![Before: after Enter, typed text shown but not saved](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81750ccc-1c52-4903-a7bf-b2eeae09ff2e)

After a reload the typed text is gone:

![Before: after reload, the typed text is lost](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46034e4a-bfde-431c-9950-e048c4138319)

## After

Same steps on this branch. The file is written on Enter, the card stays the only selected element, and after a reload the typed text is still there:

![After: after reload, the typed text is kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2e75256-c046-4386-9087-a5f5f6bcdeaf)

title: fix(core): refuse nested vfx capture canvases and scope host lookups
body:
## What

Hardens the vfx runtime against the nested `layoutsubtree` capture shape from #4405, and fixes two latent lookup bugs on the same path.

## Why

A `<canvas layoutsubtree class="hf-vfx-src">` nested inside another capture canvas's subtree blocks the renderer main thread in `drawElementImage` (`check` times out, `snapshot` hangs). The exporter now avoids emitting the nest, but the runtime should refuse it loudly instead of hanging. Two lookups were also unscoped and only hidden because the nest hangs first.

## How

- `resolveCaptureSource` calls `reportVfxError` and skips the entry when a `.hf-vfx-src` contains another one or sits inside one. A nest that only forms after a late mount is caught too, because `initVfx` re-runs after mounts.
- Host to src and host to out lookups are now `:scope >` (M2), matching the immediate-child rule already stated in the comment and used for `.hf-vfx-in`. Every exporter fixture shape already has these canvases as direct children.
- `resolveCaptureSource` reads `data-vfx-ref-visible` itself and `resolveRefSource` no longer overrides it, so a canvas reached both ways gets one `visible` value (M3).

Not in this PR: letting a `ref` name a host and bind its `.hf-vfx-out` directly (issue item 1). That is a contract change and is tracked separately.

## Test plan

- 5 new unit tests in `vfx.test.ts` (contains nest, inside nest, `:scope` src, `:scope` out, consistent `visible`). `src/runtime`: 65 files, 1724 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- New nested-backdrop browser test in `vfxDeterminism.test.ts`; all 26 tests in the file pass.
- Mutation-tested: removing each guard fails a test (contains check, inside check, each unscoped lookup, hardcoded `visible:false`, and the browser test with the guard removed).
- Not verified: the hang itself. With the guard removed this Chrome does not hang, so the browser test fails on the missing error rather than a timeout. The hang was measured on the AE-export machine.
- Commit hooks (lint, format, typecheck, fallow, commitlint) pass.

Fixes part of #4405 (items 2 and 3, plus the nest guard).

title: fix(studio): resize an element without GSAP by its own width, height and translate
body:
Follows #4799 (move and nudge by the element's own CSS translate), now on main.

## What changes

A corner resize of an element that GSAP neither sizes nor positions now saves plain CSS: the element's inline `width` and `height`, the crop scaled with the box, and the `translate` that keeps its centre where it was. That is one save and one undo step, with no animation read and no preview reload. The live element already shows the result on the frame the pointer is released.

## Why it was broken

1. Every resize went through the GSAP writer, because a GSAP commit function always exists. For an element in a file with no GSAP, that writer added a GSAP script to the file (`gsap.set` for the position, `tl.set` for the size). On release the box snapped back to its old size (or lost its size and moved, for px and % placements). The CSS size writer could not be reached.
2. The translate that keeps the centre planted was written in whole pixels, on top of whole-pixel sizes, so a px or % placed element trailed the pointer by up to 1 px.
3. A `translate` in percent follows the element's size. The first frame of a resize measured the centre while the stylesheet percent was still live, then wrote px over it, so the first frame was off by a quarter or half of the size change.

## What this does

- `gsapWritesBox` (next to `gsapWritesPosition`): GSAP owns the box when it positions the element or tweens its width or height. The resize anchor member and the resize commit both route on it, the same way #4799 routes moves on `gsapWritesPosition`.
- A resize of a box GSAP does not own goes straight to the CSS size writer, before any animation read. The size writer's own "is this GSAP-targeted" guard is gone: it rejected an element whose only tween was, say, an opacity fade.
- The CSS size writer saves the anchor with #4799's `translatePatch`, the same plain px literal a move writes, kept to a thousandth of a pixel. It still owns the crop rescale (#4743).
- A percent translate is held as the same px at press, so a growing box cannot drag it along.
- The GSAP route's old fallback to the CSS writer (reachable only without a GSAP commit function) now throws, so a GSAP-owned box is never written as CSS by accident.
- The host hook (`useDomGeometryCommit`) gets the real CSS size writer instead of a stub that rejected every such resize, and reuses that hook's offset stager instead of its own copy.
- The resize press no longer asks GSAP for the element's x/y. That snapshot (`resizeAnchor`) was never read, and on a page that loads GSAP the read itself made GSAP bake the CSS translate into its transform, so the box looked GSAP-owned and took the GSAP route.

## Edit accuracy bench, `^resize-none-` (36 cases)

Same machine, same main, the bench on main.

| | tracking | press | drop | reload | render | undo | smooth |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (main) | 12/36 | 36/36 | 0/36 (worst 222.6 px) | 36/36 | 18/36 (worst 110 px) | 36/36 | 7/36 |
| After (this PR) | 36/36 (worst 0.36 px) | 36/36 | 36/36 (worst 0 px) | 36/36 | 36/36 (worst 0.06 px) | 36/36 | 3/36 |

Nested undo can still miss under heavy load (an earlier run lost 1 nested cell: the file reverted, the live element did not); that flake sits in the nested undo path shared by move, resize and rotate and is tracked separately. Smoothness is owned by separate work and this PR adds no per-frame work.

## Tests that fail without the fix

- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: "resizes a box GSAP does not own through the CSS writer, with no GSAP write or fetch" fails with the routing line removed.
- `useDomGeometryCommits.test.tsx`: "saves the anchor as the element's own plain px translate, sub-pixel, with the size" fails with the old legacy-offset patch, and "rolls the whole gesture back once when the resize save fails" fails without the writer calling the gesture's restore.
- `manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`: "keeps the centre with the element's own plain translate when GSAP does not own the box" fails when the resize anchor keeps the legacy channel.
- `anchoredResizeCommitFeedsOffset.test.ts`: "keeps the centre on the first frame when the authored translate is a percent" fails without the press-time px hold.
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`: the resize row of "the press never asks GSAP about the element" fails if the press reads GSAP x/y.
- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: "fails a GSAP-owned resize loudly when there is no GSAP writer, never writing CSS" fails with the old CSS fallback.

## Not checked

- Resize of GSAP-owned boxes is unchanged by design and was not re-benched here.
- Legacy Studio size marks (`--hf-studio-width` and the original-size attributes) are still written by the size writer, since "Reset layer edits" restores from them. Whether a resize should write only `width`/`height` is left open.

## Before

A 240x160 box in a GSAP-free bench project, dragged from its corner to about 340x227 and released: the box is back at its old size.

![Before: after release the box is back at 240x160](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/023a333a-ff65-45be-a701-5935c88c7a10)

## After

The same gesture: the box keeps 340x227 with its centre where it was.

![After: the box keeps 340x227](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e2c31d5-1f6d-4259-9413-0b0c95d791f0)

title: fix(studio): a first animation in a sub-composition file runs from inside its template
body:
## What changes

The first GSAP edit on a GSAP-free sub-composition file now puts the GSAP script and timeline inside the file's `<template>`, where the composition loader runs them. Before, a file with no `<body>` (every sub-composition file is only its `<template>`) got the script appended after `</template>`. The loader never runs it, so that first edit was saved but never showed, in the preview or in a render.

Moves and nudges of GSAP-free elements stop writing GSAP at all in #4799. This covers the remaining ways in, such as the first animation added to a GSAP-free sub-composition.

## How
`prepareGsapMutationScript` (studio-server `routes/files.ts`) still inserts before `</body>` when the file has one. Otherwise it inserts before the file's own outer `</template>`, through core's `insertBeforeCloseTag` (which now also takes `"template"`). Core walks the markup, skipping comments and script text, and counts template depth, so a template nested inside the sub-composition's template keeps its own close tag. Only when a file has neither does it fall back to appending at the end. A file with a `<body>` keeps the `</body>` placement even when its content sits in a `<template>` (`<body><template>…</template></body>`): a root composition can hold a `<template>` (slot or clone markup) whose scripts never run, so moving the script into it would break the root case. Studio writes sub-compositions as template-only files, and every registry file with the body-wrapped shape already has GSAP, so this first-animation path does not reach them. It is a string insertion, so no `<head>` or `<body>` is added to the file.

## Test
`htmlDocument.test.ts`: "puts markup before the outer </template>, past a nested one and a commented one". It fails with first-match lookup.

`files.test.ts`: "a first animation in a sub-composition file lands inside its template". Without the fix it fails, because the script sits after `</template>`. "a first animation in a <body> file lands before </body>, outside its template" pins the body-wrapped choice above.





## Before

Main: a fixture project whose root includes a template-only sub-composition holding `#card`. Its first animation (`x` 0 to 800 over 2 s) is added through the same GSAP mutation route the test uses, and Studio is seeked to 2.0 s. The script was saved after `</template>`, so the card has not moved.

![Before: the card is still at its start at 2.0 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5f5c3691-0731-43e4-9208-a37ed2a71944)

## After

This PR, same fixture, same mutation, same seek. The script was saved inside the template, so the card is 800 px to the right at 2.0 s.

![After: the card has moved 800 px at 2.0 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b6ea7afc-9d73-43ee-8e57-6aa6f68ddbb7)



Merged below the usual size floor: this PR was opened and reviewed before PRs started being batched per lane, and PRs already in review finish as they are.

title: fix(studio): undo right after an edit undoes that edit, even before its save lands
body:
## What

Cmd+Z pressed right after an edit, before the edit's save has landed, now undoes that edit. Before, it could undo nothing or the edit before it, and the edit's save then landed after the undo and stayed. A resize or move undone that way left the element in a third state (size reverted, position not), and a nudge burst was never undone at all.

## Why

Undo first waits for pending edits (`waitForPendingDomEditSaves`), but it only saw saves already queued in the DOM edit save queue or registered as pending edits. A canvas or panel edit counts from the moment its commit is called, and many commits spend a while before their first write: a resize parses the element's animations before it writes, and a nudge burst does not call its commit until 400 ms after the last arrow key. An undo in that window found nothing pending, stepped the history, and the save landed afterwards.

## How

- Every action that saves an edit, as the DOM edit context hands it to the canvas and the panels, registers its whole promise as a pending edit when it is called. Undo's drain already waits for pending edits, so it now waits for the edit on screen and then undoes it.
- The context's action list says, for each action, whether it saves an edit. The context's type is built from that list, so a new action can't reach the canvas until someone marks it.
- A nudge burst counts as a pending edit from its first arrow key until its save lands. So undo's instant paint stays off for the whole 400 ms wait for more keys, and can't show the edit before the burst undone. Undo's drain commits a burst still inside that wait and waits for its save.
- A failed edit rolls itself back and shows its error; it never entered the history. Undo waits for every pending edit and queued save to settle, landed or failed, and never stops on a failure: one Cmd+Z after a failed edit undoes the last edit that did save, as in other editors. Other callers of the save drain (render, export) still stop on a failed save.
- A burst always ends its pending edit, even when its commit throws, so a broken commit can't hold every later undo and export.
- One tracker, `trackedStudioEdit`, counts an edit as pending from its call: the context's saving actions, timeline edits, the Delete and z-order hotkeys, and every GSAP script commit (so keyframe resets and deletes from the keyboard count too). The drain reports what happened, failures and conflicts alike, because the outside-change check needs them; only undo waits failures out. A conflict no longer cuts the drain short: it waits for the edits still running, then reports the conflict.

## Measurement

Per-frame probe in the built Studio on the edit accuracy bench's gsap=none fixtures, px placement, no rotation, root, 100% zoom. Undo is pressed on the frame after release (or after the last arrow key), then the file and the screen are read 8 s later.

| case | main: file restored | branch: file restored |
|---|---|---|
| resize | no | yes |
| nudge | no | yes |
| crop | yes | yes |


The edit accuracy bench's sequence cases (gsap=none, 6 each), 3 jobs, all builds on base 3d8325e7a4d. "File checks" is every check except smoothness: tracking, drop, reload, undo.

| Sequence | main | this PR | this PR with #4857 |
|---|---|---|---|
| nudge one key, undo on the next frame | 0/6 | 6/6 | 6/6 |
| move, nudge three keys, drag back | 6/6 | 5/6 | 6/6 |
| rotate, nudge | 6/6 | 3/6 | 6/6 |

On main the nudge-then-undo cases fail drop, reload and undo: the nudge is never undone. This PR alone breaks some of the other two rows. The cause is #4857's bug: each save's temp file reaches Studio as an outside change, and its drain now commits a nudge burst early, splitting it into two saves. With #4857 all three rows pass; #4857 is merged and this PR is on top of it.

A real outside change that arrives mid-burst still commits the burst: the drain exists so a local edit lands before Studio accepts someone else's file, and holding the burst would let the outside reload wipe it or let it save over the newer file. Only the false outside changes were the bug, and #4857 removes them. Smoothness fails in most cases on every build on this machine, main included.

In CI the edit accuracy gate now passes the six nudge-then-undo cases, and the last commit banks them in `baseline.json` from that run.

## Test plan

- [x] `DomEditContext.test.tsx`: an edit committed through the context actions, whose save has not written anything yet, holds undo's drain until it settles; an edit that fails does not fail the drain. The first fails when the action is not marked as saving, the second when the registration keeps the rejection.
- [x] `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`: a burst counts as a pending edit from its first key until its save lands; undo's drain commits a burst still inside its wait and waits for its save. The first fails without the burst's registration, the second without the flush listener (the test runs on fake timers, so the burst's own 400 ms timer can't commit it). A commit that throws still ends the burst's pending edit; fails when that isn't in a `finally`.
- [x] `useEditHistoryActions.paint.test.tsx`, over the real history engine:
  - move, nudge, then undo inside the nudge's wait: the move never shows undone, and the undo ends with the nudge undone in the file and on screen. Fails without the burst's registration.
  - an undo pressed while a save fails in the real save queue undoes the edit before it, file and box alike. Fails when undo's wait stops on the failure.
  - an undo pressed while a tracked timeline edit fails still undoes the edit before it. Fails when undo stops on a failed edit.
- [x] `useAppHotkeys.previewForwarding.test.tsx`: Cmd+Z settles pending edits before it steps the history. Fails when the hotkeys skip the settle.
- [x] `studioPendingEdits.test.ts`: a drain that meets a conflict still waits for the edits that started while it ran (fails with the old early return); `trackedStudioEdit` counts a call until it settles and reports its failure.
- [x] `useGsapScriptCommits.test.tsx`: a GSAP script commit counts as pending from its call until it lands. Fails without the tracker.
- [x] Studio typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt; the full Studio suite.

title: fix(cli): select containing source frames in snapshots
body:
## What

Snapshots select the source video frame whose presentation interval contains the resolved source time. For a 24 fps source sampled at 0.4, 22/30, and 10/30 seconds, that means frames 9, 17, and 8.

## Why

Seeking FFmpeg directly to an off-grid time discards the containing frame and returns the next frame. This shifts a baked video plate by one source frame relative to other renderers.

## Related work

Fixes #4763. Implements the source-presentation-timestamp approach approved in [the issue discussion](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues/4763#issuecomment-5920857278).

PR #4767 addresses a separate VFX post-injection capture issue (#4762); this change addresses source-frame selection.

## How

1. **Pick the frame.** ffprobe reads packet timestamps and keyframe flags, with no decoding, up to one second past the requested time. The read is measured from the stream's start, so it also covers an edit-list trim whose preroll begins before the first visible frame. Times are measured on the file's clock from the stream's exact integer start. The selected frame is the last one whose presentation time is at or before the requested time, with a small floating-point tolerance. A time before the first frame (audio leading the video) holds the first frame, as the engine does.
2. **Find a decode start.** Demuxers do not always land where they are asked: an MPEG-TS seek can land a whole keyframe group later, and an open-GOP keyframe is not a clean decode start. So, starting from the latest keyframe at or before the frame (at most three candidates), the extractor runs a stream-copy probe (`-c copy`, no decode). That probe reads which keyframe the seek actually lands on. The first candidate that lands at or before the frame, and lands on that same keyframe when sought again, is used.
3. **Extract.** FFmpeg seeks accurately to exactly that keyframe, which trims its open-GOP leading frames. It then selects the frame by its time relative to the first decoded frame (`select=gte(t-start_t, …)`), so the result does not depend on where FFmpeg puts zero for a given container. If no candidate qualifies, it decodes from the start of the file.

Both rendered-video injection and `--against` reference extraction use this rule.

Trim, playback-rate, automation, loop, and clip visibility time mapping remain in their existing shared runtime paths. A held tail samples the actual last containing frame.

Cost per sample: one ffprobe call for stream metadata and one for packets, up to six short stream-copy landing probes, and one decode from the chosen keyframe. On a 5-minute 1080p clip, a sample near the end took under 0.8 s in both MP4 and MPEG-TS. The 30-second extraction bound remains, and probing has its own 30-second/32 MiB output bound.

Without ffprobe, extraction falls back to a plain seek (the first frame at or after the time), as before. One case is not covered on that path: a held tail past the last frame returns no frame.

## Test plan

- Snapshot suite: 70 tests passed. They use real FFmpeg extraction, each compared against a full-decode `select=eq(n,k)` frame. They cover:
  - frames 9/17/8 on a 24 fps grid, exact boundaries, an irregular VFR interval and held tails;
  - fragmented MP4, MPEG-TS and MP4 with B-frames, and open-GOP MPEG-TS;
  - a start time that rounds down, and an edit-list stream-copy trim;
  - MPEG-TS with leading audio, MP4 with late video, and a TS whose timestamps start below zero (with and without ffprobe);
  - an open-GOP TS with a keyframe every 15 frames;
  - unreadable sources, which blank only that video.
- Each regression test was confirmed to fail on the commit before its fix.
- The producer ffprobe argv contract passes (87 tests).
- CLI typecheck passed.
- Repository pre-commit checks passed: typechecks, lint/format, fallow (no new findings), tracked artifacts, large files, and commitlint.
- No browser pixel reproduction is claimed for this source-extractor change.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: refactor(studio): place the selection chrome from rect variables on one wrapper
body:
## What

The selection chrome now takes its position from four CSS variables on one wrapper. The resize dots, the rotate handle, the rotation plane's transform-origin and the crop frame are each placed with `calc()` over `--hf-chrome-left/top/width/height`, and React writes those four variables from `overlayRect` at render. Every on-screen position is the same as before.

This is the first half of taking the chrome's React work off pointermove. Today every move or resize pointermove sets the overlay rect state, and about ten chrome components re-render on every step. The follow-up change in the gesture handler will write these four variables on the wrapper per pointermove, so the whole chrome follows with one style write and the rect state is set once on release. On its own this PR changes no per-frame cost, and the selection box itself keeps its numeric position until the gesture-side change, because the gesture handler still writes `box.style` directly.

The variable names have one owner, `domEditChromeRect.ts`.

## Test

`DomEditSelectionChrome.test.tsx`, "moves every handle with the rect while their own styles stay the same":
- it renders the chrome at two different rects;
- it checks that the six handles' own `left`/`top` styles are identical between the two renders, so only the wrapper changes;
- it resolves each handle's `calc()` against the wrapper's variables and checks it lands where the numeric formula used to put it (dots, rotate handle, crop frame).

On main's source it fails: the handle styles differ between the rects.

title: fix(studio): start timeline drops on an empty lane at 0 and snap to clip edges
body:
## What

A media file dropped on an empty timeline lane now starts at 00:00 instead of wherever the pointer was. Before, a drop on an empty lane left a gap before the clip (for example, a clip starting at 2 s with nothing before it).

- **Empty lane, new lane, or empty timeline:** the drop starts at 0.
- **Lane that already has clips:** the drop lands at the pointer and snaps to the nearest clip edge within `TIMELINE_SNAP_PX` (8 px), the same radius a clip move uses.
- **Magnet off:** a drop on a lane with clips keeps the pointer time; an empty lane still starts at 0. The Magnet setting promises that drops never snap while it is off (`playerStore.ts` `timelineSnapEnabled`).

The drop preview and the saved drop read the same placement, so the preview shows where the clip will land.

## How

`placeDrop` in `timelineDragDrop.ts` now runs every placement through `alignDropStart`. That function gets the timeline's clips through a new `elementsRef` option and reuses `collectTimelineSnapTargets` and `snapTimelineTime`. The asset op still moves the start to the lane's nearest free time when it commits, as it did before.

## Tests

`timelineDragDrop.test.tsx`:
- New tests: an empty timeline, an empty lane next to filled lanes, and a snap inside and outside the radius. Each one fails on main.
- The two existing tests that drop on an empty lane (the appended lane and a new lane above row 0) now expect 0.
- The other harness tests get one far-off clip per lane, so they still test placement at the pointer.


## Review

An independent adversarial review ran at `72be3523` and a delta review at the current head.

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| MAJOR | Drops snapped with the Magnet off | Fixed in `c91f37cc`, with a test |
| MINOR | The "empty lane next to filled lanes" test sets up a row no real timeline has | Kept: it checks the rule directly |
| MINOR | A drop on an audio-group header row now starts at 0 | Matches the rule (no clips on that row) |
| MINOR | No direct start-time test for block or composition drops | They share the asset path's placement |
| MINOR | The Magnet-off test checks the commit, not the preview | Both read one placement function |

Mutations: returning the placement unchanged turns 5 of 20 tests red; removing the snap, ignoring a new track, removing the Magnet check or moving it above the empty-lane rule each turn exactly one test red.

## Before

Fixture project with a 4 s title clip on lane 1. An image is dragged onto the empty lane below, about 2 s in. The preview aims at 2 s, and the clip is written with `data-start="2"`, leaving an empty gap before it.

![Before: drop preview at 2 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be00c7ed-491b-4106-b334-eabe43fdaa9c)
![Before: clip written at 2 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b42c5c6-a2f3-4a09-a6d1-e4fc2042abed)

## After

Same drag on this branch. The preview and the written clip both start at 0 (`data-start="0"`).

![After: drop preview at 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/057f0bb5-3e93-42d8-8447-24ca176df148)
![After: clip written at 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cdd6f5fe-adfc-4553-a377-0c6a9f0420ca)

title: feat(studio): a host app can mount the dock with its own panels, storage key and width
body:
## What changed

Studio's dock can now be mounted by another app that lays out only some of Studio's panels:

- `Dock`, `useDockLayoutStore`, `DockController` and `PanelId` are exported from `@hyperframes/studio`. The dock's CSS already ships in `styles.css`.
- `Dock.Root` takes three optional props, each defaulting to what Studio does today:
  - `panels`: which of Studio's panels this dock has (preview and timeline always). The default layout, the Window menu and the stored-layout check use only these.
  - `storageKey`: keeps the dock's layout under its own key, plus `:projectId`, instead of Studio's preferences. It goes through Studio's own preference storage, which gains a `key` parameter.
  - `dockWidth`: the width the side columns are sized against, for a dock that does not span the window.
- The default layout is built from the panels the dock has. With all of Studio's panels it is the same layout as before.
- A panel reopened from the Window menu, when the panel it normally reopens beside is not in this dock at all, opens beside the preview on its own side. A neighbour that is only closed keeps today's behaviour.

Studio passes none of the new props, so its dock behaves exactly as before.

## Before

![Studio's default layout at 1440x900, main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6d4592c4-af9b-4933-8ea2-dc9d24b2a0c9)
![Studio's default layout at 900x600, main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57be9fe6-a74e-4b38-a2ee-b62f9ae2a6c7)

## After

![Studio's default layout at 1440x900, this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6b88cf68-f01d-4b23-805f-bcfda28e0f3f)
![Studio's default layout at 900x600, this branch](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d00c871e-c496-44e0-af9d-98863eb22ed5)

## What I measured

- Studio's default dock in a headless browser at 1440x900 and 900x600, Before (main's dock files) and After: every group's tabs, position and size are identical (`before-groups.json` = `after-groups.json`). The only pixel differences are thumbnails that finished loading at different moments.
- `Dock.test.tsx`, new cases for a dock of preview, timeline, assets and renders:
  - it builds only those panels, one side column each, and its Window menu lists only them;
  - it stores its layout under its own key and never in Studio's preferences;
  - it falls back to its default when the stored layout names a panel it lacks;
  - it reopens a panel beside the preview when its usual neighbour is not in the dock, and in Studio's dock a panel whose neighbour is only closed is added exactly as before (that test fails if the fallback keys on closed);
  - it sizes its sides against its own width.
- All Studio tests pass (559 files at the first head; the 63 dock and preference files again at this head), along with `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `comment-ratchet` and `check-comment-citations` on the changed files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- No app mounts a subset dock yet, so the new props are exercised by tests only.
- Dragging tabs between groups in a subset dock was not tried by hand.

title: feat: keep a video's sound on the clip by default (1/8)
body:
## Summary
A video with sound now keeps its audio on the `<video>` clip (`data-has-audio="true"`, no `muted`) instead of a muted video plus a duplicate `<audio>` of the same file. Silent footage and b-roll stay `muted`. This is the default the rest of the stack builds on: `hyperframes init`, the example templates, lint, the parser, Studio's audio toggle, the producer and the skills/docs all follow the same rule.

## Changes
- **cli**: `initMedia` is the single owner of init media placeholders. A clip with an audio stream is scaffolded audible and a silent file scaffolds `muted` (probed; `__fixtures__/silent.mp4`). Filenames are URL-encoded, `--audio` is probed for duration, and the from-file a-roll is timed.
- **registry**: the example templates keep the a-roll's sound on the video.
- **lint**: video audio rules recommend keeping sound on the video. Media rules know each clip's audio state, the double-source check is time-aware, and `duplicate_audio_track` covers video.
- **parsers**: a video is either audible (`data-has-audio`) or muted, never both. `updateElementInHtml` only applies `hasAudio` to videos.
- **studio**: the audio-track toggle follows the compiler's rule. Muted/has-audio edits are atomic, and a cutout keeps its sound on a linked `<audio>`.
- **producer / engine**: hidden videos are skipped when video audio is auto-added.

title: fix(studio): fade handles show a real tooltip and a 24 px target
body:
## What

A clip's fade handles in the timeline are easy to find and say what they do, even on a short clip:

- The fade-in handle sits at the clip's top-left corner and the fade-out handle at its top-right corner, whatever the fade length. The shaded wedge and the tooltip carry the length.
- The handles paint above everything Studio draws in the clip: the name label, the waveform and the thumbnail overlays.
- Hovering a handle opens Studio's own tooltip, "Fade in 0.3 s" / "Fade out 0.4 s", using the same seconds format as the slider's value text (0.25 s reads "0.25 s").
- Each handle has a 24 x 24 px hit box. On a clip narrower than two hit boxes, each one takes half the clip's width, so they never overlap. The visible dot stays 10 px.
- The dot is opaque white with the existing dark ring (it was 55% white), so it reads on the clip in both the default and the paper timeline theme.
- The fade wedges are clipped to the clip's rounded corners. Before, they spilled past the corners.
- A press in a hovered clip's top corners now only changes a fade. It no longer starts a trim or a move there. That is a deliberate trade so the handles are easy to find.

## Why

On a short clip with fades, the dots sat near the middle of the clip top (at the end of each fade), half under the name label and the content layers. The wedge lines ran past the rounded corners. The only label was a native `title` that competed with the clip's own native `title`.

## Related work

Follows #4250, which added the fade handles.

## How

All in `TimelineClipFades.tsx`, plus one token in `theme.css`:

- Position: the hit box is `left: 0` for fade in and `left: width - hitWidth` for fade out, where `hitWidth = min(24, width / 2)`. The drag was already relative (fade length at press, plus pointer travel divided by pixels per second, clamped as before), so dragging from the corner behaves the same. Inward travel still lengthens each fade. The 2 px threshold and `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` are unchanged.
- Stacking: the clip button is its own stacking context (it is positioned and has a z-index). Inside it, the name label is z 6, the waveform layer and the thumbnail label are z 10, the selection ring is z 4, and the fade handles were z 6. The handles are now z 30.
- Tooltip: the existing `Tooltip` from `components/ui` wraps each handle with `${label} ${formatFadeSeconds(value)} s`. The handle keeps `title=""` so the clip's native title does not show over it.
- Wedges: the ramp `<svg>` takes `overflow: hidden` and `borderRadius: inherit`. The clip button carries the radius inline (8 px for a visual clip, 21 px for a sound clip). The handles are siblings of the svg, so they are not clipped.
- The dot keeps `flex-shrink: 0` and `pointer-events: none`, so on a clip narrower than two hit boxes it stays 10 x 10 and the hit box alone takes the press.
- Escape: a press never focused the handle, so Escape only reached the handle's own key handler if something else had focused it, and the release then saved the dragged fade. This was there before this PR. The drag now listens for Escape on the window (capture phase) while it lasts, the same way the timeline's range band does. It restores the fade and saves nothing, and the handle's own key handler is gone.
- `theme.css`: `--timeline-fade-dot-active` (its only use was the dot) becomes `--timeline-fade-dot: #fff`.

## What I measured

Unit tests in `TimelineClipFades.test.tsx` (17 tests), each change broken once:

- Corner position: `expected '18px' to be '0px'` (and `'288px'` for a 3 s fade).
- Relative drag from the corner (clip-local x, press at 12 and move to 162, which should give 2.5 s): the absolute-position variant fails with `expected last "vi.fn()" call to have been called with ...`.
- Stacking: `expected 6 to be greater than 10`.
- Short-clip hit boxes: `expected [ '0px', '24px' ] to deeply equal [ '0px', '15px' ]`.
- Tooltip format with a 0.25 s fade: `expected 'Fade in 0.3 s' to be 'Fade in 0.25 s'`.
- Wedge clip: `expected 'visible' to be 'hidden'`.
- Escape with focus elsewhere: press, drag past the threshold, keydown Escape on `document.activeElement`, release. On the previous head this fails with `expected "vi.fn()" to not be called at all, but actually been called 1 times` (the fade was saved).
- With the change: `TimelineClipFades`, `TimelineClip` and `Tooltip` tests, 3 files, 32 passed.
- Real layout: `tests/e2e/fade-handles.mjs` (puppeteer-core against the Studio dev server, the same pattern as the timeline viewport gate, run in that CI job) opens a tracked fixture with a 0.1 s sound clip, which is 18.75 px wide at the default zoom, and measures both dots with `getBoundingClientRect`. With the change: 10 x 10. Without `flex-shrink: 0`: `fade-in dot is 9.375x10, expected 10x10`. The unit test also checks the computed `flex-shrink` and `pointer-events`.

Other checks:

- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio is clean, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files, and `comment-ratchet` and `check-comment-citations` pass.
- In Studio's dev server (headless Chrome, 2x), with a 1 s video clip with sound at the default zoom (187.5 px wide), fade in 0.3 s and fade out 0.4 s, hovering each handle in both themes:
  - The hit boxes sit at the clip's two top corners. Each dot is 10 x 10, and its centre is 13 px from the clip's left edge or 11 px from its right edge.
  - Hit tests at five points on each dot land on the handle, so nothing covers them.
  - The tooltip reads "Fade in 0.3 s" / "Fade out 0.4 s".
- Wedge spill: each frame was compared with the same frame with the ramps hidden, counting changed pixels outside the clip's rounded shape (2 device px of slack for anti-aliasing). On main: 15 to 18 px outside. With this change: 0, in both themes.
- The fade-in dot overlaps the top-left of the name label chip by 11 px x 6 px. The dot paints above it.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real pointer drag in the browser (the drag path is covered by the unit tests).
- Touch input.
- Clips under about 20 px wide, where the two 10 px dots overlap slightly (by 0.6 px on the 18.75 px fixture clip).
- The larger top-corner targets take the top 18 px of each trim edge. The lower part of the trim edge still trims. Not measured by hand.
- Headless screenshots do not render native tooltips, so the Before captures show none. That the clip's title is suppressed is checked only as `title=""` in the DOM.

## Test plan

- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

A 1 s clip with fade in 0.3 s and fade out 0.4 s on main: the dots sit inside the clip at the end of each fade, next to the name label, and the wedge lines run past the rounded corners. Default theme, then paper theme; fade-in hovered, then fade-out.

title: fix(studio): let only user input hold back font list idle work, and retry after a failure
body:
Stacked on #4794. Retarget to main once that merges.

## What

Three follow-ups to the idle font-list processing:

1. **Only the user's input holds the work back.** The idle gate used the overlay loop's awake window, and that window is also extended by playback frames and by programmatic wakes. During a long playback the picker therefore stayed on the popular fonts. The gate now reads its own last-input time, which comes from pointer, key and wheel events only (`INPUT_EVENTS`; the loop's wake sources are those plus scroll, resize and visibility). The input listeners attach with the first overlay subscriber, so input that happens before the lists arrive still counts.
2. **A failure in the idle step no longer leaves "Loading" forever.** The step catches the error, logs it, and clears the request, so the next mount or picker open retries.
3. **Input that lands after an idle slice was queued holds that slice back.** A test now covers this; the behaviour was already there.

## Tests

`overlayFrameLoop.test.ts`:
- "holds an idle slice when input lands after it was queued";
- "does not hold idle work for playback frames or programmatic wakes".

`propertyPanelFont.test.tsx`:
- "retries on the next open when processing the lists throws".

All three fail with the two source files at #4794's head. With the re-check at the idle callback removed, the first one fails.

title: fix(studio): one Cmd+Z pressed inside the preview takes one undo step, not three
body:
## What

One Cmd+Z (or Ctrl+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z, Ctrl+Y) pressed while focus is inside the preview now takes exactly one history step. Before, it took three: after two edits, a single undo with the preview focused went back past both of them.

## Why

Studio listened for history keys three times on the preview: the app hotkeys on the iframe's window, plus a history-only forwarder on both that window and its document. A press inside the preview reached all three, and each one stepped the history.

## How

The history-only forwarder is deleted. The app hotkeys listener on the iframe window already handles undo and redo with the same typing-target guard, so the preview now has one listener and one owner of the shortcut, and the press is tracked like any other shortcut (the forwarder skipped telemetry). `handleUndoRedoKey` goes back to main's shape and is no longer exported.

Same function, adjacent bug: the cleanup removed the window listeners without the capture flag they were added with, so it never removed them. It now passes the flag, matching `usePlaybackKeyboard`.

## Test plan

- [x] `useAppHotkeys.previewForwarding.test.tsx`: one Ctrl+Z in the preview takes one undo step and is tracked once; the same for redo via Shift+Cmd+Z and Ctrl+Y; after unmount a press does nothing and the listener is removed with the capture flag it was added with. Main's listeners fail the step cases (3 steps); this branch's previous de-dupe fails the tracking cases (0 tracked); dropping the capture flag from the cleanup fails the unmount case.
- [x] Built Studio, gsap=none bench crop fixture: one Ctrl+Z in the preview after three crops sends 3 history steps on main and 1 with the fix (captures below, taken on the previous head of this branch, which reached one step by de-duplicating events instead).
- [x] Studio typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt (CI).

## Before

Three crops on a bench fixture element in the built Studio, focus inside the preview, then one Ctrl+Z. Main takes three history steps: the element and the file go back past all three crops to the start.

![Before: one Ctrl+Z walks back three crops](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d390dd3e-acaf-4325-94a9-57e6575dee18)

## After

The same single Ctrl+Z takes one history step: the element and the file go back to crop 2.

![After: one Ctrl+Z walks back one crop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f1136f9-aba9-4ef8-8bfa-296c8aeca69a)

title: fix(studio): a rotate keeps a transform-centred element in place
body:
## What

Rotating an element centred with `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` (the common centring idiom) keeps it in place, while dragging and after the save.

The CSS `rotate` property applies before `transform`, so a turn written there also turns the transform's translate: the box swung around its old centre (62 px on the bench's centred box) and, with the plain-CSS rotate save, stayed there. Now, when the element's transform translates it, the turn is written into that transform after the translate (`translate(-50%, -50%) rotate(25deg)`), which turns the box about its visual centre. A second rotate replaces its own trailing `rotate()` instead of stacking one. The CSS `rotate` property is still the target for every element whose transform does not move it. Where the turn goes is read once at press, so the draft does no per-frame style read; the save writes the same value the draft drew.

The authored transform is read from the inline style, else from the last matching stylesheet rule (specificity, `!important` and `@media` are not weighed; noted in the code).

Stacked on #4802.

## Score (edit accuracy bench with the transform-centred rotate rows from #4801, `^rotate-none-transform-`, 4 cases, same machine)

| | all but smoothness | teleport (worst swing while dragging) | drop |
|---|---|---|---|
| #4802 (before) | 0/4 | 0/4, 62.4 px | 4/4 |
| this branch (after) | 4/4 | 4/4, 0.0 px | 4/4 |

## Tests

- `manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`: a transform-centred element with an authored `rotate: 30deg` turns inside its transform after the translate, leaves the `rotate` property alone, and a second turn replaces the first.
- `plainRotation.test.ts`: the save patches the transform as drawn, and a failed save puts the inline transform back.
- Each fails with its fix reverted (never taking the transform path, appending instead of replacing, not restoring the transform).

## Before

A transform-centred box after a 25 deg turn: swung off its centre.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/50b3ae86-eb87-49c0-853d-649056a7318f)

## After

The same case turns in place.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ad3e1dd-854a-483e-92fe-4ea43460cd4d)

title: fix(cli): capture snapshot --at at the exact requested instant
body:
## What

`hyperframes snapshot --at <t>` now captures the DOM at exactly `<t>` instead of flooring it onto a 30fps grid.

## Why

Snapshot seeks through `renderSeek`, which quantizes every time onto the runtime's canonical frame grid. Snapshot never injects a render fps, so that grid is the 30fps default whatever the project's `data-fps` says. On a 29.97fps project, `--at 19.019018` rendered 19.000 and `--at 19.05` rendered 19.0333. Snapping to the project's own grid instead would still miss: `19.019018 < 570/29.97`, so a 29.97 floor lands on frame 569.

## Related work

Fixes #4430

## How

- `renderSeek` takes an additive, opt-in `exact` option next to the existing `subFrameDivisions`. With it set, the time is seeked as given (clamped at 0). Without it, quantization is unchanged.
- `seekCompositionTimeline` gets an `exactTime` option, and `snapshot` passes it for every capture. The DOM now matches the time the PNG is named after, which is also the time its `<video>` frames and `--against` reference frames are extracted at.
- Frame export never sets the flag, so render output is unchanged.
- `snapshot --help` now says each `--at` time is captured at that exact instant, not snapped to a frame.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - The issue's sweep as a runtime regression on a 29.97fps project: an exact `renderSeek` lands 19.019018 and 19.05 where asked, and a default `renderSeek` still floors them to 19.0 and 19.0333.
  - Engine: every seek frame capture sends to the page, with motion blur off and on, carries no `exact` option. This pins export to the default quantization.
  - Player: an exact seek lands off every frame grid. The existing "still floors onto the output frame grid" test is kept.
  - CLI: `snapshot --at 19.019018` asks for `exactTime: true`, and `seekCompositionTimeline` forwards `{ exact: true }` to `renderSeek`.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the synthetic repro from the issue (29.97fps, linear 1000 px/s tween) back-solves to 19.0190 and 19.0500 (main gives 19.000 and 19.0333).
- [x] Documentation updated (`snapshot --help`)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): open projects named with a colon and keep preview assets for names with #
body:
## What

Studio opens a project whose folder name contains a colon, such as `Customer story: Northwind`. Before this, Studio refused the id, and any view that builds the project's API path (the composition stack among them) threw `Invalid project ID`.

The preview also keeps a project's own assets when its name has a URL character. The injected `<base href>` used the raw name, so a project named `Take #2` got the base `/api/projects/Take #2/preview/`. The browser cut that at `#`, and every relative asset loaded from `/api/projects/Take%20` and 404'd. A `"` in a name ended the attribute early.

## Why

A colon is a legal folder character on macOS and Linux, and `encodeProjectId` already encodes it (`%3A`), so the API path and the hash route stay one path segment. On Windows a colon can never be part of a folder name; there it means a drive (`C:demo`) or a file stream (`demo::$INDEX_ALLOCATION`), which `resolve()` and `isPathWithin` do not see. So a leading drive letter stays refused everywhere, and the dev server refuses any colon id when it runs on Windows.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `isValidProjectId` refuses a leading drive letter (`WINDOWS_DRIVE_PREFIX`, `/^[a-z]:/i`) instead of any `:`. `/`, `\`, control characters, `.` and `..` stay refused.
- The dev server's `resolveProject` (`vite.adapter.ts`) also refuses any id with a colon when `process.platform` is `win32`.
- `preview.ts` builds the root preview's and every sub-composition's `<base href>` through one `previewBaseHref`, which encodes the name with `encodeURIComponent` once (the route hands over the decoded name). The fallback page served when the bundler fails now gets the same base; before, it had none, so its relative assets 404'd for every project.
- Known limit: a macOS folder whose name starts with one letter and a colon (Finder shows `A/B test` as `A:B test` on disk) still reads as a drive and stays refused.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `projectRouting.test.ts` adds "opens a folder whose name has a colon, encoded once both ways" (encode, API path, hash round trip). The existing rejection cases, including `C:` and `C:demo`, are unchanged.
  - `vite.adapter.projects.test.ts` adds "opens a folder named with a colon, which Windows would read as a file stream and refuses": it resolves on Linux, and returns null with `process.platform` set to `win32`. Removing the Windows guard fails it.
  - Both files: 42 of 42 pass on Linux.
  - `studio-server/src/routes/preview.test.ts` adds "encodes the project name in <base>, so a '#' or '"' in it keeps assets in its own folder". It covers the root preview and a sub-composition for `Take #2`, checks that `logo.png` resolves under `/api/projects/Take%20%232/preview/`, and checks that a `"` arrives as `%22`. Against `origin/main`'s `preview.ts` it fails (`/api/projects/Take #2/preview/`).
  - It also adds "keeps the encoded <base> when the bundler fails and the page is read from disk"; removing the base from the fallback fails it. The file: 82 of 82 pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: `hyperframes preview` from source on Linux, serving a fixture project in a folder named `Customer story: Northwind`, opened at `#project/Customer%20story%3A%20Northwind` in Chrome at 1440x900. With `origin/main`'s `projectRouting.ts`, Studio never leaves its loading screen ("Waiting for preview server…") although the server is up. With this change, it opens the project with its preview, compositions and timeline. The only console errors were two `/api/environment/ffmpeg` 404s, the same in both runs.
- [x] The new test fails against `origin/main`'s `projectRouting.ts` and passes here (23 of 23 in the file).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

title: fix(studio): the properties panel no longer hands GSAP an element it does not position
body:
## What changes

Selecting a layer that GSAP only fades, colours or otherwise animates without moving no longer hands that layer's position to GSAP. Its next drag or nudge then moves it by its own CSS `translate`, the same way #4799 moves a layer GSAP does not animate at all.

Before, the Properties panel read GSAP's x, y, rotation, scale and depth values for any layer with a tween, on every frame while it was selected. Any GSAP read of a transform value makes GSAP's CSS plugin fold the layer's CSS `translate`, `rotate` and `scale` into GSAP's own transform. From then on GSAP counted as owning the layer's position, so selecting a fading title was enough to send its next move through `gsap.set`.

## How

`readGsapRuntimeValuesForPanel` (`propertyPanelHelpers.ts`) still reads every non-transform value it read before, such as opacity and border radius. It reads GSAP's transform values only for a layer GSAP positions (`gsapWritesPosition`, the same check the move uses). For any other layer the panel falls back to the values it already shows when GSAP has none: the layer's CSS translate for X/Y, Studio's own rotation value (`--hf-studio-rotation`) for rotation, and identity in the 3D section.

The list of GSAP transform channels is `GSAP_TRANSFORM_KEYS` in `gsapRuntimeKeyframes.ts`. It is GSAP 3.15's CSS plugin transform list, including `transformOrigin`, `svgOrigin`, `force3D` and `smoothOrigin` and the aliases, minus `transform` itself, which GSAP reads without parsing. GSAP doesn't expose that list at runtime, so it is copied, and a test pins the origin case.

## Test

`gsapLivePreview.test.ts`: "the panel reads GSAP's transform only off an element GSAP positions". For a fade-only tween the panel reads only `opacity`; for a tween that moves the layer it reads the full transform set, as before. A fade with `transformOrigin: "0 0"` also reads only `opacity`. With the new guard removed, the fade case fails because the panel reads the nine transform channels too. With the four origin keys missing from the list, the origin case fails.

## Before

Main, a fixture with one box placed by its CSS `translate: 40px 30px` and a GSAP tween that only fades it (`opacity: 0.4`). Selecting the box with the Design panel open and dropping a +90/+60 move: the panel shows X 130 / Y 90, and the file gains `gsap.set("#target", { x: 130, y: 90 })` in the timeline script, with no change to the box's own `translate`.

![Before: the drop on main, Design panel open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0ca67210-81fc-4ca2-bd06-81642c33eb97)

![Before: the saved source gains gsap.set on line 19](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40bfcdd2-3bc5-46f8-9b85-0fd2ac8318f8)

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this branch. The panel shows the same X 130 / Y 90, and the only change to the file is `style="translate: 130px 90px"` on the box, with no `gsap.set`. The source view is shown after reloading Studio.

![After: the drop on this branch, Design panel open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7702fcbf-8adf-4ccc-81ee-0116e338de49)

![After: the saved source changes only the box's inline translate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/633a89d5-b83b-417f-8e05-ff2da720baf8)
