title: fix(studio): a layer with a min(), max() or clamp() translate moves from where it really is
body:
## What changes

A layer without GSAP whose CSS `translate` uses `min()`, `max()` or `clamp()` now moves from where it really is. That includes a layer that has a `transform` transition.

To read such a translate, main wrote a temporary inline `transform` onto the layer and read it back. If the layer has `transition: transform ...`, the browser reports the transition's starting value instead, so main read the layer's offset as 0,0. The drag then started off by the layer's own translate: 46.65 px for `translate: clamp(0px, 10%, 30px) min(40px, 25%)` on a 240x160 box. The drop landed that far off, and the file got the wrong translate. Without a transition, main's temporary write is removed in the same step of code and no frame shows it. Measured in the built Studio, both main and this branch then have a press jump of 0 px.

## How

`readTranslatePx` (`plainTranslate.ts`) now evaluates the computed `translate` itself: px, %, `calc()`, `min()`, `max()`, `clamp()`, parentheses and `+ - * /`. It reads the computed value first, where Chrome has already resolved `em`, `vw`, `vh`, `var()` and simplifiable functions such as `abs(-10%)`, so only % is left to work out. % resolves against the box `transform-box` names: the content box for `content-box` and `fill-box`, otherwise the border box. The temporary-transform reader is deleted.

Anything outside that grammar, such as `abs(10% - 50px)` or `round(10%, 7px)`, which Chrome keeps unresolved, evaluates to NaN rather than to a guess. Studio then refuses to move the layer, says why, and leaves the layer as it was:
- A drag or arrow-key nudge shows "Studio can't read this layer's translate. Move it in the Code tab." Before, a drag showed a generic toast and a nudge did nothing.
- The Properties panel disables X and Y and commits nothing.

Checked in headless Chrome 152 against the layer's real on-screen movement, including padding and border, for eleven values:
- plain px and %;
- the calc, min, max and clamp forms;
- `em`, `vw` and `vh` inside them;
- `calc(50% / 3)`;
- `abs(-10%)`.

All eleven match to 0.0001 px.

## Tests

- `plainTranslate.test.ts`:
  - "works out %s by arithmetic": the min, max, clamp and nested calc forms.
  - "reads %s as NaN, never as a guess".
  - "resolves a percent against the content box under transform-box: content-box / fill-box". Both fail if % always resolves against the border box.
  - "writes nothing to the element while it reads min(10px, 5%) clamp(0px, 10%, 30px)": a MutationObserver on the layer during the read.
  - With main's `plainTranslate.ts` in place, 9 of the original 18 fail, the MutationObserver one included.
- `manualOffsetDrag.test.ts`: "refuses a translate it can't read instead of guessing". It fails with the guard removed.
- `previewReadOnly.overlay.test.tsx`: "refuses a drag and an arrow nudge out loud, and commits nothing". It fails if the reason isn't passed on.
- `propertyPanelTransformCommit.test.ts`: the X/Y fields "are disabled" and "commit nothing and say why". The latter fails with the panel guard removed.


## Before

Main, a layer without GSAP with `translate: clamp(0px, 10%, 30px) min(40px, 25%)` and `transition: transform 0.4s`, dragged +90/+60. The layer is off by 46.65 px (its own translate) from the first move to the drop, and the file saves `translate: 90px 60px` instead of `114px 100px`. The dashed outline and cross mark where it was released.

![Before: the layer drops 46.65 px from where it was released](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/98416551-94b2-4fee-9cef-8a2978eeea17)

## After

Same layer and gesture on this branch. It is 0 px off at every step and at the drop, and the file saves `translate: 114px 100px`.

![After: the layer drops where it was released](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b2995043-c20f-452b-aa18-4b5bf9abd1cc)

title: CLI: expose engine motionBlur on `hyperframes render` (e.g. --motion-blur[=json])
body:
## Problem

v0.8.45/v0.8.46 added engine sub-frame motion blur (`motionBlur` on the render configuration: true shutter integral, adaptive 16–64 samples/frame) — a genuinely great feature. But as of v0.8.101 it appears unreachable from the CLI: `hyperframes render --help` lists no flag for it, and tracing the published bundle shows every read coming from `job.config.motionBlur` with no CLI-flag or project-file source feeding it on the local render path.

## Ask

Expose it on the CLI render command, e.g.:

```bash
hyperframes render --motion-blur -o out.mp4                    # defaults (adaptive samples, 180°, phase -90)
hyperframes render --motion-blur='{"samplesPerFrame":32}' ...  # explicit config
```

(or a `render.motionBlur` key in `hyperframes.json`, whichever fits the config model better.)

## Why

Teams rendering exclusively through the CLI (our case: scripted/batch production pipelines) currently can't use the engine blur and fall back to external N×-fps + ffmpeg `tmix` blending, which is strictly worse than the adaptive shutter integral the engine already computes. If there IS a supported local path I missed, a pointer in the render docs would also resolve this.

Happy to test a nightly. Related contribution from the same pipeline work: #4785.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(studio): a move keeps the route it chose at press through drop and save
body:
Stacked on #4830.

## What changes

A move decides whether it moves the layer by its own CSS `translate` or through GSAP once, when the gesture starts. The drop and the save then use that decision instead of deciding again.

Before, a drag decided the route three times: at press (`createManualOffsetDragMember`), when the commit arrived (`handleGsapAwarePathOffsetCommit` and the group preflight), and in the stager (`stageElementOffset`). If GSAP took the layer over between those points, the press could draft one way and the save write the other.

If GSAP has folded the layer's translate into its own transform since a CSS-route press, the save is refused, because a CSS write at that point would apply the move twice. The user sees "The animation took over this layer's position during the move, so it was not saved." and nothing is written. The refusal also resets GSAP's x/y/xPercent/yPercent to 0, which on the CSS route only ever hold the folded draft, and the gesture's own rollback puts the CSS translate back, so the layer returns to where it started. A real rotation or an authored inline transform such as `rotate(45deg) scale(1.5)` is kept. Checked in Chrome with GSAP 3.15: the box is back at its start, and still there after a seek.

A fold is "GSAP's cached x/y/xPercent/yPercent are non-zero", not merely "GSAP has parsed the transform": a parse with nothing to fold leaves them at 0, and that move saves normally. A group runs the same check in its preflight, so a group with one taken-over member writes no member at all. Since #4830 nothing on the drag path asks GSAP about a layer it doesn't position, so this is a guard, not an expected path.

## How

- **Drag and nudge** carry the press's decision (`member.plainTranslate`) on the commit: single moves through `MoveCommitOptions.plainTranslate`, group moves on each `DomEditGroupPathOffsetCommit`.
- **`handleGsapAwarePathOffsetCommit` and the group commit** use the carried route. They decide with `gsapWritesPosition` only when nothing was carried, which is the panel's and webmcp `moveTo`'s case.
- **`stageElementOffset`** takes the route as a required argument and no longer decides on its own.
- **The panel's X/Y commit** decides once, reads the current position for that route (`readMoveOffset(el, plainTranslate)`) and passes the route to the commit.
- **Unchanged:** a group member that isn't the selection keeps today's rule, decided at press without a fetch. The anchor move of a GSAP resize decides at its own entry, as it does today.

## Open item

Resize and rotate still read GSAP's x/y/rotation off an element GSAP doesn't position: the resize anchor base in `startGesture`, the resize anchor member, and the GSAP resize settle. #4805 (resize) and #4802 (rotate) rewrite exactly those lines and are still open. Once they merge, those reads move under this one decision, with a test that resizing a fade-only box leaves its next move on the CSS route.

## Tests

Each one fails with its piece of the fix reverted:
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`: "drops on the route it chose at press, even if GSAP takes the element over mid-drag".
- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: "keeps the route a gesture chose at press", for the CSS route on a layer GSAP has since taken over and the GSAP route on a layer that now looks GSAP-free, single and group.
- `useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`:
  - "refuses a CSS move GSAP has folded into its x/y, writes nothing, and hands the translate back", and its other side, "saves a CSS move GSAP has only parsed, with nothing folded into its x/y".
  - "leaves a later move's translate alone when an earlier move's save fails": the stager's rollback only puts its own value back.
- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: "writes no member when one CSS-route member has been folded since the press".
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.test.ts`: "drops every member on the route it chose at press" (group).
- `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`: "commits an element without GSAP on the CSS route".
- `propertyPanelTransformCommit.test.ts`: the panel reads and moves a GSAP-free layer by its translate and passes the route it chose.


## Before

Main with #4830, a box with `translate: 40px 30px` and a GSAP tween that only fades it, dragged +90/+60 with GSAP made to fold the box's translate into its own x/y partway through (`gsap.getProperty(box, "x")`). From the fold on, the box is 114.86 px off the pointer, and the save writes `gsap.set("#target", { x: 224, y: 156 })`, counting the translate twice, so the box ends 273 px from where it was released. White dotted: where it started. Pink dashed and cross: where it was released.

![Before: the box lands 273 px past the release and the file gains gsap.set](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7d38db8a-49c8-4c2a-87ac-24fe39d31365)

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this PR's head. Studio shows "The animation took over this layer's position during the move, so it was not saved.", the file is not changed, and the box goes back to where it started (0 px from its start). White dotted: where it started. Pink dashed and cross: where it was released.

![After: the save is refused, the file is unchanged and the box is back at its start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/acf504ce-1060-46c8-bab7-06cd56ba93d3)

title: feat(studio): graphite colour system with a light theme that passes contrast
body:
## What changes for a person using Studio

Studio's colours move to Graphite: a softer, lifted dark (the shell was near-black), and a full light theme. Every text pairing clears WCAG 4.5:1 and every icon, border, dot and focus ring clears 3:1, on every surface and state it can sit on. The player and the audio meter stay dark in both themes.

## How

- **One value per colour.** Each token in `theme.css` is `light-dark(light, dark)`, so the `color-scheme` where a colour is painted picks its half. Studio is dark; `data-theme="paper"` on the document element (the existing host hook) makes it light; the preview pane and the audio meter set `scheme-dark`, so they stay dark inside a light Studio with no copied values. The scheme rule sits in the base layer, so a host's own `color-scheme` wins.
- **Roles, not new names.** Existing public tokens keep their names and take Graphite values. Missing roles are added: `raised` (menus, popovers), `press`, `on` / `on-hover` (toggle on), `accent-hover`, `accent-ink` (accent text), `on-accent` (text on an accent fill), `ring`, `danger-ink`, `on-danger`, `warning-ink`, `text-off` (disabled only). States and lines are washes of the text colour (`color-mix`), so they work on any surface.
- **Stock colours stay stock.** `white`, `red-*` and `amber-*` keep their upstream values, so a host's own palette is untouched. `--color-neutral-*` points at roles by the job each step does in markup (light steps are text, dark steps are surfaces and lines).
- **Call sites that meant a role now say it.** Studio text, lines, dots and focus rings that used stock white, red, amber, orange, green or purple on a Studio surface use roles: timeline lane labels and tree lines, caption selection and focus rings, hover labels on inspector buttons, notices (FFmpeg, colour grading, VFX, motion), status dots, invalid-field borders, the ease curve grid and curve, the border-radius preview, the Shortcuts key caps. White stays where it sits on media, a scrim, a solid fill or a colour picker. Accent buttons are the solid accent with its hover step, popovers sit on `raised`, flat buttons go hover then press; the timeline toolbar has four readable states (idle, hover, on, on+hover).
- **File-type icons** keep their brand hue in both themes, with a darker light half that holds 3:1 on a hovered or selected row.
- **The dock follows the theme.** dockview's runtime stylesheet pins `color-scheme: dark` on its default theme class; the shell around Studio's dock now inherits Studio's scheme.
- **Contrast proof in CI.** `scripts/contrast.ts` reads `oklch()`, `light-dark()`, `color-mix(... transparent)` and nested `var()`, and a theme can reuse another's pairs (`pairsFrom`). The manifest measures every timeline pair and every chrome role against every fill it sits on, in both themes: 146 pairs pass, and the debt baseline (11 failing timeline pairs on main) is empty. A second test measures every file-type icon colour on a row at rest, hovered and selected, in both themes.
- Root fixes the ratchet surfaced: trim-handle grips were drawn at 60% of their fade opacity, so they could not hold 3:1 on a hovered clip; the pending-track label was dimmed twice (a muted token plus `opacity: 0.5`).

## Before

Main, dark (main has no light theme for the editor; its `paper` hook only recoloured the timeline).

![Before: dark editor shell, after every thumbnail loaded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b06876b5-554d-4392-b3e1-376317ecc917)
![Before: dark clip menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/252da788-82d8-4fff-b730-b269fe66cfc6)
![Before: dark Shortcuts panel and property panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/97134c47-6d61-4354-aa10-a5d41290eb65)
![Before: dark code tab and file tree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e411f541-19f0-4088-800a-3c3b801e2a6f)

## After

Dark, then light (`data-theme="paper"`), on the repo's `product-promo` example.

![After: dark editor shell, after every thumbnail loaded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a28707da-c73d-4ed9-8275-c6e0df6e7f81)
![After: light editor shell](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0beb1aec-6a5a-4c7e-8f58-469f49b2fbc8)
![After: dark clip menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cadb9528-b634-4220-829f-e68e3123563e)
![After: light clip menu](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5b9dd69-ee3e-4880-a6a4-f19cad3dbf7d)
![After: dark Shortcuts panel and property panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e61434f4-fc19-42e9-a906-eff8226bb0e7)
![After: light Shortcuts panel, player stays dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cb19cfcf-11c6-4915-9ad1-060e1296ccf5)
![After: light code tab, file-type icons](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5de7907d-05cd-4c3f-a9f7-828ab6c8a572)

## Three window sizes

The editor shell at 1280x800, 1440x900 and 1920x1080, dark then light. The rendered sweep finds 0 items under target at every size in both themes.

![1280x800, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2e076101-7d41-4c05-b429-bb8757ed4780)
![1280x800, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0b50297a-07fb-4bc6-8ed8-11703efff612)
![1440x900, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5203100f-bb15-40d4-aba1-01eb34e1b11e)
![1440x900, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f9068249-a2fb-4a2b-91a0-69519d571f0a)
![1920x1080, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f0846bd-c1ab-40e3-8085-06528ceae62e)
![1920x1080, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a98c72b5-6cdc-4f4d-8f5c-af9fcf950a36)

## Rendered contrast, measured in the built Studio

A headless Chromium 147 sweep of every visible text run (4.5:1) and svg icon (3:1) against the colours actually painted beneath it, at 1440x900. Failing items out of items checked.

| View | Main, dark | This PR, dark | This PR, light |
|---|---|---|---|
| Editor shell (timeline, property panel) | 40 of 102 | 0 | 2 (lint badge) |
| Clip menu open | 43 of 108 | 0 | 2 (lint badge) |
| Shortcuts panel open | 36 of 111 | 2 (lint badge) | 2 (lint badge) |
| Assets tab | 34 of 91 | 2 (lint badge) | 2 (lint badge) |
| Catalog tab | 33 of 95 | 2 (lint badge) | 2 (lint badge) |
| Code tab | 74 of 161 | 42 (code editor) | 42 (code editor) |

The Layers, Renders and Variables views keep the code tab open beside them, so they show the same 40 to 42 code-editor items and nothing else.

## Named exceptions

- **The code editor** keeps CodeMirror's One Dark theme in both Studio themes; its gutter and some syntax colours sit at 3.6 to 4.4:1. That theme is third-party and unchanged here; whether the editor should follow Studio's theme is a separate call.
- **The lint count badge** pulses its opacity (`animate-pulse`); at the trough its label dips below 4.5:1, at rest and at the peak it passes. Left as is; the pulse is the badge's signal.
- The deprecated Tailwind v3 JS preset stays at its old values. v3 cannot read `light-dark()` or `color-mix`; `theme.css` is the source.
- `light-dark()` needs Chrome 123, Safari 17.5 or Firefox 120. Verified in Chromium 147 only.
- A host that imports `theme.css` and themes by its own attribute sets `color-scheme` itself (light or dark); tokens it does not override then follow it.

## Verification

- `scripts/contrastRatchet.test.ts`: 146 pairs, 0 baseline debts; the file-type icon test fails when one icon goes back to its old light colour (1.68:1, the same figure the rendered sweep measured).
- `packages/studio`: the full unit suite, 6310 tests pass. The hex ratchet baseline is lowered.
- `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio: exit 0. oxlint on the changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. oxfmt: clean. `fallow audit --base` (the CI command): exit 0.

title: refactor(studio): delete the move writer no Studio path calls
body:
## What changes

Deletes `handleDomPathOffsetCommit` from `useDomGeometryCommits`. It is the old move writer that adds a move as `--hf-studio-offset-x/y` on top of the layer's translate, and no Studio path calls it.

Every move in Studio reaches `handleGsapAwarePathOffsetCommit` instead:
- the canvas drag and nudge, through `ConnectedDomEditOverlay`;
- the Properties panel's X/Y, through `StudioRightPanels`;
- webmcp's `moveTo`;
- host apps, which read the session's `handleDomPathOffsetCommit`.

`useDomEditSession` maps that name to the GSAP-aware handler. It never takes the `useDomGeometryCommits` one, which `useDomEditCommits` returned without anyone reading it.

## How

- Removes the handler from `useDomGeometryCommits` and from `useDomEditCommits`'s return.
- Deletes `buildPathOffsetPatches`. Since #4805 the resize writes its anchor as a plain translate, so the deleted handler was its last caller. `applyStudioPathOffset` stays: the seek re-apply and the drag still use it.
- The box-size, rotation and reset writers in the same hook stay, and so do the snapshot helpers and `buildClearPathOffsetPatches` (Reset).
- Removes the tests of what is gone:
  - the handler's three tests (one line of the rollback test and the two read-only-preview offset tests);
  - `buildPathOffsetPatches`'s own tests and its combined-with-box-size tests (`manualEditsDomPatches.test.ts`);
  - the persist-seam case that saved its patches (`persistSeam.integration.test.ts`);
  - the anchored-resize "persist and reload" case that modelled the old offset-variable resize save (`anchoredResizeReleaseShift.test.ts`). The anchor-loop tests in that file stay.
- Rewords the comment in `manualEditsDom.ts` that cited `buildPathOffsetPatches`.
- Deletes the GSAP fallback guard (`rejectGsapCssFallback`), the hook's `previewIframeRef` parameter and `gsapTargetCache.ts`. Since #4802 the rotate no longer uses the guard, so the deleted handler was its last caller and the cache's only consumer; their `.fallowrc.jsonc` entries go too.
- Adds `gsapTargetCache.ts` to `ALLOWED_DELETIONS` in `scripts/check-no-main-deletions.mjs`, with the reason.

## Proof it was dead

`git grep -n buildPathOffsetPatches` now finds nothing. `git grep -n handleDomPathOffsetCommit` in this repo finds the name only in:
- the session alias;
- the context;
- the overlay and panel wiring;
- webmcp;
- this hook, its `useDomEditCommits` passthrough and its tests.

The session's `useDomEditCommits` destructure (`useDomEditSession.ts`) never took it.

## Tests

`useDomGeometryCommits.test.tsx`, `useDomEditCommits.test.tsx`, `manualEditsDomPatches.test.ts`, `manualEdits.test.ts`, `persistSeam.integration.test.ts` and `anchoredResizeReleaseShift.test.ts` pass, and so does the whole studio suite (6289 tests). Studio `tsc`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the changed files.

## Before

Main at this PR's merge base, a box with no GSAP and `translate: 40px 30px`. Typing X = 100 in the Layout row saves only `style="translate: 100px 30px"` on the box; dragging it +90/+60 then saves only `style="translate: 190px 90px"`. Each panel shows the Studio after that step; below them is the saved file's diff for each step.

![Before: X = 100 saves translate 100px 30px, the drag saves translate 190px 90px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1bc606a5-1d42-45a5-82f5-0d8a814659d4)

## After

Same fixture and steps on this PR's head: the same two saves, `style="translate: 100px 30px"` and then `style="translate: 190px 90px"`, byte for byte the same files as on main.

![After: the same two saves as on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c43dd74-d8c2-4194-8004-3deb55d2be57)

## What

Fade handles in Studio are easier to grab and show a real tooltip. Layers positioned with min(), max() or clamp() move from where they really are, and projects named with a colon or # open correctly.

## Included

- #4819 fade handles show a real tooltip and a 24 px target
- #4832 a layer with a min(), max() or clamp() translate moves from where it really is
- #4829 open projects named with a colon and keep preview assets for names with #

## No visible change

Version numbers and release notes only. The changes above shipped in their own PRs with their own captures.

title: feat(studio): a light and dark theme toggle in the header that remembers the choice
body:
## What changes for a person using Studio

A sun and moon button in Studio's header flips between light and dark, with a circular reveal from the button, the same control as hyperframes.dev's theme toggle. Studio opens light the first time; after that the saved choice comes back on the next load from the first frame. The player stays dark in both. With reduced motion on, the theme switches without the reveal.

## How

- `utils/studioTheme.ts` owns the rule for Studio's own app: the saved choice (`theme` in Studio's existing `hf-studio-ui-preferences`), else light. Light is `data-theme="paper"` on the document element, the hook `theme.css` keys on; dark is no attribute.
- A short inline script in `index.html` applies the same rule before the first paint, so the saved theme paints from the first frame. `studioTheme.test.tsx` reads that script out of the parsed `index.html` and runs it against every saved value (including junk, `null` and unparsable storage) and holds it to the owner.
- The button shows the theme that is on screen, read from the document, so it stays right when something else changes the theme (another tab's save, a host).
- `ThemeToggle` is the header's ghost icon button with a tooltip, before Window. While its own transition runs it marks the document element, and only then is the browser's default crossfade switched off, so other view transitions on the page keep theirs.
- **Hosts own their theme.** The header shows the toggle only inside `ShowThemeToggle` (a context that defaults off), and only Studio's own `main.tsx` provides it. A host that embeds `StudioApp` gets no toggle, and Studio never writes `data-theme` for it. `App.tsx` is unchanged.

## Before

![Before: header has no theme control](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f016e3bd-ff7e-4f0d-ab51-873971dd1e8e)

## After

The repo's `product-promo` example at 1280x800, 1440x900 and 1920x1080.

![After: header, first run opens light, moon button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e4913a41-ce3f-4b3c-b11a-40546ac1215f)
![After: header, light, hovered](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/233ac765-f1d4-4b54-8bf0-419c4eec0a08)
![After: mid-reveal, dark growing from the button (captured with the animation slowed 4x)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3b83ca5b-7b77-45e4-89a6-0438ad545305)
![After: header, dark after one click, sun button](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4109aada-5d46-4145-8127-74371158fdac)
![After: 1280x800, first run, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b149362c-6ef7-48e8-98ae-e4f37caffc86)
![After: 1280x800, after one click, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afb90423-434e-4405-9805-607bf2c7c69a)
![After: 1440x900, first run, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9870e257-2185-4122-8b8c-38554cbd78aa)
![After: 1440x900, after one click, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/76b3b244-7401-4be1-b67f-142030be3bfb)
![After: 1920x1080, first run, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f3c368c-f7f9-4779-9fb5-08d984f9dbc6)
![After: 1920x1080, after one click, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/75189d53-ba30-45d9-8bb4-162ed3697711)
![After: dark after a reload, the choice kept](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2469b6db-1604-4ff5-a1fc-852a3306d771)

## Verification

- `studioTheme.test.tsx`: the boot script equals the owner for saved light, dark, nothing, junk, `null`, unparsable and non-object storage; first run is light; boot runs before the app module; a click flips and saves, a second click flips back; the button follows a theme set by someone else. The reveal tests stub view transitions: a keyboard press grows the circle from the button's centre to the far corner, the document is marked while the reveal runs and cleared after, a second click mid-reveal keeps the marker until its own reveal ends, and reduced motion switches with no transition. Making the button read storage, ignoring reduced motion, using the click point for a keyboard press, never setting or never clearing the marker, or letting an earlier reveal clear a later one's marker each fails its test.
- `StudioHeader.dom.test.tsx`: a header mounted with no provider (as a host mounts it) shows no toggle and leaves a host's `data-theme` alone; inside the provider it shows the toggle. Defaulting the context to on fails the first.
- 39 tests across those two files and `studioUiPreferences.test.ts` pass. `tsc --noEmit` on packages/studio: no errors. oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- In the built Studio (headless Chromium 147, the repo's `product-promo` example): the first load is light, a click reveals dark from the button (the only animation is the circle's clip-path; the crossfade is off while the marker is set, and the marker is gone after) and removes `data-theme`, and a reload boots straight into dark.

title: fix(studio): a moved layer holds through seeks and Reset puts back its authored translate
body:
## What changes

A layer that an older Studio moved with its offset variables (`--hf-studio-offset-x/y`, the `data-hf-studio-path-offset` mark and a `translate: var(...)`) now keeps today's move. Before, the move saved `translate: 140px 30px`, but the old mark and variables stayed. On the next seek, and after every reload, Studio re-applied them and put the preview back at the old position. The file, and so the render, had the new one, so the two disagreed. A resize that keeps such a layer's centre planted had the same problem.

"Reset layer edits" after a plain move now puts back the translate the author wrote, in the file and in the live preview at once. Before, for a layer Studio had only ever moved by its own translate, Reset removed the translate from the file (losing an authored `translate: 12px 4px`) and left the moved one in the preview until the reload.

## How

`writePlainMove` (`plainTranslate.ts`) is now the one place a plain translate is saved, for a move and for the resize anchor. It sets the layer's own `translate` in px, live, and returns the save's patches. If the layer still carries a legacy offset, the same call removes the offset variables and the path-offset mark, live and in the same patch, so the file and the preview change together. The seek re-apply needs both, so it no longer touches the layer.

The author's translate has one record: the existing `data-hf-studio-original-inline-translate` mark (empty when there was none).
- A legacy layer already has it, and the move keeps it.
- For any other layer, `writeTranslatePx`, the one live writer of a plain translate, records it on the first write of a gesture (the drag's first frame, a nudge, the panel), so it holds the author's value, not a drafted one. Later moves leave it alone. A cancelled drag restores the snapshot taken at press, mark included.
- Every plain move saves the mark with the translate.

Reset reads that mark: the file gets the author's translate back (or none), and `clearStudioPathOffset` now restores the live preview whenever the mark is present, then clears the marks. Undo of a Reset brings back the saved file from before it, mark included, so a second Reset works again.

Studio runs this Reset only when a GSAP animation is added to a layer that still has the old offset mark (`useGsapSelectionHandlers.ts:243`). It has no button, so there is no capture of it; the tests below prove it.

The move still starts from where the layer really is: the press reads the computed `translate`, which already resolves the old `var()` form, so nothing jumps.

On a failed save, `stagePlainTranslate` (`elementOffsetStager.ts`) and the resize (`useDomGeometryCommits.ts`) restore the whole snapshot (`captureStudioPathOffset` / `restoreStudioPathOffset`), so a legacy layer gets its mark and variables back, not only its translate. As before, the move does this only if the live translate is still the one it wrote.

## Known limit

In two rare cases the recorded original is not the author's, so a Reset restores the wrong place:
- a layer a plain move saved before this PR, which has no record, so the first move after it records the earlier move's translate;
- a moved layer later moved through the old offset-variable fallback, which records its translate at that point again.

Nothing in Studio calls Reset by hand today, so neither is reachable from the UI.

## Tests

`useDomGeometryCommits.test.tsx`. The Reset tests patch a real source string with `applyPatch`, so they check the saved file, not only the patch list. Each fails with its piece of the fix reverted:
- "a plain move of an element an older Studio moved by its offset vars":
  - "saves the move as its translate, ends the old offset, and a seek keeps it". It fails if the move leaves the variables and mark.
  - "resizes with the anchor as its translate, ends the old offset, and a seek keeps it". It fails if the resize writes only the translate.
  - "puts the old offset back whole when the move / resize save fails". Each fails if its rollback restores only the translate.
- "Reset after a plain move puts the author's translate back":
  - "restores an older Studio's layer to its authored 50% 10px, in the file and live", with no marks or variables left. It fails without the `clearStudioPathOffset` change.
  - "restores the authored 12px 4px after a drag and a second move"; "removes the translate of a layer that had none, in the file and live"; "undo of the Reset brings the move back, and Reset still restores the author's". Each fails both without the first-write record and without the `clearStudioPathOffset` change.

`useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`'s GSAP-free move now expects the mark in its patch.

## Before

Main, a box with no GSAP saved by an older Studio (`data-hf-studio-path-offset` plus `--hf-studio-offset-x: 40px; --hf-studio-offset-y: 30px`), dragged +100/+0. The drag starts from 40/30 without a jump, but at release the box snaps back to 40/30 and stays there after seeking, while the file saves `translate: 140px 30px` and keeps the old vars and mark.

![Before: the box snaps back to 40/30 while the file says 140px 30px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e5dc1874-9332-4656-a356-30de24f0092d)

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this PR's head. The drag starts from 40/30 without a jump, the box stays at 140/30 after the drop and after seeking, and the file saves only `style="translate: 140px 30px"`, with the vars and mark gone.

![After: the box stays at 140/30 and the file drops the old vars and mark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a21e5647-e44b-4d17-8c14-526bf8308341)

title: fix(studio): Escape keeps the text you typed in an in-place edit
body:
Pressing Escape while editing text in place in Studio threw away everything typed in that session. It now keeps it, the same as Enter and clicking away already do. Cmd+Z (Ctrl+Z) takes the edit back.

This matches how Figma, Keynote and Canva treat Escape in an on-canvas text edit, and it removes the one exit from an inline edit that silently lost work. `event.preventDefault()` stays, Enter and blur are unchanged, and no option or prop was added. `cancel()` is still there for the read-only path, which closes an open session without saving.

Escape during an edit is not also handled elsewhere in a way that matters: the save resolves from the edited element, not from the current selection (`handleDomRichTextCommit` in `useDomEditTextCommits.ts`), and the app hotkey Escape forwarded from the preview only acts while the razor tool is armed. The captures show the element still selected after Escape.

## What I measured

- `useInlineTextEdit.test.tsx`: 32/32 pass. "cancels on Escape" is now "commits on Escape". A new test types into a focused element with a styled run, presses Escape, and checks the save happens exactly once and carries the original styled markup as `previousHtml`, which is what a failed save restores.
- Both tests are not vacuous: with the source put back to `cancel()` they fail (2 failed, 30 passed), and pass again restored.
- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the touched files, and `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs`: all clean.
- In Studio's dev server on the repo fixture `packages/studio/tests/e2e/fixtures/design-panel-qa`, driven by Playwright: double-click the headline, End, type "!", Escape, then Ctrl+Z. Each capture's header shows the live preview text and the headline line read from `index.html` on disk at that moment.
  - Before: Escape puts "Static Headline" back and the file is unchanged.
  - After: Escape keeps "Static Headline!" and writes it to the file. Ctrl+Z ("Undid: Edit text") restores "Static Headline" in both the preview and the file.

## What I did NOT exercise

- macOS Cmd+Z: the capture ran on Linux, so it used Ctrl+Z, which goes through the same undo handler.
- Escape while an IME composition is open (Japanese, Chinese input). The browser normally uses that Escape to cancel the composition. I did not check whether the keydown reaches this handler with `isComposing` set.
- Escape with the inline text toolbar's own controls focused, and the full studio suite. CI runs those.

## Before

Typed "!" with the edit open, then Escape: the text reverts and nothing is saved.

![Before: typing with the edit open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/53b6ac60-1014-4800-977c-f695a658523e)
![Before: after Escape the text reverts and the file is unchanged](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d11b6831-6ea4-40d9-aa90-fb169f4d1bd1)

## After

Typed "!" with the edit open, then Escape: the text stays and is written to the file. Ctrl+Z restores the original.

![After: typing with the edit open](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b98c82f-313c-4556-92dc-baec63cfa922)
![After: after Escape the text stays and the file is written](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17cb122a-4c1d-48eb-8d5a-29575575eb4d)
![After: Ctrl+Z restores the original text in the preview and the file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2bd3330f-3095-4f97-8423-dddc251dd312)

title: fix(studio): undo and redo are no longer held behind thumbnail renders
body: ## What Under load, an undo of an edit inside a nested composition could paint at once while its file write landed 2.5 to 15 seconds later, or not at all within 15 s. A reload in that window brought the edit back. The same wait hit redo. Undo and redo now reach the server at once, so the write lands within a few hundred milliseconds. ## Why The browser allows six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin, and everything Studio sends to its server shares them. One goes to the `/api/events` stream for the whole session. Thumbnail renders took the rest: the server renders them one after another, so under load each request held its connection for seconds (up to 20 s to its headers). The thumbnail scheduler is meant to own thumbnail work and caps composition renders at 2. But two callers went around it: - each sidebar composition card pointed an `` straight at the render route; - the preview poster started its background render with a bare `fetch`. An edit bumps the content revision, so every edit started a fresh set of card renders, while the previous revision's renders kept their connections. Undo's first request, the file read before `POST /history/step`, then waited in the browser's queue until a render finished. In a traced run, the read was requested 9 ms after the key and went out at 9,394 ms. The server answered it in 2 ms. In two traced runs on main (72 cases), the five reads that waited 2.9 to 16 s had 6 or 7 requests open at the key, and three more were still waiting when the bench gave up. On this branch, no more than 3 were ever open. ## How - The sidebar card takes its frame from the thumbnail scheduler, through the same lease the timeline thumbnails use. It renders the frame from the scheduler's object URL. - Like main's lazy ``, a card asks only once it comes within 200 px of the composition list's visible area (the list is the observer's root, so the margin applies), so offscreen cards cost nothing. - When the card moves to a new revision, it keeps showing its last frame, and keeps that frame leased, until the new one is ready. Then it lets the old lease go. The retaining lease is taken in a layout effect, before React's passive cleanup drops the first one, so an entry the scheduler has already evicted is never released in between: not revoked, and not rendered again. - A render still loading for a stale revision is aborted. A finished frame's object URL is revoked when the scheduler evicts it, never while shown. - A failed render shows "Preview unavailable" and retries at the next revision, as before. - The poster's background render runs as scheduler work too. A new `discardWhenReleased` request option keeps that result out of the cache, so a later missing poster renders again. - So every composition render now shares the scheduler's cap of 2. Composition renders plus the event stream hold at most 3 connections, which leaves room for Studio's own requests. Other thumbnail kinds, video and image, keep their own caps as before. - `compositionThumbnailRequest` builds the request for the timeline thumbnail and the sidebar card alike. The card asks in the timeline's session and as rich work, so a composition shown in both makes one render. Opening the studio-open fixture now makes 15 thumbnail requests instead of 22: one shared fetch per scene, plus the root's and the poster's two. The work-count ceiling is banked at 15 from this PR's CI evidence, and its old note for a raise is gone, since 15 is below main's 22. CI now runs Chrome 154, and `perf-ratchet.mjs lower` refuses evidence from a browser other than the one the file records (153). So the ceiling and its browser were set by hand to exactly what the CI job measured; the other three counts were unchanged on 154. The file read before the step stays. It gives the in-place restore the file as it is now. That differs from this tab's own copy when another writer changed the file, so this tab's history can't stand in for it. Making the step's reply carry both sides of each file would remove the read; this PR leaves it alone. ## Bench The edit accuracy bench now fails the undo check when an undo or redo write lands more than `UNDO_WRITE_MAX_MS` (2,000 ms, exported from `report.mjs`) after its key. It also records the save latency, from release or the last nudge key to the edit's file write. The nested gsap=none move and nudge cases (36), at 6 jobs, on one machine, base e3ac225a9ce, measured at this PR's first commit (the branch was then rebased onto 3e011b7e5f4 without conflicts; the later commits change how cards load, not the undo path): main and this branch ran side by side twice, under the same load (15 to 27). Times are from the key or release to the file write, in ms. "Never" means the write did not land within the bench's 15 s. | Run | Undo write p50 / max | Undo writes over 2 s | Redo write p50 / max | Save write p50 / max | Undo's file read p50 / max | Requests open at the key, max | Undo check | Reload check | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | main, run 1 | 68 / never | 3 | 94 / 2,688 | 144 / 360 | 16 / 16,049 | 7 | 30/36 | 34/36 | | branch, run 1 | 68 / 282 | 0 | 75 / 580 | 100 / 324 | 18 / 91 | 3 | 36/36 | 36/36 | | main, run 2 | 96 / never | 5 | 112 / 2,737 | 108 / 310 | 19 / 15,161 | 7 | 28/36 | 33/36 | | branch, run 2 | 70 / 242 | 0 | 75 / 448 | 124 / 490 | 16 / 88 | 3 | 36/36 | 36/36 | Save latency did not change in these cases: an edit's save goes out before its own revision bump starts new renders. ## Test plan - [x] `CompositionsTab.thumbnails.test.tsx`, eight tests: - the card renders through the scheduler and never points an `` at the render route; - six cards plus the poster render keep exactly the cap in flight, and all seven still run; - a stale revision's render is aborted, and its frame's object URL is revoked on eviction, not the current one's; - a failed render shows the fallback and retries at the next revision; - a card asks only once it is near the viewport, so an offscreen card never renders ahead of a visible one; - a card keeps showing its last frame, still leased and not revoked, until the next revision's frame is ready; - it keeps that frame after the scheduler has evicted it (100 other cached entries): no second render of the old revision, and no revoke; - a card and the timeline thumbnail of the same composition make one request; What fails without what: - The first four fail with the card's old ``. - The cap test fails when the poster render fetches directly. - The viewport test fails without the viewport check, and its root assertion fails without the list as the root. - The eviction test fails with a second lease taken in a passive effect (this PR's previous head). - The last-frame test fails without the held frame. - The sharing test fails when the card asks as non-rich work. It passes with the old ``, so it pins the shared identity, not the move to the scheduler. - [x] `NLEPreview.test.ts`: a missing poster is rendered as scheduler work, so the fetch carries the scheduler's abort signal; it fails with a bare `fetch`. It is rendered again on a later visit; two cases fail when `discardWhenReleased` is ignored. - [x] `report.test.mjs`: the undo check passes an undo and redo whose writes land within `UNDO_WRITE_MAX_MS` and fails either one past it. Fails without the new rule. - [x] The three composition card test files share one mount helper, `compositionsTabTestUtils.tsx`. It also clears the scheduler's entries for the test project after each test. - [x] Studio typecheck, the Studio component, player and hook suites, oxlint, oxfmt. ## Before Ctrl+Z on a nested move in a bench fixture, 6 bench jobs, main. The undo's file read sits queued (red) behind six thumbnail renders and the event stream. It goes out at 9.4 s, and the write lands at 9,437 ms. ![Before: the undo's read queued behind thumbnail renders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1f2cf88f-f024-48bb-9a21-70fedac087e3) ## After The same case in the same window on this branch: two renders at the cap, the read and the step go out at once, and the write lands at 59 ms. ![After: the undo's read and step go out at once](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3bb29c1-f796-41d2-b677-25b494b01163)

title: feat(studio): fade handles ride the fade's end and the waveform shows the fade
body:
## What changes

Fade handles on a timeline clip now sit at the end of the fade, and an audio clip's waveform shows the fade itself.

- **The waveform shows the fade.** Each bar shrinks to the gain you hear at its centre (core `fadeGain`, linear, so it matches playback and render). The cut-away part of each bar stays as a faint ghost at 27% of its opacity, drawn only above the heard part. A 1 px dashed line marks the ramp.
- **A slim tab replaces the corner dot.** It is white, 4 x 15 px, and sits at the fade's end on the clip's top edge, following the rounded end of the pill. It grows `scaleY(1.2)` on hover and while dragged. The hit box is still 24 x 24 and centres on the tab, however long the fade. Two boxes that would overlap meet at the midpoint between their tabs. A handle with less than one 0.01 s step to move (a fade-out of 0 next to a fade-in that fills the clip) is not drawn, so it never covers its twin. A handle being dragged or focused always stays.
- **Clips without a waveform** (videos marked `data-has-audio`) keep the shaded wedge under the same dashed line.
- **Snapping.** The fade's end snaps to the playhead and to other clips' edges, using the timeline's own snap helper, radius (8 px) and snap switch. The clip's own start and end are never targets, so a short fade next to a touching clip, or with the playhead at the clip start, still drags. The tooltip says what it snapped to.
- **Keys and double-click.** The selected clip's handles join the tab order, each labelled with its clip's name. Arrows move 0.1 s, Shift+arrows 1 s, Home, Delete or Backspace set 0, End sets the maximum, and Enter on a 0 s fade adds 0.5 s. A held key previews live and saves once on release, so one undo step per press or hold. Keys are ignored while the handle is being dragged. Double-click switches a fade between 0 and 0.5 s.
- **A focused slider owns its plain keys.** A new `ownsPlainKeys` in `typingTarget.ts` (the typing check, plus `role="slider"`) is what the app's plain-key dispatcher, the canvas nudge and the caption nudge now ask. Before this, the window-level shortcuts saw Delete first and deleted the selected clip, and arrows could nudge the canvas selection. Cmd shortcuts (undo, redo, copy, paste, group) still ask `isTypingTarget`, so they keep working while a slider has focus. The timeline's focus handler also stops at a slider, so focusing a handle no longer pulls focus back to its clip. This applies to every `role="slider"` in Studio; most of them already handle their own keys.
- **A saved fade reaches the timeline store.** The quiet save already recorded automation and FX chains on the store's copy of the element; fades now go through the same path, and an undo's soft restore reads them back. Before this, the handle jumped back to the old value once its draft cleared.
- **A failed or refused save** drops the draft, rather than showing a fade the file never got. The save path already restores the live value.
- **Drags, keys and double-click all start from the same value:** the saved fade, or a pressed value whose save has not landed yet. A draft clears when its own save settles (the save syncs the store first), so a newer press survives an older save landing.
- **A fade pair that overruns the clip in the file** (a trim can leave one) steps from its saved values, as the inspector does. One change from main's drag: neither a key nor a drag moves a fade against its direction. On main, a grow drag on such a clip set the fade to 0 and the release deleted it. A single fade longer than its clip starts a drag or key from the clip's end, where it is drawn, so the first pixels of a shrink move it and a grow saves nothing.
- **Unchanged:** the saved attributes (`data-fade-in` / `data-fade-out`), the drag math, Escape-cancel, release-outside-the-window revert, and one write per drag.

How it is wired: the live draft moves up into `TimelineClip` (`useClipFadeDraft`). The clip's content reads it through `ClipFadesContext`, so the waveform redraws under the pointer before anything is saved.

## Tests

- `AudioWaveform.test.tsx`: the bars follow the fade gain, and the ghost is drawn at 27%. Replacing the gain with 1 makes this test fail.
- `TimelineClipFades.test.tsx`: the tab sits at the fade's end, plus snapping (playhead, clip edge, snapping off), double-click, the keys, and the tab order. Turning snapping off in the code makes the two snap tests fail.
- `automationStoreSync.test.ts`: a saved fade is recorded on the store's element, and an undo's soft restore reads it back.
- `tests/e2e/fade-handles.mjs`: the narrow-clip check now measures the tab, 4 x 15 in Chrome.

## Before

Main: the dot stays in the corner however long the fade is, and the readout shows there too.

![Before, default theme: hovered clip, corner dots](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2a0cbbd7-a9cc-452c-b82c-fcf59fb7b718)
![Before, default theme: dragging the fade-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4fc7d246-1a38-42a5-9bef-9d0dbdce4a98)
![Before, default theme: 1 s clip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ca55a515-2a3f-4771-a6ff-b70230900f96)
![Before, paper theme: hovered clip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/60dd0853-a4cd-42f6-af01-cbdcc7dad3be)
![Before, paper theme: dragging the fade-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/163a81cc-3f20-4edd-9703-259add826a6c)

## After

At head `ce57a0e`. The tab sits at the fade's end, the readout rides above it, and the bars shrink under the fade while the cut-away part stays as a ghost.

![After, default theme: hovered clip, tabs at the fade ends](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dca7515-a73c-453c-9e22-0402ee31d1ce)
![After, default theme: dragging the fade-in, live readout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48f3595b-634a-43fb-822d-f9b33502af5b)
![After, default theme: 1 s clip, two tabs kept apart](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13abd07b-ae1a-4ee6-8c5b-7ac513a9c072)
![After, paper theme: hovered clip](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/846fdb85-05b6-4d83-93a7-91fa8a99db5e)
![After, paper theme: dragging the fade-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d1715e15-ec9b-434b-8fba-84e12239ebfa)

Captured headless (Chrome 152, 1440 x 900 at 2x) from a fixture project: a 5.2 s music clip with a 3.1 s fade-in, a 1 s clip with fades on both ends, a long voiceover title, and a video with audio. The narrow-clip check (`tests/e2e/fade-handles.mjs`) passes at this head: each tab measures 4 x 15.

## Review

Six rounds of independent adversarial review. At `ae1ce8f4`: 2 blocking and 9 should-fix items. At `ce57a0e`: the first key-ownership fix had switched off Cmd shortcuts on focused sliders, and the full-length fade case was still open. At `1b3fac75`: a handle could vanish mid-drag after a trim left a fade-in filling the clip. Also open then: clip lengths that are not whole hundredths, double-click rounding, and missing call-site tests for the key paths. At `6389574a`: no blocking items; grow drags on an overrunning pair, the draft rule, and two fixes without a failing test. At `f4afab2c`: saved fades never reached the timeline store, so a handle jumped back after its save; a click without movement dropped a pending draft. At `c9ad0c36`: a single fade longer than its clip still had dead travel at the start of a drag. All are fixed at this head. Each fix has a test, and each test fails when its fix is reverted (mutations run against the Studio suite).

The timeline viewport gate failed at `1b3fac75` because `timeline-virtualization.mjs` still read `executablePath` after the shared Chrome launch moved. That is fixed here. On the same machine, branch and main measure the same interaction p95 (32.6 vs 32.9 ms). The gate's fixture has no audio clips.

The gate's virtualization-off arm (1,000 clips, all mounted) fails on a busy shared machine (load about 30) for main as much as for the branch: interaction p95 branch 79.7 and 98.2 ms, main 82.5 and 133.1 ms, alternating runs.

Scroll with waveforms on screen: the same gate harness, with every fixture clip turned into an audio clip with 0.4 s / 0.5 s fades and a real WAV (a local patch, not committed). 50,000 clips, row virtualization on, 160 clips mounted, branch and main alternating on one shared machine (load 17 to 37):

| Round | Branch interaction p95 | Main interaction p95 | Branch frame p95 | Main frame p95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1189 ms | 1653 ms | 1133 ms | 1600 ms |
| 2 | 1579 ms | 1827 ms | 1517 ms | 1750 ms |
| 3 | 891 ms | 814 ms | 867 ms | 767 ms |

The branch is within main's spread. Scrolling over audio clips is slow on main itself, about 25 times the plain-clip number on the same machine; that is separate from this PR and reported on its own.

Open notes, not changed: there is no snap guide line for a fade drag; a clip's drag ghost shows its waveform without the fade; a selected automation range still takes Delete before a focused handle; the handles sit inside the clip's `<button>`, as they did on main.

title: fix(studio): the timeline viewport gate judges p95 over every measured scroll step
body:
## What

The timeline viewport gate now judges scroll responsiveness on the p95 of every measured scroll step pooled, 315 steps over 5 runs at 63 per run, instead of requiring 4 of 5 runs to pass a p95 of 21 steps each. The 75 ms limit, the per-run long-task check and the memory check are unchanged.

## Why

The rollback arm (row virtualization off, 1000 rows) failed intermittently on PRs that don't touch the timeline. Evidence pulled from the gate artifacts of 160 main jobs and the failing PR jobs:

- **Not a cold run.** The failing runs sit at positions 1 to 5 at random, after the 3 warmups.
- **Not a page regression.** I traced main against a build from three days earlier on the same machine, on thread CPU time. Paint, pre-paint and layerize differ by under 5%, and no timeline commit lands near the change.
- **The runner pool changed.** Hosted runners fall into two speed classes: a fast one (median step 33 ms) and a slow one (49 ms). The slow class went from 56% of main's jobs (Sep 28 to Sep 30 09:00Z) to 79% (Sep 30 09:00Z to Oct 1 08:00Z). In a sample of main's jobs, its share of runs that fail went from 0 of 135 runs (27 jobs) to 7 of 120 (5.8%, 24 jobs) between those two windows. Over the 80 most recent CI jobs at review time, an independent count found 11 of 320 slow-class runs failing (3.4%); over the full windows the reviewer counted 1 of 255 runs before and 7 of 170 after. The fast class has never failed a run.
- **A run's p95 of 21 steps is its 2nd-worst step.** Two slow steps fail a run, so a build whose true p95 is under the limit still fails jobs.

Binomial model of the job failure rate, given the share q of scroll steps over 75 ms:

| q (steps over 75 ms) | before: 4 of 5 runs, p95 of 21 | after: pooled p95 of 315 |
|---|---|---|
| 1% | 0.3% | 0.0% |
| 2.5% (today's slow runners) | 7.6% | 0.6% |
| 5% (true p95 at the limit) | 43.7% | 51.0% |
| 8% (a real breach) | 82.4% | 98.3% |
| 12% | 98.1% | 100.0% |

## Tests

- The gate and the fade-handle check now share one Chrome launcher (`launchStudioChrome` in `chrome-executable.mjs`) instead of two copies of the same block.

- `timeline-viewport-verdict.test.mjs` (the verdict now lives in `timeline-viewport-verdict.mjs`, so it can be tested without Chrome): 16 slow steps of 315 fail and 15 pass; two slow steps in every run pass; one run slow throughout fails; a slow frame interval alone fails; a run short of samples throws instead of reading as fast; the gate fails when any one check fails. Each was run against a broken copy and fails: responsiveness dropped from the exit condition, the sample-count check removed, the verdict judged per run.
- `timelineViewportBudgets.test.ts`: the budget owner holds 63 samples per run.
- Gate sensitivity on a CI runner, with the do-not-merge draft #4848: this branch plus a fixed 45 ms main-thread stall on every timeline scroll step.
  - Rollback arm: pooled interaction p95 **89.0 ms, FAIL** (frame p95 66.7). The old rule fails it too (per-run p95 81 to 100).
  - Virtualized arm with the same stall: pooled p95 58.5 ms, so its 75 ms limit lets a 45 ms per-step stall through (frame p95 goes from 16.7 to 50 ms), as the old rule does too. Whether that limit is the right promise is an open question this PR does not change.
- This branch on a hosted runner of the slow class (per-run p95 50 to 64 on the rollback arm): pooled p95 60.2 ms on the rollback arm and 33.2 ms on the virtualized arm. Both pass.
- Added wall time per CI job: the rollback arm goes from 17 to 18 s to 34 s, the virtualized arm from 19 to 22 s to 32 s, and the gate step from 32 to 47 s to 69 s.

## Before

The old rule failing the rollback arm on changes that don't touch the timeline (CI gate artifacts):

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/564257c8-070e-4de0-8494-dd9bd68f99bb)

## After

The pooled p95 on hosted runners: this branch passes, and the injected stall fails:

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d8d613a-e66d-485f-a0f1-e1424649b095)
