title: fix(studio): a pasted element keeps the look its id gave the original
body:
## What

Copying and pasting an element on the canvas now gives the copy the same look as its original, when that look comes from CSS rules on the original's id.

## Why

A pasted element gets a new id (`badge` becomes `badge-2`) so the two stay separate. Clip paste already copies the rules keyed on the old id to the new one. Element paste did not, so a copy of an element styled by `#badge { ... }` showed up unstyled. Compositions often style elements by id, so those copies looked wrong.

## Related work

None.

## How

- Element paste now goes through the same `carryLook` that clip paste uses. When the element was copied from the file it is pasted into, each rule keyed on a renamed id is copied for the new id, and so is each animation on that id, at the same times, exactly as clip paste does.
- The element's clipboard entry now records the project it came from, as a clip's already does. A paste into another project's same-named file never borrows that file's rules.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `useClipboard.source.test.ts` copies and pastes an element styled by `#badge` and checks that the copy's computed color and letter spacing match the original's. Without the fix the copy reads `rgb(0, 0, 0)` and `normal`, and the test fails.
- [x] `useClipboard.test.ts`, `useClipboard.source.test.ts`, `clipboardPayload.test.ts` and `clipboardLook.test.ts`: 53/53.
- [x] Manual testing performed: Studio's dev server on a fixture whose one element is styled only by `#badge`. Pick it on the canvas, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V. On main the copy (`badge-2`) renders `rgb(0, 0, 0)`, `normal` spacing and no border; with this change it renders like the original.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

The pasted copy sits below the original with none of its look: black text on the dark stage, only its selection box shows.

![Before: the pasted copy is unstyled](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cbbc25a5-ca35-4cbe-b291-e45231b08b36)

## After

The copy looks like the original.

![After: the pasted copy matches the original](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a5673c4-7a63-429b-b874-6ff7979c5624)

title: fix(studio): an undo that lands mid-drag keeps the box under the pointer
body:
## What changes

Dragging a layer right after Cmd+Z no longer flashes it back to where the undo put it. The box stays under the pointer through the moment the undo lands, and the drop saves where you let go, on top of the undone file.

Before, if the previous edit's save was still pending when you pressed Cmd+Z, the undo only showed up once that save and the server's history step finished. If you had grabbed the layer by then, the undo copied every attribute of the restored file onto it, which wiped the translate the drag was drawing. For a frame, or for as long as the pointer stayed still, the box sat where the undo put it, the undone move's distance away from the pointer.

## How

`syncElementAttributes` (`gsapUndoRestore.ts`) is how every in-place restore writes a restored element onto the live one. It now also takes the element as the file being replaced had it. When the live element carries the manual-edit gesture mark (`data-hf-studio-manual-edit-gesture`), the merge keeps:
- the inline-style properties that gesture draws, whatever their value, so a press that hasn't moved yet keeps its spot;
- every other attribute and inline-style property whose live value differs from the replaced file, which the gesture changed since;
- for a move or resize, the record of the author's translate (`data-hf-studio-original-inline-translate`), so the drag's next write doesn't record its own draft as the author's.

Everything else restores as before, and a layer without the gesture mark is restored exactly as before.

What each gesture draws has one owner, next to the gesture mark in `manualEditsDom.ts`:
- a move draws `translate` and the offset variables;
- a resize draws those plus the box-size properties (`BOX_SIZE_STYLE_PROPS`);
- a rotate draws `rotate`, `transform`, `transform-origin`, `display` and the rotation variable.

- an edit (the inline text edit) draws nothing, so under its mark only what changed since the replaced file stays.

`beginStudioManualEditGesture` requires the kind, so a new caller has to say what it draws. The mark's value carries the kind.

Every live copy in the restore goes through the merge:
- `applyUndoRestoreToPreview`;
- `showRestoreInPlace`, and its put-back, which uses the restore it showed as the base;
- the edit-mark sync after a GSAP script re-run (`syncStaleEditMarks`).

This removes the jump once the undo lands. Painting the undo at once while the previous save is still pending is a separate change.

## Tests

`gsapUndoRestore.test.ts`, "an undo that lands while the layer is being dragged". Each fails with its piece of the fix reverted:
- "keeps the translate the drag is drawing and reverts the rest": the drag's translate and gesture mark stay; the undone width and `data-start` go back. It fails without the merge.
- "keeps the box where it is when the press has not moved it yet": it fails when only values that differ from the file are kept, as at this PR's first head.
- "keeps the drag's translate when the undo is shown in place", and "keeps a drag that started after the undo was shown when the undo is put back": each fails without its base.
- "keeps the drag's translate when the undo re-runs a GSAP script": it fails if the edit-mark sync copies without the base.
- "saves the drop onto the undone file, the same bytes as dragging the undone layer": the final file after the drop. It fails without keeping the author's-translate record.
- "reverts the translate under a gesture that draws nothing, such as a text edit": it fails if the edit kind keeps the move's channels.
- "restores a layer no gesture is drawing exactly as before": this test, and the existing "drops the size marks a resize left on the live element", fail if the merge also applies without the gesture mark.

## Edit accuracy rows

The 6 drag, undo, drag cases (`sequndo`, gsap none) from the edit accuracy bench in #4801, 3 runs each, at this PR's first head. Both builds use the same bench, 2 jobs. Each row shows the worst teleport, in px.

| case | main, run 1 / 2 / 3 | this branch, run 1 / 2 / 3 |
|---|---|---|
| px root | 312.4 / 312.4 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| px nested | 304.4 / 304.4 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| pct root | 0 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| pct nested | 304.4 / 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| center root | 0 / 0 / 301.2 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| center nested | 0 / 304.4 / 0 | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| failing | 6 of 18 | 0 of 18 |

The PR also takes 5 of the 6 cases out of the bench's `QUARANTINED` list (`ratchet.mjs`), where #4801 parked them for this fix, and banks them from this branch's CI gate artifact, byte for byte. In that gate, all 5 pass with no case unstable; 3 were newly passing, and the other 2 were already banked as passing on main, because the race only failed some runs.

`sequndo-none-px-r0-root-z100` stays quarantined, under the change that paints an undo at once (stacked on #4807). In one CI gate it passed 2 of 3 runs; the third had a press jump of 312.36 px. That matches the undo landing between the bench's read of the box and its press, which only painting the undo at once removes.

## Before

Main. A layer dragged, Cmd+Z right away, then pressed and held where it still shows; the move's save is slowed by 1.5 s so the undo lands while it is held. When the undo lands, the layer drops back to where the undo put it, about 100 screen px from the pointer (the ring), and stays there while the pointer holds still.

![Before: the box jumps away from the held pointer when the undo lands](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a802e3a5-865f-48a1-aad2-c045915fc6cf)

## After

The same steps on this branch. The undo lands ("Undid: Move layer") and the layer stays under the pointer. The drop saves `translate: 202.139px 216.578px` on top of the undone file, as on main.

![After: the box stays under the held pointer when the undo lands](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/153092c7-f9f6-491a-bd1d-7909b3856aee)

title: fix(studio): a focused video or audio player keeps its arrow and play keys
body:
## What changes

With a video or audio player focused (the asset preview's native controls), the keys Studio's shortcuts used to take from it now go to that player only: the arrow keys and Space, plus the playback letters (J, K, L and the rest) and the canvas, caption and snap keys. Before, the playback shortcuts claimed the arrows first: the timeline playhead stepped, the key never reached the player, and the playhead move closed the asset preview.

## Why it was broken

Every Studio key handler asks "does the focused element own this key?" before acting. The shared answer (`isTypingTarget`) covers text fields, editors, switches and comboboxes, but not a native media player, which seeks and plays with these keys itself. The playback shortcuts and the canvas nudge both relied on it.

## What this does

- `ownsPlainKeys` in `utils/typingTarget.ts` (added by #4844 for sliders) now has one list of controls that own their plain keys: `[role='slider']`, `video[controls]` and `audio[controls]`, on top of anything `isTypingTarget` claims. There is no second predicate.
- The playback shortcuts (`shouldIgnorePlaybackShortcutTarget`, which the timeline player's key handler also goes through), the canvas arrow nudge, the caption-word arrow nudge and the preview's S/G snap keys use it, and so does the app's plain-key dispatcher (#4844), so Delete on a focused player no longer deletes the selected clip.
- Three handlers kept their own copy of the text-input check: the timeline's N (snapping), K (add keyframe) and the automation selection keys (Delete, Cmd+C, Cmd+V). They now call `isTypingTarget`, so a focused picker such as the font combobox keeps its keys there too.
- The slideshow panel's in-panel Cmd+Z checked only `INPUT` and `TEXTAREA`, so Cmd+Z in a contenteditable or a select undid the panel instead of the text. It now calls `isTypingTarget` (a Cmd shortcut belongs to a text field, not to a slider).
- The playback shortcuts' own selector list dropped its slider, combobox, switch and textbox rows: `ownsPlainKeys` runs first and already claims them.
- `shouldHandleTimelineDeleteKey` was dead code (re-exported from `Timeline.tsx`, called only by its own test) with its own copy of the typing check. Deleted with its tests.
- Deliberate: N, K and the automation keys now also ignore a focused switch or combobox, the same as the app hotkeys already do. After flipping a switch (focus stays on it), K does nothing until focus moves.
- The snap keys keep their existing exclusion of a focused preview iframe: a key aimed at the composition is not a Studio shortcut.

## Handlers checked

| Handler | Keys | Predicate |
|---|---|---|
| Playback shortcuts (`usePlaybackKeyboard`) | arrows, Space, J/K/L and the other playback letters | `ownsPlainKeys` (changed) |
| Timeline player keys (`useTimelinePlayer`) | same, via `shouldIgnorePlaybackShortcutTarget` | `ownsPlainKeys` (inherited) |
| Canvas nudge (`useDomEditNudge`) | arrows | `ownsPlainKeys` (changed) |
| Caption-word nudge (`captions/keyboard.ts`) | arrows | `ownsPlainKeys` (changed) |
| Snap and grid (`SnapToolbar`) | S, G | `ownsPlainKeys` (was its own tag check) |
| Snapping toggle (`TimelineToolbar`) | N | `isTypingTarget` (was its own tag check) |
| Add keyframe (`useKeyframeKeyboard`) | K | `isTypingTarget` (was its own copy) |
| Automation selection (`useAutomationSelectionKeyboard`) | Delete, Backspace, Escape, Cmd+C, Cmd+V | `isTypingTarget` (was its own copy) |
| Slideshow panel undo (`SlideshowPanel`) | Cmd+Z inside the panel | `isTypingTarget` (was an `INPUT`/`TEXTAREA` tag check) |
| App plain keys (`dispatchPlainKey`) | letters, Delete | `ownsPlainKeys` (from #4844; now also covers players) |
| App chords (`dispatchModifierKey`, `useAppHotkeys`) | Cmd shortcuts | `isTypingTarget`, unchanged: a slider or player does not own Cmd+Z, copy or group |
| Undo and redo (`shouldIgnoreHistoryShortcut`) | Cmd+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z | `isTypingTarget`, unchanged, same reason |
| Timeline row navigation (`timelineKeyboardNavigation`) | arrows inside the timeline rows | not affected: it only runs with focus inside the timeline |

## Tests that fail without the fix

- `usePlaybackKeyboard.test.ts`: "leaves the timeline alone while a <video controls> has focus" and the `<audio controls>` row: each of ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Space, J, K and L is left unclaimed and nothing seeks or plays.
- `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`: "does not nudge the selection while a <video controls> has focus" and the `<audio controls>` row.
- `captions/keyboard.test.ts`: "leaves the arrows to a focused <video controls>" and the `<audio controls>` row.
- `SnapToolbar.test.tsx`: "leaves S and G alone while a combobox / select / switch / video player has focus" (four rows).
- `typingTarget.test.ts`: "is true for a native player with controls and for anything typing claims".
- `useAppHotkeys.test.ts`: "leaves Delete to a focused <video controls>" and the `<audio controls>` row.
- `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`: "N toggles snapping, but not while a picker that owns typing has focus".
- `useKeyframeKeyboard.test.tsx`: "leaves K to a focused picker that owns typing, like a font combobox".
- `useAutomationSelectionKeyboard.test.tsx`: "is inert while a picker that owns typing has focus".
- `SlideshowPanel.test.ts`: "leaves Cmd+Z to a text field, contenteditable and select included".

A video without `controls` still lets the playback keys step the timeline (tested).

## Before

A small fixture project with one 20 s video asset not yet on the timeline. The asset preview is open with its video paused at 0:02 and focused:

![The asset preview open, video at 0:02, focused](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8af33e93-ecc2-4dcf-bb8b-efae6e807f58)

ArrowRight: the timeline playhead steps from frame 0 to frame 1, the video never sees the key, and the preview closes because the playhead moved.

![Before: playhead 0f to 1f, the video preview closed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7120d3a9-8988-4fc6-8a76-e032c9fcea7b)

## After

The same steps: the playhead stays on frame 0, the video seeks from 2.00 s to 2.20 s, and the preview stays open.

![After: playhead stays at 0f, the video seeks to 2.20 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0e084b9-fd0f-4441-b5ef-d01d7bdad25b)

title: fix(studio): the timeline scroll gate catches dropped frames in the virtualized view
body:
The timeline viewport gate now catches a scroll that drops frames in the virtualized timeline on CI. A 45 ms stall on every scroll step used to pass it.

## What changes

- The CI virtualized arm gets its own pair of limits. Pooled over all 315 measured scroll steps, the interaction p95 must be ≤58.3 ms (3.5 frames) and the frame-interval p95 ≤25 ms (1.5 frames). In plain terms, at most 5% of scroll steps may drop a frame, and at most 5% may take 4 or more frames.
- The unvirtualized arm keeps 75/75, because its normal interaction p95 is already 49-60 ms. The primary tier keeps 50/33.3, and the throttled and high-DPR tiers keep 75/75.
- Which pair applies is decided in one place, `responsivenessLimits` in the verdict module. The gate script reads it from there.
- **One rerun per arm.** When an arm's timing attempt fails (3 warm-up runs dropped, then 5 measured runs), the gate measures that arm once more with the same protocol and fails only if both attempts fail. The loop is inside the gate script, not a CI retry. Direct-scroll and memory checks run once. The step summary prints every attempt's p95s, limits and verdict.
- **Per-step samples in the artifact.** The `timeline-viewport-gate-evidence` artifact keeps every measured step's interaction and frame interval, per arm and per attempt (`attempts[].runs[].interactions` / `frameIntervals`), so a red can be recomputed later.

## Why these numbers

A pooled p95 over 315 steps fails once 16 of them are over the limit.

**False fails on normal builds.** Every CI run today that carries per-step evidence: 68 normal virtualized attempts from 67 PR runs, judged single-shot.

| Virtualized limits (interaction / frame) | Attempts that fail | Most steps over the interaction limit |
|---|---|---|
| 75 / 75 (main) | 0 of 68 | 2 |
| 41.7 / 25 (first pick) | 14 of 68 (20.6%), pooled: 16 or more of 315 interactions over 41.7 ms or frames over 25 ms | 39 |
| **58.3 / 25 (this PR)** | **0 of 68** | **6** |

At 41.7 ms the fails were all on interactions: 17-39 steps at 3 frames, spread across all five runs (a slow runner, not a slow start), and frame intervals stayed under the limit (at most 9 steps over 25 ms). The earlier analysis predicted 0% at 41.7 from too little per-step data, so the fallback rule fired before merge and the interaction limit stepped to 58.3 ms. With the rerun a false fail needs two failed attempts in a row; at 58.3 none of the 68 had a single one.

**Catching the 45 ms stall, with the rerun.** A throwaway build injected a 45 ms stall into every timeline scroll step and ran the virtualized arm 10 times on CI.

- 20 of 20 attempts failed, so 10 of 10 gate runs failed.
- Every attempt had 270 of 315 frame intervals over 25 ms (every step that scrolls stalls), against 16 needed.
- The frame limit is what catches the stall. Interactions over 58.3 ms: 45 and 47 of 315 in stall run 1, and 0-4 in each of the other 18 attempts (interaction p95 49.6-49.8 ms), so the interaction half alone fails only run 1. At the first pick, 41.7 ms, 142-193 of 315 were over.
- The interaction limit guards what the frame interval cannot see. A step's interaction runs from the scroll write to the second frame after it; its frame interval only from the first frame to the second. Work that delays the first frame leaves the frame interval normal: with frame intervals at most 25 ms, an interaction over 58.3 ms means the first frame came more than 33 ms after the scroll.
- Single-attempt detection d: 20 of 20 observed, with a margin of 270 frame intervals against 16. With the rerun the gate fails the stall at a rate of d², which is also about 1, above the 95% bar. Counting attempts alone, 20 of 20 bounds d at ≥0.86 with 95% confidence; the step margin is what carries it.

**CI time per arm.** A normal pass runs one attempt, unchanged: about 40 s for the virtualized arm and 35 s for the unvirtualized one. A failed attempt adds one more, about 17 s on a normal build and 30 s on the stall build (a stall arm takes 67-68 s end to end). The steps per run are unchanged.

False fails are counted per arm, each against that arm's own limit: the unvirtualized arm's against its 75 ms, never toward the virtualized limit. For example, #4836's unvirtualized arm read 82, 82, 39, 49 and 47 ms interaction p95 per run on a busy runner; that counts against 75 ms.

**This PR's own CI.** The virtualized arm applied 58.3 / 25 and passed on its first attempt: interaction p95 33.2 ms with 0 of 315 steps over 58.3, and frame p95 16.8 ms with 1 of 315 over 25. The unvirtualized arm passed at 75 / 75 (61.8 / 33.4 ms).

## Tests

`timeline-viewport-verdict.test.mjs`:

- The CI virtualized arm: 16 of 315 steps two frames late fail and 15 pass; the same for frame intervals that drop a frame. Both fail with the virtualized limits set back to 75.
- The rerun: a failed attempt followed by a passing one passes; two failed attempts fail; a third attempt is never counted.
- The other arms and tiers stay at their old limits.

## Before

Main's limits on recorded CI samples: the 45 ms stall run passes.

![Main's limits pass the 45 ms stall run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d4bbfce5-74a0-4a26-9727-c3a414bdf6e1)

## After

This branch's limits and rerun on the same samples: both stall attempts fail, and a normal run still passes.

![This branch's limits fail the stall on both attempts and pass the normal run](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/14a99fc0-374f-4cc3-92ef-ba4506c7f448)

title: fix(studio): a hand edit after a preview reload draws on the element now on screen
body:
## What

After a full preview reload, a hand edit draws on the element on screen again, and a reload never lands under a gesture. This holds even when the app hosting Studio's editing session never re-renders for that reload.

A full reload loads into a hidden shadow iframe, then promotes it: the player swaps its iframe ref to the new element. Studio's editing session learned which iframe was live only from the `previewIframe` it was given at render. A host that reads its iframe ref once at render kept the retired iframe, so the selection stayed on the retired document's node. The overlay drew its handles from the live document, so the handles looked right, but the gestures and the plain CSS writers acted on the retired node:
- A rotate after a resize saved `rotate: -36deg` to the file while the element on screen stayed upright.
- A move or another resize was saved but not drawn.

## How

**The live preview has one source.**
- The player announces each promotion on the iframes' document as `{ retired, live }` (`announcePreviewPromoted` in `sceneSwap.ts`, called from `useShadowPreviewReload`).
- `useLivePreviewIframe` returns the iframe on screen: the host's iframe, then each one promoted in its place. It follows a promotion only when its own iframe was retired, and takes a new host iframe as given.
- `useDomEditSession` hands that iframe to everything that used `previewIframe`, so the preview sync moves its listeners to the new iframe and re-resolves the selection there.
- `useLivePreviewIframe` and the `PreviewPromotion` type are exported from the package entry, so a host can pass `previewIframe: useLivePreviewIframe(host)`. Wrapping twice (host and session) lands on the same iframe.

**A reload waits for the gesture on screen, and a reload older than a canvas save loads again.** One rule, at promotion, in `useShadowPreviewReload`:
- While any element in the live document carries the manual-edit gesture mark, a painted shadow is held. When the last mark ends (`afterStudioManualEditGestures`), promotion is tried again.
- Each canvas save is counted in the live document before it starts (`noteStudioManualEditSave`, called from the overlay's commit refs, so drag, group drag, resize, rotate, nudge and crop all count, plus the inline text commit). A shadow requested before a save shows the file before it: once no tracked edit is still saving, a fresh shadow loads instead of promoting it.
- A tap, cancel or anything else that saved nothing promotes the held copy as is.
- A newer reload that starts during a hold still wins: every generation change stops the old hold first.
- The hold logs when it starts and ends (`shadow-held`, `shadow-hold-ended`).

**Every gesture's mark ends.** The mark lives exactly as long as the gesture:

| Gesture | Holds? | Where its mark ends |
|---|---|---|
| Drag, group drag, resize, rotate | yes | pointerup (after the save settles), pointercancel, lostpointercapture, window blur, a switch to read-only, overlay unmount; a throw while the gesture is being armed ends it too |
| Keyboard nudge burst | yes | its own commit (timer, unmount, selection change, movement turned off) |
| Inline text edit | yes, while open | when the edit closes (commit or cancel). The save itself is a tracked pending edit, so a reload waits on it through the pending-edit drain, not the mark |
| Crop | no | its draft is overlay state and its save targets the current selection; its save is counted like the others |
| Marquee | no | it saves nothing; its commit re-reads candidates from the live document when the measured ones came from a retired one |

**No lookup on the edit path guesses which preview is on screen.**

| Lookup | Document it searches |
|---|---|
| `findElementForSelection`, `findPreviewNode`, preview sync re-resolve | the live iframe's document, passed in |
| Overlay `resolveElementForOverlay`, group overlay resolver | the live iframe's document; a cached node is reused only when it belongs to it |
| Selection from target, point or refresh | the live iframe's document, or the target element's own document |
| Marquee candidates, snap targets | the live iframe's document |
| GSAP target lookups and drag intercept | the live iframe's document and window |
| File patch target | none: the id and selector are read from the element's own document |
| Keyframe cache runtime scan | fixed here: it fell back to the host page's first `iframe[src*='/preview/']`; it now reads only the iframe ref it is given |
| `resolveIframe` (public helper) | the first iframe inside the element it is given. Nothing in Studio calls it; a host must pass one player, not a container |

Nothing on the path reads visibility, display, opacity or DOM order to decide which iframe is live.

## Tests

- `gestureHoldsPreviewReload.test.tsx` (real player, real overlay, a fake file the commit writes and each fresh shadow serves):
  - A reload that paints during a drag, of one layer and of a group, waits for the drop, then shows the drop from a fresh load.
  - A reload requested during a drag that paints after the drop is not promoted; a fresh load shows the drop.
  - pointercancel, lostpointercapture, window blur, a switch to read-only and overlay unmount each clear the mark and promote the held copy.
  - A press whose arming throws leaves no mark, and the next reload promotes.
  - An inline text edit holds a reload while open, ends its mark when it closes, and the reload after the save lands shows the saved text.
- `previewPromotionSelection.test.tsx`: after a real shadow promotion, with both previews on a host stage and the live one second, then first, the selection, the overlay's node, a rotate and a move all land on the live one, and the retired one is untouched. Control: a session that keeps the host's first iframe stays on the retired node. Plus `useLivePreviewIframe` itself and the double wrap.
- `useDomEditSession.test.tsx`: the session itself hands the promoted iframe to selection and preview sync.
- `livePreviewIframeExport.test.tsx`: the package export returns the promoted iframe after a real promotion.
- `marqueeCommit.test.tsx`: a reload promoted mid-band selects from the live document.

Each was run against a broken copy and fails: no hold; the stale check removed; the drag save not counted; no restore when arming throws; no gesture-ended event; the hold not retrying when it ends; the read-only exit removed; the text save not tracked; the text mark not ended at close; the marquee always using the measured hits; the session passing the host's iframe; the export removed; the hook following any promotion; the player not announcing the promotion.

## Before

The captures come from Studio with a one-off local patch, so that its editing session gets its preview iframe the way an embedding host does: read once, with no document-version bump on load. The steps, in a real browser:
1. Select the title.
2. Resize it from a corner.
3. Edit `index.html` outside Studio, so the preview does a real shadow reload and promotion.
4. Rotate the title by -36 deg.

On main, the file gets `rotate: -36deg` but the title on screen stays upright (computed `rotate: none`), and only a full page reload shows the turn:

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/29efd381-3fdf-4176-9ea5-e6e899d93e57)

## After

On this branch, the same steps turn the title on screen as you drag, and the file matches:

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7ebb890b-0fba-405d-8128-c7bd4fd194a1)

The hold has nothing to show on screen: a reload that would have landed under the pointer simply lands after the drop. It is covered by the tests above rather than a capture.

title: fix: a save's temp file no longer reaches Studio as an outside change
body:
## What

Every save Studio makes writes a temp file beside the target and renames it into place. The project watcher reported that temp file (`index.html.1d1117cc.tmp`) to Studio as a file of its own. It carried no write token, so Studio took it for an edit made outside the app:

- it drained pending edits, which commits a nudge burst still inside its 400 ms wait and splits it into two saves and two history entries;
- it marked the history as changed from outside, which drops the instant undo prediction;
- it refreshed the file tree and the history list.

A history step's restore wrote its own temp name (`index.html.<uuid>.tmp`) and was reported the same way. Now the watcher never reports either one, and the project file listing never counts one.

## How

- `@hyperframes/core/atomic-file` owns the temp name: `atomicTempPath` builds it and `isAtomicTempPath` recognizes it. The name is `<file>.hf<6 hex>.tmp`, so a user's own `foo.12345678.tmp` is still a project file. It stays 13 bytes, so a 242-byte name still fits under the 255-byte limit.
- The history's blob restore names its temp file with `atomicTempPath`, not a uuid of its own. Restores run one at a time on the history's queue, and the core writer retries a taken name, so 24 bits of randomness is enough.
- `shouldWatchProjectFile`, `affectsProjectSignature` and the project file walk skip temp files. The watcher only drops a path when both the first two reject it, so all three need the check. The walk also feeds the history's sweep, which could otherwise record a temp file caught mid-save as a file added outside the app.
- On macOS and Windows the CLI watcher uses `fs.watch` with `recursive`, and on Linux a watch per directory. Both report through the same filter. The Studio dev server's watcher already ignores anything that isn't `.html`, `.css`, `.js` or `.json`.

## Bench

The edit-accuracy sequence bench, nudge and rotate-then-nudge cases (12 cases, 30 saves), same base, same machine, 3 jobs. GET requests per save:

| Build | File tree refreshes | History refreshes | File reads | Preview loads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 2.97 | 6.33 | 7.80 | 0.80 |
| this branch | 0.80 | 5.47 | 7.80 | 0.80 |

The 0.80 tree refreshes left are each case's page load (24 over 30 saves). Session reloads don't change: a session reloads only when the changed path is the open composition, and a temp path never is.

The file checks (tracking, drop, reload, undo) pass in all 12 cases on both builds. In both runs the smoothness check fails in nearly every case, the same on main; it is not affected by this change.

With Studio's undo drain committing a nudge burst early (a separate PR), the seqnudge cases went from 6/6 on the reload and undo checks to 2/6, and seqrotatenudge to 4/6. With the watcher's half of this change added on top, they are back to 6/6.

### Redo writes on the two quarantined nudge sequences

`seqnudge-none-pct-r0-root-z100` and `seqnudge-none-pct-r0-nested-z100` are quarantined under this PR, because an earlier run failed their undo check on redo writes of 2,015 to 2,072 ms against the 2 s limit. Redo write, from the key to the file write, in ms:

| Where | Build | Samples | p50 | p95 | max | Over 2 s |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CI, the bench PR's last two runs | main | 12 | 60 | 106 | 106 | 0 |
| CI, this PR's run | this branch | 2 | 60 | 62 | 62 | 0 |
| one machine, 5 runs each, 2 jobs | main | 10 | 103 | 201 | 201 | 0 |
| one machine, 5 runs each, 2 jobs | this branch | 9 | 110 | 218 | 218 | 0 |

No run on either build came near the limit, so this data does not show that this PR removes the slow redo; it doesn't show the opposite either. With both builds far under 2 s, this PR takes both ids out of the quarantine list, so the gate judges them again; its 2-of-3 rerun absorbs a single slow write. One machine run on this branch errored before it started (a port clash in the bench) and is left out.

## Test plan

- [x] `fileWatcher.atomic.test.ts`, on a real file system: an atomic save and a history step's restore each reach the watcher's listener only as `index.html`. Both fail without the watcher's filter, and the history one also fails with the blob store's old uuid temp name.
- [x] `fileWatcher.test.ts`: a save's temp file is skipped, a user's `foo.12345678.tmp` and `notes.tmp` are not.
- [x] `projectSignature.test.ts`: the signature and the file listing skip a temp file and keep a user's `.tmp` file. Both fail without the check.
- [x] `atomicFile.test.ts`: `isAtomicTempPath` knows its own names and no one else's; the existing temp name and length tests pass with the new name.
- [x] core, studio-server and cli typecheck; oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files; the studio-server history suites.

## No visible change

The only `packages/studio` change is two lines in the edit accuracy bench's quarantine list. The watcher fix has no screen of its own; its effect is fewer requests per save, measured above.

title: feat(studio): paste and duplicate can keep a clip at its own time
body:
## What

`useClipboard`'s `handlePaste` and `handleDuplicate` take an optional `{ inPlace: true }`. With it, a pasted or duplicated clip keeps its original's time and goes to a track of its own, above the ones in use then. Without it, nothing changes.

## Why

A host that copies from the canvas wants the copy where the person sees the original: the same moment, the same spot. Today paste anchors at the playhead and duplicate right after the selection, so a copy made from the canvas jumps away in time.

## Related work

Follows #4852, which made a pasted element keep its look.

## How

- One option on the existing path: only the anchor time changes. Paste anchors at the copied clips' earliest start, and duplicate at the selection's earliest start (in that file's own clock, as duplicate already converts).
- The existing `resolveFreeTrack` places the copy, which always meets its original at that time, on a track above the ones in use.
- The two handlers re-indent: the formatter keeps a hook's callback inline only when it takes no arguments. Hide whitespace to see the change.
- A clip's copied start is in the clock of the composition being edited at the copy (the film's master time at the root). The clipboard now records that composition; an in-place paste uses the copied time only when it pastes into the same one, and the playhead otherwise, as before.
- Studio's own callers pass nothing, so Studio's paste and duplicate are unchanged.
- Paste's undo label and its note come from one `pasteWords` helper, and two older paste tests share their steps, which clears the Fallow audit on the touched files.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `useClipboard.source.test.ts` "a copy in place" duplicates and pastes a clip at 2 s on track 0 with `inPlace`, and checks the copy lands at 2 s on track 1. Without the change the copy lands at 5 s (duplicate) or at the 6 s playhead (paste), and both tests fail.
- [x] A clip inside a sub-composition (host at 2 s, local 1 s) pastes in place into the film at 3 s, the moment the film shows it; after switching to another composition, the same paste lands at the playhead. Without the composition check the second test lands at 3 s and fails.
- [x] An in-place duplicate of that sub-composition clip keeps its local 1 s, on track 1; without the change it lands after the clip and fails.
- [x] `useClipboard.source.test.ts`, `useClipboard.test.ts` and `clipboardPayload.test.ts`: 54/54.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: no Studio surface passes the option yet; the captures draw what the tests measured.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

![Before: the copy lands after the clip on the same track](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f6e8ad3d-3ec6-4619-ad76-f41d065c9cee)

## After

![After: the copy keeps its time, on a track of its own](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d66340a-55df-464c-ba03-68e4ac9da994)

title: fix(studio-server): a folder rename past an unreadable folder or file answers ok
body:
## What a person can do now

Renaming a file or folder in Studio's file tree answers ok even when the project holds a folder or text file that cannot be read. Before, the rename itself went through on disk, and then the request answered 500: the file tree showed an error for a rename that had already happened.

## Why

After `renameSync`, the rename route rewrites references to the old path (`updateReferences`). Its walk (`walkFiles`) listed every folder with `readdirSync`, and it read every text file with `readFileSync`. One unreadable folder or file threw, and the throw reached the route after the move was done.

## What changed

`packages/studio-server/src/routes/files.ts`:

- `walkFiles` skips a folder it may not list (`readableEntries`).
- `updateReferences` skips a text file it may not read (`readableText`). Its references stay as they are.
- Only permission errors (`EACCES`, `EPERM`) and an entry gone since it was listed (`ENOENT`) are skipped. Any other error, a disk error say, still fails the request as before.
- The folders it already skips (`node_modules`, `renders`, ...) are unchanged.

## Tests

`files.pathSafety.test.ts`, "rename reference updates":

- A rename in a project with an unreadable folder and an unreadable HTML file answers 200. The file moved with its bytes, and the readable `index.html` gets the new path. The test first checks the folder really refuses a listing. It is skipped on Windows and as root, where every folder reads.
- A rename whose scan meets a different error (a link named `link.html` that leads to a folder, so reading it fails with `EISDIR`) still answers 500.

## What I measured

- Without the change, the first test fails ("expected 500 to be 200"). With every read error swallowed instead, the second test fails. With the change, both pass.
- `files.pathSafety.test.ts` and `files.test.ts`: 136/136.
- `tsc -p packages/studio-server` 0; oxfmt and oxlint on both files clean.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Studio's file tree in a browser: the change is in the server route only.

title: feat(studio): the code editor follows studio's light and dark theme
body:
## What changes for a person using Studio

The Code tab's editor follows Studio's theme: light in a light Studio, dark in a dark one. Before, it stayed on CodeMirror's One Dark in both, so the light theme had a dark block in the left panel, and its gutter and comments sat under 4.5:1. Code keeps its familiar syntax hues: One Light's in light, One Dark's in dark, each held at 4.5:1. Types and constants, which One Light tells apart by lightness alone, are separated by hue (gold and orange) so both can hold 4.5:1 and still look different.

## How

- `components/editor/studioCodeTheme.ts` keeps One Dark's layout (which syntax tags get which colour) but paints with Studio's tokens: the editor, gutter, active line, selection and search panel use Studio's existing roles (`surface`, `text-muted`, `hover`, `on`, `raised`, `input`, `border`).
- Eight syntax roles are new tokens in `theme.css`, each a `light-dark()` pair: `--color-code-keyword`, `-name`, `-function`, `-constant`, `-type`, `-operator`, `-comment`, `-string`. Because every colour is a CSS variable, the editor follows the theme with no editor reconfiguration when the theme changes.
- A selection sits on the active line's wash, so the syntax tokens are tuned for that stack; search matches and other occurrences of the selected word carry no background of their own, only an outline (accent for the current match), so text never sits on more than the line, the active line and a selection.
- `@codemirror/theme-one-dark` is no longer used and is removed; `@lezer/highlight` (already installed through CodeMirror) becomes a direct dependency for the syntax tags.

## Before

![Before: light Studio, the code editor stays dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2ccca70-075f-41a7-8117-313cdbc32aa9)
![Before: dark Studio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79781947-f2bd-43a9-8502-1a23a346c95b)

## After

The repo's `product-promo` example, Code tab open, at 1280x800, 1440x900 and 1920x1080.

![After: 1280x800, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79cfb49f-7b02-4f29-9587-d6c92443755b)
![After: 1280x800, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/69435a9a-b44d-4a9c-8e7b-3dd9de737cae)
![After: 1440x900, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d997117-5dee-4ab7-88f9-4e04ad4a27a8)
![After: 1440x900, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/550e200f-667a-40de-9aa5-01425ff1293c)
![After: 1920x1080, light](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b77298f4-0148-413b-9e19-fa4b9d23dc7e)
![After: 1920x1080, dark](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3fd6b7d4-0b05-4f4b-bfc3-8187729d01d3)

## Verification

- `scripts/contrastRatchet.test.ts`: the manifest adds each code token on the editor's line, the active line, a selection, and a selection on the active line, in both themes: 64 new pairs, all at 4.7:1 or above (210 pairs in total, 0 debts).
- `studioCodeTheme.test.ts`: every colour the editor theme uses is a token `theme.css` declares, and it paints no literal colour. A literal comment colour or a misspelled token each fails its test.
- Rendered sweep in the built Studio (headless Chromium 147) with the Code tab open: 2 items under target in both themes at all three sizes, both the lint count badge at the trough of its pulse (unchanged by this PR). Before, the open editor accounted for 40 failing items.
- `packages/studio`: the full unit suite, 6400 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit`: no errors. oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files. `fallow audit`: no issues. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` accepts the lockfile.

title: feat(studio): export ColorField and GradientField; a style commit takes a map
body:
## What

Two small additions so a host without the editor's inspector can reuse Studio's style editing:

- `ColorField` and `GradientField` are exported from `@hyperframes/studio`. A host can show the same colour picker and gradient editor the inspector uses instead of keeping its own copy.

HyperFrames Desktop is adding fill, stroke, corner radius and shadow to its pick toolbar. Its gradient fill should be Studio's editor, not a second copy. title: feat(studio-server): a write receipt names the version the write replaced
body:
## What

`FileWriteReceipt` gains an optional `from`: the content version of the bytes the write replaced, when the writer read them. `identifyFileWrite` returns it.

## Why

A host that shows its own preview of a project (an embedding editor) can skip reloading after a write the preview already painted, by matching the watcher's echo to the write's receipt. A receipt says which bytes a write left, but not which bytes it started from. A patch route reads the file and writes `patch(read)`, so when another writer's change lands just before the patch reads, the patched bytes carry that change too, and the receipt looks the same as for a clean edit. With `from`, the host can check the write started from the bytes it last showed, and reload otherwise.

## Related work

None in this repo.

## How

`recordFileWriteReceipt` already receives the replaced bytes as `overwrote` (every API write that read the file passes them; a history restore does not). It hashes them with `fileContentVersion` once and stores `from` on the receipt; `identifyFileWrite` copies it through. A receipt recorded without `overwrote` has no `from`. The field is optional, so existing readers are unaffected.

## Test plan

- `fileVersion.test.ts`: a receipt recorded with `overwrote` reports `from` as that content's version; one recorded without it has no `from`.
- `applyFileMutations.test.ts`: after an outside write, `applyFileMutations` leaves a receipt whose `from` is the outside bytes' version.
- Both files: 16 of 16 pass; `tsc --noEmit` in studio-server: 0 errors. With `from` dropped from the stored receipt, both new tests fail.

title: fix(core): a composition made only of a set shows it at a seek in the preview
body:
## What

A composition whose root timeline is too short to have a length of its own (its only child is a `set`, duration 0) now shows that set when the preview seeks, the same as the rendered video.

## Why

The runtime wraps a root shorter than the duration floor in a floor-length timeline (`createDurationFloorTimeline`) and adds the root to it while the root is still paused. GSAP never renders a paused child when its parent seeks, so a preview seek left the set unapplied: a box resized by Studio (saved as `tl.set(el, { width, height }, 0)` on a root with no tween) reloaded at its old size. The render path already got it right, because `renderSeek` plays every registered timeline across each frame's seek.

Reproduce on main: a root `data-duration="4"`, a box at `width: 240px`, `window.__timelines.main = gsap.timeline({ paused: true }).set(box, { width: 340 }, 0)`. `__player.seek(1)` leaves the box at 240px; `__player.renderSeek(1)` gives 340px.

## Related work

Refs the Studio edit-accuracy rows for resizing a box held in place by a GSAP set.

## How

Once the floor timeline holds the root, the root is unpaused so the paused floor timeline drives it. This reuses the rule the runtime already applies to child compositions nested under a paused root (`ensureChildCandidatesActive` over `nestedCandidates`, so only a child the parent actually holds is unpaused; a timeline left on the global ticker unpaused would free-run).

Unchanged:
- A root as long as the floor is never wrapped, so it stays the captured timeline and stays paused.
- The render path: `renderSeek` still plays and re-pauses registered timelines around each seek; the set-only root renders 340px before and after.
- Every registered timeline is authored `paused: true` and the runtime owns its play state, so an author's pause is not overridden in any way the runtime did not already do for nested compositions.

## Before

The preview runtime on main, a repro composition (root `data-duration="4"`, box authored at 240x160, root timeline `set(box, { width: 340, height: 227 }, 0)` and nothing else), seeked to 1 s: the box stays 240 px wide.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/581f50e2-4c92-4bad-88db-390e8a936bf0)

## After

The same composition and seek with this PR's runtime: the box is 340 px wide, as the render shows it.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7c46a72-b04d-4d4e-aec9-45c1eb6aeeb7)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `init.test.ts` "duration floor under real GSAP": a set-only root shows 340px after a seek (fails on main with `expected '240px' to be '340px'`), and a control where a root as long as the floor stays unwrapped and paused.
- [x] `packages/core` `src/runtime`: 65 files, 1721 tests pass.
- [x] Studio edit accuracy gate (CI): 0 regressed, 4 newly passing resize rows on a box held by a GSAP set (`resize-hold-center-r0-root-z200`, `resize-hold-xpercent-r0-root-{z50,z100,z200}`), banked from that run's artifact. Their reload error fell from about 60 px to under 0.1 px. The other resize-hold rows still fail on undo, which is a separate Studio undo-restore bug.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: test(studio): score edits on GSAP-animated size, scale, rotation and keyframes
body:
## What

Follows #4801. The edit accuracy grid's GSAP axis only tweened x/y, so no case animated size, scale or rotation. This adds a `keyframes` grid of GSAP-animated targets and scores every edit against one rule:

- with the playhead ON a keyframe, the edit changes that keyframe's value;
- BETWEEN keyframes, it adds a keyframe at the playhead with the new value;
- every other keyframe keeps its value exactly;
- only properties nothing animates get plain CSS.

### The variants (keyframes at 0, 2 and 3 s)
- `size`: width and height tween;
- `scale`: scale tween;
- `spin`: rotation tween;
- `keys`: a `keyframes` array on x and width, so a resize meets keyframes;
- `fromto`: a `from` (0 to 2 s) and a `fromTo` (2 to 3 s) on x.

Each runs × the 5 gestures (move, nudge, resize, rotate, crop) × r0/r30 × root/nested × z50/z100/z200 × the playhead on a keyframe (2 s, `-on`) or between keyframes (1 s, `-mid`): 600 cases, ids like `resize-keys-px-r0-root-z100-on`.

### What each case asserts
1. At the edited time, the preview (`drop`) and the saved file (`reload`) show the new value, as for every case.
2. At every other keyframe time, each animated property reads back its pre-edit value (`keys`). GSAP's own values are read in the preview at each time, before the edit and from the saved file after a reload.
3. The preview matches the producer render at the edited time (`render`) and at the 3 s keyframe (`renderKey`).
4. The saved file has no plain CSS changed for an animated property, in the target's rule or inline (`css`).

The timeline lane's keyframe diamond is UI and is not read here.

### Bench fixes on the way
- The bench settles only once no shadow preview is waiting to be swapped in. A hidden preview holding the target means the visible one is about to go stale, and measuring it read an old box. Only keyframed cases wait for it. Elsewhere the wait made a later undo land in the preview's burst of requests, so the other cases keep main's timing.
- A drag ends at its recorded pointer-up. Before this, a release that no frame painted while the button was held never ended the drag, so travel after pointer-up passed. A box that follows the pointer after release now fails.

### How the new rows enter the gate
- `full` now runs them too (953 + 600 = 1553 cases), and CI splits it into 20 shards instead of 12, to stay near 25-30 min a shard.
- A new row has no base entry, so it counts as failing on the base branch.
  - A row that fails here is neither regressed nor newly passing, so it changes nothing and is not re-run.
  - A row that passes is newly passing, and this PR banks it from its own CI run.
- After merge the failing rows act like any failing row today. They turn a PR's gate red only if one passes 2 of 3 runs there, as "newly passing, not banked". If some prove flaky, they go on the quarantine list with the PR that fixes them.
- The gate run the bank comes from (36984514335) had no unstable case and no undo or redo write over 1 s (of 4120). Earlier runs had cases that failed on run 1 only and passed 2 of 3:
  - `crop-none-pct-r0-root-z100` and `crop-none-px-r30-nested-z50` (run 36918550317), and `crop-none-pct-r0-nested-z50` (run 36953395623): existing crop cases, about 40 px off on run 1. `crop-none-px-r0-nested-z200` shows the same first-run pattern. It is tracked as its own bug.
  - `seqrotatenudge-none-px-r0-nested-z100` (late undo in run 36926248306, late redo in run 36949992609) and `seqinflight-none-pct-r0-nested-z100` (late undo in run 36949992609): one write about 2-3 s late, with the right bytes and box. The cause is Chrome's limit of 6 connections per host: paused preview `<video>` requests each hold a connection for 35-45 s, so Studio's undo request waits for a free socket. The server itself answers in 9 ms. The Studio fix lands separately.
  - Those runs predate the change that limits the swap wait to keyframed cases. While that wait applied to every case, it made these late writes likelier: on a 2-core run, 11 of 474 undo and redo writes took over 500 ms (4 over 1 s), against 5 of 478 (none over 1 s) with main's bench.
- Quarantined under #4889: `seqnudge-none-pct-r0-nested-z100`. In run 36971408022 it failed 2 of 3 on late writes (redo 2013 ms, undo 2212 ms), with the right bytes and box, so the gate called it regressed. It is the same connection wait. Run alone 10 times on main's bench and 10 on this one, against the same Studio build on 2 cores, no write took over 1 s on either side (9/10 and 10/10 passed; main's one failure was a different undo bug). #4889 removes the wait and unquarantines it.
- This PR banks its 255 passing keyframed rows from its own CI run. The other 345 fail, and the failing assertion for each row is in the table below.

### Smoothness is banked as `smooth`
`baseline.json` used to store `pass`. That was the full verdict, smoothness included, while the gate's `accurate()` leaves smoothness out. So the field read as "passes" even though the gate counted something else. Now each meaning has one owner:
- `smooth` holds the smoothness verdict alone: no more dropped frames than the blank-page control, and no frame over 8 ms of main-thread work. That 8 ms is now a cap on the worst frame; it used to be a p95.
- `workMax` holds that worst frame's work and replaces `work`, which was the p95.
- Accuracy is never stored; `accurate()` derives it.
- The gate headline prints both counts: `accurate N (base branch B), smooth M of those`. Smooth is counted only among the accurate cases.

Smoothness is still reported only, never gated.

### CI cost
- Before: 12 shards × 25.6 min mean = 307 runner-min per PR run (from #4801's CI).
- After: 20 shards × 24.1 min mean = 481 runner-min per PR run (max 30.7 min a shard), from this PR's CI.
- If the Actions queue wait on studio PRs goes past about 10 min, the gate moves to sharding by changed area.

### Counts on main, per variant × gesture × playhead (12 cases a row)
255/600 pass every gated check. Assertion numbers follow the list above: 1 is drop and reload, 2 is keys, 3 is render and renderKey, 4 is css. Assertion 4 has no failures.
The 6/12 rows that fail only `undo` are the root-nesting half. There, undo and redo leave the right bytes, but the box sits 33-240 px off (median 122). One possible cause is a stale playhead after the undo reload, not yet confirmed.

title: fix(studio): a move keeps an authored xPercent centring set in the saved file
body:
## What

Moving, nudging or resizing an element centred with `gsap.set({ xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50 })` that also has an x/y tween now keeps the centring set in the saved file. Before, the save deleted it and the element landed half its size down and to the right.

## Why

Before a GSAP move commits, Studio removes duplicate position writes for the element. It counted every write in the `position` group as a duplicate, and that group holds `x`, `y`, `xPercent` and `yPercent`. A centring set and an x/y tween were treated as two conflicting writes and the set was deleted. The drag preview looked right, so only the drop was wrong, and reload and render then agreed with the wrong file.

## Related work

Refs #4774 (closed). It had the same idea for the writers. This PR takes only that part.

## How

- One predicate, `isXYPositionWrite` in `@hyperframes/parsers/gsap-constants` beside `PROPERTY_GROUPS`, says whether a write sets x or y. Only those can duplicate each other. An xPercent/yPercent-only set never does.
- The acorn writer's `dedupePositionWritesInScript`, its recast twin, and the Studio self-heal in `tryGsapDragIntercept` all use it.
- With the set kept, a second spot in `tryGsapDragIntercept` picked the wrong write: the stale-id re-match took the first `position` write in the fresh parse, which is the set, so the move turned the centring set into keyframes. It now matches only a write of the same kind.
- Two x/y writes are still consolidated, as before.
- On release, the flat-tween-to-keyframes commit reads the tween's start by clearing `x,y` and seeking. GSAP clears the whole transform when any part of it is cleared, and the seek only restores what the timeline owns, so the centring vanished from the preview for a few frames until the soft reload (the bench's teleport check caught a 144 px jump on the move and resize rows). The restore after the read now carries every position channel, `xPercent` and `yPercent` included.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `gsapWriter.parity.test.ts`: a centring set plus an x/y tween comes out unchanged from both writers. Fails on main.
  - `gsapRuntimeBridge.test.ts`: a drag with a centring set and a live x/y tween runs no consolidate and edits only the tween (fails on main), and a second x/y write is still consolidated.
  - Each part of the dedupe fix was reverted by itself and the matching test failed. The release-flash fix is proven by the bench's teleport check: jsdom's GSAP loses the whole transform after `clearProps`, so a unit test there cannot see it.
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Edit accuracy bench, `--filter '^(move|nudge|resize)-tween-xpercent-'` (36 cases) on Linux: every gated metric passes in all 36 (drop, reload, render, undo, tracking, press). `move-tween-xpercent-r0-root-z100` drop went from 144.24 px on main to 0.
  - CI edit accuracy gate (merged with main): 869 passing against 835 on the base branch, 34 newly passing (every `move`, `nudge` and `resize-tween-xpercent` case that failed on main), 0 regressed. Those 34 are banked from that run's artifact `baseline.json`, byte for byte, and a local replay of the gate on the banked file passes.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Captures: the bench fixture `move-tween-xpercent-r0-root-z100` (a 240x160 box at `left: 50%; top: 50%` with the centring set and an x/y tween), driven by the bench's own drag. Left: the frame at pointer release. Right: the same view once the save has landed.

## Before

![Before: the box jumps down and right after the save](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9cf5969c-1a25-4214-9c72-95e44ba77a98)

Saved script: the `gsap.set("#target", { xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50 })` line is gone.

## After

![After: the box stays where it was let go](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce77bae2-f695-43d2-97a7-47b1d0de26a5)

Saved script: the centring set is still there, and the move is a keyframe on the tween.

title: fix(studio): undoing a crop leaves a GSAP-animated layer where its file puts it
body:
Stacked on #4853; review only the commits after e185c116.

## What

An undo or redo of a crop (or any style-only edit) on a layer GSAP animates now puts the layer back exactly where its file and script put it. Before, the layer jumped: a `gsap.set` hold lost its position (10 px off on the edit-accuracy fixture), a tween counted the stylesheet `translate` twice, and a CSS `rotate` was applied twice.

## Why

The in-place undo copies the file's attributes onto the live element. That wipes what GSAP wrote inline when it first parsed the element (`translate: none; rotate: none; scale: none` and, for an off-timeline `gsap.set`, the transform itself), while GSAP's cache (`el._gsap`) keeps the values it parsed. When the script did not change (a crop changes only `style`), the restore only seeked, so GSAP never parsed the element again and the stylesheet transform came back under GSAP's own.

## Related work

Stacked on #4853 (gesture-aware attribute sync); its tests stay green. Takes the idea of #4771 (re-run the script when the sync touches an element GSAP parsed), not its branch.

## How

- `applyUndoRestoreToPreview`: when a synced element was parsed by GSAP and the document has a GSAP script, re-run the restored script in place (the soft-reload path a script change already takes), even if the script text is unchanged. A document with several GSAP scripts cannot re-run one in place, so that case reloads.
- `applySoftReload` takes those elements as `reparse` and resets GSAP's cache for exactly them. Its existing sweep only found GSAP elements that still had an inline `transform`, which the sync had just removed.

Why a re-run and not only clearing GSAP's cache and seeking: an off-timeline `gsap.set` hold has no tween left to render after the cache is cleared, so only re-running the script puts the hold back. Re-running is also what a fresh load does, so holds, tweens and rotation all match it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `gsapUndoRestore.browser.test.ts` drives real Chrome with the edit-accuracy fixtures (hold, tween, xPercent tween with CSS `rotate: 30deg`), crops the live layer, runs the undo and compares the layer's box with the box before the edit. It fails on #4853's head (hold `[600, 330]` vs `[600, 320]`; tween `[660, 367.5]` vs `[620, 337.5]`; rotated box swapped) and passes with the fix. `gsapUndoRestore.test.ts` and `gsapSoftReload.test.ts` pass unchanged.
- [x] Edit accuracy bench: the 45 `crop-(hold|tween)-*-root` cases that failed on main pass every gated metric (CI gate: 0 regressed, 49 newly passing, the 45 crop cases banked from that run's artifact). The `resize-hold-*-root` undo boxes are unchanged by this PR (the same numbers as main to 0.1 px); this PR does not fix them.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Edit-accuracy fixture `crop-hold-px-r0-root-z100` in Studio at #4853's head: crop, then Cmd+Z. The layer lands 10 px (composition) below where its file puts it; redo is off by the same 10 px.

![Before: after Cmd+Z the layer sits below the red line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bba38de-98a4-4e6e-89a8-3fec60615168)

## After

Same case with this PR: undo and redo land exactly (box error 0).

![After: after Cmd+Z the layer sits on the red line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0927a92-f6ae-48be-ab93-ed34a8870e5f)

title: fix(studio): edits on GSAP-animated layers keep their keyframes and file positions
body:
## What

This PR carries several Studio fixes for edits on GSAP-animated layers, one item per section. Items 1 (resize), 2 (cause A, undo), 3 (cause C, xPercent centring), 4 (font pick writes once), 5 (a focused field counts as an unsaved edit), 6 (a comment-ratchet test line) and 7 (an inspector edit during a preview reload) are in; later items are added as they land.

### Item 1: a resize of a layer GSAP positions but never sizes

Resizing an element that GSAP positions but never sizes (for example one placed by a `gsap.set({ x, y })` hold) now saves its new size as the element's own CSS `width` and `height`. The position part of the resize still goes through GSAP, as the compensating `x`/`y`, in the same undo step. Where the script already writes the size (a tween, a keyframe, a `from`/`fromTo`, or a size `set`), the resize still edits that animation, as before.

## Why

Before this change, the size of a GSAP-positioned box went down the GSAP route too, which wrote a new `tl.set("#target", { width, height }, 0)`. On a composition whose timeline has no tween, that set leaves the root timeline with a duration of 0, and the Studio preview never renders it. After a reload the box snapped back to its old size while keeping its new position. The file and the render had the new size; the reloaded preview did not.

The rule is one write channel per property: a `gsap.set` only where GSAP already animates that property, and a resize writes width/height, never scale.

## Related work

Refs the edit-accuracy bench's `resize-hold-*-root-*` rows. The preview not rendering a set inside a zero-duration paused root timeline is a separate runtime issue in `@hyperframes/core` and is not touched here.

## How

- `tryGsapResizeIntercept`: on the hold/no-tween branch, if no known animation for the element writes `width` or `height` (properties, `from` properties or keyframes), it returns a new `{ status: "element-size" }` outcome instead of adding a size set.
- `handleGsapAwareBoxSizeCommit`: on that outcome, the size is saved by the existing plain box-size writer (`handleDomBoxSizeCommit`, the one non-GSAP elements already use) under the gesture's undo key, and the drag offset is still forwarded to the GSAP position writer. The rescaled crop comes with it.
- The size is saved before the buffered GSAP writes and asks for no render of its own (`deferRender`), so the GSAP reload stays the gesture's last render. Saved after them, the gesture stayed open for the extra write, and a nested layer showed its timeline's start position for about 5 frames after release (the bench's teleport metric, 40 px). Saved before them with its own reseek, the reseek rendered the old tween over the settled position.
- `handleDomBoxSizeCommit` takes an optional undo key so its write joins that step.
- The plain box-size patch no longer saves GSAP's inline `scale: none` mask on an element whose transform GSAP renders. Saved, it would override a stylesheet `scale` on the next load (checked with a `scale: 1.5` element: it keeps 1.5x after a reload).

**Keyframe rule rows.** A resize writes CSS width/height only when nothing in the script animates or sets the element's size; otherwise it still edits that animation. On the keyframes grid: resize under `size`, `scale` (a real scale tween) and `keys` (its keyframes animate `width`) is unchanged by this item. Resize under `spin` (GSAP animates rotation only) and `fromto` (GSAP animates `x` only) now saves the size as CSS, because nothing animates it there, as decided; their position or rotation still goes through GSAP.

## Test plan

- `gsapResizeElementSize.test.tsx` (new): runs the real resize and drag intercepts with the real plain writer. A GSAP-positioned, CSS-sized element saves `width: 340px; height: 227px` as inline CSS, makes no GSAP write of width/height, and moves its position hold under the same undo key. Control: with a size tween, the size still goes through GSAP and no CSS width/height is written.
- `gsapResizeIntercept.test.ts`: the fade-only case now returns `element-size` with no mutation.
- The new test also pins that the CSS size is saved before the GSAP write and with `deferRender`.
- Both new assertions fail with the fix reverted (main writes `{ type: "add", method: "set", properties: { width, height } }`; without the mask skip the patch carries `scale: none`).
- Edit-accuracy bench, `--filter '^resize-hold-'` (48 rows): drop, reload and render pass on all 48. The 24 nested rows pass every metric, as on main. On the 24 root rows, reload and render were the failing metrics on main (reload 60-120 px) and now pass. Undo still fails on 21 of the 24 root rows (undone box off by 44-196 px); that is the separate in-place undo restore issue, not this writer.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

## Before

The hold fixture (`gsap.set("#target", { x: 40, y: 20 })`, CSS size 240x160) resized to 340x227, then reloaded: the box snaps back to 240x160.

![Before: resized](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2b32ff4-90ca-4782-a135-5042316e6620)
![Before: after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d49a6fd0-ed4e-4f64-85b1-d757617e1c94)

## After

Same fixture and gesture: the reloaded box keeps 340x227. The file has `width: 340px; height: 227px` on the element and `gsap.set("#target", { x: -10, y: -13.5 })`.

![After: resized, still selected, before any reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd3e0f6a-d7e5-4c23-a5cc-79567139bd36)
![After: after reload](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ac1c900d-ae93-4557-87cb-19175eccafb5)




---

### Item 2: Cause A, an undo of a style-only edit on a layer GSAP parsed

An undo or redo of a crop (or any style-only edit) on a layer GSAP animates now puts the layer back where its file and script put it. Before, a `gsap.set` hold lost its position (10 px off on the edit-accuracy fixture), a tween counted the stylesheet `translate` twice, and a CSS `rotate` was applied twice.

**Why.** The in-place undo copies the file's attributes onto the live element. That wipes what GSAP wrote inline when it first parsed the element (`translate: none; rotate: none; scale: none`, and for an off-timeline `gsap.set` the transform itself), while GSAP's cache keeps the parsed values. When the script did not change, the restore only seeked, so GSAP never parsed the element again.

**How.**
- `applyUndoRestoreToPreview`: when a synced element was parsed by GSAP and the document has one GSAP script, re-run the restored script in place, even if its text is unchanged. A document with several GSAP scripts cannot re-run one in place, so that case reloads.
- `applySoftReload` takes those elements as `reparse` and resets GSAP's cache for exactly them.

**Proof.**
- `gsapUndoRestore.browser.test.ts` drives real Chrome with the edit-accuracy fixtures (hold, tween, xPercent tween with CSS `rotate: 30deg`), crops the live layer, undoes and compares the box with the one before the edit. Without the fix 3 cases fail (hold y 330 vs 320; tween 660,367.5 vs 620,337.5; rotated box swapped); with it all pass.
- `gsapUndoRestore.test.ts` adds the several-scripts branch: a style restore on a GSAP-parsed element in a two-script file reloads. Without the branch it returns `soft`; with it, `full`.

**Keyframe rule rows.** This item writes nothing; it changes only how the preview shows an undo or redo.

#### Before (cause A)

`crop-hold-px-r0-root-z100`: crop, then Cmd+Z. The layer lands 10 px below where its file puts it; redo is off by the same 10 px.

![Before: after Cmd+Z the layer sits below the red line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bba38de-98a4-4e6e-89a8-3fec60615168)

#### After (cause A)

Same case: undo and redo land exactly (box error 0).

![After: after Cmd+Z the layer sits on the red line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f0927a92-f6ae-48be-ab93-ed34a8870e5f)


---

### Item 3: Cause C, a move on a layer centred by an authored xPercent set

A move, nudge or resize of a layer centred by an authored `gsap.set({ xPercent: -50, yPercent: -50 })` with an x/y tween now keeps that centring set in the saved file. Before, the position dedupe treated the centring set and the x/y tween as two conflicting position writes and deleted the set, so the saved layer landed half its size off (+120, +80 on the fixture).

**How.**
- One predicate, `isXYPositionWrite` in `packages/parsers/src/gsapConstants.ts`: only writes of `x`/`y` count as position writes that conflict. Both writers' dedupe (acorn and recast), Studio's self-heal before a move commit and the stale-id rematch use it.
- The drag's clearProps probe now restores every position channel, so a drag on a centred layer no longer flashes off-centre on release.

**Proof.**
- `gsapRuntimeBridge.test.ts` and `gsapWriter.parity.test.ts` keep the centring set through a move; each fails with its part reverted.
- The release flash has no unit test (the test DOM does not render it); its proof is the bench's teleport check: without that part, 19 rows failed teleport at 144 px.
- CI on main plus this item alone: 34 newly passing (`move`, `nudge` and `resize` `-tween-xpercent-` rows), 0 regressed.

**Keyframe rule rows.** The x/y keyframe a move writes is unchanged (the existing position writer); this item only stops deleting a set nothing replaces.

#### Before (cause C)

Release, then reload: the layer reloads half its size off where it was dropped.

![Before: dropped and reloaded positions differ](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7bb547ad-c2dd-42a7-8efa-b494a9073f81)

#### After (cause C)

Same gesture: the reloaded layer sits where it was dropped.

![After: dropped and reloaded positions match](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/09ba9b5e-285a-4ec3-98ed-6f7c872d19fa)




---

### Item 4: Font pick writes once

Picking an imported font for a text layer now saves the style edit and its `@font-face` rule in one file write. Before, the edit and the `@font-face` were two writes, so the file could hold one without the other and undo needed two steps.

**How.** The patch request carries the imported font (`importedFont`); the server adds its `@font-face` rule to the file's Studio font block (`studioFontFace.ts`, creating the block in `<head>` the first time) in the same write as the edit. The client-side second write is removed.

**Proof.** On the base code the route test, the helper test and 5 client tests fail; with the `fontFaceCss` handling deleted, the route test, `canvasQuickSaves` and both one-request tests fail; with the fix, `studio-server` and `studio` pass on the touched files and both typecheck.

**The `@font-face` check.** The server accepts `fontFaceCss` only as exactly one `@font-face { ... }` rule: braces only inside quoted strings, `<` nowhere (the HTML parser ends the style block at `</style` whatever the CSS quoting says), and no LF, CR or form feed inside a string or after a backslash (CSS ends a string at any of the three, so a following `}` would close the rule). Route and helper tests: a trailing second rule, two rules, `</style>` inside quotes, an unterminated quote, escaped quotes, and a CR or a form feed inside the family name each give a 400; a file path with `{}` in its name is accepted and written. Each new rejection test fails on the check before it (a trailing rule passed a `startsWith` check, braces failed a no-braces pattern, CR and FF passed a pattern that excluded only LF).

**Keyframe rule rows.** Not applicable: no GSAP write.

No captures: this item changes no pixels, only how many writes a font pick makes.



---

### Item 5: a focused combobox, switch or plain-text editor counts as an unsaved edit

`studioPendingEdits.ts` had its own "the user is typing" selector, which missed `contenteditable="plaintext-only"` (inline text editing), `combobox`, `searchbox` and `switch`. It now asks `isTypingTarget(document.activeElement)` from `utils/typingTarget.ts`, the one owner of that question.

**Proof.** `studioPendingEdits.test.ts` focuses each of the four and expects a pending edit: all 4 fail with the old selector, all pass with the shared one.

**Keyframe rule rows.** Not applicable. No captures: no pixels change.

---

### Item 6: comment ratchet, `i--` before a quoted slash

`scripts/comment-ratchet.test.mjs` adds `const a = i-- / 2 + 'a/b'; // it's` (one comment line). With `--` dropped from `stripLiterals`' value-end rule the test fails (23 pass, 1 fail); with it, 24 pass. Before this line, dropping `--` kept every test green.

---

### Item 7: an inspector edit saved while a preview reload loads stays on screen

`persistDomEditOperations` counts every DOM-patch save as a manual-edit save (start and settle), so a preview reload that is loading while the save lands does not promote a stale shadow preview over it. A selection without an element skips the count.

**Proof.** `inspectorSaveReload.test.tsx` passes with the fix, fails on main plus item 4 without the count, and fails with the count deleted (the stale shadow is promoted). `studio-server` and `studio` pass; typecheck clean.

**Keyframe rule rows.** Not applicable. No captures: the race has no UI path to drive.

---

### Edit-accuracy gate and bank

CI gate on e83ed766012 (items 1-7 plus the font check, on main c3b6e55f7eb): 951 passing vs 852, **0 regressed**, 0 unstable, 99 newly passing, banked byte for byte from that run's artifact as the last commit: 20 `resize-hold-*-root` (item 1), 24 `crop-hold` + 21 `crop-tween` (item 2), 12 `move-tween-xpercent` + 12 `nudge-tween-xpercent` + 10 `resize-tween-xpercent` (item 3). The carrier was then rebased onto main d218cec091a, which changes only CI workflow and scripts, so the banked file is unchanged; the gate on this head re-checks it. All 36 `resize-tween-{center,pct,px}` rows pass every gated metric, `resize-tween-center-r0-root-z200`'s undo included.
