title: fix(studio): soft reloads restore what GSAP wrote and holds from the saved files
body:
## What

After a soft reload of the preview (a move, an undo, a redo, a timeline timing edit), every element the reloaded script animates or holds looks the way a fresh load of the saved files shows it, including elements that live in a nested composition.

Cases reproduced on main in a built Studio (an undo walk over a generated fixture, each step compared with a fresh load) and fixed here, with the file staying the source of truth (no read of the served preview page):

1. A nested element with a stylesheet `translate` that a top-level tween animates ends up off after a soft reload: 15 px after an edit in its own composition, 11.3 px after a top-level edit.
2. A width tween creeps on every soft reload: a nested element went 288, 316, 337, 353 px against a fresh load's 250, a top-level element 366, 387, 403, 415 px against 338.
3. A timeline timing edit (dragging a clip) soft-reloads without any file: on main the dragged box sat 31.4 px off and a rotated box lost its rotation, on top of cases 1 and 2.
4. A top-level `gsap.set` hold on an element whose inline style a resize had synced away was not reset: after the undo it sat 60 px off (its stylesheet `translate` counted twice).
5. A root reload reset a `gsap.set` hold inside a sub-composition defined inline, whose script it does not re-run: the held box lost its 60 px hold.
6. A script that builds DOM (a `createElement`, a template clone) built it again on every soft reload: after move, undo, redo, undo the preview held five copies of each node.

## Why

A soft reload clears GSAP's cache on each element it rebuilds (`clearProps: "all"`, which also empties the style attribute), puts the live inline style back, then patches from the written file what GSAP wrote. What was wrong:

- **Wrong file for a nested element.** The lookup only searched the top-level file. A nested element was never found, so it kept GSAP's `translate: none` mask.
- **Only the transform family came from the file.** Anything else a tween wrote inline (a width) stayed as the live value, and the re-run tween read it back as its new start.
- **The timing-edit path passed no file**, so none of the above could come from the file there.
- **The sweep for elements GSAP holds outside a timeline** looked only at elements that still carried an inline transform, and in every composition, not only the reloaded one.
- **Re-running a script re-runs its DOM building**, and nothing removes the first run's nodes.

## Related work

Refs #4783 (closed; it fixed cases 1 and 2 by reading the served preview page, which this replaces with a file-side fix). Overlaps #4778 (draft), which restores the whole style attribute from the file for top-level elements. This PR restores only what GSAP wrote, so the runtime's own layout writes (a forced `position: absolute`, a `data-width` size) are kept; a test pins that. It is built on main, after #4869, whose re-parse targets now seed the same reset map.

## How

- **What a reset element gets back from the file:** the transform family plus every CSS property its killed tweens name in their vars (top level, `css`, `startAt`, `keyframes`). Every other property keeps its live value. Opacity keeps its own restore.
- **Which file:** the file named by the closest inlined composition host (`data-composition-file`), else the file just written.
- **Reading a nested file:** for an element written in another composition file, the caller reads that file first (`readNestedFiles` reads only the files the re-run needs) and hands the text to the soft reload, which stays synchronous. The undo, commit and timing-edit paths all do this. If a read fails, the soft reload refuses and the caller reloads the preview in full, so a failed read cannot quietly bring the bug back.
- **Timing edits:** the soft reload gets the file the edit wrote (the SDK write's `after`, or the mutation endpoint's `after` for the active composition).
- **What a reload resets:** the tweens of the re-run composition's own timeline, plus every element GSAP has touched (`_gsap`) whose nearest composition root is the reloaded one, minus anything another timeline animates. A nested composition's elements are left to its own script.
- **DOM-building scripts:** if the re-run adds elements to the page, the soft reload reports it cannot apply and the caller reloads in full (as for a script that throws).
- **Where it lives:** which elements a reload resets, what their tweens wrote and which file writes each is in `softReloadTargets.ts`; the soft reload keeps the reset itself.

Known limit: a tween of `width` on a clip the runtime sizes from `data-width` loses that runtime width at the reset, since the file has no inline width.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests. Run against main's code before #4869, 18 of the touched tests fail there and pass here. 16 fail on behaviour: the nested and root tweened-style restores, a nested composition's own reload restoring from the file just written, the nested-file reads and their failure path (soft reload, undo caller, commit caller, timing caller), the composition-scoped sweeps, the held element, the inline sub-composition's hold, and the DOM-building escalation. 1 (a nested composition's own timeline target is left alone) holds on main's behaviour and fails there only because it calls `readNestedFiles`. 1 existing test (the orphaned transform strip) fails on main only because its mock now answers the composition-root query instead of the transform selector.
- [x] The caller wiring is covered: dropping `nestedFiles` from the undo caller, the commit caller or the timing caller, dropping the timing caller's file, or turning a failed read back into "no file" each fails a test.
- [x] Edit accuracy bench, the 54 nested tween cases (move, nudge, resize) that regressed on this PR's first head: all pass their gated checks.
- [x] The 20 resize cases on a top-level `gsap.set` hold (case 4) now pass on main through #4869's re-parse; this branch's sweep fixes them on its own too (with the sweep's old inline-transform gate put back, their undo lands 50 and 196 px off).
- [x] Manual testing performed: an undo walk in a built Studio over generated fixtures, comparing every element, top-level and nested, with a fresh load after each of four steps (edit, undo, redo, undo). This branch: 0 differences on every step of every scenario below. Main:
  - move a top-level held element: 6 differences per undo or redo
  - resize a held element: 8 after the undo (the held box 60 px off)
  - drag a clip on the timeline: 10 after the drag
  - move next to an inline sub-composition: 3 (its held box lost its hold)
  - a script that builds DOM: one more copy of each node per step
  - clips the runtime lays out (`data-width`, no CSS position): 0 on main, #4778 and this branch alike
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Main. A move of a nested element that its own timeline animates: the light-green nested box sits 15 px off, the blue box lost its rotation and the purple box its held position.

![main after a nested move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/12fb78bd-3020-4b1d-bd13-bc48565a816c)

Main. Move a top-level element, undo, redo, undo: the red top-level box and the pink nested bar have grown, the light-green nested box sits off.

![main after the undo walk](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a676a2b1-b676-4bac-9e4a-3a6c82f7fb91)

## After

This branch, same steps. Every element matches a fresh load.

![branch after a nested move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c42edd52-ca4c-4c9c-b36d-ff193e01ddd9)

![branch after the undo walk](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bb18a064-8fa4-4ef8-903c-cb055489ee4b)


## Before / After: undo of a resize on a held element

Main. Resize the purple box (a top-level `gsap.set` hold), then undo: it sits 60 px down and right of where a fresh load puts it, because its stylesheet `translate` counts twice.

![main after undo of a resize on a held element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13e3ccf5-de72-4f43-a362-823353450521)

This branch, same steps: the purple box is back where a fresh load puts it.

![branch after undo of a resize on a held element](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2ca2a41-1073-425b-b1eb-b486a5653f93)

## Before / After: drag a clip on the timeline

Main. Drag the yellow box's clip later on the timeline: the yellow box sits 31.4 px off and the blue box lost its rotation (10 elements differ from a fresh load).

![main after a clip drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bec30918-8196-4d91-a4ab-139a528c0874)

This branch, same drag: every element matches a fresh load.

![branch after a clip drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90930b8e-cd41-498d-b661-38c699617329)

title: ci(studio): gates read the base the run measured, and drag frames on a quiet runner
body:
## What changed

**Base-dependent gates read the base the run measured.** Three pull request steps in `ci.yml` read a file from the base branch: the edit accuracy baseline (in each of the 12 shards and in the gate) and the perf ceilings. They fetched the base branch tip when the step ran. The shards measured the merge commit built when the run started, so when a PR that rewrites the baseline merged mid-run, the gate compared old measurements against the new baseline and failed every open PR as regressed. In one run the shards measured 846 cases at 22:09Z, the base moved at 22:22Z, and the gate at 22:32Z read 852.

All three steps now call `scripts/ci/base-file.sh`, which reads the file from the first parent of the checked-out merge commit, the base every job in the run measured. It prints that sha in the step log. A base without the file keeps the old fallbacks (an empty baseline, no ceilings), and a failed fetch now fails the step instead of passing as "no baseline".

**Drag smoothness on a quiet runner.** A new workflow, "Studio drag frames", builds the CLI (which bundles the built Studio) and runs the edit accuracy bench five times on the eight drag cases. It uploads every run's output. A last step fails the job unless the bench's blank-page control dropped 0 frames in every case of every run, so a red job means the runner was not quiet. It runs on manual dispatch with a `ref` input (default `main`) and on pull requests that change the workflow file.

## What I measured

- `scripts/ci/base-file.test.mjs` builds a shallow checkout of a merge commit, then moves the base branch to a new baseline. The script reads the old baseline and logs the parent sha (2 pass). Changed to read the base branch tip, both cases fail.
- `actionlint` on `ci.yml` reports the same 6 shellcheck notes as on main, none in the changed steps. `studio-drag-frames.yml`: exit 0.
- The drag workflow's first run on this PR passed: the blank page dropped 0 frames in every case of every run.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real mid-run base move on GitHub. The fix rests on `actions/checkout` checking out the merge commit on pull requests, and on fetching a single sha at depth 1, which checkout itself does.
- Dispatch with a `ref`. GitHub offers dispatch only for workflows on the default branch.

title: fix(studio): a reload requested while a canvas save is in flight loads again once it lands
body:
## What

Follow-up to #4856. A reload requested while a canvas save is still in flight no longer goes on screen with the file from before the save.

#4856 counts each canvas save when it starts, and a shadow reload requested before a later count loads again instead of being promoted. A reload requested after the count but before the save landed recorded the new count, so it was promoted with the old file.

## How

- `countStudioManualEditSave(element, save)` runs the save and counts it twice: as it starts and as it settles. It replaces the start-only count.
- The overlay's commit refs (move, group move, resize, rotate, crop and other canvas style commits) and the inline text commit go through it.
- The cost: a reload a save triggers itself, on the full-reload path, is counted as stale once and loads one more time. It never shows the old file.

## Tests

`gestureHoldsPreviewReload.test.tsx`:
- A reload requested during a move, a resize, a rotate and a crop, painting after the release, is not promoted; a fresh load shows the edit (one case each, so dropping any one path's count fails).
- A reload requested while the drop is still saving, painting after the save lands, is not promoted; a fresh load shows the drop.
- A press that throws before the drag is armed leaves no mark, for one layer and for a group.

The race has no path through Studio's own UI. An edit to the file from outside waits for pending saves before it reloads, and Studio's own saves queue behind each other. Only a reload a host triggers inside the save window reaches it, and that is what the new tests drive.

## Before

Main (78e84923), from the CLI's blank template in a real browser: select the title, drag it, hold its save request, edit `index.html` from outside during the hold, then let the save land. The outside edit waits for the save, so the drop shows:

![before walk](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e081909-c181-405d-bd1f-8acc685d8848)

The late-reload test, run on main with this PR's tests: the save-in-flight case fails.

![before tests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/78e2722b-a360-4d2c-9b95-b24092b1c83b)

## After

This branch, the same walk: the drop shows, the same as main, so the outside-edit path is unchanged.

![after walk](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5dbf27f2-90b8-45d3-b7a9-20325895c5a1)

The same tests on this branch all pass.

![after tests](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c9f522f-4c00-4621-8c07-306abc21ed5a)

title: fix(studio): a text edited in place shows its caret in a scaled preview
body:
## What

A text edited in place shows a visible caret. While an inline text edit is open, Studio draws its own caret: 2 px wide on screen, in the text's caret colour, standing where the real selection is. It blinks like the system caret, restarts lit on every move, does not blink under reduced motion, and is hidden while a range is selected, during input-method composition, and once the text loses focus.

## Why

The preview draws a composition at its own size and shows it scaled. At a 1920 px composition in a 600 px preview the scale is about 0.31, so the browser's 1 px caret paints at about 0.3 px: the edit opens and typing lands, but no caret can be seen. Any preview narrower than its composition has this.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `InlineTextCaret` (new, next to `InlineTextToolbar` and rendered with it by `useInlineTextEditing`) follows the same mapping as the toolbar: `position: fixed`, the iframe's box plus the composition point times the preview scale. It reads the collapsed range's last client rect (an empty text or line falls back to the text's start, one line tall), refreshes on `selectionchange`, `input`, focus, blur, composition start and end, window resize and the iframe's size, and sets the edited element's `caret-color` to transparent while it draws, restoring it after.
- The caret is portaled into Studio's own body. Inside the canvas, a transformed ancestor captures `position: fixed`, which put the caret 373 x 80 px off.
- At an element boundary (after a bold word, or on an empty line made by Shift+Enter) the collapsed range has no box. The caret then stands at the end of the node before it, or at the start of the node after it.
- It follows any move of the preview: the iframe's box is checked once per frame while an edit is open, so a pan or zoom of the stage (a transform that fires no event), the player's rescale and Studio's scroll all re-place it.
- A soft-wrap point is both one line's end and the next line's start, and the DOM does not say which. The caret keeps a side, as CodeMirror and ProseMirror do: End gives "before" (where Chrome leaves its own caret); any other key or a press gives "after", since an arrow onto a wrap point lands on the next line. With "before" it stands at the right edge of the character before it, on the earlier line.
- The inline style bar had the same `position: fixed` problem inside the transformed canvas: on a range it stood about 430 px off the text. It is portaled to Studio's body too.
- Styled text opens for editing in every browser. Deciding whether an element can be edited in place asked whether each formatting child is an instance of the preview window's `HTMLElement`. Preview nodes can carry another window's prototypes; on Chrome 154 a `<strong>` failed that test, so a text with a bold word never opened. The check now reads the child's namespace, the same realm-safe test Studio already uses for audio nodes.
- Also, from review on #4864: `recordFileWriteReceipt` takes the path, version and write token, and builds the receipt itself (test in `fileVersion.test.ts`).
- The blink is a CSS animation in `components.css` (`hf-inline-text-caret`), off under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`. The caret is keyed on its position, so each move restarts the blink lit.

## Test plan

- `InlineTextCaret.test.tsx`: the caret's position, height and width come from the selection rect through the preview scale, in the text's colour; none while a range is selected, back when it collapses; none during composition or after blur; the element's own caret colour is hidden and restored.
- `tests/e2e/inline-text-caret.mjs` (new, real Chrome, in CI next to the fade-handle check, fixture `inline-text-caret`): a double-click opens the Title with a 2 px, line-tall caret at the selection; typing moves it on; Shift+ArrowLeft hides it, ArrowRight brings it back; Escape removes it; the style bar stands by a selected range; past a bold word the caret stands at the word's end; in a paragraph wrapped onto three lines, End keeps the caret at the first line's end (after its last character, on that line) and ArrowDown moves it down a line; on an empty line made by Shift+Enter it stands at the line's start; after a window resize it still stands on the selection; under reduced motion it does not blink; blur removes it. Screenshots go to the gate's evidence artifact.

title: test(studio): add full-frame and smaller object-fit images to the edit accuracy grid
body:
## What Adds 41 image cases to the Studio edit accuracy grid: an `` with `object-fit: contain` or `cover`, full-frame (the size of its composition, at 0,0) or smaller than the frame (640x360), crossed with the five gestures (move, resize, rotate, crop, nudge), root and nested, at zoom 100 and rotation 0 with no GSAP, plus one GSAP-tween full-frame contain move for contrast. Each pointer gesture on an image also gets the stray no-button pointer move a hand drag meets. ## Why Dragging a full-frame picture placed from the asset shelf (1920x1080, `object-fit: contain`) saves a wrong translate at release, so the picture jumps away from the pointer. Mid-drag, Chromium sends hover moves with no button held, and the drag takes them as travel. The grid had only small flat `
` targets and only button-held moves, so none of its cases reached this. These cases catch it, and once it is fixed the gate keeps it fixed. ## Related work Refs #4866, which adds a keyframes grid in the same files (`grid.mjs` and `run.mjs`). Whichever lands second rebases and re-banks. ## How - `grid.mjs`: `imageCases()` builds the new rows the way `dragCases()` does. Their placement token (`imgcontainfull`, `imgcoversmall`, ...) is letters only, so `--filter '-img(contain|cover)'` selects them. The image is an inline 4:3 PNG data URL in the target colour, so nothing is fetched; contain letterboxes it in a 16:9 box and cover crops it. - The element keeps the target colour as its background, so the producer frame's pixel box is the element box. That is the box the bench measures (`DOM.getContentQuads` of the element) and the box Studio selects and drags, not the letterboxed picture inside it. - `case.mjs`: for these cases only, one `pointermove` with `buttons: 0` goes to the pressed element just before release, at (-611, +213.6) composition px from the press, where the hand repro's stray move landed. It reuses the bench's `strayMove` (added by #4880 for the pathstray rows), which now takes the press point so a handle drag gets it on the pressed handle. A CDP mouse move with no buttons ended the drag unsaved instead. - `run.mjs`: the render metric clips the expected box to the target's composition frame. A full-frame image moved by the gesture runs past the frame edge, which the producer frame cannot show; every existing case stays inside its frame, so their scores do not change. ## Results on main From this PR's gate run (CI, merged with main after #4880 and #4866): - Pass and banked (37): all 8 crop, all 8 nudge, all 9 move (including the GSAP tween), all 8 resize, and the 4 small rotates. Before #4880, the move and resize cases failed on the stray move (move drop 717.6 px, saved `translate: -610.987px 213.6px` for a +90,+60 move); they now pass, and the gate keeps them passing. - Fail (4), base-failing, so they block no one: - rotate, full-frame, root (2): the box tracks 264.6 px off the pointer and the teleport check fails. - rotate, full-frame, nested (2): render only, 83 px. A rotated full-frame box leaves the frame, which the render metric cannot score, so these two are a bench limit. - Gate: 1253 passing here, 1216 on main, 0 regressed, 0 unstable. Runner-minute impact per PR run: 41 cases x 29.1 s average = about 20 runner-minutes, spread over the 20 shards (under 2 minutes of wall time each). A PR that flips some of them adds two confirmation re-runs per flipped case. ## Before ![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68240fd7-cd15-463a-bfca-10c2995401f9) ## After ![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c824a2e-931b-442b-8a73-93b3475d5d98) ## Test plan - [x] The new cases are gated with today's rules: a new failing case has no base entry, so it blocks nothing; the 16 passing ones are banked byte for byte from the gate artifact as the last commit, and replaying the gate locally on that run passes. - [x] Per-case results on main come from this PR's own gate run. - [ ] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): undo paints a move or nudge back at once while its save is still running
body:
## What

If you press Cmd+Z while a move or a nudge is still saving, the box now jumps back to where it was in the same frame as the key. Before, it stayed at the moved place until the save and the server's undo had both landed. Under load that was often a second or more, so a drag started from what was on screen then jumped.

## Why

Undo's instant paint (from #4798) predicts the step from this tab's history and shows it in place. An edit that is still saving has no history entry yet, so the prediction would show the edit before it, and the paint is refused. The screen then waited for the server.

The same gap stayed open briefly after each save: the save ended before the history list holding its entry had been fetched, so for that moment the edit was neither pending nor known to the history.

## How

- A pending edit can now carry a live revert: a function that shows the edit undone and returns one that shows it again.
- The canvas move (single and group) and the arrow-key nudge burst register their saves as pending edits with a revert. The revert puts the moved elements back at their offset from the start of the gesture. Elements GSAP positions have no revert, so they still wait as they do today.
- When the instant paint is refused, undo paints the newest pending edit back, in the key's own task. Only the newest is painted: one Cmd+Z undoes one edit. A second Cmd+Z while that edit is still saving paints nothing and waits.
- If the server step fails or steps nothing, the edit is shown again.
- A nudge burst that undo painted back while it was still waiting for keys is still saved, so the server can undo it, but its commit no longer draws it again.
- Anything an edit starts inside its own registration (the tracked context action, a GSAP commit) counts as part of that edit, not as a newer one. An edit whose start throws ends its registration, so it cannot hold up later undos and exports.
- `recordEdit` now waits for the history list it fetches after a claim. A save therefore ends only once undo can predict it, which closes the gap above. The fetch was already requested after every claim (`void refresh()`); it is now awaited, so there is no extra request, and a save ends when that fetch returns instead of before it.
- Bench: undo and a text step's Enter now wait a frame before the next step reads the box, as a nudge already does per key.
- `seqrepeat-none-px-r0-nested-z100` and `sequndo-none-px-r0-root-z100` are out of the quarantine list. The quarantine list is now empty.

## Why the bench needed the frame

The drag that follows an undo read the box with CDP `DOM.getContentQuads` 0 to 4 ms after Studio had already moved it back in the DOM. In the failing runs that read still returned the spot before the undo, while `getBoundingClientRect` on the same element right after returned the spot after it. Reads that passed had a frame between the undo and the read.

| Traced build of this branch before the `recordEdit` wait (gsap=none, 6 cases a run) | Read the spot before the undo | Move, undo, drag back passes |
|---|---|---|
| Bench as on main, 4 runs | 1 to 4 of 6 per run | 2 to 5 of 6 per run |
| Bench waiting a frame after the key, 3 runs | 0 of 18 | 17 of 18, the miss being the gap fixed by the `recordEdit` wait |

So the bench pressed where the box had been before the frame that showed the undo. Two frames later, at mouse down, the box was no longer there, and the press started no drag. Before this PR the box stayed put until the server's undo, which hid the race.

## Bench

On one machine, 3 jobs, three runs of each build, with this branch's bench:

| Sequence (gsap=none) | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| move, undo, drag back (6 cases) | 18/18 | 18/18 |
| nudge one key, undo on the next frame (6 cases) | 18/18 | 18/18 |
| move, move, move, then the undo walk (px, nested) | 3/3 | 3/3 |

Both builds pass every run once the bench waits for the frame, so this table shows no regression; it does not measure the gain. The gain is how soon the box shows undone, which is in the captures below. "This PR" is the build one commit before the head; the only later change removes a code comment. In CI the gate passes, with nothing newly passing or unbanked: main's baseline already banks both ids taken off the quarantine list as passing.

## Test plan

- [x] `studioPendingEdits.test.ts`: only the newest edit is painted back, once, and shown again on request; nothing is painted when the newest edit has no revert; what an edit starts inside its registration is part of it; an edit whose start throws ends its registration. The last fails when a throwing start does not end the registration.
- [x] `dragUndoPaint.test.ts`: a drag whose save is still running can be painted back at once and shown again, and stops counting once its save lands. Fails when the drag registers no revert.
- [x] `useEditHistoryActions.paint.test.tsx`, over the real history engine:
  - an undo pressed while a nudge's save is queued shows the nudge undone in the key's own task, and the file and the box end undone;
  - an undo inside the nudge's wait shows the nudge undone at once, and the burst's commit doesn't draw it again.

  Both fail without the revert paint; the second also fails when the burst's commit redraws it.
- [x] `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts`: with the history list slowed by 50 ms, the step is predicted as soon as the save ends. Fails when `recordEdit` does not wait for the list.
- [x] Bench unit tests (`tests/e2e/edit-accuracy`), the Studio suite, typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt.

## Before

A move in a bench fixture with every save slowed to 1.5 s, Ctrl+Z on the frame after release, on #4807: the box stays at the moved place until the server's undo lands.

![before-queued-undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3d496178-668d-4bbf-9d57-c38c4f22a51c)

## After

The same on this branch: the box is back in the first frame after the key and stays there.

How to read the panels: each one is the last frame the browser's screencast sent at or before that time. The screencast sent no frame between 107 ms before the key and 107 ms after it, so the "50 ms after" panel repeats the frame from before the key. The first frame after the key, at 107 ms, already shows the box back at its start; the selection outline has caught up by the next frame it sent, at 209 ms. The strip cannot show how soon the box paints. That comes from the tests, which check that the box is back in the key's own task. The capture was taken on a build of the first commit of this branch; later commits change neither the move nor its revert.

![after-queued-undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a643c98e-fd89-49e5-a3a9-4564ae1e676a)

title: fix(lint): do not treat text inside quoted attributes as boolean attribute names (#4381)
body:
## What

Make `hasAttrName` in `@hyperframes/lint` quote-aware by parsing HTML attributes via `htmlparser2` instead of regex matching raw attribute text.

## Problem and user impact

When an element contains text inside single- or double-quoted attributes (such as `title="an unmuted muted clip"` or `aria-label="muted"`), the linter misinterprets the text inside quotes as a `muted` attribute.

This causes:
1. **False negatives (suppression of real errors)**: An unmuted video element with text containing the word "muted" in a title or tooltip wrongly passes lint, suppressing both `video_missing_muted` and `video_audio_double_source` diagnostics. In production, unmuted videos that lack audio synchronization or cause audio echo pass lint undetected.
2. **False positives**: Tooltips or descriptions containing words like `crossorigin` falsely trigger `media_crossorigin_breaks_preview` and fail validation.

## Root cause

`hasAttrName(tagSource, attr)` in `packages/lint/src/rules/media.ts` stripped the leading tag name and ran `new RegExp(`(?:^|\\s)${escaped}(?:\\s*=|\\s|/?>)`, "i")` directly over the raw attribute string. Because it did not parse attributes or track quote boundaries, any occurrence of an attribute name within quoted attribute values matched.

## Solution

Replaced the unquoted regex scan in `hasAttrName` with `htmlparser2`'s `Parser`. This:
- Ensures attribute values enclosed in quotes cannot impersonate attribute names.
- Preserves standard HTML boolean attribute semantics (bare attributes `<video muted>`, empty-string attributes `<video muted="">`, and valued boolean attributes like `<video muted="false">`).
- Retains case-insensitive matching for HTML attribute names.

## Related work

Fixes #4381

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - Added test case verifying text inside quoted attributes does not satisfy `muted` check, properly reporting `video_missing_muted` and `video_audio_double_source`.
  - Added test case verifying bare, valued, and case-insensitive `muted` attributes are recognized.
  - Added test case verifying `crossorigin` inside a quoted attribute value does not trigger `media_crossorigin_breaks_preview`.
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Verified reproduction script from issue #4381 fails before the fix and passes after the fix.
  - Verified `bun run --cwd packages/lint test src/rules/media.test.ts` (all 79 tests pass).
  - Verified `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `tsc --noEmit` pass with 0 errors.

title: fix(scripts): count comments after regex literals in the comment ratchet
body:
## What broke

The comment scanner behind the comment checks blanked string literals but not regex literals. A regex
such as `` /["'`]([^"'`]+)["'`]/g `` left an unpaired backtick behind, which the scanner read as the start
of a multi-line template literal, so every comment until the next backtick went uncounted. It also
read a `//` or `/*` inside a regex body (`/^\/\//`, `/\/\*[\s\S]*?\*\//`) as a comment.

Effect on the ratchet: `packages/studio/src/utils/gsapSoftReload.ts` measured 95 comment lines while
it really has 172, and merely moving that regex made a PR look like it added dozens of comment lines.

## Fix

`scanCLike` now blanks strings and regex literals in one left-to-right pass. A `/` starts a regex
unless the previous significant character is an identifier, number, `)`, `]`, `<` (a JSX closing tag),
or the line so far ends in `++` or `--`, and only when the literal closes on the same line. A regex never
closes on a comment opener, so a `/` whose would-be closer starts `//` or `/*` is treated as division;
that covers a line that opens with division continued from the line above, which a per-line scan cannot
see, while a real regex at the start of a line is still blanked. Python and the restates-code rule keep `stripStrings`.

Across the 1774 package source files, 52 change count. Every change is either comments that were
hidden after a regex (gsapSoftReload 95 -> 172, inlineSubCompositions 19 -> 158, probeStage
52 -> 106, useClipboard 20 -> 51, gsap rule 311 -> 340) or a regex body that was miscounted as a
comment (one line each). gsapSoftReload now matches a count taken with the TypeScript scanner exactly.

The ratchet compares each file against its own merge-base copy with the same script, so there is no
stored baseline to update and the higher counts cannot fail an unrelated PR.

## Test

`comment-ratchet.test.mjs` adds a source with a regex holding `'`, `"` and a backtick, followed by
line, trailing and block comments and two divisions. It measures 0 comment lines without the fix and
4 with it. Three more tests pin JSX closing tags, `++`/`--` before division, and a line that opens with
division; each goes from 0 to 1, and removing any one of the three rules fails its own test.



Merged below the usual size floor: opened minutes after the one-PR-per-lane rule landed, before the lane had it, and it fixes the comment check every PR runs, so it should not wait inside a larger PR.

title: fix(studio): a hand drag moves only with its own pointer pressed
body:
## What

A hand drag on the canvas now moves only on moves from the pointer that pressed, with its primary button still down. Other pointer moves during the drag are ignored.

## Why

Chromium re-sends the last pointer position it knows, with no button held, after a layout change. The overlay's move handler took those moves as drag travel. Mid-drag, the element flipped between the pointer and that stale point. The release then committed whichever move came last, so the drop could land hundreds of pixels from where the person let go, and their next press missed the element.

How it shows up: an image placed full-frame from the media shelf (`left: 0; top: 0; width: 1920px; height: 1080px; object-fit: contain`), dragged by +48, +24 screen px at a 0.27 canvas scale. While dragging, the draft `translate` steps 44.8 px → 179.4 px with the pointer. Between those writes, the same draft function writes `-611px 213.6px` once per stale move. The release saves `translate: -611.003px 213.594px` where the pointer asked for about `179px 90px`.

## Related work

Refs the promoted-preview selection work in 0.8.106: a different cause, but the same symptom of a drag that lands somewhere other than where it was dropped.

## How

- `GestureState` and `GroupGestureState` record the `pointerId` that started them.
- `movesGesture(gesture, e)` in `domEditOverlayGestures.ts` is the one rule: same pointer and `buttons & 1`. `onPointerMove` returns early on any other move while a single or group gesture is live. Hover, blocked moves and the no-gesture path are unchanged.
- The crop handles (`DomEditCropHandles.tsx` `updateCropGesture`) and the marquee band (`marqueeCommit.ts` `onPointerMove`) had the same bug: both commit from their last move, and a stale buttonless move at the press point undid the crop or shrank the band. Both now use the same `movesGesture` rule.
- Tests that drive the overlay with hand-built events now send `buttons: 1` on press and move, as a real drag does.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests for crop and marquee: a buttonless move back at the press point before the release; the crop still commits `inset(10px 30px 10px 10px)` and the band keeps its width. Each fails with its guard removed.
- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `gestureHoldsPreviewReload.test.tsx` gets two cases: a buttonless move, and a move from another pointer, each at a fixed point mid-drag and again as the last move before release. Both assert the draft and the saved file read `translate: 40px 20px`. With the guard removed, both fail.
- [x] `packages/studio`: `tsc --noEmit` clean, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files. The `src/components/editor`, `src/hooks` and `src/player` suites pass: 4747 tests. One run had a single failure in `useClipboard.source.test.ts` ("leaves the previous copy on the clipboard"). It does not touch pointers and passed 3 of 3 alone.
- [x] Edit accuracy grid: nine new `pathstray-*` cases (px, pct and centre placement, root and nested, r30, z50 and z200): a 180,90 drag whose last move before the release is a buttonless pointermove at the press point. Main fails all nine on drop, teleport and reload (the element is saved where it started, worst 1162 px at z50); this head passes all nine on every gated metric. The frame sampler now ignores that untrusted move as the pointer position, with a unit test. A CDP move with no button cannot model this: it ends the pointer capture, so the bench sends the move to the captured box.
- [x] Manual testing performed: an Electron host of the overlay on Linux, logging every `translate` write and every `pointermove` (`isTrusted`, `buttons`). Trusted `buttons=0` moves at one fixed point arrive between the real moves, and each one rewrites the stale offset.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): none needed.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

## Before

A generated fixture: one full-frame `object-fit: contain` image, selected, dragged 180,90 screen px, with a buttonless move at the press point just before the release. On main the image is saved back where it started (`translate: 0px 0px`).

![Before: the image is back where the drag started](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/698405e3-8c83-4dca-a458-5551cb9ff4cc)

## After

Same fixture and gesture on this head: the image stays where the pointer let go (`translate: 519.786px 259.893px`).

![After: the image lands where the pointer let go](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff9c090a-f39a-41e2-87be-ba9c73ccd69f)

## What I did NOT exercise

- A release from a second pointer still ends the gesture (`onPointerUp` has no pointer check); unchanged from main.
- If a release is never delivered, later buttonless moves are now ignored, so the element stays put until the next press instead of following the cursor.
- macOS. The stale moves were seen on Linux under Xvfb; that macOS sends them in the same way is an assumption.
- A pen or touch drag. Both report `buttons & 1` while in contact, so the rule should hold, but I did not run one.

title: fix(studio): a saved clip volume reaches the timeline store
body:
## What changed

Saving a clip's volume now updates the clip's copy in the timeline store at once, as automation, FX chains and fades already do, and undo and redo read the volume back from the preview.

- `automationStoreSync.ts`: `data-volume` joins `STORED_FIELD` (the element attribute save path, `syncStoredElementAttribute`) and `syncedFields` (the resync after DOM commits, undo and redo, `syncStoredAutomationFromPreview`).
- `timelineElementHelpers.ts`: the volume parse is shared (`parseStoredVolume`, `elementVolume`), so the sync reads volume exactly as discovery does.

## What was wrong

The store kept the volume parsed at load. After a volume save:

- **Studio's Volume field** (Design > Media): the agent's `studio_look` tool and the clip descriptions sent with Ask agent report the old level until the preview refresh re-parses the composition. On a fixture that took about 1.2 s on a quiet machine, and 2.4 to 4 s under load. An agent asked about the clip in that window gets the old number, and an edit based on it can put the old level back.
- **The element attribute save path** (`onSetElementAttributeQuiet`, which a host calls for a quick volume change): no refresh follows, so by the code the stored volume stays at the load-time level until the next reload, and anything reading `element.volume` (clip descriptions, a host's own volume control) shows it.

## What I measured

On Linux, a fixture built with ffmpeg (one video clip at volume 0.8), headless Chromium, the real `studio_look` tool called in the page; type 25% in the Volume field, Enter, read at a fixed delay:

- main: 0.8 in 10 of 10 runs at about 500 ms; 69 of 75 samples stale in the first 2.4 s under load.
- this branch: 0.25 in 10 of 10 runs; every sample at or after 500 ms reads 0.25 (63 of 63).
- Studio `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; Studio vitest 593 files passed, 1 skipped; the two new tests fail with the sync removed.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Undo and redo of a volume change in a running Studio (covered by a unit test only).
- The element attribute save path in a running Studio: no Studio control calls it with `data-volume` today; it is covered by a unit test.

## Size

Small on purpose: volume joins the two store-sync tables that automation, FX chains and fades already use,
and discovery's volume parse moves into one shared reader. Nothing else needs to change.

## Before

main, 559 ms after the save: the agent reads 0.8, the load-time level, while the file holds 0.25.

![Before: studio_look reads 0.8 after a save to 0.25](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/110a3cc1-6beb-4610-bcd9-305719660029)

## After

This branch, 523 ms after the same save: the agent reads 0.25.

![After: studio_look reads 0.25 after a save to 0.25](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0556305-feeb-42df-9175-e5edf73c7948)

title: fix(core): compile only the color grading stages a grade enables
body:
Fixes #4881.

## What was wrong

Every `data-color-grading` element drew through one fragment shader with every effect compiled in. A stage set to 0 returns early, which costs nothing on a GPU. Software GL (SwiftShader, which `check` uses when WebGL is unavailable or with `--no-browser-gpu`) and some ANGLE backends still pay for every stage on every pixel. So an adjust-only grade paid for ASCII, tape damage, crosshatch, glitch and the rest on each draw.

Measured on 0.8.106 with software GL, one 3s 1080p clip, adjust-only grade:

| | `hyperframes check` |
|---|---|
| No grading | 15s |
| Adjust-only grade | 231s |
| Same grade, main shader swapped for a passthrough | 21s |

`check` draws the grade about 60 times per run, at 3 to 4s each. On the reporter's Iris Xe with ANGLE/D3D11, that reads as a hang.

## The fix

- Each optional stage of the main fragment shader sits behind `#ifdef HF_STAGE_*`, and a guarded function falls back to returning its input.
- `FRAGMENT_SHADER_STAGES` is one table mapping each define to the grade condition that makes the stage change a pixel. That condition mirrors the shader's own `amount > 0` test.
- `useMainShader` compiles the variant for the grade's active stages, caches it per WebGL context in least-recently-used order, sized to one full Studio look-preview batch (32). It is the only way either draw site (`drawEntry`, `renderPreviewCandidate`) binds the main program. Preview, render and Studio look previews therefore share one path.
- The stage-free variant is still compiled when the context is created, so a context that cannot run the shader still fails at creation, as before.
- If a driver rejects one variant, that stage set is remembered and draws through the all-stages variant, which is the previous shader. It is not recompiled every frame.

## Equivalence and speed

- Old shader vs new shader with the derived defines, rendered in chrome-headless-shell on SwiftShader at 320x180: byte-identical `readPixels` output in 28 of 28 cases. Each stage was tested alone with its sub-parameters, plus RGB curves, hue curves, secondaries, LUT, compare, a combination, and tape sub-parameters with tape damage at 0.
- The CRT warp stays ungated. Returning `uv` directly differs from `(uv * 2 - 1) * 0.5 + 0.5` by one ulp, and that flips digital-glitch block boundaries.
- Per 1080p draw on SwiftShader: about 6s before, about 0.1s after.

## Tests

`packages/core/src/runtime/colorGrading.test.ts`, through the real runtime:
- An adjust-only grade compiles no stage.
- A grade compiles exactly the stages it enables.
- Each of the 24 stages is keyed to its own grade value: enabling only that value defines only that stage.
- A grade with everything enabled defines exactly the set of stages the shader guards. This pins the table and the GLSL against drift in both directions.
- A variant compiles once per stage set and is reused when the grade comes back.
- The least recently used variant is evicted at the cap, not one still in use.
- The variant comes from the animated grade (CSS custom properties), not the authored one.
- Look previews compile each candidate's own stages.
- A variant the driver rejects falls back to every stage, and is not retried.

Mutation-checked: all of these fail against the previous runtime. Deleting one table row fails the drift test. Swapping two predicates fails the per-stage test.

## Verification

- `vitest run src/runtime/colorGrading.test.ts`: 87 passed.
- `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/core` and `tsconfig.runtime.json`: clean.
- End-to-end, `hyperframes check` on the 1080p adjust-only repro with software GL: 231s on 0.8.106, 23s with this branch. The ungraded baseline is 15s.

## Independent review

Ranked findings from an independent adversarial review of this branch:
- Blocking: none.
- Should fix, done: fall back when a variant fails to compile instead of retrying every frame. Cover the animated-grade and look-preview selection paths with tests.
- Notes, left as they are:
  - The LUT stage is enabled whenever a LUT is configured, including while it loads. That is the same cost as before this change.
  - A new context compiles the stage-free variant plus the grade's variant.
  - The first look-preview batch can compile up to 32 variants.

_Miga_

title: fix(studio): a video cutout saves its linked audio again
body:
## Summary
Main's studio typecheck and tests broke after #4869: it removed `prepareContent` from the DOM-edit persist options and deleted its follow-up write, while #4813 relies on both. #4813's video cutout passes `prepareContent` so the original sound moves onto a linked `<audio>` beside the cutout video. On current main that option is a type error, and a cutout would be saved without its audio.

## Changes
- `PersistDomEditOperations` takes `prepareContent` again.
- `useDomEditPersist` applies it as the follow-up write over the server's patch, in the same file queue and the same undo entry. If that write fails, it shows a toast and keeps the saved patch.
- A `prepareContent` edit skips the SDK persist path, just as an imported font does: the SDK serializes only the patched DOM, so the sibling would be lost.
- An imported font still saves in a single write (the server's `fontFaceCss`), as #4869 made it.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit -p packages/studio`: 0 errors (fails on main at `useDomEditAttributeCommits.ts:278`, TS2353).
- `vitest run` in packages/studio: 599 files, 6611 tests pass. That includes #4813's "folds a document-level prepareContent into the same single undo entry", which fails on main. Making the follow-up write a no-op fails it again.

Small on purpose: main is red until this lands, so it ships alone instead of riding a larger PR.

## Before

Main: select a video with sound, Remove BG. The panel says the sound was kept on a linked audio track, but the timeline shows only the video clip, and the saved file has the video muted with no `<audio>` beside it.

![main: cutout saved with no linked audio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49615a6e-25e3-4800-872d-37bba0e6b910)

## After

This branch, same steps on the same project: the saved file now holds the linked `<audio>` with the original sound, and the timeline shows it as an audio row under the video.

![branch: cutout saved with its linked audio](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cf51d699-da7c-449a-94e4-3dec0d114253)

title: fix(studio): persist honors prepareContent again so audio edits keep their content step
body:
## What

Main fails \`Typecheck\` (\`useDomEditAttributeCommits.ts(278,13): 'prepareContent' does not exist in type …\`). #4869 removed \`prepareContent\` from \`PersistDomEditOperations\` and from the persist server path (replacing it with \`importedFont\`), while #4813's attribute batch commit (\`mediaAudioEdits\`) still passes it. Every queued PR fails its merge-group CI until this lands, and the audio edit silently loses its prepared content.

## Change

- Restore \`prepareContent\` in the persist options type.
- Take the server patch (not the SDK path) when it is set, as before.
- Write the prepared content over the patch inside the same file queue, via the restored \`writePreparedContent\`.
- The font path from #4869 (\`importedFont\`) is untouched.

## Tests

New regression in \`canvasQuickSaves.test.tsx\`: a batch commit with \`prepareContent\` writes the prepared content once. It fails without the fix. \`tsc\` is clean, and all of \`src/hooks\` plus \`mediaAudioEdits\` pass (1188 tests).

## No visible change

No pixel or UI change: this restores a save path that already existed before #4869.

title: fix(studio): keep a pick made just before a reload swaps the preview frame
body:
## What changed

A pick made in the preview could be lost when a reload swapped in a new preview frame between the pick and its message.

The player reloads a changed film in a shadow frame and promotes it once it is ready (`iframeRef.current = shadow`). A pick made on the frame still showing posts `element-picked` from that frame. When the promotion lands before the message is handled, `useElementPicker` saw a source that is no longer `iframeRef.current` and dropped it. The preview kept its own outline and the timeline selected the clip, but the host app's `pickedElement` stayed empty, so nothing that hangs off the pick showed.

`useElementPicker` now remembers each window that posted while it was the primary preview frame and accepts a pick from any of them. A window it never showed is still ignored, and a zoomed frame is trusted only while it is the active one.

## Before

A pick made while a reload swaps the preview frame, in a small harness that embeds the preview with `useElementPicker`. On main the pick is dropped:

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e14b90c-0320-4553-a27a-59c91a591519)

## After

With the fix the same pick lands:

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9b75b40-7668-43ad-868c-c4baf968c31a)

## What I measured

- `src/hooks/useElementPicker.test.ts`: 12 / 12. The swap test fails without the change (`expected undefined to be 'h1.next'`): a pick posted by the frame that was just swapped out. Only frames that were the primary preview are remembered: a zoomed override frame is accepted while it is active, and a test fails if it stays trusted after the zoom ends.
- `packages/studio` tsc clean; oxlint and oxfmt clean on both files; the studio suite under the `src/hooks` filter 1171 / 1171.
- In a host that embeds the preview, a scripted run that picks right after a reload: on the unpatched hook the pick was lost 6 times in about 35 runs; with this change, 0 in 40 (one run lost to an unrelated screenshot timeout).

## What I did NOT do

- The player still promotes without telling the picker; carrying the pick across the promotion would be a second fix in a different owner, not needed once the picker accepts the frame the pick came from.



## Size

Under 100 lines on purpose: one root fix home asked for as its own PR in this repo, carried alone into the 0.8.108 release; no other open PR here can hold it.

title: fix(studio): playhead keyframe edits keep their ease, undo names its edit and never waits on videos
body:
## What

Edits on GSAP-animated layers now write their value at the playhead into the tween the file already has. Several undo, history, host and connection fixes ride along. The edit accuracy bank comes last.

## Behaviour change

Studio's own API requests now carry no cookies, so they no longer queue behind the preview's paused videos. A host whose mounted Studio API authenticates with same-origin cookies sets VITE_STUDIO_API_SAME_ORIGIN_CREDENTIALS=true.

This applies when Studio is served from a loopback host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`). Served from any other host, Studio's requests keep same-origin credentials as before.

An edit inside a tween keeps every other tween's time. Extending a tween changes its span, so tweens placed relative to it move with it: after an edit past its end, a following call with no position, `>`, `+=` or a chained `.to()`; after an edit before its start (which writes its own position as a number), a following `<` call. These shifts are smaller than main's, which moved the edited tween to the end of the script.

### Item 1: one writer for an edit at the playhead

A move, nudge, resize (size or scale) or rotate on a property a GSAP tween animates now follows one rule: on a keyframe, change it; between two keyframes, add one at the playhead; outside the tween, extend it to the playhead and keep its authored ends. Other keyframes keep their values and times. Values come from the file's tween, or from GSAP's own parse of it where the tween leaves an end implicit (a `from()` end, a `to()` start, a CSS `translate` GSAP folds into `x`), never from the dragged element. GSAP parses a `to()` tween only once the playhead has passed its start, and every soft reload resets that; such a tween's timeline is played from the tween's start through its end and back, with the tween's channels cleared, before it is read. Starting at the tween's start lets an earlier tween on the same layer set its start value, as playback does. The gesture's live value is never read as its start, and afterwards the timeline's time and every layer's live value are put back. The edit is refused with "Edit this animation in the Code tab" only if that parse still leaves the end unknown.

Replaced writers: the size keyframe tween a resize used to add beside the existing one, the convert-then-add-keyframe and outside-range rewrites in the move, resize and rotate paths.

Root fixes on the way:
- An edit at the playhead rewrites its tween where it stands: the call keeps its place in the script and its position argument. The server used to remove the tween and append a new one at the end of the script, so any later tween placed relative to the sequence (no position, a chained `.to()`, `<`, `>`, `+=`, a label) moved.
- Studio's write-side parse now reads `addLabel`, so a tween placed at a label gets its real start there too. It read 0, which also misplaced the hold set kept before a first position keyframe.
- A rotate on a tween that turns another axis (`rotationY`, `rotationX`) holds the new angle across the whole tween, instead of turning from 0 at the tween's start. The writer now refuses a value that no keyframe carries and nothing holds, so no caller can leave a channel un-held.
- A group drag or nudge plans every member before the first write, so one member's refusal moves none.
- A move could write `x`/`y` into a tween that only animates size: the position finder fell back to any tween. It now returns only tweens that write position.
- Where two tweens meet at the playhead, the edit goes to the one whose keyframe the file states there (the later one if both do), not the one listed first.
- A drag no longer merges two real position tweens that run one after another; only holds can conflict.
- A rotate edits the rotation tween at the playhead, not the first one in the file.
- A tween shared by several elements is refused instead of moving all of them.
- A flat edit matches only a tween that carries its own channels; a keyframed tween at the same element and start no longer passes its ease or duration to it.
- A tween given a position when its call has none gets it after its last argument, so a call written with a trailing comma stays valid.
- A tween with a `delay` is matched at its real start, and the edit is written so GSAP shows the new value at the playhead, not `delay` later.
- A tween with no authored ease keeps GSAP's default ease, `power1.out`, by name. GSAP holds a resolved ease as a function, which used to read as unknown and refuse the edit. A built-in ease is named the same way; a custom ease function is still refused.
- A tween with `repeat`, `yoyo`, `repeatDelay`, `snap`, `overwrite` or `immediateRender` is edited as on main: the keyframes are written and those settings are kept.
- Every keyframe tween Studio re-writes carries the source's ease as `easeEach`. A tween-level `ease` does not ease percentage keyframes, so a linear tween re-written that way eased each segment `power1.inOut` and drifted off its path mid-segment. This covers the extend-to-playhead path, and the auto-keyframe-off whole-path and whole-property shifts when the tween authors its ease.
- An array of keyframe steps keeps GSAP's exact step times (the parse rounds them to 0.1%).
- **Behaviour change for review:** `resolveGroupTween` no longer splits a tween that mixes several property groups into one tween per group. It returns the mixed tween and the edit goes into it in place (the writer leaves its other channels alone). Why: inside one gesture the writes are buffered, so the split's re-read saw the pre-split file, and later writes targeted ids the split had already removed and were appended beside the old tweens as duplicates. A resize whose tween also animates position now writes the size and the anchor move in that one write.

### Item 2: undo pressed while an edit saves undoes that edit

Built on the pending-edit registry: an undo pressed while an edit is still saving waits for that edit and undoes it, not an edit started after the key.

- An undo of a move whose save failed stays undone and does not step back an older edit.
- The host API `revertNewestStudioPendingEdit` keeps returning the function that shows the edit again.
- A style set by its JavaScript name (`backgroundColor`, `WebkitX`) saves under its CSS name.
- A second undo pressed while the same edit saves steps back to the edit before it, instead of reading "Can't undo".

### Item 3: an edit stays saved when the history reply after it cannot be read

A history reply that is a 200 but not JSON used to reject inside the history refresh. The edit is on disk and in history either way; the refresh now logs "The history's reply was unreadable." and keeps the last history it read.

### Item 4: style fields for hosts

`ColorField` and `GradientField` are exported, and a session style commit takes a map of properties.

### Item 5: a host can move layers by exact film px

`handleDomGroupMoveBy(moves)` moves each selection by its delta in composition px, as one undo step, through the group drag's own path (for align and distribute in a host app). A member that cannot move refuses the call before anything is written. A group move or drag whose animated layers live in different files is refused too, since the group's save writes one file. Which file a layer writes to is decided by the same rule the save uses, so a layer that names the open file and one that leaves it implied count as one file. Each member is planned at its real drop before the first write.

### Item 6: an outside change during a drag waits for the drop

### Item 7: connections

- One live-updates subscription per mount: an edit no longer reopens the events stream, and a thumbnail request that is cancelled frees its slot at once, rather than when its load settles.
- `studioApiFetch` owns Studio's API requests (every call in the package moves to it, including the freeze-frame, loudness and peak-map requests that landed on main since), with a lint rule against a bare `fetch`. Requests carry no cookies, so Chrome pools them apart from the preview's media; paused videos could hold all six sockets a host gets and leave an undo waiting. The two telemetry calls go through it too: they post to PostHog's own host with the API key in the body, and a cross-origin request carries no cookies under the default either, so omitting credentials changes nothing for them.
- An opt-out for hosts on same-origin cookies, documented in the studio-server docs.
- CI runs the paused-video undo check as its own step beside the inline-text caret check, with ffmpeg installed for its fixture; its result file is uploaded with the caret screenshots.

## Since the last review (707e3d68)

- An unplayed keyframe tween clears the channels of every keyframe before it is read, so a channel that first appears in a later keyframe keeps its authored start instead of the drag's live value (55187872).
- Reading a tween the playhead has not reached now puts back each element's whole state afterwards: every attribute (style, an SVG layer's `transform`, an `attr` tween's value) and GSAP's cache, including the depth origin. Targets that are not styled elements (the runtime's own `{}` duration filler, an XML-namespace element) are skipped; before, the filler made the read throw. The filter is one shared helper, `elementTargets`, in `utils/elementGsap.ts`.
- Merged main again; the only conflict was the timeline delete, which takes main's one-request delete and keeps `studioApiFetch`.

### Earlier rounds (358a94b0)

- Merged main. Main's #4916 moved the group drag into its own hook (`useGsapAwareGroupMove`) and added keyframe usage tracking. This PR's group changes (no refusal toast for host calls, planning each member at its real drop, the one-file rule) now live in that hook. An edit at the playhead reports a keyframe add only when it adds one, as main's replaced writers did.
- Review fixes: reading a tween the playhead has not reached takes its start from the earlier tween on the same layer, as playback does, and puts back every layer's live drag afterwards; the one-file rule compares the files the save actually writes; the motion-path drag reports its keyframe add again, and an inserted start hold counts as an add.
- The fixes for the review round on 358a94b0 (delay, default ease, looping tweens, trailing comma, second undo, flat/keyframed match, cross-file group, preflight offset) are listed in the sections above.

## Test plan

- Writer: 16 tests in `gsapValueAtPlayhead.test.ts`; the 10 that go through the move, resize and rotate entry points fail on the base code (from() edit, to() edit before its first keyframe with a folded translate, refusal on an unparsed tween, parsed end beats the dragged value, array steps, no `x`/`y` into a size tween, two tweens meeting at the playhead, rotation at a boundary, size and scale resize).
- `easeEach`: four tests fail on the base code (whole-property shift of a linear flat tween and of a keyframed tween, auto-keyframe-off drag, extend-to-playhead).
- Item 3: the new history test fails on the base code.
- Duplicate tweens: a resize with buffered writes on a tween mixing `x` and `width` makes one write on the file's own id.
- Paused videos: 8 paused videos, undo socket wait limit 250 ms: before 7/7 runs fail (waits up to 10.5 s), after 8/8 pass (0 ms).
- Lint and typecheck pass on this head; the unit suites run in CI.
- In-place rewrite: 9 route tests (no position, `<` with `+=`, `>`, a label, a `from()` call, a chained `.to().to()`, and the edited tween's own `<`, label and number position). Each compares every other call's source text and resolved start before and after. All 9 fail on the base route code.
- Rotation hold: fails with either half of the fix reverted.
- Group plan: a 3-member group whose second member refuses writes nothing.
- Review fixes, each failing on the code before its fix: a `to()` tween the playhead has not reached, in real GSAP with a dragged value set (reads its authored start, keeps the live value and the playhead); a flat edit next to a keyframed tween at the same start; a trailing-comma call given a position (the old output does not parse); two undo presses started together during one save (they undo both edits: each press picks its edit at the press, and in turn skips it if another press already undid it; a failed undo changes nothing, so the next press targets that edit again; and a press whose edit was already undone, with a newer edit made since the press, says "Can't undo" as main does instead of undoing that newer edit). The abort slot release and the shared-tween refusal each fail when their line is removed.
- Second review round, real GSAP playing the written file: a delayed tween with no ease and one with `ease: "none"` show the dragged value at the playhead (the old code refused, then showed 150 for 200); a tween with no ease writes `easeEach: "power1.out"`; `expo.in` is named and a custom function refused; a `repeat: 1, yoyo: true` tween is written and keeps both. A group with members in two files writes nothing, and the group preflight plans at the member's real drop. Each fails with its fix removed.
- Since 707e3d68, real GSAP: a channel first appearing in a later keyframe saves its authored start (the written file replays 77 at the edit, 0 at the tween's start, 300 at its end; the first-keyframe-only read fails two tests); a sibling's live `attr` value survives a read beside the runtime's `{}` filler (fails on 13d7b8d1 with a TypeError, and with a style-only restore as 50 for 77); the shared target filter drops a plain object and an XML-namespace element. The undo and GSAP test files pass three runs in a row (413 tests).
- Earlier round, real GSAP: reading a tween the playhead has not reached leaves a sibling's live value and the timeline's time as they were (an earlier version moved the sibling from 77 to 50), and a later tween on the same layer reads its start from the earlier one (25, not 0) and plays the same afterwards. The motion-path drag and an inserted start hold each report a keyframe add. A group whose members name the open file or leave it implied is written (comparing raw names refused it). Main's keyframe usage tests pass against the new writer.

## Known follow-ups

- Editing a from()/fromTo() entrance at the playhead rewrites it as a keyframed to(), so the layer shows its end state before the entrance starts (pre-existing on main).
- An undo pressed while two edits are saving should target the painted-back edit's own claim id; it takes the newest claim after the key, as on main.
- The first undo after the first edit on a media-heavy project can restore nothing, because the project's history opens lazily. A fix is ready for the next PR.
- A keyframes array with different channels per step is rewritten as percentage keyframes without holding each channel, so a channel that first appears in a later step animates from 0%. A step's `delay` is copied into a keyframe's properties. Older than this PR (add-keyframe's array conversion does the same).
- Two keyframed tweens on the same element and start can still take each other's step times: the match checks only that both are keyframed. Rare.
- A whole-path or whole-property shift on a tween with no authored ease writes no `easeEach`, so its segments ease `power1.inOut` rather than GSAP's default `power1.out`. No worse than main.
- Both GSAP parsers advance the sequence without a tween's `delay`, so a call with no position after a delayed tween is placed `delay` too early. Next PR.
- Reading a tween the playhead has not reached sets it up early, as main's drag did (`gsapDragPositionCommit.ts:197-198` on main: clear the dragged channels, seek to the tween's start). Pre-existing on main, not introduced here. Two cases still differ from plain playback, both as on main: a later tween with `overwrite: "auto"` takes its property from the earlier tween before playback reaches it, and a starting value set outside the timeline (a `gsap.set` in the script) is read as 0 because the tween's channels are cleared first. The fix is to read the start without setting the tween up, and to clear only a live gesture's channels. Next PR, each case with a test that fails on main first.
- An unplayed-tween read restores the attributes of styled elements only, so an `attr` value drafted by hand on an XML-namespace element (not something Studio writes) comes back at its timeline value. Fixed in the next head, which merges main again for the core seek fix.
- A plain object tweened in the timeline gets its timeline value back after an unplayed-tween read; a value assigned to it outside the timeline is not kept. Studio writes none.
- A tween whose earlier tween on the same layer has already ended: its start should be read after seeking to 0 and then to its start. And an edit to a `repeat: -1` loop stretches every loop. Both noted in review; next PR.
- Undo presses that overlap while saves are running still have two rare orderings, both refused rather than mis-applied: a press waiting on one edit's files and a plain step back on other files can run in either order, and the second gets "Can't undo" (main undoes both there); and a press held in a queue through more than 100 other undos can forget its edit was already undone and get "Can't undo". A change made outside the app while presses are queued can still be the one a step back undoes. The root fix is for the history server to pick the edit to undo, with each press carrying the point it was pressed at. Next PR after the reader fixes.
- Several tests are slow or time-sensitive under a loaded runner and should be fixed rather than rerun: two studio-server tests whose first case pays a cold module load near the 5 s limit, a fixed half-second wait between rounds in the paused-video undo walk, a clipboard test that failed once in a full run, and the timeline virtualization and property panel tests on a heavily loaded machine. Next PR.
- About 50 call sites repeat "a layer's file, else the open file, else index.html". The GSAP writers now share one helper; the rest should move to it.
- If a project's history exceeds its 2 GB budget, pruning could drop a media file copied in the background before it is recorded.

## Before

Main at b5e3ffa6, Studio on generated fixture projects, headless Chrome.

1. Editing a GSAP tween at the playhead: a box on a linear `x` tween (5 s to 10 s, `ease: "none"`) is Alt-dragged 200 px at 8 s, which shifts its whole path. The saved keyframes have no `easeEach`, so each segment eases `power1.inOut`. At 6.17 s the box is 174 px behind where the linear path puts it (dashed outline). The dots, sampled every 0.25 s, bunch up at the ends.

![Before: GSAP path after an Alt-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b25fc8ef-28b7-443f-ae8f-8e2ed1ab9dfb)

2. Undo while an older edit is still saving: every file save is held 5 s in the browser (the same on both sides) so the steps happen at human speed. Move A, press Ctrl+Z once A's save is on the wire, then move B. The undo steps back B, the newer edit, and the screen puts A back at its start while the file keeps A's move (`translate: 300px 0px`).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08658d4a-e702-40dd-9d5f-696befb17441

3. Undo with 8 paused videos in the preview: the undo request waited 3067 ms for a connection before it was sent, and the next edit did not save within 30 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/23c2938f-e500-4a3e-a5f2-c93026480395

## After

This PR at cf082c4f, with the same fixtures and steps.

1. The same Alt-drag saves `easeEach: "none"`. At 6.17 s the box sits on the linear path (0 px off) and the dots are evenly spaced.

title: fix(studio): timeline lanes hold still while a clip drags onto a new track
body:
## What changes

Dragging a clip above the first lane to make a new track no longer makes the lanes jump. The NEW TRACK row stays in view and the clip follows the pointer onto it.

## Why it broke

`getTimelineScrollTopForGeometryChange` keeps the top visible row pinned when rows change, so a row that expands above you does not push your view. A clip drag inserts a temporary NEW TRACK row above the first lane, and the pin treated that like any other change:

- **At the top of the list** (scrollTop 0, with no top track padding, i.e. `trackPadding={{ top: 0 }}`): it scrolled down one row to keep the first lane on top. That hid the NEW TRACK row and the dragged clip, and the lanes bounced as the drag moved (traced scrollTop 0, 48, 49, 35, 63, 0 within half a second).
- **Scrolled down**: each row change during the drag pushed scrollTop back against edge auto-scroll, which also moves scrollTop during a drag.

## Fix

In `getTimelineScrollTopForGeometryChange`:

- While a clip drag is live, the pin leaves scrollTop alone, because edge auto-scroll owns it.
- At the top of the list, a row added above stays in view.

Expanding rows while scrolled and not dragging keeps the existing anchor behavior and its test.

## Tests

Two new unit tests in `Timeline.test.ts`. Both fail on main and pass here:

- At the top, a row added above keeps scrollTop 0 (main returns 48).
- During a drag, scrollTop is left to auto-scroll (main returns 110, expected 62).

The timeline, virtualization, scroll and drag test files pass: 236 tests.

## Before

A ten-lane fixture in a timeline short enough to scroll, rendered with `trackPadding={{ top: 0 }}`. The picture clip at the end of the first lane is dragged above it. The lanes bounce, and the NEW TRACK row and the clip slide out of view.

![Before: frames from the drag, lanes bounce](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/afdd8576-78e7-455c-8bdd-e554fa17ef5b)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cab6dd36-c15b-4064-84fc-03dad5f5b018

## After

Same fixture and drag. The lanes hold still, and the NEW TRACK row appears at the top with the clip on it.

![After: frames from the drag, lanes hold still](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57bb55b6-481b-4d57-afc0-19ef1e86e92d)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7feb7497-8386-40c1-aa11-a740785b1e62

title: feat(studio): a host undo key paints a still-saving move back at once
body:
## What changes for the user

In a host app that runs its own undo key (HyperFrames Desktop), Cmd+Z right after a move or nudge now puts the element back at once, as Studio's own undo has since #4877. Before, the host's undo could only wait for the save and the server step, so the element stayed moved for about a second or more.

## Why

#4877 gave a still-saving move a live revert and called it from Studio's own undo (`useEditHistoryActions`). A host with its own history (Desktop's undo goes through its main process) imports only `flushStudioPendingEdits` from the package, so it could not reach the revert.

## How

One export: `revertNewestStudioPendingEdit` from `@hyperframes/studio`, beside `flushStudioPendingEdits`. A host calls it in the key's own task and calls the returned put-back if its step does not land, as `useEditHistoryActions` does.

## Test

`studioPendingEdits.test.ts` gains a case that imports the revert through the package's public index: a still-saving move is painted back by the export, a second call paints nothing, and the put-back restores it. Without the export it fails with `revertNewestStudioPendingEdit is not a function`; with it, it passes.

## No visible change

Studio itself looks and behaves the same: this only exports an existing function. The Desktop before/after ships with the Desktop PR that calls it.

## Size

Under 100 lines on purpose: it is the one export Desktop needs from Studio 0.8.110, and no other open PR in this lane can carry it.
