title: perf(studio): manual edits stay under 8 ms per frame
body:
## What

Manual edits in Studio stay under 8 ms of main-thread work per frame in the cases where they did not: a drag right after an undo, right after nudges, and in-place text editing. The edit-accuracy bench also gets two measurement fixes and one realism change, each in its own commit so their effects stay separable.

## Why

Of the 48 bench cases that missed the smoothness bar in `baseline.json`, a 5x run on quiet runners (one case per runner, blank control page at 0 dropped frames) showed 34 passing every time on unchanged main: their banked miss was one sample taken with two cases sharing a runner. The real misses were the undo sequences (work p95 8 to 13 ms), the text cases (11 to 18 ms) and, intermittently, the nudge sequences.

The cause, traced with React's profiling build: after an undo, a save or opening a text edit, about a dozen separate state updates land on `StudioApp` over a few hundred ms (toast, tween cache, preview version, composition size, selection sync, history, thumbnails...). Each one re-rendered the whole Studio tree for 3 to 8 ms, because the root's children were not memoized and the hook results handed to them were rebuilt every render, so every handler had a new identity.

## How

- `useStableHandlers` (new): returns the same object while a hook result's data fields are unchanged, and keeps each function field at one identity that calls the latest function. Hooks return their results through it (`useTimelineEditing`, `useAppHotkeys`, `usePanelLayout`, `useGestureCommit`, `useTimelineAddAtPlayhead`, `useStudioSdkSessions`); `App.tsx` wraps the others.
- `StudioHeader`, `EditorShell`, `StudioOverlays`, `StudioLeftPanels`, `StudioRightPanels` and `TimelineToolbar` are memoized; the side panels come from `useStudioSidePanels`, the toolbar gets only the session fields it reads, and the shell context gets the four history fields it declares (an empty `undoPaths` array was new on every render).
- The frame-capture link was rebuilt with `v=Date.now()` on every render; it now takes a new stamp when the link is focused or pressed, so it is still fresh when used.
- `PropertyPanel` gets stable handlers from `StudioRightPanels`.
- The gesture-trail overlay moved to `useGestureTrailOverlay`, keeping `App.tsx` under 600 lines.
- Toasts draw on an opaque surface without `backdrop-blur-md`. A drag right after an undo dropped frames because the blur redrew what was behind the "Undid ..." toast on every frame of its 160 ms enter animation. Without the blur, the 95% surface let the timeline hint behind it show through, so the surface is now fully opaque. The feedback card shares this surface.

Bench (`packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy`):
- **Realism change, not a Studio speed-up:** the text step types one key per frame, as the nudge steps already press theirs. Typing a whole word plus Enter inside one frame is faster than any person and measured the bench.
- **Fix:** a case's work was "unknown" (an automatic smoothness fail) whenever any task in the trace lacked thread time: one cut by the trace's start or end, or a 1 µs `ThreadControllerImpl::RunTask` some runners emit inside the frames. Such a task now counts its wall time, an upper bound on its CPU time, so the rule can only get stricter; results carry `wallTimed` (how many tasks in the frames were counted that way), and `unknown` names the one remaining cause, a trace without the end mark.
- `studio-drag-frames.yml` takes `filter` and `grid` inputs and runs its five repeats as parallel jobs.

## Results

Quiet runners, the 48 cases, 5 runs each:

| | pass 5/5 | never pass |
|---|---|---|
| main | 34 | 8 |
| this PR (before the unknown-work fix) | 17 (44 of 240 runs had unknown work) | 2 |
| this PR (with it) | 38 | 0 |

Text cases, work p95 and frames over 8 ms per run (production builds, same machine, two runs per arm), to separate the Studio change from the bench change:

| | main | Studio change only | typing change only | both |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| work p95 | 8.5-15.1 ms | 7.6-10.7 ms | 8.3-9.5 ms | 5.1-6.2 ms |
| frames over 8 ms | 2-5 | 0-1 | 1-3 | 0 |

Still open: text select reaches 8.1-9.2 ms on the slowest runners, and two cases had one dropped frame in one of five runs.

## Review

Independent adversarial review at 81087421: no blocking or major findings. Minor, left as is:
- A trace task without `dur` would make that case's work NaN; the case fails rather than passing, and none has been seen in a real trace.
- Counting an untimed task at its wall time can only make a case stricter; `wallTimed` in results.json shows when it happened.
- `useStableHandlers`: a wrapper captured before its function field became `undefined` would throw if called; no caller switches a field that way.
- `usePersistentEditHistory` builds a new empty `undoPaths` array each render; the shell context no longer depends on it.
- Opening an already-focused capture link from the keyboard context menu reuses the last stamp (the `t` part predates this PR).

## Before

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b34cf993-e1d9-4df4-b239-e5ea8a8a3f8a)

## After

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dfa0d20-2491-45e8-9fc9-30ee92859586)

### Undo toast

On quiet runners, a drag right after an undo (`sequndo-none-center-r0-nested-z100`, 10 runs per arm, control page 0 dropped frames): with the blur, 14 dropped frames and 9 of 10 runs failing; without it, 1 dropped frame. The same toast before (blurred, 95% surface) and after (opaque, no blur), light and dark, zoomed 3x:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Light | ![Before, light: blurred toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06f49572-15a7-4cba-a344-54843bbb38c0) | ![After, light: opaque toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1663138-fa2a-4981-bb02-0dd79da92d8d) |
| Dark | ![Before, dark: blurred toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01c56cfe-28dc-4df5-9e8e-3ef26beac0f9) | ![After, dark: opaque toast](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fcf0d539-0f1c-4a23-ab37-c7c7520ea66c) |

## Related work

Refs the edit-accuracy bench smoothness rule.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `useStableHandlers.test.tsx` (2), `smoothness.test.mjs` (2); each fails when its fix is reverted
- [x] Existing tests for every changed file pass (20 files)
- [x] Quiet-runner 5x runs on main and on each head
- [ ] Full edit-accuracy gate shows no accuracy regression
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: Docker render image: colours shift (pinks look paler) because Debian's ffmpeg 5.1 encodes with the BT.601 formula but tags BT.709
body:
Rendering the same project with hyperframes 0.8.78 on macOS (ffmpeg 8.0.1) and in the official render Dockerfile (`node:22-bookworm-slim`, Debian ffmpeg 5.1.9) gives different colours. Strong colours shift: a pink pixel of RGB 228,41,130 on the Mac comes out as 240,65,131 in Docker. Encoding with the BT.601 formula and decoding with BT.709 predicts 243,64,131 for that pixel. Both outputs are tagged BT.709.

Switching the image to a current static ffmpeg (8.1) makes the Docker render match the Mac to within 1–2 levels. Setting `out_color_matrix=bt709` explicitly in the encode filters would probably fix it too. That second fix is untested.

Also, in the same image the background self-updater rewrote the global package mid-render, and we had to set `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` and `HYPERFRAMES_NO_AUTO_INSTALL=1`.

title: chore(renovate): stop raising engines and peer dependency floors
body:
## What

Renovate keeps the published `engines.node` and `peerDependencies` ranges as wide as they already are, instead of
raising their floor to whatever version was released that week.

## Why

`rangeStrategy: "bump"` applies to every range, including ones we publish to users:

- #4245 moved `engines.node` from `>=22` to `>=22.23.3` in five published packages. Nothing needs 22.23.x, the CLI's
  own runtime check accepts any Node 22, and the README says Node 22+. Yarn v1 and `engine-strict=true` installs fail on
  an older Node 22.
- #3935 moved the optional `aws-cdk-lib` peer range from `^2.130.0` to `^2.272.0` (two days old). Users on
  2.130 to 2.271 get an npm `ERESOLVE` on install, while the repo itself still tests against 2.254.0.

`widen` leaves a range alone when the new version already satisfies it (an open range like `>=22` never changes),
and widens a caret range like `^2.130.0` only for a new major, which the major-approval rule still gates.
Docker image tags, dependencies and devDependencies keep `bump`.

## How it was checked

`renovate-config-validator` (renovate 42.99.0) on the repo config: "Config validated successfully". The same run
with a misspelled option (`rangeStrategyy`) fails with "Invalid configuration option", so the check reads this file.

## Size

4 lines is the whole change: one package rule in the Renovate config, and nothing else needs to move with it. It stays
separate from the dependency bumps because it governs every future Renovate PR, while each bump PR is one update.
The behaviour shows on the next scheduled Renovate run.

title: fix(cli): stop browser --force from deleting chrome under running renders
body:
## What

`hyperframes browser ensure --force`, and the corrupt-archive retry, no longer delete the whole managed Chrome cache. A fresh chrome-headless-shell is downloaded into a private staging folder next to the cache and then swapped in by rename, replacing only its own version folder.

## Why

Both paths ran `rm -rf ~/.cache/hyperframes/chrome` (the forced path through `clearBrowser()`). The install lock only serializes installers, so any render or benchmark already using that binary lost chrome-headless-shell partway through its run.

Repro on main: start a long render, then run `hyperframes browser ensure --force` in another shell. The render's browser binary disappears while the download runs.

## Related work

None. `browser clear` keeps deleting the whole cache on purpose: you only run it by hand.

## How

- `downloadBrowser` installs with `cacheDir` set to `~/.cache/hyperframes/.chrome-staging-<uuid>`. That folder sits on the same filesystem as the cache, so the rename is atomic.
- `moveStagedInstallIntoCache` moves the existing version folder aside, renames the staged one into place, then deletes the old copy. If the second rename fails, the old folder is moved back. On POSIX, a process already running the old binary keeps its inode.
- The corrupt-archive retry now clears only the staging folder.
- `purgeStaleInstall` is gone. Each install starts from a fresh staging folder, so @puppeteer/browsers never sees a half-extracted target folder. A stale partial extract in the cache gets replaced by the same rename.
- An install killed by Ctrl-C or SIGTERM skips its `finally`, so its staging folder (and, if it died between the two renames, the set-aside copy) would stay behind. The next install sweeps every `.chrome-staging-*` and `.chrome-replaced-*` folder while it holds the install lock, so none of them can belong to a live installer. `browser clear` sweeps them too.
- A failed swap now gets the same `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` hint as a failed download.
- `--force` keeps skipping the cache and system-Chrome shortcuts. It no longer purges other cached versions.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: new `keeps a live reader's binary valid while a concurrent --force re-downloads it` runs against the real filesystem. Partway through the second `--force` install it reads the first install's binary path, then checks that the path holds the new build afterwards and that another version's folder survived. The fs mock gained `renameSync`, and the install mock now stages under the `cacheDir` it is given.
- [x] `restores the previous version when the staged install cannot be moved in` pins the rollback and the hint; `sweeps dirs leaked by a killed install on the next install and on clear` pins both sweeps. Each goes red when its line is removed (rollback restore, sweep in the installer, sweep in `clearBrowser`, swap error outside the hint wrapper): 1 failed, 51 passed each time. 52 passed with everything in place.
- [x] Red without the fix: with `manager.ts` reverted to main, the new test fails with `ENOENT ... chrome-headless-shell` mid-install (2 failed, 48 passed). With the fix: 50 passed, exit 0.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: fix(ci): skill docs may name the project files a workflow writes
body:
## Summary

The comment-citation gate reads markdown, so it grades skill docs. Skill workflow docs name files that the workflow writes into the user's project at run time (`frame.md`, `STORYBOARD.md`, `SCRIPT.md`, `_role.md`). Those files never exist in this repo, so every touched line naming one failed as "no such file in the repo".

This adds them as one named list in `check-comment-citations.mjs`. The exemption matches the bare name only: a repo path that merely ends in one of these names is still resolved and still fails when missing.

## Why

#3951 fixes 35 broken skill-doc links. Its "Comments" check fails on 13 lines it rewrote, all bare `frame.md`, `STORYBOARD.md` or `_role.md`. Any skill-doc PR touching such a line hits the same false failure.

## Test plan

- New case: a bare project-file name in a skill doc passes.
- New case: `skills/demo/frame.md`, a repo path ending in a project-file name, still fails with "no such file".
- Mutation: removing the `PROJECT_FILES` check fails the first case; matching on the basename instead of the bare name fails the second.
- The gate probe (`scripts/gate-probes/broken-citation.md`) is unchanged and still reports both of its dead citations.

## Size

20 changed lines: one named list, one check, two tests. The whole fix is the exemption; nothing else in the gate changes.

title: feat(studio): export timeline row order and fade handle boxes, readable fx badge
body:
## What

Two pure functions a host that draws its own timeline can import from `@hyperframes/studio`, and one readability fix:

- `displayTrackOrder(elements, collapsedGroupIds)`: the track number of each timeline row, top to bottom, as the timeline draws them. An audio group gets its anchor row with its members under it; a collapsed group's members are left out.
- `fadeHandleBoxes({ widthPx, inPx, outPx, clipBox, drawn })`: where the fade-in and fade-out handles sit on a clip (left, top, width, height, tab position). Each is centred on its fade's end and kept inside the clip; two that would overlap split at the midpoint between their tabs.
- The timeline's inactive `fx` badge text goes from `text-white/35` to `text-white/60`. Border and weight are unchanged.

## Why

- A host that draws over Studio's timeline has to know which row is which, and where the fade handles are, to stay off them. Today it can only copy Studio's math, and the copies already disagree with Studio: one ignores collapsed groups, the other misses the overlap split.
- The inactive `fx` badge measured 3.07:1 on a clip's label band and 3.13:1 on an audio clip, under the 4.5:1 text minimum.

## Related work

None.

## How

- The timeline hook's row derivation is now one pure function. `useTimelineTrackDerivations` and `displayTrackOrder` both call it, so there is one owner of the drawn row order.
- The fade handle geometry moved out of `TimelineClipFades.tsx` into `timelineClipFadeGeometry.ts` unchanged. The component calls `fadeHandleBoxes` for every handle it draws.
- The z-order mirror had a private function also named `displayTrackOrder` that returned plain sorted lanes, a copy of `timelineTrackOrder`. It is deleted and the mirror calls `timelineTrackOrder`, with no behaviour change: the mirror computes its insert row and its lane list from that same sorted list. `timelineTrackOrder`'s comment no longer claims to be the drawn row order.
- Badge contrast was measured in Studio, not estimated. For each inactive badge, the badge is hidden, the pixels under its letters are read, and the badge's real colours are composited over the worst one. The waveform starts 16 px below a clip's top (`labelInset`), so no waveform bar sits under the letters.

| Inactive `fx` badge | Before (`white/35`) | After (`white/60`) |
|---|---|---|
| On a clip's label band | 3.07:1 | 7.33:1 |
| On an audio clip, at rest | 3.13:1 | 6.39:1 |

Those two are measured. The worst state, an active audio clip under hover, works out to 5.36:1 after (about 2.6:1 before), computed from the same colours rather than read from pixels.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `displayTrackOrder` matches the hook's row order, expanded and collapsed; `fadeHandleBoxes` centres handles, gives their height, and splits overlapping ones at the midpoint.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the captures below, from Studio and a host page on a repo-style fixture.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Each new test goes red when its code is broken: ignoring collapsed groups fails the row-order test, and turning off the overlap split fails the midpoint test.

## Size

279 changed lines (193 added, 86 removed) across 10 files in `packages/studio`, about 45 of them tests.

## Before

On main, a host page that imports only from `@hyperframes/studio` cannot reach either function. It renders Studio's own fade handles but has no boxes to compare them with, and no row order.

title: fix(cli): reject extra positional arguments on every command
body:
## Summary
Every CLI command now handles positional arguments beyond the ones it declares, instead of silently dropping them. Before, `hyperframes render ./proj out.mp4` ignored `out.mp4` and rendered to the default path, and `hyperframes lint a b` linted only `a`. Now those exit with a usage error that names the extra argument and the command's usage line:

```
Unexpected extra argument for hyperframes render: out.mp4
Usage: hyperframes render [DIR] [OPTIONS]
```

Under `--json` (read from the parsed flag, so `--json=true` and `--json=1` count, `--json=false` does not, and a `--json` after `--` is an argument, not the flag) the same message goes to stdout as `{"ok":false,"error":...}`, matching the add command's existing usage error. `add` keeps its own hint on a third line: "Run add once per item, or pass a single tag to install every item tagged with it."

The two free-text commands join their words into one value instead: `hyperframes catalog lower third` searches "lower third" (it searched only "lower"), and `hyperframes tts hello world` speaks "hello world" (it spoke only "hello"). For `tts`, when the first word names an existing `.txt` file (`tts script.txt extra`), the words are not joined: tts reads the file as before and the extra word is rejected with the usage line. Text words together with `--text-file` are a usage error ("Pass text to speak or --text-file, not both.") instead of the words being dropped. `catalog` always joins, even when a word matches a file or folder name.

Also: `lambda deploy` and `lambda destroy` now fail clearly when `HYPERFRAMES_REPO_ROOT` points somewhere that is not a hyperframes checkout. Before, the bad value was silently ignored and the error that followed told the user to set the variable they had already set.

Telemetry never sees the user's arguments: the error the CLI reports carries only the command path and a count (`2 unexpected extra arguments for hyperframes render`); the detailed message above goes only to the terminal. The repo-root error likewise does not echo the `HYPERFRAMES_REPO_ROOT` value.

## Root cause
citty binds each declared positional in order and leaves the rest in `args._`. The shared command wrapper only checked flags, so every command that does not read `args._` dropped the extras. #3891 fixed this for `add` alone; this moves the check into the shared wrapper (`wrapCommand`) and deletes add's own guard.

Commands that read `args._` on purpose are on an explicit list keyed by command path: `compare`, `figma asset`, `skills update`, `timeline set`. `catalog` and `tts` are on a second list whose last positional takes every remaining word. A test loads each listed command and fails if a path stops naming a real command. Command groups (`auth`, `cloud`, `figma`, `history`, `skills`, `timeline`) are skipped by structure: citty also runs a group's own handler after its subcommand, with the subcommand name in `args._`.

## Behaviour change
A command run with more positionals than it declares now fails with exit code 1 (usage error) where it used to continue and ignore them. `catalog` and `tts` accept multi-word input. An invalid `HYPERFRAMES_REPO_ROOT` is now an error for `lambda deploy` and `lambda destroy` (before, it was ignored and both fell back to finding the checkout themselves).

## Test plan
- `command-failure-tracking.test.ts`: one test per family through citty's real `runCommand`: plain leaf (text, `--json`, `--json=true`, `--json=1`), a leaf within its declared count, a nested subcommand named by its full path, an opted-out command, the two joining commands, `tts` with a `.txt` file plus a stray word, `catalog` whose first word names a folder, and a group whose own handler citty runs after the subcommand.
- `cli.commands.test.ts`: every path on both lists resolves to a real command and loader key.
- `add.test.ts`: `add a --dir <dir> b c` through the wrapper rejects before any registry call; a single-item add still succeeds.
- `events.test.ts`: a real extra-positional usage error sent through `trackCommandFailure` produces a `cli_error` payload with the count and no argument text.
- The real `figma asset` and `skills update` definitions accept several positionals only because they are on the opt-out list; the thrown error is marked as already presented; a required positional prints as `<NAME>`.
- `tts.test.ts`: words plus `--text-file` is rejected before anything is synthesized. `add.test.ts` checks add's hint. JSON mode: `--json=1` on a command with no declared json flag gives JSON; `-- --json` does not.
- `repoRoot.test.ts`: a valid `HYPERFRAMES_REPO_ROOT` is returned; an invalid one throws.
- Each test fails with its piece of the change removed. Full `packages/cli` suite green apart from a Chromium launch timeout on the test machine; typecheck and the comment ratchet clean.

title: fix(lint): flag digit-leading ids used by toArray and ScrollTrigger selectors
body:
## What

`id_requires_css_escape` now also treats a digit-leading id as used (and so an error) when it appears in `gsap.utils.toArray("#1-x")` or in a ScrollTrigger `trigger`, `endTrigger` or `pin` value, including the `scrollTrigger: "#1-x"` shorthand.

## Why

Since #3980 the rule errors only when a selector in the composition targets the id, and it reads selectors from CSS rules and from query and tween calls. `gsap.utils.toArray` and ScrollTrigger configs also run the string through `querySelectorAll`, so `#1-x` throws there too and aborts the rest of the script, but the rule rated those ids a warning.

## Related work

Refs #3980. Carries over the `toArray` and ScrollTrigger cases from #3713, which #3980 superseded.

## How

One change to the existing `SELECTOR_CALL_PATTERN`: `toArray(` joins the call list, and a second branch matches a `trigger` / `endTrigger` / `pin` / `scrollTrigger` / `scroller` / `pinnedContainer` / `pinSpacer` key followed by a string. Both feed the same selector check as before, so escaped selectors (`#\31 23-frame`) stay warnings. A non-selector key holding the same string stays a warning.

Not covered, by design of a one-regex rule: optional-call `toArray?.(...)`, bracket access `gsap.utils["toArray"]`, computed keys `{ ["trigger"]: ... }`, a destructured `toArray`, and selector arrays (already missed for `.to([...])`). A key match has no context, so an unrelated object with a `trigger:` string also counts; that only raises an already-flagged id from warning to error.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: 13 rows in the existing `rates a digit-leading id by selector use` table, ported from #3713 plus `pin`, `endTrigger`, `scroller`, `pinnedContainer`, `pinSpacer`, a quoted key, the shorthand, and negative rows for `label`, `data-pin`, `$pin` and `spin`.
- [x] `core.test.ts` 115/115 pass. Dropping any one key, the optional quote, or `$` or `\w` from the lookbehind fails exactly one row.
- [x] No file in `registry/`, `skills/` or `packages/` uses these forms with a digit-leading id, so no existing composition changes severity.
- [ ] Manual testing performed (lint-only change)
- [ ] Documentation updated (not needed: the rule's documented behaviour is unchanged)

## Size

Small on purpose: one regex branch and the test rows that pin it. It closes the gap #3980 left from #3713 without reviving #3713's parser rewrite.

title: fix(cli): close every browser on SIGTERM and SIGINT via one launch owner
body:
## What
A CLI killed with SIGTERM or SIGINT could leave its headless Chromium running, because each command launched its own browser and nothing owned shutdown. Chromium then kept inherited sockets open and held up whatever launched the CLI.

All six CLI launch sites now go through `launchManagedBrowser` (`packages/cli/src/browser/launch.ts`). It registers every browser it opens. One SIGTERM/SIGINT handler aborts pending launches, closes the browsers (1 s grace, then SIGKILL of that browser's own pid), waits for the processes to exit, then asks the root CLI to exit (143 / 130). Puppeteer's own signal handlers are turned off so there is a single owner. The engine's GPU probe launches its own short-lived Chrome before the first managed launch, so the four commands that run it call `resolveManagedGpuMode` (installs the owner first). The probe's own browser keeps Puppeteer's handlers, which close it.

Not covered by this owner on purpose: render (its own cancellation scope), studio preview (its own shutdown).

Size note: about 250 lines added, 45 changed; most of it is the real-Chromium test.

## Before / after
Before: SIGTERM to a CLI with a live browser did not exit with the signal's code (exit 1, the signal was swallowed by Puppeteer's handler). After: the CLI closes its browsers, no Chromium for that profile remains, and it asks to exit with the signal's code (143 / 130).

## What I measured
- New `launch.process.test.ts` on a Linux box with real Chromium: SIGTERM after ready, SIGINT after ready, SIGTERM during launch. A fourth case sends SIGTERM during the GPU probe. The three launch cases assert the requested exit code and that no process carrying the profile dir remains; the probe case asserts the exit code only. 4/4 pass.
- Mutation: removing the two `process.on` lines fails the tests (the probe case when `ownSignals` is dropped from the probe wrapper).
- Real `hyperframes render` with Chromium up, SIGTERM: no new Chromium left, so the engine is not changed.
- `check:cli-process-ownership`, oxlint, oxfmt, comment-check pass.

## What I did NOT exercise
- macOS and Windows (the test is Linux only: it reads /proc).
- The other five launch sites individually; they share the same function and are not run under a signal.
- A full `tsc` pass on the box (core generated files were missing there, errors unrelated to these files).

## Known follow-ups (next PR, after the CLI release)
- SIGHUP is still left to Puppeteer's handler.
- A cancelled run reports a `command_failure`; it should report the cancellation.
- The GPU probe browser is launched by the engine outside `launchManagedBrowser`, and the studio preview launch is still unmanaged.
- Test gaps: the probe case asserts the exit code only (not that the probe Chromium is gone or that it launched); the process test is Linux only; no hard deadline on a second signal; grace SIGKILLs only the main Chrome pid.

title: fix(core): render GSAP set steps on the frame they land on
body:
## What

GSAP films that step on their frame grid render correctly on the frame each step lands on, in exports, Studio's preview and timeline thumbnails.

A film that steps frame by frame (`tl.set` to hide every frame, then `tl.set` to show one, at the same time) lost that layer on every frame that landed exactly on a step. Measured on a test film rendered with the CLI at 30 fps with a step every 0.1 s:

| Frames after 1.8 s | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| On a step (every 3rd frame) | 0 of 32 show the layer | 32 of 32 |
| Between steps | 64 of 64 | 64 of 64 |

So the exported video blinked the layer out every third frame.

## Why

Both runtime seek paths re-rendered a seek by stepping to `t + 0.001` and back to `t` (`adapters/gsap.ts`, `init.ts`). Arriving backwards, GSAP renders a timeline's children last to first, so two zero-duration steps at the same time apply in reverse order: "hide all" lands after "show frame k". The same backward arrival also fired a `tl.call` placed on `t` again on every repeated seek.

## Related work

None.

## How

- One helper, `rerenderGsapTimelineAt`, re-renders after the seek, silently: from just below `t` when `t >= 0.001`, and from just above below that, where there is no room below. The adapter and the root-timeline seek in `init.ts` both call it. On the root path the one eventful move stays the first seek, so callbacks fire once per seek, as on main.
- At `t < 0.001` this is main's nudge, so frame 0 renders exactly as on main: a `tl.set(..., 0)` on a timeline that has not moved yet applies, and a value changed outside the timeline is restored by a second seek to 0. Steps placed exactly at 0 still resolve as on main.
- Wider than steps: two overlapping tweens on one property now export as they play back. `style-4-prod`'s caption box fades one line out while the next fades in; main exported the fading-out line on 5 frames (57, 98, 283, 356, 392). Box opacity at frame 356: playback 0.977, this change 0.903, main 0.326. Its golden is regenerated in the producer Docker image (`output.mp4` only); its frames now match this change's render.
- Not reached, unchanged from main:
  - films with any zero-duration callback keep the existing `init.ts` guard, which skips the re-render (without it a `tl.call` fires twice);
  - standalone registered timelines (`seekRuntimeTimeline`, a single `totalTime`);
  - silent seeks of the root timeline (`suppressEvents: true`, such as motion-blur samples).
- The GSAP adapter now seeks eventfully first and re-renders silently, where main nudged silently first. Its callbacks at early times differ from main (seeking twice to 0 fires a `tl.call` at 0 twice on main and not at all here; seeking to 0.5 fires `onStart` once here and never on main). Production reaches the adapter only for the silent seek when adapters are discovered (`init.ts` around 3316); every eventful seek skips it while a root timeline exists (around 3981 and 4383).
- Preview only: a backward scrub across two overlapping tweens on one property can land further from playback than on main (GSAP is history-dependent there either way). Export always moves forward.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `adapters/gsap.steps.test.ts` uses real GSAP: seeking onto a step from 0, 1 and 2.7 s shows the step's frame, and a `tl.call` on the step fires once over two seeks (all four fail on main); a set at 0 applies on an unmoved timeline, and a second seek to 0 restores a value changed outside the timeline (both fail with a from-below re-render at 0). The `init.test.ts` call-shape test and `scripts/test-hyperframe-runtime-seek.ts` now expect the re-render from below.
- [x] Every core test that touches `totalTime` passes: gsap.steps 4, gsap 9, audioClockSource 3, capturedMediaIdleRoute 10, domRealm 5, entry 31, init.swapScenes 139, init 208, mediaVolumeEnvelope 19, pausedTransportInvariant 5, player 46, transportPark 35.
- [x] `bun run test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` passes on the devbox (exit 0).
- [x] Manual testing performed: the CLI render of the test film above, before and after; in the producer Docker image, `overlay-montage-prod` passes against its unchanged golden (0 failed frames) and `style-4-prod` passes against its regenerated one.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Size

About 100 changed lines in `packages/core`, half of them tests, plus one regenerated golden video. It ships alone on purpose: every render of a film that steps on its frame grid is wrong today, and the related Studio timeline change waits behind it.

title: fix(cli): a background preview launch keeps only the server its own child started
body:
## Summary

Two `hyperframes preview --background` launches for the same project, started at the same time, could adopt each other's server. Each launch waits for a newly appeared server that was not in its pre-launch snapshot. A concurrent launch's server also qualifies. The first one to answer won, even when it belonged to the other launch.

Readiness now accepts only a server listening in this launch's own process tree: the launched wrapper itself, or a process that descends from it (`isProcessDescendant`, the check the stop path already uses to prove ownership). A server that cannot be proven ours is ignored, and the launch keeps waiting for its own.

The detached child is now always started with `--force-new`. The parent has already decided to launch (its reuse check ran first), so the child must create its own listener. Without it, a child that found a sibling launch's server would reuse it and exit, and the parent would wait for a server that never appears in its process tree.

## Why

With `--port`, the wrong pick is loud but wrong: launch A asking for 3002 adopts launch B's 3003, reaps its own wrapper because 3003 misses the requested port, then reports that its child "did not stop". Without `--port`, the wrong pick is silent: the session file records another launch's server as this project's managed preview, so a later `--stop` targets the wrong process tree.

## Test plan

- New case in `previewLifecycle.test.ts`: two launches at once. Launch A (wrapper 4321, asks for 3002) answers only after launch B's server (wrapper 5555, 3003) has appeared, and after A's pre-launch snapshot. Each launch must end with its own server.
- Against main's `previewLifecycle.ts` the new case fails: B adopts A's server (pid 9876 instead of 7777).
- The detached child's arguments always end in exactly one `--force-new`; removing it fails two tests.
- The existing launch tests now declare their fake server a child of the fake wrapper, as the real process table would.
- `previewLifecycle.test.ts` + `preview.test.ts`: 85 passed. `tsc --noEmit` (cli), oxlint and oxfmt: clean. Comment ratchet: at or under base.

## Size

About 75 changed lines: one readiness predicate, the child launch flag, and their tests. Together they are one invariant: a launch only ever records the server its own child created.

title: fix(studio-server): a rename rewrites only references that name the renamed path
body:
## What changes
Renaming a file or folder rewrote every occurrence of its old path as a plain substring in project text files. Renaming `assets` to `brand` also changed `assets-backup/b.png` to `brand-backup/b.png` and the words "the assets folder" in prose.

The old path counts as a reference only where it starts and ends at a non-name character, after any `./`, `../` or `/` lead (kept). A folder is matched by what is under it, never by prose. Because a filename can hold any character a delimiter can (`a.png&b.png`, `other assets/`), a match inside the longer path of a file or folder that exists in the project is left alone: the project's real paths settle what text cannot. One function owns it (`replaceReferences`), used by the rename route.

## Tests
`files.renameReferences.test.ts` (new): the pattern on every form a project writes a path, a longer name and prose left alone, and the PATCH route renaming a folder next to `assets-backup` and prose. `files.test.ts` and `files.pathSafety.test.ts` still pass (143 tests together on miga).

## Also read as the same path
A root-relative lead (`/assets/x`), JSON-escaped (`assets\/x`) and Windows (`assets\x`) separators are rewritten, and a file's path ends at a delimiter, so `a.png@2x.png` is not taken for `a.png`.

## Known limits
A bare folder name with no `/` after it (for example `"assets"` as a config value) is no longer rewritten when its folder is renamed; it was indistinguishable from prose.

References from a nested file written relative to that file (`../assets/x` in `scenes/css/style.css` when `scenes/assets` is renamed) are still not resolved: the rewrite has no per-file base, as before this change.

title: feat(studio): track completed preview editing gestures
body:
## What

Track completed preview editing gestures through `studio:feature_used`. Add missing successful keyframe actions through `studio:keyframe` and custom inspector inputs through `studio:design_input`. Replace user-authored route text in the shared Studio telemetry envelope with a route kind and stable equality ID.

## Why

Preview gestures and several keyframe write paths bypass existing usage events. A resolved save promise alone does not establish that source changed.

## Related work

No linked issue. Existing inspector, keyboard, clipboard, and history events retain their own event names.

## How

Carry the writer outcome through geometry commits. Collect grouped GSAP writes into one gesture outcome, then enqueue one usage event. Usage-specific properties are feature, surface and method. Keyframe events include an action and, for the existing single-property add path, a property name. Batch writers return an ordered change receipt for each mutation, so a changed update cannot credit a no-op add. Recording retains its original selection and animation set through the write facade.


Every `studio:*` event inherits `url_hash` as `project`, `home` or `other`. `url_route_id` is now a random eight-hex token generated with `crypto.getRandomValues`, reused through a route-to-ID map in sessionStorage. The map stays local; neither transport sends route names or selection queries. Independent tabs receive separate tokens. A tab opened from Studio can inherit its opener's sessionStorage tokens, preserving equality within the same session.


Saved insight compatibility was checked through the read-only paginated API. **Read 404s: hashchange (door 2) vs mid-session (door 3)** compares the loaded route against later events and will use `url_route_id` for equality. **Top diverging targets (triage)** currently displays `url_hash` as a sample and will display the route kind. Their query updates are planned after merge.

Paths below are relative to `packages/studio/src/`.

| Feature | Surface | Method | Commit point |
|---|---|---|---|
| `move` | preview | drag | `components/editor/useDomEditOverlayGestures.ts:357,494` |
| `resize` | preview | drag | `components/editor/useDomEditOverlayGestures.ts:541` |
| `rotate` | preview | drag | `components/editor/useDomEditOverlayGestures.ts:447` |
| `crop` | preview | drag, button | `components/editor/DomEditCropHandles.tsx:239` |
| `nudge` | preview | keyboard | `components/editor/useDomEditNudge.ts:177` |
| `multi_select` | preview | drag, button | `components/editor/marqueeCommit.ts:145`, `hooks/usePreviewInteraction.ts:173` |
| `z_order` | preview | button | `components/editor/useDomEditZOrder.ts:177` |
| `text_edit` | preview | field | `hooks/useDomEditTextCommits.ts:281` |
| `gesture_recording` | preview | button, keyboard | `hooks/useGestureCommit.ts:355` |
| `motion_path` | preview | drag, button | `components/editor/motionPathCommit.ts:23`, `components/editor/MotionPathOverlay.tsx` |
| `snapping` | preview | button, keyboard | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:40,57` |
| `grid` | preview | button, keyboard | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:45,62` |
| `grid_spacing` | preview | field | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:27` |
| `snap_to_grid` | preview | button | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:226` |
| `ruler` | preview | button | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:122` |
| `safe_margins` | preview | button | `components/editor/SnapToolbar.tsx:122` |

`studio:keyframe` actions: `add`, `convert`, `remove_all`, `reset`. Legacy single/batch writers count changed results; SDK operations compare committed source. Replacement operations that insert a stop carry explicit add metadata. Timeline delete-all counts one gesture across its animation writes.

Missing inspector controls covered: FX parameters, effect bypass, add/remove/reorder effects, apply/remove presets, preset amount, add/edit/remove EQ and automation, native carve controls, levelling enable/remove, and multi-selection group/hide buttons. These use `studio:design_input`, not `studio:feature_used`.

Source inventory found no separate preview align/distribute action or custom guide-drag writer.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] All touched-path tests completed
- [x] Independent review and simplification for the latest random-ID head
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] New comments explain behavior constraints

Remote Linux: the gesture implementation passed 624 tests across 34 files at `8dfe0571`, followed by exact-head affected-hook tests and real canvas/keyframe captures at later heads. Recording target, consumer attribution, producer receipt and nudge mutations each failed their witness test, then passed after restoration. The random-ID follow-up passed 47 telemetry, routing and client tests at `e8a63efb`. Restoring FNV deliberately failed both complete serialized-batch privacy tests and the independent-tab test; restoring random IDs passed all 12 telemetry tests. At `5995525d`, all 47 tests passed again, both typechecks, formatting of 83 touched paths, lint, Fallow audit and production builds passed. The deliberate FNV mutation failed the same three privacy tests, then all 12 telemetry tests passed after restoration. Fresh browser captures show one move and one add event with the same random route ID.

## Size

The patch spans gesture callers and their shared save-result plumbing. Group move was extracted to retain the production file-size limit. The random route-ID implementation adds no dependency. Storage decoding and tuple validation are separate from token creation, addressing the Fallow complexity finding without a suppression. Independent source review and all three simplification reviews found no blockers at `5995525d`. Final runtime proof passed. Review and simplification marks are recorded at this head. CI is in progress.

A keyframe add persists and emits exactly one `studio:keyframe` with `action=add`. Both actual request panels show `url_hash=project` and the same random eight-hex route ID. Requests are fulfilled locally, so validation does not send analytics. The complete serialized-batch regressions separately check the entire envelope for raw names, encoded names, selection queries and the old deterministic fixture fingerprint.

title: fix(studio): show each timeline row its own layer instead of a flat bar
body:
## What

Layer rows in the timeline now show their own layer instead of a flat bar. A text layer's row draws its own words as text, in its own weight and colour and its font as Studio has it; a visual layer's row shows a picture of that layer alone. Closes desktop's text-clip report (text clips such as Subtitle and Cta tiled their rendered text as repeated thumbnails). On a project where most layers span the whole film, every one of those rows used to be a plain pale bar.

## Why it happened

Three things stacked:

1. `useRenderClipContent` only gave a layer row a picture when it was shorter than 92% of the film and its id did not contain backdrop, background, overlay, scrim or mask. A full-length layer failed the first test and fell back to the flat bar.
2. Even with a picture, a full-length row's thumbnail captured the whole frame, so every such row showed the same image.
3. Layer rows found by id or class had no selector, so a thumbnail could not ask for one layer anyway (composition hosts still got one from `data-composition-id`). `timelineElementHelpers.ts` checked "is this an HTML element" with `instanceof` against the preview window. The preview's nodes carry the editor window's prototypes (documented in core `runtime/domRealm.ts`), so the check was false for those rows on every load I ran; core's notes say it happens on some loads. The same check also stopped video and audio rows from reading their source length.

## Fix

- A layer that is only text (a text tag whose children are all text leaves, the rule the canvas text editor already uses: `isTextBearingTag` / `isEditableTextLeaf` in `domEditingDom.ts`) gets its words and computed font family, weight and colour when the row is built (`readTimelineText`, called from `applyMediaMetadataFromElement`, which both row builders go through). A layer that paints a background image or gradient is not a text layer and keeps its picture. A text row renders its words on one clipped line (`TextClipContent`), with no capture, on the layer's own background colour when it has an opaque one, otherwise on a theme strip chosen for contrast (light behind dark text, dark behind light text). The timeline's change check compares text by value, and a canvas text edit, which skips the preview reload, re-reads the edited layer's row (`refreshTimelineRowText`). `isEditableTextLeaf` moves from `domEditingLayers.ts` to `domEditingDom.ts` beside `isTextBearingTag`, so the timeline can use it without an import cycle.
- The film-length rule and the id pattern are gone, so a full-length HTML layer gets a picture like any other. Media, audio and hidden-thumbnail rows are unchanged.
- The thumbnail capture fades out the row's siblings at each level above it, so the picture shows that layer alone. One helper (`getElementScreenshotClip` in studio-server) now serves both the Vite and the CLI capture paths; the copy inside `vite.browser.ts` is deleted. Each faded sibling gets an inline `opacity: 0 !important`; the page keeps its own list of what it faded and the exact previous inline opacity, so no marker is added to the markup and each sibling's inline opacity is put back exactly. The CLI, which reuses one loaded page for later captures, restores them after every screenshot (`clearElementScreenshotIsolation`); without that, the next capture on the page came back blank.
- The thumbnail cache version goes from v4 to v5, so rows that already had a selector stop serving their old whole-frame crop. The cache key now hashes the selector instead of replacing punctuation, so `#a\.b` and `#a_b` no longer share one cached picture, and long selectors are no longer cut at 80 characters.
- Core exports its existing realm-independent element checks as `@hyperframes/core/runtime/dom-realm`, and the timeline helpers use them.

## Tests

- `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`: a full-length row with an id gets a picture.
- `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`: a row with text renders `TextClipContent`. Fails without the branch.
- `timelineElementHelpers.test.ts`: `readTimelineText` reads an `h1` with a `span` as one line with its font, weight and colour, and returns nothing for a container holding a non-text child, an empty div, or a non-text tag. The container case fails without the text-only rule.
- `screenshotClip.test.ts`: every sibling on the element's ancestor path is faded out, and the element, its subtree and its ancestors are left alone. A sibling with its own `opacity: 1 !important` is still hidden and gets that exact value back on clear, as does one whose opacity is `var(--alpha, 0|1)`. After a clear, isolating a different element hides only its own siblings.
- `thumbnail.test.ts`: `#a\.b` and `#a_b` are captured separately; the old key served the second from the first's cache.
- `studioServer.test.ts`: a selector capture clears its isolation after the screenshot. It fails without the clear. The describe block now shuts its server down after each test, because the thumbnail browser lease is module-wide and leaked one test's fake browser into the next.
- `timelineElementHelpers.test.ts`: a row whose node comes from another realm keeps its `#id` selector, and a foreign `<video>` still yields its source length. Both fail on the old check.

## Cost

Measured cold, on a 60 s fixture film with 24 rows, scrolling the whole timeline:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Rows with a picture | 12 of 24 | 24 of 24 |
| Captures | 14 | 26 |
| Median capture | 10.8 s | 11.0 s |
| Last thumbnail lands | 134 s | 201 s |

About one capture per row, so the first open of a long film takes longer to fill in. A second open hits the thumbnail cache. (That run predates text rows; those cards are now drawn as text and need no capture.)

Rows on screen first, cold, no scrolling, six rows in view, two runs each:

| | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| The 24-row film (labelled flat-colour cards) | 3 of 6 visible rows get a picture; the last lands at 34 to 36 s | All 6 visible rows draw at once as text; nothing to wait for |
| The same film with gradient cards (every row captured) | 3 of 6 visible rows get a picture; the last lands at 33 to 47 s | All 6 get a picture; the last lands at 56 s |

On the gradient film every capture this PR makes goes to a visible row (6 rows plus the composition card), where main spends 3 of its 6 on rows off screen. The last of the six lands later only because Studio's capture path renders one page at a time, about 5.5 s each; batching captures is the follow-up.

The CLI path was checked separately on the built CLI (`hyperframes preview` from source always serves through Vite): Title, then Waves, then the whole frame requested at once on one page. Before the clear, Waves and the whole frame came back blank; with it, all three are right.

## Limitation

Text rows show the words present when the timeline is built or the text is edited in Studio; words a script swaps in during playback are not tracked. A font that only the composition loads falls back to Studio's fonts in the row.

A layer is captured without its siblings, so a layer whose look depends on what is behind it (`mix-blend-mode`, `backdrop-filter`) is shown against its parent's background rather than the sibling it blends with.

## Before

A text-heavy fixture: Backdrop and Shape are visual layers; Title, Subtitle and Cta are text. On main the full-length rows are flat bars, Subtitle is a blurred, tiled picture of its words, and Cta tiles a picture of the whole frame.

![Backdrop, Shape and Title as flat bars, Subtitle a blurred tiled raster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4044bab7-fc57-4d0a-87e4-dfd717809b6e)

![Subtitle blurred and tiled, Cta tiling whole-frame pictures](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/521f7c1a-b500-447e-9edc-8846160712bd)

## After

Backdrop and Shape show their own pictures; Title, Subtitle and Cta show their own words as text, in their own colour and font (the font as Studio has it), Cta on its own red.

![Backdrop and Shape pictures, Title and Subtitle as text](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0ffa522-bf09-41ef-9f10-e341eea96036)

![Subtitle and Cta as text, Cta on its red background](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b281e76-6160-491f-b06f-55a708331d78)

title: fix(studio): keep a keyframe edit from copying other tweens' channels
body:
## What

Editing a keyframed tween in Studio at the playhead also copied the live value of every channel a *different* tween on the same element animates into the edited tween. Example: a layer with a `rotationX` keyframe tween and a sibling `to(el, { rotation: 90, duration: 3 })`. Setting RotX to 20 in the 3D panel at 2 s rewrote the first tween as `keyframes: { "0%": { rotationX: 0, rotation: 80 }, "50%": { rotationX: 20, rotation: 80 }, "100%": { rotationX: 40, rotation: 80 } }`. Two tweens then wrote rotation, and scrubbing back showed the layer stuck at 80° (0.5 s: 80° instead of the rotation tween's 28°).

The grouped path already refused to do this (a rotation commit must not carry opacity from an intro tween). The ungrouped path still did, and only for siblings that wrote the channel as a top-level var: a sibling using keyframes was left alone, so the same edit wrote different things depending on how the other tween was authored.

## How

- `readAllAnimatedProperties` no longer collects other tweens' channels. Its universal-baseline pass only ever added those channels, so it is gone too.
- The element-dependent baseline pass still skips a channel another tween writes, now asked through the shared `gsapWritesChannels`, which sees every keyframe form.
- Net: 2 files, source about -90 lines.

## Tests

- `gsapRuntimeReaders.test.ts`: real GSAP, an opacity keyframe tween plus a sibling rotation tween. It reads at 2 s, writes the edit the way the keyframe commit does (read values plus the edit at the playhead, backfilled into the other keyframes), then plays past the rotation tween's end. Rotation must be 90. On the old reader it is 80.
- Studio unit suite and typecheck pass.

## Before

The fixture above at the base of this PR, after the RotX edit at 2 s, scrubbed to 0.5 s. The layer is turned 80°, and the Rotation row shows keyframes copied into the edited tween.

![Before: the layer is held at 80 degrees after a RotX edit](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9e9e5959-6160-4050-8009-e5d8d58b7486)

## After

The same edit and scrub at this head. The edit writes only rotationX, and the layer follows the rotation tween (28° at 0.5 s).

![After: the layer follows its rotation tween](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7f527c5d-f071-4339-8a83-1f005466ca1a)

title: feat(cli): expose harness subscription usage to agents
body:
## What

Add `hyperframes usage --json` so an agent can see Claude Code, Codex, or Grok subscription usage without user setup. Available windows report percent used, percent remaining, and reset time, with the plan tier when readable. Skills check at the start and at workflow milestones.

## How

Read existing harness credentials and fixed provider endpoints without refreshing or writing credentials. Claude selects the current macOS user's keychain item before the legacy item. Missing windows remain null; unavailable or malformed usage returns unknown with a reason. Optional plan metadata stays null when unavailable. The command emits no tokens or usage telemetry and makes no update requests.

No thresholds, run plans, statusline bridge, or configuration edits. Provider quota endpoints may change; failures return unknown rather than guessed allowance.

## Source evidence

The independently implemented provider reads follow MIT-licensed OpenUsage at `ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad`:

- Claude Code: [OAuth request](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Claude/ClaudeUsageClient.swift#L100), [credential selection](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Claude/ClaudeAuthStore.swift#L340), and [system keychain command](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Services/SystemClients.swift#L322).
- Codex: [OAuth request and account header](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Codex/CodexUsageClient.swift#L79) and [window classification](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Codex/CodexUsageMapper.swift#L117).
- Grok: [billing request](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Grok/GrokUsageClient.swift#L66), [weekly period and omitted-zero decoding](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Grok/GrokCreditsConfigDecoder.swift#L20), and [weekly mapper](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Grok/GrokUsageMapper.swift#L21). Plan metadata follows the separate [settings request](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Grok/GrokUsageClient.swift#L75) and [tier decoder](https://github.com/robinebers/openusage/blob/ae49de04a2b7fc1b3cc334fcc1009276c46d82ad/Sources/OpenUsage/Providers/Grok/GrokUsageMapper.swift#L59). The official Grok CLI confirms [the request](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8/crates/codegen/xai-grok-shell/src/extensions/billing.rs#L189) and [first-party credential selection](https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/blob/2bdd1d6a6369de0e8c68132ea4539e9abd9e14a8/crates/codegen/xai-grok-login/src/model.rs#L155).

T3's [Claude SDK probe](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/b4d3d51ac99d4306d754afb5c78c49845bfac3c1/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeProvider.ts#L345) and [usage normalization](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code/blob/b4d3d51ac99d4306d754afb5c78c49845bfac3c1/apps/server/src/provider/Layers/claudeUsageLimits.ts#L134) were compared. Its query object belongs to the parent process; an independent skill-run CLI cannot reach it.

## Validation and limits

Live Claude Code read on macOS succeeded with no keychain permission dialog and no token-like output:

```json
{"status":"known","harness":"claude-code","session":{"usedPercent":23,"remainingPercent":77,"resetsAt":"2026-10-03T01:39:59Z"},"weekly":{"usedPercent":43,"remainingPercent":57,"resetsAt":"2026-10-08T20:59:59Z"},"planTier":"max"}
```

Remote focused fixtures passed: 27 parser cases and 9 actual CLI cases. Deliberately reversing remaining-percent normalization made seven witnesses fail across Claude Code, Codex, and Grok; source restored. Removing nullable tier support made the Claude CLI and Codex parser regressions fail; source restored. CLI typecheck passed remotely.

Fixtures cover all three harnesses, token-free output, unchanged auth files, exact request headers, expired logins, absent windows, and optional plan-read failure. GitHub checks provide full platform verification. Local hooks used `LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=typecheck,format,skills-manifest` after stale shared dependencies and parallel index-lock conflicts; source formatting and manifest generation ran remotely, and lint/Fallow/artifact hooks remain enabled.

Live Codex reported a weekly window with 5% used, 95% remaining, and tier `pro`; its session window was absent. Live Grok returned `{"status":"unknown","reason":"expired_login"}` without refreshing or writing credentials.

Remaining allowance is a snapshot, not a reservation or a prediction of the next video's cost.

## Size

One command, read-only provider readers, pure response normalization, focused fixtures, skill guidance and CLI reference documentation, a generated skill manifest, and a comment-citation regression.

title: fix(studio): the preview reloads when any write a commit saved is not patched on screen
body:
## What

Two preview-sync fixes in the one place every GSAP commit's preview update goes through (`applyPreviewSync` and its batch caller in `useGsapScriptCommits.ts`). Both are about a write that is saved but not yet on screen.

1. **A batch patched in place only part of what it wrote.** A batch passed on just the in-place patches that existed. When one call had a patch and another did not, the preview applied the patch, decided everything was on screen and skipped the soft reload, so the unpatched write stayed stale until a page reload. A batch now uses the in-place path only when every call in it brought a patch; otherwise it soft-reloads with the batch's own options.
2. **A deferred write with no patch lost its reload.** A group drag defers each member's preview sync and carries a missed patch to the final render through a shared latch. A write with no patch at all never set that latch, so if the last member patched in place, the reload was skipped and the earlier member kept its old position on screen. A write with no patch now counts as not on screen, the same as a missed patch.

## Edit bench

`resize-size-px-r0-root-z100-mid`, 6 runs each on one devbox: main drop 120.36 px in 6/6; #4889 alone drop 120.36 in 6/6; #4889 with this PR drop 0 in 6/6 (reload the same). A rare run passes without the fix, which is the batch race: the size and position writes only miss the reload when they land in one batch. The case's remaining undo failure is the separate undo-restore cause.

Full grid, one devbox: #4889 (acc76b98) with #4935 and this PR against #4889 alone. 261 of 1,562 cases are inaccurate with the stack, and every one of them is also inaccurate on #4889 alone, so the stack turns no passing case red.

## Before

After a corner resize at 1 s the Size field reads 370, 247 but the preview box has snapped back to the old size.

![Preview after the drop, old size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/236b88da-123d-4ba1-82a8-33edf1b9d2a7)

## After

The preview box shows the new size right after the drop.

![Preview after the drop, new size](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/293afba2-3392-4bd0-8e61-8ce10492b054)

## Test plan

- [x] `useGsapScriptCommits.test.tsx`: a batch of [size write without a patch, position write with one] soft-reloads once and never fully reloads (fails without fix 1: 0 soft reloads); a deferred write with no patch sets the latch and the final render soft-reloads (fails without fix 2). 35/35 in the file, the new cases 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Neighbours: domGroupMoveBy 9, useDomEditSession 16, useGsapAwareEditing 29, useGsapAwareEditing.groupPlan 4. tsc, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)

Rebased onto main after #4889 merged; the commits are unchanged.



Kept as its own PR under the size floor: it is the resize root fix, reviewed and bench-checked on its own, and folding it into #4935 (parsers) would mix two packages and reset both reviews.

title: fix(studio): a hovered menu row fills its row, and a host can hide the clip menu tools
body:
Right-clicking a timeline clip and highlighting a row left dark bands between the highlight and the menu edge or the divider. The panel padded its rows (`py-1`) and each divider carried a margin (`my-1`, or `mb-1 pb-1` on the clip menu's groups), so a highlighted row could never reach the edge.

The spacing and shape now have one owner, `components/ui/menuStyle.ts` (`menuClasses`): the panel, group, divider and row styles every hand-built context menu uses (clip menu and its submenu, track gap, keyframe diamond, assets, file tree, Window menu, linked clips, out-of-sync, the preview's canvas menu, the automation menu). The panel puts fill, border, shadow and radius on one element and clips its rows to that radius, so a highlighted first or last row follows the rounded corner instead of poking out of it. The clip menu's submenu is `position: fixed` so that clip does not cut it off.

`menuStyle.test.ts` fails if a hand-built menu panel (a literal `shadow-lg` plus `bg-neutral-900`) or a `role="menu"` file does not use the owner, so a new menu cannot bring the gap or the square corner back. Standardising the panel moves a few menus slightly: the Window menu's border is `neutral-700` (was `neutral-800`), the assets menu is `rounded-md shadow-lg` (was `rounded-lg shadow-xl`), and the linked-clips, out-of-sync and automation menus are `rounded-md`.

## Also in this PR: the clip menu's tools get their own switch

A host can set `clipMenuTools: false` on the timeline edit callbacks to hide the clip menu's own tools (Freeze frame, Voice, Look, Crop, Audio Gain, Duck and the link rows). Until now the only way was to withhold the handlers behind them (`onSetElementAttributeQuiet` and friends), which also switched off fade handles and volume lanes that share those handlers. Unset, the menu is unchanged. The switch hides the link rows including Delete clip only; a host sets it through `TimelineEditProvider`, not as a `Timeline` prop. It is the same component as the row fill above, so it rides in this PR.

title: capture: 0 assets cataloged when the cookie banner click reloads the page
body: On some sites `hyperframes capture` downloads no images at all. The JSON output has one warning: ``` "Asset catalog is empty — no images will be downloaded. The page may use non-standard image loading." ``` The images are plain `` tags, so that's not it. The page reloads in the middle of the capture. Still happens on 0.8.113 (latest today), default flags, 5 runs on the same URL: - 2 runs: "Asset catalog is empty" - 1 run: capture failed with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'innerHTML')`, which looks like the same reload hitting a different step - 1 run: 15 images but no logo - 1 run: everything, logo included What I see (traced on 0.8.20, the consent click and the catalog step look the same in 0.8.113): 1. `captureScrollScreenshots` clicks consent buttons before scrolling. On the site I tested, `[class*="consent"] button` matches the close button of the cookie dialog (an "acconsento" banner), and clicking it reloads the page. 2. The next `page.evaluate` in the screenshot step throws because of the navigation. The error isn't a timeout, so it gets swallowed and the step returns nothing ("0 scroll screenshots captured"). 3. `catalogAssets` then runs on the reloading page. I added a probe before each step: 21 `` right after navigation, 0 when the catalog runs (body scrollHeight 0), 20 again a few seconds later at "Extracting HTML & CSS". `extracted/page.html` comes out complete, which made this confusing at first. Only the catalog sees the empty page. On 0.8.20 it's worse: 0 of 5 runs catalog anything. It's a race, and on this site the reload usually wins. This one line before `progress("design", "Cataloging assets...")` fixes the catalog for me on 0.8.20, 33 assets in 5 of 5 runs (I haven't patched 0.8.113): ```js await page1.waitForNetworkIdle({ idleTime: 500, timeout: 15e3 }).catch(() => {}); ``` Waiting for the navigation right after the consent clicks would probably be cleaner. I haven't tried that. A second thing I hit on the same site, possibly separate: with the default 120 s `--capture-budget`, core extraction sometimes uses the whole budget. The page has four videos, one of them 4K, and my guess is the video download eats it, but I didn't measure that. The assets phase then reports `degraded` with `remainingMs: 0` and downloads nothing, even after the fix above. With the fix plus `--capture-budget 300000`, 0.8.20 got images and the logo in 3 of 3 runs. It might help to download images before videos, since images are small and the logo is often the thing people want. Repro: ``` npx hyperframes@0.8.113 capture --json --skip-vision -o out ``` I can share the URL privately if that helps. It's a client's site.

title: fix(studio-server): time history idle limits on one clock so a slow machine cannot flip them
body:
## What

History decides when an agent's turn has gone idle on one clock, and the tests that check that limit advance that clock instead of sleeping. A slow machine no longer changes which writes a turn keeps, in the tests or in a preview whose window timer fires late.

## Why

Three tests in `packages/cli/src/commands/history.test.ts` used `pause(ms)` against `historyDeps.turnIdleMs` with wall-clock margins (600 ms gaps under a 1000 ms limit, 600 or 700 ms over a 300 or 400 ms limit). When a command takes long enough to eat the margin, the gaps between writes cross the limit and a turn that should stay the agent's is filed as Outside. The test for writes closer together than the idle limit is the one that flips.

History had three clocks behind that decision:

- the engine took an injectable `now` but still called `Date.now()` for sweep times and window touches (`projectHistory.ts`, three places);
- the CLI stamped a direct turn's start with `Date.now()` (`historyOwner.ts`);
- each write is dated by its file's change time, clamped to the sweep time.

## Change

- The engine uses its own `now()` everywhere it reads the time.
- A window's idle timer no longer ends the window by itself: when it fires, the window ends only if the engine's clock says it has been idle for its limit, and otherwise re-arms for the rest. With the real clock this is the same timing as before; with an injected clock the timer can no longer end a window the clock says is still live. Each sleep is capped at Node's timer range (about 24.8 days), so a longer idle limit sleeps and checks again rather than waking after 1 ms, which is what Node does with a longer delay.
- `historyDeps.now` is the CLI's clock: it stamps turn starts, is passed into the engine it opens, and dates the "ago" column.
- The tests set that clock a day ahead of the file system and stamp the mtime of each file they write through the test helper with it, so those writes are dated when the test says. `pause()` is gone; the three tests advance the clock instead. Writes the tests do not make through the helper (the baseline files, the turn marker, undo's own writes, renames and deletes) keep real file times; no test here times one of those against the idle limit.

The default clock is `Date.now()`.

## Proof

Each history command slowed by 1.5 s (a delay added to the test's command runner for this run only):

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Slowed | 1 failed: "a turn whose writes come closer together than the idle limit stays the agent's past it" | 32 passed |
| Normal | 32 passed | 32 passed |

Each command finishing 0.8 s late, preview mode, "a turn left open ends after the idle limit": with the engine's old bare timer the window ended before the agent's write was seen and the test failed; with the clock check it passes. Disabling the idle rule itself (`projectHistory.ts`, the `takesWrite` check) now fails that test in both direct and preview mode.

The engine's own history suites (`packages/studio-server/src/history`) pass: 138 passed, 2 skipped. The new one opens a window with a 30-day idle limit and fails if any timer delay exceeds Node's range.


Under 100 changed lines: a standalone fix of the history idle clock with nothing in flight to carry it.

title: test(studio): print PASS for edit accuracy cases that pass every metric
body:
## What

The edit accuracy bench printed `FAIL` for every case in its run log, including cases that passed every metric. `score()` built each case's `checks` but never set `pass`, and the run log line (`run.mjs` verdict) and the failing-case evidence save both read `pass`. So a bare `FAIL <case> <seconds>` with no metric after it was really a full pass, and every case saved "failing" evidence.

`score()` now sets `pass` to every metric passing, smoothness included, and `false` for a case that errored. The log line then reads `PASS` for a clean case and `FAIL <case> <s> <metrics>` only when a metric failed, and evidence is saved for failing cases only, as intended.

## Scope

Only the run log line and the evidence save read `pass`. The summary, `table.md`, the ratchet gate, `baseline.json` and the sticky comment count all read the per-metric `checks`, so their numbers do not change. The per-case `pass` matches the summary's "pass everything" count (smoothness included); the headline "accurate" count leaves smoothness out on purpose, so a case can print `FAIL <case> <s> smooth` and still count as accurate.

## Tests

`report.test.mjs`: a case with every metric in range passes; one with a metric out of range fails; an errored case fails. On the old `score()` the first assertion reads `undefined`. The bench's unit tests pass (8 files, 57 tests).

## No visible change

The bench's run log and evidence folders only; nothing in Studio or the player changes.

## Size

Two lines in `score()` and one test: the bug is a missing field. It ships alone because nothing open can carry it: the other bench PRs are drafts that rebase over this one, and the misleading run log affects every bench reader today.

title: hyperframes-media: audio.mjs ignores speed on the Kokoro TTS path
body:
## Summary

`scripts/audio.mjs` reads `speed` from `audio_request.json` or `--speed`, and passes it to `synthesizeOne()` in `scripts/lib/tts.mjs`. The HeyGen branch uses it. The Kokoro branch builds the `npx hyperframes tts` argument list without `--speed`, so every Kokoro render runs at 1.0 whatever the request says. Nothing reports an error.

## Repro

One-line request, `"provider": "kokoro"`, run with `--only tts --speed 0.8` and again with `--speed 1.0`:

| speed | voice duration |
|---|---|
| 0.8 | 3.285 s |
| 1.0 | 3.285 s |

A 13-line request gave 82.389 s at both 1.0 and 0.9. Calling `npx hyperframes tts --speed 0.9` directly on the same text gave 87.5 s, so the CLI itself supports the flag.

## Fix

In `synthesizeOne()`, Kokoro branch, after the `--lang` push:

```js
  if (lang !== "en") args.push("--lang", lang);
  if (speed !== 1) args.push("--speed", String(speed));
```

With this line the same one-line request gives 4.032 s at 0.8 and 3.285 s at 1.0. The ratio is 1.23, close to the 1.25 that 1/0.8 predicts.

## Environment

- hyperframes CLI 0.8.107
- Node 22.17.0, macOS
- hyperframes-media skill folder hash 708b3ce

title: fix(media-use): forward Kokoro narration speed
body:
## What

Forward narration's resolved `speed` to the Kokoro `hyperframes tts` invocation.

## Why

The audio pipeline accepts `--speed` and passes it into `synthesizeOne`, but its Kokoro branch omits the CLI argument. As reported in #4926, changing narration speed therefore leaves the generated duration unchanged even though the direct TTS command supports it.

## Related work

## How

Pass `--speed` with the resolved numeric value converted to a string, including the default value of 1. Preserve the existing voice, output, language, and process invocation behavior. Regenerate the media-use manifest hash through the repository commit hook.

## Test plan

- Repository lint and formatting checks passed before rebasing onto current main.

- Whole-workspace tests encountered missing built package exports, fork-worker timeouts, and failures outside the changed TTS path; the run was interrupted. Whole-workspace typechecking was also interrupted. Initial commands hit a Node shim cache permission error; lint was rerun successfully with the installed Node binary.
