title: fix(studio): an undo or drop on an animated layer keeps it where it was
body:
## What

An undo, a drop or any soft reload on a GSAP-animated layer whose stylesheet sets `translate`, `rotate` or `scale` moved the layer by that CSS amount (50 px for a `translate: 40px 30px` layer). The soft reload clears GSAP's inline props and re-runs the script, but GSAP keeps the transform it parsed on first load in `el._gsap`. The re-run never folds the stylesheet transform into GSAP's again, so the CSS value applies a second time on top of GSAP's.

`applySoftReload` now marks each cleared target's GSAP transform cache stale (`_gsap.uncache = 1`) right after `clearProps`, so the next tween re-reads the element and folds the CSS transform once, as on a fresh load.

## Related work

Stacked on #4889 (base `fix/studio-playhead-writer-carrier`). Retargets to main after #4889 merges.

## Evidence

- Edit accuracy bench, the rotate family (292 cases), on an earlier #4889 head (234d2903) plus this commit: 292/292 accurate. Its raw results were not kept, and it was not rerun on the current #4889 head; CI's bench on this PR is the check at this head. On #4889 alone, CI's own shards fail 48 rotate cases, all root layers with a CSS transform under GSAP (fromto, keys, scale, spin at every zoom, undo and drop/reload).
- `gsapUndoRestore.browser.test.ts` (real Chrome): 11/11 pass, three runs in a row. Without the `gsapSoftReload.ts` change 6 of the 11 fail (keys, scale and spin layers after an undone crop or a soft reload). The test has no sleeps or fixed waits.

## Before

A layer with a stylesheet `translate: 40px 30px` under a GSAP rotation tween (the dashed box is where GSAP puts it at 1 s), on #4889 without this commit: a style edit, then undo. The layer moves 40 px right and 30 px down, the CSS translate applied a second time.

![Before: after the undo the layer has slid off its animated position](./before.png)

## After

The same edit and undo with this commit: the layer stays on its animated position.

![After: the layer stays where GSAP puts it](./after.png)

title: fix(media-use): forward TTS speed to Kokoro
body:
## What

`synthesizeOne` now passes `--speed` to `npx hyperframes tts` on the Kokoro path. Before, a request speed from `audio_request.json` or `audio.mjs --speed` never reached the CLI, so every Kokoro line rendered at 1.0 with no error. The HeyGen path already forwarded speed.

`audio.mjs` is now the only place speed is parsed, with no fallback, and it rejects zero, non-numeric values and anything outside (0, 3] up front. Before, `Number(x) || 1.0` silently turned 0 and junk into 1. The faceless-explainer, pr-to-video and product-launch-video adapters forward the raw `--speed` flag instead of keeping their own copy of that fallback.

Fixes #4926. The faceless-explainer, pr-to-video and product-launch-video adapters route through this engine, so they get the fix too.

## Verification

- `synthesizeOne(kokoro)` runs against a stub `npx` on PATH that records the real argv: `--speed 0.8` is present at 0.8 and absent at the default. Removing the fix line fails the first test.
- `audio.mjs` exits 1 with a clear message for request speed 5, 0, -1 and "fast", and for `--speed 0` and `--speed abc`. A numeric string ("0.8", as the adapters send it) passes. Restoring `|| 1.0` fails 4 of these.
- `node --test audio.test.mjs lib/tts.test.mjs`: 24 pass.
- `gen-skills-manifest --check` is in sync.
- The issue's repro: 0.8 and 1.0 both gave 3.285 s before; with the line, 4.032 s vs 3.285 s.

## Not changed (other providers)

| Provider | Speed today |
|---|---|
| ElevenLabs | dropped (the Python helper sends no voice_settings) |
| Gemini | rejected when not 1, with a clear message |
| HeyGen | forwarded, no range check |

title: Add authored chapter markers
body:
![demo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/hyperframes/authored-chapter-markers/preview.gif)

<video src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/pr-demo-assets/main/hyperframes/authored-chapter-markers/out.mp4" controls width="720"></video>

A timed clip can set `data-chapter` to a section title. Those titles become player scrubber ticks, a current-chapter chip, Studio ruler ticks, a `hyperframes chapters` listing, and MP4/MOV chapter metadata on render. A composition with no `data-chapter` is unchanged. `data-chapter` is a navigational title, not the inspector label.

## What changed

- `data-chapter` on a timed clip marks a section start at that clip's resolved `data-start`. The chapter runs until the next chapter or the end of the composition.
- `hyperframes chapters` lists index, start, title, and element id. `hyperframes compositions --json` and `hyperframes inspect --json` include the same chapters.
- Render writes chapter metadata into MP4 and MOV when any exist. `--no-chapters` skips that write. GIF, WebM, and png sequences ignore chapters and still render.
- The player shows ticks and a title chip, and `[` / `]` seek to the previous or next chapter. `chapters="off"` hides the rail. Studio draws read-only ruler ticks.
- Lint reports an empty title, a chapter with no resolvable start, or two chapters at the same start.

## Tests

Parser, lint, player, Studio ruler, CLI, and chapter-metadata tests passed on this branch.

title: perf(studio): keep timeline bulk actions under a second, hand-move at most 3 clips
body:
## What

- Dragging, keyboard-moving or edge-resizing a selection of 4 or more timeline clips is refused: the clips stay put and a toast says to select 3 or fewer, or describe the change in the prompt box. One to three clips move and resize as before.
- The multi-second waits on large projects are fixed at their causes, not hidden behind that limit (below).
- `packages/studio/tests/e2e/timeline-bulk-actions.mjs` times select-all, move 3 and delete-all in a real browser on a real project.

## Why it was slow

Measured on an 11-composition, 98-clip launch project from `heygen-com/hyperframes-launches`, built CLI, devbox.

| Cause | Fix |
| --- | --- |
| Every selected clip sent its own "does this element still exist in source" probe (98 POSTs for select-all, re-sent for the whole selection on each added clip) | Probes issued in one tick leave as one request per file; the server parses the file once |
| A timeline delete sent one `remove-element` POST per clip, each re-parsing and re-serializing the file | One `remove-elements` request, one parse |
| Each click on a clip from another file re-fetched GSAP data for every composition | Covered files stay loaded; the read revalidates and an unchanged file answers 304 |
| Any write to `index.html` re-captured every composition thumbnail (about 15 serial captures per move) | A scene page borrows only the root's `<head>`, so only a root head edit invalidates scene thumbnails; the root's own thumbnail still refreshes |

## Benchmark

Median of 5, base vs this branch, run back to back on the same devbox (load 15 to 41 while they ran).

| Action | Base | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Select all (98 clips) | 1967 ms | 648 ms |
| Move 3 clips | 1554 ms | 980 ms |
| Delete all (98 clips) | 2193 ms | 731 ms |

"Done" is foreground work only: no request in flight and no long task for 500 ms. Thumbnail and lint requests are background and not awaited. Run it with `BULK_PROJECT_DIR=<project> node packages/studio/tests/e2e/timeline-bulk-actions.mjs` after building studio and cli.

title: fix(studio): an undo or drop on an animated layer keeps it where it was
body:
## What changes for the user

Undo, redo, or dropping a resize on an animated layer whose CSS sets `translate`, `rotate` or `scale` no longer shows the layer shifted or rotated twice. The saved file was already right; the preview now matches it without a page reload.

## Cause

The runtime pads a timeline that is shorter than its composition with a zero-length tween on a plain `{}` object (`hf-runtime-filler`); authored `tl.to({}, { duration })` padding does the same. The soft reload gathered every tween target as an element, so its cache flush, `gsap.set(targets, { clearProps: "all" })`, threw on that object (`style` is undefined). An empty `catch` hid the throw, so GSAP never re-parsed the layer: its cached transform still held the CSS translate/rotate/scale it had folded in, and the stylesheet applied them a second time (+40,+30 px, or 60deg instead of 30deg). That is why keyframed, scale, spin and fromTo layers failed and a plain full-length tween did not.

## Fix

- `softReloadTargets.ts`: reset targets are elements only (`elementTargets`), the one place both target walks go through.
- `gsapSoftReload.ts`: the flush is no longer wrapped in an empty `catch`. A throw now falls to the existing full-reload path, which already records `gsap_soft_reload_outcome`, and the error is logged. The `style?.` guard that existed for non-element targets is gone.

## Tests

- `gsapSoftReload.test.ts`: a filler `{}` target is not flushed; a throwing flush returns `cannot-soft-reload` and logs. Both fail on the base.
- `gsapUndoRestore.browser.test.ts` (real Chrome, the bench's own fixtures): keys/scale/spin rows at two playhead times, through undo and through `applySoftReload` directly. 6 rows fail on the base and pass with the fix.

## Before

The bench's `resize-keys-px-r30-root-z100-on` fixture (a keyframed layer whose CSS rotates it 30deg), corner-resized at 2 s. On #4889 alone the drop shows it at about 60deg (drop off 118.7 px), and undo leaves it rotated and shifted (112.8 px off).

![Before: after the drop, the layer shows at about 60deg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6a305ca1-9aec-4bf9-ad00-fa716cd47bea)
![Before: after undo, the layer is still rotated twice and shifted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3a00df8e-9b80-40e4-894a-d618c53b01db)

## After

Same case, same box: drop, reload, undo and redo all 0 px.

![After: after the drop, the layer keeps its 30deg](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/15ed2919-5570-45a0-9d09-9b6230866482)
![After: after undo, the layer is back where it was](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f37a5502-6a06-4ba3-a4c1-b81ac588bd45)

Stacked on #4889 (`fix/studio-playhead-writer-carrier`).

title: fix(parsers): a keyframe edit no longer overrides an earlier tween at the start
body:
## What changes

Studio keeps an `hf-hold` set at t=0 for a keyframed position tween that starts after 0, so the element holds its first keyframe before the tween plays. That hold also pinned props an earlier tween on the same target already animates. With

```js
tl.from("#t", { x: -60, duration: 2 }, 0);
tl.to("#t", { keyframes: { "0%": { x: -50, y: -3.5 }, "100%": { x: 60, y: 30 } }, duration: 1 }, 2);
```

the hold wrote `x: -50` at t=0, so after a backward seek to 0 the element showed -50 instead of the `from()` start of -60. Any resize, move or nudge that writes a keyframe into the later tween did this.

The hold now skips each position prop that an earlier timeline tween on the same target writes. The decision lives in one helper, `positionHoldForAnimation` in `gsapConstants.ts`, which both writers call instead of keeping two copies:

- "Earlier" means a start the parser resolved and that comes before the keyframed tween. A start it could not resolve never counts as earlier, so the hold stays, as before.
- A global `gsap.set` is a base value, like CSS, so the hold still overrides it, as before.
- The default acorn writer resolves label positions, so an earlier label-placed tween is handled. The recast writer is the `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_WRITER=recast` migration fallback and cannot resolve labels; there it keeps the hold it always had.

Also fixed in the same function: on a one-line script the acorn sync added a newline on its second run. The inserted hold now ends its own line, matching what removal takes, so a re-sync changes no bytes.

## Edit bench

On a devbox build of #4889 (55187872) plus this PR, the 36 `(resize|move|nudge)-fromto-*-on` cases pass `keys` 36/36. Without it, `keys` fails there (move-fromto-px-r0-root-z100-on: 150). Those cases still fail `drop`/`reload` on #4889's current head for an unrelated reason: the merge of `main` into #4889 combined with #4911's seek change shows the earlier tween's end at the keyframe's time. That is tracked on #4889.

Full grid, one devbox: #4889 (acc76b98) with this PR and #4920 against #4889 alone. 261 of 1,562 cases are inaccurate with the stack, and every one of them is also inaccurate on #4889 alone, so the stack turns no passing case red.

## Tests

- `gsapParser.test.ts`, the `syncPositionHoldsBeforeKeyframes` block, runs each new case against both writers where both should agree: an earlier `from()` (hold drops x, keeps y), a global `gsap.set` base (hold kept), a later label-placed tween (hold kept), an earlier label-placed tween (acorn: no hold), and a one-line script re-sync (byte-stable). Each one fails with its fix reverted.
- parsers: gsapParser 213, gsapWriter.parity 146, gsapWriter.acorn 42, gsapWriterParity.acorn 14, gsapParser.acorn 14, gsapWriterAcorn.inline 10, motionPath 4. studio-server: files 91, files.replaceInPlace 9. tsc, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet are clean.

Rebased onto main after #4889 merged; the commits are unchanged.

title: docs: show agents where Studio edits go and how tests build, and let docs skip captures
body:
## What

Docs that tell an agent (or a new contributor) where things are, plus one CI fix so docs-only Studio changes can land.

- `packages/studio/AGENTS.md`
  - **Where a canvas edit goes:** the owner file for each hop, from the gesture through GSAP-or-plain routing, the writers, the save, the reload decision and undo.
  - **The edit accuracy bench:** what it checks, how to run one case, where results land, and how the CI gate and baseline banking work.
  - **The Before/After captures rule**, listed with the other gates.
- `packages/producer/README.md`: **Where each step lives**, the stage files `executeRenderJob` runs in order, where the capture plan is chosen, and where config comes from.
- `AGENTS.md`: tests and typecheck resolve core, parsers, lint, studio-server and player through `dist/`, so build first and rebuild a dependency after editing it. Core's `src/generated/` is build output. How to run one test file per package, including producer's per-file runner.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`
  - The stable release steps now match `publish.yml`: push a `release/vX.Y.Z` branch and merge its PR. A hand-pushed stable tag publishes nothing.
  - How to run the two comment checks locally before pushing.
- `scripts/check-pr-captures.mjs`: Markdown under `packages/studio/` and `packages/player/` no longer counts toward the captures check.

## Why

Agents changing Studio editing kept searching the whole `src/` tree for the same few owners: the resize intercept, the plain size writer, where `skipRefresh` is decided, what triggers a reload, where undo restores. The bench had no doc at all, so finding it, running one case and reading its baseline was rediscovered each time. Render work had the same shape: agents traced `renderOrchestrator.ts` to find which stage runs when and where config is resolved. The build-first rule and generated files are why fresh worktrees report test failures that are not real.

CONTRIBUTING's stable release steps described a tag push that the publish workflow no longer accepts. The current flow lives in `docs/contributing/changelog-process.mdx`; CONTRIBUTING now summarises it and links there.

The captures check exists to show behaviour. Markdown in those two packages is documentation, and nothing imports it as UI content. Without the fix, a docs-only change of 20 or more lines can never pass, because the "No visible change" exemption is capped at 20 lines.

## Related work

Does not touch the root `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` consolidation in #4579 and #4120 beyond adding a paragraph under Build & Test.

## How

- Every path and symbol named in the new Studio sections was checked against the tree.
- The map names files and functions, not line numbers, so it survives edits.
- `isWatched` in the captures script skips `*.md` and `*.mdx`. Code, styles, HTML and assets are judged as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test scripts/check-pr-captures.test.mjs`: exit 0, 74 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped, three runs in a row. With the fix reverted, exactly the new test fails (73 passed, 1 failed).
- [x] `node scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` on the three docs and the script: exit 0. An earlier wording that named run output files in backticks failed it (exit 1) and was fixed.
- [x] `node scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs`: exit 0.
- [x] `oxfmt --check` on every changed file: exit 0.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

## Review

Three adversarial review rounds. The first found that the save step named one writer where Studio has three save paths (SDK cutover, atomic batches, script edits), plus three wording issues. The second found that the producer map put worker sizing in the wrong file and implied every capture runs a separate encode. All were fixed; the final round found nothing.

## No visible change

Docs and a CI script only.

title: perf(studio): drag and resize any number of selected clips, saved in one write per file
body:
## What

Moving or resizing many selected clips on the timeline works at any count again: the 3-clip hand-edit cap is gone, and dropping 98 selected clips settles in about 1 s instead of 15 s.

- **No cap.** Drag, edge-resize and keyboard pickup accept any selection; the "Select 3 or fewer clips" refusal and toast are removed.
- **One GSAP write per file, one parse per batch.** A group move or trim sent one `gsap-mutations` request per clip, one after another, each parsing and rewriting the whole file. It now sends one `gsap-mutations-batch` request per file, and the server folds a run of clip retimes into one script parse and one hold sync. Clip lookups during the retime share one DOM walk per file instead of one selector query per clip. Ownership and rollback are unchanged: a file is one owned step.
- **Root duration synced once per file.** Every clip's patch re-parsed the file to recompute the root `data-duration`; a batch now patches every clip, then syncs once.
- **One store update per drop.** The optimistic move applied each clip to the timeline store separately, so every subscriber ran once per clip; a group drop, its rollback and a group resize now land as one update.
- **No redundant selection work after a save.** Re-resolving the selected element after the preview updates no longer asks the server again whether the same node exists in source, no longer re-applies a selection that reads the same, and the commit preflight keeps each selected element's answer until its own inputs change.
- **Keyframe cache keeps sub-composition entries.** Re-reading `index.html` deleted the `index.html#id` and bare-id entries that sub-composition files write for their own elements, so their keyframes vanished until each file was read again. `index.html` now leaves those to their owner, and a file that re-reads unchanged publishes nothing.
- **No remount when a clip joins or leaves a drag**, so thumbnails no longer reload at drag start and drop. The drag offset rides on the clip, its diamonds and its lanes directly instead of on a wrapper, so a clip adds no extra DOM node and timeline scrolling stays within the viewport gate (interaction p95 48.1 ms against 58.3). While a group drag is in flight, each of those three fades to 0.85 on its own, so where diamonds overlap their clip the bar shows faintly through them.
- **Undo during the save.** A timeline move registers a still-saving revert like canvas moves do, and Cmd+Z now reverts the edit still saving before painting an older predicted step.
- **One undo per move.** A timeline move or resize and the tween shift it triggers are now one undo step however long the tween save takes. Each move or resize gets its own history key, held until the next edit, and the tween save joins it. Before, a tween save over 300 ms split them, so one Cmd+Z put the tweens back and left the clips moved. The held key is scoped to the page, so a reload or a second tab never joins another page's step, and a delete holds its step the same way until its ripple lands. A held step is dated by its last write, not by the later edit that ends it. Single-clip move and resize moved into their own hook, `useTimelineClipTimingEditing`, beside the group one.

## Why

Dragging 4+ clips on a launch-size project took 10 to 15 s or more to land, which is why the cap existed. Profiled on the public 98-clip launch project with every clip selected, the drop paid for one GSAP request per clip, one file parse per clip on the server, one selector query per clip per retime, one existence check per selected element, and one store update per clip, each re-rendering the timeline.

## Related work

Refs #4932 (added the cap and the first bulk-action fixes). The drop is now main-thread bound (Chrome task time about equals wall time). Three follow-ups take it further, each its own PR: clips that did not change skip rendering, the post-save preview and keyframe sync stops re-publishing unchanged data, and a group move writes timing and tween positions in one save.

## How

`packages/studio/tests/e2e/timeline-bulk-actions.mjs` gains `move-all-small`, `move-all-past-end` and `resize-all-end` (select every clip, drag, drop) and reports `dropTaskMs`, the browser main-thread task time spent on the drop. "Before" is this branch's first commit (cap removed, nothing else), so both sides accept the drag. Before and after ran interleaved, one round each, five rounds, on a shared 32-core Linux box under load (load average 15 to 24).

| Action (98 clips selected) | Settled, before | Settled, after | Main-thread time, before | Main-thread time, after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Move a little | 15.1 s | 1.01 s | 11.3 s | 1.13 s |
| Move past the end | 15.4 s | 0.97 s | 11.6 s | 1.17 s |
| Resize by the end edge | 16.7 s | 1.03 s | 12.4 s | 1.15 s |

Medians of 5, measured before the rebase onto main. "Settled" is the captures' "idle". On the same box nearly idle (load 4 to 10), three runs per action at this PR's head: settled 0.83 s, 0.76 s and 0.90 s, with the save finished at 0.51 s, 0.49 s and 0.61 s. Absolute times move with the box's load (the same after build measured 0.85 to 3 s across an afternoon); compare the columns.

In a folded run of clip retimes, the per-mutation `mutationChanges` flags report whether each retime moved a value, and a hold re-sync is credited to the run's last slot; single requests credit the sync to the request that ran it. The only reader of these flags ignores retime mutations.

## Before

Every clip selected, dragged right, dropped. The banner counts from the drop and then shows three numbers: **clips placed** (first frame painted after the drop, clips at their new place), **saved** (the last file write finished) and **idle** (no request in flight and no long task for 500 ms, the same "settled" as the table). Base build, shared box at load 16 to 22: placed 233 ms, saved 16.6 s, idle 18.6 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/33251a7c-2c7a-4364-9cd2-c23470e21d21

## After

Same drag on this branch, same box and load: placed 225 ms, saved 0.84 s, idle 1.42 s.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/04f06192-b53b-47f1-96c0-54556f81deed

![after: 98 clips moved, timers at idle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/552e14c1-4287-44d6-b93c-7d865535603c)

While a save is in flight, undo reverts the move at once, a second drag is accepted and its save queues behind the first, and the preview plays tweens at their old times until the GSAP write lands. A follow-up writes timing and tween positions in one save.

### One Cmd+Z after a group move

Three clips selected and dragged right, with every tween save held 3 s; once the save finished, Cmd+Z was pressed once. The fixture is a three-clip composition built for this capture. Before is this branch without the fix (main also sends one tween request per clip, which hides the split).

Before: the clips stay at 2.61 s while their tweens and keyframes go back to 0 s.

![before: one Cmd+Z leaves the clips moved and their tweens back at 0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/91c013d3-6cec-47e6-94f2-1e70a3d2c88a)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/514707d0-d817-45be-a23f-ae518d99f7e5

After: one Cmd+Z puts the clips and their tweens back at 0 s.

![after: one Cmd+Z puts the clips and their tweens back](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/61081ec1-f0bb-4579-a898-a44a6abecc13)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d301b7b4-f4e4-489f-840b-a7ade8f97f7d

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - Hand move and hand resize accept 1, 3, 4 and 6 selected clips; keyboard pickup of a clip in a 4-clip selection starts a drag.
  - A group edit writes its GSAP changes through the batch route; the owned-chain rollback cases run through `foldGsapMutationIntoHistory`.
  - A batch of clip retimes writes the bytes single requests write in turn, with the same per-mutation change flags; the folded retime equals one call per retime, and every `#id` lookup comes from one DOM walk.
  - A batch syncs the root duration once and writes the same bytes as per-clip sync.
  - Batched store updates notify once and end in the state the same calls one by one would.
  - Re-resolving the same node keeps its source-existence answer; a replaced node asks again.
  - A group-preserving refresh that reads nothing new keeps the shown selection; the preflight re-checks only members that changed.
  - Re-reading a file to the same keyframe entries publishes nothing; re-reading `index.html` keeps a sub-composition's entries.
  - A clip keeps its DOM node when it becomes, then stops being, a drag passenger, carries the drag offset itself, and shares its parent with its neighbours (no wrapper node).
  - A move registers a revert while saving, a reverted move stays reverted when its save lands, and undo reverts the edit still saving before an older predicted step; when that edit lands while undo waits, the revert is confirmed only if its history claim counted, otherwise the move is shown again and the server's own restore applies.
  - A group move whose tween save answers after 400 ms undoes in one step with its tweens, and a second move of the same clips is its own step (real history engine); each single-clip move and resize claims its own key, which its tween fold reuses, with no window.
  - A held key from one page does not join another page's edit under the same key; a delete's step is held under the key its ripple joins.
  - A held step keeps the time of its last write when a later edit commits it.
  - Each new test fails without its change.
- [x] Manual testing performed (headless browser captures above)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: perf(core): a paused Studio drag lets the preview loop sleep until the drag ends
body:
## What

While a Studio drag is held on a paused film, the preview's transport loop now sleeps instead of ticking every frame. It wakes the moment the drag ends and runs the one reconciling seek it owes.

## Why

The manual-edit bench scores a drag as not smooth when any frame does more than 8 ms of main-thread work. On the CI gate, resize, move, crop and rotate cases miss that bar, and their worst frames recur every 20 frames. That is the paused transport's full clip-manifest post. Studio rebuilds its clip list from each post (useTimelineSyncCallbacks processTimelineMessage).

The loop was awake at all because a paused gesture marks a reconciling seek as owed, and `canParkTransport` refused to park while one was owed. So every drag ticked the whole transport each frame (timing reads, duration sync, the manifest post every 20 frames, media rebinds every 30) only to skip the seek the gesture defers.

## Related work

Small on purpose: one root cause per PR so each fix to the manual-edit bench can merge and ship on its own tonight.

Refs the manual-edit bench "not smooth" cause (resize, move, rotate, crop, nudge). Was stacked on #4889; rebased onto main after it merged, commits unchanged.

## How

Nothing is owed while the gesture is still held. The gesture watch (`createManualEditGestureWatch`) already wakes the loop when the marker clears, so `canParkTransport` now parks while a deferred seek's gesture is still active. The drop still gets its seek on the frame the marker clears (the existing "runs the reconciling seek" test). Every other wake signal is unchanged.

Review found one gap the parked loop exposes: releasing a paused-media lease only dropped the lease, so a parked loop let the released element keep playing until an unrelated wake. That was already true while idle; a parked drag makes it reachable mid-gesture. `releasePausedMedia` now wakes the loop. Its test used to start the media again after release, which fires a play event and hid the gap; it now releases alone.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `transportPark.test.ts` now pins that the loop parks mid-gesture. Red without the fix ("expected 1 to be +0"), green 3 of 3 with it. The core runtime suite otherwise passes (two tests that time out on a loaded box fail on the base too and pass alone).
- [x] Unit tests: the lease test fails without the release wake ("expected false to be true") and passes with it.
- [x] Manual testing performed: quiet-runner drag-frames A/B (Studio drag frames workflow, 12 cases per family x 5 runs, same filter, base #4889 head vs this PR's first commit):

| Family | Not smooth (base -> head) | Worst-frame work p90 ms | Spikes 20 frames apart |
|---|---|---|---|
| resize | 8 -> 3 | 8.03 -> 7.61 | 7 -> 0 |
| move | 3 -> 1 | 7.74 -> 6.89 | 4 -> 0 |
| crop | 4 -> 2 | 6.64 -> 5.98 | 0 -> 0 |
| rotate | 4 -> 0 | 5.23 -> 4.89 | 3 -> 0 |

Median per-frame work is unchanged (3.6 ms resize), as expected: this removes the periodic spike and the idle tick, not the drag's own work.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(core): music keeps playing smoothly across video cuts in preview
body:
## What

In Studio preview, a music bed now plays straight through video cuts. Before, when each shot of a sequence carried its own short sound clip (the shot's camera audio, faded in and out), the music jumped at every cut: a short gap and a skip back of 60 to 900 ms, depending on how slowly the next shot's sound started.

Export was never affected: the rendered audio of the fixture below is byte-identical on main and on this branch, and its music has no jump.

## Why

While no Web Audio buffer plays, the preview playhead follows an audio element (the clock's tier 2). It followed the first in-window `<audio>` in page order. A sub-composition placed before the music in the page put its shot sounds first, so the playhead followed a 0.48 s shot sound instead of the music. At each cut the playhead moved to the next shot's sound, which starts late (seek, play, data). Since #4679 the playhead holds while the clip it follows catches up rather than stepping back, so it held for that delay. The music kept playing through the hold, drifted ahead of the playhead, and media sync then seeked it back. That seek is the jump you hear.

## Related work

Refs #4679, whose rule that the playhead holds for the clip it follows is what turned a late shot sound into a music jump. That rule stays.

## How

`init.ts`: the clock's audio pick moves into `followedOrLongestRunningAudio`. The clip the playhead already follows keeps it, as before. Otherwise the in-window clip that runs longest takes it (`start` plus `resolveMediaElementDurationSeconds`, the existing owner of a media element's timeline length), not the first in page order. With a music bed in the window, the bed leads and a cut hands nothing over. A clip that has ended is never picked, so a bed whose file runs out early hands the playhead to a clip still playing. The buffering freeze and the never-step-back rule are unchanged, but whenever nothing is followed yet (at Play, after a seek out of the window, at a handover) they now apply to the longest clip rather than the first in page order: with a voice-over under a longer music bed, the playhead follows the bed and the picture waits for the bed if it is still loading, while the voice is the clip media sync corrects. A clip with no `data-duration` ranks as open-ended until its metadata loads.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `audioClockSource.test.ts`, new case: three 1 s shot sounds earlier in the page, each starting 250 ms late, and a 10 s music bed. Every frame the playhead must sit on the music's time, and the runtime must never write the music's `currentTime` after Play. It fails on main: the playhead lags the music by a frame from the start, and with that check removed main seeks the music from 0.30 s back to 0.05 s. Passes 3 runs in a row with the fix.
- Two more cases pin the pick: a longer bed that starts late cannot take the playhead from a playing voice it already follows, and a bed whose file ended early hands it to the clip still playing. Removing either line in the pick fails its case.
- Core runtime suite: 66 files, 1746 tests pass with the fix. `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, the comment checks and the dead-code audit pass.
- Measured in Studio on a Linux box with headful Chrome, playing across the cuts with every media event and the music element logged per frame:
  - Fixture below, 9 cuts: main seeked the music 8 and 9 times while playing (jumps of 64 to 175 ms, playhead holds of 115 to 175 ms at cuts). This branch: 0 seeks, 0 jumps, no holds; the probe's per-frame gap between music and playhead stays under 70 ms on a heavily loaded box (main: up to 180 ms).
  - A longer real-world shape (9 shots of 0.48 s with sound, plus SFX, under a 62 s music bed): main seeked the music 8 to 9 times in 2.5 s, jumps up to 1.4 s. This branch: none at the cuts.
  - The recorded sound of the captures below: the music has a click every 0.25 s. On main, 10 of 26 click intervals are off by more than 12 ms (94 to 466 ms). On this branch, 0 of 21.

## Independent review

No blocking or major findings. Three minor ones, all taken: an ended bed could win the pick (now skipped, with a test), the "followed clip keeps the playhead" rule had no test (added), and the behaviour change when nothing is followed is now stated above. One nit kept: `&& !el.loop` in the ended check is redundant, since a looping element never reports `ended`.

## Before

Studio on main (70dde41b), a fixture built for this PR from generated test patterns and tones: ten 0.48 s shots in a sub-composition, each a muted `<video>` plus its own sound clip with a 40 ms fade, under one music bed (a rising tone with a click every quarter second) that starts with the first shot. Play from 00:00.4 to 00:06.2. The readout compares the music element's time with the playhead and counts the music's seeks during playback: 10 seeks, worst gap 203 ms, and the clicks stumble at the cuts.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3c3a9abd-4ad8-4fbb-ab70-9fcf21c2db72

## After

The same steps with this branch's change on the same main: 0 seeks, the music stays on the playhead, the clicks stay even.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/01d9cd29-1d91-4d65-b74a-c6a8ed66ca66

title: perf(producer): load injected video frames by URL during export
body:
## What

Exports of compositions with video load each injected video frame by URL from the render's file server,
instead of sending it to the page as a base64 data URI on every captured frame. Output is byte-identical.

## Why

During capture, every frame with a visible video clip shipped that clip's frame (a multi-MB JPEG, base64
encoded) inside the CDP `evaluate` call. The capture page then parsed the string, fetched the data URL and
garbage-collected it on its main thread, frame after frame.

A Chrome trace of the capture browser (single worker, hyperframes-launch from the public launch-films repo,
1080p, BeginFrame capture) over the same 38 s window:

| | main (835e0c16e) | this PR |
|---|---:|---:|
| capture-page main thread per frame | 88 ms | 26 ms |
| of which handling the CDP message | 52 ms | 9 ms |
| frames captured in the window | 77 | 105 |

## Related work

Refs #1630, which turned the URL-served path off because the file server then read files synchronously
and had no Range support, so frame loads starved behind full video downloads and renders timed out. The
file server has since moved to streamed reads with Range support (`fileServer.ts`), and the extract stage
links extracted frames into the compiled dir, so the resolver #1630 left in place applies again.

## How

- `createRenderVideoFrameInjector` (`render/shared.ts`) is the one place the render builds its video frame
  injector, with the compiled-dir frame resolver. The orchestrator calls it; the stale #1630 comment goes.
- Frames outside the compiled dir still fall back to data URIs, as before. Distributed chunk renders keep
  their own injector for now: their frames live outside the served dir, so routing them needs a plan-layout
  change and comes as a follow-up PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test: the render injector hands the page `/__hyperframes_video_frames/...`, never a data URI.
      Fails with the resolver removed, passes with it.
- [x] main's file server answers `Range: bytes=100-199` with 206 and the exact bytes, and serves a frame
      through a symlinked frame dir (how the extract stage links frames).
- [x] Same output: main and this PR render hyperframes-launch to byte-identical MP4s (same md5).
- [ ] Export time, interleaved main/PR runs on the same machine (table below).

TABLE_PLACEHOLDER

title: fix(studio): dragging a keyframed layer from its middle moves the layer, not a path node
body:
## What a person sees

Select a layer whose position is keyframed, park the playhead on one of its keyframes, and drag the layer from its middle. Often the layer does not follow the pointer, then jumps on release to a spot 30 to 190 px from where it was dropped. Sometimes the edit lands on a different keyframe (the 3 s one when the playhead is at 2 s).

The press was landing on the motion path's keyframe node, not on the layer. Each node has a 14 px grab ring, and the path was drawn 30 composition px away from the layer whenever its CSS `translate` set an axis the tween does not animate. At 50% and 100% zoom, that ring covers the layer's middle. The node's own drag then wrote `y` without the translate (60 instead of 90), kept the old keyframe array, and showed only the node moving.

## The fix

- **The path is drawn where GSAP renders the layer.** `buildMotionPathGeometry` defaulted an axis the tween does not animate to 0. GSAP folds the CSS `translate` into that axis, so the default is now GSAP's live value, read with the same `readGsapPositionFromIframe` the layer drag uses as its base. The node at the playhead now sits exactly on the layer's anchor.
- **The node at the playhead is the layer.** A press on the node GSAP renders the layer at is handed to the selected layer's box (`pressSelectedLayer`). That starts the same move gesture, live preview and `commitValueAtPlayhead` write as a press on the layer, which matches the rule that an edit changes or adds the keyframe at the playhead.
- **Inside the layer's box, only a node's drawn dot is the node's.** A press on another node's wider grab ring, inside the selected layer's box, moves the layer. A press on the dot itself still drags that keyframe, as in After Effects. Outside the box, the whole ring stays the node's.
- **A move on the first or last keyframe of an eased tween changes that keyframe.** The playhead writer refused any keyframe tween eased as a whole, so dropping the layer on such a keyframe saved nothing. GSAP eases a keyframe run as a whole with `keyframes.ease || ease` (gsap 3.15, the keyframes branch of the Tween constructor) and renders the run at `ease(t)`. At 0% and 100% that is the keyframe's own time, so the writer now edits that keyframe in place and writes the ease back as the tween's own `ease`, the same curve; the rewrite used to drop it.
- **The hand-off falls back to the node.** The press goes to the layer only when the layer's box handles it (it calls `preventDefault`) and takes the pointer (not `pointer-events: none`, as while text is edited); otherwise the node drags as before. A layer press the box answers with its "can't move" notice now also counts as handled, so the notice is not followed by a node drag, and the box pauses its own updates only once the move really starts, so a refused press can no longer leave it frozen. Playback still pauses on that press, before the drag setup records which timelines are running, as any press on the canvas does; an arrow-key nudge now pauses before that snapshot too, so neither can restart a timeline the pause stopped. A selected node draws its dot 1.5x as large, and that larger dot is the node's (`dotRadius`, shared with `MotionPathNode`).
- **A timeline's default ease no longer lands on keyframed tweens.** GSAP never passes `defaults.ease` to a tween with keyframes (`_setKeyframeDefaults` skips `ease`), but the parser copied it in. Writing it back would have changed the whole curve, so the parser now matches GSAP.
- **An ease the file names by variable is written back as that variable.** The writer serialized every ease with `JSON.stringify`, so `ease: E` came back as the string `"__raw:E"` and the timeline threw on reload. Every ease the writer emits (adding, converting a flat tween, unrolling a loop) now goes through the same `valueToCode` its other values use, and a keyframes-level `ease`/`easeEach` that is a variable is kept by the parser instead of dropped.

Bounds:
- In a tween eased as a whole, a keyframe between the first and last is still refused, and so is adding a keyframe: the ease shows the layer at `ease(t)`, not at the clock time the lane draws those keyframes at. A follow-up PR gives "where GSAP actually is" one owner (array step times and the ease mapping) that the parser, the lane, the playhead park and the writer all read.
- Plain-list keyframes (`keyframes: { x: [..] }`) are still refused; they draw no nodes today.
- A press on the playhead node while the layer's move check is still pending does what a press on the layer does then: nothing yet.

Unchanged here: a drag of a node that is not at the playhead still writes through `update-keyframe`, which adds a newly animated channel to that one keyframe only. That gets its own PR stacked on this one.

## Evidence

Edit-accuracy bench on one box, `move-keys-px-r0-root-z{50,100,200}-{on,mid}`, with #4934's soft-reload fix applied (it is now on main and in this branch):

| tree | accurate | presses that landed on a node |
|---|---|---|
| base | 3/6 and 5/6 (two runs) | 4/6, every one failed |
| this branch, before the dot rule | 5/6 | 1/6 failed: `z200-mid` pressed the 2 s node's ring 7 px from the layer's middle, which the dot rule now gives to the layer |

Forced presses on `move-keys-px-r0-root-z100-on`, 3 runs each: on the base, a press on the playhead node fails every run (tracking, drop, reload and undo off by 60 px); on this branch both the node press and the layer-body press are accurate in every run.

Tests: `motionPathGeometry.test.ts`, `useMotionPathData.test.tsx`, `motionPathLayerNode.test.ts`, `MotionPathOverlay.layerPress.test.tsx`, `gsapValueAtPlayhead.test.ts`, `domEditOverlayStartGesture.blocked.test.ts`, `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`, and in parsers `gsapParserAcorn.full.test.ts`, `gsapWriter.acorn.test.ts` and `gsapWriter.varEase.test.ts`. With the source changes reverted, each of them fails. The parsers and studio-server suites and Studio's `hooks` and `components/editor` test directories pass. After merging current main, the changed test files pass 3 runs in a row and Studio typechecks clean.

The captures below are the bench's `move-keys-px-r0-root-z100-on` fixture in headless Chromium 152, playhead at 2 s on the layer's keyframe, the press forced onto the path node at the playhead, one frame per pointer step plus a cursor dot. Main often draws no motion path on load (#4957 fixes that), so both are loads where the path was drawn.

## Before

Current main. The playhead node sits 10 px above the layer's middle. Dragging it moves only the node inside the layer box; the layer stays where it was, and the bench fails tracking, drop, reload and undo.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/962fe60e-f0fe-4b0c-ae8f-694a27100e1e

## After

This branch on current main. The playhead node sits on the layer's middle, the same drag moves the layer with the node under the pointer, and every accuracy check passes.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f58c3cd-72c4-4f8c-b15d-2a618f83714e

title: fix(core): a seek onto a tween's start shows that tween, not an earlier tween's end
body:
## What

Seeking onto the exact time where a tween starts shows that tween's first value again, instead of an earlier tween's end value on the same property.

A layer with `from(x: -60)` over 0-2 s and a keyframed tween on `x` starting at 2 s showed the `from()` end at 2 s, not the first keyframe. In Studio this is what a nudge or a move on such a layer at the playhead looks like: the edit saves correctly, but the preview and a fresh load both draw the layer 35-50 px from where the file puts it.

## Why

Since #4911 both runtime seek paths re-render a seek silently by stepping to just below the target and back (`adapters/gsap.ts`, `init.ts`), so same-time `tl.set` steps apply in authored order. The seek itself has already left a tween that starts exactly at the target at local time 0. On the step down, a keyframed tween skips the render, because its own time stays clamped at 0, so its keyframe timeline never sees its start crossed. On the step back up that timeline skips too. The earlier sibling renders on both steps, so its end value wins the frame.

## How

- `rerenderGsapTimelineAt` keeps #4911's step from just below. Between the step down and the step back up, each keyframed tween that starts exactly at the target and plays forward (not paused, positive time scale, as GSAP itself requires) is moved across its own start, silently and alone: `render(2e-8)` then `render(-2e-8)` on that tween. The timeline's own step back up then renders it together with every sibling, in authored order, so a later same-time `set` still wins and an earlier one still loses. At a seek to 0 (under 1 ms) the re-render arrives from above, as on main, so siblings there keep GSAP's backward order. Nested timelines are searched only where the target falls inside them.
- Why 2e-8: GSAP treats a time under 1e-8 as 0, so 2e-8 moves the tween off its start and the step back down really crosses it. GSAP rounds a timeline's time to 1e-7, so the tween's own keyframe timeline does not move on the way up: nothing inside it starts, and no repeat of any duration GSAP can represent is crossed. The negative step is passed to that timeline as is, so it does see its start crossed.
- Three wider shapes were tried and dropped, each on a measured failure:
  - One forced `render(t, true, true)`. GSAP marks a tween active once it has rendered and never clears the mark, so a forced render redraws every such tween at its recorded start, including ones that start later (`style-5-prod`, `hdr-regression`).
  - Stepping the whole timeline just above the target first. That initialises tweens starting within the next millisecond, so an `overwrite: "auto"` tween killed the one before it, and it crossed a `repeatRefresh` boundary on the target.
  - Re-crossing the keyframed tween after the timeline's step back up. That made it win over a later same-time sibling (keyframes then `set(x: 42)` at the same time showed 5, not 42).
  - Re-crossing every tween that owns a timeline with a 1 ms, then 1 us, step. That reached a stagger's next target and a short `repeatRefresh` keyframed tween's repeats at sizes GSAP can represent, and it ignored paused and reversed children.
- The GSAP members this reads are typed locally in the adapter; a child that is not a GSAP animation is skipped. Both callers pass `getChildren` along with `totalTime`.
- `tl.call` fire counts are the same as main for every seek sequence measured with real GSAP, so the zero-duration-callback guard in `init.ts` is unchanged.
- Not fixed, and the same as main: a staggered tween, or a child timeline (not a tween) with a set at its own start, that starts exactly at the target still shows the earlier tween's end (plain seeking without any re-render shows it too); inside a repeating or yoyo timeline only the first iteration's starts are found.
- Known bound, accepted: the 2e-8 step goes through the keyframed tween's own ease, so a steep-start ease (for example `circ.out`) moves its keyframe timeline up to about 0.2 ms. A keyframe that short with `repeat` and `repeatRefresh` on relative values, inside such a tween starting exactly at the seek time, can have its repeats re-read. No film is expected to author that.

## Test plan

- [x] `adapters/gsap.steps.test.ts`, real GSAP. Fail on main: seeking onto a keyframed tween's start from 0, 1, 2, 2.5 and 3 s, and the same inside a nested timeline, seeking twice. #4911's 6 rows still pass.
- [x] Authored order at the seek time, seeking from 0, 1, 2, 2.5 and 3 s: keyframes then `set(x: 42)` shows 42 (fails with the re-cross after the step up); `set(x: 42)` then keyframes shows the first keyframe (fails on main, which shows 42).
- [x] Guards that pass on main and here, each failing with one of the dropped shapes: a tween that starts later stays put after a seek past the end (forced render); an `overwrite: "auto"` tween starting 0.5 ms after the target is not started, and a `repeatRefresh` tween keeps its value at a repeat boundary (step above the target); a stagger whose next target starts 0.1 us later with `overwrite: "auto"`, a reversed and a paused keyframed tween, and a 0.4 us `repeatRefresh` keyframed tween are left as GSAP renders them (re-crossing every owned timeline by 1 us).
- [x] gsap.steps 21, gsap 9 and init 208 tests pass, 3 runs each. The seek script passes; core's typecheck (including the runtime one), fallow audit, format, lint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [x] Producer regression on Linux, against their goldens: `hdr-regression` and `style-5-prod` pass with 0 failed frames (both failed with the forced render). Run on this head.
- [ ] Edit accuracy bench on Linux, every `*-fromto-*` case (120) and the nudge family, with #4889, #4934 and #4935: running.
- This PR's own edit accuracy gate runs main plus this PR only. There the playhead fromto cases still fail the keyframes check (the in-place keyframe edit is #4889), and 9 rotated root cases still drift after a drop (the undo and soft-reload re-read is #4934). This PR removes the drift that came from the seek re-render; it does not make those cases accurate on its own.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Size

About 100 changed lines in `packages/core`, most of them tests.

title: fix(studio): a resize saves through the route its press chose, as a move does
body:
## What changes for the user

Nothing visible in ordinary editing. A resize now saves through the same route (plain CSS or GSAP) its press chose, as a move already did, so a gesture can no longer draft one way and save the other.

## Why

Whether an edit writes plain CSS or GSAP was decided in eight places, each calling `gsapWritesPosition`, `gsapWritesBox` or `gsapWritesRotation` itself: the drag press, the rotate press, the move, group, resize and rotate commits, the property panel, and the panel's value readers. Those predicates read `_gsap.renderTransform`, which GSAP sets the first time anything touches the element's transform, including Studio's own mid-gesture writes. Move carried the press's answer into the commit, and rotate carried it when the press chose CSS; resize asked again at commit, so its answer could differ from the one its draft used. A GSAP-route rotation still checks again at commit (unchanged here; nothing found that makes that check disagree with its press).

## Change

- `editsPlainCss(el, gesture)` in `gsapRuntimeKeyframes.ts` is the one decision. The three predicates are no longer exported.
- The overlay passes the resize press's route into `onBoxSizeCommit`, as it already did for a move. A caller with no press (the panel, the host hook, the agent tool) gets the decision made once at the handler's entry, through the same function. `useDomGeometryCommit.commitBoxSize` takes the route as an optional last argument, so hosts keep working unchanged.
- The resize anchor still decides after its settle step, on purpose: the settle writes GSAP x/y, and the anchor saves what it wrote.

## Tests

`useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: a resize keeps the box route its press chose, both ways (CSS route on an element GSAP has since taken over; GSAP route on an element that now looks GSAP-free). Both rows fail on the base and pass with the change.

## Before

Real Studio on the bench fixtures, #4889 head 375d1cac: a plain CSS box and a GSAP-scaled box, corner-resized.

![Before: plain and GSAP-scaled resize on the base](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dfba9222-55a2-4bd2-a6a6-7358ee15418a)

## After

Same cases on this PR: identical results (plain: drop, reload, undo 0; GSAP-scaled: drop 0.19 px), as a behaviour-preserving change should give.

![After: same resizes, same results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b7b87409-1f85-49c7-93b6-615ba2c1ffcd)

Stacked on #4889 (`fix/studio-playhead-writer-carrier`).



Size note: 94 lines, under the 100-line floor; it is one root cause with its own review, captures and bench gate, and #4961 stacks on it, so folding it would re-run both.

title: motion-graphics: point the Builder at hyperframes-creative's motion-principles.md
body:
### Problem

`skills/motion-graphics` never references `skills/hyperframes-creative` (no mention in any file on `main`). As a result, `hyperframes-creative/references/motion-principles.md` is not on the motion-graphics read path, even though motion-graphics is the most motion-first workflow in the repo.

I checked whether its guardrails are covered elsewhere on that path (`SKILL.md`, `agents/director.md`, `agents/builder.md`, `references/builder-contract.md`, `references/motion-vocabulary.md`, plus the `SKILL.md` of `hyperframes`, `hyperframes-core` and `hyperframes-animation`). They mostly are not:

| motion-principles.md guardrail | Covered on the motion-graphics path? |
|---|---|
| Vary eases (≤2 tweens per scene with the same ease) | No |
| `.out` for entrances, `.in` for exits, `.inOut` for moves | No (only per-primitive examples in `motion-vocabulary.md`) |
| Vary duration (slowest scene ~3× the fastest) | No |
| Vary entrance direction (not always `y:30, opacity:0`) | No |
| Build / breathe / resolve scene structure | Partly (`categories/kinetic-type` only: Hook → Build → Punch → Resolve) |
| Stagger by importance, total stagger < 500ms | No |
| Exits faster than entrances | No |
| Offset the first tween 0.1–0.3s | No |

The only route to the file today is indirect (`hyperframes-animation/adapters/animate-text.md`, or the capability table in `hyperframes/SKILL.md`), so whether the Builder reads it depends on the agent's own initiative.

`hyperframes-creative/references/data-in-motion.md` has the same gap for the `charts` and `stat` categories.

### Proposed solution

A small docs-only change:

1. `skills/motion-graphics/agents/builder.md` — add a line under "Critical correctness" (or a new "Motion quality" heading): read `../hyperframes-creative/references/motion-principles.md` before writing the timeline.
2. `skills/motion-graphics/SKILL.md` Step 4 — add that file to the Builder's dispatch context list.
3. `skills/motion-graphics/categories/charts/module.md` and `categories/stat/module.md` — reference `../hyperframes-creative/references/data-in-motion.md`.

## Alternatives considered

Inlining a condensed version into `references/motion-vocabulary.md`. This avoids a cross-skill read but duplicates content that would drift from the original, so a link seems better.

Inlining a condensed version into `references/motion-vocabulary.md`. This avoids a cross-skill read but duplicates content that would drift from the original, so a link seems better.

### Additional context

While building short HTML motion pieces with an AI coding assistant (outside HyperFrames), I hit exactly the failure modes this file warns about: uniform easing, missing exits, flat timing. That is what led me to compare the motion-graphics read path against `motion-principles.md`. I have not measured the effect inside the motion-graphics workflow itself.

title: fix(studio): a host hook reloads its preview only the way the host says
body:
## What changes for the user

A host app embedding Studio's geometry commits (`useDomGeometryCommit`) must now pass `reloadPreview`. When a save cannot patch the preview in place, Studio calls the host's own reload; it no longer falls back to reloading the iframe's location behind the host's back.

## Why

The fallback (`iframe.contentWindow.location.reload()`) skipped the host's player refresh, so a host that forgot the option got a different, slower reload path that nothing exercised. A required option makes the one path explicit and fails at compile time instead.

No host in this repository omits it.

## Tests

`useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`: a type test that `reloadPreview` is required. It fails typecheck against the old optional option and passes now. The hook's existing 34 tests pass.

## Release note

Breaking for hosts of `useDomGeometryCommit` (exported from `@hyperframes/studio`): pass `reloadPreview`, your preview's own reload.

## No visible change

Type and wiring only; no screen changes.

Stacked on #4889 (`fix/studio-playhead-writer-carrier`).

title: fix(studio): dragging a keyframe's path node keeps the other keyframes where they were
body:
## What a person sees

Select a layer whose position is keyframed, and drag one of its motion-path nodes that the playhead is not on. The dragged keyframe lands right, but the keyframes after it move too. With a layer placed by a CSS `translate` and a tween that only animates `x`, dragging the 3 s node down 60 px also moves every later frame down.

## Why

A dropped keyframe node wrote `update-keyframe` with `x` and `y` on that one keyframe. When the tween did not animate `y` before, GSAP then starts `y` from its base at the tween's start, reaches the new value at that keyframe, and holds it afterwards. Every other keyframe now renders at a different `y`.

## The fix

The drop goes through the writer a layer drag uses (`commitValueAtPlayhead`), aimed at the dropped keyframe (`activeKeyframePct`). GSAP's live position is the backfill, so a channel the drop starts animating keeps its current value on every other keyframe. `commitNodeDrop` now owns how a dropped node is written:

- a keyframe through that writer;
- a keyframe with auto-keyframe off as a shift of the whole path, measured from the dragged step's own keyframe;
- a waypoint in place (unchanged).

What that writer path needed to get right for every node, not only the last:

- **The dropped keyframe is the one edited.** For array keyframes the writer works in the times GSAP actually reaches each step (`withExactStepTimes`), while a node or a lane diamond carries the parser's percentage. The writer now maps a selected keyframe by its index to its exact step time (`exactKeyframePct`), for the edit and for where it parks the playhead afterwards. The path spaces array nodes evenly, so each array node also carries its step and a drop selects the parsed keyframe at that step. Before, dropping the middle node of `[{x:60},{x:120},{x:180}]` added a fourth keyframe and left the dragged one where it was, and so did dropping the first node of `[{x:60,duration:2},{x:120,duration:1}]`.
- **An existing keyframe of a tween eased as a whole can still be dropped.** The writer refuses edits on such a tween where the ease would move the time an edit lands at. A dropped node or a selected keyframe names its keyframe by percentage, which the ease does not move, so editing that keyframe goes through, as `update-keyframe` did on main. Adding a keyframe, or editing an inner keyframe by playhead time, is still refused.
- **The nearest keyframe is the one edited.** Two steps can end under 1% apart (a 0.05 s pop step in a 10 s list parses to 50% and 50.5%). Picking a keyframe by percentage now takes the nearest within the match tolerance, not the first, so a drop on the pop step edits the pop step.
- **Array steps are timed where GSAP plays them.** GSAP plays array keyframes as steps on an inner timeline and stretches that timeline over the tween. `withExactStepTimes` divided step ends by the tween's duration, so `[{x:60},{x:120},{x:180}]` with `duration: 3` (three default 0.5 s steps) retimed to 16.7/33.3/50% and any playhead edit on it landed on the wrong keyframe. It now divides by the inner timeline's duration.
- **Rewriting an array loses nothing GSAP played.** The writer turns array keyframes into percentage keyframes, and in an array a step that leaves out a channel holds it, where a percentage keyframe would tween through. Each such step now gets the value it held: the step before's (after the edit), or for a channel a later step first animates, the start GSAP recorded for it. If GSAP has not played that step yet, the start is unknown and the edit is refused rather than guessed. Before, dropping the first node of `[{x:60,duration:1},{duration:1},{x:180,duration:1}]` to 97 played 138.5 at 2 s instead of holding 97. An array step the parser cannot read in full (a variable, a spread, or a flag such as `runBackwards: true`, which the parser used to drop silently) now makes the tween display-only, like any other dynamic tween; before, the rewrite deleted that step. Layer drags on the same tweens had both problems before this PR; this fixes them for both.
- **A step list the rewrite would change is refused, and the message names the cause.** A percentage keyframe cannot carry what some steps do, so the rewrite would retime a step's own `delay` (the tween ran a second early), run a step's `onComplete` once per keyframe, apply a relative value (`x: "-=40"`) or a `random()` again, or drop a value that comes from code. When any step has one of those, the drop is refused, with auto-keyframe on or off, nothing is written, and the toast says which: a step with its own delay; a step that runs code as it plays (`onComplete` and the like); a step with its own repeat, yoyo or stagger; a value that comes from code; a relative value; a `random()` value. Each ends with "Edit them in the Code tab." Layer drags rewrote such lists the same way on main and are refused the same way now. With auto-keyframe off (or an Alt-drag) the edit goes through the whole-path shift, which resize, rotation and the property panel also use; that shift now runs the same step check, so those edits on such a step list are refused too instead of rewritten. A group move checks every member's step list before its first write, so it refuses whole rather than moving some members. A step that animates nothing (a pause) keeps holding the step before it when a drop starts animating a new channel; a pause that opens the list holds the layer's resting value.

What a drag can still edit on a keyframe step list: steps with absolute values (numbers, colours, units such as `"50%"`, `filter: "blur(4px)"`, `clipPath`), steps with their own `duration` and `ease`, steps that leave a channel out (they hold it), and pause steps. Percentage keyframes and flat tweens are unchanged.
- **A drop the writer refuses says so.** The refusal goes through the same failure reporter a layer drag uses (`useGsapInteractionFailureTelemetry`): the same message, the `edit_blocked` event, labelled with what the drop did (move keyframe, move animation path, move waypoint), and the keyframe selection the drop made is put back, so the next resize or rotate does not write to it.

## Evidence

- `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts`: a drop on the 3 s node of `keyframes: [{ x: 60, duration: 2 }, { x: 120, duration: 1 }]` over a translate GSAP reads as `y: 30` writes `{ x: 60, y: 30 }` and `{ x: 150, y: 90 }`; with the backfill removed it fails. A drop on a tween another element shares rejects with the reason and writes nothing.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: with the middle of three equal steps selected (parsed at 50%), a drag writes `[60, 130, 180]`, and GSAP replaying the written file shows 130 at 2 s (to 0.01 px; the writer rounds percentages to 3 decimals).
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: on that `duration: 3` tween with the playhead at 2 s and nothing selected, a drag writes `[60, 130, 180]` and GSAP shows 130 at 2 s.
- `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts`: a drop on the first node of `[{x:60,duration:2},{x:120,duration:1}]` (drawn at 0%, parsed at 66.7%) edits that keyframe and keeps two. `motionPathGeometry.test.ts` and `gsapShared.test.ts` pin that array nodes carry their step.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: a plain array's path nodes read where the parser and the lane put them, though GSAP writes a default duration into every step.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: dropping the first keyframe of that hold array to 97, GSAP replaying the written file shows 97 at 2 s; on `[{x:60},{x:120,y:50}]`, `y` stays 0 through the first step.
- `gsapParserAcorn.full.test.ts`: an array with a variable, a spread or a `runBackwards: true` step parses as unresolved keyframes.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.test.ts`: on a tween eased as a whole, an edit at a percentage with no keyframe there is still refused.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: `keyframes: [{ x: 60, duration: 1, runBackwards: true }, { x: 180, duration: 1 }]` plays x 60, 45, 30, 15, 0 over its first second in GSAP. On main the parser dropped the flag, and a drop at 1.5 s wrote a file that plays 0, 15, 30, 45, 60 there, with nothing said. Now the drop is refused and nothing is written; the test fails with main's parser.
- `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts`: with auto-keyframe off, dropping the middle node of steps `[4, 1, 1]` s at x 157 shifts the path to `[97, 157, 217]`. With it on, a drop on the first node of `[{x:60,duration:2},{x:120,duration:1}]` parks the playhead at that step's exact end, 2 s.
- `MotionPathOverlay.layerPress.test.tsx`: a refused node drop shows the blocked message. `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts` also checks it leaves no keyframe selected.

- `gsapWholePropertyOffsetCommit.test.ts`: the whole-path shift refuses a step list holding `"+=40"`, an `onComplete` or `random(0, 90)`, and a layer's list with a step delay, writing nothing; `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts` refuses the step-delay drop with auto-keyframe on and off. These fail on the previous head.
- `useGsapAwareEditing.groupPlan.test.tsx`: with auto-keyframe off, a three-layer group move where one layer's step list has a step delay is refused whole, with nothing written; before, the first layer was written and the move then failed.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.test.ts`: one case per blocked step feature (delay, `onComplete`, `onInterrupt`, `repeat`, a value from code, `-=40`, `random(0, 300)`, `blur(random(1, 9)px)`) refuses with its own reason and message; absolute values and colours still rewrite; a pause step holds the dropped value of a channel the drop starts animating.
- `gsapValueAtPlayhead.realGsap.test.ts`: dropping node 1 of `[{ duration: 1 }, { x: 60, duration: 1 }, { x: 180, duration: 1 }]` to (37, 11), GSAP replaying the written file shows y 0 through the opening pause and 11 at 2 s.
- `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts`: dropping the 50% node of percentage keyframes 0/50/100 (x 0/100/200) with `ease: "power1.inOut"` to x 150 writes `[0, 150, 200]`; dropping the 0.05 s step of `[5 s x 0, 0.05 s x 100, 4.95 s x 100]` to x 150 writes `[0, 150, 100]`. `gsapValueAtPlayhead.test.ts` pins both in the planner, and that a step leaving out a channel whose GSAP start is unknown is refused.
- `motionPathCommit.nodeDrop.test.ts`: a drop on a list with step delays rejects with the delay message and writes nothing; the drop's undo label names what it moved.
- The GSAP config keys (timing, callbacks, extras) now live once in `gsapConstants.ts`; both parsers and the writer read them there instead of keeping three copies.

Each of these fails without the change. Typecheck is clean and the writer and motion-path test files pass three runs in a row.

Not changed here, and owned by a follow-up PR that gives "where GSAP actually is" one function the parser, path, lane, park and writer all read:
- For arrays without durations the parser places keyframe i at i/(n-1), while GSAP reaches it at its step end, (i+1)/n. The writer's index map makes drops edit the right keyframe anyway.
- For arrays whose steps state their durations, the path still draws nodes at even percentages while the parser and lane use the step ends; drops are right (by step), but clicking such a node parks the playhead at the even percentage, and so does the park right after a drop until the writer's own park replaces it.
- With auto-keyframe off, a plain array is shifted at the parser's i/(n-1) times, which retimes it, and a step with no value for a channel gets `0 + delta` (pre-existing, unchanged here).
- Two refusals are broader than they need to be: a base64 data URI ending in `+/=` reads as a relative value, and a plain object in a step (such as `motionPath: { path: [] }`) is described as a value from code. Both refuse rather than corrupt.
- Steps less than 0.05% apart round to the same parsed percentage, so a drop there still edits the first of them. Carrying the dropped step's index into the writer closes it.
- Step lists with delays, callbacks, repeat/yoyo/stagger, relative, random or computed values are refused, not edited. Editing them in place (only the dropped step's keys, a new channel added to every non-pause step) keeps all of those and is a follow-up.

The captures below are the bench's `move-keys-px-r0-root-z100-mid` fixture (`keyframes: [{ x: 60, width: 280, duration: 2 }, { x: 120, width: 320, duration: 1 }]`) in headless Chromium 152, playhead at 1 s, the press forced onto the 2 s keyframe's path node and dragged, one frame per pointer step plus a cursor dot; each ends on the 3 s frame. Before is current main; After is this branch on main.
