title: test(studio): pin what the one DOM edit writer saves, records and reloads
fix(core): a GSAP call added after the first seek fires once, not twice
body:
## What

A GSAP `tl.call` (or any zero-duration tween with a callback) that a composition adds to its timeline after the runtime's first seek now fires once when the playhead passes it. Before, it fired twice: once when a seek landed on it, and again on the next forward seek or frame.

## Why

After an eventful seek, the runtime re-renders the timeline silently from just below the target (`rerenderGsapTimelineAt`, #4911) so same-time `tl.set` steps land on their frame. That silent render moves a zero-duration callback's internal state, and GSAP then fires the callback again on the next forward render. So the seek path skips the re-render when the timeline holds a zero-duration callback (`hasZeroDurationCallbackTween`).

That answer was cached per timeline on the first seek (since #2037). A timeline seeked before its `tl.call` existed was cached as "no callbacks" forever, the re-render kept running, and the call fired twice.

## Related work

Found during review of #4942, but not caused by it: the stale cache is on main.

## How

`init.ts`: the cache is gone; `hasZeroDurationCallbackTween` reads the timeline's current children on every eventful seek. The answer is never stale, in either direction: a callback added after the first seek is seen, and so is one removed.

Cost: the check is one `getChildren(true, true, true)` walk per eventful seek (each playback and render frame) that stops at the first zero-duration callback. Measured with real GSAP on a heavily loaded Linux box: about 0.03 ms at 200 children, 0.18 ms at 2,000 and 1.1 ms at 10,000. Real films author a few hundred tween calls.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `init.test.ts`, new case with real GSAP: seek a timeline, then add `tl.call` at 2 s, seek to 2 s, then to 3 s. The call must fire exactly once. On main it fires twice; with the fix once, 3 runs in a row.
- Core runtime suite: 66 files, 1744 tests pass. `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, the comment checks and the dead-code audit pass.

title: fix(cli): wait for consent navigation before cataloging assets
body:
## What

After the cookie-consent dismissal clicks in `captureScrollScreenshots`, wait for the page to become ready again before any further DOM reads, and apply the same settle before the asset-catalog step.

New `waitForPageReady(page)` helper (in `navigateForCapture.ts`): `waitForNetworkIdle({ idleTime: 500, timeout: 15_000 })` → a bounded `document.readyState` poll (~15 s cap) → a second idle wait if a load was waited out. It is used in two places:

- `screenshotCapture.ts`: after the consent/dismiss click sweep (+ a 400 ms beat so a click-scheduled reload can start), before the overlay-hiding sweep and the `scrollHeight` probe.
- `coreExtractionPhase.ts`: immediately before `Cataloging assets...` — the same boundary where the reporter verified `waitForNetworkIdle` fixes the symptom.

## Why

A consent click can reload the page (some CMPs reload once consent is stored). The previous flow read the DOM without waiting on the navigation: the overlay sweep and `scrollHeight` probe ran against a torn-down or still-parsing document, scroll screenshots degraded, and `catalogAssets` could observe an empty body — `0 assets cataloged`, `0 scroll screenshots`, occasional `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'innerHTML')`. Later HTML extraction sees the recovered page, which makes the race hard to spot.

Fixes #4923.

## Related work

- Issue: #4923 (reporter verified a `waitForNetworkIdle` guard before the catalog step resolves the 0-assets failure for their site; this keeps that guard and extends it to the committed-but-still-parsing case).

## How

Two subtleties drove the design, both verified against `puppeteer-core@25.11.0` and a real Chromium:

- `waitForNetworkIdle` counts a request as in-flight only until its **response headers** arrive, so it resolves while a reloaded document is still streaming/parsing. The `readyState` poll covers that window.
- `waitForNavigation` deadlocks when armed **after** a navigation commits (its lifecycle watcher needs `framenavigated`), so it cannot guard the catalog boundary where a reload may already be in flight. The `readyState` poll works regardless of arm timing; an evaluate that throws mid-context-swap is treated as still loading.

A click that does not navigate costs one `readyState` evaluate beyond the existing idle wait — no stall.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `bunx vitest run src/capture` — 358 tests pass, including new coverage: a `waitForPageReady` unit suite (idle fast path, still-parsing poll, destroyed-context poll, bounded cap) and a `captureScrollScreenshots` reload suite (idle-out reload, sweep on the settled document, no stall without navigation, still-parsing document).
- Sabotage check: all 4 new `consent-click page reload (#4923)` tests fail on the pre-fix `screenshotCapture.ts` and pass with the fix.
- Real-browser repro (system Chromium + a local page whose consent button schedules `location.reload()` with a slowly-streamed post-consent response): pre-fix `screenshots=2 catalogImgs=0`, post-fix `screenshots=10 catalogImgs=20`.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `comment-ratchet`, `check-comment-citations`, and the lefthook `fallow` audit all pass.
- Note: two unrelated failures exist in the full CLI suite on this environment — `src/commands/history.test.ts` (also fails on clean upstream) and `motion-signature.browser.chromium.test.ts` (bundled headless-shell is an x86 binary on this ARM host; system Chromium launches fine). Neither touches the capture path.

AI-assisted. I wrote and verified this change.

title: perf(studio): a drag or resize moves the selection chrome without re-laying out Studio
body:
## What

Dragging an element on the Studio canvas no longer re-lays out Studio's page on every pointer move (an open crop preset bar still moves by left/top), and resizing one no longer re-renders the whole canvas overlay. The selection box, its corner dots, the rotate handle, the crop frame and the crop preset bar follow the gesture from CSS variables written on one element. A move costs that one style write. A resize also re-lays out the box and redraws the crop UI, because their size changes.

## Why

The manual-edit bench scores a drag as not smooth when any frame does more than 8 ms of main-thread work. Move and resize frames cost about 1.3 ms more than rotate frames, whose chrome stays still. Traces put the difference in the selection chrome. Each move set the overlay's React state, which re-rendered `DomEditOverlay` and rewrote left, top and size on about 14 chrome nodes. Studio then restyled, re-laid out and repainted its document, and the re-layout also re-ran an IntersectionObserver in the sidebar. A quiet-runner experiment that froze the chrome during drags took the resize median frame from 3.63 to 2.33 ms and move from 3.39 to 2.11 ms. Re-rendering the overlay with unchanged geometry cost only about 0.2 ms, so the cost is the DOM churn, not React itself. Putting the chrome on its own compositing layer saved only 0.16 ms.

## Related work

Refs the manual-edit bench "not smooth" cause (move and resize; crop and nudge share the overlay). Stacked on #4889. The other half of this cause, the paused preview loop, is #4938.

## How

- `selectionChromeVars` is the one owner of "overlay rect to chrome geometry": five custom properties (`--hf-sel-x/y/w/h/angle`) on a `display: contents` wrapper around the chrome. The plane rotates with `rotate(var(--hf-sel-angle))` about the box centre. The box, dots and rotate handle position themselves by `transform` from those variables. A move changes only transforms, which needs no layout; the one exception is an open crop preset bar, which follows by left/top to keep its top clamp.
- `useDomEditOverlayRects` gains `previewOverlayRect`, a gesture's per-move rect. It writes the variables on that wrapper and publishes a draft without setting React state. `setOverlayRect` (the frame loop's measured rect, which resumes at release) commits state as before. When a draft was showing, it also rewrites the variables, because React only patches what changed since its last render and a draft may have moved a value React thinks is current.
- The variables sit on a `display: contents` wrapper shared by the selection plane and the crop frame. The crop frame offsets itself by the variables' change since its last render, so a move re-renders nothing and lays out nothing. The crop preset bar, when open, moves by the same change and keeps its top clamp. The crop UI re-renders from the gesture's draft only when a resize changes the size.
- A resize still re-lays out the box and the crop UI, because their size changes. Drawing the crop UI from proportional CSS would remove that too; it is left for a follow-up once the gate shows whether resize needs it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `useDomEditOverlayRects.test.tsx` pins three things: a preview moves the chrome's variables with no render of the overlay; a gesture that settles on the already committed rect puts the variables back; the draft reaches subscribers until the next commit. Resize and drag moves call `previewOverlayRect` and never `setOverlayRect` (`anchoredResizeCommitFeedsOffset`, `shiftDragAxisLock`), which fails on the base. The Studio suite passes on a remote box (653 files). The two files that time out there, `useDomEditSession` and `PropertyPanel`, time out on the base too.
- [x] Manual testing performed: quiet-runner drag-frames A/B (Studio drag frames workflow, 12 cases per family x 5 runs, base #4889 head and this head dispatched together):

| Family | Median per-frame work, ms | Case-runs not smooth (of 60) |
|---|---|---|
| move | 3.50 -> 2.53 | 20 -> 11 |
| resize | 3.70 -> 3.31 | 22 -> 13 |
| crop | 2.79 -> 2.75 | 12 -> 12 |
| rotate (control) | 2.21 -> 2.11 | 14 -> 9 |

Those runners were noisier than earlier today (the same base scored 8 resize misses earlier), so read the medians. For scale, a build that froze the chrome during drags reached 2.33 ms for resize and 2.11 ms for move.
- [ ] Full edit-accuracy grid: results to follow.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Before

Main-thread work per frame during one drag, median of 5 quiet runs, #4889 head.

![Before: move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8b8c5c7c-2e56-4a2a-b503-43f66990a990)
![Before: resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e58d9a1e-b574-4176-9ef7-a9a4138c831c)

## After

The same cases on this head.

![After: move](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/849140bb-d19e-439d-bad2-4ca21a1f37d8)
![After: resize](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46f342f6-a738-4ebe-890e-dcd1e58886a4)

title: feat(studio,cli): add an Edit with Framey button and `hyperframes open` for HyperFrames Studio
body: ## What Point people from the CLI and the Studio preview to **HyperFrames Studio**, the desktop app (b249 is downloadable today at hyperframes.dev/studio/download). **Studio header — "Edit with Framey"** - A ghost button with Framey, the app's cursor mascot: the eye follows the pointer, a small wiggle on hover, a flight towards the app while it opens. All motion is off under reduced motion. - A press shows a **Meet Framey** card (chat to change anything, draw on a frame, watch me act out each edit) with **Get HyperFrames Studio** → the download. - Shown only where the preview server answers `GET /api/open-in-desktop` with `available: true` (macOS). The desktop app's embedded Studio has no such route, so the button never appears inside the app. - Framey's colours are tokens in `theme.css` (`--color-framey`, `--color-framey-ink`). **CLI** - `hyperframes open [dir]` hands the project folder to the app with `open -b` (released app, then Canary). Run by Claude Code or Codex it leaves `.hyperframes/agent-handoff.json` (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` / `CODEX_THREAD_ID`) so the app's next chat can pick up that conversation. Exits 1 whenever nothing opened; `--json` answers in JSON for a bad directory too. - `render` and `preview` print one line about the app. Nothing for a `--quality draft` render, a batch row, or a run inside the app (`HYPERFRAMES_DESKTOP_PROJECT`). ## One gate until the app opens handed-over folders The app learns to open a handed-over folder in hyperframes-internal#2601 (approved, not released). Until then **`HANDOFF_READY = false`** in `packages/cli/src/utils/desktopApp.ts` — the only copy: - `openInDesktop` returns `handoff-unavailable`: nothing opens and nothing is written, so `hyperframes open` prints the download line and exits 1, and no hand-off file can wait for a later release. - `GET /api/open-in-desktop` reports `handoff: false`; Studio's button reads it and only shows the Meet Framey card (no POST). - render/preview print the download line. Flipping it to `true` after that release makes the button open the project in the app and prints `Edit it with Framey: hyperframes open .` for people who have the app. Tests drive that live path through a `ready` option, so CI covers it today. **POST guard:** `POST /api/open-in-desktop` answers only Studio's own same-origin request (loopback Host via `identityAllowed`, `Origin` equal to `http://`, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when present). A cross-site POST and a rebound-host POST both get 403 (`server/desktopRoutes.test.ts`). ## Before Header today (0.8.111), light and dark: ## After Header with Edit with Framey, and the Meet Framey card a press opens, light and dark: ## Testing - `desktopApp.test.ts` (16): gated path writes nothing; live path opens, falls back to Canary, tells `not-installed` from `open-failed`, skips non-macOS, still opens a read-only project with nothing handed over; hints for gated / missing / installed / in-app. Path-portable for Windows. - `desktopRoutes.test.ts` (5): GET flags; cross-site and rebound-host POST → 403 and nothing opened; gated POST answers with the download; live POST opens this server's project. - `render/execute.test.ts`: the hint is skipped for a draft and for a batch row (`wantsDesktopHint`, `batchRowRenderOptions`). - Studio `OpenInDesktopButton.dom.test.tsx` (5, no skips): hidden without the route or off macOS; gated press shows the card and sends no POST; live press opens and toasts; live press with the app missing shows the card. - The load smoke mocks the route. Full CLI suite: 288 files pass; `fileWatcher.atomic` fails the same way on `main`. - By hand: Studio served by this branch's CLI at 1440×900 in both themes (captures above); the card fits with a one-line footer; no POST is sent while gated.

title: feat(skills): open Studio before every final render, and pitch the desktop app as the chat way to edit
body:
## What

Two changes to how the skills bring users to Studio and the desktop app.

**1. Studio opens before every final render, in every mode.** Users who only ask for a video never saw Studio: autonomous runs asked "preview first, or render?", and a "you decide" answer rendered. The final look now opens the Studio preview, then asks "render now, or what changes?". Opening it asks nothing, so it also holds when the user said not to ask. This touches the router § 6, `review-loop.md` § 4, `brief-contract.md`, and motion-graphics, faceless-explainer, product-launch-video, pr-to-video, music-to-video and general-video. talking-head-recut, embedded-captions and slideshow are unchanged.

**2. `/hyperframes` § 6 pitches the desktop app accurately.** The Studio preview already edits and saves. The app adds editing by chat with Framey, drawing on a frame, and Framey acting out each edit. The agent presents the app as the better way to keep editing, never as the only way. It always calls it "the HyperFrames desktop app", never "Studio", so the user doesn't mistake it for the preview. It mentions the app twice:
- when it opens the final Studio preview, it points to **Edit with Framey** — only when `preview` printed its `Desktop` line, so never where the button isn't there;
- after the delivery render, it passes on the render's desktop-app line: it offers to run `hyperframes open`, or gives the download link.

A direct "render this project" request stays only that: no preview first. The preview stays running after the render, and the agent says how to stop it. `/hyperframes-cli` documents `hyperframes open`.

## Depends on

Land after #4999 is released: the agent only mentions what `preview` and `render` print, so an older CLI just means it says nothing about the app.


#4951 and #4999 — the Studio button, `hyperframes open`, and the line `render` / `preview` print. On a machine without the app, that line is the download link.

## Verified (real `claude -p` sessions, fresh sandboxes, branch skills + CLI)

| Prompt (from public tutorials) | Studio opened, before | After |
|---|---|---|
| "Create an 8-second landscape video explaining the health benefits of sleep…" | no | yes, before render |
| "Make a dynamic 15-second motion graphics video… Go all out." (answered "you decide") | no | yes, before render |
| 12-second spec ending "Proceed to the end without asking questions." | no | yes, before render |
| "Create a 25-second product launch video from https://hyperframes.heygen.com…" | yes | yes |
| `/hyperframes` Brewly logo sting (guided) | when asked | without being asked |

In every run the agent said the user can edit right in Studio, named Edit with Framey for the desktop app, and passed on the render's line after the render. With the released Mac app installed, the agent offered `hyperframes open`; it ran it, the app opened the project, and Framey picked up the Claude Code conversation.

title: test(studio): the edit accuracy bench uses the port its server bound
body:
## What

The edit accuracy bench failed a case whenever its Studio port was busy. `startServer` (edit-accuracy `case.mjs`) asks the CLI for `--port N`; when another process holds N, the CLI binds the next free port and announces it, and the bench then threw `studio moved from port N to N+1`, so the case scored as an error without running. A port that something else was serving on failed the same way earlier (`port N is already serving`).

`startServer` now returns `{ child, port }` with the port the CLI announced and answers on, and `runOne` (`run.mjs`) opens Studio at that port. The asked-for port is only a starting point.

## Why

On a shared bench machine, three rotate cases errored this way in one full run while another process held one job's port; each passed 3 of 3 when rerun alone. A case's verdict must not depend on what else is listening.

## Related work

Refs the manual-edit bench work (#4760 added the bench).

## How

The CLI binds with a retry on `EADDRINUSE` and only then prints `http://localhost:<port>`, so the announced port is the one this server holds. The bench waits for that announcement and for `/api/projects` to answer on that port, as before. The "already serving" pre-check and the "moved" throw go, since both treated a busy port as a failure.

## Test plan

- Bench harness only; nothing in Studio or the player changes.
- `server.test.mjs` (new): a stand-in CLI binds a port the OS picks, not the one asked for, and announces it. With the old `startServer` it fails with `studio moved from port 1 to <n>`; with this change it passes 3 of 3, and it removes its temp dir.
- Real bench, one case (`move-none-px-r0-root-z100`, `--jobs 1 --port 47612`) while another HTTP server held 47612: before, `ERROR studio moved from port 47612 to 47613` in 1.1 s; after, accurate in 3 of 3 runs (one run flagged for smoothness only, on a loaded machine).

## Before

Main's harness, one real case, while another HTTP server holds the asked-for port: the case errors without running.

![Before: the case errors with studio moved from port 47612 to 47613](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/336be85e-78a9-4a4b-a37d-8f997f5d941d)

## After

This PR's harness, same held port, three runs: Studio starts on the next port and the case is measured and accurate each time.

![After: three runs measured, no error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cc1db382-5403-4c54-9e8a-1c8b6f89b9a5)

## Size

Two functions in the bench harness and one test. It ships alone: it fixes a flake in the harness every bench run uses, and no open PR touches these lines.

title: feat(studio): export useThumbnailStill for a host's own pictures
body: ## What Exports `useThumbnailStill(url, projectId, { sessionEpoch, priority })` from `@hyperframes/studio`: one server-rendered still for a host's own picture (a chat card, a list row), fetched through the shared thumbnail scheduler. Returns `{ status: "ready", url }` once the still has loaded, `{ status: "failed" }` if it cannot load (so a host can fall back), and `{ status: "loading" }` otherwise; a `null` url asks for nothing and reads as loading. ## Why A host that draws its own stills with a plain `` on the preview origin bypasses the scheduler's budget. Browsers allow about six HTTP/1.1 connections per host, and the preview, its data routes and every thumbnail share that origin. A burst of host-drawn stills held behind a slow render can starve the preview's own document request: after an undo, a preview waited about 36 s for its first byte while seven such stills were pending. The scheduler already caps composition fetches and aborts them while a preview reloads; the hook lets a host get the same behaviour for its own pictures instead of reimplementing it. ## How A thin hook over `compositionThumbnailRequest` and `useThumbnailLease`, both already in the package. No scheduler change, no new request kind. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests (`useThumbnailStill.test.ts`, 5 tests, 3 runs), importing the hook by package name so a dropped export fails them: ready with the object URL once loaded; asks for nothing without a url; says failed when the still cannot load; returns the same object while nothing changes; holds the fetch while a preview reloads and runs it after. - [x] `tsc --noEmit` and oxlint/oxfmt clean on the changed files. - [ ] Documentation: none, the export carries a doc comment. ## Before HyperFrames Desktop at main (Studio 0.8.114), a run that changed six scenes, then a write to `index.html` that reloads the preview. The six card stills are plain `` requests on the preview's server and hold its connections; the reload's preview document waits behind them: 13.2 s from the reload's write to its answer. ![Before: preview waits 13.2 s behind six card stills](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ad10ab5-126e-4b7f-91b9-791504b4f0bf) ![Before: the six cards](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6ac73220-df14-4d95-b36b-aca17f3e7444) ## After The same walk with the cards' stills through `useThumbnailStill` (Studio 0.8.114 plus this PR). Two stills are in flight when the reload starts; the scheduler aborts them, the preview document answers 103 ms after it is sent (393 ms after the reload's write), and the stills then load two at a time. ![After: preview in 393 ms, stills held and aborted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7210e5c5-0ea7-44d7-8637-110b7abdc514) ![After: the same six cards, all stills loaded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/282fd6ec-558a-47b9-88fa-5e1ccf8d708d) Measured with Chrome DevTools network events in a Playwright walk on the devbox (Xvfb), two runs each: Before 12.1 s and 13.2 s, After 113 ms and 103 ms from the preview request to its response.

title: ci: a test-only change under studio or player needs no captures
body:
## What

The Studio and player captures check (`scripts/check-pr-captures.mjs`) asked for Before and After screenshots on PRs that only change tests under `packages/studio` or `packages/player`. It already skipped markdown there as "docs, not behaviour"; tests are the same kind of file. Paths under a `tests/` or `__tests__/` directory and files named `*.test.*` or `*.spec.*` are no longer watched, so a test-only diff passes with nothing to show, and a test file no longer spends the "No visible change" line budget.

## Why

#4953 changes only the edit accuracy bench harness (`packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/`). The check counted its 44 lines as a Studio change and failed it, although nothing a user sees changes.

## Related work

Refs #4953.

## How

One test-path pattern next to `DOC_FILE`, applied in `isWatched`, the single filter every diffed path goes through (`parseNumstat`). The old `TEST_FILE` pattern only exempted `*.test|spec.[jt]sx?` from the visual-file rule (it missed `.mjs` and the `tests/` tree); it goes, since a test path never reaches that rule now. The existing case that passed a `.test.tsx` straight to `evaluate` now goes through `parseNumstat`, as real runs do.

## Test plan

- New case "test files under a watched package need no capture": a bench `.mjs` under `tests/`, a `.spec.tsx` and a `.test.ts` are filtered out and an empty body passes. Fails on main (all four files kept), passes here.
- `node --test scripts/check-pr-captures.test.mjs`: 75 pass, 0 fail, 3 runs in a row.
- The script against #4953's real diff with an empty body: main asks for Before and After; this branch passes.

## No visible change

CI script only.

## Size

One pattern and one test case.

title: fix(studio): the motion path draws on every load, not only when the layer's node is the frame's own
body:
## What a person sees

Three things on the motion path of a selected keyframed layer.

1. Select a layer that moves on keyframes. On many loads the motion path (the dashed line with a dot per keyframe) never appears, so the path cannot be seen, dragged or added to, until something reloads the preview.
2. When a keyframe also changes the layer's width or height, the path's nodes are drawn where the layer's centre would be at its current size, not at that keyframe's size. So the path slides around while you scrub, and a node can sit over the middle of the layer. A layer centred with `translate: -50% -50%` or `xPercent/yPercent: -50` had its whole path drawn half a width right and half a height down, on its bottom-right corner.
3. Pressing the middle of the selected layer to drag it can grab one of those nodes instead, so the drag moves a keyframe rather than the layer (the edit-accuracy bench's `move-keys-px-*-mid` cases). The path also showed no point for where GSAP starts a step list, so its first segment was missing.

## Why

**Path missing on load.** The path's data hook looks the selected layer up in the preview frame and checks it with `node instanceof frame.contentWindow.HTMLElement`. In the Studio preview the body's nodes often carry the editor window's prototypes rather than the frame's own; core's `runtime/domRealm.ts` documents this and owns the realm-free answer. The check then returns false for the layer that is plainly there, the path never gets its anchor point (`home`), and the overlay draws nothing. No error is logged.

Seen on the edit-accuracy bench with temporary logging in the overlay: the frame tick found the layer in the preview's own document (`target=true`, same document), and the check still said no (`live=false`, prototype `HTMLDivElement` from the other window). That happened in every run of `move-keys-px-r0-root-z100-on`, on the base and on #4941 alike.

The same check, a node tested against its document window's own `HTMLElement`, sat in eight more places, each failing the same silent way on those loads:

- `manualEditsSeekReapply.ts`: the studio-edited elements reapplied after a seek;
- `studioMotion.ts` (four sites): finding, restoring and rebuilding studio motion targets;
- `timelineEditingHelpers.ts`: the timeline z-index commit;
- `manualOffsetDrag.ts`: the frame element lookup;
- `webmcp/webmcpTestUtils.ts`: the test helper that fetches a preview element;
- `hooks/gsapShared.ts`: the selector written into the file when a keyframe or path is authored read ancestor ids only from editor-realm nodes, so on frame-realm loads it wrote a fragile `body:nth-child(...)` chain instead of `#scene > div:nth-child(2)`;
- `player/lib/timelineGroupInfo.ts`: the audio group observer never counted a group element the preview added or removed, so the timeline kept showing a stale label;
- `canvasContextMenuZOrder.ts`: the z-order menu's sibling list (its node-type fallback already made it safe; the window check is gone so the guard below holds).

## The fix

**Path missing on load.** Every one of them now uses core's `@hyperframes/core/runtime/dom-realm` predicates, which ask what a node is rather than which window built it; `isPreviewHtmlElement` and the hand-rolled `isHTMLElement` are gone. `noWindowBoundDomChecks.test.ts` scans Studio's sources and fails on any DOM interface read off an object (`x.HTMLElement`, `x!.Element`, `(x as T).Node`, `x["HTMLElement"]`, across a line break too), so a new window-bound check cannot land. A bare `instanceof HTMLElement` is still legitimate for Studio's own chrome, so behavioural tests cover the preview paths instead. The window gates the old constructor needed are gone.

**Nodes where the layer is.** The path's anchor (`elementHome`, now in `motionPathHome.ts`) is where the layer sits when GSAP's `x`/`y` are 0, so it follows GSAP's own transform parse. Once GSAP has parsed the layer, the percent comes from its cache (`el._gsap`), and a CSS `translate` still on the layer (a drag's preview offset) composes on top. Before GSAP has parsed it (create mode on a layer with no motion yet), the anchor sums the layer's computed `translate` and its own `transform` translate, as GSAP's parse does, and applies GSAP's fold rule: minus half the size becomes `xPercent/yPercent: -50` and stays, and the rest goes into `x`, which the new path sets. So a path created on a layer centred with `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` (inline or from a stylesheet) or `translate: -50% -50%` ends where you click; main ended it half a width left and half a height up. A GSAP cache from a fade alone holds no transform yet, so it counts as not parsed. The anchor never asks GSAP: asking makes GSAP parse the transform, which moves a plain CSS `translate` (what Studio writes when it moves a layer without GSAP) into `transform` and clears `translate`, so the next plain move counts the offset twice. Each node is drawn at the layer's centre with the width and height that keyframe sets (`nodeCentre`): a size change moves the centre by half of it from a set `left`/`top`, by minus half from a set `right`/`bottom` (read as `auto` through `computedStyleMap`), plus the percent share, so a `-50%` layer's centre stays put. The path stays put while you scrub, and the hook redraws when only a keyframe's size, the layer's size or GSAP's start changes. A layer in normal flow (flex, grid, `margin: auto`) keeps main's placement with no size shift, since layout may centre it. Adding a keyframe on the line interpolates the stored offsets, not the drawn centres.

**GSAP's start.** A step list (and a percentage list whose first key is past 0%) tweens its first step from where GSAP started the layer. That start is read from GSAP's parsed tween, each channel from the child tween that animates it (GSAP runs a percentage list as one child per property), and drawn as a small passive ring with the first segment of the line; it takes no press. It is skipped when it equals the first keyframe.

**A press inside the selected layer moves the layer; a handle keeps its own press.** A press on a node or on the path's line goes to the topmost editor control under the pointer, the path itself skipped, when that control is part of the selection's chrome: a crop, resize or rotate handle, or the selection box. Other overlay elements, such as another layer's off-canvas marker, do not take it, so a node over one still drags. So a drag from the layer's middle moves it, as #4941 promised, and a crop handle under a node still crops. The node GSAP renders the layer at is the layer anywhere. Where no control is under the pointer the node keeps its press, and if the control starts no gesture the node keeps it too. The selection chrome's wrapper is marked `data-dom-edit-chrome`; with the selection box and the crop frame, that is what the lookup accepts. A press on the path's line inside the box also moves the layer, and hovering the line there shows the layer's move cursor and no add ghost. Inside a large layer, its nodes are then dragged from the lane or after moving the playhead so the layer is elsewhere.

## Evidence

- `useMotionPathData.test.tsx`: with the frame window's `HTMLElement` a different class from the one that built the layer's node, the path's anchor is set. With the old frame-window check, it stays null. (happy-dom gives an iframe the outer window's own constructors, so a node from the outer document cannot stand in for the real split; replacing the frame's constructor is what makes the old check fail.)
- `gsapShared.writeTarget.test.ts`: with frame-built nodes, the written selector anchors on `#scene`. With the old check it wrote a `body:nth-child` chain.
- `timelineGroupInfo.realm.test.ts`: a group the preview adds updates the label. With the old check it stayed the id.
- `reapplyPositionEditsAfterSeek.test.ts`: a committed rotation is reapplied, and a legacy edit mark migrates, on a frame-built node and on an editor-built one. With the old check the editor-built one is skipped; with a bare `instanceof` the frame-built one is.
- `MotionPathOverlay.test.tsx` (jsdom, whose iframes have their own constructors): a layer node built by the editor document, as on the failing loads, takes an armed set-destination press. With the old check nothing happens.
- `noWindowBoundDomChecks.test.ts`: on the sources before this PR it lists every site above, and it fails if the deleted helper is restored or if a member read starts its own line, as the formatter writes a long cast.

- `motionPathGeometry.test.ts`: the bench's `keys` layer (260 wide at 1 s, keyframes at width 280 and 320) draws its nodes at 760 and 840, its centre at 2 s and 3 s; drawn with the layer's current 260 px width they were 10 and 30 px off. `useMotionPathData.test.tsx`: a keyframe that changes only its width redraws the node.
- `gsapRuntimeKeyframes.realGsap.test.ts` (real GSAP): that step list reads its start as x 40, width 260; a percentage list from 0%, or a step list whose first step is where GSAP started, reads none. `motionPathGeometry.test.ts` and `MotionPathOverlay.layerPress.test.tsx`: the start is drawn as a ring that takes no press, with the line starting there.
- `motionPathLayerNode.test.ts`, `MotionPathOverlay.layerPress.test.tsx`: inside the box any node's press, on its ring or its dot, selected or not, goes to the layer; a crop handle over a node or the line takes the press (and its cursor shows), not the node or the layer; outside, the node keeps it; a control that starts no gesture leaves it to the node. On the line inside the box: move cursor, no ghost, press moves the layer; outside it adds a keyframe at the stored offsets halfway between its nodes, not the drawn point. The overlay draws a node 20 px right where its keyframe makes the layer 40 px wider.
- `useMotionPathData.test.tsx`: a layer at `left: 50%` with `xPercent/yPercent: -50` anchors on its centre with no size shift; a set `left` shifts by half, a set `right` by minus half, a layer in flow not at all; the home updates when the layer's width changes around a fixed centre; the start ring appears when GSAP's start is read after the first draw. `motionPathGeometry.test.ts`: a `-50%` layer's size keyframes leave its nodes on its centre.
- `gsapRuntimeKeyframes.realGsap.test.ts`: a percentage list past 0% with x and y, or x and width, reads every channel's start.
- `useMotionPathData.test.tsx` (real GSAP, computed `translate` reported as Chromium does) and `tests/e2e/motion-path-home.mjs` (real Chromium and GSAP, `bun run test:motion-path-home:browser`): a layer's `translate: 40px 30px` and `-50% -50%` survive reading its anchor; a path created from the anchor ends on the click for a plain, a `-50%`, a minus-half-px, an untranslated, a `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` (inline and from a class), a transform-plus-translate and a faded layer with a drag offset (the centred ones ended at (580, 320) for a click at (700, 400) before); a drag's `var()` offset on a layer GSAP already moves counts; GSAP's `uncache` after `clearProps` reads as not yet parsed. Asking GSAP for the percent instead fails the translate checks.
- `DomEditSelectionChrome.test.tsx`: every pointer-active part of the rendered chrome (box, resize and rotate handles, crop handles) is inside what the path's lookup accepts. `MotionPathOverlay.layerPress.test.tsx`: a node over another layer's off-canvas marker keeps its press; a handle under the layer's own node takes it.
- Each of these fails on the code before this change, and breaking any single fix (the overlay's node placement, the home size check, the add-on-line maths, the handle lookup, the start redraw, the per-channel start read, the left/right anchor, the in-flow rule, the percent anchor) fails a test. Edit-accuracy bench on a shared test machine at the head before the handle fix, `move-keys-px-r{0,30}-root-z{50,100}-{mid,on}`, 3 runs each: tracking, press jump, keys, drop, reload, render and undo all pass. Main on the same machine fails tracking, keys, drop, reload and undo on `move-keys-px-r0-root-z100-mid`. The frame-work check (`smooth`) failed there for main and this branch alike under heavy load; CI's gate is the reference for it.

## Before

**Path missing on load.** Bench fixture, a fresh load with the layer selected at 2 s: no motion path is drawn on the layer.

![Before: a selected keyframed layer with no motion path drawn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/af7301aa-330d-4ecd-b34f-4903184eb167)

**Scrubbing a width tween.** The bench's `keys` fixture in headless Chromium 152, layer selected, playhead stepped from 0 s to 3 s: the nodes slide with the layer, and nothing marks where it starts.

![Before: path nodes slide with the layer while scrubbing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bed65fd-3d9b-4662-bea0-e34519867c7d)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a187fe57-ef59-4084-9dd9-2d2e0408c2e7

**A centred layer.** The bench's `move-tween-center` fixture (`left: 50%; translate: -50% -50%`, a 4 s `x`/`y` tween), playhead at 4 s, where the layer should sit on the path's end node. On main the path is not drawn on this load at all (the first fix above); on this PR before its percent fix the node sat on the layer's bottom-right corner. `xPercent/yPercent: -50` looks the same.

![Before: a layer centred with translate -50% draws its path node on its corner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5293343d-43c6-4542-95b2-748d995a26c0)

## After

**Path missing on load.** The same load draws the path and its nodes.

![After: the same layer with its motion path nodes drawn](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/745b4e55-af77-4fd2-a56a-cc5186377e3d)

**Scrubbing a width tween.** The nodes stay where each keyframe puts the layer: its centre is on the first node at 2 s, on the second at 3 s, and on the start ring at 0 s.

![After: path nodes stay where each keyframe puts the layer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a97c048c-09e3-43f9-8dbf-8e29de89b633)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6d4970b-4f6e-4374-8795-a82c36136bff

**A centred layer.** The end node sits on the layer's centre at 4 s, and halfway there at 2 s.

![After: the path node is the centred layer's centre](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/838bcb37-d96b-4cde-9b82-038290893a3a)

title: fix(core): torn-down runtimes stop checking readiness, and entry tests fit their timeout under load
body:
## What

The runtime entry tests no longer time out on a loaded machine; the fix is at the cause, not a longer timeout. Making that change exposed a runtime bug, also fixed here.

- `src/runtime/entry.test.ts`: the runtime is evaluated once while the file loads, then reset. Each test still evaluates a fresh copy after `vi.resetModules()`, exactly as before.
- `src/runtime/init.ts`: a torn-down runtime no longer runs its readiness check. The check scheduled at start (`setTimeout(..., 0)`) survived teardown. When it fired after a new document loaded, it wrote `__renderReady` and could add an `hf-timelines-built` listener for the dead runtime. `maybePublishRenderReady` now returns once the runtime is torn down; every caller routes through it, the timer included.

## Why

Every entry test re-imports the runtime after `vi.resetModules()`, which is how it models a page evaluating the runtime script again. The first of those imports also transforms the whole runtime module graph. That one-time cost (about 1-1.4 s on an idle machine) landed inside the first test's 5 s timeout, so under CPU contention `paints no timed clip, from script evaluation until the first visibility pass decides it` timed out, and the next test sometimes did too. File loading has no per-test timeout, so the transform now happens there.

## Related work

None.

## How

`resetRuntimeGlobals` is the old `afterEach` body, extracted so the load-time evaluation can clean up with the same steps. The readiness guard follows the `state.tornDown` early returns the runtime already uses elsewhere.

## Test plan

- [x] Idle machine, `entry.test.ts` alone: first test 922-1439 ms on main, 73-211 ms with the change, 31/31 passing, 3 runs each.
- [x] Loaded machine (full `src/runtime` suite, vitest and four busy loops pinned to the same four cores): on main the entry file failed 2 tests in all 3 runs (first test 5055-5129 ms, "Test timed out in 5000ms"). With the change it passed in all 3 runs (first test 1331-2384 ms).
- [x] New test `a torn-down runtime's pending readiness check leaves the next document alone`: passes 3 runs in a row. With the guard removed it fails with `expected false to be undefined` (the old check marked the next document not ready). `init.test.ts` 210/210 and `entry.test.ts` 31/31 pass.
- [x] `oxfmt --check`, the comment citation check and the comment ratchet pass.

Not in this PR: under the same load, the first test in `init.mediaClipIndex`, `init.swapScenes`, `init.timingResolver` and `audioClockSource`, and one in `transportPark`, still time out, on main and on this branch alike. They do not re-import anything. Their cost is the first runtime start in a fresh test file, a different cause, so they get their own fix.

## Size

Under 100 lines on purpose: a flaky test is fixed the day it is found, and nothing open carries this change.

title: fix(studio): a rotation saves through its press route; a host hook reloads only the host's way
body:
## What changes for the user

Nothing visible in ordinary editing. A rotation now saves through the route (plain CSS or GSAP) its press chose, both ways, so it can no longer draft one way and save the other.

Hosts embedding Studio's geometry commits (`useDomGeometryCommit`) must now pass `reloadPreview`. When a save cannot patch the preview in place, Studio calls the host's own reload instead of reloading the iframe's location behind the host's back.

## Why

**Rotation route.** The press already decided the route (`plainRotation`: a CSS target, or `null` for GSAP), but the release only sent it on when it was CSS. A GSAP-route rotation therefore reached the commit with no route and was decided again there, after the gesture's own writes. This finishes the route unification in #4943, where move and resize already carry their press route.

**Host reload.** The fallback (`iframe.contentWindow.location.reload()`) skipped the host's player refresh, so a host that forgot the option got a different, slower reload path that nothing exercised. A required option makes the one path explicit and fails at compile time instead. No host in this repository omits it.

## Change

- `RotationCommit.plain` is `CssRotationTarget | null`: `null` means the press chose GSAP; leaving it out means there was no press (panel, host, agent), and the commit decides once at entry through `editsPlainCss`.
- The overlay always sends the press's `plainRotation`.
- `UseDomGeometryCommitOptions.reloadPreview` is required and forwarded as is; the location-reload fallback is gone.

## Tests

- `useGsapAwareEditing.test.tsx`: a rotation the press sent down the GSAP route saves through GSAP even once the element looks GSAP-free. It fails on the base and passes now; the 21 test files that touch rotation commits pass.
- `useDomGeometryCommit.test.tsx`: a type test that `reloadPreview` is required. It fails typecheck against the old optional option and passes now; the hook's existing tests pass.

## Release note

Breaking for hosts of `useDomGeometryCommit` (exported from `@hyperframes/studio`): pass `reloadPreview`, your preview's own reload.

## Before

Real Studio on the edit accuracy bench fixtures, main: a plain CSS box and a GSAP-tweened box, rotated by the handle.

![Before: plain and GSAP rotations on main](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88553b48-8faa-41ae-adde-a29ac94a2b26)

## After

Same cases on this PR: identical results, as a routing-only change should give.

![After: same rotations, same results](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c9f14c4-d14a-422e-af2d-37188268941b)

Folds in #4945 (host reload), which was too small to ship alone.



## Size

38 lines, under the 100-line floor. Nothing open can carry it: it already folds in #4945, and the move and resize halves of the same route work shipped in #4943 and #4934.

title: fix(studio): the server picks an added effect's element id; one client for patch and gsap writes
body:
## What

"Add effect" on an element with no id of its own no longer lets two elements share an id, and Studio's `patch-element` and `gsap-mutations` writes each go through one client.

1. **The server picks the new id.** Studio used to choose the id from the live preview, set it on the element, and remove it again when the write failed. The preview and the saved file can disagree, which caused two bugs. A new `patch-element` operation, `ensure-id`, fixes both: the server keeps the element's existing id, or writes the proposed id made unique against every HTML file in the project. Sub-compositions share one preview document, so an id another composition file holds counts as taken. The scan, the patch and the write run in one synchronous step, so two adds in different files can't both pick the same id. Every `patch-element` reply now names the element's id (`elementId`). Studio sets that id on the preview only once the reply arrives, so nothing needs rolling back. This is the same split already used for clip split, duplicate and freeze frame, where the server picks the id.
2. **patch-element client.** `assignGsapTargetAutoIdIfNeeded` built its own `file-mutations/patch-element` request. It now posts through `postPatchElement` and returns the id the file holds, or `null`. A refusal is toasted with the server's reason. A reply naming no id (the element isn't in the file) now toasts "Couldn't assign element id: element not found in <file>"; main returned silently there.
3. **gsap-mutations client.** `mutateGsapScript`, `mutateGsapScriptBatch` and `postGsapMutation` each built the same POST. `requestGsapMutation` in `gsapMutationClient.ts` is now the one request, and each caller keeps its own response handling.
4. **One unique-id helper on the server.** `nextUniqueId` in `sourceMutation.ts` now serves split, duplicate, freeze frame, group and `ensure-id`. Before, there were four copies of the same `base`, `base-2`, ... loop.

## Why

Review of the first version found both id bugs:

- **A lost reply after a saved id.** The file kept the id while the preview dropped it, so the next add on a sibling saved the same id again: two elements with `id="div"`.
- **Two overlapping adds on the same element.** The first add's refusal stripped the id the second add had just saved.
- **Two overlapping adds in different composition files** (found at `67381aaf`). Each file was deduped alone, so both could save `id="div"` into one preview. A lost reply in one file did the same to a later add in another.

Both bugs come from one place: the code choosing the id could not see the file. Two copies of one request also drift apart; they already handled a refusal differently.

## How

- The refused-id toast now uses the patch client's message. With a server reason, "Couldn't save animation: <reason>" becomes "Couldn't save edit: <reason>". Without one, "Couldn't save animation: GSAP mutation failed with status <N>" becomes "Couldn't save edit".
- Studio and the studio server ship together, so no older server ever receives `ensure-id`.
- Known limit: the server makes the id unique across the project's HTML files, not against the live preview. An id that exists only in the preview (added by a script at runtime) can still repeat until the next reload. Nothing is written twice to the project.
- Every add effect on an id-less element now reads the project's HTML files once. That is cheap at today's project sizes; a cache keyed on file versions is the upgrade if it ever shows up in a profile.

## Before

An id-less element whose id write the server refuses (a forced 409 "file changed" on `patch-element`), on main:

![Refused id write on main: "Couldn't save animation: file changed"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3cebf23c-d76d-4828-9fa5-e3d5392d5842)

## After

The same refusal on this branch (captured before the `ensure-id` change; the refusal path and its toast are unchanged by it):

![Refused id write on this branch: "Couldn't save edit: file changed"](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6f1be36f-5faa-44f0-a6a7-69ca85540024)

## Test plan

- [x] `useGsapAnimationOps.test.tsx` replays each sequence through the real `patchElementInHtml` against an in-memory file:
  - The lost reply then the sibling add leaves `div` and `div-2`, and the sibling's effect targets `#div-2`. With the previous Studio code the file held `div` twice.
  - The refused-then-saved overlapping adds on one element leave the preview id equal to the file's. With the previous Studio code the preview had no id while the file held `div-2`.
  - Overlapping adds on siblings never share an id, and a saved, refused, network-failed or no-project add leaves the preview matching the file.
- [x] Server tests for `ensure-id`:
  - `sourceMutation.test.ts`: writes the proposed id, makes it unique against the file, keeps an existing id unchanged, reports no id for a missing target.
  - `files.test.ts`: the route returns `elementId` on both the changed and the unchanged reply, and an id saved in `compositions/b.html` makes the same proposal in `index.html` save as `div-2`. That test fails at `67381aaf`, and fails again if the scan is dropped or limited to root files. A second test puts ids in another file straight after a quote and after a string ending in `"/id=`; both must count.
  - All of these fail on the previous server.
- [x] `useDomEditCommitsHelpers.test.ts`: request shape (method, write token, `ensure-id` body), the returned id, `null` plus a toast for a missing target or a reply without an id, the server's reason on a refusal, a non-finite target refused before any request, a network failure passed through.
- [x] `useGsapScriptCommits.test.tsx`: the write token on the gsap request, and a refused write's reason reaching a toast. Removing the token or the refusal check now fails a test (both passed the whole hooks suite before).
- [x] The touched server and studio test files pass 3 runs in a row. Type checks for studio and studio-server are clean, and oxfmt, oxlint, fallow, comment citations and the comment ratchet all pass.
- [x] Before/After: built Studio on main and on this branch, `patch-element` answered with a 409 by request interception, "+ Add effect" on the first of two id-less `.card` elements.

Follow-ups, not in this PR:
- A refused id write still resolves `addGsapAnimation` normally, so the add handler resets an element's manual path offset although no effect was added (`useGsapSelectionHandlers.ts`).
- `file-mutations/remove-elements` still has two inline clients (`useTimelineDeleteOps.ts`, `useElementLifecycleOps.ts`) that handle a refusal differently.
- No test makes a freeze-frame or group id collide. Both now go through the shared `nextUniqueId`, which the `ensure-id` and split tests pin.

title: fix(studio): a nudge on a tweened layer keeps its keyframe while the preview reloads
body:
## What

A nudge (or drag) on a layer animated by a flat tween could save a static `gsap.set` instead of a keyframe. In the edit bench, `nudge-fromto-px-r0-root-z100-mid` wrote `gsap.set("#target", { x: 45, y: 30 })` in about 1 of 5 CI runs (for example run 37120535633, shard 2, run 1): x at t=0 moved by 100 px, and reload and undo failed with it.

## Why

`dragRoute` in `gsapRuntimeBridge.ts` picks the static route when the live preview shows no non-hold position tween for the element and the source tween is not keyframed. A `from()` is a flat tween, so for this layer the choice rested on the live read alone. When the preview was reloading at the moment of the save (that run also logged `gsap is not defined`), the live read found no tween, and the nudge wrote a static set over the animation.

The live read stays: it is what keeps a just-deleted tween from being written back from a stale cached parse. The route now also asks the current file, which the intercept already reads: if the file still has a real (non-hold) position tween for the element, the edit keeps the tween route. The intercept reads the file once, before choosing the route, and reuses that read for its existing tween-id check, so there is no extra request. The group plan passes the fresh list it already holds, so a group's plan and its commit decide alike.

## No visible change

There is nothing to capture on demand: the wrong write only happens when the save lands during a preview reload. The unit test below reproduces that state directly.

## Test plan

- [x] `gsapRuntimeBridge.test.ts`: an empty runtime with a flat `from()` in the current file keeps the tween route (red before the fix: it committed a `set`); an empty runtime with the tween gone from the file still commits a static set (the stale-cache guard). 25/25, 3 runs in a row.
- [x] useGsapAwareEditing 29, useGsapAwareEditing.groupPlan 4, domGroupMoveBy 9, gsapDragCommit 18. tsc, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [ ] One CI edit-accuracy run of the case on this head.

Stacked on #4889; retargets to main when it merges.

title: fix(cli): publish with a refused login refreshes or asks you to log in again
body:
## What

`hyperframes publish` with a credential the server refuses now stops before anything is created and says what to do:

- a login (or a saved API key): "Your login expired. Run hyperframes auth login, then publish again."
- an API key from `HEYGEN_API_KEY` / `HYPERFRAMES_API_KEY`: "HEYGEN_API_KEY was rejected. Fix or unset it, then publish again." (logging in would not help: the environment key outranks a login)

A login that expired and has no refresh token is no longer treated as "not signed in": publish stops with the same re-login message and sends nothing, and `hyperframes auth status` says "Your HeyGen login expired" instead of "Not signed in". A publish with a login that the server still answers with an unowned (unclaimed) project fails the same way. Only an owned result is saved as this directory's link. API-key publishes are unchanged: the server never makes them owned.

`--update` and `--space` need a login, because only an owned project can be updated in place or put in a team space. With an API key they now stop before uploading and say so ("--update requires a login; HEYGEN_API_KEY cannot own a project. Unset it and run 'hyperframes auth login'.", or "an API key cannot own a project" for a saved key), instead of publishing a new unowned project and ignoring the flag.

`publish` now looks up the credential once and uploads with that same credential. Before, the upload looked it up again after baking proxies, so a login that expired during the bake fell back to a saved API key and the flags were dropped after all. A login that expires during the bake is refreshed just before the upload, never swapped for another credential; a login that cannot be refreshed stops with the re-login message before anything is sent.

A token refresh never writes over a different login. If you log in as someone else while a publish is running, the old login's refresh leaves the new login exactly as it is, and publish stops with "Your login changed during publish. Run publish again."

An expired login that has a refresh token is refreshed first, as the cloud commands already do, so the common case of a stale access token publishes normally instead of failing. The warning for the old behaviour ("Your login looks expired or invalid, so --update was ignored and a NEW url was created above") is gone.

## Why

The publish API is changing so that a request carrying a credential it rejects gets HTTP 401 instead of silently publishing an anonymous project with a claim URL. Without this change the CLI would print the bare server message ("Unauthorized"), and it would send a stale access token it could have refreshed.

## How

- `resolvePublishCredential` resolves the credential and refreshes it with `refreshIfNeeded` from `cloud/auth.ts` (now exported, not copied). A refused refresh (`REFRESH_FAILED`) is the "log in again" case and stops before any request.
- Only the requests that carry the credential (`/publish/upload`, `/publish/complete`, the legacy `/publish`) turn a 401 into `CredentialRejectedError`; `publishProjectArchive` maps it to the message for that credential. A 401 from the presigned storage upload carries no credential and keeps its own error.
- The first credentialed request (`/publish/upload`) creates nothing, so a refused credential stops before the archive upload. The existing catch in `publish.ts` prints the message under "Publish failed" and exits 1.
- The credential resolver (`auth/resolver.ts`) throws `LOGIN_EXPIRED` when the stored login is expired with no refresh token and there is no saved API key to fall back to; `NOT_CONFIGURED` now means only "never signed in". `resolvePublishCredential` maps `LOGIN_EXPIRED` like `REFRESH_FAILED`, and the `--update` / `--space` preflight uses it too.
- The server owns a publish only for a bearer login (every owned publish returns `claimed: true`) and drops a bearer it cannot verify, publishing anonymously (`claimed: false`). An API key (`x-api-key`) always publishes unowned. So a login publish whose result is unclaimed raises `CredentialRejectedError` and goes through the same message mapping, and `writeProjectLink` runs only for a claimed result.
- `publish.ts` resolves the credential once, before the bake, and passes it to `publishProjectArchive` (new optional `credential`; `null` publishes anonymously, omitted resolves inside as before, which `feedback` still uses). The `--update` / `--space` preflight checks that same credential and accepts only a login (`type === "oauth"`). `resolvePublishCredential(checked)` refreshes a passed login whose expiry has passed (the resolver's `isTokenExpired`, same 60 s skew) and never resolves again.
- `persistOAuth` (`auth/oauth.ts`) takes the refresh token that was exchanged (`{ refreshed }`, replacing the `preserveMissing` flag). If the stored login no longer holds that refresh token, it writes nothing and throws `LOGIN_CHANGED`; `resolvePublishCredential` maps it to the message above. This applies to every refresh caller, not only publish. A refresh that cannot read the credentials file now reports that error instead of treating the file as empty.
- Anonymous publishing sends no credential and is unchanged.

## Rollout

Release this CLI before or with the API change (an older CLI shows "Unauthorized" on the 401). Before the API deploy, a token the server silently drops still creates an unowned project on the server, but the CLI now reports it as a failed publish with the re-login message instead of showing a claim URL or saving the link.

## Test plan

New in `publishProject.test.ts`:
- 401 on the first request: re-login message after exactly one request, which carried the bearer.
- 401 on `/publish/complete` and on the legacy multipart publish: same message.
- 401 from the storage upload: the storage error, not the login message.
- 401 with `HEYGEN_API_KEY`: names the variable.
- An expired, refreshable login is refreshed and the request carries the new token; a refused refresh asks for a new login and sends nothing.

- A stored login that is expired with no refresh token, through the real resolver and a temp credentials file: re-login message, no request sent (`publishProject.test.ts`), and `LOGIN_EXPIRED` from the resolver (`resolver.test.ts`).
- A login publish answered with an unclaimed project, staged and legacy: re-login message, no link written.
- An API-key publish answered with an unclaimed project: succeeds with its claim token, no link written. Checking every credential, or linking on any credential, fails it.
- `publish.test.ts`, through the real command and resolver: `--update` and `--space` with `HEYGEN_API_KEY`, and `--update` with a saved API key, exit 1 with the login message and never call publish; `--update` with a login publishes. The three refusals fail with the previous "any credential" check. A command test for each flag runs the real upload code with the stored login expiring mid-publish next to a saved API key: every request carries the login and the command exits 1 without a claim URL. It fails if the upload resolves again or if `publish.ts` does not pass its credential. A passed login that expired after the check is refreshed and the upload carries the new token, with no second lookup (`publishProject.test.ts`); it fails without the expiry recompute. A passed login that expired with no refresh token stops before any request; it fails without that check. A command test swaps the stored login to another account during the bake and answers the refresh without a refresh token: the other login, its refresh token and its user stay untouched, only the token request is sent, exit 1. With the guard removed it fails, because the store ends up with the old access token on the new refresh token; the `oauth.test.ts` unit test fails the same way. A refresh against a corrupt credentials file reports `INVALID_STORE` and leaves the file alone. Real CLI on Linux with `HEYGEN_API_KEY` set: both flags print the message and exit 1. `src/auth`, `src/cloud`, `src/commands/auth`, feedback, `publishProject.test.ts`, `publish.test.ts`: 369 pass, 3 runs in a row; `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt clean.

The three new tests fail on the previous head (anonymous publish, `NOT_CONFIGURED`); dropping the `LOGIN_EXPIRED` mapping fails the end-to-end test. Real CLI on Linux with an expired, no-refresh credentials file and the API pointed at a dead port: before, `auth status` said "Not signed in" and `publish --yes` tried an anonymous upload; after, `auth status` prints "Your HeyGen login expired" and `publish` prints the re-login message and exits 1, for plain publish and `--update`. `src/auth`, `src/commands/auth`, `src/cloud`, `publishProject.test.ts`, `publish.test.ts`: 355 pass, 3 runs in a row (with the feedback tests); `tsc --noEmit` clean; oxlint clean.

The first test fails on main (`Unauthorized`). Breaking the code three ways (no refresh, mapping the storage 401, dropping the API-key message) fails 2, 1 and 1 tests. `publishProject.test.ts`, `publish.test.ts` and the cloud tests: 152 pass, 3 runs in a row; CLI `tsc --noEmit` clean; oxlint clean; comment ratchet at or under base.

## No visible change

CLI text output only; nothing under Studio or the player.

## Size

Credential refresh reuse, two error types, two messages, one unclaimed-result check, one deleted branch, a login-only `--update` / `--space` check, one credential lookup per publish (refreshed, never replaced), a refresh that only writes to the login it refreshed, twenty-two tests.

title: fix(core): a call on the playhead fires once when a readiness pass runs
body:
## What

A GSAP `tl.call` that sits on the playhead fires once when the runtime runs a readiness or scene-swap pass between two seeks. Before, the next forward seek fired it a second time.

Repro on main: a call at 2 s, `renderSeek(2)` (fires once), the deferred readiness pass runs, `renderSeek(3)`: the call fires again. Studio reaches this when a scene is edited while paused on a call and then played; renders reach it through the readiness pass.

## Why

The runtime's start-up pass (`runAdapters("discover")`, run at start-up, at timeline binding, on each readiness pass and after a scene swap) re-seeks every adapter, including the GSAP adapter. That adapter seeks the root timeline, which the root seek already renders, and its silent re-render re-arms a call at the playhead, so the next eventful seek fires it again. The two seek loops already leave the GSAP adapter out while a root timeline exists; this pass did not.

Removing that redundant seek exposed a second bug it was hiding. The deferred readiness pass that init schedules with `setTimeout(0)` was never cleared on teardown. When a runtime starts again in the same window, the old pass still runs, binds the new root timeline and seeks it to the old runtime's playhead. On main, the GSAP adapter's redundant seek ran afterwards and put the timeline back.

## How

- `fix(core): a torn-down runtime no longer re-seeks the next one's timeline`: the deferred readiness timer is cleared on teardown, like the runtime's other timers.
- `fix(core): a call on the playhead fires once when a readiness pass runs`: one predicate, `isSeekedByRoot`, decides which adapters the root seek leaves out. All three adapter seeks use it: the discover pass (newly) and the two seek loops (unchanged behaviour).

## Test plan

- [x] `init.test.ts`: "fires a call on the playhead once when a readiness pass runs between seeks" fails on main (2 fires) and passes here.
- [x] `init.test.ts`: "leaves the next runtime's timeline alone after a runtime is torn down" fails with the discover change but without the timer clear (the new timeline reads the old playhead, 16.2), and passes here. With only the discover change, the existing "rebinds the injected player before reporting runtime-data applied" also fails, when it runs after the forced-rebind test.
- [x] init, gsap.steps and gsap tests 241/241, 3 runs; `src/runtime` 1764/1764; the runtime seek script passes; core's typecheck (including the runtime one), fallow audit, format, lint and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Size

About 55 changed lines in `packages/core/src/runtime`, most of them tests. It ships alone: it follows #4942, which has merged, and no other PR is open in this lane to carry it; it fixes a call that fires twice in renders and Studio.

title: fix(studio-server): history never files a hidden file as a change
body:
## What changes

Project history no longer records hidden files as someone's change. A tool's own record at the project root (`.turn-record`, `.spawn-record`) or a `.DS_Store` in any folder used to land in the history entry. Then an agent run that wrote only such a file got an Undo step with nothing a person could see. Studio's two manifests under `.hyperframes/` are still kept.

## Why here

History tracks the set `listProjectFiles` returns: the preview-signature walk. That walk skips hidden folders but not hidden file names, so root-level dotfiles got in. The filter goes in history, the single owner of what it tracks, so the preview signature stays as it is:

- `historyFiles` filters the walk for the first open and every sweep.
- `noteChange` and `hearWrites` skip hidden paths.
- An older log is cleaned once when it is read (`keptPaths`): hidden paths leave the baseline and every entry. Every entry keeps its id, emptied or not, because pins, undos, restores and callers name entries by id. Undoing an emptied entry still lands as a step, so no Undo, Redo or caller stalls on it, and Cmd+Z steps over emptied entries.

## Test

`projectHistory.test.ts`, five tests:

- "never files a hidden file name as a change, but keeps Studio's two manifests": fails without the fix (the entry lists `.turn-record` and `sub/.DS_Store`).
- "never writes a hidden file an older log still names, on undo or restore".
- "steps Undo past an older log's entry that changed only a hidden file".
- "keeps an older log's Undo that only reverted a hidden file, so its target stays undone".
- "keeps every entry an older log names, emptied ones too, and undoing one still lands".

Each older-log test fails with its part of the fix removed. All pass 3 runs in a row, and the history suites pass (143).

title: test(studio): serve the edit bench GSAP from the repo, never the network
body:
## What

The edit-accuracy bench loaded GSAP from jsdelivr in every case. When that request was slow or failed in CI, the preview logged `gsap is not defined`, the case's timeline never registered, and the case failed for a reason that had nothing to do with Studio. That is the root of the intermittent `nudge-fromto-px-r0-root-z100-mid` failure (for example run 37120535633, shard 2).

Fixtures still contain the CDN `<script>` tag a user would write. The bench now intercepts requests to the CDN host in each Studio page and answers any file of the installed gsap version from the repo's own `gsap/dist`: today the fixture's `gsap.min.js`, plus any plugin the preview server pins to the same version. Any other request to that host is blocked and its URL logged once (`edit bench: blocked <url>`), so a new remote dependency is named instead of silently reaching the network. Today that log names one URL: Studio's own MotionPathPlugin, pinned at 3.12.5 in `gsapSoftReload.ts`. Without it, `motionPath:` tweens (which no fixture or bench edit writes) cannot play, and Studio hides its "Set motion destination" toolbar button. Hiding that button can only remove overlap with a drag, and this PR's full-grid gate passed against main's baseline.

- `grid.mjs`: the fixture URL takes its version from the installed `gsap` package, so the URL and the bytes served always match. `localAsset(url)` maps a CDN URL under that version's `dist/` to the repo file, when it exists.
- `case.mjs`: `inStudio` enables the DevTools `Fetch` domain for the CDN host and fulfils matching requests from `localAsset`. A request whose frame already went away is ignored rather than ending the run.
- `grid.test.mjs` (new): writes every fixture in the full grid and fails on any http(s) URL the bench does not serve from the repo, including a mapped URL on a host the bench does not intercept.

The fixture GSAP moves from 3.14.2 to 3.15.0, the only version installed in the repo (the same version the producer uses). This PR's edit-accuracy CI runs the full grid against main's baseline, so that run is the before/after for the version change.

## Follow-up, not in this PR

The bench's `render` checks run in the producer's own browser, which still loads the fixture's CDN URL from the network (the producer also points a missing local gsap at the CDN: `GSAP_CDN_BASE` in `packages/producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`). A network failure can still fail `render` there. That needs its own fix.

## No visible change

Test-only.

## Test plan

- [x] `grid.test.mjs` passes 3 runs in a row. It fails, listing the URL, when the local map does not cover the fixture URL.
- [x] Proof the preview gets GSAP from the repo: with the fixture URL pointed at a GSAP version jsdelivr does not have (404), four cases ran with the same drag, drop and undo verdicts as with the real URL. Only `render` changed, which is the producer path above.
- [x] After the review changes, three cases on one devbox: only the 3.12.5 plugin is logged as blocked, and verdicts match main's baseline.
- [x] With the real URL, the same four cases (resize, keyframed move, nudge on a from/to tween, nested move) ran 3 times on one devbox, each time matching main's baseline verdict.
- [x] oxfmt and oxlint clean.
- [x] This PR's edit-accuracy CI run (full grid against main's baseline) passed the gate.

Kept as its own PR under the size floor: it is the bench's network root, test-only and off main, and no open PR carries bench harness changes.
