title: fix(studio): undoing a freeze frame removes the still it made
body: ## What Freeze frame, then Undo, now leaves the project as it was: the still that Freeze frame extracted into `assets/freeze/` is deleted by the Undo and put back by Redo. Before, Undo reverted the page but the still stayed in the project's files. ## Why The freeze-frame route writes two things: the page (split clip plus an ``) and a new PNG under `assets/freeze/`. `useFreezeFrame` recorded the history entry with only the page's path, so the history claim never took the PNG. Undo stepped back the page and left the PNG as an unclaimed outside change. ## Related work Refs: none. ## How - `studio-server` freeze route: the response now carries `stillPath`, the still's path from the project root (the history's naming; `imageSrc` stays relative to the page). - `RecordEditInput` gains `created?: string[]`, files an edit made that are not text. `usePersistentEditHistory.recordEdit` adds them to the claimed paths, so the history entry holds them: its Undo deletes them and its Redo restores them from the history's blob store. The hook's private copy of `RecordEditInput` is replaced by the shared type, so the field has one owner. - `useFreezeFrame` passes `created: [result.stillPath]`. - Same route, same leak: a freeze that fails after extraction starts (ffmpeg fails or times out and leaves a partial file, the page changed meanwhile, or the target vanished) now deletes that still instead of leaving an orphan. The concurrent-freeze test pinned the orphan and now expects only the still the page uses. So that a failed request can only remove a still it made, the route now claims the still's name (`open` with `wx`) before extracting, and ffmpeg writes into that claim (`-y` instead of `-n`). A freeze time past the end of the media file (a clip longer than its file, or an offset or rate) made ffmpeg exit 0 without a frame, so the page named an empty or missing PNG; an empty output now fails the freeze with "no frame at this time" and leaves nothing behind. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing performed - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments" Each changed test file run alone, 3 times, exit 0 each: - `studio-server/src/routes/freezeFrame.test.ts`: 12 passed. New: the response's `stillPath`, including from a nested page; no still left when extraction fails or when the write fails after extraction; two requests racing for one still name keep the winner's still; ffmpeg succeeding without a frame fails the freeze and leaves nothing. - `studio-server/src/helpers/freezeFrame.test.ts`: 15 passed (ffmpeg args now `-y`). - `studio/src/hooks/usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts`: 13 passed. New, on the real history engine and routes: a created file is deleted by Undo and put back by Redo. - `studio/src/hooks/useFreezeFrame.test.ts`: 3 passed. New: the hook records the still with the edit. Mutations, one per new behaviour, each turned its test red: dropping `created` from the claim, dropping `created` in `useFreezeFrame`, removing the cleanup on a failed write, removing the cleanup on a failed extraction, removing the name claim (the race test and the name-taken test fail), removing the empty-output check. `studio` and `studio-server` typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files. Manual: Studio's dev server with a 6 s generated test-pattern video; seek to 2.5 s, right-click the clip, Freeze frame, Ctrl+Z, then reload once (Studio's file tree lists files written after load only after a reload, on main too) and open Code to see the project's files. Not exercised: the raw `/undo` route's mode that keeps later edits still deletes the still while the kept page may name it (Studio and the CLI never use that mode); a client newer than its server would reject a response without `stillPath` (the two ship together); an exception thrown while writing the page still skips the cleanup; a freeze on a clip's very last frame (clip as long as its file) now fails with "no frame at this time" instead of freezing (before, it saved an empty image; a fallback to the last frame is possible later); an `open` error other than "already exists" is rethrown (a 500) but has no test; a history operation landing during the extraction can commit the still as its own outside change, as before this PR. ## Before Captured at a5f970af; the later commits change only the route's failure paths, not this flow. Freeze frame applied: ![before: freeze applied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1e794eaf-86fb-49cf-9b40-6fedd04fdac1) After Ctrl+Z the page is back, but `assets/freeze/talk-….png` is still in the project: ![before: still left after undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7e8a4c36-38f6-47c5-9930-742683deb071) ## After Freeze frame applied: ![after: freeze applied](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/991d015d-82bd-4769-acb5-00c54ad41976) After Ctrl+Z the project holds only `assets/talk.mp4` again: ![after: no still after undo](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d57612e4-d85c-4302-926a-7e289e8a5bc5)

title: feat(studio): resize every timeline layer at once from the toolbar or a layer's bottom edge
body:
## What

Timeline layers can be made shorter or taller, all at once. Two ways:

- **Layer height** slider in the timeline toolbar, next to the thumbnails toggle.
- Drag the bottom edge of any layer's header. The edge you drag stays under the pointer. Double click puts every layer back to the default 48 px.

Range is 24 to 120 px. Below 40 px, clips drop their thumbnails and show only the name bar, so a project with 10+ layers fits on screen.

## Why

With many layers, a 48 px fixed row means scrolling the timeline vertically to reach the lower ones. NLEs (Final Cut Pro, Resolve) let you shrink every track together and hide thumbnails once they are too small to read.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `playerStore.trackHeight` is the one value (clamped by `clampTrackHeight`). It is app state, not project state, so `beginTimelineSession` leaves it alone and a host can set it per project.
- `createTimelineRowGeometry` takes the layer height and exposes it as `geometry.trackHeight`; the bottom ghost lane, rows past the last and every clip bar, ghost, gap strip and marquee read it from there instead of `TRACK_H`. Keyframe and automation lanes sit under the resized bar through `getTimelineLaneTop(index, trackHeight)`.
- Headers (track, group, layer disclosure) read the store value directly.
- Thumbnails: `useRenderClipContent` treats layers under `TRACK_H_THUMBNAILS_MIN` as the existing "hidden" thumbnail mode, so there is one rule for "no thumbnails" and thumbnail generation is skipped too.
- The grip divides the pointer's travel by `row + 1`: every layer above the edge grows by the same amount, so that keeps the dragged edge under the pointer.
- Changing the layer height keeps the timeline's scroll position (`getTimelineScrollTopForGeometryChange`) instead of anchoring the top visible row. That keeps a dragged edge under the pointer while scrolled (each layer above it grows by the same amount, scrolled out or not); the slider behaves the same way.
- The grip is pointer only and out of the tab order; the toolbar slider is the keyboard path. It sits inside its own layer (the next layer's sticky header paints over anything below the line) and ends on a lost capture or a move with the button up.
- `TRACK_H` stays as the default and is still exported, with `TRACK_H_MIN` and `TRACK_H_MAX` for hosts.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed (captures below)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Each changed test file run alone, exit 0: `timelineLayout.test.ts`, `playerStore.test.ts`, `TrackHeightGrip.test.tsx`, `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`, `TimelineTrackHeader.test.tsx`, `Timeline.test.ts`. All of `src/player/components` plus the toolbar: 137 files, 1736 tests, exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` 0 errors, oxlint 0 warnings. New tests 3 runs in a row green.

Each new test fails when its code is broken: thumbnails rule removed, grip without the `row + 1` share, grip ignoring a buttonless move, clamp without the minimum, bottom pad back to `TRACK_H`, lane top back to `TRACK_H`, scroll anchoring on a height change.

Browser check on a fixture with 8 layers (Studio dev server, headless Chromium, Linux): slider to 28 px took clips from 42 to 22 px and removed every thumbnail; dragging the third layer's edge 120 px down grew every layer by 40 px and the edge ended at the pointer (948 px, 948 px); the same drag with the timeline scrolled 150 px ended at the pointer too (904 px, 904 px).

Known limits at the small end, left as they are: at 24 px an audio waveform is about 2 px tall and the beat band covers most of the active track's clip; under 40 px text clips show their name instead of their text; the thumbnails toggle keeps showing its own setting. No test drives the marquee or keyboard scroll at a non-default height (both read `geometry.trackHeight`).

## Before

![Before: fixed 48 px layers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/be3b7803-cdbe-4876-99ca-59130e9f4656)

## After

![After: default unchanged, Layer height slider in the toolbar](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b04d0770-9c86-4a13-8ee2-7b92a2bf0341)

![After: slider at 28 px, name bars only](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fccd3143-b13c-416f-a161-30b03acef7ae)

![After: dragged a layer edge, every layer taller](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e898d61-d87b-4c22-946d-b4e3d66f28e4)

![After: drag while scrolled, edge stays under the pointer](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f076e9d-b0d2-4e96-a926-762f97024253)

title: feat(studio): a host can put its own controls before the timeline's thumbnails toggle
body:
## What

`TimelineToolbar` takes a `rightActions` prop: the host's own controls, drawn first in the toolbar's right-hand group, immediately before the thumbnails toggle.

## Why

Small on purpose: this is the one Studio change a Desktop feature waits on, and no other open Studio PR can carry it.

HyperFrames Desktop puts a Script button on the right of the timeline toolbar, just left of the thumbnails toggle. The toolbar has no slot today, so a host can only place controls beside the whole right-hand group, never inside it.

## Related work

Refs the Desktop Script button, which takes this in its Studio bump.

## How

title: fix(engine): fail the render when an injected video frame cannot decode
body: ## What An export now stops with a clear error when one of a video's extracted frames cannot be decoded, instead of finishing and shipping that frame as a blank. On Linux (BeginFrame capture) the error also arrives at once, instead of after a 60 s "capture stalled" wait and a full retry. ## Why Two bugs on the same path: 1. `injectVideoFramesBatch` swallowed decode failures (`img.decode().catch(() => undefined)`). An extracted frame that is truncated or corrupt decodes to nothing, the `` is shown anyway, and the render exits 0. 2. When any capture fails, `captureFrameErrorDiagnostics` takes a `page.screenshot()` for the debug bundle. A BeginFrame page only paints when the engine sends it a frame, so that screenshot never resolves. The worker sits until the no-progress watchdog fires 60 s later, the error is reported as "capture stalled", and the whole render is retried on a screenshot session before the real error comes back. Repro: render `packages/producer/tests/render-video-overlay-stretch` once with `--frames-cache-dir `, overwrite one cached `frame_000NN.jpg` with random bytes, render again with the same cache dir. | | main | this PR | |---|---|---| | exit code | 0 | 1 | | what happens at the bad frame | ships a black frame with a broken-image icon (16.5 dB PSNR against the clean render; neighbours 46 and 53 dB) | `Video frame for "clip-a" failed to load (inline frame): The source image cannot be decoded.` | | time to fail (4 workers, BeginFrame, 32-core Linux) | n/a | 94 s, failing 0.3 s after capture starts (with only the first fix: 217 s, via a 60 s stall and a retry) | Most of the 94 s is this fixture's own 45 s sub-composition timeline wait, paid in calibration and again in the workers, on main too. ## Related work Refs #4940, which carried fix 1 alongside a perf change that was closed for not being measurably faster. ## How - `screenshotService.ts`: a rejected `decode()` now rejects the batch with the video id and the frame source (`inline frame` for data URIs, so the error never carries megabytes of base64). The injector, every capture mode and the parallel pool already propagate a rejected hook. Retrying here would not help: the frame comes from a file on disk, so a decode failure repeats every time. - `frameCapture.ts`: the diagnostics bundle skips the page screenshot for any session launched for BeginFrame and still writes the HTML and JSON. It keys on `launchCaptureMode`, not `captureMode`, because a BeginFrame-launched session can switch to drawElement mid-session and the browser still never paints on its own; the static-dedup arm in the same file gates on the launch mode for the same reason. Not exercised: capturing a BeginFrame screenshot through `HeadlessExperimental.beginFrame` for the bundle. That would advance the page's frame clock while handling an error. - Unchanged on purpose: `hyperframes snapshot` already catches injection failures and warns that the video "will appear black/stale"; a decode failure now reaches that warning instead of passing silently. The two pinned drawElement fallback routes in `shouldRetryViaPinnedFallback` retry once on any error, so there a corrupt frame costs one retry before it fails; that retry policy predates this PR. - Other `decode().catch` sites (`frameCapture.ts` image readiness, core readiness) handle images the author placed. A broken one looks the same in preview and render, so they stay as they are. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added/updated - `screenshotService.test.ts`: a frame whose `decode()` rejects must reject the batch. On main's code it fails with `promise resolved "[ 'clip' ]" instead of rejecting`. - `frameCapture-freshFallback.test.ts`: on a BeginFrame-launched session, in both BeginFrame and drawElement capture mode, a before-capture hook that throws must reject with that error, with no page screenshot, and still write `frame-error-7.json`. On main's code it times out, as production does; keyed on `captureMode` instead, the drawElement case times out. - Both files: 50/50 pass, three runs in a row. - [x] Manual testing performed: the corrupted-frame repro above, main vs this branch. - [x] engine `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet are clean on the changed files. - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): n/a - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": none added. The BeginFrame reason lives in the name `pageScreenshotCanResolve` and in this body. ## Size 87 lines, on its own on purpose: a standalone correctness fix (renders that shipped blank frames silently) with no related open change to carry it.

title: fix(studio): one owner for gsap CDN URLs, so MotionPathPlugin matches the composition's gsap
body:
## What

Every default or fallback gsap CDN URL that Studio, the preview server, the producer and the CLI write now comes from one owner, `@hyperframes/core/gsap-cdn`. The static `hyperframes init` templates keep the version written in them. As a result Studio loads GSAP's MotionPathPlugin at the version of the composition's own gsap, as the preview server already did, and a 3.15 composition no longer gets a 3.12.5 plugin.

## Why

Six places decided which gsap URL to load, each with its own pinned version:
- Studio's plugin loader (`gsapSoftReload.ts`, the one-time preview bootstrap and the soft-reload fallback) pinned MotionPathPlugin 3.12.5. Every preview fetched it onto a 3.14 or 3.15 core, and a plugin from another version registers with a GSAP compatibility warning.
- The preview server (`preview.ts`) matched the plugin to the composition, and wrote its injected gsap, CustomEase and missing-gsap fallback at its own 3.15.0.
- The producer (`htmlCompiler.ts`) pinned 3.15.0 separately for a gsap script it cannot resolve.
- A sub-composition preview with no gsap in the project head loaded a floating `gsap@3` (`subComposition.ts`).
- `hyperframes grade-compare` wrote gsap 3.14.2 into its page.
- Core's public `GSAP_CDN` (`templates/constants.ts`) pinned gsap 3.12.5. Studio writes it into the user's file when a first tween is added to a file with no gsap (`files.ts`), and the composition generator emits it.

## Related work

Found while making the edit bench serve GSAP offline (#4968), which blocks and logs the 3.12.5 request.

## How

`packages/core/src/gsapCdn.ts` (new, listed in `package-subpaths.json`) exports two functions:
- `gsapCdnDist(version?)` gives the jsdelivr `dist/` folder for a version, falling back to the default (3.15.0) for a missing or non-numeric version.
- `motionPathPluginUrl(version?)` builds the plugin URL on top of it.

How each caller uses it:
- The preview server passes the version from the composition's gsap script tag for the plugin, and the default for what it injects.
- Studio passes the loaded runtime's `gsap.version` from the preview iframe, so an inline or self-hosted gsap is matched too.
- The producer, the sub-composition fallback, grade-compare and `GSAP_CDN` use the default.

Three values change version:
- A sub-composition preview whose project has no gsap now loads the default 3.15.0 instead of the newest 3.x.
- grade-compare's page moves from 3.14.2 to 3.15.0.
- Core's exported `GSAP_CDN` moves from 3.12.5 to 3.15.0, so a first tween added to a file with no gsap, and a generated composition, now get 3.15.0. The lint rule that tells authors to add `gsap@3` is advice text, not something we load, so it stays.

## No visible change

URLs change; nothing on screen does.

## Test plan

- [x] `gsapSoftReload.test.ts`: with the iframe's `gsap.version` at 3.14.2, both the bootstrap load and the soft-reload fallback request `gsap@3.14.2/dist/MotionPathPlugin.min.js`. Both fail on main (the 3.12.5 URL) and with the version argument dropped (the 3.15.0 default). 49/49.
- [x] `subComposition.test.ts`: a project head with no gsap loads `gsapCdnDist()`'s `gsap.min.js`; it fails on main (`gsap@3`).
- [x] `templates/base.test.ts`: `GSAP_CDN` is `gsapCdnDist()`'s `gsap.min.js`; it fails on main (3.12.5). Core's generator, index and template tests 94/94, 3 runs in a row; studio-server `files.test.ts` 92/92.
- [x] `gsapCdn.test.ts` (new): a given version is used, including a major-only `3`; a missing, empty, non-numeric or path-like version falls back. 5/5.
- [x] studio-server `subComposition`, `preview` and `preview.freshAfterWrite` tests 100/100, 3 runs in a row (they pin the injected 3.15.0 tags and a `gsap@3` composition's plugin tag). producer `htmlCompiler` module-script and media-type tests 4/4; cli grade-compare tests 10/10.
- [x] tsc for core, studio-server, studio, producer and cli; `package-subpaths` check, oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet clean.

title: fix(studio): an audio track can be muted again after it is unmuted
body:
## What was wrong

On audio, `data-hidden` is the mute: preview silences the clip and the render drops it. Studio offered that toggle on audio only while it was already on, so a mute went one way:

- **Timeline track header:** an audio track showed its toggle only while muted. A track that was muted (for example music alternatives an agent writes muted) could be unmuted once, then the control disappeared and nothing could mute it again.
- **Property panel:** the same rule for an audio clip. A selected `<hf-audio-group>` had no toggle at all, muted or not: the panel offered it only with a timeline selection id, and the timeline's element hook refuses a group because a bus has no timeline row.

## What changed

- **Track header:** every audio-only track shows a speaker, "Mute track N" / "Unmute track N". Visual tracks, and tracks that mix audio with a visual clip, keep the eye ("Hide track N" / "Show track N"). This is the rule the undo entry already used (`isAudioOnlyTrack`, now in `utils/timelineInspector.ts`), so the button and its undo entry cannot disagree.
- **Property panel (flat inspector):** any audio selection shows "Mute element" / "Unmute element" in both states. A clip toggles through the same timeline path as before. A group writes `data-hidden` on the `<hf-audio-group>` through the group attribute writer (`onSetAudioGroupAttributeQuiet`), with its own undo entry. The timeline group header is unchanged: no mute or solo there. After the write lands, the panel re-reads whatever is selected at that moment, so its label follows without a reselect.
- **One owner for the words and the icon:** `player/components/hiddenToggle.tsx` (`hiddenToggleVerb`, `HiddenToggleIcon`) is used by the track rows, the panel header and both undo labels.
- `VisibilityButton` loses its `visible` prop and the spacer it rendered when withheld; nothing withholds it now.
- Comments elsewhere that said the timeline withholds the audio control are corrected.

`aria-pressed` is not set: the label already changes with the state, as the eye's does, and a toggle should not carry both.

Not changed: the classic inspector (used only with the flat inspector turned off) still shows no visibility toggle on audio, in either state.

## Tests

The new tests fail on main and pass here:

- `Timeline.test.ts`: an audio track written muted is unmuted, muted, unmuted and muted again from its header.
- `TimelineTrackHeader.test.tsx`: an audio track offers "Mute track 1" / "Unmute track 1"; a track mixing audio and a visual clip offers the eye.
- `PropertyPanel.test.tsx`: an audible audio clip offers "Mute element" and toggles through the timeline; an audio group is unmuted, muted and unmuted from the panel header, each a `data-hidden` write on the group, with the label following only through the panel's own selection refresh; and a selection the user moved to while the write was pending is the one refreshed, never the muted bus.
- `PropertyPanelFlatHeader.test.tsx`: the header names a mute on an audio selection.

The touched and neighbouring test files pass 3 runs in a row; studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

## Before

A fixture project: one audible music track, two muted alternatives and a muted group of two voice clips. On main the audible track has no control, and after "Show track 3" the third track plays with no control left to mute it again. With the muted group selected, the panel offers nothing.

![Before: start](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fff625f1-bbbf-452b-ac03-d5508c16d450)
![Before: unmuted, no control left](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c941a577-e166-4c7e-be96-3d8e16e583dd)
![Before: muted group selected, no toggle in the panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b903f376-6181-44ad-b2a8-ddc21ce4de75)

## After

Same fixture. Every audio track has a speaker: "Unmute track 3", then "Mute track 3", and `data-hidden` is back on the clip in the file. With the group selected, the panel's speaker reads "Unmute element", then "Mute element", and `data-hidden` comes off and back on the `<hf-audio-group>` in the file.

![After: unmuted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b47b9d2d-d92f-4241-aa87-df712d220b91)
![After: muted again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/42ff7b69-2325-4beb-ac18-93ceafc5f31d)
![After: group unmuted from the panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cbf7527-8248-4ec4-9ad3-f1389a74be87)
![After: group muted again from the panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a21d6be-8620-481d-9cd8-018d97f47ed5)



## Independent review

Adversarial review at the final head: 0 blocking, 0 should fix. Earlier rounds found and this PR fixed: a refresh that re-selected the muted item if the selection moved before the save landed (now refreshes the live selection, with a test that switches selection mid-save), and an inspector re-render on every canvas hover (the selection ref is now read from the actions context, next to `previewIframeRef`). The panel toggle moved to `usePanelHiddenToggle.ts` to keep `PropertyPanelFlat.tsx` under the 600-line limit.

Notes left open on purpose:
- A fast double-click writes the same value twice.
- An audio clip inside a sub-composition shows Mute, and its refusal toast still says "hide".
- `useAutomationLanes` still reads the selection ref from the selection context (hover re-render predates this PR); a one-line follow-up.
- The shared group attribute writer resolves by DOM id, so a clip that shares its group's id can receive the group's write. Predates this PR; fixed separately.

title: feat(registry): eight ad templates show their video preview in the catalog
body:
## What

Eight of the nine ad-template blocks now declare a video preview and poster, so `hyperframes catalog --json` and Studio's Blocks tab can show them in motion (the docs site already plays them live; there they gain a poster while the player loads):
ai-chat-reveal, chatgpt-exchange, claude-exchange, message-thread-reveal, notes-reveal, notification-cascade, share-sheet-carousel, slack-notification-ad.

`ai-answer-rank` stays without a preview: no rendered preview of it exists yet, so this PR does not invent a URL for it.

The backfill script now only fills blocks that declare no preview. Before, it rewrote every block's preview to the docs-images pattern, so a rerun would have pointed these eight at files that do not exist.

## Why

The ad templates carried no `preview` field, so every catalog reader showed them without motion. Rendered previews for eight of them are already published, so pointing at them needs no new render or upload.

## Related work

None.

## How

- Each item gets the existing `preview: { video, poster }` field (same shape as every other block, `packages/core/schemas/registry-item.json`), pointing at its published preview and poster. Only the source manifests change; generated catalog files are left to the catalog automation.
- Those previews were rendered from commit 254fe4bd. Each of the eight item directories on main is identical to that commit's (`git diff --shortstat 254fe4bd origin/main -- registry/blocks/<id>` is empty for each), so the previews show the current templates.
- `scripts/backfill-block-previews.ts`: `missingBlockPreview` returns the pattern URLs only when a block declares no preview; the script body runs behind the shared `isEntrypoint` guard (`scripts/entrypoint.ts`) so the function can be imported by its test.

Known limits, left as they are:
- These previews are fixed renders. If one of the eight templates is edited later, its preview must be re-rendered and the URL updated by hand; nothing turns red on its own.
- The backfill still fills a block with no preview with the docs-images URL whether or not that file was uploaded; the documented order (render, upload, then backfill) is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Every new URL answers HTTP 200 (`curl -sIL`, 16 of 16).
- [x] Each preview is 1080x1920 with the duration its manifest declares (ffprobe); posters are JPEG.
- [x] Unit test `scripts/backfill-block-previews.test.ts` (added to `test:scripts`): fills a block with no preview; keeps a preview that points elsewhere. 3 runs green; with the old overwrite restored, the second case fails.

title: fix(core): composition scripts start after web fonts are ready, so renders repeat
body:
## What

Composition scripts now start after the page's web fonts are ready (or after 5 s, with a diagnostic naming the fonts still loading). A script that measures text (`offsetHeight`, `getBoundingClientRect`, line counts for a layout) measures it in the real font on every run, so the same project renders the same frames every time, and Studio preview shows the layout the render will produce.

## Why

Two renders of the same project could differ. A script that measured a block of text before its web font had loaded laid the scene out for the fallback font; on another run the font won the race and the layout moved. On `cloud-render-launch` (public launch films repo), main produced 4 different videos in 4 renders, with 632-701 frames differing and the worst frame at 23.9 dB PSNR (a visible layout shift).

## Before

Studio preview at this PR's base. The composition's script sizes the blue frame to the headline's measured width. It runs before the Geist web font has loaded, so it measures the fallback font (1621 px) and the frame cuts through the last letter of the real headline (1675 px). Same result in 3 of 3 runs.

![Before: the frame, sized while the fallback font was showing, stops inside the headline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b3ebc300-1152-403e-9f24-02ddd7e8418e)

## After

Same project on this branch. The script runs once the font is ready, measures 1675 px, and the frame encloses the headline. Same result in 3 of 3 runs.

![After: the frame, sized once the web font loaded, encloses the headline](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46eb6c2a-7b76-4c27-9785-065254ffd876)

Captured in Chrome 152 at 1440x900 from a fixture built for this PR (Geist Bold from the repo's catalog assets, one headline, one inline script).

## Related work

None.

## How

- **Compile time, every page builder** (core bundler, producer `compileForRender`, Studio sub-composition preview, Studio motion script): body scripts get a type the browser does not run, `text/hf-after-fonts` (`+module` for modules), via one helper `deferScriptsUntilFonts` (`core/src/compiler/scriptRuns.ts`). The runtime, render-mode, bridge, JSON, importmap, template, svg and noscript scripts are left alone.
- **Runtime, one owner** (`core/src/runtime/afterFonts.ts`, called from `entry.ts`): wait for `document.fonts.ready` (capped at `FONT_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS` = 5000, past the 3 s a `font-display: block` face holds text, far under the engine's player-ready wait), then run the scripts in parser order (classic first, then modules and `src`+`defer`), awaiting each blocking external script's load, then boot the runtime. `DOMContentLoaded`/`load` listeners those scripts add after the events passed are held and fired after boot; a script that wraps `addEventListener` meanwhile keeps its wrapper. Scene swap and template compositions use the same wait.
- **Older runtimes**: a page built by this compiler but served an older runtime (for example a pinned CDN runtime) still runs its scripts: an inline head fallback runs them at `DOMContentLoaded` unless the new runtime has claimed them.
- **Studio preview, MotionPathPlugin**: the plugin tag Studio inserts after a body gsap tag takes that tag's type, so it still runs right after gsap. Studio's plugin preload (so the first motion path a user adds does not flash) used to run on the preview iframe's `load`, which can now come before a body gsap exists; it now waits for that preview runtime's `ready` message when gsap is not there yet. Only the latest preview waits, and a runtime that already booted is not waited on, so no retired preview document is kept alive.
- **CLI `layout`, `motion-shot`, `validate`** wait for `__renderReady` (the runtime's own "booted after its scripts ran" signal, already used by `snapshot`) through one helper, `waitForRuntimeReady`, before they first sample the page, instead of `__timelines`, which exists as soon as the runtime file loads.

## Measurements

A shared 8-core Linux machine, interleaved A/B, A = main, B = this branch at an earlier head with the same gate (later commits add the old-runtime fallback and the review fixes, which do not change a render on the current runtime). The machine was shared, so the 1-minute load is stated per table.

**Determinism**, `cloud-render-launch`, 2 rounds x (A, A, B, B), load 3-40:

| | distinct videos | frames that differ | worst frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 4 of 4 | 632-701 | 23.9 dB (layout shift) |
| branch | 3 of 4 | ~87 | 44 dB (anti-aliasing level) |

The layout shift is gone. A second, much smaller source of variation remains (one region of ~87 frames, anti-aliasing level); it is not font timing and is left for its own change.

**Studio open cost**, 6 launch films x 5 runs each side, ready = the film's first frame shown, load 10-23:

| film | ready median A -> B (ms) | ready p95 A -> B | playReady median A -> B |
|---|---|---|---|
| claude-paper-launch | 1177 -> 1022 | 3691 -> 2203 | 1258 -> 1078 |
| cloud-render-launch | 972 -> 980 | 1231 -> 1234 | 1089 -> 1035 |
| figma-launch | 1052 -> 1259 | 2528 -> 1633 | 1095 -> 1327 |
| hyperframes-launch | 1599 -> 1528 | 2624 -> 1892 | 2276 -> 2042 |
| spacex-launch | 1055 -> 954 | 2265 -> 1859 | 1127 -> 1011 |
| website-to-hyperframes | 835 -> 862 | 1099 -> 1403 | 913 -> 941 |

Medians move both ways by -155..+207 ms; no consistent added delay at this load.

## Known limits

- A font that never loads holds composition scripts for 5 s, once at boot and once per template composition mounted after it; a Studio scene swap that hits it falls back to a full reload.
- External body scripts (for example gsap from a CDN) start downloading when fonts are ready rather than during parsing; the open-time table above shows no consistent cost.
- A script using the "if the document is still loading, wait for DOMContentLoaded, else run now" idiom now runs before the runtime boots rather than after.
- If a page loads the runtime twice, later scripts can run before an earlier external script has loaded. Nothing runs twice.
- A Studio preview frame that never reports ready keeps at most one page alive until the next preview load.

## Review

Independent adversarial reviews at each head after the rebase onto `dda0e757b`:
- At the rebased head: no blocker or major. Fixed: the Studio plugin preload ran before a body gsap existed (now waits for the preview runtime's `ready`); the CLI test only proved the wait was called, not that it comes before sampling (now pins the order; moving the wait below the first sample fails it).
- At the preload fix: one major, fixed. A composition with no global gsap never sent a later `ready`, so the waiting listener stayed and kept every replaced preview document in memory (7 after 6 reloads). The preload no longer waits once the runtime has booted (back to 1).
- At that fix: one minor, fixed. A frame replaced before it ever booted (a crashing or missing composition) still kept its page; now only the latest preview waits.
- At the last fix: no findings. One mutant survives harmlessly (clearing the pending slot when the retry fires only releases a reference earlier).
- Found on the way, also on main, not changed here: Studio's plugin injection misses a body gsap whose URL has a query string (`gsap.min.js?v=1`) or a `defer`/`async` gsap tag; it gets its own change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `scriptRuns.test.ts`, `entry.afterFonts.test.ts` (order, font wait, timeout diagnostic, held listeners, a wrapped `addEventListener` survives, an inline script after an external one sees its global), `compositionLoader.test.ts`, `init.swapScenes.test.ts` (swap waits for fonts), `htmlBundler.test.ts`, producer `htmlCompiler.scriptOrder.test.ts`, studio-server `subComposition.test.ts`, `routes/preview.test.ts` (MotionPathPlugin follows a deferred gsap), studio `gsapSoftReload.test.ts` (preload waits for that preview's `ready`, stops at the first one, skips a booted runtime, drops a superseded wait), cli `captureCompositionFrame.test.ts` (wait precedes each command's first sample). Each changed test file run alone and green (the latest ones 3x, and in shuffled order); each fix reverted once turns its test red.
- [x] Manual: the Before/After captures above; real Chrome probes for script order, the plugin after a deferred gsap behind a slow font, and preview document counts across reloads. Determinism and open-time runs above.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(core): a call on the playhead fires once when the preview redraws it
body:
## What

A GSAP `tl.call` that sits exactly on the playhead fires once when the runtime redraws the frame between two seeks. Before, the following forward seek fired it a second time.

Repro on main: a call at 2 s, `renderSeek(2)` (fires once), the deferred readiness pass runs, `renderSeek(3)`: the call fires again. Studio reaches this when a scene is edited while paused on a call and then played; renders reach it through the readiness pass.

## Why

`rerenderGsapTimelineAt` redraws a timeline already at `t` by stepping silently to just below `t` and back, so same-time steps apply in authored order and keyframed tweens starting at `t` show their first keyframe. Leaving `t` and landing on it again silently re-arms a zero-duration call sitting exactly at `t` (GSAP 3.15, measured: from below or above, the same; a silent render to the same time does not). The discovery pass's GSAP adapter seek runs that redraw on every readiness pass and scene swap, so the call fired again on the following eventful seek.

This replaces the approach in #4965, which skipped the adapter seek once a root timeline was bound. That seek does more than the restore it duplicated: it also redraws a root that grew in place after binding and primes keyframed tweens starting at the playhead, so skipping it traded one bug for several. Fixing the redraw itself keeps all of that.

## How

- `rerenderGsapTimelineAt` snapshots the fired state of every zero-duration callback tween in the timeline (nested included) before stepping away, and restores it after landing. A redraw then leaves every call exactly as it was: a call that already fired stays fired, and a call the playhead reached silently stays due. The redraw's drawing (same-time step order, keyframe priming) is unchanged.
- `GSAP_CALLBACK_NAMES` moves to the adapter so the helper and `init.ts`'s existing callback check share one list.

The state kept is GSAP's internal `ratio` and `_zTime` (what GSAP itself reads to decide whether a zero-duration tween fires when reached). GSAP exposes no public way to keep a call's fired state across a silent render; Studio already reads GSAP internals for the same reason (`gsapParsedTween.ts`). Two narrower versions were measured and rejected: restoring `_zTime` only for calls found at the playhead by position lost a fresh call at 0 and missed calls in repeating, reversed and double-speed timelines; rendering each call just past its start lost a call the playhead reached silently.

## Test plan

- [x] `init.test.ts`: "fires a call on the playhead once when a readiness pass runs between seeks" fails on main (2 fires) and passes here.
- [x] `gsap.steps.test.ts`: for a call on the playhead, a fresh call at 0, a reversed call, and calls in a nested, repeating nested and double-speed nested timeline, each arrived at eventfully and silently, the redraw fires the call exactly as often as no redraw. With only the restore line removed, the 5 eventful rows that double-fire on main fail (6 with the init row); the silent and fresh-at-0 rows guard against over-fixing.
- [x] `init`, `gsap.steps` and `gsap` tests 253/253, 3 runs; `src/runtime` all green; core typecheck (including the runtime one), format, lint, comment ratchet and citation check clean.

## Cost

Each redraw now lists the timeline's tween tree once to find callback tweens. Measured on GSAP 3.15 (flat object tweens, warm): +0.006 ms per redraw at 1,000 tweens, +0.15 ms at 10,000. The adapter redraws on every seek with `totalTime`, including playback frames, so this is a per-frame cost on large timelines, not a one-time one.

## Size

About 100 changed lines in `packages/core/src/runtime`, a third of them tests. It ships alone: it is the root fix for the call that fires twice, split out of #4965 after review showed that PR's approach dropped work the redraw does.

title: fix(studio-server): freeze still appears whole, so a slow extraction cannot break its undo
body:
## What

Freeze frame's still now appears in the project only once it is whole. ffmpeg writes it under an atomic temp name that project history skips, and the route then publishes it with `createFileAtomically`.

## Why

The route reserved the still's final name with an empty file (`openSync(path, "wx")`) before ffmpeg ran. Project history sweeps the folder and commits outside changes after `quietMs` (2 s by default). When extraction outlasted that, history committed the empty PNG as an outside change. Studio's claim then took over a still whose "before" was that empty file, so Cmd+Z restored a 0-byte PNG instead of removing it and left an extra "Changed outside the app" entry.

## Related work

Refs #4971 (undoing a freeze frame removes its still). This closes the slow-extraction gap in it.

## How

- `extractAndPublish` (`routes/freezeFrame.ts`): ffmpeg writes to `atomicTempPath(imagePath)`. `listProjectFiles` and the CLI watcher already skip that suffix (`isAtomicTempPath`). The bytes are then published with `createFileAtomically`, which links a complete temp sibling into place and throws EEXIST when the name is taken. The temp file is removed in `finally` on every exit.
- A taken name is still refused with 409, but now at publish time rather than before extracting. Tokens are 8 random hex characters, so this only happens with a fixed token in tests.
- `createFileAtomically` (core): on a volume without hard links it writes the destination directly. A write that failed midway (full disk) left a partial file, a corrupt still or upload. It now opens with exclusive create and removes the file only when its own write or close failed after that open (a network share may report a quota only at close). A name another writer holds is never removed.
- `freezeExtractArgs` names the format (`-c:v png -f image2 -update 1`), because the temp output no longer ends in `.png`. Without it, ffmpeg refuses with "Unable to choose an output format".

## Test plan

- New: `keeps the still out of history until it is whole, so undo removes it after a slow extraction`. Real `openProjectHistory` on the project; the stub extractor half-writes its output, calls `history.flush()` (standing in for ffmpeg outlasting the quiet time, no timers), then finishes. Then Studio's claim of `index.html` plus the still, then undo. It checks the still is gone, the page is back, and there is no outside entry. With the old route code (test kept) it fails at "still on disk after undo". With history's temp-name skip removed (`projectSignature.ts`), it fails at "no outside entry". With this change it passes.
- Updated route tests: ffmpeg's output is a temp sibling, `assets/freeze` holds only the published still on success and nothing on any failure, and a taken name keeps the first still's bytes. The two refusal tests are now one `it.each`. The concurrent-request tests meet at a barrier (each extraction writes once both have started) instead of a 5 ms real timer.
- Core: `removes the partial file a direct write leaves on a full disk, keeping the error` (fails with the cleanup removed), `removes the file when a network share reports its quota only at close` (fails with the close outside the guarded block) and `keeps another writer's file when the direct write finds the name taken`.
- `src/routes/freezeFrame.test.ts` and `src/helpers/freezeFrame.test.ts`: 28/28, and core `src/atomicFile.test.ts`: 34/34, on 3 runs in a row (vitest, Linux).
- Real ffmpeg 7.0.2 through the route's default extractor, in a throwaway test against a lavfi clip: 200, the still starts with the PNG signature, and `assets/freeze` holds exactly one file (no temp left).
- `tsc --noEmit` (core, studio-server), `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the 6 files: clean. `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues`: exit 0.

Not exercised: Windows or a real volume without hard links (the fallback is tested with an injected link failure), and a Studio walk in the browser.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: feat(cli): feedback says whether a person or an agent wrote it, with the email an app attaches
body:
## What

`hyperframes feedback` can now say who wrote a report and, when an app launched the CLI for a signed-in person, carry that person's email.

- `--source person` or `--source agent` marks the report. Any other value is refused before anything is sent.
- The email comes only from the `HYPERFRAMES_FEEDBACK_EMAIL` environment variable, which the launching app sets. It is never a flag, and the CLI's project `.env` loading now skips that key, so an agent cannot attach one through a command line or a file it writes. It is not verified: a way to reply, not proof of who sent the report.
- The feedback request gains two optional fields, `source` and `email`, the email capped at 254 characters. Without them the request body is exactly what it was before.

## Why

Apps that embed the CLI send two kinds of feedback through `hyperframes feedback`: reports a person reviews and sends from a feedback button, and reports their agent files on its own. The team needs to tell the two apart when reading them, and to be able to reply to a signed-in person. Today both look the same and carry no way to reach the person.

## Related work

An embedding app can pass `--source person` from its feedback button and `--source agent` for its agent, and set the email only while the person is signed in, once this ships in a CLI release. The feedback service reads the two new fields separately; until it does, they are ignored.

## How

- `src/utils/feedbackSource.ts` owns both values: `parseFeedbackSource` (absent, valid, or refused) and `feedbackEmail` (the one environment variable, trimmed, blank as absent).
- The `.env` loader moved from `src/cli.ts` into `src/utils/dotEnv.ts` unchanged except that it skips the feedback email key; `cli.ts` still imports it lazily.
- `feedback` checks `--source` right after `--rating`, so a bad value fails the same way whether or not telemetry is on.
- `submitFeedback` adds the two fields to the existing POST; `JSON.stringify` drops them when undefined.
- The email goes only into that POST. It is not added to the telemetry event, the printed output, the environment summary or a `--file-issue` draft.
- `feedback` is no longer described as anonymous: it is, unless the launching app attaches an email.
- Docs: the `feedback` section of the CLI reference and "About feedback data" in the feedback guide say what the new flag and variable do. `--source` applies to rating reports; a `--search-miss` report carries neither.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `feedbackSource.test.ts`: parsing and the variable.
  - `feedback.test.ts`: a person report carries the email, which stays out of the telemetry event and the environment summary; an agent report without the variable carries none; an unknown source is refused with nothing sent.
  - `dotEnv.test.ts`: the loader's existing behaviour, and that it never takes the email from a project file.
  - `submitFeedback.test.ts`: both fields reach the body and the email is capped.
- [x] 22/22 across the four files, three runs in a row. Each guard has a mutation that fails a test: removing the email from the submit call, accepting any source, dropping the `.env` skip, and adding the email to telemetry.
- [x] The existing exact-body test still passes unchanged, so callers that pass neither field send the same request as before.
- [x] Documentation updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".
- [ ] Not exercised: a live POST to the feedback endpoint (the tests stub `fetch`), the embedding app's side, which lands separately, and `cli.commands.test.ts` on my box, where the engine's built `@hyperframes/core` subpaths were missing; CI runs it.

title: fix(studio): trimming keeps the playhead still; clips snap to the ruler grid
body:
## What

Two timeline editing fixes in Studio:

1. Trimming a clip's edge no longer moves the playhead. The preview still shows the frame at the dragged edge, but the playhead, the time readout and the current time stay where they were paused. Releasing or cancelling the trim puts the playhead's own frame back.
2. Dragging or trimming a clip also snaps to the ruler's visible tick lines at the current zoom, with the same guide the clip-edge snap draws. The magnet toggle (N) turns it off together with the other snap targets.

## Why

The playhead used to follow the dragged edge during a trim and jump back on release, so the paused time was lost while editing (and in hosts that route seeks through their own handler it did not always come back). Snapping only to clips, beats and the playhead made it hard to place a clip on a round time.

## Related work

Refs #4163 (added the edge-frame preview this keeps, without the playhead move).

## How

- **Preview frame without a seek:** `store/previewFrameStore.ts` owns the one way to show a frame without moving time. `useTimelinePlayer` subscribes and puts the frame on the adapter only (no `liveTime` publish, no `setCurrentTime`), ignores it while playing, and puts the playhead's frame back when it clears. The trim sets it on each move; the gesture teardown (release, Escape, cancel) clears it. `useTimelineClipDrag` no longer takes `onSeek`.
- **The edge frame never becomes the transport time:** while a paused preview frame is shown, `getAdapter()` (the one accessor every transport reader uses) hands out a view whose `getTime()` is the playhead's time and whose `play()` starts from it, unless the caller seeked through the view first (play's rewind to the in-point). So pausing, playing, frame-stepping or a reload promoting mid-trim all keep the paused position.
- **Trims snap to the playhead now:** the old exclusion existed only because the edge drove the playhead; with the playhead fixed, `includePlayhead` had no other caller and is removed.
- **Ruler grid:** `getTimelineGridStep` in `timelineRulerGeometry.ts` returns the spacing of the drawn lines (minor ticks when drawn, else major) from the same helpers `generateTicks` uses, so the grid and the ruler cannot drift. Snapping to it is arithmetic (nearest multiple), not a target list: at frame zoom a long timeline has over 100k lines.
- **A guide only where the clip lands:** clip files store the local start (and, for a resize, the duration) to the centisecond. `savedClipEdges` in `timelineElement.ts`, beside `toAuthoredStart`, says where a clip's edges sit once saved, including clips nested in a sub-composition; `guideIfSaved` drops any snap guide (grid, playhead, clip edge, beat) whose saved edge would land a pixel or more away. A grid line between two centiseconds snaps at its saved time, or not at all at extreme zoom.
- **Priority:** the grid is a fallback. A clip edge, playhead or beat within the snap radius always wins, on either edge of a moved clip.
- There was no held snap-off modifier for clip drags (Alt unlinks linked clips), so none was added; the magnet toggle is the off switch.
- **Walk:** `tests/e2e/timeline-trim-snap.mjs` with its own fixture, run in the existing Studio browser-check step of `ci.yml`.

## Before

Mid-trim: the playhead has jumped to the dragged edge (readout 00:02).

![Before: playhead follows the trimmed edge](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5c386393-f030-4163-a2e1-174f891523c3)

A clip dropped 6 px past a ruler line stays 6.5 px off it.

![Before: dropped clip sits off the ruler line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f7214e7-acba-47b1-a3ae-d94da16cd324)

## After

Mid-trim: the playhead stays at 1.2 s (readout 00:01); the guide marks the snapped edge.

![After: playhead stays while the edge is trimmed](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a801a420-b123-4106-b660-8c13e1fc7c90)

The same drop lands on the line (0.9 px, the centisecond save).

![After: dropped clip lands on the ruler line](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27644fe8-a35d-4a64-9ccf-397b6953cec6)

## What I measured

- Walk `timeline-trim-snap.mjs` in headless Chrome on Linux, 1440x900, repo fixture: on main the playhead moved 306 px during the trim and the clip landed 6.5 px off the line (exit 1); with this branch 3 of 3 runs passed (playhead at 1.203 s before, during and after the trim within 1 px; clip 0.9 px from the line).
- Unit tests (vitest), each file 3 runs, all exit 0: `timelineSnapping.test.ts` 20, `timelineClipDragPreview.test.ts` 48, `timelineLayout.test.ts` 46, `useTimelineClipDrag.resize.test.tsx` 27, `useTimelinePlayer.seek.test.ts` 19, `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts` 36, `useTimelinePlayer.test.ts` 34, `Timeline.test.ts` 83. Full `packages/studio` suite: 663 files, 7301 tests passed, exit 0. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt clean; every touched production file is under 600 lines.
- Each new test fails when its code is broken (17 deliberate breaks, only the targeted tests went red), among them: no grid line, grid not demoted across edges, preview calling `seek()`, preview applied while playing, frame not cleared at gesture end, no `getAdapter` view, play ignoring its own rewind, an unsavable grid line snapping, a trim or move guide kept where the saved edge misses, a nested clip's host offset ignored, a move judged by a rounded duration, a grid where the ruler draws no lines.

## What I did NOT exercise

- macOS or a GPU: the walk ran headless on Linux, so the captures prove behaviour, not pixels.
- HyperFrames Desktop: it picks this up on its next Studio version bump; not walked there yet.
- Group trims and group moves against the grid in a browser (covered only by unit tests).
- Frame display mode in a browser; extreme zoom where lines fall between centiseconds (unit-tested only).
- A clip whose authored duration runs past the composition end: the timeline shows it cut at the end, and moving it snaps that displayed tail (as on main). The saved tail sits further out. Fixing that needs the authored duration carried from the runtime manifest into timeline rows; left for a follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed (browser walk above)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: fix(media-use): skip a .env folder when loading HeyGen credentials
body:
## What

`loadEnvFromDir` in media-use's HeyGen helper now loads only a `.env` that is a file, and walks past a `.env` folder to the parents above it.

## Why

`heygen-tts.mjs` and `audio.mjs` crashed with `EISDIR: illegal operation on a directory, read` when any of the five folders they search held a `.env` directory (some home folders have one). `existsSync` is true for a folder, so `readFileSync` read a directory. The CLI's own `.env` loaders already survive this (they catch the read error); only this helper threw.

## Related work

None. Small on purpose: a standalone crash fix in the TTS path that HyperFrames Desktop's next media-use pin needs; no open PR touches this file to carry it.

## How

`loadEnvFromDir` now reads each candidate `.env` directly and treats `ENOENT`, `ENOTDIR` and `EISDIR` as "no env file here", so the walk goes on to the parent. There is no check before the read, so the file cannot change between a check and the read (CodeQL `js/file-system-race`). Any other read error (an unreadable `.env`, say) still throws, as before. Two cases that main skipped now throw too, `ELOOP` from a `.env` symlink that points at itself and `EACCES` from a start folder you cannot enter; neither caller can reach the second, and both are config errors worth seeing. A `.env` that is a named pipe or a symlink to a file loads as before. `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated for the media-use change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `loadEnvFromDir skips a .env folder and loads the .env file above it` in `heygen.test.mjs`.
- [x] The new test fails on main with `EISDIR` (5 pass, 1 fail) and passes with the fix: 6/6, three runs in a row on Linux.
- [x] On Linux: a `.env` FIFO loads; a missing `.env` walks up to the parent's; an unreadable `.env` still throws `EACCES`.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(media-use): a slow download no longer leaves an empty asset that undo brings back
body:
## What

media-use no longer puts an empty file at an asset's final name while it downloads. The id is still reserved on disk, but now by an empty marker under an atomic temp name (`<asset>.hfXXXXXX.tmp`), which project history skips. The asset appears under its real name only when it is written, and the marker is removed when the reservation commits or rolls back.

Also: `skills/media-use/SKILL.md` now tells the agent to tell the person, before generating a voiceover or an avatar video, that signing in to the heygen CLI with OAuth (`heygen auth login --oauth`) gives a free allowance for TTS voiceover and avatar videos, while an API key bills API credits. This comes from `references/setup-providers.md`; no allowance amounts are stated.

## Why

`allocateId` reserved an id by creating an empty file at the final path (`.media/<type>/<id><ext>`, flag `wx`) before the download. Studio's project history does not skip `.media`, and it commits outside changes after `quietMs` (2 s by default). When the download took longer, history committed the 0-byte file as an outside change; undoing past it later restored an empty asset.

## Related work

Same shape as #4982 (freeze-frame stills), which moved the still's reservation to a temp name that history skips.

## How

- `allocateId` (`media-use/lib/manifest.mjs`): under the existing lock, creates the marker `<final path>.hf<6 hex>.tmp` with `wx`, the same suffix as core's `atomicTempPath`. Studio's `projectSignature` and the CLI file watcher skip it via `isAtomicTempPath`. `nextFreeId` still counts it (its name starts with the id), so a concurrent resolve cannot take the same id during the download.
- `withReservedFile` / `withReservedFileSync`: a committed reservation removes only the marker; a failed or empty one removes the marker and any partial asset at the final path.
- The writers are unchanged: `freezeUrl` buffers the whole body and writes once, cache imports copy a complete file, and the LUT paths already rename a validated file into place.
- media-use's scripts also ship standalone in `skills/media-use` and cannot import `@hyperframes/core`, so the suffix is written out here and pinned by a test against core's `isAtomicTempPath`. `skills/media-use/scripts/lib/manifest.mjs` is the byte-identical copy the parity check requires.
- `manifest.d.mts` declares the three exports the new TypeScript test uses, like `config-lock.d.mts`.

## Test plan

- New `src/media-use/manifestReservation.test.ts` (vitest, outside `lib/` so the build does not ship it, imports core's real `isAtomicTempPath`): while a reservation is being filled, the type folder holds nothing history would commit, and a second `allocateId` gets the next id; afterwards only the asset remains. Fails on main (`expected [ 'bgm_001.wav' ] to deeply equal []`). It also fails when the marker uses a name core does not treat as temp (`bgm_001.wav.reserved`). A second test writes a partial file and then fails the download: the folder is left empty. It fails if the rollback stops removing the partial file.
- `manifest.test.mjs`: the MU-23 test now checks that the marker holds the id and that nothing sits at the final name; the LUT allocation test checks the marker.
- All media-use and skills `node:test` files plus the copy-parity check (the CI skills job's set): 772 pass, 0 fail, 3 runs in a row. The vitest media-use tests pass 3 times. Linux, Node 22.
- CLI `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt and the pre-commit hooks (fallow, skills manifest) are clean.

Not exercised: a Studio walk with a real slow download. The test uses the same `isAtomicTempPath` check that history's `projectSignature` uses.

## Size

One reservation change in `manifest.mjs` (plus its skills copy), one declaration file, two new tests, two updated assertions, one SKILL.md line.
