title: feat(media-use): clone, list and delete HeyGen voices, and accept a host OAuth token
body:
## What

Adds voice cloning to media-use and lets a host app hand media-use an OAuth token.

- `skills/media-use/audio/scripts/heygen-voice.mjs`, three commands:
  - `clone <audio.mp3|audio.wav> --name <name>`: sends the file as base64 to `POST /v3/voices/clone`, polls `GET /v3/voices/<id>` every 2 s (120 s deadline) until `complete`, prints `{"voice_id":"..."}`.
  - `delete <voice_id>`: `DELETE /v3/voices/<id>`.
  - `list --prefix <name-prefix>`: pages `GET /v3/voices?type=private` and prints `[{voice_id, name, created_at}]` for names starting with the prefix. A voice with no name is skipped; a page token HeyGen repeats stops the list with an error instead of looping.
  - Any API refusal prints HeyGen's own `error.message` (else the raw body) to stderr and exits 1.
- `lib/heygen.mjs`: `HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN` is now the first credential source, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`, so it is treated as OAuth (same cli-source headers as a credentials-file OAuth token). `heygenJSON` errors now carry `status` and the full response `body`.
- `heygen-tts.mjs`: a failed synthesis prints HeyGen's own refusal message (for example a deleted voice or a credit limit) instead of a generic line or the raw response, so a caller can show it or act on it. The message comes from one place, `heygenMessage` in `lib/heygen.mjs`, shared with `heygen-voice.mjs`.
- `heygenJSON` returns `{}` for a success with an empty body, so a `DELETE` answered with 204 reads as done.
- `references/tts.md`: routes table, credential order and a short cloned-voices section.

## Why

A desktop host signs the user in and wants to pass that token through, then clone the user's voice and narrate with it through the existing `heygen-tts.mjs`.

## Related work

Rebased onto main after #4988 merged; the token check sits at the top of the new `resolveCredential`, ahead of the API keys and the unreadable-credentials path. `skills-manifest.json` was regenerated with `gen-skills-manifest.ts`, not merged by hand.

## How

- `heygen-tts.mjs --voice <cloned id>` needed no change: `resolveVoiceId` returns a pinned voice as-is.
- The list response has no `created_at` (per the List Voices reference), so `list` reads `GET /v3/voices/<id>` for each match. The account's clone limit bounds that.
- `delete` of an unknown id exits 1 with HeyGen's `Voice not found` message. The API reference suggests callers treat that 404 as success in a delete-then-list flow; that choice is left to the caller.
- No size limit is enforced: the clone reference documents none. Background-noise removal keeps the API default (on).
- Mirrors `heygen voice clone create` from the HeyGen CLI for the request body.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `heygen-voice.test.mjs` (mocked fetch, injected clock and sleep, no real waits) covers clone happy path with polling, wav media type, refusal verbatim, `failed` status, the 120 s deadline, unsupported file type, delete ok and 404 verbatim, list with pagination and prefix filter, list refusal, and the env token on the wire. `heygen.test.mjs` covers the env token winning over an API key and reading as OAuth.
- [x] Ran `node --test` on `heygen-tts`, `heygen-voice`, `lib/heygen` and `lib/tts` tests 3 times in a row on a remote Linux box: 39/39 each run. Each fix fails its test when put back: the env-token line, the plain refusal, the `voice_id` fallback, the id escaping, the nameless voice and the repeated page token (which fails at once instead of hanging). `gen-skills-manifest.ts --check` is in sync; format and the comment ratchet pass.
- [x] `heygen-tts.test.mjs` spawns the script against a refusing endpoint and asserts HeyGen's message reaches stderr.
- [x] Manual: ran `heygen-tts.mjs "Hello" --voice <cloned id> --speed 1.2 --words w.json -o out.mp3` against a mocked fetch; the speech request carried the cloned `voice_id`, the speed and the Bearer token, and the words file was written.
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: perf(studio): long clips mount only the picture tiles in view
body:
## What

A clip's picture strip on the timeline now mounts only the tiles near the screen instead of one tile per frame width across the whole clip. This covers video, image and composition clips.

## Why

At full zoom (48 px per frame), a 10-minute clip is 864,000 px wide. Its strip mounted 18,000 tiles, about 36,000 elements, for that one clip. `MAX_VISIBLE_THUMBNAIL_FRAMES` caps how many frames get decoded, not how many tiles are mounted. The cost lands on every zoom step and on every scroll frame that has to lay out and paint the timeline.

## Related work

Refs the timeline virtualization work (`useTimelineRowVirtualization`, `TIMELINE_VIEWPORT_BUDGETS`). Rows are virtualized there, but a single clip's tiles were not.

## How

- **Only long clips.** A strip up to 4,096 px wide (about two screens) keeps every tile, as before, and is never measured or re-rendered on a scroll; it still shares the one scroll listener and is skipped in each frame's loop. Longer strips mount only the tiles near the screen.
- **The span.** `useThumbnailStripSize` is the hook all three strips already measure through. For a long strip it also reports the strip's on-screen span against the window, rounded outward to 512 px chunks, and clamped to the strip, so a strip re-renders only when it crosses a chunk. A strip more than 256 px off screen in either direction gets one empty span, the same on either side.
- **One shared tile row.** The new `ThumbnailTiles` mounts the tiles inside that span and pads the skipped width on the left, so every tile sits exactly where it did before. All three strips use it.
- **Refreshing on a scroll, in the same frame.** All strips share one scroll listener, one ResizeObserver, two IntersectionObservers and one animation frame. Each long strip remembers its last measured box. On a scroll frame, the hook reads each scroller's offset once and shifts every remembered box by the change. It measures the strips whose shifted box lands within 256 px of the screen, and every strip already showing tiles, since a move without a scroll (rows removed above it, a dock resize) leaves its box stale. Every read happens before one `flushSync` commit. A jump to anywhere in a long timeline therefore measures exactly the strips it brings on screen, in that frame, at the cost of a short scroll; far strips cost arithmetic only.
- **Moves without a scroll.** Two invisible elements cover each strip's unmounted ends. An IntersectionObserver re-measures when either nears the screen, whatever moved the strip: a drag (the drag copy moves through a wrapper), undo, a typed start time, a dock divider, a window resize. A second IntersectionObserver measures a strip as soon as it comes within 256 px of the screen. Both use `rootMargin` plus `scrollMargin`, so the band also applies inside the timeline's own scroller.
- **Why the window.** I measure against the window rather than the timeline's scroll snapshot because that snapshot is not published while scrolling when row virtualization is off (`useTimelineScrollViewport`).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## What I measured

**Unit tests** (`VideoThumbnail.test.tsx`). Each new test fails with its piece of the fix removed:
- A 10-minute clip at full zoom mounts fewer than 60 tiles, and they cover the window before and after each scroll. On main this fails with `expected 12170 to be less than 60`; without the scroll refresh it fails with `expected 431041 to be less than or equal to 100000`.
- A strip moved by something other than a scroll, as a drag moves its copy, still covers the window. Without the edge watch it fails with `expected 431041 to be less than or equal to 430500`.
- A clip wholly off screen mounts no tile.
- In `useThumbnailStripSize.test.tsx`, each fails on the head before its fix:
  - near strips are re-measured in one shared frame;
  - a jump measures the strips it brings on screen in that same frame;
  - a strip measured between a scroll and that scroll's frame is not shifted by the scroll twice;
  - strips carried from one side of the screen to the other do not re-render;
  - a strip wholly on screen does not re-render when it moves;
  - a strip on screen keeps its tiles after a move without a scroll followed by a scroll (from review);
  - a vertical scroll measures the strip it brings on screen in that frame;
  - a strip ending just off screen keeps its edge tiles (the 256 px band);
  - a short clip keeps every tile up to exactly 4,096 px, and is never re-measured on a scroll;
  - a strip far above or below the screen mounts nothing;
  - a strip is measured as it comes near, without waiting for a frame;
  - a scroll reads no strip far from the screen.
- Removing the left padding fails both tests, and in `ThumbnailTiles.test.tsx` the first mounted tile sits exactly where the padding ends.
- The changed tests pass 3 runs in a row.

**Suites and checks.** The Studio player, hooks and components suites pass (5,809 tests). oxlint, `tsc --noEmit` and the comment ratchet are clean.

**Timeline viewport gate.** The first version made the gate's 1,000-row arm (row virtualization off) take about 3.3 s per interaction. A profile of that arm showed every scroll frame reading the position of all 1,000 strips (14,331 forced style-and-layout passes against 134 on main). CI's gate at 32d5ffd6 passes both arms:
- 1,000 rows: interaction p95 48.5 ms (limit 75), frame p95 33.3 ms (limit 75), with 20,929 timeline elements on the first run against main's 20,900. Main's recent runs of this arm are 43 to 61 ms and 17 to 33 ms; the p95 moves between runs with frame timing (the previous head measured 33.0 ms), so the element count is the steadier comparison.
- virtualized: interaction p95 33.2 ms (limit 58.3), frame p95 16.8 ms (limit 25), with 1,230 timeline elements, as on main.

**Browser run, long clip** (measured at 75676618, before the gate commits; those change when strips re-measure, not what a long clip mounts). Studio dev server and headless Chrome, 1440 x 900, on a project built from the repo's `studio-open` fixture plus a generated 10-minute test-pattern video. The script zooms from fit to full (14 presses), then scrolls the timeline. Runs on main and on that head alternated, 3 each, on a shared Linux box under load (10 to 15 on 8 cores). Medians:
- Elements on the page: 37,154 to 1,030.
- Tiles in the clip: 18,000 to 43.
- Zoom to full: 7.1 s to 1.9 s, and the slowest single press from 1.8 s to 0.5 s.
- Main-thread work over 20 scroll frames: 1,973 ms to 843 ms, with layout going from 105 ms to 27 ms and paint from 200 ms to 42 ms.

**What is on screen.** Screenshots taken 1 minute into the clip are byte-identical before and after.

**Drag.** In the browser, I dragged the long clip 1,000 px at full zoom. With this head, its picture covers all 1,432 visible pixels at every step. An independent review of this PR's first version found its drag copy ran out of picture: 1,192 of 1,432 px covered, and the gap stayed. That led to the edge watch above.

## What I did NOT exercise

- **Scroll frame time on a machine with a GPU.** The box I measured on has no GPU. Each scroll frame costs about 500 ms there on both sides, almost all of it Chrome's software rasterizer (the trace shows the main thread waiting on `DisplayItemList::Raster`). So I report main-thread work, not wall-clock frame time.
- **A strip moved by a layout change, not a scroll.** Zoom, a row insert or a dock resize moves strips without a scroll. The observers repair a strip as it nears the screen, after the frame that showed it, so such a move can show one frame without pictures on a long clip.
- **The long-clip numbers on the final code.** They were measured at 75676618; the later commits change only when strips re-measure.
- **Browsers without `scrollMargin`.** They catch an unmounted end only once it is on screen, so one frame there can show a blank strip. Chrome and Electron support it.
- **A clip growing while it scrolls.** If a trim or zoom widens a clip and a scroll frame reads it before the resize report, one layout pass can hold its old last tile off screen. The review found the resize report corrects it before paint in that frame; I did not watch it in a browser.
- **The audio waveform canvas.** It is untouched; it draws one canvas the width of the clip.
- **Desktop.** It picks this up with its next Studio bump.

## Before

The timeline at full zoom, a minute into the 10-minute clip. The badge shows counts read from the page at capture time: 18,000 tiles mounted for this one clip.

![Before: 18,000 tiles mounted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cd4f73fc-5bf9-4bbf-b6e9-07c728eb081d)

## After

The same view with 64 tiles mounted. Below that: a dragged long clip that keeps its picture, and the numbers.

![After: 64 tiles mounted, same view](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a6a306a1-1cb4-45f6-848a-4ba77f600f54)

![After: the dragged clip keeps its picture](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bfc420a5-a437-4dde-b277-a2bab9d6f706)

![Before and after numbers on the final code](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/56c7cf1b-43ab-44fa-a002-3dee28622955)

title: fix(studio): the host can name Split's key on the toolbar and bind the clip menu's link keys
body:
## What changes for a user

A host app that binds Split to a key other than S (passing `splitShortcut` to the timeline, #4985) now gets the same key in the toolbar's Split tooltip, so the toolbar and the clip menu agree. Default stays S.

A host app that mounts the timeline without Studio's own hotkeys can now bind the clip menu's link keys (Cmd+L link/unlink, Option+Shift+D detach audio, Option+Backspace delete this clip only) by calling the exported `dispatchLinkShortcut` from its own keydown handler. Before this, those menu rows showed keys that did nothing in such a host.

## How

- `TimelineToolbar` takes `splitShortcut`, the same prop name and type as `Timeline`'s, with the same default (`SPLIT_SHORTCUT_HINT`). A host passes its one Split key to both.
- `@hyperframes/studio` exports `dispatchLinkShortcut` and `LinkShortcutCallbacks`.
- `dispatchLinkShortcut` now ignores keys typed into a text field itself, so a host cannot delete a clip with Option+Backspace while the user edits text. Studio's `useAppHotkeys` drops its own copy of that check; its behaviour is unchanged.

## Tests

- `TimelineToolbar.test.tsx`: the Split tooltip names S by default and the host's key when given.
- `linkShortcuts.test.ts`: Option+Backspace inside an input leaves the clip alone.
- `timelineChromeExports.test.tsx`: Cmd+L through the package export unlinks a linked pair.

Each fails with its change reverted; the three files pass 3 runs in a row.

## Before

Studio dev server on `main`, standing in for a host: `App.tsx` passes `splitShortcut="⌘B"` to the toolbar and the timeline (an uncommitted capture patch). Fixture: a 6 s test-pattern clip, playhead at 2.5 s. The clip menu names ⌘B but the toolbar tooltip still says S.

![Before: toolbar tooltip says Split at playhead (S)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9d25c6f1-92e6-459d-9595-df20feea15f8)
![Before: clip menu Split row says ⌘B](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/649c184f-abb5-4794-b996-a8a0ad1fdbf1)

## After

Same patch on this branch: the toolbar tooltip now names ⌘B, matching the clip menu (unchanged, as in Before). The link-shortcut export has no visual change in Studio; its test above covers it.

![After: toolbar tooltip says Split at playhead (⌘B)](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a2c87f6b-28d2-4af9-beb2-8e82752ce4b8)

title: fix(media-use): a credentials folder means no HeyGen credential, not a crash
body:
## What

`heygenCredential` in media-use's HeyGen helper keeps its "never throws" contract when `~/.heygen/credentials` (or `$HEYGEN_CONFIG_DIR/credentials`) cannot be read. A folder at that path no longer crashes with `EISDIR`; it means no credential.

## Why

It checked `existsSync(file)` and then called `readFileSync(file)`. `existsSync` is true for a folder, so the read threw `EISDIR`. That crashed every caller that only probes for a credential: the telemetry tag in `packages/cli/src/media-use/resolve.mjs:328` (through `heygenAuthMethod`), `heygenAvailable` in `tts.mjs:28`, and `audio.mjs:119`, which should fall back to the local voice instead. The check-then-read is also the race CodeQL flags as `js/file-system-race`. A reviewer of #4988 spotted this.

## Related work

Refs #4988 (merged), which fixed the same crash for `.env`. Small on purpose: no open PR touches this file to carry it.

## How

The credentials file is read directly, without a check first. Any read failure counts as "no credential": a missing file, a folder, a `~/.heygen` the user cannot open (left root-owned by a `sudo` login, say), or a symlink loop. That matches the function's documented contract and what main did for every case except the folder. The one change from main: an existing credentials file that can't be read now also counts as no credential instead of throwing. `heygenAuthHeaders` still throws its sign-in hint when HeyGen is actually needed. `existsSync` is no longer imported. `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `heygenAuthMethod returns null when the credentials path is a folder` (fails on main with `EISDIR`) and `... is a symlink loop` (guards the case main already handled).
- [x] 8/8 pass, three runs in a row, on Linux. A `chmod 000` config folder still returns `null`, as on main.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: test(studio): the edit bench render serves GSAP from the repo, never the CDN
body:
## What this fixes

The edit accuracy case `rotate-size-px-r0-root-z200-on` failed its `render` metric on some CI runs and passed on others with the same code (65.62 px vs 0.03 px). The failing runs also took about 30 s longer (60 s vs 29 s).

Cause: the bench's render step renders the saved project through the producer's own browser, and that browser fetched GSAP from cdn.jsdelivr.net. #4968 made the Studio half serve GSAP from the repo, but not this step. When jsdelivr stalled, the fixture's blocking GSAP script held the page load until Chrome gave the request up (about 30 s), GSAP never ran, the producer's short wait after a failed script found no timeline, and the frame showed the box at its 0 s size (240x160) instead of its 2 s size (300x200). The failing CI runs already included #4968.

A second page had the same problem: the producer's static-frame dedup opens a verification page that loads the project again from the network. The bench captures one frame, so it needs no dedup.

## Change

- `render.mjs` serves the fixture's CDN requests from the repo on the producer's page (the same `serveFixtureAssetsLocally` the Studio half uses, now exported from `case.mjs`), before the page loads.
- `render.mjs` turns static-frame dedup off for its one-frame render, so no second page fetches GSAP.
- `render.test.mjs` runs `renderBox` with the producer mocked and checks that the interception pattern covers the fixture's GSAP URL, that GSAP is served from the repo's `gsap` dist, and that dedup is off.

## Evidence

Same saved project, a proxy that accepts connections and never answers standing in for a stalled jsdelivr:

| Render step | CDN | `render` | Case time |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | answers | 0.03 px | 30 s |
| main | stalls | 65.62 px (the CI failure) | 92 s |
| this branch | stalls | 0.03 px, 3 of 3 runs | 27 s each |

- `render.test.mjs`: 3 of 3 runs exit 0. Six mutations each turn it red: no local serving ("expected [] to deeply equal ['Fetch.enable', …]"), dedup left on ("expected { playerReadyTimeout: 10000 } to match object { staticFrameDedup: false }"), an interception pattern for another host, the pattern without its trailing `*` (Chrome then matches only the exact URL; the test matches patterns the way Chrome does), and a pattern narrowed by `requestStage: "Response"` or by `resourceType: "Document"` (the test checks the whole pattern object).
- The edit accuracy test folder: 11 files, 60 tests, exit 0.
- oxfmt, oxlint, comment ratchet, comment citations and fallow audit: all exit 0.

Chrome still opens two speculative connections to jsdelivr per run with the CDN stalled. Nothing waits on them: the case time matches the run with the CDN answering.

## No visible change

Test harness only; nothing a Studio user sees changes.

## Why it ships alone

Under 100 lines on purpose: this flake can turn the required edit accuracy gate red on any unrelated Studio PR, and the next change in this area (the crop-scale render fix) touches the runtime and waits on its own decision, so nothing ready can carry it.

title: fix(core): the preview redraw leaves animations after the playhead as the seek drew them
body:
## What

The runtime's frame redraw (`rerenderGsapTimelineAt`) now leaves everything that is not on the playhead as the seek before it left it. Visible result:

- **A scene's opening `set` disappears when you step back off the scene's start.** A scene at 2 s whose first step shows a box: scrub to 3, then 2, then 1.99. On main the box stays visible at 1.99 s, before its scene starts; here it is hidden, as without the redraw. Checked in headless Chrome through the built runtime, 3 runs each: main opacity 1, this branch 0.

Also fixed in the same helper (exact on GSAP, not shown on screen in my Chrome probes):

- A reversed child that starts after the playhead is no longer drawn at its end. A reversed `set(el, { opacity: 0.8 }, 2)`, seek to 1, redraw: main 0.8, the seek alone 0.2. Same for an `immediateRender` set, a reversed set inside a nested timeline playing over the playhead, and a reversed nested timeline.
- Two sets on the playhead keep their authored order on the next seek (`set(x: 50)` then `set(x: 100, onComplete)` at 2; seek 2, redraw, seek 2.01: main shows 50).
- A call in an otherwise empty nested timeline, arrived at silently, fires as often as without the redraw (the non-blocking follow-up from #4981's review).
- An `addPause` callback inside a reversed, repeating yoyo scene fires once, not twice, when a seek follows a redraw.

## Before

Main, headless Chrome 152 through the built runtime (After built at 26523e6e; the later commits change only how scene lengths are kept), a fixture whose second scene (at 2 s) opens with a `set` that shows the card: scrub to 3 s, 2 s, then 1.99 s. The card stays drawn at 1.99 s, before its scene starts.

![Before: main keeps the scene 2 card at 1.99 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b307befb-02a2-4efa-ace2-ef0898749942)

## After

This branch, same fixture and steps: the card is gone at 1.99 s.

![After: this branch hides the scene 2 card at 1.99 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bff4e123-9839-4b08-96ff-aba3073a27e8)

## Why

The redraw steps silently to just below `t` and back. Two things leaked out of that round trip:

1. GSAP's backward render visits every child that ends after the new time, so the step down drew reversed children that start later at their end; the step back up is a forward render, which skips children that have not started, so nothing undid it.
2. GSAP remembers, per zero-duration tween and per nested timeline, which side of its start the playhead last landed on (`ratio`, `_zTime`). The round trip left that memory on the redraw's side. A nested timeline then believed it had already been left from below, so the next backward seek skipped it (the scene case). #4981 restored the memory only for tweens with callbacks, so a set without one disagreed with its sibling (the ordering case).

## How

- Children that start after the playhead (in the root, and inside nested timelines that span it) sit out both silent steps: their time scale is held at 0, which GSAP's render loops skip, and restored in a `finally`. GSAP computes a timeline's duration from its children's time scales, so the duration is settled before the hold, and the cached lengths of every ancestor of a held child are snapshotted then and put back afterwards: a paused sub-composition that GSAP re-measured during the round trip would otherwise keep a shortened length and freeze for the rest of a render (caught by the `style-5-prod` render regression in review). Putting the lengths back, rather than re-measuring, keeps the root's length independent of what happens to be paused at that moment.
- `ratio`, `_zTime` and `_act` are restored for every nested timeline and every zero-duration tween, not only callback tweens (`_act`: the redraw marks a scene it visits active, and an active scene with a restored start mark re-runs its pause on the next seek). `GSAP_CALLBACK_NAMES` goes back to `init.ts`, its only user.
- `totalDuration` is passed to the helper by both callers and added to `RuntimeTimelineLike`, which also drops a cast in `init.ts`.

Reading and writing `_ts`, `_act`, `ratio` and `_zTime` is the same GSAP 3.15 internals contract #4981 already relies on.

Known limits, from the independent review's sweeps (all rare, none worse than main in the render model): the scene lengths are put back as they were measured before the redraw, so a function-based value that adds a child to its scene during the redraw's first render keeps the old length; and in 1 of 20,000 modelled films a call at the end of a repeating `repeatRefresh` scene fires after a silent discovery redraw. The helper also assumes the timeline was rendered at `t` first (both callers seek right before it). A direct caller that skips that, on a timeline with reversed nested timelines, can still differ from no redraw; the runtime's own bind step always renders first.

## Test plan

- [x] `gsap.steps.test.ts`, each new row red on main: the scene's opening set after stepping back; the four "draws ... as without the redraw" shapes, arrived at eventfully and silently (value at the playhead and after the next seek); two sets on the playhead in authored order; a call in an otherwise empty nested timeline; a pause in a reversed repeating scene; every frame of `style-5-prod`'s typed intro rendered forward as a paused sub-composition (fails without the length restore); a timeline that grew after its last render keeps its length.
- [x] Mutations, each failing only its own rows: no hold, 8 draw rows; restore for callback tweens only, the two-sets and empty-nested-call rows; restore for zero-duration children only, the scene row; no duration settle, the length row.
- [x] Differential matrix (15 shapes × 6 playheads × 2 starting points × eventful/silent, then 5 later seeks): main differs from no-redraw in 26 of 360 cases, this branch in 4, all intended (authored order at the playhead, a set at 0 on a timeline that never moved). An independent review's random sweep (20,000 films of sets, tweens, calls, reversed, repeating, yoyo and nested scenes, the runtime's bind step modelled) found no difference from no redraw at the playhead, after the next seek, or in call counts; main differed in 326, 101 and 5 cases. A separate sweep with `addPause` and paused nested timelines still differs in 27, 7 and 46 cases (main 170, 44 and 51), none of them worse than main; all involve `addPause`.
- [x] Headless Chrome, built runtime, main vs branch: the scene case above.
- [x] `gsap.steps.test.ts` 48/48, 3 runs; `src/runtime` 1791/1791, 3 runs; core typecheck (including the runtime one), format and lint clean.

## Cost

Per redraw, GSAP 3.15, a 10,000-tween root of 100 nested scenes with one set in ten, playhead at 5 s, main and this branch run interleaved in one process: about +40% (1.56 to 2.19 ms median of 7 on a heavily loaded box; on a quiet box main is about 0.7 ms, so roughly +0.3 ms). It depends on where the playhead is: later children are held out and skipped, so with the playhead past most children an independent run measured this branch slightly cheaper than main.

## Size

About 160 changed lines in `packages/core/src/runtime`, two thirds of them tests.

title: fix(media-use): say to fix an unreadable credentials path, not to log in again
body:
## What

When `~/.heygen/credentials` (or `$HEYGEN_CONFIG_DIR/credentials`) exists but cannot be read, `heygenAuthHeaders` now names that path and says to fix or remove it, then log in. Before, it said "no HeyGen credentials … run `npx hyperframes auth login`", and that login then fails to write the same path.

## Why

A review follow-up on #4995. That PR made an unreadable credentials path count as "no credential" so probes never crash, but the error users see when HeyGen is actually needed then pointed them the wrong way. A folder at that path, or a `~/.heygen` left root-owned by a `sudo` login, stays broken after `auth login`. The CLI's own store (`packages/cli/src/auth/store.ts`) already tells users to delete the path and log in.

## Related work

Refs #4995 and #4988 (both merged).

Size: a review follow-up to #4995 (a non-blocking nit there), standalone because no open PR touches this file.

## How

An internal `resolveCredential` reads the file once and keeps the error. A missing file (`ENOENT`) is `null` as before; any other read error is `{ unreadable: { file, code } }`. `heygenCredential` maps that to `null`, so its public answer and never-throws contract are unchanged for every caller (`heygenAvailable`, `audio.mjs`, the telemetry tag). Only `heygenAuthHeaders` reads `unreadable` and throws the new hint. `pickProvider("heygen")` in `tts.mjs` had its own copy of the old "run auth login" message; it now lets `heygenAuthHeaders` throw, so both paths give the same reason and fix. `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `heygenAuthHeaders says to fix an unreadable credentials path, and to log in when there is none` (also asserts `heygenCredential()` stays `null`), and `pickProvider heygen with an unreadable credentials path says to fix that path`. Each fails on its mutation: dropping the `unreadable → null` mapping, or restoring the old `tts.mjs` message.
- [x] 23/23 in `heygen.test.mjs` and `tts.test.mjs`, three runs in a row on Linux; `oxfmt --check` clean on the four files.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: feat(cli,studio): hand off on macOS now, and open the app on Windows and Linux
body: Builds on #4951. **Review only commit 4df0660ba** — the rest is #4951 (approved), its one-line `studioApiFetch` fix, and merges of main. Once #4951 merges this shows just that commit. ## What The released Mac app (b254, hyperframes-internal#2601) takes a handed-over folder and the conversation, so the hand-off turns on for macOS. Windows and Linux keep the download until the desktop change that reads a folder from the command line ships; then `HANDOFF_READY` widens. - `hyperframes open` finds the app off macOS: the per-user install on Windows (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\HyperFrames\HyperFrames.exe`), and on Linux the AppImage the app records in `launcher.json` in its config folder. title: fix(producer): propagate useGpu to HDR layered streaming encoder
body:
### Summary

The HDR layered capture path accepts a render job with `useGpu: true`, but the option is not forwarded to `spawnStreamingEncoder()`.

`StreamingEncoderOptions.useGpu` defaults to `false`, so HDR layered renders silently use the software encoder even when GPU encoding was requested.

### Root cause

In `captureHdrStage.ts`, the streaming encoder options omit:

```ts
useGpu: job.config.useGpu,
```

The normal streaming capture stage already forwards the resolved encoder configuration, but the HDR layered stage constructs its own options object.

### Affected version

Observed in HyperFrames v0.8.114 (`01c6f6004a00ecfa6e77ab4025b47a46a5e925fc`). Please confirm whether current `main` still omits the field.

### Expected behavior

When the render job has `useGpu: true`, the HDR layered path should pass that value to `spawnStreamingEncoder()`. Encoder capability probing and fallback behavior should remain inside the existing encoder implementation.

### Proposed change

Forward the existing job configuration in `runCaptureHdrStage()`:

```ts
const streamingEncoder = spawnStreamingEncoder({
  // existing options
  useGpu: job.config.useGpu,
});
```

### Validation

Add a regression test that mocks `spawnStreamingEncoder()` and asserts that an HDR job with `useGpu: true` receives `useGpu: true`. The same test should preserve `false` when GPU encoding is not requested.

No render defaults, codec selection, or GPU fallback policy need to change.

title: fix(engine): emit hvc1 for streaming H.265 GPU outputs
body:
### Summary

The streaming encoder adds the MP4 `hvc1` sample-entry tag for software H.265, but GPU H.265 branches can omit it. Those outputs may use FFmpeg's default `hev1` tag even though the encoded HEVC stream itself is valid.

This reduces compatibility with Apple playback software and other consumers that expect parameter sets through an `hvc1` sample entry.

### Root cause

In `buildStreamingArgs()`, the existing:

```ts
args.push("-tag:v", "hvc1");
```

is nested inside the software-encoder branch. The common `codec === "h265"` decision is outside that branch, so VideoToolbox and the other supported GPU H.265 encoders do not necessarily receive the same container tag.

### Affected version

Observed in HyperFrames v0.8.114 (`01c6f6004a00ecfa6e77ab4025b47a46a5e925fc`). Please confirm against current `main`.

### Expected behavior

Every MP4 streaming H.265 path should append `-tag:v hvc1` exactly once, independently of whether the selected encoder is libx265, VideoToolbox, NVENC, VAAPI, QSV, or AMF. H.264 and VP9 paths must remain unchanged.

### Proposed change

Move the H.265 sample-entry decision after software/GPU encoder selection but keep it inside the common H.265 branch:

```ts
if (codec === "h265") {
  args.push("-tag:v", "hvc1");
}
```

### Validation

Add argument-construction tests covering:

- software H.265;
- HDR VideoToolbox H.265;
- each supported GPU H.265 encoder;
- software and GPU H.264 negative cases;
- exactly one `hvc1` tag per H.265 command.

The change is container metadata only and does not alter encoded picture data, bitrate, transfer characteristics, or HDR metadata.

fix(studio): a snap the saved clip would miss no longer moves it
body:
## What

Two review follow-ups from #4986:

1. A snap the saved clip would miss no longer moves the clip. Clip files store times to the centisecond, so at high zoom a move or tail trim could snap flush to a target, then jump a few pixels on release when the file rounded it. Now, when the saved edge would land a pixel or more off the target, the snap is not applied and the clip stays where the pointer put it.
2. A test pins that the paused preview-frame view never applies while playing.

## Why

#4986 dropped the guide for such snaps but still applied them, so the clip sat flush during the drag and jumped on release (reported in both reviews of #4986). Without the snap it previews and saves at the same place.

## Related work

Refs #4986.

## How

- `computeDragPreview` checks the move's snap against `guideIfSaved` right after `snapMoveToTargets`; a missed target falls back to the pointer's start. The guide is then whatever snap survived, so the check runs once.
- `computeResizePreview` builds the snapped trim (`onTarget`) and applies it only when `guideIfSaved` keeps its guide, for both edges.
- The `trimTargets.length > 0 || gridStep > 0` guard is gone: with the magnet on the playhead is always a target, and with it off `snapTimelineTime` returns no target.
- Host note: a host that renders `Timeline` over its own player (not `useTimelinePlayer`) gets no trim edge-frame preview; `previewFrameStore` is not exported. In-repo hosts all use `useTimelinePlayer`.
- **Walk:** `tests/e2e/timeline-snap-release.mjs` (new clips card-c and card-d in the shared fixture) zooms to the deepest level, moves a 31/30 s clip until its end is 4.8 px past card-d's start, and compares where the drag shows it landing with where it saved, both relative to card-d. The landing slot gets `data-testid="timeline-drag-landing"`, like its sibling drop preview. CI runs it after the trim-snap walk on a fresh copy of the fixture.

## Before

Deepest zoom, close-up at card-d's start (4x). While dragging, the landing slot ends flush with card-d; after release the saved clip ends past it: a 4.3 px jump.

![Before: the landing slot is flush with the edge, the saved clip is not](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b0a8e39a-6dc2-4c18-9aec-c996d6953ff5)

## After

The landing slot already shows where the clip will save, and release does not move it.

![After: the landing slot and the saved clip agree](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/19fcbc7a-b8a0-45b9-b5cc-ea910117fd01)

## What I measured

- Walk `timeline-snap-release.mjs`, headless Chrome on Linux, 1440x900, repo fixture: on main the clip jumps 4.3 px on release (exit 1); with this branch 3 of 3 runs show 0.0 px (saved start 0.32 s either way). With saves held back 2 s (request interception), main still fails and this branch passes, so the walk reads the saved start, not the drag's own. `timeline-trim-snap.mjs` still passes 3 of 3 with the larger fixture.
- Unit tests (vitest), each file 3 runs, all exit 0: `timelineClipDragPreview.test.ts` 50, `useTimelineClipDrag.resize.test.tsx` 27, `timelineSnapping.test.ts` 20, `useTimelinePlayer.seek.test.ts` 20, `Timeline.test.ts` 83. Full `packages/studio` suite: 664 files, 7325 tests passed, exit 0. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt, comment ratchet clean.
- Each new test fails when its code is broken: applying a missed move snap (2 tests red), applying a missed tail snap (1 red), letting the paused view apply while playing (1 red).

## What I did NOT exercise

- macOS or a GPU: the walks ran headless on Linux, so the captures prove behaviour, not pixels.
- HyperFrames Desktop: it picks this up on its next Studio version bump.
- A start-trim refusal in a browser: start trims save their start rounded to the centisecond already, so at normal zoom the refusal only changes the guide; it is unit-tested.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed (browser walk above)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: fix(studio-server): motion paths animate when gsap has a query string or loads deferred
body:
## What

Motion paths animate in Studio preview when the composition loads gsap from a URL with a query string or hash (`gsap.min.js?v=1`), or with a `defer` gsap tag. Before, Studio's MotionPathPlugin ran before gsap in both cases and the motion path did nothing ("Missing plugin? gsap.registerPlugin()").

## Why

Studio adds MotionPathPlugin right after the composition's gsap tag, so the plugin registers onto gsap. It found that tag by text and only recognised URLs ending exactly in `gsap.js` or `gsap.min.js`; anything else sent the plugin to `<head>`, ahead of a body gsap. A deferred gsap was recognised, but the plugin tag did not carry `defer`, so it still ran during parsing, before gsap.

## Related work

Builds on #4980 (merged), which made the plugin tag copy gsap's script type; this adds `defer` and the URL forms.

## How

- Studio finds the gsap tag with the core HTML scanner (`findStartTags`) paired with the parsed document, the way lazy preview images already do, so tags inside comments, templates and raw-text blocks (style, textarea, title) are never mistaken for the live one, and the search stays linear on any input. The earlier single pattern could backtrack polynomially (code scanning flagged it).
- A script is gsap core when its URL path ends in `/gsap.js` or `/gsap.min.js`, decided by the URL parser, so a query string or hash never matters.
- The plugin tag copies the gsap tag's `type` and `defer`, read with the HTML parser the server already uses (`linkedom`), attribute names compared case-insensitively, so `DEFER` counts and an attribute value that merely contains the word "defer" does not.
- An `async` gsap is left as it is: no later tag can be ordered after an async script, and the composition's own scripts already race it.

## Verification

Real Chrome 152, Studio preview, a composition with a motion-path tween and no manual `registerPlugin`, seeked to 1 s, 2 runs per case:

| gsap tag | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| body `<script src=".../gsap.min.js?v=1">` | dot not moved, "Missing plugin" warning | dot at (300, 150), no warning |
| `<script defer src=".../gsap.min.js">`, composition code on `DOMContentLoaded` | dot not moved, "Missing plugin" warning | dot at (300, 150), no warning |

## Test plan

- [x] `routes/preview.test.ts`: plugin follows a body gsap with a query string, with a hash; plugin is deferred after a deferred gsap; `DEFER`/`TYPE` in capitals are read; `defer` inside another attribute's value is not; a gsap tag inside a comment or a nested template is skipped for the live one; the live tag is still found after a style block, an empty comment, or a comment opener inside an attribute; a gsap `.map` file is not gsap core; a 450 KB run of `/gsap.js#` src text finishes. Red before each fix, green after (95/95, 3 runs). Mutants (case-sensitive names, raw path instead of URL path, a raw `<script` scan instead of the core scanner, the earlier regex) each turn their tests red.
- [x] Typecheck, lint, format, comment ratchet, Fallow audit.

title: fix(studio): a first animation in a full-document sub-composition plays
body:
## What

Adding the first animation to a sub-composition that is stored as a full HTML document (`<html><body><template>…</template></body></html>`, the shape registry blocks use) now plays in the preview and the render. Before, the animation was saved to the file but never ran: the card in the captures below stays put at 2 s instead of fading out.

## Why

The first GSAP edit on a file with no GSAP script adds a small bootstrap (`gsap` plus a `__timelines` entry). `prepareGsapMutationScript` (studio-server `routes/files.ts`) tried `</body>` first, then `</template>`. For a sub-composition the loader mounts the `<template>`'s content whenever the file has one (core `runtime/compositionLoader.ts`, `sourceNode = template ? template.content : doc.body`), so a script placed in `<body>` outside the template is never part of the composition. A bare `<template>` file already worked; the full-document shape did not, and a test pinned that outcome.

## How

- core `htmlDocument.ts`: `hasCompositionOutsideTemplates(html)` is true when an element outside every `<template>` carries `data-composition-id`, i.e. the composition lives in `<body>`. An id on `<html>` or `<body>` counts only when no template holds a composition (on its root or on the `<template>` tag itself): most registry components (and the docs' full-document form) put the composition id on `<html>` and again on the template's root, while a root page may carry its id on `<html>` beside an unrelated template. Comments and text are skipped, nested templates counted.
- studio-server `files.ts`: the bootstrap goes into `<body>` when the composition lives there, and into the template otherwise, each with the other as fallback. A root page whose own composition is in `<body>` beside inline `<template>`s of other compositions still gets its script in `<body>`.
- This is the only place Studio writes a script into a saved composition file; the other `insertBeforeCloseTag(…"body"…)` callers inject into the page being served.

## Before

Built CLI Studio (main 7f346492), Chrome for Testing 152, a full-document sub-composition with one CSS-only card. One `add` mutation (`to`, opacity 0, 1 s at 0) through Studio's own route, then the timeline ruler clicked at 2 s. The preview has no `sub` timeline and the card is still opaque (computed opacity 1).

![Before: main, playhead at 2 s, the card has not faded](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0da1e6a5-9510-4995-bbb1-c7dc70cc294f)

## After

Same steps on this branch: the script lands inside the template, `__timelines.sub` exists with 1 tween, and the card has faded out (computed opacity 0).

![After: this branch, playhead at 2 s, the card has faded out](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aee6205e-cbf7-462a-938b-c7f645f14677)

## Test plan

- `files.test.ts`: "a first animation in a full-document sub-composition lands inside its template" (registry-block shape) fails on main (`expected 450 to be less than 190`); "…whose composition is in <body> lands before </body>" (root page with an inline template) passes on main and guards the change. The old test that expected the script outside the template is replaced.
- `files.test.ts`: "…lands inside the template when <html> carries the composition id" (the registry-component shape, e.g. `agent-cursor.html`) fails without the `<html>`/`<body>` skip (`expected 436 to be less than 176`); "…when the <template> tag carries the composition id" covers the form where the id sits on the `<template>` tag.
- `htmlDocument.test.ts`: nine cases for the helper (root in body, beside an inline template, full-document sub-composition, id on `<html>` and `<body>`, id on `<html>` and on the `<template>` tag, root id on `<html>` beside a template with no composition, bare template, attribute only in a comment or text, nested template).
- Deliberate breaks: the helper always true fails the full-document test; always false fails the root-page test.
- `htmlDocument.test.ts` 46/46 and `files.test.ts` 98/98, 3 runs in a row; the same browser check passes for all three shapes (bare template, full document, id on `<html>`); full studio-server suite 1083 pass; `tsc --noEmit` (core, studio-server), oxlint, oxfmt clean (Linux).

Known limits, unchanged by this PR: the bootstrap's timeline key is the file's first `data-composition-id`; a sub-composition file with several templates gets the script in the first one (the render bundler also uses the first, the preview prefers `template#<id>-template`). A root page whose own id sits on `<html>` or `<body>` next to a template holding another composition would get the script in that template; no file in the repo has that shape.

Not exercised: a render through the producer (the bundler builds a sub-composition from the same template content, so it follows the same rule), and the Desktop app.

Related: triage of three open GSAP-editing reports on main. "Nested nudge and rotate are lost" and "timeline move/stretch leaves `to` tweens stuck" no longer reproduce in a real browser on main; "undo right after an edit is ignored" never loses the undo now, but a resize or rotate is not painted back until its save lands, which is the next PR.

title: fix(core): a cropped element's edge stays exact while GSAP tweens it
body:
## What this fixes

A crop on an element that GSAP scales or moves shimmered in renders: while a tween ran, the crop edge jumped by up to 1 px from frame to frame, then settled when the tween stopped. The Studio preview geometry was exact, so the export disagreed with what the author set. Six edit accuracy cases failed on this (`crop-scale-px-*-mid`, render 0.99 px and 0.77 px).

## Cause

Mid-tween, GSAP's default `force3D: "auto"` writes `translate3d(...)` instead of `translate(...)` (CSSPlugin `_renderCSSTransforms`). A 3D transform gives the element its own compositing layer, and Chrome paints a `clip-path` edge on such a layer hard, snapped to whole pixels. At a tween boundary GSAP writes the 2D form again, so the edge snaps back to the exact position. The same static page shows it without any HyperFrames code:

| Transform on a box with `clip-path: inset(0 35.55px 0 0)` | Exact right edge | Painted right edge |
|---|---|---|
| `scale(1.125)` | 815.006 | 815.0 |
| `translate3d(0,0,0) scale(1.125)` | 815.006 | 816.0 |
| `scale(1.225)` | 823.451 | 823.448 |
| `translate3d(0,0,0) scale(1.225)` | 823.451 | 824.0 |

## Change

The runtime sets GSAP's `force3D` to `false` through the public `gsap.config`, the moment GSAP loads. `installFlatGsapTransforms` runs while the runtime script evaluates (beside `installAuthoredMediaCapture` in `entry.ts`), configures a GSAP that is already there, and wraps the `window.gsap` assignment so a GSAP bundle that loads later is configured on arrival. Either way the setting is in place before a composition's own script runs `set()`, `from()` or `fromTo()`, which is when GSAP stores it on each element. The wrapper chains to an accessor already on `window.gsap` (the producer's early stub traps the same property) and installs once.

- Flat transforms stay 2D. Real 3D (`z`, `rotationX`, `rotationY`, `transformPerspective`) is still written as 3D by GSAP.
- A composition that calls `gsap.config({ force3D: true })` itself keeps its own setting.
- A page that made `window.gsap` non-configurable before the runtime (a global `var gsap` ahead of it) is not trapped: a GSAP already there is configured, one that loads after it is not and keeps 3D tweens.

## Evidence

Per-frame crop edge in a producer render of a bench case (crop on a scale tween, 30 fps, t = 1.8 to 3.2 s, 43 frames, JPEG as the bench renders, Chrome headless shell 152):

| | Max error | Mean error | Frames off by more than 0.3 px |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 0.99 px | 0.39 px | 24 of 43 |
| this branch | 0.12 px | 0.011 px | 0 |

The same case, with and without a `gsap.set()` on the element before its timeline (crop edge error at frames 30 to 66, producer render):

| Runtime | Timeline only | `gsap.set()` first |
|---|---|---|
| main | up to 0.99 px, 3D | up to 0.99 px, 3D |
| first commit of this PR (setting applied at DOMContentLoaded) | 0.01 px | up to 0.99 px, 3D |
| this branch | 0.01 px | 0.01 px |

- Edit accuracy (CI, full grid): accurate 1562, base branch 1556; the six `crop-scale-px-*-mid` cases are newly passing and no case lost its pass. `baseline.json` is the gate artifact's, committed as the gate asks. The render error itself moves both ways; see the trade below.
- Studio preview playback on two heavy repo films (registry `product-promo`, `kinetic-type`), 5 alternating rounds against main: no separable difference in per-frame main-thread work (medians 3.02 vs 3.21 ms and 3.30 vs 3.08 ms) or dropped frames. Measured with an earlier build that applied the same setting at timeline bind.
- Producer regression set, every renderable fixture rendered on main and on this branch, compared frame by frame: 61 fixtures; 22 identical; 26 differ only on edges or text antialiasing. The other 13 also differ away from hard edges, so each was re-rendered from one checkout, twice with main's runtime and once with this branch's. Main's own run-to-run noise accounts for one of them entirely (`heygen-promo-preview-assets`) and most of `style-17-prod`. In the rest, the change is fine texture and outline sharpness inside layers that move (video included), because they are now painted in the page rather than resampled as a 3D layer. Their worst frames are visually the same. Nothing moves, appears or disappears. One fixture (`hf2550-video-subcomposition-ghost`) has no renderable media in that environment and was not compared.
- Tests (`init.test.ts`, real GSAP, in page order: runtime script, GSAP bundle, composition script, DOMContentLoaded): `to()`, `from()`, `fromTo()` and `set()`-then-`to()` draw in 2D mid-tween; a `set()` then moved element draws in 2D when GSAP loaded before the runtime; a composition's own `force3D: true` is kept; an opacity-only tween writes no transform; a second install configures GSAP once; an accessor already on `window.gsap` still receives GSAP; a non-configurable `window.gsap` is configured without the runtime throwing (`init.flatGsap.test.ts`, its own file because the property cannot be removed). Seven single-line mutations of `installFlatGsapTransforms` each turn at least one test red. 3 green runs; the runtime folder (69 files, 1815 tests) passes.

## Render change: transformed layers stay crisp mid-motion

Every element GSAP moves, scales or rotates in 2D now paints in the page instead of on its own compositor layer while the tween runs. On main such an element is drawn as a resampled texture mid-tween and snaps back to a sharp paint when the tween ends; on this branch it is painted sharp throughout.

Two producer goldens are byte-strict (`maxFrameFailures: 0`) over a GSAP-rotated icon and are regenerated here with `docker:test:update` from `Dockerfile.test` (Chrome 148):

- `png-sequence`: 59 of 60 frames change, every changed pixel inside the 44 x 44 px icon, only on the ring and dot edges.
- `mov-prores`: on main this fixture already scored 30.04 to 30.06 dB against its June golden, just over the 30 dB bar, because its text renders about 1 px differently today; the icon change took it to 29.88. The regenerated golden matches today's render.
- Their `compiled.html` snapshots are left as they were: the update also rewrites them, but only for drift unrelated to this change (they do not contain the runtime), and the compile check passes either way.

![Render change: main vs this branch vs diff](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/49c41671-abe8-4e8b-aeaa-c3d5a13c8a73)

## Render accuracy trade

Chrome snaps a box's painted background to whole pixels when its layout position is fractional, in both modes. On a 3D layer the crop moves with that snap, but the crop edge itself snaps (the 1 px pop above). In 2D the crop clips at its exact position on top of the snapped background, so a cropped box at a half-pixel position paints up to 0.5 px short on an uncropped edge. Static page, Chrome 152, box at `top: 100.5px`, `height: 160px`, cropped: 2D paints 101.0 to 260.5, 3D paints 101.0 to 261.0.

Render error across the 1562 edit accuracy cases, this branch's banked `baseline.json` vs main's (the same counts on two CI runs at different heads of this branch):

| | Count |
|---|---|
| better by more than 0.015 px | 53 |
| worse by more than 0.015 px | 71 |
| worse by more than 0.1 px | 6 (`crop-tween-px-r0-*`, 0.02 to 0.26 px) |
| over 0.3 px | 12 (main 15) |
| over 0.5 px, the limit | 0 (main 6) |

The largest render error is now 0.37 px (`crop-spin-px-r0-nested-*-mid`, 0.32 on main); on main it was 0.99 px.

## Known limits

The setting reaches only elements GSAP first touches after the runtime script has run. Three paths load the runtime after a composition's own script, and there an element `set()` before its timeline still tweens in 3D:

- Studio preview's fallback when its bundler throws, which adds the runtime at the end of `<body>` (reported separately; it also affects the other script-time installs in `entry.ts`).
- The player loading a composition by URL that has no runtime, which appends it once the page has loaded (`composition-probe.ts`).
- A timeline script inline in `<head>` before the runtime.

title: test(studio): the edit bench checks the keyframe rule outside a range and for new property groups
body:
## What

The edit accuracy bench now checks Studio's keyframe rule in two places it did not reach:

- **Outside a tween's range.** The keyframed grid gains a playhead after every range (3.5 s, past the last keyframe at 3 s) and a new `late` variant, a size tween that starts at 1 s, with a playhead before its first keyframe (0.5 s). On a keyframe an edit changes that keyframe; anywhere else, before or after the range included, it adds one there, and every other keyframe must read back unchanged.
- **New property groups.** The keyframe verdict also fails when an edit makes the timeline animate a property group on the target (position, size, scale, rotation, as `classifyPropertyGroup` defines them) that nothing animated before. Keyframing `y` next to an animated `x`, or `height` next to an animated `width`, is the same property and passes; `x`/`y` written into a size-only tween fails. A static `gsap.set` hold is not a channel.

## Why

The keyframe rule (an edit to an animated property changes or adds the keyframe at the playhead and never touches the others) had known breakages listed when this bench was built: an array dropping its implicit 0%, a flat `to()` rewriting 0%, `from()`/`fromTo()` ends replaced, the range collapsing to 0 outside it, and a resize writing x/y into a size-only tween. The grid only tested playheads on or between keyframes and only read the properties already animated, so the out-of-range and new-channel classes could come back unnoticed.

Measured on main before writing this (built Studio at `6037d228`, headless Chrome 152): every one of those cases now keeps the rule. So this PR adds the guard only; no Studio code changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Bench unit tests (`keyframes.test.mjs`): the new playheads land where expected (before only on a range that starts late, after on every variant), and `openedGroups` passes another channel of an animated property, fails a new group, and ignores a `gsap.set` hold and the keys the parser never groups (`data`, `_auto`, `transformOrigin`).
- [x] Main, 50 cases (move, resize, rotate, crop, nudge on every variant at the new playheads, plus resize on and between keyframes; root, no rotation, 100% zoom): every case keeps the rule; the largest drift at another keyframe is 0.002 px (tolerance 0.01), and no case opens a property group.
- [x] Main, the same new playheads nested and at 30° rotation (80 cases): every case keeps the rule.
- [x] CI full grid at this head: all 2042 cases measured, 478 newly accurate and banked, none regressed; no new case fails the keyframe rule or writes stray CSS.
- [x] The guard is not vacuous, shown on two deliberately broken Studio builds (built CLI and Studio, root, no rotation, 100% zoom):
  - Resize writes the anchor `x`/`y` into a tween that animates only size: all 6 `resize-size`/`resize-late` cases fail the keyframe verdict with `opened: ["position"]` and no keyframe moved, so only the new check catches it.
  - An edit outside the range no longer pins the range edge: `resize-late-px-r0-root-z100-before` fails with the 1 s keyframe's width off by 87 px.

## Known failing, banked as failing

Two new cases fail on pointer tracking, not on the keyframe rule: `resize-scale-px-r30-root-z50-after` (0.53 px) and `resize-scale-px-r30-nested-z50-after` (0.52 px), limit 0.5 px. Resizing a scale-animated, rotated layer drifts by a fraction of a pixel that grows with the scale (0.30 px on a keyframe, 0.39 px between, 0.52 px after the range). They are banked as failing with no tolerance change; the fix is a separate change.

## No visible change

Bench and test files only; Studio itself does not change.

title: fix: preview and bundled scripts run where and when the author put them
body:
## What

Scripts in a Studio preview now run where and when the author put them:

- Local scripts in a bundled composition (Studio preview and the CLI's `layout`, `motion-shot`, `validate`, `compare` and `grade-compare`) keep their place, `defer`, `async`, `nomodule` and `type`. A `<script defer src="main.js">` after a deferred gsap from a CDN runs after gsap again, so the composition builds its timeline instead of failing with `gsap is not defined`. This holds under a page security policy that allows inline scripts only.
- When the bundler returns nothing, throws, or returns a page without a runtime, the preview still loads the runtime ahead of the composition's scripts, as the bundled page does. Before, the runtime came after them (bundler returned nothing) or was missing (bundler threw), so script-time installs in the runtime (authored opacity and media capture, the force3D install) ran too late or never.
- An authored script that merely reads `window.__hyperframeRuntime` (or mentions a runtime file name, or sets up `window.__player`) is no longer deleted from the preview and the bundle.

## Why

The bundler joined every local `<script src>` file into one inline script at the position of the first one. That:

- dropped `defer` and `async` (an inline script cannot be deferred), so a deferred `main.js` ran during parsing, before a deferred gsap;
- moved later files ahead of any CDN script between them (`setup.js`, gsap CDN, `main.js` became `setup.js + main.js`, then gsap).

The step that later merges adjacent inline scripts also folded in `nomodule` scripts, dropping the attribute, so legacy-only code ran in modern browsers. It only treated three type strings as JavaScript, so a script typed with another JavaScript MIME type the browser runs (`application/ecmascript`, `text/jscript`, ...) skipped the web-font gate and ran early.

Runtime stripping matched words in a script's text (`__hyperframeRuntime`, `window.__player =`, ...), so it deleted authored scripts that used them.

The preview's no-bundle path placed the runtime before `</body>`, after the composition's scripts; the bundler-threw path added none.

## Related work

Same family as #5007 (Studio's MotionPathPlugin placement after a deferred or query-string gsap); different owner, so a separate change.

## How

- `bundleProject` (`core/src/compiler/htmlBundler.ts`): each local classic script is inlined in its own tag, keeping its other attributes (`defer`, `async`, `nomodule`, a non-JavaScript `type`) and marked `data-hf-inlined-src` with the file it came from. Module and integrity-pinned scripts are untouched, as before. Every inlined local JavaScript file now goes through the same esbuild comment strip that merged runs always had (main already did this for files merged into a body script): comments, license banners and source-map comments are dropped and `fn.toString()` text changes, behaviour does not. Inlined text and merged runs go through core's `escapeInlineScriptSource`, so a file containing `</script>` or `<!--` cannot end or swallow its tag; `<!--` is now written `\x3C!--`, which stays valid inside a unicode regex.
- `inlineScriptRuns` / `isClassicInline` (`core/src/compiler/scriptRuns.ts`), shared by the bundler and the producer's render compiler: a `defer`, `async` or `nomodule` script is never merged into a run, and every JavaScript MIME type from the HTML spec counts as classic JavaScript.
- `runScriptsAfterFonts` (`core/src/runtime/afterFonts.ts`), which already runs a bundled page's body scripts once fonts are ready, and its fallback for older runtimes: a deferred file (`defer` with a `src`, or with the inlined-file mark) runs after the classic scripts, in document order, and each external script finishes loading before the next script runs. That is the browser's order for the authored page, so no `data:` URL or other source is needed. An authored inline `<script defer>` keeps running in place, as browsers run it.
- `stripEmbeddedRuntimeScripts` (`core/src/compiler/htmlDocument.ts`): a script is the runtime's own when its start tag carries the bootstrap attribute or its `src` path ends in a runtime file name, plus the existing whole-script readiness flags; text inside an authored script no longer counts. Every writer of a lasting runtime tag (bundler, Studio preview, sub-composition preview) sets the attribute. The two "is a runtime already here?" text checks that followed the strip (bundler, sub-composition preview) are gone: after the strip none is left, and the text check skipped the runtime when an authored script mentioned its attribute. The render compiler's CDN inliner (`inlineExternalScripts`) leaves a runtime file link alone, so the render file server still strips it instead of booting a second, unpinned runtime.
- `insertRuntimeTag` (`core/src/compiler/htmlDocument.ts`): the bundler's runtime placement (end of `<head>`, else after `<html>` or the doctype), moved out of `injectInterceptor`. The Studio preview applies its runtime through it on every path: it strips any runtime already in the page and inserts the preview runtime with the bootstrap attribute.

Adjacent plain inline scripts, including inlined local files with nothing between them, are still merged into one by the existing step, as before; a throw in one stops the rest of that merged script. Files separated by any other script stay separate.

Known limits, unchanged or accepted: a deferred local file in `<head>` is inlined there and still runs during parsing, as before this change, so a page that needs it to run after a deferred CDN script in `<head>` still fails (scripts in `<body>` work); a follow-up handles head order. `String.raw` text containing `<!--` in a bundled script reads back as `\x3C!--`; in a local non-JavaScript file inlined on its own (JSON, a template, `text/babel`), every `<!--` and `</script` is escaped (`\x3C!--`, `<\/script`), which its reader does not undo, so such text in a JSON string stops it parsing (main already turned these files into JavaScript). A deferred CDN script that never answers stops the scripts after it, as in the raw page (the engine's player-ready limit still ends a render). A runtime pasted inline without the bootstrap attribute is no longer recognised and would load twice; nothing in the repo writes one. Studio preview loads deferred external scripts and modules one after another, as it already did for classic ones. The fallback for runtimes older than the font gate does not wait for an inline module before a later deferred file. Studio preview always serves its own runtime, also for a bundle built with `HYPERFRAME_RUNTIME_URL`.

## Render path

Checked with real renders (CLI, Chrome 152) of four shapes on `main` and on the web-font gate build: deferred gsap + deferred local `main.js`, local `setup.js` / CDN gsap / local `main.js`, deferred gsap + `DOMContentLoaded` listener, async gsap + `DOMContentLoaded` listener (3 runs). All rendered the tween correctly at t = 1 s on both builds; a reversed control (main.js before gsap) stayed static. The render compiler inlines CDN scripts in place and keeps their `defer`, without the inlined-file mark, so renders run them exactly as before this change. It reaches the render path through `isClassicInline` (`nomodule` and the JavaScript type list), the stricter runtime strip, and the runtime-link skip above. No template, fixture or skill in the repo uses `defer` scripts.

## Test plan

- [x] `htmlBundler.test.ts` (script order): a local file around a CDN script keeps its place; a local `defer` and a local `async` file are inlined in their own tag with the attribute; `nomodule` survives on a local file and on an inline script; a local `type="text/babel"` file keeps its type; a local file containing `</script>` and `<!--` is escaped, merged and unmerged; a unicode regex matching `<!--` still compiles; a run merging a local file that has a legacy `<!--` comment with authored scripts and other files stays valid and runs all five in order; a local file with a legacy `<!--` comment inlined on its own (in `<head>`, or deferred in `<body>`) stays valid; a local non-JavaScript file keeps its text as written; an authored script reading `window.__hyperframeRuntime` survives; the runtime is still added when an authored script mentions its attribute.
- [x] `entry.afterFonts.test.ts`: an inlined deferred file runs after a later classic script, through the runtime and through the old-runtime fallback, while an authored inline defer script runs in place, through both; an inline script after an external one runs once the external one has loaded, with and without `defer`.
- [x] `htmlDocument.test.ts`: the escape keeps the matched case (`</SCRIPT>` becomes `<\/SCRIPT>`).
- [x] `scriptRuns.test.ts`: four legacy JavaScript types join a run; `text/javascript2` does not.
- [x] `subComposition.test.ts`: the preview runtime is added when the project head's script names a runtime file. Producer `htmlCompiler.test.ts`: a CDN runtime link is not inlined.
- [x] `htmlDocument.test.ts`: authored scripts that read the runtime global, query the bootstrap attribute, name a runtime file or set up `window.__player` are kept; a runtime file linked with a query string or uppercase name is stripped.
- [x] `preview.test.ts`: when the bundler returns nothing, returns a page without a runtime, or throws, the runtime loads before a composition script that calls `gsap.set()`; a disk page that already links a runtime gets exactly one; an authored script reading the runtime global survives.
- [x] `bundleScriptPolicy.test.ts` (producer integration, real Chrome): a bundled page with `script-src 'unsafe-inline'` runs its local defer script after the classic script and animates (CSS animation at 1 s after a seek). Fails on the previous `data:` URL version with a policy violation. A second Chrome test serves a deferred CDN script through request interception and checks that the inlined deferred `main.js` sees it; a third checks that a deferred local file runs after an inline module before it.
- [x] Each new test fails without its fix. Mutants: late rule back to `src`-only (runtime, fallback and Chrome tests red), merging defer/async, the old `<\!--` escape, no runtime on the bundled path, text-based stripping; each turns its own test red.
- [x] Core runtime and compiler (2282), studio-server routes and helpers (953), producer Chrome and render-order tests (15) and producer compiler and file server (194, bun), each 3 runs; CLI bundle users (layout, validate, localized fonts); producer file server (54, bun), sdk (588), engine services; core, producer and studio-server typecheck; lint, format, comment ratchet, test classification, test reachability and Fallow audit clean.

## Before

Studio preview, Chrome 152: deferred gsap from a CDN, then `<script defer src="main.js">` that builds the timeline. The bundled `main.js` runs before gsap: `Uncaught ReferenceError: gsap is not defined`, no timeline, the dot never moves.

![Studio preview error dialog: gsap is not defined](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/111b2052-c8b1-4b12-9751-1eecf7366177)

## After

Same project with this change, seeked to 1 s through the runtime: `main.js` is inlined with `defer` kept and runs after gsap, the `main` timeline exists and the dot is half-way across. 3 of 3 runs.

![Studio preview with the dot half-way across at 1 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13a209c5-ae2d-4b38-ae99-9e2a84b2ee7f)

title: fix(studio): a video's sound reads on its clip like an audio row
body:
## What

A video clip that carries sound now shows that sound on the timeline the way an audio clip does. The strip under the thumbnails takes the audio clip's own surface (`--timeline-clip-audio-bg`) and half of the clip under its label. The clip's peak badge stays whole inside the strip: there it shows only the ▲ mark, on the audio chip surface, clear of the clip's rounded corner.

## Why

Since the from-file template keeps a video's sound on the clip (#4813), the waveform strip (#4817) is the only sign that a video has sound. It drew in 38% of the clip on a 30% black wash. The bars meant for the audio surface became a low-contrast smudge in both themes, and in a host that themes its audio surface light with dark bars they disappeared. The peak readout ("▲ peaks +0.7 dBFS") was drawn faint red over the bars and ran into the clip's rounded corner, losing its last letters.

## Related work

Size: one self-contained visual fix with its tests (99 lines); nothing else belongs in it.

Refs #4813, #4817.

## How

- `AudibleVideoClipContent`: the strip's background is `var(--timeline-clip-audio-bg)`, and its share of the clip goes from 0.38 to 0.5. The bars keep their existing colour tokens, which are designed against that surface in every theme.
- `ClipPeakMarks`: the badge and its text get `data-peak-badge` / `data-peak-text`. Its look on an audio clip is unchanged.
- `components.css`: inside `.audible-video-wave`, the readout text is hidden and the mark sits on `--timeline-clip-chip-audio-bg`, vertically centred, inset by `--timeline-clip-radius`, at z-index 20: above the waveform canvas layer (10), below the fade handles (30).

## Test plan

- `AudibleVideoClipContent.test.tsx` (new): the strip paints on the audio clip surface and takes half the clip. Putting back the 0.38 share, or the black wash, fails it.
- A second test compiles Studio's own `studio.css` (as `Button.test.tsx` does) and checks the computed styles inside the strip: the readout text is hidden and the mark stacks above the waveform layer. Deleting either CSS rule fails it.
- `AudibleVideoClipContent`, `ClipPeakMarks` and `useRenderClipContent` tests: 25/25, three runs in a row. Studio `tsc --noEmit` clean, and oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.

title: fix(studio-server): undoing a change takes the media ledger back with the film
body:
## What changed

Project history keeps the media ledger, `.media/manifest.jsonl`, again. Since #4966 history skipped every hidden path except Studio's two manifests, so the ledger's record of a cutout or import was never part of the change. Undoing the change then took the film back but left the ledger naming media the film no longer uses.

A project that already ran 0.8.123 has a log that never names the ledger. On the first open after upgrading, history takes the ledger into the log's baseline as it stands, the way a first open records any file, so it is not filed as a new change and the first Undo undoes the person's edit, not the ledger. The log's baseline record then carries a `keepsLedger` mark, so later opens treat a ledger that appears as any other change. The take-in only accepts a ledger the sweep itself would list, so a ledger behind a link is never read into history.

## Why here

`isHistoryPath` is the one owner of which hidden paths history keeps. The ledger joins Studio's manifests in one kept set (`KEPT_HIDDEN_PATHS`); every other hidden name (a tool's record, `.DS_Store`) stays out.

## What I measured

- New test "takes the media ledger back with the film when a change is undone" fails without the fix (the entry lists only `index.html`) and passes with it, 3 runs in a row.
- "a log 0.8.123 wrote without the media ledger takes it in, so the first Undo undoes the edit" starts from that exact log (the person's edit recorded, the ledger on disk, the log never naming it). It fails without the fix (the first Undo deletes the ledger) and passes with it, 3 runs in a row.
- "a log 0.8.123 wrote never takes in a ledger behind a link" fails with the link check removed (a phantom entry appears on open) and passes with it.
- "a ledger made while the project was closed is a change like any file, once a log keeps the ledger" pins the marker.
- The cutout test asserts the exact files of the entry, so keeping all of `.media/` or any hidden `manifest.jsonl` fails it (both mutants checked red).
- History and project-signature suites: 156 pass; the touched tests pass 3 runs in a row.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Desktop's `tests/personWriteEntry.test.mjs`, which found this at 0.8.123: it needs a release with this fix; not run against this branch.
- An older version that rewrites a marked log drops the mark and the ledger with it, so the next open takes in the ledger as it stands, even one made while the project was closed. Such a log cannot tell the ledger the older version saw from a new one; taking it in is the side that never deletes the ledger on the first Undo.
- Other files under `.media/` (prefs, cached media) were history-tracked before #4966 and stay out after this PR; only the ledger was in scope. Whether any of them should come back is not decided here.

## Size

Small on purpose: a lone fix for a regression from #4966 in this repo, with no other open change here to carry it.

title: fix(cli): a project .env cannot set the feedback email in another letter case
body:
## What

A project `.env` can no longer set the feedback email by spelling its name in another letter case. `hyperframes_feedback_email=…` (or any mixed case) in a project `.env` is now skipped, the same as `HYPERFRAMES_FEEDBACK_EMAIL=…` already was. `hyperframes capture`, which loads the `.env` above its output folder, now applies the same rules instead of copying every key, the feedback email included.

## Why

Only the app that launches the CLI may attach an email to feedback; an agent can write a project `.env`, so `applyDotEnv` skips that key. The skip compared the name exactly. On Windows, environment variable names are case-blind, so `process.env.hyperframes_feedback_email = x` sets the same variable `feedbackEmail()` reads, and feedback that should be anonymous would carry an email from the project file.

Capture had its own `.env` parser with no skip at all. Feedback is sent only by the `feedback` command, in its own process, so that copy could not leak the email today, but it was a second set of rules for the same file.

## How

- `applyDotEnv` (`packages/cli/src/utils/dotEnv.ts`) compares the key upper-cased against `FEEDBACK_EMAIL_ENV`. `feedbackEmail()` is unchanged.
- `loadEnvFile` (`packages/cli/src/capture/scaffolding.ts`) keeps its walk up to five parent folders and hands the first `.env` it finds to `applyDotEnv`, which is now the one owner of how a project `.env` is applied.
- Side effects for capture, matching the CLI's own `.env` handling: `export KEY=…` lines and inline ` #` comments are parsed, a quoted value ends at its closing quote (so a double-quoted JSON value with unescaped inner quotes is cut short, as it already was for the CLI's own `.env`), and a variable already set to an empty string is no longer overwritten by the file.

## Test plan

- `dotEnv.test.ts`: "never takes the feedback email under another letter case" (lower and mixed case) fails on main (`expected { …(3) } to deeply equal { OTHER: '1' }`).
- `scaffolding.test.ts`: "loadEnvFile never takes the feedback email from a project file, in any letter case" writes a `.env` one folder above the start folder; it fails on main (`expected [ 'a@example.com', …(2) ] to deeply equal [ undefined, undefined, 'kept' ]`) and checks a quoted ordinary key is still loaded.
- `dotEnv`, `feedbackSource`, `scaffolding` and `captureAttempt` tests: 21 pass, 3 runs in a row (Linux). Pre-commit typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet pass.
- Not run on a native Windows machine: the tests check the rule directly, and the Windows behaviour it guards is Node's documented case-blind `process.env`.

## Size

Under the 100-line floor on purpose: a standalone privacy fix with nothing open to carry it.

## No visible change

CLI only; nothing under Studio or the player.

title: feat(studio): make edit with framey stand out in the header
body: ## What "Edit with Framey" in the Studio header stands out instead of reading like the ghost controls beside it: - an accent tint and border, semibold label, and a larger Framey (20 → 24px); - a "New" badge that stays (hidden only while the button says "Opening in the app…"); - a soft ring that pulses three times as Studio opens, then stops; none under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
