## Known limits

- Replaying to the playhead after an in-place move fires the timeline's callbacks again, as the existing fresh bind does. That predates this PR.
- A project with several inline scripts in one file is bundled into one preview script, so it still re-runs on every drag.
- Some re-prints still miss the fast path and re-run: `undefined` printed as `void 0`, and constant folding such as `"a" + "b"`.
- The script compare parses both scripts and serializes their trees: 77 to 136 ms per compare on 130 to 140 KB scripts, run twice per drop. Parsing once per drop is the next PR in this series.
- A script with `import` or top-level `await` does not parse as a classic script, so it always re-runs.

## Test plan

- [x] Real GSAP: a scene clip at 1 s moved to 4 s, then a rebind: the scene starts at 4 s and the frame matches a fresh load. Red before the fix.
- [x] A scene that a re-run root script places at 2 s stays there through a rebind and a later host move. Red before the fix.
- [x] An unmoved scene whose start does not round exactly is left in place on a rebind.
- [x] Script comparison: matches esbuild's verbatim re-print of a script; tells apart scripts that differ only in an operator, a comparison, a compound assignment, a unary operator, a regular expression, a private name, an array hole, a comma or a semicolon.
- [x] The live-retime table's host cases move in place and equal a fresh load; an operator flip inside a tween's value re-runs.
- [x] Core runtime suite, Studio live-retime and timing-sync tests 3 runs in a row; each guard broken on purpose turns its test red; typecheck, lint, format, comment ratchet, Fallow.
- [x] Built Studio, light and dark, wide and narrow: a host-clip drag moves in place, and the scene's frame matches a fresh load.

title: feat(studio): a host can hold playback so nothing starts while it is held
body:
## What

A host app can hold Studio's playback: `usePlayerStore.getState().setPlayLocked(true)`. While it is held nothing starts the film, and turning the hold on pauses a film that is playing. Seeking still moves the picture, but the scrub audio stays silent. `setPlayLocked(false)` gives playback back.

## Why

A host that edits the project underneath the preview (for example, an agent rewriting the composition) needs the film to stay still until it finishes. Pausing after a start is too late, because a frame can advance and audio can blip first. So the hold is checked where each start happens, before anything plays.

## How

- `playLocked` and `setPlayLocked` live in the readiness slice next to `timelineReady`, which already gates Play the same way. The host owns the hold, so a timeline reset leaves it alone.
- `useTimelinePlayer` checks the hold in `play()` (this covers the Play button, Space and playback requests) and in the seek that would keep playing, which also skips scrub audio while held. The loop restart in `useTimelinePlayerLoop` stops at the loop's end instead. The J/L shuttle in `usePlaybackKeyboard` returns before it changes the speed. A store subscription pauses when the hold turns on.
- `pause()` now stops the frame loop and clears the playing flag even before the preview has a player, so a hold set in that window cannot leave the bar reading Pause.

## Before

On main, with `playLocked` set on the store, Space plays the film anyway (60f to 135f in 2.5 s). Studio's own `decision-tree` example, dev build, time shown in frames.

![Before: held, Space plays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/917c7cfd-28a2-4f70-8c84-433b5b6938f6)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48fe0e84-2620-4a5c-942f-f6293051bfa3

## After

On this branch, with `setPlayLocked(true)`, Space leaves the film at 60f; after `setPlayLocked(false)`, Space plays it (60f to 135f).

![After: held, Space does nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd949fd7-bedc-48dd-b9a8-2b5d19be57b0)

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ea662ea-766f-4249-b9f9-85590a0c632a

## Tests

`useTimelinePlayer.playLock.test.ts`: while the hold is on, Play, a playback request, J and a keep-playing seek start nothing; a held seek moves the picture with no scrub audio; a looping film stops at its end; J and L keep the chosen speed; a hold set before the preview has a player still clears playing; turning it on pauses; turning it off lets Play start again.

The hold covers the film only. Sidebar and asset previews keep their own players.

title: fix(studio): a host can claim its writes under the key Studio's edit history uses
body:
## What changed

`usePersistentEditHistory` now also returns `claimKey(key)`: the exact history key its `recordEdit` claims under for a given `coalesceKey`. `recordEdit` builds its own key through it, so the hook stays the one place that knows the format.

## Why

Since #4937 every coalescing key is scoped to the page (`<page id>:<key>`), so a reload or a second tab never joins another page's step. A host that writes files itself (an import, a file replaced from disk) and claims them in the same project history, meaning to join the edit Studio saves next under the same key, had no way to learn the scoped key. Its claim stayed unscoped, so the host's write and Studio's save became two entries: one Cmd+Z took back the save and left the imported file behind.

With `claimKey`, the host claims under `claimKey(key)` and passes `key` to `recordEdit`, and both land in one entry. A host that calls `recordEdit` itself can already list its new files in `created`; `claimKey` is for a host whose backend writes and claims files without access to the hook.

## No visible change

A hook gains one returned function; nothing on screen changes. A host that adopts `claimKey` gets one undo where it had two.

## How I tested it

- New test in `usePersistentEditHistory.test.ts`, over the real history routes and engine: a host claims a new file under `claimKey(key)`, Studio saves under `key`, and one undo restores the composition and removes the file.
  - Fails on main (`claimKey` does not exist).
  - Fails when the host's key differs from the one `recordEdit` claims under (I changed `claimKey` to return the bare key while `recordEdit` kept the scoped one): the file survives the undo.
  - Passes 3 runs in a row with the change; the file's other 23 tests pass, including "a key one page holds does not join another page's edit under the same key".
- `tsc --noEmit` for packages/studio, oxlint and oxfmt on both files.

Small on purpose: one returned function and its test.

title: fix(studio): Layers rows show a kind icon, and only a group row has a caret
body:
## What a user can do now

In Studio's Layers panel, each row says what the element is with an icon people know: image, video, audio, vector, group, text or shape. Before, it showed the tag's first letters ("DI" for a div, "P", "H1"). Rows line up at the left unless they are nested: only a row with children has the expand caret (leaf rows no longer reserve its space), and each child's icon starts where its parent's label starts, one step per nesting level. Rows are inset on both sides with rounded corners, so the selected row's highlight is centred instead of running into the panel's left edge and stopping at the scrollbar.

## What changed

- New `components/editor/layerKind.ts`: `layerKindOf(element)`. `img`/`picture` is image; `video`, `audio` and `svg` are video, audio and vector. A `data-hf-group` or a composition host is a group. Text comes next, then a row with layer children (the panel's existing child count) is a group, so a plain wrapper with a caret reads as a group. Text keeps its icon even when its styled spans give it a caret, and media rows keep theirs. An element with text whose descendants are all rich-text formatting tags is text: it calls the inline text editor's own `hasOnlyFormattingChildren` (now exported), so the Text icon means Studio edits that element in place. Anything else is a shape.
- `isCompositionHost` moves from `LayersPanel.tsx` into `layerKind.ts`, so the badge's composition tint and the group icon read the same check (`data-composition-src` or `data-composition-file`).
- `LayersPanel.tsx`: the badge renders that kind's icon (with the kind as its tooltip and a `data-layer-kind` attribute) in the same 20px tile and the same selected and composition tints. The icon's tooltip carries the row's own hint ("Group · Double-click to enter group"), so hovering the icon no longer hides it. The tag-letter table is gone. A leaf row no longer reserves a caret column. One nesting level is a caret, the icon and their gaps (48px), so a child's icon starts where its parent's label starts. Rows, and the drill-in back row, are `mx-1 rounded-md`.
- `SystemIcons.tsx`: adds `ImageIcon`, `Vector` and `Folder` (Phosphor Image, BezierCurve, FolderSimple), beside the existing Film, Music, Type and Square.

## Tests

- `layerKind.test.ts` (new): 17 cases plus a children case covering every kind, `<picture>`, a wrapper with layer children (group), text with a classed span and children (still text), both composition-host attributes, rich text, text beside an image, a `<sub>` (not editable in place, so a shape), whitespace-only and media-in-a-div. It failed first because the module did not exist. Dropping the host check from the group rule fails both host cases; replacing the text check with `true` fails the image and `<sub>` cases.
- `layersPanelExport.test.tsx`: rows read their names, not tag letters ("Title", not "DiTitle"). A new case over a group nested in a group checks the kinds (text, group, image, group, image), that only a group's row starts with the caret, that a top-level leaf starts with its icon, the indents 8, 8, 56, 56 and 104px, that a plain wrapper with children is a group with a caret, that four kinds render four different icons, and that each icon's tooltip keeps its row's hint. It failed first on main ("DiTitle"). Restoring the leaf placeholder fails it, and so does the old 22px step.
- `layerKind`, `layersPanelExport`, `LayersPanel` and `domEditInlineText` tests together: 46 passed, 3 runs in a row. Each of these mutants fails at least one test: ignoring children in the group rule, checking children before text, rendering every row's icon as a shape, dropping `picture`, and a tooltip without the row's hint. `tsc --noEmit` in packages/studio shows no errors besides core's generated runtime file, which a fresh tree does not have. The comment-share ratchet passes against the merge base, and oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files.

## What I did not exercise

- The audio row: the panel lists only elements with a box on the canvas, so the fixture's `<audio>` has no row. The unit test covers its icon mapping.
- Drag-reorder in a real browser. The export test covers it in happy-dom.
- macOS pixels. The captures are headless Chromium on Linux, where the system font falls back to DejaVu Sans and labels draw 1 px above the icons' centre. The same row markup in Chromium on macOS (San Francisco) is centred to the pixel, and the row's boxes are centred in both.

## Before

Studio's Layers panel on main (6bb85af18), Vite dev server, a fixture with text, rich text, an image, a video, an svg, a long name, a dozen boxes and a two-child group. Shots are at 2x with the list scrolled to the end and Back selected: the window 1440 wide (left) and 1100 wide (right), light then dark.

Inside the group (double-click its row), light then dark: the back row runs edge to edge.

## After

This branch, same fixture and views (captured at a70f121b; every head since a0ea4709 was pixel-identical in all ten views).

title: render: "Fatal JavaScript invalid size error 268435456" in lowerAscii on large compiled HTML (since 0.8.77)
body:
### Describe the bug

Since 0.8.77, `hyperframes render` kills the Node process with `Fatal JavaScript invalid size error 268435456` (SIGTRAP, exit 133) right after frame capture starts, when the compiled `index.html` is large and has many uppercase runs. A common way to get there is many `@font-face` rules that point at local fonts, because render compile inlines every occurrence as base64. `hyperframes check` passes. 0.8.75 renders the same project.

Cause: `lowerAscii()` in `packages/core/src/compiler/htmlDocument.ts` (added in #4484) runs `text.replace(/[A-Z]+/g, fn)` over the whole HTML. A global regex replace with a callback collects every match into one V8 FixedArray before calling back. Above about 44.8M matches the array needs more than 2^27 slots and V8 aborts the process. This is not a catchable exception, and a bigger heap does not help. The producer file server runs it on every `index.html` response (`injectScriptsAtHeadStart`, then `stripEmbeddedRuntimeScripts` / `insertBeforeCloseTag`).

### Minimal reproduction

Synthetic assets only (one random 4 MB file used as a font):

```sh
npx hyperframes init repro --non-interactive --example blank
cd repro
mkdir -p fonts && head -c 4000000 /dev/urandom > fonts/synthetic.woff2
node -e '
const fs = require("fs");
let h = fs.readFileSync("index.html", "utf8").replace(/data-duration="10"/g, "data-duration=\"1\"");
let faces = "";
for (let i = 0; i < 40; i++) faces += `@font-face{font-family:"F${i}";src:url("fonts/synthetic.woff2") format("woff2")}\n`;
fs.writeFileSync("index.html", h.replace("<style>", "<style>\n" + faces));
'
npx hyperframes render --output out.mp4
```

The same V8 limit without HyperFrames:

```sh
node -e "'Aa'.repeat(45e6).replace(/[A-Z]+/g, s => s.toLowerCase())"
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the commands above.
2. The render reaches `capture_streaming` and the process aborts.

### Expected behavior

The render finishes, as it does with `npx hyperframes@0.8.75 render`.

### Actual behavior

```
# Fatal error in , line 0
# Fatal JavaScript invalid size error 268435456
 4: v8::internal::FixedArrayBuilder::EnsureCapacity(v8::internal::Isolate*, int)
 5: v8::internal::Runtime_RegExpExecMultiple(int, unsigned long*, v8::internal::Isolate*)
 8: Builtins_StringPrototypeReplace
```

Exit code 133, no frames written.

### Environment

```shell
hyperframes 0.8.133 (also 0.8.90, 0.8.131; 0.8.75 works)
Node.js v24.13.1, V8 13.6.233.17-node.40 (also v24.14.0)
macOS, darwin arm64
```

### Additional context

- A lowercase that does not build one array of all matches (a char-code scan, or the same regex on bounded chunks) keeps the length-preserving ASCII behavior that #4484 needs. A chunked version handled a 223 MB file in our tests.
- What makes the HTML this large: `embedLocalFontFaces` in render compile writes a data URI for every `@font-face` occurrence, so one font declared in N sub-compositions is embedded N times. `dedupeFontFaceRules` exists but is only used by `bundleToSingleHtml`. In our project, 5 fonts declared in each of 23 sub-compositions produced a 223 MB `index.html`. Declaring fonts once in the root avoids it on our side.
- Happy to send a PR for the `lowerAscii` part if that helps.

title: fix(cli): the blank template ships a live example tween
body:
## What

`hyperframes init` scaffolds a project that fails `hyperframes check`. The `blank` template registers a paused GSAP timeline whose only tween is commented out, so the composition is byte-identical at every seek and the `sweep_static` layout guard fires.

This PR ships the example tween live, plus a regression test.

## Why

`sweep_static` is working as designed — it exists to invalidate every other verdict from a run whose timeline never moved. The template was what was wrong.

Repro on `main` at `db12b3e`, and on the published `hyperframes@0.8.133`:

```bash
npx hyperframes init demo --non-interactive
cd demo && npx hyperframes check
```

```
Layout
  ✗ t=0s sweep_static [data-composition-id] — Timeline did not advance under seek;
    every green verdict on this run is unreliable.
      Fix: Confirm the composition seeks a paused GSAP/CSS timeline under `data-*`
      timing attributes rather than only autoplaying.
  1 error(s), 0 warning(s), 0 info(s)
...
◇  Check failed
```

`render` still succeeds and produces a correct MP4, so this is not a broken render — but it is the first thing a new user runs after `init`, it fails, and the message says the rest of the run's results are unreliable. That reads as "the tool is broken" rather than "the starting point is empty."

Two mitigating details worth knowing:

- The guard skips compositions carrying `data-no-timeline` on the composition root (`packages/cli/src/utils/checkBrowser.ts:429`), so a template with *no* timeline is fine. It is specifically a *declared but empty* timeline that trips it.
- The check only reports when duration ≥ 3s and at least 2 samples were taken, so short compositions are unaffected.

## How

`packages/cli/src/templates/blank/index.html` — uncomment the example tween that was already written in the file, targeting the `#title` the template already renders:

```js
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
// An empty timeline makes `hyperframes check` fail its own scaffold with
// sweep_static, so the example tween below ships live and is yours to edit.
tl.fromTo("#title", { opacity: 0, y: 24 }, { opacity: 1, y: 0, duration: 0.6 }, 0);
window.__timelines["main"] = tl;
tl.seek(0);
```

`packages/cli/src/commands/init.test.ts` — a new test asserting the scaffolded timeline actually carries a tween. The existing `bare init scaffolds the centered blank` test asserted `tl.seek(0)` but never checked the timeline had anything on it, which is how an empty timeline shipped. The new assertion strips comments first, so re-commenting the example fails the test rather than silently passing again.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated — the template hint in `packages/cli/src/templates/generators.ts` still reads `"Centered Inter stage, paused timeline"`, which stays accurate. Happy to reword if you'd prefer it advertise the working tween.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Verified the regression test is a real regression test — it fails on the unfixed template and passes on the fixed one:

```
fixed template:     ✓ scaffolds a blank timeline that actually advances under seek   30 passed
template reverted:  × scaffolds a blank timeline that actually advances under seek    1 failed | 29 passed
```

Manual, against the published CLI and against this branch's build:

| | `check` before | `check` after |
|---|---|---|
| `init` (blank) | ✗ 1 error, `sweep_static` | ◇ 0 issues across 9 samples |
| | `Check failed` | `Check passed` |

Gates run locally on this branch:

- `bun run lint` — full chain clean (all 11 checks, oxlint 0 warnings/0 errors across 4,082 files, skill mirror byte-identical)
- `bun run format:check` — clean across 6,322 files
- `bun run --filter @hyperframes/cli typecheck` — exit 0
- `bun run --filter @hyperframes/cli test` — 4,250 passed, 1 failed

The one failure is `renderCancellation.process.test.ts > ... exits from SIGTERM`, which is pre-existing and unrelated: it passes 4/4 in isolation on both this branch and a pristine `main`, and only fails under full-suite parallel load on this 4-core box. My diff is a static HTML template plus a string-matching test and cannot reach signal delivery.

`render` verified end to end after the change — 300 frames, 10.0s, 1920x1080 H.264, and byte-identical across two runs (`md5 efa24e21c7a5119df3879260393f2264`), so the seek determinism the tool depends on is unaffected.

## Related finding, not fixed here

The `from-file` template has the same empty-timeline shape and is reachable without `--video`: `resolveScaffoldTemplateId` (`packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts:66`) routes *any* media file to `from-file`, so `init --audio track.m4a` fails the same way.

I left it alone because the fix is a product decision rather than a bug fix, and the two obvious options both cost something:

- Uncommenting its example tween does not work — `from-file`'s `#title` lives inside an HTML comment as an author example, so there is no element to animate. GSAP would build a zero-target tween, the pixels would not change, and `sweep_static` would still fire.
- Adding `data-no-timeline` to the composition root would suppress the guard, but it would stay on the root after an author adds their own overlay and timeline, silently disarming the check for every project built on the template. That seems worse than the bug.

Uncommenting works for `init --video` only by accident — the playing video changes the sampled pixels, so the fingerprint differs regardless of the timeline. That is the argument for fixing it properly rather than relying on it. Happy to follow up once you've decided which way the template should go.

title: fix(cli): init refuses a name too long for a folder in one plain sentence
body:
## What

`hyperframes init` refuses a project name that is too long for a folder, with one plain sentence that names the limit and the name's length, before it creates anything:

```
That name is 256 bytes long; a folder name can be at most 255 bytes.
```

## Why

A name longer than the disk's folder-name limit reached `mkdirSync`, and the command exited with Node's raw error and the full path:

```
ENAMETOOLONG: name too long, mkdir '<cwd>/aaaa…'
```

Repro on 0.8.126 and on current `main`: `npx hyperframes init $(printf 'a%.0s' $(seq 300)) --example blank --non-interactive`.

## Related work

None found.

## How

- `nameTooLongMessage(name, platform)` in `packages/cli/src/commands/init.ts` checks each folder in the resolved destination (a nested name like `parent/<name>` is held to the limit per folder, not as a whole path) and measures it the way the disk does: UTF-8 bytes on Linux, UTF-16 units on macOS and Windows. The limit is 255 for all three.
- Both name paths validate the resolved destination before any disk work, so a long component removed by `..` cannot reject a valid destination: non-interactive mode prints the sentence with the usual error style; interactive mode prints it through the prompt UI and cancels. Both exit 1 and leave no folder behind.
- The sentence never echoes the name or a path.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Ran on Linux:

- New tests in `init.test.ts`, written first and red before the fix (the over-limit run printed the raw `ENAMETOOLONG` with the path):
  - a 256-character name exits 1 with the sentence, no `ENAMETOOLONG`, no path, and no folder created;
  - a 255-character name scaffolds;
  - the per-platform rule: 128 `é` (256 bytes, 128 characters) is refused on Linux and accepted on macOS, 127 `é` is accepted on Linux, a nested name is held to the limit per folder.
- Final focused checks: `init.test.ts` passed 34 tests and `init.interactive.test.ts` passed 2 tests, each run alone three times with one worker. Every run exited 0 with no skipped tests.
- Measuring by characters on Linux makes the per-platform test fail.
- Interactive mode, driven under a pseudo-terminal with a 256-character name: the prompt shows the sentence, says "Setup cancelled.", and no folder is created.
- `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli`, the pre-commit hooks (oxlint, oxfmt, fallow, typecheck), `check-comment-citations` and `comment-ratchet` pass.
- The interactive path has its own test (`init.interactive.test.ts`): a long name given on the command line and one typed into the prompt each show the sentence and leave no folder. Removing the interactive check fails it.
- A path whose oversized component is removed by `..` scaffolds its resolved destination. Checking the raw name fails this regression and reports the wrong length in both interactive cases.
- A Windows name like `parent\<256 characters>` is measured per folder. Splitting on `/` only fails that assertion.

Not exercised: a macOS or Windows run; the macOS and Windows rule is covered by the unit test only. Filesystems with a shorter limit than 255 (some encrypted or network mounts) still reach `mkdirSync` and its own error.

## Known limits

- **Older macOS disks (HFS+)** store accented letters decomposed, so a name of 128 `é` passes the check there and still fails with the raw error. Counting decomposed would wrongly refuse valid names on APFS, the current macOS format.
- **Linux writing to a Windows-format drive** (WSL's `/mnt/c`, an NTFS or exFAT USB stick) is measured in bytes, so a name that would fit there can be refused. It fails with the clear sentence, never the raw error.

## Why this PR is small

One user-facing fix with its tests; nothing else in flight shares its code path, so there is nothing to bundle it with.


## Independent review

| Audited | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Argument parsing and both init branches | Both validate the resolved destination before filesystem writes. |
| Interactive failures | Full diagnostic asserted for positional and prompted names; the parent directory remains empty. |
| Failure sensitivity | Removing interactive validation or Windows separator handling fails the corresponding tests; raw-path validation fails the normalization cases. |

title: fix(studio): a move after a resize, an undo or Add keyframe lands where it is let go
body:
## What

Draft, stacked on #5045 (its bench cases are the red cases here); retargets to main once #5045 merges.

Studio drops or misplaces a move in three gesture sequences:

- **Resize, undo, then drag on a nested element:** after the undo settles, the drag does not move the box and nothing is saved (`seqresizeundodrag-tween-px-r0-nested-z100`).

Red cases first; fixes follow on this branch.

title: feat(cli): link the desktop app to the claude code session that made a project
body:
## What

While the Claude Code session that made a project is open, the HyperFrames desktop app can send its chat to that session instead of starting an agent of its own. One agent does the work, and the terminal and the app see the same conversation. The desktop half is heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#2804; this PR is the CLI and skills half.

- **`.hyperframes/agent-link.json`** names the session (`CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`) and its inbox socket (`CLAUDE_CODE_MESSAGING_SOCKET`, Claude Code's cross-session messaging, 2.1.224+). `hyperframes open`, Studio's Edit with Framey and `preview` write it. Owner-only (0600), written atomically.
- **Resume:** a resumed session gets a new inbox. Any `hyperframes` command run in a linked project (cwd or a path argument) rewrites the link, so the app reaches it again.
- **Relay:** `preview` serves `POST /api/agent-link/message` (bearer token from the link file, loopback host only) and forwards to the inbox of the session that started it. Claude Code holds messages from outside processes when a session skips permission prompts, but delivers ones from the session's own running children. A preview started as the session's own background task is such a child. A relay is kept in the link only while it forwards to the link's inbox.
- **Skills:**
  - `/hyperframes-cli` and `preview-render.md`: under Claude Code, start the final preview with `--foreground` as the session's own background task.
  - `/hyperframes` § 6: a message from another session that says it comes from the HyperFrames desktop app is the user's own request.
  - `open` prints that hint when no relay is running.

- **App tools from a linked session** (second commit): a running session cannot be given new tools, so `hyperframes app-tools list` / `call <tool> '<json>'` reach the desktop app's picture tools and `app.look`. The endpoint comes from `.hyperframes/app-tools.json`, which the app writes for the turn it is working on (owner-only). A picture in a result is written to a file instead of printed as base64. It answers only while an app turn is working on the project; otherwise it exits 1 with a plain message.
- **Marks kept:** a link rewritten for the same session keeps the app's own marks (`briefed`, `handedOver`), so a command run mid-session does not make the app brief the session again.

Codex has no inbox, so nothing changes there: it keeps the one-time hand-off.

## Why

Today the app's Framey starts its own session and copies the last ~12,000 characters of the terminal conversation into its first message, so what the person says in the app never reaches the terminal session. Remote Control is closed to third parties, and resuming the same session from two processes makes two agents interleave one transcript. Claude Code's per-session inbox is the supported way for a local process to post into a running session.

## Related work

Refs #4951, #4999. Desktop half: heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#2804.

## How

`utils/agentLink.ts` holds the file format, the writer/refresher and the inbox post. The message format (an optional `{"type":"auth"}` line, then `{"type":"user","message":{...}}`) is the one Claude Code's own help text shows for scripts posting to the socket. `desktopRoutes.ts` mounts the relay next to the open route. `preview.ts` mints a token per server and writes the link once listening.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit: `agentLink.test.ts` (write/refresh/relay-drop/owner-only, wire format against a real unix socket), `desktopRoutes.test.ts` (relay auth, rebound host, empty text, inbox gone, link handed to `open`), `desktopApp.test.ts`. 44 pass; the preview/open/server suites pass (173).
- [x] Real Claude Code 2.1.289, macOS:
  - A session started with `--dangerously-skip-permissions` ran this branch's `preview --foreground` as its background task. That wrote the link with the relay (0600).
  - The desktop runner (internal PR) sent "How long is this composition?" and "change the background to #1a1a2e" through the relay. The session read and edited `index.html` and answered; the transcript shows `verifiedPeerPid` / `selfSent: true`.
  - With the relay killed, the direct post was held, as Claude Code documents for bypass sessions.
  - `hyperframes lint` run with a new inbox in the env rewrote the link and dropped the stale relay.
- [x] `app-tools`: `appTools.test.ts` (request, errors, pictures to files). Against the desktop's real `/mcp/image/<key>` route (hyperframes-internal#2804, mounted with `mountMcp`) during a linked turn, `list` returned the app's instructions and `app.look`, and `call app.look` reached it. After the turn: "The HyperFrames desktop app is not working on this project right now.", exit 1.
- [ ] Documentation updated (skills only; no docs page names the link)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: lint: root-relative stylesheet link in a sub-composition fails font_family_without_font_face, ../ fails invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path
body: ### Describe the bug In a sub-composition, there is no way to link a shared local stylesheet that lint accepts if the file names a font that the stylesheet declares: - `href="assets/fonts.css"` (root-relative, as `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path` asks for): `font_family_without_font_face` fires, because lint looks for the stylesheet relative to the HTML file (`compositions/frames/assets/fonts.css`) and does not find it. - `href="../../assets/fonts.css"`: `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path` fires. `collectLocalStylesheets` in `packages/lint/src/project.ts` resolves the href as `join(dirname(compSrcPath), href)`, while the traversal rule says sub-composition paths are served from the project root. ### Minimal reproduction ```sh npx hyperframes init repro --non-interactive --example blank cd repro mkdir -p assets/fonts compositions/frames head -c 20000 /dev/urandom > assets/fonts/repro.woff2 echo "@font-face{font-family:'Repro';src:url('fonts/repro.woff2') format('woff2')}" > assets/fonts.css cat > compositions/frames/scene.html <<'EOF' EOF npx hyperframes lint ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run the commands above: `font_family_without_font_face` on `compositions/frames/scene.html`. 2. Change the href to `../../assets/fonts.css` and lint again: `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path`. The same happens with the file directly in `compositions/`. ### Expected behavior The root-relative link passes lint, since lint reads `assets/fonts.css` from the project root, as the traversal rule describes. ### Actual behavior One of the two errors fires whichever way the link is written. A lint error also skips the browser checks in `hyperframes check`. ### Environment ```shell hyperframes 0.8.133 Node.js v24.13.1, macOS darwin arm64 ``` ### Additional context Our workaround is a symlink `compositions/frames/assets -> ../../assets` so the file-relative lookup finds the same file. Declaring fonts once in a linked stylesheet is how we avoid the large inlined HTML in #5069.

title: docs(skills): teach shared cut constants and fill lights for Three.js scenes
body:
## What

`skills/hyperframes-animation/adapters/three.md` gains two sections:

- **Camera Cuts Inside One Canvas**: declare each in-canvas cut once and read the constant from both the shot selector and every object's visibility window. Verify on the last frame before each cut with `snapshot --at (ceil(cut*fps)-1)/fps`.
- **Lighting Lit Meshes**: a `MeshStandardMaterial` lit by a single key light, with no ambient, env map or emissive, renders as a flat black cutout when the camera faces the light. Add a fill such as a `HemisphereLight` driven from the same source as the key at a fixed ratio, not the same number.

`skills-manifest.json` is regenerated.

## Why

A Three.js composition that switched shots by time had visibility windows written as separate literals (`t > 22.9` against a cut at `t < 23`). At 30 fps that put the next shot's meshes into frames 688 and 689 of the previous shot. Checking one still per shot did not catch it. The same scene's rocks, lit only by a sun `PointLight` while the camera faced the sun, rendered as black silhouettes. The skill covered neither case.

A re-render with the CLI matched the original output frame for frame (PSNR 34 to 39 dB), so neither problem comes from the engine.

## Verification

- `bun packages/cli/scripts/gen-skills-manifest.ts --check`: in sync (21 skills).
- `oxfmt --check`: clean.
- Claims checked against the code: `snapshot --at` seeks the exact instant (`snapshot.ts`, `exactTime: true`), and `(ceil(23*30)-1)/30 = 22.9667` is frame 689.
- An independent review flagged that the first sample used `t` at top level and that it implied copying the key light's intensity onto the fill. Both are fixed in this head.

Signed: Miga

title: test(studio): bundle the real-Chrome undo test with esbuild so its setup fits on Windows
body:
## What

The real-Chrome undo test (`gsapUndoRestore.browser.test.ts`) no longer runs out of time while it gets ready on a busy Windows runner. Before, its setup sometimes took over 60 s there and the whole file failed with "Hook timed out in 60000ms".

## Why

The setup does three things before any test runs: it launches Chrome, then builds the two modules under test into browser bundles. The two builds used Vite's library mode (Rollup), and they were most of the cost, not the launch. Timed on a Linux machine, 3 rounds:

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| Chrome launch | 0.2 to 0.7 s |
| Vite build of `gsapUndoRestore.ts` | 1.3 to 3.1 s |
| Vite build of `gsapSoftReload.ts` | 1.2 to 2.0 s |
| esbuild of `gsapUndoRestore.ts` | 85 to 122 ms (0.5 to 1 s for the first build in a fresh process) |
| esbuild of `gsapSoftReload.ts` | 80 to 89 ms |

On Windows runners this file usually takes 6 to 14 s in total. The failing run was on a runner several times slower than usual: the other real-Chrome test in the same job, which launches Chrome but builds nothing, took 20.6 s against its usual 2 to 6 s. At that speed, the setup's two builds alone pushed the hook past 60 s. The earlier fix raised the time budget; this one removes the cost instead, and leaves the budget as it is.

## How

- The test bundles each module with esbuild, the bundler core already uses for its browser IIFE builds (`buildInjectedArtifact.ts`).
- Studio's code pulls in a parser that imports Node's `fs` and `os`; the code that uses them is dropped from the bundle. Vite's browser builds turn Node built-ins into empty modules, and a small esbuild plugin in the test does the same for exactly those two, so a new one fails the build instead of going quietly empty.
- `import.meta.env` is declared as an empty object, which is what the esbuild bundle already saw, so esbuild's other warnings stay visible.
- `esbuild` becomes a dev dependency of Studio, at the version the other packages already use, so the lockfile gains one line.

## Why this PR is small

It fixes one flaky CI check on its own, so it can land and be reverted without carrying unrelated work.

## No visible change

Test-only. Studio's code, its bundle and its behaviour are unchanged; only how one test builds the modules it loads into Chrome changes.

## Test plan

- **The 11 tests pass on the esbuild bundles** on a Linux machine with Chrome for Testing, 3 runs in a row.
- **The file got faster, mostly in its setup.** Same machine, same load:
  - main (Vite): 5.8, 5.8 and 7.3 s for the whole file;
  - this branch (esbuild): 3.5, 3.0 and 3.2 s.
- **Windows.** The Windows workflow passed 3 times in a row at the final head (b3334db8c), with this file at 4.1, 4.2 and 5.4 s; recent runs before this change took 6 to 14 s, and the failing one over 60 s. The first head also passed once, at 4.8 s.
- **Lockfile.** `bun install --frozen-lockfile` passes with the one added line.

title: fix(ci): skills sync publishes hyperframes-creative past its hidden 1.0.13 and checks it went live
body:
## What

The "Sync skills to ClawHub" workflow on main has been red since 2026-09-08. Its latest failure says `hyperframes-creative: Version 1.0.13 already exists`. `hyperframes-creative` can no longer publish, so its changes have not reached ClawHub for about a month. Each run plans `latest 1.0.12; publish 1.0.13`, and the registry refuses.

1.0.13 was published on 2026-09-04 (the sync logged `Published hyperframes-creative@1.0.13`) and is now hidden. The registry answers "Version not found" for it and lists 1.0.0 to 1.0.12.

With this change, that one acknowledged case, `hyperframes-creative` with 1.0.13 taken, is published at 1.0.14. The job then fails unless the registry's `latest` for the skill is 1.0.14. Any other taken version, on any skill, still fails the job loudly, as before. **Merging this publishes `hyperframes-creative` 1.0.14 and should turn main's sync green.**

## Why

`clawhub sync` picks the next version as the registry's `latest` tag plus one patch. A hidden version keeps its number but never becomes `latest`, so every run computes 1.0.13 again and fails the same way. Rerunning cannot fix it, and the current CLI (0.23.3) chooses the version the same way.

Skipping is limited to the one version we know was hidden. A new hidden version on any skill should stop the sync until a person looks at why, rather than be published past automatically.

## How

- `scripts/clawhub-sync.mjs` runs the same `clawhub sync` as before (same owner, bump, changelog and source provenance, now with `--json`).
- `SKIPPABLE_TAKEN` names the acknowledged case (`hyperframes-creative` → `1.0.13`). Only a sync failure for exactly that skill and version is republished with `clawhub publish --version 1.0.14`, using the same owner, changelog and source provenance as the sync (including `--source-path skills/<slug>`).
- If 1.0.14 is taken too, the job fails instead of skipping further.
- After the republish, it reads the skill back as `heygen-com/hyperframes-creative`, because other owners publish skills with some of the same names. The job fails unless `latest` is 1.0.14.
- Any other failure fails the job with the registry's message: another taken version, another refusal, a refused republish, or a failed sync whose output cannot be read. A dry run behaves as before and does not preview a republish.
- The workflow calls the script and also runs when the script changes, so merging this publishes the stuck skill once.

## Test plan

- [x] `scripts/clawhub-sync.test.mjs` uses a fake CLI that replays the failure from main. These cases are covered:
  - `hyperframes-creative` is republished at 1.0.14 and read back as `heygen-com/hyperframes-creative`, with every argument of the sync, the publish and the read pinned.
  - A republish the registry accepts but does not show as `latest` fails.
  - A taken 1.0.14 fails without trying 1.0.15.
  - A taken version on another skill (figma 1.0.17, and figma 1.0.13), or another taken version of `hyperframes-creative` (1.0.15), fails with no publish.
  - A dry run passes `--dry-run` and publishes nothing.
  - Other refusals are reported without a retry.
  - A failed sync with no readable result fails.
  - A clean sync stops after one call.
  - The script exits 1 on a failed sync, so the workflow goes red.
- [x] Each of these mutations fails a test: dropping the owner from the publish or the read, the source path, `--dry-run` or the dry-run guard, the `latest` check, the exit code, the clean-sync return, the narrowing to the acknowledged version, or matching only its version and not its skill.
- [x] The suite passes three runs in a row. Format and lint are clean.
- [ ] After merge: the first run on main publishes `hyperframes-creative` 1.0.14 and shows it as `latest`.

## Known limits

- If the CLI's own retry lands a publish and then reports "already exists" for it, the job fails although the version is live. The next push syncs normally.

title: [Bug] Linux AppImage does not register the sign-in callback handler
body:
### Describe the bug

The Linux desktop AppImage can open HeyGen sign-in in the browser, but the sign-in cannot return to the running app because no handler is registered for `hyperframes-signin://` links.

This occurred with `HyperFrames-x86_64-b266.AppImage` after following the documented Linux setup, which only makes the AppImage executable and launches it.

### Link to reproduction

Official Linux download: https://www.hyperframes.dev/studio

Linux setup instructions: https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/main/docs/studio-app/index.mdx

### Steps to reproduce

1. On Linux without an existing HyperFrames sign-in URL handler, download `HyperFrames-x86_64-b266.AppImage`.
2. Make the AppImage executable and launch it, as documented.
3. Choose **Continue with HeyGen** in the app and complete sign-in in the browser.
4. The app remains waiting for the browser return.

The missing OS handler can also be reproduced without signing in or sharing an OAuth code:

```sh
xdg-mime query default x-scheme-handler/hyperframes-signin
# No output

gio mime x-scheme-handler/hyperframes-signin
# No default applications for “x-scheme-handler/hyperframes-signin”

gio open 'hyperframes-signin://callback?verification=1'
# gio: hyperframes-signin://callback?verification=1: The specified location is not supported
# Exit status 2
```

The probe URL contains no OAuth code, state, or credentials.

### Expected behavior

After the documented Linux setup, the browser can hand the sign-in callback to the running HyperFrames app.

### Actual behavior

Linux has no application associated with the sign-in callback scheme, so the return link cannot reach the app.

The AppImage contains one desktop entry, `dev.hyperframes.desktop.desktop`. It has `Exec=AppRun %U`, but no `MimeType` entry for the sign-in scheme. Its `AppRun` script only launches the executable. Inspection of the shipped app-owned startup code found callback handling, but no Linux protocol registration.

### Environment

- Desktop download: `HyperFrames-x86_64-b266.AppImage`
- Desktop package version: `0.1.0`
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Distribution: Omarchy, based on Arch Linux
- Desktop: Hyprland
- This concerns the desktop app's sign-in callback, rather than CLI rendering.

### Additional context

A temporary per-user desktop entry pointing to the same AppImage, associated with `x-scheme-handler/hyperframes-signin`, made the identical harmless `gio open` probe succeed with exit status 0. The existing app stayed running. That temporary registration was removed after diagnosis, and the original app associations were restored.

A complete authenticated sign-in after that workaround has **not** been verified. The verified result is that the OS rejects the callback without a handler and accepts it once the handler is registered.

The durable fix appears to belong to the Linux desktop app's packaging or first-launch integration: ship the scheme metadata and register a launcher that can receive the callback at the installed AppImage path.

I could not find the desktop packaging source in this public repository. If that source is maintained separately, please route this report to its owner and identify where contributors can submit the fix. A CLI-only or documentation-only change would not repair sign-in when the downloaded AppImage is launched directly.

title: fix(lint): read a sub-composition's linked stylesheet from the project root
body:
## What

`hyperframes lint` now finds a stylesheet that a sub-composition links with a plain path like `assets/fonts.css`. It still looks next to the sub-composition first. If nothing is there, it looks in the project root.

## Why

In #5074 the fonts are declared once in `assets/fonts.css` and every sub-composition links that file. Lint only looked next to the HTML (`compositions/frames/assets/fonts.css`), found nothing, and reported `font_family_without_font_face` for a font that is declared. Writing the link as `../../assets/fonts.css` trips `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path` instead, so there was no spelling that passed. The reporter ended up adding a symlink just to get through lint.

The preview and the bundler already load that link from the project root when there is no file beside the sub-composition, so lint was the one that disagreed.

## Related work

Fixes #5074

## How

In `collectLocalStylesheets` the lookup next to the file is the same as before. When it finds nothing, the same href is tried from the project root. Links that start with `/` or have a `..` segment don't get the second look, so they behave as they do on `main`.

Looking in a second place also means lint can land on a folder that happens to have the stylesheet's name, and reading it threw `EISDIR`. The file is now read with `readProjectFile` and skipped when it isn't a regular file.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added in `project.test.ts`:
  - the layout from the issue, with the sub-composition nested and directly under `compositions/` (fails on `main`)
  - a stylesheet beside the sub-composition still wins over one with the same name in the root
  - `/...` and `../...` links are not looked up in the root
  - a folder with the stylesheet's name is skipped instead of throwing
- [x] `packages/lint`: 838 passed. The CLI's lint, check and validate tests: 365 passed. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check`, the comments check, the comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Manual testing, running the CLI from source:
  - The repro from the issue: `main` reports the `font_family_without_font_face` error, this branch reports 0 errors.

title: fix(studio): a timeline jump no longer starts thumbnail loads it is about to cancel
body:
## What

When a timeline jump unmounts clips whose thumbnails are loading or queued, Studio no longer starts the queued loads that the same unmount is about to cancel.

## Why

Releasing a lease on a loading thumbnail aborts it, and the abort frees its concurrency slot. Freeing the slot called `pump()` straight away, which started the next queued job. A jump unmounts every clip in its region in one commit, so that next job was usually one whose own release came a moment later in the same commit: it started, sent its request, and was aborted. Each release in the batch repeated this, so one jump could start and cancel a load per clip.

On the Studio timeline viewport gate's fixture with the CPU throttled 2x, main sent 148 thumbnail requests in one run and finished none of them. The wasted starts and aborts land on the main thread during the next scroll steps.

## Related work

Found while profiling the "Studio: timeline viewport gate" flake. This PR does not change the gate or claim to fix its flake: on hosted runners the gate's slow tail is mostly the cost of one scroll step itself, which a follow-up PR measures and reduces.

## How

`freeSlot` (the abort and completion handler in `ThumbnailScheduler.start`) now pumps in a microtask instead of synchronously, so every release in the current task lands before anything new starts, and only clips that still hold a lease are started. React runs all of a commit's cleanups in one synchronous flush, so one jump's releases all land first. A batch queues one microtask pump per freed slot, as many pumps as main already ran, and extra pumps are harmless. The decrement of the active counters stays synchronous, so a fresh `acquire` in the same task still sees the freed slot. `acquire`, priority updates and the completion path keep their synchronous pump.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `thumbnailScheduler.test.ts` "starts nothing that a release later in the same batch drops" releases the loading job first, then a queued one, and expects the queued one never to load and the remaining one to start. It fails on main (the dropped load started, 1 call) and passes here, 3 of 3 runs. "frees an aborted job's slot at once" now asserts without waiting a tick, so it fails if the counter decrement is deferred along with the pump. The scheduler file passes 19/19 three times. Studio's other thumbnail suites (`player/lib`, `useThumbnailLease`, `useThumbnailStill`, the composition, image and video thumbnail components, and the Compositions tab thumbnails) pass 249/249 three times.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the gate's own scroll protocol on its `timeline-virtualization` fixture, Chrome 154, CPU throttle 2x, 5 runs × 63 steps per row, alternating main and this branch. Thumbnail requests in a traced run went from 148 sent / 0 finished to 16 sent / 2 finished. Scroll steps taking 4 or more frames went from 14.0%, 4.1% and 15.6% to 0.6%, 0.0% and 4.5%. Machine load varied between rows (1.6 to 7.5), which moves the frame tail, so the request count is the mechanical measure.
- [x] Format, lint, `tsc` for studio, test reachability, the Fallow audit (no new findings), the comment ratchet and comment citations all pass.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": no comment added (the ratchet allows none here); the test names carry the reason and the repro.

title: test(producer): compiler parity test runs without the network
body:
## What

`htmlCompiler.parity.test.ts > keeps each composition's link to a shared file under its own condition in preview, render and mount` failed CI with "Test timed out in 5000ms" on a PR that does not touch the producer. The test reached out to the network, so its run time depended on the runner's DNS. It now runs with no network at all.

## Why

The test links `https://cdn.example/shared.css`. Two things fetched it for real:

- The render compiler downloads external stylesheets (`fetchPublicHttpsText`, 15 s timeout) and keeps the `<link>` when that fails. Every run did a real DNS lookup for `cdn.example`.
- The test reads compiled output back with `DOMParser`, and happy-dom loads `<link rel="stylesheet">` even in a parsed document. That is the same lookup again, plus `http://localhost:3000/<file>.css` for relative links, since happy-dom's page URL is `localhost:3000`. That produced the `ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:3000` noise in the log.

When the lookup is slow, the test runs past its 5 s limit.

## How

In the test file only:

- The compiler's `fetchPublicHttpsText` is mocked to refuse at once. The compiler then keeps the link tag, which is what the test asserts.
- happy-dom's CSS file loading is turned off for this file, and a skipped file counts as loaded so happy-dom does not log an error for each link, in the same way other test files turn off iframe loading.

No production code changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Red first: with every non-local DNS lookup made to hang (a preloaded `dns.lookup` that never answers, like a slow resolver), the test on main fails exactly as in CI ("Test timed out in 5000ms", 12 of 13 passing), and with this change all 13 pass.
- [x] A normal run on main logs 51 network errors (`ENOTFOUND cdn.example`, `ECONNREFUSED localhost:3000`); with this change it logs no network or file-loading errors (only the fixtures' own expected warnings).
- [x] 13 of 13 pass, three runs in a row. Format, lint and typecheck.

title: fix(studio): drags after a resize, undo or reload land where they were pressed
body:
## What

Five gesture and keyframe fixes found by the edit-accuracy bench cases banked in #5045, and a stricter undo check in that bench:

- **A drag after undoing a nested edit moves again.** An undo that has to reload the preview cleared the selection, so the next press only re-picked the element and no drag started (`seqresizeundodrag-tween-px-r0-nested-z100`). The reload now finds the selection again, the same way a reload after an outside edit does, and drops it only if the undo removed its element.
- **A move pressed while the preview reloads lands on the new preview, at the time it was pressed.** On a page with no GSAP yet, the first Add keyframe fully reloads the preview. A move pressed during that reload ran on the old page, was saved as a plain CSS move, and the new keys overrode it (`seqfastkeys-none-px-r0-root-z100`, 40.8 px off). A press that lands while any preview reload is in flight now waits for it: the selection box follows the pointer meanwhile, and once the new preview shows the element, the drag starts there and the element catches up to the box. With no reload pending the press starts the drag at once.
  A gesture now records the playhead time (and the selected keyframe, if any) when it is pressed, and its commit keys at that time. Before, every gesture commit read the playhead when it ran, so a seek made while the press waited moved the key: pressed at 2 s, written at 3 s.
- **A box held by a zero-length `tl.set` can be resized, moved, resized and moved again while saves are slow.** The press wait now opens at the drop of any gesture that writes the script, not when the write leaves the queue, so an in-place update can no longer repaint the box without the move. Presses queued behind one another run in order, never instead of each other. Three faults in the waiting press, each with a test that failed first:
  - releasing the pointer releases capture, and the old capture-loss handler cancelled the released press; a released press now survives it, and the trailing click no longer re-picks the element;
  - a buttonless hover after the release moved the waiting outline under the pointer (290 px instead of 140 px);
  - an earlier queued press, replaying, drew over the newest waiting outline (200 px instead of 160 px).

  How a waiting press behaves, each with a test that failed first:
  - it edits the element it pressed, found again on the new preview, even if another element is selected before it runs;
  - Cmd+Z while it waits takes it back before it ever runs (it is the newest edit), instead of undoing the edit before it;
  - window blur, pointer cancel or lost capture end only a press still held; a drag already let go still lands. Turning read-only or closing the canvas drops the queue;
  - a waiting resize draws the size the resize will save (it grows about the centre), so the box does not jump when it runs;
  - an in-place scene swap counts as the preview changing, so a press waits for the new scenes and moves the swapped-in node;
  - a press never waits more than 10 s. A change that never ends (a save with no reply) then stops holding presses, which run on the page shown, as before this change, until the preview is idle again.
- **A drag started while a resize is still saving keeps its animations paused.** The resize's cleanup restarted the paused timelines and cleared the drag's start attributes in the middle of the later drag. A gesture's cleanup now skips an element a newer gesture holds.
- **An edit pins no position on a keyframed tween it did not touch.** Studio's hold (the element sits at its first key before the tween starts) was added to every position-keyframed tween in the file on any edit, which changed the opening frames of tweens nobody edited. It now applies only to tweens the edit touched, or keeps a hold that is already there, the same rule #5045 set for size holds. A clip retime counts the tweens it moved as touched.

### Bench: undo is judged by history groups

The sequence cases counted one saved file version per gesture. A resize writes its size and its position separately, so one gesture looked like two undos, and a lost move could cancel out a split resize and pass. The bench now reads the history ids from Studio's own `/history/claim` and `/history/step` or `/history/undo` replies. Each gesture must open exactly one group (a second claim of the newest group is the same gesture writing again). Each Ctrl+Z must revert the newest group, and each redo the undo it reverses. Bytes still have to match where the bench knows them: every step in a settled case, and the start and end of a fast one. A claim refused with 404 or 409, or an unreadable reply, fails the check rather than counting as nothing.

The property panel test file now loads the panel once instead of re-importing it per test; the first test was paying a cold transform and timing out (separate commit).

## Why

Rule for every Studio edit: an edit never changes frames the user did not touch, a gesture edits the element the user sees, and one gesture is one undo.

## Test plan

- [x] Red-first unit tests, each failing with its fix reverted:
  - an undo that reloads the preview keeps the selection;
  - a reload whose document lost the element drops the selection;
  - an earlier gesture's cleanup leaves a later drag's timelines paused;
  - an edit to one element pins no position on another element's untouched tween (both script writers);
  - a clip retime pins only the tweens it moved;
  - a press during a reload draws the box at the pointer, starts on the reloaded preview and moves its element there, keyed at the time pressed although the playhead moved meanwhile;
  - a drag commit keys the time its press recorded, not the playhead when it commits;
  - a released press survives the browser releasing pointer capture; a hover after release leaves the waiting outline still; a replaying earlier press leaves the newest outline in place.
- [x] Each waiting-press rule above has its own test; "the reload has begun" (`previewReloadBegun`) and "a change a press gave up on" each have one too.
- [x] The bench's group fold has its own test, which fails when the fold counts writes instead of gestures.
- [x] The changed tests pass 3 runs in a row (314 tests, no React `act` warnings). Studio components, hooks, player and utils suites: 7036 pass. Typecheck, oxlint and oxfmt clean over every changed file.
- [x] Edit-accuracy bench on a build of this head, 13 sequence cases, all accurate:

  | Metric | Pass | Worst (px) |
  |---|---|---|
  | tracking | 13/13 | 0.27 |
  | press jump | 13/13 | 0.1 |
  | teleport | 13/13 | 0.24 |
  | drop | 13/13 | 0.3 |
  | reload | 13/13 | 0.3 |
  | render | 13/13 | 0.03 |
  | undo and redo (groups, bytes, box) | 13/13 | 0 |

  Cases: `seqheldtwice-tlhold-px-r0-{root,nested}`, `seqfastkeys-none-px-r0-root`, `seqresizedrag-tween-px-r0-{root,nested}`, `seqresizeundodrag-tween-px-r0-{root,nested}`, `seqplainkeys-none-px-r0-{root,nested}`, `seq{resize,resizeundo,undo,nudgeundo}-none-px-r0-root`, all at z100. On current main the same bench gives `seqheldtwice-tlhold-px-r0-root-z100` a 312 px teleport and `seqfastkeys-none-px-r0-root-z100` a 40.8 px drop and reload error.
  The history check saw real group ids in every case and every undo and redo reverted the expected group. With the fold changed back to counting writes, `seqresizedrag-tween-px-r0-root-z100` fails undo.
- [ ] `seqheldtwice-tlhold-px-r0-root-z100` showed one 59.9 px tracking spike in one frame of its second resize once in about 13 runs on this branch (p95 0.2 px in that run). It did not come back in 10 further runs with per-sample logging, 5 of them recording video. Root cause not found; it may show up in the CI gate.
- [ ] Gesture start with no update pending: not re-measured at this head. Last measured on an earlier commit of this branch, before the waiting-press changes: max 6.8 ms, p95 2.4 ms over 58 presses. Press jump at this head is 0.1 px at most.
- [x] Smoothness (reported, not gated) swings with the box's load in both builds. Alternating main and this branch under the same load on the two worst cases gave dropped frames held box 2 vs 15 and 3 vs 127, plain-to-keys 1 vs 9 and 34 vs 4 (branch vs main): no regression visible above the noise.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Not in this PR

- The `seqplainkeys-*-nested` flake (a 248.4 px snap-back mid-drag or at the next press, with no reload in flight) is not fixed here: an A/B on this branch and main fails at the same rate. It is tracked separately.
- A waiting group press is not marked with `data-dom-edit-press-waiting`, so the bench cannot see it; no bench case covers one yet.
- A waiting press whose element is gone (an undo removed it) is dropped without a notice.
- Cmd+Z takes back a waiting press first, even if a nudge or timeline edit was made after it; redo cannot bring a taken-back press back.
- The 10 s wait limit is shorter than a slow reload's own allowance (15 s, up to three times); past it a press runs on the page shown, as on main.
- Hosts: a host that mounts Studio's canvas also gets the waiting press. `revertNewestStudioPendingEdit` is unchanged, so a host Cmd+Z that calls only it and then steps history undoes the edit before a waiting press, and the press lands after. A host takes the waiting press back first with the new export `cancelNewestStudioWaitingPress()` (true when it took one back); Desktop needs that one line when it moves to this Studio version.

## Review

Independent adversarial review, one pass per head, each finding fixed or listed here:

| Round | Blocking | Should fix | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0 | 5: a queued press replayed on whatever was selected; Cmd+Z during a wait undid the edit before it; a save with no reply held presses forever; scene swaps were not held; blur dropped released drags | All fixed, each with a test that failed first |
| 2 | 0 | 2: undoing a press queued behind one that ran left a dead waiting state; the host revert export would undo twice | Both fixed; the waiting-press cancel is its own export |
| 3 | 0 | 1 cross-repo: a host that steps history after `revertNewestStudioPendingEdit` needs `cancelNewestStudioWaitingPress()` first | Documented above; handed to the Desktop owner for its next Studio bump |
| 4 | 0 | 0 | Three test-hygiene notes left open: two waiting-press tests can cascade into neighbours when they fail before releasing their write, and the Cmd+Z slot is guarded twice so its test only catches both guards breaking |
| 5 | 0 | 0 | Comment-only commit to the repo's comment limits |
| 6 | 0 | 0 | CI gates: the four bench cases this fixes are banked; the waiting-press poll is split into smaller steps with no behaviour change; three doc comments cut for the comment-share rule |
| 7 | 0 | 0 | Round 6's minors: the rule that a waiting press is never a pending edit (a reload waits for those, and the press waits for the reload) is now a test rather than a comment; the new duplication waivers say why they exist |

Two timing-only paths stay untested: the 10 s give-up running a press two frames early, and a press whose element vanished ending at once rather than after 60 frames. Both behaved the same before this PR.

Minor findings fixed along the way: a waiting resize outline grew per side instead of about the centre; the "reload has begun" signal had no test; blur resumed box measuring under a waiting press; formatting.

## Before and After at a glance

Held box, the moment after the second move is dropped (top: main, bottom: this branch). On main the first resize's save repaints the box 312 px back from where it was dropped; here it stays.

![Held box after the drop, main above, this branch below](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fdaa9632-d273-4009-8757-8e3ecfd86716)

Fast Add keyframe, once the move pressed during the reload has settled (top: main, bottom: this branch). On main the new keys override the move and the box lands 40.8 px off; here it lands where it was dropped.

## Before

title: fix(catalog): 3D previews load their scripts under the docs host's script policy
body:
## What

The four 3D-motion catalog previews that loaded their libraries through `blob:` script URLs (Code Slice Hero, Cuboid Carousel, Orbit Card, Frost Sequence Camera Orbit) now run every script as an inline `<script>`. The docs site's policy allows that, so the live player renders the composition instead of its empty base.

## Why

The docs host sends `script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval' https:` and no `blob:`. `scripts/catalog-script-inlining.ts` fetched GSAP and the three.js modules from `/public/catalog/vendor/*.json`, wrapped them in `URL.createObjectURL(new Blob(...))` and loaded those as scripts and as import-map targets. Chrome refuses every one of them ("Loading the script 'blob:…' violates the following Content Security Policy directive"), the bootstrap's promise rejects with a bare `Event`, GSAP never defines `window.gsap`, and the composition stays on its empty base: a white player for Code Slice Hero on both the gallery and its own detail page. Reproduced in Chrome 154 on the deployed `/catalog/blocks/code-slice-hero`.

## Related work

The same policy also refuses `fetch()` of a `data:` URL (`connect-src`), which Glass Shard Title uses for its HDR environment. That is a separate item and a separate fix; it is not in this PR. A failed-state UI for a preview whose scripts fail is also a follow-up.

## How

- Classic scripts (GSAP, frost.js, Code Slice Hero's `shadows.js`/`surface.js`, and each composition script) run through one bootstrap per item. It fetches each vendor JSON and appends the text as an inline `<script>` with a `//# sourceURL=hyperframes-catalog://<item>/<name>`, in order, so an error keeps a real source. This matches the separate `<script>` tags of the original composition more closely than the old indirect `eval`. A failed fetch is logged against the item instead of rejecting silently.
- ES modules cannot run inline without a URL for their imports, so they are bundled to classic scripts with esbuild at generate time:
  - three.js, its `three.core` import and the two addons go into one shared `vendor/three-modules.json`. It defines `globalThis.__hfCatalogModules` keyed by import specifier, and the four raw three.js vendor files it replaces are removed.
  - Each item's entry module and its own modules (`cuboid-motion.js`, `orbit-scene.js`, `orbit-motion.js`) become one classic script per item. Their three.js imports stay external and resolve through that shared bundle via the `require` esbuild emits for an external import.
  - No import map and no module script are left.
- `esbuild` (already in the tree through tsx and the package builds) is declared at the root, because the generator now imports it.
- The four preview payloads and Glass Shard Title (which shares the string encoder) are regenerated with `generate-catalog-payloads.ts --only <item>`, so the fix ships when this merges, without waiting for the standing publish PR. The deployed payloads match main's committed files byte for byte, so the docs site serves `docs/` from main. The next "Publish catalog" run regenerates the same files.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated, in `scripts/catalog-script-inlining.test.ts`:
  - each of the four inlined blocks loads no script from a blob URL;
  - no committed `blocks/` or `components/` payload does either.

  All five fail on main, the generator tests and the committed payloads respectively, and pass here: 14/14, 3 runs. The import-map test is replaced by one that checks each 3D item takes only three.js specifiers from the shared bundle and keeps no import map or module script.
- [x] Script-string encoding regression: closing tags, mixed-case tags, HTML comment markers, and Unicode line separators stay data and round-trip unchanged. The test fails before the fix; all 15 inlining tests pass in three serial runs. Chrome 154 also executes the generated script and parses the following element.
- [x] The four superseded vendor payloads are listed explicitly in the existing deletion guard. Its 8 tests pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: Chrome 154, each payload mounted in a `srcdoc` iframe under a page that sends the docs host's exact CSP.
  - Main: all four fail with the blob CSP refusal and register no timeline.
  - This branch: all four register their timeline with no CSP violation. Code Slice Hero paints its headline, and Cuboid Carousel paints (187 WebGL draws).
  - Without the CSP, Orbit Card and Frost behave the same on main and this branch: headless Chrome has no WebGPU for Frost, and Orbit's frame reads flat in this harness on both.
- [x] `generate-catalog-payloads.test.ts`, `check-docs-catalog`, `tsc` for scripts, format, lint, Fallow (no new findings from these files), the comment ratchet, comment citations and tracked artifacts pass.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

## Before

The live site, Chrome 154 with a mouse (the gallery mounts live players only for a hover-capable pointer), under the deployed CSP. On the gallery, the hovered Code Slice Hero card plays as a blank white player; its detail page plays blank white too.

![before gallery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ebae58ae-1cef-4fef-99ef-7c86e10ca421)

![before detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/709d9e88-2933-41e6-9141-71decc94b5d5)

## After

The same live pages and CSP, with only the `/public/catalog/blocks/*` and `/public/catalog/vendor/*` requests answered from this branch's files: the card plays its headline, the detail page plays to its rear headline, and no CSP refusal is logged.

![after gallery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34ed00c2-33b9-41bb-ace1-e3191810df25)

![after detail](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/585cc0a7-b045-4997-ae16-52a7d4a41243)

title: perf(studio): parse saved HTML once when syncing timeline length
body:
## What changes

Timeline moves and trims parsed the saved HTML twice while synchronizing the composition length. Read the furthest clip end and the root duration from one parsed document, and reuse that result on delete. Saved markup, duration rounding, empty-timeline behavior, and delete rollback remain unchanged.

The optional precomputed duration preserves `null` as a missing root. Zero or invalid content ends return without parsing.

## Validation

At `a0dd85d0` (main merged at `43d07781`):

- Each focused test file ran alone three consecutive times: timeline edit helpers 23 passed, root duration 13, asset drop 34, delete operations 11. Editing integration tests: 61 passed, including rollback after a failed delete save.
- Mutations, each failing with an assertion: passing no precomputed root duration (two parses instead of one), reading the root duration before the zero-content check (four no-op cases parse), treating a missing root like an absent argument (`??`, two parses for a rootless composition), and returning a zero content end on delete (the length readout stays at 6 instead of 4).
- Studio typecheck, changed-file lint and formatting, comment checks, comment ratchet, Fallow audit and the main-deletions guard pass.

## Performance

Built Studio on Linux, the same launch project and one-clip timeline drag as the original measurement, 15 strictly alternating base/head rounds against `43d07781`, each round started only below load 2.5. Each round drags the clip twice: the first edit after load, then the same clip again. Main-thread work is from CPU profiles of the release-to-settle window; a long task is a run of non-idle samples over 8 ms.

| Measurement (median / p90 of 15) | Base, first drag | This PR, first drag | Base, second drag | This PR, second drag |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Total main-thread work after release | 296 / 306 ms | 280 / 295 ms | 253 / 340 ms | 223 / 301 ms |
| Longest task | 65 / 74 ms | 51 / 66 ms | 59 / 68 ms | 37 / 57 ms |
| Time in tasks over 8 ms | 207 / 216 ms | 193 / 222 ms | 175 / 244 ms | 154 / 221 ms |
| Tasks over 8 ms | 7 / 10 | 8 / 10 | 9 / 10 | 8 / 12 |
| HTML parses for duration sync, deterministic witness | 2 | 1 | 2 | 1 |

User-visible work is not worse: the medians and p90s for this PR are at or below base for total work and longest task on both drags. The earlier five-round run showed a single head round with more long-task time; across 15 rounds per side that does not reproduce. The one head round above base's p90 (first drag, round 9: 360 ms total, longest task 101 ms) spent that task in React rendering and live GSAP retiming, which this PR does not touch, and base has outliers of the same size (second drag, round 2: 428 ms total, longest 93 ms). The table does not claim a total-work saving from this change: the parse saving is about 9 ms, and round-to-round spread is larger than that.

## Before

![Before: card 13 after the timeline drop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/59d1a8e5-f200-4e04-9cd3-14d395317453)

## After

Same move on the change (captured at `9350d4ac`; the product code is unchanged since). Card placement and timeline match, and the saved HTML is byte-identical to the parent's.

![After: matching card placement with one duration-sync parse](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c10fc4a3-5ce3-41f8-b87f-e30a46c1576a)

title: fix(catalog): encode module aliases before constructing script code
body:
## What

Route the shared module alias map through the same HTML-safe JSON encoder used for inline script strings. The bundle wrapper previously interpolated plain JSON directly into generated JavaScript, which left two CodeQL improper-code-sanitization findings after #5090.

The existing helper now accepts a string or a string map. It still encodes `<` and Unicode line separators before construction. Current aliases are fixed trusted strings, so this does not claim an attacker-controlled exploit, and generated payloads remain byte-identical.

## Validation

- Red control: the completed JavaScript CodeQL scan of #5090 reports two findings originating at alias-map serialization. The follow-up scan must clear them; neither is dismissed.
- Inlining tests: 15 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on each of three serial Linux runs. Scripts typecheck, lint, and formatting exit 0.
- Regenerating all five affected block payloads and both vendor JSON files preserves every SHA-256 hash.
- An initial isolated-checkout typecheck could not resolve unbuilt workspace dependencies. Validation was repeated successfully in the prepared Linux environment; the tested source SHA-256 equals the committed file.

No player or Studio source changes.
