title: fix(studio): clip strips resize on the next frame, ending ResizeObserver loop errors
body:
## What

Thumbnail strips apply ResizeObserver sizes on the next animation frame instead of committing synchronously inside observer delivery.

`Menu`, `ContextMenu` and `Popover` given `container={null}` now open inline beside their trigger, as the menu prop docs already promised. Before, the trigger reported expanded and no menu appeared.

## Why

`useThumbnailStripSize` called the existing `measure` path directly from ResizeObserver. That path uses `flushSync`, so a strip re-render could invalidate layout while the browser was still delivering measurements, producing ResizeObserver loop errors.

Base UI 1.7's portal reads an explicit `null` container as "not resolved yet" and mounts nothing, so the documented inline meaning never reached it.

## How

- `applyResizesNextFrame` stores the latest size per strip and schedules one frame.
- The frame applies the batch through the existing measurement path.
- A strip that unmounts drops its queued size, so a strip remounted on the same box keeps its own. Releasing the final strip cancels the pending frame.
- Tradeoff: tiles reflect a reported size one frame later.
- One helper in `Menu.tsx` owns the `null` meaning: it renders a `display: contents` host right after the trigger and portals into it. `Menu`, `ContextMenu` and `Popover` all use it, so one prop type means one thing across the three. Any other `container` value, including none, is passed through unchanged.

## Related work

None.

## Test plan

- [x] Each changed test file passed three consecutive individual runs: hook 18 tests, composition thumbnail 10 tests, image thumbnail 8 tests. Every run exited 0 with no skips.
- [x] Deliberately restoring synchronous delivery failed the scheduling assertions. Removing frame cancellation failed the unmount regression.
- [x] Typecheck, lint and formatting passed.
- [x] `Menu.test.tsx` (15 tests) passed three consecutive runs. New cases: a `Menu` and a `ContextMenu` with `container={null}` open inside the trigger's parent, Escape closes, a `Popover` with `container={null}` opens inline on its first render, and a menu with no container still portals to the body. With the old files each inline case fails with `expected null not to be null`.
- [x] At the final head, each changed file passed three consecutive runs alone: hook 19, video thumbnail 17, composition thumbnail 10, image thumbnail 8, menu 15. Restoring the base hook fails the two scheduling tests; removing the queued-size drop fails the remount test with `expected '320x40' to be '300x40'`; the video thumbnail re-tile test now advances a fake frame and fails without it.
- [x] Native Chromium fixture exercised the real `ImageThumbnail` component and ResizeObserver. With the base hook, tiles changed inside 5, 4 and 4 deliveries. With the final hook, zero tiles changed inside delivery in all three runs; nine tiles rendered after resize.
- [x] Independent review and simplification passes completed at the current head.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

The fixture proves the scheduling boundary. It did not reproduce a loop error in either arm, and it does not exercise a full-editor trim gesture. The Before arm uses the base hook with the same consumer and fixture; the After arm uses the final hook.

## Before

Tiles change before the native observer callback returns.

![Synchronous thumbnail resize delivery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd984737-c3ed-4318-9dd5-a08bc1137aec)

## After

Tiles update after delivery, on the next frame.

![Thumbnail resize applied on the next frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a7529b3c-c7cf-4936-9c72-fda270c51509)

## Before (menu)

`container={null}`: the trigger reads expanded, no menu on the page.

![Menu with a null container opens nothing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/10b87a8c-571f-4bf8-b590-8c51113aa541)

## After (menu)

The same fixture: the menu opens inside the trigger's row.

![Menu with a null container opens inline beside its trigger](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/805b7e44-b6df-4a37-8011-cf33457ab80f)

title: feat(fonts): record resolver stage diagnostics on fail-closed font errors
body:
## What

Attach optional structured diagnostics to the per-compile unresolved-font `FontFetchError` (`FONT_FETCH_FAILED`), so callers can identify the resolver stage that failed without parsing the error message. Existing error names, codes, messages, `familyName` and `unresolvedFamilies` remain unchanged.

This change adds observability only; it does not introduce a new font-selection, fallback or retry policy.

## Why

A fail-closed font error identifies the required families that remain unresolved, but not whether the resolver encountered an HTTP rejection, a cached CSS response, no accepted font-face blocks, or a font-asset download failure.

## Related work

The branch incorporates the authored-link fallback from #5186, preserving its control flow, warning and result shape. Both authored and default requests are recorded separately. No linked issue.

## How

- Add typed diagnostic records and a per-compile collector in `packages/core/src/fonts/fontDiagnostics.ts`.
- Record ordered attempts in `deterministicFonts.ts` and attach the snapshot only to a newly constructed unresolved-font error. Shared, cached and retry-exhausted errors are not mutated.
- Record resolver path, authored/default request source, presence of the text parameter, CSS cache disposition, HTTP status, parser counters and font-asset outcome counts. `cssStatus: null` means no HTTP response was recorded for that attempt.
- Record each caller's cache disposition before awaiting the shared CSS lookup, including when an optional lookup joins an in-flight request that later rejects.
- Do not add family names, URLs, CSS, page text or an index into `unresolvedFamilies`. Diagnostic records use resolver order, while unresolved names use sorted order; individual records cannot be associated with names when multiple families fail.
- Leave `FONT_FETCH_UNAVAILABLE` and shared/cached errors without attached diagnostics. A swallowed optional-family failure can still appear in a later per-compile unresolved-font snapshot.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/core/src/fonts/deterministicFonts-diagnostics.test.ts`: 30/30 tests passed locally at `82e204e59`, including authored/default fallback, unchanged error fields, repeated cache hits and a synchronized in-flight rejection case.
- [x] Failing-first control: the synchronized rejection test failed on the pre-fix cache-label implementation. The join was checked before releasing the deferred response.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: no live font-provider or render validation for this change.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

### Validation at the published commit

At `82e204e59`, all 11 required checks passed, including Build, Typecheck, runtime contract, Windows tests/render, regression and the edit-accuracy gate. The runtime test job actually executed the CLI/core/engine tests; the aggregate Test check is a gate, not a separate test run. Local typecheck was not run.

The main CI run [37711021045](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/actions/runs/37711021045) completed with 41 successful jobs, two failed jobs and eight skipped jobs. Skipped jobs were not exercised. The two failures are non-required:
- **Fallow:** three reported unused collector members have production callers; two small test-duplication findings are accepted. No suppression or audit-driven restructuring was added.
- **Studio timeline viewport:** the default arm exceeded its interaction-p95 budget (60.1 ms, then 58.4 ms, against 58.3 ms). Frame timing and run-count checks passed. No rerun was performed for this revision; neither flakiness nor independence from this change is established.

The merge conflict is resolved and the combined revision received fresh review and tests. This PR is ready for review. The results above describe the completed push-triggered checks; subsequent automatic checks must be assessed separately. This validation is not a live failure reproduction or a claim that a production incident is repaired.

— Jerrai

title: feat(registry): eight more WebGPU shader backgrounds and a bundle with thirty new shaders
body:
## What

Eight more 2-second WebGPU background blocks from the MIT [Shaders](https://shaders.com) library, used as they are with their default settings: **Aurora**, **Plasma**, **Voronoi**, **Strands**, **Frost**, **Water**, **Prism** and **Stripes**. They follow #5138's six: tagged `webgpu` and `webgpu-shader`, `data-requires-webgpu`, preview video, no poster.

The shared bundle now holds thirty new shaders, so the next blocks only add their folders and never touch the bundle.

## How

- **One bundle, one list.** `godrays/source/build.mjs` owns the list of shaders; the driver imports it from a module the build generates, so a new shader is one line. The build copies the bundle into every block whose `lib/` already holds it. 1.31 MB to 1.44 MB for 30 more shaders.
- **Same library version.** Still `shaders@4.0.0`; the shader sources are byte-identical in the latest 4.0.2.
- **Licences.** The bundle now opens with a one-line MIT notice for the library. Everything in it still comes from the `shaders` package, so `shaders.THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt` is unchanged.
- **Driver unchanged.** It still renders the exact frame on each seek.

## Verification

- **Seek order, all 36 shaders in the bundle.** t = 1.5 s is pixel-identical when reached from 0, from 1.9 s, or in steps (0, 0.25, 1.0, 1.5). Frames at 1.0 and 1.75 s differ, so every shader moves. Not vacuous: a driver that passes the target time as a delta fails the same check.
- **Old six unchanged.** Godrays, Liquid Metal, Marble, Mesh Gradient, Nebula and Flowing Gradient draw pixel-identical frames at 0, 1 and 2 s with the new bundle and with main's.
- **`hyperframes check`** passes on each new block with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
- **Guard for the stacked blocks.** Two new tests in `registryBlocks.test.ts`: every block that installs a file under `compositions/lib/` ships the same bytes (a stale bundle in one block would overwrite the shared copy for all), and every shader block names a shader its bundle holds. Each fails when one block carries main's old bundle or a misspelled shader name.
- **Build.** It finds shader blocks by their `registry-item.json` and fills a new block's `lib/` with both files. Its guard now throws if either edit to the library's index misses, not only both. A clean `npm ci && node build.mjs` reproduces the committed bundle byte for byte.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and the CLI typecheck pass. Outside the tests, the PR changes only block folders.

- **Previews.** Each is `hyperframes render` of the block on a Metal GPU at 24 fps, then the same web encode as `scripts/generate-catalog-previews.ts` (1280 wide, H.264 CRF 28), which itself skips WebGPU blocks. A rendered frame at 1 s is pixel-identical to the block seeked to 1 s in the browser. Uploaded to the docs CDN under new names only; each URL serves the uploaded bytes.

## Limits

Same as #5138: one shader block per page, and a host without a GPU renders these blocks only with #5133's opt-in. Frost and Water move slowly with their default speeds.

Frames from the uploaded previews at 0.25, 1.0 and 1.75 s:

![Frames from the eight uploaded previews at 0.25, 1.0 and 1.75 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/58dbccb5-33fc-40a9-a975-244c4b6d3d2e)

title: feat(registry): eight more WebGPU shader backgrounds, from blob to fractal noise
body:
## What

Eight more 2-second WebGPU background blocks from the MIT [Shaders](https://shaders.com) library (`shaders@4.0.0`), used with their default settings: **Blob**, **Swirl**, **Lens Flare**, **Waveform**, **Goo**, **Holographic**, **Sine Wave** and **Fractal Noise**.

Stacked on #5191, which adds the shared bundle with all thirty new shaders; this merges after it.

## How

- Each block is the Godrays block with its name and `data-shader` changed: 1920x1080, `data-requires-webgpu`, tags `webgpu` and `webgpu-shader`, license `Apache-2.0 AND MIT`.
- `lib/` is a byte copy of #5191's bundle and third-party license file. This PR does not rebuild or edit the bundle.
- `preview.video` points at the docs CDN; there is no poster. Catalog pages for all thirty come in one docs PR after the four block PRs merge.

## Verification

- **Seek order.** For every block, t = 1.5 s is pixel-identical whether reached from 0, from 1.9 s, or in steps (0, 0.25, 1.0, 1.5). Frames at 1.0 and 1.75 s differ, so the check is not vacuous. The same check flagged Chevron, the original pick for this group, as a still image (its default speed is 0); Sine Wave replaced it.
- **Render matches preview.** The rendered frame at t = 1 s (24 fps, frame 25) is pixel-identical to the browser seeking the block to t = 1 s, for all eight; the frame before it differs.
- **No GPU.** On a GPU-less Linux host with the software WebGPU opt-in (#5133), each block renders the same frames as on Metal (mean difference about 0, largest single pixel 10/255) at 0, 1 and 1.5 s. Each takes 3 to 8 s for 4 frames.
- **Previews** are `hyperframes render` of each block at 24 fps, encoded like the existing six (1280x720, H.264 High). They go to the docs CDN together with the other new blocks' previews.
- **Bundle tests.** #5191's `registryBlocks.test.ts` (every shader block ships the same `lib/` and names a shader in the bundle) passes with these eight, three runs in a row. Renaming one block's shader or changing one byte of one block's bundle each fail it.
- **`hyperframes check`**: 0 errors and 0 warnings on each block.
- **Source-only.** `node scripts/check-catalog-source-pr.mjs` against #5191's branch passes; `oxfmt --check` passes.

## Limits

Same as #5138: one shader block per page, the shader runs on the film's time, and a host without a GPU renders these only with the software WebGPU opt-in.

title: fix(skills): preserve preset color roles in frame contrast checks
body:
## What

Dark brand tokens now pass `build-frame.mjs`'s contrast check for `bold-poster` and `cartesian` in product-launch-video, faceless-explainer, and pr-to-video.

## Why

With a dark canvas and light text, the palette remix produces the correct `frame.md`, but the closing check infers color roles from the remixed luminance order. Presets whose text key is `dark` or `text-primary` fall back to the darkest color, so the check compares the canvas with itself and exits 1.

The issue's palette (`#0a1628`, `#ffffff`, `#ff6b35` with usage statistics) reproduces the failure on current main. `blue-professional` passes with the same tokens because its `text` key is recognized.

## Related work

Fixes #5185.

Checked the issue discussion, timeline, open PR inventory, and searches for the issue number, build-frame, bold-poster, and contrast. No matching active implementation or claim was found. The open preset-font staging PRs #3950 and #3978 touch the builders' font path.

## How

Resolve ink and canvas from the original preset, find their keys, and read those keys from the remixed output for the final contrast check. Apply the same fix to each workflow's standalone builder and regenerate the skill fingerprints.

Add 30 command-level regression cases: dark and light brands, preserved palettes without tokens, and rejection of insufficient ink/canvas contrast across the three workflows. Six dark-brand cases fail before the fix.

## Test plan

- [x] Regression tests added: all 30 pass.
- [x] Manual reproduction: the reported dark palette passes for bold-poster, cartesian, and blue-professional.
- [x] Full CI skills command on Node 22.23.3: 853 passed, 2 skipped; standalone skill import checks: 2 passed.
- [x] `bun run build` and `bun run lint` pass.
- [x] Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt, skill-manifest sync, test reachability, comment checks, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.
- Documentation: no authored instructions change.

Full `bun run test` was also executed on macOS with Node 24.20.0 and Bun 1.4.2. It completed with 41 failures in unchanged package tests, including timeouts, real-media checks, and an HDR fixture that is still a Git LFS pointer in this checkout. Representative shader preview (10 tests), player range (20), and lint source-location (22) suites pass in isolated Node 22 runs. The full package suite is not reported as passing.

title: fix(cli): report snapshot contact sheet failures
body:
## What

When `hyperframes snapshot` cannot load Sharp or generate a contact sheet, it now prints the underlying error and confirms that the individual PNGs are still available.

## Why

The contact-sheet step runs after successful frame capture but silently catches every failure. A blocked libvips DLL therefore produces snapshots without any explanation for the missing sheet.

## Related work

Refs #4845: addresses the CLI diagnostic for contact-sheet failures. Native DLL signing and Windows Smart App Control policy are outside this change.

Checked current issue comments/assignments and open/recent PRs. #3756 touches other snapshot options; #4654 already handles missing Sharp in studio-server. No overlapping diagnostic implementation was found.

## How

Replace the silent catch with a warning using the existing error normalizer. Snapshot capture and the command's successful exit remain intact.

## Test plan

- [x] Three command regressions: Sharp import failure, sheet generation failure, and successful generation without a warning. The two failure tests fail on main.
- [x] Snapshot/contact-sheet suites: **77 passed**.
- [x] CLI build and typecheck; full repository lint and formatting; pre-commit checks including core/Studio/scripts typechecks and fallow; comments, comment ratchet, deletion guard, and test reachability passed.
- [x] Built CLI on macOS with Sharp: exit 0, two PNGs and a contact sheet.
- [x] Built CLI with a Node loader rejecting Sharp: exit 0, two valid PNGs and the original load-error warning. Both PNGs are byte-identical to the successful run.
- [x] No comments added; CONTRIBUTING.md comment checks pass.

The native-load refusal was simulated on macOS; Windows Smart App Control itself was not reproduced. The full workspace test suite was not rerun for this localized diagnostic change.

title: fix(cli): explain hardware GPU screenshot fallback
body:
## What

Linux renders that finish with `screenshot capture · hardware gpu` now receive the existing slower-capture explanation. The hardware hint names BeginFrame probe contention and suggests fewer workers.

## Why

`formatScreenshotFallbackHint` accepts only an automatically selected software GPU. In #4584, hardware-GPU workers miss the BeginFrame probe deadline and finish in screenshot mode, so the completion summary omits the hint. An explicit `--browser-gpu` request also misses it.

## Related work

Refs #4584, its third requested diagnostic. #4585 makes BeginFrame fallback an error on request; this change only adds completion guidance. The probe retry and capture behavior remain separate.

Checked the issue discussion and open/recent PRs; no overlapping hint implementation was found.

## How

Allow the Linux hint for automatically or explicitly selected hardware GPUs after an observed screenshot capture. Preserve the software hint, stay silent for explicit software requests, other platforms, unknown GPU observations, and successful or mixed BeginFrame capture.

## Test plan

- [x] Both hardware-request regression cases fail on main and pass with the fix.
- [x] Formatter and render-command suites: **120 passed**. Covers capture-mode, GPU-request and platform exclusions.
- [x] CLI typecheck and build, repository lint, changed-file formatting, pre-commit gates including fallow and core/Studio/scripts typechecks, branch comments, comment ratchet, deletion guard and test reachability passed.
- [x] Executed the formatter with the report's Linux/hardware/screenshot state and inspected the output.

The GPU contention render itself was not reproduced on this macOS machine. No capture timing, worker selection or renderer behavior changed.

body:
When a clip uses a negative `z-index` without a parent stacking context, an opaque ancestor background can cover it. The paint-order docs currently recommend CSS `z-index` without explaining this case.

Add a before/after CSS example using `isolation: isolate` beside the track-versus-layer guidance, link it from the HTML schema, and explain why the existing `negative_z_index` lint warning also appears on valid isolated layers.

The backdrop changed from background RGB (10,10,10) to authored RGB (245,230,200) in screenshots; encoded pixels stayed within 5 levels of authored RGB across all 10 frames. Both foreground layers remained visible.

title: fix(cli): audit text beneath transparent composition boxes
body:
Visible text marked `data-layout-allow-occlusion` is skipped by the contrast audit when a later transparent composition box wins `elementFromPoint`. On current main, both a direct host and a mounted sub-composition reproduce `check` exiting successfully with zero contrast checks for text whose measured ratio is 1.57:1.

Walk the ordered hit stack through unpainted composition hosts and compiler-produced inner roots, then audit the text when a probe reaches it. Keep the existing behavior for covering paint, generated content, raster/replaced elements, and browsers without `elementsFromPoint`. Paint checks are cached only for the current prepare call.

Refs #5112 ([contrast-audit follow-up](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues/5112#issuecomment-6014806388)). This addresses the audit problem; #5118 changes one registry block, and the font-readiness report remains separate.

Validation:
- Four regressions fail on main; the new 31-case suite and existing layout/contrast suites pass 221 tests.
- Real Chrome prepare/screenshot/finish checks: transparent and nested hosts report the 1.57:1 failure; opaque backgrounds, gradients, shadows, generated content and a deeper opaque cover remain excluded.
- Built CLI `check`: the direct and mounted cases now report three contrast failures across three timestamps. Readable-text controls pass all three checks; a fully opaque cover still passes with no covered-text contrast checks.
- CLI typecheck/build, repository lint, formatting, all applicable pre-commit gates, comment checks and test reachability passed.
- The exemption is deliberately limited to unpainted HTML `div`/`section` composition boxes. This is an audit correction, with no render changes. No claim that all transparent HTML/SVG paint or partial-cover contrast cases are solved.

title: docs: clarify async font measurement and timeline registration
body:
The HTML reference and GSAP adapter say timeline registration must be synchronous, although the runtime supports building after fonts load and registering the completed timeline. Script-created text can also measure against a fallback face before its requested font loads, leaving a persisted width or position wrong.

Document an explicit `document.fonts.load()` setup for measured text, with the requested weight, size, family and character ranges. The example builds the tweens and registers the timeline at the end of the callback. Align the schema and GSAP adapter with that contract, and regenerate the changed skill fingerprint.

Refs #5112. This documents a supported authoring workaround; it does not change the runtime font gate or resolve the entire issue.

Validation:
- Mintlify build validation and broken-link checks passed.
- 21 existing runtime font-gate/late-registration tests and both async-registration lint tests passed.
- Tested the exact documented JavaScript with a local WOFF2 font in Chrome 152. With the font request held, the control registers early and retains a 682.66 px underline for 520.64 px loaded text; the example registers after loading and keeps both widths at 520.64 px across forward and backward seeks.
- Both controls pass `hyperframes lint` and strict `hyperframes check`; the example passes all three contrast samples with no findings.

- Engine typecheck/build, repository lint, changed-file formatting and applicable pre-commit gates passed.
- No capture-mode, seek, compositor timestamp or rendering changes.

title: fix(core): a data script in a sub-composition no longer stops every timeline
body:
## What changes for the user

A sub-composition that carries a data block, such as `<script type="application/json" id="meta">{"title": "x"}</script>`, no longer freezes the film. Before, every scene's timeline stayed static (including scenes without the data block) and `hyperframes check` reported `page_error: Failed to execute 'replaceWith' on 'Element': Unexpected token ':'`. Now the data block stays in the DOM as written and readable with `document.getElementById("meta")`, and every timeline plays.

## Root cause

`planCompositionAssembly` (the one place both the compiler and the runtime loader decide a composition's scripts) listed every `<script>` regardless of `type`. The compiler then wrapped the JSON as a JavaScript IIFE, and the bundler merges all composition scripts (root and every sub-composition) into one `<script>`, so that single parse error stopped all of them.

## Fix

- `compositionAssembly.ts`: only scripts the browser runs (the HTML spec's JavaScript MIME types, `module`, `importmap`) are extracted. `extractedCompositionAssets()` replaces the selector at the three places that strip extracted assets from the mounted copy, so a data block stays in the content. The JavaScript MIME list moves here because this module must import nothing (it ships in the runtime bundle); `scriptRuns.ts` imports `isJavaScriptType` from it, and the compiler's public export of it now points here. `nomodule` only stops classic scripts, so `type="module" nomodule` still runs, as it does in browsers.
- `htmlBundler.ts`: a script run whose joined text does not parse is no longer merged. Each script stays its own `<script>`, so a broken script fails alone, the way separate authored scripts do in the browser. The check parses the text with acorn in script mode (`core` now declares `acorn`, already locked at the version `parsers` and `lint` use). So a top-level `return`, `new.target`, `export` or top-level `await` counts as not parsing, as it does in a `<script>`. Using a parser rather than the host engine makes the answer the same everywhere. `new Function` accepts `return`, and Bun 1.3's `vm.Script` compiles lazily and accepts any text, which would have merged a broken script again in the Bun-hosted Studio dev server. Chrome reports an inline script's SyntaxError without throwing from `replaceWith`, so the runtime's after-fonts loop keeps running the rest.
- The render path (`producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`) had its own copy of that merge with the same gap. Both now use one check, `parsesAsScript`, exported from the core compiler. Behaviour change on that path: the producer used to skip the whole merge on a page with no `<head>`; it now merges adjacent body scripts there too, under the same parse check, matching the bundler.
- Inline `<template id="X-template">` compositions in `index.html` (bundler only): the root now comes from `planCompositionAssembly`, and data scripts written beside the root are mounted next to it, the same as the `data-composition-src` path and the runtime loader.
- Escaping: a run left unmerged, and every scene-part script in `sceneParts` preview, now goes through the same comment strip and `</script>` escaping as merged runs. Scene-part scripts were never escaped on `main`, so a sub-composition script holding `"</script>"` in a string ended the script early in Studio preview.

No authoring format changes. Lint has nothing to flag: the data block is valid.

## Proof

- New tests: six in `htmlBundler.test.ts` (data block kept and readable, every runnable script parses, all three timelines' scripts survive; a sub-composition script that does not parse stays apart, with and without `sceneParts`; a script it does not merge is still escaped, including scene parts), one in `compositionLoader.test.ts` (runtime mount keeps the data block and does not inject it) and three in the producer's `htmlCompiler.scriptOrder.test.ts` (the same two cases on the render path, and body scripts merged on a page with no `<head>`). After review: a sub-composition script file with a top-level `return` stays apart (with and without `sceneParts`); a data script beside an inline template's root stays mounted; `compositionAssembly.test.ts` gains the `nomodule` rows. `parsesAsScript` is also tested directly against an obvious syntax error, a top-level `return` and `export`. That fails on any host where the check accepts garbage, and the test's own parse oracle is acorn too, so it does not depend on the engine. Each guard was undone on its own (per-run split, merge guard, producer guard, each escape) and only its own tests went red.
- Non-vacuity, re-run after rebasing on main: with `isExecutableScript` forced to `true` (every script extracted, the old behaviour), 6 tests fail across `htmlBundler.test.ts` and `compositionLoader.test.ts`, among them "keeps a sub-composition's JSON data script readable and out of the JavaScript" (`expected undefined to be 'meta'`) and "leaves a JSON data script in the mounted content instead of running it". With the merge guard in `coalesceHeadStylesAndBodyScripts` disabled, 2 fail: "keeps a sub-composition script that does not parse apart, so the others still run". With `parsesAsScript` back on `new Function`, only the two top-level `return` cases fail. With it on `vm.Script` under Bun 1.3.14, 9 fail: the three direct checks and all six "does not parse apart" cases. Under Node the same swap stays green, which is the engine dependence this removes. With the check accepting everything, the same 9 fail under both Node and Bun. With the template path's inert-script mount removed, only "mounts a JSON data script authored beside the root of an inline template composition" fails. With `nomodule` checked before `module`, only the `type="module" nomodule` row fails. Restoring the code makes all of them pass.
- At the current head: core `htmlBundler`, `compositionAssembly`, `inlineSubCompositions`, `scriptRuns` and `compositionLoader` pass 320 of 320, and producer `htmlCompiler.scriptOrder` passes 7 of 7. Both pass three runs in a row.
- Before the rebase, the wider set of related files passed three runs in a row: core `htmlBundler` 157, `compositionAssembly` 17, `inlineSubCompositions` 39, `scriptRuns` 12, `htmlParityContract` 2, `compositionLoader` 67, `init.swapScenes` 140, `entry.afterFonts` 11; producer `htmlCompiler.scriptOrder` 7, `parity` 13, `moduleScripts` 1, `mediaType` 3, `fontEmbed` 5, `htmlCompiler.test.ts` 140 (bun). `tsc` clean in core and producer.
- Two repro projects that differ by that one line: `check` on the data-block project goes from `ok=false` to `ok=true`. Snapshots at 1s, 2.5s and 3.5s are now pixel-identical to the project without it, and both scenes move.

### Before
![before: every scene static at x=0](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7fbaff72-61d3-4ffd-9341-9f3582e7cae2)

### After
![after: intro and scene animate](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/08fd6b42-b60a-4f06-88b7-1a44af96e33c)

title: fix(studio): let small picks move when dragged by their middle
body:
## What changed

On a very small selection (a few screen pixels across, e.g. a dot or thin line seen at the preview's fit scale), the four corner resize hit areas (16 px squares centred on the corners) overlapped and covered the whole element. Dragging the middle grabbed a corner handle and resized the element instead of moving it.

Each corner hit area now slides outward on a small pick so it reaches at most a quarter of each side into the element. The middle stays free for moving. Picks 32 px and larger on a side are unchanged: the handles stay centred on the corners. This follows the crop handles, which already sit just outside the box so the body stays free for moving.

A resize now measures from the corner the handle stands for, not from where the press landed. Before, the size followed the pointer's distance from the centre divided by that distance at press. A press beside the corner therefore made the corner lag the cursor: slightly for any off-corner press, and by up to 1.7 px over a drag once the handles slide outward on picks under 32 px. The handle now reports its corner on press, and the resize carries the press-to-corner offset, so the grabbed corner stays under the cursor wherever the handle is pressed. The same corner is used when a press lands while the preview reloads.

On very short picks the bottom hit areas can overlap the top few pixels of the rotate button; the rest of the button still rotates.

## Validation

- Chrome tests render 14x8, 4x4, 24x24 and a cropped 40x40 (16x16 visible) pick and check that each corner hit area reaches at most a quarter of each side into the pick and that each handle's corner marker sits exactly on the pick's corner; a 32x40 pick keeps its handles centred on the corners. All four small rows fail when the slide is removed.
- A gesture test presses 6 px beside the corner and drags 50 px outward: the box grows exactly as if the corner moved 50 px (300 wide). Without the corner offset it comes out at 294.
- Resize test files three consecutive green runs; Studio suite 7791 passed. Format, lint, type check and comment checks pass.
- Real Studio, headless Chromium, a 30x20 element in a 1920x1080 composition (about 12x8 screen pixels), dragged from its centre by 60x40 screen pixels:
  - Before: the drag commits a resize (box-size markers written, no move).
  - After: the drag moves the element (translate 155x104 composition pixels, the 60x40 drag at the preview scale). Rechecked with the corner-based resize in place: same handles, same move.

## Before

Picked, then dragged from the middle: the handles cover the element and it does not move.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79af2c94-692b-4b6a-a500-48a96e6139aa)

## After

The middle stays visible between the handles and the same drag moves the element.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c6b4c6af-4b77-4e91-8f66-edf1ba971378)

title: fix(cli): recognize ancestor gradient text masks
body:
When a heading uses `background-clip: text` and its words or lines are wrapped in child elements, `check` reports `text_not_painted` even though Chrome 150+ paints their glyphs. Recognize an ancestor's clipped gradient or solid background, match the painted background layer, and compare individual text fragments in layout coordinates because Chromium's mask ignores descendant transforms.

Keep the finding for Chrome builds below 150 and unknown browsers, transparent or missing gradients, unmatched background layers, SVG text, and glyphs outside the mask. Ancestor images with unknown transparency remain conservative. Refs #5117 for the CLI audit follow-up; the Cloud Run browser pin remains a separate issue.

Validation:
- 249 related tests passed on Node 22, including Chromium 152 screenshot comparisons; all 32 Chromium tests also passed on Chrome 148 and 150.

title: fix(parsers): respect quoted composition source attributes
body:
The shared sub-composition scanner stops at `>` inside a quoted attribute and can treat `data-composition-src` text inside another attribute as a real mount. This makes project lint miss real missing compositions and makes catalog usage report examples as mounted blocks.

Read tag boundaries outside quotes, then consume complete attributes with matching quote delimiters. Preserve source order, deduplication, template traversal, placeholder/remote filtering, and the linear scan of large truncated input. This also handles apostrophes, unquoted values, case-insensitive attribute names, and first-value semantics for duplicate attributes.

Validation:
- 1,241 parser tests passed (4 skipped, 3 todo); 90 project-lint/helper tests and 89 CLI lint/catalog tests passed.
- Eleven new regression cases fail on main. Forty-eight quoted-attribute combinations agree with the HTML parser used by rendering.
- Built CLI lint now reports the missing composition after `title="Sales > costs"`; a metadata-only source example passes strict lint/check instead of producing a phantom missing-file error.
- Parsers/lint/CLI builds and typechecks, repository lint, formatting, pre-commit hooks, comment checks, deletion guard, and test reachability passed.

The fix is limited to the shared composition-source scanner; other lint rules that read raw attributes remain separate.

title: fix(lint): read attribute values with the HTML parser
body:
When a quoted title contains `id="ghost"`, `data-start="0"`, or `data-composition-src="ghost.html"`, lint's regex attribute reader treats that text as real markup. This invents host/timing errors and can suppress the genuine missing-media-ID error.

Read raw and decoded values through the existing HTML parser, selecting character-reference decoding per caller. Raw reads keep entity text and the empty-as-absent contract; decoded reads retain Boolean attribute semantics. Actual values with opposite quotes or unquoted HTML values are read completely, and the first duplicate attribute wins.

Related investigation: closed/unmerged #2802 addressed this reader with unconditional decoded reads. This change keeps the raw/decoded distinction and verifies current source and callers. #4396 already fixes Boolean attribute-name detection; this fixes value reads.

Validation:
- All 849 lint tests and 77 CLI project-lint tests passed; eleven new cases fail on main.
- Lint findings are identical across 214 shipped example/block compositions.
- Built CLI now reports the missing real video ID; a title-only example passes strict lint/check, and a correct unquoted clip passes lint.
- Lint/CLI builds and typechecks, repository lint, formatting, pre-commit hooks, comment checks, deletion guard, and test reachability passed.

Valid unquoted attributes now participate in lint rules, so real violations in unquoted markup can newly be reported.

title: fix(lint): detect optional managed media calls
body:
Optional chaining currently bypasses `imperative_media_control`: `video?.play()`, `video.play?.()`, and optional calls on direct DOM lookups pass lint even though HyperFrames must own managed-media playback. The same rule also reports ordinary calls printed inside strings, comments, templates, or regular expressions.

Extend the existing play/pause matchers to optional property access and optional calls. Use the existing JavaScript code mask to check that bindings and controls begin in executable code, retaining real calls inside template interpolations. Existing finding messages, snippets for ordinary calls, and media IDs are preserved.

No new dependency or runtime playback change.

title: fix(slideshow): validate nested hotspot entries
body:
A parseable slideshow island containing `"hotspots": [null]` currently passes the manifest guard and crashes `hyperframes lint` with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'target')`. Other malformed entries can survive resolution and be classified as ready by the player.

Validate each hotspot in the shared parser: require an object with string `id`, `label`, and `target`, and validate the four finite numeric coordinates when a region is present. Both main-line and branch slides use the guard. This lets lint report its existing `slideshow_invalid` finding and the player classify the existing malformed-island state before initialization.

title: fix(studio): a resized corner stays on the pointer when the size rounds to whole pixels
body:
## What

During a corner resize, the grabbed corner now stays on the pointer when the element's size rounds to whole pixels. The written width and height stay whole, as before.

## Why

Studio writes resized sizes in whole CSS pixels (#4766): GSAP works out a `-50%` centring from the element's integer offset size, and a fractional size once saved a centred element 113 px off. A corner resize keeps the element's centre planted, so rounding the size moved the grabbed corner off the pointer by up to about 0.35 px times the element's rendered scale.

On a layer that GSAP scales to 1.5x, that is up to 0.53 px. The edit accuracy bench's two remaining misses, `resize-scale-px-r30-root-z50-after` (0.53) and `resize-scale-px-r30-nested-z50-after` (0.52), are exactly this.

## Related work

Refs #4766 (whole-pixel sizes stay).

## How

- `resizeRemainderShift` (`domEditResizeLocal.ts`): the shift of the pinned centre that puts the grabbed corner where the wanted size would. It is half the rounding remainder, measured along the element's own rendered edges, so rotation and GSAP scale are included. Which local corner is grabbed comes from geometry: the grabbed handle's corner on screen, relative to the centre, expressed in the element's two rendered edges. A mirrored layer (whose `se` handle sits on its local `sw` corner), a layer inside a rotated parent, and a skewed box (a rotated layer inside an unevenly scaled parent) all get the right side.
- The resize draft (`resizeDraft.ts`) pins the centre at its gesture-start point plus that shift. The release already commits the draft's anchor as the offset, so the saved file matches what the drag showed.
- `applyStudioBoxSizeDraft` returns the size it wrote. `manualEditsDom.ts` rounds once (`roundToLayoutSize` in `utils/rounding.ts`) and every write in it, flex-basis included, uses that one value.
- On a GSAP-scaled layer the resize saves as a new scale, and `finalizeScaleResizeCommit` then moves the box onto the drop point, lining up centres (the resize is centre-anchored, so a scale that cannot reproduce separately rounded width and height splits the gap evenly).
  - Static position (a `gsap.set` hold, or no position animation): the correction is written whenever it is not zero at the file's 3-decimal precision. A layer with no position animation therefore gains a `gsap.set` x/y hold holding that sub-pixel correction. This is what puts the saved box on the drop point.
  - Animated position: the 0.5 px tolerance stays, as on main. A sub-pixel correction is not worth adding a keyframe to, stretching, or refusing an authored tween, so the live box is left at its tween position and nothing is written.

Trade-off: the grabbed corner is exact, so the centre moves by half the rounding remainder and the opposite corner by the full remainder (under 0.7 px times the scale) instead.

Decision on the position hold (asked in review): kept. On the scale route the file then matches what the drag showed exactly, later drags rewrite the same hold in place, and one undo restores the file byte for byte. The alternative, feeding the unrounded size into the scale, would also need the finalize step to stop measuring against the shifted draft centre; that is a larger change to the scale route than this fix, and it can follow on its own if the extra `gsap.set` line proves noisy.

## Before

![Before: the layer corner sits 0.21 composition px off the pointer mid-drag](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5bd0d707-019b-4e69-90ee-06e009e6556f)

## After

![After: the layer corner sits on the pointer, 0.02 composition px](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/66d8b3ca-d400-4e1b-8bab-00f2080d02f9)

Both captures come from the edit accuracy bench's own fixture (the `scale` / 30 deg / root case at 200% zoom), driven headless in the built Studio from main and from this branch, 400x crop of the grabbed corner while the button is still held.

## Test plan

- [x] `anchoredResizeCommitFeedsOffset.test.ts`: a drag that asks for 300.6 x 150.3 writes 301 x 150 and commits the grabbed corner exactly where 300.6 x 150.3 puts it. Fails without the fix.
- [x] `domEditResizeLocal.test.ts`: on a 30 deg, 1.5x box each corner lands on its wanted position, on mirrored or further-turned boxes (150, 180, -120, 90 deg) and on a skewed 10 x 200 bar the grabbed corner lands where the wanted size puts it. The mirrored rows fail with signs taken from the handle name, the skewed rows fail with projected signs.
- [x] `gsapResizeIntercept.test.ts`: a scale resize leaves a static position alone when the drop is centred on the committed box, moves it by exactly 0.3 / -0.2 px when the drop sits that far off, writes nothing for a 0.0003 px drop (below the file's 3-decimal precision), and writes nothing into an animated position tween for a sub-pixel drop. The last two rows fail with a `< 1e-6` check and without the tolerance, respectively.
- [x] Studio `components/editor`, `hooks` and `utils` suites: 371 files, 4364 tests passed at the previous head; the three changed test files pass 3 runs in a row at this head. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet clean.
- [x] Edit accuracy gate: both target cases newly pass; no case lost accuracy. `baseline.json` banks only those two lines, copied byte for byte from the gate artifact; the gate replayed locally with `ratchet.mjs` passes.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Size

10 files, about +150 / -40 of source and tests, plus 2 banked lines in `baseline.json`.

title: fix(cli): validate cached versions in update metadata
body:
A malformed cached `latestVersion` currently reaches JSON `_meta` and can make `updateAvailable` true. For example, `"not-a-version"` and `["999.0.0"]` are advertised as updates even though the background cached-result path rejects invalid versions.

Share a type-checked cache reader between the fallback result and metadata. Invalid cached values are omitted from JSON metadata and no longer trigger update notices; valid versions retain the existing comparison and output.

Validation:
- 11 new cases cover invalid cache values, valid releases/prereleases, JSON serialization, and the update notice. Seven cases fail on main.
- 197 CLI tests pass across update checks, background updates, installer detection, project pins, and lint output.

The check reads the cache without starting a network request or rewriting settings.

title: feat(cli): let transcribe --to write srt or vtt straight from a media file
body:
## What changed

`hyperframes transcribe video.mp4 --to srt` used to stop with "--to can only export from transcript files. Run transcribe first.", so getting captions from a recording took two commands. Now `--to srt` or `--to vtt` on an audio or video file transcribes it and writes the sidecar in the same run, next to `transcript.json` (or at `--output`).

- Transcripts keep working as before: `--to` on a `.json`, `.srt` or `.vtt` still exports instead of importing, with the same cue rules.
- Both paths share one sidecar writer, so cue grouping, `--preserve-cues` and `--output` behave the same.
- Under `--json` the run still prints one result line; it gains `format` and `outputPath` when a sidecar was written.
- A bad `--output` fails at once, before any decoding, so a typo does not cost a long transcription. That covers a missing folder ("Output folder not found") and an `--output` that is a folder or ends in a slash ("--output is a folder", naming a file path to use instead). A caption path that would land on the input file or on the `transcript.json` the run writes is refused too ("The caption file would overwrite ..."). The check compares files, not path text: right before the caption write, by when the transcript exists, a destination that is the same file as the input or `transcript.json` is refused, so the operating system resolves every link, relative link, folder alias (`/var` and `/private/var`) and letter case. An early check refuses the common cases before transcribing. When a disk reports inode 0 (some network shares), existing files are compared by their fully resolved paths instead, so links are still caught and two different files are never called the same. It also covers the default path, so `transcribe transcript.srt --to srt` no longer rewrites its own input. A trailing `-o` with no path fails ("--output needs a file path").
- If the caption file cannot be written after transcribing, the run exits 1 and says so: "Transcript saved to ..., but the caption file ... could not be written: <reason>", instead of reporting a failed transcription.
- Transcribed words are treated as word-level when grouping cues, rather than guessed from spacing. For Chinese or Japanese this gives readable caption lines instead of one cue per recognised word. Exporting the saved `transcript.json` later still guesses from spacing, so it may split those cues differently; the docs say so.
- Audio with no speech succeeds with 0 words as before, and with `--to` writes an empty sidecar (an empty SRT, a header-only VTT). Exporting an empty transcript file still fails with "No words found".
- With `--optional`, a run skipped because whisper-cpp is unavailable writes no sidecar and exits 0. Before, `--to` on media always failed with exit 1.
- The CLI docs and `--help` examples show the new form.

## Validation

- New tests: a media file with `--to vtt --json` writes `transcript.json`, a VTT that matches the formatter's output, and exactly one stdout result naming both; a missing `--output` folder fails before transcription starts; silent audio with `--to srt` writes an empty sidecar. The first two fail on the previous code. New tests also cover an `--output` that is a folder, ends in a slash or sits under a file, an `--output` that names the input or `transcript.json` directly, through a link, through a linked folder, by its real path or in other letter case, an export whose default path is its own input, a trailing `-o`, a caption file that cannot be written after transcribing, and CJK grouping. Each new test fails when its fix is removed. Links to the transcript the run is about to create (direct, and relative inside a linked folder) keep the transcript and report that the caption file could not be written. All 63 transcribe tests pass three runs in a row. On macOS, the built-from-source CLI refuses each alias (case variant, `/private` path, link, trailing `-o`, export onto its own input) and leaves the files untouched.
- End to end with the built CLI and the real Parakeet engine on a 3.5 s generated speech clip: `transcribe hello.wav --to srt --json` exits 0, prints one result line, and writes three correct cues ("Write HTML.", "Render video.", "Built for agents.").
- `transcript.json` is named by one constant, used by both engines, the import, init and the check.
- Format, lint, type check and comment checks pass.

## No visible change

CLI only; no Studio or player code changes.

title: fix(cli): reject inherited motion assertion kinds
body:
Motion sidecars can currently resolve assertion kinds through `Object.prototype`. `"__proto__"` throws `validator is not a function`, while `"constructor"` is accepted as valid and fails later during the browser check, skipping the layout/contrast audits.

Require an own validator-table property before dispatch. These names now produce the existing indexed unknown-kind validation error, so `check` reports `motion_spec_invalid` and continues its other browser audits.

Validation:
- Six parser/file-reader regressions fail on main and pass with the fix.
- Motion spec, motion audit, and check command suites: 107 passed.
- Built CLI reproduces both failures. With the fix, each invalid sidecar returns one structured motion error while runtime/layout pass and all five contrast samples run and pass.
- Valid sidecar passes strict lint/check, evaluates 21 motion samples, and passes all five contrast samples.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint/format, pre-commit gates, comment checks, deletion guard, and test reachability pass.

title: fix(slideshow): preserve sequence keys during resolution and navigation
body:
Slideshow sequence lookup currently treats inherited object properties as branches. An undeclared `constructor`/ `__proto__` / `toString` hotspot can throw during resolution or navigation; a declared `__proto__` sequence is lost during serialization and phantom-slide filtering, and clicking its hotspot throws in the built browser bundle.

Resolve targets through a map, preserve sequence records with `Object.fromEntries`, and restrict controller lookup to own properties. Declared branches survive parsing, filtering, and navigation; unknown targets return the existing manifest diagnostic or leave navigation unchanged.

Validation:
- Six parser and four player regressions failed before the fix. Full parser suite: 1,238 passed, 4 skipped, 3 todo; slideshow suites: 154 passed.
- Full lint suite: 834 passed; CLI lint/check/update suites: 177 passed. Lint findings remain identical for all 214 shipped compositions.
- Built Chromium bundle reproduces the hotspot click error on main. With the fix it enters the branch at 11.5s and Previous restores the parent slide at 2.5s with no browser errors.
- Built CLI returns one `slideshow_unresolved_ref` for each undeclared target; a declared branch passes lint and strict check, including runtime, nine layout samples, and all five contrast samples.
- Parser, player, lint, and CLI builds; parser/player type checks; repository lint/format; pre-commit gates; comment checks; deletion guard; test reachability.

title: fix(parsers): recognize computed variable usage reads
body:
Studio's variable usage report misses reads through `window.__hyperframes["getVariables"]()` and can confidently label those declarations unused. It also skips a values alias used as the computed key of another object, leaving `scanIncomplete` false despite the value escaping.

Recognize a literal `"getVariables"` member name and skip property-position identifiers only for noncomputed members. Bracket getter reads now cross-reference declared and undeclared ids like dot calls; computed-key escapes mark the existing report incomplete.

Validation:
- Six scanner and two SDK regressions fail on main; two additional controls preserve ordinary property-name handling.
- Full parser suite: 1,240 passed, 4 skipped, 3 todo. Full SDK suite: 593 passed.
- Built SDK browser bundle verifies bracket/dot report equality, alias reads, and dynamic-access degradation in Chromium with no browser errors.
- Parser/SDK builds and type checks, repository lint/format, pre-commit gates, comment checks, deletion guard, and test reachability pass.

title: fix(sdk): preserve fragments with inert document markers
body:
A bare HTML fragment mentioning `<html>` or `<!doctype html>` in a comment, attribute, or script is currently mistaken for a full document. ID stamping injects empty `head`/`body` elements into the fragment, and the SDK returns an empty editable tree. The built `timeline ids` command also writes this malformed result without stamping the clip.

Anchor ID stamping's document test after leading comments. Use the existing compiler document parser in both SDK model paths, so fragment detection and serialization agree. Fragments now retain editable elements and survive editing/reopening; full documents keep their existing shell.

Validation:
- Four ID-stamping and three SDK regression cases fail on main; a full-document control remains valid.
- Full parser suite: 1,237 passed, 4 skipped, 3 todo. Full SDK suite: 594 passed. Compiler HTML-document suite: 55 passed. CLI ID/timeline suites: 40 passed.
- Built Chromium SDK bundles reproduce empty trees on main and verify element lookup, text edits, fragment serialization, and reopening with the fix. The full-document control serializes identically.
- Built CLI reproduces the malformed write and verifies correct stable IDs, preserved fragment content, and idempotence with the fix.
- A full project containing the affected nested scene passes lint and strict check, including runtime/layout and all five contrast samples.
- Lint findings remain identical for all 214 shipped compositions.
- Parser, SDK, lint, and CLI builds; parser/SDK types; repository lint/format; pre-commit gates; comment checks; deletion guard; test reachability pass.

title: fix(lint): parse inline script type and source attributes
body:
The inline-script syntax rule currently reads `type` and `src` with regexes. Valid unquoted or mixed-case module/importmap/JSON types receive classic-JavaScript syntax errors, while `data-src`, `data-type`, or quoted metadata mentioning those attributes can suppress a real error.

Read the actual decoded attributes with the existing HTML parser and normalize the type before applying the same four exemptions. Classic scripts with metadata are checked; true external scripts and exempt types keep their existing treatment, including first-attribute semantics.

Validation:
- 15 fail-first cases; 18 total regression/control cases cover unquoted/mixed-case/encoded types, duplicate attributes, metadata, and real external attributes.
- Full lint suite: 852 passed. CLI lint/check suites: 149 passed. Lint findings remain identical for all 214 shipped compositions.
- Built CLI verifies four formerly rejected valid fixtures, three formerly missed syntax errors, and the unchanged classic control.
- Native Chromium executes the unquoted module and reads the JSON data block without errors. The module composition passes strict check, runtime/layout, and all five contrast samples.
- Parser/lint/CLI builds, lint typecheck, repository lint/format, pre-commit gates, comment checks, deletion guard, and test reachability pass.

title: fix(lint): read actual font CSS declarations
body:
The font rules scan raw CSS for `font-family`, so unused custom properties and `content` strings can cause false missing-font errors. Quoted fake font-face declarations can also hide real missing fonts. Font tokens that are referenced by `font-family: var(--font-family)` must still be checked.

Read actual font declarations and descriptors through PostCSS. Resolve references against custom properties declared in the supplied styles, following bounded alias chains and keeping custom-property names case sensitive. Ignore unused tokens, unresolved variables, and cycles. Reuse the resolution for distributed alias warnings and locate missing-font diagnostics at the declaration that uses the token. This is static token resolution; it does not evaluate the full CSS cascade.

Validation:
- The original declaration-boundary regressions reproduce on main. Eight referenced-token checks fail on the earlier PR revision; all 55 font-rule cases and 856 lint tests pass with the revision.
- All 103 CLI lint/check/validate tests pass.
- Eleven probes compare source and built linter results, built CLI diagnostics, and real Chrome computed font families. Missing-font references, alias chains, case-sensitive names, declared faces, unused tokens, cycles, and unresolved references give the expected results with no browser errors.
- Lint and CLI builds, lint typecheck, repository lint, formatting, reachability, comment checks, and full pre-commit checks pass. Fallow finds no new issues in the two changed files.

Windows CI passes on current head `6254873`: [the current Windows run](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/actions/runs/37850997731/job/113568214912) succeeds in all four lanes, including studio-1. The earlier Puppeteer installation failure is superseded. All current checks pass or are intentionally skipped.

title: fix(cli): normalize the audio passage the clip plays
body:
On an audio or audible video clip with `data-playback-start`, `normalize-audio` measures `data-media-start` (or zero) instead of the passage playback uses. On an 8s tone with a quiet intro and louder tail, a 2s clip starting at 4s gets a +7.6dB boost instead of the required −6.4dB reduction. A preferred offset of zero is also incorrectly overridden by the legacy attribute.

Use the existing playback offset reader for the shared loudness HTML scan: `data-playback-start` takes precedence, with invalid values falling back to `data-media-start`. Preserve validation of a legacy offset when selected and preserve source attributes when writing the gain.

Validation on current main:
- Six regressions fail before the fix; all 1,239 Studio-server tests and 26 CLI normalization tests pass.
- The rebuilt CLI and real FFmpeg select the correct passage for preferred-only, conflicting, zero, legacy, and invalid-preferred controls, including existing filename handling.
- Full workspace build, Studio-server build/typecheck, CLI build, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, commit hooks, and branch comment checks pass.

Original rendering validation: persisted compositions pass lint and strict browser check. Preferred-offset and equivalent legacy-offset SDR renders contain 10 frames over 2s with matching audio measurements. Each channel is −16.1 LUFS; the existing unity mono-to-stereo upmix measures −13.1 LUFS across both channels. Repeat `--write` is byte-stable, and reference matching preserves its reference.

title: fix(cli): preserve subtitle cues across line endings
body:
Importing an SRT or WebVTT file with Windows CRLF line endings merges every cue into the first entry: the next cue's index and timing line become caption text, and its timing is lost. CR-only files import no cues.

Normalize CRLF and CR to LF before scanning SRT cue boundaries or stripping WebVTT headers. This preserves the existing cue text, stable IDs and timestamps across newline forms.

Validation:
- Five fail-first regression tests cover both formats, multiline/tagged text, round-trip export and mixed newline forms.
- All 219 transcription/Whisper tests pass (one existing skip), using a canonical macOS temporary path to avoid unrelated `/var` versus `/private/var` path assertions.
- Built CLI imports the same two cues from six LF/CRLF/CR fixtures and exports identical SRT sidecars. Both CRLF formats also patch the two correct entries into caption source, stay byte-stable on repeat import, and export the expected WebVTT.
- Native Chromium's text-track parser reads the same WebVTT cues and timestamps for all three newline forms.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, commit hooks and comment checks pass.

title: fix(cli): retain WebVTT timestamps before cue settings
body:
Importing WebVTT cues with settings such as `align:start` or `line:90%` replaces their end timestamp with zero. For example, `00:01.000 --> 00:03.500 align:start` becomes `{ start: 1, end: 0 }` and exports an SRT cue ending before it starts.

Read the timestamp token before the whitespace-separated cue settings. Keep both supported timestamp forms and the existing plain-timestamp behavior.

Validation:
- Five fail-first tests cover full/short timestamps, alignment, multiple settings, tabs, region references and SRT export.
- All 219 transcription/Whisper tests pass (one existing skip) with a canonical macOS temporary path.
- Built CLI imports and exports correct 3.5 s end times across four settings fixtures and two plain controls. The input bytes are preserved.
- Native Chromium's text-track parser reports the same cue text and times for all six fixtures.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, commit hooks and comment checks pass.

title: fix(cli): reject non-object project config roots
body:
A `hyperframes.json` containing an array, string, number or boolean is currently reported as a valid default config. Rendering consequently reports zero catalog items instead of the existing unreadable-manifest signal.

Require an object root before normalizing the parsed JSON, using the existing object guard. Partial object configs retain their defaults, unreadable configs retain the existing command fallback, and the file is never rewritten.

Validation:
- Seven fail-first cases prove incorrect read status and catalog reporting; null, corrupt, missing and partial-object controls retain their behavior.
- All 260 related config, schema, catalog, add, render-plan and telemetry tests pass.
- The built config reader correctly handles ten real on-disk fixtures and preserves their bytes.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, commit hooks and comment checks pass.

title: fix(cli): preserve caption text inside script blocks
body:
Importing caption text containing `</script>` through `hyperframes transcribe` can close the destination script and turn part of the caption into HTML. Replacement-string sequences such as `$&` and `$$` also change the text or word IDs during insertion.

Escape `<` after JSON serialization and insert the serialized data through a replacement callback. This applies Studio's existing script-data convention to the CLI patcher and preserves literal caption text, IDs and timing for both supported variable names.

Validation:
- Five fail-first failures; nine regressions cover closing-tag forms, escaped script state, dollar sequences, quotes, backslashes and Unicode.
- All 223 transcription tests pass (one existing skip).
- Built CLI plus Chromium preserves text and IDs across 18 cases; repeated imports are byte-stable and input files remain unchanged.
- All 18 composition fixtures pass lint and strict browser check, with 9 layout and 5 contrast samples each.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, commit hooks, comment checks, deletion and test-reachability checks pass.

This follows the generator fix in #3847. Transcript array-boundary parsing in #3896 remains separate.

title: perf(engine): wait for a missing composition timeline once per render, not once per browser
body:
## What

A composition whose animation is not a GSAP timeline (CSS keyframes, canvas, `requestAnimationFrame`) and whose host lacks `data-no-timeline` now pays the timeline wait once per render instead of once per browser session.

## Why

The engine waits up to the player-ready timeout (45 s by default) for every `[data-composition-id]` host to register `window.__timelines[id]`. A host that never registers costs that full wait in **every** session of a render: the calibration session, then the capture workers, and each static-frame verification page. The outcome cannot change between sessions of the same render, so every wait after the first is spent on a result already known.

A 5-second CSS-only composition (the `css-spinner-render-compat` fixture with `data-no-timeline` removed) took 93.8 s to render on a Mac: 45.6 s in calibration and 47.5 s in capture.

## Related work

Builds on the fail-fast for failed script loads (`scriptLoadFailures`) in the same poll. Does not change the timeout, the warning, or the opt-out.

## How

- `SubTimelineWaitMemo` (engine `types.ts`) is a render-scoped record of host ids whose wait already timed out. The producer creates one per render and passes it through the probe options and `buildCaptureOptions`, so every session of the render shares it. A session created without one gets its own.
- `waitForSubCompositionTimelines` replaces the two identical wait blocks in `initializeSession`. It passes the memo's ids to `pollSubCompositionTimelines`, and records the pending ids after a real timeout (not after a VFX-failure stop).
- `pollSubCompositionTimelines` skips known ids while polling, then lists hosts that are still unregistered. If a known host is still missing, the session reports `timeout` with the same pending ids and the same `sub_timeline_readiness_timeout` warning, and it skips the rebind, exactly like a session that waited. If it registered since, the session reports `ready` and rebinds.
- The static-frame verification page reuses the session's memo, so it no longer waits a second time inside the same session. It also gets the session's failed-script list, so a 404'd scene script ends its wait after the 2 s grace like the main page, instead of the full timeout.
- Only a clean timeout is remembered: the waiting session ran the full wait (no VFX stop) and saw no page errors and no failed script loads. A render whose composition throws or 404s a script keeps today's behaviour exactly, so `sub_timeline_script_failure` still reaches the render policy and still fails the render. A replaying session that already sees a failed script load reports `script_failure`, not `timeout`.
- Distributed chunks create one memo per chunk, shared by the chunk's sessions.
- `pollSubCompositionTimelines` takes an options object instead of eight positional parameters; existing callers and tests are updated.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `frameCapture-subTimelineMemo.test.ts` runs the real page-side check scripts against a fake DOM on fake timers:
  - a second session sharing the memo settles with no timer advance and reports `timeout` plus the pending id;
  - a host the memo does not name is still waited for the full timeout;
  - a memo host that has registered since reports `ready` and rebinds.
- [x] `frameCapture-staticDedupVerificationPage.test.ts`: the verification page settles with no timer advance for a memo host, and settles between 1.999 s and 2.5 s when a script failed to load.
- [x] Also in `frameCapture-subTimelineMemo.test.ts`: no memo after a page error, no memo after a VFX stop, and a replaying session with a failed script load reports `script_failure`.
- [x] Seven mutations, each red on its target test: drop the memo write; drop the skip in the page check; drop the verification page's failed-script list; drop the verification page's memo; memoise despite a page error; memoise despite a VFX stop; drop the replay's script-failure classification.
- [x] The four touched test files, 3 runs in a row: 26 passed, exit 0 each.

### Known residual differences (accepted)

- A composition that did not register in 45 s in the first session but would register within the first poll of a later session is now reported as a timeout there, without the rebind. That needs a timeline that misses a 45 s window and then appears in milliseconds.
- The static-frame verification page now stops waiting 2 s after a failed script load, the same rule the main page already applies. A composition that registers after that window is verified without its rebind, exactly as the main page captures it.
- [x] Before/After on the same Linux box (numbers below); output frames compared via `ffmpeg -f framemd5`.

### Before / After

Linux, 8 cores, software GPU (screenshot capture), Chrome headless shell 152. Median of 5 runs (min-max), same box, load1 under 8 throughout; `many-cuts` is 3 runs. Output compared by decoded frame hash (`ffmpeg -map 0:v -f framemd5`) and audio hash (`-f md5`).

| Composition | Before | After | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| CSS-only clip, no timeline (`css-spinner-render-compat` without `data-no-timeline`), 5 s | 100.1 s (97.7-106.4) | 51.1 s (50.9-51.4) | identical, all 10 runs |
| GSAP timeline on the root, nested host with a CSS spinner and no timeline, 4 s | 92.7 s (92.7-93.2) | 47.7 s (47.7-47.9) | identical, all 10 runs |
| `many-cuts` (GSAP, every host registers) | 11.45 s (11.23-12.10) | 11.30 s (11.10-11.83) | identical, all 6 runs |

Re-run at this head (2 runs per composition): video and audio hashes are identical to origin/main for all three.

Where it went: capture setup (the first session's wait) is unchanged at ~45.7 s. Frame capture drops from 46.8-49.8 s to 1.8-3.1 s because the workers no longer wait again.

The first 45 s wait per render is unchanged on purpose. Skipping it would mean guessing from the page that no timeline will ever arrive, which changes the documented `data-no-timeline` contract.

### Independent review

An adversarial review at this head found no blocking or major issues. An earlier round found one blocker, now fixed: a replaying session could downgrade a script failure to a plain timeout. Minor items accepted:

- m1: covered under "Known residual differences".
- m2: covered under "Known residual differences".
- m4: a failure that hits only a later session, after a first session that ran clean for the full timeout, is reported as a timeout there. Same class as m1: it needs sessions of one render to diverge.
- m5: the "no failed script loads" condition on writing the memo has no dedicated test. It only matters for a failure that lands in the final poll interval, and that first session already reports a plain timeout, so replaying it stays consistent.

title: fix(cli): reject inherited render quality aliases
body:
`hyperframes render --quality constructor` passes the CLI's preset validation because `constructor` is inherited by the alias object. The CLI presents an `undefined` quality, performs browser setup, and eventually fails at the producer boundary with “Render request quality is invalid.” Other inherited property names follow the same path.

Validate own alias keys with a type guard so these inputs produce the existing “Invalid quality” usage diagnostic before rendering starts. The guard also removes the lookup's type assertion. All five supported presets and their encoding settings are preserved.

Validation:

- Six inherited-name regressions fail before the fix and pass after it; 233 related CLI tests pass across seven files, including valid preset controls.
- Rebuilt CLI rejects the six inherited names and an ordinary invalid value before browser setup, writes no output, and exits `1` with the usage diagnostic.
- A valid `looks` command renders the expected 160×120, 10-frame SDR video.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, changed-file formatting, comment checks, and all commit hooks passed.

title: check and snapshot cannot target a composition file, so a second aspect ratio can only be verified as a separate project
body:
### Problem

A common delivery is the same piece in two aspect ratios, for example 16:9 (or a wider web banner) plus 9:16 for social. Following the maintainers' direction in #656 ("manual reflow per ratio"), the natural setup is one composition file per aspect with shared timing. `render` already supports this with `-c/--composition <file>`. The verification gate does not:

- `npx hyperframes check [DIR]` and `npx hyperframes snapshot [DIR]` take only a project directory and always open `index.html` (confirmed on 0.8.141 `--help` and on `main` @ 042ec2e, `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts` / `snapshot.ts` have no `composition` arg, while `render.ts` does).
- So a second-aspect file such as `index.9x16.html` can be rendered but never passes through layout, contrast, motion or snapshot review.

In practice (an agency website loop, delivered as 2970x1080 plus 1080x1920) the agent had to invent a workaround: keep one source `index.html` with CSS for both layouts behind an `.is-portrait` class, and generate a sibling project `portrait/` (own `hyperframes.json`, `package.json`, copied `assets/`, rewritten `data-width`/`data-height` and viewport meta) with a script after every edit, then run `check`/`snapshot` on each directory. It works, but it duplicates assets, needs a regeneration step that is easy to forget, and every agent reinvents it differently.

A related trap surfaced in the same build: script code that measured layout (`getBoundingClientRect`) while building the timeline read the geometry before the portrait canvas size applied, so a match-cut target landed in the wrong place in 9:16 only. Running the full toolchain per aspect is what exposed it.

The workflow skills (`motion-graphics`, `general-video`, `product-launch-video`) have no guidance for multi-aspect deliverables at all: a grep for "aspect", "portrait", "9:16" in their `SKILL.md` on `main` finds only single-canvas mentions (canvas size in the shot-plan IR, layout tables per aspect in individual category modules).

### Proposed solution

1. Add `-c/--composition <file>` to `check` and `snapshot`, with the same semantics as `render -c` (a file inside the project, `index.html` by default). The `*.motion.json` sidecar lookup already keys on the html basename "when several compositions share a dir" (`lint-validate-inspect.md`), so the discovery side seems ready for this.
2. Add a short "Multiple aspect ratios" section to the workflow skills (or once in `hyperframes-core`, linked from them):
   - one composition file per aspect, identical timeline and durations, layout differs;
   - verify every aspect with the full gate (`check -c <file>`, `snapshot -c <file>`), not only the primary;
   - geometry measured at runtime must be measured at the active aspect's canvas size (or derived from static CSS sizes), never cached from another aspect;
   - render each with `render -c <file> -o <name>-<w>x<h>.mp4`.

### Alternatives considered

- **#2455 Dual-Aspect Export** (closed, not planned): single-pass dual render with sync guarantees. This request is much smaller: only let the existing verifiers see a second file.
- **#4933 safe-frame crop packs** (open PR): crops one master into sibling windows. Useful when a crop is acceptable, but it does not cover a reflowed layout, which is what #656 recommends.
- **Sibling project per aspect** (what we do today): works with no CLI change, but needs a generator script and copies assets.

### Additional context

- Environment: hyperframes 0.8.141 (latest), Node 24, macOS arm64.
- Not a duplicate as far as we can tell: searched issues and PRs (open and closed) for "aspect ratio", portrait, "9:16", "multiple aspect", "aspect variants", "check composition", "snapshot composition", "vertical landscape". Closest hits are #2455, #656, #4933 and #4001 (portrait html/body sizing, fixed), none of which add a composition selector to `check`/`snapshot`.

title: fix(cli): preserve speaker labels in WebVTT cue text
body:
Importing a valid WebVTT cue containing `ALICE: Hello there` silently drops that cue. The parser removes uppercase colon-prefixed lines throughout the file as metadata, so it also truncates multiline captions and changes later cue IDs.

Remove the global metadata-line deletion. Header metadata already sits outside timed cue payloads and is ignored by the existing block parser. Add speaker-label and multiline regressions with an `X-TIMESTAMP-MAP` header, plus SRT/VTT round trips, preserving cue text, timing, and IDs.

Validation:

- Five new regressions fail before the fix; 220 caption/transcription tests pass afterward, with one existing platform skip.
- Actual built CLI reproduces the missing cue before the fix. Afterward, six imports preserve both cues; twelve repeated SRT/VTT exports remain stable and leave the source bytes unchanged.
- Chrome native TextTrack parsing confirms expected text and timestamps for all twelve original/exported WebVTT cases.
- Rebased on current main `188475aaf`; all package builds and the 220 related tests passed again. The rebuilt CLI reproduction, CLI typecheck, repository lint, formatting, comment checks, and all commit hooks passed on that base.

title: fix(cli): serve empty project assets without a stream error
body:
Requesting an empty local asset through the CLI's static project server throws an uncaught `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`: `createReadStream` receives an end offset of `-1`. A lint-clean composition containing an iframe that loads an empty HTML document makes `hyperframes check` exit without its result.

Return the empty `200` response directly after range validation. Valid byte-range requests against an empty file still receive `416`, and nonempty assets keep their streaming path. Add real HTTP regressions for absent/malformed range headers, all three valid range forms, and a successful project request after serving the empty asset.

Validation:

- Three new empty-response tests fail with uncaught stream errors before the fix; all six new cases pass afterward. Related server/validate/snapshot tests: 119 passed.
