- Real source-server reproduction changes from an uncaught error to `200` with zero bytes.
- Rebuilt CLI passes lint and the strict browser gate on the empty-iframe fixture: nine layout and five contrast samples, zero runtime errors.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, comment checks, and all commit hooks passed.

title: fix(cli): validate WAV format chunk bounds before reading
body:
A RIFF/WAVE file with a zero- or one-byte `fmt ` chunk makes the built-in transcription WAV reader throw `ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` while reading the format field. The worker's error then describes a buffer offset and omits the audio filename.

Require the complete 16-byte base format header before reading format fields, so truncated chunks use the existing filename-bearing unsupported-WAV diagnostic. Add short-header cases and two child-worker regressions that verify the prefixed error message.

Validation:

- Two short-header regressions fail before the fix. The related caption/transcription suite passes 222 tests with one existing platform skip; all 20 WAV/worker tests pass after adding worker regressions.
- Real FFmpeg-generated mono PCM audio still reads at 16 kHz with 16,000 samples. The malformed-file reproduction now names its file.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, comment checks, and all commit hooks passed.

title: fix(cli): preserve literal WebVTT cue text
body:
WebVTT sidecars write normalized transcript text directly as cue markup. A literal `<config>` disappears when Chrome displays the cue, and literal `<` becomes `<`. Importing encoded cues also keeps entity spellings instead of their displayed characters, so export/import does not preserve the text.

Escape ampersands and angle brackets in exported WebVTT payloads, and decode imported character references once after the existing tag removal. Reuse the existing `linkedom` dependency, protect literal less-than signs before entity decoding, and skip decoding for plain cues without ampersands. Add literal-text round trips and encoded payload cases, including numeric entities, actual cue formatting, unknown entities, and bidirectional marks.

Validation:

- Ten new cases fail before the fix; 225 caption/transcription tests pass afterward, with one existing platform skip. The final normalizer suite passes all 51 tests.
- Actual CLI: five exports/reimports and seven encoded imports preserve text and timing; repeated exports are byte-stable and leave inputs unchanged.
- Chrome native TextTrack display matches expected text and timestamps in all twelve CLI-generated or imported cases.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, comment checks, and all commit hooks passed.

title: docs(cli): explain FFmpeg setup without a package manager
body:
When FFmpeg is missing on a Mac without Homebrew, the CLI skill's troubleshooting reference offers no usable setup path even though HyperFrames already supports configured binaries. Document both `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH` / `HYPERFRAMES_FFPROBE_PATH` and project-local `.hyperframes/bin`, including their discovery precedence and Windows filenames.

Add a copyable `doctor --json` check for the two encoding dependencies. The report also includes optional tools, so checking only its overall `ok` can reject a working local encoding setup.

Refs #5232. This covers the existing-binary setup documentation; the issue's early workflow preflight and CLI hint proposals remain follow-up work.

Validation: built CLI exercised in seven cases (explicit paths, project-local binaries, both precedence controls, and each/both missing overrides), plus two incomplete-report controls. The documented jq check accepted all four working setups and rejected all missing setups. Root lint, skill cross-references, formatting, comment checks, and commit hooks passed. Confirmed the official FFmpeg download page provides macOS builds. No product behavior or dependencies change.

title: fix(capture): distinguish SVG namespaces from attribute values
body:
Capturing an inline SVG whose label contains text such as `xmlns=demo` saves a logo that fails to load as an image: `toStandaloneSvg` mistakes the label text for a namespace declaration and omits the real SVG namespace. The same regex handling also misreads xlink-looking labels and quoted tag delimiters.

Read namespace declarations and xlink usage from parsed attribute names, then insert the required declarations into the original source. Preserve artwork and label bytes, and leave already-declared SVGs unchanged. This uses the CLI's existing linkedom dependency.

Validation: seven added regressions fail on main, including an actual asset download; all 374 related capture/command tests pass with the fix. Eight Chrome 152 cases run through the real token extractor and asset downloader, then load each saved SVG as an image and verify its dimensions, label, and expected pixel. Existing namespace cases retain byte-identical source. CLI build/typecheck, root lint, formatting, comments, and commit hooks passed.

title: fix(cli): bound timeline bars for negative media starts
body:
`hyperframes timeline` crashes with `RangeError: Invalid count value` when nested media resolves to a start before project time zero. The bar renderer passes its negative column count to `String.repeat`, even though the resolved timing is valid input to the timeline description.

Bound the printed bar's starting column at zero. Preserve resolved clip timing, JSON output, and the existing fixed-width rendering for zero, positive, and beyond-project starts.

Validation: four of six added cases fail on main; all 86 timeline tests pass with the fix. Seven built-CLI projects verify text/JSON timing, forty-column bars, stable repeated output, and unchanged input files, including local/global negative starts, a fractional negative start, a clip spanning the project, and three boundary controls. CLI build/typecheck, root lint, formatting, comments, and commit hooks passed.

title: fix(cli): route timeline project directories to inspection
body:
The documented `hyperframes timeline <project-dir>` command rejects every project path as an unknown subcommand after timeline editing subcommands were added. Users cannot inspect another project by its advertised positional directory argument.

Distinguish inspection paths from the existing edit verbs before Citty dispatches. Keep flags parsed and validated, preserve `--` for literal directory names and edit arguments, and reject extra inspection arguments through the existing diagnostic helper.

Validation: five initial end-to-end regressions fail on main; final 131 related timeline, command-registration, and argument-validation tests pass. Seventeen built-CLI cases cover absolute/relative paths with spaces, flag order, current-directory inspection, subcommand/dash-prefixed directory names, separators, unknown flags, extra/missing directories, and unchanged edit plans. Repeated inspection output is stable and all input files remain unchanged. CLI build/typecheck, root lint, formatting, comment checks, and commit hooks passed.

title: docs(skills): preserve glyphs in text reveal masks
body:
Tight `line-height` with an `overflow: hidden` text mask can cut descenders and accents after a reveal has finished. Document mask padding with a compensating negative margin, explain why the mask must use the text's font size for `em` units, and link the guidance from the `mask-reveal-up` adapter.

Also describe releasing clipping on the timeline after the entrance and explain that `data-layout-allow-overflow` suppresses resting-state checks. Regenerate the skills manifest.

Refs #5231. This addresses the requested skills guidance; the reported audit behavior remains for a separate change.

Validation:
- Chrome 152, local Inter 600: compared masked and unclipped screenshots for `Betreuung`, `Ägypj`, and `Épýj` at two settled timestamps. The unpadded mask lost 1,048–3,211 visible pixels; padding preserved the complete image byte-for-byte and kept the original text position. The initial parked text remained hidden.
- Both local compositions passed `hyperframes lint` and `hyperframes check --strict --at 1.2,1.8`, confirming the current audit blind spot.
- Repository lint, final skills cross-reference checks, CLI build, and formatting passed.

title: fix(producer): close artifact frame validation gaps
body:
PNG-sequence renders can publish incomplete frame directories because the final artifact gate only checks whether the files are readable and nonempty. Pass the planned frame count through the existing expectation builder and compare it with exported top-level `frame_*.png` files, excluding audio sidecars and unrelated files. A failed check leaves the previous destination intact.

Use the directory-only tolerance reviewed in #3574 (`max(1, ceil(expectedFrames × 0.002))`); video artifacts retain the existing one-frame tolerance. WebM and HLS commonly omit usable frame-count metadata, so they continue through duration validation without a warning.

Refs #3484 and the reviewed, unmerged #3574. The transaction commit API and whole-file packet counting are unchanged.

Validation:
- The original PNG regressions reproduce on main. Five quiet-validation checks fail on the earlier PR revision; all 37 artifact transaction tests pass again after the review cleanup. Comments now describe the quiet fallback when frame metadata is unavailable.
- A rebuilt CLI render in Chrome 152 produces a two-second WebM with 10 decoded frames and no skipped-frame-gate warning.
- Full renderer fault injection removes two staged PNGs after encoding. Validation rejects 8/10 frames, marks the job failed, preserves the previous output, and cleans the transaction.
- Producer typecheck, Core/producer/CLI builds, repository lint, formatting, reachability, comment checks, and full pre-commit checks pass.

title: fix(sdk): decode scoped IDs when replaying patches
body:
An SDK edit to `hf-host/hf-leaf` emits a JSON Pointer such as `/elements/hf-host~1hf-leaf/text`. The patch reader passes that encoded segment to the scoped DOM resolver, so replay, saved overrides, and iframe synchronization lose the edit. Decode element IDs once, in JSON Pointer order, before resolving the target.

The patch format stays the same. Style, text, attribute, timing, hold, and removal patches now replay against the same nested element that the forward edit changed, including literal `~1` IDs.

Validation:

- Reproduced on main: forward style edit succeeded while emitted-patch replay and reopening saved overrides left the nested element unchanged.
- All 14 new regressions failed before the fix; all 621 SDK tests pass afterward, covering emitted patches, override replay, batch rollback, and a literal `~1` ID.
- Built SDK in Chrome 152 with a real iframe: nested text/style edits, undo, redo, iframe reload, saved-override reopening, and event replay all passed; the sibling with the same ID stayed unchanged and no runtime errors occurred.
- SDK build, repository lint, and changed-file formatting passed.

title: fix(player): honor runtime discovery and source in embeds
body:
Fixes #4002
Fixes #4003

A `src` embed can mistake the shared `window.__hf` shader namespace for the runtime bridge. On current main it can report `ready` from document metadata while seeking leaves the authored timeline at zero; nested scenes can remain unmounted. Check the actual `__player` bridge so standalone timelines remain driveable and nested scenes receive the runtime.

Use the existing validated `runtime-src` resolver for probe injection as well as `srcdoc`. A blocked or missing runtime now emits a load error with its URL, stops probing, and marks that document failed. Detach the error handler when stopping or restarting so an old script cannot fail the next document. Same-origin/loopback validation and pinned-CDN fallback stay intact.

Follows the scope described in unmerged [#4246](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/4246), with before/after captures and additional failure/recovery coverage.

## Before

Main at `188475aaf`: CDN access blocked; every embed has `runtime-src="/local-runtime.js"` and receives `seek(1)`. The shader namespace leaves its marker at x=40 instead of x=200. Nested scenes stay empty, and the plain nested embed fetches jsDelivr and times out.

![Before: main leaves shader timelines undriven and nested scenes empty](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user-github-me/hyperframes/498e9ba63ef1aab06f0b547369823675b8c95951/contribution-evidence/player-src-runtime-discovery/before.png)

## After

Identical fixture HTML, same blocked-CDN policy. All four embeds load and seek to x=200; nested scenes use `/local-runtime.js`, expose `__player`, and register their child timelines. No CDN requests or browser runtime errors.

![After: all four embeds seek correctly and nested scenes use the local bridge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user-github-me/hyperframes/498e9ba63ef1aab06f0b547369823675b8c95951/contribution-evidence/player-src-runtime-discovery/after.png)

## Validation

- Seven new probe cases fail on main; all 552 player tests pass after the fix (16 new cases including bridge priority, URL policy, late errors, failure latching, and recovery). Disabled script loading in Happy DOM is configured as successful; explicit error events test failures.
- Real Chrome 152 with built player, local GSAP, and local core runtime: four before/after embeds above; separate real 404 runtime emits its URL error in 230 ms, then changing `runtime-src` recovers and seeks correctly.
- All four fixture projects pass composition lint and strict browser checks.
- Player build/runtime-version pin, both player typechecks, repository lint, and changed-file formatting pass.
- Sandbox origin browser check passes. One-run load/scrub smoke check passes its thresholds (cold 604 ms; warm 84 ms; inline/isolated scrub p95 16.3/17.8 ms).

title: fix(sdk): preserve unquoted escapes in inline styles
body:
An inline CSS custom property such as `--label: alpha\;beta` is valid, but changing an unrelated `color` through the SDK splits at its escaped semicolon and rewrites the value. Escaped quotes and parentheses can make the scanner swallow later declarations, leaving undo unable to restore color.

Handle an escaped character before checking quote state in the existing inline-style scanner. This keeps escaped punctuation inside an unquoted value while an escaped backslash followed by an ordinary semicolon still ends the declaration.

Validation:

- Eight new regressions fail on main (four scanner cases and four public edit/undo/redo/reopen/override cases); all 616 SDK tests pass after the fix, including an escaped-backslash control.
- Built SDK in Chrome 152, real iframe synchronization: five values survive edit, undo, redo, iframe reload, and serialized reopening; baseline reproduces custom-property corruption and missing undo restoration.
- SDK build, repository lint, changed-file lint and formatting pass.
- Optional `typecheck:examples` reports existing examples/test typing errors; its output is byte-identical on unchanged main.

title: fix(sdk): correct animation calls in examples and docs
body:
When a host follows the SDK animation examples on a composition without GSAP, the capability guard currently lets the edit through and throws. Missing element IDs also produce unusable tweens. Even on supported compositions, the entrance examples emit empty tween properties and leave the element stationary.

Check `can(op).ok`, remove the unsupported preflight `id`, and pass `from` tween values through `properties` in the React, vanilla, and headless examples. Correct the guide/reference snippets and field descriptions, clarify the `GsapTweenSpec.properties` comment, and exercise the actual example helpers through the SDK test runner.

Validation:

- All **620 SDK tests** pass; 12 new regression cases fail on the unchanged examples, with an existing-animation control passing.
- All four actual documentation snippets emit the intended entrance through the SDK.
- SDK build and typechecking of all example files plus the new regression file pass. Root lint, changed-file formatting, test reachability, and commit hooks pass.
- Chrome 152 with GSAP 3.15: all four helpers change from stationary/fully visible to the intended fade/entrance; forward and backward seeks give identical states, with no runtime errors.
- All eight before/after generated compositions pass CLI lint and `check --strict --at 1`.

The optional `typecheck:examples` command also includes existing test files: its four example diagnostics are fixed; the 19 remaining test-file diagnostics are identical to `main`.\n

title: fix(gcp-cloud-run): validate progress result payloads
body:
`getRenderProgress` casts the Workflows result JSON to the expected shape without validating it. A successful response with `Chunks: {}` throws during polling; string frame counts concatenate, and negative/non-finite numbers or non-string output paths escape into the snapshot.

Normalize stage results at the JSON boundary. Ignore non-object stages and invalid chunk lists; retain valid stages, zero values, and finite non-negative numeric fields. Missing/invalid durations continue to use the existing estimated-cost fallback.

Validation:

- **118 Cloud Run tests pass** across 12 files. Eleven final regression cases fail on `main`, with valid, empty, failed, and zero-valued controls passing.
- Package build/typecheck, root lint, changed-file lint/formatting, test reachability, and commit hooks pass.
- Built SDK under Node 22 with `tsx` for workspace source exports: five local HTTP execution-response cases pass (valid, malformed chunks, invalid numbers, running, and failed).

Validation uses local response fixtures; no cloud deployment or live billing assertions.\n

title: fix(producer): distinguish project files in cache hashes
body:
Project cache keys currently concatenate each file path and its bytes without delimiting the end of the contents. A tree containing `a = "bc\0def"` hashes identically to a tree containing empty `a` plus `bc = "def"`. Both cloud adapters then skip uploading the changed tree and reuse the wrong project.

Include the byte length before each file's contents in the shared hash input. Keep deterministic traversal, the 16-character ID format, and the existing top-level skip rules. Cover the collision in the hash helper and both adapters.

Validation:

- **1,529 producer unit tests pass**, with one existing skipped test; **144 AWS tests** and **102 GCP tests** pass.
- Two hash collisions and both adapter cache regressions fail on `main`; unchanged-tree, binary/Unicode, empty-file, rename, and skip-rule controls pass.
- Producer build, all three package typechecks, root lint, changed-file formatting, test reachability, and commit hooks pass.
- Node 22 with the built producer export and local cloud transports: both adapters produce the same two distinct IDs, upload each tree once, skip the repeat upload, and preserve the correct contents in all four extracted archives.

Default project IDs change on upgrade, causing one fresh upload per project. Existing handles and explicit `siteId` overrides continue to work. No live cloud deployment was used.\n

title: fix(aws-lambda): attribute parallel history events to their states
body:
When parallel Step Functions branches interleave, the Lambda progress reader assigns every completion/failure to the latest entered state. A chunk completed after a different branch is entered loses its frame count, and its failure is reported under that unrelated state.

Carry the enclosing state through each event's `previousEventId` chain. Use that state for chunk frame counts and Lambda failures, retain the fallback for histories without parent IDs, and report `<unknown>` when an explicit parent is missing.

Validation:

- **151 AWS tests pass** across 13 files; all eight new attribution regressions fail on `main`.
- Coverage includes optimized and raw Lambda events, interleaved success/failure, pagination, unrelated-task frame counts, missing parents, and existing sequential histories.
- Package build/typecheck, root lint, changed-file formatting, test reachability, and commit hooks pass.
- Built SDK on Node 22 with the workspace `tsx` loader: four local HTTP paginated-history probes pass for success/failure in both integration formats.

No cloud deployment was used; verification uses the SDK's existing client-injection boundary.\n

title: fix(cli): reject polling waits when already aborted
body:
An abort triggered by `onTick` happens before the default sleep subscribes to the signal. The abort event has already fired, so polling waits the entire interval (10 seconds by default) before noticing cancellation.

Reject an already-aborted signal before scheduling a timer. Keep the original error reason and the existing fallback for non-error reasons. Add regressions for cancellation during the status callback, cancellation during an active wait, and normal polling with an active signal.

Validation: 112 cloud/client and cloud-command tests pass; the CLI typecheck, repository lint, changed-file formatting, and test reachability checks pass. Both new callback-cancellation cases fail on current main. A Node 22 probe using the actual cloud client against a local HTTP server measured 252 ms before versus 0 ms after with a 250 ms polling interval.

title: fix(cli): handle decoded cloud download responses
body:
`fetch` decodes content-encoded responses while retaining their compressed `Content-Length`. Cloud downloads compared the decoded bytes against that header and rejected valid gzip, deflate, and Brotli responses as truncated.

Only use `Content-Length` for unencoded or identity responses. Content-encoded downloads report their received byte count with an unknown total; fetch and the stream pipeline continue to surface transfer errors and cancellation. Preserve atomic replacement and the existing output on failure.

Validation: 119 cloud/client and cloud-command tests pass, including real HTTP coverage for gzip, x-gzip, mixed-case gzip, deflate, Brotli, stacked compression, identity, and an unknown coding. Six compressed-response regressions fail on current main. Interrupted and cancelled gzip transfers preserve the previous output; identity and unencoded truncation checks still pass. CLI build and typecheck, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability pass. A separate Node 22/local-HTTP probe reproduces the original 1,920-versus-51-byte false truncation and verifies the corrected bytes on disk.

Related: #3944 addresses a separate writer-close/cleanup race; this PR leaves that implementation to its existing author.

title: fix(cli): preserve signed upload content-type headers
body:
The direct-upload flow adds a lowercase `content-type` default before spreading the server’s signed headers. If the API returns `Content-Type` or another casing, fetch combines both values; a real HTTP request receives `application/zip, application/zip`, changing the header that the presigned request requires.

Add the ZIP default only when the normalized upload headers contain no content-type key, comparing names case-insensitively. Preserve the server’s values and casing and keep the existing handling of other headers.

Validation: 113 cloud/client and cloud-command tests pass. Five real HTTP upload cases cover title, uppercase, mixed, lowercase, and absent content-type keys; the first three fail on current main. The tests verify the received header value, one header entry, unchanged request bytes, and upload completion. A separate Node 22 HTTP probe confirms the duplicate value before and a single value after. CLI typecheck, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability pass.

title: fix(parsers): preserve URL suffixes when rewriting parent paths
body:
Parent-relative asset URLs were passed to filesystem-style path normalization with their query and fragment attached. This changed values such as `../cover.png?source=https://example.com/a//b` to `cover.png?source=https:/example.com/a/b`, and `../sprites.svg#icons/../logo` lost its filename altogether.

Split off the suffix before normalizing the pathname, then append it unchanged. Use the existing suffix splitter so parent-relative paths follow the same rule as sibling asset paths. This shared helper serves the composition compiler, CSS rewriting, and direct nested-entry rebasing.

Validation: all 1,238 parser tests pass (4 existing skips, 3 existing todos), along with 515 core compiler tests and 140 producer compiler tests. Six parser regressions and the new core integration regression fail on current main. Parser build, parser/core/runtime typechecks, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability pass. A Chrome 152/local-HTTP probe compiles a nested scene, preserves the exact stylesheet and image query strings in network requests, loads the image successfully, and reports no runtime errors.

title: fix(cli): refresh item manifests when bypassing registry cache
body:
Installing by tag requests a fresh registry index, but cached item manifests could hide newly added or removed tags for up to 24 hours. Pass `skipCache` through item and transitive-dependency resolution so an explicit refresh sees the current tags, dependencies, and file lists while retaining valid cached data if the fetch fails.

This update resolves the conflicts with current `main` and preserves its 32-request concurrency limit and switch to cached items after a timeout. `cacheOnly` takes precedence over a refresh request, so queued work does not restart network requests after that fallback has begun. The catalog contribution guide documents the resulting tag-install behavior.

Validation: full workspace build; CLI typecheck; all registry suites (273 passed, 1 skipped), including fresh/stale cache-only precedence, cached remaining items after a timeout, refreshed tags, and transitive dependencies; lint, formatting, test reachability, normal commit hooks, and both comment checks. Mint validation and link checks passed.

title: chore: release v0.8.142
body:
Prepare v0.8.142 from current main (`188475aaf`).

The main reason for this cut is #5177: the CLI accepts a HeyGen access token handed over by a host app, and HyperFrames Desktop needs a published CLI with it.

Release notes cover all 4 pull requests merged since v0.8.141 (#5151, #5169, #5174, #5177) in plain language. They also carry #5177's release note: a shell that already exports `HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN` now has it used ahead of `~/.heygen/credentials`. Package and plugin versions are updated together.

## No visible change

This PR changes release metadata and documentation only. The features and fixes described in the notes are already on main.

## Validation

- `bun run release:prepare 0.8.142` on the current main commit, after fetching tags so the range starts at v0.8.141.
- Compared the release notes against every merged pull request since v0.8.141 (`git log v0.8.141..188475aaf`).
- Local tag deleted; the publish workflow creates `v0.8.142` at the merge SHA.

title: fix(engine): invalidate cached media metadata after file changes
body:
In a long-running process, replacing a video or audio file at the same path still returns its old duration, dimensions, frame rate, or sample rate. The final-frame cache also returns the previous timestamp when a replacement keeps the same stream duration. The raw ffprobe cache tracks file identity, but the derived metadata caches bypass it on filename-only hits.

Use the existing device/inode/size/mtime/ctime identity for the video, audio, and final-frame caches. Changed or deleted files are reprobed. Unchanged files keep concurrent probe sharing; results without an available file identity are retained only while in flight. An older failed probe cannot evict a newer replacement entry.

Validation:
- Five initial regression cases fail on main; tests also cover same-size atomic replacement, absent identities, concurrent callers, and an older failed probe racing its replacement.
- 133 ffprobe tests, 135 producer tests, and 48 CLI timeline tests passed.
- Real FFmpeg/Node probes now detect replacement video dimensions/duration, audio sample rate/duration, and the final timestamp changing from 1.9s to 1.95s.
- Engine build; producer/CLI type checks; repository lint, formatting, test reachability, and complexity audit passed.
- Full engine run has nine FFmpeg color, HLS timestamp, and frame-sampling failures. All nine also reproduce on untouched main with the same local toolchain.

The HDR PNG fixture was fetched from Git LFS and verified against its recorded SHA-256 before testing.

title: aws-lambda CDK: AssembleV2 never receives AudioS3Uri: null, so every v2 render fails with PLAN_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED
body:
**Versions:** `@hyperframes/aws-lambda@0.8.134` (same construct code and handler check in 0.8.140), `aws-cdk-lib@2.272.0`.

**What happens.** `HyperframesRenderStack` builds the AssembleV2 task with `TaskInput.fromObject({ …, AudioS3Uri: null, … })`. CDK omits `null` values when it renders the state machine definition, so the deployed `AssembleV2` payload has no `AudioS3Uri` key at all. The handler's `validatePlanProtocolShape` requires `event.AudioS3Uri === null` for a v2 assemble and throws:

```
PLAN_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED: [handler] v2 assemble audio must be materialized from the manifest
```

Every chunk renders, then the execution fails at AssembleV2. The SAM template (`examples/aws-lambda/template.yaml`) keeps `AudioS3Uri: null` and works.

**Repro**
1. Deploy `HyperframesRenderStack` from `@hyperframes/aws-lambda/cdk` with default props.
2. `renderToLambda` any project with the default `planProtocol` (v2).
3. The execution fails at AssembleV2. `aws stepfunctions describe-state-machine` shows the AssembleV2 payload without `AudioS3Uri`.

**Suggested fix (either):**
- Render the null explicitly in the construct, e.g. `"AudioS3Uri.$": "States.StringToJson('null')"`.
- Relax the handler check to `event.AudioS3Uri == null` (null or absent).

A snapshot test against the synthesized/deployed definition (rather than construct props) would catch this. As a workaround we patch the rendered `DefinitionString` with `addPropertyOverride` to insert `"AudioS3Uri":null` into the AssembleV2 parameters; v2 renders then succeed.

title: Distributed (Lambda) render: Plan fails with VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED (ffmpeg_timeout) for long video clips
body:
**Versions:** `@hyperframes/aws-lambda@0.8.134`, render Lambda at 10,240 MB, 10 GB ephemeral storage.

**What happens.** A 26-minute composition with a single 576×1024 H.264 `<video>` (24 fps, ~37,800 frames) fails in Plan:

```
VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED: Video extraction failed for 1 source(s) [VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED; ffmpeg_timeout=1]
```

Plan extracts every frame of the clip in one ffmpeg process, which exceeds the default `ffmpegProcessTimeout` (300,000 ms); the Step Functions retries hit the same limit. Raising `FFMPEG_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS` on the function helps, but Plan is still bounded by Lambda's 15-minute limit, so a long video can't render as a single distributed job. Short clips (60 s) of the same footage render fine.

**Ask**
- Extract video frames per chunk (each RenderChunk extracts only its own frame range), or split Plan's extraction into parallel ranges.
- Document the practical maximum video length for the Lambda path.

**Workaround we use:** split the edit into ~4-minute parts (frame-aligned), render the parts as separate jobs in parallel, and concatenate the MP4s (video stream copy, audio re-encoded across the joins). 26 minutes renders in about 11 minutes this way.

title: fix(cli): close unused download responses before following redirects
body:
Model downloads can fail after a redirect even while the final response is streaming normally. `downloadFile` drains an unused redirect body and starts the next request immediately; an idle previous socket can then time out and reject the entire download.

Close unused redirect and rejected HTTP responses instead of draining them. Ignore request errors from responses already discarded so an earlier hop cannot reject or remove the active download's partial file.

Validation:
- Six new regression cases fail on the original code, covering redirect chains, old-hop errors, the redirect limit, and rejected responses.
- 63 tests across the downloader, Whisper/TTS/background-removal managers, and registry model downloads passed.
- A local HTTPS server reproduces a timeout through a redirect while the direct model transfer succeeds; the fixed downloader completes both transfers without uncaught errors.
- CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability passed.

title: fix(aws-lambda): preserve null audio in CDK v2 assembly
body:
CDK drops the literal `AudioS3Uri: null` from the synthesized AssembleV2 payload. The handler then rejects every v2 assembly because it requires null audio and materializes the audio from the plan manifest.

Use `JsonPath.stringToJson("null")` so the rendered state machine supplies an explicit JSON null at execution time. Add assertions against the synthesized CDK payload and controls for SAM's null field and both v1 audio paths.

Fixes #5259.

Validation: all 145 AWS Lambda tests passed; the new synthesized-payload regression fails on main. The built CDK package also emits `AudioS3Uri.$: "States.StringToJson('null')"` under CDK 2.254.0. AWS package build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability passed.

title: fix(cli): validate the complete TTS speed argument
body:
`hyperframes tts --speed` accepts values below the stated 0.1 minimum and silently reads numeric prefixes from inputs such as `1.5junk` or `1 2`. An explicitly empty value also falls back to 1.0, starting synthesis instead of reporting invalid input.

Parse the complete argument and require a finite value within 0.1–3.0. Apply the default only when the flag is omitted.

Validation: five regression cases fail on main; 49 TTS command and synthesis tests passed. The built CLI rejects below-range, trailing-text, and empty speeds before Python/model setup. CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, and test reachability passed.

title: fix(cli): honor authored durations when listing compositions
body:
`hyperframes compositions` ignores an inline root's `data-duration`: a declared 8-second composition with a 2-second child is listed as 2 seconds. External compositions have the opposite trim problem: a declared 2.5-second composition with a 7-second child is listed as 7 seconds. Invalid external declarations can also produce `Infinity` or accept numeric prefixes.

Use the existing shared duration reader and resolver for both listings. A valid authored duration wins; otherwise the command derives the duration from child ends and keeps its external script fallback.

Validation: seven regression cases fail on main; 88 CLI composition, metadata, and timeline tests passed. The built CLI lists all eight shipped example projects successfully. Engine/parser/CLI builds, CLI typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, and hooks passed.

title: fix(engine): preserve out-of-range HDR object positions
body:
HDR image setup clamps CSS `object-position` percentages to 0–100%. This pins images to an edge when the browser would place them partly or wholly outside the box; it also changes cover crops.

Preserve finite percentage values in the HDR resampler. Its existing destination bounds clip the positioned image, matching CSS placement.

Validation: 11 regression cases fail on main; 155 engine image/compositing tests and 36 producer HDR setup tests passed. The rebuilt engine matches Chrome across 12 positions, and the producer places a real 16-bit PNG correctly. Engine build, producer typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, and hooks passed.

title: fix(core): stop small previews dropping layers on heavy compositions
body:
## What

A small preview no longer rasters a composition's `will-change: transform` layers at full size. While the player shows a composition smaller than its own size, the runtime drops that hint on every layer where nothing depends on it, so those layers raster at the size they are shown. Heavy compositions stop running out of tile memory and dropping layers. Layout, paint order and pixels stay as they are in the export, and the runtime writes no inline style.

## Why

Heavy compositions dropped layers in a small preview: text, labels and overlay controls vanished for single frames while WebGL canvases stayed drawn.

Chromium never rasters a layer under a `will-change: transform` hint below the native scale (device scale x page scale), unless the shown scale is under 25% of native (`MinimumRasterContentsScaleForWillChangeTransform` in `cc/layers/picture_layer_impl.cc`). The player fits a 1920x1080 composition into its box with `transform: scale()`, so in a 528px preview on a 2x screen every hinted layer rasters 3.6x larger than it is shown. A composition with many such layers exhausts the tile budget, and the compositor draws frames with missing tiles.

Earlier heads tried CSS `zoom` (it changed text wrapping against the render), then a stand-in property on each element (`filter: opacity(1)`, then a far `perspective`). Each stand-in was visible to the editor or GSAP, so it could end up saved in a project, and went stale when classes changed. Both are gone; the transform fit stays.

## How

- `setPreviewRasterScale` (packages/core/src/runtime/previewRasterHints.ts) runs from the runtime's existing `set-display-scale` handler, which only a preview host sends (shown width / layout width). Renders never send it.
- Below 1x it adds one rule, `[data-hf-preview-raster] { will-change: auto !important }`, and puts that attribute on each layer whose computed `will-change` holds only transform hints and whose hint changes nothing:
  - the layer is positioned, so it already contains its absolute descendants and paints in the same phase;
  - no descendant, and no `::before`/`::after` of the layer or a descendant, is `position: fixed` (the hint is their containing block);
  - unless the layer has its own z-index, none of those has a z-index or a blend mode (the hint's stacking context holds them);
  - a layer that also hints `opacity` or `filter` keeps every hint, since those make boundaries of their own (for example for `backdrop-filter`).
- Layers that do not qualify keep their hint and their larger raster. That is deliberate: correctness first.
- Changes are followed while the preview is small. Any attribute change re-checks that subtree, and an added element is checked. An added stylesheet re-checks the page, again once a linked sheet loads. Inline style changes, which scripts make every frame, are handled cheaply: they give the hint back to any layer holding an element that now depends on it, and re-check a layer whose own position, z-index or inline `will-change` changed.
- Not followed, so a mark can go stale until the next change above:
  - sibling (`~`, `+`) and `:has()` rules triggered from outside the layer;
  - CSS variables set on the layer that feed a descendant's z-index;
  - rewritten `<style>` text and `insertRule`;
  - shadow roots;
  - an `opacity` or `filter` hint that reaches an already-marked layer through a rule on an ancestor's class or attribute (the layer's own changes are followed).
- Cost, from the review's measurements: following inline styles adds about 1 to 2 ms per animated frame on a laptop. A change on a container re-checks the layers under it (about 3 ms for 450 layers). An added stylesheet re-checks the whole page.
- Fine detail in a swapped layer now rasters at the size shown, so a pattern a few pixels wide in the small preview blends a little instead of being downsampled from a full-size raster. That is the point of the fix; layout, shapes and positions are unchanged.
- At 1x or more the rule and every mark are removed.
- Studio: the preview-only attributes (`data-hf-upcoming`, `data-hf-preview-lazy`, `data-hf-preview-raster`) are one list, `PREVIEW_ONLY_ATTRS` in `@hyperframes/core/studio-preview-mark`. Copy (`liveMarkupWithoutPreviewMarks`) and text edits (`buildTextField`) leave them out of what is saved, and the runtime's keep-unchanged-media check ignores them, so a marked video keeps playing through an edit (this also fixes the same rebuild for `data-hf-upcoming`). Studio's stacking model counts a marked layer as the stacking context its hint makes, so timeline z-order edits match the render.

## Measured

Synthetic composition of 48 `will-change` lyric layers (a fixture built for this PR), 528px player, DPR 2, 80 MB tile budget, full Chrome 154, 3 paired runs against the merge base. Playback for 8 s, then the player grown to 1100px and shrunk back to 528px.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Largest raster / shown size, 528px | 3.64 | 1.00 |
| Largest raster / shown size, 1100px | 1.75 | 1.00 |
| `will-change` compositor layers | 48 | 0 |
| Compositor layers | 51 | 4 |
| Main-thread busy during playback | 28.8 / 24.2 / 21.2 % | 21.1 / 20.4 / 20.9 % |
| Compositor frames in the 2.5 s after growing to 1100px | 16 / 17 / 13 | 186 / 253 / 186 |
| Frames drawn with missing tiles, Before/After capture below | 4 | 0 |

The layout of every element is unchanged (checked to 0.01px by the browser test). The paint is unchanged too: the browser test's frosted-glass and 3D probes compare the swap on and off at the same size.

## Tests

- `packages/player/tests/browser/preview-raster-size.ts` (player-perf load shard, `test:browser-raster`), fixture `tests/perf/fixtures/preview-raster`:
  - shows the composition at full size and records every element's box, a z-index paint-order probe, a flipped 3D card probe, every inline style and every computed filter;
  - shrinks the player and checks that no box moved, paint order and the 3D card are unchanged, no inline style or computed filter changed, that the layers holding a fixed child, a z-indexed child, a `::before` behind them, 3D or a mixed hint keep their hint while the others lose it, and that a layer added later loses it too;
  - at that same small size, turns the swap off and on with the `set-display-scale` message: with it off, the compositor trace must show layers rastered above 1.5x (so the measurement can fail); with it on, three traces in a row must show none. Frosted glass (`backdrop-filter` inside a hinted wrapper) and a 3D-rotated child must render the same both ways;
  - gives a child of a marked layer an inline z-index, as a script would, and checks the layer gets its hint back;
  - grows it back and checks every mark is gone.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/previewRasterHints.test.ts`: which layers are marked and which keep their hint, restore leaving the document byte-identical, late layers, class changes, inline z-index, position and `will-change` changes, added stylesheets and attribute selectors.
- `packages/studio/src/utils/authoredSource.test.ts` and `domEditingTextFields.test.ts`: copied markup and a saved text edit carry no preview mark.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/stackingContext.test.ts`: a marked layer keeps its stacking context. `init.swapScenes.test.ts`: a video carrying either preview mark is kept through a scene swap. `previewRasterHints.test.ts` also checks that nothing is injected before a `set-display-scale` arrives.
- Mutations: each of these fails at least one test: no rule, no positioned check, no fixed check, no z-index check, no blend check, no pseudo-element check, accepting mixed hints, not following inline styles, not giving holders their hint back, no restore, no observer, not re-checking a layer's own inline values, no full pass on an added stylesheet, following only `class`, and reading hints through the mark.

## Before

A 528px player on a 2x screen with an 80 MB tile budget, playing the 48-layer fixture on main (merge base). Every hinted layer rasters at 3.6x the size shown, and 4 frames are drawn with missing tiles (text cut off or gone for a frame).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/25570377-034c-4981-b04c-059060f701a0

## After

The same playback with this PR: layers raster at the size shown, no frame is drawn with missing tiles, and the layout is the same.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/68b949e8-25ee-4210-9f93-c7e17ab15bb8

## Review

An independent adversarial review ran on every head of this rework. What it found and what changed:

- An identity `filter` stand-in leaked into saved projects through Studio's blur slider and broke `backdrop-filter`; a far `perspective` stand-in could still be saved through perspective keyframes and the copy fallback. Both are gone: the runtime writes no inline style.
- Pseudo-elements, mixed hints (`transform, opacity`) and inline style changes could make a dropped hint matter. They are now checked and followed, with tests.
- Re-reading every marked layer on a container change cost about 6 ms and a re-raster per event. Now only the changed element is re-read, and a full pass decides every mark before writing any.
- The browser check's swap-off half was being turned back on by the player's own scale messages, so it compared the swapped page with itself. The test now holds those messages on the host page, asserts the swap is off, and drops the layers that keep their hint before measuring. 20 of 20 runs pass, and mutants for mask, clip-path, blend mode, a clipped 3D child, an identity filter, a near perspective and a missing hold each fail it.
- Accepted and listed under How: the restyle paths that are not followed, and the per-frame cost of following inline styles.

title: fix(cli): recover stale media cache entries
body:
A stale media-cache manifest entry makes `cachePut` report a deduplicated hit even when its cached file or completion marker is missing. Downloading identical content again therefore never restores cross-project reuse. Prompt and entity lookups can also stop at an unusable older entry.

Require a completed, nonempty file before reusing or deduplicating an entry. Re-publish stale entries from the available source, skip unusable prompt/entity matches, and resolve repeated SHA records to the latest record while counting distinct content for prefix ambiguity.

Validation: seven regression cases fail on main. Cache, manifest, candidate, media-home, and resolver suites pass, including 61 resolver and 26 manifest cases. Both source and built media-use commands recover a real WAV and reuse it automatically and by SHA. CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, and hooks passed. Tests use temporary media libraries.

title: fix(cli): select media streams before reading adopted metadata
body:
Media-use reads metadata from the first ffprobe stream. An MP4 with audio before video is therefore cataloged with the AAC codec and no dimensions; cover art can similarly be mistaken for the main stream.

Select the appropriate audio or video stream first, excluding attached pictures. Read dimensions, codec, and fallback duration from that stream, retaining the existing container-duration priority and first-stream fallback.

Validation: five regression cases fail on main. Fourteen probe cases, seven adoption cases, and 61 resolver cases pass. Both source and built media-use report and adopt the correct dimensions for real audio-first and video-first MP4s. CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, and hooks passed.

title: fix(cli): preserve voice placement when ducking empty transcripts
body:
Empty or untimed word lists are removed before audio-duck matches transcripts to voice metadata. A silent first line can therefore place later speech at 0.1s instead of 2.6s, or use the wrong voice ID for explicit offsets.

Preserve one word list per voice. Sequential placement counts empty lines’ durations and gaps; explicit offsets are required only for lines with transcript words. Apply the same correction to the CLI and standalone skill copies.

Validation: six regression cases fail on main. All 42 ducking, cut-list, token, capability, and copy-parity tests pass. Both standalone and built audio-duck commands emit the correct speech spans and volume lanes for sequential and explicit placement. CLI build/typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, hooks, and branch comment checks passed.

title: fix(core): associate GIF delays with their image frames
body:
GIF delays are counted when control extensions are read, rather than when their image frames are parsed. Images without controls get no duration, and a trailing unused control can turn a 0.4s GIF into 2.4s metadata, preventing the producer from filling its clip window.

Associate each delay with its image, normalize missing controls with the existing browser minimum, and consume plain-text controls consistently with the existing disposal walker and [GIF89a graphic-block scoping](https://www.w3.org/Graphics/GIF/spec-gif89a.txt). Comment and application extensions retain the pending control.

Validation: six regression cases fail on main; 50 focused core, producer, and CLI tests pass. Chrome confirms image timing for missing and trailing controls. A real 32px GIF now reports 0.4s and its held transcode fills a 2s clip instead of ending at 0.21s. Core build, core/producer typechecks, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, hooks, and branch comment checks pass.

The real looping transcode remains 1.05s on this FFmpeg version for both the unchanged GIF and the corrected trailing-control fixture; this is an existing encode-timing limitation. Chrome also carries a plain-text control onto an uncontrolled image, whereas this parser consumes it according to GIF89a, as its disposal handling already does.

title: fix(aws-lambda): accept a v2 assemble with no AudioS3Uri, as the CDK stack sends it
body:
## What

A CDK-deployed `HyperframesRenderStack` failed every v2 render at AssembleV2 with `PLAN_PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED`. The v2 assemble event now treats a missing `AudioS3Uri` the same as `null`, and the CDK construct and the SAM template both stop sending it.

## Why

The construct built the AssembleV2 payload with `AudioS3Uri: null`. CDK drops null-valued fields when it renders a Step Functions payload, so the deployed definition had no `AudioS3Uri` key. The handler required `AudioS3Uri === null` for a v2 assemble, so it threw on the missing field. The SAM template kept the literal null, which is why only SAM deployments worked.

## Related work

Fixes #5259

## How

- V2 reads its audio from the plan manifest, so the wire field carries nothing. `AssembleV2Event.AudioS3Uri` is now `?: null` and the handler rejects only a non-null value. `AudioS3Uri: string | null` moves from the shared base onto `AssembleV1Event`, which still uses it.
- The construct and the SAM template no longer send `AudioS3Uri` on AssembleV2, so both deployments put the same payload on the wire. Stacks deployed from an older SAM template still send `null`, which is still accepted.
- New snapshot test: every Lambda task payload in the synthesized CDK definition must equal the matching SAM payload. It checks the deployed definition rather than the construct props, so a dropped or renamed field fails CI. The test fails on the original drift (SAM `"AudioS3Uri": null` vs. no key in CDK).
- New handler test: a v2 assemble that names its own audio URI is still rejected. The existing v2 plan, chunk and assemble round trip now sends no `AudioS3Uri` and still downloads the audio from the manifest.
- The producer's local Lambda regression harness passes `AudioS3Uri` on the v1 branch only.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `bun test src/cdk src/handler.test.ts` in `packages/aws-lambda`, 32 pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: deployed the CDK construct to a scratch AWS account in us-east-1 and ran a 10 s, 30 fps composition with three audio clips, `planProtocol` v2, two chunks:

title: fix(core): seek current dotLottie players by frame

title: fix(core): preserve blocked addresses in mounted import maps

title: fix(engine): extract long video ranges in segments and keep plan uploads flowing
body:
## What

Long videos no longer fail a distributed render's plan step on ffmpeg's process timeout, and planning a long video is about twice as fast:
- The extractor splits any range over two minutes into two-minute segments that run side by side.
- Plan v2 keeps 32 blob uploads in flight instead of uploading in batches of 16.
- The Lambda docs now state the plan step's length bound.

## Why

Plan extracts every frame of a video before any chunk starts.
- **The timeout.** Extraction was one ffmpeg process over the whole range, so a long clip hit `ffmpegProcessTimeout` (300 s by default) however much of Lambda's 15-minute limit was left. That's the `VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED ... ffmpeg_timeout=1` in #5260.
- **The uploads.** Plan then published every frame as a v2 blob, 16 at a time, and each batch waited for its slowest upload. For a 26-minute clip that's 37,448 objects, and the uploads alone took 238 s of the plan step.

## Related work

Fixes #5260. This is the short fix. Having each chunk extract its own frame range would make the plan step independent of video length, but it changes the v2 plan contract shared by Lambda, Cloud Run and other distributed callers, so it's a separate design.

## How

- **Splitting (`extractVideoFramesRange`).** Applies only on the constant-frame-rate sampling path (`sampleCfrAtOutputFps`), and only when the range is longer than one segment. Shorter ranges, VFR sources and final-frame extraction run exactly the same ffmpeg command as before.
  - The split works on an integer frame count, the one `extractionFrameCountForDuration` gives a single pass, so no float-seconds subtraction can produce a near-empty segment. Each segment seeks to `start + firstFrame/fps` and takes exactly its own frames, which continue the frame numbering via `-start_number`. It samples the same absolute times as a single pass, so the frames are byte-identical.
  - Segments run on `cpus/2` workers, and each gets its own `ffmpegProcessTimeout`.
  - The first real failure aborts the rest and is the error reported. A cancel between segments reports cancellation, not a short frame set.
  - `framePathsFromDirectory` still rejects any gap or duplicate.
- **Uploads (`publishPlanV2FromExecutionPlan`).** A 32-slot worker pool replaces the batch loop. On failure it stops taking new blobs, lets in-flight uploads settle, and aborts the publisher, as before.

## Test plan

- [x] **Unit tests.**
  - New: a 130 s range from 0.5 s at 2 fps (one full segment plus 20 frames) returns 260 frames, each from the right source frame, in order. 80.3 s to 200.3 s (`120.00000000000001` s) stays one segment; this case failed on the first head of this PR. Engine extractor suite: 207/207.
  - New: one slow blob upload doesn't stop the other 40 from publishing. It fails on `main`'s batch loop. `planV2.test.ts`: 57/57.
- [x] **Manual testing.** Synthetic 26-minute 576×1024 24 fps H.264 clip (37,440 frames, 391 MB):
  - Locally, one pass vs. the segmented extractor: 0 of 37,440 frames differ.
  - Rendered on a scratch AWS stack (CDK construct, us-east-1, 10,240 MB function, 32 chunks), `main` vs. this branch:

    | | Plan step | Extract + hash | Upload | Total render |
    |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
    | `main` | 395 s | 149 s | 238 s | 12.8 min |
    | this branch | 200 s | 106 s | 85 s | 9.5 min |

    Both renders succeeded with identical output sizes. The stack has been torn down.
- [x] **Docs.** `docs/deploy/aws-lambda.mdx` → Current limits.
- [x] **Comments** follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments", and the comment ratchet passes.

title: perf(producer): extract distributed video frames in each chunk
body:
## What

With plan v2, the Plan step no longer extracts long constant-frame-rate videos. It ships each source once, and every chunk extracts only the frames it shows.

## Why

A distributed render's Plan step extracts every frame of every video before any chunk starts. On Lambda that step has 15 minutes, so video length is capped by how fast one machine can extract and upload frames. #5280 cut the 26-minute case from 395 s to 200 s, but Plan time still grows with video length.

## Related work

Refs #5260. Follows #5280, which split extraction into segments and kept Plan uploads flowing.

## How

- **Engine.** `ExtractionOptions.frameRanges` extracts only some runs of a window's output frames, named as a full extraction names them. It reuses the segment command from #5280, so the frames are byte-identical to a full extraction. `deferRangeExtraction` makes `extractAllVideoFrames` skip eligible windows. For each one it decodes only the last second to get the exact frame count, then returns `deferredRange` with no frames.
- **Plan (v2 only).** Deferred videos record `deferredRange` in `meta/videos.json` with a planDir-relative `sourcePath`. A source the plan already ships under `compiled/` is reused. Downloads and files outside the project go under `video-sources/`. The manifest's `videoDependencyMode` is `source-extract`. A source under `video-sources/` goes only to the chunks that show the video. A source under `compiled/` still goes to every chunk, as it does on `main`, because each chunk's page loads every `<video>` src during init and a missing file fails the chunk.
- **RenderChunk.** For deferred videos, the chunk walks the same frame lookup to find the frames it shows, extracts those runs into a directory beside its work dir, and fails closed if any frame is missing.

The planner still extracts in these cases:
- VFR sources (their CFR resampling phase depends on the seek point).
- Sources that need an HDR transform.
- One-frame held tails.
- Windows of a second or less.
- Windows whose frame count comes out 60% or less of the expected count, where full extraction rewrites the probed duration.

The v1 `plan()` transport is unchanged, because v1 plan directories can be shared read-only between chunks. The in-process renderer is unchanged too.

## Compatibility

This doesn't change the public API. `renderToLambda`, the CLI, the Lambda and Cloud Run events, and the SAM/CDK templates are all the same; only the plan manifest the producer writes and reads changes. A producer older than this rejects a `source-extract` manifest with `PLAN_V2_INTEGRITY_UNRECOVERABLE` before it renders anything, so a mixed-version fleet fails closed instead of rendering blank video. Lambda and Cloud Run deploy one handler for all three steps, so they never mix versions.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (`docs/deploy/aws-lambda.mdx`)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

- Engine: partial ranges at 24 and 60 fps with mid-GOP seeks write byte-identical files to a full extraction, and a deferred window running to the source end reports the full extraction's frame count at 24, 30 and 60 fps.
- Plan v2: a `video-sources/` file goes only to chunks that show the video, a `compiled/` source stays in every chunk, and a `sourcePath` outside the plan directory is rejected.
- RenderChunk: extracts exactly the frames shown, nothing past the clip, wraps loops, and fails closed on a missing source.
- v1 (the planner extracts) vs v2 (chunks extract), rendering every chunk both ways on one host and comparing chunk SHA-256s. Every chunk matched:

  | Project | Deferred videos | Result |
  |---|---|---|
  | speed-ramp (1x to 4x to 0.5x lane) | 1 | match |
  | overlay-montage-prod | 1 | match |
  | sub-composition-video (two clips, one source) | 2 | match |
  | pip-video-late-host | 1 | match |
  | nested-sequential-video-local-start | 0 (sub-second windows) | match |
  | vfr-screen-recording | 0 (VFR stays with the planner) | match |
  | 20 s from minute 11:40 of a 26-minute clip, NTSC 29.97 source with two windows, a loop, a held tail | 5 | match |

  For overlay-montage-prod I also byte-compared every JPEG a chunk extracted against the planner's frames, and all 318 were identical.
- Lambda, on a scratch stack in a test account (10,240 MB function, 576x1024 24 fps H.264):

  | Clip | Plan step | Whole render | Cost |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 26 min, before #5280 | 395 s | 12.8 min | |
  | 26 min, with #5280 | 200 s | 9.5 min | $0.93 |
  | 26 min, this PR | 20 s | 6.3 min | $0.90 |
  | 60 min, this PR, 32 chunks | 41 s | 8.3 min | $2.14 |

  The 26-minute output is the same size to the byte as the #5280 run (658,159,984 bytes). The 60-minute output has exactly 86,400 frames and lasts 3600.000 s, and sampled frames line up with the source at the right timestamps.

## Notes

- Each chunk downloads the whole source of every deferred video it shows. Reading only the byte ranges a chunk needs would cut that and is left for a follow-up.
- On one host, a chunk render occasionally differs from a rerun of itself by a few pixel values (about 80 dB PSNR). It happens most often on the first render in a process, and it happens with v1 alone. When that happened, re-rendering both sides gave matching hashes.
- A chunk must still finish inside Lambda's 15 minutes. Long renders should raise `--max-parallel-chunks`; the docs bullet now says so.

title: fix(cli): preserve portrait orientation during background removal
body:
## What

Preserve the displayed portrait dimensions when `remove-background` processes phone videos carrying a 90° or 270° rotation. A video stored as 96×64 but displayed as 64×96 now stays 64×96 through inference and the encoder instead of having its decoded rows reshaped into a scrambled 96×64 frame.

## Why

FFmpeg applies the input display matrix while decoding. The raw RGB pipe has no dimension header, and the background-removal pipeline reads it using the engine's stored stream dimensions. A quarter-turn preserves the byte count, so processing succeeds despite the incorrect row width.

## Related work

The background-removal command and dual-output contract were introduced in #612 and #637. This follows the accepted BT.709 correction in #5278 without changing its color conversion or the shared engine metadata API. Checked all 126 open PRs before committing; none changes the background-removal implementation. No separate issue is required for this self-contained correction.

## How

Read the first video stream's rotation using a bounded, asynchronous FFprobe call. Prefer its display matrix over a legacy `rotate` tag and swap width/height for quarter-turns using FFmpeg's one-degree transpose tolerance. Keep FFmpeg's autorotation enabled so the actual pixels are upright. Still images use the existing path. The probe uses the existing process helper, a 30-second timeout, and a 256 KiB output bound.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: six rotation regressions fail on main, with six passing controls. All 59 focused pipeline, inference, and manager tests pass; the final test fixture cleanup also passes all 14 rotation/output tests. Coverage includes both quarter-turn directions, legacy tags, conflicting tags, no rotation, 180°, 45°, and still images.
- [x] Manual verification: generated a valid five-frame 96×64 H.264 MP4 and a copy with a 90° display matrix. Real FFmpeg decoding reports 64×96. The main pipeline outputs a scrambled 96×64 ProRes file; fixed source and built pipeline output 64×96. Both keep all five frames. Their decoded RGB matches the upright input with maximum error 1/255. The unrotated control remains 96×64 with maximum error 2/255. These pipeline probes substitute only inference with a fixture alpha mask; they do not claim a full ONNX segmentation run.
- [x] Fresh workspace build, rebuilt CLI, CLI typecheck, repository lint (4,177 files), formatting, changed-file lint, and test reachability pass. Normal commit hooks pass. Fallow reports no introduced findings and excludes one inherited duplicate in existing test fixtures.
- [x] Documentation: no public command or option changes.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md and explain why raw frame sizing must follow the display matrix.

title: fix(lint): reject parser-invalid variable defaults
body:
## What

Reject composition variable declarations whose defaults or enum options the existing parser cannot accept.

## Why

`parseCompositionVariables` discards a number variable with `"default": "3"`, but `hyperframes lint` currently reports no declaration error. The same mismatch affects boolean and string-valued defaults, and enum declarations without an options array. A composition can pass lint while its variable disappears from the parsed metadata consumed by the editor and SDK.

## Related work

This is a small correction to the existing declaration rule. I checked all 127 current open PRs by changed path and relevant all-state searches. #4931 and #4933 also edit the composition lint files for chapter markers and crop packs; neither changes variable validation. #4391 concerns declaration placement, which current main already checks. This PR retains that behavior and does not attempt to implement those scopes.

## How

title: fix(cli): preserve authored clip length when moving
body:
## What

Preserve an end-authored clip's resolved length when moving it with the timeline CLI.

## Why

The timeline reader supports older clips with `data-start` and `data-end`. The move command checked bounds and overlaps using the original length but only changed the start attribute. A two-second clip at 1–3 seconds moved to 2 seconds became one second long; moving a two-second clip at 4–6 seconds to 1 second made it five seconds long. The same incorrect result appeared in `--plan`.

## Related work

This is a small correction to the existing timeline move command introduced in #4221. Open #5279 concerns atomic batch undo receipts; its implementation is independent, although both PRs append CLI regressions to the same test file.

## How

For a clip with an authored duration, write its already resolved duration and remove the derived/legacy end attribute alongside the new start. This follows the existing canonical timing writer's contract. Clips whose duration comes from natural media length or an image default retain their unauthored duration.

## Test plan

- [x] Eight public CLI regressions added: forward/backward end-authored moves and duration-authored/default-image controls, each in applied and planned modes. Four assertions fail before the fix; all 49 timeline cases pass afterward. Applied results are reinspected from persisted source, and planned source bytes remain unchanged.
- [x] Built package CLI under Node 22.19.0: four independent forward/backward applied/planned cases reproduce the original duration change and preserve two seconds afterward.
- [x] Frozen Bun 1.4.2 install, full workspace build, CLI rebuild/typecheck, formatting/lint, test reachability, comment checks, and normal signed commit hooks pass. No comments were added.
- Documentation: the existing canonical timing contract remains applicable.

The full CLI suite reports **4594 passed, 6 failed, 49 skipped** out of 4649 collected tests. An unchanged-production comparison with the same tests and environment reports **4590 passed, 10 failed, 49 skipped**, including the four timing regressions. Five exact failures match between runs: the history held-lock test, the atomic file watcher test, and three Sherpa installation tests. The sixth failure is in the unchanged real-filesystem watcher module: the new-directory case fails after the fix, while the manifest-write case fails in the comparison. That module has no dependency on the changed timeline helper. The full CLI suite is not reported as passing.

Validation covers CLI timing and persistence on macOS. Hosted upstream CI and maintainer review remain outstanding.

title: fix(cli): preserve CSS priority during full-page capture
body:
## What

Respect CSS priority while temporarily neutralizing fixed and sticky elements for website capture's full-page screenshot, then restore their original inline declaration.

## Why

With `position: fixed !important` in a stylesheet, assigning an ordinary inline `position: static` leaves the header fixed in `full-page.png`. An inline `position: fixed !important` also loses its priority when capture restores just its value. If the stylesheet contains `position: relative !important`, that header moves into document flow and disappears from the viewport before subsequent asset and HTML extraction.

## Related work

#2892 established the full-page plate and its temporary position override. #5171 added screenshot limits and interruption reporting. Open #4949 addresses consent-triggered navigation in `captureScrollScreenshots`; this change is confined to `captureFullPagePlate` and its CSS restoration. No existing implementation of the priority correction was found.

## How

Save the inline position's priority alongside its value, override with `position: static !important` for the plate, and restore both in the existing cleanup path. Remove both temporary markers afterward. The helper's page type lists the two methods it actually uses, allowing the tests to exercise the complete browser expressions without a page type assertion.

## Test plan

- [x] Eight regression/control cases execute the real browser expressions against a CSS DOM: important stylesheet and inline fixed/sticky rules, restoration after screenshot failure, height omission and exhausted budget, plus ordinary-position and untouched-element controls. Seven fail on current main; 26 controls pass across the initial three-file run.
- [x] All 37 tests pass across screenshot capture, degradation, core extraction and post-extraction handling.
- [x] Chrome 152 reproduces both failures on current main. Fixed source and the built CLI function neutralize the header during capture and restore the original computed style, priority and viewport pixels afterward. An ordinary sticky control also remains unchanged.
- [x] Full workspace build, CLI rebuild and typecheck, root lint, changed-file lint/format and test reachability pass.

title: fix(core): preview stops at the film's end when a scene loops forever
body:
## What changes for a user

When a scene has a GSAP tween on `repeat: -1` and the root declares no `data-duration`, Studio preview played past the end of the film. The counter read `00:08 / 00:06`, the picture went blank, the button stayed on Pause and Play could not replay the film. Now preview stops at the last frame like any other film, and Play starts again from 0.

Render was already right (6.0 s output on the same fixture). Only preview was wrong.

## Why

`resolveCompositionLengthSeconds` takes the longest of the timeline, the floors (sub-composition ends, media) and the fallback. GSAP reports about 1e10 s for a timeline that holds an infinite repeat, so the transport clock's end was 1e10 s. Studio's player paused at the real 6 s, but the runtime kept playing, so the two disagreed and the preview showed time past the end.

`timeline.ts` already treats a root timeline of `LOOP_INFLATED_TIMELINE_SECONDS` (7200 s) or longer as loop-inflated and uses the finite window instead. The clock length now follows the same rule: a loop-inflated timeline gives way to a floor or fallback when one exists. With neither, it keeps the timeline length, as before.

`hyperframes lint` already flags `repeat: -1` without a root `data-duration` (`gsap_infinite_repeat`). This change makes preview agree with render when the author leaves it in.

7200 s is also the length Studio's player rejects as loop-inflated (`sanitizeDurationSeconds`); Studio now reads the same `LOOP_INFLATED_TIMELINE_SECONDS` instead of its own literal, so the two cannot drift. The constant now lives in `compositionLength.ts` (`timeline.ts` and `init.ts` import it), so the published `runtime/composition-length` entry does not load `timeline.ts`.

## Limits

- A sub-composition host with no declared length whose own timeline loops forever is itself an endless floor, so preview stays endless there. Studio's clip list has the same limit. `hyperframes lint` already reports `repeat: -1` without a root `data-duration`.
- With no root `data-duration`, finite root animation that runs past the last floor is cut at the floor (a 20 s tween plus a looping tween and a 6 s scene gives 6 s). This is deliberate. The other option was the loop-free end (`__hf.animationEnd`, 20 s there). Cutting at the floor keeps one rule for the film's length: Studio's clip list already ends the film at the last floor, so the transport and the clip list cannot disagree. A second rule would only serve a film the linter already flags: `gsap_infinite_repeat` tells the author to set a root `data-duration` whenever `repeat: -1` is used, and that declared length always wins.
- Render reads the same clock, so a real root timeline of 2 hours or more, with no `data-duration` and a shorter floor, would now preview and render at the floor. A root `data-duration` avoids it.
- The clip list's rule (`timeline.ts`) and this one count slightly different floors (this one also counts adapter-inferred lengths).

## Tests

Standalone on purpose: one root in the runtime clock, no other open change touches it.


- `compositionLength.test.ts`: a floor or fallback wins over an endless timeline; with neither the timeline length stays; the boundary sits at exactly 7200 s. Exit 0, 23 passed, three runs in a row.
- `init.compositionLength.test.ts`: the running runtime reports 6 s for a root timeline at GSAP's endless length with a 2 s + 4 s scene. Exit 0, 11 passed, three runs in a row.
- Mutations: with the fix reverted the runtime test fails (10000000002 instead of 6), and so do two `compositionLength.test.ts` cases; `>=` to `>` fails the boundary test (7200 instead of 6).
- `timeline.test.ts`: exit 0, 71 passed. Studio: `timelineSyncHydration.test.ts` exit 0, 6 passed; `useTimelineSyncCallbacks.test.ts` exit 0, 17 passed; Studio `tsc --noEmit` clean. oxfmt, oxlint and `tsc --noEmit` for core are clean.
- Walked in Studio preview, headless, on a fixture built for this: a 2 s intro, then a 4 s scene with a yoyo `repeat: -1` tween. Play from 4 s through the end, then press Play again.

## Before

Preview runs past the end (`00:08 / 00:06`), blank picture, the button stays on Pause.

![Before: preview runs past the end, 00:08 / 00:06, blank](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a103eb12-599b-483e-8a9b-ec31e870ef62)

## After

Preview stops on the last frame at `00:06 / 00:06` and Play replays from 0.

![After: preview stops at 00:06 / 00:06 on the last frame](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/050c9644-071e-4886-ad4e-8a45467514c3)
