title: [Windows] `browser ensure` prints "Ready to render" but leaves no binary; `render` then retries the browser check for ~20 min before failing
body:
## Summary

On Windows 10, `npx hyperframes browser ensure` downloads the Chrome headless shell, prints `— Ready to render.` and exits **0** — but the executable at the path it just reported does not exist. A subsequent `hyperframes render` then keeps re-checking the browser for **1201.6 s (~20 min)** before failing with `Chrome not found`.

The user-visible result: a missing binary looks like a hang, and the fix command the error tells you to run reports success while changing nothing.

## Environment

- Windows 10 Pro 22H2 (10.0.19045), AMD64
- `hyperframes@0.8.143` via `npx`
- node v22.22.2
- Cache root: `C:\Users\<user>\.cache\hyperframes`
- The machine routes npx through a local HTTP/HTTPS proxy (`127.0.0.1:7897`) — noted for completeness; the command reported success either way

## Expected path

```
C:\Users\<user>\.cache\hyperframes\chrome\chrome-headless-shell\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\chrome-headless-shell.exe
```

## Observed — `browser ensure`

Full output (progress line collapsed):

```
T  hyperframes browser ensure
|
[browser] Cached binary missing at C:\...\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\chrome-headless-shell.exe — re-downloading...

   Source:  download
   Path:    C:\...\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\chrome-headless-shell.exe
|
—  Ready to render.
```

Exit code 0. Checked immediately afterwards:

- the path above **does not exist**
- `...\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\` is **empty**
- no `.zip`, and no `.chrome.install.lock`, remain anywhere under `.cache\hyperframes`
- ~114 MB were downloaded; 0 bytes were retained in the cache

## Observed — `render`

```
✗  Chrome not found
   Chrome binary not found at "C:\...\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\chrome-headless-shell.exe".
   Run: npx hyperframes browser ensure
```

`elapsed = 1201.6 s`, exit code 1. Essentially all of that time is spent repeating the browser check, not rendering.

## Workaround (confirmed working)

Copying a `chrome-headless-shell` distribution that already exists on the machine (Playwright's) into the exact directory `hyperframes` expects:

```
%LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright\chromium_headless_shell-<rev>\chrome-headless-shell-win64\*
  ->  C:\Users\<user>\.cache\hyperframes\chrome\chrome-headless-shell\win64-152.0.7977.30\chrome-headless-shell-win64\
```

The version mismatch (151.x vs the expected 152.0.7977.30) made no difference — the next render succeeded:

| item | value |
|---|---|
| output | 6 s, 1920x1080, 30 fps, 282.6 KB MP4 |
| end-to-end | 67.3 s (prepare 14.7 / capture 30.4 / encode 1.6 / mux 0.5) |
| per-frame | ~0.27 s with 4 workers |

So the rest of the Windows toolchain is fine; only the provisioning step is broken.

## Relationship to #2103

Same class of failure: the extractor step reports success while leaving no binary behind. In #2103 (macOS) it hung; here it returns 0 and prints `Ready to render`. #2103 was closed by #2104 (a `@puppeteer/browsers` bump), so either the Windows path is unaffected by that fix, or there is a second path where a failed/partial extract is indistinguishable from success.

## Suggested fixes

1. **Verify before claiming success**: after extraction, assert the expected executable exists and is non-zero; otherwise fail loudly instead of printing `Ready to render`.
2. **Don't swallow the underlying error**: surface the download/extract error (and the source URL + extract target) in the failure message so it can be diagnosed locally.
3. **Make `render` fail fast** when the binary is missing. Retrying the browser check for 20 minutes turns a missing file into something that looks like a hang.
4. **Re-extract, not just re-download**, when the cache entry exists but the binary is absent — that is the state `browser ensure` leaves the user in here.

title: feat(cli): models list shows which speech models transcribe can use
body:
## What changes for a user

`hyperframes models list` now shows the speech models `transcribe` can use, and `--json` prints them as one result. Before, `models` only knew `install parakeet`, so `models list` and `models list --json` stopped at the argument parser with `Missing required positional argument: NAME`. Agents ask for this command on their own when they want to know whether transcription will run locally.

```
$ hyperframes models list
parakeet parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3  Parakeet needs glibc 2.32 or newer; this system has glibc 2.31.
whisper  small                 installed
whisper  small.en              installed
whisper  tiny                  installed

$ hyperframes models list --json
{"ok":true,"models":[{"engine":"parakeet","model":"parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3","installed":false,"path":"…/parakeet/parakeet-tdt-0.6b-v3-int8","unsupported":"Parakeet needs glibc 2.32 or newer; this system has glibc 2.31."},{"engine":"whisper","model":"small","installed":true,"path":"…/whisper/models/ggml-small.bin"}, …]}
```

## How it decides

- **Parakeet** is `installed` exactly when `transcribe` would run it: the CLI's own sherpa-onnx runtime with the pinned model, or else `parakeet-mlx`. Both commands now ask one function for that (`whisper/parakeetRunner.ts`; `transcribe`'s `pickRunner` uses it too), and the row says which in `runner`. When the system cannot run it, the row carries the reason in `unsupported`. It is always listed, so a caller learns it exists and how to get it.
- **Whisper** lists each `ggml-<model>.bin` already downloaded into the whisper models folder, by the name `--model` takes. The new `listWhisperModels` helper sits beside `ensureModel` in `whisper/manager.ts`, which owns that folder. Partial or sidecar files (`.part`, `.verified`) and dangling links (which `ensureModel` would download again) are not listed.
- The JSON keeps the `{ ok, ... }` shape of `models install --json`.
- `models install` with no name, or an unknown action, still fails with exit 1 and now names both commands.

## Tests

- `commands/models.test.ts` runs `list --json` through citty's own parser (`runCommand`), where the old failure happened, and checks the unsupported-system row and the parakeet-mlx row. Exit 0, 10 passed, three runs in a row. `transcribe.test.ts` (34) and `parakeet.test.ts` (15) still pass on the shared runner check.
- `whisper/manager.list.test.ts`: no folder lists nothing; only `ggml-*.bin` files are listed; a dangling link is skipped (skipped on Windows like the repo's other symlink tests, since creating a link there can need extra rights). Exit 0, 3 passed, three runs in a row.
- Mutations: `models.ts` from main fails all three list tests with `Missing required positional argument: NAME`; an unanchored file pattern fails the listing test; dropping the unsupported guard fails the unsupported-system test; dropping the parakeet-mlx branch fails the list test and two transcribe tests; dropping the link check fails the dangling-link test; showing `unsupported` on an installed row fails the parakeet-mlx test.
- `tsc --noEmit` for the CLI, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- Ran the command from source on a Linux box: `models list --json` exits 0; `models install` (no name) and `models bogus --json` exit 1.

## Known edges

- If the whisper models path is a file rather than a folder, `models list` fails with the filesystem error instead of a JSON result.
- Whisper rows mean the model file is there; transcribe installs whisper-cpp itself on first use.
- `models list extra` ignores the extra word, as citty does for other commands.
- A Parakeet row that is not installed still names `path`: that is where `models install parakeet` puts it.

title: fix(cli): browser ensure fails when the unzip leaves no Chrome executable
body:
Fixes #5322.

## What changes for the user

- `hyperframes browser ensure` no longer says "Ready to render" when the Chrome executable it names was never written. It exits 1 and says why, including any errors the unzip tools reported.
- `hyperframes render` goes through the same install step, so it stops at "Checking browser..." with that reason instead of carrying a missing path into lint and the preflight check. Its setup worker now reports a failure as one error line that the parent reads, so the reason shows as one message instead of a Node crash dump; warnings the worker printed before failing are still shown.
- `browser ensure` exits after a failure. Before, a failed `ensure` (any failure, a network error too) printed its error and then never exited, because its spinner was never stopped. `browser ensure --force` had the same hang even on success.
- Studio renders and `doctor` show the install error as the Chrome check's detail instead of a generic "Chrome Headless Shell is required".

## Root cause

- `ensureBrowser` installs through `@puppeteer/browsers` `install()` into a staging folder, then moves it into the cache. `install()` unzips and returns the executable path **without checking the file exists**. Its only such check is for a folder left over from an earlier install. Still true in 3.2.4, the latest release.
- On Windows the unzip runs `System32\tar.exe`, then PowerShell `Expand-Archive`, then `pwsh`. A tool that fails is only written to a debug log and the next one is tried, so a failed unzip can end as a "success" with nothing written.
- We trusted that path. `downloadBrowser` now checks that the executable exists and is not empty before the install replaces anything in the cache, and passes a logger to `install()` so the swallowed unzip errors appear in the message (`NODE_DEBUG=puppeteer:browsers:*` output is still forwarded).

The reported state matches an unzip that wrote nothing. The Windows archive for 152.0.7977.30 is 119,527,247 bytes (114.0 MB, the size the report saw downloaded), and it has no folder entries. So an empty `chrome-headless-shell-win64` folder can only come from an unzip that created the parent of its first file, then wrote no files.

## The ~20 minutes in `render`

There is no retry loop on render's browser path, and no timeout anywhere in that chain, ours or `@puppeteer/browsers'`. So the 1201.6 s was work, not a wait. With the cache folder present but empty, each `render` re-downloads the 114 MB archive and unzips it once, gets the same false success, then fails later in preflight. Now it fails right after that one attempt, with the reason. Render still makes one install attempt per run when the cache is broken; that is how render provisions Chrome.

## Not verified (needs a Windows machine)

- Which unzip tool ran on the reporter's machine, and what it printed.
- How the 1201.6 s split between download and unzip.
- Whether antivirus was involved.

The next report from a machine like this will carry the unzip tools' own errors in the message.

## Also changed

`browser ensure --force` with `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` set reports "Browser found" (source `env`) and no longer records an install; it used to say "Download complete" without downloading.

## Verification

Real CLI on macOS at this head, each run with a fresh `HOME`, under a 400 s alarm so a hang shows as exit 142. The broken unzip is an `unzip` on `PATH` that exits 0 after creating only the top folder, the same state as the report:

| run | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `browser ensure`, broken unzip | "Ready to render.", exit 0, folder empty | exit 1 in 13 s: `Failed to install chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30: the archive downloaded, but .../chrome-headless-shell is missing after unzipping.` |
| `browser ensure --force`, real unzip | prints "Ready to render." then never exits (killed at 400 s) | exit 0 in 12 s |
| `browser ensure`, real unzip | | exit 0 in 15 s, 166 MB executable in place |
| `render`, broken unzip | (per the report: preflight "Chrome not found" after the re-download) | exit 1 in 13 s at the browser step, the reason and the `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` hint, no stack trace |

Tests, each file alone, 3 runs in a row, all green. Each new or repaired test was checked by breaking the code and watching only that test go red:

- `browser/manager.test.ts` (55): executable missing / 0 bytes (red on `main`); unzip errors from only the last attempt (red without the per-attempt reset); the existing rollback test now reaches the rollback again (red without the restore line).
- `commands/browser.test.ts` (4, new): every spinner stopped on failure and success, with and without `--force` (3 of 4 red on `main`).
- `renderSetupWorker.test.ts` (10) and `utils/cancellableProcess.test.ts` (2): the real worker in an unknown mode makes the parent reject with exactly its one-line reason (red when the parent ignores the error line); the reason survives the crash output around it, a cut-off or empty line falls back to the raw output, and earlier worker output is kept (red when it is dropped).
- `browser/preflight.test.ts` (25): the Chrome check keeps the thrown reason as its detail (red without it).

## Review

Independent adversarial review at this head: no blocking findings, no should-fix findings. Earlier rounds found that the new check made the existing rollback test skip the rollback, that the setup worker's error line needed tolerant parsing and had to keep earlier output, and that the Studio/doctor reason and the error wording needed work. All of those are fixed above, each with a test shown to fail without its fix.

Notes left open on purpose:
- The same "spinner still running, process never exits" pattern exists in `play`, `present` and embedded `preview` when their port lookup fails. Fixing it for every command means changing how the CLI exits after a failure, which is broader than this PR.
- No test pins the install-telemetry change (an install is recorded only when a download happened), or the parent forwarding earlier worker output (checked on a real run instead).
- An error with an empty message still shows the raw crash output, on purpose: there is no reason to show instead.

title: fix(lint): check passes valid sub-compositions and scene-relative asset paths
body:
## What changes for a user

`hyperframes check` stops failing valid sub-compositions in two ways that sent authors in circles:

- **A scene without its own size.** A sub-composition whose root has no `data-width`/`data-height` got `root_missing_dimensions` (an error), and the error stopped `check` before its browser audits. A mounted sub-composition without a size fills its host at 100% (`compositionLoader` sizes the flattened root to `100%` when it declares none), and the core skill tells sub-composition roots to use 100%. The rule now applies to the entry composition only, as its own fix hint already says. Sub-compositions are found the same way `root_dimensions_mismatch` already exempts them (`isSubComposition`).
- **A scene whose `<html>` carries its variables.** With `<html data-composition-variables=…>` around a `<template>`, the linter took `<html>` itself as the composition root and reported `root_missing_composition_id` and `root_missing_dimensions` against it. A `<html>` or `<head>` with no composition markers is now skipped when looking for the root, the same exemption a marker-less leading `<svg>` already gets, so the template's real root is found.
- **`../assets/…` in a scene.** The bundled guides write sub-composition asset paths relative to the scene file (`../assets/logo.png` from `compositions/scene.html`), and `invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path` rejected every `../` path as an error. The bundler, the producer and the preview runtime all resolve such a path from the scene's own folder (`rewriteSubCompPaths`), and project lint's missing-asset check already does too. Studio preview on the current release loads `../assets/a.png` from a scene (checked: the image is rewritten to `assets/a.png` and decodes, no failed request). The rule now flags only a `../` path that still leaves the project once resolved from the file's folder, e.g. `../../x.png` from `compositions/scene.html`, or any `../` from the root `index.html`.

- **`..\assets\x.png` in a scene.** The bundler and Studio preview rewrite a scene's `../` paths when inlining it into the root document, but only recognised `/` as a separator. A path written with backslashes was left as written, so preview resolved it against its own URL and 404'd, while render clamped it and loaded the file. `rewriteAssetPath` now reads a written `\` as `/` before decoding, so both load it. As in a browser, an encoded `%5C` stays part of the file name and a path starting with `\` stays absolute.

## How

- `HyperframeLinterOptions` gains `compSrcPath`, the file's project-relative path, the same name project lint already uses for it. `lintProject` passes it for the entry and every `compositions/` file; Studio's lint route passes the file it lints.
- The traversal rule walks each `../` path's segments from that folder and flags it only if it climbs above the project root. It is a plain segment walk, not `node:path`, because the rule also ships in `@hyperframes/lint/browser`. Without `compSrcPath` it treats the file as the project root, which keeps the old answer for callers that lint a single loose file.
- A linked stylesheet's `url()`s resolve from the stylesheet's own folder, as the browser and the bundler resolve them. `lintProject` now hands each linked stylesheet's project-relative path to the rule. Before, `url('../fonts/B.woff2')` in `styles/main.css` linked from `index.html` was a false error, and a real escape in a stylesheet linked from a nested scene could pass.
- Every relative path is walked, not only ones that start with `../`. Backslashes, `%2f` and `%2e` are normalised and entities decoded first (render decodes `%2f` into a separator), and the query and hash are dropped, so `%2e%2e/x.png`, `..\x.png`, `assets/../../x.png` and `../x.png` all count as climbing out. URLs with a scheme, absolute paths and fragments are skipped.
- The file's folder depth comes from a `..`-aware walk; an absolute or unnormalised path (`sub/../index.html`) counts as the project root, as before this change.
- The message now says what happens: render and preview clamp such a path to the project root or resolve it outside it, so it loads a different file than written, or none.
- The producer's lint passes its entry file as `compSrcPath`, so a nested entry gets the same answer there as in `hyperframes lint`.
- `browser.test.ts` now walks the browser entry's imports, including `@hyperframes/parsers` subpaths, and fails on any Node built-in. The `platform: "browser"` build cannot catch those, because the parsers package stays external.
- `findRootTag` shares one `hasCompositionMarker` check for `<body>`, `<svg>` and now `<html>`/`<head>`.

## Tests

- `rules/core.test.ts`: a template sub-composition without a size reports no `root_missing_dimensions`; `<html>` with variables around a `<template>` finds the real root.
- `rules/composition.test.ts`: the traversal tests now state the contract: `../` from the root file errors; `../assets/` from `compositions/scene.html` passes and `../../assets/` errors; from `compositions/frames/scene.html`, `../../assets/` passes and `../../../` errors. A path that dips out midway (`../assets/../../x.png`) and a `./`-prefixed file path also error.
- `browser.test.ts`: the browser entry reaches no Node built-in, including through dynamic `import()` and bare names like `path`. Re-adding a `node:path` helper to the rule fails it.
- `rules/composition.test.ts` also covers climbs written encoded, backslashed, mid-path or entity-encoded (from the root file and from a scene), absolute and `..`-containing file paths (a leading `..` never counts below the root), an encoded `%2f` climb, skipped URLs, a query or hash that would climb if read as a path, and a file linted without `compSrcPath` (treated as the project root).
- `studio-server` `routes/lint.test.ts`: the lint route passes the file it lints as `compSrcPath`.
- `project.test.ts`: a stylesheet linked from `index.html` with `url('../fonts/…')` passes; a stylesheet linked from a scene with `url('../../outside.png')` is reported.
- `project.test.ts`: through `lintProject`, a scene's `../assets/logo.png` passes while `../../outside.png` is reported, and a scene without a size does not get `root_missing_dimensions`.
- Lint's six touched test files together, three runs in a row: 471 passed each time. `tsc --noEmit` clean for lint, cli, studio-server and producer; comment ratchet clean.
- Mutations: dropping the sub-composition exemption fails one core test and one project test; keeping `<html>` as a root candidate fails the `<html>`-variables test; ignoring the file's folder fails two traversal tests and one project test; resolving stylesheets from the HTML file's folder, skipping the `%2e`/backslash normalisation, reading the query as path, dropping the normalisation, the entity decoding, the absolute-path rule, the `..`-aware depth, or the skip for URLs each fail at least one test; dropping `compSrcPath` from project lint fails the project test.
- `parsers` `rewriteSubCompPaths.test.ts`: `..\assets\x.png` from `compositions/scene.html` rewrites to `assets/x.png` (fails without the change); `a%5Cb.png` keeps its encoded backslash and `\x.png` is left alone (each fails if the swap moves after decoding or the leading-slash skip goes). 15 passed, three runs; core `inlineSubCompositions` and `htmlBundler` tests 202 passed.

## Before

`hyperframes lint` on 0.8.143, three small projects (a scene without a size, a scene with variables on `<html>` around its `<template>`, a scene using `../assets/a.png`):

```
compositions/s2.html  error root_missing_dimensions
compositions/s6.html  error root_missing_composition_id
compositions/s6.html  error root_missing_dimensions
compositions/s5.html  error invalid_parent_traversal_in_asset_path
```

## After

The same projects on this branch: none of these findings. A path that really leaves the project (`../../outside.png` from `compositions/`) is still an error.

## Not changed here

Studio's lint route treats every HTML file outside the project graph (such as `scenes/intro.html`) as a sub-composition, so such a file no longer gets `root_missing_dimensions` there. That labelling predates this change and its test pins it, so it stays.

Two older copies of the sub-composition path rewrite still read only `/`: the runtime loader's fallback for scenes loaded at runtime (`core/src/runtime/compositionLoader.ts`) and Studio's copy-to-clipboard (`studio/src/utils/authoredSource.ts`). Neither is the path preview or render takes for bundled scenes; they are left for a follow-up.

title: fix(studio-server): the preview's proxy copy jumps queued thumbnails, and abandoned copies drop
body:
## What changes

`resolveProxy` (the `./proxy-transcoder` export of `@hyperframes/studio-server`) takes a new optional argument, `{ priority?: boolean; signal?: AbortSignal }`:

- **`priority`** puts the copy ahead of every normal queued copy, and a priority ask is never refused because the queue is full. If the same clip is already queued as a normal copy, a priority ask moves that queued copy forward instead of starting a second one.
- **`signal`** lets a caller stop waiting. The copy is dropped only when it has not started yet and no caller is left waiting for it. A copy that has started is never stopped for a caller that leaves, and a caller without a signal always keeps its copy.

Callers that pass neither get the same results and errors as before, and a refused ask still moves the activity mark Studio's thumbnails use to decide whether a capture is safe to keep. That includes Studio's own preview route: it serves both the visible preview and thumbnail capture pages, and it cannot tell them apart, so giving it priority would let capture copies crowd the lane and push every other ask out. Priority is for a caller that knows which copy is on screen, such as an app embedding the preview.

## Why

The transcoder runs 2 copies at a time with 8 queued, first come first served. A screen that asks for a copy of every clip for thumbnails fills that queue, so the copy the timeline preview needs waits behind all of them, or is refused with `ProxyCapacityError` when the queue is full. A thumbnail that has scrolled out of view still holds its queued place. Repro: 12 clips of 20 s 1080p ProRes 422, 11 thumbnail asks, then the preview's ask; the preview's copy was refused at about 20 ms while the thumbnails took about 50 s.

## How

One wait queue of jobs replaces the queue of callbacks. Each job is the one shared copy for a cache key and counts the callers still waiting for it; a caller without a signal never leaves, so its copy is always made. Priority jobs are inserted before the first normal job. When the last caller leaves a job that is still queued, the job leaves the queue and the in-flight map at once, so an ask for the same clip in the same moment starts a fresh copy, and its promise rejects with an internal error that is not remembered as a failure. A full queue now refuses a normal ask before anything is registered, so a priority ask for the same clip in the same moment is still accepted. The same shape (one shared entry per key, a lease per caller, drop on the last lease) already exists for thumbnails in `routes/thumbnailGenerationCoordinator.ts`; that one also stops started work, which a proxy copy must not. The module's existing rule stands: a started ffmpeg child is never killed on a caller's behalf.

Priority asks can push the queue past its cap. That is deliberate: they are the copies a viewer is waiting on, and there are few of them.

## Verification

`packages/studio-server/src/helpers/proxyTranscoder.test.ts`, 37 tests, 3 runs in a row, all green, no timers (fake ffmpeg spawn, real temp files). New cases, each shown to fail when its behaviour is removed:

- a priority copy starts before queued copies and is accepted when the queue is full (red when the queue ignores priority, and when priority is refused at the cap)
- a priority ask moves an already queued copy forward (red without the promotion)
- a queued copy whose only caller left is dropped and not remembered as a failure (red when copies are never dropped)
- a shared queued copy stays while another caller, with or without a signal, still waits (red when a caller without a signal is ignored)
- a caller leaving a started copy does not stop it
- an ask in the same moment the last caller leaves gets a fresh copy (red when the dropped copy stays registered)
- a priority ask in the same moment a normal ask for that clip was refused is accepted (red when priority is refused at the cap)
- a dropped copy that settles after its replacement started removes only its own entry, so a later ask joins the replacement instead of starting a second ffmpeg for the same clip (red when settling deletes whatever entry is there)
- an ask refused while another project fills the queue still moves that project's activity mark, so a thumbnail captured meanwhile is not kept, and the next ask once there is room makes the copy (red when the refusal skips the mark)

title: feat(registry): seven more WebGPU shader backgrounds, from sun burst to color wheel
body:
## What

Seven more 2-second WebGPU background blocks from the MIT [Shaders](https://shaders.com) library (`shaders@4.0.0`), used with their default settings: **Sun Burst**, **Spiral**, **Plastic**, **Chrome Orb**, **Hologram**, **Heatmap** and **Color Wheel**. Same shape as #5191's blocks: tagged `webgpu` and `webgpu-shader`, `data-requires-webgpu`, preview video, no poster.

## How

- Each block is `godrays.html` with its composition id and `data-shader` changed, and a `registry-item.json` with its own name, title, description, tags and preview.
- `lib/` holds byte copies of the shared bundle and its licence file from #5191; this PR does not change the bundle.
- The `Chrome` shader's block is `chrome-orb`: `.gitignore` ignores every folder named `chrome/` (Chrome for Testing downloads), so a block folder by that name could never be committed.

## Verification

- **Seek order and motion.** For all seven, t = 1.5 s is pixel-identical when reached from 0, from 1.9 s, or in steps, and frames at 1.0 and 1.75 s differ.
- **`hyperframes check`** passes on each block.
- **Previews.** `hyperframes render` of each block on a GPU at 24 fps, encoded like `scripts/generate-catalog-previews.ts` (1280 wide, H.264 CRF 28), uploaded to the docs CDN under new names; each URL serves the uploaded bytes.
- Every bundle copy matches the shared one, every `data-shader` names a shader in it, and every block installs the licence file (the checks `registryBlocks.test.ts` runs in CI). `oxfmt --check` passes. The PR changes only the seven block folders.

## Limits

Same as #5138: one shader block per page, the shader runs on the film's time, and a host without a GPU renders these only with the software WebGPU opt-in. Plastic moves slowly with its default settings: its surface ripples, but it reads close to a still orb.

title: fix(cli): recognize painted ancestor text backgrounds
body:
Older Chromium can paint ordinary nested text through an ancestor's `background-clip: text` while dropping descendants that paint independently. Accept ordinary children and keep missing layered text reportable, including clip paths, prefixed clip paths, `will-change: clip-path`, named view transitions and independently painted wrappers.

Accept ancestor URL image layers, including `image-set(url(...))`, consistently with the direct-text path. Match each image to its text clip and retain transparent-gradient, wrong-layer, background-bounds, SVG and unknown-browser guards.

Validation:

- All 312 layout/check/unit tests pass.
- All 57 real-browser screenshot cases pass on Chrome 148, 150 and 152. On Chrome 148, the new independently painted cases match the empty screenshot and report `text_not_painted`; ordinary descendants stay visible. Chrome 150 and 152 paint these cases and pass the audit.
- The reviewed commit fails five new unit cases and six browser cases, covering the independent-paint gap and nested `image-set()` mismatch.
- Workspace and CLI builds, CLI typecheck, lint, formatting, comment checks, test reachability and normal commit hooks pass.

Refs #5117 and the review follow-up on #5207. This checker change complements #5338, which updates the container renderer's Chrome version and carries the renderer fix for #5117.

As with the direct-text path, this diagnostic accepts URL images without decoding their alpha or verifying their load success.

title: fix(producer): make sparse keyframe advice conditional

Sparse keyframe warnings printed during rendering currently imply that long GOPs cause frozen or missing frames. Explain their potential cost to preview seeking, explicitly state that rendering is unaffected, and offer re-encoding only when preview seeking is slow. The interval calculation and suggested FFmpeg command remain unchanged.

Refs #3460 and the maintainer's diagnostic wording follow-up. Single-keyframe classification was already addressed by #3998.

Validation:

- Five compiler media/probe integration tests pass, including the warning wording and a short video with a longer audio track.
- Existing render evidence: a single-GOP clip produces all 30 requested frames at eight seconds, with the first matching independent FFmpeg frame-240 output pixel for pixel.
- Full workspace build, lint, formatting, comment gates and normal commit hooks pass.

title: fix(cli): hide background preview consoles
body:
Managed background preview servers launch a detached Node process. Pass `windowsHide: true` to that console process while retaining detachment, log routing and `unref()` so the server survives the launching CLI's exit.

Custom browser executables keep their default GUI visibility. Node/libuv maps `windowsHide` to a hidden startup show state for GUI programs too, so applying it to Chrome or Edge can hide a fresh-profile browser window. The browser launch test checks its exact options and preserves profile paths, remote debugging arguments and detachment.

Refs #3476. #3960 covers separate telemetry, clipboard and port-lookup sites. This PR covers the managed preview launch and does not claim to eliminate Windows Terminal's separate detached-console behavior.

Validation:

- The custom-browser regression fails on the reviewed commit because it passes `windowsHide`; all 128 browser, preview lifecycle, preview command and auto-update tests pass with the revision.
- The preview lifecycle regression retains checks for `windowsHide`, detachment, log file descriptors, inherited environment and `unref()`.
- Workspace and CLI builds, CLI typecheck, lint, formatting, comment checks and normal commit hooks pass.
- The existing macOS built-CLI lifecycle exercise starts a detached preview, serves HTTP 200, records its live PID, stops it and confirms `not-running` using isolated state.

Native Windows visibility has not been exercised on this macOS host. The revision removes the GUI startup visibility override requested during review; only the background Node server requests a hidden window.
