title: --format mov writes ProRes with the BT.601 matrix and no colour tags, so QuickTime shifts saturated colours
body:
### Describe the bug

The ProRes branch in `packages/engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts` and `streamingEncoder.ts` returns before the colour tags and the BT.709 conversion that the H.264/H.265 path got in #4564. ffmpeg's RGB to YUV conversion defaults to BT.601, so the file holds BT.601 data and says nothing about it. AVFoundation, which is what QuickTime uses, reads untagged HD as BT.709, so saturated colours shift. It's the same problem #4899 was about, just in the MOV output.

### Minimal reproduction

Any 1920x1080 composition with saturated colours:

    npx hyperframes render --format mov --output out.mov

Then open `out.mov` in QuickTime, or read a frame with `AVAssetImageGenerator`.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Render a page of flat colour swatches with `--format mov` (same result on macOS and with `--docker`).
2. Read the centre of each swatch through AVFoundation.

### Expected behavior

The same colours the mp4 output shows.

### Actual behavior

| authored | `--format mov` today | same frames, BT.709 matrix and tags | mp4 output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 255,0,0 | 255,26,0 | 255,0,0 | 253,0,0 |
| 0,255,0 | 0,220,0 | 0,255,0 | 0,255,2 |
| 228,41,130 | 245,73,142 | 231,46,141 | 231,46,140 |
| 128,0,200 | 147,25,212 | 139,0,207 | 138,1,206 |

The last two columns match. What's left between them and the authored values is how macOS applies the BT.709 transfer to any file, the mp4 included.

### Environment

hyperframes 0.8.143, macOS 26 (rendered on the host and with `--docker`), ffmpeg 8.1.1 on the host and 5.1.9 in the image.

### Additional context

The fix would mirror #4564: convert with the BT.709 matrix and add `-colorspace bt709 -color_primaries bt709 -color_trc bt709 -color_range tv` on the ProRes path too. I tried that by hand on the same frames (`scale=out_color_matrix=bt709:out_range=tv`, then the tags) and that's the third column. WebM is untagged as well, but Chrome reads untagged VP9 as BT.601, so it looks right in browsers (checked in Chrome 154). Happy to send the PR.

title: Proposal: a known-colour render check that works on any machine
body:
### Problem

The render tests compare each output with a golden video made by the same pipeline inside the Docker test image. That catches changes, but not colours that were wrong when the golden was made: when #4564 fixed the BT.709 matrix it had to regenerate eight goldens, because the old shift was baked into them. And outside Docker nothing looks at colour. The Windows job checks size, fps and duration, and there's no render job on macOS, where renders use drawElement capture and the system ffmpeg by default.

### Proposed solution

One small composition with 20 flat swatches whose sRGB values are known: primaries, a few skin and brand-like tones, and greys from 0 to 255 including 8, 16 and 32. Render it, decode one frame using the output's own colour tags, and check the centre of each swatch against its authored value, within 2 levels. There's no golden file, so the same check runs in Docker, on Windows and on a Mac. An output without colour tags fails, since players have to guess how to read it.

I built a prototype outside the repo and ran it against an old release and the current one:

| build | where | swatches off by more than 2 | worst |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.8.78 | Docker | 13 of 20 | 39 |
| 0.8.78 | macOS | 12 of 20 | 4 |
| 0.8.143 | Docker, mp4 | 0 | 2 |
| 0.8.143 | macOS, mp4 (drawElement, screenshot and `--gpu`) | 0 | 2 |

So it would have caught the two encode problems #4564 fixed, and #4899, before they shipped. It also turned up #5380: `--format mov` writes ProRes with the BT.601 matrix and no tags. A second fixture could do the same with a known-colour video clip, to cover footage extraction too.

Where it could go, roughly in this order:

1. A fixture in `packages/producer/tests/` with the expected colours in its `meta.json`, checked by the regression harness next to PSNR, for mp4, webm, mov and png-sequence.
2. The same check in the Windows render job, which already renders a canary.
3. A macOS job, if the runners can do drawElement capture. I'm not sure they have a GPU.

### Alternatives considered

Comparing a Docker render against a Mac render directly. Chrome and ffmpeg versions differ between them, so text and edges never match exactly and you end up tuning PSNR per platform. Flat swatches with known values avoid that.

### Additional context

A few questions before I write anything. Does this belong in the regression harness, or would you rather have a separate script? Is it OK to fail untagged output, or should WebM keep relying on Chrome reading untagged VP9 as BT.601? Is ±2 a reasonable tolerance? Happy to send it in small PRs, starting with the fixture and the harness check.

title: fix(engine): encode and tag ProRes mov output as BT.709
body:
## What

ProRes mov output is now converted with the BT.709 matrix and tagged as BT.709, like the mp4 output since #4564. Background removal's mov output gets the same fix.

## Why

The ProRes branches returned before the colour handling, so ffmpeg converted with its BT.601 default and wrote no tags. QuickTime reads untagged HD as BT.709, so saturated colours shifted by up to 35 levels (pure green showed up as 0,220,0).

## Related work

Fixes #5380. Follows #4564, which did this for H.264/H.265. #5278 did the same for background removal's WebM and left its mov as it was.

## How

The filter ends with `setparams` instead of relying on `-colorspace` and `-color_*`, because prores_ks doesn't pick those options up: ffmpeg 5.1 writes no tags at all and 8.1 only the matrix. With `setparams` both versions write all three. The conversion leaves the alpha plane alone, so transparency doesn't change.

## Test plan

A new real-ffmpeg test encodes a half-transparent RGBA PNG to ProRes and checks colour (within 2 levels), alpha and the tags. On main it fails with #C83C28 off by 13 levels. I also rendered a 20-swatch page with the built CLI: the mov is now tagged BT.709 and AVFoundation (what QuickTime uses) shows the same colours as the mp4, where before it was up to 35 levels off. A transparent composition keeps the same alpha values as before (255, 129 and 0). The rest of the engine suite passes, except the libaom-av1 case on Homebrew's ffmpeg that #5379 fixes.

title: fix(runtime): graded pictures stay graded in sandboxed players
body: ## What In a sandboxed (opaque-origin) document, a color-graded picture is graded again when its server answers CORS for that document. Everywhere else nothing changes. ## Why A sandboxed iframe without `allow-same-origin` has `window.origin === "null"`, so every picture its page loads by URL is cross-origin to it. Color grading uploads the page's own `` to WebGL; that `` loads no-cors, so `texImage2D` throws `SecurityError` and the picture stays ungraded, even when the server would grant CORS. A host that inlines pictures as `data:` URLs never hits this; a host that serves them by URL does. ## Related work Tiny self-contained correction; no issue. ## How The one place grading reads pixels (`uploadSourceTexture`, from `drawEntry` and `preparePreviewFrame`) now uploads `readablePixels(source)`. In an opaque document, for an http(s) `` without `crossorigin`, that is a copy of the picture requested with `crossOrigin = "anonymous"`, cached per element and source: - while the copy loads, gradings of that picture wait and the original picture shows; the copy's load (or error) redraws every grading waiting on it; - a refused copy leaves the element, which fails exactly as before; - layout, style and object-fit still read the element; the authored `` is never modified, so a host without CORS keeps showing it. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing performed - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments" Real Chromium (headless, Linux), a page served with `Content-Security-Policy: sandbox allow-scripts` by a server that answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` to `Origin: null`, running the real grading runtime on a graded ``: | | grading status | requests for the picture | |---|---|---| | main | `unavailable`: "texImage2D ... The image element contains cross-origin data" | one, `no-cors` | | this branch | `active`: "Shader active" | the page's `no-cors` one, plus one `cors` with `Origin: null` | `packages/core/src/runtime/colorGrading.test.ts`, a picture served by URL: with an origin, grading uploads the picture itself and makes no copy; in an opaque document it uploads a CORS copy (same src, `crossOrigin` anonymous), never the picture, and five redraws while it loads give one upload when it settles; a grading started while another's copy loads is redrawn when it settles; a refused copy uploads the picture as before. 3 runs in a row exit 0. Fails without the fix: with main's `colorGrading.ts` the three opaque-document tests fail; removing the origin check fails the first test, redrawing only the first waiter fails the third; queueing a redraw per draw fails the second. `tsc --noEmit` in core, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet: clean. Not exercised: Safari and Firefox; a srcset picture whose `currentSrc` changes mid-load. ## Independent adversarial review - First pass: a snapshot picture cache was in this PR; real Chromium showed html2canvas cannot run in a sandboxed page at all (its clone iframe is cross-origin there), so it was dropped. Graded pictures confirmed in real Chromium. - Should fix, all done: every grading waiting on a loading copy is redrawn, each once (a Set of entries, not one closure per draw); a document with an origin is pinned unchanged. - Final head: nothing blocking, nothing to fix; 1000 redraws while loading give one upload.

title: fix(engine): audio duration probe reads to the end on Windows; cli tests skip bun's disk cache
body:
## What changes for the user

- On Windows, the audio duration probe always reads a file's tail to its end. Before, it could stop early without an error, so a raw `.aac` file could get a shortened duration and its audio cut off, and long files could fall back to a slow full decode.
- The Windows engine and CLI test lane stops failing at random on `main`, which was also knocking pull requests out of the merge queue.

## Root causes

There are two, independent of each other.

**1. ffprobe's open-ended read interval (engine, affects real use).** `probeDecodedAudioDuration` asks ffprobe for `-read_intervals "<start>%"`, meaning "from start to the end". For that form ffprobe allocates the interval's end fields without zeroing them (`av_malloc_array`; same code in n7.1.3, n8.1.1 and master), and later reads them. On Linux and macOS the fresh memory happens to be zero, so it works. On Windows it holds leftovers, so ffprobe sometimes stops reading early and still exits 0 with nothing on stderr. Evidence:
- On Linux, `MALLOC_PERTURB_=1` makes the bug deterministic: the open-ended read returns no frames, and `"<start>%+2147483647"` returns the real last frame.
- On Windows runners with CI's ffprobe build, the open-ended read came back empty or cut short in 39 of 7000 runs; with an explicit end, 0 of 7000.
- The failing CI value (2.496 s for a 4 s file) is exactly a read cut short after 16 frames.

Fix: give the read an explicit far end, `+2147483647` (ffprobe rejects `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`). The other `-read_intervals` callers already pass a closed interval.

**2. bun's transpiler cache on the runner's system disk (CLI tests).** `packages/cli/scripts/test-home.mjs` points `HOME` at a fresh temp folder, so the first `bun run cli.ts` in a run writes about 270 cache files there, on drive C:. The hosted Windows runner's C: has write-latency episodes of over a second per write while D: stays fast, and two cold CLI spawns sat blocked on those writes past their 30 s timeout. Reproduced on Windows runners: two cold CLIs with the cache on C: reached 32.3 s, and with the cache off none went over 2 s in 516 spawns.

Fix: the CLI test setup turns bun's transpiler cache off (`BUN_RUNTIME_TRANSPILER_CACHE_PATH=0`), as `packages/producer/de-canary-suite.sh` already does. It costs about 0.1 s per spawned CLI and nothing measurable on suite time. Moving the cache to D: would also work, but depends on how GitHub lays out its runner drives.

## Verification

- `engine/src/utils/ffprobe.test.ts` (Linux): the new test runs the real probe with `MALLOC_PERTURB_=1` and requires the true duration from exactly two ffprobe calls; the existing interval assertions now expect the closed interval. With the fix reverted, those three tests fail; with it, the duration tests pass 3 runs in a row.
- `cli/src/testHome.test.ts` (Linux): a CLI spawned with a fresh home writes no transpiler cache. It fails without the setting and passes 3 runs in a row with it. On macOS bun writes no such cache, so there it passes either way.
- Windows: see the runs of `Windows render verification` on this branch.

## Why this PR is small

It ships alone on purpose: main is red on Windows and every queued PR is ejected until it lands, so it is not bundled with other work.

title: fix(skills): skill scripts run through a symlinked skills dir and agents keep long renders alive
body:
## What changes for a user

Skill scripts now run when the skills directory is reached through a symlink, which is how agents commonly install skills. Before, `captions.mjs` (in the three video workflow skills) and `heygen-voice.mjs` compared `process.argv[1]` with the module URL as written. Node resolves symlinks in `import.meta.url` but leaves `argv[1]` as typed, so through a symlinked skills dir the check failed and the script exited 0 without doing anything.

```
$ node <symlinked skills>/pr-to-video/scripts/captions.mjs not-a-command; echo $?
0        # before: nothing ran
usage: node captions.mjs build [--storyboard …] [--audio-meta …] [--hyperframes .]
2        # after: the CLI runs
```

`packages/cli/src/media-use/lib/cube-validate.mjs`, which the CLI ships inside its media-use skill, had the same bug and uses the shared check too. Five other scripts already had a correct check (`frame-packets-core.mjs`, `carve.mjs`, `preflight.mjs`, `project-dir.mjs`, `plugin-cli.mjs`), each a private copy. The check now lives once in `skills/hyperframes/scripts/lib/main-module.mjs`, copied into each skill that needs it by `scripts/generate-skill-module-copies.mjs` (the existing mechanism for shared skill modules), and every script uses it.

## Checked

- New `main-module.test.mjs` runs the four previously broken scripts through a symlinked skills dir and expects their CLI to run, and fails if any script under `skills/` or the CLI's media-use copy reads `process.argv[1]` outside the shared helper. Against main both tests fail: all four scripts exit 0, and 14 hand-rolled checks are listed.
- The plugin launcher test fixture now copies the shared helper next to the launcher, as a real install has it.
- `skills/**/*.test.mjs`: 512 pass, three runs in a row. `generate-skill-module-copies.mjs --check` is in sync.

## Renders started by an agent tool (docs only)

A render cancels when its parent exits or when it gets SIGINT, SIGTERM or SIGHUP, by design, so Ctrl-C or a closed terminal never leaves Chrome and ffmpeg running. A tool that cleans up its process group therefore stops a render it started. To start a render that outlives its launcher, do both:

- set `HYPERFRAMES_RENDER_DETACHED=1` (documented in `packages/cli/README.md`, under `render`): the render stops watching its parent and no longer cancels itself on SIGHUP (an unhandled SIGHUP still ends the process; `nohup` makes it ignore SIGHUP, and its own process group keeps a closing terminal from sending one);
- start it in its own process group, so a group-wide SIGTERM to the launcher does not reach it: `bash -c 'set -m; HYPERFRAMES_RENDER_DETACHED=1 npx hyperframes render … < /dev/null > render.log 2>&1 &'` works on macOS and Linux (macOS has no `setsid`); from Node, `spawn(..., { detached: true })` then `unref()`.

The variable alone is not enough against a process-group kill, since the render still honours SIGTERM.

The `hyperframes-cli` skill's render section and the CLI README (which used to suggest `nohup` or `disown`, neither of which leaves the process group) now say exactly that. Checked on Linux with a parent whose whole process group gets SIGTERM mid-render: with the variable and its own group the render finishes; with only one of the two it is cancelled.

title: fix(producer): the npm package ships only its own code and no source maps
body:
## What changes for a user

`@hyperframes/producer` on npm becomes a small package of producer's own code, so it installs faster and is a far smaller upload for each release.

| `@hyperframes/producer` | packed | unpacked | files | source maps |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 21.77 MB | 76.09 MB | 242 | 119 |
| after | 0.69 MB | 2.55 MB | 123 | 0 |
| `@hyperframes/core`, for scale | 1.75 MB | 4.77 MB | 775 | 382 (1.0 MB) |

The CLI package (`hyperframes`) drops the source maps it copied in from Studio's build:

| `hyperframes` | packed | unpacked | source maps |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 10.18 MB | 34.41 MB | 12 files, 8.6 MB |
| after | 8.10 MB | 25.77 MB | 0 |

## Why it was large

Producer's build bundled everything it imports into each of its three entry points (`.`, `./server`, `./distributed`), including `@hyperframes/core`, `@hyperframes/engine`, `hono`, `linkedom` and the rest, although all of them are already declared in its `dependencies`. Each entry carried about 9 MB of the same inlined code plus a source map of about 16 MB.

The build now keeps every dependency external (`packages: "external"`), the same choice `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` and `@hyperframes/gcp-cloud-run` already make, and stops emitting source maps and declaration maps. So the tarball holds producer's own code and npm installs its dependencies as for any other package. The three entries together are now about 1.6 MB, so there is nothing left worth splitting into shared chunks. The CommonJS shim the build used to prepend for inlined CommonJS dependencies is gone with them.

Producer now depends on its own packages (`core`, `engine`, `lint`, `parsers`, `studio-server`) at the exact release version, as `core` and `studio` already do for theirs, so producer's direct dependencies are the ones it was built and tested with. `engine` itself still asks for `core` and `parsers` with a caret range; that is unchanged here.

**Worker fix.** The published package never found its two worker threads: `healthWorker.ts` and `shaderTransitionWorkerPool.ts` look for the worker file in their own directory, which is `dist/` once bundled, but the build wrote the workers to `dist/services/`. Starting the published server logged `health worker failed to start: could not resolve worker entry`. The build now writes them beside the bundles; the entry list lives in `buildEntries.mjs`, and `buildEntries.test.ts` pins the layout (it fails with main's `dist/services/` paths).

Nothing in the repo runs producer's `dist` with its dependencies inlined: the Lambda handler zip bundles producer from source (`packages/aws-lambda/scripts/build-zip.ts`), the Cloud Run image runs it under bun inside the workspace, and the CLI bundles it from source.

The CLI's build copies Studio's `dist` into its own and now skips `.map` files there; the CLI already ships no maps of its own (`sourcemap: false` in its tsup config).

## Checked

On Linux, from this branch:

- `npm pack --dry-run` on the producer and CLI packages for the numbers above, with main's build script for "before".
- A clean `npm install` of the packed producer, core, engine, parsers, lint and studio-server tarballs (as `pnpm pack` writes them for publishing; producer's packed manifest pins them at `0.8.144`). Under plain Node all three exports import, and a real render through `createRenderJob` and `executeRenderJob` completes: h264, 200x200, 30 frames.
- In that install, `startServer` from `@hyperframes/producer/server` starts its health worker (`/health listening on worker thread`, and the worker's `/health` answers 200). The published 0.8.143 logs `health worker failed to start: [healthWorker] could not resolve worker entry` for the same call. The shader-transition worker resolves from `dist/` and returns a correct crossfade for a test job; a full HDR render through the packed package was not run.
- `buildEntries.test.ts` passes three runs in a row and fails with main's layout. The lockfile's producer block matches what a fresh resolve writes, and frozen installs pass with bun 1.4.2 and with 1.3.13 (the regression image's version).
- The built CLI starts (`hyperframes --version`).

title: fix(cli): audit clipped text beneath transparent composition hosts
body:
Visible text with a `clip-path` can disappear from contrast checks when a transparent composition host sits above it. For example, adding `clip-path: inset(0)` leaves the rendered frame identical but makes `hyperframes check` miss a 1.16:1 contrast failure.

Use the existing hit-stack probe for clipped text as well as intentional occlusion. It walks only through unpainted composition containers and stops at painted covers. Fully clipped text remains excluded.

Follows the [reviewer's suggested follow-up on #5202](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5202#pullrequestreview-5462293450).

Validation: six new visible-text regressions fail on unchanged main; all 70 contrast tests pass with the fix, including six real Chromium tests. Screenshots verify that an unchanged visible frame is audited and fully clipped text stays excluded. Seven isolated runs through the rebuilt, copied CLI report contrast failures for visible, partially revealed, ancestor-clipped, and nested-root text, and pass fully clipped, painted-cover, and readable-text controls. The source and packaged browser scripts match. Browser-check tests, full workspace and CLI builds, CLI typecheck, repository lint, formatting, test reachability, comment checks, and normal commit hooks pass.

title: fix(cli): keyframes --shot on a compositions/ file mounts the scene in its project
body:
## What changes for the user

`hyperframes keyframes compositions/<scene>.html --selector "#id" --shot out.png` now works. Before, it failed with `[StaticGuard] Invalid HyperFrame contract: Composition uses GSAP but no GSAP script is loaded` and `--shot: --selector matched no element`, while the same selector against the project folder worked.

## Root cause

`--shot` bundles the target file with `bundleToSingleHtml(projectDir, { entryFile })`. For a scene file (a `<template>` mounted from `index.html` via `data-composition-src`), the bundler treated the bare template as the whole page: no root composition, none of the root's scripts (GSAP), so nothing mounted and the selector matched nothing.

Render already solved this for `render -c compositions/<scene>.html`: it reuses the project's `index.html` as the shell and keeps only the host that mounts the scene (`extractStandaloneEntryFromIndex`). That logic lived in the producer, out of the bundler's reach.

## Fix

- Move `extractStandaloneEntryFromIndex` and its helpers from the producer into `@hyperframes/core/compiler` (`standaloneEntry.ts`), with their existing tests, plus one `isTemplateEntry` check. Render and the bundler now share that code instead of each owning a copy. (Studio's composition preview route builds its page separately; it is not changed here.)
- The bundler uses it when the entry is a `<template>` file and the project's `index.html` mounts it; the page is then bundled from the project folder. Any other entry bundles exactly as before.
- The extraction used to clear the whole `<body>`, including a GSAP `<script src>` that some projects load there. It now keeps the body's library `<script src>` tags, ahead of the scene. Without this the shot exited 0 with every frame stacked in one spot; `render -c` on such a project failed with `sub_timeline_script_failure` and is fixed by the same change.
- The static guard is skipped for that generated shell: it checks authored documents, and the shell has the root's inline registration removed by design (the scene registers its own timeline once inlined), so it always printed a misleading `[StaticGuard] Missing window.__timelines registration` on a correct shot.

`snapshot` and `check` take a project folder only, so `keyframes` is the one command that reaches the bundler with a scene file.

## Verification

- Real CLI on a fixture project (a GSAP root plus `compositions/scene.html` tweening `#title`), before and after: before, the StaticGuard error, `--shot: --selector '#title' matched no element` and no image; after, the onion-skin shot of `#title` moving 0s to 3s, identical to the shot of the project folder, with no warnings. The same holds with GSAP loaded from `<body>`.

- New bundler test: a template scene entry is bundled inside the index that mounts it (the root's script is present, the sibling scene is not). It fails without the bundler change and passes 3 runs in a row.
- Core compiler tests (188) and producer `renderOrchestrator` tests (279) pass 3 runs in a row.

## Known limits

- A library `<script src>` nested inside a body element (not a direct child of `<body>`) is still dropped, as before. No index in this repo does that.
- A root timeline loaded from an external `<script src>` directly under `<body>` is now kept, so the scene shot samples the root's length, the same as the project-folder shot.
- Follow-up, unchanged by this PR: `render -c <scene>` waits for the root timeline whose inline script the shell drops.

title: perf(packages): ship npm packages without source maps and guard their size in CI
body:
## What

Smaller npm packages, and two CI checks that keep packages and the repo from growing back.

`npm pack --dry-run` on the built tree, main (063c2f8) vs this branch:

| Package | Packed before | Packed after | Unpacked before | Unpacked after | Files before → after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| hyperframes (CLI) | 10.18 MB | 7.14 MB | 34.41 MB | 21.33 MB | 589 → 560 |
| @hyperframes/studio | 7.75 MB | 5.67 MB | 31.42 MB | 22.78 MB | 1669 → 1657 |
| @hyperframes/core | 1.75 MB | 1.56 MB | 4.77 MB | 3.74 MB | 775 → 393 |
| @hyperframes/shader-transitions | 0.77 MB | 0.20 MB | 3.38 MB | 0.79 MB | 10 → 7 |
| @hyperframes/parsers | 0.72 MB | 0.18 MB | 2.95 MB | 0.80 MB | 67 → 46 |
| @hyperframes/player | 0.69 MB | 0.15 MB | 2.49 MB | 0.52 MB | 20 → 13 |
| @hyperframes/engine | 0.56 MB | 0.41 MB | 2.22 MB | 1.37 MB | 262 → 132 |
| @hyperframes/lint | 0.45 MB | 0.16 MB | 1.78 MB | 0.62 MB | 7 → 5 |
| @hyperframes/studio-server | 0.36 MB | 0.13 MB | 1.43 MB | 0.51 MB | 69 → 43 |
| @hyperframes/aws-lambda | 0.14 MB | 0.06 MB | 0.53 MB | 0.22 MB | 49 → 30 |
| @hyperframes/sdk | 0.12 MB | 0.09 MB | 0.52 MB | 0.31 MB | 89 → 45 |
| @hyperframes/gcp-cloud-run | 0.12 MB | 0.05 MB | 0.45 MB | 0.18 MB | 47 → 29 |
| **Total (without producer)** | **23.61 MB** | **15.80 MB** | **86.35 MB** | **53.17 MB** | |

@hyperframes/producer was slimmed separately in #5398 (now 0.69 MB packed / 2.55 MB unpacked, measured by this PR's own check in CI); its budget here follows that.

## Why

Published source maps were most of several tarballs and nothing needs them at runtime. The one place that enables source-map support, the Lambda stack's `NODE_OPTIONS=--enable-source-maps`, runs the deploy zip, which `build-zip.ts` already builds without maps; and a Vite 8 consumer build does not chain a dependency's map into its own (checked with a fixture: the output map points at the dependency's `dist/index.js`, not its original source). One cost: esbuild-based consumer builds (esbuild, tsup, Vite 6/7 dev) do chain them, so their debugger now shows our compiled `dist` code instead of the TypeScript source, most visibly for the minified player and shader-transitions bundles. Nothing breaks: no shipped file references a missing map. The CLI also carried studio's whole library build (`index.js`, chunks, types, maps) next to the studio app, while its server only serves `index.html`, `/assets`, `/icons` and `/favicon.svg`.

The existing large-binary check ran only as a local pre-commit hook, so `--no-verify`, a fork without lefthook, or a web edit skipped it; and it trusted `.gitattributes`, so a file matching an LFS pattern but added without git-lfs installed went in raw.

## How

- Source maps and declaration maps are no longer built for the other packages (tsup `sourcemap`, tsconfig `sourceMap` / `declarationMap`, esbuild `sourcemap`); core's `files` no longer lists them.
- `packages/cli/scripts/build-copy.mjs` copies only the four entries the CLI's studio server serves.
- `scripts/verify-packed-manifests.mjs`, which already packs every published package in CI, now checks each tarball's packed and unpacked bytes against `scripts/package-size-budgets.json`. Over budget fails. Shrinking 15% below the budget also fails, with the new number to write, so budgets only move down; raising one is an explicit, reviewed edit. A new published package without a budget fails with the line to add, and a malformed budget fails instead of switching its check off. `publish.yml` runs the same verifier before publishing, so a package over budget also stops a release; every PR that can change a tarball runs it first.
- `scripts/check-large-files.sh` gains `--range <base> <head>` and, in its git modes, sizes the blob git stores rather than the file on disk. It reads entries from `git diff --raw -z`, so each blob is read by its id (a file named like `0:clip.bin` is sized as itself), names git would quote are checked, type changes are included, submodule entries are skipped, and a name with a newline, an unreadable blob or a git error fails the check instead of passing it. CI runs it on every `pull_request` event against the merge ref's base in the change-detection job; the catalog bot's PR, whose checks come from a `workflow_dispatch` run, is not covered by this step. `registry/` stays exempt as before; a file under `docs/public/catalog/` is exempt only when it is a byte-identical copy of a `registry/` file (the docs site mirrors those assets), so anything else there is checked like any other path.
- The four skill folders the CLI bundles (`skills/hyperframes`, `hyperframes-cli`, `gsap`, `media-use`) get their own CI change filter that starts only the Build job, so a skills-only change that grows the CLI tarball still meets its size budget.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `check-large-files.test.mjs` (range mode; raw blob under an LFS pattern; non-ASCII, quote and tab filenames; a newline in a name; a symlink replaced by a binary; an unreadable blob; an unresolvable ref; staged mode with modified, type-changed and revision-syntax names; a submodule; the registry and catalog-copy exemptions in range and staged mode; backslashes in reported names), `verify-packed-manifests.test.mjs` (within, over, ratchet, missing and malformed budgets). Each passes 3 runs in a row; removing any one of those behaviours makes its test fail.
- [x] `bun run build` + `bun run verify:packed-manifests` on a clean tree before main gained #5398: all 13 packages within budget (producer's budget then lowered to the size CI measured after it); clean packed consumer install, 161 exports resolved, CLI startup.
- [x] Packed tarballs installed into a scratch project: `npx hyperframes --help`, `init`, `preview` serves the studio page with its `/assets` script and `/favicon.svg` (200), and a 10 s `render` finishes.
- [x] `check-large-files.sh --range` over the last 300 commits of main: clean. On an old commit (not on main) that added a 9 MB demo mp4 and a 901 KB mp3: both rejected.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)

## No visible change

Build, packaging and CI only. Studio and the player look and behave the same: the CLI still serves the same studio app files, and no `.tsx`, `.css` or `.html` file changes.

title: fix(lint): add missing fixHints to three lint findings
body:
Fixes #5392

## Problem

Almost every lint finding carries a `fixHint` telling the user what to change. Three did not:

- `invalid_composition_variables_declaration`, both per-entry branches in `packages/lint/src/rules/composition.ts` — an entry that isn't an object, and an entry missing/with an invalid `id`, `type`, `label` or `default`. (The two whole-array branches — unparseable JSON and not an array — already had hints.)
- `css_parse_error` in `packages/lint/src/rules/core.ts`.

Without a hint, `lint` and `check` show only the message.

## Change

- Entry-is-not-an-object: the hint shows the shape of a valid entry, mirroring the wording of the neighbouring whole-array hints.
- Entry-missing-or-invalid-fields: the hint spells out that all four fields are required, restates the accepted `type` values (the message already lists them, but the hint should stand on its own in a terminal), and says `default` is required even when nothing changes it.
- `css_parse_error`: the hint points at the position PostCSS reports and names the usual causes — a missing trailing semicolon, a property missing its colon, an unclosed brace or quote — plus the note that PostCSS drops everything after the reported line, so a stray `}` early in the block points the error at a line that looks fine.

No rule behaviour changes; findings are only given a hint they were missing.

## Tests

Existing tests that cover these codes now assert the hint is present, plus one new test for the not-an-object branch, which had no coverage of its own:

- `packages/lint/src/rules/composition.test.ts`: root-tag entry, not-an-object (new), missing-required-fields, unknown-type.
- `packages/lint/src/rules/core.test.ts`: the `css_parse_error` case.

## Verification

```
bun run --cwd packages/lint test     # 20 files, 908 tests passed
bun run --cwd packages/lint typecheck
bunx oxlint packages/lint/src        # 0 warnings, 0 errors
bunx oxfmt --check packages/lint/src
```

title: fix(core): a runtime that fails to start names its real error instead of a half-built page
body:
## What changes for the user

`hyperframes check` no longer dies with `check_runtime_failure: Cannot access 'nS' before initialization` on a project whose sub-composition registers a partial timeline, such as `window.__timelines["extra"] = { duration: 4, seek() {} }` or one whose `duration()` throws. The browser audit runs and reports layout, motion and contrast again. Preview and render of the same page stop half-initialising too.

## Root cause

During runtime start-up the timeline is announced, which builds the clip tree and the timeline payload. Both read each registered sub-composition timeline's `duration`:

- `clipTree.ts` called `registry[id]?.duration?.()`. Optional call only skips `null`/`undefined`, so a numeric `duration` was called and threw `TypeError: registry[compId]?.duration is not a function`.
- `timeline.ts` checked that `duration` was a function but did not guard the call, so a `duration()` that throws escaped too.

Either throw aborted start-up partway, before the seek helpers further down were initialised. The next seek from `check` then hit the temporal dead zone of `activateSiblingTimelines` (minified `nS`), an error that names an internal variable instead of the real cause.

The same guarded read existed in five places (`init.ts`, `timeline.ts` twice, `startResolver.ts`, `clipTree.ts`) and none of them guarded a getter that throws (two did not guard the call either). They now share one reader, `readTimelineDurationSeconds`: a finite `duration()` or `null`, with the type check inside the guard so a throwing getter or a Proxy entry reads as `null` too. Each caller keeps its own rule on top (`> 0`, or clamped at 0).

## A start-up that throws now says so

Removing the trigger leaves the class: any exception during runtime start-up left a half-built page that the next seek reported as an internal "before initialization" error. Now:

- One recorder, `recordStartupError` (`diagnostics.ts`), sets `window.__hfStartupError` ("HyperFrames runtime failed: <name>: <message>. Check the composition's scripts and window.__timelines entries; if they look right, report this as a HyperFrames bug."). A thrown value that cannot be printed is recorded as "unknown error" rather than making the recorder throw. `entry.ts` calls it when start-up throws, and the render-ready publish calls it when its timeline post throws, including publishes after start-up (GSAP batching finishing, the deferred rebind, adapter readiness). Both still rethrow. Other timeline posts (Studio's editor refresh among them) do not record: they keep their own retry.
- The page is never left marked render-ready when posting the timeline throws: the flag keeps its place (the first-frame readiness check posted with the timeline waits on it) and is cleared before the error propagates. Once recorded, the error stays set: start-up schedules its own later posts (the deferred rebind, GSAP batching finishing), and clearing on their success would erase a real start-up error and let a half-built page look ready. A render-ready publish whose timeline post throws after a full start is reported as failed too, even if a later publish succeeds, by design (fail loudly rather than render from a page that could not post its timeline).
- The CLI's readiness wait (`check`, `snapshot`, `keyframes`, `compare`, `grade-compare`, `layout`, `validate`) and the engine's render wait fail at once with that message instead of timing out or seeking a half-built page.
- `keyframes --shot` and `validate` close the browser they opened when opening the page throws, so a failed start-up ends the command instead of leaving Chrome running (it hung before; for `validate` that was already true on main).
- The render probe in the producer now catches a `duration()` that throws (it runs in the page and cannot import the shared reader); its handling of a non-finite duration is unchanged.
- `position-edits-render-inline.ts` is regenerated because the bundle it holds imports `diagnostics.ts`.
- Drive-by: a `frameCapture.ts` comment no longer cites a doc file that was never committed.

## Also in this PR (same `check` audit)

- `check`'s seek-clock probe (`collectSeekClock`) read a custom timeline's `time()` with `Number(...)`, so `time: () => null` became `0` and a working custom root looked like a stuck clock (exit 1). It now accepts only a finite number.

## Verification

- New `init.test.ts` cases run real runtime start-up and a seek with a sub-composition timeline whose `duration` is a number, a method that throws, or a getter that throws. With main's runtime files all three fail (`registry[compId]?.duration is not a function`, `boom`, `getter`); with this change they pass. `clipTree.test.ts` covers the same shapes at the unit level.
- `entry.startupFailure.test.ts`: a throwing start-up records the named error, a start-up whose timeline post throws is not left render-ready, a post that throws after start-up (the deferred rebind) is named and leaves the page not ready, and a start-up error survives a later successful post. Both fail on the previous code. The CLI and engine waits each have a test that fails without the change; `motionShot.browserClose.test.ts` and `validate.browserClose.test.ts` check the browser is closed when the runtime fails to start (both fail on the previous code); and so does the producer probe; a `checkBrowser.test.ts` case pins the null `time()` clock (fails on the previous code).
- Runtime suites (345 + 33 entry tests), the CLI capture and check tests (136), the engine frame-capture tests (55) and the producer compiler tests (141) pass 3 runs in a row; typecheck is clean for core, cli, engine and producer. Real GSAP timelines read the same as before (`0`, `null`, `NaN`, `Infinity` from `duration()` give the same results).

## Known limits

- A start-up that throws still does not tear down what it already started (the teardown is installed at the end of start-up). The page reports the error; a reload replaces it.
- The player and Studio readiness input is unchanged: it only resolves, bounded by its abort signal, so it cannot hang on a failed start-up. Studio's thumbnail capture does not read the new error yet (cosmetic).
- The CLI and engine waits read the error while they wait. A render-ready publish that throws after the wait has returned is recorded but not read by that run, which continues as it does today.
- The deprecated `validate` reports only the start-up error on such a page, not the other console errors it collected.
- A sub-composition entry that is a Proxy throwing on every property read still fails start-up (in timeline selection, not the duration read); it is now reported by name.

title: fix(studio-server): the public proxy cache path names boxed preview copies too
body:
## What changes for a user

A host app that serves Studio's preview media can now name the exact cached copy the preview asks for. Since the preview started requesting copies sized to the box it shows them in (`?hf-proxy-box=1024x724`), those copies live under a box-specific cache name, but the public `getProxyCachePath(projectDir, file, variant)` could only name the full-size copy. A host that checks which file it is about to serve (for example a cross-site guard) could not match the boxed copy, so opaque ProRes and HEVC previews failed with 403.

`getProxyCachePath` now takes the preview box as an optional fourth argument and returns the same path `resolveProxy` writes for that box. The cache key still has one owner: both go through the same internal key builder, so nothing hashes twice. Hosts get the box from the request with `parsePreviewProxyBox` and `PREVIEW_PROXY_BOX_PARAM` from `@hyperframes/core`, as the Studio preview route does. When `parsePreviewProxyBox` returns `null` (a size off the ladder), refuse the request as that route does (404) rather than passing no box, which names the full-size copy.

Without a box the function returns what it returned before.

## Checked

- New test: with a box, `getProxyCachePath` returns exactly the file `resolveProxy` writes for that box, and a different file from the unboxed copy. It fails with the previous function, which ignored the box. `proxyTranscoder.test.ts`: 38 pass, three runs in a row on Linux.

title: perf(engine): re-renders reuse the extracted frames of remote videos
body:
## What

Re-rendering a composition that uses a remote video (an `https://` `src`) no longer extracts that video's frames again. The second and later renders reuse the frames extracted the first time, the way videos in the project folder already do.

## Why

The extraction cache keys a source on its path and modification time. A remote video is downloaded at compile time and copied into the render's own compiled directory (`_remote_media/`), and the extractor reads that copy. Its path and modification time are new on every render, so the lookup always missed: every re-render ran ffmpeg over the whole clip again and wrote another full copy of the frames into the cache, which the cache's size limit then evicted.

The same problem was already handled for HDR-normalized files (the comment above `cacheKeyInputs` in `videoFrameExtractor.ts`); downloaded files were not.

## Related work

#5351 also changes `extractionCache.ts`, in the publish path (an emptied entry that still has its completion marker). Different function; no behavior overlap.

## How

- `CacheKeyInput.contentSha256` (optional). When set, the key uses the SHA-256 of the source bytes in place of path and modification time. Keys of path-keyed sources are byte-identical to before, so existing cache entries stay warm (pinned by a test).
- `ExtractionOptions.contentKeyedDirs`: directories whose files are rewritten by every render. The extractor always includes its own download directory; the producer's extract stage adds the compiled `_remote_media` directory, where compile puts downloaded remote media. Sources inside these are keyed by content. Everything else, including the project copy a distributed plan puts in its compiled directory, keeps its path key, exactly as before.
- Hashing runs just before the cache lookup, once per file, only when the cache is enabled, and stops on abort. Videos whose extraction is deferred (distributed plan v2) never reach the lookup and are not hashed. A source that cannot be hashed skips the cache, the same way a missing file already does.
- No schema bump: the frames stored for a key do not change, only which key a downloaded file maps to.
- Cost: hashing runs on every render with the cache on, including the first render on an empty cache. Measured with the same streamed SHA-256: 40 ms for a 37 MB clip, 0.74 s per GB while the file is in the page cache (as it is right after the download wrote it), 7.3 s per GB read cold from disk. The hash reads the whole file, so a few seconds taken from a very long remote video can cost more to hash than to extract; every render already downloads that whole file, which costs more again. Hashing while downloading, so no second read is needed, is a follow-up.
- Not covered: a distributed plan copies the project into its compiled directory with new modification times, so project videos there still miss on every plan, as before. Downloaded media in a plan is covered.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `videoFrameExtractor.downloadCache.test.ts` (new): a re-render reuses the frames of a remote video copied into its compiled `_remote_media` directory (the production shape), with the same frame count and first-frame bytes, and of a video the extractor downloaded itself; a downloaded video whose bytes changed extracts again; a file used by two videos is hashed once; a deferred video is not hashed; a project copy elsewhere in the compiled directory keeps its path key and is not hashed; nothing is hashed with the cache off. Each rule was broken on purpose once (caller directories ignored, whole compiled directory content-keyed, hashing before deferral) and only its own tests failed. The file passed 3 runs in a row.
  - `extractVideosStage.timelineBound.test.ts`: the producer's extract stage passes the compiled remote-media directory as `contentKeyedDirs`, in-process and distributed (9 passed).
  - `extractionCache.test.ts`: path-keyed keys equal the previous encoding exactly; content keys ignore path and modification time; the file hash, and `null` for an unreadable file.
  - On Linux: `videoFrameExtractor.downloadCache.test.ts` 7 passed, `extractionCache.test.ts` 40 passed, `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` 199 passed, each exit 0. Engine and producer `tsc --noEmit` exit 0.
- [x] Manual testing performed: real CLI renders, below.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

### Before / after

Two producer regression fixtures that use a remote video: `style-1-prod` (17 s, 1920x1080, 510 frames) and `overlay-montage-prod` (42 s, 1080x1920, 1271 frames). CLI `render --workers 4`, base `684c038` vs this branch at `649d82b4`, interleaved, 3 runs each, a fresh extraction cache at the start, on an 8-core Linux machine shared with other work.

Video extraction stage (`videoExtractMs`) and cache result:

| | base, every run | this branch, first render | this branch, re-renders |
|---|---|---|---|
| style-1-prod | 4.2 / 3.9 / 3.0 s, miss | 5.1 s, miss | 0.85 / 0.85 s, hit |
| overlay-montage-prod | 8.4 / 7.7 / 6.1 s, miss | 5.9 s, miss | 0.07 / 0.07 s, hit |

Whole render, same runs: style-1-prod base 37.8 / 30.4 / 28.2 s, this branch 32.0 (cold) / 29.6 / 25.7 s; overlay-montage-prod base 106.6 / 95.1 / 87.3 s, this branch 85.0 (cold) / 84.5 / 78.9 s. Frame capture is 75-80% of a render and moves by several seconds with load on the shared machine, so the extraction stage is the number to read.

Output: the decoded video frames (ffmpeg `framemd5` of the mp4 video stream) are identical between base and this branch in every run, for both fixtures.

A cache hit on `style-1-prod` still spends about 0.85 s in the stage; not investigated here.

The local pre-commit `typecheck` hook was skipped (`LEFTHOOK_EXCLUDE=typecheck`) because the fresh worktree lacked core's generated runtime file; the same typecheck ran clean after a full build.

title: fix(cli): list valid families when media-treatment gets an unknown capability
body:
## What changes for a user

`hyperframes media-treatment --capability <name>` with a name it doesn't know now says which names it does know, instead of only "Unknown media-treatment capability".

```
$ hyperframes media-treatment --capability adjust
before: ✗ Unknown media-treatment capability: adjust
after:  ✗ Unknown media-treatment capability: adjust. Available areas: grading, correction, wheels, curves, hue-curves, secondary, scopes, presets, finishing, palettes, animation, lut, overlays, essentials, retro-glitch, print, art.
```

The list is built from the same data the lookup walks (its area details and the effect families), so it cannot drift from what the command accepts. It lists the area names the lookup accepts (the `--capabilities` overview's families plus grading's sub-areas), rather than every control, effect, preset and palette id, which run to dozens.

`adjust` stays unknown here. Docs and skills use `adjust` only as the key inside a grading payload (`{"adjust": {"exposure": 0.1}}`), never as a `--capability` name; the matching family is `correction` (labelled "Adjust" in the overview), which the error now shows.

## Checked

- New test: every family in the overview appears in the error's list, and every name the error lists resolves. It fails on main (no list in the message).
- `media-treatment.test.ts`: 22 pass, three runs in a row on Linux. The CLI output above is from a source run on Linux, before and after.

title: fix(cli): timeline split keeps a sub-composition's place in both halves
body:
## What changes for a user

Splitting a sub-composition clip from the command line (`hyperframes timeline split <clip> <time>`) now keeps the second half's place in the scene. Before, only Studio's razor marked where each half starts inside the sub-composition (`data-playback-start`), so after a CLI split the second half restarted the scene from the beginning.

```
hyperframes timeline split '#host' 3
before:  <div id="host" ...>          <div id="host-2" ...>            (no in-point: host-2 replays the scene from 0 s)
after:   <div id="host" data-playback-start="0" ...>   <div id="host-2" data-playback-start="2" ...>
```

## Why

Every split goes through `splitElementInHtml`, but whether the element is a sub-composition was decided by each caller and passed in as a flag. Only Studio's razor passed it; the single-split route and the CLI did not. The split function now reads it off the element itself (`data-composition-src` or `data-composition-id`, what the runtime treats as a composition), and the flag is gone, so every caller gets the same result. Studio's razor behaves as before. Freeze frame is unaffected: it only accepts a `<video>` and splits it with its linked media (usually audio), never a sub-composition.

## Checked

- New split-function tests: a host with `data-composition-src` or `data-composition-id`, split with no flag, gets `data-playback-start` `0` and `2` on its halves. The existing composition-offset test now uses a real host instead of the flag.
- New CLI test: `timeline split` on a sub-composition host writes both in-points.
- All of them fail on main. On Linux, three runs in a row: studio-server split, files and freeze-frame tests (182 pass), CLI timeline tests (104 pass), Studio razor tests (20 pass). Typecheck passes for studio-server, cli and studio.

## No visible change

The only Studio edit drops the `isComposition` field from the razor's split request (`razorSplitTransaction.ts`, 2 lines), since the server now reads it off the element. The razor's result in the timeline is the same as before; the Studio razor tests pass unchanged.
