title: fix(core): a split sub-composition plays its videos from its in-point in preview and timeline
body:
## What changes for a user

After splitting a sub-composition clip in Studio, the second half now plays the videos inside it from where the split happened, in the preview and in `hyperframes timeline`. Before, Studio's split wrote each half's in-point (`data-playback-start`) correctly, but only the scene's animations honoured it: the videos inside started over as if the scene began at the second half's start.

Example from the test fixture: a 12 s scene with trimmed videos, split at 5 s. Inside the second half, a video authored at 9 to 13 s of the scene:

| | main timeline |
|---|---|
| before | 9 to 13 s (scene time, ignoring the split) |
| after | 4 to 8 s, matching where it played before the split |

Studio preview at 7 s, with a generated 12 s clip (red, then green, then blue, its own time burned in) inside one sub-composition split at 5 s:

## Before

![Before: at 7 s the second half restarted the clip, showing source 2 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad53e32c-b7aa-4de3-ab6a-f39f8c34d153)

## After

![After: at 7 s the second half continues the clip, showing source 7 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/726a381b-666f-4f08-91e3-8eab46c7e5e8)

This is the first part of making a sub-composition's in-point shift and cut the media inside it (issue #3245). Snapshot and the renderer follow in their own PRs.

## How

Only a sub-composition host with an in-point above 0 changes anything. Its local time 0 sits at the host's start minus that in-point (its origin), so everything timed inside it (media, images, text, nested scenes, and the clip rows Studio lists) is placed from that origin, the same way the scene's animations already were. The media inside plays only within the host's slot: what starts before the host is cut at its head, and the host's end cuts the tail. A clip that straddles the in-point starts at the host's start, further into its file, while its loop point, speed ramp, volume lanes and fades stay timed from the clip's own start. Nested compositions inside a split half are cut by every enclosing in-point host. Hosts are found by their composition attributes, so a host without an id counts.

Every host without an in-point, and every project without one, resolves exactly as on main on every path: start, end, audio scheduling (same-origin and cross-origin) and `hyperframes timeline`. A guard test pins that.

- `packages/core/src/mediaTiming.ts`: `hostInPointSeconds`, `compositionOriginSeconds` and `cutToHostSlots`, shared by preview and the CLI timeline.
- `startResolver.ts`: host offsets come from the origin; enclosing in-point hosts are collected by composition attributes.
- `media.ts`, `init.ts`, `webAudioTransport.ts`: preview and audio scheduling cut to in-point hosts' slots; a clip an in-point host cuts away entirely is never scheduled.
- `describeProject.ts`: `hyperframes timeline` places and cuts rows the same way, only for hosts with an in-point above 0.

Media marked as root time (`data-hf-media-start-basis="global"`) keeps its authored time. This revives the composition-origin model from an earlier attempt (#3826, closed as stale): `hostStart + (local − inPoint)`, with root-time media left alone. Its renderer, snapshot and engine parts are left for the follow-up PRs.

Not changed here, and kept as on main: a split's first half (in-point 0) behaves exactly like any unsplit host. So a clip with fades that straddles the split still fits both fades into the first half's remainder, and splitting a host that has no id still lets the first half's copy run past the split. Both come from how main treats any host without an in-point, and changing them is a separate decision. A host's playback rate still doesn't scale the media inside it. Render and snapshot run the same runtime, so they pick up part of this; their own placement code follows in the next PRs.

## Checked

- New core tests (resolver, sub-composition placement, audio scheduling, decoded-audio fallback) and a new CLI timeline test, each built from a split fixture: nested compositions inside a half, a looping clip, a speed ramp and a fade-in across the split, a relative start under a host whose in-point is past its start, and a split half without an id. They fail on main (for example `expected [ 9, 13 ] to deeply equal [ 4, 8 ]`) and pass three runs in a row on Linux.
- Guard test `init.noInPointParity.test.ts`: 13 unsplit fixtures (1 to 3 levels of nesting, root length from its animation, `data-end`, relative starts, a host without an id, a host under a different id, root-time media, looping and faded clips, same-origin and cross-origin audio, a scene trimmed shorter than its file) record each element's start, its source time and volume at 12 seek points, and what both audio routes are asked to play. The expected values were produced by running the fixtures against main's code; the test passes on main and on this branch. A few other no-in-point tests in this PR also pass on main by design.
- Full core suite: 4552 pass. CLI timeline suite: 106 pass. Studio player and hooks suites: 3858 pass. Typecheck clean for core and cli.

title: fix(studio): Studio's own text reads without em or en dashes
body:
## What

Text a person reads in Studio no longer uses em dashes (—) or en dashes (–). That covers Studio's own tooltips, toasts, empty states, errors and labels, and the messages it shows from other packages: lint findings, SDK save refusals, studio-server errors, audio FX and preset copy from core, and render errors from the producer and engine. They now use a colon, a comma, a period, parentheses, or "to" for a range. A new lint check keeps it that way.

## Why

Studio's text should use plain punctuation, and the dashes were used inconsistently across it. A lint check is the root fix: without it, new text brings them back.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `scripts/check-studio-copy-dashes.mjs` parses every non-test `.ts`/`.tsx` file under `src` in `studio`, `core`, `engine`, `lint`, `parsers`, `player`, `producer`, `sdk`, `shader-transitions` and `studio-server` with the TypeScript compiler. It fails on U+2013 or U+2014 inside string literals, template literal parts and JSX text. It reads the parsed value, so an escaped `—` counts too, and it also catches `—`, `–` and their numeric forms, which JSX keeps raw and React renders as dashes. Comments, regex literals and test files are not checked. It runs in the root `lint` script as `check:studio-copy-dashes`; its test is in `test:scripts`.
- On main it reports 304 hits: studio 106, producer 51, lint 50, core 42, engine 38, sdk 6, player 5, parsers 2, shader-transitions 2, studio-server 2. Each was rewritten by hand:
  - a pause became a colon, a comma, "so", or a new sentence (`Copy failed — check permissions` → `Copy failed. Check permissions`, `Linked audio would start after the new end — unlink or trim` → `... after the new end. Unlink or trim`);
  - a range became "to" (`0.0s – 10.0s` → `0.0s to 10.0s`, `try 600–1000` → `try 600 to 1000`);
  - a lone dash used as an empty value became a word: the Peak Amplitude readout shows `Unavailable` (no measurable peak), an unset in/out point in the shortcuts panel shows `Not set`, the text-case "none" button shows `None`, and the select placeholder `— select branch —` became `Select branch`.
  - where the dash sat in a comment inside code that ships as a string (audio worklet source, GLSL, player CSS, injected page scripts), the comment was reworded the same way; behaviour is unchanged.
- No hyphen was swapped in for a dash.
- Two narrow exemptions, each matched on its exact text in its file:
  - `core/src/compiler/compositionScoping.ts`: a comment inside injected runtime JS ("Swallow — the scoped root ..."). It is copied byte for byte into the producer's regression goldens and the docs catalog payloads, and no person reads it.
  - `core/src/figma/mediaIndex.ts`: the `"—"` empty cell of `.media/index.md`, a file written for agents. It must stay identical to the two media-use copies of the same generator, which a parity test enforces.
- Not scanned, because Studio never shows their text: `cli` (terminal output), `aws-lambda`, `gcp-cloud-run`, `sdk-playground`, and Studio's dev-only `vite.config.ts`.
- Tests that asserted the old text were updated (studio, engine `hdr`, producer `hdrMode`, cli `checkBrowser`, studio `sdkCutover.linkedTiming`). `packages/producer/de-gatecheck.sh` greps one engine log line and now matches the new wording. `docs/studio/animation.mdx` quotes the new "Computed value" notice.

## Review

Independent adversarial review of the Studio-only commits: no blocking findings. Should-fix items were addressed: the docs line, HTML entities in the check, test coverage for every node kind and the file filter, and the empty peak value wording.

## Test plan

- Check on main (bb9e507e8): exit 1, 304 hits (per package above). On this branch: passes.
- Gate test: 5/5 pass, 3 runs in a row. Each mutation fails it: removing any checked node kind, narrowing the file filter to `.ts`, dropping or narrowing any entity form, dropping the case-insensitive flag, dropping a package from the scan, or widening an exemption.
- `bun run lint` and `bun run format:check`: green.
- Typecheck green for core, engine, producer, lint, sdk, parsers, player, shader-transitions, studio-server, cli and studio.
- Test suites (Linux): core 198 files, engine 91, producer 54, lint 20, sdk 23, parsers 45, player 17, shader-transitions 6, studio-server 69, studio 694, all passing. cli: 306 files pass. 2 files (`browser/launch.process`, `motion-signature.browser.chromium`) fail the same way with and without this change, from timeouts launching the browser on that machine.
- Changed test files pass 3 runs in a row.
- Before/After captures of the Linked Selection tooltip from the Studio dev server on the `product-promo` registry example.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

## Before

![Before: Linked Selection tooltip with an em dash](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05eebbba-00e4-493b-9ebb-6c34cc1dcebb)

## After

![After: Linked Selection tooltip with a colon](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/851f1bea-f1f1-4c73-a47d-f26829fb69f8)

title: drawElement capture drops a sub-composition whose slot starts after 0 s (renders of 700+ frames)
media-use transcript-cut: -ss/-to rounded to the millisecond drop a frame at 30, 29.97 and 60 fps
body:
### Describe the bug `fmt()` in `skills/media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.mjs` rounds every time it passes to ffmpeg to 3 decimals (`round3(n).toFixed(3)`), including `-ss` and the `-to` length of each segment. At frame rates whose frame times are not whole milliseconds (30, 29.97, 60), a keep range that starts exactly on a frame can be rounded to just after it. For example, 12.866667 s (frame 386 at 30 fps) becomes `-ss 12.867`, ffmpeg's accurate seek discards that frame, and the segment starts one frame late. After the concat, the picture is one frame behind the sound from that join on, and the output is one frame short. 25 fps is unaffected, because every frame time there is a whole millisecond. Still present on `main` as of 2026-10-10. Reported to HeyGen support on 2026-10-09; support confirmed it and asked for this issue. ### Minimal reproduction ```bash ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 -f lavfi -i sine=f=440:sample_rate=48000 \ -t 30 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac src.mp4 echo '[{"text":"a","start":0.1,"end":29.9}]' > words.json node /media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.mjs --input src.mp4 --transcript words.json \ --keep "0-8,12.866667-18.4,25.9-29.9" --out cut.mp4 ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run the commands above. 2. Count the frames: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -count_packets -show_entries stream=nb_read_packets -of csv=p=0 cut.mp4` 3. Look for a timestamp gap: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -show_entries packet=pts_time -of csv=p=0 cut.mp4 | sort -n | awk 'NR>1 && $1-p>0.036 {print "gap at", $1} {p=$1}'` ### Expected behavior 526 frames (240 + 166 + 120) and no gaps. ### Actual behavior 525 frames, and a one-frame gap at 8.033 s: the second segment starts with the frame at 12.9 s instead of the one at 12.866667 s. On real 4K 30 fps footage cut into 11 segments, 3 joins slipped this way. Measured against the source with the script below, the picture ended up 100 ms behind the sound. ### Environment ```shell media-use skill from heygen-com/hyperframes (installed with `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`; fmt() is unchanged on main) ✓ Version 0.8.145 (latest) ✓ Node.js v24.10.0 (darwin arm64) ✓ CPU 15 cores · Apple M5 Pro @ 2400MHz ✓ Memory 48.0 GB total ✓ FFmpeg ffmpeg 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg ✓ FFprobe ffprobe 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe ✓ Chrome renders used HeadlessChrome/152.0.7977.30 (hardware GPU, ANGLE Metal) macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) ``` ### Additional context Suggested fix: pass `-ss` and `-to` at full precision (for example `toFixed(6)`) and keep the 3-decimal `fmt()` for display only. Workaround we use: floor each segment's start, and its frame-exact length, to the millisecond before passing them as `--keep`, so the rounding can never land past a frame.
measure.py: where each kept segment really lands in the output, in picture and in sound Usage: `python measure.py SOURCE OUTPUT SEGMENTS_JSON FPS`, where `SEGMENTS_JSON` is `[[start, end], ...]` in output order. A correct cut reads 0 ms everywhere. ```python """Where does each kept source segment really land in the output, in picture and in sound? usage: measure.py SOURCE OUTPUT SEGMENTS_JSON FPS SEGMENTS_JSON: [[start, end], ...] source ranges in output order (what the editor planned). Prints per segment: deviation of video and audio from the planned output time, and A/V offset (positive = sound late). Captions in both systems sit on the planned timeline, so "caption error" = -audio deviation (positive = caption late). """ import json, subprocess, sys import numpy as np SR = 16000 W, H = 32, 18 def audio(path): raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-map", "0:a:0", "-ac", "1", "-ar", str(SR), "-f", "f32le", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout return np.frombuffer(raw, np.float32) def frames(path): raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-map", "0:v:0", "-fps_mode", "passthrough", "-vf", f"crop=iw*0.45:ih*0.4:iw*0.5:ih*0.2,scale={W}:{H}:flags=area,format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout f = np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8).reshape(-1, H, W).astype(np.float32) f -= f.mean(axis=(1, 2), keepdims=True) return f / (f.std(axis=(1, 2), keepdims=True) + 1e-6) def main(): src, out, segs, fps = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], json.load(open(sys.argv[3])), float(eval(sys.argv[4])) As, Ao, Fs, Fo = audio(src), audio(out), frames(src), frames(out) planned = 0.0 rows = [] for i, (s, e) in enumerate(segs): L = min(1.0, (e - s) - 0.2) p = s + 0.1 # audio: normalized cross-correlation of 1 s of source sound against the output near its planned spot ref = As[int(p * SR):int((p + L) * SR)] t0 = planned + (p - s) - 0.4 win = Ao[max(0, int(t0 * SR)):int((t0 + L + 0.8) * SR)] best, lag = -2, 0 for k in range(0, len(win) - len(ref)): seg = win[k:k + len(ref)] c = float(np.dot(seg, ref) / (np.linalg.norm(seg) * np.linalg.norm(ref) + 1e-9)) if c > best: best, lag = c, k a_dev = (max(0, int(t0 * SR)) + lag) / SR - (planned + p - s) # video: best-matching run of 10 frames near the planned output frame k = int(round(p * fps)) refv = Fs[k:k + 10] j0 = int(round((planned + k / fps - s) * fps)) cands = [(float(np.abs(Fo[j:j + 10] - refv).mean()), j) for j in range(max(0, j0 - 8), min(len(Fo) - 10, j0 + 8))] sad, j = min(cands) v_dev = j / fps - (planned + k / fps - s) # audio deviation measured at p; shift to the frame instant k/fps (same linear map) rows.append((i, planned, v_dev * 1000, a_dev * 1000, (a_dev - v_dev) * 1000, best, sad)) planned += e - s print(f"{'seg':>3} {'planned_s':>9} {'video_ms':>9} {'audio_ms':>9} {'AV_ms':>7} {'corr':>5} {'sad':>5}") for r in rows: print(f"{r[0]:>3} {r[1]:>9.3f} {r[2]:>9.1f} {r[3]:>9.1f} {r[4]:>7.1f} {r[5]:>5.2f} {r[6]:>5.2f}") main() ```

title: media-use transcript-cut: millisecond frame timestamps make the renderer repeat frames
body:
### Describe the bug `transcript-cut.mjs` encodes each segment to a `.mkv` intermediate (1 ms timebase) and joins them with the concat demuxer and `-c:v copy`, so the output's frame timestamps are quantized to whole milliseconds (0.067 instead of 0.0667). At 30 fps about two thirds of the frames end up a fraction of a millisecond off the frame grid. When that cut is used as footage in a composition, the renderer looks frames up by exact time and shows the previous frame wherever a timestamp is late, while the real frame is skipped. It reads as stutter in motion. This is independent of the capture mode (the repro below renders with screenshot capture) and of #5416 (the repro uses cut points that are whole milliseconds). Reported to HeyGen support on 2026-10-09; support confirmed it and asked for this issue. Related: `transcript-cut` does not set a keyframe interval, so the renderer warns about its own output: `Video "a-roll" has sparse keyframes (max interval: 8.33s). This causes seek failures and frame freezing.` (x264's default of 250 frames at 30 fps). ### Minimal reproduction ```bash ffmpeg -f lavfi -i testsrc2=size=1280x720:rate=30 -f lavfi -i sine=f=440:sample_rate=48000 \ -t 30 -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac src.mp4 echo '[{"text":"a","start":0.1,"end":29.9}]' > words.json node /media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.mjs --input src.mp4 --transcript words.json \ --keep "0-8,12.8-18.4,25.9-29.9" --out cut.mp4 # the same cut with its timestamps put back on the 1/30 s grid (lossless) ffmpeg -i cut.mp4 -map 0 -c copy -video_track_timescale 30 cut-ongrid.mp4 for v in cut cut-ongrid; do npx hyperframes init p_$v --non-interactive --video $v.mp4 --skip-transcribe (cd p_$v && npx hyperframes render --quality standard -o ../render_$v.mp4) done ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Run the commands above. 2. Count frames off the 1/30 s grid: `ffprobe -v error -select_streams v -show_entries packet=pts_time -of csv=p=0 cut.mp4 | sort -n | awk '{d=$1-(NR-1)/30; if(d>0.0002||d<-0.0002)n++} END{print n+0, "of", NR}'` 3. Compare each rendered frame with the cut: `python framecheck.py cut.mp4 render_cut.mp4`, then `python framecheck.py cut-ongrid.mp4 render_cut-ongrid.mp4` (script below). ### Expected behavior Rendered frame N shows cut frame N for every frame. ### Actual behavior - `cut.mp4`: 528 frames, no gaps, but 352 of 528 off the frame grid. The render shows the previous frame for 89 of 528 frames (17%). - `cut-ongrid.mp4`: 0 off the grid, and 0 repeated frames in its render. On a real 4K 30 fps project (2930 frames, drawElement capture), 97 frames (3.3%) were repeats. ### Environment ```shell ✓ Version 0.8.145 (latest) ✓ Node.js v24.10.0 (darwin arm64) ✓ CPU 15 cores · Apple M5 Pro @ 2400MHz ✓ Memory 48.0 GB total ✓ FFmpeg ffmpeg 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg ✓ FFprobe ffprobe 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe ✓ Chrome renders used HeadlessChrome/152.0.7977.30 (hardware GPU, ANGLE Metal) macOS 26.6.2 (25G83) ``` ### Additional context Suggested fixes, any one of which removes the extra step: - write the intermediates as `.mov` with `-video_track_timescale` set to the frame rate's numerator, or remux the final output onto the frame grid; - in the renderer, take the nearest frame (half-frame tolerance) when looking up video frames; - set `-g` to the frame rate in the intermediate encode (one keyframe per second), as support suggested, to silence the sparse-keyframe warning. Workaround we use for 30000/1001 too: two lossless remuxes, first into a timescale of the fps numerator, then `-bsf:v "setts=pts=round(PTS/1001)*1001:dts=round(DTS/1001)*1001"`.
framecheck.py: which frame of a reference does every output frame show? Usage: `python framecheck.py REF OUT`. Compares a crop clear of overlays and prints the histogram of (matched reference frame − output frame); `{0: N}` means every frame is right. ```python """For every frame of OUT, which frame of REF (same timeline) does it show? Overlay-free crop only. usage: framecheck.py REF OUT Prints the histogram of (matched REF frame - OUT frame index) and the runs where it is not 0. """ import subprocess, sys import numpy as np W, H = 48, 27 CROP = "crop=iw*0.45:ih*0.4:iw*0.5:ih*0.2" # right-middle: clear of the title (top-left) and captions (bottom) def frames(path): raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", path, "-map", "0:v:0", "-fps_mode", "passthrough", "-vf", f"{CROP},scale={W}:{H}:flags=area,format=gray", "-f", "rawvideo", "-"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout return np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8).reshape(-1, H, W).astype(np.float32) ref, out = frames(sys.argv[1]), frames(sys.argv[2]) n = min(len(ref), len(out)) shift = [] for j in range(n): cands = [(float(np.abs(ref[k] - out[j]).mean()), k - j) for k in range(max(0, j - 4), min(len(ref), j + 5))] d0 = float(np.abs(ref[j] - out[j]).mean()) best, s = min(cands) shift.append(s if best < d0 - 0.5 else 0) # only count a shift when it is clearly better than "same frame" shift = np.array(shift) print("frames", len(ref), len(out), "| shift histogram:", {int(k): int(v) for k, v in zip(*np.unique(shift, return_counts=True))}) runs, start = [], None for j, s in enumerate(list(shift) + [0]): if s != 0 and start is None: start = j if (s == 0 or (start is not None and s != shift[start])) and start is not None: runs.append((start, j - 1, int(shift[start]))) start = j if s != 0 else None for a, b, s in runs[:40]: print(f" frames {a}-{b} ({a/30:.2f}-{b/30:.2f}s): shows ref frame {s:+d}") print("runs:", len(runs)) ```

title: Registry blocks render at 1080p size in a 4K root; scale them to the root
body:
### Problem Catalog blocks are authored at a fixed 1920×1080. Mounted with `data-composition-src` in a `landscape-4k` root (3840×2160, for example from `hyperframes init --resolution 4k`), they render at their 1080p pixel size in the top-left quarter of the frame: a lower third ends up small and mid-left, and a caption component sits in the middle of the left half. `lint` and `check` say nothing, so it only shows up in a snapshot or render. Anyone editing 4K footage, the default on most current cameras and phones, hits this with the first registry block. Raised with HeyGen support on 2026-10-09; support suggested the workaround below and asked for an issue. ### Proposed solution When a mounted block's `data-width`/`data-height` differ from the host root's, scale the mount to the root automatically (keeping the aspect ratio), or offer an attribute for it (for example `data-fit="scale"`). At minimum, have `lint` or `check` warn when a block's size differs from the root's and suggest the fix. ### Alternatives considered Scaling the mount by hand works, and is what we do today: ```html
``` It has to be repeated on every mount, and the 2 has to change for other root sizes. ### Additional context hyperframes 0.8.145, macOS 26.6.2. Seen with `lt-side-rule` and `caption-pill-karaoke`.

title: feat(core): truepeak, a lookahead true-peak limiter FX
body:
## What

`truepeak` is a new lookahead true-peak limiter FX. The existing `limiter` is an envelope follower with no lookahead and no inter-sample detection, so its ceiling does not guarantee the peak.

`truepeak` works in four steps:
- it estimates the true peak with a 4x polyphase interpolator;
- it takes the minimum gain needed over a lookahead window;
- it smooths that gain with a boxcar of the same length;
- it recovers with an exponential release.

One gain is shared by all channels. The params are `ceiling` (dBTP), `lookahead` (0.5 to 10 ms, default 3) and `release` (ms, default 80). It can be used anywhere a chain is accepted. It is the first of two stacked PRs; the second adds a composition master bus that uses it.

## Why

Cut Room is moving audio mastering into the composition. A probe against the render service found that a `limiter` with a -14 dB ceiling left the true peak 6.2 dB over.

## Measured

The probe mix was VO at +6 dB plus a music bed, with a true peak of -6.8 dBFS before limiting. It was rendered with `applyAudioFxChain` and measured with `ffmpeg ebur128=peak=true`:

| Ceiling | old `limiter` true peak | `truepeak` true peak |
|---|---|---|
| -10 | -6.8 (no action) | -10.0 |
| -14 | -7.8 | -14.0 |
| -18 | -11.0 | -18.0 |
| -24 | -13.5 | -24.0 |

A 192k AAC encode moves the `truepeak` figures by at most 0.1 dB.

The ceiling is held against a 4x oversampled estimate, so the real true peak can end above it. Checked against an ideal 16x interpolation (zero-padded FFT, cross-checked with a 16x soxr resample):
- Tones land on the ceiling to within 0.03 dB (0.38 dB at 23.9 kHz).
- Pink noise ends 0.2 to 0.6 dB over.
- Hot full-band white noise ends 1.0 to 1.7 dB over (median 1.4 dB over 28 runs of 10 to 30 s).

ffmpeg `ebur128=peak=true` is also a 4x meter and reads the same noise about 0.1 dB over, so it does not show this. An earlier figure of about 0.3 dB for broadband material came from a 96-tap windowed-sinc test meter that reads full-band noise about 0.5 dB low. The tests now use the ideal interpolator, with tolerances equal to what it measures (tones 0.01 dB, dense program 0.5 dB, full-band noise 1.35 dB).

The docs, the `hyperframes-audio` skill and the rack copy state the 4x estimate and recommend leaving at least 2 dB under a hard delivery limit (-3 dBTP for -1). `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated.

## Studio copy (round 2)

Studio shows `audioFxCopy.ts`, not the registry description, so the margin never reached a Studio user. The ceiling control no longer promises a hard limit:

| Where | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Ceiling label | Never exceed | Target ceiling |
| Ceiling hint (new, shown as the row tooltip) | none | Measured with a 4x estimate. Dense full-band sound can end up to about 1.7 dB above it, so leave headroom: -3 for a -1 dBTP limit. |
| Rack blurb | Holds the loudest moments, including the ones between samples, to a ceiling. | Pulls the loudest moments, including the ones between samples, down toward a target ceiling. |
| Reach-for line | The finished mix must not clip once it is encoded. | Peaks need to stay under a delivery limit. |
| Knob ends | A lot of headroom / Right up to the edge | A lot of headroom / Little headroom |
| Rack summary | True peak held near -1 dBTP | Peaks pulled down toward -1 dBTP |
| Registry hint | Highest true peak allowed, measured on a 4x oversampled signal. | Target true peak, measured on a 4x oversampled signal. Dense full-band sound can end up to about 1.7 dB above it. |
| `hyperframes-audio` SKILL.md | "for a hard dBTP ceiling use `truepeak`" | "for a delivery ceiling use `truepeak`", with "holds a 4x estimate at the ceiling, not the waveform itself" |

`audioFxCopy.test.ts` gains a test that the shown copy never says "never exceed", "must not clip", "never above" or "guarantee", and that the hint names the 4x estimate, 1.7 dB and headroom. `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated (`hyperframes-audio` hash changed) and `--check` passes.

## Preview and render

Both paths run the same worklet: preview in a live `AudioContext`, render in an `OfflineAudioContext` in headless Chrome.
- **Render:** the lookahead delay is trimmed, so the clip stays sample-aligned and keeps its length.
- **Preview:** it plays the delay (3.3 to 10.3 ms across the lookahead range, 3.3 ms at the default), uncompensated, and the docs now say so in ms. A seek clears the limiter's delay line and held gain on a group or master bus.
- **Changing params:** changing `lookahead` rebuilds the node, while `ceiling` and `release` update live.

## Tests

`audioFxTruePeak.test.ts` covers:
- an inter-sample peak (fs/4 at 45 degrees, sample peak 0.707, true peak 1.0) held under -6 dBTP, which the old limiter misses by more than 1 dB on the same signal;
- an abrupt onset and a dense program;
- transparency and exact latency;
- the release time constant;
- one gain shared across channels;
- live vs fixed params;
- a `__hfReset` message empties the delay line and the held gain (with a no-reset control that still carries both).

Engine tests (real Chrome + ffmpeg) check that the limiter holds a true peak and stays sample-aligned.

Not run locally (left to CI): the producer, studio and full suites.

## Round 2 minors

- **Fallow audit (non-required, was red):** the three unused exports (`TRUE_PEAK_OVERSAMPLE`, `TRUE_PEAK_DETECTOR_DELAY`, `truePeakLookaheadSamples`) are no longer exported. The same audit also counted four findings this PR introduced in tests: a 12-line clone of the worklet test's processor loader (now one shared `audioFxProcessors.test-helpers.ts`, excluded from the package build like `*.test.ts`), an 8-line FFT bit-reversal clone of `audioCarve.ts` (the test FFT now permutes by bit-reversed index), and two test bodies over the CRAP threshold (split). `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` exits 0 locally.
- **Comments (non-required, was red):** the 12-line `audioFxTruePeak.ts` header is 4 lines. Every comment block this PR adds is now 4 lines or fewer (`audioFxTail.ts`, the test header comments), and `check-comment-citations.mjs` and `comment-ratchet.mjs` pass.
- **Preview gain reduction across a seek:** fixed. The processor takes `__hfReset`; `FxChainHandle.reset()` forwards it; `attachElementFxChain().reanchor()` (what a group bus runs on a seek or replay) calls it. Per-clip chains are rebuilt on every play and were not affected.
- **Preview lookahead delay (3.3 to 10.3 ms late):** not compensated, on purpose. Pulling a media element earlier by the chain latency would put a second clock into the sync loop for a delay well under the lip-sync threshold; the docs state the figure instead.

## Questions

- `limiter` is unchanged because every preset ends in it. Should the presets move to `truepeak`?
- Preview latency (3.3 to 10.3 ms) is documented, not compensated.

— Jerrai

title: feat(audio): composition master bus (data-fx-chain on the root)
body:
## Before

The composition below is one `<video>` with audio and a `truepeak` limiter in the root's `data-fx-chain`. Studio read nothing from the root chain, so it did not count the video as audio: no meter toggle in the timeline toolbar, no program meter.

![Before: no audio meter toggle and no program meter](https://www.heygenverse.com/s/515697e3-1fca-4b7f-9d6c-15a1cc9792ad/raw)

## After

Same project. The timeline toolbar has the audio meter toggle and the Monitor meter strip shows (toggled on here), because the root's master chain is read onto the clip and an audible video under a master chain counts as audio.

![After: audio meter toggle and the Monitor meter strip](https://www.heygenverse.com/s/f5a10d89-3968-4273-86cd-c5830dec4054/raw)

Captured in a real Studio (Vite dev server) on a 6 s test video with a 330 Hz tone and a root `truepeak` at -1 dBTP. "Before" is this branch with the two `masterChain` reads in `packages/studio/src/player/lib/timelineDOM.ts` disabled, which is exactly the Studio diff against the `truepeak` PR. Not exercised: playing audio through the meter, dark theme, a muted video, a sub-composition root chain.

## What

This adds a composition master bus. A clip can belong to only one audio group, so there was no way to put one effect, such as a true-peak limiter, across the whole mix.

- The master bus is the `data-fx-chain` on the top-level composition root. No new attribute: a root's `data-fx-chain` was previously applied to nothing.
- The chain runs once over the sum of every clip and group, after each group's own chain and fader.
- A sub-composition root's `data-fx-chain` still does nothing (it is neither the master nor its clips' chain), and on clips and groups `data-fx-chain` means what it always did.
- It stacks on the `truepeak` PR.

## Preview and render

| | Where the chain runs |
|---|---|
| Preview | the transport splices the chain between the sum of clips and groups and the monitor |
| Render | `mixAudioTracks` writes a float WAV, `applyAudioFxChain` runs the chain, and ffmpeg encodes AAC last |

- Only the top-level root is read, so repeating a sub-composition cannot stack master chains. There is no lint rule: the attribute is valid on every element it can sit on.
- One behaviour change: a stray `data-fx-chain` left on a top-level root, inert before, now runs as the master bus. Nothing in this repo writes one there.
- An unreadable master chain fails the mix with `elementId: "master"`. In preview it plays dry, the same as a broken group chain.
- A render with no master chain takes the old code path unchanged.
- There is no master automation: `data-automation` on the root is not read as the master's.

## Preview joins every audible video (round 2)

The master chain exists only inside the Web Audio graph, and a `<video>` used to join that graph only for its own chain, group, automation or a volume over 1. So a talking head under a root `truepeak` played dry in preview while the music was limited, and a composition whose only audio is video got no master chain at all. Render already summed every audible element into the master.

A master chain on the top-level root is now a reason to join, like a video's own `data-fx-chain`:
- `audibleVideoNeedsWebAudio` takes a `masterChain` field (`packages/core/src/audibleVideo.ts`);
- `joinsWebAudio` in `packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts` passes `readMasterFxChain(el.ownerDocument)`;
- audio elements already always joined.

Unchanged: a root with no chain keeps a unity video on native output; muted and `data-has-audio="false"` videos stay out; a chain on a sub-composition root does not count. The root chain is read when media is scheduled (play, seek, rate change), the same moment a video's own `data-fx-chain` is read.

Tests: a plain audible video at unity under a root chain is scheduled and acquires a media element source; the same video with no root chain stays native (existing test); a video-only composition plus an audio clip both join; a muted video stays out; a sub-composition root chain does not count; at transport level a plain video played from its element goes through the master bus (`masterGain` is spliced out of the monitor). Reverting the `joinsWebAudio` line fails 3 of the new init tests, and reverting the `audibleVideo.ts` change fails those 3 plus the predicate test.

## Tests

- Engine tests (real Chrome + ffmpeg):
  - a master limiter holds the summed mix of two hot tones;
  - ordering: a group limiter at -20 with a 0.5 fader, then a +12 dB master, lands at -14 dBFS (a fader before the limiter would give -8, a master before the group -26);
  - an unreadable chain is a failure;
  - from authored HTML, a -6 dBTP limiter then a -6 dB gain in the root chain over two 0.3 tones lands at -12 dB; per clip it would read -10.4 and applied twice -18, so it runs once over the sum;
  - the sum stays float until the chain reads it (a -6 dB master gain over a +5 dBFS sum lands at -1, not at -6);
  - a fatal FX error in the master pass or in a group bus removes the work directory (`audioMixer.test.ts`).
- The root chain reaches clips only as the master; a sub-composition root's chain is neither master nor its clips' chain; the top-level root wins when both carry one.
- Also covered: the transport, the graph, shape, tail and latency.
- Not run locally (left to CI): the producer, studio and full suites.

## Docs

`docs/reference/audio-effects.mdx` gets a master-bus section. The `hyperframes-audio` skill is updated in SKILL.md, `attributes.md` and `fx-registry.md`.

## Round 2 minors

- **Temp dir on a master-pass error (`audioMixer.ts`):** the final mix now runs in `try/finally` and the group `AudioFxRenderError` rethrow removes the work directory first, so neither path leaves the float sum on disk. Both are covered by tests that fail without the change.
- **"-6 dB over two clips gives -12 dB" test:** it could not tell a per-clip chain from one over the sum (gain is linear), and its comment's "-9" was wrong. It now uses a limiter then a gain, where per clip reads -10.4 and twice reads -18.
- **Fader-order test:** `groupVolume` is 0.5 now, so the fader sits between the group limiter and the master and the test fails if either order changes.
- **Sum stays float:** new test; a 16-bit clipped sum would pass the old limiter test.
- **"Four rules exist":** now "Three rules exist" (the master-bus lint rule was removed with `data-master-fx-chain`).
- **Bad master chain:** docs now say what happens. In this repo `audio_processing_failed` blocks the render (`RenderQualityError`) under every strictness setting, so nothing is exported; preview plays dry with no message. They also say that no lint rule checks a chain's contents.
- **Sub-composition file on its own:** documented. Opened or rendered alone it is the top-level root, so its chain is the master bus there.
- **Nested-root lint gap:** moot. The lint rule that skipped `data-composition-id` elements went with `data-master-fx-chain`; no lint code is in this PR, and the docs no longer promise a warning.
- **Preview skips a seek:** the master bus re-anchors on a seek and now also clears the limiter's delay line and held gain (same `reset` as the group bus, in the `truepeak` PR).
- **Studio meter:** `hasProjectAudio` hid the meter for a video-only composition whose only routing is the root chain. `TimelineElement.masterChain` now carries the root's `data-fx-chain` (set in `timelineDOM.ts`, both the manifest and DOM paths), and the existing `audibleVideoNeedsWebAudio` call sees it. Tests in `audioMeterMath.test.ts` and `timelineDOM.test.ts`; not run locally (no Studio dependencies installed), left to CI.
- **Fallow audit (non-required, was red):** `webAudioTransport.setRate` was over the CRAP threshold; its group and master loops are one `setBusRate`. An introduced 8-line clone in the engine test is a shared `mixedPeakDb` helper. Exit 0 locally.
- **Comments:** every block this PR adds is 4 lines or fewer, and the one-line comment I had added to `audibleVideo.ts` is gone because the comment-share ratchet (run by CI, first time on that commit) refuses a raised share.

## Round 4

- **Master chain with only a producer-added track (Miguel):** the master chain was carried on each parsed `AudioElement`, so a track the producer adds itself never had it. That is `appendAutoDetectedVideoAudio` (`extractVideosStage.ts`) and the browser-discovered audio in `probeStage.ts`: a `<video>` whose `src` is set at runtime has no parsed audio entry, so the producer adds one after probing. When that was the only audio, nothing carried the chain and the export had no ceiling and no warning.
  - It is now a composition property. `parseMasterFxChain(html)` runs at compile, `CompiledComposition` and `CompositionMetadata` carry it, and `runAudioStage` passes it to `processCompositionAudio` (in-process and distributed plan). `AudioElement.masterFxChain` is removed so there is one source.
  - A static `<video>` with no `data-has-audio` was not affected: the compiler stamps `data-has-audio="true"` and the parsed track carried the chain.
  - Measured on a real local render (producer from source, software Chrome, draft quality, 3 s clip): the only audio is a `<video>` whose `src` is set by a script, and the root has a `truepeak` at -6 dBTP. The source clip peaks at -0.2 dBFS. Before this change the output peaks at -1.4 dBFS (sample and 4x true peak; the pipeline's own -1 dBTP safety lowered it 1.2 dB), 4.6 dB over the authored ceiling. With it the output peaks at -5.7 dBFS, 0.3 dB over the ceiling (the limiter holds a 4x estimate on the float mix, then AAC encoding adds a fraction of a dB). One fixture, one run each.
  - Tests: `audioStage.test.ts` (a track added by `appendAutoDetectedVideoAudio` over an empty `audios`, chain reaches the mixer); `htmlCompiler.test.ts` (the compiled composition exposes the root chain); one test per forward (`compileStage.test.ts`, `renderOrchestrator.masterBus.test.ts`, `distributed/plan.masterBus.test.ts`), each red when its forward is removed; the engine master-bus tests now pass the chain beside the tracks. Dropping the forwarding in `audioStage.ts` fails the stage test; dropping it from the compiled composition fails the compiler test; ignoring it in the mixer fails four engine tests.
- **"Never clips" (Miguel, on the `truepeak` PR):** the plain `limiter` is level-following with no lookahead, and Level after is applied past its ceiling. Studio's description, panel text, knob label and summary, and the `hyperframes-audio` skill, no longer say nothing gets past it. They say a fast or inter-sample peak can pass and point to the true-peak limiter for a delivery limit. The copy lives in files from the `truepeak` PR (`audioFx.ts`, `audioFxCopy.ts`), changed here. A copy test guards the wording; restoring the old text fails it.

## Follow-ups

- Master-bus automation, and Studio UI for authoring the master chain.
- The distributed-render path is untested.
- The pitch shifter's latency is still not trimmed in render. `chainLatencySamples` is where that fix would go.

— Jerrai

title: feat(producer): distributed renders accept 25 fps
body:
## What

Distributed renders (Lambda and Cloud Run) accept 25 fps. The distributed fps set is now `{24, 25, 30, 60}`.

## Why

25 fps is the PAL rate, and footage shot in Europe and much of the world records at it. Distributed renders refused it everywhere the set is checked, so a 25 fps project could render locally but not on Lambda or Cloud Run. Rendering it at 24 or 30 instead retimes every frame.

The set excludes non-integer NTSC rates on purpose (`docs/deploy/migrating-to-hyperframes-lambda.mdx`). 25 is an integer rate like the other three, and nothing in plan, chunk or assemble depends on which integer it is.

## Related work

No issue or open PR covers this. #5348 touches `packages/cli/src/utils/compositionFps.ts`, where this PR changes only the comment naming the set.

## How

The set is written out in each place that checks it, and this PR adds 25 to each:

- Producer: `renderConfigValidation.ts` (`ALLOWED_FPS`), the plan v2 manifest reader and writer in `planV2.ts`, the `plan.ts` config types, and `distributedFps` in `renderRequest.ts`.
- `DistributedRenderConfig.fps` in the Lambda and Cloud Run event types.
- CLI: the `--fps` checks and the `data-fps` fallback in `lambda render`, `lambda render-batch` and the `cloudrun` commands.
- Regression and plan-parity harnesses, so a 25 fps fixture runs chunked instead of being skipped.
- Docs: `lambda render --fps` in the CLI reference, the Lambda migration table and the producer tests README.

Out of scope: Studio's export menu and the local `render` docs list 24, 30 and 60. Local renders already accept any rate, so that's a separate change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - New: plan v2 writes 25 fps into its manifest and reads it back, and still rejects 50 (`planV2.test.ts`). `distributedConfigFromRequest` maps 25/1 to 25. Lambda and Cloud Run `validateDistributedRenderConfig` accept 25.
  - Tests that used 25 as their unsupported example now use 50.
  - Producer: 661/661 bun tests and 872/873 vitest tests pass. Lambda: 148/148. Cloud Run: 102/102. CLI: 1568/1569.
  - Two tests fail locally on `main` too, with or without this change: `audioPadTrim.integration.test.ts` (true peak 4.4 over a ceiling of 3, from the ffmpeg build) and `history.test.ts` (process lock timing).
- [x] Manual testing performed on a SAM stack in `us-east-2` (10,240 MB function), with the same change applied to v0.8.145:
  - 12 s, 1080×1920, 25 fps project with a video clip, 5 chunks: 300 frames at 25/1, mean SSIM 0.990 (minimum 0.989) against a local render of the same project, no dip at chunk seams, and the burned-in frame counter matches at frames 59/60, 119/120 and 239/240. Audio difference against the local render: −49 dB. Cost $0.014.
  - 40 s, 3840×2160, 25 fps, screen recording plus a camera picture-in-picture, 9 chunks: 1,000 frames, frame-exact against the source footage (camera SSIM 0.990; a one-frame shift drops it to 0.949). Cost $0.12.
  - 20.6 min, 3840×2160, 25 fps, the same screen plus camera layout from 42 source files, 256 chunks: 30,925 frames. Plan 3 min 37 s, total 21 min 29 s, Lambda compute $7.00 (258 invocations, 420,092 GB-s). The chunks ran about 40 at a time, the inline Map state's limit, whatever `--max-parallel-chunks` asked for.
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": the comment ratchet and citation checks pass.

title: tts (Kokoro, macOS): onnxruntime's telemetry aborts Python at exit, so synthesized lines are reported as failed and dropped from the narration
body:
### Describe the bug

On macOS, `hyperframes tts` intermittently reports a Kokoro line as failed **after it was synthesized**. The Python process writes the WAV and prints its JSON, then aborts during interpreter exit inside onnxruntime's 1DS telemetry teardown (SIGABRT). `synthesize.ts` treats any abnormal exit from `execFileSync` as a failure, so the CLI exits 1, and the audio skill (`skills/media-use/audio/scripts/audio.mjs`) records the line as `TTS failed — omitted` under "anomalies (non-fatal)" and still finishes with ✓. The video then plays with a sentence missing unless someone reads the log or listens. macOS also shows a "Python quit unexpectedly" dialog each time.

### Minimal reproduction

Not deterministic: the abort needs a telemetry upload response to arrive while the process is exiting. 26 short runs of the bundled synth script (sequential and 6 in parallel) were clean; the 4 aborts below all came from synth processes that had been running 15–36 s (several lines in parallel, CPU-contended).

### Steps to reproduce

1. On macOS with onnxruntime 1.30.0 (pip), generate narration with the local Kokoro voice, e.g. the faceless-explainer audio step with several lines.
2. Repeat over a day of normal use.
3. Occasionally a line is reported as `TTS failed — omitted (kokoro (npx hyperframes tts) exited with status 1)` and a Python crash report appears in `~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports`.

### Expected behavior

Every line that Kokoro synthesized is kept; a crash after the WAV is written does not drop it.

### Actual behavior

The line is dropped as non-fatal. From the 4 crash reports (identical stacks):

Main thread, during `exit()`:
`start → exit → __cxa_finalize_ranges → onnxruntime::PosixTelemetry::~PosixTelemetry → PosixTelemetry::Shutdown → LogManagerImpl::FlushAndTeardown → HttpClientManager::cancelAllRequests`

Crashing thread (the 1DS HTTP worker handling an upload response):
`WorkerThread::threadFunc → HttpClientManager::onHttpResponse → HttpResponseDecoder::handleDecode → LogManagerImpl::DispatchEvent → DebugEventSource::DispatchEvent → std::recursive_mutex::lock → system_error → std::terminate → abort`

The worker locks a static mutex that exit has already destroyed. In one run the voice log line `line 04: TTS failed — omitted (kokoro (npx hyperframes tts) exited with status 1)` was written at 14:44:34, the same second as a crash report with this stack (process started 14:44:02); re-running the voice step produced all lines.

### Environment

- hyperframes 0.8.145 (same code path on `main` at bb9e507e8, 2026-10-10)
- macOS 15.7.7 (24G720), Apple Silicon (M1 Pro)
- Python 3.14.3, kokoro-onnx 0.4.7, onnxruntime 1.30.0 (its macOS wheel runs 1DS telemetry by default)

### Additional context

**Suggested fix.**

1. Turn off onnxruntime telemetry for the TTS subprocess: pass `env: { ...process.env, ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "1" }` to the `execFileSync` call in `packages/cli/src/tts/synthesize.ts`. The variable is read once when onnxruntime loads, so the 1DS SDK never starts. Verified on this machine: a sample of the synth process 18 s in shows 10 threads including the 1DS HTTP worker (the thread that aborts) by default, and 4 threads with no 1DS code at all with the variable set. It also stops a local, "offline" voice from running Microsoft's telemetry uploader by default, which users may not expect.
2. Optional hardening: if the process exits abnormally but `outputPath` exists and the last stdout line is the expected JSON, treat the line as synthesized (the work finished before the exit-time abort).

The same abort has been reported and worked around the same way by other projects that use onnxruntime from Python on macOS, e.g. sam-dumont/immich-memories#2181, zilliztech/memsearch#747, SModelS/smodels#57, seriouslysean/transcript-combobulator#17. The underlying 1DS behaviour is microsoft/cpp_client_telemetry#1012.

I'll open a PR with (1) and a unit test.

Related: #2775 (narration silently dropped through a different cause; same "non-fatal omission passes every check" theme).

title: fix(cli): turn off onnxruntime telemetry for Kokoro synthesis
body:
## What

Run the Kokoro synthesis subprocess with `ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`.

## Why

onnxruntime's 1DS telemetry is on by default in its macOS Python wheels. When an upload response arrives while the Python process is exiting, the 1DS HTTP worker locks a static mutex that exit already destroyed and the process aborts, after the WAV was written. `execFileSync` throws, `hyperframes tts` exits 1, and the audio skill drops the line as a non-fatal anomaly, so narration can silently lose a sentence. Details, crash stacks and evidence in #5424.

## Related work

Fixes #5424. Related: #2775 (narration dropped through a different cause).

## How

One line: `env: { ...process.env, ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "1" }` on the `execFileSync` call in `packages/cli/src/tts/synthesize.ts`. onnxruntime reads the variable once when it loads, so the 1DS SDK never starts in the synth process; the rest of the environment is passed through unchanged (`HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON`, `PATH`, etc. are unaffected). The explanation lives here rather than in a code comment, per the comment-share ratchet.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `synthesize.cache.test.ts` asserts the synth call passes `ORT_DISABLE_TELEMETRY: "1"`. It fails on `main` ("expected undefined to be '1'") and passes with the change; all 31 tests in `packages/cli/src/tts/` pass (vitest 4.1.11).
- [x] Manual testing performed: sampled the synth process 18 s into a run (macOS 15.7.7, onnxruntime 1.30.0, kokoro-onnx 0.4.7): 10 threads including the 1DS HTTP worker by default; 4 threads and no 1DS code with the variable set. Synthesis output is unchanged.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": no comments added; `check-comment-citations.mjs` OK and `comment-ratchet.mjs` at or under the base share.

title: fix(media-use): keep frame precision on transcript-cut seek boundaries
body:
Fixes #5416.

### The cause

A kept range whose boundary sits on a frame was rounded to the millisecond **twice** on its way to ffmpeg, and at 29.97/30/60 fps a millisecond is enough to land just past the frame. ffmpeg's accurate seek drops everything before the time it is handed, so the frame named by the boundary is lost and the cut comes out a frame short from that join on.

The issue points at `fmt()` in `transcript-cut.mjs`. `fmt()` does round `-ss`/`-to` to 3 decimals, but fixing it alone does not fix the bug, and I measured that before settling on this shape:

- `compileCutList()` already rounds every kept range to 3 decimals in `lib/cutlist.mjs` (both in `mergeRanges` and again in `finalizeKept`), so `fmt()` never sees more precision than `12.867` in the first place.
- With `fmt()` fixed on its own, the issue's own repro still produces the same short cut.

So both roundings are changed. `cutlist.mjs` now keeps 6 decimals on the range bounds (still enough to shed float noise, which is all the rounding was for), and `transcript-cut.mjs` hands `-ss`/`-to` to ffmpeg at full precision. `fmt()` stays at 3 decimals for the times that are only printed.

### Measured

At 30 fps, cutting `0-1,1.0666666666666667-3` from a 4 s source (frame 32 is the 1.0666666 s boundary):

| | frames | gap at the join |
|---|---|---|
| before | 87 | yes, at 1.033 s |
| after | **88** | none |

88 is the correct count: frames 0-29 for the first segment, frames 32-89 for the second. 25 fps is unaffected, as the issue notes — every frame time there is already a whole millisecond, and a 25 fps cut still yields the same 73 frames.

This is the `-ss`/`-to` half of the pair; #5417 is the separate 1 ms timebase quantization on the output and is untouched here.

### Tests

- `packages/cli/src/media-use/lib/cutlist.test.mjs` — a kept range keeps sub-millisecond precision.
- `skills/media-use/scripts/transcript-cut.test.mjs` — end-to-end: a kept range starting on a 30 fps frame keeps that frame (88 frames, not 87).

Both fail on `main` and pass here. The `cutlist.mjs` change is mirrored to `packages/cli/src/media-use/lib/`, which the copy-parity check requires to stay byte-identical; `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and the existing cutlist/transcript-cut/parity suites are all clean.

title: feat(producer): write public render provenance sidecar next to outputs
body:
## What

Every successful render now writes a portable JSON receipt next to the output artifact: `out.mp4` gets `out.mp4.hf-render.json`. The sidecar records tool versions (producer / node / ffmpeg), the entry HTML sha256, the compiled-composition hash, `@font-face` families, a variables hash (count + sha256 of canonical JSON, never the raw values), format / exact-rational fps / resolution / duration / total frames, encoder facts (codec, preset, pixel format), the committed artifact's sha256 + size, per-stage wall-clock timings, worker count, HDR flag, outcome, and capture-readiness warning codes.

- **Default ON.** `--no-provenance` (or `--provenance false`) disables; `--provenance <path>` relocates the sidecar.
- **Batch mode:** each row writes its own `<row output>.hf-render.json` (verified: distinct variables hashes per row). A fixed custom path with `--batch` is rejected up front.
- **Docker mode:** the disable flag is forwarded into the container; the default sidecar lands next to the output in the mounted output directory. A custom host path with `--docker` is rejected up front (not container-visible).
- **JSON Schema** published at `packages/core/schemas/hf-render-sidecar.json` (`$id` `https://hyperframes.heygen.com/schema/hf-render-sidecar.json`); every emitted sidecar in testing validates against it (ajv, draft 2020-12).
- **Docs:** `docs/reference/render-provenance.mdx`, registered under the "Rendering paths" nav group.

## Why

Agents and CI need a machine-readable receipt beside the MP4 answering "what rendered this, from what inputs, and how" without re-running anything. Reproducibility checks, cache keys, and support triage all want it. Today the closest thing (`runtimeEnvSnapshot`, `perfSummary`) is internal-only, and the engine's embedded container tags carry only renderer name + version. The sidecar complements those tags: full receipt, separate file, deliberately excluding secrets (variable **values** are hashed, no env dump, no host paths/usernames).

## How

- `packages/producer/src/services/render/provenanceSidecar.ts`: sidecar builder + emitter. Wired into `renderOrchestrator.ts` immediately after `artifactTransaction.commit()` (the actual commit site; there is no `stages/commitArtifact.ts` in the codebase). A sidecar write failure logs a warning and never un-completes a render whose artifact already committed.
- Reuses existing producer facts at the commit site: the compiled HTML (fonts scan), the observability composition hash, the encoder preset, `perfStages`, `workerCount`, and job warnings. Producer version prefers the bundler-injected `__PRODUCER_VERSION__` define (the CLI inlines the producer via `noExternal`, where the package-walking reader can't resolve) with the filesystem walker as the unbundled fallback; ffmpeg version is probed once via the engine's binary resolution (honors `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH`) and cached.
- Threading: `--provenance` flag → render plan (`parseProvenanceArg`, tri-state) → `RenderOptions` → `createRenderRequest` (validated: `false` or non-empty string) → `RenderConfig.provenance` → orchestrator. `dockerRunArgs` forwards `--no-provenance`.
- `png-sequence` directory outputs skip artifact sha256/size; `encoder` is `null` for `png-sequence`/`gif`.

- `packages/studio-server/src/routes/render.ts`: the Studio delete route and both Studio cancel cleanups remove `<jobId>.<ext>.hf-render.json` along with the output and `.meta.json`, from one list (`renderArtifactPaths`).
- Package size: `scripts/package-size-budgets.json` raises the `@hyperframes/producer` budget to 784,260 bytes packed and 2,855,776 unpacked, this branch's measured size after merging main. The sidecar module ships in both the `index.js` and `public-server.js` bundles, which puts the package more than 1% over the previous budget.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `provenanceSidecar.test.ts` (19 tests: path resolution incl. directory outputs, font extraction, canonical variables hashing, receipt shape, secrets-not-embedded, emit integration incl. write-failure and unreadable-entry tolerance) and `render.provenance.test.ts` (12 tests: flag parsing, plan threading, batch/docker conflicts, docker arg forwarding). Producer unit lane: green except `audioPadTrim.integration.test.ts`, which fails identically on unmodified `main` in this environment (host-ffmpeg loudness variance, pre-existing and unrelated).
- [x] Manual testing performed: real end-to-end renders with the branch CLI: single render (sidecar written, `output.sha256` matches `sha256sum` of the MP4), `--no-provenance` (no sidecar), `--provenance <path>` (relocated), `--batch` with 2 rows (one sidecar per row, distinct variables hashes), sidecars validated against the JSON Schema with ajv. `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit` (producer + cli), oxlint/oxfmt, and the full lefthook pre-commit suite (incl. the fallow gate) all pass.
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable): `docs/reference/render-provenance.mdx` + `docs/docs.json`.

## Walkthrough (HyperFrames-rendered)

![HyperFrames walkthrough](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mvanhorn/hyperframes/walkthrough-assets/render-provenance-walkthrough.gif)

The demo was storyboarded first (script, beat sheet, and seam vector ledger: [`render-provenance-ce-plan.md`](https://github.com/mvanhorn/hyperframes/blob/walkthrough-assets/render-provenance-ce-plan.md)), built as a HyperFrames composition ([source](https://github.com/mvanhorn/hyperframes/blob/walkthrough-assets/render-provenance-composition.html)) that passed `hyperframes lint` and `hyperframes check` (0 errors, WCAG AA contrast), and rendered with:

```bash
node packages/cli/bin/hyperframes.mjs render /tmp/provenance-walkthrough --output walkthrough.mp4 --fps 30
```

**Self-proof:** that render exercised this PR's feature on itself. Its own receipt, [`render-provenance-walkthrough.mp4.hf-render.json`](https://github.com/mvanhorn/hyperframes/blob/walkthrough-assets/render-provenance-walkthrough.mp4.hf-render.json), records

```
"sha256": "6af87ebf6a630a417e64db98c6d6e05f50f3fa99dcc5063e3757ae3d4e8b8de1"
```

which is exactly `sha256sum` of the rendered MP4.

Rebased on `main` (bb9e507). Since main now has HLS output, the sidecar treats HLS as a directory artifact (no size or sha256) and the schema lists `hls` as a format. After the rebase: cli `tsc`, producer `tsc`, lint, oxfmt, `sync-schemas:check` and the comment checks pass; the provenance/render/docker tests (188) and producer sidecar/renderRequest tests (39) pass.

This replaces #3758, which could not be reopened.




## No visible change

The only Studio change is in `packages/studio/vite.adapter.ts`: cancelling a render now also removes its `.hf-render.json` sidecar from `renders/`. The render list only shows video files, so nothing on screen changes.

Commit 3e668fa raises the producer budget in `scripts/package-size-budgets.json` to 920 kB packed and 3.35 MB unpacked, because the provenance sidecar is real shipped code that esbuild bundles into `dist/index.js`, `dist/public-server.js` and `dist/distributed.js`. The producer tarball carries no test files or source maps from this PR. Locally it grows by about 6.3 kB packed and 24 kB unpacked over main, which already sat near the old limit.

title: drawElement batch capture never awaits __hfWaitForSeekCompletion: video frames fail self-verify and the render falls back to screenshots (0.8.140)
body:
## What happens

Rendering a composition with `<video>` clips, the drawElement self-verify fails on clip frames and the whole render is captured again on screenshots:

```
drawElement self-verify failed at frame 547: 22.2dB < 32dB vs pre-injection screenshot
Reverting worker inversion for the retry: 4 workers, plan=sdr_disk
```

Earlier renders of similar compositions failed the same check at 6–31 dB, always on a frame inside a video clip. The fast pass (44 s in the run above) is thrown away, and the screenshot pass and a separate encode follow.

## Cause

`produceDrawElementFrameBatch` (`dist/chunk-TPECLKPA.js`, from line 3274 in 0.8.140) seeks each frame of a batch with `aw.__hf.seek(t)`, then awaits `waitPaint()`. It never awaits `window.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`. The single-frame path does: `prepareFrameForCapture` calls `waitForPendingSeekCompletion` (line ~5993), which awaits `window.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`.

So with the default batch of 4 (`process.env.HF_DE_BATCH ?? "4"`, `dist/chunk-KECV5G4V.js` line ~3657), a frame whose seek completes asynchronously (a `<video>` reaching its time, or a canvas that draws it after the seek) is captured before it updates, and the self-verify compares it with a correct screenshot.

## Evidence

On the same 70 s composition (1080×1920, 30 fps, several `<video>` clips), on the same machine:

| | Default (batch 4) | `HF_DE_BATCH=1` |
|---|---|---|
| Self-verify | failed at frame 547 (22.2 dB) | passed at frames 547, 1094, 1641 and 2079 (inf dB) |
| Capture path | drawElement pass discarded, then screenshots on 4 workers | stayed on drawElement, encoding during capture |
| Total | 200.9 s | 126.0 s |

The two MP4s are 45.1 dB PSNR apart on average (worst frame 40.4 dB).

## Suggested fix

In the batch loop, await the seek's completion after `aw.__hf.seek(t)`, as the single-frame path does:

```js
if (aw.__hf && typeof aw.__hf.seek === "function") aw.__hf.seek(t);
await aw.__hfWaitForSeekCompletion?.();
```

Possibly related: #4435 (a parallel worker's first frame captures pre-seek state).

## Environment

- hyperframes 0.8.140
- chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30 (ANGLE Metal)
- macOS 27.0.1, Apple M5
- Node 22.22.3

title: fix(engine): await seek completion during drawElement batches
body:
## What

Wait for the runtime seek-completion hook after every seek in drawElement batch capture.

## Why

Batch capture currently proceeds to paint after calling `__hf.seek()`, while single-frame capture awaits `__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`. Async runtime work can therefore leave batched captures behind the requested frame, triggering a self-verify failure and screenshot fallback.

## Related work

Fixes #5429. #3941 concerns low-contrast self-verify detection and is a separate problem.

## How

Await the optional completion hook before decoding dynamic CSS backgrounds, updating GPU scenes and waiting for paint. Keep bitmap encoding overlapped and preserve the existing per-frame failure handling. Update the existing batch ordering assertion to include completion before CSS decoding.

## Test plan

- [x] Existing ordering test updated; focused engine suites: 34 passed, 3 skipped.
- [x] Engine typecheck, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, comment checks and `git diff --check` passed.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: the issue author's Mac M5 video composition and performance/PSNR comparison were not reproduced. The repository browser integration suite contains skipped validation records, not runnable browser tests.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable).
- [x] No new source comments.

The first workspace build failed on a missing `entities/decode` dependency after switching branches; dependencies were restored with a frozen-lockfile install. title: fix(producer): exports no longer fail on a video clip outside the composition's length

Distributed renders of the same composition no longer fail planning with `meta/videos.json.extracted is missing declared video ""`. ## Why Extraction already skips such a clip, and lint already warns that it is cut off. But the clip stayed in the composition's video list, so the frame-coverage gate expected its full length, found no frames and aborted a correct render; the distributed plan rejected it one step later for the same reason. Re-running fails the same way within a second: the visible clips hit the extraction cache and the same clip is skipped again, so it looks like a stale cached result even though nothing stale is involved. Repro on current main (3 s composition, one clip at 0 s and one at 4 s): ```html
``` `hyperframes render` on main fails: `Video "v-past" captured 0 of expected 60 frames (coverage 0.0%, threshold 95.0%)`. With this change it completes: a 3.000 s mp4, 90 frames, with `v-in` visible. ## Related work None open. The extractor's early skip for these clips predates this change; this makes the rest of the render agree with it. ## How - `isVideoPastTimelineEnd(video, timelineEnd)` (engine): `start >= timelineEnd`. The extractor's existing early skip now calls it. - The extract stage, which in-process and distributed renders both run, removes such clips from the composition before probing and extraction, so every later reader (coverage gate, frame lookup, HDR planning, distributed plan metadata) sees only clips that can be on screen. Deliberately not covered: clips that lie entirely before 0. A clip with no authored length carries `end` 0 (script-created media, or a `src` set from a script), the same value as an authored end at 0, so "ends at or before 0" cannot be told apart from "natural length" here. A second dropped clips with `end <= 0`, which froze natural-length clips; a third required `end > start`, which still froze a natural-length clip with a negative start. All three were caught by independent review and are replaced by the start-only rule. ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added/updated: `extractVideosStage.timelineBound.test.ts`, run with and without materialized symlinks (the stage options the distributed plan uses; the plan builder itself is not exercised by a unit test, it was checked on the repro below): a clip starting exactly at the end never reaches extraction and leaves the composition; a clip starting just before the end, and natural-length clips (`end` 0, with start 0 and with start -1), stay. An over-eager drop (`start + 0.5 >= end`): 2 failed. Without the filter: 2 failed, 9 passed. With `>` instead of `>=`: 2 failed, 9 passed. 3 runs in a row: exit 0, 11 passed. `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` unchanged: exit 0, 199 passed. - [x] Manual testing performed (`hyperframes render` built from this branch): - The repro above: main fails; this branch completes (3.000 s, 90 frames, `v-in` visible). - A video whose `src` is set from a script, no authored length: extracted, frames at 1 s and 2 s differ (it plays). - The same with `data-start="-1"`: fails with `captured 0 of expected 30 frames`, as on main. - Distributed `plan()` on the repro: main fails with `meta/videos.json.extracted is missing declared video "v-past"`; this branch plans one chunk. - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable. - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments". title: fix(ci): let the catalog republish remove its stale simulated-cursor page and superseded fonts
body:
## What

The no-deletions check now agrees to the 14 files the catalog republish removes: `simulated-cursor`'s generated docs page and payload, and 12 catalog font files no payload references any more.

## Why

The catalog bot's standing PR (#4340) cannot pass `Detect changes`: "This branch deletes 14 files that exist on origin/main". Those deletions are the generator's own output and are correct:

- `simulated-cursor` was removed from the registry in #4349 (its registry files are already agreed deletions here), but its generated `docs/catalog/components/simulated-cursor.mdx` and `docs/public/catalog/components/simulated-cursor.json` stayed on main. The generator no longer emits them.
- The 12 `docs/public/catalog/assets/*.woff2` files were referenced on main only by the old payloads of `camcorder-hud`, `thread-message-stack`, `code-snippet-dark-2026` and `code-snippet-dark-modern`. The regenerated payloads load their fonts from newly hashed files; nothing references these 12.

## Related work

## How

## Test plan

- Each font's references traced with `git grep <hash>` on origin/main (only the four old payloads) and on #4340's branch (none).

title: fix(cli): the browser download unpacks on machines without an unzip command
body:
## What changes for the user

On a Linux machine without the `unzip` command (a fresh WSL Ubuntu, slim containers), `hyperframes check` and `render` no longer fail with `Failed to download chrome-headless-shell: Extraction failed: no zip archiver is available`. The managed browser download now unpacks without any system tool.

## Root cause

The CLI downloads chrome-headless-shell through `@puppeteer/browsers`. On Linux and macOS it unzips by running the system `unzip`. When that is missing, its only fallback is the `yauzl` package, which `@puppeteer/browsers` declares as an optional peer dependency. The CLI never installed it, so with no `unzip` both paths failed and the download stopped.

## Fix

`yauzl` is now a dependency of the CLI, so `@puppeteer/browsers` finds its fallback unzipper. No CLI code changes: the library already tries `unzip` first and `yauzl` second. `yauzl` is not bundled into the CLI tarball (it is only loaded by `@puppeteer/browsers` at runtime), so the CLI's package size budget does not change.

## Also

`yauzl` is listed in the Fallow `ignoreDependencies`, next to `debug`: no CLI code imports it; `@puppeteer/browsers` loads it at runtime.

## Verification

- New `unzipFallback.test.ts` runs the real `@puppeteer/browsers` `install()` against a local server serving a chrome-headless-shell-shaped zip, with `PATH` pointing at an empty directory so no `unzip` is found. It checks the browser executable is unpacked. Skipped on Windows, where the library unzips with `tar.exe` by absolute path.
- From a clean install without `yauzl`, the test fails with the reported error (`Extraction failed: no zip archiver is available`); with it, it passes on Linux.
- The browser manager and fallback tests (60) pass 3 runs in a row; typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet are clean.

## Known limits

- On the `yauzl` path a corrupt download is not re-downloaded automatically: `@puppeteer/browsers` reports `Extraction failed: <archive path>` and drops the zip error when it combines provider failures, so the CLI cannot tell a corrupt archive from other unzip failures. Re-running the command downloads again. Upstream note: in `@puppeteer/browsers` 3.2.x, `install()` builds its `All providers failed` error from each provider error's `message` only; keeping each error as the combined error's `cause` would let callers detect a corrupt archive on this path.
- The engine and producer packages, installed on their own, use full `puppeteer`'s browser downloader, which still has no `yauzl` outside this repo. The published `hyperframes` CLI is covered.

## Why this PR is small

It is a one-dependency fix with its regression tests; the lockfile change adds only `yauzl` and `pend`.

title: fix(parsers): find FFmpeg and FFprobe installed by the project's npm installer packages
body:
## What changes for the user

A project that installs FFmpeg through npm (`@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg` and `@ffprobe-installer/ffprobe` in its own `package.json`) can now render without FFmpeg on the system `PATH`. Before, `npx hyperframes render` on such a Windows project stopped with "FFmpeg not found; FFprobe not found", and the only workaround was to prepend those packages' folders to `PATH` by hand.

## Root cause

The FFmpeg/FFprobe lookups for CLI preflight and capture, engine render and the Studio server go through one resolver, `findFfBinary` in `parsers/src/ffBinaries.ts`. It checked the env overrides, `PATH`, the project's `.hyperframes/bin` and common Unix install folders, but never the project's own npm-installed FFmpeg, so a binary sitting in the project's `node_modules` was invisible.

## Fix

`findFfBinary` now also checks an installer package as its last fallback, after `.hyperframes/bin` and the common Unix install folders, so any system FFmpeg wins over the old builds those packages ship. With Node's module resolution from the current directory (so its `node_modules`, a parent folder's, or `NODE_PATH`) it finds `@ffmpeg-installer/ffmpeg` (or `@ffprobe-installer/ffprobe`), resolves the platform package `@ffmpeg-installer/<platform>-<arch>` from there (so pnpm's isolated layout works) or else from the project (hoisted layouts), and returns the `ffmpeg`/`ffmpeg.exe` file in it only if it is executable. The Unix `@ffprobe-installer` packages ship `ffprobe` without the execute bit and rely on a postinstall `chmod`; when install scripts did not run, that file is skipped rather than reported as a working FFprobe. It only locates the binary: no code from the user's packages is loaded. Env overrides, `PATH`, `.hyperframes/bin` and the common install folders all still win, so machines with a system FFmpeg are unchanged.

## Verification

- New `ffBinaries.test.ts` cases build a temporary project with an empty `PATH` and a failing `which`: the hoisted ffmpeg and ffprobe packages are found (fail on the previous code); a pnpm-style layout, where the platform package sits next to the installer package and not in the project's `node_modules`, is found (fails when only the project is searched); a non-executable `ffprobe` is skipped (fails with a plain existence check; Unix only); a system binary in a common install folder wins over the installer package (fails when the installer lookup runs first). The tests hide the host's real install folders, so they pass on machines with FFmpeg installed.
- The resolver tests (13) pass 3 runs in a row; typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, the comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.

## Known limits

- Yarn Plug'n'Play installs have no `node_modules` folder and are not searched.
- `@ffmpeg-installer` ships FFmpeg 4.1-era builds (the `@ffprobe-installer` packages are newer 5.x builds). They render plain compositions, but variable-frame-rate video needs FFmpeg 5.1+ and fails with `VIDEO_SOURCE_UNRENDERABLE` on them; a preflight warning for an FFmpeg older than 5.1 follows in its own PR.
- On Linux and macOS, when install scripts are blocked (pnpm 10+ by default, `npm --ignore-scripts`), `@ffprobe-installer` leaves `ffprobe` without the execute bit, so it is skipped and FFprobe is still reported missing; approving the package's build script (`pnpm approve-builds`) fixes it. Windows is unaffected.
- `media-use` has its own FFmpeg lookup (env override or `PATH`) and does not use this resolver.

- The lookup starts from the current directory, as the `.hyperframes/bin` lookup does; running the CLI from outside the project does not find the project's package.

## Why this PR is small

It is a one-function change to the shared resolver with its test.
