title: Parallel render: first frame of each worker chunk is 16.7 ms late for a WAAPI animation created after load
body:
### Describe the bug A WAAPI animation that the page creates after the runtime's discover pass is still playing when a render worker makes its first seek. That first frame shows the animation 16.7 ms past the frame's time. Every later frame in the chunk is exact. With `--workers 1` the only affected frame is frame 0. With several workers, the first frame of every chunk after the first is affected, so which frames are wrong depends on the worker count. The cause is the order of two calls in the WAAPI adapter's `seek` (`packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/waapi.ts`): ```ts animation.currentTime = localTimeMs; animation.pause(); ``` On a running animation, `pause()` does not stop it at once. It schedules a pending pause. When the pause completes on the next animation frame, the browser sets the hold time from the timeline at that moment, which is one frame (16.7 ms at 60 Hz) after the time just written. See the Web Animations spec, [pausing an animation](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#pausing-an-animation-section). If `pause()` runs first, writing `currentTime` completes the pending pause right away with the written time ([setting the current time](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#setting-the-current-time-of-an-animation)). Later seeks are exact because the animation is already paused by then. The runtime's discover seek normally absorbs the late pause for animations that exist at load. An animation created later, for example inside `document.fonts.ready.then(...)` or a timer, gets its first seek from the worker instead. `packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/css.ts` (`seekAnimations`) uses the same order. Possibly related, but a different symptom: #4435 and #2477 (a worker's first frame shows the pre-seek page). ### Minimal reproduction `index.html`: ```html
``` `measure.py` prints each frame whose box position is more than 4 ms away from `frame / fps`: ```python import subprocess, sys import numpy as np W, H, fps = 1280, 80, float(sys.argv[1]) raw = subprocess.run(["ffmpeg", "-v", "error", "-i", sys.argv[2], "-f", "rawvideo", "-pix_fmt", "gray", "-"], check=True, capture_output=True).stdout row = np.frombuffer(raw, np.uint8).reshape(-1, H, W)[:, 30:50, :].mean(axis=1) row = np.where(row > 16, row, 0) centre = (row * np.arange(W)).sum(axis=1) / row.sum(axis=1) err_ms = ((centre - 23.5) / 300 - np.arange(len(centre)) / fps) * 1000 print([(f, round(e, 1)) for f, e in enumerate(err_ms) if abs(e) > 4 and 0 < f < len(err_ms) - 1]) ``` The 100 ms timer is only there to create the animation after the runtime's discover seek and before the workers start capturing. On my machine it lands in that window for most workers. Real pages hit the same window when they build animations after web fonts load. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Save the page above as `repro/index.html`. 2. `npx hyperframes@0.8.150 render repro --fps 30 --workers 4 -o w4.mp4` 3. `python3 measure.py 30 w4.mp4` 4. Repeat with `--workers 1`, and with `--fps 60`. ### Expected behavior Every frame shows the box at `24 + 300 * frame / fps` px, at any worker count. `measure.py` prints `[]`. ### Actual behavior 4 workers, 30 fps, 120 frames (chunks start at 30, 60 and 90), three runs each: | Version | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 0.8.150 | 60, 90: +16.7 ms | 30, 60, 90: +16.7 ms | 60, 90: +16.7 ms | | 0.8.144 | 90: +16.7 ms | 30, 60: +16.7 ms | 1, 30: +16.7 ms | +16.7 ms is 5 px ahead of where the frame should be. The frame after each one is exact. - 4 workers at 60 fps (240 frames): frames 60 and 180 are +16.7 ms. The offset is 16.7 ms at both frame rates, which is one browser animation frame at 60 Hz. - 1 worker at 30 fps: no late frames after frame 0. - In some 0.8.144 runs the timer fired after a worker's first seek, and that whole chunk was shifted by the chunk's start time. That comes from how the adapter sets the start of an animation created mid-render, and is separate from this report. With the two calls swapped (pause, then write `currentTime`) in the 0.8.150 runtime, three runs at 4 workers print `[]`. A larger composition that builds its animations inside `document.fonts.ready.then(...)` had frame 462 drawn 16.6 ms late at 4 workers. With the swap it is exact at 4 and 6 workers on all 189 measured frames in motion. ### Environment ```shell hyperframes 0.8.150 (also seen on 0.8.144) chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30 (ANGLE Metal), screenshot capture Node v22.23.1, ffmpeg 9.0.2 macOS 27.0, Apple M3 Ultra ``` (`npx hyperframes doctor` did not finish within two minutes on this machine, so these values come from the render log.) ### Additional context I have a fix with regression tests on a branch and can open a PR.

title: fix(core): an animation playing at its first seek shows the sought time
body:
## What

The WAAPI and CSS adapters now pause an animation before they write its `currentTime`. Both use one helper, `holdAnimationAt` in `packages/core/src/runtime/adapters/_holdAnimationAt.ts`.

## Why

An animation that is still playing when the runtime first seeks it was drawn one animation frame (16.7 ms) late on that seek.

The adapters wrote `currentTime` and then called `pause()`. On a running animation `pause()` only schedules a pending pause. When it completes on the next animation frame, the browser takes the hold time from the timeline at that moment, 16.7 ms after the time just written ([Web Animations, pausing an animation](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#pausing-an-animation-section)). Writing `currentTime` while a pause is pending completes the pause with the written time ([setting the current time](https://www.w3.org/TR/web-animations-1/#setting-the-current-time-of-an-animation)), so pausing first fixes it.

The runtime's discover seek hides this for animations that exist at load. An animation the page creates later, for example inside `document.fonts.ready.then(...)` or a timer, is still running when a render worker makes its first seek. In a parallel render that is the first frame of each chunk after the first, so those frames were late and which frames were wrong depended on the worker count.

## Related work

Fixes #5502.

Different symptom on the same worker-start frame: #4435 and #2477 (the first frame shows the pre-seek page). This change does not address those.

## How

- `holdAnimationAt(animation, timeMs, currentTimeSite, pauseSite)` calls `pause()`, then writes `currentTime`. If the first `pause()` throws (an infinite animation whose current time is unresolved), it still writes the time and then tries `pause()` once more, which keeps the behaviour the existing "still sets currentTime when pause throws" tests cover.
- `waapi.ts` `seek` and `css.ts` `seekAnimations` call it with their existing swallow site ids.
- No change to baselines, discovery or the render pipeline.

## Test plan

- New `pendingPauseAnimation.test-helpers.ts`: a fake animation that follows the spec's pending pause. `pause()` on a running animation is pending until `nextFrame()`. A `currentTime` write while a pause is pending completes it with that time.
- New `_holdAnimationAt.test.ts`: the first frame of a running animation holds the sought time; a throwing first pause still writes the time and retries the pause; a successful pause runs once.
- `waapi.test.ts` and `css.test.ts`: one regression test each, a running animation sought to 1 s reads 1000 ms after the next frame. Before the fix both read 1016.67 ms.
- `bunx vitest run src/runtime` (packages/core): 2029 passed. `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck`, oxlint and oxfmt on the changed files, `check-comment-citations`, `comment-ratchet`, `check-test-reachability` and `fallow audit --base origin/main`: all pass.
- `bun run --cwd packages/core test` has one failure, `deterministicFonts-googleSubsets.test.ts` "still embeds a local file when the page has no Google link" (5 s timeout). It fails the same way on an unmodified checkout of main.
- Render check on macOS (Apple M3 Ultra, chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30, screenshot capture). The page from the issue is a box moving at 300 px/s, created 100 ms after load, 4 workers, 30 fps, 120 frames:
  - 0.8.150 as published, three runs: chunk-start frames late by 16.7 ms in every run (60 and 90; 30, 60 and 90; 60 and 90).
  - The same 0.8.150 runtime with this change applied: three runs, every frame within 4 ms.
  - A larger composition that builds its animations inside `document.fonts.ready.then(...)`: frame 462 was 16.6 ms late at 4 workers before, and all 189 measured frames in motion are exact at 4 and 6 workers after.

title: fix(core): a render keeps a fromTo's from-values when a frame lands just after its start
body:
## What

A render no longer drops a `fromTo`'s from-only values when a frame lands less than 1 ms after the tween's start. A wipe bar like `fromTo(bar, { x: -260, opacity: 1 }, { x: 1980, immediateRender: false })` sits on an element whose stylesheet opacity is 0. When its start is 0.7 ms before a 30 fps frame, it is never drawn: the export misses the whole sweep, while playback and a direct seek both show it.

Measured with the CLI at 30 fps, `-w 1`, on a lyric video: on main the wipe at 2:26 is missing on every frame of its sweep. On this branch it is drawn, and every other frame of that section is unchanged.

## Why

Since #4911, `rerenderGsapTimelineAt` redraws every seek silently, stepping to 1 ms below the frame and back up, so same-time steps apply in authored order. #5125 re-applies from-values for a tween that starts exactly on the frame. A tween that starts inside that 1 ms is missed:

- the step down crosses its start backward, and GSAP reverts the tween's `_startAt`, putting back the pre-tween values;
- the step up re-renders only the tween's interpolated properties, so from-only values like `opacity: 1` stay reverted;
- no later frame crosses that start again, so they stay lost for the rest of the tween.

## Related work

Refs #4911, #4942, #4997, #5125: the same redraw. This extends #5125's at-start priming to every tween whose start the step down crosses.

## How

- `primeTweensStartingAt` gets the size of the step down. When `0 < local < step` for a started tween, it re-renders that tween's `_startAt` silently before the step back up, in timeline order. The step back up then renders the tween and its later siblings as before, so a later `set` still wins.
- In nested timelines, the step is scaled by each child's time scale. At `t < 0.001` the redraw steps up, not down, so nothing is crossed and nothing changes.
- **Scope note:** an earlier version of this PR changed the redraw to replay from 0, so that a frame would match a direct seek. I dropped it: GSAP's direct seek and its playback disagree when two tweens overlap on one property, and replaying from 0 sides with the direct seek. That breaks a common pattern, a slow drift with a short move on the same property inside it: playback and main resume the drift after the move, while replay-from-0 froze it at the move's end. A new test pins the playback behavior.
- **What prompted this:** a banner word whose drift tween outlives its exit tween by 20 ms ghosts on screen in exports at some frame rates. It ghosts in preview playback too, so it is the timeline's own behavior, not a render bug. It stays as is here; a check rule to flag that shape is the follow-up.

## Test plan

- [x] `adapters/gsap.steps.test.ts`, real GSAP:
  - **fails on main, passes here:** a `fromTo` starting 0.5 ms before a 30 fps frame keeps its from-only opacity on every frame of its sweep, and a later `set` still hides it;
  - **passes on main and here:** a 4 s drift with a 0.5 s move on the same property inside it matches playback on every frame. This test fails with the replay-from-0 version, which froze the drift at 300.
- [x] Producer fixture `gsap-redraw-start-and-overlap` (2.5 s, 30 fps, 1 worker) covers both shapes, with the golden generated in the producer Docker image.
- [x] The `src/runtime` suite (2031 tests) passed 3 runs in a row; core typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow are clean.
- [x] Manual testing: I rendered the affected 21.85 s section of the real project with the CLI (30 fps, `-w 1`) on main and on this branch, and diffed every frame. 20 of 656 frames differ, and all 20 are the wipe's sweep (4.87 s to 5.50 s into the section), which is now drawn. Every other frame is identical.
- [x] Full producer regression suite in Docker: 70 of 75 pass, including the new fixture. The 5 failures fail identically on main at this PR's base (details in a comment).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: feat(inspector): add the component inspector package
body:
## What

Adds `@hyperframes/inspector`, a private, opt-in package that answers "which HTML, CSS and GSAP source belongs to this element?" for an agent harness before it edits. It runs as a loopback service bound to one project, with an MCP adapter exposing `inspect_components`. Targets are a selector (optionally `within` a container), an `hfId`, or a ref returned by an earlier call; the result is the unmodified source lines for each target and its descendants, capped at 12,000 bytes.

First of three stacked PRs:
1. **This PR**: the package and its core runtime half.
2. Timeline queries and live preview inspection (stacked on this).
3. Element map, live inspection engine and Node runtime (stacked on 2).

## Why

Agents editing a composition spend most of their reads finding the source behind an element: which inline script animates it, which CSS rules apply, where a sub-composition defines it. The inspector answers that from the bundled page and its source maps instead of the agent grepping and guessing.

## How

- `packages/core/src/runtime/inspection.ts` and `inspectionTypes.ts`: the in-page query (target resolution, descendants, GSAP tweens per element, matching CSS rules). Only the inspector imports them; they are not part of the runtime bundle every composition loads.
- `htmlBundler.ts` gains an optional `scriptProvenance` callback. Without it, bundling is unchanged; the inspector passes it to map bundled inline scripts back to authored source.
- `packages/inspector`: the service, source mapping and the MCP adapter. The package is `private: true` and nothing in the CLI, Studio or producer imports it, so no user path changes.
- CI: inspector's tests are added to the test job's package list, and its manifest is copied in both Dockerfiles that list workspace manifests.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/inspector test`, `typecheck`
- [x] `bun run --cwd packages/core typecheck` (including the runtime config) and `vitest run src/compiler` (560 passed)

title: fix(skills): caption @font-face keeps every per-script font subset
body:
## What

`brandFontFaces` (captions.mjs in faceless-explainer, product-launch-video, pr-to-video) now declares each per-script subset file as its own `@font-face` with the matching `unicode-range`.

## Why

Google Fonts / Fontsource ship a face as per-script files (`source-serif-4-cyrillic.woff2`, `source-serif-4-latin.woff2`). The dedup key was family+weight+style, so only the alphabetically first file survived. In a Russian explainer the captions got only the Cyrillic subset, and every Latin word and digit fell back to a system font.

## Related work

None found.

## How

The subset is read from the filename (latin, latin-ext, cyrillic, cyrillic-ext, greek, greek-ext, vietnamese) and added to the dedup key. Ranges are copied from the Google Fonts CSS. If the family name itself contains the subset word, the file is not treated as a subset.

`frame-worker-core.md` now tells workers to prefix ids and classes with `f<frame_id>-` instead of `<frame_id>-`.

## Why

`frame_id` always starts with a digit (`03-feature`), so following the old rule literally gives ids like `03-feature-title`. `#03-feature-title` is an invalid selector for CSS, `querySelector` and GSAP. Workers either escape it (`#\30 3-feature-title`) or ship a broken selector, which the linter's unescaped-digit-id check then reports. In a real faceless-explainer run, two of eight frames hit this and needed a manual rename, including the escaped selectors and the string prefixes in the JS helpers.

title: fix(producer): stop JPEG frame capture adding colour noise to graded footage
body:
## What

Standard and high renders now capture page frames as JPEG at quality 100, instead of 95 (or 80 on the paths listed under How). Graded ProRes, VP8 and VP9 footage exported to MP4 no longer picks up blotchy colour noise. Draft renders keep quality 80.

H.264, HEVC and other non-alpha footage is a separate step that this PR leaves alone: it is still extracted as JPEG (quality 95, 4:2:0) before the page draws it.

## Why

A user exporting graded ProRes footage to 4K MP4 saw a lot of colour noise. Exporting as a PNG sequence avoided it, but much more slowly.

I rendered the same graded ProRes 422 HQ 4K clip with each step switched in turn. Each output was scored against the extracted footage frame the page draws, on a flat graded area.

- **Footage extraction is not the cause.** ProRes counts as alpha-capable, so its frames are already extracted as 16-bit PNG.
- **The final encode is not the cause.** Swapping the colour conversion filters in the encode changed nothing measurable.
- **Page capture is the cause.** Chrome's JPEG at quality 95 cuts flat graded colour into 8x8 chroma blotches and smears fine grain. Both survive the H.264 encode.

## Related work

Refs #4564 (footage colour shifts; this is a different defect, noise rather than shift).

## How

`resolveCaptureJpegQuality` in `captureImageFormat.ts` is now the one place that picks the capture JPEG quality, next to the existing capture-format choice. Three paths used to hard-code their own value; all three now read it:

| Path | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| In-process render | 95 (80 for draft) | 100 (80 for draft) |
| Probe session | 80 for every preset | 100 (80 for draft) |
| Distributed chunk capture | 80 for every preset | 100 (80 for draft) |

The probe session matters because sequential capture (disk or streaming) and the first segmented session reuse it whenever the probe opened a browser to discover the composition's duration. Those renders were capturing at 80.

The segment-resume fingerprint now includes the capture quality. A `--resume` across this change re-renders its segments instead of splicing old-quality segments next to new ones.

Quality-100 frames are larger: 5.8 MB against 3.1 MB at quality 95 for a grainy 4K frame, 1/5.7 of raw RGBA. That is past the 1/8 the disk-headroom estimate assumed. The estimate now uses 1/4 above draft's quality 80 and keeps 1/8 at 80 and below, so draft renders are estimated as before.

Every standard or high render that captures to disk now asks the pre-capture disk gate for twice the space. That covers distributed mp4 chunks (always on disk), multi-worker screenshot capture (the default on macOS and Windows), png-sequence and gif output, streaming switched off, and the drawElement fallback to disk. For example:
- On a 10 GiB scratch volume, the largest 4K distributed chunk that passes drops from about 2,330 frames to about 1,165.
- A 3,000-frame 4K render with 20 GB free used to pass and is now refused before capture, although measured grainy frames (about 17.4 GB) would have fit.

## Test plan

**Measurement.** A 2 s graded ProRes 422 HQ 4K fixture (gradient, moving test pattern, luma and chroma grain, teal/orange grade), rendered at 30 fps with `--quality high --resolution landscape-4k`. Linux, Chrome headless shell 152, software GL, ffmpeg 7.0.2 static. PSNR is frame 30 on a flat graded area against the extracted 16-bit footage frame:

| Capture | Grainy fixture | Smooth gradient fixture |
|---|---|---|
| JPEG 80 (before, single worker with the probe session reused) | 32.34 dB | not measured |
| JPEG 95 (before, parallel workers) | 35.36 dB | 45.43 dB |
| JPEG 100 (after) | 36.34 dB | 45.63 dB |
| PNG | 35.53 dB | 46.13 dB |
| Source straight to x264, same settings (floor) | 36.35 dB | 46.76 dB |

On grainy footage, quality 100 reaches the floor. PNG scores lower on that fixture because the encode samples PNG chroma point-wise. On the smooth gradient, quality 100 removes the 8x8 blotches; what remains is the 4:2:0 output itself.

**Export time.** Grainy 4K fixture, 60 frames, before/after pairs run back to back. The cost depends on which path the render takes:

| Path | Before | After | Pairs (before -> after) | Median cost |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Parallel workers (pinned to 2) | JPEG 95 | JPEG 100 | 112.9 -> 117.2 s, 114.1 -> 117.5 s, 130.0 -> 131.1 s | **+3.0%** |
| Single worker, probe session reused (duration discovered in the browser) | JPEG 80 | JPEG 100 | 125.8 -> 147.0 s, 122.3 -> 145.2 s, 123.5 -> 144.4 s | **+17.0%** (range +17 to +19%) |
| PNG capture instead, parallel | JPEG 95 | PNG | 137 -> 211 s | +54% |

A middle option, JPEG 95 on the single-worker path, measured +7.4% median (noisy: -1.5% to +14.9%) and 35.36 dB. It keeps the 8x8 blotches, so it is not used here.

**Tests.**
- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `resolveCaptureJpegQuality` per preset.
  - `runProbeStage` opens its capture session at 80 for draft and 100 for standard and high.
  - The disk estimate at quality 80, 95 and 100.
  - The segment fingerprint changes with the capture quality.

  Each new assertion fails when its code is reverted: the owner returning 95 fails three tests ("Expected: 100, Received: 95"); a fingerprint without the capture quality and an estimate threshold at 95 each fail one. Each touched suite passed 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Manual testing performed: renders above, captured JPEG quality read from the files (95 before, 100 after).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

- HDR: `hdr-regression` and `hdr-hlg-regression` pass at this head, 0 failed frames against a threshold of 0.
- The distributed chunk tests (`renderChunk.test.ts`) pass, as on main.
- Not run here: the full MP4 regression set, which CI runs. Its goldens were captured at 95 (or 80). Four fixtures with tight thresholds (two at 45 dB, two at 40 dB) may need re-baselining.
- No test reaches three call sites directly: the in-process and distributed capture options (one-line reads of the tested owner), and the line that feeds the capture quality into the segment fingerprint.
- Distributed chunks rendered by mixed worker versions during a rolling deploy can mix quality 80 and 100 frames in one output. Chunk workers are checked against the plan's ffmpeg version only.

**Before / After.** Each image has two panels:
- Left: a 4x zoom of a flat area of the grainy graded fixture, from the final MP4.
- Right: the smooth-gradient render's error against the footage frame, amplified 16x.

Before shows 8x8 colour blotches in the error and softer grain. After shows fine, even noise and the footage's grain.

**Note.** `EngineConfig.jpegQuality` (default 80) is validated but nothing reads it. Left as is; removing a public config field is a separate change.

![Before: JPEG 95 capture. Left, 4x zoom of graded grain. Right, error vs footage x16 on a smooth grade: 8x8 colour blotches](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/571edfea-519e-4ae5-9488-36bbd4e65f5f)

![After: JPEG 100 capture. Same crops: grain kept, error is fine even noise with no block structure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7eccbb45-8e54-479b-a6f4-289b7747381e)

title: feat(cli): scope check to a time range or a set of components
body:
## What

Two opt-in flags on `hyperframes check`:

- `--range <start,end>` samples only that interval of the root timeline.
- `--components <selectors>` keeps the full check but reports only findings that involve those elements or their descendants.

Without either flag, `check` behaves exactly as before.

## Why

An agent that just edited one scene at 7.8–8.2s, or one element, wants to know whether *that* is clean. A full check spends most of its time on the rest of the video and returns findings the agent did not cause and should not touch.

## Related work

Refs #5507, the first PR of the inspector stack. Same consumer (agent harnesses), no code overlap.

## How

- **`--range`**: bounds layout and contrast samples, transition samples, and the dense overlap grid. Explicit `--at` times are intersected with the range, and an empty intersection is an error. Static lint stays project-wide. Whole-timeline motion assertions and `sweep_static` detection are skipped in a range check, because they describe the whole film.
- **`--components`**: the scene is loaded and checked in full. Afterwards each browser finding is matched in the page: it is kept if its subject, or its collision, occluder or container counterpart, is inside a selected component. A selector that matches nothing fails the check.
- **Counts, `ok` and the exit code** still reflect the full result. The filter decides what is shown, it does not suppress failures.
- **Report shape**: `report.scope` records the range, the components and how many findings were hidden. The `--max-issues` cap is applied after filtering, so unrelated findings cannot use up the display budget.
- `--range` accepts `start,end` or `start:end`, the same as `snapshot --range` in #5519.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: range parsing, range sampling, transition caps inside a range, component matching in the browser driver, filtered report shape.
- [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit` and the full `packages/cli` vitest suite. Two `launch.process` shutdown tests time out on my machine on unmodified `main` too.
- [x] `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment citations, comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: fix(cli): resolve the render worker's tsx loader from the CLI install
body:
## What

In source mode, the render setup worker now resolves the `tsx` loader from the CLI's own install instead of the user's project. Under Bun it passes no loader, because Bun runs TypeScript natively.

## Why

Running the CLI from a source checkout under Node starts the worker with `--import tsx`. Node resolves that from the worker's working directory, which is the user's project, and that project usually has no `tsx`. The worker then fails before rendering starts.

To reproduce: run the source CLI under Node from a project directory that has no `tsx` in its `node_modules`, then render. Built installs are unaffected, since they run `renderSetupWorker.js` with no loader.

## Related work

Standalone.

## How

`import.meta.resolve("tsx")` from inside the CLI, falling back to the bare specifier. The loader is skipped entirely when `process.versions.bun` is set.

## Test plan

- [x] `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment gates and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [ ] Not reproduced manually in this PR; the reproduction above is from the harness that hit it.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: feat(cli): guard history turns with --exclusive, --who and --if-open
body:
## What

Opt-in guards on history turns, for agents that share a project:

- `history begin --exclusive` refuses while another agent's turn is open, instead of ending that turn.
- `history end --who <name>` refuses unless the open turn belongs to `<name>`.
- `history end --if-open` succeeds with no entry when no turn is open, instead of exiting 2.
- `HYPERFRAMES_HISTORY_ROOT` overrides where the CLI keeps history when no preview is running.

Without the new flags and the variable, every command behaves as before.

## Why

A harness opens a turn before each agent step and closes it afterwards. Today `begin` silently ends whoever else's turn is open, so two agents in one project steal each other's edits. And `end` fails when the step never opened a turn, for example after a crash or a resume. The harness needs to say "only if it is mine" and "only if one is open".

The history-root override keeps a harness run, or a test, apart from the user's own `~/.cache/hyperframes/history`.

## Related work

Standalone.

## How

- The checks run inside the existing `withOwner` callbacks, before any state changes, and refuse through the existing `Refusal` path: exit 2, or `{ok: false, error}` with `--json`.
- The text summary for `end` moved into `endedTurnText`, unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added: `--exclusive` refuses and leaves the other turn open; `end --who` refuses another agent's turn; `--if-open` with no turn.
- [x] `history.test.ts` passes (36 tests); `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment gates and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: feat(cli): snapshot a time range or one composition
body:
## What

Two opt-in flags on `hyperframes snapshot`:

- `--range <start,end>` spreads `--frames` across that interval of the root timeline.
- `--composition <id>` spreads `--frames` across the visible interval of the element with that `data-composition-id`.

Neither adds the end-of-timeline frame. You can use only one of `--at`, `--range` and `--composition`.

There are also two small output changes:

- After capture, each contact sheet is printed as an absolute path. Previously only the bare label `contact-sheet.jpg` was printed.
- The `--describe: GEMINI_API_KEY not set, skipping` line now prints only when `--describe` was passed explicitly. A plain `snapshot` with no key no longer prints it.

## Why

To review one scene, an agent today has to compute timestamps for `--at` itself. That means resolving nested `data-start` offsets and the parent's visible window by hand, and getting it wrong yields frames of a different scene. `--composition intro` does that resolution with the runtime's own start-time resolver.

The absolute path lets an agent open the sheet without guessing the output directory. The describe note was noise on every run for anyone without a Gemini key.

## Related work

#5520 (`HF_TOOL_CONTEXT`) is stacked on this one because both edit the same lines of `snapshot.ts`. The `--range` syntax matches `check --range` from #5516.

## How

- Sampling is in a new `snapshotSampling.ts`. A composition's interval is its resolved start and duration, clamped by every ancestor's.
- Composition clip ends are exclusive, so the last sample stays just inside the clip.
- `--frames` keeps its existing lenient parsing; only the ranged path validates the count.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: exact sample counts, malformed ranges, nested offsets, clamping to an ancestor, registered timeline durations, missing and ambiguous IDs.
- [x] `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment gates and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [ ] Browser run of `--range` / `--composition` on a nested fixture: not repeated on this branch.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: feat(cli): HF_TOOL_CONTEXT artifact events and project lock for agent harnesses
body:
## What

`HF_TOOL_CONTEXT` is an environment variable through which an agent harness tells one CLI invocation what it supports. Version 1 has two capabilities:

- **`events`**: `check` and `snapshot` append one `artifact.created` line per image they write to an NDJSON file the harness names. The images are frames, finding crops and contact sheets.
- **`project-lock`**: `check` and `snapshot` take `.hyperframes/project.lock` before starting a browser. A second command waits up to `waitMs`, then fails and names the holder.

Without the variable, every command behaves exactly as it does in a terminal.

## Why

A harness that runs `snapshot` for an agent has to find the images afterwards and attach them to the tool result. Today it does that by scraping stdout.

Two agents, or an agent plus a person, running `check` and `snapshot` against one project start competing browsers.

Both are harness concerns, so they are declared per call rather than switched on globally.

## Related work

Stacked on #5519, because both edit the same lines of `snapshot.ts`. Refs #5507, the first PR of the inspector stack.

## How

- `readToolContext` accepts only `version: 1` and a `capabilities` object. It ignores unknown capabilities, and any known capability whose value is invalid, so a harness can declare capabilities newer than the CLI it runs.
- The variable carries data only. No capability runs a command it names.
- A failed event write prints a warning and does not fail the command.
- The lock uses write-then-`link`, which is atomic. A lock whose process has died is taken over.
- The new docs page is `docs/developers/harness-tool-context.mdx`.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added: parsing and versioning, ignored and invalid capabilities, event lines and media types, unwritable event files, lock acquisition, waiting, timeout and dead holders, and `check` refusing while another command holds the lock.
- [x] `tsc`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment gates and `fallow audit` are clean. Fallow reports two duplicate-code groups as warnings.
- [x] Documentation updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: feat(cli): check warns when a tween ends just after a later tween on the same property
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` now warns (`gsap_tween_tail`) when a GSAP tween ends just after a later tween on the same target and property.

Example: a banner word drifts (`to x: -40` over `hold`) and exits (`to x: 2200`, 0.2 s), and the drift ends 20 ms after the exit. For that 20 ms the drift takes `x` back. Its end value, -40, is left on screen, so the word sits in the middle of the frame for the rest of the scene. That happens in preview playback and in renders, and at high frame rates on every banner. Nothing flagged it before:
- the static `overlapping_gsap_tweens` rule cannot see elements created in JS at runtime;
- even when it can, it warns on every overlap, including intended ones.

## Why

This is the timeline's own behavior, not an engine defect: GSAP plays it this way. A drift that is meant to resume after a short move has the same overlap shape. What separates the mistake is the length of the tail, a moment in the banner's case against seconds for an intended drift. So the check warns only when the earlier tween outlives the later one by at most 0.25 s, and leaves longer tails alone.

## Related work

Refs #5506, which fixes the render bug found in the same project, a dropped `fromTo` wipe.

## How

- `collectTweenRecords` runs in the check's page through `page.evaluate`. It reads every tween from each registered timeline in `window.__timelines`, walking a timeline nested in another one only through its parent. Each tween is timed on that root timeline with `globalTime`. Repeating, yoyo, keyframed and `overwrite` tweens are skipped.
- `findTweenTails` pairs tweens on the same target and property where the later one starts inside the earlier one and ends 0 to 0.25 s before it.
- Each pair becomes a `warning` runtime finding at the later tween's end time. The fix hint is to end the earlier tween first, or add `overwrite: "auto"` to the later tween.
- It reads the timelines once and seeks nothing, so the timeline state the rest of `check` audits is left alone.

## Test plan

- [x] `gsapTweenTails.test.ts`:
  - flags the banner shape;
  - leaves a 4 s drift with a 0.5 s move inside it;
  - leaves pairs on other properties, other targets or other timelines, and pairs where the later tween ends last;
  - the collector times nested tweens on the root timeline and skips repeating tweens.
- [x] The CLI `src/utils` and `check` tests (1187) pass, and typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow are clean.
- [x] Manual testing on the real project (a 2:43 lyric video with 9 sub-compositions):
  - `hyperframes check --json` reports exactly the 5 banners (22.935, 30.335, 100.836, 142.374, 155.327 s), each with a 0.020 s tail, and nothing else;
  - with `overwrite: "auto"` added to the banner exit, it reports none, and a 60 fps render no longer shows the stuck word.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): runtime check codes have no reference page today.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: feat(cli): save check, snapshot and render artifacts per revision
body:
## What

The CLI starts producing the evidence that #5524 records:

- `check` saves its JSON report, and `check --snapshots` and `snapshot` save their images under `.hyperframes/artifacts/`. Each is recorded against the revision it was made from, or marked `inputs-changed` when files changed while it ran.
- `render` registers its output, so a render inside the project is not a project change. After success it records the render, which lets superseded artifacts be cleaned.
- `clean --snapshots` also removes `.hyperframes/artifacts/{snapshots,checks}`.
- `HF_TOOL_CONTEXT` gains the `check-report` event role, now that the report exists.

## Behavior changes

These change what an existing user sees:

| Command | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `snapshot` | PNGs go to `<project>/snapshots/` | A new `<project>/.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/<id>/` per run. `--output` is unchanged. |
| `check --snapshots` | Frames and crops go to `<project>/snapshots/` | One `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/<id>/` per run |
| `check` | Writes nothing | Writes `.hyperframes/artifacts/checks/<id>.json` and records it |
| `render` | Writes only the output | Also writes `.hyperframes/render-outputs.json` and `video-state.json`, and may delete superseded artifacts as described above |

None of the new bookkeeping can fail a command:

- If `check` or `snapshot` cannot record, it prints `… was not recorded: <reason>`. The exit status still reflects the check or the capture.
- If `render` cannot register its output, it warns before rendering. Recording the render after success runs as a post-render step, which already only reports.
- A frame whose PNG header cannot be read is recorded without dimensions.

The new location keeps artifacts out of the project's tracked files and history. Each `snapshot` run no longer overwrites the previous one, and old runs are cleaned once a newer revision has been rendered.

## Related work

Builds on the history and artifact-recording APIs merged in #5524. #5520 reports these files to a harness through `HF_TOOL_CONTEXT` events; this PR adds the `check-report` event role now that the report exists.

## How

- Before running, `check`, `snapshot` and `render` ask the history owner (the preview server if one is running, otherwise the CLI) to checkpoint. They then fingerprint the project files, and compare again when recording, so a result is attributed to a revision only if nothing changed while it ran.
- `check --snapshots` uses one `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots/<id>/` per run.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added: `checkArtifacts`, `artifactCapture`, `clean`, and the contact-sheet test now passes an explicit `--output`.
- [x] In `cli`, every suite passes except the two Chromium shutdown tests that also fail on unmodified `main` on my machine.
- [x] `tsc` for cli, studio and studio-server. `bun run lint`, `oxfmt`, comment citations, comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/packages/cli.mdx`, the CLI skill, and the five skills that pointed at `snapshots/`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Before

![CLI output and project artifacts before revision-scoped evidence](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8596d02f-b69e-42c8-81c5-b7c36f16145d)

## After

![CLI output and revision-scoped artifact layout](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/453accb4-aac2-4bde-b45f-e806ad2abd77)


## Package size

`@hyperframes/studio-server` unpacked is 532,570 bytes on this head, 293 over the #5524 budget of 532,277. The extra code drops snapshot records when a reused output folder is rewritten and the new run cannot be recorded. The unpacked budget is now 559,199, five percent above that measurement.

title: feat(studio): record video state, edit targets and artifact cleanup in project history
body:
## What

Project history now maintains `.hyperframes/video-state.json`, a machine-readable snapshot of where the project stands. It also gains what is needed to tie evidence (check reports, snapshots, renders) to the revision it was made from. The CLI half that produces that evidence is #5522; this PR is the history side alone.

- **Video state.** After every history operation, Studio writes `.hyperframes/video-state.json`. It holds the current revision, whether there are unrecorded changes, the current files and each revision's files as history blob paths, who made each revision, and which elements it targeted.
- **Edit targets.** Studio's DOM edits send the edited element's `id`, `data-hf-id`, selector and selector index with the history claim. They are stored on the history entry and carried through undo, so a reader knows which element an entry changed, not only which file.
- **Checkpoint.** `ProjectHistory.checkpoint()` and `POST …/history/checkpoint` commit pending writes without ending open turns. A caller can then ask "which revision is this exact state?"
- **Artifact records** (used by #5522):
  - `beginArtifactCapture` fingerprints the project files.
  - `recordArtifacts` and `recordRenderSuccess` attribute a result to a revision only if the fingerprint did not change while it ran.
- **Cleanup.** After a render, checks and snapshots from revisions that are neither current nor among the last two rendered are deleted. Only files under `.hyperframes/artifacts/` whose hash still matches the record are touched.
- **Render outputs.** `.hyperframes/render-outputs.json` lists render outputs inside the project, so writing a render does not count as a project change.

## Behavior change

Studio now writes `.hyperframes/video-state.json`, plus a lock file beside it, after each history operation. A failed write is reported through the history's `onError` and never fails the edit. Nothing else changes for a Studio user until #5522 starts recording artifacts.

## Why

An agent working on a video needs one place that answers what the current revision is, what changed in each revision and to which element, and which check or snapshot belongs to which revision. Today it would have to reconstruct that from history internals.

## Related work

Independent of the open CLI PRs: it touches only `packages/studio` and `packages/studio-server`. #5522 builds on it.

## How

- Every write into `.hyperframes/` goes through the new `pinProjectRecord`. It is `pinWithinProject` for records no route serves, so writes stay inside the project even through symlinks.
- `video-state.json` is updated under its own lock and replaced atomically. A corrupt file is set aside as `video-state.json.invalid-<id>` and rebuilt.
- An unreadable `render-outputs.json`, or a `.hyperframes` that is a file, means "no registered outputs" to the project signature. It never fails Studio's file routes.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added: `videoState`, `artifactCleanup`, `renderOutputs` (including the unreadable registry), the history checkpoint and claim-target routes, and Studio's DOM edit targets, cutover and persistent history.
- [x] Full `studio-server` suite (1281) and Studio hooks and utils (2424) pass.
- [x] `tsc` for studio, studio-server and cli. `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, comment citations, comment ratchet and `fallow audit` are clean.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

## Package size

Package budgets rise because this PR adds the video-state/history projection and artifact cleanup code shipped in Studio and studio-server; tests and source maps remain excluded.

## Before

![Project history before the video-state projection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88b3a30b-ec3b-4577-8092-1300289a723e)

## After

![The generated video-state projection after history operations](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc494f42-e36c-46e2-9ddc-8c6acc7e7c7b)

title: fix(cli): resolve composition snapshots without browser CSS
body:
## Cause

`snapshot --composition` resolves authored timing in Node with a LinkeDOM document. A timing expression that references an element by `data-composition-id` fell through the resolver's HTML `id` lookup and called the browser-only `CSS.escape`, so a valid composition without a matching HTML `id` failed with `CSS is not defined` before capture.

## Rationale

Match `data-composition-id` by its exact attribute value instead of constructing a CSS selector. This works in browser and Node document realms, preserves HTML `id` precedence, and also handles composition IDs that would need escaping. The rest of snapshot sampling and runtime timing resolution is unchanged.

## Test plan

- Added a resolver regression with no global `CSS` namespace and a target identified only by `data-composition-id`.
- `startResolver.test.ts`: 33/33 pass.
- Core typecheck, runtime typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow, and pre-commit gates pass.

title: fix(keyframes): report unresolved GSAP timing instead of guessing rest poses
body:
## What

`hyperframes keyframes` and the GSAP parser behind it stop filling in values they cannot see. When a number can't be known statically, the CLI output now says so instead of showing a plausible guess.

**Parser (`@hyperframes/parsers`)**
- A staggered `from` still carries the rest pose Studio already reads (`y: 0`, `opacity: 1`, and the same for scale). Studio's lane uses those stops, so the reveal stays visible. The CLI is what drops the guessed pose.
- Targets held in a `const` (`const hero = "#hero"; tl.to(hero, …)`) resolve to their selector.
- An object proxy with properties or an `onUpdate` but no DOM write we can trace is labelled `proxy (unresolved DOM association)`. Only an empty `{}` with no callback is still `dwell/hold`.
- New `inspectionTiming` on each animation: `repeat`, `repeatDelay`, `delay` and `stagger` (`each` or `amount`). A field is `null` when it isn't a literal.

**CLI `keyframes`**
- `start`, `end`, `duration` and keyframe `time` can be `null`. A new `unresolved` list names what couldn't be determined: start, duration, target, keyframes, properties, totalDuration, endpointProperties or propertyExpressions.
- A staggered `from` lists `endpointProperties` as unresolved and does not show the guessed rest pose in `--json`.
- A tween with no `duration` uses GSAP's default of 0.5s rather than 0.
- New `totalDuration` covers stagger spread across matched elements, repeats and repeat delays. `end` uses it.
- A flat tween no longer synthesizes a rest-pose keyframe. A `set` is a single keyframe at 100%.
- After a tween whose delay, position, or length cannot be resolved, later cursor-relative tweens report `start: null` rather than a drifted or zero time. An absolute position keeps its known start.
- New fields `keyframeBasis`, `position` and `ease`. The text summary says "no resolved variation; runtime verification required" instead of implying a no-op.
- The motion path is drawn only when every keyframe has both `x` and `y`.
- `--shot`: corner markers are positioned for non-SVG elements.

**Lint (`@hyperframes/lint`)**
- `overlapping_gsap_tweens` already ignores `dwell/hold` and `proxy → …` labels, because they describe a role rather than an element. It now ignores the new `proxy (…)` label too. Without this, two unrelated inline proxies such as `tl.to({ _: 0 }, …)` would be reported as overlapping. Covered by a new test that fails without the fix.

## Effect on existing users

- **`keyframes --json` consumers:** these fields can now be `null`: `start`, `end`, `duration` and keyframe `time`. A staggered `from` no longer includes the guessed rest pose, and lists `endpointProperties` as unresolved.
- **Studio:** it reads the parser output, which still carries the staggered rest pose. Its full suite passes unchanged.
  - A tween targeting a `const` selector now resolves, so Studio can treat it like a tween that names its selector directly.
  - A staggered `from` still reads as a reveal (for example y 40 → 0 and opacity 0 → 1).

## Testing
- [x] `@hyperframes/parsers`: tsc, 1271 tests
- [x] `@hyperframes/core`: tsc, 4613 tests
- [x] `@hyperframes/lint`: tsc, 916 tests
- [x] `@hyperframes/studio`: tsc, 7876 tests
- [x] `@hyperframes/cli`: tsc, `keyframes` and `motionShot` tests (69)
- [x] `bun run lint`, `oxfmt --check`, `fallow audit --base origin/main`, comment ratchet and citations

title: motion-graphics: Builder writes compositions/index.html, but check/snapshot/render use the scaffold's root index.html
body:
### Describe the bug The `/motion-graphics` workflow tells the Builder to write the composition to `compositions/index.html`, but the project that the same workflow scaffolds (`hyperframes init ... --skill=motion-graphics`) has its main composition at the root `index.html`, and `check .`, `snapshot`, `render .` and `compositions` all operate on that root file. Nothing mounts or selects `compositions/index.html`, so an agent that follows the skill literally verifies and renders the blank scaffold instead of the Builder's output. References on `main` (f073281bd9): - `skills/motion-graphics/SKILL.md` lines 34, 121, 155, 156, 171 (phase table, Step 4, resume table, directory shape) - `skills/motion-graphics/agents/builder.md` line 3 - `skills/motion-graphics/agents/finalize.md` line 12 Meanwhile Step 5 runs `npx hyperframes check .` / `snapshot`, Step 6 runs `npx hyperframes render . --skill=motion-graphics ...`, and `render --help` documents that omitting `-c` renders the project's `index.html`. ### Minimal reproduction ```bash npx hyperframes init repro --non-interactive --example=blank --skill=motion-graphics mkdir -p repro/compositions ``` Then create `repro/compositions/index.html` as the Builder would (a complete standalone composition): ```html

BUILDER OUTPUT

``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set up the reproduction above. 2. `cd repro && npx hyperframes compositions` lists only `main 10.0s 1920x1080 1 element` (the root scaffold). 3. `npx hyperframes snapshot --at 1.0 --no-end` shows the scaffold's white "Title" on black. 4. `npx hyperframes render . -q draft -o ./renders/repro.mp4` produces a 10.0s video of the scaffold "Title". 5. Only `npx hyperframes render . -c compositions/index.html -o ./renders/repro-c.mp4` produces the 3.0s "BUILDER OUTPUT" video. ### Expected behavior Following the motion-graphics skill end to end should check, snapshot and render the Builder's composition. Either the Builder writes the root `index.html` (matching the scaffold, `hyperframes-core` and the project CLAUDE.md, which says "index.html - main composition (root timeline)"), or Steps 5 and 6 pass `-c compositions/index.html` / the root mounts it. ### Actual behavior The documented output path and the commands in Steps 5 and 6 point at different files. The verify gate passes against the blank scaffold (`check .` reports only a "no timeline" warning for the empty `Title` root), and the render step outputs the 10s scaffold rather than the motion graphic. An agent only avoids this by noticing the mismatch and deviating from the skill. ### Environment ```shell hyperframes doctor Version 0.8.150 (latest) Node.js v24.11.1 (win32 x64) FFmpeg ffmpeg 8.0-full_build-www.gyan.dev FFprobe ffprobe 8.0-full_build-www.gyan.dev Chrome Chrome Headless Shell v152.0.7977.30 (downloaded via `hyperframes browser ensure`) ``` Installed as the Claude Code plugin `hyperframes@hyperframes` 0.8.150; CLI invoked through the plugin's `skills/hyperframes/scripts/plugin-cli.mjs` launcher, which runs the same `hyperframes@0.8.150`. ### Additional context Suggested minimal fix: change the five `SKILL.md` references plus `builder.md` and `finalize.md` to the root `index.html`, since `hyperframes.json` already sends `add`ed blocks to `compositions/` and `compositions/components/`, which the root mounts via `data-composition-src`.

title: fix(producer): keep runtime media speed in exports
body:
## What Keep the clip speed of browser-discovered native video and audio in exports, including runtime-inserted media and media reconciled after a source update. Runtime-inserted clips also keep their `data-automation` speed ramps in picture and audio export. ## Why Browser discovery drops playback rate before the producer creates or reconciles media entries. Automatically detected video audio also drops the video's rate. A clip authored at 1.5× exports at 1×, and a runtime-inserted speed ramp plays flat. ## Related work The duplicate search found no open issue or PR for this discovery path. #5300 audits authored audio slot length; #4736 carries existing video metadata into distributed rendering; #3542 scales extraction coverage; #3536 handles snapshot rate; #5440 handles preview transport speed. These paths do not populate the missing browser-discovered rate. ## How Use the existing playback-rate reader and rate-lane resolver at the browser discovery boundary. Carry the resulting `RateSpec` through discovery and reconciliation, and inherit the video's rate when creating its audio entry. Already-collected lanes retain their scene-trimmed phase. When a browser lane replaces a scalar rate, shift the lane by the collected scene trim and recompute the source in-point using that lane. Picture and linked audio share the adjustment. The parser, probe and extraction stage share the engine's video-audio ID builder. For a scene trimmed by 2 seconds, a clip in-point of 1 second and a collected 2× rate, a browser lane that runs at 1× through the trimmed portion must start at source 3 seconds. Before this fix, it started at source 5 seconds and restarted the ramp. ## Test plan - [x] Discovery/reconciliation, detected-audio rate inheritance and serialized video/audio lane regressions cover the original missing-rate paths. - [x] Four new regressions fail before the scene-trim correction. They exercise the real collector and probe stage for video, linked video audio, native audio and runtime in-point updates. Collected trimmed lanes stay unchanged. - [x] 390 tests pass on the rebased branch across compiler, collector, probe, extraction and engine audio suites. Engine and producer builds, producer typecheck, lint, formatting, comment checks, package-cycle checks and the Fallow gate pass. - [x] Independent GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh review cleared the rebase and joint rate/loop/trim probes. - [x] Speed-ramp documentation describes trim preservation. No dependency installation was needed. Rebased onto `3d45d1b03`, preserving upstream loop propagation alongside the approved playback-rate and trim behavior. Fresh verification includes two browser checks and two strict 2-second MP4 exports of matching static and runtime-inserted clips at 1.5× with looping and a 0.25s in-point. All 60 decoded picture frames and the decoded PCM are byte-identical; every quarter-second remains audible. The collector/probe regressions cover scene-trim reconciliation. Full workspace builds were attempted, but unrelated inspector/AWS dependency gaps remain; Mintlify validation awaits CI because `mint` is unavailable locally. Minimal reproduction: generate a two-second video with a chirp, save the HTML below as `index.html`, and run `hyperframes check ` followed by `hyperframes render --fps 30 --strict-all`. The clip is inserted by JavaScript rather than appearing in the authored HTML. ```sh ffmpeg -f lavfi -i "testsrc2=size=256x64:rate=30:duration=2" -f lavfi -i "aevalsrc=0.2*sin(2*PI*(300*t+100*t*t)):s=48000:d=2" -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a aac source.mp4 ``` ```html
``` At timeline 0.2/0.5/0.8 seconds, expected chirp frequencies are 460/550/640 Hz. At output frame n, source frame must be `floor(15 + n × 1.5)`. Dropping the rate leaves the 1× timing of source frame `15 + n` and chirp frequencies 440/500/560 Hz. For the runtime-inserted ramp case raised in review, change the scalar rate to `0.5` and also set: ```js video.setAttribute("data-automation", JSON.stringify({ version: 1, lanes: [{ target: "rate", points: [{ t: 0, v: 1 }, { t: 1, v: 2 }] }] })); ``` Its exported picture and PCM audio should match the same clip placed directly in static HTML. The scalar-only revision flattened this lane to the 0.5× fallback.

title: build(inspector): publish @hyperframes/inspector to npm
body:
## What

Publish `@hyperframes/inspector` to npm alongside the other `@hyperframes/*` packages. It has been `"private": true` and missing from the publish list, so nothing outside this repo could install it. HyperFrames Desktop needs `@hyperframes/inspector/live` for live preview inspection ([heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#3773](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes-internal/pull/3773)).

- **`packages/inspector/package.json`:**
  - Drops `private`.
  - Adds `repository` and `publishConfig` (`access: public`, with exports that point only at `dist`).
  - Aligns the version with the other packages (0.8.150).
  - `files` ships only what the two exports load at runtime: `service.js`, `live.js`, the page runtime `inspection.js` (both read it from disk) and the type declarations. The local `serve`/`mcp` entry points, `server.js` and `mcp.js`, are not exported and stay out. That roughly halves the package, from 6.9 MB to 3.5 MB unpacked.
- **No `prepack`:** the inspector was the only package that rebuilt on `pnpm pack`. Under pnpm 10, which CI uses, the build output lands in `pnpm pack --json` and breaks `verify:packed-manifests`. The root `build`, which CI and `publish.yml` both run first, already builds it.
- **`packages/inspector/package-subpaths.json`:** both entry points need Node (Puppeteer and the filesystem), so they are declared `bun`/`node` and `node`. Otherwise the packed-consumer gate tries to bundle them for the browser and fails on `puppeteer-core`. `bun run sync:package-subpaths` regenerated the workspace `exports` from it.
- **Release wiring:**
  - `publish_pkg` for the inspector in `publish.yml`, after core.
  - The package in `scripts/set-version.ts`, so releases bump it.
  - Added to the root `build` script.
  - A size budget from `verify:packed-manifests`.

Existing packages and their users are unaffected; the next release adds one package to npm.

## Testing

title: fix(build): ship NodeNext-resolvable declarations from every package
body:
## What

Every package whose JavaScript or declarations come out of tsc now runs one shared post-emit step, `scripts/rewrite-relative-import-extensions.mjs`. It gives relative imports in emitted `.js` and `.d.ts` files an explicit `.js` or `/index.js`. `verify:packed-manifests` now fails when a published declaration can't be resolved by a strict Node ESM (NodeNext) consumer.

## Why

tsc copies relative specifiers into its output exactly as written. Core and inspector write bundler-style imports with no extension (`from "./types"`), so their published `.d.ts` files carried those imports too. All packages are `"type": "module"`, so a consumer compiling with `module`/`moduleResolution: "nodenext"` can't resolve them. Magi found this on #5530 (inspector, 16 errors). Core had the same bug, with 136 extensionless imports in `dist/*.d.ts`.

Core already rewrote its emitted JavaScript for this (`core_esm_extensions_rewritten`), but it skipped declarations. The packed-consumer check already used NodeNext. It missed the bug because it set `skipLibCheck: true`, which hides errors inside `.d.ts` files, and because it used bare `import "x"` side-effect imports, which tsc does not have to resolve.

## Related work

Refs #5530, which published inspector with its own declaration rewrite in `packages/inspector/build.mjs`. This PR removes that local copy, so inspector goes through the shared step like every other tsc-emitting package.

## How

- Removed inspector's local `addDeclarationExtensions`/`resolveDeclaration` from #5530 in favor of the shared step.
- Moved core's `scripts/rewrite-esm-extensions.ts` (allowlisted in `scripts/check-no-main-deletions.mjs`) to the repo root as plain ESM, so packages without tsx can use it. It now covers `.d.ts` as well as `.js`. A declaration import resolves against `foo.d.ts` or `foo/index.d.ts` and becomes `./foo.js` or `./foo/index.js`. It handles `import`/`export ... from`, side-effect imports, and `import("./x")` type expressions. An unresolvable declaration import fails the build. Unresolvable JavaScript is left alone, as before, because it may sit inside a string, and the existing packed-JS check still rejects a real one.
- The step runs after every tsc emit: core, engine and sdk (`build` script), producer, aws-lambda, gcp-cloud-run and inspector (`build.mjs`). The tsup packages (parsers, lint, studio-server, player, shader-transitions, studio) are left out on purpose. Their declarations are bundled by rollup-plugin-dts, which writes its own chunk specifiers with `.js`. Studio's bundled `.d.ts` also has `import("./TimelineCanvas")` inside a JSDoc link, which the strict mode would reject. The gate still covers those packages.
- Mass-editing the roughly 750 extensionless source imports in core and inspector was the other option. The post-emit step is smaller, matches what core already did for JS, and keeps working for future source.
- Dockerfiles that build core from source (`Dockerfile.test`, `packages/gcp-cloud-run/Dockerfile`, `examples/k8s-jobs/Dockerfile.example`) now copy the script. The gcp Dockerfile already copies `scripts/package-subpaths.mjs` the same way.
- Gate: the packed consumer now uses `import type * as ... from` for every published subpath with types. It typechecks with `module`/`moduleResolution: NodeNext`, `skipLibCheck: false`, `lib: ESNext + DOM`, and `types: ["node"]`. It also installs `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` from studio's devDependencies, because studio's declarations name React types. A failure lists error counts by owning package. The tsc step takes about 8s instead of 3s.

## Test plan

NodeNext consumer errors per package (`bun run verify:packed-manifests`, using the new gate):

| Package | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| @hyperframes/core | 94 | 0 |
| @hyperframes/inspector | 16 | 0 |
| every other published package | 0 | 0 |

tsc stops at the 94 core errors it can reach. A static count finds 136 extensionless specifiers across core's `dist/*.d.ts` before the change and 0 after.

- [x] Gate fails on current main: `Errors by package: @hyperframes/core: 94`. It passes with this change, now covering all 14 published packages (166 exports) including inspector. The inspector "before" count was measured before #5530 merged, by packing it with #5530's manifest and no rewrite.
- [x] Core's emitted JavaScript is byte-identical to main's rewritten output. Only its `.d.ts` files change. engine, sdk, producer, aws-lambda and gcp-cloud-run `dist/` are byte-identical to main.
- [x] Unit tests: `scripts/rewrite-relative-import-extensions.test.mjs` (new) covers file, directory, parent, side-effect and `import()` specifiers, plus the strict-declaration and lenient-JS cases. `scripts/verify-packed-manifests.test.mjs` adds a real tsc run under the gate's config. It fails on an extensionless declaration import and passes on the `.js` one.
- [x] `bun run build`, `bun run verify:packed-manifests`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run test:scripts` (737 node tests + 109 vitest), fallow audit, and both comment checks pass.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(catalog): match preview length to authored compositions
body:
Count Up's live catalog preview ran for five seconds although its component declares three, leaving a blank tail. Touch Indicator also inherited five seconds instead of its short tap animation.

Use the authored entry HTML duration, then an explicit manifest duration. When neither exists, omit wrapper timing so the registered animation determines the length. title: fix(inspector): stop audio waveform caches from making every live question stale
body:
## Cause

Live inspection refuses to answer when the project's source fingerprint no longer matches the one the preview was built from (`stale_preview: the project changed; query again once the preview reloads`). The inspector's fingerprint hashed every `.json` file outside a short skip list, and that list did not include the folders Studio writes caches into. When a composition with audio is opened, the timeline writes `.waveform-cache/*.json`. That changes the fingerprint, but Studio's own project signature skips `.waveform-cache`, so the preview never reloads. Every later question then answers `stale_preview` until the next real source edit. Rames found this reviewing heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#3773.

## Rationale

The preview reloads exactly when Studio's project signature changes, so the fingerprint skips every folder that signature skips (`SIGNATURE_EXCLUDED_DIRS` in `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/projectSignature.ts`). The inspector's own extra skips (`.agents`, `.claude`, `evidence`, `snapshots`) stay as they were. The file types hashed are unchanged.

## Validation

- `vitest run tests/sources.test.ts`: 4 of 4 pass. The new test writes JSON into `.waveform-cache`, `.thumbnails`, `.transcode-cache` and `.cache`, expects the fingerprint to stay the same, then expects a real `data.json` to change it.
- Fails without the fix: with `src/sources.ts` reverted, the new test fails (1 failed, 3 passed).

## No visible change

Inspector internals only. Nothing in Studio's UI changes.

title: fix(cli): bound checks of non-finishing compositions
body:
`hyperframes check` now stops when a composition script never finishes. Its single internal 120-second composition deadline starts after the browser connects, before page creation and navigation, and spans readiness, startup-error inspection, font readiness, sampling, and finding crops. Download and first boot are outside this budget. The existing `--timeout` flag retains its readiness meaning.

The failure names the active composition file and exits non-zero. Owned composition and GPU-probe browsers use managed cancellation and bounded native teardown. Cleanup failures remain visible alongside the original error. Later timer or seek callbacks are bounded, but their original child file is not attributed after the initial script returned.

The Windows workflow prepares the CLI's pinned browser and makes one warm launch before process tests. The warm browser is closed before exporting its path. This step is limited to the engine/CLI lane; the process fixture preserves Puppeteer's per-launch profile allocation.

Validation:
- The startup regression failed before the fix. It allows 150 seconds of simulated provisioning, then verifies one 120-second budget that crop readiness cannot reset.
- Early-start and reset-clock mutations fail the regression. Real CLI deadline, source-attribution, and native-cleanup witnesses also reject deliberate broken implementations.
- Windows 11: the workflow prerequisite and focused tests passed with the pinned browser. The unaccelerated command exited 1 in 123.2 seconds total, named the non-finishing child file, and its recorded native browser PID was gone.
- Linux: focused tests, typechecks, lint, unused-code audit and policy checks passed. Hosted Windows CI and current-head reviewer approval remain pending.

title: remotion-to-hyperframes: Easing.cubic is mapped to power3 (quartic); cubic is power2
body:
**Skill:** `skills/remotion-to-hyperframes/references/timing.md`

The easing table maps Remotion's cubic easing to GSAP `power3`. GSAP's `powerN` eases have exponent N+1:

| GSAP ease | polynomial |
|---|---|
| `power1` | quad |
| `power2` | cubic |
| `power3` | quart |
| `power4` | quint |

So a ported `Easing.out(Easing.cubic)` runs as a quartic ease-out.

**Affected lines (current `main`):**
- **L92:** `Easing.out(Easing.cubic)` → `ease: "power3.out"`. It should be `power2.out`.
- **L93:** `Easing.inOut(Easing.cubic)` → `ease: "power3.inOut"`. It should be `power2.inOut`.
- **L94:** `Easing.out(Easing.poly(N))` → `power<N>.out`. It should be `power<N-1>.out` (poly 2 = quad → `power1`, 3 = cubic → `power2`, 4 = quart → `power3`, 5 = quint → `power4`).
- **L135 / L144:** the worked example uses `power3.out` and says it "matches `1 - (1-t)^3` exactly". That curve is `power2.out`.

**Check with GSAP 3.15.0 at t = 0.5:**

| ease | value at t = 0.5 |
|---|---|
| `power2.out` | 0.875000 |
| `power3.out` | 0.937500 |
| cubic `1 - (1-t)^3` | 0.875000 |
| quart `1 - (1-t)^4` | 0.937500 |

**Impact we saw:** a counter tween ported with `power3.out` led its cubic original by up to about 0.27 s over a 2.6 s tween. An SSIM check per frame mostly doesn't catch it, because the error is timing: every frame looks plausible, it is just early.

**Suggested fix:**
- Change the two cubic rows and the worked example to `power2`.
- Change the `poly(N)` row to `power<N-1>`.

(L72, `overshootClamping` → `power3.out`, is marked "not validated" and may be a deliberate approximation, so I've left it out.)

We found this while testing motion libraries for frame-exact rendering. HyperFrames itself was frame-exact in every test we ran. Thanks for building it.
