title: Audio mix pads every clip to the full composition length: ~30–50 s for 190 short clips
body:
### Describe the bug

`mixAudioTracks` builds every branch as `atrim,volume,afade,adelay,apad,asetpts=N/SR/TB,atrim=0:TOTAL` and sums them with one `amix`. Every clip, including a 0.3 s sound effect, becomes a stream as long as the whole composition, so the mix costs (number of clips × composition length) in one single-threaded filter graph.

On a real composition (5 min 11 s, 190 `<audio>` elements: narration, two music beds, ~180 short sound effects) `audio_process` takes 53 s on every render. With 12 workers and `--gpu` the whole render is 4 min, so the audio step is about a fifth of it; on a 2 fps review render it is 40%.

Dropping the per-branch padding and summing with `amix ... :normalize=0` gives the same samples 2.7–3.3× faster on FFmpeg 6.1, 7.0.2, 8.1 and master.

### Minimal reproduction

Synthetic tones only. The script writes the graph `audioMixer.ts` writes today (`current`) and the same mix without per-branch padding (`nopad`), times both, and measures their difference.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Times the per-track graph audioMixer.ts writes (every branch padded to the full duration) against
# the same mix without per-branch padding (amix normalize=0, one pad on the mixed output), and
# compares the two outputs sample by sample. Synthetic tones only.
set -euo pipefail
FF="${FF:-ffmpeg}"; N="${N:-190}"; TOTAL="${TOTAL:-300}"
W=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$W"' EXIT; cd "$W"
$FF -v error -y -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=110:duration=$TOTAL" -ar 48000 -ac 2 bed.wav
$FF -v error -y -f lavfi -i "sine=frequency=880:duration=0.3" -ar 48000 -ac 2 sfx.wav
# Track 0: a bed for the whole film. Tracks 1..N-1: 0.3 s effects spread over the timeline.
ins="-i bed.wav"; starts=(0); durs=($TOTAL); vols=(0.2)
for ((i=1;i<N;i++)); do ins+=" -i sfx.wav"; starts+=("$(awk -v i=$i -v n=$N -v t=$TOTAL 'BEGIN{printf "%.3f",(i*(t-1))/n}')"); durs+=(0.3); vols+=(0.5); done
graph(){ local mode=$1 g="" mix="" i ms tail
  for ((i=0;i<N;i++)); do
    ms=$(awk -v s=${starts[$i]} 'BEGIN{printf "%d",s*1000+0.5}')
    [ $mode = current ] && tail=",apad,asetpts=N/SR/TB,atrim=0:$TOTAL" || tail=""
    g+="[$i:a]atrim=0:${durs[$i]},volume=${vols[$i]},adelay=$ms|$ms$tail[a$i];"; mix+="[a$i]"
  done
  if [ $mode = current ]; then g+="${mix}amix=inputs=$N:duration=longest:dropout_transition=0[mixed];[mixed]volume=$N[out]"
  else g+="${mix}amix=inputs=$N:duration=longest:dropout_transition=0:normalize=0[mixed];[mixed]volume=1,apad,asetpts=N/SR/TB,atrim=0:$TOTAL[out]"; fi
  echo "$g" > $mode.txt; }
run(){ graph $1; local s=$(date +%s.%N)
  $FF -v error -y $ins -filter_complex_script $1.txt -map "[out]" -c:a pcm_f32le -t $TOTAL $1.wav 2>/dev/null ||
    $FF -v error -y $ins -/filter_complex $1.txt -map "[out]" -c:a pcm_f32le -t $TOTAL $1.wav
  printf "%-8s %6.1fs\n" $1 "$(echo "$(date +%s.%N) - $s" | bc)"; }
echo "$($FF -version | head -1 | cut -d' ' -f1-3), $N tracks, ${TOTAL}s"
run current; run nopad
$FF -v info -i current.wav -i nopad.wav -filter_complex "[1:a]volume=-1[n];[0:a][n]amix=inputs=2:normalize=0,astats" -f null - 2>&1 |
  awk '/Overall/{o=1} o&&/Peak level dB/{printf "difference current - nopad: peak %s dB", $NF} o&&/RMS level dB/{print ", RMS " $NF " dB"; exit}'
```

### Steps to reproduce

1. Save the script, `chmod +x mixcost.sh`
2. `./mixcost.sh` (or `FF=/path/to/ffmpeg ./mixcost.sh`; `N` and `TOTAL` set the clip count and length)

### Expected behavior

The mix costs roughly the audio that is actually playing, not (clips × composition length).

### Actual behavior

190 tracks, 300 s, Ubuntu 24.04, Xeon E5-2686 v4:

| FFmpeg | current | nopad | difference current − nopad |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6.1.1 (Ubuntu) | 30.5 s | 11.3 s | peak −162.6 dB |
| 7.0.2 static | 25.6 s | 7.8 s | peak −162.6 dB |
| 8.1.3 | 27.0 s | 8.3 s | peak −162.6 dB |
| master N-127507 | 27.1 s | 8.4 s | peak −162.6 dB |

On the real 190-clip composition: 52.0 s → 19.1 s on 6.1, 28.2 s → 10.9 s on 7.0.2, identical output (max sample difference 1.8e-7).

### Proposal

- No per-branch `apad,asetpts,atrim`: `[i:a]atrim=0:D,volume=…,afade…,adelay=…[ai]`.
- `amix=inputs=N:duration=longest:dropout_transition=0:normalize=0` sums without re-weighting as inputs end, which is what the padding plus `volume=N` compensation achieves today; the master gain becomes `masterOutputGain` alone.
- Pad once, on the mixed output, with the same portable shape: `[mixed]volume=G,apad,asetpts=N/SR/TB,atrim=0:TOTAL[out]` (#2769, #3344).
- FFmpeg builds without `amix normalize` (before 4.4) keep today's graph, the way `-filter_complex_script` already falls back.

I extended the #3344 reproduction with this variant: on 6.1, 7.0.2, 8.1 and master it places every clip correctly, keeps t=0 silent and keeps full length, where the old `apad,atrim` shape fails on 7.0.2 and master.

One question before a PR: the test "compensates amix normalization so multi-track master gain equals track count" asserts the graph does not contain `normalize=`. Is that only about builds before 4.4, or is there another reason to avoid it? Happy to open the PR either way.

A further step, for later: summing the decoded tracks directly (Float32Array, each clip only where it plays) took 0.9 s for the same 190-clip mix and matched FFmpeg master to 1.8e-7, but it would have to reimplement fades, volume automation and the master FX chain outside FFmpeg.

### Environment

hyperframes 0.8.145 (the mix graph is unchanged on main at 6f76b30), Linux (Ubuntu 24.04), Node 24.

title: WSL2: render always falls back to SwiftShader (probe: "WebGL unavailable"; /dev/dri/renderD128 not accessible), Windows-native --browser-gpu ~5x faster; segmented capture hangs with >1 worker on Windows
body:
## Summary

On WSL2, `hyperframes render` never uses the GPU, even with an NVIDIA card that WSL can see (`/dev/dxg`, `nvidia-smi` and CUDA all work). The auto probe logs `browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)` and Chrome draws with SwiftShader. `--browser-gpu` doesn't help either: Chrome's GPU process exits during init. For a long 1080p composition this makes capture CPU-bound: a 7:23 render took **48 min**, with the three SwiftShader GPU processes using about 23 of 28 threads.

Running the same CLI natively on Windows on the same machine works: the probe finds the GPU (ANGLE / D3D11) and capture is about **5x faster** on the same composition. The workaround is below. On Windows we also hit a hang with **segmented capture plus more than one worker** (section 4).

## Environment

- Windows 11, build 10.0.26300.9550
- GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER, Windows driver 616.92
- WSL 2.4.13.0, kernel 5.15.167.4-microsoft-standard-WSL2, WSLg 1.0.65 (`DISPLAY=:0`, `WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-0`)
- Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, Mesa 23.2.1 (`libegl-mesa0`, `libgl1-mesa-dri` with `d3d12_dri.so`); no Vulkan ICDs installed
- hyperframes 0.8.153 (`npx --yes hyperframes@latest`), chrome-headless-shell 152.0.7977.30 (the CLI's own download), Node v22.17.0
- 28 logical CPUs; 15 GB RAM for WSL, 32 GB on the Windows host
- Composition: 1920x1080 at 30 fps, 7:23 (13,303 frames), 26 `<video>` (VP9 alpha WebM and H.264), 165 `<audio>`, 11 elements with `data-color-grading`

## 1. What happens in WSL2

The render log:

```
GPU: browser GPU (auto-detect)
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (HeadlessChrome/152.0.7977.30, beginframe, gl=--use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader, headlessShell=true, platform=linux)
...
rendered in 48m 12.6s
beginframe capture · software gpu · ... · capture 46m 16.5s · encode 45m 54.4s
```

While it ran, the three `--type=gpu-process` Chrome processes sat at 600 to 970% CPU each (load average 34 on 28 threads). `ffmpeg` (libx264, preset slow, CRF 15) used about 25% of one core. The encoder isn't the limit: on its own it encodes 450 of these frames in 4 s.

## 2. Why: Chrome's EGL path can't open the render node

I launched chrome-headless-shell from the CLI's cache via puppeteer-core, with `getHardwareGpuProbeArgs("linux")` (`--use-gl=angle --use-angle=gl-egl --enable-gpu-rasterization --disable-software-rasterizer`) and `--enable-logging=stderr --v=1`. The GPU process exits:

```
ERROR:ui/gl/gl_surface_egl.cc:277] No suitable EGL configs found.
ERROR:ui/gl/gl_surface_egl.cc:1021] No suitable EGL configs found for initialization.
ERROR:gpu/config/gpu_info_collector.cc:85] gl::GLContext::CreateOffscreenGLSurface failed
ERROR:gpu/config/gpu_info_collector.cc:593] Could not create surface for info collection.
ERROR:gpu/ipc/service/gpu_init.cc:123] CollectGraphicsInfo failed.
ERROR:components/viz/service/main/viz_main_impl.cc:190] Exiting GPU process due to errors during initialization
```

Mesa's own EGL fails the same way outside Chrome. I tested with a small ctypes program calling `eglInitialize` (surfaceless and default platforms) under `EGL_LOG_LEVEL=debug`:

```
libEGL warning: failed to open /dev/dri/renderD128: Permission denied
libEGL debug: EGL user error 0x3001 (EGL_NOT_INITIALIZED) in eglInitialize: DRI2: failed to load driver
```

```
$ ls -l /dev/dri/ /dev/dxg
crw-rw-rw- 1 root root   10, 127 /dev/dxg
crw-rw---- 1 root video  226,   0 /dev/dri/card0
crw-rw---- 1 root render 226, 128 /dev/dri/renderD128
$ id    # user is in 'video', NOT in 'render'
```

A default WSL2 Ubuntu user is in `video` but not `render`. Mesa therefore can't open the render node it uses to reach the D3D12 Gallium driver, and every EGL route fails.

Every WebGL probe we tried returns `WebGL unavailable`:

- `--use-angle=gl-egl`, `--use-angle=gl`, `--use-angle=vulkan --enable-features=Vulkan` (no Vulkan ICD installed) and `--use-gl=egl`, each with a plain environment and with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12`.
- `--use-angle=gl-egl` and `--use-angle=gles-egl` with `EGL_PLATFORM` set to `surfaceless`, `device`, `x11` or `wayland`.
- `--use-angle=gl-egl` and `--use-angle=gles-egl` with `EGL_PLATFORM=surfaceless GALLIUM_DRIVER=d3d12 MESA_LOADER_DRIVER_OVERRIDE=d3d12`.

**Not tested:** whether `sudo usermod -aG render $USER` plus `wsl --shutdown` lets ANGLE gl-egl reach the RTX through Mesa's d3d12 driver. Fixing the permission should at least get Mesa past the first failure. I'll report back if we try it.

## 3. Workaround: render from Windows

The same CLI, started from Windows on a copy of the project on `C:`, with portable Node 22.17.0 and FFmpeg on that process's PATH, and `--browser-gpu`:

```
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → hardware (WebGL renderer vendor="Google Inc. (NVIDIA)" renderer="ANGLE (NVIDIA, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 SUPER (0x00002783) Direct3D11 vs_5_0 ps_5_0, D3D11)")
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (HeadlessChrome/152.0.7977.30, screenshot, gl=--use-gl=angle --use-angle=d3d11, headlessShell=true, platform=win32)
```

Capture rate on the composition's first 15 s (`data-duration` cut to 15, everything else unchanged), `--quality delivery --fps 30`:

| Setup | Capture |
| --- | --- |
| WSL2, SwiftShader, 3 workers, `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true` | about 3.2 frames/s |
| Windows, `--browser-gpu`, 1 worker | 8.5 frames/s |
| Windows, `--browser-gpu`, 3 workers, `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=false` | **about 16 frames/s** |

The Windows output matches the WSL render: 450 frames, SSIM 0.989. The only visible difference is text antialiasing, because Windows rasterises fonts with DirectWrite instead of FreeType.

Our wrapper, run from WSL, works like this:
1. It mirrors the project to `C:\Users\<user>\hf-render\<project>`. It skips `node_modules`, `renders` and similar folders, plus files over 32 MB that no `.html` / `.css` references.
2. It writes a `.cmd` file that runs `npx.cmd --yes hyperframes@latest render ... --browser-gpu` with `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=false`.
3. It copies the output back.

We render from a `C:` copy rather than `\\wsl.localhost\...` because `npx.cmd` runs under cmd.exe, which can't start in a UNC directory.

## 4. Related: Windows, segmented capture with more than one worker hangs page navigation

With `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=450 HF_SEGMENT_BROWSER_RECYCLE=1 --workers 3 --browser-gpu` on Windows (screenshot capture, since BeginFrame is Linux-only), all three workers load in the **same** Chrome. The first page initialises; the second page's `page.goto` never completes:

```
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (HeadlessChrome/152.0.7977.30, screenshot, gl=--use-gl=angle --use-angle=d3d11, headlessShell=true, platform=win32)
[initSession:screenshot] page.goto start (0ms)
[initSession:screenshot] page.goto complete (649ms)
...
[initSession:screenshot] media + fonts + tailwind ready (46186ms)
[initSession:screenshot] page.goto start (0ms)
  25%  Failed: Navigation timeout of 180000 ms exceeded
```

What we observed on the same composition and machine:
- 1 worker with segmented capture: works.
- 3 workers with `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=false`: works. The log shows three `Browser launched` lines and all three pages load in under 1 s.
- 3 workers with segmented capture, and the composition stripped to its 2 in-range videos and no `<audio>`: works.

So the hang needs segmented capture, more than one worker and a media-heavy page together. We haven't isolated the cause. One guess is Chrome's limit of 6 connections per host: the first page's 26 videos and 165 audio elements could hold every connection to the local file server, so the second tab's document request never gets one. #4881 (navigation hangs with `data-color-grading` on a `<video>`, ANGLE / D3D11) may be related. This composition has 11 graded elements, but they render fine on Windows without segmented capture.

## Suggestions

1. **Make the WSL fallback actionable.** When `/dev/dxg` exists or `/proc/version` contains `microsoft`, and the hardware probe fails, the warning could say why (`/dev/dri/renderD128` not accessible to the user, or the EGL init error) and suggest the `render` group or a native Windows render. Today the only output is `probe → software (WebGL unavailable)`, and the `--browser-gpu` remediation text talks about Docker passthrough.
2. **Document WSL2 in the rendering docs**, including that a Windows-native render of the same project uses the GPU.
3. **On Windows, give each worker its own browser when segmented capture is on,** or find and fix the second-tab navigation hang above. Segmented capture is what we use in WSL to avoid OOM, so its default on Windows matters.
4. Minor: the render's local file server listens on all interfaces. On Windows that triggers a Windows Defender Firewall prompt for node.exe the first time. Binding to `127.0.0.1` would avoid it, since the browser only uses localhost.

We can share full logs, the probe scripts and the timing data.

title: feat(studio-server): accept crf, videoBitrate, videoFrameFormat and hdrMode on the render route
body:
## What

The Studio render route (`POST /projects/:id/render`) now accepts the encoder options `hyperframes render` already has, and both Studio adapters (the CLI's `studioServer.ts` and `studio/vite.adapter.ts`) pass them to the render job:

| Body field | CLI equivalent | Values |
|---|---|---|
| `crf` | `--crf` | integer, 0 to 51 for mp4, 0 to 63 for webm |
| `videoBitrate` | `--video-bitrate` | `"10M"`, `"2500k"`, `"8000000"` |
| `videoFrameFormat` | `--video-frame-format` | `auto`, `jpg`, `png` |
| `hdrMode` | `--hdr` / `--sdr` | `auto`, `force-hdr`, `force-sdr` |

## Why

The route only forwarded `draft` / `standard` / `high`, so a Studio or desktop export could not ask for what the CLI can. The prompt was film grain: a finish pass needs CRF 12 to keep its grain. On a 10 s 1080p clip with grain, CRF 16 kept about 55% of it and CRF 12 about 95%, at about 12x the file size. So every option is an opt-in override, never a new default.

## Related work

The internal desktop app's Export gets a CRF field on top of this route. No Studio UI change here.

## How

- Parsing lives in `helpers/encoderOptions.ts`. The route stays lenient about `quality`, `fps` and `resolution` as before, but an invalid encoder option returns 400, like a malformed `variables` payload, because dropping a value the user chose would render something they did not ask for.
- `crf` and `videoBitrate` are either/or, matching the CLI's guard; sending both is a 400.
- Rate control (`crf`, `videoBitrate`) is ignored for mov: ProRes has neither, and the CLI does not apply them.
- `png-sequence` and `gif` are left out on purpose. `png-sequence` writes a directory, and the route's list, serve and delete paths assume one file per render. `gif` needs the extension and MIME handling widened at about ten sites across the route and both adapters. Both are better as their own change.

## No visible change

The `packages/studio` change is three lines in `vite.adapter.ts` that pass the options to the render job. Studio's UI sends none of them yet, so nothing on screen changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: `encoderOptions.test.ts` (empty request, bitrate per format, mov ignore, crf with bitrate rejected, bad bitrates, frame format and HDR pass-through, unknown values rejected). `render.test.ts` covers forwarding through the route and 400s that start no render. 63 pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: ran `hyperframes preview` from this branch on a fixture project and posted renders to the route.
  - No `crf`: 98.8 KB. `crf: 12`: 166.9 KB. `crf: 30`: 40.9 KB. `crf: 99`: 400.
  - `videoBitrate: "400k"` through the route gave 97,790 bytes, byte-identical to `hyperframes render --video-bitrate 400k` on the same project. The CLI at 50k gave 28,873 bytes.
  - `videoBitrate` with `videoFrameFormat: "png"` and `hdrMode: "force-sdr"`: rendered.
  - `crf` with `videoBitrate`: 400. `hdrMode: "on"`: 400.
- [x] Typecheck: studio-server, cli and studio pass `tsc --noEmit`. fallow audit is clean on the changed files.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: feat(producer): accept encoder options on the render server
body:
Title: `feat(producer): accept encoder options on the render server`

### What
The producer's HTTP render server (`/render`, `/render/stream`) now takes the same encoder overrides as the Studio render route from #5549: `crf`, `videoBitrate`, `videoFrameFormat` and `hdrMode`. It calls `parseEncoderOptions` from `@hyperframes/studio-server` instead of copying the rules, which needs a new `@hyperframes/studio-server/encoder-options` subpath export.

Stacked on #5549 (its 3 commits are included until it merges; this PR adds one).

### Why
The engine honours `job.config.crf` over the quality preset, and `renderRequest.ts` already carries crf, videoBitrate, videoFrameFormat and hdrMode. `server.ts` never read crf or videoBitrate, so a `crf` key in the body was silently ignored. Cut Room wants CRF 12 masters for films with a grain finish pass; `high` is CRF 15 (`chunkEncoder.ts` `ENCODER_PRESETS`).

### Behaviour
- Rules and error messages are the helper's: crf 0-51 for mp4 and 0-63 for webm (format defaults to mp4); crf and videoBitrate are ignored for mov; crf with videoBitrate is a 400; videoBitrate must look like `10M`, `2500k` or `8000000`; videoFrameFormat is auto/jpg/png; hdrMode is auto/force-hdr/force-sdr. A bad value is a 400 on `/render` and an SSE error event on `/render/stream`.
- Nothing requested: unchanged, the quality preset applies.
- Changed: an unknown `videoFrameFormat` is now rejected instead of silently dropped; an unknown `hdrMode` string reports the helper's message.
- `hdrMode` vs `outputDynamicRange`: unchanged. They are the same policy under two names, and a conflicting pair is still a 400.

### Tests
- `server.encoderOptions.test.ts`: every option against both routes (forwarded, bounds, mov, both-together, invalid, hdrMode/outputDynamicRange match and conflict).
- `server.test.ts`: `parseRenderOptions` and `prepareRenderBody` cases.
- Removing the crf passthrough fails 8 of the 54 new cases.

### Not exercised
- No real encode at the requested settings; the tests mock the orchestrator and assert on the job config.
- The distributed render path and the internal sidecar wrapper were not run.
- The packed-consumer gate for the new export and the producer integration lane are left to CI.

— Jerrai

title: Studio render route: support PNG-sequence output
body:
## Why

`hyperframes render --format png-sequence` writes RGBA frames for compositing tools such as After Effects or Nuke. Studio's render route can't produce one, because every part of the route assumes a render is a single file.

## The design question

A PNG sequence is a directory of frames, not a file. Before writing code, decide and write down in the PR:

- **Storage:** a folder in `renders/` (named like the job id), or zip it on completion so it stays a single file?
- **Listing:** how `GET /projects/:id/renders` reports it (frame count, total size).
- **Download:** stream a zip on demand, or serve the zip written at completion?
- **Delete and cancel:** remove the whole directory safely. Reuse `resolveWithinProject` / `isPrivateProjectFile` in `helpers/safePath.ts` so a crafted job id can't escape the project.

## Where to look

- `packages/studio-server/src/routes/render.ts`: render start, list, file serve and delete routes.
- `packages/cli/src/server/studioServer.ts` and `packages/studio/vite.adapter.ts`: `startRender`, cancel cleanup, `.meta.json` sidecar paths.
- Producer support already exists: `format: "png-sequence"` in `packages/producer/src/services/renderOrchestrator.ts`.

Related: GIF output from Studio's route is a smaller version of the same widening. Doing that first may help.

## Done when

- A PNG-sequence render started from Studio can be listed, downloaded and deleted, and cancelling it leaves nothing behind.
- Route tests cover the directory case, including a path-traversal attempt on delete.

title: Studio: expose CRF, video bitrate, frame format and HDR in the render settings
body:
## Why

Studio's render route now accepts encoder overrides (#5549): `crf`, `videoBitrate`, `videoFrameFormat` and `hdrMode`. Studio's own render panel doesn't expose them yet, so only API callers can use them.

## What to build

An "Advanced" section in the render settings, folded by default, with:

- **CRF:** a number field. Blank means the Quality preset decides. Range 0 to 51 for MP4, 0 to 63 for WebM, disabled for MOV (ProRes has no CRF). Hint: "Lower = more detail, bigger file. 18 is standard; 12 keeps film grain."
- **Video bitrate:** e.g. `10M`. It is either/or with CRF, so the UI should make that obvious, and the route rejects both together with a 400.
- **Source video frames:** auto, JPG, PNG. PNG keeps exact colors from screen recordings.
- **HDR:** auto, force on, force off.

## Where to look

- `packages/studio/src/components/renders/RenderQueue.tsx`: the settings UI.
- `packages/studio/src/components/renders/renderSettings.ts`: persisted settings. Add the new fields with safe parsing of old saved values.
- `packages/studio/src/components/renders/useRenderQueue.ts`: builds the render request body.
- Validation rules to mirror: `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/encoderOptions.ts`.

## Done when

- Each option reaches the render (check the request body in a test) and blank or "auto" sends nothing.
- Switching format re-applies the per-format CRF range and disables CRF and bitrate for MOV.
- Old persisted settings without these fields still load.
- Before and after screenshots in the PR.

title: Configurable audio bitrate for renders (--audio-bitrate)
body:
## Why

Audio bitrate is hardcoded: AAC at 192k (`packages/engine/src/services/audioMixer.ts` and the MP4/MOV mux in `packages/engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts`) and Opus at 128k for WebM. Music-heavy videos may want more, and voice-only or size-capped ones may want less. There is no way to change it.

## What to change

- Add an optional `audioBitrate` (e.g. `"128k"`, `"256k"`) to the producer render config in `packages/producer/src/services/renderOrchestrator.ts` and thread it to the places that pass `-b:a`. Grep `-b:a` under `packages/engine/src` and `packages/producer/src`.
- Add `--audio-bitrate` to `hyperframes render` (`packages/cli/src/commands/render/plan.ts`), validated like `--video-bitrate`.
- Unset keeps today's values exactly (192k AAC, 128k Opus).
- Careful: the MP4 path deliberately **copies** the already-encoded AAC sidecar rather than re-encoding, to avoid a black first frame in Safari (see the comment in `chunkEncoder.ts`). The bitrate must be applied where that sidecar is encoded, not by adding a second encode at mux time.

## Done when

- `hyperframes render --audio-bitrate 128k` produces audio at about 128 kb/s (`ffprobe -select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=bit_rate`) for MP4 and WebM.
- Without the flag, output is unchanged.
- Unit tests for the flag parsing and the ffmpeg args.

title: fix(producer): keep the requested CRF in the distributed cfr re-encode
body:
## What

`assemble()`'s opt-in `cfr` re-encode now uses the same rate control the chunks were encoded with, read from `meta/encoder.json`. In order: `crf`, else `bitrate`, else the quality preset's CRF and x264 preset.

## Why

The step hardcoded `-preset medium -crf 18`. With `cfr: true`, a distributed mp4 render requested at CRF 12, at quality `high` (CRF 15, slow), or at a target bitrate was silently re-encoded at CRF 18, which throws away exactly the detail the caller asked to keep. Fine film grain is the clearest case: on a 10 s 1080p clip with a grain pass, CRF 18 keeps about 54% of the grain against about 95% at CRF 12.

## Related work

Refs #5549 (the Studio render route accepts `crf` / `videoBitrate`).

## How

- New exported helper `cfrRateControlArgs(locked)` in `assemble.ts`. It mirrors `renderChunk`'s choice (`encoder.crf ?? preset.quality`; bitrate only when no crf), using `getEncoderPreset(quality, "mp4")`.
- Default behavior is unchanged: standard quality with no override still gives `-preset medium -crf 18`.
- If both `crf` and `bitrate` are set, `crf` wins, matching the renderer's existing rule.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `cfrRateControlArgs` default, `high`, explicit crf, bitrate-only, and crf with bitrate.
- [x] ffmpeg test added: the same chunk assembled with `cfr: true` comes out bigger at a locked `crf: 10` than at `crf: 40`. Fails without the fix: with the old hardcoded `-preset medium -crf 18` restored, that test fails (15 pass, 1 fail). With the fix, all 16 pass.
- [x] fallow audit: no issues in the changed files.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(engine): keep the rightmost 8 columns of SDR MP4 at widths like 1080
body:
## What

Adds `accurate_rnd` to the yuv-to-gbrp scale in the SDR colour chains: the MP4/streaming encode filter (`sdrCaptureColor.ts`) and the SDR jpg frame-extraction filter (`videoFrameExtractor.ts`).

## Why

Since 0.8.81 (#4564), SDR colour goes through `format=gbrp`. Without `accurate_rnd`, swscale's yuv-to-gbrp conversion leaves the **last 8 columns black when the width is 16n + 8** (1000, 1080, 1112...). So every 1080x1920 portrait MP4 has had an 8 px black strip on the right. The same step in jpg frame extraction blanks the right edge of footage at those widths.

It depends on the ffmpeg version. A 1080-wide white frame through the current filter loses its last 8 columns on ffmpeg **7.1 and 8.0.1**, and is correct on **5.1** (the `Dockerfile.test` image) **and 6.1**. With `accurate_rnd` all four are correct. That is why the regression goldens, rendered on 5.1, never showed it, and why #4564's pixel tests (64 px wide) missed it.

## Related work

Fixes #5551. Regressed in #4564, whose commit notes `accurate_rnd` as "redundant" once nearest-neighbour chroma was added.

## How

- One flag on the first scale of each chain: `flags=neighbor` becomes `flags=neighbor+accurate_rnd`.
- It is also the more accurate rounding. On a 1088-wide `testsrc2` frame (a width the bug doesn't hit), the worst luma error against a float BT.601-full to BT.709-limited reference drops from 1.85 to 0.90 codes, and the mean error drops from 0.325 to 0.304.

## No visible change

This is an engine-only change, with no Studio or player UI.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added. `chunkEncoder.test.ts` checks that a 1080-wide `#C83C28` capture keeps its last 8 columns in the MP4 (within 2 codes). `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` checks that a 1080-wide clip's last 8 columns survive jpg extraction (within 5). Fails without the fix: with `accurate_rnd` removed, both new tests fail; with it, both pass.
- [x] The existing colour suites from #4564 pass: chunkEncoder, streamingEncoder, videoFrameExtractor and runFfmpeg, 404 tests.
- [x] End to end, with a 1080x1920 solid `#C83C28` composition, the luma of the last 10 columns at mid-height:
  - `hyperframes@0.8.154`: `97 97 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0`
  - this branch: `98 98 98 98 98 98 98 98 98 98`
- [x] Per-width check with ffmpeg 8.0.1. Without the fix, 1000, 1080 and 1112 lose the last 8 columns, while 720, 1088, 1100 and 1920 are fine. With the fix, all are correct.
- [ ] Producer regression goldens: `accurate_rnd` changes a small share of pixel values by about a code, so CI's PSNR comparisons will show whether any golden needs regenerating.

title: fix(engine): say why WSL renders fall back to software and how to get the GPU
body:
Part of #5548.

## What a user sees now

Under WSL, when auto GPU mode falls back to software, the log says so once, with what was checked and what to do:

```
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (probe failed (GPU probe page did not answer within 15000ms))
[hyperframes] WSL: the GPU check could not finish (see the probe line above), so this render uses software WebGL (SwiftShader) and runs at CPU speed.
  Your Linux user cannot read and write /dev/dri/renderD128 and is not in its group ("render"), which can stop Mesa from reaching the GPU.
  Fix: run `sudo usermod -aG render $USER`, then `wsl --shutdown` from Windows, reopen WSL and render again.
  Or render from native Windows (project copied to a Windows drive, run from PowerShell), where Chrome uses the GPU through Direct3D.
  Pass --no-browser-gpu to skip the GPU check and render in software.
```

- When the probe ran and found no hardware renderer, the first line says "the GPU check found no hardware GPU" instead.
- The `usermod` fix appears only when the access check fails **and** the user is not in the group that owns the node. If the user is in that group and still denied, it says so and points to `ls -l`. If the node is readable and writable, or missing, it says permissions are not the cause.
- With `--browser-gpu`, the mode stays hardware as before. Its warning keeps the "unverified" and Chrome-install (`hyperframes doctor`) advice for a failed or timed-out probe and adds the WSL checks; for a probe that found no GPU, the WSL checks replace the Docker passthrough advice. Nothing claims the render uses SwiftShader in that mode.

Before, the only output was the probe line, and `--browser-gpu` gave Docker passthrough advice.

## Why

#5548 traced the fallback to Mesa failing to open `/dev/dri/renderD128` because a default WSL2 Ubuntu user is in `video` but not `render`. That is the one cause we can check without a GPU. The note says "can stop" rather than "stops": on an Intel laptop under WSL2 the same kind of user did reach the GPU through Mesa's D3D12 driver, but Chrome took 35 to 60 s to answer, past the probe's 15 s budget.

## How

- `packages/engine/src/services/wslHost.ts`: WSL detection (moved from the CLI's telemetry so both use one detector, exported as `@hyperframes/engine/wsl-host`) and the render-node check: an access check for read and write (not an open), the owning group's name, and whether the user is in it.
- `browserManager.ts`: the probe records the WSL checks with its outcome; auto mode prints the note when it selects software; the explicit-hardware warning includes the checks. Both print once per process.
- Docs: a WSL2 section in troubleshooting, linked from the rendering guide.

## Checked on a real WSL2 machine

Windows 11, Intel graphics, WSL 3.0.3, Ubuntu 22.04, Mesa 23.2.1, a fresh non-root user in `video` but not `render`, 10 s example composition:

| Run | Probe | Output | Render |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| main (0.8.153), auto, first run | hardware (answered in time) | none | 2m 12s |
| main (0.8.153), auto, second run | software, probe timed out | none | capture 20 s |
| this branch, auto, user not in `render` | software, probe timed out | note with the `usermod` fix | 39 s |
| this branch, auto, after `usermod -aG render` + `wsl --shutdown` | software, probe timed out | "readable and writable, permissions are not the cause" | 37 s |
| this branch, `--browser-gpu`, user not in `render` | software, probe timed out | unverified warning + doctor + WSL checks; renders on hardware GL | 1m 26s |

The `usermod` + `wsl --shutdown` fix takes effect (the user gets `render` and the node becomes readable and writable). On this Intel machine it does not make Chrome use the GPU, because the D3D12 path is too slow to start, and the runs that did use hardware GL were slower than SwiftShader, so falling back is the right call here. Whether the fix gets an NVIDIA card working, as in the report, is not tested here: no NVIDIA card was available.

The same composition rendered from native Windows on that machine picked the GPU in auto mode (`ANGLE (Intel ... Direct3D11)`), which is what the note and docs point to.

## Not in this PR: the firewall prompt (#5548 suggestion 4)

The render's local file server already listens on 127.0.0.1 only. On native Windows, sampling every listening TCP socket and UDP endpoint of `node.exe` and Chrome during a full `hyperframes render` showed only `127.0.0.1` (the file server, and Chrome's debugging port), so there is nothing in the render path to rebind. The CLI commands that do bind every interface are `preview`'s port check, `play` and `present`, which are a different change.

## Tests

- `wslHost.test.ts`: detection from the kernel release and `/proc/version`; the four render-node states (denied and not in the group, denied but in the group, readable and writable, missing); a numeric group id when the group has no name; nothing outside WSL.
- `browserManager.test.ts`, with a faked WSL host: auto mode prints the note once with the right first line for no GPU and for a real 15 s page timeout; explicit hardware after a timeout or a Chrome launch failure keeps the unverified/doctor advice and never claims software; explicit hardware with no GPU gives the WSL fix instead of Docker; a WSL host with a hardware renderer stays quiet. The existing Linux and macOS warning tests now pass a non-WSL host, so they no longer depend on the machine running them.
- Broken on purpose: printing the note in hardware mode turns three tests red; dropping the group-membership check turns one red.

title: fix(skills): preserve Remotion easing mappings
body:
Cubic Remotion easing maps to GSAP `power2`; `power3` is quartic and advances the animation too early. Polynomial degree N maps to `power<N-1>`. Back easing retains its direction and overshoot parameter without a scale multiplier.

Both reference tables, the counter example and the tier-3 fixture use the corrected mapping. The fixture expresses initial transforms through `fromTo`, and its historical SSIM measurements are labeled as historical. The current-main integration regenerates the manifest for the seven published skills.

Validation on the refreshed branch: 1,212 back-easing comparisons pass. All 729 displayed counts across 243 forward, backward and repeated browser seeks match the cubic formula; the quartic control differs at 120 sampled times. The tier-3 fixture passes CLI lint and the browser gate. Formatting, manifest freshness, test reachability, normal commit hooks and both comment checks pass.

Fixes #5538.

title: fix(engine): avoid padding every audio mix input
body:
## What

Stop padding every clip to the full composition length in the main audio mix. Pad the mixed output once instead.

## Why

A short clip currently stays active in FFmpeg's filter graph for the whole composition. With many effects, that makes audio processing scale with clip count times composition duration. Fixes #5546.

## Related work

The grouped sub-mix already uses `amix=normalize=0` with a fallback for older FFmpeg builds. This applies the same compatibility approach to the main mix. No overlapping PR was open when I pushed this branch.

## How

Use `amix=normalize=0` so clips can end without changing the surviving tracks' levels. Keep the existing per-clip padding and gain compensation when FFmpeg rejects that option. The grouped sub-mix remains unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated graph tests and added a regression for the older-FFmpeg fallback. The new tests failed on the original implementation and pass with the fix.
- [x] Focused audio tests: 78 passed. Browser-free group tests: 14 passed, 2 skipped.
- [x] Compared the old and new graphs with real FFmpeg using three staggered tones. Both output 5 seconds; maximum sample difference was 1.9e-9.
- [x] Workspace build, engine typecheck, format, lint, comment checks, and commit hooks passed.
- [ ] Two group-FX tests need a browser. Chromium cannot start under this macOS sandbox (`MachPortRendezvousServer: Permission denied`), so those two tests did not pass locally. The other 14 group tests passed.
- Documentation: no user-facing option or default changes.

title: fix(engine): stop multi-worker renders hanging on media-heavy pages on Windows and macOS
body:
Part of #5548 (section 4).

## What a user sees now

On Windows and macOS, a multi-worker render of a media-heavy composition (many `<video>` and `<audio>` elements) no longer stalls when the second worker opens its page. With segmented capture this was the `Navigation timeout of 180000 ms exceeded` in #5548. Every parallel worker now runs in its own browser, as it already did on Linux.

## Why it hung

Off Linux, parallel workers shared one pooled browser. Pages in one browser share Chrome's limit of six connections per host, and every page loads from the same local file server. A page with many media elements keeps all six connections open while it buffers, so the next worker's `page.goto` waits for a free connection. With large sources none frees before the navigation timeout.

Measured on a Windows 11 laptop with the released CLI (0.8.153), a 60 s 1080p composition with 26 videos (half VP9-alpha WebM) and 165 audio clips, `HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=450 HF_SEGMENT_BROWSER_RECYCLE=1 --workers 3 --browser-gpu`:

- One browser launched for all three workers. Worker 1's `page.goto` took 0.8 s; workers 2 and 3 took 8.2 s and 8.0 s.
- Sampling Chrome's connections to the file server every 250 ms: exactly 6 established for the whole stall, and each later navigation completed only when one freed.

This composition's media is small enough that the wait ends in about 8 s; the reporter's larger sources held the connections past 180 s.

The rule for when a worker gets its own browser lived in `shouldDisableBrowserPoolForParallelWorker` and was Linux-only (BeginFrame crashes when shared). Its other conditions (headless shell present, no supersampling) were kept from the earlier BeginFrame-only rule rather than for a reason of their own. #1837 already found that sharing serializes screenshots, and #4475 meant to give each segmented worker its own browser but went through this Linux-only rule.

## The change

`shouldDisableBrowserPoolForParallelWorker` now returns true for any parallel worker. Both callers (segmented capture and the parallel coordinator) go through it, so neither path shares a browser between workers any more. The arguments it no longer reads are removed from its type and its callers.

Same Windows run with this rule applied: four browsers (probe plus three workers), each worker's `page.goto` 0.55 to 0.84 s, and the render finished in 4m 46s instead of 5m 38s.

Cost: one Chrome process per worker on Windows and macOS, as Linux already runs. Worker count sizing is unchanged.

## Tests

- `parallelWorkerBrowsers.browser.test.ts` (real Chrome): a page with ten `<audio preload="auto">` elements whose responses never finish holds the six connections, then a second worker's page must load within 5 s. With main's rule (shared browser) it fails with `Navigation timeout of 5000 ms exceeded`; with the fix it loads in under 4 s. Passed 3 runs in a row on macOS, and natively on the Windows laptop (6.9 s).
- `parallelCoordinator.test.ts`: the decision table now says parallel always isolates, single worker keeps the pool.
- `captureSegmentedStage.test.ts` passes unchanged (21 tests).

title: ci(studio): run the edit accuracy slice on PRs and the full grid in the merge queue
body:
## What

Make the Studio edit accuracy gate cheaper, while running the full grid before anything reaches main.

- **Narrower trigger.** The gate now runs only for changes on the bench's path: Studio, studio-server, core, parsers, player, sdk, lint, the CLI preview server, and the engine and producer modules it captures frames with. Test files, fixtures and docs don't trigger it.
- **Pull requests run the `pr` slice in 5 shards.** That's zoom 100 with no rotation, 435 of 2,061 cases.
- **The merge queue runs the full grid in 20 shards.**
- **Newly passing cases that aren't in `baseline.json` yet are reported, not failed.**
- **The gate fails if any shard didn't report** (`--shards N`).

## Why

- **Cost.** The gate used about 83% of all CI runner time, roughly 8 runner hours per push, and it ran on PRs that can't affect it. #5559, a two-line ffmpeg filter change in the encoder, paid for 20 shards.
- **Failures, from 170 failed gate runs since 9/30:**
  - About 45% were newly passing cases that hadn't been banked yet.
  - About 21% were build or missing-shard failures.
  - About 18% were main drifting: the same case set failed on many unrelated PRs at once.
  - About 14% look like real catches, all from Studio, core or player changes.
- **Main isn't protected today.** The gate never ran in the merge queue, so a regression that merged showed up as everyone else's failure.

## Related work

Refs #4765 (adds the gate), #4866 (12 → 20 shards).

## How

- `ci.yml`:
  - adds a separate paths-filter step with exclusions, using `predicate-quantifier: some-with-excludes`, based on `merge_group.base_sha` in the queue;
  - the shard matrix and grid depend on the event;
  - Build runs when the gate does.
- `grid.mjs`: `pr` is now zoom 100 and rotation 0 across both nestings. It held a regressed case for 10 of the 11 real catches; the old slice held 6.
- `ratchet.mjs`:
  - newly passing cases become a notice;
  - on the slice, the gate compares only the cases that ran;
  - `--shards` checks every shard reported;
  - only a full run writes a bankable baseline.
- `check-test-reachability.mjs`: accepts `!` exclusions, but only in a step that opts into `some-with-excludes`.

The required check name, "Studio: edit accuracy gate", is unchanged. It still skips, and so passes, when the filter doesn't match.

Estimated cost: about 6,700 runner hours a week down to about 2,200.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`ratchet.test.mjs`, `check-test-reachability.test.mjs`)
- [x] actionlint clean
- [x] Path patterns checked with picomatch. #5559's files no longer match; Studio, core and player files do.
- [ ] First merge queue run: confirm 20 shards, that `strategy.job-total` renders in the job names, and that the baseline comes from `base_sha`.

**For review:**
- The queue's 60 minute timeout. Build plus a full run is about 30 min before any runner wait.
- The engine and producer file lists are explicit, so a new import into those modules needs a filter entry.
- Banking newly passing cases is still manual.

## No visible change

CI configuration and bench tooling only. No product code changes.

— Rames

title: chore: release v0.8.155
perf(studio): speed up the edit accuracy bench and trim its grid
body:
## What

Makes the Studio edit accuracy bench faster per case, and trims its grid from 2,061 cases to 747. Stacked on #5566.

Two commits, so the trim can be dropped on its own:

1. `perf(studio)`: removes fixed waits. On by default, no flags.
2. `ci(studio)`: trims the grid and prunes `baseline.json` to match.

## Why

Where a case's time went, from per-phase timing on the prototype:

- **Stillness checks: about half of every case.** `settled()` waits for the preview and the box to hold still for 1000 ms, and a case calls it several times.
- **A fixed 1 s sleep, twice per case.** `openStudio` slept 1 s before settling, once on open and once after reload.
- **A 10 s wait on every no-GSAP render.** A project with no GSAP never registers a timeline, so the producer waited out `playerReadyTimeout` (10 s) in `pollSubCompositionTimelines` before capturing.
- **The blank-page smoothness control ran before every case.** It is reported, not gated.

Measured locally, 12 cases at `--jobs 1`, before and after commit 1 (the box is shared and its load average moved between 4 and 22 during these runs, so treat these as rough):

| Subset | Before, mean per case | After, mean per case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 10 single gestures (none and tween, px, root, zoom 100) plus `seqrepeat` and one keyframed case | 25.8 s | 13.8 s |
| 12 `seq*-none-px-r0-root-z100` sequence cases | 34.1 s | 15.2 s |

No-GSAP renders went from 10.4 s to between 0.2 and 0.4 s in the producer log. With the trim on top, the full grid should be about 747 cases at roughly half the old per-case time, against 2,061 before.

## Related work

Refs #5566 (base of this PR).

## How

**Commit 1: speedups**

- `case.mjs`: settle window 1000 ms to 500 ms, as a named constant (`EDIT_ACCURACY_STILL_MS` overrides it). The window still restarts on any change, so a slow save or preview swap still holds it open. 400 ms is a possible follow-up once flake rates on CI are known.
- `case.mjs`: removes the fixed `sleep(1000)` in `openStudio`. The `settled()` call right after it is the real readiness wait.
- `case.mjs`: the blank-page control runs once per gesture per browser and is reused. Its numbers stay in the report.
- `render.mjs`: when the saved project has no `__timelines` (checked from the files at render time, since adding a keyframe in Studio writes one), the producer's page marks every `[data-composition-id]` host `data-no-timeline`. That is the engine's own opt-out, read in `frameCapture.ts` (`pollSubCompositionTimelines` and `listUnregisteredTimelineIds`). Only the producer's page is changed; the Studio page and the files on disk are not.

The prototype's timing instrumentation is left out: it used module-level counters, which are wrong with `--jobs` above 1.

**Commit 2: grid trim**

- `grid.mjs`: drops zoom 200, the `pct` and `center` placements, and nested keyframed cases except a resize on a keyframe at zoom 100 without rotation (one per GSAP mode, 6 cases). Keeps every drag path and sequence case, zoom 50 and 100, both rotations and every playhead. Full grid 2,061 to 747; the `pr` slice (`zoom === 100 && rotation === 0`) 435 to 271. The 6 nested resize cases stay because two historical gate runs failed only on `resize-scale-px-r0-nested-z100-on`, so without them the `pr` slice would have passed that build (the full grid still caught it).
- Why these slices: across 444 historical result snapshots (every version of `baseline.json` plus a 1 in 5 sample of 423 PR gate artifacts), the dropped slices never caught a failure that a kept case with the same gesture, GSAP mode and playhead did not also catch. The trimmed grid still flags every historical failing snapshot.
- `baseline.json`: the 1,314 removed cases are deleted (deletions only, no other entry changes).
- `ratchet.mjs`: the gate reads the base branch's `baseline.json`, which still holds the removed cases, so without a change the passing count would fall and the gate would fail. A base case that the head's `baseline.json` no longer holds is now not counted in the base passing count or in "not run", and is listed as retired in the comment. Removing a case therefore takes removing it from `baseline.json` in the same change, which shows in review. Regressions are still judged against the base entry for every case that runs.
- Shard counts are unchanged: the `pr` slice goes from 87 to 53 cases per shard over 5 shards, and the merge queue from 103 to 37 over 20. The merge queue could likely drop to 10 shards; I left that for after the timings on CI are known.

## Risks

- **Flakes from the shorter settle window.** 500 ms leaves less margin for a late save or preview swap. Locally, the gated failures I saw were on cases that also fail on the old code under the same load (sequence subset: 5 gated failures before, 2 after; single-gesture subset: 0 before, 1 after, which passed on a re-run). Not enough runs to call the rate.
- **Rebanking.** Before banking a new `baseline.json` from these timings, the full grid should run twice on CI to see whether any case turns unstable.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `render.test.mjs` (the opt-out is applied only to a project with no timeline), `ratchet.test.mjs` (a retired case is not counted and is listed), `keyframes.test.mjs` and `grid.test.mjs` (case counts: 747 full, 271 `pr`). `vitest run tests/e2e/edit-accuracy`: 77 passed.
- [x] `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `fallow audit` against the base branch, and `check-test-reachability` (script and its tests) pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the local bench runs above, before and after, at `--jobs 1`.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not needed; `AGENTS.md` does not list grid sizes.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: refactor(inspector)!: drop the predefined agent tools; harnesses define their own
body:
## What

`@hyperframes/inspector` stops shipping agent tools. It removes `src/tools.ts` (the `inspect_components` / `query_timeline` names, descriptions and input schemas), `src/outputSchemas.ts`, the stdio MCP server `src/mcp.ts`, and the `componentsTool`, `timelineTool`, `toolContent` and `InspectionTool` exports from `@hyperframes/inspector/live`. The inspection engine and its HTTP contract (`POST /inspect`, `/timeline`, `/element-map`) are unchanged.

**Do not merge until both consumers have moved off these exports:**
- heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#3823 (Desktop's HF grep plugin defines its own tools)
- heygen-com/hyperframes-agent#17 (the eval harness defines its own tools)

## Why

The tool an agent sees (its name, description and schema) belongs to the agent harness, not to the package that provides the capability. Shipping a fixed tool definition here means a harness that wants different wording or a different shape has to fork or wrap it, and this repo ends up designing agent-facing text it does not own. Both consumers now keep their own copy, so these exports have no remaining users.

## Related work

Refs #5507, #5508, #5509 (which added these files).

## How

- Deleted `src/tools.ts`, `src/outputSchemas.ts`, `src/mcp.ts`, `tests/outputSchemas.ts`.
- Dropped the tool re-export from `src/live.ts`, the `mcp` build entry and the `mcp` script.
- `tests/transport.ts` now calls `POST /inspect` over HTTP instead of going through the MCP server, and still checks the browser starts only on the first query.
- README describes the HTTP contract and says harnesses define their own tools; it no longer calls the package private and source-only, and gains a short `POST /timeline` section.
- Deleted `INSPECT-TIMELINE.md`, which described the removed MCP tool.
- `GET /info` reports `capability: "inspection"` instead of the deleted tool name.
- `InspectRequest` and `TimelineRequest` are exported from `@hyperframes/inspector` and `@hyperframes/inspector/live`, so a harness can build its input schema from the contract.
- `scripts/check-no-main-deletions.mjs` lists the five deleted files with the reason.

## Release note (for the next version)

> **Breaking (`@hyperframes/inspector`):** the package no longer ships agent tool definitions or an MCP server. `componentsTool`, `timelineTool`, `toolContent` and the `InspectionTool` type are removed from `@hyperframes/inspector/live`, and `src/mcp.ts` is gone. Inspection itself is unchanged: call `prepareLiveInspection` or the HTTP service (`POST /inspect`, `/timeline`, `/element-map`) and define tool names, descriptions and schemas in your own agent harness; `InspectRequest` and `TimelineRequest` are now exported for that. `GET /info` reports `capability: "inspection"`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (22/22) and `bun run build` in `packages/inspector`; `dist/` no longer contains `mcp.js`
- [x] `bun tests/transport.ts <project>` against a one-element project: `{"http":true,"lazyBrowser":true,...,"browserStarts":1,"seeks":0}`
- [x] `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `check:package-subpaths`, fallow and commitlint (pre-commit hooks) pass
- [x] Documentation updated (README)

title: perf(studio): settle the edit accuracy bench on frames and network, and reuse the producer Chrome
body:
## What

Two more speedups for the Studio edit accuracy bench, stacked on #5569. Two commits:

1. Stillness checks resolve on animation frames and the page's network instead of a fixed 500 ms window.
2. One producer Chrome stays open for the whole run instead of one launch per render.

## Why

After #5569 a case still spent most of its time in `settled()`, which ran 7 to 15 times per case with a fixed 500 ms window each. In a local run with the new check, the 92 stillness checks across 12 cases took 119 ms at the median (max 6 s, a sequence case waiting out a real reload). Each render also launched and closed a producer Chrome.

## Related work

Refs #5569 (base of this PR), #5566.

## How

**Stillness (`case.mjs`)**

- `settled()` still compares the box, the set of preview frames and (keyframed cases) a pending shadow swap against the window's first read. It now resolves after 3 animation frames in a row with no change, instead of 500 ms.
- The old window also covered a late save or reload. That is now a real signal from the page's network: no request in flight, no request started or finished during the window, and every project file written since the server's last `file-change` event for it has been announced (file mtime against the event's arrival). The server's event stream and the server-rendered timeline thumbnails are not counted: the stream never ends and thumbnails take seconds without changing the preview. A request whose frame was detached is dropped.
- `EDIT_ACCURACY_STILL_MS=500` restores the old fixed window exactly, with no network signal, in case the new check proves flaky on CI. Documented in `packages/studio/AGENTS.md`.
- `openStudio` polls the seek tool every 50 ms instead of 250 ms.

**Reuse (`render.mjs`, `run.mjs`)**

- The engine already pools a producer browser per launch configuration but closes it when its last session closes. The run now holds one capture session with the renders' launch settings and its page closed, so the browser stays open and each render opens a page in it. A render that does not land in the held browser logs one warning.
- No leak between cases: each render still gets its own page and its own file server on a fresh port, and clears the browser cache before loading. Studio pages already run in a fresh browser context per case.
- A held browser that failed to launch or whose Chrome died is dropped and held again, never reused (tested). With `--jobs 2` both workers share the held browser; two renders already shared the pooled browser whenever they overlapped, so concurrency inside it is unchanged.
- Studio's server stays per case. It serves one project folder, stamps that folder on start and keeps the folder's undo history open, so switching folders under a running server would carry history between cases. Its start is polled every 50 ms instead of 200 ms.
- Same-tab reload: the bench already reloads in the same tab; nothing changed there.

## Results

Local, `--jobs 1`, mean seconds per case. The box is shared and its load average moved between 7 and 32 during these runs, so treat these as rough. Runs in the same row ran back to back.

| Subset | Before (#5569) | After | Load during |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 10 single gestures + `seqrepeat` + 1 keyframed, run 1 | 15.3 | 6.7 | 10 to 29 before, 13 to 7 after |
| same, run 2 | 17.6 | 15.2 | 20 to 30 for both |
| 12 `seq*-none-px-r0-root-z100`, run 1 | 19.0 | 22.0 | 29 to 32 before, 7 to 19 after |
| same, run 2 | 19.3 | 16.3 | 14 to 31 for both |
| `--grid pr --shard 1/8` (34 cases), `--jobs 2` | 17.5 (302 s wall) | 15.0 (260 s wall) | 30 to 22 before, 8 to 31 after |

The single-gesture gain is large on a quiet box and small under heavy load. Sequence cases spend most of their time outside `settled()` (saves, undo walks, the 3 s quiet wait for an undone sequence), so they gain less.

Pass rates: on the 34-case run, 31 of 34 pass every gated metric except smoothness on both branches. Smoothness failed widely on both because of the load and is not compared here. Flips on gated metrics other than smoothness, all on sequence `undo`: `seqresize`, `seqresizeundo`, `seqnudgeundo`, `seqrepeat`, `seqrotatenudge` and `seqplainkeys` each failed undo in at least one run on one branch, and each of the ones I re-ran also failed undo on the base branch (for example `seqresizeundo` and `seqnudgeundo` failed undo in 2 of 2 and 1 of 2 base re-runs). In the other direction `crop-scale-px-r0-root-z100-mid` failed drop, reload and render on the base branch and passed after. I could not separate a new flake from load in these runs.

## Risks

- **Flakes from a shorter settle.** If Studio ever changes the box after a quiet gap with no request, no file write and no server event, the new check measures too early. `EDIT_ACCURACY_STILL_MS=500` is the fallback.
- **Rebanking.** Before banking a new `baseline.json` from these timings, the full grid should run twice on CI to see whether any case turns unstable.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `settle.test.mjs` (network restarts the window, frame and fixed-window holds, detached requests dropped, unannounced writes keep it busy), `render.test.mjs` (the held session uses the renders' launch settings and closes its page, a dead or failed hold is replaced, cache cleared per render). `vitest run tests/e2e/edit-accuracy`: 82 passed.
- [x] `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `fallow audit --base origin/main`, `check-test-reachability` (script and its tests), `typecheck` and `typecheck:scripts` pass.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the local bench runs above.
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable): `packages/studio/AGENTS.md`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(engine): sample VFR video by timestamp so it does not freeze on FFmpeg 8
body:
## What

VFR video is now extracted by timestamp. Each output slot gets the source frame on screen at that time, and frame durations are no longer used. VFR uses the same fps filter sampling as CFR, with a `-frames:v` bound so a window that ends on a still keeps its rounded-up frame count.

## Why

On FFmpeg 8.0.1, which production renderers run, VFR screen recordings freeze. The `vfr-screen-recording` fixture fails on 8.0.1 (min PSNR 20.2 dB, 51 of 100 frames under 28 dB) and passes on 5.1 (33.7 dB).

Root cause: VFR was resampled with `-fps_mode cfr -r`. FFmpeg 8 honours each frame's duration in cfr resampling and 5.1 does not. In an mp4 with B-frames, packet durations are decode-order gaps, so they do not match presentation gaps. In the fixture clip, the frame at pts 1.708 carries a 0.425s duration, but the next frame starts 17ms later. FFmpeg 8 holds it for 13 output frames and drops 1.725 to 2.050. The same happens at 2.825 (0.375s), which drops 2.925 to 3.133.

A synthetic clip shows the same freeze (x264 `-bf 3` with gaps from `select`, added as a unit test). On 8.0.1 the old path holds one frame for 14 slots. On both versions it also cut the still before a gap short (77 of 90 frames).

## Related work

Refs #360, which added the fixture for the same class of freeze.

## How

- VFR goes through the CFR filter chain (`settb`, `setpts`, `fps=...:start_time=0:round=up`, with `-noaccurate_seek`) and the segment runner (`-t (N+1)/fps -frames:v N`). The fps filter alone ends a `-t` window at the nearest slot. The bound keeps the count `extractionFrameCountForDuration` already expects for VFR, so coverage accounting and superset slicing are unchanged.
- The two-process raw `nut` pipe, `runFfmpegPipeline` and its tests are removed. They existed only because FFmpeg 5.1 drops durations in cfr resampling once `-vf` is set, and cfr resampling is no longer used.
- The CFR path is unchanged: same arguments, same output.
- The `vfr-screen-recording` golden is regenerated on the 5.1 test image, because the old golden carries 5.1's cfr mapping (below).

## Evidence

Each extracted frame of the fixture window (`-ss 1 -t 3` at 30fps) was matched to its source frame by decoded-frame hash. The table counts slots by how many source frames they are off from the frame on screen at that tick (negative means late).

| | exact | off |
|---|---|---|
| main, FFmpeg 5.1 | 38/90 | 44 late by 1 to 2 frames, 8 early by 1 |
| main, FFmpeg 8.0.1 | 30/90 | 56 late by up to 15 frames (the freeze), 4 early by 1 |
| this PR, 5.1 | 90/90 | none |
| this PR, 8.0.1 | 90/90 | none, byte-identical to 5.1 |

Window boundaries also match on both versions: windows that start inside a gap, end inside a gap, or end on a still. A window starting inside a gap now shows the frame before the gap instead of the one after it, as CFR already does.

## Test plan

Producer regression fixtures in Docker (in-process): `vfr-screen-recording`, `speed-ramp`, `nested-sequential-video-local-start`, `portrait-edge-bleed`, `many-cuts`, `hdr-regression`, `render-video-overlay-stretch`, `video-hfid-no-id`.

| `vfr-screen-recording` min PSNR | FFmpeg 5.1 | FFmpeg 8.0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| main, old golden | 33.7 dB, pass | 20.2 dB, 51 frames failed |
| this PR, old golden | 20.0 dB (identical output on both versions; the old golden is 5.1's mapping) | 20.0 dB |
| this PR, new golden | identical (PSNR infinite), pass | 44.5 dB min, pass |

The other seven fixtures have the same per-frame PSNR on main and on this PR for each version. All pass on 5.1. On 8.0.1, `speed-ramp` fails its audio check on main too, so that failure is unrelated.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: a B-frame VFR clip sampled by timestamp; the HDR10 VFR window now expects 19 frames (the x265 reference rendered with `-fps_mode cfr` loses its trailing still); the concurrency test now expects one process per VFR clip.
- [x] Engine unit suite passes on FFmpeg 8.0.1. The new test fails on main (17 distinct frames instead of 30).
- [x] oxfmt, oxlint, `tsc` for engine and producer, fallow, and the comment checks pass.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(producer): start segmented render workers together so slow media waits overlap
body:
## What

Segmented renders with several workers now open every worker's page at the same time, so slow media readiness waits overlap instead of adding up.

## Why

Each worker's `page.goto` only started after the previous worker's `media + fonts + tailwind ready`, so any readiness wait was paid once per worker in series. Every segmented multi-worker render takes this path now that each parallel worker gets its own browser. The cause was the worker-creation loop in `runCaptureSegmentedStage`, which awaited each `createSegmentWorker` (open browser, `page.goto`, readiness waits) before starting the next. Non-segmented parallel capture already starts its workers together.

## Related work

Part of #5548 (the serial worker start reported after #5565).

## How

`openSegmentWorkersTogether` opens every worker with `Promise.allSettled`. All sessions are still ready before any segment is captured, each worker still has its own browser, and the probe session still goes to exactly one worker. If one worker fails to open, the ones that did open are kept on the worker list, so the existing `finally` closes them, as it did before.

## Test plan

- New unit test: three workers whose session factory counts how many opens are in flight. On main at most 1 is open at a time; with this change all 3 are. 22/22 pass, 3 runs in a row.
- The existing "closes the workers already opened when a later worker fails to launch" test fails if the opened sessions are dropped (checked by mutation).
- #5565's real-Chrome regression test (`parallelWorkerBrowsers.browser.test.ts`) passes.

title: fix(engine): renders under WSL use the GPU through full Chrome when the headless shell cannot
body:
Part of #5548.

## What a user sees

Rendering inside WSL2 with a graphics card, the GPU check used to try only Chrome's headless shell. On Mesa's D3D12 driver (the WSL GPU path) the headless shell can fail to set up its GL surface ("No suitable EGL configs found") even after the user joins the `render` group, while full Chrome in `--headless=new` reaches the GPU. The render then fell back to software at CPU speed.

Now, under WSL only, when the headless shell finds no GPU:

- HyperFrames tries full Chrome for Testing from Puppeteer's cache (`~/.cache/puppeteer/chrome`, the same place the HDR path already looks). If it reaches the GPU, the render uses it, captured by screenshot (full Chrome has no BeginFrame). The log says `browserGpuMode probe → hardware (full Chrome: WebGL renderer ...)`.
- If full Chrome is not installed, the WSL note says how to install it (`npx @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path ~/.cache/puppeteer`), that `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` can point at one, and that native Windows uses the GPU through Direct3D.
- If full Chrome also finds no GPU, the note says so and points to native Windows.
- The note no longer implies that joining the `render` group alone is enough.

Outside WSL nothing changes: the extra check never runs.

## How it works

- `probeAutoBrowserGpuMode` runs the usual headless-shell probe; under WSL, on a software result it probes full Chrome with the same hardware flags and remembers that browser when it gets a hardware renderer.
- `resolveCaptureBrowserPath` returns that browser for hardware-mode renders. `createCaptureSession` launches it and picks screenshot capture for it; the headless shell keeps BeginFrame.
- The full-Chrome locator moved from `hdrCapture.ts` into `browserManager.ts` (`resolveFullChromePath`) and now sorts versions numerically.
- Troubleshooting docs: the WSL2 section adds the full Chrome route.

## Tests

- `browserManager.test.ts`: under WSL, the shell finds no GPU and full Chrome does: auto and explicit hardware both resolve to hardware on full Chrome, no warning; both find no GPU: software, the note names full Chrome's result and native Windows; no full Chrome: the note gives the install command; outside WSL the locator is never called. Existing WSL tests no longer read the real Puppeteer cache.
- `frameCapture-wslFullChrome.test.ts`: the capture session launches the browser the probe chose, without BeginFrame flags; the headless shell keeps them.
- `wslHost.test.ts`: the note's two routes and the group-change wording.

All new tests fail on main. Breaking the two core lines (dropping the chosen browser from the probe result, or keeping BeginFrame for full Chrome) turns three of them red.

## Try this branch under WSL

```bash
git clone --depth 1 -b fix/wsl-gpu-full-chrome https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes.git hf-wsl-gpu
cd hf-wsl-gpu && bun install && bun run build
npx @puppeteer/browsers install chrome@stable --path ~/.cache/puppeteer
cd /path/to/project && node /path/to/hf-wsl-gpu/packages/cli/bin/hyperframes.mjs render --output out.mp4
```

Expect `browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)` for the headless shell, then `browserGpuMode probe → hardware (full Chrome: ...)`, and a `Browser launched (..., screenshot, ...)` line.

## Checked on a Windows 11 PC under WSL2 (Intel graphics, Ubuntu 22.04, Mesa 23.2.1)

We have no NVIDIA card, so the headless shell's failure was simulated: a wrapper adds `--disable-gpu` to the headless shell's GPU-mode launches only, so its GPU check answers "WebGL unavailable" right away, as the shell does on the reporter's machine. Full Chrome was installed with the command the note prints (it fetched 155.0.8059.79). Same 5 s composition, `--workers 1`.

- main (0.8.155): `probe → software (WebGL unavailable)`, the WSL note, SwiftShader render.
- this branch, default 15 s check: the shell answers "WebGL unavailable", then `probe → software (full Chrome: probe failed (GPU probe page did not answer within 15000ms))`, the note says full Chrome could not finish its check and names native Windows, and the render completes in software. On this PC Mesa's EGL start-up alone takes 90 to 100 s (`eglinfo -p surfaceless`, no Chrome involved), so any GPU check there can time out.
- this branch with the check's budget widened to 180 s in a scratch copy of the built CLI (not part of this PR): `probe → hardware (full Chrome: ... ANGLE (Microsoft Corporation, D3D12 (Intel(R) Graphics), OpenGL ES 3.0))`, `Browser launched (Chrome/155.0.8059.79, screenshot, ...)`, 150 of 150 frames, matching the software render (PSNR 62 dB). Twice. The first capture session sat at frame 0 for 60 s while Chrome's GPU process started and the existing stall retry recovered it; on the reporter's card full Chrome reached the GPU in about 0.1 s, so this Intel start-up cost should not apply there.

Render times on this PC are dominated by that GPU start-up, so they say nothing about GPU drawing speed; the reporter's machine is the one to measure.

title: fix(core): keep the colour grade on a graded video's first rendered frame
body:
Part of #5548

## What changes for users

A video with `data-color-grading` now keeps its grade on every rendered frame. Before, one frame could come out ungraded (brighter, cooler, no vignette):

- the first frame of a capture segment that lands inside a playing graded video (`HF_SEGMENTED_CAPTURE=true`), which is the case reported in #5548,
- the first frame of a parallel worker's range that lands inside one (`--workers 2` or more, no segments), and
- the first frame of a graded video that starts with a hard cut, in any render. A fade-in usually hides this one.

## Cause

When a graded video first appears on a page during a render, the producer inserts its frame image and waits for it to decode. While it decodes, the grading runtime's DOM observer re-checks the video. The video itself is hidden and the frame image is not decoded yet, so the runtime decided the clip was off screen and dropped its grade. The redraw that runs after the decode then had no graded clip to draw, so the raw frame was captured. On the next frame the clip was picked up again, so the result was a one-frame flash.

A segment start or a worker's first frame hits this because that capture session has never shown the video before. This is not a timing problem, so waiting longer before the capture would not help.

## Fix

The runtime's check for "this video is shown through an injected render frame" now counts a frame that is still decoding. The clip stays graded, and the post-decode redraw draws the right frame. This is one line in `hasInjectedRenderFrame`. Preview has no injected frames and is unchanged.

## Tests

- `colorGrading.test.ts`: the DOM observer runs while the frame decodes, then the redraw has to draw that frame. Fails on main (`redraw()` returns 0) and passes with the fix.
- `segmentedColorGrading.integration.test.ts` (integration lane, real Chrome and ffmpeg): renders a graded clip three ways: one worker with no segments (the reference), segmented with 2 workers, and 2 workers with no segments. In the last two, the second session starts inside the clip. Without the fix, the segment's first frame, the second worker's first frame and the clip's own first frame are 64 levels brighter than the graded value (3 of 4 checks fail). With the fix, all 4 pass, 3 runs in a row.

Checked by hand with a 4 s composition at `HF_SEGMENT_FRAMES=45`. On main, the segment's first frame scores 19.5 dB PSNR against the unsegmented render. With the fix, the worst frame scores 48.5 dB, which is ordinary encoder noise at a segment edge.

title: chore(docker): pin FFmpeg 8.0.1 in the Docker images and host CI
body:
## What

Pin one FFmpeg build, BtbN n8.0.1-66 (`autobuild-2026-02-28-12-59`), in every Docker image and in the host CI install action. Then regenerate the six regression baselines that change under it.

- `Dockerfile.test`, `packages/gcp-cloud-run/Dockerfile`, `examples/k8s-jobs/Dockerfile.example`, `packages/cli/src/docker/Dockerfile.render`: drop apt `ffmpeg` (Debian 5.1) and install the static build into `/usr/local/bin`, checked against its sha256. Each picks the linux64 or linuxarm64 tarball by `TARGETARCH` and fails the build on any other arch. The build step then greps both `ffmpeg -version` and `ffprobe -version` for the pinned version, so a binary that cannot run fails the build.
- `.github/actions/install-ffmpeg-linux`: 7.1.3 to the same 8.0.1 build.
- `packages/cli/src/browser/preflight.ts`: read the version from release-branch builds, which print `ffmpeg version n8.0.1-66-...`. The "n" prefix made `extractMajorVersion` return 0, which broke the CLI telemetry smoke check on the new host build. On the old n7.1.3 build it returned 1. `parseToolVersion` fell back to the whole banner line.

## Why

The tiers disagree today. The Docker images run Debian's ffmpeg 5.1 and host CI runs 7.1.3. Regression baselines are produced in the 5.1 image, so they cannot catch bugs that only show up on 7.x or 8.x, such as the right-edge black columns fixed in #5559. Pinning one build means the baselines and the shipped images use the same FFmpeg version, and we stop drifting with whatever the Debian package happens to be.

The build is a month-end BtbN release because BtbN deletes daily builds after about two weeks. Both sha256 values match that release's `checksums.sha256`.

## Related work

Refs #5559. Depends on #5572 (VFR sampling by timestamp on FFmpeg 8), which is already on main.

## How

Ran the full in-process and distributed regression suite in the new `Dockerfile.test` image against the existing baselines. Six fixtures failed. Everything else passed unchanged, including `vfr-screen-recording` and both distributed-simulated fixtures. I regenerated only those six with `--update` inside the image.

| Fixture | Why it changed |
| --- | --- |
| `style-2-prod`, `style-10-prod` | FFmpeg 8 honors the MP3 gapless header, so the SFX clips probe as 1.0s instead of 1.044898s. That changes `data-duration`/`data-end` in `compiled.html`. `output.mp4` is regenerated. `compiled.html` keeps the previous golden with only those SFX attributes changed (3 lines in style-2, 16 in style-10). |
| `vignelli-stacking` | One checkpoint at 8.06s missed the PSNR floor by 0.16 dB. The new render shows source frame 201 of the 25fps a-roll. That is the correct frame for 8.06s (201 covers 8.04 to 8.08). The old baseline showed frame 202. |
| `missing-host-comp-id`, `variables-prod`, `speed-ramp` | The AAC encoder output changed, and the RMS-envelope correlation on these flat test signals dropped below 0.9. Sample-level correlation against the source WAV is 0.9999, slightly higher than the old baseline. |

For the other four fixtures I kept the existing `compiled.html` because their compile check still passes. Only `output.mp4` changed for them.

## Test plan

- [x] Built `Dockerfile.test` locally. `ffmpeg -version` prints `n8.0.1-66-g27b8d1a017`.
- [x] Built `Dockerfile.render` for amd64. It also prints `n8.0.1-66`. I downloaded the arm64 tarball, checked its sha256 and confirmed it has the same `bin/` layout. I did not build the arm64 image.
- [x] Full regression suite in the new image (all ten CI shards): 6 failures, listed above. After regenerating them, all six pass in compare mode.
- [x] Spot checks on the new baselines. The right 8 columns have the same luma as the 8 columns next to them, so there is no black edge. Frame-aligned PSNR against the old baselines is 33 to 50 dB average. In `style-10-prod` only the last frame differs a lot: the new render keeps the a-roll visible there, and the old baseline had dropped it.
- [x] `check:gcp-cloud-run-dockerfile`, `check:tracked-artifacts`, `check-large-files.sh`, `oxfmt --check`
- [x] Unit tests added for the n-prefixed version banner (`preflight.test.ts`). `preflight`, `doctor` and telemetry event tests pass.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Left out of scope:

- `install-ffmpeg-windows` still uses a nightly master build, not 8.0.1.
- `packages/aws-lambda` ships `ffmpeg-static`.
- The install docs still say `apt install ffmpeg` / `brew install ffmpeg` for local use.
- Fixtures excluded from CI (`transparency`, `webgpu`, `field-signal-reproducer` tags) were not regenerated.

title: chore: release v0.8.156
test(lint): make catalog and scaling tests pass on Windows
body:
## What

Two tests in `packages/lint` that always fail on Windows now pass there. Test-only change; no lint rule or runtime code changes.

## Why

On a fresh Windows clone, `bun run --cwd packages/lint test` fails two tests regardless of the change being worked on, so Windows contributors cannot get a green run of the package.

To reproduce on Windows (after `bun install` and `bun run --filter '@hyperframes/{parsers,lint}' build`):

```
bun run --cwd packages/lint test
```

- `src/rules/structure.catalog.test.ts`: `AssertionError: expected 0 to be greater than 30`
- `src/utils.test.ts > stripJsStringLiterals scaling > stays linear in slash-dense input`: `AssertionError: expected Infinity to be less than 24`

## Related work

None found: no open issue or PR touches either test. This is a small self-contained test fix, so there is no separate issue.

## How

- **`structure.catalog.test.ts`**: roots were detected with `file.endsWith("/index.html")`, but `path.join` returns `\` paths on Windows, so no file counted as a root (and every file was linted as a sub-composition). It now uses `basename(file) === "index.html"`, which behaves identically on POSIX.
- **`utils.test.ts`**: each sample timed a single scan with `process.cpuUsage`, which Windows updates in ~15.6 ms ticks. The 10k-input scan finished inside one tick, read as 0 ms, and the ratio became `Infinity`. Each sample now repeats the scan until it has spent at least 50 ms of CPU time and divides by the run count. The assertion (`large / small < 24`) and input sizes are unchanged, so a quadratic scan (60x or more) still fails it. The test now spends about 0.5 s more.

## Test plan

On Windows 11 (bun 1.4.3, Node 22.19.0):

- `bun run --cwd packages/lint test`: 930/930 passed on 5 consecutive full runs (2 failures before the change).
- The scaling test alone: 15/15 passed.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and the lefthook pre-commit checks pass on the changed files.

Not run on Linux locally; CI covers it.
