title: fix(engine): renders under WSL reach the GPU on Chrome 150 and later
body:
## What

Under WSL, when HyperFrames' GPU check finds no GPU and WSLg's `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set, it checks once more with Chrome started without `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`. If that second check reaches the GPU, hardware renders launch the same way, so the headless shell HyperFrames installs (152) renders on the GPU and keeps BeginFrame capture. In every other case each Chrome keeps the environment it inherits, exactly as before.

This also removes the full-Chrome fallback from #5574. It cannot help: full Chrome and the headless shell of the same version reach the GPU or fail together.

## Why

The reporter's bisect on #5548 showed that the Chrome major version decides it: every Chrome up to 149 reaches the RTX under WSL, and every Chrome from 150 on (full Chrome and the headless shell alike) fails with `No suitable EGL configs found` / `CreateOffscreenGLSurface failed`.

The cause is tracked upstream as https://issues.chromium.org/issues/567222741. Since about 150, ANGLE uses the Wayland EGL backend whenever `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` is set. WSLg always sets it, and its compositor offers no configs for offscreen surfaces, so the GPU process cannot start. Without `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, ANGLE uses X11 EGL, which Mesa's D3D12 driver supports. That looks like a Chromium 150 regression for EGL on Mesa D3D12.

Why not always drop `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` under WSL: on a WSL machine whose X11 EGL is broken (`xcb_connect failed` on our Intel test PC), Chrome started without it but with `DISPLAY` set renders WebGL black, even on SwiftShader. Measured there: a render with the variable removed came out all black (3 of 3 runs), while the same render with it kept was correct (2 of 2). So the environment only changes when a probe has shown that the change reaches the GPU.

Pinning Chrome to 149 under WSL would also work, but it would hold WSL users on an older browser for a bug with a one-variable workaround.

## Related work

Refs #5548. Replaces the fallback added in #5574 (its shared full-Chrome lookup for HDR capture stays).

## How

- The GPU check (`probeAutoBrowserGpuMode`) owns the decision. Under WSL, after a probe that finds no GPU and with `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` set, it probes again without it and records `withoutWaylandDisplay` on its cached outcome when that probe gets hardware. The log says `browserGpuMode probe → hardware (without WAYLAND_DISPLAY: ...)`.
- `captureWithoutWaylandDisplay(resolvedMode)` answers "launch this render without it?": only for hardware renders, and only when the probe needed it. `createCaptureSession` passes the answer to `acquireBrowser`; it is part of the browser-pool fingerprint, so a pooled browser is never reused across the two environments.
- Reverted from #5574: the full-Chrome probe and route, `resolveCaptureBrowserPath`, the screenshot-mode switch for full Chrome, and the WSL note telling people to install `chrome@stable` (155 fails the same way). `scripts/check-no-main-deletions.mjs` lists the removed fallback test as an agreed deletion; `frameCapture-wslWayland.test.ts` covers the capture-session wiring instead.
- Cost: under WSL with no reachable GPU, the check runs one extra probe (up to the 15 s probe limit) before choosing software.

## Test plan

- [x] `browserManager-wslEnv.test.ts`: under WSL, when only the env without `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` reaches the GPU, the mode is hardware and the render browser launches without it; when neither or the first probe reaches it, the environment is inherited; a software render never drops it; outside WSL there is one probe.
- [x] `frameCapture-wslWayland.test.ts`: the capture session launches its browser the way the probe reached the GPU.
- [x] Each test fails when its piece is removed (retry flag, render env, capture wiring), and both files pass 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Engine `tsc` and the browserManager, browserLeasePool, wslHost, hdrCapture and frameCapture suites (410 tests) pass on Linux.
- [x] Windows test PC (Intel, WSL, Mesa 23.2.1): with the variable dropped for every launch, Chrome's environment had no `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (checked with `strace`) and renders came out black. That result is what changed this PR to the probe-gated version.
- [x] Windows test PC, this version, 3 renders: when the first probe found no GPU (cold start), the second probe ran without `WAYLAND_DISPLAY`, also found none, and the render kept `WAYLAND_DISPLAY` (checked with `strace`) and produced correct frames; when the first probe found the Intel GPU (warm start), there was no second probe and the render stayed on the GPU with correct frames. The hardware-without-`WAYLAND_DISPLAY` path needs a machine like the reporter's.
- [x] `parallelWorkerBrowsers.browser.test.ts` (from #5565) timed out its 5 s page load once on a loaded Windows runner. It passed 5 of 5 runs on this branch and on main on the Windows test PC. A shared browser never loads that page, so the limit is now 20 s: forcing both workers onto one browser still fails it, and it passes 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Documentation updated: the troubleshooting note no longer suggests full Chrome.

To check it on a machine with an NVIDIA card under WSL (clear any `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` first):

```bash
git fetch origin fix/wsl-gpu-wayland-display && git checkout FETCH_HEAD
bun install && bun run build
cd /path/to/project
node /path/to/hyperframes/packages/cli/bin/hyperframes.mjs render --output out.mp4
```

`bun run build` needs Node 22.18 or later. Expected in the log:

```text
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → software (WebGL unavailable)
[hyperframes] browserGpuMode probe → hardware (without WAYLAND_DISPLAY: WebGL renderer ... D3D12 (NVIDIA ...) ...)
[BrowserManager] Browser launched (HeadlessChrome/152..., beginframe, ...)
```

title: fix(inspector): grep timeline windows, continuation, candidates and timeline text from the Canary dogfood
body:
## What

Fixes to `grep_components` and `grep_timeline`, all reported by the agent in a Desktop Canary (b340) session with Mods on:

**Timeline numbers**
- **A nested composition host reports its own authored window.** A host with `data-start="0" data-duration="4"` was reported as `0.0000–3.7200s`, where 3.72s is when its last tween ends. After boot, the runtime strips `data-duration`/`data-end` from nested hosts and keeps them as `data-hf-authored-*`. Timeline inspection built its resolver without `includeAuthoredTimingAttrs`, so it fell back to the GSAP timeline duration. It now reads the authored attributes, as the runtime's own resolvers do.
- **One source location per line.** A one-line script listed the same `file:line` up to nine times per animation; the text and `events[].sources` are now de-duplicated by `file:line`.

**Components budget**
- **No continuation loop.** When a page fit no snippet (e.g. `maxBytes: 2048`), the report returned `nextOffset` equal to the requested offset, so continuing returned the same page forever. A page that fits no snippet now returns `nextOffset: null`; `omitted` still lists each snippet's id and size for a `snippets: [...]` fetch with a larger budget.
- **Candidates are not capped at five.** `candidates` was sliced to 5 with no way to page the rest (`.w-dot` had 25). Candidates now fill up to half the budget, longest list trimmed first, keeping at least 5 per target; the rest is still counted in `candidatesOmitted`.

**Element ids**
- **Stamping no longer reformats the file.** studio-server's id stamping rewrote each file through linkedom, so a compact one-line composition came back with its whitespace and attribute quoting changed and the agent's next `old_string` no longer matched. `stampHfIdsInPlace` mints the same ids but inserts only ` data-hf-id="…"` into the source text. If the parser did not keep the source's tags one-to-one (e.g. an unterminated tag), it falls back to `ensureHfIds`. `ensureHfIds` itself is unchanged, because the SDK relies on its normalized output.
- **The source tag is found before its id is stamped.** Desktop holds stamping while an agent is writing, so the served page has a `data-hf-id` that the file does not have yet, and `grep_components` returned no HTML for every new element. When no source tag carries the element's id, the lookup falls back to its id or classes, still only when exactly one tag matches.

**Element map**
- **The live map shows authored classes and text.** On the live preview, the map is a snapshot of the page at the playhead, so moving the playhead pushed a diff like `class="a-ch"` → `class="a-ch on"` and text like `"0.0"` → `"5.2"`. Each element whose source tag is identified (by hf id, else a unique id) now shows its authored classes, in the source's own order, and leaf text from its source. Selectors are rebuilt from those classes so they still resolve on the live page. An element whose live classes drop an authored one keeps its live state.
- **Letters a script splits out of a text node collapse to one stable line.** `#a-type` is one sentence in the file; the film's script replaces it with a span per character and then flips `a-ch` / `a-ch on` / `a-ch on cur` as the playhead moves. Those spans are not in the source, so on the real Canary diff they were 54 of the 58 changed lines. Children of a source element that has its own text are now one row, `span ×27 @1-27 (generated)`, with no class and no per-letter text, and the parent keeps the source sentence. An empty element keeps what a script appends (`i.e-p ×2` stays), because those are the content.
- **A grouped row names its children** (`i.ch ×3 @1-3`), and an id the runtime strips (`#root` on a sub-composition) stays on the line as `id="root"`. The selector itself is not `#root`: that id is gone on the live page, so a query for it still matches nothing.
- Only the live view does this, and it reads just the HTML files (`authoredHtml`), so the map still never builds the full source index (`mapSourceLifecycle.ts` holds).

**Timeline text**
- **One heading per component.** Groups were ordered by start time only, so `#benefits` appeared twice with `#root` between. Groups are now gathered by component, keeping time order inside each.
- **One relation line per pair of groups.** A repeating tween (film grain, 840 intervals) filled all eight `Relation:` lines with its own endpoint handoffs.
- **`attr` / `css` values are named.** `attr:{width:50}` read `attr: ? → ?`; it now reads `attr.width: 0 → 50`.
- **Eases.** A function ease reads `custom function` instead of `?`. A keyframes tween's own ease is shown (`steps(8) across keyframes, power1.inOut per segment`) instead of only the per-segment default.
- **Rounded numbers** in the text (`2.7`, not `2.6999999999999997`). The JSON keeps the raw value.
- **Past the end.** A query starting at or after the film's duration says so (`Requested time is past the end: the film is 120s long.`) instead of a bare `found` with nothing in it.
- **Candidates are named.** An ambiguous component listed `# div`; it now lists `.p-card div in s06-prompt`.

**Check false positives**
- **A container inside the scene can allow overlap.** `data-layout-allow-overlap` on the text or on a container inside the scene applies. A marker on the scene root still does not, and the hint says so.
- **A letter on its own fill is measured against that fill.** Contrast used the median pixel inside the box, so a circular avatar's letter was scored against the panel around it. An element with its own opaque background now uses that color.
- **Two fromTo calls warn only when they share a from-property.** A position tween beside a scale tween no longer suggests `immediateRender: false`, which would show the element early.
- **A negative z-index under a stacking-context parent stays quiet.** A same-file ancestor set to `isolation`, `opacity` below 1, `transform`, `filter`, `contain: paint` or `will-change` is enough. Isolation on an unrelated element still warns, and an unproven ancestor keeps the conditional message.
- **Tweens that only meet at an endpoint are not an overlap.** `2.35 + 0.22` is `2.5700000000000003`, so a handoff at 2.57s was an overlap. Contact within 1ms is ignored. A real shared-property overlap still is.
- **`visibility: visible` on a child is named, not paired as two texts.** It overrides an ancestor's `visibility: hidden`, so the runtime hide never reaches it. That is `visibility_escapes_segment`.
- **A sparse dot grid is not an opaque cover.** A radial gradient of 1.6px dots was treated as fully painted. Coverage is the painted fraction of the tile. A solid gradient still occludes.

**Picking and labels**
- **A faint texture veil is not the click target.** Own opacity under 0.2, a background image, and no text (the grain layer) is skipped. A child that only sets `pointer-events: none` stays unpickable, and content inside a root that sets `pointer-events: none` stays pickable.
- **An element with no id names its nearest ancestor that has one.** The timeline text reads `.a-ch in #a-type`. `withinId` is optional on `ElementRef`. The agent reads that text; the Desktop output schema did not need a change.

## Why

Agents read these outputs literally. In the session the agent called the 3.72s scene length a bug in its own film, looped on `nextOffset: 0`, could not reach 20 of 25 candidates, and lost the first page of every whole-film query to the grain layer's relations.

## Related work

Refs the Desktop Mods dogfood (hyperframes-internal, Canary b340). The Desktop half (dropping `time` from the live tool, whose preview never seeks) is heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#3944. There is no OSS issue.

## How

- `core/src/runtime/timelineInspection.ts`: `includeAuthoredTimingAttrs: true`; pass a keyframes tween's ease to `animationValues`.
- `core/src/runtime/timelineValues.ts`: expand `attr`/`css` objects into `attr.<key>` endpoints; name function eases; combine the keyframes ease with the segment ease.
- `inspector/src/mapInspection.ts`: budget-driven candidate trimming; `nextOffset: null` for a page with no snippet.
- `inspector/src/pageQueries.ts`: the page timeline carries the player's duration.
- `parsers/src/hfIds.ts`: `stampHfIdsInPlace` (a start-tag scanner that skips comments and raw-text contents, then aligns tags with the parsed elements); `studio-server/src/helpers/hfIdPersist.ts` uses it.
- `inspector/src/sources.ts`: `markup()` falls back to id/classes when no tag has the element's hf id.
- `inspector/src/authoredState.ts` (new): `withAuthoredState`, applied by `inspectElementMap` when the view has `authoredHtml` (the live view does); `sources.ts` splits the opening-tag scan out of `Sources` for it; the page snapshot records each element's child position.
- `inspector/src/timelineReport.ts`: `onePerSourceLine`, `byComponent`, `pastTheEnd`, one relation per group pair, rounded values, named candidates.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `tests/mapInspection.test.ts` (new, vitest): a 3 KB snippet under `maxBytes: 2048` gives `nextOffset: null` and is fetchable by id; 25 candidates all return under the default budget and stay within a 4096-byte budget.
  - `tests/timelineCompositions.ts`: host windows, one location per line, one heading per component (an overlapping composition reproduces the split), one relation for a repeating tween, past-the-end text, named candidates.
  - `tests/timelineValues.ts`: `attr.width: 0 → 50`, `custom function`, `steps(8) across keyframes`, `rotation: ? → 2.7`.
  - `parsers/src/hfIds.test.ts`: a no-whitespace composition and a full document with comments, script and SVG come back byte-identical apart from the inserted ids, with the same ids as `ensureHfIds`.
  - `studio-server/src/helpers/hfIdPersist.test.ts`: the file on disk keeps its own formatting.
  - `inspector/tests/sources.test.ts`: an element with a served hf id the source lacks still gets its tag; an ambiguous class still gets none.
  - `inspector/tests/elementMap.test.ts`: runtime classes and counter text map the same as at rest; script-split letters stay one `(generated)` line across two playhead states; an empty element keeps appended particles; class order follows the source; a stripped id is annotated and is not the selector.
  - `inspector/tests/live.ts`: toggling a class and text on the live page leaves the element map unchanged.
- [x] Manual testing performed (details below)
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments say why, not what

### What I measured

- Fails without the fix for this pass: with the rule and layout sources reverted, eight new assertions fail (endpoint overlap, disjoint fromTo, an isolation parent, allow-overlap on a container, the visibility escape, the sparse grid, the avatar's own background, and the overlap hint). The veil test fails if the picker still returns the texture. The timeline label test fails if `withinId` is ignored.
- Fails without the fix: with the source changes stashed, `tests/mapInspection.test.ts` fails 2/2, and `timelineCompositions.ts` / `timelineValues.ts` each fail an assertion (`actual: 8` relation lines; `attr: ? → ?`). With the old stamping, the disk test fails (`stampFileHfIds` reformats the file); without the `markup()` fallback the sources test fails (`null`); without `authoredHtml` on the live view, `live.ts` fails `runtime class and text`. With `authoredState.ts` and `elementMap.js` reverted, `elementMap.test.ts` fails 4: the `@1-3` places, the `(generated)` line, `i.word.light` and `id="root"`. The original host-window check failed with `2.8400000000000003 != 6.39`.
- With the fixes: inspector vitest 35/35, `mapSourceLifecycle.ts`, `lifecycle.ts`, `sourceRelease.ts` PASS, parsers 1273, studio-server 1303, sdk 652; `tests/timeline.ts`, `timelineCompositions.ts`, `timelineValues.ts`, `browser.ts` and `live.ts` all PASS (live after `bun run --filter @hyperframes/inspector build`).
- On a copy of the session's project, `#benefits` reads `0.0000–4.0000s` and each animation lists `compositions/benefits.html:31` once.
- `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs` and `scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` pass; pre-commit hooks pass.

### What I did NOT exercise

- Desktop or Canary against this build; that needs a release, then a bump of `@hyperframes/*` in hyperframes-internal.
- `source unknown` on every live animation reproduces on Canary b340: the packaged app's esbuild cannot spawn its binary from inside `app.asar` (`spawn ENOTDIR`), so the preview is served with no `sourceURL`. That fix is heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#3948. This PR does not change source mapping.
- Selecting an element still does not attach its source, CSS or timeline. The prompt only includes the selector, the gestures and the screenshot lines.
- `[data-composition-src]` and a query for a sub-composition's `#root` still match nothing, because the query runs on the live page, where both are gone. The map line now carries `id="root"` so the id is visible; it is not a selector.

title: chore(skills): storyboards are a board of stills with one page format
body:
## What

A storyboard is now planned as **stills on a board**, with one page format everywhere. `hyperframes-creative/references/storyboard-recipe.md` keeps its path and every link to it, and now teaches:

1. pose each shot in its composition at its key moment;
2. snapshot the stills with `npx hyperframes snapshot --at <seconds> --no-end --describe false -o boards/stills`;
3. write the board at `boards/storyboard.html`: one `class="frame"` box per still holding its image, a `class="title"` line (`01: The hook`) and a `class="time"` range (`0.0 to 3.0s`), with optional `class="words"` and `class="act"`;
4. stop for the person's go, and change only the frames they note.

Every place that taught the old sheet (a root `storyboard.html` of `id="frame-NN"` cells, drawn without the CLI) now points at that contract: the review loop's sketch pass, the frame worker's confirmed-sketch section, the sketch steps of faceless-explainer, pr-to-video and product-launch-video, music-to-video, general-video, the intent interview, production loop, `storyboard-format.md`, `story-spine.md`, `hyperframes`, `hyperframes-cli`, `hyperframes-studio`, and the two prompting docs. `STORYBOARD.md` stays the plan beside the board.

## Why

Two storyboard page formats were in use, so a board written to one was unreadable by tools built for the other ("No frames found"). One format, taught in one place, fixes that.

## Related work

None.

## How

- The recipe's sections are now § 1 the run, § 2 the page, § 3 the plan beside it; references to the old § 3 (page) and § 4 (review round) point at the new sections.
- The review loop's sketch pass now poses and snapshots instead of drawing cells, so `snapshot` is the one CLI it runs.
- `scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` lists `boards/storyboard.html` (instead of `storyboard.html`) as a file skills write into a project.
- `skills-manifest.json` regenerated.

## Test plan

- [x] `gen-skills-manifest --check`: in sync (21 skills).
- [x] `lint-skills`: 33 skill files, cross-references in 354 markdown files, no issues.
- [x] `check-skill-mirror`: OK.
- [x] `check-comment-citations` on this diff: OK; its tests: 103 pass.
- [x] `oxfmt --check` on every changed file.
- [x] `git grep` outside the changelog: no `id="frame-NN"` cell instructions or root `storyboard.html` left; the only `frame-NN` mention is the recipe's note that such boxes are not found.

## No visible change

Skill and docs text only; no Studio or player change.

title: docs(skills): document local Kokoro narration, word-timed beats and dispatch reliability
body:
## What

Adds practical learnings from building a ~4-minute narrated technical explainer with 14 scenes through `/general-video` (local Kokoro narration, word-timed reveals, sub-composition scenes built by parallel frame workers). Each item was checked against the current skills first. Items the skills already covered were left out, and claims were checked against the CLI, lint, and bundler source.

| Learning | Where |
| --- | --- |
| **Kokoro venv setup.** When `pip` is missing or PEP 668 blocks installs (Homebrew Python on macOS), use `uv venv` and `uv pip install kokoro-onnx soundfile`, then point `HYPERFRAMES_PYTHON` at the venv. Also covers one clip per line through the audio engine with `"provider": "kokoro"`, and `tts --json` → `durationSeconds`. | `media-use/audio/references/tts.md` |
| **`af_heart` pace.** About 164 wpm at speed 1.0 (planning pace is 150), so estimates from it run long. | `media-use/audio/references/tts.md` |
| **Per-clip transcription gotchas.** The input path resolves against the cwd, not `--dir` (`File not found` otherwise). `transcript.json` is overwritten in `--dir` on every run. Caption arrays (`const TRANSCRIPT = [...]`) in `.html` files under `--dir` get patched. Word `end` times can overshoot the clip. | `media-use/audio/references/transcribe.md` |
| **Hand-applied duration sync.** Slot = lead (0.6 s) + real VO + tail (0.8 s). Neighbouring slots overlap by the transition, the VO starts at slot start + lead, and lines stay one tail apart with transitions in the silence. Cues go in as scene-local word start + lead. Seams are tweened on hosts or plain wrappers, never visibility/`autoAlpha` on a `.clip`. | `hyperframes/references/production-loop.md` (new section) + pointer from `general-video` stage 6 |
| **Sub-composition asset paths.** `@font-face`/`url()`/`src` can be written relative to the sub-composition file (`../../assets/...` from `compositions/frames/`). The bundler rebases them (`rewriteAssetPath`). | `hyperframes-core/references/sub-compositions.md` |
| **Sequential VO clips need `data-duration`.** Lint treats a missing duration as open-ended, so every pair warns `duplicate_audio_track`. | `hyperframes-core/references/variables-and-media.md`, `tracks-and-clips.md` |
| **Stall watch.** 3 of 7 parallel frame workers wrote nothing to disk or their transcripts for 10–40 min. Poll artifact and transcript mtimes. After about 10 min of silence with the artifact missing, re-dispatch or build inline (4 frames took about 15 min inline). An open Studio rewrites composition files to stamp `data-hf-id`, so file changes there aren't progress. | `hyperframes/references/subagent-dispatch.md` + pointer in `general-video` stage 4 |
| **No preview harnesses.** Workers that finished had built throwaway headless-Chrome harnesses. Telling them not to launch browsers, servers or long-running processes, or run the CLI, helped. | `subagent-dispatch.md`, `frame-worker-core.md` |
| **Shared build kit + exemplar.** Append the exact kit to the design truth file (`@font-face` rules, background clip, component classes, a seeded generator for recurring motifs, recurring element specs with inline icons). Build and snapshot one exemplar before dispatch. This kept 14 frames from 6 builders consistent. | `general-video/SKILL.md` stage 4 |
| **Self-check codes that lint caught after the fact:** `template_literal_selector`, `gsap_repeated_fromto_without_baseline` (`immediateRender: false`), `overlapping_gsap_tweens`. | `frame-worker-core.md` self-check |
| **Symbol glyphs.** Captured brand fonts and the renderer's bundled families are Latin subsets with no `≤ ≥ ≈ → ✓`, so use inline SVG or words. I parsed the bundled woff2 cmaps in `fontData.generated.ts`: JetBrains Mono, Inter and Noto Sans JP all lack these code points. A local snapshot can hide this through system fallback fonts. | `frame-worker-core.md` font bullet |
| **Packets.** Write an explicit `- rules: a, b` line. Packets over 48 KB are rejected, so cite 2–3 rules per scene. | `general-video/SKILL.md` stage 1 |

Left out because the skills already cover them: spelling names phonetically for TTS (`hyperframes-creative/references/narration.md`), generating audio in the background (production-loop scheduling), and per-line TTS + transcription into `audio_meta.json` (the audio engine already does this).

## Why

Each of these cost real time in that build: a TTS setup dead end, a transcript overwritten between clips, a lint warning on every VO pair, workers silent for 40 minutes, and symbols rendering from a fallback font. None of it is in the skills an agent reads at those stages.

## Related work

None found. Tiny, self-contained docs additions.

## How

Short additions in the existing style of each file. No rewrites of unrelated text, and no code changes. New sentences stay in present tense with resolvable citations.

## Test plan

- [x] `oxfmt --check` (0.41.0, repo config) on all 9 changed files
- [x] `node scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` against `upstream/main`: OK (only warnings on pre-existing lines)
- [x] `node --test skills/general-video/scripts/frame-packets.test.mjs` (builds `_role.md` from the edited `frame-worker-core.md`)
- [x] Checked each claim against source: `packages/cli/src/api/transcribe.ts` (input resolution, `--dir`), `packages/cli/src/whisper/normalize.ts` (`patchCaptionHtml`), `packages/lint/src/project.ts` (`duplicate_audio_track`), `packages/lint/src/rules/gsap.ts` / `composition.ts` (codes), `packages/parsers/src/rewriteSubCompPaths.ts`, `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/hfIdPersist.ts`, `skills/hyperframes/scripts/lib/frame-packets-core.mjs`
- [ ] Unit tests added/updated (docs only)
- [x] Documentation updated

title: feat(cli): hyperframes audio measures where sounds land, in film time
body:
## What

`hyperframes audio` tells an agent (or a person) where a sound lands, so a cut or an animation can land on it. Today agents write throwaway ffmpeg/numpy scripts to find a whoosh's peak; this replaces those with one command that answers in film time.

```bash
npx hyperframes audio sfx/whoosh.mp3                # one file, file seconds
npx hyperframes audio sfx/hit.wav --place-at 4.2    # not in the film yet: where it lands if it starts at 4.2 s
npx hyperframes audio --element '#riser'            # one clip of the film, film seconds
npx hyperframes audio --at 12                       # every sound playing at 12 s
npx hyperframes audio --range 10,14 --only onsets   # every hit between 10 and 14 s
```

```
audio/vo_2.wav #a-v2  film 10.200–12.900, file from 0.000  voice (0.6)
  onset 10.256  steepest 10.308  peak 10.314  tail end 12.731
  hits 10.235(1.00) 10.555(0.65) 10.705(0.29) 10.740(0.22) 10.835(0.31) 10.980(0.92) ... +7
  loudness -21 LUFS, true peak -5.5 dBTP
  silent 11.055–11.300
  ▆██▇▇▇▇▇▆█▇▇▇▇▆▅▂▁▁▃██▇▇▇▇▅▇█▇▇▇▇▆▅▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▆▆▅▅▃▁
```

## How it is built

**`@hyperframes/core/audio-analysis`**: new public subpath. It holds pure functions of PCM, so they run the same in Node, Bun and the browser:

| Capability | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `moments` | onset (RMS first reaches 20% of peak), steepest rise, peak, tail end (−40 dB) |
| `onsets` | every hit with relative strength. Spectral flux of log magnitudes (default), or energy |
| `loudness` | BS.1770 gated integrated LUFS, short-term max, sample and 4× true peak, clipping |
| `silence` | quiet spans under a threshold |
| `kind` | `sfx` / `voice` / `music` guess, with the features it used |
| `envelope` | RMS level over time, optionally band-limited |

- **Provider ladder.** Every capability runs through `runLadder`, which takes a quality (`best` / `local` / `fast`), a custom order, or a pinned provider. Each step reports `answered`, `excluded`, `unavailable` or `failed`, and a failed provider falls through to the next one with a warning. Signal processing is the only provider today. Model and service providers (beats, sections, words, describe) plug in later without changing callers.
- **`hyperframes audio`** decodes with FFmpeg at the file's own rate, keeping each channel. For film queries it reads the project through `describeProject`, nested compositions included. It analyzes only the part of each file that plays, and it reads 0.1 s of context on each side so a window's edge is not reported as a hit.
- **JSON output.** Times are in file seconds, and each item carries its `placement` (`start`, `mediaStart`, `playbackRate`, `volume`, and `dataStart`, the element's own `data-start`, local to its composition). Text output prints film time.
- **Timeline rows gain `mediaStart`.** It comes from `data-playback-start` / `data-media-start`, moved forward by whatever an in-point host's cut skips. That is what maps file time onto film time.
- **Shared FFT.** The radix-2 FFT moves out of `audioCarve.ts` into `core/src/fft.ts`, so both use one copy.

## Benchmark

Every number here was measured on real files from my machine: 42 SFX, 16 voice lines and 75 music beds, taken from launch videos and agent eval projects and deduplicated by hash. The corpus is not checked in.

**Onsets.**
- **Test set:** 29 single-event SFX placed at known times. There were 160 five-second mixes holding 691 placed effects, each at 0 to −12 dB. Some mixes had a −70 dB noise floor and the rest sat over a music bed at +6, 0 or −6 dB.
- **Truth:** the placement time plus the effect's own onset on its clean file.
- **Scoring:** a placed effect counts as found when an onset lands within ±30 ms of its truth. Results are compared with librosa 0.11 `onset_detect`.

| Clean (noise floor) | recall | transient / swell | median \|err\| | false/s outside effects | ms per s of audio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **flux, threshold 0.1 (new default)** | **0.806** | 0.932 / 0.711 | **3.7 ms** | 0.14 | 8 |
| flux, threshold 0.3 (first draft) | 0.647 | 0.781 / 0.546 | 3.6 ms | 0.03 | 8 |
| flux, hop 10 ms | 0.782 | 0.945 / 0.660 | 3.3 ms | 0.12 | 4 |
| flux, 2–16 kHz band | 0.753 | 0.904 / 0.639 | 3.7 ms | 0.10 | 7 |
| energy, threshold 0.1 | 0.741 | 0.808 / 0.691 | 1.7 ms | 0.03 | 0.06 |
| librosa default | 0.800 | 0.918 / 0.711 | 7.4 ms | 0.15 | — |
| librosa superflux | 0.753 | 0.890 / 0.649 | 8.0 ms | 0.14 | — |

| Over a music bed at 0 dB | recall | median \|err\| | false/s |
|---|---|---|---|
| **flux, threshold 0.1** | **0.795** | **3.5 ms** | 1.97 |
| flux, threshold 0.3 | 0.637 | 3.2 ms | 1.43 |
| energy, threshold 0.1 | 0.719 | 3.3 ms | 4.04 |
| librosa default | 0.830 | 9.5 ms | 1.98 |

- **The default threshold changed from 0.3 to 0.1.** With the threshold measured against the strongest onset, quiet hits beside loud ones were dropped. At 0.1, recall matches librosa, and the timing error is half librosa's with no +5 ms bias.
- **Tried and rejected: normalizing strength within a 0.5–2 s neighbourhood.** It made noise in quiet spans fire, raising false alarms from 0.14 to 4.7 per second.
- **Swells are a known limit.** Whooshes and swishes are only about 70% recalled at ±30 ms, because an onset detector fires on the biggest spectral change, not where the sound becomes audible. For a single sound, `moments` is the answer to use. Energy onsets reach 0.91 swell recall at ±50 ms, but they report 2.2 extra hits inside every effect.
- **Ladder outcome:** no change. Signal processing stays the only onset provider, and librosa adds nothing worth a Python dependency.

**Codec timing.** Clean mixes were encoded to MP3 192k and AAC 192k, then decoded the way the CLI decodes them. The median onset shift was 0 ms in both. The maximum was 1 ms for AAC and 15 ms for MP3, a single outlier where the encoder smeared one transient.

**Loudness vs `ffmpeg -af ebur128=peak=true`, 124 files.**
- Integrated loudness: median difference 0.0 LU, maximum 0.1 LU.
- True peak: median difference 0.0 dB, maximum 0.2 dB.
- Speed: 3.5 ms per second of audio. It was 51 ms per second before the K-weighted block powers moved to prefix sums and true-peak interpolation was limited to samples at or above half the sample peak.

**Kind, 133 files.** 128 are labelled correctly: 39/42 SFX, 16/16 voice, 73/75 music. The first draft's duration-first rule got 97: every voice line under 4 s came out as `sfx`, and 15 ambient scores came out as `mixed`. The thresholds were set by looking at this same corpus, so treat the accuracy as in-sample. The misses are a bass impact, a keyboard loop and a glitch read as voice, plus one 1 s music sting and one vocal soundtrack.

## Tests

- **Core (21):**
  - synthetic impacts, swells and multi-hit effects;
  - BS.1770 reference values (a full-scale 997 Hz sine reads −3.01 LUFS; a second channel adds 3.01 dB);
  - inter-sample peaks;
  - classification;
  - ladder fallthrough and exclusion.
- **CLI (18 new):**
  - film/file time mapping;
  - target selection by element, second, range and boundary;
  - decoding and analyzing real WAVs through FFmpeg, skipped when FFmpeg is absent;
  - the edge-of-window case;
  - a file that cannot be read failing alone, without stopping the rest;
  - formatter capping.
- **Checked against the old code:**
  - The in-point `mediaStart` test fails without the `cutRow` change.
  - The window-edge test fails with the edge context set to 0.
  - `describeProject` suites: 48 pass.

## Placing a file not in the film yet

`--place-at <s>` answers as if the file started at that film second. `--skip-file-seconds <s>` cuts that much from its start; it is refused without `--place-at` or when it would skip the whole file, and the result warns when the cut part held the file's loudest moment. There is no `--boundary`: `--at` and `--range` cover the sounds a cut touches.

## Not in this PR

- Beats, sections, words and descriptions. The ladder has the capability names, but no provider answers them yet; `hyperframes beats` remains the beat tool.
- The agent-facing tool that formats this for the Desktop agent, which lives in hyperframes-internal and depends on a release with this command.

title: feat(cli): snapshot --keep redoes one still and leaves the others
body:
## What

`npx hyperframes snapshot --keep` adds stills to the `--output` folder instead of clearing it, and names each still for its time: `at-0s.png`, `at-1.5s.png`, `at-12.25s.png`. Snapshotting one moment again replaces only that still. The default stays the same (the folder is cleared and stills are numbered per run), so `check`, the artifact folders and existing scripts are unchanged.

The storyboard recipe is unchanged here. Older CLIs ignore an unknown `--keep` and clear the folder, and Desktop bundles an older CLI, so the recipe moves to `--keep` (and drops #5599's `redo/` step) in a follow-up once a release with the flag is what Desktop and other hosts run.

## Why

Without the flag, `snapshot` removes every PNG and JPEG in its output folder and numbers stills by their place in the run. Redoing frame B of a three-frame board wipes A and C, and B comes back as `frame-00-…`, not under the name the board points at. #5599 worked around this in the recipe: snapshot the redo into `boards/stills/redo/` and move one file over. With per-time names in a folder that is never cleared, a redo can be a single command, and a page that already points at `stills/at-3s.png` shows the new still without a rewrite.

## How

- `--keep` (default off) skips the clean-up of the output folder and names each still `at-<time>.png`, using the same time spelling as today (`formatSnapshotTimestamp`: three decimals at most, no trailing zeros). `--against` reference files follow the same names (`ref-at-…`, `pair-at-…`).
- A still's name is its time to the millisecond, so `--keep` refuses, before it captures or writes anything, a run whose distinct `--at` times share a name (for example `1.5` and `1.5004`). Across runs, one name means one moment: that is the redo.
- Stills, crops and `--against` reference frames are published with the existing safe writer (`writeCaptureFileSync`: staged, then renamed over the target), so a symlink or hard link already at a still's name is replaced, never written through. The screenshot is taken as bytes and published the same way.
- With `--keep` there is no contact sheet: the folder mixes stills from several runs, so a sheet of it would not describe this run.
- `docs/packages/cli.mdx` lists the flag.

## Test plan

title: fix(cli): a killed browser on a busy Windows machine no longer fails check
body:
## What

When `check`, `snapshot` or any other CLI command has to force-kill its browser, the close now finishes as soon as the operating system reports the process gone. Before, it waited only for Node's `exit` event. On a busy Windows machine that event can arrive many seconds after the process is already dead, and the command failed with "Browser process did not exit after forced shutdown." Linux and macOS behave as before.

## Why

`checkDeadline.process.test.ts` ("managed launches own distinct profiles while the first browser is alive") fails on Windows CI with that error. It is not only a test problem: any CLI run on a loaded Windows machine that reaches the forced kill hits the same false alarm.

Measured on a Windows 11 test machine (Intel, Node 22.23.3, Chrome headless shell 152), with the test run 10 times under 11 CPU-burner processes and 5 times idle:

| | kill → `process.kill(pid, 0)` says gone | kill → Node `exit` event |
|---|---|---|
| Loaded (27 kills) | 1 to 5 ms (all 27) | median 8.8 s, max 29.2 s; 2 kills saw no `exit` within 30 s |
| Idle, forced kill (15 kills) | 0 to 2 ms | 108 to 187 ms |

Under load the test failed 20 of 20 times; idle it passed 20 of 20. Timers fired on time (about 3 ms late), so the Node event loop was not stalled. Windows ends a killed process asynchronously: it sets the exit code right away, and Node's `exit` event follows only when termination completes.

## How

- `closeBrowser` (`browser/launch.ts`): after the forced kill, the 1 s limit now races Node's `exit` event against a 50 ms poll of `processIsAlive(pid)` (the existing helper in `utils/processTree.ts`). Whichever reports the process gone first ends the close.
- On Linux and macOS a killed child that Node has not yet reaped still answers `kill(pid, 0)`, so the poll never ends the close before `exit` there.
- A process that is still alive after the forced kill still fails the close with the same error.

## Test plan

- [x] `launch.test.ts`: a browser whose close never finishes and whose process never emits `exit`. With an already-gone pid the close resolves; it fails with the old error without the poll. With a live pid (the test process) the close still rejects "did not exit". Passes 3 runs in a row.
- [x] `launch.process.test.ts` and `checkDeadline.process.test.ts` pass on Linux (7 of 7).
- [x] CLI `tsc` and comment checks pass.

## Size

Under the 100-line floor on purpose: a standalone root fix for a Windows CI flake that also makes real CLI runs fail on busy Windows machines, with nothing open to carry it.

title: fix(cli): capture keeps fonts a page declares in its own style block
body:
## What changed

`hyperframes capture` now downloads fonts that a page declares in its own `<style>` block with a relative url.

The capture already rewrote relative `url()`s to absolute ones for linked stylesheets and `style=""` attributes. A page's inline `<style>` was copied as written, so `src: url("/fonts/Brand.woff2")` stayed relative. The font download only matches absolute `http(s)` urls, so those fonts were skipped and not counted as drops. The capture summary still listed the families, which hid the gap.

The fix resolves relative `url()`s in every `<style>` element against `document.baseURI`, in the same step that fixes `style=""` attributes. `data:`, absolute, protocol-relative and `#fragment` refs are left alone, so `filter: url(#glow)` still points at the page's own SVG.

## What I measured

- `bunx vitest run src/capture/htmlExtractor.test.ts`: 3 runs in a row, each exit 0, 1 passed.
- Fails without the fix: with `htmlExtractor.ts` from main, exit 1, 1 failed (`expected [] to deeply equal [ Array(1) ]`: no font was fetched).
- A fix that also rewrites `#fragment` refs fails too (`url(#glow)` is no longer in the head).
- The test drives `extractHtml` on a page with an inline relative `@font-face`, then feeds its output to `downloadAndRewriteFonts` and reads the font file back from `assets/fonts/`.
- `bunx vitest run src/capture`: exit 0, 39 files, 370 passed. `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean.
- Real capture of a site whose fonts are declared in an inline `<style>`: v0.8.151 saves 2 font files (the two from its linked CSS). This branch saves all 6, and `fonts-manifest.json` identifies each inline family by name and weight.

## What I did NOT exercise

- `<style>` blocks inside shadow roots or iframes: the capture doesn't read those today.
- `@import` inside an inline `<style>`: its url is made absolute, but the imported sheet is not fetched or inlined (unchanged).
- A page with a `<base href>`: covered by `document.baseURI`, not tested on a real site.

title: feat(cli): init --keep-original copies a clip as is, without transcoding
body:
## What

- `hyperframes init --keep-original` (boolean, default off): the `--video` file is copied under its own name and wired into the composition exactly as a web-safe clip is wired today. No transcode and no prompt, in interactive and non-interactive mode. Without the flag, init behaves as before.
- Theora is no longer treated as browser-safe. It leaves init's `WEB_CODECS`, so init converts it to H.264 MP4, and it joins `BROWSER_HOSTILE_CODECS` in the preview server, so preview swaps to an H.264 proxy instead of showing a blank frame.
- One row for the new flag in the `init` flag table in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.

## Why

- **Theora shows no picture.** In Chromium 152 (Electron 44.2.0 on macOS), a Theora clip in a `<video>` element loads but never shows a picture: `videoWidth` stays 0 and no frames are decoded. Init counted Theora as web-safe and copied it as is. The preview proxy then refused to convert it (`browser_safe_codec`), so the preview stayed blank.
- **The transcode in init is not always needed.** A 1-minute 4K60 HEVC 10-bit clip spends 51 s inside `init` on an Apple M4 Pro, all of it in the libx264 transcode. Render decodes every source with FFmpeg and never uses the browser's decoder, and preview already converts browser-hostile clips lazily through the proxy. Callers that rely on those paths can now skip the up-front transcode.

## How

- The flag sits next to `--skip-transcribe` in init's citty args and reaches `handleVideoFile` as a fourth parameter. With it set, the codec check is skipped and the clip falls through to the existing copy-as-is branch. Both callers (interactive and non-interactive) pass it.
- Init and the preview server still each keep their own list. Init's list is an allow-list (`WEB_CODECS`: anything else is transcoded). The preview server's list is a deny-list (`BROWSER_HOSTILE_CODECS`: only these are proxied). They differ on purpose: VP9 and AV1 are web-safe for init but get a `canPlayType` probe in preview, and an unknown codec is transcoded by init but left alone by preview. Merging them would change init's default for those codecs, so this PR edits both.
- Theora's preview entry has representative mime `video/ogg; codecs="theora"`. A browser that still decodes Theora keeps the original. Pre-warm is on because Chromium and Safari have no Theora decoder, so some client is sure to need the proxy.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `init.test.ts`: `--keep-original copies a non-web --video as is instead of converting it`. Runs init on an MPEG-4 Part 2 clip and checks that `src="clip.mov"` is wired, the bytes are identical and no `clip.mp4` exists.
  - `init.test.ts`: `converts a Theora --video to H.264 MP4`. Checks that `src="clip.mp4"` is wired and no `.ogv` is left.
  - `mediaCodecMap.test.ts`: adds `theora` to the `shouldPrewarmProxy` pre-warm cases.
  - Two small fixtures (1.7 KB MPEG-4, 4.2 KB Theora) were made by ffmpeg from `testsrc`.
- [x] Fails without the fix. I undid each change alone, ran its test, then restored the change:
  - Removing `!keepOriginal &&` from the codec check: `AssertionError: expected '<video\n        id="a-roll"\n        …' to contain 'src="clip.mov"'`
  - Putting `"theora"` back in `WEB_CODECS`: `AssertionError: expected '<video\n        id="a-roll"\n        …' to contain 'src="clip.mp4"'`
  - Removing the `theora` entry from `BROWSER_HOSTILE_CODECS`: `pre-warms theora, which has no cross-platform browser decode` → `AssertionError: expected false to be true`
- [x] Results on Linux (Node 22, vitest 4.1.11, system ffmpeg):
  - `init.test.ts`: 36/36 passed.
  - `mediaCodecMap.test.ts`: 29/29 passed.
  - The new tests passed 3 runs in a row.
  - `tsc --noEmit` passed in `packages/cli` and `packages/studio-server`.
  - `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` passed on the changed files.
  - `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` exited 0.
- [ ] Manual testing performed. Not run: an interactive `init` with the flag, a Studio preview of a Theora clip end to end, and Firefox or Safari behaviour for Theora.
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: test(engine): the warm extraction cache test checks ffmpeg did not run, not the clock
body:
## What

The engine test "reuses extracted frames on a warm cache hit" now proves the hit by checking that ffmpeg did not run again, instead of checking the hit took under 50 ms.

## Why

The 50 ms wall-clock check failed on a loaded Linux runner (`expected 101 to be less than 50`) and dropped an approved PR from the merge queue. Elapsed time measures the runner, not the cache. The comment beside the check said its purpose was to catch "a regression that accidentally triggered ffmpeg again", and that is now asserted directly.

## How

- `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` wraps `runFfmpeg` in a pass-through `vi.fn` (same behaviour for every test in the file) and asserts the call count does not change across the warm extraction. The existing `cacheHits`/`cacheMisses` and frame-count checks stay.

## Test plan

- [x] The test passes 3 runs in a row on Linux.
- [x] With the cache-hit branch changed to count the hit but extract again, it fails (`expected 4 to be 3`); the old timing check would only have caught that if ffmpeg happened to be slow enough.

## Size

Under the 100-line floor on purpose: this flake knocks approved PRs out of the merge queue today. The studio Windows flake fix joins this PR if it is ready before review.

title: fix(core): show a scene's starting state on a render's first frame
body:
## What changes for a user

The first frame of a render now shows the state a composition's timeline sets at time 0. Before, a sub-composition whose starting state comes from `tl.set(..., 0)` steps (words hidden until they animate in, positions set by the timeline) rendered frame 0 with the page's pre-timeline styles: every hidden word visible, stacked at `left: 0`. Frame 1 onward was already right. Frame 0 is also what posters and thumbnails come from.

## Root cause

GSAP does not render when a timeline is seeked to the time it already sits at. A sub-composition timeline that has never rendered sits at 0, so the render's seek to 0 (`seekRuntimeTimeline` for standalone sub-composition timelines) was a no-op and its t=0 steps first applied on the seek to frame 1. The same no-op was already written twice in `init.ts` as "force GSAP to render the current frame" (`seek(currentTime)` after nesting children, and after a timeline rebind).

## Fix

One helper, `seekGsapTimeline` in `runtime/adapters/gsap.ts`: seek, and if the timeline did not move and GSAP has never drawn it, redraw it silently with the existing `rerenderGsapTimelineAt`. "Never drawn" is GSAP's own `_initted`, read from the real timeline through a child's `parent` (the registered object can be the render-mode timeline proxy). The standalone sub-composition seek, the master seek and both "render the current frame" seeks go through it; the master's own eventful re-render is skipped when the helper already redrew.

So each timeline gets at most one extra redraw, and a nested scene the root already drew is never redrawn alone after the root (a later root tween on the same property keeps the last word).

## What I measured

- New real-render test `firstFrameStartingState.integration.test.ts` (sub-composition, web font, words hidden by `tl.set(...,0)`, revealed at 0.5 s): on `main` frame 0 mean grey level is 14.8 vs 0 for frame 1 (red); with the fix both are 0 (green, 3 runs in a row).
- New unit tests in `gsap.steps.test.ts`: a never-rendered timeline seeked to 0 applies its t=0 step; a timeline parked at one time is redrawn once, not on every seek; a `call()` at 0 still fires exactly once across seek(0), seek(0), seek(0.1).
- New `init.test.ts` case (review witness): root and nested child tween the same opacity, the later root tween wins at `renderSeek(1)` (0.9), also after the child timeline gains a step. It gave 0.5 with the first version of the helper.
- Mutations: "never drawn" forced true fails the parked and nested-precedence tests; forced false fails the frame-0 unit test and the real-render test. Nothing else goes red.
- `packages/core` `src/runtime`: 80 files, 2039 tests pass, including the existing render-nudge and zero-duration-callback tests in `init.test.ts`. Two of those mocks now record only `totalTime(t)` calls, not the no-argument read.
- Cost: a 10-scene, 30 s fixture (300 steps per scene) renders in 38.4 to 39.0 s on main and with this change, 1 worker, two runs each. The first version of the helper redrew parked scenes on every frame (4,000+ redraws on that film); this one redraws each timeline at most once.
- A real multi-scene project rendered before and after, through the same harness: only frame 0 changes. Lossless PNG frames of its first scene are byte-identical from frame 1 on.
- Reproduced on Linux (BeginFrame capture) and macOS (screenshot capture).

## What I did NOT exercise

- A timeline that is `clear()`ed and rebuilt keeps GSAP's drawn flag and its time resets to 0, so a later seek to 0 still does not redraw it (unchanged from `main`).

- Studio preview: the runtime seek is shared, so a preview parked at 0 on a never-rendered sub-composition timeline should now show its starting state too; not walked by hand.
- `player.ts`'s non-transport seek path: the runtime always passes a transport, so it is not on the render path and is unchanged.

Also: the test's frame-level reader now lives in `frameLevelsTestFixtures.ts`, shared with `segmentedColorGrading.integration.test.ts`. Fallow still reports an older 18-line clone between that file and `motionBlurVideo.integration.test.ts`, untouched here.

title: ci: a stalled history fetch in change detection is retried instead of failing the run
body:
## What

The "Detect changes" jobs (ci, regression, windows-render, player-perf) and ci's "Test reachability" now give their full-history checkout one minute and retry it once if it stalls. Each job's limit goes from 2 to 4 minutes to fit the retry.

## Why

Now and then the checkout's history fetch stalls in "Fetching the repository" until the job's 2-minute limit cancels it. That fails the whole workflow ("Change detection did not succeed"), and it has knocked PRs back several times today, #5605 and #5612 among them. Measured on the last 116 runs of these jobs:

| Workflow | Runs | Checkout median / p90 / max (healthy) | Stalled |
|---|---|---|---|
| regression | 40 | 16 / 22 / 30 s | 0 |
| windows-render | 38 | 16.5 / 23 / 41 s | 1 (cancelled at 149 s, mid-fetch) |
| ci | 38 | 16 / 22 / 45 s | 1 (cancelled at 45 s) |

A healthy fetch finishes in under a minute (slowest seen: 45 s). A stalled one does not recover before the limit, so a bigger limit alone would only make the stall wait longer. A second fetch starts a new connection.

## How

- The first `actions/checkout` gets `id: checkout`, `timeout-minutes: 1` and `continue-on-error: true`. A second checkout with the same inputs runs only if the first did not succeed, with its own 1-minute limit. If the retry also fails, the job fails as before.
- Job limits: 2 → 4 minutes.

## Test plan

- [x] actionlint reports the same findings on these four files as on main (only existing shellcheck notes), and the YAML parses.
- [x] The repo's workflow tests pass: catalog-publication, check-edit-accuracy-filter, check-test-reachability, comments-workflow, publish-workflow.
- [x] The retry path, on this PR with a temporary commit (since dropped) that pointed the first checkout at a missing ref. That checkout failed (`A branch or tag with the name 'no-such-ref-for-the-retry-proof' could not be found`), the retry checked out, and "Detect changes" passed (regression run 38611952962). A first try that cut the step limit to 0.1 minute did not time out, so step limits under a minute are not usable to simulate a stall.
- [x] With the first checkout healthy, the retry step is skipped (run 38611656354).

title: fix(cli): a long video conversion in init never stalls on ffmpeg's own log
body:
## What

- `hyperframes init` converts a non-web `--video` with ffmpeg in `transcodeToMp4`. It now spawns ffmpeg with `stdio: "ignore"` instead of `"pipe"`. Nothing ever read those pipes, and the function only returns whether ffmpeg exited 0.
- `hyperframes render --docker --quiet` no longer pipes the container's stdout without reading it. It is now ignored. stderr is still read, echoed live and kept as a bounded tail for the failure message, as before.
- Every other async child-process spawn in `packages/cli`, `packages/producer` and `packages/engine` was audited (table below). None of them needs a change.

## Why

ffmpeg writes its progress log to stderr for the whole conversion. With an unread pipe, the OS buffer (64 KB on Linux and macOS) fills, and ffmpeg blocks in `write()` forever. `init` then hangs with its spinner still running. On a stuck run, every sample of the ffmpeg process was in `__write_nocancel` under `av_log_default_callback`. Its output file had stopped growing 17 minutes earlier, at 0% CPU.

`docker run` in quiet mode has the same shape on stdout: the container's log goes to a pipe nobody reads.

## Related work

None.

## How

- The smallest change to each spawn's stdio option, in each file's existing style. No new helpers.
- `transcodeToMp4` has no failure message that uses ffmpeg's output: on failure, init prints "Transcode failed" and copies the original. So both streams are ignored rather than drained into a tail nobody prints.

### Audit: async spawns with a piped stdout or stderr

Async `spawn` only; the sync and buffered calls are in the last row. Line numbers are at this branch's base.

| Call (file:line) | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cli/src/commands/init.ts:196` (`transcodeToMp4`) | **Fixed** | stdout and stderr were piped and never read. ffmpeg's log fills the pipe and blocks. Now `stdio: "ignore"`. |
| `cli/src/commands/render.ts:849` (docker, `--quiet`) | **Fixed** | stdout was piped and never read, so a long render's log could fill it. Now ignored in quiet mode. stderr is read and kept as a bounded tail (unchanged). |
| `cli/src/capture/captureCompositionFrame.ts:580` (`runFfmpegOnce`) | Safe | stderr is read. Both callers (snapshot, grade-compare) write one frame to a file, so stdout stays empty. |
| `cli/src/utils/optionalPackages.ts:172` | Safe | stdout and stderr both have `data` listeners. |
| `cli/src/utils/stoppableExecFile.ts:48` | Safe | Both streams are collected when piped. |
| `cli/src/utils/cancellableProcess.ts:69` | Safe | Both streams are read, capped at `maxBufferBytes`. |
| `cli/src/commands/preview.ts:1454`, `:1520` (Studio dev server) | Safe | `attachStudioReadyHandler` attaches `data` listeners to both streams for the child's lifetime. |
| `cli/src/background-removal/pipeline.ts:361` | Safe | stderr is read into a tail. The decoder's stdout is the frame stream, consumed by `readFrames`. Encoders use `stdout: "ignore"`. |
| `cli/src/whisper/sherpa.ts:145` | Safe | stdout is ignored. stderr is read and bounded. |
| `cli/src/utils/openBrowser.ts:81`, `desktopApp.ts:61`, `backgroundChecks.ts:34`, `telemetry/transport.ts:173`, `processTree.ts:63` | Safe | `stdio: "ignore"`. |
| `cli/src/utils/autoUpdate.ts:221`, `commands/previewLifecycle.ts:246`, `commands/skills.ts:60` | Safe | Output goes to a file descriptor (log file or the parent's stderr), not a pipe. |
| `producer/src/plan-parity-analysis.ts:203` | Safe | Both streams have `data` listeners. |
| `producer/src/services/audioExtractor.ts:92` | Safe | stderr is read. Every caller writes to an output file, so stdout stays empty. |
| `producer/src/services/render/audioPadTrim.ts:665` | Safe | stdout is read. stderr is drained into a bounded tail by `ManagedChildProcess`. |
| `engine/src/utils/runFfmpeg.ts:159` | Safe | stderr is drained into a bounded tail by `ManagedChildProcess`. Every caller writes to a file or the null muxer, so stdout stays empty. |
| `engine/src/utils/gpuEncoder.ts:65`, `:180` | Safe | `-encoders` stdout is read, or ignored for the probe. stderr goes through `ManagedChildProcess`. |
| `engine/src/utils/ffprobe.ts:68` | Safe | stdout is read and capped. stderr goes through `ManagedChildProcess`. |
| `engine/src/services/streamingEncoder.ts:484` | Safe | Frames go in on stdin and the output is a file, so stdout stays empty. stderr goes through `ManagedChildProcess`. |
| 93 `spawnSync` / `execFileSync` / `execSync` / `execFile` / `exec` calls (cli 78, producer 9, engine 6) | Safe | Node buffers their output itself, so they cannot block on a full pipe. Output over `maxBuffer` fails the call instead of hanging. |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `init.test.ts`, `transcodeToMp4 > finishes when ffmpeg logs far more than a pipe buffer holds`. A stand-in ffmpeg (a node script set through `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH`) writes 1 MB to stderr with blocking writes, then writes the output file and exits 0. The test asserts that `transcodeToMp4` resolves `true` and the file exists. It has a 5 s timeout. It is skipped on Windows, like the other stand-in-binary tests in this package.
- [x] Fails without the fix. With `stdio: "pipe"` restored: `Error: Test timed out in 5000ms.` (`× finishes when ffmpeg logs far more than a pipe buffer holds 5009ms`). No stand-in process was left running afterwards.
- [x] Results on Linux (Node 22, vitest 4.1.11):
  - `init.test.ts` and `init.transcodeToMp4.windowsHide.test.ts`: 36/36 passed.
  - `init.test.ts`: 35/35 passed 3 runs in a row.
  - `render.test.ts`: 99/99 passed.
  - `tsc --noEmit` passed in `packages/cli`.
  - `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` passed on the changed files.
  - `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` exited 0.
  - `comment-ratchet.mjs` and `check-comment-citations.mjs` passed.
- [ ] Manual testing performed. Not run: a real long `init --video` conversion, or a real `render --docker --quiet`.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable). Not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: chore: release v0.8.158
fix(cli): check and snapshot run where a sandbox refuses to listen on localhost
body:
## What a person can do now
`hyperframes check` and `hyperframes snapshot` work inside a sandbox that refuses to listen on localhost, such as a macOS seatbelt profile that denies network binds. Today both stop with `listen EPERM 127.0.0.1` before the browser opens, so lint passes but the runtime, layout, motion and contrast checks and the stills never happen.

## Why it failed
Both commands open two listening sockets:
- `serveStaticProjectHtml` serves the project on `127.0.0.1:<port>` (`utils/staticProjectServer.ts`).
- Chrome's DevTools connection listens on a port too (puppeteer's default `--remote-debugging-port`).

A sandbox that refuses `listen()` stops the first one with EPERM (or EACCES).

## The fix
- `serveStaticProjectHtml`: when `listen()` is refused with EPERM or EACCES, the server doesn't listen. It returns an in-process origin (`http://hyperframes-<n>.localhost/`) and an `answer(request)` that runs the same request handler over an in-memory socket pair. Range requests, `?hf-proxy=` variants and the codec map are unchanged. Any other bind error still fails as before.
- `openSettledCompositionPage` (the one page opener behind check, snapshot, compare and grade-compare): for an in-process origin, Chrome launches with `pipe: true` (DevTools over stdio, no port) and `--single-process`. Requests to the in-process origin are answered with `request.respond()`; every other request continues as usual.
- Nothing changes when `listen()` works.

## Tests
- `staticProjectServer.test.ts`: with `listen()` refused (EPERM), the project is answered in-process: the page, a `bytes=2-5` Range as 206, and a 404. Nothing listens, and the origin is forgotten on close. A non-refusal bind error (EADDRINUSE) still rejects.
- `captureCompositionFrame.browserFallback.test.ts`: for an in-process origin, the launch uses `pipe: true` with `--single-process`, the page answers the project from the server and lets other requests through. A port-served project keeps the usual launch.
- Both new tests fail on main: the server rejects with `listen EPERM`. Both files pass 38/38, three runs in a row. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean on the CLI.

## Proof inside a real sandbox (macOS, `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny network-bind)'`, this branch built from source)
| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `hyperframes check <project> --json` (3 runs) | `ok: true`, browser ran (runtime and layout ok, 16 contrast samples), 4 to 5 s each |
| `hyperframes snapshot <project> --at 1,3,5 --no-end --describe false -o stills` | 3 stills and the contact sheet written |
| released 0.8.157 `check`, same sandbox | exit 1, `listen EPERM: operation not permitted 127.0.0.1` |
| this branch `check`, no sandbox | `ok: true`, unchanged |

Known gap, fixed in a follow-up: the GPU probe that runs before the page still launches its own Chrome on a DevTools port. In the sandbox it waits out its 120 s timeout and falls back to software rendering, then the check passes. The 4 to 5 s timings above include the follow-up, which gives the probe the same pipe and `--single-process`.

## What I did NOT exercise
- A project with video and audio under `--single-process` (the proof project is HTML, CSS and fonts). These paths run only when listening is refused, which today fails outright.
- A Linux sandbox (seccomp or landlock). The fallback keys on EPERM or EACCES from `listen()`, which is what those return.
- `validate`, `layout` and `motionShot` open their own pages and still need a listening server.

title: fix(core): a hidden scene's contents stay hidden when a child is set visible
body:
## What

An inactive scene can no longer paint anything inside it. The runtime adds one page-level rule: every element inside a timed clip that the visibility pass hid is `visibility: hidden !important`.

## Why

The visibility pass hides an inactive clip with inline `visibility: hidden`. Clips that hold timed elements of their own only get that (in-flow timed leaves also get `display: none`). CSS lets a descendant marked `visibility: visible` paint inside a hidden parent, and ordinary GSAP authoring writes exactly that.

Repro: a scene with a GSAP `tl.set(el, { visibility: "hidden" }, t)` plays in the preview. When the set first renders, the scene is showing, so GSAP records `visible` as the start value. Seek back to an earlier scene and GSAP writes `visibility: visible` inline on that element. The later scene is hidden, but its layer (here a dark full-frame backdrop and a blurred clip) paints over the earlier scene at every time until reload.

This only happens in the interactive preview, after playing across the boundary and seeking back. Renders and fresh seeks record the start value while the scene is still hidden, so they never write `visible`.

The existing guard (`clipChainVisibleAt`) covers timed descendants only. An untimed element inside the clip had no protection.

## Related work

Refs #5614, which also changes how the runtime seeks scenes; this PR doesn't touch seeking.

## How

`timedClipHide.ts` already appends page-level rules for hidden clips (`SKIP_HIDDEN_IMAGES`). The new rule sits beside it, keyed on the same hidden-clip selector, which is now one constant (`HIDDEN_CLIP`, with `SKIPPED_CLIP` built from it). It is added once per page, in preview and render alike. A stylesheet `!important` beats the inline values GSAP writes, and layout is untouched, so measuring an inactive scene still works. Stamped clips stay excluded, as before, because Studio owns their visibility.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test: a child set `visible` inline inside an inactive, absolutely positioned scene computes `hidden` at 1 s and 8 s and `visible` at 6 s. It fails without the change (`visible` at all three). Passes 3 runs in a row.
- [x] `vitest run src/runtime`: 80 files, 2036 tests pass. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- [x] Manual, real browser: a 4-scene project bundled for preview and seeked into the third scene, with the later scene's layer set `visible` inline (what the rewind writes). With today's runtime the frame is dark (99.84% of pixels differ from the correct frame). With this runtime it matches the correct frame (0.0% differ).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(audio): preserve subprocess causes through CLI diagnostics
body:
## What

Preserve audio subprocess causes from the engine through producer warnings to a versioned, bounded `@hf-diagnostic` CLI line. Missing executables, ordinary exits, deadlines and grouped-mix failures retain distinguishable stage/reason/exit/signal/OS-code fields.

## Why

Desktop export reports can currently say only that audio preparation failed and the CLI exited 1. The engine knows more but discards child-process evidence; group submixes also collapse typed causes. This is the independent source/CLI contract slice. Desktop ingestion follows once the contract is released.

## Related work

- https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes-internal/pull/3990 adds Desktop project-create/IPC diagnostics and has merged. This PR starts from fresh `main` and does not depend on it.
- Open #5304 routes human capture notices to stderr and touches different emitters. The new record uses piped machine output and stays silent in terminal/quiet output, including batch JSON.

## How

Keep content-free subprocess evidence on audio failures, preserve group failures, and project at most 16 allowlisted records into local and distributed warning paths. Deep-clone nested evidence in warning snapshots. For an external interruption, put the triggering failure first and sanitize at the audio-stage boundary before passing records to the shared encoder error. The error class has only a type import of the audio contract, keeping encoding-only paths independent of its runtime helper.

Re-project at the final CLI writer: no detail, element IDs, messages, stderr, paths, URLs, arguments, tokens, prompts or project contents enter this new record. No telemetry upload or consent behavior is added.

## Test plan

- 292 focused checks across CLI handler/wire (115), mixer/grouping/cloning (87), audio stage/event publisher/assembly (44), distributed plan/policy (46).
- All 687 Bun producer unit tests across 39 files pass, including encodeStage's exact 20 previously failing cases. All four assembly interruption assertions pass with the original mock and assertions retained.
- Real subprocess stand-ins induce ENOENT, exit 7, deadline/SIGTERM and group exit 9; exact fields survive mixer → producer policy → final CLI writer. POSIX executable stand-ins skip Windows; field/privacy tests run on every OS.
- A real interrupted child following 16 missing sources reproduces the ordering bug without the fix. The final writer retains the triggering failure and exactly 16 records with the fix. Real local orchestration also reaches the final writer; CLI handler tests cover ordinary/interruption failures and quiet mode.
- CLI diagnostic tests use isolated mkdtemp projects with cleanup. CodeQL SARIF traced three new temporary-file flows to the added shared /tmp/project test call; that predictable path is removed. Hosted CodeQL must re-run; no alert is suppressed.
- Mutation: removing only subprocess preservation causes five final-consumer regressions to fail; restored implementation passes.
- Fresh full workspace build, affected rebuilds, package typechecks, changed-file lint/format, test reachability, normal hooks and diff audit pass. Audit has three inherited unused interruption-error members and no new findings.
- The broader local Vitest producer attempt has one real-media AAC loudness failure (4.4 LU vs 3 LU) in unchanged audio-pad code; its threshold is retained. The full local lane is not claimed green. Hosted CI reruns on every new head.
- Probe errors keep existing stage/reason without new ffprobe child evidence. Browser/FX exceptions remain `internal`.
- No packaged Desktop, signed-in Datadog delivery, real customer media, production deployment or release exercised. These are local/component and CLI-boundary checks, not live acceptance.

title: chore: release v0.8.159
fix(cli): the GPU probe uses the pipe too, so a sandboxed check doesn't wait 120 s
body:
## What a person can do now
`hyperframes check` and `snapshot` inside a sandbox that refuses to listen on localhost start in seconds, with the GPU mode the machine supports. Before this, they first waited 120 s for the GPU probe and then fell back to software rendering.

## Why
#5618 serves the project in-process and drives the page's Chrome over a pipe when `listen()` is refused. The GPU probe that runs first launches its own Chrome, still on a DevTools port. Inside such a sandbox, that port never opens, so the probe waits out its 120 s timeout ("Timed out after 120000 ms while waiting for the WS endpoint URL").

## The fix
`resolveManagedGpuMode` takes `noListen`; its probe Chrome then launches with `pipe: true` and `--single-process`, like the page's. `openSettledCompositionPage` sets it exactly when the project is served in-process. Nothing changes when `listen()` works.

## Tests
- `launch.noListen.test.ts`: with `noListen`, the probe's launch has `pipe: true` and `--single-process`; without it, the launch is unchanged. It fails on main.
- With the #5618 tests: 41/41, three runs in a row. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.

## Proof inside a real sandbox (macOS `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1)(allow default)(deny network-bind)'`, CLI built from this branch)
- `check --json`: `ok: true`, browser ran, 4 to 5 s each (3 runs). The probe reports hardware WebGL over the pipe.
- The same check without this change spent 120 s on the probe, then fell back to software.

title: fix(cli): first render on Windows no longer fails while a new browser or ffmpeg is scanned
body:
## What changes

On Windows, the first render after Chrome or ffmpeg is freshly installed no longer fails its startup checks. When a check does time out, the error now says it timed out.

## Why

Windows antivirus scans a freshly written executable on its first launch, and the `--version` / `-version` / `-encoders` probes gave it 5 s. Measured on a Windows 11 x64 PC with Microsoft Defender (each on a fresh copy of the binary, 3 tries each):

| Binary | First launch | Second launch |
|---|---|---|
| chrome-headless-shell 152 (209 MB), CPU busy | 6.7 s, 6.7 s, 6.8 s | 41 to 46 ms |
| ffmpeg (79 MB), CPU idle | 8.8 s, 10.9 s, 13.4 s | 47 to 117 ms |

CPU load on its own is not the cause: during a 4K x265 encode at 93 to 100% CPU, `chrome-headless-shell --version` on an already-scanned binary took 42 to 55 ms across 10 runs.

A real render hit this and failed with `Chrome cannot start: Failed to run "...chrome-headless-shell.exe" --version.`, with no reason given. That was a second bug. On timeout the runner kills the process tree with `taskkill /T /F`. If the process exits before taskkill gets to it, taskkill exits with 128, and its error replaced the timeout. So the user saw neither the timeout nor its cause.

## How

- `FIRST_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000` (in `browser/ffmpeg.ts`) is the one budget for the probes of these binaries: Chrome `--version`, ffmpeg/ffprobe `-version` and both `-encoders` probes. 60 s is about 4.5x the worst first launch measured. A hung binary still fails, only later.
- `runCancellableProcess`: once the child has closed, a failed tree kill no longer replaces the reason it was stopped (timeout, abort, output limit).

## What I measured

- `cancellableProcess.killFailure.test.ts` (new): the tree kill fails and the run still rejects with `ETIMEDOUT`. On the old code it rejects with `taskkill exited with status 128`.
- The preflight tests pin the new budget. Putting it back to 5 s fails 4 of them.
- preflight, ffmpeg, cancellableProcess and processTree tests: 42 pass, 3 runs in a row on Linux. oxfmt, oxlint and tsc are clean for the changed files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- I did not rerun a full render on Windows with this build. The Windows numbers above come from timing the binaries directly.
- No macOS or Linux first-launch timing. The budget only matters where a first launch is slow.

title: fix(studio-server): history copies a changing file without stalling its sweep
body:
History copies every changed project file into its blob store with `fs.copyFile`. When the copy is a byte copy (no clone) and another writer shortens the file while it is being copied, `fs.copyFile` never returns: libuv's copy loop asks for the remaining bytes past the new end of the file, gets 0 back, and loops forever. The sweep waits on that copy, and every history operation queues behind the sweep, so undo, redo and the next sweep hang with it. The stuck copy also holds a threadpool thread for good.

A byte copy is what Linux ext4 does (CI runners included), and what macOS does on any volume that is not APFS. On xfs, btrfs and APFS the copy is a clone, which is one atomic snapshot, so the bug never shows there.

## What changes
- `blobStore.put` copies a project file through `cloneOrStream`: it first tries a forced clone (`COPYFILE_FICLONE_FORCE`), which is still one snapshot. Where the file system cannot clone, it streams the file instead, and a stream stops at the file's real end. A file shortened mid-copy is stored as whatever was read, and the next sweep sees the file's new stat and stores its real contents.
- The stream copy keeps the source's mode, as `copyFile` did, so Undo still restores an executable file with its exec bit.
- A copy that fails (a missing, unreadable or changing source) removes its temp file, so no `incoming-*` file is left in the store.
- `cloneOrCopy` is unchanged: it copies blobs out of the store, and those never change.

## What I measured
- Plain Node, no repo code (node 22.22.1, libuv 1.51.0 on Linux; node 22.23.3, libuv 1.52.1 on macOS): a 64 MB file shortened while `fs.copyFile` copies it is still copying after 5 s on ext4 (8/8 runs, with and without `COPYFILE_FICLONE`), on tmpfs (12/12) and on a non-clone copy on macOS (2/2). On xfs the copy clones and returns every time (14/14).
- The new test on a Linux ext4 temp dir: fails on main 3/3 with "the sweep never returned"; passes 3/3 at this head. On xfs it passes on main and at this head (the clone path).
- The whole `src/history` suite at this head: 178 passed, 2 skipped, on ext4 and on xfs. The three copy tests pass 3 runs in a row on ext4. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check` (0.41.0) and the comment ratchet are clean.

## The test
"a file shortened while the history copies it in" writes a 64 MB file, starts a flush, and waits on the real condition (the store's temp copy passing 1 MB, or the sweep finishing first on a disk that clones). Only then does it shorten the file. It fails within 10 s instead of hanging the run.

## Fails without the fix
- fails without the fix: with main's `blobStore.ts`, the new test fails on ext4 3/3 with "the sweep never returned".
- fails without the fix: without the temp cleanup, "leaves no partial copy in the store" fails (an `incoming-*` file is left).
- fails without the fix: streaming without the source's mode, "keeps the file's mode" fails on ext4 (644, not 755).

## What I did NOT exercise
- Windows. libuv's Windows copy does not offer a forced clone, so Windows now always takes the stream; I did not run this there.
- Upstream libuv: the copy loop itself is not fixed here.
