title: fix(cli): report spend usage for Claude plans without rate windows
body:
## What

`hyperframes usage` now reports usage for spend-metered Claude plans (for example Enterprise) instead of always returning `{"status":"unknown","reason":"invalid_usage_response"}`.

- Known Claude results gain a `spend` window (`usedPercent`, `remainingPercent`, `resetsAt: null`) read from `spend.percent`, falling back to `extra_usage.utilization`. It is `null` for Codex and Grok and for Claude plans that do not report spend.
- A well-formed response with no window at all now reports `no_usage_windows` instead of `invalid_usage_response`.
- The `hyperframes-cli` skill documents the new field and reason.

## Why

On an Enterprise login, `/api/oauth/usage` returns `200` with `five_hour: null` and `seven_day: null`; the allowance lives in `spend` / `extra_usage`. `parseHarnessUsage` accepted the shape, but `knownUsage()` found no window and returned `invalid_usage_response`, so every agent following the skills ("run `npx hyperframes usage --json` at the start…") saw usage as unknown, and the reason pointed at a malformed response that was not malformed.

Repro before this change: on a Claude Code Enterprise login, `npx hyperframes usage --json` prints `{"status":"unknown","reason":"invalid_usage_response"}`.

## Related work

None found.

## How

- `usageBudget.ts`: optional, nullable `spend` and `extra_usage` schemas (inner fields nullable too, so an absent or null figure never invalidates the whole response). `claudeSpendWindow()` prefers `spend.percent` when spend is not disabled, otherwise `extra_usage.utilization` when extra usage is enabled. Over-limit spend caps at 100% used; negative spend still fails validation.
- `knownUsage()` takes the optional spend window and returns `no_usage_windows` when every window is absent. This also changes Codex `{"rate_limit":{}}` from `invalid_usage_response` to `no_usage_windows`, since that response is also well-formed but has no window.
- Kept `spend` separate from `weekly` rather than reusing it: its period is the billing period, not a week, and it has no reset time in the response.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`usageBudget.test.ts`: spend window, `extra_usage` fallback, over-limit cap, disabled spend ignored, negative spend rejected, `no_usage_windows` for Claude and Codex; existing expectations gain `spend: null`)

title: Preview: a trimmed video clip is shown before it has a frame at its in-point (black at every cut)
body:
In `<hyperframes-player>` preview, a composition made of trimmed `<video>` clips (one source, `data-media-start` per clip) flashes black at every cut. We measured 48–132 ms of no picture at all 11 cuts of one draft, on 0.8.82 and still on 0.8.153.

**Cause.** When a clip's window starts, the runtime makes its element visible and, on the same tick, seeks it to its `data-media-start`. The element is shown while it seeks (`readyState` at `HAVE_METADATA`, `seeking` true), so the first frames after the cut have nothing to paint. Renders are unaffected, since they seek and wait on every frame.

**What fixed it for us.** Before each cut, we put the incoming clip's element on its in-point: any clip that starts within 1.5 s, is paused, isn't already seeking and isn't on its `data-media-start` gets `currentTime = mediaStart`. The runtime's activation then finds it within its hard-sync tolerance (0.5 s), doesn't seek it again, and shows a decoded frame at the cut. The 1.5 s lead covers a range request and one GOP over the network. We do this from the embedding page today, by reaching into the player's iframe. It belongs in the runtime's media sync, which already knows each clip's window and media start.

**Proposed fix.** In `syncRuntimeMedia`, for a clip that isn't active yet but starts within a lookahead window, seek its (paused) element to its `mediaStart` once, so it arrives at its window already decoded. Glad to send a PR with a runtime test that records the element's state at the moment it becomes visible.

title: feat(cli): audio answers beats, downbeats, bpm, sections and describe through a provider ladder
body:
## What

`hyperframes audio --only beats,downbeats,bpm,sections,describe` now answers the music's structure, each capability through the provider ladder #5602 set up, filled to its designed shape:

| capability | ladder (first that answers wins) | on this Mac (macOS 26.5.2, CLT only) |
|---|---|---|
| moments, onsets, loudness, silence, envelope, kind | `signal` | unchanged, real |
| beats, downbeats | `api` → `apple-mu` → `beat-this` → `signal` | `api`: real against a local stand-in server (no backend yet). `apple-mu`: **unavailable**, see below. `beat-this`: real, run here from an isolated uv env with local `small0` weights. `signal`: real |
| bpm | read off whichever provider answered `beats` (median interval + a ±4 s curve) | real; never a second tempo estimator |
| sections | `api` → `apple-mu` → `signal` | `api`: stand-in. `apple-mu`: unavailable. `signal`: real |
| describe | `api` → `apple-sound` → none | `apple-sound`: real (macOS SoundAnalysis via a Swift helper). Off macOS nothing local answers, and the value is `null` with a warning |
| words | not here: `--only words` says to use `hyperframes transcribe` | |

Every provider has `available()` returning `{ ok: true }` or `{ ok: false, reason }`. A provider that is unavailable, whose check throws, or whose run fails is passed over, and the ladder warns once per capability with every reason, e.g.

```
! beats: used signal; api unavailable (HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_API_URL is not set); apple-mu unavailable (Music Understanding needs macOS 27; this Mac runs 26); beat-this unavailable (HYPERFRAMES_BEAT_THIS_PYTHON is not set)
```

`--quality local` excludes `api`; `--quality fast` leaves only `signal`. `--provider beats=beat-this` pins one; `--full` prints each step.

### Value shapes (JSON, file seconds like the rest; `provenance.<capability>` names the provider)

```ts
beats:     { times: number[]; confidence?: number; reason?: string; snap?: SnapReport; source?: string }
downbeats: { times: number[]; meter: number | null; confidence?: "low"; snap?: SnapReport; source?: string }
bpm:       { value: number | null; curve: { t: number; bpm: number }[] }
sections:  { spans: { start: number; end: number; label: string }[]; snap?: SnapReport; source?: string }
describe:  { tags: { label: string; score: number }[]; text?: string; source?: string }
SnapReport { reference: "signal beats"; toleranceMs: number; snapped: number; unsnapped: number[]; medianShiftMs: number | null }
```

`beats.times` is empty with `reason: "no steady beat"` when the signal tracker's confidence is under 0.05, or `"too short for a steady beat"` under 6 s. Signal downbeats carry `confidence: "low"`.

## Why

Agents cut to music. A beat grid, a bar, a section change and "what is this" are what they ask about after "where does this hit". The ladder lets a better model answer when one is present, and keeps the answer measured: an `api` time is moved onto a beat signal processing actually heard.

## Measurement-led times (rule 1)

Each beat, downbeat and inner section boundary the `api` returns is snapped **one at a time** to the nearest signal-tracked beat, only when one is within **a quarter of the answer's own beat period** (125 ms at 120 BPM); otherwise it is kept and listed in `snap.unsnapped`. The service's tempo level and bar phase are kept. `snap.medianShiftMs` is the median distance moved, a direct read of how much the service and the signal agree.

Why a quarter beat: half a beat would let a time jump to the off-beat; an eighth would fail on a service that is off by a typical 20–60 ms at fast tempi. The separate beat benchmark simulated this: an API off by σ = 150 ms goes from F 0.28 raw to 0.97 snapped, and one off by only σ = 20 ms goes from 0.996 to 0.977, so snapping costs a little on an already precise answer. That cost is why it is reported per answer rather than hidden.

## The `api` contract (for the HeyGen backend route)

- `POST <HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_API_URL>`, the URL exactly as configured, no path appended.
- `Authorization: Bearer <HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_API_KEY>`. Unset URL or key → unavailable. The key is never printed or put in a result.
- Optional `HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_API_TIMEOUT_MS` (default 120000).
- Body `multipart/form-data`, two parts:
  - `request` (`application/json`):
    ```json
    { "version": 1, "capabilities": ["beats", "downbeats"], "audio": { "sampleRate": 44100, "channels": 2, "duration": 31.5 } }
    ```
    `capabilities` ⊂ `beats | downbeats | sections | describe`. The CLI asks for beats and downbeats together in one request, and for sections and describe each in its own.
  - `audio` (`audio/wav`, filename `audio.wav`): 16-bit PCM of the analyzed span, channels and sample rate as decoded.
- Response `200` `application/json`, times in seconds from the start of the uploaded audio; leave out what you cannot answer:
  ```json
  {
    "version": 1,
    "source": "free text, reported as given",
    "beats": { "times": [0.48, 0.98] },
    "downbeats": { "times": [0.48], "meter": 4 },
    "sections": { "spans": [{ "start": 0, "end": 12.1, "label": "intro" }] },
    "describe": { "text": "optional sentence", "tags": [{ "label": "music", "score": 0.91 }] }
  }
  ```
- Any other status fails that rung (the CLI falls through to the next); `{ "error": { "message": "..." } }` in the body is shown in the warning. A missing capability, or one in another shape, also fails that rung.
- No model name is in the CLI; `source` is how the service names what answered.

The types are `AudioApiRequest` / `AudioApiResponse` in `packages/cli/src/audio/analysis/providers/api.ts`.

## `apple-mu`: unavailable, and why

Music Understanding (WWDC26 session 253, `MusicUnderstandingSession`) ships with macOS 27. This Mac runs macOS 26.5.2 with only the Command Line Tools SDK 26.5, which has no MusicUnderstanding framework, so there is no SDK to build or check a helper against. The provider is therefore real only as a gate: on macOS < 27 it says `Music Understanding needs macOS 27; this Mac runs 26`; on 27+ it says `no Music Understanding helper yet: it needs the macOS 27 SDK to build`; off macOS, `macOS only`. No Swift for it is written, so nothing guesses at the API.

## `beat-this`: opt-in, never downloads

Beat This! (CPJKU, MIT) runs only through Python/PyTorch. It is available when `HYPERFRAMES_BEAT_THIS_PYTHON` names a Python that has `beat_this` (checked with `importlib.util.find_spec`, no torch import) and the `small0` weights are on disk: `HYPERFRAMES_BEAT_THIS_CHECKPOINT`, or `beat_this-small0.ckpt` in the Torch hub cache. The weights are passed as a local path, which Beat This loads with `torch.load`; with a fresh empty `TORCH_HOME` a run here created nothing there. The audio is handed over as a WAV the CLI decoded, so its own `.m4a` limitation does not apply. Install steps are in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.

## `signal` beats and sections (rule 6)

- Beats: per-band log power (5 bands/octave, 30 Hz–9 kHz, summed over channels so a polarity-flipped channel cannot cancel) → rectified flux above a ±0.4 s local mean → autocorrelation tempo with a log-normal prior around 120 BPM (+½ of the double lag) → Ellis (2007) DP with tightness 100 and a local period from 8 s windows held within 0.7–1.4× of the global one → trim weak end beats. A port of `beat-bench/scripts/tsbeat.ts` with local tempo on, as that benchmark recommended.
- Confidence = autocorrelation clarity × min(1, onset lift / 3); under 0.05 → `no steady beat`.
- Downbeats: the meter (4, or 3 with a 0.85 handicap) and phase whose beats carry the most low-band (<150 Hz) onset energy. Marked `confidence: "low"`.
- Sections: band energies in 0.5 s blocks, z-scored per band, Foote checkerboard novelty (±8 s, Gaussian taper), peaks a standard deviation over the mean and ≥ 4 s apart, boundaries snapped to the nearest beat within half a beat; a section whose mean features match an earlier one (cosine ≥ 0.9) gets its letter.

### Benchmark numbers

**This PR's synthetic grids** (scripts in the session scratchpad, not committed), built from the real corpus: real sfx hits (kick / snare / hat kits) on a known grid, 30 s, 70–170 BPM, a quarter in 3/4, over no bed, a real voice bed at −3 dB or a real music bed at −9 dB; F at ±70 ms, Acc1 ±4 %, Acc2 also allows ×2, ×½, ×3, ×⅓.

| bed | n | beat F | Acc1 | Acc2 | downbeat F | meter right |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | 30 | 0.905 | 0.733 | 1.000 | 0.903 | 0.967 |
| voice | 30 | 0.668 | 0.500 | 0.867 | 0.620 | 0.767 |
| music | 30 | 0.739 | 0.467 | 0.800 | 0.675 | 0.833 |
| all | 90 | 0.771 | 0.567 | 0.889 | 0.732 | 0.856 |

Sections, 40 cases of 3–5 real music excerpts (12–30 s each) joined end to end: boundary F 0.741 at ±3 s, 0.648 at ±0.5 s, 1.32 boundaries found per true one (some of the extra ones are real changes inside an excerpt). Speed: 3.3 ms of compute per second of audio for beats, 3.4 ms/s for sections.

On the beat benchmark's own 200-file synthetic set (read only; swing, tempo steps and drift, rhythmic beds): beat F 0.692, downbeat F 0.387; Acc1 0.484 / Acc2 0.694 on its 124 constant-tempo files.

**The separate beat benchmark** (its REPORT.md was not written; these numbers came from its run, scripts and outputs in the session's `beat-bench/`). R1 = 22 agent-synthesized scores with script grids, 15 of them at 96 BPM, not produced music:

| tracker | R1 beat F | R1 Acc1 | R1 downbeat F | synthetic F |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TS DP tracker (this `signal` rung) | 0.986 | 1.0 | 0.959 | 0.693 |
| Beat This! small0 (`beat-this` rung) | 0.995 | | 0.998 | |
| Chrome analyzer behind `hyperframes beats` | 0.437 | 0.18 | | |

It confirmed the designed order for beats and downbeats (`api` → `apple-mu` → `beat-this` small0 → `signal`). It left out madmom (its models are CC BY-NC-SA, non-commercial) and librosa (no advantage).

## Overlap with `hyperframes beats`

`hyperframes beats` is unchanged by this PR. It still runs the headless-Chrome analyzer, which scored F 0.437 and Acc1 0.18 on R1. Its tempo averages two unfolded estimates (`Math.round((onsetBpm + detectiveBpm) / 2)` in `analyzeMusicFromBuffer`, `packages/core/src/beats/beatDetection.ts`), and it phases the grid from noisy energy peaks. Next step: have `beats` write `rhythm()`'s beats (or the ladder's) to the Studio beat file.

## Tests

- core `audioRhythm.test.ts`: a steady 120 BPM grid (beats, tempo, 4/4 bars), a tempo change partway through, no beat in silence or noise or a 3 s clip, sections A B A split on beats, the snapper.
- core `audioAnalysis.test.ts`: falls through an unavailable provider and one whose check throws, with one warning carrying every reason.
- cli `providers/api.test.ts` against a local `node:http` stand-in: method, Bearer header, the multipart `request` JSON and WAV part; per-beat snapping with an invented off-grid beat kept in `unsnapped`; downbeats; bpm from api beats; sections and describe asked on their own; a 503 and a malformed answer fall through to `signal` with warnings; the key never appears in a result.
- cli `providers/localProviders.test.ts`: `beat-this` availability (unset, missing file, missing weights, package missing) with a stand-in Python script, beats + downbeats + meter from one run, a crashing run falling through; `apple-mu` reasons; `apple-sound` unavailable off macOS and a real classification on macOS.
- cli `analyze.test.ts`: bpm follows the beats' provider and is in file seconds; `--quality fast` keeps a service off.

Mutations that fail without the fix:

- Make the api keep its own beat times (`return { times: rounded(times), snap: … }` in `snappedBeats`): `posts the audio and the capabilities, and snaps each answered beat onto the signal's own` fails, `expected [0.271, 0.772, …] to deeply equal [0.241, 0.742, …]`.
- Turn off the local tempo (`cumulativeScore(local, () => period)`): `follows a tempo that changes partway through` fails, recall 0.74 < 0.85.

Runs here: core `src/audio*` 398 passed; cli `src/audio` + `src/commands` 1683 passed, 33 skipped; typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow audit (no new findings) clean. Full suites: core has 1 failure and cli has 5, all in files this PR does not touch. They also fail when run alone on this machine: core `fonts/deterministicFonts-googleSubsets` (5 s timeout), cli `whisper/sherpa`, `whisper/manager.install` and `server/fileWatcher.atomic`.

## Not exercised

- A real HeyGen backend: it does not exist yet. The contract was exercised only against the stand-in.
- `apple-mu` analysis: there is no macOS 27 here.
- Beat This! in CI: the tests use a stand-in Python. A real run here used a uv env with torch 2.5.1 and the `small0` weights.
- `apple-sound` on CI runners without Xcode CLT. It is skipped off macOS, and it compiles its helper into `~/.cache/hyperframes/audio-helpers` on first use (about 3 s).
- A cross-platform local audio tagger for `describe` off macOS. None was added.
- Uploads of very long files to the api: there is no size cap or chunking, and the full analyzed span is sent as 16-bit WAV.
- Follow-up, not in this PR: fusing beats into onsets (each hit's beat index, signed offset, on-beat flag, subdivision, downbeat).

This was meant to stack on #5602, but #5602 merged and its branch was deleted before this opened, so this PR targets `main`.

title: fix(runtime): prepare trimmed video frames before preview cuts
body:
## What

Prepare incoming trimmed video frames while they are still hidden, so continuous preview playback can show the in-point immediately at a cut.

## Why

An incoming clip currently becomes visible before its activation seek has decoded a frame. This causes the cut flash reported in #5631. Preloading bytes alone does not put the video at its trimmed in-point.

## Related work

Fixes #5631. No overlapping open PR found when starting this fix.

## How

- During playback, the runtime's indexed media pass also visits videos starting within 1.5 wall seconds. The query remains bounded by start time; paused seeks and audio visitation retain their existing behavior.
- An inactive paused video with metadata seeks to its activation source position, respecting clipped origin, rate integration, loops and source-duration clamps. Preparation neither plays the video nor registers a visible-frame seek barrier. It skips outstanding seeks, already prepared positions, export capture and injected-frame videos.
- Existing fetch ownership and drift correction remain in place. Preparation is best effort: a source that cannot load/decode within the lead time can still stall; jumps without lead time use the existing active seek path.

## Test plan

- [x] 2,056 runtime tests pass (76 suites/1,707 tests, then six initially uncollected GSAP suites/349 tests after linking an existing compatible GSAP dependency; no dependency install).
- [x] New direct sync and real init/index regressions cover entering the lookahead after playback starts, delayed metadata, no duplicate activation seek, clipped origins, loops, source clamps, rate scaling, paused/audio/export/injected-frame isolation.
- [x] Removing the pre-seek fails the direct regression; removing the index lookahead fails the real init regression.
- [x] Core build, core and runtime TypeScript checks, preview-guard lint, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt and fallow changed-file audit pass. Independent code review found no blocker and independently ran 21 focused cases.
- [x] Actual built player + runtime in Chrome 152: same 12 trimmed clips from one H.264 source, 11 cuts, 55 ms source-response latency. Before: all incoming clips first visible at readyState 1/seeking, 18–241 ms until a decoded current frame. After: all 11 first visible at readyState 4/not seeking, 0 ms measured wait. This browser shows a stale source-start frame during the before gap, rather than black. Side-by-side recording and raw per-frame traces retained; recording shared for review.
- [x] Comments explain the cut/seek invariant and hidden barrier constraint.

The monorepo pre-commit typecheck proceeds past core but cannot complete Studio with the borrowed dependency environment (missing dockview-react/html2canvas/@mcp-b/global and older Tailwind). That local hook alone was excluded after recording the failures; hosted clean-environment Typecheck remains a mandatory merge gate. No dependency manifests or lockfiles changed.

No real-user footage, native Desktop launch, Safari/mobile run, or production release is claimed. Hosted required checks and exact-head approval must pass before normal queue merge.

title: feat(cli): beats tracks the music with the TypeScript beat tracker, without Chrome
body:
Stacked on #5632 (`feat/audio-analysis-providers`), which added the TypeScript beat tracker in `packages/core/src/audioRhythm.ts`. Review that one first.

## What changed

`hyperframes beats` and Studio's beat detection now run the same code, `analyzeMusicFromSignal` in `@hyperframes/core/beats`:

1. Band energies.
2. `rhythmOf` from `audioRhythm.ts`.
3. Each beat's local RMS against the loudest beat, used as its `strength`.

- **CLI:** decodes with the same ffmpeg path `hyperframes audio` uses (`decodeAudio`). **`beats` no longer touches Chrome at all.** `headlessAnalyzer.ts`, the prebuilt `beat-analyzer.global.js` bundle and its build step are deleted. The only external dependency left is ffmpeg/ffprobe; if either is missing, the error points at `hyperframes doctor`.
- **Studio:** still decodes with `AudioContext.decodeAudioData` in the browser. `analyzeMusicFromBuffer` now passes every channel, not just channel 0, so a beat that sounds only on the right is still found and given a strength. The tracker depends only on core's `fft.ts` and Float32 math. The `pause` hook (`whenTimelineIdle`) still runs before each of the three long stages.
- **Confidence floor:** below a tracker confidence of 0.2, no beats are reported: `beatTimes: []`, `bpm: null`, `bpmConfidence: "uncertain"`.
  - Ambient or rubato music gets no invented grid.
  - The CLI's existing "0 beats → nothing written, exit 1" still applies.
  - Studio already ignores a missing or empty file.
- **`bpmConfidence`** is `"high"` at tracker confidence ≥ 0.35, `"low"` between 0.2 and 0.35, and `"uncertain"` when there are no beats. The type is unchanged.
- **`tempoOf`** (second commit) averages the intervals within 10% of the median instead of taking the median. The tracker places beats on 10 ms frames, so a 96 BPM track used to read 95.2. It now reads 96. This also changes `hyperframes audio`'s `bpm`.
- **Deleted:**
  - The bpm-detective/energy-peak merge.
  - `detectBeats`, `detectBeatsFromUrl` and `loadBpmDetective`.
  - The per-beat silence gate. It dropped every other beat on sparse tracks, which turned 96 BPM into 48.
  - `bpm-detective`, from core's and studio's `package.json`, studio's `tsup` externals, the vite `optimizeDeps` and `bun.lock`.

The `beats/<audio>.json` format is unchanged (`version`, `audio`, `beats: [{time, strength}]`), and a test now pins it byte for byte.

## Why: the old analyzer's failure modes, reproduced

`analyzeMusicFromBuffer` had three problems:

- **Averaged tempo.** It folded bpm-detective's tempo and an energy-peak tempo into one octave to compare them, then averaged the *unfolded* values. On dc8d01: (52.3 + 96) / 2 = 74.
- **Rigid phase.** It phased a rigid grid from noisy energy peaks, so even the right tempo could land on the off-beats.
- **Raw-peak fallback.** When the two tempos disagreed, it returned raw energy peaks with no grid. That happened on 39 of 75 real tracks.

The new regression test reproduces both failures on a synthetic 96 BPM track (soft clicks on every beat under loud stabs). Run against the old analyzer with bpm-detective mocked to 96, as Chrome gives it:

| stabs every | old analyzer | new |
|---|---|---|
| 2 beats | **74 BPM** ("low"), recall 0.12: the dc8d01 averaging | 96 BPM, recall > 0.95 |
| 2.2 beats | 96 BPM ("high"), **recall 0.00**: right tempo, every beat on the off-beat | 96 BPM, recall > 0.95 |

## Measured before/after

I ran both analyzers myself on the benchmark's 75 real tracks and scored them with its R1 evaluation (`eval_real.py`):

- **Before:** the base branch's `analyzeBeatsHeadless` in headless Chrome.
- **After:** this branch's `analyzeMusicFromSignal` on ffmpeg-decoded audio.

On the 22 tracks with exact script grids (15 at 96 BPM), audible spans, ±70 ms:

| | F | CMLt | AMLt | tempo right (Acc1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before (headless Chrome) | 0.437 | 0.205 | 0.319 | 18% |
| **after** | **0.887** | **0.872** | **0.872** | **91%** |
| Beat This small0 (reference) | 0.995 | 0.983 | 0.983 | 100% |

- dc8d01 goes from 74 BPM to 96 BPM ("high").
- Of the two tracks still counted wrong, both are refused (no beats) by the confidence floor; neither gets a wrong grid. At their confidence (0.13) the tracker half-times both to 48 BPM, so without the floor they would get a half-tempo grid, scored F 0.58.

Across all 75 tracks, compared against Beat This (F ≥ 0.8 counts as agree, F < 0.6 as disagree):

| | tracks given a grid | agree | disagree |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 74 | 8 | 53 |
| after | 48 | 42 | 3 |
| after, with no floor (tracker's own 0.05) | 71 | 42 | 26 |

The 0.2 floor removes 23 wrong grids and no grid that agrees with Beat This. Analysis takes about 5 ms per second of audio in bun, before decode.

**The separate benchmark's figures are higher than mine.** It reported F 0.986 and 100% tempo for "the TS tracker". That figure comes from the prototype `tsbeat.ts` on 22.05 kHz mono. The tracker as merged in #5632, run on native-rate stereo as both callers decode it, gives F 0.939 with no floor (0.887 with it). On 22.05 kHz mono it gives 0.988. The difference is two borderline tracks at confidence ≈ 0.1 that flip between 48 and 96 BPM depending on the decode, so it is noise at the tracker's edge rather than a decode bug.

## Callers checked

- `packages/cli/src/commands/beats.ts`: the only CLI caller. `--json` output (`ok`, `file`, `count`, `bpm`) is unchanged.
- `packages/cli/src/beats/headlessAnalyzer.ts` and `packages/cli/scripts/build-beat-analyzer.mjs`: deleted, along with the `build:beat-analyzer` script.
- `packages/studio/src/hooks/useMusicBeatAnalysis.ts`: calls `analyzeMusicFromUrl` with `pause`. It reads `beatTimes`, `beatStrengths` and the rest of `MusicBeatAnalysis`; the shape is unchanged.
- `packages/studio/src/utils/beatEditActions.ts`: reads `strengthAtTime`, which still uses `channelData`, `sampleRate` and `peak`. `channelData` is now the per-sample level across channels rather than channel 0.
- `TimelineRuler.tsx`, `timelineLaneProps.ts`, `playerStore.ts`: import only the `MusicBeatAnalysis` type.
- Nothing reads `bpmConfidence` except the CLI's printout and test fixtures.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/beats/beatDetection.test.ts`:
  - The 96 BPM regression (stabs every 2 and every 2.2 beats).
  - Tempo and phase on 90, 120 and 140 BPM grids at offsets.
  - Silence, hiss and an ambient pad give no beats and no tempo.
  - The three pauses.
  - A right-channel-only beat is found and has strength.
- `packages/core/src/beats/beatFile.test.ts`: `serializeBeats` output is pinned byte for byte, and round-trips through `parseBeats`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/beats.test.ts`: the built command, end to end through ffmpeg, writes `beats/assets/song.wav.json` with exactly `version`, `audio`, `beats[{time, strength}]` on the grid. A silent track exits 1 and writes nothing.
- `packages/core/src/audioRhythm.test.ts`: frame-quantized 96 BPM beats read as 96.
- Studio's `BeatStrip` and `Timeline.readOnly` tests, which use `MusicBeatAnalysis` fixtures, pass.

Each test fails without its fix:

| change made | result |
|---|---|
| new tests run against the old analyzer | 7 of 8 fail; only the pause test passes |
| floor lowered to the tracker's 0.05 | the ambient-pad case fails |
| strength taken from channel 0 | the right-channel case fails |
| median interval in `tempoOf` | the 96 BPM tempo test fails |

## Not exercised

- **No Studio walk in a browser.** As a substitute, I bundled `beatDetection.ts` with esbuild for the browser and ran `analyzeMusicFromBuffer` on `AudioContext.decodeAudioData` output in headless Chrome, on 5 real tracks at 48 kHz. Every beat the page found was within 20 ms of a CLI beat on 4 of 5 tracks (on one of those, the page found 43 of the CLI's 46). On the fifth, 130 of 142 matched, because of resampling. A 2–3 minute track takes 200–450 ms in the page. I did not open Studio, drop a track, or watch the beat lane.
- **Studio's fallback-track path** (analysis without a saved beat file) is untested here, beyond the shared function.
- **Downbeats:** `MusicBeatAnalysis` still has no field for them, even though the tracker produces them.


## Before

Actual Chrome execution of the parent analyzer (`5b8a8d091`), rendered in a browser harness. Synthetic 96 BPM clicks with loud chord stabs every 2.2 beats: 134 BPM reported, 37 beats, 25.6% recall within ±70 ms of interior reference clicks. No mocked bpm-detective. This is **not a Studio UI screenshot or a real-music benchmark**.

![Parent browser analyzer output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/3b360525845f4e3d42aac887a6d5045fd7700355/.github/pr-evidence/5634/before.png)

## After

Same deterministic audio and browser harness using the child analyzer (`65b986bce`, unchanged by the subsequent CI-only commit): 96 BPM, 47 beats, 100% recall. The screenshots display seconds 2–12; the measurements cover 30 seconds. No real backend or paid provider calls.

![Child browser analyzer output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/3b360525845f4e3d42aac887a6d5045fd7700355/.github/pr-evidence/5634/after.png)

[Reproduction script and raw measurements](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/tree/3b360525845f4e3d42aac887a6d5045fd7700355/.github/pr-evidence/5634). This exercises the shared browser analyzer; it does not verify Studio’s fallback-track lifecycle.

The CI deletion guard now explicitly lists only the removed Chrome analyzer and its build script, with replacement reasons. Its targeted test fails before the entries and passes afterward; unrelated deletions remain blocked.

title: fix(cli): retire old snapshot run folders
body:
Repeated CLI snapshots left old UUID folders, contact sheets and descriptions under `.hyperframes/artifacts/snapshots`. Completed snapshot/check runs now reclaim whole old folders while keeping the newest 10, current/latest and retained-render evidence, active captures, and a 24-hour grace period. Explicit `--output` destinations remain user-owned, including nested reuse of a managed folder.

Owner metadata is opened with no-follow/nonblocking flags, then the descriptor and current pathname are checked for regular-file, device/inode and single-link identity before reading. Lease creation records its exclusive descriptor identity; completion also checks that trusted identity before marking the opened descriptor released. Swapping the pathname cannot remove a replacement owner, and hard-linked markers are refused. Races, malformed markers and failed writes keep the run. No CodeQL suppression or dismissal is used.

Cleanup retires recorded image references durably before deleting files, revalidates directory identity and activity, refuses symlink traversal, and retries failed removals on a later capture. Capture leases last through contact-sheet/description writes and overlapping checks. Project history is preserved.

The CLI skill now asks agents to inspect full-resolution frames and decoded exports at matching times, zoom into WebGL geometry, and clean only owned disposable output. The reported Crescendo Mac graphics corruption is still being investigated; this PR does not claim to fix it.

Validation: 37 current focused tests pass under CI-matching Vitest 4.1.11 (36 history/retention plus the concurrent-check helper); the 74 CLI snapshot tests also executed successfully in hosted CI on the security follow-up. This includes disk-full persistence failure/retry, derived-file removal, active/crashed captures, explicit/nested outputs, symlink/hardlink boundaries and marker swaps before open and during completion. Guard-removal mutation fails the swap regressions; an independent reviewer also passed all 37 current focused tests, changed-file lint and formatting. The original-head studio-server typecheck, changed-file lint/format, skill lint/mirror/manifest, package subpaths and the Fallow audit pass (no new findings). Independent code review found no normal capture/release blocker. A deliberate unlink followed by inode reuse remains a local filesystem identity limitation; failed releases conservatively preserve their lease until process exit.

Local limits: reused existing dependencies and cached Vitest 4.1.11, using exact package-source aliases because borrowed exports predate the branch. Filesystem race tests explicitly use the Node environment so happy-dom does not bypass their builtin mocks. Its local studio-server typecheck cannot resolve current parser/core exports; fresh hosted typecheck is required (the previous security head passed hosted Typecheck). Two broader CLI check suites cannot collect because workspace exports/Ajv are missing, and full CLI/monorepo typecheck has missing cloud/WebGPU/Ajv dependencies. Only that local pre-commit typecheck hook was excluded; fresh hosted tests/typecheck remain required. No dependency or lockfile change.

title: fix(lint): warn on unbounded cosine powers in shaders
body:
## What

Warn when an authored GLSL shader passes `1 - dot(...)` or `1 - max(dot(...), 0)` to `pow`. Project lint now checks directly linked local authored JavaScript shader files and reports their file/line. Add the safe cosine clamp and GPU verification guidance to the CLI and Three.js skills.

## Why

A real composition produced black tears on Apple M4 Pro / ANGLE Metal because its orb shader used `pow(1.0-max(dot(vN,vV),0.0),1.6)`. Replacing the lower-only bound with `clamp(dot(vN,vV),0.0,1.0)` eliminated invalid color values at all ten sampled times; original-source controls reproduced the failure at 25, 34 and 110 seconds. The software renderer did not reproduce it. GLSL leaves negative-base `pow` undefined even with integer exponents.

## Related work

Follow-up to the GPU investigation requested by Miguel. #5635 adds snapshot retention and full-resolution visual inspection guidance; this PR adds source-level prevention. No Three.js runtime or material rewrite.

## How

`shader_unbounded_cosine_pow` is a warning for a narrow, direct expression pattern. Acorn isolates complete static shader strings; native GLSL script blocks are also checked. Linked `.js` / `.mjs` / `.cjs` files are deduplicated, contained within the project root, and exclude minified/vendor files. Browser lint remains Node-free. Escaped or normalized string contents omit coordinates when they cannot be mapped exactly.

title: feat(cli): the api provider speaks the HeyGen audio analysis contract
body:
## What

The `api` rung of `hyperframes audio` (added in #5632) now speaks the contract of HeyGen's audio analysis route:

- **Auth:** the key goes in `x-api-key` instead of `Authorization: Bearer`.
- **Idempotency:** each request carries a new `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID). The CLI does not retry, so one request is one key.
- **Upload:** the audio is uploaded as 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV. The channels are averaged, then resampled with a Hann-windowed sinc (16 zero crossings, cutoff at 0.9 of the lower Nyquist), so nothing above 8 kHz folds back in.
- **Envelope:** the answer is read as `body.data ?? body`, so `{ "data": … }` and a bare answer both work.
- `AudioApiResponse` gains `time_resolution_seconds`. Nothing reads it.

## Why

- HeyGen's API takes a HeyGen key only as `x-api-key`.
- The route requires `Idempotency-Key`, like `/v3/audio/music` and `/v3/audio/transcriptions`. A same-key retry replays the answer and is not charged again; the same key with a different body gets 409.
- The route answers in EF's standard `data` envelope.
- The model hears one channel at 16 kHz anyway. The route caps uploads at 32 MB and 600 s, so a 3-minute 44.1 kHz stereo song was at the limit and a 4-minute one was refused. At 16 kHz mono, ten minutes is 19.2 MB.

## Related work

Refs #5632. The route is heygen-com/experiment-framework#57783. Desktop's gateway, which carries the call for a chat run, is heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#4049; it now takes the run token in `x-api-key` only.

## How

- Every time is still in seconds from the start of the audio, so resampling does not change them.
- The snap step still measures beats on the signal as decoded, not on the upload.
- Resampling 600 s of 44.1 kHz audio takes about 1.8 s.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests updated: `bunx vitest run src/audio` in `packages/cli` passes 47/47.
  - The test server answers in the `data` envelope, plus one test with a bare answer.
  - Requests are checked for `x-api-key` with no `Authorization`, a UUID `Idempotency-Key` that differs per request, and a 16 kHz mono WAV.
  - A stereo 44.1 kHz test signal checks the upload. A 2 kHz tone in opposite phase between the channels must cancel. A 9 kHz tone must not alias to 7 kHz. A 440 Hz tone must survive at its level.
- [x] Mutations, each reverted on its own, fail at least one test:
  - reading the raw body;
  - keeping only the first channel;
  - skipping the resample;
  - keeping the input rate;
  - a cutoff at the input Nyquist (aliasing);
  - no idempotency key;
  - a constant key;
  - Bearer auth;
  - snapping on the uploaded signal.
- [x] Manual, end to end, all local:
  - Setup: this CLI → Desktop's real gateway (`openHeygenGateway`) → EF's real `/v3/audio/analysis` view in a local Flask app, with the model, credits and auth faked.
  - Run: `hyperframes audio click120.wav --only beats,downbeats,bpm,sections,describe --quality best --json` on a 12 s, 44.1 kHz stereo file.
  - All five capabilities came from `api`, with no warnings.
  - Three requests reached EF, each with the key in `x-api-key`, its own `Idempotency-Key`, and a 16 kHz mono WAV of 384,044 bytes. The old upload was 2,116,844 bytes.
  - Reverting each of the four changes broke the run:
    - without the envelope read, every `api` capability fell through;
    - without the resample, the route answered 400;
    - without the key, the route answered 400;
    - with Bearer, the gateway answered 401.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.
- [x] Checks: oxlint, oxfmt, `fallow audit --base origin/main` (no issues), `tsc` for cli, core, studio and scripts, and commitlint.

title: feat(core): signal rhythm is rate-independent, refuses grids in the tracker, follows chords
body:
## What

The `signal` rung is what most users get: no Python, no macOS 27, no API. This PR makes it better and measures every change against a fixed benchmark. Everything is in `packages/core/src`; no CLI or provider code changes. This covers the floor recalibration and the sections work; coarse section role labels are not in this PR (see rejected).

1. **Same answer at any decode rate** (`fix`). The tracker resamples every channel to 22.05 kHz (new `audioResample.ts`, a windowed-sinc resampler, pure TS) and averages the channels' band power. The CLI decodes at the file's native rate, Studio at the `AudioContext` rate; both now get the same beats. Mono and the same sound on two channels give identical results.
2. **One confidence floor, in the tracker** (`fix`). The floor that refuses a grid ("no steady beat") moves out of `analyzeMusicFromSignal` into `rhythm()`. `hyperframes beats`, `hyperframes audio` and `grep_audio` now share it. It is recalibrated from 0.2 (wrapper) and 0.05 (tracker) to **0.15**, just above every synthetic negative.
3. **Downbeats follow chord changes** (`feat`). The tracker now also computes a 10 fps chroma (from `fft.ts`, 4096-point). The bar phase is chosen from three cues: the low-end hit, the chord change across one beat, and the chord change across two beats. Before, it used the low end only.
4. **Sections hear harmony** (`feat`). Foote novelty runs over timbre (band energies) and chroma, weighted equally.
5. **Tuned on GTZAN dev only:** tempo prior width 1 → 0.8 octave; local tempo held within ±10% of the global tempo (was −30%/+40%); beats placed 15 ms after the onset-curve peak. The tracker was 16 ms early against annotations, median over 18.7k matched beats.

## Benchmark

- **GTZAN**, the primary set: 998 clips. One clip has no annotation and one is undecodable.
  - Split by genre: clips `00000–00049` of each genre are **dev** (tuning only), `00050–00099` are **test**.
  - Beat and downbeat annotations from `CPJKU/beat_this_annotations`.
- **R1**: 22 agent-synthesized tracks with exact script grids, scored in audible spans (#5634's table).
- **S**: 200 synthetic drum grids over real beds, with swing, tempo steps and drift.
- **Consensus**: 21 real tracks where madmom and Beat This final0 agree. Beat This final0 serves as pseudo-truth.
- **Negatives**: 38 synthetic clips with no steady beat, plus a held-out 28 from another seed.
  - Kinds: speech, scattered effects, pads, swelling noise, and ambient beds from the corpus.

Metrics come from mir_eval 0.8.2: F at ±70 ms, CMLt, AMLt, downbeat F; mir_eval trims the first 5 s. Tempo accuracy uses ±4%: Acc1 is the right tempo, Acc2 also accepts ×2, ×½, ×3 and ×⅓. **Beat This small0 is the reference ceiling** (the `beat-this` rung).

### What users get: beats after the floor (`hyperframes beats`, Studio, and now `audio`)

"before" is `main` at 1544b519a: `beats` with the wrapper's 0.2 floor. A refused clip scores 0.

| set | | F | CMLt | AMLt | Acc1 | Acc2 | downbeat F | no grid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GTZAN dev | before | 0.528 | 0.454 | 0.553 | 0.500 | 0.600 | 0.312 | 36.6% |
| | after | **0.593** | 0.511 | 0.621 | 0.570 | 0.682 | **0.394** | 28.2% |
| | Beat This small0 | 0.845 | 0.731 | 0.855 | 0.768 | 0.918 | 0.702 | 0% |
| GTZAN test | before | 0.597 | 0.512 | 0.626 | 0.566 | 0.681 | 0.342 | 28.3% |
| | after | **0.654** | 0.554 | 0.696 | 0.622 | 0.773 | **0.428** | 19.9% |
| | Beat This small0 | 0.925 | 0.847 | 0.929 | 0.853 | 0.952 | 0.843 | 0% |
| R1 (22) | before | 0.887 | 0.872 | 0.872 | 0.909 | 0.909 | 0.934 | 2 of 22 |
| | after | **0.900** | 0.891 | 0.891 | 0.909 | 0.909 | 0.908 | 2 of 22 |
| | Beat This small0 | 0.995 | 0.983 | 0.983 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.998 | 0 |
| S (200) | before | 0.531 | 0.412 | 0.539 | 0.435 | 0.589 | 0.381 | 24% |
| | after | 0.593 | 0.473 | 0.587 | 0.532 | 0.629 | 0.316 | 17.5% |
| | Beat This small0 | 0.584 | 0.392 | 0.515 | 0.395 | 0.516 | 0.371 | 3% |
| consensus (21) | before | 0.892 | 0.811 | 0.899 | 0.857 | 0.952 | | 1 of 21 |
| | after | 0.910 | 0.867 | 0.912 | 0.905 | 0.952 | | 1 of 21 |

R1 does not regress: 0.887 → 0.900. The two refused R1 tracks (297b03, 3333be) are the same two #5634 refused; refusing them is still right, because without the floor their tempo is halved.

The "before" downbeat column comes from the tracker, which had no 0.2 floor, so on that column "before" is scored on more grids than "after".

### Tracker quality without the floor

This isolates the tracker from the refusal decision. "before" is the tracker on `main` with its own 0.05 floor, which is what `hyperframes audio` used to return. "after" uses floor 0.

| set | | F | CMLt | AMLt | Acc1 | Acc2 | downbeat F |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GTZAN dev | before | 0.700 | 0.580 | 0.743 | 0.664 | 0.836 | 0.312 |
| | 22.05 kHz only (commit 1) | 0.735 | 0.600 | 0.779 | 0.686 | 0.868 | 0.307 |
| | after | **0.743** | 0.612 | 0.792 | 0.708 | 0.886 | **0.483** |
| GTZAN test | before | 0.739 | 0.614 | 0.775 | 0.697 | 0.869 | 0.342 |
| | 22.05 kHz only (commit 1) | 0.770 | 0.634 | 0.813 | 0.709 | 0.902 | 0.343 |
| | after | **0.776** | 0.638 | 0.825 | 0.725 | **0.924** | **0.504** |
| | librosa 0.11 `beat_track` (DSP reference) | 0.776 | 0.633 | 0.822 | 0.717 | 0.890 | |
| R1 | before → after | 0.939 → **0.989** | 0.872 → 0.980 | 0.951 → 0.980 | 0.909 → 1.000 | 1.000 → 1.000 | 0.934 → **0.999** |
| S | before → after | 0.680 → 0.696 | 0.507 → 0.522 | 0.693 → 0.689 | 0.484 → 0.565 | 0.694 → 0.718 | 0.381 → **0.364** |
| consensus | before → after | 0.892 → 0.947 | 0.811 → 0.912 | 0.899 → 0.958 | 0.857 → 0.952 | 0.952 → 1.000 | |

Per GTZAN genre, F before → after (test and dev together; Beat This in brackets):

| | | | |
|---|---|---|---|
| blues 0.718 → 0.729 (0.811) | classical 0.318 → 0.534 (0.650) | country 0.835 → 0.834 (0.919) | disco 0.918 → 0.929 (0.969) |
| hiphop 0.773 → 0.798 (0.976) | jazz 0.531 → 0.606 (0.856) | metal 0.718 → 0.753 (0.887) | pop 0.748 → 0.768 (0.946) |
| reggae 0.840 → 0.846 (0.906) | rock 0.790 → 0.798 (0.929) | | |

Downbeat F on GTZAN, all clips: 0.327 → 0.494. The biggest gains are disco 0.24 → 0.67, reggae 0.27 → 0.61 and rock 0.40 → 0.62.

### Refusing a grid

| | negatives given a grid (38 + held-out 28) | GTZAN dev clips refused | real corpus (75 tracks) |
|---|---|---|---|
| before, `beats` (0.2) | 0/38, 0/28 | 36.6% | 48 grids: 42 agree with Beat This, 3 disagree |
| before, `audio` (0.05) | 22/38, 15/28 | 9.8% | 71 grids: 42 agree, 26 disagree |
| after, both (0.15) | **0/38, 0/28** | 28.2% | 52 grids: 43 agree, 7 disagree |
| Beat This small0 (no floor) | 22/38 | 0% | |

The highest-scoring negative reaches 0.122, so 0.15 leaves a margin. Lowering the floor further mostly adds wrong grids; at 0.15 the dev set still keeps 42 grids with F < 0.5. Because `audio` used to give a grid at 0.05, it now refuses more often. That is the intended effect of fix 2.

### Why the floor lowers GTZAN beat F from 0.776 to 0.654

**The tracker itself is unchanged by the floor.** The drop is entirely refused clips, which score 0.

| | clips | refused at 0.15 | of the refused: Beat This F ≥ 0.8 | of the refused: our unfloored F ≥ 0.8 / F < 0.5 | refused clips by genre |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 500 | 141 (28%) | 52 (Beat This mean F 0.659) | 30 / 61 (mean F 0.533) | classical 46, jazz 27, metal 26, blues 13, rock 10 |
| test | 498 | 99 (20%) | 62 (Beat This mean F 0.819) | 31 / 37 (mean F 0.614) | classical 42, jazz 18, metal 10, rock 9, blues 6 |

- **On the test half,** the refused 20% averages F 0.614 when not refused. That accounts for the drop: 0.20 × 0.614 ≈ 0.12. On the clips that keep a grid, F is 0.816.
- **Beat This would have tracked 62 of the 99 refused test clips well.** On those clips the signal tracker gets only 31 right, and gets 37 wrong (F < 0.5).
- **The cost of refusing.** A grid is refused when our confidence cannot separate a real beat from the negatives' false ones. Mostly those are rubato classical and jazz, and dense metal. Of the clips refused, the signal tracker itself was right on about a third.
- **Trading coverage back in:** a floor of 0.10 keeps 81% of dev (mean F 0.652), but gives a grid to 3 of 38 negatives. Floor 0 keeps everything (F 0.743), but gives a grid to all 38.

### Sections: boundary F at ±3 s (F3) and ±0.5 s (F0.5), before → after

| set | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| GTZAN dev joins: 60 cases, 3–5 excerpts of one genre (10–22 s each) end to end | F3 0.775, F0.5 0.629 (1.14 found per true) | **F3 0.819, F0.5 0.663** (1.18) |
| GTZAN test joins: 60 cases, built the same way from test clips | F3 0.847, F0.5 0.728 (1.08) | **F3 0.858, F0.5 0.780** (1.14) |
| #5632's corpus joins: 40 cases | F3 0.741, F0.5 0.648 (1.32) | F3 0.742, F0.5 0.692 (1.27) |

Beat This has no sections rung, so this table has no reference column. These are joins of different recordings, which is an easier task than finding sections within one song.

### Speed (bun, one process, analysis only)

| decode | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 22.05 kHz mono (100 GTZAN clips) | 1.71 ms per second of audio | 2.36 ms/s (1.38×) |
| native rate, 44.1/48 kHz (20 real tracks) | 5.41 ms/s | 6.03 ms/s (1.11×) |
| sections, extra | 1.9 ms/s | 2.6 ms/s |

## Targets, honestly

- **Beat F ≥ 95% of Beat This: not reached, and not realistic for this design.**
  - Unfloored, the tracker reaches 0.776 on GTZAN test, 84% of Beat This's 0.925. After the floor, users get 0.654 (71%).
  - librosa's tracker uses the same Ellis DP and gets 0.776 on the same split.
  - Even with the annotated tempo given to it, our DP reaches only F 0.80 on dev (Beat This: 0.845). Phase and drift on expressive music (jazz, classical, metal) are the limit, so further tuning will not close the gap.
- **Acc2 ≥ 95%: not reached.** It is 0.924 on test unfloored (Beat This: 0.952). The remaining errors are mostly 3:2 and "other" ratios on classical music.
- **Downbeats: clear gain on produced music.** GTZAN test 0.342 → 0.504, about 60% of Beat This's 0.843.

## Tried and rejected (GTZAN dev F unless noted; reference 0.743 at the end, 0.735 after commit 1)

| change | result | why rejected |
|---|---|---|
| 8 or 12 bands/octave instead of 5 | 0.741 / 0.738 | noise-level, and R1 dropped to 0.949 |
| difference lag of 2 frames | 0.738 (later 0.741) | no gain |
| SuperFlux max-filter across frequency | 0.712; R1 0.876 | worse |
| log compression 1e7 / 1e11 | 0.743 / 0.733 | R1 0.923 / 0.940 |
| local-mean radius 0.2 s / 0.8 s | 0.736 / 0.735 | no gain |
| low band added to the DP observation (weight 0.5 / 1) | 0.698 / 0.666 | worse |
| PLP (Grosche–Müller) blended into the observation (0.5 / 1) | 0.736 / 0.627 | worse |
| DP tightness 200 / 300 | 0.750 / 0.747 | S F 0.681 / 0.677 vs 0.696 |
| tempo prior centre 105 / 135 (with widths 0.6–1) | ≤ 0.742 | no gain over 120 |
| choosing the metrical level among {1, 2, ½, 3/2, 2/3}× by ACF harmonics, onset lift and prior | 0.750 | Acc1 0.708 → 0.654 |
| the same choice as a 12-weight model fitted on dev | dev 0.761, test 0.794 | a fitted model for +0.02; kept out |
| confidence: logistic over clarity, lift, cv, ACF | dev 0.649 vs 0.61 at the floor | fitted on 38 synthetic negatives, too fragile |
| confidence: other hand-made formulas (ACF of smoothed curve, interval CV) | ±0.01 | no gain |
| harmonic cues weighted 2× over half a bar | downbeat 0.493 vs 0.483 | drum-only grids: 0.55 vs 0.69, see below |
| cues weighted by their own decisiveness, or left unnormalized | downbeat 0.45–0.48 | no clear win |
| section boundaries snapped to downbeats instead of beats | F0.5 0.655 → 0.442 | downbeats are right only half the time |
| coarse section labels (intro, body, climax, outro) | not built | no annotations to measure them |
| meter detection beyond the 3/4 handicap | not built | 469 of 494 dev clips are in 4 |

## Known costs

- **Downbeats on drum-only material get worse.** Chord cues on a drum grid with no harmony are noise.
  - #5632's synthetic drum grids, no bed: downbeat F 0.903 → 0.686; all beds: 0.732 → 0.602.
  - S: 0.381 → 0.364.
  - I took this trade for produced music (GTZAN +0.16). Weighting the cues equally, rather than the half-bar cue 2×, cuts the no-bed loss from 0.35 to 0.22.
- **#5632's synthetic grids over a voice bed:** beat F 0.668 → 0.539. The 0.15 floor now refuses more drums-under-speech, which the old 0.05 tracker floor let through.

## "Fails without the fix" mutations (all run)

| mutation | failing test |
|---|---|
| `bandFrames` uses `signal.channels` without resampling | `gives the same beats at any sample rate and for mono or the same sound on two channels`: `expected 0.25 to be less than or equal to 0.011` |
| floor back to 0.05 | `refuses an ambient pad in the tracker itself, so every caller of the signal tracker agrees`, and `reports no beats and no tempo for audio without a steady pulse` |
| downbeats from the low-band cue only (chord cues removed) | `puts the bar where the chords change when every beat hits the same`: recall 0 < 0.9 |
| resampler without the low-pass (`scale = CUTOFF`, so it folds) | `removes what the lower rate cannot hold instead of folding it down`: RMS 0.706, expected < 0.01 |

Runs here:
- core `src/audio*` and `src/beats`: 440 passed.
- cli `src/audio`, `src/commands/beats.test.ts` and `src/commands/audio`: 47 passed.
- studio `src/hooks` and `src/utils/beat*`: 1567 passed.
- core, studio, cli and scripts typecheck: clean. oxlint and oxfmt: clean. fallow audit vs `origin/main`: no issues.
- `hyperframes audio --only beats,downbeats,bpm,sections` runs end to end from the built CLI.

## GTZAN (not committed)

- **Audio:** `https://huggingface.co/datasets/marsyas/gtzan/resolve/main/data/genres.tar.gz`.
  - This is the mirror commonly used since mirdata's own GTZAN audio source (`http://opihi.cs.uvic.ca/sound/genres.tar.gz`, in mirdata ≤ 0.3.8) went offline. Current mirdata ships only `gtzan_mini`.
  - sha256 `b28cc067ff6199bd826f5d1a6931458586d64acae7f44b2e882b7a97af057531`, md5 `4c13f740bb9d223a1d74d4a7f78ca336`.
  - The md5 differs from mirdata's `5b3d6dddb579ab49814ab86dba69e7c7`: this tarball holds `.wav` instead of `.au`, plus a `.DS_Store`.
- **Annotations:** `CPJKU/beat_this_annotations` at `fd9fcc0896cb78730bae735102c8753ef3a3badd`, folder `gtzan`, MIT.
- **License:** GTZAN is research-only. No audio or derived audio is in this PR or any repo; only annotation-derived scores appear here. The benchmark scripts and outputs stay in the session scratchpad.

## Not exercised

- **No Studio walk.** I did not open Studio, drop a track or watch the beat lane. The code is pure TS with no new dependency (`fft.ts` is still the only FFT), and Studio's tests and typecheck pass, but it has not been run in a browser.
- **Long files.** Benchmarks are 30–100 s clips. Chroma adds 12 doubles per 100 ms; it is not profiled on hour-long audio.
- **CI and other platforms.** Nothing was run on CI runners or other OSes beyond what this PR's checks run.

title: fix(studio-server): an edit aimed at a clip never lands on an audio group sharing its id
body:
## What changed

An edit aimed at one element can no longer land on a different element that happens to share its `id`.

A person put an audio group in the film's root, `<hf-audio-group id="voice" data-fx-chain="...">`, and gave the voiceover clips in a sub-composition `data-audio-group="voice"`. After a later edit in Studio, the group was gone from `index.html` with no error, so the voice chain stopped applying.

- **Cause.** `findTargetElement` (`packages/studio-server/src/helpers/sourceMutation.ts`) looks the target up by `data-hf-id` first. When that finds nothing, it falls back to `getElementById(target.id)`, then to the selector.
  - Say a clip shares the group's id (`<audio id="voice" ...>`) and the request is resolved in a file where its `data-hf-id` isn't found: the clip lives in another file, or the copy it was served from is stale.
  - Then the fallback picks the group. A delete removes it, and a move writes the clip's `data-start` onto it.
  - Every save that routes through `findTargetElement` (patch, remove, split, wrap, unwrap, duplicate, freeze frame) shared this.
- **Fix, in `findTargetElement`.** A `data-hf-id` that was already in the file is that element's identity. So when a request names a `data-hf-id`, a fallback hit pinned in the file to a different one is a different element, and it no longer counts as a match. The routes already answer "not matched" safely.
- **What still lands.** A fallback hit whose `data-hf-id` was only minted by this parse (not yet written to the file) still matches. That is the case the fallback exists for: a save carrying an id served before an outside edit changed what is minted. Its test ("hfId lookup falls through to selector...") passes unchanged.
- **How.** `parseSourceDocument` records which `data-hf-id`s the raw source carried, keyed by the document it returns. `findTargetElement` reads that, so no call site changes.

## What I measured

- New test in `sourceMutation.test.ts`: a root `<hf-audio-group id="voice" data-hf-id="hf-oova">`, then remove and patch with `{ id: "voice", hfId: "hf-6egx" }`. The file comes back unchanged and the patch reports `matched: false`.
  - fails without the fix: the group is deleted ("expected '<div data-hf-id=… data-composition-id="main"><div …class="clip"…' to be '…<hf-audio-group id="voice"…'").
- `src/helpers` vitest passes 3 runs of 3 (511 tests). Full `@hyperframes/studio-server` vitest passes (1328, 2 skipped). `tsc --noEmit` passes. oxfmt and oxlint are clean on the changed files.

title: feat(cli): render telemetry reports how busy the machine's CPU was
body:
## What

`render_complete` and `render_error` now say how busy the machine's CPU was during the render, for CLI (local and `--docker`) and Studio renders:

| Property | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `cpu_busy_avg_pct` | Busy share of all cores from render start to end, 0-100 |
| `cpu_busy_peak_pct` | Busy share of all cores in the busiest 2 s window, 0-100 |
| `cpu_cores_busy_peak` | Cores at 80 % or more in that busiest window |
| `load_avg_start` / `load_avg_end` | One-minute load average at start and end (absent on Windows, where Node always reports 0) |

## Why

Events already carry the machine's core count and the worker count we picked, but not whether those cores were actually used. Without utilization we cannot tell an under-parallelized render (cores idle) from a saturated one (cores pegged, or the machine already busy with other work before the render started), so worker sizing can't be tuned from data.

## How

- `telemetry/renderCpu.ts` snapshots `os.cpus()` times at render start and end, and samples every 2 s (one unref'd interval) for the peak window. System-wide on purpose: the render's work runs in Chrome and FFmpeg child processes, so the CLI's own `process.cpuUsage()` would miss most of it. Node built-ins only, no new dependency.
- Only numbers; nothing identifying.
- Nothing is sampled when telemetry is off (`shouldTrack()` false) or when the Studio requester opted out, so opted-out installs pay nothing.
- `stop()` is idempotent and clears the interval. The CLI calls it before emitting on success and in `handleRenderError` (which every failure and abort path goes through); Studio stops it in a `finally`, so complete, failed and cancelled renders all clear it.

Note: this measures the whole machine, so other apps running at the same time count too. Read `load_avg_start` next to it to tell "the machine was already busy" apart from "the render kept it busy".

## Test fixture

`render.test.ts` passed a fixed `/tmp/project` to `renderLocal`. A render writes the project's history (turn marker, history id, owner lock) into its project folder, so on a machine where that shared path exists the tests wrote into it. CodeQL flagged the path all the way to those writes (`js/insecure-temporary-file`). The tests now use a private `mkdtemp` folder removed after the file.

## Verification

- Unit: a fake `os.cpus()` sequence gives the expected average, peak and busy-core count; the interval is cleared on stop; nothing is sampled when telemetry is off or the requester opted out. Wiring tests cover CLI success and error, Studio complete, failed and cancelled renders, and the event mapping. Each of 11 targeted code breaks (no interval sampling, no clearInterval, no telemetry gate, no opt-out gate, Windows load average, error mapping, CLI error/complete spread, Studio `finally`, Studio opt-out argument, Studio emit spread) fails a test.
- `scripts/ci/cli-telemetry-e2e.mjs` now checks the five properties on a real render through the built CLI. Ran it on Linux: all checks pass, and the captured `render_complete` carried all five with plausible values.
- `packages/cli`: tsc clean, full vitest suite green 3 runs in a row; oxlint/oxfmt clean on changed files.

title: fix(cli): upload owned audio assets before analysis
body:
## What

Upload the normalized audio span through the public asset direct-upload flow, then send the finalized asset ID to audio analysis. Reuse one uploaded asset across the three capability requests.

## Why

The approved backend contract accepts JSON with an owned asset reference; the previous multipart WAV request is incompatible. Asset upload also preserves the backend ownership and moderation checks.

## Related work

Refs https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5641 (merged), https://github.com/heygen-com/experiment-framework/pull/57783 (backend, awaiting repository Payments CODEOWNER), and https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes-internal/pull/4049 (merged at 17c084d587b631570c9035c35b67bf811d92286e).

## How

Use the existing generated asset initialization/completion client and shared direct uploader, retaining the ZIP wrapper. Normalize to 16 kHz mono WAV, upload once per decoded signal, and reference the same asset in each JSON analysis request with separate idempotency keys. Upload calls share a deadline and reject redirects; the presigned PUT carries no API key. Analysis keeps its configured endpoint and existing fallback behavior.

## Test plan

- [x] Integrated current main 49c49504a with a signed merge; core build succeeds.
- [x] 62 focused audio/upload tests pass after integration: loopback upload metadata/checksum, WAV bytes, single upload reuse, JSON asset references, distinct analysis keys, no API key on presigned PUT, redirects, resampling and stereo preservation. Existing ZIP upload tests also pass.
- [x] CLI typecheck, changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks pass.
- [x] Documentation updated for asset-upload permissions.
- Earlier cross-repository local probe exercised the changed CLI through the real gateway and EF view, with fixture auth/storage/model/ledger boundaries. This is not live provider or paid acceptance.
- No live API calls, release, package pin, publishing, or deployment. Backend rollout and a later coordinated CLI release/pin remain separate rollout prerequisites.

Current-head Rames and Magi approvals plus CI/repository gates are required before normal merge.

body:

| Published skills | 21 | 7 |
| Descriptions listed on every turn | 10.9 KB | 2.2 KB |
| `hyperframes` entry, read on every video | 21.8 KB | 6.7 KB |
| All seven entries | 470 KB for 21 | 39 KB |
| `skills/` on disk | about 18 MB | 3.9 MB |

1. **`hyperframes`** holds:
   - the render contract;
   - how to keep a project editable in Studio;

   The 13 frame presets move to `assets/`.
2. **`media-use`** shows each need with a HeyGen route beside a free local route. HeyGen: `heygen auth login --oauth` carries a free allowance, an API key bills credits, plus video-agent, avatar, clone, lipsync, translate and clipping. Free with no account: Kokoro TTS, Parakeet/whisper, background removal, the 19 bundled SFX, MusicGen and logos. `mixing.md` and `local.md` come from Studio.
3. **`hyperframes-cli` and `hyperframes-registry`** are slimmed (24.8 → 6.9 KB and 9.9 → 4.3 KB). Their detail moved whole into references.
4. **`slideshow`, `figma` and `remotion-to-hyperframes`** are slimmed (33.5 → 4.9 KB, 18.2 → 6.2 KB and 11.0 → 4.9 KB). Each keeps what only it holds:
   - `slideshow`: present and hand-off;

   - `remotion-to-hyperframes`: the Remotion lint, the SSIM check and the API map.

   - Two scripts with no CLI equivalent move to `skills/hyperframes/scripts/`: `bake-basemap.mjs`, and `locate.mjs` (grid image location).

## Why

Strong coding agents plan, sequence and check their own work; what they lack are private facts. The same restructure for Studio (hyperframes-internal#3731) raised tool and CLI correctness from 5% to 83%. This PR brings it to terminal agents, measured on the same kind of run below.

## Related work

- Refs hyperframes-internal#3731 (Studio skills) and hyperframes-internal#4142 (the Studio skills carry the storyboard recipe).
- Refs #5599 (one storyboard format) and #5610 (desktop-app hand-off wording, kept in a shorter form).

The seven entries are exempt from oxfmt, whose table padding added about 1.5 KB per entry on every read.

title: fix(cli): skip runtime by-products when fingerprinting a skill bundle
body:
## What

`hashSkillBundle` (`packages/cli/src/utils/skillsManifest.ts`) now skips files a skill directory picks up from being used rather than authored: `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `.mypy_cache/`, `.ruff_cache/`, `node_modules/` directories, and `.DS_Store`, `Thumbs.db`, `*.pyc`, `*.pyo`, `*.swp`, `*.swo`, `*~` files. Previously only `.DS_Store` was skipped.

## Why

The same hash builds the published `skills-manifest.json` from `skills/` and compares an installed skill against it. Every file in the directory went into it, so:

- Running a skill's Python (e.g. `media-use/audio/scripts/lib/gemini-auth_test.py`, which imports `gemini-auth.py` and leaves `__pycache__/gemini-auth.cpython-*.pyc`) changed the local hash. `gen:skills-manifest` then wrote a hash CI's clean checkout could not reproduce, and `--check` failed with "skills-manifest.json is out of date". This happened twice on #5651.
- On a user's machine, an installed skill that ever ran a Python script read as `outdated` permanently, since no update removes the bytecode.

Reproduction on `main` before this change:

```
mkdir -p skills/media-use/audio/scripts/lib/__pycache__
printf '\x00junk' > skills/media-use/audio/scripts/lib/__pycache__/gemini-auth.cpython-312.pyc
bun packages/cli/scripts/gen-skills-manifest.ts --check
✗ skills-manifest.json is out of date — a skill changed without regenerating it.
  ~ media-use (c4c3c723aa04bb7d → b0581facb38068ae)
```

With this change the same command prints `✓ skills-manifest.json is in sync (21 skills)`.

## Related work

Refs #5651. That branch's commit `3cd764422` ("regenerate the skills manifest from tracked files only") changes only `skills-manifest.json` data (a regeneration after the stray bytecode was removed); it does not change the generator or the hash. This PR does not touch `skills-manifest.json`, so the two do not conflict, and once this lands a local regeneration on #5651 can no longer pick up bytecode.

## How

- The skip lives in `listFilesSorted`, which both the source path (`buildManifest` → `gen-skills-manifest`) and the installed path (`hashInstalled`/`checkSkills`) go through, so the two sides stay symmetric.
- No tracked file under `skills/` matches the skip set (checked with `git ls-files skills`), so every published hash and file count is unchanged and `skills-manifest.json` needs no regeneration. Installed skills that are already current stay current.
- A name-based skip, not a `git ls-files` walk: the installed side has no git, and the hash must be computed identically on both sides.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: two cases in `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsManifest.test.ts` — `__pycache__/*.pyc` and a stray `.pyc` leave the hash and file count unchanged while a real `.py` edit changes it; `node_modules/`, `.DS_Store`, `.swp`, `~` backups leave it unchanged. Both fail without the fix (2 failed / 59 passed) and pass with it.
- [x] `cd packages/cli && bun x vitest run src/utils/skillsManifest.test.ts src/utils/skillsMirror.test.ts src/utils/skillsUpdateCheck.test.ts src/commands/skills.test.ts` → 4 files, 133 tests passed
- [x] `bun packages/cli/scripts/gen-skills-manifest.ts --check` → `✓ skills-manifest.json is in sync (21 skills)`, both on a clean tree and with a `__pycache__/*.pyc` planted in `media-use` (the reproduction above)
- [x] `bun run lint` → 0 warnings, 0 errors
- [x] `bun x oxfmt --check` on both changed files → correct format
- [x] `bun x tsc --noEmit -p packages/cli` (after `bun run --cwd packages/core build`) → exit 0, no errors
- [x] `npx -y fallow audit --base origin/main --threads 4 --fail-on-issues` → no issues in 2 changed files
- [x] `COMMENT_CHECK_BASE=origin/main node scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` → OK; `node scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs` → at or under base share
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

CLI internals only: the skill fingerprint ignores runtime by-products. Published hashes are unchanged.

title: ci(skills): hide retired skills on ClawHub once the sync has run
body:
## What

Adds a **Hide retired skills** step to `.github/workflows/sync-skills-to-clawhub.yml`. It runs the new `scripts/clawhub-unlist-retired.mjs`, which hides on ClawHub every name in `RETIRED_SKILLS` (`packages/cli/src/utils/skillsManifest.ts`) that is still listed under `heygen-com`. Each hide records that skill's `retiredSkillNotice` as its moderation note. With the workflow's existing `dry_run` input, the step only prints the names that are still listed.

**Stacked on #5651.** The base is `miao/oss-skills-slim`, so this diff shows only the ClawHub change. Retarget to `main` after #5651 merges.

## Why

#5651 retires 14 skills. `clawhub sync` stops republishing them, but each one's last version stays listed and installable on ClawHub. A public `clawhub inspect heygen-com/<name> --json` run today returns all 14, for example `general-video` 1.0.28 and `hyperframes-core` 1.0.42.

## Related work

Refs #5651

## How

What ClawHub offers (`clawhub@0.23.1`, the version the workflow pins; its `--help`, its `dist/`, and openclaw/clawhub `docs/http-api.md`):

- `clawhub hide <skill> [--reason] [--yes]`: "Hide one of your skills". In `dist/cli/commands/delete.js`, `cmdHideSkill` is `cmdDeleteSkill` with different labels. Both send `DELETE /api/v1/skills/{slug}` with `{ reason, ownerHandle }`, which the API docs describe as "Soft-delete / restore a skill (owner, moderator, or admin)". `clawhub unhide` / `clawhub undelete` restore it.
- `GET /api/v1/skills/{slug}` returns 404 "Skill not found" for a soft-deleted skill (`convex/httpApiV1/skillsV1.ts`). The script inspects first and hides only a skill that still resolves, so a rerun makes no hide call.
- `clawhub skill merge <source> <target>` also exists. It hides the source listing and keeps the old slug as a redirect to the target. This PR does not use it (see "Left for a human" below).

The script follows `scripts/clawhub-sync.mjs`: an injectable `run`, `::error::` lines, and a non-zero exit on any refusal or on an inspect failure other than not-found. It imports `RETIRED_SKILLS` and `retiredSkillNotice` straight from the TS manifest; Node 22's default type stripping handles that, because the module imports only `node:` built-ins. The workflow now also triggers on changes to the script and to `skillsManifest.ts`. Hiding is a separate step, so publishing does not depend on it.

### Left for a human

- I could not tell from here which role the `CLAWHUB_TOKEN` account holds on the `heygen-com` publisher. If it is not an owner or admin, the step fails with `403`/`Forbidden` for each name and the job goes red. Publishing still happens in the earlier step.
- An owner-initiated soft delete reserves the slug for 30 days. After that another publisher can claim the bare slug (`docs/http-api.md`: "Owner-initiated soft deletes reserve the slug for 30 days, then the slug can be claimed by another publisher"). Owner-scoped refs (`heygen-com/<name>`) are unaffected. If the bare `hyperframes-*` names should stay ours, run `clawhub skill merge heygen-com/<name> heygen-com/hyperframes` instead (`media-use` for `hyperframes-audio`). That keeps each slug as a permanent redirect, but it is a one-way owner decision, so this PR does not automate it.

title: ci(studio): re-run an edit accuracy shard on a fresh runner when its runner is too slow
body:
## What

A merge queue edit accuracy shard that lands on a slow runner now stops after its first four cases and runs once more on a fresh runner, instead of running into its timeout and dropping the PR from the queue.

## Why

In merge queue run 38754829357, `Studio: edit accuracy (7/20)` was cancelled at its 45 minute timeout and the PR left the queue. No test hung. The runner was about 5x slow before any test ran:

| | shard 7 | shards 6 and 8, same run |
|---|---|---|
| `bun run --cwd packages/core build` | 44 s | 9 s |
| workspace install | 41 s | 11-17 s |
| median case | 92 s | 14 s |
| load at the end | ~10 | ~6.7 |

The slow cases failed their time-based checks (15 previews never held still within 15 s), so 18 of 38 cases differed from the base branch, and their two confirmation re-runs started on the same slow machine. The other 19 shards took 6-9 min; shard 7 took 5-8 min in the 14 queue runs before it.

The blank-page control does not show this: its rAF p95 median was 17.1 ms on the slow runner and 16.9 / 17.0 ms on shards 6 and 8. Case wall time does.

## Related work

Refs #5646 (dropped from the queue by this run).

## How

- `slowRunner` (report.mjs): the first 4 cases' median wall time over 60 s marks a slow runner. Across all 20 shards of a healthy queue run (38730689165) the slowest first-four median was 22 s; shard 7's was 95.5 s.
- `run.mjs`: once marked, no new case starts; the browsers close as usual, `slow-runner.json` is written and the bench exits 75.
- `scripts/ci/edit-accuracy-shard.sh`: the shard step's script, unchanged, moved out of the workflow so the re-run job runs the same thing.
- `ci.yml`:
  - a shard whose bench stopped on a slow runner, or that was cancelled, marks itself (`retry`) in its evidence;
  - `studio-edit-accuracy-retry-plan` lists the marked shards;
  - `studio-edit-accuracy-retry` runs each of them once on a fresh runner and replaces that shard's evidence artifact (`overwrite: true`);
  - the gate now waits for the re-run.
- The shard timeout goes from 45 to 25 min, so a cancelled shard plus its re-run and the gate fit inside the merge queue's 60 minute check wait. Healthy shards take 6-9 min.
- The time-based checks themselves are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `report.test.mjs`: shard 7's first cases (95.5, 133.7, 57.9, 107.5 s) stop the shard; a healthy first four (22 s median) and one with a single 92.7 s case pass; fewer than 4 cases never judge.
  - `scripts/edit-accuracy-retry.test.mjs` runs the mark and plan steps' own shell. It checks that a cancelled or slow shard is marked and a successful one is not, and that the plan lists exactly the marked shards (`[7,12]`, `[]`). It also checks that the re-run replaces the evidence, that the gate waits for it, and that the timeouts fit in 60 min.
  - `check-edit-accuracy-filter.test.mjs` now follows shell scripts a step runs, so the moved bench command stays covered by the path filter.
- [x] Failing first:
  - the new workflow test fails 4/4 on main's `ci.yml`;
  - the new report tests fail 3/3 on main's `report.mjs`.
- [x] Mutants each fail a test: an unmarked cancelled shard, no `overwrite`, a gate that does not wait for the re-run, and a limit of 200 s or 20 s.
- [x] Passes 3 runs in a row: the 12 edit accuracy unit files (87 tests), the new workflow test, the filter test and the merge queue workflow test.
- [x] Manual testing performed: a real `pr` grid shard with the limit lowered to 1 s stopped after 4 cases with exit 75 and `slow-runner.json`, closed its browsers and left no orphan process. oxfmt, oxlint and actionlint are clean.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(inspector): resolve build paths with fileURLToPath on Windows
body:
## Summary
- `packages/inspector/build.mjs` resolved its own file paths with `new URL(path, import.meta.url).pathname`, which returns a POSIX-style path on Windows (e.g. `/C:/hq/hyperframes/...`). Node's `fs` functions mishandle that leading-slash-before-drive-letter form, producing `ENOENT` errors like `C:\C:\hq\...`.
- Switched to `fileURLToPath(new URL(path, import.meta.url))`, which resolves correctly on both Windows and POSIX.

## Test plan
- [x] `bun install` on Windows
- [x] `bun run build` — failed before this fix (`@hyperframes/inspector build: Error: ENOENT ...`), passes after
- [x] `bun run test` — 7875/7905 tests passing after the fix (remaining failures are environment-specific: no local Chrome binary for Puppeteer-driven browser tests, and one test timeout on a low-spec machine; unrelated to this change)
