title: fix(core): timed svg clips hide outside their window
body:
## What

A timed `<svg>` clip now hides outside its window like any other clip. Before, every `<svg data-start>` stayed visible at every time, so a seek or a snapshot showed the last full-frame SVG layer instead of the one whose window holds that time. `<div>` clips in the same composition were fine.

## Why

The runtime's visibility pass skipped every element that is not an HTML element (`if (!isHtmlElement(rawNode)) continue;`). An `<svg>` and its shapes are in the SVG namespace, so the pass never set their `visibility`. Once the first-pass hide rule lifted, they all showed. The walk that keeps a clip hidden while an ancestor clip is hidden had the same guard, so an SVG group clip could not hide a timed shape inside it.

## How

Both guards now use the existing `isStylableElement` (HTML or SVG, any realm), so every element kind a timeline clip can be gets hidden and shown the same way.

`isStylableElement` now narrows to `Element & ElementCSSInlineStyle`: TypeScript narrows an `Element` by `HTMLElement | SVGElement` to `HTMLElement` alone, which hid that the visibility helpers were still typed HTML-only. Those helpers, and `isRuntimeElementVisibleAt`, now take `Element` or the style-bearing type.

## Verification

- New test: three full-frame `<svg>` clips (0-4 s, 4-12 s, 12-20 s), each holding a timed shape that outlives it, seeked to 1 s, 5 s and 16 s; exactly one layer and its shape are visible at each time. On main it fails: `layers at 1s: expected [ '', '', '' ] to deeply equal [ 'visible', 'hidden', 'hidden' ]`.
- With only the ancestor guard reverted, the same test fails on the shapes: `shapes at 1s: expected [ 'visible', 'visible', 'visible' ] to deeply equal [ 'visible', 'hidden', 'hidden' ]`.
- A real `hyperframes snapshot --at 1,5,16` of a composition with three full-frame SVG layers (red, green, blue) through the built CLI on Linux: the center pixel reads red at 1 s, green at 5 s and blue at 16 s.
- `packages/core`: `init.test.ts` and `domRealm.test.ts` green 3 runs in a row (248 tests), tsc clean, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.




Ships alone: it is a self-contained runtime fix in `packages/core`; the only other open change from this lane is an unrelated CLI publish fix in another package, and folding them together would mix two reviews.

title: fix(cli): capture writes inline SVG logos whole and parakeet takes long audio
body:
## What

- `hyperframes capture` writes inline SVGs whole. Before, any inline SVG over 10,000 characters (often a site's logo) landed in `assets/svgs` cut mid-tag and did not parse, while the full SVG sat in `extracted/page.html`.
- `transcribe -e parakeet` no longer fails on long audio with `The value of "timeout" is out of range`.

## Why

- The in-page token extraction returned each inline SVG as `svg.outerHTML.slice(0, 10000)`, and the asset pass wrote that string as it was.
- The parakeet decode timeout was `audioSeconds * 2000`. For audio whose length is not a whole number of milliseconds that is a fraction (1851.245 s gave 3702490.25), and `execFile` only takes a whole number.

## How

- The extraction keeps the whole `outerHTML`. The asset pass, the one place that writes `assets/svgs`, skips an SVG over 2 MB and counts it under a new `size-ceiling` drop reason (shown in the capture's dropped summary and the `--json` `dropped` field) instead of writing part of it.
- The decode timeout is rounded up to whole milliseconds and capped at the largest value Node's timers accept.

## Verification

- New tests, all red on main (5 failed):
  - the real extraction script, run in happy-dom on a page with a 100 KB logo SVG: `expected 10000 to be 100935`;
  - the asset pass writes an over-10 KB logo whole and skips (and counts) a 3 MB SVG instead of cutting it;
  - `decodeTimeoutMs` for 1851.245125 s and for 10,000,000 s of audio gives a timeout `execFileSync` accepts.
- A real `hyperframes capture --json` of a local page whose header holds a 41 KB inline logo, through the built CLI on Linux: on main `assets/svgs/logo-*.svg` is exactly 10000 bytes and does not parse as XML; with this change it is 50005 bytes and parses.
- `packages/cli`: the three test files green 3 runs in a row (75 tests), tsc clean, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.

title: fix(cli): pin website capture connections to public peers
body:
## What changed
Website capture now connects only to checked public IPv4 peers. Browser navigation, redirects, subresources and secondary pages use a per-capture proxy that dials the validated numeric address. Asset, font, CSS, GIF, Lottie and standalone download requests use the same address policy with verified HTTPS and manual redirects.

The browser uses a temporary profile that disables direct WebRTC UDP, removes the implicit loopback proxy bypass and disables QUIC. Capture retains the Chromium sandbox on macOS and Windows; Linux keeps its documented compatibility exception. Capture ancestor dotenv files can supply only supported vision settings; inherited `HYPERFRAMES_NO_CAPTURE_DOTENV=1` skips loading them entirely.

## What I measured
- 47 capture/dotenv test files: 465 tests pass, including four real Chromium fixture cases.
- Eight real HTTP/TLS socket integration cases verify numeric dialing, Host/SNI, certificate rejection, private DNS refusal and cancellation.
- Controlled browser redirect to loopback: two requests before the fix, zero afterward. Private iframe/image, later DNS changes, STUN UDP and TURN TCP also reach zero prohibited fixture requests.
- The command-line WebRTC flag alone still emitted four local UDP packets; the profile preference reduces this to zero.
- Live public HTTPS smoke: the browser and Node transport both fetch example.com successfully with normal certificate verification.
- The full workspace build, CLI/core/Studio/scripts TypeScript, changed-file lint/format, normal commit hooks and the new-only Fallow gate pass. Local checks reuse cached dependency packages with task-local links; the cached test runner is Vitest 3.2.4 rather than the declared 4.1.11, so hosted CI remains required.

fails without the fix: the baseline browser reaches the loopback redirect fixture; dotenv/sandbox tests fail against the prior policy; removing the WebRTC profile preference reproduces local UDP packets.

## What I did NOT exercise
No production/private services, paid providers, or live credentials. Browser fixture coverage uses the available Chrome 147 on Linux; it does not establish macOS/Windows execution or support for arbitrary custom browser binaries. Controlled socket tests substitute the final public peer with an owned local fixture and assert the numeric dial argument.

## Compatibility
Capture is deliberately IPv4-only, rejects credentialed/non-HTTP(S) initial URLs, refuses plaintext WebSocket upgrades and rejects asset responses that ignore identity content encoding. Unsupported resources may be absent from a capture. The proxy is a request-routing boundary, not an operating-system sandbox against a compromised browser binary.


## Windows test correction
The first Windows run passed 4,926 CLI tests and failed one new assertion that treated uppercase and lowercase environment names as separate keys. Windows aliases those names. The successor separates the wrong-case dotenv rejection test from the uppercase allowed-setting control; production behavior is unchanged. All 35 focused scaffolding/dotenv tests, changed-file lint/format and normal commit hooks pass locally. Fresh hosted Windows CI remains required.


## Review follow-up

Current head `1679bd8e6` addresses both findings from review at `5f35f025`:

- **Explicit transfer deadlines:** `publicRequest` now uses the caller signal when supplied and creates its 30-second default only without one. A real HTTPS fixture streams 35 MiB over 35 seconds under a 120-second caller deadline: reviewed source aborts at 30.01 seconds; the fix completes at 35.09 seconds. Additional tests exercise default expiry and caller cancellation independently.
- **Shipped CLI dotenv boundary:** the early CWD loader is now capture-aware and shares the same vision allowlist as output-ancestor loading. Inherited `HYPERFRAMES_NO_CAPTURE_DOTENV=1` skips that early file too; inherited browser settings are preserved. Actual CLI dispatch tests cover capture with/without opt-out, inherited browser settings and unchanged non-capture behavior.
- The CLI was rebuilt and its actual `bin/hyperframes.mjs` entrypoint exercised from a temporary project with an existing Chrome path, a runtime setting and a synthetic provider key in `.env`: capture help ignores browser/runtime values, opt-out ignores the provider key too, and non-capture help retains its existing loading behavior. These are startup/help probes, not a capture or provider call.
- 85 focused transport/bootstrap/scaffolding tests passed before adding the inherited-browser control; all 32 CLI dispatch/lifecycle/registration checks pass with that control. CLI build and CLI TypeScript checks pass; normal commit hooks pass. The complete capture/bootstrap rerun passes 469 tests in 47 files; a separate actual Chrome run passes all four browser cases (473 unique passes total). The final comment-only follow-up passes the comment-share gate and normal commit hooks. Fresh hosted CI is running for this head.

No new Mac/Windows runtime, paid provider, customer content or private-service verification is claimed. The previously documented browser shutdown/profile cleanup limit remains unverified; no new cleanup guarantee is added.

## Latest review follow-up (`b0c90870a`)

This head removes one redundant comment after tested implementation `c7ca51969`; runtime and test sources are otherwise identical.

- **Leading-option dotenv boundary:** The early loader selects capture using the same first non-option command / `--` boundary as the current root Citty dispatch (the root declares no value-taking options). Both `--json capture` and `--json --verbose capture` now apply the allowlist and inherited opt-out before command loading. Existing inherited browser settings and non-capture dotenv behavior remain covered. The real CLI-dispatch matrix has fifteen cases; six added cases fail on `1679bd8e` and pass with this fix. Three rebuilt `bin/hyperframes.mjs` startup probes also pass, including leading `--json` with opt-out.
- **Signal cleanup ownership:** Capture registers its idempotent session cleanup with the shared browser signal owner before launching. Signal shutdown settles pending launches and raw-browser closure, then joins registered session cleanup before requesting root exit. Manual close and failure paths use the same cleanup and unregister it afterward. Two regressions drive the actual signal owner without calling `session.close()` first: SIGINT and SIGTERM both fail on `1679bd8e` because the explicit profile still exists at the root-exit request, and pass with the fix. Repeated manual close remains idempotent.
- **Executed:** 483 tests across 49 passing files, plus four actual-Chrome proxy/WebRTC tests run separately: **487 unique passing tests**. The retained real HTTPS test still transfers 35 MiB over 35 seconds under the caller's 120-second deadline. Two actual Chrome child-process signal probes close a page, leave non-browser work pending, and send SIGINT/SIGTERM: the explicit profile is absent and the proxy refuses connections at the root-exit request; Chrome is gone after exit with codes 130/143. CLI build, CLI typecheck, changed-file lint/format, process-ownership gate and normal signed-commit hooks passed. Cached Vitest is 3.2.4, distinct from declared 4.1.11.
- **Limits:** Signal execution was on Linux Chrome, not macOS/Windows. The signal probes use a controlled pending promise rather than a provider call. No paid provider or credential request was made. SIGKILL cannot run asynchronous cleanup. Fresh hosted CI for this successor remains a separate gate; no prior approval is transferred.

title: Render audio differs from run to run: amix input order follows prep completion order (and the −1 dBTP guard flips)
body:
### Describe the bug Rendering the same composition twice gives different audio. Between renders the decoded audio differs about 33 dB below the signal. On a composition whose true peak sits near −1 dBTP, some renders also come out 0.6 dB quieter: the log line `Audio lowered by 0.6 dB to stay under −1 dBTP` appears on some runs and not on others. It happens with `--workers 1` too. Video is not affected. We've seen it on 0.8.156 through 0.8.161, on two Macs. ### Minimal reproduction A self-contained script with synthetic assets. It needs only ffmpeg. It builds a 3 s audio-only composition (one mono tone, one stereo noise bed, 12 overlapping 0.6 s noise pops), renders it 4 times, and prints a hash of each render's decoded audio. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Builds a 3 s audio-only composition from synthetic assets, renders it 4 times, prints a hash of the decoded audio. set -e V=${V:-latest} md5=$(command -v md5sum || command -v md5) mkdir -p hf-audio-repro/a && cd hf-audio-repro gen() { ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i "$2" -af "$3" -ac "$4" -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le -y "a/$1"; } gen voice.wav "sine=f=180:d=3,aeval=val(0)*0.5+0.25*sin(2*PI*1375*t)" "volume=0.55" 1 gen bed.wav "anoisesrc=d=3:c=pink:a=0.5:s=7" "volume=0.25" 2 for k in 0 1 2 3; do gen pop$k.wav "anoisesrc=d=0.6:c=white:a=0.9:s=$((k+1))" "afade=t=out:st=0:d=0.6:curve=exp,volume=0.6" 2; done cat > index.html <
$(awk 'BEGIN { for (i = 0; i < 12; i++) printf "\n", i, i % 4, 0.2 + i * 0.21, 40 + i % 3, 0.3 + 0.05 * (i % 5) }')
EOF for i in 1 2 3 4; do npx -y hyperframes@$V render --quality delivery --workers 1 --quiet -o out-$i.mp4 . > render-$i.log 2>&1 echo "render $i: decoded audio $(ffmpeg -v error -i out-$i.mp4 -map 0:a -f s16le - | $md5 | cut -c1-12)" done ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Save the script as `repro.sh`. 2. Run `V=0.8.161 bash repro.sh`. 3. Compare the four hashes. ### Expected behavior The same composition renders to the same audio every time (identical decoded PCM), the way the video already does. ### Actual behavior On 0.8.161 (Apple M4, macOS, ffmpeg 9.0.2): ``` render 1: decoded audio abc0446d18a9 render 2: decoded audio 9b4316ea2a22 render 3: decoded audio abc0446d18a9 render 4: decoded audio 5d36e1c76aac ``` On a real 30 s composition with 53 audio tracks, 4 renders came out at two levels 0.61 dB apart. The quieter renders were the ones that logged `Audio lowered by 0.6 dB to stay under −1 dBTP`. ### Environment ```shell ✓ Version 0.8.161 (latest) ✓ Node.js v26.11.1 (darwin arm64) ✓ CPU 10 cores · Apple M4 @ 2400MHz ✓ FFmpeg ffmpeg 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg ✓ FFprobe ffprobe 9.0.2 at /opt/homebrew/bin/ffprobe ✓ Chrome cache: chrome-headless-shell mac_arm-152.0.7977.30 ``` (Relevant `npx hyperframes doctor` lines. It also reproduces on a second Mac with the same ffmpeg.) ### Additional context **Cause, as far as we can tell from the dist build:** 1. **The mix order depends on timing.** `processCompositionAudio` (`engine/src/services/audioMixer.ts`) prepares every element with `elements.map(async ...)` inside `Promise.all`. It calls `tracks.push(track)` (or `bucket.push(track)` for groups) when that element's ffmpeg prepare finishes, so the `amix` input order is the completion order. With the shim described below, we saw the order change on every render. 2. **The AAC encoder magnifies rounding.** `amix` sums its inputs in order. Swapping two inputs doesn't change a float sum, but where three or more inputs are non-zero at once, the rounding differs (about −155 dB). The native AAC encoder then writes a different bitstream from the first frame where a coding decision flips. The decoded difference is about −33 dB. 3. **The true-peak check flips on that codec noise.** `enforceAacTruePeak` (`producer/src/services/render/audioPadTrim.ts`) measures the re-encoded AAC with `ebur128`, which reports true peak in 0.1 dB steps, and compares it with −1.0 dBTP. A mix near that line reads −0.9 on some runs and −1.0 on others, so it gets lowered by 0.6 dB only sometimes. With one shuffled order we tried offline, the AAC read +0.5 dBTP, which would have lowered that render by 2 dB. **Evidence.** We set `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH` to a logging shim and captured the final mix from two renders of the 53-track composition. Their 53 input WAVs were bit-identical; only the order differed. Mixed to float WAV, the two orders came out −160 dB apart. Mixed to AAC as the renderer does, they came out −34 dB apart. **Suggested fix.** Keep document order: store each prepared track by its element index (`tracks[i] = track`, and the same for group buckets), drop the failed slots, and stop pushing on completion. Separately, applying the true-peak guard before the first AAC encode (on the float mix), or measuring with finer resolution, would stop the level depending on codec noise. **Workaround we use.** An ffmpeg wrapper set as `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH`. For the `amix` call only, it sorts the inputs by file name and renumbers the filter graph before running ffmpeg. Every other call passes through unchanged. With it, the repro and the real composition give bit-identical audio on every render, including across the two Macs.

title: fix(cli): ask to log in when publishing needs an account
body:
## What

When you publish without being signed in and the server answers 401, `hyperframes publish` now stops with:

> Publishing needs an account. Run hyperframes auth login to publish.

Before, it printed whatever the server put in its 401 body. A signed-in publish that gets a 401 still says the login expired, and every other status behaves as today (404 and 405 still fall back to the direct publish route).

## Why

Publishing is moving to signed-in uploads, so a signed-out publish will meet a 401 on the upload route. The direct publish route is no way around it for real projects, so the useful answer is to sign in.

## How

`publishProjectArchive` already turns a 401 from any publish request into a `CredentialRejectedError` and, for a signed-in publish, into the re-login message. The same branch now answers a signed-out publish with the log-in message. No request is added and nothing falls back.

## Verification

- New test: a signed-out publish whose upload route answers 401 fails with the log-in message and makes no other request. On main it fails: `expected ... 'Publishing needs an account. Run hype…' but got 'Unauthorized'`.
- The existing tests for a signed-in 401 (re-login message on the upload, finalize and legacy routes), a 401 from the storage upload, and the 404 fallback pass unchanged.
- `packages/cli`: `publishProject.test.ts` and `publish.test.ts` green 3 runs in a row (74 tests), tsc clean, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.



Ships alone: a self-contained CLI message fix the server-side change depends on; nothing else open from this lane can carry it.

title: fix(engine): preserve authored audio mix order
body:
## What

Audio track preparation remains parallel, but FFmpeg receives prepared tracks in authored element order. Group members and group creation also use that order, so scheduling no longer changes the floating-point mix.

## Why

Appending tracks as asynchronous preparation finishes changes `amix` summation order. The same composition can therefore produce different decoded audio on repeated renders.

## Related work

Refs #5669. This fixes the preparation-order race. The reported near-threshold true-peak attenuation flip on macOS remains unverified; this change preserves the existing guard.

## How

Each preparation writes to its own indexed slot. After all preparations finish, one ordered pass assembles flat tracks and group buckets. Existing failure and cancellation handling remains in place.

## Test plan

- [x] Three actual-mixer regressions force reverse preparation completion and check flat inputs, grouped members and group order. All three fail with the previous mixer and pass with this change.
- [x] 90 tests across the new order suite and existing mixer, grouping and level suites pass, including real FFmpeg grouping/level cases. Engine TypeScript check passes.
- [x] Four real-engine renders of a synthetic 14-track composition: previous source produces two decoded-PCM SHA256 values; this change produces one identical value across all four runs. Four additional increased-gain renders also match each other.
- [x] The existing producer pad/trim and true-peak path preserves that repeatability. It applies no attenuation to these fixtures; this does not reproduce the reporter's near-threshold guard flip.
- [x] Comments explain the ordering requirement and the regression forces the race without timing sleeps.

Local verification uses Linux FFmpeg 7.0.2 and cached dependencies (Vitest 4.1.11 with local source aliases), rather than the reporter's macOS/FFmpeg 9.0.2. No full HTML capture/CLI render, packaged app, customer composition or paid service was exercised. Normal repository hooks and hosted checks are separate gates.

title: perf(core): preview runtime scales with what plays, not with the film's clip count
body:
## What

The preview runtime no longer does whole-film work per media element or per frame. On a 2-hour Desktop podcast episode
(2,354 `<video>`/`<audio>` clips, 26k caption words in 23 caption sub-compositions, 38k zero-duration GSAP sets),
this is most of what froze the project window on open and held playback at 15–19 fps.

## Why

Measured in Desktop over CDP (CPU profiles, long-task observer, devtools.timeline traces) with local builds swapped in:

| Cost | Where |
|---|---|
| ~20 s per bind pass | `probeAndCacheElementVolume` → `getChildren(true,true,false)` once per media element |
| 4 of every 10 s of playback | `applyClipLayout` on every `postTimeline`: lift `display:none`, `getComputedStyle`, restore — every root clip |
| ~2× per second | the runtime's own `releaseMedia` src reset and authored-length clips' load events bumped the timing revision → full `postTimeline` |
| ~1.2 s / 8 s of playback | `rerenderGsapTimelineAt` + `hasZeroDurationCallbackTween` walked every nested child twice a frame |
| ~1.2 s / 8 s | visibility pass resolved all 2,354 media every frame |
| ~0.8 s / 8 s | per-frame `querySelector`s over 52k nodes (registered hosts, root, `[data-start]`, audio groups) |
| per payload | `resolveCssStackingContextId` re-walked one ancestor chain with `getComputedStyle` per sibling |
| open | raster-hint follower re-walked a subtree per attribute record while a caption template built |

## How

- `volumeMoversOf(timeline)`: one tween walk per pass, shared by every probe.
- `applyClipLayout` skips a clip whose inline layout, class and `data-width/height` match what it last laid out.
- Timing revision ignores the runtime's own release writes (`withoutOwnTimingRecords`) and load events of clips
  with an authored length (their window cannot move: authored duration wins in `resolveMediaDuration`).
- GSAP: landing marks are placed once per timeline structure (timing revision + direct child count) and only those
  within 0.05 s of the playhead are saved/restored; the zero-duration-callback check is cached the same way.
- Visibility pass, steady playback only: skips a root-level media clip hidden last pass, not loading/armed, whose
  window ± every look-ahead is clear of the span played and the loop start.
- Registered hosts (misses too), root composition and per-frame queries are kept for one timing revision.
- Stacking context memo by parent per payload; raster-hint checks deduped per record batch; `gsapNeverRendered` reads
  `_first`; master bus from the first composition root.

**Render path:** every new cache bypasses once render capture has started (`renderCaptureSeekStarted`), except the
layout cache (same inputs → same writes) and the authored-length event filter.

## Related work

Studio half: #5675 (independent).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added; each fails on the code before its fix (layout cache, landing-mark window — also a mutation
  check with the window disabled, stacking memo, raster batch, volume movers).
- [x] `src/runtime` + audio groups: 2,111 pass; core typecheck clean.
- [x] Producer regression suite, branch vs merge-base, case by case on one machine: 58/75 pass on both; the 17 that
  fail here fail identically on the base (same failed-frame counts; fonts/Chrome vs goldens).
- [x] In Desktop on the episode (production build): longest task on open 24–42 s → 1.1–1.6 s; playback 15–19 →
  90–108 fps (120 on an empty project); heap 1.2–1.7 GB → ~180 MB (with the Studio PR).

title: fix(producer): an ffmpeg failure names how ffmpeg ended and keeps its last line
body:
## What changed

**When the audio step of a render fails because ffmpeg stopped, the error now says how it stopped, and it keeps ffmpeg's last line, where ffmpeg names the cause.**

Renders with loud mixes (the true-peak correction pass runs) have been failing at the assemble stage with `Audio duration normalization failed: [audioPadTrim] [FFmpeg] ...` followed by ffmpeg's stream banner and nothing else, ending mid-word in `…`. Two things hid the cause:

- `describeFfmpegFailure` (`packages/engine/src/utils/runFfmpeg.ts`): when ffmpeg ends without an exit code, `formatFfmpegError` returns only `[FFmpeg] <stderr tail>`, and the signal or stop reason was dropped. It now leads with it: `FFmpeg ended without an exit code (SIGKILL).`, or the reason this process stopped it (`abort`, `inactivity`, `spawn_error`). A timeout still leads with `FFmpeg timed out ...`; an exit code's message is unchanged.
- `sanitizeProbeFailure` (`packages/producer/src/services/render/audioPadTrim.ts`): the error a person reads went through `redactTelemetryString` with its default 240-character cap, which keeps the start of ffmpeg's tail (the banner) and drops the end (the error). Paths are still redacted; the cap is lifted, since this is the thrown error, and the CLI's telemetry caps its own copy.

Under 100 changed lines: a lone fix with no other open change in this repo to carry it.

## What I measured

- `runFfmpeg.test.ts`, four new cases: a signal and a requested stop are named; a timeout and an exit code read as before.
  - Fails without the fix: the two naming cases fail. With the fix, 26 pass, 3 runs in a row.
- `audioPadTrim.test.ts`, one new case: a correction pass whose error runs past 240 characters keeps its last line.
  - Fails without the fix: the error comes back cut. With the fix, 38 pass, 3 runs in a row (`bun test`).
- `tsc --noEmit` for engine and producer; oxfmt clean on the four files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The failure itself. A render with music near -0.4 dBTP and six 48 kHz 16-bit WAV stems, in a project path with spaces, rendered cleanly on Linux (ffmpeg 7.0.2) and macOS (ffmpeg 8.1.2): the correction pass ran and lowered the audio by 1.2 dB. This change makes the next failure say what ffmpeg reported.

Issue 1 — `narration` is a contract field with no route-level policy, so `general-video` runs can ship silent
body:
# Issue 1 — `narration` is a contract field with no route-level policy, so `general-video` runs can ship silent

**Component:** skills — `hyperframes/references/brief-contract.md` + `hyperframes/references/routes/`
**Version:** hyperframes 0.8.155
**Severity:** contract gap (silent-failure class — no error, no warning, no check)

> **Prior art note:** #2775 reports the *runtime* half of silent narration (audio
> produced but never wired / never verified). This issue is the **contract** half
> one level up: the skills layer never *asks* whether narration is required in
> the first place. Fixing #2775's gate would turn the failure described here
> from "silent success" into "loud failure" — but the run would still be
> dispatched without narration because no route contract requests it.

## Summary

`brief-contract.md` § 2 declares `narration` as a shared brief field:

| Field       | Meaning                                              | Policy                   |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `narration` | `yes`, `minimal`, or `no`, plus route-specific modes | **Follow the selected route.** |

The policy delegates entirely to the route. But the route *contract* files
(`hyperframes/references/routes/*.md`) do not define it:

```
routes/product-launch-video.md   0 hits
routes/faceless-explainer.md     0 hits
routes/general-video.md          0 hits
routes/pr-to-video.md            0 hits
routes/motion-graphics.md        1 hit
routes/music-to-video.md         1 hit
```

So for most routes the chain terminates in silence: `narration` → "follow the
route" → route says nothing → nothing is required → nothing is checked.

## Why this matters (concrete repro)

A `general-video` run produced a 42s composition with **zero `<audio>`
elements** and rendered it. Every available gate reported success:

```
$ npx hyperframes check
  0 error(s), 0 warning(s) · 318/318 text checks pass WCAG AA
◇  Check passed
```

`check`'s `--json` top-level keys are `ok, strict, browserSkipped, lint, runtime,
layout, motion, contrast, hdr, snapshots` — there is no audio/voice/track/media
dimension, so a fully silent deliverable passes cleanly.

The user, not the toolchain, caught it ("没声音？"). The `narration` field was
never set, because no route asked for it.

## The asymmetry

Some workflow `SKILL.md` files discuss narration extensively:

```
product-launch-video/SKILL.md   11 hits
faceless-explainer/SKILL.md      7 hits
pr-to-video/SKILL.md             7 hits
general-video/SKILL.md           1 hit   ← only the /media-use routing table row
```

That single `general-video` hit is a routing entry ("Any media asset or
operation, including narration, BGM, …"), not a policy for when narration is
required. `general-video` is the documented fallback for *any* unmatched video
request, so it is the route most likely to be used by someone who has not
thought about narration at all — and it is the one that says least about it.

(To be precise: the gap is in the **route contract file**
`hyperframes/references/routes/general-video.md`, which is 1374 bytes and
contains 0 mentions of `narration`. The workflow's own `SKILL.md` mentions it
once, only in the media-operation routing table. Neither states a policy.)

## Suggested direction (not prescriptive)

One or more of:

1. **Give `general-video`'s route contract a narration rule** — e.g. an
   interview question ("should this be narrated?") and a documented default,
   mirroring how the specialized routes handle it.
2. **Make the policy explicit in `brief-contract.md`** for routes that do not
   define their own — otherwise "follow the selected route" is a no-op for
   anything but the specialized workflows.
3. **Consider a check dimension for declared capabilities.** If the confirmed
   brief says `narration: yes` and the assembled composition contains no
   `<audio>` (or every `<audio>` lacks an `id`, which the core skill notes means
   it is never picked up by the mixer), that is a machine-detectable
   contradiction between the brief and the artifact. Today nothing compares the
   two.

## Environment

- Windows 11, hyperframes 0.8.155, Node v22.14.0
- `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` not on PATH (used a full build from another app); `check`
  itself ran fine, so this is unlikely to be related
- TTS route used to fix it: `msedge-tts` + `zh-CN-XiaoxiaoNeural` (no HeyGen /
  ElevenLabs / Gemini credentials present; local Kokoro unavailable — missing
  `kokoro-onnx`, and `espeak-ng` absent which Mandarin phonemization needs)

## Note

This is filed as a contract/coverage observation, not a crash. The failure mode
is that everything reports success.

title: fix(core): a caption line shows again after the playhead jumps back over it
body:
## What

A caption or lyric line that hides itself at its end (`tl.set(line, { visibility: "hidden" }, end)`) no longer stays hidden after you click or drag the playhead past it and back. Before this, one jump over a line was enough to blank it in the preview for the rest of the session, while snapshots and renders still showed it.

## Why

The runtime hides an off-screen clip with an inline `visibility: hidden`, and its children inherit it. A seek that jumps over a clip renders that clip's GSAP tweens for the first time while the clip is hidden. A `set` (or `autoAlpha`) tween then records the inherited `hidden` as the value to restore. Seeking back writes that value inline, so the line stays hidden even when its clip is on screen again.

Repro on main: a clip from 2 to 4 s, a child hidden by a `set` at 3.9 s; `seek(6)` then `seek(3)` leaves the child hidden. Seeking to 3 first, then 6, then 3 shows it, because the set first rendered while the clip was visible. Renders never hit this: they move forward from frame 0.

## Related work

None found (searched open PRs and issues for seek/scrub visibility). Touches the same hidden-clip mark as #5619.

## How

- `showHiddenClips()` in `timedClipHide.ts` (the owner of the hidden-clip mark) shows the marked clips and returns the undo.
- `seekRootChildrenAndAdapters` (the one path every seek takes: clicks, scrubs, the player's `seek`, `renderSeek`) shows hidden clips around the GSAP renders only when the seek is a first render: it jumps more than a frame and a half from the last seek, to a time later than the timelines have rendered through. It hides them again before the adapters run, so an adapter that captures the page never sees them. The visibility pass after the seek decides the final state as before.
- The furthest rendered time resets when the composition's timing revision changes.
- Play ticks, frame-by-frame renders and scrubs back over already-rendered time pay nothing. A jump on a 70-clip film costs about 0.1 ms more at the median (1.4 vs 1.3 ms).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `init.test.ts` "shows a clip's child again after a seek/renderSeek skipped past the GSAP set that hides it at the clip's end". Both cases fail on main (`expected 'hidden' to be 'visible'`) and pass with the fix; the whole file passed 3 runs in a row (245/245). Disabling the lift makes both fail again.
- [x] Manual testing performed: Studio preview of a two-track fixture (background scene + captions sub-composition whose lines hide themselves at their end). Click the ruler at 0:10.5, then at 0:06: before, no caption; after, "Second line" shows. On a 3-minute lyric film with 62 such lines, a back-and-forth drag left 34 lines hidden before and 0 after (3 runs each).
- [x] Core suite: same results as main apart from the new passing test (6 files fail identically on main in a fresh checkout without sibling builds).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

Before (left) and after (right), same fixture, same clicks:

![Before: no caption at 0:06 after clicking 0:10.5 then 0:06](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/47f2e337-40f9-4350-abc2-28293bfabaad)

![After: Second line shows at 0:06 after the same clicks](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/72c9b725-d827-4054-86a3-fbc845ce813c)

title: fix(core): exported scenes keep cards that fly in, instead of one frame of each
body:
## What

A rendered scene keeps the values a tween's from-vars set, on every frame after the tween starts. Before this, a card that flies in with `fromTo(card, { x: -600, opacity: 1 }, { x: 0 })` showed on the frame its tween starts and was hidden again from the next frame, so a stack of cards flying in rendered as single-frame flashes.

## Why

The render and the preview disagreed for the same page. Two defects combine:

1. **The producer's GSAP stub wrapped GSAP twice.** GSAP's browser bundle assigns `window.gsap` twice (`_install(...)`, then `exports.gsap = gsapWithCSS` where `exports` is `window`). The stub's setter wrapped `gsap.timeline` on each assignment, so every timeline on a producer-served page was a stand-in for a stand-in, and `__hfReal` pointed at the inner stand-in rather than the timeline.
2. **The runtime compared stand-ins against GSAP's real children.** `nestedCandidates`, the `existingChildren` check, `placedIn` and the `autoNested` key all compare a registry entry (the stand-in) with GSAP's own children and parents, so a scene nested into the root never read back as nested.

What a render did with that: it nested the scene into the root, did not see it there, and left it paused. The root then read as 0 s long, so the runtime built a composite, moved the scene into it (same miss, also 0 s), and finally bound a duration-floor wrapper around the now-empty root. The scene stayed under the abandoned composite, parked at time 0. Each `renderSeek` unpauses registered timelines; unpausing snaps a child to its parent's time, so every frame re-rendered the scene at 0 with events on, which replayed a hide-at-0 tween over the card already in flight.

To reproduce on main: render the fixture below at 30 fps. Each card is visible on its start frame only (the frame-17 assertion in the new test fails with `expected '0' to be '1'`).

```html
<script>
const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
cards.forEach((c, i) => {
  tl.fromTo(c, { x: -700, rotation: -30, opacity: 1 }, { x: 0, rotation: (i - 2) * 6, duration: 0.34 }, 0.3 + i * 0.3);
});
tl.fromTo(cards, { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 0, duration: 0.01 }, 0);
window.__timelines["scene"] = tl;
</script>
```

(The scene is a sub-composition; the root registers an empty `gsap.timeline({ paused: true })`, which is a common authored shape.)

## Related work

None open for this path. A separate preview issue (a playback rebind that moves scenes into a fresh composite) shows a similar symptom and is not changed here.

## How

- `hf-early-stub.ts`: wrap a given GSAP instance once (`WeakSet`), so a stand-in's `__hfReal` is always the GSAP timeline.
- `init.ts`: one helper, `gsapTimelineOf`, gives the timeline behind a stand-in; the four identity checks in root binding use it. Nothing else in the binding changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added
  - `init.subCompositionPlacement.test.ts`: timelines registered as stand-ins under an empty root, render-seeked frame by frame and compared with the same scene played by plain GSAP. Fails on main at frame 17 (`expected '0' to be '1'`), passes with the fix, 3 runs in a row.
  - `fileServer.test.ts`: `window.gsap` assigned twice; the stand-in's `__hfReal` is the timeline and the child is nested in the parent. Fails on main (`toBeInstanceOf`), passes with the fix, 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Manual testing performed: rendered the fixture with v0.8.163 and with this branch (`beginframe`, Linux); also traced the same page in a browser through the producer file server: card opacity per frame `0×15, 1, 1, 0…` before, `0×15, 1…` after.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## What I measured

title: fix(core): scenes stop resetting during playback when the root has no animation of its own
body:
## What

In a composition whose root timeline is empty and whose animation lives in its scenes, playing in the preview no longer keeps resetting the scenes. Before this, elements that had already animated in (cards flying in one by one, for example) dropped back off screen every half second or so while playing, then crept back.

## Why

The transport seeks every registered scene timeline directly and pauses it first (`seekStandaloneRegisteredTimelines`), so a scene the root holds stays paused by design. GSAP leaves paused children out of a timeline's `duration()`. As soon as the root's cached length is invalidated (GSAP does this the first time a tween in a scene renders), the root reads as 0 s long, so the periodic bind treats it as unusable and rebinds:

1. The root reads 0 s, so the resolver builds a composite timeline, which takes the scenes.
2. The next resolve moves the scenes back into the root (they are missing from it), which is now usable, so it binds the root again.
3. A seek pauses the scenes again, the root reads 0 s again, and the cycle repeats.

Each rebind primes the new root at time 0 (`progress(0.0001)`) before seeking back to the playhead, which re-renders the scenes from their start and loses state that only a forward render sets.

Measured on a 3-minute film with 13 scenes and an empty root: 7 rebinds in 3.5 s of playback; the count of visible cards in a fly-in went 15 → 1 and 7 → 1 mid-animation. With this change: one bind for the whole run, and the cards land 0 → 30 without a drop.

## Related work

#5115 handled the same paused-children length for the missing-root composite (un-pausing before the first read). This fixes it where every length read goes through, so a later re-pause can no longer make a held root look empty.

Depends on #5692, and carries its two commits under this one until #5692 merges (then this branch is rebased to this change alone). In a render, timelines are the producer's stand-ins; with this change the empty root becomes usable, and without #5692's stand-in identity checks the resolver then re-nests the scene and a render at a keyframe boundary loses that keyframe (the edit accuracy gate's `resize-fromto-px-r0-nested-z100-on`, render 90 px off). With #5692 underneath, that frame renders as on main (x -50.073 in a producer capture at 2 s).

## How

- `readTimelineDurationSeconds` (`timelineDuration.ts`, the one helper every runtime length read uses) counts the end of each paused child timeline alongside `duration()`: start time plus total duration over the child's time scale.
- Nothing changes for timelines without paused children. Scenes keep being seeked directly, so data-playback-start and rate on a scene host still apply.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `init.subCompositionPlacement.test.ts` "keeps the scene in one root after a tween first renders, when the root's own timeline is empty". Fails on main (the scene ends up in a different timeline), passes with the fix, 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Every `packages/core/src/runtime` test file passes (2075/2075) on this branch rebased on main with #5692 underneath.
- [x] Manual testing performed: Studio preview of a 3-minute, 13-scene film with an empty root timeline, playing through a fly-in of 30 cards. Before: 7 rebinds, visible cards dropped 15 → 1 and 7 → 1. After: one bind, cards 0 → 30 monotonic.
- [x] Manual testing performed: a two-scene fixture (an intro, then 20 cards flying in one by one; the root registers an empty timeline). Played from 3.6 s and paused at 7.9 s: before, 6 binds and no card left on screen; after, one bind and all 20 cards shown.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

Before (left) and after (right), same fixture, played from 3.6 s and paused at 7.9 s:

![Before: no cards on screen at 7.9 s after playing through the fly-in](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f629d7c1-e92e-4508-8f5a-f55060efdebb)

![After: all 20 cards on screen at 7.9 s](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4f383e2d-ebd1-41cd-b580-d4549180d783)

title: skills update ignores HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS, so a pinned skills install can't stay pinned
body:
### Summary

A team that pins HyperFrames skills to one commit can't keep that pin. Twelve skills, including the `/hyperframes` router (`skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md`, §4), tell the agent to run `npx hyperframes skills update <workflow-name>` before entering a workflow. That command reinstalls the current upstream skills globally and ignores `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1`, which `skills/hyperframes/references/skill-lifecycle.md` documents as the CI and tests opt-out.

### Reproduction (commit 8e17ee9300f0142d7c01f5a670c5ed3950ceed1e)

1. Install the skills at a fixed commit and set `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` and `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1`.
2. Ask an agent for a launch video. The router runs `npx hyperframes skills update product-launch-video`.
3. The global install now holds the latest upstream skills, not the pinned commit. `packages/cli/src/commands/skills.ts` runs the installer without checking either variable.

### Request

Have `skills update` (named and bare) and `skills add` honour `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` the way `init` does: exit 0 with a one-line notice that skills are managed externally. The router's §4 step then keeps working for everyone else. A documented pin, such as `HYPERFRAMES_SKILLS_REF=<sha>`, would serve the same need.

Related: #2613 (the earlier self-update discussion).

title: fix(studio): a failed preview reload says which step it was still waiting for
body:
## What

When an edit's preview reload fails, the message now also says which step the new document was still waiting for: "The preview did not reload (it took too long to load). It was still waiting for the page and its runtime to load / its timeline to be ready / its loaders to clear. The previous preview is still showing."

## Why

Reload failures report how they ended (the reload budget ran out, or the player's probe gave up) but not what never happened, so a stuck reload cannot be traced to a cause from the report alone. Each failure now names the first readiness step that had not completed.

## How

- `failShadow` in `useShadowPreviewReload.ts` reads the shadow's state before it is discarded: no runtime bridge (`__player`) means the page and its runtime had not loaded; no pending commit means its timeline (a positive length and the restore seek's paint) was not ready; otherwise its loaders had not cleared.
- The detail is a new sentence after the existing cause, so anything matching the start of the message keeps matching. It is also logged with `logReload("shadow-failed", ...)`.

## No visible change

Only the text of an existing error message changes; nothing on screen moves or renders differently.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts` asserts the step for each case (no runtime, runtime with no length, timeline ready but loaders up). Breaking the timeline check makes its test fail.
- [x] `packages/studio/src/player`: 2303/2303, 3 runs in a row; `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed: Studio dev server, a reload whose runtime never starts: the console shows "... It was still waiting for the page and its runtime to load."
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: test(cli): stop the dotenv startup test failing at random under load
body:
## What

`cli.dotEnv.test.ts` fails now and then in CI's `Test (runtime)` shard, on a different case each time:

```
AssertionError: expected undefined to deeply equal [ ... ]
Missing URL. Pass a website URL, or use --video <project> for video download.
```

The `Missing URL` line shows what went wrong. The real `capture` command ran instead of the test's mock.

## Why

Each case imports the real CLI, which starts background imports (update check, app history, background checks) and does not wait for them. `afterEach` then queues `doUnmock` calls, and the next case queues its `doMock` calls.

Under load, one of those leftover imports is still resolving vitest's pending mock queue when the next case's import starts. The unmock can then land after the new mock, so the next case gets the real command module.

The fix: `afterEach` now waits for `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` before it touches the mocks.

## Proof

I ran 8 copies of the file at once, 3 rounds, to recreate CI's load:

| | Runs that failed |
|---|---|
| main | 9 of 24, same assertion and `Missing URL` as CI |
| this branch | 0 of 48 |

`cli.lifecycle.test.ts` and `cli.workspaceBuildGate.test.ts` follow a similar mock pattern. Under the same load, 0 of 16 runs failed for each, so they are left unchanged.

title: fix(cli): page loads stop timing out while a busy machine's Chrome warms up
body:
## What

`check`, `snapshot`, `compare`, `grade-compare`, `layout` and the motion shot no longer fail with "Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded" just because Chrome was slow to start on a busy machine. The 10 s page-load budget now starts when Chrome actually sends the page request, so it measures the page, not Chrome's warm-up.

A Chrome that never sends the request still fails: the warm-up has its own 30 s cap (puppeteer's browser-launch default), and that failure is reported as a navigation timeout too.

## Why

On a loaded Windows runner, a freshly launched Chrome sometimes waits seconds between starting its first navigation and sending the request. In 60 instrumented runs of the check-deadline process test under the full engine and cli test load, Chrome's own `sendStart` for that request reached 4.4 s, 9.5 s in one run, and over 10 s in the run that failed. The local server answered within a few ms of the connection, and Node's event loop never lagged. The 10 s budget counted that warm-up, so the check reported a navigation timeout before the page existed. That knocked a release out of the merge queue, and a user on a busy machine can hit the same failure.

## How

- `gotoWhenSent` (in `capture/navigateForCapture.ts`) starts the navigation untimed and waits for the document request to be sent: `Network.requestWillBeSentExtraInfo`, or `Network.responseReceived` for a page answered without the network (in-process answering). That wait has its own 30 s cap. Then the page gets its full budget to reach DOMContentLoaded. Both limits throw puppeteer's `TimeoutError` with a navigation-timeout message, so the existing hints and classifications still apply.
- The four `page.goto` calls that used the diagnostic navigation budget go through it: `openSettledCompositionPage` (check, snapshot, compare, grade-compare), `layout` (twice), and the motion shot.
- The edit-accuracy bench's path filter in `ci.yml` now lists `captureTimeout.ts` and `navigateForCapture.ts`, which the bench imports through `captureCompositionFrame.ts`.
- The two browser-close tests share one fake CDP session from `deprecationTestHarness.ts`.
- `withRemainingBudget` takes an optional error factory, so it can raise that `TimeoutError` instead of its stage-budget error.

## Verification

- New fake-timer tests in `navigateForCapture.test.ts`: a 25 s warm-up followed by a 9 s page load succeeds; a Chrome that never sends fails after 30 s as a navigation timeout; a page that takes longer than its budget after the send still fails. With the old plain `goto`, the first two fail.
- New real-Chrome tests in `navigateForCapture.browser.test.ts`: the send signal fires while the local server is still holding its response, so it fires at send, not at load. It also fires for a page answered by interception. Both wait on events, with no timers. If the signal waits for the response, the first test fails.
- The changed test files, the check-deadline process and unit tests, and the three browser-close and fallback tests that fake a page are green 3 runs in a row on Linux (47 tests). tsc, oxlint and oxfmt are clean.
- The full cli suite fails exactly the same tests on this branch as on main in the same Linux environment, apart from `contentExtractor.file-race.test.ts`, which also flakes on main (4 of 5 runs) and does not touch page loads.

title: test(cli): caption image test checks the close itself, not a reusable file number
body:
## What

`contentExtractor.file-race.test.ts` stops failing at random. It checked that the caption code closed the image by calling `fstatSync` on the old descriptor number and expecting `EBADF`. Descriptor numbers are reused: once the code closes fd N, any file the process opens next can get N back, and then `fstatSync(N)` succeeds. On a Linux box it failed 4 of 5 runs alone on main.

The test now records `closeSync` in the `node:fs` mock it already has, and asserts that the descriptor the code opened is the one it closed, exactly once. That records the close as it happens instead of probing a number that something else can reuse.

## Verification

- Old check with one file opened just before it (forcing number reuse): 3 of 5 tests fail every time. New check under the same reuse: 5 of 5 pass.
- New check with the code's `closeSync(fd)` removed: all 5 tests fail, so it is not vacuous.
- 3 runs in a row green, then 20 more (23 of 23). oxlint and oxfmt are clean.

title: Preview: a trimmed audio clip is heard past its end, in a hidden tab (transport stalls) and at every buffer end (lagging element unmuted)
body:
Previewing in `<hyperframes-player>` a composition that plays one source file as a series of trimmed clips (`<audio data-start data-duration data-media-start>` per kept segment of a talking-head take), parts of the take are heard that the edit removed. We found two causes. Both are in 0.8.82, and the code of both is unchanged on main (checked at v0.8.165).

**1. In a hidden tab, the transport stops while media plays on.** The transport ticks on `requestAnimationFrame` only (`scheduleNextTransportFrame`, `wakeTransport` and the initial tick in `runtime/init.ts`). A hidden document runs no animation frames, but its media keeps playing, so `syncRuntimeMedia` stops running while it does. Nothing pauses an element at the end of its clip window, and the next clip never starts, until the tab is shown again. A person listening to a draft in another tab hears the raw take, retakes included.

Reproduction: two clips from one source file, e.g. `a1` (`data-start="0" data-duration="0.733" data-media-start="0.166"`) and `a2` (`data-start="0.733" data-duration="1.467" data-media-start="1.166"`). Play, then switch tabs during `a1`. `a1` plays to the end of its source, and `a2` never starts. In a test, holding the document's animation frames reproduces it deterministically.

Proposed fix: while `document.visibilityState === "hidden"`, schedule the transport tick with a timer (16 ms) instead of `requestAnimationFrame`. On `visibilitychange`, move a pending tick to whichever scheduler the new state calls for; a frame requested just before the tab hid would otherwise never fire. Chromium doesn't throttle the timers of a page that is playing audio, so the hidden tick keeps time. A paused, hidden transport still parks as it does today. The change is about 30 lines in `init.ts`: `requestTransportTick`, `cancelTransportTick` and a `visibilitychange` listener registered with the runtime's cleanup callbacks, used in place of the four `requestAnimationFrame(transportTick)` / `cancelAnimationFrame` calls on `state.transportRafId`.

**2. When a clip's Web Audio buffer ends, its element is unmuted while it still plays.** `WebAudioTransport` plays a decoded clip as an `AudioBufferSourceNode` bounded to its window, and mutes the clip's element, which `syncRuntimeMedia` keeps playing beside the buffer. The element lags the buffer: we measured 20–75 ms in Brave (Chromium 154). On the buffer's natural `ended`, `handleSourceEnded` restores `el.muted = priorMuted` while the element is still playing, so the lag is replayed aloud until a tick pauses the element: 1–17 ms at a cut between clips, and 70–100 ms at the last clip, where no other buffer holds the clock. It happens with the tab in front too; in a hidden tab it is often longer, since Chromium repeatedly pauses the muted element and the runtime restarts it. In the 24 trials we recorded, the replay happened at every last-clip end.

Proposed fix: on a natural end, keep a non-looping element muted, and owned for `ownsElement` (so `syncRuntimeMedia`'s per-tick mute keeps applying), until the next `stopAll()`, which every pause, seek and end of playback already calls; a new claim of the element first restores it. A looping element is restored at once as today, since its buffer doesn't loop. About 30 lines in `webAudioTransport.ts` (a `_finished` map, `handleSourceEnded`, `stopAll`, `ownsElement` and a `releaseFinished` called by both schedule paths), with unit tests in `webAudioTransport.test.ts`; the existing runtime tests pass unchanged except the natural-end test, which asserted the unmute.

We run both as a patch on 0.8.82 in our studio, each with a browser test of its bug (the first fails without its fix every time; the second, a timing race, failed 5 of 6 runs without it and passes with it). Happy to open a PR (or two, one per cause) if the approach suits you.

title: perf(core): a preview's composition scripts give the page a turn every 50 ms, not one long task
body:
## What

In a preview, the runtime now hands the page back to the browser after every 50 ms of composition scripts instead of running every composition's script in one task. Scripts still run once each, in the same order, before the runtime boots. Renders are unchanged: under the producer's virtual clock (`window.__HF_VIRTUAL_TIME__`) the runner never yields.

## Why

`runScriptsAfterFonts` runs every composition script back to back. On a long film that is one very long task: in a 9-minute film with 91 sub-compositions it measured 6.5 to 7.7 s in Chrome, during which the page answers nothing (no input, no paint, no ping). Apps that host the preview and watch for a frozen page read that as a hang.

## Related work

Refs #5674 and #5675, which make playback and the Studio timeline scale with what is on screen; this is the load-time half. A follow-up will defer the scripts of compositions far from the playhead, which is what brings the time to a ready preview down.

## How

- `runScriptsAfterFonts` tracks how long the current slice of scripts has run and, past `PREVIEW_SCRIPT_SLICE_MS` (50 ms), awaits the next task before the next script.
- The next task is `scheduler.yield()` where it exists, else a `MessageChannel` message: nested `setTimeout(0)` calls clamp to 4 ms each.
- Under `__HF_VIRTUAL_TIME__` the runner does not yield, because a render's virtual clock holds timers until it advances and the yield would never return.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `entry.afterFonts.test.ts` checks that a preview takes a turn once a slice has run (scripts log `a in-place turn b ready`) and that a render takes none (`a in-place b ready`). Both pass 3 runs in a row with the rest of the file (13 of 13). fails without the fix: with main's `afterFonts.ts` the preview case logs `a in-place b ready`, with no turn.
- [x] Core runtime tests: 83 files, 2077 tests pass; `bun run typecheck`, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet pass.
- [x] Manual: the 9-minute film above in `hyperframes preview` (headless Chrome, two runs): the longest task at open went from 6.5-7.7 s to 0.88-0.96 s (the slowest single composition script). Time to a ready preview is unchanged, as expected.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(core): bundling a project no longer blocks the host's thread on esbuild
body:
## What

Bundling a project (`bundleToSingleHtml`) no longer blocks the host's thread on esbuild. Script comment stripping used esbuild's `transformSync`, which holds the calling thread until esbuild answers. A host that bundles on its main thread (a desktop app re-bundling after every edit) stalled on each script. It now uses esbuild's async `transform`, which leaves the thread free while esbuild works.

No public API changes: `bundleToSingleHtml` was already async, and every call site of the comment stripper sits inside the async `bundleProject`. The output is the same, since the same esbuild transform runs with the same options.

## Why this fix

I considered three options:
- **An async variant for hosts:** not needed, because the public entry point is already async.
- **Comment stripping without esbuild:** that would mean a second JavaScript tokenizer to keep in step with esbuild's, a larger and riskier change for the same output.
- **Async esbuild (chosen):** the smallest change that removes the sync call.

## Verification

- New `htmlBundler.esbuildAsync.test.ts`: esbuild's sync APIs are mocked to throw and record the call, and the async ones stay real. Bundling a project whose scripts carry block and line comments must strip both and make no sync call. On main it fails with `expected [ 'transformSync' ] to deeply equal []`.
- All `packages/core/src/compiler` tests green 3 runs in a row (562 tests). Both core typechecks (`tsc` and `tsc -p tsconfig.runtime.json`) are clean, as are oxlint and oxfmt.
- Desktop main-process before/after: a desktop app that bundles on its main process after each agent write, profiled over a ~140 s agent run on a Linux box. Both sides use a locally packed core, built from main and from this branch, and run twice each, alternating:

  | | Main-thread time in esbuild's sync call (`runCallSync`) | Main process busy | Max event-loop delay |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | Before (main) | 1183 ms, 1006 ms | 6876 ms, 6467 ms | 102 ms, 87 ms |
  | After (this branch) | 0 ms, 0 ms | 6080 ms, 5824 ms | 55 ms, 47 ms |

  Before, the heaviest sync chain was `transformSync` ← `stripJsCommentsParserSafe` ← `bundleProject`. After, no esbuild call appears on the main thread. The remaining bundling work there is about 150 ms per run.

title: fix(cli): check finishes on video-heavy projects, its geometry seeks skip only video-frame waits
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` finishes on video-heavy projects again. Its dense overlap grid no longer waits for each video's frame to land before it reads element boxes, so a 79 s project of 1080p H.264 clips goes from "Check did not finish within its deadline" (122 s) to a full report in 12 s, with the same findings.

## Why

A user's `check` on a 79 s project (7 H.264 1080p clips at the root, a captions sub-composition with 58 timed groups, a graphics sub-composition) returned `browser: failed` every time with "Check did not finish within its deadline", while snapshots at any time worked.

The dense `content_overlap` grid (`collectMotionOverlapSamples`, `utils/checkPipeline.ts`) seeks up to 600 times, 8 per second of video. `DENSE_GEOMETRY_SEEK_OPTIONS` already drops every post-seek settle, because `getBoundingClientRect` is valid synchronously after the seek. But `seekCompositionTimeline` still awaited the runtime's seek barrier (`__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`) on every one of those seeks, and that barrier holds until the on-screen video has seeked and decoded its frame (`holdSeekBarrierUntilVideoLands`, `core/src/runtime/media.ts`, up to 5 s). The geometry pass never reads those pixels.

## Related work

None open.

## How

- The seek barrier (`registerSeekCompletion`, `core/src/runtime/adapters/seek-dispatch.ts`) now knows which of its holds are only a video frame landing: `holdSeekBarrierUntilVideoLands` (`media.ts`) and the proxy swap (`mediaProxy.ts`) register as `"video-frame"`.
- `waitForSeekCompletion({ videoFrames: false })` waits for every other hold: frame sources' asynchronous draws (`frameSources.ts`), `hf-seek` `waitUntil` work, VFX paints, image decodes. Called with no argument, it waits for all of them, as before.
- `DENSE_GEOMETRY_SEEK_OPTIONS` sets `waitForVideoFrames: false`, and `seekCompositionTimeline` passes it to the barrier. Every other seek, the audit grid's included, still waits for video frames. A page whose runtime predates the option ignores the argument and waits for all holds, which is slow but correct.
- The geometry pass reads element boxes, not pixels, so it never needed the video frame. It does need a frame source that moves DOM to finish its draw (review finding), and it now waits for that.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests:
  - `captureCompositionFrame.test.ts`, "skips only the seek barrier's video-frame holds, while the audit seek waits for all": runs the page script the seek sends against a fake `window`, and checks the barrier is asked with `{ videoFrames: false }` for dense seeks and `{ videoFrames: true }` for audit seeks.
  - `media.test.ts`, "does not hold a geometry read for a seeking video's frame": a seeking video holds the default barrier, not the `videoFrames: false` one.

The frame-source test guards the review's case: it fails if a frame source's draw stops holding the `videoFrames: false` barrier.

The 14 s run is this version, which still drains the barrier minus its video-frame holds; the fixture has no frame sources, so nothing else holds it.

title: perf(core): hold a clip at 0 inside a later scene until it is due
body:
## What

In a preview, a video or audio clip that starts at 0 inside a scene that starts later now parses at `preload="none"`, like any other clip that is not due yet. Before, the parse-time deferral read only the clip's own `data-start`, so these clips started downloading at open and kept their buffers. Renders are unchanged: the deferral only runs in a preview.

## Why

`deferMediaUntilDue` gives later clips `preload="none"` before Chromium can start fetching them, because a `none` set mid-fetch is ignored. It decided "later" from the clip's own `data-start`, which is local to its scene. A clip at 0 in a scene at 5:00 looked like it was due now, so the parser started it, and the runtime's later `preload="none"` could not stop it. On a 9-minute film with 91 sub-compositions, 24 such clips were downloading at open, about 64 s of buffered media for scenes nowhere near the playhead.

## How

- The deferral asks the start resolver for the clip's start in the film (`resolveMediaStartForElement`), the same owner the runtime's preload window uses, instead of reading `data-start`.
- It still defers only clips with a numeric own `data-start` and an authored length, so it never holds a clip the runtime's preload window does not manage.
- A fresh resolver per mutation batch: a start that references an element not parsed yet resolves to its fallback in that batch instead of staying cached.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added in `entry.test.ts`: a clip at 0 in a scene at 0 keeps its default preload and a clip at 0 in a scene at 5 parses at `none`. Passes 3 runs in a row with the rest of the file (34 of 34). Fails without the fix: `expected [ '', '' ] to deeply equal [ '', 'none' ]`.
- [x] Core: 210 test files, all tests pass; core typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, package cycles and the comment ratchet pass.
- [x] Manual: the 9-minute film in `hyperframes preview` (headless Chrome). Clips starting more than 10 s in that had fetched anything 5 s after the preview was ready: 24 (64 s buffered) before, 0 (0 s) after, in two runs. The 3 clips near the playhead still load. 12 seeks across the film all land on their frame, and seek times and playback frame rates are within run-to-run noise of the build without this change.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: check --at hangs, then fails with Runtime.callFunctionOn: Target closed on a composition that renders successfully
body:
## Bug description

On HyperFrames 0.8.74, `hyperframes check . --at ... --browser-gpu --json` hangs for several minutes and then records `check_runtime_failure: Protocol error (Runtime.callFunctionOn): Target closed`. The same composition renders all 3261 frames successfully at delivery quality with hardware GPU.

## Reproduction

1. Use a 1080x1920, 30 fps, 108.7 second HTML composition containing one video, one audio track, GSAP timeline elements, and local PNG assets.
2. Run `HF_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MS=90000 hyperframes check . --at 31.90 --browser-gpu --json`.
3. The command stalls beyond the requested max wait and is later killed by the shell timeout. A larger multi-timestamp run wrote the attached failure shape below.
4. Run `hyperframes render . --quality delivery --workers 4 --browser-gpu`.
5. Rendering completes successfully: 3261/3261 frames, artifact validated.

## Actual result

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "runtime": {
    "ok": false,
    "findings": [{
      "code": "check_runtime_failure",
      "message": "Protocol error (Runtime.callFunctionOn): Target closed"
    }]
  },
  "layout": {"ok": true},
  "motion": {"ok": true}
}
```

The command also warns that two PNG assets (2.2 MB and 5.8 MB) exceed the 2 MB inline limit. That warning may be relevant, but browser rendering still resolves those same local assets correctly.

## Expected result

`check --at` should either complete successfully for the requested timestamps, or fail promptly with a bounded actionable error. `HF_CHECK_MAX_WAIT_MS` should prevent an unbounded hang.

## Environment

- HyperFrames: 0.8.74 (project-pinned)
- Node: v22.23.1
- macOS 27.0, Apple M3 Ultra
- Browser GPU: ANGLE Metal hardware
- Render path succeeds with `--quality delivery --workers 4 --browser-gpu`
- Lint: 0 errors; warnings only

title: fix(skills): assemble voice clips at the audio file's duration, not the frame's
body:
## Problem

`skills/faceless-explainer/scripts/assemble-index.mjs` mounted each per-frame voice `<audio>` clip with `data-duration="<frame duration>"`. The storyboard frame duration covers the frame's whole beat — content plus inter-frame padding — so the assembled voice clip's window was longer than the audio file. The runtime treats a `data-duration` longer than the media as an extended clip window, rendering the speech and then padding the remainder with silence: dead air before the next frame's line.

Reproduced in a real assembled project: resizing a voice clip in the Studio editor snapped it shorter than its placed duration, revealing the window had never matched the media. After hand-correcting the assembled `index.html`, each voice clip's `data-duration` equals its `.wav` media length (e.g. `6.91` for a 6.912s file, `15.45` for 15.445s).

## Fix

Measure the voice file with `ffprobe` — the same invocation `ensureBgmCovers` already uses for BGM — and emit the measured duration as the clip's `data-duration`. When the probe is unavailable or unreadable, assembly falls back to the frame duration with an anomaly note rather than hard-failing on missing audio tooling, matching the script's existing degrade-gracefully stance.

The other clip kinds were checked and do not share the bug:
- **BGM** is loop-extended to the full video length (`ensureBgmCovers`) before being mounted at `data-duration=TOTAL` — deliberate.
- **SFX** carries its own `cue.duration_s` authored in `audio_meta.json`, never the frame duration.
- **transitions.mjs** explicitly never touches audio elements (`if (name.toLowerCase() === "audio") return tag;`).

## Verification

- `node --test skills/faceless-explainer/scripts/assemble-index.test.mjs` — 6/6 pass: the 4 existing tests plus two new regression tests:
  - a 1.5s voice file under a 3s storyboard frame assembles with `data-duration≈1.5`, not 3;
  - an unprobeable voice file falls back to the frame duration and surfaces a `could not probe` anomaly.
- Cross-checked against a hand-corrected production assembly: the fix's probed durations match the corrected values to probe rounding.
- `bunx oxfmt --check` and `bunx oxlint` clean on both changed files.
- `skills-manifest.json` regenerated with `bun run --cwd packages/cli gen:skills-manifest` (only the `faceless-explainer` hash drifted, as expected).

title: fix(cli): prevent feedback URL crashes at emoji truncation boundaries
body:
Long feedback containing an emoji can crash `feedback --file-issue` with `URIError: URI malformed`: title/body truncation may cut between the emoji's UTF-16 surrogate halves before URL encoding. Drop an incomplete trailing high surrogate at the truncation boundary, preserving the existing length limits and ellipsis.

Validation: the same focused public test file fails two new title/body regressions on baseline and passes all 9 tests after the fix, including a complete emoji at the boundary and existing ASCII length controls. Vitest 4.1.11 with an explicit minimal one-file config and an existing dependency provider; not the complete CLI configuration.
