title: perf(core): show the first frame without waiting on far scenes' fonts
body:
## What

A preview's first frame no longer waits on web fonts that only far scenes use. The scripts that run before the first frame wait for the faces their own text uses. Everything else waits for every font, as before:
- the root's scripts and the scenes within 10 s run first
- far scenes that must run in document order (eager) run right after the runtime boots
- held scenes run when the playhead nears them

Renders and thumbnail captures are unchanged: with no preview mark nothing is held, and every script waits for every font at load.

Stacked on #5719.

## Why

The after-fonts gate waited for `document.fonts.ready`, which covers every face any laid-out text uses, hidden far scenes included. In a 9-minute film, two CJK faces of 18 MB and 25 MB are used only by scenes from 0:30 on. One of them took 5.5 s to download, so the first frame waited about 5 s for text nobody sees yet.

## How

- `waitForFonts(families)` waits only for the loading faces of the given families. It uses the same 5 s cap and the same diagnostic.
- `bootFontFamilies()` (`heldScenes.ts`) collects the font families of the text outside the scenes that wait. It walks the DOM and skips their subtrees.
- `holdFarSceneScripts` now also holds an eager scene that starts past the lead. It runs right after boot, through #5719's mount path, after the full font wait, in document order. Two kinds of scene still run at boot: one that a root script selects into (its eager reason starts with `REACHED_BY_ROOT_REASON`, now one constant shared by the compiler and the runtime), and a caption scene.
- Preview and export stay identical per script: every script still runs after the fonts its own scene's text uses. Near scenes wait for theirs; every other script waits for all fonts, as in a render.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests in `heldScenes.test.ts`: the near scene's face loads and the far eager scene's face hangs. Boot finishes having run only the near scenes and the root-reached one, and the eager scene runs once its face loads. The existing tests are updated for the eager scene now running after boot. 3 runs in a row, with `entry.afterFonts` and `init.swapScenes` (157 tests).
- [x] Fails without the fix. Each break was checked separately:
  - Boot waiting for all fonts again: the runtime never boots while the far face loads (`expected undefined to be defined`).
  - The after-boot mount removed: the eager scene never runs (`expected 'near reached ' to be 'near reached tied '`).
- [x] Core: 211 test files, 4716 tests pass. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, the comment ratchet and comment citations, and package cycles pass.
- [x] Manual: the 9-minute film in `hyperframes preview`, headless Chrome driving Studio, same machine, cache cleared.

  | | Before (#5719 alone, 3 runs) | After (3 runs) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Preview ready | 6.9 to 7.2 s | 2.3 to 4.5 s |
  | First frame | 7.0 to 7.3 s | 2.5 to 5.5 s |

  Two after-runs paint the first frame 1 to 2 s after ready, and their longest task is 0.88 s, because the far eager scenes' scripts now run right after boot. Median seek was 0.95 to 0.97 s in two runs and 2.05 s in one. Every seek lands on its frame, and playback frame rates are within noise.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(cli): preserve string fallback for non-JSON error values
body:
`normalizeErrorMessage` promises a string, but `JSON.stringify` returns `undefined` when an object's custom `toJSON` returns `undefined`, a symbol or a function. The normalizer currently passes that through, so error consumers using `.toLowerCase()` or `.includes()` can fail while trying to describe the original error.

Use the existing key-list fallback for this non-JSON result as well as serialization failures. Ordinary Error/string/object messages and the existing circular/opaque-object fallbacks retain their behavior.

Validation: the same focused public test file fails all 3 new custom-JSON cases on baseline and passes all 16 tests after the fix, including existing Error/string/plain-object/circular/opaque/primitive controls. Vitest 4.1.11 using an explicit minimal one-file config and existing dependency provider. Lockfile-version Oxlint 1.64.0, Oxfmt 0.41.0, comment citations and comment ratchet pass.

This is a reproduced utility contract defect, not a reproduced external SDK incident. Full workspace build, typecheck, CLI suite and end-to-end browser/transcription flows have not been verified locally; the earlier prescribed workspace build attempt was blocked by unavailable `tsup`.

title: feat(producer): render at 720p and 480p from a larger composition
body:
## What a user can do now

Render a video at 720p or 480p: `hyperframes render --resolution 720p` (or `480p`, or the presets `landscape-720p`, `portrait-480p`, `square-720p` and so on) gives a 1280×720 or 854×480 file from a 1080p composition, and the same presets work through the studio-server render route. Before, any preset smaller than the composition was refused ("Downsampling via --resolution is not supported").

## How

- `parsers/src/types.ts`: six presets, `{landscape,portrait,square}-{720p,480p}`, and the `720p` / `480p` aliases (aspect-agnostic, like `1080p` and `4k`). 480p at 16:9 is 854×480: 480 × 16/9 is 853.33, and 4:2:0 encoders need even sides.
- `checkOutputResolutionCompatibility` now allows a preset smaller than the composition. A smaller preset may be off by under one pixel on its long side (the 854); a larger one must still match exactly and be a whole multiple, as before. The aspect remap that `--resolution 1080p` / `4k` apply on their own (`suggestMatchingPreset`, used by the CLI preflight and the compile stage) returns only a preset in the asked tier, never another: with the looser match for smaller presets, a 1922×1080 composition asked for `4k` would otherwise have been remapped to 480p. It is refused instead, as before.
- `resolveDeviceScaleFactor` returns the long side's ratio, so a smaller preset renders at a device scale factor under 1: Chrome lays the page out at composition size and rasterizes each frame straight at 1280×720 or 854×480, the way 4K already renders at 2. For 480p that is 854/1920: the width lands on 854 exactly and the height's 480.375 rounds to 480, so no pad column is added. Output sizes round as Chrome rounds the screenshot.
- The streaming encoder was given the composition's size instead of the output size on both streaming paths (`renderOrchestrator.ts`). 4K never noticed, as both sizes are even; at 480p the encoder skipped its even-size pad and libx264 refused an odd frame (`width not divisible by 2 (853x480)`). It now gets the output size, as the disk-frame encode already did.
- The paths that refused DPR > 1 (BeginFrame, drawElement, the Linux fast-capture gate) now refuse any DPR other than 1, since none of them honor a scale; scaled renders take the screenshot path, as 4K does.
- `render/outputScaleRoute.ts`: the layered compositor (HDR content, and shader transitions in webm and mov) sizes its layers and encoder from the composition and never scales, so a scaled output on that route now stops with a named error, checked where every route and replan is settled (`syncCapturePlan`, beside motion blur's route check). Before, a 1080p request from a 4K composition with shader transitions as mov would have encoded 3840×2160. HDR with `--resolution` was already refused in preflight; 4K on this route had the same gap on main and gets the same error.

## What I measured

- Real renders from source on a Linux box (`bun src/cli.ts render registry/examples/nyt-graph --resolution 720p|480p|1080p`), checked with ffprobe: 720p `h264, 1280x720, yuv420p, 15.0 s`; 480p `h264, 854x480, yuv420p, 15.0 s`; 1080p unchanged at 1920x1080. A frame of each, looked at: same chart and layout, crisp text, and the 480p right-edge column is the page's own color (250,248,242), not a pad.
- Before the encoder-size fix the 480p render failed with `[libx264] width not divisible by 2 (853x480)`; after it, it renders.
- `outputScaleRoute.test.ts`: the real route choice for a 4K composition with shader transitions as mov (`outputSupportsPageSideShaderCompositing`, `shouldUseLayeredComposite`, `createCapturePlan`, `resolveDeviceScaleFactor`) lands on `hdr_layered` at scale 0.5 and is refused. CLI preflight and the compile stage both refuse `4k` on a 1922×1080 composition.
- fails without the fix: without the same-tier rule, the preflight and compile tests for 1922×1080 at `4k` pass the render through at 854×480; without the route check, the mov test does not throw.
- At d33c4458: producer `outputScaleRoute` + `compileStage` 18/18 three runs in a row, `shared` (bun) 9/9, cli `render` 104/104 once and its new test three runs in a row; tsc clean in producer and cli. Earlier at e72f6507: parsers `outputResolutionCompatibility` 20/20, core `index` 26/26, producer `resolveDeviceScaleFactor` 14/14, cli `render` + `parseOutputResolution` 122/122, studio-server `render` 53/53. The new cases fail on main (the presets don't exist; smaller presets are refused). tsc clean in parsers, engine, producer and cli; oxlint and oxfmt clean.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Distributed (Lambda / Cloud Run) renders at 720p/480p: the chunk worker's sizes round the same way, but I did not run a distributed render.
- Studio's render queue keeps its own copy of the rule (`RenderQueue.tsx` `scaleApplies`) and offers no 720p/480p option; unchanged here.

title: fix(cli): preserve UTF-8 BOM project configuration settings
body:
An otherwise valid `hyperframes.json` saved with a UTF-8 byte order mark is treated as unreadable, so custom registry paths and media settings are ignored. The same marker prevents the existing authoring-skill and installed-item writers from updating the config.

Accept exactly one leading marker in all three config-reading paths. Preserve it when patching existing settings, along with their indentation and unknown keys. Markers inside JSON strings remain untouched; malformed, marker-only and double-marker files remain unreadable.

Validation: the same existing public `projectConfig.test.ts` file fails 3 new regressions on baseline and passes all 42 tests after the fix. Tests use real temporary files and actual reader/normalizer/writer functions. The private minimal Vitest configuration aliases only the unrelated registry barrel to its exact default-URL constant; no mocks were committed. Existing missing-file, unmarked-config, round-trip and invalid-config controls pass. Lockfile-version Oxlint 1.64.0, Oxfmt 0.41.0, comment citations and comment ratchet pass.

Full workspace build/typecheck/suite and native Windows editor behavior have not been verified locally. The earlier prescribed workspace build attempt was blocked by unavailable `tsup`.

title: perf(core): let a scene wait when it only looks inside its own root
body:
## What

Two script patterns no longer keep a scene's scripts at load in a preview, because neither reaches outside the scene:
- a script that marks a node it found through its own `document` (`node.__hfClaimed = 1`)
- a script that reads an attribute off `<html>` (`document.documentElement.getAttribute("data-composition-variables")`)

Stacked on #5722.

## Why

A scene script's `document` is the scoped proxy, so `querySelector`, `querySelectorAll` and `getElementById` only return nodes inside the scene's own root (`compositionScoping.ts`, the wrapper's `__hfQueryAll` and `__hfGetElementById`). A generated root-finder that scans `document.querySelectorAll(...)` and sets an expando on the node it claims therefore never sees another scene's nodes. The eager check flagged it only because `__hf[A-Z]\w*` also matched a property set on an element. Reading an attribute off `<html>` writes nothing. In a 9-minute film these two patterns kept 18 of 91 scenes eager.

## How

In `REACHES_OUTSIDE_RE`:
- `__hf*` is still refused as a bare name, or as a property of `window`, `globalThis` or `self`. As a property of any other object it is allowed.
- `documentElement` is still refused, except when followed by `.getAttribute(` or `.hasAttribute(`.

The swap refusal is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added in `htmlBundler.test.ts`: four scenes. A root-finder claim scan waits, a `documentElement.getAttribute` read waits, `documentElement.classList` stays eager, and `window.__hfClaimed = true` stays eager. Passes 3 runs in a row. It fails with the old pattern: the claim scene gets `its script uses __hfClaimed`.
- [x] Core: 211 test files, 4717 tests pass. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, the comment ratchet and comment citations pass.
- [x] Manual: the 9-minute film in `hyperframes preview`, headless Chrome driving Studio, same machine, cache cleared, on the stack below this PR. Eager scenes went from 40 to 25 (the 25 keep instance counters or a shared renderer on `window`).

  | | Without this PR (3 runs) | With it (3 runs) |
  |---|---|---|
  | Preview ready | 3.8, 6.7, 6.8 s | 3.5 to 4.3 s |
  | Longest task at open | 0.49 to 0.83 s | 0.47 to 0.48 s |
  | Playback from 0 | 0.63 to 0.73 times real time | 0.56 to 0.95 times real time |

  Seeks land on their frame in every run, and the median seek is 0.83 to 1.13 s either way. This machine varies run to run, so the ranges overlap.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(cli): a page-load timeout names the script or stylesheet the page was waiting on
body:
## What

When `check`, `snapshot`, `compare`, `grade-compare`, `layout` or a motion shot fails with "Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded", the error now names the script, stylesheet or document the page was still loading:

> Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded while the page was still loading http://10.255.255.1/gsap.min.js. A <script> or stylesheet from another server holds the page until it arrives; serve it from the project instead.

The advice appears only when a named request comes from another server. At most three are named, then "and N more". If nothing was pending, the message stays exactly as before.

## Why

A starter project loads GSAP from a CDN with a blocking `<script>`. When the CDN is slow or unreachable, the page never reaches DOMContentLoaded, and `check` failed before any audit with only "Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded". It didn't say what it was waiting for, so the error read like a tool fault. Reproduced on 0.8.166 with a starter project whose GSAP URL never answers.

## How

`gotoWhenSent` already watches the page's network events. It now also tracks document, script and stylesheet requests that have started but not finished (`unfinishedPageLoadRequests`), and on a page-load timeout it lists them in the error. The message keeps its "Navigation timeout" prefix, so existing classification and hints still apply.

## Verification

- New unit tests (fake timers): a stalled cross-origin script is named with the advice; a stalled same-origin script is named without it; a finished stylesheet is not named. With the helper from main, both fail.
- New real-Chrome test: while the server holds a page's `<script>`, the tracker lists it, and once it arrives the tracker drops it. It waits on events, with no timers.
- `navigateForCapture` tests green 3 runs in a row (18 tests). tsc, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet are clean.
- End to end with the built CLI: a starter project whose GSAP URL never answers now fails with the message above.

title: fix(core): a composition mounted twice keeps each mount's own timeline
body:
## What

When one composition file is mounted by two hosts, each mount now keeps its own timeline in preview and in export. Three ways to get there were broken:

- **Split a sub-composition on the timeline.** The second half's host got a new id (`scene-split`), but its content still said `scene`. Its script then published its timeline under both ids and replaced the first half's. The first half froze at its first frame, and both hosts seeked one shared timeline, so which crop won depended on seek order (forward, back, forward could show a different source moment at the same output time).
- **Insert a project into another whose root has the same id** (two CLI-made projects are both `main`). The inserted mount kept `main` and replaced the page root's timeline, so the host's own animation never ran.
- **Reuse a scene twice** with the same id. This already worked (the runtime numbers repeats `scene__hf1`, `scene__hf2`) and is covered here so it stays that way.

## How

- `wrapScopedCompositionScript` (one place, used by both the preview loader and the render bundler): a mount still publishes its timeline under its runtime id, but it only takes the scene's authored id when that slot is empty or already its own. Inside a mount, reading `window.__timelines.<scene>` returns that mount's own timeline.
- The runtime loader and the bundler count the page root as a mount of its own id (`countPageRoot`), so a mount sharing the root's id is numbered (`main__hf1`) instead of taking the root's slot.
- Studio split and duplicate no longer rename a mount's composition id. Both halves keep the scene's id and the runtime numbers them. Already-saved `scene-split` projects play correctly through the runtime fix.
- Studio insert keeps the inserted root's own composition id on the host and gives the host an element id that is unique against the page root too.

## Verification

Each item has a test that fails on main:

| Item | Test | On main |
|---|---|---|
| Split copy replaces the first half's timeline | `compositionScoping.test.ts` "never replaces another mount's timeline under the scene's own id" | fails |
| Split renames the mount | `sourceMutationSplitAndGroup.test.ts`, 2 cases | fail |
| Mount sharing the root's id (runtime) | `compositionLoader.test.ts` "gives a mount that shares the page root's id its own runtime id" | fails |
| Same (bundler) | `htmlBundler.test.ts`, same name | fails |
| Insert reuses the root's id | `compositionInsertion.test.ts` "mounts a project whose root shares the parent root's id under its own host id" | fails |

The related core suites (loader, scoping, inline sub-compositions, scene swaps, bundler; 512 tests) and the studio-server helper suites (513 tests) pass 3 runs in a row. core and studio-server `tsc`, oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet are clean.

End to end with the built CLI, against the published 0.8.166, on three small projects:

| Project | Check | 0.8.166 | This branch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Split at 3 s, linear bar | snapshot bar x at 1 s / 2 s / 5 s / 7 s | 0 / 0 / 900 / 1260 (first half frozen) | 180 / 360 / 900 / 1260 |
| Split, preview seeks 1, 5, 2, 5, 8, 1, 5 | visible bar x | first half stuck at 0 | 180, 900, 360, 900, 1440, 180, 900 |
| Same scene on two hosts, second cropped by 2 s | snapshot and preview | correct | correct |
| Inserted project sharing `main` | HOST y / SCENE x at 2 s and 7 s | HOST never moves | 437 → 287 / 965 → 1265, mount numbered `main__hf1` |

title: chore: release v0.8.167
body:
## What

Release v0.8.167: version bump and changelog.

Long projects preview more smoothly: the preview's work now follows what is playing, not the total clip count. Bundling a project also stops freezing the app that runs it.

## Fixes

- **Core:** Bundling a project no longer blocks the host's thread on esbuild ([b1cf6e3c517](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/b1cf6e3c517e227d1dca1b212e7637c19e502a64), [#5714](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5714)).
- **CLI:** Page loads stop timing out while a busy machine's Chrome warms up ([41486b9725a](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/41486b9725ab2aae4f457d75dcd625931d103bb3), [#5705](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5705)).

## Performance

- **Core:** Hold a clip at 0 inside a later scene until it is due ([13ea8349597](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/13ea8349597bbcb874402d1771aea65766fd7ffc), [#5716](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5716)).
- **Core:** A preview's composition scripts give the page a turn every 50 ms, not one long task ([12d8df37f4d](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/12d8df37f4db8ccf019da32c97cc1352f8db9652), [#5713](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5713)).
- **Lint:** Strip stylesheet comments once per canvas zoom scan ([0bff8342c38](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/0bff8342c389c1841d3b8d858168700f13627e48), [#5712](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5712)).
- **Core:** Preview runtime scales with what plays, not with the film's clip count ([d05bc4215d5](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/d05bc4215d5757da86956217f4a8a4b2ab11b1fd), [#5674](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5674)).

## Internal

- **CLI:** Caption image test checks the close itself, not a reusable file number ([eace3d28b6c](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/commit/eace3d28b6cb721ec1f9a96d7d2ea76bf215551a), [#5707](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/pull/5707)).

## No visible change

Version bump and changelog only. Each change was captured in its own PR.

title: fix(cli): catalog search never waits on installing the on-device runtime
body:
## What changes for users

`hyperframes catalog --query <text>` returns results straight away again on a machine that has on-device search set up but whose ONNX runtime is missing (for example after a CLI upgrade pins a new runtime version). It used to npm-install `onnxruntime-node` inline first. That took about 8 s online and 78 s with the network unreachable on linux/x64, and printed install output (or an install failure) before any results.

Now only `--on-device` installs the runtime. A plain query with the runtime missing searches on word matching and adds one warning (also in the `--json` `warnings` array) naming the command that turns the on-device tier back on, so an opted-in tier never switches off silently.

After a first-time yes at the thin-results offer, the follow-up line names `hyperframes catalog --on-device`. It used to say "run the search again", which a plain re-run no longer completes. `catalog --on-device` with no query now runs the setup (consent, runtime, model, vectors) and then lists the catalog; before, it skipped setup without a query. The runtime-missing warning names the same command. The command is a fixed string, so no user query has to survive shell quoting (POSIX or Windows) or the argument parser.

Scope: this covers the runtime install only. With the runtime present and the model out of date (status `unavailable`, e.g. after a model revision change), a plain query still downloads the model inline, as before.

## How

- `prepareOnDeviceTier` takes `installRuntime`, true only for an explicit `--on-device`. Without it and with no runtime on disk, it warns and returns before `ensureLocalRuntime`, before any model or vector fetch.
- `applySearch` tries the on-device ranking only when the runtime is present. Otherwise the same query would add a second warning ("did not run: the on-device runtime is not installed yet").

## Verification

**Re-tested on 0.8.170, rebased on main.** Packed CLI, throwaway home: on-device search set up, then the runtime removed.

| | 0.8.170 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| plain `catalog --query "mask reveal" --json` | installs `onnxruntime-node` inline before answering | 0.2 s, word results, one warning naming `hyperframes catalog --on-device` |
| that exact command | | installs the runtime, ranks on-device |

The two guidance tests now run the command from the printed line through the real argument parser (citty `runCommand` with the raw arguments). Both fail when a query-free `--on-device` skips setup. 61 passed, 3 runs.

Source run at 5db0f94c, throwaway home: `catalog --on-device --json` with no consent prints the consent message (setup reached); `catalog --on-device --yes --json` sets the tier up in 5 s; the next `catalog --query "count up" --json` answers on the `on-device` tier with no warnings.

**Earlier rounds:**

- Reproduced on 0.8.166, linux/x64: with the model set up and the runtime cache removed, a plain `catalog --query "mask reveal" --json` ran `installing onnxruntime-node for on-device search, once` before returning (8.0 s online, 78.4 s with an unreachable proxy). A fresh install is unaffected (word tier, no install).
- New test `searches without installing a runtime missing beside a ready model`: fails on main (1 failed, 59 passed), passes with the change (60 passed, 3 runs). Removing the `applySearch` runtime check also fails it. The test mock now throws the real "runtime is not installed yet" error when the runtime is missing.
- The consent-check test that used a plain query to trigger the install now passes `--on-device`, the only path that installs.
- New test `after a first-time yes, names the one command that sets the tier up`: walks yes, a plain re-run with consent saved and no model or runtime (no install, word tier), then `--on-device` (installs the runtime, downloads the model). Fails with the old follow-up line; 3 green runs (61 passed each).
- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/cli and the comment ratchet are clean.

title: fix(cli): timeline lists clips nested in a timed element and lint flags ones that never show
body:
## What

`hyperframes timeline` now shows clips nested inside another timed element, and lint reports a nested clip that can never be visible.

Before, a project with timed "shot" wrappers holding timed `<video>` clips showed only the wrappers, each with `children: []`. Every clip inside was missing from the timeline, so an agent reading it saw empty shots and re-added clips that were already there.

There was a second problem behind it. A nested clip's `data-start` counts from the composition's start, not from its wrapper, and the clip only shows while the wrapper shows. Clips written with wrapper-relative times therefore never appear: in a 9-shot fixture, every clip after the first shot rendered black, and nothing said why.

## How

- **Timeline** (`describeProject`): a timed element that is not a sub-composition host now lists the timed elements inside it as rows, recursively, at their real playback time (the same start rule as the runtime).
  - The new rows appear in the wrapper's `children`, and each one points back to its wrapper through a new `parentRow` field.
  - `nested`, `host` and `hostRow` keep their sub-composition meaning. The edit commands use them to bound a sub-composition clip by its host's length, which would be wrong for a wrapper child, whose times are composition times.
- **Never visible:** a nested row whose window does not overlap its parent's gets a warning, for example `never visible: plays 0-2s, but #shot2 only shows 5-10s; a nested data-start counts from the composition, not from #shot2`. The text view now prints a row's warnings; before, it dropped them.
- **Lint:** new `nested_clip_never_visible` in the structure rules. It is a warning in the CLI and an error in Studio, like its neighbours, and it runs in sub-composition files too. The existing `video_nested_in_timed_element` and `nested_structure_needs_subcomposition` warnings say the pattern is discouraged; this one names the clips that will never be seen.
- Documented in the lint reference, with one line in the core skill.

## Verification

- Tests that fail on main:
  - `describeProject.test.ts` "lists clips nested in a timed wrapper at their playback time and says when one never shows".
  - `structure.test.ts` "flags a nested clip whose window misses its parent's" and "checks sub-composition files too". "leaves a nested clip that plays inside its parent's window" guards against false hits.
- The CLI timeline suites (108 tests) and the lint package (958 tests, including the catalog check that structure rules stay silent on every shipped registry item and skill example) pass 3 runs in a row.
- CLI and lint `tsc` are clean, as are oxlint, oxfmt and the comment ratchet.
- Built CLI on a fixture of 9 timed shot wrappers holding 40 timed videos, with wrapper-relative starts:

  | | main | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | `timeline --json` video rows | 0 | 40 |
  | Shot 1 children | 0 | 5 |
  | Rows warned never visible | 0 | 35 (every clip in shots 2-9) |
  | `lint` `nested_clip_never_visible` | 0 | 35 |


**Release notes:** `timeline` now lists timed elements nested in other timed elements, so `kind/index` refs such as `video/3` can point at a different clip than before. Use `#id` refs in scripts.

title: product-launch-video: assemble-index.mjs is not idempotent — a second run drops every approved frame video
body:
## Summary

`skills/product-launch-video/scripts/assemble-index.mjs` is not idempotent. The first run hoists each approved frame `<video>` out of its frame file and **writes the frame file back** with only a placeholder comment (`<!-- approved frame video hoisted by assemble-index -->`). A second run finds no `<video>` in the frame files, so it rebuilds `index.html` with **no footage**, and it exits cleanly without any error or warning.

## Repro (hyperframes 0.8.163)

1. A project with a frame `compositions/frames/02-x.html` that holds an approved video (`data-frame-video="approved"`, with `data-start` / `data-duration` / `data-track-index` / layout attrs).
2. Run `assemble-index.mjs`, and `index.html` has the root-level `<video>`. ✅
3. Edit any frame (e.g. a caption fix) and run `assemble-index.mjs` again.
4. `index.html` has no `<video>`, the frame file has only the hoist comment, and the render shows empty device frames.

## Cause

`guardFrame()` → `hoistApprovedVideos()` returns the stripped HTML as `repairedHtml`, and the caller persists it (`writeFileSync(compAbs, guard.repairedHtml)`, ~line 417). The hoist is meant to happen at assembly time, but it mutates the source of truth, so the operation destroys data on re-run.

## Suggested fix

Either of these would work:
- Don't write the hoist back: keep the `<video>` in the frame source and strip it only in the in-memory copy used for `index.html` (the root-dimension repair can still be persisted on its own).
- Or make the placeholder carry the full tag (e.g. a `data-hoisted` `<template>` or an attribute-bearing comment) so a re-run can re-hoist from it.

A regression test: run assembly twice on the same fixture and assert that the `<video>` count in `index.html` is equal across runs.

## Impact

Any edit-and-reassemble loop, which the review loop encourages, silently loses all footage. The only signal is a blank render, found after a full render cycle.

title: fix(cli): a browser a sandbox refuses says to rerun the command with escalation
body:
## What

When a process sandbox refuses Chrome its macOS mach service, every CLI command that opens a browser (`check`, `layout`, `validate`, snapshots, `render`) now says so in plain words and tells the caller to rerun the command with escalation, outside the sandbox. Before, the user or agent got Chrome's crash line (`FATAL:base/apple/mach_port_rendezvous_mac.cc ... bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied (1100)`), and `check` reported "Browser session never ran".

## Why

Coding agents run shell commands inside sandboxes. Codex's macOS seatbelt (`workspace-write`) has no rule allowing `mach-register`, so Chrome aborts before it starts. No Chrome flag avoids this, and Codex offers no setting to allow it (upstream openai/codex#21292, #14368, #8011). Those agents can rerun one command outside the sandbox with escalation, but only if the error tells them to.

## Related work

Same pattern as the existing launch-failure detectors, `macosOldChromeCrash.ts` and `windowsCrash.ts`.

## How

- `browser/sandboxDenied.ts` matches the `bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied` line and returns the two-line message.
- `launchManagedBrowser` is the one owner of every CLI browser launch, including the GPU probe. It now rethrows a matching launch failure with that message and keeps Chrome's error as `cause`.
- Render launches through the engine, so its error box checks the same detector first, the same way it handles the other launch-failure hints.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `browser/sandboxDenied.test.ts` puts Chrome's real failure text (copied from a sandboxed run) through `launchManagedBrowser` and expects the new message with the original as `cause`. A second test checks that other launch failures are unchanged. Fails without the fix: with the rethrow removed from `launchManagedBrowser`, the first test fails (it gets Chrome's message back).
- [x] Manual: on macOS, `hyperframes check` inside `codex sandbox` (workspace-write, network on) failed with Chrome's FATAL line before the change. With the same change applied to the published CLI, it prints the new message in both places it appeared (GPU probe and `check_runtime_failure`). Then a Codex `exec` run with `on-request` approvals was asked to verify a composition with `check` and fix its contrast findings, with no mention of sandboxes. It read the message, reran `check` with escalation, the rerun was approved, and the browser checks ran (9/9 contrast checks measured).
- [ ] Documentation updated (not needed)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(engine): a WebGPU block mounted as a sub-composition gets WebGPU like a root one
body:
## What changes for users

A WebGPU block mounted as a sub-composition (the snippet `hyperframes add aurora` prints) now gets the same WebGPU handling in render, snapshot, check, layout and motion shots as a block that is the page itself. On a machine without a GPU it renders on SwiftShader with `PRODUCER_ALLOW_SOFTWARE_WEBGPU=true`, or stops with the actionable "declares data-requires-webgpu" message. Before, it failed inside the block with `shaders: WebGPU unavailable (no-adapter)`, even with the opt-in set.

## Root cause

`compositionRequiresWebGpu` decides whether Chrome launches with WebGPU enabled, but it read only the first tag carrying `data-composition-id`, which is the page root. Every caller passes bundled HTML, where a mounted sub-composition's root keeps `data-requires-webgpu` but has its `data-composition-id` replaced by `data-hf-inner-root`. So the declaration was never seen. It now counts the page root and any mounted root. A marker on any other element still doesn't count (existing test kept).

## Verification

- Reproduced on 0.8.166, linux/x64 without a GPU, using the aurora registry block:

  | aurora | software WebGPU off | software WebGPU on |
  |---|---|---|
  | page root | engine's "declares data-requires-webgpu" message | renders |
  | mounted sub-composition | `shaders: WebGPU unavailable (no-adapter)` | same failure |

- Confirmed with `bundleToSingleHtml` that the bundled mount carries `<div data-hf-inner-root="true" … data-requires-webgpu="">` and that the first composition tag is the page root.
- New test `detects the marker on a mounted sub-composition's root in bundled HTML`: fails on main (1 failed, 86 passed), passes with the change (87 passed, 3 runs). `tsc --noEmit` in packages/engine and the comment ratchet are clean.
- End to end on the devbox: a scratch copy of 0.8.166 with only this check patched renders the mounted aurora with the opt-in, and gives the "declares data-requires-webgpu" message without it.

title: fix: hide expired SVG filter output without delaying previews
body:
## What

Timed clips containing SVG alpha-generating filters disappear at their end time. Active clips sharing the same SVG definitions keep rendering after reverse and repeated seeks. Stylesheet-authored GSAP filter.from tweens retain their correct endpoint during sequential rendering, gesture recording, keyframe inspection, live retiming and soft reloads, including short recordings that exit without a reload and cold-cache WebGL transition prewarming.

## Why

`visibility: hidden` hides a filter's input, but `feColorMatrix` can generate opaque output from transparent input. This left a black rectangle after a clip and its parent scene expired. The first fix's paint gate could also be sampled by GSAP when a stylesheet-only filter tween first initialized on an adjacent frame; inline-filter controls had missed that case. The private WebGL prewarm sampler could independently initialize the same delayed tween while the gate was still active, poisoning its endpoint after the transition.

## Related work

CLI feedback 118, reported with Desktop b397 and CLI 0.8.166. The feedback number is not a GitHub issue reference. Addresses review5556493519 / discussion4301612509 and follow-up reviews5557080753 and5558135199.

## How

Apply a final `filter: opacity(0)` paint gate to runtime-hidden hosts, preserving layout, authored inline styles and shared SVG definitions. Finish only newly created own-host filter transitions at framework gate edges; preserve existing animations, unrelated transitions and pseudo-elements. Use the same marker-preserving helper for Studio reveal/restore, gesture previews and live shader scene transitions; bundle it into standalone shader outputs.

During first forward sampling, temporarily lift only the filter gate around root, standalone child and adapter seeks, then restore it in `finally`. Sequential sampling keeps the visibility and hidden-image rules intact. Batch animation reads and gate changes; nested borrowing owns only its own flags. Studio also borrows the same filter gates in the composition iframe before its direct gesture timeline seek, restoring them in `finally` after the synchronous preview writes. Keyframe inspection borrows before DOM snapshots and restores both the timeline and DOM/cache even on errors. Live retiming borrows before schedule mutations through playhead replay. Soft reload borrows inside script execution, covering synchronous execution and both deferred MotionPath callbacks without holding gates open during network waits. The preview raster observer ignores only this temporary sampling flag, while ordinary authored style and attribute changes remain observed. WebGL prewarm samples, their post-paint resamples and playhead restoration now share one private setter that borrows from the canvas owner document and restores in `finally`. Each borrow ends before paint, capture, encoding, IndexedDB and texture awaits. Public playhead and concurrent seek handling remain unchanged.

## Test plan

Signed head `77f6f018ed46b74f362a48751c1053177cc7ca02` repairs the private WebGL prewarm setter. Fresh shader verification passes 67 tests across seven files, including nine new real-GSAP regressions for the live post-transition endpoint, nested ownership, exceptions in all three setter positions and a concurrent public seek during capture. Unit WebGL/capture are mocked; the independent browser proof below executes those systems.

Independent Linux Chrome152 with integrity-verified locked GSAP3.15.0 executes real SwiftShader WebGL, html2canvas and IndexedDB at a local HTTP origin. The reviewed bundle reproduces the exact cold-cache stylesheet-only failure: visible B remains `opacity(0)` after a public seek to3.5, while hot-cache and inline-filter controls pass. The rebuilt bundle passes all cold/hot and stylesheet/inline groups at1fps and default30fps. Twelve settled screenshots have independently decoded expected pixels; the corrected clip is pure red. At30fps, all63 synchronous sample/restoration windows borrow correctly, with zero sampling flags at RAF, blob encoding or IDB boundaries, zero page errors/warnings and no dirty feedback. This establishes the specific cold-prewarm and hot-hydration paths; it does not establish general WebGL cache invalidation, hardware-GPU rendering or encoded output.

Isolated Linux Chrome152 measurements of the exact helper plus GSAP3.15, with63 synchronous windows for a one-second30fps cold transition:100/500 hidden hosts cost0.6/2.3ms median per window (p95 up to0.9/2.8ms),36.8–36.9/152.5–153.1ms total, versus raw setter totals1.2–3.1/0.8–1.0ms. Each host uses four animation scans per window;63 windows produce126 style recalculations, zero layouts and zero residual flags. Two sequential trials per size; capture/encoding/IDB/WebGL, runtime observer delivery and production frame budgets are excluded. Hot cache pays one restoration borrow; steady runtime sampling is unchanged.

Core runtime and Studio sources and executable/declaration output bytes remain identical to the previously tested signed `2cf9bee4`/`1de72c54` runtime. Their evidence below is inherited through source and artifact hashes, rather than rerun. Shader runtime, tests, types and standalone bundle import checks are fresh for this repair.

- [x] Signed integration with exact main `066ca7e20a1612e1f59cb019bc08caf8550d0090`: 558 affected core tests, 69 producer browser contracts and the prior 58 shader tests passed against that rebuilt runtime (superseded by the fresh 67-test shader suite above). The 325 Studio tests across 18 files remain bound to unchanged Studio source hashes; current Studio types and full production build pass. This includes failing-first parser, live-retime and soft-reload coverage, deferred callbacks, nested ownership and exception cleanup.
- [x] Failing-first stylesheet tests fail 2/2 on the reviewed runtime and pass 2/2 with the correction. The raster observer regression fails before its repair and passes afterward, with an authored-attribute control.
- [x] Independent Linux Chrome152 with locked GSAP3.15.0: nine root and six child/source-offset groups pass, including early tween initialization, adjacent frames, jump boundaries and true direct jumps. All endpoints have the expected pixels and zero page errors.
- [x] Current runtime: 28 original-residue frames preserve expected expiry/shared-definition pixels; future-image requests remain zero before lookahead and one within lookahead. Actual HyperShader CSS crossfade passes with the rebuilt standalone bundle. The fresh cold/hot WebGL proof above is scoped separately from this inherited CSS control.
- [x] Failing-first iframe/gesture regressions cover the unrelated hidden sibling, outer-document decoy, short keyboard stop with no mutation/reload, and thrown seek/set cleanup. Actual React hooks in Chrome152 with locked GSAP3.15.0 reproduce the reviewed failure for exactly one and two samples; the current fix and effective base show the expected red pixel after seek3. Twelve native groups assert actual sample counts, same iframe document, zero mutations, restored flags and zero page errors. This is an actual-hooks harness with controlled RAF, not a full Studio UI walk.
- [x] Independent Chrome152/locked GSAP3.15 and MotionPath3.15: 18 soft-reload groups cover baseline/reviewed/final × stylesheet/inline × synchronous/plugin-onload/existing-load-poll routes. All three reviewed stylesheet routes fail; all final routes pass with exact endpoint pixels, same iframe document, no flags during network wait or after execution, and zero errors. Three actual parser groups and six accepted live-retime groups pass after the repair. Earlier failing-first browser packets remain preserved.
- [x] Full Studio Vite/ESM/declaration build and Studio types pass. Core/shader builds and types, published subpath/declaration imports, standalone ESM/CJS/IIFE smokes and normal signed hooks pass. Full PR comment/citation checks pass.

The main integration preserves the upstream structure cache inside the protected seek. A new 24-group native matrix covers public seek/renderSeek, backward and repeated zero, child offsets, same-time steps, callbacks and both keyframe forms. Public seek receives main's authored-order repair. Callback counts and keyframe values match plain GSAP. Capture retains an inherited limitation: backward/repeated root-zero and callback-adjacent visibility match the reviewed runtime, across all six renderSeek shapes. Exact-main source intentionally disables structure caching during capture; there is no separate main-only browser build or claim of full seek/renderSeek parity.

Performance is a measured correctness tradeoff. Fresh sequential Linux runs against this merged runtime used half-size previews, 100/500 hidden hosts with two descendants, 30 yielding frames and two trials. Runtime first-forward medians including observer delivery were 1.6/7.0 ms; the 500-host p95 was 14.5 ms. Repeated runtime frames took 0.7/1.9 ms with zero sampling scans or observer work. First-forward sampling uses four animation scans per host per frame, two style recalculations per frame and zero layout, without observer feedback. Actual gesture hooks took 1.4/5.0 ms versus 0.4/0.4 ms on the reviewed path; the 500-host p95 including observer delivery was 12.3 ms. Gesture borrowing uses four scans per hidden host per moved tick, including repeated/end-clamped times. Parser, retime and soft-reload guards use the same mechanism per accepted operation without a hot-loop benchmark claim. Initial overlapped measurements were excluded and preserved separately. These fixtures do not establish a production frame budget or encoded-video throughput.

The original fix's separate evidence remains attributed to its original artifacts: 56 Linux baseline/final frames, four actual CLI snapshots, and 56 Mac direct-runtime baseline/final frames. This successor has new Linux direct-runtime proof; it has not been run on the original private project, packaged Mac CLI or full encoded video. Local test dependencies are cached GSAP3.14.2/Vitest3.2.4 versus declared GSAP3.15.0/Vitest4.1.11; independent native probes use the integrity-verified locked GSAP3.15.0 artifact. Full monorepo build remains limited by the recorded cached inspector dependency gaps; targeted builds pass. Inline host `filter: ... !important` and `display: contents` remain outside the demonstrated fixture bounds.

## Before

Sanitized Linux Chromium 152 fixture at 2.5 seconds: the expired image leaves a black SVG filter rectangle.

![Before: expired clip leaves a black SVG filter rectangle](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce6d046c-28d4-4059-ae9f-8343c0abccbc)

## After

The same fixture and seek with the signed runtime: the expired rectangle is gone; an active sibling still uses the shared SVG definition.


![After: expired rectangle gone, active sibling still renders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6e8958a5-d6bd-4449-a9dd-8f41bf2ccde6)

title: fix(skills): preserve approved videos across reassembly
body:
## What

Preserve approved frame videos when reassembling a product-launch project.

## Why

Assembly replaced approved videos in editable frame sources with placeholders. A second assembly then silently omitted the footage, including after a failed assembly followed by a retry.

## Related work

Fixes #5733.

## How

Keep root-dimension repairs separate from video extraction. For frames with approved videos, write the video-free HTML to a generated `<src>.assembled.html` sibling and mount that copy from `index.html`. The sibling location preserves relative asset URLs. Source videos remain available for subsequent assembly and edits; generated copies are refreshed, and existing non-generated files are protected from overwrite.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated regression tests cover repeated assembly, failure followed by retry, missing root dimensions, source edits, and video-free mounted copies.
- [x] All 122 product-launch workflow tests pass (`node --test skills/product-launch-video/scripts/*.test.mjs`).
- [x] Changed-file oxlint and oxfmt checks pass.
- [x] Comment citation and comment-ratchet checks pass against `origin/main`.
- [x] `git diff origin/main --check` passes.

The new regressions fail against the original assembler. Source-level workflow checks use Node 22.22.3.

title: fix(cli): capture keeps other screenshots when Chrome refuses one
body:
## What a user can do now

`hyperframes capture` keeps going when Chrome refuses one screenshot ("Protocol error (Page.captureScreenshot): Unable to capture screenshot"). The other scroll screenshots and the full-page plate still land, and the warning names each shot that failed, where the page was scrolled to, and Chrome's reason, for example:

`2/3 requested screenshot files captured: could not capture screenshots/scroll-100.png (scrolled to 8920px): Protocol error (Page.captureScreenshot): Unable to capture screenshot`

Before, one refused shot ended the screenshot pass: every shot after it and the plate were skipped, and the warning carried only Chrome's message, with no file or position.

## Why

In `captureScrollScreenshots` every `page.screenshot()` ran inside one try. Any rejection jumped to the outer catch, which records a single `interruption` and stops. A refused shot is local to that shot: the page is still there, and the next scroll position can be captured.

## How

- `screenshotCapture.ts`: each tile's `page.screenshot()` and the plate get their own catch. A refused shot is pushed to a new `failures` list (`{ file, scrollY, message }`, `scrollY` null for the plate), and the loop moves on.
- Failures that mean the capture can't go on still end it as before: a protocol timeout (`request-timeout`), a closed page or session (`ConnectionClosedError`, or a "Target closed" / "Session closed" message; puppeteer-core 25 exports no class for those), and a refused output folder.
- `coreExtractionPhase.ts`: the screenshot warning lists each failure after any interruption cause, and the outcome is `partial` / `internal-error`, the same reason a failed shot reported before. The phase schema is unchanged.

## What I measured

- `screenshotCapture.test.ts`: a page whose 2nd screenshot is refused still writes the 1st and 3rd tiles and the plate, with `failures` naming `screenshots/scroll-055.png` at 3780 px. A page whose plate is refused keeps all tiles and names `screenshots/full-page.png`.
- `coreExtractionPhase.test.ts`: the warning text above, and outcome `partial` / `internal-error`.
- The existing interruption cases (protocol timeout, target closed) still stop the capture with the same result.
- `screenshotCapture.test.ts`, `coreExtractionPhase.test.ts` and `commands/capture.test.ts` on a Linux box: 52 passed, 0 failed, 3 runs in a row. `tsc --noEmit` for packages/cli reports nothing in `src/capture`.
- Fails without the fix: with main's `screenshotCapture.ts` and `coreExtractionPhase.ts`, the three new tests fail (capture stops at the refused shot, no `failures`, no file in the warning); the existing ones pass.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real Chrome refusing a screenshot. I couldn't make Chrome produce "Unable to capture screenshot" on Linux (several long product pages captured cleanly); the tests drive the loop with a page stand-in that refuses one call.
- Desktop's `app.capture` on top of this; it picks the change up once it pins a CLI release that carries it.

title: perf(core): scenes stop animating after their clip ends, so late playback keeps its frame rate
body:
## What changes for the user

Playing a long film from late in its timeline keeps its frame rate. Before this, a scene whose animation runs longer than its clip kept re-rendering every frame after the clip ended, while hidden. On a 9-minute film with 15 copies of one scene (each with a 120 s WebGL tween on 2-88 s clips), playback from 3:00 drove 4 copies per frame with only 1 on screen, and from 8:00 drove 2.

## Cause

`seekStandaloneRegisteredTimelines` (`packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`) re-seeks every registered scene timeline on every frame, clamped only to the timeline's own length. A clip is hidden after its end, but its timeline kept moving until its own animation finished, so hidden scenes' `onUpdate` work kept running.

## Fix

Cap the time the loop hands each scene at its host clip's end (`start + resolveDurationForElement(host)`, the same resolver that decides the clip's visibility). Before the clip ends nothing changes; after it, the scene rests at its end state and GSAP skips the re-render because the time no longer moves. A host with no resolvable length keeps today's behaviour.

## What I measured

Studio preview of the 9-minute film, headless Chrome on a shared Linux box, same 6 s window per position, 3 runs per side alternating, each run checked to be serving the intended runtime. Full tables in the comment below.

| Play from | before fps (3 runs) | after fps (3 runs) | WebGL/canvas CPU per 6 s, before -> after (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3:00 | 5.7 / 6.8 / 8.3 | 8.3 / 28.7 / 35.2 | 1876-2395 -> 346-927 |
| 8:00 | 8.7 / 5.8 / 7.7 | 14.8 / 8.5 / 38.3 | 1707-1882 -> 374-1031 |

The box ran at a load of 10-30 on 8 cores from other jobs, so fps moves with load; the CPU column is the steadier signal. Seek times are unchanged by this PR.

## Test

`init.subCompositionPlacement.test.ts`: "rests a scene's longer animation at its clip's end, where the clip hides". A 2 s clip with an 8 s tween: at 5 s the clip is hidden, the tween rests at its clip-end value (25, not 50), and a later seek runs no `onUpdate`. Fails without the fix (`expected 50 to be 25`), passes 3 runs in a row with it. The 15 neighbouring runtime test files pass (579 tests), plus `tsc`, `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint`.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Rendering (producer) output: the change is in the shared seek path, so a render seeks the same way; the clip is hidden at those times either way.
- Timelines nested into the root by the runtime: the root never propagates into them (they are kept paused), so this loop is their only driver.

title: fix(engine): exports carry full colour tags with every encoder, SDR and HDR
body:
## What changes for users

MP4/MOV exports encoded with VideoToolbox (macOS `--gpu`, or a macOS FFmpeg without libx264) now carry their full colour description:
- **SDR:** before, tagged `color_space=bt709` but `color_transfer` and `color_primaries` `unknown`, so players guessed and could show a colour cast. Now `bt709,bt709,bt709`.
- **HDR:** before, tagged `bt2020nc` but transfer and primaries `unknown`, so players treated the export as SDR. Now `bt2020nc`, `smpte2084` (PQ) or `arib-std-b67` (HLG), `bt2020`.

libx264 and libx265 exports were already fully tagged and are unchanged.

## Root cause

The encoders set colour two ways: on the frames through the conversion filters, and through `-color_primaries` / `-color_trc` output options (plus x264/x265 params). The SDR conversion only set the frames' matrix (from `scale=out_color_matrix=bt709`), and the HDR paths set nothing on the frames. VideoToolbox ignores the output options and writes only what the frames carry. With FFmpeg 8.1.1 on macOS:
- `h264_videotoolbox` given all four `-color_*` options writes `bt709,unknown,unknown`;
- `hevc_videotoolbox` with bt2020/PQ options writes `bt2020nc,unknown,unknown`.

The fix tags the frames on every path, streamed and disk (so HLS and distributed chunks too):
- **SDR:** both SDR filters (capture and raw RGB) now end in `SDR_RGB_TO_TAGGED_BT709_FILTER`, the BT.709 conversion plus `setparams` tags that ProRes already uses for the same reason.
- **HDR:** every HDR branch, including the GPU branch of the disk encoder and the raw-HDR stream that had no filter before, now appends `hdrFrameTagsFilter(transfer)`. It's built from `getHdrEncoderColorParams`, so the frame tags and the x265 params share one source.
- The `-color_*` options stay; they still set the container tags.

## Verification

- 0.8.167 on linux/x64 with libx264: default, one-worker, low-memory, segmented, HLS and HDR-source `--sdr` renders are all `bt709,bt709,bt709`, range `tv`. An HDR render keeps `bt2020nc/smpte2084/bt2020`. So the report only reproduces with VideoToolbox.
- macOS, FFmpeg 8.1.1, real VideoToolbox through the new filters:
  - `h264_videotoolbox`: `bt709,bt709,bt709` (was `bt709,unknown,unknown`);
  - `hevc_videotoolbox` main10: `bt2020nc,smpte2084,bt2020` and `bt2020nc,arib-std-b67,bt2020` (was `bt2020nc,unknown,unknown`).
- New tests run real ffmpeg and ffprobe. Each encodes through the `-vf` the arg builder produces, with a plain libx264 or 10-bit libx265 given no colour options, which like VideoToolbox writes only the frames' colour, then ffprobes the stream.
  - chunkEncoder.test.ts: SDR; HDR PQ and HLG; HDR PQ on the VideoToolbox branch.
  - streamingEncoder.test.ts: SDR captured and raw RGB frames; raw HDR PQ and HLG; raw HDR PQ on VideoToolbox.
  - On main all 9 fail. With the change, chunkEncoder (103) and streamingEncoder (84) pass, 3 runs each.
- One existing expectation updated: the GPU HDR odd-dimension test now expects the HDR tags ahead of the pad.
- `tsc --noEmit` in packages/engine and `oxfmt --check` are clean.

title: fix(lint): stop flagging dir on <html>; a render test now guards RTL export
body:
## What was wrong

`check` raised `html_dir_attribute_breaks_render` as an **error** on `<html dir="rtl">` or `dir="auto"`, saying render exports a blank video. Agents then removed `dir` from right-to-left projects to clear the error, although the export was fine.

The rule came from #1893 as an advisory while #1934 tracked the real render bug. #1934 was closed with no fix, and the bug does not reproduce today. On 0.8.163 and 0.8.166, an RTL composition renders the same frame as snapshot in every capture mode:

- Linux: beginFrame and forced screenshot;
- macOS: drawElement.

The shapes tried were portrait and landscape, `rtl` and `auto`, a root sized by CSS or only by `data-width`, an absolutely positioned root, a `<video>`, a GSAP sub-composition, and content overflowing the frame on both sides.

## The change

- The lint rule, its tests and its reference entry are removed.
- New regression fixture `html-dir-rtl` renders an RTL page through the real render path and compares it to a golden by PSNR. It has:
  - a block anchored to each side;
  - an Arabic headline;
  - a bar growing from the right;
  - a magenta page background behind the root.

  If RTL export goes blank, or capture shifts with the RTL scroll origin, PSNR collapses.

## Verified

Golden generated in the test image (`Dockerfile.test`). The fixture passes 3 runs in a row. It fails, as it should, in both of these cases:

- the RTL page hidden (`html[dir="rtl"] body { opacity: 0 }`);
- the RTL content shifted by 120 px.

Lint tests pass 3 runs in a row (949). tsc, `format:check`, the comment ratchet, the Fallow audit and the shard plan are clean.

title: fix(engine): SDR content in HLG exports sits at reference white, not peak
body:
## What a user can do now

Grade iPhone HLG HDR footage and export it in HDR without the bright parts blowing out. White text and other page content in an HLG export now sit at HDR reference white instead of the display's peak.

## Why it failed

In an HDR export, everything the browser draws (page content, SDR clips, and graded video, since grading runs in the browser as SDR Rec.709) is converted from sRGB into the output's transfer by a lookup table. The PQ branch puts SDR white at 203 nits (ITU-R BT.2408). The HLG branch fed SDR-relative light straight into the HLG OETF. That curve's input is light relative to the HLG **peak**, so SDR white landed at 100% signal, and everything below it moved up as well.

A graded HLG clip is tone-mapped to SDR, graded, then converted back through that table. So any grade lifted the whole clip toward peak.

## The fix

The HLG branch scales SDR-relative light by the scene light the inverse OETF gives for 75% signal, which puts SDR white at BT.2408 reference white, the same model as PQ. The reference-value generator (`generate-lut-reference.py`) mirrors the change, and the byte-exact probe table is regenerated from it.

## Before / After

Fixture: a 1280x720 HLG clip (BT.2020, arib-std-b67, 10-bit HEVC) with flat patches at known HLG signal levels and thin 3-pixel strokes at 95% signal standing in for small bright text. Values are mean 10-bit luma code values (legal range 64 to 940).

Before (current release), default auto mode (exports HLG):

| Region (source signal) | Source | No grade | `warm-daylight` grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| background (25%) | 284 | 284 | 431 |
| patch (75%) | 720 | 720 | 856 |
| patch (95%) | 896 | 896 | 943 (past peak) |
| thin strokes (95%) | 894 | 894 | 942 (past peak) |
| white page text | | 943 (past peak) | |
| white in an SDR clip | | 943 (past peak) | |

The same grade in an SDR export moves the background by 3 eight-bit steps; in the HLG export it moves by about 37.

After (this branch, same fixture, rendered by the producer in the Docker test image):

| Region (source signal) | Source | No grade | `warm-daylight` grade |
|---|---|---|---|
| background (25%) | 284 | 284 | 253 |
| patch (75%) | 720 | 720 | 627 |
| patch (95%) | 896 | 896 | 723 |
| thin strokes (95%) | 894 | 894 | 722 |
| white page text | | 724 (75%, reference white) | |
| white in an SDR clip | | 724 (75%, reference white) | |

Ungraded HLG footage is untouched. A graded clip still passes through SDR (grading is Rec.709), so its highlights stop at reference white instead of blowing past the peak.

## Tests

- `alphaBlit.test.ts`: the probe table is regenerated with the generator, and sRGB 255 now maps to 49151 (75% of 65535) in HLG. The invariant test now pins both transfers below peak. Removing the reference-white scaling turns 19 of its tests red.
- Regression goldens are unchanged on purpose. `hdr-hlg-regression` passes against its existing golden with this change (0 failed frames, lowest PSNR 31.2 against a floor of 28), and `hdr-regression` is PQ. The HLG fixture's page label does not appear in its render, so that golden holds no SDR content for this change to move; that missing label is a separate bug, fixed separately.

## Not in this PR

- An HDR clip carrying a grade still leaves the HDR range (grading is Rec.709 only): its highlights stop at reference white.
- Studio preview is unchanged. It already grades the same tone-mapped pixels as the export; an ungraded HLG clip only looks darker there because the browser shows it through its own HDR path.
