title: fix(producer): run the real-media HDR and plan v2 tests in CI instead of skipping them
body:
## What changes for you

The four real-media cases in `captureHdrResources.test.ts` (sub-1fps CFR, sparse VFR, non-zero stream start, unindexed negative-base MPEG-TS) and the real-ffmpeg case in `planV2.test.ts` now run in CI. Before this, they never ran there. When ffprobe crashes, the error now names the signal (`ffprobe exit with signal SIGSEGV`) instead of `ffprobe exit with code null`.

## Cause

- **The tests never ran in CI.** Both files were in the producer **unit** lane. That job installs no ffmpeg, so their `skipIf(!HAS_FFMPEG)` cases skipped on every run (latest main: `captureHdrResources.test.ts (35 tests | 4 skipped)`). The integration lane installs the pinned ffmpeg 8.0.1, and the classification manifest already says files that need ffmpeg belong there.
- **Why the MPEG-TS case went red locally.** The johnvansickle `7.0.2-static` build segfaults on one AMD EPYC 7571 test box only. It crashes (exit 139) reading any MPEG-TS input, even `ffprobe -show_packets` on a plain libx264 `.ts`, while `.mp4` reads fine. The same binary (same sha256) passes on an EPYC 9R14 box. The repo-pinned BtbN 8.0.1 build passes on both. The code under test is correct. The error said `code null` because a signal death has no exit code, which hid the crash. That is the diagnostic fix here.

## Fix

- `packages/producer/scripts/test-classification.mjs`: move `captureHdrResources.test.ts` and `planV2.test.ts` into the integration manifest.
- `packages/engine/src/utils/ffprobe.ts`: name the signal in the failure message when ffprobe dies by signal.
- Regression tests: a classification test asserts both files are in the integration lane. An ffprobe test fakes a SIGSEGV close and asserts the message.

## Measured

- `captureHdrResources.test.ts`: 35/35 with no skips, on ffmpeg 7.0.2 and 8.0.1 on the EPYC 9R14 box, and on 8.0.1 on the EPYC 7571 box (3 runs in a row). Before: 34/35 on 7.0.2 on the EPYC 7571 box, failing with `ffprobe exit with code null`, reproduced 3 times.
- `planV2.test.ts`: 64 pass, 0 fail, 3 runs in a row. Classification tests: 6/6, 3 runs. New ffprobe signal test: 3 runs green.
- Mutations: going back to the old message fails the signal test (`got '[FFmpeg] ffprobe exit with code null: '`). Dropping the two manifest lines fails the classification test.
- Engine `tsc --noEmit` clean. Repo comment checks pass.

## Not exercised

- I did not run the full integration lane locally. CI runs it on this PR.
- `audioPadTrim.integration.test.ts` is still in the unit lane, so CI still skips it. Under the pinned ffmpeg 8.0.1, its "keeps the delivered AAC below its true-peak ceiling" case fails: the true-peak corrector lowers that test signal by 4.1 dB, against the test's 3 LU loudness budget. On 7.0.2 it lowers 1.7 dB and passes. Moving it would turn this PR red, so it gets a separate fix.
- Other packages' ffmpeg-gated tests were not audited for the same skip.

title: perf(aws-lambda): build the final mp4 inside S3 with its index up front
body:
> **Draft, parked on a product decision.** This is the measured alternative to the fragmented-MP4 stitch (#5783 + #5784): the same in-S3 assemble, but the output is a regular MP4 with its index at the front, so browsers can start it from a URL. Which layout ships is still open; this PR exists so that decision rests on numbers. Results from a real 30-minute AWS run and from browsers streaming the file are below.

## What changed

On the AWS Lambda path, `format: "mp4"` renders (without `cfr`) assemble inside S3 and produce a regular **faststart** MP4: `ftyp`, then one `moov` that indexes every sample, then one 64-bit `mdat`.

- **plan**: the new `stitchMp4` option (set only by the Lambda plan handler) is locked into `meta/encoder.json`. With it, the plan fits the mixed audio to exactly `totalFrames / fps`, including the true-peak fix, and routes the audio to every chunk instead of the assembler. Same as #5783.
- **renderChunk**: after the usual encode, `muxChunkWithAudio` muxes the chunk with the plan's AAC packets that start inside its frame range (input `-ss`/`-t` at half-packet cut points plus `-copypriorss 0`; chunk 0 keeps the priming packet). The chunk stays a normal, playable MP4. It checks the video and audio sample counts it expects.
- **assemble (S3)**: `stitchMp4InS3` reads each chunk's `ftyp` and `moov` with two small ranged GETs, without reading the media. `buildStitchedHeader` merges the sample tables (`stts`, `stss`, `stsc`, `stsz`, `co64`), rebases each chunk offset to where its payload lands, and sums the durations. Then one multipart upload writes the file:
  - Part 1 is the header plus just enough leading bytes of chunk 0 (downloaded) to reach S3's 5 MiB minimum.
  - Every other part is `UploadPartCopy` of one chunk's `mdat` byte range, so those bytes never pass through the function.
  - The part rule: S3 needs every part but the last to be at least 5 MiB, and a copied part reads one source object. A range of at least 5 MiB is copied as it is. Anything smaller (the header, short chunks on short renders) is downloaded and merged into an uploaded part, which borrows just enough leading bytes of the next range when the rest of that range can still be copied. Every render length takes this path; there is no local fallback any more.
  - Any failure aborts the multipart upload. The SAM template grants `s3:AbortMultipartUpload`, which its `S3CrudPolicy` lacks (the snapshot test pins it).
- **Audio layout**: each chunk's audio packets sit inside that chunk's payload, interleaved with its video the way ffmpeg muxes any MP4. A player streaming from the start reads audio and video from the same few MB, as with today's output.
- **Audio length**: chunk 0's edit list (the 1024-sample AAC priming skip) is kept for the whole track, so the audio shows exactly its fitted length. Video gets no edit list, so its duration is not rounded to the movie timescale.
- **Local assemble** (`assemble()` in the producer) writes the same bytes: header, then each chunk's payload.
- Chunks with B-frames are refused (`ctts`, or a video edit list that does not start at 0). Production chunks encode with `-bf 0`.
- Unchanged: mov, webm and png-sequence, Cloud Run (it never sets the option), local renders, and v1 plans.

I reused the box reader from #5783 and wrote the box writer here. The repo has no MP4 box writer: I searched `packages/` for `stsz`, `stco`, `co64` and `moov`. The only installed MP4 library, mediabunny, muxes from in-memory samples and cannot write a header for payloads stored elsewhere.

## What I measured (locally)

- `mp4Stitch.test.ts` (producer): builds two synthetic chunks with known sample tables, stitches them, and reads every sample back through the new `moov`. Each sample's bytes match, along with the keyframe flags, durations and audio edit list (120 ms after the priming).
- `s3Stitch.test.ts` (aws-lambda):
  - The part planner on exact sizes: borrowing from chunk 0, copying big ranges, downloading a short chunk whole.
  - Abort on a failed part.
  - An integration test with 3 real x264 + AAC chunks (uneven, with a 1-frame tail) through an S3 stand-in that serves ranged reads and joins parts. The stand-in rejects a non-last part under the minimum, which is set to 16 KiB so these small chunks take every path that 5 MiB takes in production. Results:
    - `ffprobe -v error` prints nothing, and the top-level boxes are `ftyp, moov, mdat`.
    - `-count_packets` gives 91 video frames and the audio file's packet count.
    - The decoded frames (framemd5) and audio PCM equal today's `assemble()` output from the same chunks and audio, and so do the stream durations.
    - The local `assemble()` output is byte-identical to the S3 output.
- `handler.test.ts`: a stitched plan assembles through S3 and never calls the local join.
- 3 runs in a row green. Each of these mutations turns its test red: offsets ignoring earlier chunks, the B-frame guard removed, the priming not skipped, borrowing that leaves a short copy, no abort, and the handler skipping the S3 path.
- `plan.test.ts`, `planV2.test.ts`, `assemble.test.ts`: green. Producer and aws-lambda `tsc`, oxlint and oxfmt: clean. `fallow audit`: passes the new-only gate.

## What I measured on AWS (30-minute 1080p30 benchmark)

Same fixture as main's baseline and the fragmented-MP4 run (1800 s, looping 902 MB background video, tone audio, inputs pinned by sha256). Deployed from this branch with `--concurrency 300` and rendered with `--max-parallel-chunks 225` (225 chunks of 8 s, the same chunking as the fragmented run).

| | Today (ffmpeg join, main) | Fragmented MP4 + S3 stitch (#5784) | This PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Assemble, Step Functions state | 81.5 s | 1.8 s | **2.4 s** |
| Assemble, inside the function | download 2 GB, ffmpeg, upload 2 GB | 1.6 s | **2.2 s**: 0.06 s plan read, 2.16 s for 226 parts (3.3 MB downloaded, 2 MB header uploaded) |
| Chrome from a presigned URL, duration known | 1.8 s / 3.4 s | never within 60 s | **1.6 s / 3.1 s** |
| WebKit from a presigned URL, duration known | 5.5 s / 2.7 s | never within 60 s | **3.3 s / 5.5 s** |
| Seeks to 5, 900, 1799 s from the URL | all land | 5 s never lands | **all land** |
| Video / audio duration (ffprobe) | 1800.000 / 1800.000 s | 1800.000 / 1800.021 s | **1800.000 / 1800.000 s** |

The streaming rows come from one session: two rounds with all three layouts played back to back from presigned URLs, order rotated. "Today" is this run's output remuxed with `-movflags +faststart`, and "fragmented" is the same streams remuxed as fragmented MP4. Time to "ready to play through" (readyState 4) is left out on purpose. It also needs the link to outrun the video's 9.2 Mb/s, and on this 4-7 Mb/s link it swung from 2 s to over 60 s for the same file. On every round it moved together for this PR's file and today's layout.

- End to end: 289.5 s in Step Functions (plan 72.1 s, render map 215.0 s, assemble 2.4 s). The plan and chunk stages are main's own; this PR changes only the assemble.
- Measured cost (Lambda REPORT lines plus Step Functions): **$1.62**. 227 invocations, all OK, 0 failed, 0 timed out.
- Output, downloaded and checked:
  - 2.07 GB; `ffprobe -v error` prints nothing. Boxes: `ftyp`, a 1.99 MB `moov` at the front, one `mdat`.
  - h264 1920x1080 30/1, **54000 frames**. AAC **84376 packets** (main's count), decoding to exactly 86,400,000 samples.
  - Loudness -27.1 dB mean and -22.3 dB max, as on main. No level jump at any chunk seam.
- Pictures at 5, 900 and 1799 s are byte-identical to an earlier run's frames from the same fixture. I looked at them, and at the frames each player showed while streaming.
- Players:
  - A 10-second render from disk passes ffprobe, AVFoundation (QuickTime's engine), Chrome and WebKit, with the same frame in each.
  - Streamed from its URL, the 30-minute file plays in AVFoundation, with frames at 5, 900 and 1799 s landing exactly.
- A 10-second render on the same stack (one chunk) assembled in 0.6 s with 2 parts: header plus borrowed bytes, then one copy.
- The stack, its buckets and its log group are torn down, and nothing is left.

## Not done

- Real Safari: safaridriver needs "Allow remote automation" on the test Mac, so the browser runs above are Playwright **WebKit, not Safari**.
- Draft CI does not run; tests, typecheck, lint, format, fallow and the comment checks were run locally (listed above).
- At about 1.6k changed lines this is over our PR size. If this layout is chosen, it splits into "chunks carry their audio" and "assemble in S3".

title: perf(core): a jump posts the timeline its scene mount changed after the frame paints
body:
## What

When a jump brings a held scene into range, the runtime now posts the timeline manifest after the jump's frame paints. Before, the post ran inside the seek-completion barrier, ahead of the paint. The mount's other work (running the scene's scripts, nesting its timeline, redrawing the frame) still runs before the frame.

## Why

The timeline post rebuilds the whole film's clip manifest, and that rebuild reads computed style up every clip's ancestors. On a long film that is whole-film work. The frame being jumped to doesn't need it, but every jump that mounts a scene waited for it before painting. Only Studio's timeline reads the manifest, and it can arrive a frame later.

## Related work

Refs #5719 (this is stacked on it: the held-scene mount and `nestRanScenes` come from there). Part of making long-film jumps paint sooner.

## How

- `nestRanScenes` takes `postAfterPaint`. The held-scene mount passes it, and the scene swap after an edit keeps its immediate post.
- `postTimelineAfterPaint` queues one post for the task after the next animation frame, and coalesces mounts that land together.
- The mount also wakes the transport: its added nodes move the composition-timing revision, and the next tick would post the manifest in an animation frame, which is still before the paint. So while an after-paint post is queued, the tick's posts stand down. The after-paint post records the revision and clears the pending change, as the tick's own post does, so the change is delivered once, not dropped.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `heldScenes.test.ts` "posts the timeline a far scene's mount changes after the jump's frame paints, not before". After boot settles, a seek that mounts a far scene makes no `timeline` post before the seek barrier resolves, then exactly one post after. fails without the fix: on the parent branch's `init.ts` it fails (`expected 1 to be +0`: the post lands inside the barrier). With only the direct call moved, the tick's pre-paint post still shows up as a second post.
- [x] `heldScenes.test.ts` 5/5, 3 runs in a row; the runtime suite passes (84 files, 2091 tests); `tsc --noEmit` is clean; the comment ratchet passes.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: not measured in a browser yet. The time saved per jump comes from profiling, not from this branch.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(studio): one preview copy per video, and encoders stop with the server
body:
## What changes for the user

**One copy per video.** Each video gets one preview copy, at the largest size it is shown, instead of one per size. A smaller view is served the larger copy; a larger view replaces a smaller copy still being made.

**No encoders left behind.** Stopping the preview server stops its encoders and removes their unfinished files.

## Before, on a 265 s 1080x1920 10-bit HEVC HLG clip at playback rate 1.15 (0.8.167)

- three copies made for the one video (17 MB and 20 MB finished, a 106 MB one still encoding);
- the encoder outlived the server stop.

After (measured on the fixture):
- _to be filled in from the same fixture run on this head_

## What it does

**One copy per source, owned by the transcoder (studio-server)**
- **Names.** A boxed copy is named `<source hash>-<W>x<H>`, so the transcoder can find every copy of a source. `resolveProxy` is the one owner of which copy serves a request:
  - the exact copy if it exists, else the source's larger finished copy;
  - else a larger copy still being made, which the request joins;
  - else, if a smaller copy is still being made, it is stopped (its temp file is removed) and one copy is queued at the larger box.
  - A smaller box never starts a new copy while a larger one exists or is pending.
- **Dropping smaller files.** When a larger copy lands, the smaller copies it replaces are dropped from the cache once nothing has read them for 30 s. Chrome refills a playing video by Range request, so a file still being read is kept until it goes quiet.
- **ETag.** The preview route salts each copy's ETag with the name of the file it serves. A URL that comes to serve the larger copy therefore never revalidates as 304 against the old bytes.
- **Cache cleanup.** It recognises the new names.
- **Runtime.** `keepSized` just asks for the larger box.

**Thumbnails use a copy but never start one (studio-server, runtime).** A capture page (a server-side thumbnail or poster) marks its copy requests; the proxy eligibility decision lets it use the video's largest finished copy, whatever its size, but never start one, and without a copy it gets the original. Before, a poster asked for a source-size copy that a small preview then waited on.

**Encoders stop with the server (studio-server)**
- Every running encoder is tracked. On server exit it is killed and its temp file removed.
- This follows the engine's `killTrackedProcesses`, which the CLI calls on its crash path but which never sees studio-server's encoders.

## Tests

Each new test was checked against its change: with the change reverted, the test fails; with it restored, it passes. Every touched suite passed 3 runs in a row.

- `proxyTranscoder.test.ts`:
  - a smaller box joins a larger copy being made, or is served a finished larger copy, without a new encode;
  - a larger box stops a smaller copy being made (temp file removed, also when replaced before its encoder started) and queues one copy at the larger box;
  - a stopped copy is not remembered as failed;
  - the smaller file is dropped once nothing reads it;
  - every encoder is killed and its temp file removed on exit.
- `proxyCache.test.ts`: boxed copies and their temp files are cleaned like any other copy.
- `routes/preview.test.ts`: a URL served from another copy answers 200, not 304.

## Stack

Stacked on the seek-copy PR (#5769). The next PR on top makes Studio read a video's own file instead of its copy, and makes copies only when the page asks.

title: fix(studio): Studio shows a video's own file, not its preview copy, and copies only on request
body:
## What changes for the user

**A copy no longer leaks into Studio.** Studio keeps seeing the video's own file after a copy swaps in. Before, it saw a new source: it fetched the copy, ran its beat analysis on it again (about 2.5 s on the main thread) and regenerated its thumbnails. That froze the page for 3 s and stalled it several times over the next 15 s.

**Copies only when the page asks.** Opening a project no longer encodes copies on a guess. A copy is made only when the page's own `canPlayType` says it cannot play the file, or for the background seek copies the page itself asks for.

**Copies only when the page asks.** Opening a project no longer encodes copies on a guess. A copy is made only when the page's own `canPlayType` says it cannot play the file, or for the background seek copies the page itself asks for.

On macOS, Electron decodes 10-bit HEVC itself, yet the server pre-encoded a full H.264 copy of it at project open (229 MB, encoding through the first 100 s of playback). It now encodes only when the page asks.

## Before and After

A 10-bit HEVC clip from the repo's HLG test fixture, opened in Studio in headless Chromium on Linux, which cannot decode it, so the preview plays a copy. The property panel's source field:

## Before

![Before: the property panel's source field shows the preview copy's address](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4d0d5bac-3938-463c-871c-c85b73ebbdcc)

The field shows the copy's address. Remove BG is greyed out, because the panel cannot find the file in the project.

## After

![After: the property panel's source field shows the video's own file](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/32410e24-8235-4b21-8f48-910d79637efa)

The field shows the video's own file, and Remove BG is available again.

The panel normally cuts long paths short; in both captures the source text is set to wrap so the whole value shows.

## What it does

**The authored source stays the only source Studio sees (runtime and Studio)**
- `unproxiedSrc` (`core/src/runtime/proxySrc.ts`) is the one owner of "this element's authored src". The runtime's clip list (`timeline.ts`) and element picker (`picker.ts`) read through it.
- The runtime exposes it to Studio as `window.__hf.unproxiedSrc`. Studio reads it through one helper, `authoredSrc` (`studio/src/utils/authoredSrc.ts`), which every Studio reader of a preview media `src` now uses: the clip-list builders, the property panel's source fields, color grading, the audio fx readers and copied markup.
- The swap's `src` write is now the runtime's own write (`withoutOwnTimingRecords`), so it no longer bumps the composition timing revision. That bump rebuilt the media index and re-posted the clip list.
- Right after the write, one exact media sync puts the new file on the playhead, including while paused. Before, a copy swapped in while paused showed its first frame until the next seek or play.

**No guessing whether a copy is needed (studio-server and CLI)**
- Serving a page no longer pre-encodes copies. The pre-warm path (`shouldPrewarmProxy`, the `prewarm` flags in `BROWSER_HOSTILE_CODECS`, `injectMediaCodecMapIntoHtml`'s pre-warm loop) is removed. So is its demand telemetry (`recordProxyPrewarm`, `recordProxyRequest`, `mediaProxyDemand`), which only measured how often a pre-warm was used.
- The CLI's static project server and `hyperframes play` reached that path; Studio's preview never did.
- Kept, because they are explicit outputs rather than guesses:
  - publish bakes copies into the published bundle so it plays in any browser;
  - `check` makes copies so it can warn when one cannot be made.
- The light `./player` entry stays free of the parsers: `authoredSrc` lives in its own module.

## Tests

Each new test was checked against its change: with the change reverted, the test fails; with it restored, it passes. Every touched suite passed 3 runs in a row.

- `runtime/mediaProxy.test.ts`, `picker.test.ts`, `init.seekCopies.test.ts`: after a copy swaps in, the clip list, the picker and `window.__hf.unproxiedSrc` still give the authored src.
- `runtime/init.mediaClipIndex.test.ts`: the swap's write leaves the media index alone and puts the copy on the playhead while paused.
- `studio/src/utils/authoredSource.test.ts`, `studio/src/player/lib/timelineElementHelpers.test.ts`: Studio's clip list and copied markup use the authored src.
- `mediaProxyPreview.test.ts`: serving a page whose codec map has HEVC, ProRes and VP9 entries starts no copy. The existing `?hf-proxy=` request tests (`routes/preview.test.ts` "serves proxy bytes with Accept-Ranges...", CLI `staticProjectServer.test.ts` "serves the resolved proxy's bytes...") show a page's request does.
- `studio/src/lightEntries.test.ts` (existing): the `./player` entry loads without the parsers.

## Stack

Stacked on #5799 (one copy per video), which is stacked on #5769.

title: fix(core): pause and play leave media alone that another feature or the slideshow is driving
body:
## What

Pressing pause or play no longer moves a video that something else is in charge of: a video the color grading preview or a Studio scrub is holding while the preview is paused, and slide media while the slideshow is playing it.

## Why

Pause and play snap every on-screen video to the playhead before the regular per-frame media sync runs. The per-frame sync already leaves these videos alone; the snap did not. So pausing while the grading preview held a video jumped that video under the preview, and pressing play in a slideshow rewrote the slide video's position that the slideshow had set.

To reproduce before this change: hold a video with `window.__hf.leasePausedMedia(video)`, move it, then pause; the video is set back to the playhead. Or disable native media sync (what the slideshow player sends), seek, and play; the video is moved to the playhead.

## Related work

Stacked on #5800, which makes play place each video at its own source time in a single seek.

## How

The per-frame sync's rule for which clips the runtime may move now lives in one function: none while native media sync is disabled, and every clip except held ones while paused. Both the per-frame sync and the play/pause snap ask it, so the two can no longer disagree.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: held video left alone on pause, unheld video still placed on pause, no move on play while native media sync is disabled. The two new failure cases fail on the base branch (`expected [ 0.3 ] to deeply equal []`, `expected [ 5 ] to deeply equal []`) and each fails again when its half of the rule is removed.
- [x] Core runtime suite, player suite and core typecheck pass.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: perf(producer): distributed mp4 chunks can carry their slice of the plan audio
body:
> **Draft, parked pending a product decision on the output layout.** This is the first half of the faststart in-S3 assemble; the second half, #5805, is stacked on this PR. On its own it changes no output: nothing turns the new option on until the second half does.

## What changed

A new plan option, `chunksCarryAudio`, lets each distributed **mp4** chunk carry its own slice of the plan audio. The option is locked into `meta/encoder.json` and ignored for other formats and with `cfr`. Nothing sets it yet.

- **plan**:
  - With the option, the plan fits the mixed audio to exactly `totalFrames / fps`, including the true-peak fix. The assembler used to do that, but every chunk now needs the fitted track.
  - The audio artifact goes to every chunk as well as to the assembler.
- **renderChunk**: after the usual video encode, `muxChunkWithAudio` muxes the chunk with the AAC packets of the plan's single audio encode that start inside its frame range.
  - Input `-ss`/`-t` cut half a packet before a packet start, plus `-copypriorss 0`, so ffmpeg's rounding cannot move a cut.
  - Chunk 0 keeps the priming packet and its edit list.
  - Every packet lands in exactly one chunk, so the chunks' audio has no seams.
  - The chunk checks with ffprobe that it holds the expected video frames and audio packets, and refuses otherwise.
- **assemble (today's ffmpeg join)** still works on such chunks:
  - The concat list selects only each chunk's video track (`stream` / `exact_stream_id 1`). Without that, the chunks' AAC priming shifts every frame later by 21 ms.
  - It gives each chunk its exact video length (`duration`), because a chunk's audio can run up to one packet past its last frame.
  - The audio then comes from the plan track exactly as today.
- Unchanged without the option: every format, Cloud Run, local renders, v1 plans.

## What I measured

- `chunkAudio.test.ts`:
  - The packet-cut math on an exact grid.
  - Real x264 + AAC chunks, three uneven ones with a 1-frame tail, and a single one. The chunks' packet counts add up to the audio file's count. Today's `assemble()` on the chunks that carry audio gives the same framemd5, the same PCM and the same ffprobe stream entries (packets, durations, frame rates) as on the video-only encodes.
  - 3 runs in a row green. Each mutation turns it red: concat reading the chunks' audio too, no per-chunk `duration`, no `-copypriorss`.
- **Local distributed render** (plan, then every `renderChunk`, then today's `assemble`) of a 10 s 1080p30 fixture with a background video, GSAP title and a tone, in 5 chunks:
  - Output with the option on this branch: 300 frames and 470 AAC packets, both streams 10.000000 s, `ffprobe -v error` silent. The decoded PCM is identical to main's (same hash, 960,512 samples).
  - Frames: the same chunk videos joined by main's own `assemble()` (video-only, plan audio) give 0 different frames of 300 and the same PCM.
  - Against a fresh render on main, the frame hash matched exactly. A second main render differed from main's first in 160 of 300 frames: page capture of this fixture varies between runs on a loaded box, independent of this change.
- `plan.test.ts`: with the option, `encoder.json` carries it, and the audio is fitted to 1.000 s with peak below -1 dB. With `cfr` it is absent.
- `planV2.test.ts`: the audio goes to every chunk and the assembler. `assemble.test.ts` is green.
- Producer, engine and aws-lambda `tsc`, oxlint and oxfmt are clean. `fallow audit` passes the new-only gate. The comment checks (citations, ratchet) pass.

## What I did not exercise

- An AWS render with only this PR. The option is not set by any adapter here; the stacked PR turns it on and carries the AWS measurements.
- h265 mp4 chunks. They also encode without B-frames, so the same path applies.
- The full producer unit suite has one failure, `audioPadTrim.integration` "keeps the delivered AAC below its true-peak ceiling". It fails the same way on main with the test box's ffmpeg 8.0.1, and is not touched by this PR.
- Known cost when the option is on: every chunk downloads the fitted audio (about 43 MB for 30 minutes) and runs one extra `-c copy` mux (about 0.2 s).
