title: fix(studio): keep a preview reload waiting while a slow project boots
body:
## What changes for the user

After an edit, Studio reloads the preview in a hidden copy and swaps it in once it is ready. On a project that boots slowly (a web font the runtime waits up to 5 s for, many scripts, a busy machine), that reload failed with "The preview did not reload (Composition timeline not found after 8s)" and the edit did not show, even though Studio meant to wait much longer for it.

Now a slow reload keeps waiting and the preview updates once the project has booted. A reload still fails at once on a script error or a runtime that failed to load.

## Why it failed

The wait had three owners with three different clocks:

- Studio gives a hidden reload up to three 15 s budgets (`useShadowPreviewReload`).
- The player's probe gave up at 8 s after the frame loaded (`composition-probe.ts`), and that error went straight to Studio's reload failure.
- Studio's own readiness listener stopped listening at 5 s (`useTimelineSyncCallbacks` safety net), so a runtime that became ready later was never heard and the reload ran out its budgets.

## What it does

- The player takes a `no-load-timeout` attribute: a slow load never fails at 8 s, so the page owns the deadline. Author script errors and a runtime that failed to load still fail at once. Documented in the player README and docs.
- Studio's hidden reload player sets it, and the hidden reload skips the 5 s safety net, so Studio's budgets are the one deadline. The visible player keeps the 8 s deadline, and a retry of it clears the attribute.

## Tests

The three slow-boot tests fail on main and pass here; the author-error test is a control and passes on both:

- `probeTerminalReadiness.test.ts`: with the attribute, no error after 20 s and the player comes ready when the runtime appears; an author error still fails at once.
- `NLEPreview.slowBoot.test.ts`: a hidden reload whose runtime boots after 10 s is kept and its player comes ready; the visible player has no attribute.
- `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`: a hidden reload whose runtime boots after Studio's 5 s wait is promoted.

Run on a Linux box: the two player and studio test files 3 runs in a row (13 and 42 passed each time); the full player suite (555 passed); `src/player` and `src/components/nle` in Studio (2474 passed); player and Studio `tsc --noEmit`; oxlint on the changed files; the comment ratchet. One mutation per behaviour, each turning only its own test red: the probe's deadline check, the Studio player's attribute, and the 5 s safety-net skip.

## Before

Studio on a fixture project, edited so its runtime boots about 11 s after the reload loads (a web font held back, many small scripts). The reload is dropped at 9.4 s with the 8 s error and the old title stays.

![Before: the reload is dropped with the 8 s error and the old title stays](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6091865a-607b-4c6c-af2b-2df2143ed7be)

## After

The same edit: the reload is ready at about 12 s and the edited title shows.

![After: the reload waits for the slow boot and the edited title shows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aca9fa92-0187-496e-b777-1510ba5215dc)

## What I did NOT exercise

The Desktop app itself and Windows. The captures are headless Chromium on Linux.

title: fix(cli): check skips WebGL draws on its box-only seeks so Three.js scenes finish
body:
## What changes

`hyperframes check` no longer runs out of time on compositions with several Three.js or WebGL canvases. It used to stop with "Check did not finish within its deadline." and report nothing.

## Why it happened

Check's text-overlap pass seeks the timeline about 80 times and reads only element boxes. But every seek runs the composition's own update code, and that redraws each WebGL scene. On software WebGL (no GPU, or `--no-browser-gpu`), four 960x540 Three.js scenes cost about 0.9 s per seek, plus about 0.3 s more for the box read that waits behind those draws. That pass alone took about 95 s of check's fixed 120 s budget.

## The fix

The box-only seek (`DENSE_GEOMETRY_SEEK_OPTIONS`) now skips WebGL draw calls (`clear`, `draw*`, `blitFramebuffer`) while the seek runs. It does this through a small gate on the WebGL prototypes, installed by the first such seek. Draws outside that seek are untouched.

A skipped draw leaves the canvas stale, and seeking again to the same time redraws nothing: GSAP and the `hf-seek` dispatch both treat a repeat time as a no-op. So the next pixel-reading seek after a skipped draw first steps 1 ms off the target with draws still skipped, then lands on it, which repaints the scene. Every pixel-reading seek (layout grid, contrast, finding crops, snapshot) draws exactly as before.

## Evidence

Fixture: one 1920x1080, 10 s composition with four Three.js canvases (120 torus knots each, shadows, GSAP-driven), software WebGL, same Mac, back to back:

| | `check --no-browser-gpu` |
|---|---|
| 0.8.169 (published) | 88 s (114 s on a second run under load) |
| main + this change | 16.6 s |
| main, scene draws disabled by hand after the first frame (cost floor) | 11.8 s |

On Linux (8-core x86 box, Chrome 152 headless shell, software WebGL), 3 runs each, alternating: 0.8.169 took 51.5 / 50.8 / 51.2 s and this change took 14.0 / 14.9 / 13.9 s. Both passed there; how close a project gets to the 120 s deadline depends on the machine and how heavy the scenes are, and this pass's share of the time is what the change removes.

Per call, before vs after: a box-only seek went from about 900 ms to about 2.5 ms, and the box read after it from about 290 ms to about 1 ms. Findings are unchanged (0 layout issues, 5/5 contrast checks pass).

## Tests

`captureCompositionFrame.webglDraws.browser.test.ts` uses real Chromium with SwiftShader WebGL and a player that, like GSAP, does nothing on a repeat-time seek. It checks:
- a box-only seek leaves the canvas undrawn;
- the next pixel seek to the same time repaints it, through one 1 ms step-off;
- later pixel seeks don't step off again;
- the page's own draws outside a seek still work.

It fails on main (`expected 100 to be +0`: the box-only seek drew). With only the step-off removed it fails on the stale canvas (`expected +0 to be 100`). It passed 3 runs in a row. The existing seek tests pin the page call's arguments, so they now include the new flag.

title: fix(studio-server): send Studio's history edits to the process that owns the project's history
body:
## What

When a project's history is already open in another live process (for example a `hyperframes preview` started in the background), Studio's history calls in a second host now go to that owner. Studio's edit becomes the person's entry in the one log, and Cmd+Z works, instead of the call failing and the edit landing as an outside change.

## Why

One process at a time owns a project's history (the `owner.pid` lock). A preview server takes it as soon as Studio, or an agent's `hyperframes history begin`, asks it for history, and keeps it for as long as it runs. Background previews outlive the agent run that started them. Any other host that opens the same project then cannot open its history: before #5821 every claim failed with a bare 500, after it a 409 that names the other process. Either way the person's edit is filed as an outside change and their undo cannot take it back.

Reproduced on `main` with the real CLI, isolated HOME:
1. `hyperframes preview --no-open <dir>` (background), then `hyperframes history begin --who=Framey --label=Edit`: the preview now holds `owner.pid`.
2. A second Studio host opens the same project's history: `This project's history is open in another process (pid <preview>)`.

Opening Studio at the preview's own URL takes the lock the same way (its `PUT /selection` and history GETs). A preview that only serves a capture page (GETs only) never takes it.

## Related work

Follows #5821 (the 409 with a reason). The CLI already does this for its own commands: `historyOwner.ts` `connect()` finds a running preview and `previewOwner()` sends each call to its `/history` routes. studio-server cannot import that code (the CLI depends on studio-server), and its port scan only covers 3002 and up, so this PR uses the same pattern with the owner saying where it is.

## How

- **The owner says where it serves its history.** `openProjectHistory({ ownerUrl })` writes `{pid, url}` to `owner-url.json` beside `owner.pid` when it takes the lock, and removes it on release. `owner.pid` keeps its exact format, so older readers see no change.
- **The URL is trusted only while its pid is the live owner.** A busy open puts the URL on `HistoryBusyError` only if the file's pid is alive and still in `owner.pid`. A stale file from a dead or earlier owner is ignored.
- **The route forwards to the owner.** In `withHistory`, a busy error with a URL sends the same request (method, query, body, `X-Hyperframes-Write-Token`) to the owner's route and returns its answer. Only `http://` to `127.0.0.1`, `localhost` or `[::1]` is followed, so the write token never leaves loopback. If the owner cannot be reached or does not answer within 5 s (a preview stopped with Ctrl+Z still accepts connections), the reply is #5821's 409 with the reason.
- **The CLI preview advertises its URL** (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>/api/projects/<id>/history`) through a new `origin` option on `createStudioServer`, set once the port is bound.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (`packages/studio-server/src/routes/history.test.ts`):
  - `send Studio's edit to the process that owns the history, so it is the person's entry there`: the owner is a Studio API served over real HTTP that holds the lock. A second host's claim answers 200 and the owner's last entry is `You · Color`. Then `step back` through the second host restores the file.
  - `trust the owner's address only when it is loopback and names the live owner`: with a non-loopback URL, and with a URL under a different pid, the claim stays a 409 and nothing is forwarded.
  - `answer the 409 with the reason when the owner takes the request and never replies`: the owner's address is a server that accepts and never answers; the claim gets the 409 within the 5 s deadline.
- [x] `vitest run src/routes/history.test.ts`: exit 0, 31 passed, 3 runs in a row. Also `projectHistory.test.ts` (144 passed), `pruneHistories.test.ts` (15), CLI `studioServer.test.ts` (39), `preview.test.ts` (43), `preview.startFailure.test.ts` (1), `history.test.ts` (41), all exit 0. `studioServer.folderReplacement.test.ts` is Linux-only and skipped on macOS.
- [x] fails without the fix: with `main`'s `ownerLock.ts`, `projectHistory.ts` and `routes/history.ts`, both new tests fail. With only the pid check removed, or only the loopback check removed, the guard test fails and nothing else does. Without the 5 s deadline the never-replies test times out at 15 s.
- [x] Manual testing performed: real CLI built from this branch, isolated HOME. A background preview took the lock and wrote `{"pid":…,"url":"http://127.0.0.1:3003/api/projects/proj/history"}`. A second host edited `index.html` and claimed it (200), and `hyperframes history` (served by the preview) lists `You  Color  (index.html)`.
- [x] oxfmt, oxlint, `tsc --noEmit` for studio-server and cli, fallow, comment ratchet and citation checks: clean.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

What I did NOT exercise:
- **Hosts that open history outside these routes.** A host that keeps a project's history in its own process (for example the desktop app's own run and undo calls) still gets the busy error there. Only Studio's history routes forward.
- **Hosts other than the CLI preview advertising their URL.** Only the CLI preview passes `origin` today, so a preview's Studio facing a busy history held by another kind of host still gets the 409.
- **Echo of a forwarded undo.** The owner makes the write, so the second host's Studio may see the restored file as an outside change and reload it, instead of recognising it as its own save.
- **A forwarded call that takes longer than 5 s** (an undo restoring large media) answers 409 while the owner still finishes it; the owner's log stays right, the second host just does not see the result.
- **`HYPERFRAMES_PREVIEW_HOST=::1`.** A preview bound to IPv6 only advertises `127.0.0.1` and is not reachable there; that host keeps the 409.

title: fix(core): a scene paints no SVG filter grain before its start or after its end
body:
## What changes

A scene no longer paints SVG filter output (for example an `feTurbulence` grain layer) before its `data-start` or after its end. Before this, a scene starting at 22 s with a full-frame grain `<svg>` drew that grain over scene 1 in `snapshot --at 0.5`, in render and in the preview. The same leak also left expired scenes' filter output on screen.

## Why it happened

The runtime hides a scene outside its window with inline `visibility: hidden` and marks it `data-hf-clip-hidden`. A page rule (`timedClipHide.ts`) then forces `visibility: hidden` on everything inside it. In the fixture, the host, the `<svg>` and the `<rect>` all compute `visibility: hidden` at 0.5 s.

But Chrome still paints the output of a filter applied to a hidden element. `visibility` removes the filter's input, and generator primitives (`feTurbulence`, `feFlood`, a `feColorMatrix` with an alpha offset) draw without any input. Their output then blends into whatever is on screen.

## The fix

The same page rule now also sets `filter: none !important` on SVG content inside a hidden clip: an `<svg>` clip host and its descendants, and any `<svg>` under a hidden clip with its descendants. Only SVG reference filters (`feTurbulence`, `feFlood`) paint without input, so that is the only filter output a hidden clip can leak. CSS filter functions on HTML elements draw nothing while hidden and are left alone. When the clip enters its window the marker clears and authored filters apply again. No inline styles change, layout is untouched, and the rule is installed once per page as before, so preview, snapshot, check and render all get it.

Scoping to SVG matters for GSAP: a tween that first renders while its scene is hidden reads the element's current filter as its start value. Because HTML elements are never touched, a stylesheet `filter` on them reads the same as on main, whether the tween starts on the scene's first frame or before it, and on any seek order. No change to `seekRootChildrenAndAdapters`.

Known limit: an HTML element with `filter: url(#…)` inside a hidden clip still paints that filter's output, as on main.

`filter: opacity(0)` was tried first and poisoned `from` tween endpoints; `mask` on the hidden host did not stop the leak; `content-visibility: hidden` did, but changes the size of in-flow clips.

## Evidence

Fixture: scene 1 is flat grey (128) from 0 to 22 s. A scene at `data-start="22"` holds timed `.clip` titles and a full-frame `<svg>` with an `feTurbulence` rect and `mix-blend-mode: overlay`.

| frame at 0.5 s | 0.8.169 | this branch (measured at the first commit; the SVG-scoped rule covers the same `<svg>`) |
|---|---|---|
| `snapshot --at 0.5` | 118-220 (grain) | 128-128 |
| `render`, frame at 0.5 s | 117-219 (grain) | 128-128 |
| same scene with a plain timed `<div>` host, over black | 8-206 | 0-0 |

At 23 s the scene shows its title and grain as before.

## Tests

New case in `coreRuntimeBrowser.test.ts` (real Chrome, built runtime): two scenes with `feTurbulence` grain, one at 0-1 s and one at 2-3 s.
- At 1.5 s, with neither scene active, the frame must be exactly the background grey: on main it reads 78-244.
- At 2.5 s the active scene's grain must show (range over 20), so the rule lifts when a scene becomes visible.

Second new case, same file, two schedules: a scene at 2-3 s whose child gets `filter: blur(10px)` from a stylesheet and a `.to` to `blur(0px)` over 1 s, starting at 2 s (on the scene's first frame) or at 1.9 s (before the scene). After frame-by-frame `renderSeek`s from 0 to 2.5 s at 30 fps, the filter must be `blur(5px)` and `blur(4px)`. With an unscoped `filter: none` rule both read `blur(0px)`.

It passed 3 runs in a row. The full runtime browser contract (56), the core runtime suite (2110) and the runtime CI suite pass.

![Before (0.8.169) and after (this branch) at 0.5 s: snapshot and render, full frame and a 4x crop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/94235d0f-2dd2-43ed-8db6-290c2bb227f9)

title: fix(cli): catalog loads registry items a few at a time so a slow link no longer times them out
body:
## What changes

`hyperframes catalog --query <q> --json` no longer floods stderr with `TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout` lines, and no longer quietly searches only part of the catalog, when the registry link is slow. Item manifests now load 32 at a time instead of all ~450 at once. If one does time out, the rest are served from cache instead of waiting on the network. Failures print one summary line.

## Why it happened

The catalog search needs each item's `registry-item.json`; `registry.json` carries only names and types. `loadAllItems` started every fetch together through `Promise.allSettled`. Each fetch has its own 10 s `AbortSignal.timeout`, and all those clocks started at the same moment while ~450 responses shared one link.

On a link that can't move them all within 10 s, every response still queued at that point timed out together. Each one printed its own `skipped item "<name>": TimeoutError ...` line, and the search ran over whatever had arrived. Item manifests are cached for 24 hours, so this hits the first run of the day, a fresh machine, or a sandbox with an empty home.

## The fix

- **Bounded fetching:** `loadAllItems` runs at most 32 fetches at a time through the existing `runWithConcurrencyLimit`, moved from `commands/lambda/render-batch.ts` to `utils/concurrency.ts` so the registry code doesn't import the Lambda module. Each request's timeout now covers only its own transfer.
- **Dead network stays fast:** after a fetch fails with `TimeoutError`, the remaining items use `fetchItemManifest(..., { cacheOnly: true })`, which serves a cached copy (even a stale one) or skips the item. A blackholed network still costs one 10 s wait, not one per batch of 32.
- **One warning:** `skipped 199 items ("a", "b", "c", ...): <first reason>`, or the old single-item line when only one item fails.

## Evidence

A local HTTPS registry built from this repo's `registry/` that releases one response every 40 ms (a slow shared link), with an empty cache:

| | 0.8.169 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| wall time | 10.4 s | 18.0 s (the link's floor: 447 x 40 ms) |
| `TimeoutError` lines on stderr | 199 | 0 |
| items searched (`total`) | 248 of 447 | 447 of 447 |

The real registry over a healthy connection with an empty cache: 0.8-1.3 s before, 0.94-0.99 s after (3 runs each), 447 items either way.

## Tests

Two new cases in `registry/resolver.test.ts`:
- 100 entries with a fetch that yields once: at most 32 are ever in flight. On main 100 are.
- 100 entries whose fetch throws `TimeoutError`: only the first 32 reach the network, and exactly one summary warning is printed. On main there are 100 fetches.

With only the cache-only fallback reverted, the second case fails (100 calls). Both passed 3 runs in a row. The registry, catalog and moved-helper suites pass (335 tests).

title: fix(engine): disable Dawn's DXC on Windows so WebGPU requestDevice succeeds
body:
## What

On Windows, pass `--disable-dawn-features=use_dxc` to Chrome whenever `buildChromeArgs` adds `--enable-unsafe-webgpu`.

## Why

The `chrome-headless-shell` that HyperFrames downloads on Windows has no `dxil.dll` / `dxcompiler.dll` in its folder. Dawn's D3D12 backend tries to load them in `requestDevice()`, so the hardware adapter is found but device creation fails. three.js `WebGPURenderer` then falls back to WebGL2 without an error, and the render exits 0.

I reproduced this on a second machine with a different GPU from the one in the issue (Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26200, NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti Laptop, Ampere; cached `chrome-headless-shell` win64-152.0.7977.30, whose folder holds `vk_swiftshader.dll` but no DXC DLLs).

## Related work

Refs #5775. This PR covers suggestion 1 from the issue only. Suggestion 2 (make the `data-requires-webgpu` check request a device instead of only an adapter) changes when a render fails, so I left it out of this PR. I can follow up on it separately if you want that change.

## How

- A module-level `DISABLE_DXC_FLAG` constant next to `WEBGPU_FLAG`.
- In `buildChromeArgs`, the flag is pushed inside the existing `WEBGPU_FLAG` block when `platform === "win32"`, so it follows every path that enables WebGPU (hardware mode, and software mode with `requiresWebGpu`).
- The argument list for macOS, Linux and for launches without WebGPU does not change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: 4 cases in `browserManager.test.ts` (win32 hardware: flag present; win32 software + `requiresWebGpu`: flag present; win32 software without WebGPU: flag absent; darwin and linux hardware: flag absent). With the source change reverted, the two "flag present" tests fail; with it, `browserManager.test.ts` passes (90 passed, 1 skipped).
- [x] Manual testing: launched the cached `chrome-headless-shell` with the full argument list from `buildChromeArgs({ platform: "win32" }, { browserGpuMode: "hardware" })` on a page served from `http://127.0.0.1`, then called `requestAdapter()` + `requestDevice()`:

  | | adapter | `requestDevice()` |
  |---|---|---|
  | `main` | nvidia / ampere | `OperationError: ... DynamicLib.Open: dxil.dll Windows Error: 87` |
  | this branch | nvidia / ampere | OK |

  In software mode with `requiresWebGpu` (no `allowSoftwareWebGpu`), `requestAdapter()` returns `null` on this machine both before and after the change, so the flag has no effect there.
- [x] `node scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs`, `node scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check` and `bun run --filter @hyperframes/engine typecheck` pass.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

I did not run a full `hyperframes render` of a three.js WebGPU composition; the check above is at the `requestDevice()` level, which is where the issue's fallback starts.

title: fix(cli): a render no FFmpeg encoder can finish stops before capture, not after it
body:
## What changes

`hyperframes render --gpu` on a machine where no GPU encoder works, with an FFmpeg built without libx264 (for example conda-forge's LGPL FFmpeg 8.1.2), now stops in about a second with a message that says what is missing. Before, it captured every frame and then failed in FFmpeg with `Unrecognized option 'preset'` (or `'x264-params'`). The same applies without `--gpu` when the only H.264 encoder FFmpeg lists is a GPU encoder that doesn't actually work here.

## Why it happened

- **The render-time check skipped `--gpu`.** `render.ts` checked "can this FFmpeg encode H.264?" only for renders without `--gpu`. With `--gpu`, the engine uses a GPU encoder only if `detectGpuEncoder` finds one that passes a real encode probe. Otherwise it silently builds libx264 arguments (`-preset`, `-x264-params`), whether or not libx264 exists. FFmpeg rejects those options only when the encode starts, after capture.
- **The non-GPU fallback trusted a compiled encoder.** With libx264 missing, the check fell back to the GPU whenever `h264_videotoolbox` was compiled in, not when it worked. When the probe failed, the engine went back to libx264 and hit the same error.

## The fix

The H.264 decision now uses the engine's own probe (`detectGpuEncoder`), the same one the encoder relies on:

| | libx264 present | no libx264 |
|---|---|---|
| GPU encoder works | GPU if `--gpu`, else libx264 | GPU (any encoder that passes the probe, not just VideoToolbox) |
| no GPU encoder works | libx264 (with `--gpu`, a warning says so) | refused before capture |

- **The probe only runs when it matters:** with `--gpu` or when libx264 is missing. The default path (libx264 present, no `--gpu`) does no extra work.
- **HDR auto:** that mode may encode HEVC, so it is refused only when libx265 is missing too.
- **HLS:** never encodes on the GPU and keeps its existing rule.
- **Dead code removed:** the unused synchronous `detectH264EncoderMode`, which still encoded the old compiled-is-usable rule.

## Evidence

A real FFmpeg without libx264 (conda-forge `ffmpeg 8.1.2 lgpl`: libopenh264, VideoToolbox, Vulkan). A wrapper makes only the engine's 320x240 GPU probe fail, standing in for a machine where no GPU encoder works. Command: `render --quality delivery --fps 30 --gpu --workers 2`.

| | 0.8.169 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| outcome | captured all frames, then `Encoding failed: FFmpeg exited with code 8 ... Unrecognized option 'x264-params'` | `MP4 H.264 encoder unavailable: This FFmpeg build has no libx264 and no GPU H.264 encoder that works on this machine.` with the install hint, after 1.1 s, no capture |

Working paths still render on this branch:

| FFmpeg | flags | encoder used | GPU probe runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| LGPL build, VideoToolbox working | `--gpu` | h264_videotoolbox | yes |
| LGPL build, VideoToolbox working | none | h264_videotoolbox | yes |
| standard build | none | libx264 | no |
| standard build | `--gpu` | h264_videotoolbox | yes |

## Tests

`browser/ffmpeg.test.ts` covers the decision table:
- a compiled GPU encoder whose probe failed is refused, with and without `--gpu`;
- `--gpu` with no working GPU uses libx264;
- the refusal says whether HEVC could still encode;
- `detectH264EncoderModeForRender` asks the configured FFmpeg and probes the GPU only when libx264 is missing or `--gpu` is set.

`commands/render.test.ts` refuses a `--gpu` MP4 before the producer is loaded when no GPU encoder works and FFmpeg lacks libx264. Five tests fail on main. All passed 3 runs in a row.

title: test(engine): process tracker tests spawn node, not shell tools, so Windows runs stop timing out
body:
## What changes

The `processTracker` test that waits for a short-lived child to exit on its own now spawns the running Node binary with `-e ""` (which exists on every runner) instead of `echo`. Its near-twin, which did the same with `true`, became identical and is deleted.

## Why

`Tests on windows-latest: engine-cli` failed on an unrelated CLI-only PR with `tracks a spawned process and removes it after exit`: `Test timed out in 5000ms`. On the Windows runner, `echo` and `true` resolve to Git's MSYS tools. A first MSYS process can take seconds to start while the lane runs other suites in parallel. That cause is inferred: I could not reproduce the stall on demand. The process-tracking behaviour these tests check doesn't depend on which program runs. The tests that kill their child (`sleep`, the SIGTERM-trapping `bash`) don't wait on a natural exit and are unchanged.

## Tests

`processTracker.test.ts`: 7 passed, 3 runs in a row (macOS). The Windows lane runs it on this PR.

title: fix(cli): init writes the project into a folder with a non-ASCII name on Windows
body:
## What changes

On Windows, `hyperframes init` into a folder whose name has non-ASCII characters (for example Cyrillic `Проект`) now writes the project. Before, it exited 0 with no error and left the folder without `index.html` or any other template file. It only wrote the files init creates itself (`meta.json`, `hyperframes.json`, `package.json`).

The same fix covers two other directory copies that hit the same bug:
- the skills mirror, which copies skill folders on Windows (a Windows profile folder with a Cyrillic name);
- media-use recipe import and promotion.

## Why it happened

Node 22's `fs.cpSync(src, dest, { recursive: true })` without a `filter` takes a native C++ path (`cpSyncCopyDir`). On Windows that path copies nothing when the destination has non-ASCII characters, and reports no error ([nodejs/node#61950](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/61950)). The fix shipped in Node 24.15 and was never backported to 22.x; 22.23.1 still has it. Passing any `filter` routes the copy through Node's JS implementation, which handles these paths. `compare.ts` already passes a filter and was unaffected.

## The fix

- `utils/copyDir.ts`: `copyDirSync(src, dest, options)` always passes a filter. `init` and the Windows skills mirror use it.
- `media-use/lib/recipe-store.mjs`: its two recursive copies pass the same filter inline. The file stays self-contained because `skills/media-use` ships a byte-identical copy (the mirror parity check passes).

## Evidence

GitHub's `windows-latest` runner on Node 22, with the new test pushed on top of main without the fix:
`Tests on windows-latest: engine-cli` fails `init.nonAsciiPath.test.ts > scaffolds the template into a folder with a Cyrillic name` with `expected false to be true` at the `index.html` check. The other 347 CLI test files pass. This PR's own Windows lane runs the same test with the fix.

On macOS the bug doesn't occur (0.8.170 scaffolds `Проект` fully), so the test is green there either way.

## Tests

New `commands/init.nonAsciiPath.test.ts` runs `init` into `<tmp>/Проект` and checks that `index.html` and `hyperframes.json` exist. The existing init, media-use and mirror-parity tests pass.

title: fix(cli): check never hangs inside an agent's macOS sandbox
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` (and every other command that opens a browser) no longer hangs when an agent runs it inside Codex's macOS sandbox (`workspace-write`, the seatbelt). Before this, about one run in four never returned: no Chrome left, nothing printed after the compile step, and SIGTERM did not stop it. The agent was left quoting the last error it saw, `Protocol error (Target.setDiscoverTargets): Target closed`.

## Why

Two things combine inside the seatbelt.

1. `browserGpuMode: auto` starts a GPU probe Chrome with Metal flags. The seatbelt kills that Chrome every time (30 of 30 launches in a loop, SIGTRAP or SIGSEGV), so the probe can only fail there. Normally it fails cleanly in about 0.1 s and the command goes on in software.
2. Sometimes the probe Chrome dies just after puppeteer's `Target.setAutoAttach` was answered. Puppeteer then waits for its initial targets on a deferred that nothing settles: no timeout, and a closed connection does not reject it (`TargetManager` `#initializeDeferred`, puppeteer-core 25.8 through 25.14, the latest). `puppeteer.launch()` never resolves or rejects, and no timer or child is left to wake the process. The CLI's shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM waits for pending launches, so it waited forever too.

Repro on 0.8.169 and 0.8.170 (macOS arm64, a fresh `init --example warm-grain` project):

```sh
codex sandbox -c sandbox_mode='"workspace-write"' -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -- hyperframes check
```

5 of 6 runs finish; the other hangs indefinitely. With traces in puppeteer, the hung run's last lines were `setAutoAttach answered; awaiting initial targets`, then `chrome exit null SIGTRAP`, then nothing.

## Related work

Refs #5781 and #5734, which made Chrome start inside the seatbelt as one process over a pipe and name the refusal. This PR fixes the probe and the hang those left. No open PR touches browser startup; #5558 changes the check deadline, which only starts once the browser is ready, so it cannot bound this.

## How

- `resolveManagedGpuMode` (the one owner of every CLI GPU probe) answers `software` for `auto` when `inAgentSandbox()` is true, without starting a Chrome. An explicit `--browser-gpu` is still honoured as before.
- `launchOwnedBrowser` (the one owner of every CLI browser launch, the probe included) races puppeteer's launch against the launch's own abort signal. A timer aborts it at the launch's `timeout` (puppeteer's browser-start timeout, 30 s by default). A launch that never settles now rejects with "The browser did not finish starting within N ms.", and shutdown's abort ends it too, so a signal stops the command. A browser that arrives after the launch gave up is closed.
- An unnamed sandbox (no `CODEX_SANDBOX`) still probes. If that probe hangs, it is bounded at the probe's timeout and the command continues in software.

Not in this PR: the engine's own render launches (`browserManager`, `hdrCapture`) and the inspector call `puppeteer.launch` directly and have the same unbounded wait if Chrome dies at that moment. I have not seen it there; a follow-up can move them onto one bounded launch.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `sandboxDenied.test.ts` "gives up at its timeout, as when Chrome dies while puppeteer waits for its first targets" (a launch that never settles; times out on main). `launch.noListen.test.ts` "answers software without starting a Chrome the seatbelt would crash" (on main the probe launches). Both fail with their half of the fix removed. `src/browser` passes 3 runs in a row (164 passed); `src/browser`, `src/capture` and the check browser tests pass (657); `tsc` clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed, CLI from this branch, macOS arm64, the sandbox command above with only the project and the HyperFrames cache writable, network on:
  - `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` set (what Codex sets): 15 of 15 runs finished in 7 s with every check run, and no probe Chrome started.
  - `CODEX_SANDBOX` unset: 6 of 6 finished in 7-8 s, the probe failing cleanly to software.
  - Outside the sandbox: the probe still answers `hardware` (Apple M5 Pro, ANGLE Metal).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": none added; `launch.ts` is at its comment share, so the reason lives in the helper's name (`untilLaunchOrAbort`) and here.

title: fix(lint): back-to-back audio clips no longer count as overlapping after float rounding
body:
## What

`lint` and `check` no longer warn `duplicate_audio_track` for audio clips placed end to end on one track when the first clip's start plus duration only lands past the next start because of float rounding. For example, a clip at `data-start="21.03" data-duration="0.1"` followed by one at `data-start="21.13"` used to be reported as layered audio ("a.mp3 at 21.03-21.1s, a.mp3 at 21.13-26.1s"), because `21.03 + 0.1` is `21.130000000000003`.

## Why

The rule compared raw float ends: `a.start < b.end && b.start < a.end`. Any end that rounds a step past the next start counts as overlap. In the reported pattern (music cut at 21.03 s and laid back to back), 712 of the 3,000 two-decimal durations from 0.01 to 30 s produce such an end. The warning then sends authors and agents to "fix" a timeline that plays correctly, and trains them to ignore the real overlap warning.

Reproduced on 0.8.170: a project with `0-21.03`, `21.03-21.13` and `21.13-26.13` on track 9 gets the warning.

## Related work

None found (searched open PRs and issues for duplicate_audio_track and audio overlap).

## How

- Core already owns "one instant" comparisons for clip times: `instantTolerance`, `sameInstant` and the span helpers in `clipFacts.ts`, used by the runtime and the timeline commands. Lint cannot import core (core depends on lint), so those helpers move unchanged to a new `@hyperframes/parsers/time-spans` subpath. Both packages already depend on parsers, and the runtime already imports parsers subpaths.
- `clipFacts.ts` re-exports them, so every existing import keeps working.
- The rule uses `spansOverlap`, so ends within one instant of the next start do not overlap, and a real overlap still warns.
- The subpath is registered in `package-subpaths.json` and synced to `package.json` with `bun run sync:package-subpaths`; tsup builds it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `project.test.ts` "stays quiet for back-to-back clips whose start plus duration only rounds past the next start" fails on main (the warning is reported) and passes here, 3 runs in a row (61 passed). The existing "warns when audible videos overlap on one track" still passes.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the CLI from this branch runs `lint` on the reproducing project with no `duplicate_audio_track` (3 warnings, down from 4). Moving the third clip to start at 21.10 (0.03 s of real overlap) still warns.
- [x] Also run: core `src/runtime` and `clipFacts` (2121 passed), the runtime CI suite (`test:hyperframe-runtime-ci`), CLI `src/timeline` (113 passed), `tsc` for parsers, lint, core and cli, `check:package-cycles` and `check:package-subpaths`.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": the moved helpers keep their comments; the test says why its numbers matter.

title: fix(core): name the selector when a scoped GSAP target matches nothing
body:
## What

When a GSAP selector inside a sub-composition matches nothing, the `hyperframes check` warning now names the selector:

```
⚠ console_warning: GSAP target [data-part="reco-title"] not found. https://gsap.com
```

instead of `GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com`.

## Why

The empty name makes the warning not actionable: in a composition with several tweens there is no way to tell which target missed (request 1 in #5687).

## Related work

Refs #5687. This covers request 1 only (selector text in the message); the `--strict` escalation and a dedicated rule code (requests 2 and 3) are not part of this PR.

## How

`__hfResolveGsapTarget` in `packages/core/src/compiler/compositionScoping.ts` turns a string (or array of strings) into the in-scope elements before GSAP sees it. GSAP 3.15 builds the warning as `"GSAP target " + targets + " not found"` (`gsap-core.js`, Tween constructor), so an empty array prints as an empty string.

When the resolved list is empty, the resolver still returns an empty array (nothing outside the composition gets targeted), but that array's `toString()` returns the authored target. The non-empty path is unchanged.

The two `GSAP target  not found` lines that follow the named one come from GSAP itself (the `fromTo` from-state `set` on the already-empty `_targets`). A root composition with the same `fromTo` and no scoping prints the same three lines, so after this change a sub-composition matches root behavior.

## Test plan

Reproduction project: root `index.html` + one sub-composition (`compositions/reco.html`) with `tl.fromTo('[data-part="reco-title"]', ...)` against an element that only has `class="reco-title"`. Ran `npx tsx src/cli.ts check <proj> --no-contrast` from `packages/cli` on Windows 11.

**Before** (main `e9181d0`):
```
Runtime
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com
```

**After**:
```
Runtime
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target [data-part="reco-title"] not found. https://gsap.com
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com
  ⚠ console_warning: GSAP target  not found. https://gsap.com
```

Same `fromTo` in a root composition (no scoping), for comparison: the same three lines as **After**.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: new test in `compositionScoping.test.ts`. The resolved target is empty, `String(target)` is the selector, and a matching element in another composition is not targeted. The test fails on main and passes with the change. `npx vitest run src/compiler/compositionScoping.test.ts`: 79 passed.
- [x] Manual testing performed (reproduction above)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

`npx vitest run src/compiler` in `packages/core`: 564 passed, 2 failed. The 2 failures are the `htmlBundler.test.ts` symlink tests (`EPERM: operation not permitted, symlink`, Windows without symlink privilege), and they fail the same way on main. `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `bun run typecheck` (core), `node scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` and `node scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs` are clean.

title: fix(cli): capture works inside an agent's macOS sandbox
body:
## What

`hyperframes capture <url>` works when an agent runs it inside Codex's macOS sandbox (`workspace-write`, the seatbelt). Before this, capture there wrote no screenshots and no assets. Simple pages failed with `Page.captureScreenshot: Unable to capture screenshot`. Heavier pages stalled in core extraction until `Runtime.evaluate timed out. Increase protocolTimeout`.

## Why

Inside the seatbelt Chrome must run as one process over a pipe (#5781): child processes cannot register their mach port, so there is no GPU process. Check and snapshot launch with the engine's software flags, which include `--disable-gpu-compositing`, so they composite on the CPU and work. Capture's own flags (`captureBrowserArgs`) leave GPU compositing on. A single-process Chrome with GPU compositing and no GPU process never produces a frame, so every screenshot fails.

Bisected in the seatbelt with a single-process pipe launch and one `page.screenshot()`:

| Chrome flags | Screenshot |
|---|---|
| none | ok |
| `--use-angle=swiftshader` (capture's) | Unable to capture screenshot |
| capture's flags | Unable to capture screenshot |
| capture's flags + `--disable-gpu-compositing` | ok (3 of 3) |

Outside the sandbox the same flags screenshot fine.

## Related work

Refs #5781 (one-process launch in the seatbelt) and #5836 (no GPU probe there, bounded launches). No open PR touches capture's launch.

## How

`oneProcessOverPipe()` (`sandboxDenied.ts`) is the one place every launch inside the seatbelt goes through: capture, check, snapshot and the GPU probe. It now adds `--disable-gpu-compositing` alongside `--single-process`, each only when missing. Launches outside the sandbox are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests updated: the four tests that pin the seatbelt launch's arguments (`sandboxDenied.test.ts` ×2, `launch.noListen.test.ts`, `captureCompositionFrame.browserFallback.test.ts`) now expect `--disable-gpu-compositing`. All four fail with the previous `oneProcessOverPipe`. `src/browser` and `src/capture` pass 3 runs in a row (631 passed); `tsc` clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed, macOS arm64, the reporter's command shape `capture <url> -o <dir> --json --skip-vision --timeout 120000` inside `codex sandbox` with network on and only the project and the HyperFrames cache writable:

| | 0.8.170 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| example.com | failed in 17 s, 0 screenshots | ok in 10 s, 2 screenshots (2 of 2 runs) |
| hyperframes.heygen.com | failed in 137 s on the protocol timeout, 0 screenshots | ok in 57-59 s, 3 screenshots (2 of 2 runs), WebGL hero rendered |
| hyperframes.heygen.com outside the sandbox | ok in 36 s | ok in 34 s |

- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": one doc line reworded to name the third constraint; no lines added.

title: fix(producer): render inside an agent's macOS sandbox no longer dies on uptime
body:
## What

`hyperframes render` inside an agent's macOS sandbox (Codex `workspace-write`, the seatbelt) now ends with the message that says what to do: "The browser can't start inside this sandbox ... Rerun this command with escalation, outside the sandbox." Before this, every render there died earlier with `A system error occurred: uv_uptime returned EPERM (operation not permitted)` and a suggestion to try `--docker`, which does not help.

## Why

Each render stamps its temp work dir with an owner (`renderDirOwner.ts`), so a later render can reclaim the dirs of renders that died. The stamp records a boot identity: `/proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id` where it exists, otherwise the boot time derived from `os.uptime()`. The `/proc` read was wrapped in `attempt()`, but the `uptime()` fallback was not. macOS has no `/proc`, and the seatbelt refuses `uptime` (`uv_uptime` EPERM), so the stamp threw and the render failed before it reached Chrome.

Without a boot time, an owner record only loses the reboot check. A dead owner is still reclaimed, and a live process that reused the pid is still left alone.

Repro on 0.8.170, macOS arm64:

```sh
codex sandbox -c sandbox_mode='"workspace-write"' -c sandbox_workspace_write.network_access=true -- hyperframes render -o out.mp4
```

## Related work

Refs #5734, which added the "rerun outside the sandbox" message this now reaches. Making render itself run inside the seatbelt (one process over a pipe, as check, snapshot and capture now do) is a separate decision and not in this PR.

## How

The `uptime()` fallback goes through the same `attempt()` as the `/proc` read, so `boot` is left out when neither is available.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `renderDirOwner.sandbox.test.ts` creates a render work dir with `uptime()` throwing EPERM and the `/proc` boot id missing (so it takes the same path on Linux CI). It fails on main with the uptime error and passes 3 runs in a row with the fix; the existing `renderDirOwner.test.ts` still passes.
- [x] Manual testing performed: from this branch, the render above inside the sandbox now fails with Chrome's sandbox remediation ("Rerun this command with escalation, outside the sandbox"), not the uptime error. Outside the sandbox the same project renders as before.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": none added.

title: fix(cli): check, snapshot and Studio read project text as UTF-8
body:
## What

`hyperframes check`, `snapshot` and Studio read a project's HTML, CSS, JS and JSON as UTF-8. Before this, accented and non-Latin text in check and snapshot stills could come out garbled (`è` as `Ã¨`, `✓` as `âœ“`, `太阳系` as `å¤ªé˜³ç³»`), even in a page with `<meta charset="UTF-8">` and even when written as HTML entities. Text a script created at runtime was fine. The rendered MP4 of the same project was always correct.

## Why

The preview servers take their `Content-Type` from the shared MIME table (`studio-server/src/helpers/mime.ts`), which had no charset for text types. Without a charset in the header, Chrome uses a `<meta charset>` only when it finds one in the first 1024 bytes or inside `<head>`. Otherwise it decodes the page as windows-1252.

Measured on a no-charset `text/html` response:

| page layout | decoded as |
|---|---|
| meta first in `<head>` | UTF-8 |
| 600 KB of `<style>` in `<head>`, then the meta | UTF-8 |
| meta in `<body>` after 2 KB of head | windows-1252 |
| no meta | windows-1252 |

With `charset=utf-8` in the header, all four decode as UTF-8.

That covers the field report on 0.8.181 ("static text with meta charset UTF-8 and HTML entities shows mojibake, text created by JS is fine"):

- **Static text and entities.** Snapshot serves the project re-serialized into one page, and that turns `è` into a literal `è`. So an entity garbles just like a raw `è` once the page decodes as windows-1252.
- **Text from scripts.** A script that writes `"è"` produces the right character whatever the page encoding is.

Reproduced on 0.8.181 with a project whose `<meta charset>` sits in `<body>`: snapshot shows `CafÃ© Ã¨ Ã¹ âœ“` for both the raw and the entity line. The same snapshot from this branch shows `Café è ù ✓`, also when the loopback listen is refused (the desktop app's sandbox, where pages are answered in-process with the same headers). `render` of the same project is correct on 0.8.181 and here: its file server (`engine/src/services/fileServer.ts`) already sends `charset=utf-8`, so preview now matches render.

## How

- The shared MIME table carries `; charset=utf-8` for `.html`, `.css`, `.js`, `.mjs` and `.json`, matching the engine's table.
- Two headers that were hard-coded go through the table too: the root page in `staticProjectServer.ts` and Studio's runtime script in `studioServer.ts`.
- `play` decides whether an asset is text by its media type without parameters (`application/json; charset=utf-8` is still JSON), so a same-size, same-mtime edit to a JSON asset keeps its content-hash ETag and is served fresh.

Behaviour change: a page that declares a non-UTF-8 `<meta charset>` (for example `shift_jis`) is now decoded as UTF-8 in check, snapshot and Studio, because the header charset outranks the meta. Render already did this, so stills and export now agree.

## Test plan

- [x] `staticProjectServer.charset.browser.test.ts` (new): a page whose `<meta charset>` is outside `<head>` and past the first 1024 bytes, served through the static server snapshot uses, decodes as UTF-8 and shows `Café è ù ✓`. With the charset taken out of the table it fails with `windows-1252`. Passes 3 runs in a row.
- [x] `play.test.ts` (new case): a same-size, same-mtime edit to a `.json` asset gets 200 with the new body, and the asset is labelled `application/json; charset=utf-8`. With the old exact-string comparison it fails with 304.
- [x] `staticProjectServer.test.ts` "labels the page and its scripts UTF-8…" fails on main (`text/html`) and passes with the fix. `studioServer.file-race.test.ts` expectations updated for the runtime script and `assets/main.js`.
- [x] Manual: the field-report shape (accents, `✓`, entities, meta charset in `<body>`), snapshot and render on 0.8.181 and on this branch, as above.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": one line in the new test.

title: fix(cli): check and snapshot keep their record while another app has the history open
body:
## What

`hyperframes check`, `snapshot` and `render` keep their record (check report, snapshots, render artifacts) when another process keeps the project's history open, for example an editor app that opened the project. Before, they printed `Check report was not recorded: This project's history is open in another process (pid N).` and kept nothing.

## Why

`captureArtifactRevision` asks the history's owner to checkpoint before it fingerprints the project. With no preview server to forward to, it opened the history itself with no wait, and a process holding the lock made the whole capture throw. Only the checkpoint needs the lock: the record itself goes into `video-state.json` under that file's own cross-process lock (`updateState`), which already happens while a preview owns the history.

So a busy history now skips only the checkpoint. If the owner has filed the current files, the record lands on its current revision; if a change is not filed yet, `beginArtifactCapture` sees the mismatch and the record is unversioned, never attached to a revision that does not hold those files. Any other error still throws.

## What I measured

title: fix(cli): audio and timeline find media the way preview and render load it
body:
## What

`hyperframes audio` and `hyperframes timeline` find a clip's media file the same way preview, check, snapshot and render load it. Before this, `hyperframes audio --dir <project> --range 0,4.5 --only loudness,silence` answered `assets/music%20bed.mp3 #bed: file not found` for a project that check passes and renders with sound. Two cases:

- A nested composition (`compositions/scene.html`) using a project-root asset (`assets/…`), the convention registry blocks use.
- A percent-encoded file name (`music%20bed.mp3` for `music bed.mp3`).

## Why

The bundle that preview, check, snapshot and render load maps a nested composition's `src` with `rewriteAssetPath`: a sibling file next to the composition wins, otherwise the path is project-root-relative. The served file is then decoded. `audio` (`targets.ts`) and `timeline`'s duration probe (`describeProject.ts`) each joined the raw `src` to the composition's folder themselves, with no root fallback and no decoding. `media-treatment` already did the right two steps inline.

## How

- `resolveAuthoredAssetFile(projectDir, compositionFile, src)` in `@hyperframes/parsers/asset-resolution` is the one owner of that lookup. It runs `rewriteAssetPath` with an existence probe (as the compilers do), then `resolveExistingLocalAsset` (decodes and stays inside the project).
- `audio` targets, `timeline`'s media probe and `media-treatment` call it. `media-treatment` keeps its error messages.
- When nothing exists, `audio` still reports the authored path as not found, as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added, both failing on main:
  - `targets.test.ts`: a nested scene's `assets/music%20bed.mp3` resolves to the root `assets/music bed.mp3`, and a sibling `sfx/hit.wav` next to the composition still wins.
  - `describeProject.test.ts`: a nested scene's percent-encoded root asset is probed for its duration.
  - `src/timeline`, `src/audio` and `media-treatment` pass 3 runs in a row (202), and the parsers suite passes (1285).
- [x] Manual testing performed on the reported command shape: a project whose nested scene plays `assets/music%20bed.mp3` (3 s tone, then 2 s of silence). On the current release `audio` says file not found while `check` passes. From this branch it reports `loudness -22.4 LUFS`, `silent 3.007–4.500`.

- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": one doc line on the new function.

title: fix(cli): check and snapshot wait for a slow CDN script as long as render does
body:
## What

`check` and `snapshot` (and `layout`, `motion-shot`, `validate`) wait for a slow page load as long as `render` does. Before this, a composition whose `<head>` loads a script from a slow CDN (GSAP is the common case) intermittently failed check and snapshot with `Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded`, fine on retry, while `render` of the same project succeeded.

## Why

A parser-blocking `<script src>` holds back `DOMContentLoaded`. The diagnostic commands gave the page 10 s for it through their own `resolveDiagnosticNavigationTimeoutMs` (and `validate` had a separate 10 s floor). `render` uses the engine's `pageNavigationTimeout` (60 s, same `PRODUCER_PAGE_NAVIGATION_TIMEOUT_MS` override). Same page, two budgets.

This is not a recent regression: the 10 s budget is the same from 0.8.152 through 0.8.171. On a 130 s project with 30 sub-compositions and 1080p videos the page itself loads in under 200 ms. Only a slow external script reaches 10 s.

## How

- The separate diagnostic budgets are deleted. `resolvePageNavigationTimeout()` in the engine's `config.ts` now owns the page-navigation env read, and `resolveConfig` uses it. `pageNavigationTimeoutMs()` (`utils/renderArgs.ts`) calls it directly, without resolving the whole render config, which could print render's Windows streaming-encode warning during check. The budget is raised only by a command's own longer `--timeout`. A zero or invalid override falls back to the engine default instead of failing instantly.
- `openSettledCompositionPage` (check, snapshot), `layout`, `motion-shot` and `validate` use it. `validate`'s `NAV_TIMEOUT_FLOOR_MS` and its helper are gone, and its comment and timeout hint now say render shares the budget.
- The cold-Chrome allowance from #5705 (30 s for Chrome to send the first request) is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Browser test added: `captureCompositionFrame.slowScript.browser.test.ts` opens a composition whose `<head>` script is answered after 15 s, through the same `openSettledCompositionPage` check and snapshot use. On main it fails with `Navigation timeout of 10000 ms exceeded`; with the fix it passes 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Unit tests: `pageNavigationTimeoutMs` follows the engine default and its env override, ignores a zero or invalid override, and is only raised by a longer `--timeout`. A further test sets win32, software GPU and one worker (the case where render disables streaming encode) and requires no stderr output. It fails at the previous head, where the full `resolveConfig()` printed render's warning. `validate`'s floor test is removed with the floor. `src/capture`, `src/utils`, `validate` and `layout` pass 3 runs in a row (1845).
- [x] Manual testing performed: a project loading GSAP from a local server that answers after 15 s. On 0.8.170 and 0.8.171, `snapshot` fails with the 10 s navigation timeout while `render` succeeds. From this branch, `snapshot` (2 stills) and `check` (passed) both succeed.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": one doc line on the new function, one reworded option comment, one test comment.

title: fix(engine): a 29.97 fps camera clip exports smoothly at 30 fps
body:
## What

A 30 fps export of a camera clip shot at 29.97 fps plays smoothly. Before this, when the clip's container stores timestamps in milliseconds (common for phone and camera files), the export alternated repeated frames with skipped ones for the first second or so. On a 1.5 s test clip the source frames came out as `0,1,2,3,4,5,6,6,8,9,9,11,12,12,14,14,15,17,…`. Later exports of the same clip kept the bad frames because extracted frames are cached.

## Why

Extraction fills each output slot with the last source frame starting at or before it (`fps=…:round=up`, after a half-tick shift that absorbs whole-ms rounding when source and output rates match). Millisecond ticks place each frame up to ±0.5 ms from its true time. A 29.97 fps source drifts against 30 fps slots by only 0.033 ms per frame, so for the first ~15–25 frames that rounding noise decides which side of a slot each frame lands on: repeat, skip, repeat, skip. With exact timestamps the same clip samples correctly.

## How

- For a constant-frame-rate source (not `isVFR`), extraction snaps frame times to the stream's own frame grid in file time before sampling: `settb=AVTB, setpts = (lead + round((PTS·TB + seek − lead) × FR) / FR − seek) / TB`. Here `seek` is this ffmpeg process's `-ss` and `lead` is where the video starts in the file (`videoStreamLeadSeconds`). `PTS·TB + seek` is the frame's time since file start in every process, so single passes, segments and distributed chunks all snap to the same grid. `FR` is ffmpeg's nominal stream rate (30000/1001), not the averaged rate, which drifts on long millisecond-tick files. When ffmpeg has no constant rate (`FR` undefined), timestamps pass through unchanged. The existing half-tick shift runs after the snap.
- `SCHEMA_PREFIX` moves to `hfcache-v8-`, as its rule requires when extraction writes different frames for the same key, so warm caches stop serving the old frames.

## Test plan

- [x] Seam test added: `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` "samples a millisecond-tick 29.97 fps source the same in segments as in one pass" compares 14 segment starts against a single pass. It failed when each process anchored on its own first frame (15 slots differed), and passes now.
- [x] Test added: `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` "samples a 29.97 fps source with millisecond timestamps at 30 fps without skipping a frame" synthesizes a clip whose frames carry their own index as binary blocks, extracts 1.5 s at 30 fps, and requires no skipped frame and at most one repeat. On main it fails with the sequence above. With the fix it passes 3 runs in a row, and the extractor and cache suites pass (268).
- [x] Manual testing performed: real `render --fps 30` from this branch.
  - 29.97 fps millisecond-tick clip: one repeat, no skips (0.8.171: 7 repeats, 6 skips in the first second).
  - The same clip with `data-media-start="0.5"`: one repeat.
  - 30 fps millisecond-tick clip, exact-tick clips, and a 0.5 s media start: unchanged, every frame once.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": none added; the filter is named for what it does.

title: fix(cli): agents can apply a color correction from media-treatment's capabilities
body:
## What

An agent can apply a colour correction using only what `hyperframes media-treatment` tells it. Before this, `media-treatment --selector "#v" --grading '{"adjustments":{"exposure":0.1}}' --apply --json` failed with `Invalid color-grading grading: has unsupported key(s): adjustments. Use only the documented media-treatment keys at the top level.`, and no capability output showed what a valid payload looks like.

## Why

The grading payload's shape is defined once, by the validator's schema (`parsers/colorGradingContract.ts`): the correction controls live under `adjust` and the finishing controls under `details`. The capability catalog (`getHfColorGradingCapabilities`, printed by `--all`) named its sections after the payload keys everywhere else (`wheels`, `curves`, `hueCurves`, `secondaries`, `lut`, `palette`), but called these two `adjustments` and `finishing`. The `correction` capability listed its controls with no `apply` payload, unlike `wheels` and `curves`. An agent mapping catalog names to payload keys wrote `adjustments`, and the rejection named no valid key.

## How

- **One owner of the example.** `COLOR_GRADING_EXAMPLE` lives next to the schema, and the schema's tests require the validator to accept it.
- **Catalog follows the schema.** Its sections are now named `adjust` and `details`, and it carries `example`. `--capabilities` includes the example. `--capability correction` and `--capability finishing` show an `apply` payload taken from it.
- **The hint names the keys.** An unknown top-level key now gets `Top-level keys are "enabled", "preset", "intensity", "adjust", …`, generated from `COLOR_GRADING_TOP_LEVEL_KEYS`.
- **Docs are checked against the schema.** `colorGradingContract.docs.test.ts` validates every grading payload in `docs/` and `skills/`: inline `--grading '…'` and `data-color-grading='…'`, plus fenced JSON that uses grading sections (20 today, all valid). A docs example that drifts from the schema fails CI with its file name.

`--all` output changes two section names (`adjustments` → `adjust`, `finishing` → `details`). Nothing else in the repo reads those names.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added, failing on main:
  - The schema accepts its own example.
  - A misnamed `adjustments` container gets a hint naming `"adjust"`.
  - The catalog's sections use payload keys, and the catalog example, the `--capabilities` example and the correction `apply` all validate.
  - These pass 3 runs in a row, and so do the core grading tests (44), `media-treatment` (35) and the Studio editor tests.
- [x] Docs test is non-vacuous: changing one skills example to `adjustments` makes it fail and name `skills/media-use/references/grading.md`.
- [x] Manual testing performed from this branch on a one-video project: `--capabilities` shows `example`, `--capability correction` shows `apply`, applying that example writes the grading (`ok: true`), and `{"adjustments":…}` now gets the key list.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): existing docs already match the schema; the new test keeps them that way.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": one doc line on the docs-test helper.

title: fix(cli): preview inside a host app's agent run no longer outlives the run
body:
## What

`hyperframes preview` run by an agent inside a host app's run (the host sets `HYPERFRAMES_DESKTOP_PROJECT`) no longer starts a detached background preview. It refuses with a clear message instead:

> A host app is running this project and owns its preview, so a background preview here would outlive this run and keep the project's history locked. Use the host app's preview, or run with --foreground to keep a preview attached to this run.

With `--json` the code is `host-app-owns-preview`. Outside a host app nothing changes.

## Why

`--background` (and a bare `preview` without a terminal, which defaults to background) re-execs the CLI as a detached process (`spawnDetachedPreview`). Started from an agent run inside a host app, that preview outlived the run and the app. After any write it held the project's history lock for its whole life, so the host app's own operations on the project (for example a rename) waited for the lock and failed. The host app already owns the project's preview, so a second detached one has no job there.

## How

- `insideHostApp(env)` in `utils/desktopApp.ts` is the one check for "this run belongs to a host app". `desktopHint` now uses it too, instead of its own copy of the env check.
- `previewHostAppError(mode, env)` refuses only the background launch mode. `--foreground` and the interactive modes stay attached to the run, so they are allowed.
- `preview` checks this right after resolving the launch mode, before the startup lint or any spawn, and reports through the existing `reportPreviewFailure`.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests added in `preview.test.ts`, all failing on main:
  - Background is refused inside a host app's run.
  - Foreground, local and embedded are allowed there, and background is allowed outside one.
  - `preview <dir> --background --json` through the real command prints `host-app-owns-preview` and starts nothing.
  - `preview.test.ts` and `desktopApp.test.ts` pass 3 runs in a row (71 tests).
- [x] Manual testing performed from this branch: with the env var set, `preview . --background` prints the message (human and `--json`), and no preview process is left running.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": none added.

title: feat(studio): the desktop-app button says Install the desktop app and never dead-ends
body:
> **Do not merge yet.** The maintainer reviews this rendered result first.

## What

Studio's header button that leads to the HyperFrames desktop app:

- reads **"Install the desktop app"** beside Framey, drawn as the app draws it, with the app's moods: it breathes and blinks, its eyes circle while it waits, it hops when the app turns up, flies while a project hands over, and shakes when that fails. Its eyes follow the pointer.
- **App ready to take the project:** the button reads "Open in desktop app" and a press opens this same project in the app. A folder the preview serves from a bare `index.html` gets its `hyperframes.json` first (created only when missing), so the app no longer refuses it with "No HyperFrames project at …".
- **No app yet:** a press opens a card under the button where Framey walks three steps:
  1. **Download HyperFrames for Mac/Linux:** opens hyperframes.dev's download in a new tab. The step is done only when the tab really opened; a blocked tab names the download address.
  2. **Install it:** done only when the preview server finds the app. While the card is open and the app is not there, the card asks `GET /api/open-in-desktop` every 2 s; closing the card stops it. After a minute without the app it asks whether the download finished. Meanwhile the button reads "Finish installing" with "2 of 3".
  3. **Open the project:** the existing hand-off. If it fails, the step shows the project folder with a copy control and Try again. If the app is gone, the card goes back to step 1.
- **Linux with the app installed:** the app does not take a handed-over folder there yet, so step 3 shows the folder to drop into the app.
- **No app for this platform (Windows, "coming soon" on hyperframes.dev):** no button, so no one is sent to an app they cannot install.
- The card is a popover anchored to the button. Opening it, every state change and closing it never move the preview, inspector or timeline (measured below).

## Why

Users of the local preview did not find the desktop app: "Edit with Framey" did not say what it does, and a press could end in the app's "No HyperFrames project" dialog for a project the preview had just opened. The app opens only folders that pass core's `isHyperframesProject` (`index.html` plus `hyperframes.json`, `meta.json` or `project.json`), while preview serves any folder with an `index.html`. Sending people to a download and leaving them there also lost them between the download and the app: the card keeps the next step in view until the project is open.

## How

- `openInDesktop` (every hand-off goes through it: this button and `hyperframes open`) adds `hyperframes.json` with the existing no-overwrite `createProjectConfig` when the folder has `index.html` but fails core's project rule.
- `GET /api/open-in-desktop` says `handoff: true` only where the app is installed and can take a project, and adds `os` and `installed`. The card's install step reads the same route; nothing new on the server.
- `OpenInDesktopButton.tsx` owns the route, telemetry, the install check and the hand-off; `DesktopGuideCard.tsx` draws the card from one `Progress` value (label, Framey's mood and each step's state derive from it). Both use Studio's `Popover`, `Button` and tokens.
- `FrameyGlyph` takes an optional `mood`; the moods' motion is in `components.css`, with a reduced-motion path.
- Telemetry goes through the existing `trackStudioEvent` only.

## Telemetry contract

Every event also carries the session properties `trackStudioEvent` already adds, including `studio_version` and `tab_id` (a random id per page load).

Context properties on every event below: `os` (the preview server's platform: `darwin` / `linux` / `win32`), `app_installed` (boolean), `download_available` (boolean).

| Event | When | Extra properties |
|---|---|---|
| `studio:desktop_cta_eligibility` | once per page, when the preview server answers | `eligibility`: `open_in_app` / `download` / `no_app_for_platform` |
| `studio:desktop_cta_impression` | once per page, when the button is first on screen (IntersectionObserver) | `eligibility` |
| `studio:desktop_cta_guide` | each guide step change | `step`: `opened` / `closed` / `download_opened` / `install_detected` |
| `studio:toolbar_action` (existing) | a download press or a hand-off press | `action`: `get_desktop_app` / `open_in_desktop` |
| `studio:desktop_cta_outcome` | how a press ended | `outcome`: `opened` / `sent_to_download` / `failed`; `reason` when known: `not-installed`, `open-failed`, `handoff-unavailable`, `download_tab_blocked`, `preview_server_unreachable` |

A download is never counted as an install: `download_opened` and `sent_to_download` mean a new tab opened on the download page, nothing more. `install_detected` fires only when the preview server reports the app installed, once per page, even if the app is removed and found again.

**Correlation field:** the page's `tab_id` (a random UUID, no personal data), passed on as `hf_cta`:
- **Download:** `https://hyperframes.dev/studio/download?…&hf_cta=<tab_id>`.
- **Hand-off:** `POST /api/open-in-desktop` with body `{ "cta": "<tab_id>" }`. Only `[A-Za-z0-9-]{1,64}` is accepted. When the app took the folder, the CLI writes `.hyperframes/desktop-cta.json` = `{ "cta": "<tab_id>", "at": <ms> }` in the project.

**Unmatched today:** nothing in the app reads `desktop-cta.json` yet, and hyperframes.dev does not yet carry `hf_cta` into the installer.

## No layout shift

The real Studio build from this branch, headless Chrome at 1440x900, a fixture project. The preview server's answers were staged per scenario so every state could be driven without an app on the test machine. A probe recorded the boxes of the Compositions, Preview, Inspector and Timeline panels and of the preview stage on **every animation frame**, from the settled page through each press:

| Scenario | States driven | Frames | Distinct layouts |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mac, no app | idle, card open, download opened, app found, opening, after | 418 | 1 |
| Failed hand-off | idle, card at step 3, folder copied, Try again, card closed | 182 | 1 |
| Slow download | card open, "Still looking" after 60 s | 3727 | 1 |
| Linux, app installed | card at step 3 (drop the folder) | 49 | 1 |
| Windows | no button | 5 | 1 |

Every frame of every scenario has the same boxes (x,y,w×h): Compositions 3,43,364×494 · Preview 373,43,655×494 · Inspector 1034,43,403×494 · Timeline 3,543,1434×354 · preview stage 395,116,611×344.

## Test plan

- [x] Tests that fail on main and pass now:
  - **CLI, `desktopApp.test.ts` and `desktopRoutes.test.ts`:**
    - A bare-`index.html` folder passes `isHyperframesProject` at the moment of hand-off, and a project's own marker is left alone.
    - The hand-off is offered only where the app is installed.
    - The `cta` id is forwarded only when valid and recorded only when the app took the folder.
  - **Studio, `OpenInDesktopButton.dom.test.tsx`** (16 of 20 fail on main):
    - The copy for each state, and that a press without the app opens the card at step 1 and hands nothing over.
    - Step 1 opens the tagged download in a new tab and drops the opener; a blocked tab names the download and leaves step 1 to do.
    - The install is found only from the preview server, asked only while the card is open, and the asking stops when the card closes or the app is found.
    - A failed hand-off opens step 3 with the folder, copy and Try again; an app that is gone sends the card back to step 1.
    - Linux with the app shows the folder to drop in and posts nothing.
    - Eligibility, one impression, click and outcome properties, and that no property carries a path or counts a download as an install.
    - One `install_detected` per page when the app is found, removed and found again (review finding; fails without the page latch).
  - Breaking each on purpose fails a test: polling with the card closed, counting the download as the install, going back to the old download redirect on failure, and ignoring the server's answer.
  - All pass 3 runs in a row, with Studio's style and token gates and the header tests.
- [x] Built and run for real: the branch's Studio and CLI build, served by `hyperframes preview` on a fixture, every state above driven in headless Chrome; captures below. The browser's analytics requests were blocked, so nothing reached analytics.
- [ ] **Not run:** a press into a really installed app on macOS, and the card on a real Linux machine at this head. The hand-off path is unchanged from the earlier Linux and macOS runs of this PR; the guide on Linux was driven with the Linux route answer.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.

title: Skills structure: motion-graphics description has no "use when"; most references are not linked from SKILL.md
body:
### Problem

Checked against `main` on 2026-10-18 using Anthropic's skill authoring guidance: the description should say when to use the skill, references should be one level deep from SKILL.md, and files over 100 lines should start with a table of contents.

**motion-graphics.** The description lists what the skill produces and routes to /general-video and /hyperframes, but it has no explicit "Use when …" trigger. Choosing between motion-graphics, hyperframes and general-video is left to keyword overlap.

**hyperframes.** `SKILL.md` links only 4 of the 25 files in `references/` (intent-interview.md, plugin-installation.md, routes/remotion-to-hyperframes.md, skill-lifecycle.md). The others, including workflow-catalog.md, route-briefs.md, brief-format.md, capability-menu.md, frame-worker-core.md and most of `routes/`, are not linked from SKILL.md. Agents tend to read files reached through another reference only partially (`head -100`).

**hyperframes-animation.** `SKILL.md` links 19 of 103 markdown files. The 48 `rules/*.md` are reachable only through `rules-index.md`, the 16 `transitions/*.md` only through `transitions/catalog.md`, and none of the 22 `blueprints/*.md` is linked from SKILL.md. 58 of the 61 files longer than 100 lines have no table of contents near the top.

### Proposed solution

- Add a "Use when …" sentence to the motion-graphics description.
- List every reference file in SKILL.md with one line on when to read it (the indexes can stay).
- Add a short contents block to files over 100 lines.

### Alternatives considered

_No response_

### Additional context

If #5651 (retiring the workflow skills) supersedes part of this, feel free to close those parts.

title: fix(core): run installed formatter without bun on PATH
body:
## What

Generated TypeScript now uses the checkout's installed oxfmt through the running Node/Bun executable. A formatting failure stops generation before the existing artifact is replaced.

## Why

On Windows, PATH can contain bun.cmd/bun.ps1 without a directly spawnable bun executable. Spawning `bun x oxfmt` failed silently, so builds wrote unformatted tracked artifacts and left the checkout dirty.

## Related work

Miguel's Windows generated-artifact formatter report. No separate issue required for this correction.

## How

Resolve `oxfmt/bin/oxfmt` with createRequire and run that JS entry with process.execPath. Preserve synchronous formatting, CLI configuration and stdin-filepath. Throw with the original cause instead of returning unformatted input.

## Test plan

- [x] Six targeted tests pass, including formatting in a subprocess with PATH empty and preserving an existing file after a formatter error.
- [x] Both affected generators run twice with PATH empty; their tracked artifacts remain byte-identical.
- [x] Normal commit hooks pass: core/Studio/scripts typecheck, lint, format, fallow audit, tracked artifacts and commit message.
- [x] Independent code review and launcher checks under Node and Bun passed.

## What I measured

Before the fix, both new regressions fail: an empty-PATH subprocess returns raw source, and invalid source overwrites the existing artifact. After the fix, all six tests pass and repeated position-edits/SVG generator runs preserve tracked bytes.

## What I did NOT exercise

Native Windows execution was unavailable on the Linux devbox. No render was produced. The subprocess test removes PATH resolution entirely, reproducing the launcher failure without relying on a platform shim.

fails without the fix: PATH-empty formatting returns raw source; malformed generated TypeScript is silently written instead of throwing before publication.
