title: test(studio): the edit accuracy bench stops waiting on background lint and thumbnail images
body:
## What

The Studio edit accuracy bench no longer waits on two kinds of requests that never change the preview: Studio's background lint (`/api/projects/<id>/lint`) and `blob:` image loads (a thumbnail's image). Both are now handled like the server-rendered thumbnails already were.

## Why

Small on purpose: it unblocks main's merge queue now, and the next gate fix (the crop flip below) needs its own investigation, so nothing else can carry it.


The required "Studio: edit accuracy gate" has been taking PRs out of the merge queue that cannot affect Studio editing, one random case each time (today: a core shader PR and a release PR). The regressed case changes every run.

Across the 21 most recent merge-queue runs that still had shard artifacts, 121 of the 136 failing runs of re-run cases were the same thing: `unsettled: ["reloaded"]`. After the bench reloads the page, its stillness check timed out at 15 s, while every gated measurement was correct. That hits 3 to 10 random cases per queue run. Each is re-run twice, so every few runs one of them hits again and the gate fails. Cases with a GSAP tween or hold hit about 10x more often than plain ones (about 2.5% against 0.15%).

The stillness check treats any request in flight as "the page is still changing". With logging added to the check on a CPU-starved machine (2 cores), every timeout was held by one request that never changes the preview:

- `GET /api/projects/case/lint`: Studio lints the project in the background after the preview boots, for the lint badge. The server runs it in a worker process, which took 1.6 to 7 s per case there and occasionally over 15 s.
- `GET blob:http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<uuid>`: a thumbnail's object URL. Studio revokes it when the thumbnail is disposed, and that load can end with no finished or failed event, so the bench counted it in flight forever.

Box, preview frames and pending swaps were all still at the moment of timeout. The CI runners report load near 10 on 4 vCPUs, which is why CI sees this and an idle machine does not.

## How

- `case.mjs`: `backgroundRequest` also matches the lint endpoint and any `blob:` URL. It is exported for the test.
- `settle.test.mjs`: a test that lint, thumbnails, thumbnail blob images and the event stream are background, and that the preview, file reads and a look-alike path are not. It fails on the old rule (`expected false to be true`, the lint line).

Not changed: the 2-of-3 rule, timeouts, retries, and the grid. No case is skipped or quarantined.

## Verification

- `bunx vitest run packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/`: 12 files, 89 tests pass. With the old rule restored, the new test fails and the other 9 in the file pass.
- `settle.test.mjs` alone: 10 pass with the fix; with the old rule 1 fails (the new test, on the lint line) and 9 pass. The new test alone: exit 0.
- Before and after on a Linux box with each run pinned to 2 cores (box load 9 to 29), the 204 full-grid tween/hold/idle cases, with logging of what held each timed-out wait:

  | | Cases | Stillness timeouts | Lint requests over 1.5 s |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | main | 204 | 13 in 10 cases (12 lint, 1 thumbnail `blob:`) | waited on |
  | this PR | 204 (all) | 0 | 84, not waited on |

- This PR's CI: the edit accuracy gate passes, 271 of 271, with no unsettled snapshot. Its one re-run pair (`crop-none-px-r0-*`) is the crop flip described below.

## Also looked at

A queue run cancelled about 50 min in: the gate's steps finished and passed in 18 s, but the job was then held open and ended by its 5 min job limit ("exceeded the maximum execution time"), and the queue removed the PR on that check. That is on the Actions side, not in the gate's scripts, so nothing changes for it here.

Remaining non-reload flips in the same sample (15 of 136) are single occurrences that the 2-of-3 rule absorbs: undo (8), press jump (2), and a crop whose saved file comes out about 40 px off once (5, every one a crop case, plus 2 in this PR's run). The crop one looks like its own race and gets its own change.

## Pre-review (independent reviewer)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Can a skipped request feed the preview or a save? | No. The only lint caller is the lint badge hook (useLintModal); the server lint route is a read-only GET. Of the four `createObjectURL` sites in Studio, two are thumbnails and two are download links; the bench fixtures load no media. |
| Pattern against every `/api/projects/:id/...` route | Matches only `/lint` and `/thumbnail/*`; not files, preview, history, file-mutations, gsap mutations, `files/lint`, `/lint-rules`. |
| Test enters through the real path | Calls `backgroundRequest` directly with the same `url()`/`resourceType()` surface `watchNetwork` passes; no friendlier. |
| Absent turned into ok (`||`, `??`) | None. |
| oxlint and oxfmt on both files | exit 0. |

Blocking: none.

title: fix: check, snapshot and renders use the pinned Chrome, not an older one another tool cached
body:
## What

One rule now decides which `chrome-headless-shell` HyperFrames launches, in the CLI and in the engine:

1. The pinned build: ours (`~/.cache/hyperframes/chrome`), then the shared Puppeteer cache (`~/.cache/puppeteer/chrome-headless-shell`). The pinned build is 152, or 150 on macOS 12.
2. Otherwise, the newest shell in the shared cache that starts: it loads a blank page (`--no-sandbox --dump-dom about:blank`) and exits 0. It is probed once per path per process, with a 10 s limit, and the macOS 12 ceiling still applies. A skipped shell is logged under `NODE_DEBUG=hyperframes:browser`.

So an old shell that dies at launch is skipped, and a working stable shell (what `npx @puppeteer/browsers install chrome-headless-shell` puts there, as the CLI's own Linux hint suggests) is still used.

## Why

A field report: on a Mac where another tool had once installed Puppeteer's `chrome-headless-shell` 121, `hyperframes snapshot` and `check` failed with `net::ERR_ABORTED` at `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/`. `hyperframes doctor` showed the cached `mac_arm-121` shell dying with SIGTRAP on `--version`, and setting `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` to system Chrome fixed it.

The cause is the lookup order in `findFromCache`. It took the newest version directory in the shared Puppeteer cache, whatever its age, before looking at the pinned build in `~/.cache/hyperframes/chrome`. "Usable" only meant a non-empty file, so a 121 that cannot start beat a working 152. `render` was not affected: it already asks for the pinned build (`preferManagedChrome`).

## Related work

None open.

## How

Every Chrome launch, and where it gets its binary:

| Launch | Binary comes from |
| --- | --- |
| `render` | CLI `ensureBrowser({ preferManagedChrome })` (`preflight.ts`), handed to the engine as `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` (`commands/render.ts`), read first by `resolveHeadlessShellPath` |
| Studio server renders | same env handoff (`server/studioServer.ts`) |
| `check`, `snapshot`, `capture`, `layout`, motion shots | CLI `ensureBrowser()`, passed as `executablePath` to its own launch |
| `benchmark`, a standalone producer, the Lambda handler | the engine resolves it itself (`resolveHeadlessShellPath`), which scanned the shared cache newest-first on its own |

So the engine's resolver gets the same rule:

- The rule lives once, in `@hyperframes/engine/chrome-host-ceiling`, which the CLI already imported:
  - `managedChromeVersion`, `isManagedChromeDir` and `compareBrowserVersionsDescending` move there.
  - `shellStarts` loads a blank page once per path. `--dump-dom` is headless Chrome's own print-and-exit mode on every platform, and it goes through the launch an old build dies in. `--version` was the first probe, but on Windows it may not exit, which would stall every non-pinned shell for the full limit.
  - `pickSharedShell` returns the shared cache's pinned build, else its newest starting shell.
- Engine `resolveHeadlessShellPath`: the pinned build in our cache, then `pickSharedShell` on the shared cache. With neither, the newest build of ours, since the engine cannot download.
- CLI `findFromCache` reads the pinned cache first, then the Puppeteer cache.
- `findFromPuppeteerCache` uses `pickSharedShell`. The CLI's own copy of the version sort (`parseVersionSegments`, `compareVersionDirsDescending`) is gone in favour of the engine's.
- An explicit choice still wins: `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` and `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` come first, unchanged.
- The embedded-captions scripts (`preview-frames`, `check-overflow`, `check-rail-climax`, `measure-layout`) launch what `hyperframes browser path` prints (`hfBrowser` in `hf-cli.cjs`), so they follow the same rule. Before, each hardcoded system Chrome. Without a CLI they still use system Chrome.

## Behaviour changes

- Someone who installed a non-pinned `chrome-headless-shell` with `npx @puppeteer/browsers install` and has no HyperFrames cache still gets it, if it starts. Only a shell that fails to start is skipped.
- Engine-only renders (the SDK or the producer used directly, with no env override): before, any build in our cache came before the shared cache. Now it is our pinned build, then the newest shared shell that starts, then any build of ours. On a box whose HyperFrames cache holds only an older, non-pinned build, a newer shared shell now wins, and that can be a build someone else installed. The CLI, the shipped images and Lambda pass the env override, so they don't change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests updated in `packages/cli/src/browser/manager.test.ts`.
  - New: a Puppeteer cache holding only `121.0.6167.85` beside the pinned cache resolves to the pinned build.
  - New: a 121 that does not start is skipped.
  - New: with no pinned build, the newest working shell (148 over 99) is kept.
  - The first two fail on main, which returns the 121.
  - The test that pinned the old order ("prefers the puppeteer cache over the hyperframes cache when BOTH are populated") now asserts the pinned cache wins.
  - Puppeteer-cache fixtures name the pinned build.
- [x] Engine tests updated in `packages/engine/src/services/browserManager.test.ts`.
  - New: a shared cache holding only a `linux-121.0.6167.85` that does not start resolves to nothing, where main returns the 121.
  - New, with real stub shells: one that dies with SIGTRAP is skipped, and the newest working one (148 over 99) is kept.
  - New: the pinned build in the shared cache beats an older build of ours (150), where main returns the 150.
  - The platform-matrix fixtures name the pinned build.
- [x] `skills/embedded-captions/scripts/hf-cli.test.mjs`: the scripts launch the path a stub CLI prints for `browser path`. It fails on main (`hfBrowser` is not a function).
- [x] The skills test passes three runs in a row on a Linux box.
- [ ] Engine and CLI `tsc --noEmit` and the browser tests at this head: CI runs them.
- [x] On an arm64 Mac (macOS 26.5.1), outside any sandbox: Puppeteer's `chrome-headless-shell` 121.0.6167.85 dies with SIGTRAP on both `--version` and `--dump-dom about:blank`. The pinned 152.0.7977.30 prints its version and an empty page on both.
- [ ] Not run on Windows. The probe is `--dump-dom`, which exits there too; that is inferred from Chrome's headless mode, not run.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: fix(studio): render scratch stays out of the project and error telemetry counts real failures only
body:
## What

Studio's unhandled-rejection telemetry stops counting three things that are not Studio failures:

1. **A file-tree refresh while the preview server is gone.** `refreshFileTree` now resolves instead of rejecting when the listing request fails (network error or non-OK status). It records one `file_tree_refresh_failed` event per failure streak and stays quiet until a refresh succeeds again.
2. **Rejections that belong only to a browser extension.** The rejection listener drops a rejection when every stack frame is a `chrome-extension://`, `moz-extension://` or `safari(-web)-extension://` script. A stack with any Studio frame in it is still reported.
3. **Our own "superseded by a newer edit" cancellation.** The scene-swap cancel reason is now a `DOMException` named `AbortError` instead of a plain `Error`, so the listener's existing AbortError filter classifies it as a cancellation.
4. **A render's scratch folders are not project files.** A render writes its scratch dir (`work-<job>-XXXXXX`, or a `.<output>.hf-transaction-XXXXXX` staging dir) next to its output. With the output inside the project, the file watcher streamed a change every 300 ms for the whole render, and the file tree listed the scratch `compiled/index.html` as a composition. Both now skip those folders. Finished outputs and `renders/` still show in the tree.

## Why

Studio's unhandled-rejection rate rose several-fold in early October. Over the last 7 days, these three classes made up about 82% of it:

| Class | Share of 7-day rejections |
|---|---|
| `TypeError: Failed to fetch` from `refreshFileTree` | ~48% |
| Extension-only stacks (wallet and page-helper extensions) | ~27% |
| `superseded by a newer edit` | ~7% |

**Refresh path.** The external-change coordinator calls `void refreshFileTree?.()` after every settled file change. When the server stops answering, each delivery rejects and nothing catches it. Some tabs hit the per-tab report cap within about 20 seconds. Every other caller (upload, remove background, block install) awaited a refresh that could throw. So a successful upload whose follow-up re-list failed showed "Upload failed: network error". A failed re-list leaves the tree stale. It does not mean the caller's own operation failed, so the owner now handles it once.

**When it started.** The refresh stack first appears in 0.8.114. #4898 made the file manager's handlers stable, and with that the file-change event stream stopped being torn down and reopened while a render wrote into the project. Before, that churn dropped most change deliveries, which hid this path. In a local run with a render writing into the project folder, the previous release reopened the stream dozens of times and received a handful of changes; 0.8.114 held one stream and received a change every 300 ms, the file watcher's burst limit. The same release also made V8 name the frame `Object.refreshFileTree`, which is why the label is new.

**Superseded.** Over 99% of the tabs that reported "superseded by a newer edit" in the last 7 days also leaked AbortErrors through an extension's `window.fetch` wrapper, against under 1% of all tabs. That is the case `main.tsx` already documents: the wrapper re-rejects with our abort reason. Because our reason was a plain `Error`, the AbortError filter missed it.

## Related work

Refs #4370 (added the refresh on external change) and #4898 (stable handlers).

## How

- `core/projectFolders.ts` now owns "which folders are not project files": the render temp-dir name pattern moves here from the producer's `renderDirOwner.ts`, which imports it back, and `isProjectIgnoredDir` combines it with `PREVIEW_IGNORED_DIRS`. The CLI watcher's own `WATCHER_EXCLUDED_DIRS` was a character-identical copy of that list; it is deleted, and the watcher and the project signature both call `isProjectIgnoredDir`. The tree walk keeps its narrower list (it shows `dist/`, `renders/` and the like on purpose) and adds the render temp-dir pattern.

- `useFileTree.ts`: the request moves into `readTreeListing`, which throws on a non-OK status. The refresh catches every failure and returns. A ref remembers that this failure streak was already reported, so a server that stays gone files one event, not one per change.
- `utils/rejectionTelemetry.ts`: `errorProps` and `isCompositionAssetError` moved out of `main.tsx` unchanged, so the filters can be tested without mounting the app. `useFileTree` reuses `errorProps` for its event. `isExtensionOnlyStack` is new; it reads both V8 (`at f (url:l:c)`) and Gecko/WebKit (`f@url:l:c`) frames. The extension check runs before the cap, so extension noise cannot use up a session's 50 reports.
- `player/sceneSwap.ts`: `supersededByNewerEdit()` builds the cancel reason; `useTimelinePlayer` uses it.

The refresh does not add a retry or backoff. The next real change event, or the event stream's reconnect catch-up, is what triggers the next attempt. While the server is gone, each attempt is one local request with at most one in flight, since a new refresh aborts the previous one.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `useFileTree.test.tsx`: a refresh with the server gone resolves, keeps the tree, and reports once across two failures and again after a success. It fails on `main` because the refresh rejects with `Failed to fetch`.
  - `rejectionTelemetry.test.ts`: extension-only V8, Firefox and Safari stacks are dropped. A stack with a Studio frame under an extension's fetch wrapper is kept, and so is a stack with no frames.
  - `sceneSwap.test.ts`: a swap cancelled by a newer edit rejects with an error the listener reads as `AbortError`.
  - `fileWatcher.test.ts`: a render's work dir and transaction dir are not watched; a user folder named `work-notes` still is. `safePath.test.ts`: a render's scratch `compiled/index.html` is not listed, while the project's own files and the finished output are. Both fail on `main`.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

### What I ran (Linux, Node 22, vitest 4)

- Red on `main`: the new refresh test against the base `useFileTree.ts` fails with `TypeError: Failed to fetch` thrown out of `refresh`, the same failure the telemetry shows. The watcher test fails because the scratch file is watched; the walk test fails because the scratch `index.html` is listed.
- Green, three runs in a row each: the CLI watcher tests, the studio-server `safePath`, `projectSignature` and `renderOutputs` tests, the producer `renderDirOwner` tests, the inspector sources test and the three studio files. `tsc --noEmit` for cli, studio-server, producer, studio and core, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `comment-ratchet`, `check-comment-citations` and `fallow audit --base <merge-base> --fail-on-issues` all exit 0. Fallow keeps one warning (the moved `fallow-ignore` line counts as added) and one inherited finding (`useTimelinePlayer` size, unchanged).
- Mutations, each run on its own: report every failure, never reset the streak, rethrow, judge stacks with `some` instead of `every`, and cancel with a plain `Error`. Each one fails exactly its test and nothing else.

### What I could not verify

- The after numbers are an estimate: last week's events with these three classes removed. Tabs that hit the 50-report cap may now report rejections the cap used to hide, so the real after number can be slightly higher.
- I did not reproduce why the tree request fails while the event stream keeps delivering: it is mostly macOS in the telemetry and never happened on Linux (server killed, restarted on the same port, constant writes, a render into the project, a low open-file limit). Both fixes hold whatever that trigger is: the render no longer streams changes, and any failed refresh is handled.
- The Before/After captures fail the tree request in the browser to stage the failure; they do not reproduce the macOS trigger.
- Rejections where an extension wraps our own `fetch` (an extension frame plus Studio frames) are still reported. That is our request failing, and it is the largest remaining item.

## Before

Studio served by the CLI preview server, the file-tree request failing, five outside edits to `index.html`: each change leaves an uncaught `TypeError: Failed to fetch`, and each one reaches telemetry as `studio:unhandled_promise_rejection`.

![Before: five uncaught Failed to fetch rejections, five crash events](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aa1d8665-376b-479a-b36f-0eb54ed284bd)

## After

Same stage on this branch: no uncaught rejections, no `unhandled_promise_rejection` events, one `file_tree_refresh_failed` event for the whole streak.

![After: no uncaught rejections, one file_tree_refresh_failed event](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fa6e2c53-f64c-4fb0-b605-d4c7e5fce64f)

title: ci: the file size check fetches two commits, not the whole history, so it finishes in time
body:
## What

The "File size check" job checks out two commits instead of the repository's full history and every branch.

This PR is small on purpose: it is a CI fix on its own, and it makes every PR's file size check reliable.

## Why

The job has a one-minute limit, and `fetch-depth: 0` downloads every branch's full history before the check runs. On a busy day that alone runs past the minute, so the check fails with "The job has exceeded the maximum execution time of 1m0s" without measuring a file. A PR that touches no file under `packages/studio` can go red this way.

## Related work

None.

## How

A `pull_request` run checks out the PR's merge commit, whose first parent is the base branch's tip. So `fetch-depth: 2` plus `git diff HEAD^1 HEAD` lists exactly the files the PR changes, the same list as `origin/<base>...HEAD`. The full-scan branch for runs without a base ref is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Simulated a PR merge commit locally (a change to one `packages/studio` file, merged `--no-ff` onto `main`): `HEAD^1 HEAD` and `origin/main...HEAD` list the same file.
- [ ] This PR's own "File size check" run, which now finishes inside the minute.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: ci(repo): the packed consumer check stops failing on npm versions published minutes ago
body:
## What

The packed consumer check in `verify-packed-manifests` installs third-party dependencies with bun's `--minimum-release-age` set to one day, so it never resolves a version published minutes ago.

## Why

Twice today a merge-queue group failed in Build, not in any test: `bun install` in the clean consumer fixture got `GET .../client-lambda-3.1153.0.tgz - 404`. The fixture has no lockfile, so every third-party range resolves to the newest version on npm, and a version that was just published can be listed before its tarball is served. The tarball returned 200 a few minutes later. Every PR in those groups left the queue for it.

## How

- `installConsumer(dir)` adds `--minimum-release-age=86400` to the consumer install. `verifyPackedConsumer` calls it, and it is exported for the test.
- A same-day dependency bump (a range whose every matching version is younger than a day) makes bun refuse the install: `No version matching "<pkg>" found for specifier "^x" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds)`. The repo already installed that version, so its tarball is served. `installConsumer` reads the blocked package names from that error, lists only those in the fixture's `bunfig.toml` under `minimumReleaseAgeExcludes`, logs them, and installs once more. Any other install error still fails.
- The check still installs our packed tarballs into a clean consumer; other third-party versions are whatever npm had a day earlier.
- Not done, and why: pinning the consumer to the repo lockfile's versions. Bun overrides are per package name, and 87 of the lockfile's 872 third-party packages are locked at more than one version, so overrides would change the dependency graph rather than reproduce it. A retry on 404 would also mask a genuinely missing package.

## Verification

- Three new tests against a local fake registry run in a worker thread:
  - It lists `1.0.0` (10 days old) and `1.1.0` (just published, tarball 404). The install passes and picks `1.0.0`.
  - A same-day bump, `^1.1.0`, where `1.1.0` is an hour old. It is checked twice: once as the only version, once beside an old `1.0.0`. Both install `1.1.0`.
  - A package the registry does not have still fails the install.
- Mutations:
  - With the fallback removed, the same-day test fails with `blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds`.
  - With the age flag removed, the first test fails with `GET http://127.0.0.1:<port>/fake-dep/-/fake-dep-1.1.0.tgz - 404`, the same error as the queue failure.
- `node --import tsx --test scripts/verify-packed-manifests.test.mjs`: exit 0, 20 of 20 pass. Three runs in a row, all exit 0.
- `bun run verify:packed-manifests` against the real registry with the age flag (first commit; the same-day fallback adds only an error path): exit 0. It resolved 173 packed exports, executed 163 Node exports, and verified the clean consumer install, NodeNext declarations, Vite resolution and CLI startup.
- oxlint and oxfmt are clean on both files.

title: fix(cli): installing the CLI no longer downloads an unused code formatter
body:
## What

`hyperframes` no longer lists `prettier` as a runtime dependency. Every `npm install hyperframes` stops downloading it.

## Why

Nothing in the CLI uses it. On `main`, no file under `packages/*/src`, `scripts` or `.github` imports, requires or runs it. The built `dist` mentions it only in `// prettier-ignore` comments, and no other installed package declares it as a peer. It still cost every install about 10 MB.

## Related work

None.

## How

- Removed the `prettier` entry from `packages/cli/package.json` `dependencies`.
- Removed its two lines from `bun.lock`: the CLI workspace entry and the package entry. No other workspace depends on it. `bun install --frozen-lockfile` reports no changes with the edited lockfile.

The lockfile's other drift (workspace version fields behind `package.json`) is left alone to keep this diff to the one dependency.

## Test plan

title: fix(studio): a deselect made while an edit saves stays deselected
body:
## What

A deselect (Escape, a click on empty canvas) or a click on a different element now sticks while a style, attribute or text edit is still saving. Before this change the element you had just released came back as selected about 100 ms later.

## Why

Every edit commit resyncs the selection it started with once the save returns, so the panel reads fresh values. That resync re-applied the old selection whatever had happened in the meantime. A deselect or a new pick made during the save was undone, and the next action (Delete, a nudge, the next edit) landed on the wrong element. This was also one source of flaky cases in the edit-accuracy bench, where the next case found an element still selected.

## How

- `refreshDomEditSelectionFromPreview` is the single owner of the resync. It now runs only while the selection it was given is still the one selected (compared by target key, so a node re-keyed by a reload still matches). It checks before starting and again after the async rebuild, because the user can move on during either.
- The preview-reload sync (`useDomEditPreviewSync`) had its own copy of that body with the same race. It now calls the guarded resync and passes the live preview iframe through a new optional `iframe` argument. That keeps the existing behaviour of following a promoted shadow preview. The plumbing that only fed the copy (`applyDomSelection`, `buildDomSelectionFromTarget` and the group refresher params of the wiring and sync hooks) is removed.

## Verification

- New tests in `useDomSelection.test.ts` cover four cases: a deselect before the resync, a different pick before the resync with the saved element still in the preview, the same with the saved element gone, and a deselect while the resync is rebuilding. All four fail with main's `useDomSelection.ts` (`expected { …(20) } to be null` and similar) and pass here, three runs in a row.
- Mutation check: removing only the before-start guard fails the "saved element gone" case; removing only the after-rebuild guard fails the "deselect while rebuilding" case.
- From `packages/studio`, `vitest run src/hooks src/components/editor` passes: 306 files, 3539 tests, exit 0. From the repo root, which has no vitest config, the same command fails 55 tests on main and on this branch alike. The failures are the same tests on both. The two preview-sync suites (`useDomEditPreviewSync.test.ts`, `previewPromotionSelection.test.tsx`) pass with the new parameter.
- oxlint, oxfmt, studio typecheck and fallow audit are green.



Recorded in headless Chrome on a repo grid fixture (`crop-none-px-r0-root-z100`): crop the box, then press Escape while the save is in flight. The save response is held 450 ms, as on a busy machine.

## Before

On main the box shows "Nothing selected" for a moment, then re-selects when the save returns.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0dd94119-da22-4561-a04b-7c0805d3681c

![Before: about a second after Escape, the box is selected again](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/16d430b7-0802-4caa-bcca-3aa04b3a8dc3)

## After

On this branch it stays deselected.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2ca68bf5-475c-48ee-ade2-d77db89d2635

![After: about a second after Escape, nothing is selected](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e756368c-c81e-4dcc-af33-0c5392dad19a)

title: fix(aws-lambda): old stacks are refused before any upload; stale local copies never re-upload
body:
Follow-up to #5772 from its review: three gaps in the upgrade path that the main render path already handled.

## What changes for users

- **`lambda render-batch` and `lambda sites create` refuse a too-old stack before uploading anything.** `render-batch` uploaded the site once for the whole batch and only then reached the per-render `STACK_TOO_OLD` check, so an old stack received the upload first. `sites create` never checked. Both now call the check before `deploySite`, as `lambda render` already does.
- **An expired site file is re-uploaded only from a matching local copy.** `lambda render --site-id` always passes the project directory. When a file under `cas/sha256/` had expired and the local copy was gone or edited, the user saw a raw upload error (a missing file, or S3 rejecting the checksum) instead of `SITE_FILES_MISSING`. Now a file is re-uploaded only when its local copy hashes to the sha256 the site lists; anything else counts as missing and the render stops with `SITE_FILES_MISSING` before starting.
- **The deploy guide says where the CLI keeps a stack's state** (`.hyperframes/lambda-stack-<stack-name>.json` in the current directory) and that the other `lambda` commands read it from there.

## How

- `assertStackReadsSites` (the check `renderToLambda` already ran) is exported from `@hyperframes/aws-lambda/sdk` and takes `{ stateMachineArn, region?, sfn? }`. `render-batch` calls it unless `--dry-run`; `sites create` calls it first.
- `ensureSiteStored` hashes the local copy before re-storing it.

## Tests

- `packages/cli/src/commands/lambda/stackCheck.test.ts` (new): with a too-old stack, `render-batch` and `sites create` reject with `STACK_TOO_OLD` and never call `deploySite`. Both fail on the old order.
- `renderToLambda.test.ts`: an edited and then a deleted local copy each give `SITE_FILES_MISSING` with no upload and no execution. Fails without the hash check.
- Run on Linux on the code before the rebase onto main (identical diff, clean cherry-pick): aws-lambda and cli typecheck pass; `renderToLambda.test.ts` 18/18; `stackCheck.test.ts` + `render-batch.test.ts` 16/16; each new test red with its fix reverted; 3 consecutive green runs; `verify:packed-manifests` passes.

## Not done

- No live AWS run for this change. Each fix is a call-order or local-hash change covered by the tests above.

title: fix(core): a paused preview puts a reloaded video back at the playhead
body:
## What

A paused preview now keeps every video at the playhead after one of them loads a new source.

Before, a video whose authoring proxy (or that copy's larger size) arrived while the preview was paused restarted at frame 0 and stayed there. A clip stacked with its own background-removed cutout then showed two moments of the same person. The render was unaffected.

## Why

`mediaProxy.ts` `loadProxy()` swaps `src` and calls `load()`, which puts the element back at 0 and evicts its sync state. While playing, the next transport tick hard-syncs it. While paused, the tick only re-syncs when some media is still running (`init.ts`, the `hasRunningTimedMedia()` branch), so nothing seeks the reloaded element until the next user seek.

The copy can land after the playhead stopped:
- the first copy lands late;
- or `keepSized()` swaps in a larger copy when the player reports its display scale, which happens on its own right after a seek.

## Related work

None.

## How

`init.ts` binds a `loadedmetadata` listener on every media element, next to the proxy and route listeners already there. When the clock is paused and the page is not a render (the runtime's one render check, `mediaProxy.ts` `isRenderMode()`: the render config is set, or the video already shows injected frames), it drops the sync cursor, forces a sync, and runs `syncMediaForCurrentState()`. This is the same full visit the paused tick does when it has running media to stop.

Playing is unchanged; the tick already handles it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `init.reloadedVideoKeepsPlayhead.test.ts`.
  - It stacks a clip and its cutout at `data-start=0` and seeks to 4 s while paused.
  - It then does to the clip what `loadProxy` does (evict sync state, new `src`, `load()` back to 0) and fires the browser's `loadedmetadata`.
  - Both elements must be at 4 s.
  - Without the fix it fails: `expected +0 to be 4`. With the fix it passes three runs in a row.
  - A second test sets the render config and checks the same reload is left alone (the render drives its videos' frames). Without the render check it fails: `expected 4 to be 0`.
- [x] `src/runtime/init*`, `media*`, `pausedTransportInvariant`, `transportPark`: 19 files, 745 tests pass.
- [x] `bun run typecheck` and `oxlint` on the changed files are clean.
- [x] Manual, real Chrome against `hyperframes@0.8.177 preview`, using HEVC fixtures with a burned-in frame number (plain portrait, and stored landscape with a -90 rotation) plus a hue-shifted VP9-alpha copy stacked on top. Chrome can't decode HEVC, so the proxy path runs.
  - Paused at 4 s, after the copy grows: HEVC element `currentTime` 0, webm 4 (frame 0 under frame 120, crop below).
  - A fresh seek realigns them.
  - Playing, a swap is back in step within 300 ms.
- [x] Manual after, the same fixtures served by this branch's built CLI. Every paused step shows both layers on the same frame after each copy lands, in both fixtures (attachments below):
  - the copy the studio grows itself after a seek: before 0 vs 120, after 120 vs 120;
  - a larger copy landing while paused: before 0 vs 120, after 120 vs 120;
  - a copy landing after the clip ended: before 0 vs 188, after 187 vs 187.

  Playing is unchanged, under one frame apart.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

### Crops (fixtures: HEVC with a burned-in frame number on top, its hue-shifted VP9-alpha copy below)

Before, paused at 4 s after the first copy grows: HEVC frame 0 under webm frame 120

![before, first copy grows](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b38213a0-79a8-4d0f-b4db-e9841d86fcaf)

Before, paused at 4 s, the studio grows the copy on its own: frame 0 under 120

![before, studio-driven growth](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4371ce44-6f1a-45cb-90bb-637c14e1a8ad)

After (this branch), the same step: 120 and 120

title: test(cli): the late subresource capture test lands its assets well inside the settle cap
body:
## What

The test for late subresources in CLI captures (`captureCompositionFrame.lateSubresources.browser.test.ts`) now holds its image for 300 ms and its fetched asset for 500 ms, instead of 800 ms and 1.1 s. Both still arrive after the page's load event, and the capture code is unchanged.

## Why

The test failed on a hosted Windows runner in a merge-queue group, which removed a PR that had nothing to do with it. The capture waits for late images and fetches for at most 1.5 s after the composition reports ready, the same limit as the fixed 1.5 s sleep it replaced. The test's asset landed 1.1 s after ready, so a busy runner had almost no room left.

Timings of the settle on `windows-latest`, from a diagnostic run that logged each step (40 runs at the old delays):
- Alone: it returned at 1.20 to 1.29 s.
- With four copies running at once: up to 1.48 s, 18 ms from the cap.
- The one failure: the page had not loaded either asset by the cap. The capture never returned past an asset that had already arrived.

Only `snapshot`, `compare` and `grade-compare` use this wait; renders do not.

## How

- `IMAGE_MS` 800 → 300 and `FETCH_MS` 1100 → 500, and the comment above them says why.

## Verification

- Linux: the test passes 3 runs in a row. With the settle wait removed from `openSettledCompositionPage`, it fails with the original error, `expected { complete: false, width: +0 } to deeply equal { complete: true, width: 1, …(1) }`, so it still catches a capture that returns early.
- Windows, the same diagnostic run with the new delays: 55 of 55 passed (15 alone, 40 with four copies at once), and the full engine-cli lane passed. The settle returned at 454 to 952 ms (median 697), so the worst case is 548 ms from the cap instead of 18 ms.

title: feat(producer): render a distributed chunk as frame sub-ranges
body:
## What

A distributed render can now render one chunk as several frame sub-ranges and assemble the parts back.

- `renderChunk(planDir, chunkIndex, out, { frameRange })` (and `renderChunkV2`) render only `[startFrame, endFrame)` of the chunk's slice.
- `assemble` / `assembleV2` accept, per chunk, either one output path (unchanged) or the ordered list of that chunk's parts.
- `DISTRIBUTED_RENDER_CAPABILITIES.chunkFrameRange: true` lets callers detect support before sending a range.

## Why

Chunk sizes come from a frame budget. When a chunk turns out much slower per frame than the budget assumed (very high resolution, heavy compositions), the only retry today is the same whole chunk, which hits the same timeout again. Splitting the slow chunk and rendering the halves in parallel on retry keeps the render inside the timeout without re-planning the whole job.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `frameRange` is validated against the chunk slice (non-empty, integer, inside the slice) before any ffmpeg, plan-hash or browser work. A bad range throws `RenderChunkValidationError` with the new code `CHUNK_FRAME_RANGE_INVALID`.
- Everything that depended on the slice bounds now reads the resolved range: capture frame count and range (frame times stay absolute so seeded randomness matches), deferred video-frame extraction, encoder GOP (each part opens on its own keyframe), audio packets for plans where chunks carry audio (`chunksWithSubRange` gives each part the packets it would own as a chunk of its own), and the perf JSON.
- Each part is a self-contained chunk output (timestamps from zero, png names from zero), so `assemble` flattens the parts into the ordered file list and every existing join path works unchanged. The length check still runs against `chunks.json`; an empty part list is rejected.
- With `frameRange` omitted every value is identical to before: a png render with an explicit whole-slice range has the same sha256 as one without.
- Adapters (AWS Lambda, Cloud Run) are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `renderChunkFrameRange.test.ts` (12): validation and resolution.
  - `chunkAudio.test.ts` (9): sub-range audio cut, plus an ffmpeg check that the parts carry identical audio on the stitched path.
  - `renderChunk.test.ts -t frameRange` (4, real Chrome + ffmpeg): two halves vs the whole chunk for png-sequence (byte-identical), mp4 with chunk audio (stitched), mp4 with audio muxed at assemble, and webm. Frame count and order are exact, audio is identical, pixels match (PSNR > 35).
  - Existing distributed suites pass: assemble, planProtocol, publicExports, renderChunkFallback, mp4Stitch, planV2, crossWorkerIdempotency, chunkBoundary, renderChunk.
- [x] typecheck (producer, aws-lambda, gcp-cloud-run), oxfmt, oxlint, fallow audit.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Notes:
- webm stores timestamps in whole milliseconds, so a split point that isn't on a whole millisecond adds one more seam rounding of up to 1 ms, the same as existing chunk seams already have. Tests assert every frame stays within 2 ms of its slot. mp4 timestamps are identical whole vs parts.
- Not exercised here: BeginFrame capture mode (this host falls back to screenshot capture).

title: perf(cli): snapshot decodes phone video frames at their on-screen size, several at once
body:
## What changes for users

`hyperframes snapshot` on a project full of 4K phone video finishes in about a fifth of the time and no longer runs Chrome out of memory. A 1080x1920 project with 15 portrait 4K HEVC clips on screen, snapshotted at 16 moments, went from 600 s to 126 s, and Chrome's peak memory from 3.7 GB to 1.2 GB.

## Why it was slow

For every moment, snapshot decodes the current frame of each visible `<video>` with ffmpeg and paints it over the element. It did that one clip at a time, at the source's full resolution: each 4K portrait frame became a 2160x3840 PNG (several MB), was base64-encoded, sent to the page and decoded there, even when the clip is shown in a 360 px box. In the 600 s run, ffmpeg took 280 s and moving and decoding those full-size images took most of the rest. Seeking was already exact (only the frames at the requested moments are decoded), so that part was not the problem.

## The fix

- Each frame is scaled by ffmpeg to the size it is shown at: the short side covers the larger side of the element's on-screen box times the pixel density (the `--zoom-scale` density when `--zoom` is set). That holds at any rotation or `object-fit`, and a frame is never made larger than the source. A 4K portrait frame in a 360x384 box comes out 384x683, about 25x fewer bytes.
- The clips visible at one moment are extracted 4 at a time with the existing `runWithConcurrencyLimit` helper.

## Proof

Same project, same 16 moments, on a shared 8-core Linux machine (load around 13 during the runs, so read the numbers as relative):

| | wall | Chrome peak | frames extracted |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 600 s | 3671 MB | 240/240 |
| scaled frames only | 215 s | 2974 MB | 240/240 |
| scaled + 4 at a time (this PR) | 126 s | 1203 MB | 240/240 |

The snapshots match main: mean pixel difference under 1/255, the rest is resampling on thin lines.

The new test in `snapshot.test.ts` extracts a landscape and a portrait clip at a 32 px displayed size and checks the short side is 32, and that no scale (0) or a size larger than the source gives the source size. It fails on main (the frame comes back at full size) and passes here; the other 74 snapshot tests pass.

## No visible change

Snapshots look the same. Frames are smaller in memory only, sized to what the page shows.

title: revert(engine): render workers keep the media of FFmpeg-fed videos loaded again
body:
## What this fixes

Since #5795, renders with more than one worker fail now and then with `Invalid JPEG input at frame N: empty frame`. This puts back the old behavior: render workers keep the media of videos whose frames come from FFmpeg loaded.

## Why revert

#5795 drops the `<video>` media in each worker once FFmpeg supplies that video's frames, to save renderer memory. On some worker pages, the page then never paints. It stays visible, focused and `readyState === "complete"`, but its init commit, seek and capture all come back with no damage and no screenshot. Retrying for 3 s doesn't bring it back, so the frame is empty and the render fails.

Measured on a Linux box with CI's CLI smoke steps (3 s `testsrc2` 640x360 clip, `init --example warm-grain`, `render --workers auto --strict`, 2-3 workers):

| Build | Failed renders |
|---|---|
| main with #5795 | 8 of 60 |
| same build, only the `releaseInjectedVideoMedia(...)` call turned off | 0 of 40 |
| this revert, built from source (3 workers on every run) | 0 of 20 |
| control on the same box: this tree with #5795's code put back | 4 of 20 (all empty frame) |

The memory saving is worth having. It comes back separately, once the page that stops painting is understood.

## What the revert touches

- `frameCapture.ts`: removes `releaseInjectedVideoMedia`, `releasableVideoIds` and their three calls (session init in both capture modes, and the static verification page).
- Removes `frameCapture-releaseInjectedVideoMedia.browser.test.ts`, the test for those two functions.
- Keeps `__fixtures__/loopback.ts` and the two tests #5795 moved onto it. #5898 has since built its hung-Chrome guard on that fixture, and another browser test imports it, so a full `git revert` conflicts and would undo #5898.

## Not verified

- Not run on macOS or Windows. The failure was measured on Linux only.
- Renderer memory goes back to what it was before #5795. I didn't re-measure it.

title: fix(engine): long phone-video exports neither time out nor stall before the first frame
body:
## What changes for users

Two failures of long exports of 4K HDR phone video (60 fps HEVC, as iPhones record it), both in the step that decodes video before the first frame is captured:

- They no longer fail with `Video extraction failed for N source(s) [VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED; ffmpeg_timeout=N]`. Extraction keeps going as long as ffmpeg keeps producing frames, and still stops a run that has stopped producing them.
- A project with many cuts of a few HDR sources no longer starts one decoder per cut at once. With tone-mapping to SDR, every cut probed its source's first frame on its own, outside the extraction limit: 245 cuts of 2 files started 245 4K decoders together. Each source is now probed once, inside the extraction limit.

## Why it failed

Export decodes each clip's frames ahead of capture, in ffmpeg runs of up to 120 s of output. Each run had a fixed 300 s limit on total time. Decoding 4K 10-bit HEVC and tone-mapping it to SDR runs well below the speed that limit assumes, so a long clip was killed while it was working normally. The error is marked retryable, so the export failed only after several minutes.

Measured on a shared 8-core Linux machine, exporting a 150 s 4K HLG HEVC clip to 1080p with `--sdr`:

- 30 fps source: the first 120 s run took 295 s, 5 s inside the limit.
- 60 fps source: a 30 s run took 131 s (about 7 frames a second), so the 120 s run needed about 9 minutes. It was killed at 300 s and the export failed after 427 s with `[VIDEO_EXTRACTION_FAILED; ffmpeg_timeout=1]`.

## The fix

- `runFfmpeg` takes an optional `stallTimeout`. When set, it replaces the total deadline: ffmpeg's own progress lines are read from stderr, and the run is stopped only after that long with no new output frame. This is the same rule the streaming encoder already uses for its inactivity timeout.
- Frame extraction uses it, with `ffmpegProcessTimeout` (300 s by default) as the stall window. Every extraction run is bounded by `-frames:v`, so a run that keeps producing frames still ends.
- The timeout error now says `(no new frame for N ms)`.

## Proof

- New test: a paced run that writes frames steadily for 1.5 s against a 0.7 s timeout finishes. On main it is killed at 0.7 s.
- New test: an ffmpeg run that never gets a frame stops after a 0.5 s stall timeout. On main it hangs until the test times out.
- Both pass three runs in a row; the extractor, `runFfmpeg`, managed-process and streaming-encoder suites pass (350 tests), and the engine typecheck is clean.
- End to end on the same 60 fps clip with this branch: the 120 s extraction run took 348 s and finished cleanly, past the old 300 s limit, and the export moved on to capture. I stopped it at 58% of capture to free disk on the shared machine, so the finished file was not checked.

## Many cuts of a few sources

`readFirstFrameColour` ran for every extraction that tone-maps HDR to SDR, uncached and before the extraction slot was taken. It now uses the same per-file cache as the ffprobe metadata (`mediaFileIdentity` / `readMetadataCache` / `writeMetadataCache`, keyed by path and file identity, so an edited file is probed again) and runs inside `inExtractionSlot`. The probe reads only the source's first frame, so the tone-map settings are not part of the key. A failed probe drops its cache entry, so the next cut probes again.

No deadlock: `inExtractionSlot` is private to the extractor and wraps only bare `runFfmpeg` calls (segment runs and the single run); the probe is awaited before either, so nothing holding a slot ever waits for one.

Measured on a 14-core Apple Silicon Mac with a 10:40 1080p project of 245 cuts from two 300 s 4K 60 fps HLG HEVC portrait clips plus 424 audio clips, exported with `--sdr`:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| first-frame probes | 245 | 2 |
| most ffmpeg decoders at once | 178 | 7 (the extraction limit) |
| video extraction | 493 s | 379 s |
| time to the first captured frame | 560 s | 443 s |

The remaining extraction time is the tone-mapped decode of 246 cuts, seven at a time.

Tests: 12 cuts of 2 files make 2 probes (12 on main); with the extractor pinned to one slot, 8 tone-mapped cuts of 2 sources finish with 10 ffmpeg runs and never more than one alive (main: 16 runs, up to 8 alive); a first probe that fails is probed again on the next cut (fails with the cache cleanup removed).

## No visible change

Exports that worked before produce the same frames; only the rule for giving up on a slow run changed.

title: fix(studio-server): a history claim on Windows waits out a lock file being deleted
body:
## What changes for users

On Windows, two `hyperframes history begin` calls on one project at the same moment no longer crash one of them with `EPERM: operation not permitted, open '...\owner.pid'`. The second waits for the history lock and gets the normal refusal ("<agent>'s turn is open; it has to end before yours begins"), as on macOS and Linux.

## Why it failed

The history owner lock reads and hard-links `owner.pid`. When the owner releases the lock it deletes that file, and on Windows a file that is being deleted cannot be opened or linked for a moment: the call fails with EPERM (sometimes EACCES or EBUSY) instead of ENOENT or EEXIST. The lock treated that as a fatal error, so the waiting process exited with code 1.

Seen on a hosted Windows runner looping the existing test `serializes concurrent begin --exclusive claims under the history owner lock` 30 times with each process's stderr printed: one run in 30 had the waiting process exit 1 with `EPERM: operation not permitted, open '...\owner.pid'`; the other 29 refused with code 2 as expected.

## The fix

On Windows, an EPERM, EACCES or EBUSY while claiming or reading the lock means the lock is busy: the claimer waits and tries again until its existing deadline, then gives up with the same error. Elsewhere these errors still fail at once. Only the claim is retried, not the work after this process holds the lock. One claim attempt moved into its own function to keep the loop readable. The codes are the ones the shared atomic-file writes already treat as Windows-busy.

## Proof

`ownerLock.test.ts` makes the lock file unreadable with mode 000 (a real EACCES on Linux and macOS) and deletes it after 200 ms, as a finishing delete would:

- reported as Windows, the claim waits and then takes the lock; on main it throws EACCES at once
- on Linux it still throws at once
- an unreadable lock that never goes away still fails at the deadline
- a live owner still ends in the busy error at the deadline

20 runs in a row pass; the history suites (203 tests) and the package typecheck pass.

## No visible change

Nothing changes outside Windows, and nothing changes on Windows unless two processes race for one project's history.

title: perf(producer): the plan's true-peak check runs in parallel segments
body:
## What changes

A distributed render's plan checks the mixed audio's true peak (the -1 dBTP ceiling) with one `ebur128=peak=true` pass over the whole file. On a 30-minute render that single-threaded pass is one of the longest plan steps. It now runs as parallel segments and reports the **same value to the digit ffmpeg prints**, so the gain decision and the plan audio bytes do not change.

## Why the result is exact, not an estimate

From ffmpeg's source (n6.0, n7.0.2, n8.0.1 behave the same here):

- The true-peak meter oversamples 4x with a 32-tap filter. Each oversampled value reads 15 input samples back and 16 ahead.
- A meter that starts mid-file fills its missing history by mirroring its first samples. That can **invent** a peak: a 3-sample burst read 0.7 dB louder from a scan that starts on it than in the whole-file pass.
- A meter never measures its last 16 samples (no flush), so a cut can also **miss** a peak.
- In true-peak mode ebur128 reads fixed 100 ms blocks and logs each full block's peak (`FTPK`). The summary is the max over everything. Rounding to one decimal keeps order, so the max of printed values equals the printed max.

So:

1. Segments are whole 100 ms blocks. Every segment after the first starts one block early, and that first block's peak is dropped. That covers the previous segment's unmeasured tail and removes the mirrored-history values.
2. The first segment uses its summary. It starts at the file start, exactly like the whole-file pass.
3. The last segment uses its summary because its final partial block is only counted there. Its summary also includes the dropped first block. If that block alone could be the loudest value, the check runs one whole-file pass instead. This is rare (the test triggers it on purpose).
4. Each segment decodes from the start of the file and trims with `atrim`. It never seeks. The AAC decoder's noise substitution carries state across frames, so a seek could change samples. Decoding 30 minutes takes about 1.2 s and stops at the segment's end.

The segment count comes from the encoder's existing rule (`aacSegmentCount`: one per 60 s, at most 8), so it depends only on the duration, never on the machine. The peak value itself is not hashed. It decides whether and how the plan audio is re-encoded, and those bytes are hashed. Both are unchanged.

## Measured

**On AWS Lambda** (us-east-2, x86, 10 GB), a 30-minute 1080p30 composition with default flags. Same stack, cold start before every run, main and this branch alternating (3 runs each):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| plan step `audio-peak`, median (range) | 15.0 s (15.0-15.5) | 7.6 s (7.5-7.7) |
| whole plan step, median | 38.9 s | 30.4 s |
| submit to output file, median | 81.3 s | 73.8 s |
| plan Lambda billed time, median | 39.9 s | 31.3 s |
| plan Lambda max memory | 1797-1806 MB | 1801-1804 MB |
| planHash, plan audio sha256, output sha256 | identical in all 6 runs | identical in all 6 runs |
| cost per render (Lambda + Step Functions), range | $0.877-0.890 | $0.883-0.886 |

The plan Lambda bills about 8 s less per render; the remaining cost spread is the 204 chunk Lambdas, which this change does not touch.

**On a shared 8-core Linux box** (each job capped at 4 CPUs, load 5-15), using a 1800.5 s mix (not a whole number of 1024-sample AAC frames):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| plan step `audio-peak`, full v2 plan, 2 runs each | 8.5 s, 7.6 s | 5.8 s, 5.5 s |
| true-peak value, 30-min mix | -10.0 dBFS | -10.0 dBFS |
| planHash, 4 plans | identical | identical |
| plan audio sha256, 4 plans | identical | identical |

Whole-file vs segmented values were identical on ffmpeg 7.0.2 and 8.0.1 for: the 30-min mix (-10.0), a mix with a burst ending exactly on a segment cut (-2.0), silence (-inf), a 20.5 s clip that stays one segment (-19.7), and a loud mix (-0.1). On the loud mix, the plan's correction lowered the audio by 2.1 dB on both versions with byte-identical output (8462 packets identical: pts, dts, duration, size, flags, payload hash).

The step uses cores that are idle at this point in the plan; it does not add time. Peak memory: each ffmpeg here is about 24 MB, so 8 of them add about 165 MB for a few seconds.

## Tests

`audioTruePeak.test.ts` compares the segmented and whole-file values on 180 s WAVs (three segments). It covers a peak that ends on a cut, one at a middle segment's start, one at the last segment's start, and silence. Each guard was broken once and the test went red:

- no one-block pre-roll: a peak at the cut read -67 instead of 0.1
- counting the dropped first block: 0.8 instead of 0.1, twice
- no whole-file fallback: 0.8 instead of 0.1

The test file passed 3 runs in a row on ffmpeg 7.0.2 and 3 on 8.0.1. Rebased on main at #5917, `producer:test:unit` passes: vitest 966 passed, 1 skipped; bun 728 passed, 0 failed. Engine and producer typecheck are clean.

## Not covered

- The assemble-time pad/trim check still runs one whole-file pass. Only the plan's check changed.

title: fix(studio): keep an edit's preview waiting while the window draws no frames
body:
## What changes for a person

An edit that reloads the preview (an agent rewriting `index.html`, for example a 1920x1080 film turned into 1080x1920) now shows up once the window draws again. Before, if the window was behind other windows while the edit landed, the preview gave up after 45 s, kept the old film on screen and never retried. The person came back to a stale or black preview while the files on disk were fine.

## Why it happened

Studio swaps a reloaded film in through a hidden preview and promotes it once it is ready to show. That readiness is frame-driven: `Player` reports it two animation frames after the loaders clear. The 45 s wait (`SHADOW_READY_TIMEOUT_MS` x `SHADOW_READY_BUDGETS`) runs on the wall clock and pauses only when `document.visibilityState` is `hidden`. Some Linux desktops stop drawing frames for a window that is behind others while the page still reports `visible`. The wait then ran out with no frame drawn, and the swap failed with "The preview did not reload (it took too long to load). It was still waiting for its loaders to clear."

## The fix

`armReadyTimer` in `useShadowPreviewReload` is the one place a swap's wait is spent. It now asks for one frame when it starts a budget. A budget that ends without that frame is not spent. The frame's later arrival restarts a full budget, as showing a hidden tab already does. It restarts only if that swap is still waiting (`budgetGenRef`), so a promoted, failed or replaced swap is never re-armed. A window that draws frames keeps the exact timing it has today, and every existing timing test passes unchanged.

## Tests

`useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload.test.ts`, three new tests with a window whose frames are held while it reports visible:
- the wait is not spent while no frames are drawn, and the swap promotes once they return (fails on main);
- once frames return the swap gets its full budget, and a silent one still fails at the end of it (fails on main);
- a reload that replaced a starved one keeps its own budget when the old one's frame arrives (fails with the `budgetGenRef` guard removed).

Run on Linux: red on main (2 failed, 41 passed), then 3 runs in a row with the fix, exit 0, 44 passed. `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; oxlint 0 warnings, 0 errors on both files.

## Before

Studio dev server at `main`, a 1920x1080 project, the window's animation frames held while it reports visible, `index.html` rewritten to 1080x1920, then frames released. The old film is still showing after frames return, with the reload error.

![Before: the old 1920x1080 film is still showing after frames return, with the reload error](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/edde94f1-0760-40d0-b0a7-c4d143f38c8d)

## After

The same run on this branch: once frames return, the new 1080x1920 film is shown.

![After: the new 1080x1920 film is shown once frames return](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/34f79bb5-461a-453d-8494-5897f1e71ad7)

title: fix(core): recover refused audio automation with ramps
body:
## What

Recover audio automation after WebAudio refuses an overlapping curve. Cancel the conflicted schedule and rebuild the entire lane with ramps, retaining its endpoints and seed values.

## Why

WebAudio clamps a past curve start to its current clock without shortening its duration. The next segment can overlap that shifted curve, and its fallback ramp also throws. Clearing only that conflict and continuing with later curves prevents the exception but can replay already-elapsed audio: a sample-level reproduction showed gain rising from 0.5 to 0.7 at 32–36 ms when it should already hold 0.7.

## Related work

Addresses Jerrai's rendered-envelope feedback on the initial revision. Successful curve scheduling retains its bends. After a refusal, the whole lane degrades to linear interpolation; native-crash prevention remains unverified.

## How

On curve refusal, cancel the existing schedule and replay its sets and endpoints as ramps. Do not retry later curves, which would clamp forward again. The recovery seeds curve starts so future segments retain their intended initial values.

## Test plan

- New real WebAudio sample-level regression failed on the initial revision with a 0.2 gain error and passes after this change. It bundles the actual scheduler and checks every sample after suspension at 32 ms, both for an elapsed lane and an in-progress final ramp, with error below 0.000001. Both browser cases executed locally without skips.
- Stateful clamping regression verifies recovery leaves three ramps and no curves; successful future scheduling retains all three bends.
- Full core suite: 4,805 tests passed. Core build and core/runtime type checks passed.
- All 48 dependent engine audio-render/warmup tests and commit hooks passed. Hosted checks rerun on the revised head.
- Documentation: implementation explanation updated; no public API changed. Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

title: perf(cli): commands run without esbuild, puppeteer-core or sharp until they need them
body:
## What changes

A program that ships the CLI inside its own bundle can now leave out esbuild, puppeteer-core and sharp, or install them later, without breaking the commands that never use them. npm users see no change. esbuild and puppeteer-core stay regular dependencies. sharp moves to `optionalDependencies` in the CLI and `@hyperframes/studio-server`: npm still installs it by default, but a packager that walks declared dependencies no longer requires it.

- **esbuild, puppeteer-core:** loaded where they are used instead of at module load. A command that needs one and can't find it fails with Node's `Cannot find package 'esbuild'` error, naming the package.
- **sharp:** every use (preview image thumbnails, website capture, remove-background, `snapshot --describe`, contact sheets for `compare` and `snapshot`, `grade-compare`) goes through one loader. It uses the installed copy when there is one: any version, found the way `require` finds it from the CLI, so a host can supply its own copy on `NODE_PATH`. When sharp is missing, commands install it once into the user cache, using the same first-use path as the other optional packages. Preview thumbnails start that install in the background and keep today's "thumbnails are off" warning until it finishes; the preview itself is unaffected.
- **`HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL`:** `=1` turns off every first-use install (sharp, onnxruntime-node, @google/genai). A comma-separated list such as `=sharp` turns off only those packages. The command then fails with `<package> is not installed, and HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL turns off installing it; <feature> needs it.` A host that ships its own copies sets this so the CLI doesn't download them itself. Documented in the CLI docs.
- **One install per package per run:** callers running at the same time share it. A failed install is not retried in the same process, and preview thumbnails show its real reason.
- **Website capture without sharp** fails before downloading anything. Before this, a missing sharp would have been counted as an "unavailable" image for every asset.
- **Build check:** `bun run check:cli-lazy-deps` runs in the Build job and fails on any static import of these three anywhere in `packages/cli/dist`.
- **Duplicate runtime file:** the CLI stopped shipping a second byte-identical copy of the runtime (`dist/hyperframe-runtime.js`, 538 KB). Every reader already accepted `hyperframe.runtime.iife.js`, except one, which now looks for it first.

## Why

Before this PR, one static import in a shared chunk made a package load for every command that reached that chunk. Measured on the published 0.8.180 with esbuild, puppeteer-core and sharp deleted from the install:

| command | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--version` | ok | ok |
| `init` | `Cannot find package 'puppeteer-core'` | ok |
| `info`, `compositions` | `Cannot find package 'puppeteer-core'` / `'esbuild'` | ok |
| `lint` | exit 1 | ok, 0 errors |
| `validate` | `Cannot find package 'puppeteer-core'` | `Cannot find package 'esbuild'` (needs it to bundle) |
| `compare` | `Cannot find package 'sharp'` | `Cannot find package 'esbuild'` (needs it to bundle) |

The causes were few: two esbuild imports in core's bundler and runtime builder, four puppeteer-core value imports (two error classes checked with `instanceof`, one error constructed, one `instanceof CDPSession` in the engine), and four static sharp imports in the CLI.

Notes on the choices:
- The two puppeteer error checks that must stay synchronous now compare the error's constructor name. That matches exactly what `instanceof` matched in puppeteer-core 25, which isn't minified and has no subclasses of these. A page error or an abort signal's `DOMException` that only carries the name `TimeoutError` still does not match.
- `snapshot --describe` keeps its fallback: it resizes with sharp only when sharp is already installed, never installs it, and otherwise sends frames unresized up to the size cap, as before.
- `instanceof CDPSession` and `new TimeoutError` use `await import("puppeteer-core")` in functions that were already async, so class identity is the same module instance as before. Loading through `createRequire` would not guarantee that.
- The loader puts sharp loads ahead of the existing `try/catch` blocks that turn any error into "not an image", so a failed install can't silently reject every image.
- The installed copy is both resolved and loaded with `createRequire` from the CLI, like the pinned optional packages. `import()` ignores `NODE_PATH`. Two tests that mocked `sharp` directly now mock the loader instead.

## sharp as an optional dependency

Packed CLI tarball, installed with npm (install scripts on, as npm users get them):

| install | sharp | `init`, `info`, `lint`, `compositions`, `validate` | `compare` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm i <tarball>` | installed, with its libvips build | ok | ok, no install line |
| `npm i --omit=optional <tarball>` | absent | ok | `installing sharp for contact sheets, once`, then ok; the second run installs nothing |

In the packed manifest, `sharp` sits under `optionalDependencies` and not `dependencies`. tsup externalizes `dependencies` but not `optionalDependencies`, so studio-server's build now lists sharp as external explicitly. Without that, the package-size budget check caught studio-server inlining sharp's JavaScript. esbuild still loads under `--omit=optional`, because its own install script fetches its platform binary. Both `compare` sheets are the same size. A test pins sharp as optional in both manifests.

## What a user sees on first `compare` when sharp is missing

```
installing sharp for contact sheets, once
◇  Comparison sheet saved to …/compare.png
```
The second run prints no install line. Offline, with no cached copy:
```
✗ Compare failed: contact sheets needs sharp, and installing it failed (npm error code ECONNREFUSED). Check your network connection, then retry, or install it yourself: npm install sharp@0.35.3 --prefix "<cache>/sharp@0.35.3"
```
With `HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL=1` or `=sharp`:
```
✗ Compare failed: sharp is not installed, and HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL turns off installing it; contact sheets needs it.
```
With sharp only on `NODE_PATH`, `compare` works and nothing is installed. With sharp installed (the normal npm install), nothing changes.

## Size

Built from the same main commit on Linux x64, packed with `npm pack` and installed from the tarball in an empty folder:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `npm pack` tarball | 7,308,712 B | 7,142,427 B |
| CLI `dist/` | 22,066,101 B | 21,530,383 B |
| install tree | 105,652,643 B | 105,116,925 B |

The install tree barely moves because npm still installs all three by default. What changes is that a host can now remove them: esbuild with its platform binary is 10.5 MB, puppeteer-core 6.2 MB, and sharp with its libvips build 29.6 MB on Linux x64.

## Verification

- A build of this branch passes `check:cli-lazy-deps`. A build of main fails it with all 10 static imports listed (esbuild 2, puppeteer-core 4, sharp 4).
- Run alone, each covering test file exited 0, 460 tests total. That covers the sharp loader, background removal, content extractor, image validation, icon classifier, contact sheets, capture timeouts, screenshots, navigation, snapshot and compare sheets, grade-compare, studio-server thumbnails and light entries, core's bundler, the engine's frame capture, and the runtime file-race tests. The new tests and the check-script test passed 3 runs in a row.
- One deliberate break per new test, each red, then restored: install skipped, background install started twice, network advice dropped, sharp version outside the CLI's range, thumbnail loader not retrying, thumbnail warning repeated, the install shared by no one, the background path never consulting the install, the package list ignored or untrimmed or blocking everything, sharp not loaded before the asset download, `err.name` instead of the class name, the test's puppeteer stand-in without `TimeoutError`, `--describe` requiring sharp, sharp resolved the way `import` resolves it (no `NODE_PATH`), env var ignored, raw load error instead of the named one, remove-background skipping the loader.
- `tsc --noEmit` on cli, core, engine and studio-server, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow audit, comment citations and comment ratchet: all clean.
- End to end on a packed tarball (the tables above): main and this PR with the three packages deleted; sharp deleted, online, offline, with `HYPERFRAMES_NO_OPTIONAL_INSTALL=1` and `=sharp`, and supplied only on `NODE_PATH`; and a control with nothing deleted. The control's `compare` sheet and the sharp-deleted one are the same size.

## Pre-review

An independent reviewer read the head before the last commit, trying to break it. It found 1 blocker, 2 major and 4 minor issues. Each was reproduced, then either fixed with a test that fails on the old code or kept on purpose:

| Severity | Finding | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Blocker | A test's puppeteer-core stand-in had no `TimeoutError` (the red `Test (runtime)`) | fixed |
| Major | Website capture counted a missing sharp as unavailable images | fixed: fails before downloading |
| Major | Concurrent first uses ran npm once each | fixed: one install per package per run |
| Minor | Thumbnails said "installing" after an install failed or was turned off | fixed: they show the real reason |
| Minor | `err.name` matched page errors that only carry the name | fixed: class name |
| Minor | The lazy-deps check reads only top-level statements | kept: static imports are always top-level |
| Minor | `snapshot --describe` now needs sharp | fixed: the old no-sharp fallback is back, tested with sharp absent and installs off |

Not exercised end to end: the background thumbnail install in a live preview. That path is covered by a unit test only.

## No visible change

With dependencies installed as npm installs them by default, every command behaves as before.

title: feat(cli): cloud render uploads heavy media as HeyGen assets

Before zipping, media of 5 MB or more that the project names by path uploads as HeyGen assets, and the zip's copy of each HTML, CSS, script and JSON file points at the asset URL.
