title: fix(aws-lambda): lambda sites create uploads source files over 2 GiB and 5 GB
body:
## What

`hyperframes lambda sites create` (and any Lambda render that uploads its project) now works with source files over 2 GiB and over 5 GB, such as long 4K camera takes.

## Why

- The site id hash read every file whole. Node refuses to read a file over 2 GiB in one call, so `sites create` failed on large videos.
- Every file went to S3 in one PutObject, which S3 caps at 5 GB.

## How

- **Hashing** reads each file in 8 MiB chunks. The bytes hashed are the same, so every existing site keeps its id: 88 fixture projects in the repo hash identically before and after, and a test pins a small project's id.
- **One owner for multipart.** `multipartUpload` in `s3Transport.ts` creates, completes, and aborts on failure. The S3 stitch now uses it instead of its own copy.
- **Files over 5 GiB** go up in parts of max(64 MiB, size / 10,000), 8 in flight. Each part is hashed from disk, then streamed from disk, so memory does not grow with part size or file size. A part whose connection drops is resent from a fresh read (a streamed body cannot be replayed by the SDK's own retry).
  - Each part carries its SHA-256, and S3 checks it.
  - The uploader hashes the whole file over the bytes it sent. If that hash does not match the content address, the upload is aborted instead of completed.
  - Completion is conditional (`IfNoneMatch: *`) and pins the total size, so the content store stays write-once.
- **Files up to 5 GiB** keep the single PutObject exactly as before.
- **Render-time check.** For a multipart object S3 stores only a checksum of the part checksums, not the whole-file SHA-256. A presigned source over 5 GiB with a `COMPOSITE` checksum is therefore accepted by its recorded sha256 and size. Anything up to 5 GiB still needs S3's whole-object SHA-256, as before.
- **Content-store refresh** used CopyObject, which also caps at 5 GB. An aging object above that is now refreshed by a multipart copy onto itself.
- `uploadFileToS3` (render outputs, plan tarballs) also switches to multipart above 5 GiB.

## Tests

Each new test was checked against a targeted break of the code, and each break turned only that test red:

- A 4 GiB + 1 sparse file hashes to an id computed outside the code. On main it fails: the whole-file read runs out of memory.
- A 5 GiB + 1 file goes to the content store in checked parts with a conditional complete. A fake S3 rejects single PUTs and CopyObject over 5 GiB, as S3 does.
- A file whose bytes no longer match its digest is aborted, never completed.
- An aging object over 5 GiB is refreshed in copy parts.
- Presign accepts a composite checksum only above the single-PUT limit.

aws-lambda: 205 pass, 0 fail. producer `projectHash.test.ts`: 8 pass. Typecheck, lint, format and fallow are clean.

## Upload speed and memory (5.37 GB file, Node 22)

Measured against a local S3 stand-in that discards the bytes, so this is the client's own ceiling, not the network's. Two runs each:

| | MB/s | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| parts held in memory, 4 in flight (first head) | 731 / 762 | 550 / 482 MB |
| parts streamed from disk, 8 in flight (this head) | 695 / 710 | 158 / 152 MB |

Real S3 (us-east-2), same machine and link, Node 22, run back to back:

| | MB/s | peak RSS |
|---|---|---|
| single PUT of a 1 GiB file (aws cli), the link's one-connection ceiling | 3.8 | n/a |
| first head: parts held in memory, 4 in flight, 5.37 GB | 8.5 | 734 MB |
| this head: parts streamed from disk, 8 in flight, 5.37 GB | 11.6 | 127 MB |

During the last run one part's connection failed mid-stream (the SDK logged "non-retryable streaming request"); it was resent from disk and the upload completed. All three objects in the bucket are 81 parts, full size, and their recorded sha256 equals their key. No multipart uploads were left over, and the stack was torn down afterwards.

## Live run (real AWS stack, deployed from this branch's CLI)

- `hyperframes lambda sites create` on a project with a 5,369,757,696-byte video: exit 0, `uploaded: true`, peak memory 840 MB under Bun (the file is 5.4 GB; first head, parts held in memory).
- S3 holds it as an 81-part object (`ChecksumType: COMPOSITE`) whose recorded sha256 equals the local file's.
- `presignVerifiedS3GetUrl` from this branch signs it, and a ranged GET returns the file's first bytes. A wrong size is refused with `PLAN_ARTIFACT_DIGEST_MISMATCH`.
- Running `sites create` again: same site id, `uploaded: false`, 9 s.
- Small projects: old and new hashing take the same time on the repo's 88 fixture projects (256 KiB reads).

title: perf(studio): the npm package is 1.8 MB smaller without the web app only the CLI serves
body:
## What

`@hyperframes/studio` stops publishing the Studio web app (`dist/index.html`, `dist/assets`, `dist/icons`, `dist/favicon.svg`). The library build, `dist/styles.css` and every export are unchanged. Studio's size budget follows the package down.

| `npm pack` of `@hyperframes/studio` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Packed | 5,693,281 B | 3,875,995 B (-1.82 MB) |
| Unpacked | 22,892,498 B | 16,465,827 B (-6.43 MB) |
| Files | 1,662 | 1,649 |

`hyperframes` (the CLI) is unchanged: 7,141,900 B packed, 21,398,434 B unpacked, 585 files, both runs.

## Why

The studio build writes the web app into the same `dist` as the library. Nothing reads it from the npm package:

- **No bin, script or export serves it.** `packages/studio/package.json` has no `bin`. `dev` runs Vite on the source `index.html` at the package root; `build` writes `dist`. The published exports are `.`, `./ui`, `./player`, `./tailwind-preset` (all `dist/*.js`), `./theme.css` and `./components.css` (`src/styles`), `./styles.css` (`dist/styles.css`, kept) and `./package.json`. None of them names `index.html`, `assets` or `icons`.
- **The CLI ships its own copy, built from the workspace.** `packages/cli/scripts/build-copy.mjs:67-72` copies `index.html`, `assets`, `icons` and `favicon.svg` from `packages/studio/dist` into `packages/cli/dist/studio` at build time. `packages/cli/src/server/studioServer.ts:132-138` serves `dist/studio` next to the CLI, or `packages/studio/dist` in the monorepo; it never resolves `node_modules/@hyperframes/studio`.
- **Local studio mode does not use it either.** `packages/cli/src/commands/preview.ts:1511` needs `vite.config.ts` in the installed package, which the tarball has never shipped, so that mode only runs from a source checkout.
- **CI's studio smoke runs the Vite dev server** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, "Start studio and check for runtime errors"), not the built app.

A consumer whose Tailwind `@source` points at all of `@hyperframes/studio/dist` keeps every class the library uses. I compiled such a stylesheet with Tailwind 4.3.3 against 0.8.181, with and without the web app: 0 selectors gained, 59 lost, and the lost ones are generic words from third-party code bundled into the app (`table-row`, `grayscale`, `antialiased`).

## How

- `packages/studio/package.json`: `files` keeps `src` and `dist` and excludes the four web-app paths. The build still writes them, so the CLI's copy step is untouched.
- `scripts/package-size-budgets.json`: studio's budget becomes the values `verify:packed-manifests` asks for (measured size + 5%). Without this the ratchet fails the PR; with it, putting the web app back fails CI.

## Test plan

Full `bun run build` from a clean install, then:

- `npm pack --dry-run` of studio with the old and new `package.json` on the same build: the table above. After: no `dist/index.html`, 0 files under `dist/assets/`, `dist/styles.css` present.
- CLI `dist/studio` against the workspace build: `index.html` and `favicon.svg` have the same sha256, the 5 asset files are identical, `icons` is identical.
- `bun run verify:packed-manifests`: exit 0, "Verified 14 packages are within their size budgets", after a clean packed consumer install, Node execution, NodeNext declaration check, Vite resolution and CLI startup.
- Guard is not vacuous: with the old `files` (web app back in), `verify:packed-manifests` exits 1 with "@hyperframes/studio packed size 5715940 bytes is over its budget of 4088338" and the same for unpacked. Restored: exit 0.

## No visible change

Packaging only: the Studio UI, the CLI's `preview` and every library export are byte-for-byte the same.

title: fix(cli): a scoped keepsMoving capture ignores the page background behind it
body:
## What was wrong

Follow-up to #5960, from the review there. A scoped `keepsMoving` capture hides every box outside the scope. But the root background (and a body background that propagates to it) paints the page canvas whatever its `visibility`. So with a page background that changes over time, a still `withinSelector` scope's frames differed, and the span was read as moving instead of `motion_frozen`.

## The fix

- During a scoped capture, the isolation style also clears the `html` and `body` backgrounds, unless one of them is the scope. The screenshot is then taken with a transparent background, so nothing outside the scope's subtree reaches the frame.
- With the page cleared, painted and empty pixels can differ in alpha alone (black content revealed on the cleared page), so `framesDiffer` now compares alpha as well as RGB. Unscoped captures are opaque, so the sweep is unaffected.

## What I measured

- Checked in Chromium first: before this change, changing either the `body` or the `html` background changed a scoped capture of an unchanged element.
- New Chromium pins in `checkSweep.chromium.test.ts`, each failing when its part of the fix is removed:
  - a still `#title` over a changing `html` background stays `motion_frozen` within `#title` (fails without the background rule);
  - a black mask reveal inside a scope counts as motion (fails when alpha is ignored).
- An existing pin, a white stroke reveal inside a scope, fails if the scoped capture is opaque instead of transparent (the cleared page then defaults to white).
- `check.test.ts`, `checkBrowser.test.ts`, `checkSweep.chromium.test.ts`, `motion-signature.browser{,.chromium}.test.ts`: 244 passed, 0 skipped, three runs in a row.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Windows. The Chromium suites are opt-in there.

title: feat(core): capture motion blur runtime lifecycle
body:
## What

Wires the pure modules from #5875 into the composition runtime.

- `captureMotionBlur/index.ts`: reads the root's `data-motion-blur` attributes (`on`/`off`, `-shutter` 0–720° default 180, `-samples` 2–64 default 16, `-events="on"` to run timeline callbacks at sub-frame samples), scans for movers once per timeline, wraps the root in a capture canvas with an output canvas after it, and draws each frame in two phases (capture the root and crop the movers, hide them and capture the background, then redraw each mover along its path). `window.__hfMotionBlur.report()` says whether blur is on and, when it is off, why.
- `init.ts` / `entry.ts`: the runtime hooks (init, seek, play / pause, and a final-frame release that the engine and CLI capture wait on), and tracking of WebGL canvases.
- `pageMotionBlur.ts` and the `@hyperframes/core` export of `PAGE_MOTION_BLUR_OFF_GLOBAL`, the switch the engine sets to tell the page to stand down. Nothing sets it until #5969.

A frame whose paint never comes (2000 ms after release) is not left half-wrapped: the root goes back into the document as plain DOM, the movers are revealed, the failure is counted in `report().failedFrames` and logged once per 25, and the engine's late composite step finds nothing to finish. A paint timeout never counts toward giving up (`failures` keeps its streak meaning) and the next frame wraps again.

Blur turns itself off, and logs why, when html-in-canvas or `drawElementImage` is missing, when the engine's own sub-frame blur is on, when the composition already nests a capture canvas, or when a WebGL canvas is present or appears after init.

## Why

Part 2 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5875, which has the modules this wires together.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. Nothing blurs without `data-motion-blur="on"` on the root.

## Notes

- The root is wrapped in the capture canvas only while playing or rendering, and only when the scan found movers. Paused or scrubbing it is plain DOM, so Studio click-to-select works. Compositions with nothing moving are never wrapped.
- Pose reads are timeline seeks (no paint), interpolated with a decomposed affine.
- Preview needs html-in-canvas: Chrome 155 and earlier need `chrome://flags/#html-in-canvas`; 157 and 158 builds expose it without a flag (whether it ships in stable is not confirmed).
- This PR is the lifecycle skeleton. Device-pixel output, the render fallback for capture exceptions, the lifecycle hardening and the tests for the painting paths are in #5968; render routing and Studio are #5969; the html-in-canvas defect list is #5971.
- A user seek while a blurred frame is in flight is not specially handled: the frame in flight is not abandoned, and the request waits as the newest pending one (documented, not fixed).
- Limits inherited from #5875 apply (trails over foreground elements, a halo on transparent movers, trails leaking past `overflow:hidden`, a fast child inside a parent that moved earlier is not blurred, SVG elements are not scanned).

## Testing

`captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts` (opt-in and off switches, each reason blur stays off, wrapping and unwrapping, and paint timeouts: a released frame whose paint never comes ends as plain DOM with the failure counted, for a first frame whose output was never drawn and for a frame after one that painted, in engine mode, plus a preview run; each guard was shown to fail with its mutation applied) and `entry.test.ts` (WebGL canvas tracking is installed with the runtime). The tests for engine-driven frames, painting, and unwrap-on-pause come with #5968. `bun run build`, core `tsc --noEmit` and the core runtime tests pass; comment ratchet against #5875's branch passes; core stays under its size budget.

title: feat(core): harden the capture motion blur runtime lifecycle
body:
## What

Hardens the runtime lifecycle from #5967 so it holds up on real compositions, in preview and in renders.

- **Device pixels.** The capture and output canvases and the compositor's buffers follow the page's scale (a render's injected scale wins over a `devicePixelRatio` that fell back to 1), so a 2x or 4k render is not blurred at half resolution.
- **A render never gives up mid-video.** A frame whose capture throws is plain DOM and the next frame wraps again (counted in `failedFrames`, logged once per 25). In Studio preview, three capture exceptions in a row turn blur off for the session. Paint timeouts, which render plain and never end blur, are handled since #5967; here `failedFrames` also counts capture exceptions. A tab that stops painting while the clock keeps running (hidden or minimized) used to turn blur off for good after about 6 s.
- **A hidden preview tab rests on plain DOM.** While `document.visibilityState` is `hidden` the preview does not wrap and requests no paints (a hidden tab delivers none); blur resumes when the tab is visible again. Engine mode is unaffected.
- **Timeline callbacks stay out of the scan.** The mover scan and its restore seek always suppress events, so `tl.call()` callbacks no longer fire during discovery even with `data-motion-blur-events="on"`; only the sub-frame pose reads honour `-events`.
- **Wrapping the root no longer disturbs the page.** Wrap and unwrap move the root in the document; each move now runs through the runtime's record filter (`host.ignoreMutations`) and the adapters re-seek at the current time right after it. Measured before the fix (Chrome 152, 6 play/pause cycles): CSS animations restarted at 0 for one displayed frame on every unwrap, and the runtime's `MutationObserver` read each move as a composition change (18 stage-size and 12 timeline posts instead of 2 and 1).
- **Studio preview holds the playback seek while a blurred frame is in flight**, so the poses and both captures belong to the same time and a fast box keeps its full width. `init.ts` gets a small hold (the transport skips a playback seek while a blurred frame is busy; the next tick catches up), with its own test.
- **`adapters/waapi.ts` (shared runtime code, a small separate hunk):** after a wrap Chrome cancels the moved element's CSS animation and starts a new one, and the adapter kept reviving the cancelled (idle) one. The adapter now drops an idle animation, only when it is browser-created (`CSSAnimation` / `CSSTransition`); script-created animations are left alone. Please review that hunk on its own: it is the one change here that affects every composition, not only blurred ones.
- The host exposes `now()` for the re-seek.

## Why

Part 3 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5967.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. The correct frame is always preferred over a blurred wrong one: when the capture cannot be trusted for a frame, that frame renders sharp from the plain DOM.

## Notes

- Blurred preview frames update at half the display rate: a two-phase frame needs two paints, and the transport holds its seek until the frame completes. The pixels are correct; the rate is the cost.
- An iframe in the root still reloads when the root is wrapped; the defect list that blocks blur for it is #5971.
- Limits unchanged from #5875 and #5967 (trails over foreground elements, a halo on transparent movers, trails leaking past `overflow:hidden`, 2D flips through `scaleX = 0` blend as rotation, a fast child inside a parent that moved earlier is not blurred).
- Nothing in this PR changes a composition that does not set `data-motion-blur="on"`, except the `waapi.ts` hunk above.

## Testing

- `captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts`: wrapping and unwrapping (including the quiet-then-re-seek order and no re-seek when there is nothing to unwrap), the two-phase frames, painting and unwrap-on-pause, the render fallback, the hidden-tab rest, the opt-in switches that moved here from #5967 (shutter clamp, a browser without `drawElementImage`, the reason logged for a root that asked for blur, a nested capture canvas, opting back out, a composition where nothing moves; the paint-timeout tests now live in #5967), the callback spy for the scan, device-pixel canvases, and the guards that survived a deliberate break (exactly three failures, no seek below zero, `unwrap()` removes the hide rule, canvases and hide attributes, invisible movers are not blurred; each was shown to fail with its mutation applied).
- `compositor` device-pixel test in `composite.test.ts`; `init.blurHold.test.ts` for the preview hold; `adapters/waapi.test.ts` for the narrowed idle skip.
- `bun run build`, core `tsc --noEmit`, and the core runtime tests pass; comment ratchet against #5967's branch passes; core stays under its size budget.

title: feat(producer,studio): wire capture motion blur into renders and Studio
body:
## What

Carries capture motion blur through renders and Studio, and tightens which elements the scan blurs.

- **Engine:** `installPageMotionBlur` sets `PAGE_MOTION_BLUR_OFF_GLOBAL` before any page script runs, when the engine's own sub-frame blur is on (`--motion-blur`) or when the render must match a Studio preview that could not blur, and tells the page the render's device scale. `CaptureOptions.pageMotionBlur` carries the request.
- **Producer:** a composition whose root (the one the runtime would pick: `data-root="true"` first) sets `data-motion-blur="on"` gets a `captureMotionBlur` render-mode hint and goes through screenshot capture, because html-in-canvas needs a real paint; it is not pinned to one worker. A script-set attribute is not seen: it has to be in the HTML. The probe session carries the request's `pageMotionBlur` like every other session, so "off" survives a render with no `data-duration`.
- **Studio and Studio server:** each render request carries `previewMotionBlur`, true only if Studio's own browser has `drawElementImage` and `requestPaint`. The render route turns `previewMotionBlur: false` into `pageMotionBlur: "off"` once, so the Studio dev server and the CLI server both receive the final value.
- **Mover scan:** a large element that is see-through while it moves (a translucent sweep, a light leak, a large image or canvas with alpha) is no mover, because its crop would carry the scene beneath it along its path; its fast children still blur. An opaque large photo still blurs; `<video>` counts as opaque. The scan also skips elements moved by a 3D `rotate` axis or a z `translate`.
- **CLI `snapshot`:** injects video frames before the seek settles, matching the engine's order.

## Why

Part 4 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5968; this is where a render can use the runtime.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. Nothing blurs without `data-motion-blur="on"` on the root.

## Notes

- WYSIWYG: when Studio sends `previewMotionBlur: false` the render has no blur, even for opted-in compositions.
- Engine sub-frame blur (`--motion-blur`) and page blur never both run.
- Cost: about 1.7x median render time for a blurred composition. k3-promo, 16.5 s, 1080p30: no blur 13 s, capture motion blur 28 s, engine `--motion-blur` 27 min. Compositions that are blocked or static cost nothing extra.
- Output can differ across worker counts, at about the size of the chunk-split noise a render without blur already has; making every worker's scan find the same movers is #5990.
- `<video>` in Studio preview: a video drawn through the capture is about 2–3% darker than normal playback, visible as a small brightness change on play/pause. Renders are unaffected (video frames are injected as images). Accepted.
- Not detected as see-through movers, so they are treated as opaque: a CSS `background-image`, `mask-image` or `clip-path` that lets the scene show through; an element that is see-through over less than half of the scene is not recognised as a sweep. A large image or canvas whose pixels cannot be read (cross-origin) counts as see-through and is not blurred. All documented, not fixed.
- Limits that apply to what a render now shows: trails are drawn over foreground elements above a mover; a transparent mover carries a halo of its background inside its box; trails leak past `overflow:hidden`; a 2D flip through `scaleX = 0` blends as rotation; sub-pixel `left` steps land in whole pixels; a fast child inside a parent that moved earlier is not blurred; SVG elements are not scanned.
- Not in this PR: blur does not yet check for the things html-in-canvas captures wrongly (#5971); the engine side that tracks WebGL canvases before page scripts is #5970.

## Before

k3-promo at 9.1 s, no motion blur:

![Before: no motion blur](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fab1e3ba-3a49-4df6-8f9d-15e971181e8c)

## After

Same frame with capture motion blur (360° shutter): the pins, the text and the box smear along their paths.

![After: capture motion blur](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce1ae69b-7be0-4dde-8e23-bc8bc72ca75b)

## Testing

- Engine `pageMotionBlur.test.ts`: the off switch for engine blur and for an unsupported preview, device scale.
- Producer `htmlCompiler.test.ts`: the render-mode hint on the runtime's root, not applied when the preview could not blur; `probeStage.test.ts`: the probe session carries `pageMotionBlur`; `renderOrchestrator.test.ts` and request validation: `pageMotionBlur` is passed through and only `"off"` is accepted.
- Studio-server `render.test.ts` and CLI `studioServer.renderBrowser.test.ts` / Studio `vite.adapter.render.test.ts`: the adapters receive `pageMotionBlur: "off"` for `previewMotionBlur: false`; Studio `useRenderQueueMotionBlur.test.tsx`: the request body carries it.
- Core `discover.test.ts`: translucent, fading, colour and paint-less sweeps are no mover, opaque ones stay, large images and canvases with and without alpha, 3D individual transforms; CLI `snapshot.test.ts` and `captureCompositionFrame.test.ts`: the order of video injection and seek.
- `bun run build` and `tsc --noEmit` in core, engine, producer, cli, studio-server and studio pass; comment ratchet against #5968's branch passes; no package size budget changes.

title: feat(core,engine): track accelerated canvases before any page script runs
body:
## What

Makes the tracker that spots WebGL / WebGPU canvases see the cases that slipped past it, and counts the frames that fell back to plain DOM.

- The accelerated-canvas tracker (`pageMotionBlur.ts`) is now a self-contained function. Besides wrapping `getContext`, it wraps `transferControlToOffscreen`: a canvas handed to an `OffscreenCanvas` creates its WebGL context out of reach, so a transferred canvas counts as accelerated. Its registry lives on `window`, so independent installs agree.
- It runs before any author script. The engine evaluates it on every new document (`installPageMotionBlur`); `insertRuntimeTag`, used by the bundler and Studio's preview, puts it at the very start of `<head>` for pages that opt into blur; the runtime's own install is idempotent with both. Before, it was installed when the runtime evaluated, so a context made by an earlier author script was missed. Either miss left a frozen (Chrome 152) or black (Chrome 157) capture with blur still on.
- `report()` carries `failedFrames`, the cumulative count of frames that rendered plain DOM because their capture failed or timed out. `failures` keeps its streak meaning (it resets after a success), so an "on" report can no longer hide a render where captures keep failing.
- Core's unpacked size budget goes from 3,903,211 to 3,930,000 bytes. With the lifecycle, the compositor and the tracker, core measures 3,903,549 here, just over the old budget; the rest of the stack needs about 3,925,300 at its tip, so the ceiling is raised once, with about 4.7 KB of headroom, rather than in several PRs.

## Why

Part 5 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5969, which added `installPageMotionBlur` in the engine.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. A frozen or black canvas inside a "blurred" frame is a wrong frame, so the runtime has to know about every accelerated canvas, whenever it was created.

## Notes

- This PR only makes the runtime *see* those canvases; what it does about them (turn blur off, and say so) is the existing behaviour, extended to the full defect list in #5971.
- The tracker is a function whose source is injected, so it must stay free of imports and closures (its `toString()` is evaluated as a script).
- The engine's log line that prints `failedFrames` for a session arrives with the runtime's reason codes in #5991.

## Testing

- Core `pageMotionBlur.test.ts`: the tracker records `getContext` WebGL / WebGPU canvases and transferred canvases, is idempotent across installs, and its source runs standalone.
- Core `htmlDocument.test.ts`: the tracker goes at the start of `<head>` for a page that opts into blur, once, and not for a page that does not.
- Core `captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts`: blur stays off for a canvas handed to an `OffscreenCanvas`; `failedFrames` counts every fallback frame though the failure streak resets; engine `pageMotionBlur.test.ts`: the tracker is the first script installed.
- `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit` in core and engine, and their tests pass; comment ratchet against #5969's branch passes (the tracker's doc comment is two lines, to stay at the file's comment share); every package is within its packed and unpacked size budget.

title: feat(core): block capture motion blur on html-in-canvas defects
body:
## What

- **A defect list for html-in-canvas** (`htmlInCanvasDefects.ts`). Before the runtime wraps a composition it checks for things html-in-canvas captures wrongly; a hit turns blur off for the whole composition and the runtime says which one. In this PR: a nested capture canvas (nesting hangs the renderer), a WebGL / WebGPU canvas in the root (captured frozen; Chrome 157 fixed it), `backface-visibility: hidden` inside a 3D context (drawn mirrored), an `<iframe>` in the root (the wrap moves the root in the document and reloads the iframe, which cannot be undone), a transform on the root (ignored by the capture) and opacity below 1 on the root. Some entries apply only to a range of Chrome versions.
- **The backface scan sees more of the page's CSS:** rules nested inside a style rule (CSS nesting, with `&` resolved against the parent), sheets pulled in with `@import` (their `styleSheet`, read once each, depth capped, unreadable cross-origin sheets skipped), and adopted style sheets. Before, a nested or `@import`ed rule that computes `backface-visibility: hidden` was missed and blur stayed on with a mirrored face.
- **A face that gets `backface-visibility: hidden` from an animation is a candidate too.** The scan also takes the targets of running CSS and WAAPI animations (`document.getAnimations()`, keyframes that key `backfaceVisibility`) and, for an animation not instantiated yet (a delay, a class added later), any element whose computed `animation-name` names a `@keyframes` rule that sets it. Candidates are confirmed exactly like inline and stylesheet ones: computed hidden plus a 3D context. Before, an `@keyframes`- or `element.animate()`-only flip face had neither an inline declaration nor a rule declaring it, was never read, and with another ordinary mover the runtime stayed on and wrapped the root (reviewer finding on this PR). One `getAnimations()` pass per scan; the keyframes walk reuses the sheet walk above and the per-element read only happens when some `@keyframes` rule sets the property. Measured on a 5,000-element root (Chrome 152, scan time): 26 ms before and after; with an unused `@keyframes` rule that sets the property, 30 ms.
- **Chrome 157 support.** 157 replaces `<canvas layoutsubtree>` with `<canvas content="drawable">` plus a `drawable` attribute on captured children. The new `@hyperframes/core/html-in-canvas` subpath detects and handles both forms; blur, the VFX runtime and Studio's browser check use it. Studio's `useRenderQueue` now asks it whether the browser can blur.

## Why

Part 6 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5970.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. A wrong blurred frame is worse than a sharp one, so blur steps aside rather than draw it.

## Notes

- Shadow DOM is not scanned for backface: a hidden face inside a shadow root is not found. A flat `backface-visibility: hidden` used as a performance hack (no 3D context) is deliberately not blocked. The same holds when the hack arrives through an animation.
- The engine's fast capture still uses the old html-in-canvas API and only runs on the pinned Chrome 152; it needs the same migration before the pin moves.
- #5990 widens three entries of this list: a root `scale` / `rotate` / `translate` counts as a root transform, a root `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` is a defect, and the iframe entry covers `<object>`, `<embed>` and defined custom elements (individual `rotate` axes and z `translate` count as 3D for the backface check).
- The defects are checked when a frame is about to be drawn. Deciding them once per timeline, on every Chrome version, and sharp-frame-only handling of what the scan misses come in #5990.
- A defect on a composition sub-tree other than the root is not specifically handled; `data-motion-blur` on a sub-composition is ignored.
- A composition with an iframe in its root now stays unblurred instead of reloading the iframe on every wrap; #5968 made wrapping itself quiet for everything else (CSS animations, observers).

## Before

k3-promo at 9.1 s, no motion blur:

![Before: no motion blur](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fab1e3ba-3a49-4df6-8f9d-15e971181e8c)

## After

Same frame with capture motion blur (360° shutter): the pins, the text and the box smear along their paths.

![After: capture motion blur](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ce1ae69b-7be0-4dde-8e23-bc8bc72ca75b)

## Testing

- `htmlInCanvasDefects.test.ts`: every defect, with Chrome versions on both sides of each version bound, the iframe on every version, the nested-rule / `&` / `@import` / adopted-sheet cases (a self-importing sheet is read once; an unreadable one is skipped; a chain past the depth cap stops), and the first-match order. The animation-derived candidates: a face hidden by `@keyframes` (named, in a list of names, or not matching any name), a face a running animation keys to `hidden` (a non-hidden keyframe ignored, a target outside the root ignored).
- `htmlInCanvas.test.ts`: form detection and marking for both the `layoutsubtree` and `drawable` forms; `vfx.test.ts` (the VFX runtime uses the helper); runtime tests for blur staying off on each defect, including an iframe present at init and one added later; Studio `useRenderQueueMotionBlur.test.tsx`.
- `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit` in core and studio, and the touched packages' tests pass; comment ratchet against #5970's branch passes; no package size budget changes (core stays under the budget #5970 set).

title: perf(engine): cloud renders cut a video's audio from its URL instead of downloading the file
body:
## What changes for a user

A cloud render whose project holds long videos no longer downloads each video in full during the plan step just to take its audio. The plan now reads only the stretch the edit uses, straight from the file's signed link, the same way chunks already read video frames. The audio that comes out is byte-identical.

## Why

`processCompositionAudio` maps a project file that lives only in cloud storage to its signed URL (`urlByAbsentLocalPath`), then hands that URL to `downloadToTemp` and only afterwards trims the span it needs. So plan time and transfer tracked the size of the source files, not the length of the edit. The video extractor already uses the same map's URL in place (`videoFrameExtractor.ts`); the audio path now does too, at the one place every cloud-held audio source goes through.

- Cloud-held project files: passed to ffprobe/ffmpeg as the URL, with the existing `urlInputArgs` (TLS verify, reconnect).
- The on-disk checks (`existsSync`, the text-document sniff) apply only to local files, as on the video path.
- Authored `http(s)` sources are unchanged: still downloaded first.
- A URL probe gets the render's abort signal and is retried once, then fails the track: a network blip must not silently change how the next, successful read is mixed (local files keep today's fallback).

## Evidence

Probe with a range-serving HTTP server (30 ms first-byte delay) and a 10 min 1080p25 take (12 Mbps video, AAC audio, mov, 865 MB), cutting 247 s (41% of the take) to 48 kHz PCM:

| | requests | bytes read |
|---|---|---|
| before (download, then cut) | 1 | 865,230,769 (100%) |
| after (cut from the URL) | 4 | 360,788,125 (41.7%) |

The WAV cut from the URL and the WAV cut from the local file are byte-equal (`cmp`). ffmpeg reads the edit span straight through (video packets included), so transfer now follows the edit's share of the file. A Lambda before/after on a long 4K source follows on this PR.

Tests, each file run alone on Linux:
- `audioMixer.test.ts`: exit 0, 71 passed. Mutations, each restored after: disable the in-place branch -> the URL test fails; move the TLS flags after `-i` -> the URL test fails; swallow a failed URL probe -> the probe test fails (each run: 1 failed, 70 passed).
- `aacEncode.test.ts`: exit 0, 7 passed, 3 runs in a row. Its noise source had no seed, so `anoisesrc` drew a new random signal every run and a 0.1% margin flipped now and then (seen on a Windows lane); both noise sources are now seeded.

## Independent review

No blocker. One major (the new test needed a Linux/macOS CA bundle path, so it failed on Windows) and its follow-ups are fixed in this head. Kept as notes: an in-place read that fails is labelled as an extract/system failure rather than a download failure, the same as the video path's in-place reads; the plan step retries any failure either way.

Audited: every caller of `processCompositionAudio`, `extractAudioSegment` and `urlInputArgs`; how the plan builds the URL map and which files the Lambda leaves remote; URL redaction in errors and logs; URL lifetime against the plan's run time; byte-equal output from a range-served URL vs the local file (ffprobe JSON, tail probe, both extract shapes).
Trusting: ffmpeg's `-reconnect` flags for mid-read stalls.
Not exercised: Windows and macOS runs of the URL read beyond CI.

## On AWS Lambda

One stack (10,240 MB, us-east-2), same site, direct plan invokes, every run cold, code swapped between main and this branch. Source: one generated 50 min 1080p25 take (12 Mbps H.264 + AAC, 4.7 GB `.mov`), composition cuts 20.6 min from 15:00.

| run | plan `audio` stage | plan total (billed) | max memory |
|---|---|---|---|
| main 1 | 75.0 s | 118.3 s | 6,051 MB |
| main 2 | 74.1 s | 108.1 s | 6,048 MB |
| this branch 1 | 34.6 s | 77.0 s | 1,370 MB |
| this branch 2 | 34.8 s | 77.9 s | 1,338 MB |

The plan's audio file has the same sha256 in all four runs. The stack and its buckets were deleted after the runs.

Full 4K renders (3840x2160, 25 fps, 1,237 s cut from two 50 min HEVC takes of 1.8 GB and 4.5 GB, default flags, cold):

| run | plan | plan `audio` | wall (submit to assembled) | output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 107.2 s | 93.6 s | 227.4 s | sha256 `0a0cba17de86…` |
| this branch 1 | 55.5 s | 42.1 s | 174.2 s | sha256 `0a0cba17de86…` (identical) |
| this branch 2 | 55.8 s | 42.8 s | 174.9 s | sha256 `0a0cba17de86…` (identical) |

title: perf(core): Safari stops re-serializing inline styles on every GSAP write
body:
## What this fixes

Safari spent about a fifth of a playing film's main thread re-serializing inline styles. The runtime always injects a stylesheet that hides a hidden clip's contents with `[data-hf-clip-hidden][style*="visibility: hidden"] *` (plus SVG filter variants). A `[style]` attribute selector above the matched element makes WebKit treat the style attribute as needed for invalidation, so every inline style write re-serializes the element's whole style to text (`invalidateStyleAttribute` → `asTextAtom` → `asTextInternal`). GSAP writes `transform` and `opacity` on every animated element every frame, so a GSAP-heavy film pays that on every write. Chrome serializes lazily and doesn't pay it.

The rule now matches the runtime's own mark only:

- `[data-hf-clip-hidden][data-hf-clip-hidden] *` hides a hidden clip's contents. The attribute is doubled to keep the old rule's weight, so author rules that lost to it still lose. The visibility pass sets the mark and the inline `visibility: hidden` together (`init.ts`), as before.
- The Studio preview's image-skip rule matches the same mark instead of the inline style.
- Code that forces a hidden clip visible goes through one helper, `revealClip` in `@hyperframes/core/runtime/clip-reveal`. It sets the inline visibility and lifts the mark together and returns the call that puts the mark back, so a revealer cannot do one without the other:
  - the runtime's first-render reveal (`showHiddenClips`);
  - a shader transition's captured copy (`showSceneAndClips`);
  - the page-side compositor's scene copies in renders (`prepareComposite`), which are thrown away, so nothing is put back;
  - Studio's layer reveal, which puts the mark back only when it restores its own visibility;
  - Studio's gesture preview, which puts it back on release.
- shader-transitions bundles the helper from core at build time (`noExternal`, as the player does), so it gains no install dependency. Its build grows by the helper alone: 255,276 → 255,415 bytes ESM, 255,962 → 256,101 CJS, 255,775 → 255,914 IIFE (+139 each; +87, +71, +76 gzipped). The mark name appears once and no other core module is pulled in.
- The engine's 3D projection needs no change. It copies each original element's computed style onto its clone and rasterizes the clone in its own SVG image, where no runtime stylesheet applies. The originals carry the mark and the inline hide together, so the old and new rules match the same elements.

## Compatibility path for published shader-transitions builds

Builds of `@hyperframes/shader-transitions` already on npm and the CDN reveal scenes by inline style only. They can't lift the mark. Under the mark-only rule, a film loading one of them (a pinned version, or the unpinned CDN URL before it serves this release) would render an empty incoming or outgoing scene for part of every shader transition across a scene boundary.

**Decision (Miguel):** keep published builds rendering, chosen over shipping with a minimum shader-transitions version and a lint warning on older pins, and over holding the change.

- Builds from this change call `declareClipRevealAware()` on load.
- Once composition scripts have run, the runtime checks for a shader build on the page (its `HyperShader` global, or `__hf.transitions`) that did not declare. If it finds one, it rewrites its two injected rules back to the inline-style form (`keepInlineHideRulesForOlderShaders`). Those films render as on `main` and keep Safari's old cost. Every other film gets the fast rules.
- The flag is internal to the runtime, the same way as the existing `__hfSuppressSceneMutations`: no new authored attribute and no author-facing API.
- **When it can go:** once shader-transitions versions older than this release are no longer supported for rendering. Removing it means deleting `keepInlineHideRulesForOlderShaders`, its call in `entry.ts`, `olderShaderBuildOnPage` and the inline-style selector.
- A build loaded after the runtime starts (a script injected late) isn't detected and gets the fast rules. Shipped templates and guides load it with a plain script tag.

## Behaviour change

An author's own script that sets `visibility: visible` inline on a timed clip element while the runtime hides it no longer reveals that clip's children; they stay hidden until the runtime shows the clip. The runtime owns a timed clip's visibility, and the old behaviour cost every GSAP film this tax in Safari. Revealers inside HyperFrames (Studio, shader transitions) go through `revealClip`.

## Measured

WebKit 26.5 on a physical Mac (M4 Pro), the player playing at 960x540, page main thread from an Instruments Time Profiler trace, 6 s per run:

| | frame rate | page main thread | main thread per frame, p95 / max | frames over 8 ms (of ~385) | inline style serialization |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| two-minute GSAP film, 400 tiles, before | 32.3 / 33.4 fps | 298 / 310 ms/s | 12 / 14 to 16 ms | 94 / 96 | 19 to 20% |
| same, after | 34.6 / 34.7 fps | 191 / 193 ms/s | 7 / 9 to 10 ms | 7 / 4 | 0% |
| `gsap-heavy` film, before | 60.0 fps | 230 ms/s | 6 / 8 ms | 0 | 19% |
| same, after | 60.1 fps | 174 ms/s | 5 / 8 ms | 0 | 0% |

On AC power, two runs per arm, the old and new builds served side by side and alternated in one session. Two earlier sessions on battery in Low Power Mode (WebKit capped at 30 fps for both builds) gave the same CPU picture: 318 to 329 ms/s before, 202 to 206 after. The long film's remaining limit is painting in WebKit's GPU process, which this PR does not touch.

### Chrome, synthetic 4K film, after merging main

Chrome 152 headless on a 32-core Linux host with no GPU, so every frame is painted in software. The film is 3840x2160: 92 timed video tiles (about 31 playing at once), a scene of about 7,000 divs and 500 SVG paths that GSAP writes inline styles to every frame, and 40 later scenes, about 100 hidden clips in all. The player plays it as in Studio's preview for 10 s per run. The two builds alternate (`main` at this branch's merge base, then this head), three runs each, then one traced run each. The host was shared, with load average 10 to 25.

| | `main` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| frame rate, runs 1 / 2 / 3 (median) | 12.4 / 15.0 / 9.8 (12.4) | 18.0 / 13.7 / 12.0 (13.7) |
| dropped frames per second, median | 47.6 | 46.3 |
| style recalculation share of main-thread time (traced run) | 36% | 12.5% |
| elements restyled per recalculation, median / max (traced run) | 51 / 7,900 | 1 / 898 |

The CPU result is clear: an inline style write no longer restyles the hidden-clip rules' descendants, so most recalculations touch one element. Frame rate barely moves on this host, because software painting of 31 playing 4K-scaled videos dominates each frame. The noise between runs is larger than the gap.

### Chrome, same 4K film, on a GPU host (Apple silicon)

The same film, builds and method on an Apple silicon Mac on AC power with Low Power Mode off: Chrome 152 headless, painting on the GPU (Metal through ANGLE, with GPU compositing, rasterization and video decode enabled). Three alternating runs each, then two traced runs each. The host was shared, with load average 8 to 16.

| | `main` | this head |
|---|---|---|
| frame rate, runs 1 / 2 / 3 (median) | 56.3 / 59.1 / 56.5 (56.5) | 57.8 / 59.7 / 56.8 (57.8) |
| dropped frames per second, median | 3.5 | 2.2 |
| worst frame, runs 1 / 2 / 3 | 33 / 33 / 50 ms | 33 / 33 / 33 ms |
| style recalculation share of main-thread time (traced runs) | 48% / 46% | 21% / 20% |
| style recalculation / main-thread busy time over 10 s (second traced run) | 2.1 s / 4.6 s | 0.57 s / 2.8 s |
| elements restyled per recalculation, median / max (traced runs) | 7,842 / 7,898 and 7,740 / 7,898 | 842 / 898 both |

With a GPU, both builds play close to the 60 fps headless Chrome draws at, and the gap between their medians (1.3 fps) is smaller than the spread between runs of one build (about 3 fps). This host shows no frame-rate gain beyond noise. The CPU result repeats: style recalculation falls from under half of the main thread to a fifth, and the main thread is busy about 40% less for the same 10 s of playback, which shows up as headroom rather than frames here.

## Tests

- `timedClipHide.test.ts`:
  - No rule the runtime injects (playback or Studio preview) selects on inline style. This test fails on main.
  - A clip's contents are hidden by the mark alone; the fixture has no inline hide, so it fails on main.
  - The contents rule keeps the weight of two attribute selectors, asserted on the selector because jsdom settles `!important` ties by order.
  - `showHiddenClips` and `revealClip` lift the mark and put it back.
  - Compatibility path: with an older shader build on the page (found by its global or by `__hf.transitions`), a scene it revealed by inline style shows its text and images, and a hidden one stays hidden. With a build that declared, the fast rules stay and none of them selects on inline style.
- shader-transitions: the page-side compositor's copy of a marked scene and of its timed clips carries no mark and is visible, while the live scene keeps its mark. The html2canvas copy shows a marked scene's contents. Loading the package declares it.
- Studio: one test each for the layer reveal and the gesture preview (lift, then put back).
- Each new test was checked by breaking its code: compositor copy without `revealClip`, the compatibility path returning early, a single-attribute contents rule, and the package not declaring. Each break turned exactly its own test red.
- Real Chrome (`coreRuntimeBrowser.test.ts`), in a render and in a preview:
  - An inline style write restyles only its own element, not the hidden-clip rules' descendants. Fails with the contents rule keyed on inline style.
  - A hidden scene paints nothing, even a child or SVG shape a rewound GSAP set made visible inline. Fails without `!important` on the contents rule.
  - A scene copy forced visible inline shows its contents with an older shader build on the page and stays hidden with a current one. Fails with the compatibility path off, and with it applied to declared builds.
  - Preview images in hidden scenes stay skipped until the scene shows. Fails when the skip rule ignores the mark.
  - A later scene's child shows again after a seek or render seek past the GSAP set that hides it, and filter tweens start from the stylesheet filter. Fails when `showHiddenClips` keeps the mark.
  - Main's filter-output tests (SVG shapes, HTML layers, the scene, pseudo-elements) pass on the mark-keyed rule. They fail when the rule drops the pseudo-element layers.

## Render output

Seven existing producer fixtures, rendered to PNG at `main` and with this change (Chrome, one worker), every frame hashed:

- Byte-identical: `timed-descendant-visibility` (270 frames), `many-cuts` (168), `sub-comp-t0` (180), `page-side-shader-compositor-render-compat` (60).
- Not comparable: `style-1-prod` and `overlay-montage-prod` differ between two renders of `main` itself (96 frames for the montage).
- Changed: `gsap-letters-render-compat`, 35 of 120 frames, the same on every render. **The cause is the removed selector itself, not a change in what is hidden:** adding back a rule that never matches, `[data-hf-never][style*="never"] * {}`, restores `main`'s bytes exactly. A `[style]` selector anywhere in the page changes how Chrome paints elements whose inline transform changes each frame; without it, the edge antialiasing of the rotating letters moves by under a pixel. Frame 77: 730 edge pixels of the "H" change, PSNR 43.9 dB (the fixture's floor is 30). The edges are no softer: 518 partially covered edge pixels against 608 on `main`, with the same total edge contrast.

## CI note

The Windows `engine-cli` test lane timed out in three CLI network tests this change does not touch: the `publicNetwork` controlled-socket integration hook (30,000 ms limit), and in `cloud/download` "splits a large file into parallel ranged requests" (20,494 ms) and "streams the whole file in one request when the server ignores Range" (20,004 ms), both against a 20,000 ms limit. The same workflow passed on `main` at this branch's base. They are handed over as Windows flakes; the failed jobs are rerun at this head.

## Before

`gsap-letters-render-compat` frame 77 at `main`, the "H" cropped and scaled 4x over black:

![Before: the H in frame 77 at main, 4x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/00c748c8-be6c-4200-9bbf-67189791893d)

## After

The same crop with this change: the stroke edges land a fraction of a pixel differently, no softer.

![After: the H in frame 77 with this change, 4x](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/249414be-e58c-45f8-a722-3966e0fe466a)

## Render across a scene boundary (page-side compositor, MP4)

The `page-side-shader-compositor-render-compat` fixture with `scene-b` moved to start at 1.2 s, inside the 0.75 s to 1.6 s glitch transition, so the runtime marks the incoming scene for the transition's first half. Rendered to MP4 with page-side compositing on (the default), video frames compared by decoded-frame MD5:

| runtime | older vendored shader build | shader build from this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `main` vs this head | identical, 60 of 60 frames | identical, 60 of 60 frames |
| `main` vs this head without the compatibility path | frames 0 to 48 differ: the incoming scene loses its contents during the transition, and the encoder's lookahead carries that into earlier frames | not rendered |

Frames 26, 30 and 34 with the older shader build. Left to right: `main`, this head without the compatibility path (no "BETA"), this head:

![Frames 26, 30, 34 with the older shader build: main, head without the compatibility path, head](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ad4313bf-7573-4b99-9433-17982e5a8192)

title: fix(cli): check waits for late images and runs its browser pass in unnamed macOS sandboxes
body: ## What `snapshot`, `compare` and `check` now wait for images that load late, the same way `render` does, so their frames show what the rendered video shows. Before, the settled page these commands shoot from gave late images at most 1.5 s and then went on with no warning. An image added after the page's load event and served in 3 s came out black in `snapshot --at 0.5` (both frames, exit 0, no warning), while `render` of the same composition showed it at 0.5 s and 1.9 s. ## How - Engine: render's image wait (poll every `` until it loads or fails, report the ones still loading at the deadline, decode the loaded ones) is now one exported function, `waitForImagesReady`. Render's two capture paths call it with their existing warning, word for word. - CLI: `openSettledCompositionPage` calls the same function after its 1.5 s settle, with render's timeout (`playerReadyTimeout`, 45 s by default). If an image still hasn't loaded by then, it prints `⚠ Some images did not load within ms: . They may show blank.` - Fetch-only data keeps the 1.5 s settle as before; only `` elements wait longer, the same as render. ## Cost When every image has already loaded, the wait is a single page evaluate that returns at once. An image that never answers now holds `snapshot` and `check` for up to the 45 s timeout and then warns, the same as render does today. Before, they went on at 1.5 s and the frame was wrong. ## Tests - New `captureCompositionFrame.lateImage.browser.test.ts`: a red image added after load and served at 3 s; the settled page's screenshot must be red at the center. On main it is black (`[0, 0, 0]`); with the fix it is `[255, 0, 0]`. 3 runs in a row green, together with the existing `lateSubresources` test. - The same composition by eye with the built CLI: `snapshot --at 0.5` frames are black on 0.8.181 and red with this branch. - CLI capture, snapshot, compare, check-browser, motion-shot and validate test files: 692 tests, all green once the mocked engine in `captureCompositionFrame.browserFallback.test.ts` gained the new export (that file had failed with "No waitForImagesReady export is defined on the mock"). - Engine `frameCapture` tests: 30 files, 297 passed. - Engine and CLI `tsc` clean, oxlint and oxfmt clean. ## Also: check's browser pass inside a macOS sandbox that does not name itself This fixes a regression from #5943, which is not released yet. - **What broke:** since #5943 every CLI Chrome launch uses a pipe. Inside an agent's macOS seatbelt that does not set `CODEX_SANDBOX`, Chrome's child processes cannot register their mach port and the browser dies while starting. A pipe launch reports that only as `Protocol error (Target.setDiscoverTargets): Target closed`, without Chrome's stderr. The one-process fallback added in #5836 keys on the `bootstrap_check_in ... Permission denied` line from that stderr, so it never fired, and `check` skipped its whole browser pass (exit 1). - **Reproduced:** `check --json` on a small video project under a Codex `workspace-write` seatbelt with `CODEX_SANDBOX` unset: on main, exit 1, browser pass skipped, the error above. 0.8.181 passes the same case (its first launch used a port, whose failure carries the stderr). With `CODEX_SANDBOX=seatbelt` set, main passes too. - **Fix:** on macOS, a pipe launch whose connection closed while starting (Puppeteer's `TargetCloseError`, matched by its name so the CLI's startup chunk does not import puppeteer; puppeteer stays external and unminified in the CLI build) relaunches once as one process over the pipe, the same fallback #5836 uses. Any other protocol error, and our own launch timeout, still fail as before. Other platforms are unchanged. - **Proof:** with the built CLI of this branch, the same sandboxed command exits 0 and runs the browser pass, with and without `CODEX_SANDBOX`; `check-cli-lazy-deps` passes on that build. - **Tests:** `sandboxDenied.test.ts` gains three cases: on macOS a closed pipe launch relaunches as one process; on macOS any other protocol error stays failed; on Linux a closed pipe launch stays failed. 3 runs in a row green. Each case fails under its mutant: the new condition removed (main's behaviour), any `*Error` retried, the macOS-only check removed. - **Not covered:** the field reports of the same error on 0.8.169-0.8.181 come from a separate path that I have not reproduced (those versions launched over a port first). This change does not claim to fix them.

title: fix(producer): a render no longer publishes a short or wrong-size video silently
body:
## What

A render can no longer publish a video that is shorter or smaller than it asked for without saying why. macOS renders keep their captured frames out of the project folder, and a 4K export of an HDR project is refused before Chrome starts, with advice that actually applies.

- Frame-sequence encodes (mp4/webm/mov, chunked, GIF) run ffmpeg with `-xerror`. An unreadable frame file now fails the encode at that frame, and the error names the frame and the OS error.
- On macOS the render's scratch folder (captured frames, intermediates) moves to the system temp folder, as it already does on Windows. Linux keeps it beside the output.
- The final output check compares the encoded width and height with the size the render asked for, not only duration and frame count.
- A non-native `--resolution` with HDR footage is refused as soon as the HDR route is known, before calibration launches Chrome. The message names the real ways out: `--sdr`, or the project's own size. Before, it fired after calibration and suggested "mp4 with page-side compositing", which does not apply to HDR footage.

## Why

A field report: `render --format mp4 --fps 25 --quality delivery --crf 16 --workers 4 --sdr` captured all 695 frames, then failed with `Render artifact is truncated: expected 27.800s, probed 15.040s`. The same render with `--workers 1` was fine.

What happens:

1. Several workers capture to disk. One worker streams frames straight into the encoder, so `--workers 1` never touches frame files.
2. The capture stage checks that every frame file exists and is not empty before the encode starts.
3. The encode hands ffmpeg the pattern `frame_%06d.jpg`. When ffmpeg cannot open or read a file in the sequence, its image reader logs `Error during demuxing` and ends the input there. ffmpeg still exits 0. Reproduced on ffmpeg 7.0.2 and 8.1.1: 100 frames with frame 37 unreadable gives a 36-frame video and exit 0.
4. The encoder reports success, the mux runs, and only the final duration check notices, with no hint of the cause.

The frames were all on disk and the cut points are arbitrary, not worker boundaries, so something outside the render made a frame file unreadable at the moment ffmpeg reached it. On macOS the scratch folder sat beside the output, inside the project. Projects in folders that iCloud, OneDrive, Nextcloud or Dropbox sync hand every new frame file to the sync client while the encode is reading them. The reporter's project was in such a folder. I could not reproduce the trigger itself: four runs at the reporter's flags on Linux (disk route, screenshot capture) came out complete.

## Decision and tradeoff

Scratch in system temp on macOS was a deliberate call: sync clients never see the frames. The cost is that frames now land on the system volume. A project on a large external drive, on a Mac with a small internal disk, hits the disk-space check sooner. That check still measures the folder the frames are written to (`inspectDiskCaptureHeadroom(framesDir)`), so it now measures the system volume and fails loudly with its existing remedy. Linux is unchanged: its `/tmp` is often RAM-backed or small in containers.

`hyperframes clean` already sweeps abandoned `hf-render-*` folders in the system temp folder, and every new render reclaims them, so nothing else changes for cleanup.

### Output size check and the 4K HDR refusal

A field report: a 4K MP4 export of a 1080x1920 project with an HLG clip said "Export ready", and ffprobe showed 1080x1920 HEVC 10-bit HLG. That reproduces on 0.8.167. Since #5724 (0.8.168) the HDR route refuses a scaled output, so main no longer writes the wrong size. Two gaps remained:

- **Nothing checked the result.** The final output check compared duration and frame count only. Any route that ignores the requested size would publish silently again. It now compares width and height too. An odd side may come out one pixel larger, because 4:2:0 encodes pad it.
- **The refusal came late, with the wrong advice.** It fired at capture planning, after the calibration pass had already launched Chrome. HDR content always takes the layered route (page-side compositing requires no HDR content, and HDR output requires mp4), so the refusal now runs where HDR content is decided. The route guard stays for the shader-transition case and every replan.

**Provisional product call, pending the maintainer's confirmation:** a 4K (or any non-native size) HDR export is refused up front, naming `--sdr` or the project size. Real scaled HDR output is not built unless asked for. The earliest point that knows a project has HDR footage is the producer's source probe, so the refusal lives there, not in the CLI's pre-flight (which reads only the HTML).

## Related work

None open on this path.

## How

- `buildEncoderArgs` (the args builder for both frame-sequence encoders) puts `-xerror` first. `buildGifPal*Args` add it to the frames input.
- `-xerror` also makes a corrupt frame fatal. Today such a frame is silently dropped and the previous one repeated. Failing is the honest outcome for captured frames.
- ffmpeg's read error is printed before the encoder's summary, which pushes it out of the 15-line stderr tail we report. `frameReadFailure` pulls that line out and names the frame where reading stopped, from the frame count ffmpeg reached.
- ffmpeg prints the unreadable file and the OS reason on separate lines, and on Windows the file line comes first, so both are reported.
- `streamStartOffset.test.ts` gets the 30 s fixture-cleanup budget the other real-ffmpeg suites have had since #5368. Its cleanup timed out at vitest's 10 s default on a Windows runner in this PR's CI, after all 16 of its tests passed.
- `resolveRenderWorkDirPrefix` returns the system temp prefix for `darwin` as well as `win32`.

The extra flag adds no encode work: with all frames readable, the output is byte-identical with and without `-xerror` (md5 checked on ffmpeg 8.1.1).

## Before / after

Before (main), encoding a sequence where one frame cannot be read:

```
success: true   (36-frame video from 100 frames; the render later fails with "Render artifact is truncated")
```

After:

```
[FFmpeg] could not read a frame at frame_000010.jpg (10 of 20 read): [in#0/image2 @ ...] Error during demuxing: Is a directory
FFmpeg exited with code 235
```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `chunkEncoder.unreadableFrame.test.ts` (real ffmpeg): a 20-frame sequence with one unreadable frame (a directory under the frame's name, so it holds for any user, including root) must fail at `frame_000010.jpg` with the OS error. A chunked encode does the same at `frame_000015.jpg`. Both fail on main (the encode reports success). 3 runs green with the fix. Removing `-xerror` alone turns both red.
  - `renderOrchestrator.test.ts`: macOS resolves under the system temp folder, Linux stays beside the output. Removing `darwin` turns the macOS case red.
  - `encodeStage.test.ts`: the pinned GIF args now include `-xerror`.
  - `artifactTransaction.test.ts`: a file probed at 1080x1920 when 2160x3840 was asked for is rejected; a one-pixel pad on an odd side is accepted; the expectation carries the requested size. The rejection and size-carrying cases fail on main.
  - `outputScaleRoute.test.ts`: the refusal names `--sdr` and mp4, not page-side compositing. Fails on main.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the branch CLI rendered a 1080x1920, 27.8 s, 25 fps fixture (6 sub-compositions, 10 videos, 5 audio tracks, blend modes) three times at the reporter's flags, on the disk route with screenshot capture: 695 frames, 27.8 s each time. So `-xerror` does not trip on Chrome's screenshot JPEGs.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"
- Not run: a macOS render with the branch (the `darwin` path is covered only by the unit test). Engine `chunkEncoder.test.ts` (103), producer `renderOrchestrator.test.ts` (282), `encodeStage.test.ts` (23) and `gifEncodeArgs.test.ts` (4) pass on Linux, along with oxfmt, oxlint and the comment ratchet.

title: feat(registry): add echo-smear component
body:
## What

Adds `registry/components/echo-smear/`: a distance-adaptive streak for elements moved by a GSAP timeline. As an element moves faster, more time-offset copies trail behind it; below a speed threshold there are none. It is After Effects' Echo effect (Maximum operator) with the copy count and spacing driven by the element's own speed.

```js
attachEchoSmear(".card", tl, { length: 100, threshold: 40 });
```

`attachEchoSmear` records each target once with a quiet forward sweep of the timeline (no callbacks fire unless `callbacks: true`): its resolved transform and opacity (individual `translate`/`rotate`/`scale` folded in), filter, clip-path, transform-origin, visibility and offset box at 8 samples per frame. It then draws copies from that record, so a frame depends only on `tl.time()`, never on the path taken to it.

- Count: `round(travel * length/100 * countMult)` when the measured point moved more than `threshold/2` over the last half frame, then raised so the element's farthest corner moves at most `edgeSpacing` px between copies (`edgeSpacing: 0` gives AE's exact count and visibly stepped spins), then capped at `maxEchoes`.
- Copies live in a zero-size, isolated group inserted just before the target. The target is not wrapped, moved or restyled (parent, blend mode, pointer events and Studio picking are untouched). The group takes the target's z-index and visibility.
- Copies carry the target's resolved style through one shared class rule per target, are built to the peak count the recording shows (a target that never smears gets none), and are combined by brightest pixel.
- Ships `demo.html` (a logo skims under a word, kicks each letter up, then spirals away; formula-driven, no hand-keyed tables), `README.md`, `registry-item.json`, and `echo-smear.test.mjs` wired into `test:scripts`.

## Known limits (documented in the snippet header)

- Copies are a snapshot of the element at its recorded time for the properties above; every other style and anything on a **child** (a cursor's click ripple) is frozen at attach. Children animated by their own tweens are not mirrored.
- Motion written through `left`/`top` is not measured; motion written from a callback needs `callbacks: true`.
- An element inside an `<svg>` is skipped with a warning (attach to the `<svg>`); a `matrix3d` is carried by the nearest sample; media inside a target becomes an empty box in the copies.
- Copies use `mix-blend-mode`, so a composition using it renders on the screenshot capture path, not drawElement (confirmed from the renderer log).

## Testing

- `node --test registry/components/echo-smear/echo-smear.test.mjs`: 47 tests. The pure seams (count, matrix parsing, box point, individual transforms, track interpolation) and the engine itself run through happy-dom with a fake timeline that renders the snippet's update before the target on a backward seek, like GSAP does. One test runs real GSAP 3.15 with a `.call()` and an `onComplete` that removes the target: nothing fires at attach. Each of ~25 mutations of the production code fails a test.
- Real GSAP in Chrome: identical painted state cold, after a seek to the end, and after forward-then-back, for an `autoAlpha` mover, a `translate`-only mover and a plain mover; `elementFromPoint` at the target returns the target and every ancestor reports `pointer-events: auto`; an element named twice in one call gets one group.
- Demo: `hyperframes lint` 0 errors (one file-length warning: the demo inlines the snippet), `check --no-contrast` 0 errors; the inlined snippet is pinned to the component by a test.
- Tried on repo blocks, rendered with and without the smear: `transitions-push` (static scene, renders), `blue-sweater-intro-video`, `transitions-light`, `news-ticker` (its `text_occluded` check error is in the original block too).
- Findings from review (Magi, two further code reviews) are fixed: callbacks firing at attach, an unpickable target, re-targeted copies, a stale-visibility reverse seek, individual CSS transforms, overlapping inputs, shadow roots, parent perspective, media children, SVG children.

## Not in this PR

- `registry/registry.json`: left to the catalog publish job, as in #5487.
- Catalog preview image (`docs/images/` is gitignored): a still of the demo and the demo mp4 are ready to attach.
- Whether After Effects caps Number Of Echoes at 10 or 100 is unverified; `maxEchoes` defaults to 60.

title: perf(producer): a cloud plan corrects its audio peak from the mix itself, in parallel
body:
## What changes

A cloud render whose mixed audio peaks above -1 dBTP gets through its plan about 17 s faster on a 20-minute film, and its audio ends up closer to the mix. The plan now re-encodes the peak correction from the float mix it already has, split across the encoder's parallel segments. Before, it decoded the AAC it had just written and encoded it again on a single encoder.

Local renders are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Why

On a 20.6-min hot mix, the plan's `audio-peak` step took 36.5-37.3 s on Lambda. The scan is not the cost (3.6 s on a 4-CPU box). The cost is the correction: one single-encoder AAC re-encode of the already-encoded m4a, plus a rescan. That re-encode was also a second lossy generation.

## How

- engine `processCompositionAudio` takes `keepEncoderInputAt`. After a successful float-sum encode it moves the PCM it encoded from to that path, instead of leaving it to be deleted.
- The cloud plan asks for it when chunks carry audio, passes it to `constrainAacTruePeak` as `sourcePath`, and deletes it after the check.
- With a master FX chain, the kept file is the post-FX WAV, since that is what the AAC was encoded from.
- `defaultAacEncoder` splits into parallel segments only when it encodes from that PCM. Anything that encodes from an AAC stays on one encoder, as it does today, which covers local renders' pad/trim and peak check. The reason is that each segment decodes its input from the start. From PCM that read is free; from AAC it is a second decode per segment. Dropping the one-encoder pin for AAC input was measured: only ~5 s saved and +4.7% RMS error on 20.6 min.

## Measured

Lambda, 10,240 MB, cold, same site, hot 50-min take cut to 20.6 min. Base = main with the URL audio cut; new = base + this change.

| run | audio | audio-peak | plan total | true peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| base 1 | 34.9 s | 36.5 s | 77.4 s | -1.8 |
| new 1 | 34.8 s | 19.6 s | 60.5 s | -1.3 |
| base 2 | 35.4 s | 37.3 s | 78.1 s | -1.8 |
| new 2 | 35.1 s | 19.9 s | 60.3 s | -1.3 |

The plan audio, compared with the source span: residual RMS 0.011920 (base) vs 0.008950 (new), 25% lower. Lag 0, same sample count, and both runs of each side gave the same sha.

A 4-CPU Linux box, residual RMS against the best-fit gain of the source PCM:

| | 60 s today | 60 s new | 20.6 min today | 20.6 min new |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| residual RMS | 0.029877 | 0.028666 | 0.027247 | 0.026300 |
| lag / samples | 0 / same | 0 / same | 0 / same | 0 / same |
| true peak | -1.4 | -1.5 | -1.4 | -1.0 |

Byte changes: a cloud plan whose audio needs the peak correction now produces different audio bytes, because it is encoded from the PCM. Audio that does not need correction is unchanged, and so is every local render. No regression golden runs the plan's peak path.

## Tests

- `audioTruePeak.fakeFfmpeg.test.ts`: the correction re-encodes the PCM in parallel segments, and an AAC with no PCM is re-encoded on one encoder. Each was mutation-checked by breaking that branch. 7 passed, 3 runs in a row; each break failed only its own test.
- `audioPadTrim.test.ts`: 37 pass, unchanged.
- `audioMixer.test.ts`: the float mix the AAC was encoded from is kept at the requested path.
