title: fix(cli): a finished capture exits even when a site's DNS never answers
body:
## What changes

`hyperframes capture` resolves every page request through its own proxy (`resolvePublicAddress`). It used the system lookup with a 10 s give-up, but a system lookup cannot be cancelled: when a page loads a host whose DNS never answers (a filtered tracker, a dead CDN name), the capture moves on and prints its result, and the process then stays alive until the OS resolver times out. On macOS that is tens of seconds to minutes, so a capture that had already succeeded could run past the desktop app's 5-minute cap, be stopped, and lose its folder.

A host is now resolved in this order, giving the answer the system lookup would give:

1. **The hosts file** (`/etc/hosts`, or Windows' `drivers\etc\hosts`), read once, IPv4 entries; the first line for a name is used and every line for it must be public. Overrides and `0.0.0.0` blocks keep working.
2. **A system answer already found** for this host in this capture.
3. **c-ares** (`dns.Resolver`), cancelled after 5 s, the same choice `hostAnswers` makes.
4. **The system lookup in a short-lived child Node process**, only when c-ares has no answer (OS-only DNS such as encrypted-DNS profiles or per-domain resolvers). It is killed at the 10 s deadline, and any child still running is killed when the CLI exits. It cannot run in the CLI process: measured in a private network with a DNS server that never answers, 5 pending system lookups held even `process.exit(0)` for 30.1 s (Node waits for its lookup threads at exit).

Capture also asks the CLI to exit 100 ms after printing its result (`scheduleCliExit`, moved out of `render.ts` so both commands share it). The root exit in `cli.ts` first waits (`outputWritten`) until stdout and stderr have handed everything already written to the reader, so a large result on a slow pipe arrives whole; a reader that never reads keeps the process, as it did before. The process-ownership check now treats `*.fixture.ts` like tests: each fixture runs as its own process. The lefthook pre-commit now also runs that check: a `process.exit` outside a process root passed the local hooks and failed only in CI's Preflight (it did on this PR).

**Cost:** hosts-file and c-ares answers spawn nothing. A host c-ares cannot answer costs one child, about 41 ms (32-48 ms on a loaded Linux box), once per host per capture. If c-ares times out rather than failing fast, that first request for the host also waits up to 5 s; later requests reuse the answer.

## Proof

Same source, same private network namespace on Linux: the page loads one image from a host whose DNS server reads queries and never replies (glibc timeout 60 s).

| | capture wall time | process alive after printing its result | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | 75.2 s | 38.3 s | ok, 2 screenshots |
| this PR | 35.9 s | 0.0 s | ok, 2 screenshots |
| this PR, site name only in the hosts file | 35.4 s | 0.0 s | ok, 2 screenshots |

On main, the handles alive after the result were only pending system lookups (`GetAddrInfoReqWrap`). The released CLI behaves the same as main here.

## Tests

- `publicNetwork.process.test.ts` (new, real child processes; 8 cases, 3 runs in a row): no DNS and a stalled system lookup times out and the process is gone within 1 s of printing; the system answer is used when DNS has none; a DNS answer is used without the system; the hosts file wins over DNS; a `0.0.0.0` hosts entry is refused, also as a second line after a public one; a CLI that exits mid-lookup leaves no lookup child running; the real child script resolves `localhost`.
- `publicNetwork.test.ts`: a system answer is checked like a DNS one and asked once per host; a caller joining a running lookup keeps its own deadline and skips c-ares; DNS answers never start the child.
- `commandResult.process.test.ts` (new, 3 runs in a row): a CLI held by a stalled handle prints a 1 MiB JSON result, forced exit runs, and a reader that pauses 100 ms per chunk gets all of it with exit 0. Without the wait it got 146,176 bytes.
- `capture.test.ts`: after printing its result, or after a capture that threw, capture asks to exit (0 or 1) within 100 ms.
- Mutants, each caught: hosts file skipped; no kill on exit; a joined lookup without its own deadline; the cache read after c-ares; the child script reading the wrong argument; no exit after a thrown capture; the child without its kill deadline; no fallback; no exit after the result; no `cancel()`; no c-ares timer cleanup; exit without waiting for output; hosts file keeping only the first line.
- Run alone, each exit 0: process 8/8, commandResult process 1/1, publicNetwork 37/37, integration 11/11, captureProxy browser 4/4 (real Chrome), hostAnswers 4/4, capture 25/25, ownership check 3/3, render 105/105, commandResult 3/3. oxlint, oxfmt, tsc, fallow, comment citations and ratchet: exit 0.

## Reviews (independent agents)

| Head | Severity | Finding | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| d372fa6b | MINOR | success case did not check the process exits | fixed |
| d372fa6b | MINOR | c-ares ignores the hosts file and OS-only DNS | fixed: hosts file first, system lookup fallback |
| e7bb8b0f | MAJOR | cache read only after c-ares failed (5 s per request for hosts-only names) | fixed in 00d153fe |
| e7bb8b0f | MAJOR | hosts-file overrides of names DNS answers were ignored | fixed in 00d153fe |
| e7bb8b0f | MINOR | real child script never run by a test | fixed |
| e7bb8b0f | MINOR | a joined lookup could stretch the wait to 15 s | fixed |
| e7bb8b0f | MINOR | a pending child outlived the CLI | fixed |
| e7bb8b0f | MINOR | exit after a thrown capture untested | fixed |
| 00d153fe (bot) | P2 | forced exit 100 ms after the result truncated a large JSON result on a slow pipe | fixed in 5c4d68cf and 1e90a054: the root exit waits for stdout and stderr |
| 00d153fe (bot) | MINOR | only the first hosts-file address was checked | fixed in 5c4d68cf |

Not exercised: Windows beyond CI, a real encrypted-DNS Mac.

title: fix(cli): init --video frames the project to the clip's shape, so nothing is cropped
body:
## What

`hyperframes init --video` now sizes the new project to the clip's own shape as it plays, with 1080 on the short side and the long side rounded to an even number. A 4:3 clip opens at 1440x1080, a 3:4 one at 1080x1440, and a 21:9 one at 2520x1080. Every preset already has a 1080 short side, so a clip that matches one gets exactly that preset: 16:9 is 1920x1080 (the template's own), 9:16 is 1080x1920, 4:5 is 1080x1350, 1:1 is 1080x1080. The stage matches the clip, so the whole picture shows with no bars and nothing cut. Before, every clip landed on the template's 1920x1080 stage with `object-fit: cover`, so a 9:16 clip lost 68% of its height.

This PR no longer edits a skill. Main retired `talking-head-recut` (#5651), and the core skill already says what this PR's skill edit said: no new aspect ratio unless the request or the source calls for one (`skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md`).

## Why

The clip already answers the shape question. Asking the person, or cropping their footage until someone notices, is the wrong default. Phone clips are often stored landscape with a 90° rotation, so the probe has to read the clip as it plays, not as it is stored.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `probeVideo` reports the size the clip plays at. Width is multiplied by the sample aspect ratio when the pixels are not square (a 720x576 PAL clip at 64:45 plays at 1024x576). Then the stream's rotation (display-matrix side data, else the legacy `rotate` tag) turns width and height upright.
- `clipFrame(templateId, clip)` picks the frame: the clip's played aspect with a 1080 short side, both sides even, and the template's own size when that comes out 1920x1080. It applies only to the `from-file` template, the one whose stage is the clip. An explicit `--example` keeps its own design, and an explicit `--resolution` always wins. Both the interactive and non-interactive paths pass `resolutionPreset ?? clipFrame(...)` to `scaffoldProject`.
- No new shared preset: `applyResolutionPreset` now delegates to `applyCanvasSize(width, height)`, which writes the stage size (data attributes, inline `html, body` CSS, viewport). Only a named preset stamps `data-resolution`, which nothing reads; render takes the size from `data-width`/`data-height`.
- The `--resolution` help text says what the default now is.
- The after-scaffold step (template telemetry and transcript patch) moved into one `finishScaffold` helper. Both paths ran the same lines, and fallow flagged them as a clone.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `init.test.ts` runs `init --video` on six fixtures and checks the composition root's size:
  - a 36x64 clip (1080x1920);
  - a 64x36 clip carrying a 90° rotation (1080x1920);
  - a 48x64 3:4 clip (1080x1440);
  - a 64x48 4:3 clip (1440x1080);
  - a 64x64 clip (1080x1080);
  - a 72x72 clip with 16:9 pixels, which plays at 128x72 (1920x1080).

title: test(cli): the Chrome orphan check waits for Chrome to exit instead of 5 s
body:
## What

The Chrome orphan test waits for Chrome to exit after the CLI is killed, instead of sleeping a fixed 5 s and checking once.

## Why

`leaves no Chrome process behind when the CLI is killed mid busy-loop` sends SIGKILL to the CLI, sleeps 5 s, then requires every Chrome process it saw to be gone. On a loaded Windows runner the watchdog needs longer than that to take Chrome down: two Chrome processes were still exiting at the 5 s mark (`expected [ 7164, 680 ] to deeply equal []`). That turned the Windows engine-cli lane red on unrelated PRs and on the release branch.

## How

The fixed sleep and its one-shot assertion become `waitForTestCondition(() => alive(run.seen.chrome).length === 0, 30_000)`, the same helper and budget the next line already uses for the watchdog. A Chrome process the watchdog never kills still fails the test, at 30 s instead of 5 s.

The 3 s pause before the kill stays: it only lets the page enter its busy loop and cannot make the assertion fail.

## Related work

Refs #5943 (added the test).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- `chromeOrphans.process.test.ts`: 3 runs green on Linux (the kill case takes about 5.3 s there).
- Non-vacuous: with the wait condition made impossible, the test fails with `Condition not met within 30000 ms`.
- The file has no fixed 5 s sleep left (`grep -c "setTimeout(resolve, 5_000)"` prints 0).
- Not run on Windows locally; this PR's Windows engine-cli lane is the check.

title: fix(engine): renders use the browser the CLI picked; Linux system Chrome is not beginframe
body:
## What

Two fixes to how renders pick their browser:

1. **One precedence for the browser env vars.** With both `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` and `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` set to different binaries, the CLI chose `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` and the engine launched `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH`. The preflight checked one browser while the render ran on the other. Both now resolve through one `browserPathFromEnv` (in `chrome-host-ceiling`, which both already import), with `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` first, as the CLI documents. The engine's `resolveConfig` no longer copies `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` into `chromePath`. That copy was checked before the env, so a CLI render still launched the `PRODUCER_` binary. An explicit `chromePath` still wins. One behaviour change: with a valid `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` set, a broken `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH` is no longer reported, because it is never used.
2. **System Chrome on Linux is no longer counted as headless-shell.** The parallel capture router got `headlessShell: resolveHeadlessShellPath(cfg) !== null`. That function returns `string | undefined`, so the comparison was always true. A Linux render on system Chrome, which the engine runs in screenshot mode, was treated as beginframe, which turns the parallel-stream router on by default for the wrong capture mode. `resolveParallelCaptureMode` now takes the resolved path and checks for `undefined` itself.

## Why

Both make what the CLI decides and what the engine does disagree. The second also sends one cohort of Linux renders down a router path that was only measured for beginframe capture.

## Related work

None. A follow-up PR adds a generic seam for a host to supply its own Chromium launcher on top of the same resolvers.

## How

- `chromeHostCeiling.ts` gains `browserPathFromEnv(env)`. The engine's `resolveHeadlessShellPath` and the CLI's `findFromEnv` both call it. Each keeps its existing reaction to a missing file: the engine throws, the CLI falls through.
- `config.ts` drops its own env read for `chromePath`, so `resolveHeadlessShellPath` owns the env order for every caller.
- `resolveParallelCaptureMode({ headlessShellPath })` replaces the boolean, so the "was a shell resolved" check lives in the tested function, not at the call site.
- The comment above `findFromEnv` now states the rule without its history.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `browserManager.test.ts`: with both env vars set to different existing files, `resolveHeadlessShellPath({})` and `resolveHeadlessShellPath(resolveConfig())` both return `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH`. The block now clears both vars before each case, so a runner that exports one (the Windows job sets `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH`) cannot change a case.
  - `renderOrchestrator.test.ts`: a Linux render with no resolved shell is `screenshot`.
  - fails without the fix:
    - with `browserManager.ts` from main, the precedence test fails (1 failed, 16 passed);
    - with the check written as `!== null` again, the screenshot case fails (1 failed, 2 passed);
    - with `config.ts`'s env read put back, the `resolveConfig()` case fails (1 failed, 91 passed);
    - without the per-case env reset and with `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` set as on the Windows runner, the missing-binary case fails (1 failed, 91 passed), which is the Windows job's failure.
  - At c56e02e9, `browserManager.test.ts` plus `config.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row with `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` set (205 passed). These also pass: the CLI's `render.test.ts` (105 passed), the producer's `renderOrchestrator.test.ts` (280 passed) and the Lambda `handler.test.ts` (25 passed).
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: feat(producer): a cloud plan can leave its audio to be mixed beside its chunks
body:
## What changes

Nothing a render does today. This adds the producer pieces that let a cloud render mix its audio beside its chunks instead of before them; the Lambda wiring follows in the next PR.

- A plan can leave its audio out (`deferAudio`): mp4 chunks then render video only.
- `buildPlanAudio` makes that audio track on its own: the same mix and true-peak hold the plan makes today, from the same code, at exactly the video's length.
- The mp4 stitch takes the audio track from that one file and puts its samples right after the header, ahead of the video.

## Why

On a long 4K render the plan spends most of its time on audio (about 48 of 57 s on a 20-minute film) while no chunk can start. With audio made beside the chunks, the plan shrinks to the rest and the audio finishes long before the chunks do.

## How

- The plan's copy, compile and probe move into one helper shared by the plan and `buildPlanAudio`, so both see the same composition. Video extraction, which adds the sound of audible videos the static parse misses (a src the scene script sets), is one helper too; `buildPlanAudio` runs it deferred, so it probes without extracting long windows. The mix and the true-peak hold are likewise one helper each.
- `plansSeparateAudio` decides when audio is left out: mp4 without `cfr`, the cases the stitch can join. Any other plan mixes as before.
- The locked config records `separateAudio`, so chunks know to encode video only and the assembler knows to stitch the audio file in.
- `buildStitchedHeader(layouts, audio?)` appends the audio file's track to chunk 0's moov under a new track id and indexes its samples first. It refuses any chunk, chunk 0 included, that carries audio of its own when a separate file is given.

## Tests

- `plan.test.ts`: a plan with `deferAudio` has no audio and records `separateAudio`; `buildPlanAudio` writes a byte-identical file to the audio a carrying plan makes (a hot tone, so the true-peak hold re-encodes too), and the same for a `<video data-has-audio>` whose src the scene script sets (red before the shared extraction: no audio); `cfr` still mixes in the plan.
- `mp4Stitch.test.ts`: the separate audio's samples sit before every chunk's, with its edit list, sizes and a new track id; chunk 0 or chunk 1 carrying audio is refused (chunk 0 was red before); the local join writes the same bytes as the in-memory stitch.
- `chunkAudio.test.ts`: video-only chunks stitched with the whole plan audio give the same packets in every stream as chunks that carry their slices.
- Each new behaviour was broken on purpose and its test went red: no new track id, no peak hold, `cfr` deferring audio, audio payload placed last.
- Heavy-4K composition (20.6 min of two 50-min 4K takes, read by URL as a cloud plan reads them, ffmpeg 8.0.1): `buildPlanAudio` and today's plan write byte-identical audio (same file, same audio stream md5, 59,376,000 samples = 30,925 frames at 25 fps exactly).

Test counts: `plan.test.ts` 63 pass (the script-src test 3 runs in a row), `mp4Stitch.test.ts` 13, `chunkAudio.test.ts` 9, `assemble.test.ts` 18, each 0 fail; producer typecheck clean.

title: fix(inspector): component reports show the animation code inside large wrappers and only the film's own files
body:
## What

Two fixes to what `grep_components` (the inspector's component report) returns as source snippets:

1. A caller frame whose enclosing statement is a large wrapper — an IIFE around a whole scene — is reported as its call line instead of the whole wrapper.
2. `Sources` indexes only the files the inspected document was bundled from, so mockups, background studies and contact sheets in the project stop contributing CSS candidates, script chunks and duplicate tags.

## Why

Measured on the HyperFrames launch trilogy project in HyperFrames Desktop agent evals:

- **Animation code never reached the agent for one film.** Every call that touched `films/inspector-launch` (26) showed only a two-line dependency. The scene's `gsap` calls sit inside a 3,300-line IIFE; the outermost stack frame (`})();`) made the whole IIFE a caller snippet, `mergeSnippets` merged the small creation snippet into it, and the 65 KB result was always `omitted`. Agents fell back to `grep` and `sed` for the code the tool had found.
- **101 snippets came from files the film never loads**: `contact-sheet.html` (74), `background-studies/` (20) and `mockups/` (7), all as `matched CSS candidate`, because `Sources` walked every `.html` in the project and the runtime matched their rules against the film's elements. The same copies also make an element's opening tag ambiguous, so `markup` returns nothing for it.

## How

- `Sources.mapper`: a caller frame (not the first) that is not inside a ≤2 KB function and whose smallest enclosing statement is over 2 KB becomes a one-line snippet, and its lexical dependencies are not expanded. The 2 KB bound is the one the helper-function rule already uses (`SHOWN_WHOLE`).
- `new Sources(project, served?)`: when `served` is given, only those files are indexed. The paths come from the bundler's existing `BundleOptions.onRead`, which already reports every project file the bundle reads (entry, sub-compositions, linked stylesheets and scripts); Studio's preview uses it for invalidation. Paths are compared after `realpath`.
- The headless `Inspector` service collects its bundle's reads and passes them. `prepareLiveInspection` takes them as a new optional last argument; without it, behaviour is unchanged, so hosts can adopt it separately (HyperFrames Desktop will pass its preview bundle's reads in a follow-up).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `tests/sources.test.ts` — a caller inside a 3 KB IIFE comes back as `})();` with the creation snippet intact; a project with a mockup that copies the film's `.title` rule and `#title` tag indexes the mockup without `served` and drops it with the bundle's reads, which also makes the film's tag unique again. Both fail on `main`.
- [x] `vitest run` in `packages/inspector` (45 passed), `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`.
- [x] `bun tests/live.ts <gsap.min.js>` passes.

title: feat(core,producer): decide blur defects once per timeline, off on routes that cannot host it
body:
## What

- **Defects are decided once per timeline.** The mover scan already seeks the whole timeline, so the defect scan samples along it: a defect that only appears mid-timeline (a root that rotates, a card that flips) turns blur off from frame 0, not partway through a render. Defects now apply on every Chrome version, because the preview, the pinned render browser and Docker's browser can differ and a render must match what the preview showed. GSAP's identity matrix on a rewound root transform no longer counts as a transform.
- **The per-frame check is a backstop that costs one frame.** For what the scan missed (a root shake shorter than the scan step, a backface flip between samples, a canvas a script adds later) the frame renders sharp from the plain DOM and the runtime logs once; blur resumes when the defect is gone, instead of ending for the rest of the render. Measured with the review fix on the CLI render path (Chrome 152, quality draft, frames compared with blur off), before the change: a 1-frame shake sharpened 179 frames of a 6 s 60 fps clip, a 60 s clip with a 10.05–10.2 s shake sharpened 598 frames; after, 1 and 4 frames.
- **Four detector gaps closed.** A root moved by the individual `scale`, `rotate` or `translate` properties (identity values ignored) is a root transform; a root `mix-blend-mode` other than `normal` is a defect (`root-blend-mode`); the backface check treats an individual `rotate` with an axis or 3D angle (`rotate: y 180deg`, `rotate: 0 1 0 180deg`) and a `translate` with z as 3D (shared `individualIs3d`); and the `iframe-in-root` entry covers everything that is torn down and re-initialised when the root moves: `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>` and defined custom elements (hyphenated name with `customElements.get`). Measured on Chrome 152 against the previous build: a `scale: .5` root, a `rotate`, a `translate`, a `multiply` root, a `rotate: y 180deg` face, `<object>`, `<embed>` and a defined custom element all reported `on` and now report `off` with their code; plain compositions and flat uses (`scale: 1`, `rotate: 90deg` on a face outside 3D) still report `on`.
- **A block raised by the scan is lifted when its cause is removed or the timeline changes.** Capture-failure blocks stay for the life of the instance.
- **The WebGL / WebGPU check covers the whole document:** a render's shader-transition compositor appends its canvas to `<body>`, while preview puts it inside the root.
- **Blur is off on routes that cannot host it.** HDR renders and the layered compositor screenshot each DOM layer after hiding the others, which does not reach blur's canvases; a distributed (Lambda / cloud) chunk render has no Studio preview to match and no guarantee of html-in-canvas in the worker's Chrome. The producer sets `pageMotionBlur` to `hdr-render`, `layered-composite` or `distributed-render` there, and the runtime reports `the renderer turned it off (…)`. The distributed plan's compile-time hint no longer forces a `data-motion-blur` composition onto screenshot capture: it freezes the same capture mode as the same composition without the attribute.
- **The mover scan reads its baseline at t=0**, so every worker of a parallel render finds the same movers whatever time its scan starts. An ancestor's pan is not counted as its child's move (a first change is judged against the element's own baseline style at that time).

## Why

Part 7 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on the defect list in #5971.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. A composition must blur in every frame the scan trusts, and be sharp in the rest.

## Notes

- Defects apply on every Chrome version, so a composition that Chrome 157 would capture correctly still has blur off if an older preview browser would not. Revisit when the render pin and the support floor both pass the last affected major.
- Enabling blur runs a timeline scan that can leave about one level of noise inside blend-mode / filter effects even when blur ends up off.
- Documented, not fixed: an ancestor's pan can still be read as a child's move in some edge cases; the per-frame backstop re-reads backface on its cached candidates, which costs more when a stylesheet resets `*{backface-visibility:hidden}`. The candidates include the animation-derived faces (#5971); each rescan adds to them and they are kept for the rest of the scan, because the last sample can fall after an animation has ended (the per-frame backstop then still reads them).
- Output is not bit-identical across worker counts, at about the size of the chunk-split noise a render without blur already has. Motion shorter than one scan step (`SCAN_STEPS`) is under-measured.
- The HDR / layered / distributed routes render without blur, as before this stack existed.

## Testing

- `htmlInCanvasDefects.test.ts`: the scan finds a defect that appears at any sampled time and says where it first appeared; identity transforms are ignored; a root `scale` / `rotate` / `translate` (identity values ignored), a root `mix-blend-mode`, `<object>` / `<embed>` / defined custom elements (an undefined hyphenated tag is ignored), and a backface-hidden face turned by `rotate: y 180deg`, `rotate: 0 1 0 180deg` or a z `translate` (a flat `rotate: 90deg` is not); the document-wide WebGL check; `facesNow` reads the scan's backface candidates at the current time (a hidden face that flips into 3D after the scan is seen without rescanning; a face an animation keys to `hidden` is a candidate, stays one after the animation is gone, and is found by the scan and by `facesNow`).
- Core `captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts`: blur off from frame 0 for a mid-timeline defect; a defect the scan missed renders only that frame sharp and blur resumes; an engine frame that is sharp resolves at once and leaves the composite step idle; a block lifts when its cause is gone or the timeline changes, and a capture-failure block does not; the distributed route is named as the reason.
- `discover.test.ts`: the same movers whatever time a scan starts, an ancestor's pan is no child's move when the child's style first changes, and the scan reports each step after its seek.
- Engine `pageMotionBlur.test.ts` and producer `motionBlurRoute.test.ts`: the off reason for the HDR, layered and distributed routes; producer distributed `plan.test.ts` (the `chunkFrames.test.ts` for every chunk session is in #5991): the plan probe session and every chunk session stand blur down, and the frozen capture mode matches the plain composition's; orchestrator request validation.
- `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit` in core, engine and producer pass; comment ratchet against #5971's branch passes; every package is within its size budget.

title: feat(core,engine): report why blur is off, and what each render session did
body:
## What

Reports why blur is off, and what each render session did, so tooling and logs can tell.

- **Reason codes.** The runtime's `report()` carries a stable `reasonCode` next to the readable `reason` for every way blur ends up off: a defect code (from #5971), `unsupported-browser`, `renderer-off` and `capture-failures`.
- **`probe()`** (on `window.__hfMotionBlur`) makes the decision on demand without wrapping or painting; it is cheap once scanned and puts the playhead back.
- **`suspend()`** stops all painting for the rest of a session without changing the reported decision (and never sets the page's off switch, which would change the probe's answer). It outlives a re-init of the same root and does nothing where blur is off.
- **Engine log line.** One line per capture session from what the page reports: `[motion-blur] on reasonCode=null movers=N failedFrames=K`, after the first frame. The first-frame line cannot know about later failures, so the session end prints the same line with `(session end)` when any frame fell back to plain DOM (read with a 1.5 s timeout so a stuck page cannot hold up closing); a clean session stays quiet.
- **The first test that reads blurred pixels.** `captureMotionBlur.pixels.browser.test.ts` drives a real Chrome with html-in-canvas through the engine's frame order (seek, wait, composite, screenshot) and checks: the trail along the motion line has the hard edges of the sharp frame spread out without adding or losing ink; what does not move matches the sharp frame exactly; a box centered with `translate: -50% -50%` is blurred around where it really is; a backface-hidden card in a 3D flip renders the plain frame. `distributed/chunkFrames.test.ts` (moved here from #5990 to keep that PR under 1000 lines): a chunk session stands page blur down and asks for no engine blur. Also a face whose `backface-visibility: hidden` comes only from `@keyframes` or `element.animate()`, next to an ordinary mover, turns blur off with `backface-visibility` and renders the plain frame; a face that is hidden only between two scan samples renders just that frame plain; a flat animated backface hack stays blurred. It skips when Chrome or html-in-canvas is missing.

## Why

Part 8 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5990, whose scan decides the state this reports.

Stack goal: opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. Blur turns itself off in several cases, and without this an author or an operator cannot tell which; `hyperframes check` (#5992) builds on `probe()` and `suspend()`.

## Notes

- `state` stays `on` while individual frames fall back to plain DOM (a paint timeout, a missed defect, a failed capture): read `failedFrames` for those. A paint timeout counts in `failedFrames` but not in `failures`, which only counts capture exceptions in a row (documented, not fixed).
- Why blur is off is reported three ways after this PR: `window.__hfMotionBlur.report()` (`state`, `reason`, `reasonCode`, `movers`, `failedFrames`), the per-session log line, and, in #5992, `hyperframes check`.
- The pixel test runs against the Chrome the engine pins (152 headless shell) with the `CanvasDrawElement` feature; it is a guard for the pipeline, not a visual-quality benchmark. Limits it does not cover: trails drawn over foreground elements, a halo on transparent movers, trails past `overflow:hidden`, 2D flips through `scaleX = 0`.
- Cost: about 1.7x median render time for a blurred composition (20 real compositions, blur on vs off); a few ms of JS per blurred frame in Studio plus a one-time mover scan on first play.

## Testing

- Core `captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts`: reason codes for every off path (the earlier assertions on reason text now check codes too), `probe()` finds the movers without any paint, wrap or event and restores the playhead, does not rescan unless the timeline changes or while blur is off, reports the defect with its code and `capture-failures` after three failed frames; `suspend()` unwraps a wrapped root, stops painting, is idempotent, outlives a re-init, exists but does nothing where blur is off, and lets the probe still decide; plus the guards that need codes (one warning and the first reason stays when unwrapping throws).
- Engine `pageMotionBlur.test.ts`: the per-session line, the session-end line only when frames fell back (including when the failures ended blur), the timeout for a page that does not answer, and `closeCaptureSession` logging the closing line once before the page closes (driven through the real function); `frameCapture-motionBlur.test.ts`: the line is logged once after the session's first captured frame, says why blur is off, and stays silent for a page that never asked for blur.
- Engine `captureMotionBlur.pixels.browser.test.ts`: 4 pixel tests in Chrome 152 headless shell.
- `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit` in core and engine, and their tests pass; comment ratchet against #5990's branch passes; every package is within its size budget.

title: feat(cli): tell authors in check why motion blur is off
body:
## What

Tells authors in `hyperframes check` why motion blur is off.

- `check` reads the runtime's `probe()` for a page whose root asked for blur and reports `motion_blur_off` (warning, with a fix hint per reason code; the `iframe-in-root` hint now names `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>` and custom elements, which are all re-initialised when blur wraps the root, and a root `mix-blend-mode` has its own: move it to a child element, or drop motion blur), `motion_blur_no_movers` (info, when nothing moves fast enough to blur) and `motion_blur_unverified` (info, when the check browser has no html-in-canvas to decide with).
- It asks the runtime which root wants blur instead of reading attributes itself, so `data-root="true"` is honoured and the first composition's attribute is not mistaken for the runtime's choice. The finding is anchored (selector, data attributes, bounding box) on that same root, `data-root="true"` first and else the first composition, not on the first `[data-composition-id]` in the document.
- Right after probing it calls `suspend()` for the rest of its session. Its audits read plain DOM, so they no longer pay the roughly 10x slowdown of auditing a wrapped composition. It never sets the page's off switch, which would change the probe's answer.
- The console echo of the same message (`[motion-blur] off: …`) is dropped when a finding says it, so a finding is not shown twice; an unrelated console warning, and an error that only starts like the echo, are kept.

## Why

Part 9 of 9 in the capture motion blur stack: #5875 → #5967 → #5968 → #5969 → #5970 → #5971 → #5990 → #5991 → #5992. It builds on #5991, which gives the runtime the reason codes, `probe()` and `suspend()` this reads.

The stack delivers opt-in capture motion blur for compositions, in Studio preview and in renders, drawn with Chrome's html-in-canvas. Blur turns itself off in several cases, and without this an author who asked for `data-motion-blur="on"` cannot tell from the check output.

## Notes

- A script-set `data-motion-blur` is not supported: the attribute has to be in the HTML for the render-mode hint, and `check` reports only what the runtime decided.
- Cost of blur, from the stack's measurements: about 1.7x median render time for a blurred composition; compositions that are blocked or static cost nothing extra.
- The stack's documented limits (trails drawn over foreground elements; a halo on transparent movers; trails leaking past `overflow:hidden`; a 2D flip through `scaleX = 0` blending as rotation; sub-pixel `left` steps in whole px; a fast child inside a parent that moved earlier not blurred; SVG elements not scanned; shadow DOM not scanned for backface; blurred preview updating at half rate; video preview about 2–3% darker; worker-count output differences; the scan leaving about one level of noise) are unchanged by this PR.

## Testing

- `checkMotionBlur.test.ts`: each finding, its severity and fix hint (the widened iframe hint, `root-blend-mode`, and the accelerated-canvas hint, which now says the scan covers sub-compositions too and offers rendering that effect separately or flattening it out of the page, or dropping `data-motion-blur` on the composition), and the console-echo filter; `checkMotionBlur.page.test.ts`: the probe serialised into the page, which root it asks about, the `suspend()` right after the probe (and a runtime without `suspend`), the mover count, and a page that never opted in.
- `checkBrowser.test.ts`: a blur finding reaches the check output with its fix and its anchor, the anchor is the `data-root="true"` composition when a sub-composition comes first in the document, once when a second Chrome shares the sampling, the runtime's duplicate console line is dropped while unrelated warnings and look-alike errors stay, and nothing is added for a page that never opted in.
- `check.test.ts` still passes. `bun run build` and `tsc --noEmit` in cli pass; comment ratchet against #5991's branch passes; every package is within its size budget.

title: feat(cli): require feedback --role so reports say who the person behind the agent is
body:
## What

`hyperframes feedback` now requires `--role`: who the person behind the session is. The agent picks it from what the session and the project show, and never asks the person.

Values: `ai-builder`, `developer`, `marketer`, `creator`, `designer`, `founder`, `agency`, `educator`, `other`, `unknown` (`unknown` when the session gives nothing to go on).

## Why

Every feedback report becomes countable by who is actually using the framework through an agent, so we can see which kind of builder the OSS CLI serves most.

## How

- `--role` is checked first on every path (rating, ratingless comment, `--search-miss`). Missing or not in the list: exit 1 with one line naming the flag and all ten values, so an agent can fix the call in one retry. Nothing is sent or tracked on failure.
- The role is sent with the report (`role` in the feedback and catalog-search-miss bodies) and added as a `role` property on `cli_render_feedback`, `cli_feedback_comment` and `cli_catalog_search_miss`.
- Only the enum value travels. No free text, names, companies or reasons.
- The value list has one owner (`FEEDBACK_ROLES` in `utils/feedbackSource.ts`); the help text and error are built from it, and a test pins the skill to list every value.
- The CLI skill gets one instruction: pass `--role` from session context, `unknown` when unsure, never ask. Every `hyperframes feedback` snippet in the skills, the docs, the command's examples, the catalog's pre-filled gap command and the post-render agent hint now carries `--role`.
- The render-time interactive prompt for people at a terminal is unchanged and sends no role.

## Compatibility

- The feedback backend accepts unknown fields today, so this CLI can ship before the backend learns to store and show `role`; reports are not lost in between.
- Downstream launchers that teach agents the command must add `--role` to their instructions before they move to a CLI version with this change. Until they do, an agent's first call fails with the one-line error and has to retry.
- Agents with an older copy of the skill hit the same one-line error and retry.

## Tests

- Parser: the ten values, trimming, case and unknown values rejected, the one-line error.
- Command: each path refuses a missing or made-up role and sends nothing; the role reaches the report and its telemetry on every path; every shipped example parses with a valid `--role`.
- Payload and telemetry: `role` in both request bodies and on all three events.
- Docs and skills: every `hyperframes feedback --…` command across `skills/` and `docs/` (changelog excluded) carries `--role`, including multi-line ones; the skill instruction says never to ask the person.
- Each new test was broken on purpose (role check removed, role dropped from the body, an example without `--role`, a multi-line docs snippet without `--role`, role dropped from the search-miss event, the never-ask wording removed) and went red; three clean runs in a row after.
- Ran the CLI from source: `feedback --rating 8`, `--comment x`, `--search-miss typewriter` and `--role ceo --rating 8` each exit 1 with the one line; `--role developer --rating 8` and `--role ai-builder --search-miss typewriter` exit 0.

title: fix(catalog): token-themed component previews no longer render black
body:
## What a user sees

The live preview on seven Catalog component pages (Testimonial Card, Store Badge Lockup, Wordmark Tiles, Focus Swap, Stagger Cascade, SVG Mask Reveal, and Camera Scan Gate's scan colour) showed dark serif text on a near-black canvas. The same seven rendered that way after `npx hyperframes add` in any project without a theme pack.

After this change they render in their demo's theme, in the Catalog and in an install.

## Why

The theme contract (`themes/CONTRACT.md`) says a component reads contract tokens with a fallback, `var(--fg, #f8fafc)`, because a theme pack is optional. These seven read `var(--bg)`, `var(--fg)`, `var(--font-body)` and friends bare. With no theme pack the tokens resolve to nothing: a transparent card, inherited black text, the browser's default serif. The Catalog preview builds these components from the bare snippet, so it showed exactly that.

## Changes

- **Registry:** each of the seven now carries exact-value fallbacks taken from its own demo, so an install with no theme pack looks like the demo. Camera Scan Gate's `scanColor` default becomes `var(--brand, #22c55e)`, the fallback its CSS already uses.
- **Gate:** `scripts/registry-theme-fallbacks.test.ts` fails any registry item that reads a contract token without a fallback and does not declare it itself. The contract list is read from a theme pack, so it cannot drift. Fails on main with the seven files above; passes here.
- **Catalog preview:** the snippet preview wrapper copies the custom properties the component's demo sets on its mount and the mount's ancestors (nearest wins), and paints `var(--bg)` instead of a fixed `#0a0a0a`. So previews show the demo's theme rather than the snippet's fallbacks, including for components like Count Up that already had fallbacks.

This is a source PR: the regenerated payloads come from the catalog publish PR after merge.

## Verification

- `node --import tsx --test scripts/registry-theme-fallbacks.test.ts`: 3 pass. With this PR's registry changes stashed: 1 fail, naming the seven files.
- `node --import tsx --test scripts/generate-catalog-previews.test.ts`: 12 pass. With the generator change reverted, both new wrapper theme tests fail.
- `vitest run scripts/catalog/ scripts/generate-catalog-payloads.test.ts`: 88 pass. `tsc -p scripts`, oxlint, `oxfmt --check .` and `check-catalog-source-pr.mjs` clean.
- Payloads for all seven plus Count Up build with `generate-catalog-payloads.ts --only`. A scan of the built payloads finds no contract token that is read but never defined.

title: fix(engine): cloud renders fail instead of going silent when an audio read is cut off
body:
## What changes for a user

A cloud render whose audio read from a project file's link is cut off (an S3 error or network outage that outlasts ffmpeg's reconnects, or a link that expires mid-read) now fails the audio step as a retryable error. Before, the render succeeded and the rest of that clip played silent.

## Why

#5972 made cloud renders read a cloud-held file's audio straight from its signed link. `extractAudioSegment` trusted ffmpeg's exit code alone. When a link read fails mid-stream past the reconnects, ffmpeg logs the error, treats it as the end of the input and exits 0 with a short WAV. The mix then pads the track with silence. Before #5972 the same failure was a retried `length_mismatch` from the download. This was found in #5972's review (the drop-then-403 repro) and blocks the v0.8.182 release.

Both changes are in `extractAudioSegment` and apply only to link reads (local files are unchanged):

- `-xerror` before the input, so a failed read fails the ffmpeg run instead of ending the input early. Shown on ffmpeg 7.0.2 here. #5972's review read the same exit-on-error branch in 6.x's input loop.
- A failed link read is labelled `download_failed`, owner `system`, retryable. Without this the cut read below surfaced as `invalid_media`, owner `user`, not retryable, because ffmpeg reports the partial last packet as "Invalid data found". The probe has already read the same link as media, so a failure here is the network.

## Decisions and tradeoffs

**No output-length check.** An earlier head also compared the WAV's length with the probed source length. Review showed it fails healthy reads. A video's probed length is the picture's, so a file whose audio track ends early came up "short". I fixed that by measuring against the audio stream, and then reproduced the second case raised in review: a VBR MP3 with no Xing header and a silent opening probes as 71.1 s when it holds 20.0 s, so a clip that takes its length from the probe fails every attempt. Both reviews of #5972 named `-xerror` alone as enough. I found no exit-0 truncation that `-xerror` misses, so the check is gone.

**`-xerror` also stops on decode errors** that ffmpeg would otherwise skip. A source with a few corrupt audio packets that renders locally can now fail the cloud audio step. It is labelled retryable, so it fails twice and then stops. A cloud render that publishes damaged or partly silent audio without saying so is the worse outcome.

## Evidence

New `audioMixer.urlRead.test.ts`, real ffmpeg, a local range server:

| | healthy WAV link | WAV link cut mid-read, then 403 | healthy MP4 link, 6 s picture, 4 s audio |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | mixes | **mixes, success** (rest of the clip silent) | mixes |
| this branch | mixes | fails the track: `download_failed`, `system`, retryable | mixes |

Each test file run alone on Linux (ffmpeg 7.0.2):

- `audioMixer.urlRead.test.ts`: exit 0, 3 passed, 3 runs in a row. On main: exit 1, the cut-link case fails. On the previous head's length check: exit 1, the short-audio MP4 case fails.
- `audioMixer.test.ts`: exit 0, 72 passed, 3 runs in a row. The URL argument test now also checks that `-xerror` comes before `-i`.
- `audioMixer.{fades,grouping,level,order}.test.ts`: exit 0, 7, 16, 2 and 3 passed.
- Mutations, each restored after: drop `-xerror` -> the cut-link test and the URL argument test fail; drop the relabel -> the cut-link test fails. Run before the last commit, which only moved the two code comments into names (`FAIL_ON_READ_ERROR_INSTEAD_OF_ENDING_THERE`, `probedLinkFailedToRead`).
- The MP3 probe numbers came from a throwaway test with libmp3lame `-q:a 0 -write_xing 0` (8 s of silence, then noise): CBR 20.04 s and gentle VBR 20.06-20.11 s were correct; that file probed as 71.136 s. Not committed, because libmp3lame is not in every CI ffmpeg.
- Producer's `ffprobeArgvContract.test.ts` (it reads every ffmpeg/ffprobe argv in the repo): exit 0, 110 passed. The test's media setup now passes `-y`, so the contract reads it as an ffmpeg write, not a probe.
- Engine `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt, comment citations and the comment ratchet: exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- An https link with the production reconnect flags against a real S3 failure. The test uses plain http, which has no reconnect flags, so ffmpeg fails at the first cut instead of after two reconnects. The 403-after-reconnect path was shown in #5972's review on ffmpeg 7.0.2, where `-xerror` made it exit 251.
- Lambda's ffmpeg build. The claim that `-xerror` covers it rests on ffmpeg's input loop, not on a run there.
- The video frame extractor's in-place link reads use the same reconnect flags and no `-xerror`. Whether a cut read there quietly yields fewer frames is not tested here.

title: feat(aws-lambda): a cloud render mixes its audio beside its chunks
body:
## What changes

A cloud render mixes its audio on its own Lambda while the chunks render, instead of before them. On a 20-minute 4K film the render finishes in about 115 s instead of 165 s, at the same measured cost and with the same audio and video streams.

- The v2 plan leaves its audio out (`deferAudio`, from #5988), so the chunks start about 50 s sooner.
- A new handler action, `audio`, makes the track with `buildPlanAudio` and uploads it as `audio/audio.m4a` under the render's prefix.
- The state machine runs the chunk map and the audio task side by side (`RenderV2`, a Parallel state), then assembles from both.
- The S3 stitch takes the video from the chunks and the audio track from that one file.

## Why

The plan spent most of its time on audio (about 48 of 57 s on this film) while no chunk could start. Audio now finishes long before the chunks do, so it costs no wall time.

## How

- The plan leaves its audio out only for an mp4 without `cfr` (`plansSeparateAudio`) on a function with more than one worker. It then gives the chunk map one worker fewer (`MaxChunkConcurrency`), so the audio task always has a slot and neither branch can wait out its throttle retries behind the other. With a single worker, or for any other format, the plan mixes the audio as today.
- The plan result says which happened (`SeparateAudio`). The audio branch is a Choice on it: the `Audio` task runs only when the plan left its audio out; otherwise a Pass hands AssembleV2 no track, and no Lambda is invoked.
- It uses the plan's non-retryable error list for its retries and writes a fixed key per render, so a retry overwrites its own output.
- `template.yaml` and the CDK stack get the same `RenderV2` Parallel. Its result selector keeps `$.Render.Chunks` and `$.Render.Audio`. `AssembleV2` reads the chunk URIs and `AudioS3Uri` from there.
- The v2 assembler accepts an `AudioS3Uri` only when the plan recorded separate audio (`stitchesSeparateAudio`), and refuses it otherwise.
- `stitchMp4InS3(s3, chunkUris, destUri, { audioUri })` builds the header with the audio file as one more source. Its samples go in the uploaded header part, so no chunk bytes pass through the assembler.
- A failed audio mix throws in the audio task, as it does in today's plan, so the Parallel fails and the render fails without assembling. The difference: today it fails before any chunk runs; now chunk Lambdas already running carry on to the end and are billed.
- An mp4 composition with no audio still invokes the audio task once: it downloads, compiles and probes the project, then reports no track. That is one extra short invocation and a few state transitions per render, so "same cost" is what this film measured, not a rule.

## Output layout (A1) and players

The audio's samples sit in one run right after the header, ahead of all the video, about 1 MB per minute of audio at 128 kbps. Both streams are packet-identical to today's. Only their order in the file changes.

Measured on the 20-minute 4K output (423 MB, served by signed URL), against the same streams remuxed interleaved:

| player | this layout, first frame | interleaved, first frame | seeks and play to end |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome (headless) | 0.3-0.6 s | 0.3 s | ok |
| Safari's engine (WebKit 26.4, macOS) | 4.3 s, 4.7 s | 1.2 s | ok, no stalls |
| QuickTime's engine (AVFoundation) | 1.15 s | 1.07 s | ok |
| ffmpeg over https | decodes at 0, 618, 1230 s | - | ok |

Safari's engine reads the file in order up to its first video sample, so a long film starts about 0.15 s later per minute of audio. Downloads and range-reading players are unaffected.

**Fallback (A2):** interleave each chunk's audio after its video, as today. S3 copy parts must be at least 5 MB, so every chunk would add a ~5 MB download and upload through the assembler, an estimated +10-20 s of wall on this film. Only `buildStitchedHeader` and the part plan in `s3Stitch.ts` change, so it can follow if the start delay matters.

## Tests

- `handler.test.ts`:
  - the v2 plan defers its audio;
  - an assemble with an `AudioS3Uri` stitches the audio task's track into the same packets as chunk-carried audio;
  - a v2 assemble whose plan carries audio refuses an `AudioS3Uri`;
  - `audio` uploads the track, or reports none when the plan keeps its audio;
  - with 4 workers the plan defers its audio and the chunk map gets 3; with 1 worker the plan keeps its audio and the chunks get the one; the same holds through a reserved concurrency of 2 (chunks get 1) and 1 (audio stays in the plan).
- `s3Stitch.test.ts`: a stitch with separate audio writes the same frames and audio as the local join, at 30 and 60 fps.
- `HyperframesRenderStack.snapshot.test.ts`:
  - the SAM template and the CDK stack both run `RenderV2` (the chunk map and `Audio`);
  - `AssembleV2` takes `$.Render.Chunks[*].ChunkS3Uri` and `$.Render.Audio.AudioS3Uri`;
  - every task sends the same payload in both;
  - the audio branch is a Choice on `$.Plan.SeparateAudio`, whose other path is a Pass with no track, and `PlanV2` selects `SeparateAudio`;
  - the v1 audio paths are unchanged.
- Five mutants each turned their tests red, then were restored: the plan not deferring audio, the chunk map taking every worker beside the audio task, deferring audio with a single worker, the template sending no audio to `AssembleV2`, the S3 stitch ignoring the audio file.
- Counts: `handler.test.ts` 30 pass (3 runs in a row), `s3Stitch.test.ts` 5, snapshot 22, contract 6, `getRenderProgress.test.ts` 20; producer `plan.test.ts` 63, `mp4Stitch.test.ts` 13, `chunkAudio.test.ts` 9, `assemble.test.ts` 18; typecheck clean in both packages.

## Measured on Lambda

20.6-minute 4K composition of two 50-minute HEVC takes, 256 chunks. Each row is one cold deploy, same fixture:

| | wall | plan | Lambda-s | cost | video / audio stream md5 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 164.8 s | 56.9 s | 21,726 | $3.627 | `f0aa2f88` / `2f621f57` |
| this PR (2 runs, before the worker reservation) | 113.9 s, 116.3 s | 6.5 s | 21,643, 21,704 | $3.614, $3.624 | `f0aa2f88` / `2f621f57` |

The output file is byte-identical across runs of this PR, and its streams match main's exactly.

title: test(cli): cloud download tests split small parts so a slow Windows loopback cannot time them out
body:
## What changes

The cloud download tests that talk to a local HTTP server use 64 KiB parts instead of 8 MiB, so they move about 1/128th of the data. The part counts, range headers, drop points and retries they check stay exactly the same. `downloadToFile` takes an optional `partBytes`, next to the `fetchImpl` the tests already inject; the CLI keeps its 8 MiB default.

## Why

On Windows CI, "splits a large file into parallel ranged requests" (60 MiB) and "streams the whole file in one request when the server ignores Range" (20 MiB) hit the 20 s test timeout and dropped a PR from the merge queue. That's 2 of the last 200 Windows runs, both within 4 minutes of each other.

On those runs the rest of the CLI suite ran at its usual speed. But the two tests in this file whose server drops connections took 2 to 7 times their usual time ("resumes a range" moved 50 MiB in 7.6 s, against about 1 s). That points to the loopback carrying each connection at roughly 1 MB/s on those runners. At that rate a single 20 MiB stream needs about 21 s. On green runs the same tests take 0.3 to 3 s.

## How I looked

- **Isolated loop:** a throwaway branch looped this file and a traced copy of both transfers on `windows-latest`, idle and under 6 CPU burners. Everything passed in at most 1.3 s, with no pause of a second or more between body chunks.
- **Real lane:** two runs of the full engine and CLI lane together also passed.
- **Not reproduced:** the slow-loopback condition, so this change removes the tests' dependence on loopback throughput rather than claiming a fix for it.
- **Not localhost/IPv6:** the server already listens on and is fetched at `127.0.0.1`.

## Tests

- `download.test.ts`: 17 pass, 3 runs in a row.
- Two mutants turn it red, then were restored:
  - the first request ignoring `partBytes`: 4 tests fail;
  - splitting into one part fewer: the split test fails.
- CLI typecheck clean, comment ratchet clean, CLI process-ownership check passes.

title: perf(producer): cloud render chunks hand Chrome each video near the size it is shown
body:
## What

Cloud render chunks (Lambda and Cloud Run both run `renderChunk`) now hand Chrome each video's frames at close to the size the video is drawn, instead of always at the source's full resolution. A 4K camera shown as a small picture-in-picture bubble now reaches Chrome as a much smaller image; a video that fills the frame is unchanged.

## Why

Profiling a heavy 4K chunk (full-screen screen recording plus a camera bubble) showed capture dominating the chunk's time, and inside capture the biggest single cost was Chrome shrinking a full 4K camera frame into its small box, in software, on every frame. Reading, base64-encoding and delivering the frames over CDP was a small fraction of that; x264 encode was also small. Giving Chrome an image near its drawn size removes most of that per-frame work, so chunks finish sooner and cloud renders use less compute.

## Related work

Refs #5952 (local renders encode while capturing; independent of this change).

## How

- **Measure, then extract.** `renderChunk` now works out which frames each deferred video shows from the plan, boots its preflight browser session, and calls the new engine helper `measureVideoShownBoxes`: it seeks the page through the chunk's own frames and records each video's largest drawn box in device pixels (`getBoundingClientRect() x devicePixelRatio`, so transforms and animated zooms count). Extraction runs after that, with the box. The capture options that used to come from extraction output (which videos to skip readiness for, metadata hints for videos read by URL) now come from the plan; they are the same values.
- **Halve, don't resize.** The extractor's new `shownBox` option (SDR JPEG frames only) halves frames, with 2x2 area averaging, as many times as they still cover the box; the ffmpeg expression works from the decoded, rotated size and never upscales. An exact resize to the box was tried first: it made frames sharper and noisier than Chrome's own downscale (which averages through power-of-two levels), and output files grew noticeably. Halving keeps the drawn picture and file size close to before, at the same speed.
- **Full size kept** for anything whose pixels are read, not just drawn: colour-graded videos, any page with a canvas other than the grading canvases (WebGL / WebGPU / 2D could sample a video), `object-fit: none | scale-down`, a video never laid out in the chunk, and HDR / PNG / alpha extraction.
- **Exact per chunk.** Each chunk measures its own frames, so a video that zooms to full screen in one chunk is extracted at full size there and small in the chunks where it is small. Plan-time sampling was rejected because a zoom between samples would render blurry.
- The chunk perf sidecar records `videoShownBoxes` so a render shows which videos were shrunk.

## Test plan

Parity bar, set before measuring: per-frame SSIM against main of at least 0.99 (min) and 0.995 (mean) over the full frame, and at least 0.97 (min) inside the box the shrunk video is drawn in.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `videoFrameExtractor.test.ts`: real ffmpeg; a 64x36 source with boxes 16x9 / 20x12 / 40x20 gives 16x10 / 32x18 / 64x36 frames.
  - `videoFrameInjector-shownBoxes.browser.test.ts`: real Chrome; largest box across seeks at device scale 2, a video laid out only late, graded and `object-fit: none` excluded, a page canvas keeps everything full size.
  - `renderChunk.test.ts`: `extractDeferredVideoFramesForChunk` honours the box; a real chunk render records the measured boxes (32x18 bubble, 128x72 full) in its sidecar. The existing chunk tests (skip list, video read by URL renders the same chunk) still pass.
  - Each new test passed 3 runs in a row; each was shown to fail with its code path broken (extractor ignoring the box, measurement ignoring device pixel ratio, ignoring the page canvas, chunk extraction dropping the box).
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Heavy 4K fixture (full-screen screen recording plus camera bubble), whole film, every frame, cloud render of main vs this branch on the same day: full frame and bubble both pass the bar; the worst bubble frame checked by eye side by side. Lambda compute and cost per render went down, wall time went down, output file size stayed close to main's.
  - Zoom animation fixture (the camera grows from the bubble to full screen across chunk boundaries): every frame passes the bar; frames are shrunk only in the chunk where the camera is small.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Not exercised: H.264 sources on a cloud render (HEVC sources were); Cloud Run end to end (same `renderChunk` code path).

title: docs: say background removal can drop objects a person holds
body:
## What changed

The remove-background guide now says the included model can drop all or part of an object a person holds (a dark microphone, phone, card or instrument), and adds a "Part of a held object is missing" row to Common problems. The CLI's default model stays `u2net_human_seg`. No code changes.

## Why

A user reported that background removal on a person holding a dark microphone made parts of the mic transparent. `u2net_human_seg` is a people-only model. We measured whether a general-purpose model should replace it, with the rule to switch only if a candidate gave better edges **and** was no slower per frame. None was. The quality win is real, but the cheapest candidate is 2.8x slower, so the default stays and the guide now names the case.

## What I measured

**Candidates**, with preprocessing and ONNX files exactly as rembg v2.0.85 `rembg/sessions/*.py` (md5 of every download matched rembg's):

| model | input | normalisation | output | download |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `u2net_human_seg` (today) | 320 | ImageNet mean/std | min-max | 168 MB |
| `isnet-general-use` | 1024 | mean 0.5, std 1.0 | min-max | 171 MB |
| `birefnet-general-lite` | 1024 | ImageNet mean/std | sigmoid, then min-max | 214 MB |
| `birefnet-general` | 1024 | ImageNet mean/std | sigmoid, then min-max | 928 MB |

Every model ran through the CLI's own `createSession` / `process` path (onnxruntime-node 1.21.1, CPU provider, `graphOptimizationLevel: "all"`). Model choice and per-model preprocessing were patched into a local copy only.

**Ground truth.** I used seven green-screen clips of people from Mixkit (Mixkit Stock Video Free License), five of them holding something: a dark handheld mic (28293), a black bass guitar (23862), black phones (28311, 28286, 24388) and a black card (9099). Clip 28287 has no object. A chroma key gave the ground-truth alpha, and each frame was composited over one of three real plates (meadow, street with bikes, dark alley). That is 45 frames per clip, 315 frames in all. Metrics: IoU of the matte at 0.5, mean absolute alpha error, the same error inside a 10 px band around the true edge, false-positive rate, and recall inside a hand-set box around each held object. No clips are committed.

**Edge quality**, on the 141 frames scored for all three practical models:

| model | IoU | MAE | edge MAE | false-pos | held-object recall |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u2net_human_seg | 0.926 | 0.0121 | 0.130 | 0.0033 | 0.913 |
| isnet-general-use | 0.938 | 0.0096 | 0.106 | 0.0032 | 0.960 |
| birefnet-general-lite | 0.977 | 0.0033 | 0.056 | 0.0014 | 0.988 |

On all 315 frames, u2net vs isnet scored IoU 0.956 vs 0.959, edge MAE 0.109 vs 0.094, and held-object recall 0.912 vs 0.932. On the 15 frames where the full BiRefNet ran: IoU 0.978, edge MAE 0.052, against lite's 0.977 and 0.055 on the same frames.

Held-object recall by clip (all 315 frames, u2net / isnet): mic 0.982 / 0.996, card 0.780 / 0.790, bass 0.902 / 0.958, phone 0.984 / 0.983. In the contact sheets, u2net leaves see-through bands across the mic handle on some frames, drops the card entirely, and drops the guitar body. isnet keeps the objects but softens the body on the card clip, and picks up a background bike and a stand-mounted boom mic. BiRefNet-lite keeps the held objects cleanly. That last point matters for the captions skill, which relies on u2net leaving boom arms out of the matte (`skills/embedded-captions/references/anti-patterns.md`).

**Speed**, ms per frame through `process()`. This covers the model run plus the input/output resizes and alpha composite at 1280x720, with the first 5 frames dropped as warm-up. All models ran at the same thread settings: `intraOpNumThreads: 2`, `interOpNumThreads: 1`, one process at a time, on a shared 8-core Linux x86_64 machine under other load. The numbers are relative, not absolute.

| model | median | p90 | vs u2net | peak RSS | frames timed |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| u2net_human_seg | 754 ms | 782 ms | 1.0x | 1.1 GB | 100 |
| isnet-general-use | 2092 ms | 2234 ms | 2.8x | 1.9 GB | 100 |
| birefnet-general-lite | 9594 ms | 10140 ms | 12.7x | 11.4 GB | 22 |
| birefnet-general | 21469 ms | 25068 ms | 28x | 13.5 GB | 10 |

A u2net rerun after the others gave a 632 ms median, so the box got quieter, not busier. The ratios above are, if anything, kind to the candidates. An earlier pass at onnxruntime's default thread count put isnet at 1.7x (315 frames) and BiRefNet-lite at about 14x (8-frame probe).

**Verdict:** BiRefNet wins on edge quality and held objects, but is 13x to 28x slower and needs about 11 GB of RAM. isnet is slightly better on edges but 2.8x slower, with new false positives. None passes "no slower", so the default stays.

## What I did NOT exercise

- CoreML (the default on Apple Silicon) and CUDA. Speed ratios on those providers were not measured.
- A dedicated, quiet machine. The timings are relative only.
- The full BiRefNet on more than 15 quality frames and 10 timed frames. BiRefNet-lite was timed on 22 frames.
- Bit-exactness of mattes across thread counts. Quality frames came from both the default-thread and 2-thread runs.
- Natural footage scored against ground truth. Scored frames are green-screen composites, the chroma key is imperfect at hair and on a small spill spot, and frame-to-frame flicker was not scored. Plain (non-green) mic clips were only checked by eye.
- The end-to-end CLI video encode. ffmpeg decode and encode cost the same for every model and were left out of the timing.

title: fix(inspector): a component report under budget keeps the animation code before CSS candidates
body:
## What

When `grep_components` (the inspector's component report) cannot fit every snippet in `maxBytes`, it now keeps the code that makes the animations, not the CSS rules that come first in the file.

Snippets now fill the budget by kind, in this order:

1. `animation creation`
2. `animation caller`
3. `timeline attachment`
4. `html opening tag`
5. `animation source dependency`
6. `matched CSS candidate`

A merged snippet ranks by its highest kind. The snippets that fit are still returned in file order.

## Why

This was measured on the HyperFrames launch trilogy project, in HyperFrames Desktop agent evals. It builds on #5989, which turns a caller inside a large wrapper (an IIFE around a scene) into a one-line snippet, so the animation code becomes many small snippets instead of one 65 KB block.

With #5989 applied to the 0.8.181 bundle, a default-budget (12,000 bytes) `grep_components` call on `#scene-11` of `films/inspector-launch` still returned no animation code:

- Snippets fill the budget in file order. This film's CSS rules sit on lines 396–1200 and its script starts at line 2105, so 14 `matched CSS candidate` snippets used the whole budget.
- Every animation snippet was `omitted`.

With this change, the same call returns all ten `animation creation` snippets for the scene (lines 3257–3318), and the omitted ones are CSS candidates.

In the evals, agents worked around missing animation code by reading the file themselves:

- In N09, the agent read lines 3240–3329 right after its `grep_components` call. That is exactly the range now returned.
- In N19, the agent read 580 and 691 lines.

When asked afterwards, both said they read the file because the report had omitted the script.

## Related work

Refs #5989.

## How

- `mapInspection`: before the budget loop, the merged snippets are sorted by their highest-ranked kind. The sort is stable, so `offset`/`nextOffset` still page through one fixed order. Snippets requested by id keep the order they were requested in.
- After the loop, automatically selected snippets are sorted back into file and line order. Explicit snippet-ID responses retain request order.
- The response shape is unchanged, so hosts with an output schema for this report need no change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added in `tests/mapInspection.test.ts`:
  - under a tight budget, the `animation creation` snippet is kept while the CSS candidates above it are omitted;
  - the kept snippets come back in file order, with none omitted when the budget fits them all;
  - explicit snippet-ID requests return two snippets in reverse file order as requested (regression reproduced before the fix).
- [x] Initial author validation: `vitest run` in `packages/inspector`: 47 passed.
- [x] Followthrough validation at `a64ae9494`: `vitest run tests/mapInspection.test.ts tests/sources.test.ts`: 14 passed, including the explicit-ID regression. Lint, formatting, comment checks and normal commit hooks passed.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` pass, and so do the pre-commit hooks (tracked-artifacts, fallow, typecheck).
- [x] `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs` and `scripts/check-comment-citations.mjs` pass.
- [x] Manual: ran the patched 0.8.181 bundle (#5989 plus this ranking) against a copy of the eval project and compared default-budget reports for `#scene-07` and `#scene-11` before and after.
- [ ] Not covered: no new eval run yet. That waits for a release with both changes.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments". This change adds none.

Google, Bing and Yandex each have a free console that shows how they see a site: which pages they've saved (indexed), which searches people found them with, how many clicked, and any errors. title: fix(lint): place each scene's audio at its host's start in the audio overlap check
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` (and `lint`) stop reporting `duplicate_audio_track` for scenes that play one after another. Each scene's audio is now placed on the main timeline at its host's start and cut to its host's window, the way playback does. Scenes that really overlap still warn.

## Why

A project whose root mounts scenes in sequence, each scene holding an audible `<video>` at local time 0, got a warning for every pair of scenes: the rule read each file's local `data-start` as if it were main-timeline time. It scanned every file under `compositions/` flat, so it never knew which host mounts a file or when.

Repro on `main`: a root with two `data-composition-src` hosts at `data-start="0"` and `data-start="5"` (5 s each), each scene with `<video src="clipN.mp4" data-start="0" data-duration="5" data-track-index="0">`. `hyperframes lint` prints `duplicate_audio_track: ... clip1.mp4 at 0-5.0s, clip2.mp4 at 0-5.0s`. With this branch, no audio overlap finding.

## Related work

None open for this rule.

## How

- **One owner for nested media time.** The runtime and `hyperframes timeline` already share `mediaTiming.ts` (host start minus in-point is the scene's origin; `data-hf-media-start-basis="global"` keeps a legacy root time; host slots cut a clip). It lived in `@hyperframes/core`, which lint cannot import (core depends on lint). It moves to `@hyperframes/parsers` (new `./media-timing` subpath, added through `package-subpaths.json`); `@hyperframes/core/media-timing` re-exports it, so no importer changes.
- **One owner for reference starts.** `data-start="card-pro"` (start when that clip ends, as `docs/concepts/compositions.mdx` teaches for chained scenes) is resolved by engine's `referenceResolver.ts`, which render's audio mixer, frame extraction and `hyperframes timeline` already use. Lint cannot import engine either, so it moves to parsers the same way (`./reference-resolver`), with engine re-exporting it.
- **The rule walks what plays.** `duplicate_audio_track` walks the parsed root document and follows `data-composition-src` mounts (template content included), the same reachability `missing_or_empty_sub_composition` uses. Each composition or host shifts its children's origin and adds its authored window (the runtime clamps nested media to it). A cycle guard stops a scene that mounts itself.
- Consequences: a file under `compositions/` that nothing mounts no longer contributes audio (it never plays). The old `src:start:duration:track` de-duplication is gone, since each mount is now a distinct placement. Audio whose own `data-start` is a reference is now placed too (main skipped it).
- `isAudibleVideo` takes an attribute reader so the DOM walk and the tag-text rules share one audible-video decision.
- Known limits, unchanged from main: a host with no authored length does not cut its audio (its timeline length is only known at runtime), and inline `<template>` scenes in `index.html` are not followed.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. `packages/lint/src/project.test.ts`: scenes in sequence pass (with and without host lengths), scenes chained by reference pass while a `"s0 - 2"` overlap warns, overlapping hosts still warn, a clip longer than its scene is cut at the host's end. Three of the four are red on `main`; each part of the fix (host offset, host window, following mounts, reference resolution) was broken in turn and a different test went red each time. 3 green runs in a row.
- [x] `packages/cli/src/utils/lintProject.test.ts`: the multi-file test now mounts its scene; the open-ended format test drops the root length so the clip stays open-ended.
- [x] Full `@hyperframes/lint` suite, `lintProject.test.ts`, `parsers` `mediaTiming.test.ts`, core `startResolver`/`media` tests, engine `audioMixer`/`videoFrameExtractor` and cli `describeProject` tests (the resolver's other consumers), `package-subpaths` verification, oxlint, and `tsc --noEmit` for parsers, lint, engine, core and cli: all green.
- [x] Manual: the repro above through `hyperframes lint`, before and after.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(cli): a first render on a nearly full disk refuses at once instead of hanging
body:
## What

A render on a disk with less than 1 GB free now stops at once with the "Low disk space" box, before it downloads anything. A browser download (from a render or `hyperframes browser ensure`) refuses up front when the cache's disk has under 512 MB free, saying how much it needs and how much is free.

## Why

On a fresh machine the first render downloads Chrome Headless Shell. `render` did that before its disk check, so a nearly full disk spent its last space on the download and only then got refused. When the disk filled during extraction it was worse: `@puppeteer/browsers` extracts with `unzip` through `execFile`, which leaves unzip's stdin open. Info-ZIP unzip answers a write error with `write error (disk full?).  Continue? (y/n/^C)` and waits on stdin, so the render hung forever. It also kept the browser install lock alive, so every later render sat on "Checking browser" until it was killed.

Reproduced on Linux with CLI 0.8.181 and a 200 MB filesystem as home and temp: the render was still in `unzip` after 12 minutes, and a second render waited on the lock until its 2-minute timeout. macOS's own unzip (UnZip 6.00 with Apple's changes) behaves the same on a 20 MB RAM disk: with stdin open it waits forever, and with stdin closed it exits 50 ("disk full") in 6 ms.

## Related work

The prompt itself comes from `@puppeteer/browsers` (3.2.5 is still the latest and still runs `unzip` with stdin open). This PR keeps us out of that state; an upstream fix that closes unzip's stdin would cover the remaining race, where another process fills the disk during the download.

## How

- `commands/render/execute.ts`: `executeRenderPlan` runs `checkDisk` on the temp folder and the output folder before `ensureRenderBrowser`, with the same paths and the same 1 GB floor as the later local preflight. Docker renders are unchanged.
- Both checks first remove what a killed install left behind (`.chrome-staging-*`, `.chrome-replaced-*`), so our own leftovers never count against the floor: `downloadBrowser` already holds the install lock there, and the render takes it (`sweepKilledInstalls`) only when a leftover exists.
- `browser/manager.ts`: `downloadBrowser` checks free space at the cache root before `install()`. The 512 MB floor comes from measuring Chrome 152: the archive and the unpacked shell sit side by side in staging, 285 MB at peak on macOS arm64 (93 MB zip + 192 MB) and 381 MB on Windows (113 MB + 268 MB). Every download already runs under `withInstallLock`, which creates the cache root, so the reading is never of a missing folder.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `execute.test.ts`: at 400 MB free the render prints "Low disk space" and never calls `ensureBrowser`; at 4096 MB it goes on to the browser.
  - `manager.test.ts`: at 400 MB free `ensureBrowser` rejects with the low-disk message and `install()` never runs; at 4096 MB it downloads.
  - `manager.test.ts`: a killed install's staging folder is gone before free space is read; when free space cannot be read, the download goes ahead.
  - Both 400 MB cases fail on `main` (removed the two source changes, reran: 3 failed, the 4096 MB manager case among them because `main` never reads free space), and pass with the fix: 93/93 across `execute`, `manager` and `preflight` tests.
- [x] Manual testing performed: built this branch's CLI and ran it on a Mac with a fresh home and temp folder on a RAM disk, no browser cached.
  - 450 MB disk (437 MB free): `render` exits 1 in under a second with two "Low disk space" boxes (temp and output folder); `browser ensure` exits 1 with "needs about 512 MB to download, 436 MB free"; the cache stays empty.
  - 800 MB disk holding a killed install's 350 MB staging folder (447 MB free): `browser ensure` removes it, installs in 31 s, leaves no staging folder, 588 MB free after.
  - 800 MB disk: `render` still refuses below its 1 GB floor without downloading; `browser ensure` downloads (93 MB) and finishes in 37 s with 585 MB left.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): no doc names this order.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Not exercised: Windows (its zip path uses `tar.exe` or PowerShell, not Info-ZIP, so the hang is not known there; the space floor applies the same way), and the batch render path beyond sharing `executeRenderPlan`.
