title: fix(core): grade an image that appears after its scene starts hidden
body: ## What a user sees A color-graded `` (set with `media-treatment` / `data-color-grading`) rendered **ungraded** in `snapshot` and `render` when it was hidden at the moment grading first scanned the page: - an image in a layer that starts `visibility:hidden` and a timeline reveals later (`tl.set(layer, { visibility: "visible" })`) - an image in a sub-composition whose host starts later than 0 s - a full-frame still inserted mid-timeline inside a timed wrapper Reported on 0.8.181. The same grade worked when the scene started at 0 s, and when the layer was shown with `opacity` instead of `visibility`. ## Why `refresh()` in `packages/core/src/runtime/colorGrading.ts` decides which media gets graded, and keeps an element only if its computed visibility is visible right then. After the first reveal pass it only re-runs on a DOM child-list or `data-color-grading` change. An ancestor's `visibility` flipping (a timeline `set`, a host's clip window opening) is neither, so the image was never adopted. The per-seek `redraw()` that snapshot and render call before every capture only draws media that is already tracked. Tracked entries already follow visibility on every draw (`syncSourceAppearance`); only adoption was missing. It sometimes looked fine: grading any other element inserts its canvas, which fires the observer and rescues hidden images by accident. The tests use one project per shape for this reason. ## Fix `refresh()` now records the graded media it skipped because it was hidden. `redraw()` and `redrawAnimated()` (the seek path and the playback tick) first re-check only that list and adopt whatever has come into view, using the same visibility rule as `refresh()`. That rule now has one owner, `isShownForColorGrading`. An element leaves the list as soon as anything tries to set it up or removes it on purpose, so: - a grade Studio switches off live stays off, even while the saved attribute still grades; - media the runtime hides or un-grades itself is never re-adopted; - a page without WebGL does not retry context creation every frame (caught by the existing `allocates color grading only for the active timed media` test); - no per-frame document scan: only media still waiting to be shown is checked. ## Tests - `packages/producer/src/services/render/lateVisibleImageGrading.integration.test.ts`: a real render of the three shapes, one project each. On main all three fail at the reveal frame (level 128, the ungraded source grey); with the fix all three pass, 3 runs in a row. - `packages/core/src/runtime/colorGrading.test.ts`: an image whose ancestor starts hidden is graded once a seek (`redraw`) or a playback tick (`redrawAnimated`) shows it; both fail on main. A grade switched off live stays off, whether the image is shown or still hidden; these fail if adoption scans every graded element or if removal leaves an element on the waiting list. 103/103 pass, 3 runs. - `packages/core/src/runtime`: 2165/2165 pass. - CLI `snapshot` on the same fixtures: before, the revealed layer and the late host measured 126 (ungraded); after, 63 (graded). ## Independent pre-review No blockers, no majors. Its minor findings are addressed on this head: a live grade switched off came back on the next frame (fixed, with a test), a failed setup blocked an element for good (that skip list is gone), and the per-frame document scan (gone). | Audited | How | |---|---| | Adoption against `refresh`, `setSourceVisibility`, `setGrading`, context loss | code read plus jsdom probes | | Every `redraw` / `redrawAnimated` caller and the render-seek ordering | `init.ts`, `player.ts`, `frameCapture.ts`, `screenshotService.ts` | | Each new test fails when its part of the fix is removed | mutations, one per test | Not exercised: a real Chrome benchmark with many graded elements, Studio playback end to end, a real WebGL context loss, a render with a LUT, layered capture, Linux.

title: fix(cli): a disk that fills mid-unzip fails the browser install at once instead of hanging
body:
## What

On macOS and Linux the CLI now unzips the browser download itself, with unzip's input closed, then lets
`@puppeteer/browsers`' `install()` finish (it finds the unpacked folder, runs its setup and deletes the archive).
Windows keeps the library's own path (tar.exe or PowerShell, which never ask).

## Why

Follow-up to #6006. When the disk fills while the browser unpacks, unzip prints
`write error (disk full?).  Continue? (y/n/^C)` and waits for an answer on its input. `install()` runs unzip through
`execFile`, which leaves that input open, so the answer never comes: the first render hangs for good while holding
the install lock. #6006 refuses up front when there is clearly too little room; this covers the disk that fills
mid-unzip (another process writing, or a tight margin).

Reproduced on a 20 MB RAM disk with a 60 MB zip (`execFile("unzip", ["-o", zip, "-d", dir])`):

| unzip's input | result |
|---|---|
| left open (as `install()` runs it) | still waiting after 15 s, killed |
| closed (this PR) | exits 50 in about 0.1 s, `write error (disk full?)` |

The failure then reads `Failed to install chrome-headless-shell …: Extraction failed: … write error (disk full?)`
with the usual `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH` hint, and the staging folder is removed as before.

## How

- `browser/unzipArchive.ts`: `unzip -q -o <archive> -d <dir>` through the existing `runCancellableProcess`
  (input already closed). No unzip binary: returns false, and `install()` unpacks with its own fallback.
- `browser/manager.ts`: `install({ unpack: false })` to download, `unzipArchive` into
  `Cache.installationDir(...)` of the staging folder, then `install()`. A corrupt archive still reads as corrupt
  (unzip's own words) and still gets one re-download.

## Tests

- `unzipFallback.test.ts`, real processes: the composition against the real `install()` (our unzip lands where
  `install()` looks, it then returns the browser and the archive is gone); a stand-in `unzip` that asks the
  question and reads its input fails at once; no `unzip` on PATH returns false.
- `manager.test.ts`: linux and darwin unzip first, win32 does not; a disk that fills mid-unzip fails the install
  without calling `install()` again and leaves no staging folder.
- Each was broken on purpose and failed: no own unzip, own unzip on Windows too, input left open (the
  full-disk test times out), no missing-binary fallback.

title: fix(inspector): a component report shows the compositions and hosts that time a matched element
body:
## What

When an element matched by the component report (`grep_components`) sits inside a sub-composition, the report now also includes the tags that set its timing:

- `composition root`: each enclosing `data-composition-id` tag, plus the root that a targeted host mounts;
- `composition host`: each `data-composition-src` tag that mounts the element's file, up to the project's root composition. Repeated mounts and their ancestor branches are labeled as source candidates; all alternatives remain available rather than implying one runtime instance chain.

These are opening tags only. They come after every other snippet, so under `maxBytes` they fill only the budget that is left over. A tag that another snippet already shows is left out.

## Why

In HyperFrames Desktop agent evals (trilogy N13), agents read these lines with `Read` right after a `grep_components` call:

- the film's root tag (`films/sfx-music-launch/index.html` 48–56);
- the mounted root (`compositions/available.html` 5);
- the project root (`index.html` 14).

They needed `data-start` and `data-duration` along the chain to retime a section.

Replaying the 62 recorded `grep_components` calls from kept Mods sessions (40 Reads follow them):

| Read right after the call | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| lines in no snippet | 19 | 14 |
| lines already shown | 12 | 17 |
| inside an omitted snippet larger than the budget | 7 | 7 |
| inside an omitted snippet that fits | 2 | 2 |

The replay adds the composition snippets to each recorded result on the starting project and keeps the call's budget. All five N13 reads are now covered. The other 14 are snapshot images, scripts and CSS for classes nobody targeted.

Cost: 24 of the 62 calls gain snippets. Those calls gain a median of 4 snippets (598 bytes of code), at most 1,344 bytes.

## How

- `sources.ts`: `htmlTagsOf` records each tag's parent, `data-composition-id` and `data-composition-src`. The parent comes from an htmlparser2 pass, so void elements, implied closes, comments and raw text nest the way a browser nests them. htmlparser2 becomes an inspector dependency; it is already in the lockfile through `@hyperframes/lint`.
- `Sources.compositions(tag)` walks up from the matched tag:
  - first, the enclosing composition roots in its file;
  - then, the hosts that mount that file, with `src` resolved from the project root first and then from the host's directory;
  - it repeats from each host until it reaches the top.
  - mounted roots follow the host composition ID, matching the assembly contract; an absent ID selects the first root, while an unmatched ID adds no root.
  - mount lookups normalize path separators while retaining native file keys in reports, including Windows nested paths.
- `mapInspection` appends these snippets after the merged snippets. Merging them separately keeps them out of the other snippets' ranges.

This works with #6003: an unranked kind sorts last there, and the two branches merge without conflicts. With both applied, `mapInspection.test.ts` and `mapCompositions.test.ts` pass.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/mapCompositions.test.ts`:
  - covers an element two sub-compositions deep;
  - covers a targeted host, multiple roots, missing/no host ID, Windows source keys, and scoped/ref-selected repeated mounts;
  - skips tags that another snippet already shows;
  - under a tight budget, omits the composition snippets before the element's own snippets.
- [x] `tests/mapInspection.test.ts`, `tests/sources.test.ts`, `tests/elementMap.test.ts` and `tsc --noEmit` pass.


Validation of review fixes: 50 focused tests across `mapCompositions`, `mapInspection`, `elementMap`, and `sources` pass locally. Lint, format, comment checks, and normal commit-hook typechecks pass.


Candidate explanations consume budget only when a candidate snippet is selected; a 2,048-byte regression preserves the primary opening tag when ancestry does not fit.


Integrated current main after #6016: compact snippet IDs and co-target ordering are preserved. Candidate-only coverage remains optional and is charged only when a candidate fits. Inspector typecheck and focused compact-report/composition tests pass.

title: fix(inspector): a component report names a snippet's file and lines only in its id
body:
## What

The component report (`grep_components`) spends less of its byte budget on fields the agent never acts on, so more source fits:

- **No fixed `coverage` sentences.** Every report carried the same four disclaimers (566 bytes). The README already states those limits.
- **A snippet names its file and lines once, in its `id`** (`file:start-end`). `file`, `startLine` and `endLine` repeated the id. `targets` is shown only when the query names more than one target; with one target it was always `[0]`. `kind`, `code` and `uniqueInFile` stay (`uniqueInFile` tells an agent whether the code can be used as an exact-match edit).
- **`coTargets` lists at most three elements**, prioritizing elements outside all queried results, with `coTargetsOmitted` counting the rest. It was up to ten full element records.

## Why

Measured in HyperFrames Desktop agent stress runs. An agent asked `grep_components` for `.pt-key` with `maxBytes: 3000` and got 2,882 bytes with no snippets: eight `coTargets` (1,221 bytes), the coverage sentences (566) and the rest of the metadata left no room under the budget for even a 61-byte snippet, so all six were `omitted`.

Same project, same query, before and after this change:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `maxBytes: 3000` | 2,882 bytes, **0** snippets | 2,553 bytes, **1** snippet (the 378-byte line that creates the animation, kept first since #6003) |
| `maxBytes: 12000` | 5,923 bytes, 6 snippets | **4,136** bytes, the same 6 snippets |

At the default budget the same answer is 30% smaller: snippet metadata 1,065 → 599 bytes, `coTargets` 1,221 → 457, `coverage` 566 → 0.

## How

- `mapInspection`: the response shows each kept snippet through `shown()`, which drops `file`/`startLine`/`endLine` (and `targets` for a one-target query). The catalog keeps full snippets, so paging, explicit-ID requests and file-order sorting are unchanged. The budget loop measures the shown form.
- `coTargets` prioritizes unqueried elements before slicing to three; `coTargetsOmitted` appears only when some were left out.
- README "Output" describes the new snippet shape and the `coTargets` cap.
- Browser, film and live tests read a snippet's lines from its id through a small `tests/snippetSource.ts` helper.

The response shape changes. The Desktop agent's output schema and the two readers of a snippet's file accept both shapes in heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#4997, which lands before this ships there.

## Test plan

- [x] New unit tests in `tests/mapInspection.test.ts`: no `coverage` and a one-target snippet of only `id`/`kind`/`code`/`uniqueInFile`; two targets keep `targets`; seven co-targets list three and count four. The first and third fail on main.
- [x] `vitest run` in `packages/inspector`: 51 passed.
- [x] `bun tests/browser.ts <gsap.min.js>`: passes, including "literal snippets equal original bytes" read through the id.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, pre-commit hooks, `comment-ratchet.mjs` and `check-comment-citations.mjs` pass.
- [x] Manual: the measurement above, `Inspector` from this branch and from main against the stress project.
- [ ] Not covered: `tests/film.ts` and `tests/live.ts` (they need the film project and a live server); their change is the same id-based read as `browser.ts`.
- [ ] Not covered: a live agent run with the new shape; that waits for a release.

Review follow-up: the four-query/fifth-target regression reproduced before the fix and now passes. All 10 focused mapping tests and normal pre-commit/commit-msg hooks pass locally at `acd38ccf50073114aef6a87b185ea26a95babf7c`. The browser/stress measurements above remain author-reported evidence from the initial head.

title: fix(aws-lambda): the size check on every PR measures the package a release publishes
body:
## What changes

The package size check that runs on every PR now measures the `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` tarball a release actually publishes. The v0.8.182 publish stopped at that check (aws-lambda over its budget: 70,170 bytes packed, 254,853 unpacked) after the release PR had passed it.

- `prebuilt/template.yaml` (the SAM template a `lambda deploy` from an npm install uses) is now written by the package build, through one helper (`scripts/prebuilt-template.mjs`) that the release pin step also calls. Before, only the release pin step wrote it.
- The tarball stops shipping `scripts/*.test.ts` (3 files).
- The aws-lambda budget becomes the measured publish size × 1.05, the headroom the gate itself suggests.

## Why

PR CI and publish packed two different artifacts. PR CI runs `bun run build` and then `verify:packed-manifests`. Publish runs the same build, then `pin-handler-zip.ts`, which copies the example SAM template into `prebuilt/` (36 KB unpacked), and only then the size check. So template growth (#5997 added the audio branch to the state machine) was invisible on every PR and showed up for the first time at publish.

Only raising the budget cannot hold, because the gate also fails a package more than 15% under its budget. A budget sized for the publish artifact would have failed every PR (CI view 218,875 / 258,166 = 0.848). With both views packing the template, one budget fits both. It also means the gate now protects this: if the template ever leaves the build again, the PR's unpacked size falls under the 85% floor and its own CI fails.

`prebuiltHandler()` only treats a build as pinned when `prebuilt/handler-zip.json` exists, and only the release writes that file. A template on its own changes no runtime behaviour. `prebuilt/` stays gitignored.

## Evidence

Built at main `1d422a2f` on Linux, aws-lambda packed with `npm pack --dry-run`:

| | packed | unpacked | files |
|---|---|---|---|
| CI view, before | 62,219 | 218,875 | 40 (3 tests, no template) |
| publish view, before | 69,914 | 255,418 | 42 |
| CI view, this branch | 67,351 | 245,631 | 39 (template, no tests) |
| publish view, this branch | 67,499 | 245,872 | 40 (template + pin manifest) |
| budget, this branch | 70,874 | 258,166 | |

The publish view is shaped the way `publish.yml` runs it: the full build, then `pin-handler-zip.ts` against a stand-in zip of the real handler's byte count, so the manifest is the same length.

- `bun run verify:packed-manifests` in both views: aws-lambda raised no size issue in either, and every package's manifest and consumer-install checks passed. The run still exits 1 on this Linux box because `@hyperframes/parsers` packs 629 bytes over its budget there. Main's own CI Build passes on the same commit (run 39575039012), so that difference is the local build environment, and this PR does not touch parsers.
- `pin-handler-zip.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail, 3 runs in a row. Its template cases (the `CodeUri` rewrite and the refusal of a template it cannot rewrite) now exercise the shared helper.
- Commit hooks (lint, format, fallow, typecheck, commitlint) and the comment citation and ratchet checks: exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real publish. This lands first, then v0.8.183 cuts with the 0.8.182 notes plus this fix.
- `lambda deploy` from a packed install. Its inputs (`template.yaml` and `handler-zip.json` under `prebuilt/`) are byte-for-byte what the pin step wrote before.

title: fix(lint): check no longer fails projects that inline the GSAP library
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` failed any project that pastes the GSAP library inline (for example GSAP 3.14.2 in a caption template layer). `non_deterministic_code` scanned GSAP's own source and reported its internals: `Math.random()` in `utils.shuffle`/`utils.random` and `Date.now()` in its ticker. Because the finding is an error, `check` also skipped its render pass on those projects, and the author had no way to clear it short of removing GSAP.

## Fix

`blankInlinedGsapLibrary` (`packages/lint/src/utils.ts`) parses the script with acorn and blanks GSAP's own code with spaces, so offsets and reported lines stay correct. `non_deterministic_code` then scans what is left, as before.

GSAP's code is a call anywhere in the tree that has GSAP's UMD wrapper structure: a function expression that reads the real member `define.amd` in its own body (not inside a nested function), called with exactly `(this, function …)`. Each GSAP banner (`/*! … GreenSock … */`) or producer `/* inlined: <src> */` comment whose `<src>` URL path is an npm gsap dist file (`gsap[@version]/dist/<file>.js`; a name that only contains `gsap` does not count) belongs to at most one wrapper. First choice is the wrapper that starts right after it, skipping only whitespace, comments, `!`, `;` and `(` (minified builds, producer comments, statement separators). A banner anywhere else owns nothing. Only wrappers that own a banner are blanked, and only their own call range.

What stays checked:
- author code before or after the library, in the same statement (comma-joined), or in an outer IIFE, two-argument wrapper or UMD bundle around it
- an outer wrapper that has `define.amd` only inside a nested library
- an outer bundle around GSAP, even when a producer comment, a `;` separator or a stray banner sits inside it
- `define.amd` that appears only as text, in a string or a comment
- a wrapper whose banner is separated from it by other code, or that has no banner
- a script that only mentions GreenSock in a string or comment, or that fails to parse

Known limits:
- A hand-built copy of GSAP's wrapper and banner around author code is exempt. Proving the code really is GSAP would mean pinning file contents per GSAP version and plugin. That breaks on every release and on any re-minified copy, which brings this false positive back. This rule is already text-level and easy to bypass on purpose (`Math["random"]()`); the aim is that nothing is exempted by accident.
- Unminified GSAP files pasted inline are still flagged, as on `main`: their banner sits inside the Rollup factory, which is exactly where a bundler also puts author code that imports GSAP, so the two cannot be told apart without pinning file contents. The minified builds (`gsap.min.js` and every plugin's `.min.js`), and any copy the producer inlines with its `/* inlined: */` comment, are exempt. Caption templates inline `gsap.min.js`.

`missing_gsap_script` is unchanged. It answers a different question (is GSAP loaded anywhere), where a loose marker match is the right call.

## Proof

- 23 tests in `packages/lint/src/rules/core.test.ts` use GSAP 3.14.2's real UMD wrapper, banner and internals. Proof runs:
  - with `main`'s rule, the 4 library tests fail (pasted, producer-inlined, author script beside GSAP, author code before and after GSAP in one tag)
  - with this PR's first head (whole-script skip on any marker), the 5 regressions fail: same-tag author code, a "GreenSock" string, a comment, a spoofed banner, a spoofed inlining comment
  - with the second head (`define.amd` text check over a whole top-level statement), the 4 regressions from the second review fail: comma-joined author code, author code in an outer IIFE, and `define.amd` in a string and in a comment
  - with the third head (banner anywhere inside a call; `define.amd` found in nested functions), the 4 regressions from the third review fail: a two-argument outer wrapper, an outer UMD bundle around minified or unminified GSAP, and an outer wrapper that borrows `define.amd`
  - with the fourth head (banner falls back to any enclosing wrapper; adjacency skipped only whitespace and `!`), the 4 regressions from the fourth review fail: GSAP after a `;` separator, producer-inlined unminified GSAP in a bundle, separated GSAP in a bundle, a stray banner in a bundle
    - with the fifth head (banner falls back to the innermost enclosing wrapper that wraps no other), the Rollup regression fails: a real Rollup 4 ESM-to-UMD bundle of GSAP plus `Math.random()` / `Date.now()` reports nothing
    - with the sixth head (any `inlined:` source containing `gsap` counts), the 3 regressions from the sixth review fail: a Rollup/Terser bundle inlined from `gsap-composition.js`, `scene.js?vendor=gsap` and another domain's `gsap-demo/scene.js`
  - mutations: skipping only whitespace and `!` fails the 2 separator tests; letting the fallback own a wrapper that wraps another fails the stray-banner test
  - mutations: letting the `define.amd` search enter nested functions fails only the borrowed-`define.amd` test; choosing the outermost containing wrapper fails only the unminified-in-bundle test; dropping the adjacent-banner owner fails the 8 tests that use minified GSAP
- All 25 minified `dist/*.min.js` files of gsap@3.14.2 lint clean. The full 246 KB Rollup bundle of GSAP plus author code reports both author calls (none on the previous head); the same bundle of author code alone reports both too. Lint time for the whole matrix, back to back on one box: 13.96–14.84 s here vs 13.82–13.89 s on `main`.
- The fourth review's probes with the real, unchanged gsap@3.14.2 files inside an outer UMD bundle (producer-inlined `gsap.js` + author call; `;`-separated `gsap.min.js` + author call): this branch reports only the author's line; GSAP alone in the bundle reports nothing. `main` reports GSAP's own lines in every case.
- Real files linted at `main` vs this branch:

  | Input | `main` | this branch |
  |---|---|---|
  | full `gsap.min.js` 3.14.2 inline | `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` | none |
  | full unminified `gsap.js` 3.14.2 inline | `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` | `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` (known limit) |
  | `gsap.min.js` plus `window.seed = Math.random()` in the same tag | GSAP's line only | the author's line |
  | a real caption template project (GSAP 3.14.2 inline) | `Math.random()`, `Date.now()` | none |

  Lint time moved by 10–20 ms on these inputs, within run-to-run noise.
- Whole lint suite: 983 passed. `core` and `utils` test files: 3 runs in a row green. `tsc`, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow are clean.

title: chore: release v0.8.183
body:
v0.8.182 was tagged but never reached npm: its publish stopped at the package size check (fixed by #6017). This release ships everything listed for v0.8.182, plus #6013, #6015, #6016 and #6017.

Website capture now handles pages that reload after a cookie banner, CLI commands start faster, a repeat `check` starts with the CLI and Chrome already up, and `snapshot` and `check` wait for late images as `render` does. Renders inside a macOS sandbox no longer fail, a sharp sound at a film's start no longer grows louder with each audio pass, and `lambda sites create` takes source files over 5 GB. Cloud renders mix their audio beside the chunks and fail loudly when an audio read is cut off, a 4K camera shown small reaches Chrome near the size it is drawn, a finished `capture` exits even when a site's DNS never answers, and an unreadable frame fails a render instead of shortening it.

## Changes
- Versions bumped to 0.8.183 across the 14 published packages and 5 plugin manifests (`release:prepare 0.8.183 --from v0.8.181 --no-tag`).
- `releases/v0.8.183.md`: the v0.8.182 notes (42 PRs) plus #6013, #6016, #6015 and #6017, so 46 PRs, every one merged since v0.8.181. Checked against `git log v0.8.181..main`: none missing besides the v0.8.182 release commit itself.
- `docs/changelog.mdx`: the v0.8.182 entry becomes the v0.8.183 entry, with the same lines, the 4 additions and a sentence saying v0.8.182 never published. Users never got 0.8.182, so the changelog lists each change once, under the version that ships it. `releases/v0.8.182.md` stays as the record of the tag.

## No visible change
Version bump and changelog only; each change was captured in its own PR.

title: Player: speed button's accessible name doesn't include its visible text
body:
In `@hyperframes/player` (checked in 0.8.107, 0.8.181 and 0.8.183), the playback speed button shows "1x" but has `aria-label="Playback speed"`. Because the aria-label replaces the visible text, its accessible name doesn't contain "1x". That fails WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name, and axe-core reports it as `label-content-name-mismatch` (serious). A voice-control user who says "click 1x" can't press it.

**Suggested fix:** include the shown rate in the name and keep it updated when the rate changes, e.g. `aria-label="Playback speed: 1x"`. Or drop the aria-label and add the words with visually hidden text.

title: fix(cli): CLI tests and a refused preview stop killing orphaned Chrome
body:
## What changes

Three changes:

- Two tests in `packages/cli/src/utils/orphanCleanup.test.ts` are deleted: `killOrphanedProcesses > returns 0 when no orphans exist` and `> does not kill non-orphaned Chrome processes`.
- `preview` now runs its orphan cleanup after the host-app refusal, not before it. A preview refused inside a host app's agent run no longer kills orphaned Chrome on the way out. That is what the cleanup's own comment already required: it must not run for an invocation that never starts anything.
- `preview.test.ts` mocks `killOrphanedProcesses` for the whole file. The host-app refusal test now also checks that the cleanup is never called.

## Why

Both tests called the real `killOrphanedProcesses()`. That reads the live process table (`ps -U <uid>`) and kills every Chrome headless shell whose parent is init. So they asserted the state of the whole machine, not the function:

- **On CI they flake.** The CLI suite runs process tests in parallel, and some briefly leave a Chrome without its parent (the "kill the CLI mid busy-loop" tests do that on purpose). The release PR for v0.8.183 failed `Test (runtime)` exactly so: "expected 0 kills, got 2". Main passed the same suite on the same commit.
- **Off CI they are destructive.** Running the CLI tests on a developer's machine ran the real cleanup over that developer's whole process table. It killed any orphaned headless Chrome they owned, for example one left by another HyperFrames process or a separate Puppeteer script, and then failed the test for it.

A third test reached the same cleanup without calling it directly. The `preview` test "refuses before spawning anything" ran the real command, which called the cleanup before refusing. Moving the cleanup fixes the command; the file-wide mock keeps every other `preview` test away from the real process table.

The rule these tests meant to check, "kill orphaned Chrome, leave Chrome that still has a parent", is already covered without touching real processes. `orphanCleanup.scan.test.ts` feeds a fixed `ps` table with orphaned and parented Chrome and checks that only the orphans (101 and 103) are terminated.

## Evidence

Linux, each file run alone:

- `orphanCleanup.test.ts` + `orphanCleanup.scan.test.ts`: exit 0, 9 passed, 3 runs in a row.
- Mutation, restored after: removing the `ppid === 1` check in `killOrphansMatching` makes `orphanCleanup.scan.test.ts` fail (1 failed). The rule stays guarded after the deletion.
- CLI `tsc --noEmit`, oxfmt, lint, fallow, the process-ownership check and the comment checks: exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- macOS and Windows runs. The deleted tests and the scan test are all skipped on Windows, so on Windows this changes nothing.

title: ci: a hung Windows test run keeps its log, and commit hooks lint .mjs/.cjs files
body:
## What changes

Two small CI and tooling changes:

1. **Windows test steps get their own 16-minute limit and verbose output, and the job limit goes from 20 to 30 minutes.** The step limits cover the Studio shard step and the package-tests step in `windows-render.yml`.
2. **Commit hooks now lint and format `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.mts` and `.cts` files.** These are added to the `lint` and `format` globs in `lefthook.yml`.

## Why

**Windows hangs.** Today, when a Windows test run hangs, the 20-minute job limit cancels the whole job, and a cancelled job loses the step's log. So a hang shows up as "cancelled" with no hint of which test was running. With a limit on the step itself, that step fails first and the job finishes normally, so its log is kept. For that to work, the step limit has to fire before the job limit. The job's limit also covers setup: over the last 10 green runs, setup before the test step took up to 4m48s. Under a 20-minute job limit, a hung test would be cancelled at the job limit about 13 seconds before its own 16 minutes ran out. The job limit is now 30 minutes, so setup can take up to about 13 minutes and the step limit still fires first. No step in this job runs after a failure, so a timed-out step ends the job right away. A hang costs at most about 21 minutes of runner time, about what the old limit cost. `--reporter=verbose` prints every test name as it finishes, so the last test name in the log points at the test that hung. Over the last 8 green runs, the slowest of these steps took 9.5 minutes (engine-cli), so 16 leaves room for a slow runner and still fires before the job limit.

**Hook globs.** The hooks only matched `js/jsx/ts/tsx`, so a staged `.mjs` file was committed without lint or format. CI's `format:check` covers every file, so the gap first shows as a red CI run after the push. That happened on a recent `packages/aws-lambda/scripts/*.mjs` change.

## Evidence

- `actionlint .github/workflows/windows-render.yml`: exit 0.
- `oxfmt --check lefthook.yml .github/workflows/windows-render.yml`: exit 0.
- The commit itself went through the new hook config.

## What I did NOT exercise

- An actual Windows hang under the new limit. I couldn't reproduce the hang on demand, so the step-limit behaviour relies on GitHub's documented step `timeout-minutes`, not on an observed run.

title: test(cli): the capture network tests stop flaking on CI
body:
## What changes

Two flaky CLI capture tests are fixed. Only test files change.

- **`publicNetwork.test.ts`:** the fake DNS-lookup child processes now have a `kill()` method. A new test runs the exit hook, which kills every lookup child still running, and checks that it kills them.
- **`publicNetwork.integration.test.ts`:** the HTTPS fixture now reads a committed self-signed certificate and key from `src/capture/fixtures/` (valid until 2126, for `assets.capture-fixture.com`). Before, the test generated an RSA key with `openssl` inside `beforeAll`.

## Why

**Linux `Test (runtime)`: `TypeError: child.kill is not a function`.** `systemLookupInKillableChild` adds every lookup child to a set. An `exit` hook kills whatever is still in that set when the process exits. The unit test's fake children were bare `EventEmitter`s: they had no `kill()` and never emitted `exit`, so they stayed in the set. When the test worker exited, the hook crashed on them. Vitest reported the crash as an unhandled error only when it happened before the run finished reporting, so the failure was intermittent. The production code is right, since a real `ChildProcess` has `kill()`. The fake didn't match it.

**Windows engine-cli: `Hook timed out in 30000ms` in `beforeAll`.** The hook ran `openssl req -newkey rsa:2048` synchronously and then started three local servers. On green Windows runs, this file takes 36 to 54 s, and one of its tests takes about 35 s on its own. So the hook plus the other tests vary by up to about 19 s, close to the 30 s hook limit. The only step in the hook that can take seconds is the `openssl` child (RSA key generation, plus process start-up on a loaded runner). With a committed pair, the hook only reads two files. The test also no longer needs `openssl` installed.

## Evidence

Linux, devbox:

- `publicNetwork.test.ts` + `publicNetwork.integration.test.ts`: 49/49 passed, 3 runs in a row.
- Mutation 1, restored after: put back the bare `EventEmitter` fake. The new test fails with `TypeError: child.kill is not a function`, the CI error, now reproduced every time.
- Mutation 2, restored after: make `killLiveLookups` kill nothing. The new test fails.
- CLI `tsc --noEmit`, oxfmt, oxlint, comment citations and comment ratchet: exit 0.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A Windows run of the integration test with the committed pair. This PR's own Windows CI is that run.
- I didn't time the old `openssl` call on a CI runner. Pointing at it comes from the timing spread above, not from a measured hang.

title: fix(studio-server): keep transparency in proxies of VP8/VP9 alpha webm
body:
## What

A transparent webm, such as the output of `hyperframes remove-background`, lost its transparency in the Studio preview proxy. `hyperframes check`, Studio and publish all made an opaque H.264 copy of it.

## Why

There were two bugs on the same path.

1. **Wrong variant.** VP8/VP9 keep their alpha in a side channel, so ffprobe reports `pix_fmt=yuv420p` plus an `ALPHA_MODE=1` stream tag. Studio-server decided "has alpha" from `pix_fmt` alone, and it never asked ffprobe for the tag. `proxyVariantFor` therefore picked `h264`. The engine already read the tag; the two copies of the rule had drifted (the studio-server regex also missed `ayuv*`).
2. **Wrong decoder.** Even on the `vp8` variant, the transcode read the source with ffmpeg's native VP9 decoder, which drops the side channel. `format=yuva420p` then filled in a fully opaque alpha plane.

## Change

- New `@hyperframes/parsers/media-alpha` is the one owner of `pixelFormatHasAlpha`, `videoStreamHasAlpha` (pix_fmt or a case-insensitive `alpha_mode=1` tag) and `alphaDecoderFor` (`libvpx-vp9` / `libvpx`).
- Studio-server's probe now requests `stream_tags=alpha_mode`, sets `MediaMetadata.hasAlpha`, and the codec map uses it. Its own pix_fmt regex is deleted.
- The proxy transcode passes `-c:v libvpx-vp9|libvpx` before `-i` only when it builds the `vp8` (alpha) variant of a VP8/VP9 source.
- The engine imports the shared rule. Its regex copy is deleted, and `decoderForCodec` delegates to the shared decoder choice. Engine behavior is unchanged.

Opaque media is untouched. Its probe answer, variant, ffmpeg args and cache key are all the same as before. No proxy cache version bump is needed: before this change, no VP8/VP9 source could reach the `vp8` variant, so no stale alpha proxies exist.

## Evidence

The same project and the same half-transparent VP9 clip (`libvpx-vp9`, `yuva420p`, `alpha_mode=1`, mean alpha 127.5), run through `hyperframes check` with ffmpeg 8.1.1:

| | `.transcode-cache` entry | decoded mean alpha |
|---|---|---|
| main | `h264 / yuv420p` (.mp4) | none (opaque) |
| this branch | `vp8 / yuv420p / alpha_mode=1` (.webm) | 127.5 |

## Tests

- `parsers/src/mediaAlpha.test.ts`: the merged pix_fmt lists from both old tests, the tag in both casings, and the decoder choice.
- `studio-server/src/helpers/mediaCodecMap.test.ts`: ffprobe output for a real VP9 alpha encode now gives `hasAlpha` and the `vp8` variant.
- `studio-server/src/helpers/proxyTranscoder.test.ts`: the spawn args put `-c:v libvpx-vp9` before `-i` for `vp8` and leave `h264` alone. An end-to-end test with real ffmpeg covers probe, variant and transcode, and checks that the proxy's mean alpha stays at about 127.5. It is skipped when ffmpeg lacks libvpx.
- Mutation check: removing the tag read fails the codec-map and end-to-end tests. Removing the decoder arg fails the spawn-args and end-to-end tests.

## Package size

`@hyperframes/parsers` was already at its packed budget on main (190591 B). The new `media-alpha` subpath adds 676 B of JS and 803 B of declarations, which brings the packed size to 190958 B in CI. The budget moves to 191000 B. Nothing else in the tarball changed.

title: perf(aws-lambda): render each chunk with as many capture browsers as the function can host
body:
## What

Lambda chunk renders now run as many capture browsers as the function can host. At the default 10 GB function that is five instead of three. Other runtimes (Cloud Run, local distributed renders) and the shared worker sizing are unchanged.

## Why

On a heavy 4K chunk, capture dominates the chunk's time, and the function's CPUs sit mostly idle during it: each capture browser works through a frame as a chain of steps across its threads, so one browser uses well under one core. The shared sizing gives a 10 GB function three browsers, bound by its memory rule (a per-browser budget sized for desktop renders) and its CPU reserve. Measured on Lambda, a capture browser peaks at well under the memory that rule assumes, so the function can host more. More browsers per chunk shorten each chunk and cut the compute a render is billed for, with byte-identical output.

## How

- **A budget the runtime passes in.** `RenderChunkOptions.maxCaptureWorkers` is the number of capture browsers the runtime can host. `renderChunk` raises the shared sizing up to it, one browser per 20 frames so each browser's start-up stays a small share of its work, and never lowers it: a small chunk or a small runtime keeps today's count.
- **The Lambda handler owns its budget.** It reads the function's memory (`AWS_LAMBDA_FUNCTION_MEMORY_SIZE`), allows one browser per 2 GB (about twice a 4K capture browser's peak), and leaves one core for Node and ffmpeg. Outside Lambda the budget is unset and nothing changes. `ChunkRenderer` takes the same optional options argument `renderChunk` already accepts.
- **Visible in the logs.** Each chunk logs `{ event: "chunk_capture", chunkIndex, workers, captureMode }`, so a deployment shows how many browsers its chunks used.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `renderChunk.test.ts`: `resolveChunkCaptureWorkers` keeps the shared sizing with no budget, raises a chunk to the budget, gives each browser at least 20 frames, and never lowers the shared sizing.
  - `handler.test.ts`: without the Lambda memory variable a chunk gets no budget; with a 10 GB function it gets five (fewer on a host with fewer cores); each chunk logs its capture browsers.
  - Each new test passed 3 runs in a row and was shown to fail with its code path disabled (sizing ignoring the budget, handler not passing it, log line missing).
- [x] Manual testing performed

title: pr-to-video: fetch-pr.mjs fails outside a git repo, and `owner/repo#N` is parsed as a branch name
body:
### What happened

`skills/pr-to-video/scripts/fetch-pr.mjs` fails in two ways when the project directory it is told to work in is not a git repository — which is exactly the state the workflow leaves it in: Step 0 runs `hyperframes init` into a fresh cache dir (e.g. `~/.cache/hyperframes/pr-to-video/<owner>/<repo>/<repo>-pr-<n>`), and Step 1 then runs `fetch-pr.mjs` with that directory as cwd.

**1. No repo context → gh subcommand dies**

```
$ cd <fresh hyperframes project dir>            # not a git repo
$ node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/fetch-pr.mjs --pr "owner/repo#4584" --out-dir ./capture
failed to run git: fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git
✗ fetch-pr.mjs: gh pr view "owner/repo#4584" failed (auth / not found / private?)
```

**2. After adding repo context, the documented `owner/repo#N` ref is parsed as a branch name**

```
$ git init -q && git remote add origin https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>.git
$ node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/fetch-pr.mjs --pr "owner/repo#4584" --out-dir ./capture
no pull requests found for branch "owner/repo#4584"
✗ fetch-pr.mjs: gh pr view "owner/repo#4584" failed
```

Only a **bare number** works once the project dir has an `origin` pointing at the PR's repo:

```
$ node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/fetch-pr.mjs --pr "4584" --out-dir ./capture
✓ fetch-pr: <owner>/<repo> PR #4584 — "…"
```

### Why

`gh pr view <ref>` resolves both the repository *and* the argument against the local git context. The documented `--pr` forms (`<url | owner/repo#N | N>`) are only partially handled: the `owner/repo#N` string is forwarded verbatim as ghost's PR *selector*, so when a repo context does exist gh interprets it as a branch (`<owner>/<repo>#<n>` is not a valid PR selector for `gh pr view`).

### Expected

`--pr "owner/repo#4584"` should work from **any** directory, including a non-git HyperFrames project dir.

### Suggested fix

Parse the ref and pass the two halves separately, always pinning the repo explicitly (no reliance on cwd):

```js
// owner/repo#N  →  gh pr view N --repo owner/repo
// full URL      →  same, parsed
// bare N        →  gh pr view N  (requires a repo context, or a --repo flag)
const args = ["pr", "view", String(number), "--repo", `${owner}/${repo}`, "--json", FIELDS];
```

`gh pr view N --repo OWNER/REPO` works outside any git repository, and the follow-up `gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/pulls/N/files` is already repo-qualified, so pinning the repo fixes both failure modes. Alternatively, tell the user in the skill docs that the project dir must have an `origin` and that `--pr` takes a bare number — but that silently breaks the documented `owner/repo#N` form.

### Repro environment

- hyperframes CLI `0.8.183`, pr-to-video skill from `main` (2026-10-21)
- macOS 15 (Intel), `gh` 2.x authenticated
- PR used: `DataLinkDC/dinky#4584` (public). Same behaviour on any public PR.

title: pr-to-video: assemble-index.mjs hardcodes the jsDelivr CDN for GSAP (breaks offline / restricted-network renders)
body:
### What happened

`skills/pr-to-video/scripts/assemble-index.mjs` (line ~587) writes the assembled `index.html` with a **hardcoded jsDelivr CDN** GSAP tag:

```html
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js"
        integrity="sha384-sG0Hv1tP1lZCk9KQmrIbY/XNwi+OY84GQqhMscbnsoBFqAz8KNCil1kvfL3Hbbk2"
        crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

Every frame's composition registers its paused timeline on `window.__timelines[...]`, so if that script never loads, **no frame animates** and the render is either static or fails with no obvious pointer to the cause. In networks where `cdn.jsdelivr.net` is unreachable (mainland China routinely: the host resets the connection in <300 ms), the whole pipeline gets through Step 5 — frames built, `check` green, snapshots look fine — and only the final `render` comes out wrong. By then the failure looks like a frame bug, not a CDN bug.

Note the same project already stages **fonts** locally (`assets/fonts/*.woff2`, written by `build-frame.mjs` and referenced relatively from frame CSS), so the machinery for a self-contained project exists — GSAP is the outlier.

### Repro

```
$ cd <project>
$ node <SKILL_DIR>/scripts/assemble-index.mjs --storyboard ./STORYBOARD.md --hyperframes .
$ grep -n jsdelivr index.html
587:    <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@3.14.2/dist/gsap.min.js" …></script>
$ npx hyperframes render            # frames render, but no motion / or fails
```

Confirmed on hyperframes CLI `0.8.183`, macOS, with `cdn.jsdelivr.net` blocked at the network level. Manually vendoring the file and rewriting that one line (`./vendor/gsap.min.js`) makes the same project render correctly.

### Suggested fix

Stage GSAP the way fonts are already staged, and reference it relatively:

- `assemble-index.mjs` copies `gsap.min.js` into `assets/vendor/gsap.min.js` (from a bundled copy, or `node_modules/gsap/dist/gsap.min.js` when present) and emits `<script src="./assets/vendor/gsap.min.js"></script>`.
- Keep the CDN tag as an explicit opt-in (e.g. `--gsap=cdn`, default `local`), so hosted/Studio flows can still prefer the CDN.

Failing that, at minimum: detect at assembly time that the CDN is unreachable and print a warning pointing at the vendoring step, so the failure doesn't surface 3 minutes later as a silent static render.

### Impact

Any user on a network without jsDelivr access loses the whole pr-to-video (and product-launch-video, same engine) render path with no actionable error. Also blocks fully-offline use, which the local CLI otherwise supports end to end (local fonts, local capture, local encode).

title: perf(producer): cloud render chunks start their capture browsers while video frames extract
body:
## What

A cloud render chunk (Lambda, Cloud Run) now starts its capture browsers while it is still extracting its video frames, instead of after. Output is unchanged.

## Why

A chunk's fixed work runs one step after another: boot the preflight browser and measure each video's drawn size, extract the video frames, then start the capture browsers, then capture. Starting the capture browsers takes a few seconds and does not depend on the extracted frames, so it can run alongside the extraction. Every chunk of every render with video saves that time, and so does the compute a render is billed for.

## How

- **Extraction starts, capture starts.** `renderChunk` begins the deferred video extraction and goes straight into the capture stage instead of waiting for it. The frame lookup becomes a promise.
- **A session waits on its first frame.** `createChunkVideoFrameInjectorFactory` also takes a lookup that is still being built: each session's injector awaits it on its first injection, then behaves exactly as before (one stateful injector per session). The existing synchronous callers are unchanged.
- **Failures keep their cause.** If capture fails while extraction failed too, the chunk throws the extraction's own error (a `VideoSourceExtractionError`, for example), not the capture stage's wrapper, so callers and Step Functions routing see the same error as before. Extraction is always settled before the chunk's work directories are cleaned up, so no ffmpeg keeps writing into a removed directory.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `renderChunkFallback.test.ts`: an injector built from a lookup still being extracted holds its first injection until the lookup settles, and surfaces the extraction's failure; each session gets its own injector.
  - `renderChunk.test.ts`: a chunk whose video is read by URL from an unreachable host fails with `VideoSourceExtractionError` while its capture browsers start (without the rethrow it surfaced as a capture-stage error).
  - The existing chunk tests (deferred video by file and by URL renders the same chunk, shown-size measurement, frame ranges) pass unchanged.
  - Each new test passed 3 runs in a row and was shown to fail with its code path disabled (factory not waiting, no rethrow).
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Heavy 4K fixture (full-screen screen recording plus camera bubble) on Lambda, this branch against main on the same base, two cold runs each: output byte-identical (same video and audio stream checksums), each chunk finished sooner and compute billed per render went down in both runs.

title: fix(core): exported scenes keep their frames when later scenes are added
body:
## What

Exporting a scene gives the same frames no matter how many scenes come after it. Before, adding a scene to a long project could change the export of untouched scenes: single frames from the wrong moment (a visible flash), one-frame shifts, and animations drawn at the wrong phase.

## Why

The runtime keeps scene timelines paused at rest and unpauses them only across a root seek. GSAP counts only unpaused children in a timeline's length, and `play()` on a child does not re-measure the parent. When a scene after the playhead first renders during a seek (for example an `overwrite: "auto"` tween), it marks the root's length stale; the next length read happens while the scenes rest paused, so the root caches a length of 0. Every later root seek is then clamped to 0, so each scene is drawn once at its local time 0 before its own redraw. Stateful scenes keep that wrong state, which is the flash.

## How

`activateSiblingTimelines` in `packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts` now re-measures the root right after it unpauses the scenes (`shiftChildren(0)` marks the length dirty, `totalDuration()` recomputes it with the scenes counted). It is the one place a render seek arms the scenes, so every capture path that drives `window.__hf.seek` (local render, chunked/distributed render, HDR compositing) gets it. It runs once per seek and only when there are scenes to arm.

## Test plan

- [x] `packages/core/src/runtime/init.rootLength.test.ts`: three back-to-back scenes, one with an overwriting tween; renders frames 210 to 214 and checks the second scene is drawn only at its own times. Red without the fix, and red with only the `shiftChildren` line removed. Green 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Long real project (575 s, 24 fps), captured through the engine like a render: the frame that flashed (frame 10283) is dark on the old runtime bundle and matches its neighbours with the fix; frames 10281 to 10285 checked.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(engine): keep beginframe when a passed probe's page close is slow
body:
## What

A browser whose BeginFrame probe passed now stays in BeginFrame mode even when closing the probe page is slow. Before, a slow close turned a passing probe into a fallback to screenshot mode.

## Why

The probe checks that `HeadlessExperimental.beginFrame` returns a real PNG frame, then closes its page with a short timeout. When the machine is busy (several capture browsers starting while ffmpeg extracts video frames, as on a cloud render chunk), that close can take longer than the timeout even though the frame came back fine. The probe then reported "unsupported", that one browser fell back to screenshot mode, and a distributed chunk whose other browsers used BeginFrame failed its "all workers use one capture mode" check and had to be retried.

A slow page close says nothing about whether BeginFrame works. If a browser really is broken, the capture itself fails and the existing screenshot retry handles it.

## How

`probeBeginFrameSupport` keeps the probe's own result when page cleanup times out and only appends "probe page cleanup timed out" to the detail. A probe that failed stays failed.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
  - `browserManager.test.ts`: a probe whose PNG frame succeeds but whose page close never settles stays supported, with the cleanup note in its detail. Passed 3 runs in a row; fails with the old rule restored.
- [x] Manual testing performed
  - Seen on a heavy 4K cloud render: one chunk failed with mixed capture modes after a passing probe whose page close timed out; that is the case the test reproduces.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable.

title: fix(producer): a render whose audio peak stalls under correction no longer fails
body:
## What

A render no longer fails at assemble with "AAC true peak remained above -1 dBFS after 3 correction passes" when the encoded peak stops falling as the correction lowers the audio. Each correction pass now aims twice as far below the -1 dBTP ceiling as the one before (0.5, then 1, then 2 dB).

## Why

The correction assumed every dB of attenuation lowers the AAC peak by a dB. A production render on FFmpeg 8.1 measured:

| pass | attenuation | AAC true peak |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 dB | +1.9 dBFS |
| 1 | -3.4 dB | -0.5 dBFS |
| 2 | -4.4 dB | -0.6 dBFS |
| 3 | -5.3 dB | -0.6 dBFS |

Two dB more attenuation moved the peak 0.1 dB, so all three passes landed just above the ceiling and the render failed. Measured on Linux with FFmpeg 8.1.3 and 7.0.2 over the same mixes: 8.1's native AAC encoder overshoots its source more than 7.0.2 does (+2.0 vs +0.9 dB on one mix, -0.4 vs -1.6 dBFS on another; both meters agree with an independent 4x-oversampled numpy peak), and its peak is a noisy function of gain, with flat and reversed half-dB steps (for example -3.9 dBFS at both -3 and -3.5 dB, -5.0 at -4.5 dB but -4.7 at -5 dB).

The source's 96 kHz sample rate is not involved: every source is resampled to 48 kHz when it is extracted, before the mix.

## Related work

This is under the 100-line floor on purpose: it is a lone urgent fix for renders that fail at the last step, and nothing else open touches this loop.


Refs #3644 (the -1 dBTP guarantee and its three-pass bound), #5956 (encodes open in silence, which removes one source of growth between passes).

## How

`enforceAacTruePeak` in `audioPadTrim.ts` is the one place both the local render and the cloud plan correct the peak. Its step changes from `ceiling - 0.5 - measured` to `ceiling - 0.5 * 2^pass - measured`. The first pass is unchanged, so a render that converged in one correction gets the same bytes. Running out of passes still fails the render, as #3644 decided; this only gives the later passes room to get past a stall.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. New: "gets under the ceiling when the AAC peak stalls as attenuation grows" replays the production render's measured peaks (then 1 dB per dB beyond them). On `main` it fails the same way production did; here it converges at -7.3 dB. The two tests that pin the step arithmetic are updated. `audioPadTrim.test.ts` 38/38, three runs in a row. `assembleStage` and `audioTruePeak.fakeFfmpeg` (27), `distributed/plan` (63) and `distributed/assemble` (18) pass unchanged.
- [x] Manual testing performed. The integration test "keeps the delivered AAC below its true-peak ceiling" passes with FFmpeg 7.0.2 and 8.1.3. A 20 s composition (a 96 kHz 24-bit stereo WAV at 0.5 plus 46 short mp3 effects at 0.25 to 0.5) rendered from source with FFmpeg 8.1.3 needed a correction and delivered -1.5 dBTP. I could not recreate the production mix itself, so the regression replays its measurements rather than its audio.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(engine): a muted video no longer plays at full volume in renders that skip the browser probe
body:
## What

A `<video data-has-audio="true" muted>` whose file has an audio stream is now silent in every render, as it already was in preview and in renders that run the browser probe. Before, a render that skipped the probe mixed its sound at full volume and ignored `data-volume`.

## Why

A report said a video's `data-volume` was ignored in the render while an `<audio>`'s volume applied. Reproduced on 0.8.181 and `main` with real renders (a 440 Hz tone in the video, 880 Hz in an `<audio>` at 0.19, each measured on its own band):

| variant | `data-volume` | video tone before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `muted` + `data-has-audio="true"`, no browser probe | 1.0 / 0.5 | -24.16 / -24.16 dB (full level both times) | -76.05 dB (silent) |
| same, browser probe runs | 0.5 | -76.05 dB (silent) | -76.05 dB |
| no `muted` | 0.72 | -27.07 dB | -27.02 dB |

The `<audio>` stays at -38.57 dB throughout.

Two parsers disagreed. The audio parser skips muted videos (`isAudibleVideoElement`), so no track carrying `data-volume` existed. The video parser set `hasAudio` from `data-has-audio` alone, so `appendAutoDetectedVideoAudio` saw a video with sound and no track and added one at a hard-coded volume of 1.0. Only the browser probe's `pruneMutedBrowserMedia` cleared it, and simple projects (known duration, explicit `data-start`) skip the probe.

A muted video is silent by the existing contract: the composition guide pairs sound with `data-has-audio="true"` and no `muted`, #1322 stopped mixing muted videos, and #1969 made render match preview.

Not reproduced: the report's markup shows no `muted`. Without `muted`, `data-volume` applied correctly in every variant tried (with and without `id`, Studio-style attributes, a `data-start` offset, inside a `data-composition-src` sub-composition, and src spellings with spaces, `./` and a query string), on both 0.8.181 and `main`. If that report is a different cause, it stays open.

## Related work

Refs #1322, #1969.

## How

`parseVideoElements` sets `hasAudio` to `data-has-audio === "true"` and `isAudibleVideoElement(el)`, the same check the audio parser and the probe already apply. The fallback and the distributed plan read that field, so neither re-adds a muted video's sound.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. `mutedParity.test.ts` runs the same markup through the static parsers and the auto-detect fallback, with and without the probe's prune: the muted video stays out of the mix and the unmuted one keeps its 0.5. On `main` the no-probe case fails and the probe case passes. 4/4, three runs in a row. Engine `videoFrameExtractor` and `audioMixer` (280), `extractVideosStage` (21), `audioStage` (9) and `renderMediaCollector` (19) pass unchanged; engine and producer typecheck clean.
- [x] Manual testing performed. Real renders from source, the table above.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: feat(cloud): 4K renders work for transparent MOV and WebM
body:
## What
`hyperframes cloud render --resolution 4k` now accepts `--format mov` and `--format webm`. The producer server stops rejecting an output resolution combined with an alpha format, and the docs drop the "4K supports MP4 only" note.

## Why
The refusal assumed the alpha capture path cannot supersample. It can: rendering a transparent composition at a larger output resolution, locally and through the distributed plan/chunk/assemble path, produces the target size with a real alpha channel. The two checks were rejecting renders that work.

## How
- CLI: `validateResolutionFormatCombo` and its call are removed.
- Producer server: the alpha-format clause of `validateOutputResolutionOverride` is removed; string and unknown-preset checks stay.
- Docs: `docs/deploy/cloud.mdx` and `docs/packages/cli.mdx` keep the 1.5x billing line only.
- MP4 renders are unchanged: neither removed check ever applied to them.

## What I measured
- New `renderChunk` test: a 320x180 transparent composition planned as MOV at the `landscape` preset renders a 1920x1080 chunk with alpha (transparent corner, opaque centre). It fails with deviceScaleFactor forced to 1 (wrong size) and with JPEG capture (alpha lost).
- Server test flipped to "accepts outputResolution with an alpha format"; restoring the old gate fails it.
- Producer 60 pass / 0 fail (server + renderChunk), CLI cloud render tests 11 pass; build and pre-commit hooks clean.
- A distributed 4K render of the repo's mov-prores fixture against the local 4K render: MOV colour PSNR 89 dB mean / 74 min, alpha 104 / 89; WebM colour 62 / 59, alpha 66 / 61.

## What I did NOT exercise
- No 4K MOV/WebM render on a deployed Lambda stack yet; the distributed comparison above ran the same plan/chunk/assemble code off Lambda.

title: fix(scripts): run entrypoints from URL-encoded checkout paths
body:
## What

Fix repository script entrypoints in checkout paths containing URL-encoded characters.

## Why

Seven repository scripts compare `import.meta.url` with a raw `file://${process.argv[1]}` string. Node URL-encodes the former but not the latter, so a checkout directory containing a space, `%`, or `#` can make the command silently skip its entrypoint and exit successfully without checking or generating anything.

## Related work

Related: #5543 decodes URL pathnames in other scripts and tests. This correction instead covers seven entrypoint guards and the SVG generator import; it does not duplicate that PR or close its scope. No separate issue is needed for this self-contained correction.

## How

- Compare filesystem paths with `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)` in those seven guards.
- Keep the SVG generator's esbuild import as a file URL too, so encoded directory names do not fail during module loading.
- Exercise the real script entrypoints in disposable checkouts with encoded path characters, including invalid-input diagnostics, local generated outputs, and import-only controls.

This does not change validation rules, generated content, package APIs, dependencies, or the Node version requirement. The fixtures never publish, contact GitHub, or write outside their temporary checkout.

## Test plan

Updated by merging current main `03ed14615a2988d65ed793f004bcc4446ec89324` into the existing branch. The single adjacent-import conflict retains both `fileURLToPath` and upstream `generatedPaths`; the complete upstream implementation and other upstream changes are included, not just the import.

- 233 relevant tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped on Linux / Node 24.19.0, including path regressions, comment checks, deletion guard, release-channel validation, generated SVG checks and sanitizer parity.
- The 11 existing generated-output/exemption cases also passed with checker scripts under a path containing spaces, `%` and `#`.
- All 7 original encoded-path execution regressions still fail against this exact current main and pass with the fix; import-only controls pass.
- oxlint and oxfmt passed on all 8 PR files. Citation and comment-ratchet diff gates and `git diff --check` passed.
- The public merge commit has the reviewed complete tree and both intended parents, and GitHub shows its signature as Verified.

Full workspace build/tests, the complete root `test:scripts` aggregate, browser/render lanes, Windows/macOS and Node 22 were not rerun for this reconciliation. The original patch's Node 22.0.0 run passed the new regressions but had three unchanged TODO-link failures involving `URL.parse`; that historical result is not a full-green or current-head Node 22 claim. Remote CI still requires its own execution and approval.

AI-assisted implementation, reconciliation and tests: OpenAI Codex. The account owner has not personally rerun these checks.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed (automated CLI regressions only)
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable: no public interface change)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md; scoped citation and comment-ratchet gates passed
