title: feat(cli): read a whole recording as voice, effect and music lines
body:
## What

`hyperframes audio <file> --read` reads one whole recording — an episode, a reference video — as time-stamped lines an agent can read or grep, instead of measurements of one sound:

```
thailand.mp4 · 574.4 s · stems: bass, drums, guitar, other, piano, vocals
voice: 51 lines, 1 pauses, mean 5.1 chars/s, median pitch 190 Hz
effects: 320 in 70 sounds (S1 thump ×39, S2 thump ×32, S3 whoosh ×28, …)
music: 21 pieces, 38 breaks

22.7–34.0   voice   "1997年那场…"  5.2 chars/s (mean 5.1)  rising end
4.3         effect  riser (S24): high, attack 1620 ms, tail 0.8 s, +8 dB over music
31.7        effect  thump (S1): low, attack 70 ms, tail 0.1 s, while the music is out
39.9–59.8   music   piece 2 (bass · 100 BPM), first appearance after a break, fades from 58.3
30.9–32.1   music   break 1.2 s
```

- **voice**: sentences from a transcript (`--transcript`, or `<file>.transcript.json` beside it) with speaking rate, pitch when it is 3+ semitones off the median, and a rising or falling end; pauses of 0.4 s or more.
- **effects**: onsets in the drums stem, named by rule (riser, boom, thump, whoosh, click, tick, ding, hit), grouped by identical sound (`S1` most used), quick runs folded into one line. Hits on the music's beat and sounds more than 20 dB under the recording are left out.
- **music**: the four other non-voice stems, split at real cut-outs (each checked against the 2 s around it), with pieces matched by chroma, stem mix and tempo — `resumes` after a short break, `returns` later, or `new`.

`--range a,b` picks what is shown; the whole recording's text is cached under `.hyperframes/read-audio` per file content, with its stems.

## Stems

The default is `--quality local`, which never uploads; at `--quality best` the recording is uploaded through the asset direct-upload routes and separated by HeyGen's `/v3/audio/stems` with the CLI's HeyGen credential (`HEYGEN_API_KEY`, `HYPERFRAMES_API_KEY`, `HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN` or a saved `hyperframes auth login` credential; `HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_STEMS_URL` + `HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_API_KEY` point at another service instead, and the HeyGen credential is never sent there) (`POST` waits for the stems; in-progress or dropped requests retry the same body and idempotency key; contract in `packages/cli/src/audio/read/stems.ts`). The backend half of that route is a separate change. The `api` analysis provider now finds its credential the same way, on `/v3/audio/analysis`. Without stems, effects are read from the mix outside speech and the music is not read; with neither stems nor a transcript, voice and effects are not read at all, because the mix alone does not tell speech from music. Every case says so in a warning.

`analysis/providers/shared.ts` gains `serviceAccess` and `serviceFailure`, now shared by the analysis API provider and the stems client.

The configured separation deadline aborts encoding, upload, job requests, retry waits and downloads. Stem files use fixed names for the six documented stems and the existing atomic streaming downloader. An explicitly empty service URL disables that service. Fractional sample hops stay aligned over long recordings; cached read analyses are versioned so older timestamps are recomputed.

Incomplete responses are not cached as complete: all six documented stems must be present. Missing stems produce a fallback warning, and an incomplete cached manifest causes a later `--quality best` read to retry.

## Verification

- Followthrough baseline validation: 103 tests pass across 14 audio, upload and download test files. Includes a signal at 600 seconds, stalled upload/POST cancellation, and ignoring unknown stem names. Synthetic signals and local mock servers only; no live service calls.
- After the partial-stems repair and author protocol integration: all 6 readAudio integration tests pass, including partial-response retry and incomplete cached-manifest recovery.
- CLI typecheck, pre-commit core/studio/scripts typechecks, oxlint, oxfmt, comment checks and fallow pass using existing dependencies. Fresh GitHub CI and Docs validation pending; local Mintlify CLI was unavailable.
- The inherited support-test release-age parsing failure is repaired with the focused fix from #6058 (f9c6ba357), tested here with a mocked installer; no local install executed.
- Author-reported experiment, not rerun during followthrough: a 574 s Chinese episode with six local `htdemucs_6s` stems and a Whisper transcript took 9.4 s and about 1 GB RSS. The author checked reported breaks against per-stem levels. That episode is not in the repository.

title: fix(core): a clip's volume lane stays smooth in preview while the page is busy
body:
## What

A clip with a volume automation lane now plays its lane on a gain node of its own in preview, so the per-tick volume write can no longer step it. Preview of such a clip stays smooth while the page is busy.

## Why

In preview, a clip with a `data-automation` volume lane had two writers on one `GainNode`:

1. `WebAudioTransport` scheduled the lane as ramps on the clip's `gainNode` when the clip started.
2. `syncRuntimeMedia` sampled the same lane every tick and sent it through `setElementVolume`, which wrote `gainNode.gain.value`, about 60 times a second.

Setting `.value` on a param with scheduled ramps inserts a step at the context's current time. Each step carries the lane value from whenever the main thread ran the tick, so on a busy page (videos decoding, heavy UI) the gain jumps and the clip sounds choppy. The more the main thread lags, the larger the steps.

Repro, headless Chrome on Linux, synthetic 1 kHz tone through highpass, gain, compressor and true-peak limiter with a 0 → 1 → 0 volume lane over 6 s, 48 kHz context, main thread blocked 30-60 ms every 100 ms:

| | sample discontinuities per 6 s, not counting the clip's own end | ramp ripple (deviation from a straight ramp) |
|---|---|---|
| before | 2 to 14 (6 runs) | up to 2.3% |
| after | 0 in every run | 0.021% to 0.023% |

The same clip without a lane measures the same before and after. On an idle page, before and after are both smooth (the steps are small when ticks are on time), but before still writes ~360 times per 6 s onto the scheduled param; after, none.

## Related work

Refs the earlier change that fed the lane through the per-tick path so a scheduled envelope was not erased by the per-tick `data-volume` write (comment in `media.test.ts`, "volume automation lane"). That fix stays for clips that sound through `el.volume`; this PR gives routed clips the scheduled lane without a second writer.

## How

Invariant: **one writer per gain param.** A clip's volume lane owns a gain node of its own; the per-tick volume of a routed clip never folds the lane in. This mirrors the group bus in the same file, where the lane rides `fader` and per-tick and hidden state ride `muteGain`.

- `webAudioTransport.ts`: every routed clip, decoded or media-element, gets a lane gain of its own between its FX and its `gainNode` (`attachClipStages`), disconnected at every teardown. It is unity while the clip has no lane.
- `audioFx.ts`: the clip's FX handle books that lane gain alongside the clip's other envelopes. The lane is re-aimed on `setRate` and `reanchor`, re-booked when `data-automation` changes, cleared when the lane is removed, and booked when a lane is added mid-play. The group fader rides the same handle, so a group's lane follows rate changes and edits too.
- `media.ts`: while the transport routes the element, the per-tick volume no longer folds the lane in (it carries only what multiplies the lane, the clip fades). A routed element always has a lane gain the handle books, so routing and lane ownership are the same condition. Unrouted clips keep driving `el.volume` from the lane as before.
- `audioAutomationVolume.ts`: doc comment updated; it said a volume lane is never scheduled on a gain.

- `scripts/package-size-budgets.json`: core's unpacked budget goes from 3935667 to 3936240 bytes (+573). The budget sits at main's exact size; the lane gain, its teardown and the handle booking it are what this fix adds to the runtime bundles.

Render is unchanged: it already bakes lane × fades into the samples.

## Test plan

- [x] Lane follows the transport mid-play (`webAudioTransport.test.ts`, "volume lanes follow the transport mid-play"): rate change, `data-automation` edit, lane removal, lane added mid-play, and the group fader's rate change and edit. All 5 fail on the previous head and pass now; transport, media, FX and idle suites 300/300, 3 runs in a row; 24 neighbouring suites 467/467.
- [x] Unit tests added: `webAudioTransport.test.ts` (decoded and media-element routes keep the lane's gain untouched by `setElementVolume`) and `media.test.ts` (a routed clip's per-tick volume excludes the lane). All 3 fail on main (`expected 0.5 to be 1`; lane value re-sent) and pass with the fix; both files 242/242, 3 runs in a row.
- [x] Neighbouring audio suites: 26 files, 520 tests pass; core `tsc --noEmit` clean; `oxfmt --check` and `oxlint` clean.
- [x] Manual: real-browser A/B of the built runtime with a synthetic tone, recorded on the audio thread (numbers above).
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): n/a
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(cli): keep whisper CJK tokens as separate timed words
body:
## What

`hyperframes transcribe <9.5-min Mandarin mp4> --engine whisper --model small --language zh --json` reported `wordCount: 2`: `transcript.json` held two entries of ~280 s each, covering the whole speech. Captions and `audio --read` (which builds sentences from the transcript) had nothing to split.

## Why

`parseWhisperCpp` merges any token without a leading space into the previous word, since whisper.cpp marks word boundaries with one. Chinese and Japanese tokens never carry a leading space, not even at the start of a segment, so the whole transcript collapsed across segments. The whisper-cli args and the token loop in `transcribe.ts` are fine (the reported `wordCount` comes from `loadTranscript`).

## Change

- A token that crosses a CJK boundary starts its own word, so `用` + `AI` + `剪` stay separate; full-width punctuation (`，。！？、` …) still attaches to the word before it.
- Cues also end at `。！？`, not only `.!?`.
- The merge decision moves into `continuesWord` to keep `parseWhisperCpp` under the fallow gate.

Thai/Lao/Khmer are unchanged: their tokens are sub-word fragments, and `joinTokens` would re-space them.

## CI repair

The inherited support-CI failure parsed the version range as the package name in Bun’s minimum-release-age error. Capture the package name so the existing scoped exclusion and retry work as intended.

## Author verification

- Synthetic Mandarin speech (macOS `say -v Tingting`, no customer footage) through real `whisper-cli` + `ggml-small`, then `loadTranscript`: 1 word before → 48 per-token timed words after; a rare-character sentence gives 30.
- New `whisper-cpp CJK tokens` tests in `normalize.test.ts` use a synthetic whisper JSON fixture; all 3 fail on `main` and pass here (79/79 in the file).
- `src/whisper` + `commands/transcribe.test.ts`: 283 pass; 4 failures in `sherpa.test.ts` / `manager.install.test.ts` fail identically on unmodified `main` on this machine (a real runtime is installed).
- tsc, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow pass.

Not covered: live progress words (`segmentWords` in `transcribe.ts`) still split on whitespace, so a CJK segment shows as one interim word until the final transcript replaces it.


## Followthrough verification

- Independently ran `normalize.test.ts`: 79/79 pass using existing dependencies/generated artifacts.
- Verified `installConsumer` with a mocked child process: writes `fake-dep`, not `^1.1.0`, to the exclusion list and retries. No real package install was run locally.
- Repair lint, format, and commit hooks pass. Fresh CI validates the real install fixture.

title: fix(ci): packed consumer installs keep same-day dependency bumps on every Bun release
body:
## What

Packed consumer installs keep same-day dependency bumps working on every Bun release, and CI stops picking up a new Bun mid-day.

## Why

`installConsumer` retries an install that Bun refused under `--minimum-release-age`, excluding the refused packages. It read the package name as the first quoted token of Bun's error. Bun 1.4.4 (released 2026-10-22) swapped the two tokens:

- 1.4.3: `No version matching "fake-dep" found for specifier "^1.1.0" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds)`
- 1.4.4: `No version matching "^1.1.0" found for specifier "fake-dep" (blocked by minimum-release-age: 86400 seconds)`

On 1.4.4 the retry excluded `^1.1.0`, stayed blocked, and failed. `verify-packed-manifests.test.mjs` "installs a same-day dependency bump whose only matching version is an hour old" went red ("allowed: ^1.1.0"), so every PR's `Test (support)` fails from the first run that downloaded 1.4.4. A release's packed consumer install of any same-day dependency bump would fail the same way.

CI picked up 1.4.4 without a change in this repo because no `setup-bun` step pins a version, and with none given the action installs the latest release.

## Related work

Supersedes the one-line flip in #6058, which made the release-age regex capture the second quoted token. That fits Bun 1.4.4's message order only, breaks on the other order, and leaves Bun unpinned. This PR pairs the tokens structurally (`ageBlockedPackages`), so either order works, and pins Bun with `engines.bun`. Rebased onto main with the conflict resolved in favour of `ageBlockedPackages`.

## How

- `scripts/verify-packed-manifests.mjs`: `ageBlockedPackages(stderr)` reads both quoted tokens and takes as the package the one that Bun's `<name>@<range> failed to resolve` line pairs with the other. Both versions print that line (captured from 1.4.3 and 1.4.4 against the test's fake registry). If no such line pairs the tokens, it returns `null` and the original install error is rethrown, so an unknown future format fails visibly instead of excluding the wrong name.
- `package.json`: `"engines": { "bun": "1.4.4" }`. With no `bun-version` input, `oven-sh/setup-bun` at the pinned commit `0c5077e5` reads the root `package.json` (`src/index.ts:27-29`, `packageManager` `bun@X` or `engines.bun`, `src/utils.ts:124`), so this one field pins Bun for every `setup-bun` step that does not set a version. `packageManager: "bun@..."` would do the same for setup-bun but makes Corepack's pnpm refuse the repo, and CI and publish run `corepack enable` + `pnpm` from the root (`ci.yml:325-326`, `publish.yml:119-120`). `canary-sunset.yml` still asks for `latest` explicitly and is left as is.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `ageBlockedPackages` with both Bun message orders and a scoped name, plus two messages that must name nothing.
- [x] Red on main: with only the test file changed, the file fails to load (`does not provide an export named 'ageBlockedPackages'`); main's code under Bun 1.4.4 fails the same-day install test (`allowed: ^1.1.0`).
- [x] Green: `node --test scripts/verify-packed-manifests.test.mjs` 22/22, 3 runs each under Bun 1.4.4 and 1.4.3.
- [x] `bun install --frozen-lockfile` with the new `engines` field; `corepack pnpm@10.17.1 --version` from the repo root still runs; `check:workspace-contracts`, `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` clean.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): n/a
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"


## Size

Under 100 lines on purpose: it unblocks `Test (support)` on main for every open PR, so it ships alone rather than riding a larger change.

title: fix(cli): a check that runs out of time says which step it was in and how long each took
body:
## What

When `hyperframes check` runs out of time, its error now says which step it was in and how long each step took:

```
✗ check_runtime_failure: Check did not finish within its deadline (120 s from when Chrome was ready), while checking samples. Seconds per phase: making video copies 0.1 (before the deadline), starting Chrome 0.1 (before the deadline), loading the page 0.2, waiting for the page to be ready 2.0, checking samples 117.8.
```

Before, the whole message was `Check did not finish within its deadline.` This PR does not change how long check may run or what it checks.

## Why

On a user's Windows machine, an 8-minute talking-head project (15 videos, 33 sub-compositions) failed `check` three times in a row with `Check did not finish within its deadline`, also with `--timeout 60000`. The same project checked fine on 0.8.150, the last release before the 120 s deadline (#5537, first shipped in 0.8.153).

I could not reproduce it. Linux runs of a synthetic project of the same shape on 0.8.185 all pass:

| Synthetic 8-minute project, 15 videos, 33 sub-compositions | First run | Repeat run |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p, 3 of the 15 videos need copies | 52 s | 16 s |
| 1080p, all 15 HEVC | 145 s (110 s making copies) | 32 s |
| 4K, all 15 HEVC | 424 s (374 s making copies) | 43 s |
| 1080p, all 15 HEVC, plus 1,188 word-by-word caption spans | 56 s | 52 s |

The deadline starts when Chrome is ready, after the video copies are made, so copying time never counts against it. The user's repeat runs, with copies already made, also ran out of time. So on that machine the part of check after Chrome starts takes over 120 s, and the old message gave no way to tell which part. With this change the next report names it.

## Related work

Refs #5537 (added the deadline).
Related: #5558 lets the deadline honour `--timeout` and an env override. This PR leaves the length of the deadline alone and does not touch that change.

## How

- `CheckDeadline` already owns the check's clock. It now records the phase in progress (`enter(phase)`) and the time spent in each phase, and puts both in the error it raises when it expires.
- Each step marks its phase where it starts: `runBrowserCheck` (making copies, starting Chrome), `openSettledCompositionPage` through a new `onLoaded` hook between navigation and the render-ready wait, `runAuditGrid` (samples, overlap pass) and the finding crops.
- Copies and Chrome start are reported but labelled "before the deadline", so the counted phases add up to the 120 s.
- The message still begins with `Check did not finish within its deadline`, so anything matching that text keeps matching. The script-specific message (`<file>: its script did not finish within the check deadline`) gets the same detail.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `checkDeadline.test.ts`: walks a deadline through every phase on fake timers and asserts the exact message (6 passed, exit 0).
- `check.test.ts`: a pipeline run whose overlap pass never finishes; asserts the runtime finding says `while running the overlap pass` with the overlap pass at 120.0 s (121 passed, exit 0).
- Both files green 3 runs in a row. Also green: `checkBrowser.test.ts` (37), `checkDeadline.process.test.ts` (3), `captureCompositionFrame.browserFallback.test.ts` (8). `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/cli` exit 0; oxlint, oxfmt, fallow and the commit hooks pass.
- Mutations, each turning only the named test red:
  - drop the overlap-pass mark: the pipeline test fails;
  - stop counting the phase that is still open: both tests fail;
  - `start()` not entering "loading the page": the unit test fails.
- Built CLI, real runs:
  - the caption project: passes, exit 0, unchanged;
  - the same project with an `hf-seek` listener whose `waitUntil` never settles: exit 1 at 122 s with the message quoted under What. The counted phases sum to 120.0 s.

Not exercised: a deadline firing during the finding crops (`--snapshots`) in a real run, and any run on Windows.

title: fix(cli): history lists its entries even when this run cannot write the history
body:
## What

`hyperframes history` (the list, with or without `--json`, plus `show` and `peek`) now lists the project's recorded changes even when this run cannot write the history folder, for example on a full disk or an unwritable cache folder. It prints the history as last recorded, plus one line on stderr naming the cause:

```
[hyperframes] Could not write this project's history (EACCES: permission denied, open '<history>/<id>/project.json.hfb9fac4.tmp'); showing it as last recorded.
```

Commands that change the project through the history (`undo`, `restore`, `pin`, `begin`, `end`) still fail as before. Their job is the write.

## Why

Reading the history opens it as its owner. That writes the owner lock, the project record and copies of any changed files. If any of those writes failed, the read failed with it, and the user lost sight of every recorded change. Users on macOS hit this on 0.8.183:

- `ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '<history>/<id>/owner.pid-<pid>-<uuid>.tmp'` (full disk)
- `EPERM opening <history>/<project>/<file>.tmp` (cache folder it may not write), twice from one install

None of those writes is needed to read. `readProjectHistory` already reads the log without taking the lock or writing anything, and `withReader` already falls back to it when another process holds the history. This PR uses the same fallback when opening fails because a **write** failed (`ENOSPC`, `EDQUOT`, `EACCES`, `EPERM` or `EROFS` from a write). A read that fails while opening, such as a blobs folder it may not list or an owner file it may not read, still fails with its own error.

What the user gives up in that case: changes made since the last successful open are not filed into the history on this run. They couldn't be written anyway, and they get filed on the next open that can write.

## Related work

None.

## How

- One place: `withReader` in `packages/cli/src/utils/historyOwner.ts`, which every read-only history subcommand goes through.
- What counts as a write is decided by the failing call, not the error code alone: `mkdir`, `write`, `rename`, `unlink`, `link`, `copyfile` and the like, or a denied `open` of a file that is missing (creating it) or that this process can read (so the denial was for writing, for example appending to a read-only log). Node's error does not carry the open flags; the file's state answers which kind of open failed. Everything else propagates, including `scandir` and an `ENOSPC` from a file watcher.
- It falls back only if opening failed, never once the read has started, so a read never runs twice. A write error raised after the read began is still the command's own error.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

`history.test.ts`, seven new tests. They use real read-only folders, not mocks, and skip on Windows and as root, where permissions don't block the write:

| Test | On `main` | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| lists the history when its folder cannot be written, and says so | fails: `EACCES ... open '<root>/<id>/project.json.<x>.tmp'` | passes |
| lists the history when its log can be read but not appended to (`chmod 0444 log.jsonl`) | fails: `EACCES ... open '<root>/<id>/log.jsonl'` | passes |
| lists the history when only its stored file copies cannot be written | fails: `EACCES ... open '<root>/<id>/blobs/incoming-<uuid>'` | passes |
| a folder it cannot read (`chmod 0111` blobs) fails with `EACCES` from `scandir`, not "could not write" | passes (it has no fallback) | passes |
| an owner file it cannot read fails with `EACCES` from `open`, not "could not write" | passes (it has no fallback) | passes |
| never runs a read twice when a write error comes after it started | passes | passes |
| still fails an undo it cannot record, and leaves the files as they are | passes | passes |

title: build(aws-lambda): pinned native ffmpeg build for an arm64 Lambda image
body:
## What

A pinned, reproducible build of ffmpeg + ffprobe for an arm64 Lambda video function, under `packages/aws-lambda/image/`, plus a CI workflow that builds it natively on GitHub's ARM runners.

Nothing ships it yet: the image and the `lambda deploy` option that use it come in follow-up PRs. The default x86 ZIP deploy is untouched.

## Why

The x86 Lambda handler uses the `ffmpeg-static` binary. Its arm64 sibling is a static-glibc build that crashes on Lambda during decode, and the stock dynamic arm64 builds are too large for a ZIP function. An arm64 video function therefore ships as a container image, and that image needs an ffmpeg built against the glibc of the Lambda Node 22 base it runs on, with every codec the engine calls:

| Library | Engine caller |
|---|---|
| libx264 (r3191, the revision the x86 ffmpeg-static uses), libx265 with 8-bit and 10-bit | `engine/src/services/streamingEncoder.ts` (h264/h265 encode), `producer/src/services/distributed/plan.ts` (mp4 h265), `engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts` (HDR `yuv420p10le`) |
| libvpx (VP9 encode, VP9/VP8 alpha decode) | `engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts` (webm), `parsers/src/mediaAlpha.ts` `alphaDecoderFor` |
| libopus | `engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.ts` `muxVideoWithAudio` (webm audio) |
| libzimg (`zscale`) | `engine/src/services/videoFrameExtractor.ts` `toneMapsWithZscale` (assumed present on Linux), `core/src/hdrToneMap.ts` |
| libdav1d | AV1 source decode, same as the x86 ffmpeg-static build |
| zlib, GnuTLS | PNG frames; HTTPS inputs |

## How

- `sources.txt` pins every source by sha256 (x264 by git commit, since it has no stable tarballs).
- `Dockerfile` builds on the Lambda Node 22 image itself (pinned by digest), so the binaries link against the exact glibc they run on. Build packages come from the base's pinned Amazon Linux 2023 release.
- `build-ffmpeg.sh` links the codec libraries statically into a glibc-dynamic ffmpeg/ffprobe. Shared libraries the bare base lacks (GnuTLS, nettle) are copied beside the binaries and found through an `$ORIGIN` rpath, so the runtime image needs no package install. License files and the source pins go into `share/licenses/`. The tarball is packed deterministically (sorted, fixed mtime and owner, `gzip -n`).
- `check-ffmpeg.sh` runs in a `check` stage: the bare Lambda base plus only the built tree. It asserts the encoders, decoders, filters and protocols the engine uses. It also round-trips h264, h265, ProRes 4444, Opus, AAC and PNG; checks that VP9 alpha survives encode and libvpx decode; asserts a 10-bit HEVC encode really comes out `yuv420p10le` and runs the engine's HDR-to-SDR `zscale` chain on it; and checks HTTPS against the system trust store, where a trusted host passes and a wrong host name is refused. The `artifact` stage copies the check's summary, so no tarball can come out of a build whose check failed.
- `.github/workflows/lambda-ffmpeg.yml` builds on two separate `ubuntu-24.04-arm` runners and fails unless both tarballs are byte-identical. It runs on PRs that touch the recipe, and by hand.

## Test plan

- [x] The same recipe built and checked natively on x86_64 (Lambda Node 22 amd64 base): the check stage passed every assertion; the tarball is 29.6 MB, and only GnuTLS and nettle are bundled beside the binaries
- [x] x86_64 reproducibility: a second build with `--no-cache` produced a byte-identical tarball
- [x] The check is not vacuous: each of these makes the check stage fail, and the unmodified recipe passes: the test CA not trusted (TLS fails), alpha decoded with ffmpeg's native VP9 decoder instead of libvpx (alpha frames rejected), the bundled `libgnutls.so.30` removed (ffmpeg cannot load), the wrong-host probe pointed at the right host ("accepted a wrong host"), and an earlier 8-bit-only x265 build (ffprobe reports `yuv420p` for a `yuv420p10le` encode)
- [x] arm64: this PR's `Lambda arm64 ffmpeg` workflow (two native ARM builds, check stage, byte-identical comparison) passed at f43fc696; rerunning at this head
- [ ] Documentation updated (not yet: nothing user-facing ships in this PR)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Not exercised here: running these binaries inside Lambda itself. That is proven with the image and deploy PRs that use them.

title: feat(aws-lambda): push a prebuilt image to ECR without Docker
body:
## What

Adds two functions to `@hyperframes/aws-lambda/sdk`:

- `ensureEcrRepository({ ecr, repositoryName, tags? })` creates the ECR repository, or returns the existing one's URI when it already exists.
- `pushImageToEcr({ ecr, layoutDir, repositoryName, repositoryUri, tag, log? })` pushes a prebuilt single-platform OCI image layout (a directory) into that repository and returns `{ imageUri, digest, architecture, os }`, where `imageUri` is `<repositoryUri>@sha256:<manifest digest>`.

Adds the `@aws-sdk/client-ecr` dependency on the same `^3.1146.0` line as the other AWS SDK clients. No CLI wiring yet; callers come in a follow-up.

## Why

The arm64 video function will ship as a container image, and Lambda only runs images from the account's own private ECR. Users of the released CLI should not need Docker to get it there. The release will publish the image as an OCI layout; this function moves that layout into the user's ECR with the ECR API alone (no Docker, no registry HTTP calls).

## Related work

First piece of the container-image deploy path. Nothing else touches ECR yet.

## How

- `index.json` must list exactly one image manifest (OCI or Docker v2 schema 2). An image index, attestation manifests, or zero or several manifests throw an error naming what was found.
- Every blob (manifest, config, layers) is checked for size and streamed sha256 against its descriptor before any ECR call. A corrupt layout fails with nothing written.
- The image config must name `architecture` and `os`; both are returned so the caller can assert the platform it expects.
- `BatchCheckLayerAvailability` in batches of at most 100 digests; only blobs not `AVAILABLE` are uploaded: `InitiateLayerUpload`, parts of exactly `partSize` bytes read from disk one part at a time (inclusive `partFirstByte`/`partLastByte`), then `CompleteLayerUpload`. `LayerAlreadyExistsException` counts as uploaded.
- `PutImage` sends the manifest's exact bytes, its media type, the tag and the digest. `ImageAlreadyExistsException` counts as success, so a redeploy of the same image is a no-op.
- Uploads are sequential for now; bounded parallel layer uploads are the upgrade if push time on large layers matters.
- The Lambda handler bundle does not import the SDK subpath, so the new dependency stays out of the handler zip.
- `bun.lock`: besides the new entry, `bun install` refreshed the stale workspace version fields and dropped an unused `date-fns` entry.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `pushImageToEcr.test.ts` runs the real code path against an in-memory ECR that behaves like ECR where it matters. It tracks uploads per upload id, rejects out-of-order or non-contiguous parts, a wrong `partLastByte`, or a short non-final part, re-hashes the assembled bytes on `CompleteLayerUpload`, rejects `PutImage` when a referenced blob is missing, and caps availability checks at 100 digests. The fixture layout is built in a temp dir: one config, a 21-byte layer and a 17-byte layer, with a 7-byte part size.
  - `bun test src/sdk/pushImageToEcr.test.ts`: exit 0, 11 pass / 0 fail, three runs in a row.
  - `bun test src/handler.test.ts`: exit 0, 31 pass / 0 fail.
  - `tsc --noEmit` in `packages/aws-lambda`: exit 0. oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors. oxfmt `--check`: clean.
  - Each guarded behaviour was broken once to check that its test catches it (then reverted):
    - `partLastByte` off by one: the 5 tests that upload went red.
    - Skipping the pre-upload digest check: the tampered-blob test went red.
    - Raising the check batch size past 100: the batching test went red.
    - Rethrowing `LayerAlreadyExists`, `ImageAlreadyExists` or `RepositoryAlreadyExists`: in each case only the matching test went red.
    - Dropping the one-manifest check: the two-manifest test went red.
    - Dropping the architecture/os check: the config test went red.
    - Ignoring availability: the skip and redeploy tests went red.
- [ ] Manual testing performed. Not exercised: no call to a real ECR, and Lambda pulling the pushed image is proven in a later PR.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: feat(aws-lambda): arm64 video function image from the handler ZIP
body:
## What

The container image for an arm64 Lambda video function, and CI that builds it and runs it on a native ARM runner. Stacked on #6062, which adds the native ffmpeg build.

Nothing deploys this image yet: the release artifact and the `lambda deploy` option come next. The default x86 ZIP deploy is untouched.

## Why

Lambda arm64 needs native binaries for ffmpeg (#6062) and Chrome. Everything else in the handler ZIP is architecture-neutral JavaScript. Building the image from that same ZIP means the x86 and arm64 functions run identical handler code.

## How

- `scripts/stage-arm64-image.ts` unzips the handler ZIP into a staging `/var/task`. It replaces `bin/ffmpeg` and `bin/ffprobe` with the native tree from #6062's artifact (binaries, their two bundled libraries, licenses), then asserts both are 64-bit arm64 ELF.
  - The npm `@sparticuz/chromium` package ships x64 Chrome only. The script downloads Sparticuz's arm64 pack for the exact installed version, checks it against a sha256 pinned per version, and unpacks it over the package's `bin/`. `src/chromium.ts` calls `executablePath()` unchanged.
  - Bumping `@sparticuz/chromium` fails the staging until its arm64 pack is pinned. A handler ZIP built with `chrome-headless-shell` is refused.
- `image/Dockerfile` gains a `video` stage that only copies the staged directory onto the same pinned Lambda Node 22 base the ffmpeg was built on. One `ARG` owns that pin, and any host can build the stage without emulation.
- The workflow (renamed `lambda-arm64-image.yml`) keeps #6062's two ARM ffmpeg builds and byte-identical comparison. It adds two jobs:
  - one builds the handler ZIP the way the release does;
  - one stages and builds the image on an ARM runner, then:
    - runs the bundled ffmpeg and a real Chrome render inside it, launched with the same `executablePath()` and `args` as `src/chromium.ts`;
    - boots it under the Lambda runtime interface emulator and invokes the real handler, expecting its own "no recognised Action" error.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test scripts/stage-arm64-image.test.ts`: 5 pass, 0 fail, exit 0, three runs in a row
- [x] One mutation per behaviour, each failing only its own test: skip the arm64 ELF check, skip the pack sha256 check, skip the version-pin check, allow `chrome-headless-shell`, never swap Chrome
- [ ] This PR's `Lambda arm64 image` workflow (ARM ffmpeg x2 + match, handler ZIP, image smoke on ARM)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Not exercised here: the image running in Lambda itself. That is proven with the deploy PR.

title: feat(aws-lambda): run chunks on an optional arm64 image function
body:
## What

The SAM template (`examples/aws-lambda/template.yaml`, also the template `hyperframes lambda deploy` uses) gets an optional `VideoImageUri` parameter. When it is set, an arm64 container-image function, `<project>-video`, runs the plan and renders the chunks. The existing x86 ZIP function keeps audio and assemble.

Empty, the default, deploys exactly as before: one x86 function does everything. Nothing passes the parameter yet; the CLI option comes next (#6073).

## Why

Chunk rendering is the bulk of a render's compute and runs well on arm64. The plan must run there too: a chunk refuses a plan recorded with a different ffmpeg build (`renderChunk.ts`), so plan and chunks share one function. Audio and assemble stay on x86, so an MP4's audio, which the separate audio task encodes, is byte-identical to an x86-only deploy.

## How

- The video function lives in `examples/aws-lambda/video-function.yaml`, a nested stack (`VideoFunctionStack`) created only when `VideoImageUri` is set.
  - It is nested because `sam deploy` refuses a template with any top-level image function unless it is given an image repository, even when that function's `Condition` is false. Inline, it broke every deploy.
  - The child is plain CloudFormation, so callers need no extra capability: an `AWS::Lambda::Function` (`PackageType: Image`, arm64) and its role.
  - It gets the render function's memory, timeout, ephemeral storage, tracing, tags, environment and S3 access. It also gets `lambda:GetAccountSettings`, which the plan calls to size the render.
- Both plan tasks and both `RenderChunk` tasks (plan v1 and v2) invoke `!If [HasVideoFunction, <video function>, RenderFunction]`. Every other task is unchanged, and the state machine role may invoke both functions.
- `Runtime` and `Architectures` move from `Globals` onto the ZIP function.
- Reserved concurrency follows the chunks: with a video function, the reservation sits on it and the render function is unreserved. The plan still reads the value from its own environment to size the render.
- The chunk-invocation alarm watches whichever function renders the chunks. The video function gets its own errors alarm and a `VideoFunctionArn` output.
- The release writes `video-function.yaml` into the package beside `template.yaml`, and `lambda deploy` without a checkout stages both.
- New workflow, `Lambda SAM template`: `examples/aws-lambda/scripts/check-sam-deploy.sh` runs `sam validate --lint` on both templates. It then runs the CLI's `sam deploy` argv with fake credentials, with and without a video image, and requires each run to get past validation and stop at the first upload.

## Test plan

- [x] `bash examples/aws-lambda/scripts/check-sam-deploy.sh` with SAM CLI 1.169.0: both templates lint clean, and both deploys get past validation. The same script on this PR's previous template fails with `Missing option '--image-repositories', '--image-repository', '--resolve-image-repos'`.
- [x] `sam package` with real credentials uploads the nested template and leaves the child's `ImageUri` as the parameter reference
- [x] `bun test src/cdk/HyperframesRenderStack.snapshot.test.ts scripts/pin-handler-zip.test.ts`: 29 pass, three runs in a row. CLI `vitest run src/commands/lambda`: 65 pass, three runs in a row. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow are clean.
- [x] Each of these fails only its own test: chunks routed back to the render function, an environment variable missing from the child, the release not writing the child, the CLI staging only `template.yaml`. The contract test pins the plan and the chunks to the same function: routing either one back to x86 fails it. (Earlier: v2 chunks left on x86; role unable to invoke the video function.)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"
- [x] Real deploys with and without an image (with #6073), heavy 4K renders on both, then teardown with nothing left behind

title: fix(engine): size render workers from the container CPU limit
body:
## What

Render sizing now uses the cores the process may actually use. Worker count, video-extraction slots and the shader-transition thread pool read the host's core count (`os.cpus().length`); they now read `getUsableCpuCount()`: the host's `availableParallelism()` capped by the cgroup CPU quota (v2 `cpu.max`, v1 `cpu.cfs_quota_us` / `cpu.cfs_period_us`), floored, at least 1. The CLI's "auto workers (N cores detected)" line reports the same number.

## Why

A container limited to 6 cores on a 32-vCPU host sized itself for 32. The same container image picked a different worker count depending on which host it landed on: for a 450-frame render, 3 workers on an 8-vCPU host and up to 6 on a 16+ vCPU host (4 where the default V8 heap binds first), with the same 6-core limit. Node does not cover this: `availableParallelism()` honours a cpuset but not a CFS quota (Node 22.23.4 / libuv 1.51 in a `--cpus 2` container on an 8-core host returns 8).

## Related work

Refs #1373 (the same fix for memory: `getSystemTotalMb` already respects the cgroup memory limit). The new `systemCpu.ts` follows `systemMemory.ts`: same container-root paths, cached probe, one stderr notice, no reads off Linux.

## How

- `packages/engine/src/services/systemCpu.ts`: `parseCgroupCpuLimit`, `getCgroupCpuLimit`, `getUsableCpuCount`, exported from the engine root and as the `@hyperframes/engine/system-cpu` subpath (`package-subpaths.json`, then `sync:package-subpaths`).
- Callers moved to it: `parallelCoordinator.ts` (auto max, `computeWorkerSizing`, `getSystemResources`), `videoFrameExtractor.ts` (extraction slots), producer `shaderTransitionWorkerPool.ts` (thread clamp), CLI `present.ts`. Hardware telemetry (`perfSummary`, CLI telemetry) still reports the host.
- Status: hold. Measured on a 6-core container, the 2-worker result below is slower than the 4 workers it replaces for a 450-frame render, so the per-core budget needs revising before this merges.
- Behaviour change, on purpose: where a CPU quota is readable, auto sizing now follows the engine's own per-core budget for that quota. Example: a 6-core quota rendering 450 frames now gets 2 workers (contention cap `floor(6 / 2.5)`), on any host. Explicit `--workers` / `PRODUCER_MAX_WORKERS` are unchanged. Machines with no quota (laptops, plain VMs) are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `systemCpu.test.ts` (11: v2/v1 parsing, unlimited and malformed values, floor and minimum, larger-than-host quota, cache, stderr-only notice, unreadable file, non-Linux). `parallelCoordinator.test.ts` adds the repro (32-vCPU host, 6-core limit, 450 frames: `cpuCount` 6, 2 workers, bound by contention). Before the fix it failed with `expected 32 to be 6`. The heap test and `videoFrameExtractor.concurrency.test.ts` now fake the CPU count through the helper instead of `os.cpus`.
- [x] Each changed test file run alone, exit 0: systemCpu 11/11, parallelCoordinator 55/55, videoFrameExtractor.concurrency 5/5, systemMemory 28/28, producer shaderTransitionWorkerPool 10/10.
- [x] Mutations, each reverted: sizing back on `os.cpus()` turns 2 parallelCoordinator tests red; the helper ignoring the quota turns 4 systemCpu tests red; the extractor test given 8 CPUs instead of 2 turns 4 of its tests red.
- [x] Manual: the built `dist/services/systemCpu.js` in `node:22.23.4-bookworm-slim` on an 8-core cgroup v1 host: `--cpus 2` gives 2; `--cpus 4 --cpuset-cpus 0-2` gives 3.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` in engine, producer and cli; oxlint, oxfmt, `check:package-subpaths`, comment checks: all clean.
- [ ] Live cgroup v2 run (covered by unit tests here; the test host is v1).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix: data-volume multiplies the volume lane in preview and render
body:
## What

`data-volume` is clip gain that multiplies the volume lane. Projects setting both now sound at gain × lane. Reset gain to `1` to retain a lane's former absolute level.

Clip gain plays before clip effects; the lane plays after them. Dynamics effects therefore react to the gained signal. Group gain stays after group effects. Studio exposes separate **Gain** and **Volume** controls: Gain edits `data-volume`; Volume edits a lane point at the playhead, creating a lane when needed.

## Why

A lane previously discarded `data-volume`. The shared contract now caps their product at the existing +12 dB authored-gain ceiling. It preserves the ramp below that ceiling: gain 2 × lane 0→3 over 10 seconds is 3 at 5 seconds and reaches the ceiling at 6.6351195092 seconds. Clamping endpoints alone incorrectly made the midpoint 1.9905358528.

## How

- `gainTimesLane` owns the capped product. `gainedVolumePoints` inserts ceiling-crossing breakpoints for straight ramps and bounds sampling for bent crossings. Preview clips, groups and render consume that envelope. A pre-FX clip gain leaves only the lane's share of the capped product downstream.
- Gain edits rebook the lane. Removing a playing lane clears its held AudioParam events and restores the static clip or group baseline. Zero gain stays muted without division. Preview and render share the check for exponent and via-point bends.
- The PCM baker and FX pass receive the same envelope. Existing GSAP volume tweens keep their absolute-level behavior.
- Core's unpacked package budget changes from 3,936,240 on the base to 3,942,104 bytes, matching the built artifact. The gain stages and shared envelope helpers account for the increase. Packed core is 1,633,047 bytes, within its unchanged budget; engine remains within both budgets.

## Before

The same synthetic audio fixture, with gain 0.5 and lane 0.8 at the playhead. Only Volume is exposed.

![Before panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1c9ee53d-4e05-4295-82d6-945e952a9806)

## After

Gain shows −6.0 dB independently of the lane's −1.9 dB Volume. Captures use the pre-change and current panel sources while holding the audio fixture fixed.

![After panel](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dabf1b96-40bf-4b0a-b34f-9025b8fce991)

## Test plan

- Failing first against the previous audio implementation: transport exit 1, 4 failed / 95 passed; render envelope exit 1, 3 failed / 8 passed; mixer exit 1, 1 failed / 73 passed.
- Three serial runs of each changed audio test file: automation 40, transport 99, render envelope 11, mixer 74; every run exit 0, no skips. Covers over-ceiling products, rising/falling crossings, zero gain, gain edits and pre-FX render input.
- Deliberately removing crossings, removing the upstream-gain correction, and replacing zero gain with unity each made the new witnesses fail. Mutations restored.
- Lane-removal regression: 2 failed / 99 passed without the reset; restored implementation passed transport 101 and FX runtime 37 in three serial rounds. Real browser OfflineAudioContext PCM returned from 0.5 to 2 for both clip and group after removing the lane.
- Three runs of each changed Studio test file: panel 46 and volume automation 21, every run exit 0, no skips.
- Neighbor checks: media 153, FX runtime 37, AudioParam scheduling 23, each exit 0. Core/engine typechecks, lint, format, comment checks and commit hooks passed.
- Browser fixture: Gain changed from −6 to −3 dB without changing the lane; Volume changed the first lane point to −6 dB without changing gain. Both changes persisted in the saved HTML and after a full reload.

## What I measured

Recorded the real AudioParam schedule, native browser PCM for lane removal, mixer envelope inputs, packed artifacts, and fixture control edits with saved-file and reload checks. Unit tests and builds ran on Linux; an isolated browser drove the fixture Studio server.

## What I did NOT exercise

The ceiling delta was not auditioned through a physical audio device or measured from a new encoded output. The scheduling/mixer tests record collaborators; they do not prove codec or device behavior. Touch interaction, screen-reader output, invalid text, undo/redo, and first-time-user comprehension were not exercised in this pass.

## UX checklist

**Job:** adjust a clip's gain independently of its volume keyframes.
**One action:** edit Gain while retaining the lane, or edit Volume at the playhead.

| # | Question | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First-time purpose clear | Not exercised | Labels captured; comprehension not tested. |
| 2 | Editable controls recognizable | Y | Two labeled sliders and editable dB values. |
| 3 | User-facing words | Y | Gain, Volume, dB. |
| 4 | Equivalent editor model | Y | Clip gain offsets the lane, the requested model. |
| 5 | Guidance at the control | Not exercised | No novice guidance study. |
| 6 | Action reachable | Y | Both controls visible in Media. |
| 7 | Clear action hierarchy | Y | Paired property edits; no competing submit action. |
| 8 | Display matches data | Y | −3 dB gain and −6 dB lane checked after reload. |
| 9 | Excluded items announced | Not exercised | Hidden/deleted selection not tested. |
| 10 | Long names recoverable | Not exercised | Short fixture filename only. |
| 11 | Keyboard path | Y | Text edits committed with Enter. |
| 12 | Controls discoverable | Y | Gain and Volume visible without hover. |
| 13 | Helpful refusals | Not exercised | Invalid text not tested. |
| 14 | Refusals placed nearby | Not exercised | No refusal triggered. |
| 15 | Invalid options prevented | Not exercised | Out-of-range UI entry not tested. |
| 16 | Recover without losing work | Not exercised | Undo/redo not walked. |
| 17 | Destructive actions separated | Not exercised | No destructive edit walked. |
| 18 | Empty states explained | Not exercised | Selected audio only. |
| 19 | Visible feedback | Y | Value and preview attributes updated after Enter; latency not measured. |
| 20 | Wait progress | Not exercised | No long operation in this flow. |
| 21 | State survives reload | Y | Saved HTML and fresh preview retained both values. |

**Choice:** the two existing gain layers are exposed as two controls; neither is hidden behind a mode.
**End:** the panel shows the saved gain and lane value after reload.

title: fix(studio): the edit-accuracy gate says the shards did not run, not that accuracy fell
body:
## What

When no Studio edit-accuracy shard produced results (for example, the build failed), the gate now says so:

```
::error::Edit accuracy did not run: 0 of 5 shards reported results; see the shard jobs.
```

Before, it said `Edit accuracy fell against the base branch; see the PR comment.`, with no PR comment to see, so a build failure read as an accuracy regression. The same goes for a run where some shards did not report and nothing that ran fell (`1 of 2 shards reported results`). A case that ran and regressed still fails as a drop, even with a shard missing.

## Why

`ratchet.mjs gate` threw `no results.json from any shard` before writing `comment.md` or `gate.json`, so the step exited 1. The workflow's last step printed one fixed message for any non-zero exit. A missing shard also went through the accuracy reasons, so it exited 1 the same way.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `ratchet.mjs` owns the verdict. Exit 0 is "holds", exit 1 is "fell" (a case that ran regressed, or the passing count fell), and exit 2 is "did not run" (no shard, or some shards missing while nothing that ran fell).
- It writes `comment.md` and `gate.json` in every case, so the sticky PR comment says the gate did not run instead of being skipped. `gate.json` carries a `verdict` line.
- The workflow's last step prints that `verdict`. If the gate crashed before writing it, the step says the gate could not finish and points at its log.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

`ratchet.test.mjs`, four new tests that run `ratchet.mjs gate --shards N` as CI does, on temp files:

| Case | On `main` | With this PR |
|---|---|---|
| no shard results | fails: no `gate.json` written (the throw) | exit 2, "did not run: 0 of 5 shards" |
| 1 of 2 shards, nothing fell | fails: exit 1 (read as a drop) | exit 2, "did not run: 1 of 2 shards" |
| 1 of 2 shards, a case that ran regressed | fails: no `verdict` | exit 1, "fell" |
| every shard, nothing fell | fails: no `verdict` | exit 0, "holds" |

- Whole file: 21 passed, exit 0, 3 runs in a row.
- Mutations, each turning only the named test red:
  - zero shards exit 1: the no-results test fails;
  - a missing shard counts as a drop: the 1-of-2 holding test fails;
  - a missing shard outranks a real drop: the 1-of-2 regression test fails.

title: feat(aws-lambda): attach the arm64 video image to releases and pin it
body:
## What

Every release attaches the arm64 Lambda video function image as an OCI layout tarball, `hyperframes-lambda-video-arm64.oci.tar` with its `.sha256`, and `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` pins it (URL, sha256, bytes, version) in `prebuilt/video-image.json`. A new SDK function, `prebuiltVideoImage()`, reads that pin. Stacked on #6064.

Nothing consumes the pin yet: the CLI option that pushes the image and deploys it comes next. The x86 ZIP deploy is untouched.

## Why

A released CLI must be able to deploy the arm64 video function without a repo checkout or a Docker build on the user's machine, the same way it deploys the handler ZIP today. That needs a prebuilt image whose bytes the npm package pins.

## How

- **ARM job.** `publish.yml` gains `lambda-arm64-ffmpeg` on `ubuntu-24.04-arm`. It has the same release `if:` and the same immutable checkout as `publish`, and only `contents: read`. It builds #6062's ffmpeg artifact and uploads the tarball as a workflow artifact. `publish` now `needs` it, so a failed ARM build stops the release before anything is tagged or published.
- **Cache.** The ffmpeg tarball is cached under a key that hashes `packages/aws-lambda/image/**`.
  - GitHub only lets a run restore caches from its own ref, its PR's base branch, or the default branch. A release run (a merged release PR or a prerelease tag) saves into a scope no later release can read.
  - So `lambda-arm64-image.yml` now also runs on pushes to `main` that touch `image/**`, and copy `a` saves the same key there. Releases then compile only when the recipe changed and that push's run has not finished yet. A re-run of the same release also hits its own first attempt's save.
  - What a cache hit trusts: the tarball some earlier run wrote under that key on `main` (or this release's first attempt). On `main` that is `lambda-arm64-image.yml`, which built it from the same recipe and ran the codec check. A hit skips the compile and its codec check. `stage-arm64-image.ts` still refuses ffmpeg or ffprobe binaries that are not arm64 ELF.
- **Image build.** In `publish`, right after the handler ZIP is pinned, the image is staged from that ZIP (`dist/hyperframes-lambda-handler.zip`) and the ARM tarball with `stage-arm64-image.ts`.
  - The Dockerfile's copy-only `video` stage is built for `linux/arm64` on the x86 runner, with no emulation.
  - The output is `--output type=oci` from a `docker-container` buildx builder, with `--provenance=false --sbom=false`, so `index.json` lists exactly one image manifest.
- **Retries.** A run whose release already has the image downloads it instead of rebuilding and skips the attach step. This is the same pattern the ZIP uses. A retried run that downloads the existing ZIP still builds a matching image, because the image is built from that same ZIP.
- **One pin helper.** `pin-handler-zip.ts`'s hashing is now `pinReleaseAsset(repoRoot, asset, manifestFile)`, which writes the `.sha256` sidecar and the manifest. The ZIP keeps its move-and-template step on top of it, and `--video-image` pins the image. `HandlerZipManifest` is renamed `ReleaseAssetManifest`, since both pins share that shape.
- **Package size.** The npm package carries only the small JSON pin. The image stays a release asset.
- `publish`'s timeout goes from 20 to 30 minutes for the base image pull, the staging (Chrome arm64 pack download) and the image upload.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun test scripts/pin-handler-zip.test.ts`: 7 pass, 0 fail, exit 0, three runs in a row
- [x] CLI tests that load the adapter SDK (`prebuiltHandler`, `deploy`, `stackCheck`): 11 passed, exit 0, three runs in a row
- [x] One mutation per new behaviour, each failing only its own tests:
  - `prebuiltVideoImage` reads the handler manifest: the image pin test and the "no image when only the zip is pinned" test fail
  - the `.sha256` sidecar name drops `-arm64`: the image pin test fails
  - the pin URL names the handler ZIP instead of the asset: the image pin test fails
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` for the package, `actionlint` on both workflows: clean
- [ ] Dry run of the real publish workflow with `act`, cut before "Create GitHub Release" (no release, no upload, no npm publish)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: test(cli): run skill one-liner tests without a shell per line
body:
## What

The skill-query one-liner tests in `describeProject.test.ts` no longer start a shell per line. Each test describes its fixture once, runs the documented `node -e` programs in-process, and runs the documented `jq` lines as `jq` itself with the timeline on stdin.

## Why

On the Windows runner these three tests took 47 s, 27 s and 15 s against a 20 s limit, and failed the engine-cli lane on unrelated PRs. Each documented line ran through `bash -c` (MSYS bash on Windows), and every `node -e` line then cold-started a second Node. That is 5 to 10 bash starts and up to 10 Node starts per test, run one after another because `execFileSync` blocks inside the `Promise.all`. The jq test, with no Node at all, still took 27 s, so the shell starts dominate under a loaded runner.

## How

- `argvOf` splits a documented `<cmd> ... '<program>' <<<"$TL"` line the way bash quotes it. The lines stay verbatim from the skill doc; only the example query values are swapped, as before.
- `node -e` lines: the program runs with `runInNewContext` (the pattern in `designStyleExtractor.buttons.test.ts`), with `require("fs").readFileSync(0, "utf8")` answering the timeline and `console.log` captured through `util.format`, as Node prints it.
- `jq` lines: `execFileSync("jq", args, { input })`, one native process per line, no shell.
- Assertions are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: feat(cli): lambda deploy renders on arm64 by default; --video-arch x86_64 keeps x86
body:
## What

`hyperframes lambda deploy` now deploys the stack with an arm64 container-image function that runs the plan and renders the chunks. Audio and assemble stay on the x86 ZIP function. `--video-arch x86_64` deploys everything on x86, as before this PR.

Redeploying an existing stack without the flag moves it to arm64 and adds its `<stack>-video` ECR repository. To keep a stack on x86, pass `--video-arch x86_64` on every deploy. The Lambda guide has an upgrade note.

Depends on #6070 (the pinned image), #6063 (ECR push) and #6065 (the template's `VideoImageUri`). Its base, `feat/lambda-arm64-deps`, is #6070's branch with #6063 and #6065 merged in and nothing else, so this diff is only the CLI option and default, cost accounting and progress.

## Why

The plan and the chunks are most of a render's compute, and arm64 Lambda costs 20% less per GB-second. Users of the released CLI have no Docker, so the CLI pushes the release's image itself through the ECR API.

## How

- `videoImage.ts`: the image is the OCI tarball the installed `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` pins. The same `fetchPinned` the handler ZIP now uses downloads it and checks its sha256. The CLI then:
  - extracts it, creates `<stack>-video` in ECR and pushes it;
  - refuses anything but `linux/arm64`;
  - returns the digest-pinned URI.
- In a checkout, the release image could run different handler code from the checkout's ZIP, so it is refused there. `HYPERFRAMES_LAMBDA_VIDEO_IMAGE` points at a locally built tarball instead.
- No silent fallback to x86. Each of these errors names `--video-arch x86_64` as the way out:
  - a checkout without that image;
  - an installed adapter that pins no image;
  - `--chrome-source chrome-headless-shell`, since the image bundles sparticuz Chrome only.
- `sam.ts`: `VideoImageUri` is always sent, and is empty for x86. If it were omitted, SAM would send `UsePreviousValue` and keep a video function the user dropped. `fetchStackOutputs` reads `VideoFunctionArn`.
- State records the video function and its repository. `destroy` deletes the repository after the stack; a repository already gone counts as deleted. Switching back to x86 keeps the repository name so `destroy` still finds it.
- Cost: `getRenderProgress` takes `videoArchitecture` and prices the plan and `RenderChunk` invocations at the arm64 rate, inline and from the Distributed Map's output. `render --wait` and `progress` pass it from state.
- The repository is created with the tag `hyperframes:stack=<stack>`. An existing one is adopted only if it carries that tag (#6063), so `destroy` only ever deletes this stack's own repository.
- `policies` lists the ECR actions the push, the tag check and Lambda's image pull need.

## Test plan

- [x] `bunx vitest run src/commands/lambda` (cli): 76 pass, three runs in a row. `bun test` (aws-lambda) passes. `examples/aws-lambda/scripts/check-sam-deploy.sh` passes.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, `fallow audit`, `check:cli-process-ownership` and `comment-ratchet` are clean.
- [x] One mutation per behaviour, each failing only its own tests:
  - The default flipped back to x86 fails the default-deploy test and the default headless-shell refusal.
  - Dropping the way out from the headless-shell error fails both refusal cases.
  - Dropping it from the image errors fails the checkout and no-pin cases.
  - Earlier: `VideoImageUri` omitted for x86, no arch check, release image used in a checkout, repository name not lowercased, image URI or repository dropped by deploy, a missing repository treated as a failure, `VideoFunctionArn` ignored, chunks priced x86, the stack tag dropped from the repository call.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".
- [x] Live deploys from this branch on a real account, arm64 and x86 side by side, heavy 4K renders on both, then `destroy` with nothing left behind.

title: test(studio): sample gesture replay from one preview state
body:
## What

Prevent false tracking jumps when the edit-accuracy bench samples a queued drag as it begins replaying.

## Why

A fast keyframe sequence can start a drag while the previous save is in flight. Studio draws a waiting outline until it replays that press. The sampler read the element before replay and checked the waiting mark afterward. When replay happened between those reads, it reported the old element position as the live drag position for one sample.

A shadow-preview promotion exposed a second measurement defect: a hidden iframe can keep answering CDP geometry requests, so waiting for a detached-node error does not reliably refresh cached handles.

Both fixes are in the common measurement path. Gesture behavior, thresholds, and the banked baseline are unchanged.

## How

The edit-accuracy sampler captures the waiting outline before it reads preview geometry, then checks that the outline still has its waiting mark. If queued-press replay crossed the read, it samples again. Geometry reads also reject a cached preview handle once its iframe is hidden, using the existing handle-refresh retry.

## Test plan

- Two deterministic regressions exercise replay between reads and a hidden cached iframe. Each fails on its intended assertion when its fix is removed.
- Focused test file: three consecutive runs, each exit 0, 2 passed, 0 skipped.
- A delayed-save sequence that previously produced a large tracking jump passes all accuracy checks with the sampler fix.
- Uninstrumented `seqfastkeys-none-px-r0-root-z100`: 20/20 runs pass every accuracy check, zero errors. Maximum tracking error across all 20 runs: 0.064 px.
- The existing ratchet, explicitly scoped to this case, passes: no regressions, unstable cases, missing cases, or baseline changes. Smoothness remains false, matching the banked baseline.
- Formatter, lint, and diff whitespace checks pass.

title: test(studio): retain Chrome launch diagnostics
body:
## What

Keep the selected Chrome binary and version, launch-attempt timing, and browser startup output in Studio's real-browser test logs.

## Why

A browser-test launch can time out before its first test starts. The timeout message alone omits the chosen executable/version and the browser's recent stderr, so it cannot explain whether startup stalled before or after the DevTools endpoint appeared.

## How

The test helper reuses the existing browser-version probe, identifies each attempt, and logs how long it took to become ready or fail. Puppeteer's `dumpio` forwarding keeps browser stdout/stderr in the CI log from the start, including launches that time out. Successful launches also retain startup output.

The selected executable, browser flags, two-attempt limit, and 20-second launch limit stay the same.

## Test plan

- Diagnostic output and stderr forwarding each have an independent failing control.
- Focused helper tests cover attempt reporting, the retry limit, and preservation of the original failure: three runs, each exit 0 with 7 passed and 0 skipped. The new retry-limit assertion also fails when the implementation stops after one attempt.
- Browser resolution tests: exit 0, 9 passed, 0 skipped.
- Real-browser undo and value-edit files pass with Chrome 152: 11 and 1 tests respectively, exit 0 and 0 skipped. Their logs show the selected browser, readiness timing, and startup stderr.
- Required pre-commit typechecks, format, lint, and artifact checks pass.
- Repeated Studio CI jobs will run at one fixed PR head. The launch cause remains under investigation; those logs will determine the behavior fix.


## Windows version probe

The browser-version probe ran `chrome.exe --version`. On Windows, Chrome does not print a version for that flag: it opens a window in the user's existing browser session and prints "Opening in existing browser session.", and the call had no time limit. On a runner where Chrome is installed, that makes the probe itself a way to stall before the first test starts. On Windows the probe now reads the file's product version through PowerShell (the path passed in an environment variable, never interpolated into the command), accepts only a four-part version number, and every probe call has a 5-second limit. Other platforms still run `--version`, now with the same limit.

Tests (`vite.browserVersion.test.ts`): the Unix call is bounded; the Windows call reads the file metadata without running the browser or putting a hostile path (quotes, `$()`, `&`) into the command; output that is not a version ("Opening in existing browser session.", empty, text) is not reported as one. Typecheck, lint, format and the pre-commit checks pass.


## No visible change

This changes only the browser launcher that Studio's own tests use (`vite.browser.ts`) and its tests. No Studio or player screen, style or behaviour that a user sees is touched.

title: fix(parsers): preserve Unicode offsets when stamping IDs
body:
## What

Preserve the original source when stamping IDs into HTML containing length-changing Unicode before or inside a script/style block.

## Why

The scanner lowercased the entire HTML string to locate raw-text closing tags, then used those offsets in the original string. For example, U+0130 lowercases to two code units. That shifts the closing-tag offset and can make valid markup fall back to full serialization, rewriting unrelated attribute casing and quotes.

Small synthetic fixtures reproduce this with the exact hash-matched published b450 parser. Fresh main retains the same scanner. This was found while investigating a native lowercase-allocation failure; the actual crash caller and crash prevention remain unverified.

## Related work

Focused current open-PR comparison found no repair of this scanner. No separate issue needed for this two-file correction.

## How

Search the original source for the ASCII raw-text closing tag using a case-insensitive regex and the existing closing-tag boundary rule. Keep source offsets in the original string and avoid a full-document lowercase copy. ID minting, parser fallback and tag admission are unchanged.

## Test plan

- Two script/style regressions fail against the original source (2 fail/38 pass), then the changed file passes all40 tests and three repeats. Cases include expanding Unicode, mixed-case closing tags, whitespace before the closing bracket, ID parity and idempotence. Existing longer-tag-name boundary tests remain.
- Complete parsers suite:1323 pass/4 skip/3 todo after building the missing local core generator prerequisite; initial run had two import failures.
- Real filesystem Studio-server hfIdPersist/noFollow suites:10 pass.
- Parser typecheck/build, core build, changed-file lint/format and all commit hooks pass.
- Complete dependent core suite:5031 pass/0 fail after building the missing lint/Studio-server prerequisites. Initial attempt was non-green with missing-package import failures and5 assertions on the missing lint entry; no source or gate changes were needed.

No visual change. No customer file, native crash, host memory stress, packaged UI, release or deployment exercised. This PR does not establish the source of customer native OOMs.

title: fix(aws-lambda): retry a file upload after a dropped connection
body:
## What

A file upload to S3 now survives a dropped connection. Each retry reopens the file instead of failing the task on the first reset.

## Why

`uploadFileToS3` and the conditional put behind the content-addressed uploads sent a single `createReadStream` body. The AWS SDK never retries a streamed body; it logs "An error was encountered in a non-retryable streaming request". One connection reset from S3 therefore failed the whole invocation.

We saw it on a long distributed render: a chunk finished rendering, then its upload got `TimeoutError: socket hang up` (`ECONNRESET`). The state machine retried the task, so the render still succeeded, but it repeated the chunk's full render and stretched the render's tail. The upload code is the same on every architecture.

## How

- `sendFileBody` in `s3Transport.ts` owns "fresh stream per attempt". The single PutObject, the conditional PutObject and each multipart part go through it. Before this change only the multipart parts did this.
- It retries only a transient failure, up to 3 attempts: a dropped connection (no HTTP status), the AWS SDK's transient codes (`TimeoutError`, `RequestTimeout`, `RequestTimeoutException`; S3 sends `RequestTimeout` as HTTP 400), 429 or a 5xx. Any other S3 answer is final:
  - A 412 on a conditional create still reaches the caller, which checks whether a concurrent writer stored the same bytes.
  - A `BadDigest` is not resent.
- Changes for multipart parts:
  - A part that S3 rejects with a non-transient 4xx now fails at once, instead of being resent up to 3 times.
  - A part response with no ETag is no longer retried.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests: the fake S3 reads the whole body, then fails with a dropped connection or `RequestTimeout`/400. The single PUT and a multipart part must both succeed on the second attempt. The single-PUT cases fail on main.
- [x] A plain 400 (`InvalidArgument`) and `BadDigest` are each sent exactly once.
- [x] Retrying every error fails the plain-400, `BadDigest` and both concurrent-create tests. Treating every 4xx as final fails both `RequestTimeout` tests.
- [x] `bun test src/s3Transport.test.ts`: 27 pass, three runs in a row. The full `packages/aws-lambda` suite: 241 pass, 0 fail.
- [x] oxlint, oxfmt, `tsc --noEmit`, fallow (no issues in the 2 changed files) and the comment ratchet are clean.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: lint rejects a final unquoted font-family without a semicolon
body:
## Describe the bug Valid `@font-face` CSS is rejected when its final descriptor is an unquoted `font-family` without a trailing semicolon. This can arise in handwritten or minified CSS. The `font_family_without_font_face` error blocks lint/check and strict render preflight even though the family is declared. ## Minimal reproduction From a built repository checkout, save this as `repro-font.mjs` in the repository root: ```js import { lintHyperframeHtml } from "./packages/lint/src/hyperframeLinter.ts"; const html = `
`; const result = await lintHyperframeHtml(html, { isSubComposition: true }); console.log(JSON.stringify(result.findings.filter( (finding) => finding.code === "font_family_without_font_face", ), null, 2)); ``` No downloaded font or other asset is required to reproduce the incorrect lint result. This calls the real HTML linter and filters the relevant diagnostic. ## Steps to reproduce 1. Use main at `10c724bf555f8355199bd89db1a02fc159909dc9` (version 0.8.186) with the repository dependencies and packages built. 2. Run `bun repro-font.mjs`. 3. Add a semicolon immediately after `ProjectFont` in the `@font-face` descriptor and rerun. Quoting the family also avoids the failure. ## Expected behavior The declaration is recognized with or without its optional final semicolon. The reproduction should print `[]`. ## Actual behavior The first run returns an error with code `font_family_without_font_face` and message beginning `Font family used without @font-face declaration: projectfont.` The semicolon and quoted-name controls return no such finding. Chrome 152 CSSOM accepts both declarations as `ProjectFont`. The linter's `extractFontFaceFamilies` matcher includes the closing brace in the unquoted value, recording `projectfont}` instead of `projectfont`. ## Environment - Hyperframes 0.8.186; current-main base `10c724bf555f8355199bd89db1a02fc159909dc9`. - Linux x86_64, Node 26.11.1, Bun 1.4.1. The repository pins Bun 1.4.4; the reproduction and tests used the already-installed 1.4.1. - Vitest 4.1.11; lint package builds and typechecks successfully. - This is a static lint reproduction, not a complete video render. A full workspace build is limited by missing installed inspector/AWS dependencies; no packages were installed for this investigation. ## Additional context The correction is to stop the family-value match at `}`. Two regressions cover single-word and multiword unquoted families. The existing missing-declaration behavior remains intact. Related #1534/#1538 concern braces inside CSS comments; #2538 concerns `!important`; closed #2778 leaves the declaration extractor unchanged. None corrects this case. I have a focused fix prepared.

title: fix(cli): report failed tag installations to scripts and agents
body:
## What

`hyperframes add <tag>` now reports an incomplete installation as a failure. Scripts and agents receive exit code 1 and `ok: false` when any block fails; JSON includes each failed block's name and error. Successful installations remain available.

## Why

The tag loop catches each install error and then reports unconditional success. In JSON mode, it also drops every failure reason.

The same real source CLI process with fixture HTTP responses:

| Download results | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| All fail with HTTP 404 | Exit 0; `ok: true`; no files; no errors | Exit 1; `ok: false`; named HTTP 404 error |
| One fails, one succeeds | Exit 0; `ok: true` | Exit 1; `ok: false`; successful HTML preserved |
| All succeed | Exit 0; `ok: true` | Exit 0; `ok: true`; `errors: []` |

The issue includes a self-contained reproduction. Only HTTP responses are fixtures; dispatch, resolution, installation, filesystem writes and process exit handling use the real implementation.

## Related work

Fixes #6084.

#4432 preserves warnings from successful installs. Open #5256 refreshes item manifests during discovery; neither handles failed file installation.

## How
