title: fix(audio): fit PCM to video frames before AAC delivery
body:
## What

Local and distributed renders now use one audio stage to fit the float mix to the video's exact frame duration, apply the encoded true-peak check from that mix, and deliver AAC for packet-copy assembly. AAC encoding uses scalar DSP for consistent output across CPU architectures. Regression residual measurements now cover the whole unscaled difference, including before a silent ending.

## Why

The declared composition duration can differ from the duration of its whole video frames. Mixing to the declared seconds forced assembly to decode AAC and encode it again. That extra lossy generation changed peak correction and reduced integrated loudness by 1.5 LUFS in the native regression fixture.

## Related work

This corrects audio delivery shared by local and distributed renders. It does not change video capture or video encoding.

## How

- `runAudioStage` owns the frame-count/rational-fps duration, retained float mix, encoded peak check, and PCM cleanup.
- Both plan entrypoints and local orchestration call that stage. The plan-only peak helper is removed; assembly receives fitted AAC.
- Existing attenuation warnings and render metadata retain the measured gain reduction.
- `-cpuflags 0` is set only on the canonical audio AAC encode command. Packet-copy muxing and video encode commands retain their existing flags. Existing frame-aligned parallel segmentation remains enabled; each segment starts from PCM.

- The regression residual checker disables mixer normalization and accumulates statistics over the whole track. A silent last block can no longer erase an earlier mismatch.

## Test plan

- Native duration witness failed before the fix: the default plan was 1,120 samples short of the required frame duration.
- Native loudness witness failed on main with a 1.5 LUFS difference against a float-source reference. It must stay within 0.1 LUFS after assembly and below the delivery peak ceiling.
- Scalar-argument witness failed before the flag change. It runs real FFmpeg, pins the audio encoder arguments, checks repeated output bytes, and checks the copy mux has no CPU flag.
- Changed suites passed three serial runs on Linux. Neighbor suites, engine and producer typechecks, formatting, lint, fallow audit, package build and all six package budgets passed.
- The real-project check runs final compile, probe, audio and assembly stages against a frozen project. Its picture comes from the corresponding cloud export and is copied without video encoding. Reusing those packets is valid because this diff changes only audio delivery. The measured candidate preceded the latest clip-gain change on main; the patch rebases cleanly onto that change and its native plan suite passed three further runs with rebuilt dependencies. The final post-rebase Vitest stage and local/distributed handoff checks also passed. The CLI diagnostic fixture uses the same frame clock; its 13 tests passed three serial runs, and the CLI typecheck passed. Both comment checks and all commit hooks passed. All seven chapters measured 0.0 LUFS difference at the meter's 0.1 LUFS reporting precision, within the 0.1 LUFS limit. Compressed video packet hashes matched.

- Actual built-package checks passed on x86 and ARM through the default segmented caption route: two scalar AAC segment encodes followed by packet-copy assembly. With identical input PCM, the entire M4A was byte-identical across architectures. Native upstream PCM differs slightly between architectures, so this does not claim identical bytes for independently mixed projects.

- The existing `speed-ramp` golden predates the PCM correction. At the unchanged 16 kHz gate, scalar/golden correlation was 0.594, while scalar/non-scalar correlation was 0.9996. Gain-matched decoded RMS error against the retained float mix improved from -37.44 dBFS (old golden) to -50.14 dBFS (new delivery). Replaying correction from AAC reproduced the old golden's envelope at 0.9985 correlation. Only that fixture's MP4 golden is refreshed through the CI harness entrypoint, run natively with Node 22.23.3, Chrome 148.0.7778.167 and the exact pinned FFmpeg n8.0.1-66-g27b8d1a017 build. Three serial harness checks passed at 1.000 audio correlation, zero lag and zero failed visual frames. SHA-256 checks confirmed all 217 other fixture golden files stayed byte-identical. The original compiled HTML object is retained too, bringing the total of unchanged golden files to 218; the public compilation validator passed against that original snapshot without errors or warnings. The 16 kHz correlation threshold remains unchanged. Temporary Node and Chrome downloads were removed.
- The residual witness uses a 0.25 stereo signal for one second followed by one second of silence against silence. The old helper incorrectly reported negative infinity instead of the analytical -15.0515 dBFS. A deliberate averaging mutant reported -21.0721 dBFS and failed. The corrected native suite passed three serial runs.

title: fix(cli): preserve video frames when scenes reuse element IDs
body:
## What

When two scene files each contain `<video id="clip">`, later snapshot frames can be completely black even though the command succeeds. Give every merged media element a distinct render identity and carry it through snapshot extraction, injection, and visibility.

## Why

Inlining makes scene-local IDs ambiguous. Snapshot addressed both videos as `clip`; injection found the first video, skipped its hidden scene, and left the visible second scene without footage. Authored IDs must stay intact because scene CSS and scripts use them.

This fixes the reproduced scene-identity failure. The separate macOS report where multi-time calls fail but individual calls succeed was not reproduced with the unique-ID synthetic fixture, so this PR does not establish that report's cause.

## Related work

Reuses the existing canonical allocator and browser lookup bridge. No transcode-cache behavior changes.

## How

- Allocate render IDs after all scenes are inlined. Preserve unique existing stamps, repair duplicate stamps, and reserve media and audio-bus identities before allocating new ones.
- Install the existing bridge before capture navigation. Snapshot candidates and frame visibility use the same identity already accepted by injection.
- Preserve authored element IDs and repaired identities across recompilation.
- Raise only Core's unpacked size budget by 359 bytes for the shared bundler and allocator code. Other package budgets are unchanged.

Producer/consumer review:

| Producer | Consumer | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Combined-document allocator | Snapshot candidate collection | Unique identity across scene files, including pre-stamped inputs |
| Candidate ID | Frame extraction and injection | Passed unchanged; bridge resolves the stamped element |
| Active frame IDs | Visibility synchronization | Uses the same identity as injection |
| Repaired audio-bus IDs | Member pairing | Pairing runs after allocation and reads final stamps |

Independent review checked the complete change and hostile identity/order states, then approved the corrective delta with no remaining findings. Unit tests enter the real bundler and command paths, but mock browser infrastructure; the separate CLI captures exercise real Chromium, decoding, injection, and screenshots.

## Test plan

- Five touched test files each passed alone three times: bundler integration (2), allocator (19), screenshot service (37), snapshot command (77), and browser recovery (8). No skipped tests.
- Regression witnesses fail when the corresponding implementation changes are removed. Restoring the old allocator fails the pre-stamped integration and both new allocator behaviors.
- Real CLI fixture: synthetic 304-second, 3840×2160, 60fps HEVC MOV with rotation -180. Two scenes reuse `clip`. Three runs include forward and backward seeks; all nine images exactly match independent FFmpeg source-frame references.
- Eight-cut unique-ID control passed at nine requested times and remained pixel-identical after the fix.
- Real `check --snapshots` passed with no lint, runtime, layout, motion, or contrast issues. One expected craft warning identifies the silent synthetic fixture.
- Core, Engine, and CLI typechecks and builds passed. Packed-consumer verification passed Node execution, NodeNext declarations, Vite resolution, CLI startup, and all package-size budgets.

Browser proof is Linux Chromium. Windows recovery is covered by mocked browser tests; this does not establish macOS runtime behavior or an exported video result.

title: fix(core): a scene paints no filter output from an HTML layer before its start or after its end
body:
## What

A scene that has not started (or has ended) now paints nothing, even when one of its layers is an HTML element with `filter: url(#svg-filter)` such as an `feTurbulence` grain, with or without `mix-blend-mode: overlay`.

## Why

Such a layer from a later scene painted its grain over every earlier scene for the whole video, in preview and in snapshots. `visibility: hidden` does not stop a filter that generates pixels from no input, and the hidden-scene rule from #5828 only turned the filter off for SVG elements, so an HTML layer (or the scene element itself) with a url() filter still painted.

## Related work

Follows #5828, which fixed the same leak for an SVG rect inside the scene and then narrowed it to SVG only so filter tweens could start from their stylesheet value.

## How

- `timedClipHide.ts`: the hidden-scene `filter: none` rule now covers the scene and every element in it, not only SVG content.
- `init.ts`: a tween's first render reads its start values from computed style, so the hidden-scene rules are already lifted for it on a jump. They are now lifted for every first render, including a single-frame step into a scene. Without that, a filter tween (or any value the rule overrides) starting as frames step into its scene would read `none`.
- Rejected: `opacity: 0` on the hidden scene stops every shape but makes a later scene's `from({opacity: 0})` fade end at 0; `clip-path` stops lazy images loading; `mask`, `content-visibility` do not cover all shapes (measured in Chromium).

Cost: on each frame that renders a time for the first time, the hidden scenes get their inline visibility set and restored around the GSAP render, as already happened on jumps.

## Test plan

- `coreRuntimeBrowser.test.ts`: three leak shapes (SVG rect, HTML div inside the scene, the scene itself) at 1.5 s; the two HTML shapes fail on main with a red range of `[79, 244]` instead of a flat `[128, 128]`. A later scene's `from({opacity: 0})` fade ends at 1 as frames step into it (it ends at 0 with an `opacity: 0` hide rule). The existing filter-tween start tests at 2 s and 1.9 s keep their `blur(5px)` / `blur(4px)` start (they read `blur(0px)` when the rule applies without the init.ts change).
- 59/59 in that file, 3 runs in a row; `packages/core/src/runtime` 92 files, 2326 tests pass; typecheck, lint and format hooks pass.

title: fix(aws-lambda): make webm and mov audio in the separate audio task like mp4
body:
## What changes

WebM and MOV renders get their audio from the separate audio task, the same one mp4 already uses. Before, a WebM or MOV plan mixed and encoded its own audio.

## Why

On a stack whose plan runs on an arm64 function, a WebM or MOV render's audio came out of that function's ffmpeg build, while an x86 render's came out of the x86 build. The two builds encode AAC differently, so the same WebM render had different audio on the two architectures (a decoded null test of the two outputs peaked near -30 dBFS). MP4 never had this: its audio task always runs on the x86 function. Now every muxed format works the same way, so one function makes every audio byte whichever machine plans.

## How

- `plansSeparateAudio` defers the audio for every format except two. png-sequence copies its audio verbatim as a sidecar, and deferring it would change that sidecar's length to the video's. cfr re-encodes at assembly, and a cfr plan with separate audio would need a stitch decision of its own.
- `chunksAreStitchedMp4` also checks the plan's format: separate audio no longer implies mp4 chunks.
- The v2 assembler downloads the audio task's file when the event carries `AudioS3Uri`, as the v1 assembler already does, and joins the chunks with it.
- No state machine change: the audio branch and the assembler's `AudioS3Uri` already do not depend on the format.

## Tests

- `handler.test.ts`: a webm or mov plan with free workers defers its audio, and the assembler joins the chunks with the audio task's bytes. The audio action mixes webm and mov audio and leaves cfr and png-sequence to the plan.
- `plan.test.ts`: webm and mov plans made with `deferAudio` record `separateAudio` and ship no `audio.m4a`; png-sequence keeps its own.
- Each change was broken on purpose and its tests went red: the gate back to mp4-only (3 handler tests and the plan test), no format check in the stitch decision (the webm assemble test), no download in the assembler (the webm and mov assemble tests).
- 3 runs in a row: `handler.test.ts` 36 pass, `plan.test.ts` + `assemble.test.ts` 84 pass, 0 fail each. Producer and aws-lambda typecheck clean; oxlint, oxfmt and fallow clean on the changed files.

## Pre-review (independent reviewer)

No blockers, no majors. Minors, all accepted as notes:

| Finding | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Mixed versions during a deploy: an old assembler given a new webm/mov plan takes the mp4 stitch path and fails | `assemble.ts` `chunksAreStitchedMp4` (old code) | Fails loudly, only for renders in flight while the plan and assemble functions run different versions; old plan with new assembler works |
| Assemble side covered webm only | `handler.test.ts` | Fixed: the test now runs for webm and mov |
| The plan's `HasAudio` is now false for webm/mov when the audio is deferred, as it already was for mp4 | `handler.ts` plan result | Nothing in the repo branches on it |

Audited: the handler, events, the CDK stack and the SAM example template, the producer plan, assemble and plan v2, every reader of `plansSeparateAudio`, `stitchesSeparateAudio`, `chunksAreStitchedMp4`, `separateAudio`, `AudioS3Uri` and `HasAudio`; each changed test file run alone (exit 0); four deliberate mutations, each caught; oxlint, oxfmt and fallow.
Not exercised by the reviewer: a real Lambda run, the real ffmpeg join of webm/mov chunks with a downloaded track, an arm64 plan, a rolling deploy.

## Live check

A 2-minute 1080p WebM-with-alpha render on two stacks (plan and chunks on an arm64 function, and on an x86 function; audio and assembly on x86 in both), 3 cold runs each, with this change on top of #6089:

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Audio, arm64-planned vs x86-planned | different (decoded null test peak about -30 dBFS) | byte-identical encoded stream on all 6 runs; null test silent |
| Picture | SSIM 0.99955, alpha plane 1.00000 | unchanged |
| Invocations per render | 13 | 14 (the audio task) |

The real join of webm chunks with the downloaded track and an arm64 plan are both exercised here; mov is covered by the unit tests only.

title: ci(windows): fail a hung engine-cli test step at its deadline and name the stuck process
body:
## Problem
On Windows, the `engine-cli` test step can hang. GitHub's `timeout-minutes: 16` did not stop it: in one merge-queue run the step was still running after 31 minutes and was only cancelled when the queue rebuilt; in a repro run (step limit 40 min) it ran until the 55 min job limit killed it. The step log is not retrievable after that, so the hung test is never named, and every hang costs the merge queue 30 to 55 minutes.

## Change
- `scripts/ci/run-with-deadline.ps1` runs the step's command under its own deadline. Output streams live to the job log. At the deadline it prints the process tree (pid, parent, name, age, command line), kills the tree with `taskkill /T /F` and exits 124, so the step fails at 16 minutes and says which process was left running.
- The step output also goes to a file that is uploaded as an artifact on every run (`if: always()`).
- `warmCheck.process.test.ts` now includes the cold `check` run's stdout and stderr in its failure message; before, the child's stderr was discarded, so a failing cold check (exit 1) gave no reason.

## Verification
- On a Windows runner, a step running `Start-Sleep 600` under `-Minutes 1` ended after 61 s (throwaway branch, workflow_dispatch).
- `warmCheck.process.test.ts` alone: 10 of 10 passes on Windows with CPU load, about 13 s each.
- Not yet shown: which test hangs. This PR is the instrument for that; the cause gets its own follow-up once a hang is caught with the dump.
- The `pwsh` script was not run locally (no PowerShell on the author's machine); the only execution is the Windows run above.

title: fix(engine): hundreds of effects in one audio group mix in time, and a mix timeout is named
body:
## What

A group (`data-audio-group`) of hundreds of short effects now mixes well inside the ffmpeg deadline, and when that deadline does kill a mix the error says it timed out.

## Why

An export of a 10-minute film with ~680 effects in one audio group failed with `audio_processing_failed ... FFmpeg exited with code 255` after about 5.5 minutes. Two defects:

- The group sub-mix padded every member to the full film length before summing, so its cost grew with members x film length. The ungrouped mix already sums first and pads once.
- The kill at `ffmpegProcessTimeout` was reported as a bare exit code with the stream-mapping lines of stderr. The failure reason was already `ffmpeg_timeout`, but the detail text never said so, because the audio mixer formatted the error itself instead of using `describeFfmpegFailure` as the other ffmpeg callers do.

## Related work

Follows the group sub-mix gain work that introduced `normalize=0` there. No overlapping PR.

## How

- `mixGroupMembers`: when `amix` supports `normalize=0`, members are no longer padded one by one; the sum is padded and trimmed once to the film length, as the main mix does. Members that end early add silence either way, so the output is the same. Old ffmpeg builds without `normalize` keep the per-member padding, because their input-count compensation needs it.
- `ffmpegFailure` now builds its detail with `describeFfmpegFailure`, so a deadline kill reads "FFmpeg timed out after N ms (ffmpegProcessTimeout; ... FFMPEG_PROCESS_TIMEOUT_MS)" ahead of the stderr tail. Its callers pass the timeout they already hold.

Measured end to end through `processCompositionAudio` on the same machine, 680 members of 0.4 s spread over a 600 s film, one group: 482 s before, 107 s after (the deadline is 300 s by default). That time still includes preparing each member file; the group graph itself no longer scales with film length per member.

## Test plan

- `audioMixer.test.ts`: the group graph has one `apad`, after the sum (fails on main: `adelay=...,apad` on every member); a group sub-mix killed at the deadline reports "FFmpeg timed out after 300000 ms" with the env var named (fails on main: "FFmpeg exited with code 255").
- `src/services/audioMixer*` 6 files, 109 tests pass, including the real-ffmpeg grouped-versus-flat level checks that guard the unity sum. Typecheck, lint and format hooks pass.

body:
## What

`hyperframes check` now makes the browser-playable copy of an HEVC/ProRes video at the size that fills the composition, instead of at the source size. A 4K clip in a 1920x1080 project is copied at 2573x1448 (the composition's box on the preview size ladder) rather than 3840x2160. Copies for preview and publish are unchanged. It also clears partial copies that a stopped process left behind, once they have been untouched for 10 minutes (the old limit was an hour).

Two more changes cover a clip too long to copy inside a caller's time limit: a source over 90 seconds is copied in one-minute pieces that stay in the cache, so a stopped copy continues from its finished pieces instead of starting over; and `hyperframes check --prepare-media` makes only the copies and exits (no browser, no report), so a caller can run that step first without the check's time limit.

## Why

A check on a long 4K60 HEVC project spent its time in "making browser-playable copies". The copy re-encodes every frame at the source size, and a stopped run (a runner time limit, a closed terminal) throws the partial copy away, so the next run starts again. The page the check opens asks for a copy that fills the composition, so the 4K pixels were never needed there.

On the devbox (8 cores) a 4K60 HEVC copy runs at about 0.6x realtime, so 400 s of footage takes about 11 minutes at the source size.

## How

- The check server (`serveStaticProjectHtml`) now reads `hf-proxy-box` the way Studio's preview route does and asks `resolveProxy` for that copy. Before, it always asked for the source-size copy, so the page's request would have missed the boxed copy made up front. An invalid box, or a box without `hf-proxy`, answers 404 as in the preview route. This is the one place the page's request and the up-front copy now share a cache key. The seven callers of the server (check, snapshot, validate, compare and the others) now get boxed copies for the box their page asks for, the same copies Studio makes.
- `preResolveHostileMediaProxies` finds the composition's size (`findCompositionDimensions`), rounds it up the existing preview size ladder (`quantizePreviewProxyBox`, now exported from `@hyperframes/core`) and asks for that box. The cache-hit check uses the same box, so a repeat check finds the copy.
- `resolveProxies` takes an optional `box` per source and passes it to `resolveProxy`, which already names and sizes a boxed copy.
- `resolveProxies` first sweeps its cache folder for dead partial copies (`.tmp-*` untouched for 10 minutes, or less if `HYPERFRAMES_PROXY_CACHE_STALE_TEMP_MS` is set lower). A copy being written keeps growing its file, so a live one is kept; a copy whose ffmpeg is suspended for 10 minutes (a laptop asleep) loses its partial and is made again.
- A project with no composition size, or a video larger than the stage on the page, behaves as before.
- **Server pre-warm.** `serveStaticProjectHtml` pre-warms copies when it opens; it now asks for the page's box (`findStageProxyBox`, the same helper the up-front copy uses) instead of the source-size copy, so a check no longer starts a full-size encode next to Chrome. The other six callers of the server get the same.
- **Idle deadline.** The check no longer ends 120 s after Chrome was ready whatever it is doing. `CheckDeadline` is an idle clock: every phase entered, every sample finished, every operation that settles and every overlap batch restarts the 120 s window, and the check ends only after 120 s with none. The overlap pass was one page call over every time (up to ~240) with no way to report progress, which is where a ~70 s 1080x1920 project with 8 sub-compositions ran out at ~104 s while three `--range` slices passed; it now asks the driver for batches of eight and reports between them. A hung page still ends 120 s after its last progress, and the message reads "no progress for 120 s after Chrome was ready".
- **Resumable pieces.** A source longer than 90 seconds is encoded in one-minute pieces (`-ss/-t`), each written under a temp name and renamed to a stable `.part-<key>-<n>` name when finished, then joined with the concat demuxer without re-encoding. A copy that is killed, aborted or out of its 15 minute budget loses at most the piece in flight, and the next run (check, preview or publish, since they share the one transcoder) continues from the first missing piece. Shorter sources keep the single pass. Finished pieces are swept after an hour untouched and never while their copy is running (the 10 minute limit above applies to temp files only, otherwise it would delete the first pieces of a long copy still encoding).
- **`check --prepare-media [--json]`.** Makes only the copies, bounded per file by the existing 15 minute limit, then exits: no browser, no report, same project lock as a check, honors `--proxy/--no-proxy`. `--json` prints `{ ok, prepared: [{ file, state: "ready" | "cached" | "failed", reason? }], total, ready, failed }`; progress stays on stderr. Exit 0 when every copy is ready, 1 when any failed. Documented in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.

## Evidence

Synthetic 30 s 4K60 HEVC clip with audio in a 1920x1080 project; `hyperframes check` built from main and from this branch on the same 8-core machine (the branch run was on a busier machine):

| | main | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| copy made before the page opens | 49.8 s | 32.0 s |
| size of the copy | 145 MB | 39 MB |
| files in the cache after the check | 1 | 1 |
| requests the page made for its copy | 23 | 18, answered from the boxed copy |
| whole check | 58 s | 42 s |
| second check (copy reused) | not measured | 8 s |

About 1.5 to 1.9x less time for a 1080p composition (the ladder rounds 1080p up to 2573x1448, not 1080p); a 4K composition gets no change. For 400 s of 4K60 that is roughly 6 minutes instead of 11 on this machine, so a slower machine can still pass a runner's limit. Resumable pieces and `--prepare-media` are covered below.

Resumable pieces, synthetic 200 s 1080p HEVC with audio, Linux, ffmpeg 7.0:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Uninterrupted, 4 pieces | 50.4 s; 6000 video frames, container 200.02 s |
| Process and ffmpeg killed at 22 s, then rerun | rerun 29.1 s (22 + 29 is about 51: no restart); 6000 frames, 200.02 s, same size as the uninterrupted copy |
| Real `check --prepare-media --json`, stopped at 25 s, rerun | rerun 35 s, `state: ready`, exit 0; a third run reports `cached` in 3 ms |

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `checkBrowser.test.ts`: the copy is requested at the composition's box (2048x1448 for 1920x1080) and the cache check uses the same box. Fails without the fix.
- `proxyTranscoder.test.ts`: `resolveProxies` makes a batch's copy at the box it is given, under that box's own cache name; and it removes an 11-minute-old partial while keeping a 1-minute-old one. Both fail without the fix.
- `staticProjectServer.test.ts`: a page request with `hf-proxy-box=2048x1448` resolves that box; an invalid box and a box without `hf-proxy` answer 404. Fail without the change.
- Each of the five failed without the change and passes with it; studio-server (53 tests), `checkBrowser` and `staticProjectServer` (82) passed 3 runs in a row. `tsc` for cli, studio-server and core, oxlint, oxfmt, fallow and the commit hooks pass.

- Pieces: the rerun encodes only the missing pieces, then joins and leaves only the final file; a short source stays one pass; stale pieces are swept after an hour but not while their copy runs; `--prepare-media` enters through `createCheckCommand` (no check pipeline call, JSON shape, exit 1 on a failed copy). Removing the "skip a finished piece" line turns the resume test red (`expected [ '0', '60', '0', '60', '120' ] to deeply equal [ '0', '60', '60', '120' ]`); removing the in-flight guard turns the sweep test red. cli check tests (170) and studio-server helpers (523) passed 3 runs in a row; typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt and fallow pass.

Pre-warm: `mediaProxyPreview.test.ts` (the real pre-warm passes the box to `resolveProxy`) and `staticProjectServer.test.ts` (opening the server passes the composition's box to the injection); putting the unboxed call back turns both red. Idle deadline: new tests in `checkDeadline.test.ts` (keeps going while steps make progress then ends; a settled operation restarts the clock; the message names the phase) and `check.test.ts` (a 10-minute-class overlap pass and slow samples that each finish complete without `check_runtime_failure`). Each fails when its piece is removed: enter() no longer restarting the clock (8 red), overlap grid in one call (1 red), no per-sample progress (1 red). 136 tests green x3 including the real-Chrome process tests (`checkDeadline.process.test.ts`), tsc clean. Not exercised: a 4K60 source through the pieces, audio by ear at piece joins (frame count and duration only; the audio ends 21 ms long over 3 joins), a caller that SIGKILLs only the CLI (its ffmpeg runs to the end of the current piece and its temp file is swept after the limit), a 4K composition, a project whose videos are larger than the stage, and any Windows run.







## Size budget
`@hyperframes/studio-server` packed budget 141718 -> 142100 bytes (+382). The resumable 60 s copy pieces (`proxyTranscoder.ts`, `proxyCache.ts`) are real shipped code; packed size was 142043 (+325 over).

title: fix(core): capture blur strobing, backdrop box, glow drop-out and callback motion
body:
## What

Four fixes to capture motion blur, found by rendering Jake's eight comparison shots ("Motion blur, two ways") on the merged code and fixing each place it lost.

1. **Strobing at default settings.** A fast move used a fixed 16 taps, so a 120 px smear had 8 px steps. With no `data-motion-blur-samples`, taps are now sized to the smear (about one per 2 px, 2 to 128); an explicit count still wins.
2. **Lighter card body.** Canvas quantizes `globalAlpha` to 1/255 when drawing an image, so 1/n tap weights left coverage short (n = 104 summed to 0.81). Weights are now whole 1/255 units that sum to exactly 255. This also affected the old thinned and explicit counts.
3. **A lighter box behind text and a hard-edged box around a glow; glow and shadow dropped out.** The crop came from a capture of the whole scene, so the backdrop under a see-through mover smeared with it, and ink outside the mover's box was cut off. Each frame now captures the movers alone on a transparent layer (everything else `visibility:hidden`), and the crop grows by the mover's ink reach (box-shadow, text-shadow, filter, outline, measured during the scan).
4. **Callback-driven motion was never found.** The scan always seeked with callbacks suppressed, so a `render(t)` driven from `onUpdate` reported 0 movers even with `data-motion-blur-events="on"`. With events on, the scan now seeks the way frame reads do. Without it nothing changes.

## Notes for review

- Chrome 152 draws a mover with a rotate or scale transform at the origin, untransformed, when its **root** is `visibility:hidden`. Translation is fine. The isolation therefore keeps the root visible (background, border, shadow and outline cleared) and hides everything beneath it except the movers. There is a real-browser test for rotate and scale that fails if the root is hidden again.
- A frame is still two paints. The output is cleared on wrap instead of showing the previous wrap's last frame, since the first paint is no longer a drawable sharp frame (a blank for about two paints at play start in preview).
- The engine's forced finish before the background capture now falls back to a plain-DOM frame (counted in `failedFrames`) rather than a half frame.
- The scan contract changed on purpose: with `-events="on"` it fires timeline callbacks. Authors who opt into events already get callbacks at arbitrary sub-frame times.
- Core's unpacked size budget goes to 3,950,000 for the new `ink.ts` module (a later PR in this stack raises it again for the filter tier).

## Evidence

Rendered Jake's eight shots before and after (frames named in his notes):
- whip frame 34: the stair-stepped edge becomes a smooth ramp; the card body no longer lightens.
- waterfall frame 24: the lighter box and erased background dots are gone.
- glow frame 10 and 20: the glow smears with the button and the hard-edged box is gone.
- `render(t)` frame 13: 1 mover found (was 0) with events on.

## Tests

- Core runtime 163 tests; engine real-Chrome pixel tests (new: backdrop untouched under a see-through mover, glow carried along, rotate and scale kept in place). Each new guard was broken on purpose and a test failed: tap spacing, tap weights, the isolation CSS, the ink pad, the visible-root rule, the callback scan.
- Not run: the 400-composition corpus.

Stack: this is the bottom of three (quality fixes, then the filter fallback, then the automatic tier and defaults). Review bottom-up.

title: feat(core): capture blur falls back to per-element filters where capture cannot run
body:
## What

When capture cannot run, blur no longer turns off for the whole composition. It hands over to a **filter tier**: an SVG filter on each mover, 32 offset copies averaged along its sampled path (in pairs, so 8-bit buffers do not band), softened along the motion so a long smear does not step. It filters the live DOM, so it works over a WebGL canvas, in any Chrome, and leaves a mover's glow and shadow on the element. Turn and scale only soften (capture draws those truthfully, so it stays the first choice).

Capture cannot run when: a WebGL/WebGPU canvas is in the page, a transform or opacity or blend mode is on the root, an iframe/object/embed is in the root, `backface-visibility: hidden` sits in a 3D context, a nested capture canvas exists, the browser lacks html-in-canvas, or capture failed three times in a row in preview. The renderer's explicit off (HDR, distributed, engine blur) stays off. A scene re-init tries capture again.

## How it fits

- `tier.ts`: shared `Tier` interface, `Report` (gains `tier`), `chooseTier` (pure, tested).
- `filterPlan.ts`: pure arithmetic (offsets, softening, region) from a mover's sampled path.
- `filterTier.ts`: the DOM layer and the tier. `frames.ts`: pose reading shared with capture.
- `index.ts`: picks the tier at init and hands over when a scan turns capture off. The window report names the tier.

## Evidence

- WebGL shot (Jake's "webgl", frame 34): was entirely sharp (capture logged `off reasonCode=accelerated-canvas`); now blurred with the live gradient behind it, matching his render.
- Real-Chrome pixel test over a page with a WebGL canvas: trail present, centroid within 2 px of the sharp frame, ink conserved within 10%. Mutation-tested: disabling the fallback and skipping the filter aim each fail it.

## Notes for review

- A test-only switch (`setFilterFallbackForTests`) lets the existing capture-tier defect tests keep judging capture alone.
- Core's budgets go to 3,965,000 unpacked / 1,645,000 packed for the tier.
- The complexity gate (fallow) is clean for the new code; one inherited finding (`useRenderQueue`) is unchanged.

Stacked on `feat/capture-blur-quality`.

title: feat: automatic tier, 240°/32 defaults, check finding, and Studio stops opting out
body:
## What

1. **`hyperframes check`** reports `motion_blur_filter_fallback` (info) when the filter tier draws because capture could not run, with the cause and the way back. The engine's per-session log line gains `tier=`.
2. **Studio stops sending `previewMotionBlur`.** Every Chrome can preview blur now (the fallback covers browsers without html-in-canvas), so a render no longer has to be switched off to match a preview that could not blur. The server still accepts `false` from an older Studio.
3. **Automatic tier.** The scan notes whether any mover turns or scales (the linear part of its transform chain changes) and whether it already forms its own stacking context while it moves. When every mover only translates, the filter tier draws as well as capture and costs about what no blur costs. Anything that turns or scales, or moves without a transform, stays on capture. `data-motion-blur-tier="capture"` or `"filter"` forces a tier. `check` stays quiet for these two choices.
4. **Defaults match the shutter blur Jake built:** 240° (was 180°) and at least 32 samples (more for a long smear).
5. **Docs and skill note** describe the two tiers, the attribute, the measured cost and the findings.

## Evidence

Cost, 8 s bench (four whips), wall time including startup, two runs each: no blur 5.3–5.9 s, Jake's filter 5.4 s, ours automatic 5.2–5.4 s, capture forced 9.8 s.

Distance from Jake's own render at his settings (PSNR, higher is closer), default settings: whip 51.0 dB (was 34.6), glow 51.2, waterfall 55.7 (was 39.9), WebGL 50.6. Spin 28.2 and crash zoom 29.4 stay apart on purpose: capture streaks along the arc or zoom where his softens the whole element.

The real-Chrome pixel tests run the shared assertions (trail shape, centroid, ink conservation, backdrop untouched, glow carried, centred box) through both tiers.

## Behaviour changes to be aware of

- New public attribute `data-motion-blur-tier`.
- The automatic choice changes which tier most translation-only compositions use. It has been checked on the eight shots only; the corpus run is still to do. Blur stays opt-in (`data-motion-blur="on"`).
- A preview in a browser without html-in-canvas uses the filter tier, so a spin looks softer there than in the render. Force a tier for an exact match.

Rebased onto `main` after #6106 and #6107 merged.

## No visible change

The only Studio edit removes the 8 lines in `useRenderQueue.ts` that sent `previewMotionBlur` with a render, and its test. Blur now picks its tier from the page, so nothing on screen moves.

title: perf(studio): an idle editor stops waking the GPU four times a second
body:
## What

The overlay frame loop's safety-net poll (`IDLE_POLL_MS`, `overlayFrameLoop.ts`) requested one animation frame every 250 ms for as long as an editor stayed open. Each frame request restarts the display's vsync (a fresh `CVDisplayLink` on macOS) for a few frames, so a paused, untouched editor kept the GPU process waking ~65 times a second, the main idle battery cost in HyperFrames Desktop with a project open.

Now the poll:
- doubles its wait after each idle frame, 250 ms → 4 s (`MAX_IDLE_POLL_MS`), and resets to 250 ms on any wake. A missed wake is likeliest right after activity (a CSS transition no event reports), which is when the poll is still fast.
- stops while `document.hidden`; `visibilitychange` is already a wake source.

## No visible change

The overlays track the same geometry on the same wake sources; only how often an idle, untouched editor polls changes. Under 20 source lines, no .tsx/.css/.html.

## Measured

HyperFrames Desktop at `origin/main` (studio 0.8.186), paused project, 20 s of `app.getAppMetrics()` per run, M4 Pro. Baseline vs this change applied to the same 0.8.186 dist (two runs):

- GPU process idle wakeups: 167/s → 24 and 31/s
- Renderer idle wakeups: 40/s → 13 and 18/s
- App CPU: 0.84% → 0.38 and 0.41%

Home and playback are unchanged (other sources dominate there). Earlier isolation on the same build: removing only this loop's idle rAFs took a paused project's GPU wakeups from 85/s to 20/s. Method and charts: https://www.heygenverse.com/a/efa8d156-d36a-4c3e-80c7-c9b1a4f07dcf

## Tests

Two new cases in `overlayFrameLoop.test.ts`: the poll backs off and comes back fast after a wake, and no poll is armed while hidden. Both fail on `main` (47 polls in 12 s idle, where ≤4 is expected; 31 polls while hidden, where ≤1 is expected). All 15 pass with the change.

## Not exercised

No Studio walk in a browser; the measurement is Desktop's embedded Studio. A missed wake source now costs up to 4 s of overlay staleness after long idle instead of 250 ms; none was seen, but the wake sources were not exhaustively audited.

title: docs(cli): apply review notes from #5442 to open, timeline and history
body:
## What

Applies the three optional notes @jrusso1020 left on #5442 to the CLI reference (`docs/packages/cli.mdx`). #5442 auto-merged before I got to them.

## Why

Each note corrects something the page states:

1. **`open`**: the desktop hand-off is macOS-only for now (`HANDOFF_READY = process.platform === "darwin"` in `packages/cli/src/utils/desktopApp.ts`), so on Windows and Linux `open` always exits 1 with the download link. The page didn't say so.
2. **`timeline apply --plan`**: in text mode it prints only a count (`planned 1 file`, `a2Commands.ts`); the result and diff come with `--json`. The flag table said every `--plan` prints the result and the diff, which is true of the single verbs only.
3. **`history undo --who`**: it undoes what is still in effect from that name's *last* turn, and refuses (rather than falling back to an older turn) when nothing from that turn is still in effect (`turnTargets` in `history.ts`). The table said "that name's newest turn still in effect", which reads like the fallback.

## Related work

Follow-up to #5442 (review comments) · Refs #5386

## How

Three wording changes in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`: one sentence after the `open --json` paragraph, and one cell each in the `timeline` flag table and the `history` command table. No other files.

## Test plan

- [x] Checked each statement against current `main` and ran them with the CLI built from `main` on a fresh `hyperframes init` project:
  - `timeline apply plan.json --plan` prints `planned 1 file`; `--plan --json` returns `before`, `after` and `diff`, and nothing is written.
  - `history undo --who claude` with no entries from that name refuses with `claude has no entry still in effect`.
  - `open --json` without the app installed exits 1 with `reason: "not-installed"` and the `downloadUrl` (macOS). The Windows/Linux behaviour is from the `HANDOFF_READY` check; I don't have those machines to run it on.
- [x] `node scripts/check-docs-cli-commands.mjs`, `bun run check:docs-snippet-motion` and `check:studio-copy-dashes` pass.
- [x] `npx mint broken-links --check-redirects` passes (in `docs/`, Node 22). `mint validate` hung locally at "validating build…" without reporting an error, so I'm relying on the docs workflow for it.
- [x] Documentation updated

title: test(cli): process tests stop owning old processes that carry a reused parent pid on Windows
body:
## Problem

The Windows engine-cli lane fails now and then on process tests that wait for a Chrome or its watchdog to exit (`chromeOrphans.process.test.ts`, "Condition not met within 10000 ms").

At one such timeout the live process list had no Chrome and no watchdog. The pids the test was still waiting on belonged to an unrelated, minutes-old CI helper process, which the test had recorded as a descendant of the CLI.

Windows keeps a dead parent's pid in `ParentProcessId` and never reparents. Once a new process reuses that number, every older orphan that carried it looks like that new process's child. `testProcessDescendants` matched children by `ParentProcessId` alone, so it adopted them, then waited for them to exit, and `stopTestProcesses` would have killed them.

## Fix

A child cannot be older than its parent. `ownedDescendants` drops a process whose creation time is before its parent's, and everything below it. The Windows listing the helper already reads now includes the creation time, so there is no extra query. Linux reparents orphans to init and macOS has no start in this listing, so both keep matching on the parent pid.

## Verification

- New `processTestUtils.test.ts`: an older process carrying a reused parent pid, and its own child, are not owned; a normal tree is; a listing without start times behaves as before. With the creation-time condition removed the first test fails (`expected [ 200, 300, 400 ] to deeply equal [ 200 ]`); restored, all three pass.
- Devbox (Linux), workspace built: `processTestUtils`, `warmCheck.process`, `chromeOrphans.process` and `checkDeadline.process` pass together, 18 of 18.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and the comment ratchet are clean.
- Not run here: the Windows branch of the listing (`CreationDate.Ticks`); the Windows lane on this PR is its first run.

title: feat(studio): motion blur panel with Off / Subtle / Strong
body:
## What
A **Motion blur** tab in Studio's right dock with one three-way control: **Off / Subtle / Strong**.

- **Subtle** is the default blur: 240° shutter, samples sized to the smear.
- **Strong** is the maximum: 720° shutter, 64 samples.
- **Off** removes `data-motion-blur` and leaves the other attributes alone.

It writes the root attributes through the SDK, so a render uses the same setting and Undo works. It reads the live preview root, so it follows undo and outside edits. Locked with a note when a sub-composition is open (blur is read from the main root).

Adds `@hyperframes/core/motion-blur-settings` (attribute names, limits, parse and write helpers); the capture runtime now reads its config through it so editors and runtime share defaults.

Rebased onto `main` after #6106 to #6108 merged. The dock tab is titled **Blur**: with five tabs, "Motion blur" overflowed the default dock width by 10px.

## Verified
- Real Studio: Subtle wrote `data-motion-blur="on"`; Strong added shutter 720 and samples 64.
- Full check run: tsc, size budgets, 7753 tests; panel tests mutation-checked.

## Before

The fifth tab ("Motion blur") is clipped at the default dock width.

![Before: the Motion blur tab is clipped](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/evidence/blur-tab/shots/before.jpg?raw=1)

## After

The tab is titled Blur and fits; the panel shows Off / Subtle / Strong.

![After: the Blur tab fits](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/evidence/blur-tab/shots/after.jpg?raw=1)

title: fix(lint): tell an agent where to move a video nested in a timed wrapper
body:
## What

`media_missing_data_start` told an agent to add `data-start="0"` to a `<video>`/`<audio>` even when the element sits inside a timed wrapper. Doing so trips `video_nested_in_timed_element` ("time the wrapper OR the video, never both"), so an agent following the hint loops.

## Fix

When a timed element still encloses the media, the hint now names that wrapper and its start, and says to move the media out as a direct child of the stage with the wrapper's `data-start` and its `data-duration`. The direct case keeps the plain `data-start="0"` hint. The enclosing-wrapper check is now one helper shared by both rules, so they cannot disagree about what counts as nested.

The refusal itself is unchanged and correct: an untimed nested video would play on the root clock.

## Test

`media.test.ts`: the nested repro gets a hint naming the wrapper; applying that hint lints clean of both codes; the direct case is unchanged. Fails on main (117 pass, 1 fail), passes here (118 of 118).

title: feat(cli): check --prepare-media makes the video copies alone, and a stopped copy resumes
body:
## What

`hyperframes check --prepare-media` makes only the browser-playable video copies and exits, and a copy that is stopped continues from its finished pieces instead of starting over.

## Why

A long HEVC or ProRes video can take longer to copy into a browser-playable file than a caller allows a check to run. The copy was then killed, left a half-written temp file, and the next check started over from zero, so such a project could never finish checking from a caller with a short clock.

## Related work

Stacked on #6104 (same copy path); retarget to `main` when it merges.

## How

- `hyperframes check --prepare-media [--json]` makes only those copies and exits. It opens no browser and writes no report, and each file stays bounded by the existing 15 minute transcode limit. `--json` prints `{ ok, prepared: [{ file, state: "ready" | "cached" | "failed", reason? }], total, ready, failed }`; progress stays on stderr. Exit code is 0 when every copy is ready, 1 when any failed. It honors `--proxy/--no-proxy` and takes the same project lock as a check.
- A source longer than 90 seconds is now copied in one-minute pieces, each finished piece kept under a stable name in the cache, then joined without re-encoding. A copy that is killed, aborted or out of budget loses at most the piece in flight, and the next run (prepare or a normal check or preview) continues from the first missing piece. This lives in the one place every caller of the copy goes through, so preview and publish gain it too. Shorter sources keep the single pass they had.
- Stale pieces (older than an hour) are swept with the existing temp-file sweep.

## Test plan

Synthetic 200 s 1080p HEVC with audio, on Linux with ffmpeg 7.0:

| Run | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Uninterrupted, 4 pieces | 50.4 s; 6000 video frames, container 200.02 s |
| Process and ffmpeg killed at 22 s, then rerun | rerun 29.1 s (22 + 29 is about 51: no restart); 6000 frames, 200.02 s, same bytes as the uninterrupted copy |
| Real `check --prepare-media --json`, stopped at 25 s, rerun | rerun 35 s, `state: ready`, exit 0; a third run reports `cached` in 3 ms |

Tests: new cases for piece resume (the rerun encodes only the missing pieces, then joins and leaves only the final file), short sources staying one pass, stale-piece sweep, and `--prepare-media` entering through `createCheckCommand` (no check pipeline call, JSON shape, exit 1 on a failed copy). title: fix(engine): render into a folder whose name holds a percent sign
body:
## What

A render whose folder name holds a `%` followed by a letter (for example `12% Up`) failed every video render with "Cannot write more than one file with the same name" / `VIDEO_SOURCE_UNRENDERABLE`.

## Cause

ffmpeg reads an image-sequence path as a printf template. The frame-extraction work directory sits next to the output (`work-<id>-…` on Linux), so its `%` reached the template and `% U` parsed as a format code.

## Fix

One helper, `frameSequencePath(dir, pattern)`, doubles the `%` in the folder part. Every place that joins a folder with a frame pattern uses it: frame extraction output, the two frame-sequence encoders, and the GIF encoder input. Checked by grep: no other `%0Nd` / `%05d` pattern is built from a path. The HLS packager already refuses a `%` folder because that muxer ignores `%%`.

## Test

- Extraction into `x 12% Up` (real ffmpeg): fails on main, passes here.
- Encode from a `x 12% Up` frames folder (real ffmpeg): fails without the helper, passes with it.
- GIF input path doubles the `%`.
- The existing extractor, encoder, GIF and encode-stage tests still pass.

title: fix(producer): long renders with small frames no longer fail the up-front disk estimate
body:
## What
Disk capture no longer throws from the static pre-capture estimate. The measured projection (first 10 frames, real bytes) remains the only disk gate.

## Why
The estimate prices PNG frames as raw RGBA (width x height x 4) and JPEG at 1/8 of that. A long, mostly transparent PNG overlay (for example a caption layer over a 15 to 20 minute video) is estimated at hundreds of GB and refused up front, although its frames are a few KB each. Renders of this shape failed with `Disk capture may need ~261273.6 MB ... but only 250069.7 MB is free` while writing almost nothing.

A render that truly cannot fit is still stopped after ten frames by `createDiskCaptureProjection`, with the same error text and `--workers 1` remedy.

## Test
New `runCaptureStage` case: a png render whose raw estimate (327 KB) exceeds free space (100 KB) but whose frames are 100 bytes captures all 20 frames. It fails on main with the exact error above and passes here; `captureStage.test.ts` passes 3 runs in a row (20 tests). The old test that asserted the up-front throw is removed with `assertDiskCaptureHeadroom`; `inspectDiskCaptureHeadroom` stays for fallback planning.

## Known trade-off
A render whose first ten frames are much smaller than later ones can pass the projection and run out of disk later. Before this change the same render was refused outright.

title: fix(aws-lambda): keep the arm64 image staging script out of the published package
body:
The v0.8.187 publish job stopped in `verify:packed-manifests`: with the release's `prebuilt/` files added, `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` measured 73484 bytes packed and 267013 unpacked, over its budgets of 73369 and 266805.

`scripts/stage-arm64-image.ts` ships in the package but only runs from a checkout (the image workflow and the publish job). Nothing in `dist` or the CLI imports it, so this keeps it out of the tarball, the same as `pin-handler-zip.ts`. The budgets stay as they are.

Measured on a built tree with `prebuilt/` generated by the real template writer and stand-in pin manifests, `npm pack --dry-run`: 73022 packed and 267570 unpacked before, 71425 and 262974 after (-1597 B and -4596 B). The publish job reads about 460 B higher packed and 560 B lower unpacked than these local numbers, so it should land near 71885 and 262417.

The PR-time check could not catch this: the publish job adds the two release pins (`prebuilt/handler-zip.json`, `prebuilt/video-image.json`) before `verify:packed-manifests`, and the Build job did not. The verifier now runs the same pin script on sparse stand-ins of release size when no pins exist (and removes them afterwards), so both runs pack the same file list.

Proof, on a full build with the stand-in pins: with main's file list the check fails with aws-lambda unpacked 267013 (the exact figure the publish job reported) over 266805, packed 73405 over 73369; with the exclusion it passes (`Verified 14 packages are within their size budgets`).

## No visible change

Package file list and one CI step only.

title: fix(runtime): a composition script that shadows console no longer breaks the render runtime
body:
## What
The runtime bundle now reads `console` through `globalThis.console` (one esbuild `define`, shared by the IIFE and ESM builds).

## Why
A classic script with a top-level `const console = document.getElementById("box")` creates a global lexical binding that hides `window.console` from every later script in the page, including the runtime. The first `console.info(...)` in the runtime then throws `console.info is not a function`, and the render fails with `HyperFrames runtime failed: TypeError: console.info is not a function`. Generated compositions do this (a variable named after a UI "console" panel).

## Test
- Repro: a one-element composition with `const console = document.getElementById('box')` and a paused GSAP timeline. On main, `hyperframes render` fails with the error above; with this change it renders to 100%.
- `hyperframesRuntime.engine.test.ts` asserts the built runtime calls `globalThis.console.info(`. It fails without the `define` and passes 3 runs in a row.

## Not covered
The sub-composition script wrapper in `compositionScoping.ts` has its own `console.error` in a generated string; esbuild does not rewrite strings; it is left for a follow-up if it proves reachable.

title: fix(engine): mix any number of audio clips by summing them in stages
body:
## What

A project with a very large number of audio clips could fail its export while mixing. One ffmpeg graph held every clip of a group (or of the whole film) as its own input, and one process had a fixed 300 s deadline.

## Measured (devbox, ffmpeg 7.0.2, 4 CPUs, real ffmpeg)

- 2000 inputs in one graph at the default open-file limit of 1024: exit 232 "Too many open files" at once. 401 inputs pass at 1024 and fail at a limit of 300. The production worker's limit and ffmpeg build are not known, and the reported 401-clip project passes on this host, so this is the failure class, not proof of the production cause.
- 600 clips in one group on a 1124.5 s film: a single flat graph ran 130 s in one ffmpeg process (a 300 s deadline is only 2.3x away). Staged: the longest single process ran 12 s; the whole audio stage 59 s.
- 400 sequential clips, whole audio stage: staged 3.2 s, flat 3.9 s.

## Fix

- No cap on the clip count. Past 96 clips in one mix, slices of 96 are summed at unity gain (the group sub-mix gain law) into one running float sum, so only a few full-length files exist at once. This covers the group sub-mix and the whole-film mix, the two places that build one graph from all their inputs. A mix of 96 or fewer takes the same single-graph path as before.
- A mix process's deadline is the larger of the configured one and 100 ms per film second (about 9x the measured cost), so a very long film is not killed by a fixed 300 s.
- A failed mix keeps how long ffmpeg ran, its limit, the exit code and signal, and the last lines of its stderr (the detail was cut from the end, dropping the last words; it now keeps both ends).

## Tests (all with the fix; the first and last fail without it)

- With ffmpeg mocked, a 2000-clip film (grouped and ungrouped) never gives one ffmpeg process more than 96 inputs. Fails on main (one process with 2000).
- Real ffmpeg: 200 clips in a group and 200 ungrouped mix and land at the level of a short mix.
- Real ffmpeg: 120 stacked clips past the slice size read the same float sum as 60 clips at twice the gain (one flat graph), grouped and ungrouped; a wrong stem gain turns both red.
- A killed group mix keeps its run time and ffmpeg's last stderr line.
- The deadline grows with film length and stays 300 s for short films.
- The 150-track command-line-length test now expects two slice sums, one fold and the final mix.

The real-ffmpeg cases are sized to add about 15 s on the devbox: the runtime shard already takes about 8 of its 10 minutes.

title: fix(producer): a blank media src is no source instead of the page itself
body:
## What
`discoverMediaFromBrowser` reports an empty source for a media element whose own `src` is blank and that has no `<source src>` child.

## Why
In Chrome, `video.src` for `<video src="">` reads back as the composition page URL. The browser media discovery passed that on, the producer stripped the file-server prefix to `index.html`, and the media preflight sniffed the composition as the video's file. The render then failed before capture with `N media source(s) are text documents (HTML/XML/JSON), not media containers [elements=...]`, naming an element that never had a source. Generated compositions contain stray `<video src="">` placeholders, so this blocked whole renders for an element that plays nothing.

## Test
- Repro: a composition with `<video src="" style="display:none">` inside a box. On main `hyperframes render` fails with the error above; with this change it renders to 100% (with a `media_load_failed` warning for the empty element).
- New `htmlCompiler.test.ts` case: with the browser reporting the page URL for a blank src, discovery returns `""` for it and still returns the real source for a normal element. It fails on main (`Expected: "" / Received: "http://localhost:4000/index.html"`) and passes 3 runs in a row; the whole file passes (151).

title: fix(studio-server): the history lock works on drives without hard links
body:
## What
Taking the project-history owner lock links a prepared file into place. On drives that refuse hard links (exFAT, some network and cloud drives) that call fails with ENOTSUP/EPERM, `claim()` rethrew it, and `hyperframes check --json` passed but its report could not be recorded.

## Fix
When the link is refused with ENOTSUP, EOPNOTSUPP, ENOSYS or EPERM, `claim()` creates `owner.pid` exclusively (`wx`) instead. Without the hard-link step the file briefly exists empty, so a reader now waits on an empty lock younger than 2 s rather than evicting it; an older empty lock (crashed claimant) is still cleared.

## Tests
`ownerLock.test.ts` stubs `linkSync` to fail with each code and checks: the lock is taken and released, a live owner is still refused, a dead owner is taken over, a fresh empty lock is waited on, a stale empty lock is cleared.

title: fix(engine): encode with the same x264 and x265 thread count on any host size
body:
## What

The same captured frames encoded to different bytes on different host sizes, and chunks of one distributed render could differ. libx264 and libx265 take their thread count from the host core count when ffmpeg is not given one (x264 uses 1.5 x the cores), and their bitstream depends on that count.

## Measured (devbox, 6 CPUs via taskset, 5 s 1080p noisy fixture, ffmpeg 8.0)

- x264 medium, `-threads` 4 / 6 / 8 / 12 / 24 and auto: six different video md5s. x264 ultrafast and x265 medium: also a different md5 per thread count.
- Encode wall time, median of 3, auto vs this change (threads = CPU quota):

| CPUs | preset | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | medium | 17.96 s | 16.80 s |
| 6 | ultrafast | 2.95 s | 2.91 s |
| 8 | medium | 16.89 s | 17.23 s |
| 8 | ultrafast | 4.50 s | 3.11 s |

The box is shared and noisy (single runs vary by about 15 percent), so read it as no measurable increase, not a speedup. x265 medium measured 40 s at every thread count.

## Fix

Both software encoders (chunk encode and streaming encode, the two places that build these arguments) now pass `-threads` from `os.availableParallelism()`, which Node reads from the container CPU quota. Two pods with the same quota produce the same bytes on any node size. Hardware encoders and the other codecs are untouched.

Known limit: a pod of a different size, or a laptop, gets a different thread count and so different bytes. Only a constant would remove that, at the cost of using fewer or more threads than the machine has.

## Test

`softwareEncoderThreads.test.ts`: the thread argument tracks the quota, not the host core count, for h264 and h265 in both encoders; and a real ffmpeg encode of the production arguments gives identical bytes on a 2-core and a 7-core host (taskset). All five fail without the change.


## Size budget

`@hyperframes/engine` packed budget goes from 428347 to 428562 bytes (+215): the `softwareEncoderThreads` module and its two call sites are the whole difference on top of main. `verify:packed-manifests` passes at this head with current main merged in.

title: fix(producer): fetch inlined remote scripts under a public-network policy
body:
## What

`inlineExternalScripts` in the producer no longer fetches remote scripts with a plain `fetch`. It goes through a new `fetchPublicScript` that only fetches public addresses and re-validates every redirect hop.

## Why

The compiler fetched every http(s) script src in a composition and inlined the body into the compiled HTML, with no scheme, host, or address restriction. A composition the user downloads and renders could make their machine GET internal URLs (cloud metadata, internal services), and the inlined body sits in the compiled page where the composition's own JS can read it and send it out during the render. The CLI capture resolver in this repo already validates public addresses for the same class of fetch; the compiler path had none of that.

## Related work

No separate issue; self-contained fix. Mirrors the policy tables used by `cli/src/capture/publicNetwork.ts`.

## How

New `producer/src/services/externalScriptFetch.ts`: `fetchPublicScript` checks the scheme (http/https only), requires a public host name or literal, resolves the host and requires every resolved address to be public, using the same special-use tables as the capture resolver (IPv4-mapped and NAT64 IPv6 forms included). Redirects are followed manually, at most 5 hops, each hop re-validated. A policy refusal fails the compile, the same way an SRI mismatch already does, instead of leaving the tag for the render browser to fetch. One deliberate difference from the capture resolver: fetch cannot pin the dialed address, so a narrow DNS rebind window remains; the direct internal-address fetch is closed.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: 16 new tests in `externalScriptFetch.test.ts`, all passing. `htmlCompiler.test.ts` is back to 151 pass / 0 fail, matching the pristine baseline (the tests stub fetch, so the resolver seam is now set at file scope).
- [x] Manual testing performed: verified with a canary HTTP server on 127.0.0.1. Before the fix, both the direct `inlineExternalScripts` call and the full `compileForRender` path fetched the canary URL and inlined the marker body. After the fix, both throw ScriptFetchPolicyError and the canary receives zero requests.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): no docs change, internal fetch policy only.

title: fix(engine): an opaque ProRes clip extracts to jpg frames, only ProRes with alpha stays png
body:
## What
ProRes was always extracted to lossless PNG frames, in case a missed tag hid an alpha plane. ProRes carries alpha in the stream and ffprobe reports it in the pixel format (`yuva444p*`), so for ProRes the guess only costs size: every opaque ProRes 422 frame was written and cached as PNG.

## Fix
`resolveFrameFormat` keeps PNG for VP8 and VP9 (their alpha rides a side channel ffprobe can miss, the reason for the codec rule) and for any stream ffprobe reports with alpha. An opaque ProRes clip now follows the default, jpg. ProRes stays on the alpha-aware decoder and keeps its opaque-alpha warning; only the cached frame format changes.

## Measured
Synthetic 3840x2160 ProRes, 3 s at 25 fps (75 frames), extracted before and after on the same machine:

| clip | cache before | cache after | wall before | wall after | peak memory before | peak memory after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ProRes 422, no alpha | 199 MB (png) | 27 MB (jpg) | 4.5 s | 2.2 s | 1779 MB | 1194 MB |
| ProRes 4444 with alpha | 211 MB (png) | 211 MB (png) | 8.2 s | 7.7 s | 2908 MB | 2768 MB |

The test pattern compresses well; photographic footage gives a larger PNG, so the saving is larger there. The alpha pixel read back from the 4444 frames is identical before and after (value 32 on a 10-bit alpha of 128).

Per-render cost does not rise: JPEG encoding is cheaper than PNG, and the 4444 path is untouched.

## Tests
- `resolveFrameFormat`: ProRes without alpha is jpg, ProRes with alpha is png.
- Real extraction of a ProRes 422 and a ProRes 4444 clip: the 422 frames are `.jpg`, the 4444 frames are `.png` with the alpha value unchanged.
The two jpg assertions fail on the previous extractor and pass here; the 4444 alpha test passes on both and guards against alpha regressing.

## The abort this addresses
A long 4K ProRes source with several capture workers could abort the render: the Node process died with a V8 out-of-memory error while allocating a string inside `JSON.stringify` (`FatalProcessOutOfMemory < NewRawOneByteString < JsonStringifier::Stringify`).

Reproduced on 0.8.188 with a 5 s 3840x2160 noisy ProRes 422 clip, scaled by CSS in a 1080x1920 composition, 3 workers, Node heap capped:

| frames | heap cap 1024 MB | heap cap 2048 MB |
|---|---|---|
| png (before this change) | aborts, stack above | aborts |
| jpg (what opaque ProRes extracts to now) | renders, peak 1.4 to 1.6 GB | renders |

Each worker keeps base64 data URIs of its frames on the one Node heap, and every frame body is stringified again when it is handed to the browser. A 4K png frame is about 23 MB as a data URI, so png frames fill that budget quickly. This change removes the png frames for opaque ProRes. Sources that must stay png (ProRes 4444 or VP9 with alpha) still use the large frames; the per-worker cache budget is handled separately.

title: fix(ci): a package fails its size budget only when more than 1% over it
body:
Package size budgets are the exact packed sizes someone last measured, so any PR that adds ordinary code fails Build on a few hundred bytes. This lets a package go up to 1% over its budget before `verify:packed-manifests` fails. The budget in `scripts/package-size-budgets.json` stays the number people bump, and the 15% ratchet that makes a shrinking package lower its budget is unchanged.

Measured against what the guard exists to catch (a stray sourcemap, tests or assets in the tarball):

| case | over budget | at 1% |
|---|---|---|
| the v0.8.187 publish job, `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` | +115 B packed (0.16%), +208 B unpacked (0.08%) | passes |
| #6127, `@hyperframes/engine` | +215 B | passes |
| #6104, `@hyperframes/studio-server` | +325 B | passes |
| the ECR push, `@hyperframes/aws-lambda` | +2486 B packed (3.4%), +8846 B unpacked (3.3%) | fails, needs an explicit budget bump |

Tolerance per package is small in bytes: aws-lambda 733 B packed and 2.7 KB unpacked, engine 4.3 KB, studio-server 1.4 KB. A stray tests directory or sourcemap is tens of KB to MB, over 5% on every package. The 150 MB Lambda zip class is guarded separately by `verify:zip-size`.

The new test fails without the change: with `verify-packed-manifests.mjs` from main the two size tests fail, with the change all 23 pass (run on a built tree).

## No visible change

Build tooling only.

title: fix(engine): a long audio mix prepares its clips a few at a time
body:
## What

`audioMixer.urlRead.test.ts` no longer times out or fails with EBUSY on the Windows runner, and has been kicking PRs out of the merge queue. It now stops its mix before it deletes the mix's work folder, and its cases are not timed at 5 s.

## Why

On Windows the first two tests failed at 5 s and left `EBUSY: unlink ...\work\clip-trimmed.wav`.

Measured on the Windows runner (timing added to the tests for one run): with the machine quiet, all three tests pass in 1.6 s and every ffmpeg run takes 50 to 250 ms. In the failing run, the failure window sits inside `audioMixer.manyTracks.test.ts` (from #6120), which starts all 200 of its clips' ffmpeg processes at once for about 20 s per test, because the mixer prepares every clip under one `Promise.all`. On a 4-core runner that starves the short ffmpeg runs of the other files, so `urlRead`'s eight spawns went past its 5 s limit. The test was then abandoned with its mix still running, and the cleanup deleted a work folder an ffmpeg still had open: the EBUSY.

So the test had two defects of its own: a timing bound on a process-heavy case, and cleanup that did not wait for the work it started.

## Related work

The flake began with the test added in #6120; the URL-read test is from #5996. The grouping suite already carries a suite-level timeout for the same reason.

## How

- The mix gets an `AbortSignal`; `afterEach` aborts it and waits for it before closing the server and removing the folder. Nothing is left running at cleanup, so there is no EBUSY at any speed.
- The suite takes a 60 s timeout, so a slow runner cannot fail it. The assertions do not depend on speed.

The mixer itself started every clip's ffmpeg at once, which is what loaded the runner, so it now prepares clips in a pool of half the cores (at least 2), the same shape the frame extractor already uses. That also removes the Windows Chrome-launch timeouts seen in the same job (`parallelWorkerBrowsers`, `videoFrameTransport`), which ran in the same window as the 200-clip mixes. A new test counts the ffmpeg runs in flight during a 40-clip mix: 36 at once before, at most the pool size now.

The open-film Studio gate's two thumbnail ceilings are lowered to 13 renders and 14 requests, following the CI runner's Chrome 155. It was failing every PR that runs the gate and the merge queue.

An earlier version of this PR moved the 200-clip test into its own vitest project so it ran alone. The repo's test-reachability check cannot model vitest `projects`, so it was dropped.

## Test plan

- [x] The file passes 3 of 3 locally (Linux); the new concurrency test fails with the pool removed (36 > 4) and passes with it; audio engine suite 194 pass.
- [ ] 3 green runs of `Tests on windows-latest: engine-cli` at this head (reruns of the same job, below)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: bundleToSingleHtml throws "RangeError: Invalid string length" when one image is referenced many times
body: ### Describe the bug `bundleToSingleHtml` inlines every relative image/font under 2 MB as a base64 data URL, once per reference. The 2 MB limit is per asset, so nothing bounds the bundle as a whole: a 1.4 MB image referenced 400 times writes ~750M characters, past V8's max string length (~2^29). Under Node, `check`, `snapshot` and `render` then fail with `RangeError: Invalid string length`. (Bun has a higher limit, so this only shows on Node.) We hit this in production on lessons that repeat a counting unit (e.g. 63 copies of a 1.1 MB chair image). ### Minimal reproduction ```sh npx hyperframes init repro --non-interactive --example blank && cd repro node -e "require('fs').writeFileSync('unit.png', Buffer.alloc(1_400_000))" # add 400 × inside the composition root of index.html ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Set up the reproduction above 2. Run `npx hyperframes check` (Node 22/24) 3. See `RangeError: Invalid string length` ### Expected behavior The project bundles; repeated assets do not blow up the bundle size. ### Actual behavior `RangeError: Invalid string length` from `htmlBundler.ts`. 250 references (≈468M chars) still pass; 400 throw. ### Environment Reproduced on Node v24.16.0 (darwin arm64) against `main` @ 2ed882c; also seen in production on Linux x64 with Node 24. ### Additional context `main` already caches the file read (`createAssetInliner`), but still writes the full data URL for each reference.

title: fix(core): keep bundled HTML under V8's max string length
body:
## What

`bundleToSingleHtml` stops inlining data URLs once the bundle has inlined 256 MB of them. References past that point keep their relative URL.

## Why

Each asset under 2 MB is inlined once per reference, so an image used hundreds of times can push the bundle past V8's max string length and `check`/`snapshot`/`render` throw `RangeError: Invalid string length`. The per-asset limit cannot prevent this; only a limit on the total can.

## Related work

Fixes #6133. No overlapping open PRs found.

## How

`createAssetInliner` counts the characters it has inlined. Before returning a data URL that would exceed `MAX_INLINED_BUNDLE_CHARS` (256 MB, half of V8's limit, leaving room for the rest of the HTML), it warns once and returns `null`, so the reference falls through to its existing relative-URL path. Bundles under the cap are byte-for-byte unchanged.

Deduplicating (write each asset once and reference it) would also shrink normal bundles, but changes the output shape; this PR keeps to the crash. Happy to follow up with dedup if you prefer that direction.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `htmlBundler.test.ts`: 300 references to a 1.9 MB asset. Fails on `main` with `RangeError: Invalid string length`; passes here, with some references inlined, the rest relative, and one warning.
- [x] All 187 `packages/core` tests, oxlint, oxfmt, typecheck and lefthook pre-commit pass.
- [x] Comments say why the cap exists and how to reproduce the crash.

title: fix(engine): the video frame cache budget is shared by the capture workers
body:
## What
Every capture worker built its own video frame cache of up to 1500 MB of base64 data URIs. All workers live on the one Node heap, so the budget multiplied with the worker count, and each frame body was then stringified again to hand it to the browser. With many workers and 4K png frames (a source that must stay png, such as ProRes 4444 or VP9 with alpha) the heap ran out inside `JSON.stringify` and the render aborted:

`FatalProcessOutOfMemory < NewRawOneByteString < JsonStringifier::Stringify < Builtin_JsonStringify`

## Fix
The producer hands each injector its share of the budget: `frameCacheOptions(cfg, workers)` (one helper, `render/frameCacheBudget.ts`) divides `frameDataUriCacheBytesLimitMb` by the worker count and keeps the entry limit. The orchestrator uses it for its per-worker injectors, and the distributed chunk path does too (`createChunkVideoFrameInjectorFactory` now takes the options; `renderChunk` passes the chunk worker count). The engine is unchanged and still floors a share at 64 MB. With one worker nothing changes.

## Measured
Source builds of main and of this branch, same machine (4 vCPU, 30 GB), 1080x1920 composition with one synthetic 5 s 3840x2160 ProRes 4444 clip with an alpha plane (png frames), scaled by CSS to 3150x1772, 25 fps:

| run | main | this change |
|---|---|---|
| 8 workers, default Node heap | aborts (heap out of memory) at 76 s, peak process memory 5.0 GB | renders, 133 s, peak 2.4 GB |
| 6 workers, heap capped at 2 GB | aborts at 106 s | renders, 170 s |
| 1 worker | renders, 346 s, peak 3.9 GB | renders, 296 s, peak 2.5 GB |

With one worker the budget is unchanged (1500 MB / 1), so the two 1-worker rows run the same code; their gap is noise on a shared machine, not a speedup. The cache is a latency buffer, not a correctness requirement, so a smaller per-worker share only changes how often a frame is re-read from disk.

## A common render is not slower
1080p composition, four H.264 videos tiled, 8 workers, 30 fps, 8 s, source builds of main and this branch, same machine, runs interleaved:

| | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | mean |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main | 86.4 s | 87.5 s | 87.2 s | 87.0 s |
| this change | 74.8 s | 72.7 s | 87.5 s | 78.3 s |

No slowdown; the spread is box noise (each frame is read once per worker, so the smaller cache costs no extra disk reads here).

## Tests
`frameCacheOptions`: 6 workers get 250 MB each of 1500, and one worker or an unknown count keeps the whole budget. A second test checks that the chunk injector factory hands the options to every injector it builds, on both the plain and the awaited-lookup path; it fails on main. Both run under `bun test` here, 3 runs in a row; the 14 neighbouring chunk tests, test classification, `tsc`, format, comment checks and the package size budgets (all 14 packages) are clean.

title: fonts: format.md says Inter/JetBrains Mono are bundled, but 0.8.188 compiler fetches them from Google Fonts
body:
**Version:** hyperframes 0.8.188, macOS.

`format.md` says that Inter and JetBrains Mono are **bundled** and resolve by name. In practice, the 0.8.188 compiler **fetches them from Google Fonts at compile time** and caches them in `~/.cache/hyperframes/fonts`.

- With a warm cache, the render is byte-identical and nothing points to a network fetch. The determinism hash does not change.
- The only signal is a line on compiler stderr that mentions the fetch and the cache path.
- With a cold cache and no network, or in restricted environments, the result differs from what the docs say ("bundled").

**Reproduce:** remove `~/.cache/hyperframes/fonts`, run `npx hyperframes check` / `render` on a composition that uses `font-family: Inter`, and watch stderr or the network.

**Expected:** either actually bundle these families, or change `format.md` to say they are downloaded and cached on first use. Ideally there would also be an offline flag that fails loudly instead of fetching. Related: #5112 and #6028 (CDN dependency for offline renders).
