title: fix(cli): render -c takes an absolute entry inside the project, relative to the project
body:
## What
`hyperframes render <project> -c <entry>` validated the entry but handed the producer the string as typed:

- An absolute entry inside the project passed validation, then the producer joined it onto the project path (`<project>/<project>/entry.html`) and failed with "Entry file not found".
- A project reached through a symlinked path (for example `/tmp` on macOS, which is `/private/tmp`) compared the typed absolute path against the resolved project directory and refused its own file with "Entry file must stay inside the project directory".

## Fix
`parseCompositionEntryArg` checks the entry against both spellings of the project path (as given and its real path) and returns the entry project-relative with `/` separators, so every later step joins it onto the project exactly once. A relative entry is resolved against the project directory, as before. Paths that leave the project (`../x.html`, another directory) are still refused.

## Checked
Published CLI, same project, before: absolute entry from inside the project fails with the doubled path, absolute entry through a symlinked path fails with "must stay inside". Source build of this branch: absolute entry from inside the project, from its parent, and through a symlink all render; `-c .solo.html` (a dot-named file) renders from inside, from the parent and from another directory, as it did before; `-c ../escape.html` is still refused.

A relative `-c .solo.html` already resolved against the project on the versions I tried; I could not reproduce a case where it resolved against the working directory, so this change does not touch that path.

## Tests
`parseCompositionEntryArg`: an absolute entry inside the project returns the project-relative path, a dot-named entry stays relative, an absolute path outside the project is refused, and (real filesystem, skipped on Windows) an entry spelled through a symlink to the project is accepted. The absolute-path and symlink tests fail on main and pass here, 3 runs in a row; format, `tsc` and the comment checks are clean.

## Why this is its own PR
A standalone fix in one place (the `-c` argument parser in the CLI), independent of every other open change and affecting any script that passes an absolute entry path, so it is not folded into another PR.

title: fix(engine): a render no longer decodes the videos it replaces with extracted frames
body:
## What

A render no longer starts a video decoder for each video it replaces with extracted frames. A film cut into 163 pieces from one 1080p source renders in 1.4 GB of Chrome memory instead of 6.9 GB, with identical output.

## Why

For a video the renderer replaces with frames extracted by ffmpeg, the page's own decoder never supplies a pixel; the renderer already skips waiting for these videos (`skipReadinessVideoIds`). But the page still decoded every one: Chrome starts a parsed `<video>` at its default preload, and the runtime then forced `preload="auto"` and `load()` on each (`preloadMedia`, and the per-tick promotion in `syncRuntimeMedia`). Chrome keeps one decoder per element, so memory grows with the number of clips, not the number of distinct sources.

Measured on the devbox, one worker, 1280x720 output from one 1080p source, whole process tree sampled every 0.5 s (peak RSS):

| Clips in the film | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1.4 GB | |
| 20 | 2.1 GB | |
| 80 | 4.1 GB | 1.4 GB (with `preload="none"` authored; default attributes behave as the 163 case) |
| 163 | 6.9 GB (Chrome 6.6 GB) | 1.4 GB (Chrome 1.1 GB) |

About 34 MB per extra clip on main, none with the fix. The 163-clip output is the same 490 frames with the same per-frame hash before and after.

## Related work

Preview already loads only media near the playhead (#4682, #5716); this is the render-side equivalent. Preview is untouched: the new behaviour needs `__HF_RENDER_FRAME_VIDEO_IDS`, which only a render sets.

## How

- `engine` (`renderFrameVideoHold.ts`, `frameCapture.ts`): before any page script, the render hands the page the ids of the videos it replaces and a `MutationObserver` holds each at `preload="none"` the moment it is parsed (also for sub-compositions that add them later). It has to be at parse time: Chrome ignores a `none` set once the fetch has started.
- `core` runtime (`preloadMedia.ts`, `media.ts`): `preloadMedia` and the per-tick preload promotion leave those videos alone. One predicate, `isRenderFrameVideo`, owns the rule.

Videos the render does not replace (extraction failed, or not extracted) are not in the list and load as before, so readiness waits and native decoding are unchanged for them.

## Test plan

- [x] Failing first: `preloadMedia.test.ts` (a render-frame video is neither preloaded nor loaded; other videos and audio with the same id still are), `media.test.ts` (the per-tick sync keeps it at none), and the real-Chrome `renderFrameVideoHold.browser.test.ts` (listed ids parse at `none` at the top level, nested, and when added later; the unlisted one stays `metadata`). All fail against a no-op/old version and pass; core runtime 2342/2342 and the browser file 2/2, three runs in a row.
- [x] Engine `frameCapture` suites 300/300; `tsc --noEmit` clean in core and engine; `oxfmt` and `oxlint` clean.
- [x] Render and capture readiness: the 163-clip render reaches ready in about 1 s (unchanged), 490/490 frames identical.
- [x] Seek and playback in preview are untouched (the id list is never set outside a render).
- [ ] Documentation updated (n/a)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(sdk): a stored delete a script still looks up is hidden when overrides replay, not removed
body:
## Problem
A stored override set marks a deleted element as a bare id key set to `null`. Replaying it onto a base document removes the node (`apply-patches.ts`, the `element` remove case). Many generated compositions read nodes by id in an inline script and dereference them unguarded (`document.getElementById('x').getTotalLength()`), so a replayed delete makes the script throw before the timeline registers and the whole render fails with `sub_timeline_script_failure`.

## Fix
`applyOverrideSet` (the replay of stored overrides, used by `openComposition` and the iframe adapter) still removes the node from the live document, so the session model, element queries, timings and the iframe all treat it as deleted. When an inline script looks the node up by id (`getElementById('x')`, `querySelector('#x')`, a descendant's id, or a template-literal id), it also records the node (html, parent, position). `serializeDocument` writes that node back for the output only: hidden (`display: none`) and with `data-start` / `data-duration` / `data-end` / `data-track-index` stripped, so it is not a clip, adds no duration and its media is not mixed. The copy is taken out of the live document again after serializing, and is skipped if an undo has already put the element back.

Plain `applyPatchesToDocument` (undo/redo, host patches) is unchanged.

## Verification
- `apply-patches.scriptTargets.test.ts` (4 of 6 fail on the previous head): the replayed delete is absent from the live document and from `getElements` / `getElement`, present and hidden in `serialize()`, a deleted `<audio>` is no longer a clip, an undone delete is not written back twice, an unreferenced delete is removed as before, a plain patch still removes.
- `scriptLookups.test.ts`: id, selector-list, descendant, template-literal and non-matching lookups.
- 664 SDK tests pass, three runs.
- Real renders (CLI render, synthetic marker nodes standing in for the deleted element): for the `appendChild`, `getTotalLength` and `getBoundingClientRect` failure shapes the removed-node document fails with `sub_timeline_script_failure`; the document produced by this change renders to completion with the marker absent from the frames (a no-delete control shows it).

## Limits
Only id lookups are detected (not class or attribute selectors). A script that forces `display` back on the hidden node would show it.

title: [Studio desktop] Signed-out: clicks inside Settings do nothing — the "Continue with HeyGen" prompt opens hidden behind the Settings dialog
body:
### What happens

While signed out, I open **Settings** and click any tab (Appearance, Agent, Updates…) or control. Nothing happens: the tab does not change, there is no visible feedback. It looks as if the Settings dialog is frozen.

### Why

The sign-in prompt for a signed-out user works as the docs describe: the first trusted click on a `button` / `[role=tab]` / … is cancelled (`preventDefault()` + `stopImmediatePropagation()` in a capture-phase `click` listener on `document`) and the **Continue with HeyGen / Not now** prompt is shown, anchored to the clicked element. Further clicks are swallowed while the prompt is open.

The Settings panel, however, is a modal `<dialog>` (`showModal()`), so it sits in the browser **top layer**. The sign-in prompt is rendered in the normal document, so it ends up **underneath** the dialog. I verified it at runtime:

- `document.elementFromPoint()` at the center of the "Continue with HeyGen" button returns an element inside `dialog[open]` → the prompt is rendered but covered;
- `window.desktop.account.status()` → `{ state: "signed-out" }`;
- synthetic `element.click()` (untrusted) on the Settings tabs works, while trusted clicks are cancelled by the listener above.

So every click is silently swallowed and the user never sees why. Closing Settings (Esc) reveals the prompt; after signing in, Settings works normally.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Fresh install, signed out. Skip or dismiss the first-launch survey without clicking anything that triggers the sign-in prompt.
2. Open **Settings**.
3. Click any tab, e.g. **Appearance** → nothing happens.
4. Press Esc → the "Continue with HeyGen" prompt is visible behind where the dialog was.

### Expected

Either the sign-in prompt is shown above the Settings dialog (e.g. rendered as a popover/top-layer element or inside the dialog), or Settings closes before the prompt is shown, or Settings is reachable without the sign-in wall.

### Environment

- HyperFrames Studio `0.1.0+b465` (also seen on `b463`), Electron 44.9.3 / Chrome 152
- Linux x86_64: Arch Linux (CachyOS kernel), Wayland (niri). Installed from the official `HyperFrames-amd64.deb`, repackaged for pacman with its contents unchanged
- The issue does not look Linux-specific: it comes from how the prompt and the modal `<dialog>` are stacked

title: fix(studio): the thumbnail capture page loads media near the playhead like the preview
body:
## What

The hidden page Studio uses to screenshot thumbnails and posters now loads video and audio near the playhead, as the live preview does. A 163-clip film cut from one source needs 1.35 GB and 140 threads to make its thumbnails instead of 6.2 GB and 737, and the thumbnails are byte-identical.

## Why

The live preview page already defers media: only clips on screen or about to start load, the rest stay at `preload="none"`. The capture page (`/preview?hf-capture=1`, loaded by the thumbnail route) got no preview mark, so none of that applied and the runtime's eager pass set `preload="auto"` on and loaded every clip. Chrome keeps one decoder per element, so a film cut into many pieces mounts them all at once.

Measured on the devbox, headless Chrome, a project of 163 timed pieces cut from one 1080p source:

| | Videos loaded | Renderer memory | Renderer threads |
|---|---|---|---|
| Live preview page | 7 of 163 | ~400 MB | 36 |
| Capture page, before | 163 of 163 | 5.6 GB | 661 |

Whole thumbnail server (browser, renderers, node), three thumbnails at 0.5 s, 20.3 s and 45.1 s, peak:

| | Memory | Threads | First thumbnail |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 6.2 GB | 737 | 6.1 s |
| after | 1.35 GB | 140 | 1.9 s |

The three PNGs have the same md5 before and after.

## Related work

#4682 and #5716 added the preview's near-playhead load. #6142 is the render-side equivalent and does not touch this path.

## How

One mark, one owner of "this is a Studio preview page": the page keeps `meta[name=hyperframes-studio-preview]` and the capture page now carries it with `content="capture"`.

- `routes/preview.ts`: the capture page gets the mark (still without lazy images, so its screenshot has every image).
- `timedClipHide.ts`: `defersMedia()` is true under the mark; the hidden-image skip stays off in capture mode. `preloadMedia.ts` and `init.ts` use `defersMedia()` for media, and keep `skipsHiddenImages()` for images.
- The thumbnail seek already waits for video frames at the target time (`__hfWaitForSeekCompletion`), so a clip that is only loaded once the seek lands on it is ready before the screenshot.

## Test plan

- [x] Failing first: `init.test.ts` "loads media near the playhead" (a preview mark and a capture-mode mark hold the clips off the playhead at `preload="none"`; no mark keeps today's eager load) and `preview.test.ts` (the capture page carries the capture-mode mark and no lazy images). Both fail on main and pass; core runtime 2342/2342 and the preview route file 114/114, three runs in a row.
- [x] Studio-server 1364 passed, cli server and capture 740 passed; `tsc --noEmit` clean in core and studio-server; `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, comment checks clean.
- [x] Captured frame: thumbnails at 0.5 s, 20.3 s and 45.1 s on the 163-clip project are byte-identical before and after.
- [ ] Seek and scrub on the live preview page are untouched by this change; the preview-mark path is the same code with the same mark.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: test(studio): bank the open-film thumbnail counts on the CI Chrome
body:
## What

Lowers the two thumbnail ceilings in the Studio open-film work-count gate: renders 14 to 13 and thumbnail requests 15 to 14. The recorded browser moves from Chrome 154 to 155.

## Why

The CI runner's Chrome moved to 155 and the journey now renders one thumbnail fewer. The ratchet only goes down, so it fails any run that comes in below a ceiling until the improvement is banked. It is failing the timeline viewport gate on every PR that runs it, including a version-bump-only release PR in the merge queue.

`perf-ratchet.mjs lower` refuses evidence from a different Chrome than the one recorded, so the file is edited by hand. The new values are exactly what the CI job measured on 155; `perf-ratchet.mjs check` against that evidence passes.

## Not changed

Frame navigations (7) and document requests (2) are unchanged on 155.

title: perf(aws-lambda): warm the audio function while the plan runs
body:
## What

A render on a stack with the arm64 video function now starts the x86 render function's container at the very beginning, in a fire-and-forget invoke, so it is warm when the audio task needs it. A stack without a video function is unchanged: same states, same cost.

## Why

On an arm64 stack the plan and the chunks run on the arm64 video function, so the x86 function that mixes the audio is cold when the audio task starts. A cold audio task takes 3 to 5 s longer, and it finished after the last chunk in most renders, so the render waited for it.

## Related work

Follows the arm64 video function work; no overlapping PR.

## How

- New `WarmRender` state in the SAM template. It invokes the render function with `InvocationType: Event` and `Action: warm`. A failed or throttled warm-up is caught and the render goes on, so it can never fail a render.
- A rule in `SelectPlanProtocol` sends a v2 render to `WarmRender` only when the stack has the video function (the template's own `HasVideoFunction` condition decides the value compared). Without a video function that rule can never match, so the render takes the old path with no extra state or transition. The CDK stack has no video function and is not touched.
- The handler answers `warm` before any event parsing: it resolves Chrome, the part of the cold start the audio task would otherwise pay, and returns.

## Test plan

Measured on one arm64 stack, a 30-minute 1080p composition, 3 runs with the change and 3 without, interleaved on the same stack with nothing else running:

- Median wall time: 8.1% lower (the time the audio task outlasts the last chunk fell from 6.0 to 6.9 s down to 1.2 to 3.7 s).
- Cost per render: flat (+0.1% at the median), the extra invoke is below the noise.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated (handler answers `warm` without touching S3, and that test fails without the handler change; a template test pins the video-function gate and the caught failure)
- [x] Manual testing performed: the timing stack above, plus a real deploy of the final template as an arm64 stack and as an x86-only stack, one small render each. The arm64 execution enters `WarmRender` before `PlanV2`; the x86-only execution goes straight to `PlanV2`.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(engine): the BeginFrame start-up check waits for the first frame up to its deadline
body:
## What

The BeginFrame start-up check of each capture browser now keeps asking for the first frame until its own 2 s deadline, instead of giving up after 10 tries (about a quarter of a second). A chunk whose workers still end up in different capture modes keeps failing with a typed error.

## Why

A chunk is captured by several workers, each with its own browser, and each browser runs this check at start-up. Under CPU load a fresh renderer can take longer than 10 quick tries to draw its first surface; the check then reported "BeginFrame not supported" after 246 ms, although its deadline is 2 s, and that one worker fell back to screenshot mode while the others stayed on BeginFrame. The chunk then failed with `capture workers reported invalid or inconsistent modes: beginframe,screenshot` and only the state machine's retry recovered it, about one extra chunk run. Seen once in 1,230 browser launches (six 30-minute renders, 204 chunks each, on a Lambda stack).

## Related work

Nothing overlapping.

## How

- `probeBeginFrameSupport` loops until a PNG arrives or the probe deadline passes, instead of for a fixed 10 tries. A browser that truly lacks BeginFrame still falls back, after at most the same 2 s deadline.
- The post-capture mode check is now `observedChunkCaptureMode`, which throws a typed `MixedCaptureModesError` for a mix. It is a hard failure on purpose: retrying in BeginFrame (the state machine's retry) beats forcing the chunk into the slower screenshot mode, and the cause is now rare.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests: a renderer that draws its first frame on the 26th try is now supported (fails on main, which gives up at 10); an always-empty renderer is still reported unsupported, at the deadline; a mixed chunk fails with the typed error and is not retried in screenshot mode.
- [x] Real Chrome, N browsers started at once on 6 CPUs, interleaved before/after builds (shared test machine): 12 at once, 1 of 288 browsers fell back before and 0 of 288 after; 6 and 16 at once saw no fallback in either build (450 and 960 launches each). At 24 at once on 6 CPUs the machine is saturated and both builds hit the 2 s deadline.
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: feat(cli): check writes a progress line to stderr per sample, overlap batch and craft frame
body:
## Problem
After the video copies are made, `hyperframes check` writes nothing to stderr until it prints its report: the sampling, craft and overlap phases can run for minutes in silence. A caller that watches stderr to tell a working check from a hung one (the desktop app runs check as a child process) has to use one fixed time cap instead. The CLI's own 120 s idle deadline rearms on every unit of work, but that is invisible from outside.

## Change
One stderr line per finished unit, in the same `[hyperframes] check: ...` style as the existing copy-phase lines:
- `[hyperframes] check: samples k/N` after each layout/motion/contrast sample (shared counter across the helper page)
- `[hyperframes] check: craft k/n` after each craft frame
- `[hyperframes] check: overlap k/M` after each batch of 8 dense overlap samples

stdout (and `--json`) is unchanged; these are stderr only. The hold-probe loop stays silent (each probe is short and rearms the idle deadline internally).

## Tests
- `checkProgress.test.ts`: the line format.
- The existing dense-overlap test in `checkBrowser.test.ts` now also asserts `samples 1/1` and the last `overlap` batch line.
- Two tests that feed `Date.now` a fixed sequence now silence `console.error` first: vitest's console reads `Date.now`, so an unmocked line spends one of the mocked readings. Whole CLI suite passes three runs in a row.

title: fix(core): format generated artifacts through oxfmt's API, not a bun spawn
body:
## Summary

Fixes #5856. The codegen format step (`formatGeneratedSource`) shelled out to `bun x oxfmt` from a tsx/node process. On Windows, where PATH can carry only the extensionless bun shim, that spawn fails with `ENOENT` and the silent `catch` published unformatted artifacts — dirtying the force-tracked files under `packages/core/src/generated/` and blocking `git pull` after every build.

The formatter now calls oxfmt's JS API (`import("oxfmt")` + `format()`), so formatting runs in-process and no longer depends on a spawnable bun. The repo's `.oxfmtrc.json` is passed when present (verified byte-identical to the CLI path). The fallback for environments without oxfmt stays, but warns with the file name and error instead of swallowing them.

`buildInjectedArtifact` and its three caller scripts become `async`; `oxfmt` is declared as a `@hyperframes/core` devDependency.

## Verification

- New unit tests cover the API path, the spawn-failure fallback (injected rejection ≙ the Windows `ENOENT`), and oxfmt-reported errors: 7/7 pass via `node --import tsx --test`.
- All three artifacts rebuild byte-identical: `check:position-edits-render`, `check:svg-selector-aliases`, and `build:audio-fx-runtime` + `git diff --exit-code`.
- Windows condition simulated by scrubbing `bun` from PATH (spawn fails with `ENOENT`, confirmed); codegen output still byte-identical.
- `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Closes #5856

title: fix(core): a hidden child of a mover stays out of the blur trail
body:
## What
Follow-up to #6106, from Genesis's review there. The capture isolation CSS made every descendant of a mover `visibility: visible !important`, so a child the author had hidden with `visibility: hidden` was cropped and smeared into the blur trail.

The hide rule now skips the mover subtree, and only the mover itself is forced visible. Its descendants inherit, and keep any `visibility` they set themselves. The root rule is untouched. The CSS is the 2-line change Genesis suggested.

## Evidence
Real-Chrome pixel test: a red mover with a `visibility:hidden` green child.
- Before: 240 green pixels in the blurred frame (0 in the sharp frame).
- After: 0.

The test fails on the old CSS and passes on the new. The pixel file passes 11/11.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(engine): a composition whose script throws is skipped with a warning, not refused
body:
## What

A composition whose own script throws (a lookup of an element id that is not in the page, for example) used to leave its timeline unregistered. The renderer waited the full 45 s readiness timeout and then refused the render. Two changes:

- A thrown script now fails fast: the wait ends 5 s after the first error, and the error names the composition that is still unregistered and the thrown error (it used to say a script "failed to load").
- A nested composition that threw is skipped with a non-blocking `script_error_isolated` warning naming its element, but only while another nested composition with a live timeline remains. If nothing live would be left (a root that never registered, a single nested composition that is the whole animation, or a script file that failed to load), the render is still refused with `sub_timeline_script_failure`, now in seconds.

## How

- `frameCapture.ts`: the page-error grace is counted from the first error (load failures keep their 2 s grace). `isolateUnregisteredCompositions` registers an empty paused timeline of the host's `data-duration` for each unregistered nested composition, and returns nothing when the root is unregistered or no nested timeline is live. `recordSubTimelineWarning` emits `script_error_isolated` with the element ids, or the blocking warning with the thrown error.
- `types.ts`: new `script_error_isolated` warning code; the orchestrator's blocking list is unchanged.

Known limit: isolation needs `window.gsap` on the page.

## Evidence

Synthetic compositions, Linux, 1280x720, 4 s. Each has a static title, a nested composition whose script looks up a missing id, and (except the last row) a second nested composition with a live timeline.

| nested script throws on | 0.8.189 | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `appendChild` of a missing id | refused after the 45 s wait (142 s total) | rendered in 21 s, warning names `design` |
| `getTotalLength` of a missing id | refused (142 s) | rendered in 22 s |
| `getBoundingClientRect` of a missing id | refused (141 s) | rendered in 21 s |
| `_gsap` read on a missing element | refused | rendered in 23 s |
| same, but the throwing composition is the only nested one | refused after the wait | refused in 21 s, error names `design` |

A root-level throw is refused in 15 s total with the error naming the root composition.

## Tests

- `frameCapture-subTimelinePoll.test.ts`: bails after the grace when a script threw and nothing registers, counts the grace from the first error, still takes a late registration.
- `frameCapture-isolateScript.browser.test.ts` (real Chrome): isolates a nested throw next to a live nested timeline; keeps the blocking code for a failed root, for a single nested composition, and for a load failure. The first and the single-nested cases fail on main.
- `frameCapture-subTimelineWarning.test.ts`, `frameCapture-subTimelineMemo.test.ts`: the thrown-script message and outcome.

title: fix(studio): audio clips in the timeline share the video clip corner radius
body:
## What

Audio clips in the Studio timeline now use the same corner radius as video clips (12px). They were pills (21px).

## Why

The two kinds of clip sat in one timeline with different shapes, which reads as a mistake. The audio radius token now follows the clip radius token, so a theme that sets one still gets both, and a theme can still override the audio one on its own.

Headless Studio on a repo-style project (two video clips and one tone), same viewport. Computed radius of the clips, from the page: before video 12px, video 12px, audio 21px; after 12px, 12px, 12px.

## Before

![Before: audio clip is a pill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d89d0a7b-f568-43cd-9a8f-fddb30b6b34b)

## After

![After: audio clip matches video clips](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bcc471cd-8773-40cc-ab5a-739e119f2c47)

## Test plan

- [x] Before and after captures above

title: fix(core): preview fetches only the clips due next, and drops passed clips still downloading
body:
## What

Studio's preview now keeps fetches to the clips that matter in a fast-cut film: the clip on screen, the next one on its track, and a few more that are due soonest. A clip the playhead has passed stops downloading while it plays.

## Why

A cut sequence with dozens of short clips has most of them inside the 2 s look-ahead. Every one started a full fetch, and the clips already played kept downloading for 4 s more. With about 16 fetches in flight against the browser's 6 per origin, the clip that was due queued behind clips that were not, so later clips entered at `readyState` 1 and showed a stale frame.

Both are decided in one place, `preloadNearPlayhead` in `init.ts`:

- Upcoming clips take one of 3 slots, earliest first. A clip that is on screen or armed as next on its track never waits for a slot. A slot frees when its clip is playable, or errors.
- While playing, a clip that has passed and is still loading is released and stays released until the play stops or seeks, except a clip due at the loop start; one that finished loading stays loaded for a scrub back.

## Measured

Headless Studio on a synthetic project: 36 clips of 0.2 to 0.6 s, cut from 6 portrait sources (20 MB each) across 4 sub-compositions, played from 0 for 14 s with the link limited to 12 Mbit/s. Clips that entered their window below `readyState` 3, and clips whose first frame took over 150 ms:

| link | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 Mbit/s (7 runs) | 25 / 24 | 0 to 9 / 0 (one run: 8) |
| 6 Mbit/s (3 runs) | 30 / 30 | 28 / 2-5 |
| 40 Mbit/s | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |

At 12 Mbit/s, before: 24 clips never became ready inside their window. After: 6 of 7 runs had every clip ready on entry or within 141 ms; one run (the machine was loaded) had 8 late. Fetches in flight at once, peak: 16 before, 6 to 9 after.

## Before

Frame at 5.4 s on the 12 Mbit/s link. The burned-in timecode of the source shows the clip sitting on its first frame (00:00:00.000).

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9c0cb216-ebb0-4062-9b0e-7e5e0ecff5b6)

## After

Same moment after the change. The clip shows the frame it should (00:00:06.133).

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/07a46a66-c279-4a35-90de-06fa1c81bf64)

## Test plan

- [x] `entry.test.ts`: slots hand out earliest first and refill on `canplay`/`suspend`/`error`; a passed clip still loading is released while playing and a finished one is kept. Both fail on main's `init.ts` and pass here (37 tests in the file; core media, init and entry suites pass).
- [x] Before/after numbers above, from the same project on the same machine, built from this branch and from main.

Not changed: a render still loads every clip; the capture page and thumbnails use the same code path as the live preview and gain the same limit.

title: fix(cli): snapshot waits for the image layers a seek reveals before capturing
body: ## What `hyperframes snapshot` now waits, after each seek, for every visible image layer (``, SVG ``, CSS `background-image: url(...)`) to finish decoding, for up to 3 seconds. A layer that is still loading, or broken, when the wait ends is named in a console warning and in a `warnings` array of the `--json` envelope. ## Why `snapshot` screenshotted as soon as the seek settled and never waited for images. A layer that appears at the seek time and is still loading (large PNGs, slow or remote assets, a cold cache) came out blank or half drawn. The frame looked complete, so anyone reading it to judge the video was sent to fix things that were fine. The failure depends on load timing, so it varies from run to run. ## Related work The 120 ms image wait in `SCREENSHOT_SEEK_OPTIONS` was only used by `check`'s screenshots; `snapshot` passed `{ exactTime: true }` and had no image wait at all. ## How - `captureCompositionFrame.ts`: `waitForCompositionImages` scans visible elements for the three layer kinds and decodes each (CSS and SVG sources through an `Image` of the same URL), racing one cap. It returns the layers still `pending` or `failed`; `settleCompositionSeek` passes that on. `SCREENSHOT_IMAGE_WAIT_MS` (3 s) replaces the 120 ms and is shared by `snapshot`, `check` screenshots and `compare`. A wait only costs time while an image is loading. - `snapshot.ts`: opts in to the wait, and collects the report into `warnings`, printed as a warning and added to the `--json` envelope when non-empty. - Not covered: backgrounds on pseudo-elements, `mask-image` and `border-image`. `check` and `compare` wait but do not report. ## Test plan New `snapshot.lateImages.browser.test.ts` runs the real `snapshot` command against a project whose seek reveals a layer served over an 800 ms connection: one test each for an ``, a CSS background and an SVG ``, plus one for an image that never loads (named in `warnings`). - On `main` all 4 fail; with the change all 4 pass, 3 runs in a row. - Breaking each layer kind in the scan fails exactly its own test. - `packages/cli`: typecheck, lint and format clean; the snapshot, capture, compare and check test files pass (668 tests). - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing performed - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments" ## Before and after `hyperframes snapshot --at 1.5` on a project whose seek at 1 s reveals three image layers, each served after 800 ms. ![Before: only a broken-image outline, the other two layers missing](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/48f012ab-af59-4e5a-89aa-11da39e1824f) ![After: all three layers painted](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4314f2b7-b549-4280-adf0-b62040beea7d)

title: perf(aws-lambda): a render reads a video's audio from a small file stored beside it
body:
## What

`lambda sites create` (and the implicit upload of `lambda render`) now stores each large video's audio packets as a small object beside the video, keyed by the video's hash. The audio task of a render reads that object when it exists, instead of reading the whole video.

## Why

A video's audio is interleaved with its pictures. Mixing it from the cloud moved the whole file: for a 20-minute 4K film (two HEVC `.mov` files) the audio task read 2.5 GB to get about 20 MB of audio, at the roughly 75 MB/s a single Lambda function can pull from S3 (measured: 1, 8 and 16 parallel streams all land at 65 to 75 MB/s; separate functions each get their own). That was 33 s of the audio task's 56 s, and the audio task finished after the last chunk, so it set the render's length. Reading it with more connections in one function gave no speed-up (tried, measured, not shipped).

## Related work

Follows the Lambda audio task (separate audio beside the chunks). No overlapping PR.

## How

- `buildAudioSidecar` (producer) copies the first audio stream out of a `.mp4`/`.mov`/`.m4v` of 32 MiB or more with `-c:a copy`: no re-encode. `deploySite` stores the result at `<video's object>.audio.m4a` in the content store. It is deliberately **not** in the site's `files.json`: a site's file list is a function of the project's files only, so a machine with ffmpeg and one without still produce the same site, and an older site gets its sidecars the next time it is uploaded from a machine that can make them.
- Without a local ffmpeg, or when the audio cannot be copied as is, nothing is stored and the site is exactly as before. With no ffmpeg the CLI prints a line saying renders will read the whole video for audio and be slower.
- On the Lambda side `downloadSiteFiles` looks for the sidecar of each remote video (one HEAD) and hands its URL along with the video's. The audio mix cuts the same clip from it with the same ffmpeg arguments. A decoder has no history before a seek, so the cut starts one second early and drops that second; for an input seek this gives exactly the samples the video itself gives (checked sample by sample on a 20-minute AAC track, at whole and fractional start times). Everything else about the clip, including the probe that decides how it is cut, still comes from the video.

## Test plan

Measured on a real stack (arm64, 20-minute 4K case with two large HEVC videos), three cold runs each, same function code, only the sidecars differ:

- Audio output is **byte-identical** to the released version: the AAC stream and the decoded PCM have the same md5 as a render without sidecars.
- Audio task: 56 s to 27 s (billed 56.4 s to 26.8 s). It now ends well before the last chunk, so the render is bound by the chunks.
- Wall time (submit to done): median 73.3 s to 69.0 s (-6%; the audio had been 5 to 7 s past the last chunk).
- Cost: flat within the run-to-run noise of about 1% (medians $1.307 and $1.309); the billed audio time alone is about 0.4% lower, and nothing is added.
- 30-minute 1080p composition (no large video with audio, so no sidecar): wall 43.1 s and cost $0.60 at the median, unchanged.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: the mix from the sidecar is byte-identical to the mix from the local video, and the video is served less than a quarter of its bytes (fails on main, which reads all 44.7 MB of the video); `deploySite` stores the sidecar and leaves the site file list unchanged; without ffmpeg the same site is stored and the notice is emitted; the site download attaches the sidecar URL only when it is stored; `wantsAudioSidecar` and `buildAudioSidecar`.
- [x] Manual testing performed (stack runs above)
- [ ] Documentation updated (not applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Follow-up, not in this PR: a render whose videos are handed to the Lambda as cloud URLs without going through `sites create` has no sidecar and reads the whole video for its audio as before. The same `buildAudioSidecar` can be run wherever such files are first stored.

title: fix(sdk): a kept delete drops its media sources and a hidden video is not waited for
body:
## What

A delete that a composition script still looks up is kept in the replayed page as a hidden copy (#6143). The copy kept the original media sources, so the renderer treated it as live media: it downloaded a hidden image on every render, and a hidden `<video>` whose source cannot be fetched failed the whole render (`VIDEO_SOURCE_UNRENDERABLE`), where the same page rendered before.

- `serialize.ts`: a kept copy drops `src`, `srcset` and `poster` on every element it holds, and any inline style declaration that loads a `url(...)`. The script still finds the node; the renderer has nothing to fetch.
- `frameCapture.ts`: the video readiness wait skips a video inside a `data-hidden` node, as the audio mixer and the frame extractor already do. Without this a copy with no source waits the full 45 s readiness timeout per capture session.
- `pollVideosReady` is exported for the test.

Why standalone and under the size floor: this closes two regressions the merged change introduced for kept deletes of media; it cannot ship inside either half alone.

## Evidence

A stored composition with its draft overrides (deleted layers include a logo image), baked with the SDK before and after, then rendered 3 times each with the CLI on Linux:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| remote downloads per render | 4 (one is the hidden logo) | 3, none for the hidden node |
| render time | 10.9, 11.6, 12.2 s | 11.2, 12.2, 14.8 s (same range) |

A page whose deleted node is a `<video>` with an unreachable source, looked up by a script: before, the render fails in 3 s with `Video extraction failed ... VIDEO_SOURCE_UNRENDERABLE`; with only the SDK change it rendered but waited 147 s on the source-less video; with both changes it renders in 10.9 to 13.1 s.

## Tests

- `apply-patches.scriptTargets.test.ts`: a kept video, picture with source and img, and a div with a background image carry none of their urls; a node that was not deleted keeps its source. Fails on main, passes here.
- `frameCapture-hiddenVideoReady.browser.test.ts` (real Chrome): a source-less video inside a hidden node is ready at once; a live video that has not decoded still waits. The first fails on main. Three runs green with the engine and SDK suites.

title: fix(sdk): a delete is kept hidden when any script lookup could reach it, not only an id
body:
## What

#6143 keeps a deleted node as a hidden copy when an inline script looks it up, so the script does not throw before its timeline registers. It only recognised a literal `getElementById('x')` or `querySelector('#x')`. A script that looks the node up by class (`.halftone-svg`), by tag or attribute selector, or through a variable (`document.querySelector(path)` over a list of selectors, `getElementById(id)` in a helper) still lost the node, threw, and the render failed.

`scriptLooksUp` now keeps the delete hidden when any lookup in the page's inline scripts could reach the node or something inside it:
- a literal id, class name, tag name or selector is tested against the node and its descendants (`matches` / `querySelector`);
- a lookup whose argument is not a literal can name any node, so every delete is kept;
- a selector with a template placeholder is kept.

Cost: a page with such a script keeps hidden copies of nodes the person deleted. The copies are `display: none` and carry no media sources (separate change), so the render does not paint or fetch them.

Why standalone and under the size floor: it touches only the lookup scan and is independent of the media-source change.

## Evidence

31 renders of stored compositions with their draft overrides, from one week of failures that a literal id scan did not explain. Each was replayed with the SDK, then loaded in a real browser and its page errors counted.

| | page errors |
|---|---|
| original compositions, no overrides | 0 of 31 |
| replayed with main | 18 of 31 |
| replayed with this change | 1 of 31 (a syntax error in the composition's own script, not a lookup) |

12 distinct compositions from that set rendered with the CLI after the change, all exit 0, 6 to 44 s.

## Tests

`apply-patches.scriptTargets.test.ts`: a delete is hidden when the script looks it up by class (`querySelector` and `getElementsByClassName`) or through a variable (selector list, id variable); a delete no lookup can reach is still removed. The first two fail on main. Full SDK suite 667 tests green three runs in a row.

title: test(engine): only h264 is held to identical bytes across host sizes
body:
## What

`softwareEncoderThreads.test.ts` no longer asserts that x265 gives identical bytes on a 2-core and a 7-core host. The same assertion for x264 stays.

## Why

The h265 case failed in two merge-queue runs (one for another PR, one for #6160), so it was kicking unrelated PRs out of the queue.

Measured on a Linux host with the production encoder args, 12 encodes per setting: on an 8-core set with the same fixed `-threads`, 11 gave one hash and 1 gave another; on a 2-core set one earlier run produced three different hashes in ten encodes. So x265 output differs between runs of the same command, and a byte comparison across host sizes cannot be reliable. x264 gave one hash every time, 10 of 10 runs of the test file.

title: fix(cli): init never touches installed skills and no command removes one
body:
## What changes for you

`init` no longer refreshes, replaces or removes skills you already have. It installs the core set only when it is missing. No command removes a skill any more: `skills update` refreshes the HyperFrames skills you already have (or the ones you name) and never deletes one. `--skip-skills` works again, and `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1` still does the same. The stale-skills notice now reaches agents too: it prints to stderr after `render`, `lint` and `validate` even without a terminal and under `--json`, and stays off in CI, in dev, with `HYPERFRAMES_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` and with `HYPERFRAMES_SKIP_SKILLS=1`.

`init <name> --example blank --non-interactive` without the flag keeps working with no prompt.

## Why

Setup and update changed and deleted skills nobody had asked it to touch. A skill the user had installed under one of our names could be overwritten, and the "no longer published" purge removed skills on its own. `--skip-skills` was ignored on purpose while the skills.sh registry lagged; that reason is gone.

## How

- `init` installs missing core skills only (`updateSkills({ onlyMissing: true })`); outdated installed skills are left as they are.
- The purge and the removed-upstream detection are deleted: the `skills remove` call, the lock-entry cleanup, the "removed" status and count in `check`, the nudge count, and `update`'s `--dir` and `--source` flags (they only scoped the purge).
- A skill the install record attributes to another publisher is never compared or refreshed, even when its name matches one of ours. A skill with no record entry is still treated as ours, which is today's behaviour.
- The notice and its background check gated on a terminal, which agents never have, so they never saw it and their cache never refreshed. They now gate on the update-check opt-outs only; the CLI's own self-update notice keeps its terminal gate. `--json` stdout is unchanged; the notice only writes stderr, and the CLI's own update notices stay off under `--json`.
- Docs (`skill-lifecycle.md`, `init-and-scaffold.md`, `docs/packages/cli.mdx`, README) say the above.

## Tests

New tests fail on `main` and pass here: `update` never spawns a removal, `init`'s install leaves an outdated skill alone, a dropped skill is not an update, a run without a terminal prints the stale-skills notice and has its background check due, a same-named skill from another source is not compared, and `init --skip-skills` without the env var skips skills. The skills, manifest, init and nudge suites pass 3 runs in a row (163 tests). About 880 lines are deleted net.

title: fix(studio-server): project history no longer copies video, audio or huge files
body:
## What

Project history copied every tracked file into `~/.cache/hyperframes/history/<id>/blobs`, video and audio included. A project with a large camera file, a long recording and a render output being written grew its history by tens of gigabytes in minutes and filled the disk, so the render's own write failed. Each media file was stored at least once next to the original, and the current copies were never counted against the budget.

Now:
- Video and audio files, and any file over 64 MiB, are hashed where they are (streamed, no copy) and recorded by path and hash. `uncopied.ts` is the one place that decides which files these are.
- When history opens, copies an older version already made of such files are removed, but only when every reference to that content is a file of that kind. Text, small images and every edit history of HTML, CSS and JS stay as they are.
- Bringing back an earlier version of such a file is not offered: undo, restore and checkout of a change that needs it fail up front, before anything is written, naming the file ("An earlier version of clip.mp4 is not kept"). Everything else in history behaves as before.

- `hyperframes clean` does the same for every history in the cache, not only the ones Studio opens: it takes each history that no running process holds, applies the same rule, and `--dry-run` lists the bytes ("Video and audio copies in project history").

Not changed: the budget still counts stored bytes beyond what the current files need (a project larger than its budget keeps its history; a test pins that). With media gone, the current copies left are text and files under 64 MiB each, which cannot be shed anyway.

## Evidence

- A 50 MiB video present when history opens, and 25 MiB of video and audio written and rewritten while it is open: blob bytes stay under 1 KiB (they were the full file sizes).
- A copy planted the way an older version left it is removed on open; the text blob next to it is kept and still readable.

- Hashing in place costs no more than before: a file whose size and times have not moved is not read again (the existing stat cache), so reopening a project or saving a text edit does not rehash a large video. With a 1 GiB video, first adoption took 2.8 s instead of 5.8 s, reopening 18 ms (9 ms before), and a text-edit snapshot 29 ms (24 ms before); blob bytes 1 instead of 1,073,741,825.
- `hyperframes clean --dry-run` on a planted history listed the 2.9 MB media copy and left it; `hyperframes clean` removed it and kept the text blob.

## Tests

`reclaimUncopied.test.ts` (dry run lists and keeps; a real run removes the media copy and keeps text) and `uncopied.test.ts` (four cases): no copy for media present at open, none for media written or replaced later, a text edit is still copied while the media half of the same change cannot be undone, and reclaim on open. All four fail on main. The history suite (218 tests) and the clean command's tests is green three runs in a row. In `projectHistory.test.ts` the stand-in for "large media" is now a `.bin` file, since `.mp4` is no longer copied.

title: perf(engine): a site's remote files are probed once per render, not once per clip
body:
## What changed

Every ffprobe of a file held at a URL used to read it again over the network: the result was never kept, because a URL has no file identity to key it by. A cut-heavy edit (one `<video>` per cut over a few large sources) therefore probed the same source once per cut, in the plan and again in the audio task.

Files of a site are content-addressed: the URL's path holds the file's sha256, so its bytes cannot change. The plan now declares each site file's URL with its sha256, which gives it an identity, and the existing probe caches (media, video, audio, final-frame timestamp) keep their results for the whole render. The audio probe also stops bypassing the cache when a caller passes an abort signal: it is shared among callers of the same signal.

A URL nobody declared (a plain https source) keeps today's behavior: probed every time, since its bytes can change.

## What I measured

- New test `ffprobe.remoteIdentity.test.ts`: 5 audio plus 5 video probes of a declared URL read the server 0 times after the first round; the same probes on an undeclared URL read it every time. With the declaration made a no-op the first test fails (15 requests instead of 0).

## What I did NOT exercise

- The Lambda before/after curve (clips vs plan and audio time) is not in this PR yet; it follows from the next runs and I will add it here.
- Extraction of video frames per clip window and the audio read per cut are separate changes.

title: perf(producer): the audio task finds sound with a probe and reads URL clips in parallel
body:
## What changed

Two changes to the distributed audio task, both aimed at cut-heavy edits (one `<video>` per cut over a few large sources):

1. **No frame extraction.** The task ran the whole video extract stage (frame decoding, including a tail decode per clip window) only to learn which videos carry sound. It now probes each source for an audio stream instead and adds the same sound entries, so the mix is unchanged. With the probe cache already on main, each source is probed once however many clips use it.
2. **Clips held at a URL are read many at a time.** The mix prepares each clip in a slot sized for CPU (half the cores). A clip read from a URL spends its time waiting on the network, so those clips now use their own 16-wide slot; clips read from disk keep the CPU-sized one.

## What I measured

- `videoAudioProbe.test.ts`: three clips over a source with sound and one silent source give one audio entry for the first, and no frames are written.
- `audioMixer.urlRead.test.ts`: 24 one-second clips of a slow URL peak above the CPU-sized limit of open requests. With the new slot narrowed back to 2 the test fails (2 open requests, expected more than 4).
- Existing `buildPlanAudio` tests (a video's sound, a script-set src, deferred audio) pass unchanged.
- Before this change, on 17 and 93 clips of small sources (Lambda, arm64): the audio task's extract stage took 6.2 s and 25.7 s, and its audio stage 5.0 s and 23.2 s. On the same 93 clips with local files, the audio stage takes 5.6 s and the extract stage 2 ms with this change.

## Lambda before/after (a cut-heavy 4K edit)

A 840 s, 93-cut, 22 GB, 6-source 4K edit on a site, default flags, 3 cold runs each, same stack. Before is the release without #6172 and this change; after has both.

| | Before (3 runs) | After (3 runs) |
|---|---|---|
| Wall, submit to assemble | 388.9 / 386.7 / 302.7 s | 172.8 / 178.6 / 169.8 s |
| Lambda cost | $0.965 / $0.921 / $0.915 | $0.899 / $0.884 / $0.878 |
| Audio task | 182 / 179 s | 49.0 / 52.8 / 45.4 s |
| Audio task extract stage | ~112 s | 0.8 s |
| Max memory, plan Lambda | 3,026 MB of 10,240 | 3,034 / 3,031 / 3,035 MB |
| Max memory, audio task | 2,896 MB | 1,096 / 1,175 / 1,151 MB |

The audio task now finishes inside the chunk window. The plan (118 to 120 s here, all in its faster mode; the runs before took 198, 196 and 118 s) is now the largest part of the wall. These runs are on the first commit of this PR; the later commits only fix a start-before-timeline case and formatting.

## Probe dedupe on a site

The probes in `appendVideoAudioFromProbe` start together, one per `<video>`. On a site the sources' URLs are content-addressed (declared at compile in both the plan and the audio task), so the video-metadata cache returns the first call's in-flight promise to the rest and keeps its result: one probe per source however many clips use it. This is from the cache code, and the Lambda run's request count is the check. A plain https source that was not declared is probed per clip, as before.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Output parity (frames and audio against the baseline output) is being checked on the same runs and is not in this body yet.
- The mix itself is untouched: no change to summing order, limiter or loudness.

title: fix(studio-server): a history restore refuses to remove every tracked file
body:
## What

A project history restore no longer deletes every file in the project. It now refuses, writes nothing, and says why, in two cases:

- the restore would leave the project with no files at all (for example restoring "the start" of a history that was opened on an empty folder, so every file was added later). History's own hidden records (the media ledger and Studio's manifests) do not count as files kept, so a start that held only imported media is refused too;
- the restore targets "the start" while large files from the first open are still being copied into history, so the starting snapshot is not complete yet.

A restore that removes some files (the ones added after the chosen point) still works as before. A normal undo of the change that added a project's only file is unchanged (it does not go through restore).

## Why

A project lost its `index.html`, `compositions/*` and `assets/*` files; the folders stayed. A restore builds its plan as "every tracked file deleted, then the files at the chosen point laid back on top". When the chosen point is the start and the start snapshot is empty (history opened on an empty folder) or still missing files that are copied in the background, that plan deletes everything. File deletes do not remove folders, which matches what was left behind.

Every path that restores goes through the same function: the restore route and `hyperframes history restore`, and undo with "back to before" (the undo route, `hyperframes history undo --back-to-before`, and the Desktop chat's go-back and agent undo, which pass that mode). Going back to before a project's first recorded change is a restore of the start.

## Related work

None open for this case. Other open PRs edit the same file (media adoption on close, media not copied into history); this change is a few lines in the restore function and should rebase cleanly on either.

## How

- One guard in the engine's restore function, the single place all restore paths reach. It throws a new `HistoryRefusedError` (exported next to `HistoryClosedError`) before anything is written.
- The HTTP history routes already answer any thrown error as a 409 with its message, so they need no change.
- The CLI counts `HistoryRefusedError` as a refusal: one line on stderr (or JSON with `--json`) and exit code 2, like the other history refusals. Through a running preview server, the 409 already became a refusal.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

New tests, each entering through a real caller:

| Test | Enters through |
|---|---|
| restore of the start on a history opened empty refuses, files stay (`projectHistory.test.ts`) | `history.restore`, as the restore route and CLI call it |
| back-to-before of the first entry on that history refuses, files stay | `history.undo(id, { mode: "back-to-before" })`, as the undo route, CLI and Desktop call it |
| restore of the start when the start held only the media ledger refuses, files stay | `history.restore` |
| restore of the start while a large file is still being copied refuses; after the copy finishes it goes through | `history.restore` |
| restore to an earlier entry still removes the file added after it | `history.restore` |
| normal undo of the change that added the only file still removes it | `history.undo` |
| `POST /history/restore {point: "start"}` answers 409 with the message, files stay (`routes/history.test.ts`) | the restore route |
| `hyperframes history restore start` exits 2 with the message, files stay, both in-process and through a preview server (`commands/history.test.ts`) | the CLI command |

Failing first: with the source files reset to main and the new tests kept, the four refusal tests in studio-server failed (`promise resolved instead of rejecting`, `expected 200 to be 409`) and the CLI test failed in both modes (`expected +0 to be 2`). The two "still works" tests passed on main, as they should.

With the fix, three runs in a row of each touched file: `projectHistory.test.ts` + `routes/history.test.ts` 179 passed, 2 skipped (the same 2 skipped as on main), and `commands/history.test.ts` 50 passed. The ledger-only test also fails on main and on this PR's first commit (`promise resolved instead of rejecting`). `tsc --noEmit` for studio-server and cli, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files: clean.

Not exercised: the Desktop go-back UI against a real project (Desktop lives in another repository; a thrown error from this call reaches it the same way as its existing refusals such as "That change is already undone.", but I did not click through it).


## Package size budget

`@hyperframes/studio-server` packed budget goes from 142100 to 143700 in `scripts/package-size-budgets.json`. The guard adds real code to the package (+249 B packed, about +1 KB unpacked). The budget was already stale: main packed at 143380 B, 0.9% over the old budget and 141 B from the 1% limit, so any change here failed the merge queue's `verify:packed-manifests`. The new budget is what ships today, with the usual 1% tolerance on top.

title: fix(cli): snapshot --output clears only the frames it wrote
body:
## What

`hyperframes snapshot --output <dir>` now deletes only the images a snapshot run writes (its frame, review, `--against` and contact-sheet names). Every other image in that folder is left alone. Before this change it deleted every `.png`, `.jpg` and `.jpeg` in the folder, so `hyperframes snapshot . -o assets` or `-o .` erased the project's own images.

## Why

Data loss. The cleanup before each run used `/\.(png|jpg|jpeg)$/i` on everything in the output folder, and nothing checked that a file had come from an earlier snapshot run. A user who pointed `--output` at the project folder or its `assets/` folder lost every image in it, with no prompt and nothing in the output to say so.

## Related work

Builds on the `--keep` naming from #5605. No overlapping open PR.

## How

- One exported pattern, `SNAPSHOT_IMAGE_NAME` in `snapshot.ts`, sits next to `formatSnapshotTimestamp` and covers every image name a run writes into its folder:
  - default stills `frame-NN-at-Xs.png`
  - `--keep` stills `at-Xs.png`
  - `--against` reference frames `ref-[NN-]at-Xs.png` and pair sheets `pair-[NN-]at-Xs.jpg`
  - `--review` stills `beat-NN-at-Xs.png` and `seam-NN-S-at-Xs.png`
  - the sheets `contact-sheet[-N].jpg`, `review-beats[-N].jpg`, `review-phone[-N].jpg` and `review-seam-NN.jpg`

  `--zoom` writes under the same frame names. The cleanup uses this pattern instead of the extension check, so the files it reports as `replaced` are exactly the files it deletes.
- Why a name pattern and not a manifest of what the last run wrote: every name above is fixed by the command, so a pattern needs no extra state. A manifest would add a file the user can delete or edit, and it would miss frames written by versions that never wrote one.
- The match is now case-sensitive. The command only writes lowercase names, so `Notes.PNG` is a user file.
- The managed default folder needs no special case. Each run gets a fresh folder, so the run has nothing to clear there.
- No new flag and no prompt. Other commands keep the deletes they already do.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New tests in `packages/cli/src/commands/snapshot-contactSheet.test.ts` drive the real command through citty's `runCommand`, with the browser and server mocked the same way the file's other tests do:

- **`--output` cases.** `--output` points at `snapshots/`, at the project folder itself, and at `assets/`. Each folder starts with user images (`hero.png`, `logo.jpg`, `Notes.PNG`, `frame-hero.png`) and earlier output (default, `--keep`, `--against` and review frames, and paged sheets). After the run, every user image is unchanged, every earlier output file is gone, and the new frames are in place.
- **Review names.** Every name `reviewFrames` produces matches the pattern, so a later `--review` change that renames its stills fails here.

What I ran:
- With `snapshot.ts` from `main` and the new tests, the three `--output` cases fail with `ENOENT ... hero.png`: the user's image was deleted.
- With the fix, `snapshot-contactSheet.test.ts`, `snapshot.test.ts` and `snapshotReview.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row (100 tests each run).

What I did not exercise: a real browser capture, `--review`, `--against` or `--zoom` run end to end (their names are checked against the pattern, not captured), and Windows.

title: fix(core): color grading rebuilds the graded clips when a lost WebGL context is restored
body:
## What

After a WebGL context is lost and restored, every graded clip is graded again, including a clip that came on screen while the context was gone.

## Why

On loss the runtime marks its entries lost, and on restore it rebuilds the programs of the entries it still has. A graded clip that became visible during the loss tried to build an entry on a dead context, got none, and was never revisited: it reported "WebGL unavailable" and showed ungraded until some later scan, which does not run for a paused playhead. Restore now runs the same scan that creates entries from the `data-color-grading` attribute, so every shown graded clip gets one.

Reproduced in headless Chrome on a project with three graded clips, calling `WEBGL_lose_context` `loseContext()`, seeking to the second clip while lost, then `restoreContext()`: the second clip stayed "WebGL unavailable" before the change (also at the next seek) and is "Shader active" after.

## Test plan

- [x] New test in `colorGrading.test.ts`: a clip shown while the context is lost has no entry; after the restore event both clips are active. It fails on main and passes here (104 tests in the file pass).
- [x] Real Chrome repro above, before and after.

title: fix(core): release decoded preview audio once no clip uses its source
body:
## What

The preview audio transport now lets go of decoded audio once no clip in the film still uses that source.

## Why

When an audio clip falls back to the decoded path (for example cross-origin audio without a `crossorigin` attribute), the transport caches the decoded `AudioBuffer` by source URL. Nothing ever removed an entry except `destroy()`, so in a long editing session every source the film ever used stayed decoded in memory: each scene swap or replaced clip added buffers that were never released.

Repro: a composition with decoded-route audio clips, play, pause, change the clips' sources (or swap scenes in place), play again. Before this change the cache holds the old and new sources; after it, only the sources still in the document.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `WebAudioTransport.releaseDecodedExcept(els)` drops cached buffers whose source none of the given elements points at. The cache key is read through one helper (`decodeKey`) so the release and the lookup cannot disagree.
- `scheduleWebAudioForActiveClips` calls it with the same element list it is about to schedule. That pass is the only caller of `decodeAudioElement`, so a source it no longer visits can never be asked for again until it reappears.

Why this rule and not a playhead window or an LRU cap: each pass schedules every future clip at once, and each scheduled `AudioBufferSourceNode` already holds its own buffer. While playing, the decoded set for clips in the film is the working set, so evicting by playhead distance or by a byte cap would only add re-fetch and re-decode on the next resume or seek back (audio entering late). Dropping a cache entry never touches a playing source, because the node keeps its own reference.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added in `init.test.ts` ("decoded audio across edits"): 8 decoded clips, then an edit swaps 4 of them to new sources and playback resumes.
  - Before this change: the cache holds 12 sources (all 8 originals plus 4 new).
  - With this change: 8 (the 4 untouched plus the 4 new), and fetch is called 12 times in total, so the untouched clips are not re-decoded.
  - Mutation check: releasing every entry makes the fetch count 16 and the test fails.
- [x] `init.test.ts`, `webAudioTransport.test.ts`, `webAudioTransportIdle.test.ts`, `init.swapScenes.test.ts`: 510 passed. New test passed 3 runs in a row.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (core), oxfmt and oxlint on the changed files.
- [ ] Manual playback on a real audio device was not run.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: fix(cli): snapshot rejects a negative --at and builds its sheet from its own frames
body:
## What

Two fixes to `hyperframes snapshot`:

1. `--at` now refuses a negative, infinite, non-numeric or empty time before anything runs, with `--at must be comma-separated times in seconds, each 0 or more` and exit 1. Before, `--at -1` captured a still named `frame-00-at--1s.png`, `--at Infinity` captured one at `Infinity`, a bad entry like `NaN` was silently dropped, `1junk` was read as 1, and `--at ""` fell back to the default frames.
2. The contact sheet is built from the frames this run wrote, not from every `frame-*.png` in the output folder. Before, a user's own `frame-hero.png` in an `--output` folder landed in the sheet.

## Why

Stacked on #6176, which makes `--output` clear only the images whose names match the snapshot pattern. A `frame-00-at--1s.png` does not match that pattern, so the next run would leave it behind; and a user's `frame-hero.png` now survives the clear, so the folder glob put it in the sheet.

## Related work

Stacked on #6176 (base is its branch). Will retarget to `main` once #6176 merges.

## How

- `parseSnapshotAt` sits beside `parseSnapshotRange`, parses each entry the same way (`Number`, empty is invalid) and throws the same way (the CLI boundary prints the message and exits 1). It runs next to the `--range` parse, so the refusal comes before lint, the output folder or the browser. `--keep`'s duplicate-name check moved with it, unchanged.
- `createSnapshotContactSheet` takes the list of frame paths instead of a folder. Its only caller passes the paths the capture returned (the same list it already reports as artifacts). Order is capture order; labels still come from the `at-<time>s` part of each name. `--keep` and `--review` behave as before.
- Choice worth a look: an empty entry (`--at 1,`) and a value with trailing text (`--at 1.5s`) are now refused, matching `--range`. The documented examples all use plain numbers.

## Test plan

Through the real command (`runCommand(snapshotCommand, ...)`), in `snapshot-contactSheet.test.ts`:

- `refuses --at <value> before writing anything` for `-1`, `0.5,-1`, `Infinity`, `NaN`, `1,`, `1junk` and an empty value: the run rejects with the message, takes no screenshot and creates no output folder.
- `builds the sheet from this run's frames, not another frame-*.png in the folder`: an output folder holding `frame-hero.png` plus a two-frame run; a stub image library records every file the sheet reads, which must be exactly the two frames.

Measured: on #6176's code the new tests fail (9 failed, 15 passed: the seven `--at` cases resolve or fail with only `Command failed`, the sheet reads `frame-hero.png`, and the updated call-shape assertion sees a folder). With the fix: 24 passed, 3 runs in a row, together with `snapshotSampling.test.ts`. `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint` and `tsc --noEmit` for `packages/cli` are clean.

Not exercised: a real image library building a real sheet (the test stubs it), the CLI binary end to end, and the rest of the CLI suite.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: Caption reimport corrupts existing arrays containing ];
body:
## Describe the bug

Importing replacement transcript words can break a valid existing caption script while `transcribe` still returns exit 0 and `ok: true`. This happens when an old caption contains `];`, for example a programming screencast caption `items[i];`.

## Minimal reproduction

From a dependency-ready checkout of main `886e8696dfc43d748a221adf51678fc99d4ca74a`, create these files in a directory named `caption-repro`:

`captions.html`:

```html
<script>
const TRANSCRIPT = [{"id":"w0","text":"items[i];","start":0,"end":1}];
globalThis.captionWords = TRANSCRIPT;
</script>
```

`input.json`:

```json
[{"id":"w0","text":"Replacement caption","start":0,"end":1}]
```

Run:

```sh
bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts transcribe caption-repro/input.json --dir caption-repro --json
```

Inspect the rewritten `captions.html`. The same problem occurs with `const script` instead of `const TRANSCRIPT`.

## Expected behavior

Replace the entire old caption array, preserve the following JavaScript, and leave a valid script containing the new words.

## Actual behavior

The array-matching regex stops at `];` inside the old word string. It replaces only that prefix and leaves the rest of the old array after the new one. Compiling the output with `node:vm`'s `Script` throws `SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'start'`. Both supported variable names reproduce. The original script compiles.

| Same input | Main | Focused fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI result | Exit 0, `ok: true` | Exit 0, `ok: true` |
| Rewritten script | Invalid JavaScript, old array suffix remains | Valid JavaScript, complete replacement |
| Following caption code | Left after corrupted data | Preserved |

## Environment

Current source main `886e8696d`, package version 0.8.191. Linux x86_64, Node 26.11.1, Bun 1.4.1. The repository pins Bun 1.4.4; no version-dependent parser behavior is assumed. The real source CLI was invoked and its output compiled, without running transcription inference or playing media.

## Additional context

The cause is `patchCaptionHtml` in `packages/cli/src/whisper/normalize.ts`. This is the CLI write path. Issue #3852 and merged PR #3896 cover the separate Studio read path. PR #5226 fixes script escaping and replacement-token handling, which does not fix this existing-array boundary.

Public issues, PRs, comments and related work were checked before filing. A focused fix and two regression cases are prepared.

title: Looped audio exports only its first cycle, then silence
body:
## Describe the bug

A short music bed with native `loop` and an explicit longer slot exports only its first source cycle, then silence. The audio mix reports success. Audible video loops lose their repeated sound too.

## Minimal reproduction

From a dependency-ready checkout of main `886e8696dfc43d748a221adf51678fc99d4ca74a`, generate a synthetic one-second tone:

```sh
mkdir -p loop-repro
ffmpeg -v error -y -f lavfi -i sine=frequency=1000:duration=1:sample_rate=48000 -c:a pcm_s16le loop-repro/tone.wav
```

Save `loop-repro/repro.ts`:

```ts
import { resolve } from "node:path";
import { parseAudioElements, processCompositionAudio } from "../packages/engine/src/services/audioMixer.ts";

const dir = resolve("loop-repro");
const html = '<audio id="tone" src="tone.wav" data-start="0" data-duration="3" data-end="3" loop></audio>';
console.log(await processCompositionAudio(
  parseAudioElements(html), dir, resolve(dir, "work"), resolve(dir, "loop.m4a"), 3,
));
```

Run:

```sh
bun loop-repro/repro.ts
ffmpeg -hide_banner -i loop-repro/loop.m4a -af silencedetect=n=-50dB:d=0.1 -f null -
```

## Expected behavior

Repeat the one-second source until the three-second slot ends. With a source in-point, each cycle should start there, matching runtime playback.

## Actual behavior

Both baseline and focused fix return `success: true`, `tracksProcessed: 1`, and exactly three seconds of AAC/stereo/48 kHz output. The content differs:

| Same source and three-second slot | Main | Focused fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Detected silence | Starts at 1 s, lasts 2 s | None |
| Decoded PCM RMS in each second | `[2896, 0, 0]` | `[2896, 2896, 2896]` |

The source WAV is byte-identical in both runs. RMS samples exclude 50 ms at either edge of each second. No audio was played.

## Environment

Main `886e8696d`, engine 0.8.191. Linux x86_64, Node 26.11.1, Bun 1.4.1, FFmpeg/ffprobe n9.0.2. Repository Bun pin is 1.4.4. This directly executes the real engine parser and mixer and measures its M4A output; it does not claim a full browser/producer render.

## Additional context

`AudioElement` does not retain the native loop attribute, and `extractAudioSegment` reads only one source pass. The final mixer pads the remaining slot with silence. Runtime looping is supported, including the short background-music workflow in #41. Open #5462 and merged #5455 cover stream timing/video loop periods, not repeated audio extraction. The separately documented split-scene loop-phase limitation in #5454 is outside this reproduction.

title: fix(engine): repeat looped audio through its export slot
body:
## What

Short music tracks now repeat through their explicit `loop` slot in exported audio. Audible video loops repeat their sound too. The mixer could report success after playing one source cycle and padding the rest with silence.

Same byte-identical one-second tone and three-second slot:

| Output measurement | Main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Duration | 3.000000 s | 3.000000 s |
| Silence | 1 s through 3 s | None |
| Decoded PCM RMS per second | `[2896, 0, 0]` | `[2896, 2896, 2896]` |

## Why

The parser and producer discovery paths discarded loop intent, and audio extraction read the source only once.

## Related work

Fixes #6183. #41 establishes runtime music looping. #5455 and open #5462 address stream timing, not repeated audio extraction. Split-scene loop phase from #5454 remains outside this fix.

## How

Carry the loop flag into audio extraction. When a slot wraps, extract one cycle from the source in-point through EOF, including a video's silent tail, then repeat that finite PCM cycle before existing speed/rate processing. Input consumption and output length are bounded; the temporary cycle is removed in `finally`.

A wrapping track needs one extra extraction and one temporary PCM cycle. Ordinary non-loop extraction retains its existing path.

## Test plan

- [x] Four loop regressions fail on main; non-loop EOF and mute controls pass there.
- [x] Real FFmpeg output checked before/after with the same generated tone.
- [x] 137 engine tests pass, including trimmed loops, 2x/0.5x speed, rate ramps, slot boundaries and a video's silent tail.
- [x] Producer probe: 53 tests pass. Extraction: 22 tests pass.
- [x] Engine build, producer typecheck, lint and formatting.
- [x] Audio guide updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

Independent GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh review: no blocker found. The reviewer independently passed 102 tests plus 10 additional checks for alignment, trims, sidecar equality, envelopes, abort/timeout and cleanup..

No full browser/CLI video render, Windows run or distributed sidecar-loop integration is claimed. Local full-workspace build is limited by missing preinstalled inspector/AWS dependencies; Mintlify is absent. CI results are tracked on this PR.

title: fix(cli): preserve caption arrays during transcript reimport
body:
## What

Reimporting captions into an existing project now replaces the full transcript when an old caption contains `];`, such as `items[i];`. The CLI could report success while leaving invalid JavaScript in the caption HTML.

| Same caption import | Main | This PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `const TRANSCRIPT` with old text `items[i];` | Syntax error after import | Valid script with replacement words |
| `const script` with the same text | Syntax error after import | Valid script with replacement words |
| Following caption code | Follows a leftover array suffix | Preserved |

## Why

title: test(engine): the GPU probe tests do not start a Chrome from the host cache
body:
## What changes for you

Nothing visible. One engine test, "lets a host own GPU probe launch and cleanup", timed out at 5 s on a loaded CI runner and turned a required check red.

## Why

The test is fully mocked, but `resolveBrowserGpuMode("auto")` still looked up a real Chrome on the host. When the user's Puppeteer cache holds an older headless shell and not the managed one, that lookup starts the shell (`shellStarts` runs it synchronously, up to 10 s) before the mocked probe runs. A cold start on a busy runner can exceed the 5 s test limit.

## How

The `resolveBrowserGpuMode` tests now name a shell through `PRODUCER_HEADLESS_SHELL_PATH`, so discovery does not run. A new test puts a marker-writing fake shell in an older cache version and checks it is not started; it fails without the stub and passes with it.

## What I did not exercise

I did not reproduce the CI timeout itself. The mechanism is shown by the new test, and the cause on that runner (an older shell in its cache) is my reading of the code, not something I saw. If the test times out again, this was not the whole story.
