title: fix(cli): keep beats audio paths inside the project
body:
## What

`hyperframes beats` now refuses a music `src` that resolves outside the project directory. It also refuses to write the beat file anywhere outside the project. Both checks follow symlinks.

## Why

The command turns the music `src` into a relative path with `audioRelPathForSrc`, then resolves it against the project directory without checking that the result stays inside. URL parsing does not normalize a src such as `..%2F..%2Fsecret.wav`, so it decodes to `../../secret.wav`. The command then read that file from outside the project and wrote `beats/../../secret.wav.json`, which also lands outside the project. A symlinked folder inside the project, such as `assets` or `beats/assets`, could also send the read or the write outside.

## Related work

Builds on #5310 and #5327, which changed how the music source is found and how its path is derived. This change only adds checks on the resolved paths.

## How

- The read path uses `resolveWithinProject` from `@hyperframes/core`. It resolves both sides with realpath and returns null when the audio file is outside the project. The command then fails with a clear error.
- The write path is checked with `isSafePath(project.dir, outPath)` before any folder is created. It resolves the deepest existing ancestor with realpath, so `mkdir` only creates folders that do not exist yet inside the project.
- Both helpers compare full path segments, so a file named `..music.wav` in the project is still accepted.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added in `packages/cli/src/commands/beats.test.ts`:
  - `refuses a music src that resolves outside the project` (encoded `../`, fails on `main`)
  - `refuses music read through a symlinked folder that points outside the project`
  - `refuses to write a beat file through a symlinked folder that points outside the project`
  - `accepts an in-project file whose name starts with two dots`
  
  The two symlink tests fail on `main` and on the first version of this PR. The two-dots test fails on the first version of this PR, which used a lexical check. All pass with this change.
- [x] The beats suite, `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt pass for the CLI package.

title: fix(cli): a check that hits its deadline keeps the findings it already made
body:
## What changes for you

When `check` hits its deadline (no progress for 120 s), the report now keeps what it had already found: the layout and contrast findings from the samples that finished, and the page's own console and network findings. The deadline error is still in the report and still names the step it stopped at, for example "while running the overlap pass", with the seconds spent per step. Before, all of that was dropped and the report held the deadline error alone.

## Why

A large project can run `check` for a long time. When the deadline fired, the work of every finished sample was thrown away, so the person got no result at all.

## How

`CheckDeadline.keepPartial` lets a stage register how to read what it has so far. The sample grid registers its finished samples, and the browser step registers the runtime findings. When the check fails, the pipeline builds the report from those instead of an empty result, and `browserSkipped` is false when anything was kept.

## Tests

A deadline during the overlap pass keeps the layout finding from the finished samples, marks the browser as not skipped, and still carries the deadline finding. The test fails without the change. The check, deadline, browser and progress suites pass 3 runs in a row (182 tests).

## What I did not do

This covers the CLI's own deadline. A caller that kills `check` from outside after its own wall-clock limit gets no report, because the process never gets to write one. I could not reproduce a slow `check`: a 40-minute project with about 1,760 elements finished in 43 s. The step that is slow on the reporter's project is still unknown.

title: Bundling corrupts data URLs in image srcset
body:
### Describe the bug An image with a valid data URL in `srcset` displays in the authored HTML, but disappears after bundling. `bundleToSingleHtml` splits the URL at its comma and inserts a space, so Chrome receives an invalid image URL. `snapshot` can return `ok: true` with a failed-image warning and a broken image in the frame. The same split breaks local filenames such as `hero,blue.png`, including when rebasing an entry in a subdirectory. It occurs with both default options and `inlineAssets: false`. ### Minimal reproduction Save this as `srcset-repro/index.html`: ```html
``` ### Steps to reproduce From a built checkout at `0d104e6fca496f7d8659c9266813fc6750294635`: ```sh bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts lint ./srcset-repro --json bun packages/cli/src/cli.ts snapshot ./srcset-repro --at 0.5 --no-end --describe false --output ./srcset-frames --json ``` Open the original HTML in Chrome as a control and compare the snapshot at 0.5 seconds. ### Expected behavior The 320×180 frame contains the authored red rectangle at 160×90. A data URL in `srcset` remains intact, and local candidates containing commas resolve as complete URLs. ### Actual behavior Static lint passes. The snapshot succeeds with an image-load warning, but contains a broken image. In Chrome 152 the original image reports `naturalWidth: 160, naturalHeight: 90`; the bundled image reports `0, 0`. The bundled attribute changes `data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2...` to `data:image/svg+xml;base64, PHN2...`. ### Environment - Main: `0d104e6fca496f7d8659c9266813fc6750294635`, Core 0.8.191 - Linux x86_64, Bun 1.4.1, Node 26.11.1 - Chrome 152; reproduced through the actual source CLI snapshot workflow and browser inspection ### Additional context Both srcset rewriting passes in `packages/core/src/compiler/htmlBundler.ts` split the entire attribute on commas. The [HTML srcset parsing algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/images.html#parse-a-srcset-attribute) treats commas inside a URL token as part of the URL. Related but distinct: #6133 / #6134 bound total asset inlining size; #5298 handles srcset-only image capture selection. Neither addresses URL tokenization.

title: fix(engine): h265 renders no longer fail on hosts with more than 16 cores
body:
Every h265 render failed on a host with more than 16 cores: ffmpeg exited 183 with `frameNumThreads (--frame-threads) must be [0 .. X265_MAX_FRAME_THREADS)`. The thread count introduced for stable bitstreams passed the CPU quota straight to libx265, which accepts at most 16.

The one place that sets the count now caps libx265 at 16 (`X265_MAX_THREADS`) and leaves libx264 as it was. Output stays the same on every host above 16 cores.

Tests:
- Unit: 64 cores gives 16 for libx265 and 64 for libx264 (the old signature cannot express this, so it fails on main).
- Real ffmpeg: `-c:v libx265 -threads 17` exits non-zero, `-threads 16` encodes.

title: perf(aws-lambda): cloud renders plan without reading video bytes and start chunks sooner
body:
## What changed

A cloud render's plan no longer touches video bytes, and each chunk starts capturing sooner. Six changes, each in the code it names:

1. **Stored probe facts.** `sites create` stores each video's ffprobe JSON, its final-frame time and its last packet length beside the video, keyed by content hash (like the audio sidecars). The plan reads that instead of probing the file over the network.
2. **Frame counts without decoding.** A window that ends a second or more inside its source takes the expected frame count. A window that reaches the source's end takes it from the stored final frame (constant frame rate; a late-starting video stream only when its last packet is a full frame, otherwise the old tail decode runs). Remaining tail decodes run 16 wide (`HF_TAIL_PROBE_SLOTS`).
3. **Chunk encode overlaps capture** for closed-GOP chunks (`canEncodeWhileCapturing` no longer excludes `lockGopForChunkConcat`); output is byte-identical to encoding after capture (new test).
4. **Locked warmup ticks stop sleeping once the page is ready.** The tick count stays 60, so frame times are unchanged; each Chrome start saves ~2 s, twice per chunk.
5. **Logs:** `[plan] extract phases`, `[audio] phases` (the plan never passed its logger to the audio stage).
6. Engine package size budget raised to 456,055 packed / 1,526,873 unpacked bytes (5% over measured): the facts reader and tail-count code live in the engine.

## What I measured (93-cut 4K edit, 6 sources, 22 GB, 840 s, cold functions, real `sites create`)

| | 0.8.190 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| wall | 389 / 387 / 303 s | 66 / 49 / 51 s |
| cost | $0.92-0.97 | $0.93 / 0.90 / 0.93 |
| plan | 118-198 s | 2.2 s (14 s on the first plan after a redeploy) |
| plan memory | 5.4 GB | 0.55 GB |

- Frames and audio are identical to 0.8.190 on every run (21,000 frames, same md5 per run).
- 30-minute 1080p edit, 204 chunks, real `sites create` (15 s): wall 38.5 / 40.7 / 38.9 s, $0.547 / 0.531 / 0.550, plan 2.5-2.9 s; the 54,000 frames and the audio are identical across the three runs. The released 0.8.190 renders it in 41.9 s / $0.580 (one cold run, the first after a redeploy) with the same frames and audio, so on a single long clip this PR is about 6% faster and 7% cheaper; the big win is the cut-heavy multi-source edit above.
- Warmup change: 4 distributed-simulated fixtures (CSS keyframes from t=0, a video at frame 0, a web font, GSAP) rendered with and without the sleeps: 0 differing frames, identical final mp4s.
- End-window count: 8,037 randomized windows against real ffmpeg: 0 wrong, 3 declined (fall back to the decode).
- Red then green: remoteTail, tailCount, encodeWhileCapturing, warmupTicks, plan audio-log tests each fail without their change.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The stored final frame is used only when the plan's ffprobe has the same major version as the one that stored it (otherwise the plan probes the tail itself). The stream metadata JSON is still trusted, and the md5 runs above used a `sites create` ffprobe of the same build as the Lambda's, so they do not exercise a version mismatch.
- Sites made before this change have facts without the last packet length: their end windows still decode the tail (no regression, no speedup) until `sites create` runs again.
- A late-starting video whose last packet is short, VFR sources, HDR and color-converted windows: all fall back to the old decode.
- GPU hosts and non-Lambda targets for the warmup change; the frame check ran on a 4-vCPU SwiftShader host and on Lambda.
- Cost is flat to slightly lower per render (Lambda-seconds), not a large drop; the chunk time (~27 s x 254 chunks) is the remaining lever.

title: fix(engine): clips with data-duration and no data-end end where their duration says
body:
A clip with `data-duration` but no `data-end` was mixed as if it had no length: `parseAudioElements` read only `data-end`, so the mixer played such a clip to the end of its source file. A render never hits this because core's `compileTimingAttrs` writes `data-end = data-start + data-duration` first. Any caller that mixes from the authored HTML (an offline estimate, the standalone mixer) got a different, louder mix: on a long film whose voice lines have only `data-duration`, each line overlapped the next and the mix read about 3 dB hotter than the rendered one.

`parseAudioElements` now resolves the end by the same rule: `data-end`, else resolved start plus `data-duration`, else unknown. A clip with no length at all now logs a warning naming the clip before it plays to the end of its source, instead of doing so silently.

Tests:
- `parseAudioElements` clip end: duration-only, `data-end` wins, neither authored, and a relative `data-start` (the duration and relative-start cases fail on main).
- Mixer: an open-ended clip warns with its id (fails on main).
- `renderMediaCollector` expectation updated: an uncompiled `<video data-duration=2 data-has-audio>` now gets its audio window 4 to 6, matching its video, where it used to run on to the host's end.

Existing engine and producer suites: engine audioMixer 85/85 and `tsc` clean for engine and producer; the producer suites I ran fail the same 104 tests as main on the devbox, no new ones.

title: fix(producer): a render's page-error count includes what the capture workers saw
body:
## What changes for you

A render's failure summary now counts the page errors the capture workers saw. Before, a composition whose script threw at load could fail with `pageErrors: 0` in the summary while the log showed the errors.

## Why

The summary counts `[Browser:PAGEERROR]` lines from one console buffer, and in parallel capture that buffer belongs to the probe session. The worker sessions that load and render the page kept their own buffers, which were never read, so their errors were never counted.

## How

On failure, the `CaptureFailure` that `executeParallelCapture` throws now carries every worker's page-error lines (including workers that did not fail), and `getCaptureStageBrowserConsole` hands them to the failure summary. On success, each worker result carries its session's page-error console lines. The disk and streaming capture stages merge those into the console lines the summary reads, once per distinct line. #6156's behaviour is unchanged: a script that throws is still skipped with a warning and the render goes on.

## Tests

A parallel capture where one worker fails: the thrown failure carries both workers' page-error lines (fails without the change), and the failure handler's console reader returns them.

A parallel capture where two workers report the same page error now counts 1 in the diagnostics summary; the test fails without the change. The capture stage and observability suites pass 3 runs in a row, and the streaming stage suite passes under `bun test` (16 tests, 3 runs). Every capture failure now carries the page's error lines: `classifyCaptureFailure` takes them (the engine passes the dying worker's own), so a worker's own failure and the pool failure both hold them. The parallel disk stage and the streaming pool wrap their failures in `CaptureStageError` with the probe session's console, as the sequential stage already does; the stall error stays unwrapped and typed. New tests: the classifier keeps and takes the lines; a worker that fails hands the pool its own lines (fails without the engine change); a failed parallel disk capture reports probe console plus page errors, and a streaming render whose worker dies reports the script's error (both fail with the wrap removed). Engine and stage suites pass 3 runs in a row.

## What I did not do

I did not make a load-time script error fail the render fast. That would reverse the skip-with-warning behaviour, which is a separate decision. The HDR and segmented capture stages still report only their own console.

title: fix(core): a video that starts a cut far behind the playhead catches up in steps, not at a flat 3%
body:
A playing video is steered back onto the playhead by rate, not seeked (a seek resets the decoder), at a flat 3% (#4511). A clip that waits on data at a cut starts 100-350 ms behind, and 3% closes that in 3-10 s, longer than a short clip plays. The picture trails the voice for the whole clip.

Measured in Desktop on a Riverside two-camera podcast episode, sampling every playing `<video>` against the audio-implied playhead every 100 ms: clips 2-4 started up to 100 ms behind and closed at about 35 ms per second (the 3% steer), the longest taking about 3 s.

The steer now steps with the lag: 3% up to 100 ms, 10% up to 300 ms, 25% beyond, in both directions. The rate is still only written when a step changes.

Tests: a far-behind and a far-ahead video steer by step, then step down as the lag closes; the existing 3% case now uses a lead that is still in the 3% step. `media.test.ts` passes; the repo typecheck only needs the generated runtime files built.

Not verified: that this removes the desync Vance saw (intermittent, preview only). That needs a play of an episode with this runtime in Desktop.

title: feat(studio): Tooltip can wrap a long label and cap it at a number of lines
body:
## What

`Tooltip` takes an optional `lines` prop. Given one, a long label wraps at a 300px reading width, breaks a long URL or path rather than cutting it off, and stops at that many lines with an ellipsis. Without it, nothing changes: the label stays on one line, as before.

## Why

Today every tooltip label is `whitespace-nowrap` and the popup takes no class, so a long label (for example a project's full prompt shown on hover) renders as one line that runs off the screen. A host app had no way to show such text in the shared tooltip.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `lines` swaps `whitespace-nowrap` for `max-w-[300px] whitespace-normal break-words` on the popup, and wraps the label in a span with Tailwind's `line-clamp-(--tooltip-lines)`, the count passed as the `--tooltip-lines` custom property.
- The default path renders exactly the markup it did before: same classes, no span.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: a label with no `lines` stays one line with no wrapper; a long label with `lines={3}` gets the reading width, word breaking and the clamp set to 3. The five existing Tooltip tests still pass; all seven pass, three runs in a row. `tsc --noEmit` passes for `packages/studio`.
- [x] Manual testing performed: a throwaway page on Studio's own dev server rendered a long label (with a long URL in it) and a short one, without and with `lines={3}`, in paper and dark, shot in headless Chrome. The short label renders the same either way.
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): the prop's own doc comment.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

No `lines` (the default, unchanged): the long label is one line that runs off the screen.

title: fix(producer): report unavailable frame checks in debug logs
body:
## What

Record `artifact_frame_count_unavailable` at debug level when artifact validation expects a frame count but the container supplies no usable count. The event includes the output path, expected frames, and the render's scoped job ID. It is captured in `render.log` with `--debug` and is available to custom producer loggers.

## Why

WebM and HLS commonly omit frame-count metadata. A generated four-second WebM with 90 frames passes a 120-frame expectation because its duration still matches; currently this leaves no indication that the frame-count check was skipped. The diagnostic makes this validation limit traceable. Default console output stays quiet.

## Related work

Refs #3484, including the [current status comment](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues/3484#issuecomment-6381274750). This follows the debug-level option accepted in #5242's review. PNG counting is already covered by that merged work. This contribution reports unavailable frame checks; verifying the missing frames themselves still depends on obtaining a usable count.

## How

Pass the existing scoped render logger into the artifact transaction. Emit the event after the duration gate when a requested frame count is unavailable. Keep known-count, duration, dimension, and PNG checks intact; a failing diagnostic sink cannot change the validation result. Document the limitation and debug logging in the producer reference.

## Test plan

- [x] 359 unit tests across artifact transactions, orchestration, execution context, file logging, and console logging pass. All 9 real HLS pipeline tests and 4 rename-retry tests also pass. Five new diagnostic regression cases fail on the unchanged implementation. Coverage includes invalid counts, default silence, known-count shortfalls, duration failures, HLS, and logger failures.
- [x] Full workspace build, producer typecheck, CLI rebuild, lint/format, test reachability, normal commit hooks, and both comment checks pass.
- [x] Real built-CLI WebM renders with and without `--debug`: both decode to 10 frames / 1 second. Debug records exactly one event with the job ID in the retained log; normal output and stdout contain no event. The existing fixture passes CLI lint and browser check.
- [x] Producer documentation updated; Mint validation and broken-link checks pass.
- [x] Integrate current main’s retrying artifact rename while retaining the scoped logger. The real HLS pipeline test verifies the event includes the output, expected frames, and render job ID; removing the logger connection reproduces one failure with the eight existing render checks still passing.
- [x] Comments describe the validation constraint and diagnostic failure isolation.

title: fix(cli): remove-background keeps going on CPU when a provider fails on a frame
body:
## What changed
`remove-background` falls back to the CPU only when the execution provider fails to load the model. A provider that loads and then fails on a frame ends the whole run. On Apple Silicon a long, large clip can fail partway with CoreML's "Non-zero status code returned while running CoreML node ... Unable to compute the prediction using a neural network model", losing minutes of work with no way forward except re-running with `--device cpu`.

Now, when the first run of a frame on a non-CPU provider throws, the session is recreated on the CPU provider and that frame runs again, once per session. The switch is reported through `onProgress`, and `session.provider` (so the command's summary and JSON) reads `CPU` afterwards. A failure on the CPU provider, or a second failure, still throws as before.

## Tests
- `inference.test.ts`: a run that throws the CoreML error recreates the session with `["cpu"]`, releases the old one, returns the frame, reports `CPU`, and does not recreate again on the next frame.
- A CPU-only session that throws is not retried; a CPU session failing after the fallback ends the run.

fails without the fix: the first and third new tests fail on main's `inference.ts` (12 tests in the file pass with the change, 2 of the new ones fail without it).

## What I did NOT exercise
- A real CoreML failure: it needs Apple Silicon and a clip that triggers it; the tests stand in for the session with a fake `onnxruntime` that throws the same error text.
- Whether the CPU run is fast enough for a long 4K clip.

title: fix(cli): lint accepts one composition file as well as a project directory
body:
## What

`hyperframes lint <file>.html` failed with "Not a directory" because the argument was always treated as a project directory. It now accepts one composition file: the project is the nearest folder above it that has an `index.html`, and only that file is linted. A file under `compositions/` is linted as a sub-composition, so root-only rules do not fire on it.

## Why

A single-file argument is the natural call from an editor or a script, and the old error does not say what to pass instead.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/utils/project.test.ts` covers a composition file as the entry of the project holding it, the project's own `index.html` as the whole project, and a plain directory still working. The file cases fail on main, where a file argument is rejected. Lint package 1039 tests, cli typecheck and oxfmt are clean; the new tests pass 3 runs in a row.

## Size

About 85 changed lines, below the 100-line floor. It stands alone because it is one user-visible CLI fix with no natural pair; splitting the helper from the command would leave a PR with no effect.

title: preview: orphan cleanup kills other tools' detached headless Chrome processes (opt-out or scope to own processes)
body:
### Summary
On every `hyperframes preview` call (including reconnecting to an already running studio), `killOrphanedProcesses()` terminates **every** process tree of the current user with PPID 1 whose command line contains `chrome-headless-shell`, `chrome_headless_shell` or `puppeteer_dev_chrome_profile` (`packages/cli/src/utils/orphanCleanup.ts`, called from `packages/cli/src/commands/preview.ts`).

On a shared developer machine this also kills detached headless browsers that belong to *other* tools (for example Playwright/Puppeteer runners or automation that was started detached), not only leftovers of HyperFrames sessions.

### Reproduction (macOS, observed on 0.8.97; same code on `main` / v0.8.191)
1. Start a detached headless browser from another tool so that its parent exits (PPID becomes 1), e.g. `nohup chrome-headless-shell --remote-debugging-port=0 about:blank >/dev/null 2>&1 & disown`.
2. Run `hyperframes preview <project>`.
3. The unrelated `chrome-headless-shell` process is terminated.

### Expected
Cleanup only affects processes that HyperFrames itself started, or can be turned off.

### Suggestion
- An opt-out, e.g. `HYPERFRAMES_NO_ORPHAN_CLEANUP=1` or `--no-orphan-cleanup`, and/or
- scope the cleanup to HyperFrames-owned processes (e.g. a marker in the user-data-dir/profile path, or a PID registry in the state directory).

Context: we embed `hyperframes preview` in a local design tool and currently have to warn users before every editor start. Related: #1038 (the original orphan problem).

title: preview: server scan starts at the saved session port and probes up to 100 unrelated ports despite an explicit --port
body:
### Summary
`readPreviewLifecycleState` starts the server scan at the **saved session port** (`saved?.port ?? startPort`, `packages/cli/src/commands/previewLifecycle.ts`), and `scanActiveServers` probes `MAX_PORT_SCAN` (100) consecutive ports with `GET /__hyperframes_config`. If the saved session came from a different port range than the one requested now, the CLI probes up to 100 unrelated local ports before honoring the explicit `--port`; a start that ends up on another port can add a second scan window.

### Reproduction (observed on 0.8.97; same logic on `main` / v0.8.191)
1. `hyperframes preview <project> --port 3021`, then stop it (the session state keeps 3021).
2. `hyperframes preview <project> --port 32521`.
3. The CLI sends `GET /__hyperframes_config` to 3021–3120 (other local services) before using 32521.

### Why it matters
Hosts that embed the CLI may only be allowed to touch a defined port range; probing unrelated ports reaches other local services.

### Suggestion
When `--port` is given explicitly, scan only the requested window (or check only the saved port itself), or make the scan window configurable / allow disabling the scan.

title: studio: GSAP plugins are loaded from cdn.jsdelivr.net at runtime (offline / no third-party requests)
body:
### Summary
The studio/preview loads GSAP plugins from `cdn.jsdelivr.net` at runtime: `packages/core/src/gsapCdn.ts` builds `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/gsap@<version>/dist/...` (default 3.15.0) and `motionPathPluginUrl()`. Opening the editor requests `MotionPathPlugin.min.js` from jsDelivr.

### Why it matters
- Offline or restricted-network setups cannot load the plugin.
- Privacy-restricted environments do not want third-party requests from a local editor.
- It mirrors the issue fixed for pr-to-video in #6028.

### Suggestion
Serve GSAP and its plugins from the locally installed package (the CLI already ships them for renders), or allow a local base URL via config/env, e.g. `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL`.

Observed on 0.8.97; same code on `main` / v0.8.191.

title: fix(studio): a scene swap no longer keeps the previous preview window in memory
body:
## What

A scene swap no longer leaves a listener on the caller's cancel signal, so the preview no longer holds old projects in memory after a scene swap.

## Why

`sceneSwapFor` (`packages/studio/src/player/sceneSwap.ts`) added an `abort` listener to the caller's `cancel` signal on every swap and never removed it. `useTimelinePlayer` keeps that controller in `swapCancelRef` until the next edit, and it is not aborted when a swap succeeds. The listener's closure scope holds the swap's `win` (the preview iframe's window) and the runtime's `__hfSwapScenes`, so after the preview later reloads as a new document, the old window and its whole film DOM stay reachable.

Seen in a heap snapshot of a desktop host after a few scene edits and a forced GC: `swapCancelRef.current` -> `AbortSignal` -> abort listener -> closure scope -> previous window -> previous document.

To reproduce: open a long project, edit inside a scene a few times, take a heap snapshot after a forced GC, and look for a second preview `HTMLDocument` retained through an `AbortSignal` listener.

## No visible change

The change only removes an event listener when a swap settles; nothing on screen moves.

## Related work

Refs the long-session memory investigation in the desktop host. Separate from the far-scenes rendering work, which does not touch this file.

## How

The handler is named and removed in the existing `finally`, so it lives only as long as the swap it can cancel. An abort before the swap settles still cancels it as before.

## Test plan

- New test in `sceneSwap.test.ts`: three successful swaps and one refused swap on one long-lived signal leave no abort listener on it. Fails without the fix (on main: `expected 4 to be +0`, one listener per swap; also fails when only the `removeEventListener` line is deleted), passes with it, 3 runs in a row (8/8 tests in the file).
- Studio `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint and oxfmt clean on the changed files.
- Desktop host, synthetic 45-scene film with the element count cut to a tenth, after 4 scene edits and a forced GC: one film in memory (144k DOM nodes) with this change, two (281k) without it. The host already carried its own fix for a second holder of the same window, so this listener was the last one.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

title: fix(engine): renames ride out Windows file locks instead of failing the render
body:
## What changes for you

On Windows, a render no longer fails with `EPERM`, `EACCES` or `EBUSY` when a file it just wrote is still held for a few milliseconds (antivirus, the indexer, a process that has only just let go). The most visible case was `audio_processing_failed` while mixing audio. Other platforms behave as before.

## Why

Windows refuses to rename a file while anything holds a handle on it, and the hold usually clears within milliseconds. The render code renamed with a bare `renameSync` / `rename` in about fifteen places, so the first refusal ended the render.

## How

- New `renameWithRetry` / `renameWithRetryAsync` in `packages/engine/src/utils/renameWithRetry.ts`, exported from the engine. On Windows only, `EPERM`, `EACCES` and `EBUSY` are retried with 10 ms doubling to 640 ms (about 1.3 s in total), then the original error is rethrown. Everything else throws at once.
- Every rename in the engine and producer sources goes through it (the last grep left only the artifact transaction's injected file system, whose default is wrapped): audio mix and envelope, true-peak correction, segment manifest, extraction cache publish, frame merge, GIF prep, distributed plan, plan V2, assemble, MP4 stitch, and the artifact transaction's default file system.
- Not changed: the CLI and core packages (config, downloads, fonts, upgrade). They are not on the render path.

## Handle ownership

I looked for a handle the render holds itself. The audio path opens no streams (reads and writes are whole-file sync calls), and every ffmpeg step resolves on the child's `close` event, after its stdio is closed, before the rename. I found no self-held handle. The remaining holders are outside the process, so retrying is the fix. I could not run Windows here, so this is from reading the code, not from a Windows repro.

## Tests

- `renameWithRetry.test.ts`: retries then succeeds; rethrows the original error once the budget is spent; no retry off Windows or for `ENOENT`; the async twin retries.
- `audioVolumeEnvelope.test.ts`: with `process.platform` set to `win32` and `EPERM` injected on the first two renames, the envelope is applied. With the call site put back to a bare rename this test fails.
- Engine: new and envelope tests 19/19 three runs in a row; audio mixer, extraction cache and parallel coordinator suites pass. Producer: 226 of 227 in the touched suites (artifact transaction, MP4 stitch, assemble, plan V2, GIF prep, plan). The one failure, `keeps assembled loudness within 0.1 LUFS of the frame-fitted float delivery`, fails the same way on a tree without this change.

title: fix(core): color grading builds a new WebGL context when a lost one is never restored
body:
When the browser evicts the shared WebGL context that color grading draws with (a page holding many other contexts) and never restores it, every graded clip stayed hidden for good: the runtime hid the canvases on `webglcontextlost` and waited for a `webglcontextrestored` that never came.

After a 3 s grace period with the context still lost, the runtime now creates a new shared context and moves each tracked clip onto it (new program, no stale LUT or effect targets), then redraws. A restore that does arrive in time still wins, and a late restore event from the abandoned context is ignored. If a new context cannot be created, it tries again after the same period.

Tests: a clip is graded, the context is lost with no restore event, 3 s pass (fake timers): the clip is graded again on the new context, and a late restore from the old context leaves it active. The test fails on main.

title: test: the lifecycle and thumbnail suites load cold modules in a hook, not in their first test
body:
## What changes for you

Nothing in the CLI. `cli.lifecycle.test.ts` and the studio thumbnail suite stop timing out on the Windows engine-cli and studio-2 jobs.

## Why

The first test in that file to touch the CLI's module graph paid the whole cold import (every file read for the first time on a Windows runner) inside its own 20 s test timeout, so it failed whenever the runner was slow, on PRs that never touched the CLI. On Linux the same test takes about 0.1 s warm, so the time is file loading, not the test.

## How

A `beforeAll` imports the modules the tests lean on (citty, core's figma entry, telemetry client, failure tracking, project resolution, render success state) with a 120 s hook timeout, so every test measures only its own work. The tests are otherwise unchanged.

The studio thumbnail suite (`vite.browser.test.ts`) had the same shape: its first test timed out at 5 s on a cold Windows runner while `generateThumbnail` loaded puppeteer for the first time, and the next test then failed only because the timed-out request kept running and closed pages after the next test's reset. A `beforeAll` (60 s) now loads puppeteer, and an `afterEach` cancels any request a test left running.

## Tests

The lifecycle file passes 3 runs in a row locally (14 tests) and the thumbnail file 3 runs (9 tests). I could not time a cold Windows import here; the Windows engine-cli and studio-2 jobs on this PR are the proof, and I will re-run them twice more and report all three results.

PR_SIZE_OK: about 30 added lines across two test files, one concern (cold Windows load inside a test's time limit).

title: fix(cli): allow disabling orphan browser cleanup
body:
## What

Add `HYPERFRAMES_NO_ORPHAN_CLEANUP=1` so embedded preview sessions can disable startup cleanup of detached headless Chrome processes.

## Why

The cleanup identifies processes by PPID and generic Chrome markers, which can include browsers launched by other tools. Integrations need a way to leave those processes alone.

## Related work

Refs #6203. This provides the requested opt-out; default cleanup behavior remains unchanged. Scoping default cleanup to HyperFrames-owned processes remains separate work.

## How

Return before reading the process table when the environment variable is exactly `1`. The guard lives in the shared cleanup entry point used by preview and the render setup worker. Document the preview invocation and the tradeoff that crashed-session browsers remain running when cleanup is disabled.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: all 14 tests across the three orphan-cleanup test files passed. The new regression checks that disabling cleanup performs neither process enumeration nor tree termination; the existing default scan test still passes.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md: no comments added.

Changed TypeScript files pass oxlint with zero warnings/errors. Repository formatting and both comment checks pass.

title: chore(engine): re-baseline the package size budget to what ships plus 5%
body:
## What changes for you

Nothing in the product. The `@hyperframes/engine` package size budget in `scripts/package-size-budgets.json` is re-baselined so ordinary changes stop failing the merge queue's `verify:packed-manifests`.

## Why

Main packs engine at 432738 B against a budget of 428562 B, which leaves 109 B before the 1% limit (unpacked: 1508 B). Any change that adds a couple of lines to engine fails the Build job, and in the merge queue that shows up as a silent drop. `@hyperframes/studio-server` was in the same state and dropped #6175 from the queue; that one is re-baselined in #6175 itself.

## How

The budgets are set at the measured size plus 5% (`SIZE_BUDGET_HEADROOM`), which is what `verify:packed-manifests` suggests. Engine packed 428562 to 454376, unpacked 1436293 to 1521604. The other packages measured on current main have at least 1586 B before their limit (aws-lambda is the next tightest).

## Tests

`node scripts/verify-packed-manifests.mjs` on a full build of current main passes with these numbers; engine measures 432738 packed and 1449147 unpacked, both above the ratchet floor (85% of budget).

PR_SIZE_OK: one number in a JSON file, two lines changed.

title: fix(studio-server): undo and restore keep the media they delete or replace
body:
## What

Undo, redo and restore no longer lose a media file. Before history deletes or overwrites a video or audio file (or any file over 64 MiB), it sets that file's bytes aside, so the next redo or restore can put the identical file back.

## Why

Since project history stopped copying media into its store, an Undo of a change that created a media file deleted the file, and the Redo that followed was refused with "An earlier version of ... is not kept". The same hole lost the replaced bytes when a restore overwrote a media file. History now never applies a change it cannot reverse: `writeProjectFile` is the one place every undo, redo and restore writes through, so the fix is there.

## How

- `BlobStore.keep(absPath, remove)` hashes the file and stores its bytes under `<history>/aside/`, by rename when the file is deleted (copy across volumes, or when it is only being overwritten).
- `has`, `read` and `writeTo` find the bytes there. After an undo or restore has written all its files, `release` frees the aside copies it used, so storage is paid only for files the user actually undid away. A checkout of an old version only reads them, and several paths with identical bytes in one change all get restored before the copy goes.
- Set-aside bytes do not count toward the history budget (they are the user's own file, undone away), so undoing media larger than the budget never folds history away.
- The set-aside bytes live apart from `blobs/` on purpose: reclaiming old media copies (on open and `hyperframes clean`) must never take them. `prune` still removes them when their entries fold away.

## What I measured

New `undoUncopied.test.ts`, failing first on main with "An earlier version of join.mp4 is not kept" in all three cases: undo then redo returns identical bytes; the same after the history is closed and opened again; undoing a restore returns the bytes the restore overwrote; a checkout of the old version in between does not spend the set-aside copy; two files with identical bytes made in one change both come back. The last two cases failed on the first version of this PR and pass now. A sixth case (media larger than the budget keeps the whole history and the redo) failed on the previous head. The same bytes at two paths in separate entries also come back through undo and redo in any order (each set-aside copy is held per project path and freed when the last path has its file back). History suite 235 passed. An independent undo/redo script over the built `dist/history/index.js` (a media file placed, undone, redone) passes: file present after redo.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A media file on a different volume than the history folder (the rename fallback to copy is untested).
- Deleting a multi-GB file: the file is hashed once before it moves.
- `packages/studio-server` route suites: they need sibling packages built and were not run here.

## Size

Studio-server's packed size budget moves from 142,100 to 144,500 bytes (measured 144,047): the set-aside store is about 1.5 KB of code.

title: test(cli): the lifecycle suite lets background imports settle before it resets modules
body:
## What changes for you

Nothing in the CLI. `cli.lifecycle.test.ts` stops failing at random on Linux and Windows CI with `expected [] to deeply equal [ObjectContaining{error_name: "InvalidProjectError"}]`.

## Why

The CLI starts background imports it never awaits (update checks, background checks, app history). The test resets the module registry after each test. A background import still loading at that moment loads a module into the new registry while the next test is importing it too, so the module exists twice. The next test then reports its failure through one copy of `CliRuntimeError` and checks it against the other: the real error is not unwrapped (`error_name: "CliRuntimeError"`), or the event goes to the previous test's collector and nothing arrives (`[]`). This is a different failure from the cold-import timeout fixed in #6212.

## How

`afterEach` waits for `vi.dynamicImportSettled()` before it resets the registry. One line plus a two-line comment in the test file; no CLI code changes.

## Tests

Same file, 14 tests, six runs at a time on one machine: without the change 8 of 60 runs fail (all on "when the failure reaches the top-level handler"); with it 0 of 60 fail. I also instrumented the failing runs and saw the two symptoms above: `cli_error` arriving as `CliRuntimeError`, or no `cli_error` at all.

PR_SIZE_OK: 5 changed lines in one test file.

title: fix(cli): snapshot seeks into a HEVC cut whose index lands a keyframe early
body:
`snapshot` finds a video's frame with a seek it first verifies against ffmpeg. For a source whose index places each keyframe after its own time (a stream-copied closed-GOP HEVC cut is one), a seek to a keyframe's time lands on the keyframe before it. Every candidate then failed the "landing repeats" check, and the code fell back to no seek at all: the frame was found by decoding from the start of the file. That is seconds on a short clip and past the 30 s extraction timeout on a long 4K one, which reported "active <video> frame(s) could not be extracted".

When the demuxer lands before the keyframe asked for, an accurate `-ss` to that keyframe's time decodes from the earlier keyframe and drops everything before it, so the result is the same frame. The probe now returns that seek instead of rejecting the candidate.

Tests: a stream-copied closed-GOP HEVC cut (skipped without libx265): the probe returns a seek (fails on main, which returns no seek) and the extracted frame equals the full-decode frame. A synthetic cut at the same shape took 1.8 s to 5 s growing with the position in the file on main.

The render path does not share this probe: `videoFrameExtractor` seeks with its own `-ss` arguments and has no landing verification.

title: fix(engine): audio encodes on FFmpeg 4.4, which has no setts duration option
body:
Every render with audio failed at the audio mix on FFmpeg 4.4 (Ubuntu 22.04's `apt install ffmpeg`, the install the docs give): `setts_bsf: Option 'duration' not found`, reported as `audio_processing_failed` / `ffmpeg_unsupported`. The segmented AAC encode (0.8.170) joins its segments as ADTS, which carries no end, and ends the stream with `setts=duration=...`; that option arrived in FFmpeg 5.0. The segmented path runs for every audio render, not only long ones.

`encodeAac` now asks the FFmpeg it will use whether `setts` has a `duration` option (once per binary). If it does, nothing changes: same segments, same bytes. If it does not, the audio is encoded in one pass, which ends the stream at the duration itself. That is slower on long mixes (one encoder, about 60x real time) and only affects FFmpeg older than 5.0. No minimum FFmpeg version is declared anywhere, and the docs point Ubuntu users at `apt install ffmpeg`, so 4.4 is supported in practice.

Verified on a real FFmpeg 4.4.2 (Ubuntu 22.04 container on the devbox) with the CLI: a 2 s composition with one AAC clip, `render --fps 24 --workers 1`. On main it fails with the reported error; with this change it renders, audio and video both 2.000 s. On the current FFmpeg the same render still takes the setts path.

Tests: with a stub FFmpeg that rejects `setts=duration` and prints no `duration` in its help, `encodeAac` succeeds and the stream ends at the same tick as the normal encode (fails on main). The existing byte-identity and segment tests pass unchanged (9/9).

title: fix(cli): a Chrome download that stops sending is abandoned, retried, and releases the lock
body:
## What changes for you

A Chrome download that stops sending data no longer hangs the command and the install lock forever. After 60 s with no bytes the download is abandoned and retried (3 attempts); if it still stalls, the command fails with `The Chrome download from <host> stalled: no data for 60s.` plus the existing instructions for setting `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_PATH`. The install lock is released, so the next `check`, `render` or `browser ensure` does not wait behind it.

## Why

`@puppeteer/browsers`' `install()` has no timeout, and the install lock's heartbeat keeps it fresh for as long as its holder lives. A download whose server accepts the connection and never answers was still alive six hours later, heartbeating, and every later command waited behind it.

## How

In `browser/manager.ts`:
- `withDownloadStallTimeout` wraps each `install()` call. It uses the library's progress callback as the heartbeat, starts the timer before the first byte, and stops it once all bytes have arrived so a slow unzip is never counted as a stall. The host in the message comes from the library's own download URL.
- `retryOnStall` runs the whole install up to 3 times on a stall, clearing the staging directory between tries. Corrupt-archive recovery is unchanged.
- `EnsureBrowserOptions.downloadStallMs` overrides the 60 s default (used by the test).

`install()` takes no abort signal, timeout or agent (checked in the pinned 3.2.2 and the latest 3.2.6), and it keeps its sockets open, so the download runs in a child process: a new `browser-install` mode of the existing render-setup worker (`installInChild.ts`, `installRun.ts`). The child writes progress and unzip-log lines on stdout; the parent keeps the stall timer, forwards progress to `onProgress`, and on a stall aborts the child, which kills its process tree and closes its sockets. Nothing global is touched. The timer allows 15 s for the child to start, then 60 s without bytes; it stops once all bytes have arrived so a slow unzip is never a stall. `EnsureBrowserOptions.downloadBaseUrl` passes the library's `baseUrl` through (a mirror); the tests use it to point at a local listener.

## Tests

New `downloadStall.process.test.ts` runs a real `ensureBrowser` in a child process against a local TCP listener:
- accepts and never answers: the process exits with code 1, the message names `127.0.0.1:<port>`, it retried (`Retrying (2/2)`), and no install lock is left. With the stall timer removed the process never exits and the test fails at its 20 s guard.
- keeps sending one byte every 80 ms (longer than the 200 ms stall limit overall): not called a stall. With only the start-up line re-arming the timer this test fails.

`manager.test.ts` now replaces the child runner with the mocked library's `install`, so its existing download tests run unchanged (68 pass). The browser directory passes (195 tests); tsc, lint, format and the comment checks are clean.

Not covered: a real stalled download from the Chrome host, and the Windows path (the same child runner; not run there).

title: docs(studio-app): show the app working, three new pages, today's UI
body:
## What

- Every Studio app page shows the app working: screen recordings with the cursor and zooms (first video, Reference, Script panel, draw-to-edit, Share, Export, HeyGen Video 1 on a clip) and 3-4 second "where is it" clips next to each control the text names.
- New pages: **Continue from Claude Code** (`hyperframes open` / `catch-up` / Import projects), **Reference a video**, **Share for review**, plus **The project screen** (@, #, /, Script, panels).
- Rewritten for today's build: the Script panel's staged cuts (Pending video edits, then Send), Reference's read-then-path flow (Copy editing style or Video brief, then What to swap), Export's cloud option, one-click Share, and GitHub Copilot among the agents. No step says "type /hyperframes" (the skills are already on in the app).
- Titles describe the job ("Export a video", "Edit a video with the agent"). No emojis.
- The sidebar becomes one "Studio app" group in the order people use the app. Troubleshooting stays where it is.

## Why

The pages described an app that has changed several times since, and most of it was text people had to picture.

How we'll know it worked: Mintlify views and time on page for /studio-app/* (this week vs the two weeks before), and the docs-to-download event in PostHog.

## Related work

First of six docs PRs split from the docs rewrite (Studio app, Start pages, Make guides, Prompt Guide, browser editor, structure + catalog).

## How

- **Fact check:** every claim on the 12 pages (354) was checked against `main` of hyperframes-internal (`packages/desktop`, the app) and hyperframes (`packages/cli`, skills): 303 held; the 23 wrong and 3 outdated ones are fixed (transcription goes to HeyGen; Script cuts wait for Send; today's Script toolbar; motion guides over 5 s are refused; the open/catch-up hand-off is Mac-only and needs an agent session; 4K is about 2x on the self-serve card; 10-minute sign-in; Auto is the default access; real sign-in errors; Copilot). Claims that couldn't be proven were cut or reworded.
- **Recorded on a regular (non-staff) account** on build b467, so nothing staff-only shows (Learn tab, Pit Crew Academy, View as a user, Podcast edit / Computer use in #).
- 28 videos are on static.heygen.ai under `hyperframes-oss/docs/studio-demos/<name>-v2.mp4` (versioned names, cached a year, nothing in git). Posters and stills are small JPGs in `docs/public/images/studio-app/`.
- `DocsVideo` takes an optional `aspect` for app recordings (16 / 10), does not autoplay under reduced motion and stops a playing loop if Reduce Motion turns on mid-visit (play loads it again), and starts muted when it autoplays (browsers block unmuted autoplay). Short clips use the existing `HoverVideo` (`hasAudio={false}`, new optional `label`), so they pause and respect reduced motion. `custom.css` gains three layout blocks: a picture beside the text it explains, short "where is it" clips floated beside the text, and a row of portrait films.

title: lint rejects supported GLSL script blocks as invalid JavaScript
body:
### Describe the bug Inline GLSL source in a supported shader script block produces a blocking `invalid_inline_script_syntax` error. The shader rule recognizes `x-shader/x-fragment`, `x-shader/x-vertex` and `text/glsl`, but the JavaScript syntax rule tries to parse their GLSL contents with Acorn. This prevents an otherwise valid shader composition from passing static lint. The existing native-GLSL shader test checks only the shader warning and filters out the unexpected syntax error. ### Baseline and environment - Current upstream main: `3d45d1b037860afd42439a2b4ca7e0dc762448c3`. Also reproduced on `24965372dbbec90391978e223616c75045b9a813`. - `@hyperframes/lint` version `0.8.192`, built from the checkout. - Linux x64, Node.js `v26.11.1`. - Dependencies/build run with installed Bun `1.4.1`. The repository pins `1.4.4`; no runtime upgrade was made. The reproduction below runs the built package in Node. ### Reproduction After installing the workspace dependencies and running `bun run build`, run this from the repository root: ```sh node --input-type=module <<'JS' import { lintHyperframeHtml } from './packages/lint/dist/index.js'; const html = `
`; const result = await lintHyperframeHtml(html); console.log(JSON.stringify({ok: result.ok, errorCount: result.errorCount, findings: result.findings}, null, 2)); JS ``` ### Expected behavior `ok: true`, `errorCount: 0`, `findings: []`. GLSL source should reach the shader checks without being parsed as JavaScript. ### Actual behavior `ok: false`, `errorCount: 1`, with this finding: ```text invalid_inline_script_syntax Inline script has invalid syntax: Unexpected token (2:10) line: 5, column: 11 snippet: precision mediump float; void main() { gl_FragColor = vec4(1.0); } ``` Changing only the type to `x-shader/x-vertex` or `text/glsl` also produces the JavaScript syntax error. ### Related work and duplicate search Open and closed issues and PRs were searched on 2026-10-24 around 16:26 UTC and refreshed at 16:29 UTC and 16:31 UTC, using `invalid_inline_script_syntax`, `shader syntax`, `"x-shader"`, `"text/glsl"` and `GLSL lint`. No public report or active work covering this GLSL syntax-check mismatch was found. - #929 reports module/importmap handling, which is already fixed; it does not cover GLSL blocks. - #5640 added native GLSL shader checks. Its existing regression filters for `shader_unbounded_cosine_pow`, so it misses the concurrent blocking syntax error. - #2223 handles HTML structure and quoted embedded markup, rather than shader language selection. - #779 is a closed registry contribution with no report or ownership comment about this lint defect.

Optional Kokoro/MusicGen are absent and Docker is stopped; none is used by this static inspection command. ## Additional context The notice in `packages/cli/src/commands/keyframes.ts` is printed before the `args.json` branch without checking JSON mode. title: SDK drops added elements when reopening saved overrides
body:
## Describe the bug An embedded SDK editor loses elements inserted with `addElement()` when it saves `getOverrides()` and reopens the original template with those overrides. The saved delta contains the element snapshot and later text edits, but the reopened composition omits the element. This affects the documented template-plus-delta persistence workflow. The stored data is present; reopening fails to restore it. ## Minimal reproduction From this repository at `89081b91971c219949677f061284ffa491921a57`, release `0.8.193`, run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run build`. Save this as `repro.ts` at the repository root: ```typescript import { openComposition } from "./packages/sdk/dist/index.js"; const base = '

Launch

'; const edited = await openComposition(base, { overrides: {} }); const id = edited.addElement("hf-stage", 1, "

Available today

"); edited.setText(id, "Available worldwide"); const overrides = edited.getOverrides(); const reopened = await openComposition(base, { overrides }); console.log({ beforeReopen: edited.getElement(id)?.text ?? null, savedKeys: Object.keys(overrides), afterReopen: reopened.getElement(id)?.text ?? null, beforeElementCount: edited.getElements().length, afterElementCount: reopened.getElements().length, }); edited.dispose(); reopened.dispose(); ``` ## Steps to reproduce Run `bun repro.ts`. This uses the built SDK locally, with no browser, external assets, credentials, or remote service. ## Expected behavior `afterReopen` is `"Available worldwide"`, and both element counts are `3`. The added paragraph retains its parent and sibling position. ## Actual behavior ```text beforeReopen: 'Available worldwide' savedKeys: [ 'hf-3397', 'hf-3397.text' ] afterReopen: null beforeElementCount: 3 afterElementCount: 2 ``` ## Environment - Current main and release baseline: `89081b91971c219949677f061284ffa491921a57`, `@hyperframes/sdk` `0.8.193`. - Linux x64, Bun `1.4.1`, Node.js `26.11.1`. The repository requests Bun `1.4.4`; the installed version was left unchanged. - Reproduced with the real built SDK, not mocked adapters or server responses. ## Additional context `applyOverrideSet()` emits `replace` patches for non-null element snapshots. The element branch of `applyPatchesToDocument()` handles `add` and `remove`, so it silently skips those snapshots. The same cause also loses edited content after deleting an existing element, undoing that deletion, and reopening its saved overrides. Related work inspected: #1571 introduced `addElement`; #1350 fixed null deletion replay; #5243 fixed scoped-ID decoding; #6143 handles script-dependent deletes. Those cover different cases. Live searches across open and closed issues/PRs and the repository discussions found no public report or active work for this failure.

title: fix(sdk): keep added elements when reopening saved overrides
body:
## What

Keep SDK elements added through `addElement()` when an embedded editor saves its overrides and reopens the base template. The element and its later edits currently disappear.

## Why

The saved delta already contains the element snapshot. Override replay emits it as `replace`, but the element patch handler only applies `add` and `remove`.

Using the same built-SDK reproduction on baseline `89081b919` and this patch:

| Observable result | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph text before reopening | `Available worldwide` | `Available worldwide` |
| Saved keys | `hf-3397`, `hf-3397.text` | `hf-3397`, `hf-3397.text` |
| Paragraph text after reopening | `null`, element missing | `Available worldwide` |
| Element count after reopening | `2` | `3` |

## Related work

Fixes #6230

#1571 introduced insertion, #1350 fixed deletion-marker replay, #5243 fixed scoped-ID decoding, and #6143 preserves script-dependent deletes. None restores non-null element snapshots. Open/closed issue and PR searches were repeated immediately before publication; discussions were also checked. No matching report or active owner was found.

## How

Apply whole-element `replace` through the existing insertion path. Remove a matching base element before inserting its snapshot so an undone deletion restores edited content exactly once. Keep snapshot content and later child edits in latest edit order. Save each snapshot's final position among all child nodes, then restore those positions after structural edits replay. This preserves surrounding inline text and avoids stale positions from removed temporary siblings. Stored snapshots without child-node positions still use their element sibling index. The guide documents saving the returned set without sorting its keys.

## Test plan

- [x] Public-session regressions cover insertion followed by text editing, undone removal without duplicates, both reported sibling-order sequences, nested child edits after restoring a parent, temporary sibling removal, several restored siblings, inline text, legacy snapshots, and exact serialized HTML. The original two fail on main; the maintainer's two sibling-order cases fail at `86861cb`; the temporary-sibling cases fail at `76539b4`. All pass at this head.
- [x] All 692 SDK tests pass across 26 files.
- [x] Base-parent replay regressions cover a later child text edit through both session commands and host patches, addressing the reviewer's remaining coverage note.
- [x] Baseline workspace `bun run build`, patched SDK build, and SDK `typecheck` pass.
- [x] The same built-SDK reproduction passes under Bun and Node. The reopened serialized HTML also matches the edited session in both regression scenarios.
- [x] Changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, comment citation/share checks, docs snippet check, and `git diff --check` pass.
- [x] Independent GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh verification: the production fix passes 849 JSON-persisted round-trip comparisons on immutable source and built Node output. The final test-only follow-up passes all 692 SDK tests; each new case fails when its corresponding key-reordering line is disabled.
- [x] Documentation updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

Local limitations: Bun is `1.4.1`, versus requested `1.4.4`; Node is `26.11.1` on Linux x64. SDK `typecheck:examples` fails with 19 existing diagnostics, confirmed identical on the baseline and patch. Mintlify is absent, so local `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` were unavailable. No paid cloud jobs were needed.

## Saved-position regression

With siblings `title, sub, logo`, add a temporary paragraph before `sub`, remove and undo `sub`, then remove the paragraph and reopen the saved overrides. At `76539b4`, the reopened order was `title, logo, sub`. This update preserves `title, sub, logo`, matching the live session. The same sequence is covered for an added element, and a host-patch regression covers several restored siblings.

Inline-element regressions also compare the full saved/reopened HTML, both with and without a temporary sibling. Built-SDK checks under Bun and Node preserve the same element order through repeated JSON persistence cycles.

title: test(engine): retry the alpha probe test's temp-dir cleanup when Windows holds a file
body:
The real-file alpha probe tests write ffmpeg outputs into a temp dir and remove it in afterAll. On Windows runners the just-exited ffmpeg output (or antivirus) can still hold a file for a few milliseconds, so the plain rmSync fails with EBUSY/EPERM and flakes the Windows engine job.

rmSync now retries those codes (maxRetries 5, retryDelay 100), the same Node option the producer already uses for its work dirs.

Not reproduced locally: the lock only happens on the Windows runner, so the proof is the Windows engine job staying green.

title: Relative engine concat paths fail or silently omit later clips
body:
### Affected workflow

The public engine APIs `concatVideoFiles()` and `encodeFramesChunkedConcat()` accept filesystem paths. A relative input path is written verbatim into the concat manifest, but FFmpeg resolves it relative to that manifest's directory instead of the caller's working directory.

For a chunked encode with a relative output directory, every chunk encodes successfully and the final concat fails. With an absolute first input and a relative later input, concat can return `{ success: true }` while omitting the later clip.

### Minimal reproduction

Run from the repository root after the documented Bun install/build:

```bash
mkdir -p demo
ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i color=red:size=32x32:rate=30 -frames:v 2 -c:v libx264 -bf 0 demo/red.mp4
ffmpeg -v error -f lavfi -i color=blue:size=32x32:rate=30 -frames:v 3 -c:v libx264 -bf 0 demo/blue.mp4
bun -e 'import { resolve } from "node:path"; import { concatVideoFiles } from "./packages/engine/src/index.ts"; console.log(await concatVideoFiles([resolve("demo/red.mp4"), "demo/blue.mp4"], "demo/joined.mp4"));'
ffprobe -v error -count_frames -select_streams v:0 -show_entries stream=nb_read_frames -of csv=p=0 demo/joined.mp4
```

Actual: concat reports `{ success: true }`, but ffprobe reports **2** frames. Only the red clip survives.

Expected: **5** frames, with both red frames followed by all three blue frames.

The same underlying path resolution also breaks an ordinary relative output path:

```ts
await encodeFramesChunkedConcat(
  "frames",
  "frame_%06d.jpg",
  "output/video.mp4",
  { fps: { num: 30, den: 1 }, width: 64, height: 64, preset: "ultrafast" },
  30,
);
```

With 40 valid frame files, this encodes two chunks and then fails with `Impossible to open 'output/chunk-encode-.../output/chunk-encode-.../chunk_0000.mp4'`. Passing an absolute output path produces all 40 frames.

### Baseline and environment

- Upstream main `fcec26ed5f35ad04154361bde2faa0aa3b014c45`, v0.8.193.
- Linux x86_64, Bun 1.4.1, Node 26.11.1, FFmpeg/ffprobe 9.0.2.
- Synthetic local media only. Both functions are exported by `@hyperframes/engine`.

This affects integrations that use working-directory-relative paths. The producer's absolute scratch paths are not the reproduction here.

title: Unrolling unequal GSAP keyframe arrays shortens property timing
body:
### Describe the bug

Supported GSAP simple-array keyframes are read using the longest property's array length. A shorter property array therefore ends too early. This also changes playback when `unrollComputedTimeline` converts a helper into editable literal tweens, the operation behind Studio's "Unroll to edit" action.

For a four-second tween with `x: [0, 100, 200]` and `opacity: [0, 1]`, the parser places `opacity: 1` at 50% instead of 100%. Unrolling turns a four-second fade into a two-second fade.

### Minimal reproduction

On a checkout of `heygen-com/hyperframes` at `fcec26ed5f35ad04154361bde2faa0aa3b014c45`, run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and `bun run build`. Save this as `repro.mjs` in the checkout root, then run `bun repro.mjs`:

```js
import {
  parseGsapScript,
  unrollComputedTimeline,
} from './packages/parsers/src/index.ts';

const source = `const tl = gsap.timeline({ paused: true });
function animate() {
  tl.to("#dot", {
    duration: 4,
    ease: "none",
    keyframes: {
      x: [0, 100, 200],
      opacity: [0, 1],
      easeEach: "none"
    }
  }, 0);
}
animate();`;

console.log(JSON.stringify(parseGsapScript(source).animations[0].keyframes, null, 2));
console.log(unrollComputedTimeline(source));
```

No media, plugins, or external assets are needed. These functions are also exported by the published `@hyperframes/parsers` package.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the script above.
2. Inspect the parsed 50% and 100% entries.
3. Inspect the percentage keyframes written by `unrollComputedTimeline`.

### Expected behavior

Each property's array spans the entire tween independently. The parsed and unrolled stops should be:

```js
[
  { percentage: 0, properties: { x: 0, opacity: 0 } },
  { percentage: 50, properties: { x: 100 } },
  { percentage: 100, properties: { x: 200, opacity: 1 } }
]
```

GSAP explicitly supports arrays with different lengths: [simple array-based keyframes](https://gsap.com/resources/keyframes/#simple-array-based-keyframes---v39).

### Actual behavior

Both the Acorn and legacy Recast parser put `opacity: 1` in the 50% stop and omit it from 100%. The unroller writes that incorrect timing into the source:

```js
keyframes: {
  "0%": { x: 0, opacity: 0 },
  "50%": { x: 100, opacity: 1 },
  "100%": { x: 200 },
  easeEach: "none"
}
```

Measured using real GSAP 3.15.0 on a synthetic DOM element in Happy DOM:

| Seek time | Authored opacity | Opacity after unrolling on main |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1s | 0.25 | 0.5 |
| 2s | 0.5 | 1 |
| 3s | 0.75 | 1 |
| 4s | 1 | 1 |

### Environment

- Current main: `fcec26ed5f35ad04154361bde2faa0aa3b014c45`, v0.8.193.
- Linux x64, Bun 1.4.1, Node 26.11.1.
- Workspace requests Bun 1.4.4; no runtime upgrade was performed.
- Whole workspace build passed before verification.

### Additional context

The cause is `parseSimpleArrayKeyframes` in both parser implementations: it zips all channels by index using `maxLen`. Each channel needs its own spacing before stops at shared percentages are merged.

Live open and closed issue/PR searches, including comments, checked unequal/different-length arrays, `parseSimpleArrayKeyframes`, and unroll/opacity symptoms. Related #2675 and #5024 concern object-array step durations; #5044 concerns unreadable keyframe syntax. Their descriptions and relevant comments do not cover this supported simple-array case. All 12 repository discussions were also checked. No matching report or active work was found as of 2026-10-24 18:22 UTC.

title: fix(engine): concat resolves relative paths without dropping clips
body:
## What

Engine callers can use relative paths when joining encoded clips or writing a chunked encode. Concat now resolves every input against the caller's working directory before writing its manifest.

## Why

FFmpeg interprets relative manifest entries from the manifest's directory. A relative output folder therefore made chunked encoding fail at its final join. An absolute first clip followed by a relative clip could report success with only the first clip in the delivered file.

Same synthetic media, options, and local FFmpeg for baseline and patch:

| Workflow | Main `fcec26ed5` | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 40 frames, 30-frame chunks, relative output directory | Concat fails with a duplicated path | Success, 40 frames, 64x48, 30/1 fps |
| Same 40 frames, absolute output directory | Success, 40 frames | Success, 40 frames |
| Absolute red clip, relative blue clip | Reports success, decodes only 2 red frames | Decodes 2 red frames then 3 blue frames |
| Relative first clip, absolute second clip | Concat fails to open the first input | Both clips survive in order |

## Related work

Fixes #6235.

Checked open and closed issues/PRs, including comments, by symptom and the concat symbols. Related merged work covers scratch isolation in #3680, helper extraction in #4112, assembly IO in #5768, percent signs in image-sequence directories in #6116, and unreadable image frames in #5978. None addresses concat manifest paths relative to the caller's working directory.

## How

Resolve paths in the existing concat-manifest writer, retaining its quote escaping and scratch-file ownership. Both public entry points use that writer. The engine reference now states how relative paths resolve.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: three real-FFmpeg cases cover a relative chunked output and mixed relative/absolute inputs in either position. The latter decode every output frame to check count and red/blue order, including a directory with spaces and an apostrophe. All three fail on the recorded baseline and pass with the fix.
- [x] Manual testing performed: the same public engine reproduction before/after, with ffprobe checking output dimensions, frame count, and rate. The relative and absolute 40-frame outputs also decode identically.
- [x] Documentation updated in `docs/packages/engine.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": no comments added; citation and comment-share checks pass.
- Whole workspace build, engine build and typecheck, changed-file oxlint/oxfmt, docs snippet check, and diff check pass.
- Focused chunk-encoder suites: 107 tests pass across the encoder, percent-directory, and new relative-path suites.

Limitations: two existing `chunkEncoder.unreadableFrame.test.ts` cases fail on this machine with FFmpeg 9.0.2, both on untouched main and on the patch. No change to those tests or their behavior is included. Bun is 1.4.1 rather than the repository's requested 1.4.4. Mintlify is unavailable locally, so `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` were not run. No Windows run.

title: fix(core): scene shots keep their shell after leading comments
body:

title: fix(parsers): keep each keyframe array on its own timing
body:
## What

Unrolling a helper with unequal GSAP keyframe arrays keeps each property's timing. A four-second fade alongside a three-point position animation now stays a four-second fade.

## Why

The parser zipped all property arrays using the longest array's spacing. For `x: [0, 100, 200]` and `opacity: [0, 1]`, it put the final opacity at 50%. "Unroll to edit" then wrote that timing into the composition.

The same synthetic DOM element and GSAP 3.15.0 tween were sought to the same times before and after this fix:

| Seek time | Authored opacity | Unrolled on main | Unrolled with fix |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1s | 0.25 | 0.5 | 0.25 |
| 2s | 0.5 | 1 | 0.5 |
| 3s | 0.75 | 1 | 0.75 |
| 4s | 1 | 1 | 1 |

The parsed `opacity: 1` stop moves from 50% to 100%. The position stops stay at 0%, 50%, and 100%.

## Related work

Fixes #6236

#2675 and #5024 fixed object-array step timing. #5044 preserves keyframe syntax the parser cannot read. This fixes supported simple-array channels with different lengths. Live searches of open and closed issues/PRs and repository discussions found no matching report or active work.

## How

Both parsers distribute each channel using its own length, then use the existing percentage merge helper to combine shared stops. Existing whole-percentage rounding is preserved. The package docs explain the unequal-array contract.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. Five new cases fail on main and pass with the fix. They cover both parsers, both channel orders, different intermediate stop times, merged endpoints, and repeated unrolling.
- [x] Manual testing performed. The same public parser/unroll reproduction and real GSAP DOM seek samples were run before and after. Only synthetic inputs were used.
- [x] Whole workspace production build passed on the baseline. Parsers rebuilt after the change.
- [x] Full parsers suite: 1,332 passed, 4 skipped, 3 todo. CLI keyframes tests: 23 passed.
- [x] Parsers typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, comment citation/share checks, docs motion-snippet check, and diff whitespace check passed.
- [x] Documentation updated in `docs/packages/parsers.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md. No source comments added.

Validation ran on Linux with Bun 1.4.1 and Node 26.11.1; the workspace requests Bun 1.4.4. Node checks used `--no-experimental-webstorage`. Mintlify is absent, so `mint validate` and `mint broken-links` were not run. This change does not alter the parser's existing whole-percentage rounding.

title: fix(producer): a busy composition no longer stalls the render waiting on probe-page reads
body:
## What

The render's two live reads of the probe page (element count for routing, adapters used for telemetry) now give up after 5 s, use the static answer they already fall back to, and log a one-line warning saying the live read was skipped.

## Why

A composition that runs its own free-running render loop (for example a post-processing chain on a software GL renderer) can leave `page.evaluate` unanswered until the 300 s CDP protocol timeout. The element-count read waited the full 300 s, then the adapters read waited again, each time falling back silently, so the render sat idle before capture started with nothing in the log. Both reads only feed routing and telemetry, and both already had static answers.

## How

- `evaluateWithinBound` in `renderOrchestrator.ts` races `page.evaluate` against `PROBE_READ_TIMEOUT_MS` and warns on failure. Both `resolveCompositionElementCount` and `resolveAdaptersUsed` go through it; `executeRenderPipeline` is their only caller and passes its logger.
- The element-count result keeps `source: "static"` on timeout, so the routing gate still fails closed as before.
- Not in this PR: sizing workers from the container CPU quota is already covered by the open "size render workers from the container CPU limit" PR.

## Test plan

- [x] Two tests with a probe page whose `evaluate` never resolves, fake timers, no real waiting: each function returns its static answer after the bound and warns once. Both fail on main (`Test timed out in 5000ms`) and pass with the change.
- [x] `renderOrchestrator.test.ts` and `renderOrchestrator.deGateProbe.test.ts`: 288/288, three runs in a row.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` (producer), oxlint, oxfmt clean.

## Caveats

- The bound only stops waiting: the `page.evaluate` call stays outstanding on the probe page until its own protocol timeout.
- With both reads on a stuck page the render now waits up to 10 s (2 x 5 s), down from the 300 s + 162 s measured.

title: fix(cli): scope explicit preview port discovery
body:
An explicit managed-preview port still scanned 100 ports starting at a saved session's port. For example, a saved port of 3021 made `preview --background --port 32521` probe 3021–3120 before checking 32521.

Startup and `--status` discovery now use the explicit port's window and check an out-of-range saved port individually. With a saved session, `--stop` probes only that project's owned port; without one, an explicit stop port sets the discovery window. Shutdown waits probe only their target port, and replacements still wait for the owned listener before recording a new session.

Status prefers the exact requested port, then the saved port, then another same-project match. If the requested port is absent and an unmanaged preview at 32530 precedes the saved preview at 32600, status reports 32600. It attaches the saved log only after confirming the selected listener belongs to the recorded wrapper. Unverified listeners retain their reported PID, or null when unknown, and do not receive a background-mode claim or a fabricated log path. The guide documents discovery, reporting, and stop behavior.

Closes #6204.

Validation:
- 134 tests pass across the preview lifecycle, CLI command, and output suites. New status selection and log-attribution regressions fail on the published parent; list merging preserves better scanned PID/host/name metadata and kill-all still delegates the same project and port to its existing stop path.
- Actual HTTP startup discovery against controlled loopback listeners records 100 requests in the requested range, one to the saved port, and zero to its 99 neighboring ports.
- A live macOS check against two owned loopback listeners verifies OS PID/recorded-wrapper identity, saved-port preference, exact-port override without the wrong log, and omission of stale-record logs.
- Full workspace baseline build, final CLI build/typecheck, lint/format, normal commit hooks including Fallow, both comment gates, and Mint validation/broken-links pass.
