title: fix(studio): allow a local GSAP dependency mirror
body:
Studio eagerly loads MotionPathPlugin from jsDelivr even when a composition vendors GSAP locally. In networks where jsDelivr is unavailable, that generated request fails before the first motion-path edit.

Add `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL` for a local or private npm-style mirror. The preview server validates and normalizes it once at API startup, then passes it through preview metadata to both iframe plugin loaders. Generated GSAP, CustomEase, MotionPathPlugin, and fallback requests use the selected mirror; root and subcomposition cache keys include that selection.

The default remains jsDelivr. Runtime-selected plugin versions and existing server-side version inference stay intact. Authored resource URLs and GSAP bootstrap scripts saved into project source remain unchanged; offline projects must vendor those resources separately. Missing mirror files do not trigger a public-CDN fallback. The CLI and Studio-server docs explain the mirror layout and restart requirements.

Closes #6205.

Validation:
- 225 tests pass across the core URL helper, Studio plugin loaders, and preview/subcomposition/cache suites. Baseline controls record 26 new failures across those layers.
- Root/subcomposition/capture/disk-fallback paths, escaped metadata precedence, persistent cache invalidation, authored-plugin preservation, and bounded mirror failure recovery are covered.
- Full workspace build, root lint, server typecheck, normal commit hooks, both comment gates, and Mint validation/broken-link checks pass.
- Native Chrome 152: the same locally vendored fixture fails on the baseline when external requests are blocked, then loads through a loopback mirror after the fix. Its first motion-path edit and asynchronous reload both seek correctly at one second. A broken mirror reports failure without a public-CDN retry. The fixture passes `hyperframes lint` and the browser check.

## Before

With GSAP vendored locally and external requests blocked, Studio reports the generated MotionPathPlugin CDN failure.

![Studio reports a MotionPathPlugin CDN failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user-github-me/hyperframes/ce0dc7c0691e566b2073c7f09fc8602102c43ff0/contribution-captures/6205/before.png)

## After

With `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL` pointing to the local mirror, the first motion-path edit seeks correctly. The browser made zero external requests.

![Studio seeks the locally loaded motion path correctly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/user-github-me/hyperframes/ce0dc7c0691e566b2073c7f09fc8602102c43ff0/contribution-captures/6205/after.png)

title: Bundling repeated CSS imports drops later media conditions
body:
## Describe the bug Bundling a composition can drop its screen styles when a linked stylesheet imports the same local file first for print and then for screen. The authored page has a green background; the bundled page has a transparent background and appears white. This reproduces with the published `@hyperframes/core@0.8.193` package and baseline main `ab57d0ee1446846d81d25d7d2411ec03e9927005`. The compiler is unchanged on current main `9aadc0b9b99d92afd25215228878cee23ea47a0f`. ## Minimal reproduction Create these three files under `repro/`: `index.html`: ```html
``` `main.css`: ```css @import "shared.css" print; @import "shared.css" screen; ``` `shared.css`: ```css #box { background-color: rgb(0, 128, 0); } ``` ## Steps to reproduce With `@hyperframes/core@0.8.193` available, run: ```js import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"; import { bundleToSingleHtml } from "@hyperframes/core/compiler"; await writeFile("repro/bundled.html", await bundleToSingleHtml("./repro", { runtime: "placeholder", staticGuard: false, })); ``` Serve `repro/` over HTTP and open `index.html` and `bundled.html` in a browser using screen media. Inspect the computed `backgroundColor` of `#box`. ## Expected behavior Both imports retain their conditions. The authored page and bundle both show `rgb(0, 128, 0)`. ## Actual behavior Only the print import survives. On screen, the bundle reports `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` and appears white. The same loss happens when two parent stylesheets import a common dependency under different inherited media conditions. Repeating an unconditional dependency through two parents can also change cascade order. ## Environment - Latest published core: 0.8.193, downloaded from npm and integrity checked; its built public compiler was executed. - Baseline main: `ab57d0ee1446846d81d25d7d2411ec03e9927005`; compiler and parsers unchanged on current main `9aadc0b9b99d92afd25215228878cee23ea47a0f`. - Linux x64, Node 26.11.1, Bun 1.4.1, Chrome 152.0.7977.42. - A static CSS/bundling reproduction. No MP4 render is claimed. ## Additional context `inlineCssFile` shares a global visited-file set across sibling imports and drops every later occurrence. Cycle detection needs the active ancestor chain instead. CSS requires separate processing of each occurrence: https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#import-processing. Related #922 and #923 introduced import expansion and diamond deduplication. #4664 handles conditional stylesheet links. This report concerns repeated recursive local CSS imports, including the conditions inherited from their parents. Public issue, PR, review, comment and discussion searches found no matching report or active implementation in the checked sources.

title: fix(core): preserve repeated stylesheet imports
body:
## What

Keep a composition's styles when several local CSS imports reference the same file. A linked sheet that imports `shared.css` for print and then screen currently loses the screen rules when bundled.

## Why

The same 320 by 180 fixture was checked in Chrome with screen media. Its background is green in the authored page:

| Output | Computed background | Visible result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Published 0.8.193 bundle | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` | White |
| Main `ab57d0ee1` bundle | `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)` | White |
| This patch | `rgb(0, 128, 0)` | Green, matching the authored page |

The input is `@import "shared.css" print;` followed by `@import "shared.css" screen;`. The shared sheet sets the background to green. Two parent sheets importing that dependency under different media conditions fail the same way.

## Related work

Fixes #6249

#922/#923 added local import expansion and diamond deduplication. #4664 preserves conditions on stylesheet links. This corrects the recursive local import set. [CSS import processing](https://www.w3.org/TR/css-cascade-5/#import-processing) treats every occurrence as a separate stylesheet, so unconditional diamond imports also keep their cascade positions. Qualified imports and linked-font discovery in #5827 are outside this change.

Originally based on main `9aadc0b9b`, whose compiler and parser trees match the measured `ab57d0ee1` baseline. Current main `b97de59c8` has no changes to this PR's files.

## How

Track only stylesheets active in the current recursion chain, starting with the linked entry stylesheet. Stop actual cycles and expand each sibling import in place. The existing path checks, URL rebasing and media wrapping stay in the same path. Update the diamond regression to protect cascade order rather than deduplication. The docs also explain that repeated imports can increase bundle size.

## Test plan

- [x] Four regression cases fail on main: direct and inherited media conditions, diamond cascade order, and a cycle back to the entry stylesheet. All pass with the fix.
- [x] 201 bundler and adjacent tests pass. The 196 bundler tests also pass on Bun 1.4.4.
- [x] Baseline workspace build, patched core build and core typecheck pass.
- [x] The published 0.8.193 package and main both reproduce the missing screen rule.
- [x] 32 browser samples cover screen and print media, direct/nested imports, cascade order and cycles.
- [x] Independent GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh review passed 201 tests, 24 additional browser comparisons, five adjacent controls and three mutation controls.
- [x] Lint, formatting, diff checks, comment checks and normal commit hooks pass.
- [x] Documentation updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

No full video render was run. Mintlify is unavailable locally; no dependencies were installed.

title: fix(cli): reap only orphaned browsers HyperFrames launched
body:
## What

Orphan cleanup now kills only browsers that HyperFrames itself launched. Every HyperFrames Chrome launch passes an inert `--hyperframes-owned-browser` switch, and `killOrphanedProcesses()` only kills a PPID-1 process that carries that switch as a whole argument.

## Why

`hyperframes preview` (and the render setup worker) killed every PPID-1 process of the current user whose args contained `chrome-headless-shell`, `chrome_headless_shell` or `puppeteer_dev_chrome_profile`. That includes detached Puppeteer or Playwright browsers that belong to other tools, so embedding `preview` in another app could kill that app's browsers.

## Related work

Fixes #6203. Builds on #6213, which added the `HYPERFRAMES_NO_ORPHAN_CLEANUP=1` opt-out. That guard stays as it is and still skips cleanup entirely; this change makes the default safe for tools that never set it.

## How

- `HYPERFRAMES_BROWSER_MARKER_ARG` and `withHyperframesBrowserMarker(args)` live in a dependency-free `@hyperframes/core/browser-marker` subpath (`packages/core/src/browserMarker.ts`), so the CLI, engine, producer and inspector share one value. It is a subpath rather than the core root entry because the Cloud Run image's BeginFrame contract step imports `browserManager.ts` from source before core's generated runtime exists. The helper appends the switch once and copies the array, so a launch that passes through two wrappers (the CLI GPU probe goes through both the CLI launcher and the engine probe) still gets it once, and the engine's pool fingerprint args are not mutated.
- Chrome ignores switches it does not know, and the switch shows up in `ps` args on every platform, so it is a reliable marker. It is a switch rather than a custom `--user-data-dir`, so no launch gets a new profile directory and Puppeteer keeps creating and deleting its own temp profile exactly as before. The capture browser's existing `hf-capture-profile-*` directory is unchanged and still removed on close.
- The reaper matches the marker as a whole token, so a lookalike such as `--hyperframes-owned-browser-x` does not qualify.

### Launch sites covered

I grepped the repo for `launch(`, `puppeteer.launch`, `executablePath`, `--user-data-dir` and `userDataDir`.

Marked (product and harness code):

| Site | What launches there |
| --- | --- |
| `packages/cli/src/browser/launch.ts:123` | `launchManagedBrowser`, the single CLI launcher. Covers `check`/`validate` (`commands/validate.ts:444`), `layout` (`commands/layout.ts:226`), motion shots (`commands/motionShot.ts:422`), `capture` (`capture/launchCaptureBrowser.ts:53`, `capture/captureCompositionFrame.ts:381`) and the CLI GPU probe (`browser/launch.ts:69`), including the one-process relaunch inside an agent sandbox |
| `packages/engine/src/services/browserManager.ts:115` | Engine GPU probe (direct or through a probe lifecycle). Used by render and by preview's studio server (`cli/src/server/studioServer.ts:296`) |

title: fix(core): motion blur no longer blacks out videos inside sub-compositions
body:
With `data-motion-blur="on"` on the root, a `<video>` inside a sub-composition that also holds a moving element rendered black for the whole scene (mean luma 17.5 against 124 with blur off, 1080p and 640x360 alike). A video directly in the root, or a sub-composition with nothing moving, was fine.

Cause: for a frame with movers, `paint()` isolated the movers right away, which hides every non-mover descendant with `visibility: hidden !important`, including the `[data-composition-src]` host. The engine injects the decoded video frames only after the seek, and its injector skips a video whose sub-composition host is hidden, so the video never got its frame. A root-level video has no hidden host above it, which is why it escaped.

Fix: an engine frame now isolates the movers when it is armed (`releaseCaptureMotionBlurFrame`, called from the engine's `waitForPendingSeekCompletion` after injection and before capture). Every engine frame path (screenshot, BeginFrame, draw-element) goes through `prepareFrameForCapture`, which injects and then waits, so isolation still covers the whole movers capture. Preview keeps isolating at paint, unchanged.

Tests: new case in `captureMotionBlur/index.test.ts` (the root stays visible between an engine paint and its arm; fails without the fix). 219 core runtime tests pass 3 runs in a row. Real render of a 1080p two-scene fixture with a video and a rotating mover per scene: luma 17.5 before, 124.4 after; 640x360: 16.3 before, 126.1 after.

Before (video black, only the mover) and after:

![After: video and blurred mover](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b489df2e-0c09-4c0d-951c-174d4a4c8900)

title: Scoped descendant CSS zoom incorrectly blocks lint and check
body:
## Describe the bug Root-scoping a valid descendant zoom makes lint report that the canvas is being rescaled. This blocks `hyperframes check` before browser verification. ```css .badge { zoom: 2; } /* passes */ #root .badge { zoom: 2; } /* root_zoom_rescales_a_fixed_canvas */ ``` Both selectors apply zoom only to the same child. The composition root, html and body remain at normal zoom. This reproduces in the published `@hyperframes/lint@0.8.193` package and on main. The rule promises to allow descendant zoom. ## Minimal reproduction Save as `index.html`: ```html
Badge
``` ## Steps to reproduce 1. Run `npx hyperframes@0.8.193 lint . --json` in the fixture directory. 2. Run `npx hyperframes@0.8.193 check . --json --at 1`. 3. Change only `#root .badge` to `.badge` and repeat lint. ## Expected behavior Both forms pass lint because only the badge receives zoom. `check` should continue into browser verification. ## Actual behavior The scoped form returns one blocking `root_zoom_rescales_a_fixed_canvas` error. `check` exits 1 with `browserSkipped: true`. The unscoped control returns no findings. `#root > .badge`, `.canvas .badge` and `body .badge` also produce the false error. ## Environment - Published `@hyperframes/lint` 0.8.193: downloaded from npm, SHA-512 integrity verified, built public APIs executed. - Baseline main `ab57d0ee1446846d81d25d7d2411ec03e9927005`; relevant source unchanged on current main `7224812143d5243a83dc13cc9a0ab2a3a3897580`. - Linux x64, Node 26.11.1, Bun 1.4.4, existing Chrome 152.0.7977.42. - The CLI check comparison used a local copy of the fixture's GSAP dependency. No MP4 render was run. ## Additional context `targetsCanvasRoot` classifies the leftmost selector compound. In `#root .badge`, that compound is an ancestor constraint, not the element receiving zoom. Splitting selector lists on every comma also mishandles functional pseudo-classes. #4412 introduced this rule and explicitly allows descendant zoom, while documenting its heuristic. #5712 optimizes its CSS scanning. Neither covers this scoped-selector failure. Live issue, PR, comment and discussion searches found no matching report or active owner in the checked sources.

title: fix(lint): allow scoped descendant zoom
body:
## What

Allow descendant CSS zoom when its selector is scoped to the composition root. `#root .badge { zoom: 2 }` currently blocks validation even though only the badge is zoomed.

## Why

In the same 800 by 400 composition, the root stays at zoom 1 and the badge at zoom 2. Scoping the badge selector should not turn that into a canvas error.

| Result | Published 0.8.193 / main | This patch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.badge { zoom: 2 }` lint errors | 0 | 0 |
| `#root .badge { zoom: 2 }` lint errors | 1 | 0 |
| Scoped fixture `check` exit code | 1 | 0 |
| Scoped fixture browser verification | Skipped | Runs and passes |
| Actual canvas zoom such as `body > *` | Blocking error | Blocking error |
| Script-added root classes/data attributes | Blocking error | Blocking error |

## Related work

Fixes #6253

#4412 introduced the rule and promises descendant zoom support, but its leftmost-compound heuristic treats a scope as a target. #5712 improves scan performance without changing that classification. Fresh searches of public issues, PRs, comments and discussions found no matching report or active fix.

## How

Use the existing selector AST and known root/document identities to prove when a selector cannot reach the canvas. Child and descendant relationships can prove that the styled element is below the root. Uncertain selectors keep the existing conservative guard. Selector lists preserve commas inside functional pseudo-classes.

New positive proofs apply only to bare style blocks without at-rules. Other stylesheet contexts retain the earlier decision so namespaces and conditional rules cannot introduce a canvas error. The rule does not attempt to reconstruct the browser DOM or evaluate arbitrary CSS conditions. It adds no dependency or public API. Known canvas identities retain the guard when scripts add classes, IDs or data attributes, including inside `:is()` and `:where()`. Regression tests also pin the unknown parent of a composition rooted in head or template.

The new analysis is included in both the Node and browser bundles. The final local archive is 171,312 packed bytes and 664,715 unpacked bytes, up from 168,222 and 653,119 before this PR. The file list stays at two JavaScript files, two declarations and the manifest; no tests or source maps are shipped. Lint's budget uses the original CI measurement plus the verifier's standard 5% headroom, at 179,338 packed and 695,173 unpacked bytes. The runtime identity follow-up fits within those limits. No other package budget or verifier threshold changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Regression tests added for scoped descendants and canvas guards. All 1,141 lint tests pass on Bun 1.4.4; 207 adjacent CLI tests also pass.
- [x] Published 0.8.193 public APIs reproduce the bug. Patched source, built Node/browser-entry APIs and real CLI lint/check pass the scoped fixture.
- [x] Independent GPT-6.1 Sol xhigh review cleared `285512fcd` after 1,141 lint tests, 207 CLI tests, 403 API/Chrome cases and seven real CLI invocations. It verified runtime-added identity, nested selector alternatives, immutable exclusions, omitted HTML tags, SVG, quirks-mode casing and stylesheet namespaces/conditions.
- [x] The earlier full workspace build on base main passed. Latest lint/CLI rebuilds, lint typecheck, normal commit hooks, lint, formatting, comment and diff checks pass.
- [x] Packed archives inspected and the production size gate checked against CI/local measurements. Package-verifier tests pass.
- [x] Documentation updated.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md.

The browser comparisons use computed zoom and bounds from loaded CSS. Unknown conditions retain existing conservative behavior; this does not promise exact browser evaluation of every selector. Mintlify is unavailable locally. No full video render was run.

title: feat(studio): the blur panel turns on events with blur
body:
## What
Choosing Subtle or Strong in Studio's Blur tab now also writes `data-motion-blur-events="on"` on the composition root. Off removes it, with `data-motion-blur`, and leaves the shutter, samples and tier alone.

Why: blur finds movers by seeking the page, and runs timeline callbacks during that scan only when the events attribute is on. A composition that moves things from a `render(t)` function showed no blur on those elements. In `k3-promo`, the pendulum rods and the label pills are set from JS each frame, so they stayed sharp: 31 movers found without the attribute, 106 with it (measured in the desktop app's preview with blur on, tier capture).

The desktop flyout makes the same change in heygen-com/hyperframes-internal#5633.

## Verified
- Panel tests: 81 pass, including a new one that Subtle and Strong write the attribute. Removing `events: true` from the Subtle/Strong patch fails two of them.
- The two existing tests that described the old behavior were updated: Off now removes events, and "writes nothing when the level is already set" starts from a root that already has events on.
- `oxlint`, the comment ratchet and `tsc` for studio are clean. Docs: the Studio paragraph in the motion blur guide says Subtle and Strong turn events on and Off removes it.

## Not verified
- Not run in a real Studio. The desktop app is where I measured the mover counts.
- Cost: `events` runs timeline callbacks extra times during the scan and at each sample, so a composition whose callbacks have side effects would run them more often.
- A root with `data-motion-blur-events` set by hand loses it when Off is chosen.

## No visible change
The only source edit is a small change to which attributes the panel writes (an 8-line patch function in `motionBlurPanelModel.ts`); nothing on screen moves.

title: feat(studio): load GSAP from the CLI's bundled copy by default
body:
## What

HyperFrames Studio now loads the GSAP scripts it adds to previews (GSAP core, CustomEase, MotionPathPlugin) from files the CLI ships, served by the preview server itself, instead of from jsDelivr. Opening a project in `npx hyperframes preview` no longer makes a jsDelivr request for these scripts.

This also picks up both follow-ups from the review of #6247: renders now honor `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL`, and the setting accepts plain `http://` only for loopback hosts.

## Why

#6205: Studio requested `MotionPathPlugin.min.js` from jsDelivr every time the editor opened, which fails offline and on restricted networks and sends a third-party request from a local editor. #6247 added an opt-in mirror, but the default still went to jsDelivr.

## Related work

Closes #6205

Builds on #6247, which added `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL` and routed every Studio load site (preview document, sub-compositions, the soft-reload loader and the editor preload) through one setting. This PR changes the default behind that setting.

## How

**Lookup order** (`packages/studio-server/src/routes/preview.ts`):

1. `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL`, when set. Unchanged, still no public fallback.
2. Otherwise the host's bundled copy, when the adapter passes the new optional `gsapLocalRoot` (a same-origin path, passed like `runtimeUrl`).
3. Otherwise jsDelivr, so other hosts embedding studio-server keep today's behavior.

**Shipping the files.** `packages/cli/scripts/build-copy.mjs` copies `gsap.min.js`, `CustomEase.min.js` and `MotionPathPlugin.min.js` from the workspace's installed gsap into `dist/vendor/npm/gsap@3.15.0/dist/`. The build fails if the installed gsap version differs from `GSAP_CDN_VERSION`, so the two cannot drift silently. No new runtime dependency.

**Serving them.** `studioServer.ts` serves `/api/vendor/npm/:pkg/dist/:file`, modeled on `/api/runtime.js`. It answers only the three files at the bundled version and returns 404 for anything else. When running from source it falls back to core's installed gsap, and if no files are found it passes no `gsapLocalRoot`, so preview keeps using jsDelivr instead of breaking.

**Root-relative values** (`packages/core/src/gsapCdn.ts`). `normalizeGsapBaseUrl` still rejects root-relative values, which is right for the env var. A new `normalizeGsapLocalRoot` validates the adapter's path (no `//host`, backslash, query or fragment). `gsapCdnDist` treats a root-relative base as the local copy, which holds only `3.15.0`: any other version, such as an authored `gsap@3.14.2`, resolves to jsDelivr. The server-written meta tag carries the root, so the browser loaders in `gsapSoftReload.ts` and the editor preload follow the same rule without changes.

**Renders** (review note 1). `htmlCompiler.ts` used to rewrite a missing local `gsap/dist/*` script to jsDelivr. It now uses `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL` when set. The compiler already downloads and inlines remote scripts, so the render fetches GSAP from the mirror at compile time. The same rewrite runs on every sub-composition mounted with `data-composition-src`, at any depth, before it is compiled and hoisted. A sub-composition's script path is checked the way the inliner resolves it (a sibling file first, then the project root), so a copy that exists next to the scene is kept. An invalid value fails the render with the same configuration error Studio gives. The value is read only when a rewrite is needed, so a bad value cannot fail renders that never touch it. Renders do not use the CLI's bundled copy: they compile outside the preview server, so there is no same-origin root to point at.

**Plain http** (review note 2). `normalizeGsapBaseUrl` now accepts `http://` only for `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` and `::1`, and requires HTTPS for any other host. This covers both Studio and renders.

**Not changed, on purpose.** URLs authored in a composition stay as written, including the jsDelivr GSAP tag in the `init` templates. When Studio writes the first animation into a file that has no GSAP, it still writes the jsDelivr URL, because that file has to render outside Studio. The docs now say both.

## Before

Studio on `main` with `HYPERFRAMES_GSAP_BASE_URL` unset, opened in headless Chromium against a project that vendors GSAP locally. Every request the page and its preview iframe made was recorded; opening the editor requests `MotionPathPlugin.min.js` from jsDelivr.

![Request log on main: MotionPathPlugin from jsDelivr](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/bfd3eba23c197b479092863d9abe52fabf0bc8cf/before-requests.png)

![Studio on main](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/bfd3eba23c197b479092863d9abe52fabf0bc8cf/before-studio.png)

## After

Same project, same browser, this branch. The plugin comes from the preview server at `/api/vendor/npm`, and no request leaves the preview server's origin.

![Request log on this branch: MotionPathPlugin from the preview server, no other origins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/bfd3eba23c197b479092863d9abe52fabf0bc8cf/after-requests.png)

![Studio on this branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/bfd3eba23c197b479092863d9abe52fabf0bc8cf/after-studio.png)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New tests (19 of them fail when the source changes are reverted to `main`):

- **Default preview uses the local root, no jsDelivr.** `preview.test.ts` covers the root document, sub-composition and MotionPathPlugin injection. `studioServer.previewAssets.test.ts` exercises the real CLI server, fetches all three files from the route, and checks the 404s.
- **Version mismatch falls back to jsDelivr.** Covered in `gsapCdn.test.ts`, `preview.test.ts` and `gsapSoftReload.test.ts` (editor preload with a `3.14.2` runtime).
- **Env var precedence.** Covered in `preview.test.ts` and `studioServer.previewAssets.test.ts`.
- **http rejected for remote hosts, allowed for loopback.** Covered in `gsapCdn.test.ts` and `preview.test.ts`.
- **Render path.** `htmlCompiler.test.ts` checks that the mirror is fetched and inlined, that jsDelivr is kept when no mirror is set, and that invalid values fail. It also covers a missing GSAP script in a sub-composition and in a sub-composition of a sub-composition (both fail without the fix), and a sub-composition whose GSAP exists next to it (kept, nothing fetched).
- **Cache.** The preview ETag changes when the bundled copy replaces jsDelivr.

Run locally:

- `bun run build`, `bun run lint`, `bun run format:check`, `bun run --filter '*' typecheck`, `bun run typecheck:scripts`, `bun run verify:packed-manifests`, `bun run check:cli-lazy-deps`: all pass.
- Tests: core 5191, studio-server 1408 and studio 8023 pass. CLI: 5668 pass. 21 browser and process tests failed because Chrome timed out starting on a loaded machine. I reran five of those files on their own with chrome-headless-shell, and all 19 of their tests passed. Producer unit: 1022 pass. One integration suite, `lateVisibleImageGrading`, timed out because the local test sandbox blocks loopback listening; it does not touch this code.
- Manual: the captures above, plus a check that the served files are the GSAP `3.15.0` builds with their license headers intact.

title: fix(studio): load GSAP core when only a GSAP plugin is on the page
body:
## What

Studio preview now loads GSAP core when a page has a GSAP plugin but no GSAP core, and puts core ahead of any GSAP plugin already in `<head>`. The "is GSAP core on the page" check matches only a core script: the core file (gsap.js, gsap.min.js, or a vendored gsap-3.14.2.min.js) from a CDN, a local path, or the `/api/vendor/npm` route, or an inlined core library. Plugin files such as MotionPathPlugin and CustomEase no longer count, and neither does authored usage such as `gsap.registerPlugin(...)` or `gsap.defaults(...)`.

## Why

A composition with a motion path and Studio-edited motion, but no GSAP script of its own, previewed with no animation. Studio injected MotionPathPlugin first. Then the Studio motion step checked for GSAP with a regex that matched "gsap" anywhere in a script src. The plugin URL (`.../gsap@3.15.0/dist/MotionPathPlugin.min.js`) matched, so core was never injected. With no `window.gsap`, the plugin could not register, and both the composition's tweens and the Studio motion failed.

To reproduce on main: a project whose index.html has no GSAP script, has an inline script containing `motionPath: {...}`, and has a `.hyperframes/studio-motion.json` with one motion. Open the preview. Only MotionPathPlugin.min.js is requested, and `window.gsap` is undefined.

## Related work

Refs #6205

Overlaps with #6247 (GSAP mirror, merged) and #6256 (local GSAP by default, open). This PR does not touch the lines #6256 changes. `git merge-tree` against #6256's head (ec7502aa) merges with no conflicts.

## How

- New `packages/studio-server/src/helpers/gsapCoreScript.ts`:
  - `isGsapCoreUrl` (moved out of preview.ts and extended to accept a vendored `gsap-<version>.min.js`, which registry blocks ship).
  - `htmlHasGsapCore` counts only a core script: a core src, a producer `/* inlined: <url> */` marker whose URL is core, the core license banner (`GSAP 3.x`), or a string only the core library body contains (`Missing plugin? gsap.registerPlugin()`). Usage (`gsap.registerPlugin`, `gsap.defaults`, `gsap.to`) and the "GreenSock" text that every plugin build also carries do not count.
  - `insertGsapCoreBeforeHeadPlugin` puts core just before the first GSAP plugin script in the head (a plugin src, an inlined plugin marker, or a plugin license banner), whether authored or added by an earlier step. When the head has no plugin, callers append core to the head as before.
- `preview.ts`: Studio motion's dependencies (core, then CustomEase) are injected before the MotionPathPlugin step, and core goes ahead of any plugin already in the head. The existing "put the plugin right after the core script" logic then places an injected MotionPathPlugin after core.
- `subComposition.ts`: the sub-composition preview fallback used `headContent.includes("gsap")`, so a head with only a plugin script (or any text containing "gsap") skipped core. It now uses `htmlHasGsapCore`, and inserts core before the first plugin in the borrowed head.
- `packages/lint/src/rules/gsap.ts` `missing_gsap_script`: a src counts only when it is the core file, and inline core counts only by a core inlining marker, the core license banner, the core library body, or `_gsScope`. Dropped: any "GreenSock" text (plugins carry it too), `gsap.config/defaults/version` calls (usage), and "any inline script over 5KB that mentions gsap" (usage).
- Audited and left alone, because they detect GSAP use or rewrite every GSAP dist file on purpose rather than asking "is core loaded": the preview CDN fallback loader and producer's CDN rewrite (both cover all `gsap@x/dist/*` files), the preview CustomEase and MotionPathPlugin presence checks (they ask about one plugin, and now run after core is placed), `compositionCensus.detectGsap` and the capture content extractor (usage signals), lint's `isGsapLibraryComment` (finds any GSAP library span, core or plugin, to skip it), `htmlParser` (skips library scripts when finding animation code), the SDK's `getGsapScript` (finds the animation script block), and `grade-compare`'s fixed template.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. Each new case below fails at bd3defe75d (the head before the review fixes) and passes now.
  - `preview.test.ts`: a page with no GSAP, a motion path and Studio motion gets core, and core comes before MotionPathPlugin. A head with an authored MotionPathPlugin (alone, with `gsap.registerPlugin(MotionPathPlugin)` after it, and with another script before it) gets core inserted before that plugin.
  - `subComposition.test.ts`: a project head with only a plugin script, with and without an authored `gsap.registerPlugin(...)`, gets core before the plugin.
  - `gsapCoreScript.test.ts`: core URLs (CDN, cdnjs, `/api/vendor/npm`, relative, vendored, with a query) and the core library body match. Plugin URLs, a plugin inlining marker, a plugin license banner, authored `registerPlugin`/`defaults`/`config`/`to` calls, and core inside `<template>` do not. `insertGsapCoreBeforeHeadPlugin` places core before a plugin src, a local plugin, an inlined plugin and a plugin banner, and leaves a body-only or `<template>` plugin alone.
  - `lint/src/rules/gsap.test.ts`: plugin-only src reports `missing_gsap_script`, and so do inline `gsap.defaults(...)`, a large "GreenSock" comment, and an inlined plugin with no core. `/api/vendor/npm/.../gsap.min.js`, `assets/gsap-3.14.2.min.js` and an inline core license banner do not.
- [x] Manual testing performed: rendered the preview HTML through `registerPreviewRoutes` and loaded it in headless Chromium (puppeteer), logging script requests and page state.

**No GSAP, motion path, Studio motion (main, 19374955c7 vs this branch)**

```

title: Local image query strings break bundled compositions and snapshots
body:
### Describe the bug Local image URLs with cache-busting queries stop loading after bundling. An authored `` loads normally, but `bundleToSingleHtml()` turns it into `data:image/png;base64,?v=2`. Chrome rejects that URL with `ERR_INVALID_URL`. CLI snapshots lose the same image. ### Minimal reproduction With `@hyperframes/core@0.8.193` available, save this as `repro.mjs` and run `node repro.mjs`: ```js import { mkdirSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { bundleToSingleHtml } from "@hyperframes/core/compiler"; mkdirSync("query-repro", { recursive: true }); writeFileSync("query-repro/green.png", Buffer.from( "iVBORw0KGgoAAAANSUhEUgAAAAgAAAAICAYAAADED76LAAAAHUlEQVR4AdzKMREAAACCQI/+nbWB7sL6yH00+gABAAD//9z6uLQAAAAGSURBVAMAa8EQAfftxdwAAAAASUVORK5CYII=", "base64")); writeFileSync("query-repro/index.html", ` Image query
`); writeFileSync("query-repro/bundled.html", await bundleToSingleHtml("query-repro")); ``` ### Steps to reproduce Open `query-repro/bundled.html` in Chrome and inspect `Array.from(document.images, image => image.naturalWidth)`. The same accepted composition also fails in `hyperframes snapshot query-repro --at 0.5 --no-end --describe false`. Keep generated comparison HTML outside the composition root when running project lint. ### Expected behavior All four images remain visible after bundling. Inlining can discard a file's cache-busting query because its bytes are already embedded; the fragment should remain available. ### Actual behavior Natural widths are `[8, 0, 8, 0]`. Both query-bearing references fail. With `inlineAssets: false`, all four widths are 8. CLI snapshot warns that two images failed to load. ### Environment Reproduced on main `f21c3e3e7e8387ec9638cac2179f39c630ffabcf`, Bun 1.4.4, Node 26.11.1, Linux x64, Chrome Headless Shell 152.0.7977.30, FFmpeg n9.0.2. Also executed the integrity-verified published `@hyperframes/core@0.8.193` compiler with isolated workspace dependencies. Its affected URLs, failed image states and painted output match. This is a release-core check, not a full packaged release CLI run. ### Additional context The shared inliner appends the query to base64 data. Ordinary path rebasing needs to preserve queries and already works. This is distinct from #2417's static-server query handling and #5319's quoted CSS URL scanning.

title: Encoded external asset paths are omitted from project archives
body:
### Describe the bug A project can use `../shared/poster%20art.svg` successfully locally, then silently lose the poster when it is packed for publish or cloud rendering. The archive localizer looks for a literal `%20` filename rather than `poster art.svg`. Unicode escapes fail the same way. ### Minimal reproduction From a built repository checkout, create a synthetic project and sibling poster: ```bash mkdir -p archive-repro/project/assets archive-repro/shared ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i color=c=black:s=320x180:d=1 -an -c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p archive-repro/project/assets/clip.mp4 cat > 'archive-repro/shared/poster art.svg' <<'SVG' SVG cat > archive-repro/project/index.html <<'HTML' External poster
HTML ``` Use the same staging helper consumed by publish and cloud render to inspect the ZIP without uploading: ```bash bun --eval 'import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs"; import { createPublishArchive } from "./packages/cli/src/utils/publishProject.ts"; const archive = createPublishArchive("archive-repro/project"); writeFileSync("archive-repro/project.zip", archive.buffer); console.log(archive.fileCount);' unzip -l archive-repro/project.zip ``` ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open the original project. The green poster loads. 2. Build the archive. Move and unpack it away from the original sibling `shared` folder. 3. Open the relocated project. The poster is missing and returns 404. A plain `poster.svg` control is copied and keeps working. The real `cloud render --dry-run --json` reports the same two-file archive for the encoded case, with no error. ### Expected behavior The archive includes the sibling poster and rewrites its reference to a URL that resolves to that copied file. ### Actual behavior Only `index.html` and `assets/clip.mp4` are included. The HTML retains the unresolved `../shared/poster%20art.svg`. Local files with spaces and non-ASCII names are valid and load before packaging. ### Environment Reproduced on main `f21c3e3e7e8387ec9638cac2179f39c630ffabcf`, Linux x64, Bun 1.4.4, Node 26.11.1, FFmpeg n9.0.2. Relocated browser checks used Chrome Headless Shell 152.0.7928.2. The integrity-verified published `hyperframes@0.8.193` archive helper also omits encoded external `src` assets. That release predates #5309's poster scanning, so its plain poster behavior is not a passing control for this report. ### Additional context #1160 introduced external asset localization and #5309 added poster scanning. This is a URL decoding failure in the existing resolver, distinct from proxy baking and media offloading. No authenticated publish or cloud upload was needed to reproduce it.

title: fix(cli): check finishes on long projects with many video clips
body:
## What

`hyperframes check` now finishes on long projects with many video clips. Before, a 500 s project with 137 clips of one 1440p source failed at the 120 s deadline.

## Why

`check` loaded every `<video>` in the project at once. On that project one renderer reached 6.4 GB (all renderers together 15.75 GB). The second sampling Chrome crashed, and a crashed puppeteer page emits `error` but never settles the calls pending on it, so the run waited out the idle deadline. The same project pinned to one Chrome passed, which is how the cause was found. Narrowing with `--range` did not help: `--range 0,20 --samples 1` failed the same way, because the page loads the whole project before any range applies.

## How

- `check` marks its page with Studio's existing capture mode (`hyperframes-studio-preview` meta, `content="capture"`), the mode Studio's own screenshot path uses. Only media near the playhead loads, so decoders no longer pile up.
- The clip-fit audit (`auditClipDurations`) could no longer read the duration of audio the page never loaded, so it reads it from a detached element on the same source.
- `createPageDriver` settles every call with the page's `error` or `close`. A dead helper page now hands its samples back to the main page (the existing recovery path, which never ran for a hang), and a dead main page fails at once with "The page crashed".

Not in this PR: splitting a long check into parallel time windows. A 500 s project now checks in about half a minute, so it is not needed yet. Printing the partial report when `check` is killed by a signal is a separate change.

## Test plan

Measured on a 4-core Linux box, `check --json`, fixtures built for this (a 1440p H.264 source cut into many clips, synthetic audio):

| Fixture | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 500 s, 137 clips of one 1440p source, 41 audio | fails at 124 s | passes in 31 s |
| same project, one Chrome | 73 s | 29 s |
| same project, `--range 0,20 --samples 1` | fails at 131 s | passes in 4 s |
| same project, `--timeout 15000` | not run | passes in 17 s |
| 570 s, 957 MB H.264 | 14 s | 9 s |
| 27 s film, one-keyframe 300 s source | 11 s | 10 s |

Peak renderer memory on the first fixture went from 15.75 GB to 1.77 GB. The findings (code, severity, message) are identical before and after on the first three fixtures, compared against a one-Chrome run without the change.

- [x] Unit tests added: a helper whose page crashes and leaves its seek pending, a main page that crashes, the capture-mode marker, and the audio duration probe.
- [x] Each fix broken in turn: dead-page guard (2 tests fail), marker (1 fails), duration probe (1 fails); restored, three green runs of the three test files (48, 10 and 21 tests).
- [x] Manual testing performed (table above).

The previous helper-crash test threw `Target closed` from the seek, which real puppeteer does not do for a renderer crash. That is why the hang was not covered; the new test models the real behaviour (page emits `error`, call stays pending).

title: fix(cli): stop 'hyperframes add' hanging when a desktop clipboard is available
body:
`hyperframes add` hung forever on a Linux desktop with `xclip`, after writing the files but before printing anything.

## Cause
The copy ran `spawnSync(xclip)` with the default inherited output pipes and no timeout. `xclip` forks a background owner for the selection, and that process keeps the pipes open, so `spawnSync` never returned.

## Fix
The copy now sends the tool's output to nowhere (only the input pipe is kept) and has a 5 s timeout. A tool that cannot be reached reports "not copied", as before.

## Check
Real `xclip` under a private Xvfb, calling `copyToClipboard`: before, no return in 20 s (killed); after, `true` in 9 ms. The unit test mocks `spawnSync` and asserts the pipes are not inherited and a timeout is set (no real timers); it fails on the old code.

title: fix(cli): snapshot fails with the clip and time instead of a silent black frame
body:
`hyperframes snapshot` could return a black video frame with no explanation when FFmpeg ran out of time on a long, late-in-the-file frame (seen on a 5-minute 10-bit HEVC clip).

## Cause
When the keyframe-landing probe finds no usable seek, the fallback decoded from 0 s up to the target. On 4K HEVC that takes about 46 s against a 30 s cap, and the timeout returned `null`, which the caller only counted as "a frame missing" with no clip or time.

## Fix
- The fallback now seeks to 5 s before the target frame and decodes from there, with the same frame filter as the keyframe paths, instead of from 0 s.
- A timeout throws an error naming the clip and the time, and the snapshot records it as a finding (and a console warning) while every other clip and frame still lands. Unreadable files still return `null` as before.

## Check
Three tests fail on main and pass here: a timeout (mocked FFmpeg result, no real timer) rejects with the clip name and time; the snapshot's per-clip wrapper returns no frame and records that finding instead of throwing (any other error, such as missing FFmpeg, still propagates); and on a 12 s single-keyframe clip the frame at 10.02 s is seeked from about 5 s and equals the full-decode frame. The existing snapshot suite (78 cases, including the B-frame and open-GOP MPEG-TS cases) still passes.

Not reproduced: why the seek probe fails on the reporter's real iPhone file, which this does not address.

title: perf(core): text edits stop rebuilding the preview's caches every frame
body:
## What

Changing text in a preview no longer makes the runtime throw away and rebuild its timing caches, or rescan the page for color-graded media. Only DOM changes that can move a clip's timing, or add or remove graded media, do.

## Why

The runtime watches the document for anything that can change clip windows, durations or composition hosts, and bumps a timing revision when it sees one. Every cache keyed to that revision is rebuilt on the next read: the media clip index, the per-selector query cache, the root-composition cache and the host lookup. The watch listened to child-list changes anywhere in the document (`childList` + `subtree` on the root), and any record at all bumped the revision.

The color-grading runtime has its own observer on `body` with the same shape: any child-list record re-ran `refresh()`, a `querySelectorAll` for graded sources plus a pass over every tracked element.

A film whose scenes change text every frame (a typewriter caption setting `textContent`) therefore rebuilt all of those caches on every frame of playback. On a 50 s 4K film with 7 scenes, 112 short video clips and animated captions, the watch received 408,206 child-list records during one play-through, 245 per frame: 405k text-node swaps inside caption elements and about 1.3 inserted `<span>`s per frame, none of which carry timing.

## Related work

Refs #6189. Independent of it: none of the lines here are inside #6189's changes to `init.ts`, and the patch applies cleanly on top of it.

## How

- `runtime/mutationRecords.ts` adds one predicate builder, `createRecordFilter(selector, holds?)`: attribute records count as before (both observers already filter them), and a child-list record counts only when a node it adds or removes matches or contains `selector`, or `holds` says it contains something the caller tracks. Text and comment nodes never count.
- `createTimingRecordFilter(timingAttributes)` builds the timing selector: an element timing is read from is any element carrying one of the observed timing attributes (which include `id`, since a start can name another element, and `src`), `video`, `audio`, `source`, `script` (a script can register a timeline) or an audio group. Text and comment nodes never count.
- `init.ts` builds that predicate from the same attribute list the observer filters on (`COMPOSITION_TIMING_ATTRIBUTES`), so the observer and the predicate cannot disagree about what a timing input is. The observer callback and every `takeRecords()` site (`queryForTransport`, `readCompositionTimingRevision`, `withoutOwnTimingRecords`, `withoutOwnCompositionRecords`) now go through it.
- `colorGrading.ts` builds its filter from `COLOR_GRADING_SOURCE_SELECTOR`, with `holds` checking the elements it already tracks, so a removed wrapper still drops media graded through `setGrading` without the attribute.
- Renders are unchanged in behaviour: the render path already bypasses these caches.

## Measured

Studio-like playback of that film in `<hyperframes-player>` at 1x for the whole 50 s, headless Chrome 152 on an Apple silicon Mac with GPU compositing, GPU rasterization and hardware video decode on. Base is `main` with #6189 merged on top (the film needs #6189 to play at all); "after" adds this change. Three alternating runs each, trace on; the host was shared (load 7 to 15).

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| main-thread work per frame, median of runs (p50 / p95) | 13.5 / 42.1 ms | 11.5 / 40.0 ms |
| frames with over 8 ms of main-thread work (of ~1,650) | 1,337 to 1,373 | 1,046 to 1,131 |
| main thread busy, ms per s (median) | 705 | 647 |
| script, ms per s (median) | 562 | 498 |
| frame rate (median) | 32.8 fps | 33.5 fps |

With the timing filter alone, one profiled run each with an unminified runtime put the runtime's own time over the 50 s (outside the film's scene code) at 8.2 s before and 6.1 s after (5.0 to 3.7 ms per frame); the color-grading `refresh()` was 1.3 s of what remained.

In the profile, the four functions behind the rebuilds (`queryForTransport`, `refreshRuntimeMediaCache`, `mediaStartInput`, `isCompositionHost`, about 2.2 s together) drop out of the top of the list. Frame rate barely moves on this film because its own per-frame scene script is the larger cost; that is outside this repo.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

- `timingMutations.test.ts`, on real `MutationObserver` records: text replaced inside an untimed element and an inserted untimed element do not count; an inserted clip, a subtree holding a `<video>`, a removed clip, an inserted element with an `id`, a timing attribute edit and an inserted `<script>` do.
- `init.timingMutations.test.ts`, through the runtime: after a caption's text changes, or a plain `<span>` is inserted into it, the next seek and frame do not rebuild the media clip index; adding a clip, removing one or changing a clip's `data-start` does. Fails on `main` (`expected 1 to be +0` on the text case).
- `colorGrading.test.ts`: a text edit and an inserted plain `<span>` do not rescan for graded media (fails with the observer refreshing on every record); graded media inserted inside a wrapper is still adopted and dropped when the wrapper is removed; media graded through `setGrading` without the attribute is dropped when its wrapper is removed (fails without `holds`).
- Each part checked by breaking it: counting every record fails both text cases and the runtime text test; dropping the descendant check fails the subtree case; ignoring removed nodes fails the removed-clip case and the runtime rebuild test.
- The new and changed test files pass 3 runs in a row. Full `packages/core/src/runtime` suite: 98 files, 2,422 tests, exit 0. Pre-commit lint, format, typecheck and fallow pass; `check-comment-citations` and `comment-ratchet` pass.

title: fix(cli): a check that is stopped by a signal prints the report it has so far
body:
## What

A `check` that is stopped by SIGTERM or SIGINT now prints the report it has so far, including one finding that says it stopped before finishing, and then exits 143 or 130 as before.

## Why

Stopped by a signal, `check` closed Chrome and exited 143 or 130 with nothing on stdout. A caller that stops a long check (a package-script runner, a CI step with its own time limit) got no result at all, not even the findings the check had already made.

## How

- `browser/launch.ts` already owns SIGINT and SIGTERM. It gains `onStopSignal(listener)`, called when a stop signal arrives and before the browsers close, so a command is told while its page is still there.
- `CheckDeadline.stop(signal)` expires the check at once, the way an idle deadline does. The existing path then builds the report from the findings kept so far and adds the finding "Check stopped before finishing (SIGTERM)." No second reporting path.
- `check` registers a shutdown step that waits for the report to be printed (up to 5 s) before the process exits, so the exit cannot cut the report off.
- Also here, from the comment-share check on the previous change: the comments added there are removed and `loadCheckHtml` is renamed `loadCheckHtmlWithDeferredMedia`, so the name says what the comment did.

Not covered: a signal that arrives before `check` has started its deadline (while linting) still exits immediately with no report, as before.

## Test plan

On a 4-core Linux box, `check --json` on a 500 s project, killed 8 s in:

| Signal | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| SIGTERM | 0 bytes on stdout | exit 143, full JSON report (4.2 KB) with the stopped finding |
| SIGINT | not run (same handler) | exit 130, full JSON report with the stopped finding |

- [x] Unit tests added: `CheckDeadline.stop` ends a pending call at once and keeps the partial results; a command-level test sends SIGTERM mid-check and asserts the report is printed before exit 143.
- [x] Each part broken in turn: deadline stop (1 test fails), the pipeline's signal listener (1 fails), the wait for the report (1 fails, the exit comes before the print); restored, three green runs of `checkDeadline`, `check` and `launch` tests (9, 127 and 2 tests).
- [x] Manual testing performed (table above).

title: test: two flaky queue tests no longer race real time or the first copy's start
body:
Two tests that ejected a PR from the merge queue overnight raced real time. Test-only change.

## Download-stall test
`does not call a download that keeps sending bytes a stall` ran a real child with a 0.2 s stall window against a byte every 80 ms. Under load a delayed tick looked like a real stall (queue logs: "stalled: no data for 0.2s" on a download still sending), in three separate queue runs.

The property is that progress re-arms the watchdog, so it is now tested in `installInChild.test.ts` with a fake clock and a fake worker: progress arriving just inside the window for 20 s never aborts, and silence for the window aborts with the host and window in the message. Breaking the re-arm makes both tests fail. The process test that remains only waits for a child that is expected to end, so its inner give-up timer is now a generous bound (110 s) instead of a race against 20 s.

## Project-history test
`never copies the media of a folder that replaced the project` assumed the first copy was already running when the test replaced the folder. The copy starts asynchronously after open, so on a slow runner it had not started and nothing was copied (`expected [] to deeply equal ['a.bin']`, in two queue runs). The test now waits for the first copy to be in flight before replacing the folder. With a 150 ms stall added to the copy's start, the old test fails with that exact message and the new one passes.

## Check
- Original download-stall test: 9 of 12 failed with 16 CPU burners on a 32-core box. Fixed tests: 0 of 20 failed with 32 burners; three more plain runs green.
- Old project-history test never failed in 52 runs under load alone; the stall above is what reproduces it.

## Not in this PR
The Windows `captureCompositionFrame.slowScript` failure (`net::ERR_ABORTED` after 1.2 s, well before the 15 s script) is not fixed: 25 looped runs on a Windows runner (17 under CPU burners, 8 alongside the browser suite with two workers) never reproduced it, so there is no cause yet and no retry was added.

Stands alone: its own root cause, already approved, so folding it into another PR would reset that review.

title: perf(engine): vp9 and vp8 sources without an alpha plane extract as jpeg
body:
## What

A VP9 or VP8 video without transparency is now read into the render as JPEG frames instead of PNG. Until now every VP9/VP8 source was extracted as PNG, because its alpha can ride in a side channel that ffprobe does not always report, so the engine could not tell an opaque file from a transparent one. PNG at 4K is slow to write and slow to decode in the browser. On a plain 83-frame 4K chunk whose background is a 4K VP9 file, the chunk went from 55-60 s to about 40 s, with about 28% less CPU (22% counting the planning run too). Transparent VP9/VP8 sources keep PNG and keep their alpha.

## Why

Opaque VP9 is the common case for downloaded and screen-recorded footage, and it was paying the PNG cost that only transparent files need.

## Related work

None.

## How

- When the metadata of a VP8/VP9 stream with no alpha tag is read, one frame is decoded with the alpha-aware decoder (`libvpx-vp9` / `libvpx`, the same decoder extraction uses), scaled to 8x8 and written as rawvideo, and the pixel format of that decoded frame is read back. The result is stored as `VideoMetadata.alphaPlaneDecoded`.
- `resolveFrameFormat` keeps PNG for VP8/VP9 unless `alphaPlaneDecoded === false`. So:
  - a tagged alpha stream is decided by `hasAlpha` as today and is not probed;
  - an untagged stream whose decoded frame has an alpha plane (`yuva420p`) stays PNG;
  - a probe that fails, times out, or reads no pixel format leaves the field absent, which keeps PNG;
  - a distributed plan written by an older producer has no field, which keeps PNG.
- The decision is structural (what the decoder actually produced), not a guess from tags or file names, which is why it cannot turn a real alpha source into JPEG: the only path to JPEG is a successful decode that produced a pixel format without alpha.
- The distributed plan reader accepts the optional field and validates it as a boolean when present.

## Test plan

| File | What it covers | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `engine/src/utils/ffprobe.test.ts` | New: the decode probe on real VP9/VP8 files with and without alpha; `extractMediaMetadata` stores `false` only for untagged VP8/VP9 (not for tagged alpha, not for other codecs); a failed probe leaves the field absent | 118 passed, 4 failed (122). The same 4 HDR PNG tests fail on a clean `main` checkout in the same tree (115 passed, 4 failed of 119): their PNG fixture was a Git LFS pointer there |
| `engine/src/services/videoFrameExtractor.test.ts` | New: `resolveFrameFormat` truth table over codec x `hasAlpha` x `alphaPlaneDecoded` x requested format | 214 passed |

**1. Alpha is preserved.** 1280x720, 2 s, 25 fps VP9 with alpha (left half opaque, right half alpha 0, `yuva420p`, `-auto-alt-ref 0`), the same file with its `alpha_mode` tag stripped, and an opaque `yuv420p` VP9 of the same picture, through `extractMediaMetadata` + `extractVideoFramesRange`:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| VP9 alpha, tagged | true | (not probed) | 25 png | left 255 on 100% of pixels, right 0 on 100% |
| VP9 alpha, tag stripped | false | true | 25 png | left 255 on 100% of pixels, right 0 on 100% |
| VP9 opaque | false | false | 25 jpg | |

| Time | main: ramp tiles / at risk | this branch: ramp tiles / at risk |
|---|---|---|
| 0.2 s | 1575 / 1575 | 1668 / 1663 |
| 0.6 s | 1664 / 1664 | 1731 / 1725 |
| 1.0 s | 1701 / 1701 | 1778 / 1767 |

Both are flagged because the crf-32 source itself is already banded; this branch has 3.7-5.6% more at-risk tiles, inside the 10% bar set for this check, and the stretched images show the same bands. Between the two outputs: SSIM All 0.999436 (Y 0.999263), PSNR Y 49.7 dB.

**3. Same picture, faster.** A 4K composition whose full-frame background is a VP9 `yuv420p` file (plus a VP9 alpha overlay pair and three MP4s), chunk 0 (83 frames), `main` and this branch run alternately on the same machine:

| | Chunk wall (2 runs) | CPU user+sys (2 runs) |

title: fix(studio-server): undoing a video rename brings the file back under its old name
body:
## What

Undoing a rename of a video or audio file works again: the file comes back under its old name, and redo renames it again.

## Why

Since project history stopped copying media (#6171), undoing a media rename was refused with "An earlier version of assets/clip.mp4 is not kept, so this cannot be brought back." The rename's entry puts the same bytes back at the old path and deletes the new one. `writeAs` checks that every hash it is about to write is in the store before it writes anything, and the media bytes are not there yet. They only arrive when the delete in the same write sets the file aside (#6215). The check ran too early for the one case where the write itself provides the bytes.

Repro: in a project with history open, create `a.mp4`, rename it to `b.mp4`, then undo the rename. Before this fix, the undo throws the message above and nothing moves.

## Related work

Refs #6171, #6215.

## How

`writeAs` already orders deletes before writes, and `writeProjectFile` sets aside any media file it deletes. The pre-check now also accepts a hash that one of this write's deletes is about to set aside (the tracked hash of each deleted path). Undoing an in-place edit of a media file is still refused with the same message, because its old bytes were never kept and no delete in the write provides them (the existing `uncopied.test.ts` case still passes). A write that swaps two media files between two paths without a delete is still refused: neither file is set aside before the other one needs it.

## What I measured

- New case in `undoUncopied.test.ts`: create a video, rename it, undo, redo. Before the fix it fails with "An earlier version of join.mp4 is not kept, so this cannot be brought back." With the fix it passes: after undo the old name has the identical bytes and the new name is gone; after redo it is the other way round.
- Fails without the fix: the same case on main fails with exactly that error.
- History suite (`src/history/`): 241 passed, 3 runs in a row.
- Desktop's end-to-end rename walk (rename a video in Media, then one Cmd+Z brings back the file and its clip label) fails on 0.8.194 with this error. It passes on 0.8.194 with this exact change applied to the built package.

## What I did NOT exercise

- Undoing a rename of a media file over 64 MiB that is not a video or audio file (same path through the code; not tested on its own).
- Swapping two media files between two names in one change: still refused, as before.
- The `packages/studio-server` route suites.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed (Desktop rename walk on a built package with this change)
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## Size

Under 100 lines on purpose: a lone urgent fix that blocks the Desktop production release (its rename walk fails on 0.8.194), with no open PR in this area to carry it.

title: fix(sdk): release the parsed film when a session is disposed
body:
## What

`Composition.dispose()` now drops the parsed document and the element snapshot caches.

## Why

A disposed session kept its whole parsed (linkedom) document. Anything that still referenced the session, such as a stale closure or a React fiber's old props, therefore kept the replaced film alive, so Studio's memory grew with every film swap.

## Measured

Headless Chrome, a generated fixture project (150 clips, 2 videos, 25 off-canvas elements), swapping between two films 25 times with no other interaction, heap read after a forced GC:

| | Heap at swap 0 | Heap at swap 25 | Growth |
|---|---|---|---|
| Before | 76.8 MB | 91.9 MB | +15.1 MB |
| After | 76.1 MB | 83.7 MB | +7.6 MB |

Retained copies of the parsed film HTML in a heap snapshot at swap 25: 29 before, 4 after (the live session plus interned strings). Live documents, DOM nodes and listeners were flat in both runs.

## Not fixed here

Growth is halved, not gone: about 0.26 MB per swap remains. Stale render scopes of several memoized callbacks still chain to one another and keep a lower-case copy of each film's source and other per-swap data alive. That needs changes in several components, so it is a separate PR.

## Test

`session.dispose-release.test.ts` opens ten sessions, keeps every disposed session referenced, forces a GC and requires every parsed document to be collected. It fails on main (10 of 10 documents retained) and passes with this change, three runs in a row.

A disposed session now answers reads from an empty document instead of its old one, and outside production logs one warning with a stack the first time it is read, so a caller still holding a stale session can be found.

title: feat(lint): warn when a round-capped line hidden by its dash settings can still show a dot
body:
A line hidden before its draw tween with `stroke-linecap="round"`, `pathLength="100"`, `stroke-dasharray="100"` and `stroke-dashoffset="100"` can show a solid dot at the end of the path. It is Chrome's own behavior: the next dash starts exactly at the path end, the float conversion of `pathLength` leaves a sliver on some curves, and the cap paints it. A render, `hyperframes snapshot` and plain headless Chrome show the same dots on the same curves (3 of 48 random curves in my check), so there is nothing to fix at capture.

This adds the lint warning `svg_round_cap_hidden_dash` for that pattern on round or square caps with a `pathLength`, written as attributes or inline style, and a line in the film reference showing the safe form (gap longer than the path: `stroke-dasharray="100 120"`, `stroke-dashoffset="110"`, or keep the element `visibility: hidden` until the tween starts).

Does not warn for the safe form, butt caps, no `pathLength`, drawn or partly drawn paths, or decorative dashes. Dash values computed in script (`getTotalLength()`) are not checked; the rule only reads what is in the markup.

Checked with the built CLI: `hyperframes lint` on the 48-curve project prints the warning with the fix. 1165 lint tests pass.

Stands alone: lint and docs only, separate from the open snapshot fixes.

title: ci(release): keep the packed release tarballs as an artifact on release pull requests
body:
## What

Release pull requests (branch `release/v*`) upload the packed packages as a `release-tarballs` build artifact for pre-release testing. The Build job already packs them; it now keeps them.

## Why

A release breaks downstream users only after it is published, because the packages that will be published are not available to try beforehand. The Build job already runs `pnpm pack` for every public package to verify them, then deletes the tarballs. Keeping them lets a consumer install exactly what the release will publish and run its own checks before the release pull request merges.

## How

- `verify-packed-manifests.mjs` copies the packed `*.tgz` to `PACK_KEEP_DIR` when that is set (`keepPackedTarballs`).
- `ci.yml` sets it only when `github.head_ref` starts with `release/v`, then uploads `${{ runner.temp }}/release-tarballs/*.tgz` with 7-day retention. Other pull requests and pushes behave as before.

## Test plan

- [x] `keepPackedTarballs` has a unit test (copies the tarballs, ignores other files). Breaking the filter fails it; restored, 3 green runs.
- [ ] The upload runs only on a `release/v*` branch, so it is exercised by a throwaway `release/` branch from this commit (result below), not by this pull request's own checks.

title: fix(producer): refuse private and non-HTTPS previewUrl fetches
body:
The producer HTTP server fetched a request's `previewUrl` with a bare `fetch`, so a self-hoster's `/render` could be pointed at a cloud metadata address, localhost or an internal host, and a public URL could redirect there.

It now goes through the engine's `fetchPublicHttpsText`, the helper the producer already uses for external stylesheets: HTTPS only, private and reserved hosts refused, every redirect hop re-checked, response capped at 20 MB.

Behaviour change: an `http://` previewUrl is now refused (the failure reads "Failed to fetch previewUrl: ..."). README notes it.

Tests: five new cases (metadata over http and https, localhost, IPv6 loopback, file:) fail on main because the URL is fetched, and pass here with no fetch made; a redirect to the metadata address is refused; a public URL still renders.

Stands alone.

title: Linked narration: editing a line updates its voice-over and captions together
body:
### Problem

In a narrated video, the voice-over and the captions are made one way:

script → `hyperframes tts` → word timings (`transcribe`, or the voice engine's `words[]`) → the caption script

After that, nothing connects them. The most common review note on a narrated video is "say X instead of Y", whether it comes from the Studio, a timed comment in the desktop app, or a chat with the agent. Acting on it means:

1. voicing the line again
2. getting new word timings and re-importing the captions (heygen-com/hyperframes#6181 shows that re-import can break an existing caption script)
3. re-timing the scene, and everything after it if the length changed

In practice an agent often fixes the caption and forgets the voice, or the other way round, and the mismatch only shows when someone listens to the render. Nothing in `check` catches it.

### Proposed solution

Make each narration line one unit that the composition knows about.

- **One source per line:** `{ id, text, voice, speed }`, kept with its audio clip, its word timings, its caption words and a hash of the text. For example in a `narration.json` beside the composition, or as `data-*` attributes on the caption group.
- **Edit once:** changing a line's text (in the Studio, from the CLI, or by the agent):
  1. re-voices only that line
  2. replaces its word timings and captions
  3. moves the scene's timing if the length changed, or flags the overrun

  Other lines stay untouched.
- **Check catches drift:** `hyperframes check` reports a line whose voice text and caption text no longer match (a stale hash), as "narration out of sync".
- **A possible CLI:**
  ```sh
  hyperframes narration list
  hyperframes narration set <line-id> "new text"   # re-voice, re-caption, re-time this line
  hyperframes narration check
  ```
- **Studio:** editing a caption's text offers "Re-voice this line", and a timed comment on a narrated moment can name the line it belongs to.

### Alternatives considered

- **Fix it by hand or by the agent each time.** This is what happens now. It's error-prone, and the gap is invisible until playback.
- **Always build captions by transcribing the final mix.** The captions are then accurate, but every text change still needs a re-voice and a re-import, so editing stays slow.
- **Solve it inside one workflow skill.** I'm prototyping this in a proposed community skill, where each step's line drives its voice, captions and guide text. But that only helps that skill. The sync belongs in HyperFrames, so every narrated composition (explainers, demos, launch films with `--voice`) gets it.

### Additional context

- **Related:**
  - heygen-com/hyperframes#6349: image attachments for timed comments, the review side of this
  - heygen-com/hyperframes#6181: caption re-import
- **The skill proposal it builds on:** heygen-com/hyperframes-community-skills#24 (product-demo).
- **Offer to help:** I'm happy to work on this in core if the design fits, and would welcome guidance first: where should a line's source of truth live (a project file, or the composition HTML), and should the re-timing move later scenes automatically or only warn?

title: perf(core): avoid unnecessary motion-blur callback replays
body:
## What

Make the eventful and silent motion-blur discovery passes compare geometry by stable DOM element identity. Style-only callbacks and earlier-sibling insertion no longer make independent movers appear callback-dependent.

The change is intentionally limited to the event-dependency decision. It does not implement the broader scan caching or tier-handoff work discussed in #6867.

## Why

On untouched upstream, deterministic regressions produced four failures with 139 passing tests:

- An opacity-only callback set `readEvents=true` even though the callback did not move either element.
- Inserting a sibling before an existing mover set `readEvents=true` because the mover changed snapshot-local array index.
- Both capture and filter tiers replayed callbacks five times for one preview frame: four pose samples plus frame restoration.

The synthetic discovery workload performed 31 eventful callback invocations and 62 seeks in total, found the same single mover, and ended at the same 300 px geometry. The scan work remains 62 seeks after this change, but unnecessary per-frame callback replays fall from 5 to 0.

## Related work

Refs #6867.

This preserves the eventful-first scan, callback landing behavior, animated-ancestor coverage, and root-last restoration established by #6865.

## How

- Record per-step boxes in maps keyed by each `HTMLElement`.
- During the silent pass, read boxes for the elements found dynamic by the eventful pass even when a callback-only style remains at its final value.
- Compare the same elements at the same 1/64 px precision.
- Treat a missing eventful element or changed box as callback-dependent, while ignoring quiet-only ordering changes.

Real callback-controlled movement still produces `readEvents=true`. No public API, dependency, capture tier, filter tier, or seek ordering changes.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (not applicable; this is internal discovery behavior)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Automated results:

- Focused discovery and integration tests: 143 passed
- Motion-blur plus GSAP adapter tests: 271 passed
- Full `@hyperframes/core` suite: 5,650 passed
- Core runtime contract/coverage gate: 2,691 passed; Hyperframe linter passed
- Workspace typecheck, lint, format check, build, comment citation, comment ratchet, and Fallow audit passed

A real Chrome/GSAP probe confirmed `readEvents=false` for opacity-only and insertion cases, while genuine callback-driven movement remains `readEvents=true`. All three cases retained the expected mover and final geometry.

AI assistance disclosure: OpenAI Codex assisted with investigation, implementation, and test execution. I reviewed the complete diff and verification results.

title: fix(cli): support Antigravity global config skills discovery and mirroring
body:
## Resumen

Corrige el descubrimiento y espejado global de skills en `@hyperframes/cli` para soportar el directorio real de configuracion global de Antigravity (`~/.gemini/config/skills`) asi como las rutas globales multi-segmento definidas en `AGENT_GLOBAL_DIRS`.

## Problema

1. **Ruta global de Antigravity omitida en el espejado (`skillsMirror.ts`)**:
   - La tabla generada desde `vercel-labs/skills` (`AGENT_GLOBAL_DIRS`) registra `.gemini/antigravity/skills` y `.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills`, pero el sistema de personalizacion global de Antigravity (`agy`) carga sus skills globales desde `~/.gemini/config/skills`.
   - Cuando el usuario tiene `~/.gemini/config` inicializado, `mirrorGlobalSkills()` no replicaba las skills hacia `~/.gemini/config/skills`.
2. **Rutas globales multi-segmento ignoradas en `discoverSkillRoots` (`skillsManifest.ts`)**:
   - `discoverSkillRoots(base, scope)` escaneaba unicamente subdirectorios de un nivel (`<base>/<host>/skills` y `<base>/.config/<host>/skills`).
   - En consecuencia, `hyperframes skills check`, `hyperframes update --check` y el chequeo en segundo plano no detectaban instalaciones globales alojadas en rutas de multiples segmentos bajo `$HOME` como `~/.gemini/config/skills`, `~/.gemini/antigravity/skills`, `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills` o `~/.codeium/windsurf/skills`.
   - Ademas, `agentFromDir()` inferia `"config"` en lugar de `"antigravity"` para rutas terminadas en `.gemini/config/skills`.

## Solucion

- **`packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.ts`**:
  - Define `EXTRA_GLOBAL_DIRS` interno con `{ agent: "antigravity", base: "home", sub: ".gemini/config/skills" }` y lo incorpora en el bucle de `mirrorGlobalSkills()`.
  - Exporta `EXTRA_GLOBAL_SKILL_DIRS` con las entradas `base === "home"` de mas de dos segmentos combinando `AGENT_GLOBAL_DIRS` y `EXTRA_GLOBAL_DIRS`.
- **`packages/cli/src/utils/skillsManifest.ts`**:
  - Mantiene el modulo libre de imports relativos (solo `node:*`) para que scripts ejecutados directamente con `node --import tsx` (como `scripts/clawhub-unlist-retired.mjs`) resuelvan sin errores.
  - Actualiza `agentFromDir()` para identificar `.gemini/config/skills` como `"antigravity"`.
  - Extiende `discoverSkillRoots()`, `locateInstall()`, `presentSkills()` y `checkSkills()` con la opcion `extraGlobalDirs` (aplicada solo en `scope === "global"` y deduplicada por ruta).
- **Consumidores del CLI (`packages/cli/src/commands/skills.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/update.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsUpdateCheck.ts`)**:
  - Pasan `extraGlobalDirs: EXTRA_GLOBAL_SKILL_DIRS` a `checkSkills()` en `skills check`, `update --check` y `refreshSkillsCache()` (preservando `cwd: projectDir`).
- **Pruebas unitarias**:
  - `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsMirror.test.ts`: Verifica que `mirrorGlobalSkills()` espeja hacia `~/.gemini/config/skills` cuando existe `~/.gemini/config`.
  - `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsManifest.test.ts`: Verifica deteccion en `.gemini/config/skills`, `.gemini/antigravity/skills`, `.gemini/antigravity-cli/skills` y `.codeium/windsurf/skills`, mas inferencia de agente/scope con `--dir`.
  - `packages/cli/src/utils/skillsUpdateCheck.test.ts`: Verifica que `refreshSkillsCache()` conserva `cwd: projectDir` y pasa `extraGlobalDirs`.
  - `packages/cli/src/commands/skills.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/skills.output.test.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/update.test.ts`: Actualizan los mocks de `skillsMirror.js` con `importOriginal` y validan el paso de `extraGlobalDirs` en `update --check`.

title: fix(cli): warn at init when ffmpeg is missing and give macos a non-homebrew route
body:
## What

- `init` prints one warning line when FFmpeg or FFprobe cannot be resolved, in both the interactive and the non-interactive path. Before, it only checked when given `--video`.
- On macOS the FFmpeg install hint now also gives the routes that work without Homebrew: `HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH` / `HYPERFRAMES_FFPROBE_PATH` and `.hyperframes/bin`. The hint is shared, so `doctor`, `render`, `snapshot`, `transcribe` and the rest pick it up too.

```
FFmpeg and FFprobe not found: preview and check work, but render needs both. Install: brew install ffmpeg, or without Homebrew point HYPERFRAMES_FFMPEG_PATH and HYPERFRAMES_FFPROBE_PATH at ffmpeg and ffprobe binaries, or copy both into the project's .hyperframes/bin
```

## Why

Only `render` needs FFmpeg, so an agent could run `init`, go through design rounds and get approval before learning the binary was missing. On a Mac without Homebrew, the only remedy the CLI offered was `brew install ffmpeg`, which leads nowhere.

## Related work

Refs #5232. This covers two of the three items still open in @miguel-heygen's [status comment](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/issues/5232#issuecomment-6387946233): the macOS hint and the `init` warning. #5237 already did the docs part.
