title: feat(cli): add `hyperframes init --timeline` to start a project from an OTIO timeline
body:
## What

Adds `hyperframes init --timeline timeline.json`, which builds a project from an edit made in another editor. It reads a flat JSON description of the edit (`hyperframes-timeline/1`) and creates one clip element per cut. Source trims, speed changes, audio tracks, dissolves, freeze frames and image sequences carry over, and the media is copied into `assets/`.

A new `/import-timeline` skill ships a Python converter that produces `hyperframes-timeline/1` JSON from OpenTimelineIO (OTIO) and the other timeline formats OTIO can read.

```bash
~/.venvs/otio/bin/python -I scripts/otio_flatten.py cut.otio --width 1920 --height 1080 > timeline.json
npx hyperframes init my-video --timeline timeline.json --media-root ./footage
cd my-video && npx hyperframes check
```

New flags: `--timeline`, `--media-root` (where relative clip paths resolve) and `--link-media` (symlink instead of copy; copies on Windows and on disks that refuse links). `--timeline` can't be combined with `--video`, `--audio`, `--example`, `--tailwind` or `--resolution`.

## Why

Editors hand off cuts as EDL, Final Cut XML, AAF or OTIO. Today there is no way to bring an existing edit into HyperFrames except rebuilding it by hand. Importing the cut list lets someone start from the edit they already made and add motion graphics, captions and overlays on top.

<!-- ## Related work -->

## How

### Design decisions

**OTIO is the first supported timeline format.** It is open source, supported by major video editing softwares (including Davinci Resolve, Adobe Premiere, and Avid Media Composer) and has adapters for the other major timeline formats, so supporting it gets several formats without writing a parser for each one. The converter is tested with native `.otio`, EDL (`otio-cmx3600-adapter`), Final Cut Pro 7 XML (`otio-fcp-adapter`), Final Cut Pro X (`otio-fcpx-xml-adapter`) and GStreamer (`otio-xges-adapter`). AAF (`otio-aaf-adapter`) reads but is untested and carries no media, so it needs relinking first.

**A JSON schema plus a Python converter, rather than reading OTIO directly.** OTIO only ships Python and C++ bindings. The TypeScript bindings are in progress but not complete, and the HyperFrames CLI is TypeScript. So the boundary is a JSON schema:

- The **schema** is JSON Schema draft 2020-12, in `packages/core/schemas/timeline-import.json`, mirrored to `docs/schema/` and served at `https://hyperframes.heygen.com/schema/timeline-import.json`.
- The **converter** (`skills/import-timeline/scripts/otio_flatten.py`) uses the official `opentimelineio` package for all parsing and time math, then walks the result and prints flat facts as schema-conforming JSON.
- The **consumer** (`init --timeline`) reads only the JSON and never touches OTIO.

This keeps OTIO's precision and its file-format support without reimplementing either. Because the schema is the contract, any other tool can write the file, and a future TypeScript OTIO binding could replace the Python script without touching `init`.

### Implementation

**Core** (`packages/core/src/timelineImport/`, exported as `@hyperframes/core/timeline-import`)

- `schema.ts` parses and validates the file, and enforces the rules JSON Schema can't state: unique clip ids and fps between 1 and 240.
- `emit.ts` generates the composition HTML.
- `transitions.ts` plans dissolves. Each one is clamped to the handles (footage beyond the trim points) that ffprobe finds. A shortened dissolve is reported, and with no handle it stays a hard cut.
- `mediaOffset.ts` maps a clip's position on its source's own clock to seconds into the file. It tries the file's own start timecode, then the converter's `mediaOrigin` hint, then the value as written, and uses the first that places the clip inside the file.

**CLI** (`packages/cli/src/commands/`)

- `init.ts` wires up the flags. On failure it removes the directory it created.
- `initTimeline.ts` stages media and prints warnings: the first 20, then a count of the rest.
- `initTimelineSequence.ts` encodes image sequences to H.264 with ffmpeg. EXR is decoded to display light, and missing frames are held.
- `initTimelineOrigin.ts` reads each file's start timecode with ffprobe, including drop-frame timecode and WAV `time_reference`.

**Skill** (`skills/import-timeline/`): `SKILL.md`, `otio_flatten.py`, `otio_flatten_test.py` and `scripts/tests/fixtures/`.

### Behaviors worth knowing

- **Precision:** times are written to the microsecond. A cut at frame 10 of 29.97 fps is 0.333667 s, and rounding to 0.334 s renders one frame late. Clip starts round down and source in-points round up, so the cut frame lands on the new clip and shows the right source frame. NTSC rates stay exact (`30000/1001`).
- **Warnings:** everything skipped or approximated is reported and nothing is saved in the project. The exit code is 0 if anything imported, and non-zero only when nothing could be.
- **Missing media:** clips whose files can't be found are dropped and named. If none are found, the import stops and points at `--media-root`.

### Not supported

These are imported as hard cuts or skipped, each with a warning: wipes and other transition types, audio transitions, effects, color corrections, markers, generated media, reverse playback, remote URLs and editor-specific `metadata`.

### Catalog and docs

The skill is registered in `skills-manifest.json`, and the published skill count goes from 9 to 10. The skill list is updated in `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/guides/skills.mdx` and both `_shared` template files. The count and catalog references are also updated in `scripts/check-core-skills.mjs`, `scripts/sync-schemas.ts` and the two skill-lifecycle files. New docs are `docs/guides/import-from-otio.mdx` and `docs/reference/timeline-import.mdx`, plus a `docs/packages/cli.mdx` entry.

## Test plan

### Automated tests

Three small hand-written fixtures live in `skills/import-timeline/scripts/tests/fixtures/`, about 18 KB in all, and none is taken from a real production. `cut.otio` has a trim, a 2x speed change, a dissolve, a second lane with a 12-image sequence and an audio track. `cut.edl` is a two-cut EDL. Each has an expected-output file (`cut.expected.json`, `cut-edl.expected.json`) that the converter's output must match exactly. Media is generated with ffmpeg when the test runs, so no media is committed. Every other test builds its input in code or in a temp directory.

| Suite                                                           | Tests | Covers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/core/src/timelineImport/timelineImport.test.ts`       | 25    | schema parsing, the rules JSON Schema can't state (unique ids, fps range), HTML emission, lint-clean output                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `packages/core/src/timelineImport/transitions.test.ts`          | 36    | dissolve planning, handle clamping, fades from and to nothing, audio and non-dissolve transitions, fades kept inside the composition (replays the emitted tweens through real GSAP and checks their start times)                                                                                                                    |
| `packages/core/src/timelineImport/mediaOffset.test.ts`          | 17    | file timecode, `mediaOrigin` hint and plain-seconds fallbacks, rounding up                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/initTimeline.test.ts`                | 70    | staging, media lookup and relinking, `--link-media`, warnings and their cap, duplicate audio, missing media, timecode offsets                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/initTimelineOrigin.test.ts`          | 20    | ffprobe timecode and WAV `time_reference`, including drop-frame                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/initTimelineSequence.test.ts`        | 11    | image-sequence listing, missing and held frames                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/initTimelineSequence.encode.test.ts` | 14    | encodes real sequences with ffmpeg and decodes the output to check the frame count                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/init.timeline.test.ts`               | 19    | the flags, the flags that can't be combined, cleanup on failure                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/timelineImportSchema.test.ts`        | 99    | the schema file and the TypeScript parser agree; the format side never mentions OTIO                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `packages/cli/src/commands/initTimelineFixtures.test.ts`        | 3     | stages each fixture's expected JSON against ffmpeg-made media, then lints the project; checks the dissolve becomes a fade that starts inside the film                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `skills/import-timeline/scripts/otio_flatten_test.py`           | 87    | the converter: placement, trims, speed, nested stacks, transitions, image sequences (names checked against the library's own), bundles (including a reused folder whose files differ at the same size), `.otio`, EDL and the other adapters, output validated against the schema; the fixtures above flatten to their expected JSON |

The Python tests run with `python3 -I otio_flatten_test.py` in a venv with `opentimelineio` and its adapters. A new CI job, `Test: import-timeline converter`, installs pinned versions (`opentimelineio` 0.18.1 and the EDL, Final Cut Pro 7, Final Cut Pro X, GStreamer and ALE adapters, plus `jsonschema`) and runs them when a skill or the timeline schema changes. The job fails if any test is skipped, so a missing adapter can't pass silently, and the aggregate `Test` check requires it. The TypeScript fixture test runs in the existing CLI test shards.

### Real timelines

#### Checked against their reference renders:

- [**Animal Logic ALab trailer**](https://dpel.aswf.io/alab-trailer/) (ASWF Digital Production Example Library): converted and imported with `init`, then rendered and compared with the reference render. Cuts are exact, SSIM is 0.942 and PSNR 43.4 dB, and audio is aligned at 0 ms (6 dB hot, because the AAF lists the stems twice).

- [**AWS Picchu edit, 4096x2048**](https://dpel.aswf.io/aws-picchu-edit/) (ASWF Digital Production Example Library) (`.otioz` bundle): per-clip audio offsets match the reference for 75 of 88 clips. The render was 1024x512 at draft quality. Known differences: compound clips are skipped (black near 36.5 s and 410 s), and the editor's fades and one transform are not applied. A mismatch near 100 s comes from the OTIO itself: the clip's in-point is 46 frames from where the reference shows it, and ours matches the OTIO's frame exactly.

#### Clip placement check:

[**`darbyjohnston/otio-oc-examples`**](https://github.com/darbyjohnston/otio-oc-examples): all 12 files were flattened, and every clip's placement was compared with the OTIO library's own. All 12 place every clip identically.

| File                                                    | Rate   | Clips | Notes                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------ | ----- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ASC_StEM2_239_4K_24_100nits_Rec709_Stereo_ProRes422HQ` | 24     | 198   |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `STEM2_4k_ctm_ACES_239`                                 | 24     | 198   | its EXR sequences say a missing frame should show black; the importer holds the previous image instead and warns once, with a count of the clips           |
| `StEM2_MultipleMediaRefs`                               | 24     | 198   | each clip lists a full-resolution image sequence and a proxy `.mov`, with the proxy selected; the import uses the selected one and ignores the clip colors |
| `Chimera_3840x2160_2997fps_10bit_422`                   | 29.97  | 6     |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ElFuente_4096x2160_60fps_10bit_420`                    | 60     | 5     |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ElFuente_4096x2160_60fps_10bit_420_remix1`             | 60     | 10    | 4 dissolves and a lane of PNG overlays                                                                                                                     |
| `Meridian_UHD4k5994_HDR_P3PQ`                           | 59.94  | 83    |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SolLevante_Animatics_ver1_H264`                        | 23.976 | 63    |                                                                                                                                                            |
| `SolLevante_HDR10_r2020_ST2084_UHD_24fps_1000nit`       | 24     | 144   | 72 video clips and 72 audio clips, all cut from one `.mov` file                                                                                            |
| `sollevante_lp_vdm_16b_p3d65_pq_20200218_3840x2160`     | 24     | 72    | whole film as one TIFF sequence with no available range                                                                                                    |

**End-to-end `init` check**: a small timeline of two ffmpeg test clips with a dissolve and a tone track went through `init --timeline`, then `hyperframes lint` (0 errors, 0 warnings) and `hyperframes check` (passed). The dissolve's incoming clip starts early on its handle and the fade tween matches it.

title: ci(skills): lint skill-root paths and skill names in skill docs
body:
## What

Adds a rule to `scripts/lint-skills.ts` that fails CI when a skill doc points at a skill file, script or skill name that doesn't exist, and fixes the stale references the rule finds on current `main`. The head reports zero lint errors.

Supersedes #5874, which was closed because #5651 retired most of the skills it edited. This is a fresh branch from current `main`.

## Why

#5025 listed broken paths in the skills (items #11, #12, #19, #21). When an agent follows one, it gets a read error mid-task and either stops or makes up the missing guidance. #5026 fixed those by hand, but nothing stops the same kind of breakage from coming back.

The existing cross-reference rule only checks `./` and `../` paths. It deliberately skips the bare paths skills use to point at their own files: `references/x.md`, `<SKILL_DIR>/scripts/x.mjs`, `hyperframes/references/x.md` and `skills/<name>/…`.

Run against `2b82e39` (the commit #5025 audited), the rule reports every broken-path item in the issue (#11, #12, #19 and all five places in #21).

## Related work

Refs #5025. This covers the broken-path items only. The contradictions and wrong-fact items (#13–18, #20) need a person to compare content, and a path checker can't catch them.

- **#5874** (closed): the first version of this PR. The rule and its tests are carried over; the review feedback is addressed below.
- **#5651**: retired the workflow skills. It is why #5874 no longer applied.
- **#5026, #5028**: fixed the issue's items by hand. This adds the check that keeps them fixed.

### How the #5874 review was addressed

| Review feedback | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Rebase and rerun the rule against the skills that remain; 11-12 of the 22 files no longer exist and the manifest covers skills that are gone (miguel-heygen, jrusso1020) | New branch from current `main`. Every edit to a deleted skill is dropped, and `skills-manifest.json` is regenerated from the skills that exist (`gen-skills-manifest.ts --check` passes). |
| Land the rule and its fixes together, with a head where the rule reports zero, so the skills lint doesn't go red for every other PR (both) | `bun scripts/lint-skills.ts` reports no issues on this head. The "expected to fail" warning from #5874 is gone. |
| Three of the four open questions disappear with the deleted files; if one survives, an `allow=` marker or a doc fix is fine (jrusso1020) | All four were about files #5651 deleted (`guide.md`, `news/module.md`, `_anatomy.md`), so none remain. Nothing needs reviewer input. |
| `contentDirs` is whatever directories skills happen to ship, and `assets` is the only project dir excluded by name; `compositions/` is skipped only by accident, and the test passes for the same reason (miguel-heygen, jrusso1020) | Project dirs (`assets`, `compositions`, `.hyperframes`) are now an explicit list, checked where a path is classified instead of where the directory set is built. A new test has a skill that really ships all three directories and confirms their paths are still skipped. |
| The CI change should not touch the workflow, packages or environment (jrusso1020 checked this) | Unchanged: nothing under `.github/`, no package or lockfile changes, and the rule only reads the tree (`readdirSync`, `statSync`). |

Code review of this PR also turned up two more problems, both fixed here:

- **Windows skipped the rule.** Containment was a literal `"/"` prefix check, so on Windows no owning skill was found and nothing was reported. It now uses `path.relative` (`isWithin`), at all three places that compared paths. A sibling directory sharing a name prefix, such as `skills/foobar` against `skills/foo`, no longer counts as inside.
- **Paths could escape the skill.** `<SKILL_DIR>/../../scripts/lint-skills.ts` passed because the file exists in the checkout, though an installed skill can't see it. A target must now stay inside the skill that owns it. That exposed a regex bug: the `/beta` in `../beta/…` was read as a mention of skill `beta`, which made it a valid base. A preceding `.` no longer counts.

## How

`lintSkillPaths` runs on every skill markdown file, in prose and in fenced blocks, inside the existing skills CI job:

| Form | Rule |
|---|---|
| `<SKILL_DIR>/rest` | must exist under the referencing skill |
| `<NAME_SKILL_DIR>/rest` | must exist under skill `name` (`<HYPERFRAMES_AUDIO_SKILL_DIR>` → `hyperframes-audio`) |
| `<skill-name>/rest` | must exist under that skill |
| `skills/<name>/rest` | flagged in the distributed `skills/` set, since it only resolves from the repo root, not from an installed skill. `.claude/skills` and `.agents/skills` are exempt because they only run inside the repo |
| `references/…`, `scripts/…`, any dir a skill ships | must resolve under the referencing skill, a dir between it and the file, or a skill named in the same paragraph. There is no repo-root fallback |
| `` `/hyphenated-name` `` | must be a skill in this repo (`animate-text` is allow-listed as an upstream skill) |

Design decisions:

- **Containment.** A resolved path must lie inside the skill it was found under, so `..` can't reach repo files.
- **Paragraph scope for skill names.** Docs wrap lines like "`/hyperframes`⏎`references/storyboard.md`", so a bare path also resolves under any skill named in the same paragraph.
- **Skipped on purpose:** project paths (`assets/`, `compositions/`, `.hyperframes/`), placeholders (`<id>`, `{slug}`, `*`, `$VAR`), URLs and extensionless ids. Without these the first run produced about 140 hits, mostly paths in the user's project.
- **An opt-out marker per doc.** `<!-- skill-paths: allow=a,b -->` follows the existing `registry-items:` marker pattern, so exemptions stay visible in the doc's diff.

<details>
<summary>Fixes to skills found by the rule</summary>

- `media-use/audio/references/tts.md` and `tts-to-captions.md`: `skills/media-use/audio/scripts/…` → `<SKILL_DIR>/audio/scripts/…`, so the commands work once the skill is installed.
- `.claude/skills/changelog-video/SKILL.md` and its `.agents` mirror: `skills/hyperframes-media/scripts/heygen-tts.mjs` named a retired skill; it now points at `skills/media-use/audio/scripts/heygen-tts.mjs`.
- `style-sampling/references/remix.md`: "the hyperframes skill's `references/storyboard.md`" → `hyperframes/references/storyboard.md`.
- `allow=` markers for intentional tokens:
  - `remotion-to-hyperframes/references/api-map.md`: the literal `references/X.md` legend.
  - `hyperframes-registry/references/contributing.md`: a contributor guide that names repo scripts (`scripts/generate-catalog-pages.ts` and others), run from the repo root.
- `skills-manifest.json` regenerated for the three changed skills.
</details>

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `scripts/lint-skills.test.mjs` has the 7 `lintSkillPaths` tests from #5874 plus three new ones: project dirs skipped by name when a skill ships them, a path that escapes its skill is flagged even when the target exists, and `isWithin` with `path.win32` and `path.posix`.
- [x] Manual testing performed:
  - `bun scripts/lint-skills.ts` reports no issues on this head.
  - Run against `2b82e39` with the final rule, it flagged items #11, #12, #19 and #21 (all five places) of #5025, along with about 55 others.
  - `bun run build`, `bun run typecheck:scripts` and `bun run test:scripts` pass.
  - `coreSkillContent.test.ts`, `check-skill-mirror.mjs`, `check-skill-import-boundaries.test.mjs`, the manifest `--check`, oxlint and oxfmt pass.
  - `check-comment-citations.mjs` passes. `comment-ratchet.mjs` reports no change in comment share. It only grades `packages/*/src`, so it does not cover the `scripts/` files in this diff.
- [x] Documentation updated: the skill docs above. The rule documents its own `skill-paths: allow=` marker in the `lint-skills.ts` header.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

The Windows coverage is unit-level: `isWithin` is tested with `path.win32`, but the whole linter has not run on a Windows machine.

title: fix(parsers): resolve querySelectorAll loop variables for media src writes
body:
extractMediaSrcMutations only resolved getElementById/querySelector targets, so a script that sets a video src inside a querySelectorAll loop never reached the lint rule or the render probe: check stayed silent and render exported the authored clip.

This binds forEach callback parameters and for-of variables over a querySelectorAll(...) result to the loop selector, so the write resolves to the elements it targets. Writes through a shadowed or non-DOM binding still resolve to nothing.

Fixes #7504

Verified: parsers suite 1438 tests pass, lint suite 1286 tests pass, producer probe-stage tests 76 pass. New tests cover the forEach/for-of shapes at the parser, lint, and probe layers.

title: fix(cli): templates lists its slugs, keeps why a pull stopped, unpacks on Windows drives
body:
## What

Three fixes to `hyperframes templates`, the command the style-sampling skill uses to pull a style template:

1. **Usage.** Agents often run `templates` on its own, `templates pull` without a slug, or `pull` with a slug that isn't one of the five, expecting a list. The first two used to fail on a missing positional. Now `templates` (or `templates list`) prints the five slugs and exits 0. `pull` without a slug, or with an unknown one, exits with a usage error that names them. Error reporting only sees the fixed "Invalid command usage", never the slug the user typed.
2. **The refusal reason is kept.** A refused pull (not signed in, not on Pro, a network failure, a bad archive) printed its reason but called `failCommand()` without it, so error reporting only saw "Command failed". The `PullRefused` / `NetworkFailure` now goes through as the cause, the same way `measure` and `diff` do it. `PullRefused` also sets its `name`, so refusals group apart from crashes.
3. **Windows drive paths.** Unpacking ran `tar -xzf - -C <out>`, and on Windows that tar failed on the drive-letter `-C` directory. tar now runs with `cwd: out` and no `-C`. The target and the checks before unpacking are unchanged.

## Tests

`packages/cli/src/commands/templates.test.ts` (26) and `packages/cli/src/telemetry/events.test.ts` pass, including new cases for:
- the listing (bare and `list`);
- `pull` without a slug, and with an unknown slug;
- an unknown slug reaching failure reporting as "Invalid command usage", with the typed text absent from the message and the stack;
- the refusal arriving as the failure's cause, named `PullRefused`;
- unpacking with `cwd` and no `-C`.

I also smoke-tested the built CLI. `templates` exits 0 and prints the slugs; `templates pull` exits 2 and names them.

Docs: one line in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.

title: test(engine): mask the shutter's sweep in the blur outside check
body:
Fixes #7596

## What

Test-only change, no runtime change. The "outside the trail" check now builds its trail mask from the blur-off shutter samples at `t` as well as the whole neighbour frames.

## Why seed 63098 fails

The failure is in the test's oracle, not in the blur. In seed 63098, `#lt` (a `left`/`top` mover) crosses about 70 px between frame 5 and frame 6. Its path from x 112 to 141 sits behind the static `#fl` panel, so the only place it shows is x 142 to 146, and neither whole frame lands there:

```
row y=130, x 100..199, blur off        R = #lt, B = #fl
t=0.1667  ......RRRRRRBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB.............................
t=0.2000  ............BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBB.....RRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR...
shutter t=0.1903 (blur off, sub-frame)
          ............BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR.....
blur on at t=0.2
          ............BBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBBrrrrrrrrRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRRR
```

`measureOutside` masked only what changed across frames t±2 (dilated by 2 px), so its mask started at x 145. The 240° shutter does sweep `#lt` through x 142 to 146, and blur on correctly draws a faint trail there (`16,19,26` becomes `83,31,39`). That trail landed in the "outside" tiles at x 128 to 143, which gave the reported 2 bad tiles with a worst MAE of 4.0.

Adding the `shutterTimes(t)` samples, which are the same sub-frame poses `measureInside` already averages, to the mask covers exactly what the blur integrates. On hold frames those samples are identical to the reference, so the mask does not change there.

## Verification

Run locally with the CI's pinned `chrome-headless-shell@153.0.8010.36`:

- Before the change: `HF_BLUR_SEEDS=63098` fails with the same tiles and MAE as the nightly report (`[{"x":128,"y":112,"mae":1.77},{"x":128,"y":128,"mae":4.04}]`).
- After the change: `HF_BLUR_SEEDS=63098,62660,1-100` gives 102 of 102 passing.
- `captureMotionBlur.differential`, `.differential.filter` and `.differential.inside` give 100 of 100 passing.
- Sensitivity is unchanged. With #7293 reverted locally (`document.documentElement.append(defs)` changed back to `root.append(defs)`), seeds 1 to 200 still fail exactly the 28 seeds that carry `lastChild`, the same count #7437 reported, and no other seed fails.
- `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit` (engine), `check-comment-citations.mjs` and `comment-ratchet.mjs` all pass.

Seed 62660 (#7486) passes locally both before and after this change, so I'm not claiming it here.

title: fix(core): a system font too large for Chrome to decode is no longer embedded
body:
## What System font capture skips a face larger than 128 MB, the most Chrome decodes as a web font, instead of base64-embedding it into the page. ## Why A composition that names a large system font pays for an embed that Chrome then discards. `font-family: "Apple Color Emoji"` on macOS is the common case: `/System/Library/Fonts/Apple Color Emoji.ttc` is 183 MB. Capture reads the whole file, inlines it as a data URI of about 250 MB and logs "embedding anyway". Chrome rejects it with `OTS parsing error: Web font size more than 128MB` (`kMaxDecompressedSize` in [web_font_decoder.cc](https://source.chromium.org/chromium/chromium/src/+/main:third_party/blink/renderer/platform/fonts/web_font_decoder.cc)) and draws the text from the installed copy, so the frames come out the same as if nothing had been embedded. Measured on a 1 s, 640×360 composition with one line of emoji text, `render -w 1`, M5 Pro, macOS 26.6: | Build | `font-family` | Wall time | Peak RSS | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | 0.9.39 (npx) | `sans-serif` | 5.7 s | 249 MB | | 0.9.39 (npx) | `"Apple Color Emoji"` | 58.0 s | 5.8 GB | | this branch (built from source) | `sans-serif` | 3.0 s | 215 MB | | this branch (built from source) | `"Apple Color Emoji"` | 2.5 s | 217 MB | The MP4 this branch renders is byte-identical to the one 0.9.39 renders. On 0.8.134 the same font crashed a 31 s, 1080×1920 render for us. I have not re-run that project on 0.9.39. ## Related work No issue filed. I searched the tracker for "Apple Color Emoji" and "emoji" and found no report of this. ## How - `CHROME_WEB_FONT_DECODE_LIMIT` (128 MiB) sits next to `SYSTEM_FONT_SIZE_LIMIT`. - Each face is measured before it is read: `stat` for a whole file, the extracted length for a face taken out of a collection. A face over the limit logs a warning and is skipped. The family's other faces still embed. - A family with no face left returns `null`, so it is reported as unresolved like any other family that capture cannot supply. - The per-variant work moved into `systemVariantFaceRule`, which keeps `systemFamilyFaceRules` under the fallow complexity threshold. One behaviour change to judge: in fail-closed mode such a family now throws `Unresolved fonts in fail-closed mode` where it used to ship an embed that could not load. Minimal reproduction (`index.html` plus a local `gsap.min.js`): ```html
😀 ok
``` ## Test plan - [x] Unit tests added/updated - [x] Manual testing performed - [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable) - [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug `deterministicFonts-systemOversize.test.ts` adds three tests: a family with only an oversize face embeds nothing and warns, a mixed family embeds only the face that fits, and a fail-closed render rejects the family. The fixtures are sparse files one byte over the limit, so they take no disk and are never read. With the fix reverted, the vitest worker exits on the first of them. `bun run --filter @hyperframes/core test`: 6161 passed, 2 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are in `systemFontLocator.innerName.test.ts` and fail the same way without this change on this machine. Typecheck, oxlint, oxfmt, `fallow audit --base origin/main` and `comment-ratchet.mjs` pass. No documentation mentions the system font size behaviour, so none is updated. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [Bug]: cancelling a render does not stop HEIC or animated-GIF transcodes
body:
### Describe the bug

Cancelling a render does not stop the compile's HEIC or animated-GIF transcode. Both prep steps call `runFfmpeg` with only a timeout, so the ffmpeg child keeps running after the caller aborts, until the 300 s default expires.

`prepareHeifImageInputs` and `prepareAnimatedGifInputs` never receive `options.abortSignal`, and `compileForRender` does not pass it:

```ts
await runFfmpeg(args, { timeout });                       // heifImagePrep.ts
await runFfmpeg(request.args, { timeout });               // animatedGifPrep.ts
```

`runFfmpeg` already accepts `signal`, so the abort just never reaches the process.

### Expected Behavior

Cancelling a render stops the HEIC/GIF transcode with the rest of the compile and surfaces an abort rather than waiting for the transcode timeout.

### Actual Behavior

A composition with a large HEIC photo or a long animated GIF keeps its ffmpeg transcode running for up to five minutes after the render is cancelled.

### Reproduction

1. A composition with a large HEIC image or a long animated GIF.
2. Start a render, then cancel it while the compile is converting the image.
3. The compile does not return until the transcode times out.

The added test drives the transcode boundary directly: the request carries no `signal`, so an aborted compile cannot stop it.

title: ci: windows jobs update defender signatures before the tests, not in the middle
body:
## What

The Windows render and test jobs in `windows-render.yml` run `Update-MpSignature` right after they turn off Defender's real-time monitoring, in the same step.

## Why

The `windows-latest` image ships Defender signatures several days old. Defender updates them on its own 5.5 to 9.5 minutes into every job. For about 20 seconds its engine takes 8 to 11 CPU-seconds while the machine sits at 80 to 95% CPU, even with real-time monitoring off.

When that lands on a busy moment, tests that start processes stall past their timeouts. In one merge-queue run (44767195766), two separate runners stalled about 10 minutes in:

- `cli/src/tts/pythonIsolation.test.ts` took 63 s against its 20 s limit (740 ms normally);
- Studio's `chromeTestUtils.browser.test.ts` lost its connection to Chrome. Chrome took 5 to 11 s just to start (under 2 s normally), and a 5 s PowerShell version check timed out.

Neither test does anything wrong; the runner stalled under them.

## Related work

Refs #8296 (another Windows stall in this workflow, fixed in its test).

## How

One more line in the existing Defender step of both jobs: the update runs during setup, so the next automatic one is hours away. It takes 15 to 41 s. Excluding the workspace and temp folders from scanning does not help, since the update and its follow-up work are not file scans.

## Test plan

Measured on a throwaway branch (`credlock/probe-windows-stall`) that adds a sampler to every test lane, recording every 3 s: CPU, Defender's process CPU, its real-time state, its signature timestamp, and how long `python3 -c pass` and `powershell -Command 1` take to start.

- fails without the fix: runs 44773164701 and 44780717929. Every lane that ran past 6 minutes shows the burst, and the signature timestamp flips (image's 11/16 to 11/20) within 3 to 16 s of it. A lane with workspace/temp exclusions bursts the same way. Real-time monitoring reads off throughout.
- With the update first, run 44784304133: on all 5 lanes, no burst during the tests. Defender's process uses 0.7 to 2.9 CPU-s across the whole test window, against about 10 s before.
- The tests' own load still slows a single spawn now and then: `powershell -Command 1` peaked at 5.6 s once with the fix. So this removes the big stall, not every slow moment.

Not checked: whether the two named flakes are gone. They are rare, so a few green runs prove little; the burst they line up with is what this removes.

title: fix(skills): place sound effects by their first strong transient, not their peak
body:
## What

`skills/hyperframes/references/sound.md` told agents to place each effect so its **peak** lands one frame after its picture. This changes the moment that is lined up to the effect's **first strong transient**: the first entry in `onsets.events` with a `strength` of 0.5 or more in `npx hyperframes audio <file> --json`. A quieter lead-in before it is trimmed with `data-media-start`. Peak alignment stays only for a riser into impact, which builds into its moment.

## Why

For short hits the peak and the attack coincide, but long effects peak well after they become audible, so lining up the peak plays them early. Measured with `hyperframes audio --json` on Openverse effects used in a real project:

| Effect | First strong transient | `moments.peak` | With the peak lined up |
|---|---|---|---|
| explosion | 0.105 s | 0.639 s | the hit plays 0.53 s early |
| sub drop | 0.035 s | 1.511 s | the bass starts 1.48 s early |
| digital glitch | 0.441 s (soft noise from 0.005 s) | 0.488 s | the lead-in is audible 0.48 s early |
| boom / pop / zap | 0.005 / 0.090 / 0.085 s | 0.031 / 0.099 / 0.094 s | within 0.03 s, fine |

The person watching the render reported the sound as "about a second off" at the explosions. The renderer was not at fault: in the rendered MP4 the flashes land on exact frames (3.200, 23.200 and 27.300 s), and every placed clip sits where its `data-start` says.

## Related work

None found: I searched open and closed PRs and issues for sound, peak and transient. This is a tiny self-contained correction, so there is no separate issue. `docs/packages/cli.mdx` already says a slow sound accents on its steepest rise rather than its peak; this brings the skill in line with it.

## How

One bullet in the Effects section. The existing "one frame after its picture" rule and its reason stay. Only the moment that is lined up changes, and the riser exception is spelled out. It uses fields `audio --json` already reports (`onsets.events[].strength`, `moments.peak`) and the existing `data-media-start` attribute, so there is no new API.

## Test plan

- [ ] Unit tests added/updated: n/a, docs only
- [x] Manual testing performed: re-rendered the project with every effect placed by its first strong transient (and lead-ins trimmed with `data-media-start`), then measured the render. Picture events were found from the per-frame luma change and sound attacks from a 10 ms RMS envelope. All 11 hard hits land between 8 ms early and 22 ms late of their picture; before the change, the explosions led their flashes by about 0.53 s.
- [x] Documentation updated
- [ ] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": n/a, no code comments

I did not run `bun run lint:skills` locally because Bun is not installed on this machine. The change adds no links, relative paths, frontmatter or registry ids. The existing assertion on this file in `scripts/creator-editing-recipes.test.mjs` ("every effect on one lane") is on an untouched line.

title: fix(studio): sealed nudge starts from read-ahead without waiting on overlay rect
body:
## Summary

Arrow-key nudging in an opaque-origin preview previously skipped the overlay's gesture-start read-ahead and asked the frame sequentially (`query`, `describe`, `gesture-start`) on every burst start, adding a 10-16 ms stall and 8 probe mutations before the first draft drew. It also dropped early arrow-key presses while `overlayRect` or `groupOverlayItems` had not yet arrived, even though `acquireCanvasNudgeKeys` had already claimed the arrow keys.

This change:
1. **Starts opaque-origin nudges from `gestureStartReadAhead` synchronously** (`useDomEditNudge.ts`): consumes the overlay's resting read-ahead via `gestureStartReadAhead` + `shownFromRead` (sharing `waitingPressRef` with `useGestureStartReadAhead` in `DomEditOverlay.tsx`), draws the first step immediately with 0 port reads, and falls back to `askShownGestureStarts` on cache miss or after a save invalidates the read-ahead.
2. **Drops the unnecessary `overlayRect` / `groupOverlayItems` gate**: `resolveSingleNudgeTarget` no longer returns `null` while `overlayRect` is `null`, and `resolveGroupNudgeTargets` falls back to `groupSelections` before `groupOverlayItems` arrive. An exhaustive search of `packages/studio/src/` confirmed `originRect` has zero readers anywhere, `applyManualOffsetNudgeDraft` and nudge commit add composition-pixel deltas directly without reading `rect` or `screenToOffset`, and `filterNestedDomEditGroupItems` only inspects `element.contains`.

## No visible change

Only `packages/studio/src/components/editor/useDomEditNudge.ts` (plus unit tests) changed. The overlay appearance and final nudge positions are unchanged; only the pre-draft wait and early-key drop are removed.

## Real-app browser numbers (sealed `origin: "null"` vs unsealed)

Measured in real Studio across headless Firefox, Chrome (with `IsolateSandboxedIframes`), and WebKit, 2 runs of 8 spaced `Shift+ArrowRight` nudges each (16 nudges per browser/mode, `8/8` moved on every run):

| Browser | Mode | Frame `origin` | Before med / max (ms) | Before probe mutations | After med / max (ms) | After probe mutations |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Firefox | sealed | `"null"` | 10 / 30 (r1), 10 / 12 (r2) | 8, 8 | 4 / 6 (r1), 2 / 3 (r2) | 0, 0 |
| Firefox | unsealed | `http://127.0.0.1` | 1 / 3 (r1), 2 / 5 (r2) | 0, 0 | 2 / 3 (r1), 1 / 1 (r2) | 0, 0 |
| Chrome | sealed | `"null"` | 16.1 / 24.9 (r1), 16.5 / 19.3 (r2) | 8, 8 | 1.0 / 3.0 (r1), 1.0 / 3.2 (r2) | 0, 0 |
| Chrome | unsealed | `http://127.0.0.1` | 1.3 / 3.2 (r1), 1.0 / 2.5 (r2) | 0, 0 | 0.9 / 2.3 (r1), 1.1 / 2.6 (r2) | 0, 0 |
| WebKit | sealed | `"null"` | 14 / 22 (r1), 12 / 17 (r2) | 9, 7 | 3 / 6 (r1), 3 / 5 (r2) | 0, 0 |
| WebKit | unsealed | `http://127.0.0.1` | 2 / 4 (r1), 2 / 4 (r2) | 0, 0 | 1 / 4 (r1), 2 / 4 (r2) | 0, 0 |

## Verification

- All 6 new tests failed red before the fix and pass after:
  - `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`: early single nudge while `overlayRect === null`; early group nudge before `groupOverlayItems` arrive.
  - `useDomEditNudge.readAhead.sealed.test.ts`: read-ahead hit with 0 port reads across a multi-key burst; nested GSAP-animated layer read-ahead hit (`plainTranslate: false`); cache-miss fallback with `overlayRect === null`; post-save invalidation falling back to a fresh read (`x=100 -> 110`) and hitting refreshed read-ahead (`x=200 -> 210`) with 0 port reads.
- Focused suite (5 files, 41 tests) passed 3 consecutive runs (exit 0):
  - `src/components/editor/useDomEditNudge.test.tsx` (18)
  - `src/components/editor/useDomEditNudge.sealed.test.tsx` (6)
  - `src/components/editor/useDomEditNudge.readAhead.sealed.test.ts` (4)
  - `src/components/editor/gestureStartReadAhead.sealed.test.ts` (3)
  - `src/hooks/useEditHistoryActions.paint.test.tsx` (10)
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` (0 dead code, 0 complexity, 0 duplication), `comment-ratchet.mjs`, and `check-comment-citations.mjs` all passed.

title: test(studio): the edit bench records a sealed drag's raw pointer steps
body:
## What

The edit-accuracy bench's frame sampler now records the pointer on `pointerrawupdate` as well as on `pointerdown`, `pointermove` and `pointerup`. Bench only: no product code changes.

## Why

Since #8899, a sealed drag posts each step to the preview on `pointerrawupdate`, so the frame can paint it before Studio's own frame. The sampler only recorded the pointer on `pointermove`, which Chrome coalesces into the next frame, after that paint. It then paired a box already drawn at the new step with the pointer's previous position, and the teleport check failed every sealed move with the box "one step ahead of the pointer".

Stock Chrome 158 with the preview in its own process, 4x CPU, 8 `move-idle` cases per run:

| main | sampler | sealed teleport fails | unsealed |
|---|---|---|---|
| with #8899 | `pointermove` only | 8/8 in each of 8 runs | 0/8 |
| just before #8899 | `pointermove` only | 1/8 (a different miss: the box off its path while lagging) | |
| with #8899 | adds `pointerrawupdate` (this PR) | 0/8, 2 runs | 0/8, 2 runs |
| just before #8899 | adds `pointerrawupdate` | 0/8, 2 runs | |

## Related work

Refs #8899

## How

One more event type in the sampler's listener list. Each recorded step keeps the time it happened, so a push painted from a raw step is paired with that step; the coalesced `pointermove` that follows only repeats the position.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/teleport.test.mjs` ("pairs a push with the raw step the preview drew, before that step's pointermove") fails on main (`expected [ [ 25, 150, 110 ] ] to deeply equal [ [ 25, 160, 110 ] ]`) and passes with the fix, 3 runs in a row.
- Ran green: every test file in `packages/studio/tests/e2e/edit-accuracy` (13 files, 139 tests).

title: fix(studio): move crop frame and rotate handle with the selection box
body:
## What

Every remaining piece of a selection's chrome now moves in the same DOM write as the selection box and handles during a drag or resize, and tap/cancel restores reset the full outline and turn centre synchronously:

- The crop frame (`[data-dom-edit-crop-frame]`, dashed border and edge crop handles) now moves with the selection box in the move event. Before, it waited for React's next commit and split away as a trailing dashed ghost outline during drags (especially visible on turned layers).
- The rotate handle now lives inside the handles wrapper (`[data-dom-edit-selection-handles]`) positioned with CSS `calc()`, so a drag or resize writing the wrapper's rect carries it in the same frame instead of waiting for React.
- Every single-selection draft rect update (drag move, resize move, drag tap, resize tap, drag release, and gesture cancel) now routes through one owner (`setDraftOverlayRect` -> `drawSelectionOutline`), fixing tap and cancel branches that previously left `transform-origin` (and `left`/`top` on a resize tap) stale when a small move and release landed in one React batch.
- Adds unit coverage for the resize turn-centre write and the group waiting-press guard.

## Why

After #8909 and #8921 made the selection box, corner handles, and rotation container's `transform-origin` follow the move's own DOM write, three pieces still lagged or drifted:

- `DomEditCropHandles` renders `[data-dom-edit-crop-frame]` outside `[data-dom-edit-chrome]` (so a turned element's angle is not applied twice), and nothing updated its `left`/`top` until React rendered `overlayRect`.
- `DomEditRotateHandle` was rendered outside `[data-dom-edit-selection-handles]` using pixel positions derived from React's `overlayRect`.
- Tap and cancel paths restored `drawOutline` directly (or called `restoreGestureOverlayRect` without a DOM write), skipping `transform-origin` and (on resize tap) `left`/`top`.

## How

- `domEditOverlayGestures.ts`: replaces separate `drawOutline` + `drawChromeOrigin` exports with one `drawSelectionOutline(box, handles, rect)` that writes the box and handles wrapper rects, updates `[data-dom-edit-chrome]` `transform-origin`, and repositions the sibling `[data-dom-edit-crop-frame]` centered on `rect` (using its inline `style.width`/`style.height` with zero layout reads).
- `useDomEditOverlayGestures.ts`: `setDraftOverlayRect` calls `drawSelectionOutline` after its waiting-press guard (matching `setDraftGroupOverlayItems`), removing six duplicate call sites and ensuring drag/resize tap and `clearPointerState` cancel restore the full outline and turn centre synchronously.
- `resizeHandleLayout.ts`, `DomEditRotateHandle.tsx`, `DomEditSelectionChrome.tsx`: `rotateHandleLayout(cropInset)` positions the rotate chip with CSS `calc()` relative to the handles wrapper (`left: calc(inset.left + max(0px, 100% - (inset.left + inset.right)) / 2)`, `top: calc(100% - inset.bottom + 12px)`), and `DomEditSelectionChrome` renders `DomEditRotateHandle` inside `DomEditResizeHandles`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

fails without the fix:
- `selectionHandlesRideTheBox.test.ts` "a drag move places the crop frame in the same write as the box" fails (`expected [ '20px', '30px' ] to deeply equal [ '50px', '42px' ]`).
- `selectionHandlesRideTheBox.test.ts` "a drag tap restores the box, handles and turn centre without waiting for React" fails (`transformOrigin` stays `'142px 111px'` instead of `'140px 110px'`).
- `selectionHandlesRideTheBox.test.ts` "a resize tap restores the box, handles and turn centre without waiting for React" fails (`expected [ '17.846372px', '29.230915px', '240px', '160px' ] to deeply equal [ '20px', '30px', '240px', '160px' ]`).
- `selectionHandlesRideTheBox.test.ts` "cancelling a drag restores the box, handles and turn centre without waiting for React" fails (`expected [ '50px', '42px', '', '' ] to deeply equal [ '20px', '30px', '240px', '160px' ]`).
- `DomEditSelectionChrome.test.tsx` "places the rotate handle inside the handles wrapper so it rides the box's write" fails (`expected null not to be null`).
- Mutation checks proved the resize turn-centre test (dropping `transformOrigin` write -> `expected NaN to be close to 98.554944`), the group waiting-press test (moving `drawGroupOutline` above the waiting-press return -> `expected [ '40px', '32px', '40px', '30px' ] to deeply equal [ '', '', '', '' ]`), and the real-Chrome rotate handle layout test (`+12px` -> `+20px` -> `rotate y 4x4: expected 24 to be close to 16`) all go red when their code is broken.

Three consecutive runs of the touched test files (`selectionHandlesRideTheBox.test.ts`, `DomEditSelectionChrome.test.tsx`, `resizeHandleLayout.browser.test.ts` in real Chrome): 29/29 passed each run. `resizeHandleLayout.browser.test.ts` verifies both corner resize handles and `rotateHandleLayout` in real Chrome across 4x4, 14x8, 24x40, cropped 40x40, over-cropped 10x10, and 240x160 boxes against the previous pixel formulas. `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and `fallow` are clean.

Real Studio board on a 20° turned croppable layer dragged right and left (stock Chrome, 60 fps screen capture, 3 isolated and 3 open sessions interleaved per build; isolated preview `origin` verified `null` in every session). Table shows outline minus layer offset in pointer steps averaged over each drag (0 = outline locked to layer):

| Preview | `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| open (`d0` mean / `d0` off-frames) | `0.03 / 0.03 / 0.05` (1-2/39 off; 6/32 off on `d1`) | `0.0 / 0.0 / 0.0` (0/39 off on `d0`; 1/27 on `d1`) |
| isolated (`origin: null`, `oopifs: 1`) | `0.69 / 0.72 / 0.71` (floating dashed crop border + lagging rotate chip; 10 px spikes) | `0.65 / 0.67 / 0.67` (crop border and rotate chip fused with solid box; zero 10 px spikes) |

The remaining ~0.65-step offset on an isolated preview is the separate out-of-process iframe advancing ahead of Studio's `BeginMainFrame` via raw pointer updates (#8912); Studio's own outline renders in its very first frame (`BeginMainFrame` ~1.9 ms median, 0 dropped frames).

Not run: Firefox, WebKit, or resize-tap visual capture (covered by unit tests and real-Chrome layout test).

title: fix(producer): materialize runtime blob and inline data audio during probe
body:
## What changed

Compositions whose scripts synthesize or load audio into browser `blob:` URLs (via `URL.createObjectURL`) or embed inline `data:` audio URIs play in preview, but failed during render because `audioMixer` only reads local files and `http(s)` URLs and tried to resolve `blob:` / `data:` strings as paths inside the project folder.

- Added `packages/producer/src/services/render/stages/runtimeAudio.ts` to materialize same-origin `blob:` audio URLs from the live probe page and inline `data:` audio URIs into `compiled/__hf_runtime_audio/<sha256>.<ext>` (inside `compiledDir`, so both local and distributed renders read and clean them up through existing asset roots).
- Enforced strict same-origin checking for `blob:` URLs, per-clip (64 MiB) and total (128 MiB) byte caps, strict base64/data-URI validation, and content-hash deduplication. Failed, cross-origin, empty, or oversized sources log a warning and stay unchanged so audio mixing fails closed rather than silently dropping tracks.
- Updated `hasRuntimeMediaChanges` in `packages/producer/src/services/render/stages/probeStage.ts` to probe pages that both contain media elements and call `createObjectURL(`, even when the element is populated through a helper function whose selector cannot be resolved statically.
- Wired `materializeBlobAudioSources` (while the probe page is live) and `materializeDataAudioSources` (for both static and probed renders, ahead of `dropMediaOutsideProject` and `preflightCompositionAssetMediaTypes`) in `probeStage.ts`.

## Verification

- `fails without the fix:`
  - `packages/producer/src/services/render/stages/probeStage.test.ts`:
    - `probes when a script calls createObjectURL on a page with media elements`
    - `materializes same-origin blob audio from the probe page into compiledDir and deduplicates shared blobs`
    - `materializes inline data: audio even when no browser probe runs`
  - All three failed on `origin/main` before the fix and pass 3/3 runs with the fix.
- `packages/producer/src/services/render/stages/runtimeAudio.test.ts`: unit tests covering same-origin vs cross-origin `blob:` handling, MIME extension mapping, byte limits, revoked blobs, base64 and percent-encoded `data:` URIs, deduplication, and invalid input refusal (3/3 runs pass under `--preload ./scripts/no-network.mjs`).
- `packages/producer/src/services/render/stages/runtimeAudio.integration.test.ts` (registered in `packages/producer/scripts/integration-tests.json`): end-to-end test proving a real PCM WAV `data:` URI materializes into `compiled/__hf_runtime_audio/`, passes `dropMediaOutsideProject` and FFprobe `preflightCompositionAssetMediaTypes`, and mixes into a real `audio.m4a` via `runAudioStage` with FFmpeg (3/3 runs pass).

title: feat(runtime): expose frame-presented request and preview health metrics
body:
## Summary

Expose frame-presentation timing and playback-health metrics from inside the preview runtime so Studio and host applications receive identical readings regardless of frame origin:

1. **`frame-presented` editing request (`packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.ts`, `editingAgent.ts`, `packages/studio/src/player/lib/frameFacts.ts`)**:
   - Adds a read-only `frame-presented` request that waits for any seeking `<video>` elements inside the preview document to settle and then awaits two `requestAnimationFrame` ticks before returning `{ presented: true }`.
   - Video waits settle on `seeked`, `error`, `abort`, `emptied`, DOM disconnection (via `MutationObserver`), and agent `dispose()`, removing all listeners and observers on settlement so no listeners leak.
   - Leaves `wait-for-seek` unchanged for existing callers.
2. **Audio step p90, missed-frame counts, and motion blur summary in `preview-health` (`packages/core/src/runtime/playbackHealth.ts`, `init.ts`, `types.ts`)**:
   - Accepts the active playing, unmuted `<audio>` element from `mediaClipsInWindow` (zero per-frame DOM queries) and computes `mediaStepP90Ms` (positive steps under 500 ms over the 3 s window) alongside `over16` (gaps > 25 ms) and `over33` (gaps > 41.7 ms).
   - Reads `motionBlur` (`attr`, `shutter`, `state`, `tier`, `movers`) via `readMotionBlurSummary` only when emitting the 1 s health report (zero per-frame work).
3. **Frame shape counts in `preview-facts` (`packages/core/src/runtime/playbackHealth.ts`, `init.ts`, `types.ts`)**:
   - Adds optional `frameShape` (`canvas`, `svg`, `filter`, `tweens`) to `preview-facts`, read only on demand when `request-preview-facts` is handled (zero per-frame work).
4. **Validated Studio parsers (`packages/studio/src/player/store/previewQualitySlice.ts`)**:
   - Validates, bounds, and allowlists every new optional field in `parsePlaybackHealth` and `parsePreviewFacts`, dropping out-of-range numbers, non-finite values, oversized strings, and unknown enum values.

## Testing

- fails without the fix: `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.test.ts` (`frame-presented` suite failed with `unknown-kind`), `packages/core/src/runtime/playbackHealth.test.ts` (`emits audio step p90, missed-frame counts, and reads motionBlur only on the 1 s emit` failed with `expected undefined to be 25`), and `packages/studio/src/player/store/previewQualitySlice.test.ts` (`validates, bounds, and allowlists ...` and `validates and bounds frameShape ...` failed with `undefined`).
- Red-first unit tests verified failing before the implementation, then passing 3 consecutive runs after:
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.test.ts` (195 tests) and `editingPort.test.ts` (13 tests): verifies `frame-presented` waits for `seeked` + two animation frames, settles on `error`/`abort`/`emptied`/DOM disconnect, and removes listeners cleanly.
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/playbackHealth.test.ts` (16 tests): verifies `mediaStepP90Ms`, `over16`, `over33`, `readMotionBlurSummary` (invoked only on health emits, never per frame), and `readPreviewFrameShape`.
  - `packages/studio/src/player/store/previewQualitySlice.test.ts` (8 tests): verifies valid, nullable, and rejected/out-of-bounds payloads for `mediaStepP90Ms`, `over16`, `over33`, `motionBlur`, and `frameShape`.
- Package verification:
  - `packages/core`: `build`, `typecheck` (including `typecheck:runtime`), `lint:runtime-preview-guards`, runtime contract/behavior/seek checks, and full vitest suite (354/354 files passed).
  - `packages/studio`: `typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt`, and full unit vitest suite (851/851 passed, 1 skipped).
  - `packages/engine`: `typecheck` passed; vitest 217/222 passed (5 local MPEG-TS tests failed with `SIGSEGV` in the local static FFmpeg binary; CI verifies full engine suite).
  - `packages/producer`: `typecheck` passed; unit vitest 123/124 passed (same local MPEG-TS static FFmpeg `SIGSEGV`) and bun unit lane 54/55 passed (`videoAudioProbe.test.ts` remote-probe download path deferred to CI).

## No visible change

Pure runtime editing-port, playback-health reporting, and Studio store parser changes (`.ts` only, no UI, CSS, or DOM rendering changes).

title: feat(studio): handle canvas Delete and arrow-key nudge in opaque preview runtime
body:
## Summary

In opaque-origin previews (`origin: "null"`), canvas Delete and arrow-key nudge previously routed from Studio's parent window over the `MessagePort` to the preview frame, adding cross-frame latency before the first frame painted in Firefox and WebKit.

This PR moves canvas-selected Delete and arrow-key nudge into the preview runtime while keeping Studio as the single owner of persistence, undo history, rollback, and timeline-focused shortcuts:

1. **Focus ownership (canvas-selected vs timeline-focused)**:
   - `sealedFrameKeyboard.ts` adds a dedicated canvas focus hold (`holdSealedCanvasKeyboard` / `hasSealedCanvasKeyboardHold`) alongside the inline-text hold.
   - Clicking/selecting on the canvas overlay (`useSealedCanvasKeys.ts`, wired in `DomEditOverlay.tsx`) acquires the canvas hold and focuses the preview iframe so trusted key events arrive directly in the frame.
   - Clicking or focusing the timeline (`[data-studio-timeline]`), inspector, dialogs, or inputs releases the hold and disarms the runtime. **Canvas-selected Delete and nudge run in-frame; timeline-focused Delete keeps Studio's existing path unchanged.**
2. **Capture-first runtime listener with inline-text carve-out**:
   - `packages/core/src/runtime/editing/canvasKeys.ts` installs capture-phase `window` listeners (`keydown`, `keyup`, `keypress`, `beforeinput`, `input`) during top-level evaluation of `entry.ts` (before any composition scripts run), using native references captured at evaluation time.
   - Only `isTrusted` events are handled or forwarded; synthetic/untrusted events are ignored.
   - Active Studio-opened inline text edits (`isActiveTextEditTarget` in `textEdit.ts`) are carved out so typing, caret movement, Enter, and Escape continue to work normally. Outside active Studio text edits, `stopImmediatePropagation` prevents composition listeners from seeing Studio keystrokes.
3. **Studio shortcut forwarding**:
   - Any trusted key not handled locally as an armed Delete or arrow-key nudge is forwarded over the `MessagePort` (`onKey`), with `preventDefault` scoped to Studio's configured shortcut map (`getStudioKeys()` + `Escape`) so browser shortcuts (`Cmd+R`, `Cmd+W`, `Cmd+T`, `Cmd+L`) stay intact.
   - Studio dispatches forwarded keys onto the canvas overlay only while it holds an active canvas keyboard session on the current iframe load.
4. **Studio-owned commit/rollback and active-handle scoping**:
   - Studio arms only the active selection's handles via `arm-canvas-keys` (automatically disarmed when selection clears, read-only, playback starts, inline text edit opens, or keyframes/automation range are selected).
   - **Delete**: runtime validates non-root removable nodes, detaches the armed outermost elements immediately in the same frame (storing parent/sibling/index restore anchors under `actionId`), clears `deleteHandles` so a rapid second Delete cannot double-fire, and posts `canvas-key-action`. Studio runs its existing delete persistence path (skipping redundant `remove-elements` RPCs via `noteFrameRemovedHandles`), then sends `resolve-canvas-key-action` (`commit` or `rollback` to restore detached elements in their original DOM order).
   - **Arrow-key nudge**: runtime accumulates `totalDx`/`totalDy` synchronously across rapid key-repeat presses, draws immediately via `editingDraft.ts` (`drawDrafts`, supporting both CSS `translate` and GSAP position routes via `gsapPosition`), and posts `canvas-key-action`. Studio joins/opens `useDomEditNudge`'s debounced commit session (recording the runtime-drawn draft via `noteFrameDrawnDraft` so zero redundant `draft` RPCs are echoed) and owns debounce, save, history, and rollback.
5. **Not-in-render guard**:
   - `installPreviewKeyShield` runs only when `markedForStudio(document) && !capturePageIn(document) && window.parent !== window` and never in export/render mode (`__HF_EXPORT_RENDER_SEEK_CONFIG`), standalone builds, capture frames, or third-party embeds.

## Before

Selected canvas element in an opaque-origin preview before pressing 4x `Shift+ArrowRight`:

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/71332e4d-5a50-49e4-a761-7f1b88f7b19e)

## After

Same element after 4x `Shift+ArrowRight` (`+40 px`, drawn immediately in-frame with selection chrome synced and 0 composition key events seen):

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fe0a8027-5519-4063-be96-6a3ac533435f)

## Real-app browser verification (sealed `origin: "null"`)

Verified in real Studio across headless Firefox 161, Chrome 155 (`IsolateSandboxedIframes`), and WebKit with composition capture-phase `keydown` listeners installed on both `window` and `document`:

| Browser | Frame `origin` | Focus owner | 4x `Shift+ArrowRight` delta | `Space` forwarded | `Delete` immediate + persisted | Composition listeners heard |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Firefox 161 | `"null"` | `<hyperframes-player>` -> `<iframe>` | `+40 px` (`549.93 -> 589.93`) | `2/2` | `true` / `true` | `0` (`[]`) |
| Chrome 155 (isolated) | `"null"` | `<hyperframes-player>` -> `<iframe>` | `+40 px` (`549.93 -> 589.93`) | `2/2` | `true` / `true` | `0` (`[]`) |
| WebKit | `"null"` | `<hyperframes-player>` -> `<iframe>` | `+40 px` (`549.93 -> 589.93`) | `2/2` | `true` / `true` | `0` (`[]`) |

## Verification

- Core runtime & protocol suites (4 files, 272 tests, 3 consecutive runs, exit 0):
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/editing/canvasKeys.test.ts` (5: capture-first shield + untrusted ignored + film input blocked, rapid repeat Arrow nudges across translate & GSAP, rapid second Delete while `actionId` is in-flight + rollback DOM order restore, inline-text carve-out + Studio shortcut forwarding + browser shortcut passthrough, not-in-render/capture/unmarked guard)
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.test.ts` (190)
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.test.ts` (13)
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/entry.test.ts` (64)
- Studio suites (8 files, 101 tests, 3 consecutive runs, exit 0):
  - `packages/studio/src/components/editor/useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` (4: canvas vs timeline focus ownership, in-frame Delete + persist rollback restore, rapid repeat Arrow nudges with single debounced commit & zero redundant draft echo, forwarded shortcuts gated on canvas hold + keyframe selection disarming Delete)
  - `useDomEditNudge.test.tsx`, `useDomEditNudge.sealed.test.tsx`, `sealedFrameKeyboard.test.ts`, `useAppHotkeys.previewForwarding.test.tsx`, `useTimelineDeleteOps.test.tsx`, `useElementLifecycleOps.multiDelete.test.tsx`, `usePlaybackKeyboard.test.ts`
- Render/export suites:
  - `packages/engine`: 217/223 files (3767 tests) passed, including all browser render & motion-blur tests (the 5 failed files are pre-existing FFmpeg 7.0.2 static binary SIGSEGVs on local MPEG-TS fixtures).
  - `packages/producer`: 123/124 vitest unit files (1632 tests, 1 same local FFmpeg MPEG-TS SIGSEGV) + all bun unit tests passed.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint` (0 warnings, 0 errors), `tsc --noEmit` (`core`, `core:runtime`, `studio`), `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` (0 dead code, 0 complexity), `comment-ratchet.mjs`, `check-comment-citations.mjs`, and `filesize` (`DomEditOverlay.tsx` = 596 lines <= 600) passed.

title: fix(core): guard runtime init and paused video observer when document.body is null
body:
## Summary

When the injected runtime starts on a document whose `document.body` is `null` (for example a composition whose markup or script removed or has not yet attached `<body>`), `initSandboxRuntimeModular()` threw `TypeError: Failed to execute 'observe' on 'MutationObserver': parameter 1 is not of type 'Node'` inside `createPausedVideoFrames()` and would then dereference `document.body` again in `initVfx()` and `collectRuntimeTimelinePayload()`.

Every sibling observer in `packages/core/src/runtime/` already observes `document.documentElement` or guards `document.body`.

## Changes

- `packages/core/src/runtime/pausedVideoFrames.ts`: fall back from `document.body` to `document.documentElement` (and guard when neither exists) before calling `observer.observe(...)`, and fall back from `document.head` to `document.documentElement` when appending the hiding `<style>` element.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/vfx.ts`: accept `HTMLElement | null` in `initVfx` and `rebuildLostVfx`, returning cleanly when `root` is `null`.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/init.ts`: pass `document.body ?? document.documentElement` to `initVfx` and `rebuildLostVfx`, guard `document.body.style` dimension mirroring, and guard `document.body` when counting mounted elements.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/timeline.ts`: fall back from `root ?? document.body` to `document.documentElement` (and guard when `null`) before calling `parseElementDurationAttr`.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/afterFonts.ts`: fall back from `document.body` to `document.documentElement` before appending the deferred-module sentinel script.

## Verification

- `fails without the fix:`
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/pausedVideoFrames.test.ts` (`starts without throwing when document.body is null and still watches documentElement`, `falls back to documentElement when document.head is null on present`)
  - `packages/core/src/runtime/init.nullBody.test.ts` (`initializes and tears down cleanly when document.body is null`)
- Ran `pausedVideoFrames.test.ts` and `init.nullBody.test.ts` 3 times in a row, plus sibling runtime tests (`vfx.test.ts`, `pausedVideoCallbacks.test.ts`, `adapters/video-texture-compat.paused.test.ts`, `init.startsOnce.test.ts`, `entry.test.ts`, `entry.afterFonts.test.ts`), `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `fallow audit`.
