title: feat(parsers): narration.json model and caption-array reader
body:
Part 1 of 4 for linked narration (#6708), split as suggested there. This one adds code nothing uses yet; parts 2 to 4 build on it.

## What

Two new subpaths in `@hyperframes/parsers`:

- `@hyperframes/parsers/narration` reads, checks and writes `narration.json`, the script of a narrated project: each line's text, voice and audio file, and what it was last voiced from (`voiced`: hashes of the text, the voice settings and the WAV). Keys it doesn't know are kept on rewrite. `narrationTimingsOf()` reads each line's length and word timings from media-use's `audio_meta.json`.
- `@hyperframes/parsers/caption-array` finds `const`/`let`/`var` `script` and `TRANSCRIPT` caption arrays in HTML, reads their words (with an optional `line` tag), and splices or shifts words while every other element stays byte-identical.

No behaviour change.

## Why

#6708: a voice-over and its captions are made once and then drift apart. Lint (part 2) and the CLI (parts 3 and 4) need one shared reading of the script and of the caption arrays, and lint depends only on parsers, so the shared code lives here.

## narration.json and audio_meta.json

You asked which file is the source of truth, and whether one file could do both jobs. My proposal is two files, one job each:

- **`audio_meta.json` stays the record of what was generated.** media-use writes it; it already keys voices by line id with `path`, `duration_s` and `words`. Nothing about it changes. In part 4, `narration set` updates the re-voiced line's entry by id (the same merge-by-id #6816 adds for partial `--only tts` runs).
- **`narration.json` is the script: what each line should be.** Its text, voice, audio file, the caption array that shows it, and what it was last voiced from. It never copies lengths or word timings; those are read from `audio_meta.json` by line id. Without `audio_meta.json` (a project voiced some other way), lint still checks text, audio and links, and only asks that a line's captions fall inside its clip.

Why not one file:

- `audio_meta.json` is the engine's output. It also holds music, effects and credits, and a run without `--only` replaces the whole voice list, so a script written by hand into it would be lost on the next full run.
- Lint would have to treat an engine output as the user's input, and every media-use format change would become a narration format change.

If you'd rather have one file, the per-line fields (`text`, `voice`, `voiced`) could move into `audio_meta.json`'s voices. Only the reader here and the writers in parts 3 and 4 would change, so it's cheap to switch now, before anything depends on it.

## Related work

Refs #6708. #7861 asks for narration anchors that fail the build when a script edit removes a word; that would build on these line ids. #6816 (merge voices by id on `--only tts`) is separate and independent.

The series: #8938 (this one) → #8939 (lint rules) → #8940 (`narration list` / `init` / `check`) → #8941 (`narration set`).

## How

- `narration.ts`: the model, `parseNarrationManifest` (every problem listed, not just the first), `serializeNarrationManifest` (two-space JSON, key order kept), the voice key `provider:voice:speed:lang`, whitespace-normalised text for hashing, and comparable words for caption checks. Line ids are plain names, since they appear in attributes and caption tags.
- `captionArray.ts`: uses acorn, the same way the CLI's `findCaptionArray` does, but handles `let`/`var` and both array names, and edits by source span so untouched words keep their exact text.
- Two subpaths in `package.json`, `package-subpaths.json` and `tsup.config.ts`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `narration.test.ts` (round trip with unknown keys kept, every problem named, invalid JSON, `audio_meta.json` timings by id with bad entries skipped, voice key, text helpers) and `captionArray.test.ts` (const/let/var, `script` and `TRANSCRIPT`, words with and without `line`, splice and shift leave other elements byte-identical).
- [x] `bun run --filter @hyperframes/parsers test`: 66 files, 1,667 tests pass. `bun run check:package-subpaths` and `node scripts/check-test-reachability.mjs` pass.
- [x] Manual testing: the whole series was run end to end with real Kokoro voices and whisper captions (see part 4).
- [ ] Documentation updated: nothing user-facing yet; parts 2 and 3 add the docs.
- [x] Comments say why, not what.

title: feat(lint): detect narration drift against narration.json
body:
Part 2 of 4 for linked narration (#6708). **Builds on #8938**: until that merges, this PR also shows its commit. Only the last commit (`feat(lint): …`) is new here.

## What

When a project has a `narration.json`, `hyperframes lint` (and `check`) now warns about drift between the script, the audio and the captions:

| Code | Severity | When |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `narration_manifest_invalid` | warning | `narration.json` isn't valid |
| `narration_line_unlinked` | warning | a line has no `<audio data-narration-line>` clip, or more than one; or a clip names an unknown line |
| `narration_audio_stale` | warning | the line's text, voice settings or WAV changed since it was voiced, or the WAV is missing |
| `narration_clip_timing_mismatch` | warning | the clip plays more than 0.05 s longer or shorter than `audio_meta.json` says the voice lasts |
| `narration_captions_out_of_sync` | warning | the caption words showing a line differ in number from the voice's words, or one starts more than 0.1 s off |
| `narration_transcript_mismatch` | info | captions in sync but reading differently from the script (often "47" for "forty-seven") |

No `narration.json`, no findings. Everything is a warning or info, so drift never blocks a render. This part is read-only.

## Why

It's useful on its own: an agent or a person editing a narrated project learns that a line's voice no longer says its text, or that captions slipped, before rendering.

## Related work

Refs #6708. Follows #8938; next are `narration list` / `init` / `check` and `narration set`.

## How

- `packages/lint/src/projectNarration.ts` takes the main timeline's audio clips and the caption array's words in global time. `project.ts` adds `data-narration-line` to the audio spans it already collects, and records each mounted file's origin, so captions in a nested scene are placed at the scene's start.
- A line's caption words are the ones tagged `"line": "<id>"`, or else the untagged words inside its clip's time window, so captions made before this existed still work.
- Lengths and word timings come from `audio_meta.json` by line id (see #8938 for why they aren't copied into `narration.json`), and only when its entry describes the line's own audio file. Without it, the length isn't checked, and a tagged caption word only has to start inside its clip.
- Fix hints point at what exists today (re-voicing with media-use). Parts 3 and 4 switch them to the new commands.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `projectNarration.test.ts`, 13 cases on real projects through `lintProject`. No manifest; in sync; invalid manifest; text, voice and WAV changes; missing WAV; unlinked lines and clips; length within and past 0.05 s; shifted and missing caption words; no `audio_meta.json`; an `audio_meta.json` entry for another file; untagged words; captions in a mounted scene; transcript mismatch as info.
- [x] `bun run --filter @hyperframes/lint test`: 33 files, 1,379 tests pass.
- [x] Documentation updated: a "Narration" section in `docs/reference/lint-rules.mdx`.
- [x] Comments say why, not what.

title: feat(cli): hyperframes narration list, init and check
body:
Part 3 of 4 for linked narration (#6708). **Builds on #8938 and #8939**: until they merge, this PR also shows their commits. Only the last commit (`feat(cli): hyperframes narration list, init and check`) is new here.

## What

A `narration` command with three subcommands:

- `hyperframes narration init`: writes `narration.json` for a project voiced before it existed. It reads media-use's `audio_meta.json` and `audio_request.json` (the text comes from the request), or else clips already tagged `data-narration-line` and the caption words inside them. It tags each line's clip, all as one `history` entry. `--force` replaces an existing file.
- `hyperframes narration list`: each line, its length (from `audio_meta.json`) and its findings, or "in sync".
- `hyperframes narration check`: the narration findings from lint; exits 1 while any warning remains.

All take `--dir` and `--json`. A refusal (no `narration.json`, nothing to adopt, a file already there) exits 2 with its message.

## Why

Lint (#8939) needs a `narration.json` to compare against, and nobody should have to write one by hand for a project media-use already voiced.

## Related work

Refs #6708. Follows #8938 and #8939. Next is `narration set`.

## How

- `packages/cli/src/commands/narration.ts`: citty subcommands with lazy imports, like `timeline`. Printed text goes through `terminalLines`, and JSON answers the same with `--json` before or after the subcommand (`cli.jsonFlag.test.ts` lists the new leaves).
- `narration/init.ts` writes the script only. Lengths and word timings stay in `audio_meta.json`. Clip tagging goes through `applyFileMutations` with `expectedVersion`, and `narration/history.ts` files it as one history entry (or joins a turn that's already open).
- `narration/status.ts` runs the same `lintProject` pass and groups findings by line.
- Lint's `narration_manifest_invalid` hint now mentions `narration init`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `narration/init.test.ts`. Adopt a media-use project (text from the request, clips tagged, no timings copied, lint clean); refuse to replace unless `--force`; adopt tagged clips with no media-use; refuse a project with nothing to adopt; `list` with and without `audio_meta.json`; `check` exit codes 0, 1 and 2 through the command.
- [x] `bun run --filter @hyperframes/cli test`: the narration tests, `cli.jsonFlag.test.ts` and `printedFailureText.wiring.test.ts` pass. 5 other files fail on my Mac for local reasons (Homebrew whisper, the local ffmpeg build, macOS file-name normalisation, a file-watcher timing test); none of them touch narration.
- [x] `node scripts/check-docs-cli-commands.mjs` passes.
- [x] Documentation updated: a `narration` section in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`.
- [x] Comments say why, not what.

title: feat(cli): narration set re-voices one line
body:
Part 4 of 4 for linked narration (#6708). **Builds on #8938, #8939 and #8940**: until they merge, this PR also shows their commits. Only the last commit (`feat(cli): narration set re-voices one line`) is new here.

## What

`hyperframes narration set <id> [text]` re-voices one line and updates everything that depends on it, together, as one `history` entry:

- the clip's `src` and `data-duration`
- that line's caption words (tagged with the line), re-timed from the new take
- `caption-overrides.json`: indices after the line move; the line's own overrides stay only if its word count is unchanged
- `narration.json`: the text, voice and `voiced` record
- the line's voice in `audio_meta.json` (path, length, words), with `total_duration_s` summed again

Flags: `--voice`, `--speed`, `--dry-run`, `--no-retime`, `--force`, `--who`, `--dir`, `--json`.

## Why

#6708: editing one line should re-voice that line and keep its captions and timing in step, without regenerating the whole voice-over.

## Voices that don't repeat

`set` re-voices one line on its own, so the new take has to sound like the lines around it. That holds for a local voice: Kokoro gives the same audio for the same text and settings. A service whose voices may vary between calls could make an edited line sound different from its neighbours, so `set` refuses any provider other than Kokoro and says why:

```
narration set re-voices one line with Kokoro only, a local voice that sounds the same each time, so the line matches its neighbours. heygen voices may not repeat; re-voice every line with media-use (--only tts) instead
```

If a provider can promise repeatable output later (a fixed seed, say), it could be allowed by name.

## Related work

Refs #6708. Completes the series: #8938, #8939, #8940, then this.

## How

- The take is voiced (`synthesize`) and transcribed (`runTranscribe`) in a scratch folder outside the project. Transcribing inside the project would rewrite every caption array in it. A take with no words heard is refused.
- `narration/planSet.ts` plans every change without writing. The apply step copies the WAV to `assets/voice/<id>-<hash8>.wav`, then calls `applyFileMutations` with each file's version from before the slow voicing step, so a file edited in the meantime refuses the write ("changed while the line was re-voiced; run the command again"). The old WAV is kept, so `history undo` never points a clip at a missing file.
- A longer take that would run into the next narration clip on the same track is refused, unless `--no-retime`. Moving later clips is left out of this PR.
- `audio_meta.json` is updated only if the project has one, written as media-use writes it (two-space JSON). Other fields of the voice entry, and the rest of the file, are kept.
- Lint's fix hints now name `narration set`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `narration/set.test.ts`, with `synthesize` and `runTranscribe` mocked as in `tts.test.ts`. It covers:
  - only line l2's clip, caption words, later override indices, manifest entry and `audio_meta.json` voice change, and lint is clean afterwards
  - voicing and transcribing happen outside the project; an unchanged line is left alone; a dry run writes nothing
  - overlap refused or kept with `--no-retime`; a file changed mid-run refuses the write and leaves no WAV
  - overrides kept on an equal word count; one history entry, undone in one step (`audio_meta.json` included)
  - a non-Kokoro provider refused; no `audio_meta.json`; the command line with `--json`
- [x] Manual testing, with real Kokoro (`af_heart`) and whisper (`small.en`) on a 3-line project made the way media-use leaves one:
  1. `narration init`, then `check`: in sync.
  2. Edit l2's text in `narration.json`, then `check`: `narration_audio_stale` plus a transcript info.
  3. `set l2 --dry-run`, then `set l2`: 1.707 s, 5 words; files `index.html`, `audio_meta.json`, `narration.json`.
  4. `check` and `lint`: 0 narration findings. A take that runs into l3 is refused.
  5. `history undo` restores every file, `audio_meta.json` included.
- [x] Documentation updated: `set` in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`, and the lint fix hints.
- [x] Comments say why, not what.

title: fix(share): keep source sync destinations in local configuration
body:
## What changed

Studio and the CLI remember a folder’s source sync destination in local configuration. A copied folder starts a new cloud composition on its first sync, including when it replaces a folder at a previously used path. The first upload waits for the service to confirm creation.

After moving a folder or upgrading from a release that stored the binding in the project, choose **Reconnect a moved or upgraded project** in Studio or run `hyperframes share --reconnect` before the first sync. Select the existing cloud project and confirm its name and workspace. Reconnecting saves the destination locally. When the local files differ from the published snapshot, a second confirmation explains that the next sync can undo cloud edits. Canceling leaves the folder disconnected. Approval applies only to the local files and published snapshot that were compared.

## Package size

The share package ships the reconnect implementation, signed-in project lookup and TypeScript declarations. The size budget now reflects the measured release tarball (165,237 bytes packed and 634,432 unpacked). The package contains no tests or source maps. The existing 1% CI tolerance still applies.

## Verification

All 203 share tests, 132 focused CLI and local server tests, and 59 Studio tests passed. The divergent-folder regression test failed on the preceding implementation and passed after the fix. It covers cancellation without saving a binding, local and cloud changes between confirmations, and the next sync using the explicitly accepted base. The share package built, its packed size passed the repository size gate locally, and all pre-commit checks passed. Live workspace listing succeeded. Live upload validation is pending.

## Before

Studio offered a single action to sync project files.

![Studio Share panel before reconnect](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f18121795bc23c285f996ce518423f696394c95a/before.png)

## After

After choosing an existing project, the user sees the cloud project and workspace before confirming. Both captures show the Studio Share panel with sample workspace data.

![Studio confirmation for the selected project and workspace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/f18121795bc23c285f996ce518423f696394c95a/after.png)


With different local files, Studio asks for a second confirmation.

![Studio warning before reconnecting a folder with different files](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/9377c000d10576608296eb488da3b06de4759bb1/divergent.png)

title: fix(studio): keep the editor responsive when a preview asks for paused frames
body:
## What

Studio now reads a paused-frame `decode` message only when its `asks` list has no gaps and at most `PAUSED_FRAME_SOURCES` (4) entries. A longer list is dropped before any entry is read. The runtime checks the same limit before it sends, so a decode naming more than four sources still fails at once with "Preview decode over budget".

## Why

`parsePausedFrameAsk` accepted any array and then ran `map` and `every` over its declared length. A message can declare a length of up to 2^32-1 with no entries behind it, and walking that kept the editor busy for minutes. The four-source limit was checked by the host only after the parse finished.

## Related work

Uses the `isMessageList` check the other preview-frame readers use (`packages/core/src/runtime/protocol.ts`).

## How

- `parsePausedFrameAsk`: `Array.isArray(data.asks)` becomes `isMessageList(data.asks, PAUSED_FRAME_SOURCES)`. This checks the length first and then looks for gaps in at most four slots.
- `portPausedVideoProvider.decode` (runtime side): throws "Preview decode over budget" when it gets more than four requests. Before this change, the host sent that reply after the decode reached it. With the parser now dropping such a message, a decode over the limit would otherwise wait with no reply.
- `pausedFrameHost.decode`: drops its now-unreachable `> PAUSED_FRAME_SOURCES` branch and keeps the empty-list reply.
- I checked every other `message` listener and port handler in `packages/studio/src` (15 in all). None walks a list from the frame before bounding it.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `pausedFrames.test.ts`: a decode of 1 to 4 sources is read; a declared length of 2^32-1, five sources and a list with a gap are each refused in under a second; the runtime fails a five-source decode without posting anything.
  - `pausedVideoProvider.test.ts`: five sources and a 2^32-1 list reach no decode, and the port still answers a `suspend` straight after.
- fails without the fix: on main's `pausedFrames.ts` the core file did not finish within 90 s (the parser walking the declared length). On its own, `fails a decode of more sources than Studio reads without asking` timed out at 5 s with no reply.
- With the change: `pausedFrames.test.ts` 5/5 and the four `pausedVideoProvider*` / `pausedVideoDecoder` test files 42/42, each 3 runs in a row. `editingPort`, `editingAgent` and `pausedVideoFrames` tests 220/220. Studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the changed files.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Message parsing and tests only; no .tsx, .css or .html changed. A valid paused-frame decode behaves as before.

title: feat(lint): warn when a 3D-transformed element is far larger than the stage
body:
## What

A new lint warning, `three_d_layer_far_larger_than_stage`: an element with a 3D transform (`rotateX`, `rotateY`, `rotate3d`, `translateZ`, `scaleZ`, `scale3d`, `matrix3d`, `perspective()`) whose px `width` x `height` is more than 4 times the stage area. Checks `<style>` rules and inline styles.

## Why

A 3D-transformed layer is rasterized nearly whole, not clipped to what is on stage. An 11000x5200 `rotateX(90deg)` floor in a 1920x1080 composition is 28x the stage. Measured in an editor preview on a Linux build (17 samples over 30 s each): composited layer area median 86.8 Mpx with the floor as authored, 31.7 Mpx with the same floor at 1920x1080 (renderer 1176 vs 868 MB, GPU process 366 vs 283 MB). On macOS, where the preview shares the host app's compositor, that floor evicted the host's own tiles and its panels went blank. Nothing in lint or check named the cause.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `packages/lint/src/rules/layers.ts`, a new `layers` rule group registered in `hyperframeLinter.ts`. It reads the stage from the root's `data-width`/`data-height` and does nothing without them.
- Only px sizes and a `transform` in the same rule or inline style count. `translate3d` is left out on purpose: flat 3D translates are the usual promote-to-layer trick and keep 2D clipping.
- A warning, not an error: the render is correct, the cost is memory.
- Not covered: a size and a 3D transform set in two different rules, and transforms set from script (GSAP). Both need computed styles, which this static pass does not have.
- No existing lint helper parses the root size to numbers (`grep -rn data-width packages/lint/src`: `core.ts` and `utils.ts` read it as strings only), so the rule parses it itself.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `layers.test.ts` (warns on the 11000x5200 floor and on an inline `rotateY` wall; quiet at stage size and for a big 2D-rotated element). With the threshold raised to 100x, the two warning tests fail.
- [x] Full `packages/lint` suite: 33 files, 1370 tests passed. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] Manual: run on the composition that blanked, it reports only the floor.
- [x] Documentation updated: `docs/reference/lint-rules.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: feat(core): sealed previews can run Delete and arrow nudges in-frame once Studio arms them
body:
## What

Core half of #8935: the preview runtime can run canvas Delete and arrow-key nudges inside a sealed (opaque-origin) preview frame, and forward Studio's shortcuts back to it. All of it is gated on Studio sending `arm-canvas-keys` over the editing port. Studio does not send it until #8935 lands, so this PR changes nothing users see.

## Why

In a sealed preview, Delete and nudge round-trip from Studio's window over the `MessagePort` before the first frame paints, which adds visible lag in Firefox and WebKit. Running them in-frame removes that round trip. #8935 was about 2,000 changed lines; this splits it at the core/studio seam so each half can be reviewed on its own.

## Related work

Refs #8935 (the Studio half, stacked on this branch).

## How

- `runtime/editing/canvasKeys.ts`: a capture-first key shield plus armed actions. Once armed, a trusted Delete removes the armed elements in the same frame and posts a `canvas-key-action` that Studio commits or rolls back (`resolve-canvas-key-action`). Arrow combos draw the nudge in-frame and post cumulative steps. Other trusted keys are kept from the composition and forwarded to Studio. Inline text being edited, render, capture and export pages, and same-origin previews are never shielded.
- `editingPort.ts` / `editingAgent.ts`: the two new request kinds, with their params parsed at the port boundary. The agent's dispose also resets canvas-key state.
- `domRealm.ts`: `isDomNode`, so node checks work across realms (`instanceof Node` is banned in runtime code).
- Reuse over copies: `removeElements.ts` exports its removable-node and outermost-element checks, `editingGestureStart.ts` exports `gsapPosition`, and `textEdit.ts` adds `isActiveTextEditTarget`, so the in-frame Delete, nudge and text carve-out run the same code as the port paths. `generated/position-edits-render-inline.ts` is rebuilt output.
- Not in this PR: the load-time `installPreviewKeyShield()` call in `entry.ts`. With it, the shield would stop the editing agent's existing key-watch forwarding before Studio arms anything. It ships with #8935, so this PR stays inert until then.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated: `canvasKeys.test.ts` (shield, untrusted keys ignored, film-owned inputs blocked, same-origin and render pages never shielded, Delete commit/rollback, nudge steps), plus `editingPort.test.ts` and `editingAgent.test.ts` for the new kinds.
- [x] fails without the fix: `canvasKeys.test.ts` > "blocks film listeners, ignores untrusted keys, and removes armed targets in the same frame" fails when the shield's stop call is removed from `onShieldEvent`, and passes with it.
- [x] Core runtime and editing suites: 34 files, 648 tests, 3 consecutive runs, exit 0. `test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` exit 0. `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- [x] Inert check: main's Studio sealed-preview, hotkey and preview-channel suites run against this core: 55 files, 471 tests, exit 0.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(producer): preserve absent methods on early-stub timeline proxies
body:
## Why

`HF_EARLY_STUB` wraps timelines returned by `window.gsap.timeline()` so tween construction can be batched across frames, while the HyperFrames runtime uses feature checks (`typeof tl.timeScale === "function"`, `tl.kill?.()`, etc.) before calling optional GSAP methods.

Previously, `wrapTimeline` unconditionally attached `to`, `from`, `fromTo`, `set`, `add`, `pause`, `play`, `seek`, `totalTime`, `time`, `duration`, `getChildren`, `paused`, `timeScale`, and `kill` onto the proxy object even when the underlying timeline did not implement them. Any composition supplying a minimal or custom `window.gsap.timeline()` without optional methods such as `timeScale` or `kill` passed the runtime's `typeof` guards and immediately threw `TypeError: n.timeScale is not a function` or `TypeError: n.kill is not a function` during render capture. Passing a non-object return from `gsap.timeline()` also crashed `wrapTimeline`.

## What changed

- `packages/producer/stubs/hf-early-stub.ts`: attach each batched, chained, accessor, `getChildren`, and `kill` wrapper on the timeline proxy only when the underlying timeline defines that method as a function (preserving `this` binding via `.apply(real, args)` / `.call(real)`), and return non-object values from `gsap.timeline()` untouched.
- `packages/producer/src/generated/hf-early-stub-inline.ts`: regenerated IIFE output (`bun run --cwd packages/producer build:hf-early-stub`).
- `packages/producer/src/services/fileServer.test.ts`: regression tests covering minimal custom timelines omitting optional methods, non-object timeline returns, and full class-based timelines with prototype methods.

## Verification

- fails without the fix: `packages/producer/src/services/fileServer.test.ts` — `does not fabricate timeline methods absent from the underlying timeline` and `returns non-object timeline values untouched without crashing wrapTimeline` both failed on `main` (exit 1, 88 pass, 2 fail) before the `hf-early-stub.ts` change.
- After fix: `bun test packages/producer/src/services/fileServer.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row (exit 0, 90 pass, 0 fail each run); sibling tests `fileServer-seededRandom.test.ts` and `fileServer-virtualTimers.test.ts` passed (exit 0, 16 pass, 0 fail).
- `bun run --cwd packages/producer typecheck`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `bun run --cwd packages/producer build` all exited 0 with 0 warnings/errors.
- Not exercised: a full end-to-end headless Chrome render of a custom-GSAP composition (covered by the injected stub unit harness above; full browser CI suite runs on the PR merge ref).

title: fix(studio-server): a history lock on a disk that stops answering no longer freezes the app
body:
## What

The project history lock (`studio-server/src/history/ownerLock.ts`) now does every file call through `fs/promises`, and reads a process's start time with an async `execFile("ps")`. Before, every file call in it was sync. A disk that stops answering now leaves `takeHistoryOwnership` waiting, while the thread that called it keeps running.

The release function `takeHistoryOwnership` returns is now async, and every call to it waits on the same single release. Every caller awaits it: `openProjectHistory`, the daily prune, `reclaimUncopiedBlobs`, `registerRenderOutput` and the video-state lock.

## Why

A host that opens a project history on its main thread (the Desktop app does) froze until the disk answered. An app froze for minutes creating a project, its main thread stuck inside `open()` of the lock's `owner.pid.start` record. `O_NONBLOCK` keeps a FIFO from blocking, but it does nothing for a disk that never answers an open: only taking the call off the thread does.

## Related work

Follows the earlier moves of history reads off the thread (`historyOffThread.test.ts`, `projectHistory.openOffThread.test.ts`, `videoStateSilentDrive.test.ts`).

Opening a history still makes sync file calls after the lock. Each is a follow-up of its own:

- `Engine.start`: `readLog` (`historyLog.ts`, `readFileSync` of the log), `readStatCache` / `readJson` (`stat.json`, `adopting.json`, `went-ahead.json`), `existsSync(project.json)`.
- `historyId.ts`: `readFileSync(project.json)`, `utimesSync`, `mkdirSync`.
- `containedPath.ts`: `lstatSync` / `mkdirSync` / `renameSync` per path segment.
- `saveRecord` (`historyLog.ts`): `openSync` / `writeSync` on every entry.
- Background prune: `readdirSync`, `statSync`, `renameSync`.

## How

- A plain-word swap: each sync call becomes its `fs/promises` twin, and `replaceFileAtomically` becomes `replaceFileAtomicallyAsync`. The checks, their order and the flags are unchanged (`O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK`, `link` then `wx`, the evict lock).
- The release is created once, so a second `close()` cannot finish before the first one's release has removed the lock (`releases ownership only after every close has settled` caught that).
- `pruneGoneProjectHistoriesDaily` reads its once-a-day stamp inside the `setImmediate` it already used, so the open never reads it.

Three tests leaned on the lock being sync, and each now tests what it names:

- `snapshotRuns.test.ts`: its "disk full" spy failed the first sync `replaceFileAtomically` call, which was the lock writing its own `.start` record, not the state file. It now fails the state file's own async write.
- `projectHistory.test.ts` "refuses start while its media copy is still adopting": the media hold only gates `.bin` copies, so with `clip.mp4` it raced a 2 MB copy against the open. It now uses `clip.bin`, like its siblings.
- `videoStateSilentDrive.test.ts`: it moved the fake clock after 5 turns. It now waits for the give-up timer to exist first, since a lock that takes more turns would let the clock jump before the timer starts.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New test: `ownerLock.test.ts` "keeps the thread running while an open of the owner's start record waits on the disk". It stalls every open of `owner.pid.start` (the sync one with `Atomics.wait`, the async one with a timer) for 300 ms while a 5 ms interval pings, and expects at least one ping inside the stall.

fails without the fix: `packages/studio-server/src/history/ownerLock.test.ts` "keeps the thread running while an open of the owner's start record waits on the disk". On the base `ownerLock.ts` the stall happens and no ping lands inside it (`expected 0 to be greater than 0`); with the fix it passes, 3 runs in a row.

Ran on Linux: `packages/studio-server` vitest, 2655 passed. The 1 failure, `mediaExtensions.test.ts` "still reads clip.ts" (real ffprobe), fails the same way on the base. `tsc --noEmit`, oxlint, oxfmt and the repo's pre-commit (fallow included) pass.

Not run: Windows and macOS (CI covers them); a real stalled disk (the stall is a shim).

Not done: the lock itself has no deadline. An open that never answers now leaves `takeHistoryOwnership` pending, where before it held the thread just as long, so the app stays responsive but that open does not finish. A deadline for the claim is a separate change.

title: fix(cli): report non-stdio EPIPE crashes and guard launched browser pipes
body:
## Why

1. `packages/cli/src/cli.ts` already attaches `EPIPE` handlers to `process.stdout` and `process.stderr` for normal piped-output teardown, but its `process.on("uncaughtException")` listener also intercepted any `EPIPE` from any stream and called `handleStreamEpipe()` (`process.exit(1)` with no error box, no stack, and no error telemetry). When a child pipe (such as Chrome's CDP pipe or another subprocess pipe) emitted an unhandled `EPIPE`, the CLI exited 1 without saying why.
2. When Puppeteer launches Chrome with `pipe: true`, `PipeTransport.close()` disposes its own `error` listener on the stdio pipe (`this.#subscriptions.dispose()`). `forceCloseBrowserProcess` already attached a permanent no-op error listener to `proc.stdio` to absorb late `ECONNRESET`/`EPIPE` errors after disconnect, but `launchBrowser`, `probeHardwareWebGlInfo`, `hdrCapture`, and `launchOwnedBrowser` did not, leaving normal shutdown or mid-launch Chrome deaths able to crash the CLI via an unhandled pipe error and bypass calibration/fallback error handling.

## What changed

- `packages/cli/src/cli.ts`: removed the blanket `code === "EPIPE"` shortcut from `process.on("uncaughtException")`; `process.stdout`/`process.stderr` `EPIPE` continues to go through their stream listeners, while any non-stdio `EPIPE` now reports through `exitAfterCliFailure` (error box, diagnostic code, error telemetry) before exiting 1.
- `packages/engine/src/services/browserManager.ts` (exported via `packages/engine/src/index.ts`): extracted one idempotent `absorbBrowserPipeErrors(browser)` helper (backed by a `WeakSet` so duplicate listeners are never added) and wired it into `launchBrowser`, `probeHardwareWebGlInfo`, `forceCloseBrowserProcess`, `packages/engine/src/services/hdrCapture.ts`, and `packages/cli/src/browser/launch.ts` (`launchOwnedBrowser`).
- Audited every `puppeteer.launch(` site across `packages/*/src/`: the two remaining sites (`packages/inspector/src/service.ts` and `packages/producer/src/verifyStaticPage.ts`) do not use `pipe: true`.

## Verification

title: feat(core): hold and draw stage acts inside a sealed preview over the editing port
body:
## What changed

- Added a `stage-act` request to the runtime editing port (`packages/core/src/runtime/editing/stageAct.ts`, wired into `editingPort.ts` and `editingAgent.ts`), so a host can play its stage acts inside a sealed (opaque-origin) preview without touching the frame's document. The host keeps every motion and easing; the frame only holds, applies validated values and reports boxes.
  - `hold`: holds up to `MAX_STAGE_ACTS = 64` elements (found by the key scheme `stage-measure` returns) in their before look, borrowing only the properties each act names, and applies its first draw at once. With `deferred: true`, an element not on the stage yet is held from an in-frame `MutationObserver` callback, so it is held before the frame paints it. The frame reports it with a `stage-act-ready` event. The observer stops after `STAGE_HOLD_WATCH_MS = 30_000`.
  - `frame`: applies a batch of draws. `translate`, `scale` and `rotate` move the element's own values (`transformValues.ts`) and never replace them. Other styles are checked against a fixed list of properties and a value grammar. A draw can also type the element's own text back one grapheme at a time behind a caret. The reply is the boxes laid out after every write, read in a single layout pass.
  - `ready` and `restore`: hold the waiting elements that show now; give back some keys or all of them. `ready` also reports keys already held, so asking again after a lost reply still finds them. Restoring puts each borrowed inline property and text node back exactly as it was.
  - A `stage-input` event forwards the person's press, drop or key in the frame, only while a hold is live, so the host decides whether it ends its run.
  - One session per port, as `text-edit` keeps one: a new hold gives the previous one back, and the agent's `dispose` gives everything back.
- Validation (frame side, `parseStageActParams`): lists over the cap, non-finite or out-of-range numbers, unknown fields, unknown or `Object`-member names (`constructor`, `toString`) and unknown ops are rejected. Colours must be a hex value, a keyword or a CSS colour function with no nested call. Drawn values may call only colour functions, `radial-gradient`, `rotate`, `drop-shadow` and `calc`, so `url()`, `var()`, `image-set()` and `;` never reach an inline style.
- Added `holdPreviewStage`, `readyPreviewStage`, `restorePreviewStage`, `previewStageDrawer`, `onPreviewStageActReady` and `onPreviewStageInput` in `packages/studio/src/player/lib/previewStageAct.ts`, exported from `packages/studio/src/index.ts`. Every reply is checked against what was asked: the op matches, keys are a subset of the asked keys, counts are at most what was asked, and boxes are finite. A bad reply returns `null`, never a partial result. A `hold` with no reply in time, or a bad one, is followed by a `restore` of its keys. The port keeps order, so a late hold is undone instead of leaving elements stuck in their before look. `previewStageDrawer` sends one parent frame's draws together and keeps at most one `frame` request out. Draws made while one is out merge to the latest per key, so nothing queues behind a slow frame.
- Added `locateStageKey` and `paintedOnStage` next to `measureStageDocument` (`stageMeasure.ts`), so measuring and acting share one key scheme and one visibility test.

## No visible change

This adds an editing-port request and library wrappers (`.ts` only). No host calls them yet, so nothing on screen changes.

## What I measured

- `oxfmt` + `oxlint` on all changed files: 0 warnings, 0 errors. Pre-commit `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues`: no issues in 15 changed files.
- `@hyperframes/core build` and `@hyperframes/studio build`: passed. `node scripts/verify-packed-manifests.mjs`: 15 packages within `scripts/package-size-budgets.json`.
- `packages/core`: `tsc --noEmit` for `tsconfig.json` and `tsconfig.runtime.json` passed; `lint:runtime-preview-guards` passed; `src/runtime/editing`, `editingPort.test.ts` and `editingAgent.test.ts`: 31 files, 585 tests passed. `stageAct.test.ts` 3x with `--sequence.shuffle`: passed each time.
- `packages/studio`: `tsc --noEmit` passed; `src/player/lib`: 42 files, 487 tests passed; `previewStageAct.test.ts` 3x with `--sequence.shuffle`: 14/14 each time.
- An end-to-end port test (`editingPort.test.ts`) holds two deferred elements through a real `MessageChannel`, reveals one, receives `stage-act-ready` for both, receives `stage-input` for a key, and restores both.
- fails without the fix: removing each guard fails a test. Guards checked: the act cap, the `var()` and `url()` grammar, writing only borrowed properties, own-key table lookups (3 rows), the deferred watch cap, input forwarded only while holding, `dispose` giving holds back, typing's restore order, `ready` reporting already-held keys, and both client event dispatches in `editingPort.ts`. In `previewStageAct.ts`: the op match, asked-keys checks (holds and boxes), the hold cap, the restore count bound, a single request out, the ready-key filter, and the restore after a late hold.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real browser. Tests run in jsdom and happy-dom, so real paint timing (a deferred hold before first paint) is shown only by observer ordering, not on screen.
- A host consumer: the Desktop wiring lands after this is published.
- The removed-element ghost relay. It is a separate follow-up PR stacked on this one.

title: fix(engine): give each video frame extraction its share of the CPUs
body:
## What

Each video frame extraction ffmpeg now gets its share of the CPU budget (`-threads` for decode and encode, `-filter_threads`), instead of ffmpeg's default of one thread per core per process.

## Why

Extraction already runs up to `usableCpuCount() / 2` ffmpeg processes at once (`EXTRACTION_SLOTS`). Left to its default, each of them also starts threads per core, and each thread holds frames, so memory grew with cores x slots x frame size. Measured on one 4K 60 fps mjpeg source, extracting 5 s to 1080p JPEGs with the extractor's filter shape: peak RSS 211 MB at `-threads 2`, 1057 MB at `-threads 32`, same wall time (12.9 s vs 13.0 s on a 32-core box). On a 32-core machine that is 16 runs x ~1 GB for 4K sources. A Windows export with three 4K sources failed in extraction with ffmpeg "Cannot allocate memory" while the machine had 32 GB+ of RAM.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `EXTRACTION_THREADS = max(1, floor(cpuBudget() / EXTRACTION_SLOTS))`, next to `EXTRACTION_SLOTS` in `videoFrameExtractor.ts`. `cpuBudget()` is the helper `softwareEncoderThreads.ts` already uses for encoder threads.
- Passed as `-filter_threads` (global) and `-threads` before `-i` (decoder) on the shared `args`, so the whole-range and segmented paths both carry it, and as `-threads` on the output.
- Total extraction threads now stay near the CPU budget instead of slots x cores.

## Test plan

- [x] New `videoFrameExtractor.threads.test.ts`: with 32 CPUs mocked (16 slots), every extraction ffmpeg gets `-threads 2` before and after `-i` and `-filter_threads 2`. Fails on main (no `-threads` at all), passes with the change, 3 runs in a row.
- [x] All `videoFrameExtractor*` tests: 325 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed. The failure (`unindexed negative-base MPEG-TS`, ffprobe killed with no exit code) fails the same way on main on this machine's static ffmpeg 7.0.2, so it is not from this change; CI decides.
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for `packages/engine`.
- [ ] Not done: an end-to-end peak-memory comparison of a full render. My before/after renders were not comparable (the second reused cached frames and the sampler could not tell extraction from encode runs).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(studio-server): reopening a history no longer reads its records on the caller's thread
body:
## What

Reopening a project history, and the read-only view of one another process holds, now read the history's records through `fs/promises`. Before, those reads were sync:

- `historyId.ts`: `isRecordedFolder` is async. It reads `project.json` with `readRecordOffThread`, and the 0.8.78 copy check stats the recorded folder and reads its id off the thread. That folder may sit on a disk that is gone. `projectHistoryId` checks for the history folder with `statOffThread` and records the project with an async twin of `recordProject`.
- `historyLog.ts`: `readLog` is async. Its three callers (the engine's start, `reclaimUncopiedBlobs`, the read-only view) already ran in async code.
- The engine's start reads `stat.json`, `adopting.json` and `went-ahead.json` with `readFile`.
- The engine's constructor no longer reads `project.json`. `readOpenedFolder`, which already ran after the ownership wait, answers whether the folder is the one the history was recorded for.
- `readProjectHistory` is async, and the CLI's `historyOwner` awaits it.
- The daily prune reads each history's `project.json` and its last-used times off the thread.

## Why

Same failure as #8948, one step later: an app that opens a history on its main thread froze while the disk under the history folder (or under an old project folder the record names) stopped answering. #8948 took the lock off the thread; these are the reads that follow it on every reopen.

## Related work

Follows #8948.

The sync calls left on the write path (`persistLog` / `saveRecord` / `writeLog`, `saveJson`, `saveStatCache`, `compactGrownLog`, `whereFolder`, `fileLeftIn`, `containedPath`) are the next PR. The CLI's `clean` command keeps the sync `readRecord` / `readId` through `listProjectHistories`, since the CLI never runs on an app's thread.

## How

Each sync read swaps for its `fs/promises` twin, following the file's existing `readId` / `readIdOffThread` pair. The pure part of `recordProject` (`recordOf`, `sameRecord`) is shared by its sync and async forms. The sync one is still used by the write path until the next PR.

Anyone calling `readProjectHistory` must now await it. A caller that already returns it from an async function needs no change.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New file `packages/studio-server/src/history/projectHistory.openStall.test.ts`. It stalls every read of `project.json`, `log.jsonl`, `stat.json`, `adopting.json` and `went-ahead.json` under the history folder for 150 ms, through either the sync or the async call, while a 5 ms interval pings. It expects a ping inside every stall, for a reopen and for the read-only view.

fails without the fix: `packages/studio-server/src/history/projectHistory.openStall.test.ts` "a reopen keeps the thread running while each read of the history's records waits on the disk". On #8948's code the reopen stalls 8 times and the thread runs through none (`expected +0 to be 8`); the read-only view stalls 2 times and runs through none. With the fix both pass, 3 runs in a row.

Ran on Linux: `packages/studio-server` vitest, 2659 passed. The 1 failure, `mediaExtensions.test.ts` "still reads clip.ts" (real ffprobe), fails the same way on the base. Also ran `packages/cli` `historyOwner` tests (7 passed), studio-server `tsc --noEmit`, and the repo's pre-commit (fallow included).

Not run: Windows and macOS (CI covers them); a real stalled disk (the stall is a shim).

title: fix(core): never read an element id as a stage index path
body:
Stacked on #8950 (base `feat/stage-act-port`). `locateStageKey` only exists there.

## What changed

- `measureStageDocument` (`packages/core/src/runtime/editing/stageMeasure.ts`) now writes an element's `data-hf-id` key as `#` + the id, with `>` and `\` escaped. Index-path keys stay digits joined by `>`, so neither kind can be read as the other. Before, an element whose id was all digits (`data-hf-id="12"`) had the key `12`, which `locateStageKey` read as "body child 12". Its children's keys (`12>0`) pointed into the wrong subtree, and an id containing `>` split into a false path.
- `locateStageKey` splits a key only at unescaped `>` and removes the escapes. A `#` anchor is looked up by id, a digit anchor by body index, and anything else resolves to nothing.
- This changes the `key` format that `stage-measure` returns. Only the field's contents change, not the shape. Hosts that rebuild element lookups from keys must read the new format. The Desktop host has not pinned a release with `stage-measure` yet.

## No visible change

`.ts` only, and no host calls it yet.

## What I measured

- fails without the fix: the new `stage keys` rows in `stageMeasure.test.ts` (an id of `12` among 13 body children, an id with `>`, an id with `\>`) failed 3/3 on the old code before the fix, then passed. Removing the `#` prefix, the escape or the unescape each fails them.
- `src/runtime/editing`, `editingPort.test.ts` and `editingAgent.test.ts`: 592 passed. `stageMeasure.test.ts` 3x with `--sequence.shuffle`: 9/9 each time. The two older expectations that pinned the old key text (`hf-hero` → `#hf-hero`) are updated.
- `@hyperframes/core build` passed. Studio `previewStageMeasure.test.ts` and `previewStageAct.test.ts`: 19 passed. `oxlint` 0/0. Pre-commit `fallow` and `typecheck` passed, and `comment-ratchet.mjs` passes against the base.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real browser. Tests run in jsdom.
- The Desktop host's matching lookup change, which lands with its pin.

title: fix(render): handle missing temp dir and long Windows paths in render staging
body:
## Summary

Fixes Windows `ENOENT` render failures in three related path-handling seams:

1. **Missing temp root when reserving the render work directory (`createRenderWorkDir`)**: `executeRenderJob` created `dirname(outputPath)` before starting, but `createRenderWorkDir` assumed `dirname(prefix)` (the system temp folder on Windows and macOS) already existed. When `TEMP`/`TMP` points to a missing folder, `mkdtempSync` failed immediately with `ENOENT`. `createRenderWorkDir` now ensures `dirname(prefix)` exists via `mkdirSync(..., { recursive: true })` (using `toWin32LongPath`) before reserving the work directory.
2. **Extended-length Windows paths past 260 characters (`toWin32LongPath` + `ArtifactTransaction` + `createOwnedRenderDir`)**: `createStagingDir` already used `toWin32LongPath` (`\\?\`) to create staging directories past 260 characters, then returned the unprefixed path. Writing `owner.json` inside that directory, staging into `.<stem>.hf-transaction-XXXXXX/<stem><ext>` (which doubled the output stem and pushed valid output paths past 259 characters), validating, and committing all called `node:fs` without `toWin32LongPath`. We now export `toWin32LongPath` from `@hyperframes/core/atomic-file`, cap the transaction directory stem when doubling it would exceed 259 characters (still matching `RENDER_TEMP_DIR`), and route `owner.json` writes and `ArtifactTransaction` default filesystem operations through `toWin32LongPath`.
3. **`.mov` and `.webm` faststart bypass copy (`applyFaststart`)**: `applyFaststart` skipped remuxing `.mov` and `.webm` outputs via raw `copyFileSync(inputPath, outputPath)` (case-sensitive, without `toWin32LongPath`), failing with `ENOENT` on Windows paths over 260 characters or uppercase `.MOV`/`.WEBM` extensions. It now matches `/\.(webm|mov)$/i` and passes both paths through `toWin32LongPath`.

## Verification

- **Red-first proof** (fails without the fix: all 4 new test cases failed on `origin/main` before the production edits):
  - `packages/core/src/atomicFile.win32Paths.test.ts`: `toWin32LongPath` was not exported.
  - `packages/engine/src/services/chunkEncoder.win32Faststart.test.ts`: 3/3 failed (`copyFileSync` received unprefixed Windows paths and `.MOV` did not take the copy branch).
  - `packages/producer/src/services/render/renderDirOwner.test.ts`: failed with `ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdtemp '.../absent-temp/nested/hf-render-XXXXXX'`.
  - `packages/producer/src/services/render/artifactTransaction.test.ts`: failed with `AssertionError: expected 316 to be less than or equal to 259`.
- **After fix** (3 consecutive green runs across touched and sibling suites):
  - `packages/core`: `atomicFile.win32Paths.test.ts`, `atomicFile.test.ts`, `noBareMkdtemp.test.ts` (48 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed x3).
  - `packages/engine`: `chunkEncoder.win32Faststart.test.ts`, `chunkEncoder.test.ts` (117 passed, 0 failed x3).
  - `packages/producer`: `renderDirOwner.test.ts`, `renderDirOwner.boot.test.ts`, `renderDirOwner.sandbox.test.ts`, `artifactTransaction.test.ts` (67 passed, 0 failed x3).
- **Typecheck, build, lint, format, complexity**:
  - `bun run --cwd packages/core build`, `bun run --cwd packages/engine build`, `bun run --cwd packages/producer build` all exited 0.
  - `tsc --noEmit` across `core`, `engine`, `producer`, `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `fallow health` all passed with 0 errors.
- **Not exercised**: Real Windows NTFS host execution (verified Windows path shapes via `node:path.win32` mocks following `atomicFile.win32Paths.test.ts`; Windows CI will execute native win32 suites).

title: feat(core): stand a removed element back as a ghost in a sealed preview
body:
Stacked on #8950 (base `feat/stage-act-port`).

## What changed

When an edit removes an element, the open preview stands it back for a moment and flicks it away: the host imports the old element from the document it left. A sealed (opaque-origin) preview's old document is closed to the host, so this PR relays the element's markup instead, for the host to request before the replacing frame is promoted.

- `capture` op on `stage-act` (`packages/core/src/runtime/editing/stageGhost.ts`): the frame being replaced writes out each asked element's subtree, with its computed look on the root (the same 14 properties the open path copies) and without its `id` or `data-hf-id`. A subtree over `MAX_STAGE_GHOST_MARKUP = 65_536` characters is left out. Each call takes at most `MAX_STAGE_ACTS` targets.
- Ghost `hold` in `stageAct.ts`: the replacing frame parses the markup inert (`DOMParser`) and strips `script`, `iframe`, `object`, `embed`, `frame`, `frameset`, `base`, `meta` and `link` elements, every `on*` attribute, `srcdoc`, and any attribute whose value, with spaces and control characters removed, contains `javascript:` or `data:text/html`. It refuses markup that is not exactly one element, or whose root is itself stripped. The ghost is appended as `position: fixed`, `aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none` at the removed element's box, takes the usual `frame` draws for its flick, and is removed on `restore` or `dispose`.
- `capturePreviewGhosts` in `packages/studio/src/player/lib/previewStageAct.ts`: Studio treats each ghost as an opaque string. It checks only that each entry is a string, capped, for a key it asked, and at most as many as asked. It never parses the markup or puts it in its own DOM.

The replacing frame shows the same film in the same seal, so it loads the ghost's pictures and fonts itself, as the open path's import does, and no pixels cross. The host's rule is that a capture goes only to the replacing frame of the same film and load; that lands with the host change.

## No visible change

`.ts` only, and no host calls it yet.

## What I measured

- One row per stripped thing in `stageGhost.test.ts` (each element kind, `on*` lower and upper case, `srcdoc`, `javascript:` plain, split by a newline, in an SVG `xlink:href` and in an SVG `<set to>`, and `data:text/html`), plus a frameset root.
- fails without the fix: removing each guard fails a test. Guards checked: every stripped element kind, the `on*` and `srcdoc` rules, both URL patterns, the control-character fold, the capture size cap, removing identity on capture, the ghost parse cap and field check, `aria-hidden`, the capture target cap, and in Studio the asked-key, cap and string checks. 22 guards, 22 caught.
- Parity with the open path: a removed `<figure>` with a picture, nested inline elements and an SVG stands back with exactly the subtree `cloneNode(true)` gives, which is what the open path's import copies.
- `src/runtime/editing`, `editingPort.test.ts` and `editingAgent.test.ts`: 612 passed. `stageAct.test.ts` + `stageGhost.test.ts` 3x with `--sequence.shuffle`: 56/56 each time. Studio `src/player/lib`: 493 passed, and `previewStageAct.test.ts` 20/20 3x with `--sequence.shuffle`.
- `tsc --noEmit` for core (`tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.runtime.json`) and studio passed. `lint:runtime-preview-guards` passed. Core and studio builds passed, and `verify-packed-manifests.mjs` shows 15 packages within budget. `oxlint` 0/0. `comment-ratchet.mjs` passes against the base.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real browser or a pixel comparison. The pixel parity check (picture and nested element, both modes) runs in the host's walk once it is wired.
- The host's capture timing between "replacing frame ready" and promotion. That lands with the host change.

title: feat(core): tell the host where a press lands during a sealed text edit
body:
## What

During an inline text edit, the frame's editing session now tells its port where a press landed: a primary press in the film outside the edited text, or a right-click anywhere in the film (the text included). It posts a new `text-edit-away` event (`button`, frame-px `point`, `viewportWidth`, `keys`), and `EditingPortClient` gains `onTextEditAway`.

## Why

When the preview is sealed (opaque origin, own process), the host can't listen on the film's document. So during a sealed text edit, a click inside the film outside the text saves the text but never reaches the host's picker (nothing is let go or re-picked), and a right-click inside the film never opens the host's element menu. With an open preview the host listens on the film document directly and both work. This event gives a sealed host the same facts.

## Related work

Core half only. The host relay (map the point to the frame box, guard on its own open edit for that handle, feed the existing picker and menu replay) follows in the host app once a release carries this. Until then nothing listens, so nobody sees a change.

## How

- `packages/core/src/runtime/editing/textEdit.ts`: `passAway` adds capture `pointerdown` and `contextmenu` listeners on the session's document for the life of the session, removed in `open.stop`.
  - A primary press outside the element is posted on a `setTimeout`, so the `text-edit-ended` that the same press's blur sends (in the same task) is first on the port. A host that replays the press after the ended event replays it after the save.
  - A right-click is `preventDefault`ed (the frame's own menu stays shut) and posted at once; it doesn't blur.
  - The frame reports every primary press with its keys; the host decides whether ctrl+click on a Mac is secondary, as it already does for open previews.
  - `textEditAwayEvent` parses the event in its exact shape (button 0 or 2, finite point, positive viewport width, three boolean keys).
- `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.ts`: the client routes the event to `onTextEditAway` listeners, cleared on dispose. No new request kind and no protocol version change; an older client ignores the event.
- No `isTrusted` check in the frame: the runtime shares the film's realm, so it wouldn't be a boundary. The host guards instead (only while its own sealed edit for that handle is open, one per press, point clamped to the frame).

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/core/src/runtime/editing/textEdit.test.ts` ("tells the port where a press outside the text landed, after the ended event that saves it" and "hands a right-click anywhere in the film, the text included, to the port and keeps the frame's menu shut") failed with only the session wiring removed; `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.test.ts` ("hands a text edit's away press to its listeners and drops an off-shape one") failed with only the client routing line removed.
- Also added: no event for a press inside the text, a non-primary press, or any press after the session ends; the parser rejects every off-shape field.
- `textEdit.test.ts` + `editingPort.test.ts` + `editingAgent.test.ts`: 232/232, 3 consecutive runs. `packages/core` `tsc --noEmit` clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on the changed files.
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed: the real-app proof (both modes, origin `null` in-run) comes with the host relay, which is what makes it visible.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Core runtime and editing-port client only (`.ts`, no UI, CSS or DOM rendering).

title: fix(lint): the 3D layer size warning skips keyframe steps
body:
## What

`three_d_layer_far_larger_than_stage` no longer reports rules inside `@keyframes` (`from`, `to`, `50%`).

## Why

Review note on #8945: the rule walked every CSS rule, so a keyframe step with a px size and a 3D transform was reported under the step's name (`to`) as if it were an element. A keyframe step is not an element; the warning named nothing anyone can find.

## Related work

Refs #8945.

## How

The style-block walk skips a rule whose parent is a `@keyframes` (or vendor-prefixed `-webkit-keyframes`) at-rule.

## Test plan

title: fix(core): a held stage act still hears frame keys while sealed canvas keys are armed
body:
## What

While a stage act is held in a sealed preview, the frame keeps reporting the person's keys to Studio as `stage-input`, even when canvas keys are armed.

## Why

#8935 installs a key shield at load in sealed previews. Once Studio arms canvas keys, the shield stops each trusted key before any later window listener runs. `stageAct` listened for `keydown` with its own window capture listener, which was added after the shield, so an armed shield swallowed the keys a held stage act reports. A run that should end on a key kept going.

## Related work

Stacked on #8935, which is stacked on #8946.

## How

- `canvasKeys.ts` owns frame keydown. `listenFrameKeydown(view, listener)` adds the listener to the shield when the shield is installed on that window. The shield then calls every such listener first for each keydown, trusted or not, before it prevents or stops anything. With no shield, as in a same-origin preview, it is a plain capture listener, as before.
- `stageAct.ts` listens for `keydown` through it. `pointerdown` and `drop` keep their window listeners, because the shield never stops pointer or drop events. The `stage-input` message is unchanged.

## No visible change

Core only: the frame now reports key input it previously dropped. Nothing changes on screen until a stage-act consumer acts on that input.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `canvasKeys.test.ts` > "still reports keys to a live stage-act hold while canvas keys are armed". With Delete armed and a live hold, a trusted Delete posts `stage-input` and then the canvas Delete, and a synthetic keydown still posts `stage-input`.
- [x] fails without the fix: the same test fails when `stageAct` adds its own `keydown` window listener again; the trusted Delete never reaches the stage act.
- [x] Core editing, port and agent suites: 599 tests, 3 runs in a row. `test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` exits 0. `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The Studio sealed-keys, stage-act and preview-channel suites pass (87 tests).

title: fix(cli): cloud render finds files whose names the page writes with a percent escape
body:
## What

`hyperframes cloud render` no longer calls a file missing when the page writes its name with a percent escape, such as `My%20Video.mp4`. The two cases fixed:

1. A composition names `assets/My%20Video.mp4` and the project root holds `assets/My Video.mp4`. This is the common one: a space in a file name, escaped in the page.
2. The file's own name holds the escape (browser downloads on Windows often keep `%20` in the saved name) and the page names it as written.

## Why

The local preview finds both files, because it tries the decoded name and then the name as written. The cloud upload refused the project instead: `The composition references "assets/My%20Video.mp4", which is not in the project folder.` That happened although the file is there, so a video that plays locally could not be rendered in the cloud. A reference the film does not strictly need was left out of the upload without a word.

## Related work

None.

## How

Both changes are in `packages/cli/src/utils/publishProject.ts`:

- `includeReferencedProjectFile` looked the project root up by the raw name only. It now tries every spelling `decodeUrlPathVariants` gives, decoded first, as the preview does.
- `tryResolveExternal` stops at the first spelling for a file inside the project folder. It now orders the spellings so that one present on disk inside the project folder comes first. When both or neither are present, the order is unchanged (decoded first). Only paths inside the project folder are checked, so the CLI still never looks at another computer's share or a device path. `publishProject.networkShare.win32.test.ts` pins that, and it failed on a first version of this change that checked every spelling.

Grep for other places that resolve a reference by its raw name (`resolve(<dir>, raw…)` in `packages/cli/src`, tests excluded): none.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `publishProject.missing.test.ts`, "a file named with a percent escape", with 3 tests: the escaped space resolved from the root, a file whose own name holds the escape, and a refusal when neither spelling is on disk.
- Fails without the fix: on `origin/main` both staging tests fail with `The composition references "...%20Video.mp4", which is not in the project folder.` Reverting only the root lookup fails only the first test, and reverting only the ordering fails only the second. With the fix the file passes 3 runs in a row (11/11).
- Sibling suites: every `src/utils/publishProject*`, `src/commands/cloud/*`, `urlPath` and `privateProjectFile` test file passes (23 files, 315 tests).
- Full `packages/cli` suite on a Linux box: 4 files fail (`snapshot`, `snapshotHdrFrame`, `measure/diff-offset`, `measure/media`, 14 frame-decoding tests), and the same 14 fail on unmodified `origin/main` on that box, so they come from its ffmpeg, not from this change.

title: feat(core): paint a sealed preview's drag chrome in the same frame as the layer
body:
## What

A sealed preview can now paint Studio's selection chrome itself, in the same turn as the gesture draft that moves the layer. Studio sends a copy of its own chrome (structured data, never markup) with a drag's first draft, then only each node's placement with every later draft. The frame builds the copy in a closed shadow root on one marked host under `<html>`, and removes the host when the drag ends.

Nothing sends chrome yet: Studio's half follows in a separate PR. Until then this path is inert.

## Why

In stock Chrome a sealed preview renders out of process, so Studio's outline and the dragged layer are two compositor surfaces that Viz shows independently. Even with Studio writing its outline in the move event (0 frames late), the frame's surface for step N+1 is shown with Studio's surface for step N. On the 4x CPU bench, outline minus layer sits at +0.68 to +1.09 steps per drag on a sealed preview and 0.00 on an open one. Only a chrome the frame paints itself can share the layer's compositor frame.

## Related work

Refs the selection-chrome lag work in #8909, #8919, #8921, #8931 and the raw-step drafts in #8912.

## How

- `runtime/editing/dragChrome.ts` (new): `parseDragChrome` checks the copy, and `drawDragChrome` mounts, places or clears it. The copy may only use `div`, `span`, `svg` and `path`, SVG geometry attributes, and style maps whose names are CSS properties. A value that would make the frame fetch (`url(`, `image(`, `image-set(`, `src(`) is refused. Caps: 64 nodes, depth 6, 32 KB of nodes, 48 properties per map, 512 characters per value. An over-cap copy fails the request's validation.
- The host is `<div data-hf-ignore data-hyperframes-ignore data-hyperframes-picker-ignore data-layout-ignore aria-hidden>`, marked like the paused-frame canvas (`pausedVideoFrames.ts` `markFrameCanvas`), with `all:initial; position:fixed; inset:0; pointer-events:none`. Every chrome node is forced to `pointer-events: none !important`. The copy maps overlay px to frame px with one transform: `scale(1/s) translate(-origin)`.
- `runtime/editingPort.ts`: the `draft` request takes an optional `chrome` (null clears it). A request that carries chrome may name no draft.
- `runtime/editingDraft.ts`: `drawDrafts(drafts, chrome)` draws the chrome after the drafts in the same call. When no chrome comes and the last live draft ends, the chrome is cleared, so a cancel can never leave it behind. `editingAgent.ts` also clears it when the agent is disposed.
- Per-step placement writes happen inside the shadow root, so the document's MutationObservers see only the host's one add and one remove per drag.

Every frame-side reader of the document, checked against the host:

| Reader | Why it never carries the chrome |
|---|---|
| `editing/documentMarkup.ts` (`documentElement.outerHTML`) | runs with the host taken out (`withoutDragChrome`), and put back in the same turn |
| `editingHandles.ts` `queryElements`, `readEveryMatch` (`document.querySelectorAll`) | skip the host |
| `editingAgent.ts` `computed-styles` and `editing/motionPathHome.ts` (`document.querySelector`) | Studio's stable selectors name composition elements; the host has no id or class and sits after `<body>` |
| `editingLayers.ts:102`, `editingGestureStart.ts:238` | walk the composition root, not `<html>` |
| `editing/maxZIndex.ts`, `editing/stageMeasure.ts` | walk `document.body` |
| `sceneWindow.ts` (`host.outerHTML` of scene hosts) | scene hosts live inside `<body>` |
| `picker.ts` | skips `[data-hf-ignore]` |
| `elements-at-point`, `pointer-targets` (`elementsFromPoint`) | host and nodes are `pointer-events: none` |
| MutationObservers on `<html>` (`init.ts`, `preloadMedia.ts`, `sealedMediaCors.ts`, `previewRasterHints.ts`, `frameSources.ts`, `staticCompositionPost.ts`, `editing/stageAct.ts`) | selector-based filters; per-step writes are inside the shadow root |
| `editing/textEdit.ts` removal observer | only checks that the edited element is still connected |

Every Studio reader of a sealed frame's document goes through `document-markup` (`previewChannel.ts` `previewDocumentMarkup` / `previewDocumentCopy`): the property panel, clipboard, GSAP reads (`gsapShared.ts`), timing patches, audio-group volume, automation sync, the timeline header and sync callbacks, and first-frame telemetry. All of them get the stripped markup.

Renders: chrome only arrives over the editing port, and the port is only handed to a parent that connects to a page marked for Studio (`editingAgent.ts` `installEditingAgent`). A render page is its own top window and carries no Studio mark.

## Test plan

Proof: 4x bench pending. The bench run (outline minus layer per drag, sealed and open, at 4x CPU) lands with the Studio PR's numbers.


- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

fails without the fix:
- `editing/dragChrome.test.ts` "is drawn in the same call as the draft it rides, at the step's place, mapped into frame px" fails with the `drawDragChrome` call removed from `drawDrafts`.
- "goes with a null chrome, and with the last draft's end when Studio sends none" fails with the last-draft clear removed.
- "is in no document markup or query a drag answers" fails with `withoutDragChrome` removed from `documentMarkup`, and again with the query skip removed (`expected [ …(2) ] to have a length of 1 but got 2`).
- "refuses a copy over the node or byte caps, and anything but paint" fails with the node cap, the byte cap or the fetch check removed, one at a time.
- The `pointer-events` override and the chrome-only request each fail their assertion when removed.
- `producer/src/services/coreRuntimeBrowser.test.ts` "hands a render page no editing port, so it never paints drag chrome" (real Chrome, built runtime) fails with the agent's top-window and Studio-mark checks removed (`expected [ 'editing-connect', …(2) ] to not include 'editing-port'`).

title: fix(studio): a sealed drag's outline moves in the same frame as the layer
body:
## What

On a sealed preview, the selection outline now moves in the same frame as the layer you drag. Studio hands its outline to the frame for the length of the drag, keeps only the part that lies outside the frame, and takes it back on release.

Stacked on #8961 (the frame side). Review that one first.

## Why

In stock Chrome a sealed preview renders out of process, so Studio's outline and the dragged layer are two compositor surfaces shown independently. Since #8912 the layer's step reaches the frame before Studio's next frame, so the outline shows the step before. On the 4x CPU bench, outline minus layer sits at +0.68 to +1.09 steps per drag sealed and 0.00 open. Only an outline the frame paints in the same turn as the layer can share its compositor frame.

## Related work

Refs #8909, #8919, #8921, #8931, #8912.

## How

- `frameDragChrome.ts` (new): `paintChromeInFrameWhile(iframe, overlay, held)` starts with a sealed drag's raw steps. With the first draft it sends a copy of Studio's chrome as structured data: tag (`div`, `span`, `svg`, `path`), the computed look, SVG geometry attributes. With every later draft it sends only each node's inline placement. The copy is checked with the core's own `parseDragChrome` before it rides a request, so a copy the frame would refuse never takes the drafts down with it, and Studio simply keeps its whole chrome.
- Once the frame answers a request that carried the copy, Studio clips its chrome plane to everything outside the frame's rect (`clip-path: path(evenodd, ...)`), so the part over the stage is painted only by the frame. The part outside the stage (handles past the edge, the box when the layer hangs off stage) stays Studio's.
- On release Studio removes the clip first, then sends a chrome-only clear on the next animation frame, so the outline never blinks. A later drag's chrome is not cleared by an earlier release.
- `previewDrafts.ts`: the draft queue carries the chrome on each request it already sends (microtask-batched, one in flight). No extra message per step.
- `gestureSteps.ts`: the raw step now moves Studio's outline (single box, and group members plus group box) before the draft goes out, so the frame copies this step's outline, not the last one.
- `DomEditSelectionChrome.tsx`: the selection and group chrome render inside one plane element (`data-dom-edit-chrome-plane`) that the clip applies to.
- Studio keeps pointer capture and the edit itself. The frame's copy is paint only (`pointer-events: none`), and saves, history, captures and stage reads never see it (see the core PR).

Not covered here:

- The frame's place in the overlay is read once per drag; a zoom or scroll mid-drag is not followed.
- A frame reload mid-drag shows no in-frame outline until release; Studio's own outline is back at release.
- Rotate keeps its existing angle lag.

## Test plan

Proof: 4x bench pending. The close bar: outline minus layer at most 0.1 per drag sealed, and pooled outline vs pointer no worse than open, at 4x CPU; the off-stage part's lag measured on its own. Numbers and Before/After captures land here when the run is done.

- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

- "is left to Studio when the frame would refuse the copy, and the drafts still land" fails with the `parseDragChrome` check removed.

title: fix(core): the preview runtime's editing port ignores later changes to MessagePort and window.parent
body:
## What

The preview runtime's editing port keeps using the browser's own `MessagePort` methods and the frame's original parent, even when a page script later changes `MessagePort.prototype` or assigns `window.parent`.

## Why

The runtime evaluates before the page's own scripts, but it set the port's `onmessage` and called `postMessage` and `close` through `MessagePort.prototype` at call time. So a page script that patched those methods saw every port the runtime opened, and could post on it as if it were the runtime. `installEditingAgent` also read `window.parent` when it installed, which happens after the page's scripts run, and a page can assign that property. `canvasKeys.ts` already read `postMessage` early; the other port users did not.

## How

- New `runtime/runtimePort.ts` reads `MessageChannel`, `postMessage`, `close` and the `onmessage` setter from a probe channel when the runtime first evaluates. It exposes `createRuntimeChannel`, `postOnPort`, `onPortMessage` and `closePort`. Those use the stored methods for any browser port and fall back to the object's own methods for a stand-in object, as in tests.
- The editing agent, `watchGeometry`, `textEdit`, `stageAct`, `pausedFrames` and `canvasKeys` use them for every port call. `canvasKeys` drops its own copy of the same lookup.
- `installEditingAgent` defaults its parent to `window.parent` as read when the module evaluated.

## No visible change

The editing protocol and every message are unchanged. Studio works the same as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added: `editingAgent.portCapture.test.ts`. "keeps its port from a composition that patched MessagePort before Studio connected" patches `onmessage` and `postMessage` after the runtime loads, then connects and talks to the agent. It checks that the patches saw no runtime port and that a Delete posted through anything they saw never reaches the parent. "hands its port to the parent it loaded with, not one a composition put on window.parent" assigns `window.parent` before install and checks that the port is never handed to it.
- [x] fails without the fix: both tests in `editingAgent.portCapture.test.ts` fail with the six runtime files at `main`, and pass with this change.
- [x] Core runtime suites: 177 files, 3,889 tests, 3 runs in a row. `test:hyperframe-runtime-ci` exits 0. `tsc --noEmit` is clean. The Studio sealed-keys, sealed, preview-channel, stage-act and dom-edit-session suites pass against the rebuilt core (112 tests).
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

## Why

The test copies, turns on read failures, copies again, then pastes and expects the first copy. It gave each copy 10 ms of real time to finish its read.
