title: fix(cli): a Windows browser close no longer freezes the CLI when taskkill hangs
body:
## What

On Windows, every `taskkill` the CLI starts now stops after 5 s. That includes the synchronous one `@puppeteer/browsers` runs to end a browser, which now runs without a shell so the limit ends `taskkill` itself. A browser close can no longer freeze the CLI.

## Why

A cold render on a Windows machine printed nothing for 15 minutes after calibration, then printed `[FrameCapture] Timed out closing browser; forcing browser process shutdown`. The engine's 5 s close timer (`CAPTURE_SESSION_CLOSE_TIMEOUT_MS`) could not fire because the Node event loop itself was blocked. The render's 60 s and 120 s heartbeats never printed either.

What blocked it:

1. When puppeteer's graceful close fails while the Chrome root is still alive, `BrowserLauncher.closeBrowser` calls `browserProcess.close()`. Its `kill()` then runs `childProcess.execSync("taskkill /pid N /T /F")` (`@puppeteer/browsers` `lib/launch.js`), synchronously and with no time limit. This happens, for example, when the CDP pipe drops before the process exits.
2. `taskkill /T` builds the process tree through WMI (`taskkill.exe` queries `Win32_Process` in `root\cimv2`). WMI on that machine was hung at the time. So `taskkill` hung, and with it the whole CLI.
3. The CLI's own close has the same exposure without blocking the loop. `killWithChildren` in `browser/launch.ts` awaits an async `taskkill` with no limit, before its exit bound is armed.

Both kinds of call already go through `hideChildConsoles`, which wraps `child_process` for the whole CLI process and already special-cases `taskkill`. So the limit goes there, once. A caller's own `timeout` still wins. When the limit hits, puppeteer falls back to `proc.kill()`, and the CLI's close falls back to `child.kill("SIGKILL")`. Both paths already existed for a failed `taskkill`.

## Related work

Refs #6553 (bounded CLI browser close), #8085 (Windows process reads without PowerShell command text).

## How

- `hideChildConsoles.ts`: a `taskkill` call gets `timeout: TASKKILL_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) next to its `stdio: "ignore"`. The match now also catches a bare `spawn("taskkill", args)`, the form `terminateWindowsProcessTree` uses.
- `execSync("taskkill ...")` is passed on as `execFileSync("taskkill", args)`. A time limit on a shell command ends only `cmd.exe`, and the `taskkill.exe` it started keeps running. Once WMI recovers, that orphan could kill whatever process has reused the PID by then. Without the shell, the limit ends `taskkill.exe` itself.
- A Windows-only process test puts a hanging stand-in `taskkill.exe` first on `Path`. The stand-in is a copy of node with a preload that acts only under that name. The test runs puppeteer's exact `execSync` command and checks two things: control comes back within 10 s, and the stand-in is no longer running. Off Windows it is skipped.

## Test plan

fails without the fix: `packages/cli/src/utils/hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts` ("is ended within its limit when puppeteer runs it synchronously") blocks for 65 s and fails with `expected [Function] to throw an error`. `packages/cli/src/utils/hideChildConsoles.test.ts` ("silences and time-limits taskkill, however it is started") fails with a strict-equality mismatch on the taskkill options.

All of the following ran natively on a Windows 11 machine:

- [x] Red first on `main`: the process test failed after 65.2 s.
- [x] A draft with only the time limit was red too: the call returned, but the stand-in was still running (`expected true to be false`). That draft is not in this PR.
- [x] With the fix, the process test passed 3 runs in a row at 5.06 s each. The unit file passed 5/5.
- [x] Released CLI 0.9.102, whose close-path files match `main`, with the stand-in first on `Path`. A script loaded the CLI's `child_process` wrapper and ran `@puppeteer/browsers`'s Windows `kill()` on a real `chrome-headless-shell`. Without the fix, `kill()` returned after 64955 ms, the event loop stalled 64973 ms, and Chrome was still alive. With the fix, it returned after 5027 ms, the stand-in was ended, and Chrome was gone.
- [x] The wrapper tests and the sibling suites that start or stub `taskkill` passed natively: `processTree`, `childReaper`, `cancellableProcess.killFailure`, `orphanCleanup`, `orphanCleanup.windowsHide`, `windowsExeSearch`, `windowsChromeWatchdog`, `launch.foreignPid`, `launch.boundedClose` and `previewLifecycle`. That is 12 files: 116 tests passed and 5 were skipped.
- [x] Normal `hyperframes render` runs with the fix: auto GPU with two calibrations in 15.7 s and software in 9.9 s, both exit 0 with no close timeout.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

title: feat(studio): prototype sealed canvas keys pressed in studio and drawn in the frame on request
body:
**Prototype: do not merge until the sealed-preview timing check passes** (Delete and arrow nudge drawn no later in a sealed preview than in an open one, in four browsers). Its shape may change before then.

## What

In a sealed (opaque-origin) preview, keyboard focus stays in Studio. When the canvas has a selection armed, Studio's own Delete or arrow press asks the frame to draw it, and the frame draws it with the same in-frame code a press inside the frame used.

## Why

Keys that arrive inside the frame cannot be attributed to the person, because the page's own script runs in that realm too. Keeping the press in Studio means every save starts from a key event Studio received itself. The frame still draws the Delete or nudge without waiting on a round trip: Studio sends one request, and the frame draws on receipt.

## How

- Core: a `canvas-key` request (`pressCanvasKey`) runs the armed Delete or nudge for the current arm revision. Its params are parsed at the port. The in-frame key path and this request share `runArmedAction`.
- Studio: one capture-phase `keydown` listener, registered when the module loads, sees Studio's trusted presses of the armed combos first, sends `canvas-key`, and keeps the press from Studio's other handlers. Arming no longer moves focus into the frame.
- Not yet in this prototype: saving from Studio's own state alone, and removing frame-reported keys and actions as save triggers. Both follow once the timing check passes.

## No visible change

Delete and arrow nudges look and save the same; only where the key press is received changes.

## Test plan

- [x] `tsc --noEmit` is clean for core and studio.
- [x] On a local build in Chrome, sealed and open, these real-key cases pass: Backspace on keyframes, Delete with focus moving, first nudge saved, group Delete, and group Delete then reselect in the frame and in the timeline.
- [ ] Timing check, four browsers, sealed vs open.
- [ ] Unit tests updated for the async draw and no frame focus. Two sealed-canvas tests still assume the old focus behavior.

title: feat(studio): let a host take presses in a sealed film during a text edit
body:
## What

A host app embedding Studio can now take presses in a sealed film during an inline text edit: `setStudioTextEditAway(handler | null)`. With a handler set, Studio starts each sealed text edit with `away: true` (from #8957), and passes the frame's `text-edit-away` events for that edit to the handler with the iframe. With no handler, nothing changes.

## Why

In a sealed preview the host can't listen on the film's document. So during a sealed text edit, a click elsewhere in the film saves the text but the host's picker never learns where it landed, and a right-click in the film never reaches the host's element menu. #8957 lets the frame report those presses, but only when the text-edit `start` asks for them, and Studio is what sends that `start`. Studio can't always ask, because then a host without a replacement (standalone Studio included) would lose the film's native right-click menu. So the host opts in through Studio.

Standalone Studio itself doesn't need it: it never listens on the film document during an edit, sealed or open. Its overlay is click-through while editing, so a click away just saves through blur and a right-click gets the browser's menu in both modes.

## Related work

Refs #8957 (frame side). The host relay that maps the point into the frame box and replays it through the picker and menu follows in the host app once a release carries this.

## How

- `packages/studio/src/hooks/textEditAway.ts`: `setStudioTextEditAway`, the same shape as Studio's other host setters. `sealedTextEditAway(iframe, handle)` returns the fields the start asks with (`{ away: true }` or nothing) and, with a host, watches that edit's away events:
  - only events whose handle is that edit's are passed on;
  - one edit is watched at a time: a new start, or clearing the handler, stops the previous watch;
  - the click away that ends the edit arrives after `text-edit-ended` (the frame posts it after the saving blur), so it still passes, and it is the last one: the watch stops on a `button: 0` event. Right-clicks keep the edit open, so they keep passing.
- `packages/studio/src/hooks/useInlineTextEdit.ts`: the sealed `start` spreads those fields into its request. That is the only change in the hook; the watch lives outside it.
- `packages/studio/src/index.ts`: exports `setStudioTextEditAway` and its type.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/studio/src/hooks/inlineTextEdit.sealed.test.ts` ("hands the host a right-click during the edit, and a click away only after the text it ended is saved" and "drops an away press for another element, and any after the ended edit's own") fail with the hook change removed. Both run against the real editing agent behind a sealed frame stand-in.
- The no-host test ("asks the frame for no presses with no host, so the frame's own menu stays") fails if Studio always asks; the "drops ..." test also fails if the watch never stops.
- `inlineTextEdit.sealed`, `inlineTextEdit.lifecycle`, `useInlineTextEdit` and `useInlineTextEditing.sealed` tests: 124/124, 3 runs. `packages/studio` `tsc --noEmit` clean; `oxlint`, `oxfmt` and the comment ratchet clean.
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed: nothing changes on screen until a host registers; the real-app proof (both modes, origin `null` in-run) comes with the host relay.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Inert until a host registers a handler: no UI, CSS or rendering change.

title: fix(parsers): css parsing ignores source-map comments in the stylesheet
body:
## What

Parsing a project's CSS no longer follows a `sourceMappingURL` comment in it. Every postcss parse of project CSS now goes through one helper, `parseCss` from the new `@hyperframes/parsers/postcss` entry. The helper passes `map: false`, so postcss never looks for a previous source map. That covers lint, the compiler, font handling, Studio's source edits and the inspector. oxlint refuses a direct `postcss.parse` (or an imported `parse`) anywhere else, as it already does for `linkedom`.

## Why

`postcss.parse(css)` with no options reads the last `sourceMappingURL` comment in the text and tries to load the map it names. Inside postcss 8.5.8 to 8.5.14, which the declared `^8.5.8` range allows, it checks the named path with `existsSync` and reads it with `readFileSync`. 8.5.8 reads any path, and 8.5.14 any path ending in `.map`. Project CSS comes from the project, so a comment in a stylesheet or an inline `style` attribute decided which path lint, render or Studio opened, synchronously, when that project was linted or opened.

## Related work

Mirrors `@hyperframes/parsers/linkedom` and its `no-restricted-imports` rule in `.oxlintrc.json`.

## How

- `packages/parsers/src/postcss.ts`: `parseCss(css)` is `postcss.parse(css, { map: false })`. It is exported as `@hyperframes/parsers/postcss` (exports synced with `scripts/package-subpaths.mjs`, plus the tsup entry). `postcss` becomes a dependency of `@hyperframes/parsers`, at the range the other packages use.
- The 13 call sites switch to it: lint `styleRoots.ts`, `rules/layers.ts`, `rules/core.ts`, `project.ts` (2); core `compositionScoping.ts` (2), `svgIdNamespacing.ts`, `authoredGoogleFonts.ts`, `deterministicFonts.ts`; studio-server `sourceMutation.ts` (2); inspector `sources.ts`. No call site passed `from` or map options, so the parsed trees and their output are the same.
- `.oxlintrc.json`: `postcss.parse` and `import { parse } from "postcss"` are refused in `packages/*/src` outside the helper and tests.
- `map: false` makes postcss skip the source-map lookup in every release from 8.5.8 (checked in the 8.5.8, 8.5.14 and 8.5.28 sources).

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated:
  - `packages/lint/src/cssSourceMapComments.test.ts`: lints a page whose 3D-transform inline style, transition inline style and `<style>` block each end in a `sourceMappingURL` comment. It also lints a project whose linked stylesheet ends in one. It spies on postcss's previous-map lookup and expects no call. The page still gets its `three_d_layer_far_larger_than_stage` finding.
  - `packages/parsers/src/postcss.test.ts`: `parseCss` keeps no map from an inline `data:` comment where plain `postcss.parse` does, and prints the same CSS.
- fails without the fix: on main, the lint test fails with `expected "loadAnnotation" to not be called at all, but actually been called 3 times` (11 times for the project). With `{ map: false }` removed from `parseCss`, both new files fail the same way.
- Against postcss 8.5.8, with each comment naming its own absolute `.map` path, `strace -e trace=%file` showed lint calling `access()` on the 3D-style, transition-style and style-block paths on main. With this change it made no file call naming those paths. Both runs loaded only 8.5.8.
- With the change:
  - The new tests pass 3 runs in a row.
  - The full lint suite passes, 1373/1373.
  - core `compositionScoping*`, `svgIdNamespacing` and `fonts/` pass, 454/454.
  - studio-server `sourceMutation*` and `lightEntries` pass, 207/207.
  - `tsc --noEmit` is clean in parsers, lint, core, studio-server and inspector.
  - `oxlint` and `oxfmt` are clean on the changed files, and a scratch file with both refused forms gets 2 errors.
  - `check:package-subpaths`, `check:workspace-contracts`, `check:package-cycles` and `bun install --frozen-lockfile` pass.
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Parsing and lint config only; no .tsx, .css or .html changed. Lint findings and compiled output for ordinary CSS are unchanged.

title: fix(studio): a timeline clip loads media only from its own project's files
body:
## What

The timeline's clip pictures (image strips, video filmstrips, audio waveforms and peaks) and its duration probe now load a clip's media only from that project's own preview files, or from an external `http(s)`, `data:` or `blob:` URL. A clip `src` that names another Studio API route, another project's files, or a path that climbs out of the project (`..`, also percent-encoded) loads nothing. A composition clip whose `compositionSrc` climbs out gets no composition thumbnail. Query options on a same-origin `src` are dropped: the preview route's options are Studio's to add.

## Why

A clip's `src` comes from the preview page (the runtime's clip manifest). `resolveMediaPreviewUrl` handed a same-origin `/api/...` URL back unchanged and kept `..` segments, so the timeline could ask any Studio API route for a clip's picture, for example a thumbnail capture, a waveform or a lint run in another project, as soon as the timeline drew.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `resolveMediaPreviewUrl` is the one place every timeline media URL is built (`useRenderClipContent`, `clipPeakMap`, `clipMenuNormalize`, `mediaProbe`, the asset panel). It now always returns a file on `/api/projects/<this id>/preview/` (rebuilt from the decoded path, hash kept, query dropped), passes external `http(s)`/`data:`/`blob:` through as before, and returns `""` for anything else.
- `climbsOut` is the one check for a `..` segment; `normalizeCompositionSrc` uses it too, since a composition clip's thumbnail URL is built from `compositionSrc` (`/preview/comp/<src>` becomes `/thumbnail/<src>`), so `../../<other id>/...` reached another project's thumbnail route.
- The two places that start a load skip an empty result: `useRenderClipContent` (no image, filmstrip or waveform element) and `probeMissingSourceDurations` (no probe). Peaks and loudness already treated a non-preview URL as "not project media".
- Behaviour change: a same-origin URL already on this project's preview route now comes back as a root-relative path instead of the absolute URL. Same file.

## No visible change

Ordinary project media shows the same thumbnails, filmstrips and waveforms. Only a clip whose `src` points outside its project's files, which had no picture of its own to show, now loads nothing.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

- `thumbnailUtils.test.ts`: another API route, another project, a server-wide route, encoded and plain climbs, rooted climb load nothing; a canonical preview URL keeps its file and hash; host-only query options are dropped.
- `useRenderClipContent.test.ts`: an `img`, `video` and `audio` clip whose `src` names another route, another project or a climb creates no image, filmstrip or waveform element; a composition clip whose `compositionSrc` climbs out yields no URL with a `..` segment.
- `mediaProbe.test.ts`: such clips are never probed.
fails without the fix: `packages/studio/src/player/components/thumbnailUtils.test.ts` and `packages/studio/src/hooks/useRenderClipContent.test.ts` ("loads nothing for another API route", "asks for no media of a img clip whose src names a route outside the project's files"): all 12 new resolver and clip-content cases fail on `origin/main` (e.g. `expected 'http://localhost:5190/api/media/clip.…' to be ''`). Removing the clip-content guard fails the `img`/`video` cases, removing the audio guard fails the `audio` case, removing the probe guard fails the probe case, removing the composition check fails the composition case.
- Ran: the touched modules' and every caller's test files (16 files, 143 tests), the full studio suite, `tsc --noEmit` for studio, `oxfmt` and `oxlint` on the changed files.

title: fix(studio-server): cached waveform and preview reads never hold the server's thread
body:
## What

Studio's cache reads on a request path now run on libuv's thread pool instead of the server's thread:

- `readProjectCacheFileAsync` (in `helpers/safePath.ts`, beside the existing `isLinkFreeWithinProjectAsync`) does what `readProjectCacheFile` does, with the same checks: no link on the way down from the project root, opened without following a link, a plain file with one name, under the size cap, and on platforms without `O_NOFOLLOW` the name still being that file. Every check, open and read is async.
- The waveform and peaks routes read their cached peaks through it (`readCachedPeaks` is async), and stat the media with `fs/promises`. Touching a cache entry as used (`markWaveformCacheUsed`) is async too.
- The thumbnail route reads a cached thumbnail through it.
- A kept preview document (`createPreviewDocumentStore().read`) reads through it. `PreviewDocumentStore.read` may now return a promise; the preview route awaits it.

The CLI keeps the sync `readProjectCacheFile` (its commands run outside any server).

## Why

Studio's API runs in-process in the Desktop app, so a sync read on a request path holds the app's main thread. On a project folder whose disk stopped answering, `GET /projects/:id/waveform/*` held a Windows app's main thread inside the sync cache read until the person force-quit it.

## Related work

Still sync on Studio's request paths, as follow-ups: cache writes (`writeWaveformCache`, the preview document write, thumbnail writes), the proxy copy index (`readCopyIndex` in the transcode path), and the file-save route's backup, read and replace.

## How

`readProjectCacheFileAsync` opens with the same `O_RDONLY | O_NOFOLLOW | O_NONBLOCK` flags and reads through the `FileHandle`; any failure is a cache miss, as before. The callers only add `await`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

New `packages/studio-server/src/routes/cacheReadStall.test.ts`: every call inside the project folder, sync or async, waits 120 ms while a 5 ms interval counts; each stall must see at least one count.

fails without the fix: `packages/studio-server/src/routes/cacheReadStall.test.ts` "serving a cached waveform keeps the thread running while each read waits on the disk" (on main: 4 of 4 stalls held the thread) and "reading a kept preview document keeps the thread running while each read waits on the disk" (3 of 3). Both green with the fix, 3 runs in a row; the link and size checks keep their existing tests (`waveform.test.ts`, `previewDocumentStore.test.ts`).

Ran on Linux: `packages/studio-server` vitest, 2661 passed; the 1 failure, `mediaExtensions.test.ts` "still reads clip.ts" (real ffprobe), fails the same way on main. `tsc --noEmit` clean; pre-commit (format, lint, fallow, typecheck) clean.

Timing on a healthy disk, Linux box, main's `src` against this branch's, both loaded in one process and alternated pair by pair (400 pairs, first 20 dropped): a cached waveform request through the real route (4,000 peaks), and a kept preview document read (200 KB).

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| cached waveform request, p50 / p90 | 0.45 / 0.51 ms | 0.58 / 1.04 ms |
| kept preview read, p50 / p90 | 0.28 / 0.33 ms | 0.39 / 0.66 ms |

About 0.1 ms more per read: each async step is a thread-pool round trip. In exchange, a disk that stops answering holds that one request instead of the whole server thread.

Not run: Windows and macOS (CI covers them); a real stalled disk (the stall is a shim).

title: fix(studio): sealed previews start loading as fast as open ones
body:
## What

A sealed project preview (`sandbox-origin`) now starts loading at the same moment as an unsealed one, so its video shows about as fast.

- `primeFrameToken({ projectId, token })`, exported from `@hyperframes/studio`, lets a host that already holds a project's frame token hand it over as the project opens. The next sealed preview of that project loads under it without asking the token endpoint first. It is used once; another prime or `primeFrameToken(null)` replaces it, and a preview of any other project never uses it.
- The studio `Player` marks the sealed project preview it builds itself with a new player attribute, `src-carries-runtime`. With it, the player navigates the sealed frame by `src` right away, the outcome it already reached for such a page after reading it first.

## Why

Opening a project with the sealed preview showed its first video frame about 170 ms later than with the open preview. From navigation to the decoded frame both modes took the same time. The whole gap came before the sealed frame started to navigate, from two steps that each waited on the network:

1. The `Player` waited for the frame-token request before it created the player. The answer came back early, but turning it into a value (`fetch`, then `res.json()`, then `.then`) needs several main-thread turns, and the opening project's first render (well over 100 ms of main-thread work in both modes) took those turns. So the sealed player was created after that render; the open one is created before it.
2. The player then fetched the whole page itself to decide how to show it, and for a page that already carries the runtime it then set `src`, so the page was fetched twice, also behind that render.

Starting the token request earlier does not help: any promise that has to settle waits behind the same render. The token has to arrive as a plain value, and the opened app already has it.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `frameToken.ts`: one primed slot. `previewUnderFrameToken` takes it when it names the preview's project and clears it either way. With a primed token it returns at once and checks the token in the background: if the endpoint now answers a different token, `onStale` gets the path under the current one and the `Player` loads the preview again under it, so a stale token never leaves the preview refused.
- The token goes nowhere new. Today the page already receives it from the token endpoint: [`fetchFrameToken`](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/8cb53b8fd57d8eedd33d3d5dcb2ca5c0ed6ac5ae/packages/studio/src/player/lib/frameToken.ts#L5-L12) reads it from [`GET /projects/:id/frame-token`](https://github.com/heygen-com/hyperframes/blob/8cb53b8fd57d8eedd33d3d5dcb2ca5c0ed6ac5ae/packages/studio-server/src/createStudioApi.ts#L212-L218) and puts it in the frame's own URL. Priming hands the same value to the same place; it is not passed into the frame any other way and not logged.
- `hyperframes-player.ts`: `_loadSrc` skips `_showSealedSrc` only when the frame is sealed, the `src` is on the page's own site, and `src-carries-runtime` is set. It then writes `src` with `read: true`. The sandbox is applied before `src` is written either way. Without the attribute nothing changes: the read, the own-policy path (pages that send their own CSP or X-Frame-Options), the unreadable path and the runtime-less `srcdoc` path all run as before, so no page loads twice.
- `Player.tsx` sets the attribute only where it builds the project preview URL itself: the Studio server puts the runtime in every project preview it serves. A `directUrl` may be any page and gets no attribute. A wrong hint fails loudly: a vouched page that never brings the runtime ends in the player's `error` event at the load limit, like any composition that never boots.

## Before

![Before: open and sealed preview, 8 opens each](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/57e62229-a8b0-43c3-a6c4-7c3c00463cc8)

## After

![After: open and sealed preview, 8 opens each](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ced531f-a485-4adb-869c-c9d23a67dff8)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

fails without the fix:
- `packages/studio/src/player/lib/frameToken.test.ts` "loads a primed project's preview under its token without waiting for the token endpoint" (times out when the prime is ignored), "never loads one project's preview under another project's primed token" (fails when the project check is removed), and "hands back the path under the current token when a primed one is stale" (fails when the background check is removed).
- `packages/studio/src/player/components/Player.test.ts` "loads a sealed preview again under the current token when the primed one is stale" (fails when the reload is removed, and when a later "Retry preview" builds from the stale path) and "vouches that the sealed project preview it builds carries the runtime".
- `packages/player/src/hyperframes-player.test.ts` "loads a src its host vouches for at once, sealed before it navigates, without reading it".

Also added, passing before and after, to pin what must not change: without the attribute, the own-policy, unreadable and runtime-less paths; a vouched page without the runtime ends in an `error` event; a primed token is used once and dropped by `primeFrameToken(null)`.

- `packages/studio`: 9869 passed, 1 skipped. `packages/player`: 761/761, 3 runs in a row. Both `tsc --noEmit` clean; oxlint, oxfmt and the commit hooks clean.
- Timing (the charts above): an M-series Mac with a real GPU, a desktop app built from these packages that primes the token as a project opens, measured from the click that opens a project with one 640x360 video clip to the clip's centre being lit with the clip decoded in the frame. 8 fresh launches per arm, order swapped each round; the "before" run uses the same app and probe without these changes.

| | open preview | sealed preview |
|---|---|---|
| before | 673.5 ms median | 843.5 ms median (+170) |
| after | 650.5 ms median | 719.5 ms median (+69) |

After the change the sealed player is created and navigates within a few ms of the open one (both at about 270-290 ms after the click). The frame reports `origin` `null` in every sealed run.

title: feat(parsers): export the size the renderer compiles a composition at
body:
## What

`@hyperframes/parsers` exports `renderedCompositionSize(html)` and `compositionRootSize(root)`: the size the renderer compiles a composition at. The producer's HTML compiler now calls `compositionRootSize` instead of its own inline rule, so there is one owner of that rule.

## Why

An app that picks an output size (`--resolution`) has to know the composition's shape the way the renderer reads it. The renderer reads the first `[data-composition-id]` root's `data-width` and `data-height` with `parseInt`, and defaults each side to 1080×1920 when it is unset, or when there is no root. An app that reads the size its own way can disagree on a root with no declared size. Example: it treats that root as having no size and falls back to landscape, while the renderer compiles it portrait. It then asks for `landscape`, and the render refuses with "outputResolution landscape (1920×1080) does not match the aspect ratio of the composition (1080×1920)" after setup. Reading the renderer's own rule from the package closes that gap.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `packages/parsers/src/compositionSize.ts`: `compositionRootSize(root)` is the compiler's rule moved as is. `renderedCompositionSize(html)` parses with the package's own linkedom entry and queries the root the way the compiler does, so a scene kept in a `<template>` ahead of the root is skipped.
- `packages/parsers/src/index.ts`: exports both from the main entry, next to `compositionDuration`. The main entry already exports modules built on linkedom.
- `packages/producer/src/services/htmlCompiler.ts`: `const { width, height } = compositionRootSize(rootEl)` replaces the two inline lines. Same behaviour.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `compositionSize.test.ts` fails on main, because the module it imports doesn't exist there. This is a new export, not a behaviour change; the compiler tests below pin that the compiler's sizes stay the same.
- [x] Unit tests added: `compositionSize.test.ts` covers a declared size, a root with no size and no root (1080×1920), each side defaulting on its own, and a `<template>` scene ahead of the root. 4/4 pass.
- [x] Producer compiler tests unchanged and green: `htmlCompiler*.test.ts` 136/136 (vitest) and 223/223 (bun test).
- [x] `tsc --noEmit` clean for `@hyperframes/parsers`; no producer type errors in the touched files. The pre-commit typecheck, lint, format and fallow audit passed, as did `check:package-cycles`.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: no render was run; the compiler's values are unchanged by construction.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

Refs #4274 (removed low-use catalog items and theme variants; most of the catalog pairs above come from it).

Only dark code-snippet blocks remain, so the four editor-theme variants (including the light one) go to `code-snippet-dark-modern`, and the eight Apple Terminal themes go to `code-snippet-apple-terminal-pro`.

Redirecting those to an unrelated page would be a soft 404.

## Test plan

title: feat(core): a frame-presented wait can be asked to run longer, up to 15 s
body:
## What

`frame-presented` takes an optional `{ waitMs }` (a finite number, more than 0 and at most 15 000). The frame waits up to that long before answering `presented: false`, instead of its fixed 4 s. The editing client's timeout for that request follows `waitMs` plus one second, unless the caller passes its own `timeoutMs`. With no params, nothing changes.

## Why

A host that times seeks gives a seek up to its own limit before calling it lost. One that waits 10 s for an open preview's frame got a sealed frame's answer at 4 s, so a sealed seek taking 4 to 10 s counted as never shown while the same open seek counted as slow. Those slow seeks are what such a meter is for. With `waitMs`, a host can ask a sealed frame to wait exactly as long as it waits for an open one.

## Related work

Refs #8933, which added `frame-presented` with the fixed deadline.

## How

- `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.ts`: `parseFramePresented` accepts `{}` or exactly `{ waitMs }` within bounds; anything else is `invalid-params`, as before. An older frame refuses `{ waitMs }` the same clean way, so a host can ask again without it. `clientWaitPastFrameDeadline` sets that request's client timeout to `waitMs + 1 s`.
- `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.ts`: `waitForFramePresented` uses `waitMs` as its deadline, else the existing `EDITING_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS - 1 s`. Cleanup on settle, expiry and dispose is unchanged.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.test.ts` ("waits as long as it is asked to, so a 6 s seek still presents") and `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.test.ts` ("takes a frame-presented wait only as a bounded number of ms", "waits for a frame-presented answer as long as the frame was asked to wait, then a second more") all fail against main's source.
- `editingPort`, `editingAgent` and `playbackHealth` tests: 230/230, 3 runs; core `tsc --noEmit`, `oxlint` and the comment ratchet clean.
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed: no visible change; the host's sealed vs open seek proof comes with its consumer.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Core runtime and editing-port client only (`.ts`, no UI, CSS or rendering).

title: feat(studio): prototype sealed canvas keys acted on only right after a real click or key
body:
**Prototype: do not merge until the sealed-preview timing check passes and the approach is chosen.**

## What

In a sealed (opaque-origin) preview, Studio acts on the frame's Delete, nudge and forwarded shortcut reports only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key (`navigator.userActivation.isActive`). Keyboard focus and in-frame drawing are unchanged.

## Why

The frame reports the keys it receives, and Studio can't verify a report on its own side. Page script in the frame can't set the top page's activation, but a real click or keypress in the frame does. Checked in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit: a real click or keydown in a sandboxed frame activates the top page for 5 s. A keydown made by the frame's script never does. Drawing stays in the frame as before, so no extra hop is added before the paint.

## How

- `canvasActionRoute` hands a frame's Delete or nudge to its session only while the top page is active. A Delete outside that window takes the existing roll-back path, as an unknown arm already does.
- `forwardSealedKeys` re-dispatches a forwarded key only while the top page is active.
- A browser without `navigator.userActivation` fails closed: frame reports are not acted on.

## No visible change

Delete and arrow nudges look and save as before when the person presses the key.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key".
- [x] fails without the fix: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key" fails when the activation check always passes (the frame's Delete is saved and stays removed).
- [x] The sealed-canvas suite (10 tests) passes 3 runs in a row. Studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] Timing check, four browsers, sealed vs open.

title: fix(studio): a sealed canvas drag keeps its drop when the keyboard moves into the frame
body:
## What

In a sealed (opaque-origin) preview, a drag on the canvas keeps its drop again. Before this, the dragged element snapped back to where it started, the selection disappeared, and the next drag did nothing.

## Why

After a press on the canvas, sealed canvas keys move keyboard focus into the preview frame when the press is released. That ran in a capture listener on Studio's window, before the overlay's own release handler had committed the drag. Focus entering the frame fires `blur` on Studio's window, and `useHeldGestureCancel` cancels any gesture still held on blur. So the drag was cancelled just before its drop: the drafts were restored and the selection cleared.

## How

`useSealedCanvasKeys` moves focus into the frame in a task queued on release, after the release's own handlers have run. By then the drag has dropped and nothing is held for the blur to cancel. The same conditions are checked when it runs, plus that no new press has started. The queued focus is cleared when the hook unmounts.

## Before

Stock Chrome, sealed preview: after the drop the box is back at its start and nothing is selected.

![before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ecb6df20-f129-444d-b713-e1e500d3990d)

## After

The box stays where it was dropped, still selected, and the next drag moves it again.

![after](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3e926b2-094b-43d6-9429-279efdf9a1c4)

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "lets a drag released on the canvas finish before the keyboard moves into the frame". As a browser does, focus entering the frame blurs Studio's window, and the test checks that the canvas release runs before that blur.
- [x] fails without the fix: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "lets a drag released on the canvas finish before the keyboard moves into the frame" fails on `main` (the blur lands before the drop).
- [x] The sealed-canvas suite (10 tests) passes 3 runs in a row. Studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [x] Real browser, stock Chrome, sealed preview, two drags with real pointer input on a private display. On `main`, the first drop snaps back, 0 selection boxes remain, and the second drag starts nothing. With this change, the second drag starts where the first dropped (x 446 to 686), with 1 box. That held 3 runs out of 3.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(studio-server): finding a video's preview copy never holds the server's thread
body:
## What

Finding a video's preview copy no longer runs file calls on the server's thread. Stacked on #8971, which did the same for cached waveforms, thumbnails and kept preview documents.

- `getProxyCachePath`, `proxyCopyProgress`, `retryProxyCopy`, `proxyActivityMark`, `resolveStill` and the lookup at the start of `resolveProxy` are async. That covers the project folder's real path, the source's `stat` for its copy key (`fastCopyKey`), the copy's `lstat` check (`isProjectCacheFileAsync`), and the index that names an earlier copy of the same bytes (`readCopyIndex`).
- `readCopyIndex` reads through `readProjectCacheFileAsync`. That was the last caller of the sync `readProjectCacheFile`, so the sync reader is deleted and no new caller can come back to it. The CLI's undo backup read uses the async reader too.
- Asks for one project still reach the copy queue in the order they were made (`reachQueueInAskOrder`), though their lookups now finish in any order. A project whose disk stops answering holds only its own later asks.
- Marking a copy as just used (`utimes`) no longer waits.

Breaking for hosts: `getProxyCachePath` returns a promise. The CLI's caller is updated here; a host that calls it (Desktop) awaits it when it takes this release.

## Why

Studio's API runs in the Desktop app's main process, so a sync file call on a request path holds the whole app while a disk does not answer. On macOS, a sync read of a preview-copy index held a person's app until they force-quit it. The lookup in front of that read (`realpath`, `stat`, `lstat`) was sync too, so making only the read async would have moved the freeze one call earlier.

## Related work

Refs #8971 (stacked on it).

Still sync, as the next change: proxy cache maintenance (`maintainProxyCache` walks the cache folder after a copy is served) and the transcode job's own calls (content key, pieces, renames).

## How

The lookup is `lookUpCopy`: real path, copy key, the copy's check, then the index, all through `fs/promises`. `resolveProxy` awaits it through a per-project chain, so the synchronous part from the queue check onward runs in ask order, as before.

Test harness: the proxy tests advanced the module with microtask flushes, which a real file call never answers within. `flush()` now also waits while Node reports a file request in flight (`process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`), using the real `setImmediate` taken before any test fakes the clock. Two queue tests now name each copy instead of relying on the order ffmpeg started in for copies that already hold slots, which has no meaning for users.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

fails without the fix: `packages/studio-server/src/routes/cacheReadStall.test.ts` "finding a video's preview copy keeps the thread running while each read waits on the disk". Every file call inside the project waits 120 ms while a 5 ms interval counts. On #8971's head, 8 of the lookup's stalls held the thread; with this change none do. Green 3 runs in a row.

Ran on Linux: the named tests 3 runs each, then the covering tests once: 39 files in cli, 5 in core, 61 in studio-server, all green. `tsc` clean in cli and studio-server; Fallow audit and pre-push clean. `proxyTranscoder.test.ts` and the stall test also 6 runs in a row green.

Timing on a healthy disk, Linux box: finding a copy through its index (`getProxyCachePath`), #8971's head against this branch, both loaded in one process and alternated pair by pair (400 pairs, first 20 dropped).

| | before | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| finding a copy through its index, p50 / p90 | 0.04 / 0.05 ms | 0.12 / 0.18 ms |

About 0.09 ms more per lookup: each of its file calls is now a thread-pool round trip. In exchange, a disk that stops answering holds that one request (and that project's later asks), never the server's thread.

Not run: Windows and macOS (CI covers them); a real stalled disk (the stall is a shim).

title: fix(studio): a preview reload the server answered busy asks again after its Retry-After
body:
## What changed

When the preview server answers a reload's page with **503 and a Retry-After**, Studio now asks for the page again after that wait, up to three times, and keeps the current preview on screen meanwhile. Before, the refused page was shown as the new preview: a blank stage and a "1 error" dialog, until the next edit.

A 503 means "busy right now, ask again". The refused-frame page studio-server sends for it carries the runtime script, so Studio's shadow reload found a runtime with a 0 s timeline and promoted that page. Where the runtime did not run in it, the reload waited out its budget and gave up. Either way the reload was never tried again.

**Server**
- `helpers/previewErrorPage.ts`: the refused-frame page also sets `window.__hfPreviewRetryAfter` to the server's Retry-After in whole seconds. `retryAfterSeconds` reads the header; an HTTP date or anything else counts as none.
- `createStudioApi.ts`: `answerRefusedFrameWithPage` passes the refused response's Retry-After to that page. Every refused iframe load goes through this wrapper. The other two `previewRefusalPage` callers in `routes/preview.ts` answer 200, not 503.
- `routes/preview.ts` + `helpers/subCompositionBuild.ts`: a `/preview/comp/*` build refused at its deadline while it was still **queued** behind another build answers `Retry-After: 5`, the same value the file's other busy answers use. A build that ran out its own time gets no Retry-After: `runOffThread` throws that build away and replaces the worker, so asking again would only start it over.
- `core/src/studioPreviewMark.ts`: `STUDIO_PREVIEW_RETRY_AFTER`, the name of the window field.

**Studio**
- `player/hooks/refusedPreviewPage.ts` (new): reads a shadow frame's refused-page message and its Retry-After.
- `useShadowPreviewReload.ts`: when the shadow frame loads a refused page, the reload fails at once with that page's own message, instead of probing it as a film. `failShadow` hands the page's Retry-After to the retry. While a busy page is being asked again, its failure is logged as a warning and not reported; only the last refusal is.
- `useShadowReloadRetry.ts`: a 503 that carries a Retry-After is asked again after it (at least 1 s, at most 30 s), up to `BUSY_PAGE_RETRIES` (3) times. A 503 with no Retry-After and any 4xx are not asked again. The count resets on a reload of the user's own. A newer reload, a composition switch or an unmount cancels a pending re-ask, as for the existing timeout retry. That retry is unchanged.

The scene swap path needs no change: when its fetch gets a non-ok answer it falls back to the full shadow reload (`useTimelinePlayer.ts`, `swapFreshly(..., reloadWholeFilm)`).

## Before

Studio from source on `main`. After an edit on disk, the server answers the reload's page 503 with `Retry-After: 2` for 1.5 s. The refused page replaces the preview: blank stage, error dialog, and the edit never shows (12 s watched).

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ccdc8e1d-d3c0-4f70-8b4f-eee23534ce34)

## After

Same project, same edit, same 1.5 s of 503s, with this branch. The old preview stays up, the page is asked again after 2 s, and the edit shows 2.4 s after it was saved. No error dialog or failure toast.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40a5c347-3ec7-4133-b889-b56044eb9463)

Both runs use the same Playwright script. It edits the project's `index.html` and fulfils the preview page request with status 503, `Retry-After: 2`, and the body that the tree's own `previewErrorPage` builds (so `main`'s page has no Retry-After field). Studio's own `[hf-reload]` log for the After run shows `shadow-failed` with "The preview page could not be loaded (HTTP 503).", then the edit.

## What I measured

- **Fails without the fix**
  - At `d507f92a`, with the new tests: the client cases "does not ask again when the server did not say when to" and "waits at least a second when the server's Retry-After is 0" fail. So does the server case "refused while it waited behind another build says when to ask again; one that ran out its own time does not" (`retry-after` was null).
  - At `210883e0`, the refused-page tests through the frame's load fail 4 of 4: the page with a runtime was promoted, and no re-ask was scheduled.
  - With the failure still reported while asking again, "asks for the page again after the server's Retry-After, a bounded number of times" fails (`onPreviewReloadFailed` called after the first refusal).
- **With the fix:** these pass 85/85, 3 runs in a row on a Linux devbox:
  - `useTimelinePlayer.shadowRetry`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.reloadStill`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.reloadedTimeline`
  - `NLEPreview.slowBoot`

  On the server, `preview.compDeadline`, `subCompositionBuild.queue`, `preview.scanDeadline`, `previewErrorPage` and `preview.sandbox` pass 82/82, 3 runs in a row. lefthook pre-commit (filesize, format, lint, fallow, typecheck) is green.
- The bounded case checks timing as well as count: no new shadow at 4,999 ms after a `Retry-After: 5` refusal, one at 5,000 ms. After the third retry is refused again, nothing loads in the next 60 s, and the failure is reported once.
- The queued-deadline server test blocks the build worker with a direct `runOffThread` job, so the refused page is the one that waited, not one that ran.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A real server that is busy during a live reload. The captures inject the 503 at the network with each tree's own refused page, and the server's own answers are covered by its route and helper tests.
- A sealed (opaque-origin) preview frame. Its window can't be read, so it carries no Retry-After and is not asked again.
- macOS and Windows. The captures are headless Chrome on Linux.

## Searched first

`git grep -i "retry-after\|retryAfter" -- packages/studio/src packages/player/src packages/core/src`: Studio and the player had no Retry-After handling, and `useShadowReloadRetry` was the one retry owner, so the busy case joins it there. Core has two private Retry-After parsers, `retryAfterMs` in `figma/client.ts` and `fonts/deterministicFonts.ts`. Neither is exported, and core has no shared HTTP helper, so studio-server has its own small `retryAfterSeconds`. It reads whole seconds only, because the value goes into the page's script. A follow-up can move all three onto one core helper.

title: fix(share): wait for the host's export lookup, so a host can read its disk off its main thread
body:
## What

`@hyperframes/share` now waits for the host's `latestExportFile(dir)`. A host can answer with the export record or with a promise of it; a plain value works as before.

## Why

Share called `latestExportFile` without waiting. A host whose lookup has to touch the disk (resolve the export's real path, list its renders folder) therefore had to do that synchronously. On a drive that stops answering (an external disk asleep or unplugged, a network share that dropped), a synchronous file call never returns, and an app whose main thread makes it stays frozen until it is killed. With the lookup awaited, a host can read the disk asynchronously and give up after a bound.

## Related work

None in this repository. The host-side change, which binds an asynchronous lookup, follows once this is released.

## How

- `src/hosts.d.ts`: `latestExportFile` returns the record, `null`, or a promise of either.
- `src/reviewExport.mjs`: the four places that call it now `await` it. Two of them were synchronous helpers, so they and their callers became async:
  - `exportKeyOf` and `sourceOf` are async.
  - `bindRenderKey` is async, and `sendVersion` awaits it.
  - `reviewVersion` reads the source and the export key together (`Promise.all`).
  - The failure records in `addVersion` and `settleSavedExport` await the key.
  - `versionFacts` awaits the source.

  Nothing else changes: the same lookups run in the same order, and every caller was already async.
- `README.md`: notes the promise form.
- The CLI host (`packages/cli/src/share/host.ts`) keeps its synchronous lookup, which the widened type still accepts.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated. fails without the fix: `tests/asyncExportLookup.test.mjs` "a host whose export lookup answers later still offers its MP4 as ready". It binds a lookup that returns a promise. Before this change `reviewVersion` read the promise as an export with no path and answered `source: "not-mp4"` ("export an MP4 first"). Now it answers `"ready"`.
- [x] `packages/share`: 204 of 204 tests pass, 3 runs in a row. `tsc --noEmit` passes. The CLI type-checks with no errors that involve Share.
- [ ] Manual testing performed: no host binds an asynchronous lookup yet. That comes in the host's own change.
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable): README.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(lint): css_parse_error quotes the parser only for CSS syntax errors
body:
## What

`css_parse_error` now quotes the parser's message only when it is a CSS syntax error (`postcss.CssSyntaxError`), which is what the finding's fix hint is about. Any other error thrown while a style block is read gives the fixed message "CSS parse error: this style block could not be read." and none of that error's own text. The finding, its code, severity, location and fix hint are unchanged.

## Why

Lint findings go back to whoever asked for the lint, often over HTTP. A syntax error's message describes the CSS the caller sent. Any other error's message comes from somewhere else, such as a file read, and the caller should not see it.

## How

One condition in `packages/lint/src/rules/core.ts`, where the finding is built. It uses the same class test the rule already uses to choose the reported line. The other places that echo an error (`invalid_composition_variables_declaration`, `invalid_variable_values_json`, the import map and script checks) quote `JSON.parse` or the script parser on the page's own text, so they are left as they are.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/lint/src/rules/core.cssParseError.test.ts`, test "carries none of the text of any other error thrown while the block is read". `parseCss` is mocked to throw an error naming a file for one block. Before the fix, the finding's message is `CSS parse error: ENOENT: no such file…`.
- With the fix:
  - That file passes 2 of 2, 3 runs in a row. Its other test checks that a real syntax error still names "Missed semicolon".
  - `packages/lint/src/rules/core.test.ts` passes 200 of 200.
- Not run: the full lint package suite; CI runs it.

title: fix(lint): catch inline media with MIME parameters and wrapped base64
body:
## What

`base64_media_prohibited` now reports two forms of inline media it used to miss:

- a data URI whose media type carries MIME parameters, such as `data:audio/webm;codecs=opus;base64,...`, which is what `FileReader.readAsDataURL` returns for a `MediaRecorder` blob;
- a base64 payload wrapped across lines, which is what GNU `base64` and Python's `base64.encodebytes` produce.

Chrome plays both, so the lint rule was passing them silently.

## Why

The old pattern required `;base64,` immediately after the media subtype and a payload with no whitespace. The issue has a minimal repro for each form.

## Related work

Fixes #6590.

#6593 and #7215 took the same route; both were closed before merging (one on a Windows CI failure, one after going stale). This is the fix rebased on current `main`, with the tests the rule never had.

## How

The rule now matches a `src` attribute's whole value against a data-URI pattern that allows MIME parameters before `;base64,` and ASCII whitespace in the payload. It strips that whitespace before the 20-character minimum, the entropy sample and the KB calculation, so a wrapped payload reports the same size as an unwrapped one. Non-media data URIs, short payloads and ordinary URLs are unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated — new cases cover plain audio/video, one and several MIME parameters, LF and CRLF wrapping, tabs/spaces/form feeds, single and double quotes, a quoted parameter, uppercase `DATA:`/`BASE64`, short and whitespace-only payloads, image and font data URIs, attribute-boundary cases, and a wrapped payload's size at the KB rounding boundary (2040 characters round to 1 KB; counting the 26 CRLFs would read 2092 and say 2 KB, so the case fails if the payload is sized before the whitespace is stripped).
- [x] Manual testing performed — the two examples from the issue each produce one finding, and the size shown for the wrapped example matches its unwrapped form.
- [x] Documentation updated — the `base64_media_prohibited` note in `docs/reference/lint-rules.mdx`.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and the fix says what the rule must do and how the old pattern missed it.

Commands run in `packages/lint`:

- `vitest run src/rules/media.test.ts` → 179 passed
- `vitest run` → 1399 passed (34 files)
- `tsc --noEmit` → clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files → clean
- `fallow audit --base HEAD --fail-on-issues` → pass (no introduced complexity, duplication or dead code)

title: fix(studio): empty sidebar tabs point new users at the next step
body:

A new project opens with an empty Assets tab and one composition (the root `index.html`). Both sidebar tabs now say what to do next and offer one action:

- **Assets**, when the project has no assets: "Drop media files here or choose files to get started" and a **Choose files** button that opens the existing file picker. It is only rendered when the tab can import.
- **Compositions**, when there are none: "No compositions yet: a composition is an HTML scene in your project" and **Browse starter scenes**, which activates the catalog panel.
- **Compositions**, when the root `index.html` is the only one (the normal fresh-project state): the card stays, with the same starter-scenes guidance underneath. Two or more compositions show no nudge.

Both actions are native buttons, so Tab + Enter/Space work without extra handlers.

## Why

The empty states were a dead end for a first-run user: "Drop media files here" had no action, and "No compositions found" was false for a new project (the root `index.html` is always there) and offered nothing. The issue asks for one sentence and one keyboard-accessible action per tab.

## Related work

Fixes #5589.

#5600 and #5862 took the same approach. #5600 was approved but closed for inactivity once the Before/After captures and signed commits were the only things left. This is a fresh implementation on current `main`, with the captures below.

## How

- `AssetsTab.tsx`: `EmptyState` takes an optional `onChooseFiles`. The tab passes a file-picker click only when `onImport` exists; the no-match search branch is unchanged.
- `CompositionsTab.tsx`: a small `StarterScenesNudge` renders the sentence and a native button that calls `useDockLayoutStore.getState().activatePanel("catalog")`. It replaces the zero-composition state and renders under the list at exactly one composition.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated — two new happy-dom files cover the Assets empty state with and without `onImport`, and the Compositions empty / one / two-plus states, including the real action (file input click, catalog activation) and native-button focusability.
- [x] Manual testing performed — built Studio and checked both tabs in Chrome against a fresh `hyperframes init` project; captures below.
- [ ] Documentation updated — not applicable; no command, flag or documented behavior changed.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what.

Commands run in `packages/studio`:

- `vitest run src/components/sidebar` → 12 files, 64 tests passed
- `tsc --noEmit` → clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the four files → clean
- `fallow audit --base HEAD --fail-on-issues` → pass. `AssetsTab` was already at its complexity ceiling, so the import check lives in `EmptyState` instead of adding a branch to `AssetsTab`.

![Assets before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erywim/hyperframes/pr-evidence/pr-5589/before-assets.png)

Compositions tab, fresh project: one card, no guidance.

![Compositions before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erywim/hyperframes/pr-evidence/pr-5589/before-compositions.png)

## After

![Assets after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/erywim/hyperframes/pr-evidence/pr-5589-final/after-assets.png)
