title: refactor(studio): one exported check that a preview frame's style value fits its property
body:
## What changed

Studio checks a preview frame's text colours before using them (`colourOnly` in `packages/studio/src/player/lib/previewChannel.ts`, through `CSS.supports("color", …)`). Apps built on Studio need the same check for other style values a frame reports (widths, border styles, background colours), and today they each write their own.

`frameStyleValue(name, value)` is now that one check, exported from `@hyperframes/studio`: it keeps `value` only when this window's style parser accepts it as a value of `name` (a detached element's `style.setProperty`), and returns null otherwise, including for non-strings. `colourOnly` is now `frameStyleValue("color", value)`.

In Chromium the colour behaviour is unchanged: `CSS.supports("color", v)` and `setProperty("color", v)` accept the same values. The parser check also works under happy-dom, so the frame-colour tests no longer stub `CSS.supports`.

no visual change: same colours accepted in the browser; only the check's home and reach changed.

## What I measured

- **fails without the fix:** with `previewChannel.ts` from `origin/main` and the stub removed, `previewChannel.frameColours.test.ts` goes 3/3 red (happy-dom's `CSS.supports` accepts any value): the caret test gets the `url(…)` colour, the selection test's JSON contains `url(`, and the new per-property test refuses nothing.
- With the change: `src/player/lib/previewChannel*` 48/48 pass, 3 shuffled runs in a row, exit 0.
- happy-dom's parser on the checked values: `rgb(1, 2, 3)`, `3px`, `currentcolor` kept; `url(/x)`, `red;background:url(/x)`, `dashed;color:red` and a `url()` width refused. It also refuses `oklch(…)`, which Chromium accepts, so tests use `rgb()`.
- `packages/studio` typecheck exit 0; `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on the changed files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- The Chromium browser test (`InlineTextToolbar.browser.test.ts`) runs in CI only.
- No consumer uses the export yet; a follow-up in the app that reads frame styles will switch to it and delete its own copy.

title: fix(cli): render --json reports success, cancel and typed failure codes
body:
## What

`render --json` now prints exactly one JSON object on stdout for every outcome:

- success: `{"ok":true,"outputPath":"...","durationMs":...,"renderTimeMs":...,"bytes":...}`
- cancel during a local render (SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP): `{"ok":false,"error":{"code":"cancelled","signal":"SIGINT","message":"..."}}`, still exit 1
- failure: the shared error envelope, with the cause-specific codes already on `main` (`chrome_not_found`, `ffmpeg_not_found`, `ffprobe_not_found`, `render_locked`, `node_version_unsupported`).

`--batch --json` still prints only its batch document. Runs without `--json` are unchanged.

## Why

A script or agent could not tell success, cancel and failure apart: success and cancel printed nothing, and every failure was `runtime_error` unless it came from a typed path. The issue spells out the three shapes and the codes.

## Related work

Fixes #7408.

The error-code half landed earlier on `main`: `CliRuntimeError` carries a code, preflight failures return the typed codes, `RenderLockBusy` returns `render_locked`, and `bin/hyperframes.mjs` prints the Node version envelope. This PR completes the remaining output and verifies the earlier half.

## How

- `utils/renderJsonResult.ts` builds the success object (path, stats, and `bytes` only when the output is a regular file) and the cancel object (signal derived from `render_cancelled_by_<signal>`), and writes one line.
- `executeHeldRender` prints the success object only for `--json` without `--batch`.
- The `render` command keeps the human `Render cancelled:` line on stderr, prints the cancel object under `--json`, then exits 1.
- The help text, `docs/packages/cli.mdx` and the `hyperframes docs rendering` page describe the three shapes.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated — the success and cancel body builders (file, directory and missing output; each signal; a non-signal cancellation), a single-render success object, no object without `--json`, no success object on failure, and `--batch --json` still printing only its document.
- [x] Manual testing performed — a real draft render of a 0.5 s 320×240 composition printed exactly one success object with the path, `durationMs`, `renderTimeMs` and `bytes`; a process test starts the cancellation fixture, sends SIGINT, SIGTERM and SIGHUP, and checks one cancel object, the signal, exit 1, the stderr line and no ANSI; the same fixture without `--json` keeps stdout empty.
- [x] Documentation updated — the `render --json` row and a short three-shape paragraph in `docs/packages/cli.mdx`; the `--json` bullet in `packages/cli/src/docs/rendering.md`, which `hyperframes docs rendering` prints; the command's `--json` help text matches.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what.

Commands run in `packages/cli`:

- `vitest run src/utils/renderJsonResult.test.ts src/commands/render.cancelJson.test.ts src/commands/render/execute.test.ts src/printedFailureText.wiring.test.ts src/utils/jsonError.test.ts src/commands/docs.test.ts` → 6 files, 57 tests passed
- `vitest run src/utils/renderJsonCancellation.process.test.ts` → 4 tests passed, three runs in a row
- `vitest run src/commands/render.test.ts` → 136 tests passed
- `vitest run src/utils/jsonError.test.ts src/browser/preflight.test.ts src/utils/renderLock.test.ts src/runtimeVersion.test.ts src/commands/docs.test.ts src/commands/docs.output.test.ts` → 78 tests passed, covering the typed codes that already landed
- `tsc --noEmit` → clean; `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` on the changed files → clean
- `fallow audit --base origin/main --fail-on-issues` → exit 0: 0 dead code, 0 complexity, 0 duplication. The one warning is the fixture's `// fallow-ignore-file unused-file`, the header every process fixture here carries.

title: test(cli): process tests on Windows start a fresh executable once before timing it
body:
## What

Two Windows process tests now start their freshly made executable once, before the call they time:

- `hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts` "a hung taskkill is ended within its limit": the node copy named `taskkill.exe` runs once with no hang script before the timed `taskkill` call.
- `timeline.e2e.test.ts`: one `bun run cli.ts timeline --help` in `beforeAll` before the 30 s spawns.

Both go through one new helper, `warmTestExecutable` in `processTestUtils.ts`. Test-only change.

## Why

Both tests failed on `windows-latest` in the merge queue on 2026-11-27, each time with nothing in the diff under test, and each removed a release PR from the queue:

- `hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts`: `ENOENT ... hf-taskkill-*\pid`. The stand-in writes its pid as the first thing it runs, so it never started before `TASKKILL_TIMEOUT_MS` (5 s) ended it. The call itself ended in time (the `< 10 s` check passed).
- `timeline.e2e.test.ts`: the first two spawns hit the 30 s `spawnSync` timeout (status `null`, 30157 ms and 30421 ms), and the next three spawns of the same command passed in about 0.7 s each.

In both, the first start of a program is what took the time, not the behaviour the test checks. A freshly copied 80+ MB exe is slower on its first start than on its second.

## How

`warmTestExecutable(file, args, options)` runs the program once with a 120 s cap and throws with its output if even that fails. Searched first: no existing warm-up helper in `packages/cli` (`rg -i 'warm' --glob '*.test.ts'` finds only the warm-check feature), and this is the only test that copies `process.execPath`.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: the two `windows-latest` merge-queue failures above. Neither is deterministic: the slow first start comes from the runner and its scanning of a new file, which a test cannot stand in for faithfully, so there is no committed red-first variant.
- First start vs second start of a freshly copied `node.exe` on a Windows 11 laptop (Defender plus vendor antivirus, idle): 599/209, 581/192, 573/192, 573/188 ms over 4 fresh copies.
- With the fix on Linux: `timeline.e2e.test.ts`, `hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts` (Windows-only, skipped) and `processTestUtils.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row (86 passed, 1 skipped). oxfmt clean.
- With the fix on that Windows laptop (Bun 1.4.4, Node 22): `hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts` and `timeline.e2e.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row (83 passed). Main's `hideChildConsoles.process.test.ts` also passed 3 of 3 there: an idle laptop starts the copy in time, so it does not reproduce the race. `timeline --help` there: 478 ms first start, 354 ms second, exit 0.
- [ ] `windows-latest` on this PR.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A loaded Windows runner reproducing either race on demand.
- Other Windows flakes seen in the same queue runs: a stuck Chrome launch in `gsapSoftReloadWait.browser.test.ts` and a Google Fonts fetch in `verify:catalog-payloads`. This PR does not touch them.

title: fix(studio): sealed canvas keys act only right after a real click or key
body:
## What

In a sealed (opaque-origin) preview, Studio acts on the frame's Delete, nudge and forwarded shortcut reports only right after a real click or keypress (`navigator.userActivation.isActive`). Keyboard focus and in-frame drawing are unchanged.

## Why

The frame reports the keys it receives, and Studio can't check a report on its own side: the page's own script runs in the frame too. Page script can't set the top page's activation, but a real click or keypress in the frame does. Checked in Chrome, Firefox and WebKit:
- A real click or keydown in a sandboxed frame activates the top page for 5 s.
- Holding a key down keeps it active for the whole hold (tested 9 s), then it expires 5 s after release.
- A keydown made by the frame's own script never activates it.

Drawing stays in the frame, so no extra hop comes before the paint.

## How

- `canvasActionRoute` hands a frame's Delete or nudge to its session only while the top page is active. A Delete outside that window takes the existing roll-back path, as an unknown arm already does.
- `forwardSealedKeys` re-dispatches a forwarded key only while the top page is active.
- A browser without `navigator.userActivation` fails closed: frame reports are not acted on.

## No visible change

Delete and arrow nudges look and save as before when the person presses the key.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit test added: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key".
- [x] fails without the fix: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key" fails when the activation check always passes (the frame's Delete is saved and stays removed).
- [x] The sealed-canvas suite (12 tests) passes 3 runs in a row. Studio `components/editor`, `hooks` and `player/lib` pass (4,820 tests). Studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [x] Timing, nudges alternated session by session against `main` at like load. Stock Chrome: 0 frames late for all 50 nudges, sealed and open. WebKit: sealed matches open, 1 frame late on 49 and 48 of 50, none 2 or more frames late.

title: fix(studio): escape from a sealed canvas reaches studio without a fresh click or key
body:
## What

In a sealed (opaque-origin) preview, a bare Escape from the frame still reaches Studio when the person hasn't clicked or pressed another key in the last few seconds. So Escape cancels or deselects as it does in the open preview.

## Why

#8992 makes Studio act on keys the frame forwards only while the top page has transient user activation. Browsers never give activation for Escape. So after 5 s with no other click or key, the frame's Escape stopped reaching Studio, and the selection stayed. Escape only cancels or deselects: no file write, history step or clipboard use. It's safe to take from the frame without a fresh press.

## Related work

Stacked on #8992. It needs to land before the next release, so no release ships with Escape ignored there.

## How

`forwardSealedKeys` re-dispatches a forwarded key while the top page is active, as before. It also re-dispatches a bare Escape (no Alt, Ctrl or Meta) when the page isn't active. Every other key still needs activation.

## No visible change

Compared with today's release, Escape works the same. This keeps #8992 from changing it.

## Test plan

- [x] Test extended: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key". With activation off, the frame's Space and Delete still do nothing, and its Escape now reaches Studio.
- [x] fails without the fix: `useSealedCanvasKeys.sealed.test.ts` > "acts on a frame's Delete or forwarded key only while the person has just clicked or pressed a key" fails on #8992's head (the forwarded keys are `[]`, not `["Escape"]`).
- [x] The sealed-canvas suite (12 tests) passes 3 runs in a row. Studio `components/editor`: 2,275 tests. Studio `tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments".

title: fix(studio): a Windows Chrome's version is read beside chrome.exe before asking PowerShell
body:
## What

On Windows, Studio reads Chrome's version from the entry next to `chrome.exe` before it starts PowerShell to ask for it:

- Chrome for Testing (Puppeteer's cache) keeps a `<version>.manifest` file there.
- An installed Chrome or Edge keeps a `<version>\` folder there.

When exactly one such version sits next to the executable, `browserVersion()` returns it without starting any process. With none, or two (as during a Chrome update), it asks PowerShell as before.

## Why

`browserVersion()` started `powershell.exe` with a 5 s cap on every call. On a busy Windows runner that start alone outlasted the cap: `vite.browserVersion.test.ts` "reads the selected real Windows Chrome version from metadata" failed in a merge-queue run on 2026-11-27 after 5331 ms, logging `chrome.exe (undefined)` for a Chrome that has its version on disk.

It matters outside tests too. `findSystemChrome()` uses this version to accept an installed Chrome (134 or newer). When PowerShell is slow on someone's Windows machine, the version comes back unknown and Studio skips a Chrome that would have worked.

## No visible change

This changes which file Studio reads to learn a Windows Chrome's version. No screen, layout or style changes.

## How

`versionBesideExecutable()` lists the folder `chrome.exe` is in and keeps the names that look like `a.b.c.d` or `a.b.c.d.manifest`. `browserVersion()` takes the folder lister as a fourth argument, defaulting to `readdirSync`, following `findSystemChrome()`'s `readDirectories`. The PowerShell path is unchanged.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: the two new `vite.browserVersion.test.ts` cases (a Chrome for Testing manifest and an installed version folder, with a PowerShell runner that throws) fail on main with `expected undefined to be 'Chrome/155.0.8059.39'`, 2 of 2. With the fix they pass, and the PowerShell runner is never called.
- A new case keeps PowerShell as the answer when two versions sit next to `chrome.exe`.
- Linux: `vite.browserVersion.test.ts`, `vite.browser.test.ts` and `tests/chromeTestUtils.test.ts` passed 3 runs in a row (30 passed, 1 skipped). oxfmt clean; the comment ratchet and citation checks pass.
- Windows 11 laptop, Puppeteer's Chrome 155.0.8059.39: `browserVersion()` takes 199-230 ms per call on main and 0-1 ms with the fix (5 calls each), same answer. The three test files passed 3 runs in a row there (31 passed). Main's real-Chrome test also passes on that idle laptop, so the laptop does not reproduce the runner's slow PowerShell start.
- [ ] `windows-latest` on this PR.

## What I did NOT exercise

- An installed Chrome on Windows: the laptop has Edge's `<version>\` folder, which the unit test covers, but no installed Google Chrome.
- macOS and Linux paths: unchanged (`--version`).

title: fix(studio): a preview reload waits while the server is still answering for its page
body:
## What changed

A preview reload no longer gives up while its frame is still waiting for the server to answer with the page. Before, Studio gave a reload three 15 s budgets (45 s), counted from the moment the reload began, whether or not the page had arrived. A page that takes longer to build than that (a big project, a slow machine) was given up on while it was still on its way. The one retry waited the same 45 s for an equally slow page and was given up too, so the edit never showed, under two "did not reload" messages.

Now the wait for the server's answer belongs to the server. The page build already has its own deadlines, and the server answers when one passes:

- studio-server's root preview passes run under `ROOT_PREVIEW_DEADLINE_MS` (120 s). When a build fails or passes it, `routes/preview.ts` answers with the page built from the saved file instead, so the frame still gets a page.
- A host's own `bundle` can set its own deadline (HyperFrames Desktop ends its page builds at 60 s). A bundle that comes back empty falls back to the same saved-file page.

The budget starts once the page has arrived.

- `useShadowPreviewReload.ts`: a budget that runs out while the shadow frame has its page address but still holds the blank document it started with does not count. The frame is waiting for the server. `logReload("shadow-awaiting-server")` notes it and the budget is armed again. A sealed (opaque) frame can't be read, so its budget is spent as before. `givenAddress` is the "was given a page address" test the give-up message already used, now shared by both.

## Before

Studio from source on `main`. After an edit on disk, every request for the preview page is answered 50 s late, as a page that slow to build would be. Studio gives the reload up at 45 s, asks once more, and gives that up at 92 s. Two minutes after the edit the preview still shows the old text.

![Before](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/607cc9c1-9ff9-4837-9c6a-ef844f1eaaa2)

## After

Same project, same edit, same 50 s answers, with this branch. Studio keeps waiting (Studio's own `[hf-reload]` log shows `shadow-awaiting-server` at 15, 30 and 45 s), and the edit shows 50.4 s after it was saved, with no error message.

![After](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ea3f8683-0427-46a0-83d0-259ae21f089b)

Both runs use the same Playwright script. It edits the project's `index.html` and holds every preview page request after the edit for 50 s before letting it through to the server.

## What I measured

- **Fails without the fix:** with the new test and `main`'s `useShadowPreviewReload.ts`, "waits while its frame waits on the server for the page, and spends its budget once the page arrives" fails: the reload was given up while the page was still on its way. The other 65 tests in the file pass.
- **With the fix:** these pass 83/83, 3 runs in a row on a Linux devbox:
  - `useTimelinePlayer.shadowReload`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.shadowRetry`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.reloadStill`
  - `useTimelinePlayer.reloadedTimeline`

  `NLEPreview.slowBoot` passes 2/2. lefthook pre-commit (filesize, format, lint, fallow, typecheck) is green.
- The new test holds the shadow frame blank, with its page address, for 61 s, and the reload is not given up. When the page then arrives and never gets ready, the reload is given up once, after the normal budgets.
- The old case for a blank frame that was never given a page address still gives up after the full wait. Its message is unchanged.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A server that never answers at all. The browser ends such a navigation with its own error page, and the frame's load then fails the reload. I have not timed that.
- A sealed (opaque-origin) preview frame. Its document can't be read, so it keeps the old budget.
- macOS and Windows. The captures are headless Chrome on Linux.

## Searched first

`git grep -n "SHADOW_READY_TIMEOUT_MS\|budgetsSpentRef"` in `packages/studio/src`: the ready timer in `useShadowPreviewReload.ts` is the one place a shadow reload's wait is counted, and `shadowPagePhase` already tells a blank frame from a loading one. So the check goes there, with no new timer.

title: fix(studio): load the preview runtime before any page script in every page shape
body:
## What

The Studio preview's runtime script now loads before any page script in all document shapes. A page that opens with its `<head>` is served byte for byte as before.

## Why

Studio puts the runtime script at the start of a preview page's head so the runtime is in place before the page's own scripts run. For a page that carries a script ahead of its `<head>`, has no `<head>`, or has its `<body>` first, the runtime tag landed after that script, and a browser ran the page's script first.

## Related work

None open that overlaps. This touches only `insertRuntimeTag`'s head-start mode, whose one caller is the Studio preview (`withPreviewRuntime`).

## How

`insertRuntimeTag(html, tag, true)` now places the tag at `headContentStart(html)`, the position the preview variables and the GSAP fallback already use: inside a `<head>` that opens the page, else straight after the doctype or `<html>`, else at the top. The canvas tracker a motion-blur page gets with the runtime goes to the same place.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable, no user-visible option or command changes
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Fails without the fix: `packages/core/src/compiler/htmlDocument.test.ts` (7 red) and `packages/studio-server/src/routes/preview.runtimeFirst.test.ts` (22 red). Both green with it.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5.2</summary>

### What moves

| Page shape | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Opens with `<head>` (after an optional doctype, comments, `<html>`) | runtime first | same bytes |
| Script between `<html>` and `<head>` | page script first | runtime first, straight after `<html>` |
| Script before `<html>` | page script first | runtime first, straight after the doctype |
| Script before the doctype | page script first | runtime first, at the top |
| `<html>` with no `<head>` | page script first | runtime first, straight after `<html>` |
| No `<head>` and no `<body>` | runtime first | runtime first (top of the page, as before) |
| A `<head>` inside a comment ahead of the real one | page script first | runtime first |
| An `<svg><script>` before `<html>` | page script first | runtime first |
| `<body>` before `<head>` | page script first | runtime first |

Which preview paths were affected: the root page built by the bundler already opened with `<head>` (the bundler writes the page out again and holds page scripts for the runtime), and a single composition file's page is rebuilt from its head and body. The page served from the saved file, when the build returns nothing or throws, kept the author's shape; that is the path this changes.

### Verification

- Route test, 72 cases: nine shapes x (build runs, build returns nothing, build throws) x (no host step, a host step that parses the page and writes it out again), plus the single composition file page.
- Unit test: the eight odd shapes get the runtime and the tracker ahead of the author script with no other text changed; a page that opens with its head gets exactly the output it got before.
- Chrome 18 of 18: each served page (nine shapes, with and without the host step) loaded in headless Chrome with a stand-in runtime script that records the order; the runtime ran before the page script in every one.
- Full `packages/studio-server` suite: 2,742 pass, 1 timed out under load (`proxyTranscoder.test.ts`, "moves another project's activity mark..."), which passes when its file runs alone (102 of 102) and does not reach this code. `packages/core/src/compiler`: 818 pass.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit` in core and studio-server, `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs`: clean.

Not run: the full monorepo test and build matrix (left to CI).

### Self-review

1. **Siblings.** `insertRuntimeTag` has two callers: `withPreviewRuntime` (head-start mode, changed) and the bundler's `htmlBundler.ts` (default mode, unchanged; it places the tag before `</head>` of a page it has just written out). `withPreviewRuntime` is called from the root page build, the single composition build and the saved-file fallback; all three are covered by the route test. `injectTagsAtHeadStart` keeps its behaviour for its other callers (CLI servers, render file servers, inspector), which are not Studio previews.
2. **Failure paths.** The change is a pure string function with no state to clean up. The build-throws and build-returns-nothing paths are in the route test.
3. **Races.** None: no shared or cached value is read; the position is computed from the same string it is inserted into.
4. **Inputs.** The position comes from `headContentStart`, which reads tags the way a browser's tokenizer does (a `<head>` inside a comment or an attribute value is not a head); the unit test has a page with `<head>` text in an attribute and one with a `<head>` in a comment.
5. **Tests prove it.** See "Fails without the fix" above; the tests use the real route (`createStudioApi`) and the real bundler, and run in the default suite.
6. **Rollout.** Previews are built per request and cached by project content; a cached page from before stays valid for pages that open with their head (same bytes). An odd-shaped page cached before this change is served until the project's content changes.
7. **Normal path.** A normal page was loaded through the route and in Chrome: runtime first, output identical to before.

</details>

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(cli): a team member's checkout signs in to their own workspace and buys there
body:
## What changes for people

Someone signed in to a team workspace where they are not the admin runs `hyperframes billing subscribe` (or `add-credits`), presses Enter to pay, and today gets only "HeyGen would not open a checkout". Only a team's admin can buy its plan, so nothing they do from the terminal works.

Now the CLI says "Only this team's admin can buy its plan. Sign in to your own workspace to buy it there.", opens the sign-in page with their own workspace already picked, and once the sign-in lands there it opens the checkout in that workspace.

**The CLI stays signed in to the person's own workspace afterwards.** That is Miguel's call ("switch to the person's own space"): the plan they buy lives there, so later runs use it. A sign-in token is bound to one workspace and the CLI cannot swap it quietly, so the switch is a real sign-in.

When no one can sign in from here (no one at the terminal, SSH or a headless box), or the credential comes from the environment (`HEYGEN_API_KEY`, `HEYGEN_ACCESS_TOKEN`), which a sign-in cannot replace, nothing opens: the CLI prints "Only this team's admin can buy its plan. Run `hyperframes auth login`, pick your own workspace, and try again." The same line shows if the sign-in lands anywhere else.

## How

- `postCheckout` reads HeyGen's refusal: a 403 with code `400573` on the checkout routes comes from the workspace role check (a team member below admin). It throws `CheckoutError("checkout_team_role")` with the line above, instead of the bare "would not open a checkout".
- `signInToOwnSpace(timeoutMs)`: the person's own workspace id is their username. It runs the existing browser sign-in with `workspace_hint` set to it (the sign-in page picks that workspace first, the person can still change it), then reads the signed-in workspace back and returns whether it landed there.
- `billing`: on `checkout_team_role`, attended and with a browser, it signs in (bounded by the command's own `--timeout`) and retries the checkout once.
- `startAuthorizationCodeFlow` takes an optional `workspaceHint`; `auth login` is unchanged.
- Telemetry: `cli_billing_checkout_failed` gains the closed reason `checkout_team_role`, typed from `CheckoutFailure` so the two lists can't drift.

## Tests

fails without the fix: `plan.test.ts` "tells HeyGen's refusal of a team member below admin apart from any other" (main reads it as `checkout_rejected`), and `billing.test.ts` "signs in to the person's own space and opens the checkout there" (main ends at the refusal with no sign-in and no checkout).

Also covered: the sign-in carries the hint and reports a landing elsewhere as false; an environment credential opens no sign-in; no checkout opens when the sign-in did not land; a headless terminal opens no sign-in; `auth login` without a hint sends no `workspace_hint`.

Not covered: a real sign-in against HeyGen from a team account below admin (no such test account here). If the person signs in to a different HeyGen account in the browser, the landing check fails and no checkout opens, but the CLI keeps that new sign-in, as `auth login` would.

title: fix(studio-server): keep uploaded files that have a run of dots in their name
body:
## What

Files with a run of dots in the name (for example `clip....mp3` or `take..2.wav`) are no longer silently skipped on upload. Names that Windows would save under a different name are now refused openly, in `skipped`.

## Why

`processUploadedFiles` refused any uploaded file whose name *contained* `..`. A name like `clip....mp3` was dropped with no error, and it showed in neither `uploaded` nor `skipped`, so the person never learned why the file was missing.

That substring check also happened to refuse some names that are unsafe on Windows (`clip...`). Narrowing it must not let those through: Windows drops a trailing dot or space and refuses device names, so the file on disk would not match the name the route reports.

## Related work

Tiny self-contained correction; no separate issue.

## How

`src/helpers/uploadedFileName.ts` has two checks.

- `uploadedFileName(sent)` keeps the last component of the name the browser sent, as before. It refuses an empty name, a name holding a NUL, or a name that is exactly `.` or `..`. Those are still dropped silently, as before.
  - Since the name is already a single component, a run of dots inside it cannot leave the target folder.
- `savesUnderItsOwnName(name, platform)` refuses three kinds of name, which the route reports in `skipped` before any collision suffix is chosen:
  - a name ending in a dot or a space;
  - a Windows device name (`CON`, `PRN`, `AUX`, `NUL`, `CONIN$`, `CONOUT$`, `COM1`–`9`, `LPT1`–`9`, and the superscript `COM¹`–`³` / `LPT¹`–`³`) in any case, with or without an extension (`con.mp3`, `NUL.tar.gz`);
  - on Windows only, any name with a colon (`C:foo`, `a.mp3:x`). Colon names stay accepted on other platforms, as before this PR.
- The destination checks after these are unchanged: `isSafePath(projectDir, …)` for the path and its collision-suffixed variant, plus `isWritableProjectFile`.

## Test plan

- `src/helpers/uploadedFileName.test.ts` covers these cases:
  - a folder in the sent name is stripped (`/` and `\`);
  - dotted names are kept;
  - empty, NUL, `.`, `..`, `clips/..` and `clips\..` are refused;
  - trailing dot or space is refused;
  - device names are refused, including `com¹.mp3`, `LPT³.wav` and `CONOUT$`, while `console.mp3`, `com10.mp4`, `lpt0.wav`, `com⁴.mp3`, `coninput.txt` and `conout.mp3` are kept;
  - colons are refused on win32 and kept on linux/darwin.
- `src/routes/files.pathSafety.test.ts` covers the upload route itself:
  - a `clip....mp3` upload is written byte-for-byte and listed in `files`;
  - `clip...`, `clip.mp3 `, `con.mp3`, `CONOUT$.txt`, `com¹.mp3` and `LPT³.wav` come back in `skipped` and nothing is written;
  - `..unsafe.txt` comes back in `skipped` and nothing is written. The project's existing hidden-file write rule refuses it, unchanged by this PR;
  - `..`, `clips/..` and `clips\..` uploads write nothing.
- Fails without the fix:
  - The `clip....mp3` route test fails on the first commit's wiring (93b2295663) with `expected [] to deeply equal [ 'clip....mp3' ]`.
  - The `clip...`, `clip.mp3 ` and `con.mp3` route tests fail on 5230e8e556, which wrote those files.
  - The superscript and console device tests (one unit test and three route cases) fail on 9c567e7b1d.
  - At 7c445f38d0 all pass. `files.pathSafety.test.ts` gives 147/147 with the package's own vitest config.
- `files.pathSafety.test.ts` now runs under `// @vitest-environment node`, as five other route tests here already do. The package default, happy-dom, reads a multipart file name as Latin-1, so `com¹.mp3` reached the route garbled.
- oxfmt and oxlint are clean. The comment checks pass, both the citations check and the package comment-share ratchet.

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Not exercised:
- a real upload through the Studio UI;
- an upload on a Windows host (the colon rule is unit-tested by platform);
- the full studio-server suite locally (CI runs it).

title: fix(studio): make the preview's editing channel in Studio and send the frame one end
body:
## What

Studio now makes the preview's editing channel itself and sends the frame one end of it. The runtime serves the port it is sent and no longer posts a port to its parent. The editing protocol moves to version 2.

## Why

The editing channel was created inside the preview frame and handed up to Studio in a window message, so Studio had to take a port from whatever the frame's window posted. With the channel made in Studio, the only port Studio ever uses is one it created, and a client is ready only when that channel answers.

## Related work

Follows #8996 (the runtime script loads before any page script in every page shape), which this relies on: the runtime listens for the connect from its first evaluation. Does not touch `useSealedCanvasKeys.ts` (#8993).

## How

- **Client (`createEditingPortClient`).** Makes a `MessageChannel`, posts `editing-connect` (v2) with one port in the transfer list, and sends a `hello` on its own end. It is `ready` on the first v2 `ok` answer on that end. On each `ready` note from the frame before it is connected, it closes the unanswered channel and offers a fresh one. It never takes a port from a window message.
- **Runtime.** A capture listener on `window`, added when the runtime first evaluates, ends every connect-shaped message from the parent it loaded with, so no later listener on the page sees the port. It serves the port only for a v2 connect with exactly one port, in a page the preview server marked; otherwise it closes the ports. A connect that lands before the agent starts waits and is served when it starts. The runtime posts nothing to the parent.
- **Version 2.** A v1 client offers no port and a v1 runtime does not serve one, so a mixed pair does not connect; requests carry the version as before.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable, no user-visible option or command changes. Hosts that embed Studio's editing client take the runtime and the client from the same release, as they already do
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

Fails without the change: `packages/core/src/runtime/editingPort.test.ts` ("offers a channel at once and a fresh one on ready, and is ready only on its own channel's answer": the old client sends no port with its connect) and `packages/core/src/runtime/editingAgent.test.ts` ("ends the parent's connect at its own listener, so a page listener never sees the port").

## No visible change

Nothing Studio or the player draws changes: the Studio and player files touched are test helpers and the edit-accuracy bench's own client, and the editing channel carries the same requests and answers as before. Only how the channel is set up differs.

<details>
<summary>Claude Fable 5.2</summary>

### What changes at runtime

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Who makes the channel | the runtime, in the frame | Studio |
| Window message from frame to parent with a port | `editing-port` | none |
| When the client is ready | a port arrives from the frame's window | its own channel answers `hello` |
| Connect seen by page listeners | yes | no (ended at the runtime's capture listener) |
| Connect the runtime does not serve | ignored | its port is closed |
| Runtime starts listening | when the agent installs (after parse) | when the runtime first evaluates |
| Protocol version | 1 | 2 |

Files: `editingPort.ts` (client), `editingAgent.ts` (runtime listener), `runtimePort.ts` (reads the event's ports and ends the event with built-ins read at load), `entry.ts` (starts the listener first). The rest is tests and test harnesses that spoke the old handover: the shared Studio sealed-frame helper, the timeline harness, the browser ordering harness, the edit-accuracy bench's own client, and the producer's render-page test.

### Verification

- `packages/core` `src/runtime`: 179 files, 3,910 tests pass.
- `packages/studio` full suite: 881 files, 9,911 tests pass, including the two files that run a real sealed frame with the real runtime in Chrome (`sealedPreviewOrdering.browser.test.ts`, `sealedPreviewOrderingGenerated.browser.test.ts`).
- `packages/producer` `renderPageEditingPort.test.ts` in Chrome: a render page serves no port.
- `tests/e2e/edit-accuracy/teleport.test.mjs`: 32 pass.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, `tsc --noEmit`, `fallow audit`, `scripts/comment-ratchet.mjs`: clean.

Not run: the full monorepo test and build matrix, and the edit-accuracy bench against a live Studio (left to CI).

### One flaky browser walk, measured on both sides

`packages/studio/tests/e2e/preview-failure-retry.mjs` failed once in CI on this head (its last step: an open inline text edit must be saved after the preview fails and is retried) and passed on a re-run of the same commit. Run locally in real Chrome, 20 times on each side with a fresh fixture per run: this head (`a69e7cb20a`) failed 3 of 20, `main` (`2ade736905`) failed 6 of 20, every failure at the same wait (line 154). The walk is flaky on `main` and this change does not make it fail more often.

### Self-review

1. **Siblings.** Every speaker of the handover was found by searching for `editing-connect` and `editing-port`: the client and the runtime (changed), Studio's one client getter `previewEditingClient` (uses the client, unchanged), the edit-accuracy bench's own client (changed to make its own channel), and test harnesses (changed). The player package and the CLI do not speak it. Render pages (`PREVIEW_FOR_ANOTHER_SITE_META`) still serve no port; test kept.
2. **Failure paths.** A connect posted while the frame is mid-navigation throws in the client and is retried on the frame's next `ready`. An unanswered channel is closed when a fresh one is offered and on dispose. A connect the runtime will not serve has its ports closed, so the sender's end sees a close instead of a silent wait. When the port built-ins cannot be read at load, the runtime still ends the connect and serves nothing (tested).
3. **Races.** `ready` from the frame can land before, between or after connects: three orderings are tested, each ends with one working port. A connect that lands before the agent starts is held and served at start (tested). An answer on a channel the client has already replaced is ignored (`port1 !== offered`).
4. **Inputs.** The runtime serves only when the event is from the parent read at load, is trusted, carries exactly one port, names version 2 and the page has the preview server's mark; tests cover a connect from the page itself, another frame, no source, versions 1 and 3, another `source` value, no port and two ports. The client accepts only a plain-object answer with `v: 2` and `ok: true` on the channel it offered; a port posted by the frame's window, in the old shape at either version, is ignored (tested).
5. **Tests prove it.** With the four non-test files reverted, the two tests named above go red (run one at a time against the old source). Fixtures use the production agent and client; the port-capture file checks that patches to `MessagePort`, `MessageEvent.prototype.ports`, `stopImmediatePropagation`, `Set.add` and `Map.set` made after load do not reach the port.
6. **Rollout.** Client and runtime ship in the same release and Studio serves its own runtime to the preview, so a mixed pair arises only when a host pins them apart; then they do not connect and the preview stays read-only through the editing channel, rather than half working. No stored data or settings change.
7. **Happy path.** The full Studio suite, including the real-Chrome sealed-frame runs (saves, undo, reloads, scrubs against a sandboxed frame), passes on the new connect.

</details>

title: test(cli): studio server test cleanup waits for shutdown before deleting the temp root
body:
## What changed

The studio server test fixture's `cleanupStudioServerRoot` closed the file watcher and deleted the temp root straight away, while the server's project history could still be writing under that root. A history write landing during the delete makes `rmSync` fail with `ENOTEMPTY` (seen in a merge-queue run: `studioServer.receivedRecord.test.ts`, "lists a file holding received content again before a split-batch edit names it", `rmdir '<root>/history'`).

`cleanupStudioServerRoot` now awaits `server.shutdown()` before the delete. `shutdown()` is the server's own close path: it closes every history it opened (`histories.closeAll()`), which commits pending writes. The cleanup is async, so the 8 test files that use it now await it in `afterEach`.

No product code changes.

## What I measured

- **fails without the fix:** `packages/cli/src/server/studioServerTestFixture.test.ts` (new) holds the server's shutdown open and checks the root still exists until it finishes. With `studioServerTestFixture.ts` from `origin/main`: `expected false to be true` (the root was deleted before shutdown finished). With the change: passes, 3 runs in a row, exit 0.
- The original flake is rare: `studioServer.receivedRecord.test.ts` on `origin/main` failed 1 of 15 runs locally with the same `ENOTEMPTY`, then 0 of 30 runs (3 at a time). With the change, 0 of 30.
- All 9 test files that use the fixture, 3 shuffled runs: 89 passed, 2 skipped, and 2 failures in `studioServer.previewAssets.test.ts` (HEIC photo conversion) that fail the same way on `origin/main` on this Linux machine, so they come from its image library, not this change.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, the comment ratchet and citation checks: clean on the changed files.

## What I did NOT exercise

- `studioServer.previewNetworkShare.win32.test.ts` runs on Windows only; it is changed only to await the cleanup.
- `shutdown()` waits at most 2 s for histories to close; a close slower than that could still race the delete.

title: fix(studio): waveforms repaint on page root changes only near the screen and on new colours
body:
## What changed

Every audio clip's waveform on the timeline watched the page's root element (`<html>`) for class and style changes,
so a theme switch recolours its bars. That watcher called `draw` for every waveform, including ones far off screen,
on any write to `<html>`'s style. The app writes there for layout reasons too (the toast corner, the notice stack,
the update corner), several times through an agent run. A waveform whose strip has not been measured yet draws its
whole clip: a canvas as wide as the clip at device pixels, two `getComputedStyle` reads and three `fillRect`s per
3 px. On a long film with many audio clips, one such write repainted all of them in a single task, long enough for
the app to stop responding.

Now only a waveform near the screen watches `<html>`, and it repaints only when its bar or baseline colour actually
changed. The colour read moved into `waveformColours`, which `drawWaveformCanvas` also uses, so both read the same
two properties.

## What I measured

- fails without the fix: `AudioWaveform.test.tsx` "paints no off-screen waveform when the page's <html> style
  changes" (40 off-screen waveforms, one style write) fails on main with `getContext` called 40 times; "repaints a
  waveform near the screen on an <html> change only when its colours changed" fails on main at "a toast moved: same
  colours" (a repaint with unchanged colours). Both pass here, 3 runs in a row.
- The rest of `AudioWaveform.test.tsx` (off-screen through a zoom, near-screen redraws, fades, muted) and the 6
  covering test files pass; `tsc` in studio, lint, format, Fallow and pre-push are clean.

## What I did NOT exercise

- A theme switch in a running Studio: the test drives the colour change through computed style, not real CSS.
- A long film's timeline in a browser before and after; the change removes the off-screen repaints outright rather
  than making them cheaper.

title: fix(studio): style values from a preview frame cannot load anything in Studio's page
body:
## What

Style values a preview frame reports (computed and authored styles, and the caret and selection colours of a text edit) reach Studio only when they are values of their property and cannot load anything in Studio's page. The gradient fill field reads only one closed gradient.

## Why

These values are written into Studio's own page as styles. A value such as a `var()` whose fallback is a `url()`, a second background layer after a gradient, or a function name spelled with a CSS escape parses as CSS, so Studio's page would load whatever it names. A browser never computes values like these; a frame whose page script answers for it can send them.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `utils/cssLoads.ts` holds the one rule: a value is refused when it holds an escape, a comment, a substitution function (`var`, `env`, `attr`) or a loading function (`url`, `src`, `image`, `image-set`, `cross-fade`, `element`, `paint`), or is longer than 4,096 characters. A caller can keep `url()` or `var()` where it shows the value only as text or shuts it inside one gradient.
- `previewChannel.ts`: `frameStyleValue` applies that rule and still requires the value to parse for its property. It keeps `url()` only for `background-image`: Studio shows that url as text and loads only a project file it resolves itself. `readStyles` now passes every value through `frameStyleValue`, so computed styles, authored styles and every match of a selector get the same check the text-edit colours already had.
- `gradientValue.ts`: `parseGradient` returns null, and the field draws its default gradient (`propertyPanelFill.tsx`, `parseGradient(value) ?? buildDefaultGradientModel(fallbackColor)`), unless the value is exactly one gradient whose parentheses close in order and that loads nothing. A `var()` stop stays, as Studio already mixes those, since inside one closed gradient it cannot add a layer.

Searched for an existing check first (`grep -rn "url\\(\|image-set" packages/*/src`): core's `richTextSanitize.ts` and `editing/dragChrome.ts` each keep a check for their own case (what rich text may store, what a drag copy may paint). This one is Studio's, for values a frame reports.

Not changed: a clip whose media is on another site still shows its thumbnail loaded from that address, as before.

In a sealed preview, a filter, clip path or `box-shadow` whose value holds `url()` or `var()` now reads as unset in the inspector, as do authored values written with `var()`.

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Manual testing performed
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable): not applicable, no user-visible option or command changes
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments": they say why, not what, and a bug fix says what the code must do and how to reproduce the bug

fails without the fix: `packages/studio/src/player/lib/previewChannel.frameColours.test.ts` ("refuses a frame colour that defers to Studio's page or spells a load"), `packages/studio/src/player/lib/previewChannel.test.ts` ("reach Studio only when they cannot load anything in Studio's page") and `packages/studio/src/components/editor/gradientValue.test.ts` ("is null, so Studio draws its own default", 4 of its 5 cases): 6 tests red on `main`, green with the change.

Ran at this head: the three test files above plus `colorBrowserCanvas.test.ts` and `domEditTextCommits.sealed.test.ts` (81 tests pass), the full Studio suite (883 files, 9,929 tests pass), and the repo hooks (lint, format, typecheck, fallow). Not run: a real sealed preview in a browser.

## No visible change

Nothing Studio draws changes for a value a browser computes: real colours, gradients and background images read and show as before. Only values a browser never computes are left out.

title: fix(share): bound gitignore rules during source capture
body:
Source capture validates gitignore-style rules before constructing a matcher and checks each path before asking the matcher to evaluate its ancestors. A capture that exceeds either limit fails before it returns an inventory. An empty or comment-only ignore file keeps the usual scratch-file behavior.

Existing ordered rules, negation, two-star filenames such as `*.min.*`, and recursive directory rules such as `**/cache/**` use the package's existing matcher. The package README and source capture guide describe the rule and path limits. Callers can distinguish an unsupported rule, a path outside the limits, and an unreadable ignore file through `SourceIgnoreError.reason`.

The share package built successfully. All 207 package tests passed with `bun run --cwd packages/share test`, including comparisons with the existing matcher and a capture that exceeds the path-depth limit. The changed JavaScript passed oxlint and oxfmt.

title: fix(studio): a sealed resize saves the element's original box, as an open one does
body:
## What

A resize in a sealed preview now records the element's original box (`data-hf-studio-original-box-width` / `-height`) as the element's real size, the same values an open preview records. It used to record `0` and `0`. Open previews record exactly what they did before.

## Why

On the first resize, Studio keeps the element's original layout box. The box goes into the saved HTML, so a later edit can tell the size the author wrote from the size Studio drew. Studio measured it with the element's own `offsetWidth` / `offsetHeight`. In a sealed preview that element is Studio's stand-in for the film's element, and it has no layout, so the box was saved as 0 x 0. The draft base a resize starts from was read the same way.

## Related work

The frame already reports each pressed element's layout box when a gesture starts. Crop handles and the GSAP resize path already read it from there.

## How

- `packages/studio/src/components/editor/gestureStartLayouts.ts`: the per-press layout boxes from the gesture-start read, by handle, now in a module of their own. `manualEditsDom.ts` can't import `previewGestureStartRead.ts` without an import cycle (that one reaches `manualOffsetDrag.ts`, which imports `manualEditsDom.ts`). `previewGestureStartRead.ts` writes the boxes and re-exports `gestureStartLayout`, so crop handles and `gsapResizeIntercept.ts` are untouched.
- `packages/studio/src/components/editor/manualEditsDom.ts`: `layoutBox(element)` returns the frame's box at the press for a sealed stand-in, and the element's own offset size for anything else. The original-box stamp and the resize draft's base both use it.

Other size reads I checked on the edit commit path that could meet a stand-in:
- `domEditOverlayCrop.ts` `readElementCropFrame`: already routes a stand-in to the frame's layout.
- `domEditOverlayStartGesture.ts`: reads the gesture start's layout before the element's offset size.
- `manualOffsetDrag.ts` move probe: a stand-in has no box, so the drag takes the frame's own probe. Measured equal to open's conversion.
- `cropResize.ts` `boxOf`: reads the stand-in's offset size for crop-follows-resize, so a sealed resize skips that crop rescale here. Not changed in this PR: it is separate behaviour and needs its own check.

## Test plan

- fails without the fix: `packages/studio/src/components/editor/manualEditsDom.originalBox.sealed.test.ts` ("stamps the box the frame measured at the press, the same as open's", "starts a sealed resize draft from that box too"). Both fail against main (`['0','0']`, `{ width: 0, height: 0 }`). Putting either read back on the stand-in's own size fails its test.
- `src/components/editor` and `src/hooks` (390 files, 4320 tests) pass; the 7 touched test files pass 3 runs. `tsc --noEmit` and `oxlint` clean.
- Edit-accuracy bench at this commit (CLI built from this branch), both preview modes (sealed: the film's frame in its own process for every case, as the bench reports it), pointer at whole pixels: `move-hold-px-r0-root-z100`, `resize-hold-px-r0-root-z100`, `resize-hold-px-r0-nested-z100` and `rotate-hold-px-r0-nested-z100` save byte-identical files sealed and open. The sealed resize now records `240` / `160`, as open does; on main it recorded `0` / `0`.
- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [x] Manual testing performed: the bench runs above
- [x] Comments follow CONTRIBUTING.md "Comments"

## No visible change

Nothing on screen changes; only the saved `data-hf-studio-original-box-*` values for a resize in a sealed preview.

title: fix(core): a sealed preview keeps a clip's picture while its lighter copy is made
body:
## What

In a sealed project preview (`sandbox-origin`), a clip that is switching to a lighter copy keeps showing its own frame while the copy is made, as it already does in an open preview. Before, the clip's box went black (only the titles over it) for about 2 seconds.

## Why

When the preview steps its quality down, the runtime holds a clip off its file and sets the clip's poster to a still of the clip at the playhead (`hf-proxy-still`) until the lighter copy is ready. After that reset the browser draws the poster, not the decoded frame, until the clip plays or seeks.

In a sealed frame the browser did not send the poster's image request at all while the frame's copy request was waiting: in the request log it has no send time for the whole wait and is cancelled when the copy lands, about 2 s later. In an open frame the same request is sent at once and answers in about 50 ms. The server is not involved: stills run in their own job pool, and the same URL fetched from the sealed frame at the same moment is sent at once and answers in 44-48 ms.

## Related work

None.

## How

- `showStill` (in `packages/core/src/runtime/mediaProxy.ts`): in a sealed frame (`window.origin === "null"`, the same test `colorGrading.ts` uses for an opaque frame) it fetches the still and sets the poster to an object URL of the answer. An open frame sets the poster URL as before, unchanged.
- An answer counts only for the hold that asked for it: if `dropStill` ran or a newer still was asked for meanwhile, it is ignored. `dropStill` revokes the object URL.
- A failed or refused fetch leaves no poster, as a failed poster image does in an open frame. An answer that arrives after the page set its own poster is ignored.
- The runtime now remembers the poster its still put up, in both kinds of frame. When the copy swap holds the clip's current frame, it saves "no poster" instead of the runtime's still as the page's own, and dropping the still removes the poster only if it is still the runtime's. Before, if the copy drew its first frame only after a seek, the swap put the dropped still back (a stale still URL in an open frame, a revoked object URL in a sealed one), and dropping the still also removed a poster the page had set meanwhile.
- The fetch is readable from the sealed frame: the token path already answers a sealed frame's `fetch` of any preview file with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: null` (`opaqueFrameLoads.ts`).
